original_explanation: The OG ballpen. This is what Jose Rizal used to write his novels and stir up a revolution. Today, it's the fancy pen your boss uses to sign important documents, or the one you buy to feel 'artsy' but end up just using a regular Pilot G-Tec anyway. It's a symbol of the writer, the intellectual, the 'manunulat'.
usage_notes: While it can mean any pen, it has a more literary, formal, and slightly archaic feel compared to the common 'bolpen'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ni Rizal ang kanyang **pluma** upang gisingin ang damdaming makabayan ng mga Pilipino.","translation":"Rizal used his **pen** to awaken the patriotic feelings of the Filipinos."},{"sentence":"Isang mamahaling **pluma** ang regalo niya sa kanyang ama.","translation":"An expensive **fountain pen** was his gift to his father."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kakayahan ng isip na magpanatili at magbalik-tanaw sa mga nakaraang karanasan, impormasyon, o damdamin.
etymology: Mula sa ugat na "alaala" na nangangahulugang memorya.
original_explanation: This is your brain's 'Throwback Thursday' feature. It's that feeling when a song suddenly transports you back to your high school prom, or the smell of a certain dish reminds you of your lola's cooking. It's the mental act of revisiting your past, for better or for worse (hello, ex!). Not to be confused with its anxious cousin, pag-aalala.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa kilos ng paggunita o sa memorya mismo. Iba ang diin at kahulugan nito sa "pag-aalala" (worry).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang litratong ito ay isang magandang **pag-aalaala** ng ating kabataan.","translation":"This picture is a beautiful **remembrance** of our youth."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pag-aalaala**, masaya ang kanilang pinagsamahan.","translation":"In his **recollection**, their time together was happy."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babae na may katangiang labis, madamdamin, o eksaherado sa kilos, pananalita, at pagpapahayag ng emosyon.
original_explanation: Siya 'yung friend mong laging may 'hugot' at 'major life event' every week. Konting kibot, iiyak. Konting success, parang nanalo sa Miss Universe. Siya ang reyna ng eksena, ang bida sa sarili niyang teleserye. Over-acting, pero in a fabulous way. In short, **dramatika**.
usage_notes: Ito ang pambabaeng anyo ng 'dramatiko'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang pansinin, **dramatika** lang talaga 'yang si Anna.","translation":"Don't mind her, Anna is just being **dramatic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aklat ng mga salita ng isang wika, na karaniwang nakaayos nang paalpabeto, na nagbibigay ng impormasyon tungkol sa anyo, pagbigkas, gamit, etimolohiya, at kahulugan nito.
etymology: From *tala-* (list, record) + *tinig* (sound, voice) + *-an* (locus). Literally 'a list of sounds/pronunciations'.
original_explanation: The 'official' rulebook for words, the ancestor of Google Translate and dictionary apps. Before you could just type a word and get its meaning, you had to flip through a thick book called a **talatinigan**. It's the ultimate source of truth when you're arguing with your friends if a word is real or not.
usage_notes: A very formal word. 'Diksiyonaryo' (from Spanish 'diccionario') is much more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hanapin mo sa **talatinigan** ang kahulugan ng salitang 'marahuyo'.","translation":"Look for the meaning of the word 'marahuyo' in the **dictionary**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga linggwista ay bumubuo ng isang komprehensibong **talatinigan** ng mga katutubong wika.","translation":"The linguists are creating a comprehensive **dictionary** of indigenous languages."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasukasuan sa gitnang bahagi ng binti ng tao, sa pagitan ng hita at lulod, na nagpapahintulot sa pagbaluktot nito.
original_explanation: The part of your body that reminds you you're not getting any younger every time you squat or climb stairs. Also, the favorite landing spot for toddlers running at full speed. In the Philippines, it's also where you apply Vicks or 'manzanilla' for literally any ailment as a child.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit ang **tuhod** ko pagkatapos naming mag-hike.","translation":"My **knee** hurts after we went hiking."},{"sentence":"Lumuhod siya at ipinatong ang kamay sa kanyang **tuhod**.","translation":"He knelt and placed his hand on his **knee**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan opisyal na naninirahan ang isang tao; isang tirahan, lalo na ang isang malaki at marangyang bahay.
original_explanation: Same as 'residensiya', but this spelling is more common in casual conversations. It's the slightly less formal, more everyday spelling for a fancy house. "Nakita mo na ba yung bagong residensya nung artista?"
usage_notes: A common spelling variant of 'residensiya'. Both are acceptable and widely understood, with this version being more frequent in informal speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang address na nakalagay sa kanyang ID ay ang kanyang permanenteng **residensya**.","translation":"The address on his ID is his permanent **residence**."},{"sentence":"Pinapangarap niyang magkaroon ng sariling **residensya** balang araw.","translation":"He dreams of having his own **residence** someday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na estatwa o rebulto, karaniwang ginagamit bilang palamuti.
original_explanation: Your Funko Pop collection? Those are pigurin. The tiny Santo Niño on your dashboard? Pigurin. The little ceramic cat from Japan that waves its paw? Pigurin. Basically, any small statue you use for decoration. It's the fancy lola's version of a toy collection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng mga mamahaling **pigurin** ang kanyang estante.","translation":"Her shelf is full of expensive **figurines**."},{"sentence":"Nabasag ang paborito niyang **pigurin** na baboy.","translation":"His favorite pig **figurine** broke."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtigil, paghinto, o pagbibigay-pahinga sa isang gawain o kilos; pagbabawas ng higpit o tindi.
original_explanation: It's the concept of "letting up" or "stopping." When your boss gives you tasks without 'lubay', you're overworked. When the rain falls without 'lubay', you get floods. It's the pause you desperately need but rarely get. "Walang lubay ang trabaho" is the official motto of every BPO agent during peak season.
usage_notes: Usually used in phrases like "walang lubay" (unceasing, relentless). The root word itself is not often used alone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang **lubay** ang pag-agos ng tulong para sa mga biktima ng bagyo.","translation":"The flow of help for the storm victims is unceasing (**without letting up**)."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng **lubay** sa katatrabaho para hindi ka magkasakit.","translation":"You need a **break** from working so you don't get sick."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang makapaglabas ng malakas na tinig o sigaw dahil sa gulat, takot, sakit, o matinding tuwa.
original_explanation: When your favorite K-pop group announces a Manila concert. When you see a cockroach fly towards you. When you win the grand prize in the office raffle. It's that sudden, uncontrollable shout that just bursts out of you before you can even think.
usage_notes: The prefix 'mapa-' indicates the action is involuntary or caused by an external stimulus, distinguishing it from 'sumigaw' (to shout intentionally).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napahiyaw** ang buong sinehan sa gulat sa biglang paglabas ng multo.","translation":"The whole cinema **shouted out** in surprise at the ghost's sudden appearance."}]

translation: to be able to be loaded; to be able to ride
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kakayahang maisakay o mailagay sa loob ng isang sasakyan o lalagyan. Ito rin ay tumutukoy sa kakayahang sumakay ng isang tao.
etymology: From Tagalog `lulan` (load, passenger, cargo). The prefix `ma-` and the suffix `-an` create a verb form indicating ability or potential. This is the future tense form.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of "kasya ba?" (will it fit?). It's you trying to figure out if your whole barkada can fit in one GrabCar, or if all your pasalubong will fit in your already-overweight luggage. "Malululan kaya lahat ng gamit ko sa Lalamove?" is a classic moving-out question.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb `malanan` (to be able to load/ride).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa tingin mo ba ay **malululan** ang lahat ng kahon sa maliit na trak na iyan?","translation":"Do you think all the boxes **can be loaded** onto that small truck?"},{"sentence":"Sampung tao lang ang **malululan** sa van na ito.","translation":"Only ten people **can ride** in this van."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangyayari nang salit-salitan; may pagitan o patlang sa pagitan ng mga pagganap o pangyayari.
original_explanation: Like your motivation to go to the gym—strong on Monday, gone by Wednesday, maybe back on Friday. It describes something that's on-again, off-again, like a flickering lightbulb or a PLDT connection during a storm.
usage_notes: This is a very rare adjective. The adverb 'salit-salit' (alternatingly) is far more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ulan ay **masalit**, kaya hindi kami makapagpasya kung aalis.","translation":"The rain is **intermittent**, so we can't decide if we should leave."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **masalit** na daloy ng kuryente, nasira ang aming mga gamit.","translation":"Because of the **alternating** (flickering) flow of electricity, our appliances broke."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sausage na karaniwang inilalagay sa tinapay. Naging popular ito bilang isang meme o biro sa internet.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "hotdog," na naging popular sa Pilipinas bilang isang internet meme.
original_explanation: It's 'hotdog,' but make it a meme. This started from a viral video and became the punchline to a nonsensical joke ('Ano'ng sabi ng isda nung nahiwa siya? Edi... 'I'm tuna!'... **Hatdog**!'). It's the Filipino equivalent of a random, absurdist punchline. You use it when a joke falls flat, or just to be deliberately random and funny. It's a word that perfectly captures Pinoy internet humor.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal and online conversations as a joke or a non-sequitur punchline. It can also refer to the actual food item.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng isang **hatdog** na may keso.","translation":"Can I buy one **hotdog** with cheese."},{"sentence":"Walang kwenta 'yung joke niya, kaya sumigaw na lang ako ng '**Hatdog**!'","translation":"His joke made no sense, so I just shouted '**Hatdog**!'"}]

translation: to make someone crave; to tempt with food
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagpapakita o pag-aalok ng masarap na pagkain sa isang tao upang siya ay maglaway o maghangad na kumain nito.
etymology: From the root word "takam", meaning a craving for food.
original_explanation: The evil thing your officemate does when they open a box of J.Co donuts while you're on a diet. It's when someone posts a glorious food-porn photo on Instagram with the caption "Kain tayo!" knowing full well you can't. To be 'tinakam' is to suffer from food-induced envy.
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the person being tempted, not the food. "Tinakaman" (past tense) is different from "natatakam" (adjective/state of craving).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **takamin** sa lechon na 'yan!","translation":"Don't **tempt me** with that lechon!"},{"sentence":"**Tinakaman** niya ang mga kapatid niya gamit ang huling piraso ng cake.","translation":"He **made his siblings crave** by showing them the last piece of cake."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sinaunang sistema ng pagsulat ng mga Pilipino bago pa man dumating ang mga Kastila, na isang uri ng abugida o alpasilabaryo.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino writing system before the Latin alphabet came and colonized our notebooks. It's that cool, curvy script you see on tattoos, t-shirts, and government logos to show off Pinoy pride. It's not an 'alphabet', it's an 'abugida'. Getting a tattoo of your ex's name in Baybayin is the ancient equivalent of a modern bad decision.
usage_notes: Often mistakenly called 'Alibata'. Each character represents a consonant-vowel syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng maraming kabataan ngayon ang pagsulat ng **Baybayin**.","translation":"Many young people today are studying how to write **Baybayin**."},{"sentence":"May tattoo siya ng pangalan niya na nakasulat sa **Baybayin**.","translation":"He has a tattoo of his name written in **Baybayin**."}]

translation: then, back then, at that time (past)
meaning_filipino: Ginagamit upang tukuyin ang isang tiyak na oras o panahon sa nakaraan.
original_explanation: This is the official starting phrase for any 'dati ganito kami, ngayon...' story. It's the ultimate TBT (#ThrowbackThursday) word. 'Noon, Meralco lang ang may bill. Ngayon, pati ako, may emotional bill na.'
usage_notes: Madalas sinusundan ng 'ay' o 'ay...', o ginagamitan ng pang-angkop na '-g' (noong). Halimbawa: Noong araw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Noon**, simple lang ang buhay sa probinsya.","translation":"**Back then**, life in the province was simple."},{"sentence":"Aalis na sana ako **noon** nang bigla siyang dumating.","translation":"I was about to leave **then** when he suddenly arrived."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang direksyon o punto sa pagitan ng timog at silangan, na nasa 135 digri sa kompas.
etymology: Isang tambalang salita na binubuo ng 'timog' (south) at 'silangan' (east).
original_explanation: Basically, where most of us are. Welcome to Southeast Asia! When you're giving directions and it's not quite south and not quite east, it's 'diyan sa bandang timog-silangan'.
usage_notes: Malawakang ginagamit sa heograpiya at upang tukuyin ang rehiyon ng Asya kung saan kabilang ang Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay isang bansa sa rehiyon ng **Timog-Silangan**g Asya.","translation":"The Philippines is a country in the **Southeast** Asian region."},{"sentence":"Nasa **timog-silangan**g bahagi ng mapa ang Mindanao.","translation":"Mindanao is in the **southeastern** part of the map."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng alahas na isinusuot sa pulso o braso; maaari ring tumukoy sa pangkabit sa dulo ng manggas ng damit (cufflink).
original_explanation: It's the old-school word for a bracelet or wristlet. Your lola might call her fancy gold bracelet a manilya. It can also mean cufflinks, those little things fancy dudes use to close their shirt sleeves, making it sound a bit more de buena familia.
usage_notes: While it can mean 'bracelet', 'pulseras' is far more common in modern conversation. Its use for 'cufflink' is also quite formal or dated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinamana sa kanya ng kanyang lola ang gintong **manilya** nito.","translation":"Her grandmother bequeathed her gold **bracelet** to her."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang isang piraso ng kanyang **manilya** kaya hindi niya maisara ang manggas ng kanyang barong.","translation":"He lost one of his **cufflinks** so he couldn't close the sleeve of his barong."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o lugar kung saan ikinukulong ang mga taong nagkasala sa batas o nahatulan ng hukuman; piitan o kulungan.
etymology: Possibly from 'bilin' (entrust) and 'bidbid' (to bind), suggesting a place where people are entrusted and bound.
original_explanation: When you hear "Bilibid," you're not thinking of a vacation spot. You're thinking of the New Bilibid Prison in Muntinlupa, the most famous (or infamous) prison in the Philippines. It's the place people joke about ending up in if they do something wrong. "Pag nahuli ka, sa Bilibid ang bagsak mo!"
usage_notes: While it is a general term for prison, it is most strongly associated with the New Bilibid Prison (NBP) in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bilanggo ay dinala sa Pambansang **Bilibid**.","translation":"The prisoners were brought to the National **Prison**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kape (Coffea liberica) na kilala sa matapang na lasa at malakas na amoy, na pangunahing itinatanim sa mga lalawigan ng Batangas at Cavite.
etymology: Named after the Spanish 'barraco' (boar) due to its strong, 'masculine' flavor and aroma.
original_explanation: This isn't your fancy, overpriced latte. This is *kapeng barako*, the coffee that will slap you awake and give you the energy to face EDSA traffic, your boss, and your 'di pa bayad na credit card bill. It's strong, unapologetic, and 100% Pinoy.
usage_notes: Often used as 'kapeng barako'. It's a specific coffee varietal (Liberica) but the term is also used colloquially for any very strong black coffee.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pampagising sa umaga ang isang tasang mainit na kapeng **barako**.","translation":"A hot cup of **barako** coffee is a great way to wake up in the morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha ng kaalaman o kasanayan sa isang partikular na paksa, karaniwan sa isang akademikong tagpuan.
etymology: From Malay 'ajar', meaning 'to teach' or 'to learn'.
original_explanation: The verb form! This is the grind. The late-night coffee sessions before an exam, the endless PowerPoints in a meeting, the YouTube tutorials you watch to fix the sink. 'Mag-aral' is the process. It's what you do to hopefully get the 'aral' (the lesson).
usage_notes: This root is used to form verbs like 'mag-aral' (to study), 'aralin' (to study something specific), and 'pag-aralan' (to study/analyze something). The pronunciation stress shifts to the second syllable when used as a verb root.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **mag-aral** nang mabuti para sa pagsusulit.","translation":"I need to **study** well for the exam."},{"sentence":"**Aralin** mo ang mga dokumentong ito bago ang pulong.","translation":"**Study** these documents before the meeting."}]

translation: to cause to stagger or sway
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng pagewang-gewang, pagiray, o hindi matatag na pagtayo o paglakad ng isang tao o bagay.
etymology: From `magpa-` (causative prefix) + reduplication of `giray` (to sway, stagger).
original_explanation: This is what too much Red Horse does to a person. It's the act of making someone or something unsteady on their feet. A strong earthquake can do this to a building, or a bully can do this by pushing someone. It's the 'wobbly' verb. Picture a drunk person trying to walk a straight line—the alcohol is what's making them "magpagiray-giray."
usage_notes: Describes causing an unsteady, wobbling motion. Often associated with drunkenness, dizziness, or structural instability.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malakas na suntok sa panga ang **nagpagiray-giray** sa boksingero.","translation":"The strong punch to the jaw **caused the boxer to stagger**."},{"sentence":"Sobrang pagod at puyat ang **nagpagiray-giray** sa kanya habang naglalakad.","translation":"Extreme fatigue and lack of sleep **made him sway** as he walked."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elektronikong kagamitan na tumatanggap ng mga signal ng radyo at ginagawang naririnig na tunog. Ito ay ang mismong aparato na ginagamit sa pakikinig.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung actual na box na pinakikinggan mo. Kung ang 'radyo' ay 'yung buong konsepto (media, waves, etc.), ang 'radyo resiber' ay 'yung gadget mismo. Para siyang phone mo, at 'yung 'internet' ay 'yung signal. The receiver is the hardware.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino na mas madalas naririnig sa larangan ng electronics kaysa sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Madalas, "radyo" na lang ang ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng bagong antena ang luma niyang **radyo resiber** para gumana.","translation":"His old **radio receiver** needs a new antenna to work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng ilog kung saan ito bumubuhos at sumasama sa dagat o sa mas malaking anyong tubig; wawa.
original_explanation: It's where the river finally meets the sea. Think of it as the grand finale of the river's journey, where fresh water and salt water have their 'meet-cute'. It's also a common place name, so if someone tells you to meet them at 'Sabang,' clarify if they mean the geographical feature or the barangay.
usage_notes: Primarily a geographical term. Also a common place name in the Philippines (e.g., Sabang, Puerto Princesa).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming isda ang nahuhuli sa **sabang** ng Ilog Pasig.","translation":"Many fish are caught at the **estuary** of the Pasig River."},{"sentence":"Nagtayo sila ng maliit na pamayanan malapit sa **sabang**.","translation":"They built a small community near the **river mouth**."}]

translation: to lead to; to result in; to end up at home
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdating sa isang partikular na kalagayan, resulta, o lokasyon, lalo na sa sariling tahanan, bilang bunga ng isang serye ng mga pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the "Saan tayo hahantong?" of verbs. Pwedeng literal na "Sana all, **mauwi** sa kasalan" (hope it ends in marriage) or 'yung group project na **nauwi** sa inuman. It's about the final destination, whether it's a happy ending, a hangover, or just finally getting home after a long day.
usage_notes: Can be literal (going home) or figurative (resulting in something). The phrase 'mauwi sa wala' means 'to come to nothing'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang simpleng pagtatalo nila ay **nauwi** sa malaking away.","translation":"Their simple argument **led to** a big fight."},{"sentence":"Pagod na ako, gusto ko nang **mauwi** sa bahay.","translation":"I'm tired, I just want to **be able to go home**."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng paghihirap niya ay **nauwi** rin sa tagumpay.","translation":"All his hardships eventually **resulted in** success."}]

translation: will be happy; will become happy
meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman o pagpapakita ng kaligayahan o kasiyahan sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: That thing you keep telling yourself will happen "kapag pumayat ako," "kapag naka-graduate na," or "kapag may jowa na." It's the future tense of happiness, the goal of every "sana all." Spoiler alert: you don't need a reason para sumaya.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb 'sumaya' (to become happy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sigurado akong **sasaya** ka kapag nakita mo ang regalo niya.","translation":"I'm sure you **will be happy** when you see his gift."},{"sentence":"Balang araw, **sasaya** rin ako.","translation":"Someday, I **will be happy** too."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagkakaroon ng bingot o biyak sa itaas na labi mula kapanganakan.
original_explanation: Describes someone with a cleft lip. It's a medical term but sometimes used insensitively in the past. Best to use with caution and respect. The more formal term is 'may bingot'.
usage_notes: Maaaring ituring na hindi magalang kung gagamitin bilang panlait. Ang terminong 'bingot' ay mas ginagamit sa pormal o magalang na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang batang **ungi** ay sasailalim sa isang operasyon sa tulong ng isang charity organization.","translation":"The **harelipped** child will undergo an operation with the help of a charity organization."},{"sentence":"Ang proyektong iyon ay naglalayong tulungan ang mga batang ipinanganak na **ungi**.","translation":"That project aims to help children born with a **cleft lip**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para sa isang babae na nagpapakita ng isang partikular na istilo o 'aesthetic' na nailalarawan sa pagiging pambabae, malumanay, at pagkahilig sa mga kulay pastel at komportableng kasuotan.
etymology: Hango sa pariralang Ingles na "soft girl", isang popular na internet aesthetic.
original_explanation: The aesthetic of living in a pastel-colored dream. Think oversized sweaters, cute hair clips, journaling, drinking matcha lattes, and listening to lo-fi music. A soft girl prioritizes self-care and avoids drama. It's the opposite of the "e-girl" or "baddie" aesthetic. It's the "I just want to be happy and hydrated" vibe.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang subculture o aesthetic ng fashion at pamumuhay, lalo na sa mga platform tulad ng TikTok at Instagram.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging popular ang **soft girl** aesthetic sa mga kabataan ngayon.","translation":"The **soft girl** aesthetic has become popular among young people today."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang istilo ay very **soft girl**, mahilig siya sa mga kulay rosas at puti.","translation":"Her style is very **soft girl**, she loves the colors pink and white."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na itiniwalag, hindi na kinikilala, o tinanggihan ng kanyang pamilya, grupo, o lipunan.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'you're not my family anymore' drama. This is the plot of many teleseryes where the rich heir marries a poor but kind-hearted person against their family's wishes. They get cut off from the will, the mansion, and the family group chat. They are, quite literally, cancelled by their own bloodline.
usage_notes: Nagtataglay ng napakabigat, dramatiko, at seryosong konotasyon ng pagtanggi at pagtitiwalag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namuhay siyang mag-isa bilang isang **taong itinakwil** ng sarili niyang pamilya.","translation":"He lived alone as a **person disowned** by his own family."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang mga krimen, siya ay naging isang **taong itinakwil** ng buong komunidad.","translation":"Because of his crimes, he became an **outcast** from the entire community."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na may simbolong N at atomic number 7. Ito ay isang gas na walang kulay at amoy na bumubuo sa halos 78% ng himpapawid ng Daigdig.
original_explanation: That stuff you mostly ignored in high school chemistry class. It's the main ingredient of the air we breathe (but don't actually use). Also, it's what they put in those fancy ice cream shops to make instant, smoky desserts and what makes your bag of chips look full even when it's mostly... well, air.
usage_notes: This is a scientific term. In casual conversation, Filipinos often use the English word 'Nitrogen'. The user-provided 'Nitrohen' is a common misspelling or casual variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Nitroheno** ang pinakamaraming gas sa ating atmospera.","translation":"**Nitrogen** is the most abundant gas in our atmosphere."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **Nitroheno** sa paglago ng mga halaman.","translation":"**Nitrogen** is important for plant growth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isang opisyal na katibayan ng pagbabayad o pagtanggap ng pera.
original_explanation: The action that proves a transaction actually happened. It's what you demand from the tindera when you're buying something for the office so you can get reimbursed. "Ate, pa-resibo po!" is the battle cry of every employee on a budget. It's the ultimate "I have proof!" document.
usage_notes: Used in business, retail, and any financial transaction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng bawat tindahan na **magresibo** para sa lahat ng kanilang benta.","translation":"It is the duty of every store to **issue a receipt** for all their sales."},{"sentence":"\"Pwede po bang **magresibo** kayo para ma-reimburse ko ito?\" tanong ng customer.","translation":"\"Can you please **issue a receipt** so I can have this reimbursed?\" the customer asked."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-uunat ng mga bahagi ng katawan, lalo na ang mga braso at binti, upang maibsan ang paninigas o pagkapagod.
original_explanation: The first thing you do after waking up, or after sitting for 8 hours straight in your BPO shift. It's your body's way of saying "Thank you, next (task)!" That satisfying feeling of un-pretzeling yourself.
usage_notes: A very common, everyday action and word. Also called 'pag-uunat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang mahabang **pag-inat** ang ginawa ng pusa bago ito tuluyang bumangon.","translation":"The cat did a long **stretch** before it finally got up."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapadaan ng pagkain, inumin, o laway mula sa bibig patungo sa lalamunan at sikmura.
original_explanation: That moment you have to swallow your pride (or a really bitter pill, literally or figuratively). It's what you do after chewing your food, or when you're nervous and your throat feels dry. It's also what you do when you hear some unbelievable 'chismis' and you just have to... gulp.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for food/drink or figuratively for accepting something difficult (e.g., paglunok ng pride/dangal - swallowing one's pride).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahirapan siya sa **paglunok** dahil sa namamagang lalamunan.","translation":"He had difficulty **swallowing** because of his sore throat."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **paglunok** ng sariling dangal, pero kailangan para sa kapayapaan.","translation":"The **swallowing** of one's pride is difficult, but necessary for peace."}]

translation: to go against the grain; to be contrary
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paggawa ng isang bagay sa paraang salungat sa karaniwan, sa direksyon, o sa inaasahan; ang pagiging kontra-salunga.
original_explanation: This is the spirit of that one friend who, when everyone wants Jollibee, insists on McDo. It's cutting wood against its natural lines, which is harder and messier. In life, it's choosing the difficult path just to be different, or being the KJ (killjoy) in the group chat. 'Bakit ka ba laging suay?'
usage_notes: Less common than 'suwayin' (to disobey). 'Suayin' implies contrariness or going against a natural flow, while 'suwayin' is specifically about defying an order or rule.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap katayin ang kahoy na ito dahil kailangan mong **suayin**.","translation":"It's hard to chop this wood because you have to **go against the grain**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **suayin** sa mga plano ko, makisama ka na lang.","translation":"Don't be **contrary** to my plans, just go along with it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking pagong na karaniwang nabubuhay sa lupa.
original_explanation: This is a direct loanword from Spanish for 'tortoise'. You won't hear this at the palengke. You'll hear it in a zoo, a documentary, or from your tita who just got back from the Galápagos Islands. For everyone else, it's just a 'malaking pagong'.
usage_notes: This is a formal or technical term. 'Pagong' is the everyday word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **galapago** ay kilala sa mahabang buhay nito.","translation":"The **tortoise** is known for its long life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos sa hinaharap ng pag-alis sa isang tao o pahina mula sa listahan ng sinusubaybayan sa isang social media platform.
etymology: A Tagalog verb formation (`mag-` + duplicated first syllable for future tense) applied to the English word 'unfollow'.
original_explanation: The ultimate digital breakup move. When your friend posts too many political rants, or your ex posts a pic with their new S.O., you tell yourself, "Mag-uunfollow na talaga ako." It’s the future tense of cleansing your social media feed from bad vibes or painful memories. A modern act of self-care.
usage_notes: A Taglish verb used in the context of social media. The root 'unfollow' is an English word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung mag-post ka pa ng isang spoiler, **mag-uunfollow** na ako sa'yo!","translation":"If you post one more spoiler, I **will unfollow** you!"},{"sentence":"Sabi niya **mag-uunfollow** daw siya sa lahat ng hindi niya personal na kakilala.","translation":"He said he **will unfollow** everyone he doesn't know personally."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa pera o salapi.
etymology: Slang, possibly a syllabic reversal of 'kita' (earnings) as 'taki', which evolved into 'atik'.
original_explanation: "Atik" is old-school slang for money, like what your tito or lola might say. It's the 90s version of "kwarta" or "datung". Before G-Cash and online banking, you needed actual "atik" to buy your favorite street food. "Walang atik" means you're broke, a state many of us know too well before payday.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, colloquial settings. It is considered slang from the 1970s-90s era.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **atik** ka ba diyan? Pautang muna.","translation":"Do you have any **money** there? Can I borrow some?"},{"sentence":"Swerte, dumating na ang bonus! Dami kong **atik** ngayon!","translation":"Lucky, the bonus has arrived! I have a lot of **cash** now!"}]

translation: to send something to; to inform someone
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapadala ng isang bagay, mensahe, o impormasyon sa isang tao o lugar.
original_explanation: This means 'to send something to someone' or 'to let someone know.' It's like a verbal LBC or J&T Express. 'Paratingan mo naman ako ng balita.' (Send me some news.) or 'Paratingan mo ng pagkain si lola.' (Send some food over to grandma.) It’s the action verb for when you're not just 'parating' (coming), but you're making something 'parating' (arrive) to someone else.
usage_notes: Maaari itong tumukoy sa pisikal na pagpapadala o sa pagbibigay ng impormasyon. Ang diin ay nasa pagtiyak na makarating ang isang bagay sa destinasyon nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sige, **paratingan** ko na lang siya ng kopya ng ulat.","translation":"Okay, I'll just **send** him a copy of the report."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **paratingan** ng tulong ang mga nasalanta ng baha.","translation":"Don't forget to **send** aid to the flood victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng balat o panlabas na sapin. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang taong madaling masaktan o magdamdam.
original_explanation: Literally, something with a peel or skin, like a banana or a potato. But the real tea is when you say, 'May balat ka ba sa pwet?' It means 'Are you super sensitive?'—a classic Filipino way to call someone out for being easily offended, as if they had a secret, sensitive spot.
usage_notes: The literal meaning is straightforward. The figurative meaning, 'balat-sibuyas' (onion-skinned), is more common for 'sensitive,' but 'may balat' can carry a similar, often teasing, connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Piliin mo ang saging na **may-balat** pa at walang mantsa.","translation":"Choose the bananas that still **have skin** and no blemishes."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang biruin nang ganyan, **may-balat** 'yan.","translation":"Don't joke with him like that, he's **sensitive**."}]

translation: to cause surfeit; to be cloying
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng pakiramdam ng pagsasawa o labis na pagkabusog, lalo na sa matatamis o matatabang pagkain.
original_explanation: It's that feeling when you've eaten too much of a good thing, like the 5th slice of cake or hearing the same song on repeat for an hour. It can also apply to people—'yung sobrang sweet na jowa na nagiging 'cringey' na. Anything that's 'too much' can be nakaumay (the more common form).
usage_notes: The verb describes what causes the feeling of 'umay'. The more common form used in sentences is 'nakakaumay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **nakakaumay** ang sobrang tamis na yema cake.","translation":"A very sweet yema cake is really **cloying**."},{"sentence":"Hindi ba **nakakaumay** ang paulit-ulit na drama sa social media?","translation":"Isn't the repetitive drama on social media **tiresome/cloying**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang ornamental na may malalaki at mababangong puting bulaklak, na kilala sa siyentipikong pangalan na Crinum asiaticum.
original_explanation: This is that fancy white flower you see in gardens that looks kinda like a lily but also kinda like a spider (hence, "spider lily"). It's got a nice scent. It's the type of plant your tita who's a "plantita" would be proud to have. It's more of a garden flex than a common flower.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the Crinum asiaticum plant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakabango ng mga bulaklak ng **bakong** sa hardin tuwing umaga.","translation":"The flowers of the **Crinum lily** in the garden are so fragrant every morning."},{"sentence":"Ginamit ang dahon ng **bakong** bilang panggamot sa rayuma.","translation":"The leaf of the **spider lily** was used as a remedy for rheumatism."}]

translation: one who gives false hope; a stringer
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbibigay ng pahiwatig o pangako ng isang bagay, karaniwan sa romantikong konteksto, nang walang intensyong tuparin ito, na nagiging sanhi ng pag-asa sa wala.
original_explanation: The official villain in modern Filipino hugot culture. This is the person who's "sweet but not interested," "caring but not committed." They leave you on read but react to your stories. They give you just enough attention to keep you hoping, but never enough to make it real. Basically, a walking "seen zone." Don't be a `paasa`.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun to describe a person or an adjective to describe their actions. Strongly associated with romantic relationships and "M.U." (Mutual Understanding) situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa kanya, **paasa** lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe him, he's just a **stringer**."},{"sentence":"Napagod na akong umasa sa mga taong **paasa**.","translation":"I'm tired of hoping on people who **give false hope**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagpapadala o paghahatid ng mga bagay, sulat, o tao sa kanilang patutunguhan.
original_explanation: Think of this as the 'Send' button in real life. It's the moment your Shopee or Lazada order changes status from 'to pack' to 'to ship'. It's the official go-signal for anything that needs to move from point A to point B.
usage_notes: Commonly used in business, logistics, and military contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinihintay na lang namin ang **despatso** ng mga relief goods para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"We are just waiting for the **dispatch** of the relief goods for the typhoon victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang karaniwang tunog o huni na nililikha ng isang pusa.
original_explanation: The sound a cat makes, especially at 3 AM when it wants food, attention, or just wants to remind you who the real boss of the house is. The universal cat-call, literally.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb root (e.g., ngumingiyaw).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang malakas na **ngiyaw** ng pusa sa labas ng bintana.","translation":"I heard the loud **meow** of the cat outside the window."}]

meaning_filipino: Magiging magkakatulad sa katangian, anyo, o uri.
original_explanation: When you and your work bestie show up wearing the same Uniqlo shirt. It's that 'twinning!' moment. Also applies to exes who seem to have a 'type,' and you realize you all look like you were cast for the same role.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'magkakatulad', but 'magkakapareho' is more common in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit kaya **magkakapareho** ang sagot ninyong dalawa sa exam?","translation":"Why is it that your answers on the exam **are the same**?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong malito, hindi **magkakapareho** ang kanilang mga pangalan, magkahawig lang.","translation":"Don't get confused, their names are not **the same**, just similar."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang buo at matigas na piraso ng anumang bagay, lalo na ng lupa, asukal, o mineral.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung brown sugar na natuyo at tumigas sa lalagyan, 'yun ang bugal. O 'yung lupa na pinukpok mo para taniman ng halaman. It's a solid chunk of something, whether it's a clod of dirt, a lump of sugar, or—if you're lucky—a nugget of gold.
usage_notes: Often used for earth, sugar, salt, or even precious metals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga **bugal** ng asukal sa ilalim ng tasa ng kape ko.","translation":"There are **lumps** of sugar at the bottom of my coffee cup."},{"sentence":"Nakahanap sila ng malaking **bugal** ng ginto sa minahan.","translation":"They found a large **nugget** of gold in the mine."}]

translation: the manner or quality of repair
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o kalidad ng pagkakaayos o pagkumpuni sa isang bagay na nasira.
original_explanation: This is the "after" picture of a repair job. It's not the act of fixing (`pagkukumpuni`), but the result. "Ang ganda ng `pagkakakumpuni` ng cellphone ko, mukhang bago!" Or, "Ang pangit ng `pagkakakumpuni` ng sirang tubo, tumutulo pa rin!" It's how you judge the "galing" of the mekaniko or technician. The proof is in the `pagkakakumpuni`.
usage_notes: Used to comment on the quality of a repair.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humanga ako sa ganda ng **pagkakakumpuni** ng lumang silya.","translation":"I was amazed by the beautiful **quality of the repair** of the old chair."},{"sentence":"Nagreklamo ang customer dahil sa hindi maayos na **pagkakakumpuni** ng kanyang sasakyan.","translation":"The customer complained about the poor **manner of repair** of his car."}]

translation: for stitches to come undone; to have a seam rip open
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkalas o pagkabakbak ng sinulid na ginamit sa pagdugtong ng tela o sa pagsara ng isang sugat.
original_explanation: That awkward moment when your pants rip in the middle of a presentation. Ouch! Figuratively, it’s when someone who's supposed to be quiet suddenly spills all the tea. Parang 'konting-konti na lang, bibigay na,' tapos biglang natastasan ng tahi at sinabi lahat ng sikreto.
usage_notes: A phrasal verb. 'Tastas' means undone stitch/seam. 'Matastasan' is the potential or accidental form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **natastasan ng tahi** ang laylayan ng kanyang palda habang siya'y sumasayaw.","translation":"The hem of her skirt suddenly **had its seam rip open** while she was dancing."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng isang linggo, tila **natastasan ng tahi** ang kanyang bibig at isiniwalat ang buong plano.","translation":"After a week, it's as if his mouth's **stitches came undone** and he revealed the whole plan."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na iniaalok upang ibenta o ipagbili sa iba.
original_explanation: The magic word you see on Facebook Marketplace for pre-loved items, or on a sign outside a house. It's the official declaration that you're ready to let go of something... for the right price. "Pabenta na 'tong phone, need funds for concert tickets." It's the start of a beautiful (and sometimes frustrating) negotiation process.
usage_notes: Often used with "for" in English, e.g., "For pabenta". Can be used as a noun ("Ang pabenta ko") or an adjective ("Pabenta itong bahay").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pabenta** na raw ang lumang sasakyan ng aming kapitbahay.","translation":"Our neighbor's old car is now reportedly **for sale**."},{"sentence":"Nag-post siya sa online group ng mga gamit na **pabenta**.","translation":"She posted in an online group the items that are **for sale**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa halaga ng salapi na natitira sa sahod ng isang empleyado matapos ibawas ang mga buwis, kontribusyon, at iba pang kaltas.
original_explanation: This is the real sahod, besh. Yung nakikita mo sa payslip mo na 'Gross Pay' is just a dream. Yung **take-home** pay yung reality—yung pambayad ng bills, pang-kape, at pang-Shopee checkout. It's the 'sana all' amount that actually hits your bank account.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of salary or pay ('take-home pay'). Spelled as 'takehome' or 'take-home'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maliit lang ang **take-home** pay ko pagkatapos ng lahat ng kaltas.","translation":"My **take-home** pay is small after all the deductions."},{"sentence":"Mas mahalaga sa akin ang laki ng **take-home** kaysa sa gross salary.","translation":"The amount of **take-home** pay is more important to me than the gross salary."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng pagiging handa o preparado para sa isang gawain, pangyayari, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is your 'Laban!' mode. It's having your resume updated even when you have a job. It's having an emergency fund for 'sana-all' travel promos. It's what the NDRRMC preaches before a typhoon hits. Kahandaan is the opposite of 'bahala na si Batman.' It's being ready for anything, from a surprise quiz to a zombie apocalypse.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical, mental, or emotional preparedness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **kahandaan** ng bawat isa sa pagdating ng sakuna.","translation":"Everyone's **preparedness** is important when a disaster arrives."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **kahandaan** na harapin ang mga bagong hamon.","translation":"He showed his **readiness** to face new challenges."}]

translation: to flourish; to soar; to prevail
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-angat, pag-unlad, o pagtatagumpay nang lubos; paglipad nang mataas.
original_explanation: To be at your peak, like a K-pop group winning all the awards or your sari-sari store finally having more sales than the 7-Eleven next door. It's your 'sana all' moment, but it's actually happening to you. Your career is on fire!
usage_notes: Often used to describe success in a career, business, or field of expertise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais ng bawat artist na **mamayagpag** ang kanilang sining.","translation":"Every artist wants their art to **flourish**."},{"sentence":"Mula sa pagiging extra, siya na ngayon ang bida na **namamayagpag** sa industriya.","translation":"From being an extra, she is now the lead star who is **prevailing** in the industry."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng likas na galing o kasanayan sa sining; may kaugnayan sa sining o mga alagad ng sining.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "artistic," na hiniram naman mula sa Pranses na "artistique."
original_explanation: The vibe you're going for when you post a black-and-white photo of your coffee with a deep, unrelated caption. It's when your friend arranges their food perfectly before taking a picture for Instagram. Basically, anything done with a flair for aesthetics, whether it's genuine talent or just for the 'gram. "Ang artistik ng feed mo!"
usage_notes: A modern, colloquial borrowing from English, often used in informal conversations. The more formal Spanish-derived equivalent is "artistiko/artistika."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **artistik** ang pagkakagawa ng kanyang mga obra.","translation":"The creation of his works is truly **artistic**."},{"sentence":"May **artistik** na 'touch' ang bawat sulok ng coffee shop na iyon.","translation":"Every corner of that coffee shop has an **artistic** touch."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangyayari o bagay na naganap nang walang anumang patiunang kaalaman, hula, o paghahanda.
original_explanation: The plot twist of your life. Like a surprise quiz, a "We need to talk" message, or finding a ₱1000 bill in your old jeans. It's the universe's way of saying, "Akala mo lang 'yun!"
usage_notes: Very common phrase used to describe surprises, both good and bad. The single word "di-inaasahan" is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **hindi inaasahan** na panalo ang natanggap ng kanilang team.","translation":"Their team received an **unexpected** win."},{"sentence":"Dumating ang bonus nang **hindi inaasahan** ng mga empleyado.","translation":"The bonus arrived **unexpectedly** for the employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangyayari o isinasagawa dalawang beses sa loob ng isang taon, o bawat anim na buwan.
etymology: Isang parirala na binubuo ng 'tuwing' (bawat), 'kalahati' (kalahati), at 'taon' (taon).
original_explanation: This is the frequency of your company's performance review, that general cleaning you promise yourself you'll do, or when you finally decide to update your phone's OS. It's the official term for 'twice a year.'
usage_notes: A more formal way to say 'every six months'. Often used in business, finance, or academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagbabayad ng amilyar ay ginagawa **tuwing kalahating taon**.","translation":"The payment for real property tax is done **semi-annually**."},{"sentence":"Mayroon kaming pangkalahatang pagpupulong **tuwing kalahating taon**.","translation":"We have a general assembly **every half year**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng pisikal na puwersa o kapangyarihan upang manakit, makasira, o magdulot ng pinsala sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
original_explanation: Eto yung level-up ng away-bata. Hindi na lang 'to asaran, may kasama nang sakitan. Isipin mo 'yung eksena sa action movie na may nagwawasak ng gamit o 'yung traffic-altercation na nauwi sa suntukan. That's pure karahasan. It's the opposite of chill.
usage_notes: Often used in news reports, legal contexts, and discussions about crime and social issues.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating tuligsain ang anumang uri ng **karahasan** sa ating lipunan.","translation":"We must condemn any form of **violence** in our society."},{"sentence":"Ang pelikula ay nagpapakita ng matinding **karahasan** kaya't hindi ito angkop sa mga bata.","translation":"The movie shows extreme **violence** so it is not suitable for children."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o kumpanya na sumasang-ayon na magbigay ng mga materyales o serbisyo sa isang tiyak na presyo at takdang panahon, lalo na sa larangan ng konstruksiyon.
original_explanation: Sila yung kausap mo kapag gusto mong magpatayo ng bahay, building, o 'yung pangarap mong coffee shop. Sila ang bahala from semento to finishing touches. Minsan, sila rin yung sinisisi kapag tumutulo na yung bubong after one week.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of construction and large projects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha kami ng isang mahusay na **kontraktor** para sa pagpapatayo ng aming bahay.","translation":"We hired a good **contractor** for the construction of our house."},{"sentence":"Nag-usap na ang kliyente at ang **kontraktor** tungkol sa badyet ng proyekto.","translation":"The client and the **contractor** have already discussed the project's budget."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtatanggal ng isang bagay mula sa lalagyan o pambalot nito.
etymology: A phrase combining 'alisin' (to remove) and 'pagkakaimpake' (the state of being packed, from Spanish 'empaque').
original_explanation: The most satisfying feeling after a Shopee or Lazada 11.11 haul. This is the official term for your unboxing video. "Guys, i-alisin sa pagkakaimpake na natin ang bago kong mechanical keyboard!" It's the moment of truth where you find out if what you ordered online is legit or if you got scammed.
usage_notes: A specific phrase used for unpacking items from boxes, luggage, or packaging.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **alisin sa pagkakaimpake** ang mga gamit na ito.","translation":"Help me **unpack** these things."},{"sentence":"Sabik na siyang **alisin sa pagkakaimpake** ang kanyang regalo.","translation":"She was excited to **unbox** her gift."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang pagkain, karaniwang prutas, na iniluto at inimbak sa arnibal o asukal upang tumagal at maging panghimagas.
etymology: From 'tamis' (sweetness). The 'mi-' prefix and '-an' suffix transforms the root into a noun meaning 'something that has been made sweet'.
original_explanation: Basically, anything that's been given the sugar treatment. Think minatamis na saging, macapuno, or your titas talking about their love lives—sweet, sometimes preserved for too long, and definitely a dessert. It's the 'after-ulam' course.
usage_notes: Often refers to fruits preserved in syrup, like 'minatamis na saging' (sweetened bananas) or 'minatamis na bao' (sweetened coconut). Can be used generally for any dessert.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa panghimagas, mayroon kaming **minatamis** na saging.","translation":"For dessert, we have **sweetened** bananas."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong bumili ng isang garapong **minatamis** na macapuno.","translation":"I want to buy a jar of macapuno **preserve**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o pangyayari na lumilihis mula sa karaniwan, pamantayan, o inaasahan; di-karaniwan.
original_explanation: This is a deep cut, a word you'd use to sound 'conyo' or to describe a really weird bug in a government report. Think of it as 'weird' or 'kakaiba' with a college degree. 'May anomalo sa system, sir.' is the BPO agent's way of saying 'The computer is messing up again.'
usage_notes: Extremely rare in spoken Tagalog. The words "kakaiba," "di-karaniwan," or the English "anomalous" are far more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May natuklasang **anomalo** sa resulta ng laboratory test.","translation":"Something **anomalous** was discovered in the laboratory test results."},{"sentence":"Ang biglaang pagbabago ng panahon ay itinuturing na **anomalo**.","translation":"The sudden change in weather is considered **anomalous**."}]

translation: to announce on the radio; to radio
meaning_filipino: Ipahayag o ibalita ang isang impormasyon sa pamamagitan ng radyo.
original_explanation: Before Facebook Live and Twitter, this was the fastest way to spread news (or chismis). "Tulfo, paki-iradyo po ang nawawala kong aso!" It also means to communicate using a two-way radio, like what security guards or event organizers do. "Base, base, iradyo mo sa lahat na paubos na ang pagkain."
usage_notes: Can mean to broadcast via public radio or to communicate via a walkie-talkie.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **iradyo** ninyo na natagpuan na ang nawawalang bata.","translation":"Please, **announce on the radio** that the missing child has been found."},{"sentence":"**Iniradyo** ng pulis sa kanyang mga kasama ang lokasyon ng suspek.","translation":"The police officer **radioed** the suspect's location to his colleagues."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan kung saan ang bibig ay bukas na bukas, karaniwan dahil sa pagkagulat, pagkamangha, o pagtulog.
original_explanation: The default facial expression when you hear the latest showbiz chismis. Also the look of your officemate during a boring Zoom meeting, pretending to listen. It’s the human equivalent of a loading screen.
usage_notes: Can describe a state of surprise, sleepiness, or simply having one's mouth open.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natulog siyang **nakanganga** sa bus dahil sa pagod.","translation":"He slept **with his mouth agape** on the bus due to exhaustion."},{"sentence":"Naiwan kaming lahat na **nakanganga** sa galing ng kanyang pag-awit.","translation":"We were all left **gaping** at the excellence of her singing."}]

translation: to be arranged in layers; to be stacked
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging magkapatong-patong o pagkakaayos sa mga suson o patong.
etymology: From `magka-` (prefix indicating a state or condition) + `suson` (layer).
original_explanation: Think of a perfect sans rival cake, food containers in your ref after a fiesta, or clothes you expertly folded using the KonMari method. It's things neatly stacked on top of each other. The opposite of this is your "laundry chair" where clothes are just... a pile. `Magkasuson` is organization goals.
usage_notes: Used to describe things that are layered or stacked, like papers, clothes, or food.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magkasuson** nang maayos ang mga damit sa aparador.","translation":"I want the clothes in the closet to be **arranged in layers** neatly."},{"sentence":"Ang mga libro ay **magkasuson** sa mesa.","translation":"The books are **stacked** on the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa 'Vacation Leave,' na tumutukoy sa bayad na bakasyon mula sa trabaho na karapatan ng isang empleyado.
original_explanation: The holy grail of every BPO agent and office worker. Ito yung life force mo. Yung tinititigan mo sa portal kapag pagod ka na sa buhay. 'Boss, mag-fa-file ako ng VL sa birthday ko.' Kapag naubos na ang VL mo, aasa ka na lang sa SL (Sick Leave) kahit hindi ka naman talaga maysakit. #Diskarte
usage_notes: Pronounced as letters 'V-L'. Almost exclusively used in a corporate or office setting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gagamitin ko ang aking **VL** para sa isang linggong bakasyon sa Boracay.","translation":"I will use my **VL** for a week-long vacation in Boracay."},{"sentence":"Na-approve na ba ang **VL** na finile ko noong nakaraang linggo?","translation":"Has the **VL** I filed last week been approved?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbawas o ang halaga na ibinawas; pagliit ng bilang, sukat, o tindi.
etymology: From ka- + bawas + -an, forming a noun that signifies the result or abstraction of the root word 'bawas' (decrease).
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your payslip and there's a 'kabawasan' under 'Taxes and Deductions'. It's the opposite of 'dagdag'. Or when you thought you had a full bag of chips, but it's mostly air—that's a kabawasan of your expectations.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of finance, quantity, or intensity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **kabawasan** sa presyo ng gasolina ngayong linggo.","translation":"There's a **reduction** in the price of gasoline this week."},{"sentence":"Ang pagliban niya sa trabaho ay nagdulot ng **kabawasan** sa kanyang sahod.","translation":"His absence from work resulted in a **deduction** from his salary."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lupain o ari-arian, karaniwang nasa mga tropikal o subtropikal na rehiyon, kung saan ang mga pananim tulad ng kape, asukal, saging, o tabako ay itinatanim sa malakihang sukat.
original_explanation: Isang napakalaking farm, as in hacienda levels. Dito galing yung saging na Dole, yung pinya na Del Monte, at yung asukal na nagpapatamis sa milk tea mo. Picture a huge field of the same crop stretching as far as the eye can see.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tanyag ang Mindanao sa malalawak na **plantasyon** ng saging at pinya.","translation":"Mindanao is famous for its vast **plantations** of bananas and pineapples."},{"sentence":"Nagtrabaho ang kanyang lolo sa isang **plantasyon** ng tubo noong araw.","translation":"His grandfather used to work on a sugarcane **plantation** back in the day."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng kaukulang halaga bilang kabayaran para sa isang produkto, serbisyo, o utang sa isang tao o entidad.
original_explanation: The verb form of "sweldo day." It's what you do to your Meralco bill, your Shopee cart, or your friend you owe money to. "**Bayaran** mo na utang mo!" is a classic Filipino friendship-ender (or tester). It's the act of settling a debt, whether financial or a "debt of gratitude" (utang na loob). The focus is on WHO you are paying.
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the person or entity being paid. Contrast with 'bayarin' (to pay for something). 'Bayaran mo si Maria' (Pay Maria). 'Bayarin mo ang kuryente' (Pay for the electricity).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **bayaran** ang may-ari ng apartment bukas.","translation":"I need to **pay** the apartment owner tomorrow."},{"sentence":"**Bayaran** mo na si Aling Nena para sa kinuha mong suka.","translation":"**Pay** Aling Nena for the vinegar you got."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sasakyan na binubuo ng isang upuan o higaan na nakakabit sa dalawang poste, pinapasan sa balikat ng dalawa o higit pang tao upang dalhin ang isang pasahero.
etymology: Unknown. A historical term for a specific mode of transport.
original_explanation: The original VIP transport system, pre-Grab Premium. Imagine being carried on a chair held up by two people. It’s how royalty or the super-rich moved around in old-school teleseryes. Today, the closest thing we have is when your friends carry you home after you've had too much to drink.
usage_notes: A historical or literary term. It refers to the vehicle itself. The act of being carried this way is also sometimes described with this word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinakay sa isang **balangkat** ang maysakit na prinsesa.","translation":"The sick princess was put on a **palanquin**."},{"sentence":"Ang datu ay marangyang dinala sa kanyang **balangkat**.","translation":"The chieftain was luxuriously carried in his **litter**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsisimula ng isang gawain, kaganapan, o proseso sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of "Let's get this bread!" It's what you say before starting a new Netflix series, a new workout plan, or a new job. `Mag-uumpisa` is the promise of a beginning. It’s the Monday morning mood, the New Year's resolution vibe, the "Okay, game!" before you dive into something.
usage_notes: This is the future tense form of `mag-umpisa`. The first syllable of the root word is repeated to indicate future tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas na ako **mag-uumpisa** sa aking diet.","translation":"I **will start** my diet tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Alas-otso ng umaga **mag-uumpisa** ang programa.","translation":"The program **will begin** at eight in the morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na masigasig na nangongolekta, nakikipagkalakalan, o humahanga sa mga sapatos na pang-sports, lalo na ang mga bihirang mahanap o may limitadong edisyon.
original_explanation: Yung kaibigan mong mas inaalagaan pa ang sapatos niya kaysa sa jowa niya. May sariling toothbrush at special cleaner para sa sapatos, at handang pumila ng magdamag para sa bagong 'release'. Para sa kanila, hindi ito sapatos lang, ito ay 'investment'.
usage_notes: A modern term referring to a specific subculture of shoe collectors.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **sneakerhead**, mayroon siyang higit sa 50 pares ng sapatos.","translation":"As a **sneakerhead**, he has over 50 pairs of shoes."},{"sentence":"Pangarap ng bawat **sneakerhead** na magkaroon ng orihinal na Air Jordans.","translation":"It is every **sneakerhead's** dream to own an original pair of Air Jordans."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng serbisyo, tulong, o pag-aalaga sa isang tao, pangkat, o institusyon.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "service with a smile." It's what Jollibee crew members do, what nurses do for their patients, and what politicians promise to do for the country (emphasis on *promise*). It's the command form, like "Serve the people!" or your boss telling you, "Paglingkuran mo nang maayos ang kliyente."
usage_notes: A verb in the object-focus, imperative/infinitive form. It means "to serve [object]".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang karangalan na **paglingkuran** ang ating bayan.","translation":"It is an honor **to serve** our country."},{"sentence":"**Paglingkuran** mo ang mga panauhin natin nang may ngiti.","translation":"**Serve** our guests with a smile."}]

translation: to act as a sponsor or escort (in a wedding/baptism)
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-akto bilang isang abay o kasama sa isang seremonya, tulad ng kasal o binyag, na nagbibigay ng suporta at tulong.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of being an "abay" (groomsman/bridesmaid). When your friend asks you to **mag-abay** in their wedding, it's an honor, but also a responsibility. It means you're officially part of the entourage, the pre-nup photoshoot, and the group chat where you plan the bridal shower. It's less about escorting and more about making sure the bride doesn't have a panic attack.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of weddings, baptisms, and other formal ceremonies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napili siyang **mag-abay** sa kasal ng kanyang matalik na kaibigan.","translation":"She was chosen to **be a bridesmaid** at her best friend's wedding."},{"sentence":"Sino ang gusto mong **mag-abay** sa binyag ng anak mo?","translation":"Who do you want to **be a sponsor** at your child's baptism?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manipis at malutong na tinapay, karaniwang kinakain bilang meryenda o isinasawsaw sa kape.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino cracker, often found in giant tin cans that, once empty, are automatically promoted to become your family's official sewing kit, first-aid kit, or rice storage. Perfect for dunking in hot coffee until it reaches that critical, almost-disintegrating state.
usage_notes: Most commonly refers to the plain, unsalted square crackers like 'galletas de patatas' or 'galletas de manteca'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isawsaw mo ang **galyetas** sa mainit na kape.","translation":"Dip the **crackers** in the hot coffee."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **galyetas** ang lata na bigay ni Lola.","translation":"The can Grandma gave is full of **biscuits**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pabilog na bagay na umiikot sa isang ehe, na nagpapahintulot sa madaling paggalaw ng isang sasakyan o makina.
original_explanation: 'Yung bagay na flat kapag minamalas ka sa daan. 'Yung umiikot sa "Gulong ng Palad." Life is like this: minsan nasa ibabaw, minsan nasa ilalim. Lalo na sa biyahe, 'pag na-flat ka, nasa ilalim ka talaga.
usage_notes: Can refer to the entire wheel assembly or just the rubber tire. The phrase "Gulong ng Palad" (Wheel of Fortune) is a very common idiom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumabog ang **gulong** ng aming sasakyan sa gitna ng NLEX.","translation":"Our car's **tire** blew out in the middle of NLEX."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay ay parang **gulong** ng palad.","translation":"Life is like a wheel of fortune."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagdiriwang para sa isang babaeng malapit nang ikasal, bilang pamamaalam sa kaniyang pagiging dalaga.
etymology: From Spanish 'despedida de soltera' (farewell to singlehood for a female).
original_explanation: The 'last hurrah' before she officially becomes a Mrs. It's the Filipina version of a bachelorette party, which can range from a wholesome, tita-approved bridal shower with games and gifts, to a wild girls' night out. The male equivalent is a 'despedida de soltero'.
usage_notes: The phrase is often used in full. The male version is 'despedida de soltero'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inorganisa ng kanyang mga kaibigan ang isang masayang **despedida de soltera** para sa kanya.","translation":"Her friends organized a fun **bachelorette party** for her."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagawa o dinadala sa paraan ng paghila.
original_explanation: Think of a car being towed, a kid pulling a toy wagon, or you dragging your luggage through the airport. The object is in a state of *pahila*. It's not moving on its own; it's being dragged along, sometimes willingly, sometimes not—just like you getting pulled into another 'one last drink' by your friends.
usage_notes: Describes the manner in which something is moved. Can also be a command: 'Pahila naman ng upuan,' meaning 'Please pull the chair for me.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ang sirang sasakyan sa talyer nang **pahila**.","translation":"The broken car was brought to the workshop by being **towed**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ay masayang naglalaro ng kanilang kalesa na **pahila**.","translation":"The children were happily playing with their **pulled** wagon."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na hindi marunong tumanaw o magpasalamat sa tulong o kabutihang ipinagkaloob sa kanya.
original_explanation: This is a cardinal sin in Filipino culture. It's the person you helped get a job who then backstabs you. It's the relative you let stay in your house who then complains about the food. It's not just being unthankful; it's a deep-seated lack of gratitude that severs the 'loob' (inner self) connection. The ultimate 'wala ka man lang hiya' moment.
usage_notes: A very serious accusation in Filipino culture, as 'utang na loob' is a core value.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos ang lahat ng tulong ko sa kanya, nagawa pa niya akong siraan. Tunay siyang **walang-utang-na-loob**.","translation":"After all my help, he still managed to badmouth me. He is truly **ungrateful**."},{"sentence":"Ang taong **walang-utang-na-loob** ay parang lata na walang laman.","translation":"An **ungrateful** person is like an empty can."}]

translation: close to each other; near each other
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay o tao na may maliit na distansya sa pagitan; malapit sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: 'Yung mga bahay sa subdivision na halos walang bakod, magkakalapit. O 'yung mga pwesto sa food court 'pag lunch break, siksikan at magkakalapit. It can also mean emotionally close, like you and your bestie who are inseparable.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical proximity or emotional closeness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkakalapit** ang aming mga bahay kaya madalas kaming magkita.","translation":"Our houses are **close to each other** so we see each other often."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pandemya, naging mas **magkakalapit** ang loob ng aming pamilya.","translation":"Because of the pandemic, our family became emotionally **closer**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging kakatwa, di-pangkaraniwan, o kakaiba sa isang paraan na nakakagulat o nakakatawa.
original_explanation: This is the quality of being "weird" or "quirky." It's your friend's `pagka-kakatwa` of collecting bottle caps. It's the strange plot twist in a movie that makes you go, "Huh?" It’s that one dish on the menu that seems out of place, like sinigang-flavored ice cream. It's the essence of things that make you tilt your head and say, "Ang weird!"
usage_notes: Often used to describe a characteristic or a state of being strange. The hyphen is sometimes used for clarity but `pagkakakatwa` is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagka-kakatwa** ng kanyang mga kilos ay nakakuha ng atensyon ng lahat.","translation":"The **strangeness** of his actions got everyone's attention."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng kanyang **pagka-kakatwa**, marami pa ring nagmamahal sa kanya.","translation":"Despite his **peculiarity**, many still love him."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babae na madaling makaramdam o nagpapakita ng selos.
original_explanation: The girlfriend who audits your 'Following' list on Instagram. She needs hourly updates and will side-eye any girl who gives you a friendly 'hi.' In teleseryes, she's the one who throws water at the kontrabida. But sometimes, she's just a girl who loves fiercely and is scared to lose you. It's a fine line.
usage_notes: The feminine form of the adjective. Use 'seloso' for males.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang makipag-usap ka sa ibang babae dahil **selosa** siya.","translation":"She doesn't want you talking to other women because she is **jealous**."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang **selosa** na asawa.","translation":"She is known as a **jealous** wife."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkaskas ng isang bagay sa isang magaspang na ibabaw upang ito ay mapino o matanggalan ng balat.
original_explanation: This is the OG food processing bago pa nauso ang food processor. Ito 'yung ginagawa sa niyog para makuha 'yung gata, o sa keso para sa spaghetti. The sound and motion of scraping something to get its delicious essence.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a culinary context, especially for grating coconut or cheese using a 'kudkuran' (grater).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magkudkod** ng niyog para sa gagawin nating biko.","translation":"Help me **grate** coconut for the biko we're going to make."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang spaghetti kapag maraming kinudkod na keso sa ibabaw.","translation":"Spaghetti is more delicious with a lot of grated cheese on top."}]

meaning_filipino: Pag-inat o pagbanat ng balat, lalo na sa mga bahagi ng katawan na nagkaroon ng sugat o pamamaga; peklat na dulot ng pag-unat.
original_explanation: Think of a scar that got stretched out, or when skin is pulled taut, like when you make a 'pacute' face by pulling the corners of your eyes. It can also refer to stretch marks, the 'tiger stripes' some people get. It's about skin being pulled or stretched to its limit.
usage_notes: Not a very common word. Can be confused with 'pilat' (scar). Hilat specifically refers to the stretching aspect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iwan ng **hilat** sa kanyang balat ang malaking sugat na gumaling.","translation":"The large wound that healed left a **stretched scar** on his skin."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa mabilis na pagdagdag ng timbang, nagkaroon siya ng mga **hilat** sa tiyan.","translation":"Due to rapid weight gain, she got **stretch marks** on her stomach."}]

translation: to cause doubt; to make someone doubt
meaning_filipino: Magdulot o magbigay ng dahilan upang ang isang tao ay mag-alinlangan o magkaroon ng duda.
original_explanation: This is what your friend does when you're about to make a good decision, and they say, 'Sure ka na ba diyan?' Suddenly, you're questioning your whole life. It's planting a seed of doubt. Also what happens when your partner starts acting shady with their phone.
usage_notes: A causative verb. It doesn't mean 'to doubt' ('magduda'), but 'to cause someone else to doubt'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pabago-bago niyang pahayag ay nag-**paduda** sa mga imbestigador.","translation":"His inconsistent statements **made** the investigators **doubt**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-**paduda** sa kakayahan mo.","translation":"Don't **cause** yourself **to doubt** your own abilities."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malambing at impormal na tawag sa isang matalik na kaibigan.
etymology: Isang malambing na baryasyon ng "bes," na nagmula sa "best friend."
original_explanation: Ito 'yung cutesy version ng 'bes'. Parang 'bes' with feelings. Ito 'yung tawag mo sa kaibigan mong sinasamahan ka sa lahat ng kalokohan mo, mula pag-order ng milk tea hanggang sa pag-stalk sa crush niyo.
usage_notes: Mas malambing at personal kaysa sa "bes". Madalas na baybayin din bilang "beshy."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, **beshie**, mag-shopping tayo!","translation":"Let's go, **bestie**, let's go shopping!"},{"sentence":"Salamat sa pakikinig, **beshie**. You're the best!","translation":"Thanks for listening, **bestie**. You're the best!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pag-aayos na maihatid ang isang bagay, sulat, o pera sa isang tiyak na lugar o tao.
etymology: From the causative prefix `ipa-` and the root word `dala` (to carry, bring).
original_explanation: The lifeblood of OFWs, LDR couples, and every Filipino who has ever checked out their Shopee cart. It's the verb for sending money, a balikbayan box, a J&T package, or even a GCash transfer. The question "Na-receive mo na?" is the natural follow-up to every "Pinadala ko na."
usage_notes: An extremely common verb related to mail, packages, remittances, and all forms of delivery services.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipadala** mo na lang sa LBC ang mga dokumento.","translation":"Just **send** the documents via LBC."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **ipadala** ang allowance ko ngayong linggo.","translation":"Don't forget to **send** my allowance this week."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahan, lakas, o pondo upang isagawa, harapin, o tustusan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The ultimate question before you 'add to cart' or accept a new project: 'Makakaya ko ba 'to?' It covers everything from physical strength (Can I lift this?), financial capacity (Can I afford this?), to emotional fortitude (Can I handle this drama?). It's the cornerstone of Filipino self-assessment. 'Kaya mo yan!' is its motivational cousin.
usage_notes: A very common verb of ability. 'Makakaya' is the future tense/infinitive. 'Nakaya' is past tense. 'Kinakaya' is present tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **makakaya** mo ang lahat ng pagsubok na ito.","translation":"Don't worry, you will be **able to handle** all these challenges."},{"sentence":"Sana **makaya** ng budget natin ang pagbili ng bagong ref.","translation":"I hope our budget will be **able to afford** buying a new fridge."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang pagdulas sa isang madulas na ibabaw.
original_explanation: That heart-stopping moment when you're walking on a newly-mopped floor and your feet decide to do their own dance routine. That's mapadupilas. It’s the "Oops, I almost died" slip. The reason for all those "Wet Floor" signs.
usage_notes: "Dupilas" is more specific to slipping on a surface than the more general "dulas". The "mapa-" prefix emphasizes the accidental nature of the event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo ang dinadaanan mo at baka ka **mapadupilas** sa balat ng saging.","translation":"Watch where you're going or you might **slip** on a banana peel."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin ang isang partikular na dami o bagay mula sa isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: If 'bawahan' is about giving a discount *to a person* or *from a price*, 'bawasin' is about removing the actual *thing* or *amount*. Example: You have 10 pieces of pandesal. "Bawasin mo ng tatlo" means to *take away three pieces*. In hugot terms, "Sana feelings ko na lang for you ang binabawas mo, hindi ang budget ko."
usage_notes: Ang 'bawasin' (object-focus) ay nakatuon sa bagay na tinatanggal, habang ang 'bawahan' (locative-focus) ay nakatuon sa kabuuan kung saan may tinatanggal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi ni nanay, **bawasin** ko raw ang kanin sa plato ko.","translation":"Mom said I should **reduce** the rice on my plate."},{"sentence":"Kung sampu at **babawasin** mo ang apat, anim ang matitira.","translation":"If you have ten and you **subtract** four, six will remain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang-ugat na may mahaba at matigas na balat at maputing laman, kilala rin bilang kasaba o balinghoy.
etymology: A compound word from 'kamote' (sweet potato) and 'kahoy' (wood).
original_explanation: This is kamote's cousin, but starchier and needs more prep. You can't just eat it raw, bes, it's poisonous! But when cooked, it becomes the star of cassava cake, pichi-pichi, and sometimes, a substitute for rice during hard times. It's the 'kahoy' (wood) version of kamote because it's tougher and woodier.
usage_notes: Also known as 'kasaba' or 'balinghoy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang kakanin ay ang cassava cake na gawa sa **kamoteng-kahoy**.","translation":"Her favorite delicacy is the cassava cake made from **cassava**."},{"sentence":"Mahirap balatan ang **kamoteng-kahoy** dahil sa makapal nitong balat.","translation":"It's difficult to peel **cassava** because of its thick skin."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kilos ng pagpunta sa kabilang panig ng isang daan, ilog, o anumang hadlang.
original_explanation: That moment of pure faith when you raise your hand sa gitna ng EDSA, hoping a bus will stop for you. You're 'patawid', not just across the street, but also crossing over to a new level of commuter-warrior status. Also, the proper way to use a pedestrian lane, which many people think is just street art.
usage_notes: Used to indicate the action or intention of crossing. Often seen on signs like 'Bawal Tumawid, Nakamamatay' (No Crossing, It's Deadly).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat na tumingin sa kaliwa't kanan ang mga bata bago **patawid** ng kalsada.","translation":"The children carefully looked left and right before **crossing** the road."},{"sentence":"May **patawid** na matanda, kaya't huminto ang mga sasakyan.","translation":"An old person was **crossing**, so the vehicles stopped."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang pangunahing ikinabubuhay ay ang pagtatanim at pag-aani ng mga produkto mula sa lupa.
etymology: From `mag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `sa-` + `saka` (to farm, farming). The `magsa-` prefix denotes a profession.
original_explanation: The OG food vlogger and provider. They're the reason you have rice for your unli-rice cravings and vegetables for your 'healthy-living' phase. The backbone of the nation who works harder than your laptop's fan during a deadline.
usage_notes: Refers to a person whose occupation is farming.
