usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **magsasaka** ang nagtatrabaho sa ilalim ng sikat ng araw upang may makain tayo.","translation":"The **farmers** work under the heat of the sun so that we have something to eat."},{"sentence":"Maraming programa ang gobyerno para tulungan ang ating mga **magsasaka**.","translation":"The government has many programs to help our **farmers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alagad ng batas na miyembro ng isang organisasyon na may tungkuling panatilihin ang kapayapaan at kaayusan, ipatupad ang batas, at mag-imbestiga ng krimen.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung mga "mam/sir" na humuhuli sa mga pasaway sa kalsada, rumeresponde sa 911, at 'pag may away sa kapitbahay, sila ang tinatawag. They can be your hero or the reason for your traffic violation ticket. Also, the subject of many "Huli ka!" memes.
usage_notes: This refers to an individual police officer. The organization is 'pulisya' or 'kapulisan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumawag ka ng **pulis** dahil may nag-aaway sa labas.","translation":"Call a **police officer** because there's a fight outside."},{"sentence":"Ang isang matapat na **pulis** ay nagsisilbi sa bayan.","translation":"An honest **police officer** serves the country."}]

translation: to menstruate; to have a period
meaning_filipino: Ang buwanang pagdanas ng pagdurugo mula sa matris ng isang babae; pagkakaroon ng buwanang dalaw.
original_explanation: That time of the month. The reason for sudden cravings, mood swings, and the unexplainable urge to cry while watching a detergent commercial. The monthly visitor that no one invited but shows up anyway. "Friend, may extra napkin ka? Nagkaregla ako bigla."
usage_notes: A common and direct term. Synonyms like 'magkaroon' or 'dalawin' are also frequently used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Normal sa isang babae na **magkaregla** buwan-buwan.","translation":"It's normal for a woman to **menstruate** every month."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magkaregla** si Maria noong siya ay labindalawang taong gulang.","translation":"Maria started to **have her period** when she was twelve years old."}]

translation: to be obliged; to be forced
meaning_filipino: Ang mapilitan o matukoy na gawin ang isang bagay dahil sa isang tungkulin, batas, pangako, o pangangailangan.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na kailangan mong sumama sa family reunion kahit may lakad kayo ng friends mo. No choice ka, bes, maobliga ka ng magulang mo. Para kang na-force-leave sa trabaho, pero sa social life.
usage_notes: Often used when someone feels compelled to do something due to social pressure, debt of gratitude (utang na loob), or a formal requirement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naobliga** akong magbayad para sa lahat dahil naiwan nila ang kanilang mga wallet.","translation":"I was **obliged** to pay for everyone because they left their wallets."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maobliga** na sumagot kung hindi ka komportable.","translation":"Don't feel **forced** to answer if you're not comfortable."}]

translation: to forge, to craft, to shape
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghubog sa isang bagay, lalo na ang metal, sa pamamagitan ng init at puwersa. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay ang paglinang o pagbuo ng isang konsepto, plano, o karakter.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what a blacksmith does: heat metal and hammer it into shape. Figuratively, it's what you do to your career, your character, or your 'hugot' post. You're 'pinapanday' your future when you're grinding in your BPO job. Your parents 'pinanday' your values. It's the process of shaping something raw into something refined, often through a lot of heat and pressure.
usage_notes: Has both a literal meaning (metalworking) and a very common figurative meaning (to shape or develop something abstract).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **pandayin** ang bakal habang mainit pa.","translation":"We need **to forge** the iron while it is still hot."},{"sentence":"Sa mga pagsubok sa buhay **pinapanday** ang isang matatag na pagkatao.","translation":"A strong character is **forged** through life's challenges."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at malambing na anyo ng salitang 'ate', na ginagamit bilang tawag sa mas nakatatandang kapatid na babae o bilang magiliw na pantukoy sa isang babae.
etymology: Isang diminutive o malambing na baryasyon ng "ate".
original_explanation: This is the cuter, more casual version of "Ate." It's what you call your older sister when you're about to ask for a favor ("Ateng, pautang..."). It can also be used in a slightly playful or even gossipy tone, like what your tita might say: "Nakita mo ba si Ateng, ang ganda ng bag!" It has a certain "palengke chic" or friendly neighborhood chismosa vibe.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga impormal na pag-uusap. Maaari ring gamitin sa bahagyang mapanukso o theatrical na paraan, lalo na sa gay lingo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ateng**, ang taray ng outfit mo ngayon!","translation":"**Sis**, your outfit is fierce today!"},{"sentence":"Hoy **ateng**, bilisan mo diyan!","translation":"Hey **sis**, hurry up over there!"}]

translation: to rummage through; to search thoroughly
meaning_filipino: Ang paghahanap o paghalungkat nang masinsinan sa isang lugar o mga gamit, na kadalasan ay walang paalam at nag-iiwan ng kalat.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'halikwat'. It's what your nanay does to your bag when she's looking for 'evidence' you're not studying. "**Hinalikwat** niya ang buong aparador ko!" (She rummaged through my entire closet!). It implies a very thorough, no-stone-left-unturned kind of search.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. Implies a more intense and sometimes invasive search than "hanapin" (to look for).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **halikwatin** ang mga gamit ko nang walang pahintulot.","translation":"Don't **rummage through** my things without permission."},{"sentence":"**Hinalikwat** ng magnanakaw ang buong bahay para sa mga mahahalagang bagay.","translation":"The thief **searched thoroughly** through the whole house for valuables."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi napapalamutian; simple at walang anumang pampaganda o dekorasyon.
original_explanation: This is the "minimalist aesthetic" before it was cool. It's your condo unit before the interior designer (or your tita with a plant obsession) arrives. It's a cake with no icing, a Christmas tree with no balls. Just the plain, unvarnished truth.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na simple, hubad, o walang palamuti.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto niya ang damit na **walang-adorno**.","translation":"She prefers a dress that is **unadorned**."},{"sentence":"Ang pader ng kanyang kwarto ay **walang-adorno** at puti lamang.","translation":"The wall of his room is **plain** and just white."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o sitwasyon na nagdudulot ng matinding hirap, sakit, o pagdurusa sa pisikal o emosyonal na aspeto.
original_explanation: Ito yung ex mong hindi ka pa rin tinitigilan, yung utang na hindi mo mabayaran, o yung internet na laging nawawala sa gitna ng online meeting. Basically, anything or anyone that gives you a major headache and makes you say "Lord, why me?". Isang dalahin na nagpapabigat sa buhay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaking **pasakit** sa pamilya ang kanyang pagkakasakit.","translation":"His illness is a great **burden** to the family."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang dumagdag sa **pasakit** ng ulo ko.","translation":"Don't add to my **headaches** (sufferings)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa kapatid, na nabuo sa pamamagitan ng pagbabaligtad ng mga pantig ng salitang 'kapatid'.
etymology: From Tagalog "kapatid" through syllable reversal/play, common in Swardspeak (Beki).
original_explanation: A classic example of Filipino gay lingo or Beki language that has gone mainstream. It's from 'kapatid' -> 'patid-ka' -> reversed -> 'adika-patid' -> simplified to 'adelpa'. It's what you call your kapatid when you want to sound more chic or when you're asking for a favor. "Adelpa, pahiram pera!"
usage_notes: Slang, informal. Popularized by Beki/gay lingo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Adelpa** ko ang kasama ko sa panonood ng sine.","translation":"My **sibling** was with me watching the movie."},{"sentence":"Hoy, **adelpa**, tulungan mo naman ako dito.","translation":"Hey, **sibling**, help me out here."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong propesyonal na nagdidisenyo ng mga bagay tulad ng damit, gusali, o grapiko. Bilang pang-uri, tumutukoy sa isang bagay na gawa ng isang kilalang taga-disenyo.
original_explanation: 'Yung tito/tita mo na laging may 'LV' or 'Gucci' na gamit, whether orig or from Greenhills. Or 'yung kaibigan mong graphic artist na ang trabaho ay gumawa ng 'logo' at 'pubmat'. As a noun, it's a job title. As an adjective, it's a status symbol. 'Wow, designer bag!'
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pangngalan para sa tao at pang-uri para sa produkto. Ang pagbigkas ay hango sa Ingles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang sikat na **designer** ang gumawa ng kanyang wedding gown.","translation":"A famous **designer** made her wedding gown."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang bumili ng mga **designer** na sapatos.","translation":"She loves buying **designer** shoes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng aklatan kung saan maaaring hiramin ng mga miyembro ang mga aklat at iba pang materyales upang iuwi sa loob ng takdang panahon.
etymology: A phrase composed of 'aklatan' (library) and 'nagpapahiram' (one that lends).
original_explanation: This is the 'try before you buy' of the book world. You get to take the books home, promise to return them on time, and then completely forget until you get an overdue notice. It's like borrowing a friend's charger, but with more intellectual guilt.
usage_notes: More specific than just 'aklatan'. Often used in formal contexts to distinguish it from a reference-only library.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas ang **aklatang nagpapahiram** hanggang alas-singko ng hapon.","translation":"The **lending library** is open until five in the afternoon."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng library card para makahiram sa **aklatang nagpapahiram**.","translation":"You need a library card to borrow from the **lending library**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paulit-ulit na pagpalo o pananakit sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: It's more than just a punch. This is a full-on, no-holds-barred beatdown. Think action movie fight scenes or what happens to your laundry when you use the *palo-palo*. It implies a severe, repeated physical assault. On a lighter note, your wallet feels this after a major shopping spree.
usage_notes: A very strong word indicating violence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinumbong niya sa pulis ang **pagbugbog** na ginawa sa kanya.","translation":"He/She reported the **mauling** done to him/her to the police."},{"sentence":"Ang maling **pagbugbog** sa karne ay maaaring magpatigas dito.","translation":"The wrong **way of beating/tenderizing** the meat can make it tough."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela, karaniwang luma o retaso, na ginagamit sa paglilinis, pagpupunas, o pagpapatuyo ng mga bagay.
original_explanation: Your Tita's ultimate weapon against alikabok (dust). Before microfiber cloths went viral, the humble **trapo**—often a recycled daster or an old sando—was the OG cleaning tool. It's the reason your lola's house is sparkling clean. Don't you dare use the one for the table on the floor!
usage_notes: While it literally means rag, its homonym related to politics is more widely discussed in modern conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha ng **trapo** at punasan mo ang natapong kape sa mesa.","translation":"Please get a **rag** and wipe the spilled coffee on the table."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niyang pansahod ng tumutulong gripo ang isang lumang **trapo**.","translation":"He used an old **rag** to catch the drips from the leaking faucet."}]

translation: tamales (a type of Filipino rice cake)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kakanin na gawa sa giniling na bigas o galapong, gata ng niyog, at iba't ibang sahog tulad ng manok o baboy, na binabalot sa dahon ng saging at pinapasingawan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na *tamales*, pangmaramihang anyo ng *tamal*, mula sa Nahuatl na *tamalli*.
original_explanation: Not to be confused with its Mexican cousin! The Pinoy tamales is a savory rice cake, usually from Pampanga or Zamboanga. It's like a complete ulam-at-kanin combo wrapped in a banana leaf. Perfect for merienda, but definitely a project to make from scratch.
usage_notes: Madalas na iniuugnay sa lutuing Kapampangan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang **tamales** na tinda sa palengke ng Pampanga.","translation":"The **tamales** sold at the Pampanga market are delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o katangian ng pagiging magkakatulad o walang pagkakaiba sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: This is the squad goal for your barkada's OOTD (Outfit of the Day). It's also what your parents want to see in your grades—consistent 90s, no dips! It's the opposite of "sana all" because, in this case, "lahat meron." The state of being the same.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakapare-pareho** ng kanilang kasuotan ay nagpapakita ng kanilang pagkakaisa.","translation":"The **sameness** of their attire shows their unity."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagkakapare-pareho** sa pagpapatupad ng batas para sa lahat.","translation":"**Uniformity** in implementing the law for everyone is important."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o palitang pag-uusap ng dalawa o higit pang tao tungkol sa mga tsismis.
etymology: From Spanish 'chismes' (gossips). The '-an' suffix indicates a reciprocal or collective action.
original_explanation: This is the group chat version of gossiping. It's a collaborative effort, a symposium of tea-spilling. It's not just one person talking; it's a back-and-forth, a give-and-take of juicy details. This is what happens when the 'Marites' squad assembles. 'Nagkita-kita ang magkakapitbahay para magtsismisan sa may tindahan.'
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix makes the action reciprocal or social. It's something people do *together*.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing umaga, nagkakatipon ang mga ale sa palengke para **magtsismisan**.","translation":"Every morning, the ladies gather at the market to **gossip with each other**."},{"sentence":"Nahuli sila ng kanilang boss na **nagtsitsismisan** sa pantry.","translation":"Their boss caught them **gossiping with each other** in the pantry."}]

translation: to slice from; to cut a piece from something
meaning_filipino: Ang pagputol o pagkuha ng isang bahagi mula sa isang mas malaking kabuuan.
original_explanation: The action you do when someone says "Pahingi!" (Can I have some?). You hiwaan them a piece of your cake, lechon, or whatever you're eating. It's the verb form of sharing via slicing.
usage_notes: This is a verb with focus on the object from which a slice is taken. E.g., "Hiwaan mo ang keyk" (Slice a piece from the cake).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hiwaan** mo naman ako ng mangga, pakiusap.","translation":"Please **slice** me some mango."},{"sentence":"Sino ang nag-utos na **hiwaan** ang lechon kahit hindi pa oras?","translation":"Who ordered to **cut a piece from** the roasted pig when it wasn't time yet?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling paraan ng pagsasabi ng "sige," na nangangahulugang pagpayag, pagsang-ayon, o pag-uudyok na magpatuloy.
original_explanation: The ultimate low-effort 'yes'. It's the text-speak version of 'sige'. You use it when you're too lazy to type the extra three letters. 'Tara, kape?' '**Ge**.' It's efficient, it's cool, and it means 'I'm in'. But be careful, a dry '**ge**' can also mean 'I'm not really interested but fine, whatever.' It's all about the context (and the lack of emojis).
usage_notes: Exclusively used in informal, digital communication like texting and chatting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahiram ng ballpen mo. \"**Ge**.\"","translation":"Can I borrow your pen? \"**Sure**.\""},{"sentence":"Mauna na ako, ha? \"**Ge**, ingat.\"","translation":"I'll go ahead, okay? \"**Okay**, take care.\""}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon ng mga tao, karaniwang mga kaibigan o pamilya, upang kumain, magkuwentuhan, at magkasiyahan nang magkakasama.
etymology: Reduplication of salo (to partake, to share a meal).
original_explanation: The Pinoy potluck! It's that gathering where your tita asks if you have a boyfriend, your tito offers you a drink, the cousins are on their phones, and there's a mountain of food (with at least one spaghetti dish and a Tupperware of lumpia). It’s less about the occasion and more about the "sama-sama" part.
usage_notes: Implies sharing of food.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon kami ng munting **salu-salo** para sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"We had a small **get-together** for her birthday."},{"sentence":"Dala ka ng pagkain sa **salu-salo** natin sa Sabado.","translation":"Bring some food to our **potluck party** on Saturday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ilegal na nangangalakal o nagbebenta, lalo na ng mga ipinagbabawal na bagay tulad ng droga.
original_explanation: The villain in every Filipino action movie and news report. This isn't the person directing traffic; this is the person illegally moving contraband. A word that immediately brings to mind police raids and serious headlines. Definitely not someone you want to be associated with.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with illegal drug trade, but can also refer to traffickers of other illegal goods or even people (human trafficker).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng mga pulis ang isang kilalang **trapikante** ng droga.","translation":"The police captured a known drug **trafficker**."},{"sentence":"Ang operasyon ay laban sa mga **trapikante** ng ipinagbabawal na gamot.","translation":"The operation was against the **traffickers** of illegal drugs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, lalo na isang bata, na namatayan ng isa o parehong magulang. Bilang pang-uri, tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging walang magulang.
original_explanation: The OG 'alone in this world' character. Before all the hugot about being single, there was the classic teleserye trope of the 'ulila' who either gets adopted by a rich family or has to sell sampaguita in the streets. It's the ultimate 'kawawa naman' backstory.
usage_notes: Can function as both a noun ('Ang ulila') and an adjective ('Ang batang ulila').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **ulila** ang natulungan ng ampunan.","translation":"The orphanage helped many **orphans**."},{"sentence":"Siya ay isang batang **ulila** na lumaki sa kanyang mga tiyahin.","translation":"She is an **orphaned** child who grew up with her aunts."}]

meaning_filipino: (Di-pormal na baybay ng 'buwisit') Isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari na nagdudulot ng matinding inis, pagkabigo, o kamalasan.
etymology: From Hokkien 無衣食 (*bô-i-sít*), meaning 'without clothes and food' or 'unlucky'. Informal spelling of 'buwisit'.
original_explanation: The modern, text-friendly, and more common way to spell 'buwisit'. It's that person, thing, or situation that makes your blood boil. The Wi-Fi that disconnects during a ranked game, the client who keeps asking for 'minor revisions' that are actually a full rework, the 'seen' message with no reply. That's a bwiset.
usage_notes: Extremely common informal term. 'Buwisit' is the more formal, dictionary spelling, but 'bwiset' is king in chats, social media, and everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong kausapin, **bwiset** ka!","translation":"Don't talk to me, you're a **pest**!"},{"sentence":"Ang laking **bwiset** naman ng brownout na ito.","translation":"This power outage is such a huge **annoyance**."}]

translation: to form a clique; to join a group
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsama o pagbuo ng isang grupo ng magkakaibigan o 'barkada'.
etymology: From Spanish 'barcada' (boatload), which evolved to mean a group of friends.
original_explanation: The high school verb for finding your tribe. It's the act of officially leveling up from 'classmate' to 'ka-barkada,' which means you now have a designated group to eat lunch with and to copy homework from. It's forming your own Avengers-level squad.
usage_notes: Implies a sense of belonging and camaraderie.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis siyang **bumarkada** sa mga bago niyang katrabaho.","translation":"He quickly **joined the group** of his new coworkers."},{"sentence":"Noong college, mas pinili kong hindi **bumarkada** at mag-focus sa pag-aaral.","translation":"In college, I chose not **to join a clique** and to focus on my studies."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking isda sa dagat na may katangi-tanging mahaba at patag na nguso na kahawig ng isang espada.
original_explanation: The Zorro of the sea. It's a fish that looks like it's always ready for a duel. You see it grilled on sticks at fancy beach resorts.
usage_notes: Also spelled as 'isdang espada'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap gawing steak ang **isdang-ispada**.","translation":"**Swordfish** is delicious when made into a steak."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na naglalaman ng enerhiyang kemikal na ginagawang kuryente. Ito ang orihinal na baybay sa wikang Espanyol.
etymology: From Spanish 'batería'. This is the direct source word for the modern Filipino 'baterya'.
original_explanation: The OG, historical spelling, straight from our Spanish colonial past. Using 'bateria' today is like calling your friend 'Señorita' instead of 'Miss'—a bit old-fashioned, maybe even classy, but 'baterya' is what's on the streets and in the stores now.
usage_notes: This is the Spanish spelling and is considered archaic or historical. The modern, Filipinized spelling is 'baterya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang dokumento, '**bateria**' ang ginagamit na salita.","translation":"In old documents, '**bateria**' is the word used."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa dalawa o higit pang mga tao na magkayakap sa isa't isa, o sa isang tao na laging may kayakap na bagay.
original_explanation: This is the 'PDA level 100' version of a hug. It's when a couple is so sweet it's almost nauseating, always attached at the hip. 'Tingnan mo 'yung dalawa, yakap-yakap na naman sa gitna ng mall.' It can also describe a child clinging to a parent or a comfort object. The repetition implies continuous or reciprocal action.
usage_notes: A reduplicated form of 'yakap,' indicating reciprocity, continuation, or intensity. Often used with 'mag-' prefix as 'magkayakap-yakap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang magkasintahan na **yakap-yakap** habang nanonood ng paglubog ng araw.","translation":"I saw the couple **hugging each other** while watching the sunset."},{"sentence":"Lagi niyang **yakap-yakap** ang unan na bigay ng lola niya.","translation":"She is **constantly hugging** the pillow her grandmother gave her."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng kapatawaran ang isang tao para sa isang partikular na pagkakamali o kasalanan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `i-` (nagsasaad ng sanhi), `pagpa-` (nagsasaad ng sanhi), at `tawad` (forgiveness, bargain).
original_explanation: The formal way of saying "sorry na, please." It's what you say when you've messed up big time. It's not just "patawarin mo ako" (forgive me), but it's asking forgiveness *for* a specific action. "Lord, **ipagpatawad** mo po ang mga kasalanan ko." It carries more weight and humility.
usage_notes: Isang mas pormal at malalim na paraan ng paghingi ng tawad. Ang taong hinihingan ng tawad ay ang di-tuwirang layon, at ang pagkakamali ay ang tuwirang layon. Madalas gamitin sa mga panalangin o seryosong paghingi ng paumanhin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipagpatawad** mo sana ang aking nagawang pagkakamali.","translation":"I hope you **forgive** me **for** the mistake I made."},{"sentence":"Diyos ko, **ipagpatawad** Ninyo ang aking mga kasalanan.","translation":"My God, **forgive** me **for** my sins."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa materyal na ginamit sa paggawa ng isang bagay, o sa kalagayan ng pagiging tapos na.
original_explanation: This is the 'Made in...' tag of an item. 'Yari sa China,' 'Yari sa Divisoria.' It's also that feeling of relief when your project is finally done. 'Yari na ang report ko, pwede na mag-ML!'
usage_notes: Often used with 'sa' to denote the material, e.g., 'yari sa kahoy' (made of wood). The form 'yaring' is a contraction of 'yari na' (already finished) or 'yari ng' (made by).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mesa ay **yari** sa matibay na narra.","translation":"The table is **made of** sturdy narra wood."},{"sentence":"**Yari** na ba ang pinapagawa kong bestida?","translation":"Is the dress I asked you to make **finished**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan nagaganap ang paghahatid o pagdadala ng mga bagay. Maaari ring tumukoy sa kilos ng paghahatid sa isa't isa.
etymology: From `hatid` + `-an` suffix, indicating a place or reciprocal action.
original_explanation: This is the act of exchanging deliveries. Think of a potluck where everyone brings a dish to share—that's a form of `hatiran`. Or during Christmas, when families do `hatiran` ng Noche Buena food. It's the OG food delivery service, powered by community and chismis. 'Naghatiran kami ng ulam ni kumare.'
usage_notes: The verb form for this reciprocal action is `maghatiran`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging tradisyon na ang **hatiran** ng pagkain tuwing Pasko sa aming baryo.","translation":"The **mutual delivery** of food during Christmas has become a tradition in our village."},{"sentence":"Ang terminal ang nagsisilbing **hatiran** at sunduan ng mga pasahero.","translation":"The terminal serves as the drop-off and pick-up **point** for passengers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kahon o sisidlan para sa mga sulat at iba pang ipinadadalang koreo, karaniwang matatagpuan sa labas ng bahay o gusali.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung physical version ng inbox mo. Dito iniiwan ni kartero 'yung mga love letters na 'di mo naman natatanggap, at 'yung Meralco bill na ayaw mong makita. Sa panahon ng digital age, para na lang siyang display o lalagyan ng flyers.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit ang salitang Ingles na 'mailbox' sa Pilipinas. Ang katumbas nitong salitang Filipino na 'buson' ay bihirang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo nga sa **mailbox** kung may sulat mula sa bangko.","translation":"Please check the **mailbox** if there's a letter from the bank."},{"sentence":"Puno na naman ng flyers ang **mailbox** namin.","translation":"Our **mailbox** is full of flyers again."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtanggal sa isang tao mula sa listahan ng mga kaibigan sa isang social networking site, partikular sa Facebook.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na "unfriend", na naging popular dahil sa Facebook.
original_explanation: The social media equivalent of a friendship-ending fight. It’s more dramatic than an 'unfollow'. This is when you decide you don't even want to be digitally associated with them anymore. The "It's not me, it's you" of the Facebook world.
usage_notes: Pangunahing nauugnay sa Facebook.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-away sila kaya **in-unfriend** niya ang dati niyang best friend sa Facebook.","translation":"They had a fight, so she **unfriended** her former best friend on Facebook."},{"sentence":"Balak ko siyang i-**unfriend** dahil sa mga pinagsasabi niya tungkol sa pulitika.","translation":"I plan to **unfriend** him because of the things he says about politics."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa loob ng panahon na iyon; habang nangyayari ang isang bagay, may iba ring nagaganap.
etymology: Mula sa Sanskrit na "samantara," na nangangahulugang "sa parehong pagitan" o "pansamantala."
original_explanation: The official soundtrack of waiting. Ito yung ginagawa mo habang nag-re-render yung video, nag-da-download yung file, o naghihintay ka sa reply niya. **Samantala**, mag-scroll muna tayo sa TikTok. It’s the filler episode of your life.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin bilang transisyon sa pagitan ng dalawang sabay na pangyayari. Ang 'samantalang' ay isang baryasyon na madalas gamitin bilang pangatnig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagluluto ang nanay sa kusina. **Samantala**, ang tatay ay nagbabasa ng diyaryo sa sala.","translation":"Mother is cooking in the kitchen. **Meanwhile**, father is reading the newspaper in the living room."},{"sentence":"Maghintay ka lang diyan. **Samantala**, kukuha ako ng maiinom.","translation":"Just wait there. **In the meantime**, I'll get something to drink."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng bato, marmol, o metal na inilalagay sa puntod, na karaniwang may nakaukit na pangalan, petsa ng kapanganakan, at kamatayan ng yumaong nakalibing.
original_explanation: The original 'profile page' before social media. It has your name, your 'active' dates, and it's made of stone so it lasts longer than your last tweet. Visited mostly during Undas, where it gets a yearly cleaning and a candle-lit get-together.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nililinis nila ang **lapida** ng kanilang lolo tuwing Araw ng mga Patay.","translation":"They clean their grandfather's **tombstone** every All Saints' Day."},{"sentence":"Ipinaukit niya ang pangalan ng kanyang ina sa bagong **lapida**.","translation":"He had his mother's name engraved on the new **gravestone**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakadulong buto ng gulugod ng tao, na kilala rin sa tawag na coccyx.
original_explanation: This is the scientific but also very Filipino word for your tailbone. It's that specific spot you land on when you slip on a wet floor, and you see your whole life flash before your eyes. 'Aray, 'yung **tangginggi** ko!' is a cry of very specific, intense pain. It’s the body part you forget you have until you hurt it badly.
usage_notes: Hindi gaanong karaniwang salita; mas madalas gamitin ang 'tailbone' o 'buto sa puwet' sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumakit ang kanyang **tangginggi** matapos siyang madulas sa sahig.","translation":"His **coccyx** hurt after he slipped on the floor."},{"sentence":"Ang bali sa **tangginggi** ay nangangailangan ng mahabang panahon upang gumaling.","translation":"A fracture in the **tailbone** requires a long time to heal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdiriwang o pananatili sa isang lugar sa panahon ng Kapaskuhan.
original_explanation: The annual Pinoy migration plan. 'Saan kayo magpa-Pasko?' is the icebreaker from September to December. It's the verb for choosing whether to spend the holidays braving traffic to the province, staying in the city for the mall sales, or flying abroad to see snow for the 'gram.
usage_notes: Often used in questions about holiday plans, especially during the '-ber' months.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano naming **magpaskuhan** sa bahay ng aming lola sa probinsya.","translation":"We plan to **spend Christmas** at our grandmother's house in the province."},{"sentence":"Masarap **magpaskuhan** sa Pilipinas dahil sa mahabang selebrasyon.","translation":"It's great to **spend Christmas** in the Philippines because of the long celebration."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na nagdudulot ng abala, perwisyo, o hadlang.
original_explanation: That person or thing that just gets in the way. Yung kapitbahay na nag-vivideoke ng 2 AM on a Tuesday? Estorbo. Yung biglang brownout habang WFH meeting? Estorbo. Yung kapatid mong nanghihiram ng charger mo tapos di na binabalik? Certified estorbo. It's the reason for your 'Lord, give me patience' moments.
usage_notes: Commonly used to express annoyance. The spelling 'istorbo' is more common in informal communication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **estorbo** sa mga nag-aaral.","translation":"Don't be a **nuisance** to those who are studying."},{"sentence":"Malaking **estorbo** sa trapiko ang nasiraang trak.","translation":"The broken-down truck is a major **hindrance** to traffic."}]

translation: sponsorship of education; the act of sending someone to school
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain o pananagutan ng pagsuporta sa pag-aaral ng isang tao, karaniwang sa pamamagitan ng pagbabayad ng matrikula at iba pang gastusin sa edukasyon.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino parent flex. It's not a place, but an action—the verb of sacrifice. It's your parents working overtime, your OFW tita sending remittances, all for the noble cause of your education. "Pinapaaral kita" is the classic line that means "I'm investing in you, so please don't fail your subjects."
usage_notes: Often used in the context of a parent, guardian, or sponsor providing for a student's education. The person being sent to school is the `pinapaaral`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaking sakripisyo ang **paaral** sa mga anak.","translation":"The **sponsorship of children's education** is a great sacrifice."},{"sentence":"Sinuportahan niya ang **paaral** ng kanyang mga kapatid.","translation":"He supported the **education** of his siblings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tamaan ng kulog o kidlat. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay isang sumpa o pagbabanta na mangyari ang nasabing kaganapan.
original_explanation: An old-school curse your super-traditional lola might have muttered under her breath. It's like saying 'May you be struck by lightning!' It's so dramatic, it's almost poetic. You won't hear this in a BPO pantry, that's for sure.
usage_notes: Extremely rare in modern conversation. Used more as a curse or in old literature. 'Sana kuluguhin ka!' is the classic form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa galit ng matanda, isinumpa niyang sana ay **kuluguhin** ang magnanakaw.","translation":"In the old man's anger, he cursed that the thief **be struck by lightning**."},{"sentence":"Isang lumang kasabihan ang 'Huwag kang magtuturo ng bahaghari at baka ka **kuluguhin**'.","translation":"An old saying is 'Don't point at a rainbow or you might **be struck by lightning**'."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pag-atras, pagliit, o pagbalik sa dating posisyon o laki.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your favorite cotton shirt after you put it in the dryer on high heat. It's also that feeling when you're about to confront someone, tapos bigla kang umatras kasi 'di mo pala kaya—that's `pagkaurong` ng dila (or ng tapang). It’s the opposite of progress; it's a retreat, a shrinkage.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na pagliit, pag-atras sa isang kasunduan, o sikolohikal na pag-urong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin niya ang **pagkaurong** ng tela matapos itong labhan.","translation":"She noticed the **shrinkage** of the fabric after it was washed."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaurong** ng kanyang desisyon ay ikinagulat ng lahat.","translation":"The **retraction** of his decision surprised everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng salapi o yaman bilang puhunan sa isang negosyo o gawain upang kumita.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'I believe in you' move. It's when you give your friend money to start their online ukay-ukay or milk tea shop. You're not just giving them cash; you're magpapuhunan in their dreams (and hopefully, your future ROI). It's the adult version of lending your classmate 5 pesos for Canteen lunch.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of business, finance, or even supporting someone's personal project.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magpapuhunan** sa isang maliit na coffee shop.","translation":"She decided to **invest** in a small coffee shop."},{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang gustong **magpapuhunan** sa bago kong startup?","translation":"I wonder who wants to **provide capital** for my new startup?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging matagumpay na nakaraan sa isang hadlang, butas, o proseso ng pagsusuri.
original_explanation: When your crazy, last-minute proposal somehow gets approved by the boss, that's 'lusot.' When your alibi for coming home late works on your parents, 'lusot ka.' It's the adjective form of a successful escape or passage. It's the green light after navigating a bureaucratic maze.
usage_notes: Often used with 'na' (lusot na). Implies something has successfully passed a check, a barrier, or a process.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **lusot** na sa Kongreso ang pinapanukala naming batas.","translation":"Finally, our proposed bill has **gone through** Congress."}]

translation: act of rushing or swarming towards
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay at mabilis na pagpunta o paglapit ng maraming tao o hayop sa isang direksyon o lugar.
original_explanation: Picture this: a new milk tea shop opens and gives away free drinks for the first 100 customers. The chaos that follows? That's pagdadaluhungan. It's the human version of ants swarming a piece of candy.
usage_notes: Implies a rush or stampede, often by a crowd. The verb form 'daluhungin' is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdulot ng gulo ang **pagdadaluhungan** ng mga tao sa entablado.","translation":"The **swarming** of people towards the stage caused chaos."},{"sentence":"Inaasahan ang **pagdadaluhungan** ng mga mamimili sa unang araw ng sale.","translation":"The **rushing** of shoppers is expected on the first day of the sale."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpasok ng pagkain sa bibig, pagnguya, at paglunok nito para sa nutrisyon.
original_explanation: This is the *action*, not the adobo. It's the process. 'Yung ingay ng kutsara't tinidor, 'yung seryoso mong mukha habang sinusubo ang unang kagat ng crispy pata. It's the sacred ritual before you post 'Kain tayo!' on IG.
usage_notes: Often used in sentences describing the manner or time of eating. It's a gerund-like noun. The distinction from the noun 'food' is purely contextual.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging mabilis ang kanyang **pagkain** dahil may hinahabol siyang meeting.","translation":"His **act of eating** was quick because he was rushing to a meeting."},{"sentence":"Ang tamang **pagkain** ay mahalaga para sa kalusugan.","translation":"The proper **way of eating** is important for health."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa tindig, bikas, o kaanyuan ng katawan ng isang tao, na karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng lakas, kalusugan, at kumpiyansa.
original_explanation: This is the Pinoy version of 'swag' but for your body. It's not just about being muscular; it's about how you carry yourself. 'Yung tindig-pogi, 'yung lakad na may kumpiyansa kahit butas ang bulsa. A person with 'tikas' looks like they can carry a sack of rice or a conversation with equal ease. Think of a classic Fernando Poe Jr. pose.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ('may tikas' - has good posture) or an adjective ('matikas' - well-built).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **tikas** ang mga sundalo habang nagmamartsa.","translation":"The soldiers have a fine **bearing** as they march."},{"sentence":"Kahit matanda na si lolo, matikas pa rin ang kanyang tindig.","translation":"Even though grandpa is old, his posture is still **good**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang tao o bagay na humahalili o inilalagay sa lugar ng isa pa.
original_explanation: Yung taong nag-take over ng trabaho mo nung nag-resign ka. Or 'yung bagong jowa ng ex mo. Minsan, ito rin yung inorder mong item sa Shopee na iba sa picture. Basically, the "pampalit" when the original is gone. Hugot version: "Madali lang akong palitan, pero mahirap tapatan." Charot!
usage_notes: Can refer to people, objects, or even abstract concepts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **kapalit** ni G. Reyes bilang tagapamahala?","translation":"Who is Mr. Reyes' **replacement** as manager?"},{"sentence":"Humanap ka na ng **kapalit** para sa sirang piyesa ng makina.","translation":"Find a **replacement** for the broken machine part."},{"sentence":"Wala kang **kapalit** sa puso ko.","translation":"You have no **replacement** in my heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may kapansanan o diperensya sa pag-iisip; wala sa tamang katinuan.
original_explanation: A more serious, less casual term than 'siraulo'. This isn't just for someone acting goofy. It implies a genuine mental break or instability. It's the kind of term you'd hear in a dramatic telenovela when a character loses their mind after a great tragedy. Not a word to be thrown around lightly.
usage_notes: Maaaring ituring na nakakainsulto o hindi sensitibo. Mas mainam gamitin ang mga terminong medikal sa pormal o magalang na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinaniniwalaan ng ilan na siya ay naging **sirang-isip** matapos ang digmaan.","translation":"Some believe that he became **mentally deranged** after the war."},{"sentence":"Ang karakter sa pelikula ay isang henyo na unti-unting naging **sirang-isip**.","translation":"The character in the movie is a genius who slowly became **insane**."}]

translation: to put a wedge/stopper; to prevent from rolling
meaning_filipino: Maglagay ng kalso o pansara upang hindi gumulong o umusad ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay ang gulong ng sasakyan.
original_explanation: Imagine a jeepney parked on a steep hill in Baguio. The driver shoves a piece of wood under the tire. That's sumasagka. It's the act of preventing something from moving when it's not supposed to. In life, it's that friend who stops you from texting your ex at 2 AM. Sila ang sumasagka sa'yo.
usage_notes: A very specific term, mostly related to vehicles and using a 'kalso' (wedge/chock). Figurative use is rare but possible.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dali, **sumagka** ka ng bato sa gulong para hindi umatras ang dyip.","translation":"Quick, **put a wedge** of stone on the wheel so the jeep won't roll back."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **sumagka** sa pagkalat ng maling impormasyon sa social media.","translation":"There is a need **to stop** the spread of false information on social media."}]

translation: to turn blue; to become pale or livid
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng kulay ng balat o labi tungo sa pagiging bughaw o maputla, kadalasan dahil sa lamig, takot, o kakulangan ng hangin.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your lips when you swim in Baguio's waters, or your face when you see your ex with a new partner. It's the color of 'shookt' or extreme cold.
usage_notes: Often associated with cold, fear, or lack of oxygen.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mamughaw** ang kanyang mga labi dahil sa sobrang lamig.","translation":"His lips started **to turn blue** because of the extreme cold."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong takutin, baka **mamughaw** ako rito.","translation":"Don't scare me, I might **turn pale** here."}]

translation: homebody; person in charge of the house
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na palaging nasa bahay, o ang taong responsable sa pamamahala at pangangalaga ng isang tahanan.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'taong pagala-gala.' This is the person whose idea of a perfect Friday night is Netflix, pajamas, and a bowl of sinigang. They're the masters of their domain (the house). Can also refer to the person left to guard the house during a family outing, aka the designated 'bantay-bahay'.
usage_notes: Can be used neutrally to describe a homebody or to refer to the person managing the household.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ako ang **taong-bahay** ngayon dahil umalis silang lahat.","translation":"I'm the **person in charge of the house** today because they all left."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pamamaraan ng pagpasok ng likido sa tumbong at malaking bituka sa pamamagitan ng butas ng puwit, karaniwan upang mapadali ang pagdumi o para sa medikal na pagsusuri.
original_explanation: Okay, let's be mature about this. Ito 'yung procedure na ginagawa sa ospital (o minsan sa bahay) para "i-flush out" ang system mo down there. Parang plumbing job para sa katawan. Usually ginagawa 'to bago ang isang surgery or 'pag sobrang hirap ka nang... alam mo na. It's the ultimate 'linis-bituka' challenge.
usage_notes: Isang terminong medikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan ng **enema** ang pasyente bilang paghahanda sa kanyang operasyon.","translation":"The patient was given an **enema** in preparation for his operation."},{"sentence":"Ang madalas na paggamit ng **enema** ay hindi inirerekomenda nang walang payo ng doktor.","translation":"Frequent use of an **enema** is not recommended without a doctor's advice."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag ng utang na loob, pagkilala, o pagtanaw ng pasasalamat sa isang kabutihang natanggap.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative) + `salamat` (thanks), with reduplication of the root's first syllable (`sa-`).
original_explanation: This is what you feel when your Shopee order arrives earlier than expected. Or the long, emotional Facebook post you write on your birthday, thanking everyone from your parents to the GrabFood driver who delivered your birthday cake. It's the formal version of 'Salamat, Lord!'
usage_notes: A very common and formal word for expressing thanks, often used in speeches, letters, and formal occasions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong ipaabot ang aking taos-pusong **pasasalamat** sa lahat ng tumulong.","translation":"I wish to extend my heartfelt **gratitude** to everyone who helped."},{"sentence":"Bilang **pasasalamat**, naghanda kami ng kaunting salu-salo.","translation":"As an act of **thanksgiving**, we prepared a small get-together."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng paalala o ipagunita ang isang bagay sa isang tao.
original_explanation: Your mom telling you for the 5th time to wash the dishes. It's the human version of a Google Calendar notification, but with more potential for *sermon* as a follow-up. "Bes, **paalalahanan** mo 'ko sa meeting mamaya, lutang ako today."
usage_notes: Often used in imperative form (`Paalalahanan mo ako`). The object being reminded is the focus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paalalahanan** mo ako na may appointment ako sa doktor bukas.","translation":"**Remind** me that I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Palagi niya akong **pinapaalalahanan** na mag-ingat sa pag-uwi.","translation":"He/She always **reminds** me to be careful on my way home."}]

translation: to be able to be clothed; to provide with clothes
meaning_filipino: Mabigyan o malagyan ng damit; mabihisan.
original_explanation: This is the goal of every donation drive for victims of a typhoon. It's what you hope happens to the mannequin at the department store before you buy its outfit. It’s the act of providing clothes, a very tita/nanay verb. 'Make sure the baby is clothed.'
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang pangkakayahan, na kadalasang nagpapahiwatig ng kakayahan o posibilidad na magdamit sa isang tao o bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **madamtan** ang lahat ng nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"I hope everyone affected by the typhoon can **be provided with clothes**."},{"sentence":"Sapat ba ang badyet para **madamtan** ang lahat ng kalahok sa dula?","translation":"Is the budget enough **to clothe** all the participants in the play?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lupain o taniman na kung saan ang pangunahing pananim ay tubo (sugarcane).
etymology: From 'sakat' (a type of grass or forage) + suffix '-an', denoting a place filled with it. It has become specialized to mean sugarcane fields.
original_explanation: Before condos, there were these. This is the OG source of your milk tea's sugar. Think vast fields of tall, green stalks swaying in the wind, usually found in provinces like Negros or Batangas. It's the scenery you see on long bus rides to the province.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'tubuhan'. 'Sakatihan' is less common in modern conversation than 'tubuhan' and may sound more literary or historical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtrabaho ang kanyang lolo sa isang malawak na **sakatihan** sa Negros.","translation":"His grandfather worked in a vast **sugarcane plantation** in Negros."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling pahayag na naglalaman ng mga pangunahing punto o ideya ng isang mas mahabang akda o talumpati.
original_explanation: The TL;DR (Too Long; Didn't Read) version of anything. It's the life-saving summary of 'Noli Me Tángere' you read the night before the exam. It’s what you ask your chismosa friend for: "So, anong buod? Nagkabalikan sila o hindi?"
usage_notes: Commonly used in academic and professional settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumawa ka ng **buod** ng kabanata para sa ating ulat.","translation":"Make a **summary** of the chapter for our report."},{"sentence":"Ang **buod** ng pelikula ay hindi nagbigay-katarungan sa ganda ng kabuuan nito.","translation":"The **gist** of the movie didn't do justice to its overall beauty."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng katangian ng labis na pagtingin sa sarili, pagiging mayabang, o mapagmataas.
original_explanation: Describes that person who acts like they're the main character and everyone else is just an extra. They walk into a room and you can just feel the air change. They think they're God's gift to the world. That's someone who 'may kapalaluan'. It's a more formal way of saying 'mayabang'.
usage_notes: A more formal and literary term than 'mayabang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap siyang kausapin dahil siya ay **may kapalaluan**.","translation":"He is difficult to talk to because he **is arrogant**."},{"sentence":"Ang taong **may kapalaluan** ay madalas hindi inaamin ang kanilang pagkakamali.","translation":"A person who **has arrogance** often does not admit their mistakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lalaking baboy na hindi pa kapon at ginagamit sa pagpapalahi.
original_explanation: Ito yung "macho" na baboy sa babuyan. Siya yung pinipili para maging tatay ng mga susunod na biik. Basically, the designated baboy-daddy. Hindi siya kinakatay agad kasi mahalaga ang role niya for... ehem... reproduction.
usage_notes: Ginagamit pangunahin sa konteksto ng pag-aalaga ng hayop at agrikultura.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap si Mang Teban ng magandang klaseng **bulog** para sa kanyang inahing baboy.","translation":"Mang Teban is looking for a good quality **boar** for his sow."},{"sentence":"Malakas at malusog ang **bulog** na alaga ni Lolo.","translation":"Grandpa's pet **boar** is strong and healthy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa mga detalye, impormasyon, o ang kabuuang kuwento tungkol sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Short for 'details.' This is what you ask from a friend who just came from a date. 'Give me the deets!' It's the modern, faster way of saying 'Anong chika?' You don't want the summary, you want the full, unabridged, spicy version.
usage_notes: A very common slang term used in both English and Taglish conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mamaya ka na magkuwento, bigyan mo muna ako ng **deets** sa nangyari!","translation":"Tell the story later, just give me the **deets** of what happened first!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding antas ng galit; puno ng poot o pagkasuklam.
original_explanation: This isn't just regular 'galit' (angry) from slow internet. This is 'Hulk smash!' level of rage. It's the anger you feel when someone eats your leftover Jollibee in the office fridge, or when your Grab driver cancels after you've waited 20 minutes. It’s when your mom uses your full name. You're not just mad, you're fuming.
usage_notes: A reduplicated form of 'galit' used for intensification.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Galit na galit** ang tatay dahil sa bagsak kong marka.","translation":"My father was **furious** because of my failing grade."},{"sentence":"Naging **galit na galit** siya nang malamang niloko siya.","translation":"She became **enraged** when she found out she was cheated on."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng kasipagan, sigasig, at determinasyon sa paggawa o pag-aaral.
etymology: From "ma-" (prefix indicating 'having the quality of') + "sipag" (diligence, industry).
original_explanation: The ultimate compliment for any Filipino employee or student. This is the BPO agent taking on OT like a champ, the student who finishes all their modules ahead of time, and the parent juggling three jobs. The opposite of 'Juan Tamad'. If 'sipag at tiyaga' were a person, this is them.
usage_notes: A very common and positive descriptor for a person's work ethic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Ana bilang isang **masipag** na empleyado sa kanilang kumpanya.","translation":"Ana is known as a **hardworking** employee in their company."},{"sentence":"Kung **masipag** ka lang mag-aral, siguradong matataas ang makukuha mong marka.","translation":"If only you were **diligent** in studying, you would surely get high grades."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akda o sulatin na naglalahad ng kasaysayan ng buhay ng isang tao, na isinulat ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: Basically, the official, written version of someone's life story. Parang long-form, professional-level 'Maritess mode' on a famous person's life, from birth to death (or up to the present). It's the story of how they became who they are, written by someone else. Think of the 'Talambuhay ni Jose Rizal.'
usage_notes: "Talambuhay" is the more common, native Tagalog equivalent. "Biograpia" is used in more academic or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **biograpia** ni Apolinario Mabini ay nagpapakita ng kanyang katalinuhan at pagmamahal sa bayan.","translation":"The **biography** of Apolinario Mabini shows his intelligence and love for the country."},{"sentence":"Sumusulat siya ng isang **biograpia** tungkol sa isang tanyag na alagad ng sining.","translation":"She is writing a **biography** about a famous artist."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling salita para sa demostrasyon; isang pampublikong pagtitipon, karaniwang isinasagawa ng isang grupo ng mga tao upang ipahayag ang kanilang mga hinaing o suporta sa isang isyu.
original_explanation: 'Yung short-term for 'demostrasyon.' Kapag may rally sa kalsada, may mga hawak na placards, at sumisigaw ng mga slogan—'yan ang demos. Madalas mong makikita malapit sa Mendiola o sa EDSA. Ito ang "public chat" ng bayan bago pa nauso ang social media.
usage_notes: This is a colloquial and shortened form of "demostrasyon".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **demos** na naman daw ang mga estudyante laban sa pagtaas ng matrikula.","translation":"The students are reportedly holding a **demo** again against the tuition fee hike."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **demos**, naging matrapik sa buong abenida.","translation":"Because of the **demonstration**, the entire avenue became congested with traffic."}]

translation: to do well; to settle; to judge
meaning_filipino: Gawin nang maayos at may kahusayan; ayusin ang isang gusot o alitan; litisin o hatulan ang isang kaso.
original_explanation: This is your mom's command before a visitor arrives: "Husayin mo nga yang paglilinis mo!" (Do your cleaning properly!). It's also what a mediator does in a fight: "Let's husayin this dispute." It’s the verb form of "Galingan mo!" or "Ayusin mo!". It's about leveling up your performance or resolving a conflict.
usage_notes: Has multiple related meanings: to improve something, to put something in order, or to judge/adjudicate. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan siya ng kanyang ina na **husayin** ang pag-aaral.","translation":"His mother told him to **do well** in his studies."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukang **husayin** ng barangay captain ang alitan ng magkapitbahay.","translation":"The barangay captain is trying to **settle** the dispute between the neighbors."}]

translation: to become heavy; to weigh down
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbigat ng isang bagay, damdamin, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is that feeling when your eyelids start drooping in a 1 PM meeting, or when your heart sinks after a sad movie. It's not just physical weight. Your "dama" can mamigat (your feelings get heavy), your "talukap-mata" can mamigat (eyelids get heavy), and of course, the traffic can make your whole situation mamigat. It's the official verb for "ugh, this is heavy."
usage_notes: Can be used for physical weight, emotional burden, or sleepiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mamigat** ang trapiko pagsapit ng alas singko ng hapon.","translation":"The traffic started to **become heavy** when it reached five in the afternoon."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman kong **mamigat** ang aking dibdib nang marinig ko ang malungkot na balita.","translation":"I felt my chest **weigh down** when I heard the sad news."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na katawagan ng paglalambing, karaniwang pinaikling anyo ng 'baby' o 'babe'.
etymology: Isang pinaikli at naka-lokal na baybay ng Ingles na 'babe'.
original_explanation: A low-effort, high-impact term of endearment. It's the 'babe' for people in a hurry. You use this with your jowa, your crush, or even your bestie. 'Kumain ka na ba, bhe?' is the Philippines' national love language.
usage_notes: Karaniwan sa mga text message at kaswal na pag-uusap. Maaaring gamitin para sa mga kasintahan at malalapit na kaibigan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat ka sa pag-uwi, **bhe**.","translation":"Take care on your way home, **bhe**."},{"sentence":"**Bhe**, anong gusto mong kainin?","translation":"**Bhe**, what do you want to eat?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagkuha, pagbunot, o pag-alis ng isang bagay mula sa pinagmulan nito, tulad ng pagkuha ng mineral sa minahan o pagbunot ng ngipin.
original_explanation: That feeling when your dentist says "wisdom tooth extraction." Bigla kang mapapa-research ng soft foods for one week. It's the process of pulling something out, whether it's a tooth, data from a server, or a confession from your friend who ate the last piece of leche flan.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga teknikal, medikal, at pormal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **ekstraksiyon** ng ginto sa mga bundok.","translation":"The **extraction** of gold from the mountains is difficult."},{"sentence":"Inirekomenda ng dentista ang **ekstraksiyon** ng aking sirang ngipin.","translation":"The dentist recommended the **extraction** of my damaged tooth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng bilang na katumbas ng labindalawang dosena, o 144 na piraso.
etymology: From Spanish 'gros', which comes from French 'grosse (douzaine)', meaning 'large dozen'.
original_explanation: A throwback unit of measurement for when you're buying things in serious bulk, like Divisoria-level bulk. One 'gros' is 12 dozens, or 144 pieces. You wouldn't buy a 'gros' of iPhones, but maybe a 'gros' of pencils, buttons, or sisiw for your poultry business. It’s like the final boss of 'dosena'.
usage_notes: Less common than 'dosena' (dozen) but still used in wholesale and manufacturing contexts. 'Gruesa' is a synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng isang **gros** na butones para sa kanyang patahian.","translation":"She bought a **gross** of buttons for her dressmaking shop."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang isang **gros** ng lapis?","translation":"How much for one **gross** of pencils?"}]

translation: to be able to get something for free
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakataong makakuha ng isang bagay o serbisyo nang walang bayad.
original_explanation: The national sport of the Philippines. This is the goal when the waiter brings the bill and everyone does the "ako na" dance. It's what happens when your friend is the connect for concert tickets. To *makalibre* is a glorious victory against gastos (expenses). The best things in life are libre.
usage_notes: The ultimate goal for many Filipinos in transactions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumila siya nang maaga para **makalibre** ng kape.","translation":"He lined up early **to be able to get** free coffee."},{"sentence":"Kung bibili ka ng dalawa, **makakalibre** ka ng isa.","translation":"If you buy two, you'll **be able to get** one for free."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang seremonyang panrelihiyon, partikular sa Kristiyanismo, kung saan ang isang tao ay tinatanggap sa komunidad ng simbahan sa pamamagitan ng pagbubuhos o paglulubog sa tubig.
original_explanation: This is the baby's first-ever 'launch party.' There's a church ceremony, a new outfit, lots of godparents (ninongs and ninangs) who are expected to give 'pakimkim' (cash gift), and usually a big handaan afterwards. Metaphorically, 'binyagan' means to use something for the very first time, like your new shoes or your fresh sahod. 'Binyagan na natin 'yang bagong sweldo mo sa milk tea!'
usage_notes: The verb form is "binyagan" (to baptize someone or to use something for the first time).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gaganapin ang **binyag** ng kanyang anak sa susunod na Linggo.","translation":"Her child's **baptism** will be held next Sunday."},{"sentence":"Ang handaan para sa **binyag** ay puno ng bisita.","translation":"The reception for the **christening** was full of guests."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng koral o kulungan para sa isda na yari sa kawayan at lambat, itinayo sa mababaw na bahagi ng dagat, lawa, o ilog upang makahuli ng isda.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino fishing tech. It's that maze of bamboo sticks you see sticking out of the water when you're on a ferry or at a beach resort. It's like a trap house for fish, luring them into a place they can't easily escape.
usage_notes: A common sight in coastal and lacustrine communities throughout the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming nahuling isda sa **baklád** ni Mang Tacio kaninang umaga.","translation":"Many fish were caught in Mang Tacio's **fish corral** this morning."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **baklád** ay nakahanay sa baybayin ng Laguna de Bay.","translation":"The **fish corrals** are lined up along the shores of Laguna de Bay."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi hustong-husto; kulang sa kinakailangang dami, sukat, o kalidad.
original_explanation: Yung sweldo mo pagdating ng ika-14 ng buwan. 'Yung data allocation mo one week before the next reset. 'Yung "I love you" na walang kasamang "I'm sorry." It's the official feeling of 'kulang pa, bes.' The battle cry of 'petsa de peligro.'
usage_notes: Isang tambalang salita na gumagamit ng panangging 'di'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tulong na dumating ay **di-sapat** para sa lahat ng biktima ng bagyo.","translation":"The aid that arrived was **insufficient** for all the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Ang \"pasensya na\" ay **di-sapat** para mabura ang sakit na idinulot mo.","translation":"An \"I'm sorry\" is **not enough** to erase the pain you caused."}]

translation: to be indecisive about; to keep postponing
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pagpapaliban, pag-aatubili, o pagbabago ng isip hinggil sa paggawa ng isang desisyon o aksyon.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for chronic overthinkers and commitment-phobes. It's when you add an item to your online shopping cart, then remove it, then add it again. You **ipag-urung-sulong** the purchase. It's the endless 'should I or shouldn't I?' dance of indecision.
usage_notes: Describes the act of repeatedly delaying or hesitating on a specific task or decision mentioned as the object of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang linggo na niyang **ipinag-uurung-sulong** ang pag-amin sa kanyang nararamdaman.","translation":"For a week, he has **been indecisive about** confessing his feelings."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo pa **ipinag-urung-sulong** ang pag-apply sa trabahong iyan?","translation":"Why do you **keep postponing** applying for that job?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o grupo na sumisigaw o humihiyaw upang magpakita ng suporta, pagtutol, o matinding damdamin sa isang kaganapan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "taga-" (tagagawa ng kilos) at salitang-ugat na "hiyaw" (malakas na sigaw).
original_explanation: The hype man/woman in your life. The one in the basketball game screaming 'Defense!' or your tita at a family gathering shouting 'Uy, tumaba ka!'. Basically, anyone who adds to the noise, for better or for worse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging mga **tagahiyaw** ang buong barkada sa laban niya sa boksing.","translation":"The whole group of friends became **cheerers** during his boxing match."}]

translation: creditor; one to whom a debt is owed
meaning_filipino: Ang tao, kumpanya, o anumang entidad kung kanino ang isang indibidwal o grupo ay may pananagutang pampinansyal o utang na dapat bayaran.
original_explanation: The person you suddenly can't see when they're walking towards you. 'Yung taong bigla mong nagiging best friend 'pag malapit na ang sweldo, at bigla mong hindi kilala 'pag petsa de peligro. They are the reason for the 'seen' zone and the 'cannot be reached' phone status.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the creditor, the person or entity being owed. The person who has the debt is the 'may utang' or 'umutang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan mong makasalubong ang **pinagkakautangan** mo sa palengke.","translation":"Avoid bumping into your **creditor** at the market."},{"sentence":"Nagpadala ng sulat ang bangko bilang aking **pinagkakautangan**.","translation":"The bank, being my **creditor**, sent a letter."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na taniman o lugar kung saan maraming tumutubong bulak.
etymology: Mula sa "bulak" (cotton) + hulaping "-an" (na nagsasaad ng lugar).
original_explanation: Imagine a field full of fluffy white stuff that looks like clouds decided to chill on the ground. Hindi ito 'yung Bulacan na probinsya, kundi 'yung farm ng bulak. Parang farm ng pangarap mo, malambot pero mahirap abutin.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang plantasyon o bukirin ng mga halamang bulak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malawak ang **bulakan** sa aming bayan noong unang panahon.","translation":"The **cotton field** in our town was vast in the old days."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pandiwa na tumutukoy sa pag-akyat sa isang tiyak na bagay, lugar, o posisyon.
original_explanation: Command form. 'Yung utos sa'yo ng jowa mo: 'Akyatin mo yung puno ng mangga para may pang-ulam tayo.' Or 'yung goal mo sa buhay: 'Akyatin ang tuktok ng tagumpay.'
usage_notes: This is an object-focused verb. The object of the sentence is the thing being climbed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kaya mo bang **akyatin** ang pader na iyan?","translation":"Can you **climb** that wall?"},{"sentence":"Plano naming **akyatin** ang Bundok Apo sa susunod na taon.","translation":"We plan to **climb** Mount Apo next year."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kawalan ng awa, habag, o pakikiramay sa kapwa; pagiging manhid sa damdamin ng iba.
etymology: Literally 'hardness of the inside/will'. An idiomatic expression.
original_explanation: This is when someone's heart is basically made of stone. They see you crying over a K-drama finale and just say, 'OA mo naman.' It’s a level of emotional detachment that's colder than the office AC on a Monday morning. The opposite of a 'Marites' who feels everything; this person feels nothing.
usage_notes: A strong term describing a severe lack of empathy. Distinct from 'katigasan ng ulo' (stubbornness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang **katigasan ng loob** nang iwan niya ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He showed his **heartlessness** when he abandoned his family."}]

translation: friendship; the act of making friends
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o ugnayan ng pagiging magkaibigan; ang pagtatatag at pagpapanatili ng relasyon bilang magkaibigan.
etymology: From pakiki- (reciprocal action) + pag- (action noun) + kaibigan (friend).
original_explanation: It's the process of turning a stranger into someone you can send memes to at 3 AM. It’s the art of building your barkada, your support system, your go-to people for gossip, food trips, and emotional breakdowns. It starts with "Hi/Hello" and levels up to "Uy, libre mo 'ko."
usage_notes: Refers to the dynamic process or state of having and maintaining friendships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tapat na **pakikipagkaibigan**.","translation":"Honest **friendship** is important."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang galing sa **pakikipagkaibigan** ay dahilan kung bakit marami siyang koneksyon.","translation":"His skill in **making friends** is why he has so many connections."}]

translation: to fool around; to make a fool of each other
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng dalawa o higit pang tao na naglolokohan o nagbibiruan sa paraang walang kaseryosohan; paglalaro sa isa't isa.
etymology: mag- (verb prefix) + luku-lukuhan (reduplication and variation of 'loko', 'crazy' or 'fool', + -han reciprocal suffix).
original_explanation: This is what happens when you and your friends are bored. 'Magluku-lukuhan' is the art of mutual foolishness. It's telling silly jokes, pulling harmless pranks, and generally just acting like clowns together. But be careful, it can also mean to deceive each other, like in a relationship where both parties are playing games. 'Are we serious or are we just naglu-luku-lukuhan?' is a valid, and often painful, question.
usage_notes: The -an suffix indicates a reciprocal action. The reduplication ('luku-lukuhan') softens the meaning to 'fooling around' rather than serious deception, though context matters.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumigil na kayo sa **paglulukuhan** at seryosohin ninyo ang trabaho.","translation":"Stop **fooling around** and take your work seriously."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko alam kung seryoso ba siya o **naglu-lukuhan** lang kami.","translation":"I don't know if he's serious or if we're just **playing games with each other**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay na may kaugnayan sa loob ng isang bansa, bahay, o pamilya; hindi banyaga.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'domestic' o Espanyol na 'doméstico'.
original_explanation: Anything "local". Domestik flight? That's Cebu Pacific, not Singapore Airlines. Domestik helper? The official title for 'kasambahay'. Domestik beer? San Miguel, not Heineken. It's the opposite of 'international' or 'pang-abroad'.
usage_notes: Often used in compounds like 'domestik helper' or 'domestik flight'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mura ang pamasahe sa mga **domestik** na lipad.","translation":"The fare for **domestic** flights is cheaper."},{"sentence":"Ang pusa ay isang **domestik** na hayop.","translation":"The cat is a **domestic** animal."}]

translation: affiliation; act of joining a group or organization
meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na akto ng pagiging kasapi o miyembro ng isang samahan, organisasyon, o kapisanan.
etymology: From pa- + ki- + sapi. 'Sapi' means to join or affiliate.
original_explanation: This is the more formal version of "pakikisali". It's not just joining the "inuman" session, it's signing up for the org, paying the membership fee, and attending the general assembly. Think of it as officially changing your relationship status with a group from "It's Complicated" to "In a Relationship".
usage_notes: Has a more formal connotation than 'pakikisali', often referring to official membership in an organization.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pakikisapi** sa isang unyon ay karapatan ng bawat manggagawa.","translation":"**Affiliation** with a union is the right of every worker."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan niya ang mga benepisyo ng **pakikisapi** sa kooperatiba.","translation":"She is studying the benefits of **joining** the cooperative."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mas mahabang kamay ng orasan na tumuturo sa mga minuto.
original_explanation: The long hand on an analog clock. It's the one that moves faster than the hour hand but slower than the second hand, constantly reminding you how slowly time passes when you're in a boring meeting or how quickly it goes when you're cramming for an exam.
usage_notes: Ang katapat nito ay 'oraryo' (hour hand) at 'segundero' (second hand).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sira yata ang **minutero** ng lumang orasan ni Lolo.","translation":"I think the **minute hand** of Grandpa's old clock is broken."},{"sentence":"Tinitigan niya ang paggalaw ng **minutero** habang naghihintay.","translation":"He stared at the movement of the **minute hand** while waiting."}]

translation: the act of resting one's chin on the hand
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapatong ng baba sa isa o dalawang kamay, karaniwang tanda ng malalim na pag-iisip, pagkabagot, o kalungkutan.
etymology: From `pang-` + `(ka)lumbaba`, which is a portmanteau of `kamay` (hand) and `baba` (chin).
original_explanation: The official pose of someone "in deep thought" (or deeply bored in a Zoom meeting). It's the "thinking man" statue pose you do when you're actually just thinking about what to eat for lunch. Can also be a sign of "hugot" or deep sadness.
usage_notes: A very specific noun for a common action. The verb form 'nakangalumbaba' is more frequently used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pangangalumbaba** ay palatandaan ng malalim na problema.","translation":"His **act of resting his chin on his hand** was a sign of a deep problem."},{"sentence":"Napansin ng guro ang **pangangalumbaba** ng estudyante sa klase.","translation":"The teacher noticed the student's **chin-on-hand pose** in class."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkaing-kalye na gawa sa pinatigas na dugo ng baboy o manok, na hiniwa nang pakwadrado, tinuhog, at iniihaw.
etymology: Ipinangalan sa Betamax videotape format dahil sa pagkakahawig nito sa hugis at kulay.
original_explanation: Not the ancient video tape your tito is still hoarding! This is street food royalty. It's grilled pig's blood, cubed to look like the old Betamax tapes. Perfect with spicy vinegar. It's the 'vampire's favorite isaw'.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwan at sikat na pagkaing-kalye sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng limang **betamax** at isang isaw.","translation":"Can I buy five sticks of **betamax** and one isaw."}]

translation: a hard blow, a strong hit
meaning_filipino: Isang malakas na palo, hampas, o pukpok.
original_explanation: The sound and impact of a perfectly landed suntok from Manny Pacquiao. It's not a tap; it's a full-force, bone-shaking impact. Think of a blacksmith hitting an anvil, or a demolition crew's wrecking ball making its first contact. It’s pure, forceful impact.
usage_notes: While it is the root for 'lantakan' (to devour), in its noun form, it almost exclusively means a physical strike.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumuho ang pader mula sa isang **lantak** lamang ng wrecking ball.","translation":"The wall collapsed from just one **blow** of the wrecking ball."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o lugar na nagbibigay ng pansamantalang tirahan sa mga manlalakbay o bisita, karaniwang may bayad.
etymology: Mula sa `bahay` (house) at `panuluyan` (mula sa `tuloy`, na nangangahulugang 'pumasok' o 'manatili'). Literal na 'bahay na tinutuluyan'.
original_explanation: Think of it as the OG Airbnb or a motel. It's a place where you can crash for a night or two when you're out of town. The term is a bit old-school, but it's the place Mary and Joseph were looking for in the Panunuluyan Christmas play.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga kontekstong pangkasaysayan o panrelihiyon, tulad ng kuwento ng Pasko na Panunuluyan. Ang mga modernong katumbas ay 'hotel', 'motel', o 'inn'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanap sila ng **bahay-panuluyan** sa gitna ng gabi.","translation":"They looked for an **inn** in the middle of the night."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang mansyon ay ginawang isang marangyang **bahay-panuluyan**.","translation":"The old mansion was converted into a luxurious **lodging house**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sanaysay sa pahayagan o magasin na naglalaman ng opinyon o pananaw ng mga patnugot hinggil sa isang napapanahong isyu.
etymology: From `pangulo` (chief, head) + `tudling` (furrow, column in a newspaper). Literally, "head column."
original_explanation: This is the newspaper's official 'hugot' or 'rant' section. It's not just news; it's news with an opinion. While the rest of the paper tells you *what* happened, the pangulong tudling tells you *what the editors think about what happened*. It's the part you read to either nod in agreement or to practice your debate skills with an inanimate object.
usage_notes: A staple of journalism and print media. Often accompanied by an editorial cartoon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pangulong tudling** ngayon ay tungkol sa epekto ng bagong batas sa trapiko.","translation":"Today's **editorial** is about the effect of the new traffic law."},{"sentence":"Mahusay ang pagkakasulat ng **pangulong tudling** at nagbigay ito ng bagong perspektibo.","translation":"The **leading article** was well-written and it provided a new perspective."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling salita para sa 'bisexual,' na tumutukoy sa isang taong nagkakaroon ng romantiko o sekswal na atraksyon sa kapwa lalaki at babae.
original_explanation: Short for bisexual. It means you're not choosing from just one menu at the buffet of love. You appreciate both the sinigang and the adobo. Your heart (and eyes) are open to possibilities.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pangngalan ('Isa siyang bi.') o pang-uri ('Bi siya.'). Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga pag-uusap sa Ingles at Tagalog tungkol sa sekswalidad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinanong niya kung **bi** ako, at sinabi kong oo.","translation":"He asked if I was **bi**, and I said yes."},{"sentence":"Maraming sikat na artista ang **bi**-curious daw.","translation":"Many famous artists are said to be **bi**-curious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw ng ulo pakanan at pakaliwa (o vice versa) bilang pagpapahiwatig ng pagtanggi, di-pagsang-ayon, o kawalan ng pag-asa.
original_explanation: The universal Filipino parent response when you ask for a new phone right after they paid your tuition. It's a silent but very loud "no." It can mean "ayaw ko," "hindi pwede," or "hay, nako, anak."
usage_notes: The direct opposite of 'pagtango' (nodding).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **pag-iling** lang ang isinagot niya sa aking tanong.","translation":"Just a strong **shaking of the head** was her answer to my question."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal at nakasulat na testimonya na ibinigay ng isang saksi sa labas ng korte, na isinumpaan at maaaring gamitin bilang ebidensya; ang proseso ng pag-aalis sa isang tao mula sa isang mahalagang posisyon o kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: This is a very formal word. In law, it's that pre-game interview where lawyers grill a witness before the actual court trial. Think of those intense scenes in 'Suits' or 'How to Get Away with Murder.' It can also mean getting kicked out of power, like a CEO getting fired or a president being ousted. High-level drama.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong legal o politikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ang **deposisyon** ng saksi bilang matibay na ebidensya sa korte.","translation":"The witness's **deposition** was used as strong evidence in court."},{"sentence":"Ang **deposisyon** ng hari ay nagdulot ng malaking kaguluhan sa kaharian.","translation":"The **deposition** of the king caused great chaos in the kingdom."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagkakaroon ng lakas ng loob na harapin ang panganib, takot, o hirap.
original_explanation: This is that 'Bahala na si Batman' energy you channel when you're about to confess to your crush, ask for a raise, or eat the last piece of chicken in front of your siblings. It's your inner Darna or Captain Barbell coming out.
usage_notes: While primarily meaning courage, it can also refer to the strength or potency of something, like coffee or liquor ('tapang ng kape').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **tapang** sa pagharap sa mga pagsubok.","translation":"He showed his **bravery** in facing the challenges."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matinding **tapang** para aminin ang pagkakamali.","translation":"It takes great **courage** to admit a mistake."}]
