original_explanation: What your dad yells when you're learning to drive and you treat the gas pedal like a mortal enemy. It's the "chill lang" version for speed. Also applicable to your spending habits after payday: "Kailangan ko nang magmenor sa gastos."
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of driving, but can be used metaphorically for other activities like spending, working, or even talking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magmenor** kapag malapit ka na sa eskwelahan.","translation":"You need to **slow down** when you are near a school."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng doktor, dapat daw akong **magmenor** sa trabaho para hindi ma-stress.","translation":"The doctor said I should **slow down** at work to avoid stress."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sapilitang pagpapatapon o pagpapaalis sa isang tao mula sa sariling bayan o lugar bilang parusa.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'cancel culture' of the old world. It's when you're kicked out of your homeland, like what happened to Rizal in Dapitan. Today, it's what you feel when your family group chat kicks you out for sending too many memes. A state of being unwanted and far from home.
usage_notes: Primarily a historical and legal term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinatulan si Jose Rizal ng **destiyero** sa Dapitan.","translation":"Jose Rizal was sentenced to **exile** in Dapitan."}]

translation: to have something knocked over, to cause to fall
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng pagbagsak o pagkatumba ng isang bagay o tao.
etymology: From `magpa-` (causative prefix) + `tumba` (to fall, to be knocked over).
original_explanation: This is what you do in a bowling alley. You `magpatumba` the pins. It can also be more sinister, like in action movies where the boss orders his goons to `magpatumba` an opponent. Or it could be your cat's favorite hobby with everything on your desk.
usage_notes: Can refer to inanimate objects (like trees or bowling pins) or, in colloquial and sometimes sinister contexts, to people (to have someone defeated or even killed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-arkila sila ng mga tao para **magpatumba** ng mga lumang puno.","translation":"They hired people to **have the old trees knocked over**."},{"sentence":"Sa huling \"frame\", kailangan niyang **magpatumba** ng sampung \"pins\".","translation":"In the last frame, he needs to **knock over** ten pins."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking magalang, maginoo, at may marangal na pag-uugali, lalo na sa mga kababaihan. Sa kasaysayan, tumutukoy din ito sa isang mandirigmang nakakabayo.
original_explanation: The OG 'sana all' guy from the Spanish era. Today's kabalyero isn't on a horse, he's the one who holds the door for you, offers his seat on the MRT, and doesn't ghost you after three dates. He's the guy your lola wishes you'd bring home.
usage_notes: Often used to describe old-fashioned chivalry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang tunay na **kabalyero** si Lolo, palagi niyang pinagbubuksan ng pinto si Lola.","translation":"Grandpa is a true **gentleman**; he always opens the door for Grandma."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marka, disenyo, o salita na nilikha sa pamamagitan ng pag-alis ng bahagi ng ibabaw ng isang matigas na materyal tulad ng kahoy, bato, o metal.
original_explanation: Before tattoos became mainstream, this was the OG way to make something permanent. Think of the names carved on a tree by young lovers, the intricate designs on a baul ng lola, or that 'I was here' message on a university desk. It's a mark that's meant to last, much like the memory of your first heartbreak. Hugot!
usage_notes: Can be literal (carving on wood) or metaphorical (etched in memory).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **ukit** sa lumang silya na gawa sa narra.","translation":"The **carving** on the old chair made of narra is beautiful."}]

translation: act of inserting, tucking in, stuffing
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay o pagpapasok ng isang bagay sa isang masikip na espasyo.
original_explanation: It's how you fit one last piece of pasalubong into an already overflowing balikbayan box. It's tucking your shirt in to look presentable for a job interview. It's also what you do with that P1000 bill in your wallet, hiding it deep so you won't be tempted to spend it. Pagsusuksok is the art of fitting things where they seemingly don't belong.
usage_notes: Can also imply hiding something by inserting it into a crevice or pocket.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tamang **pagsusuksok** ng damit sa maleta ay makakatipid ng espasyo.","translation":"The proper **stuffing** of clothes into the suitcase will save space."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang kanyang **pagsusuksok** ng pera sa medyas.","translation":"I saw his **act of tucking** money into his sock."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong mas matanda, mas mataas sa ranggo o katungkulan, o nasa huling taon ng pag-aaral. Ginagamit din para sa mga 'senior citizen'.
original_explanation: Can mean three things: 1) The 'kuya' or 'ate' in your org or office you have to respect. 2) The student who's almost free from high school or college, busy with thesis and grad pics. 3) Your lolo or lola who gets a 20% discount at restaurants. 'Respect your seniors!' applies to all three.
usage_notes: Used in contexts like school ('senior high'), work ('senior manager'), and for the elderly ('senior citizen'). Can also function as a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **senior** sa kumpanya, tungkulin niyang gabayan ang mga bago.","translation":"As a **senior** in the company, it's his duty to guide the new ones."},{"sentence":"May diskwento ang mga **senior** citizen sa sinehan.","translation":"**Senior** citizens have a discount at the cinema."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nagsasagawa ng pagpaparusa sa sarili, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng paghagupit sa katawan, bilang isang anyo ng relihiyosong debosyon o penitensiya.
original_explanation: The guys you see on TV during Holy Week, whipping their backs until they bleed. It's an extreme form of 'penitensya' (penance) that's a big, and sometimes controversial, part of Filipino Catholic tradition. It's a level of devotion that makes your yearly Visita Iglesia look like a casual stroll.
usage_notes: Primarily used during discussions of Holy Week (Mahal na Araw) traditions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Daan-daang **plahelante** ang lumahok sa prusisyon sa Pampanga.","translation":"Hundreds of **flagellants** participated in the procession in Pampanga."},{"sentence":"Isang malalim na pananampalataya ang nag-uudyok sa mga **plahelante** na gawin ang kanilang panata.","translation":"A deep faith motivates the **flagellants** to fulfill their vow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na gusali o silid na nakalaan para sa pagsamba, na maaaring nakahiwalay o bahagi ng isang mas malaking institusyon tulad ng simbahan, paaralan, o ospital.
original_explanation: The mini-me version of a church. It's that small, quiet place you find in a mall, hospital, or even an airport for a quick prayer. It's the "chapel" in "Sistine Chapel" but usually, it's just a simple room with some pews and a crucifix.
usage_notes: Mas maliit kaysa sa 'simbahan' (church) o 'parokya' (parish).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdaos ng isang munting seremonya sa **kapilya** ng unibersidad.","translation":"A small ceremony was held at the university's **chapel**."},{"sentence":"Tuwing may burol, dinadala muna ang kabaong sa **kapilya** bago ilibing.","translation":"During a wake, the coffin is first brought to the **chapel** before the burial."}]

translation: to join in all together; to participate simultaneously
meaning_filipino: Sama-samang lumahok o pumasok sa isang gawain, laro, o grupo.
original_explanation: Picture a 'pabitin' at a kid's party. When the host yells "Go!", everyone dives in at once. That's magsalihan. It's the chaotic, simultaneous joining of a group. It's when a new GC is created and everyone adds their friends, or when a company announces a voluntary resignation program and people start signing up en masse. It’s a group action of joining.
usage_notes: Implies a plural or collective subject, where multiple people are joining at the same time or into the same thing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang magsimula ang palaro, nag-**magsalihan** na ang mga bata.","translation":"When the game started, the children all **joined in together**."},{"sentence":"Bukas ang pagpapatala, kaya't **magsalihan** na kayo sa ating team building!","translation":"Registration is open, so you should all **participate** in our team building!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anak o inakay ng pato.
original_explanation: A baby duck. The star of every 'Make Way for Ducklings' story. They're cute, fluffy, and follow their mom in a perfect line, unlike you and your siblings trying to navigate a crowded mall.
usage_notes: 'Bibe' is another common word for duck, so 'sisiw na bibe' is also correct and frequently used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **sisiw na pato** ay sumusunod sa kanilang ina papunta sa lawa.","translation":"The **ducklings** are following their mother to the lake."},{"sentence":"Mukha kang basang **sisiw na pato**!","translation":"You look like a wet **duckling**! (Figurative, similar to 'drowned rat')."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng biglaan at hindi mapigilang pagbuga ng hangin mula sa ilong at bibig na sanhi ng iritasyon sa loob ng ilong. Ito ay nasa panahunang panghinaharap.
etymology: From English 'achoo' or Spanish '¡Achís!'. The word is onomatopoeic.
original_explanation: The future tense of that explosive 'Achoo!' moment. It's the feeling you get when dust attacks your nose or when someone talks about you, according to old superstitions. 'Takpan mo ang bibig mo kapag maghahatsing ka,' is what your mom has been telling you since forever, and it's even more relevant in the post-pandemic world.
usage_notes: Future tense of maghatsing or humatsing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niyang **maghahatsing** siya kaya agad siyang kumuha ng panyo.","translation":"He felt that he **was going to sneeze** so he immediately got a handkerchief."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa alikabok, siguradong **maghahatsing** ako mamaya.","translation":"Because of the dust, I'm sure I **will sneeze** later."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tapat na mamimili o parokyano na palaging bumibili o tumatangkilik sa isang partikular na tindahan o nagbebenta.
etymology: From Hokkien Chinese 熟客 (si̍k-kheh), meaning "familiar guest" or "regular customer".
original_explanation: Your 'suki' is your go-to person at the palengke who gives you the freshest fish, the best price, and the latest chismis. It's a two-way relationship: you're their loyal customer, and they're your trusted vendor. In the modern world, your 'suki' could be your favorite coffee shop where they know your order by heart, or your Grab driver who you always get matched with. "Suki, tawad naman!" is the national anthem of market-goers.
usage_notes: This term is central to Filipino market culture and implies a relationship of trust and mutual benefit between a buyer and a seller.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May diskwento ka kasi **suki** kita.","translation":"You get a discount because you're my **loyal customer**."},{"sentence":"Pumunta ako sa **suki** kong manikyurista para magpa-ayos ng kuko.","translation":"I went to my **regular** manicurist to get my nails done."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sama-samang pagbubuklod o pag-iisa ng maraming elemento, grupo, o puwersa para sa isang layunin.
original_explanation: This is `magsanib` on steroids. It's not just two things joining, it's a whole barangay, a whole team, or all the Avengers assembling. When everyone decides to **magsanib-sanib** for a community pantry or a group project, that's Filipino bayanihan spirit in action.
usage_notes: The repetition 'sanib-sanib' implies multiple entities joining together, emphasizing plurality and collective action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magsanib-sanib** ng lakas upang malampasan ang krisis na ito.","translation":"We need to **combine forces** to overcome this crisis."},{"sentence":"Ang mga maliliit na negosyante ay nagplanong **magsanib-sanib** upang labanan ang malaking korporasyon.","translation":"The small entrepreneurs planned to **join together** to fight the large corporation."}]

meaning_filipino: Husto, wasto, at walang labis o kulang; tumpak sa sukat, bilang, o detalye.
original_explanation: That moment when you give the jeepney driver 20 pesos for a 10 peso fare and he gives you exactly 10 pesos back. No more, no less. "Salamat, manong, iksakto!" Also, when your chismosa friend recounts a story with perfect, unwavering detail.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'sakto'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan niya ako ng **iksakto**ng bayad.","translation":"He gave me the **exact** payment."},{"sentence":"Dumating siya sa **iksakto**ng alas-otso ng umaga.","translation":"He arrived at **exactly** eight in the morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pinakamataas na papuri, parangal, at pagsamba sa isang tao, bagay, o lalo na sa Diyos.
original_explanation: To hype someone up, but make it ✨divine✨. This isn't just saying "Galing!" (Great!). This is the level of praise you give to God, your nation, or the person who invented air conditioning. It's to put something or someone on the highest pedestal. "Let's all luwalhatiin the inventor of unli-rice."
usage_notes: A very formal and often religious term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **luwalhatiin** ang Panginoon sa lahat ng Kanyang mga biyaya.","translation":"We should **glorify** the Lord for all His blessings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagdurog ng isang bagay upang maging pino sa pamamagitan ng isang gilingan o katulad na kagamitan.
original_explanation: What you do to your coffee beans before a long shift, or what your boss does to your soul with endless revisions. 'Pa-gilingin mo na 'yang karne para sa Menudo' also applies to your patience by the end of the week.
usage_notes: This is a transitive verb, requiring an object to be ground.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **gilingin** nang pino ang mga mani para sa kare-kare.","translation":"You need **to grind** the peanuts finely for the kare-kare."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **gilingin** ang paminta.","translation":"Don't **grind** the pepper too much."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na lima (5) na dinugtungan ng pang-angkop na '-ng', ginagamit bilang panuring sa isang pangngalan.
original_explanation: The number 5, but with its 'plus one'—the linker 'ng'. You use it before a noun, like "limang piso" when you're paying for candy, or "limang minuto pa" when you're definitely not ready yet. It’s ‘lima’ in a committed relationship with the next word.
usage_notes: This is the number 'lima' (five) combined with the linker '-ng'. It is used before a noun, especially one that starts with a vowel, w, or y.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng **limang** mansanas.","translation":"Give me **five** apples."},{"sentence":"Mayroon akong **limang** alagang aso.","translation":"I have **five** pet dogs."}]

translation: to intentionally lose; to concede defeat
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagpayag na matalo o magapi sa isang kumpetisyon, laro, o argumento.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'big-brother' move when you let your younger sibling win in a video game to stop them from crying. In hugot terms, it's giving up on an argument not because you're wrong, but because you value your peace of mind more. 'Pagod na ako, kaya magpapatalo na lang ako.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madalas siyang **nagpapatalo** sa chess kapag ang kalaro niya ay ang kanyang apo.","translation":"He often **intentionally loses** in chess when his grandchild is his opponent."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpatalo** sa kanila; ipaglaban mo ang tama.","translation":"Don't **let them defeat you**; fight for what is right."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tindahan kung saan gumagawa at nagbebenta ng mga matatamis na pagkain tulad ng keyk, tinapay, at iba pang mga hinurnong produkto.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "pastelería" (tindahan ng pastelerya).
original_explanation: The mothership of all things matamis! Dito ka bibili ng birthday cake, ng pandesal sa umaga, at ng ensaymada para sa meryenda. Amoy pa lang sa labas, alam mo nang mapapagastos ka. Para siyang heaven for people with a sweet tooth.
usage_notes: Ginagamit nang palitan kasama ng "bakeshop" o "bakery". Ang "pastelerya" ay may bahagyang mas mataas na antas o tradisyonal na konotasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng cake sa **pastelerya** para sa kaarawan mo.","translation":"I bought a cake at the **pastry shop** for your birthday."},{"sentence":"May bagong bukas na **pastelerya** sa kanto.","translation":"There's a newly opened **bakeshop** on the corner."}]

meaning_filipino: May amoy na katulad ng sa maruming kanal o imburnal; tumutukoy sa isang napakabahong amoy.
etymology: Tambalang salita: 'amoy' (smell) + 'imburnal' (sewer, mula sa Espanyol na 'embornal').
original_explanation: The smell of Metro Manila during a flood. It's that uniquely pungent, gag-inducing odor from a clogged canal or an open manhole. If someone says your breath is 'amoy-imburnal,' it's not a suggestion to get a mint; it's a command to see a doctor. It’s the superlative form of ‘mabaho’.
usage_notes: Isang napakatindi at negatibong panlarawan para sa isang amoy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwanang bukas ang basurahan, magkakaroon ng **amoy-imburnal** sa kusina.","translation":"Don't leave the trash can open, it will start to **smell like a sewer** in the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Pag-ahon niya sa baha, damit niya'y **amoy-imburnal**.","translation":"When he emerged from the flood, his clothes **smelled of the sewer**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagpapakita o pagiging hayag ng isang bagay na dati'y nakatago, hindi nakikita, o wala.
original_explanation: 'Yung friend mong bigla na lang lumitaw sa party kahit sabi niya 'di siya pupunta. O 'yung pimple na biglang lumitaw sa ilong mo a day before a big date. It's the act of something suddenly becoming visible or present. The classic 'sana all' moment when your Grab driver finally lumitaw on the map after being MIA for 10 minutes.
usage_notes: A very common verb used for things appearing, people showing up, or facts coming to light.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **lumitaw** ang araw pagkatapos ng malakas na ulan.","translation":"The sun suddenly **appeared** after the heavy rain."},{"sentence":"**Lumitaw** din ang katotohanan sa huli.","translation":"The truth finally **emerged** in the end."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang lasa o kulang sa lasa, lalo na sa alat o tamis.
original_explanation: Parang pagkain sa ospital o 'yung luto ng ka-team mo na takot sa asin. It's the culinary equivalent of a boring conversation. The kind of food that makes you say, 'Tubig na lang, please.'
usage_notes: Refers to food or drinks lacking expected flavor. It is a homograph of 'matabâ' (fat), which has a different stress and final vowel sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **matabang** ang sabaw dahil nakalimutan niyang lagyan ng patis.","translation":"The soup became **bland** because she forgot to add fish sauce."},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **matabang** ang kape kung walang asukal.","translation":"For me, coffee is **tasteless** without sugar."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang utos na humihiling o nag-uutos sa isang tao o grupo na huminto sa pag-iingay o pagsasalita.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino parent/teacher weapon. Can range from a gentle 'ssshhh, tumahimik na kayo' in a library, to a thunderous '**TUMAHIMIK!**' that can stop a rampaging carabao. The tone is everything. It's the verbal equivalent of a mute button you wish you had for real life.
usage_notes: This is the command form of the verb 'tumahimik'. The exclamation point is crucial for its function as a command. The plural form is 'Tumahimik kayo!'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumahimik!** May natutulog!","translation":"**Be quiet!** Someone is sleeping!"},{"sentence":"Sabi ng guro, '**Tumahimik** kayo kung ayaw ninyong mapalabas!'","translation":"The teacher said, '**Be quiet** if you don't want to be sent out!'"}]

translation: stinky, foul-smelling (like stagnant water or urine)
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa masangsang at hindi kaaya-ayang amoy, partikular na ang amoy ng ihi o ng maruming tubig na hindi umaagos.
original_explanation: That specific, sharp, nasty smell of a public CR that hasn't been cleaned, or an alleyway used as a public urinal. It's not just 'mabaho' (smelly); it's a specific kind of pungent funk. It's the smell that makes you hold your breath and walk faster.
usage_notes: Distinct from 'baho' (general bad smell), 'anghit' (body odor), or 'panis' (spoiled food smell). 'Mabantot' is the more common adjectival form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Amoy **bantot** ang eskinita dahil maraming umiihi roon.","translation":"The alley smells **stinky** because many people urinate there."},{"sentence":"Linisin mo ang kulungan ng aso, nag-aamoy **bantot** na.","translation":"Clean the dog's cage, it's starting to smell **foul**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa posisyong baligtad; ang itaas ay nasa ibaba at ang ibaba ay nasa itaas.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na pagkatapos mong magbayad ng bills, 'yung wallet mo nakatiwarik na. Or 'yung mundo mo, nung nalaman mong may "seen" pero walang "reply". It's the state of being completely flipped over, whether it's a car, your finances, or your life choices.
usage_notes: Often used to describe something physically inverted or a situation that has gone completely wrong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan nilang **nakatiwarik** ang sasakyan sa bangin.","translation":"They found the car **upside down** in the ravine."},{"sentence":"**Nakatiwarik** ang buong bahay pagkatapos dumaan ang mga bata.","translation":"The whole house was **topsy-turvy** after the kids passed through."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, sitwasyon, o tao na nangangailangan ng maingat na paghawak o pagtrato; maselan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung state of being na 'bawal masagi, bawal magkamali.' Parang 'yung balat ng baby, 'yung bagong-luto na leche flan, o 'yung feelings ng kaibigan mong kaka-break lang. Handle with care dapat ang peg. Pwede ring tumukoy sa taong pihikan sa pagkain o gamit.
usage_notes: Ang mas karaniwang anyo nito ay 'maselan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **selan** na usapin ang dapat nilang pag-usapan.","translation":"They have to discuss a **delicate** matter."},{"sentence":"May **selan** siyang tiyan kaya hindi siya kumakain ng kung anu-ano.","translation":"She has a **sensitive** stomach so she doesn't just eat anything."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at solido na anyo ng gamot na karaniwang bilog o habilog at nilulunok.
original_explanation: The small thing you have to swallow when you have a headache, fever, or any kind of sickness. Comes in all shapes and colors. Your lola probably has a whole collection of these for her 'maintenance' meds. Not to be confused with the electronic 'tablet'!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uminom ka na ng **tabletas** para sa sakit ng ulo mo.","translation":"Take a **pill** for your headache."},{"sentence":"Inireseta ng doktor ang tatlong uri ng **tabletas**.","translation":"The doctor prescribed three kinds of **tablets**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makabagong ekspresyon na tumutukoy sa estado ng pagkaubos ng enerhiya, pasensya, o gana para sa pakikisalamuha sa ibang tao.
etymology: A Taglish calque from the English 'low social battery', combining Tagalog slang 'lowbat' (from 'low battery') and English 'social battery'.
original_explanation: The official feeling of introverts after 30 minutes at a party. Ito 'yung moment na gusto mo na lang mag-transform into a potted plant sa isang sulok. When your 'people-ing' capacity is at 1% and you need to recharge by being alone, watching Netflix, and not talking to anyone for 6-8 business days.
usage_notes: A very popular slang term among millennials and Gen Z, especially online.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sorry, uuna na ako umuwi, **lowbat social battery** na talaga ako.","translation":"Sorry, I'll go home ahead, my **social battery is really low**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng me-time. Grabe, **lowbat social battery** ko pagkatapos ng family reunion.","translation":"I need some me-time. Wow, my **social battery is so low** after the family reunion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang set o pares ng kasuotan na magkatugma ang tela, kulay, o disenyo, tulad ng amerikana at pantalon, o ng baro't saya.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "terno" (set of three, suit).
original_explanation: This is your go-to 'pang-ninong/ninang' outfit for a binyag or kasal. It's when your top matches your bottom perfectly. Pwede ring pang-girl group/boy band, para 'aesthetic' tingnan. 'Uy, naka-terno tayo today!'
usage_notes: Can refer to a formal suit (amerikana), a traditional Filipiniana dress (often with butterfly sleeves), or any casual matching top and bottom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng suot niyang puting **terno** sa kasal.","translation":"Her white **matching outfit** at the wedding is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng bagong **terno** na pantulog.","translation":"I bought a new **matching set** of pajamas."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng paggaling mula sa sakit o pagbuti ng isang kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is the verb for whatever makes you feel better. It could be the paracetamol for your headache, a bowl of 'lugaw' when you're sick, or just getting a good night's sleep after a stressful week. 'Inom ka ng gamot, 'yan ang ikagagaling mo.' (Take your medicine, that will cause your recovery.)
usage_notes: Specifically refers to recovery from illness or the improvement of a negative condition. Not to be confused with the root 'galing' which means excellence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang masustansyang pagkain at sapat na pahinga ang **ikagagaling** mo.","translation":"Nutritious food and adequate rest will **cause your recovery**."},{"sentence":"**Ikinagaling** ng pasyente ang bagong gamot na ibinigay sa kanya.","translation":"The new medicine given to the patient **caused his improvement**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi pa hinog o wala pa sa hustong gulang. Ginagamit para sa mga prutas o, sa matalinghagang paraan, sa isang taong bata pa at kulang pa sa karanasan.
original_explanation: Unripe. That green mango that's so sour it makes your whole face scrunch up. Also, your younger sibling who thinks they know everything but still asks you for money. When someone says, 'Bubot ka pa,' it's the slightly condescending way of saying, 'You're still a kid, you have no idea what you're talking about.'
usage_notes: Can be used literally for fruits and vegetables or figuratively for people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maasim pa ang mangga dahil **bubot** pa.","translation":"The mango is still sour because it's still **unripe**."},{"sentence":"Masyado ka pang **bubot** para sa ganyang klaseng responsibilidad.","translation":"You're still too **immature** for that kind of responsibility."}]

meaning_filipino: Isinagawa sa paraan ng pagbibiro; hindi seryoso o walang intensyong manakit.
original_explanation: The disclaimer you use after saying something savage. 'Uy, pabiro lang!' is the Pinoy equivalent of 'Just kidding!' It's how you test the waters with a risky joke or soften a harsh truth. Use it wisely, or you'll end up saying 'Sorry na' instead.
usage_notes: Often used as a way to soften a statement that might be taken offensively.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabi niya iyon nang **pabiro**, kaya huwag mong dibdibin.","translation":"He said that **jokingly**, so don't take it to heart."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa kanya, **pabiro** lang ang lahat ng sinasabi niya.","translation":"Don't believe him, everything he says is just **in jest**."}]

translation: in groups of three; three at a time
meaning_filipino: Sa paraan ng pagpapangkat na may tigatlong miyembro o piraso sa bawat grupo; tigatlo.
etymology: Reduplication of the first two syllables of 'tatlo'.
original_explanation: This is how you distribute things when you're being super organized (or passive-aggressive). 'Kunin niyo 'yan nang **tatlu-tatlo**,' says the teacher distributing handouts, meaning 'take three each' or 'get them in groups of three'. It implies distribution or arrangement, unlike 'tatluhan' which can just be a static group.
usage_notes: Emphasizes distribution or arrangement into groups of three. Often used with the word 'nang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinigay niya ang mga tsokolate nang **tatlu-tatlo**.","translation":"He gave out the chocolates **three at a time**."},{"sentence":"Pumasok sila sa sinehan nang **tatlu-tatlo**.","translation":"They entered the cinema **in groups of three**."}]

translation: to entrust; to yield; to give way
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng karapatan, responsibilidad, o desisyon sa iba; ang hindi pagpilit sa sariling kagustuhan at pagpayag sa nais ng kapwa.
etymology: From `magpa-` (permissive prefix) + `ubaya` (entrusting, leaving to someone else).
original_explanation: The ultimate "bahala ka na" or "sige, sa'yo na" move. It’s when you're arguing about where to eat and you finally give up: "Kayo na ang bahala, **nagpapaubaya** na ako." (You guys decide, I'm yielding.) It can also be a major "hugot" word, like when you let go of someone you love for their own happiness. #Martyr
usage_notes: Carries a sense of concession, trust, or sometimes, resignation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagod, nagpasya siyang **magpaubaya** na lang sa desisyon ng nakararami.","translation":"Because of fatigue, he decided to just **yield** to the majority's decision."},{"sentence":"Sa Diyos na lang ako **magpapaubaya** ng aking kinabukasan.","translation":"I will just **entrust** my future to God."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagputol o pagkaputol ng isang bagay na manipis at mahaba tulad ng tali, sinulid, o pisi.
original_explanation: This is the state of your last nerve during a toxic client call. Or when your cheap earphones finally give up on life. 'Konting-konti na lang, malalagot na ang pasensya ko!' is the national anthem of anyone stuck in EDSA traffic. It's the breaking point.
usage_notes: Commonly used for strings, ropes, threads, and metaphorically for patience or a connection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang gitara, baka **malagot** ang mga kuwerdas.","translation":"Be careful with the guitar, the strings might **snap**."},{"sentence":"Kapag hindi ka tumigil, **malalagot** na talaga ang pasensya ko sa'yo.","translation":"If you don't stop, my patience will really **break**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang masarap o kaakit-akit sa paningin na nagdudulot ng pagnanasang matikman o kainin ito.
etymology: From `takam` (craving, greed for food), reduplicated with the prefix `ka-` to form an adjective meaning 'causing the state of takam'.
original_explanation: The highest praise you can give to food just by looking at it. It's what you say when you see crispy pata with the skin glistening, a halo-halo overflowing with ingredients, or a perfectly grilled liempo. It’s the feeling that makes you drool and say "Penge!" even if you're not hungry. Food that is "katakam-takam" is an automatic star on your Instagram story.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used for food. Can be used metaphorically for something very desirable, but this is rare.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-post siya ng litrato ng **katakam-takam** na lechon sa Facebook.","translation":"She posted a picture of a **mouth-watering** roasted pig on Facebook."},{"sentence":"Ang amoy pa lang ng inihaw na manok ay **katakam-takam** na.","translation":"Just the smell of the grilled chicken is already **delectable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuka ng bibig nang malaki at paghinga nang malalim bilang tanda ng matinding pagkaantok, pagod, o pagkabagot.
original_explanation: This is the level-up version of a yawn. Hindi lang basta hikab, kundi maghigab na parang leon sa zoo. Usually nangyayari 'to 'pag sobrang boring ng meeting o 'pag puyat ka sa ka-scroll sa TikTok.
usage_notes: 'Higab' is a more forceful or wider yawn compared to the more common 'hikab'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maghigab** nang walang takip ang bibig, bastos tingnan.","translation":"Don't **yawn widely** without covering your mouth, it looks rude."},{"sentence":"Napansin ng lahat ang kanyang malakas na pag-**maghigab** sa kalagitnaan ng seminar.","translation":"Everyone noticed his loud **wide yawn** in the middle of the seminar."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng korona o putong na isinusuot sa ulo bilang sagisag ng kapangyarihan, karangalan, o pagkahari.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol 'diadema', mula sa Latin 'diadēma', mula sa Griyego 'diádēma'.
original_explanation: The OG 'crown' before Catriona Gray made the Mikimoto famous. It's the accessory of choice for queens, princesses, and debutantes who want to feel royal for a day. Think Wonder Woman's headband, but make it sparkly.
usage_notes: Isang pormal o pampanitikang salita. Ang 'korona' ay mas karaniwan, habang ang 'tiara' ay madalas ding gamitin bilang hiram na salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang reyna ay may suot na gintong **diadema** na puno ng diyamante.","translation":"The queen wore a golden **diadem** full of diamonds."},{"sentence":"Ipinatong ng prinsipe ang **diadema** sa ulo ng kanyang napupusuan.","translation":"The prince placed the **tiara** on the head of his beloved."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-asal na parang isang panginoon; pagpapakita ng kapangyarihan o pagiging dominante sa iba sa paraang mapagmataas.
original_explanation: This is that boss or tita who acts like they own you and everyone around them. They expect you to serve them hand and foot, parang nasa hacienda lang. It's the verb form of being a 'señorito' or 'señorita'.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of arrogance and entitlement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ng mga empleyado sa bagong manager dahil mahilig itong **mamanginoon** sa kanila.","translation":"The employees dislike the new manager because he likes to **lord over** them."},{"sentence":"Simula nang yumaman siya, nagsimula na siyang **mamanginoon** sa kanyang mga dating kaibigan.","translation":"Since he became rich, he started to **act like a lord** towards his old friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghinga paloob, partikular na ang pag-amoy ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: That first **langhap** of coffee in the morning that tells your brain, "Okay, kaya natin 'to." Or the **langhap** of fresh pan de sal from the local bakery. It’s that single, satisfying sniff that can either make your day or make you realize someone's cooking tuyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **langhap** lang ng simoy ng hangin sa probinsya, nawala na ang pagod ko.","translation":"Just one **whiff** of the provincial air, and my tiredness was gone."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng **langhap** ng bagong lutong adobo.","translation":"The **scent** of newly cooked adobo is so good."}]

translation: state of being overturned; state of being face down
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakabaligtad, nakataob, o nakasubsob.
original_explanation: This is that 'faceplant' moment, literally or figuratively. Like when your bangka flips over during an island hopping tour, or when your business plan gets completely upended by a new competitor. It's the state of being upside down and probably a little disoriented.
usage_notes: Often used for objects like boats, cups, or containers that have been turned upside down. Can also be used metaphorically for a defeat or a major setback.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat sa biglaang **pagkakataob** ng bangka sa gitna ng dagat.","translation":"Everyone was shocked by the sudden **overturning** of the boat in the middle of the sea."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakataob** ng baso ay nagdulot ng malaking mantsa sa puting mantel.","translation":"The **state of being overturned** of the glass caused a large stain on the white tablecloth."}]

translation: to become impoverished; to live in extreme poverty
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang matinding kahirapan o kasalatan sa mga pangunahing pangangailangan sa buhay.
original_explanation: This is a deep, classic Tagalog word for being broke, but on a whole other level. Hindi lang 'petsa de peligro'. Ito 'yung state na you're struggling to make ends meet, 'isang kahig, isang tuka'. It's the reality many face, a struggle to get by.
usage_notes: A formal and literary term for experiencing destitution. It implies a state of being, not just a temporary lack of money.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang lalong nag-**maghikahos** dahil sa pandemya.","translation":"Many families **became more impoverished** because of the pandemic."},{"sentence":"Nang pumanaw ang kanilang ama, nagsimulang **maghikahos** ang kanilang pamilya.","translation":"When their father passed away, their family began to **live in extreme poverty**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isa pang baryasyon ng 'shuta' sa swardspeak, na may katulad na gamit sa pagpapahayag ng matinding emosyon tulad ng pagkagulat o pagkadismaya.
etymology: From swardspeak (gayspeak), another embellished form of 'shuta'.
original_explanation: Another flavor of 'shuta' from the Beki Language Institute. Think of 'shuta' as the original, 'shutabels' as the deluxe version, and 'shutacca' as the limited edition with a different flavor profile. It's all about the ✨ a e s t h e t i c ✨ of the word.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with 'shuta' and 'shutabels' but might be perceived as more niche or 'deeper' gayspeak by some.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Shutacca**, ang ganda ng boses niya!","translation":"**Damn**, her voice is beautiful!"},{"sentence":"Nawala ko 'yung susi. **Shutacca** naman o!","translation":"I lost the key. **Damn it**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na ginagamit upang takpan o sarhan ang isang butas, siwang, o puwang.
etymology: From `paN-` + `pasak`. `Pasak` means plug or wedge. The prefix `paN-` (`pam-` before 'p') indicates the tool or material used for the action.
original_explanation: That thing you use to stop a leak. Could be a cork for a bottle, the 'pasador' for a leaky roof, or even the lumpia you stuff in your mouth to stop yourself from saying something you'll regret. It's a filler, a plug, a temporary (or permanent) solution to a hole.
usage_notes: Can be literal (a physical plug) or figurative (a temporary substitute). See also 'pamasak-butas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng lumang basahan bilang **pamasak** sa butas ng tubo.","translation":"He used an old rag as a **plug** for the hole in the pipe."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **pamasak** para sa lababo.","translation":"I need a **stopper** for the sink."}]

translation: to be scolded; to be told off
meaning_filipino: Maging paksa ng galit o sermon mula sa ibang tao; mapagalitan.
original_explanation: The receiving end of "makagalit." This is what happens after you break your mom's favorite vase, or you come home past your curfew. It's the "sermon" part of the program. "Uwi na 'ko, baka makagalitan pa ako ni Mama."
usage_notes: This is a passive form, where the subject of the sentence is the one being scolded. The actor (the one scolding) is usually introduced by "ng" or "ni".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **makagalitan** ng kanyang guro kaya nag-aral siya nang mabuti.","translation":"He didn't want to **be scolded** by his teacher, so he studied well."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay at baka **makagalitan** tayo.","translation":"Don't be noisy or we might **get told off**."}]

translation: to fight with; to compete against
meaning_filipino: Ang pakikipagtunggali, pakikipag-away, o pakikipagsapalaran laban sa isang kalaban, hamon, o pagsubok.
etymology: From 'makipag-' (to mutually do something) and 'laban' (fight, against).
original_explanation: This isn't just about physical fights (suntukan). It's fighting for your rights, fighting for the last seat on the bus, fighting for a promotion, or fighting the urge to eat another piece of lechon. It's the verb for every struggle, big or small. The battle is real, 'ika nga.
usage_notes: Can be literal (physical fight) or figurative (struggle, competition).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Handa siyang **makipaglaban** para sa kanyang mga karapatan.","translation":"She is ready to **fight** for her rights."},{"sentence":"Ang pambansang kamao ay nakatakdang **makipaglaban** sa Las Vegas.","translation":"The national fist (Manny Pacquiao) is scheduled to **compete** in Las Vegas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkawala ng gana, sigla, o pagnanais na ipagpatuloy ang isang gawain, relasyon, o pag-aaral sa isang paksa.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung nangyayari sa second week of January sa New Year's resolution mo na mag-gym. Or 'yung feeling after binge-watching 3 seasons of a series in one weekend. You were so into it, and then suddenly... meh. The spark is gone. It's the "ghosting" phase of a hobby or a crush.
usage_notes: A very common phrase used to describe a shift in personal feelings or motivation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **mawalan ng interes** sa kurso niya noong ikatlong taon niya sa kolehiyo.","translation":"He started to **lose interest** in his course during his third year in college."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang tumigil sa panliligaw, baka **mawalan ng interes** sa iyo ang nililigawan mo.","translation":"Don't stop courting her, the one you're courting might **lose interest** in you."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na sumasaklaw o nauugnay sa buong sansinukob o sa lahat ng tao at bagay sa mundo.
etymology: From 'sansinukob' (universe) and the prefix 'pan-' (relating to the whole).
original_explanation: This is 'level: universe' kind of stuff. When your hugot is no longer just about your ex, but about the very nature of love and existence itself, that's 'pansansinukob'. It's the 'Miss Universe' answer that talks about world peace. It's that feeling you get when you look at the stars and realize how small your problems (and your data allowance) are.
usage_notes: A very formal and somewhat poetic word. Not used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ay isang damdaming **pansansinukob**.","translation":"Love is a **universal** feeling."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentipiko ang mga batas na **pansansinukob**.","translation":"Scientists study the **cosmic** laws."}]

translation: remoteness; the quality of being far
meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging nasa malaking distansya o agwat mula sa isang tiyak na lugar o punto.
original_explanation: This is the feeling when you're in an LDR (Long-Distance Relationship) and you check Google Maps to see the distance between you and bae. It’s the "ang layo!" complaint when your Grab driver's pin is on the other side of EDSA during rush hour. It’s the very essence of provincial life for a city-dweller.
usage_notes: The hyphen is sometimes used to emphasize the two parts of the word, but `pagkamalayo` is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi naging hadlang ang **pagka-malayo** ng kanilang mga tirahan sa kanilang pagkakaibigan.","translation":"The **remoteness** of their homes was not a hindrance to their friendship."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagka-malayo** ng isla, bihira itong mabisita ng mga turista.","translation":"Because of the island's **remoteness**, it is rarely visited by tourists."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng masamang hangarin, balak, o intensyon na makasakit o makapinsala sa kapwa.
original_explanation: When someone gives you a compliment that feels like an insult ('Wow, ang taba mo ngayon, good health ah!'). That's a comment na 'may-malisya'. It's the green-minded tito's joke that isn't really funny, or a co-worker's 'helpful' suggestion that's actually designed to make you look bad. It's the hidden 'daga sa dibdib'.
usage_notes: Describes actions, words, or thoughts that have a hidden, negative intent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga tanong ay tila **may-malisya** at hindi lang simpleng pag-uusisa.","translation":"His questions seem **malicious** and not just simple curiosity."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong bigyan ng **malisya** ang pagtulong niya; mabait lang talaga siya.","translation":"Don't attribute **malice** to his helpfulness; he is just genuinely kind."}]

translation: condescension, act of yielding or giving in
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakumbaba o pag-ayon sa kagustuhan ng iba, na maaaring may kasamang pakiramdam ng pagiging mas mataas o nakalalamang.
etymology: From pa- + pa- + hinuhod. The root 'hinuhod' is rare and means to yield or concede.
original_explanation: It's when you finally give in to your friend's pestering to watch that K-drama, even if you don't want to. "Sige na, panalo ka na." It can also have a slightly negative vibe, like a boss "stooping down" to explain something simple.
usage_notes: This word has a slightly formal and sometimes negative connotation of condescendingly giving in.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pagpapahinuhod**, pumayag siyang ibigay ang hiling ng bata.","translation":"In his **condescension**, he agreed to grant the child's wish."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **pagpapahinuhod** sa pamamagitan ng pakikinig sa aming mga mungkahi.","translation":"He showed his **willingness to yield** by listening to our suggestions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking bangkang pangisda na may mga katig at nilagyan ng malakas na ilaw at malaking lambat (lift net) upang makahuli ng isda sa gabi.
original_explanation: Think of it as the floating BPO of the sea, working the night shift. It's a big fishing boat with outriggers and super bright lights that attract fish and squid like Pinoys to a new milk tea shop. The crew then lowers a huge net, scoops them up, and boom—ulam for tomorrow's market.
usage_notes: A specific term used in the Philippine fishing industry, particularly in the Visayas region.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming huling isda ang **basnig** kagabi.","translation":"The **basnig** had a large catch last night."},{"sentence":"Ang mga ilaw mula sa **basnig** ay tanaw mula sa dalampasigan.","translation":"The lights from the **basnig** are visible from the shore."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang laman sa loob; hungkag.
original_explanation: Para kang supot ng chicharon na puro hangin lang. Or your wallet before payday. Or your heart after they left you on 'read'. That feeling of being empty inside, 'yan ang guang.
usage_notes: Not a very common word in daily Manila-based conversations, but understood. More common in other Tagalog-speaking regions. Often used metaphorically for emotional emptiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Guang** ang loob ng kawayan.","translation":"The inside of the bamboo is **hollow**."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya'y **guang** ang kanyang dibdib matapos ang masamang balita.","translation":"He felt his chest was **empty inside** after the bad news."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkuha muli sa isang bagay na naibigay o nawala; maaari ding tumukoy sa pag-urong sa isang sinabi o ginawa, o sa paggaling mula sa isang paghihirap.
original_explanation: That moment you try to un-send a risky text message. Also, the glow-up after a breakup. "Yung ex mo, panay ang post ng travel pics. Halatang nasa 'pagbawi' stage."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis ang kanyang **pagbawi** mula sa pagkakasakit.","translation":"His **recovery** from illness was fast."},{"sentence":"Walang **pagbawi** sa mga salitang binitiwan mo na.","translation":"There is no **taking back** the words you have already spoken."},{"sentence":"Nag-isyu siya ng public apology bilang **pagbawi** sa kanyang naunang pahayag.","translation":"He issued a public apology as a **retraction** of his previous statement."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagiging may uka o lundo sa gitna; hindi patag dahil sa pagkakadiin o pagkalubog ng isang bahagi.
original_explanation: Imagine a ping-pong ball that's been slightly crushed. That dent? That's lukong. It's that sunken, caved-in shape. It could be the dent on your car, your old can of biscuits, or even a sunken cheek. It's the opposite of 'umbok' (convex).
usage_notes: Describes a surface that curves inward.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **lukong** ang bubong na yero dahil sa bigat ng bumagsak na sanga.","translation":"The metal roof became **dented** because of the weight of the fallen branch."},{"sentence":"Pansinin mo ang **lukong** na bahagi ng kalsada.","translation":"Notice the **sunken** part of the road."}]

translation: to bring something down; to lower
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaba ng isang bagay mula sa isang mataas na lugar; ang pag-alis sa isang posisyon o pwesto.
etymology: From mag- + panaog (to go down/descend). 'Panaog' is an older term related to 'baba' (down).
original_explanation: This is what you do with the Christmas decorations in January, or what a crane does with a container van. Figuratively, it's what happens to a politician after an impeachment trial. It's the act of moving something from a higher position to a lower one, whether it's a flag, a santo from an altar, or a CEO from their corner office.
usage_notes: More common in some dialects (like Bicolano and Cebuano) and in formal/literary Tagalog. 'Magbaba' is the more common, everyday equivalent in modern Manila Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nang **magpanaog** ng bandila dahil palubog na ang araw.","translation":"It is necessary to **bring down** the flag because the sun is already setting."},{"sentence":"Inutusan niya ang katulong na **ipanaog** ang mga maleta mula sa itaas.","translation":"She ordered the helper to **bring down** the suitcases from upstairs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng katawan sa posisyon kung saan ang bigat ay nakasalalay sa puwitan, karaniwan sa isang silya o sahig.
original_explanation: What your mom yells when you're blocking the TV. Also, the first command you teach your dog. In Filipino culture, it's an invitation: 'Upo muna kayo,' which means 'Make yourselves comfortable, the chismis is about to start.'
usage_notes: This is the root word. The command form is 'Umupo'. 'Maupo' is the polite form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi ng guro, '**Upo**!' sa mga maingay na estudyante.","translation":"The teacher said, '**Sit**!' to the noisy students."},{"sentence":"Pagod na ako sa kakatayo, gusto ko nang um**upo**.","translation":"I'm tired of standing, I want to **sit** down."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manipis at malutong na biskwit, karaniwang ginagamit na lalagyan ng sorbetes o kinakain bilang meryenda.
original_explanation: The OG crispy vessel for 'dirty ice cream.' It's the thing that gets soggy and starts leaking sorbetes all over your hand if you don't eat fast enough on a hot day. The ultimate race against time. Also refers to the thin wafer used for Barquillos.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to the cone for ice cream, but can also refer to other thin wafers like those for the host in communion or for barquillos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Manong, pabili po ng sorbetes, sa **apa** po ilagay.","translation":"Sir, I'd like to buy ice cream, please put it in a **cone**."},{"sentence":"Nadurog ang **apa** bago ko pa malagyan ng ice cream.","translation":"The **cone** broke before I could even put ice cream in it."}]

meaning_filipino: Lutuin ang isang partikular na pagkain sa pamamagitan ng pag-iihaw.
original_explanation: This is the action you perform on the 'ihawan'. When someone says 'ihawin mo na 'yung baboy,' it's the command to start the grilling process. It's the verb that turns raw pork, fish, or chicken into delicious 'ihaw'. The official start of the party.
usage_notes: An object-focus verb. The thing being grilled is the focus of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap **ihawin** ang pusit na may palamang kamatis at sibuyas.","translation":"It's delicious **to grill** squid stuffed with tomatoes and onions."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **ihawin** ang mga hotdog para sa mga bata.","translation":"Don't forget **to grill** the hotdogs for the kids."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na bago, hindi luma o laon, at nasa pinakamainam na kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is peak freshness. Not just 'sariwa', but 'sariwang-sariwa'. It's the isda that's still practically twitching in the palengke, the buko juice straight from the shell, or the chismis that just dropped 5 minutes ago. It's the highest tier of 'bago'.
usage_notes: The repetition of the root word intensifies the meaning, a common feature in Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sariwang-sariwa** ang hangin sa probinsya tuwing umaga.","translation":"The air in the province is **very fresh** every morning."},{"sentence":"Garantisadong **sariwang-sariwa** ang mga gulay na tinda ni Aling Nena.","translation":"The vegetables sold by Aling Nena are guaranteed to be **very fresh**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa larangan ng anatomiya, ito ay tumutukoy sa isa sa dalawang malalaking silid sa ibabang bahagi ng puso na nagbobomba ng dugo palabas nito.
original_explanation: This is a high-level science class word. Think of your heart as a duplex condo. The atria are the upstairs receiving areas, and the **bentrikulo** are the powerful downstairs units that pump the lifeblood out to the rest of the body-village. You don't hear this in the palengke, but it's crucial for your cardiologist.
usage_notes: Primarily used in medical or academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan namin ang kaliwang **bentrikulo** ng puso sa klase ng biology.","translation":"We are studying the left **ventricle** of the heart in biology class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtingala o pag-angat ng tingin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "tunghay" (to look up). Ang unlaping "pa-" dito ay bumubuo ng isang pangngalan na tumutukoy sa kilos.
original_explanation: This is another classic, literary word. Imagine a dramatic scene where the character is praying, then slowly looks up to the heavens. That action is **patunghay**. It's not just a casual 'look up'; it has a sense of reverence, hope, or deep thought. Parang sa music video, slow-mo effect tapos **patunghay** sa langit.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at makatang salita. Hindi karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap. Ang "pagtingala" ang mas karaniwang katumbas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang marahang **patunghay** ang tanging sagot niya sa aking tanong.","translation":"A slow **upward glance** was his only answer to my question."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **patunghay**, nasilayan niya ang bughaw na kalangitan.","translation":"In his **upward glance**, he saw the blue sky."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasa sa wika. Ito ay isang alternatibong baybay para sa 'lingguwista'.
original_explanation: Same as 'lingguwista', pero ito yung spelling na mas madalas mong makikita sa mga lumang libro o isusulat ng tita mo sa Facebook. Pareho lang silang expert sa chismis... este, wika.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang karaniwang baryante ng baybay ng 'lingguwista'. Ang paggamit ng '-guw-' ay ang mas pinapaboran sa makabagong ortograpiyang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang maging isang **linggwista** balang araw.","translation":"She wants to become a **linguist** someday."}]

meaning_filipino: Kulang sa liwanag o ilaw; maaari ding tumukoy sa isang bagay na hindi malinaw o mahirap maintindihan.
original_explanation: This is the more literal cousin of `di-malinaw`. It can mean a dim room perfect for horror movies (`di-maliwanag ang kwarto`). It can also mean a vague explanation, just like `di-malinaw`. If your partner says 'May problema tayo' but won't explain what it is, that's a di-maliwanag na situation. Basically, if you need to turn on a light, either literally or figuratively, you're in a di-maliwanag state.
usage_notes: Maaaring ipagpalit sa 'di-malinaw' kapag tumutukoy sa mga konsepto, ngunit ang 'di-maliwanag' ay mas karaniwan para sa literal na kakulangan ng ilaw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap magbasa sa lugar na **di-maliwanag**.","translation":"It's hard to read in a place that is **not bright**."},{"sentence":"**Di-maliwanag** sa akin kung ano talaga ang gusto niyang mangyari.","translation":"It's **unclear** to me what he really wants to happen."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa katangian ng pagiging malambot, magaan, at may malaking volume, karaniwan sa buhok o sinulid.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate hair goal for some, and a daily struggle for others. 'Buhag' hair is fluffy, frizzy, and has a personality of its own, like you just got a '70s blowout or you stuck your finger in an electric socket. It's the opposite of sleek and rebonded. Think less 'commercial model' and more 'Lion King'.
usage_notes: Primarily used to describe hair that is puffy, frizzy, or has a lot of volume. Can also describe things like cotton or yarn.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang lumabas kapag umuulan dahil nagiging **buhag** ang kanyang buhok.","translation":"She doesn't like going out when it's raining because her hair becomes **fluffy** and frizzy."},{"sentence":"Ang lambot at **buhag** ng bulak na ito.","translation":"This cotton is so soft and **fluffy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit at sunud-sunod na pag-abot o pagdating ng isang bagay o pangyayari.
original_explanation: Picture this: You're trying to get a signal for your phone, raising it up and down—that's 'abut-abot'. Or when bills arrive one after another before payday—that's also 'abut-abot'. It's the feeling of being bombarded, whether by blessings or by bills.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a series of events (frequently negative) happening in quick succession.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Abut-abot** ang mga problemang dumating sa pamilya nila ngayong taon.","translation":"The problems that came to their family this year were **one after another**."},{"sentence":"Naging **abut-abot** ang kaniyang pag-ubo dahil sa matinding sipon.","translation":"His coughing became **intermittent** because of the bad cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, hayop, o bagay na lulan o dala sa isang sasakyan.
original_explanation: You, when you're in a Grab, jeepney, or bus. "Ilan sakay niyo?" is the driver's eternal question to the barker. It can also be the stuff you're carrying, like the balikbayan box that needs its own seat.
usage_notes: Can refer to people (pasahero), animals, or inanimate objects (karga) being transported.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na ng **sakay** ang huling biyahe ng bus.","translation":"The last bus trip was already full of **passengers**."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang mga **sakay** nating babasagin.","translation":"Be careful with our fragile **cargo**."}]

translation: to go to; to head towards
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpunta o pagtahak sa isang tiyak na direksyon o lugar.
original_explanation: Like when your Grab driver finally accepts your booking and is now on the way to your pin. 'Pumatungo na siya sa location mo.' It's the formal, almost literary, way of saying 'papunta na.'
usage_notes: Often used in formal or literary contexts. `Pumunta` is the more common, everyday equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumatungo** sila sa silangan kung saan sumisikat ang araw.","translation":"They **headed** east where the sun rises."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **pumatungo** matapos ang ating pag-uusap?","translation":"Where did you **go** after our conversation?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o lugar kung saan nagtitipon ang mga Hudyo para sa kanilang mga seremonyang panrelihiyon at pag-aaral.
etymology: From Spanish 'sinagoga', from Latin 'synagōga', from Greek 'sunagōgḗ' (assembly).
original_explanation: This is the Jewish equivalent of a church or a mosque. You'll mostly encounter this word in a religious studies class or when reading the Bible. It's not your everyday palengke word, unless your palengke is in Jerusalem.
usage_notes: A loanword used specifically in a religious or historical context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagturo si Hesus sa mga **sinagoga** sa Galilea.","translation":"Jesus taught in the **synagogues** in Galilee."},{"sentence":"Ang **sinagoga** ay isang mahalagang sentro ng komunidad ng mga Hudyo.","translation":"The **synagogue** is an important center of the Jewish community."}]

translation: to divide into parts; to partition
meaning_filipino: Ang paghati-hati sa isang kabuuan sa maraming maliliit na bahagi upang ipamahagi.
original_explanation: This is what you do with the last piece of pizza when you're with five other friends. You have to 'pagbahagi-bahagiin' it so everyone gets a tiny, almost-imaginary slice. It's the art of strategic division, whether it's budget, chismis, or a single pack of pancit canton.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'bahagi' emphasizes that it's being divided into multiple, often small, pieces. The user may have intended this word from the provided 'pagbaha-bahaginin', which is a common typo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **pagbahagi-bahagiin** ang mga gawain upang mas mabilis matapos.","translation":"We need **to divide** the tasks among us to finish faster."}]

translation: to form into several small groups; to clique up
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbubuo o paghihiwa-hiwalay sa iba't ibang maliliit na grupo.
original_explanation: This is the more chaotic version of `magpangkat`. It's what happens at a family reunion when the Titas form one group to talk about their "hijos" and "hijas", the Titos form another to talk about cars, and the cousins huddle in a corner to plan their escape. It's the social dynamic of a high school cafeteria.
usage_notes: Implies division into multiple, often separate, groups. Can sometimes have a negative connotation of forming exclusive cliques.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ng manager na **nagpapangkat-pangkat** ang mga empleyado sa opisina.","translation":"The manager doesn't like it when the employees **form into cliques** in the office."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng tour guide ang mga turista na **magpangkat-pangkat** para sa pamamasyal.","translation":"The tour guide advised the tourists to **form into several small groups** for the tour."}]

translation: extremely busy, unable to find a moment's rest
meaning_filipino: Lubhang abala o maraming ginagawa kaya't hindi malaman kung ano ang uunahin; hindi mapakali.
etymology: Mula sa 'di' (not) + 'makaugaga'. Ang buong parirala ay isang idyoma.
original_explanation: This is the official state of every working adult during 'ber' months. From deadlines to Christmas shopping to family reunions, you're just running around like a headless chicken. You can't even sit down for a proper meal. 'Yan ang di-makaugaga. The BPO agent on a triple-overtime shift.
usage_notes: Isang idyomatikong ekspresyon upang ilarawan ang pagiging sobrang abala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-makaugaga** ang buong opisina sa paghahanda para sa malaking presentasyon.","translation":"The whole office is **extremely busy** preparing for the big presentation."},{"sentence":"Tuwing may bisita, ang nanay ko ay **di-makaugaga** sa pag-aasikaso sa kanila.","translation":"Whenever there are visitors, my mother is **unable to find a moment's rest** attending to them."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipagawa o ipahintulot na mailimbag at isapubliko ang isang akda, anunsyo, o anumang sulatin.
original_explanation: Before 'going viral' on TikTok, this was the original way to get seen. You write something—a story, a poem, or even chismis (as a blind item)—and you `ipalathala` it in a newspaper or magazine. It's asking the editor, 'Paki-publish po, master!'
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of literature, journalism, and official announcements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **ipalathala** ang kanyang nobela sa isang malaking publishing house.","translation":"She wants **to have her novel published** by a big publishing house."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **ipalathala** sa diyaryo ang pagbati sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"We need **to have the birthday greeting published** in the newspaper."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal o ahensya na ang trabaho ay maghanap at humikayat ng mga kwalipikadong tao upang punan ang mga bakanteng posisyon sa isang kumpanya.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na "recruiter".
original_explanation: The person who slides into your LinkedIn DMs with a "Hi, I have an exciting opportunity for you!" They are the talent hunters of the corporate jungle, the gatekeepers to your next job. They can be your best friend when you're job hunting, or the person you ghost when you're happy with your current work. They live on coffee, KPIs, and the thrill of a "signed contract".
usage_notes: Malawakang ginagamit sa konteksto ng human resources, BPO, at corporate world.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumawag sa akin ang isang **recruiter** para sa isang job interview.","translation":"A **recruiter** called me for a job interview."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang trabaho ng **recruiter**, lalo na kung niche ang hinahanap na role.","translation":"A **recruiter's** job is hard, especially if the role they're looking for is niche."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na hindi nagpapakita ng emosyon o pagiging malapit sa iba; malamig ang pakikitungo.
original_explanation: When your chatmate starts giving one-word replies. When your partner is physically present but mentally on another planet. That's malayo ang damdamin. It's the emotional equivalent of an LDR (Long-Distance Relationship) even when you're in the same room. The classic 'seen-zone' feeling, but in real life.
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression to describe emotional state or personality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula nang mag-away sila, naging **malayo ang damdamin** niya sa akin.","translation":"Ever since we fought, he has become **emotionally distant** from me."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya masamang tao, sadyang **malayo lang ang damdamin** niya sa simula.","translation":"He's not a bad person, he's just **aloof** at first."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng paglabas o pag-angat ng isang bagay mula sa isang patag na ibabaw o mula sa kinalalagyan nito.
original_explanation: That nail sticking out of the wall waiting to snag your shirt. The awkward way your phone charger sticks out from the socket. It's anything that juts out, creating an uneven surface. In social situations, it's like being the "third wheel," yung `pagkausli` mo sa date ng friends mo.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa estado ng isang bagay na nakausli o nakaangat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang **pagkausli** ng pako sa dingding para walang masaktan.","translation":"Fix the **protrusion** of the nail on the wall so no one gets hurt."},{"sentence":"Hindi maganda tingnan ang **pagkausli** ng mga buto sa kanyang likod dahil sa sobrang kapayatan.","translation":"The **jutting out** of the bones on his back doesn't look good due to extreme thinness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging malinis, maayos, at walang dumi sa katawan, kasuotan, o kapaligiran.
original_explanation: This is your mom's superpower. The ability to see a single speck of dust from across the room. It’s the opposite of your teenage brother's bedroom. It can also mean "clean" in the sense of having a clean record or conscience, like a politician who claims "Wala akong kasalanan!"
usage_notes: Can refer to physical cleanliness or moral/ethical cleanliness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinangaan siya ng lahat dahil sa kanyang **pagkamalinis** sa bahay.","translation":"Everyone admired her for her **cleanliness** at home."},{"sentence":"Pinatunayan niya sa korte ang kanyang **pagkamalinis** sa anumang akusasyon.","translation":"He proved in court his **blamelessness** in any accusation."}]

translation: to give as a Christmas gift
meaning_filipino: Ibigay bilang aginaldo o regalo sa panahon ng Pasko.
original_explanation: The verb form of "Merry Christmas to me!" It's when you decide to give something (usually something you don't need anymore) as a Christmas present. "Uy, ang ganda ng damit mo!" "Salamat, **ipapasko** ko 'to sa'yo next year." Regifting level: expert.
usage_notes: Often used in a humorous or informal context, implying regifting or giving something away specifically for Christmas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itong lumang laruan ay **ipapasko** ko na lang sa pamangkin ko.","translation":"I'll just **give** this old toy **as a Christmas gift** to my nephew."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-upo o pagpapatong sa mga hita ng isang taong nakaupo; ang bahagi ng katawan mula sa baywang hanggang tuhod ng isang taong nakaupo.
original_explanation: The best seat in the house when you were a kid, especially on your lolo's or lola's lap. As an adult, it's that awkward moment in a full jeepney when a stranger's bag is on your lap, or when you have to share a single chair with your friend. "Friend, pa-kandong muna ha, puno na eh."
usage_notes: Often used as a verb root (e.g., 'kumandong', 'kandungan'). The noun itself refers to the act or the place (the lap).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig kumandong sa kanyang ina ang bunsong anak.","translation":"The youngest child loves to sit on his mother's **lap**."},{"sentence":"Puno ang jeep, kaya **kandong** ang mga bag.","translation":"The jeep was full, so the bags were placed on **laps**."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang suot na anumang sapin sa paa, tulad ng tsinelas o sapatos.
original_explanation: The state of your feet when you're at home, feeling the cold tiles. Or when you're walking on the beach. It's the ultimate 'pambahay' mode. 'Huwag kang lumabas nang yapak, baka matusok ka!'
usage_notes: Describes the state of having no footwear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap maglakad nang **yapak** sa dalampasigan.","translation":"It feels good to walk **barefoot** on the seashore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na kinuha o ginamit na may pahintulot at may intensyong ibalik sa may-ari.
original_explanation: The national pastime. 'Pahiram ng ballpen?' 'Pahiram ng charger?' Buhay natin ay isang malaking 'hiram'. Minsan, kahit buhay, 'hiram lang sa Maykapal.' But in love? Ay, 'wag kang manghiram ng jowa, mars. That's a different story. 'Hiram' is that thing you get with a promise to return, but sometimes... nakakalimutan. #HiramPaMore
usage_notes: Can function as a noun (ang hiram / the borrowed item) or an adjective (bagay na hiram / a borrowed thing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang librong ito ay **hiram** ko lang sa kaibigan ko.","translation":"This book is just **borrowed** from my friend."},{"sentence":"Tandaan mo na ang buhay natin ay **hiram** lamang.","translation":"Remember that our life is only **borrowed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtaya ng pera o anumang may halaga sa isang laro o kaganapan na may hindi tiyak na resulta, sa pag-asang manalo ng mas malaking halaga.
original_explanation: It's what your tito does during family reunions with his mahjong set. It's betting on the 'sabong' (cockfight). On a more hugot level, it's what you do when you give someone a second chance: 'magsugal sa pag-ibig,' hoping this time, it pays off.
usage_notes: Carries a generally negative connotation, often associated with vice and addiction, though it can be used for casual betting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan siya ng kanyang mga magulang na huwag **magsugal** dahil masama itong bisyo.","translation":"His parents told him not to **gamble** because it is a bad vice."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang pag-ibig ay parang **magsugal**; minsan panalo, madalas talo.","translation":"For him, loving is like **gambling**; sometimes you win, often you lose."}]

translation: to set up on; to erect on a spot
meaning_filipino: Lagyan o tayuan ng isang bagay na patirik sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: Ito yung command sa SimCity o sa construction site: "Dito niyo itayo!" Pwedeng tent sa camping, poste ng ilaw, o kaya... kandila para sa patay. The location matters.
usage_notes: Ang pandiwang ito ay tumutukoy sa lugar kung saan itinatayo ang isang bagay. Hal: **Tirikan** mo ng tolda ang espasyong iyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tirikan** mo ng krus ang puntod ni lola.","translation":"**Erect** a cross on grandma's grave."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **tirikan** ng bahay ang lugar na laging binabaha.","translation":"Don't **build** a house on a place that always floods."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na iabot o ipasa ang isang bagay. Karaniwang ginagamit sa anyong pautos.
original_explanation: The official word for when something is just out of your reach. It's the battle cry at every Filipino dining table: "**Paabot** ng patis!" (Please pass the fish sauce!). It's a polite command, a shortcut for "Pakiaabot mo sa akin" (Please pass it to me). Master this, and you'll never have to stand up for the salt shaker again.
usage_notes: Often used as a standalone command followed by the object being requested. It's a contraction of 'pakiaabot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paabot** naman ng remote control.","translation":"**Please pass** the remote control."},{"sentence":"Anak, **paabot** nga ng baso.","translation":"Child, **please hand me** the glass."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagnanakaw o gumagamit para sa sariling kapakanan ng perang ipinagkatiwala sa kanya.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung treasurer ng class fund na biglang "nagkasakit" nung malapit na ang Christmas party at hindi na nagpakita. A dispalkador is someone who secretly steals money they were entrusted with, like from a company, an organization, or even the government. It's a high-level, white-collar kind of magnanakaw.
usage_notes: Madalas marinig sa balita o sa mga legal na usapin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ang **dispalkador** na tumangay ng milyun-milyong piso mula sa kumpanya.","translation":"The **embezzler** who took millions of pesos from the company was caught."},{"sentence":"May kasong isinampa laban sa dating tesorero dahil sa pagiging **dispalkador**.","translation":"A case was filed against the former treasurer for being an **embezzler**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isda na karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga tubig-alat at tubig-tabang sa Pilipinas, kilala sa siyentipikong pangalan na *Mugil cephalus*.
original_explanation: Ito yung isda na madalas mong makita sa palengke na binebenta by the kilo. Hindi kasing sikat ng tilapia o bangus, pero masarap din 'to, lalo na kung prito o sinigang. Parang yung quiet officemate mo na hindi pala-social media, pero 'pag kinausap mo, ang galing pala mag-Excel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap daw isigang ang sariwang **banyusan**.","translation":"They say fresh **mullet** is delicious in sour soup."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan humihinto o nagtitipon; isang base o sentro ng operasyon.
original_explanation: Think of it as a base. It could be a bus station (himpilan ng bus), a police station (himpilan ng pulisya), or a TV station (himpilan ng telebisyon). It's the official hangout spot for a specific purpose. Your barkada's 'himpilan' might be the local milk tea shop.
usage_notes: Often found in its affixed form 'himpilan' to refer to the station itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **himpil** ng pulisya ang mga suspek.","translation":"The suspects are at the police **station**."},{"sentence":"Ang susunod na **himpil** ng tren ay sa Cubao.","translation":"The next train **stop** is in Cubao."}]

meaning_filipino: Tubig na bumabagsak mula sa mga ulap sa anyo ng mga patak.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'walang pasok' (no classes) declaration for students, the ultimate traffic-inducer for commuters, and the ultimate 'bed weather' excuse for everyone else. It's the reason your Grab fare suddenly surges and why your freshly washed laundry needs a do-over. Also, a classic backdrop for dramatic hugot moments in Pinoy movies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maglaro sa labas dahil malakas ang **ulan**.","translation":"Don't play outside because the **rain** is heavy."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang tumulo ang **ulan** habang kami ay naglalakad.","translation":"The **rain** started to fall while we were walking."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang talaan ng mga gawain, kaganapan, o tipanan na nakaayos ayon sa oras at araw ng pagganap; talatakdaan.
original_explanation: The thing that dictates your life, especially if you're a student or a BPO agent. It's that Google Calendar that's filled with meetings, deadlines, and "me time" that you keep rescheduling. "Sorry, can't make it, my schedule is full" is the adult version of "My dog ate my homework."
usage_notes: The Tagalog word 'talatakdaan' exists but 'schedule' is far more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan ko muna ang **schedule** ko kung libre ako sa Sabado.","translation":"Let me check my **schedule** first if I'm free on Saturday."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang shifting **schedule** sa call center.","translation":"The shifting **schedule** at the call center is difficult."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bahagi ng katawan na sumailalim sa isang operasyon o siruhiya.
original_explanation: This is the past tense of getting sliced and diced by a doctor (in a good way!). If someone is "operado," they've had surgery. "Operado siya sa appendix." It's the medical version of "under repair." You'll often see them recovering, eating lugaw, and being pampered by the whole family.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan pagkatapos ng isang medikal na operasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kagagaling lang niya sa ospital, **operado** siya sa puso.","translation":"He just came from the hospital, he was **operated on** for his heart."},{"sentence":"Masakit pa rin ang tiyan kong **operado**.","translation":"My stomach that was **operated on** still hurts."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpisan-pisan o pagsasama-sama ng mga tao, bagay, o impormasyon sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: Parang family reunion o barkada night out. Or yung mga resibo na kailangan mo para sa reimbursement. It's any act of bringing things or people together. Pwedeng masaya (party), pwedeng stressful (documents for visa application).
usage_notes: Ito ang salitang-ugat para sa 'tipunin' at 'tipunan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng isang malaking **tipon** ang aming pamilya noong Pasko.","translation":"Our family had a big **gathering** last Christmas."},{"sentence":"Ang **tipon** ng mga lumang selyo ay mahalaga sa kanya.","translation":"The **collection** of old stamps is important to him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salita o pangkat ng mga salita na ginagamit sa di-tuwirang paraan upang magbigay ng mas malalim o makulay na kahulugan; isang uri ng idyoma o pagwawangis.
etymology: Unknown, likely a classical Tagalog literary term.
original_explanation: The OG 'hugot'. This is the high-level literary stuff you learned in Filipino class and promptly forgot. It's when you say 'pusong bato' (heart of stone) instead of 'manhid'. Tayubay is the art of saying something without saying it directly, making your message more dramatic and IG-caption worthy.
usage_notes: A formal, literary term used in the study of rhetoric and literature. 'Talinghaga' is a close synonym.
