usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paggamit ng **tayubay** ay nagpapaganda sa isang tula.","translation":"The use of a **figure of speech** beautifies a poem."},{"sentence":"Ang 'itim na tupa' ay isang halimbawa ng **tayubay**.","translation":"'Black sheep' is an example of a **figure of speech**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na dalisay, tunay, at walang halo o pagkukunwari. Maaari ring mangahulugang walang hanggan o walang katapusan.
original_explanation: "Wagas" is the love you see in old couples, yung tipong #SanaAll. It's the kind of laughter na to the highest level, yung halos maihi ka na. It's the "ultimate" or "extreme" version of an emotion. "Wagas na pag-ibig" is forever love. "Wagas makatawa" is laughing your heart out. It's the opposite of "charot lang." This is the real deal, no BS, 100% pure.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang matinding damdamin tulad ng pag-ibig, kaligayahan, o kalungkutan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **wagas** na pagmamahal sa pamamagitan ng pag-aalaga sa kanyang may-sakit na ina.","translation":"She showed her **sincere** love by taking care of her sick mother."},{"sentence":"**Wagas** ang kanyang tuwa nang manalo siya sa lotto.","translation":"His joy was **immense** when he won the lottery."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtigil o pananatili sa isang lugar sa loob ng isang tiyak na panahon.
etymology: From pa- + mam- (from ma- + lagi) + lagi. The root 'lagi' means 'always' or 'constant'.
original_explanation: Your 'staycation' at a hotel? That's your pamamalagi. The awkward length of time you stay at a relative's house, waiting for them to hint that it's time to go home? That's also pamamalagi. It's the act of staying put, whether you're a welcome guest or you've overstayed your welcome.
usage_notes: Refers to the duration of one's stay somewhere.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging masaya ang aming **pamamalagi** sa inyong tahanan.","translation":"Our **stay** at your home was a happy one."},{"sentence":"Ang **pamamalagi** ng mga turista ay nakakatulong sa lokal na ekonomiya.","translation":"The **stay** of tourists helps the local economy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na lugar o kainan kung saan maaaring bumili at kumain ng mga lutong pagkain.
original_explanation: A step up from a turo-turo, but not quite a full-blown restaurant. Ito yung go-to place ng mga empleyado for lunch break kasi mabilis, mura, at masarap (sana). The vibe is 'unli rice' and plastic-covered tables.
usage_notes: Karaniwang katumbas ng "karinderya" o "turo-turo".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bagong bukas na **eatery** sa kanto na masarap daw ang sisig.","translation":"There's a newly opened **eatery** on the corner that they say has delicious sisig."},{"sentence":"Doon tayo kumain sa paborito nating **eatery**.","translation":"Let's eat at our favorite **eatery**."}]

translation: To ignite; to cause to flare up
meaning_filipino: Pag-alabin, pagningasin, o simulan ang isang bagay na may kasamang tindi o sidhi, tulad ng apoy, galit, o damdamin.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you want to start drama. You 'ignite' the fire. Pwede ring literal, like lighting a firecracker. Or when you want to make the party more exciting, you 'pasiklabin' the energy. It's about making something small or quiet into something big, bright, and loud.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for fire or light, or figuratively for emotions, conflicts, or excitement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pasiklabin** ang isyu para hindi na lumaki pa.","translation":"Don't **ignite** the issue so it doesn't get bigger."},{"sentence":"Oras na para **pasiklabin** ang kasiyahan sa party!","translation":"It's time to **spark** the fun at the party!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ako sa responsibilidad o obligasyon para sa isang kilos o desisyon; ang pagiging may pananagutan.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na 'sagot' (answer) na nilapian upang mangahulugang 'ang akto ng pagsagot para sa isang bagay'.
original_explanation: Adulting 101: Accountability. It's owning your stuff, literally and figuratively. It's the act of facing the music when you mess up at work, or being the one to settle the bill after a group dinner. It's the opposite of making excuses or ghosting your responsibilities. You did the crime, you do the time (or at least, explain yourself).
usage_notes: Malapit sa kahulugan ng 'pananagutan' (responsibility), ngunit mas tumutukoy sa akto ng pag-ako o pagharap sa resulta.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pananagot** ng bawat opisyal sa kanilang mga nasasakupan.","translation":"The **accountability** of every official to their constituents is important."},{"sentence":"Bahagi ng kanyang **pananagot** ang paghingi ng tawad sa nagawang pagkakamali.","translation":"Part of his **act of answering for** his mistake is to apologize."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyon kung saan ang katawan ay pinagkakaitan ng sapat na suplay ng oxygen, na maaaring magdulot ng pagkawala ng malay o kamatayan.
original_explanation: This is a heavy, medical term for when you can't breathe. It's not just 'kinakapos ng hininga' from running to catch the jeep; it's the life-threatening lack of oxygen. It's a word you'd hear in a hospital drama or a crime procedural, not in everyday chika.
usage_notes: Isang terminong medikal at teknikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sanhi ng kanyang pagkamatay ay **aspiksiya** dahil sa pagkalunod.","translation":"The cause of his death was **asphyxia** due to drowning."}]

translation: to inhale; to savor the scent of
meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang pag-amoy o paghinga paloob ng hangin o ng isang partikular na bango.
original_explanation: "Go on, **langhapin** mo ang 'success'," sabi mo sa sarili mo habang naamoy mo yung bagong sahod. It's the active version of 'langhap'. You do it on purpose, like when you deeply **langhapin** the smell of the sea at the beach, trying to absorb all the non-toxic vibes before heading back to the city.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **langhapin** ang sariwang hangin sa umaga.","translation":"I want to **inhale** the fresh morning air."},{"sentence":"**Langhapin** mo ang bango ng mga bulaklak sa hardin.","translation":"**Savor the scent of** the flowers in the garden."}]

translation: to carry with a shoulder pole
meaning_filipino: Buhatin o dalhin ang dalawang bagay na magkasingbigat sa magkabilang dulo ng isang pingga na nakaatang sa balikat.
original_explanation: This is how the 'taho' vendor masters physics every morning. It's the act of carrying two heavy buckets (one with taho, one with sago and arnibal) on a bamboo pole across your shoulders, all while gracefully navigating sidewalks and calling out "Tahooooo!". The original hands-free delivery system.
usage_notes: Specific to the use of a 'pingga' or a shoulder-carrying pole, with loads balanced on each end.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maagang gumigising ang magtataho para **pinggahin** ang kanyang paninda.","translation":"The taho vendor wakes up early **to carry** his goods **with a shoulder pole**."},{"sentence":"Kailangang balanse ang bigat ng dalawang timba para madaling **pinggahin**.","translation":"The weight of the two buckets needs to be balanced so they are easy **to carry with a shoulder pole**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay ang paghuli ng isda at iba pang lamang-dagat.
etymology: From "mang-" + "isda" (fish). The prefix 'mang-' indicates a profession or habitual action.
original_explanation: The OG provider of your sinigang na isda and daing na bangus. They're the ones who brave the seas, often before sunrise, to make sure we have fish on our tables. They know more about the weather and the waves than any app, and their work is a cornerstone of life in an archipelago like the Philippines.
usage_notes: A very common word referring to the occupation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maagang pumalaot ang mga **mangingisda** upang magkaroon ng maraming huli.","translation":"The **fishermen** went out to sea early to get a big catch."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay ng isang **mangingisda** ay nakasalalay sa kabutihan ng panahon.","translation":"The life of a **fisherman** depends on the fairness of the weather."}]

translation: to endure; to bear; to suffer through
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtitiis, pagtitiyaga, o pagdadala sa isang hirap, pasanin, o hamon.
etymology: From the root "batá", meaning to endure or suffer. This root is not related to "bata" (child).
original_explanation: To endure something difficult. It's what you do during a 3-hour EDSA traffic jam, a 4-hour government seminar, or when your internet is slow and you're trying to stream a series finale. It's the verb form of 'tiis' but with a 'carry the burden' vibe. "Batahin mo lang, bes. Matatapos din 'yan."
usage_notes: This verb is often confused as being derived from "bata" (child), but it comes from a separate, less common root "batá" (to endure).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **batahin** ang lahat ng pagsubok na ito.","translation":"We need to **endure** all of these trials."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko na kayang **batahin** ang sakit.","translation":"I can't **bear** the pain anymore."}]

translation: to threaten with a blow, to brandish
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-angat ng kamay o isang bagay na hawak bilang pagbabanta na isusuntok, ipapalo, o ihahampas.
original_explanation: 'Yung eksena sa teleserye na aangat 'yung kamay ng kontrabida para sampalin 'yung bida, pero may pipigil. That's 'iamba'. It's the wind-up before the pitch, the threat before the action. "Huwag mong **iamba** sa akin 'yang tsinelas mo, 'nay!"
usage_notes: Refers to the motion of threatening to strike, not the strike itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Galit na **inamba** ng lalaki ang kanyang sinturon.","translation":"The man angrily **brandished** his belt."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko siyang **iamba** ang kamao niya pero hindi naman itinuloy.","translation":"I saw him **raise** his fist as if to strike but he didn't follow through."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na dokumento na nagbibigay ng pahintulot sa isang tao na gawin, gamitin, o magmay-ari ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: That piece of plastic in your wallet that gives you the power to drive, practice a profession, or prove you're not a minor. It's your adulting ID, the one you pray you didn't leave at home when a cop pulls you over. Also, what you need from your parents to go on that out-of-town trip with friends.
usage_notes: Can also be spelled 'lisensiya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naku, naiwan ko ang **lisensya** ko sa bahay!","translation":"Oh no, I left my **license** at home!"},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong mag-renew ng iyong **lisensya** sa pagmamaneho taun-taon.","translation":"You need to renew your driver's **license** annually."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hangin na pumapasok at lumalabas sa baga ng isang tao o hayop bilang bahagi ng proseso ng respirasyon.
original_explanation: That thing you run out of when you climb the MRT stairs. It's what you try to catch after a good gossip session with your Marites friends. 'Hinga, bes,' is the new 'Kalma lang.' It's also what smells like coffee and yosi in the morning for most BPO agents.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for respiration or figuratively for a moment of rest or life itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **hininga** ay nagpapahiwatig ng kaba.","translation":"His **breath** indicated nervousness."},{"sentence":"Hanggang may **hininga**, may pag-asa.","translation":"As long as there is **breath**, there is hope."}]

translation: to tuck at the waist; to carry at the waistband
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ipit o pagsingit ng isang bagay, tulad ng patalim o baril, sa baywang o sa loob ng bahag.
original_explanation: Think of how action stars in old Pinoy movies carry their guns—tucked into their pants at the back, no holster needed. That's 'salukbitin'. Or how a palengke vendor might tuck their money pouch into their waistband. It's the original fanny pack, but using your own clothes.
usage_notes: Often associated with carrying weapons or tools at the waist for quick access.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madaling **salukbitin** ang maliit na itak sa kanyang baywang.","translation":"It's easy **to tuck** the small bolo knife **at his waist**."},{"sentence":"Iniutos ng heneral na i**salukbit** ang kanilang mga espada.","translation":"The general ordered them **to carry** their swords **at their waistband**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ibon na nanghuhuli at kumakain ng ibang hayop para sa kanilang ikabubuhay, karaniwang may matatalas na kuko at tuka.
original_explanation: The alpha birds. The Titas of the sky who look down on everyone. Think eagles, hawks, and owls. They're the ones with sharp talons for snatching up snacks (like snakes or smaller animals) and a resting 'judgmental' face. They don't just eat seeds; they go for the kill.
usage_notes: 'Maninila' is derived from the root 'sila' (prey).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang agila ay isang halimbawa ng **ibong maninila**.","translation":"The eagle is an example of a **bird of prey**."},{"sentence":"Nakakatakot ang titig ng **ibong maninila** na iyon.","translation":"The stare of that **bird of prey** is frightening."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang produktong likido o sabon na ginagamit sa paglilinis ng buhok at anit.
etymology: From English 'shampoo', which originates from Hindi 'chāmpo' (to press, massage).
original_explanation: The magical potion you use to wash away your sins, your worries, and the smell of samgyupsal from your hair. It's the first step to achieving that "commercial-lang-ang-peg" hair flip. Also, the reason why you spend 10 minutes in the grocery aisle just reading labels.
usage_notes: The verb form 'mag-shampoo' is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naubusan na tayo ng **shampoo**, kailangan nating bumili.","translation":"We've run out of **shampoo**, we need to buy more."},{"sentence":"Anong brand ng **shampoo** ang gamit mo? Ang ganda ng buhok mo.","translation":"What brand of **shampoo** do you use? Your hair is beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-angat ng isang bagay sa mas mataas na posisyon; ang pagpapalaki o pagdaragdag sa halaga, presyo, o antas.
original_explanation: The verb for when prices go up (gas, bilihin), when your kilay needs lifting, or when a student in the front row wants to answer a question. 'Nagtaas na naman ng presyo ng sibuyas!' is the national battle cry of every tita in the palengke.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical action (raising a hand) or a conceptual one (increasing a price).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtaas** ka ng kamay kung may tanong ka.","translation":"**Raise** your hand if you have a question."},{"sentence":"Huwag sana silang **magtaas** ng matrikula ngayong taon.","translation":"I hope they don't **increase** the tuition fee this year."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtalon sa ibabaw ng isang partikular na bagay, tao, o hadlang.
etymology: From 'lukso' (jump) + '-hin' (suffix indicating a direct action on an object).
original_explanation: This is the focused version of jumping. If 'luksuhan' is the party, 'luksuhin' is the specific task. It's what you do to that puddle on the sidewalk to avoid getting your new sneakers dirty. It needs a direct object. You 'luksuhin' the 'baha' (floodwater).
usage_notes: Implies a direct object that is being jumped over.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kaya mo bang **luksuhin** ang mataas na bakod?","translation":"Can you **jump over** the high fence?"},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **luksuhin** ang kanal pero nahulog siya.","translation":"He tried to **jump over** the canal but he fell."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain, tungkulin, o hanapbuhay na isinasagawa ng isang tao, karaniwan kapalit ng suweldo o kita.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'trabajo' na nangangahulugang 'gawain' o 'pagod'.
original_explanation: The reason you can't join the Valorant game at 2 PM on a Tuesday. It's that thing you commute 3 hours for, just to answer emails that could've been a text. The 'ho' in 'Yehey, sahod!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Papasok na ako sa **trabaho**.","translation":"I'm going to **work** now."},{"sentence":"Mahirap maghanap ng **trabaho** ngayon.","translation":"It's hard to find a **job** nowadays."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na hindi inaasahan, hindi pinaniniwalaan, o hindi sumagi sa isipan na maaaring mangyari.
original_explanation: Ito yung feeling na 'shookt' ka. Yung biglang nag-message si crush, o yung nalaman mong sold out na ang concert tickets 5 minutes after release. It's the 'I did not see that coming' moment of your life.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa paglalarawan ng mga pangyayaring nakakagulat. Ang pariralang 'di-akalaing manalo' ay isang karaniwang paggamit nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **di-akalaing** tagumpay ay nagbigay inspirasyon sa marami.","translation":"His **unexpected** success inspired many."},{"sentence":"Isang **di-akalaing** pangyayari ang sumalubong sa kanila pag-uwi.","translation":"An **unimaginable** event met them when they got home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng marahan at magaan na pagpalo sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The command form of 'tapik'. It's what you do to wake up your friend who fell asleep during a meeting, or what you tell your SO to do to your back when it's itchy. 'Babe, tapikin mo nga likod ko.'
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the verb. 'Tumapik' is the actor-focus form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tapikin** mo siya sa balikat para malaman niyang nandito na tayo.","translation":"**Tap** him on the shoulder so he knows we're here."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **tapikin** ang screen ng laptop nang malakas.","translation":"Don't **tap** the laptop screen forcefully."}]

translation: to calculate, to compute, to reckon
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng kalkulasyon o pagtutuos upang malaman ang kabuuan, halaga, o resulta ng mga numero.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo sa resibo after a group dinner para malaman kung magkano ang "KKB" (kanya-kanyang bayad). It's the moment of truth when you calculate your monthly expenses and realize you spent too much on milk tea. It's the act of crunching the numbers.
usage_notes: Related to accounting, mathematics, and settling debts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumuos** ang tindera ng kabuuang halaga ng kanyang mga pinamili.","translation":"The seller **calculated** the total cost of her purchases."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng proyekto, oras na para **tumuos** ng mga gastos at kita.","translation":"After the project, it is time to **compute** the expenses and profits."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ibon na may mahaba at pakurbang tuka, karaniwang matatagpuan malapit sa mga anyong tubig.
original_explanation: A fancy bird with a long, curvy beak, like it's perpetually sipping from an invisible, fancy straw. The Egyptian god Thoth is often depicted with the head of an ibis, so you know it's a bird with some serious ancient clout. Not your everyday maya or pipit.
usage_notes: Refers to the specific type of wading bird. This is a homonym of the Tagalog verb root 'ibis', which means 'to unload'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita kami ng isang puting **ibis** na lumilipad sa may ilog.","translation":"We saw a white **ibis** flying near the river."},{"sentence":"Ang sagradong **ibis** ay mahalaga sa mitolohiyang Ehipsiyo.","translation":"The sacred **ibis** is important in Egyptian mythology."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hukuman kung saan dinidinig ang mga apela; ang Korte ng Apelasyon.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'apela' (mula sa Espanyol 'apelar') at hulaping '-han'.
original_explanation: The place where legal battles get a second round. If you lose in the lower court, you can go here and say, "Wait, hold my beer, let's try that again." It's the semi-finals before the Supreme Court championship.
usage_notes: Isang tiyak na pangalan para sa isang uri ng hukuman sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Idinulog nila ang kaso sa **Apelahan**.","translation":"They brought the case to the **Court of Appeals**."},{"sentence":"Ang desisyon ng **Apelahan** ay pabor sa akusado.","translation":"The decision of the **Court of Appeals** was in favor of the accused."}]

translation: was caught up to; was overtaken
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pag-abot o paghabol ng isang tao o bagay sa isa pang nauuna.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'huli' (huli, pagkahuli) na may gitlaping '-in-' at hulaping '-an'.
original_explanation: When you thought you were ahead of the deadline, but the deadline said 'surprise!' and caught up to you. Or when you're running for the jeepney and someone younger and faster overtakes you. 'Yung feeling na na-lap ka sa karera ng buhay.
usage_notes: Nangangahulugan ng pagiging naabutan o nalampasan mula sa likuran. Maaaring gamitin nang literal sa isang karera o metaporikal para sa mga deadline, gawain, atbp.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit mabilis siyang tumakbo, **hinulihan** pa rin siya ng kaniyang mga katunggali.","translation":"Even though he ran fast, he was still **overtaken** by his competitors."},{"sentence":"**Hinulihan** na ako ng mga bayarin ngayong buwan.","translation":"The bills have **caught up** to me this month."}]

translation: Mother (honorific); term for an older woman
meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na katawagan para sa ina o sa isang nakatatandang babae. Karaniwan itong ginagamit sa ilang rehiyon ng Pilipinas, tulad ng Ilocos.
etymology: Mula sa wikang Ilokano na 'nanang' na nangangahulugang 'ina'.
original_explanation: Think of it as the provincial Tita that's not really your aunt but you call her Tita anyway. 'Nanang' is that, but for moms or lolas. It's got that warm, probinsya vibe, often used in places like Ilocos. It’s respect and familiarity rolled into one.
usage_notes: Primarily used in Northern Luzon. While understood in other regions, 'Nanay' or 'Inay' are more common nationally.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umuwi kami sa probinsya para bisitahin si **Nanang**.","translation":"We went home to the province to visit **Nanang** (Mother/Grandmother)."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkaing niluto ni **Nanang** ay laging masarap.","translation":"The food cooked by **Nanang** is always delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay, kilos, o pag-uugali na masama, mali, o hindi kaaya-aya.
original_explanation: The default setting for kontrabidas in teleseryes. It's the feeling you get when your internet dies mid-series, or when someone spoils the ending of a movie. It’s the "Why you do this to me?" kind of bad. "Ang sama ng ugali niya" is the ultimate character assassination.
usage_notes: Pronunciation is key. /SA-ma/ is 'to go with', while /sa-MA/ is 'bad'. The stress on the last syllable changes the entire meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sama** ng panahon ngayon, mukhang uulan.","translation":"The weather is **bad** today, it looks like it will rain."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumawa ng **sama** sa iyong kapwa.","translation":"Do not do **wrong** unto others."}]

meaning_filipino: Hilingin o ipakiusap sa Diyos o sa isang pinaniniwalaang makapangyarihan sa pamamagitan ng panalangin.
original_explanation: It's what you do when your crush finally messages you back, 'Lord, sana kami na.' Or when you're praying for a seat on the MRT. You **idalangin** for something to happen, good or bad. Yes, you can also **idalangin** for your ex's new relationship to fail (the 'idalanging mapahamak' variant), but maybe focus on praying for lotto numbers instead.
usage_notes: Can be used for both positive wishes (e.g., `idalangin ang tagumpay`, to pray for success) and negative ones (`idalangin na mapahamak`, to pray for someone's misfortune).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Araw-araw kong **idinadalangin** ang kaligtasan ng aking pamilya.","translation":"Every day, I **pray for** the safety of my family."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **idalangin** ang kapahamakan ng iba.","translation":"Don't **pray for** the misfortune of others."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar, daan, o oras na mayroong siksikan at mabagal na daloy ng mga sasakyan.
etymology: From the Filipino adjective-forming prefix 'ma-' and the Filipinized spelling 'trapik' from the English 'traffic'.
original_explanation: This describes EDSA. All day, every day. It's the state of being for any major road in Manila during rush hour (which is now from 6 AM to 10 PM). If a road is 'matrapik,' better bring a book, a power bank, and the patience of a saint. It's not just traffic, it's a lifestyle.
usage_notes: Used to describe a place or a condition, as opposed to the verb 'matraffic' which describes the action of being stuck.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sobrang **matrapik** sa Maynila tuwing Biyernes ng hapon.","translation":"It is so **congested with traffic** in Manila every Friday afternoon."},{"sentence":"Humanap tayo ng daan na hindi gaanong **matrapik**.","translation":"Let's find a road that isn't so **congested**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatakda ng bilang o dami ng tao o bagay na maaaring pumasok o ilagay sa isang lugar; pag-apruba o pahintulot.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "aforo" (capacity, valuation) o posibleng korupsyon ng Ingles na "approve".
original_explanation: This sounds like the lolo's version of 'approve'. 'Aporo na ba ng misis mo yang bagong keyboard mo?' It also has a more technical meaning from Spanish 'aforo', which is the capacity limit, like the sign you see at Jollibee: 'Maximum Seating Capacity: 50 pax.' So basically, 'Na-reach na ang aporo ng pasensya ko sa'yo.'
usage_notes: Bihira nang gamitin sa modernong Filipino; mas karaniwan ang "apruba," "aprubado," o "kapasidad."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan natin kung papasa sa **aporo** ng komite ang iyong panukala.","translation":"Let's see if your proposal will pass the committee's **approval**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pandemya, binawasan ang **aporo** ng mga sinehan.","translation":"Because of the pandemic, the **capacity limit** of cinemas was reduced."}]

translation: only a piece; a mere piece
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na napakaliit ang bahagi o isang piraso lamang.
etymology: From ka- (denoting singularity or smallness) + ka- (reduplication) + piraso (piece).
original_explanation: When you order a large pizza tapos ang binigay sa'yo ng "friend" mo ay kakapiraso lang. It's that feeling of "anyare?" (what happened?). It's the diet version of sharing, usually against your will.
usage_notes: Emphasizes the smallness and singularity of the piece. Often used with a sense of disappointment or insufficiency.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kakapiraso** lang ang natira sa cake na binili ko.","translation":"There was **only a tiny piece** left of the cake I bought."},{"sentence":"Binigyan niya ako ng **kakapiraso**ng papel para sulatan.","translation":"He gave me **a mere piece** of paper to write on."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang produkto ng isang halaman na karaniwang naglalaman ng buto. Ginagamit din ito sa metaporikal na paraan upang tukuyin ang resulta o kinalabasan ng isang gawain o pangyayari.
original_explanation: Literally, the mangoes or bananas you buy at the *palengke*. Figuratively, it's the "fruit" of your labor, like finally getting your 13th-month pay after a year of OT. It can also be the consequence of your bad decisions, like the *bunga* of ghosting someone is getting blocked on all social media platforms.
usage_notes: A very versatile word with both literal and figurative meanings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matamis ang **bunga** ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"The **fruit** of the mango tree is sweet."},{"sentence":"Ang tagumpay niya ay **bunga** ng kanyang pagsisikap.","translation":"Her success is the **result** of her hard work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagpapautang ng pera na may labis o napakataas na interes.
original_explanation: This is the '5-6' system in action. Borrow P100 in the morning, pay back P120 by evening. Usurya is the reason why your friendly neighborhood lender can afford a new car while you're still struggling to pay them back. It's financial 'vampirism'.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the practice of lending money at unreasonably high rates of interest. Often associated with '5-6' lending schemes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **usurya** ay ipinagbabawal sa ilalim ng batas ng Pilipinas.","translation":"**Usury** is prohibited under the laws of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Maraming naghihirap ang nababaon sa utang dahil sa **usurya**.","translation":"Many poor people get buried in debt because of **usury**."}]

meaning_filipino: Matatag, buo, at hindi guwang sa loob; matibay at hindi madaling masira o magbago.
original_explanation: Yung friendship ninyo na kahit ilang chismis o away ang dumaan, hindi natitinag. Or yung jowa mong hindi nagche-check out ng iba. Also, yung feeling mo after kumain ng lechon—solid!
usage_notes: Often used colloquially to mean 'excellent' or 'very good', similar to the English slang 'solid'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gawa sa **solido**ng narra ang mesa.","translation":"The table is made of **solid** narra wood."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng **solido**ng ebidensya bago tayo mag-akusa.","translation":"We need **solid** evidence before we make an accusation."},{"sentence":"**Solido** ang performance ng banda kagabi!","translation":"The band's performance last night was **solid**!"}]

translation: to ask someone to tell; to relay a message
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghiling sa isang tao na iparating ang isang mensahe o impormasyon sa iba.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'pasabi na lang.' When you're too shy, too busy, or too tamad to say something directly, you ask a friend, 'Uy, makisabi ka naman kay ano na...' It's the Filipino art of using a human messenger.
usage_notes: The 'maki-' prefix here implies a request or participation in the act of saying something through another person. It's different from 'magsabi' (to tell).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puwedeng **makisabi** kay Gng. Reyes na hindi ako makakapasok bukas?","translation":"Can you please **tell** Mrs. Reyes that I can't come in tomorrow?"},{"sentence":"**Makisabi** ka na lang sa kapatid mo na kunin na niya ang mga gamit niya dito.","translation":"Just **ask** your sibling **to be told** to get their things here."}]

meaning_filipino: Iutos o ipagawa ang pagwasak o pagbuwag sa isang estruktura o gusali.
original_explanation: This is what happens to old buildings to make way for a new condo or mall. It's the "wrecking ball" verb. When a relationship is so toxic it's beyond repair, minsan kailangan mo na ring i-apply 'to: "Ipagiba mo na 'yang pader na binuo niya sa puso mo. Start fresh, bes."
usage_notes: Often used in construction, demolition, or figuratively for destroying abstract things. Note the prefix is `ipa-`, not `ipag-`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdesisyon ang gobyerno na **ipagiba** ang mga bahay na nakatayo sa danger zone.","translation":"The government decided to **have the houses demolished** that were built in the danger zone."},{"sentence":"Kailan kaya nila **ipagigiba** ang lumang sinehan sa kanto?","translation":"When will they **demolish** the old movie theater on the corner?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng kita ng isang korporasyon na ipinamamahagi sa mga may-ari ng sapi (shareholders), karaniwang batay sa bilang ng sapi na pagmamay-ari.
original_explanation: This is the 'cha-ching!' moment for stock market investors. It's the company's way of saying "Thanks for trusting us with your money, here's your share of the profits." It's like getting a bonus from a company you don't even work for. Ang **dibidendo** ang patunay na hindi lang feelings ang pwedeng i-invest.
usage_notes: Primarily used in business, finance, and economics contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **dibidendo** na natanggap ng mga investor ngayong taon dahil sa magandang kita ng kumpanya.","translation":"The investors received a large **dividend** this year because of the company's good profits."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang **dibidendo** bawat share ng stocks mo?","translation":"How much is the **dividend** per share of your stocks?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalahati ng mundo o daigdig, na karaniwang hinahati ng Ekwador (sa Hilaga at Timog) o ng isang meridyan (sa Silangan at Kanluran).
original_explanation: 'Half-world.' It's what separates the Northern peeps from the Southern peeps (Northern Hemisphere vs. Southern Hemisphere). It's a geographical term you probably last heard in your Araling Panlipunan class. Parang LDR goals, magkaibang hating-daigdig pero iisa ang puso. Char.
usage_notes: A formal, geographical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay matatagpuan sa Hilagang **Hating-daigdig**.","translation":"The Philippines is located in the Northern **Hemisphere**."},{"sentence":"Magkaiba ang panahon sa Hilaga at Timog na **Hating-daigdig**.","translation":"The seasons are different in the Northern and Southern **Hemispheres**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na may simbolong Cs at atomikong bilang na 55. Ito ay isang malambot at kulay-pilak na gintong alkali metal.
original_explanation: This is one of those words you only hear in chemistry class. You'll probably never need to ask for 'sesyum' at the palengke. It's a super reactive metal used in atomic clocks, which are way more accurate than your body clock that wakes you up at 3 AM for no reason.
usage_notes: Scientific term used in academic and technical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sesyum** ay ginagamit sa paggawa ng mga atomikong orasan.","translation":"**Cesium** is used in making atomic clocks."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang mga katangian ng elementong **sesyum** sa laboratoryo.","translation":"They are studying the properties of the element **cesium** in the laboratory."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbuo, pag-umpisa, o pagtayo ng isang organisasyon, samahan, o institusyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na ikaw at ang barkada mo ay nag-decide na gumawa ng sarili niyong clan sa Mobile Legends or mag-start ng small business na milk tea. Kayo ang founders. "Let's magtatag a new world order... of coffee shops."
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb "magtatag". It implies an action that will be done.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtatatag** sila ng isang bagong kumpanya sa susunod na taon.","translation":"They will **establish** a new company next year."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magtatatag** ng pundasyon para sa proyektong ito?","translation":"Who will **found** the foundation for this project?"}]

translation: act of reaching for something high
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-abot sa isang bagay na nasa itaas sa pamamagitan ng pag-unat ng kamay o katawan.
original_explanation: That tiptoe-and-stretch move you do to get the last can of Spam from the top shelf at the grocery. It’s what short people have to master to survive. It’s also what you do to reach for your dreams, but literally.
usage_notes: A very specific and uncommon word. 'Pag-abot' is the general and much more common term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahirapan siya sa **pagdawi** ng prutas sa mataas na sanga.","translation":"He had difficulty in **reaching for** the fruit on the high branch."},{"sentence":"Isang mabilis na **pagdawi** ang ginawa niya upang makuha ang aklat.","translation":"He made a quick **reach** to get the book."}]

translation: to heat up; to make something hot
meaning_filipino: Gawing mainit o dagdagan ang init ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay nito sa apoy, microwave, o anumang pagkukunan ng init.
original_explanation: The command you give to your younger sibling for your leftover Jollibee. '**Painitin** mo nga 'tong chickenjoy!' It's the act of bringing something back to its glorious, comforting, warm state, whether it's last night's sinigang or a conversation that has gone cold.
usage_notes: Verb in imperative/infinitive form. Other forms: `pinainit` (past), `pinapainit` (present), `papainitin` (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **painitin** ang sopas bago ihain.","translation":"Please **heat up** the soup before serving."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **painitin** ang makina ng kotse tuwing umaga.","translation":"You need **to warm up** the car's engine every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtangan sa isang mahirap na sitwasyon, sakit, o damdamin nang hindi nagrereklamo o sumusuko.
original_explanation: The official verb of the Filipino martyr complex. Ito 'yung ginagawa mo kapag LDR kayo ng jowa mo, kapag ang bagal ng internet sa Pinas, o kapag kailangan mong ngumiti sa harap ng chismosang tita. You just suck it up and **endure**. 'Konti na lang, makakaraos din.'
usage_notes: Often used in imperative form ('Tiisin mo!') to command someone to endure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tiisin** mo muna ang hirap, may ginhawa ring darating.","translation":"**Endure** the hardship for now, relief will come."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko na kayang **tiisin** ang sakit ng ulo ko.","translation":"I can no longer **bear** this headache."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagluluto ng bigas upang maging kanin, karaniwang ginagamitan ng tubig at init.
etymology: From "saing" (to cook rice). The "pag- -an" affix indicates the process of the action.
original_explanation: The most important chore in any Filipino household. If your household was a company, this would be the key performance indicator (KPI). Fail at this, and you fail at life. It's a sacred ritual that separates the 'pabigat' from the 'aasahan'. Master the perfect water-to-rice ratio using just your finger, and you've unlocked a core Filipino life skill.
usage_notes: A very specific term. You don't "magluto" (cook) rice, you "magsaing".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan ang **pagsasaing** bago ka umalis.","translation":"Don't forget the **act of cooking rice** before you leave."},{"sentence":"Dalubhasa na si Ana sa **pagsasaing** gamit ang kalang de-uling.","translation":"Ana is already an expert in **cooking rice** using a charcoal stove."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tiyak na araw sa isang buwan o taon, na karaniwang tinutukoy sa pamamagitan ng numero.
original_explanation: "Ano'ng pitsa na ngayon?" is the question you ask on a Monday that feels like a Friday. It's the number on the calendar you're staring at, waiting for payday ('pitsa de peligro'). Not to be confused with a romantic date, although you might ask for the 'pitsa' to schedule a 'date'.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the calendar date, not a romantic appointment (which is just 'date') or the fruit (which is 'datiles' or the English word 'dates').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalimutan ko kung anong **pitsa** ngayon.","translation":"I forgot what the **date** is today."},{"sentence":"Tandaan mo ang **pitsa** ng ating anibersaryo.","translation":"Remember the **date** of our anniversary."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang manatiling walang asawa o hindi mag-aasawa (para sa isang lalaki).
original_explanation: This is the life choice of a guy who decides to be a "forever single" tito. It's when a man chooses not to get married, either by choice or... well, let's just say by choice. He's embracing the bachelor life permanently.
usage_notes: The female equivalent is 'magdalaga'. This implies a conscious or eventual decision, not just the current state of being unmarried.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa dami ng kabiguan sa pag-ibig, nagpasya siyang **magbinata** na lang.","translation":"With so many heartbreaks, he decided to just **remain a bachelor**."},{"sentence":"Ang panganay na anak na lalaki ay nangakong **magbibinata** upang alagaan ang kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"The eldest son promised to **remain unmarried** to take care of his parents."}]

translation: to spend, to devote, to allocate
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaan o paggamit ng isang bagay, tulad ng oras, lakas, o yaman, para sa isang partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: When you spend your entire weekend binge-watching a K-drama instead of doing chores, you igugol your time. It's like investing your resources (time, money, effort) into something, whether it's for your career, your hobby, or your jowa. 'Saan mo ba iginugol ang sahod mo?'
usage_notes: Often used with abstract nouns like 'oras' (time), 'lakas' (strength), 'buhay' (life), 'pera' (money).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **igugol** ang kanyang oras sa pagtulong sa kapwa.","translation":"He wants to **devote** his time to helping others."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **igugol** ang iyong lakas sa mga bagay na walang kabuluhan.","translation":"Don't **spend** your energy on things that are meaningless."}]

translation: To bail out water; to scoop out liquid.
meaning_filipino: Alisin ang tubig o anumang likido mula sa isang sisidlan o lugar gamit ang isang pansalok tulad ng tabo o timba.
etymology: From mag- (verb prefix) + limas (bailing out water).
original_explanation: The official sport during typhoon season. When Baha Maries attacks your living room, you and your family grab a 'tabo' and a 'timba' and maglimas for your lives. It's an extreme workout and a bonding experience, all in one.
usage_notes: Often associated with floods or boats taking on water.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **maglimas** ng tubig sa bangka bago ito lumubog.","translation":"We need to **bail out** water from the boat before it sinks."},{"sentence":"Buong magdamag silang nagtulungan na **maglimas** ng baha sa loob ng kanilang bahay.","translation":"They worked together all night to **scoop out** the floodwater from inside their house."}]

translation: to name; to call; to dub
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng pangalan, bansag, o katawagan ang isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: It's what you do when you give your friend a nickname based on that one embarrassing thing they did. Or when the media dubs a new love team. "Siya ang itinaguring 'Pambansang Kamao'." It's the act of officially or unofficially bestowing a title.
usage_notes: Often used in a formal or literary context to mean "to be known as" or "to be called."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Jose Rizal ay **itinaguring** pambansang bayani ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Jose Rizal is **dubbed** the national hero of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang kabaitan, **itinaguri** siyang 'Anghel ng Tondo' ng kanyang mga kapitbahay.","translation":"Because of her kindness, she was **named** the 'Angel of Tondo' by her neighbors."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sukdulang kasamaan, kabuktutan, o kalupitan ng isang tao o gawa.
etymology: Nagmula sa "ka-imbi-an", na nangangahulugang ang estado o katangian ng pagiging 'imbi' (hamak, buktot, masama).
original_explanation: This is the word you use for the supervillain in a teleserye, the one who plots to steal the family fortune, poisons the protagonist, and laughs maniacally while doing it. It’s not just being bad; it’s being evil on a whole other level. It's the highest tier of "kasamaan."
usage_notes: Isang malakas at pampanitikang salita na nagpapahiwatig ng matinding kasamaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mailarawan ang **kaimbihan** na ginawa ng mga kontrabida sa kasaysayan.","translation":"The **depravity** committed by the villains in history is indescribable."},{"sentence":"Sa huli, pagbabayaran din niya ang lahat ng kanyang **kaimbihan**.","translation":"In the end, he will pay for all his **wickedness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alsa o paglaki ng isang bahagi ng katawan o bagay dahil sa pamamaga, likido, o hangin.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your eyes after a major 'iyak' session over your K-drama oppa. Or what happens to your ankle after a bad fall. It's getting puffy or swollen. Pwede rin sa pisngi ng baby, "Ang cute, namimintog ang pisngi!"
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa mga bahagi ng katawan, pag-alsa ng masa ng tinapay, o anumang bagay na lumolobo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mamintog** ang kanyang daliri matapos maipit sa pinto.","translation":"His finger started to **swell** after getting caught in the door."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **mamintog** ang masa bago ito iluto.","translation":"Let the dough **rise** (become plump) before cooking it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpulupot o pagbilo ng isang bagay tulad ng sinulid, tali, o alambre sa isang bagay o sa sarili nito. Ito ang gagawing pag-ikid.
original_explanation: Future tense of 'ikid'. Think of winding up your charger cord so it doesn't look like a plate of spaghetti, or how your lola winds yarn into a ball. "Bes, iikid ko lang 'tong sinulid para sa project natin." It’s the act of making something neatly coiled.
usage_notes: Contemplated aspect (future tense) of 'mag-ikid' or 'i-ikid'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **iikid** ang sinulid sa karete.","translation":"She **will** carefully **wind** the thread onto the spool."},{"sentence":"**Iikid** ko muna ang extension cord para hindi tayo matisod.","translation":"I **will coil** the extension cord first so we don't trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae na nasa isang romantikong relasyon sa isang tao; kasintahan. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang babaeng nakatakda nang ikasal.
original_explanation: Your girlfriend. Your jowa. The one you post on your IG stories with a cheesy caption. The word **nobya** sounds a bit more formal than 'girlfriend,' like something your lola would ask: 'May **nobya** ka na ba, apo?' It can also mean fiancée, making it the final boss before 'asawa.'
usage_notes: The male equivalent is 'nobyo'. 'Kasintahan' is a more native Tagalog equivalent. The term can mean either girlfriend or fiancée depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakilala na ni Marco ang kanyang **nobya** sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"Marco finally introduced his **girlfriend** to his parents."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng singsing na ibinigay niya sa kanyang **nobya** para sa kanilang engagement.","translation":"The ring he gave his **fiancée** for their engagement is beautiful."}]

translation: to oppress, to scorn, to maltreat
meaning_filipino: Apihin, hamakin, o maliitin ang isang tao; tratuhin nang walang paggalang o pagpapahalaga.
original_explanation: What netizens do in the comments section. When you post a harmless opinion and suddenly everyone's an expert trying to **alipustain** your entire existence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **alipustain** ang iyong kapwa dahil lamang sa kanilang estado sa buhay.","translation":"Do not **maltreat** your fellow human just because of their status in life."}]

translation: Nobility; state of being of noble blood
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging kabilang sa isang marangal o maharlikang angkan.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'alta' society. It's the state of having blue blood, being part of the royalty or nobility. Think pre-colonial 'maharlika' or the royal families in Europe. Today, we might use it jokingly to describe someone who acts very prim and proper, or someone who refuses to eat at a 'carinderia'. 'Ayaw kumain ng isaw? Grabe ang pagkadugong-marangal.'
usage_notes: A compound noun, often used in historical or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki ng pamilya ang kanilang **pagkadugong-marangal**.","translation":"The family is proud of their **noble lineage**."},{"sentence":"Sa mga nobela, ang **pagkadugong-marangal** ay madalas na isang mahalagang tema.","translation":"In novels, the state of **being of noble blood** is often an important theme."}]

translation: to ponder; to reflect on; to contemplate
meaning_filipino: Pag-isipang mabuti at malalim ang isang bagay; magnilay-nilay.
original_explanation: This is that 3 AM mood when you're staring at the ceiling, thinking about your life choices, that awkward thing you said in 2012, or kung ano uulamin bukas. It's deep thought, the kind that requires a cup of coffee or a long bus ride. Kailangan mong bulaybulayin kung magre-resign ka na ba o titiisin mo pa ang toxic mong work environment.
usage_notes: Implies a deeper, more prolonged, and serious form of thinking than 'isipin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magandang **bulaybulayin** ang mga aral na natutunan natin sa nakaraang taon.","translation":"It's good to **reflect on** the lessons we learned from the past year."},{"sentence":"Habang nag-iisa, madalas niyang **bulaybulayin** ang kanyang kinabukasan.","translation":"While alone, he often **ponders** his future."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balbal na pagbigkas ng pariralang Ingles na "Oh my God," na ginagamit upang ipahayag ang pagkagulat, pagkamangha, o matinding damdamin.
etymology: A phonetic, slang spelling and pronunciation of the English phrase "Oh my God," popularized through social media and gay lingo.
original_explanation: It's "Oh my God!" but said in a super Pinoy, often high-pitched, "I can't believe it" way. It’s the sound you make when you see a celebrity at the mall, hear the latest chismis, or see the 70% off sign. "Emeged, ang guwapo niya!" is the standard reaction.
usage_notes: Used to express shock, excitement, or disbelief, often in a humorous or exaggerated manner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Emeged**, nakapasa ako sa exam!","translation":"**Oh my God**, I passed the exam!"},{"sentence":"Nakita mo ba 'yung bagong sapatos niya? **Emeged**, ang ganda!","translation":"Did you see her new shoes? **Oh my God**, they're beautiful!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magkaroon ng yupi o pagkalubog sa isang bahagi ng ibabaw dahil sa pagkakabangga o pagkakadiin.
original_explanation: When your Grab car gets a small bump and now there's a little "dimple" on the door. Or when you drop your Hydro Flask and it's no longer perfectly cylindrical. That dent? That's a *kupi*. The state of being dented is *makuping*. It’s that minor, annoying damage that isn’t a total wreck but ruins the aesthetic.
usage_notes: Used for surfaces, especially metal, that have been indented.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mong huwag mabitawan ang lata para hindi ito **makuping**.","translation":"Be careful not to drop the can so it won't **get dented**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga maliliit at pinong butil ng bato at mineral na matatagpuan sa mga dalampasigan, disyerto, o ilog.
original_explanation: Ah, 'buhangin'. The stuff that signals "BEACH TRIP!" It's what you build castles with, what gets in your shoes, your bag, your food, and somehow follows you home for weeks. It's the reason for Boracay's fame and the main ingredient in every "I miss the beach" post. It's basically glitter from the earth.
usage_notes: A very common word. Can refer to beach sand, desert sand, or sand used in construction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaputi ng **buhangin** sa mga dalampasigan ng Palawan.","translation":"The **sand** on the beaches of Palawan is so white."},{"sentence":"Naglaro ang mga bata ng paggawa ng kastilyong **buhangin**.","translation":"The children played by making **sand** castles."}]

translation: to entertain oneself; to find solace
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aliw sa sarili upang maibsan ang lungkot, pagkabagot, o anumang bigat na nararamdaman.
original_explanation: This is a deep, old-school word for "me time." Before Netflix and chill, people would "magliliwliw." It's about finding comfort or distraction, maybe by watching the sunset, listening to music, or just daydreaming. It’s the OG way of coping before hugot culture made it loud.
usage_notes: A somewhat archaic or literary term. Not commonly used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta siya sa dalampasigan upang doon **magliliwliw** at mag-isip-isip.","translation":"He went to the beach to **find solace** there and reflect."},{"sentence":"Ang pagbabasa ng libro ang paraan niya upang **magliliwliw**.","translation":"Reading books is her way to **entertain herself**."}]

translation: to long for; to eagerly anticipate
meaning_filipino: Makaramdam ng matinding pananabik, pag-asam, o pagnanais para sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when you're waiting for your Shopee/Lazada package to be delivered. It's the 'Is it here yet? Is it here yet?' vibe. It’s the excitement for the next episode of your favorite K-drama, the 'sana bukas na agad' feeling. It's a mix of excitement and impatience.
usage_notes: Conveys a stronger, more emotional sense of looking forward to something than 'maghintay' (to wait).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **nanabik** akong makita kang muli.","translation":"I am really **longing** to see you again."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ay **nananabik** na para sa Pasko.","translation":"The children are **eagerly anticipating** Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng katas o likido mula sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagdiin o pagpisil dito.
original_explanation: This is the action verb. **Pigain** mo 'yung orange. **Pigain** mo 'yung basahan. But also, ito 'yung ginagawa sa'yo ng boss mo for information about your chismosa officemate. "Piniga ako ni Ma'am kung sino daw 'yung late!" It means to extract something forcefully.
usage_notes: Ang diin ay nasa bagay na pinipiga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pigain** nang maigi ang niyog para makuha ang lahat ng gata.","translation":"You need **to squeeze** the coconut well to get all the coconut milk."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **pigain** ang espongha at baka masira.","translation":"Don't **squeeze** the sponge too hard or it might get damaged."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng pagiging hindi sapat; ang kawalan ng isang bagay na kailangan o inaasahan.
etymology: From circumfix `ka- -an` + `kulang` (lacking, insufficient). The circumfix turns the adjective 'kulang' into a noun representing the state or quality of being insufficient.
original_explanation: The reason your project is late ("kakulangan sa oras"), why you can't buy concert tickets ("kakulangan sa budget"), or that feeling when someone says "we need to talk" ("kakulangan sa communication"). It’s that gap between what you have and what you need. The story of our lives every "petsa de peligro".
usage_notes: A very versatile word used to describe a lack of anything, whether tangible (food, money) or intangible (time, love, knowledge).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kakulangan** sa tulog ay masama para sa kalusugan.","translation":"A **lack** of sleep is bad for one's health."},{"sentence":"Mayroong **kakulangan** sa suplay ng tubig sa aming lugar.","translation":"There is a water supply **shortage** in our area."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na labis na nahuhumaling sa pagtatrabaho at madalas ay isinasantabi ang personal na buhay at kalusugan.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, this is both a badge of honor and a cry for help. It's your BPO friend who's always on OT, your boss who emails you at 2 AM, or maybe even you, powered by three cups of coffee and the fear of deadlines. We call them 'sipag' (hardworking), but when the 'sipag' starts ignoring family, friends, and sleep... that's workaholic territory. The line is thinner than your patience during rush hour.
usage_notes: Used identically to its English meaning. Can be used as a noun ('He is a workaholic') or an adjective ('She has workaholic tendencies').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyado kang **workaholic**, magpahinga ka naman.","translation":"You're too much of a **workaholic**, get some rest."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa opisina bilang isang tunay na **workaholic** na laging nag-o-overtime.","translation":"He is known in the office as a true **workaholic** who always works overtime."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang tao na mahilig magtanong o mag-usisa tungkol sa mga bagay-bagay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (na bumubuo ng pang-uri) + `tanong`.
original_explanation: ‘Yung friend mong parang walking Google search bar. Hindi nauubusan ng "bakit?" at "paano?". Perfect maging investigative journalist, o kaya 'yung kapitbahay na alam lahat ng chismis sa barangay. "Curiosity killed the cat" pero sa kanya, "Curiosity gets the tea."
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga bata na likas na mausisa, ngunit maaari ring tumukoy sa isang matanda na mapang-usisa o simpleng mahilig magtanong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiya sa guro, mas mabuting maging **matanong** kaysa manatiling walang alam.","translation":"Don't be shy with the teacher, it's better to be **inquisitive** than to remain ignorant."},{"sentence":"Ang bunsong anak ni Aling Nena ay sadyang **matanong**; lahat na lang ay gusto niyang malaman.","translation":"Aling Nena's youngest child is very **inquisitive**; she wants to know about everything."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining at agham ng pagdidisenyo at pagtatayo ng mga gusali at iba pang pisikal na istruktura.
original_explanation: Ito yung "look and feel" ng mga building. Yung itsura ng mga lumang simbahan sa Intramuros, yung design ng mga nagtataasang condo sa BGC, at yung plano ng bahay na pinapangarap mo—lahat 'yan arkitektura. It’s the art you can live in.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahanga-hanga ang **arkitektura** ng mga lumang simbahan sa Ilocos.","translation":"The **architecture** of the old churches in Ilocos is amazing."},{"sentence":"Nag-aaral siya ng **arkitektura** sa isang kilalang unibersidad.","translation":"He is studying **architecture** at a well-known university."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng malawak na kapangyarihan, lakas, o impluwensya sa iba.
etymology: From "maka-" + "pangyarihan" (power), which is derived from "yari" (to happen, to make).
original_explanation: Think of the CEO who can approve your vacation leave with a single nod, the 'tita' who knows all the chismis, or a superhero from a Marvel movie. They hold the power, the 'kapangyarihan'. This word describes them.
usage_notes: Used to describe people, entities (countries, companies), or even abstract concepts (love, faith).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang **makapangyarihan** na pinuno sa kanilang bansa.","translation":"He is a **powerful** leader in their country."},{"sentence":"Naniniwala siya sa **makapangyarihan** na epekto ng panalangin.","translation":"She believes in the **powerful** effect of prayer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, lalo na lalaki, na kasapi o tagasunod ng Simbahang Katoliko Romano; o tumutukoy sa relihiyong ito.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'católico' (Katoliko, panlalaki).
original_explanation: The default religion you see on forms in the Philippines. He's the guy who gets a palm frond for his car on Palm Sunday, goes to Simbang Gabi for the puto bumbong, and whose faith is tested daily by Metro Manila traffic. Can be used for males or the religion in general.
usage_notes: Ang anyong panlalaki o pangkalahatang termino. Gamitin ang 'Katolika' para sa mga babae.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay isang bansang mayoryang **Katoliko**.","translation":"The Philippines is a predominantly **Catholic** country."},{"sentence":"Siya ay isang **Katoliko** mula pagkabata.","translation":"He has been a **Catholic** since childhood."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay o konsepto na naisama o naging bahagi ng isang mas malaking kabuuan; legal na nakarehistro bilang korporasyon.
original_explanation: The masculine version of 'inkorporada'. While 'inkorporada' is for companies ('la corporación'), 'inkorporado' can be used more broadly for things that have been 'incorporated' or 'included'. "The feedback from the team has been incorporated into the final report." But honestly, you'll almost never hear this in casual conversation. People will just say "sinama" or "kasama na."
usage_notes: Less common than 'inkorporada' in business contexts in the Philippines. More likely to be used in its general sense of 'included' in very formal or academic writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bagong tuntunin ay **inkorporado** na sa patakaran ng kumpanya.","translation":"The new rules are now **incorporated** into the company's policy."},{"sentence":"Isang negosyong **inkorporado** ang itinatag ng magkapatid.","translation":"An **incorporated** business was established by the siblings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na tawag sa kapatid, partikular na sa kapatid na lalaki.
etymology: Slang, likely a shortened and altered form of 'kaputol', from 'kaputol ng pusod' (cut from the same umbilical cord).
original_explanation: Your 'utol' is your brother from the same mother (or another mother, if you're talking about your best bro). It's the Pinoy street term for 'bro' or 'dude' when referring to your actual sibling. It's shorter, punchier, and has that authentic 'kanto' vibe.
usage_notes: Primarily used for a brother, but can be used for a sister. Also used for very close male friends.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pare, pakilala mo naman ako sa maganda mong **utol**.","translation":"Bro, please introduce me to your beautiful **sister**."},{"sentence":"Siya ang bunso kong **utol**.","translation":"He is my youngest **brother**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon kung saan mayroong sabay-sabay o tuloy-tuloy na pagtawa ng maraming tao.
etymology: From "tawa" + "-an" suffix, indicating a place or collective/reciprocal action.
original_explanation: That beautiful sound when the whole barkada gets the joke at the same time. It's the goal of every comedian. "Puno ng tawanan ang kwarto." (The room was full of laughter.) It's the group version of 'tawa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang simpleng kwentuhan ay nauwi sa malakas na **tawanan**.","translation":"The simple chat ended in loud **laughter**."},{"sentence":"Rinig hanggang sa labas ang **tawanan** ng mga bata.","translation":"The children's **laughter** could be heard all the way outside."}]

meaning_filipino: Siyasatin o kapkapan ang isang tao sa pamamagitan ng pag-aangat ng kanyang damit upang tingnan kung may itinatago.
etymology: From 'bulislis' (the state of being lifted or rolled up, e.g., a skirt) + '-in' (verb suffix).
original_explanation: This is a more invasive search than just patting someone down. It's when the security guard at the concert lifts the hem of your shirt to check for... well, whatever you're not supposed to bring in. It's a very specific, slightly awkward, and very Pinoy way of frisking. Kailangang bulislisin ang mga bata kung may tinatago silang kendi bago matulog.
usage_notes: Implies lifting clothing (shirt, pants, skirt) to search for something hidden underneath.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **bulislisin**, wala akong tinatago!","translation":"Don't **frisk me by lifting my clothes**, I'm not hiding anything!"},{"sentence":"Kinakailangang **bulislisin** ng guwardiya ang bawat papasok sa gusali.","translation":"The guard needs to **search** each person entering the building **by lifting their clothes**."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang tigil o walang hinto sa paggawa, pagkilos, o pangyayari.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "tuloy" (continue), na may unlaping "pa-" na nagpapahiwatig ng pagpapatuloy ng isang kilos o estado.
original_explanation: Eto yung status ng traffic sa EDSA tuwing rush hour, patuloy lang ang bagal. Parang yung paborito mong series sa Netflix, patuloy kang nanonood kahit 3 AM na. O yung chismis sa office, patuloy na kumakalat hanggang sa makarating sa HR. It means 'to be continued... indefinitely'.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang aksyon na hindi natitigil. Maaari ring gamitin bilang isang pang-uri (e.g., 'ang patuloy na pag-unlad').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patuloy** siyang nagtatrabaho kahit hatinggabi na.","translation":"He **continued** to work even though it was already midnight."},{"sentence":"Ang **patuloy** na pag-ulan ay nagdulot ng pagbaha.","translation":"The **continuous** rain caused flooding."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking lalagyan na may bibig at hawakan, ginagamit sa pagsasalin at paghahain ng mga inumin tulad ng tubig o katas ng prutas.
original_explanation: The star of every handaan, fiesta, and kiddie party. This is the container for the bright orange juice or the super sweet iced tea that's always present. "Pakiabot ng pitsel, nauuhaw na ako." It's bigger than a glass, smaller than a dispenser, and is almost always made of plastic or glass. The unsung hero of hydration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Punuin mo ng tubig ang **pitsel**.","translation":"Fill the **pitcher** with water."},{"sentence":"Isang **pitsel** ng iced tea ang inorder nila.","translation":"They ordered one **pitcher** of iced tea."}]

translation: to consume completely; to finish off
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ubos ng lahat ng pagkain o inumin sa isang lalagyan; ang pagsaid.
original_explanation: That friend who, during a group dinner, makes sure no food is wasted. They'll finish the last piece of chicken, the last grain of rice, and even the last drop of soup. Sila yung expert sa pag-**tumikis** ng handa. It's the ultimate "leave no trace" policy for food.
usage_notes: Primarily used for food and drink. Has a connotation of thoroughness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gutóm na gutóm ang bata kaya't **tumikis** siya ng isang buong plato ng kanin.","translation":"The child was very hungry, so he **finished off** a whole plate of rice."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **tumikis** ang pitsel ng juice, magtira ka para sa iba.","translation":"Don't **finish off** the pitcher of juice, leave some for the others."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng kasaganaan o labis-labis na suplay ng mga pangangailangan, yaman, o pagkain.
etymology: Isang nominal na anyo na nagmula sa salitang-ugat na 'sagana' (abundant).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate #blessed life. The opposite of *petsa de peligro*. It's when the fridge is full, the pantry is overflowing, and there's always extra rice. Think of a grand fiesta table that never runs out of food. It's prosperity you can see and taste.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at medyo malalim na salita para sa 'kasaganaan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawa'y magdulot ang bagong taon ng **pananagana** sa ating lahat.","translation":"May the new year bring **abundance** to us all."},{"sentence":"Ang masaganang ani ay tanda ng **pananagana** sa kanilang bukirin.","translation":"The bountiful harvest is a sign of **prosperity** on their farm."}]

translation: to feel the urge to defecate
meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman ang paninikip o pag-ipit, partikular sa bahagi ng bituka na hudyat ng pangangailangang dumumi.
etymology: From 'mang-' and 'ipot', which literally means 'bird droppings' but is used colloquially for feces.
original_explanation: This is the 'Code Brown' alert. That sudden, cold-sweat-inducing moment in the middle of EDSA traffic when your stomach declares martial law. It's the ultimate 'hold it in' challenge where the prize is not embarrassing yourself in public. The feeling that a major project in your digestive tract is due... NOW.
usage_notes: This is a colloquial and somewhat humorous term. It is not used in formal or polite conversation. The formal term is 'dudumi' or 'magbabawas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong gulatin, baka **mangipot** ako bigla!","translation":"Don't scare me, I might suddenly **feel the urge to poop**!"},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang kaba, pakiramdam niya ay **nangipot** siya bago ang pagsusulit.","translation":"He was so nervous, he felt like he **had the urge to defecate** before the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkakaroon ng pakiramdam ng pagkasuya o pagkabagot dahil sa labis na pagkakaroon o pagdanas ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Ito yung feeling na "over na, tama na, sobra na!" Parang sa buffet, sa sobrang dami mong kinain, kahit paborito mo pa 'yan, ayaw mo nang makita. "Sawang-sawa na ako sa traffic sa EDSA!" is the national anthem of every commuter.
usage_notes: Often reduplicated as "sawang-sawa" to intensify the feeling of being extremely fed up.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sawang**-sawa na ako sa mga pangako mong napapako.","translation":"I'm so **fed up** with your broken promises."},{"sentence":"Mukhang **sawang** na ang bata sa kaniyang mga laruan.","translation":"The child seems **jaded** with his toys."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang espasyo o guhit sa gilid ng isang papel na walang sulat.
original_explanation: This is how your elementary school teacher spelled 'margin'. It's the Filipinized, phonetic spelling of the English word. While 'margin' is used in business talk, marhen is strictly for the sidelines of your Grade 4 notebook. "Lagyan ng isang pulgadang marhen," the instruction goes.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of writing, paper, and school instructions. It is less common than the English spelling 'margin' in modern usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumuhit ka ng pulang linya sa **marhen** ng papel.","translation":"Draw a red line on the **margin** of the paper."},{"sentence":"Laging malinis ang **marhen** sa kanyang mga kwaderno.","translation":"The **margins** in her notebooks are always clean."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay para sa 'sinyorita'; isang magalang na tawag para sa isang dalaga.
etymology: From Spanish 'señorita' (miss, young lady), via a phonetic spelling variation.
original_explanation: Same as 'sinyorita', just spelled with a 'u'. It's like 'color' vs 'colour' – you know what it means, but you might have a preferred version. This spelling feels a bit more phonetic to a Filipino speaker.
usage_notes: An alternative spelling of 'sinyorita'. Both are acceptable and understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bunsong anak ng Don ay isang napakagandang **sinyurita**.","translation":"The youngest child of the Don is a very beautiful **young lady**."},{"sentence":"Kumusta ka na, **Sinyurita** Isabel?","translation":"How are you, **Miss** Isabel?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar sa dagat, lawa, o ilog kung saan maraming isda ang nahuhuli para sa komersyo o pagkain.
original_explanation: It's the sea's version of a palengke, where the fish hang out before they become your sinigang. Think of it as the 'office' for fishermen. The OG source of your fresh tilapia and bangus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayaman sa isda ang **pangisdaan** sa Palawan.","translation":"The **fishing ground** in Palawan is rich with fish."},{"sentence":"Pinoprotektahan ng gobyerno ang mga lokal na **pangisdaan**.","translation":"The government protects the local **fisheries**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makaramdam o magpakita ng malaking katuwaan o kasiyahan dahil sa isang magandang pangyayari o balita.
original_explanation: This is more than just being 'happy'. This is 'leveled-up' joy. It's the feeling you get when your team wins the championship, when you pass a board exam, or when the 13th-month pay finally comes in. It’s an active, expressive happiness. Think less of a quiet smile and more of a 'YES! WOOOH!' moment. It's a pure, unadulterated 'Salamat, Lord!' kind of vibe.
usage_notes: 'Magalak' is a command or infinitive form. 'Nagalak' is the past tense. 'Nagagalak' is the present tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat tayong **magalak** sa tagumpay ng ating kapwa.","translation":"We should **rejoice** in the success of others."},{"sentence":"**Nagagalak** akong ipaalam sa inyo na nakapasa ako sa pagsusulit.","translation":"I am **joyful** to inform you that I passed the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at hindi makontrol na pangingisay o paggalaw ng katawan, kadalasang sintomas ng isang kondisyong medikal.
original_explanation: This is a serious medical term, but in a very dramatic Filipino context, it's how a Tita might describe someone having an extreme temper tantrum. 'Nagsisigaw siya na parang inaatake ng **taol**!' It's that uncontrollable shaking, whether from a medical issue or, hyperbolically, extreme emotion.
usage_notes: This is a medical term. 'Kombulsyon' is a more common modern synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala agad sa ospital ang bata nang magsimula itong atakihin ng **taol**.","translation":"The child was immediately brought to the hospital when he started having a **seizure**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ihiwalay ang mga bahagi ng isang bagay na magkadikit o magkalapit, tulad ng bibig, aklat, o mga kamay.
original_explanation: What the dentist tells you: "Ibuka mo ang bibig mo." It's also what you do to a book to start reading, or when you're about to receive blessings from the universe. Open up!
usage_notes: Often used for mouths, books, flowers, or hands. Implies opening something from a closed or folded state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi ng dentista, '**ibuka** mo nang malaki ang iyong bibig'.","translation":"The dentist said, '**open** your mouth wide'."},{"sentence":"Nang **ibuka** niya ang kanyang palad, may nakita siyang barya.","translation":"When she **opened** her palm, she saw a coin."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alala o pagbabalik-tanaw sa isang nakaraang pangyayari, tao, o bagay, kadalasan sa isang pormal o seremonyal na paraan.
original_explanation: It's like #ThrowbackThursday in verb form. When you're scrolling through old photos, listening to a song from high school, or celebrating EDSA People Power, you're *gumugunita*. It's remembering with a bit of ceremony or a lot of feelings.
usage_notes: Often used for historical events, anniversaries, or remembering the deceased. It carries a more formal and deeper tone than simply 'alalahanin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Taon-taon, **gumugunita** tayo ng Araw ng Kalayaan.","translation":"Every year, we **commemorate** Independence Day."},{"sentence":"**Gumunita** siya sa masasayang araw nila ng kanyang yumaong asawa.","translation":"She **reminisced** about the happy days with her late husband."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng pagsasala-salabat ng mga sinulid, hibla, o iba pang materyales upang makabuo ng tela, banig, o anumang kauri nito.
original_explanation: This is the OG act of creating something complex from simple threads. Think of your lola making a banig, or you trying to weave together all your alibis when your parents ask where you've been. It's the art of intertwining, whether it's fabric or stories.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of traditional crafts. "Paghahabi" is a more common, intensified form referring to the craft as a whole.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghabi** ng tela ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng kanilang kultura.","translation":"The **weaving** of fabric is an important part of their culture."},{"sentence":"Kinagigiliwan niya ang masalimuot na **paghabi** ng mga kuwento.","translation":"He enjoys the intricate **weaving** of stories."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng pag-asam o pananabik na mangyari ang isang bagay na ninanais; ang tiwala na mayroong posibilidad para sa isang positibong kahihinatnan.
original_explanation: The fuel of every Filipino waiting for the MRT, applying for a visa, or betting on lotto. It's that feeling you get when your crush 'views' your IG story. It's the 'baka sakali' that keeps us going. The ultimate source of 'hugot' and resilience.
usage_notes: A very common and culturally significant word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Habang may buhay, may **pag-asa**.","translation":"While there is life, there is **hope**."},{"sentence":"Siya ang natatanging **pag-asa** ng kanilang pamilya.","translation":"He is the sole **hope** of their family."}]

translation: to feel bad, to be resentful, to have hurt feelings
meaning_filipino: Ang makaramdam ng hinanakit, pagdaramdam, o sama ng loob dahil sa isang kilos, salita, o pangyayari na itinuturing na masakit o hindi makatarungan.
original_explanation: This is the emotional damage! It's that feeling when you were expecting a promotion but it went to the new guy. Or when you thought you and your crush had a "thing" but then you see them posting "in a relationship" with someone else. It's the official feeling of being slighted, the Tagalog version of "I feel personally attacked."
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression. 'Loob' literally means 'inside', so 'sumama ang loob' means 'the inside became bad', referring to one's inner feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumama ang loob** ni Ana dahil hindi siya inimbita sa party.","translation":"Ana **felt bad** because she wasn't invited to the party."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **sumama ang loob** mo sa maliliit na bagay.","translation":"Don't let yourself **get resentful** over small things."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa 'ina' o 'nanay'.
etymology: From swardspeak (Filipino gay lingo), likely a playful corruption of 'mother' or Spanish 'madre'.
original_explanation: Your mom, but in a fabulous, swardspeak way. When 'mommy' or 'nanay' is too plain, you call her your **mudra**. She's the one who gives you life, and also the one who gives you a 10 PM curfew. Often paired with 'pudra' for your dad.
usage_notes: Part of the Beki/gay lingo vocabulary that has crossed over into mainstream colloquial use.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpaalam na ako sa **mudra** ko na gagabihin ako.","translation":"I already told my **mother** I'll be home late."},{"sentence":"Ang **mudra** mo, laging nagtatanong kung kailan ka mag-aasawa.","translation":"Your **mother** is always asking when you're going to get married."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang reaksyon, opinyon, o impormasyon na ibinibigay bilang tugon sa isang produkto, gawain, o pagganap ng isang tao.
original_explanation: In the BPO world, this is your daily bread. 'Praise in public, coach in private'—that's the dream. But usually, feedback feels like your TL reading your chat history with your work bestie. It's also what your tita gives you about your weight, unsolicited. 'Hija, tumataba ka' is a form of... let's call it... 'cultural feedback'.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang hiram na salita na malawakang ginagamit sa mga propesyonal, pang-akademiko, at pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hihintayin ko ang **feedback** ng kliyente bago ko ipagpatuloy ang proyekto.","translation":"I will wait for the client's **feedback** before I continue with the project."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang constructive **feedback** para sa ikabubuti ng trabaho mo.","translation":"Constructive **feedback** is important for the improvement of your work."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nakabitin o nakalawlaw nang walang suporta, karaniwang dahil sa pagkalanta, pagkapagod, o pagiging mabigat.
original_explanation: Yung itsura ng balikat mo after a 12-hour shift. O kaya yung dahon ng halaman na nakalimutan mong diligan for one day. It's giving up, basically. That droopy, sad, 'wala-na-akong-pake' vibe. "Bakit laylay ang mga balikat mo?" "End of the month na, friend. Wallet ko, laylay din."
usage_notes: Often used to describe plants, clothes on a line, or a person's posture (shoulders).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **laylay** ang mga bulaklak dahil sa matinding sikat ng araw.","translation":"The flowers became **droopy** because of the intense heat of the sun."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maglakad nang **laylay** ang mga balikat; i-project mo ang confidence!","translation":"Don't walk with **drooping** shoulders; project confidence!"}]

translation: to flare up; to break out (as in a fire or war)
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagsisimula at paglaki ng apoy, galit, o kaguluhan.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you bring up politics at a family reunion. It's also literally what happens when you pour gasoline on a fire. It’s the sudden, intense eruption of something—be it flames, a fight, or a full-blown "bardagulan" online.
