usage_notes: Used for both literal fires and metaphorical outbursts of emotion or conflict.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat sila sa paggamit ng kandila upang hindi **magsiklab** ang sunog.","translation":"They were careful using the candle so that a fire would not **break out**."},{"sentence":"Maaaring **magsiklab** ang gulo kung hindi sila magkakasundo.","translation":"A conflict might **flare up** if they don't come to an agreement."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na panlunan na pinaikling anyo ng "dini", na nangangahulugang sa lugar na ito. Ginagamit pagkatapos ng salitang nagtatapos sa patinig.
etymology: Isang anyo ng "dini", na siya namang anyo ng "dito". Sumusunod sa panuntunang D-R (pagpapalit ng /d/ sa /r/ pagkatapos ng patinig).
original_explanation: "Rini" is the more casual, spoken-word version of "dito." It's what you say when you're calling your friend over: "Hoy, punta ka rini!" It's the "dito" that's wearing shorts and tsinelas. Follows the same D-R rule: you use "dini" after a consonant and "rini" after a vowel.
usage_notes: Colloquial variant of 'dini'. Used after words ending in a vowel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halika **rini** sa tabi ko.","translation":"Come **here** beside me."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka ba napunta **rini**?","translation":"Why did you end up **here**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang supling na ang kasarian ay lalaki.
original_explanation: The family's designated 'tagabuhat ng mabibigat' (carrier of heavy things) and 'taga-bukas ng mahigpit na garapon' (opener of tight jars). He's the one you send to the sari-sari store for suka and toyo.
usage_notes: Madalas na pinaikli sa "anak" lamang kapag malinaw na sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang panganay niyang **anak na lalaki** ay nag-aaral na sa kolehiyo.","translation":"Her eldest **son** is now studying in college."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malawakan at madalas ay magulong paghahanap sa isang lugar, karaniwang ginagawa ng may awtoridad upang makahanap ng ebidensya o kontrabando.
original_explanation: This is 'paghahalikwat' on steroids. This is what happens in movies when the NBI raids a warehouse. It's a no-stone-unturned, everything-gets-tossed-around kind of search. It's also what your mom does to your room looking for your 'hidden' report card, leaving a trail of chaos in her wake.
usage_notes: Often implies an official or forceful search, and usually results in a mess. More intense than 'paghahalikwat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **paghahalughog** ang mga pulis sa bahay ng suspek.","translation":"The police conducted a **thorough search** of the suspect's house."},{"sentence":"Ang ginawa ng nanay sa kwarto ko ay hindi paglilinis, kundi **paghahalughog**.","translation":"What my mom did to my room wasn't cleaning, but **ransacking**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-ukit o pagtapyas sa matitigas na materyales tulad ng bato o kahoy gamit ang pait; maaari ring tumukoy sa maliit na pait.
original_explanation: Ang pag-ukit with feelings. Kung paano ka 'sinilsil' ng mga problema mo into the person you are today. Charot. Ito yung ginagawa ng mga iskultor sa Paete, Laguna. Requires precision and patience, parang pag-move on. Unti-unting pagtapyas hanggang mabuo ang gusto mong design.
usage_notes: Maaari ring maging pandiwa: 'silsilin' (to chisel something), 'sumilsil' (to chisel).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat ang pagka-**silsil** ng pangalan sa lapida.","translation":"The **chiseling** of the name on the tombstone was done carefully."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **silsil** at martilyo upang umukit sa kahoy.","translation":"He used a **chisel** and hammer to carve the wood."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na uri o espesye ng halamang tayum (Indigofera suffruticosa), na katulad ng tayuman at pinagkukunan din ng pangkulay.
etymology: From 'tayum', the name of the plant.
original_explanation: The cousin of 'tayuman'. It's like the difference between iPhone 14 and iPhone 14 Pro – very similar, both used for the same thing (making blue dye), but technically a different species. This is for the plantitos and plantitas who are *really* into historical Philippine flora.
usage_notes: Less common than 'tayuman'. Often used interchangeably in non-scientific contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bahagyang pagkakaiba ang dahon ng **tayumin** sa karaniwang tayuman.","translation":"The leaf of the **tayumin** plant has a slight difference from the common indigo plant."},{"sentence":"Ang **tayumin** ay isa pa ring mabisang pangkulay.","translation":"The **tayumin** is still an effective coloring agent."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng sarili sa isang bagay upang umupo; pag-okupa sa isang upuan o espasyo sa pamamagitan ng pag-upo.
etymology: From 'upo' (to sit) + '-an' (verb suffix indicating action upon an object/location).
original_explanation: The act of claiming your territory with your butt. Yung sinabihan ka ng nanay mo, 'Huwag mong upungan 'yang mesa, hindi 'yan silya!' O 'yung moment na may nakita kang bakanteng upuan sa bus at gusto mo nang sabihin sa katabi mo, 'Upungan mo na, bago pa maagaw ng iba!'
usage_notes: This is the verb form. 'Upuan' is the noun (chair), while 'upungan' is the action of sitting on it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal **upungan** ang mga display na kama sa department store.","translation":"It's forbidden **to sit on** the display beds in the department store."},{"sentence":"Alin sa mga silyang ito ang gusto mong **upungan**?","translation":"Which of these chairs do you want **to sit on**?"}]

translation: to laugh (involuntarily); to burst into laughter
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang paglabas ng tunog ng katuwaan o pagkasuklam, karaniwang may kasamang paggalaw ng bibig at katawan.
original_explanation: That moment when you're trying to keep a straight face in a serious meeting, but your work bestie sends you a meme. The urge to not matawa is a real struggle. It's not a choice; it just happens. 'Tumawa' is laughing on purpose, matawa is when it bursts out of you.
usage_notes: Often used to describe an uncontrollable or sudden burst of laughter, as opposed to 'tumawa' which can be more deliberate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko mapigilang **matawa** sa biro niya.","translation":"I couldn't help but **laugh** at his joke."},{"sentence":"Nang makita niya ang itsura ko, bigla siyang **natawa**.","translation":"When she saw my face, she suddenly **burst into laughter**."}]

meaning_filipino: Biglaang naputol o nakawala mula sa pagkakatali o pagkakakabit nang may malakas na puwersa.
original_explanation: Yung pasensya mo na parang rubber band, stretched to its limit, tapos biglang... *snap*. That's bumigtal. It’s more sudden and violent than just 'naputol'. It's the final straw, the epic rage quit, the snapped cable of a suspension bridge in an action movie.
usage_notes: Implies a sudden, forceful, and often violent break. Less common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang higpit ng pagkatali, **bumigtal** ang lubid.","translation":"Because it was tied so tightly, the rope **snapped**."},{"sentence":"Parang **bumigtal** ang isang ugat sa utak ko sa sobrang inis.","translation":"It felt like a vein in my brain **snapped** from so much annoyance."}]

translation: to have a heated argument; to have friction
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng matinding pagtatalo, alitan, o hindi pagkakasundo sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
etymology: From `mag-` + `ka-` + `init` + `-an`, indicating a mutual or reciprocal state of being "heated."
original_explanation: When the "friendly" debate about politics on Facebook turns into personal attacks and blocked accounts. It's when you and your sibling argue over the TV remote and it escalates into bringing up mistakes from 10 years ago. The 'init' here isn't about temperature, it's about the 'init ng ulo' (hot-headedness).
usage_notes: Refers to emotional or verbal conflict, not physical temperature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagkainitan** ang dalawang kandidato sa gitna ng debate.","translation":"The two candidates **had a heated argument** in the middle of the debate."},{"sentence":"Iwasan nating **magkainitan** dahil lang sa maliliit na bagay.","translation":"Let's avoid **getting into a heated conflict** over small things."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-angat o pag-alis ng isang bagay mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba, na karaniwang nangangailangan ng lakas.
original_explanation: The official verb of every "lipat-bahay" session, gym day ("Leg day, bro!"), or when you have to carry the weight of your team in a group project. `Magbuhat` is the physical act of lifting something heavy, whether it's a sack of rice, a dumbbell, or the emotional baggage from your ex.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical and metaphorical lifting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magbuhat** ng mga kahon na ito.","translation":"Help me **lift** these boxes."},{"sentence":"Kailangan niyang **magbuhat** ng sarili niyang bangko para mapansin.","translation":"He needs to **lift** his own chair (praise himself) to get noticed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghingi ng payo o opinyon mula sa isang dalubhasa o eksperto.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa doktor, abogado, o kahit sa best friend mo kapag may problema ka sa lovelife. Basically, asking "Ano'ng gagawin ko, bes?" to someone who (hopefully) knows better. Pwede ring "magpa-konsulta" as a verb.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb root (e.g., kumonsulta, magpakonsulta).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Libre ang unang **konsulta** sa bagong klinika.","translation":"The first **consultation** at the new clinic is free."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **konsulta** mula sa isang abogado tungkol sa kontrata.","translation":"I need a **consultation** from a lawyer regarding the contract."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na papel o midyum na ginagamit sa pagboto, kung saan nakalista ang pangalan ng mga kandidato.
original_explanation: The magical piece of paper that holds the country's future (and a lot of drama). It's longer than your list of exes and requires more shading skills than a makeup artist. Handle with care, baka ma-spoil.
usage_notes: Eksklusibong ginagamit sa konteksto ng eleksyon at pagboto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat niyang inilagay ang kanyang **balota** sa loob ng ballot box.","translation":"She carefully placed her **ballot** inside the ballot box."},{"sentence":"Ilang oras ang inabot sa pagbibilang ng lahat ng **balota**.","translation":"It took several hours to count all the **ballots**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagwasak sa reputasyon o mabuting pangalan ng isang tao sa pamamagitan ng pagkakalat ng kasinungalingan o mapanirang-puri na mga pahayag.
original_explanation: This is the OG "cancel culture" but on a personal, often malicious level. It's what happens when someone spreads fake news or "chismis" so damaging it ruins your name. Think of it as character assassination, the kind that makes your tita give you the side-eye at the next family reunion.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang mabigat na salita para sa paninira at madalas gamitin sa legal na konteksto o seryosong akusasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniniwala sa mga sabi-sabi, layunin lang nilang **siraang-puri** ang kandidato.","translation":"Don't believe the rumors, their only goal is to **defame** the candidate."},{"sentence":"Kinasuhan niya ang kapitbahay dahil sa tangkang **siraang-puri** siya sa buong barangay.","translation":"She sued the neighbor for attempting to **slander** her in the whole village."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salaysay o naratibo na nakatuon sa pag-iibigan at romantikong ugnayan ng mga pangunahing tauhan.
etymology: Mula sa Tagalog na "kuwento" (mula sa Espanyol na "cuento") at Espanyol na "romance".
original_explanation: Your daily dose of kilig. Whether it's a Wattpad story, a K-Drama, or your own delulu narrative about you and your crush, it's a story that makes you go "sana all." The plot usually involves a meet-cute, some misunderstandings, and a dramatic airport scene.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang magbasa ng mga **kuwentong may-romansa** bago matulog.","translation":"She loves reading **romance stories** before sleeping."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang laruang baril o ang laro ng paggamit ng mga laruang baril.
etymology: Reduplication of "baril" (gun) with the suffix "-an", indicating a game or imitation.
original_explanation: The childhood game that probably got you a 'sermon' from your lola. This is playing cops and robbers, Pinoy-style, usually with plastic guns that make 'pew pew' sounds. Today, it might also mean a first-person shooter video game.
usage_notes: Can refer to the toy itself or the game played with it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglalaro ng **baril-barilan** ang mga bata sa kalsada.","translation":"The children are **playing with toy guns** on the street."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo siya ng bagong **baril-barilan** para sa Pasko.","translation":"Give him a new **toy gun** for Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang, dami, o sukat ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: In the palengke, it's asking "Magkano isang kantidad?" when you mean a specific pile or portion. In life, it's realizing that quality is better than kantidad—it's better to have 4 true friends than 4000 fake Facebook friends.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'dami'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumaas ang **kantidad** ng bigas na inaangkat ng gobyerno.","translation":"The **quantity** of rice being imported by the government has increased."},{"sentence":"Anong **kantidad** ng asukal ang kailangan para sa recipe na ito?","translation":"What **amount** of sugar is needed for this recipe?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagbabayad kung saan ang kabayaran para sa isang produkto ay ibinibigay lamang sa oras ng paghahatid nito.
etymology: Acronym mula sa Ingles na 'Cash on Delivery'.
original_explanation: The magic words that make online shopping less scary for people without credit cards. Ito 'yung 'bahala na si Batman' moment mo pagdating ng rider, sabay tanong sa buong bahay kung sino may barya. 'Bayad po muna bago buksan ang parcel.'
usage_notes: Laging binibigkas bilang mga letra (C-O-D). Ito ay isang acronym na naging bahagi na ng pang-araw-araw na usapan dahil sa e-commerce.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**COD** na lang ang payment method na pinili ko sa Shopee.","translation":"I just chose **COD** as the payment method on Shopee."},{"sentence":"Pakihanda ang eksaktong bayad, **COD** itong inorder mo.","translation":"Please prepare the exact amount, you ordered this via **COD**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mataas na plataporma o entablado sa loob ng simbahan kung saan nagbibigay ng sermon ang pari o pastor.
original_explanation: It's the OG TED Talk stage, but in a church. That special elevated box where the priest stands to deliver the homily, making sure everyone can see and hear him, especially those snoozing at the back pews.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in a religious or church context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula sa **pulpito**, narinig ang malakas na boses ng pari.","translation":"From the **pulpit**, the priest's loud voice was heard."},{"sentence":"Ang antigong **pulpito** sa aming simbahan ay gawa sa narra.","translation":"The antique **pulpit** in our church is made of narra wood."}]

meaning_filipino: Nahulog o natanggal mula sa kinalalagyan o pinagkakabitan.
original_explanation: Imagine holding too many groceries and one mango decides it's had enough and just gives up. That's lumaglag. It's not a dramatic 'fall from grace' kind of fall, more like an accidental 'oops, it slipped' situation. Also used for failing an exam. 'Lumaglag ako sa exam, bes.'
usage_notes: Often interchangeable with `nahulog`, but `lumaglag` implies something falling off from a higher position or from where it was attached, like a fruit from a tree or a button from a shirt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumaglag** ang butones ng kanyang damit.","translation":"The button **fell off** his shirt."},{"sentence":"Biglang **lumaglag** ang hinog na mangga mula sa puno.","translation":"The ripe mango suddenly **dropped** from the tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalawakan na nakikita sa itaas ng mundo; ang lugar ng mga ulap, araw, buwan, at bituin. Sa metaporikal na gamit, ito ay tumutukoy sa paraiso o lugar ng mga diyos.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'langit' (sky, heaven) at panlaping 'ka- -an'.
original_explanation: Ito yung nakikita mo pag tumingala ka—pwera na lang kung nasa loob ka ng mall. It's God's default desktop wallpaper. Dito nagaganap ang sunset-viewing-with-coffee session mo sa may baywalk. Sa mas malalim na hugot, ito 'yung lugar kung saan 'tayo na lang dalawa ang nakakaalam.' The ultimate ceiling.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa panitikan, tula, at relihiyosong konteksto. Mas pormal at malawak ang sakop kaysa sa 'langit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang asul na **kalangitan** ay puno ng mapuputing ulap.","translation":"The blue **sky** is full of white clouds."},{"sentence":"Sa gabing iyon, ang **kalangitan** ay nagliwanag dahil sa mga bituin.","translation":"On that night, the **heavens** were bright because of the stars."}]

translation: profuse flow or gush (of liquid, especially blood)
meaning_filipino: Ang sagana o malakas na pag-agos o pagdaloy ng likido, lalo na ng dugo.
etymology: A root word describing a heavy, often sudden, flow of liquid.
original_explanation: This isn't just a drip or a leak. This is a full-on gush. Think of a major nosebleed, a wound in an action movie, or when you accidentally knock over a whole bottle of ketchup. 'Grabe ang **danak** ng dugo mula sa sugat niya.' It’s dramatic and intense. It's the 'buhos' equivalent for bodily fluids.
usage_notes: Often used in its verb form 'dumanak' (to gush) or as part of the noun phrase 'pagdanak ng dugo' (spilling of blood).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangyari ang pag-**danak** ng dugo sa makasaysayang labanang iyon.","translation":"The **spilling** of blood happened in that historic battle."},{"sentence":"Bigla na lang **dumanak** ang dugo mula sa kanyang ilong.","translation":"Blood suddenly **gushed** from his nose."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tao, lugar, o institusyon na pinagkakatiwalaan o pinag-iiwanan ng isang habilin.
original_explanation: You are 'The One.' The chosen one to carry the burden, a.k.a. the habilin. You're the Sam to their Frodo, the person left to water the plants while they're on a 2-week beach trip. You are the official **habilinan** of their prized Funko Pop collection.
usage_notes: This noun refers to the recipient or depository of the 'habilin' (instruction).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ako ang naging **habilinan** ng mga lumang alahas ng aking lola.","translation":"I became the **trustee** of my grandmother's old jewelry."}]

translation: to make someone wear a uniform
meaning_filipino: Atasan ang isang tao o grupo na magsuot ng pare-parehong kasuotan o uniporme.
etymology: From pa- (causative) + pag- (causative) + uniporme (uniform), which is a loanword from Spanish 'uniforme'.
original_explanation: The memo from HR before the company-wide team building. It's the school guard's favorite line: "Bawal pumasok 'pag 'di naka-uniporme!" Basically, to enforce a dress code.
usage_notes: A very specific complex causative verb, exclusively for making people wear a uniform.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak ng management na **papag-unipormihin** ang lahat ng empleyado sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"The management plans to **make** all employees **wear a uniform** next month."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matamis na pampahid o palamuti, karaniwang gawa sa asukal, na inilalagay sa ibabaw ng mga keyk, tinapay, o biskwit.
original_explanation: The best part of any birthday cake from Goldilocks or Red Ribbon. It's the sugary, colorful stuff you either scrape off or fight your siblings for. The "icing on the cake" that makes everything better, literally.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito ng mga bata ang mamon na may maraming **aysing**.","translation":"The kids' favorite is the sponge cake with a lot of **icing**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong ubusin ang **aysing** ng keyk!","translation":"Don't finish all the **icing** on the cake!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng isang dula, pelikula, o anumang pagtatanghal; isang pangyayari na nakakatawag-pansin o madrama.
original_explanation: Can mean two things: 1) A literal scene in a movie ("Favorite ko 'yung eksena na nag-confess na siya."). 2) When someone makes a scene in public. 'Yung jowang nagsisigawan sa gitna ng mall? Ay, gumagawa ng eksena. Papansin, KSP, drama queen/king.
usage_notes: May dalawang pangunahing gamit: literal na eksena sa sining at ang kolokyal na pagtukoy sa isang madramang pangyayari.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumawa ng **eksena** dito sa opisina.","translation":"Don't make a **scene** here in the office."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng huling **eksena** sa pelikula.","translation":"The last **scene** in the movie was beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha ng pagkiskis ng mga ngipin, kadalasan dahil sa galit, pagtitimpi, o habang natutulog. Ito rin ang tunog ng bagay na gumegewang gaya ng sahig na kahoy.
original_explanation: The sound your teeth make when your boss gives you a new task at 4:59 PM on a Friday. It's suppressed rage turned into a dental problem (bruxism). Also the default sound effect in horror movies when a spooky wooden door opens.
usage_notes: Verb form is 'ngumangalitngit'. Can refer to teeth grinding or the creaking sound of objects like wood or metal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **ngalitngit** ng kanyang mga ngipin sa sobrang galit.","translation":"I heard the **grinding** of his teeth due to extreme anger."},{"sentence":"Nakakatakot ang **ngalitngit** ng lumang sahig tuwing gabi.","translation":"The **creaking** of the old floor at night is scary."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging puro, dalisay, at walang anumang halo o bahid ng dumi o kasamaan.
etymology: From `ka-` + `wagas` + `-an`, forming a noun describing the quality of being 'wagas' (pure).
original_explanation: The state of your intentions before you found out your crush was already taken. It's the "100% all-natural, no preservatives" version of a feeling or a thing. Like the love of a dog, or a fresh-from-the-ATM 1000-peso bill.
usage_notes: Often used in a poetic or formal context to describe love, intentions, or character.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahanap niya ang **kawagasan** ng pag-ibig sa isang mundong puno ng pagkukunwari.","translation":"She is searching for the **purity** of love in a world full of pretense."},{"sentence":"Ang **kawagasan** ng kanyang puso ay hinahangaan ng lahat.","translation":"The **genuineness** of his heart is admired by all."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghaharap ng kaso o pagdaan sa legal na proseso upang opisyal na wakasan ang kasal sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of the ultimate uncoupling. When you hear someone say "Diniborsiyuhan niya ang asawa niya," it's the chismis jackpot. It means one person initiated the legal breakup. It's the action of using that (currently unavailable in the PH) 'unsubscribe' button on your spouse.
usage_notes: Used in contexts where divorce is possible, such as for Filipinos married and living abroad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **diborsiyuhan** ang kanyang asawa matapos ang maraming taon ng pag-aaway.","translation":"She decided **to divorce** her husband after many years of fighting."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo ako **diniborsiyuhan**?","translation":"Why did you **divorce** me?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglalagay ng binhi sa lupa upang tumubo; o ang artipisyal o natural na paglalagay ng semilya upang magbunga ng supling.
original_explanation: In agriculture, it’s literally planting seeds. In biology or animal husbandry, it's the more... *technical* way of making babies happen, often with science involved (like for livestock or IVF). It's the very first step in the 'mag-anak ay 'di biro' process.
usage_notes: Can refer to agriculture (sowing seeds) or biology (insemination). The context is crucial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang artipisyal na **pagpapabinhi** ay karaniwan sa pag-aalaga ng mga baka.","translation":"Artificial **insemination** is common in raising cattle."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang mga magsasaka sa **pagpapabinhi** ng palay para sa susunod na anihan.","translation":"The farmers have started **sowing** rice seeds for the next harvest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling at kolokyal na katawagan para sa Starbucks, isang sikat na coffee shop chain.
original_explanation: Short for Starbucks. Kasi saying 'Starbucks' is too much effort, 'di ba? Dito ka nag-aaral, nakikipag-meeting, o tumatambay para mag-flex ng bago mong planner. 'Tara, Starbs tayo after class.'
usage_notes: Very common slang, especially among students and young professionals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **Starbs** sa Megamall mamayang 3 PM.","translation":"Let's meet at **Starbs** in Megamall later at 3 PM."},{"sentence":"Puro picture ng kape mula sa **Starbs** ang Instagram feed niya.","translation":"Her Instagram feed is full of pictures of coffee from **Starbs**."}]

translation: to scrape off, to scratch off, to chip away
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis o pagbakbak ng isang bahagi mula sa ibabaw ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagkaskas o pagkayod.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa lumang pintura sa pader bago ka mag-repaint. O 'yung pagtanggal mo ng natuyong kanin sa kaldero. Pwede ring 'yung aso niyo, kumabkab ng lupa sa garden. "May daga yatang kumakabkab sa ilalim ng sahig."
usage_notes: Implies a scratching or digging action to remove a surface layer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumabkab** ang manok sa lupa upang maghanap ng bulate.","translation":"The chicken **scratched** the ground to look for worms."},{"sentence":"Sinubukang **kumabkab** ng magnanakaw sa pader, ngunit hindi siya nagtagumpay.","translation":"The thief tried to **chip away** at the wall, but he did not succeed."}]

translation: to meet; to welcome; to greet
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpunta sa isang lugar upang hintayin at tanggapin ang pagdating ng isang tao o bagay.
etymology: From `salubong`, meaning 'meeting' or 'encounter'. The suffix `-in` makes it a verb indicating an action to be done to an object.
original_explanation: The act of meeting someone halfway, literally. Like when your GrabFood driver calls and says 'Nandito na po ako sa labas,' and you go out to get your food. You're not just waiting, you're actively going to meet them. It's also what you do for your balikbayan Tita at the airport.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of welcoming guests or meeting someone who is arriving.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Salubungin** mo ang iyong mga lolo at lola sa may pintuan.","translation":"**Meet** your grandparents at the door."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating **salubungin** ang Bagong Taon nang may sama ng loob.","translation":"Let's not **welcome** the New Year with grudges."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang utos na mag-alis ng isang bahagi, bawasan ang dami, o hinaan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the command form. When your mom yells "Bawas-bawasan mo nga yang kaka-computer mo!", she's telling you to reduce your screen time. It's the act of cutting back. Think 'lessen'.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa anyong pautos o bilang salitang-ugat para sa ibang pandiwa tulad ng 'bawasan', 'bawasin', at 'magbawas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bawas**! Masyadong malakas ang tugtog.","translation":"**Reduce** (it)! The music is too loud."},{"sentence":"Ang payo ng doktor ay **magbawas** ng pagkain ng matataba.","translation":"The doctor's advice is to **reduce** eating fatty foods."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyon kung saan ipinadadala ang mga kabataang nagkasala sa batas upang sila ay maturuan, ma-rehabilitate, at magabayan tungo sa pagbabago.
original_explanation: Basically, "Juvie" or juvenile hall. Ito yung lugar na ayaw mong mapuntahan ng pamangkin mo. Hindi siya kulungan na pang-hardcore criminal, kundi isang facility para sa mga "youth offenders" para bigyan sila ng chance na "magbagong-buhay" bago pa sila maging adult.
usage_notes: Often associated with youth detention centers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ang mga nahuling menor de edad sa **repormatoryo**.","translation":"The arrested minors were brought to the **reformatory**."},{"sentence":"Layunin ng **repormatoryo** na tulungan ang mga kabataan na itama ang kanilang landas.","translation":"The goal of a **reformatory** is to help the youth correct their path."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, karaniwang pera, na ibinibigay bilang kabayaran para sa isang produkto, serbisyo, o utang.
original_explanation: What you're frantically scrambling for in your wallet when the jeepney driver shouts, 'Bayad po!' It can be cash, GCash, or sometimes, just a promise ('Bukas na lang, manong!').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan ko ang aking **pambayad** sa bahay!","translation":"I left my **payment** at home!"},{"sentence":"Magkano ang **pambayad** sa jeep papuntang Quiapo?","translation":"How much is the **fare** for the jeep to Quiapo?"}]

translation: to make into a rope; to twist into a rope
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpili-pilipit ng mga hibla o sinulid upang makabuo ng isang lubid.
original_explanation: The act of creating order from chaos. You take a bunch of flimsy, separate strands—like different chismis from your Marites friends—and you twist them together to make one strong, solid narrative (or rope). It's the OG 'connect the dots' but for fibers.
usage_notes: Can also be used figuratively to mean 'to twist a story' or 'to complicate an issue'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuruan siya kung paano **lubirin** ang mga hibla ng abaka.","translation":"He was taught how **to twist** the abaca fibers **into a rope**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **lubirin** ang usapan, diretsuhin mo na ako.","translation":"Don't **twist** the conversation anymore, just be direct with me."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon na nakahahadlang, nakasasagabal, o nagpapahirap sa pag-abot ng isang layunin.
original_explanation: Anything that gets in your way. Slow wifi during a Zoom meeting. The MRT breaking down at 5 PM. Your tita asking 'Kailan ka ikakasal?' at a family reunion. A 'balakid' is the universe (or just your chismosa neighbor) testing your patience.
usage_notes: A very common word used in both formal and informal contexts to mean any kind of obstruction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kahirapan ay hindi dapat maging **balakid** sa pag-aaral.","translation":"Poverty should not be an **obstacle** to education."},{"sentence":"Maraming **balakid** kaming hinarap bago natapos ang proyekto.","translation":"We faced many **hindrances** before finishing the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghihintay o pag-aabang sa isang tao o pangyayari, kadalasan ay may kasamang pagbabantay.
original_explanation: The official sport of everyone waiting for their Shopee/Lazada delivery. 'On standby' mode, like a BPO agent waiting for the next call, or you, waiting for your crush to go online. It's the act of being a human 'loading...' screen.
usage_notes: Often seen in its verb form, 'antabayanan' (to watch for) or 'mag-antabay' (to wait/watch).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **antabay** ang buong pamilya sa pagdating ng kanilang mga kamag-anak.","translation":"The whole family is **waiting** for the arrival of their relatives."},{"sentence":"Mag-**antabay** tayo sa anunsyo mula sa gobyerno.","translation":"Let's **watch** for the announcement from the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na nagpapahiwatig ng paglilinaw, pagbibigay-diin, o konklusyon; katumbas ng "samakatuwid" o "kung kaya."
original_explanation: This is the super formal, almost biblical way of saying "in other words" or "so basically...". You'd use this if you were writing a legal document or a very serious thesis. In a text message, you'd just say "so," "ibig sabihin," or "ganito kasi 'yun." Using `alalaon` in a casual chat is like wearing a barong to the beach.
usage_notes: Halos palaging ginagamit sa pariralang "alalaong baga'y". Napakapormal at pampanitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay nag-aral nang mabuti; **alalaon**, nakapasa siya sa pagsusulit.","translation":"He studied well; **therefore**, he passed the exam."}]

translation: to weep for, to mourn for
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iyak nang may matinding pighati o kalungkutan para sa isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: That ugly-cry you do when your favorite character in a K-drama dies. It's not just crying; it's a full-on, snot-and-tears, "why-is-the-world-so-cruel" kind of mourning. You're not just sad for them, you're crying with them.
usage_notes: A more intense form of 'iyakan'. 'Tangis' is the noun for deep sorrow or wailing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **tangisan** ang pag-alis niya; hindi siya kawalan.","translation":"Don't **weep for** his departure anymore; he is no great loss."},{"sentence":"**Tinangisan** ng buong bayan ang pagpanaw ng kanilang minamahal na lider.","translation":"The whole nation **mourned for** the passing of their beloved leader."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdating o pagpapakita sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: When you were expected at 7 PM but you show up at 8:30 PM, Pinoy time. Your friends will be like, 'Ayan, sumipot din sa wakas!' It's the act of finally making an appearance, usually after everyone's been waiting.
usage_notes: Often used in its verb form, 'sumipot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Himala, maaga ang **sipot** mo ngayon sa opisina.","translation":"It's a miracle, your **arrival** at the office is early today."},{"sentence":"Inaasahan namin ang iyong **sipot** sa pagdiriwang.","translation":"We are expecting your **appearance** at the celebration."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gitnang bahagi o punto sa pagitan ng dalawang dulo; ang sentro o kalagitnaan.
etymology: From 'ka-' + 'hati' + '-an' suffix, forming a noun that indicates a location or state.
original_explanation: That awkward moment in a project timeline when you're halfway done but it feels like you've barely started. The 'we're halfway there' point in a long road trip, or the exact middle of the month when you're checking your bank account with one eye closed.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to the middle point of a period, space, or process. Synonymous with 'kalagitnaan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **kalahatian** na kami ng aming biyahe patungong Bicol.","translation":"We are now at the **midpoint** of our trip to Bicol."},{"sentence":"Pagsapit ng **kalahatian** ng taon, magkakaroon tayo ng ebalwasyon.","translation":"When we reach the **middle** of the year, we will have an evaluation."}]

translation: to become rough; to become coarse
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng isang ibabaw o materyal mula sa pagiging makinis patungo sa pagiging magaspang o hindi pantay.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your hands after washing dishes without gloves, or to your throat after shouting too much at a concert. It can also describe a situation that becomes difficult or a person's behavior that becomes crude. Your sweet officemate suddenly 'gumaspang ang ugali' after getting promoted.
usage_notes: Can refer to texture, sound, or behavior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gumaspang** ang kanyang mga kamay dahil sa mabigat na trabaho.","translation":"His hands **became rough** due to heavy work."},{"sentence":"Biglang **gumaspang** ang pakikitungo niya sa amin.","translation":"His way of dealing with us suddenly **became coarse**."}]

translation: to adopt as a child; to act as a godparent for
meaning_filipino: Ituring o ampunin bilang sariling anak; o gampanan ang tungkulin bilang ninong o ninang sa isang bata.
original_explanation: The verb form of making someone part of your family, either legally (adoption) or socially/spiritually (godparenting). It's the action of saying 'I choose you!' like a Pokémon master, but for a child. When your tita says she wants to 'anakin' you, it means she wants to spoil you rotten. Not to be confused with a certain Jedi who dislikes sand.
usage_notes: Katulad ng "anakan", ang kahulugan ay nakadepende sa konteksto. Ang "Anakin kita" ay maaaring mangahulugang "Aampunin kita" o, mas karaniwan, "Magsisilbi akong ninong/ninang mo/ng anak mo."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto sana kitang **anakin** sa binyag.","translation":"I would like to **act as godparent for your child** at the baptism."},{"sentence":"Pinag-iisipan nilang **anakin** ang ulilang bata.","translation":"They are thinking of **adopting** the orphaned child."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkainis, pagkadismaya, pagkadiri, o biglaang pagtawag ng pansin.
etymology: Posibleng onomatopoeic o tunog na likas sa pagpapahayag ng damdamin.
original_explanation: The ultimate multi-purpose Pinoy expression. Pwedeng panita sa kaibigang maingay: "Ya! Ang gulo mo!" Pwedeng pandiri sa nakitang ipis: "Ya! Kadiri!" Pwedeng pag-call out sa kapatid mong kinuha ang charger mo: "Ya! Akin 'yan!" It's a whole mood in one syllable.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay lubos na nakadepende sa tono ng boses at konteksto. Maaaring maging magaan o seryoso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ya**! Huwag mong hawakan 'yan, madumi.","translation":"**Hey**! Don't touch that, it's dirty."},{"sentence":"Nang makita niya ang presyo, napasabi siya ng, \"**Ya**! Ang mahal naman.\"","translation":"When she saw the price, she exclaimed, \"**Ugh**! That's so expensive.\""}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na tindahan sa isang komunidad na nagbebenta ng mga pangunahing bilihin at iba't ibang kagamitan sa maliitang pagtingi (tingi).
original_explanation: The Philippines' original convenience store, social hub, and gossip exchange center. It's where you can buy one stick of cigarette, half a cup of cooking oil, a sachet of shampoo, and get the latest chismis about the neighbor's cat. The sari-sari store is the backbone of the Filipino neighborhood economy and the first "database" you query when you need something, anything.
usage_notes: A ubiquitous feature in every Philippine neighborhood. The term is a direct loan and combination, and is used as is in both English and Tagalog conversations in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bili ka nga ng suka sa **sari-sari store** ni Aling Nena.","translation":"Can you buy vinegar at Aling Nena's **sari-sari store**?"},{"sentence":"Dati, ang aming pamilya ay may maliit na **sari-sari store** sa probinsya.","translation":"Before, our family had a small **neighborhood variety store** in the province."}]

translation: to lead, to preside, to head
meaning_filipino: Pangunahan ang isang grupo, organisasyon, o gawain; maging lider o pinuno.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pandiwa na 'ma-' at ang salitang ugat na 'puno' (chief, head).
original_explanation: To be the boss, the team lead, the president, or the groupmate who says 'kayo na bahala' but secretly makes all the decisions. It's about taking charge, whether it's for a group project, a company, or just deciding where to eat with your barkada.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at karaniwang termino para sa pamumuno o leadership.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Handa ka na bang **mamuno** sa isang malaking kumpanya?","translation":"Are you ready to **lead** a big company?"},{"sentence":"Siya ang napiling **mamuno** sa aming samahan.","translation":"He was chosen to **lead** our organization."}]

translation: to plummet, to nosedive, to fall rapidly
meaning_filipino: Mabilis at pababang paggalaw o pagbagsak mula sa isang mataas na lugar.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'bulusok' at gitlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: ‘Yung feeling mo ‘pag nakita mong bumulusok ‘yung value ng crypto na ininvest mo. O ‘yung literal na pag-dive ng eroplano. It's a fast, downward spiral, whether it's your grades, the stock market, or an actual object.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng bilis at pababang direksyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita nila kung paano **bumulusok** ang eroplano mula sa alapaap.","translation":"They saw how the airplane **plummeted** from the clouds."},{"sentence":"**Bumulusok** ang presyo ng bilihin matapos ang anunsyo ng gobyerno.","translation":"The price of goods **nosedived** after the government's announcement."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng larong pampalakasan na ginagamitan ng raketa upang paluin ang isang shuttlecock sa ibabaw ng net.
etymology: Hango sa wikang Ingles na 'badminton', ipinangalan sa Badminton House sa Gloucestershire, England, kung saan ito unang nilaro.
original_explanation: The official sport of Filipino family reunions and PE classes. It's that game where you use a racket to hit a feathery thingy (shuttlecock) back and forth. Great for working up a sweat before you attack the handaan.
usage_notes: The spelling and pronunciation are directly adopted from English. It is a very common and understood word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maglaro tayo ng **badminton** sa Sabado para magpapawis.","translation":"Let's play **badminton** on Saturday to break a sweat."},{"sentence":"Sira na ang raketa ko sa **badminton**, kailangan ko nang bumili ng bago.","translation":"My **badminton** racket is broken, I need to buy a new one."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagiging labis na sabik o hindi mapakali sa pag-aasam o paghihintay sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is your friend who keeps asking "Are we there yet?" on a road trip, or the one who messages you "u up?" at 3 AM because they have chismis. It's the feeling of wanting something to happen *now na!* Like waiting for your 13th-month pay or for your Shopee order to be delivered. Peak "atat" energy is refreshing the tracking page every five minutes.
usage_notes: Often has a slightly negative connotation of being overly eager or pushy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Atat** na **atat** na siyang umuwi para makita ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He was so **eager** to go home to see his family."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **atat**, darating din tayo doon.","translation":"Don't be so **impatient**, we'll get there eventually."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng agam-agam o pagdududa sa isang tao o bagay batay sa mga pahiwatig nang walang tiyak na katibayan.
original_explanation: This is you turning into a detective when your partner is suddenly "busy" all the time. It's that feeling you get when your officemate brings a fancy lunch and you know it's not their payday yet. The official first step of every Marites investigation.
usage_notes: Maghinala is the infinitive. Naghinala (completed), Naghihinala (ongoing), Maghihinala (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang basta-basta **maghinala** kung wala kang sapat na ebidensya.","translation":"Don't just **be suspicious** if you don't have enough evidence."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **maghinala** nang hindi na tumatawag ang kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"She started to **suspect** something when her friend stopped calling."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging sawa o pagkabagot dahil sa labis o paulit-ulit na karanasan sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when you've eaten your favorite adobo for the 5th straight day. It's the 'umay' level-up. It's also that stage in a long-term relationship where you've heard all their stories, and now you're just watching Netflix in comfortable silence... or boredom. The struggle is real.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'pagkasawa' or 'pagkabagot'. 'Kasawaan' has a slightly more formal or literary feel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kasawaan** sa paulit-ulit na trabaho ay nagtulak sa kanya na maghanap ng bagong karera.","translation":"The **weariness** from the repetitive job pushed him to look for a new career."},{"sentence":"Upang maiwasan ang **kasawaan**, sinusubukan nilang mag-date sa iba't ibang lugar.","translation":"To avoid **boredom**, they try to have dates in different places."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lalagyan na yari sa isang bahagi ng kawayan, karaniwang ginagamit sa pag-iimbak ng likido o butil.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *buŋbuŋ. A common variant is 'bumbong'.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino tumbler. Before Hydro Flasks and Stanleys, our ancestors used 'bungbong' to store water, tuba (coconut wine), or even rice grains. It's the eco-friendly, all-natural container you'd find in a probinsya setting.
usage_notes: Often associated with rural or traditional Filipino life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-igib siya ng tubig gamit ang isang lumang **bungbong**.","translation":"He fetched water using an old **bamboo tube**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking handaan o piging, o ang paanyaya para dito. Ito ay mas pormal kaysa sa 'kumbida'.
original_explanation: Think of this as the VIP version of 'kumbida'. It's not just an invitation, it often implies a grand feast or a formal banquet. If you get a 'kumbite', expect more than just spaghetti and hotdogs; we're talking lechon and a full catering setup. From Spanish 'convite'.
usage_notes: Mas madalas tumukoy sa mismong handaan o piging kaysa sa paanyaya lamang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **kumbite** ang inihanda para sa mga bisitang pandangal.","translation":"A grand **banquet** was prepared for the guests of honor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang at pangkalahatang pantawag sa isang tao, na pinagsamang salitang Ingles na 'ma'am' at 'sir', at hindi tumutukoy sa kasarian.
original_explanation: The official 'beshie' of the corporate and retail world. It's the ultimate BPO-approved, gender-neutral term of address when you're not sure who you're talking to but you need to be polite. 'Excuse me, mamser, 'yung sukli po?'
usage_notes: Commonly used in customer service, retail, and office settings as a polite, gender-neutral form of address.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pila po tayo, **mamser**.","translation":"Let's form a line, **ma'am/sir**."},{"sentence":"**Mamser**, may I help you?","translation":"**Ma'am/sir**, may I help you?"}]

meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi upang maipakulong o maibilanggo ang isang tao.
original_explanation: Basically, to get someone thrown in jail. It's the end result of a 'scam' going wrong or when 'cancel culture' escalates to a legal level. The ultimate 'you're going to jail!' move.
usage_notes: A causative verb indicating that an action or a piece of evidence is sufficient to lead to someone's imprisonment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagnanakaw ng ganoong kalaking halaga ay tiyak na **makalaboso** sa iyo.","translation":"Stealing that large an amount will surely **get you jailed**."},{"sentence":"Ang testimonya niya ay sapat para **makalaboso** ang akusado.","translation":"His testimony is enough to **cause the accused to be jailed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang sulating pananaliksik na inihaharap ng isang kandidato para sa isang akademikong digri, na naglalahad ng mga natuklasan mula sa orihinal na pananaliksik sa isang partikular na paksa.
original_explanation: The final boss of college life. Ilang tasang kape, puyat, at 'iyak-turok' moments ang puhunan mo dito. Ito yung 5-chapter document na magpapatunay kung graduate ka na o extended pa. Your relationship status with your thesis adviser is 'It's complicated'.
usage_notes: Primarily used in an academic context for undergraduate or master's level research.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong tapusin ang Kabanata 3 ng aking **tesis** ngayong linggo.","translation":"I need to finish Chapter 3 of my **thesis** this week."},{"sentence":"Pinapahirapan ako ng aking **tesis** tungkol sa 'Philippine Mythology'.","translation":"My **thesis** about 'Philippine Mythology' is giving me a hard time."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga hayop-dagat na bumubuo ng malalaki at matitigas na istraktura (coral reefs) sa ilalim ng dagat.
original_explanation: The beautiful, colorful stuff you see when you go snorkeling in Palawan or Batangas. They're like underwater cities for fish. Remember: 'Look, don't touch!' Bawal iuwi as souvenir!
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa organismong pandagat. Huwag ipagkamali sa 'kural' (corral/enclosure).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng mga **koral** sa Apo Reef.","translation":"The **corals** at Apo Reef are so beautiful."},{"sentence":"Bawal sirain ang mga **koral** dahil tirahan ito ng mga isda.","translation":"It is forbidden to destroy the **corals** because they are homes for fish."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasanayan ng maingat na paggamit ng mga yaman tulad ng pera, oras, o kuryente upang maiwasan ang pag-aaksaya.
original_explanation: The national sport of every Filipino household, especially when the Meralco bill arrives. It's unplugging every appliance, reusing Ziploc bags, and calculating if the Grab promo is cheaper than the jeepney fare. It's the voice of your nanay in your head saying "Patayin mo ang ilaw!" even when you're 30 and living alone.
usage_notes: A very common concept in Philippine culture, applied to finances, resources, and time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa taas ng bilihin, mahalaga ang **pagtitipid** ngayon.","translation":"Because of the high prices of goods, **saving** is important nowadays."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtitipid** sa kuryente ay makakatulong sa ating kalikasan.","translation":"**Economizing** on electricity will help our environment."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang malakas, tuloy-tuloy, at malalim na tunog na umaalingawngaw, tulad ng ugong ng makina, hangin, o maraming tao.
original_explanation: This is the sound of a giant beehive, a factory floor, or the inside of your head during a major family chismis session. It's a low, constant drone. Think of the sound of the electric fan on full blast, the MRT during rush hour, or the collective "hmmmm" of a crowd reacting to a shocking plot twist in a teleserye.
usage_notes: Describes a low-frequency, resonant sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mahugong** ang loob ng pabrika dahil sa mga makina.","translation":"The inside of the factory is **buzzing** because of the machines."},{"sentence":"Narinig namin ang **mahugong** na tunog ng paparating na bagyo.","translation":"We heard the **resounding** sound of the approaching storm."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hindi inaasahang pangyayari, bagay, o balita na nagdudulot ng pagkabigla, galak, o kung minsan ay pagkadismaya.
original_explanation: That feeling when your Shopee/Lazada package arrives earlier than expected. Or when your crush suddenly messages you. Pwede ring masamang sorpresa, like a surprise quiz from your terror prof. It's the ultimate plot twist of your daily life. The adult version is getting a 'sorpresa' from your Meralco bill.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang positibo o negatibong sorpresa. Ang konteksto ang nagdidikta ng emosyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakalaking **sorpresa** ang inihanda nila para sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"They prepared a very big **surprise** for her birthday."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko inaasahan ang **sorpresa** mong pagdating!","translation":"I didn't expect your **surprise** arrival!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matinding galit na pinipigilan, na madalas ay naipapakita sa pamamagitan ng pagkakagat ng mga ngipin o panginginig ng panga.
original_explanation: This is your 'pikon-talo' final form. That feeling when you're so angry but you can't shout, so you just channel all that rage into your jaw. It's the physical manifestation of 'gigil sa galit.' Think of your reaction to slow internet during a crucial online meeting or when someone spoils the final episode of your favorite K-drama.
usage_notes: Refers to a very intense, often silent, expression of anger or frustration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **pagngingitngit** ng kanyang mga ngipin, alam kong galit na galit na siya.","translation":"By the **gnashing** of his teeth, I knew he was furious."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **pagngingitngit** ang kanyang puso para sa mga nagtaksil sa kanya.","translation":"His heart was full of **suppressed rage** for those who betrayed him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaki na mapanlinlang, hindi seryoso sa relasyon, at ginagamit ang mga babae para sa sariling kasiyahan, lalo na sa sekswal na paraan, nang walang intensyon na magkaroon ng pangmatagalang ugnayan.
etymology: From English AAVE (African American Vernacular English) "fuckboy," popularized through internet culture.
original_explanation: The modern-day Don Juan, but with more selfies and less class. He's the guy who DMs you "u up?" at 2 AM, leaves you on 'seen' for three days, then replies with a fire emoji to your IG story. He collects hearts like Pokémon cards and his favorite line is "hindi pa ako ready for a commitment." Beware.
usage_notes: The spelling "fuccboi" is a deliberate internet-culture stylization.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yan, halata namang **fuccboi**.","translation":"Stop talking to him, he's obviously a **fuckboy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang siyentipikong pamamaraan upang subukin ang isang teorya, tuklasin ang isang epekto, o ipakita ang isang katotohanan.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Espanyol na 'experimento' at nilapian ng unlaping `mag-`.
original_explanation: Not just for science class! This is what you do when you mix different leftovers to create a "new" ulam. Or when you try a new hair color from a box and pray it doesn't turn orange. It's the act of trying something new, "para malaman," whether in the lab or in the kitchen.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pormal na siyentipikong konteksto at sa mga di-pormal na pang-araw-araw na sitwasyon ng pagsubok sa isang bagay na bago.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mag-eksperimento** ng mga bagong putahe sa kusina.","translation":"She loves to **experiment** with new dishes in the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Ang mga siyentista ay patuloy na **nag-eeksperimento** upang makahanap ng lunas.","translation":"The scientists are continuously **experimenting** to find a cure."}]

meaning_filipino: Suriin o siyasatin nang masinsinan at malawakan ang isang lugar upang maghanap o tumuklas ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're looking for the best ukay-ukay finds, searching for a hidden beach in Palawan, or trying to find the last piece of chicken in a bucket. It's a deep dive, a thorough search. It's not just 'hanapin' (to look for); it's an adventure. Think Dora the Explorer, but for a parking spot at the mall during Christmas season.
usage_notes: Implies a wide and thorough search of an area.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais naming **galugarin** ang mga kweba sa Sagada.","translation":"We want to **explore** the caves in Sagada."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **galugarin** ang buong bahay para mahanap ang nawawalang susi.","translation":"The whole house needs to be **searched thoroughly** to find the missing key."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghikayat o pag-udyok sa isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pakiusap o pangangako.
original_explanation: This is your friend convincing you to go out on a Friday night even though you're broke ('libre ko na!'). It's the 'add to cart' button whispering sweet nothings during a 12.12 sale. It's a gentle but persistent push to get you to say yes.
usage_notes: The verb form 'himukin' (to persuade) is more commonly used in sentences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi siya nagpadala sa **himok** ng kanyang mga kaibigan na uminom.","translation":"He did not give in to the **persuasion** of his friends to drink."},{"sentence":"Ang matamis na **himok** ng tindera ang nagpasang-ayon sa akin na bumili.","translation":"The seller's sweet **inducement** made me agree to buy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gabay, payo, o tulong na ibinibigay sa isang tao upang maging tama ang kanyang landas o desisyon.
original_explanation: Think of 'patnubay' as your human Waze. It's the advice your parents give you about life, the career counseling you get at school, or the "SPG" warning before a TV show. It's that guiding light or principle that's supposed to keep you from messing up. "Gabay at Patnubay ng Magulang ay kailangan."
usage_notes: Often seen in the phrase "Striktong Patnubay at Gabay (SPG)" on Philippine television ratings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humingi siya ng **patnubay** sa kanyang mga magulang bago magdesisyon.","translation":"He asked for **guidance** from his parents before making a decision."}]

translation: to make holy; to treat as holy
meaning_filipino: Gawing banal o ituring na parang banal ang isang bagay, tao, o konsepto.
original_explanation: This is when you try to make something or someone seem holier-than-thou, or to act like a saint. It's like your tita telling you to "pakabanalin mo ang pag-aaral mo" as if it's a sacred text, not just your calculus homework. It's the act of elevating something to a spiritual level, sometimes genuinely, sometimes with a hint of irony.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pakabanalin** ang mga materyal na bagay.","translation":"Do not **treat** material things **as holy**."},{"sentence":"Pinipilit niyang **pakabanalin** ang kanyang imahe sa publiko.","translation":"He is trying to **make** his public image **holy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampalasa na pulbos na gawa sa pinatuyo at giniling na bunga ng sili (Capsicum annuum), karaniwang may kulay mula matingkad na pula hanggang kahel.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'paprika', na mula sa Hungarian na 'paprika'.
original_explanation: That red powder you sprinkle on your deviled eggs or potatoes to make them look fancy. It's like makeup for your food, giving it a nice color and a slightly sweet or smoky flavor. Hindi ito 'yung sili na iiyak ka sa anghang, more on the "I'm here for the aesthetic" side of spices.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pampalasa at pangkulay sa pagkain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **paprika** ang manok para mas maging malasa at maganda ang kulay.","translation":"Add **paprika** to the chicken to make it more flavorful and have a better color."}]

meaning_filipino: Kalagayan ng pagiging dusta, hamak, o inalipusta; matinding kahihiyan o pag-aglahi.
original_explanation: This is when you're not just insulted, you're dragged through the mud. It's the feeling of being utterly humiliated, like when your boss scolds you in front of everyone, or when you get cancelled online for a bad take. It's a deep, soul-crushing insult.
usage_notes: A very strong and formal word for humiliation or being in a state of disgrace. Used in contexts of honor and reputation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya makalimutan ang **kadustaan** na dinanas niya sa kanilang mga kamay.","translation":"He cannot forget the **ignominy** he suffered at their hands."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtataksil ay isang **kadustaan** sa kanilang pagkakaibigan.","translation":"The betrayal was an **affront** to their friendship."}]

translation: to ask someone to teach; please teach
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na maturuan o ipakita kung paano gawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The magic word you say when you have no idea how to use the new coffee machine at the office, or when you want your friend to teach you their secret adobo recipe. It's a humble request for knowledge, the polite version of 'How do you do this?!' Usually followed by 'naman' to make it extra nice: 'Paturo naman kung paano mag-edit ng video.'
usage_notes: A common contraction of 'paki-turo.' It's a polite command or request used to ask for instruction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paturo** naman ako ng tamang daan papuntang MOA.","translation":"**Please teach** me the right way to get to MOA."},{"sentence":"Pwede bang **paturo** kung paano ito gamitin?","translation":"Can you **teach** me how to use this?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasama sa pag-upa o pagtira sa iisang silid, apartment, o bahay.
original_explanation: The person you share your living space, Wi-Fi password, and possibly your sanity with. They're the reason your instant noodles disappear and the source of mysterious hairs in the bathroom. Can be your best friend or your worst enemy, sometimes on the same day. Also known as 'ka-roommate' or 'kasama sa kwarto'.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, very common in modern urban Filipino. Often used with 'ka-', as in 'ka-roommate', or simply 'rumeyt' in casual speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aaway na naman kami ng **roommate** ko kung sino ang maghuhugas ng pinggan.","translation":"My **roommate** and I are fighting again over who will wash the dishes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha ng karapatang gumamit ng isang bagay, lugar, o serbisyo sa loob ng takdang panahon kapalit ng bayad.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "arkila", na hango sa Espanyol na "alquilar".
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa mo sa Grab, sa Airbnb, o sa videoke machine para sa birthday party. Basically, "hiramin mo muna, bayaran mo na lang." It's the foundation of the "for rent" signs you see everywhere from apartments to wedding gowns.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang salita para sa pag-upa. Ang "upahan" ay isang malapit na kasingkahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **arkilahin** ang isang van para sa ating outing sa Tagaytay.","translation":"We need to **rent** a van for our outing in Tagaytay."},{"sentence":"Magkano kung **arkilahin** ang buong resort para sa isang araw?","translation":"How much is it to **rent** the entire resort for one day?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay lupa o isipan, na pinaunlad, sinaka, o pinagyaman.
original_explanation: This is the past tense of 'linangin' (to cultivate). Parang yung pag-aaral mo for board exams, you 'cultivated' your mind. O kaya yung lupa na inararo ng magsasaka para taniman. Basically, the 'glow-up' version of something raw after putting in the work.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong perpektibo (naganap) ng pandiwang 'linangin'. Huwag ipagkamali sa salitang Ingles na 'lining' (para sa damit).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lining** ng mga magsasaka ang kanilang bukirin bago magtanim.","translation":"The farmers **cultivated** their fields before planting."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang talino ay **lining** sa maraming taon ng pag-aaral.","translation":"His intellect was **developed** through many years of study."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinagmulan, simula, o ugat ng isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: 'Yung chismis na narinig mo sa office, sino ang orihen? Saan nagsimula 'yung kwento na aalis na si boss? Parang sa family reunion, 'yung tanong na "Saan ba talaga galing ang lahi natin?". It's the source code of everything.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'pinagmulan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaalam pa ng mga historyador ang tunay na **orihen** ng ating lahi.","translation":"The historians are still determining the true **origin** of our race."},{"sentence":"Ano kaya ang **orihen** ng tradisyong ito?","translation":"I wonder what the **origin** of this tradition is?"}]

translation: To make salty; to add salt
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng asin sa isang bagay, karaniwan sa pagkain, upang magbigay-lasa o bilang paraan ng preserbasyon.
original_explanation: The move you make when your sinigang is too bland. It's the art of perfecting the flavor, but be careful, one wrong move and you've created a dish that tastes like the Dead Sea. Also what happens to your feelings when someone throws shade—nagiging maalat.
usage_notes: A command or infinitive form. 'Alatan mo' means 'Add salt to it.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **alatan** ang adobo, baka tumaas ang presyon ng dugo ni lola.","translation":"Don't **make** the adobo too **salty**, grandma's blood pressure might rise."},{"sentence":"Sabi ni nanay, **alatan** ko raw ang isda bago iprito.","translation":"Mom said I should **salt** the fish before frying."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging bangkarota; ang legal na deklarasyon ng kawalan ng kakayahang magbayad ng mga utang.
original_explanation: When your wallet has more cobwebs than cash. It's that moment you look at your credit card bill after a 12.12 sale and realize you've played yourself. The corporate version of 'wala na, finish na'.
usage_notes: A formal term used in business and finance. 'Pagkabangkarote' is a common variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang maling pamamahala sa pondo ang naging sanhi ng **pagkabangkarota** ng kumpanya.","translation":"Mismanagement of funds was the cause of the company's **bankruptcy**."},{"sentence":"Nagsampa sila ng petisyon para sa **pagkabangkarota** upang maisaayos ang kanilang mga utang.","translation":"They filed a petition for **bankruptcy** to restructure their debts."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkawala sa tamang pag-iisip o katinuan; pagkabaliw.
etymology: An idiomatic expression literally meaning "damage/breakdown of the head".
original_explanation: Literally 'damage of the head.' This is what you feel after a week of OT without pay, trying to understand government bureaucracy, or arguing with a troll online. It's the feeling of going crazy. 'Ito na ang **kasiraan ng ulo** ko!'
usage_notes: Can be used literally to mean insanity, or more commonly, hyperbolically to express extreme frustration or mental exhaustion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang walang tigil na ingay ay tila magiging **kasiraan ng ulo** ko.","translation":"The non-stop noise feels like it will be the cause of my **insanity**."},{"sentence":"Marami ang nag-alala na baka humantong sa **kasiraan ng ulo** ang kanyang matinding dalamhati.","translation":"Many were worried that his intense grief might lead to a **mental breakdown**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang baras o biga na nagsisilbing sentro ng pag-ikot ng isang gulong o pangkat ng mga gulong.
original_explanation: This is the metal stick that connects two wheels, like on a jeepney or a kariton. Without the 'ehe', your ride ain't going nowhere, it'll just be a wobbly mess. It's the unsung hero of "gulong ng palad," literally keeping things rolling.
usage_notes: A technical term used in mechanics and engineering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabali ang **ehe** ng kariton kaya hindi na kami makauwi.","translation":"The **axle** of the cart broke, so we couldn't go home anymore."},{"sentence":"Kailangang lagyan ng grasa ang **ehe** para hindi ito kalawangin.","translation":"The **axle** needs to be greased so it won't rust."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng portable na kompyuter na may touchscreen, na mas malaki sa selpon ngunit mas maliit sa laptop, at walang pisikal na keyboard.
original_explanation: The lovechild of a smartphone and a laptop. Perfect for watching Netflix in bed, online classes, and for toddlers to watch Cocomelon on repeat. Not to be confused with 'tabletas' (medicine), unless you're addicted to scrolling, which is a different kind of pill.
usage_notes: In the Philippines, 'tablet' almost always refers to the electronic device. For medicine, the Spanish-derived 'tabletas' is used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginagamit ng mga bata ang **tablet** para sa kanilang online class.","translation":"The children use the **tablet** for their online class."},{"sentence":"Mas malaki ang screen ng **tablet** kaysa sa selpon kaya masarap manood ng pelikula.","translation":"The **tablet's** screen is bigger than a cellphone's so it's great for watching movies."}]

translation: to have a premonition; to feel a sense of foreboding
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng masamang kutob, pangamba, o hindi maipaliwanag na takot tungkol sa isang bagay na maaaring mangyari.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when your mom calls you by your full name. You know something's up. It's having a premonition or a bad vibe, an inner 'uh-oh' sensor. Nang hindi siya nag-reply, nagsimula na akong **magkasalagimsim**.
usage_notes: A very specific and literary word for a negative premonition or an eerie feeling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Habang papalapit ang gabi, siya ay **nagkasalagimsim** na may masamang mangyayari.","translation":"As night approached, he **had a premonition** that something bad would happen."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magkasalagimsim**, panaginip lang iyon.","translation":"Don't **feel a sense of foreboding**, it was just a dream."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking ibon na karaniwang kulay itim at may malakas at kakaibang huni.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian na *uak*, na tumutukoy sa uwak.
original_explanation: The Goth kid of the Philippine bird world. They're often seen as bad omens in folklore, but really, they're just smart birds na laging may chismis. When you see one, you either think of a horror movie or 'Darna!'.
usage_notes: Sa pangkalahatang pakikipag-usap, maaaring tumukoy ito sa 'crow' o 'raven'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May isang **uwak** na dumapo sa bubong ng bahay namin.","translation":"There was a **crow** that landed on the roof of our house."},{"sentence":"Ang huni ng **uwak** ay pinaniniwalaang masamang pangitain ng iba.","translation":"The caw of a **crow** is believed by some to be a bad omen."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o patuyuan kung saan ibinibilad ang mga isda upang gawing daing.
original_explanation: This is the fish spa, but for, you know, making them into daing. It's where fish go to get their tan on. The whole place smells like the sea and your future delicious breakfast. Think of it as the factory floor for your favorite almusal staple.
usage_notes: Refers to the specific location, often a large open-air platform, where the process of making 'daing' (dried fish) happens.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan kami sa **daingan** at kitang-kita ang libo-libong isdang nakabilad.","translation":"We passed by the **fish drying area** and saw thousands of fish laid out to dry."}]

translation: to break, to snap, to fracture (something long and thin)
meaning_filipino: Putulin o sirain sa pamamagitan ng pagyuko o pagpiko hanggang sa ito ay magkahiwalay; partikular na ginagamit para sa mga bagay na mahaba at payat tulad ng patpat o buto.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'bali' (broken, fractured) + hulaping pandiwa na '-hin'.
original_explanation: Ito yung action na ginagawa mo sa stick ng BBQ pagkatapos kumain, or sa puso ng isang tao kapag nag-ghosting ka. You snap it in two. Pwedeng literal sa patpat, o figurative sa isang pangako. 'Binalì niya ang pangako niya.' Ouch.
usage_notes: Ang 'balihin' ay ang anyong pandiwa na nakatuon sa layon. Ginagamit ito para sa pagbali ng mahahaba at payat na bagay tulad ng patpat, lapis, o buto. Para sa pagbasag ng mas lapad o malalaking bagay, mas angkop ang 'basagin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **balihin** ang patpat gamit ang kanyang tuhod.","translation":"He tried to **snap** the stick using his knee."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka mo **balihin** ang lapis sa sobrang diin ng pagsulat.","translation":"Be careful or you might **break** the pencil from writing with too much pressure."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal na may mataas na katayuan, impluwensya, o kabuluhan sa isang partikular na larangan, lipunan, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Your "very important person" or VIP. This could be your boss, a celebrity you spotted in BGC, or your lola who always has the best chismis and the biggest pamana. Basically, someone you can't just leave on "seen."
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga dignitaryo, opisyal, o sinumang may mataas na pagtingin sa lipunan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **mahalagang tao** ang dumalo sa pagtitipon.","translation":"Many **important people** attended the gathering."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing siyang **mahalagang tao** sa industriya ng pelikula.","translation":"He is considered a **VIP** in the film industry."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghawak nang mahigpit sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is a more poetic way of saying 'to hold.' It's not just holding your phone; it's holding someone's hand on a first date. It's the way you grip your bag when walking through a crowded market. It implies a firm, deliberate grasp, like you're holding onto something important—be it a promise, a hope, or your last 100 pesos before sweldo.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwan sa panitikan at pormal na pananalita. Sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, mas madalas gamitin ang 'hawakan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit niyang **tinanganan** ang kamay ng kanyang anak habang tumatawid sila sa kalsada.","translation":"He tightly **held** his child's hand as they crossed the street."},{"sentence":"**Tanganan** mo ang pag-asang balang araw ay giginhawa rin ang buhay.","translation":"**Hold** on to the hope that one day, life will get better."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagpapahayag ng pagsang-ayon, pagpapatunay, o pagkumpirma sa isang sinabi o narinig.
etymology: A combination of 'siya' (it, that) and 'nga' (indeed, truly).
original_explanation: This is your go-to response when the 'chismis' is confirmed. Friend: 'Diba sabi ko sa'yo, sila na?' You: '**Siyanga**! Nakita ko post nila!' It's the Tagalog equivalent of 'I knew it!', 'For real!', or 'You don't say!'.
usage_notes: Often used to express enthusiastic agreement, confirmation, or mild surprise. Capitalized as it's often used at the beginning of a response. 'Siyanga pala' means 'by the way'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Siyanga**, tama ang lahat ng hula mo.","translation":"**Indeed**, all your guesses are correct."},{"sentence":"A: Umalis na raw si Mark. B: **Siyanga**? Kailan pa?","translation":"A: They said Mark already left. B: **Really**? Since when?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpasok o pagdaraan ng isang matulis na bagay, tulad ng patpat o karayom, sa isa o higit pang mga bagay upang pagsama-samahin ang mga ito.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa barbecue bago ilagay sa grill. You tumuhog the pork on a stick. It can also be used figuratively, like when a basketball player "skewers" the defense, or when you perfectly line up three tasks in a row. "Naka-dalawang meeting na ako, tapos tumuhog pa ng isa bago mag-lunch."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for cooking (skewering) or stringing beads, and figuratively for accomplishing multiple things in succession or a row.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumuhog** siya ng tatlong isaw sa isang patpat.","translation":"He **skewered** three intestines on one stick."},{"sentence":"Ang sinulid ay **tumuhog** sa lahat ng butones.","translation":"The thread **strung through** all the buttons."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, karaniwang isang patag na espasyo, kung saan ang mga uhay ng palay o ibang butil ay niyuyurakan o ginigiik upang ihiwalay ang butil mula sa tangkay.
original_explanation: Basically, this is the old-school version of a rice mill's threshing machine. Imagine a designated spot where carabaos (or people) would stomp on harvested rice stalks to separate the good stuff (the grains) from the rest. It's the agricultural equivalent of a dance floor, but for food processing.
usage_notes: This term is primarily used in agricultural contexts and is not widely known by urban speakers. 'Giikan' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ng mga magsasaka ang kanilang mga ani sa **yasakan** upang simulan ang paggiik.","translation":"The farmers brought their harvest to the **threshing floor** to begin threshing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang siyentipikong pamamaraan na isinasagawa upang subukan ang isang teorya, magpakita ng isang kilalang katotohanan, o tumuklas ng bagong kaalaman.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa pag-ibig. 'Try lang natin kung mag-work,' sabay ayun, nag-fail. Sa science, kailangan ng control group; sa love life, 'pag nag-eksperimento ka, madalas walang control.
usage_notes: The spelling "eksperiment" is also sometimes seen, influenced by the English "experiment", but "eksperimento" is the standard form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga mag-aaral ay nagsagawa ng isang **eksperimento** sa laboratoryo ng kemistri.","translation":"The students conducted an **experiment** in the chemistry laboratory."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa lasa na katulad ng sa asin o tubig-dagat; may alat.
original_explanation: The taste of the chips you promised you'd only eat one of. Also, the vibe of a gamer who just lost a match. When the cook was a little too in love and added too much salt, the result is maasin.
usage_notes: Primarily used to describe the taste of food.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **maasin** ang adobo, dagdagan natin ng kaunting tubig.","translation":"The adobo is a bit **salty**, let's add a little water."},{"sentence":"Ayokong lumangoy, masyadong **maasin** ang tubig-dagat.","translation":"I don't want to swim, the seawater is too **salty**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga sundalo; sa kolokyal na gamit, isang grupo ng magkakaibigan.
original_explanation: Your barkada, your squad, your beshies, your partners-in-crime. Sila yung mga kasama mo sa kalokohan, sa kainan, at sa iyakan. Hindi kumpleto ang gala pag wala ang buong tropa.
usage_notes: Originally meaning 'troop' of soldiers, its colloquial meaning 'group of friends' is now far more common in everyday speech. The word 'tropang' is a contraction of 'tropa na' or 'tropa ng'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Yayain mo ang buong **tropa** mamaya, manonood tayo ng sine.","translation":"Invite the whole **gang** later, we'll watch a movie."},{"sentence":"Ipinadala ang isang **tropa** ng mga sundalo sa lugar ng sakuna.","translation":"A **troop** of soldiers was sent to the disaster area."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip panao na tumutukoy sa pang-angkop na anyo ng 'sila' (kanila) o bilang tagaganap ng isang pandiwang balintiyak (ginawa nila).
original_explanation: The ultimate chismis pronoun. It's the 'they' in 'Sabi nila...' (They said...) or 'Nakita ko sila...' (I saw them...). It's also possessive, as in 'Bahay nila' (Their house). It's the word you use when you're talking about a group of people, whether you're assigning them a task at work ('Gawin nila 'yan') or blaming them for eating the last piece of lechon ('Inubos nila!').
usage_notes: 'Nila' is used as a possessive pronoun (e.g., 'bahay nila' - their house) and as the agent in passive verb constructions (e.g., 'kinain nila' - was eaten by them). It's the non-subject form of 'sila'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng bahay **nila**.","translation":"**Their** house is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Sino ang kumain ng cake? Kinain **nila**.","translation":"Who ate the cake? It was eaten **by them**."},{"sentence":"Sabi **nila**, masarap daw doon.","translation":"**They** said, the food there is delicious."}]

translation: state of being far apart; distance (between)
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging magkalayo o may malaking agwat sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: The official status of LDR couples. It's that feeling when you're in Manila and your Grab driver is still in Cavite. It's the emotional distance when you and your bestie are "not okay." It's the physical or emotional gap that makes you say, "Sana all malapit."
usage_notes: Refers to the state of being distant from each other, either physically or emotionally.
