usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng kanilang **pagkakalayo**, nanatili silang matatag.","translation":"Despite their **being far apart**, they remained strong."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakalayo** ng kanilang mga loob ang naging sanhi ng hiwalayan.","translation":"The emotional **distance** between them caused the separation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paggaling ng isang sugat, pisikal man o emosyonal; pagbabalik sa dating mabuting kalagayan.
original_explanation: The emotional equivalent of putting Betadine on your 'sugat' from a bad breakup. It's the 'time heals all wounds' process, whether it's a scraped knee or a broken heart. It's slow, sometimes ugly, but totally necessary for your character development arc.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical wounds and emotional/psychological healing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghihilom** ng kanyang mga sugat ay naging mas mabilis sa tulong ng pamilya.","translation":"The **healing** of his wounds became faster with the help of his family."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang panahon para sa **paghihilom** ng pusong nasaktan.","translation":"Time is important for the **recovery** of a broken heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagpapakita ng labis na takot at kakulangan ng tapang sa harap ng panganib, sakit, o anumang mahirap na sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That friend who sees a flying ipis and runs for the hills, leaving you to fend for yourself. Or that person who won't admit their feelings for their crush. 'Torpe' is a specific kind of *duwag* in love. Don't be a *duwag*, mag-chat ka na sa kanya!
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pangngalan (noun) upang tukuyin ang isang taong duwag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **duwag**, harapin mo ang iyong mga problema.","translation":"Don't be **cowardly**, face your problems."},{"sentence":"Tinakbuhan niya ang responsibilidad, isa siyang **duwag**.","translation":"He ran from his responsibility, he is a **coward**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sandatang pandagat na pampasabog at gumagalaw sa ilalim ng tubig upang patamaan ang mga sasakyang pandagat.
original_explanation: Same as the English 'torpedo', but this is the more Spanish-sounding version. Think of it as the 'tito' way of saying it.
usage_notes: A variant of 'torpedo', both referring to the weapon. This spelling is closer to the Spanish origin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **torpido** ang tumama sa gilid ng barko.","translation":"A **torpedo** hit the side of the ship."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw nang mabilis gamit ang mga paa sa hinaharap na panahunan.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of 'takbo' (run). It's your promise to yourself on January 1st: "Tatakbo ako araw-araw!" (I will run every day!). It's also what happens to your data allowance when you start streaming K-dramas, or what you'll do when you see a cute dog... or a scary one.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong panghinaharap (future tense). Ang salitang-ugat ay 'takbo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tatakbo** siya sa darating na halalan para sa pagka-alkalde.","translation":"He/She **will run** for mayor in the upcoming election."},{"sentence":"Kapag narinig mo ang busina, **tatakbo** ka na ba?","translation":"When you hear the horn, **will you run**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na napinsala, nasaktan, o napatay dahil sa isang krimen, aksidente, o iba pang masamang pangyayari.
original_explanation: Sila yung laging talo sa kwento. Biktima ng scam, ng chismis, ng maling akala, o ng pa-fall na bigla na lang nag-ghost. Sa office, sila yung laging napag-iinitan ng boss. Sa love life, sila yung laging naiiwan. #SanaAll hindi biktima.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin sa mga seryosong konteksto (krimen, sakuna) at sa mga kolokyal, madalas na nakakatawa o madramang sitwasyon (buhay pag-ibig, pulitika sa opisina).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **biktima** ng bagyo ay agad na binigyan ng tulong.","translation":"The **victims** of the typhoon were immediately given aid."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-inarte na parang ikaw ang **biktima** sa sitwasyong ito.","translation":"Don't act like you're the **victim** in this situation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagiging maasim ng isang bagay; ang pakiramdam ng asim sa panlasa o sikmura.
original_explanation: It's that face you make after eating green mango with bagoong. Or the feeling in your stomach when you get acid reflux from too much coffee and stress (hello, BPO life!). It can also describe a mood, like when someone's face 'turns sour' because of a bad joke. `Pangangasim ng mukha` is a classic.
usage_notes: Can refer to food turning sour, a physical sensation (like acid reflux), or a facial expression.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **pangangasim** ng sikmura sa pamamagitan ng pagkain sa tamang oras.","translation":"Avoid **acid reflux** by eating at the right time."},{"sentence":"Ang **pangangasim** ng gatas ay senyales na ito'y sira na.","translation":"The **souring** of the milk is a sign that it has spoiled."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong minamahal nang labis; paglalambing o pagmamahal. Ginagamit bilang pantawag sa isang minamahal.
original_explanation: The OG term of endearment before 'babe,' 'mahal,' or 'beh.' It's what Lolo used to call Lola in his love letters. Using 'giliw' today is either super romantic in a classic way, or you're quoting a kundiman. 'O, giliw ko...'
usage_notes: Primarily used in poetic, literary, or romantic contexts. Can be used as a term of endearment or to mean 'affection' itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Ikaw ang aking tanging **giliw**,\" sabi ng makata.","translation":"\"You are my only **darling**,\" said the poet."},{"sentence":"Ang awiting \"O, Ilaw\" ay puno ng pag-ibig at **giliw**.","translation":"The song \"O, Ilaw\" is full of love and **affection**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang legal na akto ng pagdakip at pagpigil sa isang tao na isinasagawa ng awtoridad dahil sa hinala ng paglabag sa batas.
original_explanation: When the pulis finally catches the 'kontrabida' in the teleserye. It's the official act of saying 'You're coming with me,' complete with handcuffs. The start of a whole new story arc involving lawyers and courtrooms.
usage_notes: Used in news, legal, and formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-aresto** sa suspek ay naging laman ng balita.","translation":"The **arrest** of the suspect was all over the news."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na angkop, nauukol, o para sa lahat nang walang itinatangi.
original_explanation: Think "one size fits all" or "for general patronage." A **panlahat** na CR is a unisex toilet. A **panlahat** na anunsyo is a public service announcement. It's the opposite of exclusive. It's the "sali lahat!" of adjectives. Like adobo, it's a **panlahat** na ulam—almost everyone loves it.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with `pangkalahatan`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang anunsyo ng pangulo ay isang mensaheng **panlahat**.","translation":"The president's announcement was a message **for all**."},{"sentence":"Nagdisenyo sila ng isang programang **panlahat** na kayang gamitin ng bata at matanda.","translation":"They designed a **general** program that can be used by the young and old."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi namamatay; nagpapatuloy sa pag-iral nang walang hanggan.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'forever.' Like the love of a mother, the music of the Eraserheads, or the national debt—it just doesn't die. It's the ultimate #ThrowbackThursday because it's always relevant. Think classic movies, legendary OPM songs, or that chismis about your tita that resurfaces every family reunion.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal immortality (as in myths) or figurative timelessness (as in art or legacy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala sila na ang mga diyos ay may buhay na **walang-kamatayan**.","translation":"They believe that the gods have **immortal** lives."},{"sentence":"Ang mga kanta ng bandang iyon ay **walang-kamatayan**.","translation":"The songs of that band are **timeless**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sangay ng hukbo na binubuo ng mga sundalong nakasakay sa kabayo.
etymology: A compound of 'hukbo' (army) and 'kabayuhan' (pertaining to horses, from 'kabayo').
original_explanation: The original 'fast and furious' of the army. Before tanks and jeeps, these were the guys on horseback charging into battle. Today, it's mostly ceremonial, like the guards you see in historical movies or at fancy parades. They're the OG horsepower.
usage_notes: Primarily a historical term, but can refer to modern ceremonial units on horseback.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang digmaan, mahalaga ang papel ng **hukbong-kabayuhan** sa mabilisang pagsalakay.","translation":"In old wars, the **cavalry** played an important role in swift attacks."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsasalita nang pabulong sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the verb form, the command: "Bulungan mo nga ako ng sagot sa exam." It's what you do when you're passing secrets, answers, or chismis directly into someone's ear. Sa BPO, ito yung pag-ask mo sa katabi mo "Pa'no 'to i-resolve?" nang hindi naririnig ng customer sa call.
usage_notes: This is a locative verb, indicating the recipient of the whisper. It answers the question 'whisper to whom?'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bulungan** mo si Maria na umalis na tayo.","translation":"**Whisper** to Maria that we should leave now."},{"sentence":"**Binulungan** niya ang kanyang kaibigan ng isang sikreto.","translation":"He **whispered** a secret to his friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagpapakain nang labis sa isang tao hanggang sa ito ay mabusog nang husto.
original_explanation: What every Filipino lola does to their favorite apo. 'Kumain ka pa, ang payat mo!' It's the act of showing love through an overwhelming amount of food, forcefully if necessary, until the recipient achieves the state of 'bundat'.
usage_notes: It's a causative verb, meaning 'to cause someone to become bundat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **bundatin**, baka hindi ako makatayo mamaya.","translation":"Don't **stuff me with food**, I might not be able to stand up later."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging tabingi, hindi pantay, o hindi tuwid.
original_explanation: How your selfie looks before you spend 10 minutes trying to get the perfect angle. Also describes a picture frame that's not straight on the wall. 'Bakit ngiwi 'yang pagkakangiti mo?'
usage_notes: Describes the physical state of an object or expression.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiaayos ng kuwadro, medyo **ngiwi** ang pagkakasabit.","translation":"Please fix the frame, it's hung a bit **crooked**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang aparato o proseso na gumagana nang kusa, na may kaunti o walang direktang kontrol mula sa tao.
original_explanation: Like when you see a 'SALE' sign and your feet just walk into the mall. Or when your friend starts a chismis and your ears just perk up. It's something that happens by itself, no questions asked. "Basta pagkain, awtomatik 'yan, pupunta ako."
usage_notes: Also spelled 'awtomatiko'. Can also refer to a type of car transmission.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas madaling gamitin ang mga **awtomatik** na washing machine.","translation":"**Automatic** washing machines are easier to use."},{"sentence":"**Awtomatik** na 'yan, kapag Biyernes, traffic sa EDSA.","translation":"That's **automatic**, when it's a Friday, there's traffic on EDSA."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ako sa gastusin o bayarin para sa ibang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate "libre" move. When your friend is short on cash, you tell the cashier, "Ako na po ang magbabayad" or you tell your friend, "Ipagbabayad na kita." It's the act of using your money to pay for someone else's bill. It’s what you hope your rich tita will do for your entire shopping cart.
usage_notes: The focus is on the person for whom the payment is being made, or the item being paid for on behalf of someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari mo ba akong **ipagbayad** muna sa sine? Babayaran kita bukas.","translation":"Can you **pay** for me at the movies for now? I'll pay you back tomorrow."},{"sentence":"**Ipagbabayad** na kita ng kuryente.","translation":"I'll **pay** for the electricity for you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghikayat, pag-akit, o paghimok sa isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng pag-aalok ng pabuya o benepisyo.
etymology: From Spanish 'engaño' (deceit, trick), but its Tagalog usage has evolved to mean 'entice' or 'persuade' more than 'deceive'.
original_explanation: This is the art of convincing someone. It's the 'Sige na, please?' power move. Your friend's pag-engganyo is why you ended up at a milk tea shop despite being on a diet. It's how online sellers lure you into a 'mine' spree during a live session. It's the gentle (or not-so-gentle) push towards a 'yes'.
usage_notes: Can have a slightly negative connotation of luring someone, but is often used neutrally for persuading or encouraging.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Epektibo ang kanyang **pag-engganyo** kaya marami ang sumali sa kanilang grupo.","translation":"His **persuasion** was effective, which is why many joined their group."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpadala sa **pag-engganyo** ng mga taong may masamang intensyon.","translation":"Don't be swayed by the **enticement** of people with bad intentions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng otel na may mga silid na madaling marating mula sa paradahan, karaniwang matatagpuan sa tabi ng mga pangunahing kalsada.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "motel", pinaghalong "motor" at "hotel".
original_explanation: Sa Pinas, 'pag sinabing 'motel', a certain image comes to mind. It's the place for 'short-time' stays, usually with a drive-in garage para discreet. Hindi ito yung pang-family vacation na may swimming pool. Alam na this. It's the setting for many a Filipino movie plot twist.
usage_notes: May malakas na kultural na konotasyon sa Pilipinas na iba sa orihinal na kahulugan nito sa Kanluran bilang isang simpleng otel sa tabi ng daan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **motel** ang matatagpuan sa kahabaan ng EDSA.","translation":"There are many **motels** located along EDSA."}]

translation: to triumph over; to succeed in
meaning_filipino: Ang matagumpay na malampasan ang isang hamon, pagsubok, o hadlang; ang magkamit ng tagumpay sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is your graduation speech energy. It's what you tell yourself you'll do to your thesis, your final exams, or that impossible level in a video game. To pagtagumpayan is to conquer your personal 'final boss', whether it's a difficult project or just waking up on a Monday.
usage_notes: The focus is on the thing being overcome or the goal being achieved.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pagtagumpayan** natin ang mga pagsubok sa buhay.","translation":"We need to **triumph over** the challenges in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos o galaw ng pagbabanta, karaniwang gamit ang kamay o braso, na hindi naman tinutuloy.
original_explanation: 'Yung akmang susuntok pero hindi naman tinuloy. Classic amba 'yan. Parang 'yung boss mong laging nagpaparinig na magtatanggal ng tao pero wala namang nangyayari. Puro amba lang. It's the physical version of "I'm warning you!"
usage_notes: Often used in the context of a fight or a bluff. The verb form is 'umamba' (to make a threatening gesture).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro ka lang **amba**, hindi mo naman kayang ituloy.","translation":"You're all just **threatening gestures**, you can't even follow through."},{"sentence":"Isang **amba** lang niya ay nagsitakbuhan na ang mga bata.","translation":"Just one **threatening gesture** from him and the children ran off."}]

translation: inspection; act of aiming or looking closely
meaning_filipino: Ang maingat na pagtingin, pagsusuri, o pag-asinta sa isang bagay upang matiyak ang kalagayan o tamang direksyon nito.
original_explanation: This is you squinting to read the fine print on a contract. It's what the security guard does to your bag at the mall entrance. It’s also what you do when you're trying to aim a 'tumbang preso' slipper perfectly. It's a focused, purposeful look, usually to check or verify something.
usage_notes: Implies a more thorough or focused look than just 'pagtingin' (looking).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng masusing **pagsipat** sa mga dokumento bago pumirma.","translation":"A thorough **inspection** of the documents is needed before signing."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagsipat** sa target ay laging tiyak.","translation":"His **aiming** at the target is always precise."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno na namumunga ng mangga, na karaniwan sa mga tropikal na bansa tulad ng Pilipinas.
etymology: Isang tambalang salita na binubuo ng "puno" (tree) at "mangga" (mango).
original_explanation: The OG tambayan spot in the province. Perfect for shade, duyan-swinging, and waiting for the fruit to fall so you don't have to climb. Your lola probably has one in her backyard, and the fruit from it tastes 100x better than anything you can buy from the store.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umakyat si Pepe sa **punong-mangga** para kumuha ng hinog na bunga.","translation":"Pepe climbed the **mango tree** to get a ripe fruit."},{"sentence":"Napakalamig magpahinga sa ilalim ng aming **punong-mangga** tuwing hapon.","translation":"It's very cool to rest under our **mango tree** in the afternoon."}]
related: ["puno ng niyog","puno ng saging","puno ng santol","halaman"]

translation: to hold a banquet for; to feast on
meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong pagbaybay para sa "bangketehin." Ang pagdaraos ng isang piging o handaan para sa isang tao o okasyon.
original_explanation: Same as 'bangketehin', just spelled slightly differently, maybe by your tita in a Facebook post. It's the verb form of 'let's party!' or 'let's eat everything in sight!'
usage_notes: A common misspelling or variant of 'bangketehin'. The stress pattern might slightly differ in pronunciation for some speakers, but the meaning is identical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Tara, **bangketihin** na natin 'yang lechon!\" sigaw niya.","translation":"\"Come on, let's **feast on** that lechon!\" he shouted."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng hinuha o palagay tungkol sa isang bagay na walang sapat na batayan o ebidensya.
etymology: From i- (object focus prefix) + pag- + sapantaha (hunch, suspicion).
original_explanation: This is the root of all chismis and "overthinking." It's when you see your crush's "seen" receipt but no reply, and you start to ipagsapantaha that they hate you, they're with someone else, or they were abducted by aliens. It's making a conclusion without the facts. "'Wag mong ipagsapantaha na galit siya, baka lowbatt lang!"
usage_notes: Implies a conclusion drawn from incomplete information or a lack of solid evidence. Often used with a cautionary tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **ipagsapantaha** ang motibo ng isang tao nang hindi siya kinakausap.","translation":"It's difficult to **assume** a person's motive without talking to them."},{"sentence":"**Ipinagsapantaha** ng marami na magkakaroon ng biglaang anunsyo.","translation":"Many **speculated** that there would be a sudden announcement."}]

meaning_filipino: Biglang pagbabago o pagbaba ng tono ng boses habang kumakanta o nagsasalita; sa makabagong gamit, tumutukoy din sa hindi pagtupad sa isang usapan o biglang pagkabigo.
etymology: From 'palakol' (axe). The metaphor is of an axe swing that misses its mark or fails.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'epic fail' moment for a singer. It's when you're belting out a Regine Velasquez song in the shower and your voice suddenly goes from 'Asia's Songbird' to 'distressed goat'. It can also mean flaking on a friend or a date. 'Nag-promise siyang darating, pero pumalakol.'
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of singing when a voice cracks or goes off-key. The secondary meaning of 'to flake' or 'to fail' is more colloquial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kalagitnaan ng kanyang kanta, biglang **pumalakol** ang boses ng singer.","translation":"In the middle of her song, the singer's voice suddenly **cracked**."},{"sentence":"Inaasahan naming mananalo ang team, pero **pumalakol** sila sa huling minuto.","translation":"We expected the team to win, but they **messed up** in the last minute."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtuntong o pagpatong ng paa sa isang bagay o lugar.
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na 'yapak' (talampakan, hakbang) at panlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: What you do when you get home and immediately step on the doormat to wipe your shoes. Also, what you accidentally do to your friend's brand new white sneakers, leading to an immediate 'sorry bes!' It's the action of your paa (foot) making contact with a surface.
usage_notes: Ang pandiwa ay nasa anyong naganap (completed aspect) ngunit maaari ring gamitin bilang pawatas (infinitive). Ang pangkasalukuyan ay 'yumayapak' at panghinaharap ay 'yayapak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal **yumapak** sa bagong wax na sahig.","translation":"It is forbidden **to step on** the newly waxed floor."},{"sentence":"Si Neil Armstrong ang unang taong **yumapak** sa buwan.","translation":"Neil Armstrong was the first person **to step on** the moon."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsampa ng kaso o habla sa korte laban sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: When 'mag-usap tayo' fails and 'barangayan' doesn't cut it. This is the level-up version of conflict, where you involve lawyers, courts, and a whole lot of paperwork. Basically, the climax of every teleserye's business rivalry plot.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix indicates a reciprocal action, meaning two or more parties are suing each other.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nauwi sa korte ang alitan ng magkapitbahay at sila ay nagpasya na **magdemandahan**.","translation":"The neighbors' dispute ended up in court and they decided **to sue each other**."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating hayaang umabot sa puntong kailangan pa nating **magdemandahan**.","translation":"Let's not let it get to the point where we need **to sue each other**."}]

translation: to enslave; to mistreat; to treat as a servant
meaning_filipino: Ituring ang isang tao na parang alipin; abusuhin o pagmalupitan.
original_explanation: This is what a toxic boss does to an overworked employee, or what a villain in a teleserye does to the poor, innocent 'bida'. It's not just making someone a servant, it's the act of stripping away their dignity and treating them as less than human. It's extreme 'power-tripping.'
usage_notes: Carries a very strong negative connotation of abuse and oppression.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi tama na **mang-alila** ng kapwa-tao.","translation":"It is not right to **enslave** a fellow human being."},{"sentence":"Inakusahan siyang **nang-alila** sa kanyang mga kasambahay.","translation":"She was accused of **mistreating** her house helpers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nagpapatunay o nagpapatatag sa isang pahayag, kasunduan, o estruktura.
original_explanation: This is your "resibo" (receipt) when you need to prove a point. In a legal sense, it's your evidence. In construction, it's the rebar that makes the concrete stronger. In a relationship, it's that screenshot you saved just in case. "Anong patibay mo na nandoon ka nga?"
usage_notes: Commonly used in legal, contractual, and even informal contexts to mean proof or evidence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng piskal ng matibay na **patibay** laban sa akusado.","translation":"The prosecutor needs strong **evidence** against the accused."},{"sentence":"Ang pirma mo sa kontrata ang magsisilbing **patibay** ng ating kasunduan.","translation":"Your signature on the contract will serve as **proof** of our agreement."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tribunal o lupon na binubuo ng mga opisyal ng militar upang litisin ang mga kasapi ng sandatahang lakas na akusado ng paglabag sa batas militar.
original_explanation: This is the HR department for soldiers, but for when you *really* mess up. It's a court run by the army, for the army. You won't find your typical civilian judge here; you'll be facing high-ranking officers who expect you to say 'Sir, yes, sir!'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'hukumang-militar' and 'hukumang-panghukbo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang pagsuway sa utos, naharap siya sa **hukumang-hukbo**.","translation":"Because of his insubordination, he faced a **court-martial**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapadaan ng pagkain, inumin, o anumang bagay mula sa bibig patungo sa sikmura sa pamamagitan ng lalamunan.
etymology: From 'lunok' (swallow). The final 'k' is dropped and the vowel 'o' becomes 'u' in this verb conjugation.
original_explanation: To swallow something, literally. Like that giant pill the doctor gave you, or your pride when you have to ask your parents for money again. It's the final act before something goes down your throat. 'Huwag mo nang nguyain, lulunin mo na lang!' (Don't chew it anymore, just swallow it!)
usage_notes: The object-focused verb form of 'lunok'. Also spelled as 'lunukin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihirapan siyang **lulunin** ang malaking tableta.","translation":"He is having a hard time **swallowing** the big tablet."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **lulunin** ang iyong pride at humingi ng tawad.","translation":"You need to **swallow** your pride and ask for forgiveness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o silid na naglalaman ng koleksyon ng mga aklat, peryodiko, at iba pang babasahin para sa paggamit o paghiram ng publiko o mga miyembro.
original_explanation: The original 'co-working space.' It's a quiet place full of books where you're supposed to study, but you end up just using their free Wi-Fi, charging your phone, and taking a nap. The ultimate rule: 'Bawal maingay!' The librarian is the original admin of the group chat.
usage_notes: Can refer to a public library, school library ('silid-aklatan'), or a personal collection of books.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa pampublikong **aklatan** mamayang hapon.","translation":"Let's meet at the public **library** this afternoon."},{"sentence":"Ang dami mong libro, para ka nang may sariling **aklatan**.","translation":"You have so many books, it's like you have your own **library**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtama o pagkabangga ng ulo sa isang matigas na bagay.
original_explanation: That feeling when you stand up too fast under a low ceiling or the top bunk of a double-deck bed. It's the universe's way of saying, 'Hey, slow down.' Also a classic Pinoy comedy sound effect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalimutan niyang yumuko kaya nagkaroon siya ng bukol mula sa **untog** sa pinto.","translation":"He forgot to duck, so he got a lump from the **bump** on the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Itala o ipatala ang isang pangalan, bagay, o kaganapan sa isang opisyal na listahan o talaan.
original_explanation: What you need to do with your SIM card para hindi ma-block. Or 'yung kailangan mong gawin sa LTO para sa bago mong motor. Basically, the adulting verb for making something official, from birth certificates to business names. "Bes, irehistro mo na 'yang online shop mo sa DTI!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **irehistro** ang iyong negosyo para maging legal ito.","translation":"You need to **register** your business to make it legal."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **irehistro** ang bagong silang na sanggol.","translation":"Don't forget to **register** the newborn baby."}]

translation: to be at the tail end, to be last
meaning_filipino: Mapunta o mapabilang sa hulihan ng isang pila, listahan, o kompetisyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pandiwa na 'ma-' at ang salitang ugat na 'buntot' (tail).
original_explanation: This is the opposite of being the leader; it's being the kulelat. It's when you're last in line for the free food, your name is at the bottom of the exam results, or you're the last one to get the joke. Basically, you're at the 'buntot' (tail).
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng kompetisyon o pagraranggo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung hindi ka mag-aaral nang mabuti, baka **mamuntot** ka sa klase.","translation":"If you don't study well, you might **be last** in class."},{"sentence":"Dahil nahuli siya sa pag-alis, **namuntot** siya sa mahabang pila.","translation":"Because he left late, he ended up **at the tail end** of the long line."}]

translation: to do something through a certain way; to take a certain route
meaning_filipino: Gawin ang isang bagay sa isang partikular na paraan o pamamaraan; dumaan sa isang tiyak na ruta.
original_explanation: This is your "how-to" verb. When you can't get what you want directly, you try to 'daanin' it in another way. "Hindi makuha sa santong dasalan, daanin sa santong paspasan." It's the art of the workaround, the classic Filipino "diskarte." Like when you try to win your crush over by being friends with their friends first.
usage_notes: Often used to express solving a problem or achieving something through a specific method, which might be emotional, physical, or strategic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Subukan mong **daanin** sa mabuting usapan ang inyong hindi pagkakaunawaan.","translation":"Try to **resolve** your misunderstanding through a good conversation."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **daanin** sa init ng ulo ang lahat.","translation":"Don't try to **handle** everything through anger."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging maayos, organisado, o nasa tamang lugar ng mga bagay; tumutukoy din sa pangkalahatang itsura o hitsura ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: Your mom's favorite word. "Ano ba 'yang ayos mo?" is the classic parental critique of your ripped jeans and messy hair. It's the state of things being "in order," whether it's your room, your life, or your OOTD. The opposite of "gulo."
usage_notes: Can refer to physical arrangement, one's appearance, or the state/condition of something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ang **ayos** ng iyong buhok ngayon.","translation":"I like the **style** of your hair today."},{"sentence":"Ibalik mo sa dati nitong **ayos** ang mga gamit.","translation":"Return the things to their original **arrangement**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan sa pangingisda na binubuo ng isang mahabang pamalo, pisi, at kawil na ginagamit sa paghuli ng isda.
original_explanation: Eto yung stick na may tali at hook sa dulo na ginagamit para manghuli ng isda. Parang 'yung ginagamit mo para 'mahuli' 'yung atensyon ni crush – kailangan mo ng tamang pain at maraming pasensya. It's the classic fisherman's tool, whether you're fishing for tilapia sa probinsya or for compliments on your new profile pic. The hook part is 'bingwit', and the whole rod setup is 'binwit'.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'bingwit' in casual conversation, but technically 'binwit' is the rod and 'bingwit' is the hook at the end of the line.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda siya ng kanyang **binwit** para sa pangingisda sa ilog bukas.","translation":"He prepared his **fishing rod** for fishing in the river tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking isda ang nahuli sa kanyang bagong **binwit**.","translation":"A big fish was caught on his new **fishing rod**."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilarawan bilang may mga antas o baitang na tulad ng isang hagdan; isinasagawa nang paunti-unti o may mga yugto.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung itsura ng Banaue Rice Terraces. O 'yung gupit ng buhok mo nung high school na "layered". Pwede ring ilarawan ang isang proseso, like 'yung pag-move on mo sa ex mo: hagdan-hagdan, hindi biglaan. Step-by-step, 'ika nga.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri (e.g., hagdan-hagdan na palayan) o pang-abay (e.g., hagdan-hagdang umunlad).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **hagdan-hagdan** na palayan sa Cordillera.","translation":"The **terraced** rice paddies in the Cordillera are beautiful."},{"sentence":"Ang pagbabayad sa utang ay dapat **hagdan-hagdan** para hindi mabigla.","translation":"Paying off a debt should be done **step-by-step** to not be overwhelmed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ibenta ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng subasta, kung saan ang pinakamataas na tumawad ang siyang makakabili.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'subasta', na nangangahulugang 'auction'.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your lola's antique santo when the family needs cash, or to a foreclosed property when you miss your bank payments. It's basically 'going, going, gone!' but for things you probably can't afford anymore. Like selling your pre-loved items on Carousell, but with more drama and a guy with a gavel.
usage_notes: Ang unlaping 'i-' ay nagpapahiwatig na ang pandiwa ay nakapokus sa bagay na isinusubasta.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napilitan silang **isubasta** ang mga alahas ng kanilang pamilya.","translation":"They were forced **to auction off** their family's jewelry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang diplomatikong opisyal na may pinakamataas na ranggo na kumakatawan sa isang estado sa ibang bansa.
original_explanation: The official government representative who represents the Philippines abroad. They're the top diplomat, the face of the country. But now, we also have "brand ambassadors"—influencers who are the ambasador of a whitening soap or a fast-food chain.
usage_notes: Can refer to a diplomatic ambassador or, in modern contexts, a brand ambassador.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **ambasador** ng Pilipinas sa Japan ay dumalo sa pagpupulong.","translation":"The Philippine **ambassador** to Japan attended the meeting."},{"sentence":"Siya ang napiling bagong brand **ambasador** ng sikat na kumpanya.","translation":"She was chosen as the new brand **ambassador** for the famous company."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na gumagamit ng baril, maaaring isang mangangaso, sundalo, atleta sa pamamaril, o kriminal na armado.
original_explanation: This can be the hero or the villain in an action movie. Pwedeng si Cardo Dalisay na nakikipagbarilan sa mga masasamang-loob, or the 'riding-in-tandem' na kinakatakutan. The mamamaril is anyone who shoots a gun; context is key.
usage_notes: The prefix 'mamaN-' indicates a person who habitually or professionally uses the object in the root word ('baril' or gun). The connotation can be neutral (a marksman), positive (a soldier defending), or negative (a criminal).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahabol ng mga pulis ang hindi kilalang **mamamaril**.","translation":"The police are chasing the unknown **gunman**."},{"sentence":"Mahusay na **mamamaril** ang aming lolo noong siya ay nangangaso pa sa gubat.","translation":"Our grandfather was a skilled **marksman** back when he used to hunt in the forest."}]

translation: to plead; to implore; to beseech
meaning_filipino: Ang marubdob na paghiling o pakiusap, na kadalasan ay may kasamang pagpapakumbaba at matinding damdamin.
original_explanation: The level of begging you do when you ask your team lead for an early out on a Friday before a long weekend. It's more intense than 'makiusap'. It's the 'Please, please, please!' energy you channel when you're praying hard not to get called for recitation.
usage_notes: A formal and dramatic word, often found in literature, prayers, or very emotional situations. It carries more weight than 'makiusap' (to request).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magsumamo** ang ina sa doktor na gawin ang lahat para iligtas ang kanyang anak.","translation":"The mother began **to plead** with the doctor to do everything to save her child."},{"sentence":"Araw-araw siyang **nagsumamo** sa Diyos para sa isang himala.","translation":"Every day she **implored** God for a miracle."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng isang mas malaking kabuuan; isang pangkat o dibisyon sa isang paaralan, opisina, o dokumento.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "sección" o Ingles na "section".
original_explanation: Your high school barkada was probably born here. "Anong section mo?" is the ultimate icebreaker on the first day of school. It's your class, your department at work, or that part of the grocery store where they hide the imported chocolates. It's a group, a division, a slice of a bigger whole.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa paaralan (section ng klase), opisina (department/section), dyaryo (sports section), atbp.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkaklase kami noong high school, pareho kaming nasa **Seksyon** A.","translation":"We were classmates in high school, we were both in **Section** A."},{"sentence":"Hanapin mo sa \"frozen goods\" **seksyon** ang mga hotdog.","translation":"Look for the hotdogs in the \"frozen goods\" **section**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking mamalyang-dagat na kumakain ng halaman (herbivore), may bilugang katawan, malapad na nguso, at buntot na kawangis ng sa lumba-lumba.
original_explanation: The chill, herbivore cousin of the manatee found in Philippine waters. They're the sea's original 'body positivity' icons. Legend says sailors used to mistake them for mermaids (*sirena*), which probably means those sailors needed glasses or were out at sea for way too long.
usage_notes: Madalas na napagkakamalang 'sirena' (mermaid) sa mga alamat, ngunit sa biyolohiya, ito ay tumutukoy sa hayop-dagat na *Dugong dugon*.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **duyong** ay isang nanganganib na uri ng hayop na kailangang protektahan sa ating mga karagatan.","translation":"The **dugong** is an endangered species that needs to be protected in our seas."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking **duyong** ang namataan malapit sa baybayin ng Palawan.","translation":"A large **sea cow** was spotted near the coast of Palawan."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtama o pag-unday ng paa sa isang bagay. Tumutukoy din ito sa isang tradisyonal na larong pambata sa Pilipinas na gumagamit ng bolang yari sa rattan.
original_explanation: It's both the action of kicking your problems away (or a soccer ball) and the OG Filipino hacky-sack game that required more grace than your average TikTok dance challenge. Before Mobile Legends, kids actually went outside to play this.
usage_notes: Can refer to the action of kicking or the traditional game itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **sipa** ang tumama sa bola.","translation":"A strong **kick** hit the ball."},{"sentence":"Naglalaro kami ng **sipa** sa kalye noong bata pa kami.","translation":"We used to play **sipa** on the street when we were kids."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalabas ng hangin mula sa sikmura sa pamamagitan ng bibig, na karaniwang may kasamang tunog.
original_explanation: That glorious sound you make after chugging a whole bottle of Coke. Sa ibang kultura, sign of satisfaction 'yan. Dito, 'pag 'di mo tinakpan ang bibig mo, sign 'yan na kailangan mong i-review ang good manners and right conduct mo.
usage_notes: 'Pagdighay' is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malakas na **pagdighal** ay tanda na busog na ang sanggol.","translation":"A loud **burp** is a sign that the baby is full."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang takpan ang bibig sa oras ng **pagdighal**.","translation":"Don't forget to cover your mouth when **burping**."}]

translation: to pry open; to flip up
meaning_filipino: Buhatin o iangat nang biglaan at may puwersa ang isang dulo o bahagi ng isang bagay.
etymology: From the root 'tikwas', meaning to be upturned or pried.
original_explanation: Imagine trying to open a can of corned beef without the key, so you use a spoon. That forceful, awkward prying action? That's 'tikwasin'. Also describes what happens to your hair when you wake up with a bad case of 'bed hair'—it's sticking straight up.
usage_notes: Often used for things that are pried open or flipped upwards, like lids, covers, or even a rebellious tuft of hair.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **tikwasin** ang takip ng lata gamit ang kutsilyo.","translation":"He tried to **pry open** the lid of the can using a knife."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pagsasagawa ng isang gawain o kasanayan upang mapabuti at maging dalubhasa rito.
etymology: From English 'practice', which can be traced through Spanish 'practicar'.
original_explanation: That thing your mom told you to do before a contest, an exam, or a performance. Whether it's for basketball, a new dance craze on TikTok, or your call center spiel, you need to 'magpraktis' para 'practice makes perfect' daw. Or at least, para hindi mapahiya.
usage_notes: The spelling 'mag-practice' is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magpraktis** para sa ating presentasyon bukas.","translation":"We need **to practice** for our presentation tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Araw-araw siyang **nagpapraktis** ng gitara.","translation":"He **practices** the guitar every day."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng pakikidalamhati, pakikiramdam, o pakikiisa sa kalungkutan o pagdurusa ng iba.
etymology: From maki- (social prefix) + ramay (a variant of damay, meaning sympathy or involvement).
original_explanation: Ito yung pagpunta sa burol ng kaibigan o kamag-anak para mag-abot ng tulong o sabihing 'condolence.' Hindi lang ito sa patay; pwede ring makiramay sa kaibigan mong brokenhearted o nawalan ng trabaho. It's about showing up and sharing someone's sorrow, letting them know they're not alone in their sadness.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of grief, loss, or misfortune. The 'maki-' prefix highlights the social act of joining in another's feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa kanilang bahay upang **makiramay** sa pagpanaw ng kanilang ama.","translation":"We went to their house to **offer condolences** for the passing of their father."},{"sentence":"Ang buong komunidad ay nakiramay sa mga biktima ng sakuna.","translation":"The whole community **sympathized** with the victims of the disaster."}]

translation: to conquer, to occupy, to colonize
meaning_filipino: Sakupin o pasailalim sa kapangyarihan ang isang lugar o bansa; gamitin o kunin ang isang espasyo.
original_explanation: History class 101: this is what the Spanish, Americans, and Japanese did to the Philippines. But in 2026, it's also what your officemate does when their stuff slowly creeps into your desk space. Or when one K-Pop fandom sumakop sa Twitter timeline with their hashtags. It's about taking over territory, whether it's a country or your personal bubble.
usage_notes: Has a strong connotation of invasion and control. This is the completed action (past tense) form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bansa ang **sumakop** sa Pilipinas sa loob ng daan-daang taon.","translation":"Many countries **colonized** the Philippines for hundreds of years."},{"sentence":"**Sumakop** na sa buong mesa ang mga gamit niya.","translation":"His things have **occupied** the entire table."}]

translation: to gore; to butt with horns
meaning_filipino: Pagtusok o pag-atake gamit ang sungay, na karaniwang ginagawa ng mga hayop tulad ng kalabaw o toro.
original_explanation: This is what a carabao or bull does when it's ticked off. Think of it as the animal version of a headbutt, but with pointy things. It's the ultimate 'get out of my face' move for horned creatures. Don't be the person who makes the carabao go *sumuwag*.
usage_notes: This is a verb in the completed aspect (past tense), actor-focus. The root word 'suwag' refers to the horn or the act of goring.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **sumuwag** ang kalabaw sa magsasaka.","translation":"The carabao suddenly **gored** the farmer."},{"sentence":"Muntik na akong suwagin ng toro sa Perya, buti na lang nakaiwas ako.","translation":"I was almost **gored** by a bull at the festival, good thing I was able to dodge it."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang anyong tubig, tulad ng ilog o sapa, na may malakas at mabilis na daloy.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (nagpapahiwatig ng katangian) at salitang-ugat na `agos` (daloy).
original_explanation: Yung ilog na parang traffic sa EDSA pag rush hour, tuloy-tuloy ang galaw at walang preno. Kung lovelife mo 'to, 'yung feelings na hindi mapigilan, bumubuhos lang. "Go with the flow" pero literally.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit upang ilarawan ang mga ilog, sapa, o anumang daloy. Maaari ring gamitin sa matalinghagang paraan para sa mga bagay na mabilis at tuloy-tuloy, tulad ng trapiko o usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mapanganib languyan ang ilog dahil **maagos** ito pagkatapos ng malakas na ulan.","translation":"It's dangerous to swim in the river because it has a **strong current** after the heavy rain."},{"sentence":"Naging **maagos** ang daloy ng trapiko nang buksan ang bagong skyway.","translation":"The flow of traffic became **smoothly flowing** when the new skyway was opened."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nagpapahayag ng matinding emosyon tulad ng takot, galit, o tuwa, na para bang nanginginig ang buong katawan.
etymology: From English 'shaking', popularized by internet and meme culture.
original_explanation: The feeling when you see the "seen" notification but no reply. The feeling when your boss says "Can we talk?" The feeling when your crush finally messages you back. It's the Gen Z version of "kinakabahan" or "nanginginig sa galit/tuwa". It's not a physical tremor, it's an emotional earthquake. "OMG I'm literally **shaking** rn."
usage_notes: Used hyperbolically in online conversations and text messages to express a strong emotional reaction. Often written as 'literally shaking'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalimutan ko i-mute sa Zoom tapos narinig nila lahat ng chismis, **shaking** ako!","translation":"I forgot to mute on Zoom and they heard all the gossip, I'm **shaking**!"},{"sentence":"Nanalo ako sa raffle! Literally **shaking** right now!","translation":"I won the raffle! Literally **shaking** right now!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na marunong lumangoy o na ang propesyon o libangan ay paglangoy.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'mang-' at ang salitang-ugat na 'langoy' (swim), na may pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng ugat ('la').
original_explanation: Basically, a human fish. This is the person who actually knows what to do in a pool besides just standing in the shallow end and taking selfies. From Olympic athletes to your friend who's a certified beach bum, a 'manlalangoy' is at home in the water. Sila yung hindi takot sa deep end ng life... or ng swimming pool.
usage_notes: Can refer to a professional athlete or simply someone who swims.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang pambansang **manlalangoy** ang nagwagi ng gintong medalya.","translation":"A national **swimmer** won the gold medal."},{"sentence":"Mahusay na **manlalangoy** si Eric dahil lumaki siya sa tabing-dagat.","translation":"Eric is a good **swimmer** because he grew up by the sea."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining ng maganda at masining na pagsulat ng mga titik at salita.
original_explanation: It's your friend's hobby that makes your own handwriting look like a doctor's prescription. It's the fancy, 'aesthetic' writing you see on wedding invitations and inspirational quotes on Instagram. Basically, making letters look so good you want to frame them.
usage_notes: A loanword from Spanish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang gumawa ng **kaligrapya** para sa mga imbitasyon.","translation":"She loves to do **calligraphy** for invitations."},{"sentence":"Ang sinaunang Baybayin ay isang uri ng **kaligrapya** ng ating mga ninuno.","translation":"The ancient Baybayin is a form of **calligraphy** of our ancestors."}]

translation: to be covered; to be enveloped; to be wrapped
meaning_filipino: Matakpan sa lahat ng panig; mapalibutan o mapuno ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you want your siopao to be: fully 'mabalutan' by the soft, white dough. It's also what happens to a room when the fog machine is on too high at a party. Figuratively, it's how you feel when you're 'mabalutan ng hiya' (enveloped in shame) after a major 'epic fail' moment.
usage_notes: Implies being completely covered or surrounded.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **mabalutan** ng kumot dahil sa sobrang lamig.","translation":"I want **to be wrapped** in a blanket because it's so cold."},{"sentence":"**Nabalutan** ng misteryo ang pagkawala ng alahas.","translation":"The disappearance of the jewelry was **enveloped** in mystery."}]

meaning_filipino: Gasta na dahil sa madalas na paggamit o pagkiskis; nawalan ng talim o tulis.
original_explanation: Yung tsinelas mo na five years mo nang gamit, mula college hanggang sa unang trabaho mo. Flat na flat na, wala nang swelas. 'Yan ang pudpod. O kaya 'yung lapis mong kakatasa lang, after 5 minutes ng pagsusulat, pudpod na ulit. Parang patience mo sa traffic sa EDSA.
usage_notes: Often used for tires, slippers, pencils, and anything that gets worn down by friction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pudpod** na ang gulong ng kotse, kailangan nang palitan.","translation":"The car's tires are **worn out**; they need to be replaced."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong gamitin 'yang kutsilyo, **pudpod** na at hindi makahiwa.","translation":"Don't use that knife, it's **blunt** and can't cut."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang yari sa kahoy na karaniwang ginagamit sa pagpalo, lalo na sa paglalaba noong unang panahon.
original_explanation: This is the OG "pang-hampas" your lola used for laundry before washing machines became a thing. It’s that flat wooden paddle used to beat the dirt out of clothes. Also, the low-key threat for misbehaving kids back in the day. "Isa pang 'mamaya na,' makakatikim ka ng **palu-palo**."
usage_notes: Often associated with traditional laundry methods or corporal punishment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng labandera ang **palu-palo** para tanggalin ang dumi sa mga damit.","translation":"The laundrywoman used the **paddle** to remove the dirt from the clothes."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang lumang **palu-palo** ni Lola sa baul.","translation":"I saw Grandma's old **laundry paddle** in the chest."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa balarila, ito ay isang salita, parirala, o sugnay na nagbibigay-turing o naglalarawan sa isa pang salita sa pangungusap. Karaniwang tumutukoy sa pang-uri o pang-abay.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'extra' in a sentence. It's the word that adds flavor, spice, and unnecessary details. In 'masarap na kape,' 'masarap' is the panuring. It's the supporting actor that makes the main character (the noun or verb) look good... or bad. Basically, it's the grammar term for adjectives and adverbs that you forgot after high school Filipino class.
usage_notes: Primarily a grammatical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pang-uri at pang-abay ay dalawang uri ng **panuring**.","translation":"Adjectives and adverbs are two types of **modifiers**."},{"sentence":"Sa pangungusap na 'Ang magandang dalaga ay mabilis tumakbo,' ang 'magandang' at 'mabilis' ay mga **panuring**.","translation":"In the sentence 'The beautiful lady ran quickly,' 'beautiful' and 'quickly' are **modifiers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng mga titik, salita, o simbolo sa isang papel o anumang ibabaw upang magpahayag ng ideya o kaisipan.
original_explanation: The OG way to express your feelings before PMs and DMs. This is what your prof tells you to do for your 10-page thesis, and what you do in your journal to channel your inner 'main character' energy. It's the act of putting thoughts down, whether it's a grocery list or a love letter.
usage_notes: An actor-focus verb. The person performing the action of writing is the focus of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailan ka huling **magsulat** ng liham para sa isang kaibigan?","translation":"When was the last time you **wrote** a letter for a friend?"},{"sentence":"Balak kong **magsulat** ng isang nobela tungkol sa aking mga karanasan.","translation":"I plan **to write** a novel about my experiences."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang solidong materyal na karaniwang matigas, makintab, at mahusay na konduktor ng kuryente at init (hal. bakal, ginto, tanso).
original_explanation: Can refer to two things: 1) The shiny stuff your alahas, the LRT, and your kawali are made of. 2) The music your tito who wears all black listens to. 'Tito, anong pinapakinggan mo?' 'Rock and roll to the world! Metal!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ginto ay isang uri ng mahalagang **metal**.","translation":"Gold is a type of precious **metal**."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto niyang makinig sa **metal** na musika kaysa pop.","translation":"He prefers listening to **metal** music over pop."}]

translation: to have a nightmare, to suffer from SUNDS
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang isang bangungot o ang biglaang pagkamatay habang natutulog.
original_explanation: The verb form of having that scary sleep experience. 'Sana 'di ako bangungutin mamaya.' (Hope I don't have a nightmare later.) It's the fear of every Filipino who just ate a heavy midnight snack of adobo and rice.
usage_notes: Ang anyong naganap na (past tense) ay 'binangungot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang matulog nang busog na busog, baka ka **bangungutin**.","translation":"Don't sleep on a very full stomach, you might **have a nightmare** (or suffer from SUNDS)."},{"sentence":"Madalas siyang **bangungutin** kapag pagod na pagod.","translation":"He often **has nightmares** when he is very tired."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding pakiramdam ng pag-ayaw o pagkasuklam sa isang bagay na itinuturing na marumi, nakakainis, o imoral.
etymology: From `pang-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `diri` (disgust). The `pan-` + `di-` + `diri` structure indicates the feeling or state of being disgusted.
original_explanation: It's that 'ewww' feeling you get when you see a rat in the kitchen, step on something wet while wearing socks, or read your ex's new cheesy posts. It's a full-body cringe, a visceral reaction that makes you want to sanitize your eyes and your soul. It's stronger than just 'dislike'; it's a 'kadiri-to-the-bones' level of grossness.
usage_notes: A strong emotion. 'Pagkainis' (annoyance) or 'pag-ayaw' (dislike) are milder. 'Pagkasuklam' (hatred/abhorrence) is a close synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang kanyang **pandidiri** nang makita ang bulok na pagkain.","translation":"She could not hide her **disgust** when she saw the rotten food."},{"sentence":"Nakaramdam ako ng **pandidiri** sa mga katiwaliang nabalitaan ko.","translation":"I felt **revulsion** at the corruption I heard about."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino para sa isang taong hindi sinagot o tinanggihan ng kanyang nililigawan.
etymology: A Filipinized term derived from the English word 'busted'.
original_explanation: The official status of someone in the 'friend zone.' When you confess your love and they reply, 'Salamat sa lahat, pero friends lang talaga tayo.' That's it. You're **basted**. It's the romantic equivalent of a 404 Error: feelings not found.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of romance and courtship. It can be used as an adjective ('Basted siya.') or as the root of a verb ('Na-basted ako.').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malungkot si Marco dahil **basted** siya kay Anna.","translation":"Marco is sad because he was **rejected** by Anna."},{"sentence":"Ilang beses ka na bang na-**basted** sa buong buhay mo?","translation":"How many times have you been **rejected** in your entire life?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at tuloy-tuloy na pag-agos o pagtulo ng likido, tulad ng tubig, luha, o dugo.
original_explanation: Think of a tiny stream of water flowing down a rock, or tears silently streaming down someone's face while watching a sad movie. It's not a gush, it's a gentle, steady trickle. It’s the **dalayday** of your pawis (sweat) when you're stuck in traffic without AC. It’s a very poetic word for a slow, continuous flow.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa panitikan o matulaing pagsusulat upang magbigay ng matingkad na imahe ng isang umaagos na likido.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanood niya ang marahang **dalayday** ng tubig mula sa batis.","translation":"He watched the gentle **flow** of water from the spring."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang pisngi, may **dalayday** ng luha dahil sa kalungkutan.","translation":"On her cheeks, there was a **trickle** of tears due to sadness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang may bubong na plataporma sa labas ng isang bahay, karaniwang nasa unang palapag. Ito ay bukas sa mga gilid at nagsisilbing pahingahan o tambayan.
original_explanation: Your lola's favorite spot for judging the neighbors while sipping coffee. The official waiting area for visitors you don't want to let inside the house just yet. It's the original 'work from home' station before laptops were a thing, perfect for shelling peas, reading the newspaper, or just watching the world go by.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'balkonahe' (balcony), though 'beranda' is typically on the ground floor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakahilata ang pusa sa sahig ng **beranda**.","translation":"The cat is lying on the floor of the **veranda**."},{"sentence":"Nagkakape si Lolo sa kanyang paboritong silya sa **beranda** tuwing umaga.","translation":"Grandpa drinks coffee on his favorite chair on the **veranda** every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng kasapi ng isang relihiyosong kongregasyon ng Simbahang Katoliko; mongha.
original_explanation: A woman in a habit, dedicated to religious life. In the Philippines, they're often seen as figures of quiet authority and kindness, running schools and charities. Also, the title for the head nun is 'Mother Superior,' which sounds like a BPO team lead for a holy account.
usage_notes: Can also refer to a 'mother' screw thread or a main pipe, but the primary meaning is a nun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aral ako sa isang paaralang pinapatakbo ng mga **madre**.","translation":"I studied in a school run by **nuns**."},{"sentence":"Si **Madre** Teresa ay kilala sa kanyang pagtulong sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"**Mother** Teresa is known for her work in helping the poor."}]

translation: to drag oneself; to crawl with difficulty
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-usad sa pamamagitan ng pagkaladkad sa katawan dahil sa hirap, pagod, o sakit.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "Monday morning" verb. You're not walking, you're not even crawling properly. You're dragging your whole existence across the floor just to get to the coffee machine. Parang zombie na gumagapang papunta sa sahod.
usage_notes: Often used to depict extreme exhaustion, injury, or desperation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sugatan ang sundalo kaya **humilahod** na lamang siya pabalik sa kampo.","translation":"The soldier was wounded, so he just **dragged himself** back to the camp."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod galing trabaho, halos **humilahod** na ako papasok ng kwarto.","translation":"From being so tired from work, I almost had to **drag myself** into my room."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdakip o pagsilo sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay, lalo na kung ito ay gumagalaw o nagtatago.
original_explanation: The action you do when you see a rare Pokémon, or what the police do to a 'marites' spreading fake news. It's the 'gotcha!' moment, whether it's catching a fish, a thief, or feelings for your best friend.
usage_notes: Used for catching something in motion or actively pursuing something to capture it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **hulihin** ang bola ngunit mabilis itong nakalagpas.","translation":"He tried to **catch** the ball but it quickly got past him."},{"sentence":"**Hulihin** ninyo ang magnanakaw!","translation":"**Arrest** the thief!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sagradong awit o tula, lalo na ang isa sa mga nakapaloob sa Aklat ng mga Salmo sa Bibliya.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "salmo" (psalm), mula sa Latin na "psalmus", na mula sa Sinaunang Griyego na "ψαλμός" (psalmós, "awit na sinasaliwan ng instrumentong de-kuwerdas").
original_explanation: These are the OG worship songs. King David's greatest hits playlist. Before there was Hillsong or Don Moen, there was Salmo 23 ("The Lord is my shepherd..."). It's the part of the Bible that's basically a poetry and songbook for when you're feeling grateful, sad, scared, or just want to praise the Big Guy upstairs.
usage_notes: Halos eksklusibong ginagamit sa kontekstong relihiyoso o biblikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binasa ng pari ang isang **salmo** mula sa Bibliya sa panahon ng misa.","translation":"The priest read a **psalm** from the Bible during the mass."},{"sentence":"Ang **Salmo** 91 ay isang tanyag na panalangin para sa proteksyon.","translation":"**Psalm** 91 is a popular prayer for protection."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa 'One-Time Password', isang password na may-bisa para sa isang transaksyon o pag-login lamang, karaniwang ginagamit para sa seguridad.
etymology: Akronim sa Ingles para sa 'One-Time Password'.
original_explanation: The six-digit code you get via text that gives you anxiety because it expires in 60 seconds. You need it to buy that 12.12 sale item or pay your Meralco bill online. It's the digital gatekeeper to your money.
usage_notes: Laging isinusulat sa malalaking titik bilang OTP. Binibigkas nang paisa-isang letra.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinihintay ko ang **OTP** mula sa bangko para makapag-transfer ako.","translation":"I'm waiting for the **OTP** from the bank so I can transfer."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong ibibigay ang iyong **OTP** kahit kanino!","translation":"Don't give your **OTP** to anyone!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis na papel, plastik, o metal na may butas na disenyo o letra na ginagamit upang maglipat ng disenyo sa isang ibabaw sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay ng tinta o pintura.
original_explanation: Parang template para sa mga lettering projects mo nung high school. Yung paulit-ulit mong ginagamit para sa "Projects in...". Before Canva and printers, ito ang OG graphic design tool.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **istensilin** upang maglagay ng pangalan sa kanyang T-shirt.","translation":"She used the **stencil** to put a name on her T-shirt."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng bagong set ng **istensilin** para sa aking art project.","translation":"I bought a new set of **stencils** for my art project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkawala ng paningin, pansamantala man o permanente, dahil sa labis na liwanag o iba pang sanhi.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na na-high beam ka ng kasalubong na sasakyan sa gabi, o 'yung literal na nasilaw ka sa ganda/gwapo ni crush. Pwede ring "blinded by love," 'yung tipong di mo na nakikita 'yung red flags kasi mabulagan ka na sa pag-ibig.
usage_notes: Often used literally for being blinded by light, but also figuratively for being blinded by emotions like love, greed, or anger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **mabulagan** ako sa sobrang liwanag ng araw paglabas ko ng sinehan.","translation":"I was almost **blinded** by the extreme brightness of the sun when I came out of the movie theater."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mabulagan** sa pera at kalimutan ang mas mahahalagang bagay.","translation":"Don't be **blinded** by money and forget the more important things."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ibong mandaragit na kilala sa bilis ng paglipad at matalas na paningin.
original_explanation: Basically, the sports car of the bird world. Mabilis, astig, at inspiration para sa mga pangalan ng basketball team o condo building. Not something you see every day sa Pinas unless you're watching a documentary or playing a video game.
usage_notes: A direct loanword. Not commonly used in everyday conversation unless the topic is specifically about birds of prey.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **palkon** ay isa sa pinakamabibilis na hayop sa mundo.","translation":"The **falcon** is one of the fastest animals in the world."},{"sentence":"Nakakita sila ng isang bihirang uri ng **palkon** sa kabundukan.","translation":"They saw a rare type of **falcon** in the mountains."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mekanismo, karaniwan ay pedal sa sasakyan, na nagkokontrol sa bilis ng makina.
original_explanation: Yan yung tinatapakan mo sa kotse 'pag late ka na sa work o 'pag narinig mo yung intro ng paborito mong kanta sa radyo. Also known as the 'silinyador'. 'Pag sinabing 'pindutin ang gas,' yan yun.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang "silinyador" sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, lalo na sa mga tsuper at mekaniko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madiin ang pag-apak niya sa **aselerador** para makahabol sa biyahe.","translation":"He pressed hard on the **accelerator** to catch up on his trip."},{"sentence":"Huwag biglain ang pagtapak sa **aselerador** kung madulas ang kalsada.","translation":"Don't suddenly step on the **accelerator** if the road is slippery."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gusali ng pamahalaang lokal ng isang lungsod kung saan nag-oopisina ang alkalde at iba pang opisyal; ang sentro ng administrasyong panlungsod.
etymology: From English 'city hall'. A direct loanword compound.
original_explanation: Ah, the final boss level for any adulting journey. Need a business permit? Cedula? Marriage license? You must brave the long lines, the confusing windows, and the occasional grumpy employee at the city hall. It's a place of both civic duty and epic patience-testing.
usage_notes: Used commonly in both English and Tagalog sentences. The Tagalized spelling 'munisipyo' is used for municipalities (bayan), while 'city hall' is for cities (lungsod).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong pumunta sa **city hall** para kumuha ng business permit.","translation":"I need to go to the **city hall** to get a business permit."},{"sentence":"Ikinasal sila sa **city hall** noong nakaraang linggo.","translation":"They got married at the **city hall** last week."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas at umuulit na tunog na nalilikha ng pag-uga o pagtama ng isang bagay sa iba, karaniwan ay yari sa kahoy o metal.
original_explanation: This is the sound your door makes when someone's knocking like they're the police with a warrant. It's the sound of the water delivery guy dropping the blue container. It's the 'ghost' in the attic that's probably just a rat. Louder than a 'kalansing', less rhythmic than a 'kalampag'. It's the sound that makes you jump and say, 'Ano 'yun?!'
usage_notes: Describes a heavier, looser, and often more irregular sound than 'kalansing' or 'katok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May narinig akong **kalantog** sa aming bubong kagabi.","translation":"I heard a **rattle** on our roof last night."},{"sentence":"Ang malakas na **kalantog** sa pinto ay gumising sa lahat.","translation":"The loud **knocking** on the door woke everyone up."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng kulay na dilaw o may bahid ng dilaw.
original_explanation: The color of old book pages, your teeth after too much coffee, or a shirt that was once white but has seen better days. It's not pure, vibrant yellow; it's yellow-ish. It's the color of nostalgia, and sometimes, poor dental hygiene.
usage_notes: The prefix 'ma-' turns the noun 'dilaw' (yellow) into an adjective describing something as having the quality of that color.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Madilaw** na ang mga pahina ng lumang libro.","translation":"The pages of the old book are already **yellowish**."},{"sentence":"Naging **madilaw** ang puti niyang sapatos dahil sa putik.","translation":"His white shoes became **yellowish** because of the mud."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na katumbas ng anim na raan o 600.
original_explanation: This is how your lola says "600 pesos" when she's haggling at the palengke. It's the vintage, Spanish-era way of counting money, often used by the older generation. It's "anim na raan" with a Spanish accent.
usage_notes: Bahagi ng sistema ng pagbilang sa Espanyol na ginagamit pa rin, lalo na para sa pera at ng mga nakatatanda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umabot sa **seisyentos** pesos ang binayaran niya para sa mga prutas.","translation":"She paid **six hundred** pesos for the fruits."},{"sentence":"Mayroon daw **seisyentos** na pamilya ang naapektuhan ng baha.","translation":"They said there were **six hundred** families affected by the flood."}]

meaning_filipino: May kulay o katangiang tulad ng ginto; ginintuan.
etymology: From 'ginto' (gold) and the prefix 'mala-' (like/similar to). Literally 'gold-like.'
original_explanation: Describe the sunset at Manila Bay? **Malaginto**. The color of perfectly fried chicken skin? **Malaginto**. That highlight on your cheekbones that's on fleek? **Malaginto**. It means golden, something that shines and looks precious like gold. It’s the color of luxury, success, and really good lumpia.
usage_notes: Used to describe color, sheen, or value.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang buhok ay kumikinang na parang **malaginto** sa sikat ng araw.","translation":"Her hair shone like it was **golden** in the sunlight."},{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng **malaginto** na palayan tuwing anihan.","translation":"The **golden** rice fields during harvest are so beautiful."}]

translation: act of making something revolve or orbit
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapagalaw sa isang bagay sa paraang paikot sa isang sentrong punto, tulad ng pagpapa-orbit sa planeta.
etymology: From pa- + pa- + ikit, meaning "the act of causing to revolve."
original_explanation: This is what the Earth does around the sun. On a less cosmic level, it's what you do to your toy car around a makeshift track, or what you feel your life is doing—circling the same problems. "Paikot-ikot lang." The more formal, astronomical version.
usage_notes: More formal and often used in scientific or technical contexts compared to 'pagpapaikot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentista ang **pagpapaikit** ng mga buwan sa paligid ng Jupiter.","translation":"Scientists are studying the **orbiting** of moons around Jupiter."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapaikit** ng elisi ng eroplano ang nagbibigay-daan sa paglipad nito.","translation":"The **revolving** of the airplane's propeller allows it to fly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang utos o mungkahi na pigilan na ang isang tao sa social media o sa telepono.
original_explanation: The official battle cry of your friends when you keep complaining about your toxic ex's new posts. It's the 'girl, just do it' of the digital world. Pag sinabi nilang 'Block mo na,' it's not a suggestion, it's a diagnosis. The cure? The block button.
usage_notes: Karaniwang maririnig sa mga usapan tungkol sa mga relasyon at social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kulit niya, sige na, i-**block mo na** para matahimik ka.","translation":"He's so annoying, go on, **block him now** so you can have peace."},{"sentence":"Friend: 'Nakita mo ba yung IG story niya?' Me: 'Hindi, kasi sabi mo **block mo na** di ba?'","translation":"Friend: 'Did you see his IG story?' Me: 'No, because you told me to **block him now**, right?'"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakakroon ng mga guhit, tupi, o kuluntoy sa balat o ibabaw ng isang bagay dahil sa pagtanda, pagkababad sa tubig, o pagkatuyo.
original_explanation: This happens to your fingers after a long swim, to a 'pasas' (raisin) from a grape, or to your shirt when you cram it in your bag. For humans, it's the reason the anti-aging industry is a billion-dollar business. 'Friend, anong secret mo? Bakit hindi pa nangungulubot 'yang mukha mo?'
usage_notes: Can apply to skin, fabric, paper, fruits, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mangulubot** ang kanyang mga daliri matapos magbabad sa pool.","translation":"Her fingers started to **wrinkle** after soaking in the pool."},{"sentence":"Kapag hindi mo diniligan ang halaman, **mangungulubot** ang mga dahon nito at mamamatay.","translation":"If you don't water the plant, its leaves will **shrivel** and it will die."}]

translation: young shoot of a bamboo or banana plant
meaning_filipino: Ang usbong o murang talbos ng kawayan o saging.
original_explanation: Think of it as the baby of a bamboo or banana plant. It's the plant equivalent of a newborn. In some provinces, they cook the 'supang ng kawayan' (bamboo shoots), which you might know as 'labong'. So, before it becomes the sturdy bamboo you see, it was a smol, soft 'supang'.
usage_notes: Often used in agricultural or rural contexts. 'Labong' is the more common term for edible bamboo shoots.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **supang** ng saging ang tumubo pagkatapos ng ulan.","translation":"Many young banana **shoots** grew after the rain."},{"sentence":"Ang **supang** ng kawayan ay tinatawag ding labong at masarap iluto.","translation":"The bamboo **shoot** is also called labong and is delicious when cooked."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paglalaro ng isport na badminton.
original_explanation: The go-to sport for Pinoys who want to 'mag-exercise' but don't want the full commitment of a gym membership. It's fun, you can play it almost anywhere (even in the street, watch out for cars!), and it's a great excuse for post-game milk tea. 'Tara, **magbadminton** tayo!' is the new 'Tara, kape?'
usage_notes: A verb formed by adding the prefix "mag-" to the English noun "badminton".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Niyaya niya akong **magbadminton** sa darating na Sabado.","translation":"He/She invited me **to play badminton** this coming Saturday."}]

translation: to celebrate Noche Buena (Christmas Eve feast)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa o pagdaraos ng Noche Buena, ang tradisyonal na handaan sa hatinggabi ng bisperas ng Pasko.
etymology: Mula sa "Noche Buena" (mula sa Espanyol "Nochebuena" - Good Night) + panlaping "mag-".
original_explanation: 'Yung paghahanda at pagkain kasama ang pamilya at mga kaibigan pagpatak ng midnight ng Dec 25. Ito 'yung event kung saan legal mag-extra rice ng madaling araw habang naka-pajama at nag-aabang ng regalo. The ultimate Pinoy Christmas midnight snack... na full-blown fiesta.
usage_notes: Isang salitang kultural na tumutukoy sa isang partikular na tradisyon ng Pasko sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan kayo **magno-Notsebuwena** ngayong taon?","translation":"Where will you **celebrate Noche Buena** this year?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang patay, nasawi, o hindi na gumagana.
etymology: Possibly onomatopoeic, from the sound of a gulp or a last breath.
original_explanation: Slang for "dead." You use this for dramatic effect. "Yung phone ko, nahulog sa inidoro. Tigok na." Or when your favorite character in a series unexpectedly dies: "Hala, tigok si Iron Man!" It's less formal than 'patay' and has a bit of a final, almost comedic finality to it.
usage_notes: Highly informal and considered slang. Can refer to people, animals, or inanimate objects (like electronics).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang iglap, **tigok** ang langaw na pinalo niya.","translation":"In an instant, the fly he swatted was **dead**."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa pagtawid, baka ka ma-**tigok** diyan.","translation":"Be careful crossing, you might **croak** there."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtanggal o paghiwalay mula sa pagkakakabit, pagkakadikit, o pagiging bahagi ng isang grupo o istruktura.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your Christmas decorations in February. It's also when a band member leaves to go solo. O 'yung ka-team mo sa project na biglang nag-resign a week before the deadline. "Bes, bumaklas na si ano sa team!" It's the act of taking something apart, whether it's a piece of furniture or a relationship.
usage_notes: Ito ang pandiwang nasa anyong pangkasalukuyan o pangnagdaan (actor-focus) ng salitang-ugat na 'baklas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumaklas** ang isang piyesa mula sa makina.","translation":"A piece **detached** from the machine."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **bumaklas** sa kanilang banda upang mag-solo career.","translation":"He decided to **break away** from their band to have a solo career."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang biglaan, hindi inaasahan, at walang anumang babala o pahiwatig.
etymology: Isang idyomatikong pagpapahayag. Ang "kaginsa-ginsa" ay nangangahulugang biglaan, at ang pagdaragdag ng "di-" ay nagpapatindi sa kahulugan sa halip na maging negasyon.
original_explanation: This is the 'bigla' for the literary folks, the 'sanaol' for poets. It’s when your 13th-month pay di-kaginsaginsa appears in your bank account a week early. Or when a plot twist in a teleserye hits you so hard you need a moment. It’s more dramatic and has more flair than your everyday 'bigla na lang'. The 'di-' here is a classic case of 'it's complicated'—instead of negating, it emphasizes the suddenness.
usage_notes: Isang pampanitikan at lumang salita. Ang "kaginsa-ginsa" ay mas karaniwan, ngunit pareho ang kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-kaginsaginsa**, isang anino ang dumaan sa kanyang likuran.","translation":"**Suddenly**, a shadow passed behind him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sangay ng serbisyo ng gobyerno na binubuo ng mga kawaning nagtatrabaho para sa pamahalaan, na karaniwang pinipili batay sa merito sa pamamagitan ng mga pagsusulit.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'stable job' dream of many Filipino parents for their kids. Eto yung trabaho sa gobyerno. Para makapasok ka, kailangan mo munang talunin ang final boss: ang Civil Service Exam. Once you're in, you get to experience the joys of government paperwork, 13th month pay, and the occasional 'Salamat, PRRD' tarpaulin.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa pampublikong sektor ng pagtatrabaho sa gobyerno, hindi kasama ang militar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming nagnanais na makapasa sa pagsusulit para makapasok sa **serbisyo sibil**.","translation":"Many aspire to pass the exam to enter the **civil service**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging walang awa, damdamin, o konsensya; kalupitan o kabagsikan.
original_explanation: Describes the person who designed pop-up ads, the one who leaves the last piece of pizza but it's just the crust, or a building that's just a gray, concrete box. It's the vibe of pure, cold, corporate profit-seeking over human feeling.
usage_notes: A highly figurative term used to describe extreme cruelty or a lack of empathy or aesthetic warmth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **kawalang-kaluluwa** nang saktan niya ang hayop.","translation":"He showed his **heartlessness** when he hurt the animal."},{"sentence":"Ang **kawalang-kaluluwa** ng digmaan ay nag-iwan ng maraming sugat sa sangkatauhan.","translation":"The **soullessness** of war left many wounds on humanity."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nakatakdang tumanggap ng ari-arian, titulo, o posisyon mula sa isang yumaong kamag-anak o sinundan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "tagapag-" (doer/agent of action) at sa salitang ugat na "mana" (inheritance).
original_explanation: The 'Lucky Me!' of family dynamics. This is the person who gets lola's house, dad's business, or in teleseryes, the entire hacienda. They're either the spoiled kontrabida or the humble protagonist who didn't know they were rich all along.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa parehong lalaki at babae. Ang mga hiram na salitang 'eredero' (lalaki) at 'eredera' (babae) ay ginagamit din.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang kaisa-isang anak, siya ang naging **tagapagmana** ng lahat ng kanilang yaman.","translation":"As the only child, she became the **heiress** to all their wealth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-alis sa tahanan o sa pangangalaga ng mga magulang nang walang pahintulot.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + `layas` (to go away, to roam).
