original_explanation: The classic teenage drama move after your parents say "Hangga't nakatira ka sa pamamahay ko..." (As long as you live in my house...). It involves packing a bag with 3 shirts and a teddy bear, only to come back a few hours later because you got hungry.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to running away from home or a place of responsibility.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglalayas** ay hindi solusyon sa problema ng pamilya.","translation":"**Running away from home** is not a solution to family problems."},{"sentence":"Pinagsisihan niya ang kanyang **paglalayas** noong siya ay bata pa.","translation":"He regretted **running away** when he was younger."}]

translation: to be compared to; to be likened to
meaning_filipino: Ang maihambing o maitulad sa isang bagay o tao upang ipakita ang pagkakatulad o pagkakahawig.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` + `halin-` (isang fossilized prefix) + `tulad` (like, similar).
original_explanation: It's the verb form of "para kang..." or "you're like...". When your mom says your messy room is `mahalintulad sa binagyong palengke` (can be likened to a market hit by a typhoon), that's it. It’s a very formal word for making a comparison or simile.
usage_notes: Napakapormal at pampanitikan. Ang 'maihambing' o 'maikumpara' ay ang mas karaniwang katumbas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pag-ibig ay **mahalintulad** sa isang ilog na hindi natutuyo.","translation":"Her love can **be likened to** a river that never runs dry."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay ng tao ay madalas **mahalintulad** sa isang gulong, minsan nasa ibabaw, minsan nasa ilalim.","translation":"A person's life is often **compared to** a wheel, sometimes you're on top, sometimes you're at the bottom."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng paa sa ibabaw ng isang bagay, sadya man o hindi.
original_explanation: Can be literal, like accidentally stepping on your dog's tail ('pagtapak sa buntot'), or stepping on fresh cement. Can also be figurative, like 'pagtapak sa pagkatao', which means to disrespect or trample on someone's dignity—a classic teleserye villain move.
usage_notes: Can have a neutral meaning (to step) or a negative one (to trample, disrespect).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa **pagtapak** dahil basa ang sahig.","translation":"Be careful where you **step** because the floor is wet."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtapak** sa karapatan ng iba ay hindi katanggap-tanggap.","translation":"The **act of stepping on** the rights of others is unacceptable."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraan ng pagiging nasa maliliit na grupo, pangkat, o pulutong; hindi sabay-sabay kundi paunti-unting mga pangkat.
original_explanation: How people arrive at a party—not all at once, but in small squads. 'Uy, andyan na sila Anna's barkada!' It’s also how chismis spreads, from one small group to the next.
usage_notes: Describes the manner in which people or things are grouped or arrive. It emphasizes their formation into several distinct groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pulu-pulutong** na dumating ang mga bisita sa kasal.","translation":"The guests arrived **in groups** at the wedding."},{"sentence":"Nagmartsa nang **pulu-pulutong** ang mga sundalo.","translation":"The soldiers marched **in platoons**."}]

translation: to be able to gather; to be able to collect
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang magsama-sama ng mga tao sa isang lugar, o mangolekta at pagsamahin ang mga bagay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `makapag-` (kakayahan) at salitang-ugat na `tipon`.
original_explanation: This can mean two things. First, it's the ability to get the whole barkada together for a reunion, which is a miracle in itself. Second, it's the ability to save up money ('makapagtipon ng pera') for a big purchase like a new phone or a concert ticket. It's about bringing things—or people—together.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pagtitipon ng mga tao (gathering) o pagkolekta/pag-iipon ng mga bagay tulad ng pera o gamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaasahan naming **makapagtipon** ng sapat na pondo para sa aming proyekto.","translation":"We are hoping **to be able to collect** enough funds for our project."},{"sentence":"Sana **makapagtipon** tayong lahat muli sa susunod na taon.","translation":"I hope we can all **be able to gather** again next year."}]

meaning_filipino: Naaayon sa tamang pag-iisip, lohika, o katarungan; may sapat na batayan o dahilan.
etymology: From `ma-` (having the quality of) + `katwiran` (reason, justice), from `tuwid` (straight).
original_explanation: This is when your argument actually makes sense and isn't just pure 'hugot' or 'kasi sabi ko.' It's that rare moment in a group project when someone's suggestion is logical, not just the easiest way out. It’s what you hope your boss is when you ask for a leave. 'Boss, makatwiran naman po 'yung request ko, 'di ba?'
usage_notes: Often used in arguments, legal contexts, or discussions about fairness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Makatwiran** ang desisyon ng hukom na paboran ang mga manggagawa.","translation":"The judge's decision to favor the workers was **just**."},{"sentence":"Sana ay magbigay ka ng **makatwiran** na dahilan kung bakit ka nahuli.","translation":"I hope you can give a **reasonable** explanation for why you were late."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagbibigay o pagtulong nang bukal sa loob at hindi naghahangad ng anumang kapalit o pansariling kapakinabangan.
original_explanation: This is the kind of love your mom gives. She gives you the last piece of chicken joy even if it's her favorite, and she won't bring it up in an argument three weeks later. It's giving without expecting anything in return, not even a 'thank you' post on social media. Pure generosity.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at matulain na salita para sa pagiging di-makasarili, madalas na ginagamit sa panitikan o upang ilarawan ang mga dakilang gawa ng kabutihan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang serbisyo ng mga frontliner ay isang halimbawa ng **walang-pag-iimbot** na pagtulong sa kapwa.","translation":"The service of frontliners is an example of **selfless** help to others."},{"sentence":"Ibinigay niya ang kanyang tulong nang **walang-pag-iimbot**.","translation":"He gave his help **unselfishly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging lubog o papasok, partikular na tumutukoy sa mga pisngi dahil sa pagkapayat, pagtanda, o sakit.
original_explanation: This is the look you get after pulling an all-nighter for a final exam or a major client presentation. Your cheeks just decide to retreat into your face. It's the 'puyat-na-puyat' or 'sobrang-payat' aesthetic. 'Grabe, ang hupak ng pisngi mo! Nag-diet ka ba?'
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe sunken cheeks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halatang may sakit ang matanda dahil sa kanyang **hupak** na mga pisngi.","translation":"It was obvious the old man was sick because of his **sunken** cheeks."},{"sentence":"Naging **hupak** ang mukha niya matapos ang ilang linggong pagtatrabaho nang walang sapat na tulog.","translation":"His face became **hollowed** after weeks of working without enough sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bukas at pampublikong espasyo sa isang bayan o lungsod, karaniwang napapaligiran ng mga gusali tulad ng simbahan, munisipyo, at pamilihan.
original_explanation: The OG tambayan spot before malls existed. It's the town's central park where you'd find the church, the municipal hall, and probably a statue of a national hero. It's where lolo and lola had their first date, and where town fiestas really go down.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to the central town square, especially in older, more established towns and cities in the Philippines. 'Liwasan' is a more formal Tagalog equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkita-kita ang magkakaibigan sa **plasa** pagkatapos ng misa.","translation":"The friends met at the **plaza** after the mass."},{"sentence":"Maraming nagtitinda ng fishball at kwek-kwek sa **plasa** tuwing hapon.","translation":"There are many vendors selling fishball and kwek-kwek at the **plaza** every afternoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manggagamot na dalubhasa sa pag-aaral, pag-diagnose, at paggamot ng mga sakit at kondisyon ng balat, buhok, at mga kuko.
original_explanation: The wizard you see to fight pimples, dark spots, and other 'skin-surance' claims. Your skin's best friend and your wallet's worst enemy. Sila yung nagsasabi kung anong 'hiyang' sa iyo.
usage_notes: Often shortened to 'derma' in casual conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpatingin ako sa isang **dermatologo** para sa aking allergy sa balat.","translation":"I went to see a **dermatologist** for my skin allergy."},{"sentence":"Magastos ang mga produkto na inireseta ng **dermatologo** ko.","translation":"The products prescribed by my **dermatologist** are expensive."}]

translation: to strive for; to work hard for
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa nang buong sigasig, tiyaga, at pagsisikap upang makamit ang isang layunin o mithiin.
original_explanation: The verb form of your parents' life advice. It's what OFWs do abroad, what BPO agents do on the night shift, and what students do to pass their thesis. It's pouring your blood, sweat, and tears (and maybe some instant coffee) into something you really want. 'Pagsumikapan mo para sa pamilya mo.'
usage_notes: This is a command or infinitive form. The noun form is `pagsusumikap` (the act of striving).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pagsumikapan** mong maabot ang iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"**Strive** to reach your dreams."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **pagsumikapan** ang pagkakaroon ng isang mapayapang komunidad.","translation":"We must **work hard for** the creation of a peaceful community."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng paglala o pagtindi ng isang sitwasyon, karamdaman, o problema.
original_explanation: It's what happens when you try to 'fix' things but end up making them ten times worse. Like pouring gasoline on a fire, or replying 'K' to an angry message. You're just aggravating the situation.
usage_notes: A causative verb. Its only function is to describe something that makes a bad situation even more severe.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hindi agarang pagpapatingin sa doktor ay **makalala** sa iyong sakit.","translation":"Not seeing a doctor immediately can **worsen** your illness."},{"sentence":"Ang pagdaragdag ng isyu ay **makalala** lamang sa hidwaan.","translation":"Adding another issue will only **aggravate** the conflict."}]

translation: to take turns repeatedly, to alternate constantly
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pagpapalitan ng posisyon, gawain, o pagkakataon sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao o bagay.
etymology: From 'salisi' (alternate), with reduplication ('sali-sali') and suffix '-han' to form a verb indicating a reciprocal or repeated action.
original_explanation: Parang sa group project, nag-sali-salisihan kayo sa pagiging puyat. Or sa BPO, 'yung pagpasok ng agents for day shift and night shift. It's the constant act of alternating, like a tag team match that never ends.
usage_notes: The reduplication emphasizes the continuous and repeated nature of the alternation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nag-sali-salisihan** ang araw at ulan buong hapon.","translation":"The sun and rain **alternated constantly** all afternoon."},{"sentence":"**Sali-salisihan** tayo sa pagbabantay sa tindahan.","translation":"Let's **repeatedly take turns** watching the store."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuang halaga o bilang na resulta ng pagdaragdag ng dalawa o higit pang numero; ang kabuuan.
original_explanation: The grand total. After a night out with friends, it's the scary number at the bottom of the bill that everyone has to chip in for. "Suma total, magkano inabot?" (Sum total, how much did it reach?) It’s the final count, the bottom line, the number that makes you say "Ay, ang mahal!" or "Keri lang."
usage_notes: Often used in the phrase 'suma total' to mean 'grand total'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **suma** ng lahat ng ating nagastos ngayong buwan?","translation":"What is the **sum** of all our expenses this month?"},{"sentence":"**Suma** total, mas malaki ang kita kaysa sa gastos.","translation":"**In total**, the income was greater than the expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nagmula o mamamayan ng bansang India. Sa kolokyal na gamit, maaaring tumukoy sa mga nagpapautang.
original_explanation: Refers to someone from India. But let's be real, sa Pinas, when you hear 'Indian,' your mind often jumps to the '5-6' money lender on a motorcycle. 'Nandyan na 'yung Indian!' means 'Time to pay up!' It's a widely known stereotype, often used without malice but can be problematic and is best avoided.
usage_notes: The term is sometimes used stereotypically to refer to South Asian money lenders, often in the context of '5-6' loans. This usage can be considered pejorative and is based on a generalization.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang pagkain sa bagong bukas na **Indian** restaurant.","translation":"The food at the newly opened **Indian** restaurant is delicious."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot sa **Indian** na nag-aalok ng pautang, tao rin sila.","translation":"Don't be afraid of the **Indian** man offering a loan, they are people too."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na ibon na may kulay dilaw na balahibo (bagaman may iba pang kulay), na kilala sa magandang huni nito at madalas alagaan bilang isang alagang hayop.
original_explanation: That yellow bird from the cartoons, usually seen tweeting around someone's head after they've been hit with a hammer. In real life, they're known for their singing. For titos and titas, it's a prized pet. For the rest of us, it's Tweety Bird.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to the bird species (Serinus canaria domestica).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng huni ng **kanaryo** tuwing umaga.","translation":"The **canary's** song is beautiful every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong laging may pag-asa at positibong pananaw sa hinaharap sa kabila ng mga pagsubok.
original_explanation: The opposite of your friend who always says 'wala na, finish na.' This is the person who, despite getting ghosted, still believes 'baka busy lang siya.' They see the silver lining even when the cloud is a typhoon warning signal level 5.
usage_notes: A very positive trait, often used to describe someone with a resilient spirit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit maraming problema, nananatili siyang **maasahin** na gaganda rin ang lahat.","translation":"Even with many problems, she remains **hopeful** that everything will get better."},{"sentence":"Isang **maasahin** na pananaw ang kailangan natin sa panahong ito.","translation":"An **optimistic** perspective is what we need in these times."}]

translation: to meddle; to interfere; to intervene
meaning_filipino: Ang pakikialam sa usapan, gawain, o pribadong buhay ng iba nang walang paanyaya o pahintulot.
original_explanation: To butt in where you're not wanted. It's what your tita does when she asks 'Kailan ka mag-aasawa?' at a family reunion. It’s the official verb for being a 'pakialamero/pakialamera'. The ultimate hugot line against this is, 'Huwag kang **manghimasok** sa buhay na hindi naman sa'yo.' (Don't meddle in a life that isn't yours.)
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of unwelcome intrusion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **manghimasok** sa desisyon ng kanyang mga anak.","translation":"She doesn't want **to meddle** in her children's decisions."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan ko siya na huwag **manghimasok** sa aming usapan.","translation":"I told him not **to interfere** in our conversation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagang balbal mula sa internet para sa isang lalaki na sinasabing matagumpay at tanyag ngunit mas pinipiling mamuhay nang hiwalay sa mga pamantayang panlipunan, katulad ng isang "lone wolf".
etymology: A recent English slang phrase, combining "sigma" (from the Greek alphabet, used metaphorically) and "male".
original_explanation: This is the guy in your feed who posts motivational quotes over a picture of a wolf or Keanu Reeves. He's supposedly the "lone wolf" who's too cool for the social hierarchy, unlike the "alpha" or "beta". Basically, it's a personality type invented by the internet for guys who think they're mysterious and independent. #GRINDSET
usage_notes: This is 100% internet slang and is not a traditional Filipino concept. It's used ironically or by those who follow online "manosphere" culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag niyang **sigma male** ang sarili niya dahil mas gusto niyang magtrabaho mag-isa.","translation":"He called himself a **sigma male** because he prefers to work alone."},{"sentence":"Napanood ko sa TikTok ang tungkol sa mga katangian ng isang **sigma male**.","translation":"I watched a TikTok about the traits of a **sigma male**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng tao na madaling makalimot sa mga bagay-bagay, impormasyon, o pangako.
etymology: ma- (adjective prefix) + limot (forget) + -in (suffix denoting a characteristic)
original_explanation: Are you the friend who always forgets birthdays, anniversaries, or kung saan mo nilapag 'yung phone mo 5 seconds ago? Congrats, malimutin ka. It's the polite way of saying your brain is like a computer with 1KB of RAM. 'Pasensya na, malimutin lang talaga, hindi pa manhid.'
usage_notes: Describes a person's tendency to forget.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **malimutin** si lola mula nang siya ay tumanda.","translation":"Grandma became **forgetful** ever since she got old."},{"sentence":"Isulat mo para hindi mo makalimutan, alam kong **malimutin** ka.","translation":"Write it down so you don't forget, I know you're **forgetful**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahing yunit ng pananalapi sa Estados Unidos at iba pang mga bansa.
original_explanation: It's like 'dolyar', but the spelling your tita from the province uses when she messages you on FB asking for 'pasalubong'. It's the less common, slightly more 'jologs' spelling, but everyone gets what you mean.
usage_notes: 'Dolyar' is the more standard and preferred spelling based on Filipino orthography.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkano ang palitan ng piso sa **dolar** ngayon?","translation":"What is the exchange rate of the peso to the **dollar** today?"},{"sentence":"Nag-iipon siya ng **dolar** para sa kanyang paglalakbay sa Amerika.","translation":"He is saving **dollars** for his trip to America."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalok o pagbibigay ng isang ari-arian, tulad ng bahay o sasakyan, para gamitin ng iba kapalit ng regular na bayad o upa.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino side hustle. If you have an extra room, a condo, or even a parking space, you can 'magpaupa' to earn passive income. It's the landlord life, complete with chasing down tenants for rent on the 15th and 30th.
usage_notes: The person doing the action is the landlord or owner. The person receiving the action is the tenant ('umupa').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **magpaupa** ng isang kwarto sa kanilang bahay para sa dagdag na kita.","translation":"They decided to **rent out** a room in their house for extra income."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magpaupa** sa taong hindi marunong magbayad sa tamang oras.","translation":"It's hard to **lease** to a person who doesn't know how to pay on time."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging mapalad o pagkakaroon ng magandang kapalaran.
original_explanation: That feeling when you get the last piece of chicken joy, find 100 pesos in your old jeans, or when your Grab ride arrives in 1 minute. It's the universe giving you a high-five. The opposite of 'malas'.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a day, a transaction, or a person who brings good luck. 'Buwenas na araw' means 'lucky day'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Buwenas** ako ngayon, nanalo ako sa raffle!","translation":"I'm **lucky** today, I won the raffle!"},{"sentence":"Sana maging **buwenas** ang unang araw ng ating bagong negosyo.","translation":"I hope the first day of our new business will be **fortunate**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi tuwid; may liko o baluktot.
original_explanation: Describes anything that's not a straight line, from a winding road in Baguio to the shape of your back after sitting in front of a computer for 8 hours straight. It can also be used to describe a corrupt official's path ('kurbado ang daan').
usage_notes: Often used to describe roads, shapes, or even physical posture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa **kurbado** na daan papuntang Tagaytay.","translation":"Be careful on the **curved** road to Tagaytay."},{"sentence":"Naging **kurbado** ang likod niya dahil sa maling pag-upo.","translation":"His back became **crooked** from improper sitting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong hangal, tanga, o kulang sa pag-iisip. Ito ay isang salitang maaaring ituring na nakakainsulto.
original_explanation: This is an old-school insult, the kind your lolo might have muttered under his breath. It's stronger than 'bobo' and has a more... classic, almost literary feel to it. Not something you'd hear in a BPO, but maybe in a period drama.
usage_notes: Considered a very strong and offensive insult. Its usage is now rare and largely archaic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **uslak** ng kanyang kaaway matapos siyang maloko.","translation":"His enemy called him a **fool** after he was tricked."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapadala sa mga sabi-sabi, para hindi ka magmukhang **uslak**.","translation":"Don't be swayed by rumors, so you don't look like a **simpleton**."}]

translation: to gather in small, separate groups
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbubuo ng iba't ibang maliliit na pangkat o grupo sa isang mas malaking pagtitipon; paghiwa-hiwalay sa mga kumpol.
original_explanation: Picture a high school reunion. Instead of one big happy group, everyone forms their own little circles: the "successful" ones here, the "still single" ones there, the "BFFs from Grade 6" in a corner. 'Yan ang magkumpul-kumpol. It's the opposite of one big happy family; it's a bunch of smaller, clustered happy families.
usage_notes: The reduplication of "kumpol" emphasizes the formation of multiple, distinct clusters.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng pulong, **nagkumpul-kumpol** ang mga empleyado upang pag-usapan ang mga bagong patakaran.","translation":"After the meeting, the employees **gathered in small groups** to discuss the new policies."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong **magkumpul-kumpol** diyan, halikayo at sumali sa sayawan!","translation":"Don't just **gather in your small groups** there, come and join the dancing!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaki at bilog na prutas na may matamis at makatas na laman, karaniwang kulay kahel o berde.
original_explanation: 'Yung paboritong palamig sa tag-init! Kinakayod para gawing juice, or hinihiwa for dessert. It's the less-dramatic cousin of the pakwan (watermelon). Perfect pang-fiesta or after-lunch treat para "magbawas ng umay."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si Nanay ng matamis na **milon** sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a sweet **melon** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing pantay o magkapantay ang isang bagay o ibabaw; i-ayon sa isang tiyak na linya o pamantayan.
original_explanation: This is what your boss tells the project manager to do with the budget, or what you wish you could do to your life problems. It's about making things straight and even, like using a ruler on a crooked line or trying to balance your work and love life. 'Pakitama lang 'yung alignment, parang 'yung isip mo.'
usage_notes: Often used in construction, engineering, or when talking about aligning things conceptually.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nibelahin** mo muna ang lupa bago tayuan ng pader.","translation":"**Level** the ground first before building a wall."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **nibelahin** ang mga layunin ng bawat departamento.","translation":"The goals of each department need to be **aligned**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang tama, wasto, o angkop.
original_explanation: A very common, very Pinoy way of saying 'correct!' or 'right!'. Often accompanied by a thumbs up. 'Bes, does this look good on me?' '**Korik**! That's runway-ready!'. It's the ultimate validation you can get from a friend. A variant spelling of the more common 'korek'.
usage_notes: Extremely common in casual, spoken Filipino. Used as an interjection or an adjective. The spelling 'korek' is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Korik** ang sagot mo sa number 5!","translation":"Your answer for number 5 is **correct**!"},{"sentence":"Tanong niya, 'Maganda ba ako?' Sagot ko, '**Korik**!'","translation":"She asked, 'Am I beautiful?' I answered, '**Correct**!'"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging maingat; pag-iwas sa panganib o pagkakamali sa pamamagitan ng masusing pag-iingat.
etymology: Nagmula sa "ka-ingat-an", ang kalagayan ng pagiging 'ingat' (maingat).
original_explanation: This is the noun form of "mag-ingat ka." It's the mindset you have when you're carrying a hot bowl of soup, walking on a slippery floor, or handling your friend's phone after they told you, "Ingatan mo 'yan, mahal 'yan." It's the opposite of being "burara" or careless. It's the extra level of care you take with things (or feelings) that are fragile.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga pormal na tagubilin o payo. Ang 'pag-iingat' ay mas karaniwang katumbas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakailangan ang ibayong **kaingatan** sa pagmamaneho ngayong umuulan.","translation":"Extra **carefulness** is needed when driving now that it's raining."},{"sentence":"Ang **kaingatan** ay susi upang maiwasan ang aksidente.","translation":"**Precaution** is key to avoiding accidents."}]

translation: to nickname; to brand; to call by an epithet
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isang partikular na pangalan, titulo, o taguri sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar, na kadalasan ay batay sa isang katangian.
original_explanation: This is how you get your barkada nickname. You `magbansag` someone as 'Tol,' 'Boss,' 'Bes,' or something more creative (and sometimes mean) like 'Siopao' because of their chubby cheeks. It's the Filipino art of labeling people, for better or for worse. Companies also do this to `magbansag` their products as 'The Best' or 'Number 1.'
usage_notes: Can have a neutral, positive, or negative connotation depending on the nickname or title being given.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ang **nagbansag** sa kanya bilang 'Reyna ng Kantahan' dahil sa galing niyang kumanta.","translation":"They were the ones who **nicknamed** her the 'Queen of Singing' because of her great singing ability."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magbansag** ng masamang pangalan sa iyong kapwa.","translation":"Do not **brand** your fellow person with a bad name."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng lubos na katapatan, pagtatalaga, at pagsisikap sa isang gawain, tao, o layunin.
original_explanation: This is that employee who stays online on Teams even after clocking out. The friend who will help you move apartments even during a storm. The partner who brings you food kahit LDR kayo. It's loyalty and commitment level: 9999.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang **dedikado**ng guro na laging inuuna ang kapakanan ng kanyang mga estudyante.","translation":"She is a **dedicated** teacher who always prioritizes the welfare of her students."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahaba at makitid na daanan sa loob ng isang gusali na nag-uugnay sa iba't ibang silid o bahagi nito.
etymology: From Spanish 'corredor' (corridor, runner). This is a less common spelling variant of 'koridor'.
original_explanation: Same as 'koridor.' It's that long hallway at school you run through when you're late for the next class, or the hospital passageway that's creepy to walk alone at night. It's the runway for office chismis, from the pantry to your cubicle. This is just a variant spelling.
usage_notes: 'Koridor' is the more standard and widely accepted spelling in modern Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghihintay siya sa dulo ng **koredor**.","translation":"He was waiting at the end of the **corridor**."},{"sentence":"Maingay ang mga estudyante sa **koredor** ng paaralan.","translation":"The students are noisy in the school's **hallway**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daanan, maaaring makitid o malapad, na tinatahak ng mga tao o hayop. Ginagamit din ito sa metaporikal na paraan upang tukuyin ang direksyon o kurso ng buhay.
original_explanation: Your Waze route is a 'landas'. The career path you're trying to figure out is also a 'landas'. It's the road you take, literally or figuratively. Sometimes it's a "daang matuwid" (straight path), other times it's full of potholes and wrong turns, just like EDSA on a payday Friday.
usage_notes: Very common in both literal (a path in a forest) and figurative (path in life) contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sundan mo lang ang **landas** na ito at makakarating ka sa talon.","translation":"Just follow this **path** and you will reach the falls."},{"sentence":"Bawat isa sa atin ay may kanya-kanyang **landas** na tinatahak sa buhay.","translation":"Each of us has our own **path** to take in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kaugnay sa iba sa pamamagitan ng dugo o kasal; kabilang sa iisang pamilya o angkan.
original_explanation: The people who ask "May boyfriend/girlfriend ka na?" or "Kailan ka gagraduate?" during family reunions. They're your built-in support system and your primary source of unsolicited life advice. Also, the reason you have to share the wifi password.
usage_notes: The unhyphenated 'kamaganak' is a common misspelling but generally understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming dumating na **kamag-anak** para sa Pasko.","translation":"Many **relatives** arrived for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Malayo man, itinuturing pa rin siyang malapit na **kamag-anak**.","translation":"Even if they're distant, he is still considered a close **relative**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagsasalin ng mga sinasabi mula sa isang wika patungo sa iba, karaniwan ay sa paraang pasalita.
original_explanation: Yan 'yung kaibigan mong taga-translate ng chismis from English to Tagalog and vice-versa. Sila 'yung human Google Translate sa grupo 'pag may foreigner na naligaw o 'pag nanonood kayo ng K-drama na walang subtitle.
usage_notes: Ginagamit din para sa mga taong nagbibigay-buhay sa isang karakter sa pag-arte.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng korte ng isang mahusay na **interprete** para sa dayuhang testigo.","translation":"The court needs a skilled **interpreter** for the foreign witness."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nagsilbing **interprete** namin noong kami ay naglakbay sa Japan.","translation":"He served as our **interpreter** when we traveled to Japan."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagluto ng pagkain sa mainit na mantika; isang kilos na nakumpleto na.
original_explanation: "Sino nagprito ng tuyo?!" - the question that hangs in the air, literally, for hours after the deed is done. It's the past tense of frying, an action whose delicious, oily evidence lingers long after the meal is over.
usage_notes: Simple past tense. Indicates a completed action of frying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagprito** ako ng itlog para sa almusal kanina.","translation":"I **fried** an egg for breakfast earlier."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **nagprito** ng manok kaya masarap at malutong.","translation":"He was the one who **fried** the chicken, that's why it's delicious and crispy."}]

translation: to become lazy; to feel lazy
meaning_filipino: Makaramdam o maging biktima ng katamaran; mawalan ng gana o sigla na kumilos o magtrabaho.
original_explanation: The official feeling of a Monday morning. Or a rainy Sunday afternoon. Or any time, really, when your bed and Netflix are calling your name louder than your responsibilities. It's the verb form of 'tamad'. "Huwag kang tatamad-tamad diyan!" is the battle cry of every Filipino mother to their child who has been 'natamad'.
usage_notes: Describes the action or state of becoming lazy, as opposed to the adjective 'tamad' which describes the quality of being lazy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag umuulan, madalas akong **matamad** bumangon sa kama.","translation":"When it's raining, I often **feel lazy** to get out of bed."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **matamad** mag-aral kung gusto mong pumasa.","translation":"Don't **become lazy** with your studies if you want to pass."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagbawas ng bilis o pag-usad.
original_explanation: What happens to your internet connection during peak hours. Or what traffic in EDSA does to your car, your schedule, and your soul. It's the act of slowing down, losing momentum, being laggy. 'Uy, ba't bumabagal ang usapan? Anyare?'
usage_notes: The opposite is 'bumibilis' (is speeding up).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumabagal** ang takbo ng sasakyan dahil sa matinding trapiko.","translation":"The car **is slowing down** because of the heavy traffic."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **bumabagal** ang pag-ikot ng mundo kapag kasama kita. #hugot","translation":"I feel like the world **is slowing down** when I'm with you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-angat o pagdadala ng isang bagay na may bigat.
original_explanation: This is what you do at the gym (or pretend to do for your New Year's resolution). It's also what the delivery guy does with your Shopee/Lazada package. But wait, there's more! 'Pagbubuhat ng bangko' is a classic Filipino idiom for praising yourself. So next time you see someone flexing, you know the term.
usage_notes: "Pagbubuhat ng sariling bangko" is a common idiom meaning "to praise oneself" or "to toot one's own horn."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan ang likod sa **pagbubuhat** ng mabibigat na sako ng bigas.","translation":"Be careful with your back when **lifting** heavy sacks of rice."},{"sentence":"Ayaw ng mga tao sa kasama nilang mahilig sa **pagbubuhat** ng sariling bangko.","translation":"People dislike a colleague who is fond of **praising** themself (lit. lifting their own chair)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadya o sapilitang pagkalaglag o pagkawala ng sanggol sa sinapupunan bago pa ito mabuhay sa labas.
original_explanation: "Agas" is a heavy word, referring to miscarriage. It's a deep, personal loss that is often unspoken. It's the kind of topic discussed in hushed tones or with great sensitivity. Not to be confused with the sound of flowing liquid, this "agas" carries a lot of emotional weight.
usage_notes: "Pagkalaglag" is a more common and slightly less direct term for miscarriage. The verb form is "maagasan" (to have a miscarriage).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **agas** ay isang masakit na karanasan para sa isang ina.","translation":"A **miscarriage** is a painful experience for a mother."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa aksidente, siya ay naagasan.","translation":"Because of the accident, she had a **miscarriage**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na orihinal o taal na naninirahan sa isang partikular na lugar; isang miyembro ng isang pangkat etnikong indigenous.
etymology: From ka- + tubo (to grow, to sprout).
original_explanation: This refers to the OG's of a place. The first people who lived on the land before colonizers or settlers arrived. The Aeta, Ifugao, Manobo, and many other groups are the katutubo of the Philippines, guardians of ancient culture and traditions.
usage_notes: Refers to indigenous peoples (IPs). A term of respect for the original inhabitants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating igalang ang karapatan ng mga **katutubo**.","translation":"We must respect the rights of the **indigenous people**."},{"sentence":"Maraming natutunan ang mga turista mula sa mga **katutubo** ng Palawan.","translation":"The tourists learned a lot from the **natives** of Palawan."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng isang bagay sa sariling bulsa; karaniwang may negatibong konotasyon ng pagnanakaw o paglustay ng pera na hindi sa iyo.
original_explanation: On the surface, it's just putting something in your pocket. But 99% of the time, it means you're taking something that isn't yours. It's the action of that corrupt politician who "pockets" public funds. It's a low-key way of saying "ninakaw." So if someone says "namulsa ng milyon," they didn't just find a million pesos and put it in their pocket.
usage_notes: Strongly implies theft or embezzlement, especially of money.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inakusahan ang tesorero na **mamulsa** ng pondo ng bayan.","translation":"The treasurer was accused of **pocketing** the town's funds."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masanay na **mamulsa** ng mga gamit na hindi sa iyo.","translation":"Don't get used to **pocketing** things that aren't yours."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manipis na pansit na gawa sa bigas.
original_explanation: The star of every birthday party pancit. Those thin, white noodles that magically absorb all the savory sauce and toppings. It's the "light" version compared to its thicker cousin, Canton, but let's be real, you're still getting a second plate. The official noodle of "long life."
usage_notes: A staple in Filipino cuisine, particularly for the dish "Pancit Bihon".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magluto ka ng pansit **bihon** para sa mga bisita.","translation":"Cook some **rice noodle** pancit for the guests."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong sahog sa **bihon** ang atay ng manok at chicharon.","translation":"My favorite ingredients in **rice vermicelli** are chicken liver and pork cracklings."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng pala upang maghukay, mag-alis, o maglipat ng lupa, buhangin, o iba pang katulad na materyales.
original_explanation: The original workout before gyms were a thing. It's the act of using a shovel ('pala'). Whether you're a construction worker moving sand, a gardener planting your tita-certified herbs, or a kid building a sandcastle at the beach, you're doing this. It's a surprisingly good way to get biceps.
usage_notes: The verb form directly relates to using the tool 'pala' (shovel).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magpala** ng buhangin para sa semento.","translation":"We need **to shovel** sand for the cement."},{"sentence":"**Nagpala** siya ng lupa sa hardin buong umaga.","translation":"He **shoveled** soil in the garden all morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkagulat, pagtataka, o hindi paniniwala.
etymology: Likely a shortened, informal evolution of expressions like "Ay, naku po!".
original_explanation: The official sound of Filipino "chismis" culture. It's the "OMG, really?!" or "Wait, what?" of Pinoy conversation. You use it when your friend tells you something shocking, like, "Luh, totoo ba 'yan?" It's the verbal equivalent of the wide-eyed emoji (😳).
usage_notes: Extremely common in informal, spoken Tagalog. Its meaning is heavily dependent on tone and context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Luh**, bakit ka umiiyak?","translation":"**Hey**, why are you crying? (expressing surprise/concern)"},{"sentence":"**Luh**, ang mahal naman niyan!","translation":"**Whoa**, that's so expensive! (expressing shock)"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng suporta, saklolo, o asistensya sa isang tao o gawain.
original_explanation: Ito yung "Bayanihan" spirit in action. Yung pag-abot mo ng bayad sa jeep, pag-share ng notes sa kaklase mong lutang, o pag-volunteer sa community pantry. It's the opposite of "bahala ka sa buhay mo." Basically, not being a selfish potato.
usage_notes: A fundamental verb in Filipino social interaction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumulong** si Ana sa kanyang nanay sa pagluluto ng hapunan.","translation":"Ana **helped** her mother cook dinner."},{"sentence":"Maraming kapitbahay ang **tumulong** sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"Many neighbors **helped** the typhoon victims."}]

translation: To use something as a layer/lining
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit sa isang bagay bilang sapin.
original_explanation: Similar to 'sapinan', but the focus is on the object *being used* as the layer. While 'sapinan' focuses on the surface you're covering ('Sapinan mo ang mesa'), 'sapinin' focuses on the material you're using ('Sapinin mo itong dyaryo sa mesa'). It's the difference between 'to cover the table' and 'to use this newspaper as a cover.'
usage_notes: The focus of the action is on the material being used as a layer. The object of the verb is the thing being used as the 'sapin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari mong **sapinin** ang mga dahon ng saging sa plato.","translation":"You can **use** the banana leaves **as a lining** for the plate."},{"sentence":"Itong lumang kumot na lang ang **sapinin** natin sa sahig para maupuan.","translation":"Let's just **use** this old blanket **as a mat** on the floor to sit on."}]

translation: to go with, to accompany, to join
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta kasama ng isa o higit pang tao; pagiging bahagi ng isang grupo o gawain.
original_explanation: The ultimate "sabit" move. When your friends are going out for milk tea and you say "Sama ako!", that's this. It's the FOMO verb. You're joining the party, the road trip, or even just the quick 7-Eleven run.
usage_notes: The prefix 'sum-' indicates an actor-focus verb in the past or completed tense. 'Sasama' is future tense, 'sumasama' is present. This meaning is related to companionship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumama** ako sa kanila papuntang Baguio noong isang linggo.","translation":"I **went with** them to Baguio last week."},{"sentence":"Gusto mo bang **sumama** sa aming team building?","translation":"Do you want to **join** our team building?"}]

translation: to coincide with, to happen to be on
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakataon na ang isang pangyayari ay naganap sa isang partikular na araw o kasabay ng isa pang kaganapan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (pandiwa ng kakayahan/di-sinasadya) + `taon` (year, ngunit dito ay tumutukoy sa tiyak na oras/pagkakataon).
original_explanation: 'Yung sweldo mo, **nataon** sa 11.11 sale. Or 'yung birthday mo, **nataon** sa isang long weekend. It's all about timing and coincidence. Parang 'yung bigla kayong nagkita ni ex sa mall, 'yun nga lang, may kasama siyang iba. Awkward timing.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga anyong banghay tulad ng "nataon" (pangnagdaan), "natataon" (pangkasalukuyan), at "matataon" (panghinaharap).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nataon** na Biyernes Santo ang kanyang kaarawan kaya't simple lang ang naging selebrasyon.","translation":"Her birthday **happened to be on** Good Friday, so the celebration was simple."},{"sentence":"Sana **mataon** sa Sabado ang susunod na holiday para makapagpahinga tayo.","translation":"I hope the next holiday **coincides with** a Saturday so we can rest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang de-makina na ginagamit sa agrikultura upang ihiwalay ang mga butil ng palay o ibang aning butil mula sa tangkay at ipa nito.
original_explanation: This is a high-tech machine that does the job of separating rice grains from the stalks, a process called 'giik'. Imagine a giant, noisy metal carabao that eats harvested rice stalks and spits out the precious grains. It's the farmer's best friend during harvest season.
usage_notes: A compound noun. `Panggiik` specifies the function of the `makina`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naitulong ng **makinang panggiik** sa pagpapabilis ng aming pag-aani.","translation":"The **threshing machine** was a great help in speeding up our harvest."},{"sentence":"Inimbento ang **makinang panggiik** upang mapadali ang proseso ng agrikultura.","translation":"The **threshing machine** was invented to make the agricultural process easier."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na ranggong opisyal sa hukbong-dagat ng isang bansa.
etymology: Mula sa Malay na 'laksamana', na hango sa Sanskrit na 'Lakshmana', isang bayani sa epikong Ramayana na kilala sa kanyang katapatan at husay sa pakikidigma.
original_explanation: The big boss of the navy. The final boss of the battleship. If the navy were a BPO, the **laksamana** is the country manager. They've got the most stripes on their shoulder and the biggest hat. The term itself sounds as powerful as the rank.
usage_notes: A formal, official title. Not used in everyday conversation unless one is specifically discussing naval ranks, history, or related topics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Laksamana** ang namuno sa parada ng mga barkong pandigma.","translation":"The **Admiral** led the parade of warships."},{"sentence":"Si **Laksamana** Hang Tuah ay isang maalamat na mandirigma sa kasaysayan ng Malay.","translation":"**Admiral** Hang Tuah is a legendary warrior in Malay history."}]

translation: to form waves; to become wavy
meaning_filipino: Pagkakaroon o paglikha ng mga alon sa ibabaw ng tubig; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagkakaroon ng kulot o hugis-alon sa buhok.
original_explanation: This is what the sea does when it's showing off. Also, what your hair does after a beach trip when you forget your conditioner. Figuratively, it's your emotions going up and down during a K-drama marathon.
usage_notes: Primarily for water, but can be used for hair or other surfaces that form a wave-like pattern.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **umalon** nang malakas ang dagat kaya ipinagbawal ang paglangoy.","translation":"The sea started **to form large waves**, so swimming was prohibited."},{"sentence":"Ang buhok niya ay natural na **umaalon** kapag nababasa.","translation":"Her hair naturally **becomes wavy** when it gets wet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging kasangkot, pagkakasama, o pagkakaugnay sa isang usapin, karaniwan ay sa isang krimen o hindi magandang pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is when your name gets dragged into the chismis or a problem, even if you're just an innocent bystander. Bigla ka na lang 'tagged' sa issue without your consent. 'Bakit may **dawit** ang pangalan ko diyan? Wala akong kinalaman!'
usage_notes: Commonly used in legal, criminal, or gossip contexts. The verb form 'idawit' means 'to implicate someone'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **dawit** ang pangalan niya sa malaking iskandalo sa gobyerno.","translation":"His name has an **implication** in the big government scandal."},{"sentence":"Pilit siyang idinadawit sa kasong hindi niya ginawa.","translation":"They are trying to implicate him in a case he did not commit."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na paghirang o pagtatalaga ng isang tao sa isang posisyon, tungkulin, o karangalan.
original_explanation: This is the very formal, very tito-level way of saying "to appoint." Parang sa miting de avance, "At ang ating susunod na nominado..." 'Yung ginagawa ng presidente para sa cabinet niya, or 'yung ginagawa ng barkada mo para piliin kung sino'ng bibili ng yelo.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na salita na karaniwang ginagamit sa politika, pamahalaan, at mga pormal na organisasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang komite ay **magnonombra** ng bagong tagapangulo sa susunod na linggo.","translation":"The committee will **nominate** a new chairperson next week."}]

translation: to dissolve; to abolish; to dismantle
meaning_filipino: Lansagin, wasakin, o pawalang-bisa ang isang organisasyon, istruktura, o kasunduan.
original_explanation: The action verb version of 'buwag'. Ito yung 'it's not you, it's me' but for organizations. When the management decides to **buwagin** a department, it's corporate speak for 'good luck sa job hunting'. It's also what you want to do to a toxic 'barkadahan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang kongreso na **buwagin** ang ahensyang sangkot sa katiwalian.","translation":"The congress decided to **abolish** the agency involved in corruption."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating hayaang **buwagin** ng isang maliit na pag-aaway ang ating pagkakaibigan.","translation":"Let's not allow a small fight to **dismantle** our friendship."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kasangkapan na ginagamit sa paggawa ng butas, karaniwan sa kahoy, sa pamamagitan ng pag-ikot nito.
etymology: From maliit (small) + na (linker) + barena (from Spanish 'barrena' meaning auger/drill).
original_explanation: That tiny tool your dad or lolo uses for small DIY projects. It's the pre-power tools version of a drill bit. Not as powerful as a Black & Decker, but perfect for when you need to make a small, precise hole without waking up the whole neighborhood. It's the "tito" of tools.
usage_notes: A specific term for a hand tool. "Barena" alone refers to a drill or auger in general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **maliit na barena** para butasan ang kawayan.","translation":"He used a **gimlet** to make a hole in the bamboo."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang paggamit ng **maliit na barena** para hindi ka masugatan.","translation":"Be careful using the **small auger** so you don't get hurt."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may kaparehong pangalan sa iba.
original_explanation: Your office ka-teammate who has the same name, causing constant email mix-ups. 'Uy, may email ka from HR.' 'Ay, hindi, para sa'yo 'yan, John Smith 1, ako si John Smith 2.'
usage_notes: The more common, informal term is 'tokayo'. 'Kapangalan' is slightly more formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Jose Rizal ay **kapangalan** ng ating pambansang bayani.","translation":"Jose Rizal is the **namesake** of our national hero."},{"sentence":"Nalilito ako dahil may dalawa akong estudyanteng **kapangalan** sa klase.","translation":"I get confused because I have two students who are **namesakes** in my class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lupi o tupi sa isang bagay tulad ng papel o damit; ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakatupi.
original_explanation: 'Tiklop' is when you fold something neatly, like your freshly laundered t-shirt. But in hugot culture, it's what happens to your pride when your crush leaves you on 'seen'. Biglang-tiklop, from alpha to beta in 0.5 seconds. It's the physical and emotional state of being folded up and put away.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (the fold itself, 'ang tiklop') or an adjective ('nakatiklop' meaning folded).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang **tiklop** ng mga damit sa aparador.","translation":"Fix the **fold** of the clothes in the cabinet."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang marka ng **tiklop** sa papel matapos niyang plantsahin.","translation":"The mark of the **fold** on the paper disappeared after he ironed it."}]

translation: to be able to knock down; to cause to fall
meaning_filipino: Magawang maibuwal o maibagsak ang isang bagay o tao na nakatayo.
original_explanation: That feeling of power when you finally beat the final boss in a video game. Or, more literally, what happens to a Jenga tower when someone breathes too hard. It’s the ability to bring something—or someone—down. "Isang suntok lang, kaya ko 'yang mapatumba!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang malakas na suntok, nagawa niyang **mapatumba** ang kalaban.","translation":"With one strong punch, he was able to **knock down** his opponent."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng malakas na hangin para **mapatumba** ang punong iyon.","translation":"You need a strong wind to be able to **knock down** that tree."}]

translation: to wander; to roam; to go out for leisure
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis sa isang lugar upang maglibot, mamasyal, o magliwaliw nang walang tiyak na destinasyon o layunin.
original_explanation: The national pastime of the Filipino people. 'Tara, gala tayo!' is our version of 'carpe diem'. It can mean anything from a 5-minute walk to the sari-sari store, a day trip to the mall (a.k.a. the Philippines' public park), or a spontaneous beach trip. To 'maggala' is to seek adventure, or at least a break from boredom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **maggala** sa gabi kapag hindi siya makatulog.","translation":"He likes **to wander** at night when he can't sleep."},{"sentence":"Yayain mo ang barkada mong **maggala** sa Sabado.","translation":"Ask your friends **to go out** on Saturday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang banayad at malumanay na ihip ng hangin na nagdudulot ng kaginhawaan.
etymology: Mula sa `mayumi` (gentle, modest), pang-angkop na `-ng`, at `hangin` (wind).
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na nasa tabing-dagat ka at sunset, tapos may dumaan na hangin na hindi malakas pero sapat lang para gumaan ang pakiramdam mo? 'Yan ang mayuming hangin. It’s the opposite of the stressful, malakas na hangin from a typhoon. It's the kind of breeze that makes you feel like everything’s gonna be okay.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pampanitikan o patulang parirala. Ang salitang 'mayumi' ay nangangahulugang mahinhin o banayad, at karaniwang ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang babae.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kay sarap damhin ng **mayuming hangin** sa ilalim ng puno.","translation":"It feels so good to feel the **gentle breeze** under the tree."},{"sentence":"Isang **mayuming hangin** ang humaplos sa kanyang pisngi.","translation":"A **gentle breeze** caressed her cheek."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkabulok o pagkamatay ng isang bahagi ng katawan dahil sa kakulangan ng daloy ng dugo o matinding impeksyon.
original_explanation: Ito yung nangyayari 'pag na-infect nang malala ang sugat at hindi naagapan. Parang relationship na napabayaan, namamatay at nangingitim na. Seryosong medical term ito, hindi 'yung 'kanggrena' sa wallet bago mag-sweldo.
usage_notes: Isang terminong medikal na ginagamit upang ilarawan ang nekrosis o pagkamatay ng tissue.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangang putulin ang paa ng pasyente dahil sa **kanggrena**.","translation":"The patient's foot had to be amputated because of **gangrene**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malalim at matahimik na pag-iisip o pagninilay-nilay tungkol sa isang bagay; pagbubulay-bulay.
original_explanation: This is your 'staring at the ceiling at 3 AM' moment. It's when you're deep in thought, maybe over a cup of coffee, figuring out your life choices, your career path, or why you're still single. It's the official term for 'overthinking with purpose'.
usage_notes: Often used with verbs like 'mag-nilay-nilay' (to contemplate). The reduplication adds a sense of duration or intensity to the act of thinking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng panahon para sa kaunting **nilay-nilay** tungkol sa aking kinabukasan.","translation":"I need some time for a little **contemplation** about my future."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng mahabang araw, masarap mag-isa at mag-**nilay-nilay**.","translation":"After a long day, it's nice to be alone and engage in **deep thought**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kahilingan o pahayag na tumutukoy sa pagdaragdag ng isa pa sa bilang o dami; ginagamit din upang ipakilala ang isa pang punto o dahilan.
original_explanation: The official chant for getting more of a good thing. 'Isa pa!' for another round of drinks. 'Isa pa!' for another song at karaoke. It's also the phrase your friend uses to add another piece of gossip: 'Tapos, may chika pa 'ko... **isa pa**, 'yung ex niya...' The ultimate enabler phrase.
usage_notes: Extremely common in daily conversation for requests ('one more') or adding information ('another thing is...').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng kanin! Bigyan mo pa ako ng **isa pa**.","translation":"The rice is delicious! Give me **one more** serving."},{"sentence":"Ayaw ko na sa kanya. Magulo siyang kausap. At **isa pa**, hindi siya marunong mag-reply.","translation":"I don't like him anymore. He's confusing to talk to. And **another thing**, he doesn't know how to reply."}]

translation: to be pinned under; to be run over
meaning_filipino: Mailagay sa ilalim ng isang mabigat na bagay at hindi makagalaw; masagasaan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you have five deadlines, two family problems, and a broken heart all at once. 'Yan 'yung #SanaAll workload, pero sa'yo lang. You're literally and figuratively 'madaganan' by life.
usage_notes: Can refer to being physically pinned or metaphorically overwhelmed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat ka sa pagtawid, baka ka **madaganan** ng sasakyan.","translation":"Be careful crossing, you might get **run over** by a car."},{"sentence":"Para akong **nadadaganan** ng mga problema sa trabaho.","translation":"I feel like I'm being **pinned under** by problems at work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang partikular na araw sa isang buwan o taon, na karaniwang isinusulat bilang numero.
etymology: Hiram sa Malay na 'tanggal' na nangangahulugang petsa.
original_explanation: Not to be confused with being fired! This is the 'What's the date today?' kind of 'tanggal'. It's the number on your calendar you circle for payday, your birthday, or that long-awaited vacation. It's the reason you ask, "Anong **tanggal** na ngayon?" after a long weekend, completely lost in time.
usage_notes: Ang diin ay nasa unang pantig /TANG-gal/ para sa kahulugang ito, iba sa pang-uri na /tang-GAL/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **tanggal** ng iyong kaarawan?","translation":"What is the **date** of your birthday?"},{"sentence":"Sa **tanggal** a-kinse ang aming sahod.","translation":"Our salary comes on the 15th **day of the month**."}]

translation: to be annoyed; to be exasperated
meaning_filipino: Makaramdam ng pagkainis, pagkayamot, o pagkasuya dahil sa isang nakababagot o hindi kanais-nais na sitwasyon o tao.
original_explanation: The official feeling of Metro Manila traffic at 5 PM on a payday Friday. It's when your internet dies in the middle of a Netflix cliffhanger. It's the 'low batt' warning when you have no charger. Basically, the adult version of a tantrum, but internal and with more sighs.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a state of irritation or boredom leading to annoyance. It's a stronger feeling than simply being 'inip' (bored).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong kausapin ngayon, **nabubugnot** ako.","translation":"Don't talk to me right now, I'm **feeling annoyed**."},{"sentence":"Madaling **mabugnot** si Ana kapag naghihintay nang matagal.","translation":"Ana gets **annoyed** easily when she waits for a long time."}]

translation: to make a hole in; to perforate; to puncture
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa o paglikha ng butas sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagtusok, pagpukpok, o iba pang paraan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'butas' at hulaping pandiwa na '-in'.
original_explanation: The command form of making a 'butas' (hole). It's what you do to your new leather belt after Christmas dinner, or what a 'chismosa' neighbor tries to do to your life story para may bagong topic. It's the act of piercing something, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: This is a transitive verb, requiring a direct object that receives the action of being pierced.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **butasin** ang pader para sa bagong kable ng internet.","translation":"We need **to make a hole** in the wall for the new internet cable."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka mo **butasin** ang gulong ng bisikleta.","translation":"Be careful or you might **puncture** the bicycle tire."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsusugal o pagtaya ng pera o mahalagang bagay sa isang laro na may hindi tiyak na resulta.
original_explanation: This is anything from playing 'tong-its' with your titos with actual money on the line, to betting on a cockfight, to losing your 13th-month pay in a casino. If there's money and a game of chance, it's paghuhuwego. From Spanish 'juego' (game).
usage_notes: While the root 'huwego' can mean 'game' in other contexts (e.g., huwego de silya), 'paghuhuwego' almost exclusively carries the connotation of gambling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghuhuwego** ang naging sanhi ng pagbagsak ng kanyang pamilya.","translation":"**Gambling** was the cause of his family's downfall."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal sa lugar na ito ang anumang uri ng **paghuhuwego**.","translation":"Any form of **gambling** is prohibited in this area."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang istrukturang itinayo sa tabi ng anyong tubig, tulad ng ilog o dagat, na nagsisilbing daungan o babaan ng mga bangka at maliliit na sasakyang-dagat.
etymology: Likely a regional Philippine language term that has entered Tagalog.
original_explanation: Think of it as the local, often wooden, version of a pier. It's where the fishermen park their bancas, where kids jump into the water, and where you wait for the ferry to the next island. It’s the province’s version of a bus stop, but for boats.
usage_notes: More common in coastal provinces than in major cities. 'Pantalan' is a more general and common term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghihintay ang mga mangingisda sa **bantilan** para sa pagdaong ng kanilang mga kasama.","translation":"The fishermen are waiting at the **wharf** for their companions to dock."},{"sentence":"Mula sa **bantilan**, tanaw na tanaw ang paglubog ng araw.","translation":"From the **pier**, the sunset is clearly visible."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing kilos ng paggalaw sa tubig sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng mga kamay at paa. Ito ay nasa panahunang panghinaharap.
etymology: Future tense of `maglangoy`. Formed from `mag-` + `la` (repeated first syllable of root) + `langoy` (swim).
original_explanation: The future tense of `maglangoy` (to swim). This is your plan for the weekend beach trip. "**Maglalangoy** kami sa dagat buong araw!" (We will swim in the sea all day!). It's the promise of escaping the city heat and just floating your problems away, or maybe trying to beat your friends in a race to the shore.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb `maglangoy` (to swim).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagdating natin sa resort, **maglalangoy** agad ako sa pool.","translation":"When we arrive at the resort, I **will swim** in the pool right away."},{"sentence":"Sino-sino ang **maglalangoy** sa ilog mamaya?","translation":"Who **will swim** in the river later?"}]

translation: to refuse, to decline, to quit
meaning_filipino: Tumanggi sa isang alok, paanyaya, o gawain; hindi sumang-ayon o pumayag.
original_explanation: When you see the job description requires 5 years of experience for an entry-level salary, and you just close the tab. You 'umayaw'. It's the act of saying "nope," "pass," or "I'm out." It's refusing or quitting something you were previously considering or doing.
usage_notes: A very direct way of expressing refusal or the act of quitting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa huling sandali, **umayaw** ang investor sa aming proyekto.","translation":"At the last minute, the investor **backed out of** our project."},{"sentence":"Pagod na siya kaya **umayaw** na siyang sumama sa party.","translation":"He was tired, so he **declined** to join the party."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghahanap at pagbanggit ng mga mali, kapintasan, o depekto sa isang tao o bagay, kadalasan sa paraang mapanira.
etymology: From "pintas" (flaw, criticism). The "pan-" prefix becomes "pam-" and the first syllable is reduplicated.
original_explanation: This is the national sport of some 'Marites' out there. It's when someone looks at your perfect selfie and the first thing they say is, "May dumi sa likod mo." It's the act of focusing on the one tiny flaw instead of the 99% that's good. The art of being a hater.
usage_notes: Usually implies negative, often petty, and unsolicited criticism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang katapusan ang **pamimintas** niya sa lahat ng ginagawa ko.","translation":"His **fault-finding** of everything I do is endless."},{"sentence":"Sa halip na **pamimintas**, magbigay ka na lang ng mungkahi kung paano ito mapapabuti.","translation":"Instead of **criticism**, just give a suggestion on how it can be improved."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gantimpala na nasa anyong pera na ipinagkakaloob sa isang nanalo o nakagawa ng pambihirang bagay.
original_explanation: The best kind of gantimpala for the 'praktikal' Pinoy. Forget the trophy, just give me the cash! This is the prize money in a game show, the reward for finding a lost dog, or the bonus that finally lets you check out your Shopee cart.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a reward in the form of money.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroong **gantimpalang-salapi** na nagkakahalaga ng isang milyong piso para sa makakahuli sa kriminal.","translation":"There is a **monetary reward** worth one million pesos for whoever can catch the criminal."}]

translation: to like (romantically); to have as one's type
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pagtingin o paghanga sa isang tao; ang pagiging kaakit-akit ng isang tao ayon sa pansariling pamantayan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "crush" word. Pag sinabing "tipo kita," it means "You're my type." Hindi ito tax form (BIR Form 1701), ito yung feeling na napapatingin ka sa kanya habang naglalakad sa hallway. It's the spark, the "sana all," the reason you check their profile.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit sa anyong pandiwa na "tinipo" o sa pariralang "[panghalip] ang tipo ko".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal ko nang **tipo** ang kapitbahay naming tahimik.","translation":"I've **liked** our quiet neighbor for a long time."},{"sentence":"Siya talaga ang **tipo** ng lalaking gusto kong mapangasawa.","translation":"He's really the **type** of man I want to marry."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang kalagayan kung saan ang balat o isang ibabaw ay napupuno ng maraming maliliit na umbok o butlig.
original_explanation: This is what your skin looks like after losing a fight with an army of red ants (hantik). Not just one `butlig`, but a whole bumpy, itchy landscape. `Butlig-butlig` is the plural form of your skin's suffering. Can also describe a bumpy texture, like a poorly finished wall.
usage_notes: The reduplication indicates plurality or a surface being covered with the feature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **butlig-butlig** ang kanyang likod dahil sa allergy sa pagkain.","translation":"Her back became **covered in small welts** due to a food allergy."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mababang posisyon, taas, halaga, o kalidad.
original_explanation: The opposite of taas (high/up). It's for low prices ("**baba** ng presyo!"), low scores ("**baba** ng grades ko, huhu"), or literally just "down" or "downstairs" ("Nasa **baba** siya."). It's the direction your motivation goes on a Monday morning.
usage_notes: Pronounced with stress on the second syllable: ba-BÀ. The meaning changes completely based on stress compared to its homograph 'bába' (chin). Often seen in its form 'mababa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **baba** naman ng sahod dito.","translation":"The salary here is so **low**."},{"sentence":"Pumunta ka sa **baba** para kunin ang delivery.","translation":"Go **downstairs** to get the delivery."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng buong tiwala, responsibilidad, o kapangyarihang magpasya sa iba; pagpapaubaya.
etymology: From the prefix "pa-" and the root "ubaya", an old Tagalog word meaning consent, leaving to another's discretion, or tolerance.
original_explanation: 'Bahala ka na,' but in a more formal, almost poetic way. It's letting go and letting someone else (or God, 'Bahala na si Lord') take the wheel. It's what you do when you've done everything for a group project and your groupmates are still not cooperating—you just leave it to fate. 'Ipinapaubaya ko na sa'yo ang lahat' is peak Filipino drama hugot.
usage_notes: Often used in verb forms like 'ipagpaubaya' or 'ipaubaya' (to entrust something to someone). As a noun, it signifies the concept of relinquishment itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang huling habilin ay isang **paubaya** ng lahat ng kanyang ari-arian sa kanyang anak.","translation":"His last will was an **act of entrusting** all his properties to his child."},{"sentence":"Ipinapaubaya ko na sa Diyos ang aking kinabukasan.","translation":"I am entrusting my future to God."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtugtog ng instrumentong gitara.
original_explanation: What your 'haranista' friend does to serenade their crush, or what you do in your room pretending you're a rockstar. It's the sound of 'ligaw' culture, indie gigs, and that one officemate who always brings a guitar to the company outing.
usage_notes: A verb formed by adding the infix '-um-' to the noun 'gitara'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay **gumitara** si Juan habang kumakanta si Maria.","translation":"Juan is good at **playing the guitar** while Maria sings."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **gumitara** sa kantang iyon?","translation":"Who **played the guitar** in that song?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon, pormal man o hindi, kung saan ang pangunahing aktibidad ay ang pagpapalitan ng mga usap-usapan o kuwento.
etymology: Combination of Tagalog 'chismisan' (place/act of gossiping) and English 'session'.
original_explanation: This is the meeting where the minutes are juicy and the agenda is everyone else's business. It can happen anywhere: over coffee, in a Viber group, or across the fence with your kapitbahay. A successful chismisan session leaves everyone feeling updated, slightly guilty, but mostly entertained.
usage_notes: A very common Taglish phrase. 'Chismisan' by itself can also mean the same thing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **chismisan session** na naman ang mga tita ko sa sala.","translation":"My aunts are having a **gossip session** again in the living room."},{"sentence":"Hindi kumpleto ang get-together kung walang **chismisan session**.","translation":"A get-together isn't complete without a **gossip session**."}]

translation: a false or unreliable friend; a fair-weather friend
meaning_filipino: Isang taong itinuturing na kaibigan o kumpare ngunit hindi mapagkakatiwalaan, nagkukunwari lamang, o lumalapit lamang kapag may kailangan.
etymology: A compound word from 'kumpare' (friend) and 'hilaw' (unripe, raw).
original_explanation: The 'friend' who's only your 'pare' when you have money or connections. Pag may libreng pakain, present. Pag may problema ka, seenzone. This is the guy who'll borrow money and then suddenly doesn't know you. Basically, a user-friendly friend, and you're the one being used. The 'hilaw' (unripe) part means their friendship isn't fully cooked or genuine.
usage_notes: A compound word highlighting insincere friendship. Often used to describe someone who is opportunistic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lumabas ang tunay na kulay niya, isa pala siyang **kumparing-hilaw**.","translation":"His true colors showed, he turned out to be a **fair-weather friend**."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa mga **kumparing-hilaw** na puro porma lang.","translation":"Be careful of those **unreliable friends** who are all for show."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa gawain ng matinding paghahalikan at pagyayakapan na walang kasamang pagtatalik.
etymology: Mula sa acronym na Ingles na "Make-Out Make-Out Lang".
original_explanation: Acronym for "Make-Out Make-Out Lang." It's the PG-13 version of a hookup. Just kissing, maybe some heavy petting, but that's it. It's the "walang commitment" stage of physical intimacy, perfect for when you're just testing the waters or, you know, just bored.
usage_notes: Isang napakapopular na salitang balbal. Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan (e.g., "Nagka-momol sila") o pandiwa (e.g., "Nag-momol sila").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huy, totoo ba na may nahuling nag-**momol** sa sinehan?","translation":"Hey, is it true they caught someone **making out** in the cinema?"},{"sentence":"Ang usapan lang ay **momol**, bakit naging seryoso?","translation":"The agreement was just **to make out**, why did it get serious?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malambot at sariwang keso na yari sa gatas ng kalabaw, baka, o kambing. Karaniwan itong bahagyang maalat at popular sa mga lalawigan tulad ng Laguna.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino cheese. It's that soft, slightly salty white cheese usually made from carabao's milk, wrapped in banana leaves. Perfect partner for hot pandesal. It's the artisanal, farm-to-table cheese before 'artisanal' was even a thing. Think of it as the mozzarella of the Philippines, but with more character and probinsya vibes.
usage_notes: Often eaten for breakfast with pandesal or used as an ingredient in various Filipino dishes. It is a specialty of provinces like Laguna, Bulacan, and Cavite.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang almusal kapag may mainit na pandesal at **kesongputi**.","translation":"Breakfast is delicious when there's hot pandesal and **white cheese**."},{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng sariwang **kesongputi** mula sa Laguna.","translation":"We bought fresh **white cheese** from Laguna."}]

translation: to go; to go to (a place)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos o paglipat patungo sa isang tiyak na lugar o destinasyon.
etymology: From Spanish 'punta' (point, tip), but the meaning shifted to 'destination' or 'direction' in Filipino.
original_explanation: The most basic Filipino travel verb. Before there was Waze, your tita would just say, "Magpunta ka sa may kanto, tapos tanong ka ulit." It's the command your boss gives you for an "urgent" meeting that could've been an email.
usage_notes: Often followed by 'sa' to indicate the destination.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magpunta** tayo sa palengke para mamili ng ulam.","translation":"Let's **go** to the market to buy ingredients for our dish."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **nagpunta** kagabi at hindi ka namin makontak?","translation":"Where did you **go** last night that we couldn't contact you?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pautos na pangungusap na nagbabawal sa isang tao na magsalita.
original_explanation: The classic "quiet please" with a Filipino flavor. It's what the teacher says when the class is rowdy, what your friend whispers when the chismis is about someone right behind you, or what you tell yourself when you're about to say something you'll regret. "Bes, huwag magsalita... andito si boss."
usage_notes: A direct command to stop talking. Composed of 'huwag' (don't) and 'magsalita' (to speak).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Huwag magsalita** habang kumakain.","translation":"**Don't speak** while eating."},{"sentence":"Ang sabi ng karatula: '**Huwag magsalita** nang malakas.'","translation":"The sign said: '**Do not speak** loudly.'"}]

translation: act of leaving something behind; setting aside (food)
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-iwan ng labis o bahagi ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain, para sa iba.
original_explanation: This is a core Filipino love language. It's when your mom saves you a piece of 'lechon' from the party. 'Salamat sa **pagtira** mo sa akin ng ulam, akala ko naubos na lahat.' It's the opposite of being a 'patay-gutom'.
usage_notes: The stress is on the first syllable of the root: TI-ra. Almost always refers to food.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtira** ng pagkain para sa mga hindi pa kumakain ay tanda ng paggalang.","translation":"The **act of setting aside** food for those who haven't eaten is a sign of respect."},{"sentence":"Nagagalit si Nanay kapag walang **pagtira** ng kanin na nagaganap.","translation":"Mom gets angry when no **leaving behind** of rice happens."}]

meaning_filipino: Higit sa karaniwan o kinakailangan; sukdulan sa pagiging labis o sobra.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `napaka-` (nagpapahiwatig ng sukdulang antas) at salitang ugat na `labis` (excess).
original_explanation: This is that one tita at the buffet who stacks her plate like the Leaning Tower of Pisa. Or when your "one more episode" on Netflix turns into finishing the whole season at 4 AM. It's anything that screams "OA" (over-acting) or "too much".
usage_notes: Often carries a slightly negative connotation, implying something is beyond a reasonable or acceptable limit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napakalabis** naman ang singil ninyo para sa isang tasang kape!","translation":"Your charge for one cup of coffee is **very excessive**!"},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pagmamahal ay tila **napakalabis** at nakakasakal na.","translation":"Her love seemed **very excessive** and already suffocating."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nabawasan; buo pa rin at walang anumang kinuha o nawala.
original_explanation: When you get your 13th-month pay and for a glorious 5 seconds, it's "walang bawas." Before bills, before Shopee checkouts, before the "pahiram muna" from your siblings. It's that perfect, whole amount. Also what you hope your french fries are when your friend says "Penge isa lang."
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa kantidad, kalidad, o tindi ng isang bagay na hindi nagbago o nabawasan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinalik niya ang perang hiniram nang **walang-bawas**.","translation":"He returned the borrowed money **intact**."},{"sentence":"Kahit lumipas ang maraming taon, ang pagmamahal niya para sa bayan ay **walang-bawas**.","translation":"Even after many years, his love for the country is **undiminished**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw o pag-indayog sa hangin, tulad ng isang bandila, dahon, o kamay. (Naganap na)
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na "wagayway" na may gitlaping "-um-".
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa ng bandila ng Pilipinas tuwing Lunes sa flag ceremony. Or 'yung eksena sa beauty pageant, 'yung confident na kaway ng nanalo habang umiiyak. "Mars, tingnan mo, wumagayway ang buhok ko pag-ikot ko, parang commercial ng shampoo!"
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit para sa mga bagay na iwinawagayway ng hangin, tulad ng bandila o buhok. Maaari ding gamitin para sa pag-kaway ng kamay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Buong pagmamalaking **wumagayway** ang bandila ng Pilipinas matapos ang laban.","translation":"The Philippine flag proudly **waved** after the fight."},{"sentence":"Nang makita niya ako sa malayo, **wumagayway** ang kanyang kamay bilang pagbati.","translation":"When she saw me from afar, her hand **waved** as a greeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang ilong na patag, hindi gaanong matangos, at maikli ang tulay nito.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'matangos' (sharp-nosed). It's a common, neutral-to-teasing descriptor for many Filipino noses. No shade, it's just a fact of life for many of us. If you can't easily hang sunglasses on the bridge of your nose, baka medyo **pango** ka. It's a term of endearment... sometimes.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin sa neutral na paraan, ngunit maaari ding maging isang anyo ng panunukso. Ang konteksto ang susi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong tuksuhin, alam kong **pango** ang ilong ko!","translation":"Don't tease me, I know my nose is **flat**!"},{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipino ang may **pango**ng ilong, at iyon ay bahagi ng ating katangian.","translation":"Many Filipinos have **flat noses**, and that is part of our features."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang asawa ng ama ng isang tao na hindi niya tunay na ina.
original_explanation: The villain in 99% of fairy tales and Pinoy teleseryes. But in real life, she's just your dad's new wife. The word itself carries so much dramatic baggage, thanks to pop culture. 'Hindi ako ang kontrabida sa buhay mo, I'm just your madrasta!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabait ang aking **madrasta** at tinuturing niya akong parang tunay na anak.","translation":"My **stepmother** is kind and treats me like her own child."},{"sentence":"Sa mga pelikula, madalas ay masama ang ugali ng **madrasta**.","translation":"In movies, the **stepmother** often has a bad character."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng paglalakad kung saan ang mga braso ay magkakawing o magkasama.
etymology: From `ka-` + `biki` (a root word denoting the action of linking arms).
