usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng heneral ang espiya na **magmanman** sa kilos ng mga kalaban.","translation":"The general ordered the spy to **spy on** the enemy's movements."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang praning, walang **nagmanman** sa'yo.","translation":"Don't be paranoid, no one is **spying on** you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang musikero na tumutugtog ng biyulin. Ito ay isang alternatibong baybay para sa 'biyolinista'.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "violinista", na may bahagyang pagbabago sa baybay sa Tagalog.
original_explanation: Same as 'biyolinista', just with a 'u'. It's like 'theatre' vs 'theater'—you know what it means, but one feels a bit more old-school. Still the same talented person making beautiful music with a violin.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang hindi gaanong karaniwang variant ng 'biyolinista'. Parehong tama at naiintindihan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aral siya sa ibang bansa upang maging isang mahusay na **biyulinista**.","translation":"He studied abroad to become a great **violinist**."},{"sentence":"Ang solo ng **biyulinista** ang pinakapaborito kong bahagi ng pagtatanghal.","translation":"The **violinist's** solo is my favorite part of the performance."}]

translation: to classify, to sort, to categorize
meaning_filipino: Pagbukud-bukurin o pagpangkat-pangkatin ang mga bagay o konsepto ayon sa kanilang uri, katangian, o kalidad.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa laundry—puti, de-kolor, at itim. O 'yung ginagawa ng HR sa mga aplikante: for interview, for keeps, for 'we'll call you.' Ang uriin ay ang sining ng paglalagay ng label sa lahat ng bagay para mas madaling intindihin (o i-judge).
usage_notes: Common in academic, scientific, and organizational contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **uriin** ang mga basura bago itapon.","translation":"The trash needs **to be sorted** before being thrown away."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **uriin** ang tunay na kaibigan sa mga pekeng kaibigan.","translation":"It's difficult **to classify** true friends from fake friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sangay ng agham na tumatalakay sa tunog at mga alon ng tunog; ang mga katangian ng isang silid o gusali na tumutukoy kung paano naipaparating ang tunog.
original_explanation: Ito yung science kung bakit ang ganda ng boses mo pag kumakanta sa banyo pero parang ipis na naipit pag sa sala na. Ito rin yung dahilan kung bakit ang ganda pakinggan ng live band sa Music Museum—dahil maganda ang akustika ng lugar.
usage_notes: Isang terminong pang-agham o teknikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga inhinyero ang **akustika** ng bagong concert hall.","translation":"The engineers are studying the **acoustics** of the new concert hall."},{"sentence":"Maganda ang **akustika** sa loob ng simbahan kaya't malinaw ang bawat salita ng pari.","translation":"The **acoustics** inside the church are good, that's why every word of the priest is clear."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, gawain, o pagkain na angkop o nauugnay sa panahon ng Kuwaresma.
original_explanation: This is the official tag for anything related to Holy Week. 'Pangkuwarisma' food means no meat (usually fish or veggies). 'Pangkuwarisma' movies are those epic biblical dramas shown on TV. It's the vibe of reflection, sacrifice, and patiently waiting for Easter Sunday so you can eat lechon again.
usage_notes: Used specifically in the context of the Catholic observance of Lent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda si nanay ng mga pagkaing **pangkuwarisma** tulad ng ginataang tulingan.","translation":"Mom prepared **Lenten** dishes like tuna in coconut milk."},{"sentence":"Ang pagninilay-nilay ay isang gawaing **pangkuwarisma**.","translation":"Reflection is a **Lenten** activity."}]

translation: to be cornered; to be entrapped
meaning_filipino: Ang mailagay sa isang sitwasyon kung saan walang matatakasan o malalabasan; masilo o mahuli sa isang patibong.
original_explanation: That feeling when your mom and your tita team up to ask you when you're getting married. You're trapped, no escape. It can also mean being forced into a marriage, the classic 'shotgun wedding' scenario in Filipino teleseryes.
usage_notes: Can refer to being physically cornered, trapped in a situation, or forced into marriage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang **mapikot** ng mga pulis ang magnanakaw, wala na siyang nagawa kundi sumuko.","translation":"When the thief was **cornered** by the police, he had no choice but to surrender."},{"sentence":"Sinasabing **napikot** lang daw siya kaya pinakasalan niya ang babae.","translation":"It is said that he was just **entrapped**, which is why he married the woman."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng takip ang isang bagay upang hindi ito makita, madumihan, o mapasok ng anuman.
etymology: From 'takip' (cover/lid) + '-an' (suffix indicating action upon an object).
original_explanation: The act of putting a lid on it. Whether it's the ulam on the table to keep the flies away, or your friend's mouth when they're about to spoil a series. "Bes, takpan mo muna 'yang feelings mo, nasa office pa tayo."
usage_notes: Often used as a command. 'Takpan mo' (You cover it). The object being covered is the focus of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Takpan** mo ang kaldero para mas mabilis kumulo ang tubig.","translation":"**Cover** the pot so the water boils faster."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **takpan** ang katotohanan, ngunit nalaman din ito ng lahat.","translation":"He tried to **cover** up the truth, but everyone found out anyway."}]

translation: to change, to alter, to make different
meaning_filipino: Gawing iba o magkaiba sa dating anyo, katangian, o kalagayan.
etymology: From 'iba' (other, different) and the suffix '-hin' (object-focus verb suffix).
original_explanation: This is the command you give when you want a do-over. 'Ibahin mo 'yung order ko, ayoko na pala niyan.' It's the mantra of the fickle-minded and the perfectionist. Also what you tell yourself when your ex wants to get back together: 'Sana **ibahin** mo na ugali mo.'
usage_notes: A very common verb used for changing almost anything, from a physical object to a plan, topic, or opinion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pwede mo bang **ibahin** ang kulay ng pader? Masyadong matingkad.","translation":"Can you **change** the color of the wall? It's too bright."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ibahin** ang usapan, sagutin mo ang tanong ko.","translation":"Don't **change** the topic, answer my question."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pahayag, kilos, o bagay na nagdudulot ng pinsala sa dangal, reputasyon, o mabuting pangalan ng isang tao.
etymology: From `sira` (damage) and `puri` (honor, reputation). The affix `nakasisi-` indicates the ability or tendency to cause something.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga chismis na may resibo, or worse, walang resibo pero kumalat na sa buong barangay. Parang blind item sa showbiz na naging headline sa tabloid. Sa panahon ng social media, isang maling post lang, **nakasisirang-puri** na agad. Pwedeng kasuhan ng libel 'to, bes!
usage_notes: Often used in legal contexts (libel, slander) or in serious accusations. The hyphen is standard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagpapakalat ng maling impormasyon ay isang gawaing **nakasisirang-puri**.","translation":"Spreading false information is a **defamatory** act."},{"sentence":"Nag-file siya ng kaso dahil sa mga **nakasisirang-puri** na komento laban sa kanya online.","translation":"She filed a case because of the **libelous** comments against her online."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang lagusan o pasukin dahil sa pagiging makapal, siksik, o matibay.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (hindi) at "mapaglagusan" (maaaring malagusan o madaanan).
original_explanation: Trying to get through EDSA traffic at 6 PM on a Friday? That's a di-mapaglagusan situation. It's for anything so thick or dense you can't get through it, like a dense jungle, a thick wall, or your friend's skull when you're trying to explain something simple.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga pisikal na hadlang tulad ng gubat, pader, o makapal na tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang gubat ay naging **di-mapaglagusan** dahil sa makakapal na halaman.","translation":"The forest became **impenetrable** because of the thick plants."},{"sentence":"Para siyang pader na **di-mapaglagusan** ng aming mga payo.","translation":"He's like a wall, **impenetrable** to our advice."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga larawan, ideya, damdamin, at sensasyon na kusang nararanasan ng isang tao sa isipan habang natutulog.
etymology: Mula sa "pan-" + "ginip". Ang "ginip" ay isang sinaunang salita na may kaugnayan sa pagtulog o pangitain.
original_explanation: 'Yung libreng pelikula na pinapalabas sa isip mo tuwing tulog ka. Minsan action, minsan horror (lalo na 'pag ex mo ang bida), minsan romance (sana all), at madalas, walang-kwentang indie film. Pag gising mo, minsan gusto mo pang ituloy, minsan naman gusto mo nang kalimutan forever.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin sa metaporikal na paraan upang tukuyin ang isang pangarap o ambisyon. Hal: "Panaginip lang ba na guminhawa ang buhay?"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang masamang **panaginip** ang gumising sa kanya sa kalagitnaan ng gabi.","translation":"A bad **dream** woke him up in the middle of the night."},{"sentence":"Sa aking **panaginip**, lumilipad daw ako.","translation":"In my **dream**, I was supposedly flying."}]

translation: to fool one another; to mess with each other
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng panloloko o paglalaro sa isip at damdamin ng isa't isa nang paulit-ulit.
etymology: From 'mag-' + reduplication of 'gago' + '-han' suffix, indicating a reciprocal or repeated action.
original_explanation: This is 'lokohan' level 99. It's when two people are playing mind games, leading each other on, and generally just making fools of each other. It's the official verb for a toxic situationship. 'Huy, tama na 'yang **maggagu-gaguhan** niyo. Mag-usap kayo nang diretso.' It implies a mutual, and often chaotic, deception.
usage_notes: A very informal and somewhat vulgar term. Use with caution among friends, but not in formal settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan na natin ang **maggagu-gaguhan** at aminin na natin ang totoo.","translation":"Let's stop **fooling each other** and just admit the truth."},{"sentence":"Awat na sa **maggagu-gaguhan**, pareho lang tayong masasaktan.","translation":"Stop this **messing with each other**, we'll both just get hurt."}]

translation: I hope my crush likes me back.
meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon ng pagnanais na sana'y magustuhan din ng taong lihim na hinahangaan (crush).
etymology: Isang pariralang Taglish na pinagsasama ang "sana" (I wish, hopefully) at ang salitang balbal na "crush back", na nangangahulugang pagbabalik ng nararamdaman ng isang crush.
original_explanation: A specific, highly potent variant of 'sana all'. This is the prayer you whisper when your crush looks in your general direction. It's the hopeful sigh when they 'like' your story from 24 weeks ago. The ultimate 'what if' of the romantically hopeful. 'Sana all' is for life goals, 'sana crushback' is for the heart.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-espesipikong balbal na ekspresyon na sikat sa mga nakababatang henerasyon at sa social media. Ito ay isang sub-category ng "sana all" phenomenon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-reply siya sa IG story ko... **sana crushback**!","translation":"He replied to my IG story... **I hope he likes me back**!"},{"sentence":"Ang panalangin ng marami: **sana crushback**.","translation":"The prayer of many: **I hope my crush likes me back**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagbagsak sa lupa dahil sa kawalan ng lakas, balanse, o suporta.
original_explanation: What happens to a boxer after a knockout punch. Or what you feel like doing after a 12-hour shift. It's not just falling; it's collapsing with finality, like a tree in a storm or your will to be productive on a Friday afternoon.
usage_notes: Often implies a heavy or sudden fall of a large object or person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumuwal** ang matandang puno dahil sa malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The old tree **fell down** because of the strong typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang paglalaba at lalo na ang pagpapaputi ng mga damit, karaniwang sa pamamagitan ng pagkukulo o pagbabad sa kemikal.
original_explanation: Before there was 'self-service laundry,' there was the kulahan. It’s the OG laundry spot, often a specific area in the backyard with a big basin (batya) and a fire underneath to boil-wash the whites. It's the reason why your lola's tablecloths were blindingly white.
usage_notes: The term is becoming less common with modern laundry methods but is understood, especially in rural contexts or historical narratives.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ni nanay ang mga puting kumot sa **kulahan** para paputiin.","translation":"Mother brought the white blankets to the **laundry bleaching area** to whiten them."}]

translation: is able to be raised; is being raised
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang itaas o iangat ang isang bagay. Ito rin ay tumutukoy sa pagiging dinadakila o pinapupurihan.
original_explanation: Think of this as successfully raising the flag during the morning assembly, or when your team lead praises you so much, 'naitataas ang bangko mo'. It's that feeling of being lifted, whether it's your hand in class or your ego after a compliment.
usage_notes: The 'nai-' prefix here implies ability or an involuntary action. It means something *can be* raised or *is being* raised.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang pagsisikap, **naitataas** niya ang antas ng pamumuhay ng kanyang pamilya.","translation":"Because of his hard work, he **is able to raise** his family's standard of living."}]

translation: to be distracted, to have one's attention diverted
meaning_filipino: Mawala sa pokus o pansamantalang maalis ang atensyon mula sa isang bagay na ginagawa o binabantayan.
etymology: Mula sa "lingat," na nangangahulugang pagkawala ng atensyon.
original_explanation: Kahit saglit ka lang malingat sa pagbabantay ng sinaing, tutong ang aabutin mo. Parang sa love, saglit ka lang lumingon sa iba, baka 'di ka na balikan. Stay focused, mga marupok!
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin bilang babala. Ang salitang-ugat na "lingat" ay bihirang gamitin nang mag-isa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **malingat** habang nagmamaneho.","translation":"Don't **get distracted** while driving."},{"sentence":"**Nalingat** lang ako sandali, nawala na ang pitaka ko.","translation":"My attention **was diverted** for just a moment, and my wallet was gone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paglalarawan sa isang tao o kilos na labis, pinalaking-laki, o masyadong madrama; pinaikling salita para sa 'overacting'.
original_explanation: The national descriptor for anyone who is just... *too much*. That friend who cries a river over a papercut? OA. The tita who treats a common cold like a terminal illness? Super OA. It's the Filipino's low-key way of saying, 'Girl, chill. It's not that deep.' Short for 'overacting'.
usage_notes: Ginagamit nang impormal. Maaaring bigkasin bilang 'O.A.' (o-ey) o bilang dalawang magkahiwalay na letra 'O-A'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka ngang **oa**, simpleng sugat lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't be so **dramatic**, it's just a simple wound."},{"sentence":"Napakagaling niyang umarte, hindi **oa** tingnan.","translation":"She's a great actress, it doesn't look **exaggerated**."}]

translation: as valuable as; as important as
meaning_filipino: May magkatulad na halaga, importansya, o presyo.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'kasing-' at salitang-ugat na 'halaga'.
original_explanation: What you tell your parents when they ask why you spent money on concert tickets instead of saving. 'Ma, 'yung experience po, **kasinghalaga** ng investment!' It's the ultimate justification for your 'luho' (luxuries).
usage_notes: Can refer to both monetary value and abstract importance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang pamilya ay **kasinghalaga** ng ginto.","translation":"For him, family is **as valuable as** gold."},{"sentence":"Ang opinyon mo ay **kasinghalaga** ng sa kanila.","translation":"Your opinion is **as important as** theirs."}]

translation: to conquer by force, to violate, to rape
meaning_filipino: Manupil o mang-abuso sa pamamagitan ng lakas; manggahasa o manakop nang may karahasan.
etymology: From the root 'gahis' (conquest, violation) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: This is a heavy word, used in legal, historical, or very serious contexts. It means to overpower someone completely, often through violence, military conquest, or sexual assault. Think villains in historical epics or the worst kind of criminals. Definitely not a word you use lightly.
usage_notes: A formal and strong term, often found in literature, news reports about heinous crimes, or historical accounts of invasion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Layunin ng mga mananakop na **gumahis** sa mga maliliit na kaharian sa kapuluan.","translation":"The invaders' goal was to **conquer** the small kingdoms in the archipelago."},{"sentence":"Ikinulong ang salarin na nagtangkang **gumahis** sa babae.","translation":"The culprit who attempted to **violate** the woman was imprisoned."}]

translation: to be overtaken by noon; to be late (until noon)
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-abot ng tanghali habang ginagawa ang isang bagay, na kadalasa'y nagpapahiwatig ng pagiging huli o mabagal sa pagkilos.
original_explanation: What happens when you say "5 more minutes" to your alarm clock and suddenly it's lunchtime and you haven't even showered. "Hala, tinanghali na ako ng gising!" is the official motto of the "puyat" generation.
usage_notes: Often used in the past tense "tinanghali" to mean one woke up late.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapatulog-tulog para hindi ka **tanghaliin** sa biyahe.","translation":"Don't keep dozing off so you won't **be overtaken by noon** on your trip."},{"sentence":"**Tinanghali** na naman siya ng gising kaya hindi siya nakapag-almusal.","translation":"He woke up **late (until noon)** again, so he wasn't able to eat breakfast."}]

translation: to buckle up; to fasten with a buckle
meaning_filipino: Isara o ikabit ang hibilya ng sinturon, sapatos, o anumang bagay na mayroon nito.
original_explanation: That thing you do with your seatbelt before the car moves, or with your belt after a massive buffet. It's the act of fastening a buckle. 'Ihibilya mo 'yang seatbelt mo, baka mahuli tayo!'
usage_notes: The root word 'hibilya' is not as common as the English 'buckle', but the verb form is understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuruan niya ang bata kung paano **ihibilya** ang kanyang sapatos.","translation":"She taught the child how to **buckle** his shoes."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **ihibilya** nang mahigpit ang tali ng kargamento.","translation":"The cargo strap needs to be **buckled** tightly."}]

meaning_filipino: Hanapin at matagpuan ang isang bagay o lugar sa unang pagkakataon; malaman o matuklasan ang isang impormasyon.
original_explanation: What you do on a Friday night, scrolling through Netflix to find a new series. It's that moment you finally figure out who the 'Marites' is in your friend group. 'Go, diskubrihin mo ang passion mo!' - sabi ng Tita mong gusto ka na mag-resign.
usage_notes: A verb in the object-focus form (-in). The root word 'diskubre' is less common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **diskubrihin** ang mga nakatagong ganda ng Pilipinas.","translation":"I want **to discover** the hidden beauties of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **diskubrihin** ang totoong motibo ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"She is trying **to discover** the true motive of her friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na upuan ng isang monarko, obispo, o sinumang may mataas na katungkulan; simbolo ng kapangyarihan o awtoridad.
original_explanation: This isn't just any 'upuan.' This is THE chair. The Iron Throne, the President's chair in Malacañang, the CEO's chair in the boardroom. 'Luklok' means the seat of power. The verb 'iluklok' means to enthrone or install someone in a high position. It's what every trapo (traditional politician) dreams of: ang makaupo sa luklok ng kapangyarihan.
usage_notes: The verb forms "lumuklok" (to sit on a throne) and "iluklok" (to enthrone someone) are more common in usage than the noun itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang gintong **luklok** ay para lamang sa reyna.","translation":"The golden **throne** is only for the queen."},{"sentence":"Marami ang nag-aasam na lumuklok sa pagkapangulo.","translation":"Many aspire to be seated in the presidency (i.e. become president)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, tabla, o pader kung saan ipinapaskil o idinidikit ang mga anunsyo, paunawa, o babasahin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "paskil" na hango sa Espanyol na "pasquín," isang paskil o anunsyo.
original_explanation: The analog version of your social media feed. Before Facebook walls, we had the 'paskilan' in the school hallway where you'd see the list of honors, the prom announcement, or that "WANTED: Clean As You Go" sign in the office pantry that everyone ignores.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo sa **paskilan** kung sino ang mga nakapasa sa pagsusulit.","translation":"Look at the **bulletin board** to see who passed the exam."},{"sentence":"Nagdikit siya ng anunsyo tungkol sa nawawalang aso sa **paskilan** ng barangay.","translation":"She posted an announcement about her missing dog on the barangay's **bulletin board**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sumusunod sa ikalawa; ang pangatlo sa isang pagkakasunod-sunod.
original_explanation: The person who gets the bronze medal. The third wheel on a date. The third-in-line at the milk tea shop who's praying they don't run out of pearls. It's not first, not second, but it's still on the list!
usage_notes: Used to denote the third position or item in a sequence. Can also be written as 'ika-3'. The word 'pangatlo' is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **ikatlo** siyang palapag ng gusali.","translation":"He is on the **third** floor of the building."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang **ikatlo** kong tasa ng kape ngayong araw.","translation":"This is my **third** cup of coffee for the day."}]

translation: to be able to ride; to be able to go along with
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakataong sumakay sa isang sasakyan; o, sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ang makaunawa o makisama sa isang biro, usapan, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Has two major flavors. 1) The literal 'May masakayan pa kayang jeep?' panic at 10 PM. It's about finding a ride. 2) The figurative 'Mabuti na lang at masakayan mo ang trip ng barkada.' This means you can vibe with them, you can go with the flow, you get the joke. If someone is 'hindi masakayan,' they're a killjoy or can't take a joke. Be the friend who is 'madaling masakayan'.
usage_notes: This word is versatile, covering both literal transportation and figurative social interaction. Context is key. Completed aspect is 'nakasakay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana may **masakayan** pa tayong bus pauwi.","translation":"I hope there's still a bus we **can ride** going home."},{"sentence":"Mahirap siyang biruin dahil hindi siya **masakayan**.","translation":"It's hard to joke with him because you **can't go along with** him (he can't take a joke)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matalim na bahagi ng araro na siyang humihiwa sa lupa. Maaari ring tumukoy sa nguso ng baboy o hayop na ginagamit sa pagbungkal.
original_explanation: The business end of an araro (plow), doing the dirty work of breaking ground. It's also what a pig uses to dig for treasures in the mud. Basically, it's the act of pushing your face or a tool into something to find what you're looking for, whether it's nutrients for crops or a good truffle.
usage_notes: Mayroon ding pandiwang anyo, 'isudsod' (to push with the snout/plow).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumama sa malaking bato ang **sudsod** ng araro.","translation":"The **plowshare** of the plow hit a large rock."},{"sentence":"Ginamit ng baboy ang **sudsod** nito para maghanap ng pagkain sa putikan.","translation":"The pig used its **snout** to look for food in the mud."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghahatid ng mga bagay, sulat, o pakete mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: The reason why we can all be tamad at home. Gutom? Food **delivery**. Need something from the mall? Package **delivery**. It's the magic that brings things to your doorstep, usually via a kuyang naka-motor who texts "Nasa gate na po."
usage_notes: Isang hiram na salitang Ingles na naging pamantayan sa Pilipinas, lalo na sa pag-usbong ng e-commerce at food delivery apps. Ang katumbas sa Tagalog ay "hatid" o "paghahatid".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gaano katagal ang **delivery** ng inorder kong sapatos?","translation":"How long is the **delivery** for the shoes I ordered?"},{"sentence":"May bayad ba ang food **delivery** sa lugar ninyo?","translation":"Is there a fee for food **delivery** in your area?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at bahagyang pag-agos o pagtulo ng likido, lalo na ang pawis o dugo, sa isang rabaw.
original_explanation: ‘Yung pawis na dahan-dahang dumadaloy sa likod mo habang naglalakad ka sa ilalim ng araw. It's the slow-mo version of a 'tulo,' like when your a/c is dying or when you're sweating bullets during a job interview.
usage_notes: Often used for sweat, blood, or other viscous fluids trickling down a surface. More of a 'flow' than 'tagiktik' which is a 'drip'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **tagistis** ng pawis sa kanyang noo.","translation":"He felt the **trickle** of sweat on his forehead."},{"sentence":"May **tagistis** ng mantika mula sa kawali.","translation":"There's an **oozing** of oil from the pan."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na maraming pera o ari-arian.
original_explanation: Describes someone who's "swimming in cash," your tita from the US who gives out dollars instead of candies, or that one friend who can afford to order Starbucks every single day without flinching. They've got the 'pera'. It can sometimes have a slightly negative flavor, implying they're *all about* the money.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ("isang mamera") to mean a rich person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang pamilya nila sa pagiging **mamera** sa kanilang bayan.","translation":"Their family is known for being **moneyed** in their town."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang makipagkaibigan sa mga taong ang tingin sa kanya ay isa lamang **mamera**.","translation":"She doesn't want to be friends with people who see her as just a **rich person**."}]

translation: to feed someone by hand or mouth
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakain sa isang tao o hayop sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay ng pagkain sa bibig nito gamit ang kamay o mula sa sariling bibig.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'subo' (pagkain sa bibig) + '-an' (hulapi na nagsasaad ng kilos).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'pabebe' move for couples, feeding each other cake during a birthday. Or it's what your mom did when you were a baby and couldn't hold a spoon. It's sweet, literally and figuratively, until someone gets food on their nose.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa romantikong konteksto o sa pag-aalaga ng bata o maysakit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Romantikong **sinubuhan** ni Marco ang kanyang nobya ng isang pirasong tsokolate.","translation":"Marco romantically **fed** his girlfriend a piece of chocolate."},{"sentence":"**Subuhan** mo muna ang sanggol ng lugaw.","translation":"**Feed** the baby some porridge first."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuan na malapad, malalim-lapad, at karaniwang gawa sa metal, na ginagamit sa paggisa, pagprito, at iba pang paraan ng pagluluto.
original_explanation: The OG kitchen weapon of every Pinoy nanay. It's not just a frying pan; it's a multi-purpose tool for gisa, prito, adobo, and sometimes, for threatening pasaway kids. The sound of a sandok hitting the kawali is the dinner bell of the Filipino household.
usage_notes: Isang pangunahing kagamitan sa kusinang Pilipino. Ang termino ay madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'frying pan' ngunit partikular na tumutukoy sa kawali na parang wok.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naggigisa si nanay ng bawang at sibuyas sa **kawali**.","translation":"Mom is sautéing garlic and onions in the **wok**."},{"sentence":"Mag-init ka ng mantika sa **kawali** para iprito ang isda.","translation":"Heat some oil in the **frying pan** to fry the fish."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng matinding pagkapagod sa katawan o isipan.
etymology: From 'hapo,' meaning fatigue or exhaustion, often with a sense of breathlessness.
original_explanation: The feeling after a 12-hour shift plus 3 hours of commute. Or after explaining the same thing to a client for the fifth time. It's a deep, bone-weary kind of tired, not just 'I need a nap' but 'I need a new life' tired.
usage_notes: Describes something that causes exhaustion, either physically or mentally.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakahahapo** ang maghapong pagtatrabaho sa bukid.","translation":"A whole day of working in the fields is **exhausting**."},{"sentence":"Ang pakikipagtalo sa taong ayaw makinig ay **nakahahapo** ng isip.","translation":"Arguing with a person who refuses to listen is mentally **tiring**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabago ng kulay tungo sa puti; pagkawala ng kulay. Maaari itong tumukoy sa balat na namumutla dahil sa takot o sakit, o sa pag-puti ng buhok dahil sa pagtanda.
etymology: From `puti` (white). The `pa-` prefix and reduplication `mu-` (< `pu-`) creates a noun for the process of becoming white or pale.
original_explanation: Two main contexts: 1) What happens to your face when you see a ghost, your credit card bill, or your ex with a new partner. The blood just drains from your face. 2) The lifelong goal in the Philippines, pursued via gluta drips, papaya soaps, and avoiding the sun like a vampire. Also, what happens to your hair that makes you a certified "Tito" or "Tita."
usage_notes: Can mean paleness (namumutla) or the process of whitening (nagpapaputi).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin niya ang **pamumuti** ng kanyang labi dahil sa sobrang lamig.","translation":"She noticed the **turning pale** of her lips due to the extreme cold."},{"sentence":"Ang **pamumuti** ng buhok ay natural na bahagi ng pagtanda.","translation":"The **whitening** of hair is a natural part of aging."}]

translation: to grow robustly, to develop well
meaning_filipino: Paglaki o pag-unlad ng katawan sa isang malusog at matipunong paraan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'bulas' at gitlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: Parang ‘yung pamangkin mong dati ay sakitin, tapos after a few years, biglang ang tangkad at ang siksik ng katawan. Nag-transform, nag-glow up physically. From totoy to hunk. That's `bumulas`.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa pisikal na pag-unlad ng isang tao, hayop, o maging halaman.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na **bumulas** ang mga tanim na gulay dahil sa masustansyang lupa.","translation":"The vegetable plants **grew robustly** because of the nutritious soil."},{"sentence":"Simula nang mag-ehersisyo siya, kitang-kita na **bumulas** ang kanyang katawan.","translation":"Since he started exercising, it's very noticeable that his body has **developed well**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pareho o magkahawig na tunog.
original_explanation: Yung 'puso' at 'suso' o 'mahal' at 'banal'. They are magkatunog. It's the secret sauce of every OPM love song, Pinoy rap battle, and your tita's cheesy poetry for the family reunion. It's what makes words sound like they're meant for each other.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to rhyming words (a synonym of magkatugma) but can also describe any two things that sound alike, like two different car horns.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga salitang 'ilaw' at 'araw' ay **magkatunog**.","translation":"The words 'ilaw' (light) and 'araw' (sun/day) are **rhyming**."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang dalawang busina na **magkatunog**.","translation":"I heard two horns that **had the same sound**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pambatang tula o awit na ginagamit sa pagbilang o pagpili sa isang laro, tulad ng 'pen-pen de sarapen'.
etymology: Possibly a folk creation, onomatopoeic or nonsensical.
original_explanation: The ancient algorithm Filipino kids use to decide who's 'taya' (it). It's our version of 'Eeny, meeny, miny, moe,' a ritual of pointing fingers and chanting nonsense words that somehow feels like a legally binding contract on the playground.
usage_notes: The full rhyme is often 'Pontempen, dodong, kalembang, hari, baraha, espada, bastos, kopas, sota, kabayo, rey.' It's one of many such rhymes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-**pontempen** muna kami para malaman kung sino ang taya sa taguan.","translation":"We did a **counting-out rhyme** first to see who would be 'it' in hide-and-seek."},{"sentence":"Itinuro ni Lola ang lumang **pontempen** sa kanyang mga apo.","translation":"Grandma taught the old **counting-out rhyme** to her grandchildren."}]

translation: act of improving or making something better; refinement
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapabuti, pag-aayos, o pagpapainam sa kalidad, kaayusan, o kalagayan ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're revising your thesis for the nth time, trying to make it perfect. It's a chef perfecting a recipe, or a company streamlining its processes for better customer service. It's the act of taking something good and making it 'galing' or 'mahusay'.
usage_notes: 'Husay' means 'skill' or 'orderliness'. 'Paghuhusay' is the act of applying that skill to improve or refine something. It implies a deliberate effort to make something excellent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang patuloy na **paghuhusay** ng serbisyo ang susi sa tagumpay ng aming negosyo.","translation":"The continuous **improvement** of service is the key to our business's success."},{"sentence":"Pinuri ng guro ang **paghuhusay** ng mag-aaral sa kanyang proyekto.","translation":"The teacher praised the student's **refinement** of his project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng karaniwang batong nabubuo na mineral na kabilang sa grupong pyroxene, kadalasang kulay itim o madilim na berde.
original_explanation: Kung nag-aaral ka ng geology, baka alam mo 'to. Isa siyang bato, bes. Hindi 'yung batong-bato ka na sa buhay, kundi literal na bato. Augita is a type of mineral na pang-science quiz bee lang ang laban. For the rest of us, it's just 'bato'.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino sa heolohiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita ang heologo ng mga kristal ng **augita** sa basalt rock.","translation":"The geologist found crystals of **augite** in the basalt rock."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na kulang sa tapang, determinasyon, o sigasig; duwag.
original_explanation: This is different from "walang-lakas" (physically weak). Walang-loob is about a lack of inner strength or guts. It's that person who wants to ask for a promotion but can't bring themselves to talk to the boss. Or someone who sees an injustice but is too scared to speak up. They have no 'fire in the belly'. Basically, duwag.
usage_notes: Ang "loob" ay isang malalim na konsepto sa sikolohiyang Pilipino na tumutukoy sa panloob na sarili. Ang "walang-loob" ay nagpapahiwatig ng kakulangan sa ubod na sarili na ito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paano ka magtatagumpay kung ikaw ay **walang-loob** na harapin ang mga pagsubok?","translation":"How will you succeed if you are **spiritless** in facing challenges?"},{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **walang-loob** dahil tumakbo siya sa gitna ng laban.","translation":"He was called **cowardly** because he ran away in the middle of the fight."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng inuming may alkohol na mula sa pinrosesong katas ng puno ng niyog. Ito ay karaniwang matapang at may mataas na 'proof'.
original_explanation: The Philippines' answer to vodka, but made from coconuts. It's the legendary spirit of Quezon province that can turn a quiet gathering into a full-blown fiesta, or make you question your life choices the next morning. It's often flavored with fruits like prunes or bubblegum (don't ask). Handle with care, or it will handle you.
usage_notes: Famous as a local product of the Quezon province. It has gained international recognition but is also notorious for instances of methanol poisoning from improper distillation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapang ang tama ng **lambanog** mula sa Quezon.","translation":"The **coconut wine** from Quezon has a strong kick."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi siya ng isang bote ng **lambanog** bilang pasalubong.","translation":"He brought home a bottle of **coconut vodka** as a souvenir."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malapot na likidong lumalabas sa ilong, lalo na kapag may sipon o trangkaso.
original_explanation: That green or clear stuff that decides to make a surprise guest appearance during a job interview, a first date, or a Zoom call when your camera is on. The mortal enemy of a crisp, white shirt.
usage_notes: A common and somewhat impolite word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Punasan mo ang **uhog** mo,\" sabi ng nanay sa kanyang anak.","translation":"\"Wipe your **snot**,\" the mother told her child."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na maranasan ang pagtanggal ng ulo mula sa kanyang katawan.
original_explanation: This is the more personal version of 'mapugot'. It's not just 'a head was cut off,' it's 'SOMEONE had their head cut off.' It's the difference between seeing a news report and being the subject of it. Used in the phrase 'mapugutan ng ulo'.
usage_notes: The affix '-an' indicates the location or recipient of the action. In this case, the person whose head is being cut off.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinatatakutan ng mga bilanggo na sila ay **mapugutan** ng ulo.","translation":"The prisoners were afraid that they would **have their heads cut off**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagkilos na may matinding pagmamadali; agaran at walang pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: How you pack your bags when someone says "libre kita sa Jollibee." It's the energy you have when you hear the "Taho!" vendor outside and you're still in your pajamas. It's rushed, frantic, and probably involves forgetting something important, like your wallet.
usage_notes: Reduplication of "dali" emphasizes the speed and urgency, often implying a lack of carefulness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dali-dali** siyang umalis ng bahay nang marinig ang sirena.","translation":"He **hastily** left the house when he heard the siren."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong gawin nang **dali-dali** ang desisyon, pag-isipan mong mabuti.","translation":"Don't make the decision **in a great hurry**; think about it carefully."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kataga na naglalarawan sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari na marangya, kahanga-hanga, at katangi-tangi.
etymology: From Swardspeak (Filipino gay slang). Its exact origin is debated but it has been in popular use since the 1970s.
original_explanation: The ultimate Pinoy compliment for anything extra, fabulous, or over-the-top in the best way possible. Your OOTD? Bongga! The debutante's party? Bongga! That new mall with a waterfall inside? Super bongga! It's the sound of being impressed.
usage_notes: A very popular slang term that has entered mainstream vocabulary. Can also be a verb 'bumongga' (to be fabulous) or 'pinabongga' (made fabulous).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bongga** ang suot mong damit! Saan mo nabili?","translation":"Your outfit is **fabulous**! Where did you buy it?"},{"sentence":"Naghanda siya ng isang **bongga** na party para sa kaarawan niya.","translation":"She prepared an **extravagant** party for her birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang "tara na," "umalis na," o "sige na," na hango sa salitang Ingles na "go."
etymology: Hango sa salitang Ingles na "go," na binigyan ng kakaibang intonasyon at paggamit sa swardspeak o gay lingo.
original_explanation: The Bekimon battle cry. It's the more fabulous, more energetic version of "Tara!" or "Let's go!" You don't just *go* somewhere, you *gow*! It implies immediate action, excitement, and probably a lot of chika along the way. "Tara, gow!" means the plan is 100% happening.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal conversations and is a hallmark of Philippine gay lingo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano na, besh? **Gow** na ba tayo sa mall?","translation":"What's up, bestie? Are we **going** to the mall now?"},{"sentence":"Tapos na ang meeting, **gow** na for lunch!","translation":"The meeting is over, let's **go** for lunch!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng matamis na pagkain na ang pangunahing sangkap ay asukal, karaniwang kinakain bilang panghimagas o meryenda.
original_explanation: The ultimate bribe for kids and the reason for your childhood toothaches. From the cheap but iconic "Potchi" and "Mik-Mik" you buy at the sari-sari store to the fancy imported chocolates your tita from the US brings home. A piece of kendi can solve a minor childhood crisis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si Lola ng isang supot ng **kendi** para sa kanyang mga apo.","translation":"Grandma bought a bag of **candy** for her grandchildren."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang kakain ng maraming **kendi** at baka sumakit ang ngipin mo.","translation":"Don't eat too much **candy** or your teeth might ache."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aayos ng hindi pagkakaunawaan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang panig upang magkaroon sila ng kasunduan o pagkakaisa.
etymology: `Mapag-` + `kasundo` (agreement). Verb form meaning "to bring into agreement".
original_explanation: Ito yung role mo sa barkada kapag may dalawang nag-away. Ikaw yung "mediator," yung "peacemaker." You're the one trying to get them to talk and settle their "tampuhan." Sa corporate world, this is called "conflict resolution." Sa pamilya, ito yung ginagawa ni lola para magbati ang mga magkakapatid.
usage_notes: Can refer to reconciling people or harmonizing conflicting ideas/things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng guro na **mapagkasundo** ang dalawang mag-aaral na nag-away.","translation":"The teacher tried to **reconcile** the two students who fought."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **mapagkasundo** ang kanilang magkaibang pananaw sa pulitika.","translation":"It's difficult to **reconcile** their different political views."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa matematika, isang likas na bilang na mas malaki sa 1 na walang positibong dibisor maliban sa 1 at sa sarili nito.
original_explanation: Think of it as the ultimate introvert of numbers. It doesn't like to be divided by others, only by 1 and itself. It's the 'it's not you, it's me' of arithmetic. Super independent, doesn't need anyone else to make it whole.
usage_notes: Isang tiyak na termino sa larangan ng matematika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pito ay isang halimbawa ng **bilang na basal**.","translation":"Seven is an example of a **prime number**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan namin sa klase kung paano tukuyin ang mga **bilang na basal**.","translation":"We are studying in class how to identify **prime numbers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na humihikayat o nag-uudyok sa iba na gumawa ng masama, karahasan, o rebelyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "man-" (tagagawa ng kilos) at salitang-ugat na "sulsol" (pag-udyok).
original_explanation: The 'Marites' of the group who loves to stir the pot. They're the ones whispering, "Ano, 'di mo papatulan?" (What, you won't fight back?). They thrive on drama and are the main reason why a small misunderstanding escalates into a full-blown group chat war.
usage_notes: Nagtataglay ng lubhang negatibong konotasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang makinig sa **manunulsol** na iyan, gusto ka lang niyang mapahamak.","translation":"Don't listen to that **instigator**, they just want you to get into trouble."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalipunan ng mga aklat na kinikilala ng mga Kristiyano bilang salita ng Diyos at pangunahing batayan ng kanilang pananampalataya.
etymology: Combination of 'banal' (holy) and 'kasulatan' (scripture, from root 'sulat' - write).
original_explanation: AKA The Bible. It's that really thick book your lola reads every morning, or the one they make you swear on in court. It's got stories, drama, life lessons, and some verses that end up as your tita's Facebook cover photo. Basically, the OG source material for all things Christian faith.
usage_notes: Always capitalized. Refers specifically to the Christian Bible.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbabasa siya ng **Banal na Kasulatan** tuwing umaga.","translation":"She reads the **Holy Scripture** every morning."},{"sentence":"Maraming aral ang mapupulot sa **Banal na Kasulatan**.","translation":"Many lessons can be learned from **The Bible**."}]

translation: to inject; to pierce with a needle
meaning_filipino: Magpasok ng likido sa katawan gamit ang karayom; bumaon o tumusok nang malalim.
original_explanation: What a nurse does to you with a vaccine or a shot of antibiotics. It's that 'Isang kagat lang ng langgam' moment before you feel the sting. Also used in a darker context for illegal drug use. So, context is key, people!
usage_notes: Strongly associated with medical injections or illegal drug use. Differentiated from 'magtusok' which is more general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang nars ang **magtuturok** ng bakuna sa mga bata.","translation":"The nurse will be the one **to inject** the vaccine into the children."},{"sentence":"Takot siyang **magpaturok** ng gamot.","translation":"He is afraid to **get injected** with medicine."}]

translation: suppression, the state of being restrained
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nahadlangan, nasupil, o hindi nakakakilos o nakakapagpatuloy dahil sa isang panlabas na pwersa o panloob na dahilan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you want to burst out laughing at a serious meeting, but you hold it in. Or when you want to tell your crush how you feel but you just can't. It's the act of being held back, whether by yourself ("self-control, bes!") or by something else (like your mom grabbing your arm before you buy another milk tea).
usage_notes: Can refer to both physical and emotional restraint.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ramdam pa rin niya ang sakit ng **pagkakapigil** sa kanyang mga pangarap.","translation":"She still feels the pain of the **suppression** of her dreams."},{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **pagkakapigil** sa suspek ay nagligtas sa biktima.","translation":"The sudden **restraint** of the suspect saved the victim."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sasakyang panlupa na tumatakbo sa riles, binubuo ng magkakadugtong na mga bagon, para sa transportasyon ng mga tao o kargamento.
original_explanation: The MRT/LRT experience. A metal tube where you get intimately acquainted with the armpits of strangers during rush hour. Riding the **tren** in Manila is an extreme sport that tests your patience, your personal space boundaries, and your ability to hold your breath. But hey, it beats sitting in EDSA traffic... sometimes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siksikan na naman sa **tren** kaninang umaga papuntang trabaho.","translation":"The **train** was crowded again this morning on the way to work."},{"sentence":"Mas mabilis sumakay ng **tren** kaysa mag-bus kung rush hour.","translation":"It's faster to take the **train** than the bus during rush hour."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang baso ng inuming may alkohol na puno hanggang sa labi, karaniwan sa mga sesyon ng inuman.
original_explanation: When a regular 'shot' just won't cut it. This is the 'walang-daya-dapat-pantay' version of a shot glass, filled to the brim. It's a test of friendship and liver fortitude. If someone gives you a shotpuno, they either really like you or they're trying to end you.
usage_notes: A popular slang term in Filipino drinking culture. It emphasizes a full, undiluted measure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pare, **shotpuno** dapat, bawal ang madaya!","translation":"Bro, it has to be a **full shot**, no cheating allowed!"},{"sentence":"Yung tanggero namin, laging **shotpuno** ang bigay.","translation":"Our 'tanggero' (drink master) always gives a **full shot**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o daanan na ginagamit sa pagtakas.
original_explanation: The fire exit of your life. The secret tunnel. 'Yung likod-bahay na tinatakbuhan mo 'pag siningil ka ng utang. It's the designated (or improvised) place to escape from. "Alam ko ang pugahan dito, sundan n'yo ako!"
usage_notes: Derived from 'puga' (escape) + '-han' (suffix indicating place).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naharangan ang tanging **pugahan** kaya't wala silang nagawa.","translation":"The only **escape route** was blocked, so they couldn't do anything."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian, gawi, o salitang nagpapakita ng kawalan ng paggalang, kalaswaan, o pagiging mahalay.
etymology: From Spanish 'basto' (coarse, crude) with the Tagalog circumfix 'ka- -han'.
original_explanation: That moment when Tito Boy makes a green joke at the family reunion and everyone just stares at their plate. It's the verbal equivalent of wearing shoes inside the house when you've just been told not to. Basically, anything that would make your lola get the walis tingting.
usage_notes: Can refer to anything from simple impoliteness to outright lewdness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagsabihan mo ang batang iyan, puro **kabastusan** ang lumalabas sa bibig.","translation":"You should reprimand that child, only **vulgarity** comes out of his mouth."},{"sentence":"Isang **kabastusan** ang hindi paggalang sa mga nakatatanda.","translation":"It is a form of **rudeness** to disrespect the elderly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng prutas na tropikal (Nephelium lappaceum) na may balat na malambot at mala-buhok o tinik, at may matamis at makatas na laman na nakabalot sa isang buto.
etymology: From Malay 'rambut' meaning 'hair', referring to the fruit's spiny exterior.
original_explanation: That spiky, hairy-looking red fruit that looks like it came from an alien planet. But once you peel it, you get that sweet, juicy, lychee-like goodness. It's a sign that the rainy season is here. Just be careful not to swallow the seed!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong prutas ang **rambutan** dahil sa tamis nito.","translation":"My favorite fruit is **rambutan** because of its sweetness."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang kilong **rambutan** sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of **rambutan** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na magkakabit o magkadikit, tulad ng kambal na prutas; kambal.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung saging na kambal, 'yun 'yung **apid**. Or 'yung dalawang ka-opisina mong laging magkasama, hindi mapaghiwalay, parang **apid**. It's that 'buy one, take one' bestie energy.
usage_notes: Isang di-karaniwang salita, madalas tumutukoy sa magkadikit na prutas tulad ng saging.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bihira kang makakita ng **apid** na mangga.","translation":"You rarely see a **conjoined** mango."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maliliit na patak ng likido na tumatalsik dahil sa isang puwersa o pagtama.
original_explanation: When you're frying hotdogs and the oil fights back. Yung mga maliliit na talsik ng mantika? That's **pilansik**. Or when a car speeds through a puddle and you get a 'free shower.' It's an unexpected, and usually unwanted, micro-splash.
usage_notes: `Pumilansik` is the verb form (to splatter). It is a synonym of the more common 'talsik' or 'tilamsik'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iingat siyang magprito para maiwasan ang **pilansik** ng mantika.","translation":"She cooks fried food carefully to avoid the **splatter** of oil."},{"sentence":"May mga **pilansik** ng putik sa kanyang pantalon.","translation":"There are **splatters** of mud on his pants."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapatong ng mga bagay o kargamento sa isang sasakyan, lalagyan, o tao.
original_explanation: 'Yung command na "Pre, kargahan mo na 'yung van ng mga gamit." O kaya sa games, "Time to kargahan ng G-Cash 'yung account." Basically, the act of putting stuff *into* or *onto* something else.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang-pokus sa ganapan (locative-focus verb).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kargahan** mo ng mga kahon ang trak.","translation":"**Load** the boxes onto the truck."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis ng isang bagong biniling produkto mula sa orihinal na pakete nito, na kadalasan ay kinukunan ng video para ibahagi sa social media.
original_explanation: The sacred ritual of opening your Shopee or Lazada package. It's the moment of truth: is it the right item? Is it damaged? Is it as ✨aesthetic✨ as the pictures? For influencers, it's content. For the rest of us, it's just pure, unadulterated excitement and the thrill of finally getting what you "added to cart" at 3 AM. "Wait, video-han mo 'ko, may unboxing video ako for my new phone!"
usage_notes: Direktang ginagamit bilang hiram na salita sa Tagalog/Taglish. Ang kilos ay madalas na ipinapahayag bilang 'mag-unboxing' o 'i-unbox'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gagawa ako ng **unboxing** video para sa bago kong sapatos.","translation":"I'm going to make an **unboxing** video for my new shoes."},{"sentence":"Ang saya ng pakiramdam tuwing **unboxing** ng 12.12 haul mo.","translation":"It's such a happy feeling when you're **unboxing** your 12.12 haul."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas at maligayang tawa na maririnig nang malinaw.
original_explanation: This is not your polite "hehe" or your corporate "haha" in an email. This is the full-bodied, can't-breathe, tears-in-your-eyes, "hampasin-mo-yung-katabi-mo" kind of laugh you let out when your friend tells a killer joke or trips over nothing. It's the sound of pure, unadulterated "chismis" sessions with the barkada.
usage_notes: Describes a very specific, loud, and hearty laugh. The verb form is 'humalakhak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig sa buong silid ang malutong na **halakhak** ni Maria.","translation":"Maria's crisp **guffaw** was heard throughout the room."}]

translation: to be hit by an arrow; to be pierced
meaning_filipino: Ang tamaan ng isang bagay na matulis at mabilis, karaniwan ay palaso, sibat, o bala.
original_explanation: Parang tinamaan ka ng pana ni Kupido, bigla kang na-in love sa nakasabay mo sa jeep. O kaya 'yung feeling na 'yung chismis, direct hit sa'yo. Sakit, bes! 'You've been struck!'
usage_notes: A literary and somewhat archaic word. 'Tamaan' is the more common equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kwento, ang bayani ay himalang hindi **natudla** ng kahit anong palaso.","translation":"In the story, the hero was miraculously not **hit** by any arrow."},{"sentence":"Ang puso niyang nagmamahal ay tila **natudla** ng kalungkutan.","translation":"His loving heart seemed to have been **pierced** by sadness."}]

translation: to turn one's back on; to abandon
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtalikod o pag-iwas sa isang tao o sitwasyon, na kadalasan ay nagpapahiwatig ng pagtanggi o pag-abandona.
etymology: Mula sa 'talikod' (to turn one's back), na nagmula sa 'likod' (back). Ang hulaping '-an' ay ginagawa itong pandiwang nakatuon sa layon.
original_explanation: A synonym for 'talikdan', but it feels more... physical. It's the literal act of turning your 'likod' (back) to someone. When you're arguing and your partner just turns and walks away? That's 'tinalikuran ka'. It's a non-verbal 'I'm done with this conversation.' A very dramatic move.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'talikdan', ngunit ang 'talikuran' ay maaaring maging mas kagyat at pisikal, habang ang 'talikdan' ay maaaring tumukoy sa mas abstraktong mga konsepto tulad ng mga prinsipyo o tungkulin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **talikuran** ang iyong mga responsibilidad bilang magulang.","translation":"Do not **turn your back on** your responsibilities as a parent."},{"sentence":"Masakit para sa kanya na **talikuran** ng kanyang matalik na kaibigan.","translation":"It was painful for him to be **abandoned** by his best friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging panig o pagpapahayag ng pagsang-ayon sa isang ideya, mungkahi, o pananaw.
original_explanation: This is your friend who says "Same!" in the group chat. When you're ranting about your boss and your workmate nods, that's a kasang-ayon. Sila yung kakampi mo sa debate, a.k.a. your 'yes-man' (but hopefully for good reasons).
usage_notes: Often used with 'sa' (kasang-ayon sa...). Can function as an adjective (e.g., "Ako ay kasang-ayon") or a noun (e.g., "Siya ay isang kasang-ayon").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kasang-ayon** ako sa iyong mungkahi na magbakasyon tayo.","translation":"I am **in agreement** with your suggestion for us to take a vacation."},{"sentence":"Marami siyang **kasang-ayon** sa kanyang plataporma.","translation":"He has many proponents for his platform."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang "kaya" o "kayang gawin". Ginagamit ito upang ipahayag na ang isang bagay ay posible, katanggap-tanggap, o kayang pamahalaan.
etymology: From English "carry", popularized in Filipino gay lingo (swardspeak).
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino "can-do" attitude compressed into one word. Derived from "carry," it means "I can carry it" or "I can handle it." Late-night deadline sa BPO? Keri lang. Limang project sabay-sabay? Keri 'yan. It's the verbal equivalent of a thumbs-up and a reassuring smile, even when you're secretly panicking inside.
usage_notes: Widely used in all informal contexts, from texting to office chats.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit mahirap ang exam, **keri** lang, basta nag-aral ka.","translation":"Even if the exam is hard, it's **okay/manageable**, as long as you studied."},{"sentence":"Teh, **keri** mo bang buhatin 'tong kahon?","translation":"Friend, **can you handle** carrying this box?"}]

translation: to narrate; to recount; to tell a story
meaning_filipino: Magkuwento o maglahad ng mga pangyayari sa paraang sunod-sunod at may detalye.
original_explanation: This is what your Marites friend does when they have the latest chismis. They don't just give you the headline, they give you the full script, complete with flashbacks and character analysis. 'Okay, isalaysay mo sa akin ang buong pangyayari, from the top!'
usage_notes: More formal than 'ikwento'. Often used for longer, more detailed accounts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **isalaysay** ko ang naging karanasan ko sa ibang bansa.","translation":"Allow me **to narrate** my experience abroad."},{"sentence":"**Isinalaysay** ng lolo ang kasaysayan ng kanilang pamilya.","translation":"The grandfather **recounted** the history of their family."}]

translation: act of sitting; assumption of office
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbaba ng katawan upang ilagay ang bigat sa mga pigi sa isang silya o sahig; maaari ring tumukoy sa pag-ako ng isang tungkulin o posisyon.
original_explanation: What you do for 8 hours a day in the office, questioning your life choices. Also, what a politician does after winning an election, which is called 'assuming office'. The first meaning is a relief after a long walk; the second meaning is the start of a long journey (or a long list of broken promises).
usage_notes: Has a literal meaning (sitting down) and a figurative one (assuming a role, especially in politics or leadership). The context usually makes the meaning clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos ang mahabang paglalakad, masarap ang **pag-upo** sa malambot na sofa.","translation":"After a long walk, **sitting** on a soft sofa feels good."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pag-upo** bilang bagong pangulo ay nagdala ng bagong pag-asa.","translation":"His **assumption of office** as the new president brought new hope."}]

translation: to get something with a pole or hook
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha sa isang bagay na mahirap abutin sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng isang mahabang kasangkapan na may kawit o panungkit sa dulo.
original_explanation: The ultimate Pinoy life hack for reaching things. This is what you do to get a ripe mango from a high branch using a long bamboo pole (panungkit). It's also the skill you use to fish out your keys that fell into a drain, or to grab that last bag of chips from the top shelf at the grocery. It’s the art of extending your reach.
usage_notes: The tool used is called a 'panungkit'. The action is 'sumungkit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumungkit** si Lolo ng hinog na mangga mula sa puno.","translation":"Grandpa **hooked** a ripe mango from the tree with a pole."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **sumungkit** ng silya mula sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"We need **to get** a chair from the other room (using something to pull it)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anak ng kapatid ng iyong ama o ina; isang pinsan na may parehong lolo at lola.
original_explanation: The 'official' cousin. The Grade-A, original, non-extended universe cousin. Your parents are siblings. You share at least one set of grandparents. This is the cousin you can't easily disown at family gatherings.
usage_notes: Used to specify the degree of cousinship, differentiating from more distant cousins.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **pinsang-buo** ko sa panig ng aking ina.","translation":"She is my **first cousin** on my mother's side."},{"sentence":"Magkasundo talaga kaming magpipinsang-buo.","translation":"We first cousins really get along well."}]

translation: to increase in number; to multiply
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdami o pagtaas ng bilang o kantidad ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: What happens to your unread emails over the weekend. 'Paunti nang paunti' is the dream, 'paparami nang paparami' is the reality of your bills, chores, and chismis.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa anyong 'paparami' (increasing). Ang 'magparami' ay nangangahulugang sadyang dagdagan ang bilang (e.g., magparami ng lahi - to procreate).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating mag**parami** ng mga puno, hindi magbawas.","translation":"We need to **increase the number** of trees, not reduce them."},{"sentence":"Paparami na nang pa**rami** ang mga taong nagkakasakit.","translation":"The number of people getting sick is **increasing**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang nakatalikod; ginawa nang hindi nalalaman o wala sa harapan ng kinauukulan; palamara o pailalim.
original_explanation: This word has two faces. The literal one is just doing something backwards, like walking `patalikod`. But the one that stings? That's the figurative meaning. It's the "taksil sa likod" move. When your "friend" talks trash about you the moment you leave the room, that's a `patalikod` attack. It's the classic "plastikan" culture, smiling at your face but holding a knife behind their back. Hugot level: 100.
usage_notes: The figurative meaning (treacherously) is more common in dramatic or emotional contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap magtiwala sa taong **patalikod** kung tumira.","translation":"It's hard to trust a person who attacks **treacherously** (behind one's back)."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang maglakad nang **patalikod** bilang bahagi ng laro.","translation":"He tried to walk **backwards** as part of the game."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagkilos, pag-uugali, o paggawi ng isang tao na sumasalamin sa kanyang karakter at pagpapalaki.
original_explanation: Your **asal** is your 'home training' on display. It's how you act. When your tita says, "Ayusin mo 'yang asal mo," she's telling you to fix your attitude, pronto. It's the core concept that separates a 'mabuting tao' from someone 'walang modo'.
usage_notes: A very important concept in Filipino culture, deeply tied to upbringing (pagpapalaki) and respect (paggalang).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda ang **asal** ng batang iyan, marunong gumalang sa matatanda.","translation":"That child has good **manners**; he knows how to respect elders."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **asal** ang nagdala sa kanya sa tagumpay.","translation":"His **conduct** brought him to success."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang huling bahagi, wakas, o pagtatapos ng isang bagay, kaganapan, o panahon.
original_explanation: The grand finale of your favorite teleserye where all the drama comes to a head. It's the "last day of school" vibe, the end of a project, or the final episode you've been waiting for. Can be epic, can be a letdown.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to the final part of a series, event, or period.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapahuli sa **tapusan** ng paborito mong palabas!","translation":"Don't miss the **finale** of your favorite show!"},{"sentence":"Malapit na ang **tapusan** ng Flores de Mayo.","translation":"The **end** of Flores de Mayo is near."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng martilyo upang pukpukin ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay pako.
original_explanation: The verb for when you need to do some 'panday' work around the house. It's the sound your neighbor makes at 7 AM on a Sunday morning. Also, a good way to vent your frustrations, but we recommend hammering nails, not other things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magmartilyo** ng pako para maisabit itong picture frame.","translation":"Help me **hammer** a nail to hang this picture frame."},{"sentence":"Buong araw siyang **nagmartilyo** para ayusin ang sirang bakod.","translation":"He was **hammering** all day to fix the broken fence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng pakikipag-usap o pag-aalay ng kahilingan at pasasalamat sa isang kinikilalang mas mataas na kapangyarihan o Diyos.
original_explanation: It's your direct line to 'The One Above'. You do this when you're about to take a board exam, when you're hoping your crush notices you, or when you're stuck in EDSA traffic praying for a miracle. It’s the spiritual version of sliding into someone's DMs, hoping for a favorable reply.
usage_notes: A more formal and spiritual synonym for 'magdasal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bago kumain, ugaliing **dumalangin** at magpasalamat.","translation":"Before eating, make it a habit **to pray** and give thanks."},{"sentence":"**Dumalangin** siya para sa kaligtasan ng kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He/She **prayed** for the safety of his/her family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging yumanig, nayanig, o nagulo dahil sa paggalaw. Sa kolokyal na gamit, tumutukoy din ito sa pagiging wala sa sarili o katinuan.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what happens to your brain during a rough bus ride on EDSA. Figuratively, it's the state of your brain after a 12-hour shift, five cups of coffee, and a call from your boss asking you to work on a Saturday. Yung feeling na "May turnilyo atang lumuwag sa ulo ko."
usage_notes: Can be literal (shaking) or figurative (mental instability/craziness). The figurative sense is more common in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **pagkaalog** ng buong bahay noong lumindol.","translation":"I felt the **shaking** of the whole house when the earthquake hit."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang stress, parang nararamdaman ko na ang **pagkaalog** ng utak ko.","translation":"With so much stress, I feel like my brain is being **shaken up**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay na natanggal, nahulog, o nalaglag mula sa pinagkakabitan, tulad ng dahon mula sa puno o buhok mula sa anit.
original_explanation: That stressful feeling when you see too much hair in the shower drain. Or the 'Autumn in my Heart' vibe of leaves falling from a tree. When something is detaching and falling off, it's lagas. Can also be used for your wallet's contents after a 12.12 sale. "Lagas na ang pera ko!"
usage_notes: Commonly used to describe hair fall (paglalagas ng buhok) and falling leaves.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa stress, naging **lagas** ang kanyang buhok.","translation":"Due to stress, her hair started **falling out**."},{"sentence":"Kinakailangang walisin ang mga **lagas** na dahon sa bakuran.","translation":"The **fallen** leaves in the yard need to be swept."}]

translation: just a coincidence, only by chance
meaning_filipino: Isang pangyayari na naganap nang hindi sinasadya, plinano, o inaasahan; nagkataon lang.
etymology: From ka- + taon (here related to pagkakataon - opportunity, chance) + lamang (only, just). Derived from the concept of 'nagkataon' (happened by chance).
original_explanation: The universe's way of playing a prank on you. When you bump into your ex while looking like a total mess, that's kataon lamang. When you're ranting about someone and they suddenly appear behind you, that's kataon lamang. It's the official explanation for serendipity, awkward encounters, and moments that make you think, 'Is this a sign or am I just overthinking?'
usage_notes: A very common phrase to express coincidence. Often shortened to 'Nagkataon lang.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko sinasadyang marinig ang usapan ninyo, **kataon lamang** na dumaan ako.","translation":"I didn't mean to hear your conversation, it was **just a coincidence** that I passed by."},{"sentence":"Pareho kami ng damit! **Kataon lamang** ba ito o tadhana?","translation":"We're wearing the same clothes! Is this **just by chance** or is it destiny?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng matinding pagkalito o kawalan ng kaayusan.
original_explanation: The state of your brain during a final exam you didn't study for. Also, the state of traffic on EDSA during a payday Friday downpour. It's when your thoughts are more tangled than your earphones after being in your pocket for 5 seconds.
usage_notes: The reduplication intensifies the meaning of 'gulo', indicating an extreme state of confusion or chaos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gulung-gulo** ang isip ko kung sino ang dapat kong paniwalaan.","translation":"My mind is **utterly confused** about who I should believe."},{"sentence":"Naiwan na **gulung-gulo** ang kwarto pagkatapos ng party.","translation":"The room was left in **complete disarray** after the party."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpaligid o pagkubkob sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: This is what happens when the chismosas in your neighborhood see you with a new "friend." They libutan you, asking questions from all sides. It's also what ants do to a dropped piece of candy. Basically, you're the center of attention, and there's no escape.
usage_notes: Can be used for people, objects, or places. Connotes a sense of being surrounded or trapped.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Linibutan** ng mga pulis ang gusali kung saan nagtatago ang mga suspek.","translation":"The police **surrounded** the building where the suspects were hiding."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong mag-alala, hindi namin kayo **lilibutan** ng tanong.","translation":"Don't worry, we won't **surround** you with questions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paniningil o pagkolekta ng utang o bayarin.
original_explanation: This is the official term for what your friend who lent you 500 pesos last month is doing when they post "blessed" with a picture of their new shoes. It's the "friendly reminder" from your landlord, the text from the credit card company, or the look your mom gives you when you owe her for the Shopee purchase she covered.
usage_notes: More formal than "paniningil."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang kumpanya sa **pag-ingil** ng mga bayarin.","translation":"The company is strict in the **collection** of payments."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-ingil** ng buwis ay mahalagang tungkulin ng pamahalaan.","translation":"The **collection** of taxes is an important function of the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkaramdam ng inggit o pagnanasa sa tagumpay, katangian, o pag-aari ng iba.
original_explanation: That feeling when your officemate gets promoted and you're still stuck in the same role, tapos bigla kang nag-scroll sa socmed nila. It's the 'sana all' na may halong konting sama ng loob. The green-eyed monster, but make it Pinoy.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a negative feeling of wanting what someone else has. It's different from 'pagseselos' (romantic jealousy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ka dapat **managhili** sa kapwa mo; lahat tayo ay may kanya-kanyang biyaya.","translation":"You should not **envy** your neighbor; we all have our own blessings."}]

translation: Debris or dirt that has been swept together
meaning_filipino: Mga dumi, alikabok, at basura na naipon mula sa pagwawalis.
etymology: From pa- prefix + walis (sweep/broom). The 'pa-' here indicates the result of the action.
original_explanation: The final boss of cleaning. It's that little pile of dust, hair, and mysterious tiny things you gather with a 'walis tingting' or 'walis tambo'. The hardest part is getting the 'pawalis' completely into the dustpan ('pandakot') without leaving that annoying line of dirt behind.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the pile of swept dirt, not the act of sweeping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha ang **pawalis** at itapon mo sa basurahan.","translation":"Please get the **swept debris** and throw it in the trash bin."},{"sentence":"Ang daming alikabok sa **pawalis** na ito.","translation":"There's so much dust in this **pile of swept dirt**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapatalas sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay isang kasangkapan tulad ng kutsilyo. Ito rin ay tumutukoy sa pagpapahusay ng isang kasanayan.
original_explanation: Think of it as leveling up your skills or your tools. Literally, it's sharpening a knife on a whetstone ('hasaan'). Figuratively, it's what you do when you practice your Mobile Legends hero, review for an exam, or rehearse your presentation for the boss. You're in 'grind mode'. 'Hasa lang nang hasa' is the mantra for getting good at something.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical objects (tools, blades) and abstract concepts (skills, talent, mind). The verb form is 'hasain'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **hasa** ang kutsilyo para hiwain ang karne.","translation":"The knife needs **sharpening** to slice the meat."},{"sentence":"Ang patuloy na pagsasanay ay isang mahusay na **hasa** para sa anumang talento.","translation":"Continuous practice is an excellent way of **honing** any talent."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at karaniwang gawa sa kawayan o kahoy na tulay na ginagamit sa pagtawid sa mababaw na ilog, sapa, o anumang agwat.
etymology: From Proto-Austronesian, referring to a bridge or something to cross on.
original_explanation: Your OG provincial footbridge. Think two bamboo poles and a prayer. It's the kind of bridge you cross to get to your lola's house in the province, or metaphorically, the 'bridge' you build to get your tiangge haul from Taytay, Rizal to your online shop.
usage_notes: Often refers to a simple, narrow bridge, sometimes just a single log or bamboo pole. Also a major municipality in Rizal, famous for its garment industry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan kami sa isang makitid na **taytay** para makatawid sa sapa.","translation":"We passed over a narrow **footbridge** to cross the stream."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa paglakad sa **taytay** dahil madulas.","translation":"Be careful walking on the **footbridge** because it's slippery."}]

translation: to be able to remember; to recall
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kakayahang maalala o manumbalik sa isipan ang isang pangyayari, impormasyon, o karanasan mula sa nakaraan.
original_explanation: That moment of panic when your friend asks, 'Uy, ano ulit pangalan niya?' and you're scrambling through your brain's messy files. When you finally get it, you've managed to 'makatanda'. It's also what you hope your brain does during an exam. 'Sana makatanda ko lahat ng ni-review ko!'
usage_notes: Often used with 'pa' (still) or 'na' (already). 'Makatanda pa' (can still remember), 'Hindi makatanda' (cannot remember).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit matagal na, **nakakatanda** pa rin niya ang lahat ng detalye.","translation":"Even though it's been a long time, she can still **remember** all the details."},{"sentence":"Hirap siyang **makatanda** ng mga pangalan pero madali siyang makatanda ng mga mukha.","translation":"He has a hard time **remembering** names but he can easily remember faces."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin o bunutin ang balahibo ng isang hayop, karaniwan ay manok o ibon, bilang paghahanda sa pagluto.
etymology: From 'mulmol', meaning fine hair or downy feathers.
original_explanation: This is what happens to a chicken after its... final moment... before it becomes tinola. It's the process of plucking all its feathers. Figuratively, it can mean to strip someone of their belongings or dignity, like what happens to your wallet after a trip to the mall. 'Hihimulmulan ka na ng mga bills pagdating ng sahod.'
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of preparing poultry for cooking. The root 'himulmol' can also refer to lint on clothes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **himulmulan** ang manok para sa hapunan.","translation":"Help me **pluck the feathers of** the chicken for dinner."},{"sentence":"Mabilis siyang mag**himulmol** ng ibong nahuli nila.","translation":"He is fast at **plucking** the bird they caught."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na crustacean na nabubuhay sa tubig, may sampung paa, at karaniwang kinakain.
original_explanation: The ultimate seafood. Perfect sa sinigang, gambas, o nilasing. Pero sa Pinoy slang, ito rin yung term para sa isang taong 'maganda ang katawan pero tapon ang mukha.' It's a bit mean, but it's a thing. So when someone says, 'Ang sexy niya, parang hipon,' you know what they mean. Body-ody-ody, face... uh, never mind.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa iba't ibang uri ng hipon. Ang "prawn" ay madalas na isinasalin din bilang "hipon" o "sugpo" para sa mas malalaking uri. Mayroon ding slang na konotasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong ulam ang sinigang na **hipon**.","translation":"My favorite dish is shrimp in sour soup (**sinigang na hipon**)."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang kilong sariwang **hipon** sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of fresh **shrimp** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman ang matinding pagkagusto o interes sa isang bagay, gawain, o tao, na nagreresulta sa pagkawala ng pansin sa ibang bagay.
original_explanation: It's that feeling when you start watching one episode on Netflix at 10 PM and suddenly it's 4 AM. You got so into it, you lost track of time. That's 'mawili'. It's what happens when you discover a new K-drama, a good book, or you're just really, *really* into the chismis your friend is telling you.
usage_notes: Can describe both getting lost in an activity and developing a fondness for a place or person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **mawili** sa paglalaro ng computer games at baka mapabayaan mo ang iyong pag-aaral.","translation":"Don't **get too engrossed** in playing computer games, or you might neglect your studies."},{"sentence":"Tila **nawili** na ang mga turista sa ganda ng Palawan kaya ayaw na nilang umuwi.","translation":"It seems the tourists **have become so fond** of the beauty of Palawan that they don't want to go home anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paggamit ng daya, panloloko, o estratehiya upang makalamang o makapinsala sa iba sa hindi tapat na paraan.
