original_explanation: That 'Emergency, need load' text from an unknown number. The 'I'm a Nigerian prince' email. Or when your friend says 'On the way na ako' but they're still in the shower. That's all a form of **panlinlang**.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of intentional deceit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabiktima siya ng **panlinlang** ng isang pekeng online seller.","translation":"She fell victim to the **deception** of a fake online seller."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga matatamis na salita ay puro **panlinlang** lamang.","translation":"His sweet words were just pure **trickery**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim sa Ingles na nangangahulugang "safe for work," ginagamit upang tukuyin ang nilalaman na angkop tingnan o pakinggan sa isang pampublikong lugar o propesyonal na kapaligiran.
original_explanation: The opposite of what's usually in an "sf" (shared folder). This is the content you can open on your work computer without your BPO team lead looking over your shoulder and getting you a memo. The G-rated, wholesome, "pwede-makita-ni-tita" stuff.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in online contexts to label content, often as a reassurance or a warning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mag-alala, **SFW** naman itong link na sinend ko.","translation":"Don't worry, this link I sent is **SFW**."},{"sentence":"Pakilagyan ng label kung **SFW** o hindi para alam namin.","translation":"Please label if it's **SFW** or not so we know."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng propesyonal na dalubhasa sa estenograpiya, ang sining ng mabilis na pagsusulat gamit ang mga simbolo at pagpapaikli, karaniwan sa mga korte o pagdinig.
original_explanation: The OG human voice-to-text converter, but for courtrooms and formal meetings. She's the woman who can type faster than you can talk, capturing every 'um,' 'ah,' and 'With all due respect, your Honor' in that weird-looking machine. The female counterpart to the estenograper.
usage_notes: Gender-specific term for a female stenographer. The gender-neutral or masculine form is 'estenograper'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **estenograpa** sa korte ay mabilis na itinala ang lahat ng testimonya.","translation":"The (female) **stenographer** in the court quickly recorded all the testimony."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagpapatakbo, nagmamay-ari, o may malaking bahagi sa isang pangkalakal na negosyo o kumpanya.
original_explanation: 'Yung tita mo na may online selling business, 'yung kapitbahay mong may sari-sari store, or si Henry Sy. Anyone who's in business, from the small-time 'raketero' to the big-time tycoon. They're the ones who are always "hustling".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang matagumpay na **negosyante** ang ama ni Ana.","translation":"Ana's father is a successful **businessperson**."},{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipinong **negosyante** ang nagsimula sa maliit na puhunan.","translation":"Many Filipino **entrepreneurs** started with a small capital."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasulatan mula sa isang doktor na naglalaman ng awtorisasyon para sa isang pasyente na makabili at gumamit ng isang partikular na gamot.
original_explanation: 'Yung papel na galing kay Doc na kailangan mong ipakita sa pharmacist para mabili 'yung gamot na hindi 'over-the-counter'. Ito 'yung reseta. Kung wala ito, baka Biogesic lang ang i-offer sa'yo sa botika.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa salitang "reseta", na mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang iinom ng gamot na walang **preskripsiyon** ng doktor.","translation":"Don't take medicine without a doctor's **prescription**."},{"sentence":"Nawala ko ang **preskripsiyon** kaya hindi ako makabili ng gamot.","translation":"I lost the **prescription** so I can't buy the medicine."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang direksiyong nasa pagitan ng hilaga at kanluran.
original_explanation: That awkward direction on the compass that's not quite north and not quite west. It's like being asked if you're an introvert or an extrovert and you're an ambivert. On the Philippine map, this is roughly the direction of Zambales and Pangasinan from Manila.
usage_notes: An intermediate cardinal direction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Papunta sa **hilagang-kanluran** ang direksyon ng bagyo.","translation":"The typhoon's direction is heading **northwest**."},{"sentence":"Ang Subic ay nasa **hilagang-kanluran** ng Maynila.","translation":"Subic is to the **northwest** of Manila."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na silid o bahay, karaniwang yari sa kahoy; isang silid sa barko o eroplano.
original_explanation: A loanword that's just... cabin. Whether it's a cozy log cabin for a Baguio staycation, a cramped cabin on a 2GO ferry, or the fancy-sounding 'cabin crew' on a plane, this is the word. It's a small, enclosed space that can either feel like a cozy escape or a claustrophobic trap, depending on your budget.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nirentahan namin ang isang **kabin** sa tabi ng lawa.","translation":"We rented a **cabin** by the lake."},{"sentence":"Pinuntahan ng pasahero ang kanyang **kabin** sa barko.","translation":"The passenger went to his **cabin** on the ship."}]

translation: to toy with; to play with casually
meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit na paglaruan ang isang bagay o damdamin nang walang seryosong layunin; gawing libangan lamang.
original_explanation: The act of 'breadcrumbing.' When someone keeps you on the hook but has no real intention of committing. They just **laru-laruin** your feelings for their own entertainment. Also what you do with your pen or your hair during a boring meeting.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng paulit-ulit, walang-kaseryosohang aksyon. Mas matindi ang implikasyon ng pagwawalang-bahala kumpara sa 'laruin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakainis na ang pusa na **laru-laruin** ang kawawang daga bago ito kainin.","translation":"It's annoying that the cat would **toy with** the poor mouse before eating it."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **laru-laruin** ang kaniyang tiwala kung hindi mo siya seseryosohin.","translation":"Don't just **play with** her trust if you're not going to be serious with her."}]

translation: to be sentimental; to express hurt feelings
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag ng hinanakit, sama ng loob, o malalim na damdamin, kadalasan dahil sa pagkadismaya o pakiramdam na hindi pinahahalagahan.
original_explanation: This is the Tagalog for 'mag-emote' or 'mag-hugot' because of hurt feelings. It's when your friend starts their sentence with "Hindi naman sa nanunumbat, pero..."—that's your cue, they're about to magsentimyento. It’s a low-key form of 'magdrama'.
usage_notes: Implies expressing negative or hurt feelings, often in a passive-aggressive or emotionally charged way. Different from just 'being sad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mo na siya, mahilig lang talaga siyang **magsentimyento** kapag hindi napagbibigyan.","translation":"Just ignore him, he just likes **to express hurt feelings** when he doesn't get his way."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng ilang bote, nagsimula na siyang **magsentimyento** tungkol sa kanyang ex.","translation":"After a few bottles, he started **to get sentimental** (and complain) about his ex."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sapin sa paa na karaniwang yari sa goma, walang takong, at bukas ang mga daliri.
original_explanation: The official footwear of the Filipino nation. It's used for walking, as a 'pamalo' (for discipline or killing ipis), as a 'pato' in tumbang preso, and as the ultimate weapon when thrown by an angry mother with deadly accuracy. Also known as the 'flying la chancla'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magsuot ka ng **tsinelas** para hindi marumihan ang paa mo.","translation":"Wear **slippers** so your feet don't get dirty."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang isang pares ng **tsinelas** ko sa baha.","translation":"I lost one of my pair of **flip-flops** in the flood."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang unlapi na ginagamit sa paghahambing ng dalawang bagay, tao, o konsepto na may magkatulad na katangian. Ikinakabit ito sa unahan ng isang salitang-ugat, karaniwan ay isang pang-uri.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'sing-' na nangangahulugang pagkakatulad, na dinagdagan ng 'ka-' upang bumuo ng pang-uri.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'same level' prefix. It's what you use when you want to say your ex's new partner is 'kasing-ganda ng' (as beautiful as) a movie star. It's the equality operator (=) in the grammar of Filipino comparisons. Use it to prove a point, to compliment, or to throw subtle shade.
usage_notes: This prefix is used to form adjectives of equal comparison. The form changes depending on the first letter of the root word: 'kasing-' before vowels and most consonants (k, g, h, m, n, ng, w, y), 'kasin-' before d, l, r, s, t, and 'kasim-' before b, p.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig niya ay **kasing**-init ng kape sa umaga.","translation":"His love is **as** warm **as** coffee in the morning."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **kasing**-husay ng kanyang ama sa pagpipinta.","translation":"She is **as** skilled **as** her father in painting."}]

translation: to fall down prostrate; to sprawl
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbagsak sa lupa o sahig nang nakadapa o nakahiga, karaniwang dahil sa matinding pagod, sakit, o pagkahimatay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'handusay' (nakadapa o bagsak ang katawan) at ang gitlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling mo pag-uwi galing trabaho on a Friday night. Bagsak ka na lang sa kama, wala nang pakialam sa mundo. That's **humandusay**. It's not a graceful fall; it's a 'wala-na-finish-na' kind of collapse.
usage_notes: Madalas na nagpapahiwatig ng matinding pagkapagod, panghihina, o pagkawala ng malay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos ang marathon, **humandusay** sa damuhan ang pagod na mananakbo.","translation":"After the marathon, the tired runner **sprawled** on the grass."},{"sentence":"Nakita siyang **humandusay** sa sahig dahil sa sobrang taas ng lagnat.","translation":"He was seen **fallen prostrate** on the floor due to a very high fever."}]

translation: to copy; to imitate; to model after
meaning_filipino: Tularan o gayahin ang isang modelo o halimbawa.
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na "paris" (pair, match) at hulaping "-an".
original_explanation: This is when your teacher says, "**Parisan** ninyo ang nasa blackboard," meaning 'copy what's on the blackboard.' In life, it's about finding a role model, 'yung taong gusto mong **parisan** ang success. Or 'yung classmate mo na laging pinapagalitan kasi **pinaparisan** niya 'yung sagot mo sa exam.
usage_notes: Ang ugat na "paris" ay nangangahulugang 'kapareha' o 'katulad'. Ang "parisan" ay nangangahulugang gawing kapareha o katulad ng iba, kaya't ito ay may kahulugang kopyahin o tularan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **parisan** ang masamang ugali ng kaibigan mo.","translation":"Do not **imitate** your friend's bad behavior."},{"sentence":"**Parisan** mo ang disenyo na ito para sa gagawin mong damit.","translation":"**Model** your dress design after this one."}]

translation: to be able to hinder or obstruct
meaning_filipino: Maging isang balakid, sagabal, o hadlang sa isang gawain, plano, o pag-unlad.
original_explanation: That one thing that gets in your way. Pwedeng 'yung mabagal na internet connection na makahadlang sa panonood mo ng Netflix. O 'yung toxic mong kaibigan na ayaw kang umasenso. Anything that blocks your path to success or happiness. A "kontrabida" in your life story.
usage_notes: The prefix "maka-" denotes the potential or ability to be an obstacle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi dapat **makahadlang** ang kahirapan sa pag-abot ng iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"Poverty should not be **able to hinder** you from reaching your dreams."},{"sentence":"Alisin mo ang mga silya sa daan para walang **makahadlang**.","translation":"Remove the chairs from the path so that nothing can **obstruct** it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang elektroniko na ginagamit upang kontrolin ang isang aparato mula sa malayo.
original_explanation: The scepter of the household. The one object that causes more family arguments than the last piece of lechon. Hawak mo 'to, ikaw ang hari ng TV, ng aircon, ng electric fan. Mawala lang 'to, buong pamilya nagiging search and rescue team.
usage_notes: Often just called 'remote.' The adjective 'remote' (malayo) is usually translated to Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasaan na naman ang **remote** ng TV? Hindi ko mahanap.","translation":"Where's the TV **remote** again? I can't find it."},{"sentence":"Pakikuha nga ng **remote** ng aircon, masyadong malamig.","translation":"Please get the aircon **remote**, it's too cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na panyo o piraso ng tela na karaniwang isinusuot sa leeg, ulo, o pulso bilang palamuti.
original_explanation: The stylish cousin of the 'panyo'. This is what flight attendants wear, what K-pop idols tie to their mic stands, and what you use to complete your 'Tita of Manila' OOTD. It’s too small to be a real scarf, too fancy to be a pamunas ng pawis. It's purely for fashion purposes, darling.
usage_notes: Often associated with fashion or uniforms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bahagi ng uniporme ng mga boy scout ang kulay dilaw na **panyuleta**.","translation":"A yellow **neckerchief** is part of the boy scouts' uniform."},{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng seda na **panyuleta** sa kanyang buhok.","translation":"She put a silk **scarf** in her hair."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggaya sa isang tao o bagay sa paraang nakakatuwa, nakakainsulto, o mapang-uyam.
etymology: From paN- (becomes pam-) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root 'badya' (-ma-). 'Badya' means to declare, but in this context, it takes on the sense of imitation.
original_explanation: This is high-level pang-aasar. It's not just a simple insult; it's performance art. Think of a comedian perfectly imitating a politician's voice and mannerisms, or your friend mimicking the way you walk when you're trying to be cool. It's the act of turning someone into a caricature for laughs, sometimes harmless, sometimes savage.
usage_notes: This is a less common word. A more common synonym is 'panggagaya' or 'panunuya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo ang **pamamadya** mo sa pagsasalita ko.","translation":"Stop your **mockery** of the way I speak."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang komedyante sa kanyang galing sa **pamamadya** ng mga sikat na personalidad.","translation":"The comedian is known for his skill in **making a caricature** of famous personalities."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaagapay; may magkatulad na agwat sa lahat ng punto at hindi magtatagpo kahit gaano pahabain.
original_explanation: Like you and your crush's love story: running side-by-side but never meant to intersect. Also, what your high school math teacher tried to explain using two rulers. This is the less common spelling.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang baryasyon sa pagbaybay ng 'paralelo'. Mas karaniwan at pormal ang 'paralelo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat **paralel** ang dalawang guhit na ito.","translation":"These two lines should be **parallel**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga riles ng tren ay laging **paralel** sa isa't isa.","translation":"Train tracks are always **parallel** to each other."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-subscribe sa updates o posts ng isang tao o pahina sa isang social media platform tulad ng Facebook, Instagram, o Twitter.
etymology: From English 'follow', with its meaning adapted for the social media era.
original_explanation: In the old days, it meant stalking someone physically. Now, it's the socially acceptable digital version. It's that single click that says, 'I am interested in the curated version of your life you present online.' It's the first step to becoming a fan, a hater, or just a silent lurker (marites-in-training).
usage_notes: Often used with prefixes like 'i-' (i-follow) or in gerund form 'fina-follow'. 'Follow back' is also a common phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino-sino ang mga artista na fina-**follow** mo sa Instagram?","translation":"Who are the celebrities you **follow** on Instagram?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan i-**follow** ang page namin para sa mga updates!","translation":"Don't forget to **follow** our page for updates!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw ng mga labi at mukha na nagpapahayag ng saya, galak, o pagiging palakaibigan.
original_explanation: The universal Filipino greeting, apology, and 'I-don't-know-what-to-say-so-I'll-just-do-this' expression. It's your best accessory. It's what you give the jeepney driver when you're one peso short. It's free and can make someone's day.
usage_notes: Almost always has a positive connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang matamis na **ngiti** ang sumalubong sa akin pag-uwi ko.","translation":"A sweet **smile** greeted me when I got home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging palalo, mayabang, at pagtingin nang mababa sa kapwa.
etymology: Kombinasyon ng unlaping `mapag-` (pagkahilig), unlaping `ma-`, at salitang-ugat na `taas` (high). Literal na nangangahulugang "mahilig maging mataas/nakatataas."
original_explanation: This is the "Don't you know who I am?" person. They think they're a VIP even when buying suka sa tindahan. They look down on people, literally and figuratively. Parang laging may invisible throne na inuupuan. The opposite of a "down-to-earth" person; they're more "up-in-the-clouds-with-their-ego."
usage_notes: Ang `mapagmataas` ay may matinding negatibong konotasyon ng pagtingin nang mababa sa iba. Ang pariralang `mapagmataas na tao` ay simpleng nangangahulugang "isang taong mayabang o arogante."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang yaman, siya ay naging **mapagmataas** at walang kinakausap na mahirap.","translation":"Because of his wealth, he became **arrogant** and doesn't talk to the poor."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging **mapagmataas** ay hadlang sa tunay na pakikipagkaibigan.","translation":"Being **haughty** is a hindrance to true friendship."}]

meaning_filipino: Tinutukoy ang kalangitan na natatakpan ng mga ulap; madilim o kulimlim ang panahon.
etymology: From 'ulap' (cloud), with the 'ma-' prefix indicating 'full of' or 'characterized by'. 'Ulop' is a less common root than 'ulap' but carries the same meaning of cloudiness/gloom.
original_explanation: That feeling when the sky looks like it's about to drop its hugot playlist. Perfect weather for bed-weather, instant noodles, and contemplating your life choices. Hindi pa umuulan, pero parang ang bigat-bigat na ng atmosphere, just like the tension in a family reunion.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'maulap', but 'maulop' can carry a stronger connotation of gloominess or darkness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maulop** ang langit kaya nagdala ako ng payong.","translation":"The sky is **overcast** so I brought an umbrella."},{"sentence":"Biglang naging **maulop** ang kaninang maliwanag na hapon.","translation":"The previously bright afternoon suddenly became **gloomy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malambot at esponghadong gitnang bahagi ng katawan ng ilang uri ng puno o halaman.
original_explanation: Eto yung 'puso' ng saging o ng ibang puno. Yung malambot na part sa loob na parang foam. Hindi ito yung kinakain nating 'puso ng saging' ha, ito yung mismong structural core. Parang yung soft spot mo para sa kanya kahit lagi ka niyang gino-ghost.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang teknikal na termino sa botanika at hindi karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **lumbo** ng puno ng saging bilang palamuti.","translation":"He used the **pith** of the banana trunk as a decoration."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa ikawalong posisyon o pagkakasunod-sunod sa isang serye.
original_explanation: The number after pampito and before pansiyam. Kung walo kayong magkakapatid, ikaw ang pangwalo kung ikaw ang bunso. Sa pila sa lotto, ito yung pwesto na umaasa ka pa ring may matitirang ticket.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang tukuyin ang ordinal na bilang na ika-8. Maaari ding isulat bilang "ika-8" o "pang-8".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **pangwalo** sa pila.","translation":"He is the **eighth** in line."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang **pangwalo** kong tasa ng kape ngayong araw.","translation":"This is my **eighth** cup of coffee for the day."}]

translation: to sneer at; to look down on
meaning_filipino: Tumingin nang may paghamak o pagmamaliit sa isang tao o bagay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "ismid" na nangangahulugang pagngiwi o pag-ismid.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "mata-pobre" move. 'Yung tingin na parang sinasabing "eww, you?" from head to toe. The classic kontrabida look in every teleserye. Kung tingin lang ay nakamamatay, marami nang casualty dahil sa ismiran.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit sa mga di-pormal na pag-uusap para ilarawan ang isang mapangmatang kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ismiran** ang suot niya dahil lang hindi ito mamahalin.","translation":"Don't **sneer at** what she's wearing just because it's not expensive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho o gawain ay ang pagpapanatili ng kalinisan ng isang lugar.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of every office, condo, or household. They're the ones who magically make the coffee stains on the pantry counter disappear and restore order after a chaotic party. Basically, the person who cleans up everyone else's mess.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with `tagalinis`. `Limpya` is of Spanish origin, while `linis` is native.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusapan mo ang **tagalimpya** na ayusin ang mga basura sa labas.","translation":"Please ask the **cleaner** to fix the trash outside."},{"sentence":"May iskedyul ang pagdating ng **tagalimpya** sa aming opisina.","translation":"The arrival of the **cleaner** at our office is scheduled."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay o pagbubudbod ng paminta sa isang bagay, karaniwan sa pagkain, upang magdagdag ng lasa o anghang.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your food tastes like your love life—bland and uneventful. You grab the pepper grinder and 'pamintahan mo,' adding that much-needed kick. It's the act of spicing things up, one sprinkle at a time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pamintahan** mo naman itong itlog para may lasa.","translation":"Please **put pepper on** this egg so it has some flavor."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **pamintahan** ang sabaw, baka umanghang nang sobra.","translation":"Don't **put too much pepper on** the soup, it might get too spicy."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang nag-aalab o naglalagablab; lumilikha ng malaking apoy o liyab.
etymology: From "lingas" (blaze, flame) with the "nag-" prefix and "-li-" infix for the progressive aspect.
original_explanation: This is your barbecue grill going Super Saiyan. It’s when a small flame decides it wants to be a bonfire. Can also describe your tita when she finds out you're still single: her anger is naglilingas. It's a fire that's actively and intensely burning.
usage_notes: Often used to describe fire, but can be used metaphorically for intense emotions like anger or passion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naglilingas** ang apoy sa basurahan dahil sa init ng araw.","translation":"The fire in the trash can is **blazing** because of the heat of the sun."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko kung paano **naglilingas** sa galit ang kanyang mga mata.","translation":"I saw how his eyes were **flaring up** in anger."}]

meaning_filipino: Isipin at huwag kalimutan ang isang bagay, paalala, o babala; maglagay ng marka upang matukoy.
original_explanation: This is the act of mentally screenshotting a piece of information. It's what your mom tells you after a long lecture: 'Magtanda ka, ha!' It means 'Let this be a lesson' or 'Burn this into your memory.' It can also be literal, like marking a spot. 'Magtanda ka ng page na binabasa mo.' (Mark the page you're reading).
usage_notes: Can be used as a command or a statement. It carries a sense of importance or warning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtanda** ka sa mga sinabi ko para hindi ka na magkamali ulit.","translation":"**Remember** what I told you so you don't make a mistake again."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magtanda** ng mga mahahalagang petsa sa kalendaryo.","translation":"You need to **mark** the important dates on the calendar."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, gusali, o silid kung saan isinasagawa ang mga gawaing pang-administratibo, pangnegosyo, o propesyonal.
original_explanation: The second home of every BPO agent and corporate slave. Your opisina is where the magic (and the stress) happens. It's the land of cubicles, free (but bad) coffee, gossiping officemates, and the dreaded "urgent" email from your boss. It's where you go to earn the "pambayad ng bills."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga akong pumasok sa **opisina** para tapusin ang report.","translation":"I went to the **office** early to finish the report."},{"sentence":"Magkita na lang tayo sa **opisina** mo bukas.","translation":"Let's just meet at your **office** tomorrow."}]

translation: to dilute; to make thin or watery
meaning_filipino: Dagdagan ng likido, karaniwan ay tubig, ang isang timpla upang mabawasan ang tapang, lapot, o konsentrasyon nito.
etymology: From the root word "labnaw" (thinness, wateriness) + "-an" suffix.
original_explanation: What you do to the sinigang broth when it's too sour, or to the iced tea when it's too sweet. It's also what happens to the chismis when it passes through too many people—the story gets diluted and the facts become watery.
usage_notes: Used for liquids like sauces, drinks, soups, or even chemical solutions. The opposite is "palaputin" (to thicken).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Labnawan** mo ng kaunting tubig ang kape dahil masyadong matapang.","translation":"**Dilute** the coffee with a little water because it's too strong."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **labnawan** ang pintura bago gamitin.","translation":"The paint needs to be **thinned** before being used."}]

translation: to vomit involuntarily; to be made to vomit
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang ilabas ang laman ng sikmura; maduwal.
etymology: ma- (unintentional action prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + suka (vomit)
original_explanation: That feeling when you ate something sketchy from a street vendor, or when you had one too many drinks at the office Christmas party. It’s your body’s emergency eject button. "Sa sobrang kaba ko bago ang presentation, feeling ko mapapasuka ako." Also, the reaction to seeing your ex's disgustingly sweet posts with their new partner.
usage_notes: The root word 'suka' also means vinegar. Context and pronunciation prevent confusion. Suka (vinegar) is /SU-ka/, while suka (vomit) is /su-KA/. 'Mapasuka' always refers to vomiting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napasuka** ang buntis dahil sa kanyang \"morning sickness\".","translation":"The pregnant woman **vomited involuntarily** due to her morning sickness."},{"sentence":"Halos **mapasuka** ako sa sama ng amoy.","translation":"I almost **vomited** from the bad smell."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, alok, o paraan na ginagamit upang himukin o hikayatin ang isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the 'promo' or 'freebie' that makes you click 'Add to Cart.' It's the 13th-month pay that keeps you from resigning, or the 'sample' at the grocery store that convinces you to buy the whole box. A *pahikayat* is the bait, the lure, the extra something that seals the deal.
usage_notes: Refers to the thing or method used for persuasion, not the act itself (which is 'paghikayat').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-alok ang kumpanya ng malaking bonus bilang **pahikayat** sa mga empleyado.","translation":"The company offered a large bonus as an **incentive** for the employees."},{"sentence":"Ang libreng kape ay isang magandang **pahikayat** para bumisita ang mga customer.","translation":"The free coffee is a good **inducement** for customers to visit."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging makabayan; ang pagmamahal, paggalang, at katapatan sa sariling bansa.
original_explanation: This is that feeling you get when Manny Pacquiao has a fight, a Pinoy wins an international singing contest, or you see a Jollibee abroad. It's buying local products, knowing the Lupang Hinirang by heart, and maybe even complaining about the government because you know the country deserves better. It's the 'Pinoy Pride' that's more than just a hashtag.
usage_notes: A highly valued civic virtue. Often discussed in history, social studies, and political contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtangkilik sa sariling produkto ay isang paraan ng pagpapakita ng **pagkamakabayan**.","translation":"Patronizing local products is one way of showing **patriotism**."},{"sentence":"Itinuro sa amin sa paaralan ang kahalagahan ng **pagkamakabayan**.","translation":"We were taught in school the importance of **patriotism**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang-ugat (Maranta arundinacea) kung saan nakukuha ang gawgaw (starch) na ginagamit sa paggawa ng mga biskwit, kakanin, at bilang pampalapot sa mga lutuin.
original_explanation: That old-school biscuit your lola gives you na parang natutunaw sa bibig. It's made from aruro powder. It's the OG, gluten-free, organic flour before it was cool. The stuff that makes 'uraro' cookies the ultimate pasalubong from Quezon province.
usage_notes: Madalas mapagkamalang "uraro", na tumutukoy sa biskwit na gawa sa harina ng aruro.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang gawgaw mula sa **aruro** ay masustansya at madaling tunawin.","translation":"The starch from **arrowroot** is nutritious and easy to digest."},{"sentence":"Nagtanim sila ng **aruro** sa kanilang bakuran para gawing harina.","translation":"They planted **arrowroot** in their yard to make into flour."}]

translation: to bet; to make a wager
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng pera o anumang halaga sa isang kasunduan kung saan ang mananalo ay nakabatay sa resulta ng isang hindi pa natatapos na pangyayari.
original_explanation: "Tara, magpustahan tayo, 'di 'yan sisiputin ng jowa niya." This is the national sport during basketball games, boxing matches, and elections. The 'pustahan' can be for money, a free lunch, or just bragging rights. It's the financial equivalent of "sabi ko sa'yo, eh!"
usage_notes: Often involves two or more people. Can be used as 'magpustahan tayo' (let's bet).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig silang **magpustahan** tuwing may laro ng basketball sa PBA.","translation":"They love to **make a wager** whenever there's a PBA basketball game."},{"sentence":"**Nagpustahan** kami kung sino ang unang darating sa opisina.","translation":"We **made a bet** on who would arrive at the office first."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lihim na plano o gawain na karaniwang may masamang layunin; tsismis o usap-usapan na nagdudulot ng gulo o hindi pagkakaunawaan.
original_explanation: The national sport of every barangay and office department. It's the 'tea' before 'tea' was a thing. If Marites was an Olympic event, 'intriga' would be the equipment used. It's the spice that ruins friendships and the reason why your tita gives you the side-eye at family reunions.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng tsismis o hidwaan sa pagitan ng mga tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa mga **intriga** na naririnig mo tungkol sa kanya.","translation":"Don't believe the **gossip** you hear about him/her."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **intriga** ang mundo ng showbiz.","translation":"The world of showbiz is full of **intrigue**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema o proseso ng artipisyal na pagbibigay ng tubig sa mga lupang sakahan, lalo na sa mga pananim, upang matiyak ang kanilang paglago.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "tubig" (water) at panlaping "pa-".
original_explanation: This is the lifeblood of our rice fields. It's the government project that brings water from the dam to the farms. Think of it as the farm's plumbing system. No patubig, no tubig. No tubig, no palay. No palay, no kanin. No kanin? Chaos.
usage_notes: Isang mahalagang termino sa agrikultura at inhenyeriya sibil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaayos ng mga magsasaka ang kanal para sa **patubig**.","translation":"The farmers are fixing the canal for the **irrigation**."}]

translation: to act, to portray, to perform a role
meaning_filipino: Isabuhay ang isang karakter sa isang dula, pelikula, o palabas; tumupad sa isang partikular na tungkulin.
etymology: From the root 'ganap' (complete, to happen, role) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: The official verb for actors, cosplayers, and anyone pretending to be someone they're not. When you 'gumanap ng papel,' you're playing a role. Like when you have to be the happy, well-adjusted tita at the family reunion even though you're dead inside.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the phrase 'gumanap ng/sa papel na...' which means 'to play the role of...'. It is closely related to 'gumampan' but focuses more on portrayal and characterization.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **gumanap** bilang pangunahing kontrabida sa sikat na teleserye.","translation":"She **portrayed** the main villain in the famous TV series."},{"sentence":"Bawat isa sa atin ay may mahalagang papel na ginagampanan sa lipunan.","translation":"Each one of us has an important role to **perform** in society."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagtangging suportahan o makilahok sa isang gawain, produkto, o serbisyo bilang paraan ng protesta.
original_explanation: The verb form of "boycott," a word that has been fully Filipinized. This is what happens when a celebrity says something problematic and the internet collectively decides to "cancel" their new movie. "Tara, i-boycott natin!" becomes "Bumoykoteo tayo."
usage_notes: A clear loanword, used in formal and informal contexts related to protest and consumer action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumoykoteo** ang mga mamamayan sa produkto ng kumpanyang napatunayang lumalabag sa batas-paggawa.","translation":"The citizens **boycotted** the products of the company proven to be violating labor laws."},{"sentence":"Nag-trending ang panawagan na **bumoykoteo** ang lahat sa nasabing palabas.","translation":"The call for everyone to **boycott** the said show became a trending topic."}]

translation: To tilt up; to raise one end
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-angat o pagtaas ng isang dulo ng isang bagay habang ang kabilang dulo ay nananatiling nakababa o nakapirmi.
original_explanation: What you do with your feet on the dashboard during a road trip (until your mom smacks them down). Also, that slight, almost-flirty lift of the chin. It's the opposite of being level-headed; you're literally making something unbalanced on purpose.
usage_notes: Implies an upward tilting motion from a resting position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **itikwas** ang silya at baka ka mahulog.","translation":"Don't **tilt** the chair or you might fall."},{"sentence":"**Itinikwas** niya ang kanyang mga paa sa mesa habang nagbabasa.","translation":"She **raised** her feet onto the table while reading."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ikid o pagbabalot nang paikot sa isang bagay, tulad ng ginagawa ng ahas o baging.
original_explanation: That clingy jowa, that's `magpulupot`. Or a snake. Or your earphones in your pocket. Or that one tita at the party who wraps her arm around yours and won't let go until she's done with all the chismis. It's the act of wrapping around something so tightly it's hard to get out.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for snakes or vines, or figuratively for overly clingy people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig **magpulupot** ang ahas sa sanga ng puno.","translation":"The snake likes to **coil around** the tree branch."},{"sentence":"\"Huwag kang **magpulupot** sa akin, ang init-init!\"","translation":"\"Don't **wrap yourself around** me, it's so hot!\""}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marka o bakas na iniiwan ng paa sa isang ibabaw; maaari ding tumukoy sa mismong ilalim ng paa.
original_explanation: The evidence you leave behind after walking on a wet floor your mom just mopped. Also, the bottom part of your foot that gets super dirty when you walk around barefoot. 'Ang dumi ng tapak mo!' is a classic line from every Filipino parent.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'yapak' but 'tapak' can also refer to the sole of the foot itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga **tapak** ng putik sa sahig.","translation":"There are muddy **footprints** on the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi masikip; may sapat o labis na espasyo.
original_explanation: That feeling when you try on your old jeans after a month of "healthy living" and they're suddenly **maluag**. Or when your project timeline is so generous, you have enough time to binge-watch a whole series before starting. It's the opposite of "siksikan sa MRT." It's the freedom of space, whether in your pants or your schedule.
usage_notes: Can refer to clothing, spaces, or even rules and schedules. Often used interchangeably with 'maluwang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas komportable ako sa **maluag** na damit.","translation":"I am more comfortable in **loose** clothing."},{"sentence":"**Maluag** ang daloy ng trapiko ngayong umaga.","translation":"The flow of traffic is **light/spacious** this morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga karagdagang bagay na isinusuot o ginagamit upang umakma sa damit o kasuotan, gaya ng alahas, sinturon, o bag.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles "accessory" o Espanyol "accesorio", na ginawang pangmaramihan.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga pampaganda na hindi damit. Yung hikaw, kwintas, singsing, at pati na rin yung bag na terno sa sapatos mo. Sila yung nagbibigay ng 'final touch' sa OOTD mo. Parang extra toppings sa halo-halo, mas masarap 'pag meron.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa anyong pangmaramihan para tumukoy sa mga palamuti sa katawan o damit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang bumili ng mga mamahaling **aksesorya**.","translation":"She loves to buy expensive **accessories**."},{"sentence":"Simple lang ang kanyang bestida pero bongga ang mga **aksesorya**.","translation":"Her dress was simple but her **accessories** were extravagant."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit o paglalagay ng bagoong sa pagkain bilang pampalasa o sahog.
original_explanation: That moment you're about to eat green mangoes and your friend asks you to "magbagoong." It's not just adding a condiment; it's activating flavor level 9000. It's the act of making something already good, even more deliciously Pinoy.
usage_notes: Used when adding bagoong to a dish or as a dipping sauce.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magbagoong** nang marami, baka tumaas ang presyon mo.","translation":"Don't **use too much shrimp paste**, your blood pressure might rise."},{"sentence":"Masarap **magbagoong** sa hilaw na mangga.","translation":"It's delicious to **use shrimp paste** with green mangoes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari na nagdudulot ng inis, pagkayamot, o pagkabuwisit.
etymology: From `pan-` (causative prefix) + `buwisit` (annoyance, jinx, from Minnan Chinese). The `n` in `pan-` assimilates to `m` before `b`.
original_explanation: Anything or anyone that makes you go "Haaaay, nako!" That one person in your Zoom meeting who won't mute, the slow internet when you're rushing a deadline, or that weird sound your car makes. Basically, anything that tests your patience and makes you want to scream into a pillow. Ang ultimate trigger ng inner beast mo.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective or as a noun to refer to the source of annoyance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talaga namang **pambuwisit** ang trapik sa EDSA tuwing Biyernes.","translation":"The traffic on EDSA every Friday is truly **annoying**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **pambuwisit** ngayon, masama ang gising ko.","translation":"Don't be **an annoyance** today, I woke up on the wrong side of the bed."}]

meaning_filipino: (Kolokyal) Ang akto ng pag-inom ng alak; isang sesyon ng inuman.
etymology: Etymology is uncertain, possibly onomatopoeic or a localized slang term.
original_explanation: The unofficial national sport of titos and titas on a Friday night. 'Tara, barik!' is the call of the wild for those who want to unwind with a bottle of beer or gin. It's not just drinking, it's a social ritual involving pulutan, chismis, and bad videoke singing.
usage_notes: Primarily used as slang. Can function as a noun (the session) or a verb (the act of drinking).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **barik** session mamaya sa bahay ni kuya.","translation":"There's a **drinking session** later at my brother's house."},{"sentence":"Gusto mo bang mag-**barik** pagkatapos ng trabaho?","translation":"Do you want to **drink** after work?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking kulisap na may pakpak, karaniwang itim at dilaw, na may kakayahang sumipsip ng nektar mula sa bulaklak at gumawa ng pulot.
original_explanation: The OG flying fluffball of the insect world. Not the skinny pukyutan (honeybee), but its chonkier, noisier cousin. Think of it as the tito of the garden, buzzing around, minding its own business, unless you provoke it.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'pukyutan' (honeybee) in casual conversation, but technically refers to the larger bumblebee.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **bubuyog** na pumasok sa bintana.","translation":"A **bumblebee** entered through the window."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong guluhin ang pugad ng **bubuyog**.","translation":"Don't disturb the **bumblebee's** nest."}]

translation: to do something in reverse; to do something left-handedly or awkwardly
meaning_filipino: Gawin ang isang bagay sa kabaligtarang paraan, paurong, o salungat sa karaniwan.
original_explanation: This is trying to write with your non-dominant hand. Or when you're so stressed you put your shirt on inside-out. It’s doing things backwards, like trying to move on by stalking your ex's new profile. 'Bakit mo isinasaliwa ang pagsuot ng sapatos mo?'
usage_notes: Can mean literally backwards/reversed, or figuratively going against the norm or doing something incorrectly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **isaliwa** ang proseso; sundin mo ang mga hakbang.","translation":"Don't **do** the process **in reverse**; follow the steps."},{"sentence":"Tila **isinasaliwa** niya ang lahat ng payo na binibigay sa kanya.","translation":"It seems he is **doing the opposite** of all the advice given to him."}]

translation: the manner/act of having shown or released
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng matagumpay na pagpapalabas o pagtatanghal ng isang bagay, tulad ng pelikula, palabas, o anunsyo.
etymology: From the root 'labas' (out), with affixes 'pagka-' and 'pagpa-' indicating the manner of causing something to come out or be shown.
original_explanation: The way a movie was released or a show was produced. Think of the MMFF (Metro Manila Film Festival). You'd talk about the 'pagkakapagpalabas' of a film—was it a blockbuster? Was the premiere night a success? It's the post-mortem on a public release or performance.
usage_notes: Refers to the circumstances, quality, or result of a showing, release, or performance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-usapan ang naging magarbong **pagkakapagpalabas** ng bagong pelikula.","translation":"The grand **manner of release** of the new movie was talked about."},{"sentence":"Inaasahan ng lahat ang **pagkakapagpalabas** ng susunod na episode ng serye.","translation":"Everyone is anticipating the **act of releasing** the next episode of the series."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na naglalagay ng mga mensaheng nakakagalit, mapanukso, o walang katuturan sa isang online na komunidad upang pukawin ang emosyonal na reaksyon o guluhin ang usapan.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga professional basher sa Facebook at YouTube comments section. Bayad man o for fun, trabaho nilang mang-inis, magkalat ng fake news, at sirain ang araw mo. The keyboard warriors you love to hate. Don't feed the trolls!
usage_notes: Exclusively used in the modern internet context. Not to be confused with the mythological creature, although the behavior can be monstrous.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang patulan 'yan, halatang **troll** lang ang kausap mo.","translation":"Don't engage with that anymore, it's obvious you're just talking to a **troll**."},{"sentence":"Maraming **troll** ang nag-comment sa post ng sikat na artista.","translation":"A lot of **trolls** commented on the famous artist's post."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng mataas na paggalang at pagtingin sa isang tao o bagay dahil sa mga katangian, nagawa, o kagandahan nito.
original_explanation: It's that feeling you get when you see your crush walking down the hallway in slow motion. It's what you feel for a K-Pop idol, a brilliant professor, or someone who can perfectly park their car in one go. It's respect mixed with a little bit of awe, the "sana all" feeling but in a good way.
usage_notes: A very common word for expressing positive feelings of respect and approval.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko maitago ang aking **paghanga** sa kanyang talento.","translation":"I cannot hide my **admiration** for his/her talent."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **paghanga** ay unti-unting naging pag-ibig.","translation":"His/Her **admiration** slowly turned into love."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mapagkumbaba, hindi mayabang, at may paggalang sa kapwa anuman ang katayuan sa buhay.
etymology: A compound word from 'mababa' (low) and 'loob' (inner self, will). Literally 'low inner self,' but contextually means humility, not low self-esteem.
original_explanation: The opposite of a 'flexer.' This is that person who's super successful but still eats at the carinderia, says 'po' and 'opo' to elders, and doesn't need to post their achievements 24/7. It's the ultimate green flag. True power doesn't need to announce itself.
usage_notes: A highly valued Filipino trait. 'Mapagkumbaba' is a very close synonym. The antonym is 'mayabang' or 'mapagmataas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit sikat na siyang artista, nananatili siyang **mababang-loob**.","translation":"Even though he is now a famous artist, he remains **humble**."},{"sentence":"Isang lider na **mababang-loob** ang hinahanap ng karamihan.","translation":"The majority are looking for a **humble** leader."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagputol o paghiwalay ng ulo mula sa katawan.
original_explanation: This is what happens in historical dramas or horror movies when someone gets *really* mad. It's the ultimate 'cancel culture' before social media. Not to be confused with just getting fired from a job, this is... way more final.
usage_notes: Madalas itong gamitin kasama ang pariralang 'ng ulo' (e.g., pumugot ng ulo). Ang pandiwa mismo ay nagpapahiwatig ng pagputol ng isang bagay sa bandang leeg o puno nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang madilim na kabanata ng kasaysayan, **pumugot** ng ulo ng mga kaaway ang mga mandirigma.","translation":"In a dark chapter of history, the warriors **beheaded** their enemies."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi naman literal na **pumugot** ng ulo ang boss mo, pinagalitan ka lang.","translation":"Don't worry, your boss didn't literally **decapitate** you, he just scolded you."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang pagkain, sustansya, o gawain na nakadaragdag sa timbang o taba ng katawan. Sa agrikultura, ito ay pataba para sa lupa.
original_explanation: Ah, the delicious enemies of your diet plan. Lechon, crispy pata, sisig, cake, ice cream... lahat ng masasarap! It's the food you eat when you're sad, happy, celebrating, or just bored. Your tita's favorite comment about you is probably, "Uy, tumataba ka! Anong kinakain mong pampataba?"
usage_notes: Can refer to food for humans or feed for animals. A different but related word, 'pataba', is used for fertilizer, but 'pampataba' can also be used in that context (e.g., pampataba ng lupa).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniiwasan niya ang mga pagkaing **pampataba** dahil nagda-diet siya.","translation":"She avoids **fattening** foods because she is on a diet."},{"sentence":"Ang kanin at matatamis na pagkain ay mabisang **pampataba**.","translation":"Rice and sweet foods are effective for **gaining weight**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtapak o pag-apakan nang may puwersa, na madalas gamitin sa metaporikal na paraan para sa paglapastangan o paglabag sa isang bagay na sagrado o mahalaga.
original_explanation: Pagyurak is what happens when you step on something, not by accident, but with feeling. But on a 'teleserye' level, it's used for abstract things. Pagyurak sa puso (trampling on a heart), pagyurak sa dangal (desecrating honor). The most famous combo is 'pagyurak sa katarungan' (trampling on justice), which is basically the plot of every Filipino revenge movie.
usage_notes: Most commonly heard in the phrase "pagyurak sa katarungan" (trampling on justice) or "pagyurak sa karapatan" (violating rights).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ginawa niyang panloloko ay isang **pagyurak** sa tiwalang ibinigay ko.","translation":"His deception was a **trampling** on the trust I gave."},{"sentence":"Kinondena ng mga mamamayan ang **pagyurak** sa katarungan na nangyari.","translation":"The citizens condemned the **violation of justice** that occurred."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-eempleyo o paglalapat ng isang bagay para sa isang partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your phone 24/7. It's also what your parents accuse you of when they say 'Puro ka na lang paggamit ng selpon!' Also refers to how you 'use' your brain during an exam, or how you 'use' your 'diskarte' to get the last piece of chicken joy.
usage_notes: A very general and widely used word. Can be paired with other words to specify, e.g., 'paggamit ng dahas' (use of violence).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tamang **paggamit** ng pera ay mahalagang matutunan.","translation":"The proper **use** of money is important to learn."},{"sentence":"Limitahan ang **paggamit** ng mga plastic na bagay.","translation":"Limit the **usage** of plastic things."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tanyag na Pilipinong multinational na kadena ng mga fast-food restaurant na pag-aari ng Jollibee Foods Corporation.
etymology: Isang portmanteau ng "jolly" at "bee," na nilikha ng nagtatag nito upang katawanin ang masayahin at masipag na katangian ng mga Pilipino.
original_explanation: More than just a fast-food chain, Jollibee is a cultural icon, a national treasure, and the Philippines' unofficial mascot. It's the taste of childhood birthday parties, the go-to "pasalubong" from the city, and the cure for homesickness for OFWs. The eternal rivalry with McDonald's is a national sport. You don't just eat at Jollibee; you experience a core part of being Filipino.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the brand. Often used as a landmark ("Sa may Jollibee, tapat ng simbahan").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng Chickenjoy at Jolly Spaghetti galing sa **Jollibee**.","translation":"I want Chickenjoy and Jolly Spaghetti from **Jollibee**."},{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **Jollibee** sa kanto mamayang alas-sais.","translation":"Let's meet at the **Jollibee** on the corner later at six."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga sandata na partikular na idinisenyo at ginagamit para sa mga operasyong militar o ng hukbo.
original_explanation: The kind of heavy-duty hardware you see in action movies or Call of Duty. Think assault rifles, tanks, and grenades—not the 'itak' your lolo keeps in the backyard. These are weapons specifically for the military.
usage_notes: Isang tiyak na kategorya ng mga sandata.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakumpiska ang mga awtoridad ng mga ilegal na **sandatang panghukbo**.","translation":"The authorities confiscated illegal **military weapons**."},{"sentence":"Ang paggawa ng **sandatang panghukbo** ay isang mahigpit na kinokontrol na industriya.","translation":"The manufacturing of **military weapons** is a strictly controlled industry."}]

meaning_filipino: Iniluto sa pamamagitan ng paglubog sa mainit na mantika.
etymology: From Spanish 'frito' (fried). The spelling often gets Filipinized to 'pirito' or 'prito'.
original_explanation: The default setting for most Filipino food. Isda? Pirito. Manok? Pirito. Itlog? Pirito. Galunggong? Pambansang ulam 'yan, basta pirito!
usage_notes: 'Prito' is the more common and standard spelling, but 'pirito' is widely used in spoken language and informal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang **pirito** na manok kapag bagong luto.","translation":"**Fried** chicken is delicious when newly cooked."},{"sentence":"Nag-ulam kami ng **pirito** na tilapya at kanin.","translation":"We had **fried** tilapia and rice for our meal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-imprenta at pagpapakalat ng mga aklat, pahayagan, o anumang babasahin para sa kaalaman ng publiko.
original_explanation: Before social media 'posts', this was the OG way to go viral. You write something—a book, a poem, or even some juicy chismis—and convince a company to print and sell it. It's like asking your friend with a huge following to 'share' your content, but with ink and paper.
usage_notes: This verb implies causing something to be published, often by submitting it to a publishing house or newspaper.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang **magpalathala** ng sarili niyang nobela balang araw.","translation":"It's her dream to **publish** her own novel someday."},{"sentence":"Nagsumite siya ng isang artikulo sa diyaryo upang **magpalathala**.","translation":"He submitted an article to the newspaper to **have it published**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panginginig ng katawan dahil sa ginaw, takot, o lagnat.
etymology: From pang- + kiki (obsolete word for shudder).
original_explanation: Yung feeling na nanonood ka ng horror movie mag-isa tapos biglang may kumaluskos sa labas. O kaya yung moment na kakatapos mo lang maligo ng malamig na tubig tapos nakalimutan mo yung tuwalya mo sa kwarto. Yan ang pangiki!
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with panginginig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **pangiki** sa buong katawan habang naghihintay sa resulta ng exam.","translation":"She felt a **trembling** all over her body while waiting for the exam results."}]

translation: Smelling of soil (euphemism for being very old)
meaning_filipino: Isang matalinghagang paglalarawan sa isang taong napakatanda na at ipinapalagay na malapit nang mamatay.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'boomer' roast, but for the generation even before them. It literally means 'smells like soil,' a not-so-subtle way of saying someone has one foot in the grave. You might hear this whispered about a very, very old relative who's seen it all. It’s dark humor, Pinoy style. 'Malapit na sa finish line.'
usage_notes: Isang eupemismo na maaaring ituring na bastos o nakakatawa depende sa konteksto at sa relasyon ng nagsasalita at ng pinatutungkulan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biro ng apo, \"Lolo, **amoy-lupa** ka na raw sabi nila, pero malakas ka pa sa kalabaw!\"","translation":"The grandchild joked, \"Grandpa, they say you're already **smelling of the earth**, but you're still stronger than a water buffalo!\""},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang bisyo mo, hindi ka pa naman **amoy-lupa**.","translation":"Stop your vices, you're not that **old and near death** yet."}]

meaning_filipino: Lilinisin pa lamang ang mga ngipin sa hinaharap gamit ang sipilyo at toothpaste.
original_explanation: The future tense of dental hygiene. It's the "I promise I'll do it later" version of brushing your teeth. Your mom: "Anak, magsipilyo ka na!" You: "Mamaya po, **magsisipilyo** ako pagkatapos ng episode na 'to."
usage_notes: This is the future tense of 'magsipilyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos kong kumain, ako ay **magsisipilyo**.","translation":"After I eat, I **will brush my teeth**."},{"sentence":"**Magsisipilyo** muna ako bago tayo umalis.","translation":"I **will brush my teeth** first before we leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi o paglalagay ng alinlangan sa isipan ng isang tao.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative prefix) + `pag-` + `duda` (doubt) + `-hin` (object focus suffix). `Duda` is from Spanish 'duda'.
original_explanation: This is what fake news and 'Marites' do for a living. They plant a seed of 'hala, totoo kaya?' in your brain. When someone makes you question everything you thought was true, 'yan 'yun, gusto ka nilang **papagdudahin**.
usage_notes: A causative verb indicating the act of making someone feel doubt or suspicion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **papagdudahin** ang sarili mo sa iyong kakayahan.","translation":"Don't **make yourself doubt** your own abilities."},{"sentence":"Ang mga kumakalat na tsismis ay sapat na para **papagdudahin** ang sinuman.","translation":"The spreading rumors are enough to **make anyone doubt**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikas o pag-alis mula sa isang lugar na may panganib o sakuna patungo sa isang mas ligtas na lokasyon.
original_explanation: When the volcano starts acting up or the floodwaters are rising faster than your utang, it's time to 'bumakwit'. It's the Pinoy term for 'evacuate', derived from the English word itself. Think of it as a forced, unplanned 'bakasyon' you didn't ask for, usually ending up in a crowded gym or school.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of natural disasters (typhoons, volcanic eruptions) or armed conflict.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangang **bumakwit** ng buong barangay dahil sa pagbaha.","translation":"The entire village had to **evacuate** because of the flood."},{"sentence":"Naghahanda na silang **bumakwit** bago pa man dumating ang bagyo.","translation":"They are already preparing to **evacuate** even before the typhoon arrives."}]

translation: to frisk for something; to search for a specific item by frisking
meaning_filipino: Hanapin ang isang partikular na bagay sa katawan o damit ng isang tao sa pamamagitan ng pagkapkap.
original_explanation: Very similar to 'kapkapan', but 'kapkapin' often implies you're looking for a *specific* thing. While 'kapkapan' focuses on the person being searched, 'kapkapin' focuses on the thing being searched for. 'Kapkapan mo si Juan' (Frisk Juan). 'Kapkapin mo ang kutsilyo kay Juan' (Frisk Juan for the knife). Subtle, but it's there.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb where the object is the thing being looked for. Can sometimes be used interchangeably with 'kapkapan' in casual speech, but the distinction is useful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **kapkapin** ang wallet sa bulsa ko.","translation":"He tried to **search for and grab** the wallet in my pocket."},{"sentence":"**Kapkapin** mo ang susi sa lahat ng bulsa niya.","translation":"**Search** for the key in all his pockets by patting him down."}]

translation: to be ripped open; to be torn
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng malaking punit o butas dahil sa marahas na paghila o pagpwersa.
original_explanation: Think of a bag of chips that you opened with too much rage, or your favorite jeans finally giving up at the seams after one too many samgyupsal nights. It's a tear, but with more drama.
usage_notes: Implies a forceful and often sudden tearing, more severe than 'mapunit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mong huwag **mapuknat** ang sako ng bigas.","translation":"Be careful not **to rip open** the sack of rice."},{"sentence":"Sa lakas ng hangin, muntik nang **mapuknat** ang aming tolda.","translation":"With the strength of the wind, our tent almost got **torn**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit sa paghahambing na nagsasabing ang isang bagay ay may sukat o kantidad na hindi kasinlaki ng pinaghahambingan.
original_explanation: The standard way to say something is 'smaller' in Tagalog. It's what you say when you get your online order and the item is not what you expected. 'Sa picture, malaki tingnan, pero sa personal, **mas maliit** pala.' It's also what your salary feels like compared to your bills.
usage_notes: The structure `mas` + adjective is the most common way to form the comparative degree in Filipino. The superlative is `pinakamaliit` (smallest).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bahay namin ay **mas maliit** kaysa sa bahay nila.","translation":"Our house is **smaller** than their house."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko sana ng damit na **mas maliit** ng isang sukat dito.","translation":"I would like a dress that is one size **smaller** than this."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtataas ng kamay laban sa isang tao bilang tanda ng pananakit o pagbabanta, na kasalukuyang ginagawa.
etymology: Mula sa "pinag-", pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng ugat ("bu-"), "buhat", at "-an".
original_explanation: The present tense of 'pagbuhatan ng kamay'. This is what's happening when someone is about to get a 'sampal' or 'batok'. It's the moment before the physical drama unfolds. 'Wag mo akong pagbubuhatan ng kamay!' is the classic teleserye line.
usage_notes: Halos palaging ginagamit sa pariralang "pinagbubuhatan ng kamay," na nangangahulugang pagbabanta ng pisikal na pananakit. Ito ay nasa anyong pangkasalukuyan na nagpapatuloy (present progressive).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag na huwag mo akong **pagbubuhatan** ng kamay!","translation":"Don't you ever **raise** a hand **against** me!"},{"sentence":"Nakita niya kung paano **pinagbubuhatan** ng kamay ng ama ang kanyang anak.","translation":"She saw how the father **was raising** his hand against his child."}]

meaning_filipino: May taglay na kapangyarihan, awtoridad, o impluwensya na makapagpasunod o makapagpabago ng mga pangyayari.
etymology: From naka- + pangyayari (event, happening), but in this context, it derives its meaning from kapangyarihan (power), which is also from the root yari (to make, to finish).
original_explanation: This is the "May I speak to the manager?" energy, but you ARE the manager. 'Yung HR na may hawak ng payroll. 'Yung lola na isang tingin lang, titino na lahat ng apo. They hold the power.
usage_notes: Describes a person, entity, or force that holds power or authority.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangulo ng bansa ang siyang pinaka-**nakapangyayari** sa sangay ng ehekutibo.","translation":"The country's president is the most **powerful** in the executive branch."},{"sentence":"Isang **nakapangyayari** na korporasyon ang bumili sa maliit na kumpanya.","translation":"A **powerful** corporation bought the small company."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagdidikta ng mga salita upang isulat ng iba; sa kontekstong politikal, isang pinunong may ganap at absolutong kapangyarihan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "tagapag-" (doer/agent of action) at sa salitang hiram na "dikta" (dictate).
original_explanation: The original "seen-zoner." They give the orders, you just follow. In an office setting, it's that old-school boss who makes their secretary type everything they say. In a bigger picture... well, history books have chapters on them.
usage_notes: Bagama't maaaring literal na tumukoy sa isang taong nagdidikta para sa pagtatala, mas madalas itong ginagamit sa negatibong konotasyong politikal, katulad ng "diktador."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa kasaysayan, ang bansa ay minsang pinamunuan ng isang **tagapagdikta**.","translation":"According to history, the country was once ruled by a **dictator**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha na isasagawa pa lamang sa hinaharap; pamanahong panghinaharap ng pandiwang 'kumuha'.
etymology: Future tense verb conjugation of 'kuha', formed by repeating the first syllable of the root word.
original_explanation: The future tense of 'get'. It's the promise you make before going to the store: '**Kukuha** ako ng bigas.' (I will get rice.) It's the threat your mom gives you: '**Kukuha** ako ng tsinelas!' (I will get the slipper!). It's the sound of future actions, whether a blessing or a warning.
usage_notes: This is the future tense, actor-focus ('um-' verb) form of the root 'kuha'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **kukuha** ng mga bata sa eskuwela mamaya?","translation":"Who **will get** the kids from school later?"},{"sentence":"**Kukuha** ako ng kursong engineering sa kolehiyo.","translation":"I **will take** an engineering course in college."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magdulot ng pinsala sa katawan na nagreresulta sa pagkasira ng balat; o magbigay ng matinding sakit sa damdamin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "sugat" (sugat) at panlaping -um-.
original_explanation: Can be a physical "ouch" like a papercut, or a metaphorical "ouch" like when your crush says "friends lang tayo." It's the verb for everything that leaves a mark, whether on your skin or your heart. The national verb of the Hugot Generation.
usage_notes: Anyong pangnagdaan. Maaaring gamitin sa literal o matalinhagang paraan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bubog na natapakan niya ay **sumugat** sa kanyang talampakan.","translation":"The piece of glass he stepped on **wounded** the sole of his foot."},{"sentence":"Ang masasakit na salitang binitawan niya ay labis na **sumugat** sa aking damdamin.","translation":"The harsh words he uttered deeply **hurt** my feelings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at mabilog na prutas na may luntiang balat na may mga guhit, at matamis at matubig na pulang laman na may mga buto.
etymology: From Hokkien 卜柑 (pó͘-koaⁿ), literally 'to divine tangerine'.
original_explanation: The official fruit of Filipino summer outings and fiestas. Best served chilled after a long swim at the beach. Pro-tip: Sprinkle a little salt on it to bring out the sweetness. Don't you dare eat the white part.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasarap kumain ng malamig na **pakwan** kapag tag-init.","translation":"It's so delicious to eat cold **watermelon** during the summer."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang buong **pakwan** sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a whole **watermelon** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng pagiging gising at may kaalaman sa sarili at sa kapaligiran; pagkabatid o pagkaunawa sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: That "woke" state. It's what you gain when you realize your toxic trait, or when you finally understand the political situation of the country. It's the opposite of being "marupok" or "dedma." It's your brain's software finally booting up.
usage_notes: Often used in social, political, or psychological contexts, e.g., 'kamalayang panlipunan' (social consciousness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang pagkakaroon ng **kamalayan** sa mga isyung panlipunan.","translation":"Having **awareness** of social issues is important."},{"sentence":"Nawalan siya ng **kamalayan** matapos maaksidente.","translation":"She lost **consciousness** after the accident."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o kalagayan ng hindi pagpapakita ng respeto o pagkilala sa karapatan, damdamin, o awtoridad ng iba.
etymology: Mula sa `pagka-` (estado o akto ng) + `walang galang` (walang respeto). Isang tambalang pangngalan.
original_explanation: Talking back to your elders, interrupting someone mid-sentence, using your phone while someone's talking to you—lahat 'yan forms of `pagkawalang-galang`. It's the "bastos" behavior. On social media, this is your everyday troll leaving hateful comments. It's the absence of "po" and "opo" when it's expected.
usage_notes: Isang mabigat na salita na nagpapahiwatig ng paglabag sa kagandahang-asal o respeto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **pagkawalang-galang** ang hindi pagtayo habang inaawit ang pambansang awit.","translation":"It is a great **disrespect** not to stand while the national anthem is being sung."},{"sentence":"Pinarusahan ang estudyante dahil sa kanyang **pagkawalang-galang** sa guro.","translation":"The student was punished for his **irreverence** towards the teacher."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang kawayan o patpat na may kawit o panungkit sa dulo, ginagamit sa pagkuha ng mga prutas o bagay na nasa mataas na lugar.
etymology: From salo (to catch) + sungkit (to pick with a hook/pole).
original_explanation: The official tool for ninja-level mango and santol harvesting from your neighbor's tree (kidding!). It's the low-tech, probinsya-style drone for fruit delivery. If you know how to use this, you've had a legit Filipino childhood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit si tatay ng **salungkit** para makuha ang mga hinog na mangga.","translation":"Father used a **hooked pole** to get the ripe mangoes."},{"sentence":"Masyadong mataas, kailangan natin ng mas mahabang **salungkit**.","translation":"It's too high, we need a longer **hooked pole**."}]

meaning_filipino: Maistorbo o magambala ang katahimikan o pagpapahinga dahil sa malakas na ingay o biglaang gulo.
etymology: From ma- (ability/accidental verb prefix) + bulahaw (loud noise, disturbance).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung tulog na tulog ka na tapos biglang may magvi-videoke sa kapitbahay ng 1 AM. O 'yung nasa kalagitnaan ka ng importanteng Zoom meeting tapos dumaan 'yung nagtitinda ng "Taho!". Ayun, na-mabulahaw ka.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to disturbance caused by noise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **mabulahaw** ang mga natutulog kaya dahan-dahan akong pumasok.","translation":"I didn't want to **disturb** the sleeping people, so I entered slowly."},{"sentence":"Na-**mabulahaw** ang buong klase sa biglang pagtunog ng fire alarm.","translation":"The whole class was **startled** by the sudden ringing of the fire alarm."}]

translation: a greeting session; an exchange of 'how are yous'
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalitan ng mga pagbati o pagtatanong tungkol sa kalagayan ng isa't isa.
etymology: From Spanish "cómo está". The suffix "-han" denotes a place or a reciprocal action.
original_explanation: Ito yung nangyayari sa mga reunion. Akala mo matatapos agad, pero aabutin kayo ng siyam-siyam dahil bawat tita at tito, kailangan i-update sa life story mo. Parang group chat in real life, pero may kasamang pisil sa pisngi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng mahabang **kumustahan** ang magkakaibigan pagkatapos ng maraming taon.","translation":"The friends had a long **greeting session** after many years."},{"sentence":"Ang Pasko ay panahon ng masayang **kumustahan** ng pamilya.","translation":"Christmas is a time for the family's happy **exchange of greetings**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, lalo na isang kabataan, na may tendensiyang gumawa ng mga maliliit na krimen o labag sa batas na gawain.
original_explanation: The "pasaway" of the barangay. Sila yung mga kabataang laging nasasangkot sa gulo, tambay sa kanto hanggang madaling araw, at sakit ng ulo ng mga magulang at tanod. The term sounds formal, but it's what your tita calls the neighbor's kid who's always in trouble.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga kabataang lumalabag sa batas o may mga anti-social na pag-uugali.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming programa ang gobyerno para tulungan ang mga kabataang **delingkuwente**.","translation":"The government has many programs to help juvenile **delinquents**."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing siyang **delingkuwente** dahil sa kanyang madalas na pakikipag-away.","translation":"He is considered a **delinquent** because of his frequent involvement in fights."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpasan o paglalagay ng isang bagay sa ibabaw ng ulo upang dalhin ito mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: Before backpacks and delivery apps, this was the ultimate hands-free technique. You see this in provinces where people carry baskets of fish or produce on their heads with incredible balance. It's a skill that requires a strong neck and zero trust issues with gravity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kaya pa rin ng lola na **magsunong** ng isang bayong ng gulay.","translation":"Grandma can still **carry a basket** of vegetables on her head."},{"sentence":"Sanay siyang **magsunong** ng banga na puno ng tubig.","translation":"She is used to **carrying a jar** full of water on her head."}]

translation: to cook rice by toasting then boiling
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagluto ng bigas sa pamamagitan ng bahagyang pagsasangag nito sa mantika o taba bago ito sabawan at pakuluan hanggang maluto.
original_explanation: This is the OG way to level up your kanin. Before rice cookers, there was sigang. You toast the rice grains in a bit of oil (maybe with some garlic, if you're feeling fancy) until they're golden, then add water and boil. The result? A nutty, slightly crispy-bottomed rice that's 100x better than your sad, plain steamed rice. It's the 'extra effort' rice.
usage_notes: A specific cooking technique. The resulting rice is often called 'sinangag', but 'sigang' is the act of cooking it this way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuruan ako ng lola ko kung paano mag-**sigang** ng kanin.","translation":"My grandmother taught me how **to cook rice by toasting it first**."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang bahaw kapag i-**sinigang** mo muna.","translation":"Leftover rice is more delicious if you **toast it first**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na tumutukoy sa isang tao na nasa ilalim ng impluwensya ng ipinagbabawal na gamot, o sa isang taong may magulo at hindi maayos na itsura dahil sa pagod o puyat.
etymology: Colloquial, likely derived from 'shabu' (methamphetamine), used to describe the appearance of a user, but has since broadened its meaning.
original_explanation: The look you have after pulling an all-nighter for a final exam, or after a 12-hour shift, or... well, the other thing. It’s when your hair is a mess, your eyes are barely open, and you look like you just fought a washing machine and lost. "Haggard" on a whole new level.
usage_notes: While it originates from drug culture slang, it's now more commonly used to mean extremely tired, stressed, or messy in appearance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe, mukha na akong **shabog** sa dami ng trabaho.","translation":"Wow, I look so **disheveled** from so much work."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang lumabas na ganyan ang itsura, para kang **shabog**!","translation":"Don't go out looking like that, you look like a total **mess**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pang-uri, nangangahulugang naisakatuparan o nagawa. Bilang pangalan, ito ay ang akto o kalagayan ng pagsasakatuparan ng isang pangako, utos, o plano.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *tepad, meaning 'to accomplish' or 'to arrive'.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'drawing'. When you say you'll do something and you actually do it, that's 'tupad'. It’s fulfilling a promise to your jowa, meeting a deadline for your boss, or finally achieving your #SanaAll travel goals. It's the satisfaction of a checked-off to-do list item.
usage_notes: Most commonly used in verb forms like 'tumupad' (to fulfill), 'tuparin' (to fulfill something), and 'matupad' (to be fulfilled). As a noun/adjective, it's often part of a phrase like 'tupad sa pangako'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **matupad** ang lahat ng iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"I hope all your dreams get **fulfilled**."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang taong **tupad** sa kanyang mga salita.","translation":"He is known as a person who is **true** to his words (fulfills his promises)."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtulong sa kapwa ay isang **tupad** sa ating tungkulin.","translation":"Helping others is a **fulfillment** of our duty."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging magkarugtong o magkasugpong ng dalawa o higit pang bagay, na tila ba iisang tanikala.
etymology: From `mag-` + `ka-` (denoting a pair or group) + `kawing` (link, chain).
original_explanation: Parang history ng chat n'yo ng ex mo at 'yung mga utang mo sa G-Cash, lahat yan magkakawing sa desisyon mong mag-abroad. It's the 'it's complicated' status of events, where one thing is connected to another.
usage_notes: Often used to describe abstract connections like events, ideas, or fates.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kahirapan at kawalan ng edukasyon ay mga problemang **magkakawing**.","translation":"Poverty and lack of education are **intertwined** problems."},{"sentence":"Hawak-kamay silang naglakad, ang kanilang mga braso ay **magkakawing**.","translation":"They walked hand-in-hand, their arms **linked**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng nuwes na nagmumula sa puno ng Pili (Canarium ovatum), na karaniwang matatagpuan sa rehiyon ng Bicol.
etymology: Mula sa puno ng Pili (Canarium ovatum).
original_explanation: That buttery, tear-drop shaped nut from Bicol na masarap gawing pasalubong. It's the region's pride, often coated in honey or sugar. Medyo pricey, parang pag-ibig, pero worth it.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mismong nuwes o sa puno nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong pasalubong mula sa Bicol ang matamis na **pili**.","translation":"My favorite souvenir from Bicol is the sweet **pili nut**."}]

translation: to be able to lift or raise up
meaning_filipino: Magawang itaas o iangat ang isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito.
etymology: From Spanish 'alzar' (to raise). The 'ma-i-' prefix denotes ability.
original_explanation: That feeling of victory when you finally **maialsa** the heavy-ass galon ng tubig onto the dispenser without spilling a drop. Or when your team leader manages to raise the team's morale after a bad week. It's about lifting something, whether it's physical or metaphorical, like spirits or a protest banner.
usage_notes: Can be literal (lifting an object) or figurative (raising a status, a protest, a spirit).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya **maialsa** ang mabigat na sako ng bigas.","translation":"He could not **lift** the heavy sack of rice."},{"sentence":"Layunin ng kilusan na **maialsa** ang antas ng pamumuhay ng mga maralita.","translation":"The movement's goal is to **raise** the standard of living of the poor."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang sistema o paraan ng pamumuno na may ganap na kapangyarihan ang isang tao.
original_explanation: The management style of the 'autokrat'. It's when your dad says, 'Habang nakatira ka sa bahay ko, ako ang masusunod.' That's an 'autokratik' household rule. In the office, it's the 'my way or the highway' approach. No questions, no suggestions, just follow.
usage_notes: Formal term used to describe a style, system, or personality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming empleyado ang hindi masaya sa kanyang **autokratik** na pamamalakad.","translation":"Many employees are unhappy with his **autocratic** management style."},{"sentence":"Ang isang **autokratik** na gobyerno ay bihirang tumatanggap ng pagpuna.","translation":"An **autocratic** government rarely accepts criticism."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang solidong bagay na naging likido dahil sa init; pagiging-halo ng isang sangkap sa isang likido; pagproseso ng pagkain sa tiyan.
original_explanation: What happens to your ice cream on a hot day. What happens to the sugar in your coffee. Also, what your food becomes after you eat it (`tunaw sa tiyan`). Metaphorically, it's how you feel after a long, exhausting day at work or after listening to your crush say "I love you... as a friend." Just completely melted into a puddle of feelings.
usage_notes: Can be a state (adjective) or the result of an action (verb form: 'natunaw').
