usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang matagalan sa labas ang ice cream at baka maging **tunaw**.","translation":"Don't leave the ice cream outside for too long or it might get **melted**."},{"sentence":"Hintayin mong **tunaw** na ang asukal bago mo inumin ang kape.","translation":"Wait for the sugar to be **dissolved** before you drink the coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang maganda; sukdulan sa ganda; kaakit-akit sa pinakamataas na antas.
etymology: From Tagalog 'maganda' (beautiful). The repetition of the adjective, linked by '-ng', serves to intensify the meaning to 'very beautiful'.
original_explanation: This is the 'sana all' level of beauty. It's not just 'maganda,' it's 'magandang-maganda'—like that one crush you had in high school who seemed to glow under fluorescent lights, or the perfect sunset pic that needs no filter. It's the highest praise for beauty, used for everything from a person to a view to a perfectly cooked piece of lechon.
usage_notes: The repetition of an adjective with '-ng' or 'na' in between is a common way to intensify its meaning in Tagalog (e.g., 'mabait na mabait' for 'very kind').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magandang-maganda** ang tanawin mula sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"The view from the top of the mountain is **very beautiful**."},{"sentence":"Wow, **magandang-maganda** ka sa suot mong 'yan!","translation":"Wow, you look **absolutely gorgeous** in that outfit!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, koponan, o hayop na nagwagi at napatunayang pinakamahusay sa isang kumpetisyon o labanan.
original_explanation: The G.O.A.T. The winner. The one who gets the trophy, the medal, and the bragging rights. Whether it's Manny Pacquiao in boxing, Hidilyn Diaz in weightlifting, or you in your local barangay's karaoke contest, if you're number one, you are the **kampeon**. It's the ultimate 'Sana All' moment in any competition.
usage_notes: Can also be spelled 'kampiyon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang itinanghal na **kampeon** sa paligsahan sa pag-awit.","translation":"She was declared the **champion** in the singing competition."},{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang ng buong bansa ang pagkapanalo ng kanilang pambansang **kampeon**.","translation":"The whole country is celebrating the victory of their national **champion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng katawan ng isda kung saan matatagpuan ang bibig, mata, at hasang.
etymology: Possibly related to the other 'una' meaning first/front.
original_explanation: The best part of the Sinigang na Isda for many titos and dads. While others fight for the body, the true connoisseur knows the flavor is in the una. It's the fish head, full of flavorful fat and succulent meat if you know where to look. "Sa'yo na ang katawan, akin ang una."
usage_notes: Primarily refers to the head of a fish, but can be used metaphorically for the front or leading part of something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap sipsipin ang **una** ng isda sa sinigang.","translation":"It's delicious to slurp the **head** of the fish in sinigang."},{"sentence":"Inalis niya ang **una** at buntot bago iprito ang isda.","translation":"She removed the **head** and tail before frying the fish."}]

meaning_filipino: Lalaking mangkukulam o manggagaway; ang katumbas na lalaki ng isang bruha.
original_explanation: The guy version of a 'bruha'. Think of him as the dude who knows all the cheat codes for life, but like, the dark magic kind. He's the one you go to when you want to put a 'kulang' on your ex's new jowa, but you're too scared to ask your Tita who reads tarot cards.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'mangkukulam'. While 'bruha' is more common, 'bruho' is its direct male counterpart.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsasabihan siyang **bruho** dahil sa kanyang mga kakaibang kakayahan.","translation":"They call him a **warlock** because of his strange abilities."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa sinasabi ng **bruho** na iyan.","translation":"Don't believe what that **sorcerer** is saying."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman ang ginhawa; ang pagbuti ng kalagayan mula sa hirap, sakit, o bigat ng damdamin.
original_explanation: That feeling after you finally submit a project after a week of puyat. Or when the aircon is finally fixed in the middle of summer. It’s the "Haaay, salamat!" moment of your life. The opposite of being "gipit".
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense) of the verb. It refers to a transition into a state of comfort or ease.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **guminhawa** ang aking paghinga matapos uminom ng gamot.","translation":"I felt my breathing **become easier** after taking the medicine."},{"sentence":"Nang manalo siya sa lotto, **guminhawa** ang buhay ng kanyang buong pamilya.","translation":"When he won the lottery, the life of his whole family **became comfortable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsisiksik o pagiging siksik at pipi dahil sa pagpuno nang labis sa isang lalagyan.
original_explanation: This is the state of your balikbayan box after you've sat on it just to close it. It's the ulam in your baunan that has been squished by the rice on top. It's the feeling of being in the MRT during rush hour. Anything that's been stuffed so much it becomes flat and dense. 'Pilpil na ang damit sa maleta.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe things inside a container, like food or clothes. Can be used as a verb 'pilpilin' (to stuff/compress).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **pilpil** ang kanin sa baunan dahil sa pagkakadiin.","translation":"The rice in the container became **compressed** because it was pressed down."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panawag-pansin o pagpapahayag ng damdamin na katumbas ng "Hoy!" o "Hey!" sa Ingles.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish 'oye' (listen) or a native exclamation.
original_explanation: The ultimate multi-tool of Filipino interjections. It can mean "Hey, you!", "What the heck?!", "Come here," or "Stop that!" The meaning is 99% in the tone. A soft "Oy, kamusta?" is a friendly greeting. A sharp "Oy!" from your mom means you're in trouble. It's a whole conversation in one syllable.
usage_notes: A less aggressive version of "Hoy!". Its meaning is heavily dependent on tone and context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Oy**! Pst! Halika dito.","translation":"**Hey**! Pst! Come here."},{"sentence":"**Oy**, ano ba 'yan? Ingat naman.","translation":"**Hey**, what was that? Be careful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagpepreserba ng pagkain, lalo na ng karne o isda, sa pamamagitan ng pagpapatuyo nito sa init ng araw o sa usok.
etymology: From i- (causative verb prefix) + tapa (cured meat).
original_explanation: This is the OG food preservation technique before refrigerators were a thing. It’s the process that gives us the glorious breakfast food, Tapa. So when you "itapa ang karne," you're essentially starting the journey to a delicious tapsilog. It's the art of making something last, whether it's beef or fish (tinapa).
usage_notes: Refers to the process of curing, usually by smoking or sun-drying, to make 'tapa' (cured meat) or 'tinapa' (smoked fish).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matutong **itapa** ang isda para hindi ito masira kaagad.","translation":"Learn to **cure** the fish so it won't spoil quickly."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang karneng baboy kapag **itinapa** at tinimplahan ng bawang.","translation":"Pork is delicious when it is **cured** and seasoned with garlic."}]

translation: to be able to serve; to be able to offer as a service
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang magbigay ng serbisyo o tulong sa kapwa, sa bayan, o sa isang organisasyon.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "How may I help you?" vibe, but on a deeper level. It's not just for customer service reps; it's for anyone who wants to offer their skills or time for a cause. "Anong talent ang **maipaglingkod** mo sa ating community pantry?" It’s about giving back.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or patriotic contexts, related to public service or volunteerism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anuman ang aking munting kaalaman ay handa kong **maipaglingkod** sa bayan.","translation":"Whatever little knowledge I have, I am ready **to offer in service** to the country."},{"sentence":"Itanong mo sa iyong sarili kung ano ang **maipaglingkod** mo sa iyong kapwa.","translation":"Ask yourself what you can **do to serve** your fellowmen."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbigkas ng mga salita nang malakas upang isulat o i-rekord ng iba.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa ng boss mo sa'yo 'pag tinatamad siyang mag-email. 'Pakisulat 'to...' tapos ikaw ang tiga-type. Puwede ring 'yung jowa mong laging nasusunod, siya ang nag-didikta ng takbo ng relasyon. Hugot!
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa literal na pagbigkas para isulat, o sa metaporikal na pag-atas ng mga kondisyon o utos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **idikta** sa akin ang numero ng iyong telepono?","translation":"Can you **dictate** your phone number to me?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hahayaang **idikta** ng iba ang iyong kaligayahan.","translation":"Don't let others **dictate** your happiness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtatalo, paglalaban, o hindi pagkakasundo sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang panig.
original_explanation: The national pastime, charot! From petty arguments (away-bata) to full-blown bardagulan online, 'away' is everywhere. It's the reason for 'Marites' culture, the plot of every teleserye, and the drama in your friend group. "May away na naman sila" is the start of every good chismis.
usage_notes: Can refer to a verbal argument, a physical fight, or a state of conflict.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong iwasan ang anumang **away** ngayong Pasko.","translation":"I want to avoid any **fights** this Christmas."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula sa maliit na hindi pagkakaunawaan ang kanilang malaking **away**.","translation":"Their big **quarrel** started from a small misunderstanding."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang pagbaba o pagkawala ng lakas, sigla, o bisa.
original_explanation: That 1% battery feeling, but for humans. It's when you're about to give up because of too much adulting, or when you get dizzy from the heat. 'Huwag kang **manghina**, malapit na ang weekend!' (Don't get weak, the weekend is near!) is the corporate battlecry every Friday afternoon.
usage_notes: Refers to a process or state of losing strength, either physically, emotionally, or metaphorically (e.g., an argument weakening).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **manghina** ang kanyang katawan dahil sa sakit.","translation":"His body began **to weaken** because of the illness."},{"sentence":"Kapag gutom, madaling **manghina** ang isang tao.","translation":"When hungry, a person easily **becomes weak**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong hindi naniniwala sa pagkakaroon ng Diyos. Ito ay ang Ingles na katumbas ng salitang 'ateista'.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "atheist", na nagmula sa Griyegong "atheos" (walang diyos).
original_explanation: This is the direct English loanword for 'ateista'. You'll hear this a lot in English or Taglish conversations, especially among the younger, more Western-influenced crowd. It's basically the same as 'ateista' but with a more 'conyo' or international flavor. "Like, I'm not religious, I'm an atheist."
usage_notes: Ginagamit nang palitan sa 'ateista' sa modernong Taglish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"My friend is an **atheist**, but she respects all religions.","translation":"Ang kaibigan ko ay isang **atheist**, pero nirerespeto niya ang lahat ng relihiyon."},{"sentence":"It's hard to be an open **atheist** in a very religious country.","translation":"Mahirap maging isang hayag na **atheist** sa isang napakarelihiyosong bansa."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, kilos, o salita na ginagamit upang pigilan, hadlangan, o pahintuin ang isang gawain o intensyon.
original_explanation: This is your "pang-kontra" or "pang-block." Think of it as that one friend who always reminds you of your diet when you're about to order extra rice. Or the "seen" on Messenger that stops you from messaging again. It's the ultimate "stop right there!" move to prevent something from happening.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of preventing something negative, like a crime, a bad habit, or a tantrum.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang matataas na pader ay nagsisilbing **pansawata** sa mga magnanakaw.","translation":"The high walls serve as a **deterrent** to thieves."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng epektibong **pansawata** sa pagkalat ng maling impormasyon.","translation":"We need an effective **countermeasure** against the spread of misinformation."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na dalisay; walang anumang halo o bahid ng dumi; puro at malinis.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping 'ma-' at salitang ugat na 'dalisay' (pure).
original_explanation: This is the level of purity you aspire to have in your intentions, but usually only achieve in your newly bought distilled water. It's the 'walang malisya' friend, the gold that's 24-karat, or the love that's supposedly 'true.'
usage_notes: Isang mas matindi o nagbibigay-diin na bersyon ng 'dalisay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ng isang ina ay **madalisay** at walang hinihintay na kapalit.","translation":"A mother's love is **pure** and expects nothing in return."},{"sentence":"Hinahanap niya ang **madalisay** na katotohanan sa likod ng mga kasinungalingan.","translation":"He is searching for the **unadulterated** truth behind the lies."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng sukdulang lakas, puwersa, o ingay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `napaka-` (nagpapahiwatig ng sukdulang antas) at salitang ugat na `lakas` (strength, loudness).
original_explanation: Can mean two things: 1) The 'strong' of someone who can open a new jar of peanut butter in one go, or the WiFi signal that reaches the bathroom. 2) The 'loud' of your neighbor's karaoke at 2 AM or the "PSST!" from your mom that can be heard across the entire mall. Context is key.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical strength, volume (sound), intensity (of rain, wind), or influence. The phrase `napakalakas na ulan` (very strong rain) is a common collocation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napakalakas** ng hangin kaya nagsiliparan ang mga yero.","translation":"The wind was **very strong** so the galvanized iron sheets flew off."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, hinaan mo ang radyo, **napakalakas**!","translation":"Please, turn down the radio, it's **very loud**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi na bago; nagamit na ng iba; pangalawa sa pagmamay-ari.
original_explanation: Ito ang magic word sa ukay-ukay at sa mga naghahanap ng murang kotse. "Segunda mano" means second-hand. It's proof that you don't always need something brand new to be happy. From clothes to cars to jowa (joke!), basta gumagana pa, go lang! It's practical, it's sustainable, it's very Pinoy.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit sa pariralang "segunda mano" (second hand).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili lang ako ng **segunda** na kotse dahil mas mura.","translation":"I just bought a **second-hand** car because it's cheaper."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagputol, partikular na ng mga tubo para sa produksyon ng asukal.
etymology: From `pag-` (prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of `tabad` (to cut sugarcane).
original_explanation: This is a super specific, almost vintage term. Think of the hacienderos and the sacadas. `Pagtatabad` is the OG 'harvesting' but specifically for sugarcane. It's hard, back-breaking work under the sun. You won't hear this in a BPO office, but you might hear it from your lolo who grew up near a sugar plantation in Negros. It's the agricultural equivalent of a deep cut track on a classic OPM album.
usage_notes: Primarily used in agricultural contexts, specifically within the sugar industry. It is a regional or specialized term, most common in sugar-producing provinces like Negros.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang panahon ng **pagtatabad** sa mga tubuhan.","translation":"The season for **cutting sugarcane** has begun in the plantations."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay ng mga sakada ay umiikot sa **pagtatabad** at pagtatanim.","translation":"The life of the sugarcane workers revolves around **cutting sugarcane** and planting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sandata na binubuo ng isang baluktot na piraso ng kahoy (busog) at isang matulis na patpat (palaso) na pinakakawalan sa pamamagitan ng isang tali. Maaari ring tumukoy sa palaso lamang.
original_explanation: The weapon of choice before guns were a thing. Think Katniss Everdeen, Hawkeye, or Lapu-Lapu's crew. It's also a classic hugot line: "Para kang **pana**, tinamaan ako sa'yo."
usage_notes: While technically 'pana' refers to the whole set (bow and arrow), it's often used to refer to just the arrow ('palaso'). The bow itself is 'busog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuruan siya ng kanyang ama kung paano gumamit ng **pana**.","translation":"His father taught him how to use a **bow and arrow**."},{"sentence":"Isang **pana** ang tumama sa puno.","translation":"An **arrow** hit the tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaki na mahilig mag-skateboard at karaniwang iniuugnay sa isang partikular na istilo ng pananamit at kultura.
original_explanation: Straight out of an early 2000s Avril Lavigne song. He's the guy with the baggy pants, band shirt, and a skateboard he carries everywhere even if he's just going to the sari-sari store. He says "see you later, boy" to conformity. In the Philippines, he's probably hanging out at a local skate park or trying to land a kickflip in a random parking lot. He's not just a boy who skates; it's a whole aesthetic, a lifestyle.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan hindi lamang ang libangan kundi ang buong subculture na nauugnay dito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Crush na crush niya yung **skaterboy** na laging nasa plasa.","translation":"She has a huge crush on the **skater boy** who's always at the plaza."},{"sentence":"Ang pangarap niya ay maging isang propesyonal na **skaterboy**.","translation":"His dream is to become a professional **skater boy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panlabas na bahagi ng isang gulong kung saan ikinakabit ang goma; kilala rin bilang 'rim'.
original_explanation: Yung bakal na part ng gulong ng kotse o motor na pinagmamayabang ng mga 'car show' peeps. 'Paps, anong size ng yantas mo?' The shinier and bigger, the better daw. It's the bling for your wheels.
usage_notes: Common in automotive and mechanical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpagawa siya ng bagong **yantas** para sa kaniyang sasakyan.","translation":"He had a new **rim** made for his car."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-alis at hindi pagsama sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar; paglisan.
original_explanation: Ah, the source of so much hugot. This is what your ex did to you. It's what you do to the last piece of pizza for your sibling (if you're nice). It's the 'ghosting' starter pack. `Pag-iiwan` can be as simple as leaving your keys on the table or as soul-crushing as being left for someone new.
usage_notes: Often implies leaving something or someone behind, either intentionally or unintentionally. Can be emotionally charged.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **pag-iiwan** niya ay nagdulot ng malaking kalungkutan sa pamilya.","translation":"His sudden **act of leaving** brought great sadness to the family."}]

translation: to pick up with the fingertips; to grasp lightly
meaning_filipino: Kunin o abutin ang isang bagay gamit ang mga dulo ng daliri; hipuin nang marahan.
etymology: From an old Tagalog root "damot" (to pick up with fingers) + "-in" (object-focus verbal suffix).
original_explanation: Think of how you'd pick up a single grain of rice, or that last bit of chicharon dust from the bottom of the bag. That delicate, fingertip-action is "damtin". It's a more poetic and gentle version of 'kunin' (to get). It's also used figuratively, like trying to grasp a fleeting dream or memory. "Sana'y madama't **damtin** ang pag-ibig." Deep.
usage_notes: This word is quite literary or poetic. It is rarely used in everyday conversation, favoring simpler words like 'kunin' or 'abutin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **damtin** ang nahulog na singsing mula sa siwang.","translation":"He tried to **pick up** the fallen ring from the crevice with his fingertips."},{"sentence":"Ito ay isang pangarap na kay hirap **damtin**.","translation":"This is a dream that is so hard to **grasp**."}]

translation: state of being weakened; languor; wilting
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng matinding panghihina ng katawan o isipan, na tila nawawalan ng lakas at sigla.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` (nagiging `panl-`) + pag-uulit ng unang pantig (`lu`) + salitang-ugat na `lupaypay` (hina, pagod, o lanta).
original_explanation: This is you on a Friday at 4:59 PM after a hell week. Yung feeling na drained na drained ka na, physically and mentally, na parang halaman na hindi nadiligan for a week. Your social battery is at 0%, and all you want to do is become one with your bed.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang estado ng pisikal o emosyonal na pagkaubos at panghihina. Maaari ring gamitin para sa mga halaman.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos ang maghapong trabaho sa bukid, ramdam niya ang **panlulupaypay** ng buong katawan.","translation":"After a whole day's work in the field, he felt the **weakness** of his entire body."},{"sentence":"Ang **panlulupaypay** ng mga halaman ay senyales na kailangan na silang diligan.","translation":"The **wilting** of the plants is a sign that they need to be watered."}]

meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit nang pitong beses.
original_explanation: When 'anim' (six) is not enough and 'walo' (eight) is too much. You use this when someone does something repeatedly, specifically seven times. 'Makapito siyang nag-follow up sa HR tungkol sa backpay niya.' (He followed up with HR seven times about his back pay.)
usage_notes: Part of a series: makalawa (twice), makatlo (thrice), makaapat (four times), etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Makapito** siyang tumawag sa iyo kanina.","translation":"He called you **seven times** earlier."},{"sentence":"Sinabi ko nang **makapito** na isara ang pinto.","translation":"I already said **seven times** to close the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kasunduan, patakaran, o tradisyon na hindi nakasulat sa papel ngunit sinusunod at nauunawaan.
original_explanation: Like the unwritten rule of "utang na loob" or giving a portion of your take-out to your family when you get home. It's not in a contract, but it's understood. "Verbal agreement lang, pre."
usage_notes: Often used in the context of agreements, rules, or laws.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon kaming **walang-sulat** na kasunduan na laging magtutulungan.","translation":"We have an **unwritten** agreement to always help each other."},{"sentence":"Ang batas na iyon ay **walang-sulat** ngunit alam ng lahat sa komunidad.","translation":"That rule is **unwritten** but known to everyone in the community."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang listahan ng mga pagkain at inumin na maaaring i-order sa isang restawran, karinderya, o anumang kainan.
original_explanation: The scroll of destiny you get at a restaurant that makes you say 'Ano masarap dito?' to the waiter, even after staring at it for 10 minutes. It's that laminated piece of paper where the picture looks 10x better than the actual food you'll get. Sa bahay, ang menu ay kung anong ituro ni nanay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan natin ang **menu** para makapili ng oorderin.","translation":"Let's look at the **menu** to choose what to order."},{"sentence":"Wow, ang daming pagpipilian sa **menu** ninyo!","translation":"Wow, you have so many choices on your **menu**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking sisidlang yari sa kahoy o metal, karaniwang pabilog at may umbok sa gitna, ginagamit sa pag-iimbak ng mga likido tulad ng alak, langis, o tubig.
original_explanation: Yung dambuhalang lalagyan ng tubig na pang-ipon 'pag may water interruption. O kaya yung nasa mga laro na pwedeng pasabugin. Sa Pilipinas, ito yung classic na blue drum na nagiging imbakan ng tubig, bigas, o minsan, taniman.
usage_notes: Can also refer to the barrel of a gun ("kanyon ng baril").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napuno na ang mga **barel** ng tubig-ulan.","translation":"The **barrels** are now full of rainwater."},{"sentence":"Nag-iimbak sila ng alak sa mga lumang **barel** na yari sa kahoy.","translation":"They store wine in old **barrels** made of wood."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang materyal na ginagamit sa pagtatakip o pagbabalot ng isang bagay, tulad ng papel, plastik, o dahon.
etymology: From the prefix 'pam-' (a variant of 'pan-' used before 'b' and 'p') and the root word 'balot', meaning 'to wrap'.
original_explanation: The thing you struggle to open when you're super hungry and the ulam is sealed tight. Also, the gift wrap your Tita carefully un-tapes so she can reuse it next year. In short, the first layer of any surprise.
usage_notes: Can refer to gift wrappers, food wrappers (like for 'suman'), or any protective covering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong itapon ang **pambalot** ng regalo, gagamitin pa natin iyan.","translation":"Don't throw away the gift **wrapper**, we're still going to use that."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **pambalot** para sa mga tirang pagkain.","translation":"I need some **wrapping material** for the leftover food."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kombinasyon ng mga bagay, lalo na sa isang pagkain sa restawran o sa isang serye ng mga atake sa larong bidyo.
original_explanation: The best part of any fast-food menu. Why choose between fries and sundae when you can have a value meal kombo? Also what you do in Mobile Legends to wipe out the enemy team. It's about getting more for less, whether it's food or a kill streak.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used for food deals or in gaming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-order ako ng chicken **kombo** na may kasamang large fries at coke.","translation":"I ordered a chicken **combo** that comes with large fries and coke."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong i-master ang **kombo** ng hero mo para manalo sa laban.","translation":"You need to master your hero's **combo** to win the fight."}]

translation: the act of turning one's back; abandonment; renunciation
meaning_filipino: Ang pisikal na kilos ng pag-ikot upang tumalikod, o sa metaporikal na kahulugan, ang pag-iwan, pagtatakwil, o hindi pagtupad sa isang responsibilidad, paniniwala, o tao.
etymology: From `pag-` (nominalizing prefix) + `talikod` (to turn one's back), which itself comes from `likod` (back).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "hugot" word. It can be literal, like turning your back to walk away. But more often, it's the heavy stuff: the **pagtalikod** sa responsibilidad (abandoning responsibility), **pagtalikod** sa isang kaibigan (turning your back on a friend), or **pagtalikod** sa isang pangako (breaking a promise). It's the dramatic exit in every teleserye.
usage_notes: Carries a strong, often negative, connotation of abandonment or betrayal when used metaphorically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtalikod** niya sa kanyang mga prinsipyo ay ikinagulat ng lahat.","translation":"His **renunciation** of his principles surprised everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Araruhin ang isang bukid o lupain bilang paghahanda sa pagtatanim.
original_explanation: This is the OG, old-school word for "araruhin" (to plow). You'd probably hear this from your lolo who still talks about the good old days of farming with a carabao. It sounds more poetic and dignified, like something you'd read in a Florante at Laura-era text instead of a modern agricultural manual.
usage_notes: This is a very rare and literary variant of the more common 'araruhin'. Most speakers would not recognize or use it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga pa lamang ay nagsimula na siyang **arahan** ang kanilang bukid.","translation":"It was still early when he started to **plow** their field."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghamak, paglibak, o pag-insulto sa isang tao o bagay sa pamamagitan ng mapanuksong salita o kilos.
original_explanation: This is the meaner, one-sided cousin of 'pagtutuyaan'. This isn't friendly 'asar' anymore; this is bullying. It's when someone scoffs at your idea, makes fun of your clothes, or dismisses you with a sarcastic laugh. It's the verbal equivalent of an eye-roll and a sneer.
usage_notes: More formal and carries a stronger, more negative connotation than 'panunukso' (teasing). It implies contempt and is generally a one-way action, unlike 'pagtutuyaan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya pinansin ang **pagtuya** ng mga tao sa kanyang kakaibang pananamit.","translation":"He ignored the people's **mockery** of his strange attire."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **pagtuya** ang kanyang mga salita.","translation":"His words were full of **scorn**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging maingat, mapag-iingat, o maalam sa posibleng panganib. Tumutukoy din sa pag-aalaga o pagtatago ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: 'Ingat' is the Philippines' national love language. It's more than just 'care'; it's a whole culture. It's your mom reminding you to bring an umbrella, your friend texting you to message them when you get home, and the security guard saying it as you leave the building. It's the invisible hug everyone gives you. The noun form is the *concept* of that hug.
usage_notes: While the verb/command form is more common, the noun form is used to describe the quality of being careful or the act of safekeeping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa mabuting **ingat** ang mga alahas niya.","translation":"Her jewels are in good **safekeeping**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matinding **ingat** sa pagtawid sa abalang kalsada.","translation":"Extreme **caution** is needed when crossing the busy street."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makaranas ng pakiramdam ng pagiging bago, hindi sanay, o pagkailang sa isang bagong sitwasyon, lugar, o gawain.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling mo sa first day sa bagong trabaho. Hindi mo alam kung saan ang CR, sino kakausapin mo, or kung pwede ba mag-kape anytime. You feel awkward and out of place. You're still adjusting. That's the feeling of manibago. It's the awkward phase of any new beginning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naninibago** pa ako sa bagong sistema dito sa opisina.","translation":"I still **feel unaccustomed** to the new system here in the office."},{"sentence":"Normal lang na **manibago** ka sa unang linggo mo sa ibang bansa.","translation":"It's normal to **feel strange** during your first week in another country."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang una o pinakamatandang anak sa magkakapatid.
original_explanation: The family's unpaid intern and second parent. They're the 'ate' or 'kuya' who gets blamed for everything but also holds the family together. They're the beta-testers for all parenting styles and the first to hear 'Noong panahon namin...'.
usage_notes: Ang "panganay" ay madalas gamitin nang mag-isa upang tukuyin ang pinakamatandang anak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang responsibilidad ng **anak na panganay**.","translation":"The **eldest child** has a great responsibility."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaki at matulis na patalim na karaniwang isinusukbit sa baywang.
original_explanation: This isn't your ordinary kitchen knife for chopping onions. This is the kind of blade you see in historical Filipino movies, tucked into the waistband of a Katipunero or a local datu. It's a serious, no-nonsense dagger. Think of it as the 'pang-away' version of a kutsilyo.
usage_notes: A specific and somewhat archaic term. 'Daga,' 'punyal,' or 'itak' might be more common depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakasukbit sa kanyang baywang ang isang makintab na **balisaksakan**.","translation":"A shiny **dagger** was tucked into his waistband."},{"sentence":"Ginamit ng mandirigma ang kanyang **balisaksakan** upang ipagtanggol ang sarili.","translation":"The warrior used his **large knife** to defend himself."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang organisadong gawain o inisyatiba na isinasagawa ng isang grupo ng mga tagahanga upang ipakita ang kanilang suporta, tulad ng pag-upa ng mga billboard para sa kaarawan ng isang idolo, pag-oorganisa ng mga donasyon sa ngalan nila, o paglikha ng mga banner para sa isang konsiyerto.
etymology: Direktang hiram mula sa Ingles na "fan project."
original_explanation: Eto yung team effort ng fandom. From cupsleeve events sa mga coffee shop para sa birthday ni bias, hanggang sa pag-rent ng LED billboard sa EDSA. Ito ang resibo na hindi lang pabebe ang fans, kaya rin nilang mag-organize na parang pro-level na event planner.
usage_notes: Malaking bahagi ng K-Pop fan culture sa Pilipinas, na nagpapakita ng organisasyon at dedikasyon ng mga fan base.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **fan project** para sa anibersaryo ng grupo ay isang feeding program para sa mga bata.","translation":"The **fan project** for the group's anniversary is a feeding program for children."},{"sentence":"Sumali ka ba sa pag-ambag para sa billboard **fan project**?","translation":"Did you contribute to the billboard **fan project**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may pambihirang kasanayan o kaalaman sa isang partikular na larangan; isang dalubhasa. Ginagamit din bilang titulo sa edukasyon.
original_explanation: Pwedeng 'yung boss mo, "Sabi ni master...", pwedeng 'yung degree mo, "Master in Business Ad", or 'yung tito mong magaling sa chess, "Chess master 'yan!". It's a title for someone who has leveled up, whether in a game, in the office, or in school.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pandiwa: 'ma-master' (to master something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng **master**'s degree sa ibang bansa.","translation":"He took his **master**'s degree abroad."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing siyang isang **master** sa sining ng pagpipinta.","translation":"He is considered a **master** in the art of painting."}]

translation: to part, to clear a path
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalis ng sagabal sa daan sa pamamagitan ng kamay o anumang bagay upang makagawa ng espasyo.
etymology: From Tagalog `mag-` (verb prefix) + `hawi` (to part, to clear).
original_explanation: That dramatic moment in a movie when the main character walks into a crowded room and people move aside? That's **maghawi**. Or what you have to do to the curtains to check if the chismis outside is true. Also, what you do to your long bangs (or 'hawi' hairstyle) when they get in your eyes.
usage_notes: Can refer to parting hair, curtains, tall grass, or a crowd.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangan niyang **maghawi** ng mga baging para makadaan sa gubat.","translation":"He had to **part** the vines to get through the jungle."},{"sentence":"**Maghawi** ka ng kurtina para pumasok ang liwanag.","translation":"**Part** the curtains to let the light in."}]

translation: to become hoarse; to lose one's voice
meaning_filipino: Ang mawalan o mamalat ang boses, karaniwan dahil sa sobrang pagsigaw o pagkanta.
etymology: From the root word 'paga' (hoarseness) with the -um- infix.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your voice after a karaoke marathon, a heated UAAP game, or shouting 'Darna!' at the top of your lungs. Your voice suddenly goes on an unannounced leave of absence. 'Paos' is the more common term, but pumaga is its dramatic, verb-form cousin.
usage_notes: Less common in everyday conversation than 'namamaos' or 'napaos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **pumaga** ang lalamunan ko sa kakasigaw sa konsiyerto.","translation":"My throat almost **became hoarse** from shouting at the concert."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong sumigaw, baka ka **pumaga**.","translation":"Don't shout too much, you might **lose your voice**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na sisidlan, karaniwang gawa sa katad o tela, na partikular na ginagamit para sa pag-iimbak ng mga barya.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "portamoneda" (porta-, "to carry" + moneda, "coin").
original_explanation: 'Yung maliit na pitaka na puro barya lang ang laman. Usually pag-aari ng lola mo or ng tindera sa sari-sari store. Dito galing 'yung pambayad mo sa jeep 'pag ayaw mong maglabas ng malaking pera. The OG coin purse before it became a "kikay kit" accessory.
usage_notes: This is a slightly dated but still understood term. "Coin purse" or "baryahan" are more common now.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilabas ng matanda ang kanyang **portamoneda** upang bayaran ang tinapay.","translation":"The old woman took out her **coin purse** to pay for the bread."},{"sentence":"Puno ng barya ang luma niyang **portamoneda**.","translation":"Her old **coin purse** is full of coins."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ituon ang pandinig at isipan sa isang tunog, salita, o musika; bigyan ng atensyon ang sinasabi ng isang tao.
etymology: From pa- + dinig + -an. The 'd' in dinig often becomes 'k' and vowels shift in this common but irregular verb formation.
original_explanation: This is more than just hearing; it's the active version. Hearing is the background noise of the neighbor's karaoke, but 'pakinggan' is you actually trying to figure out if they're singing the right lyrics. It's what your parents tell you to do, what your partner wishes you'd do, and what you do with your favorite podcast or that "Marites" with the latest tea. Listen up!
usage_notes: The command form is "Pakinggan mo!" (Listen!). It implies paying attention, not just the physical act of hearing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakinggan** mo ang payo ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"**Listen to** the advice of your parents."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **pakinggan** ang bagong album ng bandang iyan.","translation":"I want to **listen to** that band's new album."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao o ari-arian na may legal na dokumento o titulo na nagpapatunay ng pagmamay-ari.
etymology: Mula sa salitang `may` (has/with) at `titulo` (mula sa Espanyol na 'título' na nangangahulugang 'title').
original_explanation: Kapag sinabing may-titulo 'yung lupa, ibig sabihin legit ang pagmamay-ari, hindi ka basta-basta mapapaalis. It's like having the official receipt (OR/CR) for your life's achievements—proof of ownership, baby!
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit para sa pagmamay-ari ng lupa at ari-arian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mahal ang lupang **may-titulo** kaysa sa 'rights' lang.","translation":"Titled land is more expensive than one with just 'rights'."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **may-titulo** na ang aming bahay at lupa.","translation":"Finally, our house and lot is now **titled**."}]

translation: to cause to retreat or back away
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng pag-atras o pagbalik sa pinanggalingan, kadalasan dahil sa takot, pag-aalinlangan, o hadlang.
original_explanation: When you're about to send that risky "I miss you" text, but your pride kicks in and you delete it. That's your feelings getting "mapa-urong". It's taking a step back, whether from a scary dog, a huge responsibility, or a bad decision waiting to happen.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tahol ng malaking aso ay sapat na para **mapaurong** ang sinuman.","translation":"The bark of the big dog is enough to **make anyone retreat**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mapaurong** sa mga hamon ng buhay.","translation":"Don't **back down** from life's challenges."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang kilos o gawi na walang katuturan, kakatwa, o tila ginawa ng isang taong wala sa katinuan.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng "parang" (like/as if) at "loko" (crazy/fool, mula sa Espanyol na 'loco').
original_explanation: This is you laughing hysterically at a meme at 2 AM. Or your friend suggesting another 'get rich quick' scheme. It means acting foolish, irrational, or just plain silly. 'Tawa siya nang tawa na **parang loko**.'
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang ekspresyon upang ilarawan ang isang kilos na kakatwa o walang saysay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang tumakbo diyan na **parang loko**, baka madapa ka.","translation":"Don't run around there **like a fool**, you might trip."},{"sentence":"Sigaw siya nang sigaw na **parang loko** sa gitna ng daan.","translation":"He was shouting **like crazy** in the middle of the road."}]

meaning_filipino: (Hiram na salita) Ang matinding pananabik, pag-asam, o publisidad na nakapaligid sa isang bagay, kaganapan, o tao.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "hype," isang pinaikling anyo ng "hyperbole."
original_explanation: That feeling when a new milk tea shop opens and everyone's lining up, or when a K-drama trailer drops and the whole internet loses its mind. It's the collective "OMG, can't wait!" energy. "Hype" din 'yung friend mo na todo-promote ng bago niyang business.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang slang sa Taglish. Maaaring tumukoy sa mismong excitement (pangngalan) o sa katangian ng pagiging sikat o pinag-uusapan (pang-uri).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang **hype** sa bagong pelikula, pero maganda ba talaga?","translation":"The **hype** for the new movie is intense, but is it actually good?"},{"sentence":"Sobrang **hype** ngayon ng laro na 'yan sa social media.","translation":"That game is so **hyped** on social media right now."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng bato na mayaman sa mineral na posporus, na pangunahing ginagamit sa paggawa ng pataba sa lupa o abono.
etymology: Mula sa "bato" (stone) at salitang Espanyol na "fosfato" (phosphate).
original_explanation: The G.O.A.T. for farmers. This isn't a pretty rock; it's a working rock. It's ground up to make fertilizer, basically a superfood for plants. Think of it as the 'Berocca' for your kamote and talong, giving them the nutrients to grow big and strong.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong pang-agrikultura at kemikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **batong pospato** ay mahalagang sangkap sa paggawa ng modernong abono.","translation":"**Phosphate rock** is an important ingredient in making modern fertilizer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook o pagawaan kung saan ginagawa ang mga kasangkapang yari sa kahoy.
original_explanation: The OG workshop. Before there were startups in garages, there were tatays and titos making tables and chairs in their karpinterya. It’s the place that smells like sawdust and pure, unadulterated hard work.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the workshop, while 'karpintero' is the carpenter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ni tatay ang sirang silya sa **karpinterya** ni Mang Lito.","translation":"Father brought the broken chair to Mang Lito's **carpentry shop**."},{"sentence":"Maingay sa tapat ng bahay dahil sa ginagawang **karpinterya**.","translation":"It's noisy across the house because of the ongoing **carpentry** work."}]

translation: journalist; reporter; member of the press
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang propesyon ay ang pagkalap, pagsulat, at pag-uulat ng balita at impormasyon para sa publiko sa pamamagitan ng diyaryo, radyo, telebisyon, o internet.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung mga laging nasa gitna ng gulo, may dalang mic at camera, at hindi natatakot magtanong ng 'Bakit po?' at 'Paano po nangyari?'. From political scandals to celebrity chismis, the mamamahayag is there to get the story. They are the professional version of the Marites.
usage_notes: The prefix 'mamaN-' combined with the root 'hayag' (to announce, to reveal) indicates the person whose profession is to make things public.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang matapang na **mamamahayag** ang naglantad ng katiwalian sa gobyerno.","translation":"A brave **journalist** exposed the corruption in the government."},{"sentence":"Kinapanayam ng mga **mamamahayag** ang pangulo pagkatapos ng kanyang talumpati.","translation":"The **members of the press** interviewed the president after his speech."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng dalawa o higit pang tao na nagpapalitan ng halik sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: The verb form of PDA (Public Display of Affection). This is what you see in the climax of a rom-com, when the love team finally stops arguing and just kisses. It's a reciprocal action; it takes two to tango. 'Uy, maghalikan daw sa harap ng camera!' is what the crowd shouts at a celebrity wedding.
usage_notes: The mag- prefix and -an suffix denote a reciprocal action between two or more people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang magkasintahan na **maghalikan** sa ilalim ng puno.","translation":"He saw the couple **kissing each other** under the tree."},{"sentence":"Sa huling eksena ng pelikula, inaasahan ng lahat na **maghalikan** ang mga bida.","translation":"In the last scene of the movie, everyone expects the main characters to **kiss each other**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtiyak o pag-alam nang may katiyakan sa isang bagay; gawin ang isang bagay upang maging sigurado at alisin ang pag-aalinlangan.
etymology: From 'siguro' (maybe, perhaps), which itself comes from Spanish 'seguro' (sure, certain). The verb form 'magsiguro' shifts the meaning from 'maybe' to 'to make sure'.
original_explanation: The official verb of 'praning' (paranoid) people and responsible adults. 'Nag-lock ka ba ng pinto?' 'Oo, pero babalikan ko para magsiguro.' It's double-checking your alarm, sending a follow-up email, and asking your friend for the fifth time, 'Sure ka na ba talaga?'
usage_notes: This is a fascinating word because its root 'siguro' means 'maybe,' but the verb 'magsiguro' means the opposite: 'to remove maybes' and 'to make certain.' The more common verb for this is 'siguraduhin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magsiguro** ka na dala mo ang lahat ng kailangan mo bago umalis.","translation":"**Make sure** you have everything you need before leaving."},{"sentence":"Tumawag ako ulit para **magsiguro** sa oras ng ating pagkikita.","translation":"I called again **to make sure** about the time of our meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan ng pagkagapi o hindi pagkapanalo sa isang laban, laro, o argumento.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping pangkasanhi na "ika-" at sa salitang-ugat na "talo" (gapi, hindi nanalo).
original_explanation: This is the reason for your "L" (Loss). The `ikatalo` of your Mobile Legends team was the marksman who kept feeding. The `ikatalo` of your argument with your partner was you forgetting their monthsary. It’s the critical mistake, the fatal flaw, the cause of your "sana all nanalo" moment.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang sanhi na tumutukoy sa dahilan ng isang pagkatalo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kawalan ng pagkakaisa ang **ikatalo** ng kanilang koponan.","translation":"The lack of unity is what **caused the defeat** of their team."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging mayabang niya ang maaaring **ikatalo** niya sa eleksyon.","translation":"His arrogance could be what **causes his loss** in the election."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan sa isang madre, partikular na sa isang superyora o pinuno ng isang kumbento. Ginagamit din bilang magalang na tawag sa isang matandang babae.
original_explanation: Ito yung tawag mo sa madre (nun) sa Catholic school na pinapasukan mo, lalo na kung siya yung principal. "Good morning, Mother!" Pwede ring pang-asar na tawag sa kaibigan mong OA maka-nanay, "Okay, mother!" Or in the context of LGBTQ+ slang, the 'mother' is the head of a 'house' or a highly respected figure. She's the icon, she's the legend, and she IS the moment.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga tiyak na konteksto, tulad ng relihiyon (pagtukoy sa madre) o bilang tanda ng paggalang. Ito ay naipasok na rin sa gay lingo ng mga Pilipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si **Mother** Teresa ay kilala sa kanyang pagtulong sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"**Mother** Teresa is known for her work helping the poor."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan kami ni **Mother** Superior na mag-aral nang mabuti.","translation":"**Mother** Superior advised us to study well."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtama o pagbangga, karaniwan ng ulo, sa isang matigas na bagay.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're walking while texting and suddenly meet a wall. Ouch. 'Umpog' is the sound and the action of your head making an unscheduled meeting with a solid object. It's the universe's way of saying, 'Pay attention!' Can also be used for a clash of ideas or egos.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb root, e.g., 'naumpog' (accidentally bumped one's head), 'umumpog' (to bump one's head).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Aray! May bukol ako dahil sa **umpog** ko sa pinto.","translation":"Ouch! I have a lump because I **bumped** my head on the door."},{"sentence":"Nagka-**umpog** ang mga ulo namin nang sabay kaming yumuko para kunin ang nahulog na barya.","translation":"Our heads **collided** when we both bent down at the same time to pick up the dropped coin."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natatanging katangian o kalidad na tila nagmumula sa isang tao, lugar, o bagay. Sa modernong gamit, ito rin ay tumutukoy sa pagpapakita ng tiwala sa sarili o pagpapaganda para sa isang larawan.
etymology: From English 'aura', from Latin 'aura', from Greek 'aúra'. The modern Filipino slang usage focuses on the act of projecting a persona.
original_explanation: This is the vibe you project. In modern Pinoy slang, it's not just a mystical energy field, it's the act of projecting confidence, style, or just being extra for a photo or a social media post. 'Mag-aura' means to pose, to project, to serve looks. It's your personal brand's energy signature. Think of that friend who's always ready for an OOTD shot, even just to buy suka sa tindahan. That's peak aura.
usage_notes: The slang verb form 'mag-aura' or 'um-aura' is very popular, meaning 'to project a certain vibe' or 'to pose glamorously'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lakas ng **aura** mo ngayon, parang nanalo ka sa lotto!","translation":"Your **vibe** is so strong today, it's like you won the lottery!"},{"sentence":"Tara, mag-**aura** tayo sa bagong bukas na coffee shop.","translation":"Let's go and **project our best selves/pose** at the newly opened coffee shop."},{"sentence":"Kahit pagod sa trabaho, kailangan pa ring mag-**aura** para sa Instagram.","translation":"Even if tired from work, one still needs to **project a good vibe** for Instagram."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lutuin na gawa sa binating itlog na pinirito sa mantika o mantekilya, na kung minsan ay may halong keso, gulay, o karne.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'omelet', na mula sa Pranses na 'omelette'.
original_explanation: Ang sosyal na version ng torta. Parehong binating itlog, pero pag may cheese, bell pepper, at mushroom sa loob tapos tinupi nang maganda, biglang 'omelet' na ang tawag at tumaas ang presyo sa menu. Breakfast ng mga nagfi-feeling-hotel.
usage_notes: Ang lokal na katumbas ay 'torta', ngunit may pagkakaiba sa paraan ng paghahanda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-request siya ng cheese **omelet** para sa almusal.","translation":"She requested a cheese **omelet** for breakfast."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa o maghanda ng isang huling habilin o testamento, isang legal na dokumento na nagsasaad ng pamamahagi ng ari-arian pagkamatay.
original_explanation: This is what lolo or lola does in teleseryes that causes all the drama between the 'bida' and the 'kontrabida'. It's the legal version of 'I give you my blessing... and the ancestral home. To your evil step-sibling, I give nothing.'
usage_notes: A formal, legal term used in the context of inheritance and last wills.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bago siya pumanaw, nagpasya si Don Alfonso na **magtestamento** pabor sa kanyang tapat na katulong.","translation":"Before he passed away, Don Alfonso decided **to make a will** in favor of his loyal servant."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **magtestamento** upang maiwasan ang pag-aaway ng mga tagapagmana.","translation":"It is important **to make a will** to avoid disputes among the heirs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkalahatang tawag sa mga paraan ng pangmadlang komunikasyon, tulad ng pahayagan, radyo, telebisyon, at internet.
etymology: From English 'media', which is the plural of Latin 'medium'.
original_explanation: The source of all chismis, news, and Marites' power. From TV Patrol and 24 Oras to your favorite influencer's IG stories and that shady Facebook page. The media is the fourth estate, the fifth-column, and your tita's primary source for fake news—all at the same time. Handle with care.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to news organizations and journalists collectively. The Filipino pronunciation /MI-dya/ is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang papel ng **media** sa paghubog ng opinyon ng publiko.","translation":"The **media** plays a big role in shaping public opinion."},{"sentence":"Inakusahan ng politiko ang **media** na sila ay biased.","translation":"The politician accused the **media** of being biased."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng ingay o malakas na tunog na maaaring makagambala sa iba.
original_explanation: What your parents tell you not to do when there's a baby sleeping. What you and your friends do at a concert or when your favorite basketball team scores. It can be for fun (cheering) or to be a nuisance (your neighbor's karaoke at 2 AM). In the modern context, it's also what you do on social media to support a cause or a personality—"Let's make some noise for this!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan ng guro ang mga batang huwag **magmaingay** sa loob ng library.","translation":"The teacher told the children not to **make noise** inside the library."},{"sentence":"Tara, **magmaingay** tayo para sa paborito nating banda!","translation":"Come on, let's **make some noise** for our favorite band!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagpunta sa isang lugar na inaasahan, tulad ng paaralan o trabaho; ang hindi pagpasok sa loob ng isang espasyo.
etymology: Mula sa 'di' (not) at 'pumasok' (entered/attended), na nasa anyong pangnagdaan.
original_explanation: The official term for 'nag-cutting classes' or when you use a sick leave credit for a beach trip. It's the reason for that 'Bakit absent ka kahapon?' text from your work bestie. You were simply not there.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa pagliban sa isang obligasyon (trabaho, paaralan) o sa pisikal na akto ng hindi pagpasok sa isang lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Maria ay **di pumasok** kahapon dahil may lagnat siya.","translation":"Maria **was absent** yesterday because she had a fever."},{"sentence":"Takot ang aso kaya **di pumasok** sa loob ng bahay.","translation":"The dog was scared so it **did not enter** the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghukay sa lupa o anumang bagay na nakatabon upang makuha o ilitaw ang isang bagay. Ginagamit din sa metaporikal na paraan para sa pag-alala sa nakaraan.
original_explanation: What you do when you're looking for your ex's old social media posts from 2012. It's digging up the past, literally or figuratively. Can also be used for actual digging, like a dog looking for its bone or treasure hunters searching for Yamashita's treasure. "Huwag mo nang halukayin ang nakaraan" is the ultimate hugot line.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for digging soil and figuratively for bringing up past issues.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **maghalukay** ng mga lumang isyu para hindi na tayo mag-away.","translation":"Don't **dig up** old issues anymore so we won't fight."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **maghalukay** dito para itanim ang puno.","translation":"We need to **dig** here to plant the tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na takip na metal o plastik na isinusuot sa dulo ng daliri upang itulak ang karayom habang nananahi at maiwasan ang pagkaturok.
original_explanation: This is your lola's secret weapon against karayom attacks. It's that little metal hat for your finger, the OG armor for anyone brave enough to tackle a sewing project. Without it, your finger would look like a voodoo doll.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ni lola ang **dedal** upang hindi siya matusok ng karayom.","translation":"Grandma used the **thimble** so she wouldn't get pricked by the needle."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinsala sa kasukasuan, buto, o kalamnan, lalo na sa paa o binti, na nagdudulot ng hirap o sakit sa paglakad.
original_explanation: Yung nangyayari kapag na-wrong step ka sa hagdanan, sa kalsada, o sa pag-ibig. Bigla ka na lang di makalakad nang maayos. Minsan, kailangan ng hilot; minsan, kailangan lang ng pahinga at 'wag na ulit dumaan sa maling landas.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pang-uri (adjective) na nangangahulugang 'lame' o 'having a sprain'. Hal: "Pilay siya."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng **pilay** sa paa matapos matapilok habang naglalaro ng basketball.","translation":"He got a **sprain** in his foot after twisting his ankle while playing basketball."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang propesyon o hilig ay ang pag-awit; isang mang-aawit.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, everyone is a 'singer' (or at least, they think they are, especially with a microphone and some alcohol). It's the English word we've fully adopted because 'mang-aawit' sounds a bit too formal for the karaoke bar. From Regine Velasquez to the guy belting out 'My Way' at 2 AM, they're all singers in our hearts.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English that has been fully integrated into Tagalog. It is used more commonly in casual conversation than its Tagalog equivalent 'mang-aawit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **singer** balang araw.","translation":"Her dream is to become a famous **singer** someday."},{"sentence":"Magaling na **singer** ang kinuha nilang kumanta sa kasal.","translation":"They hired a good **singer** to perform at the wedding."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na ginagamit upang pagandahin ang anyo ng isang lugar, bagay, o pagkain.
etymology: From "pa-" (prefix for purpose/adornment) + "muti" (an archaic root possibly related to beauty or value).
original_explanation: The extra stuff that makes things pretty. It's the banderitas during a fiesta, the Christmas balls on a tree, the parsley on your steak that you don't actually eat. In short, it's for aesthetic purposes. Your minimalist friend might say it's just clutter, but for Pinoys, more palamuti means more fun.
usage_notes: A very general term for any kind of decoration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay sila ng maraming **palamuti** para sa Pasko.","translation":"They put up a lot of **decorations** for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Ang sibuyas na mura ay ginamit na **palamuti** sa ibabaw ng lugaw.","translation":"The spring onions were used as a **garnish** on top of the porridge."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdudulot o paglikha ng putik sa isang lugar; ang sadyang pagdumi sa pamamagitan ng putik.
original_explanation: This is what kids do after a light rain, much to their parents' horror. 'Huwag kayong magpaputik diyan sa labas!' It's also what happens to your brand new white sneakers when you forget it's rainy season in the Philippines.
usage_notes: Often used as a command or warning, especially to children.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paboritong gawin ng mga bata ang **magpaputik** sa bukid pagkatapos ng ulan.","translation":"The children's favorite thing to do is to **make things muddy** in the field after the rain."},{"sentence":"Sinadya niyang **magpaputik** ng sahig para inisin ang kapatid niya.","translation":"He intentionally **made** the floor **muddy** to annoy his sibling."}]

translation: to become blurry, to become unclear
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkawala ng linaw ng isang bagay, tulad ng paningin, larawan, tubig, o isang konsepto.
etymology: From the root 'labo' (blurriness, obscurity) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: That moment your vision gets fuzzy after staring at your laptop for 12 hours straight in your BPO shift? Your paningin ay lumabo. When a relationship's "label" becomes complicated, the usapan lumabo. It applies to anything that goes from clear to unclear, whether it's your eyesight, a photo, or your situationship.
usage_notes: This is the actor-focus past tense form (naganap). Can be used for vision, images, liquids, or abstract concepts like plans or relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **lumabo** ang paningin ko kaya nagpatingin ako sa doktor.","translation":"My vision suddenly **became blurry**, so I went to see a doctor."},{"sentence":"Mula nang hindi na kami nag-usap, tila **lumabo** ang aming pagkakaibigan.","translation":"Since we stopped talking, our friendship seems to have **become unclear**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na walang anumang ugnayang pampamilya o relasyon sa dugo sa isa pang tao.
etymology: Mula sa "walang" (without) at "kaanu-ano," na tumutukoy sa pagkakamag-anak.
original_explanation: That person you call 'tita' or 'tito' out of respect, but isn't actually your aunt or uncle. In the Philippines, everyone is family until proven otherwise, so when you have to specify someone is **walang-kaanu-ano**, it means they are *really* not a relative, not even a fifth-cousin-twice-removed.
usage_notes: Used specifically to clarify a lack of familial or blood relationship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit mo siya pinatira dito? **Walang-kaanu-ano** naman natin siya.","translation":"Why did you let him live here? He's **not related** to us at all."},{"sentence":"Kahit **walang-kaanu-ano**, tinulungan niya ako na parang tunay na kapatid.","translation":"Even if we're **unrelated**, he helped me like a real sibling."}]

translation: to do laundry (as a paid service); to work as a laundry person
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paglalaba ng damit bilang isang hanapbuhay o serbisyo na may bayad.
original_explanation: This is 'maglaba' but with a payslip. It's when you wash clothes not just for yourself but for others, for a fee. This is the verb for the 'labandera' or 'labandero' who saves busy professionals from drowning in their own 'labahin'. It's a legit side-hustle or full-time job.
usage_notes: Differentiated from 'maglaba' which is generally for one's own clothes. 'Maglabada' implies a service or occupation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naglilabada** si Aling Nena sa mga kapitbahay para kumita ng extra.","translation":"Aling Nena **does laundry for a fee** for the neighbors to earn extra money."},{"sentence":"Balak kong **maglabada** para may pambayad sa upa.","translation":"I plan to **work as a laundry person** to have money for rent."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang legal na pagpapawalang-bisa sa isang kasal, na nagbibigay-daan sa mag-asawa na magpakasal muli.
original_explanation: The ultimate "break na tayo" with legal papers. In the Philippines, **diborsiyo** is the stuff of heated debates, teleserye plot twists, and a dream for many who are stuck in "walang forever." It's the legal un-subscribe button for marriage that we don't have... yet. For now, it's either annulment (pretending it never happened) or legal separation (you're still married, just not living together).
usage_notes: A highly debated topic in the Philippines as it is one of the only two countries in the world without a divorce law.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipino ang sumusuporta sa pagsasabatas ng **diborsiyo** sa bansa.","translation":"Many Filipinos support the legalization of **divorce** in the country."},{"sentence":"Nag-file sila ng **diborsiyo** sa Amerika kung saan sila ikinasal.","translation":"They filed for **divorce** in America where they were married."}]

translation: to have something be pecked (by a bird)
meaning_filipino: Utos na ipakain sa isang ibon o manok sa pamamagitan ng pagpayag na tukain nito ang pagkain.
original_explanation: Literally, to have a bird peck at something. You'd use this when telling someone to feed the chickens with grains. Figuratively, it's what you do with a piece of gossip—you throw it out there for people to pick apart. 'Inilabas niya ang chismis para ipatuka sa mga Marites.'
usage_notes: Commonly used in rural or agricultural settings. The figurative meaning is a modern, slang evolution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing umaga, ang trabaho niya ay **ipatuka** ang mais sa mga manok.","translation":"Every morning, his job is to **have** the corn **pecked** by the chickens."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit at patag na bangkang kahoy na karaniwang matatagpuan sa Silangang Asya, partikular sa Tsina.
etymology: Mula sa Hokkien na "sam-pan" (三板), na nangangahulugang "tatlong tabla".
original_explanation: Think of those classic boats you see in old Chinese martial arts movies. It's not the 'bangka' you'd take to Boracay, but more of a historical river boat. From Hokkien 'sam-pan'.
usage_notes: This word is not commonly used in modern conversation and is mostly found in historical or literary texts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang matandang mangingisda ang naglalayag sa ilog gamit ang kanyang **tsampan**.","translation":"An old fisherman was sailing on the river using his **sampan**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **tsampan** ay dating karaniwang tanawin sa mga ilog ng Maynila.","translation":"**Sampans** were once a common sight on the rivers of Manila."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip panao na tumutukoy sa pag-aari ng isang pangkat na kasama ang kausap.
original_explanation: "Atin" is the ultimate "we" pronoun for possessions. It's inclusive, meaning "ours, and that includes you." It's the possessive form of "tayo". When someone shouts, "Atin 'to!", they're claiming victory for the whole team, barkada, or even the whole country (like when an athlete wins gold). It's the opposite of "amin," which means "ours, but not yours."
usage_notes: 'Atin' is the possessive form of the inclusive pronoun 'tayo' (we, including the listener). It contrasts with 'amin', the possessive of 'kami' (we, excluding the listener).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tagumpay na ito ay para sa **atin** lahat.","translation":"This victory is for all of **us**."},{"sentence":"**Atin** ang Pilipinas, mga kababayan!","translation":"The Philippines is **ours**, my countrymen!"}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang abala; puno ng mga gawain at walang anumang libreng oras.
etymology: Pag-uulit ng salitang 'okupado' para sa pagbibigay-diin.
original_explanation: Level up ng 'okupado.' Ito yung state mo during finals week, year-end closing sa office, o kapag ikaw ang taga-hugas ng plato sa fiesta. You can't even. You literally have no time to even think about being free.
usage_notes: Isang inuulit na anyo ng 'okupado' para sa mas matinding kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi na siya makasama sa lakad dahil **okupadung-okupado** siya sa trabaho.","translation":"He can't join the outing anymore because he is **very busy** at work."},{"sentence":"Naging **okupadung-okupado** ang lahat sa paghahanda para sa kasal.","translation":"Everyone became **swamped** with preparations for the wedding."}]

translation: to cause to believe, to convert to a faith
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos upang hikayatin o akayin ang isang tao na maniwala at magkaroon ng pananampalataya, karaniwan sa isang partikular na diyos o relihiyon.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate goal of a missionary or a preacher. It's the act of convincing someone to join your belief system, whether it's a religion, a philosophy, or the unwavering belief that pineapple belongs on pizza. It's about leading someone to faith.
usage_notes: A deeply religious or spiritual term. The root 'sampalataya' is a noun for faith.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Layunin ng mga misyonero na **magpasampalataya** sa mga katutubo.","translation":"The missionaries' goal is to **convert** the indigenous people **to the faith**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga himala raw ang **nagpasampalataya** sa mga taong dati'y hindi naniniwala.","translation":"His miracles supposedly **caused** the people who previously did not believe **to have faith**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakalat ng malisyosong pahayag, pasulat man o pasalita, na nakasisira sa karangalan, dangal, o mabuting pangalan ng isang tao.
etymology: A compound noun from paninira (slander) and puri (honor).
original_explanation: This is the upgraded, legal-term version of "paninira." It's when the chismis gets so bad you can actually sue someone for it. It's the act of destroying someone's "puri" (honor) with fake news. The ultimate weapon in a high-stakes office or barangay drama.
usage_notes: A specific legal and ethical term. 'Libel' if written, 'slander' if spoken.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari kang kasuhan ng **paninirang-puri** dahil sa iyong mga post sa social media.","translation":"You can be sued for **libel** because of your posts on social media."},{"sentence":"Ang **paninirang-puri** ay isang seryosong krimen sa ilalim ng batas.","translation":"**Defamation** is a serious crime under the law."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakapinagkakatiwalaang katulong o pangalawang pinuno sa isang gawain, organisasyon, o pamumuno.
etymology: Literal translation of 'right hand,' a common idiom in many languages signifying a chief assistant.
original_explanation: This is your 'Beshie for life' in a corporate or project setting. They're the person who knows all the chismis, handles your dirty work, and who you'd trust with your Netflix password. They're the Watson to your Sherlock, the Robin to your Batman, the person who gets the job done while you take the credit.
usage_notes: A common idiom used in both formal and informal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Maria ang **kanang-kamay** ng manager sa opisina.","translation":"Maria is the manager's **right-hand woman** at the office."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing ko siyang **kanang-kamay** sa lahat ng aking mga proyekto.","translation":"I consider him my **trusted aide** in all my projects."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na madaldal, tsismoso, o hindi marunong magtago ng sikreto.
etymology: Mula sa "mahaba" (long) at "dila" (tongue), isang literal na pagsasalin ng konsepto ng pagkakaroon ng 'mahaba at maluwag na dila' na hindi mapigilan sa pagsasalita.
original_explanation: The human version of a live news feed, but for chismis. This person can't keep a secret to save their life. If you tell them something 'between us,' it's already been broadcasted to the whole barangay. The opposite of 'what happens in Vegas, stays in Vegas.'
usage_notes: Isang tambalang salita na ginagamit bilang isang negatibong paglalarawan sa isang taong mahilig magkalat ng tsismis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan mo si Aling Nena, kilala siyang **mahabang-dila** sa buong baryo.","translation":"Avoid Aling Nena, she's known for being **gossipy** throughout the whole village."}]

meaning_filipino: Simula sa lugar na iyon na malayo sa nagsasalita at sa kausap.
original_explanation: The Waze/Google Maps instruction before there was Waze. When your tito gives directions, 'O, pagdating mo sa kanto, mula roon, kumanan ka.' It’s the verbal equivalent of pointing to a vague spot in the distance.
usage_notes: Ang "roon" ay ginagamit kapag ang lokasyon ay malayo sa parehong nagsasalita at nakikinig. Ito ay madalas na ipinagpapalit sa "doon" (mula doon) sa modernong pananalita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumingin ka sa bundok na iyon; **mula roon** ang agos ng ilog.","translation":"Look at that mountain; the river flows **from there**."},{"sentence":"**Mula roon**, kailangan mo pang maglakad ng isang kilometro.","translation":"**From there**, you still need to walk for one kilometer."}]

translation: hot-headed; irritable; in a bad mood
meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pahayag na nangangahulugang galit, iritado, o madaling magalit sa isang partikular na sandali.
etymology: Literally "head is hot." A common idiom for anger or irritability.
original_explanation: This is your boss on a Monday morning, your dad when the Wi-Fi is down, or you after getting a low score on an exam. It’s when your patience is zero and anyone who talks to you is taking a huge risk. "Huwag mo munang kausapin, mainit ang ulo niyan." is a survival tip in any Filipino household or office.
usage_notes: A very common idiom. The person is described as having a "hot head," not that their head is literally hot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umalis muna ako dahil **mainit ang ulo** ni tatay.","translation":"I left for a while because dad was **hot-headed**."},{"sentence":"Laging **mainit ang ulo** niya kapag puyat.","translation":"He's always **in a bad mood** when he lacks sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasunduan, komunikasyon, o pagkilos na isinasagawa sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao o pangkat, lalo na sa larangan ng negosyo o kalakalan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "transacción" at Ingles na "transaction".
original_explanation: That thing you do at the bank, on GCash, or with the tindera at the sari-sari store. It's the official term for any exchange of goods, services, or money. When your friend says "Libre mo muna, babayaran kita sa next sahod," that's the first half of a very long and risky 'transaksiyon'.
usage_notes: Ang baybay na "transaksyon" ay mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na paggamit, bagaman ang "transaksiyon" ay ang pormal at kinikilalang anyo ayon sa pamantayang ortograpiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging matagumpay ang **transaksiyon** sa pagitan ng dalawang kumpanya.","translation":"The **transaction** between the two companies was successful."},{"sentence":"I-double check mo ang detalye bago matapos ang online **transaksiyon**.","translation":"Double-check the details before finishing the online **transaction**."}]

translation: subject of a quarrel; reason for a fight
meaning_filipino: Ang bagay, tao, o isyu na pinagmumulan o sentro ng isang alitan o hindi pagkakasundo.
etymology: From the `pag-…-an` circumfix (denoting cause or locus) and the root `away` (fight).
original_explanation: This is the "pinag-ugatan ng lahat." The last piece of pizza, who gets the remote, or that 'seen' message with no reply. Anything can be a pag-aawayan if you're both hangry or stressed enough. In relationships, the usual suspects are money, time, or selos.
usage_notes: Often used to denote the specific cause or topic of a conflict.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag nating gawing **pag-aawayan** ang maliliit na bagay.","translation":"Let's not make small things the **subject of a quarrel**."},{"sentence":"Ang mana ang naging malaking **pag-aawayan** ng magkakapatid.","translation":"The inheritance became the big **reason for the fight** among the siblings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marka o larawang inilipat sa papel o ibang materyales mula sa isang molde o tipo; ang akto ng pag-imprenta.
original_explanation: Before everything was digital, **limbag** was king. It's the physical mark left by a printing press. Think of your diploma, your birth certificate, or that old newspaper your dad uses to wrap tinapa. It's the OG "publish" button. Today, it can also mean the printed version of anything, like "Nasaan na yung **limbag** na kopya ng report?"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malinaw ang **limbag** ng mga salita sa bagong aklat.","translation":"The **print** of the words in the new book is clear."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagbaligtad o pagtuwad ng isang bagay, tulad ng sasakyan o sisidlan, na nagiging sanhi ng pagkatapon ng laman nito.
original_explanation: That mini heart attack when your coffee mug tips over your laptop? That's 'pagtaob'. Or a boat flipping over in a storm. Or when you're carrying a tray of food and it goes upside down. It's the sudden, disastrous flip that ruins your day (or more).
usage_notes: Can be used literally for objects or figuratively, like a team's standing being overturned.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malakas na alon ang naging sanhi ng **pagtaob** ng maliit na bangka.","translation":"The strong waves caused the **capsizing** of the small boat."},{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siya sa pagbubuhat ng palanggana upang maiwasan ang **pagtaob** nito.","translation":"He was careful in carrying the basin to avoid its **overturning**."}]

translation: to crack; to get a crack
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng lamat o bahagyang sira o paghihiwalay sa isang solidong bagay.
original_explanation: That heart-stopping moment when you drop your phone and pray the screen didn't crack. Or when you see a small crack on your favorite mug. Pwede ring sa lupa, 'pag sobrang tuyot. 'Hala, nabitak 'yung sahig!'
usage_notes: Refers to a fissure or crack appearing on a surface. Different from `mabasag` which means to shatter completely.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa lindol, **nabitak** ang pader ng lumang bahay.","translation":"Because of the earthquake, the wall of the old house **cracked**."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mong huwag **mabitak** ang salamin.","translation":"Be careful not to **crack** the mirror."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng kapatawaran ang isang tao sa kanyang nagawang pagkakamali o kasalanan.
original_explanation: The verb form of every "I'm sorry" flower delivery and apology text. This is what you hope your friend does after you accidentally spoil the ending of their favorite series. It's the core of the classic OPM song lyric, "Patawarin mo ako..." It's harder to do than to say, and it's the basis of a thousand hugot lines about moving on.
usage_notes: The object of this verb is the person being forgiven.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **patawarin** mo ako sa aking mga pagkukulang.","translation":"I hope you **forgive** me for my shortcomings."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **patawarin** ang taong paulit-ulit kang sinasaktan.","translation":"It's hard **to forgive** a person who repeatedly hurts you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos ng paggalugad o pagsisiyasat upang matagpuan ang isang bagay, tao, o impormasyon. Nasa aspetong pangkasalukuyan.
original_explanation: The official state of being for everyone on a BPO graveyard shift (looking for a reason to live), for someone scrolling through job sites ('naghahanap ng work'), or for your tita at a family gathering ('naghahanap ka na ba ng jowa?'). It’s the perpetual search for something, whether it’s your keys, a stable job, or the will to get up in the morning.
usage_notes: A very common verb. The 'ha-' is the reduplication of the first syllable of the root 'hanap', indicating the present tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naghahanap** ako ng bagong apartment na malapit sa opisina.","translation":"I am **looking for** a new apartment near the office."},{"sentence":"Si Maria ay **naghahanap** ng hustisya para sa kanyang kapatid.","translation":"Maria is **seeking** justice for her sibling."}]

meaning_filipino: Itukoy o ipatungkol ang isang sulat, pakete, o mensahe sa isang partikular na tao o lugar. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagharap o pagtugon sa isang isyu o problema.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "i-" at hiram na salitang Ingles na "address."
original_explanation: Two meanings here. First is the LBC/J&T kind: you iadres the package to your Shopee-addict friend. The second is the BPO/corporate kind: "Team, we need to iadres the issue of low CSAT scores." It's about directing something, whether it's a package or a problem.
usage_notes: Isang halimbawa ng Taglish verb. Ang paggamit para sa "pagtugon sa isyu" ay mas karaniwan sa mga pormal o pang-opisina na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**iadres** mo ang sulat na ito sa ating manager.","translation":"Please **address** this letter to our manager."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **iadres** ang mga hinaing ng mga empleyado.","translation":"We need to **address** the employees' complaints."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi makatarungan, labag sa katwiran, o walang sapat at lohikal na dahilan.
