original_explanation: 'Yung bigla ka na lang sinabihan ng boss mo na mag-overtime sa Biyernes ng gabi nang walang dagdag-sahod. **Walang-katwiran**! O 'yung jowa mong nagselos sa ka-work mo na never mo namang nakausap. It's the logic of a toddler throwing a tantrum – it just doesn't make sense.
usage_notes: Often used to protest an unfair action or describe an illogical argument.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang desisyon na umalis nang walang paalam ay **walang-katwiran**.","translation":"His decision to leave without saying goodbye was **unreasonable**."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing ng mga manggagawa na **walang-katwiran** ang biglaang pagtanggal sa kanila.","translation":"The workers consider their sudden dismissal **unjust**."}]

translation: to be soaked, to be immersed
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkalubog o pagkatagal sa isang likido, tulad ng tubig, hanggang sa ito ay lubusang masipsip o mabasa.
original_explanation: What happens to your clothes when you forget them in the washing machine. Figuratively, it's what you do on Netflix all weekend. 'Nagbabad ako sa K-drama.' It's not just getting wet; it's about prolonged exposure, whether to water, a TV series, or your toxic ex's social media profile.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for liquids ('ibabad ang paa sa tubig') or figuratively for being engrossed in an activity ('nagbabad sa pag-aaral'). The active form is 'magbabad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **mababad** sa ulan ang mga sinampay.","translation":"Don't let the hung laundry **get soaked** in the rain."},{"sentence":"Para lumambot ang baboy, kailangan itong **mababad** sa toyo at suka.","translation":"For the pork to become tender, it needs to **be soaked** in soy sauce and vinegar."}]

translation: to commit suicide; to work oneself to death (figurative)
meaning_filipino: Kusang pagkitil sa sariling buhay. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ito ay tumutukoy sa labis na pagtatrabaho o pagpapakahirap hanggang sa maubos ang lakas.
etymology: From the prefix `magpaka-` (to deliberately cause oneself to be) and the root `patay` (dead).
original_explanation: The literal meaning is tragic and serious (to commit suicide). But in true Pinoy fashion, we use it for an OTY (overtime) warrior who's about to pass out from exhaustion. "Huy, 'wag kang magpakamatay sa trabaho, hindi ka niyan mamahalin pabalik!" It's our way of saying "take a break, bes."
usage_notes: The figurative use is very common in workplace contexts to mean 'to overwork'. However, the literal meaning is extremely serious and should be used with sensitivity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpakamatay** sa trabaho dahil walang kapalit ang iyong kalusugan.","translation":"Don't **work yourself to death** because nothing can replace your health."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding depresyon, sinubukan niyang **magpakamatay**.","translation":"Because of severe depression, he tried to **commit suicide**."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng matinding galit o ngalit sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your chill friend when you keep 'seen-zoning' their messages and borrowing their charger without returning it. You're basically pushing their buttons until they transform into the Hulk. Don't **papagngalitin** your BPO team lead by taking too many long coffee breaks.
usage_notes: A stronger form of 'galitin' (to anger). It implies a deeper, more intense rage or fury.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang walang-tigil na pang-aasar niya ay sapat na para **papagngalitin** kahit ang pinakamabait na tao.","translation":"His non-stop teasing is enough **to infuriate** even the kindest person."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **papagngalitin** sa umagang ito.","translation":"Don't **make me rage** this morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang natitiklop na panangga o harang, karaniwang yari sa kahoy at papel o tela, na ginagamit bilang palamuti o upang hatiin ang isang silid.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "biombo", na hango naman sa Hapones na "byōbu" (屏風), na nangangahulugang 'wind wall'.
original_explanation: The OG virtual background. It's that fancy, foldable wall you see in your lola's house, in spas, or in historical dramas. Perfect for hiding a messy corner of your room during a Zoom meeting or for a dramatic reveal where a character was eavesdropping behind it all along.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinago niya ang mga regalo sa likod ng **biyumbo**.","translation":"She hid the gifts behind the **folding screen**."},{"sentence":"Ang antigong **biyumbo** ay may mga dibuho ng mga ibon at bulaklak.","translation":"The antique **room divider** has paintings of birds and flowers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang larawan o disenyo na inilimbag sa isang bagay. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa kabuuang ayos, tindig, o hitsura ng isang tao.
original_explanation: On one hand, it's the print on your T-shirt (e.g., "Ganda ng estampa ng damit mo!"). On the other hand, it's your overall 'porma' or bearing. "Ang ganda ng estampa niya," could mean they carry themselves with confidence and style, like a model walking down the runway... or just someone who looks like they have their life together.
usage_notes: Has two distinct but related meanings: a physical print and a person's physical bearing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagustuhan ko ang **estampa** sa harap ng kamiseta.","translation":"I liked the **print** on the front of the shirt."},{"sentence":"Makikita sa **estampa** ng kanyang paglakad ang kanyang kumpiyansa.","translation":"You can see her confidence in the **posture** of her walk."}]

translation: to vent one's anger on; to make someone the target of
meaning_filipino: Gawing puntirya o pagbuntunan ng galit, inis, o anumang masamang damdamin.
etymology: Mula sa `mapag-` + `diskita` + `-han`. Ang salitang `diskita` ay maaaring hango sa Espanyol na 'desquitar' (gumanti, maglabas ng sama ng loob).
original_explanation: Ito yung nangyayari 'pag bad trip ang boss mo sa bahay tapos ikaw ang nakita sa office. Ikaw ang napag-initan. You become the unwilling "chosen one" for someone's bad mood. Parang sa laro, ikaw yung na-random target ng special attack, wala kang kamalay-malay.
usage_notes: Ang tuon ng pandiwang ito ay ang tao o bagay na pinupuntirya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **mapagdiskitahan** ng galit mo!","translation":"Don't **vent your anger on** me!"},{"sentence":"Kadalasan, ang mga alaga sa bahay ang **napapagdiskitahan** kapag galit ang kanilang amo.","translation":"Often, the house pets **become the target** when their owner is angry."}]

translation: it's fine; no worries; I don't mind
meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang balbal na nagpapahayag na hindi mahalaga ang isang sitwasyon, o na ayos lang ang lahat at hindi ito dapat alalahanin.
etymology: Isang pariralang balbal na pinagsasama ang 'kebs' (whatever) at 'lang' (just/only).
original_explanation: The slightly softer, more reassuring version of 'kebs'. While 'kebs' can sound dismissive, 'kebs lang' is more like 'it's all good, no biggie.' It's what you say when someone apologizes for being late, or when your friend cancels plans. 'Sorry, naubos ko 'yung ulam.' 'Kebs lang, may instant noodles pa.'
usage_notes: Karaniwang-karaniwan sa mga impormal na text at usapan. Ang 'lang' ay nagpapalambot sa maaaring maging dating na pagwawalang-bahala ng 'kebs' lamang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sorry, hindi ako makakasama mamaya. — Okay lang, **kebs lang**!","translation":"Sorry, I can't join later. — It's okay, **no worries**!"},{"sentence":"Nabasag ko yung baso mo. — **Kebs lang**, bibili na lang ako ng bago.","translation":"I broke your glass. — **It's fine**, I'll just buy a new one."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagluto ng pagkain, lalo na ng tinapay o keyk, sa loob ng isang hurno o oven.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'horno' (oven), na nilagyan ng gitlaping '-in-'.
original_explanation: The past tense of what you do to pandesal, that ube cheese pandesal you saw on TikTok, or your quarantine-baking-phase banana bread. If it went into an oven, it was 'hinurno'.
usage_notes: Partikular na tumutukoy sa pagluto sa loob ng isang hurno (oven).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang manok ay masarap dahil **hinurno** ito nang maraming oras.","translation":"The chicken is delicious because it **was baked** for many hours."},{"sentence":"**Hinurno** niya ang paborito kong chocolate chip cookies.","translation":"She **baked** my favorite chocolate chip cookies."}]

meaning_filipino: Mabilis at bahagyang paggalaw o pagpitik ng isang bahagi ng katawan; pagpilipit ng katawan dahil sa sakit, kilig, o pagkaasiwa.
original_explanation: That tiny, involuntary twitch your eye does after pulling an all-nighter to meet a deadline. It's also how you squirm when someone tickles you, or the 'kilig' wiggle you do when your crush finally replies to your IG story. Basically, any small, sudden body movement you can't control.
usage_notes: Often used as a root for the verb 'kumislot' (to twitch) or the noun 'pagkislot' (the act of twitching).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang kumislot ang kanyang talukap, senyales na gising na siya.","translation":"His eyelid suddenly twitched, a sign that he was awake."},{"sentence":"Isang bahagyang **kislot** ng kanyang labi ang nagpakita na hindi siya sang-ayon.","translation":"A slight **twitch** of his lip showed that he did not agree."}]

translation: to lead to, to result in
meaning_filipino: Ang maging dahilan upang umabot o mauwi sa isang partikular na kalagayan, lugar, o wakas.
original_explanation: When your 'one more episode' on Netflix leads to a 3 AM bedtime, your decision ihantong you to a zombie-like state at work the next day. It means 'to lead to an outcome.' It's all about cause and effect. 'Saan kaya tayo ihahantong ng desisyon na ito?' (Where will this decision lead us?).
usage_notes: Often has a slightly formal or dramatic tone, used when discussing consequences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang katamaran ay **naghatong** sa kanyang pagbagsak sa klase.","translation":"His laziness **led to** his failure in class."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **ihantong** tayo ng landas na ito sa magandang kinabukasan.","translation":"I hope this path **leads** us to a good future."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng karelasyon o kasintahan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The official 'bawal sa iba' partner. Siya yung rason kung bakit may laman ang wallet mo... ng picture niya. Siya rin ang ka-chat mo 24/7 at ang dahilan kung bakit 'di ka makasama sa 'boys' night out'. In short, your boss. Also known as 'GF'.
usage_notes: A direct English loanword universally understood and used in the Philippines, often abbreviated as 'GF'. The Tagalog equivalent is 'kasintahan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakilala na ni Mark ang kanyang **girlfriend** sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"Mark finally introduced his **girlfriend** to his parents."},{"sentence":"May **girlfriend** ka na ba?","translation":"Do you have a **girlfriend** already?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mapanlait na termino para sa isang tao na labis na naghahangad ng katanyagan at atensyon, at handang gawin ang lahat, kahit na kahiya-hiya, upang makamit ito.
original_explanation: Also known as 'KSP' (Kulang Sa Pansin) level 99. Ito 'yung gagawin ang lahat para mag-trending—mula sa paggawa ng 'issue' out of nowhere, pag-post ng mga controversial na bagay, o pagsakay sa kasikatan ng iba. Their life motto is 'Any publicity is good publicity.' They live for the likes, shares, and comments, kahit pa puro bashers.
usage_notes: A derogatory and informal term. "Papansin" or "KSP" are more common local equivalents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang pansinin 'yan, isa lang siyang **famewhore** na gustong sumikat.","translation":"Don't mind him, he's just a **famewhore** who wants to get famous."},{"sentence":"Inaakusahan siyang **famewhore** dahil sa sunod-sunod niyang kontrobersyal na posts.","translation":"She is being accused of being a **famewhore** because of her successive controversial posts."}]

translation: to be hit by a vehicle; to be run over
meaning_filipino: Ang aksidenteng pagkabangga o pagsagasa ng isang sasakyan sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
etymology: From ma- (accidental verb prefix) + bundol (a bump, collision).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ultimate fear ng mga tumatawid sa EDSA. 'Yung aksidenteng masagi ka ng motor, o mas malala, mabundol ka ng bus. Ingat sa pagtawid, bes, use the footbridge. "Tingin sa kaliwa, tingin sa kanan, baka ka mabundol."
usage_notes: Specifically refers to being hit by a moving vehicle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Muntik nang **mabundol** ang bata dahil bigla siyang tumakbo sa kalsada.","translation":"The child was almost **hit by a vehicle** because he suddenly ran into the street."},{"sentence":"May pusa na na-**mabundol** sa highway kaninang umaga.","translation":"A cat was **run over** on the highway this morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi matalas; mapurol ang talim.
original_explanation: This is your kitchen knife after a year of slicing green mangoes and opening canned goods when you can't find the can opener. It's the opposite of sharp. It's that feeling when your wit isn't hitting right, or your joke falls flat. "Ang patal ng gunting, 'di makagupit ng papel." Basically, it has lost its edge.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with "mapurol". It primarily refers to blades but can be used metaphorically for intellect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan na nating ihasa ang kutsilyo dahil **patal** na ito.","translation":"We need to sharpen the knife because it's already **blunt**."},{"sentence":"Naging **patal** ang kanyang isip dahil sa kawalan ng ehersisyo sa pag-iisip.","translation":"His mind became **dull** due to lack of mental exercise."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marka (✓) na ginagamit upang ipahiwatig na ang isang bagay ay tama, naberipika, o napili.
original_explanation: The symbol of a job well done, a correct answer in a quiz, or your crush finally viewing your IG story. The opposite of 'ekis'. From English 'check'.
usage_notes: Used in schools, offices, and everyday lists.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **tsek** ang lahat ng natapos mo nang gawain.","translation":"Put a **check** on all the tasks you've finished."},{"sentence":"Puro **tsek** ang papel ko sa pagsusulit!","translation":"My test paper is full of **checkmarks**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakbay sa tubig gamit ang sasakyang-dagat, lalo na kung ito ay may layag.
etymology: From the root word 'layag' (sail) + the '-um-' infix.
original_explanation: The OG way of travel before Cebu Pacific seat sales. It's what ancient Filipinos did to go island-hopping and what you dream of doing on a yacht in Batangas. To lumayag is to literally set sail, whether on a bangka or a big ship, and face the open water.
usage_notes: While it literally means to use a sail, it is now used more generally for traveling by sea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais ng mga mangingisda na **lumayag** habang kalmado ang dagat.","translation":"The fishermen want **to sail** while the sea is calm."},{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, **lumayag** ang ating mga ninuno patungo sa iba't ibang isla.","translation":"In ancient times, our ancestors **sailed** to different islands."}]

translation: To generalize; to include all; to take all
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsama sa lahat sa isang kategorya o paghuhusga nang walang pagtatangi; ang pagkuha sa kabuuan ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you say when someone makes a hasty generalization. "Bakit mo naman nilalahat ang mga lalaki? Hindi naman lahat kami manloloko!" It's the act of putting everyone in the same box. It can also mean "to take it all," like when you go to a buffet and someone tells you, "Huwag mong lahatin 'yung hipon, magtira ka naman!"
usage_notes: Can have a negative connotation when used in the sense of 'generalizing' people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **lahatin** ang mga pulitiko; may iilan pa ring matino.","translation":"Don't **generalize** all politicians; there are still a few decent ones."},{"sentence":"Mukhang lalahatin na niya ang lahat ng pagkain sa mesa.","translation":"It looks like he's going to **take all** the food on the table."}]

translation: to put back; to return something to its container
meaning_filipino: Ang muling paglalagay o pagbabalik ng isang bagay sa dati nitong lalagyan o kinalalagyan.
original_explanation: This is the sequel to "magsilid". It's what you have to do when you take something out and your mom catches you. "Kinuha mo, **magsilid ka na muli**!" (You took it out, now **put it back**!). It's the universal rule of "clean as you go."
usage_notes: A common phrase used to command or describe the act of returning an item to where it was stored.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos mong basahin ang libro, **magsilid ka na muli** nito sa estante.","translation":"After you read the book, **put it back** on the shelf."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwanang nakakalat ang mga gamit, **magsilid ka na muli**.","translation":"Don't leave your things scattered, **put them back again**."}]

translation: an instant; a blink of an eye
meaning_filipino: Isang napakaikling sandali o panahon, katumbas ng bilis ng pagpikit at pagdilat ng mata.
original_explanation: The official Filipino unit of measurement for how fast your sahod (salary) disappears after paying bills. 'Nandiyan lang kanina, nawala sa isang kisapmata.' It’s that magical, fleeting moment before reality hits you. Also used to describe how quickly a crush can ghost you.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang idyoma.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang **kisapmata**, nagbago ang lahat.","translation":"In the **blink of an eye**, everything changed."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang magnanakaw sa isang **kisapmata**.","translation":"The thief disappeared in an **instant**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking gusali o silid na nilagyan ng mga kagamitan para sa mga ehersisyo at palakasan.
original_explanation: Yung lugar kung saan ka nagbubuhat ng bakal para maging fit, pero pagkatapos ay kakain ka ng dalawang serving ng crispy pata. The place you go to "work out" but mostly just take selfies for IG. The modern-day alayan ng pawis.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit ang mas maikling "gym".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ang **dyimnasyum** tuwing Enero dahil sa mga New Year's resolution.","translation":"The **gymnasium** is full every January because of New Year's resolutions."},{"sentence":"Nagkita kami sa **dyimnasyum** ng paaralan para sa praktis ng basketball.","translation":"We met at the school **gymnasium** for basketball practice."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdating o pag-abot sa isang tiyak na lugar, antas, dami, o kalagayan.
etymology: From the root word 'abot' (reach) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're chasing the last jeepney at night and you finally make it—yan ang umabot. Or when your sahod finally *reaches* your bank account after a long, long petsa de peligro. It's the opposite of being 'left behind' by the train, by your crush, or by the latest chismis.
usage_notes: Can refer to physically reaching a place, reaching a certain amount (like a quota), or catching up to someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **umabot** ang sahod ko hanggang sa susunod na kinsenas.","translation":"I hope my salary **reaches** until the next payday."},{"sentence":"Hindi na kami **umabot** sa huling biyahe ng bus.","translation":"We weren't able to **catch** the last bus trip."}]

translation: to change, to alter, to revise
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapalit, pag-iiba, o pagrerebisa sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon upang ito ay maging iba sa dati nitong kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is what your partner asks you to do, but you know it's a trap. "Kailangan mong baguhin 'yang ugali mo!" It's also what you do to your Facebook status from "In a Relationship" to "It's Complicated" after a fight. It's the core of every New Year's resolution.
usage_notes: An object-focused verb. The thing being changed is the direct object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **baguhin** ang ating mga plano dahil sa biglang pag-ulan.","translation":"We need to **change** our plans because of the sudden rain."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **baguhin** ang desisyon ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"He tried to **alter** the decision of his parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Higit sa karaniwan, sapat, o kinakailangang dami, antas, o tindi. Ginagamit din bilang pang-uri na nangangahulugang labis o natira.
etymology: From Spanish 'sobrar' (to be left over, to exceed).
original_explanation: The magic word that turns a compliment into a critique ('Sobra kang payat!') or an expression of intense emotion ('Sobra akong masaya!'). It's also the reason you have three containers of adobo in the fridge from last night's party. It's the Pinoy unit of measurement for 'too much'.
usage_notes: Can function as an adverb meaning 'very' or 'too' (sobrang init), an adjective for 'excessive' (sobra ang pagkain), or a noun for 'leftovers' (May sobra ba?).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sobra** ang init ngayon!","translation":"It's **very** hot today!"},{"sentence":"May **sobra** pa bang kanin?","translation":"Is there any **leftover** rice?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maglagay ng **sobrang** asin.","translation":"Don't put **too much** salt."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga pagkaing inihahanda at ibinebenta sa mga lansangan o pampublikong lugar, karaniwang mabilis kainin at abot-kaya.
original_explanation: The Philippines' national treasure. Think isaw, kwek-kwek, fishball, and banana cue. It's cheap, delicious, and comes with a free side of 'sawsawan anxiety' (choosing between spicy vinegar, sweet sauce, or both). The real test of a strong stomach and an adventurous spirit.
usage_notes: The Taglish term is more common than the literal translation 'pagkaing kalye'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, mag-**street food** tayo pagkatapos ng klase.","translation":"Let's go eat **street food** after class."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong **street food** ay isaw ng manok na may maanghang na suka.","translation":"My favorite **street food** is chicken intestine with spicy vinegar."}]

meaning_filipino: Anyayahan ang isang tao na sumama o lumahok sa isang bagay; ang pag-imbita sa isang partikular na indibidwal.
original_explanation: This is the 'object-focused' version of inviting. It's not just inviting in general; it's you inviting a specific 'them'. '**Yayain** mo si crush sa party!' (Invite your crush to the party!). It’s the hopeful verb you use when planning a group outing and trying to get the whole barkada to actually show up.
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb. The person being invited is the object of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **yayain** si Ana sa iyong kaarawan.","translation":"Don't forget **to invite** Ana to your birthday."},{"sentence":"Sino ang gusto mong **yayain** sa sine?","translation":"Who do you want **to invite** to the movies?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamahusay o pinakamataas na antas ng kahusayan sa lahat.
original_explanation: This is the 'overachiever' level of galing. It's not just good, it's not just great, it's the 'scholar ng bayan,' 'top performer with bonus,' 'employee of the year, for the 5th time' kind of excellence. It's the superlative form, the final boss of being good at something.
usage_notes: Used to describe the absolute peak of skill or quality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kagaling-galingan** niyang mananayaw ay kinilala sa buong mundo.","translation":"Her **most excellent** skill as a dancer was recognized worldwide."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang **kagaling-galingan** sa paglutas ng problema.","translation":"He showed the **very best** in problem-solving."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang batang lalaki na nasa yugto ng pagbibinata, karaniwang nasa pagitan ng pagkabata at pagiging ganap na binata.
etymology: From Spanish *veintillo* (literally 'twenty-cent coin'), used as a diminutive suffix for a young man, influenced by *binata*.
original_explanation: Think of that awkward phase: voice cracking, sudden growth spurts, and a newfound interest in crushes. He's no longer a 'bata' but not yet a full-fledged 'binata'. He's the guy who spends hours on his hair and probably has a K-pop idol as his wallpaper. The female equivalent is 'dalagita'.
usage_notes: Refers to a male teenager. The female counterpart is 'dalagita'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **binatilyo** ay laging naglalaro ng video games sa kanyang kwarto.","translation":"The **teenage boy** is always playing video games in his room."},{"sentence":"Nagrerebelde ang maraming **binatilyo** sa kanilang mga magulang.","translation":"Many **adolescent boys** rebel against their parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na walang moralidad, tuso, at madalas na nanloloko o gumagawa ng masama sa kapwa para sa sariling kapakanan.
original_explanation: Think of the classic kontrabida in a teleserye who steals the family fortune, or the officemate who takes credit for your work with a smirk. They're the smooth-talking but ultimately treacherous character. They'll sell you out for a promo code.
usage_notes: Isang malalim at makalumang salita ng pagtuligsa. Nagpapahiwatig ito ng panlilinlang at masamang hangarin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magtitiwala sa kanya, isa siyang **taong buhong** na puro pansariling interes lang ang iniisip.","translation":"Don't trust him, he's a **scoundrel** who only thinks of his own self-interest."},{"sentence":"Ang **taong buhong** ay nagkunwaring kaibigan para lamang makapanlamang.","translation":"The **rascal** pretended to be a friend only to take advantage."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapahiwatig ng pag-aalinlangan, kawalan ng katiyakan, o isang katamtamang kalidad; hindi maganda at hindi rin pangit.
original_explanation: This is 'medyo' but with commitment issues. It's when you're asked 'Kamusta?' and the answer is neither good nor bad, just a solid 'meh.' It's the official feeling of payday being a week away. 'Yung performance niya? Medyu-medyo lang.'
usage_notes: The reduplication adds a sense of vagueness, uncertainty, or mediocrity compared to just 'medyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinanong ko kung masarap ang luto ko, ang sagot niya ay **medyu-medyo** lang.","translation":"I asked if my cooking was delicious, his answer was just **so-so**."},{"sentence":"**Medyu-medyo** ang naging resulta ng aming proyekto, hindi namin naabot ang target.","translation":"The result of our project was **just okay**, we didn't hit the target."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga tao na may magkakatulad na paniniwala sa relihiyon o pilosopiya, na kadalasang humiwalay mula sa isang mas malaking relihiyon.
original_explanation: This is a group with beliefs that are a little... different from the mainstream. Sometimes it just means a smaller religious denomination. Other times, it's what your tita calls your friend's church that she's never heard of. In movies, this is the group in matching robes chanting in a basement. The meaning can range from "small religious group" to "full-blown creepy cult."
usage_notes: Maaaring magkaroon ng negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig ng pagiging sarado o pagkasobra ng isang grupo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga haka-haka na isang **sekta** ang nasa likod ng mga misteryosong pagkawala.","translation":"There are speculations that a **sect** is behind the mysterious disappearances."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang relihiyon ay nagsimula bilang isang maliit na **sekta** bago ito lumago.","translation":"Their religion started as a small **sect** before it grew."}]

translation: to cause hardship; to put in a tight spot
meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan ng paghihirap, partikular sa aspetong pampinansyal, o pagkakaroon ng kakulangan.
etymology: From 'i-' (causative prefix) + 'ka-' (causative prefix) + 'gipit' (in a tight spot, financially distressed).
original_explanation: That feeling when it's still the 15th of the month but your wallet is already crying for 'petsa de peligro'. The unexpected car repair, the sudden need for a new phone—these are the things that 'ikagigipit' you. It's what puts you in a financially tight spot, forcing you to eat instant noodles for a week.
usage_notes: Almost always refers to financial difficulty or a scarcity of resources.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang pagkawala niya ng trabaho ay **ikinagipit** ng buong pamilya.","translation":"His sudden job loss **caused hardship** for the whole family."},{"sentence":"Mag-ipon ka para hindi ka magkaroon ng problemang **ikagigipit** mo sa hinaharap.","translation":"Save money so you won't have problems that will **put you in a tight spot** in the future."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakalungkot at masaklap na pangyayari; isang matinding kabiguan o kamalasan.
etymology: A phrase composed of `malaki` (big) and `kasawian` (misfortune, from the root 'sawi' meaning ill-fated).
original_explanation: This is a level up from 'bad trip.' It's a 'great misfortune.' Think: finding out your 13th-month pay went straight to taxes, or your favorite milk tea shop closing down permanently. It's the universe basically saying, 'Suffer, peasant.'
usage_notes: Often used in a more formal or dramatic context to describe a tragic event, a major failure, or a significant loss.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturing niyang **malaking kasawian** ang hindi pagpasa sa board exam.","translation":"He considers not passing the board exam a **great misfortune**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mag-ipon o magtipon ng mga bagay bilang isang libangan, propesyon, o para sa isang partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa Funko Pops, K-Pop photocards, o Starbucks tumblers. Hindi 'yan gastos, investment 'yan! **Kumolekta** ka lang nang **kumolekta** hanggang mapuno ang kwarto mo.
usage_notes: Broader than `kumobra`. `Kumolekta` is for collecting items (hobby), garbage, or data, while `kumobra` is specifically for collecting payment/debt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **kumolekta** ng mga lumang selyo.","translation":"He likes **to collect** old stamps."},{"sentence":"Ang gobyerno ay nagpapadala ng mga tao upang **kumolekta** ng datos para sa census.","translation":"The government sends people **to collect** data for the census."}]

translation: state of being a gay man; male homosexuality
meaning_filipino: Ang katangian, oryentasyon, o kalagayan ng pagiging isang bakla o lalaking homoseksuwal.
original_explanation: It’s the journey and the identity of being a gay man in the Philippines. It’s the flair, the wit, the strength, the "beki" language, and the unwavering ability to find the best milk tea place. It's about embracing one's identity with fabulousness and courage. "Awrah!"
usage_notes: Refers specifically to male homosexuality and the cultural identity associated with it in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkabakla** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng kanyang pagkatao.","translation":"His **state of being gay** is an important part of his identity."},{"sentence":"Marami siyang natutunan tungkol sa sarili sa kanyang pagtanggap sa kanyang **pagkabakla**.","translation":"He learned a lot about himself in his journey of accepting his **homosexuality**."}]

translation: To be touched lightly; to be grazed
meaning_filipino: Ang bahagyang masagi o madantayan ng isang bagay o tao; isang magaan at madalas ay hindi sinasadyang pagdikit.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment sa jeep na biglang nag-preno, tapos nadiitan mo 'yung katabi mong cute. Awkward! It's a light, often accidental touch. Not a full-on 'hawak', just a 'dantay' or 'sagi'. It's the physical version of a subtle hint.
usage_notes: 'Madiitan' is less common than 'masagi' or 'madikitan'. 'Diit' implies a light but firm press, while 'sagi' is more of a graze.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang may makatabi sa bus dahil ayaw niyang **madiitan**.","translation":"He doesn't want to sit next to anyone on the bus because he doesn't want **to be touched**."},{"sentence":"**Nadiitan** ng mainit na kaldero ang kanyang braso.","translation":"Her arm **was lightly touched** by the hot pot."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa "private message" o pribadong mensahe; isang direktang mensahe sa isang social media platform na tanging ang nagpadala at tumanggap lamang ang nakakabasa.
original_explanation: Stands for "private message." The backbone of Filipino online shopping. The magic words you see after a seller posts an item: "Price? PM sent." It's where the real 'chismis' and 'tawaran' (haggling) happens, away from the public eye.
usage_notes: A universally understood term in Filipino online spaces. Often used interchangeably with 'DM' (direct message).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Check mo **pm** ko sa'yo, 'te.","translation":"Check the **pm** I sent you, sis."},{"sentence":"Laging puno ang **pm** ng mga online seller.","translation":"The **pm** inbox of online sellers is always full."}]

translation: to become watery; to add water
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging malabnaw dahil sa pagdami ng tubig; o ang sadyang pagdaragdag ng tubig.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your sinigang when you add too much water to stretch it for unexpected guests. 'Hala, nagtubig 'yung sauce!' It can also mean to intentionally add water, like when you're trying to make your shampoo last longer.
usage_notes: Can refer to something naturally becoming watery (like a wound) or the act of adding water to something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magtubig** ang sugat niya kaya dinala na siya sa ospital.","translation":"His wound started to **become watery** so he was brought to the hospital."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **magtubig** sa niluluto mong adobo para hindi mawala ang lasa.","translation":"Don't **add too much water** to the adobo you're cooking so the flavor isn't lost."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng panghihimasok o paglahok sa isang usapin, gawain, o buhay ng ibang tao, na kadalasan ay walang pahintulot.
etymology: From pakiki- (prefix for social participation) + alam (know). The act of participating in knowing.
original_explanation: This is the noun form of 'pakialam'. It's the *act* of being a pakialamera/o. It’s your boss's "gentle suggestion" on your weekend plans, or your landlord asking why you had guests over. It's the unsolicited advice that feels more like a command. Basically, crossing boundaries.
usage_notes: Carries a more negative connotation than 'pakialam'. It specifically refers to the act of interfering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ko ng **pakikialam** mula sa aking mga biyenan.","translation":"I don't want **interference** from my in-laws."},{"sentence":"Ang labis na **pakikialam** ng gobyerno ay ikinabahala ng mga negosyante.","translation":"The government's excessive **meddling** worried the business owners."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagmula o naninirahan sa bansang Ireland, o may lahing mula roon.
original_explanation: The folks from the land of St. Patrick, Guinness, and U2. Kilala sila sa kanilang mga pub, pagdiriwang ng St. Patrick's Day, at sa pagiging masayahin. Kung may kaibigan kang mahilig sa green beer tuwing March, baka may dugong Irlandes.
usage_notes: The adjective form is also 'Irlandes' (e.g., 'kulturang Irlandes' - Irish culture). The country is 'Irelanda'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **Irlandes** ang lumipat sa Amerika noong ika-19 na siglo.","translation":"Many **Irish** people moved to America in the 19th century."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang banda ay pinangungunahan ng isang **Irlandes**.","translation":"His favorite band is fronted by an **Irishman**."}]

translation: to meet by chance, to encounter
meaning_filipino: Ang di-sinasadyang pagkikita o pagkakita sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The universe's way of playing matchmaker... or just messing with you. It's when you bump into your ex at the mall when you look like a total 'pambahay' mess. 'Sana all, **matagpo** ang 'The One' sa coffee shop.'
usage_notes: Refers to an unplanned meeting. Often used in literary or formal contexts. The more common verb form in everyday speech is 'makatagpo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa 'di inaasahang pagkakataon, baka **matagpo** mo ang iyong kapalaran.","translation":"In an unexpected moment, you might **encounter** your destiny."},{"sentence":"Umaasa siyang **matagpo** muli ang babaeng tumulong sa kanya.","translation":"He hopes to **meet by chance** again the woman who helped him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang labis na pagbibigay ng luho, kagustuhan, o pag-aalaga sa isang tao, lalo na sa isang bata, na maaaring magresulta sa masamang pag-uugali.
original_explanation: When your parents give you everything you want, and now you're an adult who can't handle the word "no". It's the reason why some kids throw a tantrum in the mall for a toy, or why your pet dog thinks he's the king of the house. The art of creating a "special snowflake".
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation, implying that the pampering is excessive and will lead to negative traits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang labis na **pagpapalayaw** sa bata ay maaaring makasama sa kanyang paglaki.","translation":"The excessive **spoiling** of a child can be detrimental to their development."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagpapalayaw** ng kanyang lola, lumaki siyang hindi marunong sa gawaing-bahay.","translation":"Because of his grandmother's **pampering**, he grew up not knowing any household chores."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng saklolo, suporta, o anumang uri ng kalinga sa isang taong nangangailangan.
original_explanation: That thing your friend asks for when they're moving apartments, but you're suddenly "busy." Also, what you scream internally during a surprise quiz. "Tulong!" is the Pinoy version of "SOS!"
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ('tulong') or as the root for verbs like 'tumulong' (to help) and 'tulungan' (to help someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humingi siya ng **tulong** para buhatin ang mga kahon.","translation":"She asked for **help** to lift the boxes."},{"sentence":"Malaking **tulong** ang iyong donasyon sa mga biktima ng baha.","translation":"Your donation is a big **help** to the flood victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o kilos na tapat, hindi nagkukunwari, at walang anumang itinatagong motibo o pagkukunwari.
original_explanation: This is your friend who tells you, 'Uy, tumataba ka,' not to be mean, but because they're just being real. No filters, no plastic, just pure, unadulterated honesty. Sila yung hindi 'plastikan,' as in, what you see is what you get.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang katangian ng isang tao o ang kalikasan ng kanilang mga kilos, na nagbibigay-diin sa pagiging totoo at tapat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humanga ako sa kanyang **walang-pagbabalatkayo** na pag-amin sa kanyang pagkakamali.","translation":"I admired his **sincere** admission of his mistake."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang ngiti ay **walang-pagbabalatkayo**; ramdam mo ang tunay na saya.","translation":"Her smile is **without disguise**; you can feel the genuine happiness."}]

meaning_filipino: Katumbas ng salitangkanto; mga salitang impormal na karaniwang naririnig sa lansangan at maaaring ituring na magaspang o bulgar.
etymology: Isang tambalang salita mula sa "salita" (word) at "lansangan" (street).
original_explanation: Basically the twin brother of 'salitangkanto'. It's the unfiltered, raw vocabulary you'd hear in a crowded palengke, a jeepney ride during rush hour, or a heated basketball game sa court. It can range from creative slang to words your lola would wash your mouth out with soap for saying.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'salitangkanto' ngunit maaaring magkaroon ng konotasyon na mas magaspang o bulgar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan mong gumamit ng mga **salitang-lansangan** kapag kausap mo ang iyong mga guro.","translation":"Avoid using **street slang** when talking to your teachers."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **salitang-lansangan** ang usapan ng mga tsuper sa terminal.","translation":"The conversation of the drivers at the terminal is full of **street slang**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng isang bagay tulad ng lubid o pisi upang pagkabitin, pag-ugnayin, o pagbigkisin ang dalawa o higit pang bagay.
original_explanation: Like when you tie your shoelaces, or when you finally 'tie the knot' and your single friends post 'Sana all.' It's about connecting things, whether it's a package from Shopee or your life to someone else's.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha niya ang pisi at **tumali** sa kahon para hindi ito mabuksan.","translation":"He took the string and **tied** the box so it wouldn't open."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng kawalan ng galang, kalaswaan, o kahalayan sa kilos, pananalita, o anyo.
original_explanation: That tito at the family reunion whose jokes make everyone cringe. Or that text from a random stranger that makes you want to throw your phone. It's the kind of behavior that's R-18, not safe for work, and definitely not something you'd show your lola.
usage_notes: A strong word used to describe actions, speech, or materials that are offensive to morality or decency.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan ang paggamit ng **masalaulang** pananalita, lalo na sa harap ng mga bata.","translation":"Avoid using **vulgar** language, especially in front of children."},{"sentence":"Itinuring nilang **masalaula** ang palabas kaya ito ay ipinagbawal.","translation":"They considered the show **obscene**, which is why it was banned."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o sisidlan kung saan inilalagay o itinatago ang isang bagay para sa kaligtasan o pangangalaga.
etymology: From pag- (prefix) + lagak (to deposit) + -an (locative suffix), creating a noun that means 'a place to deposit things'.
original_explanation: This is your LBC 'Kahit Saan, Padala' box, your bank's safety deposit box, or that special 'tago na alkansya' for your travel fund. A paglagakan is any place you entrust your valuables, whether it's your pera, your alahas, or your secret stash of Choc-Nut.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or financial contexts, like depositing money or entrusting something valuable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bangko ang pinakakaraniwang **paglagakan** ng pera ng mga tao.","translation":"The bank is the most common **depository** for people's money."},{"sentence":"Ginawa niyang **paglagakan** ng mga lumang liham ang isang baul na kahoy.","translation":"She used a wooden chest as a **place for safekeeping** for old letters."}]

translation: to throw; to hurl; to cast
meaning_filipino: Ang paghagis o pagbatsá ng isang bagay nang may buong lakas patungo sa isang direksyon o target.
original_explanation: A more dramatic and forceful way to say 'throw'. It's not just tossing a ball; it's hurling a stone with intent. This is the word Darna uses before she throws that big rock. "Sino ang maglalakas-loob na ipukol ang unang bato?" (Who will dare to cast the first stone?).
usage_notes: Has a slightly archaic or literary feel compared to 'ihagis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Galit na **ipinukol** ng lalaki ang bote sa pader.","translation":"The man angrily **threw** the bottle at the wall."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ipukol** sa iba ang sisi para sa iyong mga pagkakamali.","translation":"Do not **cast** the blame on others for your mistakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang paglagay ng paa sa ibabaw ng isang bagay o tao.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (pandiwa ng kakayahan/di-sinasadya) + `tapak` + hulaping `-an`.
original_explanation: We've all been there. Walking barefoot in the dark and then—ouch!—**natapakan** mo 'yung Lego brick. Or when you're in a crowded LRT and you accidentally step on someone's pristine white sneakers. The immediate, awkward "Ay, sorry po!" is the required follow-up. Can also be used figuratively for stepping on someone's pride.
usage_notes: Ang unlaping `ma-` dito ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang aksidente o hindi sinasadyang kilos. Ang sadyang kilos ay "tapakan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa paglalakad at baka may **matapakan** kang bubog.","translation":"Be careful when you walk, you might **step on** broken glass."},{"sentence":"Pasensya na, hindi ko sinasadyang **matapakan** ang iyong paa.","translation":"I'm sorry, I didn't mean to **step on** your foot."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makaramdam ng inggit o pagnanasa sa tagumpay, katangian, o pag-aari ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: That feeling you get scrolling through Instagram and seeing everyone's travel photos while you're stuck in traffic. It's that low-key 'sana all' turning into a slight bitterness. That's `mahili`. It's the cousin of `mainggit`.
usage_notes: Less common than 'mainggit' but carries a similar meaning. 'Hili' is a more classic or literary root for envy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mahili** sa narating ng iyong kaibigan; magsumikap ka rin.","translation":"Don't **be envious** of what your friend has achieved; work hard too."},{"sentence":"Tila siya ay **nahili** sa bagong laruan ng kanyang kapatid.","translation":"It seems he **became envious** of his sibling's new toy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng abaniko upang paypayan ang isang tao o bagay para magbigay ng hangin.
original_explanation: What you do for your lola when it's hot and there's a brownout. It's the manual, non-electric aircon. The '-han' at the end means you're doing it *for* someone. 'Abanikuhan mo naman ako, iho.' is a classic lola line.
usage_notes: The root word 'abaniko' refers to the hand fan itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari mo ba akong **abanikuhan**? Sobrang init.","translation":"Can you **fan me**? It's so hot."}]

translation: will be able to be used; can be used; will be useful
meaning_filipino: Nasa hinaharap na anyo ng pandiwa. Nagsasaad na ang isang bagay ay mayroong silbi, pakinabang, o maaaring gamitin sa darating na panahon.
etymology: From 'ma-' + repetition of the first syllable of the root ('ga-mit' -> 'ga-gamit'). This indicates the future potential aspect.
original_explanation: That 'Sayang, itapon' feeling? The opposite of that is 'magagamit pa 'to!' This is the mantra of every Filipino mom hoarding plastic containers, empty ice cream tubs, and 'good' paper bags. It's the future tense of resourcefulness. You're not a hoarder, you're just... prepared for a future where that broken electric fan *might* be useful for spare parts.
usage_notes: This is the future tense potential form, meaning 'will be able to be used' or 'will be usable.' It's different from 'gagamitin' which means 'will use.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itabi mo iyang lumang damit, baka **magagamit** pa bilang basahan.","translation":"Keep those old clothes, they **can be used** as rags."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng natutunan mo sa eskwela ay **magagamit** mo sa iyong kinabukasan.","translation":"Everything you've learned in school **will be useful** for your future."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malakas na tunog ng pagbagsak ng isang mabigat na bagay; tumutukoy din sa pagkabigo sa isang pagsusulit, gawain, o layunin.
etymology: From `pagka-` (gerund/manner prefix) + `lagpak` (to fall with a thud).
original_explanation: The sound your dreams make when they hit the pavement. It's the heavy thud of your bag when you get home from a toxic workday. Figuratively, it’s the ultimate "bagsak" – failing an exam, bombing a job interview, or when your "sure-win" business idea doesn't take off. The sound is "lagapak!" and the feeling is pagkalagpak.
usage_notes: Can be both literal (a physical fall) and figurative (a failure).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **pagkalagpak** ng mga libro mula sa itaas.","translation":"I heard the **thud** of the books from upstairs."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkalagpak** sa huling pagsusulit ay naging aral sa kanya.","translation":"His **failure** in the last exam became a lesson for him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maputing panlabas na bahagi ng eyeball na pumapalibot sa iris.
original_explanation: 'Yung part ng mata mo na namumula kapag puyat ka sa kakapanood ng K-drama o sa kaka-overtime. It's the background of your eye, the part that makes the colored part (iris) pop.
usage_notes: Isang tambalang pangngalan (compound noun).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namumula ang **puti ng kanyang mga mata** dahil sa kakulangan sa tulog.","translation":"The **white of his eyes** is red due to lack of sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na walang permanenteng tirahan o tiyak na patutunguhan, at palaging nasa labas na naglalakad-lakad o gumagala.
original_explanation: The OG 'laagan'. Before 'travel goals,' there was this. This could be someone who's genuinely homeless, or it could be your friend who's always out, never at home, jumping from one gimmick to another. The 'seen-zoned' message master because they're always 'on the way.'
usage_notes: Can have a negative connotation, implying aimlessness or homelessness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan ng pulis ang mga **taong pagala-gala** sa kalye tuwing gabi.","translation":"The police reprimanded the **people loitering** on the street every night."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na hindi gumagana nang maayos, wala sa tamang ayos, o may sira.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung utak mo 'pag Lunes ng umaga at hindi pa nagkakape. O 'yung schedule ng jowa mong seaman, laging disareglado kaya LDR ang bagsak. Pwede ring 'yung siklo ng buwanang dalaw na hindi mo maintindihan kung kailan darating.
usage_notes: Often used for machines, schedules, or bodily functions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **disareglado** ang tulog ko dahil sa pag-aalala.","translation":"My sleep became **irregular** because of worry."},{"sentence":"**Disareglado** na naman ang Wi-Fi, kaya hindi ako makapag-submit ng report.","translation":"The Wi-Fi is **malfunctioning** again, so I can't submit my report."}]

translation: to make abundant, to cause to be plentiful
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpaparami o pagpapayaman sa isang bagay upang ito ay maging masagana o sagana sa dami.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate goal of every Filipino handaan: to have so much food that it overflows. Think of a farmer praying for rain to **magpasagana** the harvest, or a company giving huge bonuses to **magpasagana** the employees' Christmas. It’s the verb form of 'more is more.'
usage_notes: Often used in the context of food, blessings, harvest, or wealth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mabuting patubig ay **magpapasagana** sa ani ng mga magsasaka.","translation":"Good irrigation will **make the farmers' harvest abundant**."},{"sentence":"Nanalangin sila para **magpasagana** ang biyaya sa kanilang pamilya.","translation":"They prayed to **cause blessings to be plentiful** for their family."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o kumpanya na sumasang-ayon, sa pamamagitan ng isang kontrata, na isagawa ang isang partikular na trabaho o proyekto para sa isang takdang halaga.
etymology: From 'mang-' (prefix for doer of action) + reduplicated first syllable 'kon-' + 'kontrata' (from Spanish 'contrata', contract).
original_explanation: The person you hire to build your dream house, who might become the villain in your 'sakit ng ulo' story. Master of the phrases 'On the way na po ang materyales' and 'Next week, sure na po 'yan.' A good one is a blessing; a bad one is a future episode of a Tulfo show.
usage_notes: While it can refer to any person working on contract, it most commonly refers to a building or construction contractor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-usap na kami ng **mangongontrata** tungkol sa badyet para sa renobasyon.","translation":"We already spoke with the **contractor** about the budget for the renovation."},{"sentence":"Isang mapagkakatiwalaang **mangongontrata** ang kailangan para sa proyektong ito.","translation":"A trustworthy **contractor** is needed for this project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paunang salita o panimulang bahagi ng isang akdang pampanitikan o dula na nagsisilbing introduksyon.
original_explanation: Ito yung chapter bago ang Chapter 1 na madalas mong i-skip pero importante pala sa plot. Parang sa relasyon, ito yung "getting to know" stage; hindi pa kayo pero may setup na. Ang prolog ang nagbibigay ng context bago pa man magsimula ang tunay na drama.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa panitikan, teatro, at pelikula. Ang Tagalog na katumbas ay "prologo" o "paunang salita".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **prolog** ng nobela ay naglalahad ng mga pangyayari bago ang pangunahing kuwento.","translation":"The novel's **prologue** presents the events before the main story."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong laktawan ang **prolog** dahil nandoon ang mahahalagang detalye.","translation":"Don't skip the **prologue** because the important details are there."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na nawalan ng isa o higit pang ngipin, partikular sa harap. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang kilos na padalos-dalos o walang sapat na pag-iisip.
original_explanation: 'Yung ngiti mong parang keyboard na may kulang na isang key. Or 'yung desisyon mong mag-resign nang walang backup plan—that's a 'bungaw' move, bes. It's either physically toothless or mentally reckless.
usage_notes: The meaning "harebrained" or "rash" is less common but still used, often to describe an impulsive, poorly thought-out action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tawa nang tawa ang bata kahit **bungaw** na siya.","translation":"The child kept laughing even though he was already **toothless**."},{"sentence":"Isang **bungaw** na desisyon ang umutang para lang sa bagong cellphone.","translation":"Taking out a loan just for a new cellphone is a **rash** decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghihiwalay ng butil ng palay o ibang anihin mula sa tangkay nito, karaniwang ginagawa sa pamamagitan ng pagpalo, pagyapak, o paggamit ng makina.
original_explanation: Before there were rice mills, there was 'pagiik'. It's the agricultural equivalent of a very intense dance party where farmers stomp on harvested rice stalks to separate the grains. Think of it as the original, manual method of 'unboxing' your unli-rice.
usage_notes: Primarily used in an agricultural context. It's a classic term associated with rice farming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagiik** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng proseso ng pag-aani ng palay.","translation":"**Threshing** is an important part of the rice harvesting process."},{"sentence":"Ginamit nila ang isang malaking makina para mapabilis ang **pagiik**.","translation":"They used a large machine to speed up the **threshing**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpulupot ng mga braso sa isang tao o bagay; ang pagsasagawa ng isang yakap. Ginagamit din sa metaporikal na paraan para sa pagtanggap sa isang ideya o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is the command form of 'yakap.' It's what you do when a simple noun won't cut it. 'Yakapin mo siya!' is the instruction when your friend is crying. It can also be used figuratively, like 'Yakapin ang pagbabago' (Embrace change) or 'Yakapin ang pangarap' (Embrace your dreams). From physical comfort to motivational poster realness.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The actor-focus counterpart is 'yumakap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **yakapin** ang aking mga magulang pag-uwi ko.","translation":"I want **to hug** my parents when I get home."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **yakapin** ang mga bagong hamon sa buhay.","translation":"We need **to embrace** the new challenges in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bigas na niluto sa tubig hanggang sa lumambot at maging kanin.
original_explanation: The foundation of every Filipino meal. The one thing you CANNOT run out of. If someone asks "May sinaing pa?" they're not just asking about rice, they're asking about the possibility of life, hope, and another round of ulam. Running out of `sinaing` is a low-key family crisis.
usage_notes: Can refer to the cooked rice itself or the act/result of cooking rice. Interchangeable with `kanin` in many contexts, but `sinaing` often emphasizes that it was just cooked.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Amoy pa lang ng bagong **sinaing** ay nakakagutom na.","translation":"Just the smell of newly **cooked rice** is enough to make one hungry."},{"sentence":"Pakitakpan ang **sinaing** para hindi pamahayan ng langgam.","translation":"Please cover the **cooked rice** so ants don't get into it."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagkutya; may ugaling manlibak o laitin ang iba sa paraang pasaring o direkta.
original_explanation: The language of your frenemy. 'Yung "Wow, ang ganda ng suot mo... para sa Halloween." Sarcasm is their love language, and they use it to make fun of people subtly (or not-so-subtly). It's the verbal version of an eye-roll.
usage_notes: Describes a person's way of speaking or general attitude.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala sa kanyang mga **mapangutyang** komento.","translation":"Don't worry about his **mocking** comments."},{"sentence":"Isang **mapangutyang** ngiti ang sumilay sa kanyang labi.","translation":"A **derisive** smile appeared on his lips."}]

translation: to originate from, to start from
meaning_filipino: Magsimula o manggaling sa isang partikular na punto, panahon, o pinagmulan.
original_explanation: This is the official starting gun for anything. "Magmula ngayon, diet na ako." is the national anthem of every Monday. It's the 'effective today' memo from your boss, but for life's (often broken) promises.
usage_notes: Often used with 'sa' or 'kay' to indicate the starting point or person. Can also be used with 'nang' for a point in time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magmula** sa araw na ito, bawal na ang plastik sa aming lungsod.","translation":"**Starting** from this day, plastic is now forbidden in our city."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ko sa'yo ay **magmula** sa unang beses na nakita kita.","translation":"My love for you **started from** the first time I saw you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglalagay o pagpapahid ng manipis na patong ng nikel sa ibabaw ng isang metal na bagay.
original_explanation: The verb form of making something 'nikelado'. It's what you ask the machine shop to do to your tito's old revolver to make it look brand new again. 'Paki-nikeladuhin mo nga itong piyesa ng motor ko para 'di kalawangin at para pogi tingnan.' It's the act of giving something that shiny, protective, anti-rust bling.
usage_notes: A very specific technical verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagawa niya sa platero na **nikeladuhin** ang kanyang lumang sinturon.","translation":"He had the silversmith **nickel-plate** his old belt buckle."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang bayad para **nikeladuhin** ang mga parte ng bisikleta?","translation":"How much does it cost **to nickel-plate** the bicycle parts?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na radioactive, mabigat, at kulay pilak-puti na may simbolong U at atomic number na 92.
original_explanation: 'Yung element na naririnig mo sa science class o sa mga pelikula tungkol sa nuclear power at a-bombs. Hindi ito 'yung tatanungin mo sa palengke. Kung may uranyo ka sa bahay, mas malaki pa sa Meralco bill ang problema mo.
usage_notes: Strictly a scientific and technical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **uranyo** ay ginagamit sa pagbuo ng nuclear energy.","translation":"**Uranium** is used in the creation of nuclear energy."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentipiko ang mga epekto ng **uranyo** sa kalikasan.","translation":"Scientists are studying the effects of **uranium** on the environment."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagtatanong o nagsasagawa ng pagtatanong upang makakuha ng impormasyon, karaniwan sa isang pormal na sitwasyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'taga-' (tagagawa), 'pag-' (nagpapangalan), at salitang-ugat na 'tanong'.
original_explanation: The person whose job is to ask the questions. Pwedeng sa job interview, sa isang police investigation, or yung panelist sa pageant na nagpapa-tense sa mga kandidata. Sila yung 'May I ask a question?' personified.
usage_notes: Maaaring neutral na 'interviewer' o mas matinding 'interrogator' depende sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Handa na ang mga kandidato para sa mga **tagapagtanong**.","translation":"The candidates are ready for the **questioners**."},{"sentence":"Naging mahigpit ang **tagapagtanong** sa isinagawang imbestigasyon.","translation":"The **interrogator** was strict during the investigation."}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pang-uri, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang bagay na hugis-bilog. Bilang pangngalan, ito ay isang opisyal na sulat o anunsyo na ipinamamahagi sa maraming tao.
original_explanation: As an adjective, it's something shaped like a circle, like a pizza or your logic when arguing with your parents. As a noun, it's that memo from HR that everyone gets but nobody reads until their boss asks about it. "May bagong sirkular, bawal na daw mag-TikTok sa office."
usage_notes: May dalawang natatanging kahulugan: bilang pang-uri (hugis) at bilang pangngalan (memo/anunsyo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng mesang **sirkular** para sa kanilang silid-kainan.","translation":"She bought a **circular** table for their dining room."},{"sentence":"Naglabas ng **sirkular** ang gobyerno tungkol sa mga bagong patakaran sa trapiko.","translation":"The government issued a **memorandum** about the new traffic rules."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghila sa isang bagay o tao nang may puwersa patungo sa direksyon ng gumagawa ng kilos.
original_explanation: It's the command form of 'to pull.' Like when your friend is trying to leave the party and you grab their arm and say, 'Wait, one more song!' Or when you're trying to start a stubborn lawnmower. It's also used figuratively, like when you feel 'hinahatak' (being pulled) back to your ex, even though you know it's a bad idea. A classic case of emotional gravity.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus infinitive/command form of the root word 'hatak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **hatakin** ang pisi, baka mapatid.","translation":"Don't **pull** the string, it might break."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **hatakin** ang atensyon ng guro.","translation":"She tried to **pull** (attract) the teacher's attention."}]

meaning_filipino: Pera na madaling magamit o makuha para sa agarang pagbabayad; hindi nakatali sa pamumuhunan o iba pang ari-arian.
original_explanation: This is your 'emergency fund' before 'emergency fund' was a cool financial term. It's the cash your nanay keeps in a biscuit can, or the money you have ready for the COD delivery from Shopee or Lazada. It's liquid, baby!
usage_notes: A common term in business and finance, but also used in everyday contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng **handang salapi** para sa mga hindi inaasahang gastusin.","translation":"We need **ready cash** for unexpected expenses."},{"sentence":"Laging may **handang salapi** ang negosyante para sa mga bagong oportunidad.","translation":"The businessman always has **cash on hand** for new opportunities."}]

translation: to happen to go to; to end up at
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang makarating sa isang lugar o kalagayan.
original_explanation: Yung akala mo sa Megamall ka pupunta pero dahil sa traffic at maling Waze-turn, sa Pasig ka na napunta. Or when you're just browsing Shopee for fun and you suddenly end up at the checkout page with 10 items in your cart. It's the 'paano ako napunta dito?' moment of life.
usage_notes: `Mapunta` or `napunta` implies an accidental or unplanned arrival at a location or situation. Contrast with `pumunta` (to go, intentional).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa maling direksyon, sa kabilang bayan kami **napunta**.","translation":"Because of wrong directions, we **ended up in** the next town."},{"sentence":"Sino'ng mag-aakala na sa ganitong sitwasyon tayo **mapapunta**?","translation":"Who would have thought we would **end up in** this kind of situation?"}]

translation: to contort; to twist the body unnaturally
meaning_filipino: Ibaluktot o pilipitin ang katawan sa paraang hindi karaniwan o natural.
etymology: Mula sa 'balikaw', na maaari ring may kaugnayan sa pagiging baluktot o pilipit, + hulaping pandiwa na '-in'.
original_explanation: Imagine seeing someone in a horror movie whose body starts twisting in ways it shouldn't. That's 'balikawin'. It's the kind of contortion that makes you go 'Nope!' and look away. It’s an unnatural, creepy kind of twist.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang napaka-espesipiko at bihirang pandiwa. Ipinapahiwatig nito ang isang pwersahan at hindi natural na pagpilipit, kadalasan ng mga braso, binti, o buong katawan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang sakit, tila **binabalikaw** ang kanyang buong katawan.","translation":"From so much pain, it seemed as if his whole body was being **contorted**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **balikawin** ang braso mo nang ganyan, baka mapilayan ka.","translation":"Don't **twist** your arm like that, you might get a sprain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi o yugto ng isang aklat, kuwento, o maging sa buhay ng isang tao.
etymology: Related to 'kaban' (chest), as if opening a new section or compartment of a story.
original_explanation: It's a chapter, both literally in books like Noli Me Tángere, and figuratively in life. That toxic relationship? 'Tapos na ang kabanata na 'yan.' That new job in BGC? 'Bagong kabanata.' It's how Filipinos frame new beginnings and dramatic endings. It's the 'next episode' of your life's teleserye.
usage_notes: Widely used in literature and metaphorically for life events.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa huling **kabanata** na ako ng binabasa kong nobela.","translation":"I'm on the last **chapter** of the novel I'm reading."},{"sentence":"Isang bagong **kabanata** sa aking buhay ang paglipat ko sa ibang bansa.","translation":"Moving to another country is a new **chapter** in my life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sasakyan sa isang amusement park na binubuo ng magkakabit na bagon na tumatakbo sa isang matarik at paliku-likong riles para sa libangan.
original_explanation: Short for 'roller coaster.' The ride at Enchanted Kingdom or Star City that's a metaphor for your love life: full of ups and downs, makes you scream, and you feel a little dizzy and sick afterwards, but for some reason, you might want to do it again.
usage_notes: Used as a shortened, informal term for 'roller coaster'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Takot akong sumakay sa **coaster** sa Star City.","translation":"I'm afraid to ride the **roller coaster** at Star City."}]

translation: to enthrone; to take a seat of power
meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pag-upo sa isang posisyon ng kapangyarihan o karangalan, tulad ng isang hari, reyna, o pangulo.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'umupo' (to sit). This is sitting with style, power, and a whole lot of ceremony. Think of a king taking his throne or a newly elected president taking the oath of office. In modern terms, it’s like finally getting that corner office you've been eyeing, or when your crush finally makes you their 'official' jowa—you've been enthroned in their heart.
usage_notes: Isang napakapormal na salita na ginagamit para sa pag-akyat sa kapangyarihan, maging ito man ay pang-hari, pampulitika, o panrelihiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Queen Elizabeth II ay **lumuklok** sa trono noong 1952.","translation":"Queen Elizabeth II was **enthroned** (ascended to the throne) in 1952."},{"sentence":"Inaasahan ng taumbayan na tutuparin ng bagong **lumuklok** na pangulo ang kanyang mga pangako.","translation":"The people expect the newly **seated** president to fulfill his promises."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kilos, salita, o bagay na labis na malaswa, hindi kaaya-aya, at labag sa mabuting asal o pamantayan ng lipunan.
original_explanation: This is your tita's favorite word for someone's outfit that shows 'too much skin' or for a movie scene that makes them cover their eyes. It's the 'Rated SPG' of real life. If your actions make the 'marites' squad call an emergency meeting, you're probably doing something kahalay-halay.
usage_notes: Often used in a judgmental or scolding tone to describe behavior or appearance deemed inappropriate by conservative standards.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturing nilang **kahalay-halay** ang pagsusuot ng ganoong klaseng damit sa simbahan.","translation":"They consider wearing that kind of dress to church to be **indecent**."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang mga **kahalay-halay** na biro mo.","translation":"Stop with your **obscene** jokes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sukdulan at walang katapat na awtoridad o kontrol sa isang estado, organisasyon, o larangan.
original_explanation: This is the "unlimited power" meme, but for real. It's the kind of power a mother has when she gives you "the look" and you instantly know you messed up. In politics, it's sovereignty—the nation's right to govern itself without anyone else butting in. It's the ultimate "ako ang masusunod dito" (I'm in charge here) statement.
usage_notes: Used in discussions of politics, theology, or any form of ultimate authority.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga mamamayan ang may hawak ng **kataas-taasang kapangyarihan** sa isang demokrasya.","translation":"The citizens hold the **supreme power** in a democracy."},{"sentence":"Naniniwala sila sa **kataas-taasang kapangyarihan** ng kanilang diyos.","translation":"They believe in the **supreme power** of their god."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking gusali o arena na may mga upuan sa paligid ng isang entablado, ginagamit para sa mga konsiyerto, palaro, at iba pang malalaking pagtitipon.
original_explanation: The Pinoy version is Araneta Coliseum, a.k.a. "The Big Dome." Dito nangyayari ang mga epic UAAP finals, mga concert ng K-Pop idols, at 'yung laban ni Pacquiao na pinapanood ng buong Pilipinas. Ang koliseo ang modern-day battleground for entertainment and sports.
usage_notes: Often refers to specific large venues like the Araneta Coliseum or the Mall of Asia Arena.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ang **koliseo** para sa laban ng basketbol.","translation":"The **coliseum** was full for the basketball game."},{"sentence":"Manonood kami ng concert sa sikat na **koliseo** sa Cubao.","translation":"We will watch a concert at the famous **coliseum** in Cubao."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parihabang bloke ng pinatigas na putik o luwad na karaniwang ginagamit sa pagtatayo ng mga pader at gusali.
original_explanation: The OG building block before Minecraft. It's that red, heavy thing your tito who's a construction worker always talks about. Also, what you feel like you're carrying in your backpack at the end of the semester.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang materyales sa konstruksiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matibay ang bahay na gawa sa **laryo** at semento.","translation":"A house made of **brick** and cement is sturdy."},{"sentence":"Nagpatong-patong sila ng **laryo** upang makabuo ng pader.","translation":"They stacked **bricks** on top of each other to build a wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamababang antas ng wika na karaniwang ginagamit sa mga lansangan at sa mga impormal na usapan. Ito ay mga salitang nabuo sa labas ng pamantayang wika.
original_explanation: This is the language of the 'kanto' and the 'barkada'. Think 'erpat', 'lodi', 'petmalu', 'werpa'. Balbal is the cool, ever-changing, sometimes-coded language you use with your friends but never with your lola or in a job interview. It's the Filipino language letting its hair down and having fun.
usage_notes: Refers to the category of words, not a specific word itself. It is a linguistic term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'erpat' ay isang halimbawa ng salitang **balbal**.","translation":"The word 'erpat' is an example of a **slang** word."},{"sentence":"Mahilig gumamit ng mga salitang **balbal** ang mga kabataan ngayon.","translation":"The youth today like to use **slang** words."}]

translation: bier; float for a religious statue
meaning_filipino: Isang platapormang pinapasan sa balikat, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga prusisyon upang buhatin ang mga imahen ng santo o ang kabaong.
original_explanation: The holy Uber for saints during a fiesta or Holy Week procession. It's that big, heavy, and beautifully decorated carriage carried on the shoulders of devotees. Requires more teamwork than any group project in college.
usage_notes: Primarily used in religious contexts, especially during processions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Daan-daang deboto ang nagtulungan sa pagpasan ng **andas** ng Nazareno.","translation":"Hundreds of devotees helped carry the **andas** of the Nazarene."},{"sentence":"Maraming bulaklak ang palamuti sa **andas** ng Mahal na Birhen.","translation":"Many flowers adorned the **float** of the Blessed Virgin."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang propesyonal na dalubhasa sa pag-aaral ng isip at pag-uugali ng tao, at tumutulong sa mga indibidwal na may mga suliraning mental at emosyonal sa pamamagitan ng 'talk therapy'.
original_explanation: The professional 'Marites'. Sila yung chinichikahan mo about your childhood trauma, anxiety sa work, at kung bakit ka 'ghosted' ng ka-talking stage mo, tapos may bayad. They help you unpack your baggage, unlike airlines that charge you for it.
usage_notes: Ito ang Filipinized/Hispanized na bersyon ng 'psychologist'. Hindi sila mga medikal na doktor at hindi maaaring magreseta ng gamot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inirekomenda ng guro na kumonsulta siya sa isang **psikologo**.","translation":"The teacher recommended that she consult a **psychologist**."}]

translation: to be teeming with, to swarm
meaning_filipino: Dumami nang sobra o maging siksikan sa isang lugar, partikular ang mga isda o maliliit na hayop sa tubig.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pandiwa na 'ma-' at ang salitang ugat na 'pusak' (isang malaking kawan ng isda; kasaganaan).
original_explanation: Imagine a fish pen so full of fish you could probably walk on them. That's 'mamusak'. It's the feeling of abundance, like a palengke stall overflowing with bangus, or your group chat 'namumusak sa chismis' (swarming with gossip).
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit para sa isda o iba pang buhay-tubig, ngunit maaaring gamitin sa matalinhagang paraan para sa siksikang tao o napakaraming bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing tag-ulan, **namumusak** sa isda ang ilog na ito.","translation":"During the rainy season, this river is **teeming with** fish."},{"sentence":"**Namumusak** sa tao ang Divisoria kapag malapit na ang Pasko.","translation":"Divisoria is **swarming** with people when Christmas is near."}]

meaning_filipino: Dalhin o buhatin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagpapatong nito sa ulo.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate balancing act, pre-dating any social media challenge. Imagine carrying a 'bilao' of produce or a 'banga' of water on your head while walking through a rice paddy. It's the OG hands-free mode. Not to be confused with 'sunong' which is the act, 'sunungin' is the command or infinitive form: 'You, carry this on your head!'
usage_notes: This is a traditional way of carrying things, often seen in rural areas. It requires great balance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **sunungin** ang banga ng tubig mula sa ilog hanggang sa ating bahay.","translation":"You need to **carry** the jar of water on your head from the river to our house."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **sunungin** ang isang basket ng prutas ngunit nahulog ito.","translation":"He tried to **carry** a basket of fruits on his head but it fell."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aalis ng dumi o likido sa isang ibabaw sa pamamagitan ng pagdaan ng tela o kamay.
original_explanation: The quick clean-up you do on your desk with a tissue 5 minutes before your boss arrives. That's a punas. Also, what you do to your screen after someone with greasy fingers touches it.
usage_notes: As a noun, the stress is on the first syllable. Compare with the verb command form 'punas' (/pu-NAS/).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **punas** lang, malinis na ang mesa.","translation":"Just one **wipe**, and the table is clean."},{"sentence":"Ang **punas** niya ay mabilis at magaan.","translation":"His/Her **wiping** is fast and light."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pansamantalang pagtira o pagtigil sa isang lugar, o isang tradisyonal na pagsasadula tuwing Pasko tungkol sa paghahanap nina Maria at Jose ng matutuluyan.
original_explanation: This word has two vibes. 1) The literal 'nag-Airbnb ka sa Baguio' kind of stay. 2) The Christmas-serye where actors playing Mary and Joseph go door-to-door, get rejected, and sing about it. It’s the OG story of having 'no room at the inn,' but make it a community theater production.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context. During Christmastime, it almost always refers to the religious reenactment of Joseph and Mary searching for an inn.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap kami ng disenteng **panunuluyan** sa Vigan.","translation":"We are looking for decent **lodging** in Vigan."},{"sentence":"Nanonood kami ng **Panunuluyan** sa plasa tuwing bisperas ng Pasko.","translation":"We watch the **Panunuluyan** (Christmas play) at the plaza every Christmas Eve."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang piraso ng katad o lubid na nakakabit sa suga ng kabayo, ginagamit ng sakay upang gabayan o kontrolin ito.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'manibela' ng kabayo. Kung paano mo kinokontrol ang budget mo pag 14th of the month para umabot sa sweldo, ganun din ang paghawak sa renda—mahigpit at puno ng pag-asa. Figuratively, ito yung pagkontrol sa isang sitwasyon or even sa sarili mo. 'Hawakan mo ang renda ng buhay mo!'
usage_notes: Also used metaphorically to mean 'control' or 'reign'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang hawak ng kutsero sa **renda** ng kanyang kabayo.","translation":"The coachman held the **rein** of his horse tightly."},{"sentence":"Panahon na para hawakan mo ang **renda** ng iyong kinabukasan.","translation":"It's time for you to take the **reins** of your future."}]

translation: descent; the act of going down
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbaba mula sa isang mataas na lugar patungo sa mas mababang lugar.
etymology: From pa- + N + aog ('descent'). Refers to the act of descending. The related verb is 'pumanaog' or 'manaog'.
original_explanation: That moment your mom yells 'Panaog na, kakain na!' and you have to descend from your room. It's the opposite of 'panhik' (going up). Also can be used dramatically, like 'ang panaog ng mga anghel mula sa langit.'
usage_notes: Less common than 'pagbaba'. The verb form 'pumanaog' (to descend) is more frequently used than the noun 'panaog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis ang kanyang **panaog** sa hagdanan.","translation":"His **descent** down the stairs was fast."},{"sentence":"Ang **panaog** ng imahen mula sa altar ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng pista.","translation":"The **descent** of the icon from the altar is an important part of the festival."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng muling pag-aaral o pagsusuri sa isang bagay, karaniwan bilang paghahanda sa isang pagsusulit o upang tiyakin ang kalidad at kawastuhan.
