usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **nalalabi** pa bang pag-asa para sa kanila?","translation":"Is there any hope **remaining** for them?"},{"sentence":"Sampung minuto na lang ang **nalalabi** sa ating pagsusulit.","translation":"Only ten minutes are **left** in our exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga tao na nagtipon para sa isang partikular na layunin; isang lupon o komite.
original_explanation: This is your squad, your team, your committee. 'Yung "Board of Directors" ng isang kumpanya? That's a "kalupon ng mga direktor." It's the official term for a group with a purpose, hindi lang basta barkada na nagkakape. Parang Avengers, pero sa office or community setting.
usage_notes: Used in formal contexts like business, governance, or organizations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kalupon** ng mga hukom ay nagdelibera na.","translation":"The **assembly** of judges has already deliberated."},{"sentence":"Ipinatawag ng **kalupon** ang lahat ng miyembro para sa isang pulong.","translation":"The **board** called all the members for a meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamatanda sa magkakapatid; ang unang anak.
original_explanation: The OG (Original na Gastusan). Sila yung unang investment ng pamilya, yung taga-salo ng lahat ng expectations, at ahente ng nanay at tatay sa mga nakababatang kapatid. Automatic retirement plan ng magulang.
usage_notes: Can also be used as an adjective (e.g., "ang panganay na anak").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang **panganay**, malaki ang responsibilidad niya sa kanyang mga kapatid.","translation":"As the **eldest child**, he has a big responsibility for his siblings."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **panganay** sa aming pito.","translation":"She is the **eldest** among the seven of us."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang termino sa social media para sa mga taong nag-follow sa isa't isa, lalo na sa platform tulad ng Twitter.
etymology: Pinaikling anyo ng salitang Ingles na "mutuals".
original_explanation: Your online barkada. These are the people on Twitter or TikTok you follow and who follow you back. You probably haven't met them IRL, but you know their latest chika, their K-pop bias, and their opinion on the latest trending topic. "Hi moots!" is the standard greeting to your online circle.
usage_notes: Eksklusibong ginagamit sa konteksto ng social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Sino sa mga **moots** ko ang gising pa?\" post niya sa Twitter.","translation":"\"Who among my **mutuals** is still awake?\" she posted on Twitter."},{"sentence":"Nag-organisa ng isang maliit na get-together ang ilan sa aming mga **moots**.","translation":"Some of our **mutuals** organized a small get-together."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nasa sentro o kalagitnaan ng dalawa o higit pang mga bagay, lugar, o panahon.
original_explanation: This is for anything in the middle. The middle child, the center lane in EDSA (good luck with that), the `panggitna` part of a 3-in-1 coffee mix. It's the median, the average, the one that's neither here nor there. In a group project, the `panggitna` is the person who does just enough not to fail but not enough to be the leader.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a noun ('ang panggitna') to mean 'the middle one' or 'centerpiece'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **panggitna**ng anak ay madalas na sinasabing \"peacekeeper\" ng pamilya.","translation":"The **middle** child is often said to be the family's \"peacekeeper\"."},{"sentence":"Ilagay mo ang plorera sa **panggitna**ng bahagi ng mesa.","translation":"Place the vase in the **central** part of the table."}]

translation: To feel lonely; to long for someone
meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman ang matinding kalungkutan o pangungulila dahil sa pagkakawalay o pagkawala ng isang minamahal.
original_explanation: The feeling you get at 2 AM scrolling through old photos of your ex, or when you're an OFW and you suddenly crave sinigang made by your lola. It's a deep, soul-crushing homesickness or lovesickness. It's the "I miss you" that hits different.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nangungulila** ako sa aking mga magulang mula nang magtrabaho ako sa ibang bansa.","translation":"I **have been longing for** my parents ever since I started working abroad."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mangulila**; dadalawin kita sa lalong madaling panahon.","translation":"Don't **be lonely**; I will visit you as soon as possible."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang puwang o butas sa dingding ng isang gusali o sasakyan, na karaniwang may salamin, upang makapasok ang liwanag at hangin, at upang makita ang labas.
original_explanation: The original "social media feed." This is where marites get their daily updates on the neighborhood chismis. It's a portal for sunlight, fresh air, and judging your neighbor's new haircut. Whether it's the classic capiz shell bintana or a modern glass one, it's the eye of the house.
usage_notes: A very common, everyday word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakibukas ng **bintana** para lumabas ang usok.","translation":"Please open the **window** so the smoke can get out."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko siya mula sa aming **bintana** na naglalakad sa kalye.","translation":"I saw him from our **window** walking on the street."}]

meaning_filipino: Kakaiba, bukod-tangi, o may natatanging katangian kumpara sa karaniwan.
original_explanation: That feeling when your crush treats you differently from everyone else. 'Yung tipong binigyan ka ng extra rice sa karinderya nang hindi mo hinihingi. O kaya 'yung Jollibee order mo na complete and correct, walang kulang. That's *ispesyal*. It's the VIP treatment, the 'main character' moment.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa pormal at di-pormal na konteksto. Ang baybay na 'espesyal' ay karaniwan din.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **ispesyal** na pagtingin si Ana para kay Marco.","translation":"Ana has **special** feelings for Marco."},{"sentence":"Naghanda si nanay ng **ispesyal** na hapunan para sa kaarawan ko.","translation":"Mom prepared a **special** dinner for my birthday."}]

translation: to make someone taste or experience something
meaning_filipino: Ipatikim o iparanas sa isang tao ang isang bagay, na kadalasan ay may negatibong konotasyon tulad ng hirap o parusa.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'taste of your own medicine' move. Kapag may nang-ghost sa'yo, tapos after a year, siya naman ang na-ghost, pinapalasap sa kanya ng universe ang ginawa niya. It's karma served on a silver platter, pero ikaw ang nag-utos sa waiter.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa matalinghagang paraan na nangangahulugang 'pahirapan' o 'iparanas ang kinahinatnan.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **palasapin** ng hirap ang mga taong umapi sa kanya.","translation":"He wants to **make** the people who oppressed him **experience** hardship."},{"sentence":"**Palasapin** mo siya ng sarili niyang luto para malaman niya kung gaano kaalat.","translation":"**Make him taste** his own cooking so he knows how salty it is."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sukat o dimensyon ng isang bagay; o ang metro o panukat ng bayarin sa taksi.
original_explanation: When you get in a taxi and say "Manong, medida lang po," you're putting your faith in a little machine and the driver's honesty. It's the official counter of your pesos as the kilometers tick by. Also used by mananahi (seamstresses) to get your body measurements, which can be a truly humbling experience.
usage_notes: Most commonly used in the context of taxi fares, where it is synonymous with 'metro'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakibaba na lang po ang **medida** ng taxi.","translation":"Please turn on the taxi **meter**."},{"sentence":"Kinuha ng sastre ang aking **medida** para sa gagawing barong.","translation":"The tailor took my **measurements** for the barong to be made."}]

meaning_filipino: Papunta sa ilalim ng tubig o anumang likido; malapit nang mawala sa paningin sa abot-tanaw, tulad ng araw.
original_explanation: Describes something that's on its way down. Literally, like a ship that's **palubog**. Famously, the sun at sunset is 'palubog na ang araw.' Figuratively, it can be a business that's failing, or a celebrity whose fame is fading. It's that moment of descent, just before something disappears completely.
usage_notes: Very commonly used to describe the setting sun. The prefix 'pa-' indicates direction or movement towards a state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanonood kami ng **palubog** na araw sa dalampasigan.","translation":"We were watching the **setting** sun on the beach."},{"sentence":"Mukhang **palubog** na ang barko matapos itong mabangga sa malaking bato.","translation":"The ship looks like it is **sinking** after it hit a large rock."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasuotang isinusuot sa ilalim ng pangunahing damit, karaniwang para sa kalinisan at suporta.
original_explanation: The stuff you wear that nobody's supposed to see (usually). Your undies, bra, sando, etc. The foundation of any outfit. It’s the first thing you put on and the last thing you take off. Like your internet search history, it's best kept private.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhing malinis at tuyo ang iyong **damit-panloob** bago isuot.","translation":"Make sure your **underwear** is clean and dry before wearing it."},{"sentence":"Nag-shopping siya ng bagong mga **damit-panloob** sa department store.","translation":"She shopped for new **innerwear** at the department store."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unti-unting pagbubuka ng mga talulot ng isang bulaklak; paglalahad ng kagandahan.
original_explanation: This is the "glow-up" verb of the plant world. When a flower goes from a shy bud to a full-on, vibrant, look-at-me-now blossom, it's doing `magbukadkad`. It’s the ultimate transformation, like when your quiet officemate suddenly becomes the star of the company party. It’s about revealing your full potential and beauty.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used for flowers, but can be used poetically for a person's development.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **magbukadkad** ang mga rosas sa aming hardin.","translation":"The roses in our garden have started **to bloom**."},{"sentence":"Tila isang bulaklak na naghihintay **magbukadkad** ang kanyang talento.","translation":"Her talent is like a flower waiting **to bloom**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng mga bandido; pagnanakaw, panghoholdap, at iba pang mararahas na krimen na isinasagawa ng isang grupo.
original_explanation: This is the act of being a 'bandido' or bandit. Historically, it was about highway robbers in the provinces. In modern times, 'kabandiduhan' can feel like what happens when your cell phone gets snatched in Quiapo, or when you see the corruption figures in the news. It's organized lawlessness.
usage_notes: Used in contexts of crime, lawlessness, and history.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kabandiduhan** sa kabundukan ay isa sa mga problemang sinusugpo ng mga awtoridad.","translation":"**Banditry** in the mountains is one of the problems being suppressed by the authorities."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang medikal na proseso kung saan ang dugo o mga bahagi ng dugo ay inililipat mula sa isang tao patungo sa isa pa.
original_explanation: Ito yung ultimate 'pahingi' moment sa ospital. Hindi load, hindi pera, kundi dugo. Ito yung dahilan bakit importante ang blood donation, para 'pag may nangailangan ng extra life bar, may maibibigay.
usage_notes: Isang medikal na termino. Ang 'pagsasalin ng dugo' ay tumutukoy sa mismong aksyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangan siyang sumailalim sa agarang **salinan ng dugo** pagkatapos ng aksidente.","translation":"He needed to undergo an immediate **blood transfusion** after the accident."},{"sentence":"Ligtas ang proseso ng **salinan ng dugo** sa mga modernong ospital.","translation":"The process of **blood transfusion** is safe in modern hospitals."}]

translation: To name; to identify by name
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay ng tiyak na tawag o pangalan sa isang tao, bagay, lugar, o konsepto; tukuyin kung sino o ano.
original_explanation: The "name drop" verb. It's what you do to your new pet, your startup company, or the group chat for your barkada. It's also used when you're asked to identify the culprit: "Pangalanan mo kung sino ang kumuha ng huling piraso ng pizza!" (Name who took the last slice of pizza!).
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb. The actor is typically in the `ng` form (e.g., `Pangalanan mo...` - You name...).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pangalanan** natin ang bagong tuta na 'Mochi'.","translation":"Let's **name** the new puppy 'Mochi'."},{"sentence":"Kaya mo bang **pangalanan** ang lahat ng miyembro ng SB19?","translation":"Can you **name** all the members of SB19?"}]

translation: to leave (a place); to depart from
meaning_filipino: Umalis o iwanan ang isang tiyak na lugar, tao, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The dramatic way to say 'to leave.' You don't just 'lisanin' your house to buy suka. You 'lisanin' your past, your toxic ex, or your hometown to start a new life. It carries a sense of finality and emotion. It's the verb for a hugot-filled goodbye.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. You use this when the place or person being left is the focus of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napilitan siyang **lisanin** ang kanyang pamilya upang magtrabaho sa ibang bansa.","translation":"He was forced to **leave** his family to work in another country."},{"sentence":"Oras na para **lisanin** ang masasamang bisyo.","translation":"It is time to **leave** behind bad habits."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pisikal na paghawak sa isang bagay, o sa metaporikal na kahulugan, ang pagkakaroon ng kontrol o kapangyarihan sa isang sitwasyon o tao.
original_explanation: Literally, it's holding something, like "Sino may hawak ng phone ko?" But the real tea is its other meaning: having leverage. "May hawak ako sa'yong sikreto." It's the ultimate power move in any teleserye, office drama, or chismis circle. It means you have the upper hand.
usage_notes: Can be literal (physical hold) or figurative (control, leverage, evidence).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**May hawak** siyang isang tasa ng mainit na kape.","translation":"She **is holding** a cup of hot coffee."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang kalabanin, **may hawak** siyang impormasyon laban sa iyo.","translation":"Don't go against him, he **has a hold** of information against you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o lalagyan kung saan nagsasagawa ng pagsisiga o pagpaparikit ng malaking apoy.
original_explanation: This is the designated spot for your epic bonfire night, whether sa beach for some ~aesthetic~ vibes or sa bakuran para mag-ihaw ng marshmallows. It's the official 'dito tayo mag-apoy' zone, para hindi masunog ang buong barangay. Think of it as a fire pit.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of camping, beach outings, or provincial life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa **sigaan** at baka matalsikan ka ng baga.","translation":"Be careful near the **bonfire pit** as you might get hit by embers."},{"sentence":"Sa tabi ng **sigaan** sila nagkwentuhan buong gabi.","translation":"They told stories all night beside the **bonfire pit**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtupi o pag-rolyo paitaas ng laylayan ng damit, tulad ng manggas o pantaloon, upang paiksiin ito.
original_explanation: The action you take right before getting down to serious business. Whether it's washing dishes, starting a fistfight, or wading through a flooded street in BGC, you 'lilis' your sleeves or pants. It's the universal sign for "Okay, game na."
usage_notes: The root word 'lilis' can be used as a command. Verb forms include 'maglilis', 'nililisan', 'lilisan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lilisanin** ko lang ang manggas ko para hindi mabasa.","translation":"I'll just **roll up** my sleeves so they don't get wet."},{"sentence":"Nag**lilis** siya ng pantalon bago tumawid sa baha.","translation":"He **rolled up** his pants before crossing the flood."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae, lalo na isang dalaga, na may lahing Tsino.
original_explanation: A term for a Filipina of Chinese descent, often used to describe someone with fair skin and single-lidded or almond-shaped eyes ('singkit'). It's the Pinoy way of saying 'that girl looks Chinese'. It can be a term of endearment or just a neutral descriptor, but context is key. The male version is 'Tsinito'.
usage_notes: Capitalized when referring to the ethnicity, but often seen in lowercase in casual writing. Can be considered stereotypical by some, so usage should be mindful of context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming nagsasabi na kamukha niya ay isang **Tsinita**.","translation":"Many say that she looks like a **woman of Chinese descent**."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng mga mata ng **Tsinita** na nakilala ko.","translation":"The eyes of the **Chinita** I met are beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Posibleng makaligtas o hindi maranasan ang isang hindi kanais-nais na pangyayari o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your toxic tita at a family reunion and you successfully hide in the bathroom until she leaves. 'Yan ang 'maiiwasan'. It's the life skill you use to dodge awkward conversations, extra work from your boss, or a friend asking to borrow money again. Avoidance is a skill!
usage_notes: Implies the possibility of preventing something, often something negative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung nag-aral ka lang, **maiiwasan** sana ang pagbagsak mo sa pagsusulit.","translation":"If only you had studied, your failing the exam **could have been avoided**."},{"sentence":"Hindi **maiiwasan** ang trapik sa EDSA tuwing Biyernes.","translation":"Traffic on EDSA on Fridays cannot **be avoided**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na inatasan na magbantay, mangalaga, at magprotekta sa kagubatan laban sa mga ilegal na gawain tulad ng pamumutol ng puno o pangangaso.
original_explanation: The real-life Lorax of the Philippines. They speak for the trees (and the animals). These are the brave folks who guard our forests against illegal loggers and poachers. They're the ultimate 'plantitos' and 'plantitas', protecting entire ecosystems. Their work is like being a 'tanod' for Mother Nature herself.
usage_notes: A specific type of 'tanod' or guard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang marangal na trabaho ang pagiging **tanod-gubat**.","translation":"Being a **forest ranger** is a noble job."},{"sentence":"Nahuli ng mga **tanod-gubat** ang mga ilegal na magtotroso.","translation":"The **forest rangers** caught the illegal loggers."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa lohistika; may kinalaman sa detalyado at praktikal na organisasyon at pagpapatupad ng isang kumplikadong operasyon.
original_explanation: This is the formal term for the behind-the-scenes magic that makes things happen. Planning a family reunion? You need to handle the lohistiko side—who brings the pancit, who gets the chairs, and how to keep Tita Baby and Tita Nene from sitting at the same table. It's the adulting word for "plano at pag-aasikaso."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng negosyo, militar, o malakihang pagpaplano ng kaganapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tagumpay ng proyekto ay nakasalalay sa maayos na planong **lohistiko**.","translation":"The project's success depends on a good **logistical** plan."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng problemang **lohistiko** kaya naantala ang pagdating ng mga suplay.","translation":"There was a **logistical** problem, which is why the arrival of supplies was delayed."}]

translation: to seek shelter; to seek refuge
meaning_filipino: Humingi ng kanlungan, proteksyon, o pag-aaruga mula sa iba, lalo na sa panahon ng pangangailangan o panganib.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you've had a huge fight with your parents and you run to your lola's house. You're seeking refuge, a safe space where there's free food and unconditional love, and no one's yelling at you for not washing the dishes. It can also be for stray cats seeking shelter from the rain under your car.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan tayo **magpapakupkop** kung bumagyo nang malakas?","translation":"Where will we **seek shelter** if a strong typhoon comes?"},{"sentence":"**Nagpakupkop** ang mga naulila sa isang ampunan.","translation":"The orphans **sought refuge** in an orphanage."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsusuri, pagbabago, at pagwawasto sa isang nasulat na akda, plano, o dokumento upang ito ay mapabuti.
etymology: From English 'revision', possibly influenced by the Spanish 'revisión'.
original_explanation: The bane of every creative, writer, and office worker's existence. It's when your client, boss, or professor says "Okay na, pero..." and sends back your work with a million comments. Ito 'yung "Rev 1", "Rev 2", "FINAL_na_talaga_promise_v3". Each revision chips away a small piece of your soul.
usage_notes: Commonly used in office, academic, and creative settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilang **revision** na ba ang dinaanan ng script na ito?","translation":"How many **revisions** has this script gone through?"},{"sentence":"Pinabalik sa akin ng kliyente ang disenyo para sa isang major **revision**.","translation":"The client sent the design back to me for a major **revision**."}]

meaning_filipino: Maliit na isda na karaniwang inilalata sa sarsa ng kamatis o mantika.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino survival food. The hero during typhoons, petsa de peligro, and lazy-to-cook days. Whether it's ginisang sardinas with misua and malunggay or straight from the can with hot pandesal, it's a staple in every Pinoy pantry. It's the food that says, 'I'm on a budget, but I'm still gonna eat well.'
usage_notes: Refers to both the type of fish and, more commonly, the canned product.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang dosenang lata ng **sardinas** para sa aming relief goods.","translation":"Mom bought a dozen cans of **sardines** for our relief goods."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang almusal ay sinangag na may ginisang **sardinas**.","translation":"His favorite breakfast is fried rice with sautéed **sardines**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang medikal na pagsusuri sa isang bangkay upang matukoy ang sanhi ng pagkamatay.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa sa mga crime series para malaman kung sino ang salarin. Parang pag-rereview ng conversation niyo ng ex mo para malaman kung saan eksakto nagkamali. The **autopsiya** of a dead relationship.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa kontekstong medikal at legal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinailalim sa **autopsiya** ang bangkay upang malaman ang tunay na dahilan ng kanyang pagkamatay.","translation":"The body was subjected to an **autopsy** to determine the real cause of death."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghigop ng likido o anumang malambot na bagay gamit ang bibig, madalas sa tulong ng isang tubo o straw.
original_explanation: This is the action of sucking, usually through a straw. It’s what you do with your milk tea to get the boba, or when you're trying to get the last drops of your Coke. Figuratively, it’s related to 'sipsip', the act of a suck-up or brown-noser who tries to get ahead by flattering the boss. 'Sumupsop ng biyaya' means to greedily take in blessings or benefits.
usage_notes: Has a stronger, more intense connotation than 'humigop' (to sip). Can also have a negative connotation related to being a sycophant ('sipsip').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis niyang **sinupsop** ang natitirang palamig sa baso.","translation":"He quickly **sucked up** the remaining drink in the glass."},{"sentence":"**Sumupsop** ng nektar ang mga bubuyog mula sa bulaklak.","translation":"The bees **sucked** nectar from the flower."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para sa isang monarka o pinunong Muslim, lalo na sa mga rehiyon sa Mindanao.
original_explanation: The OG boss, the chief, the head honcho in traditional Muslim communities, especially in Mindanao. Before presidents and mayors, there were sultans. They're royalty, holding a position of power and respect passed down through generations. Think of them as the kings in Filipino epic stories, but very much real.
usage_notes: Refers to a specific type of monarch in Islamic cultures, particularly relevant to the history and culture of Mindanao in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sultan** ng Brunei ay isa sa pinakamayamang tao sa mundo.","translation":"The **sultan** of Brunei is one of the richest people in the world."},{"sentence":"Kinikilala pa rin ang kapangyarihan ng **sultan** sa kanilang komunidad.","translation":"The power of the **sultan** is still recognized in their community."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng kasiglahan, kagalakan, at kawalan ng kalungkutan.
etymology: Posibleng hango sa salitang Espanyol na 'gayo' (masayahin, masigla). Ang ugat na 'gaya' para sa kasayahan ay hindi na karaniwang ginagamit nang mag-isa sa kasalukuyan.
original_explanation: This describes the vibe of a fiesta, a Christmas party, or that one friend who's always the life of the party. It's not just happy (masaya), it's actively cheerful and vibrant. The opposite of a meeting that could have been an email.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person's disposition or the atmosphere of a place or event. More descriptive than just 'masaya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **maigaya** ang pagdiriwang dahil sa mga palaro.","translation":"The celebration became **lively** because of the games."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **maigaya** na personalidad kaya marami siyang kaibigan.","translation":"She has a **cheerful** personality, which is why she has many friends."}]

translation: to stamp; to affix a seal
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapatatak ng selyo o timbre sa isang bagay, lalo na sa dokumento.
original_explanation: This is the action of making it official. When the government employee takes that big, heavy stamper and *thwacks* it on your birth certificate, that's 'timbrehan'. It's the verb form of getting that 'resibo' or proof of transaction. "Pa-timbrehan mo na 'yan sa accounting para ma-reimburse ka."
usage_notes: Ang salitang-ugat ay 'timbre' na tumutukoy sa selyo o tatak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **timbrehan** ang bawat pahina ng kontrata.","translation":"Don't forget to **stamp** every page of the contract."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing kulay pula ang isang bagay; kulayan ng pula.
original_explanation: This isn't your everyday word. It's like something you'd read in a very dramatic poem. Imagine a writer describing a sunset: "Isinapula ng dapithapon ang buong kalangitan." (The dusk reddened the entire sky.) It's the act of turning something red, either literally with paint or figuratively with blood or emotion. Very metal.
usage_notes: Primarily used in literary or poetic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **isapula** ang pader ng kanyang silid.","translation":"She wants to **make** the wall of her room **red**."},{"sentence":"**Isinapula** ng dugo ang dating malinis na sahig.","translation":"Blood **reddened** the formerly clean floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makamit ang tagumpay, magwagi, o magkaroon ng matagumpay na resulta sa isang gawain o laban.
original_explanation: The feeling of finally passing your board exams, getting that visa approved, or successfully launching your small business. It's the 'naka-ahon din' moment after all the puyat and pagtitiis. The ultimate 'sa wakas!'
usage_notes: A formal and often celebratory word for success.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsikap siyang mabuti upang **managumpay** sa buhay.","translation":"She worked very hard in order to **succeed** in life."}]

translation: to cast a shadow on; to shade
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagbibigay ng anino sa isang lugar o bagay; ang pagtakip mula sa direktang sikat ng araw.
original_explanation: Literally, to cast a shadow on something. Like when a tall building blocks the sun from your window. Metaphorically, it's what a toxic friend does to your good mood or what a surprise "urgent" task from your boss does to your weekend plans. It's all about something casting a "shade" on something else, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Location/object-focus verb. "Aninuhan mo ang halaman" means "You shade the plant."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **aninuhan** mo ang mga halaman para hindi masunog sa araw.","translation":"Please, **shade** the plants so they don't get burned by the sun."},{"sentence":"Ang malaking puno ang **umaanino** sa aming buong bakuran.","translation":"The large tree **casts a shadow on** our entire yard."}]

translation: to add an ingredient to; to mix something in
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng sahog o pampalasa ang isang lutuin o timpla.
original_explanation: This is the magic word for pancit canton when you want to make it look less like instant noodles and more like a real meal. "Sahugan mo ng boiled egg at spring onions, para mukhang special." It's the art of adding 'extra' to make something basic, 'extra special'. Level up your instant ramen game!
usage_notes: Often used in cooking to refer to adding meat, vegetables, or other main ingredients to a dish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sahugan** mo ng hipon ang ginisang ampalaya para mas sumarap.","translation":"**Add** shrimp to the sauteed bitter melon to make it tastier."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **sahugan** ng gulay ang sinigang.","translation":"Don't forget to **add** vegetables to the sinigang."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi direkta o tuwid; pahilis, patagilid, o pahalang. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang pahiwatig na hindi tuwiran.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'pa-' at salitang-ugat na 'lihis' (wala sa linya, hiwi).
original_explanation: Could be literal or figurative. Literal: 'Yung pagkabit ng picture frame sa pader na hindi pantay. Figurative: 'Yung comment ng tita mo na, 'Uy, tumataba ka,' na ang ibig sabihin ay mag-diet ka na. It's an indirect hit, a side-swipe comment. A 'parinig'.
usage_notes: Maaaring ilarawan ang isang pisikal na oryentasyon (nakatagilid) o isang paraan ng komunikasyon (di-tuwiran). Ginagamit din bilang pang-uri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumagot siya nang **palihis** upang hindi masaktan ang kausap.","translation":"He answered **indirectly** so as not to hurt the person he was talking to."},{"sentence":"**Palihis** ang pagkakabit mo ng kurtina.","translation":"The way you hung the curtain is **askew**."}]

translation: to make calm; to reassure; to secure
meaning_filipino: Gawing panatag, payapa, o tiwasay ang isang bagay o kalooban ng isang tao.
etymology: From i- (causative prefix) + panatag (calm, secure, tranquil).
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend is having an anxiety attack over a work deadline or a 'sana ol' moment. You tell them, 'Kalma lang,' and try to 'ipanatag' their loob (reassure their feelings). It's also what the police do to secure an area. It's the verb for bringing things from chaos to 'chill.'
usage_notes: Often used with 'loob' (e.g., ipanatag ang loob) to mean 'to reassure' or 'to put one's mind at ease.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ipanatag** ang loob ng kanyang ina na nag-aalala.","translation":"He tried **to reassure** his worried mother."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **ipanatag** muna ang lugar bago payagang bumalik ang mga residente.","translation":"The area must first be **made secure** before residents are allowed to return."}]

translation: to find something spicy; to be affected by spiciness
meaning_filipino: Makaramdam o maapektuhan ng anghang ng isang pagkain o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of what happens after you bravely took a bite of that 'hindi naman maanghang' dish your friend offered. It's the moment of realization, followed by a frantic search for water, milk, or sugar. 'Bes, na-maanghangan ako!'
usage_notes: Often used in the potential aspect, meaning 'to be affected by spice' or 'to accidentally find something spicy'. The subject is the one experiencing the spiciness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakarami kong nakain na sili kaya ako **naanghangan**.","translation":"I ate too much chili that's why I **was overwhelmed by the spiciness**."},{"sentence":"Kahit konting anghang lang, madali siyang **maanghangan**.","translation":"Even with just a little spice, he is easily **affected by spiciness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang bagay na binubuo ng maraming magkakapatong na suson o patong.
original_explanation: This is the adjective form. When you describe something as having many layers. 'Ang damit niya ay sapinsapin' (His clothes are layered). It's less common than saying 'patong-patong' but is perfectly correct. It emphasizes the distinctness of each layer, like in the kakanin.
usage_notes: Often interchangeable with 'patong-patong', but 'sapinsapin' can sometimes imply more distinct, neatly arranged layers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang geological formation ng bundok ay **sapinsapin** ang mga bato.","translation":"The mountain's geological formation has **layered** rocks."},{"sentence":"**Sapinsapin** ang pagkakapintura sa pader kaya mahirap tanggalin.","translation":"The paint on the wall is **multi-layered**, so it's hard to remove."}]

translation: to bite or snap at each other
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o paulit-ulit na pagkagat o pagsakmal ng dalawa o higit pang nilalang sa isa't isa, karaniwan ay mga hayop.
etymology: Mula sa "sakmal" (to snap at, seize with the mouth).
original_explanation: Ito yung eksena sa Discovery Channel kapag nag-aaway ang mga leon. Pero sa Pinoy context, ito rin yung nangyayari sa mag-jowa na nag-aaway through text, puro "seen" at passive-aggressive "k." Parang aso't pusa lang.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang palitan (reciprocal verb).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-umpisa nang mag-**sakmalan** ang dalawang aso dahil sa isang buto.","translation":"The two dogs started to **bite at each other** over a bone."},{"sentence":"Sa halip na magtulungan, nag-**sakmalan** pa ang mga pulitiko sa isyu.","translation":"Instead of helping each other, the politicians just **snapped at each other** over the issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman o damo (Sida acuta) na may mga sanga na kahawig ng isang maliit na walis. Ito ay karaniwang itinuturing na damong-ligaw.
original_explanation: The plant that looks like it's trying to be a walis but didn't quite make it. It's the 'cosplayer' of the plant world, often found in vacant lots. Your lola probably knows a dozen herbal remedies for it, while you just see it as something to pull out of the garden.
usage_notes: Also spelled "walis-walisan". The name comes from its resemblance to a small broom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tumubong **waliswalisan** sa bakanteng lote.","translation":"A lot of **broom weed** grew in the vacant lot."},{"sentence":"Ang dahon ng **waliswalisan** ay ginagamit daw na gamot sa ilang karamdaman.","translation":"The leaves of the **Sida acuta** are said to be used as medicine for some ailments."}]

translation: Filipino; of or relating to the Philippines
meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan ng isang bagay na may kaugnayan sa, nagmula sa, o katangian ng Pilipinas, ng mga mamamayan nito, o ng wika nito.
etymology: Mula sa pangalang "Felipe", na ipinangalan sa Hari ng Espanya na si Haring Felipe II (King Philip II), kung saan hinango ang pangalan ng bansa, "Las Islas Filipinas".
original_explanation: When you add 'Filipino' before a word, it becomes a whole new experience. 'Filipino spaghetti' isn't just spaghetti; it's sweet, with hotdogs, and topped with cheap, block cheese. 'Filipino time' isn't just being late; it's a cultural phenomenon of arriving 30 minutes to an hour after the set time. 'Filipino hospitality' means we'll give you our own bed and we'll sleep on the floor. It's an adjective that adds flavor, warmth, and a little bit of chaos.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang pinagmulan o katangian ng isang bagay bilang mula sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito ko ang **Filipino** spaghetti dahil sa tamis nito.","translation":"I like **Filipino** spaghetti because of its sweetness."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang tunay na **Filipino** hospitality sa mga bisita.","translation":"She showed true **Filipino** hospitality to the guests."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagkaskas o pagkayod. Ito ay tumutukoy din sa isang medikal na pamamaraan (dilation and curettage).
original_explanation: This is the action version of 'raspa'. It's what you do to get old paint off a wall. It's what the vendor does to the block of ice to make your dessert. In a more serious, hospital setting, it refers to the D&C procedure, often spoken about in hushed tones. So context is EVERYTHING. Don't ask a street vendor to raspahin your wall.
usage_notes: The medical meaning (to perform a D&C) is a very common and serious use of the word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **raspahin** ang lumang pintura bago magpinta ulit.","translation":"You need **to scrape** off the old paint before painting again."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan siya ng doktor na kailangan siyang **raspahin**.","translation":"The doctor told her she needs a **D&C (scraping)**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paniniwala na ang kaluluwa o espiritu, pagkatapos ng kamatayan, ay maaaring magsimulang muli ng isang bagong buhay sa isang bagong katawan.
original_explanation: This is that moment you joke about after a tough day at work: 'Sana sa next life, pusa na lang ako ng mayaman.' It's the ultimate 'try again' button for life, hoping you don't come back as a cockroach.
usage_notes: Often discussed in philosophical, religious, or humorous contexts about the afterlife.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala ang ilan na may **reenkarnasyon** pagkatapos ng kamatayan.","translation":"Some believe that there is **reincarnation** after death."}]

translation: to understand each other; to come to an understanding
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagkakaroon ng mutwal na pag-intindi o pagkakasundo sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate relationship goal. It's when you and your friend/jowa finally get on the same page after a long "discussion." It's that moment of clarity in a group project when everyone finally understands their role. "Sana all magkaunawaan" is the silent prayer during family reunions and team meetings.
usage_notes: A very common and important word in Filipino culture, emphasizing mutual understanding and harmony.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating mag-usap nang masinsinan para tayo'y **magkaunawaan**.","translation":"We need to talk seriously so we can **understand each other**."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **nagkaunawaan** din ang dalawang panig.","translation":"Finally, the two sides **came to an understanding**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pasilidad, na kadalasan ay mas maliit kaysa ospital, kung saan ang mga pasyente ay tumatanggap ng medikal na pagsusuri at paggamot na hindi nangangailangan ng pananatili magdamag.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung first stop mo 'pag may nararamdaman kang kakaiba sa katawan mo pero hindi pa 'ER-level' emergency. Dito ka pumupunta para sa check-up, pagkuha ng medical certificate, o pagpapabunot ng ngipin. Mas maliit sa ospital, mas abot-kaya, at mas mabilis (sana) ang pila.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtayo ng libreng **klinika** ang lokal na pamahalaan para sa mga residente.","translation":"The local government established a free **clinic** for the residents."},{"sentence":"Pumunta ako sa **klinika** para magpatingin ng aking ubo.","translation":"I went to the **clinic** to have my cough checked."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkakalubog sa isang kalagayan, lalo na sa kahirapan, bisyo, o matinding kalungkutan, na halos hindi na makaahon.
original_explanation: If `lugami` is being knocked down by sadness, `lugmok` is staying down and wallowing in it. It's when you're stuck in a rut. "Lugmok sa kahirapan" (sunk in poverty). "Lugmok sa bisyo" (wallowing in vice). It has a sense of being trapped and unable to get up. It's the state of being after the "wala na, finish na" moment, when you've accepted defeat and are just lying there.
usage_notes: Stronger and more permanent-sounding than 'lugami'. It implies being stuck in a negative state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang **lugmok** sa kahirapan dahil sa kawalan ng trabaho.","translation":"Many families are **wallowing** in poverty due to lack of jobs."},{"sentence":"Simula nang iwan siya ng kasintahan, tila **lugmok** na siya sa kalungkutan.","translation":"Since his girlfriend left him, he seems to be **sunk** in sadness."}]

translation: to treat (an illness or injury); to medicate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay-lunas o pag-aalaga sa isang tao o hayop na may sakit o sugat sa pamamagitan ng gamot o iba pang paraan.
original_explanation: When you have a cough, your mom will **maggamot** you with a mix of Vicks, ginger tea (salabat), and a lot of scolding for getting sick. It’s the act of applying medicine, whether you're a doctor treating a patient or just putting a band-aid on your kid's 'galos'.
usage_notes: Can also mean to treat or cure a problem in a more figurative sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **maggamot** ng sugat mo para hindi ito maimpeksyon.","translation":"You need to **treat** your wound so it doesn't get infected."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag, salaysay, o anumang namutawi sa bibig ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The foundation of all 'chismis' (gossip). 'Sabi nila...' (They said...) is how the best stories start. It's what your mom tells you, what your boss demands, what your crush accidentally let slip. It's the 'he said, she said' of Filipino life.
usage_notes: Often used in reported speech, e.g., 'sabi ni...' (said by...), 'sabi mo...' (you said...).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **sabi** ng doktor tungkol sa iyong kalusugan?","translation":"What did the doctor **say** about your health?"},{"sentence":"Ayon sa **sabi**-sabi, magkakaroon daw ng bonus sa Pasko.","translation":"According to **rumors**, there will supposedly be a bonus for Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalagyan na karaniwang gawa sa salamin o plastik, may makitid na bunganga, at ginagamit para sa mga likido.
original_explanation: The OG water jug bago pa nauso ang Hydro Flask. Dito nilalagay ni nanay yung toyo, suka, at kung minsan, yung panlinis na may kulay na parang juice. Ingat sa pag-inom! Also, the thing you sell to the 'magbobote' for extra cash.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay mo ang tubig sa **bote**.","translation":"Please put the water in the **bottle**."},{"sentence":"Naubos na ang isang **bote** ng ketchup.","translation":"One **bottle** of ketchup has been used up."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ugali o kilos na hindi kaaya-aya, labag sa mabuting kaugalian, at walang paggalang.
original_explanation: This is what your lola warns you about. Talking with your mouth full, not saying 'po' and 'opo', ghosting your date—all classic examples of 'masamang asal'. It's behavior that would get you a side-eye at the family reunion.
usage_notes: A common phrase referring to poor behavior or lack of etiquette.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hindi pagpapasalamat ay tanda ng **masamang asal**.","translation":"Not saying thank you is a sign of **bad manners**."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan ng guro ang estudyante dahil sa kanyang **masamang asal** sa klase.","translation":"The teacher reprimanded the student for his **bad conduct** in class."}]

translation: Go for it!; You do you!
meaning_filipino: Isang kasabihan na nagpapahiwatig ng pagsuporta o pagbibigay-basbas sa desisyon o nais gawin ng isang tao, minsan ay may bahid ng panunuya o pagwawalang-bahala.
etymology: From English "push" + Tagalog "mo" (you) + "iyan" (that). Popularized in modern Filipino social media and conversations.
original_explanation: The ultimate "I support you, but it's on you" statement. It's what your friend says when you want to text your ex at 2 AM. It's a mix of encouragement, a green light, and a disclaimer that they're not responsible for the consequences. "You do you, boo."
usage_notes: Often used humorously or sarcastically. The tone of voice is key to its interpretation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong mag-apply sa trabahong 'yon kahit 'di ako qualified. Sabi ng kaibigan ko, \"Sige, **push mo 'yan**!\"","translation":"I want to apply for that job even if I'm not qualified. My friend said, \"Okay, **go for it**!\""},{"sentence":"Magda-diet na talaga ako simula bukas. Sabi niya, \"**Push mo 'yan**, beshie.\"","translation":"I'll really start my diet tomorrow. She said, \"**You do you**, bestie.\""}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabago tungo sa isang mas mabuti, mas mataas, o mas maayos na kalagayan; pagsulong.
original_explanation: What politicians promise every election. It's when your sahod finally gets a raise after 3 years, or when the internet speed in your area goes from 1Mbps to 5Mbps. It's the opposite of your love life's status for the past 5 years. #SanaAllMayPagunlad
usage_notes: Can refer to economic, personal, or societal progress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang edukasyon ay susi sa **pag-unlad** ng bayan.","translation":"Education is the key to the nation's **progress**."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **pag-unlad** sa kanyang mga marka ngayong semestre.","translation":"The **development** in his grades this semester is very visible."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagnanakaw ng maliit na halaga o bagay, kadalasan ay ginagawa nang patago.
etymology: From `pang-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `ku-` + `kupit` (to pilfer).
original_explanation: This is the 'micro-transaction' of stealing. It's not a full-on bank heist; it's taking a few coins from your mom's wallet for a 'yosi' break, sneaking a piece of chicharon from the office pantry, or when the konduktor 'forgets' to give you the exact change. Small-time, but still a crime!
usage_notes: Specifically refers to stealing small amounts or items. Different from 'pagnanakaw' which can be for large-scale theft.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli sa akto ng **pangungupit** ng barya ang bata.","translation":"The child was caught in the act of **pilfering** coins."},{"sentence":"Ang **pangungupit** ay isang masamang ugali na dapat itigil.","translation":"**Petty theft** is a bad habit that must be stopped."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng tupi o lupi sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of what your mom yells at you to do with the mountain of clean laundry. 'Lupian mo na 'yan!' means to fold that thing, whether it's a shirt, a love letter you're hiding, or a 1000-peso bill to fit in a tiny wallet.
usage_notes: The object-focus verb form of `lupi`. `Lupiin` is a synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lupian** mo nang maayos ang mga damit para magkasya sa maleta.","translation":"**Fold** the clothes neatly so they will fit in the suitcase."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **lupian** ang pahina ng libro, gumamit ka ng bookmark.","translation":"Don't **crease** the book's page, use a bookmark."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang tinatanggal sa listahan ng mga sinusubaybayan sa isang social media platform.
etymology: Tagalog prefix 'nag-' + reduplication of first syllable 'u-' + English 'unfollow'.
original_explanation: The act of cleansing your feed, one toxic person at a time. It's like spring cleaning for your social life. 'Mare, wait lang, **nag-uunfollow** ako ng mga fake news peddlers.'
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'mag-unfollow'. Denotes an ongoing action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo, dumarami ang **nag-uunfollow** sa'yo dahil sa post mo.","translation":"Look, more people **are unfollowing** you because of your post."},{"sentence":"Habang **nag-uunfollow** siya ng mga ex, kumakain siya ng ice cream.","translation":"While she **is unfollowing** her exes, she is eating ice cream."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maliliit at malalambot na balahibo ng ibon, lalo na ng mga sisiw o sa ilalim ng mas malalaking balahibo ng adultong ibon.
original_explanation: The original fluff. Yung maliliit at malalambot na balahibo ng sisiw na binibili mo sa labas ng simbahan tuwing Linggo ng Palaspas. Parang micro-fiber pero all-natural at galing sa manok.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang unan ay puno ng **suysoy** ng gansa.","translation":"The pillow is filled with goose **down**."},{"sentence":"Makikita ang **suysoy** sa dibdib ng mga bagong pisang sisiw.","translation":"You can see the **down** on the chest of the newly hatched chicks."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, gawain, o kasuotan na angkop o para lamang sa loob ng bahay.
original_explanation: Think of your 'pambahay' clothes—that's **pantahanan**. It's anything meant for the home front. Your daster, your tsinelas, the everyday plates. It's the opposite of 'pang-alis' or 'pang-opisina'. It's your comfy, no-judgment, 'I can finally take my bra off' zone stuff.
usage_notes: Often used to describe clothing ('damit pantahanan') or chores ('gawaing pantahanan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paglalaba at paglilinis ay mga gawaing **pantahanan**.","translation":"Doing laundry and cleaning are **domestic** chores."},{"sentence":"Mas komportable akong magsuot ng damit na **pantahanan** kaysa sa maong.","translation":"I'm more comfortable wearing **home** clothes than jeans."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglaban, paghamon, o pakikipagpaligsahan sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'katunggali'. It's what you do *to* your rival. When you decide to run against the incumbent, you katunggaliin them. It's the moment you say 'Game on!' and actively try to win against someone.
usage_notes: A more formal way to say 'labanan' or 'kalabanin' in the context of rivalry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **katunggaliin** ang taong mas malakas sa iyo.","translation":"Do not **oppose** someone stronger than you."},{"sentence":"Handa siyang **katunggaliin** ang sinuman para sa pwesto.","translation":"He is ready to **compete against** anyone for the position."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit at matamis na tinapay o biskwit, karaniwang bilog at patag, na niluto sa hurno. Ginagamit din ito bilang termino sa teknolohiya para sa datos na iniimbak ng isang website sa browser ng gumagamit.
original_explanation: Yung paborito mong baon nung elementary ka, o yung kinakain mo habang nag-e-emote at nanonood ng Netflix. Pwede ring 'internet cookies', yung nagta-track ng browsing history mo kaya bigla kang may ad ng sapatos na tiningnan mo lang kanina. 'Accept all cookies?' -- a question that defines our digital lives.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng pagkain at sa teknolohiya sa internet (internet cookies).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbake si nanay ng chocolate chip **cookies**.","translation":"Mom baked chocolate chip **cookies**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong i-clear ang **cookies** ng browser mo minsan.","translation":"You need to clear your browser **cookies** sometimes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng ulo paibaba at paitaas bilang tanda ng pagsang-ayon, pagbati, o pag-unawa.
original_explanation: The universal gesture for 'yes,' 'gets ko,' or 'oo, sige.' It's what you do when your boss is explaining something in a meeting and you want to look engaged, even if your mind is on lunch. It's the silent 'amen' when your friend is ranting about their ex.
usage_notes: The opposite is 'pag-iling' (shaking the head).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang marahang **pagtango** lang ang isinagot niya sa aking tanong.","translation":"She only gave a gentle **nod** in response to my question."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtango** ng hurado ay nagbigay ng pag-asa sa kalahok.","translation":"The judge's **act of nodding** gave the contestant hope."}]

translation: music; sound (of music); playing (of an instrument)
meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha ng isang instrumento o pangkat ng mga instrumento; isang komposisyong musikal.
original_explanation: It's the sound that makes you either want to dance, cry, or question your life choices at 3 AM. The playlist for your daily commute, your 'sana all' moments, or your 'walang jowa' feels. The BGM of your life.
usage_notes: Can refer to the act of playing music ('pagtugtog') or the music itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **tugtog** sa radyo.","translation":"The **music** on the radio is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Naririnig mo ba ang **tugtog** ng gitara?","translation":"Do you hear the **playing** of the guitar?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, karaniwang magaspang na bato o espongha, na ginagamit sa pagkuskos ng katawan upang maalis ang libag o dumi.
etymology: From pang- (instrumental prefix) + hilod (to scrub off dirt from the skin).
original_explanation: The OG Filipino exfoliator. This is usually a smooth-ish, flattish stone ('bato') you find and keep in the bathroom to scrub away the 'libag' (dead skin/grime). Before loofahs and body scrubs became a thing, the panghilod was there for us, making sure we were squeaky clean. It's a low-tech, high-effectiveness skincare tool.
usage_notes: Traditionally a pumice-like stone, but can now refer to loofahs, bath scrubs, or any exfoliating tool.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaspang ang bagong **panghilod** na nabili ni nanay sa palengke.","translation":"The new **scrubber** mom bought from the market is rough."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong idiin ang **panghilod** at baka magasgas ang balat mo.","translation":"Don't press the **scouring stone** too hard or you might scratch your skin."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pagpapahayag para sa isang taong mapagkunwari, hindi tapat, o nagpapakita ng magkaibang pag-uugali sa magkaibang tao o sitwasyon.
etymology: Literal na salin ng 'two faces', isang unibersal na konsepto.
original_explanation: Ah, the classic 'plastik'. This is that 'friend' who's super nice to your face ('BFF!') but is the admin of a 'Chismis About You' group chat. They have one face for you, and another for everyone else. It's the ultimate betrayal, the showbiz-level backstabber. In short, a hypocrite.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang isang matinding negatibong paglalarawan sa karakter ng isang tao. Ang anyong pang-uri ay 'may dalawang mukha'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap magtiwala sa taong may **dalawang mukha**.","translation":"It's hard to trust a **two-faced** person."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa kanya, kilala siyang may **dalawang mukha**.","translation":"Don't believe him, he's known to be **two-faced**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mabagal kumilos, mag-isip, o umusad.
original_explanation: The mortal enemy of anyone with a deadline. It's the 'loading...' icon of human behavior. 'Ang kupad mo naman!' is the national anthem of impatient people waiting for a friend to get ready, for a cashier to give change, or for a government service to process their papers. It’s the opposite of 'diskarte'.
usage_notes: Can function as a noun ('ang kupad' - the slowness) or an adjective ('mabagal' is more common, but 'huwag kang kupad' is idiomatic). The verb form is 'kumupad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakainis ang **kupad** ng serbisyo sa opisinang iyon.","translation":"The **slowness** of the service in that office is annoying."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **kupad**, male-late na tayo!","translation":"Don't be **slow**, we're going to be late!"}]

meaning_filipino: Napakadalang; hindi madalas mangyari o makita.
etymology: Reduplication of "bihira" (rare, seldom) to intensify the meaning.
original_explanation: That friend who only messages when they need something? They contact you bihi-bihira. It's like a Grab promo code that actually works, or finding a vacant seat on the MRT during rush hour. It's an event so rare, it's worth mentioning.
usage_notes: An intensified form of "bihira".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bihi-bihira** na lang siyang umuwi sa probinsya mula nang magtrabaho sa Maynila.","translation":"He **very seldom** goes home to the province since he started working in Manila."},{"sentence":"Ang mga ganitong pagkakataon ay **bihi-bihira** lamang dumating.","translation":"Opportunities like this come **very rarely**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o lugar kung saan nagluluto ng pagkain, tulad ng kalan o pugon.
original_explanation: Your kitchen's command center. This could be a modern induction stove that sings to you, a classic gas range, or even the traditional `kalan de uling` (charcoal stove) that gives everything a smoky, nostalgic flavor. It's where the magic (and sometimes, the smoke alarm) happens.
usage_notes: Can refer to the appliance (stove) or the general area for cooking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilinis ang **lutuan** pagkatapos mong gamitin.","translation":"Please clean the **stove** after you use it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipagalaw ang isang bagay mula sa bibig pababa sa lalamunan patungo sa sikmura. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagtanggap ng isang bagay na mahirap, tulad ng kahihiyan o pagkatalo.
original_explanation: Literally, to swallow your food. Figuratively, it's what you do with your pride ('lunukin ang pride') when you have to text your ex because you need something. It's also what you do with a bitter pill—like accepting that your team lost in the UAAP finals.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally (for food/drink) and figuratively (for pride, insults, defeat).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **lunukin** ang buto ng pakwan.","translation":"Don't **swallow** the watermelon seed."},{"sentence":"Kinailangan niyang **lunukin** ang kanyang pride at humingi ng tawad.","translation":"He had to **swallow** his pride and apologize."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng pakiramdam ng pagkasuklam o pagnanais na sumuka; kasuklam-suklam.
etymology: From root 'duwal,' meaning nausea or the act of gagging. The 'naka-' and reduplication 'dudu-' intensifies the feeling it causes.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when you see your ex's super cheesy new couple photos. Or the smell of a forgotten baon in a lunchbox after a long weekend. It's something so gross or cringey, it makes you want to literally or figuratively throw up.
usage_notes: Can describe physical sensations (like a bad smell) or emotional reactions (like disgust at an action).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakaduduwal** ang amoy na nagmumula sa basurahan.","translation":"The smell coming from the trash can is **nauseating**."},{"sentence":"Ang kaniyang mga salita ay **nakaduduwal** pakinggan dahil puro kasinungalingan.","translation":"His words are **sickening** to hear because they are full of lies."}]

meaning_filipino: Pananakit o kirot na nararamdaman sa isa o higit pang ngipin.
original_explanation: The kind of pain that makes you question all your life choices, especially your relationship with candy and your fear of the dentist. It's a special kind of hell that makes you want to pull your own tooth out with pliers you saw in a Tom Hanks movie.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang karamdaman. Madalas ding gamiting dahilan o excuse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi siya nakapasok sa trabaho dahil sa matinding **sakit ng ngipin**.","translation":"He couldn't go to work because of a severe **toothache**."},{"sentence":"Ang lunas sa **sakit ng ngipin** ay ang pagpunta sa dentista.","translation":"The cure for a **toothache** is to go to the dentist."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay, kasuotan, o gawain na angkop o karaniwang ginagamit sa bukid o probinsya.
original_explanation: This is your 'probinsya' starter pack. The worn-out t-shirt, comfy shorts, and tsinelas you wear when you're not trying to impress anyone. It's the opposite of your 'pamporma'. Think of it as cottagecore, but Pinoy style.
usage_notes: Often used to describe clothes, tools, or a general style. `Damit pambukid` is a very common phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magsuot ka ng damit na **pambukid** dahil maputik doon.","translation":"Wear **farm** clothes because it's muddy there."},{"sentence":"Ang bota na ito ay sadyang ginawa para sa gawaing **pambukid**.","translation":"These boots were specifically made for **farm** work."}]

translation: the act of playing a musical instrument
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglikha ng tunog o musika gamit ang isang instrumento.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pag-` at sa salitang ugat na `tugtog` (musika; pagpapatunog ng instrumento).
original_explanation: Your neighbor's favorite hobby at 2 AM. It's the jamming session with your barkada, the solo piano practice for your crush, or the videoke marathon that lasts until sunrise. Basically, any act of making music, whether you're a rockstar or just trying to learn "Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star" on a ukulele.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling ang kanyang **pagtugtog** ng gitara.","translation":"His **playing** of the guitar is excellent."},{"sentence":"Nagsasanay siya ng **pagtugtog** ng biyolin tuwing hapon.","translation":"She practices **playing** the violin every afternoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang posisyon kung saan ang karaniwang itaas na bahagi ay nakaharap sa ibaba.
original_explanation: Like a baso on the table, placed upside down to keep dust out. Or that feeling after a long day, you just want to lie 'nakataob' on your bed and not move. Also, if a boat capsizes, 'nakataob' na 'yung bangka.
usage_notes: Used for objects that are flipped over, or for a person lying on their stomach.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwanan mong **nakataob** ang mga plato para matuyo.","translation":"Leave the plates **face down** to dry."},{"sentence":"Natagpuan ang bangka na **nakataob** sa dalampasigan.","translation":"The boat was found **overturned** on the shore."}]

translation: to fill up; to fill in
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng laman o nilalaman ang isang sisidlan o espasyo hanggang sa umabot sa takdang hangganan.
original_explanation: The command you hear at a gas station: "Boss, pa-punin!" It's what you do with a form (fill in the blanks) or your plate during a fiesta (fill it up... to the brim). It's the opposite of your bank account after a 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: A more active/command form compared to 'pumuno'. Often used interchangeably with 'punuin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **punin** mo ng tubig ang timba.","translation":"Please **fill** the bucket with water."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **punin** ang lahat ng patlang sa aplikasyon.","translation":"You need to **fill in** all the blanks on the application form."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at marahas na pagsugod, pag-atake, o pagdagsa ng anuman.
original_explanation: Imagine the doors opening for a 12.12 sale and everyone just goes wild. That's a *pagdaluhong*. It's a chaotic, forceful rush—whether it's an army attacking a fort, a mob rushing a stage, or you rushing the buffet table when they finally bring out the lechon.
usage_notes: Carries a strong sense of force and often, chaos or violence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi napigilan ng mga guwardiya ang **pagdaluhong** ng galit na mga raliyista.","translation":"The guards could not stop the **onslaught** of the angry protesters."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagdaluhong** ng bagyo ay nag-iwan ng matinding pinsala.","translation":"The **onslaught** of the typhoon left severe damage."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang-tubig (Pistia stratiotes) na lumulutang sa mga lawa, ilog, at iba pang anyong tubig na hindi umaagos.
etymology: The name of the Quiapo district in Manila is said to originate from this plant's name, as it was abundant in the Pasig River.
original_explanation: That green, leafy stuff that covers ponds and makes them look like a green carpet? That's "kiyapo". It's the plant version of a "tambay," just floating around, doing nothing, and multiplying like crazy. Also, it's the namesake of Quiapo, Manila, because the area used to be full of it. So next time you're stuck in traffic there, you can blame this plant.
usage_notes: Often confused with "water lily". "Kiyapo" refers specifically to Pistia stratiotes. The place name is spelled "Quiapo".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napuno ng **kiyapo** ang ilog kaya nahirapan nang dumaan ang mga bangka.","translation":"The river was filled with **water cabbage**, making it difficult for boats to pass."},{"sentence":"Ang mga halaman na iyon ay hindi water lily, kundi **kiyapo**.","translation":"Those plants are not water lilies, but **water lettuce**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit o pagkonsumo ng isang bagay hanggang sa wala nang matira.
original_explanation: This is your mom's command at the dinner table: "Ubusin mo 'yang pagkain mo!" (Finish your food!). It's also what happens to your salary three days after payday. 'Ubusin' is the active act of making something disappear completely, whether it's food, money, or your patience.
usage_notes: An object-focus verb. The action is to make the object 'ubos' (gone/finished).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **ubusin** ang lahat ng pagkain bago ito masira.","translation":"We need to **consume all** the food before it spoils."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ubusin** ang pasensya ko!","translation":"Don't **use up all** my patience!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang elektroniko na ginagamit upang pataasin ang antas o lakas ng isang tunog.
original_explanation: The official name for your Bluetooth speaker, the karaoke machine's amplifier, or the megaphone used by the barangay tanod. Anything that takes a sound and makes it LOUDER is a **palakas-tunog**. It's the essential tool for every Pinoy party and public announcement.
usage_notes: A compound word from 'palakas' (to make strong) and 'tunog' (sound).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sira ang **palakas-tunog** kaya mahina ang anunsyo.","translation":"The **loudspeaker** is broken, that's why the announcement is faint."},{"sentence":"Ikabit mo ang gitara sa **palakas-tunog**.","translation":"Connect the guitar to the **amplifier**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang agham panlipunan na nag-aaral sa produksyon, distribusyon, at pagkonsumo ng mga produkto at serbisyo.
original_explanation: This is that college subject that tried to explain why your baon was never enough (scarcity), why the price of instant noodles goes up (inflation), and why your parents complain about taxes. It's the study of how people, businesses, and governments make choices about money. Basically, the "adulting is hard" subject.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng kursong **Ekonomiks** sa Unibersidad ng Pilipinas.","translation":"She took up **Economics** at the University of the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng mga mata na nakaputing o nakatingin paitaas, karaniwang dahil sa pagkahimatay, sakit, o matinding emosyon.
original_explanation: This is the scary one. When someone faints or has a seizure and their eyes roll back so you only see the whites. 'Nakatirik ang mata.' Also used hyperbolically for extreme annoyance: "Napatirik ang mata ko sa ka-OA-han niya." (My eyes rolled back at her over-the-top antics.)
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe the state of one's eyes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang himatayin siya, nakita nilang **nakatirik** ang kanyang mga mata.","translation":"When she fainted, they saw that her **eyes** were **rolled back**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pambahay na pinananatiling malamig ang loob upang mapreserba ang mga pagkain at inumin.
original_explanation: 'Yung best friend ng tirang ulam. Dito mo tinatago 'yung adobo, sinigang, at kanin para 'di mapanis. Ito rin 'yung cabinet na binubuksan mo every 5 minutes kahit alam mong walang bagong laman, hoping na may magic na lumitaw na pagkain. Colloquially, "pridyider" or "ref".
usage_notes: The word "pridyider" (from English "fridge") is far more common in everyday speech. "Repriherador" is the formal, Spanish-derived term often seen in manuals or formal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilagay mo ang gatas sa **repriherador** para hindi masira.","translation":"Put the milk in the **refrigerator** so it won't spoil."},{"sentence":"Puno ang aming **repriherador** pagkatapos mamalengke.","translation":"Our **refrigerator** is full after going to the market."}]

translation: to be able to heal; to cure
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang magpagaling o magbigay-lunas sa isang karamdaman o sakit.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na nakahanap ka ng gamot sa sakit mo, physical man o emotional. Pwedeng paracetamol para sa lagnat, o pwedeng K-drama marathon para sa sawi mong puso. 'Uy, 'tong milk tea na 'to, nakakagaling ng stress!'
usage_notes: The prefix "maka-" here indicates ability or potential. "Nakagaling" is the past tense (was able to heal).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana'y **makagaling** ang gamot na ito sa iyong ubo.","translation":"Hopefully, this medicine will be able to **cure** your cough."},{"sentence":"Walang sugat na hindi **makagaling** sa paglipas ng panahon.","translation":"There is no wound that time cannot **heal**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pag-aalis ng partikular na dumi o bagay gamit ang walis. Ang diin ay nasa bagay na inaalis.
original_explanation: The more focused, 'get this thing out of my sight' version of sweeping. You're not just cleaning a place ('walisan'); you're targeting specific debris. 'Walisin mo yung mga bubog ng nakaraan' (Sweep away the broken pieces of the past). It’s about being decisive with what needs to go.
usage_notes: Focus is on the object being swept. Contrast with 'walisan' (to sweep a place).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **walisin** ang mga tuyong dahon at ipunin sa isang sako.","translation":"You need to **sweep away** the dry leaves and collect them in a sack."},{"sentence":"Wina**walis** niya ang alikabok papunta sa ilalim ng kama.","translation":"She is **sweeping** the dust under the bed."}]

translation: is fond of; finds delightful; beloved
meaning_filipino: Isang tao, bagay, o gawain na lubos na nagugustuhan, nagbibigay ng saya, o kinatutuwaan.
etymology: From 'giliw' (affection, delight), inflected as a verb. 'ka-' + duplicated first syllable 'gi' + 'giliw' + '-an'.
original_explanation: This is your 'bias' in a K-Pop group, your favorite character in a series, or that one specific milk tea flavor you always order. It’s what makes you go 'awww' or gives you that warm, fuzzy feeling. It's the target of your affection and delight.
usage_notes: Used to describe the object of someone's fondness or delight. Can function as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aso niyang si Bantay ay **kinagigiliwan** ng lahat sa kanilang lugar.","translation":"His dog, Bantay, is **beloved** by everyone in their neighborhood."},{"sentence":"**Kinagigiliwan** kong panoorin ang mga lumang pelikulang Pilipino.","translation":"I **am fond of** watching old Filipino movies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paksa o isyu na pinag-uusapan, sinusuri, o pinag-aaralan.
original_explanation: The 'agenda' for your meeting or chismis session. It's the main point, the 'what are we talking about today?' The subject of your thesis, your PowerPoint, or the latest drama you're dissecting with your bestie over coffee.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of formal or structured discussions. Can be used as a verb root 'talakayin' (to discuss).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang susunod na **talakay** ay tungkol sa budget ng proyekto.","translation":"The next **topic** is about the project's budget."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **talakay** na ito para sa kinabukasan ng kumpanya.","translation":"This **discussion subject** is important for the future of the company."}]

translation: to have a drinking session; to get drunk together
meaning_filipino: Sama-samang pag-inom ng alak hanggang sa malasing ang mga kasali.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'to drink' (uminom). This is the main event. It's the 'tagayan' session with the barkada, the 'walwalan' night out, the 'isang case' of Red Horse that magically appears on a Friday night. The suffix '-an' implies a group activity where everyone is a participant in the noble quest of getting drunk together. It's a team sport.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix denotes a reciprocal or group action. It implies a session or an event dedicated to drinking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal **maglasingan** sa kalsada, baka mahuli kayo.","translation":"It's forbidden to **have a drinking session** on the street, you might get caught."},{"sentence":"Nagkayayaan ang magkakaibigan na **maglasingan** para icelebrate ang Pasko.","translation":"The friends decided to **get drunk together** to celebrate Christmas."}]

translation: to invert, to turn upside down, to betray
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbaligtad o pagsalungat sa isang bagay, pananaw, o paninindigan.
original_explanation: This is the action form of 'talikwas'. It's what you *do* when you flip the script. 'Talikwasin mo ang pancake!' (Flip the pancake!). Or on a more dramatic note, it's what a friend does when they betray your trust. 'Huwag mong talikwasin ang ating pinagsamahan.' (Don't betray our friendship). It's the verb for turning things around, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: This is the infinitive/command form of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **talikwasin** ang katotohanan para lang pagtakpan ang iyong pagkakamali.","translation":"Don't **invert** the truth just to cover up your mistake."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **talikwasin** ang bote upang makuha ang huling patak.","translation":"The bottle needs to be **turned upside down** to get the last drop."}]

translation: to remedy; to find a solution
meaning_filipino: Ang paghanap o paggawa ng paraan upang malunasan ang isang suliranin, pagkakamali, o hindi kaaya-ayang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is the Filipino art of "diskarte" or resourcefulness. Your wifi dies before a major presentation? You magremedyo by turning your phone into a hotspot. Kulang ang budget for a birthday party? You magremedyo with a potluck. It's about finding a fix, often creatively, for any and all of life's "ay, nako!" moments.
usage_notes: Can be used for both concrete problems (e.g., fixing a broken item) and abstract issues (e.g., resolving a conflict).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magremedyo** sa sitwasyon sa pamamagitan ng paghingi ng tawad.","translation":"He tried to **remedy** the situation by apologizing."},{"sentence":"Paano kaya tayo **magreremedyo** sa kakulangan ng pondo?","translation":"How can we possibly **find a solution** for the lack of funds?"}]

translation: to make someone do something; to assign a task to someone
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pag-aatas sa isang tao na isagawa ang isang gawain.
etymology: From root `gawa` (do, make) with the causative prefix `pa-` and the object-focus suffix `-in`.
original_explanation: Similar to "pagawa," but the focus here is on the person you're making do the work. "Pagawin mo si bunso ng tsaa." (Make the youngest sibling make tea.) It’s the verb for delegation, whether you're a manager at work or the Ate/Kuya at home. You're not just having something done; you're specifically making *someone* do it.
usage_notes: The object of this verb is the person being commanded to do the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pagawin** mo si Maria ng ulat para sa pulong bukas.","translation":"**Have** Maria **make** the report for the meeting tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **pagawin** ng mga gawaing-bahay ang bisita.","translation":"I don't want to **make** the visitor **do** household chores."}]

translation: to claim as one's own; to appropriate
meaning_filipino: Gawing sarili o kunin ang isang bagay na hindi naman sa iyo sa simula, maging ito man ay may pahintulot o wala.
original_explanation: 'Yung 'mine' mo agad yung item sa online selling kahit 'di ka pa nagbabayad. Or 'yung pag-claim mo sa jowa ng iba. Oops. It's the act of taking something and making it yours, whether you have the right to or not. Think of it as putting a metaphorical flag on something (or someone), sometimes with justification (like claiming a victory), and sometimes... not so much.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation of taking something that doesn't belong to you, but can also be used neutrally for claiming responsibility or a title.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **angkinin** ang gawa ng iba.","translation":"Do not **claim** the work of others as your own."},{"sentence":"Inaasahan kong **angkinin** mo ang responsibilidad sa iyong mga pagkakamali.","translation":"I expect you to **claim** responsibility for your mistakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan kung saan ang dalawa o higit pang partido ay may pangangailangan sa isa't isa; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagkakaroon ng pagkailang o hiya sa isa't isa.
etymology: From `magka-` + `kailangan`. The nuanced meaning of 'to be awkward with each other' is related to `ilang` (awkward).
original_explanation: It's the team needing a star player and the player needing a team. A symbiotic relationship. But in a 'hugot' context, when a couple says "nagkakailangan na kami," it could mean they're becoming awkward and distant, a subtle way of saying things are not like they used to be.
usage_notes: Can mean "to need each other" or, in some contexts, "to be awkward with each other," stemming from a sense of forced interaction or unspoken issues.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang pamilya, normal lang na **magkailangan** ang bawat miyembro.","translation":"In a family, it's only normal for each member to **need each other**."},{"sentence":"Simula nang mag-away sila, tila **nagkakailangan** na sila sa opisina.","translation":"Since they had a fight, they seem to **be awkward with each other** at the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o proseso ng pagsusuri o pag-iimbestiga sa isang bagay o pangyayari upang malaman ang katotohanan.
etymology: From "pag-" (manner of) + "ka-" (abstract noun prefix) + "siyasat" (investigation), from Malay 'siasat'.
original_explanation: This is the 'detective mode' of your friend when you mention a new person you're dating. Ang pagkakasiyasat nila involves checking all social media accounts, mutual friends, and past relationships. It's the thoroughness of a government audit but applied to your love life. Or how your mom inspects your room for any sign of 'kalat'.
usage_notes: Refers to the method or quality of the investigation, not just the investigation itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa masusing **pagkakasiyasat** ng mga pulis, nahuli agad ang salarin.","translation":"Because of the thorough **manner of investigation** by the police, the culprit was immediately caught."},{"sentence":"Kinuwestiyon ang **pagkakasiyasat** sa kaso dahil tila may kinikilingan.","translation":"The **inspection process** of the case was questioned because it seemed biased."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan ng isang bagay na wasto, tama, eksakto, o walang pagkakamali.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when you guess the winning lotto numbers (but didn't bet). It's what your boss rarely says about your work, but what your chismosa neighbor always thinks her gossip is. The highest form of validation. "Tumpak!" is the Filipino equivalent of "Bingo!" or "Nailed it!".
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective or as an interjection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumpak** ang iyong sagot sa pagsusulit.","translation":"Your answer on the test is **correct**."},{"sentence":"Aha! **Tumpak**! Ikaw nga ang kumain ng ulam ko.","translation":"Aha! **Exactly**! It was you who ate my food."}]
