meaning_filipino: Ang agham na nag-aaral sa mga bagay sa kalawakan tulad ng mga bituin, planeta, kometa, at galaksiya, kasama ang kanilang mga katangian, pinagmulan, at paggalaw.
original_explanation: This is the legit, scientific version of looking at the stars. This is what astronomers at PAGASA do, not what your Tita's favorite 'astrologo' does. Astronomiya is about black holes and nebulae, not about whether you'll find love because you're a Leo. It's the science, not the "sign-ence."
usage_notes: The scientific study of celestial objects, distinct from 'astrolohia' (astrology).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **astronomiya** ay isang kamangha-manghang sangay ng agham.","translation":"**Astronomy** is a fascinating branch of science."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa **astronomiya** ang mga black hole at ang pagbuo ng mga bituin.","translation":"**Astronomy** studies black holes and the formation of stars."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang takdang oras, karaniwan sa gabi o madaling araw, kung kailan nagiging mas maramdamin, malungkutin, o nagbabalik-tanaw ang isang tao.
original_explanation: This is that 2 AM to 4 AM window when you're suddenly a philosopher, a poet, and a DJ playing sad songs. Bigla mong naaalala 'yung ex mo from 5 years ago, or 'yung aso mong nawala nung grade 3. Welcome to senti hours, the official time for overthinking and hugot.
usage_notes: Isang kolokyal na parirala na popular sa social media at sa mga kabataan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Alas tres na ng madaling araw, heto na naman ang **senti hours**.","translation":"It's three in the morning, the **sentimental hours** are here again."},{"sentence":"Nag-post na naman siya ng malungkot na kanta, mukhang **senti hours** na niya.","translation":"He posted a sad song again, it looks like it's his **sentimental hours**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sukat o dimensyon ng isang bagay; maaari ring tumukoy sa nakararami o malaking bahagi ng isang pangkat.
original_explanation: Two meanings! 1) The 'plus' in your 'Large vs. Large Plus' drink order. It's the sheer bigness of something, like the size of your backlogs. 2) The majority. 'Ang kalakihan ng klase ay bumagsak sa exam.' (The majority of the class failed the exam.) - a classic professor hugot.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical size or the majority of a group. Context is key to differentiate between 'bigness' and 'majority'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namangha ako sa **kalakihan** ng gusali.","translation":"I was amazed by the **bigness** of the building."},{"sentence":"Ang **kalakihan** ng mga empleyado ay sumang-ayon sa bagong patakaran.","translation":"The **majority** of the employees agreed to the new policy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsasagawa ng isang siruhiya o medikal na operasyon sa isang pasyente.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "opera" (mula sa Espanyol na "operar") at hulaping "-hin".
original_explanation: The verb form of the medical drama. When a doctor needs to "operahin" someone, it means it's time for surgery. "Kailangan siyang operahin agad!" is a staple line in every teleserye hospital scene. It's the act that turns someone into "operado."
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang pokus sa layon (object-focused verb).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang doktor na **ooperahin** sa lola mo?","translation":"Who is the doctor that **will operate on** your grandmother?"},{"sentence":"Kinailangan siyang **operahin** dahil sa appendicitis.","translation":"He had **to be operated on** because of appendicitis."}]

translation: Doña; a title of respect for a woman
meaning_filipino: Isang titulo ng paggalang para sa isang babae, lalo na sa isang may asawa o balo, na may mataas na katayuan sa lipunan.
original_explanation: The female version of "Don." She's the rich, powerful, and often intimidating matriarch. Think of the kontrabida in a teleserye who owns a hacienda and throws wine at people. "Donya Victorina" from Noli Me Tángere is the OG. Today, you might call your friend "Donya" as a joke if she's acting very bossy or high-maintenance. "Wow, donya ang peg, ayaw maglakad sa init!"
usage_notes: An honorific used before a woman's first name. Carries connotations of wealth, power, and sometimes arrogance. Used humorously in modern times to refer to someone acting entitled.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si **Donya** Victorina sa kanyang pagiging mapagpanggap.","translation":"**Doña** Victorina is known for being pretentious."},{"sentence":"Parang isang **donya** kung umasta ang bagong manager.","translation":"The new manager acts like a **doña**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa isang taong may edad na ngunit kumikilos o nag-iisip na parang bata pa.
etymology: Slang, possibly a portmanteau of 'borta' + 'badjing'. The meaning has shifted over time to mean 'immature man'.
original_explanation: A portmanteau of 'borta' (a muscular man) and 'badjing' (a gay man), but its modern meaning has evolved. Now it's a playful jab at a guy who's physically an adult but mentally and emotionally still a kid. Think: 30-year-old who still asks his mom to wash his clothes and spends all his money on toys. It's the male equivalent of 'pabebe.'
usage_notes: A slang term, often used humorously among friends. Can be considered mildly insulting depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang paglalaro ng video games buong araw, para kang **bonjing**!","translation":"Stop playing video games all day, you're like a **man-child**!"},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang mag-asawa dahil isa pa siyang **bonjing** na umaasa sa magulang.","translation":"He doesn't want to get married because he's still a **man-child** who depends on his parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon na nananatili sa dati nitong kalagayan at walang ipinapakitang pagbabago sa paglipas ng panahon.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'hindi' (not) at 'nagbabago' (is changing), mula sa salitang-ugat na 'bago' (new).
original_explanation: This is your tita's "updated" opinion on your love life (or lack thereof) every family reunion. It's also the price of hot pandesal in your suking panaderia since 2010. Some things are just classics. It's the "forever" that's actually real, unlike your ex's promises.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga tao, bagay, damdamin, o sitwasyon na permanente o matatag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal ng isang ina ay **hindi nagbabago**.","translation":"A mother's love is **unchanging**."},{"sentence":"Mula noon hanggang ngayon, **hindi nagbabago** ang paborito niyang ulam.","translation":"From then until now, his favorite dish has **not changed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi o bilang na naiiwan matapos bawasan o alisin ang isang parte; ang labi o sobra.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung last piece of pizza sa box na tinititigan n'yong lahat, or 'yung P500 na lang sa wallet mo a week before sahod. It's what's left. Pwede ring 'yung feelings mong natitira para sa ex mo, kahit may bago ka na. The leftovers.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pandiwa (is remaining) o pang-uri (the remaining thing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kaunti na lang ang **natitira** kong pasensya para sa'yo.","translation":"I only have a little patience **left** for you."},{"sentence":"Ang **natitira** na lang sa ulam ay para kay Tatay.","translation":"The **remaining** food is for Dad."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ikapitong araw ng linggo ayon sa internasyonal na pamantayan (ISO 8601), kasunod ng Biyernes at bago ang Linggo.
etymology: From Spanish 'Sábado', from Latin 'sabbatum', from Greek 'sabbaton', from Hebrew 'Shabbat' (שַׁבָּת), meaning 'day of rest'.
original_explanation: The best day of the week, no contest. It's the day for malling, grocery runs, family time, or simply binge-watching a series from morning 'til night. The official 'pahinga' (rest) day before the 'simba' (church) day.
usage_notes: As a proper noun, it is usually capitalized. In the Filipino cultural week, it is considered the sixth day, with Monday being the first.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa mall sa darating na **Sabado**.","translation":"Let's meet at the mall this coming **Saturday**."},{"sentence":"Tuwing **Sabado** ang araw ng aming pangkalahatang paglilinis.","translation":"**Every Saturday** is our general cleaning day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakanipis na hibla o sinulid, lalo na ang bahagi ng bumbilya na umiilaw kapag pinadaluyan ng kuryente.
original_explanation: That tiny, fragile wire inside an old-school lightbulb. It's the 'bright idea' part of the bulb that literally lights up. When it breaks, 'wala na, finish na.' Parang 'yung pasensya mo sa Monday morning, manipis at madaling maputol. Also, the stuff you use for 3D printing.
usage_notes: A technical or scientific term. Not commonly used in casual conversation unless discussing lightbulbs or specific scientific concepts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napundi na ang bumbilya dahil naputol ang **pilamento** nito.","translation":"The lightbulb burned out because its **filament** broke."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng bagong **pilamento** para sa aking 3D printer.","translation":"I need a new **filament** for my 3D printer."}]

translation: to end up disagreeing; for a plan not to push through
meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagkakasundo o hindi pagkatuloy ng isang usapan, plano, o transaksyon dahil sa pagtanggi ng isa o parehong panig.
original_explanation: That awkward moment when your barkada's travel plans slowly die in the group chat. One by one, people back out until "drawing na lang." That whole process is "nagkahindian." It's the polite Filipino way of things falling apart because someone said "hindi" (no), and then someone else did, and so on. It's the ghosting of group plans.
usage_notes: Implies a mutual or collective backing out or disagreement that leads to a plan's failure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagplano kaming magbakasyon pero **nagkahindian** sa huli.","translation":"We planned to go on vacation but **it didn't push through** in the end."},{"sentence":"Ayusin n'yo ang presyo para hindi tayo **magkahindian**.","translation":"Let's agree on a price so we don't **end up disagreeing**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang babaeng kasama ng magulang sa pagiging ninang sa binyag o kumpil; o kasama ng ikakasal bilang ninang. Ginagamit din bilang tawag sa isang matalik na kaibigang babae.
original_explanation: Your mom's official 'chismis' partner. Technically, she's the godmother to your sibling, or your godmother, making her your mom's 'kumare'. But in modern Pinoy culture, it's the term of endearment for your mom's bestie, the Tita who gives you the best Pamasko, and the one who knows all the family secrets. The male version is 'kumpare'.
usage_notes: The relationship between two women who are co-godparents is called 'mag-kumare'. It is used both as a term of address and a noun describing the relationship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta rito mamaya si **Kumare**ng Susan.","translation":"**Kumare** Susan is coming over later."},{"sentence":"Ang nanay ko at ang ninang mo ay mag-**kumare**.","translation":"My mother and your godmother are **kumares** (co-godmothers)."}]

translation: as far as the eye can see
meaning_filipino: Hanggang saan kayang tanawin ng paningin; ang lawak na nasasakop ng tingin.
etymology: Literally 'reach of the eye', from Tagalog 'abot' (reach) and 'mata' (eye).
original_explanation: That feeling when you're at the beach, looking at the horizon, and it's just endless sea and sky. Or when you're stuck in traffic on SLEX and all you can see is a sea of cars. It's the entire area visible in your peripheral vision, the maximum range of your chismis-seeking eyes.
usage_notes: A common idiomatic expression. Often used in descriptive writing or to emphasize a vast, open space.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hanggang sa **abot ng mata** ay puro palayan ang makikita mo.","translation":"**As far as the eye can see**, you will see nothing but rice fields."},{"sentence":"Nakatayo siya sa tuktok ng bundok, tinatanaw ang kalawakan sa **abot ng mata**.","translation":"He stood on the mountaintop, gazing at the expanse **as far as the eye can see**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagputol ng isang bagay sa napakaliliit na piraso gamit ang paulit-ulit at mabilis na hiwa; maaari ring mangahulugan ng pagbuhos ng maraming tama, tulad ng bala.
original_explanation: Two main vibes here. Vibe 1 (Kitchen): What you do to garlic and onions when you're angry. You don't just slice, you 'tumadtad' until they're practically a paste. It's therapy via chopping board. Vibe 2 (Action Movie): What happens to the bad guy's car in a chase scene. It gets riddled with bullets. 'Tadtad ng bala' is the classic phrase. It's the verb for extreme, repetitive piercing or chopping.
usage_notes: The word can be used literally for cooking or figuratively for being riddled with something (bullets, questions, etc.). This is the completed aspect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumadtad** siya ng bawang at sibuyas para sa ginisang ulam.","translation":"She **finely chopped** garlic and onions for the sautéed dish."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bala ay **tumadtad** sa pader ng lumang gusali.","translation":"The bullets **riddled** the wall of the old building."}]

translation: to substitute; to use as a replacement
meaning_filipino: Gamitin ang isang bagay o tao bilang kahalili o kapalit ng iba.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'next please!' move. Your phone broke? `Ipalit` mo ng bago. Your jowa is giving you a headache? Nako, `ipalit` mo na 'yan! (Just kidding... mostly). It's the act of replacing something or someone with another. From a dead lightbulb to a new hire who has to take over, `ipalit` is the verb for the job.
usage_notes: Very common verb. Can be used for objects, people, or even abstract concepts. The object being used as the replacement is the focus of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wala akong pambayad na barya, kaya itong isanlibo na lang ang **ipalit** mo.","translation":"I don't have coins to pay, so just **use** this one-thousand bill **as payment**."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **ipalit** natin kay Ana habang naka-leave siya?","translation":"Who will we **use as a substitute** for Ana while she is on leave?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng laro ng baraha kung saan ang mga manlalaro ay tumataya sa halaga ng kanilang mga hawak na baraha, na may layuning magkaroon ng pinakamahusay na kombinasyon o manalo sa pamamagitan ng pagpapaniwala sa iba na sila ay mayroon nito.
original_explanation: The official 'lamay' (wake) sport, besides tong-its and mahjong. This is where you see your titos transform into serious strategists, their faces unreadable ('poker face,' get it?). It's a game of skill, luck, and bluffing your way to victory, even if your hand is just a bunch of random cards. The pot money is usually just for fun, but the bragging rights? Priceless.
usage_notes: Refers to the card game.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdamag naglaro ng **poker** ang mga tiyuhin ko sa burol.","translation":"My uncles played **poker** all night at the wake."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng 'poker face' para hindi mabasa ng kalaban ang iyong mga baraha.","translation":"You need a 'poker face' so your opponent can't read your cards."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos na ibagsak, gibain, o patumbahin ang isang bagay na nakatayo.
etymology: From the causative prefix `ipa-` and the root word `buwal` (to fall, to be toppled).
original_explanation: This is what you do to an old, unstable wall or a tree that's threatening your roof during a typhoon. "**Ipabuwal** na natin 'yang pader bago pa may madisgrasya." On a grander scale, it's what activists shout about corrupt systems: "**Ipabuwal** ang rehimeng mapang-api!" From home renovation to political revolution, 'ipabuwal' gets it done.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal demolition (trees, walls) or figurative overthrowing (governments, leaders).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang may-ari na **ipabuwal** ang lumang bahay para magtayo ng bago.","translation":"The owner decided to **have** the old house **demolished** to build a new one."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **ipabuwal** ang punong iyon dahil malapit na sa mga kable ng kuryente.","translation":"That tree needs to be **taken down** because it's near the power lines."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng kakayahang magbata o magtimpi sa hirap, sakit, o anumang hindi kaaya-ayang sitwasyon nang hindi nagrereklamo.
original_explanation: The official trait of every commuter in Metro Manila traffic. Also describes anyone who can survive on instant noodles until payday, or someone who stays in a toxic relationship hoping things will change. It's the 'tiis ganda' and 'tiis pogi' mindset personified.
usage_notes: Describes a person's character trait of having high tolerance for suffering or difficulty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong hirap ng buhay, nananatiling **mapagtiis** ang mga Pilipino.","translation":"No matter the hardships in life, Filipinos remain **enduring**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang kalagayan na lubhang kaawa-awa, kalunus-lunos, o nakakadurog ng puso.
original_explanation: This is when something or someone is so sad, you can't help but feel sorry for them. The stray dog shivering in the rain. Your friend after a brutal breakup. The look on your face when you check your bank account after a 12.12 sale. It's a state of extreme 'aww, kawawa naman.'
usage_notes: The reduplication of 'habag' intensifies the meaning to 'very pitiful'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **kahabag-habag** ang itsura ng lungsod matapos ang malakas na lindol.","translation":"The city's appearance became **pitiful** after the strong earthquake."},{"sentence":"Natagpuan nila ang aso sa isang **kahabag-habag** na kalagayan.","translation":"They found the dog in a **miserable** condition."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paraan ng pagluluto kung saan ang pagkain ay binabalutan ng galapong o harina bago iprito. Maaari ring tumukoy sa mismong putahe.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "rebozado," na nangangahulugang "coated in batter."
original_explanation: Basically, anything na sinawsaw sa batter at pinirito. Camaron Rebosado (shrimp), Calamares Rebosado (squid)... parang yung puso mong battered and bruised, pero deep-fried to golden perfection para maging crispy on the outside, soft on the inside. Comfort food!
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa paglalarawan ng mga putahe, lalo na ang hipon (Camaron Rebosado). Kapag ginamit bilang pangngalan, tumutukoy ito sa mismong putahe.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito niyang ulam ang camaron **rebosado**.","translation":"Her favorite dish is battered shrimp (**rebosado**)."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang isdang **rebosado** kapag mainit pa.","translation":"**Battered and fried** fish is delicious while it's still hot."}]

meaning_filipino: Napakaikli o panandalian lamang; tumatagal lamang sa maikling panahon.
original_explanation: This is not a common word. The root `saglit` (a moment) is extremely common, but `masaglit` as an adjective is rare. People would say 'saglit lang' (just a moment) or 'maikli lang' (just short). If used, it would describe something as being very fleeting, like a shooting star or your salary. It sounds a bit poetic or dated.
usage_notes: Very rare. The common way to express this idea is using 'maikli' (short) or the adverb 'saglit' itself. Its usage is often considered literary or archaic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **masaglit** na tingin lang ang naibigay niya bago siya umalis.","translation":"Just a **brief** glance was what he gave before he left."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay ay **masaglit**, kaya't dapat sulitin.","translation":"Life is **momentary**, so it should be made the most of."}]

meaning_filipino: Mabilis na nagaganap o isinasagawa; sa maikling panahon lamang.
original_explanation: 'Yung sweldo mo na isang kisapmata lang, ubos na. 'Yung pag-ibig na parang summer, 'madali' lang. It's the "now you see it, now you don't" of time.
usage_notes: The stress is on the second syllable: /ma-DA-li/. This distinguishes it from 'madali' (/ma-da-LI/), meaning 'easy'. Often functions as an adverb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **madali** niyang pag-alis ay ikinagulat ng lahat.","translation":"His **quick** departure surprised everyone."},{"sentence":"**Madali** lang siyang dumaan dito.","translation":"He only passed by here **briefly**."}]

translation: marketplace; place for buying and selling
meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan nagaganap ang malawakang bentahan at bilihan ng mga produkto at serbisyo; isang pamilihan o palengke.
etymology: Mula sa 'bili' (buy/sell). Ang unlaping 'pag-' at hulaping '-an' kasama ang pag-uulit ng unang pantig ('bi') ay karaniwang tumutukoy sa lugar kung saan ginagawa ang isang kilos nang sabayan.
original_explanation: Think Divisoria, a Shopee flash sale, or your neighborhood palengke on a Sunday morning. It's a place of chaotic commerce where everyone is either buying or selling. It's the noun form of 'where the magic (of getting a good bargain) happens.'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'pamilihan' or 'palengke'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagsakan sa Divisoria ay isang tanyag na **pagbilihan** ng mga damit.","translation":"The wholesale market in Divisoria is a famous **marketplace** for clothes."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagbigay ng isang bagay bilang alay, regalo, o tanda ng paggalang o pagmamahal. Ito ay isang pormal at taimtim na pagbibigay.
original_explanation: A more formal and dramatic version of 'nagbigay.' This isn't just giving a gift; it's making an offering. Think 'Handog ng Pilipino sa Mundo' or a hero who 'naghandog ng buhay para sa bayan.' It’s giving with a capital G, often involving sacrifice, deep respect, or a TV special.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, literary, or patriotic contexts. Carries more weight and solemnity than 'nagbigay' (gave).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naghandog** sila ng mga bulaklak sa dambana ng mga bayani.","translation":"They **offered** flowers at the heroes' shrine."},{"sentence":"Ang mang-aawit ay **naghandog** ng isang konsiyerto para sa kanyang mga tagahanga.","translation":"The singer **presented** a concert for their fans."}]

meaning_filipino: Paglalarawan sa isang tao o sitwasyon na nakaranas ng kabiguan, kasawian, o masamang kapalaran, lalo na sa pag-ibig.
original_explanation: The official adjective for the "sawi sa pag-ibig" club. If your crush left you on 'seen', you're sawi. If you bet on the wrong team, you're sawi. It's the universe basically telling you, "better luck next time, p're." It's the patron saint of all things #Hugot.
usage_notes: Very commonly used in the phrase "sawi sa pag-ibig" (unlucky in love).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kuwento tungkol sa mga **sawing** mangingibig ang naging alamat.","translation":"Many stories about **ill-fated** lovers have become legends."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka habambuhay magiging **sawi**.","translation":"Don't worry, you won't be **unfortunate** forever."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae na ang hanapbuhay ay ang pakikipagtalik kapalit ng bayad.
original_explanation: Ito yung term para sa babaeng nasa industriya ng prostitusyon. It's a loaded and often derogatory term. Sa modernong usapan, some prefer "sex worker" for a less judgmental label, but 'prostituta' is the classic, harsh-sounding Spanish loanword we know.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa babae. Ang salita ay maaaring ituring na mapanira o mapanakit. Ang mas neutral na termino ay 'sex worker'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pelikula, ginampanan niya ang papel ng isang **prostituta** na may ginintuang puso.","translation":"In the movie, she played the role of a **prostitute** with a heart of gold."},{"sentence":"Maraming organisasyon ang tumutulong sa mga dating **prostituta** upang magbagong-buhay.","translation":"Many organizations help former **prostitutes** to start a new life."}]

translation: to be in danger; to be at risk
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nasa bingit ng kapahamakan, sakuna, o anumang masamang maaaring mangyari.
original_explanation: That feeling when you realize you forgot to reply to your mom's text from 8 hours ago. Or when you're walking home alone at 2 AM and you hear footsteps. It's the state of being when the universe whispers, 'You in danger, girl.'
usage_notes: An intransitive verb indicating a state of being at risk.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaaring **manganib** ang iyong kalusugan kung patuloy kang maninigarilyo.","translation":"Your health might **be in danger** if you continue to smoke."},{"sentence":"Nang dahil sa bagyo, **nanganib** ang buhay ng mga mangingisda sa laot.","translation":"Because of the storm, the lives of the fishermen at sea **were endangered**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na pinapatakbo o ginagamitan ng motor.
etymology: From Tagalog 'de-' (indicating manner or means) + Spanish 'motor'.
original_explanation: Anything that goes "vroom vroom" instead of being pushed or pulled by hand (or by kabayo). Your tricycle, bangka, or even 'yung blender mo—lahat 'yan de-motor. It's the upgrade from "de-padyak" (pedal-powered) or "de-sarasarili" (self-powered).
usage_notes: The prefix "de-" is Spanish-derived and indicates "of" or "by means of".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mabilis ang biyahe gamit ang bangkang **de-motor**.","translation":"The trip is faster using a **motorized** boat."},{"sentence":"Pinalitan na niya ang kanyang bisikletang de-padyak ng isang scooter na **de-motor**.","translation":"He replaced his pedal-powered bicycle with a **motorized** scooter."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakaliit na sukat ng likido, partikular na ng inuming may alkohol; isang katiting na dami.
original_explanation: 'Penge ngang isang **dram** ng Fundador!' Eto yung para sa mga 'isang shot lang' moments. Hindi isang baso, hindi isang bote, kundi isang patak lang para pampagana o pampatulog. Very Titos and Titas of Manila ang term.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pagtukoy sa alak o anumang inuming may alkohol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uminom lang siya ng isang **dram** ng whiskey bago umuwi.","translation":"He just drank a **dram** of whiskey before going home."}]

meaning_filipino: May dumi; hindi malinis.
original_explanation: The default setting of your sibling's room. Also, your hands after eating isaw with your bare hands. It's the opposite of malinis. Can also be used for 'dirty' thoughts or intentions. 'Madumi maglaro' = plays dirty.
usage_notes: A very common and basic adjective. The variant `marumi` is also widely used and considered more standard by some.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sahig ay **madumi** kaya kailangan itong walisin.","translation":"The floor is **dirty** so it needs to be swept."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang humawak sa pagkain kung **madumi** ang kamay mo.","translation":"Don't touch the food if your hands are **dirty**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at bilog na laruan, karaniwang gawa sa salamin, na ginagamit sa isang uri ng laro.
original_explanation: This is the OG "collectible" before Funko Pops. You'd find kids flicking these glass balls in the dusty streets, trying to win their friends' collections. The shiny, swirly ones were the "jolen" equivalent of a rare Pokemon card.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'jolen' or 'holen'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala ang paborito kong **poly** na may disenyo sa loob.","translation":"I lost my favorite **marble** that had a design inside."},{"sentence":"Magaling siyang mag-target sa laro ng **poly**.","translation":"He's great at aiming in the game of **marbles**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa panitikan; pampanitikan.
original_explanation: This is the Filipinized, 'tunog-Espanyol' version of 'literary'. It's what your strict Filipino teacher would prefer you use over the English word. It adds a bit of classic, intellectual flair. 'Wow, ang lalim ng hugot mo, pang-award, sobrang literarya!'
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pormal na pagsulat at pananalita, partikular sa larangan ng sining at panitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga tula ay may mataas na kalidad na **literarya**.","translation":"His poems have a high **literary** quality."},{"sentence":"Isang pagsusuring **literarya** ang ipinagawa ng guro.","translation":"The teacher assigned a **literary** analysis."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na hindi maaaring pagkatiwalaan o asahan.
original_explanation: Your friend who always says "On the way na ako!" but is actually still in the shower. Sila 'yung taong di-mapagkakatiwalaan pagdating sa "Filipino time." Also applies to sketchy WiFi connections and politicians' promises.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang tao, sistema, o impormasyon na hindi mapagkakatiwalaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nalaman niyang **di-mapagkakatiwalaan** ang kanyang kasosyo sa negosyo.","translation":"He found out that his business partner was **untrustworthy**."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa mga website na **di-mapagkakatiwalaan** na humihingi ng personal na impormasyon.","translation":"Be careful of **unreliable** websites that ask for personal information."}]

translation: inescapable, cannot be gotten out of
meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon o problema na hindi matatakasan o maiiwasan; walang paraan para makalusot.
etymology: Mula sa 'di' (not) + 'malulusutan' (can be escaped from/squeezed through).
original_explanation: That feeling when you're stuck in a family reunion and your Tita asks why you're still single. That's a di-malulusutang situation. Or when you have three deadlines on the same day. There's no escape, you just have to face it. It's the ultimate 'This is my life now' moment.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mga hindi matatakasang sitwasyon, obligasyon, o suliranin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagbabayad ng buwis ay isang responsibilidad na **di-malulusutan**.","translation":"Paying taxes is a responsibility that is **inescapable**."},{"sentence":"Nahuli siya sa akto, isang sitwasyong **di-malulusutan**.","translation":"He was caught in the act, a situation that **cannot be gotten out of**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalakbay sa kahabaan ng baybayin o tabing-dagat.
original_explanation: This is the scenic route. Think of a road trip where you're driving alongside the sea, windows down, with the perfect 'senti' playlist. It’s the journey along the edge, the long way home with the best view.
usage_notes: A more poetic or geographical term. Not as common in everyday speech as the 'spelling' meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasiyahan ang mga turista sa kanilang **pagbabaybay** sa mga dalampasigan ng Palawan.","translation":"The tourists enjoyed their **traversing of the coast** of Palawan's beaches."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagbabaybay** sakay ng bangka ay nagbigay sa kanila ng magandang tanawin ng mga isla.","translation":"**Coasting** on a boat gave them a beautiful view of the islands."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aktibidad na nangangailangan ng pisikal na pagsisikap at kasanayan, na nilalaro para sa libangan o bilang isang kompetisyon.
original_explanation: From barangay-level basketball with tsinelas as base, to cheering for Hidilyn Diaz in the Olympics. It's any game that makes you sweat, shout, and sometimes, pustahan with your friends. Puso!
usage_notes: Ang baybay na 'sports' ay ginagamit din paminsan-minsan, ngunit ang 'isport' ay ang Filipinized na bersyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong **isport** ay basketball.","translation":"My favorite **sport** is basketball."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **isport** para sa kalusugan ng katawan at isipan.","translation":"**Sport** is important for physical and mental health."}]

meaning_filipino: Pilit o marahas na ipasok o isubo ang isang bagay sa bibig ng isang tao.
original_explanation: A very aggressive way of feeding someone or shutting them up. It's what you want to do to someone who won't stop talking nonsense—'Gusto mo isungalngal ko 'tong sapatos ko sa bibig mo?' It's not a gentle 'subo.' It's forceful, like trying to stuff a whole siopao into your mouth in one go.
usage_notes: Isang napakatindi at agresibong salita. Nagpapahiwatig ito ng puwersa at kawalan ng pahintulot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa galit niya, halos **isungalngal** niya ang pagkain sa bibig ng bata.","translation":"In his anger, he almost **shoved** the food into the child's mouth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hindi inaasahang pangyayari na nagdudulot ng kapahamakan, kalungkutan, o pagkabigo; masamang kapalaran.
etymology: A compound word from kasawian (misfortune) and palad (palm, fate). Literally 'misfortune of fate.'
original_explanation: This is when life gives you lemons, and you have no sugar, no water, and you're allergic to citrus. It's the universe telling you, 'Not today, bes.' Like when you finally saved up for a new phone, then the aircon breaks down. That's kasawiang-palad.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat dramatic term for bad luck. Often seen in literature, news reports about accidents, or telenovelas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **kasawiang-palad** ang pagguho ng gusali na kumitil sa maraming buhay.","translation":"The collapse of the building that claimed many lives was a great **misfortune**."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng mga **kasawiang-palad**, hindi siya sumuko sa kanyang mga pangarap.","translation":"Despite the **misfortunes**, she did not give up on her dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Hilingin sa isang pari o kinikilalang awtoridad na magsagawa ng ritwal ng pagbabasbas sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: The Filipino way of spiritually "activating" something new. Got a new car? `Pabasbasan` mo sa pari para iwas-bangga. New house? `Pabasbasan` mo to drive away the bad spirits (and maybe lower the chance of leaky faucets). It's like getting a divine warranty or a spiritual insurance policy.
usage_notes: The verb form is often 'ipabasbas' (to have something blessed). 'Pabasbasan' as a command means 'to have [it] blessed'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas namin ipapa-**pabasbasan** ang aming bagong sasakyan.","translation":"We will have our new car **blessed** tomorrow."},{"sentence":"**Pabasbasan** natin ang bahay bago tayo lumipat.","translation":"Let's have the house **blessed** before we move in."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi wasto o eksakto; may pagkakamali sa detalye o sukat.
original_explanation: That feeling when you try to follow a YouTube makeup tutorial and end up looking like a clown. Or when your Waze estimate is off by 30 minutes. It's not just wrong, it's specifically *inaccurate* or *imprecise*. It's the "almost, but not quite" of mistakes.
usage_notes: Often used to describe information, measurements, or calculations that are not exact.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-tumpak** ang ibinigay niyang sukat kaya hindi nagkasya ang damit.","translation":"The measurement she gave was **inaccurate**, so the dress didn't fit."},{"sentence":"Maaaring magdulot ng panganib ang **di-tumpak** na datos.","translation":"**Incorrect** data can lead to danger."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang utos, tagubilin, o atas na dapat sundin. Maaari ding tumukoy sa kaayusan ng mga bagay.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'orden' na nangangahulugang 'utos' o 'kaayusan'.
original_explanation: That thing your boss gives you on a Friday at 4:59 PM. It's the "ASAP" in an email, the "bili ka ng suka" from your nanay, or the "Execute Order 66" for Star Wars fans. It's a command you can't refuse... or at least, you'll get in trouble if you do. Also used for food orders in a restaurant ("Ano'ng orden n'yo, ma'am/sir?").
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'utos'. Can also mean 'sequence' or 'arrangement' (e.g., in alphabetical order).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumunod ka sa **orden** ng heneral.","translation":"Follow the general's **command**."},{"sentence":"Kukunin ko lang ang **orden** ninyo para sa pagkain.","translation":"I'll just take your food **order**."}]

translation: to draw a line on; to underline
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng isa o higit pang guhit sa isang bagay, lugar, o teksto.
original_explanation: When your teacher tells you to 'underline the verb,' she's telling you to **guhitan** the verb. It's the action of putting a line on something, whether it's to highlight a 'hugot' line in a book, to mark a wall before painting, or to draw on your sleeping friend's face (don't do this).
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' indicates applying the action (drawing a line) onto something. Often used interchangeably with 'salungguhitan' for 'to underline'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Guhitan** mo ng pula ang mahahalagang bahagi ng ulat.","translation":"**Underline** the important parts of the report with red."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **guhitan** ang mga pader ng bahay.","translation":"Do not **draw lines on** the walls of the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng 'impulse control disorder' na nailalarawan sa pamamagitan ng paulit-ulit na hindi mapigilang pagnanais na magnakaw ng mga bagay na karaniwang hindi naman gaanong mahalaga.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung sakit, hindi 'yung tao. 'Kleptomania' is the irresistible urge to shoplift... for free. Hindi ito 'yung planadong pagnanakaw para sa malaking halaga; ito 'yung biglaang impulse na kunin 'yung asukal sa coffee shop, tapos pagsisihan mo pag-uwi. It's a psychological condition, a glitch in the brain's 'don't steal' button.
usage_notes: Ang pangkalahatang termino para sa karamdaman.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kleptomania** ay isang seryosong kondisyong pang-kaisipan na nangangailangan ng propesyonal na tulong.","translation":"**Kleptomania** is a serious mental condition that requires professional help."}]

translation: to allude to someone; to make an indirect remark to
meaning_filipino: Pagsabihan ang isang tao sa paraang hindi direkta, sa pamamagitan ng pahiwatig o patama.
etymology: Nagmula sa "pa-dinig-an", kung saan ang /d/ ay nagiging /r/ kapag nasa pagitan ng dalawang patinig.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "parinig." 'Pag may gusto kang sabihin sa isang tao pero 'di mo masabi nang diretso, so you post a vague but obviously targeted status on Facebook. "Huy, **paringgan** mo nga 'yung kaibigan mo na magbayad na ng utang." This is the national sport of the Philippines, perfected in family reunions and office pantry chats.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang palipat. Ang tuwirang layon nito ay ang taong pinatatamaan ng pahiwatig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo na siyang **paringgan**, kausapin mo na lang nang diretsahan.","translation":"Don't **make indirect remarks to** him anymore, just talk to him directly."},{"sentence":"Palagi niya akong **pinaparinggan** tungkol sa aking timbang.","translation":"She always **alludes to me** about my weight."}]

meaning_filipino: Idikit o paglapatin ang dalawa o higit pang bagay gamit ang pandikit o anumang malagkit na substansiya.
original_explanation: Ito yung utos sa'yo nung grade school para sa art project niyo. O kaya 'yung pakiusap ng kaibigan mo na "paglapitin" niyo na ulit sila ng ex niya. In short, the act of making two separate things become one, either with glue or with "bridge-building" skills.
usage_notes: This is a command form. The noun form for the action is 'pagdidikit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pagdikitin** mo ang mga sirang pahina ng libro gamit ang tape.","translation":"**Stick** the torn pages of the book **together** using tape."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **pagdikitin** ang dalawang piraso ng basag na plorera.","translation":"He tried **to paste together** the two pieces of the broken vase."}]

translation: to be able to prove; to verify
meaning_filipino: Magawang maipakita ang katotohanan o katumpakan ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng ebidensya.
original_explanation: This is your "I told you so!" moment, but with receipts. It's what you do in a debate, a court case, or when you show your friend the screenshots to prove your ex was lying. It's the ultimate goal of every 'Marites' looking for confirmation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng matibay na ebidensya upang **mapatunayan** ang iyong paratang.","translation":"You need strong evidence to **prove** your accusation."},{"sentence":"Sa huli, nawa'y **mapatunayan** kong tapat ang aking pag-ibig sa iyo.","translation":"In the end, I hope I can **prove** that my love for you is true."}]

translation: to respond to; to answer; to meet (a need)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng sagot, reaksyon, o solusyon sa isang tanong, pakiusap, o pangangailangan.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your boss emails you 'for immediate action.' It's also what you wish your crush would do to your DMs. From answering a formal letter to finally addressing that 'we need to talk' text, 'tugunan' is all about providing the required response or action. Please tugunan the needs of your jowa.
usage_notes: Verb, object focus. Corresponds to `tumugon` (actor focus). Used for responding to requests, needs, or situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **tugunan** ang mga pangangailangan ng mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"We need to **meet** the needs of the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya **tinugunan** ang tanong ko.","translation":"He/She did not **respond to** my question."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang legal na proseso kung saan ang isang bahagi ng sahod o ari-arian ng isang tao ay kinukuha upang bayaran ang isang utang.
original_explanation: This isn't the pretty parsley on your steak. This is when the court tells your HR, "Hoy, 'wag niyo muna ibigay buong sahod niyan, may utang sa'min 'yan!" It's the legal version of your mom taking your allowance to pay for the vase you broke.
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal and financial contexts. The term in English can also refer to food decoration, but in Filipino legal parlance, it specifically refers to wage garnishment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng korte na i-**garnish** ang kanyang sahod para sa child support.","translation":"The court ordered to **garnish** his wages for child support."}]

translation: to acclaim, to proclaim, to exhibit
meaning_filipino: Ang paghirang, pagkilala, o paggawad ng karangalan sa isang tao bilang nagwagi o natatangi. Maaari ring tumukoy sa paglalantad o pagpapakita ng isang bagay sa publiko.
original_explanation: The "And the winner is..." moment. It's when someone is officially declared the champion, whether it's in a beauty pageant, a singing contest, or who can eat the most sisig. It's the ultimate validation, the moment you get the crown (or the cash prize).
usage_notes: Not to be confused with 'tanghaliin' (to be overtaken by noon). This is related to 'tanghalan' (stage).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang **tatanghalin** na kampeon sa paligsahan?","translation":"Who do you think will be **acclaimed** as the champion in the competition?"},{"sentence":"Siya ay **itinanghal** na 'Pinakamahusay na Aktor' ng taon.","translation":"He was **proclaimed** as the 'Best Actor' of the year."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamahalaga o sentral na lungsod sa isang bansa o rehiyon, na kadalasang sentro ng pamahalaan, komersyo, at kultura.
original_explanation: This is the 'main character' city of a country or province. It's where all the action is—the government offices, the biggest malls, the worst traffic. Think Metro Manila for the Philippines. It's the city that gets all the budget and all the complaints.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Maynila ang **pangunahing lunsod** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Manila is the **capital city** of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Maraming oportunidad sa mga **pangunahing lunsod** tulad ng Cebu at Davao.","translation":"There are many opportunities in **primary cities** like Cebu and Davao."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na nagpapakita ng ugali, damdamin, o paniniwala na hindi naman niya tunay na taglay; isang taong mapagpanggap.
original_explanation: The classic 'plastik'. They act like your best friend to your face but are probably running a hate blog about you behind your back. They're the ones who post '#blessed' on Instagram but complain about everything in their group chat. Their personality has more layers than a sans rival, and none of them are genuine.
usage_notes: A strong and negative descriptor for someone's character.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap pagkatiwalaan ang taong **mapagkunwa**.","translation":"It's hard to trust a **hypocritical** person."},{"sentence":"Nagpakita siya ng **mapagkunwa** na pag-aalala, ngunit alam ng lahat na mayroon siyang masamang intensyon.","translation":"He showed **pretentious** concern, but everyone knew he had bad intentions."}]

meaning_filipino: Pag-usapan o suriin nang malaliman ang isang paksa, isyu, o suliranin.
original_explanation: This is what your professor does during a lecture or what a guest speaker does at a seminar. It's not just simple chismis; it's a deep dive. Think of it as a formal 'Let's talk about it,' but with a PowerPoint presentation and a Q&A session afterwards.
usage_notes: A formal word used in academic, professional, and journalistic settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumalakay** ang pangulo tungkol sa mga bagong plano ng gobyerno para sa ekonomiya.","translation":"The president **discussed** the government's new plans for the economy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang likurang bahagi ng katawan ng malalaking hayop tulad ng kalabaw o baka; maaari ring tumukoy sa gulod ng bundok.
original_explanation: This is the heavy-duty back, not your back that hurts from sitting all day. Think of the wide, sturdy back of a carabao you can ride on, or the spine of a mountain range you see from a distance. It’s the part that carries the weight.
usage_notes: Isang terminong pampanitikan o pang-agrikultura. Hindi ito ginagamit para sa likod ng tao ('likod').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumakay ang bata sa **balugbog** ng kalabaw.","translation":"The child rode on the **back** of the carabao."},{"sentence":"Matatanaw mula sa aming bintana ang **balugbog** ng Bundok Makiling.","translation":"The **ridge** of Mount Makiling can be seen from our window."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyon o lupon na itinatag para sa pagsusuri, pag-aaral, o pananaliksik sa isang partikular na larangan.
original_explanation: The official-sounding place where things get over-analyzed. Think of a government body with a very long name, like the 'Surian ng Wikang Pambansa' (Institute of National Language). It’s where the experts gather to make very important decisions, probably over some free coffee and skyflakes.
usage_notes: Primarily used in formal contexts, especially for names of official bodies or institutions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Surian** ng Wikang Pambansa ang nangangalaga sa ating wika.","translation":"The **Institute** of National Language is the one that takes care of our language."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan maraming kalabaw; kawan ng mga kalabaw.
original_explanation: Not to be confused with 'kalabuan' (vagueness). This is literally a 'probinsya' starter pack. The sight and smell of the countryside, featuring our national animal in groups.
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' or '-han' here denotes a place abundant in the root word (kalabaw).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap mamasyal sa **kalabuhan** tuwing umaga.","translation":"It's nice to stroll through the **place with many carabaos** in the morning."},{"sentence":"Makikita ang malawak na **kalabuhan** mula sa bintana ng bus.","translation":"The vast **carabao pasture** can be seen from the bus window."}]

meaning_filipino: Lumampas sa takdang panahon o petsa ng pagiging mabisa o magagamit.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your driver's license, your passport, or that can of sardines at the back of your pantry. It’s when something becomes invalid because you forgot to renew it. "Hala, napaso na pala yung load ko, kaya pala di ako makatext!"
usage_notes: The pronunciation is key. /ma-PA-so/ for 'get burned', /ma-pa-SO/ for 'to expire'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tiningnan niya kung **napaso** na ang kanyang lisensya.","translation":"He checked if his license had **expired**."},{"sentence":"Sayang ang pagkain kung hahayaan lang itong **mapaso**.","translation":"The food will be wasted if you just let it **expire**."}]

translation: nightmare, sudden unexplained death in sleep (SUNDS)
meaning_filipino: Isang masamang panaginip na nagdudulot ng matinding takot o pagkabalisa. Sa kulturang Pilipino, tumutukoy rin ito sa isang kondisyon ng biglaang pagkamatay habang natutulog.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang mula sa 'bangon' (to rise) at 'ungol' (to moan/groan).
original_explanation: The Filipino boogeyman that attacks you in your sleep. It's when you have a nightmare so bad you feel like you're being crushed or can't breathe. Also, the folk term for that scary phenomenon where someone dies in their sleep. It's the reason your lola tells you not to sleep with a full stomach.
usage_notes: Mayroon itong dalawang kahulugan: isang karaniwang masamang panaginip, at isang partikular na kondisyong medikal na kilala sa kultura.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagising siyang humihiyaw dahil sa isang masamang **bangungot**.","translation":"He woke up screaming from a bad **nightmare**."},{"sentence":"Maraming pamahiin ang mga matatanda tungkol sa **bangungot**.","translation":"The elderly have many superstitions about **sudden death in sleep**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinalamutiang tungkod na hawak ng isang monarko o pinuno bilang simbolo ng kapangyarihan at soberanya.
original_explanation: The blinged-out stick that kings, queens, and Santacruzan Reyna Elenas carry to show they're the boss. It's the ultimate "I'm in charge" accessory. Think of it as the original power bank.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hawak ng reyna ang gintong **setro** at korona.","translation":"The queen holds the golden **scepter** and crown."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-abot sa **setro** ay simbolo ng pagtanggap ng tungkulin.","translation":"Reaching for the **scepter** is a symbol of accepting responsibility."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong matapang o agresibo sa pagpapahayag ng opinyon, pakikipag-away, o pambabatikos sa internet, ngunit maaaring hindi ganoon katapang o prangka sa tunay na buhay.
etymology: From English 'keyboard' + 'warrior'. A direct calque used in Taglish contexts.
original_explanation: This is that person who suddenly grows a backbone and the courage of a lion the moment they're behind a screen. They're brave enough to fight with strangers over politics, showbiz gossip, or basketball, but would probably just stare at their shoes if you confronted them in person. They are the soldiers of keyboard fights, armed with a fast internet connection and a lack of filter.
usage_notes: Often used with a negative or mocking connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang daming **keyboard warrior** sa Facebook na akala mo kung sinong mga eksperto.","translation":"There are so many **keyboard warriors** on Facebook who act like they're experts."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala sa kanya, isa lang siyang **keyboard warrior**.","translation":"Don't worry about him, he's just a **keyboard warrior**."}]

translation: to prevail; to dominate; to stand out
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging mas nakatataas, mas nangingibabaw, o mas matagumpay kaysa sa iba; ang pagiging pinakamahalaga o pinakapansin-pansin.
etymology: From mang- (verb prefix) + ibabaw (top, surface, above).
original_explanation: The feeling when your 'bida' energy is so strong, you outshine everyone else. It's when your opinion wins in a group meeting, or when your adobo is declared the best in the family reunion. It's your 'main character' moment, when your voice or presence takes over.
usage_notes: Often used to describe an idea, feeling, quality, or person becoming dominant or supreme in a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa huli, ang kabutihan pa rin ang dapat **mangibabaw** sa kasamaan.","translation":"In the end, goodness should still **prevail** over evil."},{"sentence":"Kahit maraming problema, pinilit niyang hayaan na **mangibabaw** ang kanyang pag-asa.","translation":"Despite many problems, she tried to let her hope **dominate**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mabagal kumilos, mag-isip, o umusad.
etymology: Pinagsamang `pagka-` (katangian ng) at `makupad` (mabagal), na galing sa salitang `kupad` (bagal).
original_explanation: Ito yung state of being mo kapag Lunes ng umaga at hindi pa nag-kick in yung kape. Yung internet connection na PLDC. Yung ka-grupo mo na isang linggo bago mag-reply sa group chat. Basically, anything that moves at the speed of a government office queue on a Friday afternoon.
usage_notes: Karaniwang isang negatibong katangian na nagpapahiwatig ng kawalan ng episyensya o katamaran.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakainis ang **pagkamakupad** ng serbisyo sa opisinang iyon.","translation":"The **slowness** of the service in that office is annoying."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pagkamakupad**, nahuli siya sa kanyang appointment.","translation":"Because of his **sluggishness**, he was late for his appointment."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi pa hinog, luto, o nasa hustong gulang; wala pa sa tamang kalagayan o pagkakagawa.
original_explanation: That green mango you dip in bagoong? That's hilaw. The steak you ordered 'medium-rare' but came out 'still mooing'? That's hilaw. It can also describe a person who's inexperienced or immature. 'Medyo hilaw pa siya sa trabaho' means they're still a rookie.
usage_notes: Can be used for food, people (experience), or projects (unfinished). Antonyms are 'hinog' (ripe) or 'luto' (cooked).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap isawsaw sa bagoong ang manggang **hilaw**.","translation":"**Unripe** mango is delicious to dip in shrimp paste."},{"sentence":"**Hilaw** pa ang kanin, huwag mo munang hanguin.","translation":"The rice is still **uncooked**, don't take it off the heat yet."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng panlilinlang o panloloko upang makalamang sa iba, lalo na sa isang laro, pagsusulit, o relasyon.
original_explanation: Ang national sport sa exam, sa Tong-its, at minsan, sa pag-ibig. Ito 'yung paggamit ng kodigo, pagtingin sa cards ng kalaban, o pag-reply ng 'good night' sa isa habang ka-video call 'yung isa pa. Cheating is a choice, 'wag kang mandaya.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin sa iba't ibang konteksto, mula sa laro at pagsusulit hanggang sa relasyon at negosyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mandaya** sa pagsusulit.","translation":"Don't **cheat** on the exam."},{"sentence":"Nahuli siyang sinusubukang **mandaya** sa laro.","translation":"He was caught trying to **cheat** in the game."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang silid kung saan isinasagawa ang mga gawaing pang-opisina o pagtanggap ng mga kliyente at bisita.
etymology: Compound word from "silid" (room) and "tanggapan" (office/reception, from root 'tanggap').
original_explanation: The formal term for an office, which sounds way more grand than the cubicle farm you're actually in. It’s where you receive guests, clients, or a sermon from your boss. In a home context, it’s the room with the big desk that everyone else uses as a dumping ground.
usage_notes: 'Opisina' is more common in everyday speech. 'Silid-tanggapan' can also specifically mean a reception room.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **silid-tanggapan** ang manager para sa isang pulong.","translation":"The manager is in the **office** for a meeting."},{"sentence":"Iwan ninyo ang dokumento sa **silid-tanggapan**.","translation":"Leave the documents at the **reception room**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mas malalim o mas makatang paraan ng pagyakap, kadalasang nagpapahiwatig ng mahigpit at buong-pusong paggiliw o pagtanggap.
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na 'yapos' (yakap) at panlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: This is the 'Level 99' hug. It's not just a 'yakap', it's an *embrace*. The kind you see in dramatic movie reunions at the airport, complete with slow motion and a swelling orchestral score. It's a very poetic, very intense, 'I-never-want-to-let-you-go' kind of hug.
usage_notes: Mas pampanitikan o makata kaysa 'yumakap'. Nagpapahiwatig ito ng mas buo at madalas na madamdaming pagyakap. Ito ay nasa anyong naganap (completed aspect).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang magkita silang muli, mahigpit siyang **yumapos** sa kanyang ina.","translation":"When they saw each other again, she tightly **embraced** her mother."},{"sentence":"**Yumapos** siya sa pag-asang babalik pa ito.","translation":"She **clung** to the hope that he would still return."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng uod na karaniwang matatagpuan sa lupa (earthworm) o bilang parasito sa loob ng bituka ng tao o hayop (intestinal worm).
original_explanation: The squiggly thing in the soil that helps your plantita mom's garden, or the squiggly thing your doctor says you have if you don't wash your hands. Either way, it's a wiggly, slimy tube that's both helpful (in soil) and horrifying (in you). "Para kang binilbil na bulati" is the ultimate insult for someone who can't sit still.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa kapaki-pakinabang na earthworm at sa parasitikong bulate. Mahalaga ang konteksto. Ang "bulate sa tiyan" ay partikular na tumutukoy sa mga intestinal worm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **bulati** sa lupa kaya't mataba ang mga pananim.","translation":"There are many **earthworms** in the soil, that's why the plants are healthy."},{"sentence":"Pinainom ng gamot ang bata para puksain ang mga **bulati** sa tiyan.","translation":"The child was given medicine to eliminate the **intestinal worms**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip na pananong na ginagamit upang tukuyin ang pagmamay-ari ng isang bagay. Ito ang paaring anyo ng 'sino'.
original_explanation: The Tagalog version of 'Whose is this?' It's the question you ask when you find a random phone charger in your house, or when your mom finds something that isn't yours in your room. It's the possessive form of 'sino' (who).
usage_notes: This is a possessive pronoun asking about ownership. The form 'kanino' is more commonly used in modern standard Filipino, but 'nino' is also correct and understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nino** ba itong payong na naiwan sa opisina?","translation":"**Whose** umbrella is this that was left in the office?"},{"sentence":"Hindi ko alam kung **nino** ang sulat na ito.","translation":"I don't know **whose** letter this is."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan na lubhang kaawa-awa, kahabag-habag, at nakapagdudulot ng matinding habag o awa.
original_explanation: This is when something is so bad, it's beyond sad and enters the "nakakaawa" territory. Ito yung itsura ng wallet mo a day before payday. O yung eksena sa telenovela kung saan inaapi na naman yung bida. It's a situation that makes you want to reach out and say, "Huy, okay ka lang?"
usage_notes: Stronger and more dramatic than 'nakakaawa'. It implies a tragic and miserable state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kalunus-lunos** ang kalagayan ng mga pamilyang nawalan ng tirahan.","translation":"The condition of the families who lost their homes is **pitiful**."},{"sentence":"Naging **kalunus-lunos** ang kanyang pagtatapos matapos siyang malulong sa bisyo.","translation":"His end became **deplorable** after he fell into vice."}]

translation: state of being fed up; exasperation
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkaramdam ng matinding inis, pagkabagot, o pagkasawa na dulot ng paulit-ulit na problema o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling when the internet disconnects for the 5th time during your online game or presentation. 'Yung level ng inis mo na gusto mo nang ihagis 'yung modem? That's pagkakasumping. It's the final stage of grief before you explode, the "ayoko na, suko na ako" of your patience.
usage_notes: A deep, intense feeling of being fed up or exasperated. Less common in daily speech but very descriptive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata sa kanyang mukha ang **pagkakasumping** sa walang katapusang traffic.","translation":"His **exasperation** with the endless traffic was obvious on his face."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakasumping** niya ay humantong sa biglaang pag-resign sa trabaho.","translation":"His **state of being fed up** led to his sudden resignation from work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapabago sa anyo ng buhok mula sa pagiging tuwid upang maging kulot, gamit ang init, kemikal, o mga roller.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo sa buhok mo a day before a big event, hoping na mag-last 'yung curls. Pwedeng sa salon (para professional), pwedeng sa bahay gamit ang curling iron (para masunog ang daliri mo), o 'yung old-school na paraan gamit ang medyas. The ultimate 'sana gumana' beauty ritual.
usage_notes: Refers to the act of making straight or wavy hair curly. The person who does this is a 'mangungulot'. 'Magpakulot' (to have one's hair curled) is more commonly used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong ka bang **magkulot** ng buhok gamit ang plantsa?","translation":"Do you know how to **curl hair** using a flat iron?"},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magpakulot** ng buhok para sa kanyang debut.","translation":"She decided to **have her hair curled** for her debut."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pamayanan ng mga tao na may sariling teritoryo at pamahalaan; tumutukoy din sa isang bansa o sa mga mamamayan nito, o sa sentro ng isang munisipalidad.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *banua ("inhabited land, territory, village, house").
original_explanation: This word is a Swiss Army knife. It can be your hometown ("Sa aming **bayan**..."), the town proper or downtown area ("Punta tayo sa **bayan**."), or the entire country ("Para sa **bayan**!"). It's the feeling of community, the place you call home, and the nation you fight for. It's the 'B' in 'OTP' (One True Pinas).
usage_notes: The meaning is highly dependent on context. 'Bayan' can mean town center, municipality, or nation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal ko ang aking **bayan**, ang Pilipinas.","translation":"I love my **country**, the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Mamimili kami ng gulay sa **bayan** mamayang hapon.","translation":"We will buy vegetables in **town** this afternoon."}]

translation: bad weather, down time due to rain
meaning_filipino: Panahon ng masamang klima, lalo na ang tuluy-tuloy na pag-ulan, na nagiging sanhi ng paghinto sa trabaho o anumang gawain sa labas.
etymology: Mula sa mga salitang Espanyol na "agua" (tubig) at "tiempo" (panahon). Isang likhang-salita sa Espanyol ng Pilipinas.
original_explanation: When the weather gives you an unexpected, unscheduled day off. Para sa mga construction worker, mangingisda, at magsasaka, agwatyempo means 'walang kita'. For the rest of us office workers, it's an excuse to work from home, drink coffee, and watch the rain.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa masamang panahon na may kasamang ulan o bagyo, at hindi sa anumang uri lamang ng panahon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang kita ang mga mangingisda dahil **agwatyempo** na naman.","translation":"The fishermen have no income because it's **bad weather** again."},{"sentence":"Natigil ang pagtatayo ng bahay dahil sa **agwatyempo**.","translation":"The house construction was halted due to the **down time from rain**."}]

translation: to bother, to disturb, to inconvenience
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-istorbo o paggambala sa isang tao mula sa kanyang ginagawa o sa kanyang kapayapaan.
etymology: From the root 'abala' (bother, disturbance, being busy). The prefix 'mang-' indicates the actor performing the action.
original_explanation: What you're doing when you call your friend at 2 AM for no reason. It's interrupting someone's 'me time,' their work focus, or their nap. Filipinos are often overly polite about it: 'Sorry mang-abala, ha?' is the standard opening line before asking for a huge favor. It's the art of politely interrupting.
usage_notes: A very common verb, often used with 'pasensya na' or 'sorry'. The noun form is 'pang-aabala' (the act of bothering).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong **mang-abala** sa'yo pero kailangan ko talaga ng tulong.","translation":"I don't want to **bother** you, but I really need help."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, huwag kayong **mang-abala** sa mga nag-eeksamen.","translation":"Please, do not **disturb** those who are taking an exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o resulta ng paggupit ng buhok.
etymology: Contraction of `pa-` (causative/request marker) + `gupit` (cut). `Pagupit` literally means "to have one's hair cut". As a noun, it refers to the haircut itself.
original_explanation: That thing you get right before a big event, hoping it will solve all your problems. It can either be a source of immense confidence ('new hair, who dis?') or a reason to wear a beanie for two months straight. It’s what your mom forces you to get when your bangs start covering your eyes.
usage_notes: This is a noun derived from the verb phrase `magpagupit`. It's used colloquially to mean 'haircut'. The more formal term is 'gupit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bagay sa iyo ang bago mong **pagupit**.","translation":"Your new **haircut** suits you."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko na ng **pagupit**, masyado nang mahaba ang buhok ko.","translation":"I need a **haircut** already, my hair is too long."}]

translation: Going home, on the way home
meaning_filipino: Patungo o pabalik sa tirahan o pinanggalingan.
original_explanation: The best two words a BPO agent, student, or any employee can text their loved one after a long shift: 'Pauwi na.' It's the signal that freedom is near, and so is traffic, but hey, at least you're going home. It's the light at the end of the EDSA tunnel.
usage_notes: Often used with 'na' as in 'pauwi na' to mean 'on the way home now'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa daan, **pauwi** ka na ba?","translation":"Be careful on the road, are you **on your way home**?"},{"sentence":"Laging traffic sa C5 kapag **pauwi** na ang mga tao.","translation":"It's always traffic on C5 when people are **going home**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan sagana o maraming tumutubong puno ng sampalok.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'sampalok' (tamarind) at hulaping '-an' na nangangahulugang lugar.
original_explanation: It's not just one sampalok tree, it's a whole squad. A place name so common you probably have a 'Kanto Sampalukan' in your province. It's the place where you'd go to get free pampa-asim for your sinigang.
usage_notes: Ang hulaping '-an' ay karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng isang lugar kung saan matatagpuan nang marami ang salitang-ugat. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang uri ng lutuin na sinahugan ng maraming sampalok.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglaro kami sa may **sampalukan** noong kami'y mga bata pa.","translation":"We used to play at the **tamarind grove** when we were kids."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin ang balat ng isang prutas, gulay, o anumang bagay na may panlabas na balot o takip.
original_explanation: The mandatory first step before you can enjoy a mango, orange, or dalandan. It's the pre-game to eating your favorite fruit. Also a metaphor for getting to know someone's true self by peeling away their layers... or their makeup after a long day. #Hugot
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'magbalat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong ka bang **magtalop** ng pinya gamit ang kutsilyo?","translation":"Do you know how **to peel** a pineapple using a knife?"},{"sentence":"Pinakiusapan niya ang bata na **magtalop** ng patatas para sa kanilang hapunan.","translation":"She asked the child **to peel** potatoes for their dinner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tiyak na haba o hangganan ng oras na itinakda para sa isang gawain, proyekto, o layunin.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate enemy of procrastinators. The 'deadline' in BPO lingo. The reason for your all-nighters in college. The final boss of every project. It's that moment you realize, 'Bakit ko 'to ginawa sa sarili ko?'
usage_notes: Often used in formal, academic, or professional contexts. 'Palugit' or 'taning' are common synonyms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **takdang-panahon** para sa pagpasa ng proyekto ay sa Biyernes.","translation":"The **deadline** for submitting the project is on Friday."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating tapusin ito sa loob ng itinakdang **takdang-panahon**.","translation":"We need to finish this within the given **timeframe**."}]

translation: to apply on; to wipe on; to smear on
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapahid ng isang bagay (karaniwan ay likido o malapot) sa ibabaw ng isa pa.
original_explanation: This is the action of spreading something onto a surface. Think of putting palaman on your pandesal - that's "pahiran mo ng butter." Or applying lotion, or even wiping dirt *onto* something. It's the more formal cousin of "lagyan."
usage_notes: The focus of this verb is the surface or object being wiped/smeared on. Contrast with 'ipahid', where the focus is the thing being smeared.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pahiran** mo ng Vicks ang likod niya para guminhawa ang paghinga.","translation":"**Apply** Vicks on his back so his breathing will be relieved."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pahiran** ng dumi ang pader.","translation":"Don't **wipe** dirt on the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay-tuya o paglibak sa isang tao o bagay sa pamamagitan ng pag-tawa.
original_explanation: This is what happens in comment sections when someone posts a cringey take. It's the digital version of being the butt of the joke at the family reunion. 'Sige, **pagtawanan** niyo lang ang failed unboxing video ko, at least viral.'
usage_notes: Often implies ridicule or mockery, not just innocent laughter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagtawanan** ang kaniyang pagkakamali.","translation":"Do not **laugh at** his mistake."},{"sentence":"Pinagtawanan nila ang bagong gupit ko.","translation":"They laughed at my new haircut."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabaligtarang posisyon, ayos, o direksyon ng isang bagay; salungat o pabaliktad.
original_explanation: It's when you wear your t-shirt inside out AND backwards. It's the state of things being completely reversed or on the opposite side. Parang 'yung sinabi mo versus 'yung ginawa mo—magka-baliwasan.
usage_notes: A very uncommon word in daily conversation, more likely to be encountered in literature or deep Tagalog texts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **baliwasan** ang pagkakabit ng mga palamuti kaya inayos niya ito.","translation":"The decorations were placed in a **reverse position**, so he fixed it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sukat ng isang tao, hayop, o bagay mula sa ibaba hanggang sa itaas; ang katayugan.
original_explanation: The one thing Pinoys love to comment on. "Uy, tumangkad ka!" (Hey, you got taller!) is the national greeting for anyone you haven't seen in a while, even if you're already 30. It's the reason why Cherifer is a household name and why basketball is our national sport despite... well, you know.
usage_notes: Often used with the prefix 'ka-' as in 'katangkad' to describe height. 'Matangkad' is the adjective form (tall).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Likas sa kanilang lahi ang pambihirang **tangkad**.","translation":"Exceptional **height** is natural in their lineage."},{"sentence":"Sinusukat ng nars ang **tangkad** at timbang ng mga estudyante.","translation":"The nurse is measuring the **height** and weight of the students."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kasuotan sa paa na karaniwang gawa sa tela, isinusuot bago ang sapatos upang magbigay ng ginhawa at proteksyon.
original_explanation: The real MVP that saves your feet from stinky shoes. Also, the one thing that the laundry machine loves to eat, leaving you with a bunch of single, lonely pairs. "Wala na namang kapares medyas ko!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan magsuot ng **medyas** para hindi ka magka-amoy paa.","translation":"Don't forget to wear **socks** so your feet won't smell."},{"sentence":"Nawawala na naman ang isang pares ng **medyas** ko pagkatapos labhan.","translation":"One of my pair of **socks** is missing again after doing the laundry."}]

translation: to cause something to wobble or be unsteady
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng patuloy at hindi matatag na pag-alog o paggalaw.
original_explanation: This is the state of that old office chair that feels like it's about to give up on life. It's also the feeling of your brain after an all-nighter finishing a report. It's a more unstable, continuous, and slightly pathetic version of `magpaalog`. Think of a jello salad on a shaky table.
usage_notes: Implies a continuous, less forceful, and often unsteady shaking compared to 'magpaalog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong sandalan ang mesa, baka **magpaalug-alog** at matapon ang kape.","translation":"Don't lean on the table, it might **start to wobble** and the coffee will spill."},{"sentence":"Ang pagdaan ng malaking trak ay nagpangyari sa lumang tulay na **magpaalug-alog**.","translation":"The passing of the large truck caused the old bridge to **wobble**."}]

translation: manner of performance; the way it happened/unfolded
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan kung paano isinagawa o nangyari ang isang kilos, palabas, o pangyayari.
etymology: From `pag-` + `kaka-` + `ganap` (to happen, to perform). The `pagkaka-` affix describes the manner of the action.
original_explanation: This is the post-event analysis. How did the performance go? How did the heist unfold? It’s the 'how it went down' of any event, from a wedding proposal to a disastrous presentation at work. It's the difference between a 'flawless victory' and a 'hot mess.'
usage_notes: Refers to the quality or nature of a performance, event, or occurrence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinuri ng mga kritiko ang mahusay na **pagkakaganap** ng pangunahing aktres.","translation":"The critics praised the lead actress's excellent **performance**."},{"sentence":"Inaalam pa ng pulisya ang buong detalye ng **pagkakaganap** ng krimen.","translation":"The police are still investigating the full details of **how the crime happened**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng daigdig, kasama ang lahat ng nilalang at bagay dito; ang sangkatauhan.
etymology: From `isa` (one) + `-ng` + `libot` (to go around) + `-an` (suffix indicating place). Literally "that which is encompassed in one circuit/journey."
original_explanation: This is a very grand, almost poetic word for "the world." It's not just the planet; it's everything and everyone in it. Think of it as the universe from a human-centric point of view. You'll hear this in church, in epic fantasy movies (Tagalog-dubbed, of course), or when your lola is giving you life advice that spans generations. "Buong mundo" is the casual version, `sanlibutan` is the formal gown.
usage_notes: Often used in religious or literary contexts. Interchangeable with `daigdig` and `mundo` but carries a more profound, all-encompassing tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ang siyang nagpapaikot sa buong **sanlibutan**.","translation":"Love is what makes the whole **world** go 'round."},{"sentence":"Nilikha ng Diyos ang **sanlibutan** sa loob ng anim na araw.","translation":"God created the **world** in six days."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapataas ng pagnanais na kumain; pampagana.
original_explanation: That #FoodPorn shot on Instagram that makes you immediately search for the nearest restaurant. The smell of sinigang or adobo wafting from the kitchen. Anything that makes your stomach grumble and say 'Gimme that!'
usage_notes: Primarily used for food, but can be used figuratively for something that sparks interest or desire.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **nakagagana** ang amoy ng bagong lutong tinapay.","translation":"The smell of freshly baked bread is truly **appetizing**."},{"sentence":"Ang presentasyon ng pagkain ay **nakagagana** kaya marami ang umorder nito.","translation":"The food's presentation is **appetizing**, which is why many people ordered it."}]

meaning_filipino: Wala sa ayos; sira o hindi gumagana nang tama; hindi regular o naaayon sa inaasahan.
original_explanation: Describes your body clock after a long weekend, your friend's chaotic love life, or the videoke machine that only plays 'My Way' in a distorted voice. It's the general state of 'sira' or 'gulo'.
usage_notes: Commonly used to describe machines, schedules, or even personal situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Desareglado** na naman ang bentilador, kailangan nang ipaayos.","translation":"The electric fan is **out of order** again, it needs to be repaired."},{"sentence":"Naging **desareglado** ang tulog ko dahil sa pagtatrabaho sa gabi.","translation":"My sleep became **irregular** because of working at night."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na tiniyak, binitawan bilang isang salita ng karangalan, o isinumpa na tutuparin o ibibigay.
original_explanation: The past tense of 'drawing'. It's the 'forever' **ipinangako** ng ex mo, the salary increase your boss mentioned a year ago, or that reunion with your friends that never happens. Full of hope at first, but now just a memory. #SanaAllTuparin
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang singsing na ito ay **ipinangako** sa akin ng aking lola.","translation":"This ring **was promised** to me by my grandmother."},{"sentence":"Tinupad niya ang lahat ng **ipinangako** niya noong kampanya.","translation":"He fulfilled everything he **had promised** during the campaign."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na pananong na ginagamit upang alamin ang direksyon o patutunguhan. Ito ay pinaikling anyo ng "papunta sa saan."
original_explanation: The ultimate question your mom asks when you're all dressed up on a Saturday night. It's the short, slightly accusatory version of "Saan ka pupunta?" (Where are you going?). It's what you ask your Grab driver when he seems to be going in the wrong direction: "Kuya, pasaan po tayo?"
usage_notes: Used to ask for a destination or direction. Often used with a sense of urgency or confusion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasaan** ba ang biyahe ng bus na ito?","translation":"**Where to** is this bus headed?"},{"sentence":"Gabi na, **pasaan** ka pa?","translation":"It's late, **where are you off to**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na may mataas na kalidad, kinikilala bilang huwaran, at nananatili ang kahalagahan sa paglipas ng panahon.
original_explanation: 'Pag sinabing 'klasiko', ito 'yung mga bagay na hindi nalalaos. Parang 'yung mga kanta ni Sharon Cuneta, 'yung pelikula ni Dolphy, o 'yung adobo ni lola—kahit anong bagong uso ang lumabas, babalik-balikan mo pa rin. It's the OG, the standard, the 'they don't make 'em like they used to' kind of thing.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri (e.g., "klasikong awit") at pangngalan (e.g., "isa itong klasiko").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Noli Me Tángere ay isang **klasiko** sa panitikang Pilipino.","translation":"Noli Me Tángere is a **classic** in Philippine literature."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na paraan ng panunuyo o panliligaw kung saan ang dalawang tao ay nagpapalitan ng pagpapakita ng pag-ibig at pagtingin.
etymology: Salitang ugat na 'suyo' na may panlaping '-an'.
original_explanation: The OG 'getting to know' stage. Hindi pa uso ang swipe right, so may harana, may pag-iigib ng tubig, at may approval muna ni Tatay. It's mutual effort, unlike modern dating where one person is seen-zoned for three days.
