usage_notes: Tumutukoy ito sa kilos na may pagtutugunan o 'mutual' na panunuyo, hindi lamang isang panig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging tanyag sa kanilang baryo ang **suyuan** nina Marco at Clara.","translation":"The **courtship** of Marco and Clara became famous in their village."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang matamis na **suyuan** ay nauwi sa kasalan.","translation":"Their sweet **courtship** led to a wedding."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sumasamba sa mga diyos-diyosan o idolo.
original_explanation: Historically, this is someone who worships statues instead of the 'real' God. In modern terms, medyo OA na fanboy/fangirl na halos sambahin na ang kanilang 'idol'. 'Grabe ka, parang idolatra ka na kung makasigaw diyan!'
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa kontekstong panrelihiyon o pangkasaysayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuring ng mga misyonero na mga **idolatra** ang mga katutubong sumasamba sa kalikasan.","translation":"The missionaries considered the natives who worshipped nature as **idolaters**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging **idolatra** ay isang malaking kasalanan sa maraming relihiyon.","translation":"Being an **idolater** is a great sin in many religions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng kawalan ng interes, pakialam, o emosyon sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung seenzone ka niya. 'Yung 'K' lang ang reply niya sa long sweet message mo. 'Yung reaksyon mo sa office chismis na wala kang pake. That's pagkaindiperente. It's the art of having zero f*cks to give, the 'meh' of emotions.
usage_notes: A loanword that has been fully integrated into Tagalog to describe a lack of concern or interest.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakabahala ang **pagkaindiperente** ng maraming tao sa isyu ng kalikasan.","translation":"The **indifference** of many people on the issue of the environment is alarming."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkaindiperente** ay senyales na wala na siyang nararamdaman para sa iyo.","translation":"His **apathy** is a sign that he no longer has feelings for you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggamit ng isang kasangkapan upang hatiin, hiwain, o tanggalin ang isang bahagi mula sa kabuuan.
original_explanation: Can refer to anything from your mom cutting your bangs unevenly as a kid, to Meralco's 'pagputol ng kuryente' when you forget to pay the bill. It's also what you do to toxic people in your life—the ultimate 'pagputol ng ugnayan'.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical cutting, or metaphorical disconnection of services or relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagputol** ng puno ay nangangailangan ng permit mula sa DENR.","translation":"The **cutting** of trees requires a permit from the DENR."},{"sentence":"Nagbabala ang kompanya ng tubig tungkol sa **pagputol** ng serbisyo sa mga hindi nagbabayad.","translation":"The water company warned about the **disconnection** of service for those who don't pay."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkat ng mga organo sa katawan na responsable sa pagtunaw ng pagkain, pagkuha ng sustansya, at pagtatapon ng mga dumi.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "sistema" (system) at Tagalog na "pagtunaw" (digestion).
original_explanation: Ito yung internal BPO ng katawan mo. May inbound (pagkain), processing (pagtunaw), at outbound (paglabas ng... you know). Kapag nag-error 'to, parang nag-crash ang system mo after kumain ng sobrang samgyupsal.
usage_notes: Isang terminong pang-agham at pang-edukasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malusog na **sistema ng pagtunaw** ay mahalaga para sa pangkalahatang kalusugan.","translation":"A healthy **digestive system** is important for overall health."}]

translation: to unsew; to rip a seam
meaning_filipino: Kilos ng sadyang pagkalas o pagtanggal sa tahi ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: When your tailor needs to adjust your pants, they first have to `bigtasin` the original seam. It's a deliberate act of undoing. Think of it as the opposite of sewing – it's de-sewing. It's what you do when you want to remove a patch from your old school uniform or when you're dismantling something stitched together to repurpose the fabric.
usage_notes: Ang hulaping '-in' ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang kilos na ginagawa sa isang bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **bigtasin** ang lumang butones bago magkabit ng bago.","translation":"You need **to unsew** the old button before attaching a new one."},{"sentence":"**Binigtas** ng mananahi ang laylayan ng damit para ayusin ito.","translation":"The tailor **unsewed** the hem of the dress to fix it."}]

translation: to make straight; to go straight; to be direct
meaning_filipino: Gawing tuwid ang isang bagay; tumuloy nang walang likuan; sabihin ang isang bagay nang walang paligoy-ligoy.
original_explanation: What you tell the Grab driver: 'Idiretso mo lang po, Manong.' Also what you wish your friend would do instead of dropping hints: just say it directly. 'Idiretso mo na kasi ang gusto mong sabihin!' Straight to the point, walang chismis.
usage_notes: Pwedeng gamitin para sa pisikal na direksyon, pag-aayos ng bagay, o sa paraan ng pakikipag-usap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagdating sa kanto, **idiretso** mo lang ang takbo.","translation":"When you reach the corner, just **go straight**."},{"sentence":"Mas mabuting **idiretso** mo na ang usapan para matapos na.","translation":"It's better if you **are direct** with the conversation so we can finish it."}]

translation: to lay out, to spread out, to present
meaning_filipino: Ilagay nang maayos at pantay ang isang bagay sa isang ibabaw, tulad ng banig, mantel, o plano.
original_explanation: It's what you do when you're setting the table for Noche Buena, spreading the banig for an afternoon nap, or presenting your brilliant (or so you think) business plan to your boss. "Sige na, maglatag ka na ng plano mo para sa team building."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical objects (like mats or tablecloths) or figuratively for plans and ideas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **maglatag** ka ng banig sa sahig para sa mga bisita.","translation":"Please **lay out** a mat on the floor for the guests."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **maglatag** ng malinaw na estratehiya para sa proyektong ito.","translation":"We need to **lay out** a clear strategy for this project."}]

meaning_filipino: Puno ng usok; naglalarawan sa isang lugar kung saan makapal ang usok.
original_explanation: The state of your lungs after riding behind a jeepney. The ambiance of a Pinoy barbecue party where the one in charge of the grill is fanning the coals too hard. If you can't see the person across the room because of the ihaw-ihaw fumes, it's maaso.
usage_notes: Not to be confused with 'aso' (dog). The context is always about smoke or fumes. The accent is on the second syllable: /ma-A-so/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **maaso** ang kusina dahil sa nasunog na sinaing.","translation":"The kitchen became **smoky** because of the burnt rice."},{"sentence":"Lumabas muna kami dahil masyadong **maaso** sa loob ng videoke bar.","translation":"We went outside for a while because it was too **smoky** inside the karaoke bar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtusok o pag-ulos ng isang matulis na bagay, tulad ng kutsilyo o patalim, sa isang tao o bagay. Ginagamit din ito sa pagpasok ng plaka ng kuryente sa saksakan.
original_explanation: This is the stuff you see in action movies or read about in crime news. It's the act of using a sharp object, like a knife, to poke someone. On a less dramatic note, it can also refer to plugging something in, like 'pagsaksak ng charger sa outlet'. The motion is the same: thrusting something into something else.
usage_notes: Can refer to both violent stabbing and the act of plugging an electronic device into a socket. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsaksak** ay isang malubhang krimen na may mabigat na parusa.","translation":"**Stabbing** is a serious crime with a heavy penalty."},{"sentence":"Siguraduhin mong tama ang **pagsaksak** mo ng plug sa saksakan.","translation":"Make sure your **plugging** of the plug into the outlet is correct."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maitim, malagkit, at malapot na materyal na mula sa petrolyo, ginagamit bilang panakip at pantambak sa paggawa ng mga kalsada.
original_explanation: That black, sticky stuff that smells weird when it's freshly laid on the road. It's the key ingredient to making a 'kalsadang aspaltado.' In the summer, it can get so hot it feels like it's melting under your tsinelas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangangamoy sariwang **aspalto** sa lugar kung saan may ginagawang kalsada.","translation":"It smells like fresh **asphalt** in the area where a road is being constructed."}]

meaning_filipino: Higit sa karaniwan, kailangan, o katanggap-tanggap; labis-labis.
original_explanation: When your friend tells a story and adds 10 extra details that never happened for dramatic effect. OPM song lyrics are full of this: "pag-ibig na palabis." It's being "extra." It's the difference between "I'm sad" and "The sorrow in my soul is a bottomless ocean of despair." That's palabis.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation of being too much or unnecessary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **palabis** na paggamit ng palamuti.","translation":"Avoid the **excessive** use of decoration."}]

translation: to be able to provide relief or comfort
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng ginhawa, kaginhawahan, o lunas sa hirap, sakit, o bigat ng damdamin.
original_explanation: Anything that makes you go "Ahhh, life is good." Pwedeng malamig na tubig sa mainit na araw, sweldo pagkatapos ng isang mahabang buwan, o isang mahigpit na yakap galing sa mahal mo. Yung pakiramdam na nabunutan ka ng tinik.
usage_notes: Associated with physical, emotional, or financial relief. "Nakaginhawa" is the past tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **makaginhawa** sa iyong pakiramdam ang pag-inom ng mainit na sabaw.","translation":"Hopefully, drinking hot soup will **provide relief** for how you're feeling."},{"sentence":"Malaking tulong ang bonus para **makaginhawa** sa aming mga gastusin.","translation":"The bonus is a big help to **provide relief** for our expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinaikling pangalan ni Jesukristo. Ginagamit din bilang isang karaniwang pangalan ng lalaki sa mga bansang nagsasalita ng Espanyol at sa Pilipinas.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "Jesús," isang karaniwang pangalan. Sa huli ay mula sa parehong ugat ng Jesukristo.
original_explanation: Often pronounced "He-sus" in the Philippines, it can refer to THE Jesus or just your friendly neighborhood Tito Jesus. It's a name so common you might have it on your Gcash transaction history. When someone yells "Jesus, Mary, and Joseph!", they're not calling a meeting, they're just really, really surprised about the latest chismis.
usage_notes: The pronunciation /HE-sus/ is standard for the given name, while the English pronunciation /JEE-zus/ is used for the religious figure in English contexts. The name is often shortened to "Jess."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Mang **Jesus** ang hardinero sa aming subdibisyon.","translation":"Mr. **Jesus** is the gardener in our subdivision."},{"sentence":"Pinangalanan siyang **Jesus** bilang pag-alaala sa kanyang lolo.","translation":"He was named **Jesus** in memory of his grandfather."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang batang aso.
original_explanation: The cutest, most chaotic little furball that will chew your slippers and melt your heart. Also used as a political insult for a blind follower or puppet, like 'tuta ni Marcos' or 'tuta ng Kano'.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for a young dog or figuratively (and pejoratively) for a sycophant or puppet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang alaga naming **tuta** ay napakalikot.","translation":"Our pet **puppy** is very playful."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **tuta** ng kahit sinong politiko.","translation":"Don't be a **puppet** for any politician."}]

translation: to use as a chopping board
meaning_filipino: Gamitin bilang isang sangkalan o patungan sa paghiwa.
original_explanation: When you're so desperate you start looking at your thick textbook or a flat piece of wood and think, "Pwede na 'to!" That's 'sangkalanin'. It's the verb for MacGyver-ing a chopping surface.
usage_notes: A verb derived from the noun 'sangkalan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sangkalanin** ang bagong mesa!","translation":"Don't **use** the new table **as a chopping board**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matigas at makintab na bagay na nabubuo sa loob ng talaba at iba pang molusko, na lubos na pinahahalagahan bilang hiyas.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'galing sa dagat' treasure. Before we had 'Pearl' milk tea, we had the OG perlas that made the Philippines the 'Pearl of the Orient Seas.' It's what your lola receives on her 50th wedding anniversary, and what you hope to find when you're shucking oysters (spoiler: you'll probably just find oyster).
usage_notes: Also used metaphorically to mean something precious or a gem.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang kuwintas na gawa sa tunay na **perlas** ang regalo niya sa kanyang ina.","translation":"A necklace made of real **pearls** was his gift to his mother."},{"sentence":"Tinaguriang 'Perlas ng Silanganan' ang Pilipinas.","translation":"The Philippines is called the '**Pearl** of the Orient'."}]

translation: Let's go now; It's a go
meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nag-uudyok na simulan na ang isang gawain o pag-alis, o nagpapahiwatig na ang isang bagay ay aprubado o tuloy na.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung "Go!" na may kasamang sense of urgency o finality. 'Pag sinabi ng nanay mo, "Maghugas ka ng pinggan, go na!" wala ka nang choice kundi sumunod. It's the final "push" to start something. Can also mean "It's decided!" or "Let's go already!"
usage_notes: A very common colloquial phrase. The 'na' adds immediacy or confirmation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano pa'ng hinihintay natin? **Go na**!","translation":"What are we waiting for? **Let's go now**!"},{"sentence":"Okay, aprubado na ang budget. **Go na** ang project.","translation":"Okay, the budget is approved. The project is a **go**."}]

translation: something to be thrown away; disposable item
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na itatapon na, wala nang silbi, o sadyang ginawa para sa iisang gamitan lamang.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung mga bagay na "for disposal" na. Parang 'yung mga ex mong kinalimutan mo na. 'Yung plastic cup sa party, 'yung balat ng kendi, o 'yung feelings mo para sa kanya na wala nang pag-asa. Disposable, ika nga.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa basura o mga bagay na isang beses lang gagamitin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ihiwalay mo ang mga basurang nabubulok sa mga **panapon** na plastik.","translation":"Separate the biodegradable garbage from the **disposable** plastics."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong ituring na parang **panapon** ang mga lumang laruan; ipamigay mo na lang.","translation":"Don't treat old toys like they're just **trash to be thrown away**; just give them away."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na paraan ng pagtingin, pag-unawa, o pag-iisip tungkol sa isang bagay; isang personal na opinyon o saloobin.
etymology: From the root 'tanaw' (view, sight from a distance). Formed with the `pan-` prefix, where `pan-` + `tanaw` becomes `pananaw` due to assimilation (t -> n).
original_explanation: This is your personal 'sana all' or 'cancel culture' take on an issue. It's your 'two cents,' your opinion, your 'hugot' on a situation. Everyone has one, especially on social media. It's how you see the world, whether through rose-colored glasses or the cynical lens of a daily commuter.
usage_notes: A very common word used in discussions, debates, and expressing opinions. It's slightly more formal than 'opinyon' but used just as frequently.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkakaiba ang ating **pananaw** sa pulitika, ngunit magkaibigan pa rin tayo.","translation":"We have different **perspectives** on politics, but we are still friends."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **pananaw** mo sa bagong patakaran ng kumpanya?","translation":"What is your **point of view** on the company's new policy?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong metaliko na may kulay pilak-puti, malambot, at madaling tunawin, na ginagamit sa paggawa ng mga lata at bilang panghinang.
original_explanation: This is the scientific, more formal name for 'tin', the metal. You won't hear this at the palengke when buying 'de lata' (canned goods), but you might hear it in a science class or from a welder looking for 'panghinang' (solder). It's the stuff that keeps your sardines safe.
usage_notes: A technical or scientific term. 'Lata' is the common word for tin cans.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **estanyo** ay isang mahalagang sangkap sa paggawa ng solder.","translation":"**Tin** is an important component in making solder."}]

meaning_filipino: Paggalang o pagbibigay-halaga sa isang tao, bagay, o dahilan.
etymology: Reduplication of a root, possibly related to memory or thought.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "I'm doing this for you" concept. It's the reason you work overtime (alang-alang sa pamilya), the reason you bite your tongue during a family reunion (alang-alang sa kapayapaan), and the reason you share your last piece of chicharon (alang-alang sa friendship). It's the emotional fuel for sacrifice, big or small.
usage_notes: Most commonly used in the prepositional phrase 'alang-alang sa' (for the sake of). As a standalone noun, it means 'consideration' or 'respect'. The verb form 'mag-alang-alang' means 'to hesitate out of respect'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magpakita ka naman ng kaunting **alang-alang** sa mga nakatatanda.","translation":"Show a little **respect** for the elders."},{"sentence":"Walang siyang **alang-alang** sa damdamin ng iba.","translation":"He has no **consideration** for the feelings of others."}]

translation: to be scared, to be afraid
meaning_filipino: Makaranas o makaramdam ng takot.
original_explanation: That feeling when you hear a noise in the kitchen at 3 AM and you live alone. Or when your mom calls you by your full name. Or seeing "5 missed calls from Client." To 'matakot' is to have your soul momentarily leave your body due to pure, unadulterated panic.
usage_notes: A very common verb expressing the state of being afraid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **matakot** sa dilim.","translation":"Don't **be afraid** of the dark."},{"sentence":"**Natakot** ako sa nakita kong multo sa lumang bahay.","translation":"I **was scared** by the ghost I saw in the old house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan sa pagluluto na ginagamit upang magluto ng pagkain sa pamamagitan ng singaw.
etymology: From 'singaw' (steam) with affix 'pa- -an' denoting a place or tool for the action.
original_explanation: The essential piece of kitchen equipment for your siomai, siopao, and kutsinta dreams. It's basically a pot with an identity crisis—it has a second layer with holes to let the steam pass through. The official appliance of 'healthy-eating-kunwari' month.
usage_notes: Can refer to a multi-tiered metal steamer, a bamboo steamer, or even an improvised rack placed inside a regular pot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilagay mo ang siomai sa **pasingawan** nang dalawampung minuto.","translation":"Put the siomai in the **steamer** for twenty minutes."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsasailalim ng isang tao sa isang espesyal na uri ng pagkain o pagkontrol sa kinakain para sa kalusugan o pagbabawas ng timbang.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na 'diet' na nilagyan ng panlaping Tagalog na '-in'.
original_explanation: This is what your doctor, your tita, or your own conscience tells you to do after the holidays. 'Diyetahin' is the verb form of 'diet'. It's an action! "Kailangan mo nang diyetahin 'yan, puro ka na samgyupsal!" The struggle is real.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwa na nabuo mula sa isang hiram na pangngalan. Karaniwang ginagamit sa pormang utos o mungkahi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabi ng doktor na kailangan na siyang **diyetahin** dahil sa alta-presyon.","translation":"The doctor said he needs **to be put on a diet** because of high blood pressure."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang hirap sa pagsasalita nang tuluy-tuloy, na may kasamang pag-uulit o pagtigil sa mga salita o pantig.
original_explanation: This is you when your crush suddenly asks you a question. Or when your boss asks for a project update you haven't started. Your words get stuck in traffic. To magkautal-utal is to stutter or stammer, usually out of nervousness, fear, or pure, unadulterated kilig.
usage_notes: The reduplication 'utal-utal' intensifies the action of stuttering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **nagkautal-utal** nang subukang aminin ang kanyang nararamdaman.","translation":"He **stuttered** when he tried to confess his feelings."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang kabahan, baka ka **magkautal-utal** sa entablado.","translation":"Don't be nervous, you might **stutter** on stage."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ina na mag-isang nagpapalaki sa kanyang mga anak nang walang katuwang na asawa o partner.
original_explanation: The CEO of the household. She's the cook, the driver, the nurse, the teacher, and the ATM. She's the original 'strong independent woman' who runs on coffee and pure love for her kids. The real 'ilaw ng tahanan', but also the breaker, wiring, and power source.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, commonly used in Taglish conversations. The formal Filipino equivalent is 'solong ina'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **singlemom**, natutunan niyang maging matatag para sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"As a **single mom**, she learned to be strong for her family."}]

translation: the occurrence of a miracle; act of performing a miracle
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o pangyayari ng isang himala; isang di-pangkaraniwan at kamangha-manghang kaganapan na itinuturing na gawa ng isang higit na kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: When you somehow pass your exam even though you only studied the night before. Or when you find a parking spot at the mall on a December weekend. It's that 'divine intervention' feeling, the plot twist you didn't see coming but desperately needed.
usage_notes: 'Paghihimala' is the action/process, while 'himala' is the event itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami ang naniniwala sa **paghihimala** ng Itim na Nazareno.","translation":"Many believe in the **miracle-working** of the Black Nazarene."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang paggaling mula sa malubhang sakit ay isang tunay na **paghihimala**.","translation":"Her recovery from a serious illness was a true **occurrence of a miracle**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalaman o nagpapakita ng katangian ng apoy; nag-aalab, marubdob, o puno ng sidhi.
etymology: ma- (pang-uri) + apoy (fire). Ang pormang 'mainapoy' ay hindi gaanong karaniwan kumpara sa 'maapoy' o 'nag-aalab'.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung talumpati ng isang kandidato na gigil na gigil. O 'yung tingin sa'yo ng jowa mo 'pag nalaman niyang ni-like mo 'yung picture ng ex mo. Pwede ring literal, tulad ng Bicol Express na sobrang anghang. Isang mainapoy na debate, o isang mainapoy na halik. Intense, besh!
usage_notes: Ang salitang 'maapoy' ay mas karaniwang ginagamit para sa literal na kahulugan (fiery). Ang 'mainapoy' ay mas malalim o pampanitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbigay siya ng isang **mainapoy** na talumpati laban sa katiwalian.","translation":"He gave a **fiery** speech against corruption."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang kanyang **mainapoy** na galit.","translation":"I felt his **fiery** anger."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na termino para sa sitwasyon kung saan ang isang lalaki ay itinuturing lamang na parang nakatatandang kapatid ng taong gusto niya, kaya't walang pag-asang magkaroon ng romantikong ugnayan.
etymology: Isang portmanteau o pinagsamang salita ng Tagalog na "kuya" at Ingles na "zone", na halaw sa terminong "friendzone".
original_explanation: The next level of the friendzone. It's when your crush says, "You're like a brother to me." Ouch. It’s a one-way ticket to being the designated taga-hatid, taga-sundo, and shoulder to cry on, but never the boyfriend. You get all the responsibilities of a 'kuya' without any of the romantic perks. #Saklap
usage_notes: Isang modernong salitang balbal na popular sa mga kabataan at sa social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala niya may pag-asa siya, pero na-**kuyazone** lang pala siya ni crush.","translation":"He thought he had a chance, but he just got **kuya-zoned** by his crush."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang dimensyon, lawak, haba, o laki ng isang bagay na natutukoy sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng isang pamantayan.
original_explanation: 'Ano'ng sukat ng T-shirt mo?' is a question you hear at every company outing or family reunion giveaway. It's your waistline, your shoe size, the floor area of your condo. It's the quantifiable dimension of anything, from your body to your patience ('Maikli ang sukat ng pasensya ko!').
usage_notes: Very common word. Can refer to any kind of dimension.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tama ba ang **sukat** ng binili mong sapatos?","translation":"Is the **size** of the shoes you bought correct?"},{"sentence":"Kunin mo ang **sukat** ng bintana para makabili tayo ng kurtina.","translation":"Get the **measurement** of the window so we can buy a curtain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kabilang sa pangatlo sa pinakamalaking pangkat etnolinggwistiko sa Pilipinas, na pangunahing naninirahan sa Rehiyon ng Ilocos. Tumutukoy rin ito sa kanilang wika, na pormal na kilala bilang Iloko.
etymology: Mula sa "i-" (mula sa) at "looc" (look o baybayin), na nangangahulugang "mga tao mula sa baybayin."
original_explanation: Your 'kuripot' but actually just super practical and hardworking friend from the North. The Ilocanos are known for being resourceful and for their distinct cuisine like pinakbet and bagnet. When you say someone is Ilocano, you're not just talking about where they're from, but also invoking a whole cultural stereotype of being thrifty and resilient. It's also the name of their language, which has its own cool words like 'agyamanak' for 'salamat'.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa tao, wika, o kultura. Ang 'Iloko' ay ang mas pormal at teknikal na tawag para sa wika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lola ko ay isang purong **Ilocano** mula sa La Union.","translation":"My grandmother is a pure **Ilocano** from La Union."},{"sentence":"Marunong ka bang magsalita ng **Ilocano**?","translation":"Do you know how to speak **Ilocano**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng kabutihan, kabaitan, at kagandahang-asal sa kapwa; may mabuting kalooban.
original_explanation: This is more than just being "mabait" (nice). 'Magandang-loob' is a deep, inherent kindness. It's the person who helps you change a flat tire in the rain, the tita who gives you extra baon, or the stranger who returns your lost wallet with everything still inside. It's about having a "beautiful interior" or a good soul. It's a core Filipino value.
usage_notes: A compound adjective ("maganda" + "na" + "loob"). It describes a person's character.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanilang komunidad bilang isang taong **magandang-loob**.","translation":"He is known in their community as a **kind-hearted** person."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **magandang-loob**, marami ang nagmamahal sa kanya.","translation":"Because of her **benevolence**, many people love her."}]

meaning_filipino: Pilit na ipasok o ilagay ang sarili o isang bagay sa isang masikip na lugar.
original_explanation: The official verb of riding the MRT/LRT during rush hour. It's the art of making yourself fit into a space that logically shouldn't fit another human being. Also applies to finding that one last spot in the jeepney or trying to fit all your 'pasalubong' into an already full luggage. The motto is: 'Kahit masikip, kakasya 'yan!'
usage_notes: Can be used for people, objects, or even abstract ideas (e.g., squeezing information into one's brain).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumiksik** siya sa pagitan ng dalawang malaking tao sa loob ng bus.","translation":"He **squeezed in** between two large people inside the bus."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **sumiksik** diyan, wala nang lugar.","translation":"Don't **cram** yourself in there, there's no more space."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar, tulad ng bundok o daan, na may mataas at halos bertikal na anggulo ng pag-akyat o pagbaba.
original_explanation: This is that Baguio or Antipolo road that makes your car (and your prayers) go into overdrive. Yung feeling na parang aakyat ka na sa langit sa sobrang taas ng incline. Perfect description for a difficult hike, a scary driveway, or the "climb" you have to make in your career to get that promotion.
usage_notes: Describes a sharp incline or slope.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahirapan ang sasakyan na umakyat sa **matirik** na daan.","translation":"The car had difficulty climbing the **steep** road."},{"sentence":"Napakapagod akyatin ang **matirik** na bundok na iyon.","translation":"It's very tiring to climb that **precipitous** mountain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng ilong upang matukoy o maranasan ang halimuyak o baho ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The verb form. 'Amuyin mo nga 'to!' is a classic Filipino dare, which can lead to smelling something wonderful like perfume or something horrifying like your friend's kili-kili. It's the action you take before you can pass judgment on the 'amoy' (noun).
usage_notes: Mga anyo ng pandiwa: umaamoy (nagaganap), umamoy (naganap), aamuyin (magaganap). Ang 'amuyin' ay ang anyong pautos o kapag may tiyak na bagay na inaamoy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Inaamoy** ng pusa ang pagkain bago niya ito kainin.","translation":"The cat **is smelling** the food before eating it."},{"sentence":"**Amuyin** mo itong bulaklak, ang bango!","translation":"**Smell** this flower, it's so fragrant!"}]

meaning_filipino: Itigil ang pagsunod o pagsubaybay sa mga update ng isang tao o pahina sa isang social media platform.
etymology: A Taglish neologism from `mag-` (verb prefix) + English `unfollow`.
original_explanation: The digital equivalent of 'I don't want to see your face anymore.' It’s what you do to your ex after a breakup, to that tita who only posts political rants, or to that 'influencer' whose content is just... cringe. A modern act of curating your peace.
usage_notes: A clear example of code-switching becoming a standard verb in modern Filipino. The transitive form `i-unfollow` is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya akong **mag-unfollow** sa lahat ng mga account na nagdudulot ng stress.","translation":"I decided to **unfollow** all the accounts that cause stress."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magalit kung **mag-unfollow** ako sa'yo; nililinis ko lang ang feed ko.","translation":"Don't get mad if I **unfollow** you; I'm just cleaning my feed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at mabigat na kutsilyo na may malapad na talim, karaniwang ginagamit bilang kasangkapan sa paghahawan ng mga halaman o bilang sandata.
original_explanation: The ultimate probinsya multi-tool. Need to open a buko? Matsete. Need to clear some tall grass? Matsete. Need to intimidate a wayward goat? Matsete. It's the bigger, scarier cousin of the kitchen bolo knife, often seen hanging from the side of a farmer or a groundskeeper.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'itak' or 'bolo', which are more native terms for similar large knives.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **matsete** para hawanin ang daan.","translation":"He used the **machete** to clear the path."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa paghawak ng **matsete** dahil matalim iyan.","translation":"Be careful holding the **machete** because it is sharp."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling salita para sa "pangit," na nangangahulugang hindi kaaya-aya sa paningin o hitsura.
etymology: Pinaikling anyo ng salitang 'pangit'. Naging popular sa text messaging at social media.
original_explanation: Short for 'pangit.' It's the text-speak, low-key way of saying someone or something is... aesthetically challenged. You drop this in the group chat when describing a bad date or a questionable outfit. 'Friend, ang suot niya, so PG.' It's the 'iykyk' version of calling something ugly.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa impormal na pakikipag-usap, lalo na sa text at online chat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"OMG, nakita mo ba yung bagong pusa ng kapitbahay? Ang **pg**!","translation":"OMG, did you see the neighbor's new cat? It's so **ugly**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Sumuntok nang pataas, karaniwan ay nakatarget sa baba ng kalaban.
original_explanation: That legendary move from Street Fighter or Tekken. When someone says 'gusto kitang aperkatin,' they're not inviting you to a friendly match. It's the 'suntok sa panga' that sends you flying. A Tagalized word for a very specific kind of away.
usage_notes: A loanword from English, fully Filipinized with the -um- infix. Used in contexts of fighting, boxing, or action movies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa huling segundo ng laban, **umaperkat** ang boksingero at napatumba ang kalaban.","translation":"In the final second of the match, the boxer **delivered an uppercut** and knocked down his opponent."},{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat nang bigla siyang **umaperkat**.","translation":"Everyone was shocked when he suddenly **threw an uppercut**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa kalagayan ng pagiging magkadikit, magkakabit, o magkasugpong sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: Think of the LRT-1 and LRT-2 lines being connected by that walkway. Or your phone being permanently nakahugpong to the power bank because the battery is shot. It's two separate things becoming one, whether by design or by necessity.
usage_notes: Often used for physical connections, but can also be used metaphorically for ideas or groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dalawang gusali ay **nakahugpong** sa pamamagitan ng isang tulay.","translation":"The two buildings are **connected** by a bridge."},{"sentence":"Ang bagon ng tren ay **nakahugpong** sa lokomotibo.","translation":"The train car is **attached** to the locomotive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar sa baybayin kung saan maaaring dumaong o sumadsad ang mga sasakyang-dagat upang maging ligtas mula sa malalakas na alon o bagyo.
etymology: Mula sa ugat na 'sadsad' (sumayad o dumaong) at hulaping '-an' (lugar kung saan ginagawa ang kilos).
original_explanation: Think of it as the parking lot for boats. It's where ships go to chill, unload their cargo (or chismis from another island), and take a break from the wild waves of the sea. The sadsaran is the safe space for every seafarer, the final stop after a long journey.
usage_notes: Bagama't ang 'sadsad' ay maaaring mangahulugang 'run aground', ang 'sadsaran' ay tumutukoy sa isang ligtas na daungan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghihintay ang mga mangingisda sa **sadsaran** na humupa ang bagyo.","translation":"The fishermen are waiting at the **harbor** for the storm to subside."},{"sentence":"Ang **sadsaran** ng Maynila ay isa sa pinakaabala sa buong bansa.","translation":"The **port** of Manila is one of the busiest in the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyon o pook kung saan nagaganap ang pormal na pagtuturo at pag-aaral ng mga mag-aaral sa ilalim ng gabay ng mga guro.
etymology: From pa- (causative prefix) + aral (study) + -an (locative suffix), literally "a place for studying".
original_explanation: Ah, the `paaralan`. A building that holds your best memories (first crush, barkada moments) and worst nightmares (surprise quizzes, thesis defense). It's a place you couldn't wait to leave, and now you kinda miss it. Also known as "The Building Where My Baon Disappeared."
usage_notes: A general term for any educational institution, from elementary to university. 'Eskwelahan' is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumasok ka na sa **paaralan** at baka mahuli ka sa klase.","translation":"Go to **school** now or you might be late for class."},{"sentence":"Saang **paaralan** ka nagtapos ng kolehiyo?","translation":"In which **school** did you finish college?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang may hawak ng pinakamataas na kapangyarihan, awtoridad, o impluwensya.
etymology: From `pinaka-` + `makapangyarihan` (powerful), which is derived from `kapangyarihan` (power), ultimately from the root `yari` (to make/happen).
original_explanation: This is the final boss of politics, business, or even your family (usually the lola who holds the secret recipe and the land titles). It's the person or entity whose decision is final, the ultimate authority. Think of the President, the CEO, or Thanos with all the Infinity Stones. Sila ang **pinakamakapangyarihan**.
usage_notes: Used to describe ultimate authority, influence, or force.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang demokrasya, ang mga mamamayan ang **pinakamakapangyarihan** sa lahat.","translation":"In a democracy, the citizens are the **most powerful** of all."},{"sentence":"Sino sa tingin mo ang **pinakamakapangyarihan** na superhero?","translation":"Who do you think is the **most powerful** superhero?"}]

translation: to build a wall, to put up a fence
meaning_filipino: Magtayo o magpagawa ng isang pader o bakod sa paligid ng isang lugar.
etymology: From 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'pader' (wall), which is from Spanish 'pared'.
original_explanation: This is what your neighbor does when they finally get tired of your dog wandering into their yard. It's the act of building a wall ('pader'). 'Nag-usap na ang homeowners na magpader sa buong subdivision para sa seguridad.' Can also be used figuratively for putting up emotional walls. 'Huwag kang magpader sa pagitan natin.' (Don't put up a wall between us.)
usage_notes: Can be literal (construction) or figurative (emotional barriers).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **magpader** sa kanilang bakuran para magkaroon ng privacy.","translation":"They decided to **build a wall** in their yard to have privacy."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng masakit na breakup, tila nag-**pader** siya sa kanyang puso.","translation":"After the painful breakup, it seemed she **built a wall** around her heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng regular na suportang pampinansyal o sustento, karaniwan para sa pamilya, anak, o dating asawa.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative prefix) + sustento (support, sustenance), from Spanish 'sustento'.
original_explanation: This is the adulting version of 'hingi ng baon.' It's the act of providing regular financial support, like child support or alimony. It's the legal and moral obligation to provide for someone's basic needs. It's that monthly bank transfer that's non-negotiable, just like your Netflix subscription.
usage_notes: A legal and formal term related to family law and financial obligations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapasustento** sa anak ay obligasyon ng parehong magulang.","translation":"The **act of providing child support** is the obligation of both parents."},{"sentence":"Idinemanda niya ang dating asawa dahil sa hindi pagtupad sa **pagpapasustento**.","translation":"She sued her ex-husband for failing to fulfill the **provision of financial support**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balbal na pagpapaikli ng pariralang Ingles na "no problem," na nangangahulugang walang problema o ayos lang.
etymology: Mula sa pinaikling Ingles na 'no problem'.
original_explanation: The chill, text-speak version of 'walang problema.' It's what you say when a friend asks for a favor and you're too lazy to type the whole thing. 'Pre, pa-GCash 50. Balik ko bukas.' 'Noprob.'
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa impormal na pag-uusap, lalo na sa text o chat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Salamat sa tulong, ha!\" \"**Noprob**!\"","translation":"Thanks for the help!\" \"**No problem**!\""},{"sentence":"Puwede bang humiram ng notes mo?\" \"Sige, **noprob**.\"","translation":"Can I borrow your notes?\" \"Sure, **no prob**.\""}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng pagkakabit o pagsasara ng mga butones ng isang kasuotan.
original_explanation: The official action of 'getting your life together' before a job interview. You magbutones your polo, fix your hair, and try to look like you didn't just wake up 15 minutes ago. Also, what you forget to do for one button, causing an awkward situation all day.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **magbutones** ng iyong polo bago ka umalis.","translation":"Don't forget to **button up** your polo shirt before you leave."},{"sentence":"Tinulungan niya ang kanyang anak na **magbutones** ng uniporme nito.","translation":"She helped her child **button up** his uniform."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapahintulot sa isang tao na pansamantalang gamitin ang isang bagay na pag-aari mo.
original_explanation: This is the other side of "pahiram." This is you, the generous (or reluctant) soul, lending your stuff. When your friend asks "Pahiram ng charger," and you agree, you are going to pahiramin them. It's the action of lending. Pro tip: if you're going to pahiramin someone of money, be ready for it to become a donation. #Hugot
usage_notes: This is a verb where the focus is on the person being lent to.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pahiramin** mo muna si Ana ng libro, wala siyang dala.","translation":"**Lend** Ana a book for now, she didn't bring one."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **pahiramin** siya ng pera dahil hindi siya marunong magbayad.","translation":"I don't want to **lend** him money because he doesn't know how to pay it back."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng kawalan ng paggalang, respeto, o tamang pag-uugali sa kapwa; bastos.
original_explanation: Describes someone who forgot to use 'po' and 'opo' when talking to their elders. It's the kid who talks back to their nanay, the person who cuts in line, or the officemate who uses your mug without asking. Basically, anyone who acts like they were raised by wolves. Tsk tsk.
usage_notes: A strong descriptor for impolite behavior. The hyphenated form is common, but 'walang galang' as two words is also used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **walang-galang** sa mga nakatatanda sa iyo.","translation":"Don't be **disrespectful** to your elders."},{"sentence":"Tiningnan niya nang masama ang **walang-galang** na bata.","translation":"She gave the **rude** child a bad look."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na pangkat o grupo ng mga tao, lalo na ng mga sundalo, na magkakasamang nagsasagawa ng isang partikular na gawain.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "squad" o Espanyol na "escuadra".
original_explanation: Ang barkada mo na game sa lahat, from inuman to group project. Yung #squadgoals niyo ay kumain sa samgyup at mag-picture na parang cover ng album. Sa Mobile Legends, ito yung team mo na laging talo pero solid pa rin.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa kontekstong militar, pulisya, o sa mga laro at barkadahan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming **iskuwad** ang nanalo sa kumpetisyon ng Mobile Legends.","translation":"Our **squad** won the Mobile Legends competition."},{"sentence":"Isang **iskuwad** ng mga sundalo ang ipinadala sa lugar ng kalamidad.","translation":"A **squad** of soldiers was sent to the disaster area."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan sa pamilihan kung saan ang isang kumpanya o entidad lamang ang may eksklusibong kontrol sa pagbibigay ng isang partikular na produkto o serbisyo.
original_explanation: The Tagalized, more 'sarswela' sounding version of 'monopoly'. Ito yung sitwasyon na parang sa isang barangay, iisa lang ang tindahan ni Aling Nena, kaya kahit mahal ang soft drinks niya, doon ka pa rin bibili. Siya ang may hawak ng 'monopolyo' sa malamig na inumin.
usage_notes: The more common term used in general Filipino conversation and news compared to the English 'monopoly'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong panahon ng Espanyol, may **monopolyo** sa tabako.","translation":"During the Spanish era, there was a tobacco **monopoly**."},{"sentence":"Ilegal ang pagbuo ng **monopolyo** na nakakasama sa mga mamimili.","translation":"Creating a **monopoly** that harms consumers is illegal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar, tao, o bagay na pinanggagalingan o mapagkukuhanan ng isang bagay, impormasyon, o tulong.
original_explanation: 'Yung chismosa mong kapitbahay na source ng lahat ng balita sa barangay. O 'yung ATM, na source ng pera mo (hanggang sa maubos). It's where you get stuff from—be it money, information, or even 'yung ulam na hihingin mo sa katabing bahay.
usage_notes: Often used with 'ng' to specify what is being sourced (e.g., pagkunan ng yaman). Can be used interchangeably with 'mapagkukunan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang internet ay isang malawak na **pagkunan** ng impormasyon.","translation":"The internet is a vast **source** of information."},{"sentence":"Siya ang aming **pagkunan** ng lakas ng loob.","translation":"She is our **source** of courage."}]

meaning_filipino: Punit o sira, lalo na sa damit o tela, na may mahabang hiwa o tastas.
original_explanation: Imagine your favorite t-shirt after it gets snagged on a nail. That long, sad tear? That's 'gahak'. It's more dramatic than a 'punit' (a general tear) and less like a 'butas' (a hole). It’s the kind of damage that makes your lola say, 'Itapon mo na 'yan!'
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang malaki o malalang pagkapunit sa tela.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gahak** ang laylayan ng kanyang bestida matapos sumabit sa pako.","translation":"The hem of her dress was **badly torn** after getting caught on a nail."},{"sentence":"Naging **gahak** ang bandila dahil sa malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The flag became **tattered** because of the strong typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o tao na nagustuhan o naibigan nang walang malinaw na dahilan; biglaang pagkagusto o pagkahumaling.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'corazonada' na nangangahulugang 'hunch' o 'impulse from the heart'.
original_explanation: Eto yung state of mind mo kapag bigla kang nagka-crush sa isang tao na hindi mo naman talaga kilala. Parang, 'Uy, type ko siya.' Wala nang tanong-tanong. Pwedeng sa itsura, sa porma, o sa amoy ng pabango niya. Minsan, ginagamit din sa bagay, like yung sapatos na nakita mo sa mall na kahit mahal, 'kursunada ko eh, bilihin ko na.'
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa romantikong konteksto ngunit maaari ring gamitin para sa mga bagay o desisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal ko nang **kursunada** ang kapitbahay naming tahimik.","translation":"I've long **fancied** our quiet neighbor."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko alam bakit, pero **kursunada** ko talaga ang bag na iyon.","translation":"I don't know why, but I've really **taken a liking** to that bag."}]

translation: to become famous; to be known for
meaning_filipino: Ang maging kilala o tanyag, lalo na dahil sa isang pambihirang kakayahan, gawa, o katangian.
original_explanation: Yung goal ng bawat aspiring vlogger at TikToker. To go viral and mapabantog for something—hopefully for a good reason, not because of a scandal. Ito rin yung nangyayari sa isang small carinderia na na-feature sa food blog; biglang sikat!
usage_notes: Often implies becoming famous or well-known, sometimes in a specific field or for a particular reason.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **napabantog** sa larangan ng boksing sa buong mundo.","translation":"He **became famous** in the field of boxing worldwide."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang pamilya ay **napabantog** dahil sa kanilang masarap na pagluto ng adobo.","translation":"Their family **became known for** their delicious way of cooking adobo."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng koronang pampalamuti na isinusuot sa ulo, karaniwan ng mga babae sa mga pormal na okasyon, o ng mga reyna at prinsesa.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "tiara", hango sa Latin.
original_explanation: The ultimate accessory for feeling like a beauty queen, a Disney princess, or just extra fancy at your debut. It's the shiny thing on your head that says, "Yes, I am the main character today."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang nanalo sa beauty pageant ay binigyan ng bulaklak at isang makinang na **tiyara**.","translation":"The winner of the beauty pageant was given flowers and a sparkling **tiara**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim sa Ingles na nangangahulugang labis na pagtawa, kadalasang ginagamit sa di-pormal na komunikasyon sa internet.
etymology: Akronim ng pariralang Ingles na "Laughing My Fucking Ass Off".
original_explanation: The final evolution of 'haha'. When 'lol' is not enough, 'lmao' is too weak, you bring out the big guns: lmfao. This is what you type when your friend sends you a meme so funny you almost spit out your milk tea. It’s the text equivalent of a full-on, tears-streaming, can't-breathe laugh.
usage_notes: Isang bulgar na salitang balbal mula sa internet. Bagama't karaniwan, itinuturing itong di-angkop sa pormal na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita mo ba 'yung video ng pusang nahulog? **Lmfao**!","translation":"Did you see the video of the cat that fell? **Lmfao**!"}]

translation: therefore; for that reason; because of that
meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang nag-uugnay sa isang sanhi at sa resulta nito; bilang bunga o resulta ng naunang nabanggit na sitwasyon o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the Tagalog for 'And that's the tea.' or 'So, yeah, that's why.' You lay out all the receipts (the 'dahil'), and then you drop the 'doon' to point to the consequence. 'Hindi siya nag-reply sa chat mo for 3 days. **Dahil doon**, single ka na ulit.'
usage_notes: Used to connect a previously stated reason to a resulting action or conclusion. It's more formal than just saying 'kaya' (so).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging umuulan sa hapon. **Dahil doon**, palagi akong nagdadala ng payong.","translation":"It always rains in the afternoon. **Because of that**, I always bring an umbrella."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar kung saan isinasagawa o idinaraos ang isang pagtitipon, seremonya, o okasyon.
etymology: From `pag-` + `daos` + `-an` (locative suffix), meaning 'place where something is held'.
original_explanation: The 'where' of the 'ganap'. The function hall for the wedding, the convention center for the K-Pop concert, or your sala for the impromptu inuman session. It's the physical location that becomes the backdrop for all the memories (and the IG stories).
usage_notes: This is a noun referring to the place, while 'pagdaraos' is the noun for the act of holding the event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malaking bulwagan ang magiging **pagdausan** ng kumperensya.","translation":"The large hall will be the **venue** for the conference."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap pa kami ng magandang **pagdausan** para sa kasal.","translation":"We are still looking for a good **venue** for the wedding."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagkwenta, pagbilang, o pag-alam sa kabuuang halaga; isang pag-aayos ng mga pananagutan, lalo na sa pananalapi o sa isang alitan.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *tuhed, meaning 'to settle' or 'to decide'.
original_explanation: This is the 'moment of truth' for your finances. Whether it's splitting the bill with friends ('Mag-tuos na tayo'), figuring out your SSS contributions, or the final 'pagtutuos' between a telenovela hero and villain. It's the final calculation where everything is settled.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of money, debt, or a final confrontation. The verb form is 'magtuos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng handaan, nagkaroon ng **tuos** kung magkano ang gastos ng bawat isa.","translation":"After the feast, there was a **calculation** of how much each one spent."},{"sentence":"Ang huling kabanata ay ang pagtutuos ng bida at kontrabida.","translation":"The final chapter is the **reckoning** between the hero and the villain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o pangkat na may kapangyarihan o tungkuling isakatuparan ang isang batas, utos, o plano.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung 'action speaks louder than words' personified. Sila 'yung gumagawa, hindi 'yung puro plano. Sa gobyerno, sila 'yung pulis at sundalo (tagapagpatupad ng batas). Sa pamilya, sila 'yung nanay na nagsabing 'maglinis ka ng kwarto,' at pag hindi mo ginawa, sila na mismo ang gagawa... habang may kasamang sermon.
usage_notes: Often seen in formal contexts like law and management, as in 'tagapagpatupad ng batas' (law enforcer).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ahensya ang pangunahing **tagatupad** ng bagong patakaran sa kalikasan.","translation":"The agency is the main **implementer** of the new environmental policy."},{"sentence":"Bilang **tagatupad** ng huling habilin, sinigurado niyang naibigay ang lahat ng pamana.","translation":"As the **executor** of the last will, he ensured all inheritance was given."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bilang na walang bahaging praksyonal o desimal; alinman sa mga positibo o negatibong bilang, kasama ang sero.
original_explanation: Remember your Math class in high school? Integers. Numbers without 'butal' or decimal points. Unlike your sweldo na may kaltas, ang buumbilang ay solid. Walang bawas. Sana all.
usage_notes: Primarily used in mathematical or academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa araling ito, pag-aaralan natin ang mga operasyon sa **buumbilang**.","translation":"In this lesson, we will study the operations on **integers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilagay sa ilalim ng lupa o itago nang malalim sa isang bagay; maaari ring mangahulugang paglimot sa isang alaala o pagtatago ng isang lihim.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "i-" at "baon" (buried item, provision).
original_explanation: What you do with secrets, feelings for your crush who is now 'in a relationship,' or your ever-growing 'utang' sa credit card. It's the act of putting something deep down where you hope it'll never see the light of day again. 'Ibaon mo na sa limot,' as the hugot song goes.
usage_notes: Mayroon itong literal na kahulugan (maglibing sa lupa) at isang napakakaraniwang matalinghagang kahulugan (magbaon ng alaala, damdamin, o utang).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahanap nila ang ginto na **ibinabaon** ng mga pirata.","translation":"They found the gold that the pirates were **burying**."},{"sentence":"Masakit man, kailangan mo nang **ibaon** sa limot ang nakaraan.","translation":"Even if it hurts, you need to **bury** the past in oblivion."}]

translation: to compromise; to put at risk
meaning_filipino: Isakripisyo o ilagay sa alanganin ang isang bagay, tulad ng prinsipyo, kaligtasan, o reputasyon, para sa isang kasunduan o layunin.
original_explanation: When you let your friend copy your homework, you 'ikompromiso' your grades. When you eat street food from a sketchy vendor, you 'ikompromiso' your stomach. It's when you risk it all, and not always for a biscuit. It's about putting something valuable on the line.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation, implying that what is being compromised is valuable (e.g., principles, safety, quality).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ikompromiso** ang iyong mga prinsipyo para lang sa pera.","translation":"Don't **compromise** your principles just for money."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagmamadali, **naikompromiso** ang kalidad ng kanilang trabaho.","translation":"Because of the rush, the quality of their work **was compromised**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na halal na pinuno ng isang republika o bansa, o ang pinuno ng isang organisasyon.
original_explanation: The OG boss ng Pinas. Sila 'yung laging laman ng news, 'yung nagde-declare ng holiday (na inaabangan nating lahat), at 'yung may final say sa maraming bagay. Parang group leader sa project, pero ang members niya ay buong bansa.
usage_notes: Can refer to the president of a country, a company, a club, etc. The Filipino-origin word is 'pangulo', which is more formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **presidente** ng Pilipinas ay inihahalal tuwing anim na taon.","translation":"The **president** of the Philippines is elected every six years."},{"sentence":"Sino ang susunod na **presidente** ng student council?","translation":"Who is the next **president** of the student council?"}]

translation: to have someone give; to ask to be given
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap o utos na mag-abot o magkaloob ng isang bagay sa nagsasalita o sa ibang tao.
etymology: From `pa-` (to ask someone to do) + `bigay` (to give).
original_explanation: The command you use when you're too lazy to get something yourself. "Pabigay nga nung remote." It's the verbal equivalent of pointing at something you want. It's a staple in every Filipino household, used to command siblings, kids, or anyone within earshot to act as your temporary hands.
usage_notes: A command form. Often softened with "nga" or "naman". For example, "Pabigay nga..." (Please give...).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pabigay** naman ng baso ng tubig.","translation":"**Please give** me a glass of water."},{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **pabigay** itong sulat kay Ana?","translation":"Can you **have this letter given** to Ana?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang naging resulta, wakas, o bunga ng isang pangyayari, desisyon, o serye ng mga aksyon.
etymology: From 'hantong' (to end up, arrive at), with 'kina-' and '-an' affixes.
original_explanation: This is the 'final destination' of your choices. It's the 'So, what happened?' after a long story of drama. It's the grade you get after a semester of either studying hard or just 'sana all'. It’s the consequence, good or bad, of your actions. The final plot twist.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to the final state or conclusion of a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kamatayan ang naging **kinahantungan** ng bida sa pelikula.","translation":"Death was the **outcome** for the protagonist in the movie."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **kinahantungan** ng inyong pag-uusap?","translation":"What was the **result** of your conversation?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay para sa 'sangla'.
original_explanation: It's 'sangla' but on a diet, it dropped the 'g'. It means the exact same thing: pawning your stuff when you're gipit. Just a different spelling, maybe for people who are in such a hurry to get to the pawnshop they don't have time for an extra letter.
usage_notes: A common variant spelling of 'sangla.' Both are widely understood and used, though 'sangla' is considered more standard or formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong i-**sanla** ang laptop ko para pambayad ng tuition.","translation":"I need to **pawn** my laptop to pay for tuition."},{"sentence":"Nasa bahay-**sanlaan** pa rin ang kuwintas niya.","translation":"Her necklace is still at the **pawn**shop."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-itsa o paghagis ng isang bagay gamit ang kamay o braso.
etymology: From the noun 'bato' (stone), as stones are common objects to throw.
original_explanation: The command form. It's what you yell to your teammate when you need them to throw the ball. 'Bato!' It’s the pure, unadulterated action of throwing. The root of 'ibato', 'binato', 'bumabato'. It's the 'yeet' before 'yeet' was a thing.
usage_notes: Used as a command or as the root for other verb conjugations like 'ibato' (to throw something), 'bumato' (to throw), 'binato' (was thrown).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bato** mo sa akin ang bola!","translation":"**Throw** the ball to me!"},{"sentence":"Sino ang **bumato** ng papel sa guro?","translation":"Who **threw** the paper at the teacher?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pintura na tinutunaw sa tubig at ginagamit sa pagpipinta, karaniwan sa espesyal na papel.
original_explanation: Yung art materials na binili mo noong nagka-quarantine hobby ka, pero ngayon nakatambak na lang sa drawer. Ito rin yung aesthetic ng mga "artsy" cafe at IG feed.
usage_notes: Ang mas pormal o teknikal na termino ay 'akwarela'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang gumamit ng **waterkolor** sa kanyang mga obra.","translation":"She loves using **watercolor** in her artworks."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng bagong set ng **waterkolor** para sa art class.","translation":"I bought a new set of **watercolor** for art class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging mayabong, malago, o siksik ng mga halaman o dawag.
original_explanation: Think of a jungle so thick you need a bolo to get through, or your tita's plant collection that has taken over the entire balcony. That's katumukan. It's the visual representation of 'sobrang dami'.
usage_notes: Primarily used in literary or descriptive contexts related to nature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala sila sa **katumukan** ng gubat.","translation":"They got lost in the **density** of the forest."},{"sentence":"Hinahangaan niya ang **katumukan** ng mga talahib sa bukid.","translation":"He admired the **lushness** of the tall grass in the field."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likas na hilig o inklinasyon na kumilos, mag-isip, o maganap sa isang partikular na paraan; isang paulit-ulit na kilos o gawi.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung default setting mo. Kung lagi kang late, 'yan ang tendensiya mo. Kung laging nag-o-overthink sa gabi, 'yan ang tendensiya mo. It's your habit, your pattern, your 'ganito talaga ako, eh' excuse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **tendensiya** siyang maging emosyonal kapag napapagod.","translation":"He has a **tendency** to get emotional when he's tired."},{"sentence":"Ang **tendensiya** sa merkado ngayon ay ang pagtaas ng presyo ng bilihin.","translation":"The **tendency** in the market now is the increase in the price of goods."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malalim na pag-iisip, pagninilay-nilay, o pagsusuri sa isang bagay o ideya.
original_explanation: **Limi** is that state of mind when you're staring at your ceiling at 3 AM, overthinking a chat message you sent three years ago. It's deeper than just 'isip-isip.' This is serious, soul-searching stuff, the kind of heavy thinking you do before a major life decision or after watching a Christopher Nolan film.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pampanitikan o pormal na diskurso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng malalim na **limi** upang maunawaan ang talinghaga sa tula.","translation":"Deep **contemplation** is needed to understand the metaphor in the poem."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipagpatuloy o huwag itigil ang isang nasimulang gawain, paglalakbay, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: The universe's message to you when you're tired, heartbroken, or just plain 'suko na'. `Magpatuloy` ka lang. It's the "keep swimming" of the Philippines. Also what the guard says after checking your bag at the mall entrance: "Sige po, `magpatuloy` na po."
usage_notes: Extremely common verb used in all contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit maraming pagsubok, kailangan nating **magpatuloy** sa buhay.","translation":"Despite many challenges, we need to **continue** with life."},{"sentence":"Pwede na po kayong **magpatuloy** sa inyong biyahe.","translation":"You may now **proceed** with your journey."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aklat na inilalathala taun-taon na naglalaman ng mga kaganapan, larawan, at mga tala ng isang partikular na taon, lalo na sa isang paaralan.
original_explanation: The official, slightly more formal term for a yearbook. It's what your parents call it. It's the book where you find out your batchmate's full name and see who won 'Most Likely to Succeed' (and then stalk them on LinkedIn 10 years later to check).
usage_notes: This is the most direct and formal Filipino translation for 'yearbook'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilabas na ang bagong **taunang-aklat** ng unibersidad.","translation":"The university's new **yearbook** has been released."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng disenyo ng pabalat ng ating **taunang-aklat**.","translation":"The cover design of our **yearbook** is beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa relasyon ng isang lalaki sa anak ng kanyang kapatid (pamangkin), o ang kabaligtaran nito.
etymology: mag- (prefix indicating relationship) + tiyo (uncle, from Spanish 'tío')
original_explanation: The relationship dynamic between an uncle and his favorite (or not-so-favorite) pamangkin. It's the "Uy, Tiyo, penge Pasko!" and the "Ang laki mo na, iho/iha!" combo. Basically, the formal term for your built-in ATM and life-advice-giver during family reunions.
usage_notes: The 'mag-' prefix here indicates a reciprocal or plural relationship between two or more people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkamukha talaga ang **magtiyo** na sina Robert at ang pamangkin niyang si Leo.","translation":"The **uncle and nephew**, Robert and his nephew Leo, really look alike."},{"sentence":"Laging nagkukulitan ang **magtiyo** tuwing may salu-salo sa pamilya.","translation":"The **uncle and nephew/niece** are always fooling around during family gatherings."}]

translation: a place to receive wages; payroll office
meaning_filipino: Ang lugar o tanggapan kung saan kinukuha o tinatanggap ang sahod o bayad para sa pagtatrabaho.
original_explanation: The holy land on the 15th and 30th of the month. The 'sahuran' is where you line up to get your hard-earned 'sahod' (salary). It's the company cashier or the ATM, basically. The place where your 'pagod' (fatigue) becomes 'pera' (money).
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb 'sahuran' (to give salary to someone), but is more commonly used as a noun referring to the place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahaba ang pila sa **sahuran** tuwing araw ng suweldo.","translation":"The line at the **payroll office** is long every payday."},{"sentence":"Pumunta siya sa **sahuran** para kunin ang kanyang komisyon.","translation":"She went to the **place for receiving payment** to get her commission."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagbibigay ng salapi o katumbas na halaga bilang kabayaran para sa isang produkto, serbisyo, o utang.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment of truth sa cashier. Or 'yung ginagawa mo sa G-Cash para sa Shopee order mo at 3 AM. It can be for bills, for food, or para sa utang mo sa kaibigan mong naniningil na. "Nagbabayad na po, wait lang, 'di pa po tapos kumain."
usage_notes: The progressive aspect (present tense) of the verb "magbayad".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang laging **nagbabayad** ng aming mga bill sa kuryente at tubig.","translation":"He is always the one **paying** our electricity and water bills."},{"sentence":"\"Sino ang **nagbabayad** para sa lahat ng ito?\" tanong niya.","translation":"\"Who is **paying** for all of this?\" he asked."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng biglaang pagtigil sa lahat ng komunikasyon sa isang tao nang walang anumang paliwanag, lalo na sa larangan ng modernong pag-ibig.
original_explanation: "Ghosting" is the art of disappearing from someone's life without a trace. It's the ultimate 'seen-zone' level up. You were chatting, you were laughing, you were planning to meet for milk tea, and then... *poof*. They're gone. No explanation, just the deafening silence of your unread messages. It's the "walkout" of digital relationships.
usage_notes: Refers to the action or phenomenon itself. Commonly discussed in media and conversations about modern dating etiquette.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **ghosting** ay isang masakit na paraan para tapusin ang isang ugnayan.","translation":"**Ghosting** is a painful way to end a relationship."},{"sentence":"Uso na talaga ang **ghosting** sa panahon ngayon.","translation":"**Ghosting** is really common nowadays."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho ay mangolekta ng mga basura mula sa mga tahanan at establisyimento.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of your neighborhood who makes the basura magically disappear every week. You know they're coming when you hear the bell or the distinct sound of their truck at 5 AM.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the person who collects garbage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan na ba ang **basurero**?","translation":"Has the **garbage collector** passed by already?"},{"sentence":"Isang marangal na trabaho ang pagiging **basurero**.","translation":"Being a **sanitation worker** is a noble job."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa sistema o pag-uugali kung saan mayroong pagbubukod-bukod sa mga grupo o paksyon na nagpapahirap sa pagkakaisa.
original_explanation: The OG 'squad goals' but with a negative twist. It's the reason why office politics is a thing. You see this in schools, workplaces, and even government agencies. Everyone sticks to their own 'barkada' and it becomes a system of 'if you're not with us, you're against us.'
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation, implying favoritism, cronyism, and a lack of unity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ng bagong manager ang sistemang **kampi-kampi** sa opisina.","translation":"The new manager dislikes the **cliquish** system in the office."},{"sentence":"Nahihirapan umasenso ang bansa dahil sa **kampi-kampi** sa pulitika.","translation":"The country is having a hard time progressing because of **factionalism** in politics."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang propesyonal na dalubhasa sa estenograpiya, ang sining ng mabilis na pagsusulat gamit ang mga simbolo at pagpapaikli. Karaniwang tumutukoy sa lalaki o sa pangkalahatang termino.
original_explanation: The guy in a legal drama who looks like he's playing a tiny piano but is actually recording every word of a dramatic confession. He's the silent, unsung hero of the courtroom, ensuring there's a written record of who said 'I object!' with the most passion.
usage_notes: Can be used as a gender-neutral term, but often implies a male stenographer, with 'estenograpa' for the female.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha ang serbisyo ng isang **estenograper** para sa mahalagang pulong ng board.","translation":"The services of a **stenographer** were acquired for the important board meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng lupa o daan na puno ng putik at malambot dahil sa pagkabasa.
etymology: From 'ma-' (having the quality of) + 'putik' (mud). The form 'sapote' is a less common, possibly regional, variant or corruption related to the soft, mushy texture, similar to the fruit 'sapote'.
original_explanation: This is what your brand-new white sneakers look like after walking through a provincial shortcut during the rainy season. Not to be confused with the fruit, unless you literally fell into a pile of them. The more common term is 'maputik', so using this will get you some 'deep Tagalog' points.
usage_notes: This is a rare or regional term. 'Maputik' is the standard and more widely understood word for 'muddy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa paglakad, **masapote** ang bukid pagkatapos ng ulan.","translation":"Be careful walking, the field is **muddy** after the rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbuga o paglabas ng hangin mula sa baga.
original_explanation: This is the "salamat tapos na ang meeting" breath. Yung moment na sobrang stressed ka sa work, tapos you take a moment to **huminga nang palabas** and let go of the negativity. It's the official action after saying "Hay, nako!"
usage_notes: This is the direct, literal term for exhaling. The opposite is "huminga nang paloob" (to inhale).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng yoga instructor ang klase na **huminga nang palabas** nang dahan-dahan.","translation":"The yoga instructor told the class to **exhale** slowly."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang ginhawa nang **huminga siya nang palabas** matapos ang mahabang araw.","translation":"He felt relief when he **exhaled** after a long day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o arena kung saan idinaraos ang sabong o paglalaban ng mga manok na panabong.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "sakla" na isang uri ng sugal na baraha, ngunit ang "saklaan" ay naging tukoy sa sabungan.
original_explanation: Ito yung "The Hunger Games" ng mga manok. Dito nagkikita-kita ang mga tito para isugal ang pang-tuition ng anak nila sa paborito nilang manok na may pangalang "Rambo" o "Terminator". The ultimate "man cave" for sabungeros.
usage_notes: Ang "sakla" ay isang uri ng sugal gamit ang baraha. Ang "saklaan" ay halos eksklusibong tumutukoy sa sabungan (cockpit).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng tao ang **saklaan** tuwing Linggo.","translation":"The **cockpit** is full of people every Sunday."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbawal muna ang operasyon ng mga **saklaan** dahil sa pandemya.","translation":"The operation of **cockpits** was temporarily banned due to the pandemic."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o bagay na ginagamit sa pagbaak, paghati, o pagbiyak ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay kahoy o niyog.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pan-" at salitang ugat na "baak" (split). Ang /n/ sa "pan-" ay nagiging /m/ dahil sa kasunod na tunog na /b/.
original_explanation: This is the tool you grab when you need to split something in half, like that stubborn buko for your buko juice or the firewood for your lola's dirty kitchen. It's the 'divide and conquer' gadget of the household.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pang-uri (e.g., "itak na pambaak").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng matalas na **pambaak** para sa mga troso na ito.","translation":"I need a sharp **splitting tool** for these logs."},{"sentence":"Ang itak na iyan ay mabisang **pambaak** ng niyog.","translation":"That bolo is an effective tool **for splitting** coconuts."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging hindi tuloy-tuloy o paputol-putol sa pagsasalita, kadalasan dahil sa kaba, takot, o kawalan ng kasanayan.
original_explanation: That feeling when your crush suddenly talks to you and your brain short-circuits, making you unable to form a coherent sentence. "Um, ah, eh..." That's you being **gatol**. It's also what happens during a job interview when they ask, "So, what are your weaknesses?"
usage_notes: Inilalarawan ang kalidad ng pananalita sa isang partikular na sandali, at hindi isang permanenteng kondisyon tulad ng pagiging 'utal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **gatol** ang kanyang pagsasalita nang tanungin siya ng pulis.","translation":"His speech became **stammering** when the police questioned him."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa nerbiyos, **gatol** ang sagot niya sa entablado.","translation":"Because of nervousness, his answer on stage was **faltering**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang silid na itinalaga para sa pagdarasal o pagninilay-nilay.
original_explanation: The quiet corner in a Filipino home, mall, or office where you can have a moment with God. It's where you pray for a sign, for your crush to notice you, or for your data plan to last until the next payday.
usage_notes: Can refer to a small private chapel or a designated prayer area in a public space like a mall or airport.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May maliit na **silid-dasalan** sa bawat palapag ng aming opisina.","translation":"There is a small **prayer room** on every floor of our office."},{"sentence":"Tahimik kaming naghintay sa labas ng **silid-dasalan**.","translation":"We waited quietly outside the **prayer room**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na nangangahulugang walang pagbabago sa sinasabi o ginagawa; paulit-ulit at pare-pareho ang paraan o nilalaman.
original_explanation: Literally "one tone". Used to describe something that's boringly repetitive, like your boss's lecture about KPIs. "Yung sermon ni mama, iisang tono na lang palagi: 'Mag-aral ka mabuti!'" It can also mean "in unison," like a choir singing with one voice, but it's more often used for something that's become predictable and monotonous.
usage_notes: A common idiom. The context determines if it means "monotonous" (negative) or "in unison" (neutral/positive).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula noon hanggang ngayon, **iisang tono** pa rin ang kaniyang mga pangako.","translation":"From then until now, his promises are still the **same old story**."},{"sentence":"Kinanta nila ang Lupang Hinirang na may **iisang tono** at damdamin.","translation":"They sang the National Anthem **in unison** and with one feeling."}]

translation: to snatch; to swoop down and seize
meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at biglaang pagkuha o pag-agaw sa isang bagay, karaniwang ginagawa mula sa itaas pababa, tulad ng ginagawa ng isang ibong mandaragit.
original_explanation: 'Yung experience na kumakain ka ng fishball sa labas, tapos biglang may dumaang aso at **dinagit** 'yung huling tusok mo! Saklap! Or in the modern world, 'yung mga snatcher na bigla na lang hahablutin 'yung cellphone mo. Sila ay mga **mandaragit** ng gamit (at peace of mind).
usage_notes: Often associated with birds of prey ('ibong mandaragit'). When applied to humans, it implies a swift, predatory act of snatching.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na **dinagit** ng agila ang sisiw na naligaw.","translation":"The eagle quickly **swooped down and seized** the lost chick."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maglalabas ng cellphone sa madilim na eskinita baka may **mandagit**.","translation":"Don't take out your cellphone on a dark alley, someone might **snatch** it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na labis na matalino o nakatuon sa isang partikular na larangan ng pag-aaral o libangan, na kung minsan ay itinuturing na hindi marunong makisama sa lipunan.
original_explanation: This is a direct import from English, glasses and all. In the Philippines, a 'nerd' is usually the class top-notcher, the one who actually reads the textbook, or the person who can explain the entire Marvel Cinematic Universe timeline without breathing. It used to be an insult, but now, in the age of Silicon Valley and esports, being a 'nerd' is kind of a flex. 'Geek' is its cooler cousin.
usage_notes: A direct English loanword that has been fully adopted into Taglish and colloquial Filipino. The meaning is identical to its English counterpart.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinatawag siyang **nerd** ng mga kaklase niya dahil lagi siyang nasa library.","translation":"His classmates call him a **nerd** because he is always in the library."},{"sentence":"Dati, ayaw kong matawag na **nerd**, pero ngayon, proud ako sa mga interes ko.","translation":"Before, I didn't want to be called a **nerd**, but now, I'm proud of my interests."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o sandali ng pag-alis o paglisan mula sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: The moment you clock out from work, that's your pagkaalis. It's the "Bye, Felicia!" moment. It can also be dramatic, like the feeling right after your ex walks out the door. The silence after the "ghosting" starts.
usage_notes: Often used in time-based constructions, like "pagkaalis niya" (after he/she left).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging malungkot ang bahay **pagkaalis** ng aming mga bisita.","translation":"The house became sad after the **departure** of our guests."},{"sentence":"**Pagkaalis** ko sa opisina, dumaan muna ako sa mall.","translation":"**After leaving** the office, I dropped by the mall first."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng parehong halaga, sukat, o katuturan.
original_explanation: When you're trying to explain that one US dollar is not magkatumbas to one Philippine peso. Or when you realize that the effort you put into a relationship is not magkatumbas to the effort you're getting back. It's the math of life, love, and currency exchange.
usage_notes: Used for measurements, values, translations, and abstract concepts like effort or love.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang metro ay **magkatumbas** ng isandaang sentimetro.","translation":"One meter is **equivalent** to one hundred centimeters."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang pagmamahal at pag-aalaga ay **magkatumbas**.","translation":"For him, love and care are **equivalent**."}]
