meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang gamit, kasuotan, o bagay na idinisenyo upang magbigay proteksyon laban sa ulan.
original_explanation: Your anti-ulan starter pack. This refers to your trusty payong (umbrella), kapote (raincoat), or those plastic boots you wear to survive the flood-prone streets of Manila. Anything that helps you battle the 'ber' months' downpour is pang-ulan. It's the gear you need to avoid looking like a 'basang sisiw' (wet chick).
usage_notes: Can be an adjective (e.g., 'sapatos na pang-ulan' - rain boots) or a noun referring to rain gear collectively.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bota na ito ay maganda at matibay na **pang-ulan**.","translation":"These boots are nice and sturdy **for the rain**."},{"sentence":"Dalhin mo ang iyong **pang-ulan** dahil mukhang babagyo.","translation":"Bring your **rain gear** because it looks like it's going to storm."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang gulay na may tila bombilya sa ilalim ng lupa, kilala sa matapang na amoy at lasa, at ginagamit bilang pampalasa sa pagluluto.
original_explanation: The official vegetable of Filipino dramatic scenes. If you're not crying while chopping this, are you even cooking? Also, the reason your grocery bill suddenly feels like a downpayment for a condo. The true gold of the Philippine market.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maghiwa ka ng **sibuyas** para sa ginisang ulam.","translation":"Chop some **onions** for the sauteed dish."},{"sentence":"Tumataas na naman ang presyo ng **sibuyas** sa palengke.","translation":"The price of **onions** in the market is increasing again."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga gawain o aktibidad na isinasagawa sa labas ng karaniwang kurikulum o programa ng pag-aaral sa isang paaralan.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga sinalihan mong club sa school para lang may mailagay sa yearbook at para iwas-tambay. From varsity teams and dance troupes to the school paper, these are the "plus points" activities outside your regular classes that make your student life either super fun or super stressful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali si Maria sa maraming gawaing **ekstrakurikular** upang mapabuti ang kanyang kasanayan sa pamumuno.","translation":"Maria joined many **extracurricular** activities to improve her leadership skills."},{"sentence":"Ang paglalaro ng basketball ay isang popular na aktibidad na **ekstrakurikular**.","translation":"Playing basketball is a popular **extracurricular** activity."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng malalim na pag-unawa o pag-intindi sa isang bagay na mahirap o masalimuot; ang pagsisikap na maabot ang kahulugan.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable `li-` + `lirip` (to fathom, comprehend).
original_explanation: This is a level up from 'paglilining.' This isn't just thinking; it's trying to understand something really, really deep. It's the 'paglilirip' on the meaning of life, the universe, and why Jollibee chicken tastes so good. It's the mental effort you exert when trying to understand a complex philosophical text or your partner's 'it's fine.'
usage_notes: A very formal and literary word for deep comprehension.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglilirip** sa hiwaga ng sansinukob ay isang walang katapusang gawain.","translation":"The **fathoming** of the mysteries of the universe is an endless task."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng masusing **paglilirip** upang maunawaan ang kanyang tula.","translation":"Meticulous **deep thought** is needed to understand his poem."}]

translation: sound of clearing one's throat; hawk
meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha kapag pilit na inaalis ang plema o anumang bara sa lalamunan.
original_explanation: That awkward sound your tito makes before he tells a long story at a family reunion. It's the human equivalent of a computer's startup sound, but for an incoming 'habilin' or a corny joke. The official sound of "ehem, excuse me, ahem, may sasabihin ako."
usage_notes: Describes the sound itself. The action is 'sumagaak' or 'pagsagaak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **sagaak** ang narinig mula sa matanda bago siya nagsalita.","translation":"A loud **throat-clearing sound** was heard from the old man before he spoke."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng katawan na nag-uugnay sa binti at paa, na binubuo ng mga buto sa magkabilang gilid nito.
etymology: Mula sa reduplikasyon ng salitang 'bukong', na nangangahulugang 'node' o 'bukó' tulad ng sa kawayan, na tumutukoy sa hugis-bukong kasukasuan.
original_explanation: That bony part of your leg you always manage to hit on the corner of the bed or a table leg. It's the joint that decides if your "sana all" travel goals will involve walking or a wheelchair. A sprained 'bukung-bukong' is a classic drama moment in Pinoy teleseryes.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa paglalarawan ng mga pinsala tulad ng tapilok (sprain) o bali (fracture) sa naturang bahagi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namaga ang kanyang **bukung-bukong** matapos matapilok sa hagdanan.","translation":"Her **ankle** swelled after she tripped on the stairs."},{"sentence":"Ang taas ng baha ay hanggang **bukung-bukong** lang.","translation":"The floodwater was only **ankle**-deep."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng mga paniniwala na salungat sa katotohanan o makatuwirang pag-iisip, kadalasan ay sintomas ng isang mental na karamdaman.
original_explanation: The formal, slightly more serious tita of 'delulu'. You use 'delulu' for fun, for K-pop fantasies. You use 'delusional' when your friend genuinely thinks their ex, who ghosted them and is now married, is still coming back. It has a bit more weight and concern attached to it.
usage_notes: Used in both formal and informal contexts, but carries a stronger, more clinical connotation than its slang counterpart "delulu."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagiging **delusional** na siya sa pag-aakalang mananalo siya sa lotto kahit hindi siya tumataya.","translation":"He's becoming **delusional** for thinking he'll win the lottery even though he doesn't buy tickets."},{"sentence":"You're being **delusional** if you think you can pass without studying.","translation":"Nagiging **delusional** ka kung inaakala mong makakapasa ka nang hindi nag-aaral."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging madulas. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay tumutukoy sa di-sinasadyang pagkakamali sa pagsasalita o pag-iisip.
original_explanation: This has two flavors. The literal one is the 'slipperiness' of a floor after your tita mops it with floor wax—a hazard zone. The figurative one is a 'slip of the tongue,' like accidentally calling your new partner by your ex's name. Both can cause a major fall. Oops.
usage_notes: The context, especially the phrase 'kadulasan ng dila', determines whether it's literal (physical slipperiness) or figurative (a mistake).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa **kadulasan** ng sahig na bagong wax.","translation":"Be careful of the **slipperiness** of the newly waxed floor."},{"sentence":"Isang **kadulasan** ng dila lamang ang kanyang sinabi, patawarin mo na.","translation":"It was just a **slip** of the tongue, please forgive him."}]

translation: to clash; to encounter; to confront each other
meaning_filipino: Ang pagharap o pag-abot sa isang pagtutunggali, labanan, o hindi inaasahang pagtatagpo.
original_explanation: The moment you and your ex accidentally book the same coffee shop for your respective dates. Awkward! It's that unexpected, often confrontational, meeting. Nag-iwasan sila buong taon pero **nagkasagupa** pa rin sa Christmas party.
usage_notes: Implies a confrontational or conflicting encounter, not just a simple meeting ('magkatagpo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi maiiwasang **magkasagupa** ang magkaibang opinyon sa isang debate.","translation":"It's unavoidable for different opinions **to clash** in a debate."},{"sentence":"Sa finals, muling **nagkasagupa** ang dalawang higanteng koponan sa basketball.","translation":"In the finals, the two giant basketball teams **clashed** once again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sanhi ng gulo, kaguluhan, o pagkaantala; isang taong mahilig magsimula ng away o problema.
etymology: From `mang-` + `gugulo` (future tense of `gulo`, 'to cause trouble'). The noun form is derived from the actor-focus verb form for "one who will cause trouble."
original_explanation: That one person in the group chat who always starts a controversial topic. The younger sibling who bothers you while you're studying for an exam. The 'kontrabida' in your life's teleserye. They thrive in chaos.
usage_notes: Can refer to a person who is intentionally malicious or just playfully annoying. Not to be confused with the verb `manggulo` (to cause trouble).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging may isang **manggugulo** sa bawat klase.","translation":"There's always one **troublemaker** in every class."},{"sentence":"Paalisin ninyo ang mga **manggugulo** sa pagtitipon.","translation":"Get the **troublemakers** out of the gathering."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan kung saan ang isang bagay ay hindi sarado, may siwang, o malayang mapasok o makita ang loob.
original_explanation: The opposite of your bank account before payday. It's when the Jollibee is 'open 24 hours,' or when your friend's DMs are 'open for applications.' It means accessible, not closed, ready for business (or chismis).
usage_notes: Pronounced with stress on the second syllable (bu-KAS) to mean 'open'. Contrast with 'búkas' (tomorrow).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **bukas** ang pinto ng aming bahay para sa mga kaibigan.","translation":"The door to our house is always **open** for friends."},{"sentence":"**Bukas** na ba ang bagong kapihan sa kanto?","translation":"Is the new coffee shop on the corner **open** already?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang silid na bahagi ng isang bahay o gusali na inaalok upang rentahan o upahan ng ibang tao bilang tirahan.
etymology: Combination of 'kuwarto' (from Spanish 'cuarto', room) and 'paupahan' (from the root word 'upa', meaning rent).
original_explanation: A room for rent. The sign you see plastered on gates all over the university belt or near BPO hubs. It's the physical space where a 'kuwartero' or 'bedspacer' lives. Can range from a decent-sized room to a space just big enough for a mattress and a fan.
usage_notes: A compound noun describing a rental space.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng murang **kuwartong-paupahan** malapit sa kanyang trabaho.","translation":"She is looking for a cheap **room for rent** near her job."},{"sentence":"Puno na ang lahat ng **kuwartong-paupahan** sa boarding house na iyon.","translation":"All the **rooms for rent** in that boarding house are already full."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ukit o paghubog sa isang materyal, karaniwan ay kahoy o bato, gamit ang isang matalim na kasangkapan upang makabuo ng isang disenyo o anyo.
original_explanation: This is what artisans in Paete, Laguna do for a living. Imagine taking a boring block of wood and turning it into a majestic statue of a saint or a detailed miniature jeepney. It's the act of giving shape to something raw. Parang pag-shape mo sa future mo, kailangan ng focus, patience, at tamang tools. Kailangan mong lalikin ang pangarap mo.
usage_notes: The root word "lalik" refers to the act or the tool for carving. "Lalikin" is the command form. "Nilalik" is past tense, "nilalalik" is present tense, "lalalikin" is future tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan siyang **lalikin** ang isang estatwa mula sa puno ng narra.","translation":"He was ordered **to carve** a statue from the narra tree."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **lalikin** ang matigas na bato.","translation":"It is difficult **to carve** hard stone."}]

meaning_filipino: Palalimin ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay isang hukay, balon, o anumang butas sa lupa.
original_explanation: This is a deep cut, literally. It means to make something deeper. Think of it as the opposite of all the shallow people in your life. You're not just digging a hole for a septic tank; you're giving it depth and meaning. Very #Deep.
usage_notes: A very rare verb form. The more common way to express this is 'palalimin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **maglalin** ng balon para magkaroon ng sapat na tubig.","translation":"We need **to deepen** the well to have enough water."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **maglalin** pa ng pundasyon ng bahay.","translation":"They decided **to make** the house's foundation even **deeper**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o kalagayan na nagbibigay ng proteksyon, kalinga, at kapanatagan mula sa panganib o hirap.
etymology: From `kanlong`, an old word for shelter, with the `-an` suffix denoting a place. Likely related to `kalong` (to hold in one's lap).
original_explanation: Your kanlungan is your safe space. It could be your bedroom after a toxic day at work, your favorite coffee shop, or in the arms of your jowa (bf/gf). It's that place where you can finally exhale and say, "Hay, salamat." It's more than just a roof; it's a feeling of safety.
usage_notes: Has a more poetic and deep emotional connotation than just 'silungan' (shelter from rain/sun).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tahanan ay dapat maging **kanlungan** ng pamilya.","translation":"A home should be a **sanctuary** for the family."},{"sentence":"Sa bisig ng kaniyang ina, natagpuan niya ang **kanlungan**.","translation":"In his mother's arms, he found **refuge**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay-atensyon, pagpuna, o pagkilala sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: That feeling when your crush finally looks your way. That's `pagpansin`. It's the opposite of being 'seen-zoned.' It's being acknowledged, whether it's your new hair, your witty comment in the group chat, or the fact that you exist. The lack of it leads to the classic `hugot` line: 'Sana all napapansin.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Salamat sa iyong **pagpansin** sa aking bagong gupit.","translation":"Thank you for **noticing** my new haircut."},{"sentence":"Ang kulang sa **pagpansin** ay maaaring maging sanhi ng depresyon.","translation":"A lack of **attention** can be a cause of depression."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na pagpapaikli ng salitang "pare," na ginagamit bilang tawag sa isang kaibigang lalaki.
etymology: Pagpapaikli ng salitang "pare", na pinaikli rin mula sa "kumpare" (mula sa Espanyol na "compadre").
original_explanation: The go-to call sign for your male friends, barkada, or even the friendly kuya at the sari-sari store. It's the verbal equivalent of a friendly fist bump. 'Pre, anong balita?' is the official start of many 'tambay' sessions or inuman. It's the condensed, high-speed internet version of 'kumpare'.
usage_notes: Highly informal and common among male friends, but now used more broadly. The female equivalent is 'mare' or 'mars'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy **pre**, kamusta na? Tagal nating 'di nagkita!","translation":"Hey **bro**, how have you been? It's been a while since we saw each other!"},{"sentence":"Salamat sa tulong mo, **pre**.","translation":"Thanks for your help, **dude**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na pamatlig na tumutukoy sa isang lugar na malapit sa taong kinakausap. Ito ay katumbas ng 'diyan'.
etymology: Mula sa pinagsamang 'ang' at 'diyan', na naging 'andiyan' at pinaikli bilang 'andon'.
original_explanation: This is the less common, slightly more formal cousin of 'diyan'. It's like pointing at something near your friend and saying 'It's right **there** by you.' Think of it as the middle ground between 'dito' (here by me) and 'doon' (over yonder). Most people just say 'diyan' now, so using 'andon' gives you a slightly classic vibe.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'diyan' sa modernong pananalita, ngunit mas karaniwan ang 'diyan'. Ang 'andon' ay maaaring maging mas pormal o pampanitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilagay mo ang baso **andon** sa tabi mo.","translation":"Place the glass **there** beside you."},{"sentence":"**Andon** na pala sa iyo ang susi.","translation":"The key is already **there** with you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghimpil o pag-istasyon ng isang sasakyan sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: The ultimate test of a driver's skill, especially in a crowded Metro Manila mall parking lot. Finding a spot is like winning the lottery; actually parking the car without hitting anything is the championship round.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the act of parking a vehicle. The place is called 'paradahan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumarada** siya sa espasyong para lamang sa mga may kapansanan.","translation":"He **parked** in a space reserved only for persons with disabilities."},{"sentence":"Saan ba pwedeng **pumarada** dito?","translation":"Where can one **park** here?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal at pinaikling tawag sa kapatid o malapit na kaibigan, mula sa salitang 'utol'.
etymology: Pinaikling anyo ng 'utol', na baliktad na salita para sa 'kapatid' (naging 'putol' at pagkatapos ay 'utol').
original_explanation: A super-shortened, lazy way to call your 'utol' (sibling) or close friend. When "tol" or "utol" is too much effort to type. "Uy, ot, kamusta?" is peak texting efficiency.
usage_notes: Napakaimpormal at karaniwang ginagamit sa mga text message o kaswal na pag-uusap online.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ot**, pahiram naman ng charger mo.","translation":"**Bro**, can I borrow your charger?"},{"sentence":"Salamat sa tulong, **ot**!","translation":"Thanks for the help, **sis**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang itinakdang hangganan, petsa, oras, o gawain na kailangang sundin o tuparin. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa isang probisyon o tadhana.
original_explanation: That thing your professor, your boss, or even your significant other gives you. It's the boundary line you can't cross, the deadline you have to meet, the 'rules of the game'. Basically, it's the universe telling you, 'You can only go this far.'
usage_notes: Often seen in compound words like 'takdang-aralin' (homework) or 'takdang-oras' (deadline). The word 'takdang' by itself is a ligature of 'takda' + 'na'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **takda** ang lahat ng bagay sa mundo.","translation":"Everything in the world has a **limit**."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa **takda** ng batas, bawal iyon.","translation":"According to the **provision** of the law, that is forbidden."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso, sistema, o paraan ng paglalapat ng lunas; o ang lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang panggagamot, tulad ng isang klinika.
original_explanation: It can be the actual process of getting treated ('Mahirap ang gamutan para sa sakit niya') or the place where you get it, like a clinic ('Dalhin mo siya sa gamutan'). It's the whole medical journey, not just the pill.
usage_notes: This noun refers to the event, process, or location of treatment. The stress is on the last syllable: /ga-mu-TAN/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Libre ang paunang **gamutan** sa bagong bukas na health center.","translation":"The initial **medical treatment** is free at the newly opened health center."},{"sentence":"Matatagpuan ang **gamutan** ng bayan sa tabi ng munisipyo.","translation":"The town **clinic** is located beside the municipal hall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matinding pagwawasto, pagpuna, o pagsermon sa isang tao dahil sa maling nagawa.
original_explanation: This is a deep Tagalog word for a serious scolding. Imagine 'yung sermon ng nanay mo na umaabot hanggang sa kaluluwa mo. 'Yung tipong sinisingil ka sa lahat ng kasalanan mo mula pagkabata. It's not just a simple "pagsaway," it's a full-on, soul-crushing "I'm not mad, I'm just disappointed" speech.
usage_notes: A very formal and deep word, not used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya malimutan ang matinding **panunuat** ng kanyang ama.","translation":"He could not forget the severe **reprimand** from his father."},{"sentence":"Ang **panunuat** ng konsensya ay mas matindi kaysa sa galit ng iba.","translation":"The **upbraiding** of one's conscience is more severe than the anger of others."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtiklop o pag-ayos sa isang bagay, tulad ng damit o papel, upang maging mas maliit o mas maayos tingnan.
original_explanation: Your nanay's ultimate superpower. The act of transforming a mountain of freshly laundered clothes into neat, little squares. It's what you do to a letter before putting it in an envelope, or what you do to your "feelings" para 'di halata. The art of folding.
usage_notes: Primarily used for clothes, paper, and other flexible materials.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos maglaba, **tumupi** siya ng mga damit.","translation":"After doing the laundry, she **folded** the clothes."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **tinupi** ang sulat at inilagay sa kanyang bulsa.","translation":"He carefully **folded** the letter and put it in his pocket."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang utos o paalala na maging maingat upang maiwasan ang kapahamakan o panganib. Karaniwang ginagamit bilang pabaon sa pag-alis.
original_explanation: The official Filipino goodbye. It's not a real goodbye if you don't say 'Ingat ka!' It's a 3-in-1 package: 'I love you,' 'Don't die,' and 'Text me when you're home.' Can also be used as a warning, like when your friend is about to date a known 'f-boy' and you just say, 'Ingat ka diyan ha.'
usage_notes: Extremely common as a parting phrase. Often expanded to 'Mag-ingat ka' (You take care) or simply 'Ingat!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ingat** ka sa pag-uwi, gabi na.","translation":"**Be careful** on your way home, it's already late."},{"sentence":"Sige, una na ako. **Ingat**!","translation":"Okay, I'll go first. **Take care**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malakas at paulit-ulit na ingay na nalilikha ng pag-uumpugan o pagtama ng mga bagay, karaniwan ay yari sa metal.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'kalampag' (rattle, bang) at panlaping '-an'.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung sound effect kapag may multo sa Pinoy horror films. O 'yung ingay na ginagawa ng nanay mo sa kusina gamit ang mga kaldero para gisingin ka na. It's the sound of a jeepney needing a serious tune-up, or your neighbor deciding to do home repairs at 7 AM on a Sunday.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang partikular na uri ng maingay na tunog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig namin ang isang malakas na **kalampagan** mula sa kusina.","translation":"We heard a loud **clattering sound** from the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Ginising ako ng **kalampagan** ng mga construction worker sa labas.","translation":"The **banging** of the construction workers outside woke me up."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at bahagyang pagkinang o pag-ilaw, tulad ng maliliit na bituin o alitaptap.
original_explanation: Ito yung mas cute at mas maraming 'twinkle' kaysa sa 'kumutitap'. Isipin mo yung Christmas lights sa Ayala Triangle, o yung glitter sa makeup mo nung JS prom. It's not just sparkling, it's sparkling with *extra effort*.
usage_notes: Often used in poetry, songs, and descriptive writing to evoke a sense of wonder.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga alitaptap ay **kumukuti-kutitap** sa madilim na gabi.","translation":"The fireflies are **glimmering** in the dark night."},{"sentence":"Tila mga diyamanteng **kumukuti-kutitap** ang mga bituin sa kalangitan.","translation":"The stars in the sky seem like **sparkling** diamonds."}]

translation: to grant; to bestow; to award
meaning_filipino: Ibigay o ipagkatiwala ang isang bagay, karapatan, o biyaya sa isang tao bilang isang regalo o pagkilala.
original_explanation: This is a very formal, almost divine, "give." Hindi lang ito bigay, ito ay may kasamang ceremony at good vibes. This is what God gives you (blessings), what the fairy godmother gives Cinderella (a gown), or what the company gives you (a promotion, hopefully). "Sana ipagkaloob sa akin ang 13th month pay nang maaga."
usage_notes: Has a formal and often benevolent tone. Used for granting wishes, rights, awards, or blessings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawa'y **ipagkaloob** ng Diyos ang iyong mga panalangin.","translation":"May God **grant** your prayers."},{"sentence":"Ang parangal ay **ipinagkaloob** sa pinakamahusay na empleyado ng taon.","translation":"The award was **bestowed** upon the best employee of the year."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinagsama-samang presyo o importansya ng isang bagay o mga bagay; ang huling suma sa isang kalkulasyon ng gastos.
original_explanation: This is the final boss on your Shopee checkout page. It's the number that makes you think, 'Kailangan ko ba talaga 'to?' It's the 'grand total' that includes the item price, shipping fee, and any other 'patong' they can think of.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the total monetary value or cost.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano po ang **kabuuang halaga** ng lahat ng pinamili ko?","translation":"What is the **total amount** for all my purchases?"},{"sentence":"Ang **kabuuang halaga** ng pinsala ng bagyo ay umabot sa bilyun-bilyong piso.","translation":"The **total value** of the storm's damage reached billions of pesos."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katutubong pangkat mula sa Timog Cotabato, Mindanao na sinasabing namuhay nang hiwalay sa modernong sibilisasyon at nanirahan sa mga kuweba. Ang kanilang pagkatuklas noong 1971 ay naging kontrobersyal.
original_explanation: Remember that group project in Sibika/Hekasi about indigenous peoples? The Tasaday were the "stone-age" tribe discovered in the 70s living in caves, which later became a huge controversy—were they for real or was it all a hoax? They're the original "living off the grid" icons, way before it was cool.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang partikular na pangkat-etniko at sa kontrobersiyang bumabalot sa kanila.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan sa antropolohiya ang pamumuhay ng mga **Tasaday**.","translation":"The lifestyle of the **Tasaday** was studied in anthropology."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para sa isang patakaran o alituntunin; maaari ring tumukoy sa kabuuan ng organisasyon ng pulisya, bagaman ito ay isang lumang gamit.
original_explanation: This is the older, more Spanish-sounding version of 'pulisya'. It can mean the entire police organization, but more often these days it means 'policy' (like a company's HR policy). It’s a bit formal and less common now for 'police force', but you'll still hear it for 'policy'.
usage_notes: 'Pulisya' is now the standard term for the police force. 'Pulisiya' is more often used to mean 'policy', for which 'patakaran' is the more common Filipino term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa **pulisiya** ng kumpanya, bawal ang paggamit ng social media sa oras ng trabaho.","translation":"According to company **policy**, using social media during work hours is prohibited."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang **pulisiya** ay kailangan nang palitan.","translation":"The old **policy** needs to be replaced."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang titik o ponema na binibigkas nang may malayang daloy ng hangin mula sa mga baga na hindi nahaharangan sa bibig o lalamunan. Sa Filipino, ito ay ang a, e, i, o, u.
etymology: From pa- (instrumental prefix) + tinig (voice/sound), literally 'that which makes sound/voice'.
original_explanation: Remember grade school? A, E, I, O, U. That's it. That's the tweet. The five sounds that give life to all the chismis and hugot lines. Without **patinig**, we'd all just be mumbling consonants like we're beatboxing badly.
usage_notes: A fundamental linguistic term taught in primary school.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'mabuhay' ay may tatlong **patinig**.","translation":"The word 'mabuhay' has three **vowels**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kabilang sa parehong pamilya o angkan; kamag-anak.
etymology: From ka- (denoting relationship) + anak (child). Literally, "one of the same offspring/lineage".
original_explanation: The collective noun for your tito, tita, pinsan, lolo, and lola who will inevitably ask "May boyfriend/girlfriend ka na?" or "Kailan ka ikakasal?" at every family reunion. They are both your support system and your primary source of unsolicited advice.
usage_notes: A more general term for relative than 'kamag-anak', although they are largely synonymous.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating ang lahat ng kanyang mga **kaanak** para sa Pasko.","translation":"All of his **relatives** arrived for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang pamilya namin, marami kaming **kaanak** sa probinsya.","translation":"Our family is big, we have many **kin** in the province."}]

translation: to be blown by the wind; (figurative) to be spread as gossip
meaning_filipino: Literal na tangayin ng hangin; idyomatikong nangangahulugan na mabilis na kumalat ang isang balita o tsismis.
etymology: A phrase composed of `ilipad` (to be made to fly) + `ng` (by) + `hangin` (wind).
original_explanation: Literally, your laundry getting blown off the clothesline. Figuratively, it's how fast chismis spreads in the office. One person whispers something, and by lunchtime, parang **inilipad ng hangin** na ang balita sa buong floor. The original 'viral.'
usage_notes: Has both a literal and a very common idiomatic meaning. The context determines the interpretation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging usap-usapan agad ang kanilang pag-aaway, tila **inilipad ng hangin** ang balita.","translation":"Their fight immediately became the talk of the town, as if the news was **spread by the wind**."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka **ilipad ng hangin** ang mga sinampay mong damit.","translation":"Be careful or the clothes you hung out to dry might be **blown by the wind**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sobrang taba na naipon sa paligid ng tiyan at baywang.
original_explanation: Ah, the 'bilbil'. The sworn enemy of crop tops and tight shirts. It's the physical evidence of all the extra rice, milk tea, and lechon you "forgot" you ate. Your 'bilbil' is your constant companion that screams, "Remember that midnight snack? I do." Also known as "pundar ng quarantine."
usage_notes: Often used in a self-deprecating or humorous way when talking about weight gain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang mag-ehersisyo para mawala itong **bilbil** ko.","translation":"I need to exercise to get rid of these **love handles**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, 'yang **bilbil** ay simbolo lang ng masasarap na alaala.","translation":"Don't worry, those **love handles** are just a symbol of delicious memories."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na may talim na nakakabit sa isang hawakan, ginagamit sa paghiwa, pagtaga, o bilang sandata.
original_explanation: The kitchen tool that has major trust issues. Kailangan mo 'to para maghiwa ng sibuyas na magpapaiyak sa'yo, pero 'wag kang magkakamali dahil baka ikaw ang masaktan. Pwede ring pang-threat sa kapatid mong kinuha 'yung huling piraso ng fried chicken. Handle with care, both in the kitchen and in life.
usage_notes: A general term. Specific knives have more descriptive names (e.g., kutsilyong pangtinapay, kutsilyong pambalak).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa paggamit ng matalas na **kutsilyo**.","translation":"Be careful when using a sharp **knife**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **kutsilyo** para hiwain ang mangga.","translation":"I need a **knife** to slice the mango."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang trabaho ay mag-install at magkumpuni ng mga tubo, gripo, at iba pang kagamitan na may kinalaman sa daloy ng tubig at paagusan.
original_explanation: The superhero you call when your condo unit's sink is clogged or your shower drain is overflowing with... stuff you'd rather not identify. They're the masters of pipes, PVC, and that magical 'teflon tape'. You pay them not just for the labor, but for saving you from a plumbing apocalypse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumawag ka na ng **tubero**, bumabaha na sa banyo!","translation":"Call a **plumber** now, the bathroom is flooding!"},{"sentence":"Magaling ang **tubero** na kinuha namin; naayos niya agad ang tagas sa lababo.","translation":"The **plumber** we hired was good; he immediately fixed the leak in the sink."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang kasangkapang ginagamit sa pagsusulat, tulad ng pluma, lapis, o bolpen.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` ('gamit para sa') at ang salitang-ugat na `sulat` ('write'). Ang /s/ ng ugat ay nawala sa pagkakabitan ng unlapi.
original_explanation: Your trusty G-Tech or Pilot pen that you guard with your life. It's what you use to sign contracts, take down notes, or doodle when the Zoom meeting gets boring. The mightiest sword, according to your high school teacher.
usage_notes: Isang pangkalahatang termino para sa anumang pansulat, bagaman madalas itong tumukoy sa bolpen o pluma.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahiram naman ng **panulat**, naiwan ko kasi ang sa akin.","translation":"Can I borrow a **pen**, I left mine."},{"sentence":"Ginamit ni Jose Rizal ang kanyang **panulat** upang labanan ang mga mananakop.","translation":"Jose Rizal used his **pen** to fight the colonizers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtunaw ng metal at paghulma nito sa isang partikular na anyo sa pamamagitan ng molde.
original_explanation: This is the OG 3D printing. Before printers, there was just very, very hot liquid metal and a dream. Think of a panday (blacksmith) making a sword, pouring that glowing orange stuff into a mold. That's pagbubo. It's a bit more intense than pouring pancake batter.
usage_notes: This term is specific to metallurgy and foundry work.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap ang proseso ng **pagbubo** ng kampana para sa simbahan.","translation":"The process of **casting** the bell for the church is difficult."},{"sentence":"Ang galing ng panday sa **pagbubo** ng mga palamuti.","translation":"The blacksmith is skilled in the **founding** of ornaments."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakihang sagupaan o digmaan; maaari ding tumukoy sa pook kung saan naganap ang sagupaan.
original_explanation: This isn't just a fistfight; this is war. Think historical events like the Battle of Mactan ('Labanan sa Mactan'). It can also be the place of battle, like how the kitchen becomes a 'labanan' during Noche Buena preparations. The stress on the last syllable often distinguishes it from the verb form.
usage_notes: Ang pagbigkas na may diin sa huling pantig (/la-ba-NAN/) ay karaniwang tumutukoy sa pangngalan na 'battle' o 'battlefield', habang ang pandiwa ay binibigkas na /la-BA-nan/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Labanan sa Mactan ay isang makasaysayang **labanan**.","translation":"The Battle of Mactan is a historic **battle**."}]

translation: to hack or chop repeatedly with a bolo
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na paggamit ng itak o bolo sa pagputol o paghiwa ng isang bagay, karaniwan nang may puwersa.
etymology: From mag- + pan- (instrumental prefix) + taga (to chop). The 'pan-' prefix suggests using a tool for the action.
original_explanation: Imagine a provincial tito clearing a path in the jungle, or someone getting really, REALLY angry at a coconut. That's 'magpanaga'. It's not just one clean slice; it's a series of powerful, hacking motions. The verb form of 'Hulk, smash!' but with a bolo knife.
usage_notes: The prefix 'pan-' often implies the use of a tool for the action of the root word. Here, 'taga' (chop) is done with an implied tool (like a bolo or machete).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan niyang **magpanaga** ng maraming panggatong para sa pagluluto.","translation":"He needs to **chop** a lot of firewood for cooking."},{"sentence":"Nag-init ang ulo ng lalaki at bigla na lang **nagpanaga** ng puno ng saging.","translation":"The man got angry and suddenly just **started hacking a banana tree**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ikulong o ipasok sa isang bilangguan o piitan.
original_explanation: When you do something so wrong, the authorities decide your new address is Bilibid. It's the ultimate 'grounded' for adults. 'I-cancel na natin 'yan!' but legally binding.
usage_notes: This is the command/infinitive form of the verb. The root word 'bilanggo' means prisoner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang hukom na **ibilanggo** ang korap na politiko.","translation":"The judge decided to **imprison** the corrupt politician."},{"sentence":"Huwag ninyong **ibilanggo** ang isang taong walang kasalanan.","translation":"Do not **imprison** a person who is innocent."}]

meaning_filipino: Hayaang mawala o hindi na mahanap ang isang bagay, sinasadya man o hindi.
original_explanation: The more common cousin of 'iwaglit'. This is your go-to word for losing things. "Naiwala ko ang wallet ko!" is a national crisis. It can be accidental, but it can also be intentional, like when you "lose" your ex's number. "Bes, iwala mo na 'yung resibo, baka makita pa ni Misis." It's the universal verb for when something is present, and then suddenly, it's not.
usage_notes: Very common. The prefix `ma-` (`mawala`) is used when something gets lost on its own (intransitive), while `i-` (`iwala`) is used when someone loses something (transitive).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **iwala** ang tiwala na ibinigay ko sa iyo.","translation":"Don't **lose** the trust I gave you."},{"sentence":"Paano mo nalamang **iniwala** ko ang mga susi?","translation":"How did you know that I **lost** the keys?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtataksil sa isang tao, pangkat, o prinsipyo na pinagkakatiwalaan.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable `li-` + `lilo` (traitorous).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sana di na lang kita nakilala' moment. This is what you feel when your best friend eats the last piece of your favorite pizza or, on a more serious note, when someone you trusted stabs you in the back. It's the plot of every teleserye's third act. A classic 'Et tu, Brute?' moment, Pinoy-style.
usage_notes: A very strong and formal word for betrayal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglililo** ni Hudas kay Hesus ay isa sa mga pinakatanyag na kuwento ng pagtataksil.","translation":"The **betrayal** of Jesus by Judas is one of the most famous stories of treachery."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya matanggap ang **paglililo** ng kanyang pinakamatalik na kaibigan.","translation":"She could not accept the **betrayal** of her best friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaloy o paglabas ng likido o anumang bagay mula sa isang sisidlan na may butas, siwang, o sira.
original_explanation: Parang gripo na sira, may **tumagas** na tubig. Or 'yung chismis na sinabi mo sa 'best friend' mo, biglang **tumagas** sa buong office. It's when something that's supposed to stay inside, gets out. Like a secret, or oil from a badly sealed container of adobo.
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense). The infinitive is 'tumagas', the progressive is 'tumatagas', and the contemplative is 'tatagas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumagas** ang langis mula sa makina ng sasakyan.","translation":"Oil **leaked** from the car's engine."},{"sentence":"May **tumagas** na impormasyon tungkol sa sikretong proyekto.","translation":"Information about the secret project **leaked**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-aaliw sa sarili o sa iba upang magdulot ng kasiyahan at mapawi ang pagkabagot.
original_explanation: Your 'me time' activity. Whether it's scrolling through TikTok for hours, binge-watching a K-drama, or playing Mobile Legends until 3 AM. It's your personal stress reliever, your way of distracting yourself from adulting.
usage_notes: Refers to the act of amusing oneself or others.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagbabasa ng libro ang kanyang paboritong **paglibang**.","translation":"Reading books is her favorite **pastime**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng lahat ang kaunting **paglibang** upang mabawasan ang stress.","translation":"Everyone needs a little **recreation** to reduce stress."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagnanais na ang lahat ng bagay ay maging ganap, walang mali, at nasa pinakamataas na antas ng kalidad; o tumutukoy sa katangian ng pagiging ganito.
original_explanation: That one friend who aligns all the items on the table, color-codes their notes, and has a mini-breakdown if the PowerPoint font is not consistent. They're the reason the group project gets an A+, but also the reason everyone else is running on coffee and 2 hours of sleep. It's a 'blessing and a curse,' as they'd say while re-doing your work.
usage_notes: A very common English loanword used in both Tagalog and English contexts in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyado siyang **perfectionist**, kaya inabot kami ng madaling araw sa pag-eensayo.","translation":"She's too much of a **perfectionist**, that's why our practice lasted until dawn."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala sa maliliit na detalye, hindi mo kailangang maging **perfectionist** palagi.","translation":"Don't worry about the small details, you don't always have to be a **perfectionist**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang may pinakamataas na antas ng kahigpitan, sa paraang literal (pisikal) o metaporikal (patakaran).
original_explanation: This is your terror prof from college, the security guard at a high-end village, or your mom's curfew rules when you were a teenager. It's the tightest grip, the strictest policy, the 'no exceptions' rule. Yung **pinakamahigpit** na yakap is also the best, though.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical tightness (e.g., a knot, a hug) or figuratively for rules and regulations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinatutupad sa paaralang ito ang **pinakamahigpit** na patakaran laban sa pandaraya.","translation":"This school implements the **strictest** policy against cheating."},{"sentence":"Ibigay mo sa akin ang **pinakamahigpit** mong yakap.","translation":"Give me your **tightest** hug."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na nangangahulugang magsanay o tumugtog ng musika nang impormal kasama ang ibang musikero.
original_explanation: What you and your barkada do with a guitar, a beat-up cajon, and a case of beer. It's less about a perfect performance and more about the 'feels.' The soundtrack to your inuman session, featuring off-key singing and pure, unadulterated fun.
usage_notes: The act is often called 'jamming'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-**jam** tayo mamaya sa bahay, dala ka ng gitara.","translation":"Let's **jam** at the house later, bring a guitar."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko silang nagja-**jam** sa music room.","translation":"I heard them **jamming** in the music room."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagkawala ng malay o pangingisay ng katawan, na kadalasang sanhi ng sakit, takot, o matinding emosyon.
original_explanation: That moment in a cheap horror movie when the character sees the ghost and just collapses. Or when someone sees their celebrity crush in person and literally can't even. It's the body's emergency shutdown switch when things get too intense.
usage_notes: An old term. 'Pagkahimatay' is much more common for fainting. 'Paghikit' can also specifically refer to convulsions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang matinding takot ay nagdulot ng kanyang **paghikit**.","translation":"Her intense fear caused her to **faint**."},{"sentence":"Isinugod sa ospital ang bata dahil sa lagnat at **paghikit**.","translation":"The child was rushed to the hospital due to fever and **convulsions**."}]

translation: to have pity; to feel compassion
meaning_filipino: Ang makaramdam ng awa o habag para sa isang tao o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when you see a stray kitten in the rain or when your friend tells you their sad `hugot` story for the nth time. It's that "aww, kawawa naman" feeling in your chest. It's empathy level 100. It's the verb form of being a `marupok` (fragile/soft-hearted) for someone's plight.
usage_notes: A verb expressing an emotional state. Often used with 'sa' to indicate the object of pity (e.g., `mahabag sa kanya`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ba ang hindi **mahahabag** sa kalagayan ng mga nasalanta ng bagyo?","translation":"Who wouldn't **feel pity** for the situation of the typhoon victims?"},{"sentence":"**Nahabag** ako sa pulubi kaya binigyan ko siya ng pagkain.","translation":"I **felt compassion** for the beggar so I gave him food."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsusubok na gawin o makamit ang isang bagay, na maaaring magtagumpay o mabigo.
original_explanation: This is your 'susubukan ko' or 'bahala na si Batman' moment. It's the effort you put in, whether it's trying to cook a new recipe from a TikTok video, attempting to pass a killer exam, or even that awkward attempt to slide into someone's DMs. The result isn't guaranteed, but you gave it a shot.
usage_notes: Can be used for both positive and negative attempts (e.g., pagtatangkang tumakas - an attempt to escape).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagtatangka** na akyatin ang bundok ay naging matagumpay.","translation":"His **attempt** to climb the mountain was successful."},{"sentence":"Nabigo ang kanyang **pagtatangka** na dayain ang pagsusulit.","translation":"His **attempt** to cheat on the exam failed."}]

translation: to struggle with; to fight for a cause
meaning_filipino: Ang pakikilahok sa isang laban o pakikipagtunggali, karaniwang para sa isang layunin, prinsipyo, o upang malampasan ang isang malaking hamon.
etymology: From `maki-` (social prefix) + `pag-` (action prefix) + `baka` (fight, struggle). Note: `baka` here is an old word for fight, not the more common `baka` meaning 'maybe' or 'cow'.
original_explanation: This isn't your petty `makipag-away`. `Makipagbaka` is fighting the good fight. It's you and your comrades struggling against a system, an injustice, or even a disease. It has a noble, almost epic, feel to it. Think Katipuneros, activists fighting for a cause, or the whole team trying to beat a deadline from hell. It’s a collective struggle with a purpose.
usage_notes: Carries a more formal and serious tone than 'makipag-away'. It often refers to a struggle for a cause or against a significant adversary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Handa silang **makipagbaka** para sa kalayaan ng bayan.","translation":"They are ready **to fight for** the country's freedom."},{"sentence":"Araw-araw siyang nakikipagbaka sa kanyang karamdaman.","translation":"Every day she **struggles with** her illness."}]

translation: to grow; to sprout; to earn interest
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglaki o pagsibol mula sa lupa (para sa halaman); ang paglitaw sa balat (tulad ng tigyawat); o ang pagkakaroon ng dagdag na halaga mula sa puhunan (interes).
original_explanation: Three main uses: 1) What a plant does. 2) What a pimple does on your face right before a big date. 3) What your money in the bank is *supposed* to do, but at 0.01% interest, good luck with that. It's the universe's way of saying "something new has appeared here."
usage_notes: This word has multiple related meanings: botanical growth, skin blemishes, and financial interest. The context is key. This is the completed aspect (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumubo** na ang mga butong itinanim ko.","translation":"The seeds I planted have **sprouted**."},{"sentence":"**Tumubo** ang pera niya sa bangko dahil sa interes.","translation":"His money in the bank **grew** because of interest."},{"sentence":"May **tumubo** na tigyawat sa ilong ko.","translation":"A pimple **grew** on my nose."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsagawa ng isang pormal na pagdiriwang para sa ikalabing-walong kaarawan ng isang babae, na sumisimbolo sa kanyang pagpasok sa pagiging dalaga.
original_explanation: The ultimate coming-of-age party for a Pinay at 18. It’s the one night you get to be a princess, complete with 18 roses, 18 candles, and 18... bills to pay for the whole event. The goal is to make all your high school frenemies jealous on Instagram.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a girl's 18th birthday celebration in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iipon ang kanyang mga magulang para makapaghanda kapag siya ay **magde-debu** na.","translation":"Her parents are saving up to prepare for when she will **have her debut party**."},{"sentence":"Sino-sino ang imbitado sa 18 roses mo kapag **nagdebu** ka?","translation":"Who are invited to your 18 roses when you **have your debut party**?"}]

translation: to deliver; to hand over; to submit
meaning_filipino: Ang paghahatid o pagbibigay ng isang bagay sa kinauukulang tao o lugar; ang pagsusumite ng isang gawain o dokumento.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Espanyol na 'entregar' (to deliver) at nilapian ng unlaping `mag-`.
original_explanation: The official verb of Shopee, Lazada, and Grab riders. "Kuya, pa-wait, bababa na po para kunin!" It's also what you do with your project requirements right before the "due date." From packages to papers, it’s all about getting something from point A to point B (or B's hand).
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang salita sa komersiyo, lohistika, at sa akademya o opisina.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi ng rider, **mag-eentrega** siya ng parcel mamayang hapon.","translation":"The rider said he **will deliver** a parcel this afternoon."},{"sentence":"Kailangan na nating **mag-entrega** ng ating pinal na proyekto bukas.","translation":"We need to **submit** our final project tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na mayroong bitbit o dala-dalang anuman. Sa kontekstong medikal, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang taong nagdadala ng sakit o kondisyon.
etymology: Compound of 'may' (has/have) and 'dala' (carry/bring). Often written as two words, 'may dala'.
original_explanation: Like when you show up to a party and someone asks, 'Sino'ng maydala ng ice?' (Who's the one carrying the ice?). It's the person assigned to bring something. It's also that feeling when you're pregnant: 'Nagdadalang-tao.' In a more serious, 'di-masayang-usapan' context, it can be a 'carrier' of a disease.
usage_notes: Can be written as two words, 'may dala,' which is more common. 'Maydala' as one word can feel a bit more formal or literary, or imply a more permanent state of being a carrier.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat bisita ay **maydala** ng pagkain para sa salu-salo.","translation":"Each guest was **carrying** food for the potluck."},{"sentence":"Siya ay isang **maydala** ng pambihirang gene.","translation":"She is a **carrier** of a rare gene."}]

translation: To be possessed (by a spirit); to be joined by
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpasok ng isang espiritu sa katawan ng isang tao; ang pagsama o pakikipag-isa sa isang grupo o damdamin.
etymology: From the root word 'sanib', meaning 'to join' or 'to overlap'.
original_explanation: The OG 'group project.' It can be spooky, like when a spirit decides your body is a good place to crash (possession), or it can be motivational, like when you're joined by inspiration. Either way, you're no longer acting alone. Think Shake, Rattle & Roll or getting a sudden burst of 'sipag'.
usage_notes: The 'possession' meaning is common in folklore and horror. The 'joining' meaning can also be used for emotions or ideas, e.g., 'saniban ka sana ng sipag' (may diligence possess you).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinasabing **sinaniban** ng masamang espiritu ang babae kaya siya nagwawala.","translation":"They say the woman **was possessed** by an evil spirit, which is why she's running amok."},{"sentence":"Nawa'y **saniban** ka ng kasipagan ngayong Lunes.","translation":"May you **be joined by** diligence this Monday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hukay o malalim na bahagi sa lupa o daan, karaniwang sanhi ng pagkasira o pagguho.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *lə(m)bak na nangangahulugang 'lambak' o 'libis'.
original_explanation: Yan yung mga surprise na hukay sa kalsada na dahilan kung bakit napapamura ka habang nagda-drive. Parang life lang, puno ng unexpected 'labak' na kailangan mong iwasan para hindi masira ang 'gulong' ng buhay mo.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga hindi pantay na kalsada. Ang mas karaniwang anyo nito na nagpapahiwatig ng karamihan ay 'labak-labak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat sa pagmamaneho, may malaking **labak** sa kanto.","translation":"Be careful driving, there's a big **pothole** at the corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na pag-aari ng iba at sapilitang pinaglilingkod nang walang kabayaran, kalayaan, o karapatan.
original_explanation: Before 'corporate slave' was a thing, there was the OG **alipin**. Today, it's what you call yourself when you have 3 deadlines, 2 bosses, and 1 remaining brain cell. 'Alipin ng sistema.'
usage_notes: Sa kasaysayan ng Pilipinas, may iba't ibang antas nito tulad ng 'aliping namamahay' at 'aliping saguiguilid'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sinaunang lipunan, may mga taong nabubuhay bilang **alipin**.","translation":"In ancient society, there were people who lived as **slaves**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang pa-**alipin** sa masamang bisyo.","translation":"Don't be a **slave** to a bad habit."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkalahatang pagtaas ng presyo ng mga bilihin at serbisyo sa isang ekonomiya sa loob ng isang tiyak na panahon, na nagreresulta sa pagbaba ng halaga ng pera.
original_explanation: Ito yung dahilan kung bakit yung P1000 mo, parang P100 na lang 'pag nag-grocery ka. Dati, yung bente pesos mo may sukli pa sa jeep, ngayon kulang pa. Implasyon is the economic ghost that haunts your wallet and makes everything more expensive.
usage_notes: Isang terminong pang-ekonomiya na naging pang-araw-araw na salita dahil sa epekto nito sa lahat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ramdam na ramdam ng mga mamamayan ang epekto ng mataas na **implasyon**.","translation":"The citizens can really feel the effect of high **inflation**."},{"sentence":"Tumaas na naman ang presyo ng gasolina dahil sa **implasyon**.","translation":"The price of gasoline has increased again due to **inflation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng magaang riple na may mas maikling bariles kaysa sa karaniwang riple.
original_explanation: A type of gun. You'll probably only hear this word in old action movies, news reports about military hardware, or maybe in a game of Call of Duty with your lolo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga sundalo ay sinanay gumamit ng M4 **karbin**.","translation":"The soldiers were trained to use the M4 **carbine**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang walang likuan, pag-aalinlangan, o paghinto; tuwiran.
original_explanation: How you're supposed to walk home after curfew (pero hindi nangyayari). How you answer your boss when they ask if you're finished ('Yes, po!') even if you're not. It's moving from Point A to Point B without any side trips to the milk tea shop.
usage_notes: Nagsasaad ng kilos o galaw na walang paglihis o paghinto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula rito, maglakad ka lang nang **diretso**.","translation":"From here, just walk **straight**."},{"sentence":"Umuwi ka nang **diretso** pagkatapos ng klase.","translation":"Go home **directly** after class."}]

translation: to be stretched; to be pulled; to be strained (muscle)
meaning_filipino: Mahila o maunat nang may puwersa; magkaroon ng pulikat o paninigas ng kalamnan dahil sa labis na paggamit.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your muscles after your first day back at the gym ('nabatak ang muscles'). It's also what you do to a rubber band. Figuratively, it's when you 'pull' or 'recruit' a friend to join your get-rich-quick scheme or ML team. 'Tara, batakin natin si Kumpare!'
usage_notes: Can refer to physical stretching/pulling or muscle strain. In slang, 'batakin' means to recruit or pull someone into an activity. The root 'batak' can also be an adjective meaning well-built or muscular.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-warm up siya nang mabuti para hindi **mabatak** ang kanyang mga kalamnan.","translation":"He warmed up well so his muscles wouldn't **get strained**."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **mabatak** ang lubid para tumuwid ito.","translation":"The rope needs **to be pulled** taut to straighten it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa mga kaganapan, pangyayari, o kung ano ang bago sa buhay ng isang tao.
etymology: From 'ganap' (event/role) + '-s' (a common slang suffix in Filipino).
original_explanation: The Gen Z and Millennial way of asking 'What's the tea?' or 'What's happening?' It’s a catch-all for events, updates, gossip, or plans. 'Ano'ng **ganaps** sa weekend?' (What's happening this weekend?). It's 'ganap' (event) but with a zesty '-s' to make it sound more chic and less like a formal announcement.
usage_notes: Highly informal and used in casual conversations, especially among younger people and on social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, ano'ng **ganaps**? Tagal nating 'di nagkita!","translation":"Hey, what's up? It's been a while since we last saw each other!"},{"sentence":"I-update mo ako sa mga **ganaps** sa opisina habang naka-leave ako.","translation":"Update me on the **happenings** at the office while I'm on leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Maglabas o magbigay ng liwanag; magliwanag o kuminang.
original_explanation: The sun peeking through the clouds after a downpour. The glow of your phone screen in a dark room at 3 AM. Figuratively, it’s that moment of hope or a brilliant idea that suddenly appears. It's when your crush finally smiles at you and the whole world seems to get brighter. Parang may slow-mo effect at background music.
usage_notes: Often used poetically for light, hope, or beauty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Suminag** ang araw pagkatapos ng malakas na ulan.","translation":"The sun **shone** after the heavy rain."},{"sentence":"**Suminag** ang pag-asa sa kanyang mga mata.","translation":"Hope **radiated** from his/her eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may espesyal na kasanayan at kaalaman sa isang partikular na teknikal na larangan, lalo na sa pag-aayos at pagpapanatili ng mga makinarya o kagamitan.
original_explanation: The hero you call when your WiFi dies in the middle of a crucial Netflix episode or a WFH meeting. They speak a different language made of jargon like 'router configuration' and 'LAN cable' but ultimately, they are the saviors of our digital lives.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumawag ka na ba ng **tekniko** para ayusin ang aircon?","translation":"Have you called a **technician** to fix the aircon?"},{"sentence":"Ang **tekniko** mula sa internet provider ay darating bukas.","translation":"The **technician** from the internet provider will arrive tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling na may sumama sa isang tao bilang kasama, gabay, o bantay.
original_explanation: When your mom won't let you go out alone at night, she'll tell your kuya, "**Pasamahan** mo ang kapatid mo!" It's the official Filipino "buddy system" command. You're not just asking someone to go *with* you, you're asking a third party to *make* someone accompany another.
usage_notes: The 'pa-' prefix indicates a request, and the '-an' suffix indicates the person to be accompanied.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ina, maaari po bang **pasamahan** ninyo ako kay kuya papuntang palengke?","translation":"Mother, could you please **have** big brother **accompany** me to the market?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na katumbas ng siyam na sampu; ang kardinal na bilang na kasunod ng 89 at sinusundan ng 91.
etymology: A lexicalized contraction of 'siyam na pu', where 'pu' is from 'sampu' (ten).
original_explanation: The number 90. The grade you're aiming for to make your parents proud. Also, Lolo's age when he can still beat you at chess and drink a beer. 'Wow, 90! Siyamnapu na pala si Lolo!'
usage_notes: This is the standard and most common way to say 'ninety' in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lola ko ay magdiriwang ng kanyang ika-**siyamnapu** na kaarawan.","translation":"My grandmother will celebrate her **ninetieth** birthday."},{"sentence":"Mayroong **siyamnapu**'t siyam na porsyentong tsansa na umulan bukas.","translation":"There is a ninety-nine percent chance of rain tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na ekspresyon na nangangahulugang "naiintindihan ko na" o "hindi mo na kailangang magpaliwanag pa," na nagpapahiwatig ng agarang pag-unawa at pagsang-ayon.
etymology: Direct borrowing from American English slang "say less."
original_explanation: The ultimate Gen Z response that means "I get it, you don't need to explain further, I'm already on board." When your friend says "Tara, milk tea?", you just reply, "Sayless." It's the verbal equivalent of a nod and a thumbs-up, saving everyone precious seconds.
usage_notes: Used in very informal, conversational settings, especially among younger Filipinos. Often seen in chats and social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Gusto mo bang sumama sa beach?\" \"**Sayless**, game ako!\"","translation":"\"Do you want to come to the beach?\" \"**Say less**, I'm game!\""}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtalon o pag-angat mula sa isang ibabaw gamit ang puwersa ng mga binti at paa.
original_explanation: The thing you do when you see a cockroach, hear good news about your 13th-month pay, or when you're trying to look taller in a group picture. It's a more forceful, energetic jump than 'talon'. It’s the 'Yehey!' of body language.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (a jump) or a verb (to jump). 'Talon' is a general jump, 'lundag' often implies more height or energy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **lundag** ang ginawa ng bata nang makita ang regalo.","translation":"The child gave a powerful **jump** when they saw the gift."},{"sentence":"**Lundag** tayo sa Bagong Taon para tumangkad!","translation":"Let's **jump** on New Year's to get taller!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakalat ng mga buto o binhi sa lupa upang tumubo. Metaporikal na ginagamit sa pagpapalaganap ng ideya, damdamin, o balita.
original_explanation: What a farmer does with seeds. What a 'chismosa' does with gossip. This verb is all about spreading something far and wide. You can 'maghasik ng kabutihan' (sow kindness) or 'maghasik ng lagim' (sow terror), like in a horror movie. It has a very dramatic, almost biblical feel to it.
usage_notes: Often used in figurative and literary contexts (e.g., to sow fear, discord, or kindness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng terorista ay **maghasik** ng takot sa mga tao.","translation":"The terrorist's goal is to **sow** fear among the people."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang mga magsasaka na **maghasik** ng palay para sa susunod na anihan.","translation":"The farmers have started to **sow** rice seeds for the next harvest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pamunuan o dominahin ang isang lugar, grupo, o sitwasyon na parang isang hari; ang magkaroon ng ganap na kapangyarihan o kontrol.
original_explanation: This is what a king does to his kingdom. But in modern terms, it's what you do when you top the board exams, what a champion team does in a sports league, or what your Bida-Kontrabida inner voice does when you're trying to decide whether to eat more rice. It's to reign supreme over a domain, literal or metaphorical.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix indicates the place or domain being ruled. Can be used literally for kingdoms or metaphorically for emotions, situations, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **pagharian** ka ng iyong takot.","translation":"Don't let your fear **rule over** you."},{"sentence":"Matagal na panahon niyang pinangarap na **pagharian** ang kanilang kaharian.","translation":"For a long time, he dreamed of **ruling over** their kingdom."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kardinal na bilang na kasunod ng labinlima at bago ang labimpito, na isinusulat bilang 16.
original_explanation: Sweet sixteen! The age of debuts (for some), getting your student driver's permit in other countries, and feeling like you're an adult but your parents still treat you like a kid. "Debut na ni Ana, **labing-anim** na siya."
usage_notes: Ang pormang may gitling na `labing-anim` ay karaniwan, ngunit ang `labing-anim` ay malawak ding ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Labing-anim** na taon na siyang nagtatrabaho sa kumpanyang iyon.","translation":"He has been working at that company for **sixteen** years."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nag-uudyok o naghihikayat sa isang tao na kumilos o magsumikap, karaniwan ay isang gantimpala o pabuya.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung 'paramdam' ng boss mo para ganahan kang mag-trabaho. 'Yung extra cash, gift certificate, o pizza party kapag na-hit ang target. Sa BPO, ito 'yung pinaka-aabangan na 'spiff'. Basically, the 'what's in it for me?' part of any deal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-alok ang kumpanya ng malaking **insentibo** para sa mga empleyadong makakapagpapasok ng bagong kliyente.","translation":"The company offered a large **incentive** for employees who could bring in new clients."},{"sentence":"Ang 13th month pay ay nagsisilbing **insentibo** sa mga manggagawa na magpatuloy sa kanilang trabaho.","translation":"The 13th month pay serves as an **incentive** for workers to continue with their jobs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bag na gawa sa tela o ibang materyales na maaaring gamitin nang paulit-ulit bilang alternatibo sa mga plastik na supot, upang makatulong sa pangangalaga sa kalikasan.
original_explanation: The official "Tita" starter pack item. You probably have 50 of these folded up inside another, bigger eco bag. It's your badge of honor at the grocery, showing everyone you're a responsible adult who remembers to save the turtles... and also save 2 pesos for not needing a plastic bag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dala mo ba ang **eco bag**? Bawal na ang plastik sa palengke.","translation":"Did you bring the **eco bag**? Plastic is no longer allowed at the market."},{"sentence":"Laging may nakatuping **eco bag** sa loob ng backpack ko para sa biglaang pamimili.","translation":"I always have a folded **reusable bag** inside my backpack for impromptu shopping."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakatayo nang tuwid at matatag, o pagiging nakatusok sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Think of candles for a birthday cake. They are 'nakatirik' on the icing. Or a flag on a pole. Or that BBQ stick that's 'nakatirik' sa isang pirasong hotdog. It's standing straight and proud.
usage_notes: Refers to an object being placed in an upright position, often by piercing a surface.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang kandila ang **nakatirik** sa gitna ng mesa.","translation":"A candle was **standing upright** in the middle of the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalagay o naglalathala ng mensahe, larawan, o video sa isang social media platform o online forum.
original_explanation: When you see your friend going through something, and instead of talking to you, they're just nagpopost of cryptic song lyrics on their IG story. It's the modern way of expressing yourself, asking for validation, or just plain humble-bragging. "Flex ko lang po..."
usage_notes: A Tagalized verb from English. Present progressive tense, indicating an ongoing or habitual action of posting online.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **nagpopost** si Anna ng mga litrato ng kanyang mga pusa sa Facebook.","translation":"Anna is always **posting** pictures of her cats on Facebook."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka **nagpopost** ng ganyan? Baka magalit ang boss mo.","translation":"Why **are you posting** that? Your boss might get angry."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi buo, kulang, o hindi pa lubos na natatapos o nangyayari.
original_explanation: The feeling of "may kulang pa." It's an unfinished project, a love story that's "almost" but not quite, or your sweldo after all the bills are paid. In grammar, it's the imperfect tense (aspektong di-ganap), actions that are still ongoing. It’s the state of being a work-in-progress.
usage_notes: Can refer to things, situations, or even grammatical tenses (aspektong di-ganap).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang kaligayahan ay **di-ganap** dahil malayo siya sa pamilya.","translation":"His happiness is **incomplete** because he is far from his family."},{"sentence":"Nasa aspektong **di-ganap** ang pandiwang 'kumakain'.","translation":"The verb 'kumakain' (eating) is in the **imperfect** tense."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagwawakas o pagtatapos ng isang gawain, pangyayari, o panahon. Maaari rin itong gamitin bilang pang-ugnay na nangangahulugang 'pagkatapos ng'.
original_explanation: This is the 'sana all' of tasks. When you finally submit that report after three coffee-fueled all-nighters. Also used like 'after,' as in 'Matapos kang i-seen, 'di na siya nag-reply.' (After they left you on seen, they never replied.)
usage_notes: Can function as a verb (to finish) or a conjunction (after). The stress on the second syllable /ma-TA-pos/ is crucial for the verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **matapos** ang trabaho bago mag-bakasyon.","translation":"I need to **finish** the work before going on vacation."},{"sentence":"**Matapos** ang ulan, lumabas ang bahaghari.","translation":"**After** the rain, the rainbow appeared."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon ng mga taong dati nang magkakasama, tulad ng pamilya, magkakamag-anak, o magkakaklase, na muling nagsama-sama pagkatapos ng mahabang panahon.
original_explanation: That yearly (or every 5 years) event where you meet relatives you only see during Christmas and funerals, or high school classmates who are now either super successful or still look exactly the same. It's a festival of "Uy, tumaba ka!" and endless picture-taking. The main event is usually the food and the chismis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkakaroon ng malaking **reunyon** ang aming pamilya sa darating na Pasko.","translation":"Our family will have a big **reunion** this coming Christmas."},{"sentence":"Excited na ako para sa aming high school grand alumni **reunyon**.","translation":"I'm excited for our high school grand alumni **reunion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isdang-alat na karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga bahura, kilala sa masarap nitong laman at mataas na halaga sa pamilihan.
original_explanation: This is what the hero becomes at the dinner table. The **lapulapo** is the sosyal fish you order at a fancy seafood restaurant, usually steamed with soy sauce and ginger. Its price on the menu can give you a mini heart attack, but it's so good, you'll probably say 'Worth it!'
usage_notes: Refers to various species of fish in the grouper family. A popular dish is 'escabeche,' which is sweet and sour fish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkano ang isang kilo ng sariwang **lapulapo** sa palengke?","translation":"How much is one kilo of fresh **grouper** at the market?"},{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong luto sa **lapulapo** ay sweet and sour.","translation":"My favorite way to cook **grouper** is sweet and sour."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip na ginagamit sa pagtatanong upang tukuyin ang isa o higit pa mula sa isang pangkat ng mga tao, bagay, o ideya.
original_explanation: The ultimate "pili ka" question starter. "Alin ang mas bet mo, Jollibee o McDo?" is a question that can make or break friendships. It's the word you use when you're presented with options, like choosing which milk tea flavor to get.
usage_notes: Used to ask "which" when there is a choice between two or more items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Alin** sa mga ito ang gusto mo?","translation":"**Which** of these do you want?"},{"sentence":"Hindi ko alam kung **alin** ang dapat kong piliin.","translation":"I don't know **which** one I should choose."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagluto ng pagkain sa ibabaw ng nagbabagang uling o direktang apoy. Ito ang nakaraang anyo ng pandiwang "mag-ihaw".
original_explanation: The official scent of a Filipino weekend or celebration. When you smell that smoky aroma, you know someone **nag-ihaw** of liempo, isaw, or pork BBQ. It's the signal that a party, or at least a really good-smelling Tuesday afternoon, is happening.
usage_notes: Past tense of 'mag-ihaw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nag-ihaw** kami ng isda sa tabing-dagat.","translation":"We **grilled** fish by the seashore."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nag-ihaw** ng masarap na barbecue na ito?","translation":"Who **barbecued** this delicious barbecue?"}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing mas malalim ang isang bagay, tulad ng butas, ilog, o pag-unawa.
original_explanation: Ito yung sinasabi ng prof mo sa thesis defense: "Laliman mo pa ang analysis mo." It's not just about digging a deeper hole in the ground. It's about going beyond the surface level. Pwedeng sa pag-aaral, sa relationship ("Let's deepen our connection"), o sa pag-intindi sa sarili. Kapag sinabing "laliman," it means "Don't just scratch the surface, dive in!"
usage_notes: The command form of the verb. "Nilaliman" (past), "nilaliman" (present), "lalaliman" (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **laliman** ang balon para magkaroon ng sapat na tubig.","translation":"The well needs **to be deepened** to have enough water."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong **laliman** ang iyong pag-unawa sa sitwasyon.","translation":"Try **to deepen** your understanding of the situation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pook o bahaging nasa gitna ng isang bagay, lugar, o pangkat.
original_explanation: That awkward spot in the middle of the jeepney you have to squeeze into when it's rush hour. It's the center of the chismis circle, the middle slice of the pizza that everyone wants, or the center lane on EDSA where all the action happens.
usage_notes: Refers to the central location or part of something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umupo siya sa **gitnaan** ng dalawang magkaaway.","translation":"He sat in the **middle** of the two enemies."},{"sentence":"Nasa **gitnaan** ng plasa ang monumento ni Rizal.","translation":"The monument of Rizal is in the **center** of the plaza."}]

translation: to allow oneself to be enslaved; to cause someone to be enslaved
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahintulot na gawing alipin o busabusin ang sarili o ang iba.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'martyr' move. It's when you let someone treat you like their personal assistant, driver, and ATM, all rolled into one, without a single complaint. It's letting your boss give you their weekend work or letting a toxic friend walk all over you. 'Huwag kang magpaalila sa pag-ibig!' is a classic line for a reason.
usage_notes: Can be reflexive (to allow oneself to be enslaved) or causative (to cause another to be enslaved).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpaalila** sa isang trabahong hindi mo gusto.","translation":"Don't **allow yourself to be enslaved** by a job you don't like."},{"sentence":"Ang mga mapang-abusong amo ay gustong **magpaalila** ng kanilang mga kasambahay.","translation":"Abusive employers want to **enslave** their house helpers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbabago ng direksyon sa hinaharap, bilang anyong panghinaharap ng pandiwang 'liko'.
original_explanation: What the jeepney driver shouts three seconds before swerving across three lanes. It's the future tense of 'liko', representing every sudden, unannounced change of plans in your life, from career shifts to relationship statuses. "Friend, liliko na raw tayo, may bagong chika."
usage_notes: Future tense of the verb 'liko' (to turn).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Liliko** tayo sa susunod na kanto.","translation":"We **will turn** at the next corner."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, **liliko** ang sasakyan.","translation":"Be careful, the car **will turn**."}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pangalan, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang taong nakagawa ng krimen. Bilang pang-uri, ito ay naglalarawan sa isang bagay na may kaugnayan sa krimen.
original_explanation: 'Yung tao mismo na gumawa ng krimen. Sila 'yung kontrabida sa totoong buhay (at sa mga teleserye). Pag sinabing '**kriminal** na gawain,' ibig sabihin, ilegal at masama 'yung ginawa.
usage_notes: Can be a noun (a person) or an adjective (describing an act).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli na ng mga awtoridad ang **kriminal** na matagal nang pinaghahanap.","translation":"The authorities have finally caught the **criminal** who has long been wanted."},{"sentence":"Ito ay isang **kriminal** na sindikato na dapat buwagin.","translation":"This is a **criminal** syndicate that must be dismantled."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nababaluktot na tubo na ginagamit upang maglipat ng likido, karaniwan ay tubig, mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: The green or orange snake-like thing in your garage used for watering plants, washing the car, or giving your younger sibling an unexpected shower. It's the source of many childhood water fights.
usage_notes: The Spanish-derived "manguera" is also commonly used and is considered more traditional. "Hose" is a direct English borrowing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha ng **hose** at didiligan ko lang ang mga halaman.","translation":"Please get the **hose**, I'm just going to water the plants."},{"sentence":"Butas na yata ang **hose** kaya mahina ang tulo ng tubig.","translation":"I think the **hose** has a hole, that's why the water flow is weak."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkakaroon ng kulay na pula; magiging kulay pula. Ito ay tumutukoy sa pagbabago ng kulay ng isang bagay, o sa pamumula ng pisngi dahil sa hiya, kilig, o galit.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pandiwa na 'ma-' at ang pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang ugat na 'pula' (red), na nagsasaad ng kilos sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your face when your crush finally notices you, or when your mom catches you sneaking out. It's the physical manifestation of 'Sana lamunin na ako ng lupa.' Can also refer to something literally turning red, like a traffic light or your bank account statement after a 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit upang ilarawan ang pamumula ng mukha (pamumula ng pisngi) dahil sa matinding emosyon tulad ng hiya o galit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tiyak na **mamumula** ang kanyang mga pisngi kapag nalaman niyang nanalo siya sa lotto.","translation":"Her cheeks will surely **turn red** when she finds out she won the lottery."},{"sentence":"Kapag **namumula** na ang langit sa kanluran, oras na para umuwi.","translation":"When the sky in the west **is turning red**, it's time to go home."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pamamaraan, kasanayan, o mga partikular na detalye sa pagsasagawa ng isang gawain o sining; may kinalaman sa mga praktikal na kasanayan ng isang partikular na larangan.
original_explanation: The 'how-to' part of anything. It’s the reason your explanation to your parents about cloud storage doesn't make sense to them. 'Masyadong tekniko' is what they say when you're explaining something with too much jargon and not enough 'hugot'.
usage_notes: When used as an adjective, it means 'technical'. The word 'teknik' is more commonly used for the noun 'technique'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong **tekniko** ang paliwanag ng propesor, hindi ko maintindihan.","translation":"The professor's explanation is too **technical**, I can't understand it."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **tekniko** na pagsusuri ang problemang ito.","translation":"This problem requires a **technical** analysis."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o gusali na nagsisilbing dulo o hantungan ng ruta ng pampublikong transportasyon, tulad ng bus, jeep, o tren, kung saan nagbababa at nagsasakay ng mga pasahero.
original_explanation: The starting line and finish line of your daily commute saga. Dito ka makikipag-agawan ng upuan sa bus pa-probinsya, o dito mo hihintayin yung jeep na 'di na halos makita ang signboard sa dami ng karatula. Basically, the HUB of Pinoy commuters.
