usage_notes: Almost exclusively refers to transportation hubs. "Terminal ng bus," "Terminal ng jeep," "Airport terminal."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa **terminal** ng bus sa Cubao para umuwi sa probinsya.","translation":"We went to the bus **terminal** in Cubao to go home to the province."},{"sentence":"Saan ang sakayan at babaan sa **terminal** ng jeep papuntang SM?","translation":"Where is the loading and unloading zone at the jeep **terminal** going to SM?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagkakaroon ng lasang katulad ng asukal o pulot; ang kalidad ng pagiging kaaya-aya o kalugud-lugod.
original_explanation: Ito yung lasa ng leche flan ni lola, o yung ngiti ng crush mo. Pwedeng literal na lasa, pwedeng "kilig" feeling. Pero mag-ingat, 'pag sobrang tamis, baka magka-diabetes ka... o ma-fall sa maling tao.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa matalinhagang paraan upang ilarawan ang mga kaaya-ayang karanasan o damdamin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap ako ng **tamis** sa aking kape.","translation":"I'm looking for **sweetness** in my coffee."},{"sentence":"Naalala ko ang **tamis** ng aming unang pagkikita.","translation":"I remember the **sweetness** of our first meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang kasangkapan o kagamitan na ginagamit sa paghuhukay ng lupa o iba pang materyales.
original_explanation: Your trusty pala or shovel. Or that backhoe you see at construction sites that looks like a giant metal dinosaur. Anything that helps you dig a hole—whether you're planting a tree, building a foundation, or burying your past (charot!)—is a panghukay.
usage_notes: Can refer to a simple tool like a shovel or a large machine like an excavator.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang pala bilang **panghukay** sa hardin.","translation":"He used the shovel as a **digging tool** in the garden."},{"sentence":"Nirentahan nila ang malaking **panghukay** para sa konstruksyon ng gusali.","translation":"They rented a large **excavator** for the building's construction."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aklat o listahan kung saan itinatala o isinusulat ang mga pangalan, datos, o mahahalagang impormasyon para sa opisyal na rekord.
etymology: From `pa-` + `tala` (record) + `-an` (locative suffix), literally "a place for recording".
original_explanation: This is the OG spreadsheet. Before Excel, there was the `patalaan`. It's the logbook at the guard house, the class attendance sheet, the list of "utang" at the sari-sari store. It’s where things get official. "Pirma ka sa patalaan, besh."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalista ang pangalan ng lahat ng bisita sa **patalaan**.","translation":"The names of all the guests are on the **registry**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang isulat ang iyong oras ng pagdating sa **patalaan** ng opisina.","translation":"Don't forget to write your arrival time in the office **logbook**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o kalagayan ng pagkakayakap nang mahigpit sa isang tao o bagay.
etymology: From pagka- (manner/state of) + ka- (state of) + yapos (embrace).
original_explanation: That feeling when you finally hug your OFW family member at the airport after years apart. It's the "I miss you so much" hug, the "don't leave me" hug, or the "OMG, nanalo ako sa lotto" hug. It’s a tight embrace, not a BPO-style "A-frame hug". Full body contact, overflowing with feels.
usage_notes: 'Yapos' is a more intense, tighter, and often more emotional embrace than a simple 'yakap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ramdam na ramdam ko ang lungkot sa kanyang **pagkakayapos** sa akin.","translation":"I truly felt the sadness in the **way he embraced** me."},{"sentence":"Ang higpit ng **pagkakayapos** ng ina sa kanyang nawawalang anak.","translation":"The mother's **embrace** of her long-lost child was so tight."}]

translation: to ignore; to disregard; to take for granted
meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagbibigay ng pansin, halaga, o importansya sa isang bagay, sitwasyon, o tao.
original_explanation: The official verb of being 'seen-zoned.' You **ipagwalang-bahala** a message by reading it and not replying. It's the act of deliberately ignoring something. The ultimate 'hugot' is when someone you care about does this to your feelings. Ouch.
usage_notes: Used to describe the act of consciously ignoring or being indifferent towards something or someone, which is the object of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **ipagwalang-bahala** ang sakit na iyong nararamdaman.","translation":"It's hard **to ignore** the pain you are feeling."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ipagwalang-bahala** ang payo ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Don't **disregard** the advice of your parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginawang mas maikli o mas maigsi kaysa sa orihinal na haba o tagal.
etymology: From `pina-` + `ikli`. The `pina-` prefix turns the root quality (`ikli` - shortness) into a completed action ('was made short').
original_explanation: TL;DR in verb form. It's what you do to a long chismis to get to the juicy part, what your tailor does to your pants when you're vertically challenged, or what the professor does to the lecture when there's a bomb threat. It's the art of making things short and sweet (or just short).
usage_notes: Can be used for physical length, time duration, or written text. Often functions as an adjective describing the result of the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pinaikli** ng guro ang aming sanaysay dahil kulang na sa oras.","translation":"The teacher **shortened** our essay because we were running out of time."},{"sentence":"Maganda ang gupit mo, **pinaikli** mo ba ang buhok mo?","translation":"Your haircut is nice, did you **have** your hair **cut shorter**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matigas at solidong mineral na bumubuo sa kalupaan ng daigdig.
original_explanation: The OG hard-headed one. It’s what you use for 'bato, bato, pick' and what your friend is if they refuse to admit they're wrong ('pusong bato'). It can be a tiny pebble or a giant boulder. Also, the building block of most construction and chismis ('may tinatagong bato').
usage_notes: Extremely common word. Can also refer to a gem or precious stone. 'Pusong bato' means stone-hearted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinamaan siya ng maliit na **bato** sa ulo.","translation":"He was hit by a small **stone** on the head."},{"sentence":"Ang Darna ay kailangang lunukin ang **bato** para magkaroon ng kapangyarihan.","translation":"Darna needs to swallow the **stone** to gain powers."}]

translation: to be a boarder; to rent a room
meaning_filipino: Tumira sa isang bahay o gusali at magbayad ng upa para sa isang silid, karaniwang walang kasamang sariling kusina o banyo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "casera" (landlady). Ang anyong pandiwa ay nabuo sa Tagalog.
original_explanation: The life of a student or a young professional who just moved to the city. You live in a small room, share a bathroom with 5 other people, and your landlady (the 'casera') is your second mom/mortal enemy. It's the ultimate "adulting" starter pack.
usage_notes: Ito ay partikular na tumutukoy sa pag-upa ng isang silid sa loob ng isang mas malaking bahay (boarding house), hindi isang buong apartment o bahay. Ang taong gumagawa nito ay isang "kasera" o "boarder".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming estudyante ang **nangangasera** malapit sa unibersidad.","translation":"Many students **rent a room** near the university."},{"sentence":"Doon siya **nangangasera** sa bahay ni Aling Nena.","translation":"He is **boarding** at Aling Nena's house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mapagkumbaba; ang kawalan ng pagmamataas o kayabangan at ang pagkilala sa sariling limitasyon.
etymology: From ka- + pagkumbaba + -an. 'Pagkumbaba' is from 'kumbaba', an archaic form related to 'baba' (low), signifying a 'lowering' of oneself.
original_explanation: The art of being a total rockstar but acting like you're just a regular person. It's when you ace the exam and just say, 'Chamba lang.' It's the opposite of 'flex culture.' It's knowing your worth without having to post it online with a price tag.
usage_notes: A highly valued virtue in Filipino culture. It's often associated with being respectful and down-to-earth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng kanyang tagumpay, nanatili ang kanyang **kapakumbabaan**.","translation":"Despite his success, his **humility** remained."},{"sentence":"Ang tunay na karunungan ay may kasamang **kapakumbabaan**.","translation":"True wisdom comes with **humility**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis sa isang lugar na hindi isinasama ang isang tao o bagay; ang pagpapabaya o paglalagay ng isang bagay sa isang partikular na lokasyon.
original_explanation: The ultimate "hugot" verb. This is what your ex did to you. On a less dramatic note, it's what you do with your keys when you're in a hurry (`nag-iwan ng susi`). It's also what your generous friend does when they treat you to lunch (`nag-iwan ng bayad`). So, it can be painful or a blessing, depende sa context.
usage_notes: Can refer to physically leaving an object, leaving a person, or leaving a legacy/mark.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, huwag kang **mag-iwan** ng kalat sa ating silid-aralan.","translation":"Please, do not **leave** a mess in our classroom."},{"sentence":"**Nag-iwan** siya ng sulat bago umalis papuntang probinsya.","translation":"He/She **left** a letter before leaving for the province."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tanggapan o lupon ng mga patnugot (editor) na namamahala sa isang publikasyon; pamunuan o administrasyon.
original_explanation: This is the nerve center, the HQ, the bridge of the Starship Enterprise for any newspaper, magazine, or school paper. It's where the editors (mga patnugot) hang out, drink way too much coffee, and make the big decisions about what gets published and what gets rejected. It can also refer to 'management' in corporate speak.
usage_notes: Can refer to both the physical office and the collective body of editors or managers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinasa niya ang kanyang artikulo sa **patnugutan** ng pahayagan.","translation":"She submitted her article to the **editorial office** of the newspaper."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ahente, tulad ng init, radiation, o kemikal, na nagdi-disimpekta sa pamamagitan ng pagsira, pag-neutralize, o pagpigil sa pagdami ng mga mikroorganismong nagdudulot ng sakit.
original_explanation: Basically the English version of 'disimpektante'. Ito yung sinasabi mo kapag tinatamad kang sabihin yung Spanish version. "Uy, bili ka ng **disinfectant** spray." Same purpose, different spelling, mas madaling i-type sa chat.
usage_notes: Isang salitang hiram na lubos na karaniwan sa mga urban na lugar at sa mga nakababatang henerasyon. Kadalasang ipinagpapalit sa "disimpektante".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating bumili ng **disinfectant** para sa CR.","translation":"We need to buy **disinfectant** for the comfort room."},{"sentence":"I-spray mo 'yan ng **disinfectant** para sigurado.","translation":"Spray that with **disinfectant** to be sure."}]

translation: to attack, to raid, to invade
meaning_filipino: Isang kilos ng paglusob o pag-atake sa isang tao, lugar, o bagay nang may puwersa at karaniwang may karahasan.
original_explanation: When the cockroaches in your kitchen suddenly decide your midnight snack is their ancestral land. That's a 'sumalakay' moment. Or when your nanay finds out you didn't do the dishes, her verbal attack is a form of 'sumalakay' on your very soul.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of military action, raids, or even aggressive animal behavior. Can be used figuratively for an overwhelming onset of something, like sleepiness or hunger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumalakay** ang mga pirata sa barkong pangkalakal.","translation":"The pirates **attacked** the merchant ship."},{"sentence":"Biglang **sumalakay** ang antok habang ako'y nag-aaral.","translation":"Sleepiness suddenly **attacked** while I was studying."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagtatrabaho o gumagawa, karaniwan ay sa isang pisikal o manwal na larangan, upang kumita ng salapi.
original_explanation: The backbone of the economy, the one who actually builds the condos, serves your coffee, and codes the apps. They're the reason we have holidays named after labor. Sila yung nagpapa-ikot ng mundo, pero minsan sila pa yung pinapaikot.
usage_notes: Often refers to blue-collar or manual laborers, but can be used more broadly for any employee.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **manggagawa** sa pabrika ay humihingi ng mas mataas na sahod.","translation":"The **workers** in the factory are asking for a higher salary."},{"sentence":"Ngayong Araw ng Paggawa, binibigyang-pugay natin ang lahat ng **manggagawa**.","translation":"This Labor Day, we honor all **workers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o pakiramdam ng pagiging masaya, kontento, at may kagalakan sa buhay.
etymology: From 'ka-' + 'ligaya' (joy) + '-han', forming an abstract noun meaning 'the state of being happy'.
original_explanation: This is the goal, the prize, the ultimate 'sana all'. It's that feeling you get when your Shopee order arrives, your crush replies, and it's a long weekend. It's not just a fleeting 'haha', but the deep, warm feeling of 'I'm good'. The opposite of Monday mornings.
usage_notes: A very common and fundamental word for the concept of happiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tunay na **kaligayahan** ay hindi nabibili ng pera.","translation":"True **happiness** cannot be bought with money."},{"sentence":"Natagpuan niya ang **kaligayahan** sa pagtulong sa kapwa.","translation":"He found **joy** in helping others."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan o lugar na may kakulangan o kawalan ng suplay ng tubig.
original_explanation: The dreaded announcement from Maynilad or Manila Water. The reason you have to fill up every timba, balde, and planggana in the house. It's the ultimate test of your hygiene and patience. That moment you turn on the shower and nothing comes out but a sad little hiss. A true urban horror story.
usage_notes: A common household and community issue, often referring to a water service interruption.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas, **walang-tubig** sa aming lugar mula 8 ng umaga hanggang 5 ng hapon.","translation":"Tomorrow, there will be **no water** in our area from 8 in the morning until 5 in the afternoon."},{"sentence":"Ang disyerto ay isang lugar na halos **walang-tubig**.","translation":"The desert is a place that is almost **waterless**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsasagawa ng pagbigti sa isang tao o hayop.
original_explanation: This verb form focuses on the person or thing being hanged. 'Sino ang bigtihin?' (Who is to be hanged?). It's direct and object-focused. Like `bigtihan`, this is not your everyday BPO-call-center-vocabulary. This is stuff for historical dramas or crime reports. It's the command form: 'Bigtihin ang traydor!' (Hang the traitor!).
usage_notes: Ang hulaping '-in' ay nagpapahiwatig na ang aksyon ay ginagawa sa isang partikular na bagay o tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbanta ang masamang-loob na **bibigtihin** niya ang bihag kung hindi ibibigay ang ransom.","translation":"The villain threatened that he **would hang** the hostage if the ransom was not given."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na binilot o ipinulupot sa sarili nito o sa isang panloob na tubo, tulad ng papel, tela, o film.
original_explanation: Think of toilet paper, paper towels, or 'yung lumang film ng camera ng lola mo. Kahit 'yung lumpia, technically, parang mini-rolyo. It's anything that's rolled up. Parang 'yung mga plano mong hindi natuloy, naka-rolyo lang sa isang tabi. Hugot!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng isang **rolyo** ng toilet paper.","translation":"Please hand me a **roll** of toilet paper."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang isang **rolyo** ng lumang mapa para sa kanyang proyekto.","translation":"He used a **scroll** of an old map for his project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o paulit-ulit na pagsilip sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: This is the verb form for when the whole 'Marites' squad is peeking at the neighborhood drama. It's not just one person peeking; it's a group activity. 'Let's all peek at them!'
usage_notes: Ang diin ay nasa unang pantig (SI-li-pan) para sa pandiwa, na iba sa pangngalan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Silipan** natin kung ano ang pinag-aawayan nila sa labas.","translation":"Let's **peep at** what they are fighting about outside."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkain na isinasagawa sa oras ng tanghali.
original_explanation: The most important meal for any Pinoy office worker, second only to the free coffee. This is the sacred hour for adobo, sinigang, or whatever is in your baunan, shared over the latest chismis about the new hire.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **tanghalian** natin mamaya?","translation":"What's our **lunch** later?"},{"sentence":"Masarap ang ulam niya para sa **tanghalian**.","translation":"Her viand for **lunch** is delicious."}]

translation: To be entertained, to be amused, to be comforted
meaning_filipino: Makadama ng aliw, saya, o kasiyahan mula sa isang bagay; mabawasan ang lungkot o pagkabagot.
original_explanation: Your state of mind while scrolling through TikTok for three hours straight. It's what happens when your friend tells a great joke, when you watch your favorite comedian's vlog, or when a cute dog video distracts you from your deadlines. It's the perfect antidote to 'pagod na me' or 'sana all'.
usage_notes: Can mean both being entertained (from boredom) and being comforted (from sadness). The context determines the exact nuance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **naaliw** ako sa mga kwento ng lolo ko.","translation":"I was truly **entertained** by my grandfather's stories."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **maaliw** ka kahit kaunti sa munting handog kong ito.","translation":"I hope you will be **comforted** even a little by this small gift of mine."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtamo ng sugat sa katawan, karaniwan dahil sa isang aksidente o pananakit.
original_explanation: The classic result of being 'lampa' (clumsy) or getting into a 'bardagulan' (brawl). It's what happens when you try to chop onions like a celebrity chef. Emotionally, it's how your heart feels after being 'seen-zoned'. A physical or emotional 'ouchie'.
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense). Refers to receiving a wound, which can be physical or, metaphorically, emotional.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nasugatan** ang bata nang mahulog siya mula sa bisikleta.","translation":"The child **was wounded** when he fell from the bicycle."},{"sentence":"Lubhang **nasugatan** ang damdamin niya sa masasakit na salitang binitawan mo.","translation":"His feelings **were** deeply **hurt** by the painful words you uttered."}]

translation: to rummage through, to search thoroughly
meaning_filipino: Siyasatin o hanapin nang masinsinan ang isang bagay sa isang lugar sa pamamagitan ng paghahalungkat o pag-aalis ng mga nakalagay dito.
original_explanation: What your mom does to your room when she's looking for something (or checking if you're hiding anything). It's the frantic search for your keys in your bag na parang black hole. It’s not just 'looking for' something; it’s a chaotic, everything-must-be-tossed-around kind of search.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The actor-focus form is 'maghalughog'. It implies a more intrusive and messy search than just 'hanapin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **halughugin** ang buong aparador para mahanap ang lumang litrato.","translation":"I need to **rummage through** the entire cabinet to find the old photo."},{"sentence":"**Hinalughog** ng mga awtoridad ang bahay ng suspek.","translation":"The authorities **searched** the suspect's house **thoroughly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na gawa sa mga sinulid, pisi, o alambre na pinagbuhol-buhol upang makabuo ng mga butas, ginagamit sa panghuli ng isda, hayop, o bilang harang.
original_explanation: The OG tool for catching things. Whether it's for fish in the sea, butterflies in the air, or a volleyball game, the lambat is there. Metaphorically, it's the 'trap' you fall into when you get caught in a multi-level marketing scheme or a complicated relationship. 'Nahuli sa lambat ng pag-ibig.'
usage_notes: A general term for any kind of net.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inihagis ng mangingisda ang kanyang **lambat** sa dagat.","translation":"The fisherman cast his **net** into the sea."},{"sentence":"Butas ang **lambat** kaya nakawala ang mga isda.","translation":"The **net** has a hole, so the fish escaped."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at tanyag na termino para sa Jollibee, isang Pilipinong kumpanya ng fast-food na kilala sa buong bansa.
etymology: A playful, affectionate diminutive of the proper name 'Jollibee'.
original_explanation: The A-list celebrity of Filipino fast food. The one and only. The home of Chickenjoy. When someone asks 'Saan tayo kakain?' and the group chat replies 'Kahit saan,' they secretly mean Jabee. It's not just a restaurant; it's a childhood memory, a birthday party venue, and a national treasure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, mag-**Jabee** tayo pagkatapos ng klase.","translation":"Let's go to **Jollibee** after class."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng Chickenjoy, daan tayo sa **Jabee** drive-thru.","translation":"I want Chickenjoy, let's pass by the **Jollibee** drive-thru."}]

translation: is breaking, is being damaged, is getting ruined
meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang nagkakaroon ng pinsala o pagkasira; unti-unting nawawalan ng dating anyo o silbi.
original_explanation: This is the present tense of things falling apart. It's watching your phone's battery life drain from 100% to 1% in 10 minutes. It's your New Year's resolution by January 15th. It's the slow, painful process of your data plan getting used up before the next payday. It’s the “Wala na, finish na” in progress.
usage_notes: The progressive aspect (present tense) of 'masira'. It describes an ongoing process of damage, decay, or spoiling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na **nasisira** ang mga pagkain kung hindi ilalagay sa loob ng refrigerator.","translation":"Food **spoils** quickly if not placed inside the refrigerator."},{"sentence":"**Nasisira** na ang tiwala ko sa'yo dahil sa paulit-ulit mong pagsisinungaling.","translation":"My trust in you **is being ruined** because of your repeated lying."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng kuko o anumang matulis na bagay upang kaskasin ang balat, karaniwan upang maibsan ang kati.
original_explanation: The official term for what you do when a mosquito bites you, when you're nervous during a presentation, or when you're trying to remember where you left your keys ('nagkakamot ng ulo'). It's the universal solution to an itch, both literal and metaphorical.
usage_notes: "Pagkamot ng ulo" (scratching one's head) is a common idiom for being confused or perplexed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mapigilan ng bata ang **pagkamot** sa kanyang mga binti dahil sa kagat ng lamok.","translation":"The child couldn't stop **scratching** his legs because of mosquito bites."},{"sentence":"Ang madalas na **pagkamot** ay maaaring makasugat sa balat.","translation":"Frequent **scratching** can wound the skin."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtutuos o paggamit ng matematika upang matukoy ang isang halaga, bilang, o resulta.
original_explanation: That thing you do on your phone's calculator to see if you can afford milk tea after paying your bills. It's the mental gymnastics of figuring out how many leave credits you have left vs. how many long weekends there are.
usage_notes: Can be used for both literal mathematical calculation and figurative calculation (e.g., calculating risks).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **pagkalkula** ng buwis kung hindi ka sanay.","translation":"The **calculation** of taxes is difficult if you are not used to it."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng maingat na **pagkalkula**, napagdesisyunan niyang bumili ng bahay.","translation":"After careful **calculation**, he decided to buy the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal at modernong katawagan para sa isang kaibigan o kapatid, katumbas ng 'bro' o 'dude'.
etymology: Mula sa African American Vernacular English (AAVE) at British slang na 'blood', na nangangahulugang kapatid o malapit na kaibigan. Naging popular sa pamamagitan ng internet memes.
original_explanation: This is what Gen Z calls their friends. It's the 2024 version of 'bro', 'pare', 'paps', or 'chong'. If someone calls you 'blud', it means you're part of the inner circle, the barkada. 'What is blud waffling about?' is a common meme phrase.
usage_notes: Ginagamit ng mga nakababatang henerasyon (Gen Z) sa mga online na usapan. Itinuturing na napaka-impormal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hoy **blud**, ano'ng balita sa'yo?","translation":"Hey **bro**, what's up with you?"},{"sentence":"Tingin mo, ano'ng ginagawa ni **blud** doon?","translation":"What do you think that **dude** is doing over there?"}]

meaning_filipino: Kalagayan ng pagiging malabnaw o matubig, tulad ng lugaw na kulang sa bigas o putik na maraming tubig.
original_explanation: You know that feeling when you mess up cooking rice and it turns into a sad, watery porridge? That's 'lunaw'. Or the state of the path to your house after a typhoon. It's the opposite of 'malapot' (thick). Think of it as the consistency of a failed leche flan.
usage_notes: Often used to describe food consistency (like porridge or soup) or the state of mud.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ay, naging **lunaw** ang lugaw dahil naparami ang sabaw.","translation":"Oh, the porridge became **watery** because there was too much broth."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa daan, puro **lunaw** dahil sa ulan.","translation":"Be careful on the path, it's all **thin mud** because of the rain."}]

translation: Aggravator; something that worsens a situation
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, kilos o pangyayari na nagiging sanhi ng paglala o paglubha ng isang kondisyon, sakit, o problema.
etymology: From 'pang-' (instrumental prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'lala' (severity, worsening). Lit. 'that which is used to cause worsening'.
original_explanation: This is you drinking a cold soda even if you have a cough. Or you talking back to your already angry partner. It's adding fuel to the fire, poking the bear, or scratching an already itchy wound. Basically, any action that makes a bad situation go from 'uh oh' to 'THIS IS A DISASTER.'
usage_notes: Used to describe factors that exacerbate a problem, illness, or conflict.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang stress ay isang **pampalala** ng kanyang sakit.","translation":"Stress is an **aggravator** of her illness."},{"sentence":"Ang pagsisinungaling mo ay lalo lang naging **pampalala** ng sitwasyon.","translation":"Your lying just served to **worsen** the situation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikli at makabuluhang pahayag na naglalaman ng aral, payo, o katotohanan, na karaniwang ipinapasa mula sa isang henerasyon patungo sa isa pa.
etymology: From ka- + sabi (to say) + -han (noun suffix indicating a collection or place).
original_explanation: These are the OG life hacks and wisdom bombs your lola drops when you're having a crisis. Think "Aanhin pa ang damo kung patay na ang kabayo?" – the ultimate 'too little, too late' clapback. They're the original Filipino memes, passed down through generations.
usage_notes: 'Kasabihan' is more general than 'salawikain' (proverb), which is often more poetic and metaphorical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa **kasabihan**, 'Ang hindi lumingon sa pinanggalingan ay hindi makakarating sa paroroonan.'","translation":"According to the **saying**, 'He who does not look back to where he came from will not reach his destination.'"},{"sentence":"Marami tayong matututunang aral mula sa mga lumang **kasabihan**.","translation":"We can learn many lessons from old **adages**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng mga katangiang tulad ng sa langit; kaaya-aya, banal, o may kabanalan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you take the first bite of a perfect mango float. Or the vibe of a song that makes you feel like you're floating. It's anything that gives you a taste of pure, blissful, almost divine perfection.
usage_notes: The prefix 'maka-' can sometimes elevate the root noun into a sublime or intense adjective, not just indicating 'pro-' (in favor of). Here it means 'like' or 'having the quality of' heaven.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang boses ng mang-aawit ay may **makalangit** na himig.","translation":"The singer's voice has a **heavenly** tone."},{"sentence":"Isang **makalangit** na kapayapaan ang naramdaman ko sa lugar na iyon.","translation":"I felt a **divine** peace in that place."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasa sa sikolohiya na nag-aaral ng mga proseso ng pag-iisip at pag-uugali. Hindi sila mga medikal na doktor at karaniwang gumagamit ng 'talk therapy'.
original_explanation: This is just the English version of 'psikologo'. You use this word when you want to sound more formal or when you're code-switching in a meeting. 'I think we need to hire a corporate psychologist to address the burnout.'
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English. 'Psikologo' is the Hispanized/Filipinized equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"The school **psychologist** conducted a seminar on stress management.","translation":"Nagdaos ng seminar tungkol sa stress management ang **psychologist** ng paaralan."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaiba sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang bagay; isang hindi pagkakasundo o alitan; isang problema o sira sa isang makina o sistema.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung 'pagkakaiba' na nagiging 'away'. From 'May **deperensya** ang pananaw natin' (We have a difference in opinion) to 'Nagka-**deperensya** sila' (They had a falling out). It can also mean a glitch or malfunction, like when your brain has a **deperensya** and you forget your password.
usage_notes: May mas malawak na kahulugan kaysa sa 'pagkakaiba', at madalas na nagpapahiwatig ng problema o hindi pagkakasundo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **deperensya** ng dalawang produktong ito?","translation":"What is the **difference** between these two products?"},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon sila ng **deperensya** kaya sila naghiwalay.","translation":"They had a **dispute**, which is why they separated."},{"sentence":"May **deperensya** yata ang aircon, hindi lumalamig.","translation":"I think the aircon has a **malfunction**, it's not getting cold."}]

translation: act of traversing or passing through a difficult path
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdaan o pagtawid sa isang mahirap, mapanganib, o hindi pamilyar na lugar o landas.
original_explanation: This is your Waze or Google Maps journey, but on hardcore mode. It's not just passing through; it's pagkalagtas through the jungle, a mountain trail, or even the dreaded EDSA during rush hour. It implies a challenge, a journey that you have to navigate and overcome. Think of it as successfully getting from Point A to Point B when B is on the other side of a "baha" or a "daang-bakal".
usage_notes: Has a literary or formal tone. Not common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkalagtas** sa masukal na gubat ay isang malaking hamon para sa mga manlalakbay.","translation":"The **act of traversing** the dense forest was a huge challenge for the travelers."},{"sentence":"Matapos ang mahabang **pagkalagtas** sa kabundukan, narating din nila ang nayon.","translation":"After a long **traversal** through the mountains, they finally reached the village."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman (Mirabilis jalapa) na ang mga bulaklak ay karaniwang bumubuka sa hapon. Sa malawak na kahulugan, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang kamangha-manghang bagay.
original_explanation: This word is a two-for-one deal. It's the Tita-approved name for the 'four o'clock flower' that blooms in the afternoon, just in time for merienda. But it also sounds like 'marvel' because it comes from the Spanish 'maravilla'. So you can use it to describe a wonder, like the marabilya of surviving EDSA traffic on a payday Friday.
usage_notes: More commonly known as the name of a flower. The meaning 'marvel' or 'wonder' is less common in modern speech but understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namumukadkad na ang mga **marabilya** sa aming hardin tuwing hapon.","translation":"The **four o'clock flowers** in our garden are already blooming every afternoon."},{"sentence":"Isang **marabilya** ng arkitektura ang gusaling iyon.","translation":"That building is a **marvel** of architecture."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng magaspang na tela na karaniwang kulay abo; ang kulay na abo.
original_explanation: This is a deep cut. Think of the color of unpainted concrete or a cloudy, emo sky. In old-school tailoring, 'gris' was a type of sturdy, grayish fabric. Today, you'd probably only hear your lola or a historian use this word. Everyone else just says 'gray' or 'abo'.
usage_notes: Very rare in modern conversation. 'Abo' is the common term for the color gray.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pantalon niya ay yari sa telang **gris**.","translation":"His pants were made of **coarse gray** cloth."},{"sentence":"Pinapahanap ako ng lola ko ng sinulid na kulay **gris**.","translation":"My grandmother asked me to look for thread of a **gray** color."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o espasyo na itinalaga para sa paglalaro o mga aktibidad na panlibangan.
etymology: From pa- prefix + lugar (place) + -an suffix, indicating a place where an action is done.
original_explanation: Your childhood 'tambayan' before life and bills happened. It's the designated spot for patintero, tumbang preso, or just gossiping with the neighborhood kids. Think of it as the original 'co-working space' for the 'batang 90s' guild.
usage_notes: Can refer to a formal playground with swings and slides, or any open space used for playing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkita-kita ang mga bata sa **palugaran** para maghabulan.","translation":"The children met at the **playground** to play tag."}]

meaning_filipino: Isalin sa wikang Tagalog.
original_explanation: When you're trying to explain something to your non-Filipino friend and you just can't find the right English word. "Just itagalog it, besh!" It's the linguistic equivalent of code-switching, but with a specific destination: the beautiful chaos of the Tagalog language.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of translation, localization, or simply explaining something in the vernacular.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **itagalog** mo ang dokumentong ito para sa ating mga kliyente.","translation":"Please **translate** this document **into Tagalog** for our clients."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **itagalog** ang ilang konsepto sa agham.","translation":"It's difficult **to express** some scientific concepts **in Tagalog**."}]

translation: to dedicate; to devote; to allot
meaning_filipino: Ilalaan o itatalaga ang isang bagay, panahon, o pagsisikap para sa isang partikular na tao, layunin, o gawain.
original_explanation: Like when you finally decide to **iukol** your weekend to just watching K-dramas instead of doing 'work-from-home' tasks. Or when a songwriter says, "I dedicate this song..." - that's "Iniuukol ko ang awit na ito...". It's about setting something aside for a special purpose, like your 13th-month pay for a new phone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **iukol** ang kanyang buhay sa pagtulong sa mga kapus-palad.","translation":"She wants to **devote** her life to helping the less fortunate."},{"sentence":"**Iukol** natin ang ating atensyon sa mas mahahalagang bagay.","translation":"Let's **allot** our attention to more important matters."}]

translation: someone who is satisfied with or gives only the least possible effort
meaning_filipino: Isang taong kontento na sa pagbibigay o pagtanggap ng pinakamababang antas ng pagsisikap o ambag.
etymology: From the English internet slang phrase.
original_explanation: Ito yung tropa mong group project, ang ambag pang-print lang. O yung jowa na ang 'date' niyo ay pag-send lang ng TikTok video. They celebrate mediocrity like it's a gold medal. They live by the mantra: 'Why do more when you can do less?'
usage_notes: A recent internet slang term, often used humorously or critically to describe a person who consistently puts in the least effort possible.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Certified **bare minimum enjoyer** talaga siya, laging late sa meeting at walang ambag.","translation":"He's a certified **bare minimum enjoyer**, always late to meetings and with no contributions."}]

translation: indigo plant; place with indigo plants
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman (Indigofera tinctoria) na pinagkukunan ng asul na pangkulay na tinatawag na 'tina' o indigo. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang lugar kung saan sagana ang halamang ito.
etymology: From 'tayum', the name of the plant, with the suffix '-an' indicating a place where it is abundant.
original_explanation: Before your favorite denim jeans, there was tayuman. This is the OG plant that gives the 'tina' or indigo dye. It's the reason why your lola's old tapis has that deep blue color. Also, a famous street in Manila where you can buy medical supplies, probably not related to the plant anymore, but hey, history!
usage_notes: Also a well-known place name in Manila, associated with a train station and a market for medical supplies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tayuman** ay mahalaga sa industriya ng paghahabi noong unang panahon.","translation":"The **indigo plant** was important in the weaving industry in the olden days."},{"sentence":"Gumagamit sila ng katas mula sa **tayuman** upang kulayan ang mga sinulid.","translation":"They use extract from the **indigo plant** to dye the threads."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yugto o haba ng oras; ang kalagayan ng atmospera sa isang tiyak na lugar at oras; isang partikular na bahagi ng taon na may natatanging klima (hal. tag-araw, tag-ulan).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung bagay na laging kulang 'pag deadline na, pero sobrang dami 'pag naghihintay ka ng reply niya. Pwede itong weather ("Ano'ng panahon ngayon?"), pwede itong era ("Panahon pa ni Kopong-kopong 'yan!"), at pwede itong 'the right moment' ("Hintayin mo ang tamang panahon."). Multifunctional, parang Swiss Army knife.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-flexible na salita na may maraming kahulugan depende sa konteksto (time, era, season, weather).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bilis talaga ng takbo ng **panahon**.","translation":"**Time** really flies so fast."},{"sentence":"Maganda ang **panahon** kaya matutuloy ang aming lakad.","translation":"The **weather** is good so our trip will push through."},{"sentence":"Noong **panahon** ng mga Kastila, iba ang pamumuhay dito.","translation":"During the **era** of the Spaniards, life here was different."}]

translation: to get used to; to become accustomed to
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging bihasa o pamilyar sa isang gawain, bagay, o sitwasyon dahil sa paulit-ulit na karanasan.
original_explanation: It's that feeling when you've done your daily commute so many times you can do it with your eyes closed. Or when you've been on a BPO night shift for so long that being awake at 3 AM feels normal. It's your body and mind adapting. 'Mahirap sa una, pero makakasanayan mo rin.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa una, mahirap ang trabaho pero kalaunan ay **makakasanayan** mo rin.","translation":"At first, the job is hard, but eventually you will **get used to** it."},{"sentence":"Paano ko **makakasanayan** ang paggising nang maaga?","translation":"How can I **get used to** waking up early?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-indayog ng balakang o katawan habang naglalakad, na karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng kariktan o kumpiyansa.
original_explanation: It's that confident, sometimes flirty, sway of the hips when someone walks. Think of a beauty queen doing her pageant walk on stage—that's pure 'kiay'. It's not just walking; it's walking with an attitude, a little bit of landî (flirtatiousness), and a whole lot of self-assurance. The 'S-curve' in motion.
usage_notes: Also used as a verb (kumikiay, kumiay). Often associated with feminine grace but can be used for anyone with a distinct, swaying walk.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ay napapatingin sa **kiay** ng kandidata sa entablado.","translation":"Everyone's eyes are on the candidate's **sway** on stage."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng kanyang **kiay** habang rumarampa.","translation":"Her **graceful gait** is beautiful as she walks the ramp."}]

translation: The act or process of shortening
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagiging maikli o ang akto ng pagpapaliit sa haba ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your patience during rush hour traffic. It's what happens to your sahod a week after payday. It's the act of the mananahi turning your jeans into shorts. Pwedeng process (kumikli) o pwedeng action (iniklian).
usage_notes: Can refer to physical length, duration of time, or even abstract concepts like patience or life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pag-ikli** ng oras, minadali na namin ang aming proyekto.","translation":"Because of the **shortening** of time, we rushed our project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pangkat o hanay ng mga pulo.
original_explanation: Parang Pilipinas! Isang "collection" ng mga isla, na parang mga hiwa-hiwalay na chismis na bumubuo sa isang malaking kwento. We're a nation of 7,000+ islands, so we're the textbook definition of an arkipelago.
usage_notes: Isang terminong heograpikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay isang **arkipelago** na binubuo ng mahigit pitong libong pulo.","translation":"The Philippines is an **archipelago** composed of more than seven thousand islands."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang transportasyon sa isang **arkipelago** dahil kailangan mong tumawid ng dagat.","translation":"Transportation in an **archipelago** is difficult because you need to cross the sea."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gamit, kapakinabangan, o halaga ng isang bagay o gawain; serbisyo o paglilingkod.
original_explanation: The ultimate "hugot" word. "Ano pa bang silbi ko sa'yo?" (What's my purpose to you anymore?). It's the reason why you don't throw away that broken appliance (baka may silbi pa!) or why you stay in a job ("may silbi naman ako dito"). It's all about usefulness and purpose.
usage_notes: Very common in both literal and figurative contexts. 'Walang silbi' means 'useless'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong **silbi** nitong lumang remote control?","translation":"What's the **use** of this old remote control?"},{"sentence":"Gusto kong magkaroon ng **silbi** sa lipunan.","translation":"I want to be of **service** to society."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi mapakali at mamaluktot o gumalaw-galaw ang katawan dahil sa sakit, hiya, o pagkabalisa.
original_explanation: Ever been in a super awkward situation, like when your Tita asks "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?" at a family reunion? That cringey, fidgety feeling where you just want the ground to swallow you whole? That's you, about to 'mag-alumpihit'. It's also what you do when you have a bad stomachache. It's the official body language of "I'm so uncomfortable right now."
usage_notes: Describes physical restlessness due to discomfort, either physical (pain) or emotional (embarrassment, anxiety).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mag-alumpihit** sa hiya ang bata nang tanungin siya sa harap ng klase.","translation":"The child started to **squirm** in embarrassment when asked in front of the class."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding sakit ng tiyan, hindi siya tumigil sa pag-**alumpihit** sa kama.","translation":"Because of the intense stomach pain, he couldn't stop **writhing** in bed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging masikip, puno, o siksik ng mga tao o bagay sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: Ever ridden the MRT at 7 AM on a Monday? That's kasiksikan. It's Divisoria during the Christmas rush. It's that feeling when everyone in the family decides to hang out in your room. It's the physical manifestation of 'Walang personal space.'
usage_notes: Describes the state of a place being overly crowded or congested.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi na nakakatuwa ang **kasiksikan** ng trapiko sa EDSA tuwing Biyernes.","translation":"The **congestion** of traffic on EDSA every Friday is no longer amusing."},{"sentence":"Nagtiis sila sa **kasiksikan** sa loob ng evacuation center.","translation":"They endured the **crowdedness** inside the evacuation center."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapagawa o pagpapahintulot sa iba na salapidin o itirintas ang sariling buhok.
original_explanation: That childhood memory of your lola or nanay braiding your hair so tight you feel like your eyebrows are being lifted. Or what you do at the beach in Boracay to get that 'summer vibes' look.
usage_notes: The subject is the person whose hair is being braided, not the one doing the braiding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing umaga, **nagpapatirintas** si Maria sa kanyang ina bago pumasok sa eskwela.","translation":"Every morning, Maria **has her hair braided** by her mother before going to school."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magpatirintas** para sa kasal ko.","translation":"I want to **have my hair braided** for my wedding."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala para sa isang paboritong tao, karakter, o media na, sa kabila ng pagiging gusto o hinahangaan, ay may mga katangian, gawa, o opinyon na may problema o moral na kaduda-duda.
etymology: Hango sa pariralang Ingles na "problematic favorite," na naging popular sa mga online fandom.
original_explanation: That celebrity, artist, or anime character you love despite their glaring flaws. You know they're a walking red flag, but you can't help but stan. It's the "I can fix him/her!" mentality applied to your idols. You defend them in public but cringe in private. It's a whole ✨struggle✨.
usage_notes: A modern slang term used primarily online in fan communities and social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **problematic fave** ko; ang galing niyang umarte pero ang daming isyu sa personal na buhay.","translation":"He's my **problematic fave**; he's a great actor but has so many issues in his personal life."},{"sentence":"Aminin mo na, si Loki ang ultimate **problematic fave** ng lahat.","translation":"Just admit it, Loki is everyone's ultimate **problematic fave**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong pagpapakita ng damdamin o opinyon, lalo na sa pamamagitan ng pagtitipon at pagmamartsa; isang pagpapaliwanag o pagpapakita kung paano gumagana ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The formal version of "demos." Ito 'yung act of showing up in public, usually in a large group, to make a point. Pwedeng protest against a government policy, or a demostrasyon on how to use a new vacuum cleaner sa mall. Context is key!
usage_notes: Can refer to a political protest or a product/process demonstration. The context clarifies the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng malawakang **demostrasyon** sa EDSA.","translation":"There was a massive **demonstration** at EDSA."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **demostrasyon** kung paano gamitin ang bagong software.","translation":"A **demonstration** is needed on how to use the new software."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang asawa o ang kalahati ng puso o buhay ng isang tao.
etymology: From "ka-" + "biyak" (split, half), literally meaning "the other half".
original_explanation: The romantic, "pang-wedding-vow" way to say asawa. "My better half," "my soulmate," etc. This is what you call your partner when you're feeling extra sweet, not when you're asking them to take out the trash. "Ang aking kabiyak" sounds way better than "Hoy, asan na ‘yung pambayad sa Meralco?"
usage_notes: A term of endearment and respect for one's spouse. Often used in formal or romantic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakilala niya sa amin ang kanyang magandang **kabiyak**.","translation":"He introduced us to his beautiful **spouse**."},{"sentence":"Habambuhay kong mamahalin ang aking **kabiyak**.","translation":"I will love my **other half** for the rest of my life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagbigkas ng "salamat" o "thank you" sa paraang pa-cute, balbal, o impormal.
etymology: Isang paglalaro sa pagbigkas ng pariralang Ingles na "thank you".
original_explanation: The cute, pabebe way of saying 'thank you.' It's like the verbal equivalent of adding a sparkly heart emoji to your message. You say this to your crush, your BFF, or when you're trying to get away with something. It's the softer, less formal cousin of 'salamat po'.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa impormal na usapan, lalo na sa text, chat, o social media. Karaniwang ginagamit ng mga kabataan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wow, ang ganda ng regalo mo! **Tenchu** po!","translation":"Wow, your gift is so beautiful! **Thank you**!"},{"sentence":"Sige, ako na bahala dito. **Tenchu** sa tulong!","translation":"Okay, I'll take care of this. **Thanks** for the help!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang siyensiya na nauukol sa paggalaw, pag-uugali, at epekto ng mga projectiles, partikular na ang mga bala, bomba, o rocket, lalo na sa kanilang landas sa himpapawid.
original_explanation: Not your tita's chismis, but the science of how things fly through the air after being shot—like bullets, or... feelings you threw at your ex. It's what the SOCO team talks about when matching a bullet to a gun in crime dramas.
usage_notes: A technical term primarily used in law enforcement, military, and forensic science contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa pagsusuri sa **balistiks**, ang bala ay tumama muna sa pader bago sa biktima.","translation":"According to the **ballistics** analysis, the bullet first hit the wall before the victim."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng pataba o pertilayser sa lupa o halaman upang ito ay lumago nang mas malusog.
original_explanation: The act of giving your plants their 'steroids'. When you finally decide to stop being a neglectful plant parent and actually feed them something. 'Uy, kailangan ko nang pertilisahan yung mga orchids ko.'
usage_notes: A verb form created from the English loanword 'pertilayser'. The more common verb would be 'maglagay ng pataba' or 'patabain'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pertilisahan** ang lupa bago magtanim.","translation":"You need **to fertilize** the soil before planting."},{"sentence":"**Pertilisahan** mo ang mga rosas kada buwan.","translation":"**Fertilize** the roses every month."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na walang trabaho o ginagawa at karaniwang tumatambay o nagpapalipas ng oras sa isang lugar, tulad ng kanto o tindahan.
original_explanation: The OG 'bystander'. It's a classic Filipino cultural figure—the person chilling at the corner store, observing the neighborhood drama, and probably asking for "isang stick" of your yosi. It's from the English 'stand by', but Pinoy-fied to mean someone who's permanently on standby mode.
usage_notes: Mayroon ding anyong pandiwa ('tumambay') at pang-uri ('mapagtambay'). Kadalasang may negatibong konotasyon, ngunit maaari ring tumukoy sa simpleng pagpapahinga o paghihintay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napagalitan siya ng nanay niya dahil para siyang **istambay** buong araw.","translation":"His mom scolded him because he was like a **loafer** all day."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **istambay** sa kanto ang unang nakakita sa aksidente.","translation":"The **bystanders** on the corner were the first to see the accident."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng malaking kabuluhan, silbi, o halaga; hindi maaaring ipagsawalang-bahala.
original_explanation: The grown-up version of 'mahal'. While 'mahal' can be about price or feelings, 'mahalaga' is about value and significance. Your diploma is mahalaga. Your family is mahalaga. Getting 8 hours of sleep is mahalaga. It's the stuff you can't just 'seen zone' in life.
usage_notes: Mas malawak ang sakop kaysa sa 'mahal' (expensive), dahil maaari itong tumukoy sa abstrakto o hindi moneteryong halaga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang edukasyon ay isang **mahalaga**ng yaman na hindi mananakaw ninuman.","translation":"Education is a **valuable** treasure that no one can steal."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lumang yunit ng sukat ng haba na katumbas ng humigit-kumulang tatlumpu't tatlong pulgada o halos isang yarda.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na *vara* ("tungkod," "panukat na pamalo," "yarda").
original_explanation: Before 'meters' and 'feet' became the standard, people used 'bara'. It's like the lola of measurement units. You'd hear this in old markets when buying cloth. Today, it's mostly a trivia word, like knowing what a floppy disk is.
usage_notes: Itinuturing nang makaluma at pinalitan na ng sistemang metriko. Maaari pa ring matagpuan sa mga kontekstong pangkasaysayan o pampanitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ang lola ng tatlong **bara** ng tela para sa kanyang bestida.","translation":"Grandma bought three **varas** of cloth for her dress."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng pahintulot, lisensya, o pagsang-ayon sa isang tao o gawain.
etymology: From pa- + pa- + hintulot, meaning "the act of giving permission."
original_explanation: That magical piece of paper (or text from your mom) that allows you to go on that out-of-town trip with friends. It's the formal version of "sige na nga" or getting the green light from the boss to go on leave.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanghingi siya ng **pagpapahintulot** mula sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"He asked for **permission** from his parents."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **pagpapahintulot** ng mayor bago simulan ang proyekto.","translation":"The mayor's **authorization** is needed before starting the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao o bagay na may payat ngunit matikas na pangangatawan; may mahabang hubog.
etymology: Possibly from 'baling' (bend) and 'kinitan' (seen), suggesting a body whose grace is seen in its curves/bends.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino term for 'body goals.' It's not just skinny, it's elegant skinny. Think of a beauty queen's physique or that friend who can eat a whole lechon but still looks like a bamboo shoot. It's a very classic, almost poetic way to say someone is slim and graceful.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat literary term. Not commonly used in casual conversation, where 'payat' or 'slim' are more frequent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinangaan ng lahat ang kanyang **balinkinitan** na katawan.","translation":"Everyone admired her **slender** body."},{"sentence":"Ang mga dalaga sa mga lumang pelikula ay kadalasang inilalarawan bilang **balinkinitan**.","translation":"The young ladies in old movies are often described as **svelte**."}]

translation: to do or enumerate one by one
meaning_filipino: Gawin o banggitin ang bawat isang bagay nang sunod-sunod.
original_explanation: This is what happens when someone asks for a list and you give it to them, item by item. It's the verb form of 'one by one'. Think of your manager asking you to report your accomplishments or your tita asking you to list down all your exes. 'Huwag mo akong simulang **isa-isahin**, marami akong kasalanan sa'yo.'
usage_notes: Implies a detailed and thorough enumeration or process.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **isa-isahin** ang mga problema upang malutas ang mga ito.","translation":"We need to tackle the problems **one by one** to solve them."},{"sentence":"Sinimulan niyang **isa-isahin** ang mga dahilan kung bakit siya nahuli sa klase.","translation":"She began to **enumerate** the reasons why she was late for class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay ng pera bilang kapalit sa isang produkto, serbisyo, o utang.
original_explanation: The moment of truth. After adding to cart, this is the painful part. It's what you do for your Meralco bill, your Shopee checkout, and your utang to your friend. Pagbabayad is the adulting version of "game over, insert coin to continue."
usage_notes: Can be literal (money) or figurative (paying for a mistake).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalimutan kong isama sa badyet ang para sa **pagbabayad** ng kuryente.","translation":"I forgot to include the **payment** for the electricity in the budget."},{"sentence":"Ang huling araw ng **pagbabayad** ng buwis ay sa susunod na linggo.","translation":"The last day for **paying** taxes is next week."}]

translation: will be made to believe; can be convinced
meaning_filipino: Magagawang maniwala o makukumbinsi sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you try to do to your boss when you file for a sick leave on a Friday. Or what a scammer tries to do to you with a 'You've won a prize!' text. It's the act of convincing someone, making them believe something, whether it's true or a giant 'Marites-level' chismis.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of convincing, tricking, or persuading someone. The `mapa-` prefix here implies 'to be able to make someone do X'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa galing niyang magsalita, kahit sino ay kanyang **mapapaniwala**.","translation":"With his skill in speaking, he **can make** anyone **believe**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpadala sa mga pekeng balita, baka ka **mapapaniwala** sa kasinungalingan.","translation":"Don't be swayed by fake news, you might **be made to believe** a lie."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa posisyon, ranggo, o kalagayan sa isang herarkiya o sistema ng pagsusukat; baitang o grado.
original_explanation: Your 'level' in life, whether it's your grade in school (Baitang 7), your salary grade in government, or the level of your ka-Marites-an (expert level, probably). It's the social hierarchy, the floors in a mall, or the difficulty setting in a video game. 'Ibang antas na 'yan!' is the Pinoy way of saying 'That's next level!'
usage_notes: A very versatile word used in academic, professional, and social contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa ikalawang **antas** na ng kolehiyo ang aking kapatid.","translation":"My sibling is now in the second **year** of college."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating itaas ang **antas** ng ating serbisyo.","translation":"We need to raise the **standard** of our service."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mababaw na hukay na may putik o tubig kung saan nagpapagulong-gulong at nagbababad ang mga hayop tulad ng kalabaw o baboy upang magpalamig.
original_explanation: A carabao's happy place. Their personal jacuzzi. Their escape from the scorching Philippine sun. For humans, it's your bed after a 12-hour shift—the ultimate place to just sink in and forget your responsibilities. 'Hay, sarap mag-lublob sa kama.'
usage_notes: Primarily used for animals, but can be humorously applied to people seeking to immerse themselves in something for comfort.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga kalabaw ay nagpapahinga sa **lubluban** tuwing katanghalian.","translation":"The carabaos rest in the **wallowing pit** every noon."},{"sentence":"Naging parang **lubluban** ang palaruan dahil sa walang tigil na ulan.","translation":"The playground became like a **mud puddle** because of the non-stop rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makaramdam ng matinding kalungkutan, pananabik, o pangungulila, lalo na sa isang tahimik at mapayapang kapaligiran.
original_explanation: It's that specific kind of sadness you feel on a rainy afternoon while listening to a sad OPM song. It’s the feeling of 'sana all' turning into 'sana ol-d times.' More poetic than just being 'malungkot'. It's the official emotion of looking out a bus window, pretending you're in a music video.
usage_notes: Often has a poetic or literary feel, describing a deep, quiet sadness or loneliness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay madalas **mamanglaw** tuwing naaalala ang kanyang mga magulang na nasa probinsya.","translation":"He often **feels sad** whenever he remembers his parents who are in the province."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mamanglaw**; darating din ang araw na makakamit mo ang iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"Don't **be melancholic**; the day will come when you will achieve your dreams."}]

translation: to make someone drink; to give a drink to
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng inumin ang isang tao o hayop; ibigay ang isang likido upang sadyang mainom.
original_explanation: The verb for when you're taking care of a sick friend ('**Painumin** mo siya ng maraming tubig') or trying to get your friend to finally try your home-made milk tea ('**Painumin** mo si Beshy!'). It's the act of causing another being to consume liquid.
usage_notes: Verb in imperative/infinitive form. Other forms: `pinainom` (past), `pinapainom` (present), `papainumin` (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **painumin** ng gamot ang pasyente.","translation":"Don't forget **to give the patient** his medicine **to drink**."},{"sentence":"**Painumin** mo ang aso dahil mukhang pagod na pagod.","translation":"**Give the dog a drink** because it looks very tired."}]

translation: to appeal to; to seek help from
meaning_filipino: Ang paglapit sa isang tao o tanggapan na may awtoridad upang humingi ng tulong, magsumbong, o magharap ng isang usapin.
original_explanation: Parang pag-chat mo sa HR para ireklamo yung boss mo, o pagpunta sa barangay para ipa-blotter yung maingay na kapitbahay. Ito yung level-up na version ng "sumbong," kasi may formal process na kasama. You're not just complaining; you're officially seeking intervention.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, legal, or official contexts, like appealing to a court, a government agency, or a person in a high position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumulog** sa korte ang mga manggagawa upang ipaglaban ang kanilang mga karapatan.","translation":"The workers **appealed** to the court to fight for their rights."},{"sentence":"Saan ba pwedeng **dumulog** kung may reklamo sa serbisyo ng kumpanya?","translation":"Where can one **go to seek help** if there's a complaint about the company's service?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kakanin na gawa sa kinudkod na kamoteng kahoy, gata, asukal, at itlog, na karaniwang niluluto sa hurno at nilalagyan ng gata o keso sa ibabaw.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'bibingka' (isang uri ng kakanin) at 'kamoteng kahoy' (cassava).
original_explanation: The denser, chewier, and arguably yummier cousin of the regular bibingka. This is a staple dessert at fiestas and handaans. It has that distinct sticky texture and creamy, coconut-y topping that makes you forget your diet. It's the kakanin equivalent of a warm hug.
usage_notes: Madalas ding tawaging 'cassava cake' kahit sa mga usapang Tagalog, ngunit ito ang pormal na pangalan nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong panghimagas ay ang **bibingkang kamoteng kahoy** na may makapal na latik.","translation":"My favorite dessert is **cassava cake** with thick coconut curd."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na malaki, mahalaga, o seryoso ang epekto o kalikasan.
original_explanation: A Taglish word that's so common, it's practically Filipino. When a problem isn't just a "problema" but a "MAJOR problema," you know it's serious. It's the go-to adjective for adding emphasis. "Major traffic sa SLEX!" "Major hugot moment!" "She's having a major meltdown."
usage_notes: Used extensively in Taglish conversations to mean "very," "significant," or "serious."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Major** ang traffic kaya na-late ako sa meeting.","translation":"The traffic was **major** so I was late for the meeting."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi naman iyan **major** na isyu.","translation":"Don't worry, that's not a **major** issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mabangis na mamalyang karniboro na kabilang sa pamilya ng mga aso, karaniwang naninirahan at nangangaso nang pangkatan.
original_explanation: The OG bad boy of fairy tales. Before the 'f-boy' there was the lobo, tricking Little Red Riding Hood and blowing down houses. In modern terms, it can refer to a predator, a 'buwaya' in disguise, or that guy on a dating app whose profile seems too good to be true.
usage_notes: Primarily used in literature, translations, or when referring to the actual animal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kuwento ng Tatlong Biik, ang masamang **lobo** ang kanilang kalaban.","translation":"In the story of the Three Little Pigs, the evil **wolf** is their enemy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng palumpong (Gardenia jasminoides) na may mabango at puting bulaklak, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga kwintas na bulaklak o bilang palamuti.
etymology: From Spanish 'rosal' which means 'rosebush'. However, in the Philippines, the term was applied to the Gardenia flower, likely due to its fragrance and appearance.
original_explanation: That fragrant white flower that smells like heaven and is often sold outside churches alongside sampaguita. It's the flower of graduations and religious processions. It's more sophisticated than sampaguita, like the 'tita' flower to sampaguita's 'dalaga' vibe.
usage_notes: While 'rosal' in Spanish means rosebush, in the Philippines it exclusively refers to the gardenia flower (Gardenia jasminoides).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bango ng mga bulaklak ng **rosal** sa hardin tuwing umaga.","translation":"The **gardenia** flowers in the garden smell so fragrant every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isa sa pares na organ sa katawan na hugis-habas, na responsable sa pagsasala ng dugo at pagbuo ng ihi.
etymology: The organ was likely named for its shape, resembling a bean or a stone ('bato').
original_explanation: The body's internal water filter. It's the organ your tita warns you about when you drink too much soda. 'Ingatan mo 'yang bato mo!' Usually talked about in a medical context, like 'May sakit sa bato' (has kidney disease) or when someone needs dialysis.
usage_notes: The meaning is determined entirely by context, usually medical. 'Sakit sa bato' is kidney disease. 'Bato sa bato' would be kidney stones.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan niyang magpa-dialysis dahil sa sakit sa **bato**.","translation":"He needs to undergo dialysis because of his kidney disease."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-inom ng maraming tubig ay mabuti para sa iyong mga **bato**.","translation":"Drinking lots of water is good for your **kidneys**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon o kaganapan kung saan ang pangunahing aliwan ay pagtugtog o pakikinig sa musikang rock, kadalasang kinasasangkutan ng malakas na tugtugan at masiglang pakikilahok ng mga manonood.
etymology: From English 'rock' with the Tagalog suffix '-an' indicating a place or event. The reduplication 'rak-rak' implies intensity.
original_explanation: The ultimate destination for a 'rakista'. This is a rock concert, a gig, or just an intense jam session. Expect loud music, headbanging, mosh pits, and everyone shouting 'Rakenrol!'. It's the sound of pure, unadulterated rock music energy. Think Muziklaban finals or your local bar's rock night.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb form, 'magrakrakan' (to have a rock session).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, manood tayo ng **rakrakan** sa Sabado!","translation":"Let's go watch a **rock concert** on Saturday!"},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng klase, **rakrakan** agad ang bagsak ng banda namin sa studio.","translation":"After class, our band immediately had a **rock session** at the studio."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi umuusad, gumagalaw, o umuunlad; nananatili sa isang lugar o kalagayan.
original_explanation: Feeling 'estangkado' is when your career feels like EDSA traffic at 5 PM on a payday Friday – absolutely no movement. It's when your love life has been on 'seen' for a year, or when your internet connection just stops buffering. You're stuck, and there's no progress in sight.
usage_notes: Often used to describe traffic, careers, projects, or even personal growth. The root word 'estangke' (tank/pond) is less common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Estangkado** na ang daloy ng trapiko sa pangunahing kalsada.","translation":"The flow of traffic on the main road is now **at a standstill**."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **estangkado** ang aking career sa kumpanyang ito.","translation":"I feel like my career is **stagnant** in this company."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit o angkop para sa gawain ng pagkakampo.
original_explanation: The adjective for all the gear you buy for a trip you'll probably only take once. Your 'pangkamping' checklist includes the tent, sleeping bag, portable-kalan-na-minsan-lang-gagamitin, and the all-important insect repellent. It's the stuff that makes sleeping on the ground slightly more bearable.
usage_notes: A clear borrowing from English. 'Pang-camping' with a hyphen is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dalhin mo ang lahat ng gamit na **pangkamping**.","translation":"Bring all the gear **for camping**."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng bagong sapatos na **pangkamping**.","translation":"I bought new shoes **for camping**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daglat sa internet na nangangahulugang "Want to Trade" o "Nais Ipagpalit," na ginagamit upang mag-alok ng isang aytem kapalit ng iba, sa halip na pera.
etymology: Daglat mula sa pariralang Ingles na "Want To Trade".
original_explanation: Para sa mga walang pambili (WTB) o walang paninda (WTS), pero mayroon pa ring pag-asa. Ito ang barter system ng 21st century. "WTT my rare K-Pop photocard for your rare K-Pop photocard. Please, ito na lang kulang sa set ko!"
usage_notes: Karaniwan sa mga komunidad ng kolektor (e.g., trading cards, K-Pop merchandise, mga laruan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Post niya: \"**WTT** my acoustic guitar for an electric keyboard. Straight swap.\"","translation":"His post: \"**Want to trade** my acoustic guitar for an electric keyboard. Straight swap.\""},{"sentence":"Sa isang forum: \"**WTT** this rare in-game skin for another limited edition one.\"","translation":"On a forum: \"**Want to trade** this rare in-game skin for another limited edition one.\""}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sinaunang bangkang pandigma ng mga Filipino.
original_explanation: Think of this as the ancient Filipino version of a navy destroyer. It's a type of warship from our ancestors' time. You'd find this word more in a history book about pre-colonial Philippines or in a museum than in a conversation at the mall. It's a cool reminder that we had our own badass naval fleets way back when.
usage_notes: A historical term referring to a pre-colonial sea vessel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **talimangin** ay isa sa mga sasakyang pandagat na ginamit ng ating mga ninuno sa pakikidigma.","translation":"The **talimangin** was one of the sea vessels used by our ancestors in warfare."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa kasaysayan ang disenyo ng mga **talimangin**.","translation":"The design of the **talimangin** warships is being studied in history."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking hayop na pantrabaho sa bukid, karaniwang kulay itim at may malalaking sungay; kalabaw.
etymology: An old Tagalog word for carabao, now less common than 'kalabaw'.
original_explanation: This is the OG tractor of the Philippines, the national animal, the mighty kalabaw. It's big, strong, and loves chilling in the mud. Calling a person "damulag" is like calling them a big, slow, lumbering oaf. "Ang laki ng katawan mo, para kang **damulag**!"
usage_notes: 'Kalabaw' is the more common term. 'Damulag' can sound more rural or archaic. When used for a person, it's a slightly derogatory comment on their large size or slowness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaararo ng **damulag** ang bukirin ni Mang Teban.","translation":"The **carabao** is plowing Mang Teban's farm."},{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan ka namang kumilos, para kang **damulag**!","translation":"Move a little faster, you're like a lumbering **water buffalo**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Gagamit ng kamao upang biglang tamaan o hampasin ang isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: What you feel like doing to the person who spoiled the ending of your favorite series. "Susuntok ako ng pader sa inis!" It's the future tense of physical frustration, usually said but hopefully not acted upon. A warning shot fired with words.
usage_notes: Future tense of "sumuntok". The 'su-' prefix indicates the future tense of an '-um-' verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag inulit mo 'yan, **susuntok** na talaga ako.","translation":"If you do that again, I really **will punch** (someone)."},{"sentence":"Sino ba ang **susuntok** sa buwan para sa'yo? 'Wag ako.","translation":"Who **will punch** the moon for you? Not me. (A figurative expression for doing the impossible)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng keyboard sa isang computer, makinilya, o telepono upang makasulat ng mga titik at salita.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mag-` (pormang pandiwa) + salitang Ingles na `type`. Isang klasikong pandiwang Taglish.
original_explanation: What you do 90% of your day in the office, especially if you're in BPO or a corporate slave. It's the sound of productivity (or frantic chismis on Messenger). 'Mag-type ka na ng report mo!' is the modern 'get to work!'
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang pandiwang Taglish na ginagamit sa parehong pormal at impormal na sitwasyon, lalo na sa mga opisina at paaralan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **mag-type** ng email para sa kliyente.","translation":"I need to **type** an email for the client."},{"sentence":"Ang bilis niyang **mag-type** sa keyboard, parang may humahabol.","translation":"She can **type** so fast on the keyboard, like someone's chasing her."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng paglalala gamit ang yantok, karaniwang nakikita sa mga upuan at muwebles, na bumubuo ng isang butas-butas na padron.
etymology: From Spanish 'silla' (chair), adapted into a Filipino noun for the specific weaving style.
original_explanation: That classic, breezy pattern on your lola's rocking chair or the back of old-school jeepneys. It's the original air-conditioned seating, perfect for the Philippine heat. If your upuan has this, it's certified Tito-core or Lola-chic. It's what makes a chair breathe.
usage_notes: Also spelled as 'sulihia'. Refers to both the material (rattan strips for weaving) and the weaving style itself, commonly known as caning in English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasira ang **sulihiya** sa upuan ni Lolo.","translation":"The **rattan weaving** on Grandpa's chair broke."},{"sentence":"Maganda pa rin ang mga muwebles na may disenyong **sulihiya**.","translation":"Furniture with a **caning** design is still beautiful."}]

translation: to be cruel; to act cruelly
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita o paggawa ng kalupitan, karahasan, o kawalan ng awa sa kapwa o sa anumang may buhay.
original_explanation: This is the verb for kontrabidas in teleseryes. The evil stepmother who makes Cinderella scrub the floor, the loan shark who harasses the protagonist's family, or even you to a cockroach you found in the bathroom. It's being intentionally harsh and merciless.
usage_notes: A strong word indicating severe and intentional cruelty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi makatao ang **magmalupit** sa mga hayop.","translation":"It is inhumane to **be cruel** to animals."},{"sentence":"**Nagmalupit** ang mga mananakop sa ating mga ninuno.","translation":"The colonizers **acted cruelly** towards our ancestors."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mapanlait na paglalarawan sa isang taong itinuturing na pangit ang mukha.
original_explanation: A very harsh, grade-school level insult. It's like saying someone's face is so undesirable, it might as well be a foot. It’s so over-the-top mean, it’s almost funny... unless it’s directed at you. Use with extreme caution or, better yet, don't.
usage_notes: A very strong and offensive insult. Not for polite conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaasar siya ng mga kalaro niya at tinatawag na **mukhang-paa**.","translation":"His playmates were teasing him and calling him **ugly (foot-faced)**."},{"sentence":"Isang masakit na salita ang itawag sa iyong kapwa na **mukhang-paa**.","translation":"It is a hurtful word to call your fellow person **foot-faced**."}]

meaning_filipino: Patigilin ang isang bagay na gumagalaw, isang proseso, o isang gawain.
original_explanation: The command form of 'hinto'. It's what you yell at the jeepney driver when you've reached your stop ('Manong, para!'), or what your friend tells you when you're about to make a bad life decision. "Girl, **ihinto** mo na 'yang pag-stalk sa ex mo. It's not healthy."
usage_notes: The object-focus verb for 'hinto'. Used when the speaker is commanding or causing something/someone to stop.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **ihinto** mo ang sasakyan sa tapat ng panaderya.","translation":"Please, **stop** the car in front of the bakery."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **ihinto** ang pag-aaksaya ng tubig.","translation":"We need to **stop** wasting water."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang anumang sulat, marka, o laman; bakante o walang laman ang isip.
original_explanation: That feeling during an exam when you've studied for weeks, but the moment you see the first question, your mind goes completely... blangko. It's the mental equivalent of a 404 error page. Also describes a check you hope to receive, or the look on your face when someone asks you 'kamusta lovelife mo?'
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical object (like paper) or a mental state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan siyang **blangko** ang isip matapos ang mahirap na pagsusulit.","translation":"His mind was left **blank** after the difficult exam."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng isang **blangko** na papel.","translation":"Give me a **blank** piece of paper."}]

meaning_filipino: May hugis na pabilog o sirkulo; walang sulok o kanto.
original_explanation: The shape of your face after the holidays, or the shape of a 5-peso coin. It's the opposite of 'flat,' which is what you wish your stomach was. Ito rin yung shape ng 12 fruits na pinipilit mong kumpletuhin tuwing New Year's Eve para daw swertehin.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pangngalan (noun) na tumutukoy sa 'circle'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang buwan ay **bilog** na **bilog** kagabi.","translation":"The moon was perfectly **round** last night."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **bilog** na keso de bola tuwing Pasko.","translation":"The **round** Edam cheese is delicious during Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malalim na pag-iisip o pagninilay; isang kamalayan o persepsyon.
original_explanation: It's the state of being lost in thought. Picture yourself staring out a bus window with sad music playing in your earphones, thinking about your life choices. That whole vibe? That's *gunamgunam*. It's the noun form of 'gunagunahin'.
usage_notes: A literary or formal word. 'Pag-iisip' or 'pagninilay' are more common synonyms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **gunamgunam**, nakita niya ang kanyang mga pagkakamali.","translation":"In his **reflection**, he saw his mistakes."},{"sentence":"Naputol ang kanyang malalim na **gunamgunam** nang may kumatok sa pinto.","translation":"His deep **contemplation** was interrupted when someone knocked on the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkukulang o hindi pagiging sapat ng isang bagay, tulad ng suplay, pondo, o kakayahan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "sapat" na may mga panlaping "di-ka-…-an".
original_explanation: Yung feeling kapag sweldo day, pero pagtingin mo sa ATM, may utang ka pa pala. Yung isang sachet ng 3-in-1 coffee para sa isang malaking-malaking mug.
