Yung 2GB of data mo for one whole month of WFH and Netflix. It's the "kulang pa, Lord" moment in life, whether it's about money, time, or love life.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng ekonomiya, personal na pananalapi, o emosyonal na kalagayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **di-kasapatan** ng pondo ang pangunahing hadlang sa proyekto.","translation":"The **insufficiency** of funds is the main obstacle to the project."},{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang nagdurusa dahil sa **di-kasapatan** ng pagkain.","translation":"Many families are suffering due to a **shortage** of food."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtutuon ng isip o kamalayan sa isang partikular na tao, bagay, o gawain.
original_explanation: That thing your crush never gives you. The thing your boss wants when they say "Can I have your atensyon for a minute?" which really means "Prepare for a one-hour meeting." In the world of social media, this is the currency. Likes, shares, and comments are all forms of atensyon. Also known as what toddlers demand 25/8.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng buo mong **atensyon** para dito.","translation":"I need your full **attention** for this."},{"sentence":"Nakuha niya ang **atensyon** ng lahat nang siya ay kumanta.","translation":"She got everyone's **attention** when she sang."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, katangian, o paraan na ginagamit upang mahikayat, maakit, o mabighani ang isang tao o hayop.
original_explanation: It's your "rizz." The secret weapon you use to get someone's attention. Could be your killer smile, your witty jokes, or even that perfectly curated IG feed. For fishermen, it's literal bait. For job hunters, it's a stacked LinkedIn profile.
usage_notes: Can refer to a personal quality, an object, or a strategy used for attraction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang ngiti ang kanyang pinakamalakas na **pang-akit**.","translation":"Her smile is her greatest **charm**."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng hipon bilang **pang-akit** sa pangingisda.","translation":"He used shrimp as **bait** for fishing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na bahagi ng bato o metal mula sa kalawakan na nagliliyab at nag-iiwan ng maliwanag na guhit sa himpapawid kapag pumasok sa atmospera ng Earth.
original_explanation: That thing you wish upon, hoping your ex will text you back. Also known as a 'shooting star' or, in Tagalog, 'bulalakaw.' It’s basically space dust making a dramatic entrance, just like you arriving fashionably late to a party.
usage_notes: Ang katutubong katumbas nito ay 'bulalakaw'. Ang 'meteor' ay mas siyentipiko o teknikal sa gamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita kami ng isang **meteor** habang nanonood ng mga bituin kagabi.","translation":"We saw a **meteor** while stargazing last night."},{"sentence":"Ang **meteor** shower ay isang magandang palabas sa kalangitan.","translation":"The **meteor** shower is a beautiful celestial show."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga bagay, produkto, o kalakal na inilalako o ipinagbibili.
original_explanation: This is your 'paninda'—the stuff you're selling, whether it's fishball on the street, pre-loved clothes on Carousell, or your amazing skills as a freelancer. It's the "what" in your "what are you selling?" hustle.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with `paninda`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naubos agad ang **tinda** ni Aling Nena sa palengke.","translation":"Aling Nena's **merchandise** at the market sold out quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging kalat-kalat, wasak, o kumalat dahil sa isang pagsabog o malakas na puwersa.
original_explanation: Your room after you try on 10 different outfits for a night out. The contents of your bag when it accidentally spills on the floor. Popcorn flying everywhere. It's the physical state of chaos and being spread all over the place. Think of a bomb exploding: 'yung mga piraso, sabog.
usage_notes: 'Sumabog' is the verb form (to explode). 'Sabog' is the resulting state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sabog** ang mga gamit sa sahig matapos ang lindol.","translation":"The things were **scattered** on the floor after the earthquake."},{"sentence":"Naging **sabog** ang utak niya sa dami ng kailangang gawin.","translation":"His brain felt **scattered** from the number of things he needed to do."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang serbisyo ng streaming na nag-aalok ng malawak na uri ng mga palabas sa telebisyon, pelikula, anime, at dokumentaryo na maaaring panoorin gamit ang internet.
original_explanation: The ultimate reason why you have puyat, trust issues (from cliffhangers), and a backlog of adulting tasks. It's the modern-day "sine" that you watch in your pajamas while eating chichirya. The verb form, "mag-Netflix," is a legitimate weekend plan.
usage_notes: Used as a proper noun, but often used as a verb "mag-Netflix" (to watch Netflix).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wala akong gagawin sa Sabado kundi mag-**Netflix** buong araw.","translation":"I have nothing to do on Saturday but watch **Netflix** all day."},{"sentence":"Ano ang bagong palabas sa **Netflix** ngayon?","translation":"What's the new show on **Netflix** now?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nagbibigay ng pisikal na kaginhawahan at kaluwagan; pakiramdam na panatag at walang alalahanin.
original_explanation: Yung feeling kapag nakauwi ka na, nag-pajama, at humilata sa kama after a long day. O yung pakiramdam na kasama mo ang barkada mo at pwede kang maging weird nang walang judgement. That's the peak of being komportable.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical comfort (a chair) or emotional comfort (with friends).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas **komportable** matulog sa sarili mong kama.","translation":"It's more **comfortable** to sleep in your own bed."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako **komportable** sa mga taong hindi ko kilala.","translation":"I'm not **comfortable** around people I don't know."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagharap sa isang gawain na may hindi tiyak na resulta; ang pagsubok sa kapalaran sa pamamagitan ng pagpasok sa isang mapanganib o bagong karanasan.
etymology: From pakiki- (participation) + pag- (action noun) + sapalaran (game of chance, venture), from sa- (towards) + palad (fate, palm).
original_explanation: The official theme song of every OFW, probinsyano moving to Manila, or anyone starting a new business. It's taking a leap of faith. It’s leaving your comfort zone hoping for a better outcome, kahit hindi ka sure sa ending. It's the "bahala na si Batman" attitude applied to major life decisions.
usage_notes: Connotes risk, uncertainty, and adventure. Can be applied to careers, travel, or life in general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagpunta sa ibang bansa para magtrabaho ay isang malaking **pakikipagsapalaran**.","translation":"Going to another country to work is a big **venture**."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **pakikipagsapalaran** ang buhay ng isang manlalakbay.","translation":"The life of a traveler is full of **adventure**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na naninirahan sa isang partikular na lugar, bayan, o bansa.
original_explanation: The official term for your friendly neighborhood marites. They know all the chika because they're always there. Also, what you call yourself when you finally get to register to vote in your new city.
usage_notes: Used in formal contexts like legal documents, news reports, and government forms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lahat ng **residente** ng barangay ay inaanyayahang dumalo sa pagpupulong.","translation":"All **residents** of the barangay are invited to attend the meeting."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong patunayan na ikaw ay isang lehitimong **residente** ng Maynila.","translation":"You need to prove that you are a legitimate **resident** of Manila."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagsuot ng kasuotang pare-pareho ang disenyo, kulay, at anyo na itinakda para sa isang partikular na grupo, paaralan, o kumpanya.
original_explanation: The official look from elementary to your first job at a fast-food chain or BPO. It's the great equalizer—everyone looks the same, whether you're rich or just trying to survive the semester. Also, the reason why you can spot a fellow student from a mile away at the mall.
usage_notes: Common in the context of school, work, and military/police service.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ng empleyado ay inaasahang pumasok nang **nakauniporme** tuwing Lunes.","translation":"All employees are expected to come to work **in uniform** every Monday."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ay masayang naglalakad pauwi, lahat sila ay **nakauniporme**.","translation":"The children were happily walking home, all of them **wearing a uniform**."}]

translation: to share the same feelings; to be of one sentiment
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng iisang saloobin, damdamin, o pananaw sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is when you and your bestie have the same reaction to chismis without even talking. It's that telepathic connection when you both hate the same kontrabida in a teleserye. You're on the same wavelength, emotionally speaking. Samesies!
usage_notes: Can function as a verb (to become of one feeling) or an adjective (being of one feeling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bihira ang mga magkaibigang tunay na **magkadamdamin** sa lahat ng bagay.","translation":"It's rare for friends to truly **share the same feelings** on all matters."},{"sentence":"Sila ay **magkadamdamin** pagdating sa pag-ibig sa bayan.","translation":"They are **of one sentiment** when it comes to love for the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang larawan o disenyo sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng mga linya, karaniwang gamit ang lapis, pluma, o iba pang kagamitang panulat.
original_explanation: The OG way of making art before Canva and AI generators. Ito 'yung ginagawa mo sa likod ng notebook mo 'pag bored ka sa klase. From stick figures to anime characters, kung gumuguhit ka, nagdidibuho ka.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magdibuho** ng mga mukha ng tao.","translation":"He loves to **draw** people's faces."},{"sentence":"**Nagdibuho** ang arkitekto ng plano para sa bagong gusali.","translation":"The architect **drew** the plan for the new building."}]

meaning_filipino: Iligtas ang isang tao, hayop, o bagay mula sa kapahamakan, panganib, o tiyak na kamatayan.
original_explanation: This is Darna-level action. When you sumagip, you're not just helping, you're rescuing someone from real trouble—a fire, a flood, or even a deadline from hell. Your BPO team lead who takes over a difficult call is sumasagip sa'yo.
usage_notes: Carries a sense of urgency and great danger. It's a stronger term than 'tumulong' (to help).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Buong tapang na **sumagip** ng mga bata ang bumbero mula sa nasusunog na bahay.","translation":"The firefighter bravely **rescued** the children from the burning house."},{"sentence":"Ang mabilis na tulong mo ang **sumagip** sa proyekto namin.","translation":"Your quick help **saved** our project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o proseso ng pagpapatala o pagpasok ng pangalan o impormasyon sa isang opisyal na listahan o talaan.
original_explanation: The official adulting process of getting your name on a list. Voter's rehistrasyon, car rehistrasyon (hello, LTO!), SIM card rehistrasyon... It's basically the government's way of saying, "Gotcha! We know who you are." Ang ultimate pila experience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahaba ang pila para sa **rehistrasyon** ng mga bagong botante.","translation":"The line for the **registration** of new voters is long."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo nang i-renew ang **rehistrasyon** ng iyong sasakyan.","translation":"You need to renew your car's **registration**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang marahas o malawakang pag-aalsa laban sa isang pamahalaan o umiiral na sistema; ang pagdudulot ng isang radikal na pagbabago.
original_explanation: What your parents think you're doing when you lock your bedroom door. Seriously though, it's about making a huge, game-changing move, whether it's an actual People Power or just you finally deciding to clean your room after a year. A 'new hair, new me' moment can feel like a personal rebolusyon.
usage_notes: Can refer to a political uprising or a radical change in a concept or system.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang mga mamamayan na **magrebolusyon** laban sa mapang-aping rehimen.","translation":"The citizens decided to **revolt** against the oppressive regime."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **magrebolusyon** sa paraan ng pagtuturo sa mga paaralan.","translation":"He wants to **revolutionize** the way of teaching in schools."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahayag ng pagsang-ayon, pahintulot, o pag-uudyok na magpatuloy.
original_explanation: The most versatile word in the Filipino vocabulary. It can mean 'okay, sure' (Sige, sama ako), 'go ahead, I dare you' (Sige, subukan mo), 'come on!' (Sige na!), or 'this is it, let's do this' (Sige, laban!). It's the ultimate Swiss Army knife of Filipino expressions, packed with nuance depending on your tone.
usage_notes: Its meaning is heavily dependent on context and intonation. Can function as an interjection, adverb, or verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sige**, pumapayag na ako sa gusto mo.","translation":"**Okay**, I agree to what you want."},{"sentence":"Gusto mo umalis? **Sige**!","translation":"You want to leave? **Go on**!"},{"sentence":"**Sige** na, please, pautangin mo muna ako.","translation":"**Come on**, please, lend me some money first."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain o bagay na ginagawa upang maiba ang atensyon mula sa isang bagay na seryoso o nakababagot, o para sa libangan.
original_explanation: That thing you do when you're supposed to be working on a deadline but suddenly find yourself deep-cleaning the aircon or watching conspiracy theory videos. "Boss, 'di pa tapos report ko, nagkaroon kasi ng **dibersyon**... nag-sale sa Steam." It's also the classic tactic in politics or chismis to change the topic.
usage_notes: `Dibersiyon` is a less common spelling variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paglalaro ng video games ay isang magandang **dibersyon** mula sa stress sa trabaho.","translation":"Playing video games is a good **diversion** from work-related stress."},{"sentence":"Gumawa sila ng ingay bilang **dibersyon** para makatakas ang kanilang kasama.","translation":"They made a noise as a **diversion** so their companion could escape."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mula sa Netherlands (Olanda); o anumang bagay na nauugnay sa kultura, wika, o bansang Netherlands.
original_explanation: Mga tao mula sa bansa ng windmills, tulips, at keso. Sila 'yung matatangkad na foreigner na makikita mo sa mga tourist spot. At 'yung nagdala sa atin ng 'Dutch Mill', pero hindi sila 'yun.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan para sa tao o pang-uri para sa bagay. Karaniwang isinusulat na may malaking titik.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming turistang **Olandes** ang bumibisita sa Palawan.","translation":"Many **Dutch** tourists visit Palawan."},{"sentence":"Gawa sa gatas ng kalabaw ang kesong puti, hindi ito kesong **Olandes**.","translation":"Kesong puti is made from carabao's milk, it's not a **Dutch** cheese."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng matagumpay na pagdaan o pag-alis mula sa isang masikip, mahirap, o mapanganib na sitwasyon; maaari ding tumukoy sa isang butas o daanan.
original_explanation: 'Lusot' is your magic word for getting out of trouble. Failed an exam? 'Baka may paraan para makalusot.' Stuck in traffic? 'Saan kaya may lusot dito?' It's the art of finding a loophole, a shortcut, or a way to squeeze through a tight spot, whether it's a physical space or a sticky situation with your boss. It's the official sport of the 'diskarte' masters.
usage_notes: Can be used literally (passing through a small opening) or figuratively (getting out of a problem). The verb form is 'lumusot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit na mahigpit ang mga tanod, nakahanap pa rin siya ng **lusot**.","translation":"Even though the guards were strict, he still found **a way through**."}]

translation: to pick a fight with; to antagonize
meaning_filipino: Simulan ang isang pakikipag-away o sadyain na makipagtalo sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the verb for when you're the one starting the trouble. "Huwag mo akong awayin" is what you say when someone's being unnecessarily confrontational. It's the act of singling someone out to argue with. Basically, 'to fight someone'. It's the go-to verb for anyone feeling 'palaban' today.
usage_notes: The focus of the verb is on the person being targeted for a fight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi na lang niya akong **inaaway** kahit wala akong ginagawang masama.","translation":"He/She always **picks a fight with** me even when I'm not doing anything wrong."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo ba **aawayin** ang kapatid mo?","translation":"Why are you going to **fight** your sibling?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aalok o pagbabayad para sa kape ng ibang tao bilang isang anyo ng pakikisama o pasasalamat.
etymology: Isang kolokyal na anyo mula sa `mag-` + `pa-` + `is-` (isang kolokyal na infix) + `kape`. Ang mas pormal na katumbas ay `magpakape`.
original_explanation: The universal Filipino love language. When you want to catch up with a friend, 'Tara, kape tayo!' When you want to thank someone, 'Pa-kape ako next time!' When you want to bribe your way into a chismis session, you offer to `magpaiskape`. It's not just about the coffee; it's about the conversation that comes with it.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang kolokyal at modernong termino. Ang `magpakape` ay ang mas karaniwan at pormal na katumbas. Ang 'iskape' ay balbal para sa 'kape'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, **magpaiskape** ka naman, ikaw ang may bonus!","translation":"Hey, **treat us to coffee**, you're the one who got a bonus!"},{"sentence":"Sige, **magpapaiskape** ako sa inyo bukas para sa tulong ninyo.","translation":"Okay, I'll **treat you all to coffee** tomorrow for your help."}]

translation: to dangle and shake; to swish around
meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw-galaw sa isang bagay, karaniwan ng kamay o paa, habang nakabitin o nakalubog sa likido.
etymology: From i- (causative prefix) + kawkaw (onomatopoeic root for swishing/dangling).
original_explanation: Imagine you're washing your hands in a "balde" (pail) and you just swish them around. That's 'ikawkaw'. Or when a dog wags its tail so hard it looks like it's swishing in the air. It's that dangling, swishy, wiggly motion.
usage_notes: Often used for hands or feet in water, or a dangling object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ikinawkaw** niya ang kanyang mga paa sa malamig na tubig ng ilog.","translation":"She **dangled and shook** her feet in the cold river water."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ikawkaw** ang daliri mo sa sarsa!","translation":"Don't **swish** your finger in the sauce!"}]

meaning_filipino: Sobrang pagtitipid o pagiging maramot sa paggastos o pagbibigay ng pera o ari-arian.
original_explanation: Describes that one friend in the barkada who always 'forgets' their wallet when it's time to pay. They count every single peso and would rather walk 5km than pay for a trike ride. Not to be confused with being 'matipid' (frugal), this is the next level. This is 'kuripot' on steroids.
usage_notes: A strong word to describe someone as extremely stingy. Synonymous with "kuripot" and "maramot".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **imot** sa iyong mga pagpapala; matutong magbahagi sa iba.","translation":"Don't be **stingy** with your blessings; learn to share with others."},{"sentence":"Napakasama ng kanyang reputasyon dahil sa pagiging **imot** niya kahit sa sariling pamilya.","translation":"His reputation is terrible because of how **miserly** he is even to his own family."}]

meaning_filipino: Pigilin o pahintuin ang mga taong nag-aaway o nagtatalo sa pamamagitan ng pamamagitan.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'awat'. It's the action of being the peacemaker. When your two friends are having a 'bardagulan' in the group chat, and you're the one messaging them privately to calm down, you're trying to 'awatin' sila. You are the designated 'tagapag-awat'.
usage_notes: The focus of the verb is on the people being pacified. For example, "Awatin mo sila" (Pacify them).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **awatin** ang mag-asawang nagtatalo sa gitna ng kalsada.","translation":"He tried to **pacify** the couple arguing in the middle of the street."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **awatin** ang dalawang pusang naglalaban para sa teritoryo.","translation":"It's hard to **separate** two cats fighting for territory."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sisidlan na karaniwang may apat na gilid, ilalim, at takip, na gawa sa karton, kahoy, o plastik, at ginagamit sa paglalagay o pag-iimbak ng mga bagay.
original_explanation: The official residence of your Shopee/Lazada orders. It’s the balikbayan’s best friend and the ultimate moving day essential. Also used to describe someone who thinks 'inside the box' ('Masyado kang de-**kahon** mag-isip!'). And let's not forget, it's a cat's favorite place on earth.
usage_notes: Can also refer to a drawer in a cabinet. The term 'de-kahon' refers to thinking that is rigid or conventional.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot mo nga ang **kahon** ng sapatos sa ilalim ng kama.","translation":"Please hand me the shoe **box** from under the bed."},{"sentence":"Iligpit mo ang mga laruan sa loob ng malaking **kahon**.","translation":"Put the toys away inside the big **box**."}]

translation: on the off chance; just in case
meaning_filipino: Pagsasagawa ng isang bagay na may pag-aalinlangan ngunit umaasa pa rin sa isang positibong resulta; pagsubok sa tsansa.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung mindset mo 'pag nag-chat ka sa crush mo ng 'Hi!' kahit 99.9% chance na seen-zoned ka lang. O 'pag tumaya ka sa lotto. You're shooting your shot, hoping for the best but expecting... well, you know. The official word for 'might as well try.'
usage_notes: Often used at the beginning of a sentence to express a hopeful but uncertain action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pabakasakali** akong nag-apply sa trabahong iyon, at natanggap naman ako.","translation":"**On the off chance**, I applied for that job, and I actually got it."},{"sentence":"Nagdala ako ng payong, **pabakasakali** na umulan mamaya.","translation":"I brought an umbrella, **just in case** it rains later."}]

translation: one can't tell, cannot be said
meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag na nagpapahiwatig ng kawalan ng katiyakan o kakayahang magbigay ng tiyak na impormasyon o hula.
etymology: Mula sa `hindi` (not) + `masasabi` (will be able to be said), nasa anyong panghinaharap ng `masabi`.
original_explanation: This is the official motto of marites everywhere. "Hindi masasabi, pero sabi ni ano..." It's the disclaimer before dropping the chismis. Also applies to unpredictable things, like PH weather or when your Shopee delivery will actually arrive. "Darating ba siya? **Hindi masasabi**."
usage_notes: Nagbibigay-diin sa kawalan ng katiyakan at ang kawalan ng kakayahang hulaan o sabihin ang isang bagay bilang katotohanan. Madalas gamitin upang ipahayag ang pagdududa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hindi masasabi** kung kailan matatapos ang pandemya.","translation":"**One can't tell** when the pandemic will end."},{"sentence":"**Hindi masasabi** kung sino ang mananalo hangga't hindi pa tapos ang laro.","translation":"**You can't say** who will win until the game is over."}]

translation: to number; to assign a number
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagtatalaga ng bilang o numero sa isang bagay o sa isang listahan.
original_explanation: It's what you do when you're the designated 'taga-lista' for raffle tickets at a Christmas party. You write down the numbers one by one, hoping your own ticket gets picked. Or when you're numbering your 'listahan ng utang' so you don't forget who owes you what.
usage_notes: Used for the act of assigning sequential numbers to items, often in a formal or organizational context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**magnumero** ka ng mga upuan para sa mga bisita.","translation":"Please **number** the chairs for the guests."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magnumero** ng bawat dokumento para sa tamang pag-file.","translation":"We need to **number** each document for proper filing."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi mataas ang kinalalagyan; may maliit na sukat mula sa ibaba pataas; o may mababang halaga, presyo, o antas.
etymology: From the prefix 'ma-' (indicating a quality) + 'baba' (lowness, bottom, chin).
original_explanation: Describes the sale price at the mall, your phone's battery life, your chance of winning the lottery, or your energy on a Monday morning. 'Mababa ang sahod' is the national anthem of the working class. Also refers to social status ('mababang uri') or being humble ('mababang-loob').
usage_notes: A highly versatile word. Can refer to physical height, price, score, social status, volume, or even morale. Its antonym is 'mataas' (high/tall).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong **mababa** ang sweldo para sa dami ng trabaho.","translation":"The salary is too **low** for the amount of work."},{"sentence":"Ang pangarap niya ay tulungan ang mga nasa **mababang** uri ng lipunan.","translation":"Her dream is to help those in the **lower** class of society."},{"sentence":"**Mababa** lang ang pader kaya madaling akyatin.","translation":"The wall is **low** so it's easy to climb."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sikat na online gaming platform kung saan maaaring gumawa at maglaro ng mga laro ang mga gumagamit.
etymology: Mula sa pangalang pantangi sa Ingles na "Roblox".
original_explanation: 'Yung mundo kung saan mas mayaman ka pa sa totoong buhay dahil sa Robux mo. Dito nagkikita ang mga bagets para mag-adopt ng virtual na pusa, mag-parkour, o maging cashier sa isang virtual na Jollibee. It's the digital 'tambayan'.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin ng mga batang Pilipino at tinedyer upang tukuyin ang gaming platform.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anak, tama na ang paglalaro ng **Roblox** at kumain ka na.","translation":"Child, stop playing **Roblox** and eat already."},{"sentence":"Nag-ipon ako ng baon para makabili ng Robux sa **Roblox**.","translation":"I saved my allowance to buy Robux on **Roblox**."}]

translation: to stray from the path; to go astray
meaning_filipino: Ang paglihis o pag-iba ng direksyon mula sa tama, mabuti, o inaasahang gawi at prinsipyo.
etymology: From ma- (verb prefix) + lihis (to deviate) + sa (at/on) + landas (path).
original_explanation: Ito yung sinasabi ng mga magulang mo kapag sumasama ka sa "bad influence" na barkada. It's when you started out wanting to be a doctor, but now you're a full-time vlogger reviewing milk tea. To "malihis sa landas" is to get sidetracked from your goals or moral compass, often with dramatic flair. The original "sana all" gone wrong.
usage_notes: A common idiomatic expression used to describe moral or directional deviation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula nang masangkot siya sa masamang barkada, tila **nalihis siya sa landas**.","translation":"Ever since he got involved with a bad crowd, it seems **he has strayed from the path**."},{"sentence":"Pinapaalalahanan ng mga magulang ang kanilang anak na huwag **malihis sa landas**.","translation":"Parents remind their children not **to go astray**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sustansiyang kemikal na nilalapat sa balat upang pigilan ang paglago ng mga mikroorganismong nagdudulot ng impeksyon.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung best friend mo 'pag nasugatan ka. 'Yung alcohol, Betadine, o 'yung mouthwash na parang apoy sa bibig mo. Its job is to kill the germs before they throw a party in your sugat. Panlaban sa impeksyon, para 'di lumala ang drama.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pang-uri (e.g., "solusyong antiseptik").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **antiseptik** ang sugat mo para hindi ito maimpeksyon.","translation":"Put **antiseptic** on your wound so it doesn't get infected."},{"sentence":"May **antiseptik** na katangian ang ilang halamang gamot.","translation":"Some medicinal plants have **antiseptic** properties."}]

translation: to spin; to rotate; to make something turn
meaning_filipino: Piliting umikot o paikutin ang isang bagay sa sarili nitong aksis; igalaw nang paikot.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative prefix) + `inog` (spin/rotation) + `-in` (object-focus suffix). `Inog` is a less common word for 'spin'.
original_explanation: This is what you do to a beyblade, a spinning top, or the 'Wheel of Names' during a team meeting to decide who gets the next task. It's the act of causing something to rotate, whether it's a toy, a wheel, or a small amount of capital to grow your side hustle.
usage_notes: Verb in imperative/infinitive form. Other forms: `pinainog` (past), `pinapainog` (present), `papainugin` (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **painugin** ang lumang trumpo.","translation":"He tried **to spin** the old spinning top."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **painugin** ang perang ito para kumita.","translation":"We need **to make** this money **turn** (i.e. invest/use it) to earn a profit."}]

translation: to be tethered; to be tied up
meaning_filipino: Ang isang tao o hayop ay mailagay sa isang tali o posas upang hindi makagalaw o makatakas.
original_explanation: Like how you feel when you're stuck in a toxic relationship, or literally, how you tie your carabao so it doesn't run off to the next barangay. It's being held in place, whether by a rope or by your feelings.
usage_notes: Primarily used for animals, but can be used figuratively for people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **mapugal** ang aso para hindi ito makakagat ng mga dumaraan.","translation":"The dog needs **to be tethered** so it won't bite passersby."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **mapugal** sa isang relasyon na may katatagan.","translation":"He wants **to be tied down** in a stable relationship."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unti-unting pagkawala o paghina ng isang bagay, tulad ng damdamin, liwanag, alaala, o buhay.
etymology: From pag- + the first syllable of mag- (ma-) + mag- + maliw (to fade, cease).
original_explanation: This is the official feeling of a 'walang forever' moment. It's the slow fade of a love team's popularity, the dying embers of a campfire, or that hugot feeling when you realize the spark in your relationship is gone. Pagmamaliw is the poetic, melancholic process of something coming to an end. It’s not a sudden stop, but a gradual, often sad, disappearance.
usage_notes: Poetic and often used in literature, songs, and formal speech to describe the fading of emotions, light, life, or memory.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nararamdaman na niya ang **pagmamaliw** ng kanilang pag-ibig.","translation":"She could already feel the **fading** of their love."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagmamaliw** ng araw sa kanluran ay isang magandang tanawin.","translation":"The **waning** of the sun in the west is a beautiful sight."}]

translation: to take a picture of (a specific subject)
meaning_filipino: Kunan ng litrato ang isang partikular na tao o bagay bilang pangunahing paksa.
etymology: From Spanish 'retrato' (portrait). The verb is formed with the suffix '-in'.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung "Picturan mo ako!" moment. The focus is on a specific person or object. While 'retratuhan' is for the whole barkada with the background, 'retratuhin' is for your solo profile pic. It's more direct, more focused on the subject. "Bes, retratuhin mo ako, 'yung pang-profile pic ang dating."
usage_notes: See usage notes for 'retratuhan'. This verb implies a direct object as the focus of the photograph.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **retratuhin** ang lola ko habang nagkakape siya sa umaga.","translation":"I want to **take a picture of** my grandmother while she's having coffee in the morning."},{"sentence":"Sino ang gusto mong **retratuhin** para sa proyekto natin sa sining?","translation":"Who do you want to **photograph** for our art project?"}]

translation: to align; to conform; to adjust
meaning_filipino: Ibagay, itugma, o isunod ang isang bagay, kilos, o ideya sa isang pamantayan, sitwasyon, o kagustuhan.
original_explanation: This is your life skill for when you need to "read the room." You adjust your behavior to fit the situation. You "iayon" your OOTD to the party's theme. You "iayon" your proposal to what the boss wants to hear. It's the art of blending in and making things fit, like a human chameleon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **iayon** ang mga batas sa nagbabagong panahon.","translation":"The laws need to be **adjusted** to the changing times."},{"sentence":"**Iayon** mo ang iyong sagot sa tanong ng guro.","translation":"**Align** your answer with the teacher's question."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paulit-ulit na pagpasok at paglabas sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: Same vibe as 'labas-masok'. Imagine your jowa's mood swings, **labas-pasok** sa pagiging sweet at toyo. Or the Wi-Fi signal in your area. Minsan anjan, minsan wala.
usage_notes: Isang mas direktang kasingkahulugan ng "labas-masok" at madalas na ginagamit nang palitan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **labas-pasok** na lang sa ospital ang matanda dahil sa kanyang sakit.","translation":"The old man was just **in and out** of the hospital because of his illness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal at mapanirang-puri para sa isang babaeng nagbebenta ng aliw o isang taong itinuturing na may magulong buhay-pag-ibig.
etymology: Possibly onomatopoeic, from the sound of pounding or knocking ("pokpok"), metaphorically extended.
original_explanation: This is a harsh, derogatory term you definitely shouldn't use. It's an insult thrown around to shame someone, usually a woman, for their perceived sexual behavior. It's the verbal equivalent of a slut-shaming grenade. While its primary meaning is 'prostitute,' it's often used more broadly (and unfairly) as a general insult. Handle with extreme caution, or better yet, just don't use it.
usage_notes: A highly offensive and derogatory slang term. Its use is strongly discouraged as it is considered vulgar and misogynistic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumamit ng salitang '**pokpok**' dahil ito ay masakit at mapanlait sa kapwa.","translation":"Do not use the word '**pokpok**' because it is hurtful and insulting to others."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtawag sa isang tao na '**pokpok**' ay isang anyo ng berbal na pang-aabuso.","translation":"Calling someone a '**pokpok**' is a form of verbal abuse."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag o kasunduan na nagsasaad ng tiyak na gagawin o hindi gagawin sa hinaharap; isang panata.
etymology: From `pang-` + `ako` (I, me), literally meaning "my undertaking" or "I vouch for this."
original_explanation: Ah, the national currency of "sana all" and the foundation of "hugot" culture. It's what politicians give during elections and what your toxic ex gave you before they ghosted. Best served when fulfilled, but often ends up "napako" (unfulfilled). Handle with care.
usage_notes: The verb form is `mangako` (to promise). The idiom `napako ang pangako` (the promise was nailed) means a promise was broken.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuparin mo ang iyong **pangako** sa akin.","translation":"Fulfill your **promise** to me."},{"sentence":"Lahat ay pawang **pangako** na napako.","translation":"Everything was just a broken **promise**."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasuotang isinusuot sa ilalim ng pangunahing damit, karaniwang katabi ng balat.
original_explanation: Your undies, briefs, boxers, bra, sando. The first layer of your OOTD that only a select few (or the whole world, if you have a laundry line outside) get to see. The foundation of your fashion statement.
usage_notes: Commonly used as a collective term for undergarments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang magdala ng malinis na **panloob** para sa biyahe.","translation":"Don't forget to bring clean **underwear** for the trip."},{"sentence":"Nakatiklop nang maayos ang kanyang mga **panloob** sa aparador.","translation":"His **undergarments** are folded neatly in the closet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasabi o pagtukoy sa isang bagay, tao, o ideya sa isang pahayag o usapan, karaniwang sa maikling paraan.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you want to subtly drop a hint. 'Uy, may bago palang cafe sa kanto,' you say, hoping your friend gets the message. It's the verbal equivalent of a passive-aggressive post, or just, you know, mentioning something normally. 'Nga pala, 'di ko pa birthday ha, pero I like that bag...'
usage_notes: Standard verb for 'to mention.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **bumanggit** ng tungkol sa nakaraan.","translation":"Don't **mention** anything about the past."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **bumanggit** ng pangalan ko?","translation":"Who **mentioned** my name?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, koponan, o hayop na nagwagi at nanaig laban sa lahat ng kalaban sa isang kumpetisyon o paligsahan.
etymology: From English 'champion,' which came from Old French 'champion.'
original_explanation: Same as English, but with a Pinoy twist. It's not just for sports. Your lola's adobo? Champion! The person who can navigate EDSA during rush hour without losing their mind? Champion! That friend who aced an exam without studying? Champion! It's a high-five in word form, a recognition of excellence in any field, from the basketball court to the kitchen.
usage_notes: Used both in its literal sense (sports, contests) and as a colloquial adjective to mean 'excellent' or 'the best.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Hidilyn Diaz ay isang **champion** sa weightlifting.","translation":"Hidilyn Diaz is a **champion** in weightlifting."},{"sentence":"**Champion** talaga ang luto ng nanay ko, walang makakatalo.","translation":"My mom's cooking is really **the best**, nothing can beat it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipakita nang may pagmamalaki at pagyayabang ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay mga ari-arian o tagumpay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `i-` (nagsasaad ng sanhi), `pagpa-` (nagsasaad ng sanhi), at `dangya` (ostentation).
original_explanation: Same as `ipagmarangya`. It's your tita from the States posting her new designer bag on Facebook with the caption "A simple gift for myself." It's the act of making sure everyone sees what you have, usually something expensive or hard to get.
usage_notes: Kasingkahulugan ng `ipagmarangya` at `ipagyabang`. Ang unlaping `pagpa-` ay nagbibigay-diin sa kilos ng pagpapakitang-gilas sa iba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing may bago siyang gamit, kailangan niya itong **ipagparangya** sa social media.","translation":"Every time she has a new thing, she needs to **flaunt** it on social media."},{"sentence":"Hindi magandang ugali ang **ipagparangya** ang yaman sa harap ng mga naghihirap.","translation":"It's not a good habit to **show off** wealth in front of those who are struggling."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sistema ng mga prinsipyo at pamantayan hinggil sa tama at maling pag-uugali.
original_explanation: This is the more formal, 'pang-thesis paper' version of 'moral'. It’s the whole system of what's considered right or wrong by a group or society. It's the topic of deep conversations over coffee, or heated arguments on social media about politics and personal choices.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuwestiyon ng marami ang **moralidad** ng kanyang mga desisyon.","translation":"Many questioned the **morality** of his decisions."},{"sentence":"Ang pagpapanatili ng **moralidad** sa lipunan ay isang malaking hamon.","translation":"Maintaining **morality** in society is a big challenge."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang likas na kalagayan, katangian, o kahulugan ng isang bagay; ang pagkilala o pagturing sa isang bagay bilang isang partikular na uri.
original_explanation: It's like the official 'label' or 'status' of something. What is its essence? What is it considered to be? It's a deep word, like asking for the katuringan of 'love'—is it a feeling, a choice, or just a chemical reaction in the brain? More formally, it's how something is defined or regarded.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat literary term. 'Katangian' (characteristic) or 'kahulugan' (meaning) are more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ba ang tunay na **katuringan** ng pagiging isang bayani?","translation":"What is the true **nature** of being a hero?"},{"sentence":"Ang pagtulong sa kapwa ay **katuringan** ng isang mabuting tao.","translation":"Helping others is a **characteristic** of a good person."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng paa na nasa likuran, sa ilalim ng bukong-bukong.
original_explanation: Ito yung parte ng paa mo na laging bitak-bitak at nagiging kulay abo kapag hindi ka nag-lotion. Achilles' heel, but make it Pinoy. Ito rin ang unang sumasakit kapag matagal kang nakapila sa MRT o sa bayaran ng bills.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit ang aking **sakong** dahil sa bagong sapatos.","translation":"My **heel** hurts because of my new shoes."},{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng petroleum jelly sa kanyang mga **sakong** para hindi ito maging tuyo.","translation":"She put petroleum jelly on her **heels** to prevent them from getting dry."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagbibigay ng saya, libangan, o ginhawa sa damdamin.
original_explanation: This is that funny TikTok video you watch on repeat, your favorite feel-good movie, or your tita's endless supply of chismis. Anything that takes your mind off your problems and makes you smile or laugh is nakaaaliw. The opposite of nakababagot.
usage_notes: Has a dual sense of 'entertaining' (like a show) and 'comforting' (like a friend's presence). The context determines the exact shade of meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **nakaaaliw** panoorin ang mga lumang comedy films.","translation":"It's truly **entertaining** to watch old comedy films."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sasakyang may dalawang gulong na pinapatakbo ng motor.
original_explanation: The unofficial king of Philippine roads. It's your Grab delivery, your Angkas ride, and your neighbor's noisy wakeup call at 5 AM. It can fit a family of five, two sacks of rice, and a small dog. The solution to (and sometimes cause of) traffic.
usage_notes: Often shortened to 'motor' in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng bagong **motorsiklo** para sa kanyang trabaho.","translation":"He bought a new **motorcycle** for his job."},{"sentence":"Maingay ang tambutso ng **motorsiklo** mo.","translation":"Your **motorcycle's** exhaust pipe is noisy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng inklinasyon o pagpanig sa isang partikular na panig, ideya, o tao; hindi patas o obhektibo.
original_explanation: When your mom is the referee for a game between you and your sibling, but you know she's secretly rooting for the 'panganay'. That's 'may-kiling'. It's having a favorite, a bias. It’s the news outlet that only shows one side of the story or the basketball ref who seems to only call fouls on the visiting team.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical tilt or a figurative bias.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang desisyon ng hukom ay tila **may-kiling** sa mas mayaman na partido.","translation":"The judge's decision seemed **biased** towards the wealthier party."},{"sentence":"Halatang **may-kiling** ang balita dahil puro papuri lang ang sinasabi.","translation":"The news is obviously **partial** because it only says praises."}]

translation: to abuse; to take advantage of
meaning_filipino: Gawin nang labis o sobra; samantalahin ang kabaitan, kapangyarihan, o kahinaan ng iba.
original_explanation: That feeling when you've given 110% effort on a project, but your boss's feedback is still 'kulang pa'. Or when you lend a friend money once, and they suddenly treat you like their personal ATM. That's them taking advantage of your kindness. It's the act of exploiting a good thing until it breaks.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of exploiting someone's kindness, resources, or authority. It implies crossing a boundary of what is reasonable or fair.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagmalabisan** ang kabaitan ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Do not **abuse** the kindness of your parents."},{"sentence":"Ang kapangyarihan ay hindi dapat **pagmalabisan** para sa pansariling interes.","translation":"Power should not be **taken advantage of** for personal interest."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan o sanhi ng kaligayahan o kagalakan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Seeing that 'sahod is in' notification is the **ikasaya** of every employee. A surprise food delivery from your jowa? That's the **ikasaya** of your day. It's the thing that makes you go 'sana all' for someone else's good fortune.
usage_notes: A common causative verb to express what brings joy or happiness to someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagdating mo ay tiyak na **ikasaya** ni Lola.","translation":"Your arrival will surely **cause happiness** for Grandma."},{"sentence":"Ano ba ang maaaring kong gawin na **ikasaya** mo?","translation":"What can I do that will **make you happy**?"}]

translation: to leave a surplus; to do/give in excess
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaan o paggawa ng higit pa sa kinakailangan o inaasahan.
original_explanation: The Filipino hospitality default setting. It's when you cook for 5 people but the food is enough for 15, 'para sure.' Or when you give a pasalubong, you don't just give one, you give enough for their entire office. 'Magpasobra ka na, baka may humabol.' It's the opposite of 'sakto lang'.
usage_notes: Implies an intentional act of creating more than what is needed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging nagluluto si nanay na may kasamang **pagpapasobra** para may maibigay sa mga kapitbahay.","translation":"Mom always cooks with the intention of **leaving a surplus** to give to the neighbors."},{"sentence":"Mas mabuting **magpasobra** ng budget kaysa magkulang sa biyahe.","translation":"It's better to **have an excess** budget than to be short during the trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pang-akit o pagbihag sa damdamin o atensyon ng isang tao sa hinaharap; ang akto ng paghuli.
original_explanation: The future tense of 'landi.' 'Yung titig mong 'mamimihag' ng puso. Or your OOTD that you believe will capture everyone's attention at the party. Pwede ring literal, like a hunter who will capture a wild animal. But mostly, it's about capturing feelings, not animals.
usage_notes: Future tense of 'mamihag'. Can be used literally (to capture a prisoner/animal) or figuratively (to capture someone's heart or attention). The figurative sense is more common in modern usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala siyang ang kanyang ngiti ay **mamimihag** sa puso ng dalaga.","translation":"He believes his smile **will capture** the maiden's heart."},{"sentence":"Ang magandang tanawin sa tuktok ng bundok ay tiyak na **mamimihag** sa sinumang aakyat doon.","translation":"The beautiful view from the mountain top will surely **enthrall** anyone who climbs it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkain sa pagitan ng mga pangunahing oras ng pagkain tulad ng agahan, tanghalian, at hapunan.
etymology: From Spanish 'merienda' (afternoon snack), combined with the Tagalog verb prefix 'mag-'.
original_explanation: The sacred Filipino ritual that happens around 3-4 PM. It's not lunch, it's not dinner, it's the magical meal in between powered by pancit canton, fishball, or banana cue. It’s the reason why we have two words for "snack" (meryenda and... another meryenda).
usage_notes: A very common daily activity in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, **magmeryenda** tayo ng turon at sago't gulaman.","translation":"Come on, let's **have a snack** of turon and sago't gulaman."},{"sentence":"Tumigil muna kami sa pagtatrabaho para **magmeryenda**.","translation":"We stopped working for a while to **have a snack**."}]

translation: to be summoned; to be called for
meaning_filipino: Maging paksa ng isang pagtawag o panawagan, karaniwan ay biglaan o hindi inaasahan.
original_explanation: That mini heart attack when your boss's name flashes on your screen for an unscheduled call. Or when you were a kid and heard 'Pinapatawag ka sa principal's office.' It's that feeling of being summoned, and it's rarely to be told you won the lottery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla akong **napatawag** sa entablado para tumanggap ng parangal.","translation":"I was suddenly **called for** on stage to receive an award."},{"sentence":"Kinabahan siya nang **mapatawag** sa pulong ng mga board member.","translation":"She got nervous when she **was summoned** to the board members' meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ituring, kilalanin, o igalang na parang sariling ama.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'ama' at hulaping pandiwa na '-in'.
original_explanation: It's when you give someone the "Honorary Dad" award. Maybe he's your mentor, your tito, or your boss who always gives you fatherly advice (and approves your vacation leave). You basically "father-zone" him.
usage_notes: Isang bihirang gamiting pandiwa na may tiyak na kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Inamaka** niya ang kanyang ninong dahil ito ang nag-aruga sa kanya mula pagkabata.","translation":"He **treated his godfather as a father** because he was the one who raised him since childhood."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **amakin**, kaibigan lang ang turing ko sa iyo.","translation":"Don't **treat me like a father**, I only see you as a friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng musika na nagmula sa Estados Unidos na kinatatangian ng sinkopadong ritmo, improbisasyon, at malakas na indayog (swing).
original_explanation: That 'tito music' that's actually super complex and cool. It's the kind of music playing in a fancy hotel lobby or a speakeasy-themed bar. Think saxophones, walking basslines, and musicians just making stuff up on the spot (improvising). It's music for the soul... and for your expensive coffee.
usage_notes: Ang pagbaybay na 'jazz' ay mas karaniwang ginagamit, lalo na sa mga pormal na sulatin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang makinig sa mga lumang tugtugin na **dyas** tuwing gabi.","translation":"He likes listening to old **jazz** music every night."},{"sentence":"May banda ng **dyas** na tumutugtog sa bar na iyon.","translation":"There's a **jazz** band playing at that bar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pananakit o pagpaparusa sa isang tao bilang tugon sa isang naunang pinsala o kasamaang ginawa nito.
original_explanation: The plot of every other teleserye. It's when the 'api' protagonist comes back rich and fabulous to crush their enemies. In real life, it's when you post a fire selfie after a breakup. 'Sweet revenge' is its English-speaking cousin.
usage_notes: Carries a strong connotation of vengeance, but can also be used in a lighter, figurative way. Often used interchangeably with 'paghihiganti'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagganti** ay hindi kailanman nagdudulot ng tunay na kapayapaan.","translation":"**Revenge** never brings true peace."},{"sentence":"Bilang **pagganti**, kinain niya ang natirang pagkain sa ref.","translation":"As **retaliation**, she ate the leftover food in the fridge."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsira o pagbali sa isang bagay na matigas at mahaba, tulad ng patpat o sanga, sa pamamagitan ng puwersa.
original_explanation: ‘Yung feeling na gusto mong **bakliin** ‘yung SIM card mo para ‘di ka na niya ma-contact. It's the act of snapping something in two, usually out of frustration or to make a point. Like breaking a pencil after a hard exam.
usage_notes: Often used for snapping long, thin, rigid objects like sticks, pencils, or bones.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **bakliin** ang lapis ko, bago pa 'yan.","translation":"Don't **snap** my pencil, it's still new."},{"sentence":"Sinubukang **bakliin** ng bata ang sanga ng puno.","translation":"The child tried to **break** the tree branch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging abâ; karukhaan, paghihirap, o pagiging kaawa-awa.
etymology: From the root word "abâ" (lowly, pitiful) with the "ka- -an" circumfix, which forms abstract nouns indicating a state or quality.
original_explanation: This is a drama-level word. It's not just "sad" or "poor," it's the kind of deep, soul-crushing misery you see in a teleserye where the main character has lost everything. It's the state of being in the "putik" (mud), both literally and figuratively. It has the weight of generations of hardship in it. Not a word you use lightly when you're just having a bad day.
usage_notes: A formal and literary word used to describe a state of extreme poverty or wretchedness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang itaas ang kanyang pamilya mula sa **kaabaan**.","translation":"He wants to lift his family from **misery**."},{"sentence":"Makikita sa kanyang mga mata ang **kaabaan** ng kanyang pinagdaanan.","translation":"You can see in his eyes the **wretchedness** of what he has been through."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbago ng relihiyon, paniniwala, o pananaw sa buhay.
original_explanation: This is someone who had a major change of heart. That friend who used to hate K-dramas but is now a certified fan? A kumbertido. The die-hard Android user who just bought an iPhone? A kumbertido. It’s someone who crossed over to 'the other side' of a belief or preference.
usage_notes: Can be used for religion, political affiliation, brand loyalty, or any significant change in opinion or lifestyle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dati siyang kritiko, ngunit isa na siyang **kumbertido** at masugid na tagasuporta ngayon.","translation":"He used to be a critic, but now he is a **convert** and a staunch supporter."},{"sentence":"Maraming **kumbertido** sa bagong relihiyon ang dumalo sa pagtitipon.","translation":"Many **converts** to the new religion attended the gathering."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na tawag o pamagat para sa isang lalaki, lalo na sa isang may awtoridad o mas matanda.
original_explanation: The universal Filipino term of respect for any male human you don't know, from the security guard ('Sir, paki-check po ng bag'), your BPO team lead ('Sir, for escalation po'), the waiter ('Sir, ano pong order ninyo?'), to your professor. It has completely replaced 'Ginoo' in daily conversation. Often paired with 'Ma'am'.
usage_notes: Extremely common in the Philippines as a form of address.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paumanhin po, **Sir**, saan po ang pinakamalapit na CR?","translation":"Excuse me, **Sir**, where is the nearest restroom?"},{"sentence":"Good morning, **Sir**! Handa na po ang report ninyo.","translation":"Good morning, **Sir**! Your report is ready."}]

translation: fine dust (from decayed wood or bamboo)
meaning_filipino: Pinong-pinong alikabok na karaniwang nagmumula sa kahoy o kawayan na inaanay o nabubulok.
original_explanation: 'Yung alikabok na nakikita mo sa ilalim ng lumang aparador o sa sahig na gawa sa kahoy? 'Yung parang sawdust pero galing sa anay (termites)? 'Yan ang bulukabok. It's the ghost of furniture past. Parang feelings mo para sa ex mo, bulukabok na lang—dusty and decayed.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the dust-like frass left by wood-boring insects like termites or powderpost beetles ('bukbok').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga **bulukabok** sa ilalim ng mesa; senyales ito na may anay.","translation":"There is **wood dust** under the table; it's a sign of termites."},{"sentence":"Pinagpag niya ang lumang libro at umalimbukay ang **bulukabok**.","translation":"He dusted off the old book and **fine dust** billowed out."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging matamlay, kawalan ng sigla, enerhiya, o interes.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung feeling mo tuwing Lunes ng umaga, o 'pag 'di ka pa nagkakape. Parang kaluluwa mo, nag-AWOL. That state of being low-batt, both physically and emotionally. You're not sad, you're not happy, you're just... there. Like a phone at 1% battery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dama ko ang **katamlayan** sa opisina dahil wala pang sahod.","translation":"I can feel the **lethargy** in the office because it's not payday yet."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng sakit, nanatili ang **katamlayan** sa kanyang katawan.","translation":"After the illness, a sense of **listlessness** remained in his body."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng matinding puna sa isang partikular na bagay, ideya, o gawa.
original_explanation: Similar to 'batikusan', but 'batikusin' is more direct and object-focused. You don't just criticize a person, you 'batikusin' their specific action, their statement, their movie. It’s the verb for when you have a specific target for your 'batikos'.
usage_notes: The '-in' suffix makes it object-focused. You are doing the action *to* the object. 'Batikusan' can feel like criticizing a person/group, while 'batikusin' is often about criticizing a specific thing or action. They are often interchangeable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming nais **batikusin** ang sistema ng hustisya sa bansa.","translation":"Many want **to criticize** the country's justice system."},{"sentence":"Madaling **batikusin** ang gawa ng iba, ngunit mahirap gumawa ng sarili.","translation":"It's easy **to criticize** the work of others, but it's hard to create your own."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may mataas na antas ng pinag-aralan, pino ang kilos, at malawak ang kaalaman sa sining at kultura. Maaari ring tumukoy sa lupang tinamnan at inalagaan.
original_explanation: Describes someone who is 'woke' in the original sense—educated, well-mannered, and has good taste. They know which fork to use, can talk about art without sounding like they just read Wikipedia, and probably enjoy a good cup of tea. It's the human equivalent of a well-tended garden versus a patch of talahib.
usage_notes: Can describe a person (refined) or land (tilled, planted). A formal and somewhat uncommon word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata sa kanyang pananalita at kilos na siya ay isang **kultibadong** tao.","translation":"It's obvious from his speech and actions that he is a **cultured** person."},{"sentence":"Ang dating tiwangwang na lupa ay isa na ngayong **kultibadong** bukirin.","translation":"The once-idle land is now a **cultivated** farm."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak at tiwangwang na lugar na karaniwang walang naninirahan o may kaunting pananim lamang; isang disyerto o gubat.
original_explanation: This is the 'middle of nowhere' place. A wild, uninhabited area. Think Lion King's Pride Lands vs. the elephant graveyard. The graveyard is an **ilang**. It gives off a vibe of being vast, empty, and maybe a little bit lonely or dangerous.
usage_notes: Pronunciation is key. Stress is on the first syllable /I-lang/, unlike the adjective 'iláng' /i-LANG/ (a few).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naligaw ang mga manlalakbay sa malawak na **ilang**.","translation":"The travelers got lost in the vast **wilderness**."},{"sentence":"Tanging mga mababangis na hayop ang nakikita sa **ilang** na iyon.","translation":"Only wild animals are seen in that **desolate place**."}]

translation: to set on fire; to burn up
meaning_filipino: Sunugin o pag-apuyin ang isang bagay nang sadya, karaniwan sa isang malaking apoy.
original_explanation: What you want to do with your ex's old love letters (or your pile of bills). It's a more dramatic version of 'sunugin.' It's not just burning, it's making a bonfire out of it. 'Silabin na 'yang mga resibo ng luho mo para 'di ka na ma-stress!'
usage_notes: Implies a large, open flame or bonfire. More intense than 'sunugin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **silabin** ang mga tuyong dahon sa bakuran.","translation":"They decided to **burn** the dry leaves in the yard."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **silabin** ang bahay dahil lang sa isang ipis! biro niya.","translation":"Don't **set the house on fire** just because of one cockroach! he joked."}]

translation: to be able to finish; to be able to graduate
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang tapusin ang isang gawain, proyekto, o pag-aaral.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal of every student tired of puyat and deadlines, and the ultimate dream of their parents. It's that feeling of relief when you finally submit your last requirement or pass your final exam. "Kahit anong hirap, basta makatapos lang ng pag-aaral."
usage_notes: Very commonly used in the context of finishing one's studies (graduating).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsisikap siyang magtrabaho para **makatapos** ang kanyang mga kapatid.","translation":"He works hard so his siblings can **finish** their studies."},{"sentence":"Kailan ka kaya **makatapos** sa pinapanood mong K-drama series?","translation":"When will you be able to **finish** that K-drama series you're watching?"}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng puwang o agwat ang isang bagay o lugar.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend wants to sit between you and your bae on the jeepney. You 'make space.' 'Bes, puwangan mo naman ako dyan.' It's the act of creating that gap, whether it's on a bench or in a schedule.
usage_notes: The verb form of 'puwang', meaning to actively create a gap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Puwangan** mo ang mga libro sa estante para hindi magkadikit.","translation":"**Make space** between the books on the shelf so they aren't touching."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **puwangan** ang iskedyul para sa biglaang pulong.","translation":"We need to **make space** in the schedule for the sudden meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Paligiran ang isang lugar upang sakupin o piliting sumuko.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of `kubkob`. It's the action of surrounding something. When your officemates all gather around your desk because you have J.CO donuts, they are about to `kubkubin` your treats. It’s the act of creating a siege.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalak ng kalaban na **kubkubin** ang buong kuta sa loob ng isang linggo.","translation":"The enemy planned to **besiege** the entire fort within a week."},{"sentence":"Huwag ninyong **kubkubin** ang lamesa, may pagkain para sa lahat.","translation":"Don't **encircle** the table, there's food for everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging labis na sensitibo o madaling masaktan ang damdamin.
etymology: Mula sa 'pagka-' + 'maramdamin' (sensitibo, madaling masaktan ang damdamin).
original_explanation: This is your friend who gets 'tampo' if you don't 'like' their new profile pic. You have to walk on eggshells around them because any joke can be taken as a personal attack. It's the 'hugot' waiting to happen. They feel things deeply, but mostly about themselves.
usage_notes: Madalas may bahagyang negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig na ang isang tao ay madaling magdamdam o masaktan. Iba sa 'pagkamapagdamdam' na tungkol sa pakikiramay sa iba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang labis na **pagkamaramdamin** ay maaaring maging hadlang sa pakikipagkaibigan.","translation":"Being **overly sensitive** can be a hindrance to friendships."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at marangyang handaan o salu-salo, karaniwang para sa pagdiriwang ng isang mahalagang okasyon.
etymology: Salitang Tagalog na matatagpuan sa mga lumang panitikan.
original_explanation: This is the formal, almost archaic word for "party." You don't have a **piging** for your despidida. You have a **piging** if you're a datu in a historical epic or if you're in a Florante at Laura play. It's the OG "kainan na!" but with more class and probably a whole lechon. Today, you'd just say handaan or party. Using **piging** makes you sound like you're about to read from a scroll.
usage_notes: Itinuturing na pormal, pampanitikan, o medyo makalumang salita. Ang 'handaan' o 'salo-salo' ay mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na pagsasalita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **piging** ang inihanda ng hari para sa pagbabalik ng kanyang anak.","translation":"A grand **banquet** was prepared by the king for his son's return."},{"sentence":"Lahat ay maligayang dumalo sa **piging** na idinaos sa plasa.","translation":"Everyone happily attended the **feast** held at the plaza."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginawa nang hindi tinitingnan, sapilitan, o walang pag-aalinlangan; literal na nakapikit ang mga mata.
original_explanation: How you accept a task you don't want to do ('Sige na nga, pikit-mata kong gagawin 'to'). Or how you pay for something expensive you know you shouldn't have bought. It's the gesture of surrendering to fate, to your boss, or to your 'budol' impulses.
usage_notes: Can be used literally (doing something with eyes physically closed) or metaphorically (doing something reluctantly or without full consideration).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pikit-mata** niyang ininom ang mapait na gamot.","translation":"He **reluctantly** (lit. with eyes closed) drank the bitter medicine."},{"sentence":"**Pikit-mata** kong binayaran ang bill ng credit card matapos ang 12.12 sale.","translation":"I **blindly** paid the credit card bill after the 12.12 sale."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapadala ng isang bagay, mensahe, o impormasyon sa hinaharap. Ito ay isang Taglish na anyo ng pandiwa na karaniwang ginagamit sa di-pormal na usapan.
etymology: Tagalog prefix 'mag-' + future tense infix '-se-' + English root 'send'. A classic Taglish construction.
original_explanation: The future tense of 'I'll slide into your DMs.' This is what you promise your boss when they ask for the report ('Yes po, magsesend na po ako!'), or your friend when they ask for the chismis ('Wait lang, magsesend ako ng screenshots!'). It's a promise of digital delivery.
usage_notes: This is a very common Taglish verb form, used in both spoken and informal written communication (like chat or text). The formal Filipino equivalent is 'magpapadala'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magsesend** ako ng email sa iyo mamaya.","translation":"I **will send** you an email later."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magsesend** ng minutes ng meeting natin?","translation":"Who **will send** the minutes of our meeting?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kapansanan o pagkawala ng kakayahang gumalaw nang normal, karaniwan dahil sa isang aksidente o malubhang sakit.
original_explanation: This is a heavy one. 'Bumalda' means to be maimed or crippled, usually from a serious accident. It's the kind of word you'd hear in a news report: "Bumalda ang drayber matapos ang salpukan." It's the tragic outcome, the loss of function, the reason for a PWD card.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat dated term. "Naparalisa" or "nalumpo" are more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming sundalo ang **bumalda** dahil sa giyera.","translation":"Many soldiers **were crippled** because of the war."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa polio, **bumalda** ang kanyang mga binti noong siya'y bata pa.","translation":"Because of polio, his legs **became incapacitated** when he was still young."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahing ideya o paksa ng isang usapin, argumento, o diskusyon.
original_explanation: 'Yan yung "What's your point?" moment sa gitna ng chismisan o meeting. Ano ba talaga ang pinag-uusapan at bakit ito mahalaga? 'Pag sinabing "Diretsuhin mo na ang punto mo," ibig sabihin, tama na ang paligoy-ligoy.
usage_notes: Used in discussions, debates, and arguments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ba talaga ang **punto** mo sa sinasabi mo?","translation":"What really is the **point** of what you're saying?"},{"sentence":"Maganda ang kanyang mga **punto** sa debate.","translation":"His **points** in the debate were good."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng impeksiyon o pagkalat ng mikrobyo sa isang sugat o sa katawan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung nangyayari sa sugat mo 'pag hindi mo nilinis at tinakpan. O 'yung nangyayari sa puso mo 'pag 'di ka nag-move on—nagiging toxic. Pwede ring mangyari sa computer mo 'pag kung anu-anong "Download Free Movie" button ang kini-click mo. Biglang magkaka-virus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Linisin mong mabuti ang sugat mo para hindi **maimpeksiyon**.","translation":"Clean your wound well so it won't **get infected**."},{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa ospital nang **maimpeksiyon** ang kanyang kagat ng aso.","translation":"He was brought to the hospital when his dog bite **got infected**."}]

translation: to match multiple things; to reconcile various items
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasaayos o paghahanap ng katugma para sa maramihang bagay, ideya, o tao upang magkaroon ng kaayusan at pagkakaugnay-ugnay.
original_explanation: This is 'pagtugmain' on steroids. It's not just matching two things; it's a full-blown logistical challenge. Think of an event planner trying to match guests to tables, a programmer trying to reconcile different data sets, or a fashion stylist creating multiple coordinated outfits. It's a complex puzzle of making many different pieces fit together perfectly.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'tugma' implies a plural or complex matching task.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang trabaho ng wedding planner ay **pagtugma-tugmain** ang lahat ng detalye, mula sa bulaklak hanggang sa pagkain.","translation":"The wedding planner's job is **to match** all the details, from the flowers to the food."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pagtugma-tugmain** ang mga datos mula sa iba't ibang source.","translation":"You need **to reconcile** the data from various sources."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sarsa, karaniwang gawa sa kamatis, sibuyas, at sili. Tumutukoy din ito sa isang uri ng sayaw mula sa Latin America.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, 'salsa' can mean two things. First, the dip you get with your nachos at a Mexican resto. Second, that dance your Tita learns on weekends to feel young again. Either way, it's spicy and full of flavor.
usage_notes: The context usually makes it clear whether it refers to the food or the dance. For food, it's often used interchangeably with 'sarsa,' but 'salsa' specifically implies the chunky, often spicy, tomato-based dip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ipares ang **salsa** sa pritong isda.","translation":"**Sauce** pairs well with fried fish."},{"sentence":"Nag-eenjoy siyang sumayaw ng **salsa** tuwing Sabado ng gabi.","translation":"She enjoys dancing the **salsa** every Saturday night."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang gawain ay ang palihim o maingat na pagbabantay at pagmamasid sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: The more intense, high-stakes version of a 'tagamasid'. This isn't just casual watching; this is 'James Bond' level surveillance. They're the lookout for a heist, the spy in a movie, or your overprotective parent secretly watching you on your first date. There's a sense of purpose and secrecy here.
usage_notes: Carries a connotation of vigilance, secrecy, or surveillance. More intense than 'tagamasid'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga sundalo ay nagsilbing **tagamatyag** sa hangganan ng bansa.","translation":"The soldiers served as **watchers** at the country's border."},{"sentence":"May **tagamatyag** sa tore na nagbabantay kung may paparating na kaaway.","translation":"There is a **lookout** in the tower watching for any approaching enemies."}]

translation: to take turns (repeatedly); to alternate continuously
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pagsasalin-salin o pagpapalitan sa isang gawain, posisyon, o tungkulin ng dalawa o higit pang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: Think of a BPO graveyard shift. You and your teammate maghali-halili in taking calls and taking coffee breaks. It’s the constant, repeated act of taking turns. Or when you're on a long road trip, you and your friend maghali-halili sa pag-drive. It's more dynamic and continuous than just 'maghalili'.
usage_notes: The reduplication of 'hali-' emphasizes the repetitive or continuous nature of the alternation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **maghali-halili** sa pagbabantay sa pasyente ang mga nars.","translation":"The nurses need to **take turns repeatedly** in watching over the patient."},{"sentence":"Sa larong basketball, **maghali-halili** ang mga manlalaro sa pag-atake at pagdepensa.","translation":"In the game of basketball, the players **continuously alternate** between offense and defense."}]

translation: arrival; coming (of an event or time)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdating sa isang tiyak na lugar, oras, o kaganapan.
original_explanation: This isn't just arriving, like getting off a jeepney. 'Pagsapit' has a more dramatic, almost poetic feel. It’s the arrival of something significant—like 'pagsapit ng Pasko' (the coming of Christmas) or 'pagsapit ng dilim' (the falling of darkness). It's the moment the vibe shifts because *the thing* is finally here.
usage_notes: Often used for time, events, or significant moments rather than simple physical arrival of a person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdiwang ang lahat sa **pagsapit** ng Bagong Taon.","translation":"Everyone celebrated at the **arrival** of the New Year."},{"sentence":"Umuwi ka na bago ang **pagsapit** ng gabi.","translation":"Go home before the **coming** of night."}]

translation: to have one's neck twisted or sprained; to look back with a turn of the neck
meaning_filipino: Maipihit o mapilipit ang leeg, na maaaring magdulot ng sakit; lumingon sa pamamagitan ng pagpihit ng leeg.
etymology: ma- (potential verb prefix) + baliling (twist of the neck)
original_explanation: This is what happens when a chismis is so juicy you have to turn your head 180 degrees like an owl. 'Uy, ano 'yun?' and *snap*. Or when you see someone so good-looking walk by, you can't help but look back, risking a sprained neck. The official verb for 'doing a double-take'.
usage_notes: Often implies a sudden or forceful turn of the head.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **mabaliling** ang leeg ko sa kakalingon sa dumaang parada.","translation":"My neck almost **got sprained** from repeatedly turning to look at the passing parade."},{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **nabaliling** nang marinig niya ang pangalan niya.","translation":"She suddenly **turned her head** when she heard her name."}]

translation: will grow bigger; will increase in size
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtungo sa mas malaking sukat, taas, o dami sa hinaharap. Ito ang hinaharap na anyo ng pandiwang "lumaki".
original_explanation: What your Tita says every time she sees you: "Hala, ang laki mo na! Lalaki ka pa!" It's the future tense of getting bigger, whether it's your height, your savings account (sana all), or the 'tummy' you're trying to hide after the holidays.
usage_notes: Future tense of 'lumaki'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang halaman na ito ay **lalaki** nang husto kung aalagaan mo.","translation":"This plant **will grow** very big if you take care of it."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **lalaki** rin ang sweldo mo balang araw.","translation":"Don't worry, your salary **will also grow** someday."}]

translation: femme; a lesbian who presents femininely
meaning_filipino: Sa kontekstong LGBTQIA+, tumutukoy sa isang babae, partikular na isang lesbiyana o queer, na nagpapakita ng tradisyonal na pambabaeng katangian, pananamit, at kilos.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Pranses na "femme" na nangangahulugang "babae". Ginagamit sa pandaigdigang kontekstong LGBTQIA+.
original_explanation: In the local queer scene, a 'femme' is a woman who loves women and could easily be mistaken for your straight-girl crush. She might rock a dress and heels one day and a simple shirt and jeans the next. She defies the stereotype that all lesbians look a certain way. She's the 'gandang di mo inakala' na tibo pala.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa loob ng komunidad ng LGBTQIA+.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming nagulat nang malamang **femme** lesbian pala si Anna.","translation":"Many were surprised to find out that Anna is a **femme** lesbian."},{"sentence":"Ang girlfriend niya ay isang **femme** na mahilig sa makeup at fashion.","translation":"Her girlfriend is a **femme** who loves makeup and fashion."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbayad o mag-ambag ng buwis sa pamahalaan. Sa matalinghagang paraan, ito ay nangangahulugang magsakripisyo o mag-alay ng buhay para sa isang layunin.
etymology: From 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'buwis' (tax). Literally, 'to subject oneself to tax'.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what every working Filipino does: pay taxes to the BIR. Figuratively, it's a very dramatic way to say you sacrificed something, often used for heroes who gave their lives. 'Nagpabuwis ng buhay' means 'sacrificed one's life.' It's level-up from 'nag-effort.'
usage_notes: The figurative meaning 'to sacrifice one's life' (magpabuwis ng buhay) is very common in historical and nationalistic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat mamamayang may trabaho ay dapat **magpabuwis** nang tama.","translation":"Every working citizen must **pay taxes** correctly."},{"sentence":"Handa silang **magpabuwis** ng buhay para sa kalayaan ng bansa.","translation":"They are ready to **sacrifice** their lives for the country's freedom."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pansariling kuro-kuro, opinyon, o saloobin tungkol sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
etymology: From 'pa-' + 'lagay', literally 'that which is put or placed (in the mind)'.
original_explanation: Your 'feeling' or 'take' on something. When your boss asks, 'Ano'ng palagay mo dito?' they're asking for your opinion (but you better have a good one). It's a mix of thought, feeling, and assumption. The polite way to say 'I think...' is 'Sa palagay ko...'.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the phrase 'Sa palagay ko...' (In my opinion...).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **palagay** ko, uulan mamayang hapon.","translation":"In my **opinion**, it will rain this afternoon."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **palagay** mo sa bagong patakaran?","translation":"What are your **thoughts** on the new policy?"}]

translation: to acclaim as a hero, to lionize
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtrato o pagkilala sa isang tao bilang isang bayani dahil sa kanyang mga pambihirang nagawa para sa kapwa o bayan.
original_explanation: This is what we do to our OFWs, frontliners, and that one Grab driver who returns a lost iPhone. We 'mambayani' them—we put them on a pedestal and recognize their big and small acts of heroism. It's our way of saying, 'You're the real MVP.'
usage_notes: A formal and rather uncommon verb, used in contexts of honoring or celebrating someone's heroic deeds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **mambayani** sa mga gurong naglilingkod nang tapat sa kabila ng mababang sahod.","translation":"We should **acclaim as heroes** the teachers who serve honestly despite low salaries."},{"sentence":"Ginugunita natin ang kanilang sakripisyo upang sila ay **mambayani** sa alaala ng bansa.","translation":"We commemorate their sacrifice in order to **lionize** them in the nation's memory."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalagay o pagpapakabit ng baldosa sa sahig o dingding ng isang gusali o bahay.
original_explanation: The next level after `magpabahay`. Okay, may bahay ka na, pero semento pa lang ang sahig. Time to magpabaldosa! This is when you hire a "maestro" to lay down tiles, choosing between ceramic, porcelain, or granite, tapos mag-aaway pa kayo ng nanay mo sa design. It's the act of "causing tiles to be installed" to make your home look classier.
usage_notes: Specific to home/building renovation and construction.
