usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ipon sila ng pera para **magpabaldosa** ng kanilang kusina.","translation":"They saved money **to have their kitchen tiled**."},{"sentence":"Magkano kaya ang aabutin kung **magpapabaldosa** ako ng buong bahay?","translation":"I wonder how much it would cost if I were **to have the whole house tiled**?"}]

translation: to deal in rice; to put rice into
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paglalagay ng bigas sa isang lalagyan, o ang pagnenegosyo ng bigas.
original_explanation: The verb for being a rice mogul. It means to sell rice, usually on a larger scale than just one sack. When you hear about a 'bodega na nagbibigas,' you picture sacks upon sacks of Dinorado and Sinandomeng. Less commonly, it can mean to put rice into something, but that's like using a super formal word for a simple task.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of business or trade. 'Magbigay ng bigas' (to give rice) is more common for simple acts of giving.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais ng pamilya nila na **magbigas** bilang kanilang pangunahing negosyo.","translation":"Their family wants **to deal in rice** as their main business."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magbibigas** sa mga sako para sa donasyon?","translation":"Who **will put rice** into the sacks for the donation?"}]

translation: to tumble, to fall headfirst, to be overturned
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagbagsak o pagbaligtad kung saan ang itaas na bahagi ay napupunta sa ibaba.
original_explanation: Imagine tripping on a flat surface in slow motion. That's it. It's a clumsy, ungraceful fall, often head over heels. Parang yung mundo mo nung nalaman mong "work friends" lang pala kayo. Your whole world got turned upside down. Pwedeng literal na natumba, or metaphorical na pagbagsak.
usage_notes: Implies a sudden, often awkward, overturning or falling motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Muntik na siyang **matiwarik** dahil sa madulas na sahig.","translation":"He almost **tumbled** because of the slippery floor."},{"sentence":"Sa lakas ng hangin, halos **matiwarik** ang payong niya.","translation":"With the strength of the wind, his umbrella almost **got overturned**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang elektroniko na isinusuot sa ulo, karaniwang may mga earpiece para sa pandinig at isang mikropono para sa pagsasalita.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na "headset".
original_explanation: The official uniform of BPO agents, gamers, and anyone trying to look busy in a co-working space. Ito yung "Do Not Disturb" sign na sinusuot mo sa ulo. "Sorry, naka-headset ako" is the new "I'm in a meeting."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa orihinal na anyo nito sa Ingles. Walang katumbas na iisang salita sa Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng bagong **headset** na may noise-cancelling feature para sa mga online meeting ko.","translation":"I need a new **headset** with a noise-cancelling feature for my online meetings."}]

translation: To put a layer/lining on something
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay ng sapin sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'sapin'. It's the action of putting down that protective layer. 'Ma, sapinan mo ng newspaper yung table,' means you're about to do something messy, like an art project or eating crabs. It’s the setup before the main event.
usage_notes: The focus of the action is on the surface or object being covered. The object of the verb is the thing being covered.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **sapinan** ng karton ang sahig para hindi madumihan.","translation":"You need **to put a layer** of cardboard **on** the floor so it doesn't get dirty."},{"sentence":"**Sapinan** mo ng dahon ng saging ang pinggan para mas masarap kainin ang kanin.","translation":"**Line** the plate with a banana leaf so the rice is more enjoyable to eat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng laruan na karaniwang gawa sa kahoy o plastik, may matulis na dulo, at pinaiikot sa pamamagitan ng paghila sa isang nakapulupot na tali.
original_explanation: The OG fidget spinner. Before Beyblades, there was the turumpo. You wrap a string around this wooden or plastic toy, throw it just right, and watch it spin. The goal was to have the longest spin or to knock out your friend's turumpo. A true test of 90s kid skill.
usage_notes: Isang tradisyonal na larong Pilipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong ka pa bang magpaikot ng **turumpo**?","translation":"Do you still know how to spin a **top**?"},{"sentence":"Ang galing niyang maghagis ng **turumpo**; ang tagal umikot!","translation":"He's so good at throwing the **top**; it spins for so long!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sapilitang pagkuha ng pera o anumang bagay na may halaga mula sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng pananakot, pagbabanta, o paggamit ng kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: This is what happens when someone says, "Nice business you have here... it would be a shame if something happened to it." It's the "bigyan mo 'ko o malalagot ka" move. The villain's version of fundraising. The noun form, 'pangingikil' or 'kotong', is more commonly heard.
usage_notes: A serious crime. Often associated with corruption ('kotong') or criminal syndicates.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaresto ang mga opisyal na napatunayang sinusubukang **mangikil** sa mga negosyante.","translation":"The officials who were proven to be trying to **extort** from business owners were arrested."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapadala sa mga taong gustong **mangikil** sa iyo gamit ang iyong mga sikreto.","translation":"Don't give in to people who want to **blackmail** you using your secrets."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na paghampas o pagsuntok sa isang tao o bagay; ang pagpapalitan ng suntok.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'buntal' (the strike), turned into a full-blown event. It's not just one hit, it's a brawl. 'Nagbuntalan sila' means they had a fistfight. It's the action you see in movies when the hero is surrounded by goons and has to fight his way out. Less of a duel, more of a chaotic rumble.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa kilos ng pagsuntok sa isang tao nang paulit-ulit (buntalin) o ang pag-aaway ng dalawa o higit pang tao (mag-buntalan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula silang mag-**buntalan** sa gitna ng kalsada dahil sa alitan sa trapiko.","translation":"They started to **pummel** each other in the middle of the road because of a traffic dispute."}]

translation: to originate from, to be the source of
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi o pinanggalingan ng isang bagay, pangyayari, o sitwasyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pag-` (panandang pandiwari), salitang-ugat na `mula`, at hulaping `-an` (panandang lokatibo/reperensyal).
original_explanation: Ito yung "patient zero" ng chismis. Dito nagsimula ang lahat. "Saan ba 'to nagmula?" is the question you ask when you want to find the source of a problem, a rumor, or even a good idea. It's the root cause, the origin story.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwa na gumaganap bilang 'maging pinagmulan ng'. Madalas itong ginagamit sa mga konstruksyon na nakatuon sa layon. Ang anyong pangngalan nito ay `pinagmulan` (origin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang maliit na alitan ang maaaring **pagmulan** ng malaking gulo.","translation":"A small conflict can **be the source of** a big chaos."},{"sentence":"Huwag nawang **pagmulan** ng sakit ang kinain natin sa labas.","translation":"I hope what we ate outside won't **be the source of** sickness."}]

translation: to be tied down; to be bound (unintentionally or against one's will)
meaning_filipino: Maitali o magapos, madalas nang hindi sinasadya o labag sa kalooban. Sa matalinhagang paraan, nangangahulugang maging abala o konektado sa isang sitwasyon o relasyon.
etymology: ma- (unintentional/ability prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + tali (tie, string)
original_explanation: Literally, it could mean getting your shoelaces tangled. But figuratively, this is the "I can't, I'm busy" verb. It’s being tied down to work, responsibilities, or a relationship. "Gusto ko sanang sumama sa outing, kaso napatali ako sa trabaho." It's also the fear of commitment personified: "Ayaw ko pang mapatali sa isang relasyon."
usage_notes: Can be used both literally and figuratively. The figurative sense is more common in modern conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napatali** ang aso sa poste nang mapulupot ang kanyang kadena.","translation":"The dog **was tied** to the post when its chain got tangled."},{"sentence":"Maraming ayaw mag-asawa agad dahil takot silang **mapatali**.","translation":"Many don't want to marry early because they are afraid of **being tied down**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkuha ng karapatang gumamit ng isang ari-arian, serbisyo, o kagamitan sa loob ng takdang panahon kapalit ng regular na bayad.
original_explanation: The reason why half your sweldo disappears on the 15th and 30th. It's the adulting version of 'borrowing' but with contracts and security deposits. Whether it's a condo in BGC or a karaoke machine for a party, this is the process you go through.
usage_notes: Used for renting property, vehicles, or equipment. The noun 'upa' refers to the rent payment itself, while 'pag-upa' is the act of renting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap humanap ng apartment na mura ang **pag-upa**.","translation":"It's hard to find an apartment where the **renting** is cheap."},{"sentence":"Pinag-iisipan niya ang **pag-upa** ng kotse para sa kanilang bakasyon.","translation":"He is considering the **act of renting** a car for their vacation."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa kulay na puti, o sa isang taong may mapusyaw o maliwanag na kulay ng balat.
original_explanation: The ultimate compliment for many titas, and the reason why the glutathione and papaya soap industries are thriving. It can mean the color white, like 'puting bigas,' or, more commonly, fair-skinned. 'Wow, ang puti mo ngayon! Anong sabon mo?' is a classic Filipino greeting.
usage_notes: Often used to describe skin color, which can be a culturally significant topic in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niya ng sapatos na **maputi**.","translation":"He wants **white** shoes."},{"sentence":"Lahat sila sa pamilya ay **maputi**.","translation":"Everyone in their family is **fair-skinned**."}]

translation: to go around; to encircle; to mill around
meaning_filipino: Palibutan o ikutin ang isang lugar, bagay, o tao, kadalasan nang paulit-ulit.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo sa mall kapag window shopping ka lang—paikot-ikot, walang direksyon. O 'yung aso mong hindi mapakali bago matulog, iikutin muna 'yung buong higaan. It's the act of making the rounds, whether you're a security guard on patrol or just bored and pacing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan niya ang bata na **ligirin** ang buong hardin upang hanapin ang nawawalang pusa.","translation":"He instructed the child to **go around** the entire garden to look for the missing cat."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **ligirin** ng mga guwardiya ang perimeter ng gusali bawat oras.","translation":"The guards need to **go around** the building's perimeter every hour."}]

translation: To cock (a gun); to set (a trap)
meaning_filipino: Ihanda ang mekanismo ng isang bagay, tulad ng baril o patibong, upang ito ay pumatak o kumilos nang biglaan.
original_explanation: It's that tense movie moment before the action starts—the hero cocks the gun ('igkasin ang baril'). It's also setting up a mousetrap ('igkasin ang patibong'). It's the potential energy waiting to be released, like the spring in a jack-in-the-box or your patience right before you snap.
usage_notes: Often associated with weapons, traps, or spring-loaded mechanisms. The form 'umigkas' (to snap back) is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **iginikasi** ang bitag para sa mga daga.","translation":"He carefully **set** the trap for the mice."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong paglaruan 'yan, baka **umigkas** at masaktan ka.","translation":"Don't play with that, it might **snap back** and hurt you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga kaugalian at alituntunin ng magalang na pag-uugali sa lipunan o sa isang partikular na propesyon o grupo.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung GMRC (Good Manners and Right Conduct) mo—'yung 'di pagsasalita 'pag puno ang bibig, paggamit ng 'po' at 'opo', at 'di pag-spoil ng series sa social media. Basic human decency, ika nga.
usage_notes: Refers to a social or professional code of conduct. Homonym with 'etiketa' (label).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **etiketa** sa hapag-kainan, lalo na sa isang pormal na salu-salo.","translation":"Proper dining **etiquette** is important, especially at a formal gathering."}]

translation: to slide down; to slip down
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapadausdos o pagpapababa ng isang bagay sa isang makinis o madulas na ibabaw.
original_explanation: Imagine you're at a waterpark. What do you do with yourself on the giant slide? You `idausdos` yourself down. It's the action of making something slide down, whether it's a box down a ramp or yourself on a playground slide.
usage_notes: The 'i-' prefix turns the noun/concept of 'dausdos' (sliding) into a causative verb, meaning 'to cause something to slide'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **inidausdos** ang kahon sa hagdanan.","translation":"He carefully **slid** the box down the stairs."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **idausdos** ang mga plato sa mesa, baka mabasag.","translation":"Don't **slide** the plates on the table, they might break."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makaalis o makawala mula sa pagkakagapos, pagkakakulong, o anumang mahigpit na pagkakahawak.
original_explanation: That feeling of freedom when you finally log off after a toxic day at work. Or when you finally get out of a "situationship." It's escaping something that's holding you back, whether it's literal na posas (handcuffs) or figurative na utang (debt). The ultimate "Salamat, next!" moment.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of struggle and liberation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng bilanggo na **makahulagpos** mula sa kanyang selda.","translation":"The prisoner tried **to break free** from his cell."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **makahulagpos** sa kumunoy ng kahirapan.","translation":"It is difficult **to escape** from the quicksand of poverty."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panlabas na kaanyuan, hugis, porma, o hitsura ng isang bagay, tao, o konsepto.
original_explanation: Parang "build" o "version" ng isang bagay. Pwedeng pisikal, tulad ng "iba't ibang anyo ng pasta," o abstract, tulad ng "iba't ibang anyo ng pag-ibig" (naks!). Sa office, ito yung "final form" mo 'pag Biyernes, naka-casual wear at ready nang umuwi.
usage_notes: Isang napakalawak na salita na maaaring gamitin sa maraming konteksto, mula sa pisikal hanggang sa metapisikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tubig ay maaaring magbago ng **anyo** mula sa likido patungong solido o gas.","translation":"Water can change its **form** from liquid to solid or gas."},{"sentence":"Nag-iba ang **anyo** ng kanyang mukha nang malaman niya ang balita.","translation":"The **appearance** of his face changed when he heard the news."},{"sentence":"Maraming **anyo** ang pagpapakita ng pagmamahal.","translation":"Love manifests in many **forms**."}]

translation: to scrape clean; to consume to the last bit
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ubos ng lahat ng pagkain sa isang plato o lalagyan, na walang itinitirang anuman; ang pagkuha ng lahat hanggang sa wala nang matira.
etymology: From 'mag-' (actor-focus verb prefix) + 'simot' (used up, consumed completely).
original_explanation: That thing you do when the ulam is so good you scrape the plate clean, leaving no trace of sauce or rice. "Sayang ang grasya," as our lolas would say. It’s the highest form of compliment to the chef. Can also be used for money, like when you spend everything down to the last centavo before payday.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of food, but can also apply to resources like money or supplies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang sarap ng adobo, **nagsimot** siya ng kanin sa plato.","translation":"The adobo was so delicious, he **scraped** his plate **clean** of rice."},{"sentence":"**Nagsimot** sila ng natirang pera para lang makabili ng tiket.","translation":"They **used up every last bit** of their remaining money just to buy a ticket."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela na may natatanging disenyo at kulay, ginagamit bilang simbolo ng isang bansa, organisasyon, o kilusan.
original_explanation: The OG symbol of national pride. It's what gets raised every Monday morning in schools, what athletes wrap around themselves after winning, and what gets its own dedicated late-night news program title. It's the ultimate 'represent'.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'watawat', although 'watawat' is sometimes considered more formal or specific to the national flag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itaas ang **bandila** ng Pilipinas!","translation":"Raise the Philippine **flag**!"},{"sentence":"Ang bawat kulay sa ating **bandila** ay may mahalagang kahulugan.","translation":"Each color on our **flag** has an important meaning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim at malawak na butas o bangin sa lupa, karaniwang likha ng kalikasan.
original_explanation: Think of it as the ultimate 'walang forever' landscape. It's that huge, scary gap in the earth, like the Grand Canyon, or the emotional abyss you fall into after binge-watching a K-drama series and realizing it's over.
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically to describe a wide gap or division between people, ideas, or social classes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatayo sila sa gilid ng **sunganga**, namamangha sa lalim nito.","translation":"They stood at the edge of the **chasm**, amazed at its depth."},{"sentence":"May malaking **sunganga** sa pagitan ng mayaman at mahirap sa ating lipunan.","translation":"There is a great **abyss** between the rich and the poor in our society."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkamit ng malaking kayamanan o pag-angat sa estado ng pamumuhay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na 'yaman' (wealth) at panlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino dream, right after migrating to Canada. It's what you wish for when you see a shooting star, what you bet on in the lotto, and the plot of 90% of teleseryes where the poor protagonist discovers they're actually the heir to a giant corporation. 'Sana all yumaman.'
usage_notes: Ang pandiwa ay nasa anyong naganap (completed aspect) ngunit maaari ring gamitin bilang pawatas (infinitive). Ang pangkasalukuyan ay 'yumayaman' at panghinaharap ay 'yayaman'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming nangangarap na **yumaman** sa isang iglap.","translation":"Many dream of **becoming rich** in an instant."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang kasipagan, **yumaman** ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"Because of his hard work, his family **became rich**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang batayang katotohanan, paniniwala, o alituntunin na nagsisilbing gabay sa pag-iisip o pagkilos.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "simula" at hulaping "-in," na tumutukoy sa isang bagay na pinanghahawakan mula sa simula.
original_explanation: This is your personal 'code of conduct' or the 'company values' that you actually believe in. It's your 'why' – the fundamental beliefs you stand for. Parang 'yung life principles ni Rizal o 'yung 'customer first' na simulain ng isang kumpanya. It's deeper than a simple rule; it's the core belief system that guides your decisions, like 'bawal umutang sa Biyernes' or 'always be kind.'
usage_notes: A formal word often used in academic, political, or philosophical contexts. In casual conversation, people might use 'prinsipyo' instead.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagkakapantay-pantay ay isang mahalagang **simulain** ng demokrasya.","translation":"Equality is an important **principle** of democracy."},{"sentence":"Ipinaglaban niya ang kanyang mga **simulain** hanggang sa huli.","translation":"He fought for his **ideals** until the end."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinsala sa ulo kung saan ang utak ay nayayanig o naalog sa loob ng bungo, na maaaring magdulot ng pansamantalang pagkawala ng normal na paggana nito.
etymology: From pagkaka- (manner of) + alog (shake) + ng (of) + utak (brain).
original_explanation: This is what your Tita warns you about when you get hit in the head by a basketball. It's a literal "shookt" moment for your brain. Medically, it's a concussion. Colloquially, it's the feeling you get after a 12-hour shift or trying to understand government paperwork.
usage_notes: A medical term for concussion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa ospital dahil sa **pagkakalog ng utak** matapos ang aksidente.","translation":"He was brought to the hospital for a **concussion** after the accident."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang malalakas na yugyog sa ulo upang maiwasan ang **pagkakalog ng utak**.","translation":"Avoid strong shakes to the head to prevent a **brain shake**."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng malinaw at tiyak na kahulugan o katuturan ang isang salita, parirala, o konsepto.
etymology: Hango sa salitang Espanyol na 'definir', na inangkop sa anyong pandiwa ng Tagalog na may hulaping '-hin'.
original_explanation: The classic 'DTR' (Define The Relationship) move. 'Bes, i-**depinihin** mo nga, ano ba talaga tayo?' It's asking for clarity, for labels, for the official meaning of something, whether it's a word in the dictionary or the confusing status of your situationship.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na pandiwa. Sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, mas karaniwan ang 'i-define mo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **depinihin** ang salitang pag-ibig sa iisang pangungusap lamang.","translation":"It's difficult **to define** the word love in just one sentence."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **depinihin** ang mga layunin ng proyektong ito.","translation":"We need **to define** the goals of this project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip na pamatlig na ginagamit sa pagturo ng isang bagay, tao, o lugar na malayo sa nagsasalita at sa kinakausap.
original_explanation: The long-distance relationship version of "ayan." You use "ayun" to point at something far away, like your dreams, your ex, or that one jeepney you were supposed to catch. It's often followed by a pointed lip-pout, the universal Filipino laser pointer. "Ayun o!" ("There it is!").
usage_notes: Part of the 'ito/iyan/iyon' and 'dito/diyan/doon' series. 'Ayun' is the colloquial equivalent of 'iyon'. It points to something far from both the speaker and the listener.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ayun** ang bahay na tinitirhan nila, sa dulo ng kalye.","translation":"**There** is the house they live in, at the end of the street."},{"sentence":"Nakita mo ba 'yung ibon? **Ayun** o, lumilipad!","translation":"Did you see that bird? **There** it is, flying!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pangkat ng mga musikero na tumutugtog ng iba't ibang instrumento, na karaniwang pinamumunuan ng isang konduktor.
etymology: From Spanish 'orquesta', with modern Filipino orthography.
original_explanation: This is the more modern and common spelling. When you see a huge group of people on stage with violins, cellos, flutes, and giant drums, that's an **orkestra**. It's like the Avengers of classical music, assembled by a conductor (the Nick Fury) to create something epic.
usage_notes: The preferred and more widely used spelling over 'orkesta'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Manonood kami ng pagtatanghal ng Philippine Philharmonic **Orkestra** sa CCP.","translation":"We will watch the performance of the Philippine Philharmonic **Orchestra** at the CCP."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matinding disiplina upang maging kasapi ng isang **orkestra**.","translation":"Intense discipline is needed to become a member of an **orchestra**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng isang daan, landas, o anumang linya na hindi tuwid; isang kurbada.
original_explanation: That part of the road where you either make a U-turn back to your ex or turn towards your future. Also, the reason your Grab driver's ETA keeps changing. 'Isang liko na lang, malapit na tayo.' (Famous last words).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa **liko** sa kanto, madulas diyan.","translation":"Be careful at the **turn** on the corner, it's slippery there."},{"sentence":"Isang matalim na **liko** ang naghihintay sa mga motorista sa paanan ng bundok.","translation":"A sharp **curve** awaits motorists at the foot of the mountain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paunang bayad na ginagawa kapag bumibili ng isang bagay sa paraang hulugan, tulad ng bahay, lupa, o sasakyan. Pinaikli para sa 'down payment'.
etymology: Mula sa acronym sa Ingles na 'DP' (Down Payment).
original_explanation: Short for 'Down Payment'. Ito 'yung malaking halaga na kailangan mong ipunin at ibigay para masimulan ang pagbabayad sa condo, kotse, o major appliance na gusto mo. After ng DP, aalalahanin mo ang monthly amortization for the next 5 years. Welcome to adulting!
usage_notes: Karaniwan sa mga usaping pinansyal, real estate, at pagbili ng sasakyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap kami ng bahay na may mababang **DP**.","translation":"We are looking for a house with a low **down payment**."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang kailangan kong **DP** para sa kotse na 'yan?","translation":"How much **DP** do I need for that car?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging lasing na lasing o pagpapakasaya nang walang pakundangan, lalo na sa inuman o party.
etymology: Likely onomatopoeic, from the sound of vomiting or talking drunkenly. The original meaning refers to being wide open or agape, like a mouth or a wound, which has evolved to mean 'uninhibited.'
original_explanation: The battle cry for when you want to forget your deadlines, your ex, and your adult responsibilities for one night. To be 'walwal' is to party with reckless abandon, to drink until you're 'wasted,' and to wake up the next day with a killer hangover and a phone full of questionable photos. It's the Filipino 'YOLO.'
usage_notes: Primarily used by millennials and Gen Z. Can be a verb (magwalwal), adjective (walwal na), or noun (pagwawalwal).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, mag-**walwal** tayo mamaya, sweldo naman!","translation":"Let's go **party hard** later, it's payday!"},{"sentence":"Sobrang **walwal** niya kagabi, hindi na makatayo.","translation":"He was so **wasted** last night, he couldn't even stand up."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyong tubig na nabuo kapag ang isang malawak na meandro o liko ng ilog ay naputol mula sa pangunahing daloy nito, na nag-iiwan ng isang lawa na may kurbang hugis-U.
original_explanation: It's what happens when a river gets tired of its own drama and decides to 'cut off' a toxic curve. Parang sa friendship lang, after a big fight, nag-iba na ng daan, leaving behind a memory (the lake) of what it used to be.
usage_notes: A specific geographical term used in science and geography.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa heograpiya kung paano nabubuo ang isang **lawang hugis-U**.","translation":"Geography studies how an **oxbow lake** is formed."}]

translation: to cause trouble, to stir up conflict
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paglikha ng gulo, alitan, o hindi pagkakaunawaan sa pagitan ng mga tao o grupo.
original_explanation: This is the specialty of that one tita at every family reunion who asks, 'Tumaba ka yata?' or 'Kailan ka ikakasal?' They're not just asking; they're dropping a little chaos grenade and watching the fallout. It's the act of being a professional 'marites' instigator.
usage_notes: This is a more formal or literary word. In everyday conversation, people might use 'manggulo' or 'gumawa ng gulo'. It implies intentional sowing of discord.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga taong mahilig **magsigalot** para lang magkaroon ng atensyon.","translation":"There are people who love **to stir up conflict** just to get attention."},{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng diplomatiko ay pigilan ang mga bansa na **magsigalot**.","translation":"The diplomat's goal is to prevent the nations from **engaging in conflict**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan, karaniwang yari sa kahoy o plastik, na hugis-paa at ginagamit bilang gabay sa paggawa o pag-aayos ng sapatos.
original_explanation: The 'ghost foot' used by shoemakers in Marikina. It's the solid model that ensures your new shoes won't cramp your style (or your toes). Think of it as the mannequin for footwear.
usage_notes: A specific technical term used in shoemaking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat na inilapat ng sapatero ang katad sa **hulmahan ng sapatos**.","translation":"The shoemaker carefully fitted the leather onto the **shoe last**."}]

translation: to lead by the hand; to guide
meaning_filipino: Ang paggabay sa isang tao sa paglalakad sa pamamagitan ng paghawak sa kamay, braso, o pag-alalay. Tumutukoy rin sa paggabay sa isang tao tungo sa isang partikular na landas o paniniwala.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're crossing a busy street with your lola, or guiding a drunk friend back to their seat. It's a gentle, supportive leading. Metaphorically, it's what a mentor does for a newbie, or what a church leader does for their congregation—guiding them towards a certain path. It's the verb form of 'holding hands' with a purpose.
usage_notes: Implies a sense of care, support, or responsibility for the one being led.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinulungan niyang **mag-akay** sa matandang babae patawid ng kalsada.","translation":"He helped **guide** the old woman across the street."},{"sentence":"Ang tungkulin ng isang guro ay **mag-akay** sa kanyang mga estudyante sa tamang landas.","translation":"A teacher's duty is to **guide** their students to the right path."}]

translation: to have something checked in as luggage
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling na isama ang isang gamit sa mga bagaheng idedeposito para sa isang biyahe, karaniwan sa eroplano o bus.
original_explanation: The command you give your travel buddy at the airport, 'Uy, **ipabagahe** mo na 'tong maleta ko, lampas 7kg na 'yung hand-carry ko.' It's the act of surrendering your heavy stuff to the check-in counter gods, praying it doesn't get lost or end up in a different country.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of travel (air, sea, or long-distance bus) for items to be placed in the cargo hold.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga siyang pumila para **ipabagahe** ang kanyang mga dalang pasalubong.","translation":"He lined up early **to have his souvenir gifts checked in as luggage**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng lupa na itinalaga o inilaan para sa isang partikular na layunin o pangkat ng mga tao.
original_explanation: Think of it as land on reserve. It’s like that seat your friend saved for you at the crowded food court, or the budget you specifically set aside for milk tea. It has a designated purpose, whether for indigenous communities (ancestral domain) or a future condo development.
usage_notes: Often used in legal or official contexts regarding land distribution, ancestral domains, or government reservations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **lupang laan** na iyon ay para sa mga katutubong Aeta.","translation":"That **allotted land** is for the indigenous Aeta people."},{"sentence":"Mayroong **lupang laan** ang gobyerno para sa pagtatayo ng bagong ospital.","translation":"The government has a **land reservation** for the construction of a new hospital."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang organo sa katawan na responsable sa pagbomba ng dugo. Ginagamit din ito sa matalinghagang paraan upang tukuyin ang sentro ng damdamin, pag-ibig, at katapangan.
original_explanation: The body's original pump, but in the Philippines, it's mostly known for being fragile, easily broken ('durog'), and the subject of 99% of OPM songs. It's what you follow when you make questionable life decisions for love. It's also what Gilas Pilipinas plays with. Laban!
usage_notes: Can refer to the physical organ or emotions. The context determines the meaning. 'Puso' is a cornerstone of Filipino expressions related to emotion and courage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Manalo, matalo, ang mahalaga ay naglaro ka nang buong **puso**.","translation":"Win or lose, what's important is you played with all your **heart**."},{"sentence":"Sumasakit ang **puso** ko para sa mga naulila.","translation":"My **heart** aches for the bereaved."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapot at matamis na likido, na karaniwang gawa sa asukal na tinunaw sa tubig, at ginagamit sa pagkain o bilang gamot.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na 'syrup', posibleng may impluwensya ng Espanyol na 'sirope'.
original_explanation: The lifeblood of pancakes, halo-halo, and your childhood cough medicine. It's that sweet, sticky stuff that makes everything better, from breakfast to a sore throat. Also, the secret ingredient in your favorite milk tea.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa sirup para sa pagkain (maple, tsokolate) o sirup na gamot (para sa ubo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng maraming **sirup** ang iyong pancake.","translation":"Put a lot of **syrup** on your pancake."},{"sentence":"Pinainom ng nanay ng **sirup** para sa ubo ang kanyang anak.","translation":"The mother gave her child cough **syrup**."}]

meaning_filipino: Kakaiba, hindi pangkaraniwan, o natatangi sa anumang uri.
original_explanation: When 'galing' or 'wow' isn't enough. It's for that talent show contestant who hits a whistle note, or that one time the MRT had no lines. Can also be used sarcastically for something unusually dumb, 'Pambihira, ang simple lang hindi pa nagawa!'
usage_notes: Can be an expression of awe, admiration, or exasperation depending on the tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pambihira** ang kanyang talento sa pag-awit!","translation":"Her talent in singing is **extraordinary**!"},{"sentence":"**Pambihira** ka, bakit mo ginawa iyon?","translation":"You're **unbelievable**, why did you do that?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puna na ang layunin ay hindi upang makatulong o magtayo, kundi upang manira, manghiya, o magpababa sa halaga ng isang tao, gawa, o ideya.
etymology: A phrase combining `pamumuna` (criticism) and `mapanira` (destructive), from the root `sira` (to break, destroy).
original_explanation: This isn't just "Uy, tumaba ka." This is "Uy, tumaba ka. Ano nangyari sa'yo? Ang pangit mo na." It's criticism with venom. It's what bashers and trolls do for a living. The goal isn't to help you improve; the goal is to make you cry in the CR. It’s hate-commenting disguised as "just being honest."
usage_notes: A specific type of `pamumuna`. It is always negative and ill-intentioned, contrasted with 'pamumunang nakakatulong' (constructive criticism).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pamumunang mapanira** ay walang lugar sa isang malusog na talakayan.","translation":"**Destructive criticism** has no place in a healthy discussion."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pamumunang mapanira** ng mga tao, nawalan siya ng kumpiyansa sa sarili.","translation":"Because of people's **destructive criticism**, he lost his self-confidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sakramento ng pag-amin ng mga kasalanan sa isang pari upang makamit ang kapatawaran mula sa Diyos.
etymology: From Spanish 'confesar' (to confess). The Filipino form is `kumpisal`, with the affix `pang-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `ku-`.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'spill the tea' session, but with a priest and for your sins. It's the Catholic practice of telling a priest all the bad stuff you've done so you can get a spiritual reset. Think of it as clearing your spiritual browser history.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious, specifically Catholic, context. The verb form is 'magkumpisal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Oras na para sa **Pangungumpisal** bago ang Mahal na Araw.","translation":"It's time for **Confession** before Holy Week."},{"sentence":"Kinakabahan ako sa aking unang **pangungumpisal**.","translation":"I am nervous about my first **confession**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sawsawan o pampalasa na gawa sa binurong maliliit na hipon o alamang na hinaluan ng kanin. Ito ay isang tanyag na pagkain sa lalawigan ng Rizal.
etymology: A specialty from Angono, Rizal. There is a famous restaurant named after it.
original_explanation: This is bagoong's exotic cousin from Rizal. It's a fermented shrimp and rice mixture that's a love-it-or-hate-it kind of food. For the uninitiated, the smell might be a challenge, but for fans, it's the perfect funky, salty kick for fried fish or veggies. It's an acquired taste, like your Tita's taste in karaoke songs.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the fermented shrimp and rice condiment, distinct from the more common 'bagoong alamang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap isawsaw ang pritong isda sa **balawbalaw**.","translation":"It's delicious to dip fried fish in **balawbalaw**."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang Angono sa kanilang masarap na **balawbalaw**.","translation":"Angono is known for their delicious **shrimp paste condiment**."}]

meaning_filipino: (Pangalan) Isang pag-uusap, lalo na sa paraang di-pormal at sa pamamagitan ng internet. (Pandiwa) Ang akto ng pakikipag-usap sa ganitong paraan.
original_explanation: The foundation of modern Filipino relationships, whether platonic or romantic. It's how you slide into DMs, get marites updates on the group chat (GC), or talk to your BPO customer. "Seen-zoned" is the tragic ending to many chat conversations.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ('Mag-reply ka sa chat ko') or a verb, often with affixes like 'nag-chat' or 'mag-chat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-**chat** sa akin ang dati kong kaklase.","translation":"My old classmate **chatted** with me."},{"sentence":"Bakit hindi mo sinasagot ang **chat** ko sa Messenger?","translation":"Why aren't you answering my **chat** on Messenger?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paggawa ng mga kopya ng teksto o larawan sa papel o ibang materyales sa pamamagitan ng makina; ang industriya ng paglalathala.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable `li-` + `limbag` (print, impress).
original_explanation: Before your lola's Facebook posts, there was 'paglilimbag'. This is the art of making things 'official' by putting them on paper—books, newspapers, magazines, and even your tita's wedding invitations. It's the physical ancestor of hitting 'Publish' on WordPress or 'Post' on social media.
usage_notes: Refers to both the physical act of printing and the industry of publishing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang industriya ng **paglilimbag** ay nahaharap sa mga bagong hamon dahil sa digital media.","translation":"The **publishing** industry is facing new challenges because of digital media."},{"sentence":"Pinangasiwaan niya ang **paglilimbag** ng mga bagong aklat-pampaaralan.","translation":"He supervised the **printing** of the new school textbooks."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na pinanatili sa orihinal o kasalukuyang estado nito, lalo na sa pamamagitan ng kemikal na proseso o espesyal na pangangalaga.
original_explanation: Like your lola's atchara or your tita's collection of antique furniture. It means something is kept safe from decay or damage. Pwedeng pagkain (burong mangga), pwedeng lumang gusali (Vigan), o pwedeng yung alaala ng ex mo na ayaw mo pa ring i-let go... **preserbado** pa sa puso mo. Hugot!
usage_notes: Can refer to food, historical artifacts, or even abstract concepts like memories or culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mananatiling **preserbado** ang mga lumang istruktura sa Intramuros.","translation":"The old structures in Intramuros will remain **preserved**."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang isdang **preserbado** sa asin.","translation":"Fish **preserved** in salt is delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at malakas na pagdating o paglabas ng isang bagay, tulad ng hangin, ulan, o damdamin.
original_explanation: Ever had your emotions go from zero to one hundred real quick? That's a 'bugso ng damdamin'. It's that sudden surge of 'gigil' when you see a cute baby, the unexpected 'iyak' during a sad movie, or the flash of 'galit' when your WiFi dies mid-game. It's an emotional flash flood.
usage_notes: Commonly paired with "damdamin" (emotion/feeling) to mean an emotional outburst. Can also refer to a gust of wind or a downpour of rain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang **bugso** ng galit, nasabi niya ang mga bagay na pinagsisihan niya.","translation":"In a sudden **outburst** of anger, she said things she later regretted."},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **bugso** ng hangin ang nagpatumba sa mga halaman.","translation":"A strong **gust** of wind knocked over the plants."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng balat na kumapal at tumigas dahil sa paulit-ulit na presyon, pagkiskis, o iritasyon.
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung resulta ng pagbubuhat mo ng weights sa gym, 'yung pangingialam sa gitara, o 'yung pagtatrabaho gamit ang kamay. It's the battle scar of hard work. Your skin's way of saying, "Okay, nasaktan ako diyan dati, so magpapatigas na ako this time." Proof of your 'pinaghirapan'.
usage_notes: Can also be used figuratively to mean being hardened or jaded by experience. The singular form 'kalyo' is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng **kalyos** sa kamay dahil sa paghahalaman.","translation":"She got **calluses** on her hands from gardening."},{"sentence":"Makapal na ang **kalyos** sa kanyang mga paa sa kalalakad.","translation":"The **calluses** on his feet are thick from so much walking."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o hayop na mabangis, mailap, at mahirap paamuin. Maaari ring ilarawan ang isang taong masungit o madaling magalit.
original_explanation: This is your friend before their morning coffee. 'Yung tipong titingnan mo lang, parang gusto ka nang sakmalin. A balawis person is grumpy, unapproachable, and generally unpleasant to be around. Parang asong-kalye na hindi mo pwedeng hawakan. Think of a wildcat, but in human form, probably working in customer service.
usage_notes: Can describe both wild animals and ill-tempered people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siyang **balawis** sa kanilang lugar kaya walang nangangahas na lumapit.","translation":"He is known as an **ill-tempered** person in their area so no one dares to approach him."},{"sentence":"Isang **balawis** na pusa ang biglang tumalon mula sa bubong.","translation":"A **fierce** cat suddenly jumped from the roof."}]

translation: to pick (fruit) with a hooked pole
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha ng prutas o anumang bagay gamit ang isang salungkit.
original_explanation: The verb form of the great fruit heist. "Tara, salungkitin natin 'yung mga mangga bago maunahan tayo ng mga ibon o ng may-ari." It’s a test of skill, balance, and how well you can aim a long stick at a piece of fruit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **salungkitin** ang mga bayabas sa kabilang bakod.","translation":"I want **to pick** the guavas on the other side of the fence **with a pole**."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **salungkitin** ang mga bunga dahil masusukal ang mga sanga.","translation":"It's difficult **to pick the fruits with a pole** because the branches are dense."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakapayak at pinakamaliit na yunit ng isang buhay na organismo na may kakayahang gumana nang mag-isa.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung basic building block ng lahat ng buhay, parang 'yung isang pirasong LEGO na bumubuo sa buong castle mo. Not to be confused with 'selda' (jail cell) or 'cell' as in 'cellphone'. Ito 'yung pinag-aaralan sa Science class na may nucleus, cytoplasm, atbp.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa konteksto ng agham, partikular sa biyolohiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang katawan ng tao ay binubuo ng trilyun-trilyong **sel**.","translation":"The human body is made up of trillions of **cells**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan namin ang iba't ibang parte ng **sel** sa klase.","translation":"We studied the different parts of the **cell** in class."}]

meaning_filipino: Aksidenteng tumama o maibangga ang ulo sa isang matigas na bagay.
etymology: From 'untog', the act of bumping one's head.
original_explanation: The universe's way of telling you to slow down and watch where you're going. It's that sudden, sharp "Aray!" moment when you stand up too fast under a low ceiling or walk into a glass door you thought was open. Sometimes used figuratively, like "Para kang nauntog," to describe someone who suddenly had a reality check or changed their bad behavior.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to bumping the head. For other body parts, 'mabangga' is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pagbaba, baka **mauntog** ka sa kisame.","translation":"Be careful going down, you might **bump your head** on the ceiling."},{"sentence":"Parang **nauntog** si Peter at biglang naging mabait.","translation":"It's like Peter **bumped his head** and suddenly became kind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng panitikan o palabas na inilalathala o ipinapalabas nang sunud-sunod na bahagi sa loob ng isang takdang panahon.
original_explanation: This is the OG binge-watch material before Netflix even existed. Think of those classic radio dramas your lola listened to, or the primetime teleseryes that make the whole nation stop. Each episode leaves you with a cliffhanger, making you say, 'Ano na kayang mangyayari bukas?!'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'serye' or 'teleserye' in the context of television shows.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakabahan ako sa susunod na kabanata ng paborito kong **seryal** sa radyo.","translation":"I'm nervous about the next chapter of my favorite radio **serial**."},{"sentence":"Naging sikat ang artistang iyon dahil sa isang **seryal** sa hapon.","translation":"That actor became famous because of an afternoon **series**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mababang ranggong opisyal na di-komisyonado sa militar o pulisya, mas mataas sa isang pribado ngunit mas mababa sa isang sarhento.
original_explanation: In the military hierarchy, the korporal is like the team lead in a BPO. Not quite the manager (Sarhento), but definitely not a newbie agent (Pribado). They're the ones who make sure the squad is doing their drills right and not just scrolling through TikTok.
usage_notes: Ginagamit din sa pariralang 'parusang korporal' para sa corporal punishment, ngunit bilang isang pangngalan, halos palaging tumutukoy ito sa ranggo sa militar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinaas ang kanyang ranggo mula pribado patungong **korporal**.","translation":"His rank was promoted from private to **corporal**."},{"sentence":"Ang **korporal** ang namuno sa kanilang pagsasanay.","translation":"The **corporal** led their training exercise."}]

translation: to buzz, to drone, to resound
meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng isang malalim, tuloy-tuloy, at malakas na tunog, tulad ng hangin, malaking kulisap, o makina.
original_explanation: It's the sound of a giant bee, the hum of a transformer box before a brownout, or the buzz of gossip spreading through the office. 'Umugong' is a deep, resonant sound that fills the space. It can be literal, like a machine's drone, or figurative, like a rumor that's getting louder and louder. 'Umugong ang balita na may bonus daw.'
usage_notes: Actor-focus verb in the completed aspect. Describes a continuous, low-frequency sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umugong** ang malakas na hangin bago bumuhos ang ulan.","translation":"The strong wind **droned** before the rain poured."},{"sentence":"**Umugong** sa buong bayan ang balita tungkol sa kanyang pagkapanalo.","translation":"The news about his/her victory **resounded** throughout the town."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng isang lalaki na maging sanhi ng pagdadalang-tao ng isang babae.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'panagutan mo 'ko' moment. This is what happens when 'Netflix and chill' goes wrong and leads to a nine-month subscription you can't cancel. It's the verb form of creating a major life plot twist.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the male action of causing a pregnancy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **bumuntis** sa kapatid ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"He was the one who **impregnated** his friend's sister."}]

translation: act of slashing or cutting open; a slash wound
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghiwa o pagpilas nang malaki at malalim gamit ang isang matalim na bagay; ang resulta o sugat mula sa gawaing ito.
original_explanation: This is a bit more intense than a simple "hiwa". Think Zorro leaving his mark, or a chef expertly scoring a fish before grilling. It's a slash, a deep cut. It can also describe the result of that action, like "May pagkalaslas yung sako ng bigas kaya natatapon." It's a word that sounds exactly like what it is: a sharp, tearing sound - laslas!
usage_notes: Can be quite graphic. Used for deep, long cuts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ang malaking **pagkalaslas** sa tagiliran ng barko.","translation":"A large **slash** was seen on the side of the ship."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkalaslas** sa kanyang braso ay nangailangan ng maraming tahi.","translation":"The **slash wound** on his arm required many stitches."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isa sa dalawang pantay na bahagi ng isang kabuuan.
etymology: From 'ka-' (denoting partnership or a part of a whole) + 'hati' (divide).
original_explanation: Yung sahod mo after 5 minutes na matanggap. O kaya 'yung pag-ibig na binibigay niya sa'yo, hindi buo. Charot. Perfect for sharing the last piece of pizza or splitting the bill. 'Kalahati' is the universal signal for 'let's share'.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (e.g., 'ang kalahati') or an adjective (e.g., 'kalahating manok').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinigay niya sa akin ang **kalahati** ng kanyang sandwich.","translation":"He gave me **half** of his sandwich."},{"sentence":"**Kalahati** na lang ang laman ng bote ng kape.","translation":"The coffee jar is only **half** full."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay ang pagmamaneho o pagpapaandar ng isang bangka o maliit na barko, karaniwang para sa pagtawid ng mga pasahero.
original_explanation: The barkero is the OG Grab driver of the river. He's the guy who takes you across a river or to another island when there's no bridge. You trust him with your life (and your groceries from the market) for a small fee.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkano ang bayad sa **barkero** para makatawid sa ilog?","translation":"How much is the fee for the **boatman** to cross the river?"},{"sentence":"Naghihintay ng pasahero ang mga **barkero** sa daungan.","translation":"The **boatmen** are waiting for passengers at the port."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagsang-ayon, permiso, o kawalan ng pagtutol sa isang mungkahi o gawain.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'seen-zoned.' When someone says they're 'payag', it means they're game. 'Libre ka ba sa Friday? Manood tayo ng sine.' 'Oo, payag ako!' It's the green light, the go signal, the 'yes' you were hoping for.
usage_notes: Often used to express consent or agreement to a proposal. While 'payag' can mean 'hut' in some other Philippine languages (like Cebuano), in standard Tagalog it almost exclusively means 'to agree'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Payag** ka bang sumama sa amin sa beach?","translation":"Are you **willing** to come with us to the beach?"},{"sentence":"Hindi ako **payag** sa gusto mong mangyari.","translation":"I don't **agree** with what you want to happen."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maayos na paglulong o pag-ikid ng isang bagay na manipis at mahaba tulad ng banig, alpombra, o lubid.
etymology: From mag- (verb-forming prefix) + kidkid (to roll up).
original_explanation: This is what you do with the banig (sleeping mat) every morning before you go to school or work. It's the act of rolling something up neatly for storage. Think rolling up a poster, a yoga mat, or even the giant tarp after a fiesta.
usage_notes: Specific to rolling up long, flat items like mats, carpets, or sails. More specific than 'magrolyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magkidkid** nitong banig.","translation":"Help me **roll up** this mat."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng piknik, sila ay nag-umpisang **magkidkid** ng kanilang sapin.","translation":"After the picnic, they started **to roll up** their ground mat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang angkop na pagkakataon o kalagayan upang maisagawa ang isang bagay o makamit ang isang layunin.
original_explanation: The more formal, corporate-sounding cousin of "pagkakataon." You hear "oportunidad" in job interviews ("Salamat po sa oportunidad na ito") or business proposals. It’s what your tita from a networking company is always offering you: a "great business oportunidad." It feels heavier and more significant than a simple "chance."
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pormal na pananalita at pagsulat, tulad sa negosyo, akademya, at pormal na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong sayangin ang **oportunidad** na makapag-aral sa ibang bansa.","translation":"Don't waste the **opportunity** to study abroad."},{"sentence":"Binigyan niya ako ng **oportunidad** na patunayan ang aking sarili.","translation":"He gave me an **opportunity** to prove myself."}]

translation: a species of medicinal plant (Premna odorata)
meaning_filipino: Isang mabangong palumpong o maliit na puno (Premna odorata) na may mga dahon na ginagamit sa tradisyonal na panggagamot, karaniwan para sa ubo at sipon.
original_explanation: Your lola's go-to herbal medicine before Vicks Vaporub was a thing. If you had a cough, she'd probably boil some alagaw leaves for you to drink or make into a 'suob' (steam inhalation). It's part of the OG Pinoy herbal starter pack, along with oregano and lagundi.
usage_notes: Known for its aromatic leaves and use in traditional Filipino folk medicine. It is officially recognized by the Philippine Department of Health as a medicinal plant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpakulo si Lola ng dahon ng **alagaw** para sa aking ubo.","translation":"Grandma boiled **alagaw** leaves for my cough."},{"sentence":"Mabisa raw na gamot sa kabag ang tsaa mula sa **alagaw**.","translation":"They say tea from **alagaw** is an effective remedy for gas pains."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang relihiyosong prusisyon na idinaraos tuwing buwan ng Mayo, na isinasadula ang paghahanap ni Santa Elena sa Banal na Krus. Ito ay karaniwang bahagi ng pagdiriwang ng Flores de Mayo.
etymology: From Spanish `Santa Cruz de Mayo`, meaning "Holy Cross of May".
original_explanation: This is the official, full name for the Santacruzan, the grandest beauty pageant-slash-religious procession of the year. It's the highlight of May, where the most beautiful ladies of the barangay get to be "Reyna Elena" for a night, walking under a fancy arc with their equally fancy escort. It's a celebration of finding the Holy Cross, but for many, it's also about finding the perfect gown and makeup artist.
usage_notes: Commonly shortened to `Santacruzan`. It's the culminating event of the month-long Flores de Mayo festival.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pamangkin ko ang napiling Reyna Elena para sa **Santa-Krus-de-Mayo** ngayong taon.","translation":"My niece was chosen as the Queen Helena for this year's **Santacruzan**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaki at malapad ang bibig na tapayan o banga na karaniwang sisidlan ng tubig.
original_explanation: The OG water dispenser of our ancestors. Before plastic gallons and filtered water stations, there was the 'taganas'. It's a big clay pot used for storing water, vinegar, or sometimes for fermentation. Think of it as the rustic, earthy cousin of your modern kitchen containers.
usage_notes: This is an old, almost obsolete term. Most people today would just use 'banga' or 'tapayan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Punuin mo ng tubig-ulan ang **taganas** sa likod-bahay.","translation":"Fill the **large earthen jar** in the backyard with rainwater."},{"sentence":"Natagpuan sa isang lumang kweba ang isang basag na **taganas**.","translation":"A broken **large, wide-mouthed earthen jar** was found in an old cave."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang komposisyong musikal na may mga salita o liriko, karaniwang inaawit ng isa o higit pang boses.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "canta", anyong pautos ng "cantar" (kumanta).
original_explanation: The national pastime of the Philippines, right next to basketball and chismis. Every Pinoy has a go-to kanta for the videoke machine, usually something by Aegis or Frank Sinatra. It's the soundtrack to our traffic jams, family gatherings, and heartbreaks.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb root.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong pakinggan ang mga **kanta** ni Ben&Ben.","translation":"I love listening to the **songs** of Ben&Ben."},{"sentence":"Anong **kanta** ang gusto mong isunod sa videoke?","translation":"What **song** do you want to play next on the videoke?"}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang tumupad sa tungkulin o obligasyon; mapagkakatiwalaan at may pananagutan sa mga kilos.
original_explanation: The opposite of your friend who says 'On the way na ako!' when they're still in the shower. A 'responsable' person is the group project leader who actually does the work, the panganay who sends money home without being told, or anyone who remembers to pay their Shopee SPayLater on time. Basically, an adultier adult.
usage_notes: Can refer to both being accountable for something and being a dependable person in general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang panganay, siya ang **responsable** sa pag-aaral ng kanyang mga kapatid.","translation":"As the eldest, he/she is **responsible** for his/her siblings' education."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng mga lider na **responsable** at tapat.","translation":"We need leaders who are **responsible** and honest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tali o panali, karaniwang gawa sa tela o katad, na ginagamit upang higpitan ang sapatos.
original_explanation: That thing that's always untied when you're in a hurry. The 'sintas' is the humble shoelace, the unsung hero that keeps your shoes from flying off your feet. It's also a classic movie trope: 'Excuse me, your sintas is untied,' is the low-budget way to start a conversation with your crush.
usage_notes: Can also refer to other types of laces or thin ribbons, but overwhelmingly means shoelace.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talian mo ang **sintas** ng sapatos mo, baka ka madapa.","translation":"Tie your **shoelace**, you might trip."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng bagong pares ng **sintas** na kulay pula.","translation":"I bought a new pair of red **shoelaces**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado o bansa kung saan ang kapangyarihan ay nasa mga mamamayan at kanilang mga inihalal na kinatawan, at mayroong pangulo sa halip na isang monarko.
original_explanation: Ito yung gobyerno na parang group project sa school. May leader (presidente), may mga groupmates (mamamayan), at dapat lahat nag-aambag. Ang pinagkaiba lang, sa republika, hindi mo pwedeng i-drop ang mga groupmate mong tamad. Welcome to the Republic of the Philippines!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay isang **republika** na may demokratikong pamahalaan.","translation":"The Philippines is a **republic** with a democratic government."},{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang natin ang Araw ng **Republika** tuwing Hulyo 4.","translation":"We celebrate **Republic** Day every July 4."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglilingkod o pagtatrabaho para sa isang tao, pamilya, o institusyon na gagawin sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of serving someone. It's what you tell your parents you'll do for the country when you graduate ("Maninilbihan ako sa bayan!"), or more practically, what an OFW might say before leaving to work abroad. It has a noble, formal ring to it, more than just "magtatrabaho." It implies service and dedication.
usage_notes: Future tense of 'manilbihan'. Often carries a sense of duty or formal service.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng kanyang pag-aaral, siya ay **maninilbihan** sa kanilang probinsya bilang isang doktor.","translation":"After his studies, he **will serve** in their province as a doctor."},{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipino ang nangibang-bansa upang **maninilbihan** at kumita para sa pamilya.","translation":"Many Filipinos go abroad to **work for** and earn for their family."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi mapapantayan o mahihigitan sa halaga, ganda, o anumang katangian.
etymology: Parirala: "wala" (none) + "-ng" (linker) + "makatumbas" (can equal/match), mula sa ugat na "tumbas" (equivalent).
original_explanation: This is how you describe your mom's cooking, Jollibee Chickenjoy, or the love of your life (charot!). It’s something so special, so perfect, that nothing else can compare. "The best ever!" "S-tier!" "GOAT (Greatest of All Time)!" It's that feeling when you find the perfect milk tea flavor and you know, deep in your soul, that nothing will ever be as good.
usage_notes: Isang malakas at mariing parirala na ginagamit upang ipahayag ang pinakamataas na papuri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal ng isang ina ay **walang-makatumbas**.","translation":"A mother's love is **incomparable**."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang ganda ng Pilipinas ay **walang-makatumbas** sa buong mundo.","translation":"For him, the beauty of the Philippines is **unequaled** in the whole world."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na may dalawang panga na pinaglalapit o pinaglalayo sa pamamagitan ng pag-ikot ng isang turnilyo, ginagamit upang mahigpit na hawakan ang isang bagay habang ito ay ginagawa.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'torsillo' o posibleng baryasyon ng 'tornillo'.
original_explanation: That heavy metal clamp in your Lolo's workshop that looks like a medieval torture device. It's used to hold wood or metal super tight so you can saw, drill, or file it without it moving. It's got a stronger grip than your clingy ex. Also called a 'gato'.
usage_notes: Kilala rin bilang 'gato' sa maraming konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipitan mo sa **tursilyo** ang kahoy para hindi gumalaw.","translation":"Clamp the wood in the **vise** so it won't move."},{"sentence":"Mahirap mag-lagari kung walang **tursilyo**.","translation":"It's hard to saw without a **screw press**."}]

meaning_filipino: Matindi at taimtim na damdamin, karaniwang tumutukoy sa kalungkutan, pag-ibig, o pananabik na nadarama nang malalim sa puso.
original_explanation: That 'senti' mode you get into at 2 AM, listening to sad OPM songs. It's the 'hugot' level: Expert. It's the feeling you get when you see your ex's wedding photos on Facebook. Sincere, deep, and usually painful.
usage_notes: A literary or formal word used to describe profound, often solemn or melancholic, emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **tagimtim** ang kanyang huling paalam.","translation":"His final goodbye was full of **intense emotion**."},{"sentence":"May **tagimtim** na lungkot sa kanyang mga mata.","translation":"There is a **heartfelt** sadness in his/her eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang umunawa o maintindihan ang isang bagay; pag-aalala o pagkalinga.
original_explanation: Yan 'yung wala ka 'pag math class. Pero 'yan din 'yung binibigay mo sa kaibigan mong heartbroken for the nth time. "Sige, iiyak mo lang, I'm here to listen." 'Pag may intindi ka, you get it, whether it's a concept or a feeling.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga anyong pandiwa tulad ng 'intindihin' (to understand), 'umintindi' (to understand), at 'maintindihan' (to be able to understand).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malawak ang kanyang **intindi** sa nararamdaman ng iba.","translation":"He has a deep **understanding** of what others feel."},{"sentence":"Paumanhin, pero wala akong **intindi** sa sinasabi mo.","translation":"Sorry, but I have no **understanding** of what you are saying."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng kagustuhan o pagkagiliw sa isang tao, bagay, o ideya, na para bang ito ay tinamaan sa puso, partikular sa konteksto ng social media.
etymology: From ma- (ability/accidental verb prefix) + puso (heart) + -an (locative/object-focus suffix).
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'puso' (heart). Originally meant 'to feel something in your heart,' but in the age of social media, it's the official term for 'to heart' or 'to like' a post. 'Ma-heart mo naman 'yung profile pic ko!' It's the digital equivalent of a thumbs-up, but with more kilig.
usage_notes: Primarily used in social media contexts, like Facebook's 'heart' reaction. A modern neologism based on digital interactions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **mapusuan** mo ang regalo ko para sa'yo.","translation":"I hope you will **like** the gift I have for you."},{"sentence":"**Mapusuan** mo kaya ang bago kong post sa Instagram?","translation":"Will you **heart** my new post on Instagram?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aklat-liturhikal na naglalaman ng mga teksto, panalangin, at rubriko para sa pagdiriwang ng Misa sa buong taon.
original_explanation: This is the priest's "script" for the Mass. It's that big, fancy book on the altar that tells him what to say and do. It's got all the readings, prayers, and instructions, so he doesn't mess up the holy service. Think of it as the director's cut of the Mass.
usage_notes: Ito ang aklat na ginagamit ng pari sa altar sa pagmimisa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binuklat ng pari ang **misal** sa tamang pahina para sa Misa ng Linggo.","translation":"The priest opened the **missal** to the correct page for Sunday Mass."},{"sentence":"Nakalagay sa **misal** ang lahat ng panalangin para sa seremonya.","translation":"All the prayers for the ceremony are in the **missal**."}]

translation: to put a cover on; to wrap
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng pabalat o takip sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The act of putting a cover on something. Ito 'yung ginagawa mo sa mga bago mong notebook bago magpasukan. Kinukuha mo 'yung plastic cover, gunting, at tape. Kailangan perfect ang pagkakalagay, walang bubbles!
usage_notes: The root is 'balat' (skin/wrapper) but the action is to add a 'pabalat' (cover).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pabalatan** mo ang mga aklat para hindi agad masira.","translation":"**Put a cover on** the books so they don't get damaged easily."},{"sentence":"Inutusan niya akong **pabalatan** ang regalong ibibigay niya.","translation":"He/She instructed me **to wrap** the gift he/she will give."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-iba ng direksyon, landas, o paksa; pag-iwas o hindi pagsunod sa inaasahan o pamantayan.
original_explanation: When you're driving on SLEX and a bus suddenly cuts you off—that's paglihis. In conversations, it's when you're talking about work deadlines and your friend suddenly talks about the latest chismis. It's going off-topic, whether on the road or in a meeting.
usage_notes: Can be literal (changing physical path) or figurative (digressing from a topic or norm).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **paglihis** ng dyip ay nagdulot ng kaunting gulo sa trapiko.","translation":"The jeep's sudden **swerving** caused a bit of chaos in the traffic."},{"sentence":"Iwasan natin ang **paglihis** sa orihinal na paksa ng ating pagpupulong.","translation":"Let's avoid **digression** from the original topic of our meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang koleksyon ng mahahalagang bagay tulad ng ginto, pilak, at mga hiyas; anumang bagay na may mataas na halaga o itinuturing na napakahalaga.
original_explanation: Not just the pirate kind with the 'X' on the map. Your 'tesoro' could be your collection of K-Pop photocards, your Lola's secret adobo recipe, or that one piece of 'hugot' that perfectly describes your love life. It's something you value immensely, even if it's not literally gold.
usage_notes: Mas pampanitikan o pormal kaysa sa karaniwang salitang 'kayamanan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal ng aking pamilya ang tunay kong **tesoro**.","translation":"My family's love is my true **treasure**."},{"sentence":"Naniniwala ang ilan na may nakatagong **tesoro** si Yamashita sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Some believe that Yamashita has a hidden **treasure** in the Philippines."}]

translation: to make something blurry or unclear
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paggawa sa isang bagay na maging malabo, hindi malinaw, o mahirap maunawaan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pangkauusalan na "pa-" at "panlabo" (na hango sa "labo").
original_explanation: This is what happens to your vision after a long night of K-drama, or what politicians do to an issue they don't want to answer directly. It’s making things hazy, whether it’s your eyesight, a photo, or the truth. "Pinalabo mo usapan natin" is the relationship version.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal (para sa paningin/larawan) o patalinhaga (para sa mga ideya/sitwasyon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **papanlabuin** ang isyu sa pamamagitan ng pag-iiba ng usapan.","translation":"Don't **complicate/make the issue unclear** by changing the topic."},{"sentence":"Ginagamit ang filter na ito upang **papanlabuin** ang mga gilid ng litrato.","translation":"This filter is used to **make the edges of the photo blurry**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga durog o basag na butil ng bigas na nahihiwalay sa buong butil sa proseso ng paggiling.
original_explanation: You know when you're washing rice and you see those tiny, broken pieces? That's binlid. It's the "rejects" of the rice world, but it's perfect for making lugaw (porridge) because it cooks faster and gets mushier. It's the underdog of the bigasan.
usage_notes: Often associated with making congee (lugaw/arroz caldo) or used as animal feed. It is generally cheaper than whole grain rice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas masarap gamitin ang **binlid** sa paggawa ng lugaw dahil mas malapot ito.","translation":"It's better to use **broken rice grains** for making porridge because it becomes thicker."},{"sentence":"Naghiwalay siya ng isang takal na **binlid** para ipakain sa mga manok.","translation":"She set aside a cup of **broken rice grains** to feed the chickens."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na pudpod, gasgas, o numipis na dahil sa madalas na paggamit, pagkiskis, o katagalan.
original_explanation: That feeling when your favorite pambahay t-shirt is so thin you can almost see through it. Or when the treads on your shoes are gone because you walked all over the mall looking for a specific Funko Pop. Your brain after a week of OT (overtime) is also sayod. It’s the physical state of being “pagod na pagod” (very tired).
usage_notes: Often used for fabric, ropes, tires, or any object that wears down with friction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sayod** na ang mga gulong ng kanyang bisikleta.","translation":"The tires of his bicycle are already **worn-out**."},{"sentence":"Palitan mo na 'yang tsinelas mo, **sayod** na ang swelas.","translation":"Change your slippers already, the sole is **worn-out**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sasakyang-pantubig na may layag upang mapagalaw ng hangin.
original_explanation: Before jetskis and yachts, ito ang OG pamporma sa dagat. Parang vinta pero mas generic. Perfect for that dramatic 'Moana' moment, singing "See the line where the sky meets the sea? It calls me!" habang naglalayag palayo sa responsibilities.
usage_notes: A descriptive compound noun referring to any boat equipped with a sail.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **bangkang-may-layag** ang marahang umuusad sa gitna ng karagatan.","translation":"A **sailboat** moves slowly in the middle of the ocean."}]

translation: to give a gift or share (upon arriving from a trip)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pasalubong o anumang regalo sa isang tao, lalo na bilang pagbabahagi ng biyaya o bilang isang pormalidad. Maaari ring tumukoy sa sapilitang paghingi ng bahagi o regalo.
etymology: From 'balato' (a small gift, often from winnings). The suffix '-han' makes it a verb of action towards something or someone.
original_explanation: This is the act of giving pasalubong, but with a slight twist. It can be the friendly "Heto o, balatuhan kita ng dried mangoes galing Cebu." Or it can be the more demanding, "Hoy, kadarating mo lang galing Japan! Balatuhan mo naman kami!" It's the social tax you pay for traveling.
usage_notes: Can mean both to give a share/gift, or to demand a share/gift. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Balatuhan** mo naman ako ng tsokolate pag-uwi mo.","translation":"**Give me some** chocolate as a gift when you get home."},{"sentence":"Nanalo siya sa lotto kaya binalatuhan niya ang lahat ng kaibigan.","translation":"He won the lottery so he **gave a share** to all his friends."}]

meaning_filipino: May katangiang mabilis magliyab o sumiklab kapag nalapit sa apoy; tumutukoy din sa taong mabilis magalit.
etymology: From madali (easy) + -ng (linker) + magsiklab (to ignite, to flare up).
original_explanation: Literally, this is gasoline or alcohol—don't smoke near them. Figuratively, it's your friend who goes from zero to 'Hulk smash!' in 2.5 seconds kapag naasar. Sila yung 'pikon' o 'mainitin ang ulo.' You have to walk on eggshells around them.
usage_notes: Describes both physical flammability and a person's volatile temperament.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilayo mo ang gas sa apoy dahil ito ay **madaling magsiklab**.","translation":"Keep the gasoline away from the fire because it is **flammable**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong biruin si Boss ngayon, **madaling magsiklab** ang ulo niyan kapag stressed.","translation":"Don't joke with the Boss today, he's **short-tempered** when stressed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng tagpi o piraso ng tela o ibang materyal upang takpan ang butas o sira sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Like trying to fix a broken heart with a band-aid, or when you realize your budget for the month won't make it so you have to "patch" things up by borrowing from your 'ipon' for your GrabFood addiction. "Tagpiin mo muna yung budget, besh."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit para sa damit, gulong, o maging sa badyet. Ang bagay na tinatagpian ang pokus ng pandiwa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **tagpiin** ang butas sa aking lumang maong.","translation":"I need to **patch** the hole in my old jeans."},{"sentence":"**Tagpiin** mo na lang muna iyang gulong para makauwi tayo.","translation":"Just **patch** that tire for now so we can go home."}]

translation: act of taking a turn; working a shift
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghalili o pagpapalitan sa isang gawain o posisyon; ang pagganap sa isang takdang oras ng trabaho.
original_explanation: The BPO and healthcare life in one word. It's that moment you're waiting for your shift to end so the next person can take over. It’s the 'ikaw naman' moment, whether sa trabaho, sa paghugas ng pinggan, or sa pagbabantay sa tindahan.
usage_notes: Commonly used in professional settings like hospitals, factories, and call centers to refer to shift changes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maayos ang naging **pagturno** ng mga nars sa ospital.","translation":"The **changing of shifts** of the nurses at the hospital was orderly."},{"sentence":"Oras na para sa **pagturno** ng mga guwardiya.","translation":"It's time for the guards' **turnover**."}]

translation: to be raided; to be attacked
meaning_filipino: Biglaang sugurin o lusubin ng isang pangkat upang manakit, manira, o magnakaw.
original_explanation: This is what happens to a villain's lair in an action movie. Or a refrigerator at 2 AM when you're hungry. It’s a sudden, forceful invasion. In the digital world, it's your social media account getting flooded with comments from a rival fanbase. It implies being overwhelmed by an aggressive force.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of military attacks, police raids, or even aggressive animal behavior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kuta ng mga pirata ay **sinalakay** ng mga sundalo.","translation":"The pirates' fort **was raided** by the soldiers."},{"sentence":"Baka **masalakay** ng mga langgam ang asukal kung hindi mo ito itatago.","translation":"The ants might **attack** the sugar if you don't store it properly."}]

translation: to fall flat on one's face; to stumble and fall face-first
meaning_filipino: Biglaang pagbagsak o pagkatumba kung saan ang mukha ang unang tumama sa lupa o sahig.
etymology: ma- (unintentional action prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + subasob (fall face down)
original_explanation: The most ungraceful way to fall. It’s not just tripping; it’s a full-on, face-first dive into the pavement. This happens when you’re rushing, not looking where you’re going, and life decides to teach you a lesson in humility. "Sa sobrang pagmamadali ko, napasubasob ako sa harap ng crush ko." The universe has a dark sense of humor.
usage_notes: A very descriptive word for a specific type of fall.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nadulas ang bata sa basang sahig at **napasubasob**.","translation":"The child slipped on the wet floor and **fell flat on his face**."},{"sentence":"Muntik na akong **mapasubasob** dahil sa malaking bato sa daan.","translation":"I almost **fell face-first** because of a large rock on the path."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magdulot ng sakit, pisikal man o emosyonal, sa isang tao o anumang may buhay.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'hugot' verb. It's what your ex did to you. It's also what you do to your pinky toe when you bump into furniture at 3 AM. It can be physical pain ('pananakit') or emotional damage. The ultimate 'ouch' word.
usage_notes: 'Manakit' is the act of *inflicting* pain, while 'masaktan' is the state of *feeling* pain or being hurt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko intensyon na **manakit** ng damdamin ng iba.","translation":"It's not my intention **to hurt** the feelings of others."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang di-pangkaraniwang pagpapakita ng isang nilalang na sobrenatural, tulad ng isang multo, santo, o espiritu.
original_explanation: The spooky stuff. It's when you see a white lady on Balete Drive or when a saint supposedly appears to someone. It's not just a ghost (multo); an apparition is more... dramatic. It's a full-on spectral appearance, the kind that makes it to the evening news during Halloween season.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with religious or supernatural events, carrying more weight than the common 'multo' (ghost).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming deboto ang naniniwala sa **aparisyon** ng Birheng Maria sa iba't ibang lugar.","translation":"Many devotees believe in the **apparition** of the Virgin Mary in various places."},{"sentence":"May kuwento tungkol sa isang **aparisyon** ng sundalong Hapon sa lumang gusali.","translation":"There is a story about an **apparition** of a Japanese soldier in the old building."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na nagkokontrol sa daloy ng likido o gas sa pamamagitan ng pagbubukas, pagsasara, o bahagyang pagharang sa mga daanan.
original_explanation: Ito yung bagay na pinipihit mo para buksan o isara ang tubig sa gripo o gasul. Parang sa relasyon, kailangan mo ng 'balbula' para i-regulate ang feelings, para hindi biglang bumuhos lahat at magka-dramahan. Control the flow, bes.
usage_notes: Commonly used in plumbing, mechanical, and industrial contexts.
