usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisara ang **balbula** ng tangke ng tubig.","translation":"Please close the **valve** of the water tank."},{"sentence":"Sira yata ang **balbula** ng LPG kaya nangangamoy.","translation":"The **valve** of the LPG tank might be broken, that's why it smells."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na hindi kayang abutin ng isipan, hulaan, o isipin na mangyayari dahil sa pagiging pambihira o sukdulan nito.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (not), unlaping "ma-", pag-uulit ng unang pantig "hi-", at salitang-ugat na "hinagap" (imagination, premonition).
original_explanation: 'Yung sweldo mo after 5 years sa BPO, tapos biglang nanalo ka ng 1 billion sa lotto. 'Yung lifestyle change? Di-mahihinagap. Hindi mo man lang na-imagine in your wildest dreams. Beyond akenat 'yan.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat literary term. Not common in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sakit na naramdaman niya ay **di-mahihinagap** ninuman.","translation":"The pain he felt was **unimaginable** to anyone."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-unlad ng teknolohiya sa susunod na 100 taon ay **di-mahihinagap** sa ngayon.","translation":"The advancement of technology in the next 100 years is **inconceivable** today."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag ng kawalan ng kaalaman o kasiguraduhan tungkol sa isang bagay. Katumbas ng "Hindi ko alam." Ang mas karaniwang anyo nito sa kasalukuyan ay "Ewan".
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang pinaikling anyo ng pariralang "ay, alam ko ba?" na naging "ay-alam" at kalaunan ay "aywan" o "ewan."
original_explanation: This is the OG "IDK." Before we typed "Ewan," our grandparents were already dropping this classic. It's the polite but firm way of saying "That's not my circus, not my monkeys" or "Wala akong pake, besh." Often used interchangeably with its more popular sibling, "Ewan."
usage_notes: Madalas itong ginagamit kasama ang "ko" (Aywan ko!). Ang "Aywan" ay medyo mas makaluma kumpara sa mas karaniwang variant nitong "Ewan."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Aywan!** Huwag mo akong tanungin diyan.","translation":"**I don't know!** Don't ask me about that."},{"sentence":"Tinanong niya kung kailan ang dating, sagot ko'y **aywan**.","translation":"He asked when the arrival is, my answer was **I don't know**."}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa "rich kid" o anak-mayaman. Tumutukoy sa isang taong lumaki sa marangyang pamilya.
etymology: Acronym for the English phrase 'rich kid'.
original_explanation: That classmate who always has the latest iPhone, whose baon is from Starbucks, and whose "pamalengke" outfit is branded from head to toe. That's an **RK**. "Ay, 'di 'yan sasama sa carinderia, **RK** 'yan eh."
usage_notes: Used as a label, sometimes with a hint of envy, judgment, or simple observation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata namang **RK** siya, laging may driver at yaya.","translation":"It's obvious she's a **rich kid**, she always has a driver and a nanny."},{"sentence":"Magkano ba ang budget mo? Pang-normal o pang-**RK**?","translation":"How much is your budget? For a normal person or for a **rich kid**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng kamay na parang sumasagwan sa hangin upang tumawag ng pansin o magsenyas sa isang tao na lumapit.
etymology: From "um-" (actor-focus infix) + "kabyaw" (a large ladle, or the motion of using one).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo 'pag tinatawag mo 'yung jeep na malayo pa, 'yung parang naghahalo ka ng malaking-malaking sabaw sa ere. Hindi lang simpleng 'kaway', mas desperate at mas malaki ang motion. "Hoy! Para!" sabay kabyaw.
usage_notes: Describes a specific type of wave, a large, beckoning gesture, often to call a vehicle or a person from a distance. The root word 'kabyaw' is a large ladle used in sugar mills, and the verb mimics the scooping motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumabyaw** siya sa paparating na bus para huminto ito.","translation":"He **waved his hand** at the approaching bus to make it stop."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko si Maria sa kabilang kalsada kaya **kumabyaw** ako para tawagin siya.","translation":"I saw Maria on the other side of the street so I **waved** to call her."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon ng pagpapalakas ng loob na nagsasabing ipagpatuloy lamang ang ginagawa o ninanais sa kabila ng pagod o hirap.
etymology: Mula sa Taglish na "push" at sa Tagalog na partikulong "lang" (lamang).
original_explanation: The shorter, more casual version of "I-push mo 'yan!" It's what you tell yourself when you're on your 5th coffee of the day trying to beat a deadline. It's a mix of encouragement and resignation. "Pagod na ako, pero **push lang**." (I'm tired, but I'll just keep going.) It's the mantra of the working class and the over-caffeinated student.
usage_notes: Isang pariralang pampalakas-loob na ginagamit upang sabihin sa isang tao (o sa sarili) na magpatuloy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit maraming problema, **push lang** nang **push lang**.","translation":"Even with many problems, just **keep going** and **keep going**."},{"sentence":"Malapit na ang deadline, **push lang**!","translation":"The deadline is near, just **push through**!"}]

translation: to oppose each other; to contradict one another
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay na pagtutol o pagsalungat ng dalawa o higit pang panig sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: Ito yung eksena sa meeting na ayaw magpatalo ng bawat department. Parang debate sa Congress pero sa office pantry. 'Ayoko niyan!' 'Hindi pwede 'yan!' Hanggang sa mag-uwian na lang kayo nang walang napagkasunduan.
usage_notes: The '-han' suffix implies a reciprocal or mutual action between two or more parties.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumigil na kayo sa pag-**magkontrahan** at magtulungan na lang para sa proyekto.","translation":"Stop **opposing each other** and just work together for the project."},{"sentence":"Laging nag-**kokontrahan** ang isip at puso ko pagdating sa'yo.","translation":"My mind and heart are always **in conflict** when it comes to you."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing mas makitid o mas maliit ang espasyo o lawak ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: It's what the 'sastre' (tailor) does to your pants after you've lost weight. It's what happens to your budget when unexpected bills arrive. It’s also what you ask the jeepney driver to do metaphorically when you say 'pakisiksik na lang po,' asking people to make the space narrower so you can fit.
usage_notes: The root word 'kitid' is an adjective meaning 'narrow'. 'Kitiran' is the verb 'to make narrow'. The opposite is 'lawakan' (to widen).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**kitiran** mo naman ang laylayan ng pantalon ko.","translation":"Please **make** the hem of my pants **narrower**."},{"sentence":"**Kinitiran** nila ang kalsada para magtayo ng mga tindahan.","translation":"They **narrowed** the road to build stalls."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang matingkad ang pagkapula; kulay na masidhi sa pula.
original_explanation: Not just red, but *extra* red. Like your face when your mom starts showing baby pictures to your friends. Or the color of the stoplight when you're already late for your BPO shift. It's the Siling Labuyo of colors.
usage_notes: The repetition of the root word is a common way to form superlative adjectives in Tagalog, indicating a high degree of the quality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pulang-pula** ang mga labi niya dahil sa bagong lipstick.","translation":"Her lips are **very red** because of the new lipstick."},{"sentence":"Naging **pulang-pula** ang kanyang pisngi sa hiya.","translation":"His cheeks became **crimson** with embarrassment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kapatid na lalaki ng ama o ina; o ang asawa ng tiya. Ginagamit din bilang magalang na tawag sa mas matandang lalaki na hindi kamag-anak.
original_explanation: Your dad's or mom's brother, sure. But in the Philippines, 'Tito' is also any of your parents' male friends, your boss, your older male cousin, or just a random guy in his 30s-50s who cracks dad jokes, wears New Balance sneakers, and loves '80s rock. The female equivalent is Tita. Being a 'Tito' is a whole lifestyle.
usage_notes: Used as a term of address and a noun. Capitalized when used before a name (e.g., Tito Boy). 'Tiyo' is the more formal, less common equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tito** ko ay kapatid ng aking ina.","translation":"My **uncle** is my mother's brother."},{"sentence":"'Kamusta po, **Tito**?' ang bati ng bata sa kaibigan ng kanyang ama.","translation":"'How are you, **Uncle**?' the child greeted his father's friend."}]

translation: Sablay (the academic sash of the University of the Philippines)
meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na kasuotang pang-akademiko ng Unibersidad ng Pilipinas na isinusuot sa balikat sa halip na ang tradisyonal na toga at cap. Ito ay may mga sagisag na kumakatawan sa unibersidad.
etymology: From the general meaning of 'sablay' as something draped over the shoulder, adopted by the University of the Philippines.
original_explanation: The ultimate flex for a UP student. It's not just a sash; it's a symbol of surviving hell week, hell sem, and the whole UP system. Wearing the Sablay is the goal. Moving it from the right shoulder to the left during the ceremony is the moment. Seeing your parents cry while you wear it is the reward. It's the most coveted 'sabit' in Philippine academia.
usage_notes: Highly specific to the University of the Philippines. Using it in other contexts for a sash would be incorrect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isuot mo nang may dangal ang iyong **Sablay**.","translation":"Wear your **Sablay** with honor."},{"sentence":"Pinangarap niyang makapagsuot ng **Sablay** sa araw ng kanyang pagtatapos.","translation":"She dreamed of wearing the **Sablay** on her graduation day."}]

translation: to emulate; to imitate (as a model)
meaning_filipino: Gayahin o sundin ang halimbawa ng isang tao o bagay na itinuturing na modelo o huwaran.
etymology: Nagmula sa `pag-` + `tularan` (gayahin), na galing sa ugat na `tulad` (katulad, kapareho).
original_explanation: This is the "sana all" verb. It's when you see someone so successful, kind, or amazing that you want to be just like them. "Dapat siyang pagtularan." It's looking up to your lola, your favorite celebrity who does charity work, or that one officemate who finishes all their tasks on time and still has a life. It's the act of setting someone as your role model.
usage_notes: Ito ay nasa anyong pandiwang pautos o pawatas na nakapokus sa layon, na nangangahulugang 'dapat gayahin' o 'gayahin bilang modelo'. Ang katumbas nitong pangngalan ay 'pagtulad' (act of imitating).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang kasipagan ay dapat **pagtularan** ng lahat.","translation":"His diligence should be **emulated** by everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging tamad, walang ginagawa, at palaging nakahiga o nakahilata lamang.
etymology: A reduplicative and blended compound from `pahiga` (lying down) and `hilata` (sprawled). The `hila` part adds a sense of being dragged down by laziness.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'palamon' or 'tambay' mode. It's more than just resting; it's a lifestyle of being unproductive and just sprawling around the house. It's what your parents accuse you of doing during summer vacation. You're not just *pahiga* (lying down), you're *pahila-hilata*—professionally doing nothing.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of laziness and unproductiveness. Can also be used as an adverb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Buong araw lang siyang **pahila-hilata** sa bahay at nanonood ng TV.","translation":"He was just **idly lying around** the house all day watching TV."},{"sentence":"Napagalitan siya ng nanay niya dahil sa pagiging **pahila-hilata**.","translation":"His mother scolded him for **loafing**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakaplanong gawain, kadalasang may partikular na layunin at nangangailangan ng malaking panahon, na isinasagawa ng isang tao o grupo.
original_explanation: Ito yung dahilan ng mga puyat mo nung college. Ito rin yung 'Build, Build, Build' ng gobyerno. Pwede ring personal, like 'Project: Magka-jowa before 30' o 'Project: Balik-Alindog Program.' Basta may plano, may deadline, at may effort, proyekto 'yan!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong tapusin ang **proyekto** ko sa agham bago ang Biyernes.","translation":"I need to finish my science **project** before Friday."},{"sentence":"Ang pagpapatayo ng bagong tulay ay isang malaking **proyekto** ng pamahalaan.","translation":"The construction of the new bridge is a major government **project**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hilingin o iutos sa isang tao na lagdaan ang isang dokumento, o lagyan ng pirma ang isang partikular na lugar sa isang papel.
etymology: From the root word 'pirma' (signature, from Spanish 'firma') and the verbal affix 'pa- -han', indicating the location or object of the action.
original_explanation: Ah, the life of every student, employee, or anyone dealing with Philippine bureaucracy. This is the verb for getting something signed. Your clearance form? Papirmahan mo sa lahat ng department. Your excuse letter? Papirmahan mo sa nanay mo. This verb focuses on the *thing* or *place* being signed. "Saan ko ba 'to papirmahan?" is a question that echoes in government offices everywhere.
usage_notes: Focuses on the object or location being signed. Contrast with 'papirmahin', which focuses on the person signing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **papirmahan** ang kontratang ito sa aming CEO.","translation":"I need to **have this contract signed** by our CEO."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **papirmahan** ang attendance sheet bago umuwi.","translation":"Don't forget to **have the attendance sheet signed** before going home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng loro (parrot) na may puting balahibo, partikular ang Cacatua haematuropygia o red-vented cockatoo.
original_explanation: 'Yung ibon na puti na mukhang sosyal at kung minsan ay natututong magsalita. Hindi 'yung maya na common, ito 'yung medyo rare at magandang alagaan. Pero bawal hulihin 'yan, critically endangered!
usage_notes: Refers to a specific species of bird, also known as the 'katala' or red-vented cockatoo. It is a critically endangered species native to the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang pambihirang **abukay** ang dumapo sa puno.","translation":"A rare **white parrot** landed on the tree."},{"sentence":"Ang **abukay** ay isa sa mga nanganganib na uri ng ibon sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The **white parrot** (abukay) is one of the endangered bird species in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha o paghuli ng isda o iba pang bagay mula sa tubig gamit ang isang uri ng lambat o salaan na may hawakan.
original_explanation: Picture yourself by a fishpond or aquarium. That small net you use to scoop out a fish? That action is 'pagsakyod'. It's also used for ladling soup or sauce, that scooping motion to get liquid out of a big pot. It’s a gentle, scooping-up action.
usage_notes: Usually involves a tool like a small net (sakyod) or a ladle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat ang kanyang **pagsakyod** sa gintong isda mula sa aquarium.","translation":"His **scooping** of the goldfish from the aquarium was careful."},{"sentence":"Isang **pagsakyod** lang ng sinigang, busog ka na.","translation":"Just one **ladleful** of sinigang, and you're already full."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahing kakayahan na umunawa, mag-isip, at humatol sa isang praktikal at makatwirang paraan na inaasahan sa halos lahat ng tao.
original_explanation: 'Yung bagay na "common" pero hindi na ganoon ka-common ngayon. 'Yung alam mong 'wag tatawid 'pag green ang ilaw para sa sasakyan, o 'wag mag-post ng picture ng ATM card mo online. Kung kailangan mo pa i-Google, baka kulang ka na sa sintido-kumun.
usage_notes: A direct loan phrase from Spanish. Often used to call out someone's lack of practical judgment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo naman ang iyong **sintido-kumun** bago ka magdesisyon.","translation":"Please use your **common sense** before you make a decision."},{"sentence":"Wala talagang **sintido-kumun** ang taong nagtapon ng basura sa ilog.","translation":"The person who threw trash in the river really has no **common sense**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang trabaho ay magbantay sa pinto o tarangkahan ng isang gusali, tulad ng hotel o apartment.
original_explanation: 'Yung unang bumabati sa'yo sa hotel o condo, 'yung nagbubukas ng pinto at tumutulong sa bagahe mo. Hindi lang siya security guard, may class. Siya 'yung may uniform na maganda at laging nakangiti (kahit pagod na). Sa soccer, siya 'yung "goalkeeper".
usage_notes: Also used in sports, specifically soccer (football), to mean "goalkeeper".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binati kami ng **portero** pagpasok namin sa hotel.","translation":"The **doorman** greeted us as we entered the hotel."},{"sentence":"Ang galing ng **portero** ng kabilang koponan; walang nakalusot na bola.","translation":"The opposing team's **goalkeeper** was excellent; no ball got past him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbaluktot o pagbibigay-hugis sa isang bagay, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng puwersa o init.
original_explanation: Think of a panday (blacksmith) hammering hot metal into a blade. That's paghutok. It's also what your strict parents or a tough mentor does to your character—molding you into a responsible (or traumatized) adult.
usage_notes: Can be literal (bending metal) or metaphorical (shaping a person's character or skills).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matinding init para sa **paghutok** ng bakal.","translation":"Intense heat is needed for the **shaping** of steel."},{"sentence":"Ang mahigpit na pagsasanay ay isang paraan ng **paghutok** sa disiplina ng mga atleta.","translation":"Strict training is a way of **molding** the discipline of athletes."}]

translation: to go far away; to distance oneself
meaning_filipino: Sadyain ang pagpunta sa isang malayong lugar o sadyang ilayo ang sarili mula sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
etymology: From the prefix `magpaka-`, which signifies an intense or deliberate effort to become or do something, and the root word `layo` (far/distance).
original_explanation: That moment when you just want to book a one-way ticket to Siargao and ghost everyone. "Gusto ko na lang magpakalayo" is the official slogan of the burnt-out and the brokenhearted. It's the ultimate 'unfriend' button for real life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para makalimot, nagpasya siyang **magpakalayo** at manirahan sa probinsya.","translation":"To forget, she decided to **go far away** and live in the province."},{"sentence":"Minsan, kailangan mong **magpakalayo** para makita ang tunay na halaga ng mga bagay na iniwan mo.","translation":"Sometimes, you need to **distance yourself** to see the true value of the things you left behind."}]

meaning_filipino: Matinding galit o inis na pilit na pinipigilan, na karaniwang naipapakita sa pamamagitan ng pagngangalit ng mga ngipin.
original_explanation: You know that feeling when your internet dies in the middle of a crucial online meeting? You can't scream, so you just clench your jaw and make a low growling sound. That's **gitil**. It's the silent, teeth-grinding rage you feel when someone cuts you in line. It's the physical manifestation of "gigil na galit."
usage_notes: Madalas na may kasamang 'pagngangalit ng ngipin'. Ito ay isang panloob at pinipigilang galit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata sa kanyang mukha ang **gitil** habang nakikinig sa mga kasinungalingan.","translation":"The **repressed anger** was obvious on his face while listening to the lies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bukana o bunganga ng isang ilog kung saan ito bumubuhos patungo sa dagat, lawa, o iba pang anyong tubig.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *babaq na nangangahulugang 'ibaba' o 'bukana'.
original_explanation: Ito yung "exit point" ng ilog, parang ikaw lang sa isang toxic relationship. Dito nagtatagpo ang tubig-tabang at tubig-alat, a perfect metaphor for your mixed feelings.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin bilang pangalan ng lugar (hal. Wawa, Rizal; Wawa Dam).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming mangingisda ang nag-aabang sa **wawa** ng ilog.","translation":"Many fishermen wait at the **mouth** of the river."},{"sentence":"Dinala kami ng bangka sa may **wawa** kung saan mas kalmado ang tubig.","translation":"The boat took us to the **estuary** where the water was calmer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang utos o pakiusap na gawin muli ang isang sinabi o ginawa.
original_explanation: This is the polite but firm "Ano 'yun, 'di ko narinig?" It's what you say in a noisy coffee shop, during a laggy video call, or when your lola is telling a story and you missed the juicy part. Basically, "Run that back, please."
usage_notes: Often used in the form "Paulit nga?" (Can you repeat that?) or as a direct command. It's a shortened, more immediate form than "pakisuyong ulitin."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paulit** nga ng sinabi mo, hindi ko narinig.","translation":"**Repeat** what you said, I didn't hear it."},{"sentence":"Guro: 'Juan, **paulit** ng huling talata.'","translation":"Teacher: 'Juan, **repeat** the last paragraph.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng baging na may malalaki at pahabang bunga na karaniwang ginagawang gulay.
original_explanation: That pale green vegetable that's a staple in ginisang upo or tinola. It's 90% water, just like your tears when you realize it's upo for dinner again. Healthy, but not exactly the life of the party.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng **upo** sa palengke para sa pananghalian.","translation":"Mom bought a **bottle gourd** at the market for lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga taong magkasama sa isang paglalakbay o paglalakbay.
etymology: From `ka-` (companion) + `alakbay` (a variant/old form related to `lakbay`, journey).
original_explanation: Your travel buddy. The person you split the Grab fare with on the way to the airport. The one who takes your Instagram photos at every tourist spot. You are `magkaalakbay`. It can also be used metaphorically for people who are on the same journey in life, like you and your workmates surviving another week.
usage_notes: This is a less common word. `Kasama sa paglalakbay` or `kasama sa byahe` are more frequently used. `Magkaalakbay` has a more literary or poetic feel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging mabuting magkaibigan ang dalawang **magkaalakbay** na nagkakilala sa tren.","translation":"The two **fellow travelers** who met on the train became good friends."},{"sentence":"Tayo ay mga **magkaalakbay** sa landas ng buhay na ito.","translation":"We are **fellow travelers** on this path of life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paunang at agarang tulong na ibinibigay sa sinumang nagtamo ng karamdaman o pinsala, na may layuning mapreserba ang buhay, maiwasan ang paglala ng kondisyon, at maitaguyod ang paggaling.
etymology: Kombinasyon ng "pangunahin" (primarya, mula sa "una") at "lunas" (remedy, cure).
original_explanation: This is the stuff you do *before* the real doctors arrive. Think of it as the 'Tita who knows everything' remedy for a scrape, a fever, or even a minor heartbreak. It's the Band-Aid, the Vicks VapoRub, the "inom ka lang ng tubig" advice all rolled into one. It's the immediate, often temporary, fix.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa "pangunang lunas". Binibigyang-diin ng "pangunahin" ang pagiging 'primaryo' o 'pangunahin', habang ang "pangunang" ay tumutukoy sa 'pauna' o 'unang' hakbang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat lahat ay may kaalaman sa **pangunahing lunas** para sa mga emergency.","translation":"Everyone should have knowledge of **first aid** for emergencies."},{"sentence":"Ang paglalagay ng yelo ay **pangunahing lunas** para sa sprain.","translation":"Applying ice is the **primary remedy** for a sprain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng aswang sa mitolohiyang Pilipino na may kakayahang magpalit ng anyo, karaniwang nagiging ibon, at sinasabing naghahanap ng mga buntis upang kainin ang sanggol sa sinapupunan. Ang pangalan nito ay hango sa tunog na 'tik-tik' na ginagawa nito.
etymology: Onomatopoeia, from the 'tik-tik' sound the creature supposedly makes.
original_explanation: This is not your friendly neighborhood Marites. In Philippine folklore, the 'tiktik' is a type of 'aswang', often a bird-like creature, that scouts for pregnant women. Its 'tik-tik' sound is a terrifying form of misdirection: the louder it is, the farther away it is, but when the sound becomes faint, it's right beside you. Chills.
usage_notes: A specific creature in Philippine mythology, often considered a scout for a more powerful aswang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinaniniwalaan ng mga matatanda na ang tunog na iyon sa gabi ay mula sa isang **tiktik**.","translation":"The elders believe that that sound at night comes from a **tiktik**."},{"sentence":"Naglagay sila ng bawang sa bintana para itaboy ang **tiktik**.","translation":"They put garlic on the window to repel the **tiktik**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paninira o pagpinsala nang malawakan, karaniwang dulot ng isang kalamidad, sakit, o digmaan.
original_explanation: This is what happens when a super typhoon decides to give your town a 'makeover'. It's nature's version of a rage quit, leaving everything in shambles. Think Ondoy, Yolanda – that level of destruction. It's the 'wala nang natira' moment.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of natural disasters, epidemics, or war.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsalanta** ng bagyo ay nag-iwan ng malaking pinsala sa agrikultura.","translation":"The **devastation** of the typhoon left huge damage to agriculture."},{"sentence":"Hindi malilimutan ng mga tao ang tindi ng **pagsalanta** sa kanilang bayan.","translation":"The people will not forget the intensity of the **ravaging** in their town."}]

translation: pastel (a type of pie or pastry)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuin na inihurno, na may palamang karne o manok na may sarsang gatas o krema, at nababalutan ng masa.
original_explanation: Hindi ito krayola! Ito yung parang chicken pot pie ng Pinas. Madalas handa sa mga fiesta o Noche Buena. Creamy chicken filling na nakabalot sa flaky crust. Parang empanada na nag-level up at naging mas 'sosyal'. Comfort food na lasang Pasko.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang partikular na maalat na pagkaing inihurno, kadalasang may creamy chicken filling, katulad ng isang pot pie. Karaniwan sa ilang rehiyon tulad ng Bulacan at Pampanga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lola ko ang pinakamasarap gumawa ng chicken **pastel**.","translation":"My grandmother makes the most delicious chicken **pastel**."},{"sentence":"Nag-order kami ng isang buong **pastel** para sa salu-salo.","translation":"We ordered a whole **pastel** for the get-together."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na ginagamit bilang palamuti o pampaganda sa isang lugar o bagay.
original_explanation: Anything that's 'for display only.' It's the fancy plates in the 'platera' that you can't eat on, the throw pillows on the sofa you're not supposed to lean on, and the Christmas lights you put up in September. Basically, its only job is to look pretty and add ~aesthetic~. It's the 'pampaganda' for your house, your event, or your ube cake.
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective (bagay na pandekorasyon) or a noun (Ginamit ko ito bilang pandekorasyon). The `pang-` affix indicates purpose.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng mga bulaklak na **pandekorasyon** sa sala.","translation":"Mom bought flowers **for decoration** in the living room."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kainin iyan, prutas na waks lang iyan na **pandekorasyon**.","translation":"Don't eat that, it's just a wax fruit that's **decorative**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghinto, pagpigil, o pag-awat sa isang gawain o pangyayari, karaniwang isang negatibo o di-kanais-nais.
original_explanation: The word your lola screams when you and your cousins are about to demolish the house during a family reunion. "Sumawata na kayo!" means "Stop it already!". It has a stronger-than-usual connotation of putting an end to chaos or something excessive. It's the verb form of "Tama na, sobra na!"
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect of the verb. It is often used in the command form "sumawata ka/kayo!" to demand an immediate stop to a chaotic or negative action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi **sumawata** ang mga bata sa paglalaro hangga't hindi sila pinapagalitan.","translation":"The children did not **stop** playing until they were scolded."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **sumawata** na ang kanyang pag-iyak.","translation":"I hope her crying **ceases**."}]

translation: to make or eat champorado (chocolate rice porridge)
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa o pagkain ng tsamporado, isang uri ng lugaw na may tsokolate.
original_explanation: The official verb for rainy day comfort food activities. It's when you decide to whip up a pot of that glorious chocolate rice porridge, best paired with tuyo (dried fish). It’s not just cooking; it’s a whole mood. 'Umuulan! Tara, magtsamporado tayo!'
usage_notes: Can mean either 'to make champorado' or 'to eat champorado,' depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magtsamporado** mamaya dahil malamig ang panahon.","translation":"I want to **make/eat champorado** later because the weather is cold."},{"sentence":"Nag-aya si Lola na **magtsamporado** kami para sa meryenda.","translation":"Grandma invited us to **have champorado** for our afternoon snack."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang instrumentong pangmusika sa pamilya ng perkusyon na binubuo ng mga kahoy na bar na pinapatunog sa pamamagitan ng pagpalo ng mallets.
original_explanation: Yung instrumentong mukhang rainbow na pinapalo-palo mo nung kinder ka. Yung nagbigay sa'yo ng unang taste of musical genius mo bago mo nalaman na 'Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star' lang pala kaya mong i-play. It's the happy-sounding instrument that looks like a colorful skeleton's rib cage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natutong tumugtog ng **silopono** ang bata sa kanyang klase sa musika.","translation":"The child learned to play the **xylophone** in his music class."}]

translation: to go astray; to be led to a bad end
meaning_filipino: Maligaw ng landas sa buhay; mapunta sa masamang kalagayan o kapahamakan, lalo na sa aspetong moral.
original_explanation: This is the official term for 'naligaw ng landas.' It's what your lola fears will happen if you hang out with the wrong crowd or stay out too late. Think of a promising student who drops out to become a full-time 'marites' or gets into bad habits. They've **napariwara**. It's the scenic route to disappointment.
usage_notes: Carries a strong moral and directional (life path) connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng kanyang mga magulang na umiwas sa masamang barkada upang hindi **mapariwara**.","translation":"His parents advised him to avoid bad company so he wouldn't **go astray**."},{"sentence":"Maraming kabataan ang **napariwara** dahil sa droga.","translation":"Many youths have **been led to a bad end** because of drugs."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng pakiramdam ng inggit o pagnanais na magkaroon ng kung anong mayroon ang iba.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'nakaka-' at salitang-ugat na 'inggit'.
original_explanation: What you feel when your friend posts their Japan travel photos while you're stuck in traffic on a Monday. Or when your officemate gets a promotion you were also eyeing. It's the 'Sana all' feeling in adjective form.
usage_notes: Naglalawaran ng isang bagay, sitwasyon, o katangian na nagiging sanhi ng pagkainggit ng iba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakakainggit** ang bago niyang kotse.","translation":"His new car is **enviable**."},{"sentence":"Ang relasyon nila ay **nakakainggit** tingnan.","translation":"Their relationship is **enviable** to look at."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o lugar, partikular na ang ulo, na may napakaraming kuto.
etymology: From "kuto" (louse) + "-an" (suffix indicating a place or abundance).
original_explanation: The ultimate playground horror story for any Filipino kid. If your head was itchy, your mom would threaten you with a suyod (fine-toothed comb) because you might be 'kutunan'. It's a low-key insult you throw at someone with messy hair, even as a joke.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (a lice-infested person/head) or an adjective (lice-infested).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng guro ang magulang ng batang **kutunan** na gamutin ito agad.","translation":"The teacher advised the parent of the **lice-infested** child to treat it immediately."},{"sentence":"Ayaw kong tumabi sa kanya, baka maging **kutunan** din ako.","translation":"I don't want to sit beside them, I might get **infested with lice** too."}]

translation: to serve someone; to be of service to
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng serbisyo, pag-aalaga, o paglilingkod sa isang tao, pangkat, o layunin.
original_explanation: This is that "serve the people" energy, whether you're a government official, a waiter during the lunch rush, or just being a good child to your parents. It's the act of dedicating your effort *to* someone. "Sino ang pinagsisilbihan mo?" isn't just a question for heroes; it's also for when you see your friend being an "alipin ng pag-ibig" (slave to love).
usage_notes: The `-han` suffix indicates that the action is directed towards a person, place, or entity, focusing on the recipient of the service.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang karangalan na **pagsilbihan** ang ating bayan.","translation":"It is an honor to **serve** our country."},{"sentence":"Sino ang dapat kong **pagsilbihan** ng kape?","translation":"Whom should I **serve** coffee to?"}]

meaning_filipino: Atasan, pilitin, o maging sanhi upang ang isang tao ay magbayad para sa isang produkto, serbisyo, utang, o bilang kaparusahan.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you lose a bet. Or when it's your turn to treat the barkada for lunch. "Sige, talo ka, kaya ikaw ang papagbayarin namin!" It's the act of forcing someone to shoulder the cost. Also, a word feared by anyone with 'utang'.
usage_notes: Causative verb from the root 'bayad' (payment). Often used interchangeably with the simpler 'pagbayarin', but 'papagbayarin' can sometimes imply a more complex situation or making multiple people pay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **papagbayarin** mo sa lahat ng nasirang gamit?","translation":"Who will you **make pay** for all the broken things?"},{"sentence":"Dapat lang na **papagbayarin** ang mga may kasalanan sa batas.","translation":"It is only right to **make** those who have wronged the law **pay**."}]

meaning_filipino: (Pangalan) Isang natatanging kalidad o katangian na tila pumapalibot sa isang tao o bagay. (Pandiwa) Ang pagpapakita ng tiwala sa sarili, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng pag-pose para sa isang larawan.
etymology: From English "aura", popularized in Philippine gay lingo and mainstream slang with a new verb meaning.
original_explanation: Originally your spiritual energy field, but now it's the act of serving a look, striking a pose, and projecting confidence for the 'gram. It's your inner Sassa Gurl coming out. When someone tells you to "awra," they're telling you to stop looking like a passport photo and start looking like a magazine cover. "Rampa na, besh! Awra!"
usage_notes: The verb form ("mag-awra," "umawra") is a very popular modern slang term. The noun form is less common than the slang verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang **awra** ng bagong manager, parang laging galit.","translation":"The new manager has a strong **aura**, like he's always angry."},{"sentence":"Tara, mag-picture tayo! **Awra** ka diyan!","translation":"Let's take a picture! **Strike a pose** over there!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para sa isang uri ng pananalita na pinaghahalo ang Ingles at Tagalog sa isang partikular na paraan, o sa taong gumagamit nito, na karaniwang iniuugnay sa mga nakatataas na uri sa lipunan.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa Espanyol na "coño", isang bulgar na salita, ngunit nag-iba ang kahulugan sa Pilipinas at naging katawagan sa isang sociolect.
original_explanation: 'Like, you know? It's so hard to make commute. It's so traffic, you know? I'll make sama to you later, I'll just make sundo my friends first.' It's that way of speaking, a mix of English and Tagalog with specific grammar quirks, often associated with students from exclusive schools. It's a vibe, a lifestyle, a meme.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan (isang konyo) o pang-uri (konyo magsalita). Maaari itong maging mapanlait, ngunit madalas ding ginagamit nang pabiro.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihirapan akong intindihin ang mga **konyo** kung minsan.","translation":"I sometimes find it hard to understand **Conyos**."},{"sentence":"Naging **konyo** ang pananalita niya mula nang mag-aral sa Maynila.","translation":"His way of speaking became **Conyo** since he started studying in Manila."}]

translation: to intensify; to worsen; to aggravate
meaning_filipino: Gawing mas matindi, mas malala, o mas marahas ang isang sitwasyon, damdamin, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: To turn the drama up to 11. When a small argument becomes a huge fight because someone brought up something from 5 years ago. "Wag mo nang **patindihin** ang away!" (Don't make the fight worse!). It's adding fuel to the fire, whether it's a conflict, a feeling of love (kilig), or the heat of the sun.
usage_notes: Can be used for both positive (intensify love) and negative (intensify conflict) situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagdaragdag ng sili ay lalong **magpapatindi** sa anghang ng ulam.","translation":"Adding chili will further **intensify** the spiciness of the dish."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **patindihin** ang sitwasyon sa pamamagitan ng pagsisinungaling.","translation":"Don't **worsen** the situation by lying."}]

translation: unharmed; untouched; minding one's own business
meaning_filipino: Hindi ginagalaw, hindi sinasaktan, o hindi pinakikialaman; nasa payapang kalagayan.
etymology: From `di-` (not) + `naaano` (being done something to). The root 'ano' (what) is used very flexibly here.
original_explanation: The state of being when you're just minding your own business. 'Nananahimik ako dito, di-naaano, tapos bigla mo akong uutusan?' It's the ultimate 'leave me alone' status. It means you were perfectly fine and undisturbed before someone or something came along to mess things up.
usage_notes: Very common in colloquial speech. It carries a sense of being in a peaceful, neutral state before an interruption.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pusa ay natutulog lang at **di-naaano** nang bigla itong gulatin ng aso.","translation":"The cat was just sleeping and **unharmed** when the dog suddenly startled it."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo ako sinisisi? **Di-naaano** ako dito ah!","translation":"Why are you blaming me? I'm just here, **minding my own business**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng mga katangian, paniniwala, at pinagmulan na nagpapakilala at nagbubukod sa isang tao o grupo mula sa iba.
etymology: From `pag-` (nominalizer) + `kaka-` (means/instrument) + `kilala` (to know someone) + `-an` (nominalizing suffix). Literally, 'the means by which one is known'.
original_explanation: This is your "Sino ka ba?" answer. It's your national ID, your passport, your SSS number, but also so much more. It's your being a Filipino, a gamer, a Swiftie, a BPO agent, a "tita" of Manila. It's your unique barcode in the supermarket of life. Your `pagkakakilanlan` is what makes you, you.
usage_notes: A fundamental concept in social studies, psychology, and personal reflection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalagang malaman mo ang iyong sariling **pagkakakilanlan**.","translation":"It is important to know your own **identity**."},{"sentence":"Ang wika ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng ating **pagkakakilanlan** bilang mga Pilipino.","translation":"Language is an important part of our **identity** as Filipinos."}]

translation: to alight, to perch, to land on
meaning_filipino: Ang paglapag o pagbaba sa isang lugar, partikular na tumutukoy sa mga ibon, insekto, o sasakyang panghimpapawid. Maaari ring gamitin sa metaporikal na paraan para sa damdamin o sakit.
original_explanation: This is the graceful landing of something light. A butterfly on a flower? 'Dumapo'. A bird on a wire? 'Dumapo'. When you're tired and you finally see a vacant seat on the MRT, you 'dumapo' on it like you've found an oasis. It can also be used for feelings, like 'sana'y swerte ang dumapo sa akin' (I hope luck lands on me).
usage_notes: While literally for birds/insects, it's commonly used metaphorically for feelings, illnesses, or luck descending upon a person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang magandang paruparo ang **dumapo** sa kanyang daliri.","translation":"A beautiful butterfly **alighted** on her finger."},{"sentence":"Biglang **dumapo** sa kanya ang isang matinding kalungkutan.","translation":"A deep sadness suddenly **landed upon** him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o pangkat ng mga tao na pinili upang magbigay ng hatol o puntos sa isang paligsahan, kumpetisyon, o sa isang kaso sa korte.
original_explanation: Sila yung may power na sabihing "You are the weakest link, goodbye!" sa mga contestants ng singing contest. Sila rin ang dahilan kung bakit kinakabahan ang lahat from "Tawag ng Tanghalan" to Miss Universe. The ultimate "we have decided" people.
usage_notes: While it can mean 'juror' or 'jury', its most common use in the Philippines is for a judge in a competition (like a singing contest, beauty pageant, etc.).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang mga **hurado** sa patimpalak sa pag-awit.","translation":"The **judges** in the singing contest are strict."},{"sentence":"Sino-sino ba ang mga **hurado** para sa Miss Universe ngayong taon?","translation":"Who are the **judges** for Miss Universe this year?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paunang salita, kilos, o bahagi ng musika na nagsisilbing panimula sa isang mas malaking akda o kaganapan.
original_explanation: Ito yung intro ng kanta bago kumanta si Regine Velasquez. Sa usapan, ito yung "Uhm, friend, 'wag ka sana magagalit..." bago ka mangutang. Ito yung mga paligoy-ligoy at pampalubag-loob bago mo ibagsak ang aaminin mo. A pasakalye is the warm-up before the main event.
usage_notes: Often used figuratively to mean a preamble or preliminary statement before getting to the main point.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **pasakalye** ng kantang iyon; nakaka-excite pakinggan ang kabuuan.","translation":"The **introduction** of that song is beautiful; it makes you excited to hear the whole thing."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang mag-**pasakalye** pa, sabihin mo na ang gusto mong sabihin.","translation":"Stop with the **preamble**, just say what you want to say."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay o pagkakalat ng isang bagay na pinulbos o maliliit na piraso sa ibabaw ng iba.
etymology: From the root word 'budbod' meaning 'to sprinkle'.
original_explanation: How you add cheese to spaghetti, Milo to your ice cream, or chismis to a conversation. It's that final, glorious dusting of something extra. The command form is 'Budburan mo!' (Sprinkle it!).
usage_notes: The verb form is 'magbudbod'. 'Budburan' is the imperative form or used to indicate the object on which something is sprinkled.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **budburan** mo ng asukal ang kape ko.","translation":"Please, **sprinkle** sugar on my coffee."},{"sentence":"Ang cake ay dapat **budburan** ng chocolate shavings.","translation":"The cake should be **sprinkled** with chocolate shavings."}]

translation: to jerk; to snap; to flick
meaning_filipino: Biglaang haltakin o pitikin ang isang bagay gamit ang daliri.
original_explanation: It's that quick, sudden flicking motion. Like when you 'saltikin' a rubber band at your classmate, or 'saltikin' an ant off your table. It’s the Tagalog version of a 'yeet', but for small things and with your fingers.
usage_notes: Refers to a specific, sharp, and quick motion, usually done with the thumb and another finger. The root 'saltik' can also mean 'mentally unhinged' or 'crazy', as in 'May saltik sa ulo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **saltikin** ang tainga ng kapatid mo, masasaktan siya.","translation":"Don't **flick** your brother's ear, he'll get hurt."},{"sentence":"**Saltikin** mo nga ang gagambang iyan palayo.","translation":"**Flick** that spider away."}]

translation: sugar miller; one who deals in sugar
meaning_filipino: Isang taong nagtatrabaho sa paggawa o pagbebenta ng asukal; may-ari ng gilingan ng tubo.
original_explanation: The OG sugar daddy. Not the kind you find on dating apps, but the hacendero who owns vast sugarcane plantations. They're the big bosses of the sugar industry, the ones who make the sweet stuff happen on a massive scale.
usage_notes: Often associated with large landowners (hacienderos) in provinces like Negros Occidental.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang kanilang pamilya bilang mga mayamang **asukarero** sa Visayas.","translation":"Their family is known as wealthy **sugar millers** in the Visayas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panapal na medikal na idinidikit sa balat upang maibsan ang sakit o pamamaga, karaniwang naglalaman ng mga halamang-gamot o kemikal.
original_explanation: This is your lola's go-to solution for everything from a simple backache to 'pasma.' It’s that minty, sometimes spicy, patch that makes you smell like a walking pharmacy. Think Salonpas or a DIY version made of crushed ginger and leaves. It's the OG pain reliever before we all got addicted to pills.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay si Lola ng **emplasto** sa likod niya dahil sa pananakit.","translation":"Grandma put a **medicinal plaster** on her back because of the pain."},{"sentence":"Mabisa ang **emplasto** na gawa sa dahon ng sambong.","translation":"The **poultice** made from sambong leaves is effective."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panday na partikular na gumagawa at humuhubog ng mga kagamitang yari sa bakal.
original_explanation: This is the specialist version of 'panday'. If 'panday' is a 'doctor,' 'panday-bakal' is a 'surgeon.' This person specifically works with iron and steel, making everything from farming tools to weapons. They're the ones you go to when you need a custom-made 'gulok' for your backyard jungle or iron grilles for your windows to keep the 'chismosa' neighbors out.
usage_notes: More specific than the general term 'panday'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ama ni Jose ay isang **panday-bakal** na gumagawa ng mga araro.","translation":"Jose's father is a **blacksmith** who makes plows."},{"sentence":"Bihira na lang makahanap ng tunay na **panday-bakal** sa panahon ngayon.","translation":"It's rare to find a true **blacksmith** these days."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging pinipigilan, ginigipit, o inaapi; ang akto ng pagdiin sa leeg upang hindi makahinga.
original_explanation: That feeling when you have three deadlines, your boss is messaging you at 10 PM, and your internet is lagging. You feel 'sikil'. It's being choked, literally or figuratively, by pressure, a person, or a system. It's the ultimate "I can't breathe" moment, whether it's from stress or a real headlock.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'sikilin' (to oppress/choke). It has a strong, often violent connotation, both physically and metaphorically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nararamdaman nilang **sikil** ang kanilang karapatan sa pagpapahayag.","translation":"They feel that their right to expression is **oppressed**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sikilin** ang pangarap ng iyong anak.","translation":"Do not **suppress** your child's dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa "right now" o sa mismong sandaling ito; ngayon din.
etymology: Acronym for the English phrase 'right now'.
original_explanation: The official adverb of the 'ASAP' culture. Your boss messages you, "Need the report **rn**." Your friend texts, "San ka na? Dito na me **rn**." It's the short, slightly urgent way of saying 'ngayon na!'.
usage_notes: Primarily used in text messages and online chats.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sorry, 'di ako pwede **rn**, may ginagawa ako.","translation":"Sorry, I can't **right now**, I'm doing something."},{"sentence":"Ano'ng ulam n'yo **rn**? Papakita ko lang sa pusa ko kung ano'ng 'di niya kinakain.","translation":"What's your food **right now**? I'm just going to show my cat what it's not eating."}]

translation: to smirk at, to grin at
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isang ngisi sa isang tao o bagay, kadalasan bilang tanda ng panunuya o lihim na katuwaan.
original_explanation: When you see your friend trip but you can't laugh out loud, so you just give them *that* look. It's the verb form of that kontrabida smile. You're actively directing that mischievous grin at someone.
usage_notes: Object-focused verb. 'Ngisihan mo siya' means 'Smirk at him/her.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nginisihan** lang ako ng kapatid ko nang mahuli ko siyang kumukuha ng pagkain sa ref.","translation":"My sibling just **grinned at** me when I caught them getting food from the fridge."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang set ng mga strap at kabit na isinusuot sa tao o hayop upang ikabit sa isang bagay para sa kaligtasan, suporta, o kontrol.
original_explanation: 'Yung sinusuot mo 'pag mag-zipline ka para 'di ka mahulog sa ere. O 'yung parang "damit" ng aso mo na kinakabitan ng tali para ipasyal. Basically, 'yung seatbelt ng katawan mo for extreme activities or for your furbaby.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa kaligtasan sa mga gawain tulad ng rock climbing, pagtatrabaho sa matataas na lugar, o bilang gamit para sa mga alagang hayop.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhing mahigpit ang iyong **arnes** bago ka umakyat sa pader.","translation":"Make sure your **harness** is tight before you climb the wall."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng bagong **arnes** para sa alaga kong aso dahil mas komportable ito kaysa kwelyo.","translation":"I bought a new **harness** for my pet dog because it's more comfortable than a collar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kapangyarihan o karapatang magbigay ng utos, gumawa ng desisyon, at ipatupad ang pagsunod.
original_explanation: Ito yung power na meron ang nanay mo para utusan kang bumili ng suka kahit nanonood ka ng Netflix. O yung guard sa mall na nagsasabing "Sir/Ma'am, pacheck po ng bag." Sila yung may say, at for that moment, you just have to follow. Sa office, ito yung boss mo. Sa kalsada, yung pulis. Sa puso mo... well, baka 'yung crush mo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga pulis ay may **awtoridad** na manghuli ng mga lumalabag sa batas.","translation":"The police have the **authority** to arrest lawbreakers."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa bagay, tao, o pangyayari na nauuna sa pagkakasunod-sunod, ranggo, o kahalagahan.
original_explanation: The ultimate "dibs". "Ako una!" (I'm first!) in line for food. The una in "sana all" is the person who got the blessing first. It's the start of everything, the numero uno, the OG. It can also mean 'before' as in "Una sa lahat, maghugas ka ng kamay." (Before anything else, wash your hands.)
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective (unang araw - first day) or an adverb (una siyang dumating - he arrived first).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **una** sa pila.","translation":"She is the **first** in line."},{"sentence":"**Una**, kailangan mong mag-aral mabuti bago ka maglaro.","translation":"**First**, you need to study well before you play."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakabatay o nakadepende sa isa o higit pang kondisyon o sitwasyon; may pasubali.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'Oo, pero...' ng buhay mo. Papayagan kang lumabas, *pero* dapat kasama si bunso. May bonus ka, *pero* dapat ma-hit ang target. Parang pag-ibig na may terms and conditions. Your freedom is kondisyonal.
usage_notes: Frequently used in legal, business, and grammatical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang paglaya ay **kondisyonal** at kailangan niyang mag-report sa pulisya linggu-linggo.","translation":"His release is **conditional** and he needs to report to the police weekly."},{"sentence":"Binigyan siya ng **kondisyonal** na pag-apruba para sa kanyang loan.","translation":"She was given **conditional** approval for her loan."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng deposito o paunang bayad ang isang bagay o serbisyo; maglagak ng pera sa isang akawnt.
original_explanation: This is what you do at the bank para may pang-'travel goals' ka, or what you tell the cashier at the palengke, 'Deposituhan ko lang po muna itong bayong, babalikan ko.' It's the act of leaving something of value (usually money) somewhere.
usage_notes: Often used in financial contexts (banks, payments) or in a more literal sense of placing something in a specific location for safekeeping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **deposituhan** ang iyong bank account buwan-buwan para lumago ang ipon mo.","translation":"You need to **deposit into** your bank account monthly for your savings to grow."},{"sentence":"Sino ang magde-**deposituhan** ng bayad para sa ating outing?","translation":"Who will **deposit** the payment for our outing?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang silid o lugar kung saan gumagawa ang isang pintor, litratista, o iba pang alagad ng sining; isang lugar kung saan ginagawa ang mga palabas sa radyo o telebisyon, o nirerekord ang musika.
original_explanation: 'Yung lugar kung saan nagaganap ang magic! Pwedeng photo estudyo para sa pang-profile pic na photo shoot, recording estudyo para sa future hit song mo, o 'yung estudyo-type condo unit na kasya lang ang kama mo at ang mga pangarap mo.
usage_notes: Can refer to an artist's workspace, a broadcast studio, or a studio-type apartment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-record sila ng bagong album sa isang sikat na **estudyo** sa Quezon City.","translation":"They recorded a new album in a famous **studio** in Quezon City."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing bahagi ng isang grupo, gawain, o usapan; ipasok o idagdag.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'OP' (out of place). This is what you secretly wish your crush would say to their friends: 'Uy, isali natin siya sa group chat.' Also the battle cry during group projects: 'Isali niyo na lang pangalan ko, ako na bahala sa food.'
usage_notes: A very common verb used in social contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **isali** si Ana sa listahan.","translation":"Don't forget **to include** Ana on the list."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **isali** ang sarili ko sa usapan pero nahihiya ako.","translation":"I want **to include** myself in the conversation but I'm shy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isang parte o kabuuan ng isang bagay sa iba; ang paghati-hati ng isang bagay upang maipamahagi.
original_explanation: The ultimate group project or potluck verb. It's what your mom tells you to do with your chichirya with your siblings. In the online world, it's hitting that 'Share' button on a meme or a 'Marites' post. To 'magbahagi' is to not be 'madamot' (selfish).
usage_notes: Can refer to sharing physical things, information, or feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **magbahagi** ng iyong kaalaman sa mga kasamahan mo.","translation":"It's important to **share** your knowledge with your colleagues."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magbahagi** ng kanyang pagkain sa pulubi.","translation":"He decided to **share** his food with the beggar."}]

translation: to get stuck in mud; to be bogged down
meaning_filipino: Mailubog o maipit sa putikan, kumunoy, o isang mahirap na kalagayan kung saan hindi makakilos o makausad.
original_explanation: Ever been in a jeepney that gets stuck in mud during a typhoon? That's 'mabalaho'. It's also a perfect metaphor for getting stuck in a dead-end job, a toxic situationship, or level 247 of Candy Crush. You're bogged down and can't move forward.
usage_notes: Often used literally for vehicles stuck in mud, but also figuratively for being stuck in a predicament.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung dadaan ka sa bukid, baka **mabalaho** ang iyong sasakyan.","translation":"If you pass through the field, your vehicle might **get stuck in the mud**."},{"sentence":"**Nabalaho** siya sa utang kaya hindi na alam ang gagawin.","translation":"He **got bogged down** in debt so he doesn't know what to do anymore."}]

translation: to fetch water with a pail
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsalok o pagkuha ng tubig mula sa isang balon, poso, o ilog gamit ang timba.
original_explanation: Before faucets were a thing everywhere, this was the daily workout. 'Timbain' is the verb for fetching water, usually from a well ('balon') or a communal pump ('poso'). It’s the act of lowering the 'timba' and hauling it back up. In modern terms, it's what you do when the water company announces a service interruption and you need to fill up every container you own.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the action of using a 'timba' to get water, often from a deep source.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **timbain** ang tubig mula sa balon dahil walang kuryente.","translation":"We need to **fetch water from** the well with a **bucket** because there's no electricity."},{"sentence":"**Timbain** mo na ang tubig habang malakas pa ang tulo sa gripo.","translation":"**Fetch** the water **with a pail** now while the flow from the faucet is still strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na madaling tumawa, malimit na masaya, o may magaan na disposisyon.
etymology: From the affix 'pala-' (indicating fondness or habit) + 'tawa' (laugh).
original_explanation: The friend in your group who laughs at everything, even your corniest jokes. They're the human equivalent of the '😂' emoji. Their laughter is the official background music of your barkada.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong problema, nananatiling **palatawa** si Anna.","translation":"Whatever the problem, Anna remains **fond of laughing**."},{"sentence":"Masarap kasama ang mga taong **palatawa** dahil nakakahawa ang kanilang saya.","translation":"It's nice to be with people who are **fond of laughing** because their joy is contagious."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga balitang kumakalat na hindi tiyak ang katotohanan at karaniwang nagmumula sa usap-usapan ng mga tao.
original_explanation: The official currency of every Marites and Mosang in the neighborhood. It's the 'tea' that gets spilled, the 'chika' that gets passed around, the 'according to my source' that has no actual source. Sabi-sabi is the reason your tita thinks you're getting married just because you posted a picture with a friend.
usage_notes: Almost always carries a negative or unreliable connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniniwala sa mga **sabi-sabi**, alamin mo muna ang totoo.","translation":"Don't believe in **rumors**, find out the truth first."},{"sentence":"**Sabi-sabi** lang daw na magkakaroon ng bonus.","translation":"They say it's just **hearsay** that there will be a bonus."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng isang bagay, karaniwang matulis o ang daliri, upang bahagyang itulak o tusukin ang isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the action of poking someone or something. Think of that annoying friend who keeps poking you on Facebook messenger, or when you use a barbecue stick to get the last piece of isaw. It’s a light, sometimes playful, sometimes irritating, push or prick. It's less intense than 'tumusok' (to pierce).
usage_notes: Can be done with a finger or an object. Often implies a quick, light action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumundot** siya sa tagiliran ko para makuha ang atensyon ko.","translation":"He **poked** me in my side to get my attention."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **sinundot** ang pagkain sa kawali para malaman kung luto na.","translation":"He carefully **nudged** the food in the pan to see if it was cooked."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na napakalaki, malakas, o may monumental na sukat, katulad ng mga Titan sa mitolohiyang Griyego.
original_explanation: Basically means 'sobrang laki'. You can describe a 'titanikong traffic' in EDSA or a 'titanikong effort' to pass your final exams. Of course, everyone's first thought will be Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet. 'My Heart Will Go On' is the unofficial anthem for anything **titaniko**.
usage_notes: While it can be used, 'napakalaki' or 'higante' are more common in everyday speech. Its use often carries a sense of drama or literary flair.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **titaniko**ng pagsisikap ang kinailangan upang maitayo ang dambuhalang gusali.","translation":"A **titanic** effort was needed to construct the giant building."}]

translation: to expose; to reveal; to come out
meaning_filipino: Ilabas sa publiko o ipakita ang isang bagay na dating nakatago o lihim; ibunyag ang tunay na pagkatao o katotohanan.
original_explanation: When the chismosa finally drops the receipts. It's the grand reveal, the 'sabi ko na nga ba!' moment. It can also be a powerful act of self-revelation, like coming out or finally admitting you're the one who finished the last piece of leche flan. It's bringing something from the shadows into the light.
usage_notes: Has a strong connotation of revealing something previously hidden, which can be a secret, a crime, or one's identity. The object-focus form 'ilantad' is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **maglantad** tungkol sa katiwalian sa kanilang kumpanya.","translation":"He decided **to expose** the corruption in their company."},{"sentence":"Panahon na para **maglantad** ka ng iyong tunay na nararamdaman.","translation":"It's time for you **to reveal** your true feelings."}]

translation: a cry or shout (to drive away animals)
meaning_filipino: Isang malakas na sigaw o hiyaw, karaniwan upang itaboy ang mga hayop (tulad ng ibon sa bukirin) o bilang pampasigla.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'shoo shoo!' sound effect. Before there were scarecrows, there was the farmer's **pasaw**. It's the loud, booming shout you do to scare away the neighbor's chickens from your freshly washed laundry. The vocal equivalent of waving your arms frantically.
usage_notes: A very specific and uncommon word, mostly related to agricultural or rural contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **pasaw** ang pinakawalan ng magsasaka para itaboy ang mga maya.","translation":"The farmer let out a loud **shout** to drive away the sparrows."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **pasaw** ng mga mangingisda habang hinihila nila ang lambat.","translation":"I heard the **encouraging cry** of the fishermen as they pulled the net."}]

translation: to be the source of one's livelihood
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi o paraan ng pagpapatuloy ng buhay, karaniwan sa aspetong pangkabuhayan o pinagkukunan ng kita.
original_explanation: This is your 'why' for waking up at 5 AM for your BPO shift or setting up your online shop. It's what you do to pay the bills, buy milk tea, and fund your K-drama subscriptions. Your 'raket' is your 'pinagkakakitaan' which is your 'ikabubuhay'.
usage_notes: Often used in its future tense form 'ikabubuhay' or past tense 'ikinabuhay' to refer to a means of living.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtitinda ng isda ang **ikinabuhay** ng kanilang pamilya sa loob ng maraming taon.","translation":"Selling fish was what their family **used as a livelihood** for many years."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong maghanap ng trabahong **ikabubuhay** ko.","translation":"I need to find a job that will **be my source of livelihood**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may ugaling isapubliko o ibunyag ang mga lihim, kamalian, o anumang impormasyon na dapat sana ay itinatago.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (na nagsasaad ng tendensiya o hilig) at `buko` (ibunyag, isawalat).
original_explanation: Eto yung tropa mong walking Marites. Hindi mo pa tapos ang kwento, alam na ng buong barangay. Sila yung tipo na sasabihan mo ng, "Huy, secret lang natin 'to ha," tapos maya-maya, trending ka na sa group chat. The ultimate whistleblower, whether for justice or for the chismis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat ka sa kanya, **mapagbuko** 'yan ng sikreto.","translation":"Be careful with them, they're **prone to exposing** secrets."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa isang **mapagbuko** na empleyado, nalaman ang katiwalian sa kumpanya.","translation":"Because of a **whistleblowing** employee, the corruption in the company was discovered."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng tulong o suporta, lalo na sa panahon ng pangangailangan o kalamidad.
original_explanation: Pag may bagyo o pandemic, dito mo makikita ang bayanihan spirit. Yung LGU mo umayuda sa inyo ng de lata at bigas. Parang 'sana all' moment pero para sa basic needs.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of government or NGO assistance during calamities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umayuda** ang mga kapitbahay sa nasunugang pamilya.","translation":"The neighbors **helped** the family whose house burned down."},{"sentence":"Mabilis na **umayuda** ang pamahalaan sa mga biktima ng lindol.","translation":"The government quickly **provided aid** to the earthquake victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bulalas na nagpapahayag ng matinding damdamin tulad ng galit, pagkadismaya, o pagkagulat. Ito ay bulgar na salita na hango sa salitang Espanyol na "puta".
etymology: Mula sa korapsyon ng salitang Espanyol na "puta" (prostituta), na ginagamit bilang isang mura o bulalas.
original_explanation: The PG-13 version of its more hardcore mom, "puta." It's the "fudge" to "f*ck." You shout this when you stub your toe, when your internet dies mid-Zoom call, or when you realize you left your wallet at home. It's a curse word trying to be polite, but failing... hilariously.
usage_notes: Itinuturing na bulgar at bastos, bagaman bahagyang mas magaan kaysa sa pinagmulang salita nito. Madalas gamitin bilang ekspresyon ng pagkadismaya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pota**, ang sakit ng pagkakabagsak ko!","translation":"**Damn**, my fall really hurt!"},{"sentence":"Naiwan ko ang payong ko, **pota** umulan pa!","translation":"I left my umbrella, **crap** it's raining!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtutuos, pagbibilang, o pag-alam sa halaga o kabuuan ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay may kinalaman sa numero o pera.
original_explanation: This is you trying to figure out if your 'sahod' can survive the next 15 days after paying bills, buying groceries, and treating yourself to milk tea. It's the math you do in your head at the 'palengke' to see if your budget is still intact. Also known as 'adulting'.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of finances, but can apply to any form of calculation or tallying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling siya sa **pagkukuwenta** ng mga gastusin para sa kanilang negosyo.","translation":"She is good at the **computation** of expenses for their business."}]

translation: to investigate; to examine; to scrutinize
meaning_filipino: Suriin nang masinsinan at maingat; magsagawa ng imbestigasyon upang matuklasan ang katotohanan.
etymology: From Malay 'siasat' (investigate, inquire), which is from Arabic 'سِيَاسَة' (siyāsa), meaning 'policy' or 'governance'.
original_explanation: What your girlfriend does to your phone when you're in the shower. It's a deep dive, a full-blown investigation. On a serious note, it's what detectives do, what auditors do to your company's 'creative' expenses, and what you do to the online menu for 20 minutes to find the most 'sulit' meal. 'Kailangan nating **siyasatin** kung saan napunta ang budget.'
usage_notes: Implies a thorough and careful examination, more formal than just 'tingnan' (to look). It suggests an official or serious inquiry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga pulis ay naroon upang **siyasatin** ang pinangyarihan ng krimen.","translation":"The police are there to **investigate** the crime scene."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **siyasatin** ang bawat detalye ng kontrata bago pumirma.","translation":"We must **scrutinize** every detail of the contract before signing."}]

translation: in a sitting manner, while seated
meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng paggawa ng isang bagay na isinasagawa habang nakaupo.
original_explanation: This is the default mode for most office workers. "Trabaho ko? Paupo lang maghapon." It describes any activity you do while your butt is glued to a chair—eating, working, watching K-dramas. The opposite of "lakad-lakad".
usage_notes: Describes the manner in which an action is performed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinamayan niya ang lahat ng bisita nang **paupo** dahil masama ang pakiramdam niya.","translation":"He shook the hands of all the guests **while seated** because he wasn't feeling well."},{"sentence":"Nakakapagod din pala ang trabahong **paupo** buong araw.","translation":"Work done **in a sitting manner** all day can also be tiring."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nangangahulugang lubos na kawalan o walang natira kahit isa man lamang mula sa isang grupo o kabuuan.
etymology: Combination of 'isa' (one), 'man' (even), 'ay' (is), and 'wala' (none). 'Ma'y' is a contraction of 'man ay'.
original_explanation: The dramatic way of saying 'zero,' 'none,' or 'ubos na.' It's what your mom says when she asks who ate the cookies and you look at the empty jar. 'Nag-iwan ba kayo para sa akin?' '**Isa ma'y wala**!' It has more emotional impact than just saying 'wala.'
usage_notes: A common idiomatic expression. Emphasizes complete absence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa dami ng aplikante, **isa ma'y wala** siyang napili.","translation":"Out of all the applicants, he chose **not even one**."},{"sentence":"Nang buksan ko ang wallet ko, **isa ma'y wala** na akong nakitang pera.","translation":"When I opened my wallet, I saw there was **not even one** bill left."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pahayag o patotoo, lalo na ang ibinibigay sa ilalim ng panunumpa sa isang korte ng batas, o isang pahayag ng paniniwala sa relihiyon.
original_explanation: This is the official 'resibo'. It's the story you tell under oath, the 'tea' you spill in court. It can also be the emotional speech at a prayer meeting about how you passed your board exams. It's your personal truth, delivered for everyone to hear.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa parehong legal at relihiyosong konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **testimonyo** ay naging susi sa paglutas ng kaso.","translation":"His **testimony** was key to solving the case."},{"sentence":"Nagbahagi siya ng kanyang **testimonyo** ng pananampalataya sa harap ng kongregasyon.","translation":"She shared her **testimony** of faith in front of the congregation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panahon ng pagdiriwang ng Pasko, na sa Pilipinas ay karaniwang nagsisimula sa buwan ng Setyembre at nagtatapos sa Enero.
etymology: From `Ka-` + `Pasko` + `-han`. `Pasko` is from Spanish 'Pascua' (Easter, but used for Christmas in the Philippines).
original_explanation: In the Philippines, this isn't just a day, it's a four-month marathon. The moment Jose Mari Chan's voice hits the mall speakers in September, 'Kapaskuhan' has officially begun. It's the season of bibingka, simbang gabi, traffic, 13th-month pay, and endless family reunions where your titas ask 'Kailan ka ikakasal?'.
usage_notes: Always capitalized. Refers to the entire Christmas period, not just December 25th.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ramdam na ramdam na ang diwa ng **Kapaskuhan** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The spirit of the **Christmas season** can really be felt in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Isang maligayang **Kapaskuhan** sa inyong lahat!","translation":"A merry **Christmas season** to you all!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pag-alis o pagbawas ng bahagi ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay buhok, sa pamamagitan ng paggupit.
original_explanation: The action you do *to* someone. 'Magkano magpa-gupit sa salon niyo?' It can also mean to cut a piece *from* something, like a coupon from a newspaper. 'Gupitan mo nga ng coupon yung dyaryo.'
usage_notes: A location/beneficiary-focus verb. You 'gupitan' *someone* of their hair, or you 'gupitan' a newspaper *of* a coupon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang nag-**gupit** sa iyo? Ang ganda ng buhok mo!","translation":"Who **cut your hair**? Your hair looks great!"},{"sentence":"**Gupitan** mo ako ng bangs, please.","translation":"Please **cut** my bangs for me."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng aruga, proteksyon, at pagmamalasakit sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
etymology: Root word 'kalinga' means care or protection. Also a province and an indigenous group in the Cordilleras.
original_explanation: This is the next-level pag-aalaga. It's not just feeding someone; it's making sure they're warm, safe, and emotionally okay. It's the OFW parent's motivation, the nurse's gentle touch, the lola's constant 'Kumain ka na ba?' It’s that deep, nurturing care that feels like a warm hug for the soul.
usage_notes: A deep and tender word, often implying protection and nurturing. More profound than 'pag-aalaga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkalinga** ng isang ina ay walang kapantay.","translation":"A mother's **care** is unparalleled."},{"sentence":"Nagpakita siya ng **pagkalinga** sa mga hayop na naligaw.","translation":"He showed **care** for the stray animals."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang pag-ngiwi o pag-iba ng anyo ng mukha dahil sa sakit, pait, o pagkadismaya.
etymology: From `ma-` (involuntary action prefix) + `pa-` (causative prefix) + `ngiwi` (grimace, twisted smile).
original_explanation: 'Yung reaction mo pag nakakita ka ng sobrang cringey na post, o 'pag natikman mo 'yung kape na walang asukal. It's that involuntary "yuck face" you make. The physical manifestation of "awkward" or "ouch".
usage_notes: An involuntary action verb, often a reaction to something unpleasant. Common forms are `napangiwi` (past) and `mapapangiwi` (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **napangiwi** sa pait ng gamot na kanyang ininom.","translation":"He **winced** at the bitterness of the medicine he drank."},{"sentence":"Tiyak na **mapapangiwi** ka sa sobrang asim ng mangga.","translation":"You will surely **grimace** from the extreme sourness of the mango."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan o sangkap na ginagamit upang pag-isahin o pagsamahin ang dalawa o higit pang bagay.
original_explanation: This is your weapon of choice for making juice, coffee, or even cement. It can be a simple spoon (sandok), a whisk, or that giant mixer truck causing traffic. It's the tool that brings different things together, like you and your crush sa team-building... sana all.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang kasangkapan (hal. kutsara, batedor) o sa isang sangkap (hal. harina bilang pampalapot).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang sandok na ginagamit kong **panghalo** sa sopas.","translation":"The ladle I use as a **mixer** for the soup is missing."},{"sentence":"Magdagdag ka ng arina bilang **panghalo** para lumapot ang sarsa.","translation":"Add flour as a **mixing agent** to thicken the sauce."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paghuli ng isda o iba pang hayop sa tubig gamit ang lambat.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'mang-' at ang salitang-ugat na 'lambat' (net). Nagaganap ang asimilasyon kung saan ang 'ng' ay nagiging 'n' at idinurugtong sa salitang nagsisimula sa 'l'.
original_explanation: Literally, to fish with a net. But in modern hugot culture, 'manlambat' is what you do when you're trying to catch feelings, a potential jowa, or clients. You cast a wide net (a charming smile, a witty post, a good sales pitch) and hope you catch something good, not just a 'seen-zone'.
usage_notes: This is a verb. The noun for 'a fisherman who uses a net' is 'manlalambat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Araw-araw siyang nagpupunta sa dagat para **manlambat**.","translation":"He goes to the sea every day **to catch fish with a net**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **manlambat** ng maraming isda para sa pista.","translation":"We need **to catch** a lot of fish **with a net** for the festival."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking baboy na hindi pa kinakapon at may kakayahang magparami.
original_explanation: The alpha male of the pigpen. He's the reason why there are so many cute little piglets running around. In the human world, it's a less-than-flattering term for a guy who's a bit too aggressive in his 'pursuits'.
usage_notes: The meat from a 'barakong baboy' is said to have a stronger, more gamey smell and taste ('anggo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang amoy ng kulungan ng **barakong baboy**.","translation":"The pen of the **boar** has a strong smell."}]

translation: to pull towards oneself, to rake in
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghila o paghakot ng isang bagay papalapit sa sarili, karaniwang gamit ang kamay o isang kasangkapan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "akin 'to!" move. 'Yung ginagawa ng mananalo sa tong-its, kumabig ng taya. Or 'yung corrupt na politiko, kumabig ng kaban ng bayan. Pwede ring sa buffet, kumabig ka ng lahat ng tempura bago maubusan.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for raking things or metaphorically for amassing wealth or power, sometimes with a negative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumabig** siya ng malaking halaga ng pera sa casino.","translation":"He **raked in** a large amount of money at the casino."},{"sentence":"Gamit ang kalaykay, **kumabig** siya ng mga tuyong dahon.","translation":"Using a rake, he **pulled** the dry leaves **towards himself**."}]

translation: to sneak out; to bring out secretly
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha o paglalabas ng isang bagay mula sa isang lugar sa paraang tago, maingat, at hindi napapansin ng iba.
original_explanation: This is the move you pull when you're "borrowing" your sister's clothes without asking. Or when you're trying to get a midnight snack from the ref without waking up your parents. It's the art of the 'diskarte' ninja move. In the corporate world, this is called 'leaking' a document.
usage_notes: A phrasal verb combining 'ilabas' (to bring out) and 'palihim' (secretly). Emphasizes the clandestine nature of the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ilabas nang palihim** ang mga pagkain mula sa party.","translation":"He tried to **sneak out** the food from the party."},{"sentence":"Bago ang opisyal na anunsyo, may nag-**labas nang palihim** ng mga detalye ng proyekto.","translation":"Before the official announcement, someone **secretly brought out** (leaked) the project details."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang video o larawan na nilikha at in-edit ng isang tagahanga, na karaniwang nagtatampok sa kanilang idolo at gumagamit ng mga clip, musika, at special effects upang maipakita ang kanilang paghanga.
etymology: Direktang hiram mula sa Ingles na "fan edit."
original_explanation: Ito yung mga astig na video sa TikTok o Twitter na gawa ng fans. Yung mga slow-mo, may sad music, o minsan thrist trap na compilation ng mga moments ng idol mo. Sila yung content creator ng fandom na walang bayad, puro passion lang.
usage_notes: Isang mahalagang bahagi ng online fan culture, lalo na sa mga platform tulad ng TikTok, Instagram, at Twitter.
