usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umiyak ako sa ganda ng **fan edit** na napanood ko tungkol sa love team nila.","translation":"I cried because of the beautiful **fan edit** I watched about their love team."},{"sentence":"Nag-request siya ng **fan edit** ng kanyang bias na may kasamang kanta ng Ben&Ben.","translation":"She requested a **fan edit** of her bias featuring a Ben&Ben song."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang sustansya, tulad ng langis o grasa, na ipinapahid sa mga bahagi ng makina upang mabawasan ang pagkiskisan at mapadali ang paggalaw.
original_explanation: The official 'pampadulas' for everything in life that's experiencing too much friction. From the squeaky door of your apartment to the rusty gears of a jeepney. It's the solution for things that are stuck. Yes, *those* things, too. We're a modern dictionary.
usage_notes: A loanword. The native Tagalog equivalent is 'pampadulas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **lubrikant** para sa bisagra ng pinto.","translation":"A **lubricant** is needed for the door hinge."},{"sentence":"Bumili ng **lubrikant** si kuya para sa kadena ng kanyang motor.","translation":"My older brother bought **lubricant** for his motorcycle's chain."}]

translation: to crouch; to squat; to cower
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-upo sa mga sakong habang nakabaluktot ang mga tuhod, o ang pagyukod nang may takot o hiya.
original_explanation: This is the pose you strike when you're hiding from someone you owe money to, or when you're trying to make yourself small during a horror movie. It can also be the literal squatting position people do while waiting for a jeepney or gossiping on a street corner. It's a mix of hiding, resting, and cowering.
usage_notes: While `yumukyok` is the root, this form `magyumukyok` is less common. The more frequent form would be `yumukyok` or `nakayukyok`. The `mag-` prefix suggests initiating or doing the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang dumating ang guro, **nagyumukyok** sa takot ang batang nag-ingay.","translation":"When the teacher arrived, the noisy child **cowered** in fear."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magyumukyok** diyan, tumayo ka at harapin mo ang problema.","translation":"Don't just **crouch** there, stand up and face your problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagsusuri, pagwawasto, at pagbabago sa isang teksto, larawan, audio, o video upang mapabuti ito bago ilathala o gamitin.
original_explanation: What you do to your selfie for 30 minutes before posting it on Instagram. It's also what you wish you could do to your life choices. In the office, it's that never-ending cycle of "please edit per my comments" from your boss.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa anyong 'i-edit' o 'mag-edit' sa Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong i-**edit** ang video para sa aking vlog.","translation":"I need to **edit** the video for my vlog."},{"sentence":"Paki-**edit** naman nitong essay ko bago ko ipasa.","translation":"Please **edit** my essay before I submit it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kakayahang tularan, kopyahin, o sundan ang isang kilos, anyo, istilo, o katangian ng iba.
original_explanation: That moment when you try to follow a TikTok dance tutorial and... you just can't. 'Hindi ko `magaya` 'yung steps!' It's the struggle of trying to replicate something, from your idol's OOTD to your lola's secret adobo recipe. The opposite of 'original, 'wag nang kopyahin.'
usage_notes: Similar to 'magawa', this combines the root 'gaya' (imitate) with the ability prefix 'ma-'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong subok ko, hindi ko talaga **magaya** ang pirma niya.","translation":"No matter how hard I try, I really **can't copy** his signature."},{"sentence":"Madali lang **magaya** ang sayaw na iyon kung papanoorin mong mabuti.","translation":"That dance is easy **to be able to imitate** if you watch closely."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahiwatig ng pagbabawas, kakulangan, o mas mababang antas. Ginagamit din sa matematika para sa subtraction.
original_explanation: The opposite of "plus". Sa math, ito yung "minus" sign (-). Sa buhay, ito yung "less". Halimbawa, menos gastos this month kasi malapit na ang 13th month pay. O kaya, 'pag umorder ka ng kape, "Miss, menos sugar po." It's the battle cry of the budget-conscious and the health-conscious.
usage_notes: Very common in both mathematical and general contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sampu **menos** dalawa ay walo.","translation":"Ten **minus** two is eight."},{"sentence":"Sana **menos** traffic na bukas.","translation":"Hopefully there's **less** traffic tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga napakaliit na mikroorganismo na may iisang selula, na matatagpuan halos sa lahat ng dako. Ang ilan ay nagdudulot ng sakit habang ang iba ay kapaki-pakinabang.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Espanyol na 'bacteria', mula sa Latin.
original_explanation: The reason your mom tells you to wash your hands. **Bakterya** are those tiny invisible things that can either make you sick (E. coli!) or make you healthy (hello, Yakult!). It's the go-to villain in commercials for hand sanitizers and soaps.
usage_notes: Used in both scientific and everyday health contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maghugas ng kamay upang maiwasan ang masasamang **bakterya**.","translation":"Wash your hands to avoid bad **bacteria**."},{"sentence":"May mga **bakterya** na tumutulong sa ating panunaw.","translation":"There are **bacteria** that help our digestion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan itinatambak o itinatapon ang mga basura at iba pang mga kalat.
etymology: From `pa-` + `tambak` (pile, heap) + `-an` (locative suffix), literally "a place for piling things".
original_explanation: This is the final resting place for your empty Shopee packages, your takeout containers, and all the things you threw away. It’s the mountain of trash, the `tambakan` on a grand scale. It's also what your room looks like when your mom hasn't visited in a month. "Ano ba 'to, kwarto o patambakan?"
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a designated area for dumping waste, often on a large, municipal scale.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang amoy mula sa **patambakan** ay umaabot sa aming barangay.","translation":"The smell from the **dump site** reaches our neighborhood."},{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang nabubuhay sa pamamagitan ng pangangalakal sa **patambakan**.","translation":"Many families make a living by scavenging in the **landfill**."}]

translation: to cause to sway or wobble unstably
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng paggalaw nang hindi matatag o paroo't parito, na tila mawawalan ng balanse.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung lasing na pauwi galing inuman, try hard maglakad nang diretso pero nagpagiwang-giwang pa rin. O kaya 'yung budget mo bago dumating ang sweldo, pa-sway sway na lang, alanganin.
usage_notes: The `magpa-` prefix indicates causing or allowing something/someone to do the action of the root word. The reduplication `giwang-giwang` intensifies the swaying motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang malikot, baka **magpagiwang-giwang** ang bangka at tumaob tayo.","translation":"Don't move around so much, you might **cause the boat to sway unstably** and we might capsize."},{"sentence":"Ang malakas na hangin ay **nagpagiwang-giwang** sa mga puno ng niyog.","translation":"The strong wind **caused the coconut trees to sway unstably**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan nagtatagpo o nagkrus ang dalawa o higit pang mga kalsada o landas.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'krus' (cross) at hulaping '-an', na tumutukoy sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: That chaotic spot in the middle of EDSA where four roads meet and everyone plays a game of 'chicken.' Metaphorically, it's that 'what now?' moment in your life, like choosing between a stable job and your passion project. A literal and figurative 'sana all' may daan.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for roads or metaphorically for a point of decision.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **krusan** ng Ayala at Buendia.","translation":"Let's meet at the **intersection** of Ayala and Buendia."},{"sentence":"Nasa isang **krusan** ngayon ang kanyang karera.","translation":"His career is now at a **crossroads**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sangay ng kemistri na nakatuon sa pag-aaral ng mga prinsipyong pisikal na namamahala sa pag-uugali ng materya sa antas na molekular at atomiko.
etymology: Hango sa mga salitang Ingles na "physical" at "chemistry".
original_explanation: Ito yung subject sa college na nagtatanong kung bakit may 'spark' sa inyo, pero in a scientific way. Dito mo malalaman na hindi lang feelings ang may 'potential energy', pati mga molecules din. Basically, the science behind the 'chemistry' you feel, but with more math and less hugot.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa kontekstong pang-akademiko at siyentipiko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pisikal kemistri** ay isang mahirap ngunit mahalagang kurso para sa mga kumukuha ng BS Chemistry.","translation":"**Physical chemistry** is a difficult but important course for those taking BS Chemistry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o pook kung saan maaaring magpahinga.
original_explanation: The official name for the 'smoking area' or the office pantry where all the real talk (aka chismis) happens. Pwede ring bench sa park, waiting shed sa tapat ng school, o 'yung balikat ng kaibigan mo. Basically, any spot you can crash and burn for a few minutes is a pahingahan.
usage_notes: Can also metaphorically refer to a person one finds comfort and rest in.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gawin nating **pahingahan** ang lilim ng punong iyon.","translation":"Let's make the shade of that tree our **resting place**."},{"sentence":"Ang aming opisina ay may komportableng **pahingahan** para sa mga empleyado.","translation":"Our office has a comfortable **lounge** for the employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang propesyon ay ang pagdugtungin ang mga piraso ng metal sa pamamagitan ng proseso ng welding o paghihinang.
original_explanation: The guy in your neighborhood wearing a mask that looks like it's from a sci-fi movie, creating sparks bright enough to make you see spots for an hour. They're responsible for your rehas (window grills), gates, and the occasional tricycle sidecar repair. A true master of 'kapit-tuko' but with metal.
usage_notes: This English loanword is used far more frequently than its Tagalog counterpart, 'manghihinang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating tumawag ng **welder** para ayusin ang sirang gate.","translation":"We need to call a **welder** to fix the broken gate."}]

meaning_filipino: Matinding antas o tindi ng isang damdamin, pangyayari, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is a word for feelings that are not 'pabebe'. It's the 'gigil' level of anger, the 'sobra-sobra' level of love, or the 'walang-patawad' level of heat during a summer afternoon in Manila. It’s drama, passion, and force rolled into one poetic word. Think of the climax of a teleserye—that’s pure 'sidhi'.
usage_notes: Often used in literature and formal speech to describe powerful emotions or conditions. Can function as a noun (intensity) or an adjective (intense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ramdam ko ang **sidhi** ng kanyang galit sa paraan ng kanyang pagsasalita.","translation":"I could feel the **intensity** of his anger in the way he spoke."},{"sentence":"Sa **sidhi** ng pag-ibig niya, handa siyang gawin ang lahat.","translation":"With the **ardor** of his love, he is prepared to do everything."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tela na may malambot at makinis na ibabaw, karaniwang gawa sa seda, koton, o sintetikong hibla.
original_explanation: That super smooth, kinda shiny fabric that looks and feels expensive, even if you just got it from Divisoria. It's what your lola's couch might be made of, or that one 'pang-party' dress you own. Think of the texture of a red velvet cupcake, but for clothes.
usage_notes: Often used to describe luxurious or formal items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang suot niyang damit ay gawa sa mamahaling **belbet**.","translation":"The dress she was wearing was made of expensive **velvet**."},{"sentence":"Malambot ang pulang **belbet** na kurtina.","translation":"The red **velvet** curtain is soft."}]

translation: to perform a miracle, to happen miraculously
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa o pagganap ng isang himala; ang pagkakaroon ng isang pangyayaring hindi maipaliwanag ng agham o karaniwang karanasan.
etymology: From Spanish 'milagro' (miracle), combined with the Tagalog verb prefix 'mag-'.
original_explanation: What you're hoping your sweldo would do on the 29th of the month. It's when something impossible happens, like finding a seat on the MRT during rush hour, or your internet not lagging during an online game. "Sana magmilagro ang traffic sa EDSA."
usage_notes: Can be used both literally (in a religious context) and hyperbolically or sarcastically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tila **nagmilagro** ang panahon at biglang tumigil ang malakas na ulan.","translation":"It seems the weather **performed a miracle** and the heavy rain suddenly stopped."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magmilagro** para matapos ang lahat ng gawaing ito sa loob ng isang oras.","translation":"You need to **perform a miracle** to finish all this work in one hour."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magulang (ama o ina) ng asawa ng isang tao.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang hango sa salitang Espanyol na "bien" (mabuti), ngunit ang eksaktong pinagmulan ay hindi tiyak at naging bahagi na ng wikang Filipino sa mahabang panahon.
original_explanation: The collective term for your spouse's parents. Sila 'yung source ng "mana ka sa nanay/tatay mo" comments. Your relationship with your `biyenan` can be a sitcom, a drama, or hopefully, a heartwarming family movie.
usage_notes: Isang salitang neutral sa kasarian. Para tukuyin, sinasabi ang 'biyanang-lalaki' o 'biyanang-babae'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta kami sa bahay ng aking **biyenan** sa Linggo.","translation":"We are going to my **parent-in-law's** house on Sunday."},{"sentence":"Mahal na mahal ko ang aking mga **biyenan**.","translation":"I love my **parents-in-law** very much."}]

translation: to ask to lean on; to let oneself lean
meaning_filipino: Paghiling na sumandal o ipatong ang bigat sa isang bagay o tao para sa suporta.
original_explanation: The ultimate "pabebe" move or a sign of true exhaustion. When you're sleepy on the bus, you whisper to your friend, "**Pasandal** ha?" before your head lands on their shoulder. It's also that feeling when you're so tired from adulting, you just want to find a wall and go **pasandal** for a minute. It's a request for support, both literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: Can be a gentle request or a description of an action (adverbial).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari bang **pasandal** muna sa balikat mo? Inaantok na ako.","translation":"Can I **lean** on your shoulder for a bit? I'm getting sleepy."},{"sentence":"Umupo siya nang **pasandal** sa pader dahil sa pagod.","translation":"He sat down, **leaning** against the wall because of fatigue."}]

translation: a type of Chinese rice wine
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng alak na gawa sa bigas na orihinal na nagmula sa Tsina, na kilala rin sa pangalang Siok Hoc Tong.
etymology: Mula sa Hokkien na "siâu-heng-chiú" (紹興酒), na tumutukoy sa Shaoxing wine. Ang pangalang komersyal na "Siok Hoc Tong" ay nagpasikat sa katawagan.
original_explanation: This is the Titos' and Lolos' secret potion, often kept in a dusty bottle in the corner cabinet. It's that strong Chinese rice wine they say is "pampainit ng katawan" (to warm the body) or a cure-all for everything from colds to "pasma". Usually brought out during special occasions or when someone needs a "real drink". The smell is... memorable.
usage_notes: Ang spelling na "siyoktong" ay isang popular na pagbabaybay. Ang inumin ay kilala sa matapang nitong amoy at lasa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglabas ng isang bote ng **siyoktong** si Lolo para sa mga bisita.","translation":"Grandpa brought out a bottle of **Chinese rice wine** for the guests."},{"sentence":"May nagsasabing mabisa raw ang **siyoktong** para sa sipon.","translation":"Some say that **sioktong** is effective for colds."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sentro o pokus ng atensyon, interes, o aktibidad; ang pinakatampok na bahagi.
original_explanation: The spotlight. Ito yung lugar kung saan lahat nakatingin. Sa isang family picture, ito yung bagong baby. Sa chismisan, ito yung topic na pinag-uusapan. Kung ikaw ang nasa 'tampukan', good luck, you're the main character for today.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa tao, bagay, o paksa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong kasal ang naging **tampukan** ng kasiyahan.","translation":"The newlyweds became the **focal point** of the celebration."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalakad-lakad o pamamasyal, kadalasan para sa libangan.
etymology: From `pag-` (prefix indicating action) + `gala` (to wander, to roam).
original_explanation: This is the simpler, one-time version of 'paggagala'. If 'paggagala' is your weekend lifestyle, 'paggala' is what you do on a Tuesday afternoon when you're bored. 'Isang mabilis na paggala lang sa mall, ha?' (Just one quick stroll at the mall, okay?) It's the base action of wandering around.
usage_notes: This is the basic noun form. 'Paggagala' (with reduplication) implies a more frequent, habitual, or longer duration of the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paggala** sa parke ay nakakatulong para mabawasan ang stress.","translation":"The **act of strolling** in the park helps to reduce stress."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng trabaho, ang hilig niya ay ang **paggala** sa mga bookstore.","translation":"After work, his hobby is **wandering** around bookstores."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginagamit bilang palamuti o pampaganda sa isang lugar, kasuotan, o anumang bagay upang magdagdag ng ganda o karangyaan.
original_explanation: Your mom's collection of ceramic figurines, the parol you hang at Christmas, the tassels on a jeepney—those are all adorno. It's anything that adds a little ✨pizzazz✨ to something plain. It's the Pinoy love for "design," even if it sometimes borders on horror vacui (fear of empty spaces).
usage_notes: A general term for decorations. "Palamuti" is a more common native equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng makukulay na **adorno** ang kanilang bahay para sa Pasko.","translation":"Their house is full of colorful **ornaments** for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng iba't ibang **adorno** sa kanyang damit para sa parada.","translation":"She put various **decorations** on her dress for the parade."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang paninigas at pananakit ng kalamnan, na karaniwang tinatawag na kalambre o pulikat.
original_explanation: That feeling when your leg suddenly decides to turn into a rock at 3 AM for no reason. 'Aray, kinakalamay ako!' is the official battle cry. It's your muscle's way of saying 'I hate you' and seizing up in protest, usually after a long day of walking or a sudden weird movement.
usage_notes: A less common term for having cramps. The more common verbs are 'pulikatin' or 'kalambrihin'. The root 'kalamay' (cramp) is not to be confused with 'kalamay' (rice cake).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madalas **kalamayin** ang binti niya pagkatapos tumakbo.","translation":"His leg often **gets cramped** after running."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong mag-unat baka ka **kalamayin**.","translation":"Don't stretch too much or you might **get a cramp**."}]

translation: to give birth to, to bring forth
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagsilang o paglalabas ng sanggol mula sa sinapupunan ng ina; maaari ring tumukoy sa paglikha o paglalabas ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The most literal meaning is to give birth. It's the grand finale of a 9-month journey. But it can also be used figuratively, like giving birth to an idea, a project, or a masterpiece. Parang pagkatapos ng maraming puyat sa thesis, sa wakas, "iniluwal" mo na ang final paper mo.
usage_notes: A more formal and poetic term for "to give birth" than the common "manganak". Can also be used figuratively.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ligtas na **iniluwal** ni Maria ang isang malusog na sanggol na lalaki.","translation":"Maria safely **gave birth to** a healthy baby boy."},{"sentence":"Ang hirap at sakripisyo ng mga bayani ang **nagluwal** sa ating kalayaan.","translation":"The hardship and sacrifice of the heroes **brought forth** our freedom."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagsasama-sama ng dalawa o higit pang sangkap, bagay, o tao upang bumuo ng isang pinag-isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: Think 'halo-halo'. The name itself is the action! It's what you do with cement and water, gin and tonic, or your different groups of friends at your birthday party (and hoping they get along). It's the fusion of cultures, languages (Taglish!), and flavors that makes the Philippines so unique.
usage_notes: Can be literal (mixing ingredients) or figurative (mingling with people, mixing of ideas).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sikreto sa masarap na adobo ay nasa tamang **paghahalo** ng toyo, suka, at bawang.","translation":"The secret to delicious adobo is in the correct **mixing** of soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic."},{"sentence":"Hindi maiiwasan ang **paghahalo** ng iba't ibang kultura sa panahon ng globalisasyon.","translation":"The **blending** of different cultures is unavoidable in the age of globalization."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na idinurugtong sa isang pahayag upang ipaalam na ito ay isang biro, hindi seryoso, o isang kasinungalingan.
etymology: Origin is debated, but it's a staple of Filipino gay lingo that has become mainstream. Some theories link it to 'char' (as in burnt/fake) or the Visayan expression 'aron ingnon' (to make it seem).
original_explanation: The OG "get out of jail free" card for anything you said that was either too honest, too harsh, or a complete lie. It's the verbal equivalent of the 😉 emoji. You can confess your undying love, then immediately say "charot!" to save yourself from embarrassment.
usage_notes: Can be used to soften a harsh truth, retract a statement, or simply indicate a joke.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal kita... **charot**!","translation":"I love you... **just kidding**!"},{"sentence":"Grabe, ang taba ko na. Ay, diet na ako. **Charot**.","translation":"Wow, I'm so fat now. Oh, I'm on a diet. **Just kidding**."}]

translation: to fight for, to struggle for
meaning_filipino: Ang masigasig na pakikipaglaban o pagsisikap na makamit o mapagtagumpayan ang isang bagay na mahalaga.
etymology: From mag- (verb prefix) + baka (a fight, struggle). Note: this root 'baka' is different from 'baka' (cow) or 'baka' (maybe).
original_explanation: This isn't just a physical fight. "Magbaka" is to hustle, to grind, to fight for your dreams. It's what you do when you're reviewing for the board exams, working two jobs for your family, or trying to defend your thesis. It's the verb form of 'laban lang!'
usage_notes: Implies a noble struggle or a determined effort against odds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magbaka** para sa isang mas magandang kinabukasan.","translation":"We need to **fight for** a better future."},{"sentence":"Patuloy siyang nagbabaka upang mabigyan ng hustisya ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He continues to **struggle** to bring justice to his family."}]

translation: to be possessed (by a spirit); to merge
meaning_filipino: Ang mapasukan ng isang espiritu o masamang elemento. Sa ibang konteksto, ang pagsama o pagiging bahagi ng isang grupo o organisasyon.
original_explanation: The OG horror movie plot device. 'Pag may biglang nag-iba ng boses, lumaki ang mata, at nagsalita ng Latin, 'yan na 'yon—nasaniban! It's when a spirit or 'engkanto' decides your body is a good place to crash. In a less spooky, more corporate context, it can also mean to merge or affiliate with another company. 'Nasanib na ang Company A sa Company B.' From spooky to stocks!
usage_notes: Has two distinct meanings: supernatural possession and formal joining/merging. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi nila, madaling **masaniban** ang mga taong mahina ang loob.","translation":"They say people who are weak-willed can easily **be possessed**."},{"sentence":"Ang maliit na kumpanya ay **nasanib** sa isang malaking korporasyon.","translation":"The small company **merged** with a large corporation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakakulong na pasilyo o patyo sa loob ng isang kumbento, monasteryo, o simbahan, na nagsisilbing lugar para sa paglalakad, pagninilay, at panalangin ng mga monghe o madre.
original_explanation: Isipin mo 'yung mga lumang simbahan sa pelikula kung saan naglalakad 'yung mga madre o pari sa isang pasilyo na may garden sa gitna. 'Yun ang 'klaustro'. It's a very specific architectural feature, parang private garden walkway for religious folks to get their zen on. Very old-school, very 'The Name of the Rose.'
usage_notes: Isang napaka-espesipikong termino sa arkitektura at relihiyon. Hindi pang-araw-araw na gamit maliban kung ikaw ay arkitekto, historyador, o pari.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tahimik na naglalakad ang mga monghe sa **klaustro** ng monasteryo tuwing hapon.","translation":"The monks walk silently in the monastery's **cloister** every afternoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauugnay sa o tumutukoy sa larangan ng operasyon o siruhiya sa medisina.
original_explanation: This is the formal, almost-sounds-like-a-spell word for anything related to surgery. 'Surgical mask,' 'surgical procedure,' 'surgical precision.' You use this word when you want to sound extra smart or when you're watching a medical drama dubbed in Tagalog. 'Kailangan ng pasyente ng interbensyong kirurhika!'
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pormal at teknikal na termino. Sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap, mas madalas sabihin ang 'pang-opera' o gamitin ang salitang Ingles na 'surgical'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtanggal ng appendix ay isang pamamaraang **kirurhika**.","translation":"Removing an appendix is a **surgical** procedure."},{"sentence":"Gumamit sila ng mga instrumentong **kirurhika** sa operasyon.","translation":"They used **surgical** instruments in the operation."}]

translation: to become dented; to be crushed
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng anyo ng isang bagay dahil sa pagkakadiin, pagkakabagsak, o pagkakapukpok, na nag-iiwan ng marka o lundo.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your car door after a close encounter with a jeepney. Or your baon's lunchbox when it gets squished inside your bag. It's that sad state of being dented, crumpled, or deformed. It's the physical manifestation of "na-stress."
usage_notes: The `mag-` prefix here indicates that the subject undergoes the change, becoming dented. `Mayupi` is a more common form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pagdadala ng lata para hindi ito **magyupi**.","translation":"Be careful carrying the can so it won't **get dented**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa aksidente, **nagyupi** ang unahang bahagi ng kotse.","translation":"Because of the accident, the front part of the car **became crushed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng mga ideya o prinsipyo na naglalayong magpaliwanag ng isang bagay, na karaniwang batay sa mga pangkalahatang prinsipyo na hiwalay sa mga bagay na ipinapaliwanag.
original_explanation: In science, it's a well-tested explanation for why things happen. Sa chismis, ito yung hula-hula mo kung bakit hindi ka na ni-replyan ni crush. 'Teoriya ko, may iba na siyang ka-chat.' It's your educated guess, your hypothesis, your 'what if' scenario that you and your friends spend hours dissecting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa **teoriya** ni Darwin, ang mga species ay nagbabago sa paglipas ng panahon.","translation":"According to Darwin's **theory**, species change over time."},{"sentence":"May **teoriya** ako kung sino ang kumuha ng pagkain sa ref.","translation":"I have a **theory** about who took the food from the fridge."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng matinding takot o sindak; nakapangingilabot.
etymology: From `ka-` + reduplication of the first two syllables of `kilabot` (terror). The `ka-` prefix here denotes a quality.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when you see your phone bill after a month of non-stop data usage. Or when you realize it's Monday tomorrow and you haven't done any of your weekend chores. It's the ultimate "OMG, no!" moment. The stuff of horror movies and final exams you didn't study for.
usage_notes: Often used to describe something extremely scary, like a horror movie, a terrible accident, or a monstrous creature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kakila-kilabot** ang mga kuwentong multo na narinig namin kagabi.","translation":"The ghost stories we heard last night were **terrifying**."},{"sentence":"Isang **kakila-kilabot** na krimen ang naganap sa lumang bahay.","translation":"A **horrifying** crime took place in the old house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghahanap ng impormasyon o sagot sa pamamagitan ng isang katanungan. Ito ay ang nakaraang anyo ng pandiwang 'magtanong'.
original_explanation: That moment you slid into someone's DMs with "Sino ka po?" or when you finally got the courage to ask your crush out (and maybe got rejected). It's what you did when you couldn't find the CR in the mall and had to approach the security guard. You nagtanong because Google Maps can't find everything.
usage_notes: Ito ang perpektibong aspekto (past tense) ng pandiwang 'magtanong'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagtanong** ang bata kung nasaan ang kanyang nanay.","translation":"The child **asked** where his mother was."},{"sentence":"**Nagtanong** ako sa tindera kung magkano ang isang kilong bigas.","translation":"I **asked** the vendor how much a kilo of rice costs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng laruan na karaniwang gawa sa kahoy at may matulis na dulo, na pinaiikot sa pamamagitan ng pagpulupot at paghagis gamit ang isang tali.
original_explanation: Ito yung laruan bago pa nauso ang Mobile Legends. Yung kahoy na paikutan mo ng tali tapos ibabato mo sa lupa para umikot. Ang goal: patagalin ang ikot o tamaan at sirain ang trompo ng kalaban. The original battle royale.
usage_notes: 'Turumpo' is a more common variant. This is a traditional Filipino game.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling si Lito magpaikot ng **trompo**.","translation":"Lito is good at spinning a **top**."},{"sentence":"May gasgas na ang **trompo** ko dahil sa laban namin kahapon.","translation":"My **spinning top** has a scratch from our battle yesterday."}]

translation: will text; will send a text message
meaning_filipino: Gagamit ng cellphone upang magpadala ng mensaheng text (SMS) sa hinaharap. Ito ay ang gagawing pagpapadala ng text.
original_explanation: The national past-time of the Philippines, second only to breathing. It's what you do when you have 'chismis' to share but you're too lazy to call. 'Girl, **magtetext** ako sa'yo later, may scoop ako!'
usage_notes: Future tense of the verb 'magtext'. Extremely common in daily conversation across all demographics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtetext** na lang ako kapag malapit na ako sa bahay ninyo.","translation":"I **will just text** when I'm near your house."},{"sentence":"Sabi niya **magtetext** siya pagkatapos ng trabaho.","translation":"He said he **will text** after work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagpapatawa sa pamamagitan ng mga kilos na katawa-tawa o hangal; isang payaso.
etymology: From Spanish "lacayo" (lackey, footman), which evolved in meaning in Tagalog to refer to a jester or clown.
original_explanation: Before 'clown' became a modern insult for someone acting foolishly online, we had 'lukayo.' It's the classic court jester, the guy whose job is to be silly. Today, you might call your friend who's always making corny jokes or doing funny dances a 'lukayo.' It's less of an insult and more of a 'you're such a goofball' term.
usage_notes: Can be used affectionately or as a mild insult for someone acting foolishly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hari ay may isang **lukayo** na laging nagpapangiti sa kanya.","translation":"The king has a **jester** who always makes him smile."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-asal-**lukayo** sa harap ng mga bisita.","translation":"Don't act like a **buffoon** in front of the guests."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagiging mas mahaba sa sukat o tagal ng panahon.
original_explanation: This is what you wish would happen to your weekend and what you dread happening to your boss's speech. It's the **paghaba** ng pila sa bangko, ng traffic sa EDSA, or ng buhok mo when you badly need a haircut. It’s the process of something getting longer, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Can refer to length in space (e.g., hair, a line) or duration in time (e.g., a meeting, a story).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin niya ang **paghaba** ng kanyang buhok matapos ang ilang buwan.","translation":"She noticed the **lengthening** of her hair after a few months."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **paghaba** ng kuwentuhan, inabot na sila ng hatinggabi.","translation":"Because of the **prolongation** of the conversation, they stayed up until midnight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaba ng posisyon, katayuan, o antas sa isang organisasyon, militar, o anumang herarkiya.
original_explanation: This is the corporate version of being "demoted" from your barkada's group chat admin. It's the opposite of a promotion. It’s when you go from being the team lead to just... a team member again. The ultimate "uno reverse card" from your boss. Saklap.
usage_notes: A formal term used in corporate, military, or organizational contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkababa ng ranggo** ay resulta ng hindi magandang performance.","translation":"His **demotion** was the result of poor performance."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya matanggap ang desisyon tungkol sa kanyang **pagkababa ng ranggo**.","translation":"He could not accept the decision regarding his **demotion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, paksa, o usapin na tiyak na magiging sanhi ng debate, hindi pagkakasundo, o pagtatalo.
original_explanation: That last slice of pizza in the box that everyone's eyeing. Or that one political topic your tito brings up at every family reunion that's guaranteed to start a 'heated discussion.' It's the subject matter of future marites-level chismis or a full-blown comment war on social media.
usage_notes: This is in the future tense, indicating that an argument or debate is bound to happen regarding a specific topic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hatian sa mana ay isang isyung **mapagtatalunan** ng magkakapatid.","translation":"The division of the inheritance is an issue that **will be argued over** by the siblings."}]

meaning_filipino: Painumin ang isang tao ng alak hanggang sa malango o malasing; sadyain na malasing ang isang tao.
original_explanation: The act of intentionally getting someone drunk. Sometimes it's a 'fun' party game, other times it's a sketchy tactic. 'Pare, **lasingin** natin si birthday boy!' It's what happens when the 'tagay' master keeps refilling your glass before you can even finish it.
usage_notes: This is a transitive verb, requiring an object (the person being made drunk). The term 'lasing-lasingin' is a more emphatic or repetitive form which is less common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **lasingin** ang bisita, nakakahiya.","translation":"Don't **get** the guest **drunk**, it's embarrassing."},{"sentence":"May masamang balak yata sila, sinusubukang **lasingin** si Ana.","translation":"I think they have bad intentions, they are trying to **get** Ana **drunk**."}]

translation: abjectness; state of being lowly or despised
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging mababa, aba, o walang halaga sa paningin ng iba; ang pagdanas ng matinding kahihiyan o pag-aalipusta.
original_explanation: This is the feeling of being the 'kontrabida' in your own life story, where everyone seems to look down on you. It's that rock-bottom, 'api-apihan' feeling you see in teleseryes before the character's grand 'makeover' and 'revenge' arc. It’s being treated like you’re not even a ‘ghost’ employee, but a ghost, period.
usage_notes: Carries a very strong sense of being debased or looked down upon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang matinding **pagkahamak** nang siya ay ipahiya sa harap ng lahat.","translation":"He felt extreme **abjectness** when he was shamed in front of everyone."},{"sentence":"Mula sa **pagkahamak**, bumangon siya at naging matagumpay.","translation":"From a **state of being lowly**, she rose and became successful."}]

translation: Credits to the owner (often abbreviated as CTTO)
meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na ginagamit bilang pagkilala sa orihinal na may-ari ng isang litrato, teksto, o anumang materyal na ibinabahagi online, lalo na kapag hindi tiyak kung sino ang partikular na may-ari.
etymology: English phrase, popularized by social media usage. Abbreviated as CTTO.
original_explanation: The magic spell you type on Facebook when you share a meme or a photo you just grabbed from somewhere else. It's the internet's way of saying, "Hindi sa'kin 'to pero ishine-share ko, 'wag n'yo 'ko kasuhan." The ultimate get-out-of-jail-free card for online sharing. CTTO na lang, para safe.
usage_notes: Almost always used in the context of sharing digital content. The abbreviation "CTTO" is extremely common and often used in place of the full phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng litratong ito! I-share ko nga. (**Credits to the owner**.)","translation":"This photo is beautiful! I'll share it. (**Credits to the owner**.)"},{"sentence":"Nakita ko lang sa feed ko, **CTTO**.","translation":"I just saw this on my feed, **CTTO** (Credits To The Owner)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha ng pagkiskis ng mga tuyong bagay, tulad ng mga dahon, papel, o tela.
etymology: From a root word `gaskas` imitating the sound.
original_explanation: This is the official sound of horror movies set in a probinsya. The 'kagaskas' of leaves could be the wind... or it could be a white lady about to ask for directions. It's also the sound of you trying to sneak a snack late at night and the plastic wrapper betraying you with its loud rustling.
usage_notes: An onomatopoeic word for the sound of friction between dry, light objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May narinig akong **kagaskas** sa likod ng bahay.","translation":"I heard a **rustling sound** behind the house."},{"sentence":"Ang **kagaskas** ng mga tuyong dahon ay nakakatakot sa dilim.","translation":"The **rustling** of dry leaves is scary in the dark."}]

meaning_filipino: Mabasa o maabutan ng ulan, lalo na kapag nasa labas at walang proteksyon.
original_explanation: The official term for getting caught in the rain without an umbrella. That sudden downpour during your commute that ruins your hair, your shoes, and your entire mood. 'Nako, na-maanuran na naman 'yung mga sinampay!'
usage_notes: Implies being caught unexpectedly or undesirably in the rain. 'Maulanan' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdala ka ng payong para hindi ka **maanuran**.","translation":"Bring an umbrella so you won't **be rained on**."},{"sentence":"**Naanuran** ang mga damit na isinampay ko sa labas.","translation":"The clothes I hung outside **got rained on**."}]

translation: tinkle; the sound of a small bell
meaning_filipino: Ang mahina at matinis na tunog na nalilikha ng isang maliit na kampana o batingaw.
original_explanation: This is the sound of the sorbetero (ice cream vendor) approaching your street, the tiny bell on your cat's collar, or the bell on a hotel reception desk. It's a light, cheerful, attention-getting sound. It's the onomatopoeia for 'Hey, I'm here!' in the most charming way possible.
usage_notes: Purely onomatopoeic, referring to the sound itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **kuliling** ng kampana ng sorbetero.","translation":"I heard the **tinkle** of the ice cream vendor's bell."},{"sentence":"Ang pusa ay may laso na may **kuliling** sa leeg.","translation":"The cat has a ribbon with a **small bell** on its neck."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masusing pagsisiyasat o pag-alam sa isang bagay, lalo na sa opinyon, damdamin, o intensyon ng isang tao sa paraang hindi direkta.
etymology: Mula sa "sonda" (probe, sounding lead) + "-hin" (hulaping pandiwa). Ang "sonda" ay mula sa Espanyol na "sonda".
original_explanation: This is the art of "pakiramdaman." You're trying to figure out what someone is thinking without asking them directly. Parang 'pag tinanong mo 'yung crush mo, "May lakad ka ba sa Sabado?" para malaman kung single ba siya. You're probing, fishing for information. Politicians are masters of this, trying to gauge public opinion before making a move.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng imbestigasyon, relasyon, o maniobrang politikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **sondahin** ang opinyon ng kanyang mga kasamahan tungkol sa bagong patakaran.","translation":"He tried to **sound out** his colleagues' opinions about the new policy."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **sondahin** ang lalim ng kanyang pagkatao.","translation":"It's difficult to **fathom** the depth of his character."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtawag sa isa't isa; isang komunikasyon sa pamamagitan ng telepono.
etymology: From "tawag" + "-an" suffix, indicating a place or reciprocal action.
original_explanation: This is when the communication is two-way. "May tawagan kami" means "We have a call scheduled" or "We call each other." It's that moment your BPO friend says, "Wait lang, may tawagan pa ako," meaning they have another call in the queue.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to a phone call specifically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal ang naging **tawagan** namin kagabi.","translation":"Our **phone call** last night was long."},{"sentence":"May usapan kaming **tawagan** mamayang alas-tres.","translation":"We agreed to have a **call** later at three o'clock."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o katangian ng pagiging tanga; isang gawaing nagpapakita ng kawalan ng pag-iisip o pang-unawa.
original_explanation: This is the official term for when you do something dumb. Like replying 'okay' to an LBC tracking number, sending a rant about your boss *to* your boss, or falling for the same 'pa-fall' person for the nth time. It’s that facepalm moment, but in noun form. The national sport, according to hugot culture.
usage_notes: A very common word, often used in jest, frustration, or self-deprecation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsisisihan ko ang **katangahan** kong iwan ang wallet ko sa taxi.","translation":"I regret my **stupidity** for leaving my wallet in the taxi."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang **katangahan** mo sa pag-ibig!","translation":"Stop your **foolishness** in love!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maingat na pag-iisip o pag-unawa sa damdamin at kalagayan ng iba; pagbibigay-halaga.
original_explanation: This is the "pakisama" you show to people. It's not playing loud music at 3 AM because your neighbors are sleeping. It's giving up your seat on the MRT for a senior citizen. It's the basic human decency that keeps society from turning into a chaotic free-for-all. "Bigyan mo naman ako ng konting konsiderasyon!"
usage_notes: Often used to ask for empathy or understanding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magpakita ka naman ng **konsiderasyon** sa mga kasama mo sa bahay.","translation":"Show some **consideration** for your housemates."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang desisyon ay ginawa nang walang **konsiderasyon** sa magiging epekto nito sa iba.","translation":"His decision was made without **consideration** for its effect on others."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang posisyon ng katawan kung saan ang likod ay nakabaluktot paatras, na nagpapatingkad sa dibdib at tiyan.
original_explanation: The "I'm sexy and I know it" pose for your IG OOTD. It's when you arch your back to make your chest and butt more prominent. Also the default position when you're stretching after sitting in front of your laptop for 8 hours straight. "Tito/Tita stretch na 'yan."
usage_notes: Can be a noun (the posture itself) or an adjective (describing someone in that posture). The verb form is 'lumiyad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naka-**liyad** siyang naglakad na parang modelo.","translation":"She walked with her **back arched** like a model."},{"sentence":"Ang sakit sa likod ay nagiging sanhi ng kanyang pagiging **liyad**.","translation":"The back pain is causing his **arched posture**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, lalo na isang kemikal o gamot, na nagpapawalang-bisa sa epekto ng lason o iba pang substansiya.
etymology: Compound of "pamatay" (killer/extinguisher, from root 'patay') and "bisa" (effect, potency).
original_explanation: The "undo" button for poison or a bad decision. It's the chaser you take after a strong drink, the water you drink after eating something too spicy, or the funny meme you look at after a stressful meeting. It kills the effect.
usage_notes: Often used in a medical or chemical context, but can also be used figuratively.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap ang mga siyentipiko ng **pamatay-bisa** para sa lason ng ahas.","translation":"The scientists are searching for an **antidote** for the snake's venom."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-inom ng gatas ay nagsisilbing **pamatay-bisa** sa anghang.","translation":"Drinking milk serves as a **neutralizer** for the spiciness."}]

translation: to fail; to malfunction; to misfire
meaning_filipino: Ang hindi gumana nang maayos, magkaroon ng depekto, o hindi makamit ang inaasahang resulta.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `palya` (failure, misfire), from Spanish 'fallar' (to fail).
original_explanation: That dreaded moment when your laptop freezes during a presentation, or when the car won't start on a Monday morning. That's your device 'nagpapalya'. It's when something stops working as it should. Can also apply to people's plans. 'Nagpalya ang plano naming mag-beach dahil biglang umulan.'
usage_notes: Often used for machines, engines, or plans. 'Pumalya' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag nagsimulang **magpalya** ang makina, dapat ipaayos agad.","translation":"When the engine starts to **malfunction**, you should have it fixed immediately."},{"sentence":"Huwag sana tayong **magpalya** sa ating mga pangako.","translation":"Let's hope we don't **fail** on our promises."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng masangsang at hindi kaaya-ayang amoy, katulad ng amoy ng nabubulok na bagay o hindi dumadaloy na tubig.
original_explanation: The smell of a public CR you wish you never entered. The scent of a canal or 'estero' on a hot day. It's a very specific kind of 'mabaho' that's sharp, pungent, and makes your nose wrinkle instantly. Not to be confused with 'maanghit' (B.O.) or 'mapanghi' (urine-specific). 'Maantot' is the general-purpose, really bad smell.
usage_notes: Describes a strong, unpleasant, often stagnant or decaying smell.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itapon mo na ang basura dahil **maantot** na.","translation":"Throw out the garbage because it's already **foul-smelling**."},{"sentence":"May **maantot** na amoy na nanggagaling sa ilalim ng lababo.","translation":"There's a **pungent smell** coming from under the sink."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyong medikal kung saan ang isang tao ay may mababang bilang ng pulang selula ng dugo o hemoglobin, na nagreresulta sa pamumutla at panghihina.
original_explanation: Eto yung palagi kang mukhang pagod, maputla, at laging sinasabihan ng nanay mo na kumain ka ng atay ng manok. Not a vampire thing, just a 'you need more iron in your life' thing. Parang anemic din yung wallet mo bago mag-sweldo.
usage_notes: Is a common descriptive phrase for someone who looks pale or is medically diagnosed with anemia.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madalas siyang mahilo dahil **kulang sa dugo**.","translation":"She often gets dizzy because she is **anemic**."},{"sentence":"Payo ng doktor, kumain siya ng mga pagkaing mayaman sa iron dahil **kulang siya sa dugo**.","translation":"The doctor's advice was for her to eat iron-rich foods because she is **anemic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng marahas o malakas na paglanghap sa pamamagitan ng ilong, karaniwang dahil sa sipon, pag-iyak, o pag-amoy ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: That sound you make when your allergies are acting up, you just watched a sad K-drama, or you're trying to figure out if the sinigang is ready. It's the official background noise of flu season. Can also refer to the darker act of inhaling illegal substances, but in everyday use, it's mostly about the sipon (cold).
usage_notes: Can have a negative connotation when referring to drug use. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naririnig ko ang kanyang **pagsisinghot** mula sa kabilang kwarto; tiyak na may sipon siya.","translation":"I can hear his **sniffling** from the other room; he surely has a cold."},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **pagsisinghot** ang ginawa niya para maamoy ang pabango.","translation":"She gave a loud **sniff** to smell the perfume."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang organisadong grupo ng mga tao na may magkakatulad na ideolohiya at layuning pampulitika, na naghahangad na makakuha ng kontrol sa gobyerno. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang panig sa isang laban, laro, o argumento.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'partido' (party, group; divided).
original_explanation: Sa pulitika, ito 'yung 'teams' or 'colors' (red, yellow, blue, etc.). 'Pag eleksyon, lahat may **partido**. Sa inuman, ito 'yung tanong na 'Kaninong **partido** ka? Sa Red Horse o sa San Mig Light?' Sa chismis, ito yung 'Kaninong side ka?'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong **partido** ang sinusuportahan mo sa darating na halalan?","translation":"Which political **party** are you supporting in the upcoming election?"},{"sentence":"Nahati ang grupo sa dalawang **partido** dahil sa hindi pagkakasundo.","translation":"The group was split into two **factions** due to a disagreement."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakatigil; hindi gumagalaw; nakahimpil.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol 'parado', ibig sabihin ay 'stopped' o 'standing'.
original_explanation: Your Grab driver when they're 'on the way' but the GPS hasn't moved in 10 minutes. Also, your brain during a 3 PM meeting after a heavy lunch.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga sasakyan na nakatigil o nakaparada.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal nang **parado** ang kotse sa garahe.","translation":"The car has been **parked** in the garage for a long time."},{"sentence":"Bakit **parado** ang trapiko sa EDSA?","translation":"Why is the traffic **stopped** on EDSA?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalagyan na karaniwang yari sa salamin o plastik, ginagamit sa pag-inom ng likido tulad ng tubig o softdrinks.
original_explanation: Your trusty sidekick for everything from water to that Emperador you're trying to forget. Also the thing your Tita insists you put on your back for 'lamig' (ventosa). Not to be confused with 'tasa' (cup), which is its hotter cousin for coffee or tea.
usage_notes: Generally refers to a drinking vessel without a handle, for cold drinks. 'Tasa' is used for a cup with a handle, typically for hot beverages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot mo nga ang isang **baso** ng malamig na tubig.","translation":"Please pass a **glass** of cold water."},{"sentence":"Nabasag niya ang **baso** kaya kailangan niyang maglinis.","translation":"He broke the **glass** so he needs to clean up."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hayop mula sa Aprika na kamag-anak ng kabayo, kilala sa kanyang natatanging balat na may mga itim at puting guhit.
original_explanation: A horse in pajamas. That black-and-white animal you only see in zoos or children's books. Also, what you call a pedestrian crossing ('zebra crossing'), though most people just say 'tawiran'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita kami ng **sebra** sa Manila Zoo.","translation":"We saw a **zebra** at the Manila Zoo."},{"sentence":"Ang paboritong hayop ng anak ko ay ang **sebra**.","translation":"My child's favorite animal is the **zebra**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagawa nang may pagkakaisa at sabay-sabay na pag-agapay ng isang grupo.
original_explanation: This is 'tulungan' on steroids. It's the "Avengers, assemble!" moment of Filipino community work. Imagine a family of 20 preparing for Noche Buena, everyone has a task, there's chaos, laughter, and somehow, everything gets done. That's 'tulung-tulong'.
usage_notes: Emphasizes the collective, cooperative, and simultaneous nature of the help. Often used with 'na' (e.g., 'tulung-tulong na binuhat').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tulung-tulong** na binuhat ng magkakapitbahay ang mga gamit mula sa nasusunog na bahay.","translation":"The neighbors worked **all together** to carry the belongings from the burning house."},{"sentence":"Ang paglilinis ay mabilis na natapos dahil **tulung-tulong** sila.","translation":"The cleanup was finished quickly because they were **helping one another**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paunang bayad o bahagi ng sahod o bayarin na kinuha bago pa man ang takdang araw ng pagbabayad.
original_explanation: The "vale" you get from your boss when petsa de peligro hits you hard. It's the money that saves you mid-month but also makes you cry on the actual payday. The adelanto is the financial equivalent of a movie spoiler: you get the good part now, but the ending (your payslip) is less exciting.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to an advance on salary or payment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humingi ng **adelanto** ang karpintero para makabili ng materyales.","translation":"The carpenter asked for an **advance payment** to buy materials."},{"sentence":"Naubos na ang **adelanto** ko, malayo pa ang sahod.","translation":"My **cash advance** is already gone, and payday is still far away."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kataas-taasang diyos o manlilikha sa sinaunang mitolohiyang Tagalog bago dumating ang Kristiyanismo.
original_explanation: The OG 'Lodi' of the pre-colonial Philippines. Before we said 'Thank God,' our ancestors were probably saying 'Salamat, Bathala!' He was the CEO of the heavens, managing other deities or 'anitos'. Think of him as the original 'bahala na' guy, as in 'let Bathala handle it.'
usage_notes: Often used in historical, cultural, or literary contexts. Sometimes used poetically to refer to the Christian God. The phrase 'bahala na' is believed to be a shortening of 'bahala na si Bathala' (Let God handle it).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala ang mga ninuno natin kay **Bathala** bilang pinakamakapangyarihang diyos.","translation":"Our ancestors believed in **Bathala** as the most powerful god."},{"sentence":"Sa mga tula, madalas banggitin ang pangalan ni **Bathala**.","translation":"In poems, the name of **Bathala** is often mentioned."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nag-aaral ng isang kalakal, sining, o trabaho sa ilalim ng isang bihasang manggagawa sa loob ng isang takdang panahon.
original_explanation: Basically, the 'Padawan' to a 'Jedi Master'. You're the newbie, the intern, the student who's learning the ropes from a senior. You do the grunt work, make the coffee, and hope to absorb all their skills (and maybe their job someday, charot). Think of it as on-the-job training before you can call yourself a pro.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa Taglish. Ang mga katumbas sa Filipino ay "aprentis" o "nag-aaral na manggagawa".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang bagong **apprentice** ng sikat na chef.","translation":"He is the new **apprentice** of the famous chef."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **apprentice**, marami pa akong kailangang matutunan.","translation":"As an **apprentice**, I still have a lot to learn."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae na may ugaling mapagmataas, mayabang, at mahirap lapitan o kausapin.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "chiflado" (crazy, conceited), na naging "suplado" sa Filipino.
original_explanation: She's the girl who'll look you up and down, raise an eyebrow, and then ignore you. The queen of the "seen-zone." You'll see her in teleseryes as the rich kontrabida who makes life hard for the bida. She probably has a resting bitch face, but sometimes, she's just an introvert. Or maybe she just doesn't like you. Taray!
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a female. The male counterpart is "suplado".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **suplada** kaya kaunti lang ang kaibigan niya.","translation":"She's known for being **snobbish**, that's why she has few friends."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, mukha lang siyang **suplada** pero mabait talaga.","translation":"Don't worry, she just looks **snobbish** but she's actually kind."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng malalim na emosyonal na koneksyon o pagmamahal sa isang tao, na kadalasang ginagamit sa konteksto ng romantikong relasyon na hindi pa opisyal.
original_explanation: The official status of someone in the 'M.U.' (Mutual Understanding) stage. You're not officially a couple, but you might as well be. You text good morning and good night, know each other's coffee orders, and your friends are tired of hearing about them. When someone asks 'kayo na ba?' and you say 'hindi, pero we're... attached,' it means you're emotionally invested but avoiding the label. The #1 rule is: 'bawal maging attached,' but everyone breaks it.
usage_notes: Used as a Taglish/slang term, almost exclusively in the context of romantic or pre-romantic relationships. It implies an emotional connection that may or may not be reciprocated or defined.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi niya friends lang daw pero parang nagiging **attached** na ako.","translation":"He said we were just friends but I think I'm getting **attached**."},{"sentence":"Rule number one sa FWB: bawal maging **attached**.","translation":"Rule number one in FWB (Friends with Benefits): don't get **attached**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa wika, tao, o anumang bagay na nagmula sa o may kaugnayan sa rehiyon ng Guangdong (dating Canton) sa Tsina.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "cantonés", na tumutukoy sa mga bagay mula sa Canton (Guangdong).
original_explanation: Basically, the language you hear in classic Jackie Chan and Stephen Chow movies. It's also the source of some of our favorite Filipino-Chinese dishes. If you go to a Chinese restaurant in Binondo and they serve you siopao and dim sum, you're experiencing a taste of Kantones culture.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri (e.g., lutuing Kantones) o pangalan (e.g., Nagsasalita siya ng Kantones).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong siyang magsalita ng **Kantones** dahil lumaki siya sa Hong Kong.","translation":"He knows how to speak **Cantonese** because he grew up in Hong Kong."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang mga putaheng **Kantones** sa restaurant na iyon.","translation":"The **Cantonese** dishes in that restaurant are delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o paggamit ng trangka upang isara at siguruhing hindi mabubuksan ang isang pinto, bintana, o tarangkahan.
original_explanation: The OG way to secure your house before smart locks were a thing. It's that final 'clunk' sound that tells you, 'Okay, safe na from the outside world... and from mga unwanted bisita.' It's the physical version of setting your social media to private.
usage_notes: Used for the action of putting a bolt or latch in place, usually on a door or gate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtrangka** ka ng pinto bago ka matulog.","translation":"**Lock** the door before you sleep."},{"sentence":"Nakalimutan niyang **magtrangka** kaya nakapasok ang aso.","translation":"He forgot to **bolt** (it), that's why the dog got in."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay ng kalinga, proteksyon, at atensyon sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay upang matiyak ang kalusugan, kaligtasan, at kapakanan nito.
etymology: Mula sa ugat na "alaga" (ward, pet, one being cared for).
original_explanation: This is the OFW parent's primary motivation, the reason for the 'alaga sa yaman' skin whitening lotion, and what you do for your pet, your plant, or your jowa when they have a cold. It's the act of looking after someone or something, often with a lot of love and sometimes with a lot of 'kulit'.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa tao, hayop, halaman, o kahit mga bagay na nangangailangan ng maintenance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Salamat sa iyong walang sawang **pag-aalaga** sa akin noong ako'y may sakit.","translation":"Thank you for your tireless **care** for me when I was sick."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-aalaga** ng halaman ay nangangailangan ng pasensya.","translation":"The **nurturing** of plants requires patience."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o gawi ng pagpapakita ng romantikong interes sa isang tao sa paraang mapaglaro, hindi seryoso, o malandi.
original_explanation: It's the art of the "subtle" (or not-so-subtle) pa-cute. The extra-long eye contact with the cute barista, the "accidental" brushing of hands, the witty banter in the DMs. It's the pre-game before the "in a relationship" status. Some call it "being friendly," others call it Level 1 paglalandi.
usage_notes: Can have a slightly negative or playful connotation depending on the context and the speaker's intent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na 'yang **paglalandi** mo sa katrabaho natin.","translation":"Stop your **flirting** with our coworker."},{"sentence":"Hindi **paglalandi** ang tawag doon, palakaibigan lang talaga siya.","translation":"That's not called **flirting**, he/she is just really friendly."}]

translation: to cause to sprout or grow
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdudulot o pagpapahintulot sa pagtubo o pag-usbong ng isang bagay, tulad ng halaman, ideya, o damdamin.
original_explanation: Think of a gardener carefully tending to seeds until they sprout. That's "magpasibol". But it's not just for plants! It's also for ideas. A good teacher can "magpasibol" ng curiosity in her students. A supportive community can "magpasibol" of new artists and leaders. It’s the act of creating the right conditions for something new and wonderful to begin growing. It’s the verb for nurturing potential.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for plants or figuratively for ideas, feelings, movements, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng samahan ay **magpasibol** ng mga bagong lider sa komunidad.","translation":"The organization's goal is to **cause new leaders to grow** in the community."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magpasibol** ng buto ng ampalaya sa kanilang bakuran.","translation":"She tried to **make** bitter melon seeds **sprout** in their yard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at paulit-ulit na pagtapik sa isang bagay o tao, karaniwan gamit ang palad.
etymology: From `pikpik` (a gentle pat) with the infix `-um-`.
original_explanation: It's that gentle 'tap-tap' on the back your friend gives you when you're down, saying 'kaya mo 'yan.' Or how you pat a baby's back to help it burp. It's a comforting, light touch. 'Pumikpik siya sa balikat ko.'
usage_notes: Refers to a lighter, more repetitive action than `tumapik` (to tap). `Pikpikin` is the object-focus form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumikpik** siya sa likod ng aso para pakalmahin ito.","translation":"He gently **patted** the dog's back to calm it down."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman kong may **pumikpik** sa aking balikat.","translation":"I felt someone **patting** my shoulder."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghahagis o pagkakalat ng likido o anumang maliliit at hiwa-hiwalay na bagay sa iba't ibang direksyon.
original_explanation: What happens during the Basaan Festival in San Juan, or when a car speeds through a puddle beside you while you're waiting for a jeep. It can also be the 'pagsaboy ng biyaya' (showering of blessings) or, more excitingly, 'pagsaboy ng pera' by a politician during a campaign.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging masaya ang pista dahil sa **pagsaboy** ng tubig sa mga lansangan.","translation":"The festival became fun because of the **splashing** of water on the streets."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsaboy** ng abo ng yumaon sa dagat ay huling habilin niya.","translation":"The **scattering** of the deceased's ashes at sea was his last wish."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahilig at madalas magsalita; madaldal.
original_explanation: That one friend who can narrate their entire life story, plus the life stories of their three closest friends, all in one jeepney ride. They provide the live commentary to your life you never asked for. The human equivalent of an unli-data plan, but for words.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa klase bilang isang **masalita** ngunit matalinong mag-aaral.","translation":"She is known in class as a **talkative** but intelligent student."},{"sentence":"Mabuti na lang at hindi siya **masalita**, kaya ligtas ang sikreto mo.","translation":"It's a good thing he's not **talkative**, so your secret is safe."}]

translation: act of winding thread or string around something
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpulupot o pag-ikid ng sinulid, tali, o alambre sa isang bagay, tulad ng sa karihan o pulunan.
etymology: From `pag-` + `bi-` (reduplication of the first syllable of the root) + `bidbid` (to wind, to coil).
original_explanation: Think of how they prepare the "longganisa" at the palengke, tying it into segments. Or when you're so bored you start winding your earphone cables around your finger until they're a tangled mess. That's pagbibidbid. It’s an old-school word for coiling or wrapping something thin tightly.
usage_notes: This is a less common word, often associated with crafts, fishing, or weaving.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabusisi ang **pagbibidbid** ng sinulid sa habihan.","translation":"The **winding** of the thread on the loom is meticulous."},{"sentence":"Tinulungan niya ang mangingisda sa **pagbibidbid** ng lambat.","translation":"He helped the fisherman in the **coiling** of the net."}]

meaning_filipino: Pinipigilan o hindi pinalalabas, tulad ng damdamin, ihi, o dumi.
original_explanation: Ever been in a 5-hour bus ride from Manila to Baguio with no stopovers? That feeling of needing to pee but holding it in? That's `binbin`. It's suppressing something that desperately wants to come out, whether it's ihi, sama ng loob, or a spoiler for the latest series everyone's watching.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of bodily functions or strong emotions. The verb form is 'binbinin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masama sa kalusugan ang laging **binbin** ang ihi.","translation":"It's bad for the health to always have your urine **retained**."},{"sentence":"**Binbin** niya ang galit sa kanyang dibdib.","translation":"He **suppressed** the anger in his chest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang patak-patak na pag-agos o pagdaloy ng isang likido mula sa isang sisidlan o butas.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pag-` at sa salitang ugat na `tulo` (patak ng likido).
original_explanation: That annoying sound from the kitchen faucet at 3 AM. It's the 'tagas' from the roof during a typhoon, the 'uhog' running down your nose when you have a cold, or the sweat dripping down your face after climbing five flights of stairs because the elevator is broken. Any slow, steady drop of liquid is 'pagtulo'.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa mga likido tulad ng tubig, pawis, luha, o maging sipon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayusin mo na ang **pagtulo** ng gripo para hindi masayang ang tubig.","translation":"Fix the **dripping** of the faucet so water isn't wasted."},{"sentence":"Napansin ko ang **pagtulo** ng luha sa kanyang mga mata.","translation":"I noticed the **dripping** of tears from her eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutol o lumaban sa isang utos, sitwasyon, o pisikal na pagpipigil.
etymology: From root 'palag', meaning to wriggle or struggle.
original_explanation: When you're about to be 'ipis-shamed' by your mom with a slipper and you actually try to fight back. It's that sudden burst of defiance, whether it's against your boss's unreasonable OT request or when your friend tries to steal the last piece of chicken. 'Huwag kang papalag-palag diyan!'
usage_notes: Often used to describe physical struggling or verbal defiance. The command form is 'Huwag kang pumalag!' (Don't resist!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit hinuli na ng pulis, **pumalag** pa rin ang magnanakaw.","translation":"Even after being caught by the police, the thief still **resisted**."},{"sentence":"Hindi na ako **pumalag** nang kunin niya ang huling piraso ng pizza.","translation":"I didn't **fight back** when she took the last piece of pizza."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o hayop na mabagal kumilos, tamad, o walang sigla.
original_explanation: This is that feeling on a Monday morning when you've had zero coffee. Or when your internet connection is so slow, you feel like you're back in the dial-up era. You're not just slow ('mabagal'); you're **bugating**—lethargic, with the energy of a sloth on vacation.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation, implying laziness or a lack of vitality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyado kang **bugating** kumilos, mahuhuli na tayo sa flight!","translation":"You're moving too **sluggishly**, we're going to miss our flight!"},{"sentence":"Dahil sa init ng panahon, pakiramdam ko ay **bugating** ang buong katawan ko.","translation":"Because of the hot weather, my whole body feels **lethargic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawa o higit pang bagay, ideya, o tao na nasa magkabilang dulo ng isang ispektrum o direksiyon; hindi magkatugma.
etymology: From `magka-` (denoting a relationship between two or more) + `salungat` (opposite).
original_explanation: Yung kayo ng ex mo. You're polar opposites. Siya mahilig sa K-Pop, ikaw sa heavy metal. Siya gusto ng aircon, ikaw gusto ng bukas na bintana. In short, hindi kayo compatible. You're going in different directions, like EDSA on a Friday payday.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkasalungat** ang aming mga opinyon tungkol sa pulitika.","translation":"Our opinions about politics are **opposite**."},{"sentence":"Nakatayo sila sa **magkasalungat** na kanto ng kalye.","translation":"They stood on **opposite** corners of the street."}]

translation: to be flanked by; to be placed in the middle of
meaning_filipino: Ilagay sa pagitan ng dalawang bagay o tao; palibutan sa magkabilang panig.
etymology: From "gitna" (middle/center) with the circumfix "pa- -an" and a different stress pattern than 'pagitan'.
original_explanation: You, when you're the third wheel. You're literally being 'pagitnaan' by the couple. It’s also what happens to the ham in a ham-and-cheese sandwich. You're the object in the middle of two other things.
usage_notes: The object being placed in the middle is the subject of the sentence (e.g., 'Ang bata ay pinagitnaan ng mga magulang niya.').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagitnaan** ng away ang mga bata.","translation":"Don't place the children **in the middle of** a fight."},{"sentence":"Ang munting bahay ay **pinagitnaan** ng dalawang malaking gusali.","translation":"The small house was **flanked by** two large buildings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapadaan ng pagkain, inumin, o anumang bagay mula sa bibig patungo sa lalamunan at sikmura.
original_explanation: What you do when the chismis is so hot, you just have to **lumunok** and listen. It's also what you do to your pride ('lunukin ang pride') when you need to apologize. "Bes, ang hirap **lumunok** ng tableta ng katotohanan."
usage_notes: The general term for swallowing. Can be used for food, drink, medicine, or abstract things like pride.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahirapan siyang **lumunok** dahil sa namamagang lalamunan.","translation":"He had difficulty **swallowing** because of his sore throat."},{"sentence":"Kinailangan niyang **lumunok** ng masasakit na salita mula sa kanyang amo.","translation":"He had to **swallow** (endure) harsh words from his boss."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulisap na kilala sa malakas at mataginting na tunog na nililikha ng mga lalaki, lalo na tuwing tag-init.
original_explanation: The official soundtrack of summer in the province. That incredibly loud, almost-deafening buzzing sound from the trees that starts when the sun is at its hottest. It's nature's way of saying 'Ang init, 'no?'
usage_notes: Not as commonly used as the English word, but understood, especially in more formal or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ingay ng mga **sikada** ang hudyat na tag-araw na.","translation":"The noise of the **cicadas** is a sign that it is already summer."},{"sentence":"May nahuli siyang **sikada** sa puno ng mangga.","translation":"He caught a **cicada** on the mango tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Pumunta o gawin ang isang bagay kasama ng iba; i-ayon ang sarili sa isang kilos, agos, o uso.
etymology: From 'sabay' (together, at the same time) with the actor-focus infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'go with the flow' verb. It can mean literally going with someone ("**Sumabay** ako sa kanya pauwi"). It can mean joining a trend ("**Sumabay** sa TikTok dance challenge"). It can even mean to happen at the same time ("**Sumabay** ang ulan sa pag-alis namin"). It's the art of timing, of joining in, of not being left behind (or just saving on Grab fare by carpooling).
usage_notes: A very versatile word. Context is key to know if it means to physically go with someone, to join a trend, or to coincide with an event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puwede ba akong **sumabay** sa iyo pag-uwi mamaya?","translation":"Can I **go with** you on your way home later?"},{"sentence":"**Sumabay** siya sa uso at bumili ng bagong smartphone.","translation":"He **went with** the trend and bought a new smartphone."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **sumabay** sa masamang impluwensya ng barkada.","translation":"Don't **go along with** the bad influence of your friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mabangong halamang-gamot (herb) na may siyentipikong pangalan na Ocimum basilicum, karaniwang ginagamit bilang pampalasa sa pagluluto, lalo na sa lutuing Italyano.
original_explanation: That leafy green thing you put on pizza or pasta to make it feel fancy. It's the herb that makes pesto sauce green and delicious. In the Philippines, it's sometimes confused with balanoy or sulasí (holy basil), which is its local cousin.
usage_notes: The English pronunciation /BEY-sil/ is also common. It is related to, but distinct from, the local 'sulasí' or 'balanoy' (holy basil).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay ako ng sariwang **basil** sa aking spaghetti.","translation":"I put fresh **basil** on my spaghetti."},{"sentence":"Ang amoy ng **basil** ay nagpapaalala sa akin ng lutong Italyano.","translation":"The smell of **basil** reminds me of Italian cooking."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakasara at hindi mabuksan dahil sa paggamit ng trangka o kandado.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "trangka" (bar, bolt) na hiram sa Espanyol na "tranca", na nilagyan ng hulaping "-ado".
original_explanation: The status of your front door at night, or your heart after a bad breakup. "Sorry, we're closed." It's that moment of panic when you realize you left your keys inside and the door is trangkado. Time to call the locksmith, or in matters of the heart, your best friend with a tub of ice cream.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang isang pang-uri upang ilarawan ang isang pinto, bintana, o anumang bagay na may kandado.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhin mong **trangkado** ang pinto bago ka umalis ng bahay.","translation":"Make sure the door is **locked** before you leave the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na espasyo, puwang, o siwang sa pagitan ng dalawang bagay.
original_explanation: Yung maliit na **awang** sa pinto kung saan ka sumisilip para tingnan kung gising pa parents mo. O yung **awang** sa puso mo na naiwan niya, na kahit anong gawin mo, hindi na mapunuan. Charot.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang pisikal na puwang o isang metaporikal na agwat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May sinag ng araw na pumapasok sa **awang** ng bintana.","translation":"There's a ray of sun entering through the **gap** in the window."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang **awang** ng aming henerasyon sa mga magulang namin.","translation":"There is a big generation **gap** between us and our parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang negatibo o hindi kanais-nais na bahagi o katangian ng isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is the side of someone you don't want to see. Like your super chill officemate who turns into a monster when their food delivery is late. Or the 'masamang panig' of working from home: the electricity bill.
usage_notes: Can refer to a person's negative traits or the downside of a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong ilabas ang **masamang panig** niya; magagalit talaga iyon.","translation":"Don't bring out his **bad side**; he will get really angry."},{"sentence":"Ang **masamang panig** ng teknolohiya ay ang pagiging sanhi nito ng adiksyon.","translation":"The **negative aspect** of technology is its potential to cause addiction."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay ng paunang impormasyon o hudyat tungkol sa isang posibleng panganib, suliranin, o masamang mangyayari. Ito ang anyong pangnakaraan ng pandiwang "magbabala".
original_explanation: 'Yung sinabi na sa'yo ng nanay mo "Umuwi ka nang maaga," pero 'di ka nakinig. Tapos pag-uwi mo, sarado na 'yung pinto. She nagbabala you. It's the "I told you so" before the "I told you so" happens. From friendly advice to a full-on threat, it all starts with this.
usage_notes: The root 'bala' has multiple meanings (e.g., bullet). In this verb form, it always means 'to warn'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagbabala** ang PAGASA tungkol sa paparating na malakas na bagyo.","translation":"PAGASA **warned** about the approaching strong typhoon."},{"sentence":"**Nagbabala** na ako sa iyo na huwag siyang pagkatiwalaan.","translation":"I already **warned** you not to trust him."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang produkto, ari-arian, o bagay na ipinagbibili, binibili, o ipinapalit sa isang transaksyong pang-komersyo.
original_explanation: The stuff you see on Shopee or Lazada. It's the 'paninda' in the palengke, the 'haul' from your 11.11 shopping spree, or the items your officemate is selling online. Anything that can be bought or sold is kalakal.
usage_notes: This is a root word itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumarami ang mga **kalakal** mula sa Tsina sa ating mga pamilihan.","translation":"The **goods** from China are increasing in our markets."},{"sentence":"Ang pangangalakal ng mga ilegal na **kalakal** ay mahigpit na ipinagbabawal.","translation":"The trading of illegal **merchandise** is strictly prohibited."}]

translation: to shriek in a suppressed way; to squeak
meaning_filipino: Paglikha ng isang mataas at pigil na tunog o sigaw, karaniwan dahil sa pagkagulat, takot, o tuwa.
original_explanation: The sound you make when you see a cute dog, a giant cockroach, or your celebrity crush in person. It's not a full-blown scream, just a high-pitched "eep!" that's stuck in your throat. The official sound of *kilig*.
usage_notes: Conveys a sound that is both high-pitched and held back, often involuntarily.
