usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umimpit** sa tuwa ang dalaga nang bigyan siya ng bulaklak.","translation":"The young lady **squealed** with delight when she was given flowers."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko siyang **umimpit** sa takot nang biglang mamatay ang ilaw.","translation":"I heard her **let out a suppressed shriek** in fear when the lights suddenly went out."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay-pugay o pagpapakita ng paggalang o pakikipagkaibigan sa isang tao sa hinaharap.
etymology: Future tense of the verb "bati" (to greet).
original_explanation: That awkward moment when you see a former colleague at the mall and you have to decide in 0.5 seconds if you'll greet them or pretend you're busy checking out the price of corned beef. "Babati ba ako o hindi?" is the new "To be or not to be?".
usage_notes: This is the future tense form. "Bumati" is past tense, "bumabati" is present tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mamaya, **babati** ako sa aking lola para sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"Later, I **will greet** my grandmother for her birthday."},{"sentence":"Sino ang unang **babati** sa kanya pagdating niya?","translation":"Who **will greet** him first when he arrives?"}]

translation: to press (a button), to tap (on a screen)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdiin ng daliri o isang bagay sa isang buton, teklado, o touchscreen upang ito ay gumana.
original_explanation: The official verb of the digital age. You do this a thousand times a day—on your phone, the remote, the elevator, the ATM. It's the modern-day equivalent of casting a spell. "Pindot to add to cart." "Pindot to send." "Pindot to ignore call."
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense). Present: `pumipindot`, Future: `pipindot`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumindot** siya sa maling buton kaya namatay ang computer.","translation":"He **pressed** the wrong button, so the computer turned off."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **pumindot** ng doorbell nang paulit-ulit?","translation":"Who **pressed** the doorbell repeatedly?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na marupok, madaling masira, o magkalamat.
original_explanation: Describes something that's one wrong move away from shattering. Like dry, old wood, cheap plastic toys from Divisoria, or your patience during a traffic jam on EDSA. 'Huwag mong hawakan 'yan, gapak na.' (Don't touch that, it's brittle.)
usage_notes: The pronunciation shifts stress to the last syllable (/ga-PAK/) when used as an adjective, differentiating it from the noun (/GA-pak/).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **gapak** ang mga lumang dokumento dahil sa katagalan.","translation":"The old documents became **brittle** due to age."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi makapagdudulot ng anumang pinsala, sira, o kapahamakan.
etymology: Mula sa 'di' (not) + 'makapipinsala' (will be able to harm), na nasa aspetong panghinaharap.
original_explanation: Like that intern who just makes coffee and photocopies. They're not gonna crash the system or lose a major client. They're di-makapipinsala. Or that 'diet' soda you're drinking—in theory, harmless, but we all know the truth.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay o tao na hindi nagdudulot ng banta o panganib.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang laruang ito ay gawa sa materyales na **di-makapipinsala** sa mga bata.","translation":"This toy is made from materials that are **harmless** to children."},{"sentence":"Tiniyak ng doktor na ang gamot ay **di-makapipinsala** kahit inumin nang matagal.","translation":"The doctor assured that the medicine is **harmless** even if taken for a long time."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapalihis o pagpapatuis sa isang bagay mula sa tuwid o orihinal na anyo nito; maaari ding tumukoy sa pag-iiba ng katotohanan.
original_explanation: That thing you do to the truth when you're trying to get out of trouble with your parents. Or what happens to your principles when the temptation is real. "Yung pagbaluktot niya sa kwento, parang pretzel na, 'di na malaman kung saan nagsimula."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbaluktot** ng bakal ay nangangailangan ng matinding lakas.","translation":"The **bending** of the steel requires immense strength."},{"sentence":"Hindi katanggap-tanggap ang **pagbaluktot** sa mga katotohanan ng kasaysayan.","translation":"The **distortion** of historical facts is unacceptable."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o bagay na nananatiling matatag, hindi natitinag, o hindi nagbabago sa kabila ng mga pagsubok o puwersa.
etymology: From "walang" (without) and "tinag" (a slight movement, being stirred).
original_explanation: That stoic BPO agent who just got yelled at by a customer but their voice remains perfectly calm and follows the script. Or your lola's faith that remains strong no matter what happens. It's the ultimate "unbothered" state, showing immense emotional or physical fortitude. The human version of a mountain.
usage_notes: Conveys a sense of strength, stability, and resilience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng mga kritisismo, nanatili siyang **walang-tinag** sa kanyang mga paniniwala.","translation":"Despite the criticisms, he remained **unshaken** in his beliefs."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang puno ng akasya ay **walang-tinag** kahit dumaan ang malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The old acacia tree was **unmoved** even after the strong typhoon passed."}]

meaning_filipino: Patawan ng hatol o parusa ng isang hukuman pagkatapos mapatunayang nagkasala.
etymology: From ma- (ability/involuntary action prefix) + sentensiya (sentence, verdict, from Spanish 'sentencia') + -han (locative/benefactive suffix).
original_explanation: This is the final boss level of 'mapagalitan'. It's not your mom telling you off; it's a judge with a gavel. When you get 'masentensiyahan', it means the court has spoken, the verdict is in, and you're about to face the consequences. It’s the 'find out' part of the 'f*ck around and find out' equation, legal edition.
usage_notes: Strictly used in a legal context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari siyang **masentensiyahan** ng habambuhay na pagkakakulong.","translation":"He could **be sentenced** to life imprisonment."},{"sentence":"Matapos ang mahabang paglilitis, **nasentensiyahan** din ang akusado.","translation":"After a long trial, the accused was finally **sentenced**."}]

translation: to be confirmed (in the Catholic sacrament)
meaning_filipino: Ang tumanggap ng sakramento ng Kumpil sa Simbahang Katoliko.
original_explanation: This is the Catholic level-up after baptism. You get a sponsor (ninong/ninang), the bishop taps you on the cheek, and you officially become a "soldier of Christ." It's a big deal for Catholic families, often followed by a handaan (feast). It’s that one time you have to memorize stuff about the Holy Spirit and get a new middle name for a day.
usage_notes: Exclusively used in the context of the Catholic sacrament of Confirmation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ng kabataang Katoliko sa aming parokya ay kailangang **makumpilan** bago mag-asawa.","translation":"All the Catholic youth in our parish need **to be confirmed** before getting married."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing paglalabas ng ihi mula sa katawan bilang isang natural na proseso.
original_explanation: The polite (or not-so-polite) way of saying you're gonna take a leak. 'Yong bigla mong sinabi sa kalagitnaan ng sine, "Sandali, **mag-iihi** lang ako." It's a call of nature that can't be ignored, just like your ex's late-night texts.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong panghinaharap ng 'umihi'. Bagaman mas karaniwan ang 'iihi ako', ang 'mag-iihi ako' ay ginagamit din at tama sa gramatika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uminom ako ng maraming tubig kaya tiyak na **mag-iihi** ako mamaya.","translation":"I drank a lot of water so I will surely **urinate** later."},{"sentence":"Saan ba ang banyo? Kailangan kong **mag-iihi**.","translation":"Where is the restroom? I need to **pee**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsampa ng apela sa isang mas mataas na hukuman o awtoridad; manawagan o humingi ng tulong, awa, o pagsasaalang-alang.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'apela' (mula sa Espanyol 'apelar') at hulaping '-han'.
original_explanation: What you do when your grade is 94 and you need that .5 to get a flat 1.0. "Ma'am, baka pwedeng apelahan 'yung grade ko?" It's also for serious legal stuff, like when you think a court decision was unfair and you take it to the next level.
usage_notes: May dalawang pangunahing gamit: isa sa konteksto ng batas (legal appeal) at isa sa pang-araw-araw na panawagan (personal appeal).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang abogado na **apelahan** ang desisyon ng korte.","translation":"The lawyer decided **to appeal** the court's decision."},{"sentence":"Susubukan kong **apelahan** ang emosyon ng mga manonood sa aking talumpati.","translation":"I will try **to appeal to** the emotions of the audience in my speech."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng matinding pagod o panghihina ng katawan at isip dahil sa labis na paggawa o hirap.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'pagod' from your daily commute. This is the deep-seated exhaustion you feel after finishing a thesis, pulling an all-nighter for a client presentation, or after a week-long fiesta. It's the 'I can't even' level of tired. The more poetic, dramatic cousin of 'pagod'.
usage_notes: "Pagal" and "pagkapagal" are more formal, literary, or dramatic than the everyday word "pagod".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ramdam na ramdam ang **pagkapagal** sa kanyang mukha matapos ang mahabang paglalakbay.","translation":"The **fatigue** was very evident on his face after the long journey."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkapagal**, agad siyang nakatulog pag-uwi.","translation":"Because of **exhaustion**, he immediately fell asleep upon arriving home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nilikha, binuo, o isinakatuparan; isang kilos o aksyon na isinagawa.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *gaway na nangangahulugang "gawin" o "gumawa".
original_explanation: Ito yung output mo, yung project na pinagpuyatan mo, o yung excuse na binuo mo para 'di makapasok sa work. 'Gawa ng China' vs 'Gawa sa Marikina' - it's all about the origin story of a product. It's the 'what' that was done.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin kasama ang "ng" upang tukuyin ang gumawa (hal. gawa ng bata) o ang "sa" upang tukuyin ang pinagmulan (hal. gawa sa Japan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda ang **gawa** ng mga sapaterong Pilipino.","translation":"The **work** of Filipino shoemakers is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtulong sa kapwa ay isang mabuting **gawa**.","translation":"Helping others is a good **deed**."}]

translation: to make something round; to form into a ball
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang bagay na may hugis bilog o pabilog.
original_explanation: The action you do when making palitaw, kutsinta, or even just rolling up paper into a ball to shoot into the trash can. It’s the art of turning something shapeless into a perfect circle or sphere.
usage_notes: Primarily used in cooking or crafts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuruan ako ni Lola kung paano **magbilog** ng masa para sa bilo-bilo.","translation":"Grandma taught me how to **form** the dough **into balls** for bilo-bilo."},{"sentence":"Pakitapos **magbilog** ng mga siomai na iyan.","translation":"Please finish **rolling** those siomai **into shape**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng dumi o uling na karaniwang makikita sa mukha, na nagbibigay ng itsurang hindi malinis.
etymology: From ma- (adjective prefix) + dusing (smudge, grime on the face).
original_explanation: This is the specific kind of dirt on a person's face, like a smudge of chocolate, ink, or soot. It’s what you see on a kid who just played outside all day, or on your own face after eating a powdered donut. It's cuter than 'marumi' (dirty). 'Uy, may tsokolate ka sa pisngi, ang **marusing** mo!'
usage_notes: `Marusing` is almost always used to describe a person's face. `Marumi` is more general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang batang naglalaro sa kalye ay umuwing **marusing** ang mukha.","translation":"The child playing in the street came home with a **grimy** face."},{"sentence":"Punasan mo ang bibig mo, **marusing** ka dahil sa kinain mong biko.","translation":"Wipe your mouth, you're **smudged** because of the biko you ate."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maputing likido na nagmumula sa mga glandula ng mammary ng mga babaeng mamalya para sa nutrisyon ng kanilang mga supling. Ginagamit din bilang pangkalahatang tawag sa anumang likidong kahawig nito.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang mula sa pamilyang wikang Austronesian.
original_explanation: The OG pampatangkad and pampatibay ng buto. The reason you have cereal in the morning. Also, a slang term for something very easy, "gatas lang 'yan" (that's just milk), meaning it's a piece of cake. Or when something is super white, "maputi parang gatas".
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa anumang uri ng gatas (baka, kambing, soy, almond), ngunit karaniwang tumutukoy sa gatas ng baka maliban kung may ibang tinukoy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uminom ka ng **gatas** bago matulog para tumangkad ka.","translation":"Drink **milk** before you sleep so you'll grow taller."},{"sentence":"Pahingi naman ng konting **gatas** para sa kape ko.","translation":"Can I have a little **milk** for my coffee?"}]

translation: became tight, was in a tight spot (financially)
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang kakapusan o kahirapan, lalo na sa usaping pananalapi; ang pagsikip ng kalagayan.
original_explanation: That dreaded "petsa de peligro" feeling before payday when your wallet is crying. It's when you're forced to choose between load and lunch. It's the state of being financially "in a pickle." The antonym of "guminhawa".
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense) of the verb. It almost always refers to financial hardship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula nang mawalan siya ng trabaho, talagang **gumipit** ang kanilang pamilya.","translation":"Since he lost his job, their family really **fell into a tight spot** financially."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi tayo guminhawa noon pero hindi rin tayo **gumipit**.","translation":"Don't worry, we weren't well-off before, but we were never **in a tight spot** either."}]

translation: to be able to pull out; to be able to draw out
meaning_filipino: Ang magkaroon ng kakayahang bunutin, kunin, o ilabas ang isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito, na kadalasan ay mahirap gawin.
original_explanation: That feeling of triumph when you finally pull a very tight pair of shoes off your foot after a long day. Or when you manage to get cash from an ATM that's "offline." Figuratively, this is the origin of "hugot" culture – "mahugot ang feelings" means to be able to draw out deep-seated emotions, usually about love and heartbreak. You're pulling something from deep inside.
usage_notes: Can be literal (pulling a physical object) or figurative (drawing out emotions, ideas, or information).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hirap siyang **mahugot** ang espada na nakabaon sa bato.","translation":"He is having difficulty **pulling out** the sword embedded in the stone."},{"sentence":"May mga alaala na mahirap **mahugot** mula sa isipan.","translation":"There are memories that are difficult **to draw out** from the mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pook na hindi direktang nasisikatan ng araw, karaniwang nasa ilalim ng isang puno o istruktura, na nagbibigay ng kanlungan mula sa init.
original_explanation: That precious spot under a big mango tree during a scorching summer afternoon. It's the universe's natural air-conditioning, the perfect place for a siesta, some chismis with the kapitbahay, or just hiding from your responsibilities for a while. Your phone screen's best friend when you're trying to text outdoors.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to the shade cast by trees. 'Anino' refers to a shadow cast by any object, while 'lilim' specifically refers to the cool, shaded area.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magpahinga muna tayo sa **lilim** ng puno.","translation":"Let's rest for a while in the **shade** of the tree."},{"sentence":"Masarap matulog sa duyan sa ilalim ng **lilim**.","translation":"It's nice to sleep on a hammock under the **shade**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay o paggawa ng isang bagay na magdudulot ng kagalakan o kasiyahan sa isang tao.
original_explanation: Your love language. The goal when you buy your jowa milk tea, when you let your mom win at Scrabble, or when you send a funny meme to a sad friend. It's the verb form of 'sana all happy.'
usage_notes: An object-focus verb. The person being made happy is the object of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **pasayahin** ang kanyang nalulungkot na kaibigan.","translation":"He is trying to **make his sad friend happy**."},{"sentence":"Simple lang akong **pasayahin**, bigyan mo lang ako ng pagkain.","translation":"It's simple to **make me happy**, just give me food."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng labis na pagmamalaki sa sariling katangian, ari-arian, o nagawa, kadalasan sa paraang nakakainis sa iba.
etymology: From 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'mayabang' (boastful), which comes from the root 'yabang'.
original_explanation: The official sport of anyone who just got their 13th-month pay. It's when you post your new iPhone, your Starbucks cup, and your travel pics all in one day. Basically, "flexing" before "flex" was a thing. The opposite of being low-key.
usage_notes: Often used with a negative connotation. It implies showing off in an irritating way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magmayabang** dahil lang nanalo ka sa raffle.","translation":"Don't **be boastful** just because you won the raffle."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magmayabang** tungkol sa kanyang bagong kotse.","translation":"He likes to **brag** about his new car."}]

translation: to wear down, to make blunt
meaning_filipino: Gawing pudpod o mapurol ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paggamit o pagkiskis.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung action na ginagawa mo sa krayola ng kapatid mo 'pag inis ka sa kanya. O 'yung ginagawa ng kalsada sa sapatos mo 'pag lagi kang naglalakad. The act of making something pudpod. "Huwag mong pudpurin 'yang pambura ko!"
usage_notes: The verb form of 'pudpod'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinadya niyang **pudpurin** ang dulo ng lapis para hindi magamit.","translation":"He deliberately **blunted** the tip of the pencil so it couldn't be used."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **pudpurin** ng panahon ang galit mo sa kanya.","translation":"Let time **wear down** your anger towards him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tawag sa pinuno ng isang barangay o maliit na pamayanan sa Pilipinas bago dumating ang mga Espanyol.
etymology: From Malay 'datu' or 'datuk', meaning chieftain or grandfather.
original_explanation: The original bossman of the pre-colonial Philippines. A **datu** was like the barangay captain, mayor, and judge all rolled into one. They were the original influencers of their time. Lapu-Lapu wasn't just a fish name, he was a powerful **datu**.
usage_notes: A historical term referring to pre-colonial rulers. In modern Mindanao, the title is still used by traditional leaders.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Lapu-Lapu ay isang tanyag na **datu** mula sa Mactan.","translation":"Lapu-Lapu was a famous **chieftain** from Mactan."},{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya sa Mindanao ang may lahing **datu**.","translation":"Many families in Mindanao have **datu** lineage."}]

meaning_filipino: Madaling masira, mabasag, o bumigay dahil sa kahinaan ng materyal o istruktura. Sa makabagong gamit, tumutukoy din sa isang taong madaling mahulog ang damdamin o bumigay sa tukso.
original_explanation: Literally, it's something physically weak, like a cheap plastic chair or a dry twig. But in the age of 'hugot', it means you're emotionally fragile. You see a cute smile from your crush and you're ready to fall in love? Congrats, **marupok** ka. It's the official adjective of people who fall too fast and get ghosted.
usage_notes: Has a very popular modern slang meaning related to romantic vulnerability.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang umupo diyan, **marupok** ang silyang iyan.","translation":"Don't sit there, that chair is **fragile**."},{"sentence":"Isang 'hi' lang niya, bibigay ka na agad? Ang **marupok** mo naman!","translation":"Just one 'hi' from them and you give in already? You're so **emotionally vulnerable**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging magkakasama; ang unyon o pagkakabuklod ng dalawa o higit pang tao o bagay.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + sama (to go with, accompany).
original_explanation: This is the #SanaAll of relationships. It's the goal of every team building, barkada outing, and family reunion. It's what you have with your work bestie who gets your coffee order without asking. On a more serious note, it's the legal and emotional state of being together, as in 'ang aming pagsasama bilang mag-asawa.'
usage_notes: A very common and versatile word. It can refer to romantic relationships, friendships, family bonds, or even the mixing of ingredients.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang matibay na **pagsasama** ay nangangailangan ng tiwala at pag-unawa.","translation":"A strong **relationship/companionship** requires trust and understanding."},{"sentence":"Ipinagdiwang nila ang ikasampung taon ng kanilang **pagsasama**.","translation":"They celebrated the tenth year of their **being together**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan sa palakasan, karaniwang gawa sa kahoy o metal, na ginagamit upang pumatama ng bola sa mga larong tulad ng baseball o softball.
original_explanation: The wooden or metal stick you use to hit a ball in baseball. Not the flying animal ('paniki'), and not the start of a province name ('Batangas'). It's a direct loanword, used as is in sports contexts.
usage_notes: Used almost exclusively in the context of sports like baseball and softball. The Tagalog word for the animal is 'paniki'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hawakan mo nang mahigpit ang **bat** bago ka pumalo.","translation":"Hold the **bat** tightly before you swing."},{"sentence":"Nabasag ang kanyang paboritong **bat**.","translation":"His favorite **bat** broke."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makapangyarihang lantsa na ginagamit upang hilihin o itulak ang ibang malalaking sasakyang-dagat na hindi makagalaw nang mag-isa, lalo na sa masisikip na daungan.
original_explanation: This is the small but mighty gym bro of the sea. The **lantsang pambatak** (tugboat) is that tiny boat you see pushing or pulling a massive container ship that's like 100 times its size. It's proof that size doesn't matter; it's all about the 'torque'. It's the supportive friend who helps you move your entire condo's worth of stuff using their sheer will and power.
usage_notes: This is a noun phrase composed of 'lantsa' and the adjective 'pambatak', linked by '-ng'. It functions as a compound noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinulungan ng dalawang **lantsang pambatak** ang malaking barko na makadaong sa piyer.","translation":"Two **tugboats** helped the large ship dock at the pier."},{"sentence":"Kahit maliit tingnan, napakalakas ng makina ng isang **lantsang pambatak**.","translation":"Even if it looks small, the engine of a **tugboat** is very powerful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng isang bagay na natutukoy sa pamamagitan ng pang-amoy; maaaring ito ay halimuyak (mabango) o baho (mabaho).
original_explanation: The ultimate detector. It can be good (amoy-bagong-luto) or bad (amoy-medyas na 'di nilabhan for a week). It’s how your mom knows you were out late ('Amoy-araw ka!') or how you know the kapitbahay is cooking adobo again. It's a neutral word, but the context and the word it's paired with is everything.
usage_notes: Isang napakapangunahin at maraming gamit na salita. Maaaring isama sa ibang salita upang ilarawan ang mga tiyak na amoy (hal. amoy-lupa, amoy-pawis).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bango ng **amoy** ng sampaguita sa gabi.","translation":"The **scent** of sampaguita is so fragrant at night."},{"sentence":"May masamang **amoy** na nanggagaling sa basurahan.","translation":"There is a bad **odor** coming from the trash can."}]

translation: to assist; to do carefully; to support
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtulong o pagsuporta; ang paggawa ng isang bagay nang may pag-iingat at dahan-dahan.
original_explanation: What you tell your friend carrying the birthday cake: "Alalay lang!" (Be careful!). It's the act of supporting someone, either physically (like helping a lola cross the street) or emotionally. It means to handle with care, to take it slow, to not mess things up.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin bilang isang utos o pakiusap: "Alalay!" o "Alalayan mo!". Ito ang anyong-ugat ng pandiwa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Alalay** sa pagbuhat ng babasaging kahon.","translation":"**Be careful** in lifting the fragile box."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **alalay** ng maysakit para makatayo.","translation":"The sick person needs **support** to stand up."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang utos o kilos na lagyan ng laman ang isang espasyo, kakulangan, o patlang.
original_explanation: "Fill in the blanks." That's literally what "Punan ang patlang" means. It's what you do with application forms, empty water bottles, and the void left by your favorite K-drama after the finale.
usage_notes: This is a command or infinitive form, used to direct someone to fill something or to describe the action of filling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Punan** mo ng sagot ang bawat patlang.","translation":"**Fill** in each blank with an answer."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **punan** ang mga bakanteng posisyon sa kumpanya.","translation":"The vacant positions in the company need to be **filled**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang uri ng pagkaing inihanda sa pamamagitan ng pagluto; isang putahe.
original_explanation: The main event of any Filipino meal. It's the ulam that goes with the mountain of rice on your plate. When someone asks "Anong lutuin natin?", they're not just asking for a recipe, they're starting a national debate between Adobo, Sinigang, or a dark horse like Bicol Express.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with `ulam` (viand).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang paborito mong **lutuin** ng nanay mo?","translation":"What is your favorite **dish** that your mom cooks?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdurog o paglamas sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng matinding diin; o ang proseso ng paglabas ng isang sisiw o hayop mula sa itlog.
original_explanation: This has two major vibes. First, it's what happens when a chick breaks out of its shell—hatching. Second, it's what you do to a cockroach with your tsinelas. It's the act of crushing something, whether it's garlic for your sinigang, a pimple (don't do it!), or your hopes and dreams when you see your electricity bill.
usage_notes: The context (e.g., 'itlog' for egg, 'bawang' for garlic) is crucial to distinguish between 'hatching' and 'crushing'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinihintay namin ang **pagpisa** ng mga itlog ng manok.","translation":"We are waiting for the **hatching** of the chicken eggs."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpisa** sa bawang ay nagpapalabas ng aroma nito.","translation":"The **crushing** of the garlic releases its aroma."}]

meaning_filipino: Isakatuparan ang isang aksyon, trabaho, o gawain; lumikha o bumuo ng isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa `gawa` (do, make) at hulaping `-in` (object-focus suffix).
original_explanation: The ultimate command. The Nike slogan of Tagalog: 'Just do it.' - 'Gawin mo lang.' It's what your boss tells you, what your mom tells you, and what you tell yourself at 3 AM facing a deadline. It's the verb that makes the world go 'round, from making coffee (gawin ang kape) to making a decision (gawin ang desisyon).
usage_notes: Ito ang pinakakaraniwang pandiwa na object-focus para sa "to do" o "to make". Ang paksa ng pangungusap ay ang bagay na ginagawa o nililikha.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang dapat kong **gawin**?","translation":"What should I **do**?"},{"sentence":"Masarap ang keyk na **gagawin** ko para sa iyo.","translation":"The cake I will **make** for you is delicious."}]

translation: to sun-dry; to expose to the sun
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng isang bagay sa ilalim ng sikat ng araw upang matuyo o mainitan.
original_explanation: The original Filipino solar-powered dryer. What your nanay tells you to do with the laundry ('**Ibilad** mo na 'yan!'), the fish (to make daing), and sometimes, you, when you've been inside playing video games all day. 'Magpa-araw ka, 'wag kang mag-**ibilad** sa computer!'
usage_notes: The focus is on the thing being put out in the sun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **ibilad** nang mabuti ang mga damit para hindi bumaho.","translation":"You need to **sun-dry** the clothes well so they don't smell bad."},{"sentence":"**Ibinilad** niya ang mga isda upang gawing tuyo.","translation":"She **exposed the fish to the sun** to make dried fish."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng pagiging hindi masaya, bigo, o may dinaramdam na hinagpis o pighati.
original_explanation: The OG sad. The default setting when your crush leaves you on "seen." It's the feeling of seeing your food delivery app say "Order Canceled" or when it's payday but you've already paid all your bills. It's the everyday, common-cold version of sadness, unlike its more dramatic cousin, 'malumbay'.
usage_notes: The most common word for "sad".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Malungkot** ako dahil hindi ako nakapasa sa pagsusulit.","translation":"I'm **sad** because I didn't pass the exam."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **malungkot**, may bukas pa.","translation":"Don't be **sad**, there's still tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang butil (cereal grain) na ginagamit sa paggawa ng pagkain, inumin tulad ng serbesa, at pakain sa hayop.
original_explanation: That healthy grain your fitspo friend puts in their soup or salad. It's also the main ingredient that becomes beer, so you can thank barli for your San Mig Light. It's the grain that lives a double life: one in the health food aisle, the other at the bar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masustansya ang sabaw na may halong **barli**.","translation":"The soup mixed with **barley** is nutritious."},{"sentence":"Ang **barli** ay isa sa mga pangunahing sangkap ng serbesa.","translation":"**Barley** is one of the main ingredients of beer."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghahangad, pag-asam, o pagkagusto sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is your 'Sana all' moment turned into a verb. When you see your friend's travel pics, a new gadget, or their Jollibee meal, and you desperately want it for yourself? That feeling is 'naisin'. It's the 'add to cart' button of your heart.
usage_notes: Often used in a more formal or literary context than 'gusto'. It implies a deeper, more heartfelt desire.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano pa ba ang maaari mong **naisin** kung nasa iyo na ang lahat?","translation":"What more could you **wish for** if you already have everything?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang organo sa loob ng katawan na kahugis ng isang supot na nag-iipon ng ihi mula sa mga bato bago ito ilabas.
original_explanation: Your body's original 'holding area'. It's that one friend who keeps saying '5 more minutes' but you know they're about to burst. When your pantog calls, you answer. No excuses, especially during a long bus ride or in the middle of a movie.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a medical or biological context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ako ng doktor na uminom ng maraming tubig para malinis ang aking **pantog**.","translation":"The doctor advised me to drink a lot of water to cleanse my **bladder**."},{"sentence":"Sumasakit ang **pantog** niya dahil sa UTI.","translation":"His/Her **bladder** hurts because of a UTI."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw na hindi matatag o pagewang-gewang, tulad ng isang lasing na naglalakad o isang gusaling inuuga ng lindol.
original_explanation: How you walk after a few too many bottles of Red Horse. Or how an old, rickety wooden bridge feels when you cross it. It's that unstable, wobbly movement that makes you feel like things are about to fall apart.
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense) of the verb. It describes an unstable, side-to-side motion. Often reduplicated as 'gumiray-giray' for emphasis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gumiray** ang poste ng ilaw dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"The light post **swayed** because of the strong wind."},{"sentence":"Pagkatayo niya, **gumiray** siya dahil sa hilo.","translation":"When he stood up, he **staggered** due to dizziness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng amag na karaniwang tumutubo sa mga mamasa-masang lugar, gaya ng damit, pader, o pagkain.
original_explanation: That gross, smelly stuff that grows on your damp clothes when you forget them in the washing machine for three days. It's the enemy of every condo dweller during the rainy season. "Amoy tagulamin yung tuwalya, hindi natuyo nang maayos!"
usage_notes: Madalas ding gamitin upang ilarawan ang amoy (`amoy-tagulamin`) bukod sa mismong amag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **tagulamin** ang mga damit na naiwan sa loob ng aparador.","translation":"The clothes left inside the cabinet developed **mildew**."},{"sentence":"Kailangang linisin ang pader para maalis ang **tagulamin**.","translation":"The wall needs to be cleaned to remove the **mold**."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang babae na ang kilos, pananamit, o gawi ay karaniwang iniuugnay sa mga lalaki.
original_explanation: Used to describe a girl who's 'one of the boys.' She can out-drink you, burps louder, and isn't afraid to get her hands dirty. It's often said with a mix of surprise and admiration (or sometimes, old-school judgment). "Kumilos ka nga nang maayos, **parang lalaki** ka kung gumalaw!"
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang babae na nagpapakita ng mga katangiang karaniwang panlalaki. Maaaring maging neutral, positibo, o negatibo depende sa konteksto at tono.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang lider ng grupo nila, kumilos siyang **parang lalaki**.","translation":"She is the leader of their group, she acts **like a man**."},{"sentence":"Bihira siyang magsuot ng bestida dahil mas komportable siyang manamit nang **parang lalaki**.","translation":"She rarely wears dresses because she's more comfortable dressing **like a boy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, gawain, o proseso na may kaugnayan sa halalan o eleksiyon.
original_explanation: This word pops up more often than your long-lost relatives during campaign season. **Panghalalan** describes anything and everything related to elections: the drama, the jingles that get stuck in your head, the free t-shirts, and the solemn duty of shading a ballot. It's the adjective for the Philippines' national sport.
usage_notes: Often used to modify nouns like `kampanya` (campaign), `araw` (day), or `batas` (law).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang seguridad sa mga presinto tuwing araw ng **panghalalan**.","translation":"Security is tight in the precincts during **election** day."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ang pamimigay ng pera sa panahon ng kampanyang **panghalalan**.","translation":"Giving away money is prohibited during the **electoral** campaign period."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw sa isang bagay o tao nang pabalik-balik at may puwersa.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'alog' (shake) at hulaping '-in' (tuldok-layon na pandiwa).
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa mo sa bote ng ketchup para lumabas 'yung natitirang laman. O 'yung ginagawa ng nanay mo sa'yo kapag ayaw mo pang bumangon sa umaga. "Gising na! Male-late ka na!" sabay alog.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang iutos o ilarawan ang kilos ng pagyanig sa isang bagay. Maaaring gamitin para sa mga pisikal na bagay o sa metaporikal na paraan, tulad ng paggising sa isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Alugin** mo muna ang gamot bago inumin.","translation":"**Shake** the medicine first before drinking."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **alugin** ang mesa, natatapon ang kape ko.","translation":"Don't **shake** the table, my coffee is spilling."}]

meaning_filipino: Nahahati sa maraming maliliit na bahagi o kompartimento; bitak-bitak o may mga lamat (tulad ng tuyong lupa).
original_explanation: Parang 'yung abs ng a-list celebrity, may divisions. O 'yung lupa sa probinsya 'pag tag-init, tuyot na tuyot. Pwede ring 'yung puso mo after a breakup, basag, durog, pitak-pitak.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa mga pisikal na kompartimento o mga bitak/lamat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **pitak-pitak** ang dating matabang lupa dahil sa matinding tagtuyot.","translation":"The once fertile land became **cracked** due to the severe drought."},{"sentence":"May **pitak-pitak** na lalagyan siya para sa kanyang mga turnilyo.","translation":"He has a **compartmentalized** container for his screws."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong mahilig maghanap ng mali o kapintasan sa iba o sa mga bagay-bagay; mapunahin.
etymology: Mula sa "pala-" (unlaping nagpapahiwatig ng pagkahilig) + "pintas" (puna) + "-in" (hulaping pang-uri).
original_explanation: That one tita at every family reunion who will notice you gained weight. Or your boss who finds a typo in slide 97 of your 100-slide presentation. They have a PhD in Fault-Finding. Sila yung tipo ng tao na kahit perpekto na, may makikita pa ring mali.
usage_notes: Mayroon itong negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig na ang tao ay laging at madalas na di-makatarungang namumuna.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **palapintasin** sa gawa ng iba.","translation":"Don't be so **critical** of others' work."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **palapintasin**, kaya iilan lang ang kaibigan niya.","translation":"She is known for being **fault-finding**, which is why she has few friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging kulang sa kasiyahan o hindi makuntento sa kung anong mayroon.
etymology: Mula sa `hindi` (not) + `masiyahan` (to be satisfied), mula sa ugat na `siya` (joy, satisfaction).
original_explanation: 'Yung kaibigan mong inorder na lahat ng laman ng menu pero naghahanap pa rin ng dessert. Or 'yung feeling na kahit na-promote ka na, parang may kulang pa rin. The "what's next?" mindset on steroids. Parang black hole ng needs and wants, laging gutom, laging **hindi masiyahan**.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng estado ng kawalan ng kasiyahan o pagiging hindi kontento.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong ibigay sa kanya, tila siya'y **hindi masiyahan**.","translation":"No matter what is given to him, he seems **to not be satisfied**."},{"sentence":"May mga taong likas na **hindi masiyahan** sa simple't payak na buhay.","translation":"There are people who are naturally **not satisfied** with a simple and plain life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit o hindi pangunahing daanan, landas, o eskinita, na karaniwang nagsisilbing mas mabilis na ruta.
original_explanation: The shortcut you take when Waze gives up on you. It's that sketchy-looking eskinita or dirt path that promises to cut your travel time in half but might also lead you to a dead end or a pack of territorial dogs. Use at your own risk.
usage_notes: Madalas tumutukoy sa isang daanang hindi sementado o bihirang gamitin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan tayo sa **bulaos** para iwasan ang trapik sa highway.","translation":"Let's take the **shortcut** to avoid the traffic on the highway."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na ginagamit upang takpan o balutin ang isang bagay para sa proteksyon o dekorasyon, tulad ng sa aklat o regalo.
original_explanation: The 'cover' of a book, the wrapper of a Choc-Nut, or the case for your phone. It's the first thing you see. It's the reason why you 'don't judge a book by its...' alam mo na.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda ang disenyo ng **pabalat** ng bagong nobela.","translation":"The design of the new novel's **cover** is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Itapon mo nang maayos ang **pabalat** ng kendi.","translation":"Throw the candy **wrapper** away properly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masinsinang paghahanap o paghalungkat sa isang bagay o lugar upang makita ang isang partikular na kagamitan o impormasyon.
original_explanation: This is what your mom does to your room when she's looking for something you "borrowed." It's a full-on investigation, a deep dive into every nook and cranny. Think of it as the physical version of scrolling through someone's old social media posts. Walang makakatakas sa bulatlat.
usage_notes: Often implies a somewhat messy or forceful search. The verb form is 'bulatlatin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malawakang **bulatlat** ang isinagawa ng mga pulis sa bodega.","translation":"The police conducted a thorough **search** of the warehouse."},{"sentence":"Sa ginawang **bulatlat** sa kanyang bag, nakita ang nawawalang pitaka.","translation":"In the **rummaging** of her bag, the missing wallet was found."}]

translation: a type of local sweet; scraper
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng matamis na gawa sa buri o niyog na karaniwang inilalagay sa pinatuyong dahon. Maaari ring tumukoy sa instrumentong pangkaskas.
etymology: From `kaskas` (to scrape), referring to how it is made or eaten.
original_explanation: A classic 'pasalubong' from the provinces! It's that disc of super-sweet muscovado or coconut candy, often wrapped in palm leaves. It's so hard you need to scrape it (hence the name, from 'kaskas' - to scrape), which is the perfect metaphor for trying to get your salary to last until the 30th.
usage_notes: More known as a specific delicacy from certain regions like Antique.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng **pakaskas** bilang pasalubong mula sa aming byahe.","translation":"We bought **pakaskas** as a souvenir from our trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at simpleng tirahan na karaniwang gawa sa mga magaang materyales tulad ng nipa, kawayan, o kahoy.
original_explanation: A small, humble hut, often made of nipa and bamboo. Think of a simple bahay kubo. Nowadays, it's also a popular concept for seafood restaurants ('dampa-style') where you buy fresh seafood from a nearby market (palengke) and have the restaurant cook it for you ('paluto'). So it can mean a humble home or a place for a glorious seafood feast.
usage_notes: Can refer to a poor dwelling or, in a modern context, a type of seafood restaurant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatira ang mangingisda sa isang maliit na **dampa** malapit sa dagat.","translation":"The fisherman lives in a small **hut** near the sea."},{"sentence":"Tara, kumain tayo sa **dampa** sa Macapagal. Ako na ang pipili ng hipon.","translation":"Let's go eat at the **dampa** in Macapagal. I'll pick the shrimp."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang gamot na may maliliit at puting bulaklak, karaniwang ginagawang tsaa na pampakalma.
original_explanation: This is the go-to tsaa for when you're stressed from work, can't sleep because of anxiety, or have an upset stomach (kabag). Your lola might have also rubbed the oil version on your tummy as a kid. It's the official 'kalma ka lang' herb.
usage_notes: Refers to both the plant and the tea or oil ('aceite de manzanilla') derived from it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uminom ka ng tsaa ng **mansanilya** para makatulog ka nang mahimbing.","translation":"Drink **chamomile** tea so you can sleep soundly."},{"sentence":"Pinapahiran ng nanay ng langis ng **mansanilya** ang tiyan ng sanggol.","translation":"The mother rubs **chamomile** oil on the baby's stomach."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na larangan ng pag-aaral o trabaho kung saan ang isang tao ay nagiging dalubhasa.
original_explanation: Yung area na doon ka magaling. Sa office, ikaw 'yung "taga-gawa ng PowerPoint." Sa pamilya, ikaw 'yung "taga-ayos ng WiFi." Sa med school, ito 'yung pipiliin mo after mo maging general practitioner, kung saan mo gustong tumutok: sa puso (cardio), sa balat (derma), o sa puso ng may-ari ng balat (psychiatry).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **espesyalisasyon** ay sa larangan ng corporate law.","translation":"His **specialization** is in the field of corporate law."},{"sentence":"Pinili niya ang cardiology bilang kanyang **espesyalisasyon** sa medisina.","translation":"She chose cardiology as her **specialization** in medicine."}]

translation: To sit on the ground or floor
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-upo nang direkta sa sahig o lupa, kadalasan ay may naka-unat o naka-krus na mga binti.
etymology: Possibly from `lupa` (ground) + `gi` (a suffix indicating position or manner).
original_explanation: This is what you do when all the chairs in the coffee shop are taken, or during a protest rally, or when you're just too tired and dramatically drop to the floor. It's the act of sitting on the ground, Filipino-style, often done with a certain level of 'bagsak' or exhaustion.
usage_notes: Often seen as `lumupagi` (verb) or `nakalupagi` (adjective/state).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod, **lumupagi** na lang siya sa sahig.","translation":"Exhausted, he just **sat on the floor**."},{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang **nakalupagi** sa parke habang nagpapalipas ng oras.","translation":"Many people were **sitting on the ground** in the park while passing the time."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag o sitwasyon na ang tunay na kahulugan ay kabaligtaran ng literal na sinasabi, o isang kalagayan na may magkasalungat na aspekto na tila hindi magkatugma ngunit totoo.
original_explanation: It's the universe's ultimate "Gotcha!" moment. A firefighter's house burning down? That's pagbabalintuna. Complaining about traffic while being part of the traffic? Pagbabalintuna. Winning the lottery and then dying the next day like in that Alanis Morissette song? Peak **pagbabalintuna**. It's life's way of being a sarcastic troll.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **pagbabalintuna** na ang bumbero ang nasunugan ng bahay.","translation":"It is a great **irony** that the firefighter's house was the one that burned down."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **pagbabalintuna** ang kanyang mga sinabi, kailangan mong unawain ang mas malalim na kahulugan.","translation":"His statements were full of **paradox**; you need to understand the deeper meaning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng tumutulong sa panganganak ng isang ina. Karaniwang tinatawag ding hilot.
original_explanation: The OG healthcare professional of the barangay. Before hospitals were a thing, the kumadrona was your go-to for everything from a safe delivery to probably some herbal remedies for 'pasma'. They're the original frontliners, armed with experience and a whole lot of 'tiwala'.
usage_notes: Habang ang "hilot" ay maaari ring mangahulugang midwife, ang "kumadrona" ay mas tiyak sa tulong sa panganganak. Ang "hilot" ay maaari ring tumukoy sa isang tradisyonal na masahista.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag nila ang **kumadrona** nang magsimulang mag-labor si Ana.","translation":"They called the **midwife** when Ana started going into labor."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang utang na loob namin sa **kumadrona** na nagpaanak sa aking ina.","translation":"We owe a great debt of gratitude to the **midwife** who delivered my mother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng nakakaing langis na nakukuha mula sa sapal, gata, o pinatuyong laman ng matandang niyog.
original_explanation: The holy grail of Pinoy oils. Your lola used it for everything: cooking, moisturizing your hair, treating skin problems, and even as a general-purpose *haplas*. Now, it's globally famous as "virgin coconut oil" and costs 5x more in health stores. We've been on that trend since the 1800s.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas masarap daw magluto ng pritong isda gamit ang **langis ng niyog**.","translation":"They say it's more delicious to cook fried fish using **coconut oil**."},{"sentence":"Nagpapahid siya ng **langis ng niyog** sa buhok para kuminis.","translation":"She applies **coconut oil** to her hair to make it smooth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang kontrolin ang sariling damdamin, pagnanasa, o kilos; pagtitimpi at pag-iingat sa pagpapasya.
etymology: Likely a compound of 'hunos' (control, change) and 'dili' (mind, self, consciousness).
original_explanation: This is your ability not to splurge your entire sahod on 12.12 sales. It's what stops you from replying to that toxic ex's 'miss u' text at 2 AM. It's having the self-control to say 'no' to a third serving of lechon. A very rare superpower in this day and age.
usage_notes: A very formal and deep word, often found in literary or religious texts. The more common, everyday term is 'pagpipigil sa sarili'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakailangan ang matinding **paghuhunusdili** upang malampasan ang mga tukso sa buhay.","translation":"Great **self-control** is needed to overcome life's temptations."},{"sentence":"Ipinamalas ng lider ang kanyang **paghuhunusdili** sa gitna ng krisis.","translation":"The leader showed his **prudence** in the midst of the crisis."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kristalinang mineral na binubuo ng sodium chloride (NaCl), ginagamit bilang pampalasa at preserbatibo sa pagkain.
original_explanation: The OG pampalasa. The one thing you can't live without in the kitchen, unless you're on a low-sodium diet. It's the reason why dried fish exists and why fries are life. Also, what you feel when you're being 'maalat' or unlucky in a game.
usage_notes: A fundamental cooking ingredient.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakidagdagan ng kaunting **asin** ang adobo.","translation":"Please add a little **salt** to the adobo."},{"sentence":"Ang **asin** ay mahalaga sa pag-iimbak ng pagkain noong unang panahon.","translation":"**Salt** was important for preserving food in the old days."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay ng detalye o dahilan upang maging malinaw at maunawaan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: "Let me explain..." This is what you say when your mom finds your online shopping receipts, or when your boss asks why you're late. It's the act of trying to make sense of a situation, whether you're guilty or not. From teachers explaining lessons to you explaining your life choices.
usage_notes: The root 'liwanag' means 'light', so 'nagpapaliwanag' literally means 'making something light' or 'shedding light on' a topic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpapaliwanag** ang guro tungkol sa bagong aralin.","translation":"The teacher is **explaining** the new lesson."},{"sentence":"Mahirap paniwalaan kahit **nagpapaliwanag** na siya nang paulit-ulit.","translation":"It's hard to believe even if he is **explaining** over and over again."}]

translation: to lift something for someone; to raise a hand against someone
meaning_filipino: Itaas ang isang bagay para sa kapakanan ng iba; o, bilang idyoma, manakit o pagtaasan ng kamay ang isang tao.
original_explanation: This word is a drama queen. On one hand, it's the helpful act of lifting a heavy grocery bag for your lola. On the other hand, it's the ultimate telenovela moment: 'Huwag mo akong pagbubuhatan ng kamay!' (Don't you dare raise a hand against me!). It's all about context: helping hand or hurting hand?
usage_notes: The phrase 'pagbuhatan ng kamay' is a very common and strong idiom for physical abuse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailanman ay hindi ko siya **pagbubuhatan** ng kamay.","translation":"I will never **raise a hand against** him/her."},{"sentence":"Paki-**pagbuhatan** mo naman ako ng mga kahon na ito.","translation":"Can you please **lift** these boxes **for** me."}]

translation: in various places; in different locations
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa maraming at magkakaibang pook o lokasyon.
etymology: Mula sa "sa" (in/at) + "iba't ibang" (marami at magkakaiba, pinaikling "iba at iba na") + "lugal" (pook).
original_explanation: Your travel blogger friend's favorite caption. It's the status of your online orders from different sellers on Lazada or Shopee. It's also where you can find branches of Jollibee, not just in the Philippines but all over the world.
usage_notes: Ang pariralang "iba't iba" ay isang pangkaraniwang konstruksyon na nangangahulugang "various" o "different kinds of".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtinda siya ng kakanin **sa iba't ibang lugal** sa bayan.","translation":"She sold rice cakes **in various places** in town."},{"sentence":"Makikita ang magagandang tanawin **sa iba't ibang lugal** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Beautiful sceneries can be seen **in different locations** in the Philippines."}]
related: ["kung saan-saan","sa lahat ng dako","sa iba't ibang panig"]

translation: to bow; to bend down (the head)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbaba o pagbaluktot ng isang bahagi ng katawan, karaniwan ay ang ulo, bilang tanda ng paggalang, kalungkutan, pag-iisip, o pagsunod.
original_explanation: That action you do when you pass in front of elders ('mano po'). Or when you're trying to avoid eye contact with a prof who's about to call you for recitation. Or that 'walk of shame' when you mess up the presentation and have to go back to your seat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iyuko** mo ang iyong ulo bilang paggalang sa watawat.","translation":"**Bow** your head as a sign of respect for the flag."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **iyuko** ang iyong noo; harapin mo ang problema.","translation":"Don't **bow** your head; face the problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Labis na pagod at hirap sa paghinga dahil sa matinding gawain, pagtakbo, o karamdaman.
etymology: Reduplication of 'hapo' (fatigue, panting) to denote intensity.
original_explanation: This is you after climbing five flights of stairs because the LRT elevator is broken again. Or your brain cells after a whole day of meetings that could've been an email. You're not just tired, you're *pagoda tragedy* level tired, gasping for air and questioning your life choices.
usage_notes: The reduplication 'hapung-hapo' is much more intense than simply being 'hapo' (fatigued) or 'pagod' (tired). It specifically implies being out of breath.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hapung-hapo** ang manlalaro matapos ang limang set ng tennis.","translation":"The player was **exhausted** after five sets of tennis."},{"sentence":"Dumating siyang **hapung-hapo** sa opisina dahil hinabol niya ang bus.","translation":"He arrived at the office **breathless** because he chased the bus."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mahigpit na community quarantine kung saan ipinagbabawal ang paglabas ng bahay maliban sa mga awtorisadong tao o para sa mahahalagang gawain, ipinatupad upang pigilan ang pagkalat ng isang sakit tulad ng COVID-19.
etymology: Akronim mula sa Ingles na "Enhanced Community Quarantine".
original_explanation: The collective trauma of 2020. The era of Dalgona coffee, TikTok dances, online shopping sprees, and endless Zoom meetings. It's when 'Ayuda' became a love language and 'Quarantine Pass' was the most powerful ID you could possess. We all became homebakers and plantitos/plantitas during ECQ.
usage_notes: Naging pang-araw-araw na salita noong kasagsagan ng pandemya ng COVID-19 sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong panahon ng **ECQ**, natuto akong magluto ng iba't ibang ulam.","translation":"During the **ECQ** period, I learned to cook different dishes."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit na ipinagbawal ang pagtitipon-tipon sa ilalim ng **ECQ**.","translation":"Gatherings were strictly prohibited under the **Enhanced Community Quarantine**."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na ginagamit upang pasiklabin o palakasin ang apoy. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay tumutukoy sa bagay na nagpapasidhi ng damdamin gaya ng pag-ibig, galit, o sigasig.
original_explanation: Literally, this is your lighter fluid. But figuratively? It's that one 'chismis' that starts family drama. It's the 'kilig' scene in a teleserye that makes you ship the love team harder. It's the motivational speech that finally gets you to the gym. It's anything that turns a small spark into a raging fire, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Frequently used metaphorically to refer to strong emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga salita ay nagsilbing **pampaalab** ng galit ng mga tao.","translation":"His words served as an **inciter** of the people's anger."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng tuyong dahon para gawing **pampaalab** sa siga.","translation":"He was looking for dry leaves to use as **kindling** for the bonfire."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na binubuo ng maliliit at hiwa-hiwalay na butil o grano.
etymology: Nagmula sa pag-uulit ng salitang 'butil' (grain) upang ilarawan ang katangian ng pagiging binubuo ng mga butil.
original_explanation: Describes a texture, like sand, sugar, or un-fluffy rice (kaning-lamig). It's made of tiny grains. Can also describe how something appears, like beads of sweat ('butil-butil na pawis'). Parang 'yung pag-iipon mo, butil-butil... pa-barya barya lang.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the texture of food like rice, or physical phenomena like sweat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Butil-butil** ang pawis sa kanyang noo dahil sa matinding pagod.","translation":"Sweat formed in **beads** on his forehead due to extreme exhaustion."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang kanin kapag ito ay **butil-butil** at hindi malagkit.","translation":"Rice is delicious when it is **grainy** and not sticky."}]

meaning_filipino: May lasang gaya ng sa apdo o ampalaya; tumutukoy din sa isang masakit, malungkot, o hindi kaaya-ayang karanasan.
original_explanation: Like your ex. Or ampalaya. Or the coffee you made with too much grounds and not enough sugar. It's the taste of unsweetened dark chocolate and regret. Can also describe a painful memory, a harsh truth, or any 'hugot' moment that leaves a bad taste in your soul.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for taste or figuratively for emotions and experiences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mapait** man ang katotohanan, kailangan mo itong harapin.","translation":"Even if the truth is **bitter**, you need to face it."}]

translation: Lord; Master; a revered religious icon
meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para sa Panginoon o Diyos; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang pinipitagan na imahen o estatwa ng isang santo o ni Hesus.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *puqun meaning 'base of a tree, source, origin, ancestor, lord'.
original_explanation: This word has big 'master' energy. It's used to refer to God ('Panginoon') or a revered religious statue, like the Black Nazarene (Poon na Itim na Nazareno). It carries a deep sense of devotion and reverence. Think of the frenzied but faithful crowds during the Nazareno feast—that's Poon-level devotion.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in a religious context. Capitalized when referring to God or a specific revered icon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinadagsa ng mga deboto ang prusisyon ng **Poon** na Itim na Nazareno.","translation":"Devotees flock to the procession of the **Lord** Black Nazarene."},{"sentence":"Nag-alay sila ng panalangin sa harap ng **Poon**.","translation":"They offered a prayer in front of the **revered icon**."}]

translation: to take a large bite; to gouge out
meaning_filipino: Kumuha ng malaking subo o piraso sa pamamagitan ng bibig; tumuklap o bumakbak ng isang bahagi.
original_explanation: This is that monster bite you take from a Jollibee Chickenjoy leg when you haven't eaten all day. It can also mean when a chunk of a road suddenly collapses. "Bes, dahan-dahan sa pagkain, baka umukab ka ng buong plato!"
usage_notes: Often used hyperbolically to describe someone eating voraciously or a chunk being taken out of something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gutom na gutom ang aso kaya **umukab** ito nang malaki sa tinapay.","translation":"The dog was so hungry it **took a huge bite** out of the bread."},{"sentence":"**Umukab** ang isang malaking bahagi ng lupa sa gilid ng bundok.","translation":"A large chunk of earth **was gouged out** from the mountainside."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daglat para sa "Year 2000." Tumutukoy ito sa panahon sa pagpasok ng ika-21 siglo, at partikular sa pangamba sa "Y2K bug" kung saan maaaring magkaroon ng malawakang pagpalya ang mga computer system.
etymology: Daglat mula sa pariralang Ingles na "Year 2000", kung saan ang "K" ay kumakatawan sa "kilo" o sanlibo.
original_explanation: The OG "end of the world" party na hindi natuloy. Akala ng lahat, mag-shu-shutdown ang mga bangko, eroplano, at pati toaster mo dahil sa computer bug. Now? It's a whole aesthetic: low-rise jeans, butterfly clips, metallic outfits, at a general vibe of futuristic optimism. "Girl, ang outfit mo today, very Y2K!"
usage_notes: Ngayon ay mas karaniwang ginagamit bilang pang-uri upang ilarawan ang fashion, musika, at kultura mula sa huling bahagi ng 1990s at unang bahagi ng 2000s.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naaalala ko pa ang takot ng mga tao noong papalapit ang **Y2K**.","translation":"I still remember people's fear as **Y2K** was approaching."},{"sentence":"Ang pormahan niya ay parang bumalik sa panahon ng **Y2K**.","translation":"Her style is like a throwback to the **Y2K** era."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na sumusunod sa mga utos, alituntunin, o payo nang walang pagtutol.
etymology: ma- (adjective-forming prefix) + sunod (follow, obey) + -in (suffix indicating propensity)
original_explanation: The ideal 'panganay' or 'bunso' according to Filipino parents. The employee who says "Yes, sir!" and actually does the work. This is the kid who doesn't need to be told twice to buy suka from the sari-sari store. The opposite of 'pasaway'.
usage_notes: A positive trait, highly valued in Filipino culture, especially in children and subordinates.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang **masunurin** na anak at laging nakikinig sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"She is an **obedient** child and always listens to her parents."},{"sentence":"Maging **masunurin** sa batas trapiko upang makaiwas sa aksidente.","translation":"Be **compliant** with traffic laws to avoid accidents."}]

translation: to make or sell wooden clogs
meaning_filipino: Gumawa o magtinda ng bakya, isang uri ng tradisyonal na sapin sa paa na yari sa kahoy.
original_explanation: To be a craftsman of classic Filipino footwear. Before Crocs and Havaianas, there was the mighty bakya. This person keeps that iconic click-clacking tradition alive, one wooden shoe at a time.
usage_notes: Refers to the occupation or act of being a 'bakya' maker or vendor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa Laguna, may mga pamilyang daan-daang taon nang **nagbabakya**.","translation":"In Laguna, there are families who have been **making wooden clogs** for hundreds of years."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado ng pagkainis, pagkabugnot, o pagka-aburido dahil sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The feeling when your internet drops during a crucial online meeting, or when someone chews with their mouth open. It's that low-key pikon level before you go full Hulk mode. The 'Ay, ka-beastmode!' starter pack.
usage_notes: Often used in its verb form 'naiirita' (is being irritated) or 'nakakairita' (is irritating). The adjective 'irita' is more direct and informal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Irita** na ako sa paulit-ulit mong tanong.","translation":"I'm **irritated** with your repetitive questions."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, **irita** na ang boss.","translation":"Don't be noisy, the boss is already **annoyed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging maputla o mapusyaw ng isang kulay.
original_explanation: This is the color of your officemate's face on a Monday morning before their first cup of coffee. It's also the shade of your favorite shirt after you accidentally washed it with bleach. Not quite white, just a sad, faded version of its former self.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the quality of being pale or light in color, not necessarily in brightness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makikita ang **kapusyawan** sa kaniyang mga labi dahil sa takot.","translation":"The **paleness** of his lips could be seen due to fear."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko gusto ang **kapusyawan** ng pinturang ito para sa dingding.","translation":"I don't like the **lightness** of this paint for the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng regular na trabahong pinagkakakitaan; isang gawain o posisyon sa isang kumpanya.
original_explanation: This is the elusive treasure everyone's searching for after graduation. It's your 'work', your 'racket', your '9-to-5'—the reason you have to wake up early on a Monday. Having a good **empleyo** means you can finally afford your milk tea addiction and contribute to the family budget.
usage_notes: More formal than 'trabaho'. Often used in news reports or official documents regarding labor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap maghanap ng **empleyo** sa panahon ngayon.","translation":"It's hard to find **employment** nowadays."},{"sentence":"Ang gobyerno ay nangako na lilikha ng mas maraming **empleyo**.","translation":"The government promised to create more **jobs**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mababaw na sugat sa balat na sanhi ng pagkakagasgas sa isang magaspang na bagay.
original_explanation: That little scratch you get from your friend's cat who's not in the mood, or from a rogue zipper, or when you accidentally scrape against a concrete wall while trying to avoid traffic. It's not a deep cut, just a 'battle scar' from everyday life. It stings when you put alcohol on it.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'gasgas' or 'kalmot', but 'kalmot' is specifically from an animal's claw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **galmos** ang braso ng bata pagkatapos maglaro sa labas.","translation":"The child's arm was full of **scratches** after playing outside."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ako ng **galmos** sa binti dahil sa pusa.","translation":"I got a **scratch** on my leg because of the cat."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lalaking tumatayong pangalawang magulang at gabay sa isang batang binibinyagan, kinukumpilan, o ikinakasal.
etymology: From Spanish 'padrino' (godfather), with the '-ng' honorific possibly influenced by Chinese kinship terms.
original_explanation: Your designated gift-giver every Christmas and birthday. In Filipino culture, a 'ninong' is a godfather, a sponsor in baptism, confirmation, or marriage. They are expected to be a spiritual guide, but for most kids, they are the reliable source of 'aguinaldo' (Christmas cash). Choosing a 'ninong' is a strategic move for parents, hoping to secure a good connection for their child.
usage_notes: The female counterpart is 'ninang' (godmother). The child they sponsor is called an 'inaanak' (godchild).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta kami sa bahay ng **ninong** ko para magmano at humingi ng aguinaldo.","translation":"We're going to my **godfather's** house to show respect (by placing his hand on our forehead) and ask for a Christmas gift."},{"sentence":"Si Mayor ang kinuha nilang **ninong** sa kasal.","translation":"They chose the Mayor to be their wedding **godfather** (sponsor)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mabilis at malakas na pagpalo sa mukha gamit ang bukas na palad.
original_explanation: The classic Pinoy telenovela confrontation move. Before the hair-pulling, there's the 'sampal'. It’s that shocking, stinging rebuke that says, 'How dare you?!'. The sound it makes is the unofficial soundtrack of betrayal.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin sa paraang matalinhaga, tulad ng 'sampal ng katotohanan' (slap of reality).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malutong na **sampal** ang dumapo sa kanyang pisngi.","translation":"A crisp **slap** landed on her cheek."},{"sentence":"Ang pagbagsak niya sa pagsusulit ay tila isang **sampal** sa kanyang pagmamataas.","translation":"Failing the exam felt like a **slap** to his pride."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkaramdam ng kasiyahan, galak, o kagalakan dahil sa isang pangyayari, bagay, o tao.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *lugud, na nangangahulugang 'pag-ibig, pagmamahal'.
original_explanation: This is that "I'm so proud of you, anak!" feeling your parents get when you finally graduate. It's a more formal, deep kind of happiness. It's not just "masaya," it's "delighted." Like when your crush finally views your IG story. 'Yan, 'yan ang pure lugod.
usage_notes: Kadalasang nagpapahiwatig ng kasiyahan o malalim na kagalakan. Mas pormal kaysa sa 'masaya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nalulugod** akong ipaalam sa inyo na kayo ang nanalo sa patimpalak.","translation":"I am **pleased** to inform you that you have won the competition."},{"sentence":"**Nalulugod** ang mga magulang sa matataas na marka ng kanilang anak.","translation":"The parents are **delighted** with their child's high grades."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis ng dumi, alikabok, o anumang nakakapit sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng malakas na pag-uga o pagwagwag nito.
original_explanation: What you do to a rug before bringing it inside. Also what you do to your ex's memories. Charot! Just shake it off, 'ika nga ni Taylor Swift. "Ipayagpag mo 'yang basahan sa labas, huwag dito sa loob."
usage_notes: Often used for fabric, mats, or any flexible object that can be shaken to remove loose particles. A synonym is 'ipagpag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipayagpag** mo muna ang tuwalya bago isampay.","translation":"**Shake off** the towel first before hanging it to dry."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong dito **ipayagpag** ang maalikabok na panyo.","translation":"Don't **shake off** the dusty handkerchief here."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta sa iba't ibang lugar, malapit man o malayo, para sa iba't ibang layunin tulad ng paglilibang, pag-aaral, o trabaho.
original_explanation: The official verb for your #TravelGoals. Whether you're going on a weekend getaway to La Union or backpacking across Southeast Asia, you're "naglalakbay". It's the act of exploring places beyond your usual tambayan.
usage_notes: A general term for traveling. Its future tense is `maglalakbay`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap kong **maglakbay** sa buong mundo balang araw.","translation":"It's my dream **to travel** the whole world someday."},{"sentence":"Nais nilang **maglakbay** patungong Batanes sa susunod na taon.","translation":"They want **to travel** to Batanes next year."}]

translation: something used for closing; lock; cover
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, kasangkapan, o mekanismo na ginagamit upang isara ang isang butas, daanan, o lalagyan.
etymology: From Spanish 'cerrar' (to close) via Filipino 'sara', and the prefix 'pan-' (instrument for).
original_explanation: This is your 'closure' device. It can be the zipper on your jeans, the takip on your Tupperware, or the padlock on your gate para di makapasok ang mga magnanakaw (o yung manliligaw na ayaw mo). Metaphorically, ito yung 'move on' button mo sa isang ex, the final block on social media. The end. Fin. Sarado na.
usage_notes: A general term. Can be a lock (kandado), a lid (takip), a zipper (siper), etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **pansara** ng bote.","translation":"The **cover** for the bottle is missing."},{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng bagong **pansara** para sa pinto.","translation":"Buy a new **lock** for the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nakaayos o nakabuklad sa isang patag na ibabaw.
original_explanation: This is how you find the banig (mat) or the picnic blanket at the park. It's also the state of your life plans before reality hits and messes everything up. 'Nakalalatag na sana ang lahat, bigla siyang nag-chat.'
usage_notes: Often used for things like mats, blankets, plans, or items for sale.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakalalatag** na ang mga paninda sa palengke pagsikat pa lang ng araw.","translation":"The goods are already **laid out** in the market as soon as the sun rises."},{"sentence":"Malinaw na **nakalatag** sa kontrata ang lahat ng tuntunin.","translation":"All the rules are clearly **laid out** in the contract."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nahaluan ng anumang ibang sangkap, bagay, o impluwensya; dalisay.
original_explanation: Like your *kape* (coffee) without sugar or creamer—just pure, bitter truth. Or chismis that comes straight from the source, no edits, no additions. It's the "100% pure" label on a product. Can also describe intentions—goodwill with no strings attached. It's the opposite of halo-halo.
usage_notes: Used for substances (e.g., pure gold, pure juice) and abstract concepts (e.g., pure intention).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sabi sa bote, ito raw ay **walang-halo** na katas ng prutas.","translation":"The bottle says this is **unmixed** fruit extract."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pagtulong ay **walang-halo** na pagkukusa.","translation":"His help was of **pure** initiative."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinuno o tagapamahala ng isang tanggapan ng koreo.
original_explanation: The OG "padala" master. Before LBC, J&T, and Shopee Express, siya ang boss ng lahat ng sulat at package. Kung may hinahanap kang lumang love letter mula kay Lolo, siya ang tatanungin mo. Sila ang gatekeeper ng snail mail.
usage_notes: Isang opisyal na titulo ng trabaho, ngunit hindi na gaanong karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan dahil sa pagbaba ng paggamit ng tradisyonal na koreo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinausap ng alkalde ang **posmaster** tungkol sa pagpapabuti ng serbisyo ng koreo sa bayan.","translation":"The mayor spoke with the **postmaster** about improving the town's postal service."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangalawang suliranin o sitwasyon na nagpapahirap sa isang umiiral nang problema; isang di-inaasahang sagabal.
original_explanation: Ito yung biglang pagdating ng ex mo sa party kung saan kasama mo ang bago mo. O sa medical terms, yung 'good for 2-3 days' na lagnat mo na naging pneumonia. Yan ang komplikasyon.
usage_notes: Often used in both medical and general contexts to describe an additional problem.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **komplikasyon** ang kanyang operasyon.","translation":"His surgery had a **complication**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkawala ng ebidensya ay isang malaking **komplikasyon** sa kaso.","translation":"The loss of evidence is a major **complication** in the case."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kakulangan, kamalian, o hindi pagtupad sa inaasahan o sa tungkulin.
etymology: From `pag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of `kulang`.
original_explanation: This is the main character in every Filipino teleserye family drama. "Nagkulang ba ako bilang ina?" It's that feeling when your data runs out before payday, or when your contribution to the group project wasn't enough. It's the gap between "sana all" and "what you actually got."
usage_notes: Carries a sense of failure to meet an obligation or expectation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inamin niya ang kanyang **pagkukulang** sa pamilya.","translation":"He admitted his **shortcomings** towards his family."},{"sentence":"Anuman ang **pagkukulang** ng proyekto, kailangan nating solusyunan.","translation":"Whatever the project's **deficiency** is, we need to solve it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking dayuhan na hindi mamamayan ng bansang kanyang kinaroroonan.
original_explanation: He's the male tourist you try to overcharge at the palengke (just kidding... or are we?), or the expat who has surprisingly mastered the art of karaoke. A man from a foreign land.
usage_notes: Ito ang panlalaking anyo ng "ekstranghera".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **ekstranghero** ang nagtanong sa akin ng direksiyon papuntang estasyon ng tren.","translation":"A male **foreigner** asked me for directions to the train station."},{"sentence":"Nagtatrabaho bilang guro ng Ingles ang **ekstranghero** sa aming komunidad.","translation":"The male **foreigner** works as an English teacher in our community."}]

translation: to use as a pretext; to use as a chopping board
meaning_filipino: Sa literal na kahulugan, ang paggamit ng sangkalan bilang patungan sa paghiwa. Sa metaporikal na kahulugan, ang paggamit ng isang tao o dahilan bilang panakip-butas upang maisakatuparan ang isang hangarin.
original_explanation: The literal meaning is what your mom does with a chopping board before making sinigang. The figurative meaning is the juicy part: when you use someone or something as an excuse. 'Ginawa mo lang akong sangkalan para makalabas ka!' (You just used me as an excuse so you could go out!). Classic 'palusot' move.
usage_notes: Has two distinct meanings. The context usually makes it clear whether it's literal (kitchen) or figurative (making excuses). The figurative use often carries a negative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **sangkalanin** sa iyong mga kalokohan.","translation":"Don't **use me as a pretext** for your foolishness."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magsangkalan** ng bawang at sibuyas para sa gisa.","translation":"I need to **use a chopping board** for the garlic and onions for the stir-fry."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang karangalan, puri, at paggalang sa sarili na inaalagaan at hindi dapat yurakan.
etymology: A root word central to Filipino moral and social values.
original_explanation: This is your self-respect, your integrity, your 'face'. It's that thing you refuse to compromise, even for a better job or a jowa. It's why you pay your debts, keep your promises, and don't post cringe stuff online. "Mas mahalaga ang **dangal** kaysa pera." It's the core of your character, the reason you can look at yourself in the mirror. A very big deal in Filipino culture.
usage_notes: 'Karangalan' is a close synonym, but 'dangal' often refers more to innate, internal honor, while 'karangalan' can also refer to honors or awards received from others.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinaglaban niya ang kanyang **dangal** hanggang sa huli.","translation":"He fought for his **honor** until the end."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging tapat ay tanda ng malaking **dangal**.","translation":"Being honest is a sign of great **dignity**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng espasyo o pagkakataon sa iba; pag-urong upang makadaan o makapuwesto ang iba.
original_explanation: Literally 'give place.' It's what you do in traffic when you let another car merge. It's also what you do in an argument when you concede a point to keep the peace. Sa office, ito yung pag-step aside para ma-promote yung junior mo kasi alam mong deserve niya. It's about accommodation and not being a 'bida-bida' all the time.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa parehong literal (espasyo) at metaporikal (pagkakataon) na kahulugan. Madalas gamitin sa anyong pandiwa ('magbigay-lugar').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-**bigay-lugar** sa opinyon ng iba ay tanda ng pagiging bukas-isip.","translation":"**Accommodating** the opinions of others is a sign of being open-minded."},{"sentence":"Mag-**bigay-lugar** ka sa mga sasakyang galing sa kanan.","translation":"**Give way** to vehicles coming from the right."}]

translation: to lose courage, to be discouraged
meaning_filipino: Maranasan ang pagkawala ng tapang, sigasig, o pag-asa na harapin ang isang pagsubok o sitwasyon.
etymology: A phrase composed of 'panghinaan' (from 'hina', weak) and 'ng loob' (of the inner self/will). Literally, 'to be weakened of inner spirit'.
original_explanation: This is when your inner fighting spirit suddenly logs off. It's the feeling you get when you see 500 unread emails on a Monday morning, or when your crush posts a "happily in a relationship" status. It's your motivation bar hitting zero.
