usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaong ang malaking barko sa **puwerto** ng Maynila.","translation":"The large ship docked at the **port** of Manila."},{"sentence":"Maraming kalakal ang dumadaan sa **puwerto** araw-araw.","translation":"A lot of goods pass through the **port** every day."}]

translation: to return to (someone/something); to get back together with
meaning_filipino: Puntahan muli ang isang lugar, tao, o bagay; muling ipagpatuloy ang isang relasyon o gawain.
etymology: Mula sa 'balik' (return) + hulaping '-an' na nagpapahiwatig ng lokasyon o tatanggap ng kilos.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'Marupok 101' move. Ito yung pag-accept mo ulit sa friend request ng ex mo, tapos a few weeks later, 'in a relationship' na ulit kayo. Pwede ring literal, like 'balikan mo yung naiwan mong payong.' Pero aminin, mas madalas itong gamitin sa love life. 'Huwag mo na siyang balikan!'
usage_notes: Ang layon ng 'balikan' ay ang tao, lugar, o bagay na binabalikan. Mayroon itong malakas na konotasyon ng pakikipagbalikan sa dating kasintahan sa kolokyal na paggamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **balikan** ang kanyang dating kasintahan.","translation":"She decided to **get back together with** her former boyfriend."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **balikan** ang mga aralin mula noong Lunes.","translation":"We need to **go back to** the lessons from Monday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha o pagdampot ng isang bagay mula sa sahig, lupa, o anumang mababang lugar.
original_explanation: The 5-second rule in action. When you drop your food and you have to decide if it's still good to eat. That action of grabbing it from the floor? That's 'pumulot'. Also what you do when you see a 100-peso bill on the sidewalk.
usage_notes: Specifically for picking things up from a lower surface.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang nalaglag na pitaka at agad itong **pumulot**.","translation":"He saw the fallen wallet and immediately **picked it up**."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan ang mga bata na **pumulot** ng kanilang mga kalat pagkatapos maglaro.","translation":"The children were taught to **pick up** their mess after playing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kakayahang mamitas, pumulot, o mangolekta ng mga bunga ng pananim. Sa metaporikal na antas, ito ay tumutukoy sa pagtanggap ng resulta ng isang gawain.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what farmers do during harvest season. Figuratively, it's you 'reaping what you sow.' Nag-aral ka mabuti? You'll harvest good grades. Nag-invest ka sa crypto? Hopefully, you'll harvest profits and not luha. It's the result of your pagtatanim (planting/effort).
usage_notes: The 'nakaa-' prefix indicates an ability to perform the action of the root word. 'Nakaaani' means 'is able to harvest'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas ay **nakaaani** na kami ng saganang bigas mula sa aming bukirin.","translation":"Finally, we **are able to harvest** an abundance of rice from our field."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang labis na pag-iisip o pagsusuri sa isang bagay, kadalasan hanggang sa puntong ito ay nagdudulot na ng pagkabalisa o pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: The national sport of anyone who has ever received a "K." or a seen-zone message. It's when you analyze a simple situation until you've written a 10-part teleserye in your head, complete with villains and a dramatic climax. "Nag-overthink na naman ako" is the battle cry of the anxious and the "marupok." The phrase "overthink malala" means to overthink severely.
usage_notes: A very common Taglish verb. It can be conjugated using Filipino affixes: nag-overthink (past), nag-o-overthink (present), mag-o-overthink (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo masyadong **i-overthink** 'yung sinabi niya.","translation":"Don't **overthink** what he said too much."},{"sentence":"Gabi-gabi akong nag-o-**overthink** kung tama ba ang mga desisyon ko sa buhay.","translation":"Every night I **overthink** whether I'm making the right decisions in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nasa bingit ng kapahamakan, sakuna, o pinsala.
original_explanation: This is that "May ahas!" feeling you get when your significant other says "We need to talk." It's the state of being in deep trouble, whether it's facing a deadline you forgot or realizing you left your wallet at home after a big dinner. It's the official emotion of "lagot."
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of physical danger, financial risk, or relational jeopardy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **panganganib** ang buhay ng mga naiwan sa gumuhong gusali.","translation":"The lives of those left in the collapsed building are in **danger**."},{"sentence":"Ang labis na pag-utang ay naglalagay sa iyong kinabukasan sa **panganganib**.","translation":"Excessive borrowing puts your future at **risk**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinong pulbos na gawa sa sinunog na pinaghalong luwad at apog, na kapag binasa ay tumitigas at nagsisilbing pandikit sa mga bato at buhangin upang makagawa ng mortar o kongkreto.
original_explanation: The magic powder that holds the Philippines together, literally. From skyscrapers in BGC to the DIY extension of your tita's house. Pag may nakita kang construction worker na parang a-absent sa class picture dahil sa puti-puti sa mukha, malamang semento ang dahilan. The foundation of every Filipino dream house... and every unfinished road project.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating bumili ng sampung sako ng **semento** para sa pader.","translation":"We need to buy ten bags of **cement** for the wall."},{"sentence":"Nagkamali ng timpla ng **semento** kaya hindi masyadong matibay ang pagkakagawa.","translation":"The **cement** mixture was wrong, so the construction isn't very sturdy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging malaya, may sariling pamamahala, at hindi napapasailalim sa kapangyarihan o kontrol ng iba.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "I'm my own boss" status, but for a country. It's the reason we have a holiday on June 12. It’s about having your own flag, your own government, and your own problems to solve. On a personal level, it's that feeling when you finally move out of your parents' house and pay your own bills. Freedom! (with responsibilities).
usage_notes: A very formal and patriotic word, often used in historical and political contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang natin ang Araw ng **Kasarinlan** tuwing ika-12 ng Hunyo.","translation":"We celebrate **Independence** Day every 12th of June."},{"sentence":"Ang **kasarinlan** ng isang bansa ay sagrado at dapat ipagtanggol.","translation":"A nation's **sovereignty** is sacred and must be defended."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng batong sedimentaryo na mayaman sa kerogen, isang organikong materyal na maaaring gawing langis o krudo sa pamamagitan ng pag-init.
original_explanation: The rock that's full of potential... and oil. It's not liquid gold yet, but with enough pressure and heat, it can be. Think of it as a pre-paid card for gasoline; the value is locked inside. It's the geological equivalent of 'mayaman 'to 'pag naproseso.'
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino na ginagamit sa heolohiya at sa sektor ng enerhiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga heologo kung paano kukuha ng enerhiya mula sa **batong-langis**.","translation":"Geologists are studying how to extract energy from **oil shale**."}]

translation: to find fault with; to point out mistakes
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpuna sa kamalian ng iba; ang paghahanap o pagtukoy ng mga mali sa isang gawa o sinabi.
original_explanation: This is being that person who's always correcting grammar, pointing out a tiny flaw in a project, or saying 'Actually...' in a conversation. It's the act of being a fault-finder. While it can be helpful, sometimes it just feels like nitpicking. 'Huwag mo akong **mamali**in sa harap ng maraming tao.' (Don't point out my mistakes in front of many people.)
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation of being overly critical. The object-focused form 'mamaliin' is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mamali** ng gawa ng iba pero ang sarili niyang trabaho ay hindi perpekto.","translation":"He loves to **find fault** in others' work but his own work isn't perfect."},{"sentence":"Sa halip na **mamali**, bakit hindi ka na lang tumulong?","translation":"Instead of **pointing out mistakes**, why don't you just help?"}]

translation: the gay community; all gay people (collectively)
meaning_filipino: Isang makabagong termino na tumutukoy sa kabuuan ng komunidad ng mga bakla o homoseksuwal, na para bang isang bansa o malaking pangkat.
etymology: Combination of "accla" and the English word "nation," creating a humorous and empowering term for the gay community. Popularized on social media.
original_explanation: Welcome to the Republic of the Acclas! This is the collective term for the entire gay community, imagined as a powerful, interconnected network. The "accla nation" is quick to mobilize online to support a cause, cancel a problematic celebrity, or collectively obsess over the latest BL series. They have their own language (bekimon), economy (supporting queer artists), and foreign policy (judging international pageant contestants).
usage_notes: Used online and in casual conversations to refer to the collective power, opinion, or presence of the gay community in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naku, 'wag mong kalabanin 'yan, malakas ang backer niyan sa **accla nation**.","translation":"Oh, don't pick a fight with them, they have strong backers in the **gay community**."},{"sentence":"The **accla nation** has spoken: MUPH crown for a deserving queen!","translation":"The **gay community** has spoken: MUPH crown for a deserving queen!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit o limitado na antas ng kaalaman, karunungan, o pag-unawa sa isang partikular na paksa.
etymology: Isang parirala na binubuo ng 'kaunti' (maliit na dami) at 'dunong' (kaalaman).
original_explanation: This is what you have after watching a 3-minute YouTube tutorial on how to fix a leaking faucet. It's the 'A little knowledge is a dangerous thing' concept. You know just enough to be confident, but not enough to actually be competent. 'May kaunting dunong ako sa Photoshop' means you know how to use the crop tool and maybe a filter.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of the proverb 'Ang kaunting dunong ay mapanganib' (A little knowledge is a dangerous thing). It can also be used humbly to describe one's own limited expertise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa pagbibigay ng payo kung **kaunting dunong** lang ang taglay.","translation":"Be careful in giving advice if you only possess **a little knowledge**."},{"sentence":"Kahit **kaunting dunong** sa pagluluto ay malaking tulong na.","translation":"Even **a little knowledge** in cooking is already a big help."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglilinis ng katawan gamit ang tubig at sabon sa hinaharap. Ito ay ang anyong pangkasalukuyan ng pandiwang 'ligo'.
etymology: ma- (verb prefix) + li- (future tense reduplication) + ligo (bath)
original_explanation: The standard Filipino excuse for not being able to answer a call or do a chore right away. 'Wait lang, maliligo ako.' It's the future tense, the promise of getting clean. The ultimate self-care promise you make to yourself after a long, sweaty day commuting.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb 'ligo' (to bathe). The other forms are 'naliligo' (present) and 'naligo' (past).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maliligo** ako pagdating ko sa bahay.","translation":"I **will take a bath** when I get home."},{"sentence":"Sino ang huling **maliligo**? Pakipatay ang ilaw sa banyo.","translation":"Who **will be the last one to bathe**? Please turn off the light in the bathroom."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang okupado; sukdulan ang pagiging marami ang ginagawa at walang panahon para sa iba.
etymology: Reduplication of 'abala' (busy) to intensify the meaning.
original_explanation: This is the 'ber' months version of 'abala'. It's not just busy, it's 'cannot-even-reply-to-your-chat' busy. This is you during finals week, or your mom preparing for Noche Buena, or any BPO agent during queueing.
usage_notes: An intensified form of 'abala' (busy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Abalang-abala** ang lahat sa paghahanda para sa pista.","translation":"Everyone is **very busy** preparing for the fiesta."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagdaragdag ng haba, saklaw, o itatagal ng isang bagay, panahon, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you ask for a deadline extension. It's also what happens to a meeting that should've been an email. You're basically stretching something out, whether it's time, a story, or your patience. 'Boss, pwedeng **magpalawig** ng break time?'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang guro na **magpalawig** ng oras para sa pagsusulit.","translation":"The teacher decided to **extend** the time for the exam."},{"sentence":"Huwag na nating **magpalawig** pa ng usapan; dumiretso na tayo sa punto.","translation":"Let's not **prolong** the conversation anymore; let's get straight to the point."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuwag o paglusaw sa isang grupo, organisasyon, o samahan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung nangyayari sa K-Pop group kapag nag-away-away na ang mga miyembro o 'di kaya'y nag-expire na ang kontrata. Parang 'yung tropa n'yo noong high school na nag-disband na rin kasi may mga jowa na at kanya-kanyang buhay. 'Walang forever,' sabi nga nila.
usage_notes: Used as a Taglish verb. Filipino speakers often use it directly. Conjugations like 'nag-disband' or 'mag-di-disband' are common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malungkot ang mga fans nang ianunsyo na mag-di-**disband** na ang kanilang paboritong banda.","translation":"The fans were sad when it was announced that their favorite band would **disband**."},{"sentence":"Nag-**disband** ang grupo namin sa thesis dahil sa hindi pagkakasundo.","translation":"Our thesis group **disbanded** due to disagreements."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na hayagang pumupuna, tumutuligsa, o kumokondena sa mga gawa, ideya, o kilos ng iba, lalo na sa mga usaping pampubliko o pampamahalaan.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'comment section warrior' but make it formal. Before social media, they wrote scathing editorials in newspapers. Today, they might be political analysts, activists, or even that one tito at family gatherings who has an opinion on EVERYTHING the government does. A manunuligsa is not just a basher; they often have well-reasoned (or at least, well-articulated) arguments. They are the designated watchdogs of society.
usage_notes: A formal term, often used in the context of politics, arts, or social commentary. Carries a strong sense of opposition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang matapang na **manunuligsa** ng katiwalian sa gobyerno.","translation":"He is known as a brave **critic** of corruption in the government."},{"sentence":"Maraming **manunuligsa** ang hindi sumang-ayon sa bagong patakaran.","translation":"Many **detractors** did not agree with the new policy."}]

meaning_filipino: Pilit na kumawala o umalpas mula sa pagkakatali, pagkakakapit, o anumang humihigpit.
original_explanation: This is the feeling of finally breaking free. Imagine escaping from your lola's super tight 'bless' hug, or more seriously, finally resigning from a toxic job. It's that moment of liberation when you manage to get out of a situation that's holding you back. Freedom!
usage_notes: Past tense of 'humagpos'. Refers to the act of struggling and succeeding in getting free.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humagpos** ang aso mula sa tali at tumakbo palayo.","translation":"The dog **broke free** from its leash and ran away."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **humagpos** sa pagkakahawak ng mga dumakip sa kanya.","translation":"He tried to **get loose** from the grip of his captors."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging sapilitan o ang paggamit ng dahas o impluwensya upang pilitin ang isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay laban sa kanyang kalooban.
original_explanation: That feeling when your boss 'volunteers' you for overtime on a Friday night. It's not *really* a choice, is it? You're doing it, but under duress. Yan ang pagkapuwersa. Parang napilitan ka lang.
usage_notes: The prefix 'pagka-' here denotes the state or manner of something happening, often involuntarily or suddenly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkapuwersa** sa kanya na umamin, hindi naging balido ang testimonya.","translation":"Because he was **forced** to confess, the testimony was not valid."},{"sentence":"Ramdam ang **pagkapuwersa** sa kanyang ngiti; halatang hindi siya masaya.","translation":"The **forced nature** of his smile was palpable; it was obvious he wasn't happy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang murang usbong o bagong sibol na bahagi ng isang halaman, tulad ng dahon o sanga.
original_explanation: The "newbie" of the plant world. It's that tiny green thing that gives you hope that the monggo seeds from your kid's science project will actually grow. It's a symbol of new beginnings, like when you see a new "suloy" of a relationship after being single for a long time. #SanaAllMaySuloy
usage_notes: Often used in a literal botanical sense, but can be used metaphorically for new ideas, hope, or beginnings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga bagong **suloy** na tumutubo sa puno ng mangga.","translation":"There are new **shoots** growing on the mango tree."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat **suloy** ay tanda ng bagong pag-asa.","translation":"Every **sprout** is a sign of new hope."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang propesyon ay ang pagbubuo at pag-aayos ng mga pahina ng isang aklat sa pamamagitan ng pagtahi o pagdikit upang maging isang buong libro.
original_explanation: The OG 'crafter'. Before everything was mass-produced, this was the person who literally stitched your stories together. Today, they're the artisans you find in small, cool shops who can fix your favorite but falling-apart novel or create a custom journal that's too beautiful to write in.
usage_notes: This is a very specific occupational term. `Tagatahi` alone means 'sewer' or 'tailor'. The phrase `ng aklat` is essential.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ko ang luma kong diksyonaryo sa isang **tagatahi ng aklat** upang kumpunihin.","translation":"I brought my old dictionary to a **bookbinder** to be repaired."},{"sentence":"Bihira na ngayon ang mga sanay na **tagatahi ng aklat**.","translation":"Skilled **bookbinders** are rare nowadays."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at ritmikong paggalaw o pag-ugoy, karaniwan ng mga braso, balakang, o ng buong katawan.
original_explanation: How you walk when you're feeling confident, like you're on a runway. Or the gentle swing of your arms while strolling in the park with your crush. It's the 'sashay' in 'sashay away'.
usage_notes: Often associated with a graceful or rhythmic movement. It's softer and more gentle than 'pag-indak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malamyos na **pag-imbay** ng kanyang mga kamay ay bahagi ng sayaw.","translation":"The gentle **swaying** of her hands is part of the dance."}]

translation: to pinch; to hold with tongs
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng daliri o anumang kasangkapan tulad ng tiyani upang mahigpit na hawakan o kurutin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: That feeling when your tita pinches your cheeks so hard you see stars. 'Ay, ang taba-taba ng pamangkin ko!' *sabay sipit*. Also, what you do to grab that last piece of lechon skin with tongs before your cousin gets it.
usage_notes: Often used for pinching with fingers or using tools like tongs or clips.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sipitin** mo nga 'yung yelo para sa juice.","translation":"Can you **get** the ice with the tongs for the juice."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sipitin** ang pisngi ng bata, masasaktan siya.","translation":"Don't **pinch** the child's cheek, you'll hurt him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mapanlinlang na anyo, kilos, o pananalita upang itago ang tunay na pagkatao, layunin, o damdamin.
etymology: From 'pabalat' (cover) + 'kayo' (you, plural/formal, but here likely a corruption or fusion referring to appearance). It is essentially a compound word.
original_explanation: Yung ngiti mo sa customer kahit 10 minutes na lang bago matapos ang shift mo at pagod na pagod ka na. 'Yung 'okay lang ako' mo sa kaibigan mo kahit hindi naman talaga. It's the mask you wear, the act you put on. It's your social game face.
usage_notes: Often used with the word 'lang' (pabalatkayo lang).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lahat ng kabaitan niya ay isang **pabalatkayo** lamang.","translation":"All of his/her kindness is just a **facade**."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang pagiging mahiyain bilang **pabalatkayo** sa kanyang tunay na intensyon.","translation":"He/She used shyness as a **disguise** for his/her true intentions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho o tungkulin ay magbuhat o magdala ng mga bagay, kargamento, o mensahe.
original_explanation: The designated 'human hanger' for your jacket and shopping bags at the mall. Or, more formally, the Lalamove or Grab driver who brings your online shopping haul. In a group project, they're the person assigned to bring the cartolina and pentel pen.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikaw ang **tagadala** ng ating mga gamit sa pag-akyat sa bundok.","translation":"You are the **carrier** of our things for the mountain climb."},{"sentence":"Ang **tagadala** ng masamang balita ay hindi kinagigiliwan.","translation":"The **bearer** of bad news is not well-liked."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng maingat at malalim na pag-iisip o pag-aaral sa isang paksa.
original_explanation: If 'pagninilay' is thinking about your life, 'pagnuynoy' is like trying to solve a puzzle in your head. It's more focused and analytical. Think of a detective piecing clues together or you trying to understand the ending of a Christopher Nolan film.
usage_notes: Often considered a more literary or profound term than 'pag-iisip'. The form 'pagnunuynoy' is a more classic or poetic variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagnuynoy** sa mga sinaunang kasulatan ay nangangailangan ng pasensya.","translation":"The **pondering** of ancient scriptures requires patience."},{"sentence":"Isinantabi niya ang lahat para sa **pagnuynoy** sa solusyon ng problema.","translation":"He set everything aside for **deep thought** on the problem's solution."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng interaksyon sa Twitter kung saan hinihiling ng isang user na i-retweet ang kanilang post upang mabuksan ang isang pribadong mensahe (DM) o makatanggap ng isang partikular na tugon o impormasyon.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'Retweet to Open'.
original_explanation: Stands for 'Retweet to Open.' This is the Twitter version of 'give me something to get something.' Usually used by fan accounts or roleplayers. They'll post something intriguing and say 'RTO for the tea' or 'RTO for the full pic.' It's a way to boost engagement, parang pa-raffle lang na ang premyo ay chismis.
usage_notes: Isang partikular na jargon sa Twitter, lalo na sa mga fandom at roleplaying communities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-post siya ng '**rto** for a surprise' para dumami ang followers niya.","translation":"She posted '**rto** for a surprise' to gain more followers."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa mga **rto** na 'yan, clickbait lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe those '**retweet to open**' posts, they're just clickbait."}]

meaning_filipino: Husto, wasto, o eksakto sa sukat, oras, o kalagayan; walang labis, walang kulang.
original_explanation: That "Goldilocks" moment. Not too hot, not too cold. Not too early, not too late. It's when your Grab car arrives the exact moment you step outside, or when the last piece of liempo is yours for the taking. Perfect timing!
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ipahayag ang perpektong oras o pagiging angkop. Maaari ring maging pang-uri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tamang-tama** ang dating mo, kakaluto lang ng hapunan.","translation":"Your arrival is **perfectly timed**, dinner was just cooked."},{"sentence":"Ang damit na ito ay **tamang-tama** sa akin, hindi masikip at hindi maluwag.","translation":"This dress is a **perfect** fit for me, not too tight and not too loose."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang pagkuha o pagbasag ng mga bato, graba, at iba pang katulad na materyales mula sa lupa o bundok. Lugar ng pagtitibag.
original_explanation: A place where mountains go to die so we can have gravel for our driveways and materials for our buildings. A tibagan is basically a rock quarry. It's dusty, noisy, and looks like a giant took a huge bite out of a hillside. It's the source of the materials that build our cities, but also a source of major environmental debates.
usage_notes: Often seen as 'tibagan ng bato' (stone quarry).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mapanganib ang trabaho sa **tibagan** ng bato.","translation":"The work at the stone **quarry** is dangerous."},{"sentence":"Maraming trak ang pumipila sa **tibagan** para kumuha ng graba.","translation":"Many trucks are lining up at the **quarry** to get gravel."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gamot na nasa anyong maliit, bilog, at solido na nilulunok.
original_explanation: Yung maliliit na bagay na kailangan mong inumin para gumaling. Minsan mahirap lunukin, parang pride. Ito yung Spanish-sounding na kapatid ng 'tableta'.
usage_notes: Isang mas lumang termino na hiram sa Espanyol. Ang mas karaniwang ginagamit ngayon ay 'tableta' o 'gamot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inireseta ng doktor ang mga **pildoras** na ito para sa kanyang sakit ng ulo.","translation":"The doctor prescribed these **pills** for her headache."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng markang ekis (X) sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'ekis'. This is the action of marking something with an 'X'. 'Yung teacher mo, "Ekisan n'yo ang mga maling spelling." Or in a more dramatic sense, "In-ekisan niya ang pangalan ko sa buhay niya." (She crossed my name out of her life.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**ekisan** ang lahat ng aytem na wala na sa stock.","translation":"Please **put an X-mark** on all the items that are out of stock."},{"sentence":"**Inekisan** ng guro ang aking sagot dahil kulang ito.","translation":"The teacher **put an X-mark** on my answer because it was incomplete."}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa 'independent.' Tumutukoy sa mga pelikula, musika, o anumang likhang-sining na ginawa sa labas ng malalaking komersyal na kumpanya o sistema.
original_explanation: Your go-to term for anything that's not mainstream. Indie films? 'Yung mga pelikulang mapapaisip ka ng malalim at hindi laging happy ending. Indie music? 'Yung banda na napanood mo sa isang maliit na bar sa Cubao X bago pa sila sumikat. It's the art that's made for art's sake, not just for profit.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of film (indie film), music (indie band), and games (indie games).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming magagandang **indie** film ang kalahok sa Cinemalaya ngayong taon.","translation":"There are many good **indie** films participating in Cinemalaya this year."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang makinig sa mga **indie** band sa Spotify.","translation":"She loves listening to **indie** bands on Spotify."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao, lalo na sa isang babae, na may matangkad at payat na pangangatawan ngunit may magandang hubog.
original_explanation: The body type that makes your lola say "Kain ka pa, ija, ang payat mo!" but makes everyone else on Instagram go #BodyGoals. It's not just skinny (payat); it's elegantly slender, like a beauty queen or a K-Pop idol. It’s the "effortlessly slim" look.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person's physique in a complimentary way. "Balingkinitan" is the more standard spelling, but this variant is also widely understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **balangkinitan** na dalaga ang nagwagi sa patimpalak.","translation":"A **slender** young woman won the competition."},{"sentence":"Hinahangaan niya ang **balangkinitan** na katawan ng mga mananayaw.","translation":"She admires the **svelte** bodies of the dancers."}]

translation: to persevere; to strive; to be persistent
meaning_filipino: Ang patuloy na pagsisikap na makamit ang isang layunin sa kabila ng mga hadlang o paghihirap.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "sige lang, laban lang!" verb. It's the OFWs working abroad, the students pulling all-nighters for their thesis, and anyone trying to survive Metro Manila traffic daily. To magpunyagi is to have the grit of a BPO agent on their 10th coffee during a night shift.
usage_notes: Carries a strong sense of determination and diligence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpunyagi** sa iyong pag-aaral upang makamit ang iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"You need to **persevere** in your studies to achieve your dreams."},{"sentence":"**Nagpunyagi** siyang itaguyod ang kanyang pamilya nang mag-isa.","translation":"She **strove** to support her family on her own."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mapaligiran nang husto ng mga kaaway o kalaban, na pumipigil sa pagpasok o paglabas sa isang lugar; mapalibutan.
original_explanation: Think of it as the ultimate "you're trapped" scenario. In history, it's when an army surrounds a castle. In modern life, it's when you're the only one in the office who knows how to fix the printer, and suddenly your cubicle is surrounded by desperate colleagues. You have been "makubkob".
usage_notes: A formal word, mostly used in historical, military, or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal na panahong **nakubkob** ng mga mananakop ang lumang siyudad.","translation":"The old city **was besieged** by invaders for a long time."},{"sentence":"Hindi nagtagal at **nakubkob** ng mga pulis ang pinagtataguan ng mga kriminal.","translation":"It wasn't long before the criminals' hideout **was surrounded** by the police."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magaan at maliit na motorsiklo na may plataporma para sa mga paa ng nagmamaneho.
original_explanation: Yung sasakyan na parang baby ng motor. Perfect pang-hatid-sundo sa jowa o pang-food delivery. Mas cute kaysa motor, mas mabilis kaysa bike. Pag may nakita kang naka-pastel color na ganito, for sure, aesthetic ang feed niyan sa IG.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa de-motor na scooter, hindi sa laruang tinutulak ng paa (kick scooter).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mabilis makarating sa opisina gamit ang **iskuter** dahil nakakalusot sa traffic.","translation":"It's faster to get to the office using a **scooter** because it can weave through traffic."},{"sentence":"Nag-iipon siya para makabili ng bagong **iskuter**.","translation":"He is saving up to buy a new **scooter**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay o bigkas para sa taksimetro; isang aparato na sumusukat sa bayarin sa taksi.
etymology: A variant spelling/pronunciation of English 'taximeter' or Tagalog 'taksimetro'.
original_explanation: This is the 'palengke' version of 'taksimetro'. It's what you'd actually hear someone say in a real conversation. Same device, different pronunciation, same anxiety when you see the numbers jump in traffic.
usage_notes: A common colloquial variant of 'taksimetro'. It is more frequently used in casual speech than the more formal 'taksimetro'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit parang ang bilis ng **taksimiter** mo, kuya?","translation":"Why does your **taximeter** seem so fast, sir?"},{"sentence":"Dapat may selyo ng gobyerno ang bawat **taksimiter**.","translation":"Every **taximeter** should have a government seal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sistema ng mga alituntunin, pamamaraan, at pormal na asal na sinusunod sa mga opisyal na seremonya, diplomasya, o sa anumang partikular na sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga 'rules' na kailangan mong sundin para hindi ka mapagalitan o maging epic fail. Sa BPO, ito yung script na binabasa mo. Sa ospital, ito yung health and safety procedures. Noong pandemic, ito yung 'wear mask, wash hands, social distance.'
usage_notes: Widely used during the COVID-19 pandemic to refer to health and safety guidelines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang sundin ang lahat ng health **protokolo** upang maiwasan ang pagkalat ng sakit.","translation":"All health **protocols** must be followed to prevent the spread of the disease."},{"sentence":"May sinusunod na **protokolo** sa palasyo kapag may bumibisitang pinuno ng ibang bansa.","translation":"There is a **protocol** followed in the palace when a leader from another country visits."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang bisa, saysay, o epekto ayon sa batas o kasunduan.
original_explanation: From the Spanish "nulo". This is the legal term for something that's totally invalid, like it never existed. Think of a contract you signed without reading the fine print, or a marriage that gets annulled. "Yung 'us' natin, parang **nulo** na, walang bisa." #Hugot. It's the "Ctrl+Z" of legal agreements.
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal, formal, or academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Idineklara ng korte na **nulo** ang kanilang kasal.","translation":"The court declared their marriage **null** and void."},{"sentence":"Ang kontratang iyon ay **nulo** dahil sa pandaraya.","translation":"That contract is **invalid** due to fraud."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging baog o kawalan ng kakayahang magkaanak. Ginagamit din ito upang ilarawan ang isang lupain na hindi mataba o isang proyektong hindi nagbunga.
etymology: From 'baog' (infertile, sterile) with the circumfix 'ka- -an' to form an abstract noun.
original_explanation: This is when the 'plantito/plantita' journey fails and the plant just won't give you a new leaf. In humans, it's a sensitive topic, often the subject of family drama in teleseryes. For projects, it's that 'great idea' that never took off, the ultimate 'drawing'.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat clinical term. Can be used literally for biological infertility or metaphorically for unproductive ventures or land.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming mag-asawa ang dumaranas ng problema sa **kabaugan**.","translation":"Many couples experience problems with **infertility**."},{"sentence":"Ang **kabaugan** ng lupa ang dahilan kung bakit walang tumutubong halaman.","translation":"The **barrenness** of the land is the reason why no plants are growing."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapahayag ng tanong o pagtatanong; may katangian ng pagsisiyasat.
original_explanation: Yan yung tono ng nanay mo 'pag tinanong ka, "Saan ka na naman galing?" Akala mo simpleng tanong lang, pero parang nasa police station ka na at suspect ka sa pag-ubos ng ulam sa ref.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng gramatika (pangungusap na interogatibo) o sa legal na pagsisiyasat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangungusap ay nasa anyong **interogatibo** dahil ito ay nagtatanong.","translation":"The sentence is in an **interrogative** form because it asks a question."},{"sentence":"Ginamit ng pulis ang **interogatibo**ng pamamaraan upang makuha ang katotohanan.","translation":"The police used an **interrogative** method to get the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging aprubado o matagumpay na paglampas sa isang pamantayan, pagsusulit, o pagtatasa.
original_explanation: The most beautiful word you can see next to your name after a hellish final exam or a nerve-wracking job interview. It's the opposite of "bagsak" and the reason for celebratory milk tea. When your thesis defense is pasado, you can finally see the light at the end of the tunnel.
usage_notes: Commonly used for exams, grades, bills in law, and quality control checks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **pasado** na ako sa board exam!","translation":"Finally, I **passed** the board exam!"},{"sentence":"Hindi **pasado** sa quality control ang mga produktong may depekto.","translation":"Products with defects did not get a **passing** grade in quality control."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian na tumutukoy sa isang tao na madaling magalit o mabilis uminit ang ulo kahit sa maliliit na bagay.
etymology: From 'ma-' + repetition of the first syllable of the root ('ga-lit' -> 'ga-galit') + '-in' suffix.
original_explanation: You know that one tita who gets mad when the wifi is slow, the coffee is cold, or the sinigang is not sour enough? That's 'magagalitin'. It's for people whose patience level is perpetually at 1%. They have a short fuse, like a firecracker you light up and have to throw away immediately. Best to give them space... and maybe a Snickers.
usage_notes: Describes a personality trait rather than a temporary state of being angry ('galit').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **magagalitin** si lolo mula nang magkasakit siya.","translation":"Grandfather became **irritable** ever since he got sick."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong biruin nang sobra ang boss natin, **magagalitin** pa naman iyon.","translation":"Don't joke too much with our boss, he's quite **short-tempered**."}]

translation: to raid; to invade; to assault
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang biglaan at marahas na pag-atake o pagsalakay.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'lusob.' This is what your officemates do to the pantry when someone brings a birthday cake. 'Tara, lusubin na natin yung cake ni Ma'am!' It's to attack or swarm a place, whether it's a military target or the last piece of lechon.
usage_notes: Verb form of 'lusob'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang heneral na **lusubin** ang kuta ng mga kalaban sa madaling-araw.","translation":"The general decided to **raid** the enemy's fortress at dawn."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagbabago, hindi kumukupas, o hindi natatapos; walang hanggan.
original_explanation: This is the stuff of OPM love songs and wedding vows. It’s that 'forever and ever, amen' kind of love. A love that doesn't fade, like your lola's devotion to her apo or your undying craving for Jollibee. It's eternal, unfading, the opposite of 'walang forever.'
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga kontekstong patula o romantiko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig niya para sa bayan ay **walang-maliw**.","translation":"His love for the country is **unfading**."}]

translation: food cooked to order; a request to cook something
meaning_filipino: Isang serbisyo kung saan ipinapaluto ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain, sa ibang tao; o ang pagkaing resulta nito.
original_explanation: The ultimate life hack for when you're at the palengke (wet market). You buy fresh seafood or meat, then go to a nearby carinderia and say "**Paluto** po!" They'll cook it for you for a fee. It’s like having a personal chef for a day without the celebrity price tag. Also a command: "Ma, **paluto** naman ng adobo!"
usage_notes: Functions as a noun ("Ang sarap ng paluto natin!") or as a command/request ("Paluto ka naman."). The concept is very popular in dampa-style seafood restaurants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng sariwang isda sa palengke at naghanap ng **paluto**.","translation":"We bought fresh fish at the market and looked for a **place that cooks food to order**."},{"sentence":"**Paluto** mo itong manok, gawin mong tinola,\" sabi ni nanay.","translation":"**Have this chicken cooked**, make it tinola,\" said mother."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasaayos ng mga bagay, gawain, o tao sa isang sistematikong paraan upang makamit ang isang partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: The favorite verb of every OC friend, student council officer, and events planner. It's what you do before a big party, a family reunion, or when your room looks like a disaster zone after a long week. It's the process of turning 'kalat' into 'ayos' and 'gulo' into 'plano.'
usage_notes: Can refer to organizing things, events, or people (e.g., a union).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **mag-organisa** ng mga libro sa aparador.","translation":"Help me **organize** the books on the shelf."},{"sentence":"Sila ang naatasang **mag-organisa** ng Christmas party ng kumpanya.","translation":"They were assigned to **organize** the company's Christmas party."}]

meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit na pagbibigay ng tugon sa paraang walang galang o pabalang, karaniwan sa nakatatanda o may awtoridad.
etymology: From the root word 'sagot' with reduplication, indicating a repeated or intensified action, often with a negative connotation.
original_explanation: This is not just answering. This is 'pagsasagot na pabalang.' It's what gets you the classic Pinoy mom line: 'Aba! Sumasagot-sagot ka na ah!' It implies disrespect and a smart-alecky tone. You're not just replying; you're challenging.
usage_notes: The repetition of the root word 'sagot' implies a continuous, often annoying or disrespectful action. It's different from the simple, neutral act of 'sumagot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagalitan si Ben ng kanyang ina dahil lagi siyang **sumasagot-sagot**.","translation":"Ben was scolded by his mother because he always **talks back**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **sumagot-sagot** sa iyong lola; magpakita ka ng respeto.","translation":"Don't **talk back** to your grandmother; show some respect."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aklat na naglalaman ng mga pangunahing aralin para sa mga nagsisimulang matutong bumasa.
etymology: Isang parirala na binubuo ng 'panimula' (beginning), pang-angkop na '-ng', 'aklat' (book), 'sa' (for), at 'pagbasa' (reading).
original_explanation: This is your "A-Ba-Ka-Da" book, the OG source of knowledge before Wikipedia and Google. A panimulang-aklat sa pagbasa is a primer, the book that taught you that "Ang pusa ay nasa puno." It's full of simple words and big pictures, the literary equivalent of baby steps. The foundation of every bookworm's journey.
usage_notes: Isang tiyak na termino sa larangan ng edukasyon. Ginagamit din ang salitang hiram na 'primer'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'Abakada' ay isang halimbawa ng **panimulang-aklat sa pagbasa**.","translation":"The 'Abakada' is an example of a **beginner's reading book**."},{"sentence":"Binilhan niya ng **panimulang-aklat sa pagbasa** ang kanyang anak na limang taong gulang.","translation":"She bought a **primer** for her five-year-old child."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar na puno ng makakapal at magugulong halaman, damo, at sanga, na mahirap daanan.
original_explanation: Parang gubat sa likod-bahay niyo na hindi natabas ng isang taon. O parang buhok mo pagka-gising sa umaga. It's that wild, untamed, 'jungle-y' vibe where you'd expect a kapre to be chilling.
usage_notes: Often used to describe forests, abandoned lots, or any unkempt area with dense vegetation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap maglakad sa **masukal** na gubat dahil sa dami ng baging.","translation":"It's difficult to walk in the **overgrown** forest because of the many vines."},{"sentence":"Nilinis nila ang **masukal** na bakuran.","translation":"They cleaned the **overgrown** yard."}]

translation: to cause someone to take a nap; to lull to sleep
meaning_filipino: Dahan-dahang patulugin o hikayatin na umidlip nang saglit.
original_explanation: What you do to a baby by gently rocking them. Or what a boring 3-hour Zoom meeting does to you. The meeting will 'paidlipin' you whether you like it or not. The struggle is real.
usage_notes: Implies lulling someone into a light, short sleep (a nap), as opposed to 'patulugin' which is for a longer, deeper sleep.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **paidlipin** ang sanggol sa pamamagitan ng paghehele.","translation":"She tried to **lull the baby to nap** by singing a lullaby."},{"sentence":"Ang mahinang musika ay sapat na para **paidlipin** ako.","translation":"The soft music is enough to **make me nap**."}]

translation: to act treacherously, to betray cruelly
meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng karahasan, kataksilan, o matinding kalupitan sa kapwa.
original_explanation: This is next-level drama, pure teleserye kontrabida level. It's not just betraying someone; it's doing it in a cruel, evil way. That friend you trusted with your business idea? He **tumampalasan** when he stole it and claimed it was his. It’s an act of a villain.
usage_notes: A very strong and formal word, often found in literature, historical accounts, or formal speeches. Not used in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pinagkakatiwalaan niyang alagad ay **tumampalasan** at ipinagkanulo siya sa mga kaaway.","translation":"His trusted follower **acted treacherously** and betrayed him to the enemies."},{"sentence":"Hinding-hindi mapapatawad ng hari ang sinumang **tumampalasan** sa kaharian.","translation":"The king will never forgive anyone who **acts traitorously** against the kingdom."}]

translation: to enjoin; to instruct; to entrust
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng mahalagang bilin, utos, o paalala sa isang tao na dapat tuparin, alalahanin, o pangalagaan.
original_explanation: This isn't just a simple reminder; it's the "huling habilin" level of instruction. It's what your parents do before a long trip: '**Ipagtagubilin** ko sa'yo ang mga halaman at si Bantay!' They're entrusting you with a sacred duty. You don't just hear it; you feel the weight of it.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or serious contexts, like giving final instructions, a last will, or entrusting a very important task.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bago umalis, **ipinagtagubilin** ng lolo ang pangangalaga sa kanilang lumang bahay.","translation":"Before leaving, grandpa **entrusted** the care of their old house."},{"sentence":"Ito ang tanging **ipagtagubilin** ko sa iyo: maging matapat ka palagi.","translation":"This is the only thing I will **enjoin** you with: always be honest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sentral o pangunahing tanggapan o base ng isang organisasyon, kumpanya, o militar.
original_explanation: The main base. The mothership. The HQ. For a BPO company, it's the main site where the big bosses are. For the Avengers, it's Stark Tower. For a network of chismosas, it's the corner sari-sari store.
usage_notes: Compound word. Often used in formal, military, or corporate contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpulong ang mga heneral sa **punong-himpilan** ng militar.","translation":"The generals met at the military **headquarters**."},{"sentence":"Ang **punong-himpilan** ng aming kumpanya ay nasa Makati.","translation":"Our company's **headquarters** is in Makati."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging isang panatiko; ang pagkakaroon ng labis, masidhi, at kadalasa'y hindi makatwirang sigasig o paghanga para sa isang bagay, tao, o paniniwala.
etymology: Mula sa `pagka-` (estado ng pagiging) + `panatiko` (panatiko, mula sa Espanyol na 'fanático').
original_explanation: This is the general term for being a stan. It's the hardcore basketball fan who gets into fistfights over his favorite team. It's the political supporter who treats elections like the UAAP finals. It's passion turned up to 11, sometimes to the point where logic leaves the chat.
usage_notes: Ang pangkalahatan at mas karaniwang termino para sa panatisismo, na angkop sa anumang kasarian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkapanatiko** sa relihiyon ay maaaring maging mapanganib kung ito'y nagiging bulag.","translation":"Religious **fanaticism** can be dangerous if it becomes blind."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkapanatiko** sa pulitika ay dahilan ng pakikipag-away niya sa kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"His political **fanaticism** is the reason for his fights with his friends."}]

translation: to reform; to renew one's life
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabago ng isang tao tungo sa mas mabuting kalagayan o pagkatao; ang pagtalikod sa dating masamang gawi.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'New Year, New Me' but for your entire life. It's when someone decides to leave their 'Marites' ways or their toxic past behind and starts fresh. Think of it as a spiritual or personal system reboot. From 'sira-ulo' to 'role model', that's pagbaguhing-buhay.
usage_notes: A compound word from 'pagbago' (to change) and 'buhay' (life). This is a verb in its command/infinitive form (`-in` verb with `pag-`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Layunin ng programa na **pagbaguhing-buhay** ang mga nalulong sa masamang bisyo.","translation":"The program aims **to reform the lives** of those addicted to bad vices."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbagsak o pagdapa kung saan ang mukha ang unang tumama.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "subasob" at panlaping -um-.
original_explanation: That super un-glamorous moment when you trip and your face decides to kiss the pavement. It's the "epic fail" of walking. Parang 'yung pag-fall mo sa kanya, biglaan at masakit sa mukha.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-deskriptibong salita para sa isang partikular na uri ng pagkahulog. Anyong pangnagdaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napatid siya sa bato kaya siya **sumubasob** sa putikan.","translation":"He tripped on a rock and **fell face first** into the mud."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod, halos **sumubasob** na ang manlalaro sa sahig.","translation":"From extreme exhaustion, the player almost **plunged headlong** onto the floor."}]

translation: to release; to let go; to set free
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay-laya sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay na dating nakakulong, nakatali, o nasa ilalim ng kapangyarihan. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagpapalabas ng emosyon o saloobin.
etymology: From magpa- (causative) + kawala (state of being free/loose).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'Let It Go' verb. Whether you're releasing your ex's stuff (finally!), freeing a bird from a cage, or just letting out a huge sigh after a toxic Zoom meeting, you're magpakawala. It's the act of unclenching your fist, literally or metaphorically.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical release (e.g., prisoners, animals) or emotional/abstract release (e.g., feelings, a sigh).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magpakawala** ng mga alitaptap sa hardin.","translation":"She decided to **release** fireflies in the garden."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpakawala** ng sama ng loob para gumaan ang pakiramdam mo.","translation":"You need to **let go** of your resentment to feel better."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng suhol o "pampadulas" sa isang tao, lalo na sa isang opisyal, upang mapabilis ang isang transaksyon o makakuha ng pabor.
etymology: From `magpa-` (causative prefix) + `dulas` (slip/slippery). The figurative meaning is a common euphemism.
original_explanation: Literally means "to make something slippery," but 99% of the time, it means you're giving someone some "lagay" or "tong" to get what you want faster. It's the unofficial "express lane" fee in some government offices. "May pampadulas ka ba diyan?" is the low-key question for "Are you going to bribe them?"
usage_notes: This term is almost exclusively used in the context of bribery and corruption. The literal meaning "to make something slippery" is rarely used with this specific verb form; one might say "gawing madulas" instead.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siyang **magpadulas** para daw mapabilis ang pag-release ng kanyang lisensya.","translation":"He was advised to **give a bribe** to speed up the release of his license."},{"sentence":"Tanggihan nating **magpadulas** at labanan ang korapsyon.","translation":"Let's refuse to **bribe** and fight corruption."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, pangyayari, o katangian na hindi maipaliwanag ng karaniwang kaalaman o ng mga batas ng kalikasan; kataka-taka at kamangha-mangha.
original_explanation: This is when something so unbelievable happens, you just have to say "Sana all!" It's finding a parking spot at the mall on a payday weekend. It's your internet connection not lagging during an important online meeting. It's your salary lasting until the next payday. Pure magic!
usage_notes: The `ka-` prefix intensifies the meaning of 'himala' (miracle).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kahima-himalang** pangyayari ang kanyang paggaling mula sa malubhang sakit.","translation":"His recovery from the serious illness was a **miraculous** event."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-ahon ng Pilipinas mula sa krisis ay tunay na **kahima-himala**.","translation":"The Philippines' recovery from the crisis is truly **miraculous**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan o pangyayari na lubhang nakapagdudulot ng matinding lungkot, pighati, o awa.
original_explanation: This is "kalungkutan" on steroids. Hindi lang basta malungkot, kundi tragic levels. Ito yung balita na mapapa-"grabe naman" ka na lang. It's the "Shake, Rattle & Roll" of sadness – it's a whole tragic episode.
usage_notes: An intensified form of 'malungkot', often used to describe situations or news rather than just personal feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kalungkut-lungkot** ang sinapit ng mga biktima ng bagyo.","translation":"The fate of the storm victims was **very sad/tragic**."},{"sentence":"Isang **kalungkut-lungkot** na balita ang aming natanggap kaninang umaga.","translation":"We received a **deplorable** piece of news this morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginagamit upang takpan o isara nang mahigpit ang isang butas o siwang.
original_explanation: Parang takip sa bote ng wine, o yung goma sa lababo para hindi umagos ang tubig. Sa usapang hugot, ito yung ginagawa mo sa tenga mo kapag ayaw mong marinig ang chismis o ang panenermon ng nanay mo. Minsan, kailangan mo ng **pasak** sa puso para 'di na pumasok ang mga maling tao.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb "ipasak" (to plug) or "pasakan" (to put a plug on).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **pasak** ng lababo kaya tuloy-tuloy ang agos ng tubig.","translation":"The **stopper** for the sink is missing, so the water keeps draining."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng tela bilang pansamantalang **pasak** sa butas ng banga.","translation":"He used a piece of cloth as a temporary **plug** for the hole in the jar."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pandamdam na nagpapahayag ng biglaang pagkakabunyag, pagkahuli sa akto, o isang matagumpay at biglaang pangyayari.
etymology: Onomatopoeia, from English 'boom'. Its specific slang usage was popularized by Filipino comedian Vice Ganda.
original_explanation: This isn't just the sound of an explosion. In Pinoy slang, it's the sound of a truth bomb dropping. It's the first word in the iconic phrase 'Boom, panis!' (Boom, spoiled/busted!), used when you catch someone in a lie, expose a secret, or make a mic-drop-worthy point. It's the verbal equivalent of a 'gotcha!' moment.
usage_notes: Almost always used in the phrase 'Boom, panis!' or a variation. It signifies a moment of sudden revelation or victory.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi niya diet siya pero nakita ko siyang kumakain ng lechon. **Boom**, panis!","translation":"He said he was on a diet but I saw him eating lechon. **Boom**, busted!"},{"sentence":"Akala niya hindi ko alam ang sikreto niya, pero narinig ko lahat. **Boom**!","translation":"He thought I didn't know his secret, but I heard everything. **Boom**!"}]

translation: bilimbi; a type of sour fruit
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit at maasim na prutas na pahaba, karaniwang ginagamit bilang pampaasim sa mga lutuin tulad ng sinigang o paksiw.
etymology: Possibly from Malay 'belimbing masam' or a related Austronesian language.
original_explanation: The OG sour-pucker! It's that small, green, acidic fruit that looks like a tiny cucumber. If you want next-level asim for your sinigang, you use kamyas. Also great with a dip of salt or bagoong if you're brave enough. Your face will definitely do the 'asim-kilig' scrunch.
usage_notes: Scientific name: Averrhoa bilimbi. A common backyard fruit tree in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang sinigang na hipon kung **kamyas** ang pampaasim.","translation":"Shrimp sinigang is more delicious if **bilimbi** is used as the souring agent."},{"sentence":"Pumitas si Lola ng **kamyas** sa kanilang bakuran.","translation":"Grandma picked some **kamyas** from their yard."}]

translation: to be weakened; to become weak
meaning_filipino: Maging mahina o mabawasan ang taglay na lakas, sigla, o impluwensya.
original_explanation: Like your WiFi signal when you move two rooms away from the router. Or your motivation to go to the gym on a Friday night. It's when something loses its power, volume, or intensity, whether it's your phone's battery or your will to adult.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical strength, signal strength, influence, volume, or emotional fortitude.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapalipas ng gutom upang hindi **mapahina** ang iyong katawan.","translation":"Don't skip meals so that your body will not **be weakened**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng katawan sa pagitan ng dibdib at balakang na kinalalagyan ng mga organo para sa pagtunaw ng pagkain; ginagamit din bilang metapora para sa konsensya.
original_explanation: This is your gut, literally and figuratively. It's the organ that complains when you eat too much samgyupsal ('masakit ang sikmura ko'). It's also your conscience, the thing that 'churns' when you do something wrong ('hindi kaya ng sikmura ko'). It's the seat of both hunger and guilt.
usage_notes: The dual meaning of physical stomach and metaphorical conscience is very common. The idiom 'hindi masikmura' means 'cannot stomach it' or 'find it morally unacceptable'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumukulo ang **sikmura** ko sa gutom.","translation":"My **stomach** is growling with hunger."},{"sentence":"Hindi naatim ng kanyang **sikmura** ang katiwaliang nakita niya.","translation":"His **conscience** could not stomach the corruption he witnessed."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pag-aatubili, pag-aalinlangan, o kawalan ng buong-loob na pagsang-ayon na gawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is you when your friend asks 'Libre mo 'ko?' and you pause for 5 seconds before saying yes. It's that feeling of 'Should I or shouldn't I?'—the hesitation before committing. Parang 'yung pag-amin mo sa crush mo, you're all 'bantulot' because you're scared of getting rejected.
usage_notes: Often used with 'nag-' to form the verb 'nagbabantulot' (is hesitating).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **bantulot** na tanggapin ang alok na trabaho sa ibang bansa.","translation":"She is **reluctant** to accept the job offer abroad."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **bantulot** na ipahayag ang iyong saloobin.","translation":"Don't be **hesitant** to express your feelings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtawag o pagtitipon ng mga tao para sa isang pag-uusap o pagpupulong.
original_explanation: The favorite phrase of every team lead, manager, and HOA president. When you hear 'Magpapatawag ako ng meeting,' you know someone's about to magpapulong. It's the corporate version of 'Upo, usap tayo.' Can be a source of productivity or a sign that this could have been an email.
usage_notes: A very common term in professional, organizational, and community settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang CEO na **magpapulong** ng lahat ng department heads.","translation":"The CEO decided to **call a meeting** of all department heads."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magpapulong** para planuhin ang Christmas party.","translation":"We need to **hold a meeting** to plan the Christmas party."}]

translation: to have someone/something checked (by a professional)
meaning_filipino: Dalhin ang isang tao o bagay sa isang propesyonal, karaniwan ay isang doktor o mekaniko, upang masuri ang kalagayan o kondisyon nito.
etymology: From pa- (causative prefix) + tingin (look/check). The 'pa-' prefix here indicates having an action done by someone else.
original_explanation: This is the adulting version of 'patingin'. It's not about being nosy; it's about being responsible. When your cough lasts for three weeks, your mom says, "Mag**patingin** ka na sa doktor!" It means to get yourself checked out. Also works for cars ("Ipatingin mo na 'yan sa mekaniko"). It's the verb for seeking an expert opinion when you know something is wrong.
usage_notes: The actor-focus form is 'magpatingin' (to go get oneself checked). The object-focus form is 'ipatingin' (to have something checked by someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpatingin** sa doktor dahil sa iyong matagal nang ubo.","translation":"You need to **get checked** by a doctor because of your persistent cough."},{"sentence":"Ipa**patingin** ko na bukas ang kotse dahil may kakaibang tunog.","translation":"I will **have** the car **checked** tomorrow because it's making a strange noise."}]

translation: There it is (near the person spoken to)
meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip na pamatlig na tumutukoy sa isang bagay o lugar na malapit sa taong kausap. Katumbas ng "iyan."
original_explanation: The official word for "I told you so." 'Pag nadapa ka, maririnig mo, "**Ayan**! Kasi hindi ka nag-iingat!" It's also used to point something out. "**Ayan** na yung inorder mong milk tea!" It's the shorter, more common version of 'iyan'. It carries a certain tone, either excitement, warning, or pure schadenfreude.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa pasalitang komunikasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ayan** na ang bus, bilisan mo!","translation":"**There's** the bus, hurry up!"},{"sentence":"Sabi ko sa'yo mag-aral ka, **ayan** tuloy, bumagsak ka.","translation":"I told you to study, **so now** you failed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o katangian ng pagiging bago, moderno, o hindi pa nararanasan. Tumutukoy sa anumang pagbabago o inobasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling when you unbox a new phone. 'Yung amoy ng bagong libro o sasakyan. This is the "new new" that gets everyone excited—a new milk tea flavor, a new Netflix series, or a new system at work that everyone has to learn (and complain about). Kabaguhan is the opposite of "luma" and "gasgas na."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **kabaguhan** sa teknolohiya ang lumabas ngayong taon.","translation":"Many **innovations** in technology came out this year."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **kabaguhan** sa sistema ay nakatulong mapabilis ang proseso.","translation":"The **new changes** in the system helped speed up the process."}]

translation: to try, to test, to prove
meaning_filipino: Subukan ang isang bagay upang malaman ang kalidad, bisa, o katotohanan nito. Patunayan.
etymology: From Spanish 'probar' (to try, to test, to prove).
original_explanation: The 'sana all' of testing things. Before you 'add to cart', you might want to 'purbahan' it first. It's like taking a free sample at the grocery, or test-driving a car, or even that first "I love you" to see how they react. It's the act of gathering evidence.
usage_notes: A colloquial alternative to 'subukan' or 'patunayan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Purbahan** mo itong bagong luto ko.","translation":"**Try** this new dish I cooked."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **purbahan** kung gumagana pa ang lumang radyo.","translation":"We need to **test** if the old radio still works."}]

translation: to restrain oneself; to hold back
meaning_filipino: Kontrolin ang sarili upang hindi gawin, sabihin, o ipakita ang isang bagay; pagtitimpi.
original_explanation: That superhuman strength you need when you see a 50% off sale but it's not yet payday. Also, the face you make when a chismosa tita asks "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?" and you just smile instead of screaming. "Magpigil ka, bes, 'wag mo patulan."
usage_notes: Refers to self-control over actions, words, or emotions. `Pigilan` is the object-focus form (to restrain someone/something else).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magpigil** ng tawa habang nagsasalita ang kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"She tried to **hold back** her laughter while her friend was speaking."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magpigil** ng galit kapag ikaw ay inaapi.","translation":"It's hard to **restrain** your anger when you are being oppressed."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkain o anumang bagay na kinakain upang magbigay-sustansya.
original_explanation: An old-school word for food, often heard from our lolos and lolas. It's the OG "kain" before "food trip" became a thing. If someone asks "Nasaan ang komida?", they're not just hungry, they're *classically* hungry.
usage_notes: This is a somewhat dated term, more common among older generations or in certain regions. 'Pagkain' is the universally used term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inihanda na ni Lola ang **komida** para sa tanghalian.","translation":"Grandma has already prepared the **food** for lunch."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **komida** sa pistang iyon.","translation":"The **meal** at that festival was delicious."}]

translation: to take on passengers; to load
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahintulot o pagpapasok ng mga pasahero o kargamento sa isang sasakyan.
original_explanation: This is the primary job of jeepney, bus, and taxi drivers. It's the art of turning a 10-seater van into a 20-seater with the mantra, 'Sige, kasya pa 'yan!' Also what you do when you let your friend ride in your car.
usage_notes: This verb focuses on the action of the driver or operator loading people or goods into a vehicle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal **magsakay** ng pasahero sa lugar na iyon.","translation":"It is forbidden to **take on passengers** in that area."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na masigasig na nagtataguyod o sumusuporta sa isang layuning panlipunan o pampulitika.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga estudyante (o datihang estudyante) na laging may bitbit na placard sa Mendiola o sa SONA. Sila yung boses ng mga walang boses, laging nananawagan ng pagbabago, at hindi takot ipaglaban ang karapatan ng bayan. Sa socmed, sila yung laging may "thread" tungkol sa isyung panlipunan.
usage_notes: Madalas na may negatibong konotasyon sa ilang sektor, ngunit positibo para sa mga grupong nagtataguyod ng karapatang pantao at reporma.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **aktibista** ang nagprotesta laban sa bagong batas.","translation":"Many **activists** protested against the new law."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang **aktibista** para sa karapatan ng mga kababaihan.","translation":"She is known as an **activist** for women's rights."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahaba at makapal na tali na yari sa pinilipit na mga hibla ng abaka, niyog, o sintetikong materyales, ginagamit sa pagtatali, paghila, o pag-akyat.
original_explanation: The OG multi-tool before Swiss knives were cool. It's for tying your kalabaw, playing tug-of-war at the barangay fiesta, or for the classic 'luksong-lubid'. In hugot terms, it's what you use to tie things down, hoping they won't leave... but sometimes you just have to let go.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng matibay na **lubid** para itali sa duyan.","translation":"Get a strong **rope** to tie to the hammock."},{"sentence":"Naglaro kami ng luksong-**lubid** noong aming kabataan.","translation":"We played jumping **rope** during our youth."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang uri ng pagkain na karaniwang kinakain nang paunti-unti gamit ang mga daliri, tulad ng mani, buto ng pakwan, o chichirya.
etymology: From "kutkot" (to pick at, to nibble). The "-in" suffix makes it a noun referring to the thing to be picked at.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga pampalipas-oras mo habang nanonood ng Netflix or K-Drama. Mani, butong pakwan, popcorn, chichirya—lahat ng pwedeng kurutin at isubo nang hindi kailangan ng plato. The official food of 'marites' sessions and long road trips.
usage_notes: Refers to a specific category of snacks, usually dry and eaten with fingers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng maraming **kutkutin** para sa movie marathon natin.","translation":"I bought a lot of **snacks** for our movie marathon."},{"sentence":"Paborito niyang **kutkutin** ang inihaw na mais habang naglalakbay.","translation":"His favorite **finger food** is grilled corn while traveling."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa damdaming taos-puso, wagas, at walang halong pagkukunwari.
original_explanation: This is the 'Sana All' level of love and affection. It's not the flirty 'crush lang,' but the deep, genuine, 'ipapakilala ko sa magulang ko' kind of feeling. It’s pure, like your love for Jollibee Chickenjoy, walang halong biro.
usage_notes: Often used in romantic or poetic contexts to describe feelings, love, or intentions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakikita sa kanyang mga mata ang **matimyas** na pag-ibig para sa iyo.","translation":"You can see in his/her eyes the **sincere** love for you."},{"sentence":"Isang **matimyas** na pasasalamat ang ipinaabot niya sa lahat ng tumulong.","translation":"She extended a **heartfelt** thank you to everyone who helped."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawaing labis na masama, hindi makatarungan, o malupit; kalupitan o kabuktutan.
etymology: From ka- + tampalasan + -an, where tampalasan means a wicked person or traitor.
original_explanation: This isn't just simple 'kasamaan' (evil). This is villain-level evil. Pang-kontrabida sa teleserye. 'Yung tipong magnanakaw na ng kaban ng bayan, magpapahirap pa sa mga inosente. It's an act so outrageous it makes you go, 'Sino'ng kinain mong demonyo?!'
usage_notes: A very strong and formal word, often used in legal, religious, or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **katampalasanan** ang ginawa niya sa kanyang sariling pamilya.","translation":"He committed an **atrocity** against his own family."},{"sentence":"Ang pagpatay sa mga walang kalaban-laban ay isang uri ng **katampalasanan**.","translation":"Killing the defenseless is a form of **wickedness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang amoy o lasa ng isang prutas na sobra na sa pagkahinog, karaniwang may bahagyang lasa ng alkohol dahil sa permentasyon.
original_explanation: That specific smell of a mango or banana that's been sitting on the counter for too long. It’s not quite rotten (bulok) yet, but it's past its prime. It's the fruit equivalent of 'overthinking'—it was good, but now it's a bit complicated and has a weird aftertaste. It's that 'I should have eaten this yesterday' feeling in a word.
usage_notes: A very specific term related to fruits, particularly bananas and mangoes. Not a common word for everyone, but well-understood in contexts involving fruits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayoko na ng saging na 'yan, may **anos** na.","translation":"I don't want that banana anymore, it has that **overripe taste**."},{"sentence":"Amoy **anos** na 'yung mga mangga sa basket.","translation":"The mangoes in the basket smell **overripe**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na naging lapad o sapad, partikular na ginagamit sa paglalarawan ng ilong na pango.
original_explanation: 'Yung ilong mong parang nasagasaan ng pison sa sobrang pagka-flat. Hindi lang 'pango' level, 'alipapa' level. It's the kind of flat that makes you wonder if gravity was extra harsh on you.
usage_notes: Isang napakadalang na salita na halos sa panitikan na lamang matatagpuan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagkakasuntok, naging **alipapa** ang ilong ng boksingero.","translation":"Because of the punch, the boxer's nose became **flattened**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsasara o pagkakabit ng mga butones ng isang kasuotan.
original_explanation: That thing your mom yells at you to do before you leave for school or church. "Hoy, magbitones ka ng polo mo!" It's the final step to looking 'disente' or presentable.
usage_notes: Used for clothing like shirts, polos, jackets, or pants that have buttons.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magbitones** ng damit ko, hindi ko maabot ang likod.","translation":"Help me **button up** my dress, I can't reach the back."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **magbitones** ng iyong polo bago pumasok sa opisina.","translation":"Don't forget **to button up** your polo shirt before entering the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Umakit o bumighani sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng angking ganda, galing, o kakaibang katangian.
original_explanation: That moment when you weren't interested at first, but then they started talking about their passion for 90s anime and suddenly... *ay, iba pala siya*. That's the power of 'humalina'. It's the rizz that just works, the charm that sneaks up on you, like a good coffee or a perfectly seasoned adobo.
usage_notes: Past tense. The subject is the one that caused the attraction or fascination.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng kanyang tinig ay **humalina** sa lahat ng nakikinig.","translation":"The beauty of her voice **charmed** everyone listening."},{"sentence":"Sa akin ay **humalina** ang simpleng pamumuhay sa probinsya.","translation":"The simple life in the province **attracted** me."}]

meaning_filipino: Nag-udyok, nag-engganyo, o nagkumbinsi sa isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay o maniwala sa isang ideya.
original_explanation: Yung kaibigan mong humikayat sa'yo na mag-order ng milk tea kahit nagtitipid ka, sabay sabi ng 'Deserve mo 'to!' Sila 'yung reason kung bakit wala kang savings. This is the power of a true 'budol' master.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **humikayat** sa akin na subukan ang bagong trabaho.","translation":"She was the one who **persuaded** me to try the new job."},{"sentence":"**Humikayat** ang gobyerno sa mga mamamayan na magpabakuna.","translation":"The government **encouraged** the citizens to get vaccinated."}]

translation: to take pictures of each other
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng dalawa o higit pang tao na sabay-sabay o halinhinang kumukuha ng litrato ng isa't isa.
etymology: mag- (verb prefix) + litrato (from Spanish 'retrato', meaning 'portrait') + -han (reciprocal action suffix).
original_explanation: The official sport of every Filipino reunion, vacation, or even just a random coffee date. 'Maglitratuhan' is the reciprocal act of taking photos. 'Picturan mo 'ko dito, tapos ako naman sa'yo.' It's the foundation of every Instagram feed and the reason why someone's phone storage is always full.
usage_notes: The -an suffix implies a reciprocal or group action. 'Kumuha ng litrato' is one person taking a picture. 'Maglitratuhan' is people taking pictures of each other.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa Baguio para **maglitratuhan** sa gitna ng mga pine tree.","translation":"We went to Baguio to **take pictures of each other** amidst the pine trees."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng graduation, nagkayayaan ang magkakaibigan na **maglitratuhan**.","translation":"After graduation, the friends decided to **have a pictorial** together."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang metaliko, karaniwang kawad o baras, na ginagamit upang makasagap o magpadala ng mga electromagnetic wave para sa radyo o telebisyon.
original_explanation: The old-school version of your WiFi router. It's that metal thing on the roof your dad used to shout at you to adjust ('O, kaliwa! Kanan! Ayan, malinaw na!') just to get a clear signal for a boxing match. In the bug world, it's the feelers they use to sense if you're about to smack them with a tsinelas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating ayusin ang **antena** para luminaw ang palabas sa TV.","translation":"We need to fix the **antenna** to get a clearer picture on the TV."},{"sentence":"Mahaba ang **antena** ng ipis.","translation":"The cockroach has long **antennae**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pagtitipon o salu-salo na idinaraos upang salubungin o parangalan ang isang tao, o upang ipagdiwang ang isang okasyon tulad ng kasal.
original_explanation: Ito yung part 2 ng kasal o binyag. Dito nangyayari ang totoong party. The main event kung saan may libreng pagkain, open bar (kung swerte), at ang walang kamatayang "Mabuhay ang bagong kasal!". Ito rin ang venue para sa tita mong magtatanong kung kelan ka naman ikakasal.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa handaan pagkatapos ng isang seremonya. Ang baybay na 'resepsyon' (walang 'i') ay karaniwan ding ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginanap ang **resepsiyon** ng kasal sa isang mamahaling hotel.","translation":"The wedding **reception** was held in an expensive hotel."},{"sentence":"Maraming bisita ang dumalo sa **resepsiyon** para sa bagong ambassador.","translation":"Many guests attended the **reception** for the new ambassador."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalis o paghahagis ng isang bagay na hindi na kailangan o gusto, partikular na ang basura.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your ex's stuff after a breakup, your trash after a party, or your money on 11.11 sale items you don't really need. It's the act of getting rid of something. The MMDA is watching your 'pagtatapon' habits!
usage_notes: Commonly refers to waste disposal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tamang **pagtatapon** ng basura ay mahalaga para sa kalikasan.","translation":"Proper **disposal** of trash is important for the environment."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **pagtatapon** ng pagkain; maraming nagugutom.","translation":"Avoid **throwing away** food; many are hungry."}]

translation: to appoint, to assign, to dedicate
meaning_filipino: Itakda o iukol ang isang tao, bagay, o gawain para sa isang partikular na layunin, posisyon, o tungkulin.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your manager suddenly makes you the 'lead' for a new project without asking you first. You've been 'volun-told'. It's also what you do when you dedicate a karaoke song to your crush, hoping they get the message. 'I **magtalaga** this song to you!'
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like government, business, or religious service.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangulo ay **magtatalaga** ng bagong kalihim ng edukasyon.","translation":"The president will **appoint** a new secretary of education."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magtalaga** ng kanyang buhay sa pagtulong sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"He decided to **dedicate** his life to helping the poor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian na naglalarawan sa isang bagay na permanente, hindi nagbabago, o regular na nangyayari o umiiral.
original_explanation: This is the 'official' or 'tenured' version of something. Think 'lagiang customer' (suki) at your favorite milk tea shop, or your 'lagiang pwesto' sa office pantry. It's the state of being a permanent fixture, for better or for worse. The term 'lagiang dami' (constant quantity) is its most famous, albeit nerdy, use.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang bagay na hindi pabago-bago. Ang pariralang 'lagiang dami' ay partikular na nangangahulugang 'constant quantity' sa agham at matematika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bilis ng liwanag ay isang **lagiang** halaga sa larangan ng pisika.","translation":"The speed of light is a **constant** value in the field of physics."},{"sentence":"May **lagian** siyang kita mula sa kanyang mga ari-arian.","translation":"He has a **regular** income from his properties."}]

translation: to do a little sewing; to stitch together (figurative)
meaning_filipino: Pagsasagawa ng bahagya o paisa-isang pananahi; pagdurugtong ng mga bagay sa pamamagitan ng sinulid at karayom sa maliit na paraan, o pag-uugnay ng mga ideya o kwento.
etymology: From 'mag-' (verb-forming prefix) + 'tahi-tahi' (reduplication of 'tahi', meaning sewing, implying a small or scattered action).
