In a relationship, it's the "Saan ka galing? Bakit ngayon ka lang?" interrogation. You are being asked to justify your actions and prove their worth or explain their failure.
usage_notes: A formal term. 'Sulit' here means accounting or reckoning, not 'worth it'. The root is from the compound 'bigay-sulit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat mong **ipagbigay-sulit** ang bawat sentimong ginastos mo mula sa pondo ng bayan.","translation":"You must be **held accountable** for every cent you spent from the public funds."},{"sentence":"**Ipagbigay-sulit** mo ang iyong mga pagkakamali sa proyektong ito.","translation":"**Answer for** your mistakes in this project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay o pagbibihis ng sapatos sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what you do for your little pamangkin who can't tie their own laces yet. It's the act of being the official 'shoe-putter-onner'. Your mom might yell, 'Hoy, sapatusan mo na 'yung bata, aalis na tayo!' ('Hey, put the kid's shoes on, we're leaving!').
usage_notes: Used when the action is being done *to* someone else. The object of the verb is the person being shod. Contrast with 'mag-sapatos', which means 'to wear shoes' (oneself).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **sapatusan** ang anak natin dahil mahuhuli na siya sa eskwela.","translation":"Help me **put shoes on** our child because he's going to be late for school."},{"sentence":"Kahit malaki na siya, kailangan pa ring **sapatusan** ng yaya.","translation":"Even though he's grown, the nanny still has to **put his shoes on** for him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o pangkat ng mga tao na nagpasimula, nagtayo, o nagbuo ng isang organisasyon, samahan, o institusyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'taga-' (tagagawa), 'pag-' (nagpapangalan), at salitang-ugat na 'tatag' (to establish, found).
original_explanation: The OG. The one who started it all. Sila yung may vision, yung nag-isip ng concept, at nag-effort para mabuo ang isang kumpanya, club, or even a small group chat. Think Mark Zuckerberg for Facebook, or your lola who started the family's carinderia business.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng kahalagahan at pinagmulan. Ginagamit para sa mga negosyo, organisasyon, at kilusan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **tagapagtatag** ng kilalang kumpanyang iyon.","translation":"He is the **founder** of that famous company."},{"sentence":"Pinarangalan ang mga nabubuhay na **tagapagtatag** ng samahan.","translation":"The living **founders** of the organization were honored."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mamalyang-dagat (marine mammal) na karaniwang matatagpuan sa malalamig na katubigan, may makinis na katawan at mga palikpik (flippers).
etymology: Salitang tambalan ng "karnero" (tupa) at "dagat" (dagat), isang calque o direktang salin ng konsepto.
original_explanation: Literally "sheep of the sea". It's a seal! You know, the cute, barking, fish-eating animals you see balancing balls on their noses in ocean parks. They're the sea doggos. Why "sheep"? Maybe because they're kinda plump and chill like sheep? The old folks had their reasons.
usage_notes: Isang literal na pagsasalin na nagkokonekta sa hitsura o katangian ng hayop sa isang kilalang hayop sa lupa. Ang salitang "poka" ay mas karaniwang hiram na salita para sa "seal".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita kami ng mga **karnerong-dagat** na nagpapahinga sa mga bato.","translation":"We saw **seals** resting on the rocks."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **karnerong-dagat** ay mahuhusay na manlalangoy.","translation":"**Seals** are excellent swimmers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang itim, malagkit, at malapot na materyal na hinango mula sa petrolyo, at karaniwang ginagamit sa paggawa ng kalsada at pagpapatag ng mga ibabaw.
original_explanation: Yan yung itim na inilalatag sa kalsada para maging smooth ang byahe mo, pero sobrang init niyan 'pag bago pa lang. Amoy pa lang, alam mo nang may road project ang DPWH. 'Pag nakakita ka niyan, either may bagong kalsada o may tinatapalan lang na butas na parang band-aid sa sugat ng kahapon.
usage_notes: Ang "asphalt" sa Ingles ay madalas ding gamitin sa mga pangungusap sa Tagalog. Ang "aspalto" ang pormal na Tagalog na katumbas nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mainit pa ang bagong buhos na **aspalto** sa daan.","translation":"The newly poured **asphalt** on the road is still hot."},{"sentence":"Nagreklamo ang mga motorista dahil sa mga butas sa **aspalto**.","translation":"Motorists complained about the potholes in the **asphalt**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng pinal na pasya o hatol tungkol sa isang bagay o usapin.
original_explanation: Ito yung verb form ng 'disisyon.' Kapag sinabing '**Disisyunan** mo na 'yan!', ibig sabihin, 'Mag-decide ka na, please lang, 'wag mo nang patagalin pa!' Para kang nasa 'Deal or No Deal' at kailangan mo nang pumili between the banker's offer and your briefcase.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin ang anyong 'desisyunan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan na nating **disisyunan** kung saan tayo magbabakasyon.","translation":"We need to **decide on** where we will go for vacation."},{"sentence":"**Disisyunan** mo na kung tatanggapin mo ang alok na trabaho.","translation":"**Make a decision about** whether you will accept the job offer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sasakyang ginagamit upang ihatid ang kabaong na naglalaman ng labi ng isang yumaong tao patungo sa simbahan o sa huling hantungan nito.
original_explanation: The final ride. It's the GrabCar for your last trip on Earth, but with more flowers and crying relatives. The original "slow ride," but not in a good way.
usage_notes: A specific type of "karo" (carriage) used exclusively for funerals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahan-dahang umuusad ang **karo ng patay** sa kalsada.","translation":"The **hearse** moved slowly down the street."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdating sa wakas ng isang gawain, kaganapan, o panahon sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The mantra of every student during finals week and every employee on a Friday afternoon: 'Matatapos din 'to.' (This will also end.) It's the light at the end of the tunnel, the promise that your suffering (or your shift) has an expiration date.
usage_notes: Future tense of the verb 'matapos' (to finish).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailan kaya **matatapos** ang pandemyang ito?","translation":"When **will** this pandemic **end**?"},{"sentence":"**Matatapos** ang pelikula sa loob ng dalawang oras.","translation":"The movie **will finish** in two hours."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magpahinga sa isang estado ng kawalang-malay kung saan ang katawan at isipan ay nagpapalakas.
original_explanation: The ultimate solution to 99% of your problems. Stressed sa work? Matulog ka. Gutom? Matulog ka muna. Brokenhearted? I-tulog mo na lang 'yan. It's the Filipino's national pastime and universal cure-all.
usage_notes: The most basic and common verb for 'to sleep'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **matulog** nang maaga dahil may pasok ako bukas.","translation":"I need **to sleep** early because I have work tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Masarap **matulog** kapag umuulan.","translation":"It feels good **to sleep** when it's raining."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa sukdulang kahirapan, kababaan ng kalagayan, o kaapihan.
original_explanation: This is the state of the third-party character in a teleserye after the bida gets everything. It's being so down in life that you feel like a 'sawi sa pag-ibig, sawi sa career' meme. It’s a level of humility or poverty that’s dramatic and profound.
usage_notes: A very strong and dramatic word. Used more in literature, songs, and formal speech than in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa trahedya, naiwan siyang **abang-aba** at walang makain.","translation":"Because of the tragedy, he was left **miserable** and with nothing to eat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mahabang upuan na may sandalan at patungan ng braso, na karaniwang kayang upuan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: That fancy-sounding word your tita uses for a sofa, especially the small, elegant-looking one in the sala that no one is actually allowed to sit on. It's usually covered in plastic or a very precious-looking throw. It’s a step up from a 'sofa', and leagues away from a humble 'monobloc'.
usage_notes: Less common than 'sofa'. Often implies a more formal or elegant piece of furniture. This is a homonym of 'kanape' (appetizer).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umupo ka muna sa **kanape** habang hinihintay mo siya.","translation":"Please sit on the **sofa** while you wait for him."}]

translation: to criticize; to point out a flaw
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpuna o pagpansin sa isang kamalian, kapintasan, o pagkukulang ng isang tao o bagay.
etymology: From the root word 'batik' which can mean a spot, stain, or blemish, hence figuratively a flaw.
original_explanation: What your relatives do during a family reunion. "Uy, tumaba ka." "Wala ka pa ring jowa?" It's the act of finding a flaw, whether it's constructive criticism or just plain 'Marites-level' observation.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation, implying fault-finding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang ginawa ang kritiko kundi **bumatik** sa bawat pelikulang kanyang napanood.","translation":"The critic did nothing but **criticize** every movie he watched."},{"sentence":"Sa halip na **bumatik**, bakit hindi ka na lang tumulong?","translation":"Instead of **criticizing**, why don't you just help?"}]

meaning_filipino: 1. Isang matamis at malagkit na likido na gawa ng mga pukyutan mula sa nektar ng mga bulaklak. 2. Isang malambing na tawagan para sa isang minamahal.
original_explanation: Can be two things: 1) The pampatamis for your tea, also known as 'pulot-pukyutan'. 2) The pampatamis for your life, the person you text 'kain ka na' to. Often shortened to 'hon' or 'honi'. It's the universal password for your partner's phone (just kidding... maybe).
usage_notes: Used both for the food item and as a term of endearment. The Tagalog word for the food is 'pulot' or 'pulot-pukyutan', but 'honey' is extremely common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap lagyan ng **honey** ang tsaa kapag may ubo ka.","translation":"It's good to put **honey** in your tea when you have a cough."},{"sentence":"'**Honey**, huwag mong kalimutan bumili ng bigas pag-uwi,' sabi ni misis.","translation":"'**Honey**, don't forget to buy rice on your way home,' said the wife."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kosmetikong paggamot at pagpapaganda sa mga kuko at kamay.
etymology: From Spanish 'manicura' or English 'manicure', ultimately from Latin 'manus' (hand) + 'cura' (care).
original_explanation: This is the official term for getting your nails did. It's the process of cleaning, filing, and painting your fingernails, often accompanied by some serious chismis with the manikyurista. A fresh manikyur can make you feel like you can conquer the world, or at least your next Zoom meeting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpa-**manikyur** siya bilang paghahanda sa kasal ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"She got a **manicure** in preparation for her friend's wedding."},{"sentence":"Magkano na ngayon ang isang sesyon ng **manikyur** at pedikyur?","translation":"How much is a session of **manicure** and pedicure now?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahilig makialam o manghimasok sa usapan, buhay, o gawain ng iba na hindi naman siya kasali.
original_explanation: The 'Marites' in chief. This is your tita who asks 'Kailan ka mag-aasawa?' at every family gathering. They're the officemate who leans over your shoulder to see what you're typing, or the neighbor who knows your Shopee delivery schedule better than you do. They live for other people's business.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang konsepto sa kulturang Pilipino, madalas na iniuugnay sa tsismis at kawalan ng paggalang sa personal na espasyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakainis ang mga **taong mapanghimasok** na laging may opinyon sa buhay mo.","translation":"**Meddling people** who always have an opinion about your life are annoying."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **taong mapanghimasok**, alam ni Aling Nena ang lahat ng tsismis sa kanilang barangay.","translation":"As an **intrusive person**, Aling Nena knows all the gossip in their barangay."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar na inaasahang mapupuno o aapawan ng tubig-baha sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The annual prophecy for many low-lying areas in Metro Manila during typhoon season. When PAGASA says 'heavy rainfall,' your neighborhood group chat starts spamming 'Babahaan daw tayo!' It's the reason why your ground-floor appliances suddenly learn how to swim.
usage_notes: This is the locative/object-focused future tense, indicating the place that will experience the flood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa balita, **babahaan** na naman ang Marikina dahil sa malakas na ulan.","translation":"According to the news, Marikina **will be flooded** again because of the heavy rain."}]

translation: to be filled; to become full
meaning_filipino: Maging puno o umabot sa hangganan ng kapasidad ng isang lalagyan o espasyo.
original_explanation: Yung feeling mo kapag long weekend at puno na ang booking mo sa beach. Or yung jeepney sa umaga na kahit isang hininga na lang ang kasya, may sasakay pa. Also applies to your patience kapag na-reach mo na ang quota mo sa ka-plastikan for the day. 'Pasensya ko, malapit nang mapuno!'
usage_notes: Can refer to physical spaces, containers, or abstract concepts like patience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malapit nang **mapuno** ang timba dahil sa malakas na ulan.","translation":"The pail is about to **be filled** because of the strong rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking mahilig makipag-ugnayan sa maraming babae nang sabay-sabay, na walang intensyong magseryoso; babaero.
original_explanation: The guy your mom warned you about. He's got a different 'Babe' for every day of the week, a phonebook that looks like a BPO directory, and more excuses than a student on deadline day. His theme song is probably 'Bebot' by the Black Eyed Peas. A certified 'paasa'.
usage_notes: Used identically to its English meaning. 'Babaero' is the more traditional Tagalog equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siyang **playboy** sa buong campus kaya iwasan mo siya.","translation":"He's known as a **playboy** on the whole campus, so avoid him."},{"sentence":"Sa huli, nagsisi rin ang **playboy** nang iwan siya ng lahat.","translation":"In the end, the **womanizer** regretted it when everyone left him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang walang kulay, walang lasa, at walang amoy na likido na bumubuo sa mga ilog, lawa, karagatan, at ulan, at siyang batayan ng mga likido sa katawan ng mga buhay na organismo.
original_explanation: The ultimate life-hack. Thirsty? Drink tubig. Hot? Ligo sa tubig. Broke until payday? Tubig-tubig muna sa kanin. From the 'baha' during typhoons to the 'mineral water' you buy at 7-Eleven, it's the most essential, and sometimes most destructive, thing in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng isang basong **tubig**.","translation":"Please pass a glass of **water**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating magtipid ng **tubig** dahil sa El Niño.","translation":"We need to conserve **water** because of El Niño."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkalahatang kapakanan at maayos na kalagayan ng isang komunidad o lipunan, kasama ang kalusugan, edukasyon, at seguridad.
etymology: A phrase composed of 'kagalingan' (well-being) and 'panlipunan' (social, from 'lipunan').
original_explanation: This is 'kagalingan' (welfare) but for the whole squad, the whole barangay, the whole country. It's the goal of government agencies like DSWD. It means everyone has access to basic needs, is safe, and has a chance to succeed. It's the ultimate group project.
usage_notes: A formal term used in sociology, political science, and government.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga programa ang gobyerno para sa **kagalingang panlipunan**.","translation":"The government has programs for **social welfare**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkakaisa ay susi sa pagkamit ng **kagalingang panlipunan**.","translation":"Unity is the key to achieving **social welfare**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lihim at tila maliliit na gawain na maaaring ituring na pagtataksil sa isang romantikong relasyon, bagaman hindi ito umaabot sa pisikal na pakikipagtalik.
original_explanation: Ito yung pag-like mo sa lahat ng post ng ex mo, pag-reply sa story ng 'work friend' mo nang "ang ganda mo naman," o pag-delete ng chat history para walang ebidensya. Technically, hindi ka nanloloko, pero parang nag-a-apply ka na for the position. It's the "free taste" of cheating.
usage_notes: A very modern, 21st-century term used primarily by millennials and Gen Z to describe ambiguous actions in a relationship that blur the lines of fidelity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtatago niya ng chat nila ng katrabaho niya ay **microcheating** na para sa akin.","translation":"His hiding their chats with his coworker is already **micro-cheating** for me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na nagpapahiwatig ng posibilidad, kawalan ng katiyakan, o pagkakataon; katumbas ng "marahil" o "baka".
original_explanation: This is the more poetic, almost-archaic cousin of "baka" (maybe). You wouldn't use this when texting your friend "Baka malate ako." You'd use it in a dramatic monologue or a heartfelt "kundiman." It's the "perhaps" you use when pondering life's great mysteries. "Kaypala'y magkita tayong muli sa ilalim ng buwan." See? Instant drama.
usage_notes: Considered literary or old-fashioned. 'Marahil' and 'baka' are far more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kaypala**'y hindi na siya babalik pa.","translation":"**Perhaps** he will not be coming back anymore."},{"sentence":"Sa ating muling pagkikita, **kaypala**'y masaya na ang lahat.","translation":"When we meet again, **perhaps** everyone will be happy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malambot na batong apog na ginagamit sa pagsulat sa pisara o pagguhit sa sahig.
original_explanation: The ammunition of every Filipino teacher before the age of whiteboards and smartboards. Also, the primary tool for drawing piko (hopscotch) grids on the sidewalk. That dusty feeling on your hands is part of the core memory.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha mo nga ang **tsok** sa mesa ng titser.","translation":"Please get the **chalk** from the teacher's table."},{"sentence":"Puro **tsok** ang likod ng damit mo.","translation":"Your back is covered in **chalk**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sistematikong pag-aaral at pagsisiyasat sa isang paksa upang makatuklas ng mga bagong kaalaman o makapagpatunay ng mga teorya.
original_explanation: Ah, the national sport of Filipino college students. It's the process of having 50 browser tabs open, fueled by instant noodles and coffee, trying to find 'related literature' at 3 AM. It’s also what you do to your crush's social media profile, scrolling back to their 2012 posts. That, my friend, is also `pagsaliksik`.
usage_notes: A very common word in academic and formal settings. Often used interchangeably with 'pananaliksik'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsaliksik** ay mahalagang bahagi ng pag-aaral sa kolehiyo.","translation":"**Research** is an important part of college studies."},{"sentence":"Nagsagawa sila ng masusing **pagsaliksik** tungkol sa epekto ng social media.","translation":"They conducted a thorough **investigation** on the effects of social media."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na kusang-loob na ibinibigay sa isang tao nang walang bayad, karaniwan upang ipagdiwang ang isang okasyon o bilang tanda ng pagmamahal.
original_explanation: The cause of both holiday stress and joy. Can be anything from a crisp 1000-peso bill from a generous ninong to a fruitcake that gets passed around every Christmas until it's practically a family heirloom. The best ones are 'pasalubong' you didn't even ask for.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap ako ng maraming **regalo** noong aking kaarawan.","translation":"I received many **gifts** on my birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isagawa ang isang pag-atake sa isang partikular na target, tao man o bagay.
etymology: From 'atake' + '-in' suffix, indicating a direct object focus.
original_explanation: The focused, one-way version of 'atake'. This is the 'go' signal. When your squad leader in a game says "Atakihin ang base!", you go. When your mom tells you "Atakihin mo na 'yang mga hugasin," it means wage war on those dirty dishes. It's a command to direct your offensive energy towards a specific target.
usage_notes: The '-in' suffix marks the object of the attack as the focus of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalak nilang **atakihin** ang kampo sa gabi.","translation":"They planned **to attack** the camp at night."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang **atakihin** nang personal.","translation":"Don't **attack** him personally."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makina na gumagamit ng enerhiyang elektrikal upang makabuo ng mekanikal na pag-galaw.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng Ingles na "motor" at Espanyol na "de corriente" (ng kuryente).
original_explanation: Ito yung puso ng e-bike at e-scooter mo. Yung dahilan kung bakit umaandar ang electric fan mo nang hindi ka nagpapaypay. Basically, magic na pinapagana ng Meralco bill. Tahimik pero malakas... umandar at kumain ng kuryente.
usage_notes: Madalas paikliin bilang "e-motor" o "motor" lamang sa konteksto. Ang "de-koryente" ay isang klasikong paraan ng pagsasabing "electric" na hango sa Espanyol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasira ang **motor na de-koryente** ng washing machine kaya hindi na ito umiikot.","translation":"The **electric motor** of the washing machine broke, so it doesn't spin anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtrato sa isang tao bilang alipin o mas mababa; ang pagpapakita ng kapangyarihan sa isang mapanupil na paraan.
original_explanation: This is when someone acts like they're the main character and everyone else is just an extra. Think of a micromanager boss who breathes down your neck, or that one groupmate who rejects all your ideas and insists on their own. It's giving "Ako ang bida dito" energy in the worst way possible.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of oppression or arrogance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **panginoonin** ang iyong mga nasasakupan.","translation":"Do not **lord over** your subordinates."},{"sentence":"Ayaw ng mga empleyado na **pinanginoon** sila ng kanilang manager.","translation":"The employees do not want to be **dominated** by their manager."}]

translation: act of looking out (from a window)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtingin sa labas mula sa isang bintana, pinto, o anumang mataas na bukanan.
original_explanation: The official hobby of every Marites in the neighborhood, peeking through the window to get the latest chismis. It's what you do when you hear the 'pot-pot' of the taho vendor or the ice cream truck's jingle.
usage_notes: Specifically implies looking out and often down from an elevated opening like a window or balcony.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging ugali na niya ang **pagdungaw** sa bintana tuwing umaga.","translation":"It became her habit **to look out** the window every morning."},{"sentence":"Isang mabilis na **pagdungaw** lang ang ginawa niya para tingnan kung sino ang dumating.","translation":"He only took a quick **look out** to see who had arrived."}]

translation: a huge amount, a ton of
meaning_filipino: Isang napakaraming bilang o dami ng isang bagay; hindi mabilang sa dami.
etymology: From `sang-` (one) + `ka-` + `terba` (a large, unspecific amount). The origin of 'terba' itself is debated but is used colloquially.
original_explanation: The official measurement for your workload on a Monday morning, the amount of chismis your tita has, or the number of unread messages in your family's Viber group. It’s not a precise number; it's a feeling. The feeling of "OMG, ang dami!"
usage_notes: Informal and colloquial. Used to express a very large, often overwhelming, quantity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **sangkaterba** akong labahin na naghihintay sa bahay.","translation":"I have a **ton of** laundry waiting at home."},{"sentence":"**Sangkaterba** ang dumating na bisita sa piyesta.","translation":"**A huge amount** of guests arrived at the festival."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalaman ng maraming maliliit na bahagi o impormasyon; masusi at nagbibigay-pansin sa mga detalye.
original_explanation: Describes your friend who can recount the entire plot of a K-drama, including what the characters wore and ate in each scene. Also describes your boss who wants the report to be so madetalye that it includes the timestamps of your bathroom breaks. Meticulous to a fault.
usage_notes: A very common adjective in both casual and formal settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong maging **madetalye** sa iyong ulat para maunawaan ito ng lahat.","translation":"You need to be **detailed** in your report so that everyone can understand it."},{"sentence":"Gumawa siya ng isang **madetalye** na plano para sa kanilang bakasyon.","translation":"She made a **detailed** plan for their vacation."}]

translation: faint line or mark; slight scratch
meaning_filipino: Isang manipis na guhit, marka, o mababaw na galos sa isang ibabaw.
original_explanation: That tiny, almost invisible scratch on your phone screen that you can't see, but you *know* is there, and it haunts your soul. Also the faint line on the floor marking where the furniture used to be before you rearranged your room for the 5th time during lockdown.
usage_notes: Often used to describe very fine lines or scratches.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May maliit na **linggit** sa salamin ng kotse.","translation":"There is a small, **faint scratch** on the car's windshield."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **linggit** sa kanyang palad ay nagpapakita ng kanyang pagiging masipag.","translation":"The **faint lines** on his palm show his diligence."}]

translation: to treat (someone); to apply medicine to
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagbibigay ng gamot sa isang tao, hayop, o partikular na bahagi ng katawan upang gumaling.
original_explanation: The command to apply meds. When your friend gets a cut, you tell them, 'Gamutan mo 'yan ng Betadine!' It's the act of playing doctor for a minor injury, or what a real doctor does to a patient.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus verb form, meaning 'to apply medicine TO something/someone'. Stress is on the second syllable: /ga-MU-tan/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gamutan** mo agad ang sugat ng bata para hindi ito maimpeksyon.","translation":"**Apply medicine** to the child's wound immediately so it doesn't get infected."},{"sentence":"Siya ang gumamot sa mga biktima ng aksidente.","translation":"He was the one who **treated** the accident victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagkakaroon ng resulta o ani; hindi nagtatagumpay sa layunin.
original_explanation: Ever spent the whole day "working" but at 5 PM, you realize you've accomplished nothing but scrolling through TikTok? That's a walang-bunga day. It's like a group project where everyone just talks but no one actually does the work. Effort na nauwi sa wala.
usage_notes: Used literally for plants that do not bear fruit or figuratively for efforts, meetings, or discussions that yield no results.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng sampung taon, nanatiling **walang-bunga** ang kanilang puno ng mangga.","translation":"After ten years, their mango tree remained **barren**."},{"sentence":"Naging **walang-bunga** ang aming pag-uusap dahil ayaw niyang makinig.","translation":"Our discussion became **fruitless** because he didn't want to listen."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sistemang pangkalawakan na binubuo ng Araw at lahat ng mga bagay na umiikot dito, kabilang ang mga planeta, buwan, asteroid, at kometa.
original_explanation: That thing you had to memorize in elementary school Science class: Merkuryo, Venus, Daigdig, Marte, Hupiter, Saturno, Urano, Neptuno. It's the Sun's giant barkada, and Earth is that one friend who has too much drama (and too many people). Pluto is the friend who got kicked out of the group chat.
usage_notes: A technical, scientific term. The '-ng' linker connects the noun 'sistema' and the adjective 'solar'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Daigdig ay ang pangatlong planeta sa ating **Sistemang Solar**.","translation":"Earth is the third planet in our **Solar System**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga astronomo ang mga misteryo ng **Sistemang Solar**.","translation":"Astronomers study the mysteries of the **Solar System**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking kawali na karaniwang yari sa bakal, ginagamit sa pagluluto para sa maraming tao.
original_explanation: The final boss of all kawalis. Ito 'yung ginagamit sa mga fiesta, 'yung kasya isang buong baboy para gawing lechon paksiw. If your handaan doesn't have a **talyasi** bubbling with something delicious, is it even a real handaan?
usage_notes: Distinct from 'kawali' due to its much larger size, typically used for large-scale cooking during fiestas and events.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagluluto si Nanay ng sinigang sa malaking **talyasi** para sa lahat ng bisita.","translation":"Mother is cooking sinigang in a large **vat** for all the guests."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng dalawang tao para buhatin ang mainit na **talyasi**.","translation":"It takes two people to lift the hot **cauldron**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o tao na napili mula sa maraming pagpipilian; ang kilos ng pagpili na naganap na.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na `pili` (pili) at gitlaping `-in-` na nagsasaad ng nagdaang kilos sa pokus ng layon.
original_explanation: The past tense of "to choose." This is what happens when you finally pick a flavor at the milk tea shop after staring at the menu for 10 minutes. It's also a major source of "hugot." "Sa dami ng tao sa mundo, bakit siya pa ang **pinili** mo?" (Of all the people in the world, why did you **choose** him/her?). It can be a triumph (you were chosen for the job!) or a tragedy (you weren't the one chosen).
usage_notes: Past tense, object-focus form of the verb `piliin` (to choose). Can also function as an adjective (e.g., `ang mga piniling kandidato` - the chosen candidates).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pinili** niya ang asul na damit kaysa sa pula.","translation":"She **chose** the blue dress over the red one."},{"sentence":"Ikaw ang **pinili** ng puso ko.","translation":"You are the one my heart **chose**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na sulat, lalo na ang isa na may didaktiko o eleganteng katangian, na karaniwang matatagpuan sa anyong pampanitikan o sa mga banal na kasulatan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'epístola', na mula sa Latin na 'epistola'.
original_explanation: A fancy word for 'sulat' or letter. Think of St. Paul's letters in the Bible, hindi 'yan basta-bastang "Hi, musta?" na text. Ito yung mga sulat na may malalim na hugot at life lessons. Parang 'yung long message na sinend mo sa ex mo at 2 AM, 'yun na 'yung modern **epistola** mo.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong pampanitikan, pangkasaysayan, at panrelihiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binasa ng pari ang isang **epistola** mula sa Bagong Tipan.","translation":"The priest read an **epistle** from the New Testament."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **epistola** ni Rizal ay nagpapakita ng kanyang pagmamahal sa bayan.","translation":"Rizal's **epistles** show his love for the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na itinuturing na kapareha sa isang gawain, lalo na sa sayaw, laro, o sa isang romantikong relasyon.
original_explanation: Your partner-in-crime, your dance partner for the JS prom, or your 'jowa'. In short, the other half of your 'sana all' moment. Not to be confused with 'pares' (the food) or 'pareho' (the feeling when you both have the same crush). From the Spanish 'pareja'.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga tao, samantalang ang 'pares' ay mas madalas para sa mga bagay (maliban kung pagkain ang pinag-uusapan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang magiging **pareha** mo sa sayaw?","translation":"Who will be your **partner** in the dance?"},{"sentence":"Ang ganda tingnan ng mag-**pareha** na iyon.","translation":"That **couple** looks so good together."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mataas na lupa sa gilid ng isang anyong tubig tulad ng ilog, lawa, o dagat.
original_explanation: It's the 'gilid' of a river or sea. Where you have picnics, where the bangka docks, where kids play, and where dramatic movie characters stare off into the distance contemplating life. It's the boundary between solid ground and 'baka malunod ako.'
usage_notes: Can refer to the bank of a river, lake, or the seashore. `Baybayin` is more specific to the sea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglaro ang mga bata sa **pampang** ng ilog.","translation":"The children played on the **riverbank**."},{"sentence":"May nakita kaming malaking bangka na nakadaong sa **pampang**.","translation":"We saw a large boat docked on the **shore**."}]

meaning_filipino: Punong-puno at halos walang natitirang espasyo; masinsin ang pagkakalagay.
original_explanation: This is the state of the MRT at 8 AM. Yung feeling na pati kaluluwa mo, nakikipagsiksikan na. Also applies to your bag after a trip to Divisoria, or your phone's memory after taking 1,000 selfies. 'Siksik, liglig, at umaapaw na biyaya' is the ultimate goal.
usage_notes: Often used in the phrase 'siksik, liglig, at umaapaw,' which means 'packed, shaken, and overflowing,' usually referring to blessings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Siksik** ang mga tao sa loob ng bus tuwing rush hour.","translation":"The people are **packed** inside the bus during rush hour."},{"sentence":"Ang laman ng kahon ay **siksik** sa mga damit.","translation":"The contents of the box are **densely packed** with clothes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o kumpanya na bumibili at nagbebenta ng mga partikular na produkto. Maaari ring tumukoy sa taong namamahagi ng mga baraha sa isang laro.
original_explanation: This person can either sell you your dream car or deal you a bad hand in tong-its. In the Philippines, you have your suking 'dealer' for everything—from the legit car dealer your tito recommends, the 'dealer' of pre-loved bags in Greenhills, to the one who deals the cards during the family reunion's mahjong session. The context is everything!
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context, from legal commerce (car dealer) to games (card dealer) to illegal activities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpunta kami sa **dealer** ng kotse para tumingin ng bagong modelo.","translation":"We went to the car **dealer** to look at new models."},{"sentence":"Ikaw ang taya, kaya ikaw ang **dealer** sa baraha.","translation":"It's your turn, so you're the **dealer** for the cards."}]

translation: to be convinced to buy something; to be swindled
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging biktima ng panloloko o ang matagumpay na pagkumbinsi sa isang tao na bumili ng isang bagay nang hindi planado.
etymology: Tagalog 'budol' + English past tense suffix '-ed'. A classic Taglish construction.
original_explanation: The past tense of 'budol'. This is what happens *after* you've been convinced. 'Na-budol ako ng kaibigan ko' means 'My friend convinced me.' You went to the mall for one thing and came home with five bags. You've been budoled.
usage_notes: Highly informal and slang. Used to describe both being scammed and being persuaded to make an impulse purchase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayun, na-**budol** na naman ako ng 2-for-1 promo.","translation":"And there, I got **suckered in** by the 2-for-1 promo again."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko lang sana tumingin, pero na-**budol** ako ng saleslady.","translation":"I just wanted to look, but I **was convinced** by the saleslady to buy."}]

translation: to be independent; to live on one's own
meaning_filipino: Ang pamumuhay nang hiwalay at hindi umaasa sa iba; ang pag-angkin sa isang bagay para sa sarili lamang.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal of every young adult stuck living with their parents. It's about getting your own place, paying your own Meralco bill, and finally being able to eat ice cream for dinner without judgment. Also what you do with the last piece of pizza.
usage_notes: Can mean 'to be independent' or, in a slightly negative context, 'to hoard' or 'to keep to oneself.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos niyang grumaduate, nagpasya siyang **magsarili** at lumipat sa Maynila.","translation":"After she graduated, she decided to **be independent** and move to Manila."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **magsarili** ang lahat ng kaalaman, ibahagi mo sa iba.","translation":"Don't **keep** all the knowledge **to yourself**, share it with others."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang yugto sa isang umuusbong na relasyon kung saan masusing sinisiyasat ng isang tao ang social media profile at mga nakaraang aktibidad ng taong kanyang nagugustuhan.
original_explanation: Eto yung bago ka pa lang mag-chat sa crush mo, inalam mo na lahat. From their mother's maiden name to their ex's new partner's dog's birthday. Buong Facebook, Instagram, at Twitter feed niya, na-scan mo na. Kasama na diyan ang pagtingin sa mga tagged photos from 2012. Ingat lang sa pag-double tap!
usage_notes: A modern slang term describing the initial 'research' period before or during early courtship, done primarily online.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tapos na ako sa **stalking phase**, alam ko na kung saan siya nag-aral ng high school.","translation":"I'm done with the **stalking phase**; I already know where he went to high school."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang pahalata na nasa **stalking phase** ka, baka matakot siya.","translation":"Don't make it obvious you're in the **stalking phase**, you might scare them off."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maikling salawal na ang haba ay hanggang sa itaas ng tuhod.
original_explanation: The official uniform for staying at home, pambahay chic. Also what you wear when you go to the palengke or play basketball with the kapitbahay. Not to be confused with 'short', which is what your salary feels like after paying all the bills.
usage_notes: Commonly used in everyday conversation as a direct loanword. The Tagalog word 'korto' is also used but 'shorts' is more prevalent among younger generations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magsuot ka ng **shorts** at t-shirt, mainit sa labas.","translation":"Wear **shorts** and a t-shirt, it's hot outside."},{"sentence":"Naiwan ko sa gym ang paborito kong **shorts**.","translation":"I left my favorite **shorts** at the gym."}]

translation: to slash; to make a gash
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggawa ng mahaba at malalim na hiwa sa isang bagay o tao gamit ang matalim na kagamitan.
original_explanation: The verb form. It's what you do when you're angry at a box from Shopee and decide to open it with extreme prejudice. Or, in a more serious context, it's the act of inflicting a slash. A very direct and often violent action.
usage_notes: Often used with an object, indicating what is being slashed. The '-in' suffix marks it as an object-focus verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **laslasin** ang kahon, baka masira ang laman.","translation":"Don't **slash** the box, you might damage the contents."},{"sentence":"Binalaan siya na huwag **laslasin** ang sarili dahil sa matinding kalungkutan.","translation":"He was warned not to **cut** himself due to extreme sadness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na hulaan o sabihin ang isang bagay na hindi tiyak o lingid sa kaalaman.
original_explanation: When you have chismis but you want to make it dramatic. 'Teh, may sasabihin ako sa'yo... pahula muna kung sino nakita ko sa mall kanina!' The official start-up command for any juicy gossip session.
usage_notes: Used informally as a command or request, like in a game or when sharing a secret playfully.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May regalo ako sa'yo, **pahula** ka muna!","translation":"I have a gift for you, **try to guess** first!"},{"sentence":"**Pahula** kung saan ako pupunta bukas.","translation":"**Guess** where I'm going tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkapâ o paghahanap ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagsalat, lalo na sa dilim o kapag hindi makakita.
etymology: From root `apuhap` (to grope for). The `pag-` prefix and reduplication of the first vowel `a` create a noun for the action.
original_explanation: This is what you do when the power goes out and you're looking for your phone or a candle. It's the frantic patting of your pockets for your keys, or trying to find the light switch in a dark room you're not familiar with. It can also be used figuratively, like when you're fumbling for the right words to say after you messed up: "Ah... eh... kasi..."
usage_notes: Can be literal (physical searching) or figurative (searching for an idea or word).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa dilim, narinig ko ang kanyang **pag-aapuhap** sa dingding para hanapin ang pinto.","translation":"In the dark, I heard his **groping** on the wall to find the door."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pag-aapuhap** ng mga salita ay nagpapakita ng kanyang kaba.","translation":"His **fumbling** for words shows his nervousness."}]

translation: to let out (steam, anger); to vent
meaning_filipino: Ilabas o payaang sumingaw ang init, usok, o matinding damdamin.
original_explanation: This is what you do after a horrible day at your BPO job. You call your bestie to 'isungaw ang galit'—to vent all your frustrations about your toxic boss. It's also what a pressure cooker does: it lets out steam so it doesn't explode. Same concept, really. You need to release the pressure before you go boom.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa singaw/usok o sa matalinghagang paraan para sa mga damdamin tulad ng galit o pagkadismaya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **isungaw** ang iyong galit sa pamamagitan ng ehersisyo.","translation":"You need **to vent** your anger through exercise."},{"sentence":"Binuksan niya ang takure para **isungaw** ang init bago ito hugasan.","translation":"She opened the kettle **to let out** the steam before washing it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng saklay na karaniwang ginagamit nang pares, na sumusuporta sa katawan mula sa kili-kili.
original_explanation: Your unwilling best friend after a bad game of basketball or after slipping on a freshly mopped floor at SM. It can also be used metaphorically for a person you're emotionally dependent on, your 'sakit sa ulo' but also your support system. 'Siya ang naging muleta ko noong mga panahong lugmok ako.'
usage_notes: Partikular na tumutukoy sa mga saklay sa kili-kili, bagaman kung minsan ay ginagamit nang mas malawak para sa anumang pantulong sa paglakad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangan niyang gumamit ng **muleta** matapos mabalian ng binti.","translation":"He needed to use **crutches** after breaking his leg."},{"sentence":"Ang mga kaibigan niya ang nagsilbing **muleta** niya sa panahon ng kalungkutan.","translation":"His friends served as his **crutch** during his time of sadness."}]

translation: to act like a lady; to embrace one's femininity
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos o pag-asal na inaasahan sa isang babae ayon sa pamantayan ng lipunan; ang pagtanggap at pagpapahayag ng pagiging babae.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mag-` (gumanap ng kilos), `paka-` (pagsisikap na maging), at salitang-ugat na `babae` (woman, female).
original_explanation: This is what your lola tells you when you're acting too much like a 'tomboy' or being too loud. 'Hija, `magpakababae` ka naman.' It means to act more 'feminine'—sit properly, speak softly, be graceful. In a modern sense, it can also be a powerful call to embrace womanhood in all its forms, defying old stereotypes. It's the journey from 'one of the boys' to a full-fledged 'dalagang Pilipina'.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay maaaring maging tradisyonal (pagsunod sa gender roles) o moderno (empowerment). Ang tono ay maaaring maging mapanuto o naghihikayat depende sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi ng lola ko, dapat daw akong matutong **magpakababae**.","translation":"My grandmother said I should learn to **act like a proper lady**."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang **magpakababae** ay ang pagiging matatag at may sariling paninindigan.","translation":"For her, to **embrace her femininity** means to be strong and have her own principles."}]

translation: to hit, to strike; to deliver a line
meaning_filipino: Ang paghampas o pagpalo nang may lakas; o ang pagbibitaw ng isang pahayag, komento, o biro.
original_explanation: Two main uses: 1) The literal 'sumuntok' or 'humampas' (to punch/hit). 2) The more common modern use: when someone drops a witty comment, a savage comeback, or a cheesy pick-up line. 'Bumanat ka na naman ng hugot!' is a national pastime. This is the verb form of making 'banat'.
usage_notes: Has both a literal meaning of striking and a very common colloquial meaning of delivering a line (witty, hurtful, or romantic). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **bumanat** sa kapatid mo!","translation":"Don't you **hit** your sibling!"},{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **bumanat** ng, 'Sana charger ka na lang, para 'di kumpleto araw ko 'pag wala ka.'","translation":"He suddenly **delivered a line**, 'I wish you were a charger, so my day wouldn't be complete without you.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Angkop o kasama sa isang pamantayan, kategorya, o grupo; natanggap.
original_explanation: When your crush's standards are 'tall, dark, and handsome' and you're... well, you. You're not 'pasok'. But when your resume perfectly matches the job description, you're 'pasok na pasok'! It's the feeling of making the cut, whether for a team, a job, or the family budget.
usage_notes: Pronunciation is key to differentiate from 'pasok' (enter). The stress is on the second syllable for 'qualified'. Often used in the context of budgets, criteria, or standards.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa tingin mo ba ay **pasok** ang sapatos na ito sa budget ko?","translation":"Do you think these shoes **fit** within my budget?"},{"sentence":"Lahat ng kwalipikasyon mo ay **pasok** sa hinahanap namin.","translation":"All your qualifications are **included** in what we are looking for."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o damdamin ng paunang pag-alam o pagdama sa isang bagay na mangyayari sa hinaharap, kadalasan ay negatibo.
original_explanation: That gut feeling you get that something's about to go down, like when your boss calls you for a "quick chat" on a Friday afternoon. It's the universe sending you a spoiler alert, but usually for a drama, not a comedy.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative or anxious connotation. More formal than 'kutob'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **paghihinagap** si Aling Nena na may masamang mangyayari sa kanyang anak.","translation":"Aling Nena had a **foreboding** that something bad would happen to her child."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **paghihinagap** ay nagkatotoo nang biglang bumuhos ang malakas na ulan.","translation":"Her **premonition** came true when the heavy rain suddenly poured."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na naunawaan, naintindihan, o malinaw na.
original_explanation: The classic, slightly formal way of saying 'Got it!' or 'Understood.' It's what your boss says after you explain a complex process, or what you say to your parents to show you're listening (even if you're not). It's the verbal checkmark that means 'Okay, we're on the same page. Next!'
usage_notes: Often used as a single-word response.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Entendido**, sir. Sisimulan ko na po ang gawain.","translation":"**Understood**, sir. I will start the task now."},{"sentence":"Malinaw ba ang mga panuto? **Entendido**?","translation":"Are the instructions clear? **Understood**?"}]

translation: To throw; to hurl; to pitch
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghagis o pagbato ng isang bagay nang may pwersa, karaniwan ay gumagamit ng kamay.
original_explanation: This is a more intense 'hagis' or 'bato'. It’s not just a toss, it’s a throw with intent and force. Think of a baseball pitcher's fast ball, or when you're so mad you 'pukol' your phone onto the bed (hopefully not the floor). It's a throw with 'gigil'.
usage_notes: Often implies a stronger, more forceful throw than 'hagis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang **pukol** ng bola ng manlalaro ng baseball.","translation":"The baseball player's **pitch** of the ball is strong."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang galit niya, halos ma**pukol** niya ang hawak na baso.","translation":"In his extreme anger, he almost **hurled** the glass he was holding."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at karaniwang marangyang sasakyang pandagat na ginagamit para sa pagliliwaliw, paglalayag, o karera.
original_explanation: The ultimate #SanaAll water vehicle. It's not a balsa, it's not a bangka, it's a **yate** – a floating mansion for the super-rich to party on while the rest of us are stuck in EDSA traffic. If you own one, you've probably made it in life. Or you're a politician.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita namin ang isang malaking **yate** na nakadaong sa Subic Bay.","translation":"We saw a large **yacht** docked at Subic Bay."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa baligtad na posisyon; kung saan ang itaas na bahagi ay nasa ibaba at ang ibabang bahagi ay nasa itaas.
original_explanation: When your world goes 'tiwarik', everything's gone crazy. It's like finding out your favorite milk tea shop uses powdered juice, or when your Grab driver goes in the complete opposite direction. Literally, it’s what happens when a jeepney flips over, but figuratively, it's the state of your life during Mercury retrograde.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical orientation or figuratively to mean a situation has gone completely wrong or opposite of what's expected.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naaksidente ang bus kaya ito'y **tiwarik** sa gitna ng kalsada.","translation":"The bus got into an accident, so it was **upside down** in the middle of the road."},{"sentence":"Naging **tiwarik** ang mundo niya nang malaman niyang hindi siya mahal ng kanyang minamahal.","translation":"His world turned **upside down** when he found out the one he loves doesn't love him back."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbibigay ng dalubhasang paghatol o opinyon, lalo na sa sining, panitikan, musika, o pelikula.
original_explanation: The professional version of a 'Maritess.' They get paid to give their opinions on movies, food, or books. Also, anyone on the internet with a keyboard and an opinion. 'Everyone's a critic,' as they say.
usage_notes: Usually refers to a professional critic, but can be used colloquially for anyone who is very critical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinuri ng mga **kritiko** ang pagganap ng pangunahing aktor.","translation":"The **critics** praised the lead actor's performance."}]

translation: connection; the way something is joined or connected
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagkakakonekta o pagkakabit ng dalawa o higit pang bagay upang maging magkaugnay.
etymology: From `pag-` + `ka-` + `ka-` (reduplication) + `dugtong`. The prefix `pagkaka-` refers to the manner of connection.
original_explanation: This is how two separate chismis are connected to form a mega-chismis. It's the joint, the link, the "what connects A to B." Think of the Skyway connecting SLEX and NLEX, or how your story connects to your friend's alibi.
usage_notes: Often used for physical connections or for linking stories, ideas, or parts of a whole.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahina ang **pagkakadugtong** ng dalawang kable kaya nawalan ng internet.","translation":"The **connection** of the two cables was weak, so the internet was lost."},{"sentence":"Malinaw ang **pagkakadugtong** ng mga ebidensya laban sa suspek.","translation":"The **connection** of the evidence against the suspect is clear."}]

meaning_filipino: Naaayon sa katotohanan o realidad; hindi huwad, peke, o gawa-gawa lamang.
original_explanation: The ultimate fact-checker word. You use it to confirm if the chismis is legit ('Totoo ba?'). You use it to emphasize you're not kidding ('Promise, totoo!'). It’s the difference between 'fake news' and 'breaking news.' In a world of filters and curated posts, everyone's just looking for something 'totoo'.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang tanong ('Totoo?'), pahayag, o pang-abay ('totoong masaya'). Madalas inuulit para sa diin ('totoong-totoo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako makapaniwala na **totoo** ang lahat ng narinig ko.","translation":"I can't believe that everything I heard is **true**."},{"sentence":"**Totoo** bang nanalo ka sa lotto?","translation":"Is it **true** that you won the lottery?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang espasyo, hukay, o puwang sa isang bagay na karaniwang tumatagos mula sa isang panig patungo sa kabila.
original_explanation: The reason why your 'ipon' (savings) in your piggy bank isn't growing—kasi `butas` ang bulsa mo (your pocket has a hole). It's that annoying gap in your socks, the pothole on EDSA that can swallow a small car, or a flaw in an alibi. "May butas ang kwento mo." (Your story has holes.)
usage_notes: Can be a noun (a hole) or an adjective (having a hole, e.g., "butas na medyas").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **butas** ang gulong ng kotse kaya na-flat ito.","translation":"The car tire has a **hole**, that's why it went flat."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang bumili ng balde na **butas**.","translation":"Don't buy a pail that has a **hole**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng matamis na gawa sa kinayod na niyog na niluto sa arnibal o asukal na pula.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino sweet tooth-killer. It's shredded coconut swimming in caramelized sugar, so sweet it'll make your fillings vibrate. Comes in two forms: the soft, gooey kind you eat with a spoon, and the hard, flat disc that could double as a weapon. The perfect pasalubong from a provincial trip.
usage_notes: A popular delicacy and pasalubong (souvenir) in many Philippine provinces.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong ubusin ang **bukayo**, magtira ka para kay bunso.","translation":"Don't finish the **bukayo**, leave some for the youngest."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong pasalubong ay **bukayo** mula sa Baguio.","translation":"My favorite souvenir is **coconut candy** from Baguio."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lambat na may maliliit na butas, ginagamit sa panghuhuli ng maliliit na isda, hipon, o alamang.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping 'paN-' (nagiging 'pan-') at sa salitang-ugat na 'sambil', isang lumang salita para sa 'pagsalo' o 'paghuli gamit ang net'.
original_explanation: This isn't your ordinary fishing net. It's the high-resolution, ultra-fine version for catching the small fry, literally. Think of it as the fisherman's tool for catching *dilis* or tiny shrimp for making *bagoong*. It's a net that doesn't let the little guys get away. A bit like your mom's ability to notice every small detail you thought you hid.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino sa pangingisda. Hindi karaniwang naririnig sa pang-araw-araw na usapan maliban sa mga komunidad ng mangingisda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dala ng mangingisda ang kanyang **panambil** upang manghuli ng alamang.","translation":"The fisherman brought his **fine-meshed net** to catch shrimp paste fry."},{"sentence":"Napuno ng maliliit na isda ang **panambil** pagkatapos itong ihagis sa ilog.","translation":"The **fine-meshed net** was filled with small fish after it was cast into the river."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking kasangkapan, karaniwang gawa sa kahoy, na may mga pinto at istante, ginagamit na lalagyan ng mga damit, kumot, at iba pang gamit sa bahay.
original_explanation: The classic Pinoy closet, usually made of heavy narra wood, that smells like your lola's mothballs and secrets. It's where you find old photo albums, your baptismal gown, and that one shirt you've been looking for since 2015.
usage_notes: A staple piece of furniture in many Filipino households, often passed down through generations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinago ni Lola ang kanyang mga alahas sa loob ng lumang **aparador**.","translation":"Grandma kept her jewelry inside the old **wardrobe**."},{"sentence":"Pakiayos ng mga damit mo sa **aparador**.","translation":"Please arrange your clothes in the **closet**."}]

translation: to allow oneself to be caught; to be late intentionally
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagkilos upang mahuli o madakip; o ang sinasadyang pagdating nang hindi sa takdang oras; o ang pagpayag na maging pinakahuli sa isang pila o karera.
etymology: From mag- (actor-focus verb prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + huli (late, last, caught).
original_explanation: This has a few meanings. 1) When you're playing hide-and-seek and you're tired, so you "accidentally" make a noise para magpahuli. 2) "Filipino time" in verb form: when you intentionally show up late to an event to make a grand entrance. "Magpapahuli ako ng 30 minutes para hindi ako maunang dumating sa party." 3) Letting someone else go first, making yourself the last one.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context: being caught (`mahuli`), being late (`mahuli`), or being last (`huli`). `Magpahuli` is the causative/permissive form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na akong magtago kaya **nagpahuli** na lang ako.","translation":"I was tired of hiding so I just **let myself be caught**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpahuli** sa klase bukas dahil mayroon tayong pagsusulit.","translation":"Don't **be late** for class tomorrow because we have a quiz."},{"sentence":"Bilang respeto, **nagpahuli** siya sa pila para sa mga senior citizen.","translation":"Out of respect, he **let himself be last** in line for the senior citizens."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akdang pampanitikan; kagamitan sa paglikha ng panitikan. Ito ay isang lumang salita.
etymology: From `pan-` + `takda` (assigned, set). It refers to something created or set down in writing.
original_explanation: This is a deep Tagalog word, the kind your Lolo would use while reading a dusty book. Think of it as the OG "content." Before blogs, vlogs, and TikToks, there was `panakda`—the actual written stuff, like poems and essays. It can also mean the tool used for it, like a classic pen. It's the whole literary shebang.
usage_notes: This is a very formal and somewhat archaic term. `Akda` is far more common in modern usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga **panakda** ay naglalaman ng malalim na pag-ibig sa bayan.","translation":"His **literary pieces** contain a deep love for the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mapalibutan o mapaligidan ng mga bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
etymology: From ma- (ability/accidental verb prefix) + ligid (surround) + -an (locative suffix).
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na nasa gitna ka ng chismisan at lahat ng mata, nakatutok sa'yo. Or 'yung bahay niyo, maligiran ng mga panindang ukay-ukay tuwing Sabado. It's when you're the center of attention, whether you like it or not.
usage_notes: Often used to describe being physically surrounded or being in the midst of a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **maligiran** ng mga taong negatibo.","translation":"He/She doesn't want **to be surrounded** by negative people."},{"sentence":"Ang aming bahay ay **naliligiran** ng matataas na puno.","translation":"Our house **is surrounded** by tall trees."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggawa ng isang bagay sa kabila ng kahirapan o pagtutol; ang paggamit ng puwersa o determinasyon upang makamit ang isang layunin.
original_explanation: This is your friend insisting 'isa pa, isa pang beer!' at 2 AM. It's you trying to make a relationship work even when all the signs say 'log off na, bes.' It can be good (effort, perseverance) or bad (forcing the issue, being pushy). It's the classic Filipino 'pilit' smile when a relative you don't like visits.
usage_notes: The meaning can range from positive perseverance to negative coercion depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pagpipilit**, natapos din niya ang kanyang pag-aaral.","translation":"Through his **effort** (insistence), he was finally able to finish his studies."},{"sentence":"Ayaw ko ng **pagpipilit**; kung ayaw mo, huwag na.","translation":"I don't like **insistence**; if you don't want to, then don't."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balon na may manwal na bombang ginagamit upang kumuha ng tubig mula sa ilalim ng lupa.
original_explanation: The original "unli-water" station of the province. This is where you get your arm workout for the day, pumping that rusty handle up and down. The water is usually ice-cold and perfect for a "tabo" bath on a hot day. It's a symbol of community and simpler times.
usage_notes: Karaniwan sa mga probinsya o mga lugar na walang sentralisadong sistema ng tubig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumila ang mga tao sa **poso** upang kumuha ng malinis na inuming tubig pagkatapos ng bagyo.","translation":"People lined up at the **water pump** to get clean drinking water after the typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong tumatanggap ng medikal na atensyon, pangangalaga, o paggamot.
original_explanation: Ito yung taong naghihintay ng tatlong oras sa waiting room ng clinic para sa 10-minute check-up. Sila rin yung laging tinatanong ng mga kamag-anak, "Ano daw sabi ng doktor?" after ng bawat appointment. Kailangan nila ng maraming 'pasyensya'. Gets?
usage_notes: Ginagamit lamang sa kontekstong medikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **pasyente** ang naghihintay sa emergency room.","translation":"There are many **patients** waiting in the emergency room."},{"sentence":"Ang **pasyente** ay pinayuhang magpahinga nang mabuti.","translation":"The **patient** was advised to rest well."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsuporta o pagnanais na magkaroon ng romantikong relasyon sa pagitan ng dalawang tao, na karaniwan ay mga tauhan sa isang akda, pelikula, o mga totoong tao (celebrity).
etymology: From English 'relationship', shortened to 'ship' in fan culture.
original_explanation: Fandom term, short for 'relationship'. Ito yung gusto mong maging mag-jowa ang dalawang tao, fictional man o totoo. 'I-ship ko talaga si Popoy at Basha.' Kapag may bago kang OTP (One True Pairing), sila ang 'shini-ship' mo. It's the act of playing virtual matchmaker for your faves.
usage_notes: Almost always used as a verb with Tagalog affixes, e.g., 'shini-ship', 'i-ship'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal ko nang **shini-ship** ang dalawang bida sa K-drama na iyon.","translation":"I've been **shipping** the two main characters in that K-drama for a long time."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo kaming i-**ship**, magkaibigan lang kami!","translation":"Don't **ship** us, we're just friends!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pamalit na walang tiyak na kahulugan, ginagamit kapag hindi maalala o ayaw banggitin ang isang salita, bagay, o ideya.
etymology: From Filipino gay slang (Swardspeak). The exact origin is unclear, but it functions as a placeholder word.
original_explanation: The ultimate life-saver word when your brain decides to take a coffee break. Can mean anything from "that thing" to "that situation" to "you know what I mean, girl." The Swiss Army knife of Pinoy slang. The OG "whatever."
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'churva'. It's a highly versatile term in informal conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha naman ng **chorva** sa ibabaw ng mesa.","translation":"Please get the **whatchamacallit** on top of the table."},{"sentence":"Ang dami niyang sinabing **chorva** na hindi ko naintindihan.","translation":"He said a lot of **stuff** that I didn't understand."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isda na karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga tubig-alat at tubig-tabang, na kilala sa pagtalon nito mula sa tubig.
original_explanation: A type of fish you'd find in the 'palengke' (wet market). It's not as high-profile as 'bangus' or 'tilapia', but it's a staple. Also, don't confuse it with the 80s hairstyle, though both were probably popular at the same time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap iprito ang sariwang **banak**.","translation":"Fresh **mullet** is delicious when fried."},{"sentence":"Nakabili si nanay ng malalaking **banak** sa palengke kaninang umaga.","translation":"Mom was able to buy big **mullets** at the market this morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na bagay na hugis bilog o singsing, karaniwang gawa sa metal, na ginagamit bilang palamuti, pang-ugnay, o bahagi ng isang mekanismo.
original_explanation: This is the fancy, Spanish-derived word for 'singsing' (ring). You'd probably hear this from your lola when she's talking about her old jewelry. It can also refer to any ring-shaped object, like the rings on a binder or the rings used in construction. Think of it as the 'alta' version of a ring.
usage_notes: While 'singsing' is more common for finger rings, 'anilyo' can be used for that and other ring-shaped objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lumang kuwaderno ay pinagbuklod ng mga kalawangin nang **anilyo**.","translation":"The old notebook was bound by rusty **rings**."},{"sentence":"Isinuot niya ang gintong **anilyo** na pamana ng kanyang lola.","translation":"She wore the gold **ring** inherited from her grandmother."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng "kilig" o isang pakiramdam ng pananabik at saya, karaniwang may kinalaman sa romantikong sitwasyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'nakaka-' at salitang-ugat na 'kilig'.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when your crush looks at you, or when your favorite love team has a scene together. It's the butterflies in your stomach, the sudden urge to squeal and hit your friend. The 'ayieee' moment.
usage_notes: Halos palaging ginagamit sa mga kontekstong romantiko o 'cute'. Isang konseptong malalim na nakaugat sa kulturang Pilipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakakakilig** ang mga banat ng manliligaw niya.","translation":"Her suitor's pickup lines are **romantically thrilling**."},{"sentence":"May **nakakakilig** na eksena sa bagong K-drama.","translation":"There's a **thrilling** scene in the new K-drama."}]

meaning_filipino: Mula sa isang lugar na may malaking agwat o distansya; hindi malapitan.
original_explanation: The default setting for most relationships during the pandemic. It's how you admire your crush from across the classroom, or how your OFW parent shows their love. Malayuan is the art of being there without actually being there, powered by video calls, chat messages, and a whole lot of 'miss na kita.'
usage_notes: Can refer to physical distance or a method of interaction. Often used in 'pag-ibig na malayuan' (long-distance love).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinapanood lang niya ang parada nang **malayuan**.","translation":"He was just watching the parade **from a distance**."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **malayuan** na relasyon, pero kinakaya nila.","translation":"A **long-distance** relationship is hard, but they are managing it."}]

translation: to have something leveled or flattened
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-utos o pagsasagawa na gawing pantay o patag ang isang ibabaw o lugar.
original_explanation: This is what you do to the lumpy batter for your hotcakes. Or what construction workers do to a plot of land before building a house. In relationships, it's what you do after a 'tampuhan' - you try to 'iron things out' or magpatag ng gusot.
usage_notes: Used in construction, landscaping, cooking, and metaphorically for resolving conflicts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha sila ng mga trabahador para **magpatag** ng lupa kung saan itatayo ang bahay.","translation":"They hired workers to **level** the land where the house will be built."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang ayusin ang kanilang gusot, ngunit mahirap **magpatag** ng nasirang tiwala.","translation":"They tried to fix their issues, but it's hard to **smooth over** broken trust."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang patakarang pang-emergency na naghihigpit sa paggalaw ng mga tao o paglabas sa isang komunidad, karaniwang ipinapatupad upang kontrolin ang pagkalat ng sakit o para sa seguridad.
original_explanation: Ah, 2020's most popular English word that became a Filipino household term. Lockdown meant Dalgona coffee, TikTok dances, online selling, and asking "Anong level ng ECQ na ba tayo?" It's the reason you became a plantito/plantita or a home baker. It was the ultimate "you shall not pass" on a national scale.
usage_notes: Naging pangkaraniwan sa Pilipinas simula noong pandemya ng COVID-19.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit na ipinatupad ang **lockdown** sa buong Metro Manila.","translation":"A strict **lockdown** was implemented across Metro Manila."},{"sentence":"Maraming negosyo ang nagsara noong panahon ng **lockdown**.","translation":"Many businesses closed during the **lockdown** period."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o akto ng paggawa o pagsasabi ng isang bagay nang higit sa isang beses.
etymology: Mula sa `pagka-` (paraan o estado ng) + `ulit` (gawing muli).
original_explanation: Ever explained something to your team lead and they ask you to explain it again, but slower? That's `pagkaulit`. It's also that feeling when your favorite series gets a terrible reboot, and you're just witnessing the `pagkaulit` of the same plot points but worse. It's the "here we go again" moment.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa paraan o estado ng pag-uulit ng isang bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkaulit** ng kanyang paliwanag, mas naintindihan namin ang leksyon.","translation":"Because of the **repetition** of his explanation, we understood the lesson better."},{"sentence":"Ayaw ko na ng **pagkaulit** ng parehong pagkakamali.","translation":"I don't want a **recurrence** of the same mistake."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na lubos na bukas o nakaawang, tulad ng pinto, bintana, o sugat.
original_explanation: Imagine seeing a door na hindi lang bukas, kundi *super* bukas, as in pwede nang dumaan ang isang kalabaw. O yung bibig ng kaibigan mo kapag narinig niya yung latest chismis. That's `wakawak`. It’s not just open, it's dramatically, scandalously open.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga pinto, bintana, bibig, o sugat upang bigyang-diin ang antas ng pagkakabukas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwang **wakawak** ang pinto kaya nakapasok ang magnanakaw.","translation":"The door was left **wide open**, which is why the thief was able to enter."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang **wakawak** na sugat sa kanyang binti.","translation":"I saw the **gaping** wound on his leg."}]

translation: a type of sea bass; grouper
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isdang-dagat na kabilang sa pamilya ng lapu-lapu (grouper) o sea bass.
original_explanation: A fish you might find at the palengke that your mom points at and says is "masarap isigang." It's a cousin of the more famous Lapu-Lapu. If you're not a fisherman or a die-hard market-goer, you've probably eaten it without knowing its name.
usage_notes: Not a very common term outside of fishing communities or wet markets. Often just generically called 'isda' (fish) or mistaken for other similar-looking fish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap daw ipaksiw ang isdang **bangasin**.","translation":"They say the **bangasin** fish is delicious when cooked in vinegar stew."},{"sentence":"Nakahuli ng malaking **bangasin** ang mangingisda.","translation":"The fisherman caught a large **grouper**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpasok at paglabas ng hangin sa baga; ang hangin na nalalanghap o ibinubuga.
original_explanation: That thing you're holding while waiting for your crush to reply, for your grades to be posted, or for the MRT to finally move. Also what your boss tells you to do ('Hinga, take a break') right before giving you another urgent task. It's the OG 'keep calm and carry on.'
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang salitang-ugat. Ang mga anyo nito ay humihinga (breathing), paghinga (the act of breathing), at hininga (the breath itself).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malalim na **hinga** ang kailangan mo para kumalma.","translation":"You need a deep **breath** to calm down."},{"sentence":"Isang malalim na **hinga** bago siya sumagot.","translation":"One deep **breath** before she answered."}]

meaning_filipino: Gamitin ang isang bagay bilang sapin o suporta sa ulo sa pagtulog o paghiga.
original_explanation: That moment in the bus or FX when you're so sleepy, you just **iunan** your head on your backpack, your friend's shoulder, or even the cold window. Anything can be a pillow if you're sleepy enough. "Pwede ba kitang iunan?" is a classic 'pabebe' or 'papansin' move.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod, kaya niyang **iunan** ang kanyang bag para makatulog.","translation":"Being so tired, he can **use his bag as a pillow** to sleep."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **iunan** ang braso ko, nangangalay ako!","translation":"Don't **use my arm as a pillow**, it's getting numb!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang gawain o libangan ay ang pagsisid sa ilalim ng tubig, maaaring para manghuli ng isda, maghanap ng perlas, o para sa rekreasyon.
etymology: From 'sisid' (dive). The ma- and -n- prefix/infix creates an agent noun, "one who dives".
original_explanation: The original Filipino freediver. Before it was a cool IG hobby, the 'maninisid' was the guy who dove for pearls or spearfished for a living, often with just a pair of homemade goggles and incredible lung capacity. Today, it can also mean a scuba diver exploring the reefs of Palawan.
usage_notes: Refers to a person who dives, often as a profession or a regular activity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang bihasang **maninisid** si Tatay, kaya niyang abutin ang ilalim ng dagat.","translation":"My father is an expert **diver**; he can reach the bottom of the sea."},{"sentence":"Nag-aalok ang resort ng kurso para sa mga gustong maging **maninisid**.","translation":"The resort offers a course for those who want to become a **diver**."}]

translation: to dress someone; to put clothes on someone
meaning_filipino: Paglalagay ng damit sa isang tao o bagay.
etymology: From "damit" (clothes) + "-an" (suffix indicating the object of an action).
original_explanation: This is what your mom did to you when you were a baby, or what you do to your pet chihuahua when it's cold. It's the act of dressing up another being, not yourself. A stylist, for example, will 'damtan' a celebrity for the red carpet. "Damtan mo nga yung aso ng sweater."
usage_notes: Focuses on the person or object being dressed. Contrast with "magdamit," which is reflexive (to dress oneself). "Bihisan" is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Damtan** mo na ang bata at baka sipunin.","translation":"**Dress** the child now before he catches a cold."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nag-aayos at nag**dadamtan** sa mga manika sa museo.","translation":"She is the one who fixes and **dresses** the dolls in the museum."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang astronomical na bagay na binubuo ng isang makinang na spheroid ng plasma. Sa karaniwang gamit, ito ay ang mga tuldok ng liwanag sa kalangitan sa gabi.
original_explanation: The OG source of light before Meralco. It's a star. But in the Philippines, it's also what we call celebrities ('Siya ay isang sikat na bituin sa pelikula'), the things you wish upon when you're feeling hopeless, and the main decoration of our Christmas parol. It's the ultimate symbol of hope and fame.
usage_notes: Used both literally for celestial bodies and figuratively for celebrities, aspirations, or star-shaped objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng mga **bituin** ang kalangitan ngayong gabi.","translation":"The sky is full of **stars** tonight."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **bituin** sa industriya ng musika.","translation":"Her dream is to become a famous **star** in the music industry."}]

translation: to bombard with a cannon; to cannonade
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-atake o pagpapatama sa isang target gamit ang kanyon.
original_explanation: This is the verb form. What do you do with a cannon? You 'kanyunin' things. It means to blast something with a cannon. Metaphorically, it's what your boss does to your weekend plans with an urgent report, or what your feed feels like during election season—it gets bombarded.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa kontekstong historikal o militar. Maaari ring gamitin sa paraang patalinhaga para sa labis na pag-atake sa isang tao o bagay, gamit man ay salita, gawain, o tanong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ang mga sundalo na **kanyunin** ang pader ng kuta.","translation":"The soldiers were ordered to **bombard** the walls of the fort."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **kanyunin** ng tanong, isa-isa lang!","translation":"Don't **bombard** me with questions, just one at a time!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon para sa pagsasayaw, karaniwan ay idinaraos sa mga plaza o pampublikong lugar tuwing may pista o pagdiriwang.
original_explanation: The original Pinoy dance party, pre-ZoukOut and Ultra. Think fiesta in the province, a live band playing cha-cha and sweet music, and the whole barangay dancing in the town plaza. It's where your lolo and lola had their first date. The modern version might have a DJ, but the spirit of community dancing is the same.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with fiestas and rural celebrations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagyaya ang mga kaibigan ko na pumunta sa **bayle** sa plasa mamayang gabi.","translation":"My friends invited me to go to the **dance party** at the plaza later tonight."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang **bayle** pagkatapos ng prusisyon para sa pista ng bayan.","translation":"The **dance** started after the procession for the town fiesta."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mabangong likido na karaniwang gawa sa mga esensiyal na langis o aromatikong sangkap, ginagamit upang magbigay ng kaaya-ayang amoy sa katawan.
original_explanation: That liquid courage you spray on before a date. From the high-end Jo Malone your rich tita from the US gave you, to the Bench body spray you've had since high school. Your 'pabango' game.
usage_notes: The more common native term is 'pabango'. 'Perpume' feels a bit more classic or sometimes even 'coño'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bango ng **perpume** mo, anong tatak niyan?","translation":"Your **perfume** smells so good, what brand is that?"},{"sentence":"Nag-iipon siya para makabili ng mamahaling **perpume**.","translation":"She is saving up to buy an expensive **perfume**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagtanggap o pagsang-ayon sa isang bagay; pagbibigay ng pahintulot o pag-apruba.
original_explanation: The act of giving your 'go signal.' It's what your boss does to your leave request (sana!), or what your parents do when you ask for permission to go on a trip with friends. "In-okehan na ng manager ang budget para sa Christmas party!" (Translation: Let the games begin!)
usage_notes: A colloquial verb form of 'okey'. Common in informal speech and writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisabi kung **okehan** mo ang design na ito.","translation":"Please tell me if you'll **approve** this design."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya in**okehan** ang plano ko kaya kailangan kong ulitin.","translation":"He didn't **give the go-ahead** for my plan so I have to redo it."}]

translation: To grimace; to twitch the lips
meaning_filipino: Ang bahagyang pagpilipit o paggalaw ng mga labi, karaniwan upang ipahiwatig ang pagpipigil sa tawa, pag-iyak, o pagkadismaya.
