usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Ana sa opisina bilang isang tunay na **manraraket**; nagbebenta siya ng yema cake at insurance.","translation":"Ana is known in the office as a true **hustler**; she sells yema cake and insurance."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **manraraket** ay sanay sa pagbalanse ng oras sa pagitan ng kanilang pangunahing trabaho at mga sideline.","translation":"**People who do sideline jobs** are used to balancing time between their main job and their side hustles."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang amoy o lasa ng kanin o ibang pagkain na nasunog o natusta nang bahagya sa ilalim ng kaldero.
original_explanation: The smell that causes panic in a Filipino household. It's that distinct, slightly-burnt aroma of rice (sinaing) that stuck to the bottom of the pot because someone forgot to turn off the stove or add enough water. It's the smell of "Ay, sunog ang kanin!" followed by a frantic scraping of the pot. Some people secretly like the crispy, burnt part (tutong), though.
usage_notes: Primarily used to describe burnt rice, but can be extended to other scorched foods.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Amoy **supok** ang sinaing, baka nasunog na.","translation":"The cooked rice smells **burnt**, it might be scorched already."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang kumain ng kanin na may lasang **supok**.","translation":"He doesn't like to eat rice that has a **scorched** taste."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang tumalbog nang mataas o paulit-ulit kapag bumagsak sa isang ibabaw.
original_explanation: Like a brand new basketball, or your ex who keeps coming back after you break up. It has 'bounce back' energy, whether it's a good ball or a bad relationship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Matalbog** ang bola kaya masayang paglaruan sa labas.","translation":"The ball is **bouncy** so it's fun to play with outside."},{"sentence":"Ayaw ko sa kutson na ito, hindi gaanong **matalbog**.","translation":"I don't like this mattress, it's not very **bouncy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagbibihis o ang ugali ng paggamit ng isang partikular na uri ng kasuotan.
original_explanation: The present tense of your daily 'porma'. It can mean what you're wearing right now ("Nagsusuot ako ng pambahay") or your general style ("Hindi siya nagsusuot ng maikli"). It’s the verb for every OOTD, from WFH-chic to palengke-ready.
usage_notes: Present progressive ("is wearing") or habitual present ("wears"). Past tense is "nagsuot".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit ka **nagsusuot** ng jacket? Ang init-init!","translation":"Why are you **wearing** a jacket? It's so hot!"},{"sentence":"Palagi siyang **nagsusuot** ng itim.","translation":"She always **wears** black."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagiging matipid; mahusay sa pamamahala ng pera o yaman upang maiwasan ang pag-aaksaya.
original_explanation: When you choose the unli-rice option, that's being *ekonomikal*. When you buy the "family size" shampoo bottle because the price per ml is lower, that's being *ekonomikal*. It's the official adjective of every practical Pinoy who knows how to stretch a peso. It's not about being cheap (kuripot), it's about being smart (wais).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas **ekonomikal** kung bibili ka ng maramihan sa halip na paunti-unti.","translation":"It's more **economical** if you buy in bulk instead of little by little."}]

translation: to connect; to relate; to link
meaning_filipino: Pagdugtungin o pag-isahin ang dalawa o higit pang bagay, ideya, o tao upang magkaroon ng relasyon o koneksyon.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're trying to play matchmaker: "Ugnayin natin si Mark at si Anna!" It's also what your prof asks you to do in an essay: "Ugnayin ang Noli Me Tangere sa kasalukuyang isyu ng lipunan." You're basically building a bridge between two separate islands, whether they're people, ideas, or events. The goal is to create a network, a link, a connection.
usage_notes: The root word 'ugnay' means connection or relation. 'Ugnayan' is the noun form (relationship, connection).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ugnayin** ang mga ebidensya para malutas ang kaso.","translation":"He tried to **connect** the pieces of evidence to solve the case."},{"sentence":"Mahalagang **ugnayin** ang aralin sa tunay na buhay ng mga mag-aaral.","translation":"It's important to **relate** the lesson to the students' real lives."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging una o higit sa iba sa isang karera, kompetisyon, o anumang larangan; lumamang.
original_explanation: This is your goal during the 11.11 sale: to check out your cart before everyone else. In the office, it's what that one super competitive colleague is always trying to do. "Kahit nahuhuli sa simula, nagawa pa rin niyang umungos sa huli."
usage_notes: Often used in the context of competition, races, or progress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa huling yugto ng karera, biglang **umungos** ang kabayong dehado.","translation":"In the final stretch of the race, the underdog horse suddenly **got ahead**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang sipag at talino, **umungos** siya sa lahat ng kanyang mga kasabayan.","translation":"Because of his diligence and intelligence, he **surpassed** all of his peers."}]

translation: To snatch or grab suddenly; to juggle.
meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis na pag-agaw, pagdaklot, o pagsalo sa isang bagay; ang paglalaro sa pamamagitan ng paghahagis at pagsalo ng mga bagay.
original_explanation: Imagine you're in a crowded MRT and someone's phone starts to fall. That quick, reflexive grab to save it? That's 'siklutin'. It can also mean to snatch something away, like how your sibling 'siniklot' the last piece of fried chicken from the plate. It’s a sudden, upward grabbing motion.
usage_notes: Derived from the game 'siklot', the verb captures the upward snatching/catching motion. It implies quickness and dexterity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **siklutin** ang nahuhulog na baso.","translation":"He tried to **snatch** the falling glass."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **siklutin** ang pagkain sa mesa!","translation":"Don't **snatch** the food from the table!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kaugalian ng pagpapabukas o pag-antala sa paggawa ng isang gawain o tungkulin na dapat nang tapusin.
etymology: From `pag-` + `pa-` + reduplicated `liban` (absent, except). The repetition implies a continuous act of putting things off.
original_explanation: The national sport of students and employees everywhere. "Mamaya na, 5 minutes pa." It's when you have a month to do a project and you start it the night before the deadline, powered by coffee and regret. The motto is "Due today, do today."
usage_notes: A very specific and common term for procrastination.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapaliban-liban** ay kaaway ng tagumpay.","translation":"**Procrastination** is the enemy of success."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pagpapaliban-liban**, hindi niya natapos ang kanyang mga takdang-aralin.","translation":"Because of his **procrastination**, he wasn't able to finish his assignments."}]

translation: to watch over, to guard from a high place
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabantay o pagmamasid nang may pag-iingat at atensyon, karaniwan mula sa isang mataas na lugar.
original_explanation: Like a human CCTV. It's what your chismosa neighbor does from their window, watching your every move. Or a security guard in a tower, but with more judgment. The key is the vantage point.
usage_notes: Implies watching from a vantage point, like a tower, a hilltop, or a high window.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumatyaw** ang gwardiya mula sa tore upang masubaybayan ang buong perimetro.","translation":"The guard **watched over** from the tower to monitor the entire perimeter."},{"sentence":"Ang mga agila ay **bumatyaw** sa kalangitan, naghahanap ng masisila.","translation":"The eagles **watched from above** in the sky, looking for prey."}]

translation: a type of electronic dance music and dance style
meaning_filipino: Isang genre ng electronic dance music at istilo ng sayaw na nagmula sa Davao City, Pilipinas. Ito ay kilala sa simpleng beat, malakas na bass, at mga paulit-ulit na tunog na may kasamang natatanging galaw ng katawan na parang naglalakad.
etymology: Coined by DJ Love, the creator of the music style in Davao. The origin of the word itself is debated.
original_explanation: The OG viral Filipino dance craze before TikTok. It's that jerky, almost robotic walking dance you see in fiestas and on jeeps, set to a distinct 'tugs-tugs' electronic beat. It's wonderfully weird, uniquely Pinoy, and guaranteed to be a conversation starter.
usage_notes: Refers to both the music genre and the dance style.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumasayaw sila ng **budots** sa gitna ng kalsada.","translation":"They are dancing **budots** in the middle of the street."},{"sentence":"Ang tugtog na iyan ay parang **budots**.","translation":"That music sounds like **budots**."}]

translation: to cause to sweat; to become sweaty
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng paglabas ng pawis sa katawan, karaniwan dahil sa init, pagod, o kaba.
original_explanation: The default state of being in the Philippines between March and May. You walk from your house to the sari-sari store and you're instantly "mapapawis." Also happens during a job interview, a thesis defense, or when you see your crush walking towards you.
usage_notes: Can be used as both a verb (mapapawis, to become sweaty) and an adjective (mapawis, a sweaty person). This entry focuses on the verb form initiated by 'mapa-'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang tatakbo sa ilalim ng araw at baka ka **mapawis** nang husto.","translation":"Don't run under the sun or you might **get very sweaty**."},{"sentence":"Siya ay madaling **mapawis** kaya lagi siyang may dalang pamaypay.","translation":"He **sweats** easily, so he always brings a fan."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng paputok na gawa sa pulbura na nakabalot sa papel at pinagsama-sama sa isang mahabang mitsa.
etymology: From Spanish 'cohetes' (rockets, firecrackers). The '-s' at the end is a common pluralization pattern in Filipino for Spanish loanwords.
original_explanation: The OG noisemaker for New Year's Eve before everyone got scared of losing a finger. It's that long string of tiny firecrackers that you light up, throw, and run away from, hoping it doesn't chase you back. The sound is iconic, like a tiny, angry machine gun.
usage_notes: Primarily used during New Year's celebrations. Many types are now illegal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat ang lahat sa pagsisindi ng **kortsetes** noong Bagong Taon.","translation":"Everyone was careful when lighting the **firecrackers** on New Year's."}]

translation: to let cool down; to have something cooled
meaning_filipino: Hayaan o gawing presko o malamig ang isang bagay. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagpapakalma sa isang taong galit o mainit ang ulo.
etymology: From 'presko' (fresh, cool, from Spanish 'fresco') and the verbal affix 'pa- -in', meaning to cause to become fresh/cool.
original_explanation: This word works in two ways. Literally, it's for food: "Papreskuhin mo muna 'yung sopas bago mo ipakain sa bata" (Let the soup cool down first...). Figuratively, and more juicy, it's for people. When your friend is raging about their ex, you tell them, "Kalma, papreskuhin muna natin yang ulo mo." (Calm down, let's let your head cool down first). It's the verbal equivalent of telling someone to chill.
usage_notes: Can be used for temperature (synonymous with 'palamigin') or for emotions (synonymous with 'pakalmahin'). The figurative use is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itabi mo muna 'yang mainit na kanin at **papreskuhin** bago ilagay sa ref.","translation":"Set aside that hot rice and **let it cool** before putting it in the fridge."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mo muna siyang mag-isa para **papreskuhin** ang ulo niya.","translation":"Leave him alone for a while to **let him cool down**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na 40; katumbas ng apat na sampu.
etymology: Pagsasama ng 'apat na pu', kung saan ang 'pu' ay pinaikling 'sampu'.
original_explanation: The age when your Tita starts calling you "iho/iha" with a hint of pity if you're still single. It's also the number of minutes you *thought* your commute would be, but then EDSA happened. Also, "kuwarenta" is its cooler, Spanish-derived cousin.
usage_notes: Ang 'kwarenta' (mula sa Espanyol) ay mas karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, lalo na sa pagtukoy sa presyo o edad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroong **apatnapung** estudyante sa aming klase.","translation":"There are **forty** students in our class."},{"sentence":"Nagdiwang siya ng kanyang ika-**apatnapung** kaarawan.","translation":"She celebrated her **fortieth** birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain o pag-aaral na ibinibigay ng guro sa mga mag-aaral upang gawin sa labas ng klase, karaniwan sa bahay.
original_explanation: The original 'work from home' setup. That thing your teacher gives you that makes you question your life choices over the weekend. The reason why your childhood included the phrase, 'Ma, pa-print.'
usage_notes: A very common word in the context of education.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang gawin ang iyong **takdang-aralin** sa Matematika.","translation":"Don't forget to do your **homework** in Mathematics."}]

meaning_filipino: Malakas at walang tigil na buhos ng ulan na nagdudulot ng pagbaha; agos ng tubig-baha.
original_explanation: This isn't just your regular 'ulan'. This is the kind of rain that makes you check PAGASA's updates every 5 minutes and wonder if you should start building an ark. It's the floodwater rushing down the street, carrying everything with it. Parang 'yung sunod-sunod na problema, 'di ka pa tapos sa isa, may dumarating na namang banos ng kasunod.
usage_notes: A more poetic and intense word for heavy rain or flood than the common 'baha' or 'malakas na ulan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malakas na **banos** ay nagdulot ng malawakang pagbaha sa buong bayan.","translation":"The heavy **downpour** caused widespread flooding throughout the town."},{"sentence":"Hindi kami makaalis ng bahay dahil sa rumaragasang **banos** sa kalsada.","translation":"We couldn't leave the house because of the rushing **floodwater** on the street."}]

translation: to give shelter to; to let someone take cover
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng kanlungan o pansamantalang tirahan sa isang tao o hayop, lalo na mula sa init ng araw o ulan.
etymology: From pa- + silong (space underneath a house, shelter) + -in.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na biglang umulan tapos may nakita kang waiting shed or tindahan at sinabi ng may-ari, "Dito muna kayo." Ayun, pinasilong ka. It's the act of letting someone take refuge, parang 'yung kaibigan mong pinapatulog mo muna sa inyo kasi nag-away sila ng jowa niya.
usage_notes: A command or request form of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasilungin** mo muna ang mga bata sa loob dahil malakas ang ulan.","translation":"**Let** the children **take shelter** inside because the rain is strong."},{"sentence":"Mabuti na lang at may nagmagandang-loob na **pasilungin** kami sa kanilang tahanan.","translation":"It's a good thing someone was kind enough to **give us shelter** in their home."}]

translation: to trade; to engage in commerce
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagbili at pagbebenta ng mga produkto o serbisyo sa pagitan ng mga tao, kumpanya, o bansa.
etymology: From 'makipag-' (to mutually do something) and 'kalakal' (trade, merchandise).
original_explanation: Before Shopee and Lazada, this was the OG way to get stuff. It's the formal term for business, whether it's your tita selling Avon, your neighbor with a sari-sari store, or countries swapping bananas for electronics. The art of "buy and sell."
usage_notes: Often used in the context of history, economics, or formal business.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, ang mga Pilipino ay nakikipag-**makipagkalakalan** sa mga Tsino.","translation":"In ancient times, Filipinos used to **trade** with the Chinese."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **makipagkalakalan** para sa ekonomiya ng isang bansa.","translation":"Engaging in **commerce** is important for a country's economy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang direksyon o punto sa pagitan ng timog at kanluran, na nasa 225 digri sa kompas.
etymology: Isang tambalang salita na binubuo ng 'timog' (south) at 'kanluran' (west).
original_explanation: That part of the Philippines where you'll find Palawan, a.k.a. paradise on Earth. When your GPS says 'turn southwest,' this is it. It's the love child of 'Timog' (South) and 'Kanluran' (West).
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa heograpiya, nabigasyon, at mga ulat-panahon. Ang katumbas na hangin ay ang Habagat o Southwest Monsoon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Palawan ay matatagpuan sa **timog-kanluran** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Palawan is located in the **southwest** of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Umihip ang hanging habagat mula sa **timog-kanluran**.","translation":"The southwest monsoon blew from the **southwest**."}]

translation: to poke; to nudge (with a finger)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaiti o pag-abot sa isang bagay o tao gamit ang daliri o isang manipis na bagay upang makuha ang atensyon nito o upang ito ay galawin.
original_explanation: The OG 'poke' feature, way before Facebook. It's that subtle (or not-so-subtle) finger-jab you give someone to get their attention, usually when you want to share some chismis in a quiet room. 'Psst!' in physical form.
usage_notes: Implies using a finger or a small, thin object (like a stick) to poke, prod, or pick at something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kuhitin** ang natutulog na pusa.","translation":"Don't **poke** the sleeping cat."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **kuhitin** ang dumi sa kanyang kuko.","translation":"He tried to **pick at** the dirt under his nail."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pag-alis ng bayag o organong pangreproduksiyon ng isang lalaking hayop o tao upang hindi na ito makapag-anak.
original_explanation: What the vet does to your pet cat or dog so they don't contribute to the growing population of strays. It's the ultimate "snip-snip" procedure. In human context, it's used hyperbolically to mean rendering someone powerless or emasculated. "Ayaw ko na mag-asawa, baka kapunin lang ako!"
usage_notes: Primarily used for animals. Using it for humans is often metaphorical or hyperbolic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinayo ng beterinaryo na **kapunin** ang alagang aso para maging mas kalmado ito.","translation":"The veterinarian advised **to neuter** the pet dog to make it calmer."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **kapunin** ang mga alagang pusa upang makontrol ang kanilang pagdami.","translation":"Pet cats need **to be neutered** to control their population."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matinding paggalang, paghanga, o pagsamba sa isang tao, bagay, o nilalang na itinuturing na sagrado o napakahalaga.
etymology: From "pintuho" (adoration). The "pan-" prefix becomes "pam-" and the first syllable of the root is reduplicated.
original_explanation: This is how K-Pop fans feel about their 'bias'. It's that next-level devotion, like how your lola reveres her Santo Niño, or how you look at the last piece of Jollibee Chickenjoy. It's pure, intense admiration.
usage_notes: A deep and formal word, often used in religious or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pamimintuho** sa sining ay makikita sa kanyang mga obra.","translation":"His **adoration** for the arts is evident in his masterpieces."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita ng mga deboto ang kanilang **pamimintuho** sa pamamagitan ng taunang prusisyon.","translation":"The devotees showed their **veneration** through the annual procession."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kakaning Pilipino na gawa sa gata ng niyog, mais, at asukal, na pinalapot ng gawgaw.
original_explanation: The white, jiggly, sweet square of happiness you find at every Filipino party. It's not a real fiesta without a llanera of maja blanca, usually topped with latik or toasted coconut. It's the dessert that says, "I'm simple, but I'm delicious and everyone loves me."
usage_notes: Often used as a shortened form of "maja blanca."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-abot nga ng isang hiwa ng **maja**.","translation":"Please pass a slice of the **maja blanca**."},{"sentence":"Si Lola ang pinakamasarap gumawa ng **maja** sa buong angkan.","translation":"Grandma makes the most delicious **maja blanca** in the whole clan."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may maamo at kaaya-ayang itsura, katulad ng karaniwang paglalarawan sa isang anghel.
original_explanation: That person who looks so pure and innocent, you'd think they wouldn't even hurt a fly. 'Yung tipong itsurang 'di makabasag-pinggan, but you know deep down, they're probably the one who finished the last piece of leche flan without telling anyone.
usage_notes: Often used to describe someone with a gentle, beautiful, or deceptively innocent face.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit **mukhang-anghel** si Clara, may tinatago pala siyang kalokohan.","translation":"Even if Clara is **angelic-looking**, she's apparently hiding some mischief."},{"sentence":"Lahat ay nabighani sa **mukhang-anghel** na dalaga.","translation":"Everyone was captivated by the **angelic-looking** young lady."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na gumagawa at nag-iiwan ng isang testamento o huling habilin.
original_explanation: This is the main character in any legal drama about inheritance. The 'testador' is the one who wrote the will, the 'huling habilin', that everyone is now fighting over. They're the one who decides who gets the house in Forbes Park and who gets the collection of old magazines. The ultimate 'tagapamana'.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga legal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa batas, dapat may sapat na pag-iisip ang **testador** sa oras na gawin ang testamento.","translation":"According to the law, the **testator** must be of sound mind at the time of making the will."},{"sentence":"Pinirmahan ng **testador** ang dokumento sa harap ng kanyang abogado.","translation":"The **testator** signed the document in front of his lawyer."}]

meaning_filipino: Burahin o alisin ang isang bagay, lalo na ang datos o impormasyon sa isang elektronikong kagamitan. Ito ay nasa anyong pawatas o pautos.
original_explanation: The digital version of 'out of sight, out of mind.' It's the modern way to get rid of evidence, bad memories, or that 1GB Genshin Impact update that's eating up your phone storage. Also a great way to deal with toxic people online. Just click and poof!
usage_notes: A very common Taglish verb used in digital contexts. The base form 'mag-delete' can be used as an infinitive or an imperative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magdelete** ng mga hindi magandang komento sa iyong post.","translation":"You need **to delete** the nasty comments on your post."},{"sentence":"**Magdelete** ka na ng picture natin, break na tayo.","translation":"**Delete** our picture now, we're broken up."}]

translation: to feel romantic excitement; to be thrilled (romantically)
meaning_filipino: Maranasan ang pakiramdam ng kilig; makaramdam ng biglaang tuwa at pananabik dahil sa isang romantikong pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the verb form, the actual experience of the 'kilig'. If 'kilig' is the noun, 'kiligin' is the action of your heart doing a backflip. You don't just *have* kilig, you *kiligin*. It's an involuntary reaction. You can't help it. "Pinakilig niya ako" (He made me feel kilig) is the ultimate goal of any Filipino suitor.
usage_notes: Often used in the actor-focus form "kinikilig" (is feeling kilig) or "kinilig" (felt kilig).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko mapigilang **kiligin** tuwing ngumingiti siya sa akin.","translation":"I can't help but **feel giddy** whenever he smiles at me."},{"sentence":"Sino ba naman ang hindi **kikiligin** sa isang harana?","translation":"Who wouldn't **be romantically thrilled** by a serenade?"}]

translation: String; Cord; Something used for tying
meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, tulad ng lubid, sinulid, o alambre, na ginagamit sa pagbigkis o pagbuhol.
original_explanation: The OG zip tie. It's that all-purpose string you look for when you need to tie up a plastic bag of ulam, secure a box, or even fix your broken tsinelas in an emergency. Sa Pinas, even a piece of straw from a walis tingting can become a **pantali**. Resourcefulness at its finest!
usage_notes: A general term. Specific types include 'lubid' (rope), 'pisi' (twine), 'sinulid' (thread).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **pantali** para sa mga kahon na ito.","translation":"Get something **to tie** these boxes with."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang lastiko bilang **pantali** sa kanyang buhok.","translation":"She used a rubber band as a **tie** for her hair."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na patpat na gawa sa kahoy o papel na may kemikal sa dulo na nagliliyab kapag ikiniskis sa isang magaspang na ibabaw.
original_explanation: Before lighters and automatic stoves, this was the key to unlocking fire. It's what your lola uses to light the gasul or the katol for mosquitoes. That distinct smell of a newly-lit posporo is pure nostalgia. Pro tip: 'wag paglaruan, baka mapalo ka ng tsinelas.
usage_notes: Still commonly used, especially in kitchens and for lighting candles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng isang kahon ng **posporo** sa tindahan.","translation":"Get a box of **matches** from the store."}]

meaning_filipino: Masdan o panoorin ang isang pangyayari o kaganapan, karaniwan sa isang pormal na paanyaya o utos.
original_explanation: This is what your chismosa neighbor does from their window. It's like having a front-row seat to the drama unfolding, whether it's a neighborhood squabble or a new delivery from Shopee. In formal settings, it's the official invitation to 'come and see,' like for a theatrical play or a graduation ceremony. 'Patunghayan natin ang susunod na kabanata ng buhay ni Marites.'
usage_notes: Often used in formal or literary contexts, like in scripts or formal invitations. It means 'to let (someone) witness' or 'to present for viewing.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patunghayan** natin ang pagtatanghal ng mga bata.","translation":"Let us **witness** the children's performance."},{"sentence":"Inaanyayahan ang lahat na **patunghayan** ang makasaysayang pagdiriwang.","translation":"Everyone is invited to **observe** the historic celebration."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paghiling o pagsasabi ng ninanais mula sa iba.
original_explanation: The root word of every 'pahingi ako' you've ever heard at the dinner table or when your friend opens a bag of chips. It's the fundamental human action of wanting what someone else has and vocalizing it. The success rate varies greatly.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang salitang-ugat. Ang mga karaniwang anyo nito ay humingi (to ask), hiningi (asked for), hinihingi (is asking for), at hihingin (will ask for).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiya na **humingi** ng tulong.","translation":"Don't be shy to **ask for** help."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **hinihingi** mo para sa Pasko?","translation":"What are you **asking for** for Christmas?"}]

translation: to break into pieces, to tear apart
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghahati, pagputol, o pagsira sa isang bagay upang maging maliliit na bahagi.
original_explanation: What you want to do to your alarm clock every morning. O kaya, yung ginawa ng ex mo sa puso mo, 'di ba? Pineraso niya.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for objects or figuratively for emotions, trust, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **pirasuhin** ang karton para magkasya sa basurahan.","translation":"We need to **tear apart** the cardboard so it fits in the trash bin."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pirasuhin** ang tiwala na ibinigay ko sa iyo.","translation":"Don't **break into pieces** the trust I gave you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na sinasabi o ginagawa upang magpatawa o magbigay-aliw, na hindi dapat seryosohin.
etymology: Possibly from Malay 'biru' (confusion, disorder), which could have evolved to mean jest or trickery.
original_explanation: The foundation of Filipino bonding. It's the 'charot' at the end of a serious-sounding statement, the 'joke lang!' after a teasing comment. It can be a simple knock-knock, a witty one-liner, or the entire reason your tito is laughing by himself in the corner. If someone says, 'Huwag kang mapipikon, biro lang,' brace yourself.
usage_notes: A very common word. The verb form is 'magbiro' (to joke) or 'biruin' (to joke with someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong seryosohin ang sinabi niya, **biro** lang iyon.","translation":"Don't take what he said seriously, it was just a **joke**."},{"sentence":"Magaling siyang magpatawa at laging may baon na **biro**.","translation":"He's good at making people laugh and always has a **joke** ready."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapatuloy o pagpapanatili ng isang gawain, kuwento, o kalagayan.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + `tu-` (reduplication of first syllable of root) + `tuloy` (continue).
original_explanation: This is what happens when the "To be continued..." screen appears. It's the act of pushing through, whether it's finishing a K-drama series in one weekend or actually finishing your report after a long coffee break. The opposite of 'drawing' or giving up.
usage_notes: Not to be confused with `pagpapatuloy`, which is a more common synonym. `Pagtutuloy` can also imply the act of proceeding with something that was paused.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtutuloy** ng kuwento ay mababasa sa susunod na kabanata.","translation":"The **continuation** of the story can be read in the next chapter."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagtutuloy** ng edukasyon para sa magandang kinabukasan.","translation":"The **continuation** of education is important for a good future."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng hindi pagiging kontento o masaya sa isang sitwasyon, resulta, o kaganapan.
original_explanation: This is what you feel when you order something online and what arrives is a sad, "expectation vs. reality" meme. It's the feeling of getting your salary and realizing it's already gone after paying bills. It's the general "meh" feeling towards life, a job, or even a meal that just didn't hit the spot. The opposite of "Sana all."
usage_notes: Can refer to emotional, professional, or consumer dissatisfaction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinahayag ng mga manggagawa ang kanilang **pagkawalang-kasiyahan** sa mababang sahod.","translation":"The workers expressed their **dissatisfaction** with the low wages."},{"sentence":"Mayroong pangkalahatang **pagkawalang-kasiyahan** sa serbisyo ng kumpanya.","translation":"There is a general **discontentment** with the company's service."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghagis o pagbato ng isang bagay, karaniwan sa isang direksyon o patungo sa isang target, madalas sa paraang hindi pormal.
original_explanation: The more casual, almost dismissive way of saying "throw." It's not the powerful "bato" or the graceful "hagis." It's what you do with trash into a bin ("i-itsa mo na 'yan"), a coin for "toss coin," or when you pass a small object to a friend from a short distance. It has a slight "bahala na" energy.
usage_notes: Often used in its imperative form "Itsa mo!" (Throw it!). Can also be spelled as 'echa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itsa** mo nga sa akin 'yang unan.","translation":"**Toss** that pillow over to me."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong i-**itsa** kung saan-saan ang basura mo.","translation":"Don't just **throw** your trash anywhere."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging malupit, hindi sibilisado, o walang pinag-aralan; kabastusan.
etymology: From 'pagka-' (state/quality of being) + 'barbaro' (barbarian, uncivilized), from Spanish 'bárbaro'.
original_explanation: This is how you describe someone who cuts in line, talks loudly in the cinema, or puts their feet up on the jeepney seat. It's uncivilized behavior, the opposite of 'GMRC' (Good Manners and Right Conduct). Basically, acting like you were raised by wolves... no offense to the wolves.
usage_notes: Used to describe actions or a state of being that is considered crude, cruel, or uncivilized.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinondena ng lahat ang **pagkabarbaro** ng mga mananakop.","translation":"Everyone condemned the **barbarism** of the invaders."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya kinunsinti ang **pagkabarbaro** ng kanyang mga tauhan.","translation":"He did not tolerate the **barbaric behavior** of his men."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-unawa sa isang konsepto, sitwasyon, o damdamin ng isang tao; pag-unawa.
etymology: From `pag-` (nominalizer) + `intindi`, which is derived from the Spanish `entender` (to understand).
original_explanation: This is what you give your friend who's going through a tough breakup, even if it's the fifth time with the same person. It's the patience of a BPO agent dealing with a furious customer. It's more than just hearing (pakinig) or knowing (alam); it's about processing the 'why' and the 'how' and giving grace. Ang level-up version ng 'gets ko.'
usage_notes: Often used in the context of interpersonal relationships, empathy, and patience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng mahabang **pag-iintindi** sa mga taong may pinagdadaanan.","translation":"Long **understanding** is needed for people who are going through something."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o bagay na ginagamit sa pagkatok o pagpukpok, tulad ng martilyo o maso.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` ('gamit para sa') at ang salitang-ugat na `tuktok` ('knock'). Ang unang /t/ ng ugat ay nawala sa pagkakabitan ng unlapi.
original_explanation: The judge's gavel in a courtroom drama. Or that small hammer the doctor uses to test your reflexes. Basically, any tool whose main purpose in life is to go 'tok, tok, tok.'
usage_notes: Hindi gaanong karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan; mas madalas gamitin ang pangalan ng partikular na kagamitan (e.g., martilyo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng huwes ang kanyang **panuktok** para patahimikin ang korte.","translation":"The judge used his **knocker** (gavel) to silence the court."},{"sentence":"Ang martilyo ay isang uri ng **panuktok**.","translation":"A hammer is a type of **knocker**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng isip o damdamin na walang pag-aalala, takot, o pagkabalisa; payapa at tiwasay.
original_explanation: That feeling you get after you've submitted your report right on the deadline, or after you've finally paid off your credit card debt. "Panatag na loob ko." It's the opposite of "praning." It's when your mind is chill, you're not overthinking, and you feel secure. Parang 'yung feeling 'pag alam mong may sahod na bukas.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin kasama ang salitang "loob" (panloob na sarili) tulad ng sa pariralang "panatag ang loob".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Panatag** ang kanyang kalooban dahil alam niyang ligtas ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"His heart is **at ease** because he knows his family is safe."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko lang ng isang **panatag** na buhay, malayo sa gulo.","translation":"I just want a **serene** life, far from trouble."}]

translation: to be able to attract; to entice
meaning_filipino: Ang magkaroon ng kapangyarihan o katangiang makahikayat o makabighani ng pansin, paghanga, o pagnanais.
original_explanation: The power of a "SALE" sign to a certified tita. The "rizz" of a charming suitor. The delicious smell of sinigang that calls you to the dinner table. It's the ability to pull something or someone towards you, whether it's customers, admirers, or just plain attention. "Paano ba makaakit ng swerte?"
usage_notes: Can be used for romantic attraction, attracting customers, or simply drawing attention. The more common form is 'nakakaakit' (is attractive).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumagamit sila ng magagandang display para **makaakit** ng mga mamimili.","translation":"They use beautiful displays **to attract** customers."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang ngiti ay sapat na para **makaakit** ng kahit sino.","translation":"Her smile is enough **to attract** anyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tore na may maraming patong-patong na bubong, karaniwang matatagpuan sa Silangang Asya at may kaugnayan sa relihiyong Budismo.
etymology: From Portuguese 'pagode', from a Dravidian language, possibly via Persian. A loanword.
original_explanation: You know, that cool-looking tower you see in pictures of Japan, China, or Korea with the curly roof edges. It's a staple in travel vlogs and the background of many 'finding myself in Asia' profile pictures. Not to be confused with the feeling of being tired, though a long climb up one might make you feel that way.
usage_notes: A specific architectural term. Not a native Tagalog word but is understood. Homonym with the slang term for 'tired'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakamamangha ang mga gintong **pagoda** sa Thailand.","translation":"The golden **pagodas** in Thailand are amazing."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang bisitahin ang lahat ng sikat na **pagoda** sa Asya.","translation":"She wants to visit all the famous **pagodas** in Asia."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng isang bagay o kapangyarihan sa paraang mali, sobra, o nakapipinsala; ang pagmamaltrato.
original_explanation: When your boss makes you do O.T. without pay, that's them umabuso sa power nila. When you eat a whole tub of ice cream in one sitting, you're umabuso sa sarili mo. It’s taking advantage of a person, a situation, or even your own credit card to a harmful degree.
usage_notes: Can refer to abuse of power, substance abuse, or physical/emotional abuse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi tama na **umabuso** sa kabaitan ng isang tao.","translation":"It's not right to **abuse** a person's kindness."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya na itigil na ang **umabuso** sa alak.","translation":"He was advised to stop **abusing** alcohol."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain, na madaling mabali o masira at lumilikha ng tunog kapag kinakagat o dinidiinan.
original_explanation: The defining characteristic of a perfect lechon kawali, chicharon, or fried chicken skin. It's that ASMR-worthy crunch that tells you the food is fresh and glorious. It can also describe a curse word delivered with perfect, sharp enunciation. "Ang lutong ng mura!"
usage_notes: The hyphen is optional. `Pagkalutong` is also correct. Primarily used for food, but can be used metaphorically for sounds, particularly curses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sikreto sa masarap na pritong manok ay ang **pagka-malutong** ng balat.","translation":"The secret to delicious fried chicken is the **crispiness** of the skin."},{"sentence":"Nagulat ako sa **pagka-malutong** ng kanyang pagmumura.","translation":"I was surprised by the **crispness** of his cursing."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na para sa dalawang tao, binubuo ng dalawang bahagi, o ginagawa nang pares-pares.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'dalawa' (two) at hulaping '-han' na nagpapahiwatig ng paraan o grupo.
original_explanation: This is the 'buddy system' word. 'Yung upuan sa sinehan na **dalawahan**? Perfect for a date. 'Yung K-drama trope na may love triangle, pero eventually, may isang magiging **dalawahan** lang sa dulo. It's anything designed for or done by two. Think tandem bike, a duet, or splitting the bill.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri ('upuang dalawahan') o pangngalan ('Gawin nating dalawahan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng bisikletang **dalawahan** para sabay kaming makapag-ehersisyo.","translation":"We bought a tandem bicycle (**for two**) so we can exercise together."},{"sentence":"Ang kompetisyon ay may kategoryang isahan at **dalawahan**.","translation":"The competition has solo and **duo** (by pairs) categories."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang sapat na kaalaman, pinag-aralan, o kamalayan sa isang partikular na bagay o sa pangkalahatan.
original_explanation: The person who asks 'Bakit ka pagod? Nakaupo ka lang naman sa office maghapon.' (Why are you tired? You just sit in the office all day.) It's the label you mentally slap on someone who cuts in line, argues with facts, or is generally clueless about basic social etiquette.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective ('isang ignoranteng tao') or a noun ('isa siyang ignorante').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **ignorante** sa mga nangyayari sa paligid mo.","translation":"Don't be **ignorant** of what's happening around you."},{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **ignorante** dahil sa kanyang mga walang-batayang komento.","translation":"He was called **ignorant** because of his baseless comments."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o establisyimento kung saan nagbebenta ng gasolina at iba pang panggatong para sa mga sasakyan.
original_explanation: The modern-day oasis for drivers. Not just for "pa-gas," but also for CR breaks, buying overpriced snacks, checking tire pressure, or as the easiest landmark for giving directions ("Sa kanto, 'yung may Shell, kumanan ka."). It's the pit stop of life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **gasolinahan** sa may kanto ng EDSA.","translation":"Let's meet at the **gas station** on the corner of EDSA."}]

meaning_filipino: Labis na katakawan sa pagkain; pagiging masiba o labis-labis kung kumain.
original_explanation: This describes that one friend at the "eat-all-you-can" buffet who takes the "all you can" part as a personal challenge. They're not just hungry, they're on a mission. It’s a state of extreme food lust, where the plate is piled high and no food is safe. Think fiesta-level eating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **pakabuya** ang taong iyon, naubos niya ang limang platong kanin.","translation":"That person is truly **gluttonous**; he finished five plates of rice."},{"sentence":"Naging **pakabuya** siya sa handaan kagabi.","translation":"He became **voracious** at the party last night."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa posisyong ang ulo at itaas na bahagi ng katawan ay nakahapay pauna at pababa, kadalasan bilang tanda ng paggalang, kalungkutan, o pag-iwas.
original_explanation: The default position when you're walking past your crush so they don't see you blushing. Also, the pose of shame when your mom finds your stash of bad grades. In a more formal sense, it's a sign of respect, like when you pass in front of elders. It's the physical embodiment of 'pasintabi po.'
usage_notes: Can indicate respect, shame, sadness, or simply the physical action of looking down.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay laging **nakayuko** kapag dumadaan sa harap ng mga nakatatanda.","translation":"He is always **bowing** when passing in front of elders."},{"sentence":"Malungkot siyang pumasok sa kwarto na **nakayuko** ang ulo.","translation":"He sadly entered the room with his head **stooped**."}]

translation: to press with a fingertip; to dot
meaning_filipino: Mariing diinan o tusukin ang isang bagay gamit ang dulo ng daliri o anumang matulis na bagay.
original_explanation: Ever tried to get your lolo's attention while he's watching TV? You gently idutdot his shoulder. Or when you're putting ketchup on your fries, one meticulous drop at a time? 'Yan ang pag-dutdot. It's also what you do to your phone screen when you're 'seen-zoning' someone. A very specific, targeted poke.
usage_notes: Often implies a gentle but firm and repetitive poking or pressing action. Can also mean to apply something in dots.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **idutdot** ang daliri mo sa cake, hindi pa natin hihiwain 'yan.","translation":"Don't **poke** your finger into the cake, we haven't sliced it yet."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **idinutdot** ang gamot sa bawat sugat.","translation":"He carefully **dotted** the medicine on each wound."}]

translation: to cause someone to curse at you; to provoke cursing
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang bagay na nagiging sanhi upang murahin ka o ang isang tao ng iba.
original_explanation: This is when you do something so annoying, so infuriating, that the only logical response from the other person is a string of curses. Cutting someone off in traffic, spoiling the latest movie, or telling your mom you lost the Tupperware she lent you—all excellent ways to 'magpamura'. You're basically asking for it.
usage_notes: Distinct from 'magmura' (to curse) and the adjective 'mura' (cheap). This verb implies you are the target or cause of the cursing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang gagawa ng ikaiinis niya kung ayaw mong **magpamura**.","translation":"Don't do anything that will annoy him if you don't want to **get cursed at**."},{"sentence":"Talaga bang sinadya mong **magpamura** sa guwardiya para lang mapansin?","translation":"Did you really intentionally **provoke the guard into cursing at you** just to get noticed?"}]

translation: To describe, to portray, to illustrate
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng katangian, anyo, o deskripsyon ang isang tao, bagay, lugar, o pangyayari sa pamamagitan ng salita o sining.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend asks, 'So, anong itsura niya?' and you have to paint a picture with words. 'Matangkad, maputi, chinito... parang Korean actor!' It’s the verb for turning thoughts and images into words or art. Parang paggawa ng character sketch sa fan fiction.
usage_notes: A very common word in both spoken and written language, especially in storytelling and descriptions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **ilarawan** sa salita ang ganda ng paglubog ng araw sa dalampasigan.","translation":"It's hard to **describe** in words the beauty of the sunset on the beach."},{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **ilarawan** ang hitsura ng magnanakaw?","translation":"Can you **describe** the appearance of the thief?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na tawag sa isang babae, na pinaikli mula sa salitang Ingles na 'sister', ginagamit bilang paglalambing o pangkaraniwang tawag sa kaibigan, kapatid, o kahit estranghero.
etymology: Mula sa pinaikling salitang Ingles na 'sister'.
original_explanation: The go-to call sign for your female friends, barkada, or even the friendly ate selling you something online ("Thanks, sis!"). It's the verbal equivalent of a supportive head nod. Can also be used with a hint of sarcasm: "Okay, sis."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa social media at text messaging bilang isang kolokyal na pantawag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sis**, saan mo nabili 'yang damit mo? Ang ganda!","translation":"**Sis**, where did you buy that dress? It's beautiful!"},{"sentence":"Hi **sis**, available pa po ba ito?","translation":"Hi **sis**, is this still available?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kulungan, karaniwang gawa sa mga baras na metal o alambre, para sa mga hayop o ibon.
original_explanation: Parang yung puso mo, nakakulong sa "what ifs" ninyo. Charot. Ito yung kulungan ng lovebirds, as in yung literal na ibon, hindi kayo ng jowa mo. Mas kilala ito sa spelling na 'hawla'.
usage_notes: Ang mas karaniwang baybay at gamit sa modernong Filipino ay 'hawla'. Ang 'haula' ay itinuturing na luma o di-karaniwan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa loob ng gintong **haula** ang alagang ibon ng prinsesa.","translation":"The princess's pet bird is inside a golden **cage**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan hinuhukay mula sa lupa ang mga mineral, tulad ng ginto, karbon, o diyamante.
original_explanation: This isn't your ex's DMs; this is where people dig for actual gold and other precious stuff. Think Baguio gold mines or the controversial mining sites you see on the news. It's a place of hard labor, potential wealth, and often, a whole lot of environmental issues.
usage_notes: Can be used figuratively to mean a source of something valuable, e.g., "mina ng impormasyon" (a mine of information). The word "minahan" is a more common and specific term for a mining site.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming manggagawa ang nagtatrabaho sa **mina** ng ginto.","translation":"Many workers are employed at the gold **mine**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gamitin ang isang pagkakataon, sitwasyon, o kahinaan ng isang tao para sa sariling kapakinabangan, na kadalasan ay may negatibong konotasyon.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "aprovechar" (to take advantage of), na may dinagdag na panlaping Tagalog na "-an".
original_explanation: The Tagalog version of 'seize the opportunity,' but with a slightly shady, opportunistic twist. It's when you see a 'Buy 1 Take 1' sale and you buy 10. It's also used negatively, like when someone uses your kindness for their own gain. 'Huwag mo akong **aprobetsahan** dahil lang mabait ako sa'yo!' It's the classic 'hugot' line for people who feel used.
usage_notes: Maaaring magkaroon ng positibo (take advantage of an opportunity) o negatibong (exploit someone) kahulugan depende sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Aprobetsahan** mo ang pagkakataon habang nandito pa ang iyong lola.","translation":"**Take advantage** of the opportunity while your grandmother is still here."},{"sentence":"Masama ang **aprobetsahan** ang kahinaan ng iyong kapwa.","translation":"It is bad to **take advantage of** your fellow person's weakness."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **aprobetsahan** ang long weekend para mag-out of town.","translation":"We should **take advantage of** the long weekend to go out of town."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ikaapat na planeta mula sa Araw sa sistemang solar, na kilala rin bilang Pulang Planeta.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'Marte', ang pangalan ng diyos ng digmaan sa mitolohiyang Romano, na siyang ipinangalan sa planeta.
original_explanation: The OG Red Planet. Not your tita's bestie, but the actual planet Elon Musk wants to turn into a subdivision. It's the place we look at when we wonder if there's life out there, or just a lot of red dust and rocks.
usage_notes: A proper noun and should be capitalized.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap ng mga siyentista na makarating sa planetang **Marte**.","translation":"Scientists dream of reaching the planet **Mars**."},{"sentence":"Ang **Marte** ay mas maliit kaysa sa Daigdig.","translation":"**Mars** is smaller than Earth."}]

translation: fell flat on one's back; dropped dead
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagbagsak na nakatihaya, kadalasan ay walang buhay o malay.
original_explanation: This is a very dramatic fall. Think action movie villain getting shot and falling backward, or that feeling after a 12-hour shift where you just want to fall flat on your bed. It’s not just falling; it’s falling flat, often with a sense of finality or extreme exhaustion.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a dead body or someone who has fainted and fallen backward. It's a very descriptive and somewhat dramatic word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos tamaan ng bala, **bumulagta** ang kawatan sa kalsada.","translation":"After being hit by a bullet, the thief **fell flat on his back** on the street."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod, gusto ko na lang **bumulagta** sa kama.","translation":"From extreme exhaustion, I just want to **drop dead** on the bed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain na walang kabuluhan, puno ng kalokohan, o kawalang-hiyaan.
etymology: From the Spanish-derived curse word `tarantado` (stupid, jerk) + `ka-` and `-an` affixes to form a noun describing the act or quality.
original_explanation: This is the mother of all 'kalokohan'. It's not just simple naughtiness; it's next-level foolishness, often with a hint of being an asshole. Think pranks that go too far, office gossip that ruins careers, or politicians' promises. That's katarantaduhan. It’s the stuff that makes your parents or your boss shake their head and say 'Ano na namang katarantaduhan 'to?!'
usage_notes: A strong, informal, and mildly vulgar word. Not typically used in polite or formal company.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang **katarantaduhan** mo at magseryoso ka sa buhay.","translation":"Stop your **foolishness** and get serious with your life."},{"sentence":"Puro **katarantaduhan** ang laman ng isip ng batang iyan.","translation":"That kid's mind is full of **nonsense**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hungkag na instrumentong metal, karaniwang hugis-tasa, na gumagawa ng tunog kapag pinatama ng isang bagay sa loob o labas nito.
original_explanation: The English word for 'kampana' that everyone just uses. It's the sound that signals 'recess na!', 'uwian na!', or 'andyan na 'yung sorbetero!'. From the church bell to the doorbell to the tiny bell on your cat's collar, it's the universal sound for 'Hey, listen up!'.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with its Tagalog counterpart 'kampana' or 'batingaw,' but 'bell' is more common for smaller, modern devices like doorbells.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pindutin mo ang **bell** sa gate.","translation":"Press the **bell** at the gate."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **bell** ng ice cream vendor.","translation":"I heard the **bell** of the ice cream vendor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ikabit ang pamatok o paningkaw sa isang hayop, karaniwan ay kalabaw o baka, upang makahila ng araro o kariton.
original_explanation: Old-school Uber setup for your carabao. It's the act of gearing up your beast of burden before a long day of plowing the fields. Think of it as putting the key in the ignition, but for farming.
usage_notes: Primarily used in agricultural or historical contexts involving draft animals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maagang gumising ang magsasaka upang **magsingkaw** ng kanyang kalabaw.","translation":"The farmer woke up early to **harness** his carabao."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong matutunang **magsingkaw** nang mahigpit para hindi makawala ang baka.","translation":"You need to learn to **yoke** it tightly so the cow won't get loose."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang prutas o butil na nasa hustong gulang na, malambot, at karaniwang matamis at handa nang kainin.
original_explanation: This is that perfect mango—hindi na kulay green, hindi pa overripe na parang may hangover. 'Yung tamang-tama lang ang tamis at lambot. Figuratively, ito rin yung sinasabi sa'yo ng tita mo about your love life: "Hayaan mo lang mahinog 'yan, 'wag magmadali." It means waiting for the perfect timing.
usage_notes: Primarily for fruits, but can be used metaphorically for plans, ideas, or maturity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hintayin nating **mahinog** ang mga mangga bago natin pitasin.","translation":"Let's wait for the mangoes to become **ripe** before we pick them."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga ideya ay hindi pa **mahinog** para sa isang malaking proyekto.","translation":"His ideas are not yet **mature** enough for a big project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakapangunahin at pinakamaliit na yunit ng istruktura ng lahat ng nabubuhay na organismo. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa isang maliit na silid sa bilangguan o isang maliit na pangkat sa loob ng isang organisasyon.
original_explanation: Flashback to high school biology class! The building block of life. Mitochondria is the powerhouse of the selula. Also, in a different, more serious context, it can refer to a small, organized group, often with a political or clandestine purpose. Or, you know, a prison cell. So, context is key, from your own body to a revolutionary movement.
usage_notes: Can refer to a biological cell, a prison cell, or a small group/unit within a larger organization.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa biyolohiya ang iba't ibang bahagi ng **selula**.","translation":"Different parts of the **cell** are studied in biology."},{"sentence":"Bumuo sila ng isang lihim na **selula** upang isulong ang kanilang adbokasiya.","translation":"They formed a secret **cell** to advance their advocacy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking gusali o pangkat ng mga gusali na naglalaman ng iba't ibang tindahan, kainan, at lugar-libangan.
original_explanation: The modern-day plaza of the Philippines. The default answer to "Saan tayo?" It's our refuge from the heat, the place for dates, family outings, and window shopping. From SM to Robinsons to Ayala, the mall is not just a place to shop, it's a cultural hub with free aircon.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, fully integrated into Filipino. Often used with Filipino grammar, e.g., 'nag-mall' (went to the mall), 'sa mall' (at the mall), 'mag-mall' (to go to the mall).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita na lang tayo sa entrance ng **mall**.","translation":"Let's just meet at the entrance of the **mall**."},{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa **mall** para lang magpalamig.","translation":"We went to the **mall** just to cool down."}]

translation: to be able to equal or match
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang maging kapantay o katumbas sa halaga, kalidad, o antas.
original_explanation: That feeling when you try to find a dupe for a high-end product. Can this P200 foundation 'makatumbas' the P2000 one? It's the ability to match or be equivalent to something else, whether it's in price, skill, or love. "Walang makakatumbas sa pagmamahal ng isang ina." (Nothing can equal a mother's love.)
usage_notes: Used for comparing value, quality, or abstract concepts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang halaga ng pera ang **makakatumbas** sa tunay na kaligayahan.","translation":"No amount of money can **equal** true happiness."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng kandidatong **makakatumbas** sa kwalipikasyon ng dating empleyado.","translation":"He is looking for a candidate who can **match** the qualifications of the former employee."}]

translation: to be shaded, to be covered
meaning_filipino: Malagyan ng lilim o masilungan mula sa sikat ng araw o anumang bagay na nasa itaas.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-`, salitang ugat na `yungyong` (shade cast by something), at hulaping `-an`.
original_explanation: Kapag tirik na tirik ang araw at naghahanap ka ng puno para di ka masunog, ang gusto mo ay mayungyungan. It's to be covered or shaded by something above you, like an umbrella, a tree, or even the shadow of a taller person. Literal na 'throwin' shade,' but in a good, protective way.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa paraang patula. Ang salitang ugat na 'yungyong' ay tumutukoy sa akto ng pagbibigay lilim o sa lilim mismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humanap tayo ng malaking payong para **mayungyungan** tayong lahat.","translation":"Let's find a big umbrella so we can all **be shaded**."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **mayungyungan** ng malagong puno habang nagbabasa.","translation":"She wants **to be shaded** by a lush tree while reading."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na paglalahad ng mga katotohanan o kaganapan, pasulat man o pasalita.
original_explanation: That thing your boss asks for at 5 PM on a Friday. It's also what Noli de Castro delivers on TV Patrol. From a school book report to a police report to a weather report ('ulat panahon'), it's basically an official summary of 'anong nangyari?' or 'anong chika?'. The formal version of a 'sumbong'.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb 'mag-ulat' (to report).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong tapusin ang aking **ulat** para bukas.","translation":"I need to finish my **report** for tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa **ulat** ng PAGASA, may paparating na bagyo.","translation":"According to the PAGASA **report**, there is an approaching typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang inumin na nakapag-aalis o nakababawas ng pakiramdam ng pagkauhaw.
etymology: Compound of "pamatid" (from 'patid', to cut/trip, but here means 'to cut off/stop') and "uhaw" (thirst).
original_explanation: Your best friend on a hot day after walking under the noon sun. Could be a cold bottle of water, a buko juice from the street vendor, or that ridiculously sweet sago't gulaman. Anything that stops you from feeling like a human desert.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malamig na tubig ang pinakamabisang **pamatid-uhaw**.","translation":"Cold water is the most effective **thirst quencher**."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap kami ng buko juice na **pamatid-uhaw** pagkatapos ng aming laro.","translation":"We were looking for coconut juice as a **thirst quencher** after our game."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o lugar kung saan ginagamot ang mga taong may sakit o pinsala.
original_explanation: The more formal, slightly old-school word for 'ospital'. You'll see this on government-run health centers and provincial hospitals. It sounds more serious and, let's be honest, a bit more intimidating than 'ospital'. It's where you go when 'pagalingin' is the goal.
usage_notes: While 'ospital' is more common in everyday conversation, 'pagamutan' is prevalent in formal writing, news reports, and official government names for health facilities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinugod siya sa pinakamalapit na **pagamutan** matapos ang aksidente.","translation":"He was rushed to the nearest **hospital** after the accident."},{"sentence":"Ang pampublikong **pagamutan** ay nagbibigay ng libreng serbisyo sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"The public **hospital** provides free services to the poor."}]

translation: Absolutely everything; all in all; the sum total
meaning_filipino: Isang pagdidiin sa salitang "lahat," na nangangahulugang ang kabuuang-buo, walang anumang natira o kulang.
original_explanation: This is "lahat" on steroids. It’s the ultimate, final, no-take-backs version of "all." When your ex says, "Ibinigay ko sa'yo ang lahat-lahat sa akin," that’s pure hugot. It’s the total of your GrabFood order including the delivery fee and the tip. It’s the sum of all your fears before a big presentation. Lahat-lahat na.
usage_notes: Used for emphasis to mean "absolutely everything."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lahat-lahat**, umabot sa isang libong piso ang aming nagastos.","translation":"**All in all**, our expenses reached one thousand pesos."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **lahat-lahat** sa buhay ko.","translation":"He/She is **absolutely everything** in my life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan para sa pagdurog ng mani, kadalasang ginagamit sa paghahanda ng mga panghimagas o sarsa.
original_explanation: That thing you need for making kare-kare from scratch or for the topping on your halo-halo. It could be a high-tech grinder or just a bottle rolling over peanuts inside a plastic bag. Resourcefulness is key!
usage_notes: Maaaring isang partikular na aparato o isang pangkalahatang termino para sa anumang paraan ng pagdurog ng mani.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wala kaming **pandurog ng mani**, kaya bote na lang ang ginamit ko.","translation":"We don't have a **peanut crusher**, so I just used a bottle."},{"sentence":"Ang sikreto sa masarap na kare-kare ay ang bagong durog na mani mula sa **pandurog ng mani**.","translation":"The secret to delicious kare-kare is freshly crushed peanuts from the **peanut crusher**."}]

translation: to cause to become fragrant; to spread fragrance
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng pagkalat o paglabas ng isang mabangong amoy mula sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what flowers, perfumes, and your mom's adobo do. Sila 'yung **nagpapahalimuyak** sa buong bahay. It's the act of making a place smell good, whether it's sampaguita, scented candles, or 'yung bagong saing na kanin. The ultimate goal of air fresheners.
usage_notes: A more poetic and positive word than just 'magpaamoy' (to cause to smell). `Halimuyak` specifically refers to a pleasant scent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bulaklak ng sampaguita ay **nagpapahalimuyak** sa buong hardin.","translation":"The sampaguita flowers **spread their fragrance** throughout the whole garden."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng insenso para **magpahalimuyak** sa silid.","translation":"He used incense to **make the room fragrant**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang prutas na hindi pa lubos na hinog ngunit hindi na rin masasabing hilaw; nasa pagitan ng pagiging hilaw at hinog.
etymology: From the prefix 'ma-' (denoting a quality) and 'nibalang', a term describing a state of ripeness.
original_explanation: That mango that's not totally sweet yet but also not super sour. Perfect to eat with bagoong as a side dish. It's like your feelings for them—not yet a sure 'yes' but no longer a 'no'. It's complicated, but delicious. The 'it's complicated' stage of a fruit's love life.
usage_notes: Primarily used for fruits like mangoes, papayas, and bananas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto kong kainin ang papaya kapag **manibalang** pa ito.","translation":"I prefer to eat the papaya when it's still **semi-ripe**."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang kilong **manibalang** na mangga para isawsaw sa bagoong.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of **half-ripe** mangoes to dip in shrimp paste."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bawat isa sa maliliit at manipis na piraso na bumabalot sa katawan ng isda at ilang uri ng reptilya. Ginagamit din ito sa kolokyal na pananalita para tumukoy sa balakubak.
original_explanation: What you have to scrape off a fish before you cook it, making the whole kitchen smell... fishy. Also, the "snow" on your shoulders if you use the wrong shampoo. "Uy, may kaliskis ka sa balikat mo!" is a low-key way of saying "You have dandruff."
usage_notes: Has a primary meaning (fish scales) and a very common secondary, colloquial meaning (dandruff).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinulungan ko si nanay na mag-alis ng **kaliskis** ng isda sa palengke.","translation":"I helped mom remove the **scales** from the fish at the market."}]

translation: a servant who works only for food
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng alila o katulong na ang tanging kabayaran sa serbisyo ay pagkain at tirahan, at hindi tumatanggap ng sahod.
original_explanation: This is the OG "for exposure" gig. Imagine working a full-time job where your salary is just... unli-rice. It's a term for someone who's being taken advantage of, getting paid in "experience" and free meals instead of actual cash.
usage_notes: A derogatory, idiomatic term highlighting extreme exploitation. It has historical roots but is used metaphorically today to describe unfair labor practices.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuring siyang parang **alilang-kanin** ng kanyang malupit na tiyahin.","translation":"She was treated like a **servant who works only for food** by her cruel aunt."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang papayag na maging **alilang-kanin** lang sa kumpanyang iyan!","translation":"Don't agree to be just a **servant paid only in food** in that company!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa musikang ginagamitan lamang ng mga instrumentong hindi de-kuryente, gaya ng gitara; isang pagtatanghal na may ganitong uri ng musika.
original_explanation: Ito yung "unplugged" version ng paborito mong kanta. Tipong chill lang, gitara at boses lang, sapat na. Perfect for coffee shop dates or "senti" nights. Pag sinabing "acoustic night" sa bar, asahan mo nang maraming hugot songs ang tutugtugin.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng musika. Madalas ipinagpapalit sa "akustika" ngunit may magkaibang pokus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang **akustiks** na bersyon ng kantang iyon.","translation":"I prefer the **acoustic** version of that song."},{"sentence":"May **akustiks** na tugtugan sa bar mamayang gabi.","translation":"There's an **acoustic** gig at the bar tonight."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang gawain o paraan ng pagsukat ay sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng dangkal o ang haba mula sa dulo ng hinlalaki hanggang sa dulo ng kalingkingan.
original_explanation: Before 'yung mga metro stick at measuring tape, may mga **mandadangkal**. Sila 'yung original na human ruler. 'Pag nagpapagawa ka ng lamesa sa karpintero noon, "Sige, sukatin mo ng sampung dangkal." Sila 'yun. Today, sila 'yung tropa mong expert mag-estimate ng size ng pizza just by looking.
usage_notes: This is a very rare word, formed from the 'man-'(doer) prefix and the root 'dangkal' (handspan). It's more of a descriptive noun than a common job title.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang bihasang **mandadangkal** ang matandang karpintero sa aming nayon.","translation":"The old carpenter in our village was an expert **one who measures by handspans**."},{"sentence":"Walang dalang panukat kaya ang **mandadangkal** na lang ang ginamit na paraan.","translation":"They had no measuring tool, so the **one who measures by handspans** was the method used."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman na may mahahaba at malutong na tangkay na karaniwang ginagamit bilang gulay sa pagluluto o kinakain nang hilaw.
original_explanation: 'Yung gulay na parang stick na may kakaibang amoy. Paborito ng mga tita na nagju-juice para maging healthy. Madalas side character sa sopas, afritada, at buffalo wings.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang sangkap sa iba't ibang lutuin, parehong lokal at internasyonal. Ang lokal na katumbas nito ay kintsay, bagaman may kaunting pagkakaiba sa lasa at laki.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **celery** ang afritada para bumango.","translation":"Add **celery** to the afritada to make it fragrant."},{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng isang tali ng **celery** sa supermarket.","translation":"Buy a bunch of **celery** at the supermarket."}]

translation: to break ties with; to have a falling out
meaning_filipino: Ang pagputol ng magandang ugnayan o pagkakaibigan sa isang tao, na kadalasan ay nagreresulta sa hindi pagkakaunawaan o alitan.
etymology: From makipag- (social verb prefix) + sira (break, destroy).
original_explanation: This is the dramatic 'unfriend' button in real life. It's when you have a major fight with your BFF and you decide you're not friends anymore. It's the opposite of 'makipagbati'. It's the end of an era, often fueled by chismis, utang, or a love triangle.
usage_notes: The makipag- prefix implies a mutual action or a situation involving the other person, even if the decision to break ties is one-sided. It's about the relationship itself breaking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **makipagsira** sa iyo dahil lang sa maliit na hindi pagkakaunawaan.","translation":"I don't want to **have a falling out** with you just because of a small misunderstanding."},{"sentence":"Nagdesisyon siyang **makipagsira** sa kanyang kasosyo sa negosyo.","translation":"She decided to **break ties** with her business partner."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng pag-aalinlangan o pag-uurong-sulong ng isang tao sa paggawa ng isang desisyon o kilos.
original_explanation: This is when a situation or a person gives you major "pause." Like when your crush finally asks you out, but you remember your five pending deadlines – that's your workload making you magpaatubili. Or when the food delivery app shows a P200 delivery fee for a P150 meal. The situation itself is causing you to hesitate and rethink your life choices.
usage_notes: Less common in casual conversation, more in formal or literary writing. The subject of the verb is the person or thing causing the hesitation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang laki ng gastusin ay siyang **nagpaatubili** sa kanya na ituloy ang plano.","translation":"The large expense was what **made him hesitate** to continue with the plan."},{"sentence":"Huwag sanang **magpaatubili** sa iyo ang mga pagsubok na darating.","translation":"I hope the coming challenges won't **cause you to hesitate**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na bahay na karaniwang yari sa mga likas na materyales tulad ng kawayan, nipa, at pawid.
original_explanation: The iconic Filipino bahay kubo. It's that simple, rustic hut you see in provinces, made of bamboo and nipa leaves. It's the ultimate symbol of simple, rural life. It's naturally air-conditioned and the subject of that folk song everyone had to memorize in elementary school.
usage_notes: Ang buong pangalan nito, "bahay-kubo," ay mas karaniwang ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtayo sila ng isang maliit na **kubo** sa tabi ng bukid.","translation":"They built a small **hut** beside the farm."},{"sentence":"Masarap magpahinga sa **kubo** dahil presko ang hangin.","translation":"It's nice to rest in a **nipa hut** because the air is fresh."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na buo, walang kulang, lubos, o perpekto.
original_explanation: This is the '100% legit, no holds barred, full-on' version of something. A 'ganap na babae' is a fully realized woman. 'Ganap na kadiliman' is pitch black darkness, the kind where you can't even see your hand in front of your face. It's the opposite of 'medyo lang' or 'pwede na.' It's the final form.
usage_notes: Often used with 'na' to modify a noun, e.g., 'ganap na kalayaan' (absolute freedom).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakamit niya ang **ganap** na kaligayahan sa piling ng kanyang pamilya.","translation":"She achieved **complete** happiness with her family."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng **ganap** na pagkakaisa upang malampasan ang krisis na ito.","translation":"We need **absolute** unity to overcome this crisis."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasama o kabilang sa parehong pangkat ng mga sundalo; isang kapwa sundalo.
etymology: From ka- (denoting companionship or being part of a group) + sundalo (soldier).
original_explanation: Your buddy in the army. Your 'tropa' or 'brad' in uniform. The person you share a bunk with, complain about your sergeant with, and would trust with your life in the trenches. Think of it as your work-bestie, but your work involves national security.
usage_notes: The prefix 'ka-' is very productive in Filipino for creating nouns that mean 'fellow,' 'co-,' or 'partner.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinahagi niya ang kanyang rasyon sa kanyang mga **kasundalo**.","translation":"He shared his rations with his **fellow soldiers**."},{"sentence":"Tinalikuran siya ng kanyang mga dating **kasundalo** matapos siyang maakusahan ng pagtataksil.","translation":"His former **fellow soldiers** turned their backs on him after he was accused of treason."}]

translation: to scramble for; to work hard with one's hands
meaning_filipino: Ang masigasig na paggawa o pagkilos gamit ang mga kamay upang makamit o makuha ang isang bagay, kadalasan sa gitna ng kakulangan o kompetisyon.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `kumamot` (related to grabbing or scratching for something).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "diskarte" verb. Imagine the last piece of lechon kawali on the plate, and everyone's tinidor is flying. That's magkumamot. It's also what your parents did, working multiple jobs, para lang mapag-aral ka. It's the hustle, the grind, using your bare hands (figuratively) to get what you need.
usage_notes: Implies effort, urgency, and sometimes competition. It's more intense than just "magtrabaho" (to work).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magkumamot** para may maihanda tayo sa Pasko.","translation":"We need to **work hard** so we can prepare something for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Nag-agawan ang mga bata at **nagkumamot** para sa mga pabitin.","translation":"The children competed and **scrambled** for the items in the pabitin."}]

translation: to catch; to join for a meal
meaning_filipino: May dalawang pangunahing kahulugan: (1) Ang akto ng pagsalo o pagdakma sa isang bagay na nahuhulog o inihagis. (2) Ang pakikiupo at pakikisabay sa isang gawain, lalo na sa pagkain sa isang hapag-kainan.
original_explanation: 1. The literal 'OMG save it!' moment when your phone slips from your hand and you 'sumalo' it just before it hits the concrete. 2. The heartwarming 'Uy, kain tayo!' moment when you arrive and your family/friends are already eating, and they invite you to 'sumalo'. It's catching both falling objects and free meals.
usage_notes: Has two common meanings: catching a physical object and joining a meal. Context is key. 'Sumalo sa salu-salo' means to join the party/feast.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis niyang **sinalo** ang nahuhulog na baso.","translation":"He quickly **caught** the falling glass."},{"sentence":"Halika, **sumalo** ka sa aming hapunan.","translation":"Come, **join** us for dinner."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa katangian ng pagiging mahiyain, pino kumilos, at hindi magarbo o maingay.
etymology: Pag-uulit ng isang ugat, na karaniwan sa mga wikang Austronesian upang ipahiwatig ang tindi o isang partikular na kalidad.
original_explanation: The Maria Clara vibe. It's the trait lolas want to see in their apo. Speaking softly, moving gracefully, and generally not causing a scene. In modern terms, it's the opposite of being 'walang preno' or 'kalog.' It's the 'low-key lang' attitude personified.
usage_notes: Madalas na naglalarawan sa kilos o pag-uugali ng isang tao, lalo na ng isang babae. Ang 'mahinhin' ang karaniwang anyo ng pang-uri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **hinhin** niya ay hinahangaan ng marami.","translation":"Her **modesty** is admired by many."},{"sentence":"Kilala si Maria bilang isang dalagang may **hinhin**.","translation":"Maria is known as a young woman of **gentleness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pag-aalis o pagtatanggal sa isang tao mula sa pagiging kasapi ng isang samahan, organisasyon, o relihiyon.
original_explanation: The ultimate "You're fired!" or "You can't sit with us." It's not just being kicked out; it's a formal, often dramatic, removal from a group. Think getting kicked out of a religious group, a political party, or even that exclusive K-Pop fan club for breaking the rules. It's the official act of being declared an outsider.
usage_notes: A very strong and formal word, often used in religious, political, or organizational contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahaharap siya sa **pagtitiwalag** mula sa partido dahil sa kanyang mga ginawa.","translation":"He is facing **expulsion** from the party because of his actions."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtitiwalag** sa isang miyembro ay isang seryosong desisyon.","translation":"The **excommunication** of a member is a serious decision."}]

translation: will undress; will take off clothes
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aalis ng kasuotan sa katawan sa hinaharap. Ito ang aspektong kontemplatibo ng pandiwang 'hubad'.
original_explanation: That moment when you get home after a long day in Manila traffic and the first thing you want to do is get out of your tight jeans. "Sino maghuhubad ng sapatos sa loob ng bahay?" - every Filipino mom. It's the future tense of getting comfy.
usage_notes: This is the future tense form of the verb 'maghubad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maghuhubad** muna ako ng basang damit bago ako umupo.","translation":"I **will take off** my wet clothes first before I sit down."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maghuhubad** dito, maraming tao!","translation":"Don't **undress** here, there are many people!"}]

translation: will be delivered (of a baby); will be assisted in giving birth
meaning_filipino: Tutulungan o pangangasiwaan sa proseso ng pagsisilang ng isang sanggol.
original_explanation: This is what the OB-GYN or the *hilot* (traditional midwife) does. The pregnant woman is the one giving birth (`manganganak`), but the doctor is the one who will "make her give birth" or assist her. "Si Dra. Santos ang **papanganakin** sa misis ko." It’s not forceful; it means she will be the one to deliver the baby.
usage_notes: This verb refers to the action of the person assisting the birth (e.g., doctor, midwife), not the mother giving birth ('manganganak').
