usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sikat na doktor ang **papanganakin** sa reyna.","translation":"The famous doctor **will deliver** the queen's baby."},{"sentence":"Ligtas siyang **pinanganak** ng kanyang lola na isang hilot.","translation":"She was safely **delivered** by her grandmother who was a traditional midwife."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagwagi sa isang laban, kompetisyon, o paligsahan. Naranasan ang pagkagapi.
original_explanation: The official feeling of every Filipino basketball fan during the last two minutes of a close FIBA game. It's the "sakit, 'no?" moment when your bet in the elections, your favorite UAAP team, or your Mobile Legends squad doesn't come out on top. You tried your best, but your best wasn't enough. Hugot level: 100.
usage_notes: Past tense of the verb 'matalo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Natalo** man sa laro, panalo pa rin sa puso ng bayan.","translation":"**Even if defeated** in the game, still a winner in the hearts of the nation."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang malungkot kung **natalo** ka, ang mahalaga ay lumaban ka.","translation":"Don't be sad if you **lost**, what's important is that you fought."}]

translation: to be rained on; to shower with something
meaning_filipino: Literal na mabasa ng ulan, o sa matalinhagang paraan, ang pagtanggap ng sunod-sunod at napakaraming bagay, tulad ng papuri, bala, o biyaya.
original_explanation: Literally, getting caught in the rain without an umbrella. Figuratively, it's what happens when you post a cute selfie and get showered with 'heart' reactions, or when a politician gets showered with questions from the press. It means to be deluged by something.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for rain or figuratively for an overwhelming amount of anything.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagmadali siyang umuwi para hindi **paulanan** ang mga sinampay.","translation":"She hurried home so the laundry wouldn't **be rained on**."},{"sentence":"Matapos manalo sa lotto, **paulanan** siya ng mga kamag-anak na nanghihiram ng pera.","translation":"After winning the lottery, he was **showered** with relatives wanting to borrow money."}]

translation: to scoop up water; to fetch water (with a container)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng tubig o anumang likido mula sa isang lalagyan o pinagmulan gamit ang isang sisidlan tulad ng tabo o timba.
etymology: From `salok`, the act of scooping water.
original_explanation: This is what you do with a 'tabo' in the bathroom when the shower is broken. You dip the 'tabo' into the 'timba' (pail) and 'salukin' the water to pour over yourself. It's a fundamental life skill in many Filipino households, especially during a water interruption.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to scooping liquids, most commonly water, from a larger source into a smaller container.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Salukin** mo ng tubig ang banga gamit ang tabo.","translation":"**Scoop water** from the earthen jar using the dipper."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **salukin** ang sabaw mula sa kaldero.","translation":"I need **to scoop** the soup from the pot."}]

translation: to be cured, to get well
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa proseso ng paggaling o pagbuti ng kalagayan mula sa isang sakit o karamdaman.
original_explanation: This is the 'get well soon' verb. When you catch a cold from the BPO office's arctic aircon or after getting soaked in the rain, you hope na 'galingin' ka agad. It's about recovering from sickness. Not to be confused with 'galingan' (to do well). You 'galingan' your exam, but you hope 'galingin' ka from your flu.
usage_notes: This word is less common in modern spoken language than 'gumaling' or 'magpagaling'. It can feel a bit more formal or literary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **galingin** ka na sa iyong ubo at sipon.","translation":"I hope you **get well** soon from your cough and cold."},{"sentence":"Mukhang hindi siya **ginaling** sa trangkaso kahit uminom na ng gamot.","translation":"It seems he wasn't **cured** of the flu even after taking medicine."}]

meaning_filipino: Makulay at maluwag na kasuotan na isinusuot ng isang payaso para sa pagpapatawa.
original_explanation: That ridiculously colorful, oversized outfit you see at children's parties. Can also be used figuratively for someone whose fashion sense is... questionable. 'Uy, para kang naka-damit-payaso' is not a compliment. It's the OOTD for when you want to look like you got dressed in the dark during a circus explosion.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for a costume or figuratively for a very loud or mismatched outfit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagrenta siya ng **damit-payaso** para sa birthday party ng kanyang anak.","translation":"He rented a **clown costume** for his child's birthday party."},{"sentence":"Ang suot mong polka dots at stripes ay parang **damit-payaso**!","translation":"Your polka dots and stripes outfit looks like a **clown costume**!"}]

translation: to get along with others; to interact with fellow human beings
meaning_filipino: Ang pakikisalamuha o pakikitungo sa ibang tao sa isang maayos at magalang na paraan, na kinikilala ang pagkakapantay-pantay bilang kapwa-tao.
etymology: From 'makipag-' (to mutually do something) and 'kapwa' (fellow human being, other).
original_explanation: This is the core of Filipino social life. It's not just about being nice; it's about seeing yourself in others and treating them with respect, whether they're your boss, the security guard, or the 'taho' vendor. It's the opposite of being a snob. It's the reason why we can make friends even in a long queue for the MRT.
usage_notes: A deep cultural concept related to "pakikisama" but with a stronger emphasis on empathy and shared humanity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tunay na Pilipino ay marunong **makipagkapwa**.","translation":"A true Filipino knows how to **get along with others**."},{"sentence":"Itinuro sa amin ng aming mga magulang ang kahalagahan ng **makipagkapwa**-tao.","translation":"Our parents taught us the importance of **interacting well with our fellow human beings**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan sagana o maraming matatagpuang suso (isang uri ng kuhol).
original_explanation: A snail farm, or just that really damp, mossy part of your lola's garden where all the snails hang out. It’s where you go hunting for "ginataang suso" ingredients, armed with a pail and a lot of patience.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix denotes a place where the root noun ('suso' - snail) is abundant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa **susuhan** sa tabi ng ilog para manghuli ng aming uulamin.","translation":"We went to the **place with many snails** by the river to catch our food."},{"sentence":"Maingat kang maglakad diyan dahil madulas sa **susuhan**.","translation":"Walk carefully there because it's slippery in the **snail-infested area**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang taong lubhang magastos o walang pakundangan sa pagwaldas ng pera o yaman. Madalas itong ginagamit sa pariralang "prodigal son" (alibughang anak).
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "prodigal," hango sa Latin na "prodigere" (to drive away, to waste).
original_explanation: The original "nag-abroad, umuwing walang naipon." This isn't just someone who splurges on milk tea; this is the person who inherits a fortune and spends it all on lavish parties and bad investments. The term is most famous from the Bible story about the 'prodigal son' who came home broke and was still welcomed with a feast—a scenario every financially-struggling Pinoy dreams of.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in reference to the biblical parable of the "Prodigal Son," which is "Alibughang Anak" in Filipino. The direct use of "prodigal" in a Tagalog sentence is rare and literary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kuwento ng **prodigal** son, o alibughang anak, ay tungkol sa pagpapatawad.","translation":"The story of the **prodigal** son is about forgiveness."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng kanyang **prodigal** na pamumuhay sa siyudad, umuwi siyang walang-wala.","translation":"After his **prodigal** lifestyle in the city, he returned with nothing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o libingan kung saan inililibing ang mga yumao, karaniwang may kaugnayan sa isang simbahan o lumang estruktura.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'final resting place' before memorial parks became a thing. Think old, Spanish-era churchyards with creepy statues. It's the setting for 90% of Filipino horror movies, where a 'white lady' is practically a required resident. Often used interchangeably with 'sementeryo', but 'pantiyon' has a more classic, almost spooky vibe.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'sementeryo'. 'Pantiyon' has a slightly more archaic or formal feel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dadalawin namin ang puntod ni lolo sa **pantiyon** sa Araw ng mga Patay.","translation":"We will visit grandpa's grave in the **cemetery** on All Souls' Day."},{"sentence":"Maraming kuwento ng kababalaghan ang naikakabit sa lumang **pantiyon** sa aming bayan.","translation":"Many ghost stories are associated with the old **cemetery** in our town."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng keso na bilog ang hugis at nababalutan ng pulang pagkit. Karaniwang inihahanda ito tuwing Pasko at Bagong Taon sa Pilipinas.
etymology: From Spanish "queso de bola" (ball of cheese).
original_explanation: The official cheese of Philippine Christmas. This is the red, waxy ball of salty goodness that magically appears on every Noche Buena table, sitting right next to the hamon. You know the holidays are near when you see stacks of keso-de-bola at the supermarket. It's a status symbol and a Christmas staple, even if you only eat it once a year.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to Edam cheese.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hiwain mo na ang **keso-de-bola** para sa ating Noche Buena.","translation":"Slice the **Edam cheese** now for our Noche Buena."},{"sentence":"Masarap isama sa ensaymada ang ginadgad na **keso-de-bola**.","translation":"Grated **Edam cheese** is delicious on top of ensaymada."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang numerong 100; isang yunit ng pagbilang na katumbas ng sampung sampu.
original_explanation: The number that comes after 99. Usually followed by "na piso" when you're asking your parents for money. "Isang daan" can get you a decent meal, or if you're in BGC, maybe just a bottle of water.
usage_notes: Pronounced /DA-an/ with the stress on the first syllable. Often used with a number prefix (e.g., isa-ng daan, dala-wang daan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng isang **daan**.","translation":"Give me one **hundred**."},{"sentence":"Mahigit limang **daan** katao ang dumalo sa pagtitipon.","translation":"More than five **hundred** people attended the gathering."}]

translation: to bow one's head; to stoop
meaning_filipino: Ang pagyuko ng ulo bilang tanda ng paggalang, kalungkutan, o pag-iisip.
original_explanation: It's that move you do when you pass by older relatives to do the 'mano po'. It's also the default posture when you're scrolling through your phone in bed, or when you realize you've sent a risky text to the wrong person. A sign of respect, shame, or just plain bad posture.
usage_notes: Can denote respect, submission, sadness, or concentration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinaugalian na niyang **mag-uko** ng ulo kapag dumadaan sa harap ng simbahan.","translation":"He has made it a habit to **bow his head** when passing in front of the church."},{"sentence":"Nakitang **nag-uko** ng ulo ang bata habang pinapagalitan.","translation":"The child was seen **stooping** his head while being scolded."}]

meaning_filipino: Isa pang salitang balbal para sa isang lalaking homoseksuwal; isang mas maikli at karaniwang mas malambing na bersyon ng 'beki'.
etymology: Pinaikling anyo ng salitang balbal na 'beki'.
original_explanation: The shorter, cuter, and more casual version of 'beki'. It's what you call your gay best friend. "Uy, **beks**! Kamusta?" is the standard greeting. It’s the friendship-level term, like the difference between "friend" and "bes."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit bilang pantawag (vocative) sa isang kaibigan na beki.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, **beks**, manood tayo ng sine.","translation":"Let's go, **beks**, let's watch a movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tableta na gawa sa purong kinaskas na buto ng kakaw, karaniwang ginagamit sa paggawa ng mainit na tsokolate.
original_explanation: This is the OG hot chocolate, the stuff of a Tita's dreams and rainy day comfort. Forget Swiss Miss. This is pure, unadulterated, sometimes gritty, always amazing chocolatey goodness, usually made into 'tsokolate eh' (thick) or 'tsokolate ah' (thin). Perfect with pandesal or ensaymada.
usage_notes: Often spelled as 'tablea'. It's unsweetened, so you control the sugar level.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumawa si Lola ng mainit na tsokolate gamit ang **tabliya** mula sa Batangas.","translation":"Grandma made hot chocolate using **tablea** from Batangas."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang champorado kapag tunay na **tabliya** ang ginamit.","translation":"Chocolate rice porridge is more delicious when real **tablea** is used."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggisa o pagluluto ng mga sangkap sa kaunting mantika sa loob ng maikling panahon bago idagdag ang iba pang sahog o likido.
original_explanation: This is the first step of any Pinoy ulam. Before your kusina smells like heaven (or your neighbor's business), you have to **magsangkutsa** the holy trinity: bawang, sibuyas, kamatis. It's the 'opening prayer' of Filipino cooking.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a culinary context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **magsangkutsa** ng bawang at sibuyas para lumabas ang aroma.","translation":"Don't forget to **sauté** the garlic and onions to bring out the aroma."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magsangkutsa** muna ng manok bago ilagay ang sabaw.","translation":"You need to **sauté** the chicken first before adding the broth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng berdeng madahong gulay na karaniwang ginagamit sa mga ensalada at palamuti sa pagkain.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'lechugas,' pangmaramihang anyo ng 'lechuga.'
original_explanation: The green, leafy stuff that makes your samgyupsal or burger feel slightly healthier. It's the 'gulay' part of your 'extra rice' meal that you pretend to like for #fitness.
usage_notes: Minsan ay binabaybay na 'litsugas'. Ginagamit nang palitan sa salitang Ingles na 'lettuce'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-dagdagan ng **letsugas** ang aking burger.","translation":"Please add more **lettuce** to my burger."},{"sentence":"Sariwa ba ang mga **letsugas** na ito sa palengke?","translation":"Is this **lettuce** from the market fresh?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagkilos o pagsasalita na sinasadya o may layuning magdulot ng pagkainis o pagkayamot sa ibang tao.
original_explanation: When someone keeps poking you on Facebook even when you're 'Active 30m ago.' That's done in a **pa-inis** way. It’s the subtle art of being a low-key kontrabida in someone's daily life, like chewing loudly on a Zoom call or spoiling a series.
usage_notes: Often used to describe an action or a tone that is intentionally irritating. It describes how an action is performed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumagot siya nang **pa-inis** kaya lalo akong nagalit.","translation":"He answered in an **annoying manner**, which made me even angrier."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang ngumiti nang **pa-inis** habang ako'y nagseseryoso.","translation":"Don't smile in a **provokingly annoying way** while I'm being serious."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking ibong mandaragit, partikular ang Nisaetus philippensis o Philippine hawk-eagle.
etymology: Compound of "banog" (Visayan for hawk) and "lawin" (Tagalog for hawk/eagle).
original_explanation: This is the OG badass bird of the Philippine skies, not to be confused with the bigger, more famous Philippine Eagle (agila). Think of it as the highly skilled, agile fighter jet to the agila's heavy bomber. It's a portmanteau of "banog" (a Visayan term for hawk) and "lawin" (hawk/eagle).
usage_notes: Often used in literature and mythology to symbolize swiftness, sharp vision, and power.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **banoglawin** ang mabilis na dumagit sa ahas sa bukirin.","translation":"A **hawk-eagle** swiftly snatched the snake in the field."},{"sentence":"Ang mga mata niya ay sinlinaw ng sa **banoglawin**.","translation":"His eyes are as sharp as a **hawk-eagle's**."}]

translation: serving of food, setting the table
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aayos at paglalagay ng pagkain sa hapag-kainan upang pagsaluhan.
etymology: From 'hain' (to serve food). 'Pag-ha-hayin' is the noun for the act of serving.
original_explanation: This is what your mom yells before dinner: 'Maghain na!' It’s the process of taking the food from the kaldero and putting it into serving dishes, setting the table, and making everything look presentable before the family attacks the food. It's the final step before the 'kainan na!'
usage_notes: Specifically refers to preparing food on the dining table. The verb form 'maghain' is more commonly used in commands.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghahayin** ng Noche Buena ay isang masayang tradisyon ng pamilya.","translation":"The **serving** of the Noche Buena feast is a happy family tradition."},{"sentence":"Tulungan mo ako sa **paghahayin** ng hapunan.","translation":"Help me with the **setting of the table** for dinner."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsisimula ng isang paglalakbay o pag-alis mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng sasakyang pandagat o panlupa.
original_explanation: This is the official term for "umalis" when you're starting a long journey. "What time tumulak 'yung bus pa-Baguio?" It has a sense of setting sail or embarking on a trip. It’s what you say when your barkada is finally complete for the beach trip and the van starts moving.
usage_notes: Often used for scheduled trips, like buses, ships, or planes. Implies the beginning of a journey.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumulak** ang barko kaninang alas-sais ng umaga.","translation":"The ship **departed** at six o'clock this morning."},{"sentence":"Maaga kaming **tumulak** para iwasan ang trapik.","translation":"We **set off** early to avoid the traffic."}]

translation: to stink, to emit a foul odor
meaning_filipino: Maglabas ng mabaho o masangsang na amoy.
original_explanation: The reason you discreetly move away from someone on a crowded MRT. It’s what happens to the basurahan when you forget to take it out for three days. The ultimate 'eww' moment.
usage_notes: A very informal and somewhat crass word for smelling bad. 'Bumaho' is a more common and slightly more neutral equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umantot** ang buong kwarto dahil sa nabubulok na pagkain.","translation":"The whole room **stank** because of the rotting food."},{"sentence":"Hala, parang may **umantot** na daga sa ilalim ng lababo.","translation":"Oh no, it seems like a rat **stinks** under the sink."}]

translation: to route, to direct a path
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtakda o paggabay sa isang partikular na daanan o landas na dapat sundin ng isang tao, sasakyan, o bagay.
original_explanation: Before Waze and Google Maps, your parents would 'iruta' your trip. It's the act of telling the driver, 'Doon ka sa EDSA, tapos kanan sa Ayala, tapos diretso lang.' Nowadays, it's what your GPS does for you, except it can't scold you for missing a turn. 'Na-reroute ka na naman, bes!'
usage_notes: Commonly used in logistics, transportation, and travel planning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **iruta** nang maayos ang mga delivery truck para maiwasan ang trapik.","translation":"The delivery trucks need to be **routed** properly to avoid traffic."},{"sentence":"**Iruta** mo ang ating biyahe sa mga daan na hindi gaanong siksikan.","translation":"**Route** our trip through the less congested roads."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pabilog na espasyo sa isang salubungan ng mga kalsada kung saan ang trapiko ay umiikot sa isang direksyon sa palibot ng isang gitnang isla.
original_explanation: That giant circle in the middle of the road that confuses both new drivers and Waze. You're supposed to go around it, but everyone just cuts each other off. It's the ultimate test of your *diskarte* as a Filipino driver. Famous examples are the Welcome Rotonda in QC and that one in Tagaytay where you always get stuck in traffic.
usage_notes: A common term in Philippine geography and transportation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa may monumento sa gitna ng **rotonda**.","translation":"Let's meet at the monument in the middle of the **roundabout**."},{"sentence":"Dumaan ka sa **rotonda** at kunin mo ang pangatlong labasan.","translation":"Go through the **rotunda** and take the third exit."}]

translation: to enrich oneself; to become rich
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-iipon ng malaking kayamanan o pag-aari; gawing mayaman ang sarili.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal after getting your 13th month pay, but then Shopee and Lazada happen. It's the dream of every networking 'prospect' and the plot of many teleseryes involving a long-lost heir. "Join our team and learn how to magpayaman!"
usage_notes: This is an actor-focus verb. The object-focus counterpart is `payamanin` (to make someone/something rich).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsisikap siyang **magpayaman** sa pamamagitan ng pagtatayo ng sariling negosyo.","translation":"She is striving to **enrich herself** by starting her own business."},{"sentence":"Marami ang sumali sa investment scheme na nangakong tutulungan silang **magpayaman** nang mabilis.","translation":"Many joined the investment scheme that promised to help them **become rich** quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pagwawala o pagiging marahas ng isang tao nang walang malinaw na dahilan; tumutukoy din sa taong nasa ganitong kalagayan.
etymology: Spanish 'juramentado' (one who has taken an oath, specifically an oath to die fighting).
original_explanation: This is your office-mate after their 10th cup of coffee, 5th client escalation, and finding out na may a-attend pa silang meeting na "could have been an email." It's the final form of being "gigil." Historically, it referred to Moro warriors in a suicidal charge against invaders. Today, it's more like a "mental health day" waiting to happen.
usage_notes: This term has a specific historical context related to the Moro people, but its modern usage is generalized to mean anyone going berserk.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-**huramentado** ang lalaki sa palengke matapos siyang madukutan.","translation":"The man went **berserk** in the market after he was pickpocketed."},{"sentence":"Parang mag-**huhuramentado** na si boss sa dami ng trabaho.","translation":"It looks like the boss is about to go **amok** from the amount of work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng mga bisita o mga taong dumadalaw sa isang tahanan, pagdiriwang, o lugar.
original_explanation: This is the official trigger for the 'general cleaning' panic mode in a Filipino household. When you hear 'May darating, magkaka-panauhin tayo!', it means you have to hide all the kalat, bring out the good plates, and prepare more food than necessary. To `magkapanauhin` is to play the role of a host.
usage_notes: 'Panauhin' is the guest. 'Magkapanauhin' is the state of having a guest or guests.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging handa ang pamilya nila tuwing sila ay **magkapanauhin**.","translation":"Their family is always prepared whenever they **have guests**."},{"sentence":"Sa Pasko, tiyak na **magkapanauhin** tayo mula sa iba't ibang probinsya.","translation":"On Christmas, we will surely **have guests** from different provinces."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng inuming kape na gawa sa espresso at steamed milk, karaniwang may manipis na layer ng foam sa ibabaw.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "latte", na mula sa Italyanong "caffè latte" (kape na may gatas).
original_explanation: The go-to coffee order for people who want to say they drink coffee but don't actually want to taste too much of it. It's the "pwede na" of the coffee world – not too strong, not too sweet (before you add 5 pumps of syrup). The official drink of co-working spaces and "catching up" with friends.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang hiram na salita sa mga urban na lugar sa Pilipinas, lalo na sa mga kapihan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-order ako ng isang grande, non-fat, extra hot na **latte**.","translation":"Please order me a grande, non-fat, extra hot **latte**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mas mababa sa kalidad, ranggo, o halaga kumpara sa iba.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na nakita mo yung ex mo na may bago nang mas maganda/gwapo sa'yo, tapos feeling mo ang imperyor mo. O 'pag 'Made in China' yung nabili mong gamit tapos nasira agad, iisipin mo imperyor ang quality. It's the opposite of 'premium' or 'superior'.
usage_notes: Medyo pormal. Mas karaniwan ang 'mas mababa ang kalidad' sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong ituring na **imperyor** ang iyong sarili sa iba.","translation":"Do not consider yourself **inferior** to others."},{"sentence":"Marami ang naniniwala na **imperyor** ang kalidad ng mga produktong peke.","translation":"Many believe that the quality of fake products is **inferior**."}]

translation: to lower; to reduce the intensity of
meaning_filipino: Gawing mas mahina ang lakas, tunog, o antas ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The command you give your neighbor who's blasting karaoke at 2 AM on a Tuesday. It's the action of turning down the volume, the drama, or even your expectations for a
usage_notes: Often used as a command (imperative mood). Can refer to volume, speed, or intensity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hinaan** mo ang apoy para hindi masunog ang sinaing.","translation":"**Lower** the flame so the rice doesn't burn."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **hinaan** ninyo ang inyong mga boses sa loob ng silid-aklatan.","translation":"Please, **lower** your voices inside the library."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng magkakaibigan na madalas magkakasama at may malapit na ugnayan.
etymology: From Spanish 'barcada' (boatload), meaning people who traveled together on the same ship.
original_explanation: Your barkada is your ride-or-die crew, your squad, your chosen family. They're the ones you go on food trips with, the ones you message in the group chat at 2 AM, and the ones who will roast you but will fight anyone else who tries. It's not just a group of friends; it's a social institution.
usage_notes: A core concept in Filipino social life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta kami sa beach kasama ang buong **barkada**.","translation":"We're going to the beach with the whole **squad**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, tutulungan ka ng **barkada** mo.","translation":"Don't worry, your **group of friends** will help you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay sa wasto o kaaya-ayang kalagayan; pag-aareglo, pagkukumpuni, o pagpapaganda. Ito ang anyong pangnakaraan ng pandiwang "mag-ayos".
original_explanation: Two main meanings: 1) You fixed something broken, like when your Tito nag-ayos the WiFi for the 5th time this week. 2) You glammed up. "Wow, nag-ayos ka yata?" is the Pinoy way of saying "You look nice today, what's the occasion?" It's the opposite of the "pambahay" look.
usage_notes: Can refer to fixing an object, arranging things, settling a dispute, or grooming oneself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nag-ayos** siya ng kanyang sarili bago umalis para sa party.","translation":"She **fixed herself up** (groomed herself) before leaving for the party."},{"sentence":"Si Tatay ang **nag-ayos** ng sirang gripo sa kusina.","translation":"Dad was the one who **fixed** the broken faucet in the kitchen."}]

translation: to be swayed gently, to be rocked
meaning_filipino: Ang marahang paggalaw o pag-indayog nang pabalik-balik, tulad ng isang duyan o sanga ng puno na hinihipan ng hangin.
original_explanation: Imagine yourself on a hammock in La Union, with a cold drink in hand. That gentle rocking motion? That's it. It's the opposite of "yugyugin" which is more like an earthquake. This is chill, relaxed, 'pampatulog' vibes.
usage_notes: The reduplication `uguy-ugoy` emphasizes the gentle, repetitive, and often prolonged nature of the swaying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **pauguy-uguyin** ka ng duyan hanggang sa makatulog.","translation":"Let the hammock **rock you gently** until you fall asleep."},{"sentence":"Ang mga sanga ng niyog ay **pauguy-uguyin** ng amihan.","translation":"The coconut fronds are being **swayed gently** by the north wind."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging marami ang ginagawa, okupado, o walang libreng oras.
etymology: Same root as the noun, but used as a descriptor.
original_explanation: The default status of every working adult in Manila. It's what you say when you want to politely decline an invitation from your friend to a 'kain-tayo-libre-mo' session. 'Sorry, friend, abala ako sa work.'
usage_notes: Pronunciation is key: stress on the last syllable /a-ba-LA/ distinguishes it from the noun 'abala' (hassle).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi siyang **abala** sa kanyang trabaho kaya hindi na nakakauwi nang maaga.","translation":"She is always **busy** with her work so she can't come home early anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang laruan o sandata na may hugis Y na balangkas, may dalawang goma, at ginagamit sa pagpapahilagpos ng maliliit na bato o iba pang prohektil.
original_explanation: The original Pinoy childhood weapon of mass destruction (for fruits and cans). Bago nagkaroon ng ML at CoD, ito ang source of pride ng mga batang lalaki sa kalye. All you need is a Y-shaped branch, rubber from an old interior, and a steady hand. Si Dennis the Menace, Pinoy version.
usage_notes: Ang hulaping '-dor' ay nagsasaad ng gumagawa ng aksyon o instrumento, mula sa salitang-ugat na 'tira' (bumato/bumaril).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng bata ang kanyang **tirador** upang makuha ang mangga sa puno.","translation":"The child used his **slingshot** to get the mango from the tree."},{"sentence":"Pinagbawalan siyang magdala ng **tirador** sa paaralan.","translation":"He was forbidden to bring a **slingshot** to school."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at malakas na pagkuha o pagdaklot sa isang bagay, kadalasan ay biglaan at may puwersa.
original_explanation: What you do when there's only one piece of lechon skin left on the platter. It's also the action of a 'snatcher' on the street. Figuratively, it’s 'grabbing the opportunity' ('pagsunggab sa pagkakataon'). It's quick, decisive, and you better not hesitate.
usage_notes: Implies speed and force, more aggressive than `pagkuha` (act of getting).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis ang **pagsunggab** ng agila sa kanyang biktima.","translation":"The eagle's **snatching** of its prey was swift."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa mga mandurukot na naghihintay ng pagkakataon para sa **pagsunggab** ng gamit.","translation":"Be careful of snatchers waiting for an opportunity for the **snatching** of belongings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na larong pambata kung saan lumulukso ang isa o higit pang manlalaro sa ibabaw ng isang lubid na pinaiikot.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino cardio workout before fitness gyms were a thing. This is the classic street game where two people swing a rope and you jump in the middle, trying not to get tripped up. The chant 'Mother, mother, I am sick...' is its unofficial theme song.
usage_notes: Can refer to the game itself or the act of playing it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglaro kami ng **luksung-lubid** buong hapon sa kalye.","translation":"We played **jump rope** all afternoon on the street."},{"sentence":"Ang **luksung-lubid** ay isang magandang ehersisyo.","translation":"**Jumping rope** is a good exercise."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa hinaharap na panahunan ng pandiwang yakap; ang kilos ng pagyakap na isasagawa pa lamang.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of a hug. It's the promise of comfort. 'Wag ka nang malungkot, **yayakap**in kita.' (Don't be sad anymore, I will hug you). It’s also what you tell your dog or cat you'll do after a long day at work. The ultimate antidote to a stressful day, but in future-tense form.
usage_notes: This is the future tense, actor-focus form of the verb 'yakap'. The object-focus future tense is 'yayakapin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkauwi niya galing abroad, **yayakap** siya nang mahigpit sa kanyang mga anak.","translation":"When he comes home from abroad, he **will hug** his children tightly."},{"sentence":"Sino ang unang **yayakap** sa'yo sa iyong pagbabalik?","translation":"Who **will hug** you first upon your return?"}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi para sa publiko; pansarili o hindi pang-karaniwan.
original_explanation: This is your 'me time' setting. When you put your account on `pribado` mode, you're telling the world, 'Bawal ang chismosa.' It's the opposite of being a public figure; it's for your inner circle only, like a secret GC or a diary you hide from your mom.
usage_notes: Commonly used for places, information, or social media accounts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginanap ang kasal sa isang **pribado**ng resort sa Palawan.","translation":"The wedding was held at a **private** resort in Palawan."},{"sentence":"Naka-**pribado** ang Instagram account niya kaya hindi ko makita ang mga posts niya.","translation":"Her Instagram account is set to **private** so I can't see her posts."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining o gawain ng pananahi; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang babaeng mananahi (kosturera).
original_explanation: Before Zara and Shopee, there was the neighborhood 'kosturera'. She's the magical person who could turn a piece of 'tela' into your prom gown, fix your too-long pants, or patch up the hole in your favorite shirt. The original fashion designer for the masses.
usage_notes: When referring to the person, 'mananahi' is more common now, but 'kosturera' (feminine) or 'sastre' (masculine, for a tailor) is also used. 'Kostura' often refers to the craft itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay ang **kostura** ng damit na ito kaya matibay.","translation":"The **sewing** on this dress is excellent, that's why it's durable."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at paulit-ulit na paggagasgas o pagkiskis ng isang bagay sa ibabaw ng iba; maaari ring tumukoy sa mabilis na pagpapatakbo ng sasakyan.
etymology: Likely onomatopoeic, imitating the sound of scraping.
original_explanation: Two main meanings: 1) The sound and action of scraping something, like getting ice for halo-halo or using a 'pang-kaskas' for a coconut. 2) The act of a 'kaskasero' driver. That jeepney driver who treats EDSA like a race track? That's pure **kaskas**.
usage_notes: As a noun, it can refer to the act or the result (the scrape mark). The meaning of "speeding" is idiomatic and very common in the context of driving.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **kaskas** ng mga sanga sa aming bubong.","translation":"I heard the **scraping** of branches on our roof."},{"sentence":"Tigil na sa **kaskas** mo sa pagmamaneho, delikado iyan!","translation":"Stop your **speeding** when you drive, that's dangerous!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may sapat o higit pa sa sapat na yaman at ari-arian upang mamuhay nang maginhawa at walang kakapusan.
etymology: From `tao` (person) + `na` (that) + `nakaluluwag` (is able to make loose/spacious, i.e., comfortable) + `sa buhay` (in life).
original_explanation: This is your 'tita' who always travels abroad, or your friend who can afford to buy concert tickets without checking their bank account. They're not necessarily 'mayaman' in the crazy rich Asian sense, but they're definitely not struggling. They're living comfortably, the goal of every 'alipin ng salapi'.
usage_notes: A more polite and less direct way of saying someone is rich or well-to-do.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi na niya kailangang mag-alala sa pera dahil isa siyang **taong nakaluluwag sa buhay**.","translation":"She doesn't have to worry about money anymore because she is a **person who is well-off**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkawala ng talim ng isang bagay, o ang paghina ng isang kakayahan o talino.
original_explanation: Like that kutsilyo in the kitchen that can't even cut a tomato anymore. Or your brain after a whole day of back-to-back Zoom meetings. Your skills (and the knife) have pumurol.
usage_notes: This is the completed or past tense form of the verb. The infinitive is 'pumurol' and the present progressive is 'pumupurol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumurol** na ang lapis ko kaya kailangan kong tasahan.","translation":"My pencil **became dull** so I need to sharpen it."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **pumurol** ang iyong mga natutunan.","translation":"Don't let what you've learned **become dull**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, marka, o salita na kumakatawan, tumatayo, o nagpapahiwatig ng isang ideya, bagay, o relasyon.
original_explanation: The 'resibo' of a deeper meaning. Parang yung ♾️ na simbulo ng forever niyo (na nag-break din naman). Or the three stars and a sun sa flag, which is a simbulo of our nation. It's something that represents something else.
usage_notes: A more formal/loanword version. The native Tagalog equivalent is 'sagisag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kalapati ay isang **simbulo** ng kapayapaan.","translation":"The dove is a **symbol** of peace."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **simbulo** na ginamit ng makata sa kanyang tula?","translation":"What **symbol** did the poet use in his poem?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng malupit, marahas, o hindi makatarungang pagtrato sa isang tao o bagay; pagmamalabis sa kapangyarihan o awtoridad.
etymology: From the nominalizing prefix 'pag-a-' + 'abuso' (from Spanish 'abuso', meaning 'abuse').
original_explanation: This is a heavy one. It's when someone misuses their power, whether it's a boss overworking their staff (power-tripping), someone hurting a loved one, or even just taking advantage of the 'unli-rice' promo a little *too* seriously. It's crossing the line from use to misuse, often with harmful consequences.
usage_notes: The prefix 'pag-a-' turns the root word 'abuso' (abuse) into the act or process of abusing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinigil na niya ang **pag-aabuso** sa kanyang kalusugan sa pamamagitan ng pagtigil sa paninigarilyo.","translation":"He stopped the **abuse** of his health by quitting smoking."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-aabuso** sa kapangyarihan ay isang malubhang isyu sa lipunan.","translation":"The **abuse** of power is a serious societal issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matinding damdamin ng galit, pag-ayaw, o pagkamuhi sa isang tao o bagay.
etymology: Mula sa ugat na "poot" (galit, muhi). Ang unlaping "pagka-" ay nagbibigay-diin sa estado o damdamin ng pagkapoot.
original_explanation: 'Yung nararamdaman mo sa traydor mong ex, o sa taong umubos ng huling piraso ng lechon. That deep, simmering **pagkapoot** is a powerful emotion. It's the villain's origin story.
usage_notes: Isang napakatinding salita, mas matindi kaysa sa "galit".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkapoot** ay isang mabigat na pasanin sa dibdib.","translation":"**Hatred** is a heavy burden in the heart."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang alisin ang **pagkapoot** na nararamdaman niya para sa kanyang kaaway.","translation":"He tried to remove the **animosity** he felt for his enemy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling paglalakbay o pamamasyal na isinasagawa ng isang grupo, karaniwan para sa paglilibang, pag-aaral, o partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: This is the academic term for 'field trip'. Ito yung pinakahihintay mong event sa school kasi walang klase at makakasama mo ang barkada sa bus. Required ang parent's permit at baon na masarap. The OG 'travel goals' ng mga estudyante.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng paaralan o organisadong grupo. Ang "eskursyon" ay isang karaniwang alternatibong baybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming klase ay magkakaroon ng **eskursiyon** sa National Museum sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"Our class will have an **excursion** to the National Museum next month."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbawal muna ang mga **eskursiyon** sa paaralan dahil sa isyu ng kaligtasan.","translation":"School **field trips** were temporarily banned due to safety issues."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpalo sa mukha o ibang bahagi ng katawan gamit ang bukas na palad.
etymology: From sum- (actor-focus infix) + sampal (slap), with reduplication of the first syllable (sa-) to indicate progressive aspect.
original_explanation: The signature move of every teleserye kontrabida. It's the physical manifestation of "How dare you?!". It can also be used figuratively, like "parang sumasampal sa mukha ko ang katotohanan" (the truth is like slapping me in the face). It's the present tense of delivering a dramatic, open-palmed strike.
usage_notes: This is the progressive or present tense, indicating the ongoing action of slapping. It can be literal or metaphorical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pelikula, ang bidang babae ay laging **sumasampal** sa kontrabida.","translation":"In the movie, the female protagonist is always **slapping** the antagonist."},{"sentence":"Ang malakas na hangin ay tila **sumasampal** sa aming mga mukha.","translation":"The strong wind felt like it was **slapping** our faces."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging hindi tuwid; baluktot o kurbado.
original_explanation: Describes your spine after carrying the team in a group project. Or that picture frame you just can't seem to hang straight. 'Friend, liko 'yung eyeliner mo.'
usage_notes: Pronunciation differs from the noun. The stress is on the second syllable (/li-KO/) when used as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **liko** ang pako dahil sa tigas ng pader.","translation":"The nail became **bent** because of the hardness of the wall."},{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang pagkakabit, **liko** ang kurtina.","translation":"Fix how you hung it, the curtain is **crooked**."}]

translation: to shake off dust or dirt; (slang) to go somewhere after a wake
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis ng alikabok o dumi sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pag-uga o pagpalo nito. Sa kulturang popular, ito ay tumutukoy sa ritwal ng pagpunta sa ibang lugar pagkatapos dumalaw sa burol upang hindi "sumunod" ang kaluluwa.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `pagpag` (to shake off). The slang meaning is a cultural extension.
original_explanation: Literally, ito 'yung ginagawa mo sa basahan o carpet para matanggal ang alikabok. But culturally, ito 'yung "mandatory" stopover sa 7-Eleven or coffee shop after visiting a wake (burol). Sabi ng matatanda, para daw hindi ka sundan ng multo pauwi. So you **magpagpag** muna before going home. It's a superstitious detour.
usage_notes: The word has two very distinct meanings: a literal, everyday action and a deeply ingrained cultural/superstitious practice related to funerals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**pagpag** naman ng mga unan sa labas.","translation":"Please **shake off** the dust from the pillows outside."},{"sentence":"Galing kami sa burol, kaya kailangan nating **magpagpag** muna sa isang kainan.","translation":"We came from a wake, so we need to **make a stopover somewhere first** (to shake off spirits)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsusuri sa dalawa o higit pang bagay upang matukoy ang kanilang pagkakatulad at pagkakaiba.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your mom sees your cousin's grades. "Paghambingin mo nga ang grades niyo ni Kevin!" It's also what you do when choosing between two milk tea shops or two potential life partners. It's the art of 'this or that'.
usage_notes: The verb is in the imperative/infinitive form. "Hambingin" is the direct command, while "paghambingin" often refers to the general act of making a comparison.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paghambingin** mo ang dalawang larawan at sabihin kung ano ang kanilang pagkakaiba.","translation":"**Compare** the two pictures and tell what their differences are."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **paghambingin** ang pag-ibig sa pera.","translation":"It's difficult to **compare** love and money."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghahanda o ang kalagayan ng pagiging handa para sa isang partikular na layunin, gawain, o okasyon.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo bago ang exam, bago ang date, o bago ka harapin ni misis pag-uwi mong late. From cooking adobo to acing a job interview, the key is **preparasyon**. No **preparasyon**? Naku, bahala na si Batman.
usage_notes: Commonly used in both formal and informal contexts. Interchangeable with 'paghahanda'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naitutulong ng maagang **preparasyon** sa pagharap sa mga sakuna.","translation":"Early **preparation** is a great help in facing disasters."},{"sentence":"Kulang ka sa **preparasyon** kaya ka bumagsak sa test.","translation":"You lacked **preparation**, that's why you failed the test."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing sagana o marami ang isang bagay. Paramihin ang ani, biyaya, o anumang pinagkukunan.
original_explanation: This is your prayer to the universe when your startup is just getting started. You want to 'make it rain' blessings, clients, and revenue. It's the verb form of wanting that 'pasagana' lifestyle. "Lord, **pasaganain** Niyo po ang aming benta."
usage_notes: This is a command or a goal-oriented verb to increase something's quantity or abundance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **pasaganain** ang produksyon ng bigas sa ating bansa.","translation":"We must **make abundant** the production of rice in our country."},{"sentence":"Nanalangin siya na **pasaganain** ang biyaya sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He prayed to **make the blessings plentiful** for his family."}]

translation: to be bothered by one's conscience
meaning_filipino: Makararanas ng paninisi o pag-uusig mula sa sariling konsensya dahil sa isang maling nagawa o nasabi.
original_explanation: This is that feeling you get after you told your mom you were 'studying' but you were really out with friends. It's your inner Tito Boy Abunda asking 'Is it worth it?' while you're trying to sleep. You've been seen-zoned by your own conscience.
usage_notes: Implies a strong sense of guilt or moral conflict coming from within.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi siya makatulog sa gabi dahil **nabubudhian** siya sa kanyang ginawa.","translation":"He can't sleep at night because **he is bothered by his conscience** over what he did."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **mabudhian** ang mga politikong nangurakot sa kaban ng bayan.","translation":"Hopefully, the politicians who stole from the nation's coffers **will be bothered by their conscience**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghithit ng sigarilyo o tabako.
original_explanation: The old-school term for 'yosi break.' Before vaping was a thing, this was the go-to verb. You'd see your lolo sitting on the porch, mananabako, while contemplating the meaning of life or the price of rice. It's more formal-sounding than 'mag-yosi.'
usage_notes: A more formal or literary term for smoking. 'Manigarilyo' or 'mag-yosi' are more common in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na itigil na ang **manabako**.","translation":"The doctor advised him to stop **smoking tobacco**."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos kumain, ugali na niyang **manabako** sa labas ng bahay.","translation":"After eating, it's his habit to **smoke tobacco** outside the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang medikal na kondisyon kung saan ang lente ng mata ay nagiging malabo, na nagiging sanhi ng paglabo ng paningin.
original_explanation: This is a medical term, but in Pinoy culture, it's what every lolo and lola eventually complains about. 'Hindi na ako makabasa, anak, baka may katarata na ako.' It's the OG eye filter, but the kind you can't just turn off. Also used metaphorically for someone who is 'blind' to the truth, e.g., 'May katarata ka ba? Hindi mo ba nakikita na niloloko ka lang niya?'
usage_notes: Primarily a medical term, but can be used figuratively to mean 'blindness' to a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan operahan ang **katarata** sa mata ni lola.","translation":"The **cataract** in grandma's eye needs to be operated on."},{"sentence":"Ang maagang pagpapatingin sa doktor ay makatutulong upang maiwasan ang paglala ng **katarata**.","translation":"Early consultation with a doctor can help prevent the worsening of a **cataract**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong sobrang madaldal o masalita, madalas tungkol sa mga walang kwentang bagay.
original_explanation: Yung kaibigan mo na hindi nauubusan ng kwento, from their breakfast to their pet's dream. The human equivalent of a non-stop notification alert. 'Ang ingay mo, para kang yapper!' It’s the star of every 'yap session'.
usage_notes: A modern slang term borrowed directly from English, popular with younger generations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa grupo bilang ang pinakamalakas na **yapper**.","translation":"He is known in the group as the biggest **yapper**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampasabog na hugis-sigarilyo na naglalakbay sa ilalim ng tubig at idinisenyo upang sirain ang mga barko o submarino.
original_explanation: The underwater missile you see in submarine movies. It's the thing that goes 'ping' on the sonar before it goes 'BOOM' on the enemy ship.
usage_notes: The pronunciation follows the English word. The Spanish-derived spelling 'torpido' is also used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpakawala ng **torpedo** ang submarino.","translation":"The submarine launched a **torpedo**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lupain o taniman na puno ng mga puno ng niyog.
original_explanation: Imagine a sea of coconut trees stretching as far as the eye can see. That's a **niyugan**. It's the setting for many provincial horror stories, but also the source of our beloved buko juice and gata. It's the OG tropical paradise backdrop, minus the filter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malawak na **niyugan** ang kanilang pamilya sa probinsya ng Quezon.","translation":"Their family owns a vast **coconut plantation** in the province of Quezon."},{"sentence":"Nagtago ang mga bata sa **niyugan** habang naglalaro ng taguan.","translation":"The children hid in the **coconut grove** while playing hide-and-seek."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging padapa o ang akto ng pagbagsak na una ang mukha.
original_explanation: This is the most ungraceful way to fall. It's not a simple trip; it's a full-on, face-first dive onto the pavement. Imagine running to catch the jeep, tripping, and ending up *sungaba* on the ground. It's a mix of physical pain and epic-level hiya (embarrassment). 'Pasensya na, late ako, sumungaba ako sa hagdan.'
usage_notes: This is a root word. The actor-focus verb is 'sumungaba' (to fall face-first). The descriptive state is 'nakasungaba' (to be lying prone/face-down).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagmamadali, **sumungaba** siya sa putikan.","translation":"In so much hurry, he **fell flat on his face** in the mud."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko siyang **nakasungaba** sa sahig, lasing na lasing.","translation":"I saw him lying **prone** on the floor, very drunk."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na kulang sa praktikal na pag-iisip o pangunahing kakayahang humusga nang tama sa mga pang-araw-araw na sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Describes that person who brings a fork to a lugawan, or the one who asks "Gising ka pa?" when they see you online at 3 AM. They have book smarts, maybe, but zero street smarts. Common sense is not so common, apparently.
usage_notes: A loan phrase that is fully integrated into Tagalog. Often used as a mild insult or an expression of frustration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talaga namang **walang-sentido-komun** ang taong nagtapon ng basura sa harap ng sarili niyang bahay.","translation":"The person who threw trash in front of their own house truly has **no common sense**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **walang-sentido-komun**, isipin mo muna bago ka gumawa.","translation":"Don't be **without common sense**, think first before you act."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na kapasiyahan o desisyon na ginawa ng isang grupo. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa kalidad ng isang imahe o sa solusyon sa isang problema.
original_explanation: Your New Year's 'resolusyon' is to go to the gym... which you'll forget by February. It's also that formal document the barangay council passes to declare a new fiesta queen. And in the tech world, it's why your 1080p Netflix stream looks way better than that pirated camcorded movie from 2005. High-def drama!
usage_notes: A word with multiple meanings: a formal decision, a personal goal (like a New Year's resolution), or the clarity of an image/screen.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasa ng **resolusyon** ang konseho na nagbabawal sa paggamit ng plastik.","translation":"The council passed a **resolution** banning the use of plastic."},{"sentence":"Isa sa mga New Year's **resolusyon** ko ay ang mag-ipon ng pera.","translation":"One of my New Year's **resolutions** is to save money."},{"sentence":"Mataas ang **resolusyon** ng camera sa bagong telepono niya.","translation":"The camera on his new phone has a high **resolution**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakawala ng malalim na hininga bilang pagpapahayag ng kalungkutan, pagod, o pagkabigo ukol sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the physical manifestation of "sana all." You see your friend's travel pics and you just ipagbuntung-hininga your empty wallet. It's the "hay nako" sigh. It’s what you do when you see your electricity bill, when your crush posts a picture with their jowa, or when you remember you have work on a Monday. It's sighing *because* of something specific.
usage_notes: A descriptive and somewhat literary verb. It externalizes an internal feeling (like frustration, sadness, or relief) through a sigh, directed at a cause. The root is from the compound 'buntong-hininga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mo kailangang **ipagbuntung-hininga** ang mga problema; harapin mo ang mga ito.","translation":"You don't need to just **sigh over** your problems; face them."},{"sentence":"**Ipinagbuntung-hininga** na lang niya ang kanyang pagkabigo sa pagsusulit.","translation":"He just **sighed over** his failure in the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masidhi at maingay na pagtatalo o pag-aaway ng dalawa o higit pang tao dahil sa hindi pagkakasundo.
original_explanation: This isn't a simple "disagreement". This is a full-blown verbal war, the kind you see on teleseryes or between neighbors fighting over a parking spot. It's loud, it's intense, and everyone can hear it. Think of it as the sound effect for "Maritess mode: activated."
usage_notes: Implies a noisy, verbal conflict. It's a reciprocal verb, meaning it requires two or more participants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naririnig sa buong kapitbahayan ang mag-asawang **nagbabangayan** tuwing gabi.","translation":"The couple who **quarrel** every night can be heard throughout the neighborhood."},{"sentence":"Tigilan niyo na ang **pagbabangayan** dahil lang sa politika.","translation":"Stop your **heated arguing** just because of politics."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandama o persepsiyon sa tunog sa pamamagitan ng tainga; ang akto ng pagbibigay-pansin sa tunog.
original_explanation: The root word for listening. You won't hear "kinig" by itself, but you'll always hear its children: "Makinig ka!" (Listen!), "Nakikinig ako" (I'm listening), or "Pakinggan mo 'to" (Listen to this). It's what your mom yells when you're on your phone, what your boss expects in a meeting, and what you do when the latest chismis drops.
usage_notes: This is a root word and is almost always used with affixes like 'ma-', 'paki-', '-in', 'naki-', etc., to form verbs like 'makinig', 'pakinggan', and 'nakikinig'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Makinig** ka sa payo ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"**Listen** to your parents' advice."},{"sentence":"Wala siyang **pakikinig** sa sinasabi ko.","translation":"He has no **interest in listening** to what I'm saying."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng hadlang sa isang daanan o espasyo, na pumipigil sa paggalaw o tanaw.
original_explanation: This is when something gets in your way. Your view of the concert stage is naharangan by someone's 'Salamat Shopee' placard. The driveway is naharangan by a badly parked car. It's the state of having an obstacle placed in front of what you want to see or where you want to go. The focus is on the path/view, not the thing being blocked.
usage_notes: The object of this verb is the path or view that is being blocked, not the person or thing trying to pass. Compare with 'maharang' which focuses on the person/thing being intercepted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko makita ang palabas dahil **naharangan** ako ng matangkad na tao sa unahan.","translation":"I can't see the show because my view **is blocked** by a tall person in front."},{"sentence":"**Naharangan** ang daan dahil sa natumbang puno.","translation":"The road **was blocked** by a fallen tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang pangit o hindi kaaya-aya ang itsura.
etymology: Slang, likely a playful variation of 'chaka'.
original_explanation: The evil twin of 'chaka'. It's what your brutally honest friend says about your ex, or what you mutter under your breath when you see a bad outfit. 'Girl, ang cheka ng suot niya, promise!'
usage_notes: Part of Filipino gay lingo (swardspeak) that has entered mainstream slang. Used informally to describe people or things. Considered rude if used seriously.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka mukhang **cheka** sa damit na 'yan.","translation":"Don't worry, you don't look **ugly** in that dress."},{"sentence":"Ay, ang **cheka** ng pelikula! Sayang ang bayad.","translation":"Ugh, the movie was **terrible**! A waste of money."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang maging sanhi ng pagkaligaw o pagkalito ng isang tao sa direksyon o katotohanan.
original_explanation: Like following Waze into a dead-end alley. Or believing a "Get Rich Quick" scheme shared by your tita on Facebook. It's anything that promises one thing but leads you somewhere else entirely, leaving you confused and probably broke.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for getting lost geographically, or figuratively for being misled or deceived.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga maling karatula sa daan ay **nakapagliligaw** ng mga turista.","translation":"The wrong signs on the road are **misleading** to tourists."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa mga balitang **nakapagliligaw** sa social media.","translation":"Be careful of **deceptive** news on social media."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng paggawa ng isang bagay upang malaman kung ito ay magagawa, epektibo, o totoo. Ito rin ay tumutukoy sa pagbibigay ng pagsubok o hamon sa isang tao.
original_explanation: Ito yung status mo 'pag nag-apply ka sa work, 'pag nag-aaral ng bagong skill, o 'pag sinisikap mong mag-move on. "At least sumusubok ako!" ay ang battle cry ng mga hindi sumusuko. Pwede ring negative, like "Sino ka para sumubok sa pasensya ko?"
usage_notes: This is the present tense form. Past tense is 'sumubok'. Future tense is 'susubok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumusubok** akong matutong magluto ng adobo.","translation":"I am **trying** to learn how to cook adobo."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **subukin**, pagod ako.","translation":"Don't **test** me, I'm tired."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na itinalaga sa isang posisyon o tungkulin. Maaari ring mangahulugang tanyag, kilala, o bantog dahil sa isang partikular na katangian o gawain.
original_explanation: This is the official, legit, 'may paper trail' kind of status. It can mean someone was formally appointed to a position, like a 'nombrado' director in a government agency. It can also mean someone is so famous (or infamous) for something, they are 'nombrado' for it—like a 'nombradong magnanakaw' (renowned thief). It's got that old-school, slightly formal, Spanish-era vibe.
usage_notes: Has two main senses: 1) officially appointed, and 2) well-known or famous for a particular trait or skill, which can be positive or negative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang **nombrado** na abogado sa kanilang bayan.","translation":"He is a **renowned** lawyer in their town."},{"sentence":"Ang bagong **nombrado** na hepe ay nangakong tatapusin ang korapsyon.","translation":"The newly **appointed** chief promised to end corruption."}]

translation: taking turns; a system of turns
meaning_filipino: Isang sistema o paraan ng pagpapalitan o pagsasalitan sa paggawa ng isang bagay o pagtanggap ng isang benepisyo.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'turno' (turn) + hulaping Tagalog na '-han'.
original_explanation: Like a group chat deciding who pays for the next milk tea order. Or in a BPO, it's the shifting schedule. Everyone gets a chance, whether it's for a task, a reward, or a responsibility. The goal is fairness, but someone always feels they got the 'graveyard shift' of the deal.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng mga shift sa trabaho, laro, o mga pinaghahatiang responsibilidad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon kaming **turnohan** sa paghuhugas ng mga plato sa bahay.","translation":"We have a **system of taking turns** for washing the dishes at home."},{"sentence":"Paano ba ang **turnohan** ng mga guwardiya sa gabi?","translation":"What is the **rotation/shift system** for the guards at night?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang itinakdang kahihinatnan o kapalaran ng isang tao; ang suwerte o kamalasan sa buhay.
etymology: Metaphorical extension from 'palm' (of the hand), referencing the practice of palmistry (pagbasa ng palad) to tell one's fortune.
original_explanation: Your 'kapalaran'. The reason why you met your jowa on a random Tuesday, or why you keep getting the same toxic boss in every job. When things go wrong, you say 'Ganyan talaga ang palad ko.' When things go right, you say 'Salamat sa magandang palad!' It's the universe's script for your life's teleserye.
usage_notes: Used metaphorically to mean fortune or destiny. Often interchangeable with 'kapalaran'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iba-iba ang **palad** ng bawat tao.","translation":"Each person has a different **fate**."},{"sentence":"Nasa mga kamay natin ang pagbabago ng ating **palad**.","translation":"Changing our **destiny** is in our hands."}]

translation: to be caught by the morning; to have breakfast late
meaning_filipino: Abutan ng umaga habang ginagawa ang isang bagay; huli na para sa almusal, o kumain ng almusal sa hindi tamang oras.
original_explanation: Kapag nag-marathon ka ng K-drama, siguradong maaagahan ka sa panonood. Tapos paggising mo, tanghali na, so brunch na 'yun, hindi na breakfast. You were caught by the morning binge-watching.
usage_notes: Implies that an activity lasted all night and continued into the morning. Can also mean to be late for breakfast.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang dami ng trabaho, **naagahan** na ako sa opisina.","translation":"With so much work, I was **caught by the morning** at the office."},{"sentence":"Gising na, baka **maagahan** ka pa sa pagkain.","translation":"Wake up, you might **have your breakfast late**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aparatong optikal na nagpapalabas ng imahe (o mga gumagalaw na imahe) sa isang ibabaw, karaniwan ay isang puting screen o dingding.
original_explanation: Ito yung machine na ginagamit sa meeting room para makita ng lahat yung PowerPoint presentation mo. Kung malabo ang proyektor, malabo rin ang chance mong ma-promote. Charot. It's the lifeblood of classroom reports and corporate presentations.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga opisina, paaralan, at sinehan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakipatay ang ilaw para mas malinaw ang kuha sa **proyektor**.","translation":"Please turn off the lights so the image on the **projector** is clearer."},{"sentence":"Sira yata ang **proyektor**, ayaw gumana.","translation":"I think the **projector** is broken, it won't work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o resulta ng pagdurugtong ng dalawa o higit pang piraso ng tela, balat, o ibang materyales gamit ang sinulid at karayom. Tumutukoy din sa bawat isang dugtong na nalilikha.
original_explanation: 'Yan yung ginagawa sa damit mong butas o sa sugat mong naghiwalay. Parang relasyon, kailangan ng tahi para maging buo ulit. Pwedeng gawa ng nanay mo, ng sastre, o ng doktor. Pag pangit ang tahi, halata ang pinagdaanan.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa mismong gawain ng pananahi, sa resulta (isang dugtungan), o sa isang indibidwal na tusok ng karayom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malinis ang **tahi** ng damit na ito kaya mukhang mamahalin.","translation":"The **stitching** on this dress is clean so it looks expensive."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng ilang **tahi** ang sugat niya sa braso.","translation":"His arm wound needs a few **sutures**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain o proseso ng pagsasama-sama o pagbubuklod bilang isang entidad o grupo na may iisang layunin o damdamin.
etymology: From pakiki- (reciprocal action) + pag- (action noun) + isa (one).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "sana all" moment for a group. When your team finally clicks, or when everyone in the comments section agrees on something for once. It's the opposite of "divide and conquer"—it's "unite and win." Think People Power, or your barkada deciding on one place to eat without a 30-minute debate.
usage_notes: Carries a strong sense of unity, solidarity, and common purpose. Often used in social, political, or spiritual contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pakikipag-isa** ng mga mamamayan ay mahalaga sa pag-unlad ng bansa.","translation":"The **solidarity** of the citizens is important for the nation's progress."},{"sentence":"Nanawagan ang lider para sa **pakikipag-isa** ng lahat ng miyembro.","translation":"The leader called for the **unification** of all members."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng pag-aaral o bahagi ng isang kurso, lalo na sa distance learning, na naglalaman ng mga aralin at gawain.
original_explanation: The source of puyat for students (and parents) during the pandemic. Ito 'yung sandamakmak na papel na kailangan mong sagutan, na minsan mas mahirap pa intindihin kaysa sa ex mong 'di malaman kung ano'ng gusto. "Sagot mo, module ko" became the new "kopyahan."
usage_notes: Became an extremely common word in the Philippines due to the shift to modular distance learning during the COVID-19 pandemic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong tapusin ang lahat ng **module** ko bago ang Biyernes.","translation":"I need to finish all my **modules** before Friday."},{"sentence":"Tinutulungan ni nanay ang anak niya sa pagsagot ng **module**.","translation":"The mother is helping her child answer the **module**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na opisyal na tagapagpaganap ng isang lungsod, bayan, o munisipalidad.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na *mayor*, nangangahulugang "greater" o "older", na naging titulo para sa isang punong-bayan.
original_explanation: 'Yung boss ng isang city o munisipyo. Sila 'yung laging may tarpaulin 'pag may fiesta o graduation, bumabati sa lahat. Sila rin 'yung nag-aapruba ng mga proyekto at kung minsan, 'yung dahilan ng traffic dahil sa motorcade.
usage_notes: The term is used universally in the Philippines for the head of a local government unit (LGU) like a city or municipality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **mayor** ng aming lungsod ay nagbigay ng ayuda sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The **mayor** of our city gave aid to the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng permit mula sa opisina ng **mayor** para sa iyong negosyo.","translation":"You need a permit from the **mayor's** office for your business."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela o anumang katulad na materyal na ipinapatong sa ulo bilang panakip o palamuti.
original_explanation: The OG pashmina or scarf your lola wears to church. It can be a veil, a shawl, or any cloth you put on your head to protect you from the sun, to show reverence, or to hide a bad hair day when you bump into your crush at the mall.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa iba't ibang uri ng panakip sa ulo tulad ng belo, alampay, o bandana.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsuot ng puting **pandong** ang mga babae sa loob ng simbahan.","translation":"The women wore a white **head covering** inside the church."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang kanyang alampay bilang **pandong** para hindi masilaw sa araw.","translation":"She used her shawl as a **head covering** to avoid the glare of the sun."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para sa isang bagay o gawi na may kaugnayan sa kulturang "Jejemon," na kilala sa kakaibang paraan ng pagtetext at pananamit noong huling bahagi ng dekada 2000.
etymology: Nagmula sa "hehe," isang karaniwang paraan ng pagtawa online, na inistilo bilang "jeje" sa text.
original_explanation: The OG "cringe." Before "aesthetic," there was "jeje." It's that specific brand of early 2000s Pinoy internet culture: typing "3ow ph0wzz," wearing oversized caps sideways, and having multi-colored hair. It's a vibe, a historical artifact of the Friendster era.
usage_notes: Often used humorously or nostalgically. Can be slightly derogatory depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko yung mga lumang picture ko, ang **jeje** ng pormahan ko dati!","translation":"I saw my old pictures, my style back then was so **jeje**!"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong i-type nang **jeje**, hindi ko maintindihan.","translation":"Don't type in **jeje**-speak, I can't understand it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagwawaldas o maling paggamit ng ipinagkatiwalang pera o ari-arian para sa pansariling kapakanan.
original_explanation: This is the 'biglang yaman' story with a dark twist. When the condo association treasurer suddenly has a new car and goes on a European tour, you might suspect some pagkalustay of funds. It's spending money that isn't yours, often with disastrous, headline-worthy results.
usage_notes: A legal and financial term referring to the misappropriation of funds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahaharap siya sa kasong **pagkalustay** ng pondo ng kumpanya.","translation":"He is facing charges for the **embezzlement** of company funds."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mahinang tunog ng mabilis ngunit hindi malakas na agos ng tubig, gaya ng sa isang batis o sapa.
original_explanation: This is the ASMR of the province. It's the sound your Lolo's farm's irrigation canal makes, or the gentle stream you cross during a hike. It’s nature’s white noise machine, perfect for lulling you to sleep or making you want to pee.
usage_notes: Purely an auditory noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tanging maririnig mo sa gubat ay ang **sagawsaw** ng tubig sa batis.","translation":"The only thing you could hear in the forest was the **babbling** of water in the stream."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalubhaan, katindihan, o pagiging seryoso ng isang bagay o sitwasyon. Tumutukoy din sa puwersang humihila sa mga bagay patungo sa sentro ng daigdig.
original_explanation: This is the formal, "nasa korte ka" version of 'grabe'. You use grabedad when the situation is no longer just 'grabe traffic,' but 'grabe, may international crisis.' It's the word you pull out when you need to sound serious and educated, like in a thesis defense or when explaining to your parents why you failed a subject. It has weight, just like the scientific concept it's named after.
usage_notes: A more formal word for "seriousness" or "severity." Less common in casual conversation compared to "grabe" or "kalubhaan."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi pa nila lubos na nauunawaan ang **grabedad** ng kanilang mga pagkakamali.","translation":"They still don't fully understand the **severity** of their mistakes."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **grabedad**, ang lahat ng bagay ay nahuhulog pababa.","translation":"Because of **gravity**, all things fall down."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang seremonyang panrelihiyon at sakramento sa Simbahang Katoliko kung saan ginugunita ang pag-aalay ni Kristo sa krus. Ito ang sentral na gawain ng pagsamba.
original_explanation: It's the Sunday obligation for your lola. It's that one hour where you have to sit still, try not to fall asleep during the homily, and remember the right responses. Also the prime time to see your crush from the other barangay and check out everyone's "Sunday's best" OOTD.
usage_notes: Madalas na isinusulat na may malaking titik. Ang salita ay maaaring isama sa iba upang tukuyin ang uri ng Misa (hal., Misa de Gallo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magsisimula ang **Misa** sa ganap na ika-siyam ng umaga.","translation":"The **Mass** will start at exactly nine in the morning."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay habang may **Misa**.","translation":"Don't be noisy during the **Mass**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa, o nagtataglay ng, asido na matatagpuan sa mga prutas tulad ng limon at dalandan.
original_explanation: Ito yung asim-kilig factor ng mga prutas like calamansi, lemon, at orange. 'Yung "citric acid" na nakasulat sa ingredients ng C2 o Nestea Iced Tea? 'Yun 'yun. Siya ang dahilan kung bakit napapapikit ka sa asim.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit bilang "asidong sitriko" (citric acid).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga prutas na **sitriko** ay mayaman sa Bitamina C.","translation":"**Citric** fruits are rich in Vitamin C."}]

meaning_filipino: (Balbal) Isang babaeng tanyag o kinikilala bilang pangunahing halimbawa ng kulturang "kanal," na walang takot na ipinapakita ang kanyang pagiging prangka at hindi pino.
etymology: Combination of Tagalog 'kanal' (gutter, low-brow) and English 'queen'.
original_explanation: She's the icon who proves that being 'kanal' isn't just for the boys. She's loud, she's proud, and her humor can make a sailor blush. She's the one who'll order isaw with extra rice while wearing heels. An unbothered, unapologetic queen of the people.
usage_notes: A title, often bestowed ironically or as a term of endearment, celebrating a woman's unapologetic and down-to-earth persona.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang tunay na **Kanal Queen**; walang arte sa katawan.","translation":"She's the real **Kanal Queen**; she has no pretentions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang huling bahagi o wakas ng isang bagay, gawain, o yugto. Tumutukoy rin ito sa seremonya ng pagkumpleto ng isang antas ng pag-aaral.
original_explanation: The end of an era. Pwedeng a sad ending sa K-drama, the end of your free trial on Netflix, or the most awaited moment for every student: graduation! It's the finish line, the final chapter, the 'salamat, next' moment. Time to throw your toga cap in the air!
usage_notes: Pagtatapos is commonly used to mean 'graduation' in academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malapit na ang **pagtatapos** ng pelikula.","translation":"The movie's **ending** is near."},{"sentence":"Inaabangan ng lahat ang araw ng kanilang **pagtatapos** sa kolehiyo.","translation":"Everyone is looking forward to their college **graduation** day."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtayo o pagtaas ng mga balahibo ng hayop o buhok ng tao, karaniwan dahil sa takot, galit, o lamig.
etymology: From pa- + mam- (from ma- + balukag) + balukag. The root 'balukag' means 'bristle'.
original_explanation: This is your body's reaction when you get the creeps. When you feel a sudden chill or hear a scary story and the hair on your arms stands up? That's pamamalukag. It's the same thing a cat does when it gets scared, making itself look bigger. For humans, it's our built-in 'nope' sensor activating. It's basically the physical form of 'kilabot'.
usage_notes: Closely related to 'paninindig ng balahibo' (hair standing on end).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **pamamalukag** ng aking mga balahibo nang may bumulong sa dilim.","translation":"I felt my hair **bristling** when someone whispered in the dark."},{"sentence":"Makikita ang **pamamalukag** ng balahibo ng pusa kapag ito'y nagagalit.","translation":"You can see the cat's fur **bristling** when it's angry."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis o paglaya mula sa isang mapanganib, hindi kanais-nais, o nakakulong na sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The great escape! This is what you do from your responsibilities on a Friday night. It's the feeling of logging off after a long day of WFH. It's also what happens in every action movie when the hero breaks out of jail. That's a **pagtakas**.
usage_notes: Can be literal (escaping from prison) or figurative (escaping from problems).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagtakas** mula sa bilangguan ay laman ng mga balita.","translation":"His **escape** from prison was all over the news."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nasa kabilang dako, karaniwang sa kabilang panig ng dagat; maaari ring mangahulugang higit pa, mas malaki, o karagdagan.
original_explanation: This is a fancy word you use when you want to sound smart. Instead of saying 'more effort,' you say '**ibayong** pagsisikap.' It's like adding 'extra' or 'next-level' to something. '**Ibayong** dagat' is the classic term for 'overseas,' where your OFW relatives are.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like news reports or speeches. 'Ibayong-dagat' is a common compound word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakailangan ang **ibayong** pag-iingat sa pagmamaneho kapag umuulan.","translation":"**Greater** caution is needed when driving while it's raining."},{"sentence":"Marami siyang kamag-anak sa **ibayong** dagat.","translation":"He has many relatives **overseas**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na tawag sa isang kaibigang lalaki; isang ekspresyon ng pagkadismaya, pagtataka, o pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: The universal sound of millennial and Gen Z disappointment, disbelief, or casual greeting. It's a whole conversation in one syllable. Can mean "Hey," "Dude, seriously?", "I can't believe you just did that," or "That's crazy." If you have to ask what bruh means, you're probably a tito. Bruh.
usage_notes: Highly context-dependent. The tone of voice is crucial to its meaning. Can be used as a pronoun ('Hey bruh') or an interjection ('Bruh... really?').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bruh**... seryoso ka ba diyan?","translation":"**Bruh**... are you serious about that?"},{"sentence":"Uy **bruh**, kamusta?","translation":"Hey **bruh**, how are you?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bituin sa gitna ng sistemang solar na nagbibigay ng liwanag at init sa mundo. Tumutukoy rin ito sa isang yugto ng panahon na katumbas ng 24 na oras.
original_explanation: The ultimate source of life and, for us Pinoys, the reason we need umbrellas even when it's not raining. It dictates whether it's a good day to do laundry ('maaraw'). It's also how we measure our lives, from 'kaarawan' (birthday) to 'araw-araw' (everyday hustle). It can be your best friend (beach day!) or your worst enemy (traffic at noon).
usage_notes: The dual meaning of 'sun' and 'day' is very common. Context, such as time of day or accompanying words ('buong araw' - whole day, 'sikat ng araw' - sun's rays), makes the meaning clear.
