usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasikat ng **araw** kaninang tanghali.","translation":"The **sun** was so bright this noon."},{"sentence":"Anong **araw** ang kaarawan mo?","translation":"What **day** is your birthday?"},{"sentence":"Pitong **araw** sa isang linggo.","translation":"Seven **days** in a week."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa tradisyong Kristiyano, ang huling linggo ng Kuwaresma at ang linggo bago ang Pasko ng Pagkabuhay, kung kailan ginugunita ang pasyon, pagkamatay, at muling pagkabuhay ni Hesukristo.
original_explanation: The one week a year when most of Manila empties out and heads to the beach or the province. For the devout, it's a time for Visita Iglesia, Pabasa, and processions. For many others, it's the first long vacation of the year. The TV stations stop showing noontime shows and play 'The Ten Commandments' on a loop. Traffic disappears, but good luck finding an open convenience store on Good Friday.
usage_notes: Refers to the Holy Week in the Christian tradition, a major holiday and cultural event in the Philippines. Also known as 'Mahal na Araw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang umuuwi sa probinsya tuwing **Semana Santa**.","translation":"Many families go home to their provinces during **Holy Week**."},{"sentence":"Ang **Semana Santa** ay panahon ng pagninilay-nilay para sa mga Katoliko.","translation":"**Holy Week** is a time of reflection for Catholics."}]

translation: to stop intermittently; to keep stopping
meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit o madalas na paghinto sa isang gawain, paggalaw, o paglalakbay.
original_explanation: That moment in EDSA traffic when you move two inches then stop for five minutes. Repeat until your clutch leg cries for mercy. It's the 'start-stop' relationship you have with your diet every weekend.
usage_notes: The reduplication 'tigil-tigil' implies an intermittent, repeated, or hesitant action, as opposed to a single, decisive stop ('tumigil').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpatigil-tigil** sa pag-aaral kung gusto mong makapasa.","translation":"Don't **keep stopping** your studies if you want to pass."},{"sentence":"Ang sasakyan ay **nagpatigil-tigil** dahil sa matinding trapiko.","translation":"The car **kept stopping** because of the heavy traffic."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng duyan o upuang nakabitin na ginagamit upang mag-ugoy, lalo na para sa pagpapatulog ng sanggol.
original_explanation: The OG baby rocker. Before Fisher-Price, there was the 'indayon'. It's a cradle or hammock, usually made of rattan or cloth, na iniuugoy para patulugin si baby. Parang 'yung pag-ugoy-ugoy ng feelings mo sa kanya, 'di mo alam kung saan papunta.
usage_notes: This is a more traditional and less common word than 'duyan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahimbing ang tulog ng sanggol sa kanyang **indayon**.","translation":"The baby is sleeping soundly in his **cradle**."},{"sentence":"Gumawa ng **indayon** na yari sa yantok ang lolo.","translation":"Grandfather made a **swing** made of rattan."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagsali o pakikibahagi sa isang gawain, paligsahan, o kaganapan.
original_explanation: When the group chat is planning an "outing" but you're broke, so you just "seen" the message. It's the official status of anyone who chooses to stay home and watch Netflix instead of joining the team building. "Absent." "No-show."
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense) of the verb. The infinitive is 'di-lumahok' or 'hindi lumahok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami ang **di-lumahok** sa halalan dahil sa takot sa virus.","translation":"Many **did not participate** in the election for fear of the virus."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **di-lumahok** sa laro dahil masama ang kanyang pakiramdam.","translation":"He **did not participate** in the game because he was not feeling well."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking isda na karaniwang may kulay-rosas o pulang laman, kilala sa paglangoy pabalik sa mga ilog kung saan sila ipinanganak upang mangitlog.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "salmon", isang salitang-hiram.
original_explanation: The "sosyal" na isda. If tilapia is for everyday ulam, salmon is for special occasions, date nights, or when you get your 13th-month pay. It's the fish that's rich in Omega-3, which supposedly makes you smarter. It’s also a color—that fancy pinkish-orange shade you see in bridesmaid dresses.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isda at sa kulay. Ang pagbigkas ay karaniwang sunod sa Ingles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal ang kilo ng sariwang **salmon** sa palengke.","translation":"A kilo of fresh **salmon** is expensive at the market."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang pagkain ay inihaw na **salmon** na may kasamang asparagus.","translation":"Her favorite food is grilled **salmon** with asparagus."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at marahas na paggalaw ng katawan na hindi makontrol, sanhi ng hindi-sinasadyang pag-urong ng mga kalamnan.
original_explanation: Medically, it's a serious seizure. But in everyday Pinoy drama, it's how you describe someone having an extreme reaction. "Nung nalaman niyang may iba na si ex, parang kinukumbulsyon sa kakaiyak." It's a physical manifestation of an emotional breakdown.
usage_notes: Used both in a medical sense and hyperbolically for strong emotional reactions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala sa ospital ang bata matapos itong magkaroon ng **kombulsyon** dahil sa taas ng lagnat.","translation":"The child was brought to the hospital after having a **convulsion** due to high fever."}]

meaning_filipino: Pambihirang tapang, lakas ng loob, o kabayanihan, lalo na sa harap ng panganib.
original_explanation: This is a superhero-level word. It's not just regular 'tapang' (bravery). **Giting** is the courage of Jose Rizal, the valor of our frontliners during the pandemic, the gallantry of an OFW working abroad for their family. It's bravery with a purpose, with a sense of nobility. It's what we celebrate on Araw ng Kagitingan (Day of Valor).
usage_notes: Isang pormal at makatang salita na ginagamit upang ilarawan ang kabayanihan at tapang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinamalas ng mga sundalo ang kanilang **giting** sa larangan ng digmaan.","translation":"The soldiers showed their **valor** on the battlefield."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na kasunod ng tatlo at sinusundan ng lima; katumbas ng apat (4).
original_explanation: The number 4. From the Spanish 'cuatro'. Often used when telling time ('alas kuwatro' - 4 o'clock) or when you're playing cards. Also, in old-school grading systems, a 'cuatro' was a failing grade. 'Naka-kuwatro ka na naman sa math!'
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with the native Tagalog term 'apat'. Spanish-derived numbers are common in specific contexts like time, age, money, and counting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Alas **kuwatro** na ng hapon, kailangan ko nang umuwi.","translation":"It's already **four** in the afternoon, I need to go home."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng **kuwatro** na pirasong pandesal.","translation":"Give me **four** pieces of pandesal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pambansang sining pandigma at palakasan ng Pilipinas, na gumagamit ng mga patpat, talim, at kamay. Kilala rin bilang Eskrima o Kali.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "arnés" (harness/armor), dahil ang mga maagang anyo nito ay ginamit sa mga dula-dulaan (moro-moro) kung saan ang mga aktor ay nakasuot ng baluti.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung PE class mo na may dalang dalawang yantok (rattan sticks). The OG Filipino martial art. Akala mo naglalaro lang ng patpat, pero 'pag tinamaan ka, may 'aray' factor. It's our national sport, a dance of sticks that can seriously mess someone up.
usage_notes: Itinalaga bilang pambansang palakasan at sining pandigma ng Pilipinas sa ilalim ng Republic Act No. 9850.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling si Danilo sa **arnis** dahil bata pa lang ay tinuruan na siya ng kanyang lolo.","translation":"Danilo is good at **arnis** because his grandfather taught him since he was young."},{"sentence":"Ang **arnis** ay bahagi na ng kurikulum sa edukasyong pisikal sa mga paaralan.","translation":"**Arnis** is now part of the physical education curriculum in schools."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na pamayanan o komunidad, karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga pook-rural o lalawigan, na mas maliit kaysa sa isang bayan.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *nayun na nangangahulugang 'magkasama, sa pangkalahatan'.
original_explanation: Think "probinsya" vibes. 'Yung lugar kung saan mas kilala mo pa 'yung mga manok ng kapitbahay mo kaysa sa mga tao sa kabilang kanto sa Maynila. It's the countryside, the barrio, where life is simpler and the air is fresher. The setting of every Fernando Poe Jr. movie.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'baryo', ngunit ang 'nayon' ay maaaring magkaroon ng mas makata o tradisyonal na dating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming sariwang prutas at gulay sa aming **nayon**.","translation":"There are many fresh fruits and vegetables in our **village**."},{"sentence":"Simple lang ang pamumuhay sa isang maliit na **nayon**.","translation":"Life in a small **countryside** is simple."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alagad ng sining na lumilikha ng mga anyong tatlong-dimensyonal sa pamamagitan ng pag-ukit o paghubog sa mga materyales tulad ng kahoy, bato, o metal.
original_explanation: The artist who can turn a boring block of wood or a chunk of stone into something beautiful, like a saint for the local fiesta or an abstract piece for a museum. They're the OG 3D printers, using chisels and mallets instead of plastic filament. Think of the masters who carved the Ifugao rice terraces (figuratively) or the statues in Paete, Laguna.
usage_notes: A specific term for a sculptor, an artist who carves.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang tanyag na **manlilok** ang gumawa ng monumentong iyon.","translation":"A famous **sculptor** made that monument."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **manlilok** ng Paete ay kilala sa kanilang galing sa pag-ukit sa kahoy.","translation":"The **sculptors** of Paete are known for their skill in wood carving."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamalayong bahagi o dulo ng isang bagay; ang hangganan o katapusan.
original_explanation: This is the 'end of the line'. The last bus stop. The final episode of your favorite K-drama. It's as far as you can go before you either have to turn back or fall off. Sa relasyon, ito yung 'Dito na lang tayo.' Ouch.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical end ('kadulu-duluhan') or a conceptual/temporal end.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakarating sila sa **kaduluhan** ng isla bago lumubog ang araw.","translation":"They reached the **farthest end** of the island before the sun set."},{"sentence":"Sana'y hindi humantong sa **kaduluhan** ng ating pagkakaibigan ang problemang ito.","translation":"I hope this problem doesn't lead to the **end** of our friendship."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matinding paghanga, paggalang, o pagsamba na ipinapakita sa isang tao, lalo na sa isang nililigawan o isang taong itinuturing na dakila.
original_explanation: This is next-level admiration. Hindi lang 'to crush. This is 'I will write you poems and sing you harana' level of simping. It's the kind of adoration you give to your ultimate bias in a K-Pop group or the way lolo looked at lola back in the day. Pure, intense, almost worshipful admiration.
usage_notes: A very deep and somewhat archaic word. Not used in everyday conversation, but common in literature, poetry, and formal declarations of love.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga tula ay puno ng **pintuho** para sa kanyang minamahal.","translation":"His poems are full of **adoration** for his beloved."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **pintuho** sa dalaga sa pamamagitan ng pag-aalay ng mga bulaklak.","translation":"He showed his **great admiration** for the young woman by offering flowers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtugis o paghahangad na maabutan ang isang tao, bagay, o layunin.
original_explanation: The frantic rush to meet a deadline. The feeling of running after the last jeep at night. The hugot version: 'May **habol** pa ba ako sa puso niya?' (Am I still in the running for their heart?). It's the pursuit, the chase, the hustle.
usage_notes: Refers to the chase or pursuit itself. The action is 'humabol' (to chase) or 'habulin' (to chase someone/something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigil na ang **habol**! Sumusuko na ako.","translation":"Stop the **chase**! I surrender."},{"sentence":"May **habol** siyang deadline kaya hindi siya makakasama.","translation":"He is chasing a deadline so he can't join us."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng paanyaya o imbitasyon sa isang tao upang dumalo sa isang pagtitipon, lugar, o gawain.
original_explanation: Ito yung verb form ng "Tara!" o "Sama ka?" Yung ginagawa mo sa group chat para magkayayaan kumain sa labas. "Bes, anyayahan mo na si crush sa party, now or never!"
usage_notes: Mas pormal ito kaysa sa 'imbita' o 'yaya'. Ang 'anyayahan' ay may pokus sa taong iniimbitahan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano kong **anyayahan** ang lahat ng aking kaibigan sa aking kaarawan.","translation":"I plan **to invite** all my friends to my birthday."},{"sentence":"**Inanyayahan** niya ako na manood ng sine.","translation":"He/She **invited** me to watch a movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Mailagyan o malagyan ng isang bagay na isinasaboy o ikinakalat nang paunti-unti sa ibabaw nito.
original_explanation: Like when your crush finally notices you and you get sprinkled with a little bit of kilig. Or more literally, when you ask for extra cheese powder on your fries and the food crew goes to town. 'Sige, kuya, mabudburan mo na ng pag-asa ang puso ko.'
usage_notes: This is a potential verb, often used to express the possibility or action of something being sprinkled onto a surface.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **mabudburan** ng keso ang aking spaghetti.","translation":"I want my spaghetti **to be sprinkled** with cheese."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mong huwag **mabudburan** ng alikabok ang mga bagong labang damit.","translation":"Be careful not to get the newly washed clothes **sprinkled** with dust."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na ginagamit upang magdagdag ng ganda o palamuti sa isang lugar, bagay, o pagkain.
etymology: From 'pang-' (instrumental prefix) + 'palamuti' (decoration). The word 'palamuti' itself comes from 'pa-' + the archaic root 'lamuti'.
original_explanation: The Christmas lights your dad insists on putting up in September. The sprinkles on a cake. The throw pillows on the sofa that you're not actually allowed to use. Anything that's there to make things look pretty but often has no practical function. Also known as 'gastos.'
usage_notes: While 'palamuti' is the decoration itself, 'pampalamuti' is the *thing used for decorating*. In practice, they are often used interchangeably.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng mga parol at iba pang **pampalamuti** para sa Pasko.","translation":"We bought lanterns and other **decorations** for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Ang mga hiniwang gulay ay nagsilbing **pampalamuti** sa ulam.","translation":"The sliced vegetables served as a **garnish** for the dish."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang modelo, huwaran, o padron na siyang batayan sa paggawa o pagkopya ng isang bagay.
etymology: From 'gaya' (to imitate) + '-han' suffix, creating a noun that means 'place/thing for imitation'.
original_explanation: This is the master copy, the OG file, the 'template' before Canva existed. The sewing pattern your lola uses, the answer key your classmate is hiding, the 'peg' for your new haircut—lahat 'yan gayahan.
usage_notes: Distinct from 'gayahin' (the verb 'to copy'). 'Gayahan' is the thing being copied from.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha ng mananahi ang **gayahan** para sa bestida.","translation":"The seamstress took the **pattern** for the dress."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang sulat-kamay ay napakaganda kaya ginawa kong **gayahan**.","translation":"Her handwriting is so beautiful that I made it my **model** to copy."}]

translation: to stay permanently; to reside always
meaning_filipino: Manatili o tumira sa isang lugar sa mahabang panahon o nang permanente.
etymology: From `pa-` + `malagi` (to be always present) + `-an`. The root is `lagi` (always).
original_explanation: The opposite of "ghosting." This is when someone decides to stay for good. "Nag-Japan for 3 months, pero sa Pinas pa rin piniling pamalagian." It's putting down roots. It's choosing your forever home, or in a hugot sense, choosing that person you want to 'pamalagian' with.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat poetic word. 'Manatili' or 'tumira' are more common for everyday use.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinili ng pamilya na **pamalagian** ang probinsya kaysa sa magulong siyudad.","translation":"The family chose to **reside permanently** in the province rather than in the chaotic city."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pagmamahal ang nais kong **pamalagian** sa aking puso.","translation":"Your love is what I want to **always keep** in my heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpunta sa isang tao o lugar upang makipagkita, kumustahin, o manatili nang panandalian. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagdating ng isang bagay na hindi inaasahan, tulad ng antok o sakit.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'dalaw' (visit) at hulaping pandiwa na '-in' (object-focus).
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'visit'. It's what you do when your lola says 'di mo na ako dinadalaw!' It's also what you hope your crush would do. But on the flip side, it can also mean being 'visited' by something else, like when you're in a boring meeting and you're suddenly 'dinalaw ng antok' (visited by sleepiness).
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang nakapokus sa layon (object-focus). Ang paksa ng pangungusap ay ang dinadalaw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano naming **dalawin** ang aming mga lolo at lola sa Pasko.","translation":"We plan **to visit** our grandparents on Christmas."},{"sentence":"Habang nag-aaral, madalas akong **dalawin** ng antok.","translation":"While studying, I am often **visited by** sleepiness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ayos o paraan ng pagtayo o pag-upo ng isang tao; ang pangkalahatang tindig o hitsura.
original_explanation: Your porma, your tindig, your "how you carry yourself." Ito 'yung sabi ng lola mo na "Ayusin mo 'yang pag-upo mo, dalaga ka pa naman!" o 'yung paglakad mo na parang may-ari ka ng mall kahit window shopping ka lang. Good posture can make you look 10 lbs lighter and 100% more confident.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa pangkalahatang anyo o porma ng isang tao, hindi lamang sa tindig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda ang **postura** ng mga sundalo kapag nagmamartsa.","translation":"The soldiers have good **posture** when they march."},{"sentence":"Inaayos niya ang kanyang **postura** sa harap ng salamin bago ang kanyang job interview.","translation":"She is fixing her **posture** in front of the mirror before her job interview."}]

translation: to roll one's eyes; to glare with
meaning_filipino: Gamitin ang mga mata upang magpakita ng matalim na tingin bilang pagpapahayag ng galit o pagkayamot.
original_explanation: While `irapan` is "to glare *at someone*", `i-irap` is about the action itself, focusing on the eyes as the instrument. "Wala akong masabi, kaya inirap ko na lang ang mga mata ko." It's the physical action of weaponizing your eyeballs.
usage_notes: This form is less common than `irapan` or `umirap`, but is grammatically correct. It focuses on the eyes as the "instrument" for glaring, as in 'iirap ang mga mata'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **iirap** sa akin ang mga mata mo, bata ka!","translation":"Don't you **roll** your eyes **at** me, you child!"},{"sentence":"**Inirap** niya ang kanyang mga mata at saka tumalikod.","translation":"She **rolled** her eyes and then turned away."}]

translation: to make a gap in; to leave a space
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng puwang o awang ang isang bagay; lumikha ng espasyo.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang "awang" na may hulaping "-an".
original_explanation: Ito yung act of creating a space. "Bes, **awangan** mo naman ako diyan sa upuan." o "Kailangan mong **awangan** ang schedule mo para sa self-care." It's about intentionally making room for something... or someone.
usage_notes: Ito ang pandiwang anyo ng 'awang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**awangan** mo nang kaunti ang mga halaman para masikatan ng araw.","translation":"Please **leave a small space** between the plants so they can get sunlight."}]

translation: To browse through pages; to open a book
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbubuklat o pagbubukas ng mga pahina ng isang aklat, magasin, o anumang babasahin upang magbasa o tumingin.
original_explanation: The pre-internet version of "scrolling." `Magbuklat` is the act of flipping through the pages of a book, a magazine, or your old photo albums. It's what you do in a bookstore when you're trying to decide if a book is worth buying, or what your parents do when they find your old "slumbook" and threaten to read it out loud. It's an act of discovery, one page at a time.
usage_notes: More specific than `magbukas`. `Magbukas` is just opening the cover, `magbuklat` implies turning the pages inside.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magbuklat** ng mga lumang libro sa silid-aklatan.","translation":"He loves to **browse through the pages** of old books in the library."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nilalang na nagmula sa labas ng daigdig; isang dayuhan o banyaga na hindi pamilyar sa isang lugar o kultura.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na 'alien', na isinunod sa palabaybayang Filipino.
original_explanation: Yung taga-ibang planeta na laging sinasabi ni Kuya Kim. O 'yung feeling mo sa family reunion kapag tinanong ka ng tita mo kung bakit wala ka pa ring jowa. You feel like an outsider, an alyen.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa mga extraterrestrial at para ilarawan ang pakiramdam ng pagiging iba o hindi kabilang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala ka ba sa mga **alyen**?","translation":"Do you believe in **aliens**?"},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay isang **alyen** ako sa sarili kong bansa.","translation":"I feel like an **alien** in my own country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong labis ang pag-iingat sa mga detalye; maselan o sobrang maingat sa paggawa ng isang bagay upang maging perpekto.
original_explanation: Ito yung ka-groupmate mo na chine-check bawat period at comma sa report. Sila yung tipo na hindi makakatulog kapag hindi pantay ang margin ng document. Sa love life, sila yung nag-o-overthink sa bawat text message na natatanggap.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang babae. Ang panlalaking anyo ay "iskrupuloso".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iskrupulosa** si Aling Nena sa paglilinis kaya walang alikabok sa bahay niya.","translation":"Aling Nena is **meticulous** in cleaning, so there's no dust in her house."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagiging **iskrupulosa** ng editor, naging perpekto ang pagkakalathala ng libro.","translation":"Because of the editor's **scrupulous** nature, the book's publication was perfect."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking piraso ng tela, papel, o tarpaulin na may nakasulat na mensahe, islogan, o larawan, karaniwang itinatanghal sa publiko.
original_explanation: The modern, English-derived cousin of 'bandila'. This is your "Welcome to the Grand Alumni Homecoming!" tarpaulin, your "Congratulations, Graduates!" sign, or the giant "For Lease" sign on an empty building. If it's made of tarpaulin and has a message, it's a baner.
usage_notes: A Filipinized spelling and pronunciation of the English word 'banner'. Often used interchangeably with 'tarpaulin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpagawa sila ng malaking **baner** para sa kaarawan ng kanilang lola.","translation":"They had a large **banner** made for their grandmother's birthday."},{"sentence":"Paki-tali nang mahigpit ang **baner** para hindi liparin ng hangin.","translation":"Please tie the **banner** tightly so it won't be blown away by the wind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho o gawain ay ang magmaneho ng isang sasakyan tulad ng kotse, bus, dyipni, o trak.
original_explanation: Sila ang mga hari ng kalsada! Mula sa jeepney **drayber** na kayang magsukli habang nagmamaneho sa EDSA, hanggang sa Grab **drayber** na aalukin ka ng tubig at kendi, sila ang nagpapatakbo ng Pilipinas, literally. Sila rin ang may hawak ng playlist (at ng aircon). 'Manong, para!'
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang hiram na salita na halos ganap nang pinalitan ang 'tsuper' sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Bayad po,\" sabi ko sa **drayber** ng dyip.","translation":"\"Here's my payment,\" I said to the jeepney **driver**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unti-unting pagkawala o pagbabago ng kulay ng isang bagay, karaniwang dahil sa pagkabilad sa araw, paglalaba, o paglipas ng panahon.
original_explanation: Like your favorite black shirt that's now a sad shade of gray after too many washes. Or, in a #hugot sense, it's what happens to feelings over time. "Ang dating matinding pag-ibig, ngayon ay kumupas na." Ouch.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to color, but can be used metaphorically for feelings, memories, or intensity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumupas** na ang kulay ng kurtina dahil laging naarawan.","translation":"The color of the curtain has **faded** because it's always exposed to the sun."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **kumupas** ang ating mga alaala.","translation":"Don't let our memories **fade**."}]

translation: to maintain; to preserve; to keep
meaning_filipino: Ang patuloy na pag-iingat o pagpapanatili sa isang bagay, kalagayan, o katangian upang hindi ito magbago o mawala.
etymology: Mula sa `pa-` + `tili` (isang bihirang salitang-ugat na nangangahulugang 'manatili') + `-hin`.
original_explanation: Very similar to `panatilihan`, but this is more common. It's the "keep it that way" verb. "Panatilihin mo 'yang ngiti mo." (Keep that smile.) "Panatilihin ang social distancing." Ito 'yung active effort para hindi magbago ang isang bagay, from your rank sa Mobile Legends to your "it's complicated" relationship status.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa `panatilihan`, ngunit mas karaniwan ang `panatilihin` sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Nakatuon ito sa pagpepreserba ng estado o kalidad ng isang bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **panatilihin** ang magagandang tradisyon ng ating lahi.","translation":"We must **preserve** the beautiful traditions of our people."},{"sentence":"**Panatilihin** mong malinis ang iyong kuwarto.","translation":"**Keep** your room clean."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aparato na ginagamit sa mga taksi at iba pang sasakyang pampubliko upang sukatin ang distansya ng biyahe at kalkulahin ang pamasahe.
original_explanation: The magical box in a taxi that's supposed to give you a fair price but sometimes feels like it's running faster than the car itself, especially in traffic. "Manong, paki-on po ng taksimetro. Ayaw ko po ng 'estimasyon' lang."
usage_notes: Often shortened to 'metro'. 'Taksimiter' is a common colloquial variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tiningnan ng pasahero ang tumatakbong numero sa **taksimetro**.","translation":"The passenger looked at the running numbers on the **taximeter**."},{"sentence":"Sirâ daw ang **taksimetro** kaya nangongontrata ang drayber.","translation":"The driver claims the **taximeter** is broken, that's why he's negotiating a fixed price."}]

translation: to use as a pattern; to model after
meaning_filipino: Isang baryasyon ng 'padronin'. Gamitin bilang isang huwaran, modelo, o gabay sa paggawa ng isang bagay na katulad.
etymology: From 'padron' (pattern, from Spanish 'padrón') + '-in' (object-focus suffix). A common phonetic spelling of 'padronin'.
original_explanation: This is the 'sound it out' version of 'padronin'. Same meaning: to use something as a template or pattern. It's the 'pwede na 'yan' spelling, but everyone gets what you mean. The more formal people might correct you to 'padronin'.
usage_notes: A common colloquial spelling and pronunciation variant of 'padronin'. While widely understood, 'padronin' is considered the more standard form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi ng sastre, kaya niyang **padrunin** ang anumang istilo.","translation":"The tailor said he can **use as a pattern** any style."},{"sentence":"Gusto mo bang **padrunin** natin itong plano?\" tanong niya.","translation":"Do you want us **to model** our plan after this?\" he asked."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng nagtatanghal o nagtatrabaho sa isang sirko.
original_explanation: The OG "strong independent woman" who can probably juggle more things than your daily schedule. She's the star of the show, the trapeze artist, the acrobat – basically, the ate who literally runs circles around everyone. The male version is 'sirkero'.
usage_notes: Ang katumbas nito sa lalaki ay 'sirkero'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang galing ng **sirkera** sa trapezoid, parang lumilipad.","translation":"The **female circus performer** on the trapeze was amazing, it was like she was flying."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **sirkera**.","translation":"Her dream is to become a famous **female circus performer**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hanay ng mga taong nagpoprotesta o nagbabantay sa labas ng isang lugar, karaniwan upang pigilan ang iba na pumasok o upang ipahayag ang isang hinaing.
original_explanation: When a group of employees or students are so done with the management that they stand outside the building with signs and chant slogans. It's the IRL version of a fiery group chat, but with more sun exposure and the risk of being on the evening news.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'mag-piket' (to picket).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **piket** ang mga manggagawa sa harap ng pabrika.","translation":"The workers held a **picket** in front of the factory."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **piket**, pansamantalang nahinto ang operasyon.","translation":"Because of the **picket**, operations were temporarily halted."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi tumatanggap ng responsibilidad o hindi nananagot sa mga kilos o gawain.
original_explanation: Describes that person in a group project who disappears after the title page is made. They have zero accountability. It's the 'seen-zoned your message about the bills' energy. They make a mess and expect someone else to clean it up, literally or figuratively. The opposite of 'adulting.'
usage_notes: A formal and strong term to denote a lack of responsibility or accountability.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang lider na **walang-kapananagutan** ang nagdulot ng gulo sa organisasyon.","translation":"A leader **without accountability** caused chaos in the organization."},{"sentence":"Hindi maaaring maging **walang-kapananagutan** ang isang magulang sa kanyang mga anak.","translation":"A parent cannot be **irresponsible** towards their children."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang butas o siwang sa bubong kung saan tumutulo ang tubig, lalo na kapag umuulan.
original_explanation: The ultimate enemy during rainy season. It's that *plak, plak, plak* sound that forces you to strategically place baldes, palangganas, and kaserolas all over the house. The unofficial percussionist of a typhoon.
usage_notes: A very common household problem and term in the Philippines, especially during the monsoon season.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating ipaayos ang bubong dahil marami nang **gotera**.","translation":"We need to have the roof repaired because there are already many **leaks**."},{"sentence":"Paki-ilag ang mga gamit diyan, may **gotera**.","translation":"Please move the things from there, there's a **roof leak**."}]

translation: to wallow in mud; to trample in mud
meaning_filipino: Maglaro o maglublob sa putik o anumang basang-basa at malapot na lugar.
original_explanation: This is what carabaos do for a living and what kids do for fun after a typhoon. It's the act of happily splashing, stomping, and generally making a mess in a muddy puddle. The sound 'pisak' even sounds like squishing mud. It's the opposite of being 'maarte' or prim and proper.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of mud or very wet, muddy ground.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwang-tuwa ang mga bata na **maglapisak** sa putikan pagkatapos ng ulan.","translation":"The children were overjoyed to **wallow in the mud** after the rain."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maglapisak** diyan, marurumihan ang bago mong sapatos!","translation":"Don't **trample in the mud** there, you'll get your new shoes dirty!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtatanim ng impormasyon sa isipan upang matandaan ito nang walang tulong ng anumang gabay; kabisaduhin.
etymology: Mula sa "sa" + "ulo", na literal na nangangahulugang "sa ulo".
original_explanation: This is what every Filipino student does before an exam. 'Panatang Makabayan'? Sauluhin. The multiplication table? Sauluhin. Your lines for the school play? Sauluhin. It's the act of brute-force memorization, committing something to your 'ulo' (head) until you can recite it in your sleep. It's less about understanding and more about perfect recall.
usage_notes: Ang hulaping '-hin' ay nagpapahiwatig na ang isang bagay ang siyang isinasaulo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **sauluhin** ang lahat ng pangalan ng mga bayani.","translation":"I need to **memorize** all the names of the heroes."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **sauluhin** ang isang mahabang tula.","translation":"It is difficult to **memorize** a long poem."}]

translation: to break apart; to scatter; to dismantle
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghihiwa-hiwalay o pagkakalat-kalat ng isang grupo o buong bagay sa maraming bahagi.
etymology: From 'pag-' (infinitive prefix) + 'watak-watak' (scattered) + '-in' (object-focus suffix). The root 'watak' is reduplicated.
original_explanation: This is the 'divide and conquer' move. It's what happens to your group project when the leader is MIA. It's also what your mom does to the lechong manok at the dinner table. Figuratively, it’s what chismis does to a solid barkada – pinagwawatak-watak ang samahan!
usage_notes: Implies a forceful or deliberate act of separation or dispersal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng kaaway na **pagwatak-watakin** ang kanilang hukbo.","translation":"The enemy tried **to scatter** their army."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating hayaang **pagwatak-watakin** ng intriga ang ating pamilya.","translation":"Let's not allow intrigue **to break apart** our family."}]

meaning_filipino: May simpleng anyo, karaniwang magaspang ang pagkakayari, at nagpapahiwatig ng buhay sa kabukiran o probinsya.
original_explanation: Yung aesthetic ng mga cafe sa Tagaytay o sa mga farm-to-table restaurant. Medyo "probinsya" feels pero in a stylish, Instagrammable way. Think unpolished wood, mason jars, and anything that looks charmingly old or handmade. It’s the "I want to escape the city but still have good Wi-Fi" vibe.
usage_notes: Primarily used in design, architecture, and lifestyle contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinili nila ang **rustika** na tema para sa kanilang kasal.","translation":"They chose a **rustic** theme for their wedding."},{"sentence":"Ang mga muwebles sa bahay-bakasyunan ay may **rustika** na disenyo.","translation":"The furniture in the vacation house has a **rustic** design."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbibigay ng opinyon, paliwanag, o pagsusuri sa isang paksa, partikular sa radyo, telebisyon, o pahayagan.
original_explanation: The person whose job is to have an opinion on everything, from basketball games to politics. Think of them as the professional "Marites" or "Tolits" of the news world, but they get paid for their chismis. They're the voice you hear explaining why your team is losing or why the traffic is bad (again).
usage_notes: Often refers to sports, political, or social analysts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang **komentarista** sa kanyang matapang na pananaw sa politika.","translation":"The **commentator** is known for his bold views on politics."},{"sentence":"Magaling magpaliwanag ng laro ang bagong **komentarista** sa basketball.","translation":"The new basketball **analyst** is great at explaining the game."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na ginagamit bilang pamalit sa anumang hindi nais o hindi na kailangang tukuyin nang tiyakan; katumbas ng 'at iba pa' o 'kung ano-ano'.
etymology: Mula sa salitang balbal na 'ekla' o 'echos', na karaniwang ginagamit sa Swardspeak o gay lingo.
original_explanation: This is the upgraded, more *sosyal* version of 'echos' or 'charot'. It's the verbal equivalent of an eye-roll and a hair flip. When you're telling a story and can't be bothered with the details, you just sprinkle in some 'eklavou'. "So ayun, nag-away sila about the project, the deadline, the budget, and eklavou." It's the ultimate filler word for the modern Filipino storyteller. Also spelled 'eklavu'.
usage_notes: Ang 'eklavu' ay isang karaniwang baryasyon. Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga impormal, kolokyal, at Swardspeak (gay lingo) na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dami niyang sinabi, kesyo pagod daw siya, masakit ang ulo, at kung ano-ano pang **eklavou**.","translation":"She said so many things, that she was tired, had a headache, and all that other **whatever**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang salikop o panulukan ng dalawang kalye.
original_explanation: The Filipino version of a community hub. It's not just a street corner; it's a waiting area for jeepneys, a gossip central for *marites*, a meeting point for your *barkada* ("kita-kits sa kanto"), and sometimes, a stage for the local *tambay*. The 'kanto' is where life happens, one jeepney ride and chismis at a time.
usage_notes: Also used in the phrase "kanto boy" to refer to someone who hangs out on street corners, often with a tough or street-smart image.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-abang ka na lang ng dyip sa **kanto**.","translation":"Just wait for a jeepney at the **street corner**."},{"sentence":"Nagkakape ang magkakaibigan sa tindahan sa **kanto** tuwing umaga.","translation":"The friends have coffee at the store on the **corner** every morning."}]

translation: to ascertain, to make sure, to ensure
meaning_filipino: Ang alamin o siguruhin ang katotohanan o katiyakan ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the "double check mo, bes" verb. Before sending that risky text. Before checking out your online shopping cart. Before believing in chismis. You need to matiyak na tama ang info. It's the act of confirming something so you don't mess up. "Pakitanong ulit para matiyak natin."
usage_notes: Often used in formal and informal contexts to mean "to make sure."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **matiyak** na nakasara ang pinto bago ka umalis.","translation":"You need **to make sure** that the door is locked before you leave."},{"sentence":"Tumawag siya sa opisina upang **matiyak** ang oras ng pulong.","translation":"He called the office **to ascertain** the time of the meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal o pampanitikang salita para sa pagdating o pag-abot sa isang pook. Ito ay may mas malalim at maringal na konotasyon kaysa sa 'dumating'.
original_explanation: This is the 'dumating' that went to a private school and studied Shakespeare. It's the fancy, literary version of 'to arrive.' You don't say your Grab 'dumatal'. You use this for epic moments, like in a poem: 'At sa wakas, ang pinakahihintay na bayani ay dumatal.' It's got that old-school, Florante at Laura vibe. Using this in a casual conversation will get you some weird looks, unless you're being dramatic for laughs.
usage_notes: Strictly for literary, formal, or poetic use. It sounds unnatural in modern, everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang **dumatal** ang balita, ang buong kaharian ay nagalak.","translation":"When the news **arrived**, the whole kingdom rejoiced."},{"sentence":"Hihintayin kita hanggang sa **dumatal** ang takipsilim.","translation":"I will wait for you until twilight **arrives**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsasagawa ng isang sesyon ng pag-inom ng alak, karaniwan ay kasama ang mga kaibigan o kasamahan.
original_explanation: The national sport after basketball. It's when the Titos of the group gather 'round a table with a case of beer and a plate of sisig, ready to solve the world's problems, one 'shot' at a time. It's not just drinking; it's a sacred ritual of storytelling, bonding, and questionable life advice. 'Tara, magbarikan tayo!' is the grown-up version of 'Tara, laro tayo!'
usage_notes: Often used in informal, social contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aya ang mga katrabaho ko na **magbarikan** pagkatapos ng shift.","translation":"My officemates invited me to **have a drinking session** after our shift."},{"sentence":"Bawal **magbarikan** sa kalsada, baka mahuli kayo ng tanod.","translation":"It's forbidden to **have a drinking session** on the street, the village guard might catch you."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng katangiang nakabibighani o nakahahalina sa paningin, pandinig, o damdamin.
etymology: Reduplication of 'akit' (attraction, charm) with the prefix ka-, which intensifies the quality.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'maganda' (beautiful). This is 'stop-what-you're-doing-and-stare' level of attractive. It's the travel spot on Instagram that gives you wanderlust, the perfectly plated adobo that makes your mouth water, or the person who walks into a room and everyone just... notices. It’s got that magnetic pull.
usage_notes: Can describe people, places, things, or even ideas. It implies a strong, almost magnetic appeal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tunay na **kaakit-akit** ang mga tanawin sa Palawan.","translation":"The sights in Palawan are truly **captivating**."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **kaakit-akit** na ngiti.","translation":"She has a **charming** smile."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtutol, pagkontra, o paggawa ng isang bagay na kabaligtaran sa inaasahan, napagkasunduan, o sa karaniwang pamantayan.
original_explanation: Ito yung pagiging 'kontrabida' mo sa group project. Yung lahat agree na sa idea, tapos bigla kang may ibang gustong gawin. It's the act of being contrary or swimming against the current. Parang yung nag-oorder ng kanin sa Starbucks. That's pagsaliwa.
usage_notes: Implies a deviation from a norm, rule, or agreement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsaliwa** niya sa utos ng hari ay nagdulot ng malaking gulo.","translation":"His **act of going against** the king's order caused a huge trouble."},{"sentence":"Isang **pagsaliwa** sa tradisyon ang kanyang ginawang pag-aasawa.","translation":"Her marriage was a **contradiction** to tradition."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matalik na kaibigan o kasama; isang taong may malapit na ugnayan at pinagkakatiwalaan.
etymology: Maaaring mula sa "ka-" (nagpapahiwatig ng pagsasama) + "totoo" (tunay), na nangangahulugang "tunay na kasama".
original_explanation: Before "beshie," "mars," or "frenny," there was "katoto." It's an old-school, almost poetic way to say "my dude" or "my confidante." Think of the friends your lolo would share a drink with while reminiscing about the "good old days." It implies a deep, time-tested bond.
usage_notes: Medyo pormal o pampanitikan ang dating sa modernong usapan. Madalas gamitin sa mga kontekstong pangkasaysayan o pormal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halika, aking **katoto**, at tayo'y magkape.","translation":"Come, my **close friend**, and let's have coffee."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing niya akong higit pa sa kaibigan, isa raw akong tunay na **katoto**.","translation":"He considers me more than a friend, he says I am a true **comrade**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa ikalima sa isang pagkakasunod-sunod; ang sumusunod sa ikaapat at sinusundan ng ikaanim.
original_explanation: When you're the **panlima** in the Jollibee queue and the person in front of you gets the last piece of Chickenjoy. Saklap. Also, the fifth person in a group of four friends—the official taga-picture.
usage_notes: Used as an ordinal number. 'Ikalima' is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **panlima** sa magkakapatid.","translation":"He is the **fifth** among the siblings."},{"sentence":"Nasa **panlima** akong pwesto sa pila.","translation":"I am in the **fifth** spot in the line."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hayop na may malambot na katawan at may dalang bahay na shell, karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga tubigan o basang lugar.
original_explanation: The original slowpoke. In the Philippines, this isn't just a garden pest. The native ones are a delicacy, cooked in coconut milk ('ginataang kuhol'). The invasive golden apple snail ('golden kuhol'), however, is the bane of rice farmers. So, it's either your next pulutan or the villain of the rice paddy.
usage_notes: Can refer to various types of snails. In a culinary context, it usually means freshwater snails. The 'golden kuhol' is a specific, well-known invasive species in rice fields.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang ginataang **kuhol** lalo na kung medyo maanghang.","translation":"**Snails** in coconut milk are delicious, especially if a bit spicy."},{"sentence":"Maraming **kuhol** sa palayan pagkatapos ng ulan.","translation":"There are many **snails** in the rice field after the rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng damo (Chrysopogon aciculatus) na may maliliit at matutulis na buto na kumakapit sa damit o balat ng hayop.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'amor seco', na literal na nangangahulugang 'tuyong pag-ibig', isang mapanuksong pangalan para sa paraan ng pagkapit nito.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'stage-5 clinger' of the plant world. You walk through a grassy field, and suddenly your pants and socks are covered in these tiny, spiky seeds that are a pain to remove. It's the bane of anyone wearing socks and slippers while taking a shortcut through a vacant lot. The name is ironic, from Spanish 'amor seco' (dry love), because it sticks to you, but it's not a pleasant kind of attachment.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa partikular na halaman at sa mga makakapit na buto nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **amorseko** ang medyas ko pagkatapos naming maglaro sa damuhan.","translation":"My socks were full of **bur-grass** after we played on the lawn."},{"sentence":"Mahirap tanggalin ang mga **amorseko** sa balahibo ng aso.","translation":"It's difficult to remove **bur-grass** from a dog's fur."}]

translation: To go to (a place); to visit
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtungo sa isang tiyak na lokasyon o lugar. Ginagamit kapag ang pokus ng pangungusap ay ang lugar na pinatutunguhan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "punta" na may hulaping "-han".
original_explanation: This is the verb you use when the destination is the star of the show. It's not just 'to go', it's 'to go TO a specific place'. 'Puntahan natin yung bagong coffee shop!' The focus is on the coffee shop, not just the act of going. It's what you do to a place.
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb where the object is the location being visited or gone to.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **puntahan** ang Vigan sa susunod na taon.","translation":"I want **to go to** Vigan next year."},{"sentence":"**Puntahan** mo si Lola sa probinsya at kumustahin mo siya.","translation":"**Go to** (visit) Grandma in the province and check how she is."}]

translation: to be deceived; to allow oneself to be deceived
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpayag o pagiging biktima ng panlilinlang o panloloko ng iba.
original_explanation: When you fall for a "legit investment" from a friend's cousin's officemate that promises 100% returns in one week. It’s believing the "On my way!" text when you know they just woke up. Hugot version: "Nag-palinlang ako sa mga matatamis niyang salita."
usage_notes: Can mean either to be actively deceived by someone, or to passively allow the deception to happen.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang basta-basta **palinlang** sa mga pekeng balita sa internet.","translation":"Don't just **be deceived** by fake news on the internet."},{"sentence":"Marami ang nag**palinlang** sa pyramid scheme na iyon.","translation":"Many **were deceived** by that pyramid scheme."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangalan na ibinibigay bilang tanda ng paglalambing o pagkakakilanlan, bukod sa tunay na pangalan; bansag.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang `layaw` (pag-aalaga nang may paglalambing), dahil ang isang palayaw ay isang uri ng verbal na paglalambing.
original_explanation: Yung 'Babe,' 'Love,' 'Pangga,' o 'Bunso' mo. It's not your government name, but it's what people who know you (or love you, or want to annoy you) call you. Every 'Jun-jun' and 'Baby Girl' in the Philippines knows this.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'bansag', bagaman ang 'palayaw' ay maaaring magkaroon ng mas magiliw na konotasyon habang ang 'bansag' ay maaaring neutral o mapanukso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **palayaw** niya sa bahay ay 'Bunso' kahit siya ay panganay.","translation":"His **nickname** at home is 'Bunso' (youngest) even though he is the eldest."},{"sentence":"Marami siyang **palayaw**, pero 'Inday' ang pinakakilala sa kanya.","translation":"She has many **pet names**, but 'Inday' is what she's most known for."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyon o sistema ng pamamahala sa isang bansa, estado, o komunidad; pamahalaan.
etymology: From 'pa-' + 'bahala' + '-an'. A place where responsibility ('bahala') is managed. A more formal variant of 'pamahalaan'.
original_explanation: This is the formal, textbook term for 'government.' You'll see this in news reports and history books. It's the 'pamahalaan' that's wearing a barong and being very serious. It's the high-level, almost poetic version of 'gobyerno'.
usage_notes: This is a more formal and somewhat archaic synonym for 'pamahalaan.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pabahalaan** ay may tungkuling pangalagaan ang kapakanan ng mamamayan.","translation":"The **government** has the duty to protect the welfare of the citizens."},{"sentence":"Maraming isyu ang kinakaharap ng kasalukuyang **pabahalaan**.","translation":"The current **administration** is facing many issues."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng isang tao na nasa bingit ng kamatayan, kung saan nag-aagawan ang buhay at kamatayan.
original_explanation: "Agaw-buhay" is the ultimate cliffhanger. It's that dramatic scene in a teleserye where the hero is in the hospital, the EKG is beeping erratically, and the family is crying outside. It literally means "life-snatching," as if life and death are in a tug-of-war. Used to describe someone in critical condition.
usage_notes: Used to describe a person in a critical, near-death state. The person is said to be "nag-aagaw-buhay".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa ospital ang biktima at **agaw-buhay**.","translation":"The victim is in the hospital and is **dying**."},{"sentence":"Maraming oras siyang nag-**agaw-buhay** bago tuluyang pumanaw.","translation":"He was at the **point of death** for many hours before finally passing away."}]

translation: to make furrows; to plow a line
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng mga guhit o tudling sa lupa, karaniwang ginagamit sa pagsasaka bago magtanim.
original_explanation: This is the OG way of preparing a field for planting. Imagine a farmer with a carabao, plowing straight lines in the soil. That action is 'magtudling.' It's about creating the perfect rows for your seeds to grow, like organizing your files into neat folders, but for dirt.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of agriculture and farming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maagang gumising ang magsasaka upang **magtudling** sa kanyang bukirin.","translation":"The farmer woke up early to **make furrows** in his field."},{"sentence":"Gumamit sila ng makina para mas mabilis na **magtudling** sa malawak na taniman.","translation":"They used a machine to **make furrows** more quickly in the wide plantation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagdiriwang ng kapaskuhan sa isang partikular na lugar o kasama ang mga partikular na tao.
etymology: From Spanish 'Pascua' (Easter, but adapted for Christmas in the Philippines).
original_explanation: It's the annual "Saan tayo mag-Pasko?" question. It's the verb for the entire Christmas migration, whether you're going home to the province, flying to another country, or just staying home in your pajamas with Noche Buena leftovers.
usage_notes: This verb is often used in the future tense ('magpapasko') or past tense ('nagpasko') to discuss holiday plans or experiences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa probinsya kami **magpapasko** ngayong taon.","translation":"We will **spend Christmas** in the province this year."},{"sentence":"Maraming OFW ang umuuwi para **magpasko** kasama ang kanilang pamilya.","translation":"Many OFWs come home to **spend Christmas** with their families."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagkasira o pagkabulok ng organikong materyal sa pamamagitan ng pagkilos ng mga mikroorganismo.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung nangyayari sa saging na iniwan mo sa bag mo for a week. O sa feelings mo para sa ex mong 'di ka minahal, hinayaan mo na lang mabulok sa limot. Pwede ring gamitin sa sistema, "bulok na sistema," meaning a corrupt or rotten system.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for organic decay or figuratively for moral or systemic corruption.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwan ang pagkain sa labas dahil baka ito ay **mabulok**.","translation":"Don't leave the food outside because it might **rot**."},{"sentence":"Hahayaan ko na lang siyang **mabulok** sa bilangguan dahil sa mga kasalanan niya.","translation":"I will just let him **rot** in jail because of his crimes."}]

translation: to make dirty, to soil, to defile
meaning_filipino: Gawing marumi o maglagay ng dumi sa isang bagay na malinis.
original_explanation: What your mom thinks you do to the living room 5 seconds after she cleans it. To 'parumihin' is to mess things up, whether it's your white shirt with ketchup, your clean reputation with some chismis, or the floor with your muddy shoes. The opposite of 'Tita-approved'.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical dirt or figuratively for reputation or honor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **parumihin** ang sahig, kakalinis ko lang.","translation":"Don't **make** the floor **dirty**, I just cleaned it."},{"sentence":"Ginawa nila ang lahat upang **parumihin** ang kanyang pangalan.","translation":"They did everything to **defile** his name."}]

translation: to writhe, to squirm, to twist
meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw ng katawan sa paraang paikot-ikot o paurong-sulong, karaniwan dahil sa sakit, hirap, o matinding emosyon.
original_explanation: It's how your body reacts when you accidentally see your ex's wedding photos on Facebook. Or when you eat something super spicy that you weren't prepared for. Your whole body just goes into full-on contortionist mode.
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense). Present: `pumipilipit`, Future: `pipilipit`. Can describe physical pain or emotional discomfort.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumilipit** siya sa sakit ng tiyan matapos kumain sa labas.","translation":"He **writhed** in stomach pain after eating out."},{"sentence":"Nang tanungin siya tungkol sa pera, **pumilipit** siya sa upuan at hindi makasagot nang diretso.","translation":"When asked about the money, he **squirmed** in his seat and couldn't answer directly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng hindi pagwawagi o pagkakaroon ng mas mababang puntos sa isang laban, kompetisyon, o argumento.
original_explanation: Ito yung feeling na umasa ka sa 13th month pay para sa Christmas shopping, tapos natalo ka lang sa online bidding. O kaya yung moment na akala mo kayo na, pero "friends" lang pala. The ultimate "sana all" moment mo ay naging "sana olats".
usage_notes: Often used in the context of sports, games, elections, and arguments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi matanggap ng boksingero ang kanyang **pagtalo** sa laban.","translation":"The boxer could not accept his **defeat** in the fight."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtalo** sa argumento ay hindi nangangahulugang mali ka palagi.","translation":"**Losing** an argument doesn't always mean you're wrong."}]

meaning_filipino: Piliting ibaluktot o ikurba nang paatras, karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga daliri, kamay, o ibang bahagi ng katawan.
original_explanation: This is what happens in old action movies when the hero catches the villain's finger and bends it the wrong way. It's that comically painful-looking bend. You might jokingly tell your friend who won't return your Tupperware, "Isoli mo na 'yan kundi babalikukuin ko daliri mo!"
usage_notes: Implies a forceful, often unnatural bending, usually of a limb or joint. It has a slightly threatening or aggressive connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wrestling, isang paraan para sumuko ang kalaban ay **balikukuin** ang braso nito.","translation":"In wrestling, one way to make an opponent submit is to **forcibly bend** their arm **backwards**."},{"sentence":"Nagbanta siyang babalikukuin ang daliri ng magnanakaw kung hindi isasauli ang kinuha nito.","translation":"He threatened to **bend back** the thief's finger if he didn't return what he stole."}]

meaning_filipino: Umiyak nang may malakas na tunog at hikbi, karaniwang sanhi ng matinding kalungkutan o sakit.
original_explanation: The slightly less dramatic cousin of 'humagulgol'. It's still a heavy, emotional cry, but maybe with fewer sound effects. Think of the sob you let out when you realize you left your baon at home, or when your internet connection dies mid-meeting. Still painful, but not full-on 'Maalala Mo Kaya' level.
usage_notes: Past tense. Often used interchangeably with 'humagulgol', though some speakers perceive it as slightly less intense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humagulhol** siya sa balikat ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"She **sobbed** on her friend's shoulder."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katayuan, tungkulin, o panahon ng panunungkulan bilang pangulo ng isang bansa, organisasyon, o kumpanya.
original_explanation: The ultimate promotion. The highest seat in the land (or the company, or the homeowners' association). It's the job that comes with a big house (Malacañang), a cool car, and millions of people either loving you or making memes about you. It's the state of being "The Boss" with a capital B.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa opisina o termino ng isang pangulo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pagsubok ang hinarap ng bansa sa panahon ng kanyang **pagkapangulo**.","translation":"The country faced many challenges during his **presidency**."},{"sentence":"Nangangarap siyang balang araw ay marating ang **pagkapangulo**.","translation":"He dreams of one day achieving the **presidency**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babae na hindi kaaya-aya ang pag-uugali, nakakainis, o mahirap pakisamahan.
original_explanation: 'Yung officemate mong laging may reklamo, laging naka-simangot, at parang laging may dalaw. Siya 'yung tipo na 'pag nag-good morning ka, ang isasagot, "Anong maganda sa morning?" The female version of a killjoy. The male counterpart is `antipatiko`.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa babae. Ang katumbas para sa lalaki ay "antipatiko".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw siyang kausapin ng mga tao dahil siya ay **antipatika**.","translation":"People don't want to talk to her because she is **unpleasant**."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **antipatika** sa mga baguhang empleyado.","translation":"She is known for being **disagreeable** to new employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matibay at patayong haligi, karaniwang gawa sa kahoy, bakal, o semento, na ginagamit bilang suporta sa isang istruktura o para kabitan ng kawad ng kuryente o telepono.
original_explanation: 'Yung nakatayo sa kanto na madalas mong mayakap 'pag lasing ka na pauwi. O kaya 'yung sandalan mo habang naghihintay ng jeep na puno na naman. Sa basketball, ito 'yung big man na nire-rely on mo sa ilalim ng ring. "I-poste mo!"
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga poste ng kuryente o telepono. Ginagamit din sa isports tulad ng basketball para ilarawan ang posisyon malapit sa ring.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumangga ang motorsiklo sa **poste** ng kuryente.","translation":"The motorcycle crashed into the electric **post**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong iihian ang **poste** na iyan dahil may nakakabit na CCTV.","translation":"Don't urinate on that **pole** because a CCTV is attached to it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng paligsahan kung saan ang layunin ay maging pinakamabilis na makarating sa takdang pook o tapusin ang isang gawain.
original_explanation: Before it was a car on a drag strip, it was a horse. Before it was a horse, it was just two people running. Lumba is a race. Pabilisan. From lumba-ng kabayo (horse race) to the pasabog na lumba-han ng motor sa kanto niyo. It's all about speed.
usage_notes: This is the root word for 'karera' in some contexts, but 'lumba' itself as a noun is less common than 'karera' or 'paligsahan'. Often seen in compounds like 'lumbang-kabayo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging sikat na manonood sa **lumba** ng mga kabayo ang kanyang ama.","translation":"His father became a famous spectator at the horse **races**."},{"sentence":"Ang **lumba** sa pag-unlad ng teknolohiya ay walang katapusan.","translation":"The **race** for technological advancement is endless."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging angkop, bagay, o akma sa isa pa.
original_explanation: When your outfit just works. When the new hire fits perfectly with the team's chaotic energy. When the bagoong perfectly complements the mangga. That's 'kaugma'. It's the satisfying click of two things fitting together, whether it's people, ideas, or flavors. The opposite of 'sana all' because you actually found the perfect match.
usage_notes: Less common in everyday speech than 'bagay' or 'tugma' but more formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga ideya ay **kaugma** sa layunin ng ating kumpanya.","translation":"His ideas are **compatible** with our company's goals."},{"sentence":"Hindi lahat ng tao ay **kaugma** ng iyong pagkatao.","translation":"Not all people are **harmonious** with your personality."}]

translation: to arrange in a line or row
meaning_filipino: Ayusin sa isang tuwid na linya o hanay.
original_explanation: Think of your teacher in elementary school yelling 'Pumila!' or 'Line up!'. This is the more formal verb for that. It's arranging things (or people) in a neat row, like lining up for the MRT, arranging books on a shelf, or setting up chairs for a seminar.
usage_notes: Common in formal instructions, military drills, or organizing objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ihilera** ninyo ang mga upuan sa likod ng silid.","translation":"**Arrange** the chairs in a **row** at the back of the room."},{"sentence":"**Inihilera** ng tindera ang mga panindang prutas.","translation":"The vendor **lined up** the fruits she was selling."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang serye ng magkakabit na mga argolya o kawing, karaniwang gawa sa metal, na ginagamit sa paggapos, paghila, o pagpigil.
original_explanation: It's a chain. Literally, the thing you use to lock your bike. Figuratively, it's what's holding you back. 'Yung utang mo sa credit card, 'yan ang **tanikala** mo. Or that toxic relationship you can't seem to leave. It symbolizes anything that restricts your freedom, from debt to 'masamang bisyo'.
usage_notes: Often used in a figurative sense to denote bondage or oppression.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalag na siya mula sa **tanikala** ng kahirapan.","translation":"He has been freed from the **shackles** of poverty."},{"sentence":"Ginamit ng mga pulis ang **tanikala** upang isara ang kalsada.","translation":"The police used a **chain** to close the road."}]

translation: to splash about in water, to wade playfully
meaning_filipino: Ang masayang paglalaro sa mababaw na tubig sa pamamagitan ng paghampas o pagpadyak dito gamit ang mga kamay o paa.
original_explanation: This is what you do at the beach when you're too scared to actually swim in the deep part. You just stay in the shallows and magtampisaw—splashing your feet, kicking the water, and generally just enjoying the feeling without the commitment of a full swim. It's the aquatic equivalent of 'window shopping'. Also what kids love to do in puddles after it rains.
usage_notes: Implies shallow water and a playful, carefree attitude.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masayang **nagtampisaw** ang mga bata sa dalampasigan.","translation":"The children were playfully **splashing about** on the seashore."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko lang **magtampisaw** sa baha, sabi ng batang pasaway.","translation":"I just want to **wade playfully** in the flood, said the naughty child."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang matinis at nagngangalit na tunog, karaniwang mula sa sahig na yari sa kahoy o kawayan, o isang lumang pinto.
original_explanation: The sound your wooden floor makes at 3 AM when you're trying to sneak to the fridge for a midnight snack. It's the official soundtrack of horror movies set in old Filipino houses.
usage_notes: An onomatopoeic word referring to the sound of friction on wood or bamboo. Infinitive/past tense. Present: 'umaalatiit'. Future: 'aalatiit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **umalatiit** ang sahig na kawayan nang may dumaan.","translation":"The bamboo floor suddenly **creaked** when someone passed by."},{"sentence":"Ayaw kong gumalaw dahil baka **umalatiit** ang kama at magising siya.","translation":"I don't want to move because the bed might **creak** and wake him up."}]

meaning_filipino: Patatawan ng kaparusahan sa hinaharap dahil sa isang pagkakasala o paglabag.
original_explanation: The future tense of 'lagot ka.' This is what your boss means when they say 'Let's talk on Monday' after you messed up a big presentation on a Friday. You know the whole weekend that you **maparurusahan**. It's the impending doom you feel before facing the consequences.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a punishment that will happen in the future.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sinumang lumabag sa batas ay **maparurusahan**.","translation":"Anyone who breaks the law **will be punished**."},{"sentence":"Sinabi ng nanay na **maparurusahan** ang hindi magliligpit ng kanilang higaan.","translation":"The mother said that those who don't fix their beds **will be punished**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakatakip o nababalutan ng isang bagay tulad ng papel, tela, o plastik.
original_explanation: This is what your Christmas gifts look like before Dec 25. It's also you, bundled up in a thick blanket during a rainy day. Or your feelings, all wrapped up and hidden because 'it's complicated.'
usage_notes: Ang bigkas ay may diin sa unang pantig /BA-lot/ upang maiba sa pagkain na /ba-LOT/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Balot** sa makapal na kumot ang sanggol upang hindi ito ginawin.","translation":"The baby is **wrapped** in a thick blanket so it won't get cold."},{"sentence":"Laging **balot** ng hiwaga ang kanyang katauhan.","translation":"His personality is always **shrouded** (wrapped) in mystery."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal (Kr) na isang 'noble gas'. Sa kulturang popular, ito ang pangalan ng planeta kung saan nagmula si Superman.
original_explanation: Usually, ito 'yung home planet ni Superman na sumabog. Kaya 'pag sinabi mong 'You are my Kryptonite,' ibig sabihin, ikaw ang kahinaan niya. Huwag malito sa Krypton na nasa periodic table of elements, maliban na lang kung science major ka.
usage_notes: Almost always refers to the fictional planet from DC Comics in popular conversation. The chemical element is rare in daily talk. The word is capitalized when referring to the planet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Superman ay nagmula sa planetang **Kripton**.","translation":"Superman came from the planet **Krypton**."},{"sentence":"Ang **kripton** ay isang 'noble gas' na may atomic number na 36.","translation":"**Krypton** is a noble gas with an atomic number of 36."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng ibabaw na hindi patag, may anggulong pataas o pababa.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're walking in San Francisco, or hiking up a mountain in Rizal. Your calves are burning because the road is **dahilig**. It's the opposite of 'flat earth' logic. Also, the angle of your phone when you're trying to get that perfect selfie from above.
usage_notes: Describes a surface, like a road, hill, or roof.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pagbaba, **dahilig** ang daan.","translation":"Be careful going down, the road is **sloping**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng alagang hayop na may makapal na katawan at maikling mga binti, karaniwang inaalagaan para sa karne nito. Tumutukoy din ito sa karne mula sa hayop na ito.
original_explanation: The MVP of every Filipino fiesta. Whether as lechon, adobo, sinigang, or sisig, this animal is our national hero of cuisine. It can also be a pang-uri (adjective) to describe your messy room, your friend who eats with their mouth open ("Ang baboy mo kumain!"), or how you feel after a buffet.
usage_notes: Can refer to the live animal or the meat (pork). Also used as a derogatory adjective for messiness or gluttony.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang sinigang na **baboy** na luto ni Nanay.","translation":"Mom's sinigang na **baboy** (pork in sour soup) is delicious."},{"sentence":"May alagang dalawang **baboy** si Lolo sa likod-bahay.","translation":"Grandpa is raising two **pigs** in the backyard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkukumpuni ng butas o punit sa damit o tela sa pamamagitan ng pagtatahi gamit ang karayom at sinulid.
original_explanation: What your lola does to your favorite butas-butas na pambahay shirt, saving it from its destiny as a basahan (rag). It's the original life hack for sustainable fashion, fixing small holes so you don't have to throw the whole thing away. A true art form.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to mending small holes or tears in fabric, not large-scale sewing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuro sa amin sa klase ng Home Economics kung paano **magsulsi** ng medyas.","translation":"We were taught in Home Economics class how **to darn** socks."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magsulsi** nitong butas sa aking pantalon bago ito lumaki.","translation":"I need **to mend** this hole in my pants before it gets bigger."}]

translation: to attack (a person/thing); to charge at
meaning_filipino: Tiyakang paglusob o pagdaluhong sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the more personal version of 'sugod'. It's not the place, it's the *person* or *thing*. Imagine your friend owes you money and you see them at the mall. 'Sugurin mo na!' your other friend whispers. It's the action of confronting or charging directly at a specific target.
usage_notes: Focuses on the person or object being attacked, as opposed to `suguran` which focuses on the location.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Galit na galit ang aso kaya sinubukan nitong **sugurin** ang kartero.","translation":"The dog was very angry so it tried to **charge at** the mailman."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sugurin** ang problema; pag-isipan mo muna.","translation":"Don't just **attack** the problem; think about it first."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpatong ng isa o dalawang tuhod sa sahig o lupa, karaniwan bilang tanda ng pananalangin, paggalang, o pagsuko.
original_explanation: The physical act of dropping to your knees. You do this in church, when you're proposing (sana all!), or when you're begging your professor not to give you a failing grade. It’s the universal sign for 'I surrender,' 'I'm sorry,' or 'Please, Lord, pa-pasa po sa exam.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumuhod** ang magnanakaw at humingi ng tawad.","translation":"The thief **knelt** and asked for forgiveness."},{"sentence":"Sabay-sabay na **lumuhod** ang mga tao sa simbahan para manalangin.","translation":"The people in the church **knelt** simultaneously to pray."}]

meaning_filipino: Makakaramdam ng pagkapagal o pagkaubos ng lakas sa hinaharap.
etymology: From ma- (potential/future) + pagod (tired). The first syllable of the root is reduplicated for the future tense.
original_explanation: Ang official status ng lahat ng commuters sa EDSA. Ito yung sinasabi mo sa sarili mo bago pa lang mag-start ang work week. 'Monday pa lang, pero sure akong mapapagod na ako agad.' Also the classic line in hugot: 'Mapapagod din akong mahalin ka.'
usage_notes: Future tense of `mapagod` (to get tired).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung tatakbo ka ng marathon, siguradong **mapapagod** ka.","translation":"If you run a marathon, you **will** surely **get tired**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ako **mapapagod** na tulungan ka.","translation":"Don't worry, I **will not get tired** of helping you."}]

translation: to vlog; to create a video blog
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglikha at pag-publish ng isang video blog o 'vlog', karaniwan sa mga platform tulad ng YouTube.
etymology: A Tagalog verb formation (`mag-`) applied to the English clipped compound 'vlog' (video log).
original_explanation: The 2020s version of 'keeping a diary'. Instead of 'Dear Diary,' it's 'What's up, guys! Welcome to my channel!' `Magvlog` is the act of documenting your life—from your 'what I eat in a day' to your latest travel adventure—for the whole world (or at least your subscribers) to see. It’s turning your life into content. Don't forget to like and subscribe!
usage_notes: A very common Taglish verb. This is the infinitive form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong subukang **magvlog** tungkol sa aking mga alagang aso.","translation":"I want to try **to vlog** about my pet dogs."},{"sentence":"Maraming artista ngayon ang nagpasyang **magvlog** para makakonekta sa kanilang mga tagahanga.","translation":"Many celebrities nowadays have decided **to vlog** to connect with their fans."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hindi maayos, magulo, o nakakalat ng mga bagay sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: This is the default state of your bedroom when you're looking for an outfit, or the aftermath of a toddler with a box of toys. It's the physical manifestation of "kalat," the mess you promise your mom you'll clean up "mamaya na." Can also refer to the spread of *chismis* (gossip).
usage_notes: Often used to describe a messy or disorderly state. Can also refer to the act of spreading something, like news or germs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagalit si nanay dahil sa **pagkakalat** ng mga laruan sa sala.","translation":"Mom got angry because of the **messiness** of the toys in the living room."},{"sentence":"Pinag-iingat ang lahat sa mabilis na **pagkakalat** ng sakit.","translation":"Everyone is being warned about the rapid **spread** of the disease."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbabago ng direksyon, karaniwan sa isang kanto o kurbada ng daan.
original_explanation: The most important word you need to know when giving directions to a taxi or Grab driver. 'Sa kanan po sa kanto, Manong!' That pagliko can be the difference between reaching your destination and ending up in a totally different barangay. It's also a metaphor for a major change in your life path.
usage_notes: Primarily used for physical turning, like in driving or walking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa **pagliko** dahil madulas ang kalsada.","translation":"Be careful when **turning** because the road is slippery."},{"sentence":"Isang maling **pagliko** lang at naligaw na kami sa siyudad.","translation":"Just one wrong **turn** and we were already lost in the city."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasama o katabi sa isang lakad, seremonya, o paglalakbay; karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga kasama ng ikakasal sa seremonya ng kasal.
original_explanation: Your designated sidekick for a formal event, especially a wedding. They're the ones who fix your train, hold your flowers, and make sure you don't trip. In life, your 'abay' is your ride-or-die, the person you tag in memes, your travel buddy. Sila yung kasama sa hirap at ginhawa, at sa pila sa milk tea.
usage_notes: Commonly heard during wedding preparations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Maria ang napili kong maging pangunahing **abay** sa aking kasal.","translation":"I chose Maria to be my maid of honor (**escort**) at my wedding."},{"sentence":"Sino ang mga **abay** mo sa debut mo?","translation":"Who are your **escorts** for your debut?"}]

translation: to disturb, to bother, to interrupt
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pag-abala o pag-istorbo sa kapayapaan, katahimikan, o ginagawa ng iba.
original_explanation: The official verb for that one officemate who asks you a question when you're clearly wearing headphones, the telemarketer who calls during dinner, or the neighbor who decides 7 AM on a Sunday is the perfect time for karaoke. It's the act of being an 'istorbo'. The motto is 'Do not disturb,' pero may mga pasaway talagang gustong manggambala.
usage_notes: Implies a deliberate or at least a noticeable disruption.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, huwag kang **manggambala** habang may online meeting.","translation":"Please, do not **disturb** while there's an online meeting."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **manggambala**, kaya tahimik lang siyang pumasok sa silid.","translation":"He didn't want **to bother** anyone, so he entered the room quietly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang seremonya kung saan ang isang tao ay pormal na itinalaga sa isang ministeryo o tungkuling panrelihiyon, gaya ng pagiging pari, pastor, o diyakono.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung "graduation" para sa mga magiging pari o pastor. After years of study and discernment, ito na 'yung final boss level kung saan opisyal na silang binibigyan ng authority to lead a church. It's a huge deal, with special clothes, prayers, and lots of family pictures afterwards.
usage_notes: Tiyak na tumutukoy sa kontekstong panrelihiyon. Huwag ipagkamali sa "ordenansyon" o "ordinansa".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinaluhan ng buong pamilya ang kanyang **ordinasyon** bilang bagong pari.","translation":"The whole family attended his **ordination** as a new priest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pag-boykot; ang pagsasagawa ng sama-samang pagtanggi sa isang produkto, serbisyo, o entidad bilang protesta.
original_explanation: The command form of 'boykot'. This is what you yell (or post on social media) when you want everyone to stop supporting something. "Guys, boykotin natin 'yang coffee shop na 'yan, mahal na 'yung kape, 'di pa masarap!" It's the "let's cancel them" verb.
usage_notes: This is the verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais nilang **boykotin** ang mga produktong gawa sa bansang iyon.","translation":"They want **to boycott** the products made in that country."},{"sentence":"**Boykotin** ang sinehan kung masyadong mahal ang tiket!","translation":"**Boycott** the cinema if the tickets are too expensive!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong kasabwat o tumulong sa paggawa ng isang krimen, ngunit hindi ang pangunahing salarin. Partikular na tumutukoy sa isang babae.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'Marites' na nag-gatekeep ng chismis, pero hindi siya yung gumawa ng issue. Sa krimen, siya yung nagbantay sa labas habang may nanloob, o nagtago ng ebidensya. Hindi siya ang bida sa krimen, pero may special participation. The female version of a sidekick in crime.
usage_notes: Ito ay ang pambabaeng anyo. Ang panlalaki ay "aksesoryo". Huwag ipagkamali sa "aksesorya" (accessories).
