usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinasuhan siya bilang isang **aksesoriya** sa krimen ng pagnanakaw.","translation":"She was charged as an **accessory** to the crime of theft."},{"sentence":"Itinanggi ng babae na siya ay naging **aksesoriya** sa pagtakas ng kanyang kasintahan.","translation":"The woman denied being an **accessory** to her boyfriend's escape."}]

translation: to allow oneself to be left behind; to stay behind
meaning_filipino: Ang sadya o sinasadyang pagpapahintulot na maiwan sa isang lugar o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling when your friends are all going out but you're too tired, so you say, "Sige, paiwan na lang ako." It's the official verb for JOMO (Joy of Missing Out). It can also be a bit sad, like when you volunteer to be the one left behind. "Okay lang, mauna na kayo, paiwan ako." *cries internally*
usage_notes: A reflexive-like verb where the subject allows the action of 'being left' to happen to them.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **paiwan** sa probinsya habang nagbabakasyon sila sa siyudad.","translation":"I want to **stay behind** in the province while they vacation in the city."},{"sentence":"Nagdesisyon siyang **paiwan** upang alagaan ang kanilang maysakit na ina.","translation":"He decided to **be left behind** to take care of their sick mother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino para sa isang mamamayan ng Pilipinas o isang taong may lahing Pilipino. Ang pambabaeng katumbas nito ay "Pinay".
etymology: A colloquial contraction of "Pilipino", with the "-oy" suffix being a common diminutive in Tagalog. Popularized in the 1920s by Filipino immigrants in the United States.
original_explanation: The unofficial, but universally understood, nickname for a Filipino. It's a term of endearment and pride. 'Pinoy' pride is that feeling you get when a foreigner knows adobo, or when Manny Pacquiao wins a fight, or when a Filipino artist gets international recognition. It's us.
usage_notes: "Pinoy" is the masculine or general term. "Pinay" is used for females.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipagmalaki ang pagiging isang tunay na **Pinoy**.","translation":"Be proud of being a true **Filipino**."},{"sentence":"Ang **Pinoy** Big Brother ay isang sikat na palabas sa telebisyon.","translation":"**Pinoy** Big Brother is a famous television show."}]

translation: to deny; to disown; to renounce
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtanggi o hindi pagkilala sa isang bagay, tao, o paniniwala na dati nang kinikilala o inaangkin.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa ng ex mo noong tinanong ng nanay niya kung kayo pa ba. Biglang "Sino po? Hindi ko po kilala 'yan." Ouch. It's to disown or deny something or someone, like Peter denying Jesus three times, but make it about chismis.
usage_notes: A more formal and intense version of 'itanggi'. It implies a deeper level of rejection or betrayal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking kasalanan ang **magtatwa** sa sariling magulang.","translation":"It is a great sin to **disown** one's own parents."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **magtatwa** ng iyong mga responsibilidad bilang isang mamamayan.","translation":"Do not **renounce** your responsibilities as a citizen."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matanda at mayaman na babae na nagbibigay ng suportang pinansyal o mga mamahaling regalo sa isang mas batang karelasyon, karaniwan ay isang lalaki.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na slang na 'sugar mommy'.
original_explanation: The female counterpart of the sugar daddy. She's the Tita who's not just 'of Manila' but 'pays for Manila'. She'll fund your startup, buy you a condo, and give you a black credit card. The ultimate 'girl boss' who invests in... well, younger assets.
usage_notes: Slang na termino, ang pambabaeng bersyon ng 'sugar daddy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang guwapong binata ay tila may **sugar mommy** na laging kasama sa mga mamahaling restaurant.","translation":"The handsome young man seems to have a **sugar mommy** who's always with him at expensive restaurants."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang makahanap ng **sugar mommy** para hindi na magtrabaho.","translation":"His dream is to find a **sugar mommy** so he doesn't have to work anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng matinding pagkapagod sa pag-iisip, na nagreresulta sa kawalan ng pokus at enerhiya para sa mga gawaing mental.
original_explanation: Ito yung feeling mo after ng 8-hour Zoom meeting na puro salita pero walang nangyari. O after mong mag-explain sa nanay mo for the 10th time kung paano gumamit ng Facebook. You're not sleepy, you're not physically tired, pero yung utak mo, nag-file na ng resignation letter.
usage_notes: This is an English phrase commonly used in Taglish conversations. The direct Tagalog translation 'pagod ang isip' is also used but 'mentally drained' is more common in urban/professional settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe, **mentally drained** na ako sa trabaho ngayong linggo.","translation":"Wow, I'm so **mentally drained** from work this week."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo muna akong kausapin, **mentally drained** ako sa exam.","translation":"Don't talk to me for a bit, I'm **mentally drained** from the exam."}]

translation: to toast (something); to pan-fry without oil
meaning_filipino: Lutuin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay sa isang mainit na kawali nang walang mantika.
original_explanation: This is the command form. It's what your lola yells from the living room while watching her teleserye: '**Sangagin** mo na 'yung bawang!' (Toast the garlic now!). It's the action you take to turn plain old rice into glorious sinangag, or pale peanuts into a crunchy snack. It's the culinary technique of applying dry heat to achieve maximum flavor potential.
usage_notes: An object-focus verb. The thing being toasted is the focus of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong sunugin ang bawang na **sinasangag** mo.","translation":"Don't burn the garlic you are **toasting**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **sangagin** ang mga mani bago ito durugin.","translation":"You need to **toast** the peanuts before crushing them."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang alinman sa limang bahagi na karaniwang matatagpuan sa dulo ng kamay o paa ng tao at ibang mga bertebrado.
original_explanation: Your body's built-in tools for typing "hahaha" without actually laughing, pointing at the chismis, and swiping right on Tinder. Also used for getting the last bit of sauce from a plate. We specify "daliri sa kamay" (finger) or "daliri sa paa" (toe) if we need to be clear, but usually, context is king.
usage_notes: While it can mean both finger and toe, it more commonly refers to fingers unless specified as "daliri sa paa" (toe).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahiwa niya ang kanyang **daliri** habang nagluluto.","translation":"She cut her **finger** while cooking."},{"sentence":"May limang **daliri** tayo sa bawat paa.","translation":"We have five **toes** on each foot."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay o magpaabot ng pasasalamat sa isang tao dahil sa isang bagay na ginawa o ibinigay.
original_explanation: After a successful team project, you treat everyone to lunch. It's your way to **pasalamatan** them for not leaving you on 'seen' during crunch time. It's the corporate love language.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **pasalamatan** ang lahat ng tumulong sa akin.","translation":"I want to **thank** everyone who helped me."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **pasalamatan** ang iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Don't forget to **thank** your parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagbibihis ng damit sa isang tao o bagay.
etymology: From 'damit' (clothes) + '-an' (verb suffix indicating action upon an object).
original_explanation: What you do to a baby, a toddler, or a Barbie doll. It's the act of putting clothes on someone (or something) who can't do it themselves. 'Damitan mo na yung bata, aalis na tayo!' is a classic parent line.
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the person/thing being dressed, not the clothes. Contrast with 'magdamit' (to wear clothes, to dress oneself).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **damitan** ang manika.","translation":"Help me **dress** the doll."},{"sentence":"**Damitan** mo na ang kapatid mo at malamig sa labas.","translation":"**Put clothes on** your sibling, it's cold outside."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tunog na malutong at sunod-sunod, tulad ng pag-aapoy ng tuyong kahoy, pagyapak sa tuyong dahon, o pagprito ng malutong na pagkain.
original_explanation: Imagine stepping on a giant bag of chicharon, or the sound of your hair after using a super strong hairspray. It's that ASMR-like sound of something dry and crispy breaking. It's also the sound your joints make when you stand up too fast after a long Netflix binge.
usage_notes: This is an onomatopoeic word, meaning the word itself imitates the sound it describes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **langasngas** ng mga tuyong dahon sa aking paglakad.","translation":"I heard the **rustling sound** of the dry leaves as I walked."},{"sentence":"Ang **langasngas** ng nilulutong lechon kawali ay nakakagutom.","translation":"The **crackling sound** of the lechon kawali being cooked is appetizing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpilipit o pagbaluktot ng katawan nang paulit-ulit, karaniwang dahil sa sakit, hirap, o matinding damdamin.
original_explanation: That awkward dance you do when you really, really have to pee but the meeting is still ongoing. Or when you eat something super spicy and you're trying to play it cool, but your insides are having a fiesta. It's the body's involuntary reaction to extreme discomfort or pain.
usage_notes: The repetition in 'pili-pilipit' emphasizes the continuous, repeated nature of the writhing or squirming motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **magpapili-pilipit** sa sahig dahil sa matinding sakit ng tiyan.","translation":"He started to **writhe** on the floor because of intense stomach pain."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpapili-pilipit** diyan, sabihin mo na kung ano ang problema.","translation":"Don't just **squirm** there, just say what the problem is."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging tuliro, litó, o pansamantalang nawala sa sarili dahil sa pagkabigla o pagkalito.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'ma-' at salitang ugat na 'tanga' (stupid, dumb).
original_explanation: That moment when your brain just blue-screens. You're not necessarily 'tanga' (stupid), but something just happened that made you go AFK mentally. It's when someone asks you a simple question and you just stare blankly, processing... processing... still processing. Parang na-lag ang utak mo.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang reaksyon sa isang biglaang pangyayari. Mas tumutukoy sa isang estado kaysa sa isang permanenteng katangian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Natanga** ako sa biglaang tanong ng guro.","translation":"I was **dumbfounded** by the teacher's sudden question."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng larong pambata kung saan may isang taya (ang lawin) na sumusubok humuli sa ibang manlalaro (mga sisiw) na prinoprotektahan ng isa pang manlalaro (ang inahin).
etymology: From 'lawin' (hawk), with reduplication and '-an' suffix, meaning "to play hawk" or "hawk-like".
original_explanation: A classic Pinoy childhood game, the OG version of tag. There's a 'mother hen' (inahin) protecting her 'chicks' (sisiw) from a 'hawk' (lawin). It's pure chaos, screaming, and running. It can also refer to a kite that looks like a hawk.
usage_notes: The game is also called 'Lawin at Sisiw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglaro ng **lawin-lawinan** ang mga bata sa plasa.","translation":"The children played the **hawk-and-chick game** at the plaza."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ayos o tindig ng katawan; ang paraan ng pagkilos o pagpapakita ng sarili na nagpapahiwatig ng saloobin o katayuan.
etymology: Likely from Spanish 'hacer' (to do/make), as in 'hacer un gesto' (to make a gesture), which was adapted and shortened.
original_explanation: It's the vibe you give off just by standing there. 'Asta-mayaman' is pretending you can afford everything at the Greenbelt boutique. 'Asta-matapang' is walking through a dark 'eskinita' like you own the place, even if you're secretly about to cry. It's your body language's loud-and-clear statement.
usage_notes: Often used with a descriptor, like 'asta-mayaman' (rich-person posture) or 'asta-maton' (thug-like bearing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **asta** lang 'yan na matapang pero mabait 'yan.","translation":"Don't worry, that's just a tough **demeanor**, but he's actually kind."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa **asta** niya na galing siya sa hirap at nagsikap.","translation":"You can see in his **bearing** that he came from poverty and worked hard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na nag-uugnay sa naunang pahayag bilang sanhi ng kasunod na resulta o konklusyon.
original_explanation: This is the verbal equivalent of the 'therefore' (∴) symbol in math. It's the pivot point in an argument. 'The project is due tomorrow, and you haven't started. Dahil dito, you're not going out tonight.' It’s the phrase that connects the problem to the inevitable, often unpleasant, consequence. It's the 'and that's why...' of Tagalog.
usage_notes: A common transitional phrase in formal writing and speech to show cause and effect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang ulan at bumabaha na sa kalsada; **dahil dito**, kanselado ang mga klase.","translation":"The rain is heavy and the streets are already flooding; **because of this**, classes are cancelled."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nanalo sa kompetisyon. **Dahil dito**, siya ang kakatawan sa bansa.","translation":"She won the competition. **Therefore**, she will represent the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang haba ng panahon o espasyo; kalawakan o katagalan ng isang bagay, pangyayari, o panahon.
original_explanation: This is that feeling when the meeting could have been an email. The *kalawigan* is the unnecessary length, the "OMG, how long is this gonna take?" vibe. It can also refer to a vast, open space, like the ocean. It's about stretchiness, whether in time or space.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary word. "Katagalan" is more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **kalawigan** ng panahon, unti-unting naghilom ang kanyang mga sugat.","translation":"In the **duration** of time, his wounds gradually healed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mababaw; kakulangan sa lalim ng isip, damdamin, o kaalaman. Maaari ding tumukoy sa pisikal na kababawan ng tubig.
original_explanation: When someone's life goals are just for the 'gram, or they only care about looks and clout. It's the "I-can't-even" attitude towards serious issues. Also, literally, it's the part of the swimming pool where you can stand up and not drown. So it can be a good thing, or a 'hugot' thing.
usage_notes: Used both literally for physical depth (e.g., of water) and metaphorically for intellectual or emotional depth. The metaphorical sense is more common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Manatili ka lang sa **kababawan** ng pool kung hindi ka marunong lumangoy.","translation":"Just stay in the **shallow part** of the pool if you don't know how to swim."},{"sentence":"Ayoko sa mga taong puro **kababawan** lang ang alam sa buhay.","translation":"I don't like people who only know **superficiality** in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsunod sa isang utos, batas, regulasyon, o kahilingan nang walang pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: This is your BPO agent voice: "**Pagtalima** sa company policy." It's the opposite of being 'pasaway'. It’s what your parents expect when they give you an order. It's following the rules, toeing the line, and doing what you're told. Very formal, very official-sounding.
usage_notes: A formal word, often used in legal, military, or official contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagtalima** sa mga batas trapiko para sa kaligtasan ng lahat.","translation":"**Adherence** to traffic laws is important for everyone's safety."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng gayuma o mahiwagang paraan upang akitin o paibigin ang isang tao.
original_explanation: When someone is so head-over-heels for a person that everyone else thinks is a bad choice, the chismosa in the corner will whisper, "Nako, parang ginayuma." It's the mythical explanation for a love that defies logic, like you've been hit by a love potion from a Filipino folklore albularyo.
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense) of the verb. It is often used hyperbolically to describe intense attraction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang tingin pa lang, tila ba **gumayuma** ang kanyang mga mata sa binata.","translation":"With just one look, it was as if her eyes had **charmed** the young man."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa kwento, **gumayuma** ang diwata upang walang sinumang makapasok sa kanyang kagubatan.","translation":"According to the story, the fairy **cast a spell** so that no one could enter her forest."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na puno; sobra sa kapasidad ng lulan o karga.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung level up ng "kargada." 'Yung balikbayan box na kailangan mo pang upuan para lang maisara. 'Yung bus na pa-probinsya tuwing Holy Week. 'Yung utak mo after a whole day of meetings. Kargadung-kargado lahat 'yan.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng kasobrahan o pagiging sukdulan ng pagkarga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kargadung-kargado** ang jeep kaya hindi na kami sumakay.","translation":"The jeep was **overloaded**, so we didn't get on anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o kilos ng pagpunta muli sa isang lugar, estado, o kondisyon na pinanggalingan.
original_explanation: This is the 'sana all' ng mga LDR couples at OFWs. It’s also the action ng ex mong biglang nag-chat ng 'hi' after months of silence. Pwedeng pagbabalik sa probinsya (balikbayan), pagbabalik ng sukli (keep the change!), o pagbabalik sa dati (throwback).
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin bilang salitang-ugat para sa maraming pandiwa at pangngalan na may kaugnayan sa pagbabalik, tulad ng `bumalik` (to return), `ibalik` (to return something), `balikan` (to return to someone/something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaabangan ko ang iyong pag-**balik**.","translation":"I am waiting for your **return**."},{"sentence":"Ang **balik**-aral ay mahalaga bago ang pagsusulit.","translation":"A **review** (return-study) is important before the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Kawalan ng katarungan o pagiging patas; isang gawain na lumalabag sa karapatan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Ito yung feeling na mas mataas ang grade ng kaklase mong nangopya lang sa'yo. O kaya yung na-promote yung kasama mo sa office na laging pa-kape-kape lang habang ikaw, pagod sa OT. It's the universe screaming, 'That's not fair!'
usage_notes: Ang unlaping 'in-' ay nagpapahiwatig ng pagkakait o kawalan ng salitang ugat na 'hustisya' (justice).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **inhustisya** ang nangyari sa kanya.","translation":"A great **injustice** happened to him."},{"sentence":"Lumalaban sila kontra sa **inhustisya** sa lipunan.","translation":"They are fighting against social **injustice**."}]

translation: to be carried away by a current
meaning_filipino: Madala o matangay ng agos ng tubig o anumang likido.
original_explanation: Literally, what happens to your tsinelas in a flood. Figuratively, it’s you getting carried away by your feelings ('nagpaanod sa emosyon'), by a trend, or by a juicy piece of chismis. 'Go with the flow' taken to its most literal and sometimes disastrous conclusion.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for objects in water and figuratively for emotions or influence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bahay ang **naanod** ng malakas na baha.","translation":"Many houses were **carried away** by the strong flood."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpaanod** sa masamang impluwensya ng iyong mga kaibigan.","translation":"Don't let yourself **be carried away** by the bad influence of your friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o katangian ng pagiging ulol; isang gawain o pahayag na walang katuturan, katawa-tawa, o labas sa matinong pag-iisip.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping 'ka-', salitang-ugat na 'ulol' (baliw, sira-ulo), at hulaping '-an', na tumutukoy sa kalagayan o gawain ng pagiging ulol.
original_explanation: This is the official term for 'kalokohan' when you're trying to sound smart or extra angry. It's the 'WTF moment' you have when you see someone's questionable life choices on social media. 'Tigilan mo na 'yang kaululan mo!' is the classic parent-to-teenager line that means 'Stop your nonsense!'
usage_notes: This is a strong, derogatory term. While 'ulol' is a direct insult to a person, 'kaululan' refers to the act or state of foolishness itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano na namang **kaululan** ang pinaggagawa ninyo?","translation":"What **foolishness** are you up to again?"},{"sentence":"Puro **kaululan** ang laman ng isip ng taong iyan.","translation":"That person's mind is full of **craziness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Uumpisahan pa lamang ang isang gawain, pangyayari, o proseso sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The future tense of "start." It’s the promise of a new beginning, whether it’s the concert that’s "about to start," the class that **will start** in 5 minutes, or the diet that **will start**... tomorrow. For sure. Promise.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of 'magsimula'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magsisimula** ang palabas sa loob ng limang minuto.","translation":"The show **will start** in five minutes."},{"sentence":"Bukas pa ako **magsisimula** sa aking bagong trabaho.","translation":"I **will start** my new job tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paglipas ng mahabang panahon; sa huli.
etymology: From ma- + laon + -an. 'Laon' means old or of long standing.
original_explanation: This is that feeling when you're waiting for your Shopee/Lazada order. You know it's coming, just not today, maybe not tomorrow, but malaunan, it will arrive. It's the 'in due time' of life, the universe's way of saying, 'Chill ka lang, darating din 'yan.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe an outcome that happens after a significant passage of time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Malaunan**, natutunan din niyang magpatawad.","translation":"**Eventually**, she also learned to forgive."},{"sentence":"Tiyak na magtatagumpay ka rin **malaunan** kung hindi ka susuko.","translation":"You will surely succeed **after a long time** if you don't give up."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng keso na malambot, puti, at medyo maalat, na karaniwang gawa mula sa gatas ng kalabaw. Ito ay isang lokal na espesyalidad sa ilang lalawigan tulad ng Laguna at Bulacan.
original_explanation: The Philippines' answer to mozzarella or feta. This is our local, artisanal white cheese, traditionally made from carabao's milk. It's soft, slightly salty, and often wrapped in banana leaves. Perfect when paired with hot pandesal and a cup of coffee. It's the kind of breakfast that makes you feel nostalgic and proud of local produce.
usage_notes: A specific type of unaged, soft white cheese native to the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap na almusal ang mainit na pandesal na may palamang **kesong puti**.","translation":"Hot pandesal with **white cheese** filling is a delicious breakfast."},{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng sariwang **kesong puti** mula sa Laguna.","translation":"We bought fresh **white cheese** from Laguna."}]

translation: to become thick; to become viscous
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng isang likido tungo sa pagiging malapot o mas makapal ang konsistensiya.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'mang-' at ang salitang-ugat na 'lapot' (thickness/viscosity). Nagaganap ang asimilasyon.
original_explanation: This is what happens to the gravy when you let it simmer, the chismis when more details are added, or the traffic on EDSA at 5 PM. 'Manlapot' is the process of thickening. It's that perfect, rich consistency you want in your kare-kare sauce, but the absolute worst thing for your morning commute.
usage_notes: Primarily used in cooking to describe sauces, soups, or liquids thickening. The past tense is 'nanlapot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Haluin mo ang sarsa hanggang sa ito ay **manlapot**.","translation":"Stir the sauce until it **thickens**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa lamig, **nanlapot** ang tsokolate.","translation":"Because of the cold, the chocolate **thickened**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing makintab o maningning ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagpahid o pagkuskos.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your shoes before a job interview, the silverware before Noche Buena, or your car before a date. It's the act of buffing something until it reflects your own proud, smiling face. It's the verb form of "✨sparkle✨".
usage_notes: A very specific verb for making something lustrous.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **pakinangin** ang sahig na kahoy.","translation":"Help me **polish** the wooden floor."},{"sentence":"Kanyang **pinakinang** ang mga tropeo na napanalunan niya.","translation":"He **shined** the trophies that he had won."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng yerba (herb) na may maliliit at mababangong dahon, karaniwang ginagamit bilang pampalasa sa pagluluto, lalo na sa mga lutuing Kanluranin.
original_explanation: That fancy-smelling plant you buy in a tiny, expensive packet at the supermarket to make your roasted chicken feel more 'continental.' You probably can't tell its taste apart from rosemary or oregano, but the recipe video said to add thyme, so you obey. It's the 'pang-sosyal' version of dahon ng sibuyas.
usage_notes: Used in culinary contexts, especially for Western dishes. The English pronunciation is retained.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdagdag ka ng kaunting **thyme** sa manok bago ito isalang sa oven.","translation":"Add a little **thyme** to the chicken before putting it in the oven."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makina para sa paglilimbag ng teksto o larawan; maaari ring tumukoy sa lugar o pagawaan kung saan ginagawa ang paglilimbag.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung lolo ng printer mo. Dito ginagawa 'yung mga libro, diyaryo, at posters bago pa nauso ang digital. Kung may business ka at kailangan mo ng 1,000 flyers, sa **imprenta** ka pupunta, hindi sa home printer mo unless gusto mong maubos ang ink at pasensya mo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala niya ang mga manuskrito sa **imprenta** para mailathala bilang libro.","translation":"He brought the manuscripts to the **printing press** to be published as a book."},{"sentence":"Nagpagawa kami ng mga imbitasyon sa isang **imprenta** sa Recto.","translation":"We had invitations made at a **print shop** in Recto."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o gusali na may partikular na layunin, tulad ng hintuan ng tren o bus, himpilan ng pulisya, o pasilidad para sa brodkasting.
original_explanation: Your stop. Can be the train station (MRT/LRT), the bus station in Cubao, the police station where you get a blotter, or the radio station playing your breakup songs (Love Radio, anyone?). It's a designated point for stopping, waiting, or operating.
usage_notes: Ang pagbigkas ay /is-ta-SYON/, hindi /is-TEY-shon/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **istasyon** ng tren sa may Taft Avenue.","translation":"Let's meet at the train **station** near Taft Avenue."},{"sentence":"Tumawag ka sa pinakamalapit na **istasyon** ng pulis.","translation":"Call the nearest police **station**."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumilos sa paraang mapaglaro, kaakit-akit, o may pahiwatig ng romantikong interes upang makuha ang atensyon ng iba.
original_explanation: The art of 'pabebe' waves and subtle hair flips. It's that thing you do when your crush walks by. Before DMs, there was the masterful art of the 'pamaypay' and stolen glances. Now it's sending memes and reacting with the right emoji. The game has changed, but the goal is the same.
usage_notes: Can have a playful or sometimes negative connotation, depending on the context and intent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maglandi** sa opisina, hindi ito ang tamang lugar.","translation":"Don't **flirt** in the office, this is not the right place for it."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan siya ng kanyang kaibigan na subukang **maglandi** nang kaunti para mapansin.","translation":"Her friend told her to try **to flirt** a little to get noticed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag ng intensyon na magdulot ng pinsala, sakit, o kaparusahan bilang paghihiganti o pamimilit.
original_explanation: This is what your boss gives you when they say "I need this EOD," what your mom gives you with "Umuwi ka nang maaga kundi...", or what the dark clouds signal before a downpour. It’s the vibe check before something bad happens. Parang 'yung "we need to talk" message from your jowa—a clear and present banta to your peace of mind.
usage_notes: Can refer to a verbal threat, a physical sign of danger, or an abstract risk.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng **banta** sa kanyang buhay kaya nagtago siya.","translation":"He received a **threat** on his life so he went into hiding."},{"sentence":"Ang pagbabago ng klima ay isang malaking **banta** sa ating planeta.","translation":"Climate change is a huge **threat** to our planet."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nanghihinayang; ginagawa o ibinibigay nang buong-puso at walang anumang pagsisisi.
original_explanation: That feeling when you spend your whole sahod on a K-pop concert ticket and you're like, 'Worth it!' You do something with no regrets, kahit mag-instant noodles ka pa for the rest of the month.
usage_notes: Can describe a person's attitude or the manner in which an action is done (adverbially).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Walang-hinayang** niyang ibinigay ang lahat ng kanyang naipon para sa operasyon ng kapatid.","translation":"He **unsparingly** gave all his savings for his sibling's operation."},{"sentence":"Kahit mahal, binili ko ang libro dahil alam kong **walang-hinayang** ako.","translation":"Even though it was expensive, I bought the book because I knew I would have **no regrets**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng simetria; pagkakaroon ng magkatumbas o balanseng mga bahagi sa magkabilang panig ng isang sentral na linya o punto.
original_explanation: This is your crush's face, where the left side is a perfect mirror of the right. It's the butterfly's wings. It's that feeling of satisfaction when you fold a piece of paper perfectly in half. In design, it's pleasing to the eye. In kilay, it's the ultimate goal: 'Kilay is life, dapat may-simetria!'
usage_notes: A technical term used in art, mathematics, science, and aesthetics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang disenyo ng lumang simbahan ay **may-simetria** at talagang kahanga-hanga.","translation":"The design of the old church is **symmetrical** and truly admirable."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilubog at hayaan ang isang bagay sa likido, tulad ng tubig o sarsa, sa loob ng isang takdang panahon.
original_explanation: The secret to any good Pinoy BBQ. You "ibabad" the pork in a mix of soy sauce, calamansi, and banana ketchup. It's also what you do with your feet in a basin of warm water after a long day, or what happens to your brain after binge-watching a K-drama series for 12 hours straight. You're just soaking in it.
usage_notes: Primarily used in cooking and cleaning contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **ibabad** ang manok sa toyo't kalamansi.","translation":"Don't forget to **marinate** the chicken in soy sauce and calamansi."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **ibabad** ang mga puting damit sa bleach para pumuti.","translation":"You need to **soak** the white clothes in bleach to whiten them."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa estado ng mahigpit na paghawak o pagkapit sa isang bagay upang hindi mahulog o mawalay.
original_explanation: Parang ikaw sa jeep kapag siksikan at biglang preno. Nakakapit ka sa bakal for dear life. Pwede ring sa relasyon, 'yung kahit toxic na, nakakapit ka pa rin. Kapit-bisig!
usage_notes: Describes the state of holding on tightly. Often used figuratively for emotional attachment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bata ay mahigpit na **nakakapit** sa kamay ng kanyang ina.","translation":"The child is tightly **clinging** to his mother's hand."},{"sentence":"Kahit sa huling hibla ng pag-asa, siya ay **nakakapit**.","translation":"Even to the last thread of hope, she is **holding on**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging masikap, masigasig, at mapursigi sa isang gawain o layunin.
original_explanation: This is your energy level when you're trying to impress your crush's parents, a new boss, or when you're the first one to line up for a seat sale. It's the 'sipsip' energy but for a noble cause... most of the time. The quality of being a 'masugid na tagahanga' (ardent fan).
usage_notes: Often used to describe a follower, a student, or a worker who shows great dedication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkamasugid** niya sa pag-aaral ay nagbunga ng matataas na marka.","translation":"Her **diligence** in studying resulted in high grades."},{"sentence":"Hinangaan ng lahat ang **pagkamasugid** ng mga boluntaryo sa pagtulong sa mga nasalanta.","translation":"Everyone admired the **zealousness** of the volunteers in helping the victims of the calamity."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng pagkainip o kawalan ng interes dahil sa walang ginagawa o dahil sa paulit-ulit na gawain.
original_explanation: This is the official feeling of a long weekend with no plans and no internet. It's the Sunday afternoon slump, the "ghost month" sa office, or being stuck in a Zoom meeting that could have been an email. Kabagutan is when you've scrolled through all your social media feeds and still have nothing to do. The enemy of the productive, the best friend of "sana all may jowa."
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'pagkabagot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para malabanan ang **kabagutan**, naghanap siya ng bagong libangan.","translation":"To fight **boredom**, he looked for a new hobby."},{"sentence":"Ang **kabagutan** sa trabaho ay maaaring magdulot ng pagbaba ng produktibidad.","translation":"The **boredom** at work can lead to a decrease in productivity."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng isang sulatin o teksto na binubuo ng isa o higit pang pangungusap na tumatalakay sa isang partikular na punto o ideya.
original_explanation: In school, this was the block of text your teacher told you to write about your summer vacation. In work emails, it's that giant wall of text from your boss that you have to read three times to understand. "TL;DR" was invented because of very long "parapos". Pro-tip: use paragraphs to make your long "chika" on Messenger easier to read.
usage_notes: A standard academic and literary term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Basahin ang unang **parapo** ng kuwento.","translation":"Read the first **paragraph** of the story."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat **parapo** ay dapat may pangunahing ideya.","translation":"Each **paragraph** must have a main idea."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap o utos na tanggapin ang isang bagay, o ipatanggap ito sa iba.
original_explanation: The verbal equivalent of holding out a gift and saying "Here, take it!" It's what you say when you're trying to give someone something, from a simple pasalubong to a project you're delegating. "Patanggap mo naman 'to kay boss." It’s the polite way to make sure something gets received.
usage_notes: Often used with 'paki-' to be more polite (`pakipatanggap`). It's a causative command, meaning you're asking someone to cause something to be accepted, either by them or a third party.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patanggap** mo na itong maliit na regalo.","translation":"**Please accept** this small gift."},{"sentence":"**Patanggap** mo ang sulat na ito sa sekretarya.","translation":"**Have** the secretary **accept** this letter."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng pagsang-ayon o pagpayag sa isang mungkahi, opinyon, o pasya.
original_explanation: The verb for when the squad finally decides on where to eat, or when your parents actually approve of your life choices. It's the "O, sige na nga" moment, but in its formal, past-tense form. It's the opposite of what happens in most online comment sections.
usage_notes: This is the completed (past tense) actor-focus form. 'Pumayag' is a close synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumang-ayon** ang lahat ng miyembro sa bagong patakaran.","translation":"All the members **agreed** to the new rule."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **sumang-ayon** din siyang sumama sa aming lakad.","translation":"Finally, she **agreed** to join our trip."}]

translation: to solicit a response, to have someone reply
meaning_filipino: Humingi o maghintay ng sagot o reaksyon mula sa isang tao o grupo.
original_explanation: That feeling when you send a risky meme to the group chat and you wait for someone to react. You're trying to `magpatugon`. It's like posting "thoughts?" on social media or asking "ok ka lang?" to a friend who is clearly not okay, hoping they'll open up.
usage_notes: A less common word, often found in more formal or literary writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpadala siya ng liham upang **magpatugon** sa kanyang mga katanungan.","translation":"He sent a letter to **solicit a response** to his questions."},{"sentence":"Ang guro ay nagtanong upang **magpatugon** ng mga ideya mula sa mga mag-aaral.","translation":"The teacher asked a question to **elicit a response** of ideas from the students."}]

translation: to cause to stutter; to pretend to stutter
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasanhi sa isang tao na magsalita nang may pag-aatubili at pag-uulit ng mga pantig; maaari ring tumukoy sa sinasadyang paggaya sa pagsasalitang utal.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your crush suddenly talks to you and your brain short-circuits. Or, it's what a teleserye character does to act innocent or scared. "Nagpautal-utal siya sa pagsagot para hindi siya paghinalaan."
usage_notes: Can mean either to cause someone else to stutter (due to fear, surprise) or to feign stuttering oneself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang tanong ng guro ay **nagpautal-utal** sa estudyante.","translation":"The teacher's sudden question **caused the student to stutter**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpautal-utal** diyan, sabihin mo na ang totoo.","translation":"Don't **stammer** there, just tell the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Angkop o napapanahon; tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nangyayari, magagamit, o masagana sa isang partikular na panahon o yugto.
original_explanation: This is the Tagalog for "in season." When mangoes are everywhere and cheap, they're `sa-panahon`. When it's rainy season and everyone's getting the flu, the flu is `sa-panahon`. It can also mean 'timely' or 'fashionable'. "Yang OOTD mo, hindi na 'yan sa-panahon, 'teh!"
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga prutas, gulay, o sakit na dumarating sa partikular na season.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mura ang mangga ngayon dahil **sa-panahon** ito.","translation":"Mangoes are cheaper now because they are **in season**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangatnig na nag-uugnay ng dalawang magkaibang pagpipilian o alternatibong ideya. Ito ay pinaikling anyo ng 'o kaya ay'.
original_explanation: This is the formal, slightly dramatic cousin of 'o'. It's what you use when you're presenting two equally serious options, like choosing between two job offers or deciding whether to unfriend an ex 'o kaya'y' i-block na lang for good. It adds a little bit of flair to your indecisiveness.
usage_notes: Isang mas pormal o pampanitikang alternatibo sa simpleng 'o' (or).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pwede kang mag-aral nang mabuti, **o kaya'y** magsisi ka sa huli.","translation":"You can study well, **or else** you will regret it in the end."},{"sentence":"Manatili tayong tahimik, **o kaya'y** umalis na lang tayo rito.","translation":"Let's remain quiet, **or rather**, let's just leave this place."}]

translation: to go overseas; to cross the sea
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakbay sa ibayo ng dagat, karaniwang tumutukoy sa pagpunta sa ibang bansa para magtrabaho o manirahan.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal of many Filipinos, second only to getting a visa. This is the act of becoming an OFW, a balikbayan, or just someone going on a much-needed beach trip to another island. It's literally "to cross the sea," but emotionally, it means seeking better opportunities or just a really good vacation.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipino ang nangangarap na **magtawid-dagat** para sa kanilang pamilya.","translation":"Many Filipinos dream of **going overseas** for their family."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magtawid-dagat** at magtrabaho sa Canada.","translation":"She decided to **cross the sea** and work in Canada."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pambihirang lakas na karaniwang iniuugnay sa mga kalalakihan; pisikal na puwersa na hindi gaanong gumagamit ng isip o estratehiya.
original_explanation: Literally "man-strength." This is what you call the power needed for tasks like opening a ridiculously tight jar lid (bubuksan ng de-lakas-lalaki), moving heavy furniture, or any situation where you just need to apply pure, unadulterated muscle. It often implies using force over finesse.
usage_notes: Isang tambalang pang-uri. Maaaring magkaroon ng bahagyang negatibong konotasyon na kawalan ng pagpipino o paggamit ng puwersa nang hindi nag-iisip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Idinaan na lang niya sa **lakas-lalaki** ang pagbukas ng nasirang pinto.","translation":"He just used **brute force** to open the broken door."},{"sentence":"Hindi lahat ng bagay ay nadadaan sa **lakas-lalaki**.","translation":"Not everything can be solved with **manly strength**."}]

translation: to put; to place; to assume
meaning_filipino: Ilagay o ipuwesto ang isang bagay sa isang partikular na lugar; o maniwala sa isang bagay bilang isang haka-haka o teorya.
original_explanation: This is a 2-for-1 verb! First, it means 'to put' or 'to place' something, like when your mom tells you where to put the groceries. Second, it means 'to assume' or 'to suppose'. "Magpalagay tayo na mananalo ka sa lotto..." (Let's assume you win the lotto...). It's about placing things, whether it's a vase on a table or an idea in your head.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context. 'Magpalagay ng...' usually means 'to put', while 'Magpalagay tayo...' means 'Let's assume...'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magpalagay** ka ng palamuti sa mesa.","translation":"**Place** some decoration on the table."},{"sentence":"**Magpalagay** tayo na totoo ang sinasabi niya, ano ang susunod na hakbang?","translation":"Let's **assume** what he's saying is true, what's the next step?"}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na maraming bulaklak, o sa pananalita na gumagamit ng malalalim at magagarang salita.
etymology: From ma- (adjective prefix indicating 'having much of') + bulaklak (flower).
original_explanation: Two meanings: 1) Literal, like your lola's garden na puno ng blooms. 2) Figurative, 'yung pananalita ng manliligaw mo noong unang panahon, puro "parang tala sa kalangitan ang iyong mga mata." Sobrang mabulaklak, parang speech sa pageant. Today, we call it "flattery" or "being extra."
usage_notes: Can be literal (full of flowers) or figurative (ornate, florid language).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hardin nila ay **mabulaklak** tuwing tagsibol.","translation":"Their garden is **full of flowers** during spring."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **mabulaklak** mong pananalita at sabihin mo na ang totoo.","translation":"Stop your **flowery** words and just tell the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkubli o pag-iwas na makita ng iba; maglagay ng sarili sa isang lugar na hindi madaling matagpuan.
original_explanation: Ginawa mo 'to nung bata ka 'pag naglalaro ng tagu-taguan. As an adult, ito 'yung ginagawa mo 'pag nakita mo sa mall 'yung inutangan mo. You **tumago** behind a mannequin. It's the act of making yourself disappear, at least for a moment.
usage_notes: This is an archaic or less common verb form for 'to hide'. The more common verb form is 'magtago'. 'Tumago' is the completed aspect (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumago** ang bata sa ilalim ng kama upang hindi siya makita.","translation":"The child **hid** under the bed so he would not be seen."},{"sentence":"Saan ka ba **tumago** kanina? Hinahanap kita.","translation":"Where did you **hide** earlier? I was looking for you."}]

translation: to pickle; to preserve in brine
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-iimbak ng pagkain, karaniwan ay isda, prutas o gulay, sa solusyon ng asin, suka, o iba pang pampaasim upang mapreserba at mabago ang lasa nito.
original_explanation: This is how we get atchara from papaya or 'burong isda'. You **magburo** something by letting it ferment in a salty or sour solution. It's also a metaphor for letting a problem or a grudge sit and fester. 'Huwag mo nang i-buro 'yan sa isip mo' (Don't let that fester in your mind).
usage_notes: Can refer to pickling vegetables ('atchara') or fermenting fish/shrimp with rice ('burong isda'/'balao-balao').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong ang nanay ko na **magburo** ng manggang hilaw.","translation":"My mother knows how to **pickle** unripe mangoes."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **magburo** ng isda sa kauna-unahang pagkakataon.","translation":"They tried to **preserve** fish in brine for the first time."}]

meaning_filipino: Magpakita ng kalungkutan o pighati dahil sa pagkamatay ng isang tao o pagkawala ng isang mahalagang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the feeling when your favorite K-drama ends, your go-to milk tea shop closes down, or, on a more serious note, when someone passes away. To **mourn** is to process a loss. It's the official dress code of wearing black and listening to sad songs on repeat.
usage_notes: Used to denote the act of mourning for a specific person or thing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang buong bayan ay nagtipon upang **ipagluksa** ang pagpanaw ng kanilang lider.","translation":"The entire town gathered to **mourn** the passing of their leader."},{"sentence":"Nararapat lamang na **ipagluksa** natin ang pagkawala ng ating kalayaan.","translation":"It is only right that we **mourn** the loss of our freedom."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng panitikan o pananalita na gumagamit ng ordinaryong wika at istrukturang pang-gramatika, taliwas sa tula na may sukat at tugma.
original_explanation: Ito yung normal na pagsusulat. Yung mga nobela, short stories, at kahit mga Facebook rants mo, prosa 'yan. Basically, any writing that isn't trying to be a poem for your crush. It's the "walang-halong-charot" form of writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas sanay siyang sumulat ng **prosa** kaysa sa tula.","translation":"She is more used to writing **prose** than poetry."},{"sentence":"Ang mga sanaysay ni Nick Joaquin ay halimbawa ng mahusay na **prosa**.","translation":"The essays of Nick Joaquin are examples of excellent **prose**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga organikong sustansya na kailangan ng katawan sa maliit na dami para sa normal na paglaki at kalusugan.
original_explanation: The stuff your mom tells you to take so you don't get sick. Whether it's from fruits, veggies, or that orange-flavored tablet you loved as a kid. Sa panahon ngayon, ang bitamina C ay parang holy grail. "Uminom ka na ba ng bitamina mo?" is the new "I love you."
usage_notes: A common household and medical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga prutas ay mayaman sa iba't ibang **bitamina**.","translation":"Fruits are rich in various **vitamins**."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ako ng doktor na uminom ng **bitamina** C araw-araw.","translation":"The doctor advised me to take **vitamin** C every day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng karne, karaniwang mula sa hita o balikat ng baboy, na pinreserba sa pamamagitan ng pag-aasin, pagpapatuyo, o pagpapausok.
original_explanation: The star of Noche Buena and the reason you have leftover sandwiches until New Year. It's that sweet and salty, pineapple-glazed goodness that makes Christmas feel like Christmas. Also known as 'jamón' in Spanish, but we just made it our own.
usage_notes: The pronunciation is key. Stress on the last syllable (/ha-MÓN/) means the food. Stress on the first syllable (/HA-mon/) means a challenge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang buong bola ng **hamon** para sa Pasko.","translation":"Mom bought a whole ball of **ham** for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Masarap gawing palaman sa pandesal ang natirang **hamon**.","translation":"Leftover **ham** is delicious as a filling for pandesal."}]

translation: there (far from both speaker and listener)
meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na pamatlig na tumutukoy sa isang lugar na malayo sa nagsasalita at sa kinakausap.
original_explanation: The more common, active version of 'doon'. It's your go-to word when pointing at something in the distance. 'Nasaan ang forever mo?' '**Andoon**, naghahanap pa ng iba.' (Where's your forever? Over **there**, still looking for someone else.) It's the location of your ex, your dreams, and the next available Grab car on a rainy Friday night.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit na kapalit ng 'nandoon'. Ang 'andoon' ay bahagyang mas nakatuon sa estado ng pagiging naroroon, habang ang 'nandoon' ay maaaring magpahiwatig ng pagdating o presensya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Andoon** sa kabilang kalsada ang Jollibee.","translation":"The Jollibee is **there** across the street."},{"sentence":"Tingnan mo, **andoon** na ang eroplanong sasakyan natin.","translation":"Look, our plane is **there** already."}]

translation: to have something listed; to enlist
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatala o paglalagay ng pangalan o anumang bagay sa isang listahan.
original_explanation: Yung moment na sinabi ng team leader mo, "Guys, palista na ng orders para sa milk tea," at biglang nag-vibrate ang buong office. It's the act of getting on a list, whether for food, attendance, or 'yung mga may utang sa'yo.
usage_notes: The prefix 'pa-' indicates a causative verb, meaning to cause or ask someone to do the action of the root word. Here, it means to ask someone to list something or to allow oneself to be listed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Palista** naman ng pangalan ko para sa raffle,\" sabi ni Ana.","translation":"Please **enlist** my name for the raffle,\" said Ana."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **palista** sa barangay para makakuha ng ayuda.","translation":"You need to **get listed** at the barangay to receive aid."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging magaslaw, bastos, o walang pinong pag-uugali; kawalan ng kapinuhan.
etymology: Nagmula sa "ka-ilap-an", kung saan ang 'ilap' ay tumutukoy sa pagiging mailap o hindi sanay sa tao. Ang unlaping 'ka-' at hulaping '-an' ay bumubuo ng pangngalan na nagsasaad ng isang katangian o kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of being "classy." Think of someone who tells green jokes at a funeral or chews with their mouth wide open on a first date. It's behavior that makes you cringe and say, "Walang modo." It’s the vibe of being uncivilized or unrefined.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang malalim at bihirang gamiting salita sa Tagalog. Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang mga kasingkahulugang 'kabastusan' o 'kagaslawan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi katanggap-tanggap sa pormal na pagtitipon ang gayong **kailapan** ng pananalita.","translation":"Such **crudeness** of speech is unacceptable at a formal gathering."},{"sentence":"Pinuna siya dahil sa **kailapan** ng kanyang mga kilos.","translation":"He was criticized for the **vulgarity** of his actions."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon na nagdudulot ng sagabal, istorbo, o perwisyo.
original_explanation: This is your neighbor's karaoke at 2 AM. It's that 'urgent' email from your boss at 10 PM. It's the slow internet when you're in a Zoom meeting. Anything that makes you say, 'Pwede ba, 'wag ngayon?' is nakaaabala. The ultimate vibe killer.
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective describing something ('nakaaabala ang ingay') or as a verb ('Nakaaabala ka sa pag-aaral ko'). The 'nakaa-' prefix indicates that the root word's action is what the subject is doing or causing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasensya na kung **nakaaabala** ako sa iyong pagpapahinga.","translation":"I'm sorry if I'm **disturbing** your rest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mapagkumbaba; ang hindi pagmamataas o pagiging mayabang sa kabila ng mga tagumpay o kakayahan.
etymology: From `kababaan` (lowness) + `ng` + `loob` (inner self, will). Literally "lowness of the inner self". The roots are 'baba' and 'loob'.
original_explanation: It's that rare trait of being a total rockstar at something but acting like you're still learning the ropes. It's when you win the lottery and still eat at the local carinderia. It's the opposite of the "flex lang nang flex" culture.
usage_notes: A highly valued Filipino trait, often associated with good character and respectfulness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinangaan siya ng lahat dahil sa kanyang **kababaang-loob**.","translation":"Everyone admired him for his **humility**."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng kanyang yaman, nanatili ang kanyang **kababaang-loob**.","translation":"Despite his wealth, his **modesty** remained."}]

translation: is panting; is out of breath
meaning_filipino: Nakakaranas ng mabilis at hirap na paghinga, karaniwang sanhi ng pagod, matinding ehersisyo, o kaba.
original_explanation: Yung state mo after habulin ang jeep, o 'yung puso mong humihingal sa kaba nung nakita mo si crush. Also, the sound of your wallet after a 12.12 sale. 'Habol-hininga' ang peg.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humihingal** ang aso pagkatapos naming maglaro ng habulan.","translation":"The dog **is panting** after we played catch."},{"sentence":"Tumatakbo siya nang mabilis kaya siya **humihingal** ngayon.","translation":"He ran fast, that's why he **is out of breath** now."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtitipon ng isang grupo ng mga tao sa isang lugar para sa isang partikular na layunin o okasyon.
original_explanation: This is what happens during family reunions, team buildings, or EDSA People Power. It's the act of coming together as a group. Think Noche Buena when all the titos, titas, and pinsans you haven't seen all year suddenly appear. It's the plural, more festive version of `magsamahan`. Let's magsama-sama for inuman later!
usage_notes: Involves reduplication of the root 'sama', which emphasizes the collective and group nature of the action. Implies a larger group than 'magsamahan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Pasko, ugali na ng aming pamilya na **magsama-sama** sa bahay ng lola.","translation":"Every Christmas, it's our family's tradition to **gather together** at grandma's house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang doktrina o pananaw na ang sariling kapakanan ang siyang pangunahing layunin at motibasyon ng lahat ng kilos.
original_explanation: This is the "-ism" for people who live by the motto "Me, myself, and I." It's the philosophy of being 'bida-bida' (the main character) in your own life, sometimes at the expense of others. It's less about being boastful (that's egotismo) and more about a deep-seated belief that your own interests are all that matter.
usage_notes: A more philosophical or psychological term than the more common "pagiging makasarili" (being selfish).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa pilosopiya ang konsepto ng **egoismo**.","translation":"The concept of **egoism** is studied in philosophy."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **egoismo** ang dahilan kung bakit wala siyang permanenteng kaibigan.","translation":"His **egoism** is the reason why he has no permanent friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang pang-ugnay na ginagamit sa paghahambing kung saan ang ikalawang paksa ay isang tiyak na tao na ipinakikilala ng panandang 'kay'.
etymology: Isang konstruksyong panggramatika na pinagsasama ang pang-ugnay na 'kaysa' at ang pantukoy na pantao na 'kay'.
original_explanation: This is the specific 'than' you use when the comparison gets personal. 'Mas magaling kumanta si Sarah G kaysa kay Regine.' You're not just comparing things, you're comparing *people*. This is the *marites*-level of comparison, perfect for debates about who's the better actor or who's your real best friend.
usage_notes: Eksklusibong ginagamit kapag ang inihahambing ay pangalan ng tao. Para sa mga pangngalang pambalana (hal. 'guro'), 'kaysa sa' ang ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas matangkad si Dave **kaysa kay** Michael.","translation":"Dave is taller **than** Michael."},{"sentence":"Bakit mas pinapaboran mo si Anna **kaysa kay** Maria?","translation":"Why do you favor Anna more **than** Maria?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kardinal na bilang na kasunod ng limampu't siyam at bago ang animnapu't isa; katumbas ng anim na sampu.
original_explanation: The magic number for senior citizen discounts. It's also the number of minutes in an hour you spend scrolling on TikTok when you should be working. In the palengke, it's what the tita haggles down to from an initial price of 'otsenta.'
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with the native Tagalog 'animnapu'. The Spanish-derived numbers are often preferred for prices, ages, and time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sesenta** pesos po ang isang kilo ng mangga.","translation":"One kilo of mangoes is **sixty** pesos."},{"sentence":"Magdiriwang na siya ng kanyang ika-**sesenta** kaarawan sa susunod na taon.","translation":"She will celebrate her **sixtieth** birthday next year."}]

translation: will do the laundry, will wash clothes
meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing kilos ng paglilinis ng mga damit at iba pang tela gamit ang tubig at sabon. Ito ay nasa panahunang panghinaharap.
etymology: Future tense of `maglaba`. Formed from `mag-` + repetition of the first syllable of the root `la` + `laba` (laundry).
original_explanation: The dreaded Sunday chore. "Maglalaba ako" is the battle cry before you face that mountain of dirty clothes. This is the future tense of `maglaba`. It means you're about to engage in the ancient art of kuskos (scrubbing), piga (wringing), and sampay (hanging to dry). Or, you know, just pushing a button on the washing machine.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb `maglaba` (to do laundry).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maglalaba** ako bukas dahil wala na akong malinis na damit.","translation":"I **will do the laundry** tomorrow because I have no clean clothes left."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **maglalaba** ng mga kurtina?","translation":"Who **will wash** the curtains?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, gusali, o silid kung saan isinasagawa ang mga gawaing pang-opisina, pang-negosyo, o administratibo. Isang mas pormal o lumang katawagan para sa tanggapan.
etymology: From pan- + tanggap + -an. A place for receiving (tanggap) people or business. A variant of 'tanggapan'.
original_explanation: This is the more formal, almost vintage, term for 'opisina' or 'tanggapan'. You'd probably hear this in a government documentary or from your lolo talking about his first job. It's the place where dreams of a 13th-month pay are made and where the coffee is either free or terrible.
usage_notes: Less common than 'tanggapan' or the loanword 'opisina'. It sounds more formal and slightly dated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas ang **pananggapan** ng munisipyo mula Lunes hanggang Biyernes.","translation":"The municipal **office** is open from Monday to Friday."},{"sentence":"Nagsumite siya ng kanyang mga dokumento sa **pananggapan** ng rehistrador.","translation":"He submitted his documents to the registrar's **office**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa takilya ng isang sinehan o teatro kung saan ibinebenta ang mga tiket. Ginagamit din ito upang ilarawan ang komersyal na tagumpay ng isang pelikula batay sa kinita nito.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Ingles na 'box office'.
original_explanation: This is the Tagalized 'box office'. It's where you line up to buy movie tickets, or more commonly now, the term you hear when a movie is a massive hit. 'Wow, **baks-opis** hit ang movie ni Kathryn!' It's the ultimate measure of whether a film is a blockbuster or a 'flop-buster'.
usage_notes: A direct loanword, used in entertainment and film contexts. Often used in phrases like 'baks-opis king/queen'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumila kami sa **baks-opis** para bumili ng tiket sa bagong pelikula.","translation":"We lined up at the **box office** to buy tickets for the new movie."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng pelikula niya ay tumatabo sa **baks-opis**.","translation":"All of his movies are hits at the **box office**."}]

meaning_filipino: Angkop, tugma, o bagay sa isa't isa, partikular na sa ugali, panlasa, o katangian.
original_explanation: This is your work bestie, your chismis buddy, the one who gets your weird sense of humor. 'Yung tipong, "Ay, kabagay kami niyan, pareho kaming ayaw sa maagang team huddle." It's about finding someone or something that just *clicks* with you, whether it's a person, a pair of shoes, or the last piece of siomai.
usage_notes: Often used to describe relationships, friendships, or items that go well together.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila talaga ang **kabagay** dahil pareho silang mahilig sa maanghang na pagkain.","translation":"They are really **compatible** because they both love spicy food."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **kabagay** ang boss ko, laging mainit ang ulo.","translation":"I'm not **compatible** with my boss, he's always hot-headed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang wikang natutuhan at ginagamit ng isang tao mula sa kanyang pagkabata; ang katutubong wika.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'ina' at 'wika', na tumutukoy sa 'mother language' o unang wika.
original_explanation: This is your first language, the one your nanay used to scold you or tell you to eat. It's the language you dream in, the one you use for 'chismis' with your childhood friends. Before you learned English for your BPO job, you were a master of your Inang-wika.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga talakayang akademiko at pampanitikan, lalo na tuwing 'Buwan ng Wika'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating pagyamanin at ipagmalaki ang ating **inang-wika**.","translation":"We should enrich and be proud of our **mother tongue**."},{"sentence":"Ang Filipino ang ating pambansang wika, ngunit marami sa atin ay may iba't ibang **inang-wika** tulad ng Cebuano o Ilokano.","translation":"Filipino is our national language, but many of us have different **mother tongues** like Cebuano or Ilocano."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago sa katangian, anyo, o kalagayan ng isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Sabi mo for your New Year's resolution: "This year, kailangan ko nang **mag-iba**." Or 'yong tanong mo sa jowa mong biglang nanlamig: "Bakit ka nag-iba?" It's the verb for transformation, wanted or unwanted.
usage_notes: Ito ang pawatas (infinitive) na anyo. Ang aspektong naganap na ay 'nag-iba' at ang aspektong magaganap ay 'mag-iiba'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napagdesisyunan niyang **mag-iba** ng landas sa kanyang karera.","translation":"He decided to **change** his career path."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi **mag-iiba** ang pagtingin ko sa iyo.","translation":"Don't worry, my perception of you will not **change**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sapilitang pagpapatapon o pagpapaalis sa isang tao mula sa sariling bansa o tahanan bilang isang uri ng parusa.
original_explanation: What happened to Rizal in Dapitan. Sa modern terms, ito 'yung feeling mo 'pag na-seen ka sa group chat at walang pumansin sa'yo. Para kang na-exile sa sarili mong barkada. Very dramatic.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at makasaysayang termino. Bihirang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap ngunit karaniwan sa mga aklat ng kasaysayan at panitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong panahon ng mga Kastila, maraming Pilipinong makabayan ang **idinistiyero** sa ibang bansa.","translation":"During the Spanish era, many Filipino patriots were **exiled** to other countries."},{"sentence":"Nagbanta ang diktador na **idistiyero** ang lahat ng kanyang kritiko.","translation":"The dictator threatened **to exile** all of his critics."}]

translation: act of being pulled or plucked out forcefully
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkabunot o pagkahugot ng isang bagay, tulad ng buhok o damo, nang biglaan at may puwersa.
etymology: From pagka- (state of) + labnot (to pluck or pull out forcefully).
original_explanation: This is the feeling when you get your eyebrows threaded for the first time. Ouch! It's also what happens when you try to pull one weed from your garden and a whole chunk of earth and other plants comes with it. It's a sudden, sharp, 'yanking' motion. Very similar to 'pagkalabnit', but more about 'plucking' or 'uprooting' than 'peeling'.
usage_notes: Often used for hair, weeds, or things deeply rooted that are pulled out suddenly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napasigaw siya sa sakit ng **pagkalabnot** ng kanyang buhok.","translation":"She shouted in pain from the **forceful pulling** of her hair."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkalabnot** sa masamang damo ay kailangan upang lumusog ang mga pananim.","translation":"The **plucking out** of weeds is necessary for the plants to grow healthy."}]

translation: to do something one by one; to single out
meaning_filipino: Gawin ang isang bagay nang paisa-isa; pagtuunan ng pansin ang isa mula sa isang grupo.
original_explanation: When your crush posts a group picture and you zoom in on their face—that's "inisahan mo." Or when a teacher calls on students one by one for recitation. It's the act of focusing on a single item or person from a larger set.
usage_notes: The "-han" suffix here implies action directed towards something or done in a particular way (one by one).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **isahan** ng tingin ang mga bagong empleyado para hindi sila mailang.","translation":"Don't **single out** the new employees with your stare so they won't feel awkward."}]

translation: salting; the act of preserving with salt
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglalagay ng asin sa pagkain upang mapreserba ito o magdagdag ng lasa.
original_explanation: This is what your lola does to make burong isda or itlog na maalat. It's the OG food preservation tech before refrigerators became a thing. Think of it as marinating, but with a whole lot of salt and patience.
usage_notes: Often refers to the process of curing fish, meat, or eggs with salt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **pag-aasin** ng isda para hindi ito masira.","translation":"The proper **salting** of fish is important so it doesn't spoil."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-aasin** ay isang tradisyonal na paraan ng pag-iimbak.","translation":"**Salting** is a traditional method of preservation."}]

translation: to be able to drag; to accidentally involve
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang hilahin ang isang bagay sa lupa; o di-sinasadyang mahila o maisama sa isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: When you manage to drag your lazy friend out of bed to go to the mall. Also, when your name gets dragged into office 'chismis' you had nothing to do with. You got involved against your will.
usage_notes: Can mean to successfully drag something heavy (potential) or to unintentionally involve someone/something (causative/accidental).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat siya nang **makaladkad** niya ang buong sako ng bigas.","translation":"He was surprised when he was **able to drag** the whole sack of rice."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **makaladkad** sa gulo nila.","translation":"I don't want to **be dragged** into their mess."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang ornamental na may makukulay na bulaklak at dahon, karaniwang itinatanim sa mga hardin o paso.
original_explanation: That plant your Tita of Manila is obsessed with, the one she posts on her Facebook My Day more than pictures of her own kids. It's got those fancy leaves and sometimes pretty flowers. A staple in the 'plantito/plantita' starter pack, right next to the snake plant and the pothos.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa halamang Begonia, isang sikat na panloob na halaman sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng mga **bigonya** na nakatanim sa hardin ni Lola.","translation":"The **begonias** planted in Grandma's garden are beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasinlaki o kasintaas ng isang bundok; tumutukoy sa napakaraming dami o tumpok ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Describes your laundry pile after a long weekend. Or the amount of work waiting for you on a Monday morning. "May gabundok akong labahin!" is the official battle cry of the weekend.
usage_notes: A common hyperbolic adjective to describe a large pile or quantity of something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **gabundok** siyang utang na kailangang bayaran.","translation":"He has a **mountain** of debt to pay."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng pista, may **gabundok** na hugasing plato sa kusina.","translation":"After the fiesta, there was a **huge amount** of dishes to wash in the kitchen."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang labis, hayagan, at kung minsan ay bastos na paraan ng paglalandi. Ito ay may negatibong konotasyon kumpara sa 'landi'.
original_explanation: This is 'landi' on beast mode, and not in a good way. It's the level of flirting that makes other people uncomfortable. It's the difference between a witty DM and an unsolicited 'pic'. While 'landi' is playful, '**landit**' is often seen as desperate or inappropriate. It's the cringe-worthy sequel nobody asked for.
usage_notes: Carries a stronger, more negative connotation than 'landi'. Often implies a lack of subtlety or decorum. The adjective form is 'malandit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi na iyon landi, hayagang **landit** na ang ginagawa niya.","translation":"That's not just flirting anymore, what he's doing is outright **vulgar flirtatiousness**."},{"sentence":"Nakakainis ang **landit** ng taong iyon.","translation":"That person's **excessive flirtatiousness** is annoying."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging angkop, tama, o akma sa isang partikular na sitwasyon, tao, o layunin.
original_explanation: When your outfit is on point, your crush finally notices you, or your kilay is perfectly even—that's when you say, "Bagay!" It's the ultimate compliment for compatibility, whether in fashion, romance, or food pairings. "Bagay kayo!" is the official seal of approval from your chismosa friends for your new significant other.
usage_notes: Pronunciation is key to differentiate from the noun form. For the adjective, the stress is on the second syllable (/ba-GAY/).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bagay** sa iyo ang suot mong damit.","translation":"The dress you're wearing is **suitable** for you. (or: looks good on you)"},{"sentence":"Sa tingin ko, hindi **bagay** ang planong iyon sa ating sitwasyon.","translation":"I think that plan is not **appropriate** for our situation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng muling pag-aaral, pagsusuri, o pagbabalik-tanaw sa isang aralin, dokumento, o gawain upang ito ay matandaan o mapabuti.
original_explanation: The verb form of your pre-exam panic. It's the action of doing the 'repaso'. "Sige, **repasuhin** natin 'yung mga notes." It's the "let's go over this one more time" before you submit your work or take the test, hoping a miracle happens and you spot a typo.
usage_notes: The action word for 'repaso'. Used when instructing or stating the action of reviewing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **repasuhin** mo ang email bago mo ipadala.","translation":"Please, **review** the email before you send it."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **repasuhin** ang lahat ng kabanata para sa pagsusulit bukas.","translation":"We need **to go over** all the chapters for the exam tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan sa pagkain na may hawakan at mga tulis sa dulo, na ginagamit sa pagtuhog o pag-ipit ng pagkain.
original_explanation: The trusty sidekick of the spoon (kutsara). In the Philippines, the spoon is the star player, but the `tinidor` is the essential assistant, used for pushing food onto the spoon or spearing that stubborn piece of lechon. A true Filipino dining experience is the 'kutsara't tinidor' combo.
usage_notes: Almost always paired with 'kutsara' (spoon). The pair is called 'kubyertos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha mo nga ako ng kutsara at **tinidor**.","translation":"Can you please get me a spoon and **fork**."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **tinidor** para durugin ang patatas.","translation":"She used the **fork** to mash the potatoes."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na angkop, umiiral, o magagamit lamang sa isang partikular na panahon o okasyon.
original_explanation: That bibingka and puto bumbong that only shows up during '-ber' months. The 'summer' collection at the department store. The 'limited time only' McSpicy flavor. It's anything that has an expiration date on its relevance, making you want it more because you know it won't be there forever. FOMO-inducing.
usage_notes: Describes things that are only available or relevant during certain seasons (e.g., Christmas, summer, rainy season).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mangga ay isang **pampanahon** na prutas.","translation":"The mango is a **seasonal** fruit."},{"sentence":"Naglabas sila ng mga **pampanahon** na dekorasyon para sa Pasko.","translation":"They released **seasonal** decorations for Christmas."}]

translation: to be able to hurt (someone); to cause pain
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng sakit, pisikal man o emosyonal, sa isang tao o anumang may damdamin.
original_explanation: This is the root of all hugot lines. 'Yung sinabi ng ex mo na "I didn't mean to hurt you." Ay, nako, 'di mo sinasadyang makasakit? Pwede ring physical, like when you accidentally elbow someone in a crowded jeepney. "Sorry po, hindi ko sinasadyang makasakit." It's the ability or potential to inflict pain, intentionally or not.
usage_notes: Can refer to both physical pain and emotional hurt. The prefix "maka-" denotes ability or potential.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maging maingat sa iyong mga salita upang hindi ka **makasakit** ng damdamin ng iba.","translation":"Be careful with your words so you don't **hurt** other people's feelings."},{"sentence":"Ang tindi ng sikat ng araw ay **makasasakit** sa balat kung hindi ka maglalagay ng sunblock.","translation":"The intense heat of the sun can **hurt** the skin if you don't apply sunblock."}]

meaning_filipino: Maglaan ng puhunan, salapi, o yaman sa isang negosyo, proyekto, o tao na may layuning kumita o magkaroon ng pakinabang sa hinaharap.
etymology: Mula sa 'pa-' + 'puhunan' + hulaping '-an'. Ang 'puhunan' ay kapital o investment.
original_explanation: It's when you put your money (or time, or effort) into something hoping it pays off. Like investing in stocks, funding your friend's milk tea business, or even spending time on a person you hope to have a future with. The ultimate 'sana all may ROI' (Return on Investment) move.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na termino para sa pamumuhunan. Sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap, ang mga tao ay maaaring sabihin na 'mag-invest sa...'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak niyang **pamuhunanan** ang isang maliit na kainan.","translation":"He plans **to invest in** a small eatery."},{"sentence":"Ang edukasyon ay isang bagay na dapat laging **pamuhunanan**.","translation":"Education is something that should always be **invested in**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang taong nagwagi sa isang laban, laro, o anumang uri ng kompetisyon.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Espanyol na *ganado*, na nangangahulugang 'nanalo' o 'kumita'.
original_explanation: Describes the state of being the winner. It's that "I'm on top of the world!" feeling after your Mobile Legends team clutched the win, or when you snagged the last discounted air fryer during a flash sale. You didn't just participate, you conquered. #SanaAll
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa impormal na usapan. Maaari ring gamiting pandiwa sa anyong 'nanalo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Panalo** ang pambato ng Pilipinas sa katatapos lang na beauty pageant.","translation":"The Philippines' representative **is victorious** in the recently concluded beauty pageant."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko **panalo** ako sa buhay nang makapasa ako sa board exam.","translation":"I felt like I **won** at life when I passed the board exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkain, lalo na ang karne, na idinaan sa proseso ng pagsasangkutsa.
original_explanation: This is the *result* of the pre-cooking stage. It's the pork that has been sautéed and is now waiting patiently to be turned into a glorious adobo or menudo. It's not the final dish, but it's the promising "work in progress" that smells amazing already.
usage_notes: Refers to the food item itself after being parboiled or sautéed. Less common than the verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tikman mo ang **sangkutsa**, baka kulang pa sa alat.","translation":"Taste the **parboiled meat**, it might need more salt."},{"sentence":"Ang **sangkutsa** pa lang, ulam na.","translation":"Just the **sautéed dish** itself is already a meal."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na may matulis at makitid na dulo, tulad ng karayom, dulo ng lapis, o palaso.
original_explanation: Think of a perfectly sharpened pencil, ready to stab the paper (or your enemy, charot!). Or the tip of a barbecue stick before you put the isaw on it. If it's pointy and sharp at the end, it's matilos. Perfect for writing, sewing, or... chismis. "Ang tilos ng dila mo!" (Your tongue is so sharp!)
usage_notes: Distinct from `matalim`, which refers to the sharpness of a blade's edge. `Matilos` is specifically about the sharpness of a point.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong **matilos** ang dulo ng lapis kaya nabutas ang papel.","translation":"The tip of the pencil was too **pointed**, so it poked a hole in the paper."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paghawak ng pako dahil **matilos** ito.","translation":"Be careful holding the nail because it is **sharp**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang paraan ng pagluluto kung saan ang isang pagkain, tulad ng isda, manok, o gulay, ay nilalamnan ng mga giniling na sangkap.
original_explanation: The "surprise inside" of Pinoy cuisine. It's when you take a perfectly good bangus or chicken and say, "You know what this needs? To be completely deboned and then stuffed with a party of ground meat, veggies, and raisins." Rilyeno is the culinary equivalent of doing extra credit—so much work, but the result is always a showstopper at any handaan.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (the dish itself, e.g., "ang rilyeno") or an adjective ("rilyeno-ng bangus").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong ulam tuwing Pasko ay **rilyeno**ng manok.","translation":"My favorite dish during Christmas is **stuffed** chicken."},{"sentence":"Mahirap gawin ang **rilyeno**, pero sulit ang sarap.","translation":"It's difficult to make **relleno**, but the taste is worth it."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang materyal, karaniwang kahoy o uling, na sinusunog upang makalikha ng apoy para sa pagluluto o pagpapainit.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang mula sa pamilyang wikang Austronesian.
