meaning_filipino: Isang tao, karaniwang lalaki, na lumalaban sa toro sa isang arena bilang isang uri ng panoorin o isport, na kilala bilang 'bullfighting'.
original_explanation: Siya yung matapang (o baliw?) na lalaki na nakikipaglaro sa toro sa loob ng arena, armado lang ng pulang tela (muleta) at espada. Parang 'yung ginagawa mo kapag tinatag mo 'yung galit mong boss sa meeting—ikaw ang torero, siya ang toro. Good luck.
usage_notes: Ang "matador" ay isang mas tiyak na termino para sa 'bullfighter' na siyang pumapatay sa toro sa huli. Ang 'torero' ay isang pangkalahatang termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **torero** sa Espanya.","translation":"He dreams of becoming a famous **bullfighter** in Spain."},{"sentence":"Sugatan ang **torero** matapos siyang suwagin ng toro.","translation":"The **bullfighter** was wounded after being gored by the bull."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkahilig o pagpanig sa isang direksyon, pananaw, o grupo. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pisikal na pagtagilid ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: It's your 'bias' in K-Pop terms, but for everything else. It's your political leanings, your preference for adobo with or without soy sauce, or which side of the bed you sleep on. 'May kiling talaga siya sa paborito niyang estudyante.' The phrase 'kiling ng kabayo' (horse's mane) is a specific usage, referring to how the mane leans to one side.
usage_notes: While it can mean physical tilting, it's more commonly used to describe partiality, bias, or a tendency. The phrase 'kiling ng kabayo' (horse's mane) is a specific noun phrase using this word, but the primary meaning is inclination.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata ang kanyang **kiling** sa isang partido sa pulitika.","translation":"His **bias** towards one political party is obvious."},{"sentence":"May bahagyang **kiling** ang tore kaya ito'y kinukumpuni.","translation":"The tower has a slight **lean**, which is why it is being repaired."},{"sentence":"Ang haba ng **kiling** ng kabayong iyon.","translation":"That horse's **mane** is long."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tina na nag-iiba ng kulay (nagiging pula sa asido at asul sa alkampurado) na ginagamit upang subukin ang kemikal na katangian ng isang likido.
original_explanation: You remember this from high school chemistry, right? The 'litmus paper' that tells you if something is acidic or basic. In everyday talk, it's used metaphorically. A 'litmus test' is a single, decisive test to see what something or someone is truly made of. 'Yung reaction niya sa traffic, 'yun ang litmus test ng pasensya niya.'
usage_notes: Kadalasang ginagamit kasama ng salitang 'test' o 'paper'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng mga estudyante ang **litmus** paper para sa kanilang eksperimento sa agham.","translation":"The students used **litmus** paper for their science experiment."},{"sentence":"Ang pagharap sa krisis ay isang **litmus** test para sa isang lider.","translation":"Facing a crisis is a **litmus** test for a leader."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi pangunahin; may mas mababang priyoridad, ranggo, o kahalagahan kumpara sa una.
original_explanation: This is the B-plot in a movie, the side hustle to your main job, the backup plan. It's not the star of the show, but it's still important. Think "secondary character" who sometimes steals the scene, or "secondary source" for your thesis paper when you can't find the primary one.
usage_notes: Often used to describe things of lesser importance compared to the primary one, like `pangalawahang epekto` (side effect) or `pangalawahang layunin` (secondary objective).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paglalaro ng mobile games ay **pangalawahan** lamang sa kanyang mga pag-aaral.","translation":"Playing mobile games is only **secondary** to his studies."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating isaalang-alang ang mga **pangalawahang** epekto ng bagong patakaran.","translation":"We must consider the **secondary** effects of the new policy."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa o nagbibigay ng edukasyon, kaalaman, o kasanayan.
original_explanation: This is the formal term for anything that's supposed to teach you something, like those field trips to museums that were really just an excuse to hang out with your crush. An "edukasyonal" TV show is what your mom switches to when she thinks you've been watching too much anime.
usage_notes: Used to describe materials, programs, or activities intended for learning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **edukasyonal** na video ang mapapanood online.","translation":"There are many **educational** videos that can be watched online."},{"sentence":"Ang lakbay-aral ay isang **edukasyonal** na karanasan para sa mga estudyante.","translation":"The field trip is an **educational** experience for the students."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang dumulas pababa sa isang madulas o matarik na ibabaw.
etymology: From `ma-` (potential passive prefix) + `dusdos` (a downward slip or slide).
original_explanation: That mini heart attack when you're walking on a mossy, wet, or steep path and your foot suddenly loses its grip. It's a slip, but specifically a downward sliding one. 'Mag-ingat ka sa pagbaba sa bundok, baka ka madusdos.' It's the universe telling you gravity is not your friend today.
usage_notes: Describes an accidental downward slide, different from `madulas` which can be a slip on a flat surface.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Buti na lang at may nakapitan ako, kundi ay **nadusdos** na ako sa bangin.","translation":"Good thing I grabbed onto something, or else I would have **slipped and slid** down the ravine."},{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan sa paglakad diyan dahil madulas at baka ka **madusdos**.","translation":"Walk slowly there because it's slippery and you might **slip and slide down**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o makina na ginagamit sa paggawa ng tela sa pamamagitan ng pagsasalit-salit ng mga sinulid.
original_explanation: This is the OG 3D printer of our ancestors. Before CNC machines, there was the **panghabi**, turning simple threads into beautiful traditional textiles. It's the ultimate tool for making something amazing out of, well, a tangled mess—kind of like my love life.
usage_notes: Refers to the instrument or tool used for weaving.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lumang **panghabi** ng lola ay nakatago pa rin sa bodega.","translation":"Grandma's old **loom** is still kept in the storage room."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng tiyaga sa paggamit ng **panghabi** upang makabuo ng magandang disenyo.","translation":"Patience is needed when using a **loom** to create a beautiful design."}]

translation: to entrust something to someone; to leave instructions with someone
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iiwan ng tagubilin, utos, o isang bagay sa pangangalaga ng isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa 'bilin' (instruction, something entrusted). Ang hulaping '-an' ay nagpapahiwatig ng tao o lugar na tumatanggap ng kilos.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for 'Huwag mong gagalawin 'yan!' or 'Pakainin mo 'yung aso ha!'. It's what your mom does before she leaves for the palengke, leaving a list of chores and warnings. It's the act of passing on responsibility, whether it's a task, a secret, or the last piece of pizza in the fridge.
usage_notes: The object of this verb is the person being given the instructions or the thing to look after.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **pagbilinan** mo ng mga bata habang wala ka.","translation":"**Entrust** the children **to** her while you are away."},{"sentence":"'Huwag ninyong **pagbilinan** ng sekreto 'yan, madaldal 'yan,' biro niya.","translation":"'Don't **entrust** a secret **to** that person, they're talkative,' he joked."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging kabahagi o kasama sa isang pangkat, layunin, o paniniwala; pagiging sang-ayon.
original_explanation: When you're "in on it." You're part of the team, the plan, or the belief. "Kaisa ako sa pananaw mo" means "I'm with you on that," "I share your view." It's about unity and agreement. Think of it as joining a group chat for a specific cause, whether it's for a group project or overthrowing a toxic manager. You are one with the cause.
usage_notes: Often followed by "sa" or "ng". For example, "Kaisa sa layunin" (one with the goal).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kaisa** kami ng buong bayan sa pagsuporta sa ating mga atleta.","translation":"We are **one with** the entire nation in supporting our athletes."},{"sentence":"Lagi siyang **kaisa** sa mga desisyon ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"He is always **in agreement with** his parents' decisions."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang masama, nakatatakot, o hindi kaaya-aya ang kalidad o katangian.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na nakita mo 'yung ex mo na may bago, tapos mas maganda/gwapo pa sa'yo. Terible! O kaya yung traffic sa EDSA pag Friday payday. That's the textbook definition of terible.
usage_notes: Often used as an intensifier, similar to "sobrang" or "grabe". Can describe a situation, a person's quality, or a feeling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Terible** ang init ng panahon ngayong tag-araw.","translation":"The heat this summer is **terrible**."},{"sentence":"Nakaranas kami ng **terible** na trapik sa SLEX.","translation":"We experienced **terrible** traffic on SLEX."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na pagkakatulad o pagkakawangis sa itsura; walang pagkakaiba sa anyo.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'looks like.' This is 'OMG, clone ba 'yan?!' level of similarity. It's the intensified version of 'kamukha', like when you see a celebrity's kid and they are a carbon copy. The ultimate 'mana sa nanay/tatay' comment.
usage_notes: An intensified form of 'kamukha'. The '-ng' linker is added for euphonic reasons.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kamukhang-kamukha** ng anak niya ang sikat na artista.","translation":"Her child is the **spitting image** of the famous actor."},{"sentence":"Para silang kambal, **kamukhang-kamukha** nila ang isa't isa.","translation":"They're like twins, they look **exactly alike**."}]

translation: to fall asleep on (something/someone); to oversleep
meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang makatulog habang may ginagawa, may kausap, o nasa isang lugar; o ang lumampas sa oras ng paggising.
original_explanation: 'Yung ka-chat mo na biglang 'di na nag-reply? Baka na-**tulugan** ka lang. Or 'yung alarm mo na nag-snooze ka nang nag-snooze hanggang sa na-**tulugan** mo na ulit at late ka na sa work. The struggle is real.
usage_notes: This is an object-focused verb. The 'thing' being 'slept on' (a person, a movie, a class, an alarm) is the object of the sentence. Ex: 'Natulugan ko ang pelikula' (I fell asleep on the movie).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasensya na, **natulugan** kita kagabi habang magkausap tayo.","translation":"I'm sorry, I **fell asleep on** you last night while we were talking."},{"sentence":"Naku, **natulugan** ko ang alarm! Mahuhuli na ako sa klase.","translation":"Oh no, I **overslept** my alarm! I'm going to be late for class."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan kung saan ang isang pangyayari ay malapit nang maganap ngunit hindi natuloy.
original_explanation: This is the official word for every "malapit na pero hindi pa" moment in your life. It's the story of your life when you're 5 minutes late for the bus, when you almost hit your monthly sales quota but missed it by one, or when you thought you were going to get the last piece of lechon but your tito beat you to it. "Muntik na" is the universe telling you, "Nice try, besh."
usage_notes: Almost always used with 'na' as in 'muntik na'. It can be used for both positive and negative near-misses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Muntik** na akong mahulog sa hagdanan!","translation":"I **almost** fell down the stairs!"},{"sentence":"**Muntik** na niyang makuha ang unang gantimpala.","translation":"He **nearly** won the first prize."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matindi at di-mapigilang pagkawili o pagkagusto sa isang tao, bagay, o ideya.
original_explanation: Your K-Pop bias? 'Yan ay pagkahumaling. 'Yung kaibigan mong hindi maka-move on sa ex niya after 5 years? Pagkahumaling. 'Yung pag-check mo ng Shopee app every 5 minutes during a 9.9 sale? Pagkahumaling. It's that intense, can't-stop-thinking-about-it level of fascination or obsession.
usage_notes: Can be used for people, hobbies, or ideas. It implies a very strong, almost irrational level of interest.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkahumaling** sa sining ay nagsimula noong bata pa siya.","translation":"His **fascination** with art started when he was still a child."},{"sentence":"Mapanganib ang **pagkahumaling** sa isang tao na hindi ka naman gusto.","translation":"It's dangerous to have an **obsession** with a person who doesn't even like you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahiwatig ng pag-iral, pag-aari, o pagkakaroon ng isang bagay, katangian, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: 'May' is the ultimate 'meron' or 'wala' starter pack. May jowa? May pera? May time ka ba? It's the word that defines your current status in life, love, and finances. It's the 'have' in 'have and have-nots'. If you want something, you start with 'Sana may...'.
usage_notes: Used before nouns, pronouns, verbs, and adjectives. It is distinct from 'mayroon', which is often used before a phrase or at the end of a sentence. 'May' is always followed immediately by the word it modifies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**May** aso kami sa bahay.","translation":"We **have** a dog at home."},{"sentence":"**May** tao ba sa loob?","translation":"**Is there** anyone inside?"},{"sentence":"**May** problema ka ba?","translation":"Do you **have** a problem?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at panandaliang pagdikit o paghipo sa isang ibabaw.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "dampi" (marahang hipo) at ang gitlaping "-um-".
original_explanation: The opposite of a slap. It's that gentle breeze that 'touches' your face, or the way your crush's hand 'brushed against' yours and you overthink it for a week. It’s a touch so light, it’s almost not there, but you definitely felt it. Kilig-level touch.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang napakagaan na paghipo, kadalasan ay may romantiko o malumanay na konotasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumampi** ang malamig na hangin sa aking balat.","translation":"The cold wind **touched lightly** against my skin."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman kong **dumampi** ang kanyang kamay sa aking balikat.","translation":"I felt his hand **brush against** my shoulder."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagwawakas ng buhay ng isang tao, hayop, o anumang may buhay; kamatayan.
etymology: From `pagka-` (the state or manner of) + `matay` (a variant of 'patay', to die).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'end of contract,' the final log-out, the point where you stop seeing 'seen' and start seeing 'remembering.' It's the reason for lamay, 9-day novenas, and a whole lot of family drama over 'mana.' The most permanent ghosting there is.
usage_notes: Can refer to the event of dying or the state of being dead.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **pagkamatay** ng alaga nilang aso ay ikinalungkot ng buong pamilya.","translation":"The sudden **death** of their pet dog saddened the whole family."},{"sentence":"Inaalam pa ng mga pulis ang sanhi ng **pagkamatay** ng biktima.","translation":"The police are still investigating the cause of the victim's **demise**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong labis ang pagkagutom o kasakiman sa pagkain; ginagamit din bilang isang salitang mapanlait para sa taong napakahirap.
original_explanation: Literally 'dead from hunger.' It's what you call your friend who eats their own food in 2 minutes and then stares at yours with pleading eyes. 'Para kang patay-gutom!' Can be an insult meaning poor and destitute, or just a friendly jab at someone who's a bottomless pit at an 'unli-rice' restaurant.
usage_notes: Can be derogatory, implying someone is so poor they are starving. In casual contexts among friends, it's often used hyperbolically to mean 'gluttonous' or 'famished.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang kumain na parang **patay-gutom**; dahan-dahan lang.","translation":"Don't eat like a **famished person**; just go slowly."},{"sentence":"Tinulungan ng organisasyon ang mga taong itinuturing na **patay-gutom** sa lansangan.","translation":"The organization helped the people considered **destitute** on the streets."}]

translation: a light pat, a gentle tap
meaning_filipino: Isang marahan at magaan na pagpalo o pagdantay ng kamay sa isang tao o bagay, karaniwang bilang tanda ng pag-akit ng pansin, pagpapahiwatig ng pagsang-ayon, o pagpapakita ng pagmamahal.
original_explanation: It's that gentle 'psst' but with your hand. The kind of touch your crush gives you on the shoulder that makes you overthink for a week. Or what your boss does right before saying, 'May na-receive akong email from HR...'
usage_notes: Often implies affection or getting someone's attention gently. The verb form is 'tapikin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **tapik** lang sa balikat mula sa kanya, kinilig na ako.","translation":"Just one **pat** on the shoulder from them, and I already felt giddy."},{"sentence":"Binigyan niya ng magiliw na **tapik** ang alagang aso.","translation":"He gave his pet dog an affectionate **pat**."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng biglaang pag-aapoy o pagliliyab; o, magpasimula ng isang marahas na damdamin, gulo, o digmaan.
original_explanation: This is for igniting things—literally, like a fire, or figuratively, like a chismis or a revolution. One wrong comment can **papagsiklabin** a Twitter war. It's about adding fuel to the fire, whether it's a real bonfire or the burning 'galit' of your partner when you forget your anniversary.
usage_notes: Used for both literal fire and metaphorical outbursts of emotion or conflict.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang maliit na alitan ay maaaring **papagsiklabin** ang isang malaking gulo.","translation":"A small disagreement can **ignite** a huge conflict."},{"sentence":"Gumamit sila ng gasolina para mas mabilis **mapagsiklab** ang siga.","translation":"They used gasoline to **make the bonfire flare up** faster."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng bathala o itinuturing na may pambihirang kapangyarihan at kagandahan; sa modernong gamit, isang babaeng napakaganda.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'dios' (god) na may pambabaeng panlapi na '-a' (diosa).
original_explanation: The highest compliment you can give a Filipina. It's not just "maganda" (beautiful), it's next-level, ethereal, Anne Curtis-level beauty. When your friend posts a new profile pic and she looks stunning, the proper response is "OMG Diyosa!". It's the ultimate "slay, queen!" validation.
usage_notes: Ang katumbas nito sa lalaki ay 'diyos' (god). Madalas gamitin bilang papuri o hyperbole para sa isang babaeng may pambihirang ganda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para siyang isang **diyosa** sa kanyang suot na puting bestida.","translation":"She looks like a **goddess** in her white dress."}]

translation: To imitate; to copy; to emulate
meaning_filipino: Ang paggaya o pagsunod sa halimbawa, kilos, o gawa ng iba.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping 'man-' at salitang-ugat na 'tulad'.
original_explanation: Basically, 'copycat'. When your sibling gets praised for being studious and your parents tell you, 'Dapat **manulad** ka sa kapatid mo,' that's the word in action. It can be positive (emulating a role model) or negative (plagiarism, 'gaya-gaya puto-maya').
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa anyong pautos na 'tumulad' o sa kontekstong naghahambing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana'y **manulad** ang ibang opisyal sa kanyang katapatan.","translation":"Hopefully, other officials will **emulate** his honesty."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **manulad** sa mga taong walang pangarap.","translation":"Do not **be like** people who have no dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pagtama o pagbangga sa isang bagay o tao, lalo na ng isang sasakyan.
original_explanation: That split-second "oh sh*t" moment in traffic when a jeepney suddenly swerves and hits your side mirror. It's the reason why dashcams are a must-have in Manila. Can also refer to bumping into someone in a crowded MRT train during rush hour.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of traffic accidents. The verb form is "mabundol" (to be hit/run over) or "bumundol" (to hit/collide with).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwasan ng tsuper ang **bundol** sa tumatawid na pusa.","translation":"The driver avoided a **collision** with the crossing cat."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa pagtawid, baka ka mabundol.","translation":"Be careful when crossing, you might get **run over**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at matulis na piraso ng metal na may patag na ulo, ginagamit na pangkabit sa pamamagitan ng pagpukpok nito sa mga bagay tulad ng kahoy.
original_explanation: The OG life-joiner before super glue and 3M tape. You need a hammer, some courage (so you don't hit your thumb), and this little metal guy to hang that "Live, Laugh, Love" sign your tita gave you. It’s the essential tool for every Pinoy dad's toolbox, right next to the electrical tape and WD-40.
usage_notes: Huwag ipagkamali sa halamang 'pakó' /pa-KO'/, na may diin sa huling pantig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng martilyo at **pako** para isabit ang bagong painting.","translation":"I need a hammer and a **nail** to hang the new painting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking nakapag-aral o miyembro ng pangkat ng mga edukadong Pilipino noong panahon ng kolonyalismong Espanyol na naghangad ng reporma.
original_explanation: These were the OG "woke" Pinoys of the 19th century. The educated, middle-class dudes like Jose Rizal, Marcelo H. del Pilar, and Graciano Lopez Jaena who studied abroad and came back wanting reforms. They were the original social media influencers, but using newspapers like La Solidaridad instead of TikTok.
usage_notes: A specific historical term for the Filipino educated elite during the late Spanish colonial period.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Jose Rizal ay isang tanyag na **ilustrado**.","translation":"Jose Rizal was a famous **ilustrado**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **ilustrado** ang nanguna sa Kilusang Propaganda.","translation":"The **ilustrados** led the Propaganda Movement."}]

translation: to have someone recite a poem, to commission a poem
meaning_filipino: Hilingin o atasan ang isang tao na bumigkas o sumulat ng isang tula.
original_explanation: This is what you ask your artsy friend to do for your crush's birthday. "Bes, `magpatula` ako sa'yo, bayaran na lang kita ng milk tea." It’s commissioning a 'spoken word' performance, old-school style.
usage_notes: Can mean either to have someone recite a poem or to have someone compose a poem for an occasion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagustuhan ng hari ang makata kaya't siya ay laging pinatatawag upang **magpatula**.","translation":"The king liked the poet so he was always summoned to **have him recite a poem**."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magpatula** para sa kanilang anibersaryo.","translation":"He decided to **commission a poem** for their anniversary."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain, na mahirap nguyain o kagatin dahil sa pagiging matigas o hindi na sariwa. Sa matalinhagang gamit, tumutukoy ito sa isang taong kuripot o mahirap hingan ng pabor o pera.
original_explanation: This word has two major flexes. First, food: 'yung steak na parang rubber tire, or 'yung chicharon na hindi na malutong. That's *makunat*. Second, people: 'yung friend mo na laging "naiwan 'yung wallet," o 'yung tita mong never nag-abot ng pamasko. Super *makunat* 'yan. It's the opposite of tender (for food) and generous (for people). The struggle is real, whether you're chewing or asking for balato.
usage_notes: The meaning (tough food vs. stingy person) is determined entirely by context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Reklamo ng customer na **makunat** daw ang inorder niyang litson kawali.","translation":"The customer complained that the lechon kawali he ordered was **tough**."}]

translation: to set sail; to depart; to proceed
meaning_filipino: Umalis o tumulak sa isang paglalakbay, partikular sa paglalakbay-dagat. Sa mas malawak na kahulugan, ito ay nangangahulugang tumuloy o magpatuloy.
original_explanation: From the Spanish word 'largo' (long, or a command to depart). This is the classic 'let's bounce' for sailors and seafarers. Think of an OFW seaman's ship about to maglargo for a 9-month contract. In a less literal sense, it can mean to just go ahead or proceed with something, like a project manager saying, 'O sige, maglargo na kayo sa next phase.'
usage_notes: Originally nautical, but its meaning has expanded to mean 'to proceed' or 'to go ahead' in certain contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas ng umaga **maglalargo** ang barko patungong Cebu.","translation":"The ship will **set sail** for Cebu tomorrow morning."},{"sentence":"Nang matanggap ang senyas, **naglargo** na ang grupo.","translation":"Upon receiving the signal, the group **proceeded**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging walang ginagawa, kadalasang nakabukas ang bibig, at tila naghihintay o nag-iisip nang malalim nang walang partikular na dahilan.
original_explanation: This is you during a long, boring Zoom meeting where you've turned off your camera. You're just staring into space, mouth slightly open, not thinking about anything productive. It's the human equivalent of a loading screen that's frozen. 'Uy, 'wag kang tumunganga diyan, tulungan mo ako magbuhat!'
usage_notes: Often implies a state of being unproductive or cluelessly idle. Can be used as a verb root (e.g., tumunganga).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **tumunganga** lang diyan habang nagtatrabaho ang lahat.","translation":"Don't just **stand there gaping** while everyone else is working."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko siyang **nakatunganga** sa bintana, parang may malalim na iniisip.","translation":"I saw him **staring blankly** out the window, as if deep in thought."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lungsod sa lalawigan ng Kabite, Pilipinas, na kilala sa kanyang makasaysayang kahalagahan at bilang isang mabilis na umuunlad na sentrong urbano.
etymology: Possibly from 'bakood' or 'bakod' meaning 'fence' or 'high ground'.
original_explanation: Usually spelled 'Bacoor'. It's that city in Cavite that's basically the gateway from Manila. If you're from the south and work in the city, you know the traffic here all too well. It's famous for marching bands and a whole lot of people.
usage_notes: This is a proper noun, the name of a city. The spelling 'Bakoor' is non-standard but understood; the official spelling is 'Bacoor'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Taga-**Bakoor**, Kabite ang aking mga magulang.","translation":"My parents are from **Bacoor**, Cavite."},{"sentence":"Matindi ang trapik papuntang **Bakoor** tuwing rush hour.","translation":"The traffic going to **Bacoor** is heavy during rush hour."}]

translation: to be imprisoned; to be jailed
meaning_filipino: Ang maparusahan sa pamamagitan ng pagkulong sa isang bilangguan o piitan.
original_explanation: The literal "go to jail, do not pass Go, do not collect 200 pesos." It's being put behind bars. Figuratively, it can also feel like being trapped in a toxic relationship or a dead-end job. "Parang nabilanggo ako sa utang ko sa credit card."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari siyang **mabilanggo** nang habambuhay dahil sa kanyang krimen.","translation":"He could **be imprisoned** for life because of his crime."},{"sentence":"Ang inosenteng tao ay hindi dapat **nabilanggo**.","translation":"An innocent person should not have **been jailed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aari o pagkuha sa isang bagay na para bang sa iyo. Bilang katangian, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang bagay na likas o taal sa isang tao.
original_explanation: "Angkin" is that special something you have, your 'it' factor. "May angkin siyang ganda" means she has a natural, unique beauty. But as a verb ("angkinin"), it gets dramatic. It's to claim something, sometimes something that isn't yours. It’s the stuff of teleseryes: "Aangkinin kita!" (I will claim you!). It's about ownership, whether it's talent, property, or someone's heart.
usage_notes: A versatile root word. 'May angkin' + [adjective] means 'has an innate [quality]'. The verb 'angkinin' (to claim) is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **angkin** siyang talino sa matematika.","translation":"She has an **innate** talent in mathematics."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **angkinin** ang hindi sa iyo.","translation":"Do not **claim** what is not yours."}]

translation: to knead; to mash; to squeeze with hands
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdiin, pagpiga, at paghalo sa isang bagay gamit ang mga kamay.
original_explanation: The command form of 'lamas'. 'Go on, get your hands dirty.' This is what the recipe tells you to do. It's the act of squishing, kneading, or mashing something thoroughly. Your tita might also say this about your back when she gives you a 'hilot': 'Lalamasin ko lang itong likod mo.'
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the thing being kneaded or mashed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **lamasin** nang mabuti ang masa para sa tinapay.","translation":"You need **to knead** the dough well for the bread."},{"sentence":"**Lamasin** ang ampalaya na may asin para mabawasan ang pait.","translation":"**Mash** the bitter gourd with salt to reduce its bitterness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan inihahanda at pinatutubo ang mga punla bago ilipat sa permanenteng taniman.
original_explanation: Think of this as the pre-school for plants. It's the safe, controlled environment where baby seedlings get their start in life before they're thrown into the real world (your garden) to face the harsh realities of pests and inconsistent watering.
usage_notes: Used in agriculture and gardening contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inihanda ng magsasaka ang **pagpunlaan** para sa mga buto ng kamatis.","translation":"The farmer prepared the **seedbed** for the tomato seeds."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bagong sibol na halaman ay nasa **pagpunlaan** pa.","translation":"The new sprouts are still in the **nursery**."}]

translation: To strut, to sashay, to walk the runway
meaning_filipino: Ang paglakad nang may angas, kumpiyansa, at istilo, na katulad ng ginagawa ng isang modelo sa isang runway. Ang salitang-ugat na ito ay ginagamit sa mga anyong pandiwa tulad ng rumampa, mag-rampa, o irampa.
etymology: From Spanish 'rampa' (ramp), which became associated with the fashion runway.
original_explanation: When you're feeling your OOTD and you walk down the hallway like it's a fashion show. That's 'rumarampa'. It's not just walking; it's walking with *attitude*. Think Catriona Gray's lava walk. From the office lobby to the palengke, any place can be your runway.
usage_notes: This is the root word. It is commonly used with verb affixes: rumampa (to strut), mag-rampa (to strut), irampa (to parade something). 'Pa-rampa' is a popular colloquialism meaning 'to show off by walking'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Galing niyang **rumampa** sa entablado!","translation":"She's great at **strutting** on stage!"},{"sentence":"Hayaan mo siyang **mag-rampa**, bago ang sapatos niya.","translation":"Let her **sashay**, her shoes are new."},{"sentence":"**Irampa** mo 'yang bagong damit mo!","translation":"**Strut** in your new dress!"}]

translation: to have something made or done
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling sa iba na gumawa, kumumpuni, o lumikha ng isang bagay.
etymology: From root `gawa` (do, make) with the causative prefix `pa-`.
original_explanation: "Pagawa" is your go-to phrase when you need something done but you can't (or won't) do it yourself. "Pagawa ako ng assignment." "Pagawa ng duplicate key." It's the magic word for outsourcing your life, from school projects to getting your phone fixed.
usage_notes: This is a command or request form. The object of the verb is the thing to be made or done. Often used in its inflected form `ipagawa`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pagawa** mo na ang sirang gripo sa tubero.","translation":"**Have** the plumber **fix** the broken faucet."},{"sentence":"Saan kaya ako pwedeng **pagawa** ng customized na t-shirt?","translation":"Where can I **have** a customized t-shirt **made**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Pananakit, kirot, o anumang hindi kaaya-ayang pakiramdam sa bahagi ng tiyan.
original_explanation: The immediate consequence of eating a week-old adobo or trying that sketchy-looking street food. It's the 'I shouldn't have eaten that' feeling, often accompanied by a mad dash to the nearest CR. Can range from a simple indigestion to a full-blown LBM (Loose Bowel Movement) drama.
usage_notes: 'Sakit ng tiyan' and 'sakit sa tiyan' are both commonly used and interchangeable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakarami kong kinain kaya may **sakit ako sa tiyan** ngayon.","translation":"I ate too much, that's why I have a **stomachache** now."},{"sentence":"Ang **sakit ng tiyan** ay maaaring sintomas ng mas malubhang karamdaman.","translation":"A **stomachache** can be a symptom of a more serious illness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng restriksyon o pagtatakda na hindi maaaring gawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "bawal" move. It's not just saying "don't do it," it's officially making it a rule. Think "Bawal Umihi Dito" signs, but you're the one making the sign. When your parents say, "Ipinagbabawal ko na ang paggamit mo ng cellphone pagkatapos ng alas-diyes," that's the final word. It's the legislative branch of the household making a law.
usage_notes: The focus is on the thing being prohibited.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipagbabawal** ng gobyerno ang paggamit ng single-use plastics.","translation":"The government will **prohibit** the use of single-use plastics."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo **ipinagbawal** ang pag-ibig natin?","translation":"Why did you **forbid** our love?"}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyang-diin o linawin ang isang punto o pahayag upang hindi magkaroon ng pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo sa meeting kapag ayaw mong may mag-claim na "hindi ko narinig" o "nalito ako." You put your foot down, tapos inuulit-ulit mo 'yung point mo na parang sirang plaka pero with authority. "Ipagdiinan mo sa kanila na bawal ang OT if 'di approved."
usage_notes: Often used in arguments, instructions, or clarifications to ensure a point is understood and taken seriously.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **ipagdiinan** na ako ang nagbayad para sa hapunan kagabi.","translation":"I want to **emphasize** that I was the one who paid for dinner last night."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **ipagdiinan** sa mga bata ang kahalagahan ng paggalang sa nakatatanda.","translation":"The importance of respecting elders needs to be **stressed** to the children."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hiwa ng karneng baboy mula sa bahagi ng tiyan, na may magkakahalong patong ng taba at laman.
etymology: From Spanish `tiempo` (time), possibly referring to a cut of meat that takes time to cook tender. Often spelled as 'liempo'.
original_explanation: The holy grail of Pinoy ulam. That glorious slab of pork belly, whether inihaw, adobo, or deep-fried into chicharon. It's the reason your diet fails every weekend. It's the star of every handaan and the cause of many a tito's high blood pressure. Worth it.
usage_notes: A staple in Filipino cuisine. 'Inihaw na liempo' (grilled pork belly) is a national favorite.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ihaw kami ng **liyempo** sa beach.","translation":"We grilled **pork belly** at the beach."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong ulam ang sinigang na baboy na may **liyempo**.","translation":"My favorite dish is pork sinigang with **pork belly**."}]

translation: to be able to make someone happy; to be able to bring joy
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang magdulot ng kaligayahan o kasiyahan sa isang tao.
original_explanation: A level up from `makapagpangiti`. This is the goal of every birthday surprise, every Jollibee party, every K-Drama happy ending. It’s the ability to cause genuine happiness. "Wala nang mas makapagpapasaya sa isang magulang kundi ang makitang maayos ang kanyang mga anak."
usage_notes: Implies a deeper sense of joy or happiness than just a smile.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang simpleng 'salamat' ay sapat na para **makapagpasaya** sa kanya.","translation":"A simple 'thank you' is enough to **make him happy**."},{"sentence":"Nagtatrabaho siya sa abroad para **makapagpasaya** at mabigyan ng magandang buhay ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He works abroad to **be able to make happy** and give a good life to his family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging huli sa takdang oras o ang pagkakaroon ng antala sa isang gawain o proseso.
etymology: From `pagka-` (state of being) + `atraso` (delay), from Spanish `atraso` (delay, backwardness).
original_explanation: This is the default state of Manila traffic. It's the "Filipino time" stereotype personified. When your Grab driver is still 15 minutes away but the app says 2, pagkaatraso. When your internet provider promises to fix your connection today but shows up next week, pagkaatraso. It's the national pastime of waiting.
usage_notes: Used for delays in schedules, payments, or projects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaatraso** ng proyekto ay nagdulot ng malaking problema sa kumpanya.","translation":"The **delay** of the project caused a big problem for the company."},{"sentence":"Paumanhin po sa aking **pagkaatraso**, matindi po ang trapik.","translation":"My apologies for my **tardiness**, the traffic was terrible."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na madaling mainis, magalit, o magpakita ng pagkayamot.
original_explanation: This describes a person whose default mood is 'bugnot'. They're the human equivalent of a grumpy cat. They get annoyed easily, a walking 'Do Not Disturb' sign. If you have a 'tito' who's always complaining, or a boss who gets mad at the slightest mistake, sila 'yung **bugnutin**. You have to walk on eggshells around them.
usage_notes: Describes a personality trait or a recurring mood, not just a fleeting feeling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **bugnutin** si lolo mula nang magretiro siya sa trabaho.","translation":"Grandpa became **irritable** ever since he retired from work."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang kausapin ngayon, **bugnutin** 'yan kapag kulang sa tulog.","translation":"Don't talk to her now, she's **cranky** when she lacks sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o gawain ng paggalaw sa tubig sa pamamagitan ng mga kamay at paa.
original_explanation: Your one and only defense when the resort's infinity pool turns out to be 10 feet deep. Also, what you wish you could do to get away from your responsibilities.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of sports, recreation, or survival.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay ang kaniyang **paglangoy** kaya siya nanalo sa kompetisyon.","translation":"His **swimming** was excellent, which is why he won the competition."},{"sentence":"Ang **paglangoy** sa dagat ay isa sa mga paborito kong gawin tuwing tag-init.","translation":"**Swimming** in the sea is one of my favorite things to do during summer."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kulay ng malinis na kalangitan o malalim na dagat; isa sa mga pangunahing kulay.
original_explanation: The color of your Ateneo shirt, the water in El Nido (if you're lucky), and your feelings when you get 'seen-zoned.' It's the color of Monday blues after a long weekend and the checkmark on a verified celebrity's social media account.
usage_notes: Can be used as both a noun (the color blue) and an adjective (blue-colored). 'Bughaw' is a native Tagalog synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito niyang kulay ang **asul**.","translation":"Her favorite color is **blue**."},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng isang kahon na may **asul** na laso.","translation":"She received a box with a **blue** ribbon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng matinding panghihina o kawalan ng sigla, na halos wala nang lakas upang makakilos.
etymology: From 'pan-' (causative prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of 'lata' (weak, limp).
original_explanation: This is 'panlalambot's' bigger, more dramatic sibling. Yung feeling na hindi ka lang pagod, parang hihimatayin ka na. It's the 'I can't even' of physical states. Perfect description for your energy level after listening to a 3-hour meeting that could have been an email.
usage_notes: Indicates a more severe weakness than 'pagod' (tired) or 'panlalambot'. It implies a profound lack of energy, bordering on collapse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding init, nakaramdam siya ng biglaang **panlalata**.","translation":"Because of the intense heat, he felt a sudden **faintness**."},{"sentence":"Ang **panlalata** ay maaaring senyales ng dehydration.","translation":"**Lethargy** can be a sign of dehydration."}]

translation: the act of preparing or dressing up; adornment
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aayos sa sarili o sa isang lugar, kasama ang paglalagay ng mga palamuti o dekorasyon, bilang paghahanda sa isang okasyon.
etymology: `pag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `ga-` + `gayak`. The reduplication denotes a more thorough or festive preparation.
original_explanation: This is what you do for two hours before a party. The whole ritual: shower, skincare, makeup, choosing an outfit, rejecting that outfit, choosing another one, doing your hair... that's paggagayak. It's also what your barangay does before a fiesta, decking out the streets with banderitas. It's getting ready, but make it extra.
usage_notes: Implies a more elaborate or festive preparation than just 'paghahanda' (preparation). 'Paggayak' (without reduplication) is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang **paggagayak** ng plasa para sa darating na pista.","translation":"The **act of decorating** the plaza has begun for the upcoming fiesta."},{"sentence":"Ang tagal ng **paggagayak** mo, male-late na tayo!","translation":"Your **act of getting ready** is taking so long, we're going to be late!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing kilos ng pananalangin o pakikipag-usap sa Diyos o sa isang sinasamba sa hinaharap. Ito ang anyong panghinaharap ng pandiwang 'magdasal'.
original_explanation: Your response when your tita asks about your love life. "Ako po ay magdarasal na lang." It's the future tense of `magdasal`. It's what you promise to do before a big exam, after a major "sanaol" moment, or when your Grab driver is navigating a very tight eskinita.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb "magdasal" (to pray). The noun form with the same spelling refers to the person praying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magdarasal** ako para sa iyong mabilis na paggaling.","translation":"I **will pray** for your speedy recovery."},{"sentence":"Mamaya, **magdarasal** ang buong pamilya bago kumain.","translation":"Later, the whole family **will pray** before eating."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan o materyales na ginagamit sa pagtuturo. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa isang bagay na ginagamit sa pagturo ng direksyon o lokasyon.
original_explanation: This can be your teacher's old-school wooden stick, a fancy laser pointer in a corporate presentation, or even your lola's nguso (pursed lips) giving you directions. Anything used 'for pointing' or 'for teaching' falls under panturo. The prefix 'pan-' plus 'turo' (to point/to teach) makes it a super versatile word.
usage_notes: Derived from 'pan-' + 'turo' (point/teach). The meaning depends on which sense of 'turo' is used. It can mean 'pointer' or 'instructional material'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumagamit ang guro ng mga makukulay na larawan bilang kagamitang **panturo**.","translation":"The teacher uses colorful pictures as **teaching materials**."},{"sentence":"Kinuha niya ang patpat at ginawang **panturo** sa mapa.","translation":"He took the stick and used it as a **pointer** on the map."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang bagay, ideya, o pahayag na tinatanggap bilang totoo o tama ng isang tao o grupo.
etymology: From the root 'paniwala' (belief), which is derived from 'tiwala' (trust). This form functions as a verb ('is believed') or a noun ('a belief').
original_explanation: It's your 'truth' – whether it's a religious doctrine, a scientific fact, a conspiracy theory from your tito, or the chismis you heard from Marites. If you accept it as real, 'yan ang pinaniniwalaan mo.
usage_notes: Can function as a verb (is believed) or a noun (a belief, synonymous with 'paniniwala'). Context determines the function.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pinaniniwalaan** ng marami na magdudulot ito ng suwerte.","translation":"It **is believed** by many that this will bring good luck."},{"sentence":"Iba-iba ang **pinaniniwalaan** ng bawat tao pagdating sa relihiyon.","translation":"Each person has different **beliefs** when it comes to religion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng kasaganaan sa buhay, yaman, at kaginhawaan; malayo sa kahirapan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate #SanaAll goal. It's not just being rich (mayaman); it's living a comfortable, prosperous, and stable life. It's the opposite of "isang kahig, isang tuka." When your lola wishes you "kariwasaan," she's hoping you get that high-paying job, a nice house, and enough money to treat the whole family to Jollibee without checking your bank account first. It's the Filipino dream.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat literary term for prosperity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hangad ng bawat magulang ang **kariwasaan** para sa kanilang mga anak.","translation":"Every parent wishes for a **prosperous life** for their children."},{"sentence":"Nakamit niya ang **kariwasaan** dahil sa kanyang sipag at tiyaga.","translation":"He achieved **affluence** because of his diligence and perseverance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis na piraso ng bakal na binalutan ng sink (zinc) upang hindi kalawangin, karaniwang ginagamit bilang bubong ng bahay.
original_explanation: The official soundtrack of a rainy day in the Philippines. The louder the rain on your yero roof, the more justified you are to cancel all your plans and just sleep. Also, the thing your neighbor's cat uses as a runway at 3 AM.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the G.I. sheets used for roofing, often corrugated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lakas ng patak ng ulan sa aming bubong na **yero**.","translation":"The raindrops are so loud on our **galvanized iron** roof."},{"sentence":"Kailangang palitan ang mga kinakalawang na **yero** bago dumating ang tag-ulan.","translation":"The rusty **metal sheets** need to be replaced before the rainy season arrives."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang espasyo sa pagitan ng dalawang linya o patag na nagtatagpo. Tumutukoy din sa isang partikular na pananaw o paraan ng pagtingin sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Your "anggulo" is your take on things, like your best selfie angle or your hot take on the latest chismis. When someone says "Tingnan mo sa ibang anggulo," they're telling you to stop being stubborn and see it from another perspective, maybe even theirs. It's the geometric and intellectual version of finding your light.
usage_notes: Can be used literally in geometry/photography or figuratively for perspective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong hanapin ang tamang **anggulo** para maganda ang kuha ng litrato.","translation":"You need to find the right **angle** to take a good picture."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong tingnan ang problema sa ibang **anggulo**.","translation":"Try looking at the problem from a different **point of view**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagsasanay ng katawan upang mapabuti o mapanatili ang pisikal na kalusugan at kaangkupan.
original_explanation: That thing you promise to do every New Year's but only lasts 'til January 15. It's your Zumba session with the titas, your "beast mode" at the gym, or even just jogging around the block to burn off that extra rice. Paghehersisyo is the official term for your #FitnessGoals journey.
usage_notes: A common Tagalized word. The prefix `pag-` + reduplication of the first syllable (`e-` -> `he-`) indicates a continuous or habitual action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging bahagi na ng aking araw-araw na gawain ang **paghehersisyo**.","translation":"**Exercising** has become part of my daily routine."},{"sentence":"Inirekomenda ng doktor ang regular na **paghehersisyo** para sa kanya.","translation":"The doctor recommended regular **exercising** for him."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagpapakita ng pagtatampo o pagkayamot sa pamamagitan ng pagpapalabi o pagbabago ng ekspresyon ng mukha.
original_explanation: This is the OG "pabebe wave" before it was cool. It's when you push your lower lip out like a sad duckface because you didn't get the last piece of lechon, or your crush left you on 'seen'. It's the physical manifestation of 'tampo'.
usage_notes: Often confused with 'ngumuso' which is a more direct action of pointing with the lips. 'Ngumungo' implies the emotional state of sulking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ngumungo** ang bata dahil hindi siya binilhan ng laruan.","translation":"The child **pouted** because they didn't buy him a toy."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **ngumungo** diyan, hindi bagay sa'yo.","translation":"Stop **sulking** over there, it doesn't suit you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng fungus na karaniwang may katawang hugis-payong at tumutubo sa mamasa-masang lugar, na maaaring nakakain o nakalalason.
original_explanation: That thing you put on pizza or in your sizzling sisig. Parang lovelife ng iba, 'they sprout like mushrooms after the rain' - bigla na lang sumusulpot kung saan-saan. The English word 'mushroom' is also very commonly used.
usage_notes: The phrase "parang kabute" (like mushrooms) is a very common idiom used to describe something that appears or multiplies suddenly and rapidly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang adobong **kabute** na may halong tokwa.","translation":"Mushroom adobo with tofu is delicious."},{"sentence":"Nagkalat ang mga **kabute** sa gubat pagkatapos ng malakas na ulan.","translation":"Mushrooms were scattered in the forest after the heavy rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Paglalabas o pagkakaroon ng isang partikular na amoy.
original_explanation: The state of emitting a certain scent. Pwedeng mabango, pwedeng mabaho. "Nangangamoy bagong sahod!" (smells like payday!) or "Nangangamoy pawis ka na." (you're reeking of sweat). It's the nose's way of judging you.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa parehong kaaya-aya at hindi kaaya-ayang amoy. Ang konteksto ang nagdidikta ng konotasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nangangamoy** adobo ang buong bahay.","translation":"The whole house **smells like** adobo."},{"sentence":"Magpalit ka na ng damit, **nangangamoy** araw ka na.","translation":"Go change your clothes, you're **reeking of** sun (i.e., sweat from being outdoors)."}]

meaning_filipino: Maglabas ng malakas at mahabang tunog na tulad ng sa aso o lobo.
original_explanation: This is what your neighbor's dog does at 3 AM for no reason. Or what your friend does when they see their K-Pop idol in a concert. "Nang makita niya ang presyo ng bilihin, halos umulol siya sa gulat."
usage_notes: Primarily used for dogs and wolves, but can be used metaphorically for humans expressing extreme emotion. The root 'ulol' also means 'crazy' or 'rabid' as an adjective, but the verb form specifically means 'to howl'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing kabilugan ng buwan, naririnig naming **umulol** ang mga aso sa malayo.","translation":"Every full moon, we hear the dogs **howl** in the distance."},{"sentence":"**Umulol** sa tuwa ang mga tagahanga nang lumabas ang kanilang idolo.","translation":"The fans **howled** in delight when their idol came out."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng impeksiyon sa balat na dulot ng fungus na karaniwang tumutubo sa singit at mga hita, na nagdudulot ng pangangati at pamumula.
original_explanation: 'Yan yung resulta 'pag 'di ka nagpunas nang maigi after maligo o 'pag na-trap ang pawis sa singit mo. Parang buni na na-assign sa maling lugar. Medyo TMI (Too Much Information) i-discuss sa public, pero common problem 'to, lalo na sa mga atleta.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit sa kontekstong medikal o sa pang-araw-araw na usapan tungkol sa kalusugan at kalinisan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang pasyente na gumamit ng antifungal cream para sa kanyang **hadhad**.","translation":"The doctor advised the patient to use an antifungal cream for his **jock itch**."},{"sentence":"Naku, ang kati-kati ng **hadhad** ko!","translation":"Oh no, my **jock itch** is so itchy!"}]

translation: to wear a bandolier or sash; to put on a sword belt (as a group)
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay na paglalagay o pagsusuot ng sakbat, tulad ng sinturon ng espada o bandolera, kadalasan ng isang grupo.
etymology: From 'sakbat' (sash, sword belt) + suffix '-an' (denoting a reciprocal or group action).
original_explanation: Imagine the Katipuneros or a squad of soldiers all gearing up at the same time, putting on their sword belts or sashes across their chests. That's sakbatan. It's the group-action version of getting ready for battle, very #SquadGoals, 1896 edition.
usage_notes: A rare, literary word. The '-an' suffix here implies a collective or reciprocal action, meaning people are doing it to each other or all at once.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-utos ang heneral, at ang mga kawal ay nagsimulang mag-**sakbatan** ng kanilang mga espada.","translation":"The general gave the order, and the soldiers began to **put on their sword belts**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng puwersa upang maialis o mapagalaw ang isang bagay palapit sa pinagmumulan ng puwersa.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your friend who doesn't want to leave the party yet. 'Tara na!' sabay hila. It's also what you do to the 'PUSH' door because you didn't read the sign. Classic. Pwede ring emotional pull, 'yung 'hinihila ka pabalik ng nakaraan.' Hugot!
usage_notes: The counterpart of itulak (to push).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**hilahin** mo ang pinto para bumukas.","translation":"Please **pull** the door to open it."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **hilahin** pababa sa mga problema mo.","translation":"Don't **pull** me down with your problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng kapahamakan, kasawian, o anumang uri ng pinsala sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you trust the wrong 'marites' and make a life-altering decision based on their chismis. Your bad choices will be the **ikapanganyaya** of your future. It's the ultimate 'you played yourself' moment that leads to major regret.
usage_notes: This is a formal and literary term, often used to describe the cause of a grave or serious negative outcome. The root 'panganyaya' itself means misfortune or peril.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kaniyang pagiging pabaya ang **ikapanganyaya** ng buong pamilya.","translation":"His negligence will **cause the misfortune** of the whole family."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumawa ng desisyon na maaaring **ikapanganyaya** ng iyong kinabukasan.","translation":"Don't make a decision that could **cause harm** to your future."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng panliligaw o pagpapakita ng romantikong interes sa isang tao.
etymology: From 'diga' + '-han' suffix. 'Diga' possibly from Spanish 'diga' (tell/speak), implying speaking words of love.
original_explanation: This is old-school Pinoy flirting, a level up from "paramdam." It's the act of making your move, the "panliligaw" itself. While 'ligawan' is more common, 'digahan' has a more classic, almost theatrical vibe, like something you'd hear in a harana. "Digahan mo na, baka maunahan ka pa ng iba!"
usage_notes: A more colloquial or dated term for 'ligawan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal na niyang gustong **digahan** si Maria.","translation":"He has long wanted **to court** Maria."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiya, **digahan** mo na ang crush mo!","translation":"Don't be shy, go and **woo** your crush!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkain na gawa sa itlog na binati at niluto sa mantika o mantequilla, karaniwang inihahain tuwing almusal.
original_explanation: The default breakfast for when you're too lazy to cook anything else. Just beat some eggs, add salt, maybe some milk or tomatoes, and pray it doesn't stick to the pan. The official "pampuno sa ulam" when the budget is tight.
usage_notes: While 'binating itlog' is the direct translation, the English term 'scrambled egg' is widely used and understood in restaurants and homes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng **scrambled egg** at sinangag para sa almusal.","translation":"I want **scrambled egg** and fried rice for breakfast."},{"sentence":"Pakilagyan ng keso ang **scrambled egg** ko, pakiusap.","translation":"Please add cheese to my **scrambled egg**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang karanasan, tao, o bagay na mananatili sa alaala at hindi makakalimutan.
original_explanation: Your first love, your first heartbreak, the first time you tasted authentic ramen, or that time you tripped in front of everyone at the mall. These are core memories. Sila 'yung mga di-malilimutan. The ultimate 'sana all' is to be someone's di-malilimutan moment for a good reason, not a bad one.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwan at makahulugang pang-uri para sa mga di-malilimutang pangyayari o tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming paglalakbay sa Batanes ay isang **di-malilimutang** karanasan.","translation":"Our trip to Batanes was an **unforgettable** experience."},{"sentence":"Ang kabutihan niya sa akin ay isang bagay na **di-malilimutan**.","translation":"His kindness to me is something **unforgettable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang radioactive na metalikong elementong kemikal na may simbolong Cf at atomic number na 98.
etymology: From English 'Californium', named after the state and university of California.
original_explanation: That one really hard question in your high school chemistry quiz that you just guessed. It's named after California, not a showbiz love team. You'll probably never use this word unless you're a nuclear physicist or a die-hard fan of the periodic table.
usage_notes: This is a direct loanword, a scientific term. The spelling is adapted to Filipino phonetics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Kalipornium** ay isang elementong gawa ng tao at hindi natural na matatagpuan sa daigdig.","translation":"**Californium** is a man-made element and is not naturally found on earth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aklat o hanay ng mga aklat na naglalaman ng impormasyon tungkol sa iba't ibang paksa, karaniwang nakaayos nang paalpabeto.
original_explanation: The OG Wikipedia. Before Google, if you had a school project, you'd have to lug this heavy, multi-volume beast from the library. It's what your parents used to win arguments before they could just search online.
usage_notes: A somewhat dated term, with 'ensiklopedya' being more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahanap ko ang sagot sa aking takdang-aralin sa isang lumang **palakipan**.","translation":"I found the answer to my homework in an old **encyclopedia**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paraan ng pagluluto kung saan ang pagkain ay naluluto sa pamamagitan ng singaw ng kumukulong tubig.
etymology: From 'singaw' (steam) with affix 'pina- -an' denoting action done upon something.
original_explanation: The cooking method for when you're on a diet, or when you want your siomai and fish to be perfectly moist. It's the 'healthy' option on the menu, cooked using the hot vapor from boiling water. Basically, food cooked in a sauna.
usage_notes: Can also function as a verb in object-focus form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masustansya ang **pinasingawan** na isda.","translation":"**Steamed** fish is nutritious."},{"sentence":"**Pinasingawan** niya ang mga gulay para hindi mawala ang sustansya.","translation":"She **steamed** the vegetables so the nutrients wouldn't be lost."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang mataas; may sukat na higit sa karaniwan patayo o paitaas.
etymology: From the intensifier prefix "napaka-" and the root word "taas" (high).
original_explanation: That condo in BGC that seems to touch the clouds? **Napakataas**. The standards your parents set for your love life? **Napakataas** din. It's the superlative of 'up there'.
usage_notes: Describes physical height of objects or abstract concepts like standards, prices, or fever. Add "-ng" for following nouns, e.g., "napakataas na pangarap".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napakataas** ng mga gusali sa Makati.","translation":"The buildings in Makati are **very tall**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magtakda ng **napakataas** na ekspektasyon para hindi ka masaktan.","translation":"Don't set **very high** expectations so you won't get hurt."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos o desisyon na ginawa nang hindi bukal sa kalooban o labag sa sariling kagustuhan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you say "yes" but your soul screams "no." Ginagawa mo yung isang bagay na laban sa loob mo. Like agreeing to go to a family reunion when you'd rather binge-watch a series, or smiling at a customer who's been yelling at you for 10 minutes. It's the ultimate 'tiis-ganda' or 'tiis-trabaho' move.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang kilos na ginawa nang walang tunay na pahintulot o pagnanais. Ang kasalungat nito ay 'bukal sa loob'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumayag siyang sumama, ngunit halatang **laban sa loob** niya.","translation":"She agreed to come, but it was obviously **against her will**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bayad para sa pagsakay sa isang pampublikong sasakyan tulad ng dyip, bus, o tren.
etymology: From `paN-` + `pasahe`. `Pasahe` is from Spanish 'pasaje', meaning passage or fare. The `paN-` prefix (`pam-` before 'p') is used to form nouns indicating payment for something.
original_explanation: The daily sacrifice you offer to the gods of commute. It's the reason your 100-peso bill magically turns into loose change. "Manong, bayad po!" is the sacred chant to hand this over. In modern times, it's the load in your Beep card or the amount you pray is "sakto lang" for your Grab ride.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to payment for a ride or passage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtaas na naman ang **pamasahe** sa dyip.","translation":"The jeepney **fare** has increased again."},{"sentence":"Wala akong barya para sa **pamasahe**, buo ang pera ko.","translation":"I don't have coins for the **fare**; my money is in a whole bill."}]

translation: to have someone take care of
meaning_filipino: Ibigay o ipagkatiwala sa iba ang responsibilidad ng pag-aalaga sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
original_explanation: Eto yung ginagawa mo sa aso mo kapag aalis ka for the weekend: "Ipaalaga mo muna kay beshie." O kaya yung ginagawa ng mga OFW sa kanilang mga anak. It's the ultimate trust fall—handing over something or someone precious for another person to look after.
usage_notes: Isang causative verb na nagpapahiwatig ng paglilipat ng tungkulin ng pag-aalaga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kanino mo **ipaaalaga** ang mga halaman habang nasa bakasyon ka?","translation":"To whom will you **have** your plants **taken care of** while you're on vacation?"},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **ipaalaga** muna ang bata sa kanyang ina.","translation":"She decided to **have her mother take care of** the child for a while."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-ismid, pagpapakita ng paghamak o hindi pagsang-ayon sa pamamagitan ng pag-iling o pagbaling ng mukha.
original_explanation: That "taray" look your tita gives you when you're wearing ripped jeans at a family reunion. It's the silent, judgmental head turn of a kontrabida in a teleserye. It's the physical manifestation of "eww" or "how dare you." More than just a side-eye, it's a full-on dismissal.
usage_notes: A very specific non-verbal gesture of contempt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **pag-iring** lang ang isinukli niya sa alok na tulong.","translation":"She only returned a **sneer** to the offer of help."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa kanyang **pag-iring** ang hindi pagsang-ayon sa plano.","translation":"Her disapproval of the plan was very evident in her **scornful look**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng magiliw o mapaglarong pag-uugali upang makakuha ng atensyon, lalo na sa romantikong paraan.
original_explanation: The art of 'pabebe' with a goal. It's the subtle hair flip, the extra-long eye contact, the witty banter in the DMs. It's not a crime, it's a skill. When your friend says "Ang landi mo!", it can be a compliment or a warning, depending on who you're flirting with.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (e.g., "puro ka landi") or an adjective ('malandi'). The connotation can range from playful to pejorative depending on context and tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na nga 'yang **landi** mo at mag-aral ka na.","translation":"Stop your **flirtatiousness** and just study."},{"sentence":"Ang lakas ng **landi** ng babaeng iyon sa lahat ng lalaki.","translation":"That woman's **flirtatiousness** towards all the men is intense."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mayroon kang regular na sekswal na relasyon nang walang romantikong pangako o ugnayan. Isang akronim para sa "fuck buddy".
original_explanation: Fubu is the no-strings-attached, 'walang label' setup before 'walang label' was cool. It's short for "fuck buddy." It's purely physical, no feelings involved (supposedly). It's the situationship your Tita warns you about, but you get into anyway.
usage_notes: A very direct and informal slang term. Used in casual conversations among peers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi sila mag-jowa, **fubu** lang daw.","translation":"They're not a couple, just **fuck buddies**, apparently."}]

translation: to hold or celebrate (despite difficulties); to get through
meaning_filipino: Isagawa o idaos ang isang pagdiriwang, pagpupulong, o anumang okasyon, kadalasan sa kabila ng mga hadlang o kakulangan.
original_explanation: This is the Filipino spirit of "the show must go on." Kahit gipit, you find a way to celebrate a birthday. Kahit umuulan, the fiesta continues. It's about making something happen, pushing through adversity. "Kahit simple lang, basta mairaos natin ang Pasko nang magkakasama." It's resourcefulness and resilience in verb form.
usage_notes: Often implies overcoming some difficulty or limitation to make an event happen. A close synonym is 'idaos', but 'iraos' carries a stronger connotation of overcoming challenges.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinikap nilang **iraos** ang kasal sa kabila ng biglaang pagbuhos ng ulan.","translation":"They managed **to hold** the wedding despite the sudden downpour."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mairaos** ang proyektong ito bago matapos ang buwan.","translation":"We need **to get this project through** before the end of the month."}]

translation: state of being startled or wide-eyed in shock
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng biglaang pagkabigla o pagkatakot, na karaniwang may kasamang panlalaki ng mata.
original_explanation: Your face when your mom walks into your room at 3 AM and you're still scrolling through TikTok. It's the 'nahuli ka' look. That wide-eyed, deer-in-the-headlights moment of pure, unadulterated shock.
usage_notes: Specifically implies being startled with wide eyes. More intense than 'pagkabigla'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos mahulog siya sa kanyang upuan sa **pagkagulilat**.","translation":"He almost fell from his chair in **shock**."},{"sentence":"Bakas sa mukha ng bata ang **pagkagulilat** nang biglang tumunog ang kulog.","translation":"The child's face showed his **startled state** when the thunder suddenly roared."}]

translation: to knock or tap on something repeatedly
meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit na katukin o pindutin nang marahan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The action that produces the 'kalatok'. This is what you do when you're impatient waiting outside a locked door. O 'yung ginagawa ng prof mo sa table para makuha ang atensyon ng klase. 'Huwag mo ngang **kalatukin** 'yang ballpen mo, ang ingay!'
usage_notes: Implies a repeated or rhythmic tapping, often lighter than 'katukin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kalatukin** ang salamin ng akwaryum; natatakot ang mga isda.","translation":"Don't **tap on** the aquarium glass; you're scaring the fish."},{"sentence":"Naiinis ako kapag may **kumakalatok** sa mesa habang ako'y nagtatrabaho.","translation":"I get annoyed when someone **repeatedly taps** on the table while I'm working."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na hayagang tumututol, sumasalungat, o hindi sumasang-ayon sa isang panukala, patakaran, o opinyon.
etymology: Nagmula sa "man-" + pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng ugat ("tu-") + "tutol" (hindi pagsang-ayon).
original_explanation: The 'kontrabida' in a meeting who always has a "but..." or "I object!". They're not necessarily wrong, they just see things differently. In a family setting, this is the tita who questions your life choices during reunions. On a larger scale, they're the activists on the streets.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na termino para sa isang taong tumututol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging may **manunutol** sa bawat bagong patakaran na ipinapatupad.","translation":"There is always an **objector** to every new policy being implemented."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng martilyo upang pukpukin, ipasok, o basagin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The verb form of that DIY energy. It's the action of repeatedly hitting something with a hammer. Can be literal, like hammering a nail, or figurative, like when your boss 'martilyuhins' you with deadlines. 'Huwag mo akong martilyuhin ng mga tanong!' (Don't hammer me with questions!).
usage_notes: An object-focus verb. The thing being hammered is the 'ang' phrase or its pronoun equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **martilyuhin** nang dahan-dahan ang pako para hindi bumaluktot.","translation":"You need to **hammer** the nail slowly so it doesn't bend."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **martilyuhin** ang pader sa galit niya.","translation":"He wants **to hammer** the wall in his anger."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panahon ng taon kung kailan matindi ang sikat ng araw at kakaunti o walang pag-ulan.
original_explanation: The official season of beach trips, halo-halo, and 3-in-1 coffee na nagiging iced coffee. It's when your electric fan becomes your best friend and you sweat in places you didn't know you could. Araw-araw feeling mo nasa sauna ka.
usage_notes: In the Philippines, this corresponds to the dry season, typically from March to May.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing **tag-araw**, paborito naming pumunta sa beach.","translation":"During the **dry season**, we love going to the beach."},{"sentence":"Napakainit talaga kapag **tag-araw** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"It's really hot during **summer** in the Philippines."}]

translation: to allow oneself to be cheated
meaning_filipino: Hayaan ang sarili na malinlang o maloko ng iba; magpatalo nang sadya.
original_explanation: When you're playing with your 5-year-old pamangkin and you let them win in a race. That's you, nagpa-daya. Or in a more 'hugot' sense, it's when you know someone is playing with your feelings, but you let them anyway. "Alam ko namang niloloko niya lang ako, pero nag-padaya pa rin ako." Ouch.
usage_notes: The 'pa-' prefix indicates allowing the action of the root word ('daya' - cheat) to happen to oneself. Often used in the form 'magpadaya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **padaya** sa mga matatamis niyang salita.","translation":"Don't **allow yourself to be deceived** by his sweet words."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pampasaherong sasakyan na may regular na ruta at humihinto sa mga takdang lugar upang magsakay at magbaba ng mga pasahero.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "bus," pinaikling anyo ng "omnibus."
original_explanation: Ang Hari ng EDSA. Ang sasakyang nagturo sa ating lahat ng pasensya, diskarte sa pagsiksik, at ang abilidad na makatulog kahit nakatayo. Dito mo maririnig ang classic lines na "Bayad po," "Para po," at ang walang kamatayang "Sampu pa, aalis na!" kahit mukha nang lata ng sardinas sa loob.
usage_notes: Karaniwang binibigkas na /bas/, hindi /bəs/ tulad sa Ingles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumakay ako ng **bus** papuntang Baguio.","translation":"I rode a **bus** going to Baguio."},{"sentence":"Laging puno ang **bus** tuwing rush hour.","translation":"The **bus** is always full during rush hour."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kasuotang pambabae na isinusuot mula sa baywang pababa.
original_explanation: The OG uniform for Maria Clara, but now it's what you wear when you want to feel cute or when it's too hot for pants. From mini to maxi, it's a staple in every Pinay's closet, perfect for that "dalagang Pilipina" look or a "sana all" OOTD post.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si Ana ng bagong **palda** para sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"Ana bought a new **skirt** for her birthday."},{"sentence":"Masyadong maikli ang **palda** mo, baka masita ka ng lola mo.","translation":"Your **skirt** is too short, your grandma might scold you."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang itulad o ipantay sa iba upang makita ang pagkakatulad o pagkakaiba.
etymology: ma- (ability) + i- (object focus) + ha- (future tense repetition) + hambing (compare)
original_explanation: This is what you say when you see your ex's new partner and you can't help but... well, 'maihahambing' mo talaga. It's the moment you size something up against another, like comparing the price of Jollibee to McDo, or your current salary to your previous one.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of evaluation, judgment, or finding similarities. The future tense implies a potential for comparison.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda niya ay hindi **maihahambing** sa iba.","translation":"Her beauty **cannot be compared** to others."},{"sentence":"Walang **maihahambing** sa sarap ng luto ni nanay.","translation":"Nothing **can compare** to mom's cooking."}]

translation: to place oneself; to know one's place
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtungo o pagpwesto sa isang angkop na lokasyon; ang pagkilos nang naayon sa posisyon, estado, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The classic Filipino parental advisory: 'Matuto kang lumugar!' It means know your place, stay in your lane, and don't be a 'feeling close'. It's about having situational awareness, whether you're a guest in someone's house or a junior employee in a board meeting. It's the antidote to being epal.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pautos o pampayong tono, na nagsasabi sa isang tao na kumilos nang naaangkop ayon sa kanilang papel o sa kontekstong panlipunan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang bisita, dapat marunong kang **lumugar** sa bahay ng may bahay.","translation":"As a guest, you should know how **to place yourself** (behave appropriately) in the host's house."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya marunong **lumugar** kaya marami ang naiinis sa kanya.","translation":"He doesn't know **his place**, which is why many are annoyed with him."}]

translation: to be made an accomplice; to be conspired with
meaning_filipino: Maging kasama o katuwang sa isang lihim na plano o sabwatan, kadalasan ay para sa masamang layunin.
original_explanation: When you get roped into your friend's scheme to surprise-prank another friend, you become `masabwat`. It’s being an accomplice, whether for a surprise birthday party or for hiding the fact that you both ate the last piece of cake. It’s teamwork, but with a hint of secrecy and potential trouble.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation of being involved in a conspiracy or plot, but can be used playfully for harmless secrets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sinumang mapatunayang **nasabwat** sa krimen ay mananagot din sa batas.","translation":"Anyone proven to have been **made an accomplice** in the crime will also be held accountable by the law."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong idamay diyan, ayokong **masabwat** sa kalokohan ninyo.","translation":"Don't involve me in that, I don't want to be **part of your conspiracy** of foolishness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makapal na tela na may hinabing disenyo o larawan, karaniwang isinasabit sa dingding bilang palamuti o sining.
original_explanation: That giant, fancy cloth hanging in your rich tita's house that you're not allowed to touch. It's like a painting but made of thread, usually depicting some historical or mythical scene. Think of it as the analog, high-end version of a poster.
usage_notes: A very rare word in modern conversation. Most would just use the English word 'tapestry' or a more general term like 'palamuti sa dingding' (wall decoration). The standard Filipino spelling is 'tapiseriya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lumang **tapiserya** ay nagpapakita ng isang tagpo mula sa kasaysayan ng Espanya.","translation":"The old **tapestry** shows a scene from Spanish history."},{"sentence":"Mahal ang halaga ng mga antigong **tapiserya** mula sa Europa.","translation":"Antique **tapestries** from Europe are very expensive."}]

translation: bar chow, food appetizer eaten with alcoholic drinks
meaning_filipino: Pagkain, karaniwang maalat o mamantika, na isinasabay sa pag-inom ng alak, serbesa, o iba pang inuming nakalalasing.
etymology: Mula sa `pang-` at `pulutan` (mula sa `pulot`, na nangangahulugang 'damputin'). Literal na 'para sa pagpulot [gamit ang daliri habang umiinom]'.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of every 'inuman' session. It's the food you munch on to keep you from getting drunk too fast. Sisig, crispy pata, chicharon bulaklak, mani (peanuts)... the list goes on. It's not a full meal, it's a 'pampabagal ng tama.' The perfect partner for your Red Horse or San Mig Light.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-espesipikong terminong pangkultura na may kaugnayan sa kultura ng pag-inom ng mga Pilipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-order tayo ng sisig para gawing **pangpulutan**.","translation":"Let's order sisig to have as our **bar chow**."},{"sentence":"Kahit mani lang, basta may **pangpulutan**, masaya na ang inuman.","translation":"Even if it's just peanuts, as long as there's **food to go with the drinks**, the drinking session is happy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang masidhing damdamin ng pagmamahal, pagtatangi, o pagnanais para sa isang tao, bagay, o gawain.
original_explanation: The OG 'hugot' word. It's deeper than 'gusto' (like/want) but can be less formal than 'mahal' (love). 'Ano ang **ibig** mong sabihin?' ('What do you mean?') is the polite way of saying 'WTF are you talking about?'. As a noun, it's the kind of love they write poems about.
usage_notes: Often used as a pseudo-verb to mean 'want'. 'Ibig sabihin' is a set phrase meaning 'meaning' or 'it means'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **ibig** para sa bayan ay hindi matatawaran.","translation":"His **love** for the country is immeasurable."},{"sentence":"**Ibig** kong maglakbay sa buong mundo.","translation":"I **want** to travel the whole world."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **ibig** sabihin ng salitang ito?","translation":"What is the **meaning** of this word?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakasulat na katibayan na natanggap ang isang partikular na halaga ng pera o mga kalakal bilang bayad.
