etymology: Likely a contracted or variant form of `patalisin` (from root `talis`, meaning 'sharpness'). The form has become standard in many regions.
original_explanation: What you do to a kitchen knife before slicing the ingredients for adobo, or what you do to your wit before a debate. It's the act of making something dull sharp and effective. Parang pag-review bago mag-exam, you're sharpening your mind!
usage_notes: A common verb for sharpening blades. `Hasain` is a more formal synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**patain** mo naman itong kutsilyo, mapurol na.","translation":"Can you please **sharpen** this knife, it's already dull."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **patain** ang dulo ng lapis bago gamitin.","translation":"You need to **sharpen** the tip of the pencil before using it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aayos at paglalagay ng mga gamit sa loob ng isang lalagyan tulad ng maleta, kahon, o bag para sa paglalakbay o paglilipat.
original_explanation: The official start of your vacation! It's the verb form of what you do the night before a flight, trying to fit a week's worth of OOTDs and pasalubong into one carry-on bag to avoid baggage fees. 'Mag-impake ka na!' is the battle cry of every excited (or stressed) traveler.
usage_notes: The root word is often used as a verb itself in commands, e.g., "Impake mo na 'yan!" (Pack that up!). Verb conjugations include "mag-impake", "nag-impake", "nag-iimpake", "mag-iimpake".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang mag-**impake** para sa biyahe namin bukas.","translation":"I need to **pack** for our trip tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **impake**hin ang iyong pasaporte at tiket.","translation":"Don't forget to **pack** your passport and ticket."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa kalagayang lubhang kaawa-awa, hamak, at kasuklam-suklam.
etymology: From ka- (denoting quality) + reduplication of dusta (wretched, from Sanskrit 'duṣṭa').
original_explanation: This is when a situation is so bad, it's beyond 'nakakaawa.' Think of the living conditions in a disaster zone or how you feel after your 13th-month pay disappears in one day of Christmas shopping. It's that level of tragic.
usage_notes: The reduplication 'dusta-dusta' intensifies the meaning, making it 'most deplorable' or 'utterly wretched.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kadusta-dusta** niyang kalagayan ay bunga ng maraming maling desisyon sa buhay.","translation":"His **deplorable** condition is the result of many wrong decisions in life."},{"sentence":"Nakatira sila sa isang **kadusta-dusta** na barung-barong.","translation":"They live in a **wretched** shanty."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapalipad at paglalaro ng saranggola o borador.
etymology: From Spanish 'volador' (flyer, flying thing). The Spanish 'v' is often pronounced and written as 'b' in Tagalog.
original_explanation: To fly a kite. A classic Filipino childhood summer activity, usually done in an open field. Involves a lot of running, getting tangled in strings, and yelling "taas pa!" (higher!). The adult version is trying to make your dreams take flight despite strong winds of adversity. Charot.
usage_notes: 'Saranggola' is a more common term for kite, but 'borador' is also widely understood, especially in certain regions. 'Guryon' is another synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing tag-araw, paborito ng mga bata na **magborador** sa bukid.","translation":"Every summer, it's the children's favorite activity **to fly a kite** in the fields."},{"sentence":"Naisipan naming **magborador** sa tabing-dagat dahil malakas ang hangin.","translation":"We decided **to fly a kite** by the seashore because the wind is strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa bilang na higit sa isa; para sa malaking bilang o dami. Sa balarila, ito ang anyong pangmaramihan ng isang salita.
original_explanation: This is the 'for the whole barangay' mode. When you buy 'pangmarami' at the palengke, you're buying in bulk. In grammar, it's the plural form ('mga bata' vs 'bata'). It's the opposite of 'solo flight'. Think of it as the Costco or S&R version of anything—bigger, more, and meant for sharing (or hoarding).
usage_notes: Can be used in a grammatical context (plural form) or a general context (for many people/items).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'sila' ay isang panghalip na **pangmarami**.","translation":"'They' is a **plural** pronoun."},{"sentence":"Bumili tayo ng bigas na **pangmarami** para mas makamura.","translation":"Let's buy rice **in bulk** to save money."}]

meaning_filipino: Dahan-dahang iurong o isulong ang isang bagay; ilipat nang paunti-unti.
original_explanation: This is how you move furniture when you're alone and don't want to scratch the floor. `Paisurin mo lang`, like how you slowly slide out of a family gathering you don't want to be in. Just a little bit at a time until you're at the door.
usage_notes: The phrase "nang unti-unti" (gradually) is often added for emphasis but is inherent in the word's meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paisurin** mo nang kaunti ang mesa para magkasya ang isa pang silya.","translation":"**Move** the table **incrementally** so another chair can fit."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **paisurin** ang mga sasakyan upang makadaan ang ambulansya.","translation":"The cars need to be **moved gradually** to let the ambulance pass."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagluha at pag-iyak bilang pagpapahayag ng matinding damdamin tulad ng kalungkutan, sakit, o kagalakan.
original_explanation: The national past-time after watching a dramatic teleserye finale or a heartbreaking Thai commercial. It's the body's way of saying, "This hugot is too real." Sometimes happens out of joy, like when your food delivery finally arrives.
usage_notes: A fundamental human action and a very common verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umiyak** siya nang buong gabi dahil sa lungkot.","translation":"She **cried** the whole night because of sadness."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot **umiyak** kung kailangan mo.","translation":"Don't be afraid **to cry** if you need to."}]

translation: to send; to be carried away (emotionally)
meaning_filipino: 1. Mag-utos o magpahintulot na dalhin ang isang bagay sa isang lugar o tao. 2. Hayaan ang sarili na maimpluwensyahan o madominahan ng isang malakas na damdamin.
etymology: From 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'dala' (to carry). Literally 'to cause to be carried'.
original_explanation: The OFW anthem. This is what your relatives abroad do every month: magpadala ng pera or a balikbayan box. It's the core of the remittance economy. But wait, there's more! It also means to get carried away by your feelings. 'Huwag kang magpadala sa galit mo.' (Don't be carried away by your anger.) It's the ultimate 'hugot' verb.
usage_notes: The two meanings (send vs. be emotionally influenced) are distinct and very common. Context will make it clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas ako **magpapadala** ng pera para sa pamilya ko sa probinsya.","translation":"Tomorrow I will **send** money to my family in the province."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan ko siyang huwag **magpadala** sa sabi-sabi ng iba.","translation":"I told her not to **be carried away** by what others say."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa panitikan; may katangian ng sining ng pagsulat at pagpapahayag.
original_explanation: For your inner bookworm or creative writer. If it's pampanitikan, it's something you'd discuss in your Filipino class, like a Florante at Laura meme or a "spoken word" piece about your ex. It's high-brow, artsy-fartsy stuff, but make it Filipino.
usage_notes: Describes works, styles, or discussions related to literature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagwagi siya sa isang **pampanitikan** na patimpalak.","translation":"She won in a **literary** contest."},{"sentence":"Malalim ang kahulugan ng mga simbolong ginamit sa akdang **pampanitikan** na iyon.","translation":"The symbols used in that **literary** work have deep meaning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong walang hanapbuhay o pinagkakakitaan.
original_explanation: The official status of many fresh grads before they land their first job. Also known as "tambay," "palamunin," or "nag-aabang ng ayuda." It's that phase in life where your main job is to browse JobStreet and update your LinkedIn profile while dodging your tita's questions about when you're getting a job.
usage_notes: A very direct and common term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipino ang naging **walang-trabaho** dahil sa pandemya.","translation":"Many Filipinos became **unemployed** because of the pandemic."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang buhay kapag **walang-trabaho**.","translation":"Life is hard when you are **jobless**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang patag na ibabaw ng isang silid o gusali na tinatapakan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'suelo' na nangangahulugang 'lupa' o 'sahig'.
original_explanation: Yung nilalakaran mo sa loob ng bahay na kailangan laging may tsinelas para di ka mapagalitan ni Mama. Also, the stage for your TikTok dance challenges. Huwag malito sa 'sweldo' (salary), kahit pareho silang mabilis madumihan at kailangan ng maintenance.
usage_notes: Habang ang 'sahig' ay ang pangkalahatang termino, ang 'suwelo' ay karaniwang ginagamit para sa mga yari sa semento, baldosa, o kahoy sa loob ng isang istraktura.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpagulong siya ng bola sa makintab na **suwelo**.","translation":"He rolled a ball on the shiny **floor**."},{"sentence":"Basain mo ang basahan at punasan ang **suwelo** sa kusina.","translation":"Wet the rag and wipe the **floor** in the kitchen."}]

translation: to treasure, to hold dear, to cherish
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng sukdulang pagpapahalaga, pag-ibig, o pag-iingat sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is next-level 'mahalin'. It's not just loving something, it's treating it like a rare Pokémon card or the last piece of chicharon. It's the 'ingatan mo 'yan, ha?' kind of love. You 'pakamahalin' a family heirloom, a promise from your SO, or that one perfect photo where you actually look good.
usage_notes: The 'paka-' prefix intensifies the root word, implying 'to do something to the utmost'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat mong **pakamahalin** ang tiwalang ibinigay niya sa iyo.","translation":"You must **treasure** the trust she gave you."},{"sentence":"**Pakamahalin** mo ang mga huling sandali ninyo nang magkasama.","translation":"**Cherish** your last moments together."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pandiwa sa aspektong panghinaharap na tumutukoy sa gagawing pagluluto sa ibabaw ng baga o apoy.
original_explanation: This is the 'plano' stage. 'Yong text mo sa group chat: "Guys, **mag-iihaw** kami sa Sabado, punta kayo!" It's the promise of future inihaw na liempo and good times. The future tense of happiness.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong panghinaharap ng 'mag-ihaw', na nagsasaad ng intensyon o plano na magluto sa paraang pag-iihaw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mamayang gabi, **mag-iihaw** kami ng barbecue sa bakuran.","translation":"Later tonight, we **will grill** barbecue in the yard."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **mag-iihaw** ng mais para sa ating meryenda?","translation":"Who **will grill** the corn for our snack?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging maselan, pabebe, o labis na pag-arte sa kilos o pananalita na hindi natural.
etymology: From ka- + arte (from Spanish 'arte' meaning art, but used in Filipino to mean affectation) + -han.
original_explanation: That extra-ness you didn't ask for. When your friend refuses to eat at a carinderia because "it's, like, so unhygienic?" or someone who has a full-blown dramatic monologue over a minor inconvenience. It's the opposite of "chill." It's the "ma-art" level-up.
usage_notes: Often used with a negative or teasing connotation. 'Kaartihan' is a common variant with the same meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na nga 'yang **kaartehan** mo, kumain ka na lang.","translation":"Just stop your **fussiness** and just eat."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa sobrang **kaartehan**, wala tuloy siyang nagustuhan sa mga pagpipilian.","translation":"Because of so much **pickiness**, she didn't like any of the choices."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap o utos na alisin ang kasuotan sa katawan ng iba.
original_explanation: The command given to a toddler who just played in the mud. 'Anak, pahubad na, ang dumi mo!' Not to be confused with what happens in a steamy romance novel, though it could be that too. Context is key!
usage_notes: This is a causative request or command form. 'Pa-' asks someone to perform the root word's action on someone/something else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pahubad** mo na ang basang damit sa bata bago siya magkasakit.","translation":"**Have** the child **undress** from the wet clothes before he gets sick."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng doktor, '**Pahubad** po ng pang-itaas para ma-check ko ang likod ninyo.'","translation":"The doctor said, '**Please take off** your top so I can check your back.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ipinapatong sa iba upang hindi ito malipad o gumalaw; bigat.
original_explanation: ‘Dagan’ is that heavy thing you put on top of the sinigang lid so the steam doesn't escape. It's also the emotional baggage from your ex that you're still carrying. The ultimate 'pabigat'.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb 'daganin' (to place weight on something) or 'madaganan' (to be crushed by something heavy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **dagan** ang mga papel para hindi liparin ng hangin.","translation":"Put a **weight** on the papers so they don't get blown away by the wind."},{"sentence":"Ayokong maging **dagan** sa pamilya ko.","translation":"I don't want to be a **burden** to my family."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang inuming alkoholiko na gawa mula sa pinakatamis na katas ng mansanas.
original_explanation: The tita-approved alcoholic drink for New Year's Eve. It's less intimidating than hard liquor and feels fancier than beer. It’s what you drink when you want to feel a bit celebratory but still have to wake up early the next day.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to apple cider, especially the sparkling, low-alcohol version popular during Christmas and New Year celebrations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magbukas tayo ng **sidra** para salubungin ang Bagong Taon.","translation":"Let's open a bottle of **cider** to welcome the New Year."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang **sidra** kaysa sa champagne dahil mas matamis ito.","translation":"I prefer **cider** over champagne because it's sweeter."}]

translation: a loud thud; a rumbling or banging sound
meaning_filipino: Isang malakas at mababang tunog na nalilikha ng pagbagsak ng isang mabigat na bagay o paggalaw sa loob ng isang lalagyan.
original_explanation: That mysterious sound from the kitchen at 2 AM. Was it the cat, a ghost, or just the ice dispenser? That's a *kalambog*. It's the sound of your upstairs neighbor who seems to be rearranging furniture at midnight. It’s not a sharp crack, but a heavy, resonant *thud*.
usage_notes: Often implies a heavy object moving or falling. Can also describe the sound of liquid sloshing heavily inside a container. A common synonym is 'kalabog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **kalambog** mula sa itaas na palapag.","translation":"I heard a **loud thud** from the upper floor."},{"sentence":"Ang **kalambog** ng tubig sa galon ay nakakairita.","translation":"The **rumbling sound** of the water in the container is irritating."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o pamilya na may sapat o higit pang kakayahang pinansyal at hindi naghihirap.
original_explanation: Not exactly 'Crazy Rich Asian' level, but definitely not 'isang kahig, isang tuka.' These are the people who can afford the extra large milk tea with pearls, order GrabFood without checking the delivery fee, and their aircon is probably on 24/7. They're comfortable, they're stable, they're #blessed.
usage_notes: A polite way to say someone is rich or financially stable, less direct than 'mayaman'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang pamilyang **may-kaya** ang nakatira sa malaking bahay na iyon.","translation":"A **well-off** family lives in that big house."},{"sentence":"Kahit **may-kaya** sila, simple pa rin ang kanilang pamumuhay.","translation":"Even if they are **affluent**, they still live a simple life."}]

translation: grandmother; term of address for an old woman
meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na katawagan para sa lola o sinumang matandang babae.
etymology: Mula sa Tsinong Hokkien na '阿媽' (a-má), na nangangahulugang 'lola'.
original_explanation: Ang ultimate source ng lumpiang shanghai, unconditional love, at pamana. Ang impo ang laging may baon na kendi sa bulsa at kwento tungkol sa 'panahon namin.' She's the matriarch, the queen of the lola-verse. It's the more intimate, Chinese-Filipino version of 'lola'.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga pamilyang may lahing Tsino, ngunit naging popular na rin sa pangkalahatan. Mas malapit sa 'lola' kaysa sa 'inang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mano po, **impo**,” sabi ng bata.","translation":"“Your hand, please, **grandma**,” said the child."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng luto ng **impo** ko.","translation":"My **grandmother's** cooking is delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking patalim na karaniwang may dalawang talim at matulis na dulo, ginagamit bilang sandata o kagamitan.
original_explanation: Think of it as the bigger, scarier cousin of your kitchen knife. It's the kind of blade you see in historical Filipino movies, used by warriors like Lapu-Lapu. In the province, it might just be a tool for cutting thick grass or coconuts. Definitely not something you want to see during a heated argument in the palengke.
usage_notes: Often associated with historical, martial, or rural contexts. It is a type of 'itak' or 'bolo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng mandirigma ang kanyang **sundang** upang ipagtanggol ang sarili.","translation":"The warrior used his **dagger** to defend himself."},{"sentence":"Isang antigong **sundang** ang nakasabit sa dingding ng lolo.","translation":"An antique **large knife** was hanging on grandpa's wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraan ng paghila o pagbatak sa isang bagay o tao sa lupa o sa anumang ibabaw.
original_explanation: This is how you feel when your friends force you to go out when you just want to stay home and binge-watch. 'Sumama ako nang pakaladkad.' It's also literally how you'd move a heavy sack of rice or a misbehaving toddler through a mall. It implies unwillingness and friction.
usage_notes: Often used to describe being forced to go somewhere against one's will, or the physical act of dragging something heavy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa presinto nang **pakaladkad**.","translation":"He was brought to the precinct by being **dragged along**."},{"sentence":"Kinuha niya ang sako ng bigas nang **pakaladkad** dahil sa bigat nito.","translation":"He took the sack of rice by **dragging** it because of its weight."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na pabaya, magulo, at hindi maingat sa sariling kaayusan, mga gamit, o gawain.
original_explanation: Your roommate who treats the floor as their closet and the sink as a science experiment. Their motto is 'Bukas ko na lilinisin,' but 'bukas' never comes. The human personification of a cluttered desktop with 100+ icons.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe people, particularly their habits or personal space.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kwarto niya ay sobrang gulo, napaka-**burara** niyang tao.","translation":"His room is so messy, he's such a **slovenly** person."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan ako ni nanay na huwag maging **burara** sa mga gamit ko.","translation":"My mom told me not to be **messy** with my things."}]

translation: dragnet; a type of large fishing net
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaki at malapad na lambat na ginagamit sa pangingisda, partikular na para sa panghuhuli ng maraming isda nang sabayan.
original_explanation: This isn't your friendly neighborhood fishing net ('lambat'). This is the BFG (Big Friendly Giant) of nets, used for serious, large-scale fishing. It's the kind of net that says, 'We're not just here for tilapia; we're here for the whole school.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe a dragnet or a large seine net. It is much less common in everyday conversation than the general term 'lambat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ang mga mangingisda ng **lambang** upang makahuli ng tone-toneladang isda.","translation":"The fishermen used a **dragnet** to catch tons of fish."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ang paggamit ng **lambang** sa ilang protektadong bahagi ng karagatan.","translation":"The use of a **large fishing net** is prohibited in some protected marine areas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may kapansanan sa pandinig; hindi makarinig.
original_explanation: This is the traditional Tagalog word for a deaf person. It's a bit old-fashioned and can sometimes be seen as less polite than the more modern 'may kapansanan sa pandinig' (person with hearing disability). It's straightforward, but using person-first language is now preferred. Be mindful of context. Note: This is different from the English loanword 'binge' (/bɪndʒ/) (like binge-watching).
usage_notes: While a valid Tagalog word, modern usage prefers 'may kapansanan sa pandinig' or simply 'hindi makarinig' for politeness. It is important to distinguish this from the English loanword 'binge' (/bɪndʒ/).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumagamit siya ng sign language para makausap ang kanyang kaibigang **binge**.","translation":"He uses sign language to talk to his **deaf** friend."},{"sentence":"Maraming **binge** ang natutulungan ng mga bagong teknolohiya.","translation":"Many **deaf people** are being helped by new technologies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng hindi pagkakaroon ng gusto, paghanga, o pagtanggap sa isang tao, bagay, o ideya.
original_explanation: When you see pineapple on pizza and your whole being just says "NOPE." Or that feeling when your friend starts dating your ex. It's that internal, sometimes visceral, "I'm not a fan" reaction. The opposite of having a crush.
usage_notes: This is a formal or literary term. 'Ayaw' is the everyday word for 'dislike' or 'don't want'. 'Hindi gusto' is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya itinago ang kanyang **di-pagkakagusto** sa mungkahi.","translation":"He did not hide his **displeasure** with the suggestion."},{"sentence":"Ang **di-pagkakagusto** sa isang tao ay hindi sapat na dahilan para saktan siya.","translation":"The **dislike** of a person is not a sufficient reason to hurt them."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtaas o pag-igting ng tulin o dalas ng isang kilos o pangyayari.
original_explanation: 'Yung tibok ng puso mo nung nakita mong nag-reply si crush. Or 'yung takbo mo nung nalaman mong may aso sa likod mo. It's when things go from 0 to 100 real quick. **Bumilis** ang internet connection nung nawala na 'yung bagyo.
usage_notes: Stative verb indicating a change of state. It means 'to become fast'. Present: bumibilis. Future: bibilis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **bumilis** ang takbo ng kotse sa highway.","translation":"The car's speed on the highway suddenly **accelerated**."},{"sentence":"**Bumilis** ang paggaling niya mula nang uminom siya ng gamot.","translation":"His recovery **sped up** since he started taking medicine."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkalahatang pakiramdam ng saya, kaluwagan, at panandaliang yaman na nararanasan tuwing araw ng sahod.
etymology: A modern, code-switched English phrase widely adopted in the Philippines.
original_explanation: That magical, temporary feeling of being a millionaire for about 24 hours between 'sweldo' hitting your bank account and 'bayarin' taking it all away. It's the sudden urge to eat at a nice restaurant, add everything to your Shopee cart, and treat your friends. The official scent of this feeling is Jollibee Chickenjoy and the sound is the ATM dispensing cash.
usage_notes: A very popular slang phrase, especially among young professionals and BPO employees. Used almost exclusively in informal, online, or casual conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang **payday feels**, nag-shopping at kumain kami sa labas!","translation":"The **payday feels** are intense, we went shopping and ate out!"}]

translation: to pacify; to make peaceful; to put in order
meaning_filipino: Gawing tiwasay, payapa, o maayos ang isang sitwasyon o lugar.
original_explanation: This is what you try to do when your two best friends are fighting. You become the peacemaker. It's also the goal of every BPO agent handling an irate caller: "Ma'am/Sir, kalma lang po, we will resolve this." You take a chaotic situation and try to bring it back to a state of calm and order.
usage_notes: Implies an active effort to restore peace or order.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan ng mga lider na **patiwasayin** ang magulong sitwasyon sa komunidad.","translation":"The leaders are trying to **pacify** the chaotic situation in the community."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkalat o pagtalsik ng likido o maliliit na bagay nang walang tiyak na direksyon.
original_explanation: Imagine a jeepney speeding through a puddle on a rainy day—that's saboy. Or when a priest blesses the crowd with holy water. It's also what happens when you try to eat 'sinigang' too fast and the soup goes everywhere. A controlled mess, sometimes.
usage_notes: Often used as a verb root: 'sumaboy' (to splash), 'isaboy' (to scatter something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwasan niya ang **saboy** ng putik mula sa dumaang sasakyan.","translation":"He avoided the **splash** of mud from the passing vehicle."},{"sentence":"Ang **saboy** ng mga butil ng bigas ay para sa kasaganaan.","translation":"The **scattering** of rice grains is for prosperity."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahayag ng pagkayamot, pagkadismaya, o pagwawalang-bahala sa isang bagay o pahayag.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang onomatopoeic o salitang nagpapahayag ng damdamin.
original_explanation: The sound you make when someone tells a corny joke, or when your friend cancels plans at the last minute. It's a short, sharp, and slightly nasal dismissal. The verbal equivalent of an eye-roll. 'Ay, ang corny mo. Nye.'
usage_notes: Lubos na impormal at pang-usapan. Ang tono ng pagsabi ay napakahalaga sa kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala ko may surprise, 'yun lang pala. **Nye**!","translation":"I thought there was a surprise, but it was just that. **Meh**!"},{"sentence":"Sinabi niyang mahal niya ako, tapos biglang 'di na nagparamdam. **Nye**.","translation":"He said he loved me, then suddenly ghosted me. **Ugh, whatever**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangatnig na nagpapahayag ng pagsalungat o pag-iba sa inaasahan; sa kabila ng.
original_explanation: This is the formal 'pero' or 'kahit na'. It's the ultimate 'hugot' transition. 'Mahal na mahal kita... **gayon pa man**, kailangan na kitang iwan.' It adds that extra dramatic flair, like a teleserye scene-ender.
usage_notes: A formal conjunction used to introduce a contrasting idea. 'Gayunman' is a common, slightly shorter alternative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na siya sa trabaho, **gayon pa man** ay nagawa pa rin niyang magluto ng hapunan.","translation":"She was tired from work, **however**, she still managed to cook dinner."},{"sentence":"Maliit ang kanyang sahod, **gayon pa man**, masaya siya sa kanyang buhay.","translation":"His salary is small, **yet** he is happy with his life."}]

translation: chin rest; anything used to support the chin
meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na ginagamit na tukod o suporta sa baba, o ang mismong kilos ng pagpapatong ng baba sa kamay o sa isang bagay.
etymology: A combination of `salo` (to catch, to support) + `baba` (chin).
original_explanation: That classic 'bored in a meeting' or 'daydreaming in class' pose where you prop your chin on your hand. Your hand, in that moment, is your 'salumbaba'. It's the physical manifestation of 'Sana Biyernes na' or deep in thought about your life choices.
usage_notes: Can refer to the object used for support or the action itself (pag-salumbaba).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga kamay ay nagsilbing **salumbaba** habang malalim siyang nag-iisip.","translation":"His hands served as a **chin rest** while he was deep in thought."},{"sentence":"Napansin ng guro ang pag-**salumbaba** ng estudyanteng inaantok.","translation":"The teacher noticed the sleepy student **resting his chin on his hand**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaang pag-atake na isinasagawa bilang tugon o ganti sa isang naunang pagsalakay ng kalaban.
original_explanation: This is the military or strategic version of 'ganti.' Think of it as a 'no, you!' move in a fight. The enemy attacks your base, so you launch a gantihang-salakay on theirs. It's the clapback in warfare or even in a heated office debate.
usage_notes: Primarily used in military, strategic, or conflict-related contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda ang mga sundalo para sa posibleng **gantihang-salakay** mula sa kaaway.","translation":"The soldiers prepared for a possible **counter-attack** from the enemy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagdadaglat na orihinal na nangangahulugang "good game" sa mga laro. Sa kolokyal na Filipino, maaari rin itong mangahulugang "tapos na," "patay na," o "lagot na" sa isang negatibong sitwasyon.
etymology: Mula sa acronym ng Ingles na "good game".
original_explanation: From the gaming world, it means "good game." But in the Philippines, it's evolved. Forgot your wallet? GG. Boss caught you on Facebook? GG. Your crush saw you trip? Super GG na. It's the universal sign that you're totally, completely screwed.
usage_notes: May dalawang magkaibang kahulugan depende sa konteksto: ang literal na "good game" at ang kolokyal na "lagot na".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nice game, **GG** sa inyo.","translation":"Nice game, **good game** to you all."},{"sentence":"Naiwan ko ang report ko sa bahay, **GG** na 'to.","translation":"I left my report at home, I'm **screwed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang linya o punto na nagmamarka ng katapusan o gilid ng isang lugar, sakop, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: The line you shouldn't cross. In relationships, it's your 'non-negotiables'. In geography, it's the sign that says "You are now leaving Metro Manila." For your data plan, it's that dreaded text from your telco saying you've used up your GBs. It's the point where things stop, so you better know where it is.
usage_notes: The form 'hangganan' is more commonly used but both mean the same thing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malinaw ang **hanggahan** ng aming lupa.","translation":"The **boundary** of our land is clear."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng bagay ay may **hanggahan**.","translation":"Everything has a **limit**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay o paglalagay ng liwanag sa isang lugar, bagay, o tao.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your phone's flashlight when you drop your keys in the dark. It's the act of pointing a light source at something. "Bes, **tanglawan** mo nga dito, nahulog yata P100 ko." It can also be figurative, like when a good teacher illuminates a difficult subject.
usage_notes: The verb form of 'tanglaw'. Focuses on the action of directing light.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tanglawan** mo ang daan upang hindi tayo matisod.","translation":"**Light up** the path so we don't stumble."},{"sentence":"Kanyang **tinanglawan** ang madilim na sulok ng silid.","translation":"He **illuminated** the dark corner of the room."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking sasakyang pandagat na ginagamit sa paglalakbay o paghakot ng mga kargamento sa ibabaw ng tubig.
original_explanation: Before Cebu Pacific, there was the barko. It's how your lola from the province visited Manila. It's slower, you might get seasick, but the experience of watching the sea for hours is a different kind of vibe. Also, the root of 'barkada,' because people used to become friends on long boat trips.
usage_notes: A general term for large sea vessels. For smaller boats, 'bangka' is used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumakay kami ng **barko** papuntang Cebu.","translation":"We rode a **ship** going to Cebu."},{"sentence":"Dumaong sa pantalan ang malaking **barko** ng kargamento.","translation":"The large cargo **ship** docked at the pier."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang likidong nakukuha mula sa kinayod na laman ng niyog, na ginagamit bilang sangkap sa pagluluto.
original_explanation: This is the more formal, 'complete name' version of 'gata'. It's what you say when you want to be specific, like telling your tita you need "milk of the coconut," not just any milk. It's the same delicious, artery-clogging goodness, just said with more syllables.
usage_notes: Mas deskriptibo ngunit ang salitang 'gata' lamang ay mas karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Bicol Express ay niluluto sa **gata ng niyog** at sili.","translation":"Bicol Express is cooked in **coconut milk** and chili."},{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng isang lata ng **gata ng niyog** sa tindahan.","translation":"Buy a can of **coconut milk** at the store."}]

translation: to come to a mutual understanding
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-abot sa isang kasunduan o pagkakaunawaan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang partido sa pamamagitan ng bukas na komunikasyon.
etymology: From maki- (social prefix) + pag- (action prefix) + unawa (understanding) + -an (social suffix).
original_explanation: Ito yung goal ng bawat 'let's talk' na text. Yung pag-uusap niyo ng jowa mo para magka-level na ulit kayo ng expectations at hindi na mag-away. Sa BPO, ito yung 'call de-escalation' para kalmado na ulit si customer. The art of finding common ground.
usage_notes: A very positive social verb, emphasizing reconciliation and mutual effort to understand each other.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga para sa mag-asawa na **makipag-unawaan** upang mapanatili ang kanilang pagsasama.","translation":"It's important for a married couple to **come to a mutual understanding** to maintain their relationship."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng mga lider na **makipag-unawaan** sa mga nagpoprotesta.","translation":"The leaders tried to **come to a mutual understanding** with the protesters."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ibabang bahagi ng isang bahay o gusali, lalo na ang espasyo sa ilalim ng pangunahing palapag ng isang bahay na itinaas mula sa lupa.
original_explanation: The original Filipino basement, but make it open-air. Sa mga bahay-kubo o lumang bahay sa probinsya, ito yung space sa ilalim kung saan nakatago ang mga alagang manok, panggatong, o yung luma mong bike. Sometimes, it's where the best neighborhood chismisan happens, habang naghihimay ng gulay. It's the cool, shady spot perfect for an afternoon nap.
usage_notes: Madalas na iniuugnay sa mga tradisyonal na bahay na Pilipino (bahay kubo) na nakatayo sa mga tukod.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglalaro ang mga bata sa **silong** ng bahay para hindi mainitan.","translation":"The children are playing in the **space underneath the house** to avoid the heat."},{"sentence":"Inilagay ni Lolo ang mga sako ng bigas sa **silong**.","translation":"Grandpa placed the sacks of rice on the **ground floor**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pag-aaruga, pag-aalaga, at proteksyon, lalo na sa mga nangangailangan o mas mahina.
original_explanation: Ito yung tita mong laging may dalang pagkain at nagtatanong, "Kumain ka na ba, anak?" Sila yung mga fur parent na turing sa alaga nila ay parang tunay na anak. It’s that nurturing, protective vibe that makes you feel safe and cared for, like a warm hug or a bowl of sinigang on a rainy day.
usage_notes: Has a strong connotation of protective care, often associated with mothers, nurses, and caregivers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **mapagkalinga** na ina si Aling Nena sa kanyang mga anak.","translation":"Aling Nena is a **caring** mother to her children."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng mga lider na **mapagkalinga** sa kalikasan.","translation":"We need leaders who are **nurturing** towards the environment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabangong dahon mula sa puno ng laurel, ginagamit bilang pampalasa sa pagluluto, lalo na sa mga pagkaing tulad ng adobo at paksiw.
original_explanation: The one thing in adobo that you're not supposed to eat but you accidentally do anyway. It's the flavor wingman, the aromatic support character in many Filipino stews. You know the food is legit when you see a floating **dahon ng laurel**.
usage_notes: A compound noun referring to a specific culinary herb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang maglagay ng **dahon ng laurel** sa adobo para bumango.","translation":"Don't forget to put a **bay leaf** in the adobo to make it fragrant."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa panlabinsiyam na posisyon o pagkakasunod-sunod sa isang serye.
original_explanation: You're almost at 20, but not quite. It's the last year of being a teenager. It's that awkward "almost an adult but still can't rent a car" phase. In history, it’s the century of Jose Rizal and the Philippine Revolution.
usage_notes: Used to denote the 19th item in a sequence. Can be written as "ika-19".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong **ikalabinsiyam** na siglo isinulat ni Rizal ang kanyang mga nobela.","translation":"Rizal wrote his novels in the **nineteenth** century."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang **ikalabinsiyam** na beses na sinabi kong ayoko.","translation":"This is the **nineteenth** time I've said I don't want to."}]

translation: to put in order; to settle (a dispute)
meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pahayag na nangangahulugang ayusin ang isang gusot, pag-ugnayin ang mga nag-aaway, o ibalik sa kaayusan ang isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is what a tired mom, a barangay captain, or an HR manager tries to do all day. It's trying to make two warring factions (e.g., your two 'marites' titas, or the marketing and sales teams) finally agree on something. It's basically saying "Can't we all just get along?" but in a more formal, almost musical way. It's about restoring the peace and making things harmonious again.
usage_notes: An older, more formal or literary idiom. Not common in casual conversation but understood in formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag ng kapitan ang dalawang pamilya upang **ilagay sa armonia** ang kanilang alitan.","translation":"The captain called the two families to **settle** their dispute."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **ilagay sa armonia** ang magkakaibang panig sa politika.","translation":"It's difficult to **put in order** the different political sides."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang labanan o pag-aaway, lalo na sa pagitan ng mga armadong pwersa.
original_explanation: Ito yung bakbakan, gera, o away. Pwedeng literal na kombate sa pagitan ng mga sundalo, o yung kombate mo sa antok tuwing Lunes ng umaga sa office. O di kaya yung verbal kombate niyo ng jowa mo kung saan kayo kakain.
usage_notes: Can be used for literal armed conflict or figuratively for any intense struggle or argument.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming sundalo ang nasugatan sa kasagsagan ng **kombate**.","translation":"Many soldiers were wounded in the heat of the **combat**."},{"sentence":"Handa na ako para sa **kombate** laban sa sandamakmak na labahin.","translation":"I'm ready for the **battle** against this huge pile of laundry."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangangahulugang katatapos pa lamang umalis o lumisan. Ito ay nasa aspetong perpektibong katatapos.
etymology: Formed by repeating the first syllable of the root word "alis" (ka- + alis = kaalis) and then repeating the "ka-" prefix for the recent perfective aspect (ka- + kaalis = kaaalis).
original_explanation: The official word for that "Sayang! Kakaalis lang niya!" moment. It's the sound of a near-miss. You just missed the bus, your friend just left the house, the Grab driver just drove off. The repeated first syllable "ka-" is the grammatical equivalent of the word "just" in "just happened." It's the tense of regret and bad timing.
usage_notes: The "ka-(repeat first syllable of root)" construction is a common way to form the recent perfective aspect in Tagalog (e.g., kakain - just ate, kaliligo - just bathed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kaaalis** lang ng bus, kailangan nating maghintay ng susunod.","translation":"The bus **just left**, we need to wait for the next one."},{"sentence":"Nang dumating ako, **kaaalis** na pala nila.","translation":"When I arrived, they had apparently **just left**."}]

translation: to be delayed, to be late
meaning_filipino: Maantala o mahuli sa takdang oras o iskedyul.
original_explanation: Classic Filipino time. When your friend says "OTW," but they're still in the shower. 'Umatraso' is what happened to their schedule. It's the action of being delayed or causing a delay.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of schedules, payments, or projects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umatraso** ang byahe namin dahil sa matinding trapiko.","translation":"Our trip **was delayed** due to heavy traffic."},{"sentence":"Kapag **umatraso** ka sa bayad ng upa, magkakaproblema ka sa landlady.","translation":"If you **are late** with the rent payment, you will have a problem with the landlady."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panahon sa pagitan ng hapon at gabi kung kailan unti-unting nawawala ang liwanag ng araw.
etymology: Mula sa pagsasama ng mga salitang "takip" (cover) at "silim" (dimness, gloom).
original_explanation: That 'golden hour' for your IG story before it gets too dark and you need a flash. Perfect for dramatic silhouettes and hugot moments while staring into the distance, thinking about your life choices or that person who left you on read. Also, the time when your mom yells, "Pumasok na kayo, mga bata! Gabi na!"
usage_notes: Ang anyong may gitling na "takip-silim" ay karaniwan din at katanggap-tanggap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagandang pagmasdan ng **takipsilim** sa dalampasigan.","translation":"It's so beautiful to watch the **dusk** on the beach."}]

translation: to have something reviewed; to have something checked
meaning_filipino: Ipasuri o muling pag-aralan ang isang bagay, tulad ng dokumento o desisyon, upang matiyak ang kawastuhan nito.
original_explanation: This is what your boss tells you after you submit a report you finished at 3 AM. "Okay, good first draft. **Iparepaso** mo muna sa legal." It's the act of getting a second pair of eyes on something, whether it's your thesis, a contract, or your OOTD picture before you post it.
usage_notes: Commonly used in academic and professional settings for documents, drafts, and other work that needs verification.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **iparepaso** ang kontrata sa isang abogado bago mo pirmahan.","translation":"You need **to have** the contract **reviewed** by a lawyer before you sign it."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang abilidad o kapasidad na gawin o isakatuparan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The official slogan for giving up (or being realistic). It’s what you say when your friend asks you to go out but your bank account is crying. It's the "pass muna ako, bes" of physical, financial, or emotional capacity.
usage_notes: A very direct way to state inability. Can be softened by adding "yata" or "ko yata" (e.g., "Hindi ko yata kaya" - I don't think I can).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hindi kaya** ng suweldo ko ang bagong iPhone.","translation":"My salary **cannot** afford the new iPhone."},{"sentence":"Pagod na ako, **hindi** ko na **kaya** mag-overtime.","translation":"I'm tired, I **cannot** work overtime anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikipagpalitan ng mga biro o katuwaan sa isa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: This is the Pinoy love language. It's teasing your friends, exchanging silly jokes, and just generally having a light, fun time with people. It's the opposite of being serious. From the "knock-knock" jokes in the office pantry to the friendly roasting (`asar-talo`) with your barkada. Just be careful not to take it too far, or it might turn into `makipag-away`.
usage_notes: Implies a friendly, light-hearted, and mutual exchange of jokes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap **makipagbiruan** sa mga taong hindi pikon.","translation":"It's fun **to joke around with** people who aren't easily offended."},{"sentence":"Pumunta siya sa party para lang **makipagbiruan** at kumain.","translation":"He went to the party just **to joke around** and eat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na hayop na karaniwang may anim na paa, katawang nahahati sa tatlong bahagi (ulo, toraks, at tiyan), at kadalasang may mga pakpak.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung mga maliliit na nilalang na bigla na lang sumusulpot sa bahay niyo—ipis, langgam, lamok. Sila 'yung dahilan kung bakit may tsinelas kang laging handa o 'di kaya'y baygon. Basically, your unwanted roommates that don't pay rent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **insekto** ang naaakit sa ilaw tuwing gabi.","translation":"Many **insects** are attracted to the light at night."},{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng kulambo para hindi ka makagat ng **insekto** habang natutulog.","translation":"Use a mosquito net so you won't get bitten by **insects** while sleeping."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hinala o pagdududa sa isang tao o bagay; ang taong pinaghihinalaan sa isang krimen o maling gawain.
original_explanation: It's that 'praning' feeling you get when your partner is suddenly quiet, or when your officemate is being too nice. Sa crime shows, ito yung 'person of interest'. "May sospetsa ako kung sino umubos ng ulam sa ref." It can be the feeling of suspicion or the person you're suspicious of.
usage_notes: Maaaring mangahulugan ng pakiramdam ng paghihinala ("may sospetsa ako") o ang taong pinaghihinalaan ("siya ang sospetsa").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangunahing **sospetsa** ng mga pulis ay ang hardinero.","translation":"The police's primary **suspect** is the gardener."},{"sentence":"May **sospetsa** ako na hindi siya nagsasabi ng buong katotohanan.","translation":"I have a **suspicion** that he is not telling the whole truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain o proseso ng pagbibigay ng kasiyahan, libangan, o ginhawa sa isang taong nalulungkot, nababagot, o nababalisa.
original_explanation: This can mean two things. 1) The G-rated version: what you do to make a crying friend feel better—treating them to milk tea, watching a comedy movie, or just listening. It's providing comfort. 2) The more... 'adult' version, sometimes used euphemistically for entertainers or prostitution ('aliw-iw'). But in general use, it's all about providing comfort and distraction.
usage_notes: Maaaring mangahulugang 'entertainment' o 'consolation'. Mahalaga ang konteksto. Maaari rin itong maging euphemism sa ilang sitwasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta sila sa sinehan para sa kaunting **pag-aaliw**.","translation":"They went to the cinema for a little **entertainment**."},{"sentence":"Ang musika ay nagbibigay **pag-aaliw** sa kanyang kalungkutan.","translation":"Music provides **comfort** to his sadness."}]

translation: in a little while; later; shortly
meaning_filipino: Sa loob ng ilang sandali; hindi magtatagal; pagkaraan ng maikling panahon.
etymology: Reduplication of `maya`, an old word for a moment or instant.
original_explanation: This is the official Filipino time unit for 'just a sec.' When your mom says 'maya-maya,' it could mean in five minutes or after she finishes her K-drama episode. It's that flexible, non-committal timeframe between now and 'mamaya na.'
usage_notes: Used to indicate a short, but often unspecified, amount of time in the near future.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maya-maya** ay darating na ang inorder nating pagkain.","translation":"The food we ordered will arrive **in a little while**."},{"sentence":"Magpahinga ka muna, tatawagin kita **maya-maya**.","translation":"Rest for now, I will call you **later**."}]

translation: to drag oneself; to walk laboriously
meaning_filipino: Ang maglakad nang may kahirapan, na tila hinihila ang mga paa dahil sa pagod, sakit, o bigat ng dalahin.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung paglalakad mo pauwi after a 12-hour shift, o 'yung itsura mo papuntang kusina para kumuha ng tubig at 3 AM. You're not just walking, you're dragging your entire existence. Para kang zombie na pagod sa life.
usage_notes: Connotes extreme tiredness, weakness, or being weighed down physically or emotionally.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **maghilahod** na ang matanda sa pag-akyat ng hagdanan dala ang mabigat niyang bayong.","translation":"The old woman was almost **dragging herself** up the stairs carrying her heavy market bag."},{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod mula sa bukid, **naghilahod** siya pauwi.","translation":"Extremely tired from the farm, he **walked laboriously** on his way home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na inuutusan o binibigyan ng gawain; katulong o lingkod.
original_explanation: Before Grab or Lalamove, you had the 'utusan'. This is the person you send to the sari-sari store to buy suka and toyo. In a corporate setting, it's the intern who gets sent on coffee runs. In a 'hugot' context, it's you, when your crush asks you to do things for them but won't commit. 'Hindi ako P.A. (personal alalay), 'no!'
usage_notes: Can sometimes have a slightly negative or demeaning connotation, so 'katulong' (helper) is often preferred in formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang aming pinagkakatiwalaang **utusan** sa bahay.","translation":"She is our trusted **helper** at home."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong ituring na parang **utusan** ang iyong mga kasama.","translation":"Don't treat your companions like they are mere **servants**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lumagpas na sa takdang panahon o bisa; hindi na balido.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "pasado" na nangangahulugang "past" o "passed."
original_explanation: That moment of panic when you realize your driver's license or passport is 'paso na' and you have a trip next week. It's the state of that can of sardines at the back of your pantry from 2019. Check your expiration dates, people!
usage_notes: Pronunciation is key to differentiate from 'paso' (burn). The stress is on the second syllable for 'expired'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paso** na ang lisensya ko kaya kailangan ko nang mag-renew.","translation":"My license is already **expired** so I need to renew it."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang kainin 'yan, **paso** na ang expiration date.","translation":"Don't eat that anymore, the expiration date has **lapsed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na pumapasok sa isang lugar, karaniwan ay isang tahanan o gusali, nang walang pahintulot upang magnakaw.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `man-` (tagagawa ng kilos) + `loob` (loob). Literal na "isang taong pumapasok sa loob."
original_explanation: Ito 'yung kontrabida sa mga Pinoy action films na laging tumatakbo sa eskinita. Sila 'yung dahilan kung bakit may rehas ang mga bintana at may sampung lock ang pinto mo. The OG home invader.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga ulat sa balita tungkol sa mga pagnanakaw sa bahay o gusali.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng mga pulis ang **manloloob** habang papalabas ito ng bahay.","translation":"The police caught the **burglar** as he was leaving the house."},{"sentence":"Nag-ingat ang buong barangay dahil may kumakalat na balita tungkol sa isang **manloloob**.","translation":"The whole neighborhood became cautious because news was spreading about a **robber**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging magkaiba o hindi magkapareho sa anyo, ugali, o kalikasan.
original_explanation: Yung itsura niyo ng kapatid mo. Pareho kayo ng magulang, pero siya mukhang K-drama star, ikaw mukhang pagod. Or 'yung "expectations vs. reality" 'pag umorder ka online. That gap between the ideal and the real is the land of di-pagkakatulad.
usage_notes: Isang neutral na termino para sa paglalarawan ng mga pagkakaiba sa pagitan ng mga bagay, tao, o ideya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng kanilang **di-pagkakatulad**, nanatili silang matalik na magkaibigan.","translation":"Despite their **differences**, they remained best friends."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang **di-pagkakatulad** ng luma at bagong bersyon ng software.","translation":"There is a big **dissimilarity** between the old and new versions of the software."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalahad, pagpapaliwanag, o pagkukuwento ng mga pangyayari, detalye, o impormasyon sa isang maayos at malinaw na paraan.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're telling your friends the 'chika' from last night's party, complete with sound effects and acting. It's the official term for storytelling, whether you're a writer crafting a novel, a lawyer presenting a case, or just your tita recounting her entire life story for the fifth time.
usage_notes: A more formal term for storytelling or giving an account.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tapat na **pagsasaysay** ng kasaysayan para sa mga susunod na henerasyon.","translation":"The honest **narration** of history is important for the next generations."}]

translation: to be able to outsmart or deceive
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang manlinlang, mandaya, o malampasan sa talino ang iba sa paraang hindi tapat.
etymology: From "gulang," which can mean age but also cunning or trickery.
original_explanation: This is the skill of a 'diskarte' master who uses their powers for evil. Yung kaklase mong nangopya pero siya pa 'yung nakakuha ng perfect score. O 'yung nagbenta sa'yo ng "original" na sapatos pero Class A lang pala. They played you.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of deceit and trickery. "Nakagulang" is the past tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapaloko sa kanya; sanay siyang **makagugulang** ng kapwa.","translation":"Don't be fooled by him; he is used to **deceiving** others."},{"sentence":"Akala niya ay **makagugulang** siya sa batas, ngunit nahuli rin siya.","translation":"He thought he could **outsmart** the law, but he was eventually caught."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging balakid o sagabal sa daan o sa pag-usad ng isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: 'Yung magulang ng jowa mo na ayaw sa'yo. Sila 'yung **humadlang** sa inyong forever. O kaya 'yung mabagal na internet connection 'pag may importante kang Zoom meeting. It's the ultimate 'hadlang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking bato na **humadlang** sa daan kaya hindi kami makadaan.","translation":"A large rock **obstructed** the road so we could not pass."},{"sentence":"Walang sinuman ang dapat **humadlang** sa iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"No one should **hinder** your dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang hindi pagpansin o pagbalewala sa isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: The active verb form of 'dedma.' This is when you make a conscious decision to 'seen zone' someone in real life. It's a power move. Example: 'Dinedma niya lahat ng red flags.' (She ignored all the red flags.)
usage_notes: A transitive verb that requires an object to be ignored.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit man, kailangan mong **dedmahin** ang mga negatibong komento para sa iyong kapayapaan.","translation":"Though it hurts, you need **to ignore** the negative comments for your peace of mind."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **dedmahin** ang text ko!","translation":"Don't **ignore** my text!"}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang sunggaban o dakpin ang isang bagay na inihagis, nahuhulog, o gumagalaw patungo sa iyo.
original_explanation: That feeling of victory when you drop your phone but your foot reflexes kick in and you manage to catch it before it hits the ground. It's also what your 'sana all' friend does—they're always there to catch you when you fall (emotionally or financially).
usage_notes: Often used in its completed aspect 'nasalo' (was able to catch).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Subukan mong ihagis ang bola at tingnan natin kung **masalo** ko.","translation":"Try throwing the ball and let's see if I can **catch** it."},{"sentence":"Sana'y laging may handang **masalo** sa iyo sa tuwing ikaw ay nanghihina.","translation":"I hope there's always someone ready **to catch** you whenever you are feeling weak."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bansa sa Timog-silangang Asya na binubuo ng libo-libong mga pulo, at may kabisera sa Jakarta.
original_explanation: Yung kapitbahay nating sobrang daming isla, parang Pilipinas lang pero mas marami pa. Dito galing ang Indomie, na national food na rin yata ng mga Pinoy college students at dormers. Home of Bali, the ultimate "eat-pray-love" destination.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbakasyon kami sa Bali, **Indonesia** noong isang taon.","translation":"We vacationed in Bali, **Indonesia** last year."},{"sentence":"Ang **Indonesia** at Pilipinas ay parehong miyembro ng ASEAN.","translation":"**Indonesia** and the Philippines are both members of ASEAN."}]

meaning_filipino: Madaling kapitan ng sakit o karamdaman; may mahinang pangangatawan.
etymology: From `sakit` ("illness") + `-in` (suffix indicating tendency or proneness), with the `ma-` prefix.
original_explanation: This is your friend who always has an MC (Medical Certificate) ready. They collect illnesses like others collect Funko Pops. A slight change in weather? They're sick. Someone sneezed in the next barangay? They're sick. They're the reason Vicks VapoRub and Neozep sales are always stable.
usage_notes: Describes a person's general state of health, not a specific instance of being sick.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil **masakitin** si Ana, lagi siyang pinapayuhan ng kanyang ina na mag-ingat.","translation":"Because Ana is **sickly**, her mother always advises her to be careful."},{"sentence":"Ang batang **masakitin** ay kailangang bigyan ng masustansyang pagkain.","translation":"A **sickly** child needs to be given nutritious food."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng mga kosmetiko sa mukha upang pagandahin o baguhin ang itsura.
etymology: From English 'makeup', combined with the Tagalog verb prefix 'mag-'. This is a clear example of Taglish verb formation.
original_explanation: The "mag-transform tayo" verb. That 30-minute to 2-hour process of turning from a "puyat na BPO agent" into a "fresh lang, 'di halata" goddess. It's the modern-day war paint for facing traffic, deadlines, and your ex.
usage_notes: A modern, colloquial term derived from English. The more traditional term would be "mag-ayos" or "magpaganda".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magmeykap** bago ang aming Zoom meeting.","translation":"I need to **put on makeup** before our Zoom meeting."},{"sentence":"Natagalan siya dahil nag-aral pa siyang **magmeykap** sa YouTube.","translation":"She took a long time because she was still learning how to **put on makeup** from YouTube."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggugol ng magdamag sa pagbabantay sa isang namatay bago ito ilibing; ang pagsasagawa ng lamay.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of what you do at a wake ('lamay'). It's that all-nighter you pull, not for a project deadline or for a video game, but to accompany the deceased and their family. It involves unlimited coffee, cheap biscuits, endless rounds of card games, and catching up with relatives you only see at weddings and funerals.
usage_notes: This verb specifically refers to the act of holding the vigil or wake. The noun for the event itself is 'lamay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **lamayin** ang labi ng kanilang lola hanggang sa araw ng libing.","translation":"We need to **hold a wake for** their grandmother's remains until the day of the burial."},{"sentence":"Sino-sino ang mag-iistay para **lamayin** si Mang Karding ngayong gabi?","translation":"Who will stay to **keep vigil for** Mang Karding tonight?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakasalalay o lubos na umaasa sa tulong, suporta, o kontrol ng iba o ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Ito yung state of being mo kapag 'di ka makapag-function nang walang kape sa umaga, o kapag 'di mo kayang mag-move on kasi attached ka pa rin sa ex mo. It's that 'can't live without you' feeling, whether it's for a person, a substance, or Wi-Fi.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa emosyonal, pinansyal, o pisikal na pag-asa sa isang bagay o tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating iwasan ang labis na **dependensiya** sa teknolohiya.","translation":"We should avoid excessive **dependency** on technology."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **dependensiya** sa alak ay nagdulot ng maraming problema.","translation":"His **dependency** on alcohol caused many problems."}]

translation: to turn; to revolve; to circulate
meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw sa isang paikot na paraan, pagbabago ng direksyon, o paglibot sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: The completed action of `umiikot`. The fan *turned*. Your world *spun*. The chismis *circulated*. It's also what you did when you realized you left your wallet at home and had to go back. "Umikot ako pabalik." It's the verb for any kind of turning, spinning, or going-around action.
usage_notes: This is the perfective (completed) aspect of the verb. Contrasts with the progressive `umiikot`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umikot** ang sasakyan para bumalik sa pinanggalingan.","translation":"The car **turned** to go back where it came from."},{"sentence":"Mabilis na **umikot** ang balita tungkol sa kanilang pagpapakasal.","translation":"The news about their wedding **circulated** quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang hindi tiyak ngunit maliit na bilang o dami.
original_explanation: When you don't have an exact number, you use **ilang**. '**Ilang** minuto na lang' (Just a few more minutes) is the classic Filipino response when you're running late. It's the vague quantifier for 'not many, but more than one.'
usage_notes: Used as a determiner before a noun. The stress on the second syllable /i-LANG/ distinguishes it from 'Ílang' /I-lang/ (wilderness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **ilang** tao na naghihintay sa labas.","translation":"There are **a few** people waiting outside."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng **ilang** taon, nagkita silang muli.","translation":"After **some** years, they met again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na walang trabaho, pinagkakakitaan, o permanenteng mapagkukunan ng kita.
original_explanation: The official term for being a *tambay*. It's that awkward phase after graduation or after getting laid off. It's when your main job is sending out resumes on JobStreet and LinkedIn and your main skill is "available anytime for an interview." The opposite of a workaholic.
usage_notes: A direct and common way to state that someone is jobless. 'Walang trabaho' is a more casual synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang naging **walang-hanapbuhay** dahil sa pandemya.","translation":"Many people became **unemployed** because of the pandemic."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng bagong apartment kahit **walang-hanapbuhay**.","translation":"He is looking for a new apartment even though he is **jobless**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masusing paghahanap o pag-alam sa pinagmulan o kinaroroonan ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagsunod sa mga bakas o palatandaan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate Marites/detective move. When your friend says 'he's just a friend' but you see his name tagged in a post from 2018, you 'pagbakas-bakasin' their entire digital footprint. It's about connecting the dots, following the trail of resibos, IG stories, and shared Spotify playlists to find the truth.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'bakas' (trace/mark) implies a thorough and meticulous search. This is a verb in its command/infinitive form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng detektib na **pagbakas-bakasin** ang mga huling sandali ng biktima.","translation":"The detective tried **to trace** the victim's last moments."}]

translation: to cause; to bring about; to result in
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi o dahilan ng isang pangyayari, kalagayan, o resulta.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'cause and effect' verb. 'Yung pagpindot mo ng 'snooze' ay pwedeng magdulot ng pagiging late mo sa work. 'Yung pag-reply mo sa 'hi' ng ex mo ay pwedeng magdulot ng gulo. It's the verb that reminds you that actions have consequences, bes.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the outcome or consequence of an action or event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malakas na ulan ay maaaring **magdulot** ng baha.","translation":"Heavy rain can **cause** flooding."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **magdulot** ng kapayapaan ang ating pag-uusap.","translation":"I hope our conversation **will bring about** peace."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-atas sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng isang legal na dokumento (subpoena) na humarap sa korte.
etymology: From English 'subpoena', adapted into a Tagalog verb form.
original_explanation: When the drama gets real and escalates from a heated exchange on Facebook to a legal battle. To **subpenahin** someone is to serve them a subpoena. It's the government's official way of saying, "See you in court." You hear this a lot on TV news about politicians or celebrities.
usage_notes: A legal term that has entered common parlance through media. The root 'subpena' is the Tagalized noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano ng komite na **subpenahin** ang mga opisyal na sangkot sa anomalya.","translation":"The committee plans **to subpoena** the officials involved in the anomaly."},{"sentence":"Kapag hindi ka dumating, maaaring **subpenahin** ka ng korte.","translation":"If you don't show up, the court might **subpoena** you."}]

translation: to invite; to persuade to come along
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghikayat o pagkumbinsi sa isang tao na sumama sa isang gawain o lugar.
original_explanation: This is the 'Tara, sama ka!' verb. It's when you try to convince your friend to join you, whether it's for a coffee run, a road trip, or to help you move furniture. It's a low-pressure invitation, less formal than 'anyayahan'. It's the 'budol' before the actual 'budol'.
usage_notes: Often used in an imperative or object-focus form. The root word 'yakag' means an invitation or act of persuasion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Yakagin** mo ang buong barkada para mas masaya.","translation":"**Invite** the whole squad so it's more fun."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan siyang **yakagin** ng kanyang mga kaibigan na lumabas.","translation":"His friends tried to **persuade him to come along** to go out."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng pintura sa isang ibabaw, alinman bilang isang gawaing sining o para sa pagprotekta at pagpapaganda ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is your artist friend's favorite hobby, turning a blank canvas into a masterpiece. It's also what your dad does every summer—repainting the gate a slightly different shade of brown. Whether you're Bob Ross creating happy little trees or just giving your bedroom wall a fresh coat, you're 'nagpipinta'.
usage_notes: Can refer to both artistic painting and functional painting (e.g., painting a house).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong matutong **magpinta** ng mga tanawin.","translation":"I want to learn how to **paint** landscapes."},{"sentence":"Sila ay **nagpinta** ng buong bahay bilang paghahanda sa Pasko.","translation":"They **painted** the whole house in preparation for Christmas."}]

translation: to live luxuriously; to display ostentation
meaning_filipino: Mamuhay nang marangya o magpakita ng labis na karangyaan at kasaganaan.
original_explanation: From the root word 'rangya' (luxury/ostentation). This is the verb form of 'flexing.' It's when someone starts living the high life, showing off their new gadgets, designer bags, and travel photos. Think of that friend who suddenly got a high-paying job abroad and now their IG feed looks like a luxury brand catalog. Sila yung rumangya. It's living a life of 'sana all.'
usage_notes: Madalas may bahid ng paghuhusga o inggit kapag ginagamit, na nagpapahiwatig ng pagiging mapagpasikat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Simula nang manalo siya sa lotto, **rumangya** na ang kanyang pamumuhay.","translation":"Ever since he won the lottery, his lifestyle has **become luxurious**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **rumangya** at baka ma-scam ka lang.","translation":"Don't **display your wealth** too much, you might just get scammed."}]

meaning_filipino: Matinding kislap o liwanag na nagmumula sa isang bagay; kaningningan.
original_explanation: This is the bling-bling effect. It's the sparkle in your crush's eye, the glitter on your Christmas decor, or the shine of a freshly polished floor. It's more about the dazzling light itself, whereas 'kinang' is more about the reflective quality of a surface. 'Ningning' is the performance, 'kinang' is the potential.
usage_notes: Often contrasted with 'liwanag' (light). A famous Filipino saying is 'Ang ningning ay madaling makasilaw, ngunit ang liwanag ay tumutulong sa paghanap ng daan.' (Brilliance can easily blind, but light helps find the way.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakasilaw ang **ningning** ng mga bituin sa kalangitan.","translation":"The **sparkle** of the stars in the sky is blinding."},{"sentence":"Ang **ningning** ng kanyang tagumpay ay inspirasyon sa marami.","translation":"The **brilliance** of her success is an inspiration to many."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pakikipagkasundo o pagtatakda ng isang pagkikita sa isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'tipan' at hulaping '-in'.
original_explanation: This is the action verb for "tipan." It's when you actively set that super serious meeting or romantic date. "Tipanin mo siya sa park" means "Set a meeting with him/her at the park." It has a certain romantic, old-world charm, like you're arranging a rendezvous straight out of a Jose Rizal novel.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na pandiwa. Ang anyong naganap ay "tinipan", pangkasalukuyan ay "tinitipan", at panghinaharap ay "titipanin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **tipanin** ang kanyang kasintahan sa ilalim ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"He wants to **set a meeting with** his beloved under the mango tree."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **tipanin** ang isang taong laging abala.","translation":"It's hard to **make an appointment with** a person who is always busy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o gusali kung saan isinasagawa ang pananahi, pag-aayos, o paggawa ng mga kasuotan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "tahi" at hulaping panlunan na "-an".
original_explanation: Dito mo dinadala yung mga damit na kailangan i-alter, ipa-repair, o ipagawa from scratch. Ito ang 'clinic' ng mga damit. Dito nagaganap ang magic bago ang graduation, kasal, o JS prom. Ang headquarters ng mga mananahi at sastre.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa pisikal na lugar kung saan nagaganap ang pananahi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magpapagawa ako ng bestida sa **tahian** ni Aling Nena.","translation":"I will have a dress made at Aling Nena's **sewing shop**."},{"sentence":"Dinala ko sa **tahian** ang pantalon kong napunit.","translation":"I brought my torn pants to the **tailor shop**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tulong o saklolong ibinibigay sa isang taong nasa panganib, kagipitan, o kagyat na pangangailangan.
original_explanation: This isn't just your regular "tulong." `Panaklolo` is the dramatic, superhero-style rescue. It's the friend who arrives with food when you're broke before payday, the BPO agent who calmly guides you when your internet dies mid-presentation, or the "resbak" you call when you're in trouble. It’s help that comes in the nick of time.
usage_notes: `Panaklolo` is a more formal and slightly dramatic word for 'help' compared to the everyday `tulong`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumigaw siya para humingi ng **panaklolo** nang makita niya ang sunog.","translation":"She shouted to ask for **help** when she saw the fire."},{"sentence":"Agad na dumating ang mga pulis upang magbigay ng **panaklolo**.","translation":"The police arrived immediately to provide **aid**."}]

translation: act of stamping, marking, or branding
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay ng marka, selyo, o tatak sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: It's that satisfying *thump* when the government employee stamps your document, or when you put your custom 'Ex Libris' stamp on a new book. It's the physical act of leaving a mark, whether it's a 'PAID' stamp on a bill or branding cattle. In a hugot sense, it's like how an ex leaves a 'tatak' on your heart.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis ang **pagtatatak** ng mga resibo sa munisipyo.","translation":"The **stamping** of receipts at the municipal hall is fast."},{"sentence":"Kasama sa proseso ang **pagtatatak** ng logo sa bawat produkto.","translation":"The process includes the **marking** of the logo on every product."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang agham at sining ng pag-aaral, pagtukoy, paggamot, at pag-iwas sa sakit; maaari ring tumukoy sa gamot.
original_explanation: The dream course of every Filipino parent for their child. It's the whole universe of doctors, hospitals, prescriptions, and that one subject in college that made you cry (hello, organic chemistry). It's both the pill you take for a headache and the entire profession dedicated to making that headache go away.
usage_notes: Can refer to the field of study ('nag-aaral ng medisina') or the actual medication ('uminom ng medisina'), though 'gamot' is more common for the latter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang mag-aral ng **medisina** upang makatulong sa kapwa.","translation":"She dreams of studying **medicine** to help others."},{"sentence":"Ang mga halamang-gamot ay isang alternatibong uri ng **medisina**.","translation":"Herbal plants are an alternative form of **medicine**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na bumibisita sa isang tahanan, lugar, o okasyon; bisita.
etymology: Mula sa `pa-` + `saog` ('baba') + `-in`. Ang ideya ay "isang taong pinapanaog o tinatanggap sa ibabang bahagi ng bahay".
original_explanation: Your bisita! The reason why you suddenly clean the entire house and bring out the "special" plates that you never use. Whether it's your tita from the province, your friends coming over for K-drama night, or an unexpected food delivery guy, they're all your panauhin. The VIP of the household, at least for a day.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang salita. Maaaring gamitin sa pormal at di-pormal na sitwasyon. Ang "bisita" ay mas karaniwang kasingkahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maghanda tayo ng masarap na pagkain para sa ating mga **panauhin**.","translation":"Let's prepare delicious food for our **guests**."},{"sentence":"Ang **panauhin** pandangal sa pagtatapos ay isang kilalang siyentipiko.","translation":"The **guest** of honor at the graduation is a famous scientist."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay o tao na nasa ika-90 na posisyon sa isang serye o pagkakasunod-sunod.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're in a super long queue for concert tickets and you're the 90th person. Or when your lola celebrates her ninetieth birthday. It's not a number you use every day, but when you do, it usually means something is either very old, very long, or you've been waiting for a *very* long time.
usage_notes: An ordinal number. The prefix "ika-" is more commonly used to form ordinal numbers (e.g., "ika-siyamnapu").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang namin ang kanyang **pansiyamnapu** na kaarawan.","translation":"We are celebrating his **ninetieth** birthday."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **pansiyamnapu** sa listahan ng mga naghihintay.","translation":"She is the **ninetieth** on the waiting list."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang direkta o tuwid patungo sa isang direksyon; walang pagliko o pag-ikot.
original_explanation: What the Grab driver asks you: "Sir, paderetso lang po ba tayo dito?" (Sir, are we just going straight ahead here?). It's the opposite of "paligoy-ligoy" (beating around the bush). If you want the chismis, you tell your friend, "Paderetso na, ano ba talaga nangyari?" (Get straight to the point, what really happened?).
usage_notes: The 'pa-' prefix indicates direction or movement towards.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula rito, maglakad ka lang nang **paderetso** at makikita mo na ang simbahan.","translation":"From here, just walk **straight ahead** and you will see the church."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nag-oorganisa, nangangasiwa, at tumatanggap ng panganib ng isang negosyo o kalakalan.
etymology: Mula sa Pranses na "entrepreneur", at hiniram sa Ingles.
original_explanation: Ito yung tropa mong nag-umpisa sa pagbebenta ng yema spread online, tapos ngayon may sarili nang café. Sila yung mga taong mas gugustuhing magpuyat para sa sariling business kesa mag-render ng OT para sa iba. Ang motto: "Diskarte at dasal."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa Filipino na walang salin. Ang katumbas na salitang "negosyante" ay mas madalas gamitin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipinong **entrepreneur** ang nagsimula sa maliit na puhunan.","translation":"Many Filipino **entrepreneurs** started with small capital."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging isang **entrepreneur** ay nangangailangan ng tiyaga at pagiging malikhain.","translation":"Being an **entrepreneur** requires patience and creativity."}]

translation: to cause trouble for; to inconvenience; to harm
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng abala, pinsala, o anumang makasasama sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: When you're not just being an 'abala' (inconvenience), you've leveled up to actively causing damage or major stress. It’s what your kapitbahay thinks you’re doing when you practice karaoke at 10 PM. It’s what you want to do to the person who stole your lunch from the office fridge.
usage_notes: Has a stronger connotation than 'abalahin' (to bother). It implies some level of harm or serious trouble.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **perhuwisyuhin** sa mga problema mong ikaw mismo ang gumawa.","translation":"Don't **cause me trouble** with problems you yourself created."},{"sentence":"Ang tanging layunin niya ay **perhuwisyuhin** ang negosyo ng kanyang katunggali.","translation":"His only goal is to **harm** his competitor's business."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakalaking kaldero o kawa, karaniwang ginagamit sa pagluluto para sa malaking bilang ng tao, tulad ng sa mga pista o malalaking pagtitipon.
original_explanation: The final boss of kalderos. This is the gigantic pot you only see during fiestas, used for cooking 'pakain' for the whole barangay. It's so big, you probably need a boat paddle to stir the contents. This is where they cook the free lugaw during campaign season.
usage_notes: Augmentative of 'kaldero', meaning a very large pot. Often used interchangeably with 'kawa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kalderon** ng kare-kare ang niluto para sa pista.","translation":"A **large cauldron** of kare-kare was cooked for the fiesta."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng dalawang tao para buhatin ang **kalderon**.","translation":"It takes two people to lift the **large cauldron**."}]

translation: to ride as a passenger (on a motorcycle or bicycle)
meaning_filipino: Sumakay sa likuran ng isang tao sa motorsiklo, bisikleta, o kabayo.
etymology: From Tagalog 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'angkas' (a passenger riding behind the driver, especially on a two-wheeled vehicle).
