original_explanation: This is the official verb of motorcycle taxi apps like Angkas. When you 'book a ride' and sit behind the driver, you are the 'angkas' and the action is 'mag-angkas'. It's the ultimate Manila traffic hack, a test of trust between you and the driver as you weave through EDSA.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to riding as a back-rider on a two-wheeled vehicle or an animal like a horse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal **mag-angkas** ng bata sa motorsiklo kung walang helmet.","translation":"It's forbidden **to have a child ride as a passenger** on a motorcycle without a helmet."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **mag-angkas** para makarating agad sa opisina.","translation":"I need **to ride as a passenger** (on a motorcycle) to get to the office quickly."}]

translation: to subside; to abate; to recede
meaning_filipino: Bumaba o kumalma ang isang bagay na dati'y matindi o mataas, tulad ng baha, lagnat, o galit.
original_explanation: This is what you pray for when you have a high fever, when EDSA is a parking lot because of flooding, or when your boss is on a rampage. It means to go down, to get less intense. 'Sana *humupa* na ang baha.' (I hope the flood subsides.) 'Hayaan mo munang *humupa* ang galit niya.' (Let his anger subside first.)
usage_notes: Used for various phenomena that decrease in intensity: floods, fever, emotions, swelling, storms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **humupa** na rin ang baha sa aming kalye.","translation":"Finally, the flood on our street has **subsided**."},{"sentence":"Uminom siya ng gamot upang **humupa** ang kanyang lagnat.","translation":"He/She took medicine for his/her fever to **abate**."}]

translation: to be the cause of chaos/trouble
meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan o sanhi ng kaguluhan, pagkalito, o kawalan ng kaayusan.
original_explanation: This is the friend who suggests "one last drink" at 3 AM. It's the "optional" system update that bricks your phone. It's the reason why the group chat is on fire and why HR wants to see you.
usage_notes: Focuses on the specific thing or action that brings about a state of disorder or conflict.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagkawala ng wifi ang **ikinagulo** ng buong opisina.","translation":"The loss of wifi **was the cause of chaos** for the whole office."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumawa ng anumang **ikagugulo** ng sitwasyon.","translation":"Don't do anything that **will cause trouble** in the situation."}]

translation: was exterminated, was eradicated, was annihilated
meaning_filipino: Lubusang nalipol, nawala, o namatay; ganap na winasak o tinapos.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'nasira' (damaged) or 'nawala' (lost). This is total annihilation. Think Thanos snap. It's what you want to happen to cockroaches in your kitchen, a computer virus, or a really bad idea. It means wiped out, gone, zero survivors.
usage_notes: A very strong word implying complete destruction or elimination.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napuksa** ang lahat ng peste sa bukid dahil sa bagong pestisidyo.","translation":"All the pests in the field **were exterminated** because of the new pesticide."},{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng kampanya ay upang **mapuksa** ang kahirapan sa bansa.","translation":"The campaign's goal is to **eradicate** poverty in the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdulot ng kalituhan sa isang tao; gawing tuliro ang isang indibidwal.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your crush gives you mixed signals. One day they're super sweet, the next day they're 'seen.' They're not just confusing you, they're actively 'tuliruhin' your heart. It's a verb for causing mental chaos.
usage_notes: Object-focused verb. The person being confused is the object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang **tuliruhin** sa mga kumplikadong tanong.","translation":"Don't **confuse** him with complicated questions."},{"sentence":"Tila tinutuliro ng mga pagbabago sa sistema ang mga empleyado.","translation":"It seems the changes in the system are **bewildering** the employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sagisag, tanda, o marka ng isang tanggapan, ranggo, organisasyon, o karangalan.
original_explanation: 'Yung patch sa uniform ng pulis, 'yung pin sa coat ng isang opisyal, o 'yung logo ng eskwelahan mo sa iyong ID lace. 'Yan ang insigniya. It's the bling that says 'I belong' or 'I'm important.' Parang 'yung blue check sa social media, pero sa totoong buhay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **insigniya** sa kanyang balikat ay nagpapakita na isa siyang heneral.","translation":"The **insignia** on his shoulder shows that he is a general."},{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niyang isuot ang **insigniya** ng kanilang samahan.","translation":"He proudly wears the **emblem** of their organization."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng salita na hindi pormal at karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pakikipag-usap ng isang partikular na grupo ng mga tao.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung mga words na kung isasagot mo sa lola mo, mapapakamot siya sa ulo. 'Lodi', 'petmalu', 'werpa', 'charot'—lahat 'yan salitang-balbal. The language of the streets, of memes, of your group chat. It's the ever-changing, 'di-pormal na vocabulary ng Pinoy.
usage_notes: 'Balbal' is one of the levels of language in Filipino, representing the lowest, non-standard, and often ephemeral vocabulary. It is also known as 'salitang-kalye' (street language).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang \"erpat\" ay isang **salitang-balbal** para sa \"ama\".","translation":"\"Erpat\" is a **slang word** for \"father\"."},{"sentence":"Mabilis magbago ang mga **salitang-balbal** na ginagamit ng kabataan.","translation":"The **slang words** used by the youth change quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na pinagkakatiwalaan sa pag-iingat at pamamahala ng pondo ng isang organisasyon, samahan, o pamahalaan.
original_explanation: The one in the barkada who always says, "KKB tayo" (Kanya-Kanyang Bayad). In any group project, student council, or even your local homeowners' association, the 'tesorero' is the one holding the purse strings. They're the person you have to be nice to if you want your budget approved. Basically, the CFO of the tropa.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit nang palitan sa 'ingat-yaman'. Ang 'tesorero' ay mas karaniwan sa mga pormal na titulo sa organisasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tesorero** ng klase ang maniningil ng ambagan para sa Christmas party.","translation":"The class **treasurer** will collect the contributions for the Christmas party."},{"sentence":"Kinausap ng pangulo ang **tesorero** tungkol sa kasalukuyang pondo ng samahan.","translation":"The president spoke with the **treasurer** regarding the organization's current funds."}]

translation: to make bitter; to make worse
meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang paggawa sa isang sitwasyon na maging mas masakit, mas mahirap, o mas hindi kaaya-aya.
original_explanation: Ito yung action na ginagawa ng kontrabida sa teleserye. Hindi lang sila masama, sinisigurado pa nilang mas lalong magdudusa ang bida. Parang na-wrong send ka na nga ng message, tapos na-screenshot pa at pinost sa group chat. Ginawa mo nang masama, pinili mo pang pasaklapin.
usage_notes: Carries a strong sense of intentionality in making a bad situation worse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **pasaklapin** pa ang sitwasyon sa pamamagitan ng pagsisinungaling.","translation":"Don't **make the situation worse** by lying."},{"sentence":"Tila sinadya ng tadhana na **pasaklapin** ang kanyang araw.","translation":"It seems fate deliberately chose to **make his day more bitter**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagbibigay ng kasiyahan o kaaya-ayang pakiramdam; kalugud-lugod sa paningin, pandinig, o pakiramdam.
etymology: From the root word 'aya', which means pleasantness or agreeableness.
original_explanation: The vibe of a coffee shop with good wifi, comfy chairs, and a barista who doesn't judge your complicated order. It's the feeling of a cool breeze on a hot day. If a place or a person makes you feel relaxed and welcome, they have a maaya presence. It's the 'good vibes only' of adjectives.
usage_notes: Often used to describe atmosphere, weather, or a person's disposition. Can be used interchangeably with 'kaaya-aya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagandang gumising sa umaga kapag **maaya** ang panahon.","translation":"It's so wonderful to wake up in the morning when the weather is **pleasant**."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **maaya** na personalidad kaya marami siyang kaibigan.","translation":"She has an **agreeable** personality, which is why she has many friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng maraming hindi kinakailangang salita o detalye; hindi direkta sa punto; paligoy-ligoy.
original_explanation: This describes someone who won't get straight to the point. It's your officemate who takes 20 minutes to ask a simple question, or a politician answering with everything but a 'yes' or 'no'. In a hugot context, it's when you ask 'Ano ba tayo?' and the answer you get is full of 'basta masaya tayo 'di ba?'—that's pure ligoy.
usage_notes: Often used with 'paligoy-ligoy' for emphasis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiinis ako sa mga sagot niyang punô ng **ligoy**.","translation":"I get annoyed with his answers that are full of **verbiage**."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang magpaligoy-**ligoy** pa, sabihin mo na ang totoo.","translation":"Don't be **roundabout** anymore, just tell the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bantas ( ) na ginagamit upang ihiwalay ang isang salita, parirala, o pangungusap na hindi gaanong mahalaga sa diwa ng pangunahing pangungusap ngunit nagbibigay ng dagdag na impormasyon.
original_explanation: That thing in grammar you use for side comments (like this one). It's the written version of whispering something to your friend in the middle of a meeting. In Tagalog, the more common term is 'panaklong', but 'parentisis' is for when you want to sound more academic or 'conyo'.
usage_notes: Ang salitang 'panaklong' ay mas karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan at sa pagtuturo sa mga paaralan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilagay mo sa loob ng **parentisis** ang mga hindi importanteng detalye.","translation":"Put the unimportant details inside the **parenthesis**."},{"sentence":"Ang taon ng kanyang kapanganakan (1987) ay nakasulat sa tabi ng kanyang pangalan, na nasa **parentisis**.","translation":"His birth year (1987) is written beside his name, which is in **parenthesis**."}]

translation: a plan that won't happen, a flaked plan
meaning_filipino: Sa kolokyal na gamit, tumutukoy ito sa isang plano, usapan, o lakad na hindi natuloy.
etymology: Semantic shift from the literal English "drawing", possibly implying the plan only exists "on paper" or as a concept and not in reality.
original_explanation: The slang meaning that hits too close to home. It's for all those group chat plans that start with "Tara, kape!" and end with... nothing. It's the official term for all the "see you soon" promises that get lost in the void. "Drawing ka na naman!" means "You're all talk, no action!"
usage_notes: Extremely common slang, especially among younger generations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala ko tuloy na ang bakasyon, **drowing** lang pala.","translation":"I thought the vacation was a go, it turned out to be just a **flaked plan**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawan ng lunas ang isang karamdaman o pinsala upang bumuti ang kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is what doctors do, what your mom's 'Vicks VapoRub' is supposed to do, and what you wish time could do to a broken heart. It's the process of making something sick or broken, well again. "Pagaling ka!" is the ultimate Filipino get-well-soon card.
usage_notes: The root 'galing' in this context refers to wellness or recovery, not to be confused with 'galing' meaning excellence or skill.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa ospital upang **pagalingin** ang kanyang sakit.","translation":"He was brought to the hospital to **cure** his illness."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **pagalingin** ng panahon ang lahat ng sugat.","translation":"I hope time will **heal** all wounds."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-udyok o pagsulsol sa isang tao upang gumawa ng isang bagay, karaniwang isang negatibong aksyon.
original_explanation: This is the Marites starter pack. It's when you whisper to your friend, "Uy, 'di ba sabi mo magre-resign ka na? Gawin mo na!" It's the art of planting a mischievous idea in someone's head and watching the chaos unfold. To be the devil on someone's shoulder.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of encouraging bad behavior or conflict.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **paudyukan** sa mga kaibigan mong mahilig sa gulo.","translation":"Don't be **instigated** by your friends who love trouble."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan siyang **paudyukan** ng katrabaho na magreklamo sa HR.","translation":"His co-worker tried to **incite** him to complain to HR."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi totoo; huwad; peke. Sa musika, ito ay nangangahulugang wala sa tamang tono o sintunado.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung "I'm okay" mo pero umiiyak ka sa loob. Parang 'yung branded bag na nabili mo sa Greenhills. O parang 'yung boses ng kaibigan mo sa karaoke na masakit sa tenga. Anything that isn't the real deal—be it an object, a feeling, or a musical note—is **palso**.
usage_notes: Can refer to objects (counterfeit) or sound (out of tune). 'Peke' is a more common synonym for counterfeit items, while 'sintunado' is more specific for music.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga alahas na ito ay mukhang totoo pero **palso** pala.","translation":"These jewels look real but are actually **fake**."},{"sentence":"Naging **palso** ang kaniyang pagkanta dahil sa kaba.","translation":"His singing became **out of tune** because of nervousness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakahalaga o pundamental na alaala na humuhubog sa pagkatao o pananaw ng isang indibidwal.
etymology: From English "core memory", popularized by the 2015 film "Inside Out".
original_explanation: Yung mga alaalang hinding-hindi mo makakalimutan at parang naging parte na ng pagkatao mo. Tipong 'pag naaalala mo, either sobrang saya mo or sobrang sakit. 'Yung first time mong kumain ng Jollibee, o 'yung graduation mo—yan, core memory 'yan! Unlocked!
usage_notes: Often used on social media to describe a significant and cherished moment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Yung unang family trip namin sa beach, **core memory** talaga 'yun para sa akin.","translation":"Our first family trip to the beach is truly a **core memory** for me."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa araw na ito, bagong **core memory** unlocked!","translation":"Thanks for this day, new **core memory** unlocked!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng pagsang-ayon, pagpapasimula ng isang bagong paksa, o pagtatapos ng isang usapan.
original_explanation: The classic tito/tita way of saying 'O, sige na,' 'Okay, game,' or 'Alright, moving on...' before they tell a long story or change the topic during a family gathering. It's the verbal equivalent of a nod and a deep breath.
usage_notes: Used to transition a conversation, express agreement, or reluctantly concede a point.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Buweno!** Kung iyan ang gusto mo, pagbibigyan kita.","translation":"**Alright!** If that's what you want, I'll give it to you."},{"sentence":"**Buweno**, simulan na natin ang pagpupulong.","translation":"**Well**, let's start the meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging gising ngunit hindi pa lubos na mulat ang diwa, karaniwan pagkatapos ng biglaang pagkagising o mula sa mahimbing na tulog.
original_explanation: That zombie mode you're in for the first 10 minutes after your alarm goes off. You're awake, but your brain is still buffering. You might accidentally put salt in your coffee. It's the struggle between the dream world and the "Kailangan mo na bumangon" reality. Verb form: `maalimpungatan` (to be startled from sleep).
usage_notes: Describes the groggy, disoriented state immediately upon waking. Not to be confused with just being sleepy (antok).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa estado pa ako ng **alimpungatan** nang sagutin ko ang telepono.","translation":"I was still in a **state of being half-awake** when I answered the phone."},{"sentence":"Naalimpungatan ako dahil sa lakas ng kulog.","translation":"I was **startled from my sleep** because of the loud thunder."}]

translation: to be able to measure, measurable
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kakayahang alamin ang sukat, laki, halaga, o lawak ng isang bagay.
etymology: ma- (potential verb prefix) + susukat (future tense of 'sukat')
original_explanation: "Hindi **masusukat** ang pag-ibig ko sa'yo." The classic hugot line. It's for things you can't quantify, like love, happiness, or your data consumption while scrolling through TikTok. For things you *can* quantify, like your waistline after the holidays, you also use this word, but with more dread.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical measurements or figuratively for abstract concepts. The form 'nasusukat' is the present tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi **masusukat** sa pera ang tunay na pagkakaibigan.","translation":"True friendship cannot **be measured** by money."},{"sentence":"Tingnan natin kung **masusukat** ng metro ang haba ng lamesa.","translation":"Let's see if the length of the table can **be measured** by the meter stick."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng isang sasakyan na biglaang huminto o nasira habang nasa daan.
original_explanation: The ultimate Manila nightmare. You're cruising along C5, feeling good, then suddenly your car just dies. You're now a public nuisance, blocking traffic, getting cursed at by jeepney drivers. You are officially 'nakatirik'.
usage_notes: Specifically used for vehicles that have broken down.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang trapik dahil may bus na **nakatirik** sa flyover.","translation":"The traffic is terrible because a bus is **stalled** on the flyover."}]

meaning_filipino: Pinahiran o binalutan ng manipis na ginto; kulay ginto.
original_explanation: The original 'bling'. Before it was 'gold-plated', it was durado. It's that fancy, shiny gold look on church altars, antique furniture, or your tita's flashy earrings that are probably not real gold but look expensive anyway. It's the art of making something look more 'sosyal' with a touch of gold.
usage_notes: Often used to describe religious icons, antiques, and decorative items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang retablo ng lumang simbahan ay **durado**.","translation":"The altarpiece of the old church is **gilded**."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang koleksyon ng mga **durado** na kutsara at tinidor.","translation":"She has a collection of **gold-plated** spoons and forks."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng malalim na paggalang at pagkilala sa isang tao, lalo na sa mga nakatatanda o may katungkulan.
etymology: From "pitagan" (respect, reverence). The "pan-" prefix becomes "pam-" and the first syllable of the root is reduplicated.
original_explanation: This is the 'po' and 'opo' energy. It's the 'mano po' gesture you do for your elders. It's the opposite of pamimilosopo. It's that built-in Filipino software that reminds you to be polite and show deference, especially to anyone who looks older than your ate or kuya.
usage_notes: A formal word for respect, often implying a sense of awe or deference to authority or age.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinamalas niya ang kanyang **pamimitagan** sa pamamagitan ng pag-mano sa mga nakatatanda.","translation":"He showed his **respect** by doing the 'mano' gesture to the elders."},{"sentence":"Dapat manatili ang **pamimitagan** sa pagitan ng mga mag-aaral at ng kanilang mga guro.","translation":"**Reverence** must be maintained between students and their teachers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aalis, pagtatanggal, o pagpapalabas ng isang bagay o tao mula sa isang grupo o sistema.
original_explanation: The Hunger Games ng office, a.k.a. performance review season. O kaya yung process sa PBB kung saan isa-isang nawawala ang housemates. It's the act of getting rid of something, whether it's a contestant, a problem, or toxins from your body (sabi ng mga nagbebenta ng tea).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang susunod na bahagi ng programa ay ang **eliminasyon** ng mga kalahok.","translation":"The next part of the program is the **elimination** of the contestants."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **eliminasyon** ng basura para sa kalikasan.","translation":"Proper **elimination** of waste is important for the environment."}]

meaning_filipino: Harapin o lahukan ang isang mahirap, mapanganib, o mahalagang gawain, tulad ng labanan, kompetisyon, o trabaho.
etymology: From 'sabak' (engagement in battle/work) with the actor-focus infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: To dive headfirst into chaos. When you **sumabak** sa rush hour commute, you're a warrior. When you **sumabak** sa final exams with no sleep, you're a hero (or just a crammer). It's taking on a challenge, whether it's a literal battle, a tough project at work, or facing the Divisoria crowd during Christmas season. It’s game time!
usage_notes: Carries a connotation of difficulty, challenge, or intensity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Handa na ang mga sundalong **sumabak** sa labanan.","translation":"The soldiers are ready to **engage in** battle."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng training, **sumabak** agad siya sa bagong proyekto sa BPO.","translation":"After the training, she immediately **plunged into** the new project at the BPO."}]

meaning_filipino: Tingnan o tanawin nang mabilisan at hindi direkta.
original_explanation: That quick, ninja-level look you give your crush when they pass by. It’s not a stare (*titig*), it’s a peek. It's the 'I'm not looking but I'm totally looking' move. You **sulyapan** the menu when you're on a budget, you **sulyapan** your phone during a boring meeting, and you definitely **sulyapan** the chismis happening two tables away.
usage_notes: The root word is 'sulyap' (noun, a glance). 'Sulyapan' is the verb form meaning 'to glance at something/someone'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **sulyapan** ang sagot ng katabi niya sa exam.","translation":"He tried to **glance at** his seatmate's answer on the exam."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilang **sulyapan** ang magandang dalaga sa kabilang mesa.","translation":"He couldn't help but **glance at** the beautiful lady at the other table."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahaba at manipis na piraso ng isang bagay na pinunit o hiniwa, karaniwan ay papel, tela, o dahon.
original_explanation: Think of what a paper shredder produces. Those are 'gayas'. It's what's left of old love letters when you're in your 'move on' phase. Also, the strips of banana leaves used for certain kakanin. It’s a more destructive, strippy version of 'punit' (tear).
usage_notes: Often seen in its verb form 'gayasín' (to shred something). As a noun, it refers to the resulting strips.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkalat ang mga **gayas** ng papel sa sahig.","translation":"The **shreds** of paper were scattered on the floor."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **gayas** ng dahon ng saging bilang panali.","translation":"He used a **strip** of banana leaf as a tie."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa matematika, isang buumbilang na maaaring positibo, negatibo, o sero; ito ay isang bilang na walang bahaging praksyonal o desimal.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga numerong walang arte. Walang '.5' or '1/4'. Kung ano sila, 'yun na 'yun. Either you're a whole person, a whole negative person, or just plain zero. No in-betweens, walang M.U. (Mag-isang Unit).
usage_notes: Isang tiyak na termino sa larangan ng matematika. Kilala rin bilang "buumbilang".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang -5, 0, at 27 ay mga halimbawa ng **bilang na lantay**.","translation":"-5, 0, and 27 are examples of **integers**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong gamitin ang mga **bilang na lantay** sa paglutas ng problemang ito.","translation":"You need to use **integers** to solve this problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng pagkabingi o pagkawala ng pandinig.
original_explanation: That moment when the sound system at a concert is too loud, or when your auntie screams right next to your ear. It's the reason you're going 'HUH?! ANO?!' for the next five minutes. It's the cause of temporary (or permanent) hearing loss.
usage_notes: Used to describe the cause of deafness, whether temporary or permanent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sobrang lakas ng putok ay maaaring **ikabingi** mo.","translation":"The extreme loudness of the explosion might **cause your deafness**."},{"sentence":"Halos **ikinabingi** ko ang sigawan ng mga tao sa concert.","translation":"The shouting of the people at the concert almost **made me deaf**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapahayag ng sukdulang kahusayan, kakayahan, o pagiging epektibo sa isang gawain o larangan.
original_explanation: This is what your Tita says when you sing at the family reunion, even if you're slightly off-key. It's the ultimate Filipino compliment for any skill, from acing an exam to cooking the perfect adobo. The verbal equivalent of a chef's kiss.
usage_notes: A very common and versatile compliment for skill, performance, or intelligence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napakagaling** mong mananayaw!","translation":"You are an **excellent** dancer!"},{"sentence":"Wow, ang bilis mong natapos! **Napakagaling**!","translation":"Wow, you finished so quickly! **Brilliant**!"}]

translation: to become lively; to be invigorated
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago tungo sa isang mas masaya, masigla, at aktibong kalagayan.
original_explanation: That feeling when your sahod finally comes in. Or when the coffee kicks in. Or when your crush replies to your IG story. Biglang sumigla ang buong pagkatao mo. It's the opposite of being "lutang."
usage_notes: Refers to a change in state, from less energetic to more energetic. Can apply to people, a party, the economy, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumigla** ang paligid nang tumugtog ang masayang musika.","translation":"The atmosphere **became lively** when the happy music played."},{"sentence":"Tila **sumigla** ang pasyente pagkatapos makatanggap ng magandang balita.","translation":"The patient seemed to **brighten up** after receiving good news."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtakbo o pag-abante upang maabutan ang isang tao, bagay, o layunin na nauuna.
original_explanation: Parang ikaw, trying to meet a deadline na kahapon pa dapat sinimulan. O 'yung feeling na **humabol** ka sa jeep pero iniwan ka pa rin. Relate? That's the *habol* life. Ito rin yung ginagawa mo sa acads 'pag patapos na ang sem.
usage_notes: Can also mean 'to try to catch up' with a schedule, a lesson, or a deadline.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humabol** ang pulis sa magnanakaw.","translation":"The police **chased** the thief."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **humabol** sa mga aralin dahil lumiban ako kahapon.","translation":"I need to **catch up** on the lessons because I was absent yesterday."}]

meaning_filipino: Matinding sidhi o alab ng damdamin, tulad ng pag-ibig, galit, o pananampalataya.
original_explanation: This is a deep Tagalog word, the kind you find in poems or old love songs. It's not just love, it's that burning, all-consuming passion. Think of the intense patriotism of a hero or the fiery love in a classic Filipino movie. It's the "sana all" version of feelings. It's the opposite of being dead inside.
usage_notes: A literary or formal word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ramdam sa kanyang mga salita ang **dubdob** ng pagmamahal sa bayan.","translation":"You can feel in his words the **fervor** of his love for the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na istruktura na may bubong, karaniwang nasa gilid ng kalsada, kung saan maaaring maghintay at sumilong ang mga tao, lalo na ang mga nag-aabang ng pampublikong sasakyan.
etymology: Mula sa mga salitang Ingles na "waiting" at "shed."
original_explanation: Ang official tambayan ng mga commuter, umaraw man o umulan. Dito nangyayari ang lahat: pag-abang sa jeep na laging puno, pag-iwas sa matinding sikat ng araw, at minsan, pagiging temporary shelter sa biglaang buhos ng ulan. Ito rin ang lugar kung saan mo makikita ang iba't ibang anunsyo, mula sa "Tubero" hanggang sa "Bili kami Bote/Dyaryo." Isang Pambansang Silungan.
usage_notes: Ang katumbas sa Tagalog ay "hintayan" o "silungan," ngunit ang Ingles na termino ay mas karaniwang ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-abang kami ng bus sa **waiting shed**.","translation":"We waited for the bus at the **waiting shed**."},{"sentence":"Puno ng tao ang **waiting shed** dahil biglang umulan nang malakas.","translation":"The **waiting shed** was full of people because it suddenly rained hard."}]

translation: can be compared; can be likened
meaning_filipino: May kakayahang ihalintulad o ihambing sa isang bagay na may pagkakatulad.
etymology: From `ma-` (potential prefix) + `itutulad` (future tense of `itulad`, to liken). The root is `tulad` (like, similar to).
original_explanation: This is the engine of all analogies and similes. When you say, "Ang traffic sa EDSA ay maitutulad sa isang napakabagal na parking lot," you're using this verb. It's for finding similarities, drawing parallels, and making sense of one thing by explaining it in terms of another. The ultimate tool for poets and people trying to explain complex things to their lola.
usage_notes: This form is in the potential, future aspect ('can be compared'). The completed aspect is 'naitulad' ('was compared') and the infinitive potential is 'maitulad' ('to be able to compare').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang ganda ay **maitutulad** sa isang bulaklak sa parang.","translation":"Her beauty **can be likened** to a flower in a field."},{"sentence":"Walang sinuman ang **maitutulad** sa 'yo, ikaw ay natatangi.","translation":"No one **can be compared** to you, you are unique."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging labis na tuyo at malutong dahil sa matagal na pagkabilad sa init ng araw o apoy.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung nangyayari sa isdang binilad mo nang sobrang tagal sa araw—nagiging super crunchy. O 'yung balat mo pagkatapos mag-beach nang walang sunblock. O 'yung litson na naiwan sa initan. 'Yung itsura mong tayangtang after ng isang buong araw na field trip. Basically, anything that's been roasted by the sun to the point of crispiness.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para ilarawan ang pagkain (tulad ng tuyo o daing) o mga bagay na naiwan sa ilalim ng araw. Maaari ring maging pandiwa: "matayangtang".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **tayangtang** ang mga damit na isinampay dahil sa tindi ng sikat ng araw.","translation":"The clothes on the line became **over-dried** and stiff because of the intense heat of the sun."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong iprito ang isda at baka maging **tayangtang**.","translation":"Don't fry the fish too much or it might become **over-dried** and crispy."}]

translation: to look up, to raise one's head
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-angat ng ulo at mukha upang tumingin sa itaas o sa isang partikular na direksyon.
original_explanation: You know that moment in a movie when the shy protagonist, who's been looking down the whole time, finally lifts their head to face their destiny (or their crush)? That's 'tumunghay'. It's the opposite of 'yumuko' (to bow your head). It implies a shift from being downcast to being aware and looking forward or upward.
usage_notes: Carries a slightly formal or literary tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula sa kanyang pagkakayuko, dahan-dahan siyang **tumunghay** at ngumiti.","translation":"From his bowed position, he slowly **looked up** and smiled."},{"sentence":"**Tumunghay** siya sa kalangitan at pinagmasdan ang mga bituin.","translation":"He **raised his head** to the sky and watched the stars."}]

meaning_filipino: Abutan ng dilim sa isang lugar; maratnan na madilim ang isang pook.
original_explanation: This is that panic moment when you're hiking or on a road trip and the sun sets faster than you expected. Suddenly, you're in the dark, literally. 'Uy, bilisan natin, baka madiliman tayo sa daan!' It's the official verb for losing the race against sunset.
usage_notes: Often used as a warning to hurry up before evening.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magmadali tayong umuwi para hindi tayo **madiliman** sa daan.","translation":"Let's hurry home so we won't **be caught by nightfall** on the road."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **madiliman** sa gubat kaya maaga akong babalik.","translation":"I don't want to **be in the dark** in the forest, so I will return early."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghingi o pagkolekta ng bayad, utang, o anumang obligasyon sa pananalapi mula sa isang tao o entidad.
original_explanation: The official sport of your landlady, the 5-6 Bombay, and your friend who always remembers you owe them ₱20 from two years ago. It's the act of chasing what's rightfully yours, whether it's rent, a loan, or that coffee you paid for. The present/infinitive form of the threat, "Due date na, besh!"
usage_notes: This verb is often used in financial or transactional contexts. The future tense 'maniningil' is also very common and can function as a noun ('collector').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailan ka ba **maniningil** ng utang sa kanya?","translation":"When are you going to **collect** the debt from him?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiya na **maningil** para sa serbisyo mo.","translation":"Don't be shy to **charge** for your service."}]

translation: to feel ashamed; to become shy
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng damdamin ng hiya o pagiging mahiyain dahil sa isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is that feeling when your mom pulls out your baby pictures in front of your crush. Or when you try to sing in a videoke and your voice cracks on the first note. The `magka-` prefix implies you *acquired* or *were overcome by* the feeling of shame or shyness. It's an involuntary reaction to an awkward social situation.
usage_notes: Can mean to feel ashamed of something one did, or to become shy in a social context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagkahiya** siyang humarap sa mga tao matapos ang nangyari.","translation":"He **felt ashamed** to face people after what happened."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magkahiya**, sumali ka sa aming usapan.","translation":"Don't **be shy**, join our conversation."}]

translation: let me hug you; (can I) have a hug
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap upang makayakap o payagan ang sarili na yumakap sa isang tao.
etymology: From `pa-` (request prefix) + `akap` (hug). A contraction of 'paki-akap' or 'pahingi ng akap'.
original_explanation: The ultimate "I need comfort" command. It's what you say to your BFF after a bad day, or to your mom when you miss her. It's not asking *for* a hug, but asking *to give* a hug that you also receive. It's a mutual request. "**Paakap** nga, besh. Ang bigat ng araw ko." (Let me hug you, bestie. My day was so heavy.) It's the verbal equivalent of opening your arms.
usage_notes: A very common, intimate, and often gentle request.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umiiyak ang bata at sinabi sa ina, '**Paakap** po.'","translation":"The child was crying and told their mother, '**Let me hug you**.'"},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng matagal na hindi pagkikita, ang una niyang sinabi ay, '**Paakap**!'","translation":"After not seeing each other for a long time, the first thing she said was, '**Have a hug!**'"}]

translation: to have something carried on the shoulder
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aatas o pagpapahintulot sa iba na ilagay o buhatin ang isang bagay sa ibabaw ng balikat.
original_explanation: It's like asking your friend, "Bes, pakidala naman nitong sako ng bigas sa balikat mo, bigat eh." You're delegating the shoulder-carrying task. It's the verb form of asking someone to be your human crane for a moment.
usage_notes: The prefix "magpa-" indicates causation, meaning to cause or let someone do the action of the root word. Here, "pasang" is to carry on the shoulder.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magpasang** ka na lang ng sako sa kargador para hindi ka mapagod.","translation":"Just **have** the sack **carried on the shoulder** by a porter so you don't get tired."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na maraming damit o kasuotan.
original_explanation: This is you after a massive ukay-ukay haul or a 12.12 sale. Your closet is overflowing but you still have 'nothing to wear.' It's the opposite of that one friend who seems to own only three t-shirts.
usage_notes: Isang direktang salitang naglalarawan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Madamit** si Anna dahil mahilig siyang mamili online.","translation":"Anna **has many clothes** because she loves shopping online."},{"sentence":"Kahit **madamit** siya, iisa lang ang paborito niyang T-shirt.","translation":"Even if she **has a lot of clothes**, she only has one favorite T-shirt."}]

translation: To endure with great effort; to grudgingly bear
meaning_filipino: Ang patuloy at paulit-ulit na pagtitiis sa isang bagay kahit na ito ay lubhang mahirap o labag sa kalooban.
original_explanation: This is `tiisin` level-up. It's not just enduring, it's enduring while probably sighing heavily every five minutes. Ito 'yung ginagawa mo sa trabahong ayaw mo na pero kailangan mo ng pambayad ng bills. You're not just enduring; you're actively, consciously, and maybe complainingly **enduring** it moment by moment.
usage_notes: The reduplication implies a continuous, difficult, and often reluctant act of endurance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **tiis-tiisin** ang masungit na boss para sa pamilya ko.","translation":"I have to **grudgingly bear** with my grumpy boss for my family."},{"sentence":"**Tiniis-tiis** ko ang mahabang byahe sa EDSA araw-araw.","translation":"I **endured with great effort** the long commute on EDSA every day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahalang na biga o piraso ng kahoy o metal na karaniwang inilalagay sa itaas ng pinto o bintana, na kadalasang may salamin para sa bentilasyon o liwanag.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'travesaño' (pahalang na biga).
original_explanation: That thing in your lola's old house above the door that you never knew the name of. It's like the architectural equivalent of a forgotten T-bill. Sounds fancy, but it's just a wooden plank that helps with the 'singaw'.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa arkitektura at konstruksyon, lalo na sa paglalarawan ng mga lumang bahay na may disenyong Espanyol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May magandang ukit ang **trabisanyo** sa lumang bahay.","translation":"The **transom** in the old house has beautiful carvings."},{"sentence":"Binuksan niya ang **trabisanyo** para pumasok ang hangin.","translation":"He opened the **transom** to let the air in."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang mahalaga at kinakailangan; hindi maaaring mawala.
original_explanation: That thing you absolutely cannot live without. During the pandemic, it meant 'frontliners' and 'groceries.' In your daily life, it's probably coffee, Wi-Fi, and your phone charger. "Bes, esensiyal ang chismis para sa mental health ko."
usage_notes: Naging napakakaraniwang salita noong panahon ng pandemya ng COVID-19.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malinis na tubig ay **esensiyal** para sa kalusugan.","translation":"Clean water is **essential** for health."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing na **esensiyal** na manggagawa ang mga nars at doktor.","translation":"Nurses and doctors are considered **essential** workers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aso na may rabies o impeksiyon sa utak na nagdudulot ng pagiging agresibo at di-pangkaraniwang pag-uugali.
original_explanation: Literally 'crazy dog.' It's what you shout when a stray is foaming at the mouth and chasing the neighborhood kids. Metaphorically, it's that one person who goes berserk for no reason, like your boss during month-end closing or someone who gets extreme road rage in EDSA traffic. 'Chill ka lang, 'wag kang parang asong ulol.'
usage_notes: Ginagamit din bilang isang metapora para sa isang taong galit na galit, hindi makontrol, o mapanganib.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa daan, may nakawalang **asong ulol** daw sa kabilang kanto.","translation":"Be careful on the street, they say a **rabid dog** is loose on the other corner."},{"sentence":"Naging parang **asong ulol** siya sa galit nang malaman niyang niloko siya.","translation":"He became like a **rabid dog** in anger when he found out he was cheated."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking sako na karaniwang yari sa magaspang na tela tulad ng burlap o jute, ginagamit na lalagyan ng bigas, mais, o iba pang butil.
original_explanation: The palengke-grade backpack. This isn't your fancy Herschel bag; this is the heavy-duty sako that carries 50 kilos of rice, charcoal, or your tita's ukay-ukay haul. If you've ever played in a sack race during a fiesta or school sportsfest, you've definitely been inside a **kostal**.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'sako'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinasok niya ang mga bote sa loob ng isang **kostal** para i-recycle.","translation":"He put the bottles inside a **sack** to be recycled."}]

meaning_filipino: May katangian na marupok, babasagin, o madaling masira kapag nabagsak o tinamaan.
original_explanation: Literally, this is the 'FRAGILE' sticker on a balikbayan box full of glasswares. Figuratively, this is your heart after watching a sad K-drama, or your ego when your crush leaves you on 'seen.' Handle with care, beshie.
usage_notes: Used for both physical objects (glass, ceramics) and abstract concepts (heart, trust, ego).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng babala ang kahon dahil **madaling mabasag** ang laman niyan.","translation":"Put a warning on the box because its contents are **fragile**."},{"sentence":"Ang tiwala ay parang salamin na **madaling mabasag**.","translation":"Trust is like glass that is **easy to break**."}]

translation: to put in a will; to bequeath
meaning_filipino: Isama o ilagay sa isang legal na dokumento ng huling habilin (testamento) ang ari-arian o nais ipamana.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'Huling Habilin' move. This is what you do when you want to make sure your favorite apo gets the ancestral home and not the cousin you hate. 'Isatestamento' means you're officially putting it in your last will and testament, making it legally binding. It's the formal version of 'Sayo na 'to 'pag namatay ako.'
usage_notes: A formal term used in legal and inheritance contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano niyang **isatestamento** ang kanyang mga libro sa pampublikong aklatan.","translation":"He plans to **bequeath** his books to the public library."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang bahay ay **isinatestamento** sa panganay na anak.","translation":"The old house was **put in the will** for the eldest child."}]

translation: to hit; to spank; to strike
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng hampas o palo ang isang tao o bagay, karaniwan bilang parusa o gamit ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'the chancla' or 'the walis tambo'. It's the ultimate threat from Pinoy moms when you're being too pasaway. In sports, it's what you do to a volleyball. In love, it's what your heart feels like when you see your crush with someone else.
usage_notes: Can range from a light tap to a strong strike. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan ng nanay ang bata na **paluin** siya kapag hindi tumigil sa pag-iyak.","translation":"The mother warned the child that she would **spank** him if he didn't stop crying."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang matapang, masangsang, at hindi kaaya-ayang amoy.
etymology: The root word 'sangsang' also means a strong, often unpleasant, odor. The 'mu-' may be a variant or intensifier.
original_explanation: That smell that hits you in the face and makes your nose hairs curl? That's "musangsang". It’s the smell of a blocked canal, durian (for some people), or a garbage truck passing by on a hot day. It's a smell so strong it almost has a physical presence. It's the opposite of "mabango".
usage_notes: Describes a very strong, usually unpleasant, smell.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **musangsang** na amoy na nagmumula sa basurahan.","translation":"There is a **pungent** smell coming from the trash can."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya makain ang durian dahil sa **musangsang** nitong amoy.","translation":"He couldn't eat the durian because of its **reeking** odor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa 'Very Important Person.' Tumutukoy sa isang tao na binibigyan ng espesyal na pagtrato dahil sa kanyang katayuan, yaman, o impluwensya.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga taong hindi pumipila. Sa concert, sila yung nasa harap. Sa events, may sarili silang lounge na may libreng pagkain. Sa kalsada... well, 'wag na nating pag-usapan. Feeling VIP ka rin kapag 'yung suki mo sa palengke ay tinataguan ka ng pinakamagandang tinda.
usage_notes: Pronounced as individual letters 'V-I-P'. Used as both a noun and an adjective ('VIP treatment').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May special entrance para sa mga **VIP** sa concert.","translation":"There is a special entrance for the **VIPs** at the concert."},{"sentence":"Ginawa niya akong parang **VIP** noong dinalaw ko siya sa bahay nila.","translation":"She treated me like a **VIP** when I visited her at their house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hiwa ng karne mula sa tagiliran o bahagi ng tiyan ng hayop, partikular na ng baka.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish 'lapa', which has multiple meanings, but in this context refers to a flat section.
original_explanation: When you go to the palengke and ask the butcher for that specific cut of beef for your bistek or mechado. It's the part of the cow that's probably done a lot of core work.
usage_notes: A specific term used in butchery and cooking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakihiwa ng manipis ang **lapa** para sa bistek.","translation":"Please slice the **flank steak** thinly for bistek."},{"sentence":"Isang kilo ng **lapa** ang inorder ko sa karinderya.","translation":"I ordered one kilo of **flank** at the eatery."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng kagalakan, kasiyahan, o aliw.
original_explanation: 'Yung video ng pusa na nahulog sa upuan. 'Yung kwento ng lola mo tungkol sa kabataan niya. 'Yung effort ng jowa mo na sorpresahin ka kahit fail. Nakatutuwa is that warm, fuzzy feeling you get from something cute, funny, or genuinely pleasing. It's the wholesome version of "LOL".
usage_notes: Expresses a sense of delight, amusement, or pleasure. It is a very common and positive expression. Often used interchangeably with 'nakakatuwa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakatutuwa** ang mga batang naglalaro sa parke.","translation":"The children playing in the park are **delightful**."},{"sentence":"**Nakatutuwa** namang isipin na naaalala mo pa rin ako.","translation":"It's **pleasing** to think that you still remember me."}]

meaning_filipino: Pera na yari sa metal at may maliit na halaga; sinsilyo.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "varia", nangangahulugang 'iba-iba' o 'samut-sari', na malamang tumutukoy sa sari-saring maliliit na barya.
original_explanation: That's the stuff that jingles in your pocket and is the sworn enemy of laundry machines. It's what you use to pay for jeepney fare ("Barya lang po sa umaga!"), buy fishballs, or give to carolers during Christmas. It's small in value, but super essential for daily life.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin upang tukuyin ang mga barya mismo, o pangkalahatang maliit na halaga ng pera. Ang `sinsilyo` ay isang direktang kasingkahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **barya** para sa pamasahe sa dyip.","translation":"I need **coins** for the jeepney fare."},{"sentence":"Wala akong **barya**, buo ang pera ko.","translation":"I don't have **loose change**, my money is in whole bills."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagputol sa isang bagay gamit ang isang matalas na kasangkapan tulad ng kutsilyo. Ito ay ang nakaraang anyo ng pandiwang "hiwa".
original_explanation: What your mom does to the onions before she cries (or you cry). It's how you prep your mangoes for a perfect mango-graham dessert. In hugot terms, it's what your ex did to your heart. 'Hiniwa mo ang puso ko!'
usage_notes: Past tense of "hiwa" (to slice). Usually refers to food preparation but can be used for other cutting actions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **hiniwa** ang sibuyas para sa ginisa.","translation":"She carefully **sliced** the onion for the sauté."},{"sentence":"**Hiniwa** niya ang papel sa dalawang piraso.","translation":"He **cut** the paper into two pieces."}]

meaning_filipino: Isama o ilahok ang isang tao sa isang gawain, paligsahan, o grupo, kadalasan ay sa ngalan niya o may pahintulot.
original_explanation: When your mom thinks you're the next singing sensation and signs you up for the barangay talent show without your knowledge. "Bakit may pangalan ako dito?!" "Ah, oo, pinasalihan kita." It's being 'volun-told' to join something, Pinoy-style.
usage_notes: Focuses on the person being entered or made to join. Compare with 'pasalihan', which focuses on the activity or group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **pasalihin** ang anak ko sa swimming class.","translation":"I want to **make my child join** the swimming class."},{"sentence":"Sino ang gusto mong **pasalihin** sa paligsahan?","translation":"Who do you want to **enter** in the contest?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kahalagahan, kabuluhan, o katumbas na halaga ng isang bagay, serbisyo, o konsepto.
original_explanation: It's the 'know your worth' of things. Like when you're selling something on Carousell and the buyer lowballs you, you stand firm on its *balor*. It's the price tag, but also the sentimental value you can't quite quantify. 'Di lang presyo, kundi 'yung 'feels' din.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng komersiyo, pagtatasa, o abstraktong kahalagahan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **balor** sa merkado ng lumang alahas na ito?","translation":"What is the market **value** of this old piece of jewelry?"},{"sentence":"Hindi matutumbasan ng pera ang **balor** ng ating pagkakaibigan.","translation":"Money cannot equal the **value** of our friendship."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng masinsinang paghahanap sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagkakalkal o pagbubungkal, na kadalasan ay nagdudulot ng kalat.
original_explanation: Very similar to 'halukay', but with a slightly more intense, almost frantic energy. Think of a thief ransacking a room for valuables. That's 'halungkat'. It's the 'I-will-find-this-thing-even-if-I-destroy-everything' level of searching that leaves a huge mess.
usage_notes: Often used as a verb stem (e.g., halungkatin). As a noun, it refers to the chaotic act itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang **halungkat** na ginawa ng magnanakaw sa aming bahay.","translation":"The **ransacking** the thief did in our house was intense."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng kanyang **halungkat**, mas lalong gumulo ang kwarto.","translation":"After his **rummaging**, the room became even messier."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagwawakas sa buhay ng isang tao o hayop; tapusin o ubusin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The command to make someone 'utas'. This is the classic line of the Pinoy movie kontrabida to his goons. 'Utasin niyo ang lahat ng sagabal!' It's more dramatic and sinister than just saying 'patayin.' It means to terminate with prejudice, to finish the job completely.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a violent context, meaning 'to kill.' It carries a strong, often dramatic or cinematic, connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinag-utos ng masamang hari na **utasin** ang lahat ng kanyang mga kalaban.","translation":"The evil king ordered to **kill** all of his enemies."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi kita uutasin dahil lang sa natapon mong kape.","translation":"Don't worry, I won't **finish you off** just because of the coffee you spilled."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasa o taong may malalim na kaalaman sa pag-aaral ng wika, kasama ang estruktura, kasaysayan, at paggamit nito.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga taong kayang i-breakdown kung bakit "sana all" at "edi wow" ay valid forms of communication sa Pilipinas. Hindi lang sila basta polyglot na maraming alam na wika, pinag-aaralan nila yung mismong 'science' behind language. Sila yung totoong grammar police, pero with a degree.
usage_notes: Ang baybay na 'linggwista' ay karaniwan din ngunit ang 'lingguwista' ang sumusunod sa makabagong ortograpiyang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang kilalang **lingguwista** ang nagbigay ng panayam tungkol sa mga wika ng Pilipinas.","translation":"A famous **linguist** gave a lecture about the languages of the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na pinuno ng isang bansa, republika, kumpanya, o organisasyon.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'bida' (protagonist) or 'kontrabida' (antagonist) of a nation's teleserye, depending on who you ask. They're the CEO of the country, the one who gets all the credit and all the blame. The Pangulo is the person whose face is all over the news and whose decisions fuel family debates during Noche Buena.
usage_notes: While it can mean 'head' of any organization, it most commonly refers to the President of the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Pangulo** ng Pilipinas ay naninirahan sa Palasyo ng Malacañang.","translation":"The **President** of the Philippines resides in Malacañang Palace."},{"sentence":"Sino ang nahalal na bagong **pangulo** ng aming student council?","translation":"Who was elected as the new **president** of our student council?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan o bahagyang pagdikit o pagtama sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: That awkward moment in a crowded elevator or MRT when you're trying not to touch anyone, but your arm keeps sumasal sa katabi mo. It's a light, often accidental, touch. Not to be confused with a full-on 'hawak' or 'hipo'. Think of it as a physical "excuse me, po."
usage_notes: This is a less common word. 'Sumasagi' or 'dumadampi' are more frequent synonyms. It describes a very light, often brief or incidental, physical contact.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay may **sumasal** sa aking balikat habang naglalakad ako sa dilim.","translation":"I felt something **brushing against** my shoulder as I walked in the dark."},{"sentence":"Ang laylayan ng kanyang bestida ay **sumasal** sa sahig.","translation":"The hem of her dress was **touching lightly** on the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Inihagis o inilagay sa basurahan; pinabayaan o hindi na pinahalagahan.
original_explanation: What you did to your ex's stuff after the breakup. Or what your mom says you did to your life when you didn't become a doctor. "Sayang lang ang pag-aaral mo, itinapon mo lang!" It's the act of discarding something, whether it's literal trash or a metaphorical opportunity.
usage_notes: Past tense of 'itapon'. Can be used literally for garbage or figuratively for opportunities, relationships, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itinapon** niya ang mga lumang damit na hindi na kasya sa kanya.","translation":"She **threw away** the old clothes that no longer fit her."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong sabihing parang basura mo lang akong **itinapon**!","translation":"Don't you dare say you just **threw** me **away** like trash!"}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pang-uri, tumutukoy sa mga bagay, gawain, o taong may kaugnayan sa simbahan o sa mga klerigo. Bilang pangngalan, tumutukoy ito sa isang taong-simbahan o pari.
original_explanation: Think anything and everything related to the Church hierarchy. Not just the Sunday mass, but the whole organizational chart—bishops, priests, the rules they follow, the special clothes they wear. If it smells like incense and involves formal church business, it's probably *eklesyastiko*. It’s a high-level, formal word you'd hear from a historian or a news anchor, not from your tita at the palengke.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pormal at bihirang salita, ginagamit lamang sa mga kontekstong panrelihiyon, akademiko, o pangkasaysayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga batas **eklesyastiko** ay mahigpit na ipinatutupad sa loob ng kanilang diyosesis.","translation":"The **ecclesiastical** laws are strictly implemented within their diocese."},{"sentence":"Isang kilalang **eklesyastiko** ang namuno sa isinagawang pagpupulong.","translation":"A known **clergyman** led the meeting that was held."}]

translation: rich in dreams (but poor in reality)
meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pahayag para sa isang taong maraming pangarap at ambisyon ngunit salat o kulang sa materyal na bagay o sa kasalukuyang katotohanan.
original_explanation: The official motto of someone whose bank account is crying but whose Pinterest board is thriving. They have a million-dollar mindset but only ₱50 in their GCash. It’s a slightly sarcastic but also hopeful way to describe someone who has big ambitions but is currently broke AF. "I'm not poor, I'm just pre-rich... sa panaginip."
usage_notes: Used to describe a person, often with a mix of pity, sarcasm, or encouragement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wala man akong pera ngayon, **sagana sa panaginip** naman ako.","translation":"I may not have money now, but I'm **rich in dreams**."},{"sentence":"Lagi siyang nagkukuwento tungkol sa kanyang mga plano, pero tila **sagana sa panaginip** lang.","translation":"He always talks about his plans, but it seems he's just **abundant in dreams** (and nothing else)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-ipit sa balat gamit ang dulo ng hinlalaki at hintuturo.
original_explanation: The official love language of Filipino titas when they see your chubby cheeks. It's a gesture that can mean 'I find you adorable!' or 'You're in big trouble, mister!' depending on the force and the look in their eyes. Also, the B-plot of every Filipino child's life story.
usage_notes: Can be a gesture of affection or a mild form of punishment. The verb form is 'kurotin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap ako ng masarap na **kurot** sa pisngi mula kay Lola.","translation":"I received a fond **pinch** on the cheek from Grandma."},{"sentence":"Isang matalim na **kurot** ang ganti niya sa panunukso ko.","translation":"A sharp **pinch** was her retaliation for my teasing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsasama o pagsilong ng dalawa o higit pang tao sa ilalim ng iisang proteksyon, tulad ng payong, laban sa ulan o araw.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino rom-com move. It's raining, you see your crush without an umbrella. You approach and ask, "Gusto mo **sukob**?" Instant movie scene. It’s sharing one umbrella and trying not to get your bag, your shoes, and your feelings wet.
usage_notes: The verb is "sumukob" (to take shelter with someone) or "makisukob" (to ask to share shelter).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-alok siya ng **sukob** sa ilalim ng kanyang payong noong biglang umulan.","translation":"He offered to **share his shelter** under his umbrella when it suddenly rained."},{"sentence":"Romantiko ang eksenang **sukob** sa mga pelikula.","translation":"The scene of **sharing an umbrella** is romantic in movies."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagiging pinakadulo o nasa katapusan ng isang pagkakasunod-sunod, serye, o panahon. Maaari rin itong mangahulugang nahuhuli sa takdang oras.
original_explanation: This is the status of your friend who's always "on the way" but is actually still in the shower. It's also the "last" piece of pizza everyone is too shy to get. Also, the "last" episode of your favorite K-drama that you're not ready to watch. "Pahabol" is its first cousin.
usage_notes: The meaning changes based on context (e.g., 'huling kabanata' - final chapter; 'huli sa klase' - late for class). The pronunciation /hu-LI/ distinguishes it from /HU-li/ (catch).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **huli** na dumating sa pagpupulong.","translation":"She was the **last** to arrive at the meeting."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang **huli** kong babala sa iyo.","translation":"This is my **final** warning to you."},{"sentence":"Lagi siyang **huli** sa klase.","translation":"He is always **late** for class."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumuha ng tubig mula sa isang balon o poso para sa ibang tao.
original_explanation: 'Paki-igiban mo nga ako ng tubig pangligo.' This is a request that echoes through provincial life. It's not just fetching water, it's performing an act of service for someone else. It's the younger sibling's duty, the suitor's way of showing 'sipag at tiyaga' to his beloved's parents.
usage_notes: A benefactive verb. 'Igiban mo ako' means 'Fetch water for me'. Contrast with 'umigib' (to fetch water for oneself).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iginiban** ni Cardo ng tubig ang kanyang lola.","translation":"Cardo **fetched water for** his grandmother."},{"sentence":"Maaari mo ba akong **igiban** ng isang baldeng tubig?","translation":"Could you **fetch** a bucket of water **for me**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang huling kainan sa isang araw, na karaniwang ginagawa sa gabi.
original_explanation: The main event after a long day. The meal you think about since 3 PM. It's where families (are supposed to) gather and talk about their day, or where you sit alone watching Netflix. The meal that comes from 'hapon' (afternoon), but eaten at night. 'Anong ulam sa hapunan?' is a question of national importance.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'maghapunan' (to eat dinner).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging sabay-sabay kumain ng **hapunan** ang aming pamilya.","translation":"Our family always eats **dinner** together."},{"sentence":"Inihanda na ni nanay ang masarap na **hapunan**.","translation":"Mom has prepared a delicious **dinner**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawin muli ang isang bagay; bumalik sa dating ginagawa o kalagayan.
original_explanation: Like when you thought you passed the exam, but the prof says "May final project pa pala," so you have to umuli sa pagpupuyat. It's the universe telling you, "Try again, bes."
usage_notes: Often interchangeable with 'umulit'. 'Umuli' can sometimes imply returning to a previous state or action, while 'umulit' is more general for repetition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **umuli** sa mga pagkakamaling nagawa mo na.","translation":"Don't **repeat** the mistakes you've already made."},{"sentence":"Kahit pagod na, **umuli** pa rin siya sa pag-akyat para tulungan ang kasama.","translation":"Even though he was tired, he still **went back** to climbing to help his companion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sulok o kanto kung saan nagtatagpo ang dalawa o higit pang kalye.
original_explanation: The OG tambayan. The iskina is where you wait for a jeep, meet up with friends, buy fishballs, and hear all the latest chismis. It's the social media feed of the barangay, IRL. 'Sa may kanto, sa may iskina.'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'kanto'. 'Iskina' sounds a bit more classic or traditional.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **iskina** malapit sa tindahan ni Aling Nena.","translation":"Let's meet at the **street corner** near Aling Nena's store."}]

meaning_filipino: Ikuwento o isawalat ang isang bagay, lalo na ang isang lihim, nang walang pag-iingat o pag-aatubili.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'keep secret.' When your friend tells you 'Huwag mong ipagkakalat,' and you immediately run to your other friend and spill all the tea. That's you, **idinadaldal** mo lahat. The 'i-' prefix makes the secret the object you're 'chattering' about. The official verb of every Marites.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo sanang **idaldal** ang sikreto ko kahit kanino.","translation":"Please don't **blab** my secret to anyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng dibdib ng manok na karaniwang walang buto at maraming laman.
original_explanation: The "healthy" part of the chicken, 'yung laging tinitira ng mga nagda-diet sa inasal. It's the opposite of the leg part (paa). When someone asks "Anong part ng manok gusto mo?" and you say "pitso," you're either on a fitness journey or you just really hate dealing with bones. The "white meat" of the Pinoy chicken world.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the breast part of a chicken, often in a culinary context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang **pitso** kaysa sa paa ng manok.","translation":"I prefer chicken **breast** over the leg part."},{"sentence":"Dalawang order ng chicken inasal, parehong **pitso** po.","translation":"Two orders of chicken inasal, both **breast** part please."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-atas o pagpapahintulot sa isang ina na magpasuso sa sanggol, o ang paglalagay ng sanggol sa dibdib upang sumuso.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative) + `suso` (breast; to suckle) + `-hin` (object-focus suffix), with reduplication of the root's first syllable.
original_explanation: This is a very direct, and often gentle, term. It's what a lola might say to a new mom: "Naku, iyak na nang iyak ang bata, *pasusuhin* mo na." (Oh, the baby is crying so much, let him/her breastfeed now.) It's all about nurturing and care, a fundamental part of motherhood.
usage_notes: The word `suso` can mean "breast" or "to suckle". `Pasusuhin` is the causative form, meaning "to cause to suckle".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pasusuhin** ang sanggol tuwing dalawa hanggang tatlong oras.","translation":"The baby needs **to be breastfed** every two to three hours."},{"sentence":"Inutusan ng doktor ang ina na **pasusuhin** ang kanyang anak.","translation":"The doctor instructed the mother **to breastfeed** her child."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tatak ng smartphone na sikat noong unang bahagi ng 2000s, na kilala sa pisikal na keyboard nito. Sa botanika, ito ay isang uri ng maliit at nakakaing prutas na kulay itim kapag hinog.
etymology: From English 'BlackBerry', a brand name. Phonetic spelling.
original_explanation: The phone that defined an era of BPO agents and 'business-minded' titos. Before the iPhone reigned supreme, having a Blakberi meant you were important. You could hear its iconic notification sound from a mile away. Today, it’s mostly a relic, a reminder of the good old days of BBM (BlackBerry Messenger) and endless 'group chats' before Viber and Messenger took over.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively refers to the old phone brand, not the fruit, in a Philippine context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naaalala mo pa ba noong **Blakberi** pa ang uso at lahat tayo ay may BBM PIN?","translation":"Do you still remember when the **BlackBerry** was the trend and we all had a BBM PIN?"},{"sentence":"Nasa baul ko pa yata yung luma kong **Blakberi**.","translation":"I think my old **BlackBerry** is still in my storage chest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang dalampasigan o baybay-dagat, karaniwang may buhanginan.
original_explanation: The fancier, more poetic cousin of 'beach'. This is what you see in old Filipino movies or read in poems. It's the place where the hero and heroine have their romantic walk at sunset. It's basically 'dalampasigan' but with a more classic, literary vibe.
usage_notes: A more literary or archaic term for 'beach' or 'coastline'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagandang pagmasdan ng paglubog ng araw sa **pasigan**.","translation":"It is beautiful to watch the sunset on the **shore**."},{"sentence":"Naglakad sila sa buhangin ng **pasigan**.","translation":"They walked on the sand of the **beach**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na paraan ng pagsasabi ng 'tara na' o pag-anyaya sa pagkilos.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na pariralang 'Let's go.'
original_explanation: The battle cry of your barkada when the plan is finally 'GO!' whether it's for a road trip, a milk tea run, or just logging into a game. It's 'Tara na!' but with more hype and less syllables. The official starting gun for any 'kaladkarin' moment.
usage_notes: Lubhang impormal. Ginagamit sa mga text message, social media, at kaswal na pag-uusap, lalo na sa mga kabataan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tapos na ang work, inom na! **Lezzgo**!","translation":"Work is done, let's drink! **Let's go**!"},{"sentence":"Game na? **Lezzgo**, G na!","translation":"Is the game on? **Let's go**, I'm game!"}]

meaning_filipino: Painitin o lutuin ang isang bagay tulad ng tinapay o kape hanggang sa ito ay bahagyang masunog o maging kulay kayumanggi at malutong.
original_explanation: The verb for making your pandesal crispy again for breakfast, or for when you stay under the sun too long at the beach and you get 'toasted.' It's that perfect state between 'golden brown' and 'sunog'.
usage_notes: Commonly used for bread, coffee beans, or even getting a tan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magtusta** ng tinapay para sa almusal.","translation":"I want **to toast** some bread for breakfast."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong magbilad sa araw at baka ka **matusta**.","translation":"Don't stay under the sun too long or you might get **toasted**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat o bilang na binubuo ng labindalawang (12) piraso.
original_explanation: Your go-to unit of measurement when buying eggs, donuts, or roses for your nanay. "Pabili po ng isang dusenang itlog." It's that magic number 12. If you want to sound a bit fancy, you say "isang dusena" instead of "labindalawa."
usage_notes: Very common in commerce, especially in markets (palengke).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang **dusena**ng mansanas sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a **dozen** apples at the market."},{"sentence":"Ang isang kahon ay naglalaman ng kalahating **dusena**ng bote ng softdrinks.","translation":"One box contains half a **dozen** bottles of softdrinks."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mekanismo na ginagamit upang isara at panatilihing ligtas ang pinto, bintana, o kahon, na karaniwang binubuksan gamit ang isang susi.
original_explanation: The original anti-marites device for your kwarto. Ito yung reason kung bakit hindi mo basta-basta mabubuksan yung pinto ng CR kapag occupied. Pag sira ang seradura mo, parang open relationship lang 'yan – kahit sino pwedeng pumasok.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa buong mekanismo ng kandado sa pinto, na madalas ay kasama na ang doorknob.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sira na ang **seradura** ng pinto kaya kailangan na itong palitan.","translation":"The door's **lock** is broken, so it needs to be replaced."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng pagkapahiya, pag-aalangan, o kawalan ng kumpiyansa dahil sa isang sitwasyon o kilos na itinuturing na hindi angkop.
original_explanation: That feeling when you wave at someone and they don't wave back because they weren't looking at you. Or when your mom shows your baby pictures to your new jowa. That cringe, face-hiding, 'lupa, kainin mo na ako' moment is pagkahiya.
usage_notes: Describes the internal feeling of shame or embarrassment, as opposed to `kahihiyan` which can also refer to the disgraceful event itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang kanyang **pagkahiya** matapos mahulog sa harap ng maraming tao.","translation":"She couldn't hide her **embarrassment** after falling in front of many people."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkahiya**, hindi na siya sumama sa mga pagtitipon.","translation":"Because of **shame**, he no longer joined gatherings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon ng pagpapalakas ng loob na nangangahulugang 'ipagpatuloy lamang ang pakikipaglaban' o 'huwag sumuko'.
original_explanation: The national motto of every Filipino student, BPO agent, and anyone trying to survive adulting. It's our version of "keep calm and carry on," but with more grit and less tea. Sinisigaw mo 'to sa sarili mo habang nag-rerender ng OT, nagrereview for finals, o nakikipagsiksikan sa MRT. A mantra for resilience.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang ekspresyon na pampalakas-loob.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit mahirap ang buhay, **laban lang**!","translation":"Even if life is hard, **just keep fighting**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Naka-ikid, baluktot, o hindi tuwid ang anyo dahil sa pagpihit o pagbaluktot.
original_explanation: That feeling in your gut when you see your ex with someone new. Or literally, that twisted-up doughnut-like bread glazed with sugar. It can also describe a complicated situation, a 'twisted' plot, or how your words sound when you're trying to explain to your mom why you came home at 3 AM. 'Huwag mong ipilipit ang kwento!'
usage_notes: Can also be a noun referring to a type of twisted, glazed bread. The verb form is `pilipitin` (to twist something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **pilipit** ang alambre matapos paglaruan ng bata.","translation":"The wire became **twisted** after the child played with it."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng mainit na **pilipit** sa panaderya.","translation":"I bought warm **twisted bread** from the bakery."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na paghigop ng hangin sa pamamagitan ng ilong, karaniwan dahil sa sipon, pag-iyak, o pag-amoy ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na iiyak ka na pero pinipigilan mo, kaya sound trip mo na lang 'yung ilong mo. O 'yung ka-opisina mong may allergic rhinitis tuwing umaga. Also, 'yung aso mong hinahanap kung saan mo tinago 'yung chichirya.
usage_notes: The repetition ("singhut-singhot") implies a continuous or repeated action, often involuntarily due to crying or a cold.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kanina pa **sumisinghut-singhot** ang bata dahil sa matinding sipon.","translation":"The child has been **sniffling** for a while because of a bad cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang instrumentong pangmusika na may apat na kuwerdas, mas malaki nang kaunti sa biyolin at may mas mababang tono.
original_explanation: It's that musical instrument that looks like a violin but is slightly bigger and has a deeper, more mellow voice. Sa isang orchestra, parang siya yung Tita na chill lang, hindi kasing 'bida-bida' ng violin pero essential sa harmony. It's the alto voice of the string family.
usage_notes: Not to be confused with "biyolin" (violin). The English spelling "viola" is also commonly used in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang mahusay na manunugtog ng **biola** sa isang sikat na orkestra.","translation":"She is a skilled **viola** player in a famous orchestra."},{"sentence":"Mas malalim ang tunog ng **biola** kaysa sa biyolin.","translation":"The sound of a **viola** is deeper than that of a violin."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mamimili na nagpapareserba o uma-order ng isang produkto ngunit walang intensyong bayaran o kunin ito.
etymology: From English "bogus" + "buyer". A modern term popularized by online selling.
original_explanation: The worst nightmare of every online seller. Sila 'yung mga pa-mine nang pa-mine sa live selling, tapos 'pag siningil mo na, seenzone ka na lang. They reserve items for the "joy" of it, leaving the seller with a canceled order and trust issues. #JoyReserver #Scammer
usage_notes: This is a very specific term used in the context of e-commerce and online selling in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"I-po-post ko sa social media itong **bogus buyer** para hindi na makapanloko ng iba.","translation":"I will post this **bogus buyer** on social media so they can't scam others anymore."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa dami ng **bogus buyer**, kailangan na ng downpayment bago i-ship ang item.","translation":"Because of the number of **bogus buyers**, a downpayment is now required before the item is shipped."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pasukan o daan papasok sa isang lugar. Sa konteksto ng pananalapi, ito ay ang paunang bayad o deposito para sa isang malaking pagbili.
original_explanation: Has two main gigs. First, it's the 'grand entrance,' the way you walk into a party like you own the place. It's the literal doorway or gate. Second, and more painfully, it's the 'down payment' for that condo or car you've been dreaming of. It's the first big hurdle to adulting. One entrada is fabulous, the other is financially stressful.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context, whether physical (entrance) or financial (down payment).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **entrada** ng bagong gusali.","translation":"The **entrance** of the new building is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Kailangan naming mag-ipon para sa **entrada** ng bahay.","translation":"We need to save up for the **down payment** on the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang prinsipyo o hanay ng mga prinsipyo na itinakda ng isang awtoridad bilang hindi mapag-aalinlanganang katotohanan, lalo na sa relihiyon o pilosopiya.
etymology: Mula sa Huling Latin "dogma" ("prinsipyong pilosopikal"), mula sa Griyegong "dogma" ("opinyon, prinsipyo").
original_explanation: Ito yung "kasi sabi nila" or "basta, 'yun na 'yun" version 2.0, with academic and religious flavor. The non-negotiables, the core beliefs of a group, the "Terms and Conditions" you accept without reading. Questioning it is like asking your lola why her adobo recipe is the best—you just don't.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng relihiyon, pilosopiya, o pulitika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **dogma** ng simbahan ay dapat sundin ng mga kasapi nito.","translation":"The **dogma** of the church must be followed by its members."},{"sentence":"Mahirap baguhin ang isang **dogma** na matagal nang pinaniniwalaan.","translation":"It is difficult to change a **dogma** that has long been believed."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng sama ng loob, pagdaramdam, o galit dahil sa isang nagawang kasalanan o hindi magandang karanasan.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when your friend eats the last piece of pizza you were saving. It’s that low-key, simmering sama ng loob. You're not screaming mad, but you're definitely keeping receipts. 'Parang may-hinanakit siya sa'yo, hindi ka niya pinapansin.'
usage_notes: Describes a person holding a grudge or feeling resentful. It's a step beyond 'tampo' (a light sulk) and implies a deeper, longer-held grievance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula nang hindi siya na-promote, palagi na siyang **may-hinanakit** sa kanyang amo.","translation":"Ever since he wasn't promoted, he has always been **resentful** towards his boss."},{"sentence":"Mahirap magtrabaho kasama ang taong laging **may-hinanakit**.","translation":"It's hard to work with someone who always **has a grudge**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampublikong sasakyan sa Pilipinas, na orihinal na gawa mula sa mga naiwang military jeep ng Amerika pagkatapos ng Ikalawang Digmaang Pandaigdig.
etymology: Mula sa pinagsamang salitang Ingles na 'jeep' at 'jitney'.
original_explanation: The one and only "King of the Road." It's a moving piece of Filipino art, a classroom on wheels where you learn to say "bayad po" while passing a stranger's fare, and a test of your ninja skills to get off at the right "para" spot. Riding a diyipni during rush hour is a core Philippine experience.
usage_notes: Ang mas karaniwang baybay ay 'jeepney' ngunit ang 'diyipni' ay ang bersyon na sumusunod sa palabaybayang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na ang **diyipni** kaya sasabit na lang ako sa likod.","translation":"The **jeepney** is full, so I'll just hang on the back."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gulay mula sa pamilya ng repolyo na may puti at siksik na kumpol ng mga bulaklak na siyang kinakain.
original_explanation: Yung albino version ng broccoli. Laging present sa Chopsuey, pero bihira maging bida. Ginagamit din ng mga nagda-diet bilang 'cauli-rice.' Healthy pero aminin mo, mas masarap pa rin ang kanin.
