usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa pagluluto at sa mga usapang pangkalusugan o pagda-diet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakidagdag naman ng **cauliflower** sa listahan ng bibilhin sa palengke.","translation":"Please add **cauliflower** to the market shopping list."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan kong gumawa ng 'cauli-rice' pero iba pa rin talaga ang kanin.","translation":"I tried making 'cauli-rice' but real rice is still different."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng pagkapagod, pamamanhid, o paninigas ng kalamnan dahil sa matagal na paggamit o pananatili sa isang posisyon.
original_explanation: The official feeling of call center agents after an 8-hour shift, students after writing a 10-page essay by hand, or anyone who's held their phone up for too long while lying in bed. It's that pins-and-needles-meets-muscle-soreness combo in your hand, arm, or neck.
usage_notes: A very common word describing a physical sensation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **pangangawit** ng aking kamay matapos ang maghapong pagsusulat.","translation":"I felt the **fatigue** in my hand after a whole day of writing."},{"sentence":"Upang maiwasan ang **pangangawit**, mag-unat-unat paminsan-minsan.","translation":"To avoid **muscle strain**, stretch every now and then."}]

translation: to pass by, to go through
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglakad, pagbiyahe, o paggalaw sa isang lugar upang makarating sa iba; ang pagdanas ng isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino verb for 'I was just in the neighborhood!' even if you're 2 hours away. It can mean literally passing by a place ('Dumaan ako sa Jollibee'), or going through something heavy ('Marami na siyang dinaanan na pagsubok'). It's the 'seen-zoned' message that just passed by, or the ex you wish would just pass by and never come back.
usage_notes: A very common verb with both literal (passing a location) and figurative (experiencing a trial) meanings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumaan** ka ba sa palengke kanina?","translation":"Did you **pass by** the market earlier?"},{"sentence":"Lahat tayo ay **dumadaan** sa mga pagsubok sa buhay.","translation":"All of us **go through** challenges in life."},{"sentence":"**Dumaan** lang ako para kumustahin ka.","translation":"I just **dropped by** to see how you are."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng makapal at matigas na papel o plastik, karaniwang parihaba, na ginagamit sa iba't ibang layunin tulad ng pagkakakilanlan, pagbabayad, o paglalaro.
original_explanation: Your life in a small rectangle. Could be your ATM card (ang dahilan kung bakit ka pa buhay sa a-kinse at a-trenta), your Beep card (ang best friend mo sa MRT), or your company ID (ang paalala na may trabaho ka pa bukas).
usage_notes: Isang modernong hiram na salita; ang tradisyonal na salita ay "tarheta".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan ko ang credit **kard** ko sa bahay.","translation":"I left my credit **card** at home."},{"sentence":"Pakita po ng inyong ID **kard** sa pagpasok.","translation":"Please show your ID **card** upon entry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong anunsyo o pahayag, kadalasan ay may layuning manghikayat o magbenta ng produkto, serbisyo, o ideya.
etymology: From `pa-` + `talastas` (to know, to be aware), meaning "to make known".
original_explanation: It's that 30-second song-and-dance on YouTube you can't skip, the giant billboard on EDSA causing traffic, or the "Last-Two-Minutes" Jollibee commercial that makes you cry. It's a public notice, whether you want to see it or not. From a simple "Bawal Umihi Dito" sign to a full-blown TV ad, it's all a `patalastas`.
usage_notes: Can refer to a wide range of public notices, from simple signs to complex multimedia campaigns.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita mo ba ang bagong **patalastas** ng sabon sa TV?","translation":"Did you see the new soap **commercial** on TV?"},{"sentence":"Naglabas ng **patalastas** ang gobyerno tungkol sa bagong batas.","translation":"The government issued an **announcement** about the new law."}]

translation: to run aground; to fall flat (on one's rear)
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang sumayad o tumigil sa pag-usad, tulad ng isang bangka sa mababaw na tubig; o biglaang mapaupo o bumagsak.
etymology: From 'ma-' (potential) + 'pa-' (causative) + 'sadsad' (to run aground; to slump down).
original_explanation: Two meanings! 1) For boats: when your romantic sunset cruise with bae ends with the bangka getting stuck in the sand because of low tide, it has **napasadsad**. Awkward. 2) For people: when you slip on a freshly mopped floor at SM and land flat on your butt, you've also **napasadsad**. The physical embodiment of 'bagsak.'
usage_notes: Can be used literally for vehicles (especially boats) running aground, or figuratively/literally for a person falling or slumping down heavily.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napasadsad** ang aming bangka sa dalampasigan dahil sa lakas ng alon.","translation":"Our boat **ran aground** on the shore because of the strong waves."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod, **napasadsad** siya ng upo sa sahig.","translation":"From extreme exhaustion, she **fell flat** sitting on the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakakaranas ng hindi pagkatunaw ng pagkain sa tiyan, na nagdudulot ng pananakit, paglaki, o kabag.
original_explanation: The feeling you get after an 'unli-rice' promo or after Christmas Noche Buena. You feel so full that you can't move, and you swear you'll never eat again... until the next meal. Your stomach feels like a basketball. 'Na-impatsado ako sa lechon!' is a national sentiment.
usage_notes: Describes the physical discomfort of indigestion. "Na-impacho" is also a common variation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang kumain nang sobra para hindi ka maging **impatsado**.","translation":"Don't eat too much so you won't get **indigestion**."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **impatsado** ako dahil sa dami ng kinain kong kanin.","translation":"I feel **bloated** because of the amount of rice I ate."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bantas (,) na ginagamit upang magpahiwatig ng isang maikling paghinto sa isang pangungusap o upang paghiwalayin ang mga aytem sa isang serye.
etymology: Pinaghihinalaang mula sa isang salitang Austronesian, ngunit ang tiyak na pinagmulan ay hindi malinaw.
original_explanation: The punctuation mark that tells you to take a breath. In a sentence, it's a pause. In a relationship, it's the "it's complicated" status. Hindi pa tuldok, pero hindi rin tuloy-tuloy. It's the reason why "Let's eat, grandma" is very different from "Let's eat grandma."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng **kuwit** upang paghiwalayin ang mga pang-uri sa iyong listahan.","translation":"Use a **comma** to separate the adjectives in your list."},{"sentence":"Ang isang **kuwit** ay nagpapahiwatig ng maikling pagtigil sa pagbasa.","translation":"A **comma** indicates a short pause in reading."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pampalambing na hango sa Ingles na "baby," na ginagamit bilang tawagan para sa kasintahan, asawa, o sinumang malapit sa puso.
etymology: From English 'baby', with a Filipino pronunciation and spelling affectation.
original_explanation: The cutesy, pabebe way of saying 'baby'. It's the term of endearment you use when you're trying to be extra sweet, maybe because you want something (like the last piece of chicken) or you did something wrong. "Sorry na, bebe ko." It's one step away from 'bebelabs'. Famous because of the AlDub phenomenon's "pabebe wave".
usage_notes: Popularized by the AlDub tandem in the mid-2010s. Can sound overly cute or childish to some.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumain ka na ba, **bebe** ko?","translation":"Have you eaten, my **bebe** (baby)?"},{"sentence":"Ang tawagan ng magkasintahan ay '**bebe**'.","translation":"The couple's term of endearment is '**bebe**'."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong kumikilos nang walang pagsasaalang-alang sa moralidad o sa kung ano ang tama at mali; hindi nakakaramdam ng pagkakasala.
etymology: Mula sa "walang" (without) at "konsiyensiya" (conscience), na hiram sa Espanyol na "conciencia".
original_explanation: 'Yung nang-utang sa'yo tapos siya pa 'yung galit 'pag sinisingil mo. O 'yung sumisingit sa mahabang pila sa MRT na parang walang nakikita. Sila 'yung mga taong **walang-konsiyensiya**. Their moral compass is not just broken; it was probably never included in the package.
usage_notes: A strong insult or criticism of someone's character and lack of morals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Walang-konsiyensiya** ang taong nagnakaw ng tulong para sa mga biktima ng kalamidad.","translation":"The person who stole aid for the calamity victims is **unscrupulous**."},{"sentence":"Paano mo nagawa iyon? Talaga bang **walang-konsiyensiya** ka?","translation":"How could you do that? Are you really **without a conscience**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng pagbubuo, pagbubukas, o pagsisimula ng isang organisasyon, institusyon, o samahan.
original_explanation: This is the 'grand opening' moment for anything major. Think of it as the ribbon-cutting ceremony for a new company, the first meeting of a new club, or the day a republic declares its independence. It’s the official 'We exist now!' announcement.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, historical, or business contexts. 'Pagtatatag' is the noun form of the act, while 'itinatag' is the past tense verb 'was founded'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtatatag** ng Republika ng Malolos ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng ating kasaysayan.","translation":"The **establishment** of the Malolos Republic is an important part of our history."},{"sentence":"Pinangunahan niya ang **pagtatatag** ng isang bagong charity foundation.","translation":"He led the **founding** of a new charity foundation."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng mga anggulo o sulok; matulis o hindi bilugan ang hugis.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "angular" o Ingles na "angular".
original_explanation: This is a direct loanword from English. It’s what you call a jawline that can cut glass. It describes something with sharp corners and defined lines, not soft and curvy. Think of a Minecraft block, not a Jollibee mascot.
usage_notes: Isang hiram na salita na ginagamit sa mga kontekstong teknikal, artistiko, o deskriptibo. Mas karaniwan ang paggamit ng "anggulo" (angle).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng arkitekto ang isang disenyong **anggular** para sa gusali.","translation":"The architect used an **angular** design for the building."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **anggular** na mukha na bagay sa kanya.","translation":"He has an **angular** face that suits him."}]

meaning_filipino: Materyales na ginagamit sa pagbabalot ng isang bagay, o ang bagay na mismo na nakatakdang ibalot.
original_explanation: Could be two things: 1) The gift wrapper you buy in National Bookstore. 2) The leftover food from a fiesta that you ask to be wrapped for takeout. "Ate, pa-take out po. Isang pabalot ng lechon, please." It's the national sport of party-goers.
usage_notes: Can refer to the material for wrapping or the item requested to be wrapped.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng magandang **pabalot** para sa regalo mo kay nanay.","translation":"Buy a nice **wrapper** for your gift to mom."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi siya ng maraming **pabalot** mula sa handaan.","translation":"He brought home a lot of **take-home food (to be wrapped)** from the feast."}]

translation: to pull out; to draw from
meaning_filipino: Kumuha o bunutin ang isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito. Sa makabagong gamit, tumutukoy sa pagkuha ng emosyon o aral mula sa isang karanasan.
original_explanation: The OG meaning is to pull something out, like your wallet (ouch). But in modern Filipino culture, *humugot* means to draw deep, angsty, or profound emotion from personal experience, usually about love or life struggles. It's the national sport of turning pain into a relatable quote. 'Sana all may jowa' is a product of someone who *humugot*.
usage_notes: Has a literal meaning (to pull) and a very popular figurative, modern meaning (to draw emotion).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humugot** siya ng pera mula sa kanyang pitaka.","translation":"He/She **pulled out** money from his/her wallet."},{"sentence":"\"Bakit ka **humuhugot** diyan? Iniwan ka na naman ba?\"","translation":"\"Why are you **getting all emotional** there? Did someone leave you again?\""}]

meaning_filipino: Isa pang baryasyon ng "siz," na isang impormal na pantawag sa isang babae, na nagmula sa salitang Ingles na "sister."
etymology: Baryasyon ng "siz," na pinaikling anyo ng salitang Ingles na "sister." Ang pagdaragdag ng 't' ay karaniwan sa gay lingo para sa istilo.
original_explanation: It's "siz" but with a little extra ✨spice✨. The '-t' at the end adds a certain flair, a little bit of sass. It's the version you use when you're feeling extra chummy or when you're about to spill some major tea. "Sizt, may chika ako!" hits different than just "Siz, may chika ako."
usage_notes: Mas karaniwan sa online chats at sa mga komunidad na pamilyar sa gay lingo. Medyo mas niche kaysa sa "siz".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy **sizt**, nakita mo ba yung bagong post niya?","translation":"Hey **sis**, did you see their new post?"},{"sentence":"Pak, ang ganda ng outfit mo, **sizt**!","translation":"Wow, your outfit is amazing, **sis**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na makinis, banayad, at walang gaspang o sagabal.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'magaspang' or 'sabit'. 'Yung takbo ng kotse na parang nasa ulap ka. 'Yung pick-up line na hindi cringe. 'Yung transaction sa government office na natapos in 5 minutes. Smooth, 'di ba? That's suwabe.
usage_notes: Can be used to describe texture, movement, a person's personality, or a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng takbo ng bagong kotse, napaka-**suwabe** sa kalsada.","translation":"The new car runs beautifully, it's very **smooth** on the road."},{"sentence":"**Suwabe** ang naging diskarte niya kaya napasagot niya agad ang nililigawan.","translation":"His approach was **smooth**, that's why the person he was courting said yes to him right away."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng pagkakaroon ng interes, kasiyahan, o libangan sa isang bagay o gawain.
original_explanation: Your 'kawilihan' is your passion project, your side hustle, your 'me time' activity. It's what you do when you're not adulting. Whether it's K-Pop, gaming, gardening, or watching mukbang videos, 'yan ang kawilihan mo. The thing that sparks joy, as Marie Kondo would say.
usage_notes: Often used to describe hobbies or things one takes pleasure in.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagbabasa ng libro ang kaniyang pangunahing **kawilihan**.","translation":"Reading books is her main **hobby**."},{"sentence":"Walang sinuman ang makakapantay sa **kawilihan** niya sa pag-aalaga ng halaman.","translation":"No one can match her **interest** in taking care of plants."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsagawa ng pansamantalang pagtigil sa pagtatrabaho bilang isang grupo upang iprotesta ang mababang sahod, hindi magandang kondisyon sa trabaho, o ipaglaban ang isang karapatan.
original_explanation: When the entire team decides to collectively 'log off' not because it's 6 PM, but because the management is trash. To **magwelga** is the ultimate group project against unfair labor practices. It involves placards, chanting, and a shared frustration that's stronger than the office Wi-Fi. It's the corporate version of 'tampo', but with legal and economic consequences.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with labor unions, activism, and protests.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang mga manggagawa na **magwelga** upang hilingin ang umento sa sahod.","translation":"The workers decided to **go on strike** to demand a wage increase."},{"sentence":"Binalaan ng unyon ang kumpanya na sila ay **magwewelga** kung hindi tutuparin ang kanilang mga kasunduan.","translation":"The union warned the company that they **will go on strike** if their agreements are not fulfilled."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o kumpanya na nagbebenta ng mga produkto nang direkta sa mga mamimili, karaniwan sa maliit na dami.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga nagbebenta nang tingi-tingi. From the big malls like SM and Robinsons to your suking tindahan sa kanto that sells you shampoo by the sachet. Even the online seller you bought your skincare from on Shopee is a retailer. Sila ang final stop bago makarating sa'yo ang isang produkto.
usage_notes: Commonly used in business and commerce contexts in the Philippines. The concept is also known as 'nagbebenta nang tingi' or 'tindera/tindero'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **retailer** ng mga damit ang magbubukas sa aming lugar.","translation":"A large clothing **retailer** will open in our area."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng bigas mula sa isang local na **retailer**.","translation":"I bought rice from a local **retailer**."}]

meaning_filipino: Utusan o himukin ang isang tao o grupo na magbigay ng ambag o kontribusyon para sa isang layunin.
original_explanation: This is what your team leader does when there's an office potluck. "Okay guys, papag-ambagin ko kayo ng tig-100 pesos for the birthday celebrant." It's the act of making everyone chip in, whether it's for food, a gift, or a group project.
usage_notes: A causative verb. The prefix 'papag-' indicates causing or making someone do the action of the root word, in this case 'ambag' (to contribute).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ang **papag-ambagin** natin para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"We will be the ones to **make them contribute** for the typhoon victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na kasunduan ng mga naglalabanang panig upang pansamantalang itigil ang labanan o digmaan.
original_explanation: Ito yung moment na nag-away kayo ng jowa mo, tapos pareho na kayong pagod at gutom, kaya sabi niyo, "Okay, ceasefire muna. Kain muna tayo." 'Yan ang armistisyo. Pansamantalang kapayapaan para makahinga at mag-recharge bago mag-away ulit (o magbati na).
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng digmaan, malalaking alitan, o sa biro para sa personal na hindi pagkakasundo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nilagdaan ang **armistisyo** noong ika-11 ng Nobyembre, na nagpatigil sa Unang Digmaang Pandaigdig.","translation":"The **armistice** was signed on the 11th of November, which stopped the First World War."},{"sentence":"Kailangan na natin ng **armistisyo** sa walang katapusang away na ito sa group chat.","translation":"We need a **truce** in this never-ending fight in the group chat."}]

translation: act of exposing a secret; revelation
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalantad o pagsisiwalat ng isang lihim, kasinungalingan, o isang bagay na itinatago.
etymology: From `pang-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `buko` (`bu-`) + `buko`. `Buko` itself means 'exposed' or 'discovered'.
original_explanation: This is the 'tea-spilling' moment. It's when Marites finally reveals the chismis she's been holding onto, exposing someone's secret plan or hidden relationship. The ultimate 'Aha! Huli ka!' moment, often powered by screenshots and receipts.
usage_notes: `Pambubuko` is the act of doing the exposing. The tool for exposing is `pambuko`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pambubuko** sa korapsyon ay nagdulot ng malaking iskandalo.","translation":"His **act of exposing** the corruption caused a huge scandal."},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng banta dahil sa kanyang **pambubuko** sa sindikato.","translation":"She received a threat because of her **revelation** about the syndicate."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na salita na katulad ng "charot" o "charing," ginagamit upang ipahiwatig na ang naunang sinabi ay hindi totoo o isang biro lamang.
etymology: A modern, often text-based, variant of 'charot.'
original_explanation: The ✨aesthetic✨ version of "charot." It's what you say when you're kidding, but you want to do it with a little more class and sass. It's the Gen Z, minimalist, clean-girl version of a classic Filipino expression.
usage_notes: Often seen in online chats and social media posts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"I woke up like this. **Chariz**.","translation":"I woke up like this. **Just kidding**."},{"sentence":"Diet na ako bukas, promise. **Chariz**!","translation":"I'm going on a diet tomorrow, I promise. **Joke**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lalaking nakararanas ng matinding kawalan ng pag-asa o nangangailangan nang lubos.
original_explanation: The male counterpart of 'desesperada'. Ito 'yung tropa mong nag-PM sa lahat ng kakilala para mangutang pang-date. O 'yung nag-aabang sa 7-Eleven ng hatinggabi baka sakaling may mag-aya ng libreng siopao. The 'sige na, please' energy is strong with this one.
usage_notes: Eksklusibong ginagamit para sa lalaki. Ang katumbas nito para sa babae ay 'desesperada'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **desesperado** si Mario nang malaman niyang malapit nang maputulan ng kuryente.","translation":"Mario became **desperate** when he learned his electricity was about to be cut off."}]

translation: to be transferred; to be moved
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang mailipat o maisalin mula sa isang lugar, posisyon, o kalagayan patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na bigla kang nilipat ng team sa office nang walang pasabi. Or when your jowa suddenly moves their feelings from you to someone else. "Bes, na-malipat na yata yung pwesto mo sa puso niya." It's the ultimate "you've been reassigned" moment, for things, files, or feelings.
usage_notes: The "ma-" prefix often indicates potential or ability. "Malipat" means something can be moved or was moved, depending on the context and verb focus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **malipat** ang mga gamit bago dumating ang bagyo.","translation":"The things need **to be moved** before the storm arrives."},{"sentence":"Sana **malipat** na ako sa day shift para hindi na ako laging puyat.","translation":"I hope I **get transferred** to the day shift so I won't always be sleep-deprived."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang magdulot ng malaking pinsala, sira, o kapahamakan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ugali ng ex mong dumaan lang sa buhay mo para sirain ang peace of mind mo. Parang bagyo na 'di mo inasahan, biglang nanira at umalis. Pwede ring 'yung chismis na kumalat sa office na **mapaminsala** sa career mo.
usage_notes: Often used to describe natural disasters, pests, or actions with severe negative consequences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagyong dumaan ay **mapaminsala** sa mga pananim.","translation":"The typhoon that passed was **destructive** to the crops."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang mga **mapaminsalang** bisyo tulad ng paninigarilyo.","translation":"Avoid **harmful** vices like smoking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag ng pagtanaw ng utang na loob, pagkilala, o pasasalamat para sa isang kabutihan, pabor, o tulong na natanggap.
etymology: From Malay 'selamat', ultimately from Arabic 'salāma' (safety, peace).
original_explanation: It's what you do when someone gives you the last piece of Chickenjoy, when your Grab driver finds a shortcut to beat the traffic, or when your salary finally comes in. It's the action of saying 'Salamat!' and genuinely meaning it. The core of *utang na loob*.
usage_notes: A fundamental verb in Filipino culture, reflecting the importance of gratitude and 'utang na loob' (debt of gratitude).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magpasalamat** sa lahat ng tumulong sa akin.","translation":"I want to **thank** everyone who helped me."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **magpasalamat** sa biyayang natatanggap araw-araw.","translation":"Don't forget to **be grateful** for the blessings received every day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking mamamayan ng Estados Unidos ng Amerika. Ang pambabae ay 'Americana'.
original_explanation: Colloquially, "Kano" for short. The dude your Pinay tita married and now she's living her best life in California. Also, a type of coffee that's basically espresso with hot water, for when you need that caffeine kick but can't handle the pure strength, just like how we sometimes need to 'water down' our feelings.
usage_notes: The female form is 'Americana'. The shortened, more common slang is 'Kano' (for male) and 'Kana' (for female). The standard Filipino spelling is 'Amerikano'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming turistang **Americano** ang bumibisita sa Palawan.","translation":"Many male **American** tourists visit Palawan."}]

translation: to take care of; to attend to
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng atensyon, alagaan, o tapusin ang isang gawain, bagay, o pangangailangan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'adulting' verb. It's what you do with your bills, your clients at work, the mountain of laundry, or your jowa who's having a bad day. 'Ako na bahala' mode activated. It's the opposite of 'seen-zoned'.
usage_notes: Often implies handling something completely or managing a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **asikasuhin** mo muna ang mga bisita habang nagluluto ako.","translation":"Please, **attend to** the guests first while I'm cooking."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **asikasuhin** ang mga papeles para sa aking passport.","translation":"I need to **take care of** the paperwork for my passport."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking uri ng lambat na nakakabit sa mga kawayan at ibinababa sa tubig upang makahuli ng isda, na pinapatakbo sa pamamagitan ng isang pingga.
original_explanation: Imagine a giant, spider-like contraption made of bamboo hovering over a river. That's the salambaw. It's like a big mechanical scoop for fish, operated by a lever. It's old-school Filipino engineering, no high-tech fish finders needed, just pure physics and good timing.
usage_notes: Often seen in rivers and coastal areas, it is a traditional fishing method that uses a large, mounted net on a raft.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malalaking isda ang nahuli ng **salambaw** kaninang umaga.","translation":"The **large fishing net** caught big fish this morning."}]

translation: Gnashing of teeth; intense suppressed anger or passion
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pagkagat ng mga ngipin dahil sa matinding galit, pagkasuklam, o pagnanasa.
etymology: From 'pang-' (used for forming nouns) + 'gigil' (intense, suppressed emotion).
original_explanation: This is that feeling when your internet dies in the middle of a crucial online game, or when you see your crush with someone else. You're not screaming, but your jaw is working overtime. It's the physical manifestation of "gigil," that untranslatable urge to squeeze something cute or to punch a wall.
usage_notes: Often associated with anger, but can also be used for intense affection or frustration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ramdam mo ang **panggigitil** sa kanyang mga kamao habang nagsasalita ang kaaway.","translation":"You could feel the **intense anger** in his fists as his enemy spoke."},{"sentence":"Sa **panggigitil** niya sa aso, halos hindi na ito makahinga.","translation":"From his **intense (but affectionate) squeezing** of the dog, it could barely breathe."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsasalita nang labis o walang tigil sa hinaharap; mag-iingay sa pamamagitan ng pagsasalita.
etymology: From "daldal" (chatter), with reduplication of the first syllable ("da-") to indicate future tense.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of being a "Marites." It's the promise of future chismis. When your friend says, "OMG, wait 'til I see you," you know they 'dadaldalan' about all the tea they've gathered. It's the verbal equivalent of a machine gun firing.
usage_notes: Future tense of the verb "dumaldal" or "magdaldal."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag nagkita-kita ang magkakaibigan, siguradong **dadaldalan** sila hanggang umaga.","translation":"When the friends meet, they will surely **chatter** until morning."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, baka **dadaldalan** mo lang ang lahat ng sikreto natin.","translation":"Don't be noisy, you might **blab** all our secrets."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-umpisa o pagganap sa isang gawain o kilos. Sa anyong pautos, ito ay nangangahulugang "umpisahan mo na."
original_explanation: This is the 'Game na!' or 'Let's go!' command. When your friend is taking forever to tell a story, you say 'Simula na!' (Start already!). It's the verbal green light, the starting gun. It's less formal than 'magsimula' and more direct.
usage_notes: The pronunciation shifts to /SI-mu-la/ when used as an imperative command, stressing the first syllable. The noun form is /si-mu-LA/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Simula** na ang palabas!","translation":"The show is **starting** now!"},{"sentence":"Sige na, ikuwento mo na. **Simula**!","translation":"Go on, tell your story. **Start**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panig sa isang kaso na nagsasampa ng reklamo o paratang laban sa isang tao o entidad sa korte.
original_explanation: In the telenovela of the courtroom, this is the character who points their finger and dramatically says, "Siya ang pumatay!" They are the one who starts the legal drama, the person who files the case because they feel they've been wronged. Sila yung nag-demanda.
usage_notes: A legal term for the party who initiates a lawsuit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tagasakdal** ay nagprisinta ng matibay na ebidensya laban sa akusado.","translation":"The **plaintiff** presented strong evidence against the accused."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **tagasakdal** sa kasong isinampa laban sa kumpanya?","translation":"Who is the **complainant** in the case filed against the company?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghahanda at pagdadala ng sandata para sa layuning protektahan ang sarili o umatake.
original_explanation: What you do when you're about to enter a 'bardagulan' on social media—you arm yourself with screenshots and receipts. Literally, it's what soldiers or rebels do. Figuratively, it's arming yourself with knowledge before an exam or with strong arguments before a debate.
usage_notes: Can be used in a literal military context or figuratively to mean preparing oneself with tools, information, or arguments for a confrontation or challenge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang mga mandirigma na **magsandata** para sa nalalapit na laban.","translation":"The warriors decided to **arm themselves** for the upcoming battle."},{"sentence":"Bago pumasok sa debate, kailangan mong **magsandata** ng sapat na datos at ebidensya.","translation":"Before entering the debate, you need to **arm yourself** with sufficient data and evidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi makatarungang pagtrato sa iba't ibang kategorya ng mga tao, lalo na batay sa lahi, edad, o kasarian.
original_explanation: When the building guard follows you around because of how you're dressed. Or when a job posting says 'For female applicants only, with pleasing personality.' It's the unfair 'pili' system of life that the SOGIE Bill fights against.
usage_notes: A serious term used in social, legal, and political discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **diskriminasyon** batay sa kasarian ay labag sa batas.","translation":"**Discrimination** based on gender is against the law."},{"sentence":"Dumanas siya ng **diskriminasyon** sa trabaho dahil sa kanyang edad.","translation":"She experienced age **discrimination** at work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng kuko o anumang matulis na bagay upang maibsan ang kati sa balat.
original_explanation: That feeling when a mosquito bites you and you just have to... **kamot**! It's the act of scratching an itch. Sometimes, sobrang sarap magkamot, but then you get a 'sugat' (wound). Also used figuratively when you're 'nagkakamot ng ulo' (scratching your head) because you're confused or have no money.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'kamutin' (to scratch something) or 'magkamot' (to scratch oneself).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mapigilan ng bata ang **kamot** sa kagat ng lamok.","translation":"The child couldn't stop the **scratching** on the mosquito bite."},{"sentence":"Tigil na sa kakakamot, baka magsugat 'yan.","translation":"Stop scratching, it might become a wound."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalantad o pagpapakita ng isang bagay na dating nakatago, nakasikreto, o hindi alam ng publiko.
original_explanation: This is what happens in a "Tulfo" episode. It's the grand reveal, the unmasking, the spilling of the tea. It can be about exposing a scam, revealing a secret relationship, or just presenting your project to the board. It's taking something from the shadows and putting it under the spotlight.
usage_notes: Often carries a connotation of exposing something negative or secret, but can also be neutral (e.g., exposing film to light).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghantad** sa katotohanan ang nagpabagsak sa korap na opisyal.","translation":"The **exposure** of the truth is what brought down the corrupt official."},{"sentence":"Ang sobrang **paghantad** sa araw ay masama sa balat.","translation":"Too much **exposure** to the sun is bad for the skin."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hayop na may malamig na dugo, tulad ng palaka o salamander, na may kakayahang mabuhay kapwa sa lupa at sa tubig.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Ingles na 'amphibian', na nagmula sa Griyegong 'amphibios' (living a double life).
original_explanation: Basically, a frog or a toad. That creature that can chill in the water and on land, living its best two lives. It's the animal kingdom's version of someone who can code-switch perfectly between English and Tagalog.
usage_notes: Pang-akademiko o pang-agham ang paggamit nito. Sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, mas ginagamit ang pangalan ng mismong hayop (e.g., 'palaka').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang palaka ay isang halimbawa ng **ampibyan**.","translation":"The frog is an example of an **amphibian**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa klase ng Biology ang siklo ng buhay ng mga **ampibyan**.","translation":"The life cycle of **amphibians** is being studied in Biology class."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paratang o akusasyon, lalo na kung walang sapat na katibayan; paninisi sa isang tao para sa isang pagkakamali o krimen.
original_explanation: When someone points a finger at you and says "Ikaw 'yan 'no!" even if you're innocent. That's a bintang. It's the reason for family dramas ("Sino'ng umubos ng ulam?!") and workplace conflicts ("The report is late because of you!"). A false accusation is 'bulaang bintang'.
usage_notes: Often used with verbs like "pagbintangan" (to accuse someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **bintang** ang ipinataw sa kanya na walang matibay na ebidensya.","translation":"A huge **accusation** was laid against him without solid evidence."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko matanggap ang **bintang** mo na ako ang kumuha ng pera.","translation":"I cannot accept your **blame** that I was the one who took the money."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng panghalip na ginagamit sa pagtuturo o pagtukoy sa lokasyon ng isang pangngalan na malapit o malayo sa nagsasalita, sa kinakausap, o sa pinag-uusapan.
etymology: From `panghalip` (pronoun) + `na` (linker) + `pamatlig` (demonstrative, from `pa-` + an old root `patlig` meaning 'to point').
original_explanation: The 'turo-turo' (point-point) pronouns. A **panghalip na pamatlig** is what you use when you're too lazy to say the actual name of the thing. 'Pakikuha mo nga *'yan*.' (Can you get *that*?). *Ito* (this), *iyan* (that, near you), *iyon* (that, over there). It's the grammar of pointing, perfect for the palengke or when telling chismis: '*'Yun* oh, *'yun* ang ex niya!' (*That one* over there, *that's* her ex!).
usage_notes: This is a specific type of pronoun. The three main demonstrative pronouns are `ito/dito/nito`, `iyan/diyan/niyan`, and `iyon/doon/niyon`, which indicate proximity to the speaker, the listener, or someone/something distant from both.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'ito', 'iyan', at 'iyon' ay mga **panghalip na pamatlig**.","translation":"'This', 'that', and 'that (over there)' are **demonstrative pronouns**."},{"sentence":"Ginagamit natin ang **panghalip na pamatlig** upang ituro ang isang bagay.","translation":"We use **demonstrative pronouns** to point at an object."}]

translation: to use as a reason; to make an excuse
meaning_filipino: Gawing sanhi, katwiran, o paliwanag sa isang pangyayari o kilos.
original_explanation: When you're late for your 9 AM shift and you blame the traffic, the rain, and Mercury in retrograde. Whatever you point to as the culprit for your tardiness, that's what you **idahilan**. It's the art of finding a scapegoat for your own actions, a certified Pinoy survival skill.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **idahilan** ang pagod mo para iwasan ang iyong mga responsibilidad.","translation":"Don't **use** your fatigue **as an excuse** to avoid your responsibilities."},{"sentence":"Ano na naman ang **ididahilan** mo sa iyong pagiging huli sa klase?","translation":"What will you **use as a reason** this time for being late to class?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng Misa kung saan ang mga panalangin ay binibigkas lamang ng pari at hindi inaawit. Ito ang mas simple at karaniwang anyo ng Misa.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'misa rezada' ('dinasal/binigkas na misa').
original_explanation: This is the standard, no-frills, "recited" Mass. Unlike the Misa Kantada, there's no singing from the priest. It's quicker, more straightforward, and is the type of Mass you'd typically attend on a weekday or for the early morning/late evening services. The "express" version.
usage_notes: Ito ang kabaligtaran ng Misa Kantada. Bagaman karaniwan ang gawain, ang mismong termino ay hindi gaanong ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mabilis matapos ang **Misa Resada** kaysa sa Misa Kantada.","translation":"The **Recited Mass** finishes faster than the Sung Mass."},{"sentence":"Dahil may pasok pa ako, sa **Misa Resada** ako ng 6 AM dumalo.","translation":"Because I still have work, I attended the 6 AM **Recited Mass**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit bilang pang-abay na tumutukoy sa isang bagay, lugar, o paraan na malayo sa nagsasalita at sa kausap.
original_explanation: The OG 'like that.' This is the word for describing something far from both you and the person you're talking to. 'See that mountain over there? Ganoon kataas 'yung pangarap ko.' It's the parent of the slang 'ganern' and 'ganoin.' It's also used to mean 'in that manner' when referring to something previously mentioned. 'So you broke up? Bakit ganoon?' (Why did it happen like that?).
usage_notes: Part of the three-level system of Tagalog demonstratives: 'ganito' (like this, near me), 'ganyan' (like that, near you), 'ganoon' (like that, far from both of us).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"A, **ganoon** pala ang dapat gawin. Salamat!","translation":"Oh, so it's supposed to be done **like that**. Thanks!"},{"sentence":"Ang bahay nila ay nasa dulo ng kalye, **ganoon** kalayo.","translation":"Their house is at the end of the street, it's **that** far."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na kumakatawan sa isang bansa sa pakikipag-ugnayan sa ibang mga bansa.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Ingles na "diplomat" o Espanyol na "diplomático".
original_explanation: The person in your friend group who can stop a fight between two of your friends who just broke up. They're masters of "damage control" and choosing the right words. They can tell you your idea is terrible without making you cry. In real life, they're the people with cool passports who go to fancy parties for a living, representing the Philippines.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay katulad na katulad ng katumbas nito sa Ingles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang mahusay na **diplomat** ay kailangang maging magaling sa pakikipag-usap.","translation":"A good **diplomat** needs to be skilled in communication."},{"sentence":"Ipinadala ang mga **diplomat** upang ayusin ang tensyon sa pagitan ng dalawang bansa.","translation":"The **diplomats** were sent to resolve the tension between the two countries."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pamahalaan kung saan ang kapangyarihang pampulitika ay hawak ng militar.
etymology: From "hukbo" (army) and "pamahalaan" (government). The "-ing" linker connects them.
original_explanation: Think of it as a government run by generals instead of politicians. It's what happens when the Armed Forces decides they're tired of the usual 'trapo' drama and take over. Less elections, more marching orders.
usage_notes: This is a formal term used in political science and history. It's often associated with martial law or a coup d'état.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinatupad ang isang **hukbuhing pamahalaan** matapos ang bigong kudeta.","translation":"A **military government** was established after the failed coup d'état."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng kulay tungo sa itim o mas madilim na tono.
original_explanation: What happens to your skin after a 3-day beach trip to Boracay without sunblock. Also what happens to a banana when you forget about it for a week. "Hala, umitim na yung saging!"
usage_notes: Can refer to skin tanning, food spoiling (like bananas), or objects changing color.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magpahid ka ng sunblock para hindi ka **umitim**.","translation":"Apply sunblock so you don't **darken** (get a tan)."},{"sentence":"**Umitim** ang siko niya dahil sa laging pagpapatong sa mesa.","translation":"His elbow **darkened** because he always rests it on the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matamis na pagkaing hinurno na gawa sa harina, asukal, itlog, at iba pang sangkap.
original_explanation: The star of every Filipino birthday party, second only to the birthday person. Whether it's from Red Ribbon, Goldilocks, or a fancy bakeshop, a celebration isn't complete without a **cake**. Also, a slang term for something easy, as in 'piece of cake'.
usage_notes: Malawakang ginagamit sa Filipino. Ang salitang hango sa Espanyol na "pastel" ay mas bihirang gamitin at karaniwang tumutukoy sa ibang uri ng pastry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang bumili ng **cake** para sa kaarawan ni nanay.","translation":"Don't forget to buy a **cake** for mom's birthday."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng chocolate **cake** na dala mo!","translation":"The chocolate **cake** you brought is delicious!"}]

translation: retaliation; revenge; something used for reciprocation
meaning_filipino: Isang kilos, bagay, o paraan na isinasagawa bilang tugon o katumbas sa isang naunang ginawa, ito man ay mabuti (gantimpala) o masama (paghihiganti).
original_explanation: This is the 'resbak' culture. Yung sineen-zone ka niya, kaya sineen-zone mo rin siya. Yung binigyan ka ng kapitbahay mo ng ulam, kaya bibigyan mo rin sila ng ulam (pero sa ibang lalagyan para di halatang binalik lang). It's the law of reciprocity, Philippine-style. Can be petty revenge or a thoughtful return of favor.
usage_notes: The context determines if it's for revenge or for returning a good deed. Often implies a negative connotation (retaliation) unless specified.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang ginawa ay isang **pangganti** sa mga nanakit sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"What he did was an act of **retaliation** against those who hurt his family."},{"sentence":"Naghanda ako ng meryenda bilang **pangganti** sa tulong mo kahapon.","translation":"I prepared snacks as a **way to repay** you for your help yesterday."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumagamit ng puwersa upang maigalaw ang isang bagay palapit sa sarili o sa isang partikular na direksyon.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung kaibigan mong laging humihila sa'yo pabalik sa toxic mong ex. Or 'yung gravity ng kama tuwing Lunes ng umaga, humihila sa'yo pababa. Pwede ring 'yung amoy ng bagong lutong pandesal na humihila sa'yo palabas ng bahay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kalabaw ang **humihila** ng araro sa bukid.","translation":"The carabao **is pulling** the plow in the field."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo **humihila** ang buhok ng kapatid mo?","translation":"Why **are you pulling** your sibling's hair?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglunok ng isang likido; ang utos na gawin ang nasabing kilos.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "inom" na may hulaping "-in".
original_explanation: The command your mom gives you when you're sick: 'Inumin mo 'tong gamot!' (Drink this medicine!). Or what your friend yells at the bar: 'Inumin mo na 'yan!' (Drink that up!). It's the action part of the beverage equation.
usage_notes: Ito ay nasa anyong pautos (imperative). Ang diin ay nasa ikalawang pantig, na iba sa pangngalang 'inumin' (/i-nu-MIN/).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **inumin** ang gamot tatlong beses sa isang araw.","translation":"You need **to drink** the medicine three times a day."},{"sentence":"**Inumin** mo na ang kape mo bago pa lumamig.","translation":"**Drink** your coffee before it gets cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na puno ng sigla at enerhiya; napakasigla.
original_explanation: Ito yung feeling mo after payday! Yung parang kaya mong takbuhin ang EDSA at mag-zumba sa gitna ng traffic. It's the "extra rice" version of 'masigla'. Maximum energy, good vibes only, parang host ng morning show.
usage_notes: A reduplicated adjective used for emphasis, meaning 'very lively' or 'full of energy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Masiglang-masigla** ang mga bata habang naglalaro sa parke.","translation":"The children were **very lively** while playing in the park."}]

translation: a unit of measure for grain
meaning_filipino: Isang lumang yunit ng panukat para sa mga butil, tulad ng palay o mais, na katumbas ng dalawampu't limang (25) salop.
etymology: From an old Tagalog or other Philippine language term for a measure. The Hispanized spelling is 'cavan'.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'bulk order'. Before we were adding to cart by the kilo, farmers were measuring their harvest by the kabang. It's a measurement from our agricultural roots, a reminder of a time when wealth was counted in sacks of rice, not followers on TikTok. Mostly heard from your grandparents or in probinsya settings.
usage_notes: This term is now considered archaic or technical in many urban areas, largely replaced by kilograms. One cavan of rice is now commercially understood as 50kg, though the traditional measure is 25 gantas (salop).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ani nila ay umabot sa isandaang **kabang** na palay.","translation":"Their harvest reached one hundred **units** of unhusked rice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang de-baterya na nagbibigay ng artipisyal na liwanag, karaniwang hawak-kamay.
etymology: From English 'flashlight', respelled according to Tagalog phonology.
original_explanation: Your best friend during a brownout. It's that thing you can never find when the lights suddenly go out, and when you do, the batteries are probably dead. Also the required tool for telling scary stories under a blanket.
usage_notes: The spelling is a Filipinized version of the English word. The English spelling 'flashlight' is also commonly used in writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hanapin mo nga ang **plaslayt** at nag-brownout na naman.","translation":"Please find the **flashlight** because there's a brownout again."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng **plaslayt** para makita ang daan sa dilim.","translation":"We need a **flashlight** to see the path in the dark."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para sa isang tao na labis na nagsisikap makuha ang pag-apruba ng isang grupo, kadalasan sa paraang nagpapababa sa iba o sa sarili upang maging katangi-tangi.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na 'pick me,' na nagpapahiwatig ng pagnanais na mapili o mapansin. Naging popular sa online discourse at feministang kritisismo.
original_explanation: Basically the gender-neutral version of 'pick me girl'. It's that person in the office who tells the boss, "Actually, I love working overtime!" habang the rest of you are dying. They want to be chosen, to be seen as 'different' and 'better', kahit pa ang kapalit ay ang sanity ng lahat.
usage_notes: Isang slang term na ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang partikular na uri ng pag-uugali. Maaari ding gamitin bilang pangngalan ('She's a pick-me') o pang-uri ('That's such a pick-me thing to say').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Pick Me** ng dating niya, laging kontra sa opinyon ng karamihan para lang mapansin.","translation":"He gives off such a **Pick Me** vibe, always going against the majority opinion just to get noticed."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagka-**Pick Me** niya, sinabi niyang masaya siyang magtrabaho kahit walang bayad.","translation":"Being such a **Pick Me**, she said she was happy to work even without pay."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pantukoy na ginagamit bago ang isang pangngalang pantangi ng tao sa kaukulang palagyo.
original_explanation: The little word that's basically a spotlight operator for people's names. You can't just say 'Juan is coming.' You have to give him a proper intro: 'Parating na **si** Juan.' It's the grammatical version of pointing at someone. Without 'si', your sentence about a person sounds naked and wrong.
usage_notes: Used for singular personal names in the nominative case (as the subject). The plural form is 'sina' (e.g., 'sina Juan at Maria'). The possessive/objective form is 'ni'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumakain **si** Maria ng mangga.","translation":"**Maria** is eating a mango."},{"sentence":"Sino ang kasama mo? **Si** Pedro.","translation":"Who is with you? **Pedro**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging kaaya-aya at pino sa anyo o pamamaraan.
original_explanation: This is that 'effortless chic' vibe. It's Heart Evangelista in Paris, it's a perfectly tailored suit, it's a simple but stunning table setting. It's not just about being 'maganda', it's about having class and sophistication. The modern, sleek spelling of 'elegansiya'.
usage_notes: The more common and modern spelling. "Elegansiya" is an older variant. Can be used as a noun for "elegance" or an adjective for "elegant".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **elegansya** talaga siyang magdala ng damit.","translation":"She really has an **elegance** in how she wears clothes."},{"sentence":"Ang simple pero **elegansya** ng disenyo.","translation":"The design is simple but **elegant**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdurugo mula sa loob ng ilong, na karaniwang sanhi ng pagkapunit ng maliliit na ugat sa bahaging ito.
original_explanation: That moment when your brain is overheating from a difficult exam, a stressful day at work, or simply from the intense summer heat, and your nose decides to stage a dramatic, bloody exit. It's the body's way of saying 'System overload! Please restart.'
usage_notes: Can also be used figuratively to mean extreme difficulty or mental exertion, as in "Dugo't balinguyngoy ang inabot ko sa exam," meaning "I went through blood and nosebleeds for that exam."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla na lang nagkaroon ng **balinguyngoy** si Ana dahil sa sobrang init.","translation":"Ana suddenly had a **nosebleed** because of the extreme heat."},{"sentence":"Nakaka-**balinguyngoy** ang mga tanong sa math quiz.","translation":"The questions on the math quiz are **nosebleed**-inducing (figuratively difficult)."}]

translation: to shake off; to dust off
meaning_filipino: Alisin ang isang bagay, tulad ng alikabok o tubig, sa pamamagitan ng pag-uga o pagpagpag.
original_explanation: What you do to your shoes after walking on a dusty road, or to your jacket after a light drizzle. It's the "pagpag" you do to shake off dirt, bad vibes, or, according to superstition, spirits after a wake. "Taylor Swift told us to Shake It Off, but our lolas have been telling us to iwagwag it for centuries."
usage_notes: A common action. Different from `yugyugin` (to shake a container) or `alogin` (to shake something to mix it). `Iwagwag` is specifically for removing something from a surface by shaking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iwagwag** mo muna ang basahan bago mo gamitin.","translation":"**Shake off** the rag first before you use it."},{"sentence":"**Iwinagwag** niya ang alikabok mula sa kanyang pantalon.","translation":"He **dusted off** the dust from his pants."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagbibigay-alam o pagpapaunawa sa isang tao ng isang mahalagang impormasyon o katotohanan.
original_explanation: This is the high-level, 'Noli Me Tángere' way of saying 'to let someone know.' You don't just text 'FYI.' You formally `magpatalos`. It’s like sending a company-wide memo, but with the gravitas of a historical decree. Very formal, very literary.
usage_notes: A formal and literary term. 'Ipaalam' or 'ipabatid' are more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibig kong **magpatalos** sa inyong kamahalan ng isang mahalagang balita.","translation":"I wish to **inform** your majesty of important news."},{"sentence":"Ang liham ay isinulat upang **magpatalos** sa mga mamamayan ng kanilang mga karapatan.","translation":"The letter was written to **make the citizens aware** of their rights."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na sasakyang hila o tulak ng kamay, karaniwang may dalawa o apat na gulong, na ginagamit sa paghakot ng mga kagamitan o paninda.
original_explanation: The Filipino's all-purpose mobile storage unit. You see it everywhere: the taho vendor's mobile kitchen, the junk shop collector's treasure chest, the palengke vendor's delivery truck. It's the humble, non-motorized workhorse of the Filipino streets. If you see a "kariton" parked outside, someone's probably selling something delicious or useful nearby.
usage_notes: Madalas na iniuugnay sa mga naglalako sa kalye o mga mangangalakal ng basura.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng mga bote at karton ang **kariton** ng magbobote.","translation":"The junk collector's **pushcart** is full of bottles and cardboard."},{"sentence":"Itinutulak niya ang kanyang **kariton** ng sorbetes tuwing hapon.","translation":"He pushes his ice cream **cart** every afternoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng mga tubo, kanal, o estero na nagsisilbing daanan ng labis na tubig, lalo na ang tubig-ulan o maruming tubig, papalayo sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung dahilan kung bakit bumabaha sa Maynila... o kung bakit *hindi* dapat bumabaha. Yung mga kanal sa gilid ng kalsada na laging puno ng plastic at styrofoam? 'Yan ang **drainage** system natin. Minsan gumagana, madalas nagpapanggap lang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Barado na naman ang **drainage** sa aming kalye kaya konting ulan lang, baha na agad.","translation":"The **drainage** on our street is clogged again, so it floods immediately with just a little rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging labis na maselan, masusi, at mapili sa mga detalye; pagiging pihikan.
original_explanation: This is the energy of someone who color-codes their spreadsheet, arranges their bookshelf by genre AND author's last name, or sends back food at a restaurant because it's not 'exactly' right. It's the 'OC' (obsessive-compulsive) trait before it was a clinical term. The opposite of 'pwede na 'yan.'
usage_notes: A less common word, often used to describe someone who is extremely particular and hard to please.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang matandang dalaga sa kanyang **pagkamauyad** sa kalinisan.","translation":"The old maid was known for her **fastidiousness** when it comes to cleanliness."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkamauyad** niya sa pagkain ay nagpapahirap sa mga kasama niya.","translation":"His **meticulousness** with food makes it difficult for his companions."}]

translation: to gag; to retch; to feel nauseated
meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng pagkahilo na tila masusuka, o ang akto ng pag-ubo na parang may isusuka ngunit walang lumalabas.
original_explanation: It's that "I'm-about-to-vomit" feeling, but nothing comes out. That reflex you get when you smell something really, *really* bad. O kaya 'yung feeling mo pagkatapos ng "Hell Week" sa BPO at nakakita ka na naman ng kape. It’s the prequel to "suka." The body's final warning before an eruption.
usage_notes: Describes the physical sensation or action of gagging, which may or may not lead to actual vomiting (pagsusuka).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **dumuwal** ako sa sama ng amoy sa basurahan.","translation":"I almost **gagged** from the awful smell of the garbage."},{"sentence":"Nang mapainom siya ng mapait na gamot, nagsimula siyang **dumuwal**.","translation":"When he drank the bitter medicine, he started **to retch**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mamamayan na may karapatan at kuwalipikasyong bumoto o pumili ng opisyal ng pamahalaan.
etymology: From `mang-` + `hahalal` (future tense of `halal`, 'to elect'). Literally, "one who will elect."
original_explanation: The person with the real 'power,' at least for one day every few years. You're the one who lines up for hours under the sun, gets your finger stained with indelible ink, and then complains about the government for the next six years. You are the ultimate client, and election day is your chance to leave a 'customer review.'
usage_notes: A formal term used in civics, news, and political discussions. The more common, everyday term is 'botante'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng bawat **manghahalal** na bumoto nang matalino.","translation":"It is the duty of every **voter** to vote wisely."},{"sentence":"Daan-daang libong **manghahalal** ang inaasahang darating sa mga presinto.","translation":"Hundreds of thousands of **voters** are expected to arrive at the precincts."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na ilawan na karaniwang gumagamit ng gas, alkohol, o langis bilang panggatong, at may mitsa.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'lamparilla' (maliit na lampara).
original_explanation: The original 'low-batt' mode lighting. This is the go-to device during a brownout before power banks and rechargeable fans became a thing. It gives off that spooky, horror movie vibe, perfect for telling ghost stories.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsindi kami ng **lamparilya** noong nag-brownout.","translation":"We lit a **small lamp** when the power went out."},{"sentence":"Ang liwanag mula sa **lamparilya** ay sapat lamang para makita ang daan.","translation":"The light from the **alcohol lamp** was just enough to see the way."}]

translation: to become fashionable, to be in trend
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging popular o kalakaran ng isang estilo, gawi, o bagay sa isang partikular na panahon.
etymology: From "uso" (trend, fashion), which is from Spanish 'uso' (use, custom).
original_explanation: Remember when Dalgona coffee was life? Or when everyone was doing the 'Tala' dance challenge? 'Yun, umuso 'yun. It's the word for anything that goes viral and becomes the "in" thing, until the next trend comes along.
usage_notes: "Uso" is the noun (trend), "umuso" is the verb (to become a trend).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umuso** na naman ang mga damit na may maluluwang na manggas.","translation":"Clothes with wide sleeves have **become fashionable** again."},{"sentence":"Sana **umuso** naman ang pagiging mabait sa lahat.","translation":"I hope being kind to everyone **becomes the trend**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking gumagawa o nagbebenta ng tabako.
etymology: From Spanish 'tabaquero' (a man who works with tobacco).
original_explanation: The male counterpart of the tabakera. The dude version. The guy who knows his tobacco leaves better than his own family tree.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sanay na sanay ang mga kamay ng **tabakero** sa pagbabalot ng tabako.","translation":"The **male cigar maker's** hands are very skilled in rolling tobacco."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may kakulangan sa talino, pang-unawa, o bilis ng pag-iisip; hangal o tanga.
original_explanation: Sounds like its meaning. It’s that person who asks 'Bakit?' after you've explained something five times. More endearing than 'bobo,' but more insulting than 'tanga.' It's the kind of stupid that makes you shake your head with a sigh. 'Ang **tunggak**, iniwan bukas 'yung gate!'
usage_notes: An old-fashioned but still understood insult. It has a slightly more literary or formal feel than 'tanga' or 'bobo'. Can also be used as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **tunggak**, gamitin mo ang iyong isip.","translation":"Don't be an **idiot**, use your brain."},{"sentence":"Pinarusahan siya dahil sa kanyang **tunggak** na pagkakamali.","translation":"He was punished for his **stupid** mistake."}]

translation: to be short of; to be insufficient
meaning_filipino: Magkulang sa isang bagay; hindi umabot o sumapat sa kinakailangan.
original_explanation: This is the official feeling of 'petsa de peligro'—that week before payday when your budget is screaming for help. When your funds, patience, or even time 'mangapos', it means you're running dangerously low and about to run out. It's the state of being 'kinakapos'.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of finances, resources, or time. The form 'kinakapos' (present progressive) is very commonly used to describe the state of being short on funds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung hindi ka magtitipid, tiyak na **mangangapos** ka bago dumating ang sweldo.","translation":"If you don't save, you will surely **be short of money** before payday arrives."}]

translation: in one's mind, mentally, in thought
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nagaganap o umiiral lamang sa loob ng isipan, kamalayan, o imahinasyon ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is your personal 'overthinking' headquarters. When you're rehearsing an argument you had yesterday, planning a conversation for tomorrow, or imagining winning the lottery, it's all happening 'sa pag-iisip' mo lang. It's the mental multiverse where you're the main character in every scenario.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ipakita ang pagkakaiba ng kung ano ang nasa isip lamang kumpara sa kung ano ang tunay na nangyayari.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sa pag-iisip** ko, nanalo na ako sa lotto ng sampung beses.","translation":"**In my mind**, I've already won the lottery ten times."},{"sentence":"Magkaiba ang sinasabi niya sa totoong nararamdaman **sa pag-iisip** niya.","translation":"What he says is different from what he truly feels **in his thoughts**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kilos ng pag-ako sa mga responsibilidad na karaniwang kaakibat ng pagiging isang nasa hustong gulang, tulad ng pagbabayad ng bills, pagtatrabaho, at pamamahala ng sariling buhay.
etymology: From the English word "adult" + "-ing", used as a gerund. It has been fully adopted into modern Filipino slang.
original_explanation: The new Olympic sport where the events include: paying bills on time, cooking something that isn't instant noodles, and successfully booking a Grab on a rainy payday Friday. The prize? More bills. Welcome to the club.
usage_notes: A very popular slang term among millennials and Gen Z to describe the struggles and mundane tasks of adult life. Often used with a sense of weariness or 'hugot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Parte ng **adulting** ang pag-file ng sarili mong income tax return.","translation":"Part of **adulting** is filing your own income tax return."},{"sentence":"Pagod na ako sa **adulting**, pwede bang maging pusa na lang?","translation":"I'm tired of **adulting**, can I just be a cat?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng militar na binubuo ng ilang batalyon, na karaniwang pinamumunuan ng isang koronel.
original_explanation: This is a super formal, rarely used word unless you're watching a historical war movie. Think of it as a big barkada of soldiers, a whole squad-up, but the military version. Like, a whole BPO floor, but for fighting.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong historikal o militar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **rehimyento** ng mga sundalo ay ipinadala sa malayong probinsya.","translation":"The **regiment** of soldiers was sent to a distant province."},{"sentence":"Kasapi ang kanyang lolo sa isang makasaysayang **rehimyento** noong panahon ng digmaan.","translation":"His grandfather was a member of a historic **regiment** during the war."}]

translation: Picot; a decorative loop in needlework
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampalamuting tahi sa gilid ng tela, na bumubuo ng maliliit na silo o buhol.
original_explanation: The fancy, frilly edge you see on your lola's handkerchiefs, old-school pillowcases, or baby clothes. It's that extra little detail that says 'I have time and skill.' It's the crocheted equivalent of adding 'po' and 'opo' to your sentences—pure class.
usage_notes: Primarily used in sewing, crochet, and embroidery contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang gilid ng panyo ay may magandang **pikadura**.","translation":"The edge of the handkerchief has a beautiful **picot** stitch."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan ako ng lola ko kung paano gumawa ng **pikadura**.","translation":"My grandmother taught me how to make a **picot** stitch."}]

translation: the act of washing one's face
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paghuhugas o paglilinis ng mukha gamit ang tubig at, kung minsan, sabon.
original_explanation: The first step to becoming a functional human in the morning. It's that moment you splash cold water on your face and wonder about your life choices. The official cure for a 'puyat' face, even if it's just for five minutes.
usage_notes: The 'hi-' prefix here implies a more thorough or deliberate action than a simple 'paghilamos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghihilamos** sa umaga ay nakakagising ng diwa.","translation":"The **act of washing one's face** in the morning awakens the senses."},{"sentence":"Importante ang tamang **paghihilamos** para maiwasan ang pimples.","translation":"Proper **face washing** is important to avoid pimples."}]

meaning_filipino: Mawala nang tuluyan; maglaho.
original_explanation: Parang sweldo mo pagka-receive. One moment it's there, the next, wala na. O parang yung nangako ng 'walang iwanan' pero bigla na lang nag-ghost. It's the magic trick no one likes.
usage_notes: Often used in a more poetic or dramatic sense than `mawala`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig niya ay tila bulang biglang **naparam**.","translation":"His/Her love was like a bubble that suddenly **vanished**."},{"sentence":"Sa isang iglap, **naparam** ang lahat ng kanyang pinaghirapan.","translation":"In an instant, everything he worked for **disappeared**."}]

translation: a hit; a strike; a spanking
meaning_filipino: Ang akto o resulta ng paghampas; isang tama o dagok.
original_explanation: The noun form of "Lagot ka!" It's the 'hampas' itself. "Isang palo lang, 'di ka na umulit." It can be the strike in baseball, the beat of a drum, or the spank that was threatened by your mom. It's the consequence made physical.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical blow, a strike in a game, or a beat in music.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakalakas ng **palo** ng karpintero sa pako.","translation":"The carpenter's **strike** on the nail was very strong."},{"sentence":"Ang unang **palo** sa tambol ang hudyat ng simula ng parada.","translation":"The first **beat** of the drum signaled the start of the parade."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang tao, pangkat, o entidad na kalaban o kakompetensya sa isang paligsahan, labanan, o anumang uri ng pagtutunggalian.
original_explanation: Your katunggali is your rival. It could be the other team in a basketball game, the other candidate in an election, or even that officemate who's also eyeing the same promotion (and the last piece of pizza in the pantry). The frenemy you love to beat.
usage_notes: Can be used in sports, politics, business, or even personal relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang aking pangunahing **katunggali** sa pagka-pangulo ng klase.","translation":"He is my main **rival** for class president."},{"sentence":"Kahit magkaibigan, sila ay magka-**katunggali** sa loob ng kort.","translation":"Even though they are friends, they are **opponents** on the court."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa balarilang Filipino, ito ang aspekto ng pandiwa na nagsasaad ng kilos na hindi pa nasisimulan ngunit binabalak pa lamang gawin. Tinatawag ding aspektong panghinaharap.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung "sana all" o "drawing" tense sa grammar. Lahat ng plano mo na hindi pa nangyayari, nandito. "Kakain," "matutulog," "mag-aaral," "magbabayad ng utang." Puro plano, hindi pa sure kung mangyayari. It's the future tense, full of hope and good intentions.
usage_notes: This is a grammatical term for the future tense of a verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang \"aalis\" ay nasa aspektong **kontemplatibo**.","translation":"The word \"aalis\" (will leave) is in the **contemplative** tense."},{"sentence":"Itinuro ng guro ang tatlong aspekto ng pandiwa: perpektibo, imperpektibo, at **kontemplatibo**.","translation":"The teacher taught the three aspects of the verb: perfective, imperfective, and **contemplative**."}]

translation: to get a manicure; to apply a manicure
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng pangkulay o pampaganda sa mga kuko sa kamay.
original_explanation: That feeling when you just got your nails done and you can't open a can of soda. "Girl, pa-open naman ng Coke, kaka-magmanikyur ko lang eh." It's the official verb for self-care day, usually followed by "mag-pedikyur".
usage_notes: Can mean to apply a manicure to oneself or to someone else, or to have a manicure done by a professional.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta ako sa salon para **magmanikyur** bago ang party.","translation":"I'm going to the salon to **get a manicure** before the party."},{"sentence":"Galing niyang **magmanikyur**, parang professional.","translation":"She's so good at **doing manicures**, like a professional."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang itaas ang paningin o tumingin sa itaas.
original_explanation: What you do when you hear an airplane, a drone, or a loud thud from your upstairs neighbor. Also the default reaction when someone shouts 'Hala, may flying ipis!' You can't help it. Your neck just does the thing automatically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla akong **napatingala** nang may dumaang eroplano.","translation":"I suddenly **happened to look up** when an airplane passed by."},{"sentence":"**Napatingala** ang mga tao sa ganda ng fireworks display.","translation":"The people **looked up** at the beauty of the fireworks display."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilatag o ihanda ang pagkain sa hapag-kainan para pagsaluhan; ialay.
original_explanation: This is what your nanay tells you to do before everyone eats. It's the act of setting the table, serving the ulam, and basically presenting the food like a sacrifice to the gods (or just your hungry family). Think 'plating' but for a family-style Filipino meal.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of meals or religious offerings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **ihayin** mo na ang adobo para makakain na tayo.","translation":"Please **serve** the adobo so we can eat now."},{"sentence":"Marapat lamang na **ihayin** natin ang pasasalamat sa Panginoon.","translation":"It is only right that we **offer** our thanks to the Lord."}]

translation: to preach; to moralize; to give as advice
meaning_filipino: Ituro o ibigay bilang aral o payo, lalo na sa aspetong moral, etikal, o espirituwal.
etymology: From `i-` (causative prefix) + `pangaral` (sermon, advice). `Pangaral` itself is from `pang-` + `aral` (lesson).
original_explanation: This is what your lola does when you come home late. It's the act of giving a sermon or a lecture, usually about morals, good conduct, or life lessons. It can be from a priest in a church, a teacher in a classroom, or your mom when she sees your grades. 'Lagi niyang ipinapangaral sa amin ang kahalagahan ng pagiging matapat.'
usage_notes: Strongly associated with moral or religious instruction. Can sometimes be used sarcastically to mean 'to lecture someone'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal sa kapwa ang laging **ipinapangaral** sa simbahan.","translation":"Loving one's neighbor is what is always **preached** in church."},{"sentence":"Paulit-ulit na **ipinangaral** ng aming mga magulang ang kahalagahan ng edukasyon.","translation":"Our parents repeatedly **gave as advice** the importance of education."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, sitwasyon, o tanong na mahirap unawain, lutasin, o harapin.
original_explanation: The adulting version of "problema." It's not just a flat tire; it's the existential dread of inflation, traffic, and your ever-growing backlogs. When your "problema" graduates with a master's degree, it becomes a "suliranin." It's what your group project becomes when only one person is doing all the work.
usage_notes: More formal and serious than 'problema'. Often used in academic, political, or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kahirapan ay isang malaking **suliranin** ng bansa.","translation":"Poverty is a major **problem** for the country."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating humanap ng solusyon sa **suliranin** na ito.","translation":"We need to find a solution to this **problem**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gas na walang kulay, lubhang nasusunog, at ginagamit sa pagwe-welding at pagputol ng metal kapag hinaluan ng oksiheno.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "acetileno", na hinango sa internasyonal na terminong siyentipiko.
original_explanation: Yan yung gas na ginagamit ng mga welder sa talyer. Yung nagbibigay-buhay sa mala-lightsaber nilang torch. Amoy pa lang, alam mo nang may nagwe-welding sa malapit. Partner 'yan ng oxygen tank para maging super init ng apoy.
usage_notes: Teknikal na termino. Ang "asetileno" ay isang alternatibong baybay na mas malapit sa Espanyol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iingat ang welder sa paggamit ng tangke ng **asetilen**.","translation":"The welder is careful in using the **acetylene** tank."},{"sentence":"Ang **asetilen** ay kailangan para sa oxy-acetylene welding.","translation":"**Acetylene** is needed for oxy-acetylene welding."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng insekto na may malalaki at karaniwang makukulay na pakpak.
etymology: Reduplication of 'paro', an archaic word for butterfly.
original_explanation: That feeling you get in your stomach when your crush looks at you? That's 'butterflies'. The actual insect is a paru-paro. They're like the fabulous version of a moth who decided to go out in the daytime. Also, a classic subject for Grade 1 drawing projects.
usage_notes: The standard spelling is hyphenated as 'paru-paro', but 'paruparo' is also commonly seen.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May isang magandang **paru-paro** na dumapo sa bulaklak.","translation":"A beautiful **butterfly** landed on the flower."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ay masayang naghahabulan ng mga **paru-paro** sa parang.","translation":"The children were happily chasing **butterflies** in the field."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging suko o pagod na sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon dahil sa paulit-ulit na karanasan dito.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get after eating the same adobo for five straight days. It's the 'I'm so over it' emotion. That feeling when your crush keeps playing with your feelings? 'Sawa na ako.' That feeling when you've been stuck in EDSA traffic for three hours? 'Sawa na ako.' It's the endpoint of your patience, the final destination of being umay.
usage_notes: Madalas sinusundan ng salitang 'na'. Halimbawa: 'Sawa na ako.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sawa** na ako sa paulit-ulit niyang mga dahilan.","translation":"I'm **fed up** with his repetitive excuses."},{"sentence":"Hindi ka ba nasasawa sa pagkain ng manok araw-araw?","translation":"Don't you get tired of eating chicken every day?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling sa isang tao na kunin ang isang bagay para sa iyo.
original_explanation: That moment when you're super comfy in bed and you ask your younger sibling, 'Uy, pakuha naman ng tubig.' It's the ultimate 'tamad' power move. The 'paki-' prefix is your magic word for getting things done without moving a muscle.
usage_notes: A request form of the verb 'kunin' (to get). The 'pa-' prefix indicates that the action is being done by someone else at the speaker's request.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakuha** mo naman ang remote sa mesa.","translation":"Could you please **have someone get** the remote from the table for me?"},{"sentence":"Nag-utos si nanay na **pakuha** ng mangga sa kapitbahay.","translation":"Mom ordered to **have someone get** mangoes from the neighbor."}]

translation: rawr (an expression of affection or playfulness)
meaning_filipino: (Balbal/Internet Slang) Isang ekspresyon na ginagamit sa online chat o text, na karaniwang nangangahulugang "I love you" sa "dinosaur language" o isang paraan ng pagiging mapaglaro o 'cute'.
etymology: Mula sa onomatopeya sa Ingles para sa dagundong ng dinosaur, na naging popular bilang internet slang.
original_explanation: The "I love you" of the jejemons and early 2010s internet culture. It's the sound a 'cute' dinosaur makes. If someone messages you "rawr" today, they're either being ironic, nostalgic, or they just woke up from a 10-year coma. "Rawr means I love you in dinosaur."
usage_notes: Naging popular noong panahon ng 'Jejemon' at emo subcultures sa Pilipinas. Ngayon ay madalas gamitin nang may kabalintunaan (ironically).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-message siya sa akin ng, 'Gandang gabi, **rawr**!'","translation":"He messaged me, 'Good evening, **rawr**!'"},{"sentence":"Naalala ko pa noong uso ang 'jejeje' at '**rawr**' sa text.","translation":"I still remember when 'jejeje' and '**rawr**' were popular in texts."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilis o tulin ng paggalaw ng isang bagay sa isang tiyak na direksyon.
original_explanation: A very formal, almost scientific-sounding word for 'speed.' You won't hear this in everyday chismisan. It's the word your physics teacher uses, or what you might see in a technical manual for a car. It's 'bilis' but with a college degree. Think of it as the 'speed' you use when you're trying to sound smart.
usage_notes: A formal and technical term. 'Bilis' or 'tulin' are far more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakalkula ng mga siyentipiko ang **belosidad** ng kometa.","translation":"The scientists are calculating the **velocity** of the comet."},{"sentence":"Kailangang panatilihin ang tamang **belosidad** upang hindi maaksidente.","translation":"One must maintain the correct **speed** to avoid an accident."}]

translation: to pair up, to form a tandem
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsamahin ang dalawang tao o bagay upang bumuo ng isang pares o pangkat.
original_explanation: This is the origin story of every 'love team' in showbiz, like KathNiel or DonBelle. When two actors or actresses magtambal, they are paired up for a project, and fans hope they become a real-life couple. It can also mean pairing up for a group project or a political ticket.
usage_notes: Commonly used in entertainment (love teams) and politics (running mates).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ang napiling **magtambal** para sa bagong teleserye.","translation":"They were chosen to **pair up** for the new TV series."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang dalawang kandidato na **magtambal** para sa darating na halalan.","translation":"The two candidates decided to **form a tandem** for the upcoming election."}]

translation: to break down; to have a falling out
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkasira o pagkawala ng tamang paggana ng isang bagay o makina; o ang pagkasira ng isang relasyon o pagkakaibigan.
