usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisabi sa kanya na **i-text** ako kapag nakauwi na siya.","translation":"Please tell him to **text** me when he gets home."},{"sentence":"**I-text** mo sa akin ang listahan ng mga bibilhin sa palengke.","translation":"**Text** me the list of things to buy at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, karaniwang babae, na mayroong lihim at labas-sa-kasal na relasyon sa isang taong may asawa na.
etymology: From the verb "kabit" (to attach, to connect), implying an 'attached' or secondary person.
original_explanation: The main character in every Pinoy teleserye that involves sampalan and a dramatic confrontation scene at a fancy restaurant. The word that launches a thousand 'Marites' investigations. It's not just a person, it's a plot device.
usage_notes: This term has a very strong and specific cultural connotation in the Philippines, almost exclusively referring to a "mistress" and carrying heavy social stigma. Pronunciation stress is on the second syllable, unlike the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging malaking iskandalo ang pagbubunyag na may **kabit** ang sikat na politiko.","translation":"The revelation that the famous politician had a **mistress** became a huge scandal."},{"sentence":"Ang tema ng pelikula ay tungkol sa hirap ng buhay ng isang **kabit**.","translation":"The movie's theme is about the difficult life of a **paramour**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagtutulungan ng dalawa o higit pang tao sa isang lihim at karaniwang masamang balak o gawain.
original_explanation: Like when your officemates secretly plan a mass resignation, leaving you with all the work. Or when the neighborhood Mariteses gather to piece together the latest chismis. It's teamwork, but for shady purposes.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation of conspiracy against someone or something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalak ng mga magnanakaw na **magsabuwatan** upang pasukin ang bangko.","translation":"The thieves planned to **conspire** to break into the bank."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong **magsabuwatan** laban sa inyong kaibigan.","translation":"Do not **conspire** against your friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng sobrang laya na kadalasang humahantong sa kapabayaan, pag-abuso, o kawalan ng pananagutan.
original_explanation: That feeling when your parents are out of town for the weekend. You think you can do anything, but it usually just ends with you eating instant noodles for three straight days and not cleaning the house. Also known as "libertinism" sa mga pa-deep.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation, implying a lack of responsibility or discipline that comes with freedom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **labis na kalayaan** ay maaaring magdulot ng kapahamakan.","translation":"**Excessive freedom** can lead to ruin."},{"sentence":"Ipinagkamali niya ang tiwala sa **labis na kalayaan**.","translation":"He mistook trust for **license** (to do whatever he wanted)."}]

translation: to do something with someone; to accompany
meaning_filipino: Sumama o gawin ang isang bagay kasama ang isa pa. Magsagawa ng kilos na kasabay ng kilos ng iba.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'sana all' verb. When your friend starts singing videoke off-key, you sabayan them out of solidarity (or to drown them out). It's the 'I'll go with you' when your crush decides to get milk tea. It's doing something *together* with someone else.
usage_notes: Often implies doing an action alongside or in sync with someone else, not just physically accompanying them.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sabayan** mo akong kumanta ng paborito nating kanta.","translation":"**Sing** our favorite song **along with me**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **sabayan** sa pagkain, ang bilis mong maubos!","translation":"Don't **eat at the same time as me**, you finish so quickly!"}]

translation: to direct; to lead to; to bring to
meaning_filipino: Dalhin, ihatid, o ituon sa isang partikular na lugar, direksyon, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is what a Waze or Google Maps voice does. It tells you where to go. 'In 300 meters, **idako** ang sasakyan sa kaliwa.' It's about directing something—your gaze, your car, your life, or even a conversation—towards a specific point.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Idako** mo ang iyong mga mata sa entablado.","translation":"**Direct** your eyes to the stage."},{"sentence":"Sinisikap ng gobyerno na **idako** ang ekonomiya tungo sa pag-unlad.","translation":"The government is trying to **lead** the economy towards progress."}]

translation: to cause to age; to let something mature or ferment
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagpapatagal sa isang bagay upang ito ay tumanda, maging luma, o dumaan sa proseso ng permentasyon para sa mas mainam na kalidad.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa sa keso, alak, o kahit sa bagoong para sumarap. You let it sit and **magpagulang**. Parang sa love life, minsan kailangan mo munang ipagulang ang feelings bago umamin. 'Wag atat!
usage_notes: Often used in the context of food and beverage preparation, like aging wine, cheese, or vinegar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpagulang** ng suka nang ilang buwan para maging mas maasim ito.","translation":"You need to **let the vinegar age** for a few months for it to become sourer."},{"sentence":"**Nagpagulang** sila ng baka para lumambot ang karne nito.","translation":"They **aged** the beef to make the meat tender."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang larawan na ginagamit ng isang tao upang kumatawan sa kanyang sarili sa isang social media account, chat application, o online profile. Pinaikli para sa 'display picture'.
etymology: Mula sa acronym sa Ingles na 'DP' (Display Picture).
original_explanation: Short for 'Display Picture'. Ito 'yung profile pic mo sa Facebook, Twitter, o Instagram. Madalas, ito 'yung aabutin mo ng 300 takes para makuha ang tamang anggulo. 'Yung 'I woke up like this' pero 5 am ka pa nag-makeup.
usage_notes: Karaniwang slang sa Pilipinas, ipinagpapalit sa 'profile pic'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng bago mong **DP** sa Facebook!","translation":"Your new **DP** on Facebook is beautiful!"},{"sentence":"Palitan mo na 'yang **DP** mo, kuha pa 'yan noong 2015.","translation":"Change your **DP** already, that one was taken back in 2015."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na namumuno, gumagabay, o nangunguna sa isang grupo, organisasyon, o kilusan.
original_explanation: The groupmate who actually does the work. The kuya or ate in the barkada who decides where to eat. The class president, the team captain, the BPO team lead—anyone who takes charge. Hopefully, they're a good lider and not just someone who's good at being pabida.
usage_notes: Ang baybay na 'lider' ay mas pormal at karaniwan sa panitikan, habang ang 'leader' ay madalas gamitin sa pasalitang paraan o sa konteksto ng negosyo (hal. team leader).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang nahalal na bagong **lider** ng aming samahan.","translation":"He was elected as the new **leader** of our organization."},{"sentence":"Ang isang mahusay na **lider** ay nakikinig sa kanyang mga miyembro.","translation":"A good **leader** listens to their members."}]

translation: to be buried in ruins; to have something collapse on
meaning_filipino: Matabunan o mapinsala dahil sa pagguho ng isang istruktura, lupa, o anumang bagay.
original_explanation: Imagine your Jenga tower finally giving up on life and collapsing on a poor, unsuspecting game piece. That's `maguhuan`. It's what happens when things fall apart, literally, on top of you. Also, the state of your life after seeing your ex with someone new.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of landslides, collapsed buildings, or other disasters.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat sa pagdaan doon, baka **maguhuan** ka ng mga bato.","translation":"Be careful passing there, you might get **buried by falling** rocks."},{"sentence":"Nangangamba ang mga residente na **maguhuan** sila ng lupa dahil sa tuloy-tuloy na pag-ulan.","translation":"The residents are worried they will be **buried by a landslide** due to the continuous rain."}]

meaning_filipino: May anyo o korte na katulad ng isang puso.
original_explanation: The default shape for anything Valentine's Day-related, from chocolates to throw pillows. Also used to describe the face shape of many artistas. "Yung unan na hugis-puso na may mukha ni Daniel Padilla."
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective describing something, or a noun referring to the shape itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan niya ako ng isang kahong tsokolateng **hugis-puso**.","translation":"He gave me a box of **heart-shaped** chocolates."},{"sentence":"Gagawa ako ng mga pandesal na **hugis-puso** para sa almusal.","translation":"I will make **heart-shaped** pandesal for breakfast."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng isang bagay kapalit ng pera o bayad.
original_explanation: The national sport of Filipinos every 12.12, payday, or sahod. It's that 'add to cart' and 'checkout' moment that brings temporary happiness. 'Yung **bumili** ka ng kape na 200 pesos pero minimum wage ka lang. Deserve mo 'yan.
usage_notes: Actor-focus verb in the completed aspect. Present: bumibili. Future: bibili. This is one of the most fundamental verbs in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumili** si nanay ng bagong sapatos para sa akin.","translation":"Mom **bought** new shoes for me."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **bumili** ng masarap na bibingka?","translation":"Where did you **buy** that delicious rice cake?"}]

translation: to cause to bleed; to have blood drawn
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aatas o pagiging sanhi ng pag-agos ng dugo mula sa isang sugat o sa katawan. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa proseso ng pagkuha ng dugo para sa medikal na pagsusuri.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you get into a fight, literally. Or when you go to the clinic for a blood test and the med-tech says, "Sir, close your fist po," and you suddenly feel lightheaded. It's the act of making blood come out, whether by accident (sugat) or on purpose (blood donation).
usage_notes: Can refer to causing an injury that bleeds, or voluntarily having blood drawn for medical purposes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpunta siya sa Red Cross para **magpadugo** at makatulong sa mga nangangailangan.","translation":"He went to the Red Cross to **have his blood drawn** and help those in need."},{"sentence":"Ang matalas na bato ang **nagpadugo** sa kanyang tuhod.","translation":"The sharp rock **caused his knee to bleed**."}]

translation: to make someone dance; to ask someone to dance
meaning_filipino: Hikayatin, utusan, o yayain ang isang tao na sumayaw.
original_explanation: What your tita does to you at every family reunion. 'Halika, iho, **pasayawin** mo ang tita mo!' It's also that feeling when a banger song comes on and the beat just forces you to move, parang pinapasayaw ka ng kanta.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The person being made to dance is the object. Can mean either 'to ask to dance' or 'to command/force to dance.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kitang **pasayawin** sa ilalim ng mga bituin.","translation":"I want to **ask you to dance** under the stars."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **pasayawin**, dahil hindi ako marunong.","translation":"Don't **make me dance**, because I don't know how."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga sangkap, lalo na ang mga pampalasa, na inihahalo sa pagkain upang magbigay ng lasa at aroma.
original_explanation: Your lola's secret weapon. Ito yung kumpletong set ng pampalasa—bawang, sibuyas, paminta, at kung anu-ano pang magic—na nagpapabuo ng ulam. Parang group project, kailangan kumpleto ang rikado para maging successful ang menudo o adobo. Pag may kulang, 'di pasado sa quality control ni nanay.
usage_notes: Often refers to the sauteed base of garlic, onions, and tomatoes (gisa).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumpleto na ba ang **rikado** para sa lulutuin mong kaldereta?","translation":"Are the **ingredients** complete for the caldereta you are cooking?"},{"sentence":"Igisa mo muna nang mabuti ang mga **rikado** bago ilagay ang karne.","translation":"Sauté the **condiments** well first before adding the meat."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga maliliit at mumurahing bagay na palamuti o gamit na walang gaanong halaga o pakinabang.
original_explanation: 'Yung mga cute pero 'di mo naman talaga kailangan na binibili mo sa Divisoria, Mr. DIY, o sa tiangge. Keychains, maliliit na figurines, ref magnets—lahat 'yan abubot. Parang feelings mo sa kanya, akala mo valuable, pero abubot lang pala. Hugot!
usage_notes: Often used to refer to clutter or small, inexpensive decorative items. Can have a slightly negative connotation of being useless.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na ng **abubot** ang kwarto niya kaya kailangan na niyang maglinis.","translation":"Her room is full of **trinkets** so she needs to clean up."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng maraming **abubot** bilang pasalubong.","translation":"He bought a lot of **trinkets** as souvenirs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtitipon o pangongolekta ng mga bagay, tao, pondo, o impormasyon mula sa iba't ibang mapagkukunan.
etymology: From `pag-` (verb prefix indicating action) + `kalap` (to gather, to recruit).
original_explanation: This is the OG "pabida" move of every student leader or org member. Pagkalap ng pondo for the Christmas party, pagkalap ng members for the new club, or pagkalap ng chismis from your Marites neighbor. It's the act of actively seeking out and collecting things, whether it's money for a cause, people for a team, or data for your thesis. It's the hustle before the main event.
usage_notes: Commonly used in contexts of fundraising, recruitment, and research. Often interchangeable with `pangangalap`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkalap** ng donasyon para sa mga biktima ng bagyo ay naging matagumpay.","translation":"The **gathering** of donations for the typhoon victims was successful."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang **pagkalap** ng mga ebidensya para sa kaso.","translation":"The **collection** of evidence for the case has begun."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang partikular na pangalan, salita, o parirala na ginagamit upang tukuyin ang isang tao, bagay, konsepto, o lugar.
original_explanation: It's the official name for things. Like how "marites" is the unofficial `katawagan` for a chismosa, or how "WFH" is the `katawagan` for "working from home." It’s the label we agree to use so we all know what we're talking about, from scientific terms to the latest slang.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or academic contexts to refer to specific terms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang tamang **katawagan** para sa instrumentong ito sa medisina?","translation":"What is the correct **term** for this medical instrument?"},{"sentence":"Maraming bagong **katawagan** ang umusbong sa panahon ng social media.","translation":"Many new **terminologies** have emerged in the age of social media."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hugis na may pabilog na anyo kung saan ang lahat ng punto sa gilid ay magkakapareho ang layo mula sa gitna.
original_explanation: Yung shape na dinodrawing mo nung kinder ka pa. Sa meeting, ito yung 'let's circle back' na ginawang drawing. Sa Pinas, yung bilog sa prutas tuwing New Year's, para daw swerte. O kaya yung bilog ng magkakaibigan na nag-iinuman.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mismong hugis o anyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumuhit ka ng isang malaking **bilog** sa papel.","translation":"Draw a big **circle** on the paper."},{"sentence":"Bumuo sila ng **bilog** at nagsimulang mag-usap.","translation":"They formed a **circle** and started to talk."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng matinding kahirapan, kakulangan sa mga pangunahing pangangailangan, at pagtitiis.
original_explanation: This is the state of your wallet before payday, also known as 'petsa de peligro.' It's when you're surviving on instant noodles and free water refills from the office dispenser. The struggle is real, bes.
usage_notes: Often used in dramatic or formal contexts to describe extreme poverty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang dumaranas ng matinding **paghihikahos** dahil sa pandemya.","translation":"Many families are experiencing extreme **hardship** because of the pandemic."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga pangarap ay hindi napigilan ng **paghihikahos**.","translation":"Her dreams were not stopped by **destitution**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tubig na binasbasan ng pari at ginagamit sa mga ritwal ng Simbahang Katoliko.
original_explanation: The OG spiritual disinfectant. It's the water you see at the church entrance that your lola makes you dip your fingers in to make the sign of the cross. Also used by priests to bless houses, cars, and even your pet dog on St. Francis of Assisi's feast day. In horror movies, it's basically acid to aswangs and demons.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to holy water in a Catholic context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagwisik ng **bindita** ang pari sa bagong bahay.","translation":"The priest sprinkled **holy water** on the new house."},{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng kaunting **bindita** bago umalis ng simbahan.","translation":"She took a little **holy water** before leaving the church."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang naglalarawan sa isang tao na may mababang taas at malaking katawan.
original_explanation: The classic Filipino descriptor that's either an insult or a term of endearment, depending on who's saying it. Sounds like a character description from a folk tale, but is more often used by your tita to describe someone she saw at the palengke.
usage_notes: This is a very common descriptive phrase, often used together to describe a person's build. It is very direct and can be considered rude or offensive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilarawan niya ang suspek bilang isang lalaking **pandak at mataba**.","translation":"He described the suspect as a man who was **short and fat**."},{"sentence":"Madaling tandaan ang hitsura niya dahil siya ay **pandak at mataba**.","translation":"His appearance is easy to remember because he is **short and fat**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng palupo ang isang istraktura o bubong.
original_explanation: This is the verb for putting the 'palupo' (the roof's spine) in place. It's the crowning moment of framing a house. "Tapos na bang **palupuhan** 'yang bahay? Para may bubong na tayo sa Pasko!"
usage_notes: A very specific construction term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas ng umaga ay **palupuhan** na ng mga karpintero ang itinatayong bahay.","translation":"Tomorrow morning, the carpenters will **install the ridgepole** on the house being built."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **palupuhan** ang bubong kapag malakas ang hangin.","translation":"It's difficult **to install the ridgepole** on the roof when the wind is strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maindayog at parang alon na paggalaw ng balakang habang naglalakad.
original_explanation: It's that confident, rhythmic sway of the hips when someone walks. Think beauty queen walking on stage, or that person in the office who walks like they own the place. It's not just walking; it's walking with attitude and a little bit of a bounce. "Grabe ang **imbay** ng balakang niya, parang laging may background music!"
usage_notes: Almost exclusively refers to the swaying of hips.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napapalingon ang lahat sa **imbay** ng kanyang paglalakad.","translation":"Everyone turns their head at the **sway** of her walk."},{"sentence":"Ang malambot na **imbay** ng mga mananayaw ay kaaya-ayang pagmasdan.","translation":"The gentle **swaying motion** of the dancers was pleasant to watch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mismong gawain ng pandaraya, o isang sitwasyon kung saan laganap ang pandaraya.
original_explanation: This is the noun form. It's the 'cheating' that happens in a group setting. Think exams where everyone's sharing answers, a card game with marked cards, or during an election. It's the 'kalokohan' on a larger scale. 'Ang gulo ng laro, puro **dayaan**!'
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' denotes a collective action or the 'venue' of the root word 'daya' (cheat).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagreklamo sila dahil sa laganap na **dayaan** noong eleksyon.","translation":"They complained because of the widespread **cheating** during the election."},{"sentence":"Ayoko ng **dayaan**, dapat patas ang laban.","translation":"I don't like **cheating**, the fight should be fair."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang walang tigil at malakas na pagsasalita o pag-ungot, karaniwang may kasamang panenermon o pagrereklamo.
etymology: From "pag-" (verbal noun prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root "talak" (to nag).
original_explanation: You know that sound your mom or tita makes when you haven't cleaned your room for a week? That's pagtatalakan. It's a verbal machine gun of scolding, complaints, and "I told you so's". It's the background music to many Filipino households. Think of the iconic "bungangera" character.
usage_notes: Almost always has a negative connotation, implying noisy, annoying, and lengthy scolding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Rinig sa buong kapitbahayan ang **pagtatalakan** ni Aling Nena sa kanyang asawa.","translation":"The whole neighborhood could hear Aling Nena's **scolding** of her husband."},{"sentence":"Sawà na ako sa araw-araw na **pagtatalakan**.","translation":"I'm tired of the daily **nagging**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nangunguna o gumagawa ng panloloko o pandaraya (estapa) upang makakuha ng pera o ari-arian mula sa iba.
original_explanation: The main character in an 'estapa' story. This is the person with the silver tongue and a business plan that defies logic but sounds amazing. They'll promise you double-your-money in a week, sell you land they don't own, or recruit you into a pyramid scheme disguised as 'networking'. They are the 'budol-budol' masters of the financial world.
usage_notes: A very negative term for a person who commits fraud.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa taong iyan, kilala siyang **estapador** sa aming lugar.","translation":"Be careful of that person, he's a known **swindler** in our area."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging tapat, totoo, at naaayon sa katotohanan o realidad.
etymology: Pinagsamang `pagka-` (katangian ng) at `makatotohanan` (makatotohanan), na mula sa ugat na `totoo`.
original_explanation: Ito yung quality ng kaibigan mong walang preno, sasabihin niya sa'yo na 'di bagay sa'yo yang damit mo. It's the anti-Marites quality—based on facts, not on 'sabi-sabi'. Sa art, ito yung painting na mukhang picture, o yung pelikula na sobrang relatable ang mga eksena, parang buhay mo. No filter, just pure, unadulterated 'sakit pero totoo.'
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa katangian ng isang tao (pagiging tapat) o sa kalidad ng isang likhang sining o kwento (realismo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinuri ng mga kritiko ang **pagkamakatotohanan** ng pelikula.","translation":"The critics praised the **realism** of the film."},{"sentence":"Kahit masakit, kailangan nating harapin ang **pagkamakatotohanan** ng sitwasyon.","translation":"Even if it hurts, we need to face the **truthfulness** of the situation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtutupi o pag-aayos ng isang bagay na malambot o manipis, tulad ng damit, kumot, o papel, sa pamamagitan ng pagpapatong ng isang bahagi sa ibabaw ng isa pa.
original_explanation: The household chore that separates the truly organized from the rest of us who just stuff everything into the closet. Also what you do to a secret note before passing it in class. "Anak, bago ka mag-ML, tulungan mo muna akong maglupi ng mga damit."
usage_notes: General term for folding soft or flat items. 'Itiklop' is a close synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong ka bang **maglupi** ng bed sheet na may garter?","translation":"Do you know how to **fold** a fitted sheet?"},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos mamalantsa, kailangan nang **maglupi** ng mga damit.","translation":"After ironing, it's time to **fold** the clothes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bansa at kontinente na matatagpuan sa Oceania, kilala sa mga natatanging hayop nito tulad ng kangaroo at koala.
original_explanation: The land down under, or as many Pinoys call it, 'Aus-SIE'. It's the dream destination for many Filipino professionals seeking better opportunities, or just a really, really big island with kangaroos and guys who say 'mate'. Also, home to Chris Hemsworth, which is a significant national resource.
usage_notes: Often pronounced /os-TRAL-ya/. The demonym is 'Australyano' (male) or 'Australyana' (female).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipino ang nangangarap na magtrabaho sa **Australia**.","translation":"Many Filipinos dream of working in **Australia**."},{"sentence":"Nakita mo ba yung mga kangaroo noong nagbakasyon ka sa **Australia**?","translation":"Did you see the kangaroos when you vacationed in **Australia**?"}]

translation: to become weak, to languish, to become listless
meaning_filipino: Ang paghina ng katawan, sigla, o ng isang gawain; ang pagkawala ng enerhiya o kasiglahan.
original_explanation: That feeling after a 12-hour shift plus OT. You're like a phone battery at 1%. That's you, 'tumamlay'. It also applies to the economy or sales. 'Biglang tumamlay ang benta pagkatapos ng Pasko' (Sales suddenly weakened after Christmas).
usage_notes: Used for people's energy, emotions, or for abstract concepts like business or a party.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumamlay** ang kanyang katawan matapos ang mahabang pagkakasakit.","translation":"His body **became weak** after a long illness."},{"sentence":"Nang umalis ang pinakamagaling na mang-aawit, **tumamlay** ang kasiyahan sa party.","translation":"When the best singer left, the energy at the party **fizzled out**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakahuli sa isang serye o pagkakasunod-sunod; ang sukdulan o wakas.
etymology: Reduplication of the root `tapos` with `ka-` and `-an` affixes, indicating an intensified or ultimate state of 'end'.
original_explanation: This is the 'at the very, very, VERY end' end. It's not just the end, it's the *ultimate* end. Yung katapus-tapusan mong sahod bago mag-Pasko. Yung katapus-tapusan na episode ng favorite K-drama mo. It adds a sense of finality and drama.
usage_notes: Used to emphasize the finality of something, often with a sense of gravity or importance. It's a stronger version of 'huli' or 'wakas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **katapus-tapusan** ng lahat, pamilya pa rin ang ating babalikan.","translation":"At the **very end** of it all, family is still what we return to."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang **katapus-tapusan** na babala ko sa iyo.","translation":"This is my **final** warning to you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagkaalala sa isang bagay, impormasyon, o gawain na dapat sanang natatandaan.
original_explanation: "Sorry, nalimutan ko." — The most overused but sometimes true excuse in the Philippines. Ito yung dahilan kung bakit ka bumalik sa bahay kasi naiwan mo wallet mo, o kung bakit single ka pa rin (charot!). The opposite of 'tandaan'.
usage_notes: Past tense of 'malimutan'. Very common verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasensya na, **nalimutan** kong may usapan pala tayo ngayon.","translation":"I'm sorry, I **forgot** that we had an appointment today."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong sabihing **nalimutan** mo na naman ang birthday ko!","translation":"Don't tell me you **forgot** my birthday again!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng baril na may umiikot na silindro (cylinder) na naglalaman ng mga bala.
original_explanation: Yung baril na madalas mong makita sa mga action movie ni FPJ. Hindi ito 'yung kailangan mong i-slide para magkarga ng bala sa chamber; iikot lang 'yung gitna. Parang 'yung puso mong paulit-ulit na nasasaktan, pero sige pa rin.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga baril, krimen, o sa mga pelikulang aksyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatago sa ilalim ng unan ang luma niyang **revolver**.","translation":"His old **revolver** was hidden under the pillow."},{"sentence":"Inimbestigahan ng pulisya ang **revolver** na nakuha sa crime scene.","translation":"The police investigated the **revolver** found at the crime scene."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaigting na anyo ng 'sobra' na nagpapahiwatig ng sukdulang kalabisan o kasaganaan na higit pa sa inaasahan o katanggap-tanggap.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'sobra'. This is 'sobra' on steroids. Ito yung level ng handaan sa fiesta na isang barangay ang kayang pakainin. Ito rin yung drama level ng kaibigan mong umiiyak dahil lang na-seen zoned. It's extra, extra, read all about it!
usage_notes: Used to emphasize an extreme excess, much more intense than 'sobra'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sobra-sobra** ang pagkaing inihanda niya para sa Pasko.","translation":"She prepared an **exceeding** amount of food for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal na ipinapakita niya ay **sobra-sobra**.","translation":"The love he/she shows is **superabundant**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o legal na gawain ng pagkupkop at pag-aalaga sa isang bata na hindi sariling anak, at pagbibigay dito ng lahat ng karapatan ng isang tunay na anak.
etymology: From root `ampon` (to adopt). The `pag-` prefix and reduplication of the first vowel `a` create a noun meaning 'the act of...'.
original_explanation: This is when you legally (or sometimes, informally) take in a child, a pet, or even a friend's plant that they can't take care of anymore. It's like saying "I choose you!" but with more paperwork and lifelong commitment. Think of it as adding a new member to your team, but the team is your family.
usage_notes: Often used in legal, social, and familial contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-aampon** ay isang marangal na paraan upang magbigay ng pamilya sa isang ulila.","translation":"**Adoption** is a noble way to give a family to an orphan."},{"sentence":"Pinag-iisipan nilang mabuti ang proseso ng **pag-aampon**.","translation":"They are carefully considering the process of **adoption**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pamahalaan kung saan ang kapangyarihan ay hawak ng isang pinuno o maliit na grupo na namumuno nang may kalupitan at walang pagsasaalang-alang sa batas o karapatan ng mamamayan.
original_explanation: Ito yung ultimate "because I said so" ng gobyerno. Isipin mo 'yung boss mong micro-manager, pero sa scale ng buong bansa. Walang democracy, walang "sana all," puro "sumunod ka na lang." Parang group project na isa lang ang nasusunod, at laging mali pa.
usage_notes: Ang "tirania" ay isang alternatibong baybay na hindi na gaanong ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-aalsa ng mga tao ay bunga ng matagal na **tiraniya** ng diktador.","translation":"The people's uprising was a result of the dictator's long-standing **tyranny**."},{"sentence":"Kinokondena ng buong mundo ang **tiraniya** sa bansang iyon.","translation":"The whole world condemns the **tyranny** in that country."}]

translation: to be compatible with (often regarding medicine, food, or environment)
meaning_filipino: Ang maging angkop, kaayon, o mabuti ang epekto sa isang tao, partikular na tumutukoy sa pagkain, gamot, klima, o kapaligiran.
original_explanation: This is the Pinoy version of "vibing with" something, but for your body. When a new skincare product doesn't give you breakouts, "hiyang ka." When you move to a new place and you don't get sick, "hiyang ka sa lugar." It's your body's way of giving a thumbs-up. If not, "hindi ka hiyang," and it's back to the drawing board (or the Mercury Drug).
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of health and well-being. It implies a sense of suitability or positive reaction between a person and an external factor. Often used in the negative form "hindi hiyang".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **mahiyang** sa akin ang bagong sabon na binili ko.","translation":"I hope the new soap I bought will be **compatible with** my skin."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya **nahiyang** sa klima sa Canada kaya bumalik siya sa Pilipinas.","translation":"He was not **compatible with** the climate in Canada, so he returned to the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa "non-player character." Tumutukoy sa mga tauhan sa isang laro na hindi kontrolado ng isang manlalaro. Sa kolokyal na gamit, isang taong kumikilos na parang walang sariling pag-iisip o paulit-ulit ang sinasabi.
etymology: Acronym from the English gaming term "non-player character".
original_explanation: Acronym for "Non-Player Character." Originally a gaming term for characters you can't control. Now, it's a meme-level insult for someone who seems to be running on a script, has no original thoughts, or just blends into the background. Yung kaklase mong laging "Present po, ma'am" lang ang ambag sa buong sem? Baka **npc** 'yun.
usage_notes: Used in gaming, internet culture, and as a modern slang term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kausapin mo 'yung **npc** sa tindahan para makuha ang susunod na quest.","translation":"Talk to the **NPC** in the shop to get the next quest."},{"sentence":"Para siyang **npc**, paulit-ulit lang ang kuwento niya.","translation":"He's like an **NPC**, he just repeats his stories."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw o pagyanig ng isang bagay na dati ay matatag dahil sa kawalan ng paninimbang.
original_explanation: That mini-heart attack when the monobloc chair you're sitting on suddenly shifts. 'Umuga' is when something stable becomes unstable. It could be a wobbly table, a loose tooth, or even your conviction when faced with a tempting offer. 'Umuga ang desisyon ko.' (My decision wavered.)
usage_notes: This is the actor-focus, completed aspect form. 'Umuga ang ngipin' (The tooth became loose).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umuga** ang mesa nang sandalan mo ito.","translation":"The table **wobbled** when you leaned on it."},{"sentence":"Biglang **umuga** ang gusali noong lumindol.","translation":"The building suddenly **became shaky** during the earthquake."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkakabuhol-buhol o pagkakabit-kabit ng mga bagay tulad ng sinulid, buhok, o alambre na nagiging sagabal.
original_explanation: The state of your earphones after you put them in your pocket for 0.5 seconds. It's the Christmas lights you swore you packed neatly last year. It’s also a messy love triangle—a total 'salabid' of feelings and 'resibos'.
usage_notes: Often used to describe wires, threads, or even complicated situations. Can also be used as a verb 'sumalabid' (to get tangled).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiayos ang **salabid** ng mga kable sa likod ng TV.","translation":"Please fix the **tangle** of wires behind the TV."},{"sentence":"Ang buhok niya ay puno ng **salabid** dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"Her hair is full of **tangles** because of the strong wind."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paniningil o pag-iipon ng pera, bayad, o donasyon. Ito rin ang tawag sa halaga o bagay na naipon.
original_explanation: This is the action word for 'koleksyon' (the money kind). 'Yung taga-Bumbay na dumadaan sa umaga? Nangongolekta 'yun. Yung sobre na umiikot sa simbahan? Para sa kolekta 'yun. It's the act of getting the cash.
usage_notes: Often used for church offerings, fees, or debt collection. Can be a noun (the collection itself) or a verb (to collect).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **kolekta** sa simbahan noong nakaraang Linggo.","translation":"The **collection** at church last Sunday was large."},{"sentence":"Siya ang inatasang mag-**kolekta** ng bayad sa kuryente.","translation":"He was assigned to **collect** the electricity payments."}]

translation: to ride; to get on; to board
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpasok o pag-akyat sa isang sasakyan upang maglakbay.
original_explanation: The command you hear from the bus conductor: "Sakay na, paalis na!" It's the action of getting into a vehicle, or sometimes, "getting on" a trend. "Gusto mo sumabay sa trip? Sakay na!"
usage_notes: This is the root word and imperative form. The action is more commonly expressed using conjugated forms like 'sumakay' (to ride), 'sasakay' (will ride), and 'nakasakay' (is riding/has ridden).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sakay** na sa jeep bago pa tayo iwanan,\" sigaw niya.","translation":"\"**Get on** the jeep before it leaves us,\" he shouted."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **sumakay** sa bagong roller coaster.","translation":"I want **to ride** the new roller coaster."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may pambihirang kaalaman, kasanayan, o karanasan sa isang partikular na larangan; bihasa.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'expert'. Before we had 'guro', 'master', or 'sensei', we had 'dalub'. It's that level of skill where you don't need to Google anything anymore. You ARE the Google. Ang lolo mong kayang ayusin ang kahit anong sira sa bahay? Dalub.
usage_notes: Often used as a prefix to form other words related to expertise, like `dalubhasa` (expert), `dalubwika` (linguist), `dalub-isip` (philosopher). It's rarely used on its own today.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **dalub** na manggagamot ang tumingin sa kanya.","translation":"An **expert** doctor checked on him."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging **dalub** sa isang sining ay nangangailangan ng maraming taon ng pagsasanay.","translation":"Being an **expert** in an art requires many years of practice."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos na isinagawa sa nakaraan kung saan pinagdugtong ang mga tela o iba pang materyales gamit ang sinulid at karayom.
original_explanation: This is the past tense of sewing. Your lola who fixed your ripped jeans? 'Si lola ang nanahi niyan.' This is the OG life skill before fast fashion and Shopee hauls. Knowing how to do this meant you could fix anything from a button to a broken heart... okay, maybe just the button.
usage_notes: This is the completed or past tense form of the verb 'manahi' (to sew).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **nanahi** ng sarili niyang bestida para sa pagtatapos.","translation":"She **sewed** her own dress for graduation."},{"sentence":"**Nanahi** ng butas sa medyas ang aking ina kagabi.","translation":"My mother **sewed** the hole in the sock last night."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang lukot, yupi, o kulubot; makinis at plantsado.
original_explanation: Like your life before adulting, or that one shirt you ironed perfectly for a date only for it to rain. It's the ideal state of your bedsheets, your polo shirt for a job interview, and your life plans (before reality hits).
usage_notes: Can refer to literal smoothness (fabric) or a figurative lack of problems. "Walang gusot" is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhin mong **hindi gusot** ang isusuot mong damit para sa interbyu.","translation":"Make sure the clothes you'll wear for the interview are **not wrinkled**."},{"sentence":"Sana ang buhay ko ay kasing **hindi gusot** ng bagong plantsang punda.","translation":"I wish my life were as **smooth** as a newly ironed pillowcase."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, gawain, o gamot na nagdudulot ng antok o nakatutulong sa isang tao na makatulog.
original_explanation: This is anything that makes you sleepy. It could be your professor's monotone lecture, the boring afternoon meeting, a warm glass of milk, or that 'Lo-fi beats to study/relax to' playlist. It's your secret weapon against insomnia or the unavoidable curse of the 2 PM post-lunch slump.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagbabasa ng libro ay epektibong **pampaantok** para sa akin.","translation":"Reading a book is an effective **sleep-inducer** for me."},{"sentence":"Uminom siya ng chamomile tea bilang **pampaantok**.","translation":"She drank chamomile tea as a **soporific**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga gawain na may kaugnayan sa pamamahala ng isang bansa o lugar, lalo na ang debate o hidwaan sa pagitan ng mga indibidwal o partido na may kapangyarihan o umaasang makamit ito.
original_explanation: Ah, the national sport! It's the art of running the country, or at least the art of getting elected so you *can* run the country. It’s the reason why your tito and tita are fighting on Facebook during election season. It’s a mix of public service, drama, and sometimes, a full-blown teleserye.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa agham ng pamahalaan, sining ng pamamahala, o sa madalas na magulong pagsasagawa nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mainit ang usapan tungkol sa **politika** tuwing papalapit ang eleksyon.","translation":"The discussion about **politics** gets heated whenever the election is near."}]

translation: act of parting or clearing the way
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aalis ng sagabal o pagbubukas ng daan sa pamamagitan ng kamay o anumang bagay.
etymology: pag- (prefix indicating action/process) + hawi (to part, to clear)
original_explanation: That dramatic moment in a teleserye when someone parts the curtains to reveal a secret. Or when you're trying to get through a crowded Divisoria aisle, "excuse me po," while doing the paghawi motion. It's clearing a path, whether it's through hair, tall grass, or a sea of people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang **paghawi** ng kurtina, nasilayan niya ang magandang tanawin.","translation":"With one **parting** of the curtain, she saw the beautiful view."},{"sentence":"Ang **paghawi** niya sa mga tao ay nagbigay-daan sa ambulansya.","translation":"His **clearing** of the people made way for the ambulance."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa simula o sa panimulang bahagi ng isang kaganapan, proseso, o yugto ng panahon.
original_explanation: The official phrase for 'Akala ko noon...' It's the setup for a plot twist in any chismis or life story. 'Sa una, akala ko masungit siya, 'yun pala ang kulit!' It's the 'before' in a 'before and after' comparison, whether it's about a person, a new job, or your feelings for someone.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ipakilala ang isang paunang estado o kilos na madalas ay may kaibahan sa kung ano ang nangyari sa huli.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sa una**, mahirap talaga matuto ng bagong wika, pero habang tumatagal ay gumagaling ka.","translation":"**At first**, it's really hard to learn a new language, but you get better over time."},{"sentence":"Akala ko ayos lang kami, pero 'yun pala ay **sa una** lang masaya.","translation":"I thought we were okay, but it turns out it was only happy **in the beginning**."}]

translation: to be able to return (something); to cause to return
meaning_filipino: Ang magkaroon ng kakayahang isauli ang isang bagay; ang maging dahilan upang ang isang tao o bagay ay bumalik.
original_explanation: When you lend money to a friend and you actually get it back. Wow, na-mapabalik mo! Also, the feeling when your ex wants to get back together. 'Sinusubukan niya akong mapabalik sa kanya.' Good luck with that.
usage_notes: Can refer to returning a physical object, or causing a person/situation to revert to a previous state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **napabalik** ko na rin ang librong hiniram ko sa library.","translation":"Finally, I was **able to return** the book I borrowed from the library."},{"sentence":"Hindi na natin siya **mapapabalik** dahil masaya na siya sa iba.","translation":"We can't **make** him **return** anymore because he's already happy with someone else."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang organismo na nabubuhay sa o sa loob ng ibang organismo (ang host) at nakikinabang sa pamamagitan ng pagkuha ng sustansya mula rito, na kadalasang nagdudulot ng pinsala sa host. Ito ay kolokyal na baybay ng 'parasito'.
etymology: Mula sa kolokyal na pagbaybay ng salitang Ingles na 'parasite'.
original_explanation: This is the Tagalized spelling of 'parasite,' but it sounds more like something your tita would say when she's talking about your cousin's new 'friend' who's always borrowing money. 'Ay nako, 'yang si Junjun, may bagong parasait na naman!' It's less clinical than 'parasito' and has a more gossipy, palengke vibe.
usage_notes: Ang 'parasait' ay isang kolokyal na bersyon ng 'parasito' at madalas ginagamit sa impormal na usapan upang tukuyin hindi lamang ang biyolohikal na organismo kundi pati na rin ang isang taong pabigat o palamunin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinatawag niyang **parasait** ang mga taong umaasa lang sa iba at walang ginagawa.","translation":"He calls people who just depend on others and do nothing **parasites**."},{"sentence":"May mga **parasait** sa bituka na kailangang purgahin.","translation":"There are intestinal **parasites** that need to be purged."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nakakaramdam o nagpapakita ng habag, awa, o pakikiramay sa kapwa.
original_explanation: This is the kontrabida in every teleserye. The loan shark who takes your last 20 pesos. The person who eats the last piece of pizza without asking. It's pure, cold-hearted villainy. The type of person who'd spoil the latest Marvel movie just for fun.
usage_notes: Isang mabigat na pang-uri na naglalarawan ng matinding kawalan ng habag o kunsensya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **walang-awa** na magnanakaw ay kinuha ang lahat ng kanilang ipon.","translation":"The **merciless** thief took all their savings."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang **walang-awa** na pinuno noong unang panahon.","translation":"He was known as a **ruthless** leader in ancient times."}]

meaning_filipino: Patawan ng multa o parusang pinansyal bilang kabayaran sa isang paglabag o kasalanan.
etymology: From Spanish "multa" (fine). The prefix "pag-" and suffix "-hin" create a passive verb form, meaning "to be the object of fining."
original_explanation: This is what happens when you get caught breaking a rule, especially traffic rules. The MMDA officer says, "Sir/Ma'am, ticket po." and suddenly, your budget for milk tea is gone. You're being asked to pay up for your mistake. It's the universe's way of saying, "Oops, that'll cost you."
usage_notes: This is a passive verb. The active form is "magmulta" (to fine someone). "Pagmultahin" focuses on the person receiving the fine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pinagmulta** siya ng isang libong piso dahil sa maling pagparada.","translation":"He **was fined** one thousand pesos for illegal parking."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-jaywalk kung ayaw mong **pagmultahin**.","translation":"Don't jaywalk if you don't want **to be fined**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng ang hanapbuhay ay ang paglalaba ng damit ng ibang tao.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'lavandera' (laundress), na mula sa 'lavar' (maghugas).
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood clothes-washing superhero. Before washing machines and laundromats became a thing, the 'labandera' was essential. Today, the term can also jokingly refer to the person in the household assigned to laundry duty, or even yourself when facing a mountain of dirty clothes after a long vacation. "Nag-apply ako bilang labandera sa sarili kong bahay."
usage_notes: Ang katumbas nito para sa lalaki ay 'labandero'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Sabado dumarating ang aming **labandera**.","translation":"Our **laundrywoman** comes every Saturday."}]

translation: to form a pair; to become a couple
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo ng tambalan, lalo na sa romantikong konteksto, o ang pagtatambal ng dalawang bagay na magkabagay.
etymology: From mag- (verb-forming prefix) + paris (pair), which is likely from English 'pairs'.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'shipping' a love team. When two people you've been teasing finally get together, you can say, 'Ayun, nagparis din sa wakas!' (There, they finally became a couple!). It can also be used for things, like when you find the other sock that's been missing for weeks. 'Sa wakas, nagparis na ang medyas ko!'
usage_notes: Often used for romantic couples or for items that naturally come in pairs (socks, shoes, earrings). Can be synonymous with 'magpareha' but carries a stronger connotation of a matched set or a romantic couple.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ang dalawang bida na inaasahang **magparis** sa bagong teleserye.","translation":"They are the two leads who are expected to **become a couple** in the new TV series."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong **magparis** ng sapatos na babagay sa iyong damit.","translation":"Try to **form a pair** of shoes that will match your dress."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi magkapantay sa timbang, sukat, o halaga; walang balanse.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'di-' (hindi) at salitang-ugat na 'timbang' (weight, balance).
original_explanation: That one friend who does all the work in a group project? The situation is 'di-timbang'. It's also when you're buying from the palengke and you suspect the scale is rigged. Classic 'di-timbang' scenario.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal weight or figurative balance, like in relationships or justice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **di-timbang** ang laban dahil mas marami sila.","translation":"The fight became **unequal** because there were more of them."},{"sentence":"Reklamo ng mga manggagawa ang **di-timbang** na sahod at benepisyo.","translation":"The workers complained about the **unbalanced** wages and benefits."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang karaniwan ngunit hindi pormal na pagbaybay ng salitang 'lengguwahe'. Tumutukoy sa sistema ng komunikasyon.
original_explanation: This is how most people type 'language' on Messenger. It's faster, gets the point across, and nobody's grading your spelling in a group chat (unless may friend kang grammar nazi). It's the 'pwede na 'yan' version. Madalas ding gamitin ang 'lenggwahe'.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang ngunit hindi pormal na pagbaybay. Ang mas pormal na baybay ay 'lengguwahe'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iba-iba ang **lengwahe** ng pag-ibig.","translation":"The **language** of love is diverse."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng paggawa o pagsabi ng isang bagay na may diin, bigat, o puwersa.
original_explanation: When you say something mariin, you mean it. Parang 'yung pag-sabi ng nanay mo ng "AYOKO," at alam mong final answer na 'yun. It's the opposite of half-hearted. It can be about pressure (a mariin na pagpindot) or about speech (a mariin na pagtanggi). It's emphasis with a capital E.
usage_notes: Can function as both an adjective describing a noun (e.g., 'mariing pagtanggi' - a forceful denial) or an adverb modifying a verb (e.g., 'mariin niyang sinabi' - he said it forcefully).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mariin** niyang itinanggi ang mga akusasyon laban sa kanya.","translation":"He **forcefully** denied the accusations against him."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **mariin** na pagpapatupad ng batas trapiko.","translation":"There needs to be an **emphatic** enforcement of traffic laws."}]

translation: the entire world, the whole earth
meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng lahat ng lupa sa daigdig; ang buong mundo.
original_explanation: Literally "one whole land." It's the ultimate #squadgoals for the planet. Think of it as Earth's group chat, kasama lahat ng kontinente, walang na-seen zone.
usage_notes: Often used in a grand, poetic, or formal context to refer to the entire planet or all of humanity's domain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagbabago ng klima ay isang hamon sa buong **sangkalupaan**.","translation":"Climate change is a challenge for the **entire world**."},{"sentence":"Nangarap siyang maglakbay sa iba't ibang dako ng **sangkalupaan**.","translation":"He dreamed of traveling to different parts of the **whole earth**."}]

translation: to resuscitate; to cause to regain consciousness again
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggawa ng paraan upang muling magkamalay o bumalik ang ulirat ng isang tao na nawalan nito.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'sana all bumabalik' move. It's what paramedics do, not what you try to do with your ex's feelings after you ghosted them. It's bringing someone back to the land of the living, literally. Think of it as rebooting a person who has crashed.
usage_notes: This is a very specific and somewhat formal or medical term. It's not used in everyday casual conversation. The more common term is 'buhayin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng mga doktor na **magpamalay-taong muli** sa pasyenteng naaksidente.","translation":"The doctors tried to **resuscitate** the patient who was in an accident."},{"sentence":"Isang himala ang matagumpay na pagtatangkang **magpamalay-taong muli** sa nalunod na bata.","translation":"The successful attempt to **bring the drowned child back to consciousness** was a miracle."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagsasalita o tumutugon; tahimik at walang sinasabi.
original_explanation: That awkward silence in the elevator with your boss. Or when your friend gets caught in a lie and they just stand there, unable to speak. 'Walang-imik' is the sound of 'seen-zone'. It's a silence that's louder than words, often because of shock, guilt, or 'tampo'.
usage_notes: Describes a state of silence, often implying an emotional reason behind it (e.g., anger, sadness, surprise).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanatili siyang **walang-imik** habang pinapagalitan ng kanyang ina.","translation":"She remained **silent** while being scolded by her mother."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng balita, lahat kami ay naiwang **walang-imik** sa gulat.","translation":"After the news, all of us were left **speechless** in shock."}]

translation: to oppose, to contradict, to defy
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtutol, pagkontra, o hindi pagsang-ayon sa isang utos, patakaran, o opinyon ng iba.
original_explanation: This is what you do when everyone in the group chat wants to eat at a place you hate. You become the 'kontrabida' and 'sumalansang' their choice. It's the official verb for being 'that guy' who always has a counter-argument, whether it's about politics or pineapple on pizza.
usage_notes: Commonly used in formal discussions, debates, and legal contexts. It is the more standard term compared to its variant 'sumalangsang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang senador ay **sumalansang** sa panukalang batas.","translation":"The senator **opposed** the proposed bill."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **sumalansang** sa desisyon ng nakararami.","translation":"It's difficult **to oppose** the decision of the majority."}]

translation: to be able to court; to be able to woo
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahan o pagkakataong manuyo o mamanhikan sa isang tao upang hingin ang pag-ibig nito.
original_explanation: Before DMs, there was 'panliligaw'. This is the ability to finally start the whole process of courting someone—bringing flowers, serenading (harana), or in today's world, sending good morning texts and G-Cash. "Kailan ka kaya magkakalakas ng loob na makapagligaw kay crush?"
usage_notes: The pronunciation stress on 'LI' often distinguishes it from its homonym meaning 'to mislead'. Refers to the act of romantic pursuit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi pa siya handang **makapagligaw** dahil sa pag-aaral.","translation":"He is not yet ready **to be able to court** anyone because of his studies."},{"sentence":"Sana **makapagligaw** ako sa kanya bago siya umalis papuntang probinsya.","translation":"I hope I can **get to court** her before she leaves for the province."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taimtim na pangako o sumpa, kadalasan ay may kinalaman sa relihiyon o isang malalim na personal na dedikasyon.
etymology: Hinihinalang mula sa salitang Sanskrit na `praṇata` (प्रणत), na nangangahulugang "nakayuko, masunurin".
original_explanation: This is your "Level 99 promise." Hindi lang 'to basta "promise, cross my heart." Ito 'yung pangako na may kasamang sakripisyo. 'Yung paglalakad mo sa Quiapo nang nakayapak tuwing Pista ng Nazareno? Panata 'yan. 'Yung promise mo sa sarili mong magda-diet ka na talaga this time? Panata 'yan (na laging napapako). It's a vow you make to a higher power, or to your highest self.
usage_notes: May malakas na kaugnayan sa debosyon sa relihiyon, ngunit maaari ring gamitin para sa isang seryosong personal na pangako.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Taon-taon niyang tinutupad ang kanyang **panata** sa Poong Nazareno.","translation":"Every year, he fulfills his **vow** to the Black Nazarene."},{"sentence":"Naging **panata** niya ang pagtulong sa mga batang lansangan.","translation":"Helping street children became her solemn **pledge**."}]

translation: Rice bran extract; Vitamin B supplement
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng food supplement na gawa mula sa darak ng palay (rice bran), mayaman sa Vitamin B complex, at karaniwang ibinibigay sa mga bata upang pampagana sa pagkain at panlaban sa sakit na beriberi.
etymology: Named after the brand 'Tiki-Tiki', which became a genericized trademark. The original source is 'tiki-tiki' or rice bran.
original_explanation: The legendary orange liquid that every Pinoy kid from the 80s and 90s was forced to drink. It's the 'pampagana' (appetite booster) that your mom swore by. The taste was... an acquired one. Now it's a brand, but the word **Tikitiki** itself has become synonymous with any vitamin syrup you give a kid to make them eat their veggies. It's the taste of a healthy, slightly traumatic, Filipino childhood.
usage_notes: While it is a brand name, it is widely used as a generic term for vitamin B supplements for children in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinapainom ng nanay ng **Tikitiki** ang anak niya para ganahan itong kumain.","translation":"The mother gives her child **Tikitiki** to boost his appetite."},{"sentence":"Amoy **Tikitiki** ang gamot na ito.","translation":"This medicine smells like **Tikitiki**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa halaga ng pera o yaman na inilalaan upang magsimula o palaguin ang isang negosyo o proyekto.
original_explanation: This is the 'pera' part of 'pera o bayong'. It's the money you risk to start your milk tea shop or online ukay-ukay business. When someone says 'talo ako sa puhunan,' you know their venture went south. It's the seed money you pray will grow into a money tree, not just... well, a tree.
usage_notes: Partikular na tumutukoy sa konteksto ng kapital sa negosyo o paunang pamumuhunan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kulang pa ako **sa puhunan** para masimulan ang aking pinapangarap na coffee shop.","translation":"I'm still lacking **in capital** to start my dream coffee shop."},{"sentence":"Bumalik din kaagad ang ginastos niya **sa puhunan** matapos ang isang buwan.","translation":"He quickly recovered what he spent **on the investment** after one month."}]

translation: to fumigate with incense; to perform a smoking ritual
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng ritwal ng pagpapausok, karaniwan ay gamit ang insenso, uling, at tawas, upang itaboy ang masasamang espiritu o gamutin ang isang karamdaman na pinaniniwalaang sanhi ng 'usog' o 'balis'.
original_explanation: This is the OG Filipino way of clearing bad energy, way before sage smudging became a trend. It's when your lola burns a mysterious concoction in a can to cure you from an unexplained stomach ache after a stranger complimented your cheeks. "Nang nabalis daw ang bata, pinayuhan silang magluop."
usage_notes: Strongly associated with Filipino folk medicine and superstition, particularly the concepts of 'usog' (an affliction caused by a greeting from a stranger with a strong spirit) and 'balis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan daw **magluop** para mawala ang pagod at bigat ng pakiramdam.","translation":"They say it's necessary to **perform a smoking ritual** to get rid of fatigue and a heavy feeling."},{"sentence":"Itinuro ng albularyo kung paano **magluop** gamit ang tawas at dahon ng bayabas.","translation":"The folk healer taught how to **fumigate** using alum and guava leaves."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging abala o pagkakaroon ng maraming gawain.
etymology: Phonetic spelling of the English word "busy".
original_explanation: The default status of every working adult in Manila. "Kamusta?" "Eto, bisi." It's the polite way of saying "I have no time for your chika right now." It can mean you're buried in deadlines, stuck in traffic (which is a full-time job), or just binge-watching a K-drama and don't want to be disturbed.
usage_notes: A very common, informal, and casual way to say "busy". The original English spelling "busy" is also frequently used in Taglish sentences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasensya na, **bisi** lang talaga ako ngayon.","translation":"Sorry, I'm just really **busy** right now."},{"sentence":"Lagi siyang **bisi** sa trabaho kaya hindi na nakakasama.","translation":"He's always **busy** with work so he can't join us anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daglat para sa pariralang Ingles na "On my way," na nangangahulugang "papunta na" o "parating na."
etymology: From the English acronym 'OMW' (On My Way).
original_explanation: The classic Pinoy text message excuse. 'OMW' could mean they just woke up, are still in the shower, or are actually stuck in EDSA traffic. It's the Schrodinger's cat of punctuality; you won't know if they're coming until they actually arrive. The more traditional version is 'OTW'.
usage_notes: Used almost exclusively in text messages, chats, and social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wait lang, **omw** na ako!","translation":"Wait a bit, I'm **on my way**!"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **omw** na ang inorder mong pagkain.","translation":"Don't worry, the food you ordered is **on its way**."}]

translation: to pull out; to uproot; to extract
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis o pagtanggal ng isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito sa pamamagitan ng paghila.
original_explanation: The command you give when you want something pulled out. Like telling the dentist to pull your wisdom tooth, telling your friend to pull out a grey hair, or what you do to your SIM card when you're finally upgrading your phone. Also, what you do to weeds in the garden or... "hugot" feels from your heart.
usage_notes: The object to be pulled out is the focus of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **bunutin** ang masamang damo sa hardin.","translation":"I need to **pull out** the weeds in the garden."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **bunutin** ang saksakan kung basa ang iyong kamay.","translation":"Don't **pull out** the plug if your hands are wet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ikabit ang pamatok sa isang hayop, tulad ng kalabaw o baka, upang magamit sa pag-aararo o paghila ng kariton.
original_explanation: The OG "plug and play" for carabaos. Before horsepower, there was carabao-power, and this is the verb for getting it all hooked up. It's about getting the beast of burden ready for a hard day's work in the field.
usage_notes: Primarily used in an agricultural or rural context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga pa lang ay kailangan nang **isingkaw** ang kalabaw para sa pag-aararo.","translation":"The carabao needs **to be yoked** early for plowing."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagmamahal, kabaitan, at pag-aaruga sa paraang banayad at kaiga-igaya.
original_explanation: The default setting of a Pinoy grandparent. 'Yung boses ng crush mo 'pag kausap ka niya sa phone. It's that sweet, gentle, caressing way of talking or acting that can melt anyone's heart. The opposite of 'gigil.'
usage_notes: A highly positive trait in Filipino culture, associated with showing affection and care.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang mga Pilipino sa pagiging **malambing** sa kanilang mga mahal sa buhay.","translation":"Filipinos are known for being **affectionate** towards their loved ones."},{"sentence":"May **malambing** siyang tinig na nakakakalma.","translation":"She has a **gentle** voice that is calming."}]

translation: to treat someone (in a certain way)
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pakikitungo o pagtrato sa isang tao.
original_explanation: How you act towards someone. Your mom might say, 'Huwag mong magtarato ng ganyan sa bisita!' when you're being a brat. It's about the vibe you give off. Are you treating them like a VIP or like an unskippable YouTube ad? Your 'pagtatarato' matters.
usage_notes: This word is less common now, with "trato" or "tratuin" being more frequently used. It has a slightly dated or formal feel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi maganda ang paraan ng kanyang **pagtatarato** sa mga empleyado niya.","translation":"The way he **treats** his employees is not good."},{"sentence":"Dapat kang matutong **magtarato** sa mga nakakatanda sa iyo nang may paggalang.","translation":"You should learn to **treat** your elders with respect."}]

meaning_filipino: May katangian ng pagiging manloloko; madalas gumamit ng daya o panlilinlang.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung online seller na "iPhone 15 Pro Max, ₱5,000" ang post, pero bato ang ipapadala. O 'yung kaibigan mong nangutang tapos biglang "seen" ka na lang forever. A **mapandaya** person is an expert in "budol-budol" and making you question your life choices.
usage_notes: Describes someone who is habitually or skillfully tricky and dishonest.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa mga **mapandayang** alok na nangangako ng mabilisang yaman.","translation":"Beware of **deceptive** offers that promise quick wealth."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang **mapandayang** manlalaro.","translation":"He is known as a **deceitful** player."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pasalitâ o pasulat na komunikasyon, impormasyon, o tagubilin na ipinapadala o iniiwan para sa isang tao.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'seen' pero walang reply. Yung 100+ unread chats mo sa group project. O yung 'Good morning!' text mula kay crush na bumubuo ng araw mo. A mensahe can make or break your day.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap ako ng **mensahe** mula sa aking boss kaninang umaga.","translation":"I received a **message** from my boss this morning."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang basahin ang **mensahe** ko sa'yo mamaya.","translation":"Don't forget to read the **message** I sent you later."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang bagay, kulay, o istilo na hindi bumabagay, hindi tumutugma, o hindi angkop kapag ipinares sa iba.
etymology: Mula sa "walang" (without) at dinobleng "ka-bagay" (match, something that fits).
original_explanation: Describes your outfit when you get dressed in the dark. It's polka dots with stripes, neon green with brown, socks with sandals—the ultimate fashion crime according to your stylish friend. It's when things are so out of place together, they give you a slight headache. 'Hindi terno' on a spiritual level.
usage_notes: Used for fashion, design, color combinations, or even pairing of ideas that do not go well together.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang suot niyang sapatos ay **walang-kabagay-bagay** sa kanyang damit.","translation":"The shoes she's wearing **do not match** her dress at all."},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **walang-kabagay-bagay** ang mga kulay na pinili mo para sa pader.","translation":"For me, the colors you chose for the wall are **unsuitable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang serye ng mga utos, gawain, o kaganapan na paulit-ulit na isinasagawa hanggang matugunan ang isang partikular na kondisyon o hanggang sa ito ay sadyang itigil.
original_explanation: Para sa mga programmer, ito 'yung code na ayaw mong maging infinite kasi crash ang abot mo. Sa buhay, ito 'yung paulit-ulit na cycle ng gising-trabaho-kain-tulog. Kapag sinabing, 'keep me in the loop', ibig sabihin, isama mo ako sa chismis o update. 'Stuck in a loop' ka 'teh?
usage_notes: Primarily used in technical, programming, business, or casual Taglish contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisama ako sa email **loop** para sa proyektong iyan.","translation":"Please include me in the email **loop** for that project."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating ayusin ang **loop** sa code para hindi ito mag-infinite.","translation":"We need to fix the **loop** in the code so it doesn't become infinite."}]

translation: chest, heart (as the seat of passion)
meaning_filipino: Isang makalumang salita para sa dibdib, na itinuturing na sisidlan ng matinding damdamin o dubdob.
original_explanation: This is some next-level, balagtasan-era Tagalog. Think of it as the poetic version of "chest" or "heart." It's not the physical organ, but the place where you feel that intense "dubdob" (fervor). When someone says "sa aking dubduban," they mean "in the depths of my heart/soul." It's so deep, you'd probably only hear it in a kundiman or a historical drama.
usage_notes: Extremely rare and poetic. Not used in modern conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sakit na nadarama sa kanyang **dubduban** ay hindi maipaliwanag.","translation":"The pain felt in his **heart** could not be explained."}]

translation: little by little; gradually; in installments
meaning_filipino: Sa paraang dahan-dahan, paunti-unti, o bahagi-bahagi.
etymology: Reduplication of 'utay,' which means a small piece or part.
original_explanation: How you pay for your Shopee/Lazada 'SpayLater' purchases. Or how you move on from a breakup. It's not a one-time big-time thing, but a process done in small, manageable chunks. 'Utay-utay lang ang bayad, para 'di mabigat.' It’s the philosophy of 'dahan-dahan lang, baka mapatid.'
usage_notes: Describes an action done gradually or in increments. Often used in the context of payments, consumption, or completing a task.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Utay-utay** ang pagbabayad niya sa kanyang mga utang.","translation":"He pays his debts **little by little**."},{"sentence":"Mas maganda kung **utay-utay** ang pag-aaral para sa exam, hindi 'yung biglaan.","translation":"It's better to study for the exam **gradually**, not all at once."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging madaling makalusot, makatakas, o makaiwas sa mga hadlang, responsibilidad, o kaparusahan.
etymology: From `pagka-` (quality of being) + `malusutin` (prone to slipping through).
original_explanation: This is the skill of that office-mate who always manages to avoid work. It's the "diskarte" of a driver weaving through impossible traffic. It can also describe a corrupt official who always gets away with it, like an eel covered in grease. The human equivalent of a "ninja move".
usage_notes: Often has a connotation of cunning, trickery, or being evasive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang pulitiko sa kanyang **pagkamalusutin** sa mga kontrobersiya.","translation":"The politician is known for his **elusiveness** in controversies."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pagkamalusutin**, hindi siya nahuli ng mga guwardiya.","translation":"Because of his **slipperiness**, he wasn't caught by the guards."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mamayani, mangibabaw, o magpakita ng higit na kapangyarihan o galing kaysa sa iba sa isang partikular na larangan o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling when your Mobile Legends team, which was losing badly, suddenly makes a comeback and wipes out the enemy. That's you, 'dumomina'. It's the Pinoy version of 'pwnage' or 'beast mode'.
usage_notes: Commonly used in contexts of competition like sports, video games, or even business.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Duminomina** ng Gilas Pilipinas ang huling quarter ng laban.","translation":"Gilas Pilipinas **dominated** the final quarter of the match."},{"sentence":"Sa simula ay mahiyain siya, ngunit sa huli ay **duminomina** ang kanyang talento sa pagkanta.","translation":"At first she was shy, but in the end her singing talent **dominated**."}]

translation: to clear out; to scoop out everything
meaning_filipino: Ganap na alisin o kunin ang lahat ng laman ng isang sisidlan o lugar.
original_explanation: Imagine a buffet and you're the last one in line. The person before you just committed a **limasin** on the Lechon Kawali tray. They took everything, leaving you with nothing but the sad little bits of fried garlic. It’s the act of emptying something completely, whether it’s a pot of adobo or someone's bank account.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa konteksto ng pag-ubos ng laman, pagkain, o pera.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **limasin** ang ulam, magtira ka para sa iba.","translation":"Don't **scoop out all** the food, leave some for the others."},{"sentence":"**Limasin** mo ang tubig sa baha gamit ang balde.","translation":"**Clear out** the floodwater using the bucket."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga bituin na bumubuo ng isang padron o hugis sa kalangitan; maaari ding tumukoy sa kabuuan ng mga bituin.
etymology: From "ka-" + "bituin" (star) + "-an", meaning a collection or place of stars.
original_explanation: What you see when you're feeling poetic or romantic, looking up at the night sky outside the city. It's the OG light show before Netflix and chill. Also, the title of your crush's IG photo dump when they go to Baguio or the province.
usage_notes: A more poetic or literary term for "mga bituin" (stars) or a constellation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagandang pagmasdan ang **kabituinan** sa gabing walang ulap.","translation":"It's so beautiful to watch the **starry sky** on a cloudless night."},{"sentence":"Itinuro niya sa akin ang iba't ibang **kabituinan** tulad ng Orion.","translation":"He pointed out to me the different **constellations** like Orion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang harang, pader, o balakid na yari sa mga pinagpatong-patong na bato.
original_explanation: Basically a wall made of rocks. Think of it as the original 'firewall' or the 'seen zone' in chat—a barrier you can't easily get past. In politics, it's the 'pader' between the government and the people's demands.
usage_notes: Not a very common word; 'pader na bato' (wall of stone) is more frequently used. This word is more descriptive and poetic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtayo sila ng **batuharang** upang protektahan ang kanilang mga tanim.","translation":"They built a **stone barrier** to protect their crops."},{"sentence":"Ang matandang **batuharang** ay gumuho na dahil sa lindol.","translation":"The old **stone wall** has collapsed due to the earthquake."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na pantawag sa isang babaeng kamag-anak na kapatid ng magulang o asawa nito; ginagamit din bilang pormal na titulo na sinusundan ng pangalan. Ito ang anyong Espanyol ng 'tiya' o 'tita'.
original_explanation: The more formal, 'hacienda' version of 'Tita'. You use Tia when referring to your rich grand-aunt who lives in an ancestral house and probably has a Spanish surname. It's like 'Tita' but with old money vibes. 'Tita' goes to the mall; 'Tia' manages the family lands.
usage_notes: Often used before a name (e.g., Tia Maria). It is less common in everyday conversation than 'Tita' but is prevalent in literature, formal contexts, and among families with Spanish heritage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga alahas na ito ay pamana pa ni **Tia** Corazon.","translation":"These jewels are an inheritance from **Aunt** Corazon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na madalas kasama, kausap, o nakakasalamuha sa mga sosyal na pagtitipon o sa pang-araw-araw na buhay.
etymology: From `ka-` + `halubilo` (mingling, socializing). The origin of `halubilo` itself is uncertain but is related to `halo` (mix).
original_explanation: This is your 'kain-tayo-sa-labas' buddy, your 'chismis' partner in the office pantry, or the people you make small talk with at a party. It's anyone you mingle with. If you're an introvert, just thinking about having too many 'kahalubilo' can drain your social battery. The verb form, 'makihalubilo', is what your mom tells you to do at family reunions instead of just staring at your phone.
usage_notes: Often used in the plural form `mga kahalubilo`. The verb `makihalubilo` (to mingle, to socialize) is more commonly used than the noun form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang makipag-usap sa kanyang mga **kahalubilo** sa trabaho.","translation":"He likes to talk with his **associates** at work."},{"sentence":"Iwasan mo ang masasamang **kahalubilo**.","translation":"Avoid bad **company** (people you socialize with)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap o pautos na paraan upang ipagawa sa iba ang pagpindot sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay isang buton o switch.
etymology: From the root word 'pindot' (press) and the prefix 'pa-', which indicates a request or command to have the action done by someone else.
original_explanation: The official word for "Can you press the button for me?" Used when you're too lazy to get up and turn on the fan, when your hands are full and you need someone to press the elevator button, or when you're in a jeepney and need to pass your fare. "Manong, papindot po ng para."
usage_notes: This is a command or request form, often used in the phrase 'papindot po'. It functions as a verb in a request structure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay mo na rin 'to sa Shopee cart ko, **papindot** na lang ng 'place order'.","translation":"Please add this to my Shopee cart, just **press** 'place order' for me."},{"sentence":"Anak, **papindot** nga ng remote, palitan mo ang channel.","translation":"Child, please **press** the remote for me, change the channel."}]

translation: to hiss or whistle at each other (to get attention)
meaning_filipino: Sabay-sabay o palitan na gumawa ng tunog na "psst" upang tawagin ang pansin ng isa't isa, kadalasan nang patago o hindi pormal.
original_explanation: The group chat before group chats existed. It's the sound of multiple people going "Psst! Psst!" to each other across a classroom to pass a secret message, or what your titas do in the palengke to call each other without shouting. It's a symphony of subtle, attention-grabbing hisses.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix implies a reciprocal or group action. The base verb 'sumitsit' is to hiss at one person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magsitsitan** ang mga estudyante nang pumasok ang kanilang crush sa silid-aralan.","translation":"The students started **hissing at one another** when their crush entered the classroom."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong **magsitsitan** dito, nasa simbahan tayo.","translation":"Don't **hiss at each other** here, we're in a church."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamahalagang gampanin o karakter sa isang dula, pelikula, o anumang sitwasyon.
etymology: Kombinasyon ng "pangunahin" (primary) at "papel" (role, mula sa Espanyol na 'papel').
original_explanation: This is the 'bida' in the teleserye of life or work. It's the person who has the most lines, the most screen time, and the most drama. In a group project, it's the person who ends up doing most of the work but also gets the most credit (or blame).
usage_notes: Ang 'papel' dito ay nangangahulugang 'role', hindi 'paper'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang gumanap sa **pangunahing papel** sa bagong pelikula.","translation":"She played the **lead role** in the new movie."},{"sentence":"Ano ang iyong **pangunahing papel** sa proyektong ito?","translation":"What is your **main role** in this project?"}]

meaning_filipino: Mayroon o tinubuan ng amag; isang uri ng fungus na karaniwang tumutubo sa mga nabubulok o basang bagay.
original_explanation: That sad moment when you reach for the loaf of bread in your pantry only to find it has green, blue, or black spots. It's the science experiment growing in the Tupperware you forgot in your office drawer for two weeks. Basically, it's the universe telling you, 'Huwag mo nang kainin 'yan, bes.'
usage_notes: Used to describe food, walls, clothes, or any object that has developed mold.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itapon mo na ang tinapay na iyan dahil **maamag** na.","translation":"Throw away that bread because it's already **moldy**."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng problema sa **maamag** na pader dahil sa palaging pagtagas ng tubig.","translation":"There was a problem with the **moldy** wall because of the constant water leak."}]
