meaning_filipino: Isang pansamantalang istrukturang yari sa metal o kahoy na ginagamit ng mga manggagawa sa konstruksiyon upang maabot ang matataas na bahagi ng isang gusali.
original_explanation: That metal jungle gym you see on the side of buildings under construction. It's the BPO agent's view from the 25th floor, watching construction workers who are probably braver than most of us.
usage_notes: The root word 'andamyo' is also used to mean the same thing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat na umakyat ang karpintero sa **andamyuhan**.","translation":"The carpenter carefully climbed the **scaffolding**."},{"sentence":"Naglagay sila ng **andamyuhan** sa paligid ng simbahan para sa pagkukumpuni.","translation":"They put up **scaffolding** around the church for repairs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng paglalahad o pagpapakita ng katangian, anyo, o kalikasan ng isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari sa pamamagitan ng salita o sining.
original_explanation: This is how something or someone is painted, literally or figuratively. Think of how your friend describes their ex (the villain edit), how a movie portrays a historical hero, or how you describe yourself on your dating profile vs. reality. It's all about the spin, the angle, the *pagkakalarawan*.
usage_notes: Refers to the way something is represented or described.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi sumang-ayon ang mga kritiko sa **pagkakalarawan** sa bida sa pelikula.","translation":"The critics did not agree with the **portrayal** of the protagonist in the film."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **pagkakalarawan** ng makata sa kanyang tula.","translation":"The poet's **depiction** in his poem is beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sapilitang kontribusyong pinansyal na ipinapataw ng isang pamahalaan sa mga indibidwal o korporasyon upang mapondohan ang mga gastusin ng estado.
original_explanation: The thing you pay every April 15th that makes you question all your life choices. It's the government's subscription fee for 'citizenship'. You know, for roads, public schools, and... other things. "Yung sweldo ko, parang dumaan lang para magbayad ng taks at bills."
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, often used interchangeably with 'buwis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang binabawas na **taks** sa sahod ng mga empleyado.","translation":"A large amount of **tax** is deducted from the employees' salaries."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang mag-file ng iyong income **taks** return.","translation":"Don't forget to file your income **tax** return."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing mas malaki ang isang bagay; alagaan at arugain ang isang bata hanggang sa ito'y lumaki.
original_explanation: The command form of 'making something bigger.' This can be your muscles at the gym, your budget for Shopee, or your role in your company. It's also what your parents did for you, which they'll remind you of every time you forget to wash the dishes. 'Pinalaki kita nang maayos!'
usage_notes: Can refer to physical size, abstract concepts (like a problem), or raising a living being.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Palakihin** mo ang litratong ito para mas makita natin.","translation":"**Enlarge** this photo so we can see it better."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **palakihin** ang isang anak nang nag-iisa.","translation":"It's hard **to raise** a child alone."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na nahaluan na o nalagyan na ng timpla at handa nang ihain o gamitin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'templado' (tempered, mixed).
original_explanation: The state of being 'just right'. Your 3-in-1 coffee is 'timplado' right out of the sachet. When the sinigang is perfectly sour, it's 'timplado'. It means the work is done, ready to serve, no more adjustments needed.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na dumaan na sa proseso ng pagtitimpla.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Timplado** na ang juice, kaya puwede nang inumin.","translation":"The juice is already **mixed**, so it's ready to drink."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang manok na **timplado** na bago iluto.","translation":"I prefer chicken that is already **seasoned** before cooking."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o sitwasyon na nakatanggap ng biyaya, pabor, o kabutihan, karaniwan mula sa Diyos o sa mabuting kapalaran.
original_explanation: That feeling when you get the last piece of chicken joy. When the universe conspires in your favor, from finding a 20-peso bill in your old jeans to getting your leave approved. The ultimate hashtag for any good thing that happens. #Blessed. #Pinagpala.
usage_notes: Commonly used in religious or spiritual contexts, but also widely used in a secular way to mean 'lucky' or 'fortunate'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **pinagpala** ako dahil sa aking mapagmahal na pamilya.","translation":"I feel **blessed** because of my loving family."},{"sentence":"Isang **pinagpala**ng araw ang hatid ng magandang panahon.","translation":"The good weather brings a **blessed** day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng materyal na madaling magliyab o masunog kapag nadarang sa apoy o matinding init.
etymology: From Tagalog "takaw" (greedy) and "apoy" (fire), literally "greedy for fire".
original_explanation: Like your patience during super heavy traffic on EDSA on a payday Friday. One wrong move, and you'll explode. These are materials that love drama and will literally catch fire at the slightest provocation.
usage_notes: Used to describe materials like gasoline, paper, or dry wood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paggamit ng mga bagay na **takaw-apoy** malapit sa kalan.","translation":"Be careful when using **flammable** items near the stove."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon na humihikayat sa isang indibidwal na gumawa ng isang bagay na mali, imoral, o hindi kanais-nais.
original_explanation: That extra cup of milk tea even when you're over budget. That 'one last episode' on Netflix at 2 AM. That piece of chismis you don't want to hear but you're listening to anyway. That's 'tukso'. It's the universe testing your self-control, and most of the time, the universe wins.
usage_notes: Can also be a verb: 'tuksuhin' (to tempt someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan mo ang **tukso** para hindi ka magkasala.","translation":"Avoid **temptation** so you won't commit a sin."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkain ng matatamis ang aking malaking **tukso**.","translation":"Eating sweets is my biggest **temptation**."}]

translation: something used for sweeping; a broom
meaning_filipino: Anumang kagamitan, karaniwan ay isang walis, na ginagamit sa paglilinis o pag-aalis ng dumi sa sahig.
original_explanation: This is your weapon of choice against dust bunnies and your younger sibling's mess. It could be the classic walis tingting for the yard or the walis tambo for inside the house. Before vacuum cleaners, this was the OG cleaning tech.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa mismong walis o gamitin sa mas pangkalahatang paraan para ilarawan ang anumang gamit sa pagwawalis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **pangwalis** at linisin mo ang kalat sa sahig.","translation":"Get a **broom** and clean the mess on the floor."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang isang karton bilang pansamantalang **pangwalis**.","translation":"He used a piece of cardboard as a temporary tool **for sweeping**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtanggi, hindi pagsang-ayon, o pag-urong sa isang gawain o kasunduan. Ito ay nasa pangkasalukuyang anyo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na 'ayaw' (dislike, don't want) at panlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're about to finish a tough project and your body or brain just says 'nope.' 'Ayoko na, umaayaw na ako!' It's the process of giving up, backing out, or simply saying no. It's the verb form of that 'ayaw ko na' hugot.
usage_notes: Anyong pangkasalukuyan ng pandiwang 'umayaw'. Ipinahihiwatig nito ang pagbabago ng isip mula sa paggusto o paggawa ng isang bagay patungo sa hindi na paggusto o paggawa nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **umaayaw** agad, malapit na nating matapos.","translation":"Don't **quit** just yet, we're almost finished."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pinakamataas na antas o digri ng isang katangian. Sa balarila, ito ang anyo ng pang-uri o pang-abay na nagpapakita ng pinakasukdulang katangian (hal. pinakamataas, pinakamabilis).
original_explanation: This is the 'extra' level of description. Not just 'maganda' (beautiful), not just 'mas maganda' (more beautiful), but 'PINAKAmaganda' (most beautiful). It's the language of hype, marketing, and your proud tita describing her favorite pamangkin. 'You are the best-est!' is a very superlatibo (and grammatically questionable) statement.
usage_notes: Used both as a noun ('ang superlatibo') to refer to the concept or the word form, and as an adjective ('antas na superlatibo') to describe the superlative degree. In Tagalog grammar, this is achieved with the prefix 'pinaka-'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'pinakamabait' ay isang halimbawa ng pang-uring nasa anyong **superlatibo**.","translation":"'Pinakamabait' (kindest) is an example of an adjective in the **superlative** form."},{"sentence":"Puro **superlatibo** ang ginamit niyang salita para ilarawan ang kanyang karanasan.","translation":"He used purely **superlatives** to describe his experience."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, salik, o pangyayari na nagiging sanhi ng paglala o pagiging mas malubha ng isang sitwasyon, kalagayan, o karamdaman.
original_explanation: The complete opposite of a solution. This is when you try to 'fix' something but only make it worse. Pouring water on a grease fire, telling someone to 'calm down' when they're angry, or adding more utang to pay for existing utang. It's the 'panggatong sa apoy'—the fuel to the fire.
usage_notes: The antonym of `pampabuti` (something that improves).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagpupuyat ay **pampalubha** ng sakit.","translation":"Staying up late **worsens** an illness."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang magsalita, **pampalubha** lang 'yan ng sitwasyon.","translation":"Don't talk anymore, that will only **aggravate** the situation."}]

translation: to pretend to be angry; to feign anger
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapanggap o pagpapakita ng galit na hindi naman tunay na nararamdaman.
original_explanation: This is your friend's 'galit' when you forget to buy them pasalubong. It's not real anger, just drama for effect. It's that performance you put on for your parents when they tell you to wash the dishes, even though you were going to do it anyway. The 'galit' is more for show, like a teleserye kontrabida practicing in the mirror.
usage_notes: The suffix '-galitan' comes from the reduplication of 'galit' and the suffix '-an', which often implies a simulated or playful action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maggalit-galitan** diyan, alam kong natutuwa ka sa sorpresa namin.","translation":"Don't **pretend to be angry**, I know you're happy with our surprise."}]

translation: You're just kidding; You're being difficult
meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang balbal na nagsasabing ang isang tao ay nagbibiro, nagpapalusot, o gumagawa ng hindi makatwirang bagay.
etymology: A common construction from the slang word "eme" and the pronoun "ka" (you).
original_explanation: The "Girl, stop" or "You're too much" of Pinoy slang. You say "eme ka" when your friend is being extra dramatic, telling a wild story, or just generally being a handful. It's a playful way to call someone out on their BS. "Ayaw mo sumama? Eme ka! Kanina lang sabi mo game ka." (You don't want to come? You're being difficult! You just said you were game a while ago.)
usage_notes: The tone can range from playful teasing to genuine annoyance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Diet ka raw pero umorder ka ng extra rice? **Eme ka**!","translation":"You said you're on a diet but you ordered extra rice? **You're kidding me**!"},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang mag-**eme ka** diyan, sabihin mo na ang totoo.","translation":"Stop **being difficult** over there, just tell the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o grupo na pormal na sinampahan ng kaso o pinagbibintangan ng isang krimen o pagkakasala.
original_explanation: Ito yung tao sa korte na nakaupo sa "hot seat," pinagpapawisan habang tinatanong ng abogado. Sila yung laging laman ng "24 Oras" o "TV Patrol" na may takip sa mukha. Tandaan: "innocent until proven guilty," pero sa mata ng mga chismosa, guilty na agad.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa kontekstong legal at pormal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumangging magbigay ng pahayag ang **akusado** sa korte.","translation":"The **accused** refused to give a statement in court."},{"sentence":"Ang **akusado** ay nahaharap sa kasong pagnanakaw.","translation":"The **defendant** is facing theft charges."}]

meaning_filipino: Gaganap ng isang laro o aktibidad para sa libangan o kumpetisyon. Ito ay nasa aspetong panghinaharap ng pandiwa.
original_explanation: Future tense of 'play'. This is what your friend says when you ask them to hang out, but they have a Valorant tournament to attend. "Sorry, pre, maglalaro ako ng Valo mamaya." It's the ultimate excuse for both kids and adults.
usage_notes: This is the future tense form of the verb 'maglaro'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maglalaro** kami ng basketball sa Sabado.","translation":"We **will play** basketball on Saturday."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **maglalaro** mamaya sa finals?","translation":"Who **will play** in the finals later?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapad na piraso ng matibay na tela na ikinakabit sa palo ng isang bangka o barko upang saluhin ang hangin at magbigay-tulak dito.
original_explanation: Ito yung parang kumot ng barko na nagpapaandar sa kanya bago pa nauso ang de-makinang sasakyang pandagat. Sa life, minsan kailangan mo lang itaas ang 'layag' mo at magtiwala kung saan ka dadalhin ng hangin ng tadhana. #BahalaNaSiBatman
usage_notes: Can also be used metaphorically to mean journey or adventure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinaas ng mga mangingisda ang **layag** upang simulan ang kanilang paglalakbay.","translation":"The fishermen raised the **sail** to begin their journey."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay ay isang mahabang paglalakbay na may sarili nitong **layag**.","translation":"Life is a long journey with its own **sail**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim na hukay sa lupa na pinagkukunan ng tubig, na kadalasa'y hindi umaasa sa makina.
original_explanation: Think of this as the original source of *marites*—the village well where everyone gathers to get water and spill the tea. Before office water coolers, there was the *balong*. It's the OG social media feed of the barrio.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga tagpuang rural o probinsiyal. Naiiba sa 'poso' na karaniwang may mekanikal na bomba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng isang timbang tubig sa **balong**.","translation":"Fetch a pail of water from the **deep well**."},{"sentence":"Malinaw at malamig ang tubig mula sa aming **balong** sa probinsya.","translation":"The water from our **well** in the province is clear and cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kulay na nasa pagitan ng pula at bughaw; lila.
original_explanation: It's the Spanish-derived word for purple, making it sound a bit more *alta* than the more common "lila" or the English "purple". You'd use "murado" to describe the color of an expensive gown, a fancy wine, or maybe the color of the sky during a really dramatic sunset. It's the color of royalty, or at least the color of ube everything.
usage_notes: Less common than 'lila' in everyday conversation but understood. Often appears in literature or when describing specific shades.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang obispo ay nakasuot ng **murado** na abito.","translation":"The bishop was wearing a **purple** robe."},{"sentence":"Pininturahan niya ang kanyang kuko ng kulay **murado**.","translation":"She painted her nails a **purple** color."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghabol o pagtugis sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
etymology: From `pang-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `ha-` + `hagad` (chase). This `pang-` + reduplication form often indicates an intense or repeated action.
original_explanation: This is the official term for what you do when the GrabFood driver is 'nearby' but you see his little motorcycle icon going in the opposite direction on the map. It's the frantic **panghahagad** to catch the last jeepney at night, or chasing after your dreams (or your crush who just left you on 'seen').
usage_notes: Describes the action or process of chasing, often with a sense of urgency or persistence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napagod ang aso sa **panghahagad** sa pusa sa buong bakuran.","translation":"The dog got tired from **chasing** the cat all over the yard."},{"sentence":"Ang **panghahagad** ng hustisya ay isang mahabang proseso.","translation":"The **pursuit** of justice is a long process."}]

translation: to crash into; to cause to collide
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbangga nang may puwersa ng isang bagay sa iba.
original_explanation: Like when you're rushing to beat the red light and another car does the same thing. What happens next? 'Yan ang pag-isalpok. It's the action of making something forcefully collide with another, whether it's a car, your head against the wall after seeing your bills, or your cart into someone else's at the grocery.
usage_notes: The 'i-' prefix here makes the object being moved to collide the focus of the sentence. For example, 'Isalpok mo ang kotse' means '(You) crash the car'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **isalpok** ang sasakyan sa pader!","translation":"Don't **crash** the car into the wall!"},{"sentence":"Sinadyang **isalpok** ng tsuper ang bus para maiwasan ang mas malaking sakuna.","translation":"The driver intentionally **crashed** the bus to avoid a bigger disaster."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng alinlangan o kawalan ng tiwala sa isang tao, bagay, o pahayag.
original_explanation: When your friend says "On the way na ako" but you know they're still in the shower. O kapag 'yung jowa mo biglang naging extra sweet for no reason. It's that gut feeling, that "parang may mali" vibe. The opposite of "tiwala lang, bes."
usage_notes: A verb directed at an object or person. 'Magduda' is the actor-focus form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagdudahan** ang kanyang katapatan dahil lang sa mga sabi-sabi.","translation":"Don't **doubt** his loyalty just because of rumors."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula niyang **pagdudahan** ang alok na trabaho nang hingan siya ng pera.","translation":"He started **to doubt** the job offer when they asked him for money."}]

meaning_filipino: Manipis na patak ng tubig na namumuo sa mga ibabaw ng bagay sa labas, karaniwan tuwing gabi o madaling-araw dahil sa paglamig ng hangin.
original_explanation: The 'aircon ng kalikasan' that settles on leaves and car windshields early in the morning. It's the reason your shoes get wet when you walk on the grass at 5 AM. In hugot terms, it's like a past relationship: cold, disappears when the sun comes out, and makes things a little blurry.
usage_notes: Can also refer to a light mist or fog. 'Mahamog' is the adjective form, meaning 'dewy' or 'misty'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng umaga na may **hamog** pa sa mga dahon ng halaman.","translation":"The morning is beautiful with **dew** still on the leaves of the plants."},{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan sa pagmamaneho dahil makapal ang **hamog** sa daan.","translation":"Drive slowly because the **mist** on the road is thick."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na alpombra o basahan na inilalagay sa sahig sa may pinto upang pagpagisan o pagpunasan ng sapatos bago pumasok.
original_explanation: The thing you step on before entering a house. Usually says "Welcome" but has seen more dirt than your group chat history. In the Philippines, this is where you leave your tsinelas before going inside.
usage_notes: Ang katutubong katumbas ay "basahan sa pinto" o "pahiran ng paa".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipagpag mo ang tsinelas mo sa **doormat** bago ka pumasok.","translation":"Wipe your slippers on the **doormat** before you come in."},{"sentence":"Bagong bili ang **doormat** kaya huwag mong dudumihan.","translation":"The **doormat** is newly bought so don't get it dirty."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng lason o anumang sangkap na maaaring makapinsala o pumatay kapag kinain, nasinghot, o nahawakan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'nakaka-' at salitang-ugat na 'lason'.
original_explanation: Can be literal, like a snake's venom or spoiled food. But more often used today for a 'toxic' person, a bad relationship, or a stressful work environment. 'Umalis ka na diyan, girl, nakakalason 'yang jowa mo!'
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa literal na kahulugan para sa lason at sa makabagong-pananalita para sa 'toxic' na relasyon o kapaligiran.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kainin ang kabuteng iyan, baka **nakakalason**.","translation":"Don't eat that mushroom, it might be **poisonous**."},{"sentence":"Ang tsismis ay isang **nakakalason** na ugali sa opisina.","translation":"Gossip is a **toxic** habit in the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang grupo o bunton ng mga bagay na magkakasamang nakasalansan o nakakumpol.
original_explanation: Like that 'tumpok' of laundry in the corner of your room that's slowly becoming a new roommate. Or the 'tumpok' of unwashed dishes in the sink judging you. In the palengke, it's a small pile of veggies or fruits sold for a fixed price, like "isang tumpok ng sili, sampung piso."
usage_notes: Often seen in markets (palengke) to describe small piles of produce sold together for a fixed price.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng isang **tumpok** ng kamatis sa palengke.","translation":"I bought a **pile** of tomatoes at the market."},{"sentence":"May isang malaking **tumpok** ng mga damit na kailangan labhan.","translation":"There is a big **heap** of clothes that need to be washed."}]

translation: the state of being stretched or pulled taut
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging mahigpit na nahila o naunat, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa mga kalamnan o materyales.
original_explanation: This is that feeling when you've been sitting in a jeepney for too long and you finally stand up. Your muscles are all tight. Or it's how a rubber band feels right before it snaps. It's the state of being fully stretched, literally 'pulled'.
usage_notes: Refers to the physical state of tension or being stretched.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **pagkabatak** ng mga kalamnan sa kanyang likod matapos magbuhat ng mabigat.","translation":"He felt the **stretching/tightness** of the muscles in his back after lifting something heavy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar ng libangan na may mga larong pinapatakbo ng barya o token, tulad ng mga video game, redemption game, at iba pang elektromekanikal na laro.
original_explanation: The happiest place on Earth for 90s kids. The land of Timezone, World of Fun, and Glico's. It's where you blew your entire 'baon' on tokens to play Street Fighter, Dance Dance Revolution, or that basketball shooting game to win tickets for a cheap plastic toy. The sound of an arcade is the official soundtrack of Filipino childhoods.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the amusement center, not the architectural feature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **arcade** mamaya pagkatapos ng klase.","translation":"Let's meet at the **arcade** later after class."},{"sentence":"Naubos ko ang pera ko sa paglalaro ng Tekken sa **arcade**.","translation":"I spent all my money playing Tekken at the **arcade**."}]

meaning_filipino: Kunin o sipsipin ang pera o yaman mula sa isang tao o institusyon.
original_explanation: Same family as 'huthutan', but this one focuses on the *thing* being taken. "Hinuthot niya lahat ng pera sa kaban ng bayan." It's the action of taking the cash, the goods, the inheritance. It's the verb for what the corrupt politician does to the national budget.
usage_notes: The object of this verb is the money or item being extorted. Contrast with 'huthutan' where the object is the person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano nilang **huthutin** ang lahat ng ipon ng matanda.","translation":"They plan to **extort** all the old man's savings."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **huthutin** ang iyong pinaghirapan.","translation":"Don't let them **siphon off** your hard-earned money."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikipag-usap o pag-aalay ng panalangin sa isang itinuturing na diyos o mas mataas na kapangyarihan.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + `dasal` (prayer), which is from Spanish 'rezar' (to pray).
original_explanation: Your direct line to The One Above. It's what you do before a major exam, when you're stuck in EDSA traffic and late for work, or when your crush finally messages you. The ultimate 'sana' and 'please' moment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagdarasal** araw-araw ay bahagi ng kanilang buhay.","translation":"**Praying** daily is part of their life."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutan ang **pagdarasal** bago kumain.","translation":"Don't forget the **prayer** before eating."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ruta, landas, o kalye na maaaring lakaran o pagbiyahean ng mga sasakyan at tao.
original_explanation: The thing you complain about every day because of traffic. It can be the literal 'kalsada' full of potholes, or the metaphorical 'daan' ng buhay mo na puno ng 'hugot' at challenges. Also, the reason why Waze is your best friend.
usage_notes: Pronounced /da-AN/ with the stress on the second syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maluwag ba ang **daan** sa EDSA ngayon?","translation":"Is the **road** on EDSA clear now?"},{"sentence":"Lahat tayo ay may kanya-kanyang **daan** na tinatahak sa buhay.","translation":"We all have our own **path** to follow in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Mayaman sa o nababalutan ng langis; madulas dahil sa langis.
original_explanation: Your face after a long, humid commute. The lechon kawali you know is bad for you but eat anyway. The feeling of your hair on the second day of not showering. Also used to describe a "slimy" person—someone who's overly smooth and insincere, like a B-movie villain.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal (pagkain, balat) o sa matalinghagang paraan (pagkatao).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong kumain ng pagkaing masyadong **malangis**.","translation":"I don't like to eat food that is too **oily**."},{"sentence":"May **malangis** siyang ngiti na hindi ko magustuhan.","translation":"He has a **greasy** (smarmy) smile that I don't like."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi ganap na lumaki o umunlad; bansot; pandak dahil sa kakulangan sa nutrisyon o sakit.
original_explanation: Yung halaman mong alagang-alaga mo pero ayaw pa ring tumangkad, parang 'yung career mo. O kaya 'yung ka-gym mo na laging nagbubuhat pero hindi lumalaki ang muscles. That's mabunsol. It's the physical manifestation of 'potential not realized.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe plants, animals, or sometimes people who are small for their age or kind.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **mabunsol** ang paglaki ng mga pananim dahil sa matinding tagtuyot.","translation":"The growth of the crops became **stunted** due to the severe drought."},{"sentence":"Kahit **mabunsol** ang aso, malakas naman itong tumahol.","translation":"Even if the dog is **underdeveloped**, it barks loudly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, lalo na isang istraktura, na itinayo upang magsilbing paalala sa isang tao o kaganapan.
etymology: Hispanized spelling of English 'memorial', or directly from Spanish 'memorial'.
original_explanation: Ito ang Tagalized version ng 'memorial'. Pareho lang sila ng meaning. Parang "Jollibee" vs "Jollibee's". Ito yung word na gagamitin ng lolo mo, while "memorial" is what you'd see on the insurance paper. Example: Rizal Monument is a memoryal to our national hero.
usage_notes: This is a direct synonym of 'memorial' but with a more localized spelling and pronunciation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Bantayog ng mga Bayani ay isang **memoryal** para sa mga biktima ng Martial Law.","translation":"The Bantayog ng mga Bayani is a **memorial** for the victims of Martial Law."},{"sentence":"Nag-aalay sila ng bulaklak sa **memoryal** tuwing anibersaryo ng kanyang pagkamatay.","translation":"They offer flowers at the **memorial** every anniversary of his death."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na uri ng kutsilyo, karaniwang ginagamit sa pagbabalat ng prutas, pagtasa ng lapis, o iba pang maliliit na gawain.
original_explanation: Your lolo's favorite tool for everything. Need to open a box? Kampit. Need to peel a mango? Kampit. Need to fix something small? Kampit. It's the original, low-tech Swiss army knife of the Pinoy household.
usage_notes: Generally refers to a small, single-edged blade, often used for general utility purposes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **kampit** para balatan ang mangga.","translation":"He used the **small knife** to peel the mango."},{"sentence":"Laging may dalang **kampit** ang karpintero sa kanyang bulsa.","translation":"The carpenter always carries a **utility knife** in his pocket."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na lugar, espasyo, o lokasyon.
original_explanation: The more formal, almost poetic, cousin of 'lugar'. You use this when you want to sound a bit more serious or dramatic. 'This place will be our new home' is 'Ito ang magiging bago nating tirahan.' But 'This sacred site...' is 'Ang banal na pook na ito...'. See the difference? It adds a little gravitas.
usage_notes: Often used in compound nouns like 'pook-pasyalan' (tourist spot) or 'pook-dasalan' (place of worship).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Luneta Park ay isang makasaysayang **pook** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Luneta Park is a historical **site** in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Maraming magagandang **pook**-pasyalan sa probinsya ng Palawan.","translation":"There are many beautiful tourist **spots** in the province of Palawan."}]

translation: to make equal; to be tied (in a game)
meaning_filipino: Maging magkapantay o magkapareho sa bilang, puntos, o katayuan; maging tabla.
original_explanation: In basketball, this is when the underdog team hits a buzzer-beater to tie the game, and the crowd goes wild. In life, it's when you finally earn enough to be on the same level as your 'frenemy'. It means to make things even-steven, whether it's a score, a debt, or a social standing. 'Quits na tayo.'
usage_notes: Commonly used in sports and competitions. Can also be used for settling debts or disputes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa huling segundo ng laro, **pumatas** ang iskor kaya nagkaroon ng overtime.","translation":"In the last second of the game, the score was **tied**, so they went into overtime."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong magbayad para **pumatas** ang utang mo sa akin.","translation":"You need to pay so your debt to me will be **made equal** (settled)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang itinakdang panahon o huling araw para sa pagtupad ng isang gawain, pagbabayad, o anumang obligasyon.
original_explanation: This is the BPO agent's and student's mortal enemy. It's the deadline breathing down your neck. The "due date" for your Meralco bill. That terrifying moment when the client says, "I need this EOD." It's the ultimate 'pampastress' but also the ultimate motivator for a 'Pinoy-style' cramming session.
usage_notes: The root 'taning' means a set period or term. 'Taningan' is the endpoint of that period.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **taningan** sa pagpasa ng ating proyekto?","translation":"What is the **deadline** for submitting our project?"},{"sentence":"Binigyan kami ng isang linggong **taningan** para bayaran ang utang.","translation":"We were given a one-week **time limit** to pay the debt."}]

meaning_filipino: Tutungo sa isang lugar o direksyon nang walang pagliko o paghinto.
etymology: From 'diretso', which is from Spanish 'derecho'. The 'di-' is a reduplication of the first syllable of the root to indicate future tense.
original_explanation: The future tense of "going straight ahead." It's what you tell the taxi driver when you don't want any detours. It's also your game plan after a long day at work: "Uwi na ako, didiretso na sa kama." No side trips, no extra drama, just straight to the goal.
usage_notes: Future tense of the verb 'dumiretso'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagbaba mo ng bus, **didiretso** ka lang sa kalyeng iyon.","translation":"After you get off the bus, you **will go straight** down that street."},{"sentence":"Hindi na ako sasama sa kanila, **didiretso** na ako pauwi.","translation":"I won't join them anymore, I **will go straight** home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng mabilis na pag-ikot sa sariling aksis; pagpihit nang paikot.
etymology: From `pag-` (nominalizer) + `ikod` (spin, twirl). A less common synonym for `ikot`.
original_explanation: This is what a ballerina does on stage. It's what you do when you're dizzy ('nahihilo'). It's the celebratory twirl when you wear a new dress. While `pag-ikit` is orbiting around something, `pag-ikod` is spinning in place, like a spinning top (trumpo).
usage_notes: More specific than `pag-ikot`. It emphasizes a fast, repeated spinning motion on an axis. It is a common word in Visayan languages for 'turn' or 'spin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humanga ang lahat sa bilis ng **pag-ikod** ng mananayaw.","translation":"Everyone was amazed at the speed of the dancer's **spinning**."}]

translation: to aim at; to point at (a weapon)
meaning_filipino: Itutok ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay sandata o anumang maaaring makapanakit, sa isang direksyon o target.
original_explanation: This is what a movie 'kontrabida' does before delivering his evil monologue. He'll **iumang** his baril at the hero. On a less dramatic note, it's what you do with a water gun during a summer outing, aiming it at your unsuspecting friend. "Ready, aim, fire!" is "Handa, iumang, putok!"
usage_notes: Typically implies pointing something with the intent to threaten or attack.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat nang **iumang** ng magnanakaw ang patalim sa biktima.","translation":"Everyone was shocked when the robber **aimed** the blade at the victim."},{"sentence":"**Iniumang** niya ang kanyang kamao, handang sumuntok.","translation":"He **aimed** his fist, ready to punch."}]

translation: to be hit on target; to get it right (by chance)
meaning_filipino: Aksidenteng matamaan o matumbok ang isang bagay. Maaari ring mangahulugang maging tama o wasto nang hindi inaasahan.
etymology: ma- (unintentional/ability prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + tama (hit, correct)
original_explanation: This is the feeling of accidentally guessing the correct answer on a multiple-choice exam. "Hula lang 'yun, pero napatama ko!" Or when you throw a balled-up piece of paper towards the trash can from across the room and it goes in. It’s that lucky shot, the unintentional bullseye. Can also be used for being physically hit: "Ingat, baka mapatama ka ng bola."
usage_notes: Can mean a physical hit or getting something correct by chance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya sinadyang **mapatama** ang bola sa bintana.","translation":"He didn't mean to **hit** the window with the ball."},{"sentence":"Nanghuhula lang ako sa lotto, pero sino'ng nakakaalam, baka **mapatama** ko ang jackpot.","translation":"I'm just guessing on the lotto, but who knows, I might **get it right** and hit the jackpot."}]

translation: of the same level, equal to
meaning_filipino: May parehong antas, sukat, o halaga.
original_explanation: The goal of every 'sana all' comment. When you see your friend's travel pics and you're stuck in traffic, you wish your life was kapantay theirs. Also, the reason why you split the bill down to the last centavo with your friends. #FairIsFair
usage_notes: Can also function as a noun meaning 'an equal'. For example, 'Wala siyang kapantay' (He/She has no equal).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang pagmamahal niya sa kanyang mga anak ay **kapantay**.","translation":"For her, her love for her children is **equal**."},{"sentence":"Nagsisikap siyang maging **kapantay** ng kaniyang mga kapatid sa tagumpay.","translation":"He strives to be **of the same level** as his siblings in success."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdadala ng isang bagay, tao, o mensahe sa isang tiyak na lugar o patutunguhan.
etymology: From 'hatid' (deliver, escort). 'Pag-ha-hatid' is the noun form for the act of delivering.
original_explanation: This is the job of your Grab/Lalamove rider. It's also what you do for your crush, 'hatid-sundo' style. It's basically moving something or someone from Point A to Point B, whether it's your Shopee parcel, a pizza, or your younger sibling to school.
usage_notes: Common in daily life. 'Ihatid' is the more common verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang serbisyo ng **paghahatid** ng pagkain ay napakapopular ngayon.","translation":"Food **delivery** service is very popular nowadays."},{"sentence":"Ang **paghahatid** sa huling hantungan ay isang malungkot na sandali.","translation":"The **escorting** to the final resting place is a sad moment."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, lugar, o konsepto na may kaugnayan sa dagat. Sa kasaysayan, ito rin ay isang uri ng larong patula.
original_explanation: 'Dagatan' is the adjective form of 'dagat'. So 'yamang-dagatan' is marine resources. But wait, there's more! Historically, it's also a poetic game/debate held during a wake, kinda like a pre-colonial rap battle to honor the dead. So it's either about fish or about spitting bars. Wild.
usage_notes: As an adjective, it modifies nouns (e.g., 'buhay-dagatan' - marine life). The noun form referring to the poetic joust is archaic and mostly found in literature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayaman ang Pilipinas sa mga likas na yamang-**dagatan**.","translation":"The Philippines is rich in **marine** natural resources."},{"sentence":"Ang **dagatan** ay isang tradisyonal na laro ng tula na isinasagawa sa mga lamay.","translation":"The **dagatan** is a traditional poetic game performed at wakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, kumpanya, o entidad na gumagawa ng mga produkto sa malakihang paraan, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng makinarya sa isang pabrika.
original_explanation: The big boss of the factory, the one who makes the stuff we buy. Think of the name on the tag of your shirt or the logo on your phone—the 'pabrikante' is the company behind it. They're the source, the 'gumawa' on a massive, industrial scale.
usage_notes: Often used in business or industrial contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **pabrikante** ng bagong kotse na ito?","translation":"Who is the **manufacturer** of this new car?"},{"sentence":"Direktang umorder sa **pabrikante** para mas makamura.","translation":"Order directly from the **manufacturer** to get a lower price."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagkilos o pag-uugali na ipinapakita sa publiko na hindi tumutugma sa tunay na nararamdaman o intensyon; pagkukunwari.
etymology: Mula sa "pakita" (to show) + "tao" (person/people). Literal na "para makita ng tao."
original_explanation: This is when you're super nice to your tita in person, but you're complaining about her in the family group chat. It's putting on a "good person" mask for public consumption. Basically, plastic ka, girl. It’s all about keeping up appearances, even if deep down, you're rolling your eyes.
usage_notes: Nagtataglay ng malakas na negatibong konotasyon ng kawalan ng sinseridad at pagiging ipokrito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagiging matulungin niya ay **pakitang-tao** lang pala.","translation":"His helpfulness turned out to be just **for show**."},{"sentence":"Sawa na ako sa mga pulitikong puro **pakitang-tao**.","translation":"I'm tired of politicians who are all **hypocritical**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalok, pagbibigay, o pagtanggap ng anumang bagay na may halaga upang maimpluwensyahan ang kilos ng isang tao na nasa posisyon ng kapangyarihan o tiwala, karaniwan ay isang opisyal ng pamahalaan.
original_explanation: This is the formal, 'pang-abogado' term for 'lagay' or 'suhol'. You'd hear this in a courtroom drama or a Senate hearing, not sa pakikipag-usap sa traffic enforcer. It's 'suhol' wearing a barong.
usage_notes: This is a formal and legal term. The more common, colloquial words are 'suhol' and 'lagay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahaharap siya sa kasong **soborno** matapos tanggapin ang pera mula sa kontratista.","translation":"He is facing a **subornation** case after accepting money from the contractor."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtanggap ng **soborno** ay isang malubhang krimen.","translation":"Accepting a **bribe** is a serious crime."}]

translation: to come from, to originate from
meaning_filipino: Tumukoy sa pinagmulan o pinanggalingan ng isang bagay, tao, o ideya.
original_explanation: This is the 'provenance' verb. Where did that chismis come from? 'Saan nanggaling 'yan?' Where are you from? 'Saan ka nanggaling?' It's about tracing something back to its source, whether it's a package from Shopee, a brilliant idea, or your messy ex who suddenly reappeared.
usage_notes: The form 'nanggaling' (past/perfect tense) is extremely common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang balitang iyan ay **manggaling** dapat sa isang mapagkakatiwalaang source.","translation":"That news should **come from** a trustworthy source."},{"sentence":"Saan ka ba **nanggaling** at basang-basa ka ng ulan?","translation":"Where did you **come from** that you're soaked from the rain?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paggawa ng isang bagay upang maging sanhi ng paninibugho o selos sa isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pangkauusalan na "pa-" at salitang-ugat na "panibugho".
original_explanation: Ito yung "mag-post ka ng picture kasama ex mo" move para lang mag-react si current. The act of intentionally poking the jealousy bear. It's petty, it's drama, and it's surprisingly effective.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang pangkauusalan (causative verb), na nangangahulugang nagiging sanhi ito para maramdaman ng ibang tao ang emosyon ng salitang-ugat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **papanibughuin** sa pamamagitan ng pagbanggit sa pangalan niya.","translation":"Don't try to **make me jealous** by mentioning their name."},{"sentence":"Sinadya niyang **papanibughuin** ang kanyang asawa para malaman kung may pakialam pa ito.","translation":"She intentionally tried to **make her husband jealous** to see if he still cared."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang di-pangkaraniwan at kamangha-manghang pangyayari na sinasabing gawa ng isang higit-sa-natural na kapangyarihan o hindi maipaliwanag ng siyensya.
original_explanation: That moment your Grab driver arrives in 2 minutes during rush hour. Or when your internet is stable during a typhoon. Or when your crush replies to your IG story. It's the universe saying, 'Sige na nga, para sa'yo 'to.'
usage_notes: This is a less common noun form. More commonly, people would say 'pagkakaroon ng himala' (having a miracle).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang paggaling ay isang tunay na **paghimalaan**.","translation":"His recovery was a true **occurrence of a miracle**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na sukat ng lupa, na kadalasang tumutukoy sa isang teritoryo, bansa, o pag-aari.
original_explanation: This is 'lupa' but on a grander scale. It’s not just a patch of dirt; it's a whole territory. Think 'Game of Thrones' but in the Philippines – ang lupain ng mga Reyes. It can be your ancestral land in the province or the entire "land of the free" (tinubuang lupain). It has a sense of ownership and belonging.
usage_notes: More formal and expansive than `lupa`. Often used to refer to a nation (e.g., `sinilangang lupain` - motherland) or a large estate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipagtatanggol namin ang aming minanang **lupain**.","translation":"We will defend our inherited **land**."},{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ang aking sinilangang **lupain**.","translation":"The Philippines is my native **land**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biro o nakakatawang komento; maaari ring tumukoy sa paraan, sistema, o pamamaraan ng paggawa ng isang bagay.
etymology: From Spanish "chiste" (joke). The meaning evolved in Filipino to also include 'system' or 'method'.
original_explanation: This word is a multi-tool. It can mean a joke or a punchline ('Ano'ng siste doon?'). It can also mean the 'system' or 'the way things work'. When you finally figure out the 'siste' of the MRT queue, you've unlocked a life skill. It's the 'how-to' or the 'hack' of a situation.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context. 'Walang siste' can mean 'not funny' or 'ineffective/disorganized'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko nakuha ang **siste** ng biro niya kanina.","translation":"I didn't get the **punchline** of his joke earlier."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong alamin ang **siste** ng pag-commute sa EDSA para hindi ka ma-late.","translation":"You need to learn the **system** of commuting on EDSA so you won't be late."}]

translation: to treat someone to a burger
meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na pandiwa na nangangahulugang manlibre ng burger sa isang tao.
etymology: From the slang causative prefix `pa-` (to treat someone) and the English loanword `burger`.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino peace offering or celebratory move. "Sorry na, **paburger** ako." or "Nanalo ako sa raffle, **paburger** kayo!" It's a portmanteau of 'pa-' (the prefix for treating someone) and 'burger'. Simple, effective, and delicious.
usage_notes: This is a very common slang construction. You can replace 'burger' with almost anything: 'pakape' (treat to coffee), 'pa-ice-cream', 'pashanghai' (treat to lumpia shanghai).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paburger** ka naman, birthday mo!","translation":"**Treat us to burgers**, it's your birthday!"},{"sentence":"Kung papasa ka sa exam, **paburger** ako sa'yo.","translation":"If you pass the exam, **I'll treat you to a burger**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang akda, tulad ng libro o pelikula, na batay sa sariling karanasan o buhay ng may-akda.
original_explanation: When a movie, song, or book is basically a thinly veiled chismis about the creator's own life. It's the artist's way of saying, "This is my story, deal with it." Think of it as a public diary entry that gets published.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming naniniwala na ang nobela ay isang akdang **awtobiyograpiko**.","translation":"Many believe that the novel is an **autobiographical** work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtungo sa isang lugar sa pamamagitan ng paglalakad; ang paggamit ng mga paa sa paggalaw mula sa isang pook patungo sa iba. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang lugar na madalas lakaran.
original_explanation: This is the verb form for when you and your barkada decide to walk somewhere, maybe because walang masakyan or you're just saving pamasahe. "Tara, lakaran na lang natin papuntang 7-Eleven!" It can also mean the place you walk *on*, like a path.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin bilang utos o mungkahi. Maaari ring gumana bilang pangngalan na nangangahulugang 'isang lugar para sa paglalakad' o 'isang kaganapan sa paglalakad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malapit lang ang palengke, kaya nating **lakaran**.","translation":"The market is just nearby, we can **walk to it**."},{"sentence":"Ginawang **lakaran** ng mga tao ang bagong tayong tulay.","translation":"The newly built bridge became a **walkway** for the people."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng palaman o laman ang loob ng isang pagkain, karaniwan bago lutuin.
original_explanation: The verb form of making your food extra. Think of that glorious Rellenong Bangus or chicken. It's the process of taking something, emptying it out, and then stuffing it with a more delicious, flavorful mix. It’s like giving your food an internal upgrade.
usage_notes: The noun form is 'relyeno' (stuffing). 'Relyinuhin' is a common misspelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasarap **relyenuhin** ang manok ng giniling na may pasas.","translation":"It's delicious to **stuff** the chicken with ground meat and raisins."},{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **relyenuhin** itong bangus para sa Noche Buena.","translation":"Help me **stuff** this milkfish for Christmas Eve dinner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang metal na may tulis o gulong na may ngipin na ikinakabit sa takong ng bota ng isang mangangabayo upang udyukan ang kabayo. Ginagamit din sa anyo ng tari para sa mga panabong na manok.
original_explanation: These are the sharp, pointy things you attach to your boots to tell your horse "G!" or, more commonly in the Philippines, the deadly blades attached to a fighting cock's leg in a *sabong*. It’s the original “pampabilis ng kilos,” but for animals.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of horse riding or cockfighting (sabong).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinabit ng sabungero ang matalim na **espuwelas** sa kanyang manok.","translation":"The cockfighter attached the sharp **spurs** to his rooster."}]

translation: to get entangled; to be intertwined
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging magkakabuhol-buhol o magkapulupot ng mga bagay tulad ng sinulid, alambre, o buhok.
original_explanation: Your earphones in your pocket. That's it. That's the explanation. It's when things get hopelessly tangled, like a messy love triangle or the Christmas lights you swore you packed neatly last year. Ayusin mo 'yang mga wire, baka **magkasalabid**.
usage_notes: Describes the state of being tangled. The more intense version is 'magkasala-salabid'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiinis ako kapag **nagkasalabid** ang earphones sa loob ng bag ko.","translation":"I get annoyed when my earphones **get entangled** inside my bag."},{"sentence":"Maaaring **magkasalabid** ang mga kuwento ng buhay natin sa hindi inaasahang paraan.","translation":"The stories of our lives can **become intertwined** in unexpected ways."}]

meaning_filipino: Butasan ang isang bagay gamit ang barena o balbike.
etymology: From "barena" (drill), which is from Spanish "barrena" (auger, drill).
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa ng karpintero para makagawa ng butas sa pader o kahoy, hindi lang para sa picture frame mo, kundi para sa chismis na gustong makalusot. 'Barenahan' is to make a hole, literally for construction, figuratively for getting info.
usage_notes: The root word 'barena' means drill. The suffix '-an' makes it a verb to perform the action on an object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Barenahan** mo ang pader para maisabit natin itong salamin.","translation":"**Drill a hole in** the wall so we can hang this mirror."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pagtingin sa paligid sa paraang tila may hinahanap, aligaga, o nag-iingat.
original_explanation: This is you in a crowded mall during a 12.12 sale, desperately looking for a specific shop. It's also the "Hala, nasaan na si Mama?" panic look of a child in SM. Or when you're late for a meeting and you're scanning the coffee shop for your boss, hoping they haven't seen you yet.
usage_notes: Describes a state of being restless, anxious, or searching.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Palinga-linga** ang magnanakaw habang naghahanap ng kanyang bibiktimahin.","translation":"The thief was **looking around furtively** while searching for his next victim."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka **palinga-linga** diyan? May hinahanap ka ba?","translation":"Why are you **glancing about**? Are you looking for something?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may likas na kagandahang-loob, matulungin sa kapwa, at handang magbigay ng tulong o donasyon nang walang hinihintay na kapalit.
etymology: From 'mapag-' (prefix indicating inclination or fondness for) + 'kawanggawa' (charity, from 'kawang' meaning flock/group and 'gawa' meaning work).
original_explanation: This is your tita who's always organizing a fundraising drive for a cause, or your friend who can't say no to a street kid selling sampaguita. They have a big heart and an open wallet for those in need. Sila yung laging 'for a cause' ang status sa FB.
usage_notes: Often used to describe individuals or organizations dedicated to social welfare.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang kanilang pamilya sa pagiging **mapagkawanggawa** sa kanilang komunidad.","translation":"Their family is known for being **charitable** in their community."},{"sentence":"Isang **mapagkawanggawa** na negosyante ang nag-donate ng mga computer sa aming paaralan.","translation":"A **philanthropic** businessman donated computers to our school."}]

translation: to have someone herd or shepherd
meaning_filipino: Utos o pakiusap na pangalagaan at bantayan ang isang kawan ng hayop, tulad ng tupa o kambing.
original_explanation: Like telling your eldest cousin to watch over the younger, rowdier kids at a family gathering. You're not just babysitting, you're *herding*. Can also be used for your chaotic friend group when you assign one responsible friend to keep everyone together.
usage_notes: Derived from the Spanish word 'pastor' meaning shepherd.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **ipastol** ang mga kambing sa mas luntiang bahagi ng bukid.","translation":"You need to **have** the goats **herded** to the greener part of the field."}]

translation: to belch out; to burp out
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalabas ng hangin mula sa tiyan patungo sa bibig, na karaniwang may kasamang tunog.
original_explanation: That sound you make after chugging a whole bottle of Coke. It's the verb for burping something out. In some cultures, it's a sign of a satisfying meal. In others, it's what your tita tells you not to do at the dinner table ("Huy, 'wag kang dumighal dito!").
usage_notes: The more common verb form is 'dumighal' (to burp, intransitive). 'Idighal' is transitive, meaning 'to belch out (something)'. For example, 'idighal ang hangin' (to belch out the air).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **maidighal** niya ang kinain niyang mansanas sa sobrang busog.","translation":"He almost **burped out** the apple he ate from being too full."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos uminom ng soft drinks, mahirap pigilang hindi **dumighal**.","translation":"After drinking soft drinks, it's hard to stop yourself from **burping**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang halagang kailangang bayaran para sa isang produkto o serbisyo; o ang mismong akto ng paghingi ng bayad sa isang utang.
original_explanation: The most terrifying notification you can receive, second only to "we need to talk." Whether it's the Meralco bill, your credit card statement after a shopping spree, or a text from a friend saying, "Bes, 'yung utang mo," the **singil** is the adult world's constant, scary reminder that nothing is free.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating na ang **singil** sa kuryente at tubig ngayong buwan.","translation":"The **bill** for electricity and water arrived this month."},{"sentence":"Nakakahiya man, kailangan kong gawin ang **singil** sa mga utang sa akin.","translation":"Even if it's embarrassing, I need to do the **collection** for the debts owed to me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyoma para sa isang lugar na napakaliblib, hindi kilala, o mahirap hanapin.
original_explanation: This is how your tita describes the province she grew up in, a place Waze and Google Maps would surrender to find. "Saan 'yan?" "Wala sa mapa!" It’s the ultimate hidden gem, a place so remote it doesn’t exist in the digital world, only in stories and memories.
usage_notes: Isang idyomatikong ekspresyon para sa isang napakalayo o hindi kilalang lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang baryo nila ay halos **wala sa mapa** sa sobrang layo.","translation":"Their village is practically **not on the map** because it's so far away."},{"sentence":"Nagtayo sila ng resort sa isang islang **wala sa mapa**.","translation":"They built a resort on an **obscure** island."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng pagiging magkasosyo; isang samahan o kumpanya na binuo ng dalawa o higit pang indibidwal bilang mga kasosyo.
original_explanation: This is the official name for your business with your 'sosyo'. It's the legal entity, the "partnership" itself. It's what you register with the DTI. More formal than just saying 'yung negosyo namin.' "Itinayo namin ang sosyuhan noong isang taon."
usage_notes: Isang mas pormal at legal na termino sa negosyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa hindi pagkakasundo, napagdesisyunan nilang buwagin ang kanilang **sosyuhan**.","translation":"Due to disagreements, they decided to dissolve their **partnership**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagak ng kaukulang halaga o ari-arian sa hukuman bilang garantiya para sa pansamantalang paglaya ng isang akusado.
original_explanation: That scene in every Pinoy action movie where the hero's sidekick gets arrested and the bida has to scramble for cash. To 'magpiyansa' is to pay the court to get someone out of jail temporarily. It's basically a super expensive 'get out of jail free' card that you still have to pay for.
usage_notes: Strictly a legal term. The amount is set by the court.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng kanyang pamilya na maghanap ng pera para siya ay makapag-**piyansa**.","translation":"His family tried to find money so he could **post bail**."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya maaaring **magpiyansa** dahil mabigat ang kasong isinampa laban sa kanya.","translation":"He cannot **post bail** because the case filed against him is a serious one."}]

translation: to cause to become pale or faded
meaning_filipino: Gawing maputla, kupas, o lipas ang kulay ng isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa 'pa-' + 'mughaw' + hulaping '-in'. Ang 'pughaw' ay nangangahulugang maputla.
original_explanation: That thing the sun does to your dark-colored shirts when you leave them out to dry for too long. It's also what happens to your enthusiasm for your job after a few years, or the 'kilig' in a long-term relationship if you don't work on it. The color just... drains away.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang medyo bihirang salita. Ang 'kupasin' o 'paputlain' ay mas karaniwang mga kasingkahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong ibilad sa araw ang damit at baka ito ay **pamughawin**.","translation":"Don't leave the clothes under the sun or it might **cause them to fade**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakakahawang sakit, lalo na sa mga bata, na sanhi ng isang virus at nagdudulot ng lagnat at pulang pantal sa balat.
original_explanation: The OG childhood illness that every Lola warns you about. Before COVID, this was the virus that made moms panic. It's the reason you got those shots as a baby. Getting it means no playing outside and lots of soup.
usage_notes: The medical term for the disease.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang bakuna upang maiwasan ang sakit na **tigdas**.","translation":"Vaccination is important to prevent the disease **measles**."},{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa ospital dahil sa mataas na lagnat na dulot ng **tigdas**.","translation":"He was taken to the hospital due to a high fever caused by **measles**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging bahagi o miyembro ng isang grupo, organisasyon, o samahan.
etymology: From "pag-" (manner of) + "ka-" (abstract noun prefix) + "sapi" (member, to join).
original_explanation: It's your official entry into a group. Whether it's pagkakasapi sa isang K-Pop fandom, sa SSS, o sa "Samahan ng mga Nag-aabang ng 13th Month Pay," it means you're in! You have the ID, you're in the group chat, you're one of them now. Congrats, you belong.
usage_notes: Used for formal and informal groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya ang kanyang **pagkakasapi** sa sikat na club.","translation":"He is proud of his **membership** in the famous club."},{"sentence":"May bayad ang aplikasyon para sa **pagkakasapi** sa kooperatiba.","translation":"There is a fee for the application for **membership** in the cooperative."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtuon ng atensyon o pagkilala sa pagkakaroon ng isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is what you hope your crush does when you walk past them. It's the opposite of being 'seenzoned'. When you magbigay-pansin, you're acknowledging someone's existence, listening to their 'chika', or noticing their new haircut. Not doing this is the fastest way to get a 'Hindi mo na ako mahal' text.
usage_notes: The verb 'pumansin' is a more common and direct synonym in many contexts. 'Magbigay-pansin' often implies a more deliberate act of giving attention.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Salamat sa **pagbibigay-pansin** sa aking mga mungkahi.","translation":"Thank you for **paying attention** to my suggestions."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang **bigyan-pansin**, nagpapapansin lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't **pay him any attention**, he's just seeking attention."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na langgam, karaniwang kulay pula o itim.
original_explanation: Not just any ant, but those tiny, almost invisible ones that seem to appear out of nowhere when you drop a single crumb of Choc-Nut. They're the ninjas of the ant world. You don't see them coming, but suddenly there's a whole army on your table.
usage_notes: More specific than the general term 'langgam'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May linya ng **guyam** na papunta sa natapong asukal.","translation":"There's a line of **small ants** going to the spilled sugar."},{"sentence":"Kinagat ako ng **guyam** sa paa, ang kati!","translation":"A **small ant** bit me on the foot, it's so itchy!"}]

meaning_filipino: Itabi o iparada ang isang sasakyang-dagat tulad ng bangka o barko sa pampang, pantalan, o daungan.
original_explanation: It's the maritime equivalent of parking your car. You find a spot at the pier, throw the ropes, and make sure your bangka doesn't float away. When the ship has arrived, it's time to **idaong**.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang kapitan na **idaong** ang barko dahil sa papalapit na bagyo.","translation":"The captain decided to **dock** the ship because of the approaching storm."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtanda o pag-abot sa hustong gulang o pagkahinog.
original_explanation: That thing that happens to cheese, wine, and people. For people, it's when your back starts to hurt for no reason, you prefer a quiet night in, and you start saying 'noong panahon namin...' It's not just getting old, it's (hopefully) getting wiser.
usage_notes: Can be used for people, animals, and even inanimate things that improve with age like wine or cheese. When used for fruits, 'nahinog' is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat tayo ay **gugulang** balang araw.","translation":"We will all **age** someday."},{"sentence":"Habang **gumugulang** ang keso, lalong sumasarap ang lasa nito.","translation":"As the cheese **ages**, its flavor becomes better."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagiging labis na masiba o may matinding pagnanasa, lalo na sa pagkain.
original_explanation: That friend who, despite just having eaten, will still ask if you're going to finish your food. They are the ones who always lose the 'last piece' etiquette challenge. The human vacuum cleaner of the barkada.
usage_notes: Often used with a noun, like 'takaw-kain' (greedy for food) or 'takaw-tingin' (gets hungry just by looking at food). Can also be used figuratively for greed in other things, like 'takaw-kapangyarihan' (power-hungry).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **takaw**, ipagtira mo naman ang mga bisita.","translation":"Don't be so **greedy**, leave some for the guests."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **takaw** sa pansin.","translation":"He is known for being an attention **hog**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sumama ang lasa o amoy, karaniwan sa mga pagkaing may mantika o taba na naluma na.
original_explanation: What happens to that mani or chicharon you forgot you had in the pantry for a year. It's the flavor of disappointment when you bite into old cooking oil. Your lola would say, 'Huwag mo nang kainin 'yan, umanta na!'
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the spoilage of fats and oils, giving a distinct stale or foul taste and smell.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umanta** na ang mantikang ginamit mo kahapon.","translation":"The oil you used yesterday has **become rancid**."},{"sentence":"Itapon mo na 'yang lumang mani, baka **umanta** na 'yan.","translation":"Throw away those old peanuts, they might have **gone rancid** already."}]

translation: to stomp one's feet repeatedly, to throw a tantrum
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at malakas na pagpadyak ng paa sa sahig, karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng matinding galit, pagkadismaya, o pagmamaktol, lalo na sa mga bata.
original_explanation: This is the signature move of a toddler in the toy section who didn't get the giant teddy bear. It's the physical manifestation of 'I want it NOW!' Also seen in adults when the Wi-Fi suddenly dies during a crucial Netflix scene. The feet start stomping, and the drama begins.
usage_notes: A very descriptive word, often associated with children's tantrums or extreme frustration. The repetition in the word ('saldak-saldak') emphasizes the repeated action of stomping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumaldak-saldak** ang bata nang hindi siya bilhan ng laruan.","translation":"The child **stomped his feet repeatedly** when he wasn't bought a toy."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **sumaldak-saldak** diyan na parang bata!","translation":"Don't **throw a tantrum** there like a child!"}]

meaning_filipino: Dalusay, puro, at walang anumang halo o dagdag.
original_explanation: The real deal. 100% legit, no fillers. Like 'taganas na ginto' (pure gold), or that feeling of 'taganas na kaligayahan' (pure happiness) when your 13th-month pay comes in. It's the opposite of 'may halo', 'fake', or 'half-baked'.
usage_notes: A formal or literary word. Not commonly used in casual conversation, where 'puro' is more frequent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iyon ay **taganas** na katotohanan at walang halong kasinungalingan.","translation":"That is the **absolute** truth with no mix of lies."},{"sentence":"Isang singsing na gawa sa **taganas** na ginto ang kanyang regalo.","translation":"A ring made of **pure** gold was her gift."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manggagamot na gumagamit ng mga halamang-gamot, ritwal, at dasal sa panggagamot na hindi nakabase sa modernong siyensya.
original_explanation: The OG healthcare provider in the province before HMOs were a thing. If you get sick, your lola would probably suggest seeing the albularyo first for 'usog' or 'na-maligno' before even considering a trip to the hospital. They're the masters of tawas, hilot, and mysterious herbal concoctions.
usage_notes: Often viewed with skepticism by modern medicine but remains a respected and integral part of rural Filipino culture and alternative medicine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala nila ang bata sa **albularyo** dahil sa hindi maipaliwanag na lagnat.","translation":"They brought the child to the **folk healer** because of an unexplainable fever."},{"sentence":"Naniniwala pa rin ang iba sa kakayahan ng isang **albularyo** na magpaalis ng masasamang espiritu.","translation":"Some still believe in the ability of a **folk healer** to cast out evil spirits."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahusay sa pagbigkas ng tula o talumpati nang may angkop na damdamin at kilos.
original_explanation: Ito yung kaklase mo nung elementary o high school na laging pambato sa Declamation Contest tuwing Buwan ng Wika. Sila yung may malalaking boses at dramatic hand gestures, na parang laging galing sa isang dula sa teatro. Yung tipong bibigkasin ang "Ang Puno" na may kasamang iyak at paghampas sa dibdib. The OG spoken word artist.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang tanyag na **deklamador** ang nagtanghal sa aming paaralan.","translation":"A famous **orator** performed at our school."},{"sentence":"Nagsasanay siyang maging isang magaling na **deklamador** para sa darating na patimpalak.","translation":"He is practicing to be a great **declaimer** for the upcoming competition."}]

translation: to get to know each other
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-alam sa pagkatao, pangalan, at katangian ng isa't isa; ang pagtatatag ng paunang ugnayan.
etymology: From mag- (reciprocal action prefix) + kilala (to know someone).
original_explanation: This is the "getting to know you" stage. It's what happens during the first day of class, a team-building activity, or a first date. "Magkilala muna tayo" is the polite way of saying "Hold your horses, let's see if we even like each other first."
usage_notes: Implies a mutual action between two or more people. Can refer to the first moment of meeting ('nagkilala') or the ongoing process.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan sila ng pagkakataon na **magkilala** bago simulan ang proyekto.","translation":"They were given a chance **to get to know each other** before starting the project."},{"sentence":"Sa isang coffee shop kami unang **nagkilala**.","translation":"We first **met** (and got to know each other) at a coffee shop."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela o papel na sumisipsip ng likido, karaniwang ginagamit sa pagpapatuyo ng katawan pagkatapos maligo o pagpupunas ng mga kamay.
original_explanation: Your best friend after a shower. Comes in many forms: the good-for-guests 'tuwalya', the everyday 'tuwalya' that's seen better days, and the 'Good Morning' towel that is somehow the most absorbent of them all. Also, the thing you forget to bring to the bathroom 90% of the time, resulting in a mad dash back to your room.
usage_notes: A household staple.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha mo nga ang malinis na **tuwalya** sa aparador.","translation":"Can you please get a clean **towel** from the cabinet?"},{"sentence":"Isinampay niya ang basang **tuwalya** sa labas para matuyo.","translation":"She hung the wet **towel** outside to dry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na uka o lubog, karaniwan sa pisngi o baba, na lumilitaw kapag ang isang tao ay ngumingiti.
original_explanation: Yung 'pampacute' feature sa mukha mo na lumalabas 'pag ngumingiti ka. Sabi nila, 'hinipuan daw ng anghel' nung baby ka pa. Sa panahon ngayon, 'yan 'yung asset mo sa selfie. #blessed
usage_notes: Isang napaka-espesipikong salita para sa katangiang ito sa mukha.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lumalabas ang kanyang **biloy** kapag siya ay tumatawa.","translation":"His **dimple** shows when he laughs."},{"sentence":"Ang cute ng baby, may **biloy** sa magkabilang pisngi.","translation":"The baby is so cute, with **dimples** on both cheeks."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging walang kinikilingan; hindi pumanig sa alinmang panig sa isang alitan, argumento, o kompetisyon.
original_explanation: Your role when your two best friends are having a fight. You're Switzerland. You just listen, nod, and offer food, without saying "Sinabi ko na sa'yo e." You're just there for the chismis but without the commitment of taking a side.
usage_notes: Often used in discussions about conflicts, arguments, or opinions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan kong maging **neutral** sa away nila, pero mahirap.","translation":"I'm trying to be **neutral** in their fight, but it's difficult."},{"sentence":"Dapat **neutral** ang isang tagapamagitan sa usapan.","translation":"A mediator in a discussion should be **neutral**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol o may kaugnayan sa litograpiya, isang paraan ng pag-imprenta mula sa isang bato o metal na plaka.
original_explanation: This is a very technical term for a specific type of printing, usually for art. It's the kind of word you'd hear in a museum, a fine arts class, or a vintage print shop. It's the 'OG' of high-quality image reproduction, way before your inkjet printer was a thing.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino sa sining at pag-iimprenta.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita sa eksibit ang ilang mga gawang **litograpiko** mula sa ika-19 na siglo.","translation":"The exhibit showed several **lithographic** works from the 19th century."},{"sentence":"Ang prosesong **litograpiko** ay nangangailangan ng espesyal na kasanayan.","translation":"The **lithographic** process requires special skills."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking instrumentong de-kuwerdas na may apat na kuwerdas, tinutugtog gamit ang arko habang nakaupo.
original_explanation: The violin's bigger, deeper-voiced, and more soulful sibling. It's the instrument that looks like you have to hug it to play it. Its sound gives off major dramatic or romantic vibes, perfect for a movie's climax or a classy coffee shop playlist.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malungkot na tunog ng **biyolonselo** ay umalingawngaw sa buong silid.","translation":"The sad sound of the **cello** echoed throughout the room."},{"sentence":"Natututo siyang tumugtog ng **biyolonselo** tuwing Sabado.","translation":"She is learning to play the **cello** every Saturday."}]

translation: to crown, to place something on the head of
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng putong o korona sa ulo ng isang tao bilang tanda ng karangalan, pagkahari, o tagumpay.
original_explanation: The act of crowning someone. Think pageant night when they finally announce the winner and place that sparkly tiara on her head. Or when you graduate and they put that awkward square hat (mortarboard) on you. 'Putungan ng korona' is the ultimate glow-up moment.
usage_notes: Ang salitang-ugat na 'putong' ay tumutukoy sa isang tradisyonal na pantakip sa ulo o korona ng mga Pilipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **puputungan** ng korona bilang Reyna ng Flores de Mayo.","translation":"She will be the one **to be crowned** as the Queen of Flores de Mayo."},{"sentence":"**Pinutungan** ng mga bulaklak ang nanalong atleta.","translation":"The winning athlete was **crowned** with flowers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kumpol ng malalaki at makukulay na balahibo, karaniwang ginagamit bilang palamuti sa sumbrero, kasuotan, o sa ulo ng kabayo.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'extra' accessory before bling was a thing. Think of the fancy feathers on a general's hat, a festival dancer's headdress, or a showgirl's costume. It's the sartorial equivalent of saying "Look at me!" without saying a word. The more extravagant the plumahe, the bigger the 'sana all' energy.
usage_notes: Used to describe decorative feathers, especially in historical, military, or festive contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga mananayaw ay may suot na makukulay na **plumahe** sa kanilang ulo.","translation":"The dancers wore colorful **plumes** on their heads."},{"sentence":"Ang **plumahe** sa sombrero ng heneral ay tanda ng kanyang mataas na ranggo.","translation":"The **plumage** on the general's hat is a sign of his high rank."}]

translation: (a person who speaks) Taglish in a stereotypically upper-class manner
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, karaniwang mula sa mataas na antas ng lipunan, na ang paraan ng pagsasalita ay pinaghahalo ang Tagalog at Ingles sa isang partikular na paraan na may kasamang natatanging punto o intonasyon. Maaari ring tumukoy sa mismong paraan ng pagsasalita.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "coño", isang bulgar na ekspresyon, na naging katawagan sa mga mestizong Espanyol at sa paglipas ng panahon ay iniugnay sa mga mayayamang Pilipino na nagsasalita ng pinaghalong Ingles at Tagalog.
original_explanation: It's like, the speech pattern of people from exclusive schools, you know? They make *halo-halo* the English and Tagalog, and it's like, so *maarte*. 'Can you make *sundo* me from school? It's so *traffic*, like, super *grabe*!' That's the vibe. It's both a person and a language.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin bilang isang stereotype, na maaaring may negatibo o nakakatawang konotasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **conyo** pakinggan ang pagsasalita niya, pero mabait naman.","translation":"His way of speaking sounds a bit **conyo**, but he's a nice person."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong kausapin na parang **conyo**, hindi kita maintindihan.","translation":"Don't talk to me like a **conyo**, I can't understand you."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kahoy o anumang katulad na materyal na marupok na dahil sa anay, bukbok, o katandaan.
original_explanation: That old wooden chair in your lola's house that you're scared to sit on? That's probably 'gipo.' It's wood that's been weakened by time, termites (anay), or moisture, making it fragile and ready to crumble. It's the reason why you can't trust old cabinets or floorboards. Think of it as wood that's past its expiration date.
usage_notes: Specifically used to describe the state of wood or similar materials that have become weak and brittle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, **gipo** na ang sahig na kahoy sa bahay na iyan.","translation":"Be careful, the wooden floor in that house is already **rotten**."},{"sentence":"Pinalitan na namin ang mga haligi dahil **gipo** na ang mga ito.","translation":"We already replaced the posts because they were **brittle**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa katangian, pagkakakilanlan, o kalagayan ng pagiging isang lalaki.
original_explanation: This is the "for men" label on everything from shampoo to life expectations. It’s the check box for 'Male' on a form. In a deeper sense, it's the whole cultural package of what it means to be a 'lalaki' in the Philippines – from being the 'haligi ng tahanan' to being expected not to cry ('Lalaki ka, 'wag kang iiyak!').
usage_notes: A formal, technical term used in biology, sociology, and official documents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pormularyo, isinulat niya ang kanyang **kasariang panlalaki**.","translation":"On the form, he wrote his **male gender**."},{"sentence":"Ang **kasariang panlalaki** ay isa sa dalawang tradisyonal na pag-uuri ng kasarian.","translation":"The **male gender** is one of the two traditional classifications of gender."}]

translation: flaking or shredding (of meat/fish); detailed analysis
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghihiwalay ng laman ng isda, manok, o karne mula sa buto sa pamamagitan ng kamay. Sa makabagong gamit, tumutukoy rin ito sa masusing pagsusuri sa isang paksa.
original_explanation: This is what you do to leftover chicken adobo to make chicken flakes for your pandesal. It's the meticulous work of shredding fish for palabok toppings. But wait, there's more! In a modern, 'hugot' sense, 'himay' is what you and your friends do to a problematic text message from your crush. You analyze it word by word, emoji by emoji. "Hinihimay namin 'yung chat niya." It's a deep-dive analysis, breaking something down into its smallest parts.
usage_notes: Has both a literal (culinary) and a figurative (analytical) meaning. The verb form is 'himayin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **himay** ng isda ay kailangan para sa paggawa ng siomai.","translation":"The **shredding** of the fish is needed to make siomai."},{"sentence":"Ginawan namin ng masusing **himay** ang bawat detalye ng kanyang kwento.","translation":"We did a detailed **analysis** of every detail of his story."}]

translation: to become a member; to join an organization
meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagiging kasapi o miyembro ng isang samahan, kapatiran, o organisasyon.
original_explanation: This is the official 'Sign up here!' verb. When you finally decide to join that gym, a church group, or the Illuminati, you makisapi. It’s more formal than 'sumali' because it implies membership and belonging to an established group with rules and probably a membership fee or an initiation rite.
