usage_notes: Refers to formally joining a group with a defined membership, like a club, association, or political party.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **makisapi** sa isang organisasyon na tumutulong sa mga hayop.","translation":"She wants **to join** an organization that helps animals."},{"sentence":"Bago ka **makisapi** sa kooperatiba, kailangan mong dumalo sa isang seminar.","translation":"Before you can **become a member** of the cooperative, you need to attend a seminar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng isang bagay gamit ang kamay sa paraang pasakmal o maramihan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo sa free-taste sa supermarket, o sa popcorn bowl habang nanonood ng nakakakabang movie. Hindi paisa-isa, kundi isang buong **dakol**. The art of getting as much as you can in one go. Efficiency, 'ika nga.
usage_notes: The action implies taking a large quantity with one's hand, often in a slightly greedy or hurried manner. The noun form, also 'dakol', means 'a handful'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **dakol** ng kanin ang kanyang kinuha dahil sa gutom.","translation":"He took a large **handful** of rice because he was hungry."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **dumakol** ng kendi, bigyan mo rin ang iba.","translation":"Don't **grab a handful** of candy, give some to the others."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno (Bauhinia purpurea) na may mga dahong hugis paru-paro at mga bulaklak na kulay lila, rosas, o puti. Ang mga dahon nito ay ginagamit bilang pampaasim sa ilang lutuin.
original_explanation: Hindi ito 'yung lumilipad na butterfly, kundi 'yung puno na 'yung dahon niya, kamukha ng pakpak ng butterfly. Kung mahilig ka sa sinigang pero ayaw mo ng sobrang asim ng sampalok, pwedeng dahon ng alibambang ang gamitin. It's the 'low-key asim' alternative.
usage_notes: Ang mga dahon nito ay ginagamit na pampaasim sa mga pagkain tulad ng sinigang o paksiw sa ilang mga rehiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap gamiting pampaasim sa isda ang dahon ng **alibambang**.","translation":"The leaves of the **orchid tree** are delicious as a souring agent for fish."},{"sentence":"Namumulaklak na ang mga puno ng **alibambang** sa aming hardin.","translation":"The **orchid trees** in our garden are now in bloom."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking instrumentong pangmusika na may mga kuwerdas na patayo at tinutugtog sa pamamagitan ng pagkalabit sa mga ito gamit ang mga daliri.
original_explanation: That big, fancy, angelic-looking instrument you see in orchestras or cartoons when a character goes to heaven. It looks like it would be super relaxing to play, but probably costs more than your monthly rent. The person playing it is called an 'alpista'.
usage_notes: Hindi isang pangkaraniwang instrumento sa Pilipinas, ngunit naiintindihan ang salita. Ang manunugtog nito ay tinatawag na 'alpista'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tugtog ng **alpa** ay nakakapagpakalma.","translation":"The music of the **harp** is calming."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang matutong tumugtog ng **alpa**.","translation":"She dreams of learning to play the **harp**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sekswal o romantikong naaakit sa mga taong may kaparehong kasarian. Bilang pang-uri, naglalarawan sa katangiang ito.
original_explanation: A clinical, formal term you'd see in a textbook or a news report. While technically correct, in everyday chika, people are more likely to use terms like 'beki', 'bakla', 'tomboy', or simply 'gay' or 'lesbian'. Using 'homosekswal' can sound a bit dated or overly formal, like calling a 'jeep' an 'auto calesa'.
usage_notes: This is a formal, sometimes clinical term. More common colloquial terms exist, such as 'bakla' for men and 'tomboy' for women, which are being reclaimed by the community.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagiging **homosekswal** ay hindi isang sakit.","translation":"Being **homosexual** is not a disease."},{"sentence":"May mga batas na nagpoprotekta sa karapatan ng mga taong **homosekswal**.","translation":"There are laws that protect the rights of **homosexual** people."}]

meaning_filipino: May malaking halaga, kabuluhan, o epekto; kinakailangan o mahalaga.
original_explanation: Yung bagay na hindi mo pwedeng i-seen-zone. Parang deadline sa trabaho o 'yung anniversary niyo ng jowa mo. Kapag sinabing **importante**, 'wag mong balewalain kundi yari ka.
usage_notes: Very common adjective, often used interchangeably with 'mahalaga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Importante** ang pag-aaral para sa magandang kinabukasan.","translation":"Education is **important** for a good future."},{"sentence":"May **importante** akong sasabihin sa iyo mamaya.","translation":"I have something **important** to tell you later."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na pariralang naglalarawan sa isang tao o bagay na labis-labis o sobra sa pagsisikap, na minsan ay may bahid ng pagiging hindi natural o pilit.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na 'very giving' na binigyan ng bagong, madalas na sarkastikong, kahulugan sa kontekstong Filipino slang, partikular sa kulturang beki at Gen Z.
original_explanation: Originally meant generous, but Gen Z and the beki community flipped it. Now, it means you're trying too hard. Yung outfit mo, 'very giving.' Yung pag-pose mo sa picture, 'very giving.' It's the side-eye comment for someone doing the absolute most. 'Girl, the five-minute dance number for a 15-second TikTok? That's very giving.'
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay lubos na nakadepende sa konteksto at tono. Maaaring maging papuri (sincere effort) o kritisismo (trying too hard).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo ang pa-production number niya sa birthday niya, **very giving**!","translation":"Look at her production number for her birthday, she's **giving it her all**! (can be sarcastic)"},{"sentence":"**Very giving** naman ang outfit mo para sa isang mabilis na pagtakbo sa grocery.","translation":"Your outfit is a **bit much** for a quick grocery run."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglabas ng bula o bagay na tila bula mula sa bibig o sa isang sisidlan.
etymology: The root word 'bulak' means cotton, likely relating to the white, fluffy appearance of foam.
original_explanation: What happens to your mouth if you accidentally taste soap. Or when a pot of soup boils over and creates a foamy mess. It's the act of bubbling or frothing up and spilling over. A very visual word for a messy situation.
usage_notes: Not to be confused with 'bulak' (cotton). The verb specifically refers to foaming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumulak** ang bibig ng aso matapos makakain ng lason.","translation":"The dog's mouth **foamed** after eating poison."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang galit, tila **bumulak** ang kanyang bibig sa mga sinasabi.","translation":"In so much anger, it was as if his mouth **spewed** his words."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagkaing gawa sa namuong gatas ng balatong (soybean), na karaniwang hinuhubog na parang kesong puti. Ito ay kilala rin bilang tokwa.
etymology: From Japanese 'tōfu' (豆腐), which itself is from Chinese 'dòufu' (豆腐).
original_explanation: The more 'conyo' way of saying 'tokwa'. It's that white, jiggly block of soy you see in the palengke. It's the star of Tokwa't Baboy, the quiet partner in a stir-fry, and the go-to meat substitute when you're trying to be healthy... for a day.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with 'tokwa', although 'tokwa' is more common in everyday Filipino vernacular, especially in markets and local eateries. 'Tofu' is more common in restaurants, supermarkets, and health-conscious circles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magprito ka ng **tofu** para sa Tokwa't Baboy.","translation":"Fry some **tofu** for the Tokwa't Baboy."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang **tofu** kaysa sa karne sa sisig.","translation":"I prefer **tofu** over meat in sisig."}]

translation: member of a group; someone gathered with
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kabilang o kasama sa isang pangkat o pagtitipon.
original_explanation: Your "ka-tropa," "ka-barkada," or "ka-team." If you're all gathered for a KBBQ night, you're all kalipon. It's the person who's part of the same "tipon" (gathering) as you.
usage_notes: The prefix 'ka-' indicates being part of the same group. Similar to 'kasama' but specifically implies being part of a gathering or collection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **kalipon** niya sa samahan ay nagbigay ng suporta.","translation":"The **members of his group** in the organization gave their support."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yugto ng panahon na katumbas ng isang libong taon; isang milenyo.
original_explanation: The amount of time it feels like you're waiting for your online order to arrive. Also the length of your crush's 'seen-zone' reply time. It's the Pinoy version of 'forever,' used to describe anything that takes an excruciatingly long time, like EDSA traffic on a payday Friday.
usage_notes: Often used hyperbolically to mean 'a very long time'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit lumipas pa ang **sanlibong taon**, hindi kita malilimutan.","translation":"Even if **a thousand years** pass, I will not forget you."},{"sentence":"Parang **sanlibong taon** ang hinintay ko sa pila para lang sa kape.","translation":"It felt like I waited **a thousand years** in line just for coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan ng katangian ng pagiging tuso, mapanlinlang, o mapagsamantala sa kapwa.
etymology: Mula sa 'ka-..-an' at 'gulang', kung saan ang 'gulang' dito ay tumutukoy sa karanasang ginagamit sa panlilinlang.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung diskarte ng tropa mong laging nakakalibre ng pamasahe o pagkain. It's the "art of the deal" but in a sneaky, palengke-haggling, sometimes shady way. Not necessarily evil, but definitely street-smart and opportunistic. Think of a political strategist's moves or how someone talks their way out of a traffic violation.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugang ito ay hindi gaanong karaniwan kaysa sa 'maturity' at lubos na nakadepende sa konteksto. Ito ay may negatibo o alanganing konotasyon. Bagaman maaari ring gamitin bilang pangngalan (cunningness), madalas itong naglalarawan sa isang kilos o katangian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamitan niya ng **kagulangan** na paraan ang kanyang mga kalaban.","translation":"He used **cunning** methods against his opponents."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa kanyang mga **kagulangan** na ngiti.","translation":"Be wary of his **deceitful** smiles."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha ng kumukulong likido o ng hangin na dumaraan sa tubig.
etymology: Onomatopoeic, imitating the sound of bubbling.
original_explanation: 'Yung tunog ng kumukulong tubig para sa instant noodles mo at 3 AM. O 'yung sound effect sa tiyan mo 'pag gutom ka na pero nasa gitna ka ng meeting. 'Glug glug glug.' 'Yan ang bulubok.
usage_notes: Purely describes the sound of boiling or gurgling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **bulubok** ng kumukulong sopas mula sa kusina.","translation":"I heard the **bubbling sound** of the boiling soup from the kitchen."},{"sentence":"May **bulubok** sa loob ng tubo kaya't malamang ay may hangin ito.","translation":"There's a **gurgling** in the pipe, so it probably has air inside."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa sinuman o anuman sa isang pangkat o pagpipilian nang walang partikular na pagtukoy.
original_explanation: The "bahala ka na" or "Kahit ano" of pronouns. When your friend asks what you want to eat and you say, "Alinman diyan, okay lang," it means you're either super easy-going or you've given up on life and will accept any fate (or food).
usage_notes: Often spelled as two words "alin man", but "alinman" is the standard form. It expresses a lack of preference or an acceptance of any option available.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Alinman** ang piliin mo, susuportahan kita.","translation":"**Whichever** you choose, I will support you."},{"sentence":"Puwede kang kumuha ng **alinman** sa mga libro.","translation":"You can take **any** of the books."}]

translation: to celebrate; to acclaim; to hail
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdiriwang o pagbibigay ng masiglang papuri at pagkilala sa isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "Sana all!" but in a good way. It's what you do when your favorite team wins the championship, or when a Filipino wins an international competition. You go out and ipagbunyi their victory! It’s the feeling of collective pride and celebration. Think parades, confetti, and lots of cheering. It’s a very grand, almost nationalistic, way of celebrating.
usage_notes: Carries a tone of great honor, pride, and public celebration. More formal than 'ipagdiwang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **ipagbunyi** ang tagumpay ng ating mga atleta.","translation":"We should **celebrate** the victory of our athletes."},{"sentence":"**Ipagbunyi** natin ang Araw ng Kalayaan!","translation":"Let us **acclaim** Independence Day!"}]

translation: makes something last; causes to remain
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa aksyon o katangian na nagiging sanhi upang ang isang bagay, kalagayan, o relasyon ay manatili nang mas matagal.
etymology: From nakapag- (causative, ability) + pa- (causative) + a form derived from 'lagi' (always), related to 'pamamalagi' (the act of staying).
original_explanation: This is the secret ingredient for 'forever'. It's the constant 'good morning' texts that keep the relationship going, the regular maintenance that keeps your car running, or the trust that makes a friendship endure. It's the effort that fights against 'expiration dates'.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of preservation, relationships, or maintaining a state or condition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tamang pag-iimbak ng pagkain ay **nakapagpapamalagi** ng pagiging sariwa nito.","translation":"Proper food storage **makes its freshness last**."},{"sentence":"Ang tiwala at respeto sa isa't isa ang **nakapagpapamalagi** sa isang matibay na pagsasama.","translation":"Mutual trust and respect are what **cause a strong relationship to remain**."}]

translation: to consume all; to use up completely
meaning_filipino: Ubusin o gamitin ang lahat ng isang bagay hanggang sa wala nang matira.
original_explanation: This is what your younger sibling does to the entire box of Choc-Nut you were saving. Or what you do to your sweldo three days after payday. Mang-ubos is the art of leaving no survivors, whether it's food, data allowance, or your monthly budget.
usage_notes: The 'mang-' prefix often implies a more intense, deliberate, or habitual action of 'ubos' (to finish).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mang-ubos** ng pagkain sa handaan; magtira ka para sa iba.","translation":"Don't **consume all** the food at the party; leave some for others."},{"sentence":"Ang hilig mong **mang-ubos** ng pasensya ko!","translation":"You love to **use up all** of my patience!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging una sa isang karera, kompetisyon, o listahan; ang mamuno o maging lider ng isang grupo.
original_explanation: This is what every student gunning for valedictorian, every contestant in a beauty pageant, and every basketball team in the finals wants to do. It's to be number one, the leader of the pack, the 'bida'. In traffic, it's what every driver tries to do, often with chaotic results.
usage_notes: Can mean 'to lead' in a race or 'to lead' as in being a leader.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang inaasahang **manguna** sa susunod na halalan.","translation":"He is expected to **lead** in the next election."},{"sentence":"Nagsikap siyang mag-aral upang **manguna** sa klase.","translation":"She studied hard in order to **be first** in her class."}]

translation: state of being submerged; state of being in debt
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging lubog sa tubig o anumang likido. Sa matalinhagang paraan, tumutukoy ito sa pagiging baon sa utang o malubhang problema.
original_explanation: Can be literal or figurative. Literal: The state of Metro Manila streets during a typhoon. Figurative: The state of your finances after adding to cart on 11.11. "Pagkakalubog sa utang" is a national mood for many. It's when you're so deep in something (water, debt, problems), you can barely see the light.
usage_notes: Has both a literal (sinking) and a common figurative (debt, problems) meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis ang **pagkakalubog** ng barko matapos itong bumangga.","translation":"The **sinking** of the ship was fast after it crashed."},{"sentence":"Hirap siyang bumangon dahil sa kanyang **pagkakalubog** sa utang.","translation":"He is having a hard time getting back on his feet because of his **state of being deep in debt**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iyak nang mahina at may kasamang reklamo o pagdaing, karaniwang ginagawa ng mga bata o hayop.
original_explanation: That annoying, low-volume, high-pitched complaining sound a kid makes when they don't get the toy they want. It's less than a full cry, more than just being quiet. It's the soundtrack of a spoiled toddler in the mall. Also used for puppies whimpering.
usage_notes: Often associated with children or a child-like way of complaining or showing slight pain/discomfort.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **umingil** ang bata nang hindi siya bilhan ng laruan.","translation":"The child started to **whine** when they didn't buy him a toy."},{"sentence":"Naririnig ko ang tuta na **umingil** sa labas ng pinto.","translation":"I can hear the puppy **whimpering** outside the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal at nakasulat na utos mula sa isang korte o awtoridad na nag-aatas sa isang tao na gawin o itigil ang isang partikular na gawain.
original_explanation: This is a legal term you hear in courtroom dramas. "Warrant of arrest" is `mandamyento de aresto`. It's the universe's official "you're in deep trouble" paper. When the police show up with a **mandamyento**, you can't just say "seen" and ignore it.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in legal or very formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglabas ang korte ng **mandamyento** de aresto laban sa suspek.","translation":"The court issued a **warrant** of arrest against the suspect."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nilang sundin ang **mandamyento** na itigil ang konstruksyon.","translation":"They need to follow the **official order** to stop the construction."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos na ginawa kung saan ang isang lalagyan ay nilagyan ng laman hanggang sa umabot sa hangganan nito.
etymology: Past tense of 'punuin', from the root 'puno' (full).
original_explanation: What you did to your water bottle before heading to the gym. Or what your crush did to your heart... with love (sana all!). It's the past tense of 'to fill.' 'Bes, pinuno ko na 'yung pitsel ng tubig.'
usage_notes: The stress is on the last syllable: pi-nu-NO. This differentiates it from the noun 'pinuno' (leader).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pinuno** niya ng hangin ang mga lobo para sa salu-salo.","translation":"He **filled** the balloons with air for the party."},{"sentence":"**Pinuno** ko ang balde ng tubig mula sa gripo.","translation":"I **filled** the bucket with water from the faucet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuin na yari sa giniling na karne, karaniwang may patatas, karot, at pasas.
original_explanation: The ultimate ulam hack for when you're on a budget. It's ground meat stretched with potatoes and carrots, sometimes with the controversial pasas (raisins). It’s the 'giniling' you see in every carinderia, the reliable, go-to meal.
usage_notes: A very common Filipino dish. The composition varies by region and family recipe.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si nanay ng **pikadilyo** para sa hapunan.","translation":"Mom brought home **picadillo** for dinner."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **pikadilyo** kapag may kasamang pritong saging.","translation":"The **picadillo** is delicious when paired with fried plantains."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging malaya, nagsasarili, at hindi napapasailalim sa kontrol o kapangyarihan ng iba; kasarinlan.
original_explanation: Freedom! 'Yung feeling na wala ka nang utang sa credit card mo. O 'yung pag-alis mo sa bahay ng parents mo at natutunan mong magluto ng kanin na hindi tutong. It's about being your own boss, whether as a country celebrating on June 12th or as a person celebrating payday.
usage_notes: The spelling 'independensiya' with an 'i' is also used but 'independensya' with an 'e' is more common in modern usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang natin ang Araw ng **Independensya** tuwing Hunyo 12.","translation":"We celebrate **Independence** Day every June 12."},{"sentence":"Ang pinakamahalaga sa kanya ay ang kanyang pinansyal na **independensya**.","translation":"The most important thing to her is her financial **independence**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sapin sa paa na karaniwang yari sa katad o goma at may matigas na suwelas, na isinusuot upang protektahan ang mga paa.
original_explanation: Your 'porma' isn't complete without the right kicks. Whether it's the latest Jordans, your office leather shoes, or the Marikina-made ones your mom bought you, the sapatos makes or breaks the OOTD. It's the foundation of your fit, literally.
usage_notes: A general term for any type of closed-toe footwear. It's used in the singular form ('sapatos') to refer to a single shoe or a pair of shoes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bagong bili ang **sapatos** ko kaya maingat ako sa paglakad.","translation":"My **shoes** are brand new, so I'm walking carefully."},{"sentence":"Hubarin ang iyong **sapatos** bago pumasok sa bahay.","translation":"Take off your **shoes** before entering the house."}]

translation: disgraced (female); a woman who got pregnant out of wedlock
meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng nawalan ng karangalan o reputasyon, partikular na tumutukoy sa isang babaeng nagdalantao nang hindi pa kasal.
original_explanation: This is a very old-school, judgmental term for a woman who got pregnant before getting married. It's the kind of word your lola might whisper about a neighbor. Thankfully, society's getting more progressive, so this term is becoming less powerful, but the "Marites" culture keeps it alive. It basically means "fallen woman."
usage_notes: Isang salitang may mabigat at negatibong konotasyon, at itinuturing na makaluma at mapanghusga sa modernong panahon. Ang panlalaking katumbas ay 'disgrasyado'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuring siyang **disgrasyada** ng kanilang komunidad matapos malaman ang kanyang kalagayan.","translation":"She was considered **disgraced** by their community after they found out about her situation."},{"sentence":"Lumayas siya sa kanilang bahay dahil sa takot na tawaging **disgrasyada**.","translation":"She ran away from home for fear of being called a **disgraced woman**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mag-aaral ng medisina na sumasailalim sa praktikal na pagsasanay sa isang ospital bilang bahagi ng kanilang kurikulum bago maging isang lisensyadong doktor.
original_explanation: A future doctor running on fumes, instant coffee, and the sheer will to survive a 36-hour duty. They are the backbone of the hospital's workforce, often seen sprinting through hallways. If you see someone sleeping upright in a corner of the ER, that's probably an interno. The final boss before becoming a real doctor.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a medical student in their internship year. It's a formal and respected stage in a doctor's training.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod ang mga **interno** pagkatapos ng kanilang 24-oras na duty sa ospital.","translation":"The **medical interns** are exhausted after their 24-hour duty at the hospital."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **interno**, natutunan niya ang maraming praktikal na kasanayan sa medisina.","translation":"As a **medical intern**, he learned many practical skills in medicine."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay pamaypay, nang pabalik-balik upang makalikha ng hangin. Tumutukoy din sa pagkaway.
original_explanation: The OG aircon. It's what you do with a pamaypay (a hand fan) during a brownout or when you're stuck in a hot, crowded jeepney. It can also mean to wave something, like waving a flag or waving goodbye. 'I-paypay mo nga 'yang usok palayo.'
usage_notes: The root word itself can act as a command in its imperative form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paypay** ka naman diyan, ang init!","translation":"**Fan** over here, it's so hot!"},{"sentence":"I**paypay** mo ang bandila para makita ng lahat.","translation":"**Wave** the flag so everyone can see."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sasakyang pampasahero na may tatlong gulong, pinalalakad sa pamamagitan ng pagpadyak tulad ng bisikleta, at may sidecar para sa isa o dalawang pasahero.
original_explanation: The eco-friendly, leg-powered version of a tricycle. It's your go-to ride for short distances inside a subdivision or when you're navigating tight market streets (palengke). The fare is usually cheap, and you get a nice breeze, plus a free leg workout for the driver. It's the king of 'looban' (inner streets).
usage_notes: Sometimes used interchangeably with 'padyak', which is the act of pedaling but also refers to the vehicle itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumakay na lang tayo ng **pedicab** papuntang palengke.","translation":"Let's just take a **pedicab** to the market."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang bayad sa **pedicab** mula rito hanggang sa kanto?","translation":"How much is the **pedicab** fare from here to the corner?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng pagtataka, panggigilalas, o pagkamangha sa iba.
original_explanation: This is a bit of a deep cut. It's not something you *do* intentionally like 'magpatawa' (to make someone laugh). It's more like your actions or a situation *causes* people to wonder. For example, 'Ang bigla niyang pagyaman ay nagpataka sa kanyang mga kapitbahay.' (His sudden wealth caused his neighbors to wonder). It's the verb form of making people go 'Hmm, anong meron?'
usage_notes: Less common in everyday conversation than its root 'taka' (wonder) or the adjective 'nakapagtataka' (puzzling). It implies an indirect causation of wonder. The more common form is 'makapagpataka'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga kakaibang kilos ay **nagpataka** sa amin.","translation":"His strange actions **caused us to wonder**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumawa ng bagay na **magpapataka** sa iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Don't do anything that will **make your parents wonder/suspicious**."}]

translation: to be placed in the friend zone
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging itinalaga sa 'friendzone'; ang kilos ng paglalagay sa isang tao sa nasabing sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The past tense of your romantic hopes and dreams. It's the official status update when your crush says, 'Ang sweet mo talaga... para kang kapatid ko.' You've been officially knighted as 'Sir/Ma'am Hanggang Kaibigan Lang.'
usage_notes: Used to describe the state of being in the friend zone or the act of putting someone there. Can function as a verb in Taglish sentences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabi niya na mahal niya ako bilang kaibigan. Ayun, na-**friendzoned**.","translation":"She said she loves me as a friend. And there, I got **friendzoned**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo naman akong i-**friendzoned**.","translation":"Please don't **friendzone** me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at malalim na mangkok, karaniwang may takip, na ginagamit para pagsilbihan ng sabaw o sopas.
original_explanation: That big, fancy bowl your lola brings out only during Noche Buena or special occasions. It's the "bahay" of the sopas or sinigang before it gets distributed into individual bowls. It usually comes with a matching ladle. Kung sa modern terms, ito 'yung "server" ng ulam na may sabaw.
usage_notes: Isang salitang hindi na gaanong karaniwan, dahil marami ang tumutukoy na lamang dito bilang "lalagyan ng sopas" o "serving bowl".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilipat niya ang nilutong sinigang sa **sopera**.","translation":"She transferred the cooked sinigang into the **tureen**."},{"sentence":"Nabasag ang takip ng mamahaling **sopera** na minana pa niya sa kanyang lola.","translation":"The lid of the expensive **tureen** she inherited from her grandmother broke."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan inaalagaan ang mga sanggol at maliliit na bata; o isang lugar kung saan pinalalaki at ibinebenta ang mga halaman.
original_explanation: Two main meanings: 1) The daycare or playroom for babies, the 'start-up incubator' for future kulit kids. 2) The place where 'plantitos' and 'plantitas' go to heaven—a garden center filled with baby plants waiting for a new home.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay nakadepende sa konteksto, maaaring para sa mga bata o para sa mga halaman.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniwan muna namin ang bunso sa **nursery** ng simbahan habang may misa.","translation":"We left the youngest at the church **nursery** during the mass."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng mga bagong halaman sa **nursery** sa tabing daan.","translation":"I bought new plants at the roadside **nursery**."}]

translation: Drawing tool; something used for drawing
meaning_filipino: Anumang kasangkapan o kagamitan na ginagamit sa paggawa ng mga linya o marka, tulad ng lapis, bolpen, o ruler.
original_explanation: Anything you can draw with. Your Mongol No. 2 pencil, your Pilot G-Tec, your kid sibling's Crayola, your Wacom stylus, or even a piece of charcoal. If it makes a line, it's a `pangguhit`. It's the official tool for doodling during a boring meeting or lecture.
usage_notes: A general term that can encompass a wide variety of drawing or writing instruments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang paborito kong **pangguhit** kaya hindi ako makapag-drawing.","translation":"My favorite **drawing tool** is missing, so I can't draw."},{"sentence":"Ang mga arkitekto ay gumagamit ng iba't ibang **pangguhit** para sa kanilang mga plano.","translation":"Architects use various **drawing tools** for their plans."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay o paggawa ng isang resibo para sa isang transaksyon o pagbabayad.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of getting that precious piece of paper. When the tindera asks "Resibuhan ko, Ma'am/Sir?" she's asking if you need proof of purchase. In the corporate world, this is what the accounting department hunts you down for. No resibo, no reimbursement. So yes, please, resibihin mo.
usage_notes: The '-in' suffix marks the object being 'receipted' as the focus of the verb. Can also mean 'to receive something', but 'to issue a receipt for' is a common, specific usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **resibihin** lahat ng gastusin para sa iyong business trip.","translation":"You need to **get a receipt for** all the expenses for your business trip."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **resibihin** ninyo ang bayad ko.","translation":"Please, **issue me a receipt** for my payment."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng may kleptomania, isang karamdaman sa pag-iisip na nag-uudyok sa isang tao na magnakaw nang hindi dahil sa pangangailangan kundi dahil sa hindi mapigilang salpok.
original_explanation: Siya 'yung kakilala mong babae na bigla na lang may nawawalang ballpen sa desk mo 'pag umalis siya. Ang 'kleptomana' ay may sakit na pagnanakaw—hindi dahil masama siyang tao o kailangan niya 'yung bagay, kundi dahil may urge siyang hindi mapigilan. It's a mental health issue, not just simple theft.
usage_notes: Ang hulaping '-a' ay nagpapahiwatig ng kasariang pambabae, isang katangiang minana mula sa Espanyol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang pamilya kung paano tutulungan ang **kleptomana** na malampasan ang kanyang kondisyon.","translation":"The doctor advised the family on how to help the **kleptomaniac** (female) overcome her condition."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyong lupa na nakausli o nakaabot sa dagat o lawa.
original_explanation: Think of a piece of land that's being a 'pasaway' and jutting out into the water. It’s that pointy part of the coastline you see on maps, perfect for lighthouses or dramatic movie scenes where the hero stares out into the sea contemplating their life choices.
usage_notes: A geographical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May parola sa dulo ng **tangos**.","translation":"There is a lighthouse at the end of the **cape**."},{"sentence":"Maganda ang tanawin mula sa tuktok ng **tangos**.","translation":"The view from the top of the **promontory** is beautiful."}]

translation: to cause to stumble or falter repeatedly
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng paulit-ulit na pagtigil o pagkabalam sa paglakad o pag-usad.
original_explanation: This is you trying to walk on a rocky beach in flip-flops. Or trying to explain something complicated but you keep losing your train of thought. It's a start-stop, jerky motion, like a buffering video stream on a 1Mbps connection.
usage_notes: The root 'untol' means a halt or stop. Reduplication signifies repetition or intermittence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang baku-bakong daan ay **mapauntul-untol** sa sinumang maglalakad.","translation":"The uneven road will **cause anyone walking to stumble repeatedly**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kaba, siya ay **mapauntul-untol** sa kanyang talumpati.","translation":"Because of nervousness, he **kept faltering** in his speech."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lalagyan ng inumin, karaniwang may takip, na idinisenyo upang mapanatili ang temperatura ng likido sa loob nito, mainit man o malamig.
original_explanation: The official accessory of every BPO agent, student, and tita in Manila. It's not just a water bottle; it's a status symbol. The bigger and more branded your tumbler, the more hydrated and 'put-together' you seem. Losing your tumbler is a modern-day tragedy.
usage_notes: A very common English loanword that has been fully adopted into Filipino everyday language.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan ang **tumbler** mo para may mainom kang malamig na tubig sa gym.","translation":"Don't forget your **tumbler** so you have cold water to drink at the gym."},{"sentence":"Puno ng kape ang **tumbler** ko para magising ako sa night shift.","translation":"My **tumbler** is full of coffee to keep me awake during the night shift."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagsasaad ng kilos na mag-iiwan ng komento o puna sa hinaharap, karaniwan sa social media.
original_explanation: The threat you make under your breath when you see a ridiculously wrong post online. 'Ay, 'pag 'di ako busy mamaya, magcocomment talaga ako diyan.' It’s the future tense of online bardagulan (brawling).
usage_notes: This is the future tense of 'magcomment'. It is exclusively used in the context of social media or online forums.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magcocomment** ako sa post mo mamaya pagkatapos ng trabaho.","translation":"I **will comment** on your post later after work."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **magcocomment** kung wala kang magandang sasabihin.","translation":"Don't **comment** if you have nothing nice to say."}]

translation: to trust, to have faith in
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng matibay na paniniwala at pagtitiwala sa isang tao, bagay, o higit sa lahat, sa Diyos.
original_explanation: This is your 'bahala na si Batman' but with more spiritual conviction. It's the trust you put in your team during a do-or-die presentation, or the faith you have that your GrabFood order will arrive despite the rain. It's holding on to a belief even when the odds are stacked against you.
usage_notes: Often has a spiritual or religious connotation, synonymous with 'manampalataya', but can be used in a secular context for deep trust.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **manalig** na malalampasan din natin ang pagsubok na ito.","translation":"We need to **trust** that we will also overcome this trial."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **nananalig** sa kakayahan ng kanyang mga anak.","translation":"She **has faith in** the abilities of her children."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na tumutukoy sa isang lugar o lokasyon na hindi tiyak, hindi pinangalanan, o bilang panimula sa isang sugnay na naglalarawan ng lugar.
original_explanation: The GPS of Tagalog sentences, but for when you don't have the exact address. It's for pointing to a general direction, a vague memory of a place, or just anywhere but here. 'Pumunta ka **kung saan** ka magiging masaya' is the ultimate hugot line for letting go.
usage_notes: Used to introduce a clause about an unknown or unspecified place (wherever), or a specific but relative place (where).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumalik siya sa probinsya **kung saan** siya lumaki.","translation":"He returned to the province **where** he grew up."},{"sentence":"Itapon mo 'yan **kung saan** hindi makikita ng bata.","translation":"Throw that away **wherever** a child won't see it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ahensya o organisasyon ng pamahalaan na responsable sa pagpapatupad ng batas at pagpapanatili ng kaayusan; maaari ring tumukoy sa gusali o istasyon ng pulis.
original_explanation: This is the whole squad, the entire organization. If 'pulis' is one Avenger, 'pulisya' is the whole Avengers Initiative. It also refers to the police station itself, a.k.a. "presinto." So if someone says "Dinala siya sa pulisya," it means he was taken to the station.
usage_notes: Distinct from 'pulis' (the person). 'Pulisya' refers to the institution or the place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagreklamo siya sa **pulisya** tungkol sa nawawala niyang pitaka.","translation":"She filed a complaint with the **police** about her missing wallet."},{"sentence":"Ang Philippine National Police o PNP ang pambansang **pulisya** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The Philippine National Police or PNP is the national **police force** of the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng nagtatrabaho sa isang restawran o kainan na ang tungkulin ay kumuha ng order, maghatid ng pagkain at inumin, at asikasuhin ang mga pangangailangan ng mga kostumer.
original_explanation: The female counterpart of the serbidor. Siya yung ate na ngingitian ka kahit pang-sampung beses mo nang tinanong kung may 'service water'. She balances multiple tables, remembers who ordered the diet coke, and does it all without breaking a sweat. A true multi-tasking queen.
usage_notes: Partikular na tumutukoy sa babaeng serber.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magalang na kinuha ng **serbidora** ang aming mga order.","translation":"The **waitress** politely took our orders."}]

translation: to cause someone to go crazy/mad
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng pagkawala sa tamang pag-iisip o pagkasira ng ulo ng isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping 'ika-' (panlaping sanhi) at 'baliw' (crazy, insane).
original_explanation: Usually used as a hyperbole for when something is driving you nuts. "Yung traffic sa EDSA, ikinabaliw ko na!" It's the feeling of being pushed to your absolute mental limit by a person, a situation, or a slow internet connection during a crucial Zoom meeting.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang sanhi. Maaari itong gamitin nang literal, ngunit mas madalas itong ginagamit sa matalinhagang paraan upang ipahayag ang matinding pagkadismaya o pagkahumaling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sobrang selos ay maaaring **ikabaliw** ng isang tao.","translation":"Excessive jealousy can **cause a person to go mad**."},{"sentence":"**Ikinabaliw** ng mga tagahanga ang paglabas ng kanilang paboritong banda.","translation":"The fans **went crazy** over the appearance of their favorite band."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o pag-uugali ng pagpapakita ng kayabangan, pagmamalaki, o pagiging arogante.
etymology: From "sikal" (arrogance, boastfulness). The verbal noun is formed through reduplication and the "paN-" prefix.
original_explanation: That feeling when someone posts their new iPhone, condo, and Euro trip all in one day. That's the vibe. It's the act of being 'mayabang' or flexing too hard, to the point that it's annoying. The 'look at me, I'm better than you' energy.
usage_notes: A less common term for "kayabangan" or "pagyayabang".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi maganda ang labis na **paninikal** sa kapwa.","translation":"Excessive **boasting** towards others is not good."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **paninikal** ang dahilan kung bakit iilan lang ang tunay niyang kaibigan.","translation":"His **arrogance** is the reason why he has only a few true friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estruktura, tulad ng estatwa o gusali, na itinayo upang parangalan ang isang tao o gunitain ang isang mahalagang pangyayari.
original_explanation: That big statue in the middle of the plaza that everyone uses as a meeting point? That's a "munumento". It's the ultimate landmark, usually of a hero riding a horse or holding a sword. In modern terms, your crush's IG profile is a "munumento" to their glorious life that you visit daily for "research purposes".
usage_notes: A direct loanword, used in formal contexts related to history, art, and architecture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **munumento** ni Rizal sa Luneta ay isang tanyag na pasyalan.","translation":"The Rizal **monument** in Luneta is a famous landmark."},{"sentence":"Nag-alay sila ng mga bulaklak sa paanan ng **munumento** ng mga bayani.","translation":"They offered flowers at the foot of the heroes' **monument**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hayag, lantad, at walang anumang pagtatangka na itago; kawalan ng hiya sa paggawa ng isang bagay sa publiko.
etymology: From 'lantad' (exposed) with the 'ka-...-an' circumfix, which creates a noun denoting a quality or state.
original_explanation: This is the 'walang hiya' mode, full-on display for everyone to see. It's that couple doing PDA level 99 in the MRT. It's the politician's corruption na 'harap-harapan'. It’s posting your whole breakup drama on social media, complete with screenshots. No more secrets, it's all out in the open. 'Ang kalantaran ng kanilang away sa Facebook, mas maganda pa sa teleserye!'
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation, implying shamelessness or indecency in an open, public manner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko matiis ang **kalantaran** ng kanilang pag-uugali sa harap ng mga bata.","translation":"I can't stand the **blatantness** of their behavior in front of the children."},{"sentence":"Ang **kalantaran** ng pagnanakaw sa gobyerno ay nakakagalit.","translation":"The **flagrancy** of theft in the government is infuriating."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay, isyu, o usapin na konektado o nababatay sa mga prinsipyo at probisyon ng konstitusyon ng isang bansa.
original_explanation: This is the phrase you hear from lawyers on TV, politicians giving speeches, or your very serious friend in law school. It's the ultimate "This is a big deal" qualifier for any legal or political issue. If something is "may kaugnayan sa saligang-batas," it's not just simple chismis; it's national-level, primetime-news-worthy drama.
usage_notes: A formal phrase used in legal, academic, and political discourse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng Korte Suprema ang mga kasong **may kaugnayan sa saligang-batas**.","translation":"The Supreme Court is studying the cases **related to the constitution**."},{"sentence":"Ang isyu ng pagbabago sa termino ng pangulo ay isang usaping **may kaugnayan sa saligang-batas**.","translation":"The issue of changing the presidential term is a matter that is **constitutional**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging maselan, mabusisi, o labis na pagbibigay-pansin sa maliliit na detalye, na kung minsan ay humahantong sa pagiging 'nitpicky'.
etymology: From `ka-` + `busisi` (to scrutinize, meticulous) + `-an`, forming an abstract noun for the state of being meticulous.
original_explanation: This is the energy of your boss who asks you to revise the report for the 10th time because the font size is 11.5 instead of 12. It's that tita who inspects your house for dust with a white glove. It can be a good thing (detail-oriented) or a bad thing (OCD, nitpicky). It's the opposite of the "pwede na 'yan" culture.
usage_notes: Can have either a positive connotation (thoroughness) or a negative one (being overly fussy) depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang **kabusisian** pagdating sa trabaho.","translation":"She is known for her **meticulousness** when it comes to work."},{"sentence":"Naiinis ako sa sobrang **kabusisian** niya sa lahat ng bagay.","translation":"I get annoyed with his extreme **fussiness** about everything."}]

meaning_filipino: Isagawa ang pagtutupi o paglilipit ng isang bagay, tulad ng damit o papel.
original_explanation: This is your number one household chore nemesis. The endless pile of laundry that needs folding. "Magtitiklop" is the act of turning a mountain of chaotic clothes into neat little squares that you'll probably mess up by tomorrow morning looking for your favorite shirt.
usage_notes: Commonly used for clothes, paper, and other foldable items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos maglaba, kailangan mo pang **magtitiklop** ng mga damit.","translation":"After doing the laundry, you still have to **fold** the clothes."},{"sentence":"**Magtitiklop** ako ng mga sulat at ilalagay sa sobre.","translation":"I will **fold** the letters and put them in an envelope."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang delikadong tela na gawa sa sinulid o hibla sa isang bukas na parang web na pattern, na ginawa sa pamamagitan ng makina o kamay.
original_explanation: Yung materyal sa damit ng lola mo, sa panyo, o sa kurtina na parang gawa sa sapot ng gagamba pero maganda version. Staple sa mga disenyo ng Barong Tagalog at Filipiniana. Minsan, ito rin 'yung design sa punda ng unan na ayaw mong gamitin kasi baka masira.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa pananahi at disenyo ng damit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang damit pangkasal niya ay may mga palamuting **engkahe**.","translation":"Her wedding dress had **lace** decorations."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang nilabhan ang lumang mantel na may **engkahe**.","translation":"She carefully washed the old tablecloth with **lace**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pagkakapareho, pag-aangkop, o pagiging akma sa isa pa. Ito ay tumutukoy sa isang kilos na tapos na.
original_explanation: Like when your outfit finally matches your mood (all black). Or when the numbers in your spreadsheet finally tally and you can go home. It's the "click" you feel when you meet someone with the same weird sense of humor. It's the opposite of that feeling when you use the wrong charger for your phone.
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **tumugma** ang aming mga iskedyul.","translation":"Finally, our schedules **matched**."},{"sentence":"Hindi **tumugma** ang kanyang salaysay sa ebidensya.","translation":"His statement did not **correspond** with the evidence."}]

translation: to ask for something on someone's behalf
meaning_filipino: Humingi ng isang bagay para sa kapakanan o para sa ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'pasabay' verb. It's when you ask for something, not for yourself, but for someone else. 'Pumunta ka sa office ni Ma'am? Pwede mo ba akong ihingi ng form?' (You're going to Ma'am's office? Can you ask for a form for me?). It's the verb for wingmen, helpful friends, and kids asking their mom to ask their dad for something.
usage_notes: The structure is `ihingi (ng something) (ang/si person)`. Example: `Ihingi mo ng tubig si Lola.` (Ask for water for Lola.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pwede mo ba akong **ihingi** ng tawad kay Ana?","translation":"Can you **ask for** forgiveness from Ana **on my behalf**?"},{"sentence":"**Ihingi** mo ng dagdag na kanin ang kapatid mo.","translation":"**Ask for** more rice **for** your sibling."}]

translation: To spread or stretch out one's arms.
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-unat ng dalawang braso patagilid, palayo sa katawan, na parang bumubuo ng isang tuwid na linya.
etymology: From root word "dipa" (the length of outstretched arms, a fathom).
original_explanation: The classic "Titanic" pose: "I'm the king of the world!" That's *dumipa*. It's also what you do when someone's measuring your arm span, or when you're trying to stop people from passing through a narrow hallway. It's the human version of spreading your wings.
usage_notes: "Dipa" as a noun is a unit of measurement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumipa** siya para yakapin ang kanyang mga anak.","translation":"She **stretched out her arms** to hug her children."},{"sentence":"Pinatayo kami at pinagawa ng ehersisyong **dumipa** at yumuko.","translation":"They made us stand up and do an exercise of **stretching out our arms** and bending over."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang panginginig ng katawan dahil sa lamig, takot, sakit, o matinding emosyon.
original_explanation: Eto yung feeling mo kapag sobrang lakas ng aircon sa office, o nung nag-confess ka sa crush mo. Pwede ring dahil sa takot nung nanood ka ng horror movie mag-isa. Your body is doing the cha-cha against your will.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa "nanginginig".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nangangatog** siya sa ginaw dahil hindi siya nagdala ng dyaket.","translation":"He was **shivering** from the cold because he didn't bring a jacket."},{"sentence":"**Nangangatog** ang kanyang mga tuhod habang naghihintay ng resulta ng exam.","translation":"His knees were **trembling** while waiting for the exam results."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na napudpod, numipis, o nasira dahil sa patuloy na pagkiskis, paggamit, o pagyurak.
original_explanation: This is the state of your favorite t-shirt after being worn 1,000 times. It's the condition of the doormat that has seen too many shoes. Or your patience at the end of a long work week. **Yatyat** means it's been rubbed the wrong way (literally) so many times that it's now thin, frayed, and about to give up. The physical form of 'pagod na ako.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe fabric, ropes, or other materials that degrade from friction. Can also be a verb root ('yatyatin' - to wear something out).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **yatyat** na ang laylayan ng kanyang lumang pantalon.","translation":"The hem of his old pants has become **frayed**."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang gamit, **yatyat** na ang lubid.","translation":"From so much use, the rope is now **worn-out**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa hinaharap na kilos ng isang halaman na mamumukadkad o maglalabas ng bulaklak.
original_explanation: This is the "glow up" for plants. It's the future tense of blooming. It’s what you hope your sampaguita plant will do. Metaphorically, it's what your parents hope you'll do after they've invested so much in your education—you will finally "magbubulaklak" and become successful. It's the promise of beauty and fruition after a period of growth.
usage_notes: Future tense of "mamulaklak". The "mag-" prefix is also used here.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa tagsibol, **magbubulaklak** na ang mga puno ng cherry.","translation":"In spring, the cherry trees **will bloom**."},{"sentence":"Alagaan mo 'yang halaman at tiyak na **magbubulaklak** 'yan.","translation":"Take care of that plant and it **will surely flower**."}]

translation: to become infrequent, to become scarce
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging bihira o pagbaba ng dalas ng pag-iral, paglitaw, o pagganap ng isang bagay o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your friend's 'paramdam' after they get into a new relationship. Their messages and calls start to dumalang. It's the 'minsan na lang' feeling. It can be about anything that becomes less frequent—the rain during summer, your salary by the 15th, or plot twists in a predictable teleserye.
usage_notes: Used to describe something that used to be frequent but is now happening less often.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumalang** na ang kanyang pagbisita mula nang lumipat siya ng bahay.","translation":"His visits have **become infrequent** ever since he moved."},{"sentence":"Habang papalapit ang tag-araw, **dumadalang** ang pag-ulan.","translation":"As summer approaches, the rain **becomes more scarce**."}]

translation: to be respectful; to show respect
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng pagpapahalaga, pitagan, o kortesiya sa kapwa, lalo na sa mga nakatatanda.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'po' and 'opo'. It’s the action of 'mano po'. It's calling your older sister 'ate' and the guy at the BPO pantry 'kuya'. To 'maggalang' is to practice one of the core Filipino values, showing deference and kindness, especially to elders. It's respect, but in verb form.
usage_notes: A foundational verb in Filipino culture and ethics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuruan kami ng aming mga magulang na **maggalang** sa mga nakatatanda.","translation":"Our parents taught us **to be respectful** of our elders."},{"sentence":"Dapat kang **maggalang** sa opinyon ng iba kahit hindi ka sang-ayon.","translation":"You should **show respect** for the opinions of others even if you don't agree."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong naghahanda at naghahain ng mga inuming may alkohol sa isang bar o restawran.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of your Friday night out. Sila yung tiga-timpla ng pamatay-sakit mo after a rough week, or your celebratory drink 'pag may good news. They're part chemist, part therapist, and 100% patient with your drunken "isa pa nga!" requests.
usage_notes: Isang direktang hiram na salita, karaniwang ginagamit sa pormal at impormal na mga sitwasyon sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling mag-mix ng cocktail ang **bartender** sa bagong bukas na bar.","translation":"The **bartender** at the newly opened bar is great at mixing cocktails."},{"sentence":"Nag-apply siya bilang **bartender** sa isang hotel.","translation":"He applied as a **bartender** at a hotel."}]

translation: to be cast as the lead; to be the main character
meaning_filipino: Ang mapili o gumanap bilang pangunahing tauhan sa isang palabas, pelikula, o kwento.
etymology: From "ma-" (prefix) + "bida" (from Spanish "vida" meaning life, but in Filipino context means "protagonist").
original_explanation: 'Yung friend mong laging nagpo-post ng "main character energy"? Gusto laging mabida. It means to be the star of the show, whether literally in a movie or figuratively in a group project or a family drama.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for actors or figuratively for someone who likes to be the center of attention.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap ng bawat artista na **mabida** sa isang blockbuster na pelikula.","translation":"It's every actor's dream to **be cast as the lead** in a blockbuster movie."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mo namang **mabida** ang iba, hindi laging ikaw ang sentro ng usapan.","translation":"Let others **be the main character** for once; you're not always the center of the conversation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbigkas ng mga salita sa isang tao, kadalasan sa paraang pagalit, upang pagsabihan o ituwid ang isang pagkakamali.
original_explanation: Ito yung moment na sesermunan ka ng nanay mo dahil gabi ka na umuwi. 'Huwag mo akong pagsalitaan nang ganyan!' is the classic line of someone who feels disrespected, usually after being told a hard truth. It's the verbal version of a manager's 'Please see me in my office.'
usage_notes: The focus is on the person being spoken to. Often carries a negative or confrontational connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagsalitaan** nang masakit ang iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Do not **speak to** your parents harshly."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan niya ang kapatid na huwag siyang **pagsalitaan** sa harap ng mga bisita.","translation":"He told his sibling not to **tell him off** in front of the guests."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdama o pagsalat sa isang bagay o tao gamit ang kamay o ibang bahagi ng katawan.
etymology: From pang- (nominalizing prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root + hipo (touch, caress).
original_explanation: This word is a bit tricky. On one hand, it's just touching something, like feeling the texture of a fabric. On the other, darker hand, it's the word used for unwanted touching or groping. It's the reason for the "Bawal manghipo" signs. Context is everything; it can go from innocent to criminal real quick.
usage_notes: Can be neutral, but often carries a negative connotation of inappropriate or unwanted touching, especially in legal and social contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng **panghihipo**, natukoy ng bulag na bata ang hugis ng laruan.","translation":"Through the **act of touching**, the blind child identified the shape of the toy."},{"sentence":"May kaso siyang kinakaharap dahil sa **panghihipo**.","translation":"He is facing a case because of **groping**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kakanin na gawa sa galapong at gata, na may iba't ibang kulay sa bawat patong; tumutukoy din sa mga bagay na magkakapatong-patong.
original_explanation: First, it's that delicious, colorful, chewy kakanin with latik on top. Ube, langka, and white layers fighting for your attention. Second, it's a metaphor for anything with a lot of layers, like your 'toxic' work environment, your complicated love life, or the 'resibo' (receipts/proof) you've collected against a frenemy. 'Grabe, sapinsapin ang problema niya.'
usage_notes: Can be literal (the food) or figurative (layers of problems, clothes, etc.). When used figuratively, it is often synonymous with 'patong-patong'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong panghimagas ang **sapinsapin**.","translation":"My favorite dessert is the **layered rice cake (sapinsapin)**."},{"sentence":"Hinarap niya ang **sapinsapin** na problema sa opisina.","translation":"He faced the **layers** of problems at the office."}]

translation: come to think of it; as a matter of fact
meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na ginagamit sa pagpapakilala ng isang bagong punto o realisasyon na sumusuporta o nagpapabago sa naunang pahayag.
etymology: Combination of 'kung' (if), 'sa' (in/on), and 'bagay' (thing/matter). Literally 'if in the matter of'.
original_explanation: The 'Actually...' or 'On second thought...' of Tagalog conversation. It's the pivot point in an argument with your jowa, or when you suddenly realize something important in the middle of a chismis session. 'Ay, oo nga no... **kung sa bagay**...'
usage_notes: Used to introduce a counter-point, a clarification, or a sudden realization that adds nuance to a conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ko sanang sumama, pero **kung sa bagay**, masaya rin sigurong manood ng sine.","translation":"**Come to think of it**, it might be fun to watch a movie, even though I didn't want to go initially."},{"sentence":"Mahal ang bilihin ngayon. **Kung sa bagay**, noon pa man ay mataas na talaga ang presyo.","translation":"Prices are high today. **As a matter of fact**, prices have always been high."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang sapat na dahilan, ebidensya, o katotohanan na sumusuporta.
original_explanation: The official term for "chismis" from a "Marites." It's that accusation your friend makes based on a cryptic IG story. It's a conclusion built on pure vibes and zero facts. "Source: trust me, bro." That's a 'walang-batayan' claim right there.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang mga paratang, tsismis, o takot na walang katibayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga paratang laban sa kanya ay napatunayang **walang-batayan**.","translation":"The accusations against him were proven to be **baseless**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa mga balitang **walang-batayan**.","translation":"Don't believe in **unfounded** news."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikipag-usap o pag-aalay ng kahilingan, pasasalamat, o papuri sa isang kinikilalang Diyos o mas mataas na kapangyarihan.
etymology: From the verb 'manalangin' (to pray), which is rooted in 'dalangin' (prayer). The noun `pananalangin` refers to the act itself.
original_explanation: This is your direct line to the 'higher ups.' It's what you do before an exam you didn't study for, when you're stuck in EDSA traffic and about to be late, or when you're hoping your online shopping order arrives today. It's the spiritual version of sending a very important email.
usage_notes: 'Dasal' is a more common, everyday synonym. 'Pananalangin' sounds more formal, profound, and is often used in religious services or formal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang taos-pusong **pananalangin** ay nagbibigay ng kapayapaan sa isip.","translation":"Sincere **prayer** brings peace of mind."},{"sentence":"Sama-sama tayong mag-alay ng isang **pananalangin** para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"Let us offer a collective **prayer** for the typhoon victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghahalo ng iba't ibang sangkap upang makamit ang tamang lasa, balanse, o temperatura, lalo na sa mga inumin o pagkain.
original_explanation: This is your inner chemist/bartender coming out. It's the art of mixing your 3-in-1 coffee to the perfect consistency, getting the right amount of sugar in your iced tea, or balancing the salt and pepper in your adobo. One wrong move and you've ruined the whole batch. It's a high-stakes kitchen operation.
usage_notes: Can refer to mixing drinks, seasoning food, or even tempering one's mood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling sa **pagtitimpla** ng cocktail ang bartender na iyon.","translation":"That bartender is great at **mixing** cocktails."},{"sentence":"Si nanay ang bahala sa **pagtitimpla** ng sauce para sa spaghetti.","translation":"Mom is in charge of **seasoning** the sauce for the spaghetti."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng halaman na sumusuporta sa dahon, bulaklak, o bunga; ang pinakapunong bahagi ng isang bagay na manipis at mahaba.
original_explanation: The "handle" of a flower or fruit. When you give someone a rose, you're holding it by the tangkay. It's also that part of the kangkong your lola tells you to cut off, or the part of the cherry you try to tie into a knot with your tongue.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat niyang hinawakan ang **tangkay** ng rosas upang hindi matinik.","translation":"She carefully held the **stem** of the rose to avoid the thorns."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong isama ang matitigas na **tangkay** ng kangkong sa luto.","translation":"Don't include the tough **stalks** of the water spinach in the dish."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng isang problema o suliranin na nabigyan na ng solusyon o kasagutan.
original_explanation: The feeling of relief after you finally figure out a complex Excel formula or untangle your earphones. It's the 'Aha!' moment when a problem is no more. When your conflict with a friend is resolved, 'Lutas na.' When the mystery of the missing Tupperware lid is solved, 'Lutas na ang kaso.' It's the satisfying end to a struggle.
usage_notes: Often used with 'na' (lutas na). The verb form is 'lutasin' (to solve).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **lutas** na ang matagal na naming problema sa tubig.","translation":"Finally, our long-standing problem with the water supply is **solved**."}]

meaning_filipino: Panghalip panao na tumutukoy sa dalawang tao: ang nagsasalita at ang kinakausap. Isang pinagsamang anyo ng 'ko' at 'ka'.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'you and me against the world' pronoun. It's more intimate than 'tayo' (which includes everyone else). 'Kita' is the pronoun for secret plans, inside jokes, and sweet nothings whispered between two people. When someone says 'Mahal kita,' it's a direct line from their heart (ko) to yours (ka).
usage_notes: A dual pronoun that combines the actor 'ko' (I) and the object 'ka' (you). For example, 'Bibigyan kita' means 'I will give you'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal **kita**.","translation":"I love **you**."},{"sentence":"Tutulungan **kita** sa iyong takdang-aralin.","translation":"I will help **you** with your homework."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o gawain ng labis na paggasta o pag-aaksaya ng pera, yaman, o anumang mapagkukunan nang walang pag-iingat o pagtitimpi.
etymology: From the prefix `ka-` (indicating an abstract quality) and `bulagsak` (wasteful, prodigal).
original_explanation: This is when your 'treat yourself' mentality goes into overdrive. It's buying the latest iPhone when your old one is fine, ordering everything on the menu for a TikTok video, or swiping your credit card like it's an unlimited free pass. The opposite of being 'wais' or 'kuripot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang iyong **kabulagsakan** at mag-ipon ka para sa kinabukasan.","translation":"Stop your **wastefulness** and save for the future."},{"sentence":"Ang **kabulagsakan** sa paggamit ng kuryente ay nagpapalaki ng ating bayarin.","translation":"The **extravagance** in using electricity increases our bills."}]

translation: to have something (an animal) killed/slaughtered for a purpose
meaning_filipino: Mag-utos o maging dahilan ng pagpatay sa isang hayop para sa isang tiyak na okasyon, layunin, o selebrasyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `i-` (nagsasaad ng sanhi), `pagpa-` (nagsasaad ng sanhi), at `patay` (dead).
original_explanation: This is what happens before a big fiesta or handaan. "Uy, birthday ni lolo, **ipagpatay** natin siya ng baboy!" It's the act of commissioning the slaughter of an animal (usually a pig, chicken, or goat) for a feast. It's not about the killing itself, but about preparing for a celebration.
usage_notes: Halos eksklusibong ginagamit para sa pagkatay ng mga hayop para kainin, karaniwan para sa isang espesyal na kaganapan. Ang tao/kaganapan kung para kanino kinatay ang hayop ay ang di-tuwirang layon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-order si Mayor na **ipagpatay** ng sampung baka ang mga bisita para sa pista.","translation":"The Mayor ordered to **have ten cows slaughtered for** the guests for the fiesta."},{"sentence":"**Ipinagpatay** kami ni Tatay ng manok para sa aming tanghalian.","translation":"Father **had a chicken killed for** us for our lunch."}]

translation: to be able to borrow money; to be able to get something on credit
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang makahiram ng pera o bagay mula sa isang tao o institusyon, na may kasunduang ito ay isasauli o babayaran sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: 'Yung skill na na-unlock mo kapag petsa de peligro na pero may tiwala pa rin sa'yo si Aling Nena sa tindahan. "Lista mo na lang muna, ija." It's not just about borrowing; it's about having good credit, kahit sa sari-sari store level.
usage_notes: The prefix 'ma-' here indicates ability or potential. It's different from 'umutang' (to borrow) or 'mangutang' (to borrow, often habitually).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay may **mautang** ako para sa matrikula ng anak ko.","translation":"I hope I can **borrow money** for my child's tuition."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **makautang** kung wala kang maipapakitang patunay ng kita.","translation":"It's hard to **be able to get a loan** if you can't show proof of income."}]

translation: to break a promise, to renege
meaning_filipino: Hindi tumupad sa isang pangako, kasunduan, o salitang binitiwan.
original_explanation: The ultimate friendship-ender. When your friend says 'libre kita next time' and 'next time' never comes. Or when someone promises 'ikaw lang, sapat na' but ends up having a '2nd-quarter new project'. It's the act of being 'paasa' (one who leads someone on).
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of betrayal and untrustworthiness. 'Talusira' as a noun or adjective refers to a person who does this.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang kasalanan ang **magtalusira** sa isang sagradong panata.","translation":"It is a sin **to break** a sacred vow."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya mapagkakatiwalaan dahil sanay siyang **magtalusira** sa usapan.","translation":"He cannot be trusted because he is used **to reneging** on agreements."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, kumpanya, o bansa na gumagawa, naglilinang, o nagbibigay ng mga kalakal o serbisyo. Sa sining, siya ang namamahala sa pinansyal at administratibong aspeto ng isang produksyon.
original_explanation: Siya yung may pera. Sa pelikula o TV show, siya yung naghahanap ng pondo para matuloy ang prodyek. Sa negosyo, siya yung manufacturer. Basically, sila ang "The Provider" ng team. Pag wala sila, drawing lang lahat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **prodyuser** ng pelikula ang pumili sa mga artistang gaganap.","translation":"The movie's **producer** chose the actors who will perform."},{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay isa sa mga nangungunang **prodyuser** ng niyog sa buong mundo.","translation":"The Philippines is one of the top **producers** of coconut in the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang gamot, inumin, o substansiya na nagdudulot ng pagpapakalma, pagpapatulog, o pagbabawas ng pagkabalisa.
original_explanation: The medical term for "pampatulog" or "pampakalma." Ito 'yung iniinom mo kapag 'di ka na makatulog dahil sa anxiety sa trabaho, o 'yung binibigay sa aso mong maingay tuwing may paputok sa New Year. Basically, a chill pill, literally.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a substance, not a state of being.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan ng doktor ng **kalmante** ang pasyenteng hindi mapakali.","translation":"The doctor gave a **sedative** to the restless patient."},{"sentence":"Mabisa ang **kalmante**ng ito para sa mga may matinding pagkabalisa.","translation":"This **tranquilizer** is effective for those with severe anxiety."}]

translation: to be found, to be located
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakita o pagkatuklas sa eksaktong lokasyon ng isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: What you hope happens when you use 'Find My iPhone.' It's also the goal of every 'tropa' trying to find that one hidden gem of a restaurant. 'Saan **matatagpuan** ang Jollibee dito?' is the first question of any Pinoy tourist abroad.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The actor-focus counterpart is 'makahanap' (to be able to find).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan po **matatagpuan** ang pinakamalapit na istasyon ng MRT?","translation":"Where can the nearest MRT station **be found**?"},{"sentence":"Hindi **matagpuan** ni Ana ang kanyang mga susi kahit saan.","translation":"Ana's keys cannot **be found** anywhere. (Ana cannot find her keys anywhere.)"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng mga paa o kuko upang maghalungkat o maghanap ng isang bagay sa lupa o sa isang bunton.
original_explanation: This is the signature move of a chicken looking for worms or your dog frantically trying to find where it buried that bone. It's also you, at 2 AM, doing a pagkaykay through the fridge for leftovers. It’s a chaotic, sometimes desperate, search.
usage_notes: Often associated with animals, but can be used metaphorically for rummaging through things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaykay** ng manok sa hardin ay nakakainis dahil sinisira nito ang mga halaman.","translation":"The chicken's **scratching** in the garden is annoying because it destroys the plants."},{"sentence":"Matapos ang isang oras na **pagkaykay** sa mga lumang papeles, nahanap din niya ang birth certificate niya.","translation":"After an hour of **rummaging** through old papers, he finally found his birth certificate."}]

meaning_filipino: Papunta sa wakas o katapusan; malapit nang mayari.
original_explanation: The state of your patience at 4:55 PM on a Friday. It's the feeling when you're on the last episode of a series, or the last page of a book. It's an ongoing process of completion. "Huwag kang maingay, natatapos na ang movie!" It's the light at the end of the tunnel, but you're still in the tunnel.
usage_notes: Present tense of 'matapos'. Indicates that an action or event is currently in the process of concluding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dito na **natatapos** ang ating palabas para sa araw na ito.","translation":"Our show for today **is ending** here."},{"sentence":"Makinig ka, **natatapos** na ang pasensya ko sa iyo.","translation":"Listen, my patience with you **is ending**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kaalaman o kamalayan tungkol sa isang impormasyon, katotohanan, o pangyayari. Isang pormal na katumbas ng "nalalaman".
etymology: From na- + reduplication of the first syllable 'ba' + batid (to know, be aware of).
original_explanation: This is the formal, almost poetic way of saying "nalalaman" (to know). You won't hear this in everyday chismis. You'll find it in news reports, official statements, or maybe from your very proper Lola. "Ayon sa aming source, nababatid ng lahat ang kanyang sikreto." Sounds way more dramatic than "alam ng lahat," right?
usage_notes: A more formal synonym for 'nalalaman'. Used in literature, formal speech, and journalism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nabababatid** ng pamahalaan ang hirap na dinaranas ng mga mamamayan.","translation":"The government **is aware of** the hardships being experienced by the citizens."},{"sentence":"Lingid sa iyong **pagkabatid**, matagal na siyang may gusto sa iyo.","translation":"Unknown to you (without your **awareness**), he/she has liked you for a long time."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babala o paalala tungkol sa isang posibleng panganib, problema, o masamang kahihinatnan.
original_explanation: An English word we use so much it might as well be Tagalog. From your mom giving you a "warning" look not to take the last piece of chicken, to the "slippery when wet" sign. It's the universe (or your boss) telling you, "Hey, 'wag kang ano diyan."
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with the Tagalog word 'babala'. Extremely common in both spoken and written Filipino, especially in professional and official contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo muna siya ng **warning** bago mo isumbong.","translation":"Give him a **warning** first before you report him."},{"sentence":"May **warning** ang PAGASA tungkol sa paparating na bagyo.","translation":"PAGASA has a **warning** about the approaching typhoon."}]

translation: to be late/last; to be caught
meaning_filipino: Maging nasa likuran o pinakadulo sa isang pila, karera, o proseso; o di kaya ay madakip o matuklasan sa paggawa ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The ultimate two-for-one Tagalog verb! It's what happens when you're late for the meeting ('napahuli ka sa oras') and also what happens when you get caught scrolling IG during that meeting ('napahuli ka ng boss mo'). It's the verb for both being the last one to the party and getting busted at the party.
usage_notes: This word is polysemous, deriving its two meanings from the root 'huli' which can mean either 'last/late' or 'catch'. Context is crucial to determine the intended meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumising siya nang tanghali kaya **napahuli** siya sa klase.","translation":"He woke up late so he **was late** for class."},{"sentence":"**Napahuli** ang magnanakaw dahil sa mabilis na pagresponde ng mga pulis.","translation":"The thief **was caught** because of the police's quick response."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging hindi direkta sa pagsasalita o pagkilos; ang paggamit ng maraming salita nang hindi agad tinutukoy ang pangunahing punto.
original_explanation: This is the specialty of politicians during interviews and your friend who owes you money. Instead of a straight "yes" or "no," you get a whole backstory, three side-stories, and a philosophical question. It's the verbal equivalent of taking the scenic route from Quiapo to Baclaran via NLEX.
usage_notes: Almost always has a negative connotation, implying evasion or time-wasting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiinis ako sa **pagkamaligoy** ng kanyang mga sagot.","translation":"I'm annoyed by the **evasiveness** of his answers."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **pagkamaligoy** at sabihin mo na ang totoo.","translation":"Stop **beating around the bush** and just tell the truth."}]

translation: to shell; to analyze; to shred
meaning_filipino: Alisin ang balat, buto, o hibla ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain; suriin nang detalyado ang isang konsepto, problema, o teksto.
original_explanation: This is what you do to *hipon* (shrimp) before you can eat it – you peel it. It's also what your manager does to your report when they're looking for mistakes, or what you do to your crush's social media profile to find clues about their life. You're breaking it down piece by piece. 'Himayin mo nga 'yang problema para maintindihan natin.'
usage_notes: Can be used literally for food (shredding meat, shelling nuts) or figuratively for analyzing problems, texts, or situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **himayin** ang manok bago ilagay sa adobo.","translation":"You need to **shred** the chicken before putting it in the adobo."},{"sentence":"**Himayin** natin ang bawat detalye ng kontrata.","translation":"Let's **analyze** every detail of the contract."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na mayroon nang mga puting buhok, karaniwang sanhi ng pagtanda o stress.
original_explanation: Stress sa work? Problema sa lovelife? Thesis? Baka 'yan ang dahilan kung bakit may-uban ka na. Having gray hair isn't just about age anymore; it's a battle scar from adulting.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal o upang ipahiwatig ang stress at pagtanda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bata pa si Anna ngunit **may-uban** na siya dahil sa pagod.","translation":"Anna is still young but she already **has gray hair** due to exhaustion."},{"sentence":"Iginagalang namin ang aming lolong **may-uban** na.","translation":"We respect our grandfather who now **has gray hair**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsumite ng isang pormal na aplikasyon o kahilingan para sa isang bagay, tulad ng trabaho, pautang, o permiso.
original_explanation: That feeling when you send your resume to 100 companies on JobStreet and pray that one of them calls you back. It's the official sport of fresh grads and career-shifters. Basically, 'to shoot your shot' but for professional purposes.
usage_notes: This is a very common Taglish verb used in formal and informal contexts, especially regarding jobs, school admissions, and loans.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umaplay** ako para sa posisyon ng manager.","translation":"I **applied** for the manager position."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **umaplay** online para sa visa.","translation":"You need to **apply** for the visa online."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagbabalewala, pagwawaldas, o pagpapawalang-halaga sa isang bagay, pagkakataon, o payo.
etymology: From `wala` (none, gone). Verb form created through affixation and reduplication.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your diet on a weekend, your budget during a 12.12 sale, or your ex's advice. It’s actively making something 'wala' (gone). It's the art of pretending something doesn't exist or treating it like it has no value. 'Winalawala mo lang ang chance natin!' is a classic hugot line.
usage_notes: Often used in past tense `winalawala` or present tense `winawalawala`. It implies a deliberate action of making something gone or worthless.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Winalawala** niya ang lahat ng perang minana niya sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"He **squandered** all the money he inherited from his parents."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **walawalahin** ang mga payo ko dahil para rin 'yan sa ikabubuti mo.","translation":"Don't **disregard** my advice because it's for your own good."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay, lalo na ang pondo, kagamitan, o programa, na inilaan para sa proseso ng pagbabakuna.
