original_explanation: This is what your teacher yells during the flag ceremony: 'Mag-hilerahan nang maayos!' (Form a proper line!). It's also what you do with your shot glasses before a round of 'Tagay!'. Or organizing your Funko Pops on a shelf. Basically, putting things in a neat line.
usage_notes: The root is 'hilera' (noun, 'row'). Hilerahan is the object-focus verb. 'Humilera' is the actor-focus verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**hilerahan** ang mga silya sa harap ng entablado.","translation":"Please **arrange** the chairs **in a row** in front of the stage."},{"sentence":"**Hilerahan** mo ang mga libro sa estante ayon sa kulay.","translation":"**Arrange** the books on the shelf **in a line** according to color."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kumpol ng mga bunga na magkakasamang tumutubo sa iisang tangkay, tulad ng saging o ubas.
original_explanation: What you see at the palengke when the bananas are all clinging to one stem for dear life. It's a fruit squad. One whole buwig of saging is a commitment, perfect for a family merienda or for your tita's fruit salad.
usage_notes: Primarily used for fruits that grow in large clusters like bananas, grapes, or lanzones.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si Nanay ng isang **buwig** ng saging na saba.","translation":"Mom bought a **bunch** of saba bananas."},{"sentence":"Ang bigat ng **buwig** ng ubas na ito!","translation":"This **cluster** of grapes is heavy!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahaba at malalim na hiwa na karaniwang gawa ng isang matulis na bagay.
original_explanation: That long cut you get, either from a knife in the kitchen, paper when you're rushing a report, or metaphorically, from a painful breakup text. It's a cut that means business, more intense than a simple 'hiwa'.
usage_notes: Can refer to both physical cuts and, figuratively, deep emotional wounds. It has a more intense connotation than 'hiwa' (cut).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **laslas** ang kaniyang braso matapos ang aksidente.","translation":"He had a **gash** on his arm after the accident."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat salita niya ay parang **laslas** sa aking puso.","translation":"Her every word felt like a **slash** across my heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mapanlinlang na pamamaraan o gawain upang makakuha ng pera o ibang benepisyo mula sa iba sa pamamagitan ng panloloko.
original_explanation: 'Yung text na "Congrats, you've won 1M pesos from a raffle you never joined!" o 'yung online seller na biglang nag-deactivate ng account pagkatapos mong magbayad. Basically, any form of 'budol-budol' in the digital age. If it's too good to be true, it's probably a scam.
usage_notes: Widely used and understood. Can also be used as a verb ("na-scam").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniniwala diyan, halatang **scam** 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe that, it's obviously a **scam**."},{"sentence":"Maraming nabiktima ng investment **scam** na iyon.","translation":"Many fell victim to that investment **scam**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip paari sa ikatlong panauhan na tumutukoy sa pag-aari ng isang tao, bagay, o hayop.
original_explanation: The OG 's/he said'. This is how you say something belongs to 'him' or 'her' when you're telling the chismis. 'Kinuha niya ang kanyang gamit.' (He/She took his/her things.) It's the formal version of 'niya' when used before the noun.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit bago ang pangngalan na tinutukoy nito, tulad ng 'ang kanyang libro'. Ang mas karaniwang ayos sa pang-araw-araw na usapan ay ang paglagay ng 'niya' pagkatapos ng pangngalan: 'ang libro niya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala ang **kanyang** payong sa gitna ng ulan.","translation":"**His/Her** umbrella was lost in the middle of the rain."},{"sentence":"Ibinigay ng guro ang papuri sa **kanyang** mag-aaral.","translation":"The teacher gave praise to **his/her** student."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkauna sa oras o pagkakasunud-sunod, o pansamantalang kalagayan.
original_explanation: "Muna" is the ultimate Filipino word for procrastination and prioritization. "Teka, meryenda muna." (Wait, snack first.) "Chill muna tayo." (Let's chill for a while.) It's the polite way of saying "I'll get to it... eventually." It's the pause before the action, the coffee break before the deadline grind.
usage_notes: A very common particle used to sequence actions or to indicate a temporary state. Often placed after the verb or the first word of the predicate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-aral ka **muna** bago ka maglaro.","translation":"Study **first** before you play."},{"sentence":"Sandali lang, tatawag **muna** ako.","translation":"Just a moment, I'll make a call **first**."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka **muna** umalis.","translation":"Don't leave **yet**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtataksil sa isang tao, grupo, o sa bayan; paglabag sa tiwala o katapatan.
etymology: From 'kanulo' (a less common word for treachery), combined with 'pagka-' to form a noun. More commonly associated with 'taksil'.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'Et tu, Brute?' moment. This is when your best friend reveals your secrets, or when a character in your favorite teleserye turns out to be the villain all along. It’s the kind of betrayal that fuels hugot lines for generations. The 'Marites' who spills the beans on her own friend is a prime example.
usage_notes: A very strong and formal word for betrayal, often used in historical, literary, or dramatic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakanulo** sa bayan ay ang pinakamabigat na kasalanan ng isang kawal.","translation":"The **betrayal** of the country is a soldier's gravest sin."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya matanggap ang **pagkakanulo** ng kanyang pinagkakatiwalaang kaibigan.","translation":"He could not accept the **treachery** of his trusted friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga mamamayan na sinanay bilang mga sundalo ngunit hindi bahagi ng regular na hukbong sandatahan, na maaaring tawagin para sa serbisyo sa panahon ng kagipitan.
original_explanation: Think of them as the "on-call" army of a town. Sila 'yung mga regular na mamamayan—tindero, magsasaka, titser—na biglang nagiging sundalo kapag may emergency. Parang barangay tanod na level-up at may mas seryosong training.
usage_notes: Often heard in news reports about conflicts, especially in rural or provincial areas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binuo ng mga residente ang isang **milisya** upang ipagtanggol ang kanilang bayan.","translation":"The residents formed a **militia** to defend their town."}]

meaning_filipino: Patigilin sa pag-iyak ang isang tao.
etymology: From i- (verb prefix) + tahan (to stop crying).
original_explanation: The magic word every parent, tita, or older sibling tries to use on a crying child. "Itahan mo na 'yan, bibigyan kita ng candy." It's the verbal equivalent of a pacifier, an attempt to negotiate a ceasefire with the tear ducts.
usage_notes: Used specifically for stopping someone from crying. The command form is "Tahan na!" (Stop crying!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **itahan** ang sanggol sa pamamagitan ng pag-awit.","translation":"She tried **to stop** the baby **from crying** by singing."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **maitahan** ang aking pag-iyak matapos mapanood ang pelikula.","translation":"I couldn't **stop** my crying after watching the movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng paggamit ng pandikdik o halo sa isang bayuhan upang durugin, pulbusin, o tanggalin ang balat ng mga butil o iba pang bagay.
original_explanation: When you need to crush something, literally. Like, pounding garlic for adobo or pounding your chest in frustration after seeing your ex's wedding photos. It's the action you do *with* the `bayuhan`. Figuratively, it's what you feel like doing to your laptop when the Wi-Fi dies during a crucial Zoom meeting: "Gusto kong bayuhin 'tong keyboard!"
usage_notes: The imperative form is also 'bayuhin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **bayuhin** nang maigi ang mga butil ng kape para lumabas ang aroma nito.","translation":"You need **to pound** the coffee beans well for their aroma to come out."},{"sentence":"**Bayuhin** mo na ang bawang at sibuyas para sa ginisang isda.","translation":"**Pound** the garlic and onions now for the sautéed fish."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi labis at hindi kulang; katamtaman; sapat lamang.
original_explanation: The Goldilocks of Tagalog. Not too hot, not too cold, but *just right*. It's that feeling when you add just enough sugar to your coffee, or when the aircon is at the perfect temperature. It's the opposite of OA (over-acting) or 'kulang sa pansin'.
usage_notes: Often used to describe quantity, quality, or degree. The phrase 'tamtamang halaga' means a fair or reasonable price.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo lang ng **tamtaman** na asin ang niluluto mo.","translation":"Just put a **moderate** amount of salt in what you're cooking."},{"sentence":"Sa **tamtamang** halaga, mabibili mo na ang de-kalidad na sapatos.","translation":"For a **reasonable** price, you can already buy high-quality shoes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng portable na kompyuter na maaaring dalhin kahit saan at gamitin habang nakapatong sa kandungan.
original_explanation: The modern-day 'kandungan.' It's your office, your cinema, your gaming console, and your portal to the world of unending Zoom meetings. The source of your back pain and the reason you can 'work from home' (read: work from bed).
usage_notes: A direct loanword, universally understood in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan ko ang charger ng **laptop** ko sa opisina.","translation":"I left my **laptop** charger at the office."},{"sentence":"Ang bagal na ng **laptop** ko, kailangan ko na sigurong mag-upgrade.","translation":"My **laptop** is so slow now, I probably need to upgrade."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagpapanatili sa isang bagay upang hindi ito masira, magbago, o mawala.
etymology: From Spanish 'preservar' with the Tagalog suffix '-hin'.
original_explanation: Ito yung command form. 'Hoy, **preserbahin** mo yang natitirang pasensya ko!' o kaya, 'Kailangan nating **preserbahin** ang mga gubat.' It's the act of keeping something safe and sound, whether it's your sanity during traffic or the last piece of leche flan in the ref.
usage_notes: The verb form, instructing or stating the need to preserve something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin nating **preserbahin** ang ating kultura at tradisyon.","translation":"It is our duty **to preserve** our culture and traditions."},{"sentence":"Paano ba **preserbahin** ang mga gulay para tumagal?","translation":"How do you **preserve** vegetables to make them last longer?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae na nagkaroon ng anak nang hindi kasal.
original_explanation: Literally 'maiden-mother.' This term used to carry a heavy stigma, but in 2026, it's often used with a sense of respect for a woman's strength. A 'dalagang-ina' is a single mom, a superwoman juggling work, life, and raising a child on her own. She's the ultimate multitasker, the CEO of her household.
usage_notes: The term has evolved from being purely descriptive and sometimes pejorative to being a term of empowerment for single mothers. 'Solong magulang' is a more neutral, modern equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **dalagang-ina**, mag-isa niyang itinaguyod ang kanyang anak.","translation":"As a **single mother**, she raised her child all by herself."},{"sentence":"Maraming programa ang gobyerno para suportahan ang mga **dalagang-ina**.","translation":"The government has many programs to support **unwed mothers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang empleyado sa isang opisina, tindahan, o ahensya ng gobyerno na may tungkuling mag-asikaso ng mga papeles, talaan, o pag-asiste sa mga kliyente.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of any office or government agency. They're the ones who know where your "for process" papers are actually located. Be nice to the clerk; they hold the keys to the bureaucratic kingdom and can either make your day smooth or send you to Window 4, then 7, then back to 2.
usage_notes: The Filipinized spelling 'klerk' is also sometimes used but less common in formal writing. The generic term 'kawani' can also be used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinigay ko ang mga dokumento sa **clerk** sa Window 3.","translation":"I gave the documents to the **clerk** at Window 3."},{"sentence":"Nagtatrabaho siya bilang **clerk** sa isang law firm.","translation":"She works as a **clerk** in a law firm."}]

translation: confession, revealing the truth, being sincere
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsasabi ng katotohanan, lihim, o tunay na nararamdaman sa isang tao nang may katapatan.
original_explanation: This is the moment of truth. 'Yung aamin ka na sa crush mo ('Uy, gusto kita'), 'yung sasabihin mo na sa magulang mo na bumagsak ka sa isang subject, or the big reveal in a teleserye ('Ako ang tunay mong ina!'). It's laying your cards on the table, for better or for worse. Heavy breathing required.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of love, secrets, guilt, or any situation requiring honesty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagtatapat** ng pag-ibig ay nagpabago sa lahat.","translation":"His **confession** of love changed everything."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng lakas ng loob para sa isang tapat na **pagtatapat**.","translation":"It takes courage for a sincere **confession**."}]

translation: to be able to get past; to surpass
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang daanan o higitan ang isang hadlang, pagsubok, o hangganan.
original_explanation: When you finally move on from your ex. When you beat the high score in a game. When you survive another 'hell week' at work. It's the feeling of overcoming an obstacle, big or small. You're past it now.
usage_notes: A potential verb indicating the ability to overcome or go beyond a certain point, limit, or challenge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa tulong ng lahat, umaasa kaming **makalampas** sa krisis na ito.","translation":"With everyone's help, we hope to **get past** this crisis."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong mag-aral nang mabuti para **makalampas** sa pagsusulit.","translation":"You need to study well to be **able to pass** the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maging kilala, popular, o bantog sa maraming tao dahil sa isang pambihirang kakayahan, gawa, o katangian.
original_explanation: When you go viral. That TikToker who no one used to notice? They suddenly **tumanyag** because of one dance challenge. It's the journey from 'seen zone' to superstar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis siyang **tumanyag** dahil sa kanyang angking galing sa pag-arte.","translation":"She quickly **became famous** because of her natural talent in acting."},{"sentence":"Ang banda ay **tumanyag** hindi lang sa Pilipinas kundi pati na rin sa ibang bansa.","translation":"The band **became famous** not just in the Philippines but also in other countries."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbibigay ng mga lektyur o panayam, karaniwan sa isang kolehiyo o unibersidad.
original_explanation: Yung prof mo na favorite subject ka ata kasi lagi kang tinatawag para sa recitation. Sila yung may hawak ng Powerpoint, pangarap, at grado mo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming **lektyurer** sa Pilosopiya ay napakagaling magpaliwanag.","translation":"Our **lecturer** in Philosophy is very good at explaining."}]

meaning_filipino: Bahagi ng katawan ng mga ibon, insekto, o paniki na ginagamit sa paglipad. Ginagamit din ito upang tukuyin ang katulad na istruktura sa isang eroplano.
original_explanation: What angels, airplanes, and Chickenjoy have in common. It's the thing that allows flight, whether literal (birds) or culinary (the best part of the fried chicken, fight me!). It also represents freedom, like "spreading your wings" when you finally move out of your parents' house.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa mga hayop at sasakyan, o sa matalinghagang paraan para sa kalayaan at ambisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng mga kulay sa **pakpak** ng paru-paro.","translation":"The colors on the butterfly's **wings** are so beautiful."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong parte ng manok ang **pakpak**.","translation":"My favorite part of the chicken is the **wing**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manunulat na lumilikha o sumusulat ng mga nobela.
original_explanation: A **nobelista** is a novelist, someone who writes those long, complicated stories we call 'nobela.' Think José Rizal or Lualhati Bautista. They're the architects of worlds, the puppeteers of characters, and the reason you had to write that 10-page book report in high school.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Lualhati Bautista ay isang tanyag na **nobelista** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Lualhati Bautista is a famous **novelist** in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang **nobelista** at makapaglathala ng sarili niyang aklat.","translation":"Her dream is to become a **novelist** and publish her own book."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng biglaan at hindi planadong pagbili ng mga bagay sa Shopee, na kadalasang natutuklasan lamang pagkatapos na ma-check out ang mga item.
etymology: Combination of 'Shopee' (brand name) and 'budol' (Tagalog slang for being swindled or tricked, from the 'budol-budol gang' modus operandi). In this context, it means tricking yourself into buying things.
original_explanation: The modern 'budol-budol'. Ito yung akala mo titingin ka lang, pero biglang may 5 items ka na sa cart at na-click mo na ang 'Place Order'. Usually fueled by sales (11.11, 12.12), cute packaging, or a 'life-changing' TikTok recommendation. Ang pagsisisi ay laging nasa huli, kapag dumating na ang delivery at ang bank statement.
usage_notes: A very common phrase in modern Filipino online culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasensya na, hindi ako makakasama sa gala, biktima ako ng **Shopee budol**.","translation":"Sorry, I can't join you guys, I'm a victim of a **Shopee impulse buy**."},{"sentence":"Ito na naman ang mga **Shopee budol** ko for this week.","translation":"Here are my **Shopee impulse buys** for this week again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng karamdaman kung saan ang katawan ay hindi makagawa o hindi magamit nang maayos ang insulin, na nagreresulta sa mataas na antas ng asukal sa dugo.
original_explanation: What your tita warns you about when you have your third cup of milk tea with 100% sugar. It's the universe telling you to maybe chill on the extra rice and soft drinks. The national 'bawal sa akin 'yan' excuse during Noche Buena.
usage_notes: Ang pagbaybay na 'diabetes' (mula sa Ingles) ay mas karaniwan na ngayon, ngunit ang 'dyabetes' ay ang bersyong nakaayon sa palabaybayang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang pasyente na mag-ehersisyo upang makontrol ang kanyang **dyabetes**.","translation":"The doctor advised the patient to exercise to control his **diabetes**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkain ng masyadong matatamis ay maaaring magpataas ng panganib sa pagkakaroon ng **dyabetes**.","translation":"Eating too many sweets can increase the risk of developing **diabetes**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pagbibigay ng tugon, paliwanag, o solusyon.
original_explanation: This is the action you take when your boss asks 'Tapos na ba?' or your mom calls you for the 5th time. 'Sumagot ka!' is the classic parent line when they want you to talk back (but not really). It's the verb form of not leaving someone on 'seen'.
usage_notes: The primary verb forms are 'sumagot' (actor-focus, to answer) and 'sagutin' (object-focus, to answer something). The pronunciation of the verb root remains the same, but stress shifts in conjugation, e.g., /sa-gu-TIN/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumagot** ka sa tanong ko.","translation":"**Answer** my question."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **sagutin** ang lahat ng e-mail bago mag-uwian.","translation":"You need **to answer** all the emails before going home."}]

meaning_filipino: Mag-ukol ng damdamin ng pag-ibig, pagtingin, o pag-aruga sa isang tao, bagay, o konsepto.
original_explanation: The verb form of the national emotion. It's what OFWs do for their families from thousands of miles away. It's what you promise in front of a priest or a judge. It's what makes you text "kain ka na?" and what makes you cry during a sad Filipino movie. Be careful, this is different from the other `magmahal`!
usage_notes: This refers to the emotion of love. It has a homonym that means 'to become expensive'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tunay na kaibigan ay handang **magmahal** nang walang kondisyon.","translation":"A true friend is ready to **love** unconditionally."},{"sentence":"Natuto siyang **magmahal** muli pagkatapos ng maraming pagkabigo.","translation":"He learned to **love** again after many heartbreaks."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang maramdaman, pisikal man o emosyonal; manhid.
original_explanation: Dalawa lang 'yan: either manhid ka na sa sakit dahil sa sobrang dami ng pinagdaanan mo, or ikaw yung taong di-nakakaramdam ng feelings ng iba. Puwede ring literal, tulad ng binti mong namanhid sa tagal ng pagkakaupo sa inidoro habang nag-scro-scroll.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical numbness or emotional insensitivity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa anesthesia, **di-nakakaramdam** ng sakit ang pasyente.","translation":"Because of the anesthesia, the patient is **not feeling** any pain."},{"sentence":"Masyado kang **di-nakakaramdam** sa pinagdadaanan ng kaibigan mo.","translation":"You are too **insensitive** to what your friend is going through."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagtutol o hindi pagsang-ayon sa isang ideya, kilos, o panukala; pagiging kasalungat o kontra.
original_explanation: When you're the only one in the group chat who hates the movie everyone loves. When your parents want you to be a doctor but you want to be a vlogger. That feeling of being against the grain, of opposing the popular vote? That's salansang. You're basically going against the flow. The ultimate 'kontrabida' stance.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or literary contexts to mean 'in opposition to'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang opinyon ay **salansang** sa pinaniniwalaan ng nakararami.","translation":"His opinion is **contrary** to what the majority believes."}]

translation: to ripen; to cause to mature
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapabilis sa paggulang o pagkahinog ng isang prutas o anumang bagay na nangangailangan ng panahon upang maging handa.
original_explanation: This is what you do to that green mango you bought from the palengke. You wrap it in paper or bury it in rice to make it ripen faster. Metaphorically, it's about letting an idea, a plan, or even a person mature. Parang sa love life, 'wag madaliin, hayaan mong pahinugin muna ang feelings. Baka mapakla!
usage_notes: Often used for fruits. Can be used metaphorically for ideas, plans, or emotional maturity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **pahinugin** muna ang mga saging bago gawing banana cue.","translation":"We need to **ripen** the bananas first before making them into banana cue."},{"sentence":"Mas mabuting **pahinugin** muna ang plano bago ito isagawa.","translation":"It's better to let the plan **mature** first before executing it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matapat at malalim na pag-uusap sa pagitan ng dalawang tao kung saan ibinabahagi nila ang kanilang tunay na nararamdaman o saloobin.
etymology: Reduplication of "puso" (heart) with the preposition "sa" (to/at), creating a literal "heart to heart" meaning.
original_explanation: The "let's get serious" talk. This is when the chismis stops and the real tea is spilled. It's the conversation you have with your best friend at 3 AM, usually involving tears, a pint of ice cream, and life-altering advice about love or career.
usage_notes: Refers to a very sincere and open conversation, implying emotional vulnerability and honesty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon kami ng **puso sa puso** na pag-uusap kagabi.","translation":"We had a **heart-to-heart** talk last night."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng isang **puso sa puso** na usapan para maayos ito.","translation":"We need a **heart-to-heart** conversation to fix this."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasama o kasabay sa pag-aaral sa isang paaralan o klase.
etymology: From ka- (denoting companionship) + eskuwela (school, from Spanish 'escuela').
original_explanation: Your fellow student, the one you copy notes from, the group project member who either does all the work or none at all. Your 'batchmate.' You share the same trauma from surprise quizzes and terror teachers.
usage_notes: Can refer to someone in the same class ('kaklase') or just someone who attends the same school.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Maria ay dati kong **kaeskuwela** noong high school.","translation":"Maria was my former **schoolmate** in high school."},{"sentence":"Nagkita-kita ang mga dating **kaeskuwela** sa isang reunion.","translation":"The old **schoolmates** saw each other at a reunion."}]

translation: to have something changed; to cause a change
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paggawa ng pagbabago sa isang bagay, katangian, o kalagayan.
etymology: From mag- (actor-focus verb prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + iba (different, other).
original_explanation: The ultimate "new hair, new me" verb. Nagpaiba ka ng hair color after a breakup. It’s actively causing a transformation. It’s what you do when you want a different result, like when your usual 'diskarte' isn't working on your crush, so you decide to magpaiba of strategy. The phrase "magpaiba sa hitsura" is the classic glow-up move.
usage_notes: Often followed by "ng..." to specify what is being changed. E.g., `magpaiba ng gupit` (to get a different haircut), `magpaiba ng plano` (to change the plan). The user's query `magpaiba sa hitsura` means 'to change one's appearance'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magpaiba** ng kulay ng kanyang buhok.","translation":"She decided to **have** her hair color **changed**."},{"sentence":"Para sa Bagong Taon, gusto kong **magpaiba** ng hitsura.","translation":"For the New Year, I want to **change** my look."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng tanda, simbolo, o numero sa isang bagay upang ito ay matukoy, maiwasto, o mabigyan ng puntos.
original_explanation: 'To mark something.' What your teacher does to your test paper with a red pen. Or what you do to your calendar to count down the days to payday or your next vacation trip. 'Hoy, markahan mo 'yang sabi mo, ha!' (Hey, mark your words!).
usage_notes: This is the imperative or object-focus form of the verb. 'Magmarka' is the actor-focus form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**markahan** mo ang mga papel na ito, Gng. Reyes.","translation":"Please **grade** these papers, Mrs. Reyes."},{"sentence":"**Markahan** mo sa mapa kung saan tayo magkikita.","translation":"**Mark** on the map where we will meet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panghuli, wakas, o hindi na mababago. Ang huling bahagi o yugto ng isang bagay.
etymology: From Spanish 'final' or directly from English 'final'.
original_explanation: 'Pinal na po.' The magic words that end all negotiations at the palengke. Also, that feeling of dread when your prof says 'This is the pinal exam.' It means no more chances, no more revisions, game over, submit your papers.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with the English word 'final' in many contexts, especially in informal speech. Can also function as a noun ('ang pinal').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ito na ang **pinal** na desisyon ng komite.","translation":"This is the **final** decision of the committee."},{"sentence":"Nag-aaral siya para sa kanyang **pinal** na pagsusulit.","translation":"He is studying for his **final** exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Iniluto sa pamamagitan ng pagprito nang bahagya sa kaunting mantika kasama ang mga pampalasang tulad ng bawang, sibuyas, at kamatis.
original_explanation: The holy trinity of Pinoy cooking: bawang, sibuyas, kamatis. If you smell this, someone's about to cook something good. 'Ginisa' is the flavor base, the opening act for almost every ulam. It's the 'pampagana' scent wafting from your neighbor's kitchen. If a dish is 'ginisa,' it's guaranteed to have that savory, home-cooked taste.
usage_notes: A fundamental cooking technique in Filipino cuisine. It can be a verb (Ginisá ng nanay ang gulay) or an adjective describing the dish (Ginisang Munggo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong ulam ang **ginisang** ampalaya.","translation":"My favorite dish is **sautéed** bitter melon."},{"sentence":"**Ginisa** muna niya ang bawang at sibuyas bago ilagay ang manok.","translation":"She first **sautéed** the garlic and onions before adding the chicken."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maliit na anak ng manok o iba pang uri ng ibon.
etymology: Posibleng onomatopoeic, mula sa tunog na 'si-si' na ginagawa ng isang sisiw.
original_explanation: Not to be confused with blame/regret! This 'sisi' is the cute, yellow, fluffy baby chicken you see during Easter or in provincial farms. They're adorable until they grow up and start waking you up at 4 AM.
usage_notes: Ang pagbigkas ay mahalaga. Ang /SI-si/ ay pagsisisi, habang ang /si-SI/ ay ang anak ng manok. Ang mas karaniwang salita para dito ay 'sisiw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang daming maliliit na **sisi** na sumusunod sa kanilang inahing manok.","translation":"There are so many small **chicks** following their mother hen."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng kulay-rosas na **sisi** sa perya.","translation":"He bought a pink-colored **chick** at the fair."}]

translation: to roast (in the style of litson)
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-iihaw ng isang buong hayop, tulad ng baboy o manok, sa paraang katulad ng paggawa ng litson.
original_explanation: The 'verb-ification' of litson. Ito 'yung action na ginagawa mo 'pag sobrang special ng bisita mo. Sa office, 'pag na-hot seat ka sa presentation, parang nili-litson ka na rin sa dami ng tanong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano nilang **litsunin** ang alagang baboy para sa darating na pista.","translation":"They plan **to roast** the pig they raised for the upcoming fiesta."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging matulin o mabilis; ang bilis ng paggalaw o pagkilos ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the formal, scientific term for 'bilis.' You'd see this in a physics textbook, not in a conversation about who can finish their food first. It’s the 'velocity' to the everyday 'speed.' Think of it as the word you'd use to sound smart when describing how fast the internet connection is (or isn't).
usage_notes: More formal than 'bilis'. Used in technical or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusukat ng mga siyentipiko ang **katulinan** ng liwanag.","translation":"Scientists measure the **velocity** of light."},{"sentence":"Ang **katulinan** ng pag-unlad ng teknolohiya ay nakakamangha.","translation":"The **swiftness** of technological development is amazing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-agos o pagpapadanak ng dugo, kadalasan ay dahil sa sugat o karahasan.
original_explanation: Think old-school action movies where the hero gets a tiny cut and suddenly there's parugo everywhere. It's the dramatic spilling of blood. Not to be confused with the 'dugo' from your nose when you see your electricity bill.
usage_notes: A literary or formal term. Not used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang labanan ay nagresulta sa matinding **parugo**.","translation":"The battle resulted in severe **bloodshed**."},{"sentence":"Iwasan natin ang **parugo** at mag-usap nang mahinahon.","translation":"Let's avoid **bloodshed** and talk calmly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang opisyal na pagsusuri sa mga account o tala ng isang organisasyon, kumpanya, o indibidwal.
original_explanation: The verb that strikes fear into the hearts of accountants and treasurers. When someone says they're going to 'mag-odit,' it means they're about to check your receipts, spreadsheets, and justifications for that 'team-building' expense in Boracay. It's the corporate version of your mom checking your browser history.
usage_notes: Commonly used in business, finance, and government contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Taun-taon, may isang external na kumpanyang dumarating para **mag-odit** sa aming libro.","translation":"Every year, an external company comes to **audit** our books."},{"sentence":"Nag-utos ang hepe na **mag-odit** sa lahat ng gastusin ng departamento.","translation":"The boss ordered an **audit** of all the department's expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Patawan ng kaparusahan ang isang tao o entidad dahil sa isang pagkakamali o paglabag.
original_explanation: To 'parusahan' is to deliver the consequences. It's what happens when you break the rules. From getting grounded by your parents for a low grade, to getting a penalty in a game, to a judge sentencing a criminal. It's the action part of 'you're in big trouble!'
usage_notes: The verb form of 'parusa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat **parusahan** ang sinumang lumabag sa batas.","translation":"Anyone who breaks the law should be **punished**."},{"sentence":"**Pinarusahan** ng guro ang mga estudyanteng hindi gumawa ng takdang-aralin.","translation":"The teacher **punished** the students who didn't do their homework."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang partikular na paraan ng pagsasalita na naghahalo ng wikang Ingles at Tagalog, na may kasamang mga partikular na salita, parirala, at intonasyon na karaniwang iniuugnay sa mga "conyo".
original_explanation: This is the 'language' of the conyos. It's not just Taglish; it has its own rules. Like, you make verbs by adding 'make' before a Tagalog word (e.g., 'make *kain*') or using English verbs with Tagalog objects. Example: 'Let's make *bili* some *tusok-tusok* the fishball.' It's a whole linguistic phenomenon, tbh.
usage_notes: Isang impormal at kolokyal na termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihirapan akong intindihin ang **conyospeak** ng mga pinsan ko.","translation":"I have a hard time understanding my cousins' **conyospeak**."},{"sentence":"Viral sa TikTok ang video niya na ginagaya ang **conyospeak**.","translation":"Her video imitating **conyospeak** went viral on TikTok."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang utos na ilagay o ipatong ang isang bagay sa isang partikular na lugar.
etymology: 'pa-' + 'lagay'. A causative verb form, often used as a command.
original_explanation: This is the command form, a bit more forceful or direct than 'pakilagay'. It's what your mom says when she's had enough: 'Palagay mo nga 'yan sa mesa!' (Put that on the table, now!). The root 'lagay' means 'to put', and 'pa-' makes it causative, like 'Cause it to be put there.'
usage_notes: This form is a command. It is the root of verbs like 'ipalagay' (to have something put).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Palagay** mo na lang diyan sa upuan ang mga dala mo.","translation":"**Just put** your things there on the chair."},{"sentence":"Anak, **palagay** naman ng mga plato sa lababo.","translation":"Child, **please put** the plates in the sink."}]

translation: to be for one's good; to cause improvement
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng kabutihan, kagalingan, o pag-unlad ng isang tao o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is your mom's favorite word when she's trying to make you do something you don't want to do. 'Kumain ka ng gulay, para sa ikabubuti mo 'yan.' It's the ultimate 'it's for your own good' card. Can also refer to something that makes a situation better.
usage_notes: Often used in the future tense 'ikabubuti' to refer to a future benefit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sundin mo ang payo ng iyong mga magulang dahil ito ay para sa iyong **ikabubuti**.","translation":"Follow your parents' advice because it is **for your own good**."},{"sentence":"Sana **ikabuti** ng lahat ang bagong patakaran.","translation":"I hope the new policy will **cause improvement** for everyone."}]

translation: to mangle, to shred, to crush completely
meaning_filipino: Ang pagwasak o pagdurog sa isang bagay hanggang sa mawala ang orihinal nitong anyo.
original_explanation: What happens to your heart after watching a sad K-drama. Or what a blender does to fruit. It's destruction level 99. Hindi lang 'sira', hindi lang 'wasak', kundi **lumuray** talaga.
usage_notes: A very strong word for destruction, implying something is broken or torn into unrecognizable pieces.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **lumuray** ang sasakyan dahil sa tindi ng banggaan.","translation":"The car was almost **mangled** due to the intensity of the collision."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **lumuray** ang iyong puso dahil lang sa isang pag-ibig.","translation":"Don't let your heart **be crushed completely** just because of one love."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamalaki at pinakamataong kontinente sa mundo, matatagpuan sa silangan at hilagang bahagi ng mundo.
etymology: From Spanish 'Asia', from Latin 'Asia', from Ancient Greek 'Ἀσία' (Asía).
original_explanation: The biggest, most crowded, and arguably most interesting continent on Earth. It's where you find K-pop, anime, pad thai, the Great Wall, and of course, the Philippines! It's the home of diverse cultures, amazing food, and a whole lot of traffic. We're not just in it, we're a huge part of what makes it awesome.
usage_notes: Always capitalized as it's a proper noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay isang bansa sa Timog-silangang **Asya**.","translation":"The Philippines is a country in Southeast **Asia**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang walang pera o naubusan ng pondo.
etymology: From Beki Lingo (Filipino gay slang), its origin is speculative but widely understood. It is sometimes playfully associated with the comedian Super Tekla.
original_explanation: When your wallet is on a diet, or when petsa de peligro hits you hard. It's that feeling when you check your bank account after a 12.12 sale and it's crying. "Friend, kape tayo?" "Sorry, pass muna, tekla ako today."
usage_notes: Highly informal and considered slang. Use with friends or in very casual settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag muna tayong lumabas, **tekla** pa ako bago mag-sweldo.","translation":"Let's not go out yet, I'm still **broke** before payday."},{"sentence":"Pa-Gcash muna, friend. **Tekla** na ang lola mo.","translation":"Can you Gcash me first, friend? Your girl here is **penniless**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang muling pag-post o pagbabahagi ng isang bagay na nauna nang na-post sa social media.
original_explanation: 'Yung nakita mo 'yung meme na sobrang relatable, tapos shinare mo sa wall mo. 'Yan, nag-repost ka. It's the digital version of saying "Same!" or "Eto, oh, tingnan n'yo!". Basically, pagnanakaw ng content with credit (minsan).
usage_notes: A very common term in the context of social media. Often used in its English form or with Filipino affixes like "ni-repost" (reposted) or "i-repost" (to repost).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**repost** naman nitong anunsyo para mas maraming makakita.","translation":"Please **repost** this announcement so more people can see it."},{"sentence":"Ni-**repost** niya ang lumang litrato nila para sa kanilang anibersaryo.","translation":"He/She **reposted** their old photo for their anniversary."}]

translation: to match; to equal; to level with
meaning_filipino: Abutin o tularan ang antas, kalidad, o nagawa ng isang tao o bagay.
etymology: From the root 'pantay' (equal, level) and the suffix '-an' (to apply the root's action to something).
original_explanation: That feeling when you're trying to match your sibling's achievements so your parents will finally get off your back. Or when you try to 'level up' your OOTD to match your crush's standards. 'Sana all kayang **pantayan** ang effort ko.'
usage_notes: Often used in the context of achievements, standards, or quality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **pantayan** ang galing sa pag-awit ng kaniyang ina.","translation":"It's difficult **to match** her mother's singing talent."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **pantayan** ang mga marka ng nangungunang estudyante sa klase.","translation":"He is trying **to equal** the grades of the top student in the class."}]

translation: to unfold; to come out (of the closet)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbubuklat o paglalabas ng isang bagay na nakatago o nakatiklop. Sa modernong gamit, tumutukoy din ito sa pag-amin ng isang tao sa kaniyang oryentasyong sekswal o pagkakakilanlang pangkasarian.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what you do to a banig (sleeping mat) or a flag—you unfurl it. But in today's Philippines, it's famously used for 'coming out of the closet'. It's the ultimate "This is me!" moment, moving from hidden to proudly displayed. Think of it as finally unfurling your own personal rainbow flag.
usage_notes: The meaning of 'coming out' is now the more common usage, especially among younger generations. The original meaning of 'unfurling' is still understood but less frequent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magladlad** ng kanyang tunay na pagkatao sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He decided to **come out** and show his true self to his family."},{"sentence":"**Magladlad** ka ng banig para may mahigaan tayo.","translation":"**Unfurl** a mat so we have somewhere to lie down."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtamo ng sugat o pinsala; mayroong sugat.
etymology: From 'sugat' (wound) + '-an' (suffix indicating a state or condition).
original_explanation: This is you after a bad breakup, a tough day at work, or literally after you trip on a random sidewalk crack. You're sugatan. You need a band-aid, a hug, or a bucket of fried chicken. Or all three.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective (may sugat) or a verb (to wound someone, sugatan). This entry focuses on the adjective form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinugod sa ospital ang **sugatan** na biktima.","translation":"The **wounded** victim was rushed to the hospital."},{"sentence":"Puso ko'y **sugatan** dahil sa kanyang paglisan.","translation":"My heart is **wounded** because of their departure."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan kung saan ang isang utang o bayarin ay nabayaran na nang buo. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa natitirang balanse.
original_explanation: That beautiful, beautiful feeling when your credit card balance is zero. Saldado na! It means your debt is settled. It's the opposite of 'utang'. In accounting or business, it can also mean the final balance or amount. The goal in life is to have all your debts saldado.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of finance, debts, and payments. Can be used as a noun ('ang saldo') to mean 'the balance'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **saldado** na ang lahat ng aking utang!","translation":"Finally, all my debts are **paid up**!"},{"sentence":"Magkano ang **saldado** sa account mo?","translation":"What is the **balance** in your account?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nilikha o ginawa bunga ng sining, imahinasyon, o paggawa. Ito ay maaaring isang obra, akda, o anumang produkto ng malikhaing pag-iisip.
original_explanation: Yung masterpiece mo, yung artwork mo, yung sinulat mong tula para kay crush, o kahit yung bagong recipe na naimbento mo sa kusina. Lahat 'yan **likha** mo. It's your 'work', your 'creation'. #ProudCreator
usage_notes: Often used in the context of art, literature, and divine creation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang pambihirang **likha** ang Spoliarium ni Juan Luna.","translation":"The Spoliarium by Juan Luna is an extraordinary **creation**."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat tula niya ay **likha** ng pusong nasaktan.","translation":"Each of her poems is a **work** of a broken heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o silungan kung saan inaalagaan at pinananatili ang mga kabayo.
original_explanation: The horse's version of a condo unit. It's where you keep kabayos, and if you're a rich haciendero in a teleserye, you probably have a dramatic confrontation scene in a kuwadra while petting your favorite steed. For most people, it's just a word they know from Spanish-era stories.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinasok ng kutsero ang kanyang kabayo sa **kuwadra** pagkatapos ng maghapong pamamasada.","translation":"The coachman put his horse into the **stable** after a whole day of work."},{"sentence":"Malinis at maayos ang mga **kuwadra** sa hasyenda nila.","translation":"The **stables** in their hacienda are clean and orderly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsisimula ng apoy o ningas, o ang pagpapakita ng gilas o husay sa paraang kapansin-pansin.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative prefix) + siklab (flare-up, outburst).
original_explanation: This is what happens when someone suddenly flexes their new iPhone, their promotion, or their 'galing' sa basketball. It's the act of showing off, making a big scene, or literally starting a fire. Think of it as the 'pasabog' moment in a performance or a heated argument. 'Nagpapasiklab na naman si kumpare sa bagong kotse niya.'
usage_notes: Can be used literally for starting a fire, or figuratively for showing off skills, anger, or creating a spectacle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapasiklab** ng kanyang galing sa pagluluto ay nagpahanga sa lahat.","translation":"The **showing off** of her cooking skills impressed everyone."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **pagpapasiklab** ng apoy malapit sa mga tuyong dahon.","translation":"Avoid the **ignition** of fire near dry leaves."}]

translation: to make something fit; to make exact or sufficient
meaning_filipino: Gawing sapat o eksakto ang isang bagay; iakma upang magkasya.
original_explanation: Think of your mom trying to fit one more 'tupperware' of ulam into an already full ref. "Hustuhin mo na 'yan diyan!" Or when you're budgeting your sweldo until the next payday, you have to 'hustuhin' the money you have left. It's the art of making things work with what you've got.
usage_notes: A transitive verb indicating the action of making something fit or sufficient.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **hustuhin** ang badyet para sa buong buwan.","translation":"We need to **make** the budget **fit** for the whole month."},{"sentence":"**Hustuhin** mo ang pagkain para sa lahat ng bisita.","translation":"**Make** the food **sufficient** for all the guests."}]

translation: to leave instructions; to entrust something
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iwan ng tagubilin, mensahe, o isang bagay na ipinagkakatiwala sa pangangalaga ng iba.
original_explanation: This is the classic 'bago umalis ng bahay' move. Your mom will maghabilin of a million things: 'Lock the door, turn off the lights, don't talk to strangers, may pagkain sa ref.' It's a mix of leaving instructions and entrusting you with responsibility. The analog version of sending a detailed PM.
usage_notes: Can be about leaving a message, an order, or even a last will and testament ('huling habilin').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bago umalis si Nanay, **nag-habilin** siya na hugasan namin ang mga plato.","translation":"Before Mom left, she **left instructions** for us to wash the dishes."},{"sentence":"**Maghabilin** ka lang sa sekretarya kung may kailangan ka.","translation":"Just **leave a message** with the secretary if you need anything."}]

translation: act of exposing to air or heat (to dry or warm)
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalantad o pagbibilad ng isang bagay sa hangin, araw, o apoy upang matuyo o uminit.
etymology: From `pag-` + `CV` (first syllable repetition) + `yangyang` (to expose to heat/air).
original_explanation: This is what you do with your hands over a fire on a cold night in Baguio. Or when you're trying to dry a single spot on your shirt with a hair dryer because you're late for work. It's the act of toasting or warming something by exposing it to a heat source or air. It's like a very focused 'pagbibilad' (sunning).
usage_notes: Often used for warming hands over a fire or drying something with directed heat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatulong ang **pagyayangyang** niya ng kanyang mga paa sa tabi ng apoy upang mabawasan ang kanyang ginaw.","translation":"**Exposing** his feet near the fire helped reduce his coldness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang produktong gawa sa gatas na karaniwang ipinapahid sa tinapay o ginagamit sa pagluluto at pagbe-bake.
original_explanation: The 'sosyal' cousin of margarine. It's what you spread on pandesal when you're feeling a bit fancy. In the Philippines, the line between `mantikilya` (butter) and margarine is often blurred, with many popular brands being margarine but still colloquially called `mantikilya`.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'margarina' (margarine) in casual conversation, though technically distinct.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **mantikilya** para sa pandesal.","translation":"Please pass the **butter** for the pandesal."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang cake kung tunay na **mantikilya** ang gagamitin.","translation":"The cake is more delicious if real **butter** is used."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang may pinakamaliit na bilang o dami sa isang grupo o paghahambing.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'sana all.' This is what you have when it's 'petsa de peligro' and your wallet is on life support. It’s the number of people who actually liked your controversial Facebook post. The smallest slice of cake your tita gives you because 'you're on a diet.' The goal is to have the 'pinakakaunti' problems.
usage_notes: Used for countable and uncountable nouns to denote the minimum quantity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa lahat ng klase, ang Filipino ang may **pinakakaunti** na takdang-aralin.","translation":"Of all the classes, Filipino has the **least** amount of homework."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nakakuha ng **pinakakaunti** na boto.","translation":"He/She received the **fewest** votes."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng pambihirang katangian ng kabutihan, katapangan, o kahalagahan; marangal.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "lodi" or "petmalu" level. It's not just for heroes like Rizal or Bonifacio. **Dakila** rin ang nanay mo na nagigising ng 4 AM para ipagluto ka, o 'yung frontliner na rumaraos sa pandemic. It’s greatness with a purpose, with a heart. The highest praise you can give someone.
usage_notes: A formal and high-praise word used for people, actions, or concepts of exceptional worth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **dakila**ng bayani si Dr. Jose Rizal.","translation":"Dr. Jose Rizal is a **great** hero."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ng isang ina ay tunay na **dakila**.","translation":"A mother's love is truly **noble**."}]

translation: very dressed up; all dolled up
meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang taong labis na nag-ayos o nagbihis para sa isang okasyon; bihis na bihis.
etymology: Reduplication of 'gayak' (dress, adornment) to show intensity.
original_explanation: This is you when there's a party and the dress code is 'casual' but you show up looking like you're going to the Met Gala. It’s that “extra” level of porma. Your lola will say this when she sees you ready for your JS prom. Slay!
usage_notes: The repetition of 'gayak' emphasizes the intensity of being dressed up.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gayak na gayak** si Maria para sa kanyang debut.","translation":"Maria is **all dolled up** for her debut party."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka **gayak na gayak**? Pupunta ka lang naman sa palengke.","translation":"Why are you so **dressed up**? You're just going to the market."}]

translation: to engage in cockfighting; to make cocks fight
meaning_filipino: Ipaglaban ang dalawang tandang na manok bilang isang uri ng sugal o libangan.
original_explanation: A favorite pastime of many a tito. It's not just about two chickens fighting; it's a whole culture of breeding, betting (kristo!), and intense drama in the cockpit arena. The online version, 'e-sabong', became a huge phenomenon. It's the ultimate 'manly' hobby that your lola probably hates.
usage_notes: Specific to the cultural practice and sport of cockfighting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang pumupunta sa sabungan tuwing Linggo para **magsabong**.","translation":"Many people go to the cockpit on Sundays **to engage in cockfighting**."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbawal ng kanyang asawa na siya ay **magsabong** dahil nauubos ang kanilang pera.","translation":"His wife forbade him **to engage in cockfighting** because their money was running out."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o bagay na madaling magkaroon ng kulubot o puno na ng kulubot.
original_explanation: The adjective version. Describes someone whose skin is starting to look like a raisin (love you, lola!), or that one shirt material that gets wrinkly the moment you look at it. 'Ay, linen pala 'to, kulubutin.'
usage_notes: The suffix '-in' here turns the noun/adjective 'kulubot' into a descriptor indicating a characteristic or tendency.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat tayo ay tatanda at magiging **kulubutin** ang balat.","translation":"We will all grow old and our skin will become **wrinkled**."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang isuot ang blusang iyon dahil **kulubutin** ang tela.","translation":"She doesn't want to wear that blouse because the fabric is **prone to wrinkling**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng pagkabigo o kalungkutan na sanhi ng hindi natupad na inaasahan o pag-asa.
etymology: From Spanish 'desmayo' (fainting, dismay). In Tagalog, the meaning shifted from fainting to the emotional state that might cause it.
original_explanation: The feeling when you order something online vs. what you actually get. The look on your face when the Jollibee crew says, 'Sir, out of stock po ang chickenjoy.' It's the official emotion of Monday mornings. Also a verb form: 'Nadismaya ako.'
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (pagkadismaya) or as the root of a verb (madismaya, nakakadismaya).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang kanyang **dismaya** sa resulta ng pagsusulit.","translation":"She couldn't hide her **dismay** at the exam results."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang **dismaya** ng mga tagahanga nang matalo ang kanilang paboritong koponan.","translation":"The fans' **disappointment** was great when their favorite team lost."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng baril na gawa sa kamay, kadalasang walang lisensya at ilegal na ginawa.
original_explanation: This is the DIY version of a firearm. Often crudely made, unreliable, and definitely not something you'd see in a James Bond movie. The term **paltik** is synonymous with underground, unlicensed guns, the kind you hear about in crime reports. It's the 'Class C' of weaponry.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to homemade or unregistered firearms, often associated with criminal activities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakumpiska ng mga awtoridad ang isang bag na puno ng mga **paltik**.","translation":"The authorities confiscated a bag full of **unlicensed firearms**."},{"sentence":"Delikadong gumamit ng **paltik** dahil baka pumutok ito nang hindi inaasahan.","translation":"It's dangerous to use a **paltik** because it might fire unexpectedly."}]

meaning_filipino: May malakas na tunog o likha ng maraming ingay; hindi tahimik.
original_explanation: The state of every Filipino family gathering, the classroom when the teacher leaves, or the inside of your head when you have five deadlines and your crush just said "hi". Also, your neighbor's karaoke session at 2 AM on a Tuesday.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kayong **maingay** dahil natutulog ang bata.","translation":"Don't be **noisy** because the child is sleeping."},{"sentence":"Napakagulo at **maingay** sa palengke tuwing umaga.","translation":"It's very chaotic and **loud** in the market every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maingay at paulit-ulit na pag-aaway o pagtatalo tungkol sa maliliit o hindi mahalagang bagay.
original_explanation: This is pagtatalo's petty little brother. It's not a serious debate; it's that endless back-and-forth about who didn't wash the dishes or why you're 5 minutes late. It's the kind of argument that goes nowhere and just gets louder. Think of two vendors in the palengke arguing over a few pesos. It's high-volume, low-substance arguing.
usage_notes: Implies a more chaotic, noisy, and often pointless argument compared to `pagtatalo`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumigil na kayo sa inyong **pagtataltalan** at magbati na.","translation":"Stop your **bickering** and make up already."},{"sentence":"Walang katapusan ang **pagtataltalan** ng dalawang pulitiko sa telebisyon.","translation":"The **wrangling** of the two politicians on television is endless."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bayad na ibinibigay sa isang ahente o empleyado para sa bawat benta o serbisyong naisagawa; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang pangkat ng mga tao na inatasan para sa isang partikular na gawain.
original_explanation: That extra cash you get on top of your salary for hitting your sales target, parang bonus round sa video game ng pagiging empleyado. It can also mean a government body, like the "Komisyon sa Halalan" (COMELEC), which is like the referee for the national sport of elections.
usage_notes: Has two common meanings: 1) a fee for a service (sales commission) and 2) a formal group or committee (a government commission).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang nakuha niyang **komisyon** sa pagbebenta ng bahay.","translation":"She got a large **commission** from selling the house."},{"sentence":"Ang **Komisyon** sa Wikang Filipino ang nangangalaga sa ating pambansang wika.","translation":"The **Commission** on the Filipino Language is the one that takes care of our national language."}]

translation: to put a diaper on someone
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng lampin ang isang sanggol o sinuman na nangangailangan nito.
original_explanation: The verb form of dealing with a baby's business. It's the action of changing or putting on a diaper. New parents become expert-level at this, able to do it in the dark, with one hand, while singing 'Baby Shark'.
usage_notes: This is the action verb for putting a diaper on a subject. The noun for diaper is 'lampin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **lampinan** si baby pagkatapos niyang maligo.","translation":"Don't forget to **put a diaper on** the baby after his bath."},{"sentence":"Ate, tulungan mo akong **lampinan** ang pamangkin mo.","translation":"Sister, help me **put a diaper on** your nephew."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook o malawak na lupain na itinalaga para sa paglilibing ng mga yumao. Tinatawag din itong kampo santo.
original_explanation: The original subdivision. Dito mo dinadala yung mga bulaklak na hindi mo naibigay sa kanya. Dagsaan ang tao tuwing Undas, na parang reunion ng mga buhay para sa mga patay. It's the place where 'rest in peace' is the official motto, but gets super noisy and festive once a year.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpunta kami sa **sementeryo** noong Araw ng mga Patay upang magtirik ng kandila.","translation":"We went to the **cemetery** on All Souls' Day to light candles."},{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang nag-picnic sa tabi ng puntod sa **sementeryo**.","translation":"Many families had a picnic beside the grave in the **cemetery**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagtatagal o pag-antala sa paggawa ng isang bagay; pagiging matagal.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizing prefix) + luwat (long time, delay).
original_explanation: This is the 'wait lang' that turns into 'wait forever.' It's the feeling you get when the loading bar is stuck at 99%, or when your friend says 'OTW' but is still clearly at home. It's the epitome of Filipino time, the art of making things take longer than they should.
usage_notes: More formal or literary than 'pagtatagal' or 'pagkaantala'. It implies a slowness or tardiness that causes delay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagluluwat** ng tulong, lumala ang sitwasyon.","translation":"Because of the **delay** of help, the situation worsened."},{"sentence":"Hindi na ako magtataka sa **pagluluwat** ng proyekto.","translation":"I will no longer be surprised by the **prolonged duration** of the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nakikipaglaban sa isang duwelo o pormal na labanan, karaniwang gamit ang espada o baril, upang ayusin ang isang usapin ng karangalan.
original_explanation: Basically, a historical drama character. Think Zorro or the guys in 'Heneral Luna' settling beef with swords or pistols instead of subtweets. Today's *duwelista* fights in comment sections or online game lobbies.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong pangkasaysayan, pampanitikan, o pantasya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Antonio Luna bilang isang magiting na **duwelista** noong kanyang panahon.","translation":"Antonio Luna was known as a valiant **duelist** during his time."},{"sentence":"Sa mga pelikula, ang **duwelista** ay laging may matikas na tindig.","translation":"In movies, the **duelist** always has an elegant stance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng kulay pula o ang pagbabago ng kulay tungo sa pula, tulad ng sa balat dahil sa hiya, galit, o iritasyon.
etymology: From `pula` (red). The `pa-` prefix and reduplication `mu-` (< `pu-`) creates a noun describing the state or process of becoming red.
original_explanation: The physical "seen-zoned" notification your face gets when your crush suddenly talks to you. It's also your skin's reaction to trying that new skincare product from a random online seller, or the look of your face after getting scolded by your boss. It’s your body's built-in lie detector and kilig meter.
usage_notes: Can refer to blushing from embarrassment/shyness (`pamumula ng mukha`) or redness from inflammation or irritation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilan ang **pamumula** ng kanyang pisngi nang purihin siya.","translation":"She couldn't stop the **blushing** of her cheeks when she was complimented."},{"sentence":"Ang **pamumula** ng balat ay maaaring senyales ng allergy.","translation":"The **redness** of the skin could be a sign of an allergy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pagsubok sa lasa ng isang pagkain o inumin.
original_explanation: The ultimate invitation at any Pinoy handaan. 'Tikman mo 'tong luto ko!' (Taste my cooking!). It's not just about sampling; it's a request for validation. It can also be used figuratively, like 'tikman ang tagumpay' (to taste success) or, more dramatically, 'tikman ang bagsik ng aking galit!' (taste the fury of my anger!).
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The root word is 'tikim'. 'Tikman' is the command or infinitive form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tikman** mo itong adobo, baka kulang pa sa asin.","translation":"**Taste** this adobo, it might need more salt."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **tikman** ang lahat ng pagkain sa buffet.","translation":"She wants **to taste** all the food at the buffet."}]

meaning_filipino: Iutos o ipagawa sa iba ang pagpapakinis ng isang bagay, tulad ng kahoy, gamit ang liha.
original_explanation: The 'delegation' version of making something smooth. You see a rough wooden table and instead of getting splinters yourself, you call Mang Berto the karpintero and say, 'Ipaliha mo na lang 'tong lamesa.' It's project management for home improvement.
usage_notes: A causative verb used in carpentry and woodworking. Implies ordering or requesting someone else to perform the action of sanding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipaliha** mo sa kanila ang sahig bago barnisan.","translation":"**Have them sand** the floor before applying varnish."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **ipaliha** ang mga lumang upuan para magmukhang bago.","translation":"We need **to have the old chairs sanded** to look new."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang manipis na pirasong nahiwa mula sa isang bagay, lalo na sa pagkain tulad ng karne, prutas, o gulay.
original_explanation: This is a kitchen term. It's the thin piece of onion for gisado, ampalaya for pinakbet, or potato for your homemade fries. It’s more precise than 'hiwa' (cut), implying thinness. If your mom tells you to 'gayat' the onions, she doesn't want big chunks!
usage_notes: Primarily used in cooking. 'Gayatin' is the verb form 'to slice'. 'Gayat' as a noun is the resulting slice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdagdag ka ng ilang **gayat** ng sibuyas.","translation":"Add a few **slices** of onion."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat **gayat** ng kamatis ay dapat magkakapareho ng kapal.","translation":"Each **slice** of tomato should have the same thickness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng mga tuntunin at regulasyon na ipinatutupad sa isang pamayanan o bansa; batas.
original_explanation: Not your friend or supporter in a game (that's the English 'ally'). This is a deep Tagalog word for 'law,' pronounced /A-lay/. You'd sound super formal or like you're reciting an old poem if you use this instead of 'batas.'
usage_notes: Extremely rare and poetic. 'Batas' is the universally used word. The pronunciation is crucial to differentiate it from the English word 'ally'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lahat ay dapat sumunod sa itinakdang **ally** ng kaharian.","translation":"Everyone must follow the established **law** of the kingdom."},{"sentence":"Ang paglabag sa **ally** ay may kaukulang parusa.","translation":"Violating the **law** has a corresponding punishment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglulunsad ng isang bagay o ang pagbaba mula sa isang sasakyan.
original_explanation: The moment you step off the jeepney and your feet hit solid ground. Or when a company finally releases that new product they've been hyping up for months. It's the grand reveal, the official start, the 'baba na po!' moment.
usage_notes: More commonly seen in its verb forms: 'ilunsad' (to launch), 'lumunsad' (to disembark). As a noun, it refers to the act itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagumpay ang **lunsad** ng bagong proyekto ng pamahalaan.","translation":"The **launch** of the government's new project was successful."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng mahabang biyahe, naging ligtas ang kanilang **lunsad** sa daungan.","translation":"After a long journey, their **disembarkation** at the port was safe."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na gumagana nang kusa o walang interbensyon ng tao; isang kilos na ginagawa nang hindi na pinag-iisipan.
original_explanation: 'Kusa.' It's the magic behind ATMs, vendo machines, and your 'auto-reply' when you're on vacation leave. It's also that 'automatiko' reaction of saying 'po' and 'opo' to your elders, or grabbing your phone the moment you wake up. Some things are just programmed into the system, whether it's a machine or a Pinoy. Also refers to a type of car transmission for those who can't be bothered with a clutch.
usage_notes: Can also be used as an adverb ('automatikong nagsara'). The 'k' ending is common in Filipino spelling of English '-ic' words.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ilaw sa pasilyo ay **automatik** na bumubukas kapag may dumadaan.","translation":"The light in the hallway turns on **automatic**ally when someone passes by."},{"sentence":"**Automatik** na ang pag-abot ko ng bayad sa jeep kapag may nag-abot sa akin.","translation":"My passing of the fare in the jeepney is **automatic** whenever someone hands it to me."}]

translation: to make something turn; to bend something
meaning_filipino: Gawing may liko o hindi tuwid ang isang bagay; ibaluktot o ikurbada.
original_explanation: This is the command form. It's what you tell someone to do. 'Boss, palikuin ko na po ba yung kotse sa kanto?' (Boss, should I turn the car at the corner now?). It can also mean to bend something that was straight. 'Sinubukan niyang palikuin ang alambre para maging kawit.'
usage_notes: Similar to 'palihisin' but 'palikuin' is more physical (turning a car, bending a wire) while 'palihisin' is often more abstract (changing a topic).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **palikuin** ang isang matigas na bakal gamit lang ang kamay.","translation":"It's hard **to bend** a hard piece of steel using only your hands."},{"sentence":"**Palikuin** mo ang sasakyan sa susunod na kanto.","translation":"**Turn** the car at the next corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang butas o hukay sa lupa, karaniwang ginagawa ng mga hayop upang maging kanilang tirahan o taguan.
original_explanation: Your bedroom after a week of WFH deadlines, or a rabbit's cozy home. It's any small, enclosed space you retreat to, whether you're a cute bunny or just avoiding adult responsibilities. Parang 'yung kwarto mo na ayaw mong labasan. It's also used for a criminal's lair.
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically for a criminal's hideout.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtago ang kuneho sa kanyang **lungga**.","translation":"The rabbit hid in its **burrow**."},{"sentence":"Natunton ng mga pulis ang **lungga** ng mga magnanakaw.","translation":"The police tracked down the thieves' **hideout**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kulay na nasa pagitan ng berde at kahel sa ispektrum ng liwanag; ang kulay ng hinog na saging, mangga, o ng araw.
original_explanation: It's the color of ripe mangoes, a taxi, and the sun in your kid's drawing. In the Philippines, it's also a politically charged color, often associated with the Aquino family and the People Power Revolution. So yeah, wearing a yellow shirt can sometimes be a statement.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun to mean 'the color yellow.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito niyang kulay ang **dilaw** dahil nagpapaalala ito sa sikat ng araw.","translation":"Her favorite color is **yellow** because it reminds her of sunshine."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bulaklak ng mirasol ay matingkad na **dilaw**.","translation":"The sunflower's petals are a bright **yellow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kulang sa paninindigan, madaling sumuko sa panggigipit, at walang sariling desisyon o prinsipyo.
original_explanation: Literally 'a person without a spine.' This is your friend who agrees with everyone to avoid conflict, or a politician who changes their stance depending on who's funding them. They can't stand up for themselves or for what's right. Sila yung 'yes man' na kahit mali, go lang nang go.
usage_notes: A strong insult, questioning someone's character and integrity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **taong walang-gulugod**; panindigan mo ang iyong mga sinabi.","translation":"Don't be a **spineless person**; stand by what you said."}]

meaning_filipino: Malakas at malinaw ang tunog; kilala, tanyag, o may malaking impluwensiya.
original_explanation: This word has two vibes. First, the literal one: "Ang **matunog** na sampal na narinig ng buong barangay." (A resonant slap heard by the whole village). Second, the chismis/career version: when a name is "ringing bells." "Uy, **matunog** ang pangalan niya para sa promotion." It means someone is famous, influential, or the talk of the town.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for sound or figuratively for reputation and influence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **matunog** na 'hindi' ang isinagot niya sa alok.","translation":"She answered with a **resounding** 'no' to the offer."},{"sentence":"Galing siya sa isang **matunog** na pamilya ng mga politiko.","translation":"He comes from a **well-known** family of politicians."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilagay sa isang lugar na hindi madaling makita o matagpuan; lingid sa kaalaman ng iba.
etymology: From `tago` (hide). `Naka-` indicates the state of being hidden.
original_explanation: Ito yung pera na tinago mo sa medyas para may pang-Grab ka kinabukasan. O yung feelings mo para sa kanya, **nakatago** sa likod ng "Uy, friend!" Yung sikreto ng pamilya na bawal pag-usapan. Lahat tayo may **nakatago**—resibo man 'yan ng online shopping o pangarap na 'di pa nasasabi.
usage_notes: Very common word. Can refer to physical objects, secrets, or emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May pera siyang **nakatago** sa ilalim ng kutson.","translation":"He has money **hidden** under the mattress."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng kanyang mga lihim ay **nakatago** sa isang lumang talaarawan.","translation":"All her secrets are **concealed** in an old diary."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na ginagamit upang pagtakpan, punan, o takpan ang isang butas, hukay, o anumang espasyo.
original_explanation: Think of it as the 'Ctrl+Z' for holes in the ground. It's the soil you use to bury something, whether it's treasure, a dead pet, or your past mistakes (kidding!). In construction, it's the earth used to fill and level land. The verb 'tabunan' means to cover something, like how you'd get buried in work before a long weekend.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'tabunan' (to cover something with) or 'magtabon' (to cover).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit nila ang lupa bilang **tabon** sa malalim na hukay.","translation":"They used the soil as a **fill** for the deep pit."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, baka matanggal ang **tabon** sa balon.","translation":"Be careful, the **cover** on the well might come off."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang modo, magaspang ang pag-uugali, o bastos sa pananalita at pagkilos.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish "vargas" or "bárbaro" (barbaric, wild), but its direct origin is debated. It has been integrated into Tagalog to mean coarse behavior.
original_explanation: Parang yung tito mong lasing na kung ano-ano ang sinasabi sa family reunion. Walang filter. O yung nag-overtake sa'yo tapos siya pa galit. It's the opposite of 'po' and 'opo'. It's rudeness level 9000.
usage_notes: A strong word to describe someone's lack of manners. Often used interchangeably with 'bastos' but can imply a more unrefined or uncultured kind of rudeness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **bargas** makipag-usap sa mga nakatatanda.","translation":"Don't be **rude** when talking to elders."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **bargas** at palamura.","translation":"He is known for being **coarse** and foul-mouthed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unti-unting pagbaba o pagliit ng isang bagay, tulad ng baha, lagnat, o galit.
original_explanation: That feeling of relief when the EDSA traffic finally starts moving, when your fever goes down after taking meds, or when your friend finally calms down after a major "hugot" session. It's the "Okay, we're back to normal" phase.
usage_notes: Commonly used for floods, fevers, swelling, emotions (like anger), and even noise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinihintay namin ang **paghupa** ng baha bago lumabas ng bahay.","translation":"We are waiting for the **subsidence** of the flood before leaving the house."},{"sentence":"Gumaan ang kanyang pakiramdam sa **paghupa** ng kanyang lagnat.","translation":"He felt better with the **easing** of his fever."}]

translation: in cooking, when it comes to cooking
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa larangan, sining, o proseso ng paghahanda ng pagkain sa pamamagitan ng init.
etymology: Mula sa `sa` (in/at) + `pagluluto` (the act of cooking), na mula sa `pag-` + `luto` (cook).
original_explanation: This is the domain of titas, celebrity chefs, and food vloggers. When you talk about someone's skills 'sa pagluluto', you're either praising their adobo recipe that's been passed down for generations or judging their instant noodle 'hacks'. It's the arena where 'secret ingredients' are king.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang tukuyin ang konteksto o larangan ng pagluluto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si lola ang pinakamagaling **sa pagluluto** ng sinigang sa pamilya.","translation":"Grandma is the best **at cooking** sinigang in the family."},{"sentence":"Marami siyang natutunan **sa pagluluto** mula sa panonood ng mga video online.","translation":"She learned a lot **about cooking** from watching videos online."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bilog na bagay na umiikot sa isang ehe. Isang hindi pangkaraniwang varyant ng salitang 'ruweda' o 'gulong'.
original_explanation: Ito yung luma at pormal na tawag sa gulong. Parang 'yung sinasabi ng lolo mo na "Ayusin mo ang roda ng kariton!" bago pa nauso ang "Pa-vulcanize ng gulong ng Fortuner ko, please." It's the vintage version of 'wheel'.
usage_notes: Bihirang gamitin. 'Gulong' ang pang-araw-araw na salita para sa 'wheel'. Ang 'ruweda' ay mas karaniwan para sa 'ferris wheel' o sa mas pormal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga sinaunang karwahe ay may malalaking **roda** na gawa sa kahoy.","translation":"The ancient carriages had large **wheels** made of wood."}]

translation: to examine, to analyze, to inspect
meaning_filipino: Ang masusing pagtingin, pag-aaral, o pagsisiyasat sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon upang matukoy ang katangian, kalagayan, o katotohanan nito.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo sa profile ng bagong friend request. O kaya yung ginagawa ng nanay mo sa'yo mula ulo hanggang paa 'pag aalis ka ng bahay. Sa trabaho, ito yung "due diligence" bago mag-launch ng project. Basically, "stalking with a purpose".
usage_notes: This is the completed action (past tense) form. The infinitive is 'sumuri'. The present tense is 'sumusuri'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumuri** ang doktor sa resulta ng aking mga laboratory test.","translation":"The doctor **examined** the results of my laboratory tests."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **sumuri** nang mabuti sa bawat detalye ng kontrata.","translation":"We need to **analyze** every detail of the contract carefully."}]

translation: to be filled with; to be overcome with (emotion)
meaning_filipino: Punuin o malukuban ng isang matinding damdamin, tulad ng lungkot, takot, o ligaya.
original_explanation: This is a very deep, very 'makata' (poetic) word. It's when an emotion completely takes you over. It's not just 'malungkot' (sad), it's being 'sakbibi ng kalungkutan' (overcome with sadness). It's the feeling you get when your favorite K-drama character dies, or when you finally get your 13th-month pay. It's an emotional full-body takeover.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used for strong emotions. It's a literary or formal term, often found in literature, songs, and formal speeches.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka pababayaang **sakbibihin** ng kalungkutan.","translation":"Don't worry, you won't be left **to be overcome** with sadness."},{"sentence":"Nang manalo siya sa lotto, siya ay **sinakbibi** ng di-maipaliwanag na kagalakan.","translation":"When he won the lottery, he **was filled** with unexplainable joy."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang tuwiran; walang hinto, paglihis, o pag-aatubili.
original_explanation: How you're supposed to go home after work, but you still somehow end up at the milk tea shop. 'Uwi nang **deretso**!' - Your Mom, probably. It's moving from point A to point B without any side quests.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng klase, umuwi ka nang **deretso** sa bahay.","translation":"After class, go **straight** home."},{"sentence":"Pumunta siya **deretso** sa opisina ng manager para magreklamo.","translation":"She went **directly** to the manager's office to complain."}]

meaning_filipino: Gagamit ng salapi sa hinaharap para sa pagbili ng produkto o serbisyo.
original_explanation: The battle cry of someone who just got their sahod (salary) or 13th-month pay. 'Bukas, **maggagasta** ako!' It's the future tense of 'budol'. You're planning to unleash your purchasing power, whether it's on Shopee, at the mall, or on a milk tea binge.
usage_notes: This is the future tense form. The infinitive is 'maggasta'. Almost exclusively refers to spending money.
