usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maggagasta** nang sobra sa iyong badyet.","translation":"Don't **you go spending** beyond your budget."},{"sentence":"Sa susunod na sahod, **maggagasta** ako para sa bagong sapatos.","translation":"Next payday, I **will spend** on new shoes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o resulta ng unti-unting pagkatuklap o pagtanggal ng panlabas na bahagi ng isang bagay, tulad ng pintura o balat.
original_explanation: Ito yung nangyayari sa bagong nail polish mo isang araw pa lang. O sa pintura sa pader na parang nagbabalat, sinasabayan ang pagguho ng mga pangarap mo. Charot. It's the physical version of your patience slowly eroding during a traffic jam sa EDSA.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa unti-unting pagkasira ng isang ibabaw (surface).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkabkab** ng pintura sa pader ay senyales na kailangan na itong kumpunihin.","translation":"The **flaking off** of the paint on the wall is a sign that it needs to be repaired."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang epekto ng acid rain sa **pagkabkab** ng mga lumang monumento.","translation":"They are studying the effect of acid rain on the **erosion** of old monuments."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa kalagayan ng sukdulang kahirapan; lubhang mahirap at halos walang anumang pag-aari.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'petsa de peligro' broke. This is 'isang kahig, isang tuka' (one scratch, one peck) level of poverty. It's when you're so broke, your wallet has cobwebs and even the rats in your house have packed up and moved out. The superlative form of 'mahirap'.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'dukha' serves to intensify the meaning to the highest degree.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pamilyang iyon ay **dukhang-dukha** at nangangailangan ng tulong.","translation":"That family is **extremely poor** and in need of help."},{"sentence":"Maraming organisasyon ang tumutulong sa mga **dukhang-dukha** sa ating lipunan.","translation":"Many organizations help the **destitute** in our society."}]

translation: to dig up; to rummage through
meaning_filipino: Ang paghuhukay o paghahanap sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagkakalkal o pagbubungkal.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'halukay' (paghuhukay o pagkakalkal) at ang gitlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa baul ng lola mo para maghanap ng vintage clothes. O 'yung pag-check mo sa old DMs ng ex mo para sa 'resibo'—that's you, emotionally **humahalukay**. It's digging for something, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa literal na paghuhukay sa lupa o sa paghahalungkat sa isang tumpok ng mga gamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humalukay** siya sa cabinet para hanapin ang kanyang lumang photo album.","translation":"She **rummaged** through the cabinet to find her old photo album."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang mga arkeologo na **humalukay** sa lugar kung saan maaaring may nakabaong sinaunang banga.","translation":"The archaeologists decided to **dig up** the area where ancient jars might be buried."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagpapakita ng kawalan ng kaalaman o pagpili na manatiling walang alam tungkol sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: It's the act of playing dumb. Like when your mom asks who ate the last piece of leche flan and you suddenly don't know anything. It's different from 'mangmang' (ignorant), which is a state. 'Magmangmang' is an action, a choice. It's the "I don't know what you're talking about" defense mechanism. In the age of fake news, some people choose to 'magmangmang' about facts.
usage_notes: 'Magmangmang' or more commonly 'magmangmang-mangahan' implies a deliberate act of pretending to be ignorant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magmangmang-mangahan**, alam kong narinig mo ang utos ko.","translation":"Don't **feign ignorance**, I know you heard my command."},{"sentence":"Pinili niyang **magmangmang** sa mga katiwaliang nangyayari sa kanyang paligid.","translation":"He chose to **be ignorant** of the corruption happening around him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino para sa kalagayan ng pag-iisip kung saan ang isang tao ay labis na nalulong sa mabababaw o walang katuturang nilalaman, lalo na mula sa internet, na humahantong sa pagbaba ng antas ng talino o kritikal na pag-iisip.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you scroll through TikTok for 5 hours straight, watching nothing but dance challenges and 'savage' clapbacks. Your brain turns to mush, and you start speaking in memes. It's the mental equivalent of eating junk food all day. "Grabe, puro skibidi toilet na lang alam ng pinsan ko, tinamaan na ng brainrot."
usage_notes: A modern internet slang term used to describe the perceived negative effects of consuming low-quality online content.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang pagbababad sa social media, baka magka-**brainrot** ka niyan.","translation":"Stop spending so much time on social media, you might get **brain rot** from that."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain, salita, o bagay na mahalay, bastos, at walang galang na lumalabag sa pamantayan ng kagandahang-asal.
original_explanation: This is the R-18 stuff. 'Yung mga green jokes ng tito mo, 'yung mga malalaswang sayaw sa TikTok, o 'yung mga comment sa social media na bastos. Anything that makes you go, 'Eww, kadiri! Ang bastos naman niyan!' ay isang uri ng **kalaswaan**.
usage_notes: A strong word used to denote something that is morally or socially indecent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **kalaswaan** sa iyong pananalita, lalo na't may mga bata.","translation":"Stop the **vulgarity** in your speech, especially since there are children."},{"sentence":"Ang pelikula ay binigyan ng R-18 rating dahil sa mga eksena ng **kalaswaan**.","translation":"The movie was given an R-18 rating because of scenes of **lewdness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alsa o paglobo ng isang bagay dahil sa panloob na presyon, init, o pamamaga.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your 'tita' arms when you wear a tight shirt, or what your pandesal does in the oven. It’s that 'poof' effect, whether it's from rising dough or rising body fat after the holidays.
usage_notes: Can be used for food, body parts, or inanimate objects that swell.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umasbok** ang tinapay habang niluluto sa hurno.","translation":"The bread **bulged** while baking in the oven."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang pag-asbok ng kaniyang mga ugat sa braso.","translation":"The bulging of his veins on his arm was very visible."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang patibong o kagamitan na ginagamit sa panghuhuli ng mga hayop. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, isang mapanlinlang na plano o sitwasyon upang mahuli o mapahamak ang isang tao.
original_explanation: Can be a literal trap for 'yung daga sa kusina mo, or a metaphorical one, like that "buy 1 take 1" sale for something you don't need—it's a bitag for your wallet! Or that friend request from a profile with 0 friends and a stolen photo? Bitag 'yan, 'wag i-accept. Think of Ben Tulfo's show, that's the energy.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for animal traps or figuratively for deceptive schemes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahulog ang daga sa **bitag** na inilagay niya.","translation":"The rat fell into the **trap** that he set."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa mga online scam, isa 'yang uri ng **bitag**.","translation":"Be careful of online scams, that is a type of **trap**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtataas ng kamay laban sa isang tao bilang tanda ng pananakit o pagbabanta, na naganap na.
original_explanation: The past tense of the teleserye drama moment. The hand has been raised. The threat has been made. Ito yung nangyari bago ka nag-walk out. The completed action of disrespect.
usage_notes: Anyong pangnagdaan (past tense) ng 'pagbuhatan'. Tulad ng kasalukuyang anyo nito, halos palagi itong ginagamit kasama ng pariralang 'ng kamay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailanman ay hindi siya **pinagbuhatan** ng kamay ng kanyang asawa.","translation":"Her husband never once **raised** a hand **against** her."},{"sentence":"Nang siya ay **pinagbuhatan** ng kamay, napilitan siyang umalis.","translation":"When a hand was **raised against** her, she was forced to leave."}]

translation: to be torn to shreds; to become tattered
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging watak-watak o sira-sira dahil sa maraming punit.
etymology: From 'magka-' + reduplication of 'punit' (tear). The reduplication indicates multiple tears or a state of being completely torn.
original_explanation: This is the state of your favorite t-shirt after a decade of loyal service. Or your submitted report after your terror prof is done with it. Or your heart after finding out your crush is "in a relationship." It's being completely and utterly torn apart.
usage_notes: Describes a state of being severely torn or tattered.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong basta iwanan ang mga papel diyan, baka **magkapunit-punit**.","translation":"Don't just leave the papers there, they might **get torn to shreds**."},{"sentence":"**Nagkapunit-punit** ang lumang bandila dahil sa malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The old flag **became tattered** because of the strong typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng di-patas na pagtrato o pagbibigay ng higit na pabor sa isang tao o grupo kumpara sa iba.
etymology: Taglish, from Tagalog 'may' (to have) and English 'favoritism'.
original_explanation: The ultimate "sana all" complaint. This is what you say when your sibling gets the bigger piece of chicken, or when your boss only praises one person in the team meeting. "Grabe, si Sir talaga, may favoritism!" It's the battle cry of the un-favored.
usage_notes: A very common Taglish phrase used in offices, schools, and family settings to call out unfairness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ko sa gurong 'yan, halatang **may favoritism** siya sa klase.","translation":"I don't like that teacher, she clearly **shows favoritism** in class."},{"sentence":"Inakusahan ang manager na **may favoritism** dahil laging ang kaibigan niya ang napo-promote.","translation":"The manager was accused of **having favoritism** because his friend always gets promoted."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakihang labanan o sagupaan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang armadong grupo.
original_explanation: Think of it as the ultimate showdown. Not just a simple "away," but a full-blown "batalya" like in Mobile Legends when it's a 5v5 clash for the Lord. Or the "batalya" sa MRT during rush hour just to get a spot inside the train.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of war, history, or epic struggles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Batalya** sa Mactan ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The **Battle** of Mactan is an important part of Philippine history."},{"sentence":"Handa na ang mga sundalo para sa susunod na **batalya**.","translation":"The soldiers are ready for the next **combat**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng karangalan, karingalan, o pambihirang kagandahan at kadakilaan.
original_explanation: Ito yung feeling pag nakita mo yung Mayon Volcano sa isang perfect, cloudless day. O yung entrance ng isang beauty queen sa Miss Universe. Sobrang grand at nakaka-wow. Yung tipong mapapahinto ka at masasabi mong, "Ang dingal!" It's grandeur with a capital G.
usage_notes: Isang napakapormal at pampanitikang salita. Hindi ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap. Ang pangngalan nitong 'karingalan' ay mas kilala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **dingal** ng paglubog ng araw sa Manila Bay ay hinahangaan ng lahat.","translation":"The **magnificence** of the sunset at Manila Bay is admired by all."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita sa parada ang **dingal** ng kulturang Pilipino.","translation":"The parade showed the **splendor** of Filipino culture."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa panahon sa simula ng isang araw o sa mas maagang bahagi ng isang takdang oras.
original_explanation: "Aga" is that feeling when your alarm goes off at 4 AM for your BPO shift, or when your tita shows up for the 8 AM party at 6:30 AM. It's the opposite of "Filipino time." It's being *too* ready, *too* soon. "Ang aga mo naman!" can be both a compliment and a complaint.
usage_notes: Often used with the prefix "ma-" to form the adjective "maaga" (early). "Aga" by itself is less common in full sentences but frequent in exclamations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **aga** mo namang dumating!","translation":"You arrived so **early**!"},{"sentence":"Bukas ng **aga**, kailangan ko nang umalis.","translation":"Tomorrow **morning** (early), I need to leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng negosyo na nagpapautang ng pera kapalit ng isang mahalagang bagay bilang kolateral, na tinatawag na sangla.
original_explanation: The 'kapit sa patalim' financial institution. You'll see them everywhere, often with a smiling mascot. It's where your lola's necklace goes on a temporary vacation when tuition is due or when you need cash *pronto*. Also known by its Tagalog name, 'sanglaan'.
usage_notes: The native Tagalog term 'sanglaan' is also very common and used interchangeably.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinangla niya ang kanyang singsing sa **pawnshop**.","translation":"She pawned her ring at the **pawnshop**."},{"sentence":"Maraming **pawnshop** sa kanto ng aming kalye.","translation":"There are many **pawnshops** at the corner of our street."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging karapat-dapat o pagkakaroon ng kahalagahan at kwalipikasyon; batayan ng pagpapasya na nakabase sa kakayahan.
original_explanation: This is the 'resibo' or proof of your achievements. When your boss promotes you 'based on merit,' it means you got it because you're actually good at your job, not just because you're the 'tito's pamangkin'. It's the opposite of the 'palakasan' system.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, legal, or academic contexts. The English word 'merit' is also frequently used in code-switching.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagpili ay dapat batay sa **merito** at hindi sa personal na koneksyon.","translation":"The selection should be based on **merit** and not on personal connections."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan ng korte ang **merito** ng kaso.","translation":"The court studied the **merits** of the case."}]

translation: having no money to pay, unable to pay
meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang magbayad o walang perang pambayad sa isang utang, serbisyo, o produkto.
original_explanation: The official state of being on 'petsa de peligro' (the days before payday). When the GrabFood cart is full but the G-Cash balance is empty. It’s the polite way of saying 'wala akong pera' when the waiter brings the bill.
usage_notes: A common phrase to express inability to pay. It is a statement of a current state, referring to a future or required action of paying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paumanhin po, pero **walang-ibabayad** ang pasyente para sa ospital.","translation":"I'm sorry, but the patient has **no money to pay** for the hospital."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko sanang sumama pero **walang-ibabayad** sa ticket.","translation":"I'd like to go, but I'm **unable to pay** for the ticket."}]

translation: daily life, livelihood, way of life
meaning_filipino: Ang pang-araw-araw na pamumuhay, gawain, o hanapbuhay ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the daily grind. The 'raket' you do to survive. It's less about the grand philosophical meaning of 'buhay' and more about the practical, 'how-to-pay-the-Meralco-bill' side of things. 'Diskarte lang sa buhay-buhay' is the mantra.
usage_notes: Refers to the mundane, routine aspects of life and making a living.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang magsipag para sa ating **buhay-buhay**.","translation":"We need to work hard for our **daily life/livelihood**."},{"sentence":"Ganito lang ang aming simpleng **buhay-buhay** sa probinsya.","translation":"This is just our simple **way of life** in the province."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangangahulugang mahina ang pag-iisip, mabagal umunawa, o hindi matalino. Karaniwang ginagamit sa pariralang 'mapurol ang isip' o 'mapurol ang utak'.
original_explanation: This is what you feel after a 12-hour shift—your brain just refuses to brain. It's when someone tells a joke and you only get it three hours later. Often used as an insult ('Mapurol ka ba?') but also as a self-deprecating comment ('Sorry, mapurol ang isip ko ngayon, puyat'). It's the mental equivalent of a buffering YouTube video.
usage_notes: Almost always used with 'isip' or 'utak' (e.g., 'mapurol ang isip', 'mapurol ang utak'). Can be considered offensive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang tawaging **mapurol** ang isip, baka nahihirapan lang siyang umintindi.","translation":"Don't call him/her **dull-witted**, maybe he/she is just having a hard time understanding."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng araw mula sa paglubog ng araw hanggang sa pagsikat nito; ang panahon ng kadiliman sa loob ng isang araw.
original_explanation: The time for BPO workers to grind, for marites to convene, for lovers to have "deep talks," and for everyone else to either binge-watch a series or overthink their life choices until 3 AM. "Gabi na" is the signal to either go home or for the *inuman* to just be getting started.
usage_notes: The opposite of "araw" (day). "Magandang gabi" is the standard evening greeting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap matulog kapag malamig ang **gabi**.","translation":"It's nice to sleep when the **night** is cold."},{"sentence":"Nag-aaral siya mula umaga hanggang **gabi**.","translation":"She studies from morning until **night**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling anyo ng isang salita o parirala, na karaniwang binubuo ng mga unang titik nito.
original_explanation: BFF, LOL, SKL, IDK—lahat 'yan **daglat**. It's how we shorten everything kasi tamad tayong mag-type or magsulat. Mula sa "G." para sa "Ginoo" hanggang sa "DOST" para sa "Department of Science and Technology," buhay natin ay puno ng daglat.
usage_notes: Can refer to both abbreviations (like Mr. -> G.) and acronyms (like NASA).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'Gng.' ay **daglat** para sa salitang 'Ginang'.","translation":"'Gng.' is the **abbreviation** for the word 'Ginang' (Mrs.)."},{"sentence":"Maraming **daglat** ang ginagamit sa text messaging para mapabilis ang pag-uusap.","translation":"Many **abbreviations** are used in text messaging to speed up conversation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng electromagnetic radiation na may kakayahang tumagos sa karamihan ng mga bagay, kabilang ang katawan ng tao. Ginagamit sa medisina upang makita ang loob ng katawan, lalo na ang mga buto.
etymology: Mula sa pinagsamang salitang Espanyol na "rayos" (rays) at "equis" (ang pangalan ng letrang 'X'). Isang direktang pagsasalin ng "X-ray".
original_explanation: Ito yung kailangan mo kapag feeling mo may nabali sa'yo—either buto mo o puso mo. Pero sa hospital, buto lang ang kaya nilang i-check. "Pa-rayos-ekis ka na, baka hindi lang pala pilay 'yan." The ultimate "what's inside counts" technology.
usage_notes: Ang salitang "X-ray" (binibigkas na /eks-rey/) ay mas karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Ang "rayos-ekis" ay mas pormal o kung minsan ay ginagamit para sa pagbibiro.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita ng **rayos-ekis** na may bali ang kanyang braso.","translation":"The **X-ray** showed that his arm was broken."},{"sentence":"Kailangan siyang sumailalim sa **rayos-ekis** ng dibdib para sa kanyang medical exam.","translation":"He needs to undergo a chest **X-ray** for his medical exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos na nakilahok sa isang alitan, argumento, o pisikal na labanan sa ibang tao o pangkat sa nakaraan.
original_explanation: The past tense of "bardagulan." This is what you tell your friends happened last night. "Nakipag-away ako sa jowa ko, kaya single na ulit ako. Charot!" It’s the completed action of conflict.
usage_notes: Past tense of 'makipag-away'. Implies a completed fight or argument.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahapon, **nakipag-away** siya sa kanyang kapatid.","translation":"Yesterday, he **fought** with his sibling."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang magalit, **nakipag-away** na sila at bati na ulit.","translation":"Don't be angry anymore, they already **fought** and have made up again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bunton o tumpok ng anumang bagay; tumutukoy sa napakaraming dami.
original_explanation: This is the word for "a whole freakin' lot," but specifically in a pile. Got a mountain of laundry? `Santambak` na labahin. Your boss dropped a ton of work on you before a long weekend? `Santambak` na trabaho. It's the visual representation of being overwhelmed. Picture a dump truck unloading—that's `santambak`.
usage_notes: Used to describe a large quantity of something, usually in a disorganized pile. Can be used for both physical objects and abstract concepts (like work or problems).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **santambak** na hugasing plato sa lababo.","translation":"There's **a heap of** dishes to be washed in the sink."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng bakasyon, **santambak** na trabaho ang bumungad sa kanya.","translation":"After the vacation, **a pile of** work greeted him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang miyembro ng Rotary Club, isang pandaigdigang samahan ng mga propesyonal at lider ng negosyo na nagkakaloob ng serbisyong pangkawanggawa.
original_explanation: You know those successful titos and titas in your town? The doctors, lawyers, and business owners who meet up for lunch and then fund a school library or a medical mission? That's them. Being a Rotarian is a sign that you've "made it" and are now in the "giving back to the community" phase of your life, complete with plaques and photo-ops.
usage_notes: Used to refer to a member of the Rotary Club. It's a proper noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tatay ko ay isang aktibong **Rotarian** sa aming probinsya.","translation":"My father is an active **Rotarian** in our province."},{"sentence":"Nag-organisa ang mga **Rotarian** ng isang feeding program para sa mga bata.","translation":"The **Rotarians** organized a feeding program for the children."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pamamahagi ng malalaking datos o electronic files sa internet; isang malakas at mabilis na agos ng tubig o ulan.
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood source for 'free' movies, software, and games back in the day. It's the digital 'tiangge' where you download things of questionable legality. Also, the original meaning, which is a super heavy downpour, like 'OMG, may bagyo!' levels of rain.
usage_notes: Used in both its original English meaning (heavy rain/flow) and its modern tech meaning (file sharing). The tech meaning is more common in Taglish conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-download ako ng bagong pelikula sa **torrent**.","translation":"I downloaded a new movie from a **torrent**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **torrent** ng ulan, bumaha sa kalsada.","translation":"Because of the **torrent** of rain, the street flooded."}]

meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit na pag-iling, na karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng matinding pagkadismaya, pagtanggi, o kawalan ng pag-asa.
etymology: Reduplication of `iling` (shake of the head) to show intensity or repetition.
original_explanation: This isn't just a 'no,' it's a 'hell no' or a 'tsk tsk tsk.' It's the reaction of your lola seeing your ripped jeans. It's your reaction when you see your Meralco bill. The **iling-iling** is a gesture loaded with disappointment, resignation, or disbelief. 'Friend: 'Umutang na naman ako sa 5-6.' You: *iling-iling*.'
usage_notes: The repetition intensifies the meaning of a single `iling`, conveying stronger emotion like deep disappointment or frustration. The verb form is `umiling-iling`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iling-iling** na lamang ang naisagot ng ale nang malamang nanakawan siya.","translation":"The **repeated shaking of her head** was all the lady could manage when she found out she was robbed."},{"sentence":"Napuno ng **iling-iling** at buntong-hininga ang kwarto habang pinapanood nila ang balita.","translation":"The room was filled with the **shaking of heads** and sighs as they watched the news."}]

translation: the manner of care or protection
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o antas ng pag-aalaga, pagprotekta, o pag-aaruga na ipinagkaloob sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This isn't just care (`kalinga`), but the *way* care is given. It's the difference between a nurse who just does their job and one who treats you like family. "Ramdam na ramdam ko ang `pagkakakalinga` ng lola ko." It's the quality of the TLC (tender loving care). It’s how your plant thrives because of the way you water it, or how a pet is happy because of the way it's treated.
usage_notes: Focuses on the quality and method of the care provided, not just the act itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang kapantay ang **pagkakakalinga** ng isang ina.","translation":"The **manner of a mother's care** is unparalleled."},{"sentence":"Ipinagpapasalamat niya ang **pagkakakalinga** sa kanya ng mga nars sa ospital.","translation":"He is thankful for the **way he was cared for** by the nurses at the hospital."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang nagpapahayag ng kawalan ng interes, paghamon, o pag-uugnay sa isang naunang nabanggit na paksa.
etymology: From 'ano' (what) + 'naman' (particle indicating contrast, shift, or retort).
original_explanation: The official phrase of the 'pake-alamero' and the 'wala akong pake'. It's the verbal equivalent of a shrug or an eye-roll. 'Maganda siya.' 'Eh, **ano naman**?' ('She's beautiful.' 'Eh, **so what**?'). It's the ultimate comeback when you have no other comeback. Use with caution, may cause tampo.
usage_notes: The tone is crucial. It can be a neutral "and what about...?" or a very confrontational "so what?". The prefix 'E' or 'Eh' often precedes it to add emphasis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayaman daw ang pamilya niya. E, **ano naman** kung mayaman sila?","translation":"They say her family is rich. Eh, **so what** if they're rich?"},{"sentence":"Ikaw, **ano naman** ang masasabi mo tungkol dito?","translation":"You, **what about you**, what can you say about this?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng mga kilos o gawain upang mapanatili o mapabuti ang kalusugan ng katawan o isipan; ang paggamit ng isang karapatan o kakayahan.
etymology: From 'ehersisyo', from Spanish 'ejercicio'. The 'e' is often dropped in colloquial speech, becoming 'hersisyo'.
original_explanation: The command form for 'use it or lose it.' This is what your brain tells your body to do after eating a whole lechon, or what your tita from the US tells you to do with your 'right to remain silent' when another tita asks about your love life.
usage_notes: A less common verb form compared to 'mag-ehersisyo'. This form is transitive, focusing on the thing being exercised (e.g., a right, a body part).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **hersisyuhin** ang iyong karapatang bumoto.","translation":"You need to **exercise** your right to vote."},{"sentence":"Payo ng terapista na **hersisyuhin** niya ang naninigas na braso.","translation":"The therapist's advice is for him to **exercise** his stiff arm."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabiguang matugunan o maibigay ang isang pangangailangan, kahilingan, o responsibilidad.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (hindi) at "pagkakatugunan" (state of being able to respond/meet).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung nag-chat ka sa customer service tapos puro bot ang sumasagot. O 'yung gobyerno na nangako ng tulong pero hanggang ngayon "for processing" pa rin ang status. It's the ultimate "seen zone" from people and institutions that are supposed to help you.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pormal na konteksto na may kaugnayan sa serbisyo, responsibilidad, o pangangailangan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **di-pagkakatugunan** sa mga pangangailangan ng mga nasalanta ay nagdulot ng malawakang pagkadismaya.","translation":"The **failure to meet** the needs of the victims caused widespread dismay."},{"sentence":"Inireklamo nila ang **di-pagkakatugunan** ng ahensya sa kanilang mga sulat.","translation":"They complained about the agency's **unresponsiveness** to their letters."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, kilos, o salita na hindi angkop o nababagay sa sitwasyon, panahon, o lokasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling when you wear a gown to a beach party, or make a "That's what she said" joke during a company board meeting. Your comment, your outfit, your very existence in that moment is `wala sa lugar`. It's the cringe-worthy awkwardness of not reading the room.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na maling pagkakalagay o, mas karaniwan, sa sosyal o kontekstwal na hindi pagiging angkop.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biro niya ay **wala sa lugar** dahil seryoso ang pinag-uusapan.","translation":"His joke was **inappropriate** because the topic of discussion was serious."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **wala ako sa lugar** sa mamahaling handaan na iyon.","translation":"I felt **out of place** at that expensive party."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang abutin o marating, alinman sa paraang pisikal o metaporikal.
original_explanation: Like your crush who doesn't know you exist. Or the top shelf at the grocery store where they put the good imported stuff. It's that goal, person, or thing that's just out of reach, making you feel like a T-Rex trying to make a bed.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical distance or figuratively for goals, dreams, or social status.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa itaas na estante ang libro kaya **di-maabot** ng bata.","translation":"The book is on the top shelf, so it's **unreachable** for the child."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang pangarap na maging artista ay tila **di-maabot**.","translation":"For her, the dream of becoming an actress seems **unattainable**."}]

translation: to become fierce, to act savagely
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng labis na kabagsikan, kalupitan, o pagiging mabangis, tulad ng isang hayop na nananakmal o isang taong nagagalit nang husto.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your chill boss finally snaps after the 10th revision request. It's going from "Okay lang" to "RAWR!" It's the transformation into a wild, fierce state. Also applies to your mom when you come home past curfew. "Nagalit ang amo at nagbangis sa mga tamad na empleyado."
usage_notes: Often used to describe a sudden, intense display of anger or ferocity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit ang pinakamaamong aso ay maaaring **magbangis** kapag sinaktan.","translation":"Even the most gentle dog can **become fierce** when hurt."},{"sentence":"**Nagbangis** ang bida sa pelikula matapos patayin ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"The protagonist in the movie **acted savagely** after his family was killed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o lalagyan kung saan pinapakain ang mga alagang hayop, lalo na ang mga manok o ibon.
etymology: From `pa-` (locative prefix) + `tukâ` (peck) + `-an` (locative suffix). "A place for pecking."
original_explanation: This is the designated dining area for your chickens. Think of it as their mini-canteen where they get their daily dose of darak or corn. If you see a bunch of chickens flocking to one spot, that's the patukaan.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of raising poultry or birds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nilinis ni Mang Kardo ang **patukaan** bago siya naglagay ng bagong pagkain para sa mga manok.","translation":"Mang Kardo cleaned the **feeding trough** before he put new food for the chickens."},{"sentence":"Nag-aagawan ang mga sisiw sa **patukaan**.","translation":"The chicks are scrambling at the **feeding area**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkagat o pagkain sa isang bagay nang paulit-ulit at may ingay, karaniwan sa matitigas na pagkain.
etymology: From the onomatopoeic root "ngabngab", with the prefix "pag-" to form a noun.
original_explanation: You know that sound someone makes when they're eating chicharon or cornick? That's it. It's the sound of pure, crunchy enjoyment. It can also be what a dog does to a bone. It’s not a quiet, polite nibble; it's a full-on, noisy, satisfying gnaw.
usage_notes: An onomatopoeic word, the sound mimics the action. Often implies a noisy or somewhat messy way of eating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Rinig na rinig ang **pagngabngab** niya ng buto ng manok.","translation":"His **gnawing** on the chicken bone could be clearly heard."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **pagngabngab** ng yelo, masama iyan sa ngipin mo.","translation":"Stop your **noisy munching** of ice, that's bad for your teeth."}]

translation: to declare; to state; to narrate
meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagpapahayag, paglalahad, o pagsasalaysay ng isang bagay, ideya, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is a very formal word. Parang 'make a declaration' ang dating. Hindi mo ito sasabihin sa kaibigan mong, "Pre, magsaysay ka nga ng chismis." Pang-Panatang Makabayan, SONA, o courtroom drama lang ang level nito. It means 'to state' or 'to narrate' with authority and significance.
usage_notes: Primarily used in formal, literary, or official contexts. Not common in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang testigo ay tumayo upang **magsaysay** ng lahat ng kanyang nalalaman.","translation":"The witness stood up **to state** everything he knew."},{"sentence":"Hayaan ninyo akong **magsaysay** ng isang kwento ng kabayanihan.","translation":"Allow me **to narrate** a story of heroism."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na nagpapasimula o nagtatakda ng isang bagong uso o estilo na kalaunang ginagaya ng marami.
original_explanation: Ito yung friend mong laging nauuna sa lahat—sa fashion, sa music, sa memes. Bago pa man mag-viral sa TikTok, alam na niya. Siya yung reason kung bakit ka napabili ng air fryer o kung bakit alam mo yung latest coffee shop na "hidden gem" kuno. Sila ang nagse-set ng standard, tayo ang taga-sunod.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga usapang fashion, social media, at kultura. Isang modernong hiram na salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **trendsetter** sa aming opisina pagdating sa OOTD.","translation":"She's the **trendsetter** in our office when it comes to OOTD (Outfit of the Day)."},{"sentence":"Ang mga kabataan ngayon ay gustong maging **trendsetter** sa TikTok.","translation":"The youth today want to be **trendsetters** on TikTok."}]

translation: to care for; to nurture; to support
meaning_filipino: Mag-alaga, kumalinga, o tumangkilik sa isang tao, lalo na sa isang nangangailangan o mas bata.
etymology: From Tagalog 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'andukha' (to care for, adopt).
original_explanation: This is the OG 'Tita/Tito' move. It's about taking someone under your wing, whether it's a new hire at the office you guide through the BPO jungle, a younger sibling you help with their homework, or a stray cat you decide to feed. It's a formal, deep word for nurturing and supporting someone.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat literary term. 'Mag-alaga' is much more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng mga magulang na **mag-andukha** sa kanilang mga anak.","translation":"It is the duty of parents **to care for** their children."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nag-**andukha** sa ulilang pamangkin.","translation":"She was the one who **nurtured** the orphaned nephew."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa tao, wika, o kultura na nagmula o may kaugnayan sa Cebu at iba pang bahagi ng Visayas at Mindanao. Ito ang pangalawa sa pinakamalaking wika sa Pilipinas.
etymology: Mula sa pangalan ng lugar na "Cebu" + hulaping Espanyol na "-ano", na nangangahulugang "mula sa/kaugnay sa".
original_explanation: Ang mga 'Bisdak' (Bisayang Dako)! Sila 'yung mga kababayan natin mula sa Cebu at karatig-lugar. Ang wika nila, 'yung may malambing na 'gugma' para sa pag-ibig. Huwag mo silang tatawaging 'dialect' lang, it's a language, okay? Maayong adlaw!
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pangngalan para sa wika o tao (isang Cebuano), at pang-uri para ilarawan ang isang bagay (kulturang Cebuano).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong siyang magsalita ng **Cebuano** dahil lumaki siya sa Davao.","translation":"He knows how to speak **Cebuano** because he grew up in Davao."},{"sentence":"Ang lechon **Cebuano** ay kilala sa buong mundo.","translation":"The **Cebuano** lechon is known worldwide."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis at mahabang piraso ng tela o materyal, karaniwang ginagamit bilang palamuti, pantali sa buhok, o sa pagbabalot ng regalo.
original_explanation: That cute ribbon you use to tie up a gift, your hair, or the lechon belly. It's the final touch that says 'I made an effort.' Also, the thing your cat will inevitably play with more than the actual gift. From the Spanish 'lazo'.
usage_notes: Can refer to the ribbon material itself or the bow tied from it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nilagyan niya ng pulang **laso** ang regalo para sa kanyang ina.","translation":"She put a red **bow** on the gift for her mother."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **laso** sa buhok mo!","translation":"The **ribbon** in your hair is beautiful!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa isang lalaking bading o homoseksuwal, na kadalasang ginagamit sa paraang mapaglaro o minsa'y mapanlait.
etymology: From 'bading' + '-ette' (a diminutive or feminizing suffix). A form of swardspeak or gay lingo.
original_explanation: A swardspeak (gay lingo) term for 'bading'. It's like putting a French-sounding suffix on it to make it sound... 'classier'? Or just funnier. Used among friends, it's playful. Used by a stranger, it can be offensive. Context is key, 'teh!
usage_notes: The tone can vary from affectionate to derogatory depending on the speaker and context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halika rito, mga **badette**! May chika ako!","translation":"Come here, gays! I have some gossip!"},{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang tawaging **badette** kung hindi mo siya kaibigan.","translation":"Don't call him a **badette** if you're not his friend."}]

translation: to honor, to give tribute to
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng parangal o pagkilala sa isang tao o entidad.
original_explanation: This is the action version of "parangal". It's what the emcee does during an awards night: "At ngayon, ating pararangalan ang ating top agent for this month..." It's when you finally give your mom that "Best Nanay in the World" mug you bought from the mall.
usage_notes: This is a location/beneficiary-focus verb. The object being honored is marked by 'ang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nararapat lamang na **parangalan** ang mga bayaning nagbuwis ng buhay para sa bayan.","translation":"It is only right **to honor** the heroes who gave their lives for the country."},{"sentence":"**Parangalan** mo ang iyong mga magulang sa lahat ng kanilang sakripisyo.","translation":"**Honor** your parents for all their sacrifices."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang samahan o pagkakabuklod ng mga tao na may iisang layunin, paniniwala, o pinagmulan, na ang turingan ay parang magkakapatid.
etymology: Mula sa "kapatid" (sibling) + mga panlaping "ka-" at "-an", na tumutukoy sa isang kolektibong grupo o relasyon.
original_explanation: It's your squad, your barkada, your org, your fraternity/sorority, or even your church group. It’s the feeling of belonging to a group that has your back, whether it's for a project, a cause, or just a weekend inuman. Think Katipunan, but with less fighting and more team-building seminars.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa mga pormal na organisasyon (tulad ng mga fraternity o orden ng relihiyon) at sa mga impormal na ugnayan ng pagsasama.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kapatiran** ng mga Katipunero ang naging susi sa simula ng rebolusyon.","translation":"The **brotherhood** of the Katipuneros was the key to the start of the revolution."},{"sentence":"Masaya ang **kapatiran** sa aming opisina tuwing Christmas party.","translation":"The **fellowship** in our office is joyful during the Christmas party."}]

translation: to make stronger; to increase the volume/intensity
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaragdag ng puwersa, intensidad, o volyum sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The command form of "lakas." When your mom tells you to "Lakasan mo ang boses mo!" she wants you to speak up. When you're listening to your favorite song, you tell the driver, "Manong, pakilakasan po!" to turn up the volume. It's the verb for amplifying anything, from your voice to the electric fan's speed.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa anyong pautos. Maaaring gamitin para sa tunog, bilis, puwersa, atbp.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**lakasan** mo naman ang aircon, ang init!","translation":"Please **turn up** the aircon, it's so hot!"},{"sentence":"**Lakasan** mo ang iyong loob at harapin ang mga pagsubok.","translation":"**Strengthen** your will and face the challenges."}]

translation: to match in value, to give as an equivalent
meaning_filipino: Ibigay bilang katumbas o kapalit na may parehong halaga o sukat. Ipantay sa halaga, kalidad, o importansya.
original_explanation: This is the 'make it fair' verb. It's about finding an equal exchange. You 'itumbas' the effort your partner gives. You try to 'itumbas' the love your parents gave you. In a more literal sense, if you borrow 100 pesos, you should 'itumbas' the same amount when you pay it back. It's the core of 'fairness' and 'reciprocity.' Walang short-changing dapat!
usage_notes: Refers to equivalence in value, which can be monetary, quantitative, or abstract (like effort or love).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong premyo ang maaari mong **itumbas** sa kanyang katapatan?","translation":"What prize can you **give as an equivalent** for his loyalty?"},{"sentence":"Walang halaga ang kayang **itumbas** sa pagmamahal ng isang ina.","translation":"No amount can **equal** a mother's love."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malinaw, walang kulay, at malapot na likidong may matamis na lasa, ginagamit sa mga pampaganda, pagkain, at gamot.
original_explanation: That secret ingredient in your lotion that makes your skin feel smooth and not dry like a "daing na isda". It's a master of moisture, found in everything from soap to cake frosting. It's the reason why some special effects "tears" in movies look so real and sticky.
usage_notes: A chemical/technical term. Often seen in ingredient lists of cosmetics and food products.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **gliserina** ay isang karaniwang sangkap sa mga sabon upang mapanatili ang kahalumigmigan ng balat.","translation":"**Glycerine** is a common ingredient in soaps to maintain the skin's moisture."},{"sentence":"Gumagamit sila ng **gliserina** sa paggawa ng yelo sa pelikula para hindi ito madaling matunaw.","translation":"They use **glycerine** to make ice in movies so it doesn't melt easily."}]

meaning_filipino: Dumalo at makisaya sa isang pistang-bayan, karaniwang sa ibang lugar, upang makikain at makiisa sa pagdiriwang.
etymology: Mula sa `mang-` + `pista`. Ang 'pista' ay hango sa salitang Espanyol na 'fiesta'.
original_explanation: The national sport of Pinoys before the pandemic. It's when you go to another town or barangay just to eat for free during their fiesta. The goal is to visit as many houses as you can. "Tara, mamista tayo sa kabilang bayan, fiesta daw ni San Isidro!"
usage_notes: Nangangahulugan ng paglalakbay sa isang lugar para lamang sa pagdiriwang ng pista.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Mayo, maraming taga-siyudad ang umuuwi sa probinsya para **mamista**.","translation":"Every May, many city dwellers go home to the province to **celebrate fiestas**."},{"sentence":"Nagkayayaan ang magkakaibigan na **mamista** sa Bulacan.","translation":"The friends decided among themselves to **go fiesta-hopping** in Bulacan."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hindi makapagsalita, karaniwan dahil sa matinding hiya, takot, o pagkagulat.
original_explanation: Yan 'yung feeling mo 'pag tinawag ka for recitation pero 'di ka nagbasa. Bigla kang naging umid. O 'pag nakita mo si crush tapos bigla kang kinausap, tapos ang nasabi mo lang ay "uhm... ah..." You're not physically mute, na-mental block ka lang.
usage_notes: Describes a temporary state of being unable to speak, not a permanent disability.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **umid** ang dila niya sa harap ng maraming tao.","translation":"His tongue became **tied** in front of many people."},{"sentence":"Napatingin na lang siya at nanatiling **umid** sa gulat.","translation":"He just stared and remained **speechless** in shock."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kabilang sa lahi o relihiyon ng Hudaismo.
original_explanation: A term for a Jewish person. Sometimes used in a historical or religious context, like when lola tells stories from the Bible. You might also hear the variant 'Hudiyo'.
usage_notes: Ang 'Hudiyo' ay isang alternatibong baybay. Ginagamit bilang pangngalan (isang Hudio) at pang-uri (kulturang Hudio).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **Hudio** ang naninirahan sa Israel.","translation":"Many **Jews** live in Israel."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang mga tradisyon ng mga **Hudio**.","translation":"They are studying the traditions of the **Jewish** people."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katutubong alpabeto ng wikang Tagalog na binubuo ng dalawampung titik (a, b, k, d, e, g, h, i, l, m, n, ng, o, p, r, s, t, u, w, y).
etymology: From the first four letters 'a-b-k-d'. Coined by Lope K. Santos and based on the Spanish 'abecedario'.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino alphabet before they added the extra letters from Spanish and English. It's the 'simple life' version of our writing system, before things got complicated with C, F, J, Ñ, Q, V, X, and Z. Think of it as the Nokia 3310 of Filipino alphabets.
usage_notes: The 'abakada' has been officially replaced by the modern 28-letter Filipino alphabet. It is now primarily taught for historical and literary context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong elementarya, ang **abakada** ang unang itinuro sa amin.","translation":"In elementary school, the **abakada** was the first thing taught to us."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalarawan sa isang tao, bagay, lugar, o pangyayari sa pamamagitan ng salita.
original_explanation: Yung tanong sa'yo ng chismosa mong tita tungkol sa bago mong jowa. 'So, idiskribe mo nga siya sa akin, iha.' You then proceed to paint a picture with words, hopefully a good one. Ito ay ang Tagalized version ng 'describe'.
usage_notes: Isang pangkaraniwang salitang hiram na na-Filipinize. Ang pormal na katumbas nito ay 'ilarawan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **idiskribe** ang nararamdaman ko ngayon.","translation":"It's hard **to describe** what I'm feeling right now."},{"sentence":"Kaya mo bang **idiskribe** ang hitsura ng nawawalang aso?","translation":"Can you **describe** the appearance of the missing dog?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtigil sa isang kilos, gawain, o paggalaw.
original_explanation: What the jeepney driver does when you shout "Para!". What your heart does for a split second when you see your crush. What you wish your officemate would do when they start telling a boring story. It's the ultimate 'pause' button of life.
usage_notes: A very common verb for any kind of cessation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Huminto** ang sasakyan sa tapat ng pulang ilaw.","translation":"The vehicle **stopped** at the red light."},{"sentence":"Sana **huminto** na ang ulan para makauwi na tayo.","translation":"I hope the rain **stops** so we can go home."}]

translation: to be able to do; to be able to perform or execute
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang matupad, magawa, o maisakatuparan ang isang plano, utos, o gawain.
original_explanation: This is the word for turning plans into action. It’s the difference between "drawing lang" and "nangyari talaga." When your boss gives you a difficult task, the goal is to **maisagawa** it successfully. It's the verb form of "Get it done!"
usage_notes: Often used in formal or professional contexts, referring to tasks, plans, or projects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paano natin **maisagawa** ang proyektong ito kung kulang tayo sa pondo?","translation":"How can we **execute** this project if we lack funds?"},{"sentence":"Mahalaga na **maisagawa** ang operasyon sa lalong madaling panahon.","translation":"It is important **to be able to perform** the operation as soon as possible."}]

meaning_filipino: (Archaic) Isang watawat o bandila.
etymology: Uncertain, possibly from a historical Spanish term. Highly obscure.
original_explanation: Super deep cut Tagalog. This is the word for 'flag' you'd find in a dusty history book from the 1800s. If you use this today, people will just look at you funny and say, "Ano daw? You mean 'flag'?" It's the lolo of 'bandila'.
usage_notes: Extremely rare or obsolete. 'Bandila' or the English 'flag' are the standard terms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinaas ang **plag** ng rebolusyon sa Pugad Lawin.","translation":"The **flag** of the revolution was raised in Pugad Lawin."},{"sentence":"Ang disenyo ng lumang **plag** ay iba sa kasalukuyan.","translation":"The design of the old **flag** is different from the current one."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na itinuturing na walang silbi, halaga, o ambag sa lipunan; isang taong pabigat.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang "walang kuwenta" (worthless) at "tao" (person). "Kuwenta" ay hiram sa Espanyol na "cuenta" (account, count, worth).
original_explanation: This is a heavy insult. It's what you mutter under your breath about that groupmate who did absolutely nothing for the project but shows up on presentation day. Or someone who consistently brings negativity and problems without ever contributing a solution. Calling someone a **walang-kuwentang tao** is basically saying they're a human-shaped placeholder with zero value. Use with caution!
usage_notes: A very strong and offensive insult. "Walang-kuwenta" can be used alone as an adjective for things or people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong pakinggan ang sinasabi niya; isa siyang **walang-kuwentang tao**.","translation":"Don't listen to what he says; he's a **worthless person**."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay isa siyang **walang-kuwentang tao** matapos siyang tanggalin sa trabaho.","translation":"He felt like a **good-for-nothing person** after being fired from his job."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na may dalawang braso na pinagsasanib sa isang dulo, ginagamit sa paghawak, pag-ipit, o pagbuhat ng mga bagay.
etymology: From `pan-` (instrumental prefix) + `sipit` (to pinch, to hold with tongs; also means claw/pincer).
original_explanation: The ultimate "don't-touch-with-your-bare-hands" tool. Essential for flipping hotdogs and pork belly on the grill, getting ice for your drink without using your kamay, or picking up that one piece of charcoal that fell. Your kitchen's best friend during fiestas and handaans.
usage_notes: Can refer to kitchen tongs, medical forceps, or industrial pincers. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **pansipit** para baligtarin ang iniihaw na isda.","translation":"Use the **tongs** to flip the fish being grilled."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng doktor ng **pansipit** para sa operasyon.","translation":"The doctor needs **forceps** for the operation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sinaunang kagamitan sa pagbibilang na binubuo ng isang kuwadro na may mga baras kung saan nakalagay ang mga butil na maaaring galawin.
original_explanation: The original calculator. Before your phone had a calculator app, before Casio, there was this. It's that wooden toy with beads you probably played with as a kid, not knowing it was used for serious math by ancient merchants and your local 'tindera' in the 80s.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natuto siyang magbilang gamit ang **abako**.","translation":"He learned how to count using an **abacus**."}]

translation: to cause hardship; to make someone suffer
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paglalagay sa isang tao sa isang kalagayan ng paghihirap, pagdurusa, o kahirapan.
original_explanation: This is what villains in telenovelas do to the bida. It's also what your terror prof does by giving a surprise exam on a Friday. To intentionally make life difficult for someone. 'Huwag mo akong **papaghirapin** pa, please lang, pagod na ako.'
usage_notes: A strong term indicating the deliberate infliction of difficulty or suffering on someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng kontrabida ay **papaghirapin** ang buhay ng bida.","translation":"The villain's goal is to **make the protagonist's life difficult**."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo ba gustong **papaghirapin** ang buhay mo sa pagpili ng maling desisyon?","translation":"Why do you want to **make your life difficult** by making the wrong decisions?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng guhit sa ilalim ng isang salita o parirala upang bigyan-diin.
original_explanation: This is the action version of `salungguhit`. It's what your teacher tells you to do, and you grab your red ballpen. In life, to "salungguhitan" something is to make a mental note, to emphasize a lesson learned, usually the hard way. "Salungguhitan mo: 'wag na 'ko mag-reply sa ex ko at 3 AM."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Salungguhitan** mo ang lahat ng pandiwa sa talata.","translation":"**Underline** all the verbs in the paragraph."},{"sentence":"Paulit-ulit niyang sinabi iyon, na para bang gusto niyang **salungguhitan** ang bawat salita.","translation":"He repeated it, as if he wanted **to underscore** every word."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook o kainan kung saan nagbebenta at naghahain ng mga lutong may kari (curry).
etymology: Mula sa "kari" (curry) + hulaping "-han" (lugar). Ang "kari" ay mula sa Tamil na "kaṟi".
original_explanation: Ito yung OG na karinderya na specialista sa curry. Bago pa nag-boom ang mga Japanese curry house, mayroon nang karihan sa kanto na nagbebenta ng manok na may sabaw na dilaw. Think of it as the ancestor of your favorite curry spot.
usage_notes: This term is less common now, often replaced by the more general "karinderya" or "kainan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan kami sa **karihan** sa may palengke para bumili ng ulam.","translation":"We passed by the **curry eatery** near the market to buy a dish."},{"sentence":"Sikat ang **karihan** ni Aling Nena dahil sa masarap niyang luto.","translation":"Aling Nena's **curry place** is famous because of her delicious cooking."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na patungan o sapin na inilalagay sa ilalim ng baso o tasa upang protektahan ang ibabaw ng mesa mula sa halumigmig o init.
original_explanation: Yung bagay na laging sinasabi ng nanay mo na gamitin mo para hindi magasgasan 'yung bagong-biling lamesa. It's the adult version of a placemat, but just for your drink. The unsung hero that prevents water rings and family arguments.
usage_notes: A common household term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo itong **coaster** para sa malamig mong baso.","translation":"Use this **coaster** for your cold glass."}]

translation: to womanize; to take as a mistress
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikipag-ugnayan sa isang babae bilang isang kalaguyo o kerida; ang pagkuha sa isang babae upang maging kabit.
original_explanation: The verb form of having a side-chick or being a serial womanizer. It's the action that leads to dramatic teleserye confrontations. 'Huwag mong babaihin ang anak ko!' is the classic line from a protective parent to a potential heartbreaker.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative and serious connotation related to infidelity. The more common term for the general act is 'mambabae'. 'Babaihin' is object-focused, on the woman being pursued.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan ng ama ang manliligaw na huwag **babaihin** ang kanyang anak.","translation":"The father warned the suitor not to **make a mistress out of** his daughter."}]

meaning_filipino: Tanyag, sikat, o lubos na kinagigiliwan ng marami sa isang partikular na panahon.
etymology: Possibly from the sound of something hitting its mark.
original_explanation: That feeling when your TikTok video goes viral overnight. If something is patok, it's the 'in' thing, the talk of the town. It's the song you hear in every jeepney, the milk tea flavor everyone is lining up for, the 'budol' item that's always sold out. It's a certified banger.
usage_notes: Often used in media and marketing to describe trends.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patok** ngayon sa mga kabataan ang mga Korean drama.","translation":"Korean dramas are a **hit** with the youth nowadays."},{"sentence":"Naging **patok** sa takilya ang pelikula niya.","translation":"Her movie became a box-office **hit**."}]

translation: shaking from crying, convulsing with sobs
meaning_filipino: Isang matalinghagang paglalarawan sa isang tao na ang katawan ay nanginginig o yumayanig nang husto dahil sa matinding pag-iyak.
original_explanation: This isn't just simple crying. This is the ugly cry. 'Yung tipong nanood ka ng "Hachiko" or "Miracle in Cell No. 7" at hindi mo na mapigilan. Your whole body is shaking, you can't breathe, and you're making weird noises. It's that post-breakup, bagsak-sa-exam, or saw-a-heartbreaking-GMA-documentary kind of cry.
usage_notes: A very literary and dramatic phrase. 'Humindik' means to shake or tremble, often from fear or strong emotion. 'Pananangis' is a deep form of weeping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan siyang **naghuhumindik sa pananangis** sa isang sulok ng silid.","translation":"She was found **convulsing with sobs** in a corner of the room."},{"sentence":"Matapos malaman ang masamang balita, napaupo na lang siya at **naghuhumindik sa pananangis**.","translation":"After learning the bad news, she just collapsed into a seat and was **shaking from crying**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos, gawa, o pahayag na hindi maaaring ipagtanggol o bigyan ng katwiran dahil ito ay malinaw na mali, labag sa moralidad, o walang basehan.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (not), "maipagsang-" (prefix for being able to defend something), at "sanggalang" (shield/protection).
original_explanation: 'Yung friend mong nangopya sa exam, nahuli, tapos nagalit pa sa prof. 'Yung ginawa niya? Di-maipagsasanggalang. Walang excuse, walang palusot. It's just plain wrong and you can't even try to defend it.
usage_notes: A formal and strong word used in contexts of justice, morality, and argumentation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga ginawang krimen ay **di-maipagsasanggalang** sa anumang korte.","translation":"The crimes he committed are **indefensible** in any court."},{"sentence":"Ang ginawa niyang panloloko sa kanyang mga kaibigan ay isang bagay na **di-maipagsasanggalang**.","translation":"His act of cheating his friends is something **unjustifiable**."}]

meaning_filipino: May malaking distansya mula sa ibabaw hanggang sa ilalim; hindi mababaw. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang bagay na mahirap unawain o masidhi.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling mo para sa ex mo na hindi mo ma-move on-an. Or 'yung usapan niyo ng tropa mo at 3 AM about the universe. Pwede ring literal, like 'yung part ng swimming pool na bawal sa 'di marunong lumangoy. 'Ang lalim!'
usage_notes: Can refer to physical depth, emotional intensity, or intellectual complexity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong **malalim** ang ilog kaya't delikado itong tawirin.","translation":"The river is too **deep**, so it's dangerous to cross."},{"sentence":"**Malalim** ang iniisip niya kaya hindi niya kami napansin.","translation":"He was in **deep** thought, so he didn't notice us."}]

translation: Sore loser; touchy; easily angered by teasing
meaning_filipino: Isang taong madaling magalit o mainis kapag tinutukso o natatalo sa laro.
original_explanation: That friend who flips the Monopoly board when they start losing. The officemate who gives you the silent treatment after a friendly joke. In the world of online gaming, sila 'yung nag-ra-rage quit. Being 'pikon' is the fastest way to kill the vibe. 'Huwag kang pikon, laro lang 'to!'
usage_notes: A very common personality descriptor. The state of being 'pikon' is 'pagkapikon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo na siyang asarin, **pikon** 'yan.","translation":"Don't tease him anymore, he's a **sore loser**."},{"sentence":"Natatawa na lang ako kapag tinatawag akong **pikon**.","translation":"I just laugh whenever they call me **touchy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng kawalan ng interes, malasakit, o emosyon sa mga bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
etymology: Mula sa `pagka-` (estado ng pagiging) + `walang bahala` (walang pakialam). Isang tambalang pangngalan.
original_explanation: The official feeling of "K." or "Bahala ka sa buhay mo." It's when you see your ex with someone new and you feel... absolutely nothing. It's scrolling past bad news because you're already numb. It's the ultimate 'deadma' mode. The opposite of 'pakealamero'.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang estado ng emosyonal na paglayo o kawalan ng pag-aalala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkawalang-bahala** sa pag-aaral ay nag-aalala sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"His **indifference** towards his studies worries his parents."},{"sentence":"Ikinasama ng loob niya ang **pagkawalang-bahala** ng kaibigan sa kanyang mga problema.","translation":"She was hurt by her friend's **apathy** towards her problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang istilo o kalakaran sa pananamit, palamuti, o pag-uugali na popular sa isang partikular na panahon.
original_explanation: Kung ano ang uso. 'Yung mga damit na nakikita mo sa TikTok na pag sinuot mo, feeling mo part ka ng "it" crowd. Minsan, 'yung mga pantalon na butas-butas; minsan, 'yung mga damit na parang galing sa ukay-ukay ng lola mo. Ang moda ay pabago-bago, parang feelings niya para sa'yo.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to clothing fashion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging sunod sa **moda** ang pananamit ni Anna.","translation":"Anna's clothing is always in **fashion**."},{"sentence":"Ano ba ang **moda** ngayon sa mga kabataan?","translation":"What is the **trend** among the youth today?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng pagluha o pag-iyak ng isang tao, sinasadya man o hindi sinasadya.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mag-` (gumanap ng kilos), `pa-` (sanhi), at salitang-ugat na `iyak` (cry).
original_explanation: The specialty of K-dramas, sad movie endings, and sometimes, your toxic ex. Anything that can successfully make the waterworks happen can `magpaiyak`. It could be a touching story, a painful breakup message, or even just chopping a lot of onions for your sinigang. 'Grabe, ang galing **magpaiyak** ng pelikulang 'yon!'
usage_notes: Maaaring intensyonal (tulad ng panunukso) o hindi intensyonal (tulad ng paghahatid ng masamang balita).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo na akong **paiyakin**, please.","translation":"Don't **make me cry** anymore, please."},{"sentence":"Ang mga sibuyas ay may kakayahang **magpaiyak** ng tao.","translation":"Onions have the ability to **make people cry**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauugnay sa pandinig o sa kakayahang makarinig.
original_explanation: This is a very academic-sounding word. You'd probably hear this in a psychology class or a doctor's office, not in the palengke. "My learning style is more **awditibo**," is something a college student might say. For everyone else, it's just "mas natututo ako 'pag nakikinig."
usage_notes: A formal, technical term. Less common in everyday conversation. The more common Filipino concept is simply 'pandinig' (hearing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga taong may memoryang **awditibo** ay madaling makatanda ng mga narinig na impormasyon.","translation":"People with **auditory** memory can easily remember information they've heard."},{"sentence":"Ang mga balyena ay gumagamit ng mga senyas na **awditibo** upang makipag-usap sa isa't isa.","translation":"Whales use **auditory** signals to communicate with each other."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahinang tunog o ugong, karaniwang mula sa ibon, insekto, o makina.
original_explanation: That quiet buzz your ref makes at 3 AM. Or the sound a bird makes when it's not fully committed to singing. It's a sound so faint, you're not sure if you heard it or if it was just your tinnitus acting up.
usage_notes: 'Bahagya' means slight or faint, and 'huni' is a chirp, hum, or song (usually of a bird or insect).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **bahagyang huni** lang ng ibon ang maririnig sa katahimikan ng umaga.","translation":"Only a **faint chirp** of a bird could be heard in the morning silence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-umbok at pagiging malaki at malakas, tulad ng alon o usok na papalaki. Karaniwang ginagamit bilang isang pang-uring pampanitikan.
etymology: From 'bulang' (foam, froth), with reduplication of the first syllable 'bu' and infix '-um-'. The root might be related to Malay 'gelembung' (bubble).
original_explanation: Think of the waves in Siargao that look both majestic and terrifying. Or the thick smoke from a really good inihaw station at the palengke. It’s a very dramatic, almost poetic word for something swelling up with force.
usage_notes: This is a very descriptive, literary word. Often seen in the phrase 'gumugubulang na alon' (surging waves), where it functions as an adjective. 'Gumubulang' is the past/completed form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinalubong ng mga mangingisda ang **gumugubulang** na alon sa laot.","translation":"The fishermen faced the **surging** waves in the open sea."},{"sentence":"Nakita nila ang **gumugubulang** na usok mula sa nasusunog na gusali.","translation":"They saw the **billowing** smoke from the burning building."}]

translation: to have a grating or jarring sound
meaning_filipino: Paglikha ng isang matinis, hindi kaaya-aya, at nakakairitang tunog, karaniwan mula sa pagkiskis ng dalawang bagay o sa isang boses.
original_explanation: Eto yung tunog ng kuko sa blackboard, o yung boses ng officemate mong nagrereklamo nang walang tigil. Parang tunog ng sirang speaker na pilit pa ring ginagamit. Nakakakilabot at nakakabingi sa inis.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang boses o tunog na nakakairita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nangangalirang** sa pandinig ang kanyang pagtili.","translation":"Her scream was **grating** to the ears."},{"sentence":"Ayaw kong pakinggan ang boses niya dahil **nangangalirang**.","translation":"I don't want to listen to his voice because it's **shrill**."}]

translation: to put on a cover/lid; to cover
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng takip o pansara sa isang bagay, o ang pagsuot ng anuman sa ulo na nagsisilbing panakip.
original_explanation: What you do to the pot of adobo to keep the flavor from escaping. Also, what you do with a huge hat or helmet to cover your head, whether to avoid the sun, for safety, or to hide from someone you owe money to.
usage_notes: Can refer to covering a container with a lid or covering one's own head.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **magsaklob** ng kaldero para mas mabilis kumulo ang tubig.","translation":"Don't forget to **put a lid on** the pot so the water will boil faster."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag, opinyon, o reaksyon na isinulat o sinabi bilang tugon sa isang bagay, lalo na sa social media.
original_explanation: Dati, 'komento' lang. Ngayon, it's the thing you type on Facebook, TikTok, or Instagram. Pwedeng 'pa-shoutout po!', 'Sana all!', o isang buong essay na nagdedebate sa isang issue. Puwede ring pandiwa: 'Nag-comment ako sa post mo.'
usage_notes: Mas karaniwan na ngayon kaysa sa katumbas nitong 'komento,' lalo na sa konteksto ng internet. Maaari ding gamitin bilang pandiwa (to comment / mag-comment).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Basahin mo 'yung mga **comment** sa post, nakakatawa.","translation":"Read the **comments** on the post, they're funny."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang mag-**comment** kung wala kang magandang sasabihin.","translation":"Don't **comment** if you have nothing nice to say."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho o hilig ay mangolekta o maningil ng mga bagay, tulad ng bayad, buwis, o mga kagamitan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung kinatatakutan mo 'pag 'di ka pa bayad sa credit card o sa 5-6. Sila 'yung kakatok sa pinto niyo. Pwede ring 'yung friend mong nag-iipon ng Funko Pops or K-Pop photocards—kolektor din 'yun!
usage_notes: Often refers to a debt collector, but can also mean a hobbyist collector.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating na ang **kolektor** ng kuryente.","translation":"The electricity bill **collector** has arrived."},{"sentence":"Isang masugid na **kolektor** ng mga selyo ang aking lolo.","translation":"My grandfather is an avid stamp **collector**."}]

translation: to whistle at each other; to exchange whistles
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng sipol o pag-iingay gamit ang bibig upang tawagin ang pansin ng isa't isa, o bilang hudyat.
etymology: From `pa-` + `suwit` (whistle) + `-an` (referential suffix), implying an interaction between two or more parties.
original_explanation: This is the old-school way of calling your friend from across the street before everyone had cellphones. "Hoy! *Pasuwitan* mo nga si Mark para lumingon!" It can also be the sketchy catcall someone does on the street, which is definitely NOT cool. Or, it could be a secret signal between two people, like in a spy movie set in Quiapo.
usage_notes: Can be neutral (calling attention), negative (catcalling), or secretive (signal). The `pa-` prefix with the `-an` suffix suggests a reciprocal or interactive action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-usap ang magkaibigan na mag-**pasuwitan** na lang sila bilang hudyat.","translation":"The friends agreed to just **whistle at each other** as a signal."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **pasuwitan** mo lang ako kapag kailangan mo ng tulong.","translation":"Don't worry, just **whistle at me** if you need help."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng matulis o matalim na dulo.
original_explanation: Think of the perfect kilay on fleek, that sharp, defined point at the end? That's 'tilos'. Or the tip of a barbecue stick you're trying not to poke your eye with. It's all about that pointy end.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the shape of an object's tip, like a pencil, a knife, or a mountain peak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magingat ka sa **tilos** ng lapis, baka matusok ka.","translation":"Be careful with the **pointed** tip of the pencil, you might get pricked."},{"sentence":"Ang bubong ng kanilang bahay ay **tilos** ang disenyo.","translation":"The roof of their house has a **pointed** design."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng madahong gulay na may mapuputing tangkay at luntiang dahon, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga lutuing Filipino.
etymology: From Hokkien Chinese 白菜 (pe̍h-chhài), meaning 'white cabbage'.
original_explanation: The default leafy green in many Filipino dishes like nilaga and bulalo. It's affordable, readily available in any palengke, and absorbs the soup's flavor really well. If your life feels bland, maybe you just need some pechay... in a super savory broth. It's the wingman of vegetables.
usage_notes: A staple vegetable in Filipino cuisine. 'Pechay Baguio' refers to Napa cabbage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong lutuin ang **pechay** para malutong pa rin.","translation":"Don't overcook the **bok choy** so it's still crunchy."},{"sentence":"Maglalagay ako ng maraming **pechay** sa nilaga.","translation":"I will put a lot of **bok choy** in the stew."}]

translation: to join a group; to become a member of
meaning_filipino: Sumali o maging kasapi sa isang samahan, organisasyon, o pangkat.
original_explanation: The act of clicking 'Join Group' on Facebook, but in real life. It's when you decide to become part of a barkada, a school org, a BPO team, or even a cult (let's hope not). It's the step you take from being an outsider to an insider. "Aniban mo na kasi kami sa DOTA team!"
usage_notes: 'Aniban' is the verb form meaning 'to join'. The noun for the group itself is 'samahan' or 'organisasyon'. 'Kaanib' is the member.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **aniban** ang pinakasikat na club sa paaralan.","translation":"She wants **to join** the most popular club in school."},{"sentence":"Pinag-iisipan kong **aniban** ang kooperatiba sa aming barangay.","translation":"I'm thinking of **becoming a member of** the cooperative in our barangay."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakabuklod o pagiging isa; pagkakaisa.
original_explanation: This is the noun form of being united. It's the goal of every group project, family reunion, and national campaign. `Kaisahan` is that beautiful, often elusive, state where everyone is on the same page. It's the "Teamwork makes the dream work" vibe, but in a more profound, formal sense. It's what politicians promise during elections and what basketball coaches preach in the dugout.
usage_notes: More formal than 'pagkakaisa', but they are largely synonymous.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kaisahan** ng bansa ay mahalaga para sa pag-unlad.","translation":"The **unity** of the country is important for progress."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita nila ang **kaisahan** sa pamamagitan ng pagtutulungan sa panahon ng krisis.","translation":"They showed **oneness** by helping each other during the crisis."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang hayagan, lantaran, o matindi ang isang damdamin, opinyon, o kilos, kabaligtaran ng "lowkey".
etymology: English slang, from "high-key" lighting in photography, which reduces contrast. The slang meaning is an ironic reversal.
original_explanation: The opposite of your "lowkey" feelings. This is when you're not hiding it anymore. "Highkey want to resign na." "Highkey crushing on that barista." It's stating your truth, your feelings, your desires out loud, for the whole Marites network to hear. It's being proud and loud about it, no more secrets.
usage_notes: A recent English slang import popular among Filipino millennials and Gen Z. Used in Taglish sentences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Highkey** naiinis na ako sa bagal ng internet.","translation":"I'm **obviously** getting annoyed with the slow internet."},{"sentence":"**Highkey** akong umaasa na may 13th month pay sa June.","translation":"I'm **intensely** hoping for a 13th-month pay in June."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinuno o tagapamahala ng isang unibersidad, kolehiyo, simbahan, o seminaryo.
original_explanation: The 'big boss' of a university, especially a Catholic one like UST. They're like the school's CEO or president. If the dean is the department head, the rektor is the one who sits in the biggest, most air-conditioned office on campus.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga institusyong akademiko at relihiyoso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong **rektor** ng unibersidad ay pormal na iniluklok sa pwesto.","translation":"The new **rector** of the university was formally installed in office."},{"sentence":"Isang paring Dominikano ang kasalukuyang **rektor** ng Pontifical and Royal University of Santo Tomas.","translation":"A Dominican priest is the current **rector** of the Pontifical and Royal University of Santo Tomas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na madaling umiyak o may tendensiyang umiyak kahit sa maliliit na bagay.
original_explanation: The official title of that one friend in the barkada who cries during commercials, proposals, and even when a cute puppy is shown on screen. A term of endearment for the 'soft-hearted' or a light insult for someone who's 'mababaw ang luha' (whose tears are shallow).
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective ('Siya ay iyakin') or a noun ('Ang iyakin ng grupo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula pagkabata, talagang **iyakin** na ang kapatid ko.","translation":"Ever since childhood, my sibling has really been a **crybaby**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **iyakin**, harapin mo ang problema nang matatag.","translation":"Don't be **prone to crying**, face the problem with fortitude."}]

meaning_filipino: Salitang nagpapahayag ng kawalan ng kaalaman o kasiguraduhan tungkol sa isang bagay. Katumbas ng "hindi ko alam".
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino conversation ender. It can mean 'I don't know,' 'I don't care,' 'Whatever,' 'Leave me alone,' or 'Let's talk about something else.' The tone is everything. A quick 'ewan' is dismissive. A long, drawn-out 'Ewaaaan...' with a shrug is pure, unadulterated cluelessness. It's the verbal equivalent of the 🤷 emoji.
usage_notes: Extremely common. Often paired with 'ko' ('ewan ko') to mean 'I don't know'. Can be used alone to express frustration or indifference.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ewan** kung saan siya nagpunta.","translation":"**I don't know** where he/she went."},{"sentence":"Tinanong ko siya pero ang sagot lang niya ay '**ewan**'.","translation":"I asked him/her but his/her only answer was '**I don't know**'."}]

meaning_filipino: Iparehistro ang isang imbensyon o likha sa isang tanggapan ng gobyerno upang magkaroon ng eksklusibong karapatan dito.
original_explanation: This is what you tell your friend when they come up with a brilliant, world-changing idea like "adobo-flavored ice cream" or a "traffic-proof flying jeepney." You gotta protect your intellectual property, bes! "Huy, ang galing niyan! **Ipapatente** mo na 'yan bago maunahan ka!"
usage_notes: Used in the context of inventions, business ideas, and protecting intellectual property.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano ng imbentor na **ipapatente** ang kanyang bagong makina.","translation":"The inventor plans **to have** his new machine **patented**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng labis na pagkagiliw o pagpapacute sa isang tao sa paraang mapaglaro o hindi seryoso.
original_explanation: When you start acting extra cute and charming because your crush is nearby. It's the art of the 'pabebe' wave, the subtle hair flip, or laughing a little too loudly at their not-so-funny jokes. The OG 'landî'.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a playful, sometimes coy or coquettish, way of flirting. Can have a slightly negative or judgmental connotation depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **umalembong** diyan at baka makita ka ng nobyo mo.","translation":"Don't **flirt** there, your boyfriend might see you."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **umalembong** sa mga bagong empleyado sa opisina.","translation":"She likes to **flirt** with the new employees at the office."}]

translation: to droop, to sag, to wilt
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaba o pagbagsak ng isang bagay dahil sa pagod, kabigatan, o kawalan ng lakas at suporta.
original_explanation: Your shoulders after a 12-hour shift. The leaves of your houseplant when you forget to water it. 'Yung energy level mo pag 3 PM na at wala pang kape. That's lumaylay. It's the physical manifestation of "I give up."
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects (branches, clothes on a line) and also for abstract things like spirit or enthusiasm ('nanghina ang loob').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumaylay** ang mga dahon ng halaman dahil sa tindi ng sikat ng araw.","translation":"The plant's leaves **wilted** because of the intense heat of the sun."},{"sentence":"Nang marinig niya ang masamang balita, tila **lumaylay** ang kanyang mga balikat.","translation":"When he heard the bad news, his shoulders seemed to **droop**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng pag-aalis ng lupa o iba pang materyales upang makabuo ng butas, kanal, o pundasyon, na kadalasang tumutukoy sa isang patuloy o masusing gawain.
