original_explanation: This is what happens when your dog tries to bury its bone in your prized garden. It's also what treasure hunters do in movies, or what construction workers do before building your future BGC condo. 'Paghuhukay' implies the *ongoing process* of digging, like you're really in the middle of it, versus just the single act.
usage_notes: The 'pag-' prefix and the duplication of the first syllable of the root ('hu') indicate a continuous, repeated, or more intense action of digging. It's the progressive gerund form. 'Paghukay' is the infinitive/base gerund, while 'paghuhukay' emphasizes the ongoing nature of the work.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghuhukay** para sa bagong MRT line ay nagdulot ng matinding trapiko.","translation":"The **excavation** for the new MRT line caused heavy traffic."},{"sentence":"Ipinagpatuloy nila ang **paghuhukay** sa pag-asang makahanap ng ginto.","translation":"They continued their **digging** in the hope of finding gold."}]

translation: Sulking (with an expectation of being coaxed)
meaning_filipino: Isang banayad na pagdaramdam o paghinanakit sa isang malapit na tao, na ipinapahiwatig sa pamamagitan ng pananahimik o paglayo, at naghihintay ng suyò o pag-amo.
original_explanation: This is the Filipino love language of silent treatment. It's not full-blown anger; it's a cold shoulder with a hidden 'Please notice me and say sorry' sign. It's when your partner gives you one-word answers because you forgot your monthsary. The only cure is 'suyo' (sweet coaxing), usually involving food. It's a non-confrontational way of saying "I'm hurt, and you better fix it."
usage_notes: A culturally specific term that doesn't have a perfect English equivalent. It's a mix of being hurt, sulking, and expecting reconciliation. It's almost exclusively used for people you have a close relationship with.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtatampo** niya ay tumagal ng isang linggo.","translation":"Her **sulking** lasted for a week."},{"sentence":"Daanin mo na lang sa lambing ang **pagtatampo** ng iyong kasintahan.","translation":"Just use affection to deal with your girlfriend's **sulking**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging hindi nagkakamali o kawalan ng kakayahang magkamali.
original_explanation: This is a very deep, high-level word. It's the quality your mom thinks she has when she gives you life advice ('mother knows best'). In a more serious context, it's a concept in theology, like the 'papal infallibility' of the Pope. For the rest of us mortals, this is a non-existent trait.
usage_notes: A very formal and rare word, primarily used in theological, philosophical, or academic discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang doktrina ng **impalibilidad** ng Papa ay isang mahalagang turo sa Simbahang Katoliko.","translation":"The doctrine of papal **infallibility** is an important teaching in the Catholic Church."},{"sentence":"Walang sinumang tao ang may angking **impalibilidad**; lahat ay maaaring magkamali.","translation":"No human being possesses **infallibility**; everyone can make mistakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na lumilikha at nag-a-upload ng mga video sa platapormang Youtube, kadalasan bilang isang propesyon o libangan.
original_explanation: The modern-day celebrity. Someone who films their life, their travels, their "mukbang" sessions, or their "unboxings" for likes, shares, and subscribers. The dream job of many Gen Z Pinoys, right next to being a TikToker or a K-Pop star.
usage_notes: Hiram na salita. Ang katumbas sa Filipino ay maaaring 'vlogger' o 'tagalikha ng nilalaman'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **Youtuber** balang araw.","translation":"She dreams of becoming a famous **Youtuber** someday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapad at pangunahing daanan na idinisenyo para sa mabilis na paglalakbay ng mga sasakyan, karaniwang may mga toll at limitadong pasukan at labasan.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na 'expressway'.
original_explanation: Ang NLEX, SLEX, at Skyway. Dito mo mararamdaman ang tunay na bilis... maliban kung rush hour, kung saan nagiging a very expensive parking lot. Ito rin ang setting ng maraming Pinoy road trip movie montages.
usage_notes: Karaniwang binabaybay at binibigkas sa paraang Ingles. Ang mas pormal na katumbas ay 'mabilisang daanan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mabilis ang biyahe kung dadaan ka sa **expressway**.","translation":"The trip is faster if you take the **expressway**."},{"sentence":"Magkano na ngayon ang toll sa **expressway** papuntang Baguio?","translation":"How much is the toll on the **expressway** to Baguio now?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbuo at paglabas ng bunga sa isang halaman. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ito ay ang pagkakaroon ng magandang resulta mula sa isang pagsisikap.
original_explanation: This is the ROI (Return on Investment) of the plant world. After all the watering and care, the mango tree is finally 'namumunga'. Metaphorically, it's the result of all your hard work. That project you spent sleepless nights on? When it finally succeeds, 'namumunga na ang pagod mo.' It's the tangible proof that your efforts weren't 'drawing lang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang puno ng mangga sa aming bakuran ay **namumunga** na.","translation":"The mango tree in our yard is now **bearing fruit**."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **namumunga** na ang lahat ng kanyang pagsisikap sa negosyo.","translation":"Finally, all his efforts in the business are **bearing fruit**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang serye ng pananalangin, serbisyo sa simbahan, o debosyon na tumatagal ng tatlong magkakasunod na araw, karaniwan bilang paghahanda para sa isang kapistahan o para sa isang natatanging layunin.
etymology: Mula sa wikang Espanyol na "triduo", mula sa Latin na "triduum".
original_explanation: This is the Catholic version of a 3-day sale or a 3-day concert festival, but for your soul. Imbes na new phone or merch ang habol mo, grasya at milagro ang target. It’s a spiritual marathon, not a sprint. Usually happens before a big fiesta, proving that Filipinos love a good countdown, whether it's for a saint's day or a new iPhone release.
usage_notes: Halos kapareho ng "triduum", ngunit mas karaniwan ang "triduo" sa mga lokal na parokya at sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magsisimula na bukas ang **triduo** para sa pista ng aming patron.","translation":"The **triduum** for the feast of our patron saint will begin tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Dumalo ang maraming deboto sa tatlong araw na **triduo**.","translation":"Many devotees attended the three-day **triduum**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang bagay na katulad o kapareho ng sa iba; pagtulad sa kilos, anyo, o gawa ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: When you see your seatmate's 'aesthetic' notes and suddenly your notebook looks exactly the same. It's also what happens when you copy your idol's OOTD, from head to toe. "Copy-paste lang ang peg."
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense) of the verb. The infinitive is 'gumaya', present is 'gumagaya', and future is 'gagaya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gumaya** siya sa istilo ng pananamit ng kanyang paboritong artista.","translation":"She **copied** the fashion style of her favorite celebrity."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka ba **gumaya** sa sagot ko? Ayan, pareho tayong bagsak.","translation":"Why did you **copy** my answer? See, now we both failed."}]

translation: to give as advice; to advise
meaning_filipino: Ibigay bilang isang mungkahi o gabay na dapat sundin; magbigay ng payo.
original_explanation: What your best friend does when you have a love life crisis. "Ano ba ang dapat kong gawin?" and they'll tell you what they would 'ipayo'. It's the verb form of giving that unsolicited (but often needed) advice.
usage_notes: This verb focuses on the advice itself being given. The verb 'payuhan' focuses on the person receiving the advice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tanging **maipapayo** ko sa iyo ay maging matatag ka.","translation":"The only thing I can **advise** you is to be strong."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **ipapayo** mo sa isang taong nalilito?","translation":"What would you **give as advice** to someone who is confused?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng matinding damdamin ng paghanga, pag-ibig, o awa na parang nilulusaw ang puso.
original_explanation: 'Yung titig ni crush na para kang ice cream sa ilalim ng araw. 'Yung "I love you" ng isang bata. 'Yung tingin ng aso mo 'pag aalis ka ng bahay. Nakatutunaw ng puso. It's that feeling that makes your insides go all soft and gooey.
usage_notes: Almost always used figuratively to mean 'heart-melting'. The literal meaning 'able to cause melting' (e.g., nakatutunaw na init) is less common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga ngiti ay **nakatutunaw** ng puso.","translation":"Her smiles are **heart-melting**."},{"sentence":"May **nakatutunaw** na tingin ang pusa habang humihingi ng pagkain.","translation":"The cat has a **heart-melting** look while asking for food."}]

meaning_filipino: Madaling magbago ng isip, desisyon, o damdamin; hindi permanente o matatag.
original_explanation: Yung kaibigan mong sabi mag-a-outing kayo, tapos biglang ayaw na. O 'yung ex mong 'I love you' ngayon, 'It's complicated' bukas. Parang weather forecast sa Pilipinas, hindi mo masabi. This is the ultimate 'palit-isip' mode.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person's mood or decisions, or even the weather.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pabagu-bago** ang isip niya kung saan kami kakain.","translation":"His/Her mind is **fickle** about where we should eat."},{"sentence":"Mahirap asahan ang mga pangako niya dahil **pabagu-bago** siya ng desisyon.","translation":"It's hard to rely on his/her promises because he/she is **erratic** with decisions."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang ibabaw, lalo na ang daan, na may maraming hukay o hindi pantay.
original_explanation: This is the final boss version of 'labak'. Eto yung kalsada sa probinsya na parang dinaanan ng herd of angry carabaos. Yung tipong kailangan mo ng sports bra at kidney belt para lang makarating sa destinasyon mo. Perfect description for your emotional state after a rough week.
usage_notes: Ang pag-uulit ay nagbibigay-diin sa dami o kalubhaan, na nangangahulugang napakaraming hukay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Labak-labak** ang daan papunta sa bukid kaya't mabagal ang aming biyahe.","translation":"The road to the farm was **full of potholes** so our trip was slow."}]

translation: house clothes; casual wear for home
meaning_filipino: Damit o kasuotan na para lamang gamitin sa loob ng bahay; karaniwang simple, maluwag, at komportable.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pan-" at salitang ugat na "bahay". Ang /n/ sa "pan-" ay nagiging /m/ dahil sa kasunod na tunog na /b/.
original_explanation: Your official WFH uniform. The faded daster, the PE shorts from high school, the free t-shirt from a fun run 10 years ago. These are your 'pambahay'. Clothes you would never be caught dead wearing outside, unless it's a quick run to the sari-sari store. Comfort over style, always.
usage_notes: Bagaman pangngalan, madalas itong gumagana bilang pang-uri (e.g. "damit na pambahay").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magbihis ka muna ng **pambahay** pagdating mo galing sa eskwela.","translation":"Change into your **house clothes** first when you get home from school."},{"sentence":"Ang mga shorts na ito ang paborito kong **pambahay**.","translation":"These shorts are my favorite **casual wear for home**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paggamit nang higit sa kinakailangan o nararapat; pang-aabuso sa kapangyarihan o pribilehiyo.
etymology: From pag- + the first syllable of mag- (ma-) + mag- + labis (excess).
original_explanation: Think of a corrupt politician using public funds for their personal vacation. That's pagmamalabis. Or when your team lead takes all the credit for your hard work. It's the act of going way over the line, usually for personal gain, and often at someone else's expense. The noun form of being 'extra' in the worst possible way.
usage_notes: The noun form of 'magmalabis'. Refers to the act of abuse or excessiveness, often in the context of power, authority, or resources.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagmamalabis** sa kapangyarihan ay isang uri ng katiwalian.","translation":"The **abuse** of power is a form of corruption."},{"sentence":"Itinigil niya ang kanyang **pagmamalabis** sa pagkain ng matatamis.","translation":"He stopped his **overindulgence** in eating sweets."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panginginig ng katawan dahil sa ginaw, takot, o matinding damdamin.
original_explanation: That sudden, uncontrollable body shake you do when it's freezing cold in the BPO office, or when someone tells a ghost story that's a little too real. It's your body's built-in vibrator mode for when it's cold, scared, or sometimes, even 'kinikilig'.
usage_notes: Often used as a root word for the verb 'kaligkigin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kaligkig** ang gumapang sa kanyang likod nang marinig niya ang halinghing.","translation":"A **shudder** ran down his back when he heard the whimper."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **kaligkig** dahil sa malamig na hangin.","translation":"I felt a **chill** because of the cold wind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagpili o hatol na ginawa matapos ang masusing pag-iisip o pagsasaalang-alang.
original_explanation: Ito yung moment na nag-iisip ka kung mag-o-order ka ba sa FoodPanda o magtitipid na lang. O kung magre-resign ka na ba o titiisin mo pa yung boss mo. Basically, 'pasya' in its more formal, corporate-sounding form. 'Ano na ang final **disisyon** mo?'
usage_notes: Ito ay isang karaniwang varyant ng pagbaybay para sa 'desisyon'. Parehong anyo ay tinatanggap at nauunawaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap gumawa ng **disisyon** kapag pagod ka.","translation":"It's hard to make a **decision** when you're tired."},{"sentence":"Ang pinal na **disisyon** ay nasa kamay ng manager.","translation":"The final **decision** is in the hands of the manager."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natural na proseso ng pagpapalit ng balat o panlabas na anyo ng mga hayop tulad ng ahas at insekto. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay tumutukoy sa pagbabago ng pagkatao o anyo.
original_explanation: This is a snake's version of a 'glow up'. It sheds its old, tired skin to reveal a fresh new one. Metaphorically, it's what you do when you leave your toxic past behind and start a new chapter. New year, new me? That's a form of paghuhunos.
usage_notes: Primarily a biological term, but frequently used metaphorically for personal transformation and significant change.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinanood ng mga bata ang **paghuhunos** ng isang ahas sa terrarium.","translation":"The children watched the **molting** of a snake in the terrarium."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pag-alis sa probinsya ay simula ng kanyang **paghuhunos** tungo sa pagiging isang matagumpay na negosyante.","translation":"Her leaving the province was the start of her **transformation** into a successful entrepreneur."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging nakabitin o nakalawlaw nang maluwag at walang suporta mula sa ibaba.
original_explanation: That feeling when your phone charger is hanging precariously from the socket, or when you're on a crowded MRT and you can't get a good grip, just dangling there. It describes something hanging loosely, swaying with gravity. 'Nakabayubay' is the state of being. Example: 'Yung sapatos na isinabit sa poste, nakabayubay.'
usage_notes: Often used in its verb form 'nakabayubay' (is dangling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bayubay** ang mga binti ng bata habang nakaupo siya sa mataas na silya.","translation":"The child's legs were **dangling** as he sat on the high chair."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang isang ahas na nakabayubay mula sa sanga ng puno.","translation":"I saw a snake **hanging loosely** from a tree branch."}]

translation: to treat each other as siblings
meaning_filipino: Ang pagturing sa isa't isa na parang tunay na magkapatid sa dugo, kahit na hindi magkaano-ano.
etymology: From `mag-` (reciprocal verb prefix) + a complex infix/prefix related to `kina` + `kapatid` (sibling).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'sana all' of friendships. It's when you're so close to your bestie that you're practically family, minus the squabbles over the remote control (well, maybe). You've got each other's backs, you can borrow clothes without asking, and your parents have basically adopted them. #FriendshipGoals
usage_notes: This verb implies a deep, mutual, and chosen familial bond between people who are not related by blood. It describes the relationship itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit hindi sila magkadugo, **magkinakapatid** ang turingan nina Ana at Liza.","translation":"Even though they are not related by blood, Ana and Liza **treat each other as siblings**."},{"sentence":"Sa aming barkada, lahat kami ay **magkinakapatid**.","translation":"In our group of friends, all of us **have a sibling-like relationship**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marubdob na pagnanais o interes sa paggawa ng isang bagay; ang katangian ng pagiging masipag at masigla.
etymology: From ka- + sigasig + -an, forming an abstract noun referring to the peak or state of being zealous.
original_explanation: This is your energy level during the first week of a new job or the first month of your gym membership. It's that 'all-out' feeling before the burnout hits or before you realize your salary doesn't match your effort. The peak of your 'new year, new me' phase.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the peak or height of one's diligence or passion for a task.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **kasigasigan** siya ng kanyang karera nang magpasya siyang mag-abroad.","translation":"He was at the **peak** of his career when he decided to go abroad."},{"sentence":"Iba ang **kasigasigan** ng mga kabataan sa pagsuporta sa kanilang mga idolo.","translation":"The **fervor** of the youth in supporting their idols is on another level."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang-ugat (Zingiber officinale) na may maanghang na lasa, ginagamit bilang pampalasa sa pagluluto at bilang halamang-gamot.
original_explanation: The ultimate tita ingredient. If your throat is itchy, salabat (ginger tea). If the tinola is bland, more `luya`. If you need to ward off evil spirits (or just a cold), `luya` is the answer. It's the spicy root that powers the Filipino kitchen and home pharmacy.
usage_notes: A staple in Filipino dishes like Tinola, Arroz Caldo, and Paksiw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay si nanay ng maraming **luya** sa tinola para mas malinamnam.","translation":"Mom put a lot of **ginger** in the chicken soup to make it more flavorful."},{"sentence":"Mabisa raw ang salabat na gawa sa **luya** para sa namamaos na lalamunan.","translation":"They say tea made from **ginger** is effective for a hoarse throat."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng anyong pandulaan sa isang salaysay o pangyayari; o ang labis na pag-arte o pagpapakita ng damdamin.
original_explanation: This is when someone turns a minor inconvenience into a full-blown teleserye episode. Spilled coffee? Cue the dramatic monologue. Slow internet? Time for a dramatic faint. It's the art of "OA" (Over-Acting), a national pastime. The opposite of "chill".
usage_notes: Can refer to a formal theatrical adaptation or, more commonly in colloquial speech, to someone being overly emotional or dramatic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsasadrama** ng kuwento ni Rizal ay nakatulong upang mas maunawaan ito ng mga mag-aaral.","translation":"The **dramatization** of Rizal's story helped the students understand it better."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na nga 'yang **pagsasadrama** mo, simpleng problema lang 'yan.","translation":"Stop your **making a scene**, it's just a simple problem."}]

translation: to salt; to add salt to
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagbubudbod ng asin sa isang bagay, karaniwan sa pagkain, upang magbigay-lasa o bilang preserbatibo.
original_explanation: The verb form of unleashing the salt bae. It's what you do to your fries, your steak, or the fish you're about to dry under the sun. 'Asinan mo pa, bes, kulang sa alat.'
usage_notes: Can be a command or an infinitive. Distinguishable from the noun 'asinan' (salt bed/container) by context and stress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **asinan** ang isda bago ito iprito.","translation":"You need **to salt** the fish before frying it."},{"sentence":"**Asinan** mo nang bahagya ang kamatis para mas lumabas ang lasa.","translation":"**Add salt** to the tomato lightly to bring out its flavor more."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o tao na labis na sinasamba o hinahangaan na parang isang diyos, na kadalasan ay itinuturing na maling pagsamba. Isang anito o idolo.
etymology: Pag-uulit ng salitang 'diyos' (mula sa Espanyol na 'dios'), na may panlaping '-an' na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkakatulad o imitasyon.
original_explanation: This is your ultimate bias in K-Pop, the celebrity you worship, or even that crush you can't stop thinking about. It's someone you've placed on a pedestal so high, they can do no wrong in your eyes. "Huwag kang magkaroon ng ibang diyus-diyusan," says the Bible. "But have you seen my BTS photocard collection?" says the ARMY.
usage_notes: May dalang negatibong konotasyon ng maling pagsamba, ngunit maaari ring gamitin sa modernong konteksto bilang hyperbole para sa matinding paghanga o 'fandom'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang pera ang kanyang **diyus-diyusan**.","translation":"For him, money is his **idol**."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang pagtrato sa artistang iyan na parang **diyus-diyusan**.","translation":"Stop treating that celebrity like a **false god**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining o akto ng pagsusuri at paghatol sa merito ng mga akdang pampanitikan o masining; isang mapanuring sanaysay o pag-aaral.
original_explanation: What your boss gives you during your performance review, what your titas give you about your life choices, and what netizens give everyone on social media. It can be constructive (helpful) or destructive (Maritess-level chismis).
usage_notes: Can refer to both a single piece of criticism or the general act of critiquing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumanggap ng maraming **kritika** ang bagong pelikula mula sa mga manonood.","translation":"The new movie received a lot of **criticism** from the audience."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **kritika** sa nobela ay nailathala sa isang pambansang pahayagan.","translation":"His **critique** of the novel was published in a national newspaper."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mapurol o kulang sa liwanag, kislap, o sigla, partikular sa ilaw o sa mga mata.
original_explanation: 'Yung look ng mga mata mo after an all-nighter finishing a report, or after crying over a K-drama finale. It's the opposite of 'sparkling eyes.' May lamlam ang mga mata niya—puyat ba 'yan o hugot?
usage_notes: Often used to describe eyes ('lamlam ng mata') or light ('lamlam ng ilaw').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kita sa **lamlam** ng kanyang mga mata ang kanyang pagod at kalungkutan.","translation":"You could see in the **somberness** of his eyes his fatigue and sadness."},{"sentence":"Sa **lamlam** ng kandila, aninag ko ang kanyang mukha.","translation":"In the **dimness** of the candle, I could make out his face."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-alis o pagbakbak ng isang bagay na nakadikit sa ibabaw ng iba pa, tulad ng pintura, balat, o etiketa.
original_explanation: That super satisfying (or frustrating) feeling of peeling off a price sticker in one go. Or when your sunburn starts to peel and you look like a shedding lizard. It's the action of removing a surface layer. "Bes, huwag mong tuklapin 'yung sugat, magkakapeklat 'yan!"
usage_notes: Used for things that are stuck on a surface, like paint, posters, scabs, or skin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **tuklapin** muna ang lumang pintura bago magpinta ulit.","translation":"The old paint must be **peeled off** first before painting again."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang sinubukang **tuklapin** ang selyo ng lumang sulat.","translation":"He carefully tried to **peel off** the seal of the old letter."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng katapatan; hindi nagtataksil o nandaraya; totoo sa sinasabi at ginagawa.
original_explanation: Being a 'tapat' friend is like being a human power bank—always there, reliable, and won't suddenly go to 1%. It's the opposite of that friend who 'seen-zones' you when you need them most. #SanaAllTapat
usage_notes: Describes a person's character of being truthful and devoted. Stress is on the last syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang **tapat** na kaibigan sa hirap at ginhawa.","translation":"She is a **loyal** friend through thick and thin."},{"sentence":"Mananatili akong **tapat** sa aking mga pangako.","translation":"I will remain **faithful** to my promises."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sugal na ginagamitan ng baraha, na karaniwang nilalaro sa mga lamay o libangan, kung saan tumataya ang mga manlalaro sa mga barahang ilalabas ng isang bangka.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "monte", na tumutukoy sa isang tumpok (ng baraha).
original_explanation: A classic Filipino card game often played at wakes ('lamay') to keep people awake. It's basically a game of chance where you bet on which card will show up. It's the reason your tito lost his 13th-month pay last Christmas and why wakes can sometimes feel like a mini-casino.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with gambling, especially during wakes and fiestas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdamag silang naglaro ng **monte** sa lamay.","translation":"They played **monte** all night at the wake."},{"sentence":"Naubos ang pera niya sa kakalaro ng **monte**.","translation":"He lost all his money from constantly playing **monte**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakaangat o nakataas mula sa isang kalatagan; nakaumbok.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish `calzar` (to shoe, to wedge) or `alzar` (to raise).
original_explanation: Think of the text on your credit card, the bumps on a Braille book, or that one pimple that decides to pop up before a big date—it's kalsa. It's anything that's not flat, something that's raised and wants to be noticed. Like your kilay that's perfectly "on fleek" and stands out.
usage_notes: Often used to describe textures, surfaces, or something physically propped up.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kalsa** ang mga letra sa pabalat ng lumang libro.","translation":"The letters on the old book's cover are **embossed**."},{"sentence":"Naglagay sila ng pampatigas para manatiling **kalsa** ang unan.","translation":"They put a stiffener to keep the pillow **raised**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng anyo tungo sa pagiging bilog.
original_explanation: What happens to your face during the holidays after all the Noche Buena and Media Noche feasts. Or when the moon is full. **Bumilog** na naman ang tiyan ko, puro kasi samgyup!
usage_notes: Stative verb indicating a change of state. It means 'to become round'. Present: bumibilog. Future: bibilog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumilog** ang buwan kagabi kaya maliwanag sa labas.","translation":"The moon **became round** (full) last night, so it was bright outside."},{"sentence":"**Bumilog** ang kanyang mga mata sa gulat nang makita ang sorpresa.","translation":"Her eyes **became round** in surprise when she saw the surprise."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang balbal mula sa Ingles na ginagamit upang paghambingin ang dalawang magkaibang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon na may magkatulad na pangkalahatang pakiramdam, katangian, o "vibe".
original_explanation: The go-to phrase for connecting two totally unrelated things that somehow feel identical. Your chaotic Tita at a family reunion and a Mariah Carey diva moment? **Same energy**. That picture of a cat judging you and your boss during a performance review? **Same energy**. It's the Theory of Relativity for memes.
usage_notes: Used to create humorous or insightful comparisons, often accompanied by two side-by-side images.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Yung hitsura ng pusa ko 'pag ayaw maligo at yung hitsura mo 'pag Monday morning? **Same energy**.","translation":"The look on my cat's face when it doesn't want a bath and your face on a Monday morning? **Same energy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking silid sa isang bahay o gusali na ginagamit para sa pagtanggap ng mga bisita o para sa mga pormal na pagtitipon.
original_explanation: The OG living room before it became the 'sala'. It's that fancy room your lola would only let you use when a priest or a politician visits, and where the plastic-covered sofa resides. Not to be confused with the 'parlor' where you get your hair did, though both come from words meaning 'reception room'.
usage_notes: While 'sala' is more common for a home's living room, 'salon' often implies a larger, more formal hall or parlor, like in old ancestral houses or public buildings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga maharlika ay nagtipon sa **salon** ng palasyo.","translation":"The nobles gathered in the palace's **hall**."},{"sentence":"Buksan ninyo ang mga bintana sa **salon** para pumasok ang hangin.","translation":"Open the windows in the **parlor** to let the air in."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghimagas na yari sa pula ng itlog, gatas kondensada, gatas evaporada, at asukal, na may arnibal (caramel) sa ibabaw at ilalim.
original_explanation: The king of Filipino desserts. The reason why there are so many leftover egg whites (leading to meringue). It's that jiggly, sweet, caramel-topped slice of heaven you see at every fiesta, birthday, and Noche Buena. If you can make a good leche flan, you're basically marriage material.
usage_notes: Isang pangunahing panghimagas sa mga pagdiriwang sa Pilipinas. Kadalasang hugis-itlog (llyanera) o bilog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong panghimagas ang **leche flan** na gawa ni Lola.","translation":"My favorite dessert is the **leche flan** made by Grandma."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong ubusin ang **leche flan**, magtira ka para sa iba!","translation":"Don't finish the **leche flan**, leave some for the others!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malawakan at mabilis na pagkalat ng isang nakahahawang sakit sa isang populasyon sa loob ng isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: Ito yung mas pormal at mas common na term kaysa "epidemik". Kung ang pandemic ay world tour ng virus, ang epidemiko ay parang major concert lang sa isang bansa o rehiyon. Malaki na, pero localized pa. Naging bukambibig ito noong kasagsagan ng kung anu-anong health scares.
usage_notes: Mas ginagamit ito sa pormal na pagsulat at balita kumpara sa "epidemik".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtaas ng kaso ng tigdas ay umabot na sa lebel na **epidemiko**.","translation":"The rise in measles cases has reached an **epidemic** level."},{"sentence":"Nagsagawa ng malawakang pagbabakuna upang maiwasan ang **epidemiko**.","translation":"Mass vaccinations were conducted to prevent an **epidemic**."}]

translation: To attach; to enclose; to include.
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasama ng isang bagay sa isa pa, karaniwan bilang isang karagdagan o kalakip sa isang sulat, dokumento, o pakete.
original_explanation: The OG 'attach file' button. Before email, you'd **ilakip** your 2x2 photo with your resume. It means to include something with something else. 'Please **ilakip** the receipt' is something you'd hear when processing reimbursements. It’s putting two or more things together to be sent or considered as one package.
usage_notes: Very common in formal, business, or academic contexts, especially concerning documents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **ilakip** ang iyong resume sa email.","translation":"Don't forget to **attach** your resume to the email."},{"sentence":"**Inilakip** niya ang isang liham sa regalong ipinadala.","translation":"She **enclosed** a letter with the gift she sent."}]

translation: dryness; the state of being dry
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkawala ng halumigmig o pagiging hindi basa.
original_explanation: 'Yung lalamunan mo the morning after a serious 'inuman' session. Or your love life. Or your bank account before 'sweldo.' That state of lacking moisture or funds is pagkatuyo.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal dryness (of skin, land, laundry) or figurative dryness (of a topic, a person's life, finances).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng lotion para maiwasan ang **pagkatuyo** ng iyong balat.","translation":"Use lotion to prevent the **dryness** of your skin."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkatuyo** ng ilog ay isang masamang senyales para sa mga magsasaka.","translation":"The **state of being dry** of the river is a bad sign for the farmers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tubo o pakinabang na nakukuha mula sa isang negosyo, puhunan, o anumang gawain.
original_explanation: The reason your tita from Divisoria wakes up at 3 AM. It's the 'tubo' or profit you make from selling stuff, whether it's pre-loved clothes online or your baked goodies. When someone asks 'Magkano **ganansya** mo diyan?' they're asking for the real chismis about your business.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of business, finance, or any activity where a return is expected.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maliit lang ang **ganansya** sa pagbebenta ng tingi-tingi.","translation":"There is little **profit** in selling retail items."},{"sentence":"Ang mahalaga ay hindi lang **ganansya**, kundi ang serbisyo sa komunidad.","translation":"What's important is not just **profit**, but the service to the community."}]

meaning_filipino: Hilahin o buhatin ang isang mabigat na bagay nang may puwersa, karaniwan sa tulong ng sasakyan o makinarya.
etymology: From English 'haul' + i- (causative prefix). The root 'haula' itself is not a native Tagalog word.
original_explanation: This is a direct Tagalized loanword from English 'to haul'. It's what you do when your car breaks down and you need a tow truck to 'ihaula' it to the shop. Or when you buy so much stuff from the ukay-ukay that you need help to 'ihaula' your shopping bags home.
usage_notes: Primarily used for vehicles or very heavy objects. A clear English borrowing, often seen in news reports about vehicle recovery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangan nilang **ihaula** ang kotse palabas ng putikan.","translation":"They needed to **haul** the car out of the mud."},{"sentence":"Sino ang mag-**ihaula** ng lahat ng kahon na ito paakyat sa apartment?","translation":"Who will **haul** all these boxes up to the apartment?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim na paggalang at pagpaparangal, karaniwang ipinapakita sa mga nakatatanda, may awtoridad, o mga sagradong bagay at lugar.
original_explanation: It's more than just 'respect.' It's the 'mano po' level of respect. It's the hush that falls over the room when lola starts telling her stories. It's how you're supposed to act in church, but also how you should act when someone is presenting their thesis. It’s that deep-seated reverence that's a cornerstone of Filipino culture.
usage_notes: A deeper, more formal form of respect than 'galang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpakita siya ng **pagpipitagan** sa mga nakatatanda sa pamamagitan ng pagmamano.","translation":"He showed **respect** to the elders by doing the 'mano' gesture."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpipitagan** sa watawat ay tanda ng pagmamahal sa bayan.","translation":"The **reverence** for the flag is a sign of love for the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng radyasyong elektromagnetiko na ginagamit upang makita ang loob ng katawan, lalo na ang mga buto. Ito rin ang tawag sa imaheng nalilikha ng prosesong ito.
original_explanation: That spooky black and white picture of your skeleton that the doctor orders when you fall down the stairs. It's how they check if your 'pag-ibig' is the only thing broken, or if your bones are, too. Also, your bag goes through this at the airport and MRT security.
usage_notes: Common medical and security term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong bumalik sa ospital para kunin ang resulta ng aking **eksrey**.","translation":"I need to go back to the hospital to get the result of my **X-ray**."},{"sentence":"Nakita sa **eksrey** na may bali ang kanyang braso.","translation":"The **X-ray** showed that his arm was broken."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang paraan ng pagtatrabaho kung saan ang isang tao ay self-employed at hindi nakatali sa isang partikular na employer sa pangmatagalang panahon.
original_explanation: 'Yung trabaho na ikaw ang sarili mong boss. Pwede kang mag-work from home, sa coffee shop, o sa beach. Sounds cool, 'no? Pero ikaw din ang sarili mong HR, accounting, at sales department. You have the freedom to choose your work hours, pero minsan, it also means working at 2 AM to meet a deadline for a client in another timezone. The ultimate "raket" culture, but make it professional.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective (freelance writer) or a noun (doing freelance).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa siyang **freelance** graphic designer kaya flexible ang oras niya.","translation":"She is a **freelance** graphic designer so her time is flexible."},{"sentence":"Maraming **freelance** na trabaho ang makikita online.","translation":"There are many **freelance** jobs available online."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kompuwestong kemikal (CaC₂) na karaniwang ginagamit upang pabilisin ang paghinog ng mga prutas tulad ng saging at mangga.
original_explanation: The magic powder your suking fruit vendor uses to make green mangoes turn yellow overnight. It's basically a fruit time-machine. You know the mangoes were ripened with kalburo when they're sweet on the outside but still sour near the seed. The life hack (or cheat code) of the fruit world.
usage_notes: Primarily associated with the artificial ripening of fruits. It releases acetylene gas when exposed to moisture, which acts as a ripening agent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nilagyan nila ng **kalburo** ang mga saging para mahinog agad.","translation":"They put **calcium carbide** on the bananas to ripen them quickly."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang prutas na natural ang pagkahinog at hindi minadali sa **kalburo**.","translation":"Fruits that ripen naturally are more delicious than those rushed with **calcium carbide**."}]

translation: to decree; to ordain; to destine
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatakda o pag-uutos ng isang batas, patakaran, o kapalaran na hindi mababago.
original_explanation: This is a high-level, celestial, or governmental kind of verb. It’s what fate (tadhana) does. It's what the constitution does. 'Ang batas ay nagtatadhana...' is how serious legal documents start. It’s not just setting a rule, it’s carving it in stone. Parang 'pag sinabi ng nanay mo na 'Ako ang batas sa pamamahay na ito,' she's basically using this verb.
usage_notes: A very formal word, primarily used in legal, literary, or philosophical contexts. Not used in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Saligang Batas ang nag**tadhana** ng mga karapatan ng mamamayan.","translation":"The Constitution **decrees** the rights of the citizens."},{"sentence":"Sino ang maaaring **magtadhana** ng ating kapalaran?","translation":"Who can **ordain** our destiny?"}]

translation: to split something open, to cleave
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng kilos na hatiin o paghiwalayin ang isang buong bagay sa dalawang bahagi.
original_explanation: This is the action word. It's what you *do* to the coconut. "Biakin mo na 'yang puso ko, sige!" is peak Filipino drama. It's the command form: "Go on, split it!"
usage_notes: This is an object-focused verb. The action is being done *to* something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **biakin** ang isang buko kung mapurol ang iyong kutsilyo.","translation":"It's hard **to split open** a coconut if your knife is dull."},{"sentence":"**Biakin** mo ang tinapay para sa ating dalawa.","translation":"**Split** the bread for the two of us."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay at lansakang pag-alis ng mga tao mula sa isang lugar patungo sa mas ligtas na pook, karaniwan dahil sa panganib o kalamidad.
original_explanation: This is the official term for "Bes, baha na, let's go na sa evacuation center!" It's the community-level 'takbo!' when a volcano is about to erupt, a super typhoon is coming, or there's a fire. It's a group activity you never want to be a part of.
usage_notes: Refers to a mass or group action, not an individual one. The root 'likas' can also mean 'to move house' or 'transfer'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ang mga residente na **maglikasan** bago pa man dumating ang malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The residents were advised to **evacuate** even before the strong typhoon arrived."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **maglikasan** ang mga tao mula sa paanan ng bulkan.","translation":"The people from the foot of the volcano have started to **evacuate**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mayroon o nababalutan ng maraming kaliskis.
original_explanation: Parang balat ng isda, ahas, o 'yung siko mo pag hindi ka nag-lotion. "Friend, makaliskis 'yang legs mo, mag-moisturize ka naman." Also used to describe a poorly cleaned fish at the palengke.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for animals or figuratively for dry skin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isdang bangus ay **makaliskis** kaya mahirap linisin.","translation":"The milkfish is very **scaly**, so it's hard to clean."},{"sentence":"Naging **makaliskis** ang kanyang balat dahil sa sobrang init.","translation":"Her skin became **scaly** because of the extreme heat."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilubog o isawsaw nang bahagya at mabilis ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay daliri o pagkain, sa isang likido.
original_explanation: That thing you do when you're testing the water temperature at the beach before you fully commit, or when you dip your pandesal in coffee. It's a quick, tentative dip, not a full-on plunge. You're just 'dawdaw'-ing.
usage_notes: Often used for dipping fingers or food into a liquid like water, sauce, or coffee.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magdawdaw** ng daliri sa sarsa kung gagamitin pa iyan ng iba.","translation":"Don't **dip** your finger in the sauce if others will still use it."},{"sentence":"Mahilig si Lolo na **magdawdaw** ng biskwit sa kanyang kape tuwing umaga.","translation":"Grandpa loves to **dip** biscuits into his coffee every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang kagamitan, kasangkapan, o kemikal na ginagamit sa paglilinis.
original_explanation: A slightly more 'conyo' or old-school way of saying 'panlinis'. It's what your abuela might ask for when she means the Zonrox or Domex. Comes from the Spanish 'limpia'.
usage_notes: Less common than 'panlinis' but understood, especially among older speakers or in certain regions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **panlimpya** at tanggalin mo ang mantsa sa sahig.","translation":"Get a **cleaner** and remove the stain on the floor."},{"sentence":"Mabisa ba ang bagong **panlimpya** na binili mo?","translation":"Is the new **cleaning agent** you bought effective?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na lihim na nagmamanman o nag-iimbestiga upang makakuha ng impormasyon; isang espiya o detektib.
original_explanation: The original 'Marites'. A 'tiktik' is a spy, the person secretly gathering intel. It could be a government agent, a private eye, or just your nosy kapitbahay trying to figure out who visited you last night. They operate in stealth mode to get the chismis... or state secrets.
usage_notes: Can also refer to the act of spying itself ('pagtitiktik').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpadala ng **tiktik** ang kalaban upang alamin ang kanilang plano.","translation":"The enemy sent a **spy** to find out their plan."},{"sentence":"Gumanap siyang isang **tiktik** sa bagong pelikula.","translation":"He played a **detective** in the new movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap o utos na ipabukas sa iba ang isang bagay na nakasara.
original_explanation: The magic word you use when the 'garapon' of peanut butter is too tight, the door is stuck, or you're too lazy to get up and open the window. It's the ultimate act of delegation for opening things. "Hoy, bunso, pabukas nga nitong bote ng ketchup!"
usage_notes: A command or request form. The full form would be something like 'Maaari bang pabukas...?' (Can you please open...?).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pabukas** naman ng pinto, may dala-dala kasi ako.","translation":"**Please open** the door, as I am carrying something."},{"sentence":"Nag-utos siya sa bata na, '**Pabukas** ng bintana para pumasok ang hangin.'","translation":"He ordered the child, '**Have the window opened** so the air can come in.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang sukatin ang lalim; hindi maunawaan o matalos ang kabuuan.
etymology: From 'di-' (not) + 'ma-' (ability prefix) + 'arok' (to fathom, to sound the depth of).
original_explanation: Like trying to understand your parents' logic for keeping old, broken appliances. Or trying to figure out why your internet connection is slow despite paying for a high-speed plan. Some things are just di-maarok.
usage_notes: Often used in a figurative or literary sense to describe things that are profound, mysterious, or complex.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ng isang ina ay **di-maarok** ang lalim.","translation":"A mother's love is **unfathomably** deep."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, **di-maarok** ang mga patakaran ng bagong software.","translation":"For him, the rules of the new software are **unfathomable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panahon ng tatlong araw ng pananalangin o pagdiriwang, lalo na sa liturhiya ng Simbahang Kristiyano. Ang pinakakilala ay ang "Easter Triduum" na sumasaklaw mula Huwebes Santo hanggang Sabado de Gloria.
etymology: Mula sa Latin na "triduum", na nangangahulugang 'isang tatlong araw na panahon'.
original_explanation: The holiest 3-day weekend of the year for Catholics. It's the spiritual equivalent of a season finale cliffhanger. From the Last Supper (Maundy Thursday), to the ultimate sacrifice (Good Friday), ending in the quiet anticipation of the greatest comeback story ever told (Black Saturday). For many Filipinos, this also means no-meat diet, no loud music, and a trip to the province or the beach.
usage_notes: Mas pormal at teolohikal ang dating kaysa sa 'triduo'. Karaniwang tumutukoy sa "Easter Triduum" o "Paschal Triduum".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Mahal na Araw ay nakasentro sa Paschal **Triduum**.","translation":"Holy Week is centered on the Paschal **Triduum**."},{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang ng Simbahan ang **Triduum** ng Pagkabuhay ni Kristo.","translation":"The Church celebrates the **Triduum** of Christ's Resurrection."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng paunang paalala o hudyat tungkol sa isang posibleng panganib, suliranin, o mahalagang pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is what your mom does before she gets really mad: "Ibabala ko na sa'yo, isa na lang." It's the official heads-up. PAGASA does this with typhoons, your office HR does this with memos, and chismosas do this before dropping the tea ("Friend, ibabala ko lang, may nakita ako..."). It's a warning shot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ibabala** mo sa kanila na may paparating na malakas na bagyo.","translation":"**Warn** them that a strong typhoon is coming."},{"sentence":"Matagal na niyang **ibinabala** ang pagbagsak ng ekonomiya.","translation":"He had long **warned** about the collapse of the economy."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa katawan ng tao o hayop.
original_explanation: This is anything related to your body. 'Pangkatawan na ehersisyo' is your workout or zumba session. 'Pangangailangang pangkatawan' is your need for food, sleep, and maybe a good massage after a long commute. It's the opposite of 'pang-isipan' (mental) or 'pang-espiritwal' (spiritual). Basically, it's the 'body' in 'body, mind, and soul'.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay na may kinalaman sa pisikal na katawan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pangkatawan** na ehersisyo para sa kalusugan.","translation":"**Physical** exercise is important for health."},{"sentence":"Nakaranas siya ng pananakit na **pangkatawan** matapos ang aksidente.","translation":"He experienced **bodily** pain after the accident."}]

meaning_filipino: Magiging nasa iisang antas, taas, o kalagayan; walang nakalalamang.
original_explanation: The goal of every group project member who did nothing but hopes for the same grade as the leader. Also, the ideal state of your kilay (eyebrows) after spending 30 minutes trying to make them twins, not just sisters. 'Sana all pantay-pantay.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa ilalim ng batas, dapat **magkakapantay** ang tingin sa lahat ng mamamayan.","translation":"Under the law, the view of all citizens should be **equal**."},{"sentence":"Tiyakin mong **magkakapantay** ang pagkakahati mo ng cake.","translation":"Make sure your division of the cake **is equal**."}]

translation: to be hit (by a vehicle); to collide with
meaning_filipino: Masalpok o tamaan ng isang bagay na gumagalaw, karaniwan ay sasakyan.
original_explanation: The #1 fear of anyone crossing EDSA. 'Tumingin ka sa dinadaanan mo, baka ka mabangga!' It’s the verb for accidental collisions, whether it's a car hitting another car, or you bumping into your crush in the hallway and all your books fly everywhere, movie-style.
usage_notes: Most commonly used for vehicular accidents, but can also be used for people or objects colliding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Muntik nang **mabangga** ng rumaragasang motor ang tumatawid na matanda.","translation":"The old person crossing the street was almost **hit** by a speeding motorcycle."},{"sentence":"Nagmamadali ako kaya **nabangga** ko ang pinto.","translation":"I was in a hurry so I **collided with** the door."}]

translation: to include; to enter (someone in a contest)
meaning_filipino: Isama ang isang tao o bagay sa isang grupo, gawain, o listahan.
original_explanation: This is what your friend does when they sign you up for a fun run without your permission. It's the act of adding someone to the group chat, the team, or the list of "sponsors" for a binyag. "Sino'ng gustong magsali sa K-pop dance cover contest?" It’s the verb form of inclusion, whether you like it or not.
usage_notes: The focus is on the actor who is doing the including. Contrast with 'sumali' (to join), where the focus is on the person joining.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan na **magsali** ng pangalan ko sa listahan.","translation":"Don't forget to **include** my name on the list."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magsali** ng kanyang anak sa isang paligsahan sa pag-awit.","translation":"She decided to **enter** her child in a singing contest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit o paglaan ng salapi para sa isang partikular na layunin, produkto, o serbisyo.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na kakasweldo mo lang pero by tomorrow, kailangan mo na ulit 'magasta' para sa bills, Foodpanda, at Shopee checkout. The circle of life ng mga alipin ng salapi.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of spending money, but can also mean to expend energy or resources. The more common Filipino term is 'gumastos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magasta** nang labis sa mga bagay na hindi mo naman kailangan.","translation":"Don't **spend** too much on things you don't really need."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magasta** ang budget nang matalino para umabot ito hanggang sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"We need to **spend** the budget wisely so it lasts until next month."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapahayag ng damdamin o mensahe sa paraang hindi pasalita, karaniwang ginagamit para ilarawan ang mga mata.
original_explanation: When your eyes do the talking for you. 'Yung tingin na parang sinasabi, "Gusto ko ng milk tea," or "Please, 'wag mo na akong i-seen." It’s that look that says a thousand words without uttering a single one. Very expressive, very dramatic.
usage_notes: Halos palaging ginagamit upang ilarawan ang mga mata ('mga matang nangungusap') at gumaganap bilang isang pang-uri sa ganitong konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinitigan niya ako ng may mga matang **nangungusap**.","translation":"He/She stared at me with **expressive** eyes."},{"sentence":"Kahit hindi siya nagsasalita, **nangungusap** ang kanyang mga tingin.","translation":"Even if he isn't talking, his gazes are **speaking**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing mas malala o mas masama ang isang sitwasyon o kondisyon.
original_explanation: The verb form of making things worse. It's what you do when you pour gasoline on a fire. 'Huwag mo na siyang kausapin, baka palalain mo lang ang galit niya.' It's the active choice to escalate drama, intentionally or not.
usage_notes: The opposite of 'pabutihin' (to improve).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagpupuyat ay maaaring **palalain** ang iyong sakit.","translation":"Staying up late can **worsen** your illness."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **palalain** ang problema.","translation":"Don't **aggravate** the problem anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng takip sa bintana na binubuo ng mga pahalang o patayong slat na maaaring i-adjust upang makontrol ang pasok ng liwanag at hangin.
original_explanation: That thing on the window your mom yells at you to clean, slat by dusty slat. Perfect for 'marites' mode, when you need to peek outside without being too obvious. Way more old-school than curtains.
usage_notes: Commonly refers to the older, wooden or plastic slat blinds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-angat naman ng **persiyana** para pumasok ang liwanag.","translation":"Please raise the **blinds** to let the light in."},{"sentence":"Maalikabok na ang mga **persiyana** sa lumang bahay.","translation":"The **blinds** in the old house are already dusty."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang literal na ilaw na nagbibigay-diin sa isang tao o bagay sa entablado; sa matalinghagang paraan, ito ay ang pagiging sentro ng atensyon ng publiko.
original_explanation: That thing every "bida-bida" (attention-seeker) craves. When someone is in the "spotlight," all eyes are on them, whether it's for winning a beauty pageant, acing a presentation at work, or being the subject of the latest office chismis. It's the opposite of being "sidelined." Some people love it, some people dread it.
usage_notes: Used both literally for a stage light and, more commonly, figuratively for being the center of attention.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa kanya ang **spotlight** matapos siyang manalo sa patimpalak.","translation":"The **spotlight** was on her after she won the contest."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang laging nasa **spotlight** kaya mas pinipili niyang magtrabaho sa likod ng kamera.","translation":"She doesn't like always being in the **spotlight**, so she prefers to work behind the camera."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pagsasanhi na magbigay ng isang babala o paunang paalala tungkol sa isang panganib o mahalagang impormasyon.
original_explanation: This is what PAGASA does every time a typhoon is about to hit the PAR. They magpababala to the public. It's not just warning someone directly; it's causing a warning to be disseminated. Your condo admin might magpababala about a scheduled power interruption. It's an official heads-up, a "Hey, something's coming, be ready!" kind of action.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of official announcements, safety, and public information.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ahensya ng gobyerno ay **nagpababala** tungkol sa paparating na malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The government agency **had a warning issued** about the approaching strong typhoon."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magpababala** sa lahat ng residente na mag-ingat sa mga magnanakaw.","translation":"We need to **have a warning issued** to all residents to be careful of thieves."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino para sa kalagayan ng pagiging walang pera.
original_explanation: The official status of every Filipino five days before 'sweldo' (payday). It's that feeling when your wallet has more pictures than cash, and your GCash balance is crying. The opposite of 'sana all'.
usage_notes: A very common Taglish slang term to describe a lack of funds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako makakasama sa Biyernes, **brok** na ako.","translation":"I can't join on Friday, I'm already **broke**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking kasintahan o karelasyon sa isang romantikong ugnayan.
original_explanation: The OG 'jowa'. Before 'bebe ko', 'babe', or 'mahal', there was the classic 'nobyo'. He's the guy you introduce to your parents when you're finally ready for the 'kayo na ba?' interrogation at the family reunion.
usage_notes: The female counterpart is 'nobya'. Often used interchangeably with modern slang like 'jowa' or the more formal 'kasintahan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakilala na ni Ana ang kanyang **nobyo** sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"Ana finally introduced her **boyfriend** to her parents."},{"sentence":"Ang sweet naman ng **nobyo** mo, laging may dalang pasalubong.","translation":"Your **boyfriend** is so sweet, he always brings a small gift."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong walang awa, malupit, at kayang manakit ng kapwa nang hindi nakakaramdam ng pagsisisi.
original_explanation: The villain in every teleserye who orders someone to be 'taken care of' without batting an eyelash. A person who can betray a friend for personal gain. Literally 'cold blood,' it describes someone who is terrifyingly devoid of empathy or compassion. The ultimate kontrabida trait.
usage_notes: A very strong idiom used to describe a cruel or ruthless person, often a criminal or villain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tanging isang taong **malamig ang dugo** ang makagagawa ng ganoong karumal-dumal na krimen.","translation":"Only a **cold-blooded** person could commit such a heinous crime."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang negosyanteng **malamig ang dugo** at walang pakialam sa kanyang mga empleyado.","translation":"He is known as a **ruthless** businessman who doesn't care about his employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng pangkulay sa talukap ng mata, karaniwang tinatawag na 'eyeshadow'. Maaari ring mangahulugang paglikha ng anino o lilim.
original_explanation: A makeup tutorial verb. 'Okay, besh, now we're going to magsombra using this warm palette.' It's the act of putting on eyeshadow. Or, in a more dramatic hugot sense, it's what your ex did to your life—cast a dark shadow over it. Charot.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of applying makeup (eyeshadow). The meaning 'to cast a shadow' is less common and more literal or poetic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong siyang **magsombra** ng mata para sa mga espesyal na okasyon.","translation":"She knows how to **apply eyeshadow** for special occasions."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magsombra** ang malaking puno sa aming bakuran habang palubog ang araw.","translation":"The large tree in our yard began to cast a shadow as the sun was setting."}]

translation: the act of packing provisions or allowance
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghahanda o pagbibigay ng pagkain, pera, o iba pang kailangan para sa isang paglalakbay, trabaho, o paaralan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate act of Filipino parental love. It's your mom waking up at 4 AM to cook your lunch, or your dad slipping you extra cash 'para sa pamasahe'. Pagbabaon is the reason you survive until the next sahod (payday).
usage_notes: Differentiated from the other 'pagbabaon' (burying) by context. This one relates to food, money, or supplies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Araw-araw, ang nanay ang nag-aasikaso ng **pagbabaon** ko ng pananghalian.","translation":"Every day, my mother takes care of **packing** my lunch **provisions**."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagbabaon** ng sapat na tubig kung aakyat ka ng bundok.","translation":"The **act of packing** enough water is important if you're going to climb a mountain."}]

translation: can be bribed, is susceptible to bribery
meaning_filipino: Nagagawang tanggapin ang suhol; maaaring mahikayat o mabili sa pamamagitan ng pera o pabor kapalit ng isang paborableng desisyon o aksyon.
original_explanation: This describes someone whose principles are for sale. Give them a little 'lagay' or 'padulas' and suddenly, rules can be bent. It's the person who can be convinced to look the other way for the right price. In short, they have a price tag.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation, implying corruption and lack of integrity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga opisyal na madaling **mapasuhol** kaya't laganap ang korapsyon.","translation":"There are officials who **can be easily bribed**, which is why corruption is rampant."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya **napasusuhol** dahil matibay ang kanyang mga prinsipyo.","translation":"He **is not susceptible to bribery** because his principles are strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estruktura, karaniwan sa palaruan, na may makinis at pahabang dalisdis kung saan nagpapadulas ang mga bata.
original_explanation: The Tagalog word for a playground slide, which is way cooler than just saying 'slide'. It's where you got your first scraped knee and your first taste of gravity. The **dausdusan** is a core memory for every Batang 90s. Synonymous with 'padulasan'.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with 'padulasan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglalaro ang mga bata sa **dausdusan** sa parke.","translation":"The children are playing on the **slide** at the park."},{"sentence":"Ingat ka sa pag-akyat sa **dausdusan** at baka ka mahulog.","translation":"Be careful climbing the **slide** or you might fall."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng matinis at magaspang na tunog, karaniwan ay mula sa pagkikiskisan ng dalawang bagay, tulad ng sahig na kahoy o hindi nalangisang bisagra.
original_explanation: The official sound of every Filipino horror movie. It's that noise your lola's aparador makes at 3 AM, or the sound of the wooden stairs when you're trying to sneak back in past curfew. If your joints lumangitngit, you're either a horror movie ghost or it's time to see a doctor.
usage_notes: An onomatopoeic word. It describes a high-pitched, grating sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumangitngit** ang luma naming pinto sa tuwing binubuksan ito.","translation":"Our old door **creaks** every time it is opened."},{"sentence":"Naririnig kong **lumangitngit** ang sahig sa ikalawang palapag.","translation":"I can hear the floor **creaking** on the second story."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng hugis o anyo ng isang silindro.
original_explanation: The shape of your tumbler, a can of spam, a Pringles can, or the concrete posts of the LRT. It's that tube-like shape that's a pain to gift-wrap.
usage_notes: A formal, technical term. In everyday speech, people might say 'hugis-lata' (can-shaped) or 'parang tubo' (like a pipe).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tangke ng tubig ay may **silindrikal** na hugis.","translation":"The water tank has a **cylindrical** shape."},{"sentence":"Gumamit sila ng mga blokeng **silindrikal** para sa pundasyon.","translation":"They used **cylindrical** blocks for the foundation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpindot, paghilot, at pagmanipula sa mga kalamnan at malambot na tisyu ng katawan upang maibsan ang sakit o tensyon.
original_explanation: What you desperately need after a week of OT, a long commute on EDSA, or carrying all the grocery bags. It's the legit, 'hilot' way to fix your 'lamig sa likod' or the fancy spa version with essential oils. A gift from the heavens for the perpetually pagod.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **masahe** dahil masakit ang likod ko.","translation":"I need a **massage** because my back hurts."},{"sentence":"Isang oras na Swedish **masahe** ang kinuha niya sa spa.","translation":"She got a one-hour Swedish **massage** at the spa."}]

translation: to let someone ride; to load onto a vehicle
meaning_filipino: Pasakayin ang isang tao o ilulan ang isang bagay sa sasakyan.
original_explanation: The classic jeepney barker's command. It's the act of getting someone or something on board, from passengers in a UV Express to your groceries in a tricycle. Metaphorically, it's when you get swept up in someone else's trip. 'Huwag kang magpa-**isakay** sa kwento niyan, baka ma-scam ka.'
usage_notes: Can refer to people or objects being loaded.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**isakay** na lang itong mga kahon sa likod ng trak.","translation":"Please **load** these boxes onto the back of the truck."},{"sentence":"**Isakay** mo na ang bata sa kotse, aalis na tayo.","translation":"**Let** the child **ride** in the car, we are about to leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paulit-ulit na pagpalo o paghampas gamit ang isang bagay na mahaba at nababaluktot, tulad ng latigo o sinturon.
original_explanation: Old-school parental discipline, but make it dramatic. This is more than just a 'palo' (hit); it implies a whip-like object (like a belt or branch) and a swift, stinging motion. The kind of punishment you see in historical dramas. Not to be confused with 'hagurin' which is to stroke. One is ouch, the other is aaah.
usage_notes: The root 'hagpos' (whip) is a homonym of 'hagpos' (slack, loose). The two are unrelated in meaning. This verb implies a more severe and often repeated action of striking compared to 'hampasin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan siya na **hahagpusin** siya ng sinturon kung hindi siya susunod.","translation":"He was warned that he would be **whipped** with a belt if he didn't obey."},{"sentence":"Sa lumang pelikula, madalas **hinahagpos** ng kontrabida ang bida.","translation":"In old movies, the villain often **lashes** the hero."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang guro na may mataas na antas ng kaalaman at karaniwang nagtuturo sa isang kolehiyo o unibersidad.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga guro sa college na either magiging life mentor mo or dahilan ng mga sleepless nights mo. Sila yung nagbibigay ng grade na "uno" o "singko" na huhubog sa 'yong pagkatao. Terror propesor? We've all had one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming **propesor** sa Pilosopiya ay napakagaling magpaliwanag.","translation":"Our Philosophy **professor** is very good at explaining."},{"sentence":"Pinapasa na bukas ang proyekto sa klase ni **Propesor** Reyes.","translation":"The project for **Professor** Reyes's class is due tomorrow."}]

translation: to make something red; to cause to blush
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapalit ng kulay ng isang bagay upang maging pula; ang maging sanhi ng pamumula ng pisngi dahil sa hiya o kilig.
original_explanation: Two modes for this word. Mode 1: You're an artist or designer and you magpapula the logo to make it pop. Mode 2: Your crush just looked at you for 0.5 seconds, and now your cheeks are doing the magpapula on their own. It's the body's natural reaction to 'kilig' or extreme 'hiya'.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal coloring or the physiological act of blushing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpapula** ng tela para sa costume.","translation":"You need to **make** the cloth **red** for the costume."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang tuksuhin, baka **magpapula** na naman ang mukha niyan.","translation":"Don't tease him, his face might **turn red** (blush) again."}]

translation: to be broken, to be damaged, to spoil
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pinsala, depekto, o pagkasama na nagiging sanhi ng hindi na paggana o pagiging hindi na kaaya-aya.
original_explanation: What happens to your phone when you drop it face down. What happens to food left outside the fridge. What happens to your diet plans when someone brings a box of donuts to the office. "Huwag mo sanang masira ang tiwala ko sa'yo" is the ultimate hugot line.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical objects, food (spoiling), or abstract concepts like trust or reputation. The past tense is 'nasira'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang laruan na iyan para hindi **masira**.","translation":"Take care of that toy so it won't **get broken**."},{"sentence":"Nalaglag ang cellphone niya kaya **nasira** ang screen.","translation":"His cellphone fell, that's why the screen **got damaged**."},{"sentence":"Baka **masira** ang ulam kung hindi ilalagay sa ref.","translation":"The food might **spoil** if it's not put in the fridge."}]

translation: to go beside; to move to the side of
meaning_filipino: Ang paglapit o pagpunta sa gilid ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: It's the action of closing the gap. When you have a crush on someone in a group, you 'casually' tabihan them for the group picture. It’s the move you make in a crowded jeepney to get closer to the window.
usage_notes: This verb focuses on the action of moving to the side of something/someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tabihan** mo ang iyong kapatid para magkasya tayo sa sopa.","translation":"**Go beside** your sibling so we can all fit on the sofa."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **tabihan**, may sakit ako.","translation":"Don't **come near my side**, I'm sick."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na kulungan o espasyo na dinisenyo para sa pag-aalaga ng mga baboy.
original_explanation: Literal na bahay ng baboy. Minsan, ito rin ang tawag sa kwarto ng kapatid mong makalat. "Ano ba 'yan, parang kulungan ng baboy ang kwarto mo!"
usage_notes: Can be used literally or as a common idiom for a very messy or dirty place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Araw-araw nililinis ni Mang Tonio ang **kulungan ng baboy**.","translation":"Mang Tonio cleans the **pigpen** every day."},{"sentence":"Linisin mo nga ang kwarto mo, mukha nang **kulungan ng baboy**!","translation":"Clean your room, it looks like a **pigsty**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan inililibing o inilalagak ang mga labi ng mga pumanaw.
original_explanation: The place that suddenly becomes a massive family reunion spot every November 1st. For the rest of the year, it's a quiet, spooky place. But during 'Undas' (All Saints' Day), the **libingan** transforms into a festival ground with food, card games, and families camping out, proving that Filipinos can find a way to have a party anywhere, even here.
usage_notes: Refers to the location where burials take place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkita-kita ang buong pamilya sa **libingan** para sa Araw ng mga Patay.","translation":"The whole family met at the **cemetery** for All Souls' Day."},{"sentence":"Ang Libingan ng mga Bayani ay isang makasaysayang **libingan** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The Heroes' Cemetery is a historic **burial ground** in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na dokumento na nagpapatunay ng pagkakakilanlan at paninirahan ng isang mamamayan, na kinakailangan para sa iba't ibang transaksyon sa pamahalaan at komersyo.
original_explanation: Ito yung resibo na binabayaran mo sa barangay hall para patunayan na existing ka sa Pilipinas. Kailangan mo 'to 'pag kumukuha ng NBI clearance, passport, o 'pag manunumpa ka sa kaso. Tandaan mo si Bonifacio at ang pagpunit ng sedula? Yes, that's the one. History, bes!
usage_notes: Madalas na tinatawag ding "community tax certificate" sa mga opisyal na dokumento.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ako ng bagong **sedula** sa munisipyo para sa aking mga papeles.","translation":"I got a new **community tax certificate** at the municipal hall for my documents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tagasunod ng anumang denominasyon ng Kristiyanismo sa Kanluran na hiwalay mula sa Simbahang Katoliko noong panahon ng Repormasyon.
original_explanation: Sa Pilipinas, kung hindi ka Katoliko, malaki ang chance na ito ang itatawag sa'yo ng mga lola, kahit na Born Again, Adventist, o iba pa ang church mo. Ito yung general term para sa mga 'kapatid' na non-Catholic Christians.
usage_notes: The word is capitalized when referring to the specific religious group. It can be used as a noun (a Protestant person) or an adjective (Protestant church).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lolo ko ay isang debotong **Protestante**.","translation":"My grandfather is a devout **Protestant**."},{"sentence":"Maraming simbahang **Protestante** ang naitayo sa aming bayan.","translation":"Many **Protestant** churches were built in our town."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga kasuotang nagamit na, may dumi, pawis, o amoy, at nangangailangan ng paglalaba.
etymology: From `marurumi` (plural form of `marumi`, from `dumi` or dirt) + `-ng` (linker) + `damit` (clothes).
original_explanation: The official contents of your laundry basket, also known as 'labahin'. It's that mountain on your chair that seems to grow on its own. When your mom sees it, you're one sermon away from World War III.
usage_notes: This is the standard term for laundry waiting to be washed. The singular form is `maruming damit`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ihiwalay mo ang puti sa de-kolor kapag maglalaba ka ng **maruruming damit**.","translation":"Separate the whites from the colored ones when you're washing **dirty clothes**."},{"sentence":"Ang dami na namang tambak na **maruruming damit** sa laundry basket.","translation":"There's a huge pile of **laundry** in the basket again."}]

meaning_filipino: Inalis, tinanggal, o natalo sa isang kompetisyon, proseso, o grupo.
original_explanation: Yung feeling mo kapag hindi ka na-shortlist sa job application, o kapag na-seen-zone ka. Sa reality shows, ito yung madramang moment na, 'I'm sorry, pero ikaw ang **eliminado** ngayong gabi.' Basically, you're out. Game over. Try again next season.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng mga paligsahan, laro, at reality television shows. Ang pambabaeng anyo ay "eliminada".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Eliminado** na ang paborito kong kalahok sa singing contest.","translation":"My favorite contestant in the singing contest has been **eliminated**."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng round na ito, isa sa kanila ay tiyak na **eliminado**.","translation":"After this round, one of them will surely be **eliminated**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpatay sa isang tao, lalo na kung ang biktima ay isang kilalang tao o kung ang pagpatay ay may motibong politikal o isinagawa nang may pananambang.
original_explanation: This isn't just regular murder; this is the stuff of headlines and history books. Think Rizal, Ninoy Aquino, or a character in a crime thriller. It's a calculated, often political, killing. It’s murder with a capital 'M' and a Wikipedia page.
usage_notes: Carries more weight and formality than 'pagpatay'. It often implies a premeditated and significant killing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpaslang** sa lider ay nagdulot ng malawakang kaguluhan.","translation":"The **assassination** of the leader caused widespread chaos."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang nanghihina o bagsak ang katawan at kalooban dahil sa matinding pagkabigo, kalungkutan, o karamdaman.
original_explanation: This is beyond just "sad." This is "sawi" level 100. It's that feeling when your crush gets married, you didn't get the promotion, and your Shopee order was cancelled, all in one day. You're not just sad, you're emotionally and physically drained, nakahandusay sa sahig ng kalungkutan. It's the "wala na, finish na" feeling.
usage_notes: A very descriptive and somewhat dramatic word for extreme despair.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos malugi ang kanyang negosyo, siya ay naiwang **lugami** at walang pag-asa.","translation":"After his business went bankrupt, he was left **dejected** and hopeless."},{"sentence":"Naging **lugami** ang kanyang pakiramdam nang malaman niyang hindi siya nakapasa sa pagsusulit.","translation":"He felt **downcast** when he found out he didn't pass the exam."}]

translation: to cause an uproar; to disturb noisily
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang malakas at magulong ingay; ang pag-istorbo sa isang lugar sa pamamagitan ng paggawa ng ingay, gulo, o iskandalo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'bulahaw' (gulo) na dinugtungan ng hulaping '-in'.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of creating a 'bulahaw'. It's what happens when someone shouts 'SALE!' in a department store or 'May sunog!' in a crowded place. It's actively turning a peaceful situation into a chaotic one. Don't be the person who likes to **bulahawin** the office with personal calls.
usage_notes: Katulad ng 'bulabugin' ngunit mas nagbibigay-diin sa magulo at maingay na resulta, hindi lamang sa simpleng pag-istorbo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ninyong **bulahawin** ang library.","translation":"Do not **disturb** the library (noisily)."},{"sentence":"Binulahaw ng mga raliyista ang buong abenida.","translation":"The rallyists **caused an uproar** along the entire avenue."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay o paggamit ng damit o anumang kasuotan sa katawan sa kasalukuyang sandali.
original_explanation: This is your OOTD in action. 'Yung moment na sinasabing "Anong isusuot ko?" tapos after 30 minutes of staring at your closet, may napili ka na. That's the *isinusuot* phase. It's the 'present tense' of your fashion statement.
usage_notes: The present tense, progressive aspect of the verb 'isuot'. It describes the action of wearing something right now.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang damit na **isinusuot** niya ay regalo mula sa kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"The dress she **is wearing** is a gift from her friend."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo **isinusuot** ang sapatos ko?","translation":"Why **are you wearing** my shoes?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatrabaho bilang isang tsuper o tagapagmaneho ng sasakyan.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for becoming a Grab driver, a jeepney driver, or your family's designated driver for life. It's the act of taking the wheel as your profession or main hustle. 'Gusto ko magtsuper para maka-ipon.'
usage_notes: Commonly used for professional drivers of public or private vehicles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang **magtsuper** ng sarili niyang dyipni balang araw.","translation":"He dreams of **working as a driver** of his own jeepney someday."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magtsuper** sa gabi para madagdagan ang kita.","translation":"I need to **work as a driver** at night to supplement my income."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw ng kamay nang pabalik-balik bilang tanda ng pagbati, pamamaalam, o pagtawag ng pansin.
original_explanation: The universal Filipino gesture for 'Hi,' 'Bye,' or 'Psst, over here!' It's the subtle kaway to a friend across the mall, the frantic kaway to catch the jeepney driver's attention, or the beauty queen's pageant kaway. A simple gesture packed with a dozen meanings.
usage_notes: Ito ang salitang ugat na ginagamit bilang pandiwa. Madalas ginagamit sa mga anyong `kumaway` (naganap na), `kumakaway` (nagaganap), at `kakaway` (magaganap).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumaway** siya sa akin bago umalis.","translation":"He **waved** at me before leaving."},{"sentence":"**Kumakaway** ang bata mula sa bintana.","translation":"The child **is waving** from the window."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng protesta kung saan ang mga kalahok ay uupo sa isang lugar at hindi aalis hanggang hindi napapakinggan ang kanilang mga hinaing.
original_explanation: The ultimate "Dito lang kami" protest move. It's when a group gets so fed up, they collectively decide to park their butts somewhere—like a lobby, an office, or a street—and refuse to leave.
