It's less about shouting and more about being an unmovable, seated inconvenience for a cause.
usage_notes: A loanword verb, often heard in the context of activism, labor disputes, or student protests. The root 'sisti' is a Filipinized form of 'sit-in'. The '-an' suffix implies reciprocal or group action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbanta ang mga manggagawa na **magsisistihan** sila sa harap ng pabrika.","translation":"The workers threatened that they **would hold a sit-in** in front of the factory."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula silang **magsistihan** noong Lunes para iprotesta ang mababang sahod.","translation":"They started to **hold a sit-in** on Monday to protest the low wages."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga tao na may malapit na ugnayan, pagtitiwala, at pagmamahal sa isa't isa; mga kaibigan.
original_explanation: More than just 'kaibigan', 'friends' is what you call your barkada, your beshies, your day-ones. They're the ones you send memes to at 3 AM, the ones who'll help you move a couch, and the ones who'll tell you, 'tama na 'yan, lasing ka na.'
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with 'kaibigan' but often implies a modern, barkada-style relationship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkikita kami ng mga **friends** ko mamaya sa mall.","translation":"I will meet with my **friends** later at the mall."},{"sentence":"Hindi lang sila katrabaho, **friends** na rin ang turingan namin.","translation":"They're not just colleagues, we treat each other as **friends**."}]

translation: to compose; to invent (a story); to fabricate
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang akda, kuwento, o komposisyon mula sa imahinasyon; ang pag-imbento ng isang salaysay na hindi totoo.
original_explanation: This is what writers, songwriters, and your neighborhood chismosa do best. They create something from nothing. 'Huwag kang mangatha ng kwento!' is what you tell your friend who's exaggerating their 'How I Met Your Mother' story for the tenth time.
usage_notes: Can be used positively (to compose a literary piece) or negatively (to fabricate a lie).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay siyang **mangatha** ng mga tula tungkol sa pag-ibig at kabiguan.","translation":"She is skilled at **composing** poems about love and heartbreak."}]

translation: in front of; in the presence of
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa lugar na nasa unahan ng isang tao o bagay, o sa presensya ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This means "in front of." It could be literal, like "Magkita tayo **sa harapan** ng mall." Or it could be about presence and accountability, like "Uminahon siya **sa harapan** ng mga magulang niya." (He admitted it in front of his parents). It’s where things happen out in the open, for everyone to see. No hiding. The opposite of "sa likod" (behind).
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na lokasyon o sa metaporikal na presensya. Madalas ding gamitin ang anyong "sa harap ng".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magkalat **sa harapan** ng bahay.","translation":"Don't make a mess **in front of** the house."},{"sentence":"Nagsalita siya nang buong tapang **sa harapan** ng madla.","translation":"He spoke with full courage **in front of** the crowd."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela o materyal na isinusuot sa sanggol o taong hindi makontrol ang pagdumi o pag-ihi.
original_explanation: Before Pampers became the generic term, this was it. It's the OG baby wrapper. Think of those white cloth diapers your lola used to wash by hand, held together by a safety pin. It’s the retro, eco-friendly (kinda) version of a modern diaper.
usage_notes: This term is becoming less common in urban areas, where 'diaper' is more prevalent. It often refers specifically to cloth diapers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang palitan na ang **palampinan** ng sanggol.","translation":"The baby's **diaper** needs to be changed."},{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, **palampinan** na gawa sa tela ang gamit ng lahat.","translation":"In the old days, everyone used **swaddling cloths** made of fabric."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng mga buto na bumubuo sa balangkas ng katawan ng isang tao o hayop.
etymology: Uncertain origin, but likely a native Austronesian term for a skeletal frame.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'body reveal' after everything else is gone. It's what's left when you've given your all to your work, your love life, or just trying to survive EDSA traffic. 'Yung totoo, after this deadline, kalansay na lang ako.' Also, the star of every Halloween party and science class.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for a biological skeleton or figuratively for the framework of something (e.g., 'kalansay ng gusali').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nakitang **kalansay** ng tao sa lumang balon.","translation":"A human **skeleton** was found in the old well."},{"sentence":"Tanging ang **kalansay** na lamang ng nasunog na bahay ang natira.","translation":"Only the **framework** of the burned house remained."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdampi ng mga labi sa isang tao o bagay; ang pandiwang anyo ng salitang 'halik'.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'halik'. It's the action itself. What you do. When your crush is finally your jowa, you don't just *give* a 'halik', you **halikan** them. It's also what you do to your lola's hand when you 'mano po'.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus verb. The actor-focus form is "humalik".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **halikan** ang kamay ng iyong lola bilang paggalang.","translation":"Don't forget **to kiss** your grandmother's hand as a sign of respect."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **halikan** ang pisngi ng sanggol ngunit natutulog pa ito.","translation":"She wants **to kiss** the baby's cheek, but it is still sleeping."}]

translation: to patch, to plaster, to apply a poultice
meaning_filipino: Maglagay ng panakip o pantakip sa isang butas, sugat, o sira upang ayusin o gamutin ito.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'quick fix' verb. Got a leak in the roof? Magtapal ka ng sealant. Got a small wound? Magtapal ka ng Band-Aid. Your friend is heartbroken? Magtapal ka ng... well, maybe just give them ice cream. It's about covering up a flaw, whether it's a hole in the wall or a hole in your soul (kidding!).
usage_notes: Used for both literal patching (walls, tires) and applying medicinal patches or poultices.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **magtapal** ng butas sa pader bago ito pinturahan.","translation":"You need to **patch** the hole in the wall before painting it."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan siya ng kanyang ina kung paano **magtapal** ng dahon ng bayabas sa sugat.","translation":"His mother taught him how to **apply** a guava leaf poultice on a wound."}]

translation: to be able to guard; to be able to watch over
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahan o pagkakataong magbantay o mag-alaga sa isang bagay, lugar, o tao.
original_explanation: Like being the designated "bantay" for the group's belongings at the beach while everyone else is swimming. Or when you're the only one sober enough to make sure your drunk friends get home safe. "Sino ang makatanod sa mga gamit natin mamaya?"
usage_notes: "Tanod" is often associated with a barangay tanod (village watchman). This verb extends that idea to the ability to perform the act of guarding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating humanap ng **makatanod** sa bahay habang nasa bakasyon tayo.","translation":"We need to find someone who can **watch over** the house while we are on vacation."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya **makatanod** nang maayos dahil inaantok na siya.","translation":"He can't **guard** properly because he is already sleepy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang batayan, dahilan, o paliwanag sa isang kilos o paniniwala; pagiging tama o naaayon sa batas at moralidad.
etymology: From `ka-` + `tuwid` (straight, right) + `-an`, forming the abstract noun for 'righteousness' or 'reason'.
original_explanation: This is your 'why.' Your alibi. Your defense when someone asks, 'Bakit mo ginawa 'yun?' It's the logic you present in a debate, the hugot you use to justify your life choices, or the reason you give your boss for being late. When you say 'May katuwiran ako,' you're saying, 'I have my reasons, and they're valid (to me, at least).'
usage_notes: Can also be spelled colloquially as 'katwiran'. It encompasses both logical reason and moral rightness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang iyong **katuwiran** sa pag-alis nang maaga?","translation":"What is your **reason** for leaving early?"},{"sentence":"Ipaglaban mo ang iyong **katuwiran** kung alam mong nasa tama ka.","translation":"Fight for your **righteousness** if you know you are in the right."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tayutay na tuwirang naghahambing ng dalawang magkaibang bagay na hindi gumagamit ng mga salitang pantulad tulad ng 'gaya ng', 'tulad ng', o 'parang'.
original_explanation: This is the literary version of "Sana all." It's when you say "You are my sunshine" instead of "You are *like* my sunshine." You're not just comparing, you're equating. It's a high-level compliment or insult, no 'parang' or 'tulad ng' to soften the blow. In short, it's direct to the point, like your friend telling you, "Bes, isa kang alamat."
usage_notes: A key literary device taught in Filipino class. The opposite of simile (pagtutulad).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang \"Siya ay isang halimaw sa galit\" ay halimbawa ng **pagwawangis**.","translation":"\"He is a monster in anger\" is an example of a **metaphor**."},{"sentence":"Mahusay ang makata sa paggamit ng **pagwawangis** upang ipahayag ang kanyang damdamin.","translation":"The poet is skilled in using **metaphor** to express his feelings."}]

meaning_filipino: Magtanong nang masinsinan at detalyado upang malaman ang katotohanan; siyasatin.
original_explanation: This is what your Tita does at family reunions. She'll usisain you about your love life, your salary, your weight... everything. It's like being in a friendly but very thorough police interrogation.
usage_notes: Implies a more detailed and persistent line of questioning than simply 'tanungin' (to ask).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **usisain** tungkol sa personal kong buhay.","translation":"Don't **question me closely** about my personal life."},{"sentence":"Nais ng imbestigador na **usisain** ang bawat testigo sa kaso.","translation":"The investigator wants to **inquire** with every witness in the case."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng paghingi ng bayad para sa isang utang, serbisyo, o obligasyon.
etymology: From pan- + singil, with reduplication of the first syllable of the root word.
original_explanation: That dreaded moment when your friend who treated you to milk tea last week suddenly messages "uy, friend..." Or when the landlord knocks on your door on the 15th of the month. It's the act of collecting what's due, whether it's money, a promise, or an explanation for why they left you on read.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of debt, bills, rent, or any form of payment collection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **paniningil** ng buwis ngayong taon.","translation":"The **collection** of taxes is strict this year."},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap ako ng text para sa **paniningil** ng aking credit card.","translation":"I received a text for the **billing** of my credit card."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit at malambot na tinapay na may katangi-tanging hugis na parang sumbrero o takip.
etymology: From Spanish 'bonete' (a type of clerical cap), referring to its shape.
original_explanation: Not the hat, but the bread! It's that classic, slightly sweet, soft bread roll from the *panaderia* that looks like a little chef's hat or a mushroom cap. Perfect for dipping in coffee. It's the less famous but equally delicious cousin of *pandesal*.
usage_notes: A common item in local bakeries (panaderia).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng sampung pisong **bonete**.","translation":"Please give me ten pesos worth of **bonete**."},{"sentence":"Masarap isawsaw sa kape ang mainit na **bonete**.","translation":"It's delicious to dip a warm **bonete** in coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit sa isang bagay, tulad ng oras, pera, o pagkain, sa paraang hindi kapaki-pakinabang, walang katuturan, o sobra-sobra.
etymology: Hango sa salitang Sanskrit na "kṣaya" na nangangahulugang pagkasira o pagkawala.
original_explanation: This is your mom's ultimate enemy. It's ordering too much food you can't finish, buying another pair of shoes you don't need with your 13th-month pay, or spending hours scrolling on social media instead of working. In short, it's the 'sayang' culture personified.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa pagwawaldas ng yaman tulad ng oras, pera, pagkain, o pagsisikap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-aaksaya** ng pagkain ay isang malaking problema sa buong mundo.","translation":"The **waste** of food is a huge problem worldwide."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **pag-aaksaya** ng oras sa mga bagay na hindi mahalaga.","translation":"Stop the **wasting** of time on things that are not important."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng mga bagay o tao sa lahat ng dako ng isang lugar o bagay; pagkulong o pagpuno sa paligid.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'pa-' (nagpapahiwatig ng pagpapagawa), salitang-ugat na 'libot' (umikot, gumala), at hulaping '-in' (tumuon sa layon).
original_explanation: Parang chismis tungkol sa'yo sa office, kumakalat hanggang sa ma-realize mong napapalibutan ka na. Or 'yung mga aso ng kapitbahay na biglang nag-aabang sa'yo 'pag may dala kang pagkain. The act of making something go all the way around something else.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pag-uutos o pakiusap na paligiran ang isang bagay o lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Palibutin** ninyo ng bakod ang buong lupain.","translation":"**Surround** the entire land with a fence."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating hayaang **palibutin** tayo ng mga negatibong isipin.","translation":"Let's not let negative thoughts **surround** us."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kagamitang nabibitbit na lumilikha ng apoy, karaniwang ginagamit sa pagsindi ng sigarilyo o kandila.
original_explanation: The most-borrowed item in any inuman session. "Pahiram ng layter!" is a national catchphrase. It's that magical device that disappears from your pocket and reappears in your friend's. Essential for birthdays (for the cake), for smokers, and for when the power goes out and you need to find the candles.
usage_notes: Spelled phonetically. The English spelling "lighter" is also commonly used in written text.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala na naman ang **layter** ko, sigurado akong may kumuha na naman.","translation":"My **lighter** is missing again, I'm sure someone took it again."},{"sentence":"May **layter** ka ba? Magsisindi lang ako ng kandila.","translation":"Do you have a **lighter**? I'll just light a candle."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahilig na bahagi ng lupa, tulad ng gilid ng isang burol, bundok, o anumang mataas na lugar.
original_explanation: That part of the mountain hike where you're questioning all your life choices. It's not flat, it's not a cliff, it's that "Aray ko, tuhod ko!" angle. Perfect for when you want to roll down dramatically after a "major tampo" moment.
usage_notes: Can also refer to a gentle downward flow of water.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat siyang bumaba sa matarik na **dalisdis** ng bundok.","translation":"He carefully descended the steep **slope** of the mountain."},{"sentence":"May maliit na batis na umaagos sa **dalisdis**.","translation":"There is a small stream flowing down the **incline**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang paggalang na tumutukoy sa lolo, partikular sa mga pamilyang may lahing Tsino.
original_explanation: This is what you call your lolo if your family owns a hardware store or a restaurant that has been around for generations. 'Ingkong' is the patriarch, the OG, the one who gives out the thickest ang pao on Chinese New Year. He's got stories for days and probably knows the secret to making the best siopao in town.
usage_notes: A term of respect and endearment specific to Chinese-Filipino culture. Often paired with 'Amah' (grandmother).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang bilin ni **Ingkong** na mag-aral kami nang mabuti.","translation":"**Grandfather**'s strict instruction was for us to study well."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng matinding inggit o pananaghili sa tagumpay, pag-aari, o katangian ng ibang tao.
etymology: From `pang-` + `imbulo` (envy), a less common word than 'inggit'.
original_explanation: This is the "Sana all" feeling turned dark. It's when you see your friend's travel pics on IG and you're stuck in traffic on EDSA, and a small, bitter part of you whispers, "Bakit siya, hindi ako?" It's the low-key resentment you feel when your officemate gets promoted and you don't. The root of many a teleserye kontrabida's motivation.
usage_notes: A more formal and intense word for 'inggit' (envy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pangingimbulo** ay maaaring sumira ng pagkakaibigan.","translation":"**Envy** can destroy friendships."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pangingimbulo**, siniraan niya ang kanyang katrabaho.","translation":"Because of **jealousy**, she slandered her coworker."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagtukoy sa bigat ng isang bagay gamit ang timbangan; paglalagay sa isang estado ng pagkakapantay o balanse.
original_explanation: Kapag hindi ka sigurado kung mas matimbang ba ang feelings mo o ang utang mo sa credit card, kailangan mong i-check. You have to weigh your priorities. 'Yan ang pag-itimbang sa buhay. It's about figuring out what carries more weight, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal weighing on a scale or metaphorical balancing of options, ideas, or feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itimbang** mo muna ang bigas bago natin isalin sa sako.","translation":"**Weigh** the rice first before we transfer it to the sack."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **itimbang** ang mga kalamangan at kawalan bago magdesisyon.","translation":"One must **balance** the pros and cons before making a decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay na may kaugnayan, para sa, o ginagamit ng hukbo o sandatahang lakas.
original_explanation: Anything that screams "Descendants of the Sun" vibes. Camouflage pants, combat boots, military-grade equipment, or even the strict discipline your dad imposes. If it's for or related to the army, it's panghukbo. Parang 'yung haircut mo na "flat top," panghukbo 'yan!
usage_notes: Used to describe things related to the military or army.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga sasakyang **panghukbo** ay dumaan sa EDSA para sa parada.","translation":"The **military** vehicles passed through EDSA for the parade."},{"sentence":"Sumailalim siya sa pagsasanay na **panghukbo**.","translation":"He underwent **military** training."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa posisyong nakabaluktot ang katawan paabante habang ang puwitan ay nakaturo paitaas o palabas.
original_explanation: The official pose when you drop your phone under the car seat and have to fish it out. Also, a classic comedy trope in Filipino movies, usually followed by someone accidentally bumping into them. Not to be confused with a proper deadlift form.
usage_notes: Often used humorously or to describe a vulnerable or awkward position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tawa kami nang tawa sa pusa na **nakatuwad** habang umiinom sa gripo.","translation":"We were laughing so hard at the cat that was **bent over** while drinking from the faucet."},{"sentence":"Nahirapan siyang kunin ang barya dahil **nakatuwad** siya sa ilalim ng mesa.","translation":"He had a hard time getting the coin because he was **bent over** under the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagliligtas o sumasagip sa iba mula sa panganib, kapahamakan, o kasalanan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "tagapag-" (doer/agent of action) at sa salitang ugat na "ligtas" (safe).
original_explanation: That friend who arrives with a car when you're stranded in the rain. The BPO agent who finally fixes your internet connection at 2 AM. Or, on a grander scale, the hero of the story, like Darna or Captain Barbell. The ultimate 'sana all.'
usage_notes: May malakas na konotasyong relihiyoso (hal. Hesukristo bilang Tagapagligtas) at heroiko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa mga biktima ng baha, ang mga sundalo ang kanilang mga **tagapagligtas**.","translation":"For the flood victims, the soldiers were their **rescuers**."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing ng marami si Hesus bilang **Tagapagligtas** ng sanlibutan.","translation":"Many consider Jesus as the **Savior** of the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lupon o pangkat ng mga tao na nagtitipon upang magbigay ng payo, magpasya, o mamahala.
original_explanation: This is the 'board meeting' of your local government. The Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) is where future trapos are born, and the Sangguniang Panlungsod is where ordinances get debated forever. Think of it as the official group chat for making community decisions.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of Philippine government bodies like Sangguniang Panlalawigan (Provincial Board) or Sangguniang Barangay (Village Council). The verb form is 'sumangguni' (to consult).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpulong ang **sangguni** upang talakayin ang bagong ordinansa.","translation":"The **council** met to discuss the new ordinance."},{"sentence":"Mahalagang sumangguni sa mga eksperto bago magdesisyon.","translation":"It's important to consult experts before making a decision."}]

translation: to give honor to; to dignify
meaning_filipino: Magkaloob ng karangalan, respeto, o pagkilala sa isang tao, bagay, o kaganapan.
original_explanation: This is the act of putting someone or something on a pedestal, in a good way. It's like giving a standing ovation, awarding a medal, or simply acknowledging someone's hard work. It's the opposite of "cancel culture." It's giving credit where credit is due and elevating something to a place of respect.
usage_notes: Used in formal settings, ceremonies, or when discussing respect and reputation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang parangal ay isang paraan upang **bigyang-dangal** ang mga natatanging Pilipino.","translation":"The award is a way to **give honor to** the outstanding Filipinos."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **bigyang-dangal** ang ating pambansang watawat.","translation":"We must **dignify** our national flag."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng tulong, suporta, o gabay sa isang tao upang hindi ito matumba, masaktan, o magkamali.
original_explanation: To be the designated human 'crutch' for your friend who's had one too many San Migs. It's being the supportive BFF who holds their hair back, or the QA who assists a new agent on their first call. To give support, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Infinitive/past tense. Present: 'umaalalay'. Future: 'aalalay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **umalalay** sa matanda habang tumatawid ito ng kalsada.","translation":"He was the one who **assisted** the old person while crossing the street."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **umalalay** sa iyong kaibigan sa panahong ito ng pagsubok.","translation":"You need to **support** your friend during this trying time."}]

translation: to report news; to spread news
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-uulat o paghahatid ng balita sa iba, pormal man o hindi.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung trabaho ng mga Marites at Tolits sa kanto. Bago pa man lumabas sa TV Patrol, alam na nila 'yung chismis. Sila 'yung unofficial news bureau ng barangay. 'Hoy, narinig mo na ba? Si ano...' 'Yan, mamalita na 'yan.
usage_notes: Can be used for formal news reporting (by a journalist) or informal gossiping. The prefix 'mamaN-' indicates a habitual or professional action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga reporter ay laging handang **mamalita** anuman ang panahon.","translation":"Reporters are always ready **to report the news** whatever the weather."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mamalita** ng mga pangyayari sa aming opisina.","translation":"She loves **to spread news** about the happenings in our office."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nililikha ng aso, karaniwang bilang babala, pagbati, o pagpapahayag ng damdamin.
original_explanation: It's the sound your neighbor's dog makes at 3 AM that makes you question your life choices. It's the dog's version of "Sino ka diyan?!" or "Uy, may Shopee delivery!"
usage_notes: "Tahol" is specifically for dogs. Other animals have different terms for their sounds (e.g., "ngiyaw" for cats, "huni" for birds). The verb form is "tumahol".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lakas ng **tahol** ng aso sa labas.","translation":"The dog's **bark** outside is so loud."},{"sentence":"Isang **tahol** lang mula kay Bantay, alam na naming may tao.","translation":"Just one **bark** from Bantay, and we know someone's there."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tunog na napakataas, matinis, at kung minsan ay hindi kaaya-aya sa pandinig.
original_explanation: The sound of your alarm clock that you want to throw against the wall. The sound of chalk screeching on a blackboard. The sound of your Tita screaming your name from across the mall. That's 'matin-is.' It's the audio equivalent of a needle prick.
usage_notes: Describes sounds, particularly voices or noises that are unpleasantly high. The more common spelling is 'matinis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **matin-is** na boses kapag kumakanta ng matataas na nota.","translation":"She has a **high-pitched** voice when singing high notes."},{"sentence":"Nakakabingi ang **matin-is** na tunog ng pito ng pulis.","translation":"The **shrill** sound of the police whistle is deafening."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-iibayo ng lakas, puwersa, o sigla; ang pagbuti ng kalagayan mula sa sakit.
original_explanation: This is your glow-up moment. The paglakas of your WiFi signal after moving the router. The paglakas of your confidence after a new haircut. The paglakas of the rain right after you've washed your clothes. It's anything getting stronger, louder, or better—from your health to the typhoon signal.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical strength, health recovery, or the intensification of a phenomenon like a storm or a sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglakas** ng ulan ang naging sanhi ng baha.","translation":"The **intensification** of the rain caused the flood."},{"sentence":"Ikinatuwa ng pamilya ang mabilis na **paglakas** ng kanilang lola mula sa sakit.","translation":"The family was happy with their grandmother's quick **recovery** from her illness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pagiging maruming-marumi, madungis, at puno ng pinaghalong dumi at pawis.
original_explanation: That feeling after a whole day of commuting via jeep, MRT, and tricycle, with extra pollution and sweat. It’s beyond just 'marumi'; it's a level of dirtiness that makes you want to jump into a drum of alcohol. The state of your white uniform after a rainy day playing patintero.
usage_notes: Describes a person or object covered in a layer of grime and sweat. More intense than 'marumi' or 'madungis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umuwi siyang **limahid** sa dumi pagkatapos maglaro ng putik.","translation":"He came home **grimy** with dirt after playing in the mud."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang hahawak sa akin, **limahid** ang mga kamay ko.","translation":"Don't touch me, my hands are **filthy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga butil ng kanin na natira at dumikit sa palayok; mga maliliit na bagay o mumo na walang gaanong halaga.
original_explanation: This is the original 'sana all' for ants. Yung mga tutong o kanin na naiwan sa kaldero after everyone has eaten. It can also refer to any tiny, insignificant crumb or particle, like the 'mumo' from your Choc-Nut that gets everywhere.
usage_notes: Not as common as 'tutong' for burnt rice, but 'mismis' can refer to any leftover grains, burnt or not. It's also used metaphorically for small, insignificant things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinayod niya ang mga **mismis** sa kaldero para ipakain sa manok.","translation":"She scraped the **leftover rice grains** from the pot to feed the chickens."},{"sentence":"Wala nang natira kundi mga **mismis** ng tinapay sa mesa.","translation":"Nothing was left but bread **crumbs** on the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Pilit na kumawala o makalaya mula sa isang pagkakagapos, pagkakakulong, o anumang sitwasyong naghihigpit.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `um` (infinitive infix) + `alpas` (to break loose). The combination emphasizes the effort.
original_explanation: That feeling when you finally log off after a 12-hour shift. It's what your inner self wants to do when stuck in a toxic relationship or a dead-end job. It's the ultimate 'suko na ako, bahala na si Batman' moment, but with more action and less resignation.
usage_notes: Often used in a literary or dramatic context to describe a forceful struggle for freedom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng bilanggo na **mag-umalpas** mula sa kanyang selda.","translation":"The prisoner tried to **break free** from his cell."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **mag-umalpas** sa mahigpit na pagbabantay ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"She wanted to **break free** from her parents' strict supervision."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinuno ng isang kolehiyo o kagawaran sa isang unibersidad o pamantasan.
original_explanation: Siya yung "final boss" ng college department mo. Kung may reklamo ka na hindi na kaya ng prof mo, sa kanya ang punta mo. Sila yung nag-aapruba ng lahat, mula sa curriculum hanggang sa suspension. 'Pag pinatawag ka sa office ng dekano, either sobrang galing mo o may nagawa kang kalokohan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinausap ng mga mag-aaral ang **dekano** ng kanilang kolehiyo tungkol sa mga isyu sa pasilidad.","translation":"The students spoke with the **dean** of their college about issues with the facilities."},{"sentence":"Pinarangalan ang aming **dekano** dahil sa kanyang mahusay na pamumuno.","translation":"Our **dean** was honored for his excellent leadership."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagsasalita, hindi gumagalaw, o hindi tumutugon.
etymology: From `di-` (not) + `kumikibo` (present progressive form of kibo, 'to speak or react').
original_explanation: That moment when you ask your friend "Galit ka ba?" and they just stare blankly into the distance. That's the "di-kumikibo" stage of tampo. It’s the ultimate silent treatment. Also applies to your laptop when it freezes.
usage_notes: Describes a state of silence or inaction, often implying something is wrong, someone is upset, or a device is malfunctioning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kanina pa siyang **di-kumikibo** sa isang sulok.","translation":"He's been **unresponsive** in a corner for a while now."},{"sentence":"Bakit **di-kumikibo** ang kompyuter ko?","translation":"Why is my computer **not responding**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang asosasyon o network ng mga negosyante na itinatag upang itaguyod at protektahan ang mga interes ng mga miyembro nito sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: This is the official 'tropa' of the business world. It's where the big bosses, entrepreneurs, and company owners hang out to network, lobby the government, and basically make sure business is booming. Think of it as a barkada for businesses.
usage_notes: A formal term used in business and economic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpulong ang mga miyembro ng **Kamara-de-Komersiyo** upang talakayin ang epekto ng bagong buwis.","translation":"The members of the **Chamber of Commerce** met to discuss the effect of the new tax."},{"sentence":"Ang Philippine **Kamara-de-Komersiyo** ay naglabas ng pahayag tungkol sa ekonomiya.","translation":"The Philippine **Chamber of Commerce** released a statement about the economy."}]

translation: to bristle, for hair to stand on end
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagtayo ng mga buhok o balahibo sa katawan dahil sa takot, lamig, o matinding damdamin.
etymology: From 'mang-' and the root 'kislig'. The root itself is rarely used but is related to the concept of standing stiffly.
original_explanation: This is your body's built-in horror movie detector. That feeling when you're alone at night and hear a 'psst' from a dark corner? Your balahibo will **mangislig**. It's the physical manifestation of 'kinilabutan,' when your hair follicles collectively decide to stand up in protest or terror.
usage_notes: Almost always used in the phrase 'mangislig ang balahibo' (for hair to bristle). It is a more literary or dramatic synonym for 'manindig ang balahibo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nangislig** ang aking mga balahibo nang may marinig akong umiiyak sa lumang bahay.","translation":"My hair **bristled** when I heard someone crying in the old house."},{"sentence":"Sa tuwing napapanood ko ang eksenang iyon, **nangingislig** pa rin ako sa takot.","translation":"Every time I watch that scene, I still get goosebumps (**my hair still bristles**) from fear."}]

translation: to throw away (as trash); to discard
meaning_filipino: Itapon ang isang bagay dahil ito ay itinuturing na basura o wala nang halaga.
original_explanation: The act of getting rid of something, whether it's actual garbage, your ex's old love letters, or a project proposal that got rejected for the 5th time. It's the ultimate act of 'decluttering'—physically, emotionally, or professionally. 'Huwag mo akong magbasura!' is a hugot line for 'Don't treat me like I'm disposable!'
usage_notes: Can be used literally for trash, or figuratively for discarding ideas, feelings, or people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**magbasura** naman ng mga lumang diyaryo sa bodega.","translation":"Please **throw away** the old newspapers in the storage room."},{"sentence":"Matapos ang lahat, ganun na lang kadali para sa kanya na **magbasura** ng aming pinagsamahan.","translation":"After everything, it was so easy for him/her to just **discard** what we had."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa musika, ang interbal sa pagitan ng isang nota at isa pang nota na may kalahati o doble ng dalas nito. Ito rin ay tumutukoy sa isang serye ng walong nota.
original_explanation: 'Yung range ng boses mo sa videoke, mula sa pinakamababa hanggang sa 'My Way' na high note na halos ikamatay mo na. Kung kaya mo 'yung isang buong oktaba nang hindi sintunado, pwede ka nang mag-audition sa The Voice.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga usaping pang-musika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahanga-hanga ang abilidad niyang umabot ng tatlong **oktaba**.","translation":"Her ability to reach three **octaves** is amazing."},{"sentence":"Ituro mo sa akin ang mga nota sa loob ng isang **oktaba** sa piyano.","translation":"Teach me the notes within one **octave** on the piano."}]

translation: to press against; to stuff into; to shove in one's face
meaning_filipino: Ang mariing pagdiin, pagsiksik, o pagdikit ng isang bagay sa isa pa.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa pandesal para isawsaw sa kape. O 'yung pag pinipilit mong isaksak 'yung charger sa saksakan. Pwede ring ipamukha: 'Huwag mong iduldol sa akin ang pagkakamali ko!' It has that forceful 'shove it in' energy.
usage_notes: May diin sa pwersa. Maaaring gamitin sa literal na paraan para sa mga bagay, o sa makasagisag na paraan para sa mga ideya, kasalanan, o sisi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **iduldol** ang daliri mo sa cake!","translation":"Don't **press** your finger into the cake!"},{"sentence":"Lagi na lang niyang **idinuduldol** sa akin na kasalanan ko ang lahat.","translation":"He always **shoves it in my face** that everything is my fault."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagdurog o paggiling ng pagkain sa bibig gamit ang mga ngipin bilang paghahanda sa paglunok.
original_explanation: Step one of eating. It's what your mom tells you to do properly: "Nguyaing mabuti ang pagkain!" (Chew your food well!). This is the action that turns a lechon kawali into something swallowable. Also, what you do to bubblegum to annoy your teacher.
usage_notes: A basic and essential verb related to eating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masama sa tiyan ang hindi **magnguya** nang maayos ng pagkain.","translation":"It's bad for the stomach not **to chew** food properly."},{"sentence":"Hilig niyang **magnguya** ng chewing gum pagkatapos kumain.","translation":"He likes **to chew** chewing gum after eating."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-udyok o pag-atas sa isang tao na magsalita o magpahayag ng kanyang saloobin.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa ng teacher sa class-recitation sa tahimik mong kaklase. O kaya yung ginagawa ng chismosa mong tita sa family reunion para umamin ka kung may jowa ka na. 'Pilit siyang pinagsasalita ng mga pulis.' It's about compelling or giving someone the floor to talk.
usage_notes: The focus is on causing the action of speaking in another person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **pagsalitain** ang testigo ngunit ayaw nitong magbigay ng pahayag.","translation":"They tried **to make** the witness **speak** but he refused to give a statement."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **pagsalitain** ang bata tungkol sa nangyari.","translation":"Let the child **be made to speak** about what happened."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang talunin o lupigin sa anumang laban, tunggalian, o pagsubok.
etymology: From 'di-' (not) + 'ma-' (ability prefix) + future tense 'gagapi' from the root 'gapi' (to defeat, to conquer).
original_explanation: This is how you feel after drinking three cups of coffee and finishing a week's worth of work in one night. You are a force of nature, an unstoppable BPO agent, simply di-magagapi. Also, the fighting spirit of every Pinoy supporting Manny Pacquiao.
usage_notes: A strong, often epic or heroic term used to describe something undefeatable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala sila na ang kanilang koponan ay **di-magagapi** ngayong season.","translation":"They believe their team is **invincible** this season."},{"sentence":"Ang diwa ng pagkakaisa ng mga Pilipino ay isang lakas na **di-magagapi**.","translation":"The Filipino spirit of unity is an **unconquerable** force."}]

translation: to leave (angrily), to run away, to scram
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at madalas ay galit na pag-alis sa isang lugar; pagtakas o paglayo nang walang paalam.
etymology: From the root word 'layas' (roaming, vagrant) + the '-um-' infix.
original_explanation: The ultimate "I'm out!" move. This isn't just leaving; this is leaving with *drama*. It's what a teenager threatens to do when grounded, or what you tell a cockroach in your room: "Lumayas ka!" It's a departure with an attitude. Scram! Get lost!
usage_notes: Has a strong, negative, and often dismissive or angry connotation. It's not a neutral "to leave" ('umalis').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagalit ang nanay at sinabihan ang pusang-gala na '**lumayas**!'","translation":"The mother got angry and told the stray cat to '**scram**!'"},{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding away, nag-empake siya at **lumayas** ng bahay.","translation":"Because of a huge fight, he packed his bags and **ran away** from home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nahihiya o nag-aatubiling ipahayag ang kanyang romantikong damdamin sa taong kanyang nagugustuhan.
etymology: From Spanish 'torpe' meaning clumsy, awkward, or dull.
original_explanation: The classic Pinoy term for a guy (or girl!) who's too shy to make a move on their crush. They'll write poems, stalk social media, and move mountains in their head, but can't even say 'hi' in person. The opposite of 'diskarte'.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of courtship and romance. Can also function as a noun to refer to the person ('Isang torpe si Juan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang maging **torpe**, aminin mo na ang nararamdaman mo.","translation":"Don't be **romantically shy** anymore, just admit what you feel."},{"sentence":"Ang kaibigan ko ay isang **torpe**; isang taon na siyang may gusto sa'yo pero hindi makapagsalita.","translation":"My friend is a **shy suitor**; he's liked you for a year but can't say a word."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga produkto o kalakal na itinitinda o ipinagbibili.
original_explanation: Basically, the stuff you sell. Your paninda. This is the word your lola might use for the items in her sari-sari store or the things being sold in Divisoria. It sounds more formal and grand than just 'tinda'.
usage_notes: A somewhat dated or formal term. 'Paninda' or 'produkto' are more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bagong **merkansia** ang dumating sa bodega.","translation":"A lot of new **merchandise** arrived at the warehouse."},{"sentence":"Inilabas ng tindera ang kanyang mga **merkansia** sa palengke.","translation":"The vendor displayed her **wares** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, tao, o kultura na nagmula o may kaugnayan sa Silangan, partikular sa Asya.
original_explanation: The formal, slightly old-school way to say something is "from the East" or "Asian-style." Think "Silanganang Mindoro" (Oriental Mindoro). It's the adjective version of 'silangan' when you're talking about places and people, not just where the sun pops up.
usage_notes: Often capitalized when referring to specific geographic or political regions like 'Silanganang Mindoro'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Silanganang** Mindoro ay kilala sa magagandang dalampasigan.","translation":"**Oriental** Mindoro is known for its beautiful beaches."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan niya ang kulturang **Silanganan**.","translation":"He is studying **Oriental** culture."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon na mayroong banta ng pinsala, kapahamakan, o anumang masamang maaaring mangyari.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when your mom calls you by your full name. It's that 'uh-oh' moment, the red flag, the final boss music starting to play. Whether it's walking alone at night in a dark alley or submitting a project one minute before the deadline, `peligro` is what makes your life insurance agent nod knowingly.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'panganib' (the native Tagalog term) and 'delikado' (adjective form).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang lumabas nang mag-isa sa gabi, puno ng **peligro** sa daan.","translation":"Don't go out alone at night, the road is full of **danger**."},{"sentence":"Inilagay mo sa **peligro** ang iyong buhay para sa kanya.","translation":"You put your life in **danger** for him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak at bukas na lupain, karaniwang natatamnan ng damo at walang gaanong puno.
original_explanation: That wide-open space you see in pre-nup shoots. It's not a bukid (farm), not a gubat (forest), but a big, grassy area perfect for running dramatically towards your love interest, ala-90s movie.
usage_notes: Refers to a large, open field, often uncultivated. It's a more expansive version of 'parang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtakbuhan ang mga bata sa malawak na **kaparangan**.","translation":"The children ran around in the vast **field**."},{"sentence":"Isang munting kubo lamang ang nakatayo sa gitna ng **kaparangan**.","translation":"Only a small hut stood in the middle of the **prairie**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng kahihiyan sa isang tao; ang pagpaparamdam sa iba na sila ay mababa o kahiya-hiya.
original_explanation: This is that feeling when your mom shouts your full name in the middle of SM, or when your Tita asks "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?" in front of everyone at the family reunion. It's public shaming, Pinoy-style. It can be intentional (like a boss reprimanding you in a meeting) or unintentional (like your baby picture being used as a meme). The result is the same: you wish the ground would swallow you whole.
usage_notes: The noun form of the verb "manghiya" (to shame someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang panunukso at **paghiya** sa kapwa ay isang uri ng pambu-bully.","translation":"Teasing and **shaming** others is a form of bullying."},{"sentence":"Tumigil ka sa **paghiya** mo sa akin sa harap ng mga kaibigan ko.","translation":"Stop your **humiliation** of me in front of my friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking sisidlan, karaniwang yari sa sako para sa mga butil tulad ng bigas, o yari sa kahoy bilang baul para sa mga damit at mahahalagang gamit.
original_explanation: Think of it as the ultimate Filipino storage solution. Before Dropbox and Google Drive, there was the 'kaban ng bigas' in the kitchen and the 'kaban ng yaman' (a chest of treasures) that lola keeps her old photos and alahas in. It's a unit of survival and memory.
usage_notes: 'Isang kaban' is a standard unit for a large sack of rice, traditionally 50kg.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang **kaban** ng bigas para sa buong buwan.","translation":"Mother bought a **sack** of rice for the whole month."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng napakaliit na organismong may iisang selula (protozoan) na karaniwang matatagpuan sa tubig-tabang, at may hugis na parang tsinelas.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "paramecium," na mula sa Bagong Latin na "Paramecium," at sa Griyegong "paramēkēs" (oblong).
original_explanation: Remember that weird slipper-shaped blob you had to draw in high school biology? 'Yun 'yon. The OG single-celled organism that's probably living its best life in your water bottle if you don't wash it enough.
usage_notes: Isang terminong siyentipiko na ginagamit sa biyolohiya at mga kaugnay na larangan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan namin ang galaw ng **paramisiyum** sa ilalim ng mikroskopyo.","translation":"We studied the movement of the **paramecium** under the microscope."},{"sentence":"Ang **paramisiyum** ay isang halimbawa ng isang protozoan.","translation":"The **paramecium** is an example of a protozoan."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging lasing o nasa ilalim ng impluwensya ng alkohol o ipinagbabawal na gamot. Ito ay isang balbal na salita.
etymology: From the inverted form of the Tagalog word "tama" (hit, effect, correct).
original_explanation: Galing sa "tama" na binaliktad. 'Pag may amats ka, 'yun 'yung feeling na lumilipad ka na kahit nakaupo ka lang, o bigla kang nagiging super friendly sa lahat ng tao sa party. Parang 'yung friend mong biglang nag-English with an accent after two bottles of beer. "May tama na."
usage_notes: A slang term, very common in informal conversations, especially among younger people. The root 'tama' in this context means the 'effect' or 'hit' of a substance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe na ang **amats** ko kagabi, kung anu-ano na ang nasabi ko.","translation":"I was so **drunk** last night, I said a lot of nonsensical things."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magmaneho kung may **amats** ka pa.","translation":"Don't drive if you're still **tipsy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsisimula, paglulunsad, o pag-udyok sa isang gawain, proyekto, o kilusan.
original_explanation: This is the 'grand launch' button. It's what happens when a new product drops, a new program is started, or a new kilig serye begins. It's the official push, the 'Let's get this party started!' moment. Think of it as the opposite of procrastination; it's the act of actually starting something.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of projects, campaigns, or formal beginnings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbubunsod** ng bagong programa sa kalusugan ay pinangunahan ng DOH.","translation":"The **launching** of the new health program was led by the DOH."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang epekto ng **pagbubunsod** ng community pantry sa maraming komunidad.","translation":"The **initiation** of the community pantry had a big effect on many communities."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, gawain, o pagkain na naglalayong magdulot ng liksi o bilis sa pagkilos.
original_explanation: Think of it as your real-life 'power-up' or 'buff.' 'Yung energy drink bago ka mag-basketball, 'yung stretching exercises mo bago ka humabol sa jeep, o 'yung kape para bumilis ang isip mo sa work. It's your cheat code for agility.
usage_notes: Can refer to food, drink, exercise, or even a metaphorical boost.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang saging daw ay mabisang **pampaliksi** ng katawan.","translation":"They say bananas are effective for **making the body agile**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng kape bilang **pampaliksi** ng utak.","translation":"I need coffee as something to **quicken** my brain."}]

meaning_filipino: Umawit para sa isang partikular na tao; ialay ang isang awit sa isang tao.
original_explanation: The verb form of a "harana" or a karaoke dedication. Hindi lang basta "kumanta," kundi may pinaglalaanan ka ng kanta. 'Yung tipong, "This song is for you," sabay titig sa crush mo. "Gusto sana kitang ipagkanta pero sintunado ako, kaya idaan na lang natin sa Spotify playlist."
usage_notes: A beneficiary-focused verb. The act of singing is done *for* someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kitang **ipagkanta** sa kaarawan mo.","translation":"I want to **sing for you** on your birthday."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **ipagkakanta** mo sa videoke mamaya?","translation":"Who will you be **singing for** at the videoke later?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang araw ng taon, ang Enero 1; ang pagdiriwang ng pagsalubong sa isang bagong taon.
original_explanation: The one night a year when it's totally acceptable to make a lot of noise with torotot and firecrackers to 'drive away evil spirits' (or just to annoy your neighbors). It's the season of Media Noche, 12 round fruits, polka dots, and 'New Year, New Me' posts that last for about a week.
usage_notes: Commonly written as two words, 'Bagong Taon'. The single-word form 'bagongtaon' is less common but understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Manigong **Bagong Taon** sa inyong lahat!","translation":"Happy **New Year** to you all!"}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng paso o pagkasunog dahil sa matinding init.
etymology: From naka- (causative prefix) + reduplication of first syllable of root pa- + paso (burn, scald).
original_explanation: 'Yung unang higop mo sa bagong timplang kape o sa sabaw ng bulalo. Also, 'yung tingin sa'yo ng boss mo after mo mag-file ng vacation leave sa pinaka-busy na week. It can be a literal or figurative burn.
usage_notes: Describes something hot enough to cause a burn.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, **nakapapaso** ang sabaw ng sinigang.","translation":"Be careful, the soup of the sinigang is **scalding**."},{"sentence":"Ang langis na kumukulo ay **nakapapaso**.","translation":"The boiling oil is **burning** hot."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing lugar ng pagdalo o pagpunta ng mga tao para sa isang okasyon; utos na dumalo.
original_explanation: Like when your crush's party is happening and your friend says, "Go na! Padaluhan mo na para makita mo siya!" It's telling someone to grace an event with their presence. The venue is *to be attended*.
usage_notes: Often used in the imperative mood, instructing or requesting someone to attend an event. The 'pa-' prefix indicates causation, and '-an' suffix indicates the location/recipient of the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Padaluhan** mo naman ang pulong mamaya para may kinatawan ang ating grupo.","translation":"Please **attend** the meeting later so our group has a representative."}]

translation: to wear a suit; to wear formal attire
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsuot ng pormal na kasuotan, karaniwang tumutukoy sa trahe de boda (wedding suit) o anumang pormal na damit para sa isang okasyon.
original_explanation: To suit up! It's what you do for a job interview, a wedding, or a very fancy date. That feeling of putting on a suit and suddenly feeling like a corporate boss or a secret agent. "Kailangan kong mag-gym, hindi na kasya ang ipapang-**magtrahe** ko sa kasal."
usage_notes: Often implies wearing a full suit (trahe de boda), but can be used for other formal wear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ng mga lalaki ay kailangang **magtrahe** para sa kasal.","translation":"All the men need to **wear a suit** for the wedding."},{"sentence":"Bihira lang siyang **magtrahe** dahil mas komportable siya sa simpleng damit.","translation":"He rarely **wears formal attire** because he's more comfortable in simple clothes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may interes, pagnanais, o pakikilahok sa isang partikular na bagay, usapin, o gawain.
original_explanation: In a meeting, this is the person who's actually listening, not just waiting for the free coffee. They're the ones who ask questions, join the bidding, or slide into your DMs because they're genuinely curious about your 'How to bake ube cheese pandesal' online course. They're the 'target audience' you're looking for.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at direktang termino na ginagamit sa negosyo, legal, o pangkalahatang konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon bang **taong interesado** na bumili nitong lumang sasakyan?","translation":"Is there an **interested person** who wants to buy this old car?"},{"sentence":"Lahat ng **taong interesado** ay inaanyayahang dumalo sa pulong mamayang hapon.","translation":"All **interested persons** are invited to attend the meeting this afternoon."}]

translation: to be startled; to be shocked
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang biglaang pagkagulat, pagkabigla, o pagkatakot dahil sa isang hindi inaasahang pangyayari, tunog, o kilos.
original_explanation: This is your reaction when someone jumps out from behind a door to scare you. It's that mini heart attack you get when your phone, on silent, suddenly rings at full volume. Yung "Ay, kabayo!" moment mo. That's `magitla`.
usage_notes: `Magitla` is an intransitive verb, often used with the actor-focus prefix `ma-`. The root `gitla` means shock or startle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, baka **magitla** ang natutulog na sanggol.","translation":"Don't be noisy, you might **startle** the sleeping baby."},{"sentence":"Ako ay **nagitla** nang biglang may kumalampag sa bintana.","translation":"I **was startled** when something suddenly banged on the window."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang karne o laman na mula sa baboy, isa sa pinakakaraniwang uri ng karne na kinokonsumo sa Pilipinas.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "carne" (karne) at Tagalog na "baboy" (pig).
original_explanation: The undisputed king of Filipino cuisine. From adobo to sinigang to lechon, pork is the star player. It's the "bida" in every handaan. If Filipino food was the Avengers, pork would be Iron Man – versatile, popular, and the heart of the team.
usage_notes: Ang "-ng" ay isang pang-ugnay (linker) na nagdudugtong sa "karne" at "baboy".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang kilong **karneng-baboy** para sa sinigang.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of **pork** for the sinigang."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang **karneng-baboy** sa adobo kaysa manok.","translation":"I prefer **pork** in adobo over chicken."}]

translation: to argue, to debate, to quarrel
meaning_filipino: Magpalitan ng magkasalungat na kuro-kuro o opinyon, na maaaring humantong sa hindi pagkakasundo.
original_explanation: The national pastime during family reunions, especially when politics or the latest showbiz chismis is brought up. It can be a friendly debate over who makes the best adobo, or a full-blown argument that ends with someone walking out. Also what happens when you and your Grab driver both insist your Waze route is faster.
usage_notes: Can range from a friendly debate to a heated argument. The noun form 'pagtatalo' means 'argument' or 'debate'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong **magtalo** tayo dahil lang sa pera.","translation":"I don't want us **to argue** just because of money."},{"sentence":"Mahilig **magtalo** ang magkapatid kung sino ang gagamit ng kompyuter.","translation":"The siblings love **to argue** about who gets to use the computer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos o direksyon na papunta sa isang liko o kurbada; hindi tuwid.
original_explanation: When the Grab driver is following Waze and the voice says 'Turn left,' the car is moving 'paliko.' It's the opposite of straight. Also describes a road with lots of curves, like the ones going up to Baguio or Tagaytay. 'Mag-ingat sa daan, paliko at matarik.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe the direction of movement or the nature of a path. Can function as both an adverb and an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang lumihis **paliko** ang sasakyan upang iwasan ang aso.","translation":"The car suddenly swerved, **turning**, to avoid the dog."},{"sentence":"Ang daan papunta sa aming probinsya ay **paliko** at makitid.","translation":"The road to our province is **curving** and narrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kalagayan, bagay, o lugar na labis na marumi, nakaririmarim, at hindi kaaya-aya.
original_explanation: This is not just 'marumi'. This is next-level dumi. Imagine the state of a shared CR in a dorm at the end of the semester, or a street corner that hasn't seen a street sweeper since the last election. That's mayurya. It's the kind of dirty that makes you want to take a bath twice.
usage_notes: This is a very strong and somewhat literary word for 'dirty'. You won't hear this in everyday conversation but might encounter it in literature or formal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **mayurya** na estero ay pinagmumulan ng sakit sa komunidad.","translation":"The **squalid** canal is a source of disease in the community."}]

meaning_filipino: Naging madali o mabilis gawin; (kolokyal) tinamaan o natamaan ang isang target o layunin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "dali" (bilis o gaan) at ang gitlaping "-um-".
original_explanation: Two meanings here. First, when your project suddenly 'became easy' because the terror prof was absent. Second, when you 'hit' the jackpot, or when your witty comeback 'hit' its mark perfectly. 'Dumali ka, pre!' means 'You nailed it!'
usage_notes: May dalawang karaniwang gamit: literal na 'naging madali' at kolokyal na 'tinamaan' o 'nagtagumpay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumali** ang pagsusulit dahil nakapag-aral ako nang mabuti.","translation":"The exam **became easy** because I studied well."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **dumali** rin ang tamang numero sa lotto!","translation":"Finally, the correct number in the lotto **hit**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinuno o tagapamahala ng isang paaralan.
original_explanation: Ang final boss sa eskwelahan. Siya 'yung pinupuntahan mo 'pag na-guidance ka at kailangan na ng parent-teacher-student conference. Sila ang may hawak ng mikropono tuwing flag ceremony at may kapangyarihang mag-suspend ng klase 'pag bumabagyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinatawag ng **punungguro** ang mga magulang ng mag-aaral.","translation":"The **principal** summoned the student's parents."},{"sentence":"Ang ating bagong **punungguro** ay mahigpit ngunit makatarungan.","translation":"Our new **principal** is strict but fair."}]

translation: to be the object of envy
meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan o layon ng inggit o selos ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: Ito yung state of being na "sana all" ang comment sa'yo ng mga tao. Yung ikaw ang subject ng inggit, in a good or bad way. Kapag pinost mo 'yung travel pics mo sa Europe, 'yan, pinapanaghilian mo ang mga ka-work mo na nasa office pa.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwa na hindi gaanong karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, ngunit lumalabas sa panitikan. Ang mas karaniwang anyo ay "kainggitan."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang tagumpay ay **pinapanaghilian** ng marami niyang katunggali.","translation":"His success **is the object of envy** for many of his rivals."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang gawain, sistema, o tao na hindi tapat, baluktot, at may kasamang panloloko o katiwalian.
original_explanation: When you hear this word, think of politicians with unexplained wealth or transactions that seem fishy. It's the reason why 'under the table' deals exist. A system is 'patiwali' if you need a 'padrino' or 'lagay' just to get basic services done. It's the opposite of 'fair and square'.
usage_notes: Often used to describe systems, governments, or actions rather than just people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming mamamayan ang sawà na sa **patiwaling** sistema ng gobyerno.","translation":"Many citizens are fed up with the **corrupt** system of government."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghingi ng payo, opinyon, o impormasyon mula sa isang tao o pangkat na itinuturing na may sapat na kaalaman.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're about to make a major life decision, like changing careers or getting a new haircut. You message the group chat: "Guys, need your opinions..." That's you about to kasangguniin your friends. It's the act of using your 'phone-a-friend'.
usage_notes: A formal verb. The common equivalent is 'konsultahin' or 'tanungin'. It implies seeking expert or trusted advice. The object of the verb is the person/thing being consulted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **kasangguniin** ang mga eksperto bago magdesisyon.","translation":"We should **consult** the experts before making a decision."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **kasangguniin** ang kanyang mga magulang tungkol sa kanyang planong mag-abroad.","translation":"She wants **to consult** her parents about her plan to go abroad."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng kilos o pagsasabi ng mga salita na may layuning hamakin, libakin, o maliitin ang isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The official sport of Marites and online trolls. It's when you make fun of someone, either to their face or behind their back, often in a mean-spirited way. Think of it as the 'la' in 'walang kwenta' – that extra spice of insult. Don't be the person who does the kutyain-ing.
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb. The actor form is "mangutya".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kutyain** ang kanyang mga pangarap dahil lang iba ito sa iyo.","translation":"Don't **mock** their dreams just because they're different from yours."},{"sentence":"Madalas siyang **kutyain** ng kanyang mga kaklase dahil sa kanyang kakaibang pananamit.","translation":"He was often **ridiculed** by his classmates because of his unique way of dressing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pandiwa sa aspektong pangnagdaan na tumutukoy sa kilos ng pagnanakaw o pagkuha ng isang bagay na pag-aari ng iba nang walang pahintulot.
etymology: From the root word "nakaw" (theft) with the infix "-um-".
original_explanation: The past tense of "to steal." It's what happens to your Jollibee chickenjoy if you leave it unguarded. It's also what that ex did to your heart. "May **numakaw** ng payong ko sa labas ng 7-Eleven!" or the more dramatic "**Numakaw** siya ng halik." Either way, something was taken without permission.
usage_notes: "Nagnakaw" is more commonly used in everyday speech. "Numakaw" can sound more literary or formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang magnanakaw ang **numakaw** ng kanyang pitaka habang siya'y natutulog sa bus.","translation":"A thief **stole** her wallet while she was sleeping on the bus."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **numakaw** ng huling piraso ng pizza?","translation":"Who **stole** the last piece of pizza?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mahusay, dalubhasa, o eksperto sa isang gawain o larangan.
original_explanation: This is the noun form of 'Ang galing mo!' It's the proof of your skills, your talent, your 'galing.' The thing you show off to get a promotion or win a competition. It’s your KSA (Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities) in your resume, summarized.
usage_notes: Used to refer to a person's demonstrated ability or talent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinangaan ng lahat ang kanyang **kagalingan** sa pagtugtog ng gitara.","translation":"Everyone admired his **skillfulness** in playing the guitar."},{"sentence":"Ipinamalas niya ang kanyang **kagalingan** bilang isang lider.","translation":"She demonstrated her **excellence** as a leader."}]

translation: to have a drinking session with others
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsali sa isang grupo upang uminom ng alak o anumang inuming may alkohol, karaniwan bilang isang paraan ng pakikisalamuha.
original_explanation: The quintessential Filipino social activity. It's not just about getting drunk; it's about `pakikisama` (getting along). It's where secrets are shared (`lasing na, eh`), problems are solved (or forgotten), and friendships are forged over a shared bottle of gin and a plate of sisig. The sacred ritual often involves a `tagay` (a shared glass passed around). It's a social verb if there ever was one.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to drinking alcoholic beverages in a group setting. 'Uminom' is just 'to drink', but 'makipag-inuman' is a social event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Yayain mo sila Jojo na **makipag-inuman** mamaya pagkatapos ng trabaho.","translation":"Invite Jojo and the others **to have a drinking session** later after work."},{"sentence":"Bawal na siyang **makipag-inuman** dahil sa utos ng doktor.","translation":"He's forbidden from **having drinking sessions** on doctor's orders."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o instrumento na ginagamit upang lumikha ng butas sa isang bagay, tulad ng papel, katad, o metal.
etymology: From `pan-` (instrument prefix) + `butas` (hole). The `n` in `pan-` assimilates to `m` before `b`.
original_explanation: This is any tool whose life purpose is to make a hole. From the humble office paper puncher to the power drill your Tito uses for his DIY projects. It's the OG 'cancel' tool for paper. Got a mistake on a document? Pambutas to the rescue para ma-file sa ring binder at 'di na makita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hiram muna ako ng **pambutas** para sa mga dokumentong ito.","translation":"Can I borrow a **hole puncher** for these documents?"},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang matulis na bato bilang **pambutas** sa bao ng niyog.","translation":"He used the sharp rock as a tool **to make a hole** in the coconut shell."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking laging maayos at maganda ang pananamit; makisig.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "postura" na nangangahulugang 'tindig' o 'ayos'.
original_explanation: Your Tito who refuses to wear a simple t-shirt, even sa bahay. He's the guy in a crisp polo, slacks, and leather shoes while everyone else is in shorts and pambahay. He's got that 'gentleman' vibe down, always looking sharp.
usage_notes: The masculine form of `pusturyosa`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong **pusturyoso** ang nobyo niya; laging amoy pabango at naka-plantsa ang damit.","translation":"Her boyfriend is too **dapper**; he always smells of cologne and his clothes are always ironed."},{"sentence":"Kahit matanda na si Lolo, **pusturyoso** pa rin siyang manamit.","translation":"Even though Grandpa is old, he still dresses in a **dapper** way."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marka o sugat sa balat na dulot ng pagkuskos o paghiwa ng matulis na bagay, lalo na ng kuko ng hayop tulad ng pusa.
original_explanation: The love language of your cat. One minute you're petting them, the next minute you have battle scars on your arm. It's also what you get from your girlfriend when you forget your anniversary. The mark is temporary, but the memory (and the sting) is forever.
usage_notes: Specifically implies a scratch from claws or fingernails, as opposed to 'gasgas' which is a more general term for a scratch or abrasion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **kalmot** ang braso ko dahil sa aming alagang pusa.","translation":"My arm is full of **scratches** because of our pet cat."},{"sentence":"Nag-iwan ng malalim na **kalmot** sa kanyang mukha ang naging away nila.","translation":"Their fight left a deep **scratch** on his face."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na lalagyan na karaniwang may hawakan, ginagamit sa pag-inom, lalo na ng mga maiinit na likido tulad ng kape o tsaa.
original_explanation: Your best friend during those late-night study sessions or early morning BPO shifts. It holds the magic liquid (kape!) that makes you a functional human being. It's the smaller, more sophisticated cousin of the 'baso' (glass) and the 'tabo' (dipper).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtimpla siya ng kape sa paborito niyang **tasa**.","translation":"She prepared coffee in her favorite **cup**."}]

translation: The act of being a nuisance; disturbance
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o akto ng pagiging sagabal, abala, o perwisyo sa iba.
original_explanation: This is the state of being a major 'istorbo' (nuisance). It’s not just a single act, but the quality of being disruptive. Think of the neighbor who does karaoke at 2 AM, the slow Wi-Fi during a crucial Zoom meeting, or that officemate who keeps asking questions you just Googled for them. That's the essence of 'pagka-estorbo'. It's the opposite of 'good vibes only.'
usage_notes: Often used to express annoyance or frustration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paumanhin sa aking **pagka-estorbo** sa inyong pag-uusap.","translation":"Sorry for being a **nuisance** to your conversation."},{"sentence":"Ang ingay mula sa construction ay isang malaking **pagka-estorbo** sa aming pag-aaral.","translation":"The noise from the construction is a huge **disturbance** to our studies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng malakas at paulit-ulit na pag-alog o pag-uga sa isang bagay o tao.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'yugyog' (shake, jolt) at ang hulaping '-in' na ginagawa itong isang pandiwa.
original_explanation: What you want to do to the vending machine when it eats your money. Or what your mom does to you to wake you up when you're faking sleep. It's a more intense, more aggressive "alogin." Think of the song: "Shake, shake, shake... yugyugin mo!"
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa paggising sa isang tao, paghalo ng likido sa isang lalagyan, o pag-alog ng puno para mahulog ang bunga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **yugyugin** nang mabuti ang bote bago ito inumin.","translation":"You need to **shake** the bottle well before drinking it."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **yugyugin** ang natutulog na kapatid para magising.","translation":"He tried to **shake** his sleeping sibling to wake him up."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, tao, o pangyayari na nagdudulot ng kagalakan, ligaya, o kasiyahan.
original_explanation: Your personal happiness booster. It could be a milk tea break, a cute dog video, getting your sahod, or a message from your crush. It's your go-to "pampagood-vibes" when the adulting gets too real. Basically, anything that sparks joy, Marie Kondo-style, but with more kilig.
usage_notes: Can be a person, thing, or activity that causes happiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang alaga kong aso ang aking **pampasaya** araw-araw.","translation":"My pet dog is my **source of joy** every day."},{"sentence":"Magpatugtog tayo ng **pampasaya** na kanta.","translation":"Let's play a **cheery** song."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na salu-salo o handaan, karaniwang bilang pagdiriwang ng isang tagumpay, kaarawan, o sahod. Tumutukoy din ito sa biglaang pagsabog ng gulong ng sasakyan.
original_explanation: The most beautiful word a Filipino employee or student can hear. 'May sahod na, bloaut naman diyan!' It's the unwritten rule that when you get a promotion, a bonus, or it's your birthday, you're socially obligated to treat your friends or colleagues to a meal. It can be anything from Jollibee to a fancy restaurant, as long as it's your treat. It's the Pinoy version of 'I'll get this one.'
usage_notes: Has two main meanings: a party/treat and a flat tire. The context usually makes the meaning clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kaarawan ko bukas, kaya may **bloaut** sa opisina!","translation":"It's my birthday tomorrow, so there's a **blowout** at the office!"},{"sentence":"Na-late kami dahil nagka-**bloaut** ang gulong ng jeep.","translation":"We were late because the jeepney's tire had a **blowout**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na sayaw sa Pilipinas na ginagaya ang galaw ng ibong Tikling, kung saan ang mga mananayaw ay mabilis na umiiwas sa nag-uumpugang mga kawayan.
etymology: Named after the 'tikling' bird. The '-in-' infix signifies 'to be like' or 'in the manner of'.
original_explanation: The national dance that's also a high-stakes ankle workout. It's that dance with the bamboo poles that makes you hold your breath every time you see it, hoping nobody's feet get caught. It mimics the 'tikling' bird avoiding traps, which is basically what you're doing with the clacking bamboo. One wrong step and *ouch*.
usage_notes: A staple performance in Filipino cultural shows and school foundation days.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Tinikling** ay isa sa mga pinakatanyag na katutubong sayaw ng Pilipinas.","translation":"**Tinikling** is one of the most famous native dances of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Magaling siyang sumayaw ng **Tinikling**; hindi man lang nasagi ang kanyang mga paa.","translation":"She's great at dancing the **Tinikling**; her feet didn't even get hit."}]

translation: a long, hanging branch or vine; a pendulous object
meaning_filipino: Isang mahaba at nakalaylay na sanga, baging, o anumang bagay na malayang gumagalaw habang nakabitin.
original_explanation: Think Tarzan's favorite ride. It's that long, droopy branch or vine hanging from a tree, swaying in the wind. It can also describe the graceful, hanging movement of a dancer's arm or even long, flowing hair. It has a very poetic, almost romantic, feel to it.
usage_notes: Often used in a literary or descriptive context. Can also be used as a verb 'lumambayog' (to sway while hanging).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng unggoy ang **lambayog** upang tumawid sa kabilang puno.","translation":"The monkey used the **hanging vine** to cross to the other tree."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **lambayog** ng puno ng balete ay nakakatakot sa dilim.","translation":"The **pendulous branches** of the balete tree are scary in the dark."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na pagpapaikli para sa salitang "anibersaryo."
etymology: A clipped form of the English word "anniversary", which itself is from Spanish 'aniversario'.
original_explanation: The short and sweet term for 'anniversary'. It's the one day a year you can't forget, or else... 'bahala ka sa buhay mo'. This is the trigger for mandatory couple posts on social media with a caption that's longer than the actual relationship. 'Happy 1st monthsary-anniv, babe!'
usage_notes: Very common in casual conversation, texting, and social media. It's a Taglish staple.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan tayo kakain para sa ating **anniv**?","translation":"Where are we eating for our **anniv**?"},{"sentence":"Happy 5th **anniv** sa paborito kong BPO company!","translation":"Happy 5th **anniv** to my favorite BPO company!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas at matinis na tunog na nililikha ng bibig, karaniwang nagpapahayag ng matinding damdamin tulad ng galit, takot, o kagalakan.
original_explanation: Your default reaction when you see a cockroach flying towards you. A sigaw is that primal noise you make when you're super scared, super angry (like when your internet dies during a ranked game), or super happy (like when your bias notices you at a concert). It's your voice on max volume.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (a shout) or a verb root ('sumigaw' - to shout).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **sigaw** ang narinig mula sa kabilang bahay.","translation":"A loud **shout** was heard from the next house."},{"sentence":"Ang **sigaw** niya ay puno ng takot at pag-aalala.","translation":"Her **scream** was full of fear and worry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, karaniwan ay tsuper, na nagmamaneho nang napakabilis at walang pag-iingat.
etymology: From "kaskas" (speeding) + Spanish suffix "-ero" (denoting a person associated with an activity or characteristic).
original_explanation: That driver who weaves through traffic like they're in a 'Fast & Furious' movie. The one who makes you grip the safety handle and pray to all the saints. Jeepney, bus, or private car, if they drive like there's no tomorrow, they're a **kaskasero**.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe drivers. The feminine form "kaskasera" exists but is much less common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinuli ng pulis ang **kaskasero** na tsuper ng bus.","translation":"The police caught the **reckless** bus **driver**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **kaskasero** sa daan.","translation":"Don't be a **speeder** on the road."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa katangian o kilos ng isang tao (hindi kailangang babae o ina) na nagpapakita ng pagiging maalaga, mapag-aruga, at responsable, na karaniwang iniuugnay sa isang ina.
etymology: Tambalan ng salitang Ingles na "mommy" at "vibes".
original_explanation: When someone in your friend group is the designated taga-alaga. They're the one who always has tissue, band-aids, hand sanitizer, and extra cash. They make sure everyone gets home safe after a night out. They don't have to be a mom, they just radiate that 'I got you, anak' energy.
usage_notes: Isang modernong pariralang balbal (slang) na popular sa mga nakababatang henerasyon at sa social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya talaga ang may **mommy vibes** sa barkada, laging may dalang gamot at snacks.","translation":"She really has the **mommy vibes** in our friend group, always bringing medicine and snacks."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakabitin, pagkakakawit, o pagkasangkot sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Like your Christmas lantern na nakalimutan mo nang tanggalin in February. Or that piece of plastic bag na sumabit sa tricycle. It's anything that's caught on or dangling. Also, a state of being for anyone trying to ride a jeepney during rush hour—'nakasabit' sa estribo.
usage_notes: As a verb, it can be 'sumabit' (to get snagged) or 'isabit' (to hang something). As an adjective, 'nakasabit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **sabit** na sinulid sa laylayan ng damit mo.","translation":"There's a thread **snagged** on the hem of your dress."},{"sentence":"**Isabit** mo ang basang tuwalya sa sampayan.","translation":"**Hang** the wet towel on the clothesline."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin ang dumi, kalat, o anumang bagay na marumi sa isang lugar o bagay upang ito ay maging maayos at kaaya-aya.
original_explanation: The national weekend anthem. The sound of a vacuum cleaner on a Saturday morning, the smell of floor wax, and your mom yelling "Walang aalis hangga't hindi pa malinis ang bahay!" That's the signal to maglinis. It's the ultimate chore, the cure for 'tamad-itis', and the prerequisite for getting your wifi password back.
usage_notes: A very common, general-purpose verb for cleaning anything.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **maglinis** ng buong bahay bago dumating ang mga bisita.","translation":"I need to **clean** the whole house before the visitors arrive."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **maglinis** ng iyong kuwarto tuwing umaga.","translation":"Don't forget to **clean** your room every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang grupo, pangkat, o indibidwal na may partikular na opinyon, paniniwala, o interes sa isang usapin, debate, o alitan.
original_explanation: In any chismis, there are always two sides. "Kaninong panig ka?" means "Whose side are you on?". It's Team A vs. Team B, the prosecution vs. the defense, or you vs. your sibling arguing over the TV remote.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga konteksto ng hidwaan, debate, o mga legal na usapin.
