usage_notes: Often used for things that are split into two distinct parts, like wood, coconuts, or even figuratively, a heart.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang itak para gawing **biak** ang buko.","translation":"He used the bolo to **split** the young coconut open."},{"sentence":"Ang daan ay **biak** dahil sa lindol.","translation":"The road was **cracked open** because of the earthquake."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang kasuklam-suklam, nakapandidiri, o karima-rimarim.
etymology: The root 'rimarim' means disgust or loathing. The 'nakari-' prefix intensifies this.
original_explanation: This isn't just "yucky," this is next-level disgusting. It's the word you use for a horrific crime scene on the news, not for a cockroach in your shoe. It's the feeling you get when you see extreme injustice or depravity. It's a very strong, formal, and intense word. "Ang balita tungkol sa korapsyon ay tunay na nakaririmarim."
usage_notes: A very strong adjective used to express extreme disgust and moral outrage. Not for everyday use.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **nakaririmarim** na krimen ang naganap sa kanilang lugar.","translation":"A **loathsome** crime occurred in their area."},{"sentence":"**Nakaririmarim** ang amoy na nagmumula sa basurahan.","translation":"The smell coming from the garbage is **disgusting**."}]

translation: wretchedness; misery; state of being lowly
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging kaawa-awa, dukha, o hamak.
etymology: From the prefix "pagka-" (state of being) + "aba" (lowly, alas).
original_explanation: It's the feeling you have on Monday morning when you see your workload. It's the vibe of a telenovela protagonist who's lost everything. It's not just being poor ('hirap') or sad ('lungkot'); it's a deep state of misery and lowliness, the kind that makes you want to sing a dramatic 'birit' song in the rain.
usage_notes: "Aba" can also be an interjection of surprise, but in this context, it means lowly or pitiful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang sukdulang **pagkaaba** matapos siyang iwan ng lahat.","translation":"She felt extreme **wretchedness** after everyone left her."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng kanyang **pagkaaba**, hindi siya nawalan ng pag-asa.","translation":"Despite his **state of misery**, he did not lose hope."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumalsik o magsaboy ng maliliit na patak ng likido sa iba't ibang direksyon.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na naghuhugas ka ng plato tapos biglang may tumalsik na tubig galing sa gripo na may kasamang sebo at konting kanin. 'Yun na 'yun. O kaya 'yung oil pag nagpiprito ka ng isda, biglang nag-concert at nag-mosh pit sa mukha mo. That's mamilansik.
usage_notes: Often used for liquids like water, oil, or mud spattering in small droplets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa pagprito ng isda dahil baka **mamilansik** ang mainit na mantika.","translation":"Be careful when frying fish because the hot oil might **spatter**."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang dumaan sa putikan dahil baka **mamilansik** ang dumi sa kanyang puting pantalon.","translation":"He doesn't want to walk through the puddle because the mud might **splash** onto his white pants."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natuyong uhog o sipon sa loob ng butas ng ilong.
original_explanation: That little treasure you mine from your nose when you think no one's looking. It's gross, everyone does it, and it's the number one reason to always have an opaque face mask on during a video call.
usage_notes: A common, if slightly impolite, word used by all ages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"May **kulangot** ka sa ilong,\" bulong ng kaibigan niya.","translation":"\"You have a **booger** in your nose,\" his friend whispered."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan ng ina ang kanyang anak na gumamit ng panyo para linisin ang **kulangot**.","translation":"The mother taught her child to use a handkerchief to clean out a **booger**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang araw sa karaniwang linggo ng pagtatrabaho, kasunod ng Linggo at bago ang Martes.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'lunes', na mula sa Latin na 'dies Lunae' (araw ng buwan).
original_explanation: The official enemy of the weekend. The day your alarm clock's 'snooze' button works the hardest. That feeling of 'sana weekend na ulit' starts here. It's the day of flag ceremonies, new weekly reports, and the collective sigh of the entire workforce.
usage_notes: Standard term for Monday. Usually capitalized as it is a proper noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **Lunes** para pag-usapan ang proyekto.","translation":"Let's meet on **Monday** to discuss the project."},{"sentence":"Ayoko pumasok, **Lunes** na naman.","translation":"I don't want to go to work, it's **Monday** again."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging magkamukha, magkawangis, o magkapareho sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: This is the 'copy-paste' or 'Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V' of life. It's why people say you look like your dad, why your new boyfriend has the same toxic traits as your ex, or why all milk tea shops seem to have the same menu. It’s the resemblance, the likeness, the 'spot the difference' game where you can't find any.
usage_notes: A very common word used for comparing people, things, ideas, or situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **pagkakatulad** ang kultura ng Pilipinas at Mexico.","translation":"There are many **similarities** between the cultures of the Philippines and Mexico."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **pagkakatulad** ng magkapatid.","translation":"The **resemblance** between the siblings is very clear."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, aklat, o anumang bagay na mapagkukunan ng impormasyon o payo; isang lupon na kinokonsulta.
etymology: From ka- + sangguni + -an. Denotes a place, object, or person for 'sangguni' (consultation).
original_explanation: This is the 'Sources:' section in your thesis paper. It's the Wikipedia page you secretly checked, the chismosa neighbor you asked for the latest scoop, or the senior colleague you ask when you don't know the answer. Your 'phone-a-friend' option.
usage_notes: Used both for human sources (a consultant) and inanimate sources (a book, a website). In government, 'Sangguniang Bayan/Panlungsod/Panlalawigan' are local legislative councils.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalista sa dulo ng aklat ang lahat ng **kasanggunian**.","translation":"All the **references** are listed at the end of the book."},{"sentence":"Ang aming guro ang naging **kasanggunian** namin para sa proyekto.","translation":"Our teacher became our **source** for the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Tulong na ibinibigay sa anyo ng bigas, karaniwang mula sa pamahalaan, isang organisasyon, o isang indibidwal para sa mga nangangailangan.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino "ayuda" or aid. During elections, calamities, or company Christmas parties, this is the most anticipated giveaway. It's more valuable than a gift certificate. Seeing a politician's face on a sack of rice during campaign season is the classic "pabigas" move. It literally means "for rice," but it symbolizes care, community support, and sometimes, political strategy.
usage_notes: Often associated with government aid (`ayuda`) or political campaigns.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap kami ng **pabigas** mula sa LGU noong kasagsagan ng lockdown.","translation":"We received **rice assistance** from the LGU during the height of the lockdown."},{"sentence":"Taun-taon, may **pabigas** ang kumpanya para sa lahat ng empleyado.","translation":"Every year, the company has a **rice dole-out** for all employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nangangahulugang biro lamang o hindi seryoso ang sinabi. Katumbas ng 'biro lang'.
etymology: A clipping of 'charot', another slang term meaning 'just kidding'. Popularized in Filipino gay culture.
original_explanation: The Pinoy version of adding "jk" to your text. You drop a truth bomb, see the shocked faces, then save yourself with a quick "Chos!" It's the get-out-of-jail-free card for verbal assassins and tsismosas.
usage_notes: Usually uttered at the end of a sentence to indicate that the statement was a joke.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanalo daw ako sa lotto... **chos**!","translation":"They said I won the lottery... **just kidding**!"},{"sentence":"Ikaw ang pinakamaganda sa balat ng lupa, **chos**!","translation":"You're the most beautiful on the face of the earth, **joking**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang babae ay magdalang-tao dahil sa pakikipagtalik sa isang lalaki.
etymology: From 'buntis' (pregnant). The prefix 'ma-' and suffix '-an' create a passive verb form, indicating that the subject is the one who becomes pregnant.
original_explanation: This is the passive form of 'getting someone pregnant.' It's what happens when things get a little too 'Netflix and chill' and someone ends up with a +1 for the next nine months. It's a classic teleserye plot point.
usage_notes: The focus is on the person who becomes pregnant. The actor (the one who caused the pregnancy) is usually introduced with 'ng'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Labis ang takot niyang **mabuntisan** nang wala sa panahon.","translation":"She is terrified of **getting pregnant** at the wrong time."},{"sentence":"Nabalitaan kong **mabuntisan** daw ni Marco ang kanyang kasintahan.","translation":"I heard that Marco's girlfriend **was impregnated** by him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing pagkilos ng paggunit, pagkapit, o pag-ari sa isang bagay o tao gamit ang kamay sa hinaharap.
etymology: From the root word 'hawak' (hold) with the future tense prefix 'ha-' (repetition of the first syllable).
original_explanation: The future tense of 'hold'. It's what you tell your friend who's about to fall ('Hahawak ako sa'yo!'), what the sign on the LRT says you should do to the handrails, or the promise of a K-drama lead ('Kahit anong mangyari, hahawak ako sa kamay mo.').
usage_notes: Standard future tense form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **hahawak** ng banner sa ating parada?","translation":"Who **will hold** the banner in our parade?"},{"sentence":"**Hahawak** ako nang mahigpit para hindi ako mahulog.","translation":"I **will hold** on tight so I don't fall."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali na inilaan para sa pagsamba o serbisyong panrelihiyon.
original_explanation: Hindi lang ito 'yung mga sinaunang building sa Greece or Egypt. Sa Pinas, ito 'yung malalaking bahay-sambahan ng ibang relihiyon, tulad ng Templo ng mga Mormon o mga templong Buddhist. Isipin mo na lang, ito 'yung level-up version ng kapilya o simbahan. Isang lugar para sa mataimtim na pagninilay-nilay at pagdarasal.
usage_notes: Mas madalas gamitin ang "simbahan" para sa mga Katolikong gusali ng pagsamba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumalaw kami sa isang antigong **templo** sa Cebu.","translation":"We visited an ancient **temple** in Cebu."},{"sentence":"Ang **templo** ay isang sagradong lugar ng pagsamba.","translation":"The **temple** is a sacred place of worship."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay o pagwiwisik ng isang bagay sa isang partikular na lugar o ibabaw.
original_explanation: This is the command form. Kung yung jowa mo nag-order ng pizza at walang chili flakes, sasabihin mo, "Buluburan mo ng sili, beh!" It's the 'sprinkle it on' command. Parang 'pag sinabi ng boss mo, "Buluburan mo ng positive comments 'yang report para magmukhang maganda."
usage_notes: This is a locative verb form, indicating the place or object where the sprinkling action is directed. A common synonym is 'budburan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Buluburan** mo ng niyog ang puto bumbong.","translation":"**Sprinkle** coconut on the puto bumbong."},{"sentence":"Ang mesa ay kanyang **binuluburan** ng mga talulot ng bulaklak.","translation":"She **sprinkled** the table with flower petals."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na salitang panagot na katumbas ng "oo," ginagamit kapag nakikipag-usap sa mga nakatatanda o sa mga taong may mataas na katungkulan.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa pagsasama ng "oo" at ng panandang paggalang na "po".
original_explanation: The ultimate sign of respect in the Filipino language. It's "yes" but with a premium subscription. You use "opo" with your parents, lola, your boss, or anyone older than you to avoid getting the "wala kang galang" speech. It's the verbal equivalent of the "mano po." If "oo" is a text message, "opo" is a handwritten letter.
usage_notes: Laging ginagamit kasama ng "po" sa iba pang bahagi ng pangungusap para sa tuluy-tuloy na paggalang. Ito ang buong sagot, samantalang ang "po" ay idinadagdag sa mga pangungusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumain ka na ba, iho? \"**Opo**, lola. Katatapos ko lang po.\"","translation":"Have you eaten, son? \"**Yes (politely)**, grandma. I just finished.\""},{"sentence":"Pakidala nito sa lamesa. \"**Opo**, itay.\"","translation":"Please bring this to the table. \"**Yes (politely)**, dad.\""}]

meaning_filipino: Ang oras sa simula ng araw kung kailan nagsisimulang magliwanag ang kalangitan bago sumikat ang araw.
etymology: From "buka" (to open) and "liwayway" (dawn). Literally "the opening of dawn."
original_explanation: This is that magical, pre-traffic, pre-stress moment of the day. It's the time when roosters (and BPO agents ending their shift) are most active. It’s the universe telling you, 'Okay, game na, another day to make a living or make 'sana all' comments on Instagram.' The most poetic time of day before the chaos begins.
usage_notes: A very poetic and descriptive term for dawn.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsisimula nang magtrabaho ang mga magsasaka sa **pagbubukang-liwayway** pa lamang.","translation":"The farmers already start working at the very **dawn**."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng kulay ng langit tuwing **pagbubukang-liwayway**.","translation":"The color of the sky is beautiful during **daybreak**."}]

translation: to hold one's head or face in one's hands
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghawak sa ulo o mukha gamit ang mga palad, karaniwan bilang tanda ng pag-aalala, pagod, o matinding pag-iisip.
original_explanation: That moment when you see your credit card bill and you instinctively put your face in your hands? That's **sapupuhin**. It's the universal pose for 'OMG what have I done?', 'Ang dami kong trabaho!', or 'Sakit ng ulo ko sa'yo.'
usage_notes: Derived from 'sapupo', which is the noun for the action of holding one's head in one's hands.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagawa na lang niyang **sapupuhin** ang kanyang ulo sa tindi ng problema.","translation":"He could only **hold his head in his hands** because of the severity of the problem."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sapupuhin** ang iyong mukha, harapin natin ito nang magkasama.","translation":"Don't **hold your face in your hands**, let's face this together."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na sakdal, reklamo, o kaso na inihain sa korte ng batas; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang mariing kahilingan.
original_explanation: Kapag may nag-file ng demanda laban sa'yo, hindi ito 'yung "demand" ng jowa mo na mag-reply ka agad. This is the serious, legal kind of trouble. May kasamang abogado, hearing sa korte, at sandamakmak na stress. It's the ultimate "magkikita tayo sa barangay" level-up.
usage_notes: Can mean both a legal lawsuit and a strong demand, but the legal context is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsampa siya ng **demanda** laban sa kumpanya dahil sa hindi makatarungang pagtanggal sa trabaho.","translation":"He filed a **lawsuit** against the company for unjust termination."},{"sentence":"Ang **demanda** ng mga manggagawa ay umento sa sahod.","translation":"The **demand** of the workers is a wage increase."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakakahawang sakit, lalo na sa mga bata, na dulot ng birus at nagdudulot ng lagnat, ubo, at mga pulang butlig sa balat.
original_explanation: The OG childhood disease bago pa nauso ang kung anu-anong variants. Ito 'yung sakit na kapag narinig ng nanay mo, auto-quarantine ka na at bawal maligo for a week. The red spots are its signature look. Thanks to vaccines, it's not as common, but the fear it strikes in the hearts of Pinoy moms is timeless.
usage_notes: Often used with 'magka-' as in 'magkatikdas' (to have measles).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang bakuna laban sa **tikdas** para sa mga sanggol.","translation":"The vaccine against **measles** is important for babies."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **tikdas** ang kapatid ko noong bata pa siya.","translation":"My sibling had **measles** when he was young."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng hirap sa pagsasalita kung saan nauulit o humahaba ang mga tunog, pantig, o salita; pagkakaroon ng pagkautal.
etymology: Reduplication of the first syllable of the related root 'utal'.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you try to talk to your super-crush for the first time. Your brain is working fine, but your mouth hits a major traffic jam on EDSA. It's the 'uhm... ah... eh...' when you're caught in a lie or put on the spot during a presentation.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective ('Siya ay ut-utin') or to describe the action. The root word 'utal' is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **ut-utin** kapag kinakabahan.","translation":"He **stutters** when he's nervous."},{"sentence":"Naging **ut-utin** ang bata dahil sa takot.","translation":"The child started **stammering** out of fear."}]

translation: to look from side to side (in confusion or denial)
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na paggalaw ng ulo sa magkabilang panig, na kadalasang nagpapahiwatig ng pagtanggi, pagkalito, o paghahanap.
etymology: From `magpa-` and the reduplicated root `lingos` (to look sideways, to shake one's head).
original_explanation: This is the classic "Who, me?" move. When the teacher asks who was talking and everyone in the back row starts to 'magpalingus-lingos'. It's different from 'magpalingun-lingon' (looking back). This is a side-to-side head shake, the physical embodiment of "Wala akong alam diyan, sir/ma'am!"
usage_notes: Often implies denial, innocence, or being clueless. It's a physical gesture of shaking the head from side to side while looking around.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang tanungin kung sino ang umubos ng ulam, **nagpalingus-lingos** ang lahat ng bata.","translation":"When asked who finished the food, all the children **looked from side to side** innocently."},{"sentence":"Siya'y **nagpalingus-lingos**, litung-lito sa mga nangyayari.","translation":"She **kept looking from side to side**, completely confused by what was happening."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kabibe; isang alternatibong anyo o pagbigkas para sa salitang kabibe.
etymology: Likely a variant of 'kabibe', possibly with a shift in stress to denote a smaller size (diminutive).
original_explanation: It's the younger, smaller sibling of 'kabibe'. Some say it's just a different way to say it, like 'kumusta' vs 'kamusta'. Basically, if a 'kabibe' is a full-sized clam, a 'kabibi' might be the tiny, cute ones you use for DIY crafts.
usage_notes: Less common than 'kabibe' and often considered a variant spelling or a diminutive form. The pronunciation stress can differ to distinguish it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng maliliit na **kabibi** ang buhangin.","translation":"The sand is full of tiny **seashells**."},{"sentence":"Ginawa niyang kwintas ang mga **kabibi**.","translation":"She made the small **seashells** into a necklace."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang instrumentong pangmusika na parang organo na pinapatunog sa pamamagitan ng hangin mula sa isang apakan o bellows.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung keyboard ni lola na kailangan mo pang i-pump gamit ang paa para tumunog. Parang pinaghalong piano at accordion. Madalas mong makikita sa mga lumang simbahan o bahay, na nagbibigay ng nostalgic, medyo creepy na background music.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang partikular na uri ng lumang instrumento. Bihirang-bihira nang makita o gamitin ngayon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong siyang tumugtog ng lumang **armonyo** na pamana pa ng kanyang lola.","translation":"He knows how to play the old **harmonium** inherited from his grandmother."},{"sentence":"Ang tunog ng **armonyo** ay nagpapaalala sa kanya ng kanyang kabataan sa probinsya.","translation":"The sound of the **harmonium** reminds him of his youth in the province."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng pagpapaalam o paghahayag ng pag-alis, kadalasan ay may kasamang damdamin ng lungkot o pormalidad.
etymology: Reduplication of the first syllable of the root word 'paalam' (pa-) and affixation (pa- + paalam). This form indicates the act or manner of doing the root word.
original_explanation: That dramatic scene at the airport. The last episode of your favorite series. The "ghosting" phase when you realize they're not coming back. It’s the formal version of "paalam," often implying a longer, more significant departure than just leaving the office. It's the "see you again" that might actually mean "goodbye."
usage_notes: The -ma- infix suggests a prolonged or formal action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging madamdamin ang kanyang **pamamaalam** sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"His **farewell** to his family was emotional."},{"sentence":"Ang huling kabanata ay tungkol sa **pamamaalam** ng bida.","translation":"The last chapter is about the hero's **act of saying goodbye**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglilinis ng katawan gamit ang tubig at sabon; ang pagbuhos ng tubig sa katawan.
original_explanation: The past tense of your daily ritual (hopefully!). Ito yung ginawa mo na kanina bago ka pumasok sa office, o yung gagawin mo mamaya after mo mag-commute sa init ng Pinas. The ultimate reset button for the Filipino body.
usage_notes: Can mean both taking a shower (using a 'tabo' or showerhead) or bathing in a body of water like a river or the sea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naligo** ako ng malamig na tubig para magising ang diwa ko.","translation":"I **took a bath** with cold water to wake myself up."},{"sentence":"Kahapon, **naligo** kami sa dagat buong hapon.","translation":"Yesterday, we **bathed** in the sea the whole afternoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng isang piraso ng materyal, gaya ng tela, upang takpan ang isang butas o punit. Ito ay ang nakaraang anyo ng pandiwang 'magtagpi'.
original_explanation: This is what your lola did to your favorite pambahay shorts after you snagged them on a nail. It's the OG way of upcycling before it was cool. Think of it as a low-budget, high-love repair job. You nagtagpi the hole in your jeans, hoping no one notices it's a different shade of denim.
usage_notes: Ito ang perpektibong aspekto (past tense) ng pandiwang 'magtagpi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagtagpi** siya ng lumang kumot para gawing basahan.","translation":"She **patched** an old blanket to make it into a rag."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagtagpi** sa butas ng aking pantalon?","translation":"Who **mended** the hole in my pants?"}]

translation: prone to being nervous; easily flustered; a nervous person
meaning_filipino: Isang taong may likas na tendensiyang maging nerbiyoso o madaling kabahan.
etymology: From 'nerbyos' + '-in' (suffix indicating a tendency or characteristic).
original_explanation: If 'nerbiyosa/o' is what you *are* in a moment, 'nerbyusin' is who you *are* as a person. It's a personality trait. This is the person in your group project who panics from day one. They see a small problem and their brain immediately plays the "Mission Impossible" theme on full blast. "Kalma lang, 'wag kang masyadong nerbyusin." is their life's soundtrack.
usage_notes: Describes a personality trait rather than a temporary state. It's gender-neutral.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **nerbyusin** talaga ako, lalo na kapag nagsasalita sa harap ng maraming tao.","translation":"I'm really a **nervous person**, especially when speaking in front of many people."},{"sentence":"Kilala siyang **nerbyusin** sa opisina, pero napakagaling niyang magtrabaho.","translation":"She's known as someone **prone to being nervous** at the office, but she's a very good worker."}]

translation: to stare at; to fix one's gaze on
meaning_filipino: Ituon nang mariin at matagal ang paningin sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: More intense than 'itingin'. This is when you're not just looking, you're *staring*. Like how you look at your food delivery app tracking the rider's progress. Or how you look at your crush walking down the hallway in slow motion (in your head). That focused, unblinking gaze? That's 'ititig'.
usage_notes: Implies a longer, more intense, and focused act of looking compared to 'tingin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ititig** nang ganyan, baka matunaw siya.","translation":"Don't **stare** at him like that, he might melt."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **ititig** ang mga mata sa magandang tanawin mula sa bintana.","translation":"She wanted to **fix her gaze on** the beautiful view from the window."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kaldero na karaniwang may mahabang hawakan, ginagamit sa pagluluto, lalo na ng mga sarsa o pagpapakulo.
original_explanation: Not to be confused with the baked dish. This is the OG kitchen essential, the one your mom uses to cook sinigang, adobo, or just to boil water for your coffee. It's also the same pot that gets banged on during noise barrages or protests. A truly multi-purpose item.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a deep cooking pot, usually with one long handle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isalin mo ang sabaw sa malinis na **kaserola**.","translation":"Pour the soup into a clean **saucepan**."},{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang maliit na **kaserola** para magpakulo ng itlog.","translation":"Use the small **casserole pot** to boil eggs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging bulok, sira, o tiwali, lalo na sa moral o panlipunang aspeto. Ito ay sumasalamin sa malalim na pagkasira.
etymology: From `ka-` (abstract noun prefix) + `burok` (rotten). The variant `kabulukan` from the more common root `bulok` is used more frequently.
original_explanation: This is when something is rotten to the core. It can be literal, but it's often figurative, like a system riddled with corruption. It's a stronger, more visceral word than just 'kasamaan'. It implies a deep, systemic decay, like finding mold in the very foundations of a house.
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically to describe moral or social decay. "Kabulukan" is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais nilang ilantad ang **kaburukan** sa loob ng ahensya.","translation":"They want to expose the **corruption** within the agency."},{"sentence":"Ang amoy ng **kaburukan** ay nanggagaling sa tambak na basura.","translation":"The smell of **rottenness** is coming from the pile of garbage."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hayop na may malalaking ngipin sa harap, malapad na buntot, at kilala sa paggawa ng mga dam sa mga ilog. Maaari ring tumukoy sa langis na mula rito.
original_explanation: This is one of those words you only encounter in a science textbook or a crossword puzzle. A beaver. A what? Exactly. We don't have them in the Philippines, so the only 'kastor' we know is probably 'castor oil', the legendary pampurga your lola threatens you with.
usage_notes: Very rare in conversation as beavers are not native to the Philippines. More commonly associated with 'langis-kastor' or castor oil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kastor** ay isang mahusay na arkitekto ng kalikasan.","translation":"The **beaver** is an excellent architect of nature."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang **kastor** sa pagtatayo ng mga dam gamit ang mga puno.","translation":"The **beaver** is known for building dams using trees."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng suklay na may maliliit at magkakadikit na ngipin, karaniwang ginagamit sa pag-alis ng kuto. Sa metaporikal na gamit, ito ay nangangahulugang masusing paghahanap o pagsisiyasat.
original_explanation: The OG anti-kuto weapon, that fine-toothed comb your nanay used on your hair in elementary school. By extension, it's what the NBI does when they're investigating a case—a 'salugsog' is a search so thorough, they're basically looking for lice in the country's metaphorical hair.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for the comb or figuratively for a meticulous investigation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **salugsog** para alisin ang mga lisa sa buhok ng kanyang anak.","translation":"She used the **fine-toothed comb** to remove the nits from her child's hair."},{"sentence":"Isinagawa ng mga pulis ang isang masusing **salugsog** sa buong gusali.","translation":"The police conducted a thorough **search** of the entire building."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpulupot o pagyakap nang mahigpit sa isang bagay o tao, tulad ng pagpulupot ng ahas.
original_explanation: Parang yung yakap ng jowa mong seloso/selosa, hindi ka na makahinga. O kaya yung pagkakapulupot ng earphones mo sa bulsa na parang may sariling buhay. Pwede ring ahas, literally.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang pagpulupot ng ahas. Maaari ding gamitin sa matalinhagang paraan para sa isang mahigpit na yakap. Ang anyong pandiwa nito ay 'lingkisin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang ahas na may **lingkis** sa sanga ng puno.","translation":"He saw the snake **coiled** around the tree branch."},{"sentence":"Halos hindi siya makahinga sa mahigpit na **lingkis** ng kanyang ina.","translation":"She could barely breathe from her mother's tight **embrace**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglilinis ng ngipin gamit ang sipilyo at toothpaste.
original_explanation: That thing you're supposed to do three times a day but you only remember after your morning coffee. Your dentist is judging you. It's the sound your housemate makes at 2 AM after a late-night instant noodle snack.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'magsipilyo'. The noun 'sipilyo' means toothbrush.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Habang **nagsisipilyo** ako, naisip ko ang lahat ng maling desisyon ko sa buhay.","translation":"While I **was brushing my teeth**, I thought about all my wrong life decisions."},{"sentence":"**Nagsisipilyo** ka ba bago matulog?","translation":"Do you **brush your teeth** before sleeping?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malambing na awit na kinakanta upang patulugin ang isang sanggol o bata. Kilala rin bilang hele.
etymology: Nagmula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian na *uyayi* na nangangahulugang 'pag-awit ng pampatulog'.
original_explanation: The OG sleep-inducing sound before Spotify's 'Deep Sleep' playlists existed. It's the 'ili-ili tulog anay' your lola would sing to you. An uyayi is a song filled with so much love and tenderness, it can knock out a hyperactive toddler (or a stressed-out adult).
usage_notes: Ang 'hele' ay isang mas karaniwang kasingkahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinantahan ng ina ng isang matamis na **uyayi** ang kanyang anak.","translation":"The mother sang a sweet **lullaby** to her child."},{"sentence":"Ang tunog ng ulan ay parang isang **uyayi** sa aking mga tainga.","translation":"The sound of the rain is like a **lullaby** to my ears."}]

meaning_filipino: Sumasang-ayon, umaayon, o nababatay sa isang pamantayan, kasunduan, o utos.
original_explanation: Kapag sinabi ng nanay mo na, 'Umuwi ka bago mag-10 PM,' at umuwi ka ng 9:59 PM, komporme ka sa utos niya. Kapag ang presyo sa resibo ay tugma sa presyo sa estante, komporme rin 'yan. It's about things matching up as they should.
usage_notes: Often used with 'sa' (e.g., 'komporme sa batas' - in accordance with the law). Can also mean 'agreeable'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat ang lahat ng desisyon ay **komporme** sa patakaran ng kumpanya.","translation":"All decisions must be **in accordance with** company policy."},{"sentence":"**Komporme** ako sa mungkahi mo.","translation":"I am **agreeable** to your suggestion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho ay mangolekta ng bayad, utang, o taya.
original_explanation: The friendly neighborhood collector. Sila yung nagpapaalala sa'yo na may obligasyon ka, from your monthly hulugan sa appliance, to your taya sa jueteng (oops!), to the ambagan for the fiesta. Pag nakita mo siyang papalapit sa gate niyo, alam mo na: "May bayarin na naman!"
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga nangongolekta ng bayad para sa utang, hulugan, o ilegal na sugal tulad ng jueteng.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinihintay ko ang **kobrador** mula sa appliance store para sa buwanang hulog.","translation":"I'm waiting for the **collector** from the appliance store for the monthly payment."},{"sentence":"Nahuli ng mga pulis ang **kobrador** ng jueteng.","translation":"The police arrested the jueteng bet **collector**."}]

meaning_filipino: Subukang gawin ang isang bagay, lalo na ang isang mahirap o mapanganib; magkaroon ng intensyon o balak.
original_explanation: This is the verb for 'A for effort.' It's when you try to do something, but there's a strong implication that you might fail. 'Nag-tangka siyang magluto ng adobo, pero nasunog.' (He attempted to cook adobo, but it got burnt.) It often carries a hint of daring or even foolishness. When someone tries to do something bad, like 'magtangkang magnakaw' (to attempt to steal), it's definitely negative.
usage_notes: Often implies an unsuccessful or incomplete action. Can have neutral or negative connotations depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magtangka** na tumakas dahil mahuhuli ka rin.","translation":"Don't **attempt** to escape because you will eventually be caught."},{"sentence":"**Nagtangka** siyang ayusin ang sirang gripo pero lalo lang lumakas ang tulo.","translation":"He **tried** to fix the broken faucet but the leak just got worse."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang bagay na maging malinaw, maliwanag, o madaling maunawaan.
original_explanation: This is what you tell your partner after they give you a one-word answer: "Magpalinaw ka nga, ano'ng ibig sabihin ng 'K'?" It's the act of demanding clarity. It can be literal, like waiting for the floodwaters to clear ('magpalinaw ng tubig'), or figurative, like trying to understand confusing instructions from your boss.
usage_notes: A causative verb. The subject causes something else to become clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta ako sa HR para **magpalinaw** tungkol sa bagong patakaran ng kumpanya.","translation":"I went to HR **to get clarification** on the company's new policy."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magpalinaw** ng isip bago gumawa ng mahalagang desisyon.","translation":"We need **to clear** our minds before making an important decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging masaya; isang pagdiriwang o okasyon na puno ng galak at ligaya.
original_explanation: This is the vibe at a Filipino family reunion when the lechon arrives. It's the pure joy of getting your 13th-month pay. It can be the feeling itself (happiness) or the event causing it (a party). Think fiestas, Christmas parties, and karaoke nights that last until 3 AM.
usage_notes: Can refer to the abstract feeling of happiness ('kaligayahan') or a concrete event like a party or festival.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **kasayahan** ang buong bahay noong Pasko.","translation":"The whole house was full of **festivity** during Christmas."},{"sentence":"Wala siyang mapagsidlan ng kanyang **kasayahan** nang malaman niyang nakapasa siya sa board exam.","translation":"He couldn't contain his **happiness** when he found out he passed the board exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng impeksiyon sa balat na sanhi ng fungus, na nagiging sanhi ng makati at pabilog na mga marka.
original_explanation: That annoying, itchy, circular rash that makes you want to scratch your skin off. It's the skin condition that anti-fungal cream commercials love to feature. If someone says "may buni ka," it's not a compliment. Time to visit the derma or the pharmacy!
usage_notes: A common term in Filipino for the fungal skin infection tinea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpahid siya ng gamot sa kanyang **buni** sa braso.","translation":"He applied medicine to the **ringworm** on his arm."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagang balbal sa internet para sa mga Pilipino, na madalas may negatibong konotasyon at tumutukoy sa mga Pilipinong gumagamit ng nakakainis o bastos na pag-uugali online, lalo na sa mga laro.
etymology: A portmanteau of 'Pinoy' and 'noise', originating from online gaming communities.
original_explanation: The infamous term you hear in the world of online gaming (like Dota 2 or Valorant) when a Filipino player is being, well, annoying. It's a mix of 'Pinoy' and 'noise.' It started as an insult but has been somewhat reclaimed by the community, sometimes used jokingly among Filipino gamers themselves. 'Peenoise pride!' is the sarcastic battle cry.
usage_notes: Primarily used in online gaming and meme culture. Can be offensive depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **peenoise** ng kalaro niya dahil ang ingay niya sa voice chat.","translation":"His teammate called him **peenoise** because he was so noisy on voice chat."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **peenoise**; maglaro ka nang maayos.","translation":"Don't be a **peenoise**; play properly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kemikal na sangkap na idinisenyo upang puksain o patayin ang mga kulisap at iba pang maliliit na peste.
original_explanation: The ultimate weapon against the flying ipis. It's that spray can you grab when a cockroach suddenly gains the ability to fly and terrorize the whole house. Your go-to solution for uninvited six-legged guests.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si tatay ng bagong **pamatay-kulisap** para sa mga langgam sa kusina.","translation":"Dad bought a new **insecticide** for the ants in the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paggamit ng **pamatay-kulisap** at siguraduhing may takip ang mga pagkain.","translation":"Be careful when using **insecticide** and make sure the food is covered."}]

meaning_filipino: Itanggi o hindi aminin ang isang bagay, katotohanan, o relasyon sa isang tao.
original_explanation: The "it wasn't me" verb. Ito 'yung ginagawa ng tropa mo 'pag tinanong kung sino umubos ng huling piraso ng pizza. On a more serious note, this is the Peter-denying-Jesus-thrice kind of verb. "Huwag mo akong ipagkaila pag sikat ka na, ha?"
usage_notes: A strong word for denial, often implying betrayal or hiding the truth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ipagkaila** ang kanyang pagkakasala, ngunit may ebidensya laban sa kanya.","translation":"He tried to **deny** his guilt, but there was evidence against him."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **ipagkaila** na may nararamdaman pa rin siya para sa dati niyang kasintahan.","translation":"It's hard to **deny** that he still has feelings for his ex-girlfriend."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay ng tapang o lakas ng loob sa isang tao.
original_explanation: What a shot of liquor is supposed to do before you confess your feelings. Or the pep talk your best friend gives you before a job interview. It's the act of instilling courage, whether through words, actions, or a little liquid courage. "Bes, patapangin mo ako, aamin na ako sa kanya!"
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The object is the person being made brave. Can also mean 'to make something stronger' in taste, like a soup or sauce, by adding more 'tapang' (potency/strength of flavor).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **patapangin** ang kanyang loob bago ang pagsusulit.","translation":"He is trying to **make himself brave** before the exam."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **patapangin** ang bata sa maling paraan.","translation":"Don't **embolden** the child in the wrong way."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawakang pag-aalsa o pagbabago sa pamahalaan o sistemang panlipunan, kadalasang ginagamitan ng dahas.
original_explanation: Hindi lang ito yung pinag-aralan natin sa history class. Ito rin yung nangyayari sa office kapag nagtaas ng presyo ang kape sa pantry, o sa bahay kapag may nagpalit ng Wi-Fi password nang walang pasabi. A call to arms for justice... or for the internet connection.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa malalaking pagbabago, politikal man o teknolohikal (e.g., Industrial Revolution).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang EDSA **Rebolusyon** ay isang mapayapang pag-aalsa ng mamamayan.","translation":"The EDSA **Revolution** was a peaceful citizen uprising."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa kasaysayan ang mga sanhi ng **Rebolusyon** ng 1896.","translation":"The causes of the **Revolution** of 1896 are studied in history."}]

translation: a hit; a strike; a correct guess
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-abot o pagpapatama ng isang bagay sa target nito; isang matagumpay na hula.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling 'pag tinapon mo 'yung basura from across the room at pumasok sa basurahan. Swak! **Tama**! Also, 'yung "high" na nararamdaman, either from love (tinamaan ng pag-ibig) or... other things. "May **tama** na ako, pre."
usage_notes: The pronunciation shifts stress to the second syllable /ta-MA/ compared to the adjective /TA-ma/. It's the root word for 'tamaan' (to be hit) and 'tumama' (to hit).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **tama** ng bola ang sumapol sa kanyang ulo.","translation":"A strong **hit** from the ball struck his head."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng numero sa lotto ay naging **tama** niya.","translation":"All his lottery numbers were a **correct guess**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong propesyonal na nagbibigay ng serbisyong masahe.
original_explanation: The hero your body needs, but not the one it deserves (because you keep slouching). Sila 'yung may magic hands na kayang hanapin 'yung 'lamig' sa likod mo with pinpoint accuracy. The person you trust with your tired muscles and your 'Aray, diyan po!' comments.
usage_notes: Gender-neutral in common Tagalog usage, although it originates from a masculine-ending Spanish word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpatawag ako ng **masahista** para sa nanay kong laging nananakit ang likod.","translation":"I called for a **masseuse** for my mother whose back always hurts."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng sikolohikal na manipulasyon kung saan ang isang tao ay sistematikong pinagdududa sa kanyang sariling memorya, persepsiyon, at katinuan.
etymology: From the 1938 play 'Gas Light' and its film adaptations, which became a popular psychological term in the 2010s.
original_explanation: The official sport of toxic exes and manipulative bosses. It's when they do something wrong, but somehow, by the end of the conversation, you're the one apologizing. "Hindi, nag-o-overreact ka lang" or "I never said that, guni-guni mo lang 'yan" are its national anthems. It makes you question your own sanity until you feel like you're the 'sira' one.
usage_notes: A very modern and popular loanword, often used in conversations about psychology and relationships. It is conjugated using Filipino affixes, e.g., 'gini-gaslight', 'nag-gaslight'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang papayag na i-**gaslight** ka niya; totoo ang naramdaman mo.","translation":"Don't let him/her **gaslight** you; what you felt was real."}]

translation: to be able to poison; to be poisonous
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahan o katangiang magdulot ng lason o pagkalason sa isang tao o hayop.
original_explanation: What a toxic person can do to your good vibes. Or literally, what that sketchy-looking street food *might* do to your stomach. It's the ability to cause harm, whether to your body or your soul. Be careful with what (or who) you consume!
usage_notes: Can refer to the ability of a substance to poison, or the act of being able to poison someone/something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang maliit na patak ng kemikal na iyon ay sapat na para **makalason**.","translation":"One small drop of that chemical is enough **to be able to poison**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kainin ang kabuteng iyan, baka **makalason**.","translation":"Don't eat that mushroom, it might **be poisonous**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang matining na tunog sa pamamagitan ng pagbuga ng hangin mula sa bibig na hinugis sa isang partikular na paraan, o sa pamamagitan ng isang kagamitang tinatawag na pito o sipol.
original_explanation: What your tatay does when he's fixing the car, what the traffic enforcer does when you beat the red light, and what that creepy guy at the corner does when you walk by. It can be a happy, carefree sound or an annoying catcall. The referee's favorite action.
usage_notes: Can refer to whistling with the mouth or with a whistle instrument.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig **sumipol** si Lolo habang nagdidilig ng mga halaman.","translation":"Grandpa loves to **whistle** while watering the plants."}]

translation: will look out at; will view
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtingin sa malayo, karaniwan mula sa isang mataas na lugar, upang pagmasdan ang isang tanawin o abangan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa rooftop bar, hawak ang mamahaling cocktail, looking at the city lights and contemplating your life choices. O 'yung pag-akyat mo sa overpass para lang tingnan ang traffic. "From this viewpoint, I will look out at my future... and see more bills."
usage_notes: Future tense of "magtanaw". Can also mean to look back with gratitude (magtanaw ng utang na loob).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula sa tuktok ng bundok, tayo ay **magtatanaw** sa kagandahan ng kalikasan.","translation":"From the top of the mountain, we **will view** the beauty of nature."},{"sentence":"Lagi siyang **magtatanaw** ng utang na loob sa mga tumulong sa kanya.","translation":"He will always **look back with gratitude** to those who helped him."}]

translation: a type of Filipino vegetable stew
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuing Pilipino na binubuo ng iba't ibang gulay na pinakuluan lamang sa tubig na may bagoong o isda, at hindi ginigisa.
original_explanation: The "clean eating" version of sinigang's cousin. It's a vegetable soup where everything is just boiled together, usually with some bagoong for that umami kick. It's what your lola makes when she wants you to eat your veggies. Healthy, but let's be real, you're probably looking for the fried chicken on the side.
usage_notes: Ang mga sangkap na gulay ay nag-iiba-iba sa bawat rehiyon. Tanyag ang mga bersyon ng Batangas at Pampanga. Ito ay iba sa dinengdeng o laswa, bagaman magkatulad ang konsepto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang **bulanglang** na may kasamang inihaw na isda.","translation":"The **vegetable stew** is delicious with a side of grilled fish."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, gawain, o pahayag na walang kabuluhan, kahalagahan, o epekto.
original_explanation: Like arguing with a troll online or trying to explain to your lola why you're still single. It's an effort that leads nowhere. Basically, shouting into the void. Useless, bes.
usage_notes: A very common expression to denote futility or lack of purpose.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niyang **walang-saysay** ang lahat ng kanyang pagsisikap.","translation":"He felt that all his efforts were **futile**."},{"sentence":"Isang **walang-saysay** na usapan ang nangyari dahil walang nakinig.","translation":"It was a **pointless** conversation because no one was listening."}]

translation: to help carry a load; to assist
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtulong sa pagbuhat o pagdadala ng isang mabigat na bagay, karaniwang ginagawa ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: This is a specific kind of `tulong`. It's when you and a buddy carry a couch up five flights of stairs. It's the physical manifestation of "teamwork makes the dream work," especially when the dream is just getting the new refrigerator into the kitchen without scratching the floor. You can't `tumuwang` alone; it requires a partner.
usage_notes: Past/Completed aspect of the verb. Implies partnership in a physical task.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumuwang** si Pedro sa kanyang ama sa pagbuhat ng sako ng bigas.","translation":"Pedro **helped** his father carry the sack of rice."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **tumuwang** sa iyo sa paglipat ng mga gamit?","translation":"Who **assisted** you in moving the things?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapalit ng perang papel sa mga barya o sensilyo.
original_explanation: The magic trick you ask the tindera to perform on your ₱1000 bill at 7 AM when you're just buying one piece of candy. 'Ate, pasensya na po, pa-sensilyo po sana.' It's the verb form of needing loose change, often met with a sigh or a death stare.
usage_notes: The command form is 'Sensilyuhin mo' or 'Pasensilyo po'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **sensilyuhin** itong isang libong piso ko?","translation":"Can you **break** this one thousand peso bill of mine **into small change**?"},{"sentence":"Kailangang **sensilyuhin** ang malalaking pera para may panukli sa mga customer.","translation":"The large bills need to be **exchanged for coins** to have change for the customers."}]

translation: going in and out repeatedly; having a criminal record
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paulit-ulit na pagpasok at paglabas sa isang lugar. Sa kolokyal na gamit, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang tao na madalas makulong at mapalaya.
etymology: Mula sa pinagsamang salitang `labas` (out) at `masok` (isang baryasyon ng `pasok`, in).
original_explanation: This is the revolving door of life. Pwedeng literal, like a Grab driver na **labas-masok** sa village gate. Or, it can be a "guest" of the Bilibid Hilton, yung tipo na parang may season pass sa kulungan. "Oh, si Mang Kanor, labas-masok na naman 'yan sa presinto."
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang isang taong may kasaysayan ng pagkakakulong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay kilala bilang isang **labas-masok** sa bilangguan.","translation":"He is known for being **in and out** of prison."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang trabaho, **labas-masok** siya sa opisina ng hepe.","translation":"Because of his job, he's constantly **going in and out** of the chief's office."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng panonood o pag-broadcast ng media nang direkta sa internet, tulad ng mga pelikula, serye, o laro.
etymology: Taglish, from English "stream" with Tagalog affix "nag-".
original_explanation: The official past time of the 'puyat' nation. This is you at 3 AM, telling yourself "isa na lang na episode" while watching a K-drama, or watching your favorite gamer shout after getting sniped. It's how we consume content now, from Netflix to a live-selling 'ate' on Facebook.
usage_notes: A very common Taglish word for the present progressive tense. The past tense is "nag-stream".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumagal ang internet kasi sabay-sabay kaming **nagsistream** ng Netflix.","translation":"The internet slowed down because we were all **streaming** Netflix at the same time."},{"sentence":"Sino ang paborito mong gamer na **nagsistream** sa Twitch?","translation":"Who is your favorite gamer who **streams** on Twitch?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ibon na karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga basang lugar o latian, partikular ang espesye na *Porzana carolina*.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'sora', isang uri ng ibon.
original_explanation: This isn't the spiky-haired hero from Kingdom Hearts. Ito 'yung ibon na malamang hindi mo pa nakikita sa totoong buhay unless birdwatcher ka o nakatira ka malapit sa isang latian. It's a shy, secretive bird, kind of like your introvert friend at a party.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-espesipikong termino na pangunahing ginagamit sa ornitolohiya o ng mga mahilig sa ibon. Hindi karaniwang naririnig sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita ang mga birdwatcher ng isang pambihirang **sora** sa Candaba Swamp.","translation":"The birdwatchers saw a rare **sora** at the Candaba Swamp."}]

translation: to go on strike; to revolt
meaning_filipino: Ang sama-samang pagtigil sa paggawa o pagtutol ng isang grupo laban sa isang awtoridad o patakaran bilang anyo ng protesta.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'aklas' (strike/revolt) at unlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: When the whole team has had enough of the toxic boss and decides to file a group resignation. Or when workers protest for better wages. On a smaller scale, it's when you and your siblings team up and refuse to do chores until your parents increase your allowance. It's a collective 'We've had enough!' moment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umaklas** ang mga manggagawa dahil sa mababang sahod at hindi makatarungang kondisyon sa trabaho.","translation":"The workers **went on strike** due to low wages and unfair working conditions."},{"sentence":"Nagbanta ang mga estudyante na **umaklas** kung hindi ibababa ang matrikula.","translation":"The students threatened **to revolt** if the tuition fee is not lowered."}]

translation: something used to expose or reveal
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, salita, o kilos na ginagamit upang ilantad o isiwalat ang isang lihim o kamalian.
etymology: From `pang-` (which becomes `pam-`) + `buko` (to expose, to find out).
original_explanation: This is the 'receipt' you drop to win an argument. The screenshot, the audio recording, the CCTV footage. It's the piece of evidence you use for the grand reveal, the weapon for your 'Marites moment'. Not to be confused with the act itself (`pambubuko`). This is the *tool* for the act.
usage_notes: More specific than `pambubuko`. `Pambuko` is the instrument/means, while `pambubuko` is the action. However, they are often used interchangeably in casual speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang litratong ito ang gagamitin kong **pambuko** sa kanya.","translation":"I will use this photograph as my tool **to expose** him."},{"sentence":"Naghanap siya ng matibay na ebidensya bilang **pambuko** laban sa politiko.","translation":"He looked for strong evidence to use **for exposing** the politician."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos o paggalaw nang pabalik-balik dahil sa pagiging maluwag ng pagkakakabit o pagkakapuwesto.
original_explanation: This is what happens to a screw that isn't tight enough, or a tooth that's about to fall out. It's that wobbly table leg at the karinderya that you have to fix with a folded piece of paper. Figuratively, 'may kalog' means someone is a bit crazy or eccentric. "May kalog ata sa utak 'yan."
usage_notes: Describes a state of looseness or instability. The causative form is `makalog` (to be shaken). The verb `mag-alog` means "to shake something."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magkalog** ang turnilyo ng upuan.","translation":"The chair's screw started to **become loose**."},{"sentence":"Delikado ang tulay na iyan dahil **nagkakalog** na ang mga tabla.","translation":"That bridge is dangerous because the planks are already **becoming shaky**."}]

translation: to be filled with; to have something poured onto
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng laman sa pamamagitan ng paglilipat ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay likido o butil, mula sa isang lalagyan; malagyan.
original_explanation: What you hope happens to your bank account on payday. Or when your friend finally shares the 'chismis' and fills you in on the details. It's the act of being the recipient of a transfer, whether it's water into a glass, Gcash to your phone, or tea (gossip) into your brain.
usage_notes: This verb is in the 'ma- ... -an' form, indicating potential and location. It means 'to be able to be the recipient of a pouring/transfer'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha ang baso nang **masalinan** na kita ng juice.","translation":"Please get the glass so I can **pour** juice **into it** for you."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **masalinan** ng biyaya ang lahat ng nangangailangan.","translation":"I hope all those in need may **be filled** with blessings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-ukol na ginagamit upang tukuyin ang paksa o tema ng isang usapin.
etymology: Ang 'hinggil' ay may hindi tiyak na pinagmulan, ngunit ang pariralang 'hinggil sa' ay gumaganap bilang isang yunit.
original_explanation: The formal, 'email-to-your-professor' version of 'about.' You use this when you want to sound smart in a meeting. 'My presentation is *hinggil sa* Q3 KPIs.' It's the 'as per my last email' of prepositions.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na pariralang pang-ukol. Sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap, mas karaniwan ang 'tungkol sa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang seminar ay **hinggil sa** tamang pangangalaga sa kalikasan.","translation":"The seminar is **regarding** the proper care for the environment."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang ilang katanungan **hinggil sa** bagong patakaran.","translation":"He has some questions **concerning** the new policy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nakikibahagi sa mga laro ng pagkakataon na may kasamang taya o pusta, karaniwan ay pera.
original_explanation: This is someone who lives by the mantra 'one more game.' From tong-its with the kapitbahay to online casinos, a manunugal is always chasing the thrill of the win. They're the ones who say 'bawi na lang next time' after losing their 13th-month pay. Their life is a high-stakes game of 'bahala na si Batman.'
usage_notes: Carries a generally negative connotation, implying addiction or irresponsibility, but can also be used neutrally.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pera ang nawala sa **manunugal** na iyon.","translation":"That **gambler** lost a lot of money."},{"sentence":"Ipinayo sa kanya na iwasan ang pagiging isang **manunugal**.","translation":"He was advised to avoid being a **gambler**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagsasaad na ang sinabi ay isang biro lamang at hindi dapat seryosohin. Katumbas ng "biro lang".
etymology: A variant of 'charot,' likely influenced by gay lingo.
original_explanation: A softer, more playful version of "charot." It's the "hehe, joke lang po" disclaimer you add after saying something slightly shady or making a wild claim. Often used with a smile to diffuse any potential tension.
usage_notes: A softer, more playful alternative to 'charot.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Libre kita mamaya... **charing**!","translation":"My treat later... **just kidding**!"},{"sentence":"Ang ganda mo ngayon, ah! Mukha kang mayaman. **Charing** lang!","translation":"You look beautiful today! You look rich. **Just kidding**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mahinhin, mayumi, at may malinis na puri.
original_explanation: The vibe of Maria Clara, but make it modern. It's about being low-key, humble, and not flexing on the 'gram. It's the 'hindi ako maganda, cute lang' energy. In older contexts, it's the gold standard for a 'dalagang Pilipina,' but now it's more about having a quiet confidence and grace.
usage_notes: Often associated with traditional Filipino values of modesty, especially for women.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkamatimtiman** ay isa sa mga katangiang hinahangaan sa kanya.","translation":"Her **modesty** is one of the traits admired in her."},{"sentence":"Sa lumang panitikan, ang **pagkamatimtiman** ay isang mahalagang katangian ng isang dalaga.","translation":"In old literature, **demureness** was an important quality of a maiden."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal at magalang na tawag sa isang babae, lalo na sa isang may katungkulan o mataas na posisyon.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na 'madam', na mula sa Pranses na 'ma dame' (aking ginang).
original_explanation: The official title for your boss, your client, a strict teacher, or any woman in a position of authority you don't want to mess with. Also what you call the tita who asks 'kelan ka ikakasal?' just to be respectfully sarcastic. 'Yes, madam.'
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang hiram na salita na ginagamit sa mga pormal na okasyon at sa negosyo sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"'Ano po ang maipaglilingkod ko sa inyo, **madam**?' tanong ng saleslady.","translation":"'How may I help you, **ma'am**?' the saleslady asked."},{"sentence":"Ipapasa ko na po ang report kay **Madam** Cruz.","translation":"I will now pass the report to **Madam** Cruz."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-abot, pagsasakatuparan, o pagiging totoo ng isang pangarap, layunin, o pangako.
original_explanation: This is the feeling when your Shopee order finally arrives. Kidding aside, it's the *~official~* realization of a dream. Passing the board exams, graduating, or finally opening that coffee shop you've always wanted—that's the katuparan of your dreams. The ultimate #SanaAll moment becoming your #FinallyMine moment.
usage_notes: Deeply associated with dreams, promises, and goals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang makapagtapos ng pag-aaral ay **katuparan** ng aking mga pangarap.","translation":"Graduating is the **fulfillment** of my dreams."},{"sentence":"Nagagalak kami sa **katuparan** ng inyong mga plano.","translation":"We are happy for the **realization** of your plans."}]

translation: to ponder, to reflect deeply upon
meaning_filipino: Ang malalim at paulit-ulit na pag-iisip o pagninilay-nilay sa isang bagay o ideya.
original_explanation: This is next-level overthinking. It's not just 'isipin' (to think), it's turning something over and over in your mind, like a mental rotisserie chicken. You do this when you're trying to make a big life decision, analyzing a cryptic text from your crush, or just having a 3 AM existential crisis.
usage_notes: A more literary and intense version of 'pag-isipan'. The repetition of 'guna' emphasizes the repetitive, deep nature of the thought process.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **gunagunahin** ang mga posibleng kahihinatnan ng iyong desisyon.","translation":"You need to **ponder** the possible consequences of your decision."},{"sentence":"Lagi niyang **ginugunaguna** ang sinabi mo kahapon.","translation":"He is always **reflecting deeply upon** what you said yesterday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang patag na disk na gawa sa vinyl kung saan naka-ukit ang tunog na muling pinapatugtog sa pamamagitan ng isang turntable o ponograpo.
etymology: From Spanish `placa` (plate, plaque), extended to mean a flat disc.
original_explanation: What your tito or dad calls their "vinyls." Before Spotify and MP3s, this was the height of music technology. Now, it's back in style for hipsters and audiophiles who swear the "warmth" of a plaka is superior. Also, a source of major 'hugot' when you hear the phrase "parang sirang plaka" (like a broken record).
usage_notes: Often used in the idiom "sirang plaka" (broken record) to describe someone who is repetitive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May koleksyon ng mga lumang **plaka** ang lolo ko.","translation":"My grandfather has a collection of old **vinyl records**."},{"sentence":"Paulit-ulit ka, para kang sirang **plaka**!","translation":"You're so repetitive, you're like a broken **record**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na litrato, karaniwang kasinglaki ng isang business card, na nagtatampok sa isang artista, lalo na ang mga K-pop idol, na kasama sa mga album o merchandise.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'photocard', isang portmanteau ng 'photo' at 'card'.
original_explanation: The modern-day anting-anting for K-pop stans. This small piece of laminated paper featuring your bias can either make your day or drain your G-cash account. The thrill of the 'pabunot' (random pull) is real. Trading, selling, and hunting for that rare 'PC' is a national sport. 'WTS/LFB PC ni bias' is a common battle cry on stan Twitter PH.
usage_notes: Isang mahalagang bahagi ng kultura ng K-pop at pagkolekta ng merchandise. Kadalasang tinatawag na 'PC'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ang makuha kong **photocard** sa album ay si Jungkook!","translation":"I hope the **photocard** I get in the album is Jungkook!"}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi angkop, hindi wasto, o hindi sumasang-ayon sa isang pamantayan, batas, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: When your outfit doesn't match the dress code, or your joke doesn't land at a formal dinner. 'Di-naaayon ang suot mo sa simbahan!' It's that feeling of being out of place or doing something that goes against the rules, written or unwritten. It’s the corporate way of saying 'That's not how we do things here.'
usage_notes: Often used in formal or official contexts to mean 'contrary to' or 'in violation of'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga kilos ay **di-naaayon** sa patakaran ng kumpanya.","translation":"His actions are **not in accordance with** company policy."},{"sentence":"Isang tugon na **di-naaayon** sa tanong ang kaniyang ibinigay.","translation":"He gave a response that was **inappropriate** for the question."}]

translation: to command; to order; to decree
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng isang pormal na utos, kautusan, o direktiba na dapat sundin.
original_explanation: This is what your boss does on a Friday afternoon, right before you're about to log off. 'Pakigawa nito, ASAP.' That's them using their power to `mag-atas`. Also what your nanay does when she wants the house cleaned.
usage_notes: Carries a formal and authoritative tone, often used in legal, military, or managerial contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang pangulo na **mag-atas** ng agarang pagpapatupad ng bagong batas.","translation":"The president decided to **decree** the immediate implementation of the new law."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nag-atas** sa iyo na gawin iyan?","translation":"Who **ordered** you to do that?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon kung saan ang pangunahing gawain ay ang pag-inom ng alak o anumang inuming nakalalasing; maaari ring tumukoy sa lugar kung saan nagaganap ang pag-inom.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "inom" na may hulaping "-an".
original_explanation: The Filipino version of group therapy, but with more San Miguel, pulutan, and a videoke machine blasting My Way. It's where secrets are spilled, hugot lines are born, and someone inevitably becomes the 'tagay master'. Starts with 'Isang bote lang,' ends with 'Sino ako? Bakit ako nandito?' the next morning.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa kaganapan o sa lugar. Hal: "Pumunta tayo sa inuman" (lugar). "Nasa inuman kami" (kaganapan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkayayaan ang magkakaibigan para sa isang **inuman** pagkatapos ng trabaho.","translation":"The friends decided to go for a **drinking session** after work."},{"sentence":"Maingay sa kapitbahay dahil may **inuman**.","translation":"It's noisy at the neighbor's house because there's a **drinking session**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naging walang bisa o saysay; pinawalang-bisa.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na sinabi mo sa jowa mo, "Pagod na ako," tapos ang sagot niya, "Pagod din ako." Boom! Na-invalidate ang pagod mo. It's when your winning lottery ticket turns out to be from last year's draw. All that excitement for nothing.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para ipahayag na ang isang bagay ay nawalan na ng bisa o kinansela na, pormal man o sa usaping damdamin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Na-invalidate** ang boto niya dahil sa maling pagpuno ng balota.","translation":"Her vote **was invalidated** due to incorrectly filling out the ballot."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko **na-invalidate** lahat ng pinaghirapan ko.","translation":"I feel like all my hard work **was invalidated**."}]

translation: I like that; That's my type; I'm for that
meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahayag ng matinding pagkagusto, pagsang-ayon, o pag-apruba sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon.
etymology: Isang pariralang balbal na binubuo ng "bet" (gusto), "ko" (akin), at "'yan" (iyan).
original_explanation: The official stamp of "I LIKE IT!" in Pinoy slang. Sinasabi mo 'to 'pag may nakita kang damit na bagay sa'yo, narinig na chismis na juicy, o nakitang pagkain na mukhang masarap. "Bet ko 'yan" is a whole mood. It's an affirmation, a declaration, a vibe.
usage_notes: Isang kumpletong pangungusap na nagpapahayag ng personal na gusto o pag-apruba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wow, ang ganda ng sapatos! **Bet ko 'yan**!","translation":"Wow, those shoes are beautiful! **I like those**!"},{"sentence":"Plano nilang mag-videoke mamaya. **Bet ko 'yan**!","translation":"They plan to do videoke later. **I'm for that**!"}]

translation: to shred; to tear to pieces
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pagpunit o pagwasak sa isang bagay hanggang sa maging maliliit na piraso.
original_explanation: This is what you do to an ex's photos after a bad breakup. It's not just 'punit' (tear), it's total annihilation. Think of a cat with a roll of toilet paper, or what a politician's reputation looks like after a scandal. It can be literal, like shredding documents, or figurative, like destroying someone's argument in a debate. *Luray-luray* means completely shredded.
usage_notes: Implies a more violent or thorough tearing than `punitin`. The state of being shredded is `luray`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **lurayin** ang sulat na nagdulot sa akin ng pighati.","translation":"I want to **shred** the letter that caused me anguish."},{"sentence":"Ang pusa ay mahilig **lurayin** ang anumang papel na makita nito.","translation":"The cat likes to **tear to pieces** any paper it sees."}]

translation: to mess up; to confuse; to disturb
meaning_filipino: Gawing magulo o hindi maayos ang isang bagay; lituhin ang isip ng isang tao; gambalain.
original_explanation: What your younger sibling does to your room two minutes after you've cleaned it. Also what your ex does to your mind when they text "Hi" at 2 AM. The standard reply is "Huwag mo **guluhin** ang nananahimik na."
usage_notes: A very versatile word. Can refer to messing up a physical space, confusing a person's thoughts, or disturbing someone's peace.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, huwag mong **guluhin** ang mga papel sa aking lamesa.","translation":"Please, don't **mess up** the papers on my desk."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **guluhin** ang isip ko bago ang pagsusulit.","translation":"He's trying to **confuse** my mind before the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: (Di-pormal) Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, gawi, o katatawanan na itinuturing na mababang-uri, magaspang, o walang-pinag-aralan.
etymology: Semantic extension of 'kanal' (gutter), likening the quality to something from a gutter.
original_explanation: When you call something 'kanal', you're saying it's jologs, baduy, or has that distinct 'amoy-estero' vibe. It's the kind of humor your titas might frown upon, the fashion choices that defy all logic, the content you secretly watch at 2 AM. It's the beautiful, chaotic mess of Pinoy pop culture, often embraced with ironic pride.
usage_notes: This is a modern slang term, often used to describe a certain type of humor, aesthetic, or behavior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tawang-tawa ako sa mga **kanal** memes sa Facebook.","translation":"I'm laughing so hard at the **low-brow** memes on Facebook."},{"sentence":"Medyo **kanal** ang dating ng biruan nila, pero nakakatawa.","translation":"Their banter is a bit **gutter**-level, but it's funny."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na bagay mula sa kalawakan na nagliliyab at nag-iiwan ng landas ng liwanag kapag pumasok sa himpapawid ng Daigdig.
original_explanation: A shooting star! That thing you make a wish on, hoping your crush will finally notice you or that your Shopee package will arrive tomorrow. It's space junk, but make it romantic.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with "bulalakaw," which is the native Tagalog term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaswerte namin na makakita ng pagbagsak ng isang **mityoro** kagabi.","translation":"We were so lucky to see a **meteor** fall last night."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o katangian ng pagiging malupit, marahas, o walang-awa na parang hayop.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'salbahe', na hango sa salitang Espanyol na 'salvaje' na nangangahulugang 'wild' o 'savage'.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung level ng ka-toxic-an na ultimo demonyo mapapa-iling na lang. 'Yung ugali na parang laging kulang sa aruga at galit sa mundo. It's giving main villain energy, pero 'yung walang character development.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at medyo malalim na salita na hindi karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Mas madalas gamitin ang 'kalupitan' o 'kabangisan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinondena ng buong mundo ang **kasalbahihan** na naganap sa digmaan.","translation":"The whole world condemned the **savagery** that occurred during the war."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang dulo o lugar na patutunguhan; ang kahihinatnan o kinahinatnan ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: 'Hantong' is the 'and what happened?' part of the story. It's the final destination. 'Saan ba 'to hahantong?' (Where will this lead?) is the question you ask about a budding office romance, a political scandal, or your ever-growing Shopee cart. It's the end of the line, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: This root word is most frequently encountered in its affixed forms, such as 'humantong' (to end up), 'kinahantungan' (the result/outcome), and 'hahantungan' (the future outcome).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kulungan ang **hantong** ng mga masasamang-loob.","translation":"Jail is the **final destination** for criminals."},{"sentence":"Ang di-pagkakaunawaan ay may malungkot na **hantong**.","translation":"The misunderstanding had a sad **outcome**."},{"sentence":"Hindi natin alam kung ano ang magiging **hantong** ng proyektong ito.","translation":"We don't know what the **end result** of this project will be."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang panig ng barya, karaniwang nagpapakita ng isang mukha o simbolo, salungat sa panig na "krus".
original_explanation: This is the "heads" in your "heads or tails" game, but Filipino style: "kara o krus?" It's the deciding factor for who pays for lunch, who gets the last piece of pizza, or who has to do the unang sampa sa presentation. A tiny piece of metal holding immense power.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the phrase "kara o krus" for flipping a coin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan natin kung **kara** o krus ang lalabas.","translation":"Let's see if it will be **heads** or tails."},{"sentence":"Pumili ka, **kara** o krus?","translation":"You choose, **heads** or tails?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging kapareho ng gawi, asal, o kinasanayan ng isang tao.
etymology: From `ka-` (denoting a companion or shared quality) + `ugali` (habit, character).
original_explanation: Your work bestie who also needs coffee at 3 PM sharp. Your sibling who also leaves their clothes on 'the chair'. That's your 'kaugali'. It's finding someone whose weird habits perfectly match your weird habits. It's the 'OMG, you too?!' of friendships.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person with whom one shares a particular trait or behavior. Can also function as a noun ('someone with the same habit').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Ana ay **kaugali** ko sa pagiging maingay tumawa.","translation":"Ana is **someone with the same habit** as me of laughing loudly."},{"sentence":"Hinanap niya ang mga taong **kaugali** niya sa pananaw.","translation":"He looked for people who were **of the same character** as him in perspective."}]

translation: A swarm, a mob, a tumultuous crowd
meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at magulong pagdagsa o pagkukumpulan ng maraming tao sa isang lugar o sa paligid ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: Picture this: a celebrity walks into a mall, or 168 opens a new bale of ukay-ukay. That chaotic, human wave pool you suddenly find yourself in? That's a dumog. You might lose a slipper, but you were *there*.
usage_notes: Often implies a lack of order and a sense of being overwhelmed by the sheer number of people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging isang malaking **dumog** ang concert nang biglang umakyat sa stage si Daniel Padilla.","translation":"The concert became a massive **swarm** when Daniel Padilla suddenly went on stage."},{"sentence":"Iwasan mo ang **dumog** ng mga tao sa Quiapo tuwing Biyernes.","translation":"Avoid the **mob** of people in Quiapo every Friday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali na nakalaan para sa pagsamba ng mga Kristiyano; tumutukoy din sa isang partikular na denominasyong Kristiyano o sa kabuuan ng mga mananampalataya.
etymology: From Spanish 'iglesia' (church), from Latin 'ecclesia', from Ancient Greek 'ἐκκλησία' (ekklēsía, 'assembly').
original_explanation: The building you only see the inside of during Christmas, Easter, and when your tita forces you to go to Simbang Gabi. It's the place for weddings, baptisms, and the occasional 'misa de gallo.' Whether it's the grand Manila Cathedral or the local chapel, the 'iglesya' is a landmark in every Pinoy town.
usage_notes: 'Simbahan' is a more common synonym for the building, while 'Iglesya' can also refer to a specific denomination (e.g., Iglesia ni Cristo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpunta ang pamilya sa **iglesya** para sa misa ng Linggo.","translation":"The family went to **church** for Sunday mass."},{"sentence":"Ang **Iglesya** Katolika ay may malaking impluwensya sa kultura ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The Catholic **Church** has a huge influence on Philippine culture."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkukunwaring banal o relihiyoso; ang pagpapakita ng kabanalan na hindi bukal sa kalooban at kadalasang may layuning mapuri o makakuha ng pabor.
etymology: Ang pag-uulit ng salitang `banal` ay nagpapahiwatig ng panggagaya o pagkukunwari.
original_explanation: This is that person in your feed who posts "God is watching" on a picture of someone wearing shorts, but you know for a fact they ghosted three people last week. It's the performance of holiness, not the practice. It's being more concerned with looking like a saint than actually being a decent human being. All for the 'holy' clout.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang iyong **pagbabanal-banalan**, alam namin ang tunay mong ugali.","translation":"Stop your **sanctimoniousness**, we know your true character."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagbabanal-banalan** ay isang paraan lamang upang makuha ang boto ng mga tao.","translation":"His **pretense of holiness** is just a way to get people's votes."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa isang sistema ng pamahalaan kung saan ang kapangyarihan ay hinahati sa pagitan ng isang sentral na awtoridad at mga nasasakupang yunit pampulitika.
original_explanation: This is about a system of government where power is shared between the national government and local states or regions. Think of it like a group project where the project manager (national gov't) sets the main goals, but each team member (local state) has the freedom to decide how they'll do their part. It's a hot topic in Philippine politics, often debated with the same passion as choosing between Jollibee and McDo.
usage_notes: Primarily used in political and governmental contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng gobyerno ang paglipat sa isang **pederal** na sistema.","translation":"The government is studying the shift to a **federal** system."},{"sentence":"Ang mga batas **pederal** ay ipinapatupad sa buong bansa.","translation":"**Federal** laws are enforced throughout the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagsasabi o pagsusulat ng mga titik na bumubuo sa isang salita sa tamang pagkakasunod-sunod.
original_explanation: That thing you always get wrong on "Filipino" vs "Pilipino". It's the basis of elementary school spelling bees and the reason you get corrected by grammar-conscious friends online. Proper pagbabaybay separates the men from the bois.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to orthography. The loanword 'spelling' is more common in casual conversation.
