usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihirapan ako sa **pagbabaybay** ng mga salitang hiram sa Ingles.","translation":"I have difficulty with the **spelling** of words borrowed from English."},{"sentence":"Itinuturo sa mga bata ang tamang **pagbabaybay** sa unang baitang pa lang.","translation":"Correct **spelling** is taught to children as early as the first grade."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa bilang na isang milyon (1,000,000) o isang napakaraming bilang.
original_explanation: The amount of money you wish you had after every 'petsa de peligro'. It's also the number of chismis you hear in a day. 'Bes, may sang-angaw na rason para maging masaya, 'wag kang magpa-apekto diyan.'
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa paraang eksaherado o hyperbole upang ipahiwatig ang 'napakadami'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanalo siya ng **sang-angaw** na piso sa lotto.","translation":"He won **one million** pesos in the lottery."},{"sentence":"May **sang-angaw** na tanong ang isip ko tungkol sa kanya.","translation":"I have **a million** questions in my mind about him."}]

translation: to criticize harshly, to attack verbally
meaning_filipino: Ang matinding pagpuna o pag-atake sa isang tao o bagay, lalo na sa paraang berbal o sa pamamagitan ng pagsulat, karaniwan sa social media.
original_explanation: When you 'bash' someone, you're not just disagreeing with them. You're going full-on keyboard warrior mode, attacking them personally. It's the national sport on social media, especially when a celebrity does something mildly controversial. The opposite of 'sana all.'
usage_notes: Often used in the context of online criticism. The verb form is often inflected using Filipino affixes, e.g., 'binabash,' 'i-bash.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang i-**bash** dahil lang iba ang opinyon niya.","translation":"Don't **bash** him just because he has a different opinion."},{"sentence":"Lagi siyang bina-**bash** ng mga tao sa internet.","translation":"He is always being **bashed** by people on the internet."}]

translation: to shoo away, to drive off
meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pagtataboy o pagpapaalis sa mga hayop, insekto, o kung minsan ay tao, sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: This is what you do to the fly that won't leave your adobo alone. 'Shoo! Shoo!' That's the essence of **bugawin**. It’s the action of waving your hand to drive away a pesky mosquito, a stray cat asking for food, or that 'marites' neighbor trying to eavesdrop on your conversation.
usage_notes: Commonly used for animals and insects, but can be used colloquially and sometimes rudely for people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bugawin** mo nga 'yung mga langaw sa ibabaw ng pagkain.","translation":"Please **shoo away** the flies from on top of the food."},{"sentence":"Sinubukang **bugawin** ng guwardiya ang mga taong nagkukumpulan sa entrance.","translation":"The guard tried to **drive off** the people crowding at the entrance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pisikal, emosyonal, at mental na pagkapagod na dulot ng matagal at labis na stress, lalo na sa trabaho.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na "burnout," na ginagamit sa modernong sikolohiya.
original_explanation: Ito yung feeling na pagod ka na sa pagod. Yung kaluluwa mo, nag-file na ng resignation letter pero yung katawan mo, kailangan pa rin mag-log in sa work. Pag na-experience mo na 'to, kahit 12 hours of sleep, parang 12 minutes lang. Official status ng mga taga-BPO at healthcare workers tuwing "hell week."
usage_notes: Isang modernong katawagan na malawakang ginagamit sa konteksto ng trabaho at kalusugang pangkaisipan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa sunod-sunod na overtime, nakakaramdam na siya ng matinding **burnout**.","translation":"Because of consecutive overtime shifts, he is now feeling severe **burnout**."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **burnout** sa pamamagitan ng pagkakaroon ng work-life balance.","translation":"Avoid **burnout** by having work-life balance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mag-aaral na may pinakamataas na marka sa kanyang nagtapos na klase, na karaniwang nagbibigay ng talumpati sa pagtatapos.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'bida sa graduation'. Sila yung #1 sa klase, akyatin ang stage with the most medals, at magbibigay ng speech na magpapaiyak sa mga magulang. Sila ang rason kung bakit may "Anak, tignan mo si [insert name of balediktoryan], gayahin mo." pressure from your parents.
usage_notes: A formal academic title.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang anak ni Aling Nena ang naging **balediktoryan** ng klase ngayong taon.","translation":"Aling Nena's child became the class **valedictorian** this year."},{"sentence":"Pinangarap niyang maging **balediktoryan** mula pa noong elementarya.","translation":"She dreamt of becoming the **valedictorian** since elementary school."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kulay na nasa pagitan ng bughaw at pula sa ispektrum ng liwanag; kulay ube.
original_explanation: It's that royal, mysterious color. Think ube halaya, the BTS fandom color, or the color of your lola's favorite flower. It's not quite blue, not quite purple, it's bioleta.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'ube' or 'lila'. Can also be used as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pininturahan niya ng **bioleta** ang kanyang silid.","translation":"She painted her room **violet**."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang kulay ay **bioleta**.","translation":"Her favorite color is **violet**."}]

translation: to make someone believe; to convince
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagkumbinsi o paghimok sa isang tao na maniwala sa isang bagay, na maaaring totoo o hindi.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pangkauusalan na "pa-" at salitang-ugat na "paniwala".
original_explanation: This is the classic "Marites starter pack." It's what you do when you're trying to sell a story, whether it's a legit business proposal or just convincing your friends that you *really* saw that celeb sa BGC. It’s the art of persuasion, Filipino style.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng panlilinlang o pagkumbinsi sa isang taong may pag-aalinlangan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niya akong **papaniwalain** sa kanyang mga kasinungalingan.","translation":"He tried to **make me believe** his lies."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **papaniwalain** ang mga tao kung wala kang ebidensya.","translation":"It's hard to **convince** people if you don't have evidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Nawalan ng katinuan sa pag-iisip; nabaliw.
original_explanation: This is what happens after a month-long OT with no VLs approved. It's the state of your mind when you're explaining the same thing for the 5th time to a client. It's not just 'broken', it's 'mentally fried'. The ultimate 'sumabog na ang brain cells ko' moment.
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression. The object (e.g., 'bait' (sanity), 'ulo' (head), 'tiyan' (stomach)) specifies what was 'broken' in a non-literal sense. 'Nasira ang tiyan' means to have an upset stomach.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tila **nasira ang bait** niya dahil sa sobrang pagod at puyat.","translation":"It seems he **lost his mind** from extreme exhaustion and lack of sleep."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos niyang malaman ang balita, para siyang **nasira ang ulo** at hindi mapakali.","translation":"After he found out the news, it was like he **went crazy** and couldn't stay still."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling o pagkuha ng bayad para sa isang produkto, serbisyo, o utang.
original_explanation: The most dreaded text message you can receive: "Friend, baka naman..." This is the official verb of the Bumbay, the landlord on the 15th, and your workmate who "forgot" their wallet during lunch last week. The act of "singil" can make or break friendships.
usage_notes: A very common word in financial and commercial transactions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Oras na para **sumingil** ng upa sa mga nangungupahan.","translation":"It's time to **collect** rent from the tenants."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar o bagay na may maraming bato.
original_explanation: 'Yung daan papunta sa hidden falls na 'yan? Super mabato, sis. Kailangan mo ng good hiking shoes, hindi 'yung pekeng Crocs mo. It's the kind of road that makes you question your life choices while trekking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mabato** ang daan patungo sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"The path to the mountain's peak is **rocky**."},{"sentence":"Mahirap magtanim sa **mabatong** lupa.","translation":"It's hard to plant in **stony** soil."}]

translation: to cause to turn yellow, to color yellow
meaning_filipino: Gawing kulay dilaw ang isang bagay, o hayaan itong maging dilaw dahil sa pagkaluma, sakit, o ibang proseso.
etymology: From 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'dilaw' (yellow). 'To cause to be yellow.'
original_explanation: Can mean two things: 1) Actively coloring something yellow, like adding food coloring or dyeing your hair. 'Gusto niyang magpadilaw ng buhok para sa summer.' 2) Letting something become yellow, like old books in a baul, or leaves in the fall. It was also a political term, referring to associating with the 'yellow' political party.
usage_notes: Can be intentional (coloring) or unintentional (aging, decay). Has political undertones in certain contexts in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng luyang dilaw sa kanin para **magpadilaw** nito.","translation":"She added turmeric to the rice to **color it yellow**."},{"sentence":"Ang kakulangan sa tubig ay maaaring **magpadilaw** sa mga dahon ng halaman.","translation":"Lack of water can **cause the leaves of the plant to turn yellow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ama na mag-isang nagpapalaki sa kanyang mga anak nang walang katuwang na asawa o partner.
original_explanation: A real-life superhero who juggles work, cooking, cleaning, and being a dad, all on his own. He's the one packing baon, checking homework, and giving the best hugs. Basically, a 'haligi ng tahanan' with extra steps.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, commonly used in Taglish conversations. The formal Filipino equivalent is 'solong ama'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saludo ako sa mga **singledad** na nagsisikap para sa kanilang mga anak.","translation":"I salute the **single dads** who work hard for their children."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay para sa "karinderya"; isang maliit na kainan na karaniwang naghahain ng mga lutong-bahay.
original_explanation: This is the "old school" or slightly less common spelling of "karinderya." It's like writing "color" vs "colour." Everyone knows what you mean, but one is just seen more often. The food is just as good, though!
usage_notes: Ang "karinderya" ang mas karaniwang ginagamit na baybay sa kasalukuyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bagong bukas na **karinderia** sa kabilang kanto.","translation":"There's a newly opened **eatery** on the other corner."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang kanilang menudo sa **karinderia** na iyon.","translation":"Their menudo at that **eatery** is delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pambihira at kamangha-manghang pangyayari na pinaniniwalaang gawa ng isang higit-sa-karaniwang kapangyarihan, tulad ng Diyos.
original_explanation: When you pass an exam you didn't study for, that's a milagro. When EDSA traffic is clear on a payday Friday, that's a milagro. When your Grab driver finds your house without calling you 5 times, that's a divine milagro. It's God's little "surprise, beshie!" moment in your life.
usage_notes: A very common word used both in religious contexts and sarcastically for any surprisingly fortunate event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **milagro** ang kanyang paggaling mula sa malubhang sakit.","translation":"His recovery from the serious illness was a **miracle**."},{"sentence":"**Milagro** at nakasakay ako agad ng bus ngayong umaga!","translation":"It's a **miracle** I was able to board a bus right away this morning!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng kabanalan na hindi totoo o taos-puso; pagpapanggap na banal.
etymology: From `ka-` + `santo` (saint) + `-han` (suffix indicating a quality or place).
original_explanation: This is the "holier-than-thou" attitude. It's when someone acts super religious and pure on the outside, but their actions don't match. Parang 'yung tita mong laging nasa simbahan pero number one chismosa sa barangay. All form, no substance. #Blessed pero #Judgemental.
usage_notes: Carries a negative and critical connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang iyong **kasantuhan**; alam naman namin ang tunay mong ugali.","translation":"Stop your **pretense of holiness**; we all know your true character."},{"sentence":"Marami ang naiinis sa **kasantuhan** ng politikong iyon.","translation":"Many are annoyed by that politician's **hypocrisy**."}]

translation: can be done; can be carried out; can be implemented
meaning_filipino: May kakayahang isakatuparan, gawin, o ipatupad ang isang plano, gawain, o proyekto. Ito ay tumutukoy sa posibilidad na mangyari ang isang bagay sa hinaharap.
etymology: From `ma-` (potential prefix) + `isasagawa` (future tense of `isagawa`, which comes from `i-` + `sagawa`). The ultimate root is `gawa` (to do, to make).
original_explanation: This is the "Kaya ba?" or "Kakayanin ba?" of project management. Before you commit to that O.T. (overtime), you ask your boss, "Maisasagawa ba natin 'to by the deadline?" It's the future tense of 'can do', full of hope and a little bit of anxiety.
usage_notes: This verb is in the potential, future contemplative aspect, indicating that something can possibly be done or accomplished in the future.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi **maisasagawa** ang proyekto kung walang sapat na pondo.","translation":"The project **cannot be carried out** without sufficient funds."},{"sentence":"Tingin mo ba **maisasagawa** natin ang lahat ng plano para sa bakasyon?","translation":"Do you think we **can implement** all our plans for the vacation?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging payat na payat, lalo na sa mukha, na nagpapakita ng gutom, pagod, o sakit.
original_explanation: The look you have after a week of OT, surviving only on coffee and instant noodles. Your cheeks are sunken in, and you look like you've seen a ghost (or your credit card bill). It's the ultimate 'haggard na haggard' look.
usage_notes: Describes a state of extreme thinness, often with a negative connotation of being unhealthy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **lungkag** ang kanyang mga pisngi dahil sa matinding karamdaman.","translation":"His cheeks became **gaunt** due to severe illness."},{"sentence":"Napansin ko ang **lungkag** na anyo ng pulubi sa kalye.","translation":"I noticed the **emaciated** appearance of the beggar on the street."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang seremonya o ritwal na isinasagawa upang pormal na tapusin ang panahon ng pagluluksa para sa isang yumaong mahal sa buhay, karaniwang isang taon matapos ang kamatayan.
etymology: From `pagbababa` (the act of bringing down/ending) and `luksa` (mourning). Literally 'the lowering of mourning'.
original_explanation: This is the cultural 'go signal' to start wearing colors again after a year of wearing black for a departed loved one. It's the transition from 'sana all' to 'move on.' It's a bittersweet event, a mix of remembrance and the permission to fully live again, often marked by a mass and a family meal.
usage_notes: A significant Filipino cultural practice marking the first death anniversary. The family traditionally wears black or white during the mourning period.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginanap ang **pagbababa ng luksa** para sa lolo noong isang linggo.","translation":"The **end of the mourning period** for grandpa was held last week."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na propesyonal na sinanay upang puksain ang mga mapanganib na sunog. Tinatawag ding bombero.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga real-life superheroes na sumusugod sa apoy habang tayong lahat ay tumatakbo palayo. Also, the reason why calendars with shirtless men exist. They're the ultimate 'sana all' when it comes to bravery.
usage_notes: The native Tagalog term 'bombero' (from Spanish 'bombero') is more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang maging isang **firefighter** paglaki niya.","translation":"He wants to be a **firefighter** when he grows up."},{"sentence":"Dumating agad ang mga **firefighter** para apulahin ang sunog.","translation":"The **firefighters** arrived quickly to put out the fire."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at malakas na pagpalo o paghampas sa isang bagay o tao, karaniwan gamit ang isang mahabang bagay tulad ng patpat o pamalo.
original_explanation: Imagine a cartoon character going wild with a club. Or how you beat a dusty rug ('yantok') against a wall. It's a violent, repetitive hitting motion. It's the action that goes with the sound 'PAK! PAK! PAK!'. Not a gentle tap, but a full-on, no-holds-barred 'hambalos'.
usage_notes: A very strong and violent word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa galit, nauwi sa **paghahambalos** ng pinto ang kanilang pag-aaway.","translation":"Because of anger, their fight ended with the **thrashing** of the door."},{"sentence":"Ang **paghahambalos** sa mga unan ay isang paraan niya para maglabas ng sama ng loob.","translation":"The **striking** of pillows is one of his ways to release pent-up frustration."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng biglaang pagbuga o paglabas ng materyales tulad ng lava, abo, at gas mula sa isang bulkan.
original_explanation: The Earth's version of a major breakout. When a volcano can't hold it in anymore and just spews lava and ash everywhere. Think Mayon Volcano having a bad day. It's also what happens to your face after eating too much oily food.
usage_notes: Ito ang mas pormal at Espanyol na baybay. Ang "erupsyon" ay ang mas karaniwang kolokyal na baybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdulot ng malawakang paglikas ang **erupsiyon** ng Bulkang Pinatubo.","translation":"The **eruption** of Mount Pinatubo caused a massive evacuation."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentipiko ang mga senyales ng posibleng **erupsiyon**.","translation":"Scientists are studying the signs of a possible **eruption**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na tumutukoy sa isang tao na may kabagalan sa pag-iisip, tanga, o hangal.
etymology: Origin uncertain, likely from gayspeak or street slang.
original_explanation: The more 'gentle' way of calling someone 'tanga'. It's what your friends call you when you trip on a flat surface or ask an obvious question. It has a hint of affection, like 'bless your heart'. If 'bobo' is a punch, 'shunga' is a playful slap.
usage_notes: A very common, informal term. While less harsh than 'tanga' or 'bobo', it can still be offensive depending on the tone and context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **shunga** ko! Naiwan ko ang wallet ko sa bahay.","translation":"I'm so **silly**! I left my wallet at home."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **shunga**, halata namang niloloko ka lang niya.","translation":"Don't be **stupid**, it's obvious he's just fooling you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang modernong kolokyal na termino para sa mainitang pagtatalo o awayan na nangyayari sa internet, partikular sa mga social media platform, comment section, o forum.
etymology: From English 'keyboard' + 'fights'. A direct calque used in Taglish contexts.
original_explanation: This is the modern-day sabong (cockfight), but instead of roosters, you have two (or more) people furiously typing angry comments at each other on Facebook or Twitter. It's a battle of caps lock, ad hominem attacks, and 'receipts' (screenshots). The prize? Bragging rights and the temporary satisfaction of 'winning' an argument with a stranger you'll never meet.
usage_notes: A slang term that has become very common with the rise of social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napuyat na naman ako kakabasa ng mga **keyboard fights** sa comment section.","translation":"I stayed up late again reading the **online arguments** in the comment section."},{"sentence":"Iwasan mo nang pumatol sa mga **keyboard fights**; sayang lang sa oras.","translation":"Avoid engaging in **keyboard fights**; it's just a waste of time."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagsasaad na ang isang bagay na matagal nang hinihintay o inaasahan ay naganap, dumating, o natapos na.
original_explanation: The feeling of getting your 13th-month pay. The moment your Shopee parcel arrives. The end credits of a 3-hour meeting. 'Sa wakas!' is the national sigh of relief when the 'sana' becomes 'eto na'. It’s the ultimate 'The wait is over!' exclamation, often accompanied by a sigh or a silent prayer of thanks.
usage_notes: Nagpapahayag ng kaginhawaan, katuparan, o ang pagtatapos ng isang mahabang paghihintay. Madalas gamitan ng tandang padamdam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sa wakas**, Biyernes na!","translation":"**Finally**, it's Friday!"},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng sampung taon, **sa wakas** ay natikman din niyang muli ang adobo ng kanyang ina.","translation":"After ten years, he **at last** tasted his mother's adobo again."}]

translation: to be in several piles; to be piled up messily
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng maraming bagay na nakasalansan o nakatambak sa iba't ibang tumpok nang walang kaayusan.
original_explanation: This is your room when your mom says, "Linisin mo 'yang kwarto mo!" It's when clothes, books, and random stuff are in messy little mountains everywhere. Parang 'yung mga papeles sa government office na naghihintay ng pirma.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a messy or chaotic state of piled objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagkabuntun-bunton** ang mga maruruming damit sa sahig ng kanyang silid.","translation":"The dirty clothes were **in messy piles** on the floor of his room."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **magkabuntun-bunton** ang mga gawain mo.","translation":"Don't let your tasks **pile up messily**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghigop ng isang likido sa pamamagitan ng bibig, kadalasan gamit ang isang dayami o straw.
original_explanation: The literal meaning. What you do with a straw to your Zagu or milk tea. 'Sipsipin mo na 'yang bubble tea mo, baka matunaw ang yelo.' It's the action of sipping.
usage_notes: The stress is on the second syllable for the verb/action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **sipsipin** ang sabaw ng sinigang direkta mula sa mangkok.","translation":"He likes to **sip** the sinigang broth directly from the bowl."},{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan niyang **sinipsip** ang mainit na kape.","translation":"He slowly **sipped** the hot coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa teolohiyang Kristiyano, ito ang pangalan ng isang arkanghel na nagrebelde laban sa Diyos at naging si Satanas o ang Diyablo.
original_explanation: The OG 'fall from grace.' Before he was Satan, he was *Lusiper*, the 'light-bringer.' In Pinoy culture, his name is the go-to for anything supremely evil or mischievous. A naughty kid might be called 'anak ni Lusiper'. He's the ultimate kontrabida in the celestial teleserye.
usage_notes: The spelling is adapted from the Spanish 'Lucifer'. It is used in religious and cultural contexts to refer to the Devil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa Bibliya, si **Lusiper** ay isang kerubing naging simbolo ng kasamaan.","translation":"According to the Bible, **Lucifer** was a cherub who became a symbol of evil."},{"sentence":"Ang kuwento ng pagbagsak ni **Lusiper** ay isang babala laban sa pagmamataas.","translation":"The story of **Lucifer's** fall is a warning against pride."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtanggap o pagkakaroon ng pananalig sa isang bagay, pahayag, o tao na magaganap sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The future tense of belief. This is the word you use when your friend promises to treat you for lunch "next time" and you sarcastically say, "Maniniwala na sana ako..." (I was about to believe...). It's the currency of trust, hope, and sometimes, extreme gullibility. It's the foundation of every "sana all" moment.
usage_notes: Future tense of 'maniwala'. It expresses a future state of believing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit ano pa ang sabihin nila, **maniniwala** ako sa iyo.","translation":"Whatever they say, I **will believe** you."},{"sentence":"Sino ba ang **maniniwala** sa ganyang kalokohang kwento?","translation":"Who **will believe** such a ridiculous story?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matinding liwanag na pansamantalang nakabubulag o nakahihirap sa pagtingin.
original_explanation: That feeling when a car with its high beams on is coming at you, and you suddenly understand what it's like to be a deer in the headlights. Also applies to the "silaw" you feel from a celebrity's fame or your crush's blindingly perfect smile. #NasisilawAko
usage_notes: Can be used literally for light or figuratively for fame, wealth, or beauty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakainis ang **silaw** mula sa kotseng kasalubong.","translation":"The **glare** from the oncoming car is annoying."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masilaw sa yaman, ang mahalaga ay pagkatao.","translation":"Don't be dazzled by wealth, what's important is character."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipulupot ang mga braso sa isang tao o bagay; magsagawa ng pag-akap.
original_explanation: The command or the action. When someone says, 'Akapin mo ako,' they're not just asking for physical contact; they're asking for reassurance, for a silent 'I'm here for you.' It's also what you do to your sweldo on payday before it disappears.
usage_notes: The verb form, directly instructing or describing the act of hugging. Often used interchangeably with 'yakapin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **akapin** ang aking mga magulang pag-uwi ko.","translation":"I want **to hug** my parents when I get home."},{"sentence":"**Akapin** mo ang unan kung natatakot ka.","translation":"**Hug** the pillow if you're scared."}]

translation: going to a fiesta; attending a festival
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpunta at pakikilahok sa isang pista o pagdiriwang, karaniwan sa ibang bayan o barangay.
etymology: From "pista" (fiesta, festival), which is from Spanish "fiesta". The "pan-" prefix becomes "pam-" and the first syllable of the root is reduplicated.
original_explanation: The Pinoy version of 'party-hopping' or 'festival-crawling'. It's when you strategically visit relatives in different towns just in time for their local fiesta to get free food. The goal is to collect experiences (and lechon) from every celebration.
usage_notes: Implies traveling to a fiesta, often as a guest.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging tradisyon na ng aming pamilya ang **pamimista** sa Bulacan tuwing Mayo.","translation":"**Going to the fiesta** in Bulacan every May has become our family tradition."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutan ang pasalubong pagkatapos ng iyong **pamimista**!","translation":"Don't forget to bring back souvenirs after your **fiesta-attending**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pananakit o hirap sa pag-ihi, na karaniwang sintomas ng impeksyon sa daluyan ng ihi (urinary tract infection o UTI).
original_explanation: That awful feeling when peeing feels like you're passing tiny shards of glass. It's the body's painful notification that you probably have a UTI. The number one reason why your lola tells you not to sit on hot surfaces or to stop holding your pee during a movie marathon.
usage_notes: A specific medical term, but widely understood in the Philippines, often associated with UTI.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang pasyenteng uminom ng maraming tubig upang maibsan ang kanyang **balisawsaw**.","translation":"The doctor advised the patient to drink plenty of water to alleviate his **painful urination**."},{"sentence":"Ang **balisawsaw** ay isang karaniwang sintomas ng UTI.","translation":"**Dysuria** is a common symptom of a UTI."}]

translation: to weep together; to sob loudly in unison
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay na pag-iyak nang malakas at may matinding damdamin, kadalasan ay may kasamang hikbi at pananangis.
original_explanation: This is what happens during the finale of a Korean drama when the main couple finally gets together after 16 episodes of suffering. Everyone in the room just starts bawling their eyes out. It's a group cry session, the kind you have with your besties after a really bad breakup or when you all get your 13th-month pay.
usage_notes: The -an suffix and the mag- prefix indicate a reciprocal or group action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **maghagulhulan** ang mag-anak nang mabalitaan ang trahedya.","translation":"The family began to **weep together** when they heard about the tragedy."},{"sentence":"Huwag na tayong **maghagulhulan** dito, nakakahiya sa mga kapitbahay.","translation":"Let's not **sob loudly together** here, it's embarrassing to the neighbors."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng paglalakad nang hirap o hindi pantay dahil sa sakit o pinsala sa isa o parehong binti o paa.
etymology: From "pilay" (lame, limp). The "pan-" prefix becomes "pam-" and the first syllable of the root is reduplicated ("-pi-") to form a noun of action/state.
original_explanation: That awkward walk you do the day after leg day at the gym, or when you've been sitting on your foot for too long and it falls asleep. It's the physical manifestation of 'tiis-ganda' after wearing high heels all night.
usage_notes: Refers to the act or condition of limping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa kaniyang **pamimilay** ang hirap na dinanas niya sa pag-akyat ng bundok.","translation":"His **limping** clearly showed the difficulty he experienced climbing the mountain."},{"sentence":"Ang **pamimilay** ng aso ay senyales na kailangan na itong dalhin sa beterinaryo.","translation":"The dog's **lameness** is a sign that it needs to be taken to the vet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang murang usbong ng kawayan na karaniwang ginagamit bilang sangkap sa pagluluto.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *rabuŋ na nangangahulugang 'usbong ng kawayan'.
original_explanation: The baby bamboo that gets sacrificed to become a delicious ginataan or adobo dish. It's the ultimate 'para sa ekonomiya' story of the plant world. Kinda crunchy, kinda weirdly textured, but a provincial delicacy na hahanap-hanapin mo.
usage_notes: Isang sikat na sangkap sa maraming lutuing Pilipino, lalo na sa mga probinsya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang ginataang **labong** na luto ni Lola.","translation":"The **bamboo shoot** in coconut milk that Grandma cooks is delicious."},{"sentence":"Naghanap kami ng sariwang **labong** sa palengke.","translation":"We looked for fresh **bamboo shoots** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na tawag sa isang kaibigang lalaki, katumbas ng 'pare' o 'kaibigan'.
etymology: Possibly from Cebuano slang, or a shortened, affectionate term. Some sources link it to Chinese-Filipino influence.
original_explanation: The Visayan/Mindanao equivalent of the Luzon 'pare' or 'paps'. It's a term of endearment and casual respect between male friends. If someone calls you 'chong', you're in. It's the sound of brotherhood, usually followed by 'Tagay!' or 'Asa ta mangaon?' (Where are we eating?).
usage_notes: Very common in the Visayas and Mindanao regions, but understood and sometimes used in Luzon as well. Often paired with 'bai' (e.g., 'Chong, bai!').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Chong**, kamusta na? Tagal nating hindi nagkita.","translation":"**Bro**, how are you? It's been a while since we last saw each other."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa tulong mo, **chong**.","translation":"Thanks for your help, **pal**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilagay ang buto, punla, o halaman sa lupa upang ito ay tumubo at lumaki.
original_explanation: The literal act of becoming a #plantito or #plantita. But also, it's what you do with a grudge: "Itanim mo sa isip mo, hinding-hindi ko 'yun makakalimutan!" (Plant this in your mind, I will never forget that!). It’s planting a seed, whether it’s a literal mongo sprout for a school project or a seed of doubt in your friend's mind about her toxic jowa.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for agriculture or metaphorically for ideas, feelings, or memories.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda raw **itanim** ang kamatis sa buwan ng Mayo.","translation":"They say it's good to **plant** tomatoes in the month of May."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-**itanim** ng galit sa iyong puso.","translation":"Don't **plant** anger in your heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Hayaang makaraan o hindi pansinin; huwag pigilan o samantalahin ang isang pagkakataon.
original_explanation: 'Seenzone' in verb form. It's when you intentionally ignore a mistake, like when your friend is 30 minutes late again. 'Sige, palampasin na natin 'to.' It's also what you do to an opportunity you regret not taking, like that piso fare to Japan. 'Sayang, pinalampas ko.' It's the official verb of 'let it slide' and 'what if.'
usage_notes: Can mean to intentionally overlook something (forgive/ignore) or to unintentionally/intentionally miss an opportunity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **palampasin** ang pagkakataong ito.","translation":"Don't **let** this opportunity **pass**."},{"sentence":"**Palampasin** na lang natin ang maliit niyang pagkakamali.","translation":"Let's just **overlook** his small mistake."}]

translation: to reduce the price of something for someone
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbabawas sa presyo ng isang bilihin para sa isang partikular na mamimili.
original_explanation: This is the magic word you whisper to the tindera at the palengke. It's the more formal-sounding cousin of 'tawaran.' When your mom sends you to the market, she'll probably say, 'Rebahahan mo na lang kay Aling Nena,' because you're a suki. It's the financial dance of Filipino commerce.
usage_notes: Often used as a command. 'Rebahahan mo ako' (Give me a discount).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Suki, **rebahahan** na kita ng sampung piso.","translation":"Regular customer, I'll **reduce the price** by ten pesos for you."},{"sentence":"Puwede bang **rebahahan** mo pa ang presyo?","translation":"Can you **reduce** the price further for me?"}]

translation: to be able to contain; to be able to hold
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang maglagay ng nilalaman o laman sa loob ng isang sisidlan, espasyo, o konteksto.
original_explanation: Like your tiyan after a fiesta or your brain during a review for a board exam. It's the ability to actually *fit* something inside something else. "Kaya pa ba ng eco-bag mo na makapaglaman ng isa pang kilong bigas?"
usage_notes: Often used in the context of containers, capacity, or even abstract concepts like a story containing details.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating bumili ng mas malaking baunan para **makapaglaman** ng sapat na pagkain para sa outing.","translation":"We need to buy a bigger container to **be able to hold** enough food for the outing."},{"sentence":"Ang isang maikling sanaysay ay dapat **makapaglaman** ng isang malinaw na mensahe.","translation":"A short essay should **be able to contain** one clear message."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kulay na mapusyaw na kayumanggi na may madilaw-dilaw na tono, karaniwang ginagamit para sa uniporme.
etymology: From English khaki, from Urdu khākī "dust-colored", from Persian khāk "dust".
original_explanation: The official color of your dad's "good" shorts, security guard uniforms, and Boy Scout trousers. It's that brownish-beige that screams "practical" and "ready for anything." If "sensible" were a color, it would be kaki.
usage_notes: Refers to the color.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan niyang magsuot ng **kaki** na pantalon para sa kanyang uniporme.","translation":"He needs to wear **khaki** pants for his uniform."},{"sentence":"Ang pader ay pininturahan ng kulay **kaki**.","translation":"The wall was painted the color **khaki**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o ugali ng madalas na pagkalimot sa mga bagay-bagay.
original_explanation: This is the default state of your brain when you walk into a room and instantly forget why you went there. It's blaming your "pagka-malilimutin" for forgetting your friend's birthday, your wedding anniversary, or where you put the car keys five seconds ago. A national condition, probably.
usage_notes: The hyphen is optional but often used. `Pagkamalimutin` is also correct. `Malilimutin` is an adjective formed from a reduplicated root `li-limot`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pagka-malilimutin**, lagi niyang tinitingnan ang kanyang kalendaryo.","translation":"Because of his **forgetfulness**, he always checks his calendar."},{"sentence":"Ibinibintang niya sa pagod ang kanyang **pagka-malilimutin**.","translation":"She blames her **absent-mindedness** on fatigue."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagputol sa isang partikular na bagay o bahagi gamit ang isang kasangkapang panggupit.
original_explanation: Very similar to 'guntingin', but derived from 'gupit' (haircut/cut). Think of it as the general command to 'cut it.' While 'guntingin' emphasizes the tool (scissors), 'gupitin' focuses on the act of cutting itself. 'Gupitin mo na 'yang litratong 'yan, 'wag mo nang tingnan, masasaktan ka lang.'
usage_notes: Object-focus verb, interchangeable with 'guntingin' in many cases. 'Gupitin' is slightly more common for general cutting actions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **gupitin** ang papel na iyan, mahalaga iyan.","translation":"Don't **cut** that paper, it's important."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **gupitin** ang damo sa bakuran.","translation":"We need **to cut** the grass in the yard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagluluto kung saan ang karne, isda, o gulay ay iniihaw sa ibabaw ng mainit na uling o apoy, kadalasan ay tinutusok sa isang patpat. Tumutukoy rin ito sa mismong pagkaing inihaw.
etymology: Hiram sa Ingles na 'barbecue', na mula sa Espanyol na 'barbacoa'.
original_explanation: The quintessential Pinoy street food. Pork slices skewered on a thin bamboo stick, marinated in a sweet and savory sauce, then grilled over charcoal until slightly charred. Best enjoyed with a side of spicy vinegar. It's not a real Pinoy party if there's no barbekyu. Also, the name of your tito's favorite weekend activity.
usage_notes: Ang 'barbikyu' ay isang karaniwang alternatibong baybay. Ang Ingles na 'barbecue' ay madalas ding ginagamit sa mga menu at karatula.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng sampung **barbekyu** at tatlong isaw.","translation":"I'd like to buy ten sticks of **barbecue** and three sticks of isaw (grilled intestines)."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng timpla ng **barbekyu** ni Aling Nena.","translation":"Aling Nena's **barbecue** marinade is delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tawag-paggalang sa kapatid na babaeng mas matanda o sa sinumang babaeng itinuturing na mas may edad.
etymology: Mula sa Hokkien Chinese na "a-chi" (阿姊), na nangangahulugang "nakatatandang kapatid na babae".
original_explanation: The OG. The firstborn daughter. She's your second mom, your personal ATM, your fashion consultant, and the one who gets blamed for everything you do. You also call the lady at the carinderia "Ate," the saleslady at SM "Ate," and basically any woman slightly older than you "Ate" to be respectful. She's the CEO of the "pasa-load" corporation.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bago ang isang pangalan (hal. Ate Jane) o bilang isang standalone na pantawag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ate**, pahiram naman ng damit mo.","translation":"**Older sister**, can I borrow your clothes?"},{"sentence":"Pabili po, **Ate**.","translation":"I'd like to buy something, **Ma'am**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang linya na iginuguhit sa ilalim ng isang salita o parirala upang bigyan ito ng diin o pansin.
original_explanation: Before the highlight tool and Ctrl+U, this was the OG way of saying "Take note, bes, lalabas 'to sa exam!" In the digital age, it's the <u> tag in HTML or the thing you accidentally click in Word and can't figure out how to turn off.
usage_notes: Can also be used metaphorically to mean "emphasis."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **salungguhit** ang mahahalagang detalye sa kontrata.","translation":"Put an **underline** on the important details in the contract."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang panalo ay isang **salungguhit** sa kahalagahan ng pagsisikap.","translation":"His victory is an **emphasis** (underline) on the importance of hard work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at mahalagang simbahan na binigyan ng espesyal na pribilehiyo ng Santo Papa. Ito ay may natatanging kahalagahan sa kasaysayan, arkitektura, o relihiyon.
original_explanation: It's like the VIP section of churches. Not every big church is a basilica; it has to be given that special title by the Pope. Think of the Quiapo Church (Basilica of the Black Nazarene) or the Manila Cathedral (Minor Basilica). It's the church equivalent of getting a blue checkmark.
usage_notes: Refers to a specific type of Roman Catholic church with special papal designation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Basilika** ng Itim na Nazareno sa Quiapo ay dinarayo ng maraming deboto.","translation":"The **Basilica** of the Black Nazarene in Quiapo is visited by many devotees."},{"sentence":"Maraming makasaysayang **basilika** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"There are many historical **basilicas** in the Philippines."}]

translation: to buy wholesale; to buy in bulk
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbili ng isang produkto sa maramihang bilang o sa kabuuan nito, karaniwan para sa mas mababang presyo o para muling ibenta.
etymology: From `ma-` + `pakyaw`, from Minnan Chinese 拍僥 (phah-kiáu), meaning 'to corner the market'.
original_explanation: This is your 'tita mode' activated at the palengke or Divisoria. You're not just buying one kilo of mangoes; you're buying the whole 'kaing' (basket). It's also what concert ticket scalpers do, or what a sari-sari store owner does at the grocery. 'Ubusin na natin, **mamakyaw** na tayo ng tickets!'
usage_notes: Associated with business (reselling), getting a bulk discount, or hoarding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpunta siya sa Divisoria para **mamakyaw** ng mga paninda para sa kanyang tindahan.","translation":"She went to Divisoria to **buy goods wholesale** for her store."},{"sentence":"Plano nilang **mamakyaw** ng lahat ng isda mula sa mga mangingisda.","translation":"They plan to **buy all** the fish **in bulk** from the fishermen."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paksa, isyu, o suliranin na nangangailangan ng paglilinaw, talakayan, o paglilitis.
original_explanation: This is when 'usapan' graduates and gets a law degree. It's not just a chat anymore; it's a *problem*. It could be a legal case ('may usapin siya sa korte'), a political issue ('usapin ng teritoryo'), or that unresolved 'DTR' talk with your partner. It's the heavy stuff.
usage_notes: Has a formal and serious connotation. Often related to legal, political, or deeply personal conflicts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang agawan ng lupa ay isang malubhang **usapin** sa kanilang pamilya.","translation":"The land dispute is a serious **issue** in their family."},{"sentence":"Maraming **usapin** ang tinalakay sa Senado ngayong linggo.","translation":"Many **matters** were discussed in the Senate this week."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangangahulugang ang bawat isa ay may bahagi, halaga, o bilang na isang daan.
original_explanation: The standard "pamasko" or "aguinaldo" from a mid-level tito or tita during Christmas. It's not the mega-Tito level of 500 or 1000, but it's a solid, respectable tigisangdaan. Enough to make the kids happy.
usage_notes: A compound word showing distribution of a specific number. Can also be written as "tig-isang daan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tigisangdaan** ang naging ambag ng bawat miyembro para sa proyekto.","translation":"Each member contributed **one hundred for each** for the project."},{"sentence":"Noong Pasko, binigyan kami ng ninong namin ng **tigisangdaan**g piso.","translation":"Last Christmas, our godfather gave us **one hundred pesos each**."}]

translation: to spurt, to splash, to squirt
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagtilamsik o pag-agos ng likido mula sa isang sisidlan o pinagmulan dahil sa presyon.
original_explanation: That moment when you try to open a can of soda that's been shaken, and it sprays everywhere. Or when you step on a Zesto juice box. Or, more dramatically, the 'dugo' effect in a Pinoy action film. That sudden, uncontrolled burst of liquid is 'pumulandit'.
usage_notes: Describes a forceful and often messy ejection of liquid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumulandit** ang dugo mula sa kanyang sugat.","translation":"Blood **spurted** from his wound."},{"sentence":"Nang buksan niya ang gripo, **pumulandit** ang tubig sa kanyang mukha.","translation":"When he opened the faucet, water **splashed** onto his face."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pagsasagawa o pag-eensayo ng isang gawain upang mapabuti ang kasanayan o pagganap.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative) + praktis, a Tagalog borrowing from English 'practice'.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo bago ang isang job interview (sumasagot sa salamin) o bago manligaw ('Hi, crush!' *sabay takbo*). It's the grind before the glory. 'Practice makes perfect' ang English counterpart, pero sa atin, 'pagpapraktis' ang simula ng lahat, mula sa pag-gitara hanggang sa pag-apply ng eyeliner.
usage_notes: A very common Taglish/Filipinized word. The more traditional term is 'pagsasanay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Araw-araw ang **pagpapraktis** ng banda para sa kanilang concert.","translation":"The band's **practicing** is done daily for their concert."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng mas maraming oras sa **pagpapraktis** ng pagsasalita ng Ingles.","translation":"You need more time in **practicing** speaking English."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakalma o pagbabalik sa estado ng kapayapaan at katahimikan.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative) + pa- (progressive aspect) + yapa (from payapa, peace). Lit. 'the act of causing to be peaceful'.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa ng nanay mo kapag nag-aaway kayo ng kapatid mo over the TV remote. O 'yung pag-abot mo ng kape sa officemate mong high-blood sa umaga. It's the art of de-escalation, whether in a family feud or a diplomatic crisis.
usage_notes: Can be used for calming people, situations, or even oneself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapayapa** sa umiiyak na sanggol ay isang malaking hamon.","translation":"The **act of calming down** a crying baby is a big challenge."},{"sentence":"Bahagi ng kanyang tungkulin ang **pagpapayapa** sa mga nag-aaway na grupo.","translation":"Part of his duty is the **pacification** of the warring groups."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o pangkat ng mga tao na may napakababang antas ng pamumuhay at salat sa mga pangunahing pangangailangan.
etymology: From 'ma-' (having the quality of) + 'dalita' (suffering, misery, extreme poverty).
original_explanation: This is the more formal, almost biblical way of saying 'mahirap'. You'll hear it in speeches by politicians or in social studies class when discussing poverty. It’s like using 'impoverished' instead of just 'poor.' It carries a weight of systemic hardship, not just being broke before payday.
usage_notes: 'Maralita' is a more formal and often more empathetic term than 'mahirap'. It is frequently used in sociological and governmental contexts, as in 'mga maralitang tagalungsod' (the urban poor). It can also function as a noun to mean 'a poor person' or 'the poor'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang programa ng gobyerno ay naglalayong tulungan ang mga **maralita** sa ating lipunan.","translation":"The government's program aims to help the **poor** in our society."},{"sentence":"Namuhay siyang **maralita** ngunit hindi nawalan ng pag-asa.","translation":"He lived an **impoverished** life but never lost hope."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng espesyal, magiliw, at mapag-arugang pagtrato sa isang tao, lalo na sa isang kasintahan, na para bang siya ay isang prinsesa.
original_explanation: The gold standard for dating, as seen on TikTok. This is when your S.O. opens doors for you, carries your shopping bags, peels your shrimp, and basically treats you like royalty. It's the 'sana all' vibe that makes single people question their life choices. The bare minimum? According to Gen Z, yes.
usage_notes: A very modern, social media-driven slang term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Deserve ko naman ng **princess treatment** pagkatapos ng lahat ng pinagdaanan ko.","translation":"I deserve the **princess treatment** after everything I've been through."}]

translation: to lock oneself up; to confine oneself
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng sarili sa loob ng isang saradong lugar at hindi paglabas, kadalasan ay dahil sa sariling kagustuhan o dahil sa matinding emosyon.
original_explanation: What you do after a major 'sana all' moment on social media, a breakup, or when you just need a break from adulting. 'Magkukulong ako sa kwarto' is the universal Filipino sign for 'Do not disturb, I'm having a moment.' It's self-imposed quarantine, basically.
usage_notes: Madalas na nagpapahiwatig ng boluntaryong pagkakakulong dahil sa mga kadahilanang emosyonal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos ang pag-aaway, nagpasya siyang **magkulong** sa kanyang silid.","translation":"After the fight, she decided to **lock herself up** in her room."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magkulong** sa library para magbasa buong araw.","translation":"He likes to **confine himself** in the library to read all day."}]

translation: to carry something, to bring something
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbubuhat o pagdadala ng isang bagay mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba. Ito ay anyong pautos o layon ng pandiwa.
original_explanation: The imperative form of "dala". It's what your mom yells when you're about to leave the house: "Dalhin mo payong!" It's the emotional baggage you carry from your ex, the 'pasalubong' you bring for your family, or the heavy workload you take home from the office. Basically, to bring it, carry it, bear it.
usage_notes: Ito ang pokus sa layon ng pandiwang "magdala". Halimbawa: "Dalhin mo ang bag" (You carry the bag) vs "Magdala ka ng bag" (You bring a bag). Ang "dalain" ay isang mas pormal o matandang anyo ng "dalhin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **dalain** mo ang mga aklat na ito sa silid-aklatan.","translation":"Please, **bring** these books to the library."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **dalain** ang sama ng loob sa matagal na panahon.","translation":"It's hard **to carry** a grudge for a long time."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagiging sanhi ng antok o nagdudulot ng kakayahang makatulog.
original_explanation: Anything that can knock you out faster than a boring lecture on a hot afternoon. It could be a warm glass of milk, a rainy day, that ASMR video, or your boss's voice during a long meeting. Your personal 'off' switch.
usage_notes: Can refer to medicine, food, activities, or ambient conditions that cause sleepiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-inom ng tsaa na chamomile ay **nakapagpapatulog**.","translation":"Drinking chamomile tea **induces sleep**."},{"sentence":"Ang mahinang musika ay **nakapagpapatulog** sa sanggol.","translation":"The soft music **makes the baby sleepy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa buong itatagal ng buhay; walang katapusan.
original_explanation: The ultimate promise... and the ultimate scam, depending on who's saying it. It's the "I love you 3000" of Tagalog. Heard in wedding vows ("pag-ibig na habang-buhay") and also in loan agreements ("utang na habang-buhay"). It's the "forever" that we all chase, whether in love or in debt.
usage_notes: Isang tambalang salita na maaaring gumana bilang pang-abay (adverb) o pang-uri (adjective).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumpaan nila ang pag-ibig na **habang-buhay**.","translation":"They vowed their **lifelong** love for each other."},{"sentence":"Siya ay hinatulan ng **habang-buhay** na pagkakakulong.","translation":"He was sentenced to **life** imprisonment."}]

translation: to give satisfaction; to please; to bring joy
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdudulot ng ligaya, galak, o lugod sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the main goal of every food vlogger tasting crispy pata, every stand-up comedian landing a joke, and every Jollibee crew member serving your order. It's the act of delivering happiness, whether it's through a perfect 'shot puno!', a well-executed prank, or simply by being present.
usage_notes: A positive and frequently used term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Layunin ng palabas na **magbigay-kasiyahan** sa mga manonood.","translation":"The show's objective is to **bring joy** to the audience."},{"sentence":"Simpleng bagay lang pero **nagbigay-kasiyahan** na sa kanya.","translation":"It was a simple thing, but it already **gave him satisfaction**."}]

meaning_filipino: Yari sa ginto; may kulay o katangiang tulad ng ginto.
original_explanation: Something that's literally made of gold or just looks like it. Think of Manny Pacquiao's championship belts, the scepter of a beauty queen, or that ridiculously shiny jewelry your rich tita wears. It also describes a 'golden age' or a 'golden opportunity'—something precious and valuable.
usage_notes: Derived from 'ginto' (gold) with the suffix '-an'. Can be literal (gintuang kuwintas - golden necklace) or figurative (gintuang puso - golden heart).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng isang **gintuang** medalya sa paligsahan.","translation":"She received a **golden** medal in the competition."},{"sentence":"Inaalala nila ang **gintuang** panahon ng kanilang kabataan.","translation":"They reminisce about the **golden** era of their youth."}]

meaning_filipino: Matibay na paniniwala at pagtitiwala sa isang bagay, tao, o konsepto, lalo na sa isang kapangyarihang espirituwal, nang walang tiyak na katibayan.
original_explanation: `Panalig` is your trust level: 100%. It’s believing your favorite K-pop group will win the Daesang. It's trusting that your friend will pay you back (eventually). On a deeper level, it's your faith in a higher power, the universe, or even just in yourself. It's what you hold on to when things get tough, your "kapit lang" anchor.
usage_notes: Often used in a religious or deeply personal context. It suggests a more profound trust than the more common `tiwala`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matibay ang kanyang **panalig** sa Diyos sa kabila ng mga pagsubok.","translation":"Her **faith** in God is strong despite the trials."},{"sentence":"Ang **panalig** niya sa kanyang kakayahan ang nagdala sa kanya sa tagumpay.","translation":"His **belief** in his abilities brought him to success."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagang balbal para sa isang lalaking kaakit-akit o itinuturing na guwapo; maaari ring gamiting pangkalahatang pantawag sa isang kaibigang lalaki.
etymology: From Spanish 'papi' (daddy), re-appropriated in Philippine slang as a term of endearment or address for attractive men or male friends.
original_explanation: The ultimate "tito" term of endearment for a good-looking guy, a friend, or that gym bro you always see. It's the male equivalent of "chix." "Papi, pa-order ng isang kape!" You hear this everywhere, from the palengke to the club. It's a step up from "kuya" and a bit more playful than "sir."
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, spoken Filipino. Can be used as a term of address or a descriptor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy **Papi**, kamusta na? Long time no see!","translation":"Hey **dude**, how are you? Long time no see!"},{"sentence":"Ang daming **papi** sa gym kanina, nakakagana mag-workout.","translation":"There were so many **handsome guys** at the gym earlier, it makes you motivated to work out."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng ngiti sa isang tao o bagay bilang pagpapahayag ng positibong damdamin.
original_explanation: The active verb for spreading good vibes. It's what you do to your crush from across the room, hoping they notice. It's the polite thing to do when you make eye contact with a stranger. 'Yung tipong, ngitian mo na lang ang problema.
usage_notes: Object-focused verb. 'Ngitian mo sila' means 'Smile at them.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ngitian** mo lang ang mga taong nagdududa sa kakayahan mo.","translation":"Just **smile at** the people who doubt your abilities."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sopas na may pansit (noodles) na nagmula sa mga Tsino, karaniwang inihahain na mainit at may sahog na manok, baka, o baboy.
etymology: From Hokkien Chinese `肉麵` (bah-mī), meaning "meat noodles".
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino comfort food for a rainy day or when you're feeling sick. It's our version of chicken noodle soup, but with that distinct Chinese-Filipino flavor. Best paired with siopao and a sense of "okay lang kahit umuulan, may mami naman."
usage_notes: A very common food item. Often sold in "mami-han" or noodle houses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap humigop ng mainit na **mami** kapag malamig ang panahon.","translation":"It's nice to sip hot **mami** when the weather is cold."},{"sentence":"Nag-order siya ng beef **mami** at isang siopao para sa meryenda.","translation":"He ordered beef **mami** and a siopao for his snack."}]

translation: to pile up, to stack, to heap
meaning_filipino: Ang mag-ipon o magpatong-patong ng mga bagay sa isang lugar nang walang partikular na ayos.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your laundry chair. You magtambak clothes on it until it becomes a 'closet'. It's also what happens to your workload right before a long weekend. The opposite of 'Marie Kondo-ing'.
usage_notes: Often implies a messy or large quantity of items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, huwag kang **magtambak** ng mga maruruming plato sa lababo.","translation":"Please, do not **pile up** dirty dishes in the sink."},{"sentence":"**Nagtambak** na naman ang mga gawain ko sa opisina dahil sa pagliban ko kahapon.","translation":"My tasks at the office **piled up** again because of my absence yesterday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang palihim na pagmamasid o pag-espiya sa isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari, kadalasan mula sa malayo o sa isang tago na lugar.
original_explanation: This is the Marites starter pack. When you're trying to get the latest chismis about your neighbor, you're 'namiminto'. It's like being a low-key private investigator, but your only client is your own curiosity. Your target? The 'kapitbahay na may bagong kotse' or 'yung ex na may bago nang jowa'.
usage_notes: This verb implies a sense of secrecy or stealth in the act of observing, similar to 'spying' or 'peeking'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Namiminto** ang pusa sa butas kung saan nagtatago ang daga.","translation":"The cat is **observing** the hole where the mouse is hiding."},{"sentence":"Nahuli siyang **namiminto** sa pag-uusap ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"He was caught **spying** on his parents' conversation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na pansalok ng tubig na gawa sa bao ng niyog na may hawakang kawayan.
original_explanation: The OG, eco-friendly, artisanal tabo. Before the age of brightly colored plastic, this was the go-to dipper. It's got that rustic, provincial, back-to-basics vibe. You'll see this in historical films or maybe in your lola's house in the province. It's the hipster version of the modern tabo.
usage_notes: Less common now, often seen as a decorative or traditional item.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nostalgic ang pakiramdam kapag gumagamit ng **tabong-bao** sa pagligo.","translation":"It feels nostalgic when using a **dipper made of coconut shell** for bathing."},{"sentence":"Ang **tabong-bao** ay isang halimbawa ng katutubong kagamitan.","translation":"The **coconut shell dipper** is an example of an indigenous utensil."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim sa Ingles para sa "Outfit of the Day," na tumutukoy sa kasuotang isinusuot ng isang tao sa isang partikular na araw, kadalasang ibinabahagi sa social media.
etymology: Mula sa akronim ng Ingles na "Outfit of the Day".
original_explanation: The national pastime of Pinoys on Instagram. Before you leave the house, you gotta document the drip. Your #ootd is your battle armor for the day, whether you're heading to the mall, a coffee shop, or just your sala for a Zoom meeting. It's the modern-day "porma."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit bilang isang hashtag sa mga social media platform tulad ng Instagram at Facebook.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ganda ng **ootd** mo ngayon, sis! Saan mo nabili 'yang damit mo?","translation":"Your **OOTD** is great today, sis! Where did you buy your dress?"},{"sentence":"I-post mo na ang **ootd** mo bago tayo umalis.","translation":"Post your **OOTD** before we leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing sari-sari o magkakaiba ang mga bagay upang magkaroon ng pagkakaiba-iba at hindi maging pare-pareho.
etymology: From the reduplicated root 'iba-iba' (various, different kinds) and the suffix '-hin'. The reduplication emphasizes variety and multiplicity.
original_explanation: This is 'ibahin' on shuffle mode. It's not just changing one thing, it's making a bunch of things different from each other. Like when you're trying to make your IG feed look interesting, you **iba-ibahin** your posts: selfie, food, travel, meme, repeat. It prevents things from becoming 'sawa' or boring.
usage_notes: Used to express the action of making a set of items diverse, not just changing a single item.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **iba-ibahin** ang ating mga produkto upang makaakit ng mas maraming mamimili.","translation":"We need to **diversify** our products to attract more customers."},{"sentence":"**Iba-ibahin** mo ang iyong ehersisyo araw-araw para hindi ka tamarin.","translation":"**Vary** your exercises every day so you don't get lazy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, balita, o kaganapan na biglaan, nakakagulat, at malaki ang epekto, na maihahalintulad sa isang pagsabog. Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng aliwan o tsismis.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative) + `sabog` (explode, scatter). The literal meaning is "something made to explode".
original_explanation: The showbiz and social media term for a "bombshell" or "big reveal." It's not a literal explosion, but an emotional or social one. A celebrity announcing a secret wedding? That's a pasabog. Your friend arriving at the reunion in a glow-up transformation? Pasabog! It's anything done for maximum shock and awe.
usage_notes: While it can mean a literal explosive device, it's more commonly used in its slang meaning in modern conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking **pasabog** daw na ilalabas ang vlogger mamayang gabi.","translation":"The vlogger will reportedly drop a huge **bombshell** tonight."},{"sentence":"Ang OOTD mo, pang-**pasabog** talaga sa party!","translation":"Your OOTD is truly a **stunner** for the party!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pari na kumakatawan sa isang obispo o mas mataas na opisyal ng simbahan, o isang kura paroko.
original_explanation: Ito yung assistant to the regional manager ng Simbahang Katoliko. Sila yung in-charge sa parokya kapag wala si Father Principal. Think of them as the OIC (Officer-in-Charge) ng simbahan.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa kontekstong panrelihiyon, partikular sa Katolisismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **bikaryo** ang namuno sa misa noong Linggo.","translation":"The **vicar** led the mass on Sunday."},{"sentence":"Itinalaga siya bilang **bikaryo** heneral ng diyosesis.","translation":"He was appointed as the **vicar** general of the diocese."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing malambot ang isang bagay na dati ay matigas, sa pamamagitan ng pagluluto, pagbababad, o iba pang proseso.
original_explanation: This is what you do to the beef for your kaldereta so it doesn't feel like you're chewing on a shoe. It's also what your friend tells you to do to your heart ('palambutin mo puso mo') after your third breakup this year. From tough to tender, literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: Commonly used in cooking contexts, but also figuratively for emotions or attitudes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **palambutin** muna ang karne bago igisa.","translation":"The meat needs to be **tenderized** first before sautéing."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **palambutin** ang puso ng kanyang ama.","translation":"He is trying to **soften** his father's heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagsisilbing sagabal, balakid, o hadlang sa isang gawain, layunin, o pag-usad.
original_explanation: That one super slow car in the fast lane on EDSA. Or your 'marites' neighbor who keeps interrupting you when you're trying to work from home. Anything or anyone that blocks your way and makes things difficult is 'nakahahadlang'. It's the ultimate 'pabigat'.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical objects, people, or abstract concepts (like fear).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang takot ay isang damdaming **nakahahadlang** sa ating pag-unlad.","translation":"Fear is an emotion that is **hindering** our progress."},{"sentence":"Inalis nila ang mga batong **nakahahadlang** sa daan.","translation":"They removed the rocks that were **obstructing** the road."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining, agham, at industriya ng pagpapalipad ng mga sasakyang panghimpapawid.
original_explanation: The whole world of flying—planes, pilots, airports, and the overpriced food inside them. It's the industry that makes OFWs' homecomings and our Cebu beach trips possible.
usage_notes: A formal term used in technical or official contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging epekto ng pandemya sa industriya ng **abyasyon**.","translation":"The pandemic had a huge effect on the **aviation** industry."},{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng kurso na may kinalaman sa **abyasyon**.","translation":"He took a course related to **aviation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglakad nang may tiyak at sabay-sabay na hakbang, karaniwang ginagawa ng mga sundalo, miyembro ng banda, o mga nagpoprotesta.
etymology: Mula sa `pag-` + `magmartsa` (lumakad nang sabay-sabay), na hiram sa Espanyol na `marchar` (magmartsa).
original_explanation: That thing you were forced to do in CAT/ROTC under the hot sun. "Kaliwa, kanan, kaliwa, kanan!" It's also what activists do in the streets to protest, or what a marching band does during a fiesta. Basically, walking with purpose and in unison.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa pormal at sabay-sabay na paglakad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsanay sila ng **pagmamartsa** para sa darating na parada.","translation":"They practiced **marching** for the upcoming parade."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagmamartsa** ng mga raliyista ay nagdulot ng mabigat na trapiko.","translation":"The **marching** of the rallyists caused heavy traffic."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahin at sentral na simbahan ng isang diyosesis, kung saan matatagpuan ang opisyal na trono o 'cathedra' ng obispo.
original_explanation: That really big, grand, and historically significant church in a city, like the Manila Cathedral. It's the "main branch" of the churches in a region, where the bishop hangs his hat. Perfect for wedding pictorials or a Visita Iglesia stop.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the principal church of a diocese.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Katedral** ng Maynila ay isang tanyag na makasaysayang pook.","translation":"The Manila **Cathedral** is a famous historical site."},{"sentence":"Maraming turista ang bumibisita sa **katedral** tuwing Mahal na Araw.","translation":"Many tourists visit the **cathedral** during Holy Week."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sandata na hugis tubo kung saan inilalagay ang isang maliit na palaso (dart) at hinihipan nang malakas upang patamaan ang target.
original_explanation: The original long-range weapon, used by indigenous tribes long before sniper rifles were a thing. It's like a straw, but for delivering a very pointy, often poisoned, "message". The ultimate "pfft" of death.
usage_notes: Karaniwang iniuugnay sa mga katutubong kultura, lalo na sa pangangaso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga katutubo ay gumagamit ng **sumpit** para manghuli ng maliliit na hayop sa gubat.","translation":"The indigenous people use a **blowgun** to hunt small animals in the forest."},{"sentence":"May lason ang dulo ng palaso na inilalagay sa **sumpit**.","translation":"The tip of the dart placed in the **blowpipe** is poisoned."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may pormal na pinag-aralan, nagpapakita ng mabuting asal, at may malawak na kaalaman.
original_explanation: This is the guy your parents approve of. He has a degree, a stable job, speaks respectfully ('po' and 'opo' game is strong), and probably doesn't post cringe-worthy stuff online. Being 'edukado' is the gold standard for Filipino parents looking for a son-in-law.
usage_notes: The masculine form is often used as the general term for an educated person regardless of gender.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ng mga magulang ko na makapangasawa ako ng isang lalaking **edukado**.","translation":"My parents want me to marry an **educated** man."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa kanyang pananalita na siya ay isang taong **edukado**.","translation":"It's very evident in his speech that he is an **educated** person."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkain na gawa sa harina, tubig, at pampaalsa na karaniwang iniluluto sa hurno.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *tapay, meaning "fermented food" or "yeast". The prefix "ti-n-" suggests it's "something that has been fermented".
original_explanation: The OG. The foundation of pandesal, monay, Spanish bread, and your tita's "pasalubong from Baguio" raisin bread. It's the ultimate palaman-delivery-system, whether for palaman, cheese, or Reno Liver Spread. In a religious context, it's a big deal. In a daily context, it's what you dip in your kape. Simple as that.
usage_notes: A general term for all kinds of bread.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng mainit na **tinapay** para sa almusal.","translation":"Mom bought warm **bread** for breakfast."},{"sentence":"Masarap isawsaw ang **tinapay** sa mainit na tsokolate.","translation":"It's delicious to dip **bread** in hot chocolate."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na gumagawa, nag-aayos, o nagbebenta ng mga alahas.
original_explanation: The person you go to when you need to pawn your family heirloom to pay for tuition. Or, the person who sells you the engagement ring that costs three months' salary. They're the experts in all things shiny and expensive. Think of the shops in Ongpin or Greenhills.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit nang palitan sa 'mag-aalahas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpagawa ako ng bagong singsing sa sikat na **alahero** sa Meycauayan.","translation":"I had a new ring made by a famous **jeweler** in Meycauayan."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa walang nakuha o walang puntos sa isang laro o kompetisyon; katumbas ng sero.
etymology: Posibleng nagmula sa "walang laman" na katangian ng isang bao ng niyog matapos alisin ang laman nito.
original_explanation: This is what you get in a game when you totally fail to score. Yung feeling na nag-exam ka tapos wala kang nasagot. In card games, if you get 'bao', it means you didn't win a single hand. It's the "try again next time, bes" of scoring.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga laro at iskor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naka-limang laro na kami ng tong-its pero **bao** pa rin ako.","translation":"We've played five games of tong-its already, but I'm still **skunked** (have zero wins)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o pagawaan kung saan isinasagawa ang proseso ng pagtubog o pagbabalot ng isang manipis na suson ng metal sa ibabaw ng ibang metal, karaniwan para sa proteksyon o pampaganda.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "tubog" (plated) at panlaping "pa-" at "-an".
original_explanation: This is where you bring your old, tarnished jewelry or car parts to get them covered in a new shiny layer of gold, silver, or chrome. It's a "plating shop." It's the spa day for your alahas, making them look brand new again. "Dalhin mo sa patubugan 'yang singsing mo para kumintab ulit."
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino na karaniwang nauunawaan sa konteksto ng alahas, metalwork, at automotive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May kilala ka bang magaling na **patubugan** ng silver?","translation":"Do you know a good **shop for** silver-**plating**?"}]

translation: to be able to grant, to accommodate a request
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahan o pagkakataong pagbigyan o ibigay ang hinihiling o ninanais ng isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (nagsasaad ng potensyal o kakayahan) + `bigay` (ibigay) + hulaping `-an` (nagsasaad ng direksyon o lokasyon).
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na nagpaalam ka sa boss mo for a last-minute leave at pumayag siya, 'yun 'yung napagbigyan ka. O 'yung hiling mo sa magulang mo na bagong phone, at sa wakas, after one year ng pangungulit, napagbigyan din. It's the feeling of "Yes! Approved!" for a request you've been making.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwa, hindi tulad ng 'mapagbigay' na isang pang-uri. Ito ay nasa aspetong potensyal, na nangangahulugang 'kayang pagbigyan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **mapagbigyan** mo ang hiling kong makita ka bago ako umalis.","translation":"I hope you can **grant** my wish to see you before I leave."},{"sentence":"Hindi lahat ng gusto natin sa buhay ay **mapagbibigyan**.","translation":"Not everything we want in life can be **granted**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pakikialam o pagsingit sa usapan ng iba nang hindi hinihiling o binibigyan ng pagkakataon.
original_explanation: The national pastime of many titas and titos in a conversation. It's when someone cuts you off mid-sentence just to say something completely unrelated or to correct a minor detail. The verbal equivalent of cutting in line.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation of being rude. A close synonym is 'pagsabat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi magandang ugali ang **pagsabad** sa usapan ng may usapan.","translation":"It's not good manners to **butt in** on other people's conversations."},{"sentence":"Nagalit ang guro dahil sa **pagsabad** ng estudyante habang siya'y nagsasalita.","translation":"The teacher got angry because of the student's **interrupting** while she was speaking."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang butas sa lupa na resulta ng paghuhukay, na maaaring gamitin bilang libingan, pundasyon, o para sa ibang layunin.
original_explanation: This is the hole you dig, literally. Sometimes it's for planting a tree, sometimes for building a house foundation. Other times, it's a grave, which is why people say "isang paa mo nasa hukay" (one of your feet is in the grave) when you're being reckless or are very old. It's the OG 'digging yourself into a hole'.
usage_notes: Can refer to any hole dug in the ground, but often carries a somber connotation of a grave.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malalim ang **hukay** na ginawa para sa pundasyon ng bagong gusali.","translation":"The **pit** dug for the foundation of the new building is deep."},{"sentence":"Nag-iwan sila ng mga bulaklak sa tabi ng **hukay**.","translation":"They left flowers beside the **grave**."}]

translation: to make (someone) be honest; to straighten out
meaning_filipino: Hilingin o pilitin ang isang tao na magsabi ng totoo o maging tapat.
original_explanation: The goal of every interrogation scene, whether it's in a police station or just your mom asking where you were last night. "Patapatin mo nga 'yang kaibigan mo, sino ba talaga ang may kasalanan?" It's the act of getting someone to stop lying and just spill the tea. To make them go straight.
usage_notes: The root 'tapat' can mean 'honest' or 'straight/directly across'. So `patapatin` can also mean 'to align something' or 'to make something face something directly', but the 'make honest' meaning is more common in social contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng detektib na **patapatin** ang suspek.","translation":"The detective tried to **make the suspect be honest**."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **patapatin** ang isang taong sanay magsinungaling.","translation":"It's hard to **make a person be honest** if they are used to lying."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **patapatin** ang mga mesa sa isa't isa.","translation":"You need to **make the tables align** with each other."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng materyal, karaniwang kahoy o bato, na isinisingit sa pagitan o ilalim ng isang bagay upang ito ay pumantay, tumigil sa paggalaw, o hindi gumulong.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of wobbly tables and runaway cars. Ito 'yung tsinelas, piraso ng karton, o tinuping papel na nilalagay mo sa ilalim ng paa ng mesa para hindi na umuuga. Sa mga jeepney, ito 'yung kahoy na nilalagay sa gulong para hindi gumulong paatras sa paakyat na kalsada. It's the ultimate Filipino life hack for stability.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa praktikal at mekanikal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **kalang** ang gulong ng sasakyan para sigurado.","translation":"Put a **chock** on the car's wheel just to be sure."},{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng papel at gawing **kalang** sa ilalim ng mesa.","translation":"Get some paper and use it as a **shim** under the table."}]

translation: maybe you could...; a gentle hint or request
meaning_filipino: Isang magalang at di-tuwirang paraan ng paghiling o pagpapahiwatig ng isang bagay, kadalasan sa pabirong tono.
etymology: Combination of 'baka' (maybe) and 'naman' (a particle for emphasis or contrast).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'pahaging' or subtle hint phrase. When your friend gets their 13th-month pay, you say, 'Baka naman...' with a meaningful look. It's a low-pressure way of asking for something, a gentle nudge. 'Maybe you'd be so kind as to... treat me to coffee?' It's half-joking, half-serious, and 100% Filipino.
usage_notes: The rest of the request is often left unsaid and implied through context and tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, ang dami mong pasalubong! **Baka naman**...","translation":"Hey, you have a lot of souvenirs! **Maybe you could share some**..."},{"sentence":"Nakita kong may bagong bukas na samgyupsal diyan. **Baka naman** pautang.","translation":"I saw a new samgyupsal place opened there. **Maybe you could** lend me some money."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pagkuha ng serbisyo ng isang awditor upang suriin ang mga talaang pampinansyal ng isang kumpanya o organisasyon.
etymology: From `magpa-` (causative prefix) + `audit` (from English). This is a loanword verb construction.
original_explanation: This is the corporate version of "Saan napunta ang pera?" You magpaaudit when you need an official third party to check the books and make sure no one's been treating the company funds like their personal G-cash wallet. It's a necessary evil in business to ensure transparency, unless you're the one who's been "creative" with the expenses, then it's just pure terror.
usage_notes: Used in business, finance, and government contexts. The root 'audit' is an English loanword.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Taun-taon kailangang **magpaaudit** ng aming kumpanya para sa BIR.","translation":"Every year our company needs to **have an audit** for the BIR."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang board na **magpaaudit** dahil sa mga hinala ng katiwalian.","translation":"The board decided to **have an audit conducted** due to suspicions of corruption."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kanin na niluto sa maraming tubig hanggang sa lumambot at maging malapot. Tumutukoy rin sa mismong proseso ng pagluluto nito.
