original_explanation: This is the noun or verb form of comfort food. It's the act of turning simple bigas into the warm, soupy goodness that is lugaw. It’s what your mom makes when you're sick, when it's raining, or when you're just plain sad. It’s the culinary equivalent of a warm hug.
usage_notes: The word is formed from the root 'lugaw' with the infix '-in-', indicating something that has been made or cooked. Thus, 'linugaw' is 'made into lugaw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **linugaw** na bigas ay mainam na pagkain para sa may sakit.","translation":"Rice **made into porridge** is good food for someone who is sick."},{"sentence":"Nag-request ako ng **linugaw** na may maraming bawang at luya.","translation":"I requested **porridge** with lots of garlic and ginger."}]

translation: act of opening the mouth wide; gaping
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbuka ng bibig nang malaki.
etymology: From the root "nganga" (open-mouthed), with the prefix "pag-" to form a noun.
original_explanation: This is what you do at the dentist's office ("Say 'ahhh'"). It's also the face you make when you see something shocking or unbelievable, like the latest 'chismis' or your Meralco bill. It's the physical manifestation of being shookt.
usage_notes: Can refer to the literal act of opening the mouth or figuratively to a state of being dumbfounded or idle ("nakanganga" - gaping, doing nothing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hirap ng **pagnganga** nang matagal sa dentista.","translation":"The **act of opening the mouth wide** for a long time at the dentist is difficult."},{"sentence":"Napatingin siya sa akin na may kasamang **pagnganga** dahil sa gulat.","translation":"He looked at me with a **gape** out of shock."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay na may kaugnayan sa lupa, pagsasaka, o sa pamamahala ng mga lupain.
original_explanation: This is the brother of 'agrarya'. They mean the same thing, but 'agraryo' is the masculine form from Spanish. You use it to describe masculine nouns. For example, 'isang sistemang agraryo' (an agrarian system). Basically, if you're talking about land, farming, and policies about them, this is your go-to formal adjective.
usage_notes: 'Agraryo' and 'agrarya' are often used interchangeably in modern Filipino, but traditionally they follow Spanish gender agreement rules with the noun they modify.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang batas na **agraryo** ay naglalayong protektahan ang mga karapatan ng mga magsasaka.","translation":"The **agrarian** law aims to protect the rights of farmers."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan nila ang iba't ibang modelong **agraryo** sa Asya.","translation":"They studied various **agrarian** models in Asia."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi angkop o tama ang oras o pagkakataon para sa isang pangyayari o gawain.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang binubuo ng 'hindi' (not) at 'panahon' (time/season).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'it's not you, it's me' excuse, but for situations. When your parents ask why you're still single, or when you want to buy that milk tea but it's 'petsa de peligro'. It's the universe's way of saying, 'Wait lang, 'di pa ready ang script mo.'
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ipahayag na ang tiyempo para sa isang bagay ay hindi naaangkop o hindi paborable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hindi panahon** para magbiruan ngayon dahil seryoso ang sitwasyon.","translation":"This is **not the right time** for joking because the situation is serious."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko sanang mag-resign pero **hindi panahon** dahil sa pandemic.","translation":"I wanted to resign, but it's **not the right time** because of the pandemic."}]

meaning_filipino: Makuhaan ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay pera o pitaka, mula sa bulsa o bag nang hindi namamalayan.
original_explanation: The official verb for that 'OMG, asan na wallet ko?!' moment after riding the MRT during rush hour. It's the passive experience of being victimized by a 'mandurukot.' Your pocket/bag is the crime scene, and you're the unsuspecting victim.
usage_notes: This is in the potential aspect, meaning 'to be able to be pickpocketed' or 'to happen to be pickpocketed.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa Divisoria para hindi ka **madukutan**.","translation":"Be careful in Divisoria so you don't **get pickpocketed**."},{"sentence":"Nalungkot si Ana nang **madukutan** siya ng cellphone sa bus.","translation":"Ana was sad when her cellphone **was stolen from her pocket/bag** on the bus."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lantsa na ginagamit sa paglilipat ng mga kargamento mula sa malalaking barko na nakadaong malayo sa pampang patungo sa piyer.
original_explanation: Imagine a huge container ship, the "main event," that can't get close to the shore. The **lantsa-de-deskarge** is the "support act." It's a smaller boat that zips back and forth, unloading all the Shopee and Lazada packages (aka cargo) from the big ship and bringing them to the pier. It's the delivery guy for the sea.
usage_notes: A technical term used in maritime and port operations. 'Deskarge' comes from Spanish 'descargar' (to unload).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na naglipat ng mga sako ng bigas ang mga **lantsa-de-deskarge**.","translation":"The **discharge boats** quickly transferred the sacks of rice."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng maraming **lantsa-de-deskarge** kapag malaki ang barkong dumating.","translation":"Many **lighters** are needed when a large ship arrives."}]

meaning_filipino: Idiin ang daliri sa isang buton, teklado, o katulad na mekanismo upang ito ay gumana.
original_explanation: The command you give when you want someone to interact with literally any device made after 1980. "Pindutin mo 'yung 'like' button." "Pindutin mo 'yung doorbell." "Huwag mong pindutin 'yan, baka masira!" It's the verb that runs our tech-dependent lives.
usage_notes: The object-focused command or infinitive form. The focus is on the thing being pressed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **pindutin** ang 'send' pagkatapos mong i-type ang mensahe.","translation":"Don't forget **to press** 'send' after you type the message."},{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **pindutin** ang pulang buton para sa emergency.","translation":"Please **press** the red button for an emergency."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng nakasulat na mensahe na ipinapadala sa isang tao, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng serbisyo postal.
original_explanation: Before DMs, PMs, and emails, this was the OG way to slide into someone's life. It’s a physical letter written on paper, sealed with love (or just saliva), and sent via the post office. Today, it’s reserved for super formal things (liham-rekomendasyon) or super romantic, old-school gestures (liham-pag-ibig). Writing one is a major effort, so receiving one feels extra special.
usage_notes: More formal than 'sulat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumulat siya ng isang **liham** para sa kanyang mga magulang na nasa abroad.","translation":"She wrote a **letter** for her parents who are abroad."},{"sentence":"Ang **liham**-pag-ibig na iyon ay itinago niya sa loob ng maraming taon.","translation":"She kept that love **letter** for many years."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsamahin o pag-isahin ang dalawa o higit pang bagay, elemento, o ideya upang bumuo ng isang bago at buong entidad.
original_explanation: Think of it as the secret to the perfect adobo—the soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, and pepper all merging into one glorious flavor. Or when two separate chismis from different sources suddenly connect and you have the complete, scandalous picture. It’s creating a whole that's greater than the sum of its parts.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, literary, or culinary contexts to mean the blending of elements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **maglangkap** ang mga sangkap bago hanguin ang niluluto.","translation":"Let the ingredients **merge** before taking the dish off the heat."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang tula, pinilit niyang **maglangkap** ang luma at bagong pananaw.","translation":"In his poem, he tried **to incorporate** old and new perspectives."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging madaling magalit o mainis.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pagka-" (estado ng pagiging) at "magagalitin" (madaling magalit).
original_explanation: This is you before your morning coffee. This is your friend who gets hangry. It's that tita who complains about everything at the family reunion. Basically, the default mood of anyone stuck in EDSA traffic.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang katangian ng personalidad na madaling mag-init ang ulo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko maintindihan ang **pagkamagagalitin** niya tuwing umaga.","translation":"I can't understand his **crankiness** every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang umangkop o iakma sa maraming iba't ibang gawain, tungkulin, o aktibidad.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung kaibigan mong singer, dancer, vlogger, at marunong pa magluto ng adobo. Pwede sa lahat ng raket. O kaya 'yung jacket mo na pwede sa office, sa mall, at pang-motor pa. Yan ang bersatil!
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang tao o bagay na maraming gamit o talento.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **bersatil** na aktor si John Lloyd Cruz dahil kaya niyang gumanap sa drama at komedya.","translation":"John Lloyd Cruz is a **versatile** actor because he can perform in both drama and comedy."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng isang **bersatil** na kasangkapan na magagamit sa iba't ibang uri ng pag-aayos.","translation":"We need a **versatile** tool that can be used for different kinds of repairs."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang pigilan o pahintuin sa ginagawa o sa isang pagkilos; nagpapatuloy nang walang abala.
original_explanation: The 'Unstoppable' meme, but in Tagalog. It's you with your unli-rice, the chismis from your tita, or a K-Pop group's comeback. Walang makakapigil! It’s the energy of a freight train and a determined fan base combined.
usage_notes: Used to describe a person, force, or movement that shows strong momentum and determination.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-angat ng teknolohiya ay isang puwersang **di-mapapatigil**.","translation":"The rise of technology is an **unstoppable** force."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang determinasyon, tila **di-mapapatigil** si Lea sa pag-abot ng kanyang pangarap.","translation":"With her determination, it seems Lea is **unstoppable** in reaching for her dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng kalmadong pagwawalang-bahala, na para bang hindi apektado o interesado sa mga nangyayari sa paligid.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'pake ko' or 'dedma' attitude. This is that person who sees a major issue blowing up on Twitter, and their only reaction is a slow blink. Or your crush who sees you, but acts like you're just another piece of furniture. 'Nonchalant yarn?' is the go-to sarcastic comment from a friend when you're trying too hard to act cool. A 'nonchalant bf' is the guy who replies 'k' to your long, emotional message.
usage_notes: A direct English/French loanword used in Taglish conversations, especially to describe a person's cool, indifferent, or 'pa-cool' behavior. The phrases 'nonchalant bf' and 'nonchalant yarn' are very common in modern colloquial speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit bagsak ang grades niya, **nonchalant** lang siyang pumasok sa klase.","translation":"Even though his grades were failing, he just came to class looking **nonchalant**."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang maging **nonchalant** pero halata namang kinakabahan siya.","translation":"He tried to be **nonchalant** but it was obvious he was nervous."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahing tanggapan o sentro ng operasyon ng isang organisasyon, kumpanya, o militar.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na "headquarters", na isinunod sa baybaying Filipino.
original_explanation: 'Yung main branch. Sa barkada, ito 'yung bahay kung saan kayo laging tumatambay. Sa pamilya, ito 'yung kusina kung saan nagaganap lahat ng chismisan at mahalagang desisyon. "Tara sa hedkwarters!" means "Let's go to our usual spot!"
usage_notes: Ginagamit din ang mga salitang "punong-tanggapan" o "himpilan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **hedkwarters** ng pulisya ay nasa Kampo Crame.","translation":"The police **headquarters** is at Camp Crame."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang patayong suporta o haligi, karaniwang yari sa bato o kongkreto, na sumusuporta sa isang arko, entablatura, o iba pang bahagi ng isang gusali.
original_explanation: Parang yung kaibigan mong laging andyan para sa'yo, your 'rock'. Sa construction, ito yung matibay na poste na sumasalo sa bigat ng building. Sa buhay, ito yung mga taong pinagkakatiwalaan mo na hindi ka bibitawan.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin sa metaporikal na paraan upang tukuyin ang isang pundasyon o pangunahing suporta ng isang grupo o ideya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **pilar** ng sinaunang templo ay nananatiling nakatayo.","translation":"The **pillars** of the ancient temple remain standing."},{"sentence":"Siya ang itinuturing na **pilar** ng kanilang pamilya.","translation":"He is considered the **pillar** of their family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkalahatang publiko, mga tao, o ang karamihan sa isang lipunan.
etymology: Possibly from Sanskrit `mantra` (counsel) or related to `dala` (to carry, as in carrying a collective identity). The exact origin is debated.
original_explanation: The 'madlang people' that hosts on noontime shows always greet. It’s everyone, the general public, the crowd. If you're doing something for the madla, you're doing it for the people, for the masses. It's a more formal way of saying 'everyone.'
usage_notes: Often used in the phrase `madlang-tao` to emphasize 'the people.' Common in media and formal speeches.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang anunsyo ay para sa kaalaman ng buong **madla**.","translation":"The announcement is for the information of the entire **public**."},{"sentence":"Isang pagtatanghal na bukas sa **madla**.","translation":"A performance open to **the public**."}]

translation: a strike, a lash, a blow
meaning_filipino: Ang malakas na pagpalo o pagtama ng isang bagay sa iba, tulad ng alon sa dalampasigan o latigo sa balat.
original_explanation: The sound and action of waves crashing on the shore ('hampas ng alon'). It's also the result of your sibling getting on your last nerve and you finally retaliate with a pillow. It's a forceful impact, whether from nature or from a person who's had enough.
usage_notes: Can be both literal (a physical strike) and figurative (the 'blow' of a tragedy). The verb form is 'hampasin' (to strike something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lakas ng **hampas** ng alon kaya nasira ang pader.","translation":"The **strike** of the waves was so strong that the wall was destroyed."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang malamig na **hampas** ng hangin sa kanyang mukha.","translation":"She felt the cold **blow** of the wind on her face."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na bahagi ng buhok na tumutubo sa ibang direksyon kumpara sa iba; maaari ring tumukoy sa maliit na ipu-ipo o alimpuyo sa tubig.
original_explanation: That stubborn patch of hair on your head that has its own life and refuses to cooperate with your comb, gel, or life decisions. It's the original 'bad hair day' culprit. It can also mean a small whirlpool, which is basically a balinsuso for water.
usage_notes: More commonly used to refer to a cowlick. The 'whirlpool' meaning is less common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong ayos niya sa buhok, halata pa rin ang kanyang **balinsuso**.","translation":"No matter how he styles his hair, his **cowlick** is still obvious."},{"sentence":"May nabuong **balinsuso** sa gitna ng batis.","translation":"A small **whirlpool** formed in the middle of the stream."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatabi o pag-iimbak ng isang bagay, tulad ng pera o datos, para sa paggamit sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: Infinitive form. Ito yung goal mo sa buhay, pero laging nauunahan ng "add to cart". Sa BPO, ito yung utos ng TL mo bago mag-end shift: "Magsave ka ng work, baka magka-system issue!"
usage_notes: A very common Taglish verb used in both financial and technological contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magsave** ng pera para sa aking kinabukasan.","translation":"I need **to save** money for my future."},{"sentence":"Pindutin ang Ctrl+S para **magsave** ng iyong dokumento.","translation":"Press Ctrl+S **to save** your document."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng sukdulang kahirapan o kawalan; pagiging maralita sa pinakamatinding antas.
etymology: From ka- + dayukdok + -an. 'Dayukdok' means extreme hunger or poverty.
original_explanation: This is a very deep Tagalog word for 'sobrang hirap.' Level 99 poverty. Yung tipong hindi na lang 'isang kahig, isang tuka,' kundi wala nang matuka. It's a word you'd find in classic literature or a very serious documentary.
usage_notes: A very formal and somewhat archaic word. Not used in casual conversation. `Kahirapan` is the common term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang naghihirap sa **kadayukdukan** sa mga liblib na lugar.","translation":"Many families suffer in **extreme poverty** in remote areas."},{"sentence":"Ang nobela ay tungkol sa pag-ahon ng isang tao mula sa **kadayukdukan**.","translation":"The novel is about a person's rise from **destitution**."}]

translation: a simian-like monster or ghoul; swagger
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halimaw o maligno sa mitolohiyang Pilipino na sinasabing may wangis ng isang malaking unggoy; maaari ring tumukoy sa paglalakad na may pagyayabang o pagpapakitang-gilas.
etymology: Hindi tiyak ang pinagmulan, posibleng mula sa isang lokal na terminong mitolohikal.
original_explanation: This is a deep cut from Filipino folklore, a big monkey-like monster. Think of it as a less famous cousin of the Kapre. But in some contexts, it can also mean a swagger, that 'lakad-mayaman' or 'angas' walk you do when you just got your sahod.
usage_notes: Bihira ang salitang ito. Ang kahulugang 'halimaw' ay mula sa alamat. Ang kahulugang 'pagyayabang sa paglakad' ay mas bihira pa at maaaring panrehiyon lamang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinatatakutan ng mga bata ang kuwento tungkol sa **balikaw** na naninirahan sa gubat.","translation":"The children were afraid of the story about the **balikaw** that lives in the forest."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **balikaw** ang kanyang paglakad matapos manalo sa kompetisyon.","translation":"His walk was full of **swagger** after winning the competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong dalubhasa sa pag-aaral ng kasaysayan o isang mahusay na tagapagsalaysay ng mga kuwento.
original_explanation: The official term for your lolo who has a story for *everything*, or the historian you follow on TikTok like Ambeth Ocampo who makes 'chismis' about historical figures. It's someone who makes the past interesting, whether it's national history or just family gossip. The OG 'Maritess.'
usage_notes: More formal than 'kuwentista' (storyteller). Often implies a degree of authority or expertise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Ambeth Ocampo ay isang kilalang **estoryador** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Ambeth Ocampo is a well-known **historian** in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Ang lolo ko ang **estoryador** ng aming pamilya; alam niya ang lahat ng kuwento.","translation":"My grandfather is the **storyteller** of our family; he knows all the stories."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglapit at pagtali ng sasakyang-dagat tulad ng barko o bangka sa daungan o piyer.
original_explanation: This is what ships do after a long journey at sea. They find a port and magdaong to rest, unload cargo, or let people off. It's the nautical equivalent of finally finding a parking spot at the mall on a payday weekend.
usage_notes: Specific to maritime contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghihintay ang mga mangingisda ng tamang panahon upang **magdaong**.","translation":"The fishermen are waiting for the right time to **dock**."},{"sentence":"Saan tayo pwedeng **magdaong** para magkarga ng suplay?","translation":"Where can we **anchor** to load supplies?"}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing bilog ang isang bagay; hubugin sa anyong sirkulo.
original_explanation: The action of making something round. Like when you're making palitaw or bilo-bilo for merienda and you need to roll the dough into little balls. It's the 'verb form' of your New Year's resolution to get a rounder... uh... savings account.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang palipat; nangangailangan ng tuwirang layon (object).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Biluhin** mo ang masa para gawing pandesal.","translation":"**Make** the dough **round** to make pandesal."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **biluhin** ang mga piraso ng luwad bago ito ihulma.","translation":"The pieces of clay need to be **made round** before they are molded."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na hindi mamamayan ng isang bansa; isang dayuhan. Bilang pang-uri, tumutukoy ito sa anumang bagay na nagmula sa ibang bansa.
etymology: From Sanskrit वणिज (vaṇija), meaning 'merchant, trader,' as early foreigners encountered were often traders.
original_explanation: Anyone who isn't Pinoy. Your friendly neighborhood expat, the tourist asking for directions to the nearest Jollibee, the K-Pop idol you stan. It can also describe things, like 'produktong banyaga' (foreign product). It's not necessarily negative, just a way of saying 'not from around here.'
usage_notes: Can be used as both a noun ('Ang mga banyaga...') and an adjective ('kulturang banyaga'). 'Dayuhan' is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **banyaga** ang namamasyal sa Boracay tuwing tag-init.","translation":"Many **foreigners** tour Boracay during the summer."},{"sentence":"Mas tinatangkilik niya ang mga pelikulang Pilipino kaysa sa mga **banyaga**.","translation":"He patronizes Filipino films more than **foreign** ones."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglabag sa isang kasunduan, pangako, o panunumpa; pagtataksil sa tiwala.
etymology: From 'talo' (defeat/lose) and 'sira' (break), but the combined meaning refers to breaking one's word or faith.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginawa ng kaibigan mong nangako na ililibre ka pero biglang "nagka-amnesia". O yung ex mong nagsabing "ikaw lang," pero may iba pa palang "ikaw" sa phonebook niya. It's the ultimate "walang isang salita" move.
usage_notes: A very strong word implying betrayal and dishonesty. The user-provided 'pagtalusiraan' is a verb form, while this entry is for the base noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtalusira** sa kasunduan ay maaaring humantong sa kaso.","translation":"A **breach of contract** can lead to a lawsuit."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya mapapatawad ang **pagtalusira** ng kanyang pinagkakatiwalaang kaibigan.","translation":"She cannot forgive the **treachery** of her trusted friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na pinaniniwalaang may taglay na kapangyarihang mahiwaga na nagbibigay proteksyon o suwerte sa may-ari nito.
original_explanation: The OG power bank. Ito 'yung anting-anting ni lolo na bawal daw hawakan. Pwedeng kwintas, bato, o kahit kapirasong papel na may Latin na dasal. Sabi nila, nagbibigay ito ng proteksyon laban sa bala, aswang, o sa masamang tingin ng ex mo. Sa modern times, ang agimat mo ay 'yung fully-charged phone at wallet na may laman.
usage_notes: Deeply rooted in Philippine folklore and folk Catholicism. 'Anting-anting' is a very common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May dala siyang **agimat** upang hindi siya tablan ng anumang kapahamakan.","translation":"He carries an **amulet** so that no harm will befall him."},{"sentence":"Naniniwala siyang ang medalyon ay isang mabisang **agimat**.","translation":"He believes the medallion is an effective **talisman**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalagyan na karaniwang yari sa hinabing materyales tulad ng yantok, kawayan, o plastik, na ginagamit sa pagdadala o pag-iimbak ng mga bagay.
original_explanation: The OG tote bag. Whether it's for your laundry, your groceries at the palengke (bayong), or the thing you shoot a ball into, it's a basket. In the office, it's where your brilliant ideas (and trash) go. In romance, it's where you can get 'basted' or 'basket-ed' (rejected).
usage_notes: The Filipino word 'bayong' or 'buslo' refers to specific types of baskets. 'Basket' is also used in the context of basketball.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Punuin mo ang **basket** ng mga prutas.","translation":"Fill the **basket** with fruits."},{"sentence":"Sino ang maglalaba ng **basket** ng maruruming damit?","translation":"Who will wash the **basket** of dirty clothes?"}]

translation: to have a mistake made; to make a mistake together
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pagkakamali o paggawa ng kamalian, madalas ay kasama ang isa pa.
etymology: From 'magka-' (prefix indicating having or experiencing) + 'sala' (mistake, sin, fault).
original_explanation: This is when you and your bestie both mess up. Like when you 'magkabisala' in your dance practice and end up looking like confused flamingos. Or when two politicians 'magkabisala' in their statements and the whole country facepalms. It’s a shared 'oops' moment.
usage_notes: This is not a very common word. People would more likely say 'nagkamali' or 'parehong nagkamali'. 'Magka-' here implies either having a fault or two parties sharing a fault.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iingat sila na huwag **magkabisala** sa kanilang plano.","translation":"They are being careful not to **have a mistake** in their plan."},{"sentence":"Kung **magkabisala** man tayo, sabay nating haharapin.","translation":"If we ever **make a mistake together**, we will face it together."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na nangangahulugang kumikilos bilang kinatawan, sa kapangyarihan, o para sa kapakanan ng isang tao, pangkat, o konsepto.
original_explanation: The ultimate "I'm just the messenger" or "I'm doing this for a higher cause" card. You use it for everything from "In the name of the Father..." to "Sa ngalan ng pag-ibig, gagawin ko ang lahat!" (In the name of love, I'll do everything!). It can be super formal, like a legal declaration, or super dramatic, like a line from a teleserye. Use 'ng' for common nouns (ng pag-ibig) and 'ni' for proper names (ni Rizal).
usage_notes: Use "ng" before common nouns (e.g., sa ngalan ng batas - in the name of the law) and "ni" before personal names (e.g., sa ngalan ni Dr. Jose Rizal).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinanggap ko ang parangal **sa ngalan ng** aking buong koponan.","translation":"I accepted the award **in the name of** my entire team."},{"sentence":"Ipinaglalaban nila ang karapatan **sa ngalan ni** Ka Pepe.","translation":"They are fighting for their rights **in the name of** Ka Pepe."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na paghila sa buhok ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The signature move in any classic Pinoy 'telenovela' catfight. It's what happens when 'kontrabida' meets 'bida'. It's not just a pull; it's an act of war. Can also happen between siblings fighting over the TV remote. The verb form, 'sabunutan', is the main event.
usage_notes: The act is 'sabunot', the mutual act or event is 'sabunutan' (a hair-pulling fight). The verb is 'sabunutan' (to pull someone's hair).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **sabunot** ang natanggap niya mula sa galit na babae.","translation":"She received a strong **pull of her hair** from the angry woman."},{"sentence":"Nagkasakitan sila at nauwi sa **sabunutan** ang kanilang pag-aaway.","translation":"They hurt each other and their fight ended in a **hair-pulling** match."}]

translation: to be misplaced; to be lost from sight or memory
meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan upang mawala o maligaw ang isang bagay; mawala sa isipan o paningin.
original_explanation: That moment of panic when you can't find your phone, keys, or wallet. It didn't just disappear, it was "mapa-waglit" — temporarily misplaced into another dimension (probably under the sofa cushions). It can also happen to a thought you were *just* about to say.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang iyong selpon at baka **mapawaglit** mo sa palengke.","translation":"Be careful with your cellphone, you might **misplace** it at the market."},{"sentence":"Sa dami ng iniisip, madaling **mapawaglit** sa aking isipan ang mga maliliit na detalye.","translation":"With so much on my mind, it's easy for small details to **get lost** from my thoughts."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bisa o epekto ng isang bagay, tulad ng gamot, lason, o armas, na tumatagos o gumagana sa pinatutungkulan nito.
original_explanation: That "It's working!" feeling. When the Biogesic finally kicks in and your headache disappears. Or when your 'sermon' to your younger sibling finally makes them wash the dishes. "Walang talab sa kanya ang pangaral ko, matigas talaga ang ulo." It can also mean when a blade or bullet penetrates something.
usage_notes: Often used with 'walang' (no) to mean 'ineffective' ('walang talab'). Can refer to the effect of medicine, advice, weapons, or even magic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis ang **talab** ng gamot na ito laban sa lagnat.","translation":"The **effect** of this medicine against fever is fast."},{"sentence":"Parang walang **talab** ang mga bala sa suot niyang agimat.","translation":"It seems the bullets have no **effect** on the amulet he is wearing."},{"sentence":"Sana may **talab** ang mga sinabi ko sa kanya.","translation":"I hope what I said to him has an **effect**."}]

translation: to be humble; to humble oneself
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagpapakita ng kababaang-loob, pag-amin sa pagkakamali, o pag-iwas sa pagyayabang.
etymology: From magpa- (causative) + kumbaba (a variant of kababaan, humility). 'kumbaba' itself is from ka- + baba.
original_explanation: This is the antithesis of 'flex culture.' It's the act of taking the lower seat, admitting you're wrong, or just not bragging about your achievements. When you have a fight with your jowa and you know it's your fault, it's time to magpakumbaba and say sorry. It's about putting your ego in check and choosing peace or righteousness over being 'right.'
usage_notes: A virtue-related verb, often used in moral or relational advice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit gaano ka na katagumpay, matuto ka pa ring **magpakumbaba**.","translation":"No matter how successful you've become, you should still learn to **be humble**."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magpakumbaba** at humingi ng tawad para matapos na ang gulo.","translation":"He decided to **humble himself** and ask for forgiveness to end the conflict."}]

meaning_filipino: Mabilis na pag-agaw o pagkuha sa isang bagay, karaniwang ginagawa nang biglaan at mula sa itaas, tulad ng isang ibong mandaragit.
original_explanation: Parang 'snatcher' sa Recto, pero version ng mga hayop. Yung agila na biglang kukunin yung sisiw, or yung kaibigan mo na biglang kukunin yung last piece ng french fries sa plato mo. That swift, surprise grab is 'dagit'.
usage_notes: Often used to describe birds of prey. The verb forms are `dumagit` (actor focus) and `dagitin` (object focus).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na **dinagit** ng lawin ang ahas sa damuhan.","translation":"The hawk quickly **snatched** the snake from the grass."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka may **dumagit** ng cellphone mo.","translation":"Be careful, someone might **snatch** your cellphone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kasangkapan, karaniwang yari sa salamin o plastik na may gomang dulo, na ginagamit upang magbigay ng likido nang paunti-unti o patak-patak.
etymology: From "pan-" + "patak" (drop). The "n" in the prefix "pan-" assimilates to "m" before a root word starting with 'p'.
original_explanation: That little tool for your eye drops or for giving your baby their vitamins. It's the MVP when you need to control the flow, unlike your feelings for your crush which are more like a waterfall. One drop at a time lang dapat.
usage_notes: Used for medicine, laboratory work, or any application requiring precise liquid dispensing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **pamatak** para sa gamot sa mata.","translation":"She used a **dropper** for the eye medicine."},{"sentence":"Ilang patak lang ang kailangan, kaya dahan-dahan sa paggamit ng **pamatak**.","translation":"Only a few drops are needed, so be careful when using the **dropper**."}]

translation: to aspire to, to desire intensely
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatakda ng isang bagay bilang isang matinding hangarin o pagnanasa; ang pagsisikap na makamit ang isang mithiin.
original_explanation: The verb form of your #LifeGoal. This is the 'to do' part of your 'sana all.' It's actively wanting, dreaming, and working towards something. Example: 'Lunggatin mong maging debt-free by 2027!'
usage_notes: This is the object-focus verb form of 'lunggati'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ba ang **nilulunggati** mo sa buhay?","translation":"What do you **aspire to** in life?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot na **lunggatin** ang pinakamataas na pangarap.","translation":"Don't be afraid to **desire intensely** the highest dream."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pagpapahintulot sa isang tao o hayop na lumangoy.
etymology: Mula sa "pa-" (unlaping pautos) + "langoy" (lumangoy) + "-in" (hulaping tuon sa layon).
original_explanation: That moment when your cool tito throws you into the pool and shouts "Swim!" even if you're just a toddler. It's the sink-or-swim approach to life, literally. "Sige na, palanguyin mo na 'yang aso, tingnan natin kung marunong."
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang pautos na nangangahulugang maging sanhi o payagan ang isang tao/bagay na lumangoy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **palanguyin** ang bata sa malalim na bahagi ng dagat.","translation":"Don't let the child **swim** in the deep part of the sea."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **palanguyin** ang aking alagang aso sa ilog.","translation":"I want to **make** my pet dog **swim** in the river."}]

translation: act of completely undressing; total nudity
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalis ng lahat ng saplot sa katawan hanggang sa maging ganap na walang damit.
etymology: From "paghuhubad at hubad", meaning "undressing and naked".
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "walang tago". It’s not just taking off a jacket; it’s going full-on birthday suit. Think of it as the final scene in a dramatic movie when a character sheds their old self, or what you do in the privacy of your bathroom before a much-needed shower after a long day commuting. It's about being completely bare, literally and sometimes figuratively.
usage_notes: The structure "pag-X-'t-X" (e.g., pagtakbo't takbo, pag-iyak at iyak) intensifies the action. Here, it implies a complete and total state of undressing and being naked.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang eksena ng **paghuhubu't-hubad** ay tinanggal sa bersyon na ipinalabas sa telebisyon.","translation":"The scene of **complete undressing** was removed from the version shown on television."},{"sentence":"Ang **paghuhubu't-hubad** sa publiko ay labag sa batas.","translation":"**Public nudity** is against the law."}]

translation: impulse buys; great finds from impulse shopping
meaning_filipino: Mga produktong binili nang hindi planado, kadalasan dahil sa impluwensya ng social media o mga kaibigan, na itinuturing na maganda o sulit na pagbili.
etymology: A modern Taglish phrase combining the slang 'budol' (impulse buy) and English 'finds'.
original_explanation: The trophies from your latest shopping 'budol'. These are the things you bought on impulse from Shopee, Lazada, or TikTok Shop that you now proudly show off. 'Hindi ko 'to kailangan, pero ang ganda! #BudolFinds'.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of online shopping and social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"I-share mo naman ang iyong mga latest **budol finds** mula sa online sale.","translation":"Please share your latest **impulse buys** from the online sale."},{"sentence":"Itong air fryer ay isa sa mga pinakamagandang **budol finds** ko.","translation":"This air fryer is one of my best **impulse-buy finds**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtutol, pagkontra, o hindi pagsang-ayon sa isang ideya, utos, o daloy. Ito ay isang baryasyon ng salitang 'pagsalansang'.
original_explanation: This is the act of being a 'kontrabida.' When everyone is going right, you go left. 'Pagsalangsang' is going against the current, whether it's a literal current of water or the 'current' of popular opinion. It's defiance, opposition, arguing against a proposal just because. Think of it as the spirit of a protest or a debate. (Note: This is a less common variant of 'pagsalansang').
usage_notes: A variant of the more common 'pagsalansang'. Both mean the same thing and imply active resistance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagsalangsang** sa agos ng ilog ay nagpakita ng kanyang lakas.","translation":"His **going against** the river's current showed his strength."},{"sentence":"Hindi ikinatuwa ng pinuno ang **pagsalangsang** ng kanyang mga tauhan sa bagong patakaran.","translation":"The leader was not pleased with his people's **opposition** to the new rule."}]

translation: to mock; to ridicule; to scorn
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglibak, pagkutya, o paghamak sa isang tao o bagay sa paraang sarkastiko.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'uyam' (sarcasm) at hulaping '-in', na nagsasaad ng aksyon na gagawin sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'uyam'. This is what you do when you deploy that high-level sarcasm. To uyamin someone is to hit them with a 'Wow, ang aga mo!' when they arrive an hour late. It's the action of being a professional 'mambabara'.
usage_notes: Isang mas pormal o pampanitikang paraan upang sabihin ang 'pagtawanan' o 'kutyain'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **uyamin** ang kanyang mga pangarap.","translation":"Do not **mock** his dreams."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **uyamin** ang mga taong hindi niya gusto.","translation":"He likes to **ridicule** people he doesn't like."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o kilos ng hindi pag-alala sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na nag-effort ka nang sobra para sa kanya, tapos bigla siyang nakakalimot sa anniversary n'yo. Parang system update lang na nag-reformat ng memory. O kaya 'yung moment na pumasok ka sa kwarto tapos 'di mo na alam bakit ka nandun. That's you, nakakalimot.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a state of forgetting, either as a habit or in a specific moment. The prefix "nakaka-" can also imply "causes one to forget," but "nakakalimot" is almost always used for the actor forgetting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Minsan, **nakakalimot** na akong kumain dahil sa dami ng trabaho.","translation":"Sometimes, I **forget** to eat because of so much work."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala kung **nakakalimot** siya, matanda na kasi.","translation":"Don't worry if he **forgets**, it's because he's already old."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na salaysay, karaniwang kinasasangkutan ng mga supernatural na nilalang o pangyayari, na nagpapaliwanag ng isang natural na kababalaghan o ng kasaysayan ng isang pamayanan.
original_explanation: The stories your lola told you about kapres and manananggals. Also, the belief that "bawal magwalis sa gabi" or that you'll get rich from that networking scheme your friend is pushing. Basically, a story that's more "chismis" than science.
usage_notes: Used for ancient myths as well as modern misconceptions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **mito** lamang na masama ang pagligo sa gabi kung ikaw ay may sakit.","translation":"It's just a **myth** that taking a bath at night is bad when you're sick."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o resulta ng pagpili sa isang tao para sa isang posisyon, tungkulin, o karangalan.
original_explanation: This is the 'sashaying' moment. 'Yung tinawag ang pangalan mo as the new team lead, or when your friend gets chosen as the muse for the office sportsfest. It's the official act of being appointed or chosen. The 'And the new Miss Universe is...' moment.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like government, corporate appointments, or official selections.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdiwang ng buong bayan ang **pagkahirang** sa kanya bilang bagong hukom.","translation":"The whole town celebrated his **appointment** as the new judge."},{"sentence":"Maraming tumutol sa **pagkahirang** sa bagong direktor ng kumpanya.","translation":"Many objected to the **selection** of the new company director."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking nagpapakita ng mga katangian, kilos, at damdaming karaniwang iniuugnay sa kababaihan, o isang lalaking sekswal na naaakit sa kapwa lalaki.
etymology: From Old Tagalog *bakla* meaning confusion or uncertainty. The shift in meaning to 'homosexual' is a more modern development.
original_explanation: Originally just meaning 'confused' or 'undecided,' it's now the common term for a gay man in the Philippines. They're often the life of the party, the wittiest person in the room, and your go-to for brutally honest life advice. Often used with affection among friends, but can be a slur depending on tone and context.
usage_notes: While widely used, the term can be considered pejorative by some. Tone and intent are crucial. The LGBTQ+ community in the Philippines has reclaimed the word, but its use by outsiders can still be sensitive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kaibigan kong **baklâ** ang nag-ayos ng buhok ko para sa party.","translation":"My **gay** friend fixed my hair for the party."},{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya na siya ay isang **baklâ**.","translation":"He is proud to be a **gay** man."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol o may kinalaman sa kalusugan ng katawan at isipan.
original_explanation: Anything related to your "fitspo" goals. That green smoothie you hate but drink anyway? That's for 'pangkalusugan' reasons. Your HMO card, the fun run you joined, the advice to "drink 8 glasses of water"—it all falls under this. It's the opposite of a 'cheat day'.
usage_notes: Very common in media, government programs (DOH), and daily life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang mga ehersisyong **pangkalusugan** araw-araw.","translation":"Daily **health** exercises are important."},{"sentence":"Nagbigay siya ng payong **pangkalusugan** sa mga kabataan.","translation":"He gave **health**-related advice to the youth."}]

translation: to get a splinter; to be pierced by a sharp object
meaning_filipino: Ang mapasukan ng maliit at matulis na bagay, tulad ng tinik o subo ng kahoy, sa balat.
original_explanation: That super annoying feeling when a tiny piece of wood (like from a barbecue stick or a wooden bench) decides to make your finger its new home. It's a small problem that causes a surprisingly big amount of drama and requires tweezers and a brave friend.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to being pierced by a small, sharp object like a splinter, thorn, or shard. The verb form is 'nasalubsob' (got a splinter).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Aray! **Nasalubsob** yata ako ng tinik ng isda.","translation":"Ouch! I think I **got pierced by** a fish bone."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang umupo diyan sa lumang upuan, baka ka **masalubsob**.","translation":"Don't sit on that old chair, you might **get a splinter**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng pagiging masaya, kuntento, at nasisiyahan sa kasalukuyang sitwasyon o kalagayan.
original_explanation: The feeling of 'pwede na 'to'. Hindi ka super happy, hindi ka malungkot. You're just... chill. Parang 'yung feeling after a good meal, or when your Grab driver doesn't cancel on you. The Filipino version is 'kuntento', which is often a life goal.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit sa Filipino ang salitang 'kuntento', na hiram din sa Espanyol ('contento'). Ang paggamit ng 'content' bilang pang-uri ay hindi gaanong madalas sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit simple lang ang buhay, siya ay **content** na sa piling ng kanyang pamilya.","translation":"Even with a simple life, he is **content** in the presence of his family."},{"sentence":"She was **content** with the small victory.","translation":"She was **content** with the small victory."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o tulung-tulong na pagdadala ng mga bagay, karaniwang gamit ang kamay.
original_explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work... especially when you're carrying all the groceries from the car. 'Tara, **bitbitan** na tayo!' It's the bayanihan spirit applied to your palengke haul or when moving apartments. Can also refer to the handle of a bag or container.
usage_notes: Often used to imply mutual or shared carrying. Can also function as a noun referring to a handle ('ang bitbitan ng basket').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **bitbitan** ng mga donasyon para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"There was a **session of carrying** donations for the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Matibay ba ang **bitbitan** ng maleta mo?","translation":"Is the handle of your suitcase sturdy?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan nag-eehersisyo ang mga tao gamit ang iba't ibang kagamitan para sa pisikal na kalusugan.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'gym', pinaikling anyo ng 'gymnasium'.
original_explanation: The place you pay for every month but only visit the first week of January. Para sa mga gustong maging "fit-spiration" pero nauuwi sa "eat-spiration" pagkatapos ng isang oras na workout. Dito rin nagaganap ang mga "gym-selfie" for the 'gram.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang isang hiram na salita sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, lalo na sa mga kabataan at sa urban na lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta ako sa **gym** mamaya para mag-workout.","translation":"I'm going to the **gym** later to work out."},{"sentence":"Nag-enroll siya sa **gym** para magpapayat.","translation":"She enrolled in a **gym** to lose weight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng mukha na nasa ilalim ng bibig; ang panga.
original_explanation: Your **sapo** is your chin. It's where you rest your hand when you're deep in thought, pretending to listen in a meeting, or showing off that new jawline from your gym grind. Not to be confused with 'baba', which is more common.
usage_notes: While 'baba' is the common word for chin, 'sapo' is a more literary or archaic term, sometimes also referring to the jaw area.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatukod ang kanyang palad sa kanyang **sapo** habang malalim na nag-iisip.","translation":"His palm was propped on his **chin** while he was deep in thought."},{"sentence":"Tinamaan ng bola ang kanyang **sapo** kaya medyo nahilo siya.","translation":"The ball hit his **jaw**, so he felt a bit dizzy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng tumatanggap ng pensiyon, karaniwan dahil sa pagreretiro sa trabaho o bilang benepisyaryo.
original_explanation: She's your tita who's living her best life post-retirement. After decades of working, she's now a professional world traveler, Zumba enthusiast, or a full-time plantita, all funded by her pension. She's the one sending good morning messages with flower GIFs in the family group chat.
usage_notes: Ito ang pambabaeng anyo ng 'pensyonado'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lola ko ay isang **pensyonada** mula sa pagiging guro.","translation":"My grandmother is a **pensioner** from being a teacher."},{"sentence":"Abala ang mga **pensyonada** sa kanilang lingguhang ballroom dancing.","translation":"The female **pensioners** are busy with their weekly ballroom dancing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang damdamin ng pagkainis, pagkabagot, o pagkadiri na dulot ng isang bagay na paulit-ulit, nakakairita, o hindi kanais-nais.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when the internet connection drops for the 10th time during an important meeting. It's the 'Nakakainis na, ha!' vibe. It's less intense than 'galit' (anger) but more fed up than 'inis' (annoyed). It's the emotional equivalent of an eye-roll that you can feel in your soul.
usage_notes: A common emotion that can range from mild annoyance to strong disgust or exasperation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang kanyang **pagkasuya** sa paulit-ulit na tanong.","translation":"She couldn't hide her **exasperation** at the repetitive questions."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkasuya** ko ay umabot na sa sukdulan.","translation":"My **exasperation** has reached its limit."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling o pagkuha ng isang bagay mula sa iba, kadalasan bilang isang pabor, tulong, o donasyon.
original_explanation: The art of asking for something, whether it's *balato* from a friend who just got their *sahod*, or asking your boss for a raise. It's the official verb for the "pahingi naman ako ng konti" culture. Not quite begging, not quite demanding, but somewhere in that polite but persistent sweet spot.
usage_notes: Used when asking for something tangible or intangible from someone. The focus is on the act of soliciting or requesting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiya na **manghingi** ng tulong kung kinakailangan.","translation":"Don't be shy to **ask for** help when needed."},{"sentence":"Pumunta siya sa opisina ng mayor upang **manghingi** ng donasyon para sa mga nasalanta.","translation":"He went to the mayor's office to **solicit** donations for the calamity victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Mula sa salitang "ubod" na nangangahulugang sentro o kaibuturan, ito ay tumutukoy sa sukdulan o pinakamatinding antas ng kasamaan.
original_explanation: This is not just 'bad', this is 'kontrabida sa teleserye' level of bad. The final boss of kasamaan. The person who cuts in line, steals your parking spot, and then takes the last piece of chicken joy. 'Ubod' here means 'to the core', so this person is evil to their very core.
usage_notes: 'Ubod ng' is an intensifier that can be used with other adjectives (e.g., 'ubod ng ganda' - extremely beautiful, 'ubod ng yaman' - extremely rich). This specific phrase is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang karakter na ginagampanan niya sa pelikula ay **ubod ng sama**.","translation":"The character she plays in the movie is **extremely evil**."},{"sentence":"Talaga namang **ubod ng sama** ang taong nanakit sa isang matanda.","translation":"A person who would hurt an old person is truly **extremely evil**."}]

translation: to be able to make someone sleep; to put to sleep
meaning_filipino: Magawang makatulog ang isang tao o hayop; magdulot ng antok.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your prof's lecture is more effective than any sleeping pill, or when you finally manage to put the baby down for a nap after hours of rocking. It's the magic trick every parent and bored student wishes they could perform on command.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **mapatulog** ang sanggol sa pamamagitan ng pag-awit.","translation":"She tried to **make** the baby **sleep** by singing."},{"sentence":"Ang gamot na ito ay kayang **mapatulog** kahit sino.","translation":"This medicine can **put anyone to sleep**."}]

meaning_filipino: Itinabi, itinukoy, o itinalaga para sa isang partikular na tao, bagay, o layunin. Ito ay nasa anyong pangnagdaan.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your 13th-month pay. A portion is for bills, a portion for gifts, and a portion for that milk tea you've been craving. You've 'allocated' or 'dedicated' it. "Inilaan ko ang puso ko sa'yo, pero binalewala mo lang." #Hugot
usage_notes: A very common word in formal writing, speeches, and dramatic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Inilaan** ng gobyerno ang malaking pondo para sa edukasyon.","translation":"The government **allocated** a large fund for education."},{"sentence":"**Inilaan** niya ang kanyang buhay sa pagtulong sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"He **dedicated** his life to helping the poor."}]

translation: a covering or shroud; a place of covering
meaning_filipino: Isang takip o anumang bagay na ginagamit bilang panakip o pananggalang, tulad ng kulambo o malaking tela.
original_explanation: Think of this as a big, protective covering. It could be a mosquito net ('kulambo') creating a safe zone from dengue, a thick blanket you hide under during a horror movie, or a canopy of leaves providing shade. Metaphorically, it's the feeling of being enveloped or protected, like being under the 'lambungan' of your mother's care.
usage_notes: 'Lambong' is the more common root word, meaning 'veil' or 'shroud'. The '-an' suffix here suggests a place or an encompassing object. It's less common than 'kulambo' or 'takip'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit nilang **lambungan** ang malaking dahon ng saging nang biglang umulan.","translation":"They used a large banana leaf as a **covering** when it suddenly rained."},{"sentence":"Ang gabi ay nagsilbing **lambungan** sa kanilang pagtatago.","translation":"The night served as a **shroud** for their hiding."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin ang mga marka, sulat, o datos mula sa isang ibabaw o digital na talaan.
original_explanation: What you wish you could do to your embarrassing Facebook posts from 2010. To **magbura** is to delete, to wipe clean. Also, what your prof does to the lecture notes on the whiteboard just as you're about to copy the last line.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magbura** ng mga lumang file sa aking computer para magkaroon ng espasyo.","translation":"I need to **erase** old files on my computer to create space."},{"sentence":"**Magbura** ka ng sulat sa pisara pagkatapos ng klase.","translation":"**Erase** the writing on the board after class."}]

translation: to bite (repeatedly); to be prone to biting
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pagkagat o ang pagkakaroon ng ugaling kumagat, karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga hayop o maliliit na bata.
original_explanation: This is what your neighbor's dog does when it escapes the gate. Or what a toddler does when they're teething and cranky. It's not just a single bite (that's 'kagat'), it's a habit or a series of bites. 'Huwag kang lalapit, nangangagat 'yan!' is a public service announcement.
usage_notes: The prefix 'mang-' implies a habitual or repeated action. Contrasts with 'kumagat' (to bite, single action) or 'kagatin' (to bite something, object-focused).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan kami na huwag hawakan ang aso dahil mahilig itong **mangagat**.","translation":"We were warned not to touch the dog because it is prone to **biting**."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mangagat** ng gamit ang tuta dahil sa pananakit ng gilagid.","translation":"The puppy started to **bite** things repeatedly because its gums were hurting."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi maluwag; mahirap paluwagin o kalasin; istrikto sa pagpapatupad ng mga alituntunin.
original_explanation: Your terror prof in college, your mom when you ask to go out past curfew, or your jeans after a festive Noche Buena. Lahat 'yan `mahigpit`.
usage_notes: Can describe physical tightness (a grip, a knot) or strictness (a rule, a person).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong **mahigpit** ang pagkakatali ng sapatos ko.","translation":"The knot on my shoes is too **tight**."},{"sentence":"Ang tatay ko ay **mahigpit** pagdating sa mga grado.","translation":"My father is **strict** when it comes to grades."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos ng kamay, ulo, o anumang bahagi ng katawan upang magpahiwatig ng isang mensahe o utos nang walang salita.
original_explanation: A variation of 'sinyal', but this one leans more towards physical gestures. It's the 'psst' with a nod of the head, the subtle eye-roll your friend gives you when your tita asks if you're getting married yet, or the hand gesture the parking attendant uses to guide you into a ridiculously tight spot.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'sinyal', but 'sinyas' (or 'senyas') more specifically implies a physical gesture or hand signal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ng **sinyas** ang pulis upang patigilin ang mga sasakyan.","translation":"The police officer used a hand **signal** to stop the vehicles."},{"sentence":"Isang kindat lang ang **sinyas** niya at naintindihan ko na agad.","translation":"Just one wink was his **signal** and I understood immediately."}]

translation: to rest, to take a break
meaning_filipino: Ang pansamantalang pagtigil sa paggawa o anumang aktibidad upang manumbalik ang lakas ng katawan at isipan.
original_explanation: The sacred command for every BPO agent, student, and overworked employee. It's that 15-minute coffee break, the weekend sleep-in, or the 'SL' (Sick Leave) you take for mental health reasons. 'Puyat ka na naman? **Magpahinga** ka uy!' It's the universe's way of telling you to log off and touch grass.
usage_notes: A fundamental word for daily life. 'Mamahinga' is a more formal synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng mahabang araw ng trabaho, masarap **magpahinga**.","translation":"After a long day of work, it's nice to **rest**."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan kami ng aming guro na **magpahinga** muna ng sampung minuto.","translation":"Our teacher told us to **take a break** for ten minutes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na nagpapahiwatig ng lokasyon sa hulihang bahagi o espasyo ng isang bagay. Ito ay halos kasingkahulugan ng "sa likod ng".
original_explanation: This is the slightly more formal cousin of "sa likod ng." You'd use this when describing where you parked your car ("sa likuran ng mall") or where the "dirty kitchen" is located. It's less for emotional support and more for giving actual, physical directions.
usage_notes: Often interchangeable with "sa likod ng," but can sometimes imply a larger area at the back rather than just immediately behind.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malawak na hardin **sa likuran ng** bahay.","translation":"There is a wide garden **at the back of** the house."}]

translation: to be intimidated; to act effeminately
meaning_filipino: Matakot, mangamba, o panghinaan ng loob; o kumilos na parang bakla.
etymology: From 'bakla' + '-in' suffix. The secondary meaning of 'to be intimidated' stems from the stereotype of effeminate men being weak or cowardly.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'bakla'. It can mean to act gay, but more often it's used colloquially to mean 'to get scared,' 'to chicken out,' or 'to be intimidated.' It's what your friends say when you're too scared to talk to your crush: 'Huwag kang baklahin diyan!'
usage_notes: This term carries a strong sense of machismo and can be considered offensive or homophobic, as it equates being gay with being weak or cowardly. Use with caution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **baklahín**, harapin mo ang iyong mga problema.","translation":"Don't **be intimidated**, face your problems."},{"sentence":"Tila **binakla** siya ng malakas na sigaw ng kanyang amo.","translation":"It seems he **was intimidated** by his boss's loud shout."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay-katwiran sa isang kilos, paniniwala, o desisyon; pagpapaliwanag upang ipakita na ito ay tama o makatarungan.
etymology: Mula sa `pag-` + `magmatuwid` (magbigay-katwiran), na mula sa `matuwid` (tuwid, tama).
original_explanation: Ito yung "let me explain" mo kapag nahuli ka sa kasalanan. It's your attempt to prove you're right, even when you're probably wrong. Minsan, defense mechanism lang. Minsan, sign of self-righteousness. "Hindi sa nagmamayabang ako, pero..."
usage_notes: Maaaring neutral (pagbibigay ng dahilan) o negatibo (pagiging mapagmagaling, paggawa ng dahilan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahaba ang kanyang naging **pagmamatwid** ngunit hindi pa rin siya pinaniwalaan.","translation":"His **justification** was long, but he still wasn't believed."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pagmamatwid**, sinabi niyang para sa kabutihan ng lahat ang kanyang ginawa.","translation":"In his **reasoning**, he said that what he did was for the good of everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging matakaw o labis na pagkain; kasibaan.
original_explanation: That state you enter during a 'kain-all-you-can' buffet. It's eating like you've been personally wronged by the concept of hunger. It’s not just being 'gutom' (hungry); it’s being 'patay-gutom' (starving) on a spiritual level. Think of a buwaya (crocodile) at a feeding frenzy. That's siba.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a voracious or greedy manner of eating. The adjective form is 'masiba' (gluttonous). Can also be used figuratively for greed in other contexts. The abstract noun form is 'kasibaan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **siba** niya sa pagkain, naubos agad ang handa.","translation":"Because of his **gluttony**, the food at the feast was quickly finished."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong masiba sa harap ng mga bisita; iwasan mo ang **siba**.","translation":"Don't be too voracious in front of the guests; avoid **gluttony**."}]

translation: to get food stuck in one's teeth
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng tinga o maliit na piraso ng pagkain na naipit sa pagitan ng mga ngipin.
etymology: From magka- (to have/get) + tinga (food particle stuck in teeth).
original_explanation: The awkward moment after eating popcorn or a mango when you smile for a picture and your friend whispers, "Bes, may tinga ka." This is the verb for that specific, universally embarrassing situation. To have *tinga*. Use a toothpick, stat!
usage_notes: A very specific and common verb related to eating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi akong **nagkakatenga** kapag kumakain ako ng mais.","translation":"I always **get food stuck in my teeth** when I eat corn."},{"sentence":"Tumingin ka sa salamin, baka **nagkatinga** ka.","translation":"Look in the mirror, you might have **gotten food stuck in your teeth**."}]

translation: to become addicted; to be deeply engrossed
meaning_filipino: Maging labis na nahuhumaling, gumon, o masangkot nang malalim sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay bisyo, sugal, o masamang gawain.
original_explanation: This is what happens when 'one more episode' on Netflix turns into finishing three seasons overnight. Or when your 'testing lang' sa mobile games turns into spending your baon for in-game currency. You got sucked in deep. Iwasang **mapalulong**, bes, baka maubos ang pera at oras mo.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation, often associated with addiction or destructive habits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kabataan ang **napapalulong** sa masamang bisyo dahil sa maling barkada.","translation":"Many youths **become addicted** to bad vices because of the wrong crowd."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula lang sa maliit na taya hanggang sa tuluyan siyang **napalulong** sa sugal.","translation":"It just started with a small bet until he completely **became addicted** to gambling."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasa o taong nag-aaral ng lingguwistika, ang siyentipikong pag-aaral ng wika at estruktura nito.
original_explanation: The ultimate "actually..." person when it comes to language. They're the ones who get genuinely excited about syntax, phonetics, and the etymology of "Marites." They don't just speak languages; they study the blueprint of how we speak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga **linggista** ang ebolusyon ng wikang Filipino.","translation":"**Linguists** are studying the evolution of the Filipino language."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **linggista**, interesado siya sa iba't ibang dialekto sa Pilipinas.","translation":"As a **linguist**, she is interested in the different dialects in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang establisyimento o ahensya kung saan maaaring magpadala o tumanggap ng pera, karaniwan mula sa ibang bansa.
original_explanation: The modern-day lifeline of the Filipino family. Ito ang lugar kung saan mo kinukuha ang pinagpaguran ni Mama/Papa/Tita/Tito/Ate/Kuya from abroad. Basically, the temple where you pray your padala arrives on time for bills payment, tuition, or the latest Shopee sale.
usage_notes: Widely used as a loan phrase in the Philippines. Often associated with specific brands like Palawan Express, Cebuana Lhuillier, Western Union.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumila si Aling Nena sa **remittance center** para kunin ang padala ng anak niya mula sa Dubai.","translation":"Aling Nena lined up at the **remittance center** to claim the money sent by her child from Dubai."},{"sentence":"Bukas ba ang **remittance center** kahit Linggo?","translation":"Is the **remittance center** open even on Sundays?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may matipuno, malakas, at malusog na pangangatawan.
original_explanation: This is your gym bro, your "hunk," your action star. Someone who is 'pisigan' is physically well-built, strong, and looks like they can carry all your grocery bags, your emotional baggage, and probably a sack of rice all at once. Think Fernando Poe Jr. or your local crossfit coach.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe a person's physique, particularly a man's.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **pisigan** na lalaki ang bida sa pelikula.","translation":"A **robust** man is the star of the movie."},{"sentence":"Naging **pisigan** ang kaniyang katawan dahil sa araw-araw na pag-eehersisyo.","translation":"His body became **well-built** because of daily exercise."}]

meaning_filipino: (Kolokyal) Ang kalagayan o gawain na nagdudulot ng pinsala sa emosyonal o mental na kalusugan; pagiging nakakalason sa isang relasyon o kapaligiran.
etymology: Isang neolohismong Taglish. Mula sa Ingles na "toxic" + mga panlaping Tagalog na "ka-" at "-an", na lumilikha ng isang pangngalan para sa estado ng pagiging nakakalason.
original_explanation: This is the vibe in your office when everyone's backstabbing each other for a promotion. It's your Tita asking why you're still single at a family reunion. It's that "friend" who only messages you when they need something. Basically, any situation that makes you want to "i-unfriend" or "i-block" someone in real life. Avoid at all costs for your mental health's sake.
usage_notes: Lubhang karaniwan sa moderno, lalo na sa mga online, na pag-uusap ng mga Pilipino. Ito ay isang salitang Taglish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umalis na ako sa group chat na 'yun, grabe ang **ka-toxican**.","translation":"I already left that group chat, the **toxicity** was too much."},{"sentence":"Iwasan natin ang **ka-toxican** sa pamilya para sa mas masayang pagsasama.","translation":"Let's avoid **toxicity** in the family for a happier relationship."}]

translation: to postpone; to defer; to omit
meaning_filipino: Ipagpaliban o ipagpaubaya sa ibang araw ang isang gawain o pangyayari; huwag isama.
original_explanation: The official verb of 'procrastination'. 'Yung meeting na dapat today, i-move sa next week? Iniliban. 'Yung exam na hindi ka pa ready? Sana pwedeng iliban. It's the "mamaya na" or "bukas na lang" mindset turned into a formal action.
usage_notes: Can mean to postpone an event, or to skip/omit someone/something from a list.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa masamang panahon, napagpasyahang **iliban** ang sports festival.","translation":"Due to the bad weather, it was decided to **postpone** the sports festival."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating **iliban** si Ana sa listahan ng mga inimbitahan.","translation":"Let's not **omit** Ana from the list of invitees."}]

translation: on time, just in time, punctual
meaning_filipino: Pagdating o paggawa ng isang bagay sa takdang oras; hindi nahuhuli at hindi rin masyadong maaga.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of "Filipino time." It's that rare, beautiful moment when your friend actually shows up at the agreed-upon 7 PM, not 7:30 PM. In the BPO world, this is non-negotiable. Being 'husto sa oras' for your shift is life.
usage_notes: A phrase emphasizing punctuality. A combination of 'husto' (exact) and 'oras' (time).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating siya nang **husto sa oras** para sa aming pulong.","translation":"He arrived **just in time** for our meeting."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong maging **husto sa oras** kung ayaw mong maiwan ng bus.","translation":"You need to be **on time** if you don't want to be left by the bus."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matibay na tela na karaniwang yari sa lino, bulak, o abaka, na ginagamit sa pagpipinta, paggawa ng layag, tolda, sapatos, at iba pang mga bagay.
original_explanation: That blank slate for your artistic ambitions, whether you're the next Fernando Amorsolo or just doing a paint-by-numbers kit. It's also the material of your favorite Converse or Vans sneakers and the 'trapal' that provides shade in the market.
usage_notes: Can refer to the artist's canvas or the material in general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinuhos ng pintor ang lahat ng kanyang damdamin sa puting **kanbas**.","translation":"The painter poured all his emotions onto the white **canvas**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging palibut-libot o palakad-lakad nang walang malinaw na layunin o direksyon. Ito ay nagpapahiwatig ng mas madalas o mas matagal na paggala kaysa sa 'pagala'.
original_explanation: This is the upgraded version of 'pagala'. It's you, after a major life crisis, walking around Luneta at 2 AM questioning your existence. It's that cat that visits your backyard, then your neighbor's, then the street corner, like it's on a grand, pointless tour. It's the official status of someone who is 'job-hunting' but is really just going to different coffee shops every day.
usage_notes: The reduplication of 'gala' intensifies the meaning, emphasizing the aimlessness and continuous nature of the wandering. Can function as both an adjective describing a noun or an adverb describing a verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko siyang **pagala-gala** sa mall na parang may malalim na iniisip.","translation":"I saw him **wandering aimlessly** in the mall as if he was deep in thought."},{"sentence":"Ang mga pusang **pagala-gala** ay madalas humihingi ng pagkain sa mga residente.","translation":"The **roaming** cats often ask for food from the residents."}]

translation: to roast; to heat over fire
meaning_filipino: Ang pagluto o pagpainit ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paglalantad nito sa init ng apoy o baga nang walang mantika o ihawan.
original_explanation: Before air fryers, there was salangin. It's the act of putting something (like fish, corn, or hotdogs on a stick) directly over embers or a small flame. Think beach barbecue or what you do to a marshmallow before it catches fire. It's the OG, smokey way of cooking.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'ihaw' (to grill), but 'salang' implies a more direct, simpler heating process, sometimes without a grill grate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap **salangin** ang mais at pahiran ng mantikilya.","translation":"It's delicious **to roast** corn and brush it with butter."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipag-utos sa iba na patayin ang isang tao o hayop.
original_explanation: The ultimate villain verb. This is what the kontrabida in the teleserye whispers to their henchman about the bida. It's not just 'to kill' (pumatay), it's 'to order a killing'. On a less dramatic note, it's also used for pests: 'Ipamatay mo na sa hardinero 'yang mga daga.' (Have the gardener kill those rats).
usage_notes: A causative verb indicating that the subject of the sentence is ordering or causing the act of killing, not performing it themselves.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-utos ang reyna na **ipamatay** ang lahat ng kanyang kaaway.","translation":"The queen ordered **to have** all her enemies **killed**."},{"sentence":"Gusto na niyang **ipamatay** ang manok para sa kanilang hapunan.","translation":"He wants **to have** the chicken **killed** for their dinner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking halamang may makahoy na katawan (puno) at mga sanga.
original_explanation: Ang OG provider ng shade, oxygen, at WiFi para sa mga ibon. Dito ka umaakyat 'pag bata ka, sumisilong 'pag umuulan, at pinagkukunan ng mangga. Sa panahon ng social media, sila rin ang background sa mga #NatureLover posts mo.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary term for 'puno' (tree).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakataas ng **punungkahoy** ng niyog sa aming bakuran.","translation":"The coconut **tree** in our yard is very tall."},{"sentence":"Bawal pumutol ng **punungkahoy** nang walang pahintulot.","translation":"It is forbidden to cut down a **tree** without permission."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar na maluwag, mahangin, at walang sagabal sa paningin; o sa isang isipan na payapa at walang alalahanin.
original_explanation: That feeling when you finally finish cleaning your room, or when your inbox is finally at zero. It's the opposite of 'siksikan sa MRT.' A liwalas space gives you room to breathe. A liwalas mind is when you've finally moved on from your ex and blocked them on all platforms. #SanaAll
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin para ilarawan ang panahon (maaliwalas na panahon) o ang kalooban (maaliwalas na pag-iisip). Ang 'maaliwalas' ay ang mas karaniwang anyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasarap manirahan sa bahay na may **liwalas** na sala.","translation":"It's so nice to live in a house with a **spacious** living room."},{"sentence":"Matapos ang mahabang bakasyon, naging **liwalas** ang kanyang pag-iisip.","translation":"After a long vacation, her mind became **clear**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nagbabalik sa isipan ng isang nakaraang pangyayari, tao, o lugar; ang kakayahan ng isip na mag-imbak at bumawi ng impormasyon.
etymology: Reduplication of 'ala'. Possibly related to a Proto-Malayo-Polynesian root meaning 'to be aware' or 'to remember'.
original_explanation: 'Yung bagay na iniwan sa'yo ng ex mo na hindi mo na alam kung itatapon mo o itatago. Can also be the good times you keep replaying in your head when you're stuck in traffic. 'Sana alaala na lang kita.' #hugot
usage_notes: Can mean both the mental concept of a memory and a physical object that serves as a memento (souvenir).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang litratong ito ay isang magandang **alaala** ng ating kabataan.","translation":"This picture is a beautiful **remembrance** of our youth."},{"sentence":"May mga **alaala** na masarap balikan, at mayroon ding masakit.","translation":"There are **memories** that are pleasant to look back on, and there are also painful ones."}]

translation: herd of horses, stable, stud farm
meaning_filipino: Isang grupo o kawan ng mga kabayo; maaari ding tumukoy sa lugar kung saan inaalagaan at pinalalahian ang mga kabayo.
etymology: From kabayo + -han, where the suffix '-han' denotes a collective group or a place associated with the root word.
original_explanation: Think of a hacienda in a teleserye. The rich guy always owns a 'kabayuhan'. It’s the collective noun for a squad of horses, or the place where they hang out—like a stable, but sounds way more majestic.
usage_notes: The suffix '-han' denotes a collective group or a place associated with the root word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ang mga turista sa **kabayuhan** ng asyenda.","translation":"The tourists were brought to the hacienda's **stables/stud farm**."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking **kabayuhan** ang makikita sa malawak na parang.","translation":"A large **herd of horses** can be seen on the vast field."}]

translation: the act of calming someone down; appeasement
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kilos ng pagpapakalma sa isang taong galit, balisa, o labis na nag-aalala.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + -pa- (reduplication of first syllable of the root) + hinahon (calmness).
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend is having a breakdown over a failed exam or a breakup. It's the 'Hinga, beshie' moment. It involves a lot of listening, patting on the back, and maybe offering milk tea or sisig. It's the art of de-escalation, turning a fiery 'Gigil mo si ako!' into a calmer 'Hay, nako.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan niya ng **pagpapahinahon** matapos marinig ang masamang balita.","translation":"He needs **calming down** after hearing the bad news."},{"sentence":"Mahusay ang nanay sa **pagpapahinahon** ng umiiyak na sanggol.","translation":"The mother is good at the **act of calming down** a crying baby."}]

meaning_filipino: Matatamo o makukuha sa hinaharap, karaniwang sa pamamagitan ng pagsisikap.
original_explanation: This is the formal, almost poetic, word your lola uses for your life goals. While you say 'Sana makuha ko yung promotion,' she'll say 'Sa tulong ng Diyos, makakamtan mo ang iyong mga pangarap.' It’s 'getting it' but with a sprinkle of destiny and hard work.
usage_notes: A more formal and profound word than `makukuha`. Often used for abstract goals like success, peace, or justice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng sipag at tiyaga, **makakamtan** mo ang tagumpay.","translation":"Through hard work and perseverance, you **will be able to achieve** success."},{"sentence":"Ang hustisyang matagal na nilang inaasam ay malapit nang **makamtan**.","translation":"The justice they have long been hoping for **will soon be obtained**."}]

translation: to bewitch, to cast a love spell
meaning_filipino: Paggamit ng gayuma o salamangka upang paibigin o akitin ang isang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sana all' move from before dating apps existed. When your crush won't notice you, you resort to... *alternative* methods. It's the magical equivalent of sliding into someone's DMs, but with more herbs and chanting. "Bes, na-manggayuma ata ako, 'di ko siya maalis sa isip ko!"
usage_notes: Often used hyperbolically to describe intense infatuation, but also refers to the literal practice in Philippine folklore.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga kwentong bayan, may mga mangkukulam na kayang **manggayuma**.","translation":"In folktales, there are witches who can **cast love spells**."},{"sentence":"Para siyang nabighani, tila na-**manggayuma** sa ganda ng dalaga.","translation":"He seemed captivated, as if **bewitched** by the lady's beauty."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakatanggal o pagkawala sa tamang puwesto ng isang buto sa kasukasuan.
original_explanation: Ito yung nangyari sa'yo nung nag-feeling athlete ka sa sportsfest niyo pero 'di ka naman nag-warm up. The classic "wrong landing" injury. A trip to the manghihilot or the ER usually follows.
usage_notes: Refers to joint dislocation or a severe sprain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nalinsad** ang balikat ng manlalaro ng basketball.","translation":"The basketball player's shoulder **was dislocated**."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa paglalakad diyan at baka ka madulas at **malinsad**.","translation":"Be careful walking there, you might slip and get a **sprain**."}]

meaning_filipino: Labis na nagagalak, nasisiyahan, o nahuhumaling sa isang bagay, tao, o gawain.
original_explanation: This is when you're so into something, it's almost an addiction. Like how your tita is wiling-wili sa K-drama, she forgets to cook dinner. Or how you're wiling-wili sa ka-chat mo, you forget you have a 9 AM meeting tomorrow. It's peak enthusiasm, bordering on obsession.
usage_notes: The reduplication of 'wili' intensifies the meaning to 'very' or 'extremely' fond.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Wiling-wili** ang mga bata sa bagong video game.","translation":"The children are **extremely pleased** with the new video game."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **wiling-wili** sa pag-aalaga ng kanyang mga halaman.","translation":"She is **very fond** of taking care of her plants."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging nakahihigit sa iba sa ranggo, kapangyarihan, kalidad, o kahalagahan.
