original_explanation: That feeling when you have the complete set of a K-Pop group's photocards and your friend doesn't. It's the "I'm better than you" vibe, sometimes seen in office politics or family reunions when comparing life achievements. The opposite of being humble.
usage_notes: Used in formal or literary contexts to discuss concepts of power, quality, or social standing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita ng manlalaro ang kanyang **superyoridad** sa chess.","translation":"The player showed his **superiority** in chess."},{"sentence":"Hindi dapat magkaroon ng **superyoridad** ang isang lahi sa iba.","translation":"One race should not have **superiority** over another."}]

translation: to gather; to assemble; to save up
meaning_filipino: Magsama-sama sa isang lugar; o mangolekta o mag-ipon ng mga bagay o salapi.
original_explanation: "Magtitipon" is what your family does for Noche Buena, what your barkada does for an inuman session, or what you do with your salary to finally buy that PS5. It can be about gathering people (reunion!) or gathering things/money (ipon!). It's all about bringing things together in one place.
usage_notes: Can refer to people assembling or to someone saving/collecting items or money.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtitipon** ang buong angkan para sa Pasko.","translation":"The whole clan will **gather** for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magtipon** ng pera para sa aking pag-aaral.","translation":"I need to **save up** money for my studies."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahapding pakiramdam sa dibdib o lalamunan na sanhi ng pag-akyat ng asido mula sa sikmura.
original_explanation: That feeling when you binge on samgyupsal and spicy noodles at 2 AM. It's your esophagus sending you a fiery "I hate you" message. Parang may mini-volcano na pumuputok sa dibdib mo. The official feeling of "sin-gastric."
usage_notes: A medical or physical sensation. A somewhat formal or literary term; 'heartburn' or 'acidic' are more common in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inatake na naman ako ng **alimpuso** dahil sa dami ng kinain kong maanghang.","translation":"I'm having a **heartburn** attack again because of all the spicy food I ate."},{"sentence":"Uminom ka ng gamot para sa **alimpuso** mo.","translation":"Take medicine for your **acid indigestion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakauna sa lahat sa isang pagkakasunod-sunod, na walang sinuman o anuman ang nauna pa; nagbibigay-diin sa pagiging una.
etymology: Isang pormang nagbibigay-diin sa pamamagitan ng pag-uulit ng salitang 'una' kasama ang mga panlaping 'ka-' at '-han'.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'first.' Not just 'una,' but THE very first. Your first love, the first man on the moon, the first Jollibee in Europe. It's the OG, the pioneer, the one that started it all. 'Siya ang kauna-unahan kong 'The One That Got Away'.'
usage_notes: Used to emphasize primacy and historical significance. It refers to the first in a chronological or sequential order.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ito ang **kauna-unahan** niyang pelikula.","translation":"This is his **very first** movie."},{"sentence":"Ang Luneta Hotel ang isa sa mga **kauna-unahan** at natitirang istraktura ng French Renaissance architecture sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The Luneta Hotel is one of the **first-ever** and remaining structures of French Renaissance architecture in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at marangyang pagdiriwang o pista, karaniwang may kasamang kainan at kasayahan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "raya" (na nangangahulugang 'malaki' o 'dakila' sa ilang wika sa Pilipinas, at may kaugnayan sa Malay na 'raya' na nangangahulugang 'great' o 'grand').
original_explanation: Imagine the biggest, grandest fiesta you've ever been to. Lechon everywhere, non-stop music, and everyone's invited. That’s a rayahan. It’s not just a party; it’s a full-blown spectacle. The kind of celebration where "extra" is the minimum requirement.
usage_notes: Madalas na nauugnay sa mga pagdiriwang na may kinalaman sa kultura o relihiyon, tulad ng Eid al-Fitr (Hari Raya). Ang salita ay hindi gaanong karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na Tagalog sa Maynila ngunit mas nauunawaan sa ilang rehiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **rayahan** ang inihanda para sa pagdating ng sultan.","translation":"A **grand celebration** was prepared for the sultan's arrival."},{"sentence":"Ang pista sa kanilang bayan ay isang tunay na **rayahan**.","translation":"The fiesta in their town is a true **festivity**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa panghalip na "ako" na ginagamit sa gay lingo o swardspeak.
etymology: Isang salitang balbal (gay lingo) na hinango sa salitang "Ako", posibleng may impluwensya mula sa tunog ng "aray" o bilang isang mapaglarong pagbabago lamang.
original_explanation: This is Beki for "Ako". Instead of saying "Ako na ang bahala," a beki might say, "**Aroy** na ang bahala, 'teh!" It's part of the colorful, ever-evolving world of swardspeak. Parang may pagka-reyna vibes, 'di ba? Use with flair and confidence.
usage_notes: Mahigpit na ginagamit sa impormal na usapan, partikular sa loob ng LGBTQ+ community at sa mga pamilyar sa gay lingo. Itinuturing na kolokyal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Aroy** ang nagbayad ng lahat, mga 'day!","translation":"**I** paid for everything, girls!"},{"sentence":"Sabi niya, '**Aroy** muna, bago ang iba.' Charot!","translation":"She said, '**Me** first, before others.' Just kidding!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyong lupa na nakausli sa tubig at napapaligiran ng tubig sa halos lahat ng panig nito maliban sa isang bahagi na karugtong ng mas malaking kalupaan.
original_explanation: A piece of land that's being extra, sticking itself out into the water. It's the land equivalent of that one person in a group photo who leans way out to be in the frame. The Bataan Peninsula ('Lawis ng Bataan') is a famous example.
usage_notes: A geographical term. 'Tangway' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Lawis** ng Bataan ay isang makasaysayang pook sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The Bataan **Peninsula** is a historical place in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng pamaypay o anumang bagay upang lumikha ng daloy ng hangin para sa sarili.
original_explanation: The human-powered aircon during a brownout or inside a non-airconditioned jeepney. It's an art form, from the subtle wrist-flick of a kolehiyala to the furious flapping of a tita sa palengke. The official gesture for "Ang init!"
usage_notes: Can also mean to fan someone else (`paypayan`). `Magpaypay` is reflexive (fanning oneself).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **magpaypay** gamit ang kanyang notbuk dahil sa init sa loob ng silid-aralan.","translation":"She started to **fan herself** using her notebook because of the heat inside the classroom."},{"sentence":"Kahit may aircon, mahilig pa ring **magpaypay** si Lola.","translation":"Even with an aircon, Grandma still likes to **fan herself**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na tawag o pamagat para sa isang babae, lalo na sa isang may katungkulan, guro, o nakatatanda. Pinaikling anyo ng 'madam'.
original_explanation: The default honorific for your female boss, a teacher, a government employee, or the lady at the customer service counter you're trying to win over. Use it generously. 'Yes, Mam! Thank you, Mam!'
usage_notes: Often spelled as 'Ma'am' in formal writing, but 'Mam' is common in casual Filipino text and speech. Always used with respect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mam**, tapos na po ang report na pinapagawa ninyo.","translation":"**Ma'am**, the report you asked for is finished."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, sitwasyon, o pahayag na nagdudulot ng katuwaan, pagtawa, o libangan.
etymology: From `ka-` + (reduplicated `tawa`) + `-an`, signifying a source or place of laughter.
original_explanation: The reason why Vice Ganda and Michael V are national treasures. It's the meme you saved, the stand-up special you're watching on Netflix, or your tito's corny joke during the family reunion. Anything that makes you go "HAHAHA" instead of "hay nako."
usage_notes: Can refer to a joke, a funny situation, or the genre of comedy itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **katatawanan** ang palabas na aming pinanood.","translation":"The show we watched was full of **comedy**."},{"sentence":"Naging **katatawanan** sa opisina ang kanyang maling na-send na message.","translation":"His wrongly sent message became a **joke** at the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatalaga o paghirang sa isang tao sa isang partikular na posisyon, tungkulin, o karangalan.
original_explanation: This is the action of making someone 'nombrado'. It’s the moment your boss points at you and says, 'Ikaw ang bagong team lead,'—that’s being 'ninombrahan'. It’s a very corporate or government-sounding word. Think of it as the verb for getting a promotion or a special project, complete with a formal announcement.
usage_notes: This is the verb form. The object of the verb is the person being appointed. The root 'nombra' comes from Spanish for 'name'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano ng pangulo na **nombrahan** ang isang tapat na kaalyado sa gabinete.","translation":"The president plans **to appoint** a loyal ally to the cabinet."},{"sentence":"Sino ang dapat nating **nombrahan** bilang kinatawan ng klase?","translation":"Who should we **name** as the class representative?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa o may katangian ng isang Mesiyas o isang tagapagligtas.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol 'mesiánico', na mula sa 'Mesías'.
original_explanation: Parang yung kaibigan mong laging may 'savior complex,' akala mo siya ang sugo ng langit para ayusin ang lovelife mo. 'Girl, I have a Mesyanik plan to get you and your crush together!'
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa kontekstong panrelihiyon o sa makabagong pananalita upang ilarawan ang isang taong may labis na paniniwala sa sarili bilang tagapagligtas. Ang 'Mesianik' ay isang varyant sa pagbaybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga kilos ay may **Mesyanik** na kalikasan, na para bang siya ang itinakdang magligtas sa lahat.","translation":"His actions have a **messianic** quality, as if he were destined to save everyone."},{"sentence":"Pinuna ng mga kritiko ang **Mesyanik** na tono sa kanyang mga talumpati.","translation":"Critics pointed out the **messianic** tone in his speeches."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tore o mataas na istruktura na may malakas na ilaw sa tuktok, na nagsisilbing gabay sa mga barko sa dagat, lalo na sa gabi o sa masamang panahon.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'farola' (lantern, street light, lighthouse).
original_explanation: Yung 'strong, silent type' na tore sa tabi ng dagat. Hindi man nagsasalita, pero 'yung ilaw niya, sign na 'Dito ang daan, 'wag kang maligaw, bes.' Parang 'yung kaibigan mong laging nandiyan para i-guide ka 'pag lost ka na sa buhay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matatanaw ang luma at magandang **parola** mula sa dalampasigan.","translation":"The old and beautiful **lighthouse** can be seen from the shore."},{"sentence":"Ang ilaw ng **parola** ang naging gabay ng mga mangingisda pauwi.","translation":"The light of the **lighthouse** guided the fishermen home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim sa Ingles na "down to f*ck," na nangangahulugang handa o bukas sa pakikipagtalik.
original_explanation: An acronym borrowed from Western internet/dating app culture. It means "Down To F*ck." It's a very direct, no-nonsense way of saying you're looking for a sexual encounter. You'll see this on Tinder or Grindr profiles. Definitely not something you'd say to your lola.
usage_notes: Explicit slang. Used in digital communication and dating apps.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalagay sa profile niya na **DTF** daw siya.","translation":"It says on his profile that he's supposedly **DTF**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagbabago o pag-aaltera ng isang dokumento, ulat, o anumang talaan upang manlinlang o magtago ng katotohanan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'doktor' + hulaping '-in', na hango sa Ingles na 'to doctor' (to tamper).
original_explanation: What you do to your parent's signature on a permission slip, or what politicians do to official receipts. It's the art of "creative editing" for personal gain. The OG "fake news" on a personal level.
usage_notes: This is a colloquial usage derived from the English phrase "to doctor a document". It is not a formal medical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **doktorin** ang resibo para lumaki ang iyong reimbursement.","translation":"Don't **falsify** the receipt to increase your reimbursement."},{"sentence":"Pinaghihinalaang dinoktor ang ebidensya laban sa akusado.","translation":"The evidence against the accused was suspected to have been **doctored**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hungkag, walang laman, o kawalan ng kabuluhan at layunin.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling pagkatapos mong mag-marathon ng K-drama series for 12 hours straight. Pag-on mo ng ilaw, a-alas tres na ng umaga, may pasok ka pa, at narealize mo ang **emptiness** ng buhay mo. Also, the state of your wallet after the 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: Used to describe both physical emptiness (like a hollow space) and emotional/existential emptiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang matinding **kahungkagan** matapos siyang iwan.","translation":"He/She felt a deep **emptiness** after being left."},{"sentence":"Ang **kahungkagan** ng dibdib ng estatwa ay sinadyang disenyo.","translation":"The **hollowness** of the statue's chest was an intentional design."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o instrumento na ginagamit upang buksan ang isang bagay na selyado o nakasara, tulad ng lata, bote, o pinto.
original_explanation: The MVP of any inuman session. It's the tool you frantically search for when you have a cold bottle of beer but no way to open it. Can also be your teeth, if you're brave (and unwise). Also applies to can openers for your precious hoard of tuna.
usage_notes: Often specified further, e.g., `pambukas ng lata` (can opener), `pambukas ng bote` (bottle opener).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **pambukas** ng de-lata.","translation":"The can **opener** is missing."},{"sentence":"Pahiram ng **pambukas** ng bote, pare.","translation":"Friend, can I borrow the bottle **opener**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Maayos, makinis, at malinis ang pagkakagawa; walang bahid ng pagkakamali o gaspang.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'pwede na 'yan.' This is the goal for your thesis, your presentation for the boss, or your makeup look for a first date. It's when every detail is perfect, clean, and flawlessly executed. It's that satisfying feeling of a job done right.
usage_notes: Can be used to describe a physical object, a piece of work (like writing or a project), or even a person's movements or actions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pulido** ang pagkakagawa ng mga sapatos na galing Marikina.","translation":"The craftsmanship of shoes from Marikina is **well-finished**."},{"sentence":"Gusto ng kliyente na maging **pulido** ang bawat detalye ng proyekto.","translation":"The client wants every detail of the project to be **polished**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang halaga o bagay na ibinibigay bilang kapalit ng isang produkto, serbisyo, o pagkakautang.
etymology: From ka- + bayad + -an, referring to the collective or total 'bayad' (payment).
original_explanation: The 'resibo' for your life choices. Whether it's paying for your Shopee 'add to cart' spree or the karma you get for ghosting someone, lahat 'yan may kabayaran. It's the reason you work—to get that sweet, sweet 'kabayaran' on the 15th and 30th.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal payment (money) or figurative compensation (consequences).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **kabayaran** para sa lahat ng inorder ko?","translation":"What is the **payment** for everything I ordered?"},{"sentence":"Ang kapaguran niya ay nagkaroon ng sapat na **kabayaran** nang manalo siya sa kompetisyon.","translation":"His fatigue was sufficiently **compensated** when he won the competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay ng utos, direksyon, o pamumuno sa isang grupo o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Channeling your inner general, team lead, or even that one friend who decides where everyone's eating for lunch. It’s when you take charge and tell people, "Okay, ganito ang gagawin natin."
usage_notes: Often used in military, police, or formal leadership contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang heneral ang **kumumando** sa buong batalyon.","translation":"The general **commanded** the entire battalion."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **kumumando** na itigil ang produksyon?","translation":"Who **commanded** to stop the production?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang plano, gawain, o ideya na hindi posible o praktikal na isakatuparan o gawin.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (not), "ma-", "isa-", at "sagawa" (isang anyo ng 'gawâ', na nangangahulugang gawin).
original_explanation: 'Yung plano n'yo ng barkada na mag-La Union this weekend pero biglang may bagyo, wala pang sahod, at may pasok ka pa pala. 'Yung trip? Di-maisasagawa. Drawing lang. Not gonna happen.
usage_notes: Commonly used in planning, project management, and formal discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kakulangan ng pondo, ang proyekto ay **di-maisasagawa** sa ngayon.","translation":"Due to lack of funds, the project is **unfeasible** for now."},{"sentence":"Ang planong magtayo ng tulay gamit ang papel ay malinaw na **di-maisasagawa**.","translation":"The plan to build a bridge using paper is clearly **impracticable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Madalas o madaling mangako, na hindi palaging nangangahulugang natutupad ang mga ito.
original_explanation: This is your friend who says 'Libre kita next time!' but 'next time' never comes. Or that ex who promised 'I can change,' but didn't. Politicians during campaign season are the ultimate form of this. All talk, all promises, but the follow-through is perpetually 'pending'. #Paasa
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation, implying that the promises are empty, unreliable, or not kept.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa kanya, sadyang **mapagpangako** lang talaga ang taong iyon.","translation":"Don't believe him, that person is just **prone to making promises**."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang politiko bilang **mapagpangako** tuwing panahon ng eleksyon.","translation":"The politician is known for being **prone to making promises** during the election season."}]

meaning_filipino: May bahid o tigmak ng dugo.
original_explanation: Literally, "bloody." This is what your white shirt looks like after a failed attempt at opening a bottle of Datu Puti vinegar. Or your knee after tripping on a random sidewalk tile. "Hala, duguan ang daliri mo!"
usage_notes: Can be used literally (covered in blood) or figuratively (e.g., 'duguan laban' - a bloody conflict).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinakbo sa ospital ang **duguan** na biktima.","translation":"The **bloody** victim was rushed to the hospital."},{"sentence":"Nag-iwan ng **duguan** na bakas ang magnanakaw.","translation":"The thief left a **bloody** trail."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasuotan na isinusuot sa ibabaw ng iba pang damit, o anumang bagay na nagsisilbing panakip sa ibabaw.
original_explanation: Your jacket, coat, hoodie, or cardigan. It's the extra layer you grab when the office AC is on full blast or when you want to complete your fashion statement. In food, it's the sprinkles on your ice cream or the cheese on your pizza. Ang pang-ibabaw ang nagbibigay ng final touch!
usage_notes: Refers to a specific item used as a covering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan ko ang aking **pang-ibabaw** sa sinehan.","translation":"I left my **outerwear** at the cinema."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang keso bilang **pang-ibabaw** sa spaghetti.","translation":"Cheese is a delicious **topping** for spaghetti."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng walis na yari sa mga pinatuyong tangkay ng halamang tambo, karaniwang ginagamit sa loob ng bahay para sa makinis na sahig.
original_explanation: The OG indoor vacuum cleaner of the Philippines. Perfect for sweeping dust, pet hair, and all the 'feelings' you've been trying to ignore. Your lola's favorite weapon against both dirt and misbehaving apos.
usage_notes: "Tambo" refers to the Phragmites karka grass, whose flower stalks are used to make the broom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **walis na tambo** para malinis ang alikabok sa sahig.","translation":"Get a **soft broom** to clean the dust on the floor."},{"sentence":"Mas maganda ang **walis na tambo** sa sementadong sahig kaysa sa tingting.","translation":"A **soft broom** is better on a cemented floor than a stick broom."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nasa estado ng pagkasira o pagkaagnas, karaniwan dahil sa natural na proseso ng pagkabulok o pagguho.
original_explanation: Think of that fruit you forgot at the bottom of your bag for a week. 'Yun, agnas na. It's the state of something breaking down, like a forgotten friendship or an old building. It’s nature’s way of hitting the reset button, but for organic matter.
usage_notes: Often used in scientific, biological, or geological contexts, but can also be used metaphorically for relationships or structures.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita nila ang **agnas** na katawan ng isang hayop sa gubat.","translation":"They saw the **decomposed** body of an animal in the forest."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa matagal na pagkakababad sa tubig, **agnas** na ang pundasyon ng lumang bahay.","translation":"Because of long-term water exposure, the foundation of the old house is now **eroded**."}]

translation: more than words can say; beyond words
meaning_filipino: Isang pagpapahayag na hindi sapat ang mga salita upang ilarawan ang isang damdamin, karanasan, o katotohanan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your food finally arriving at the restaurant. Or when your crush messages you first. It's a feeling so intense, so pure, that "masaya" or "happy" just doesn't cut it. It's the "I love you 3000" of Tagalog expressions.
usage_notes: This phrase is more poetic or literary than colloquial. A more common way to express this is "hindi kayang ipaliwanag ng mga salita" (cannot be explained by words).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal ng isang ina ay **labis sa mga salita**.","translation":"A mother's love is **beyond words**."},{"sentence":"Ang pasasalamat ko sa iyo ay **labis sa mga salita**.","translation":"My gratitude for you is **more than words can say**."}]

translation: to show; to appear; to demonstrate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapamalas o paglalantad ng isang bagay upang makita ng iba; ang pagpunta o pagharap sa isang lugar o tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'show and tell' verb. It can mean 'to show' something, like magpakita ng new phone. It can mean 'to appear' or 'show up', like when your friend who's always late finally decides to magpakita at the party. It can also mean 'to demonstrate' an emotion, like magpakita ng gilas (show off skills) or magpakita ng motibo (show one's motive... very teleserye!).
usage_notes: A very versatile and common verb with multiple nuances depending on the object and context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magpakita** ka naman sa birthday ko, ha?","translation":"**Show up** at my birthday, okay?"},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **magpakita** ng kanyang bagong alagang aso sa lahat.","translation":"She wants to **show** her new pet dog to everyone."},{"sentence":"Dapat kang **magpakita** ng respeto sa mga nakatatanda.","translation":"You should **show** respect to elders."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na sagutin ang isang tanong, tawag, o sulat. Ibigay ang kasagutan.
original_explanation: This is what your teacher says before handing out a pop quiz: "**Pasagot** nitong 1 to 50." It's a request or command for someone to provide an answer. It's also what you say when you hand your phone to your friend because you don't want to talk to the person calling: "**Pasagot** mo nga, sabihin mo tulog ako."
usage_notes: Used as a polite command or request. It's the root form of the causative verb, often appearing in this form for requests.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasagot** naman ng tanong ko, kaibigan.","translation":"**Please answer** my question, my friend."},{"sentence":"Kung may tumawag, **pasagot** mo na lang sa sekretarya.","translation":"If someone calls, just **have the secretary answer** it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aaral sa mga katangiang pisikal ng daigdig, ang atmospera nito, at ang epekto ng aktibidad ng tao dito.
original_explanation: Your high school subject where you had to memorize all the capitals of the world, only to forget them and rely on Google Maps as an adult. It's the "why" behind why Baguio is cold and why traffic is bad in Metro Manila (spoiler: it's not just the cars).
usage_notes: The formal term is 'heograpiya', but 'giyograpi' is common in spoken language.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa klase ng **giyograpi**, pinag-aaralan namin ang iba't ibang anyong lupa at anyong tubig.","translation":"In **geography** class, we study the different landforms and bodies of water."},{"sentence":"Ang **giyograpi** ng Pilipinas bilang isang arkipelago ay nakaaapekto sa kultura at ekonomiya nito.","translation":"The **geography** of the Philippines as an archipelago affects its culture and economy."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pag-asenso, pagyaman, o pagbuti sa kalagayan, partikular sa ekonomiya, teknolohiya, o lipunan.
etymology: From 'unlad' (progress, development). The 'ma-' prefix denotes 'having the quality of'.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal for every country, company, and sometimes, your love life. Ito 'yung estado na hindi ka na "one day millionaire" after payday. For a country, it means good infrastructure, stable Wi-Fi, and fewer politicians making memes of themselves. For a person, it means you can afford the extra large milk tea without checking your bank account. #SanaAllMaunlad
usage_notes: Often used in the context of economics, societal progress, and national development.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap ng bawat Pilipino ang isang **maunlad** na bansa.","translation":"The dream of every Filipino is a **prosperous** country."},{"sentence":"Naging **maunlad** ang kanilang negosyo dahil sa kanilang sipag at tiyaga.","translation":"Their business became **prosperous** because of their hard work and perseverance."}]

translation: to burst into flames; to flare up
meaning_filipino: Biglaang pag-apoy o paglaki ng apoy; mag-alab nang malaki at matindi.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you pour gasoline on a fire, literally or figuratively. A small spark can 'magliyab' into a huge blaze. It's also used for emotions. Yung 'slight' inis mo sa ka-team mo na ayaw mag-contribute, tapos bigla siyang nag-file ng leave sa peak ng project? That's when your anger will 'magliyab'. From zero to one hundred, real quick.
usage_notes: Used for literal fires and figuratively for intense emotions like anger or passion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula sa isang kandila ang sunog na **nagliyab** sa buong gusali.","translation":"The fire that **burst into flames** throughout the whole building started from a single candle."},{"sentence":"**Nagliyab** sa galit ang kanyang mga mata nang marinig ang balita.","translation":"His eyes **flared up** in anger when he heard the news."}]

translation: to have; to possess; to exist
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o pagtataglay ng isang bagay, katangian, o karanasan; ang pag-iral ng isang bagay.
etymology: From 'magka-' (to have/acquire) + 'doon' (there), evolving into 'karoon' as the base form for having/existence.
original_explanation: The ultimate wish ng mga single, "Sana **magkaroon** na ako ng jowa." Also what your tita asks you at family reunions about your sahod, "May ipon ka na ba?" It's the state of having or acquiring something, from a new phone to a new problem.
usage_notes: Often used to express possession, the existence of something, or the occurrence of an event. 'Mayroon' is a common alternative for expressing existence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **magkaroon** tayo ng pagkakataong maglakbay sa susunod na taon.","translation":"I hope we **get** a chance to travel next year."},{"sentence":"Nag-aaral siyang mabuti upang **magkaroon** ng magandang kinabukasan.","translation":"He is studying hard in order **to have** a good future."}]

translation: let me see; may I see
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na pahintulutang makita, masilip, o masuri ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The official word of every chismosa/chismoso everywhere. When your friend gets a text and smiles, "**Patingin**!" When someone is looking at Shopee sales, "**Patingin** nga!" It's the polite (or not-so-polite) way of saying 'lemme see that' and inserting yourself into the situation.
usage_notes: Often used as a standalone command or request. It's a very common phrase in daily interactions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patingin** nga ng hawak mong 'yan, mukhang masarap.","translation":"**Let me see** what you're holding, it looks delicious."},{"sentence":"Maaari bang **patingin** ng iyong resibo?","translation":"May I please **see** your receipt?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng labis na puwersa, karahasan, o kalupitan laban sa isang tao o bagay, lalo na sa konteksto ng sekswal na pananakit.
original_explanation: This is a heavy, serious word. It's not just simple violence; it's brutal, forceful, and often has sexual undertones (from the root 'gahasa' - rape). Think of action movie fight scenes that are too realistic, or the grim realities of crime reports. It's the raw, ugly, and violating use of force. No humor here.
usage_notes: Kagahasaan is a stronger and more formal term than 'karahasan' (violence). It often implies a violation or sexual assault.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pelikula ay binatikos dahil sa labis na **kagahasaan** na ipinakita nito.","translation":"The movie was criticized for the excessive **violence** it showed."},{"sentence":"Biktima siya ng **kagahasaan** at ngayon ay naghahanap ng hustisya.","translation":"She was a victim of **brutality** and is now seeking justice."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng dalawa o higit pang tao na paulit-ulit na nagsasampalan o nagpapalitan ng sampal.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + sa- (repetition/reciprocal action) + sampal (slap) + -an (location/reciprocal action marker).
original_explanation: The iconic scene in every Pinoy teleserye. You know, the one with dramatic music, a zoom-in on the face, and a slap so loud you can hear it from the next barangay. It’s a mutual exchange of high-fives... to the face. Not recommended for conflict resolution in real life, unless you want to go viral for the wrong reasons.
usage_notes: Implies a reciprocal or mutual action, unlike 'pananampal' which can be one-sided.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nauwi sa **pagsasampalan** ang mainit na pagtatalo ng mag-asawa.","translation":"The couple's heated argument ended in them **slapping each other**."},{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat nang magsimula ang **pagsasampalan** ng dalawang aktres sa gitna ng taping.","translation":"Everyone was shocked when the two actresses started a **slapping match** in the middle of the taping."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng pagsang-ayon o pagsuporta sa isang naunang sinabi, gawa, o ideya.
etymology: Taglish slang phrase combining English 'supportive' and 'yarn', a playful corruption of 'iyan' (that).
original_explanation: "Slay! Go bestie! We love that for you!" - basically the Pinoy internet version of saying "I agree and support that idea/person." It's what you type in the comments when your friend posts a selfie after a breakup. "Yarn" is a playful corruption of "iyan" (that).
usage_notes: Primarily used in online conversations, social media comments, and informal chats among younger generations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-post siya ng new look niya. **Supportive yarn** tayo diyan!","translation":"She posted her new look. We're **supportive of that**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang posisyon o ranggo ng isang tao o grupo na nasa pinakahulihan sa isang kompetisyon, karera, o anumang uri ng paligsahan.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'champion.' The 'sana all' when everyone else is getting a medal. If a group project had a ranking, the kulalat is the one who contributed the least. In a race, it's the person you see still running when the winners are already doing interviews. 'Okay lang maging kulalat, at least tinapos ang laban!'—a classic line to console yourself.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ('ang kulalat') or an adjective ('siya ay kulalat'). It carries a slightly informal and sometimes teasing tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kasamaang palad, ang aming koponan ang naging **kulalat** sa paligsahan.","translation":"Unfortunately, our team ended up in **last place** in the competition."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang maging **kulalat** sa klase kaya nag-aaral siya nang mabuti.","translation":"He doesn't want to be the **tail-ender** in class, so he studies hard."}]

translation: to plate with gold; to value as gold
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng ginto o balutan ng ginto. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay ang pagpapahalaga nang lubos sa isang bagay na parang ginto.
original_explanation: The act of making something look expensive by covering it in gold. Or, more poetically, it's when you treat something or someone as precious as gold. Like how you 'gintuin' your last piece of Choc-Nut or that one friend who always has your back. It's about assigning immense value.
usage_notes: A verb formed from 'ginto' (gold). The command form is 'gintuin mo' (plate it with gold/value it as gold).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinag-utos ng hari na **gintuin** ang kanyang trono.","translation":"The king ordered to **plate his throne with gold**."},{"sentence":"Dapat mong **gintuin** ang bawat payo na galing sa iyong mga magulang.","translation":"You should **value as gold** every piece of advice from your parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o kagamitan na ginagamit sa paggawa ng isang bagay, lalo na sa mga gawaing nangangailangan ng katumpakan, tulad ng sa musika, agham, o medisina.
original_explanation: Pwedeng gitara, piano, o drums. Pwede ring scalpel ng doktor o beaker ng scientist. Minsan, ito rin 'yung tawag mo sa kaibigan mong ginamit lang para mapalapit ka sa crush mo. Ouch.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa instrumentong pang-musika, isang kasangkapan, o isang paraan upang makamit ang isang layunin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong siyang tumugtog ng iba't ibang **instrumento**ng pangmusika.","translation":"He knows how to play various musical **instrument**s."},{"sentence":"Ang wika ay isang mahalagang **instrumento** sa komunikasyon.","translation":"Language is an important **instrument** in communication."}]

meaning_filipino: Binahagi o ipinamahagi sa limitadong sukat o dami; nirasyon.
etymology: Taglish, from the prefix na- (indicating passive voice, past tense) + English word 'ratio'. The more traditional Tagalog word is 'nirasyon'.
original_explanation: This is a very corporate or BPO term. When your boss says the budget for the team outing was 'naratio', it means you're getting a small bag of chips instead of a buffet. It's the polite way of saying 'your request has been denied due to budget constraints' or 'hinati-hati na, 'wag ka nang umangal.'
usage_notes: Primarily used in business or office settings. A clear example of code-switching becoming a standard term in certain environments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naratio** na ang mga bonus kaya huwag umasa nang malaki.","translation":"The bonuses **were rationed** so don't expect too much."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kakulangan, **naratio** ang paggamit ng kumpanya sa kuryente.","translation":"Due to the shortage, the company's electricity use **was rationed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isa sa apat na pangunahing direksyon, ang dako kung saan sumisikat ang araw.
original_explanation: The direction you face when you're trying to get that perfect sunrise selfie for your IG story. It's the opposite of 'kanluran' (west), where the sun goes to sleep, probably tired from all the drama it witnessed during the day.
usage_notes: Often used in geography, navigation, and giving directions. It is one of the four cardinal directions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumisikat ang araw sa **silangan**.","translation":"The sun rises in the **east**."},{"sentence":"Nakatira sila sa bandang **silangan** ng Maynila.","translation":"They live in the **eastern** part of Manila."}]

translation: to peck; to rap or knock lightly
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpukpok o pagkatok nang marahan at paulit-ulit, karaniwan ay gamit ang daliri, o ang pagtuka ng ibon gamit ang tuka nito.
original_explanation: Two meanings! 1) What a chicken does to its food. Like you with a bowl of peanuts or sunflower seeds, picking at them one by one. 2) A light knock on the door, not the kind that sounds like a debt collector. More like a 'Tao po, pwedeng maki-charge?' kind of knock.
usage_notes: Can refer to a bird pecking ('tuka') or a person knocking lightly ('katok'). The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **tuktukin** ng manok ang mga palay.","translation":"Don't let the chicken **peck** at the rice grains."},{"sentence":"May **tumutuktok** sa bintana.","translation":"Someone is **rapping lightly** on the window."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na pagpapaikli ng pariralang "ika ko" o "ang sabi ko".
original_explanation: The Tagalog version of "I said what I said." It's what you say right after dropping a truth bomb or a savage comment in the group chat. It's the mic drop after you've made your point. "Sabi nang 'wag, eh. Ikako," your nanay says, holding a slipper.
usage_notes: Highly colloquial and used in spoken language. It emphasizes that the speaker is repeating or confirming what they previously said.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, **ikako**.","translation":"Be careful, **I said**."},{"sentence":"\"Ang ganda niya,\" **ikako** sa sarili.","translation":"\"She's beautiful,\" **I said** to myself."}]

translation: to make the same; to make identical
meaning_filipino: Gawing magkatulad o magkamukha ang dalawa o higit pang bagay.
etymology: From 'i-' (causative prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'pareho' (same, alike), from Spanish 'parejo'.
original_explanation: When you show a picture to your barber and say, "Boss, ganito," this is what you're asking them to do. It's the act of making something identical to another. "Pakisuyo, **ipareho** mo ang kulay ng pintura sa pader." Also what you do when you copy your classmate's homework, but you change it a bit para 'di halata.
usage_notes: Similar to 'ipantay' but emphasizes sameness in appearance or quality rather than just level or position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan kong **ipareho** ang luto ko sa luto ni nanay, pero iba pa rin.","translation":"I'm trying **to make** my cooking **the same** as my mom's, but it's still different."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta sa isang mas mababang lugar o posisyon; pagbawas sa halaga, antas, o tindi; nasa anyong pangnagdaan.
original_explanation: What you did when the jeepney driver yelled 'Para!'. Also what happened to your bank account after the 12.12 sale. It means to go down, get off, or decrease.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical descent, or a decrease in value, price, or intensity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumaba** siya mula sa ikalawang palapag.","translation":"He/She **went down** from the second floor."},{"sentence":"**Bumaba** ang presyo ng sibuyas ngayong linggo.","translation":"The price of onions **decreased** this week."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-inom o pag-ubos sa isang likido, karaniwan ay sabaw, sa pamamagitan ng pagsipsip.
original_explanation: If 'higop' is the sound, 'higupin' is the command. 'Higupin mo ang sabaw!' (Slurp the soup!). This is what your nanay tells you when you're sick and she gives you hot tinola. It focuses on the liquid itself being consumed. It's the 'finish the soup' verb.
usage_notes: The focus of this verb is the liquid being sipped. Contrast with 'higupan', which focuses on the container.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sarap **higupin** ng mainit na sabaw kapag umuulan.","translation":"It's so good **to sip** hot soup when it's raining."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **higupin** lahat, tirhan mo naman ako!","translation":"Don't **slurp** it all, leave some for me!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa hinaharap na pagkakaroon ng magandang ugnayan, pag-unawaan, o pagiging magkasundo ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
etymology: From mag- (verb-forming prefix) + -ki- (future tense infix) + click (English loanword).
original_explanation: This is the future tense of finding your new bestie or work-wife. It’s that feeling when you first meet someone and you just *know* na "uy, magkakasundo kami nito." It's the opposite of awkward silence; it's instant chemistry, whether for friendship, a work project, or even romance.
usage_notes: Used to predict compatibility between people. The root verb is "mag-click". "Magki-click" is the future tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa tingin ko, **magki-click** kayo ni Anna dahil pareho kayong mahilig sa K-Pop.","translation":"I think you and Anna **will click** because you both love K-Pop."},{"sentence":"Sana **magki-click** ang mga bagong miyembro sa team.","translation":"I hope the new team members **will click** (with each other)."}]

meaning_filipino: Laging tumatama; hindi kailanman sumasablay o nagkakamali sa pag-asinta o pagtantiya.
etymology: Mula sa 'walâ' (none) + salitang Espanyol na 'mintis' (miss, failure).
original_explanation: Think of a basketball player who never misses a free throw, or your chismosa neighbor who's always right about the latest gossip. It means 'without fail,' 'always hits the mark,' 'surefire.' Yung reseta ng lola mo para sa ubo? Walang-mintis 'yon!
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri na naglalarawan sa pangngalan, o pang-abay na naglalarawan sa pandiwa (hal. 'Walang-mintis siyang dumarating').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Walang-mintis** ang kanyang mga hula sa basketball.","translation":"His basketball predictions are **unerring**."},{"sentence":"**Walang-mintis** siyang dumarating tuwing alas-otso ng umaga.","translation":"**Without fail**, he arrives at eight in the morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pinsala sa kasukasuan kung saan ang dulo ng buto ay naalis sa normal nitong posisyon.
original_explanation: The painful result of trying to be athletic when you're clearly not. One wrong move playing basketball or a bad fall from trying a TikTok dance, and boom, your joint decides to go on a separate vacation. Time to see the 'manghihilot'.
usage_notes: Maglinsad is the intransitive verb (to become dislocated), while malinsad is more common. For example, "Nag-ingat siya para hindi maglinsad ang balikat niya" vs "Nalinsad ang balikat niya."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla siyang napasigaw nang **maglinsad** ang kanyang tuhod habang naglalaro.","translation":"He suddenly screamed when his knee **got dislocated** while playing."},{"sentence":"Delikado ang pagbuhat ng mabigat dahil baka **maglinsad** ang iyong likod.","translation":"Lifting heavy things is dangerous because your back might **get sprained**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagpapaikli ng pariralang "ang wika nila" o "ayon sa kanila," ginagamit sa pag-uulat ng sinabi ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is the classic "sabi nila" but make it formal. It's the Filipino version of "according to them" or "they said." Ginagamit mo 'to kapag nagre-report ka ng chismis na narinig mo, pero gusto mo sound educated. "Uulan daw bukas, anila."
usage_notes: Often used in formal writing and speech. It's a shortcut to attribute a statement to a group of people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda raw ang pelikula, **anila**.","translation":"The movie is good, **they said**."},{"sentence":"Hindi na matutuloy ang pagpupulong, **anila**, dahil sa masamang panahon.","translation":"**According to them**, the meeting will not push through because of the bad weather."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagluluto kung saan ang mga sangkap, karaniwan ay bawang at sibuyas, ay piniprito nang bahagya sa kaunting mantika bago ihalo ang pangunahing sahog.
original_explanation: The holy trinity of Pinoy cooking: bawang, sibuyas, at kamatis sizzling in a pan. If your house doesn't smell like 'gisa' at least once a day, are you even in a Filipino household? Ito yung 'Step 1' sa 90% ng mga recipe sa 'Lutong Bahay' cookbook.
usage_notes: The base of many Filipino dishes. The verb form is 'gisahin' or 'igisa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bango ng **gisa** mo, ano'ng niluluto mo?","translation":"Your **sauté** smells good, what are you cooking?"},{"sentence":"Magsimula sa **gisa** ng bawang at sibuyas.","translation":"Start with a **sauté** of garlic and onions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglabas ng isang matinis at nakatutulig na tunog o sigaw.
original_explanation: This is the sound you make when you see a cockroach fly. It's the sound of your favorite K-pop idol appearing on stage. It's also the sound of rusty brakes on a jeepney. A high-pitched sound of either pure terror or pure delight. No in-between.
usage_notes: "Pag-iirit" (with reduplication) implies a more continuous or repeated act.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig sa buong bahay ang **pag-irit** niya nang makita ang daga.","translation":"Her **shriek** was heard throughout the house when she saw the rat."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-irit** ng mga tagahanga ay umalingawngaw sa buong stadium.","translation":"The **squealing** of the fans echoed throughout the stadium."}]

translation: to stomp, to stamp one's feet in anger
meaning_filipino: Ang malakas na pag-apak ng paa sa sahig o lupa, karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng galit, pagkadismaya, o pagmamaktol.
etymology: From 'dabog' (a noisy stamp of the foot) with the -um- infix.
original_explanation: The official sound effect of a Filipino 'tampo'. It's that dramatic exit when your parents don't let you go out. You stomp your feet, maybe slam a door for good measure. It's the physical manifestation of 'Hmp! Bahala ka diyan!'
usage_notes: Specifically implies stomping out of frustration, anger, or protest, often associated with childish tantrums but used by adults too.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumabog** ang bata nang hindi ibili ng laruan.","translation":"The child **stomped his feet** when he wasn't bought a toy."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **dumabog** na parang bata, mag-usap tayo nang maayos.","translation":"Don't **stomp around** like a child, let's talk properly."}]

translation: very little; a very small amount
meaning_filipino: Isang napakaliit o halos wala nang natitirang bilang o dami; ang pinakamaliit na antas na maiisip.
etymology: Nagmula sa pag-uulit ng salitang 'kaunti' upang bigyang-diin ang kasukdulan ng pagiging maliit ng dami o bilang.
original_explanation: This is the amount of patience you have left during EDSA traffic at 6 PM. It's the data allowance you have on the 30th of the month. It's your 'sahod' after 'ambagan' for the officemate's birthday, despedida, and baby shower. It's the 'kakarampot' level of existence.
usage_notes: The linking particle '-ng' is attached to the first instance of the word. This is the most common way to form the superlative idea of 'kaunti' through reduplication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kaunting-kaunti** na lang ang pag-asa kong manalo sa lotto.","translation":"I have **very little** hope left of winning the lotto."},{"sentence":"Ang natira niyang pera ay **kaunting-kaunti** na lamang.","translation":"The money he had left was a **very small amount**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na tirahan ng isang pinuno ng estado, tulad ng hari, reyna, o presidente; isang malaki at marangyang gusali.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'palacio' (palace), na mula sa Latin na 'palatium'.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'bahay ng mayaman.' Sa Pinas, automatic na 'to ang Palasyo ng Malakanyang. Pero in general, ito yung bahay na sobrang laki at ganda, parang sa Disney movie. Yung tipong may sariling zip code at kailangan mo ng Waze para mahanap ang banyo.
usage_notes: Pinakakaraniwang tumutukoy sa Palasyo ng Malakanyang sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Palasyo** ng Malakanyang ang opisyal na tahanan ng Pangulo ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The Malacañang **Palace** is the official residence of the President of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Nangarap siyang tumira sa isang **palasyo** na parang prinsesa.","translation":"She dreamed of living in a **palace** like a princess."}]

translation: to make (people) face each other; to cross-examine
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghaharap sa dalawa o higit pang tao upang alamin ang katotohanan sa isang isyu o pangyayari, karaniwan upang paghambingin ang kanilang mga pahayag.
etymology: From `pag-` (verbal noun prefix) + reduplication of `tapat` (to be in front of, to be honest) + `-in` (object-focus suffix). It literally means 'to make them be in front of each other'.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'Marites Summit'. You bring Person A and Person B into the same room to finally get the real story. It's like a live-action version of reading two different comment threads about the same chismis and trying to figure out who's telling the truth. The goal? To stop the 'he said, she said' and get to the 'we said it to each other's faces'.
usage_notes: This verb is often used in legal, investigative, or conflict-resolution contexts to resolve discrepancies in testimonies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pagtapat-tapatin** ang dalawang saksi para malaman kung sino ang nagsasabi ng totoo.","translation":"The two witnesses need to be **made to face each other** to know who is telling the truth."},{"sentence":"Sa halip na mag-away sa chat, mas mabuting **pagtapat-tapatin** na lang sila para magkaunawaan.","translation":"Instead of fighting over chat, it's better to **have them face each other** to come to an understanding."}]

meaning_filipino: Tukuyin ang kabuuang halaga o bilang ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng aritmetika o pagtutuos.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "cuenta" (account, bill) na may panlaping Tagalog na "-hin".
original_explanation: This is what you do when you get the bill at a group dinner and everyone only has 1000-peso bills. It's the mental math required to see if your sahod can survive the 12.12 sale. "Kuwentahin mo nga kung magkano lahat ng na-add to cart ko."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **kuwentahin** nang mabuti ang lahat ng iyong gastusin.","translation":"You need **to calculate** all your expenses carefully."},{"sentence":"**Kuwentahin** mo kung ilan lahat ang darating sa party para makapaghanda tayo ng sapat na pagkain.","translation":"**Calculate** how many people are coming to the party so we can prepare enough food."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng isang bahagi sa iba; ang paghahati-hati ng isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: What you do with your chichirya with your friends (or not). It's what vloggers do when they share their 'blessings' on camera. It’s the core concept of a 'community pantry.' Sharing is caring, and the Filipino word for it is **pagbabahagi**.
usage_notes: Can refer to tangible things (food, money) or intangible things (knowledge, stories, feelings).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbabahagi** ng kaalaman ay isang paraan ng pagtulong sa kapwa.","translation":"The **sharing** of knowledge is a way of helping others."},{"sentence":"Naging maayos ang **pagbabahagi** ng mana sa magkakapatid.","translation":"The **dividing** of the inheritance among the siblings was orderly."}]

translation: to feel cold, to be chilled
meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman ang lamig o ginaw; ang kalagayan ng pagiging malamigin.
original_explanation: This is what happens to you when you forget your jacket for the Baguio trip. 'Hala, ginawin ka niyan!' (Oh no, you'll get cold!). It's the state of *becoming* cold.
usage_notes: Often used as a warning ('Huwag kang magpaginaw') or to state a fact ('madaling ginawin'). Not to be confused with the adjective 'ginawin' which describes a person who is sensitive to cold.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magsuot ka ng dyaket para hindi ka **ginawin**.","translation":"Wear a jacket so you won't **feel cold**."},{"sentence":"Madali akong **ginawin** kapag umuulan.","translation":"I easily **get chilled** when it rains."}]

translation: to turn a blind eye; to ignore deliberately
meaning_filipino: Sadyaing huwag pansinin o kilalanin ang isang bagay na alam mong nangyayari, lalo na kung ito ay mali o hindi kaaya-aya.
original_explanation: That thing you do when your friend is making a questionable life choice but you're too tired to argue. Or when a politician sees corruption but does nothing. You just 'ipikit ang mata' and pretend you didn't see anything. It's the national sport of selective vision.
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression. The literal meaning is 'to close the eyes', but it is almost always used figuratively to mean 'to ignore'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **ipikit ang mata** sa kahirapang nakikita mo sa paligid.","translation":"It's hard to **turn a blind eye** to the poverty you see around you."},{"sentence":"Pinili niyang **ipikit ang mata** sa mga kasalanan ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"He chose to **turn a blind eye** to his friend's mistakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa digmaan, militar, o sa hukbo; may katangiang pang-militar.
original_explanation: Think 'martial law' (batas marsyal). It's anything that has to do with the military, war, or strict, soldier-like discipline. It’s got that serious, rigid, 'fall in line!' vibe. Not to be confused with the planet Mars or your tita's best friend, Mars.
usage_notes: Most commonly heard in the Philippines in the context of 'batas marsyal' (martial law).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Idineklara ang batas **marsyal** sa buong bansa.","translation":"Martial law was declared across the country."},{"sentence":"Ang musika ay may himig na **marsyal** na karaniwang tinutugtog sa mga parada.","translation":"The music has a **martial** tune that is usually played in parades."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na kasama sa isang pangkat, gawain, o pag-aari; mayroong parte o bahagi sa isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: You're kabahagi of the group project (kahit 'taga-print' ka lang). You're kabahagi of the family chismis (kahit 'taga-kain' ka lang sa reunion). You're a shareholder, a team member, a contributor. Basically, you're part of the team, for better or for worse. "We're all in this together!"
usage_notes: Can refer to being part of a group, an inheritance, a company, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat mamamayan ay **kabahagi** sa pag-unlad ng bansa.","translation":"Every citizen is **part of** the nation's progress."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **kabahagi** sa aming maliit na negosyo.","translation":"He is a **partner** in our small business."}]

meaning_filipino: Idiin o pigain ang isang bagay upang maalis ang likido sa loob nito, o upang makuha ang katas.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa basahan bago ka magpunas ng sahig. O 'yung ginagawa sa calamansi para sa toyo. Minsan, ito rin ang ginagawa ng boss mo sa'yo pag malapit na ang deadline, piga-piga ang utak mo for ideas.
usage_notes: Commonly used for laundry (`magpiga ng damit`), fruits (`magpiga ng calamansi`), or coconuts (`magpiga ng niyog`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpiga** ng basahan nang mabuti bago mo ipunas sa sahig.","translation":"You need to **wring** the rag well before you wipe the floor."},{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magpiga** ng mga kalamansi para sa ating sawsawan.","translation":"Help me **squeeze** the calamansi for our dipping sauce."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mataas na ranggong pari sa Simbahang Kristiyano na may awtoridad sa isang diyosesis o isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: In the Catholic hierarchy, they're the area managers. The obispo is a high-ranking priest who's in charge of all the churches and priests in a specific region (a diocese). They're the ones you see in fancier robes during big masses, and they're often sought for their opinions on national issues, turning them into surprise political commentators.
usage_notes: Specific to Christian, particularly Catholic, terminology.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **obispo** ang nanguna sa misa para sa kapistahan.","translation":"The **bishop** led the mass for the fiesta."},{"sentence":"Kinapanayam ng media ang **obispo** tungkol sa kanyang pananaw sa bagong batas.","translation":"The media interviewed the **bishop** about his views on the new law."}]

translation: to be recovered; to be retrieved
meaning_filipino: Ang muling makuha o maibalik ang isang bagay na nawala, naagaw, o naipahiram.
original_explanation: 'Yung dignidad mong nawala nung nag-chat ka sa ex mo? Mahirap nang mabawi 'yan. Or 'yung 500 pesos na hiniram ng "friend" mo last year, good luck trying to get it back. It's the act of reclaiming what was once yours.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical objects, money, or abstract concepts like honor or time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan ng pulisya na **mabawi** ang mga ninakaw na alahas.","translation":"The police are trying to **recover** the stolen jewelry."},{"sentence":"Sana **mabawi** ko ang puhunan ko sa negosyong ito.","translation":"I hope I can **get back** my investment in this business."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kumpanya o organisasyon na responsable sa paghahanda, pag-iimprenta, at pamamahagi ng mga aklat, pahayagan, magasin, at iba pang nakasulat na materyal.
original_explanation: The place where books are born! It's the company that decides if your manuscript is the next big hit or just another file in the 'reject' folder. Think of it as the record label for authors.
usage_notes: A more formal term. 'Publishing house' or 'publisher' are common English equivalents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinasa niya ang kanyang manuskrito sa isang kilalang **lathalaan**.","translation":"She submitted her manuscript to a well-known **publishing house**."},{"sentence":"Ang **lathalaan** ang nagpasya na ilabas ang aklat sa susunod na taon.","translation":"The **publication** decided to release the book next year."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilagay sa tabi ng isa pa bilang suporta, gabay, o katulong; isabay o iakma.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "i-" at salitang-ugat na "agapay" (pag-alalay o paglalagay sa tabi).
original_explanation: Imagine you're walking with your lola and you put your arm out for her to hold on to. That's "inagapayan." It's giving support by being right there beside someone. In a less literal sense, it's about aligning your plans with someone else's. "Iagapay mo ang schedule mo sa schedule ko."
usage_notes: May literal na kahulugan (pisikal na pag-alalay) at metaporikal na kahulugan (pag-akma ng plano o kilos).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iagapay** mo ang iyong braso sa balikat niya upang hindi siya matumba.","translation":"**Place** your arm **alongside** his shoulder so he won't fall."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **iagapay** ng gobyerno ang mga programa nito sa pangangailangan ng mamamayan.","translation":"The government needs to **align** its programs with the needs of the citizens."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae na legal na hiwalay sa kanyang asawa sa pamamagitan ng diborsiyo.
original_explanation: She's the "it's complicated" status made official, but for women. In a country where divorce isn't legal (yet?), being a **diborsyada** often means you got divorced abroad. She's not just a 'hiwalay', she's got the paperwork to prove it. She's the main character in her own story of starting over.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a female. The male counterpart is `diborsyado`. The spelling `diborsiyada` is also used but less common. As divorce is not legal in the Philippines (except for Muslims), this term usually applies to Filipinos divorced in other countries or to foreigners.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **diborsyada** na siya nang bumalik sa Pilipinas.","translation":"She was already a **divorcée** when she returned to the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Ang kaibigan kong **diborsyada** ay mas masaya ngayon.","translation":"My **divorced** friend is happier now."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na puno; nag-uumapaw sa isang katangian, damdamin, o bagay.
original_explanation: When you're not just happy, you're "puspos ng kagalakan." It's being so full of something—joy, gratitude, or even anger—that it's practically overflowing. Think of your lola's love for you, or your credit card bill after a 12.12 sale. It's the "extra" version of "puno".
usage_notes: Often used in a formal or literary context, especially in religious settings (e.g., "puspos ng grasya" - full of grace).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang puso ay **puspos** ng pasasalamat.","translation":"Her heart is **filled with** gratitude."},{"sentence":"Isang buhay na **puspos** sa pag-ibig at paglilingkod ang kanyang ipinamuhay.","translation":"She lived a life **replete** with love and service."}]

meaning_filipino: May takda, hangganan, o limitasyon; hindi para sa lahat.
original_explanation: This is what your parents call the movies you want to watch but can't. It's also your data plan by the end of the month. Basically, 'bawal' but with more class. "For your eyes only," but everyone else seems to be looking.
usage_notes: Commonly used in Taglish, especially for movie ratings (R-18), access to places, or information. Often used interchangeably with the Tagalog-ized `restrikto`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Restricted** ang pelikula kaya hindi ka pa pwedeng manood.","translation":"The movie is **restricted** so you can't watch it yet."},{"sentence":"May mga **restricted** areas sa loob ng military camp.","translation":"There are **restricted** areas inside the military camp."}]

translation: to go crazy; to go mad
meaning_filipino: Mawala sa tamang katinuan ng isip; magkaroon ng sakit sa pag-iisip.
original_explanation: Can be literal, but mostly used for when the WiFi is slow, your crush finally messages you, or when you hear the same Christmas song for the 100th time in November. 'Mababaliw na ako sa 'yo!' can be a declaration of intense love or extreme annoyance. The official emotion for dealing with Manila traffic.
usage_notes: Used both literally for mental illness and hyperbolically for frustration, excitement, or infatuation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang stress sa trabaho, pakiramdam ko ay **mababaliw** na ako.","translation":"With so much stress at work, I feel like I'm **going to go crazy**."},{"sentence":"**Nababaliw** ako sa tuwing ngumingiti ka.","translation":"I **go crazy** every time you smile."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa hinaharap na anyo ng pandiwa. Nagsasaad na ang isang tao o isang gawa ay tatanggap ng gantimpala, premyo, o pagkilala.
etymology: From 'ma-' + repetition of the first syllable of the root ('gan-timpala' -> 'ga-gantimpala') + '-an' suffix.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'your hard work will pay off' verb. It's what you hope for after endless overtime, cramming for finals, or being a good person even when no one's watching. It’s the universe (or your boss) finally giving you your 13th-month pay, a promotion, or just good karma. The opposite of 'na-scam'.
usage_notes: Future tense, potential/passive voice. The person or thing being rewarded is the subject.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lahat ng iyong sakripisyo ay **magagantimpalaan** balang araw.","translation":"All your sacrifices **will be rewarded** someday."},{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang **magagantimpalaan** bilang 'Employee of the Month'?","translation":"I wonder who **will be rewarded** as 'Employee of the Month'?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong labis na naghahangad ng atensyon o pagkilala mula sa iba, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng paggawa ng mga bagay na kapansin-pansin.
original_explanation: The official term for someone who posts 30 IG stories a day or fakes a 'sana all' moment for likes. They're 'KSP' (Kulang Sa Pansin). They live for the validation, the comments, and the 'seen' notifications. Basically, they're the main character in their own teleserye, and they need an audience.
usage_notes: Often abbreviated as KSP in colloquial speech and text. It carries a negative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi siyang nagpo-post ng mga malulungkot na status para mapansin; sobrang **kulang-pansin**.","translation":"She always posts sad statuses to get noticed; she's so **attention-seeking**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **kulang-pansin** sa social media.","translation":"Don't be an **attention-seeker** on social media."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ilegal na paggamit o pagnanakaw ng pera o ari-arian na ipinagkatiwala sa isang tao para sa pansariling kapakinabangan.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizing prefix) + lustay (to embezzle, to squander).
original_explanation: This is the 'where did the money go?' drama, usually involving public funds. It’s when the budget for a bridge ends up funding someone's new mansion. It's the act of treating entrusted money—like the class fund, the office party budget, or the nation's treasury—as your personal shopping allowance. A classic move in political 'chismis'.
usage_notes: A legal and financial term strongly associated with corruption and breach of trust.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahaharap siya sa kasong **paglustay** ng pondo ng bayan.","translation":"He is facing charges of **embezzlement** of public funds."},{"sentence":"Ang **paglustay** ay isang uri ng pagnanakaw at pagtataksil sa tiwala.","translation":"**Misappropriation** is a form of theft and betrayal of trust."}]

translation: to let something improve; to wait for a better condition
meaning_filipino: Ang paghihintay o pagbibigay ng pagkakataon para sa isang sitwasyon o kalagayan na bumuti o gumanda.
etymology: From mag- (actor-focus verb prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + inam (goodness, fineness, quality).
original_explanation: This is the verb of strategic waiting. When you're sick, you `nagpapainam` ng pakiramdam (wait to feel better). When the weather is bad, `magpainam` muna tayo ng panahon bago umalis. In relationships, sometimes you need to `magpainam` muna ng sitwasyon before talking about a problem. Give it space. Let it breathe.
usage_notes: `Magpainam` is often used for situations, feelings, or weather. It implies waiting for a natural improvement. `Painamin` means to actively improve something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpapainam** lang ako ng pakiramdam bago pumasok sa trabaho.","translation":"I'm just **waiting to feel better** before going to work."},{"sentence":"Huwag muna nating pag-usapan 'yan, **magpainam** muna tayo ng sitwasyon.","translation":"Let's not talk about that yet, let's **wait for the situation to improve** first."}]

translation: to glide, to skim, to swoop
meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at mababang paglipad o pagdaan sa ibabaw ng isang bagay, tulad ng ibon sa ibabaw ng tubig o dahon na tinatangay ng hangin.
original_explanation: Parang drone shot sa kasal mo, 'yung camera ay nagsalipadpad sa ibabaw ng mga bisita. Pwede ring 'yung puso mo noong nag-chat si crush, sumalipadpad sa tuwa. It's that graceful, low-level swooping motion.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the movement of birds, leaves, or paper carried by the wind. It implies a light, almost effortless movement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagsalipadpad** ang mga tuyong dahon sa kalsada dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"The dry leaves **skimmed** across the road because of the strong wind."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ko ang ibon na **sumalipadpad** malapit sa lawa.","translation":"I clearly saw the bird that **swooped** near the lake."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagtatanim sa isipan o pagsasaulo ng isang bagay hanggang sa ito ay matandaan nang walang tulong o gabay.
original_explanation: ‘Yung effort na ginagawa mo para matandaan ‘yung script na binigay ng jowa mo kung paano ka magso-sorry sa kanya. Also, what you tell yourself you'll do before an exam, but you end up just staring at the book. "Kabisahin mo ‘to: ‘di ka na niya babalikan."
usage_notes: A command or infinitive form. The object-focused verb for memorizing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kabisahin** mo ang lahat ng linya mo para sa dula.","translation":"**Memorize** all your lines for the play."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **kabisahin** ang periodic table of elements.","translation":"It's difficult **to memorize** the periodic table of elements."}]

translation: to junk; to throw away; to dismiss
meaning_filipino: Itapon dahil wala nang halaga o pakinabang; sa kontekstong legal o pormal, ito ay ang pagwawalang-bisa o hindi pagtanggap sa isang mungkahi, kaso, o ideya.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "i-" at sa salitang Espanyol na "basura" (trash).
original_explanation: From the Spanish word for trash, 'basura'. This is what happens to your brilliant idea during a brainstorming session when your boss says 'Next!' Also what you do to your ex's stuff after a breakup. It's the ultimate act of 'You're cancelled.' Pwedeng ibasura ang ebidensya, ang proposal, o ang feelings mo para sa kanya.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang pandiwa sa kolokyal at pormal na usapan. Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na basura o sa mga abstraktong konsepto tulad ng ideya, panukala, o kaso sa korte.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ibasura** mo na 'yang mga lumang damit na hindi mo na sinusuot.","translation":"**Throw away** those old clothes that you don't wear anymore."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang korte na **ibasura** ang kaso dahil sa kakulangan ng ebidensya.","translation":"The court decided to **dismiss** the case due to lack of evidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging paos o pagkawala ng tinig, karaniwang dahil sa labis na paggamit ng lalamunan o sakit.
original_explanation: Yung nangyayari sa boses mo after ng concert ng paborito mong K-Pop group, o pagkatapos mong mag-videoke nang tatlong oras straight. Yung boses mo, parang tunog ng sirang pinto. "Sorry, may tingig ako, 'di ako makasigaw."
usage_notes: A less common word for hoarseness. 'Paos' or 'malat' are more frequently used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa walang tigil na pagsigaw sa konsiyerto, nagkaroon siya ng **tingig** kinabukasan.","translation":"Because of the non-stop shouting at the concert, he became **hoarse** the next day."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagdaragdag ng tubig o ibang sangkap sa isang likido upang ito ay dumami o bumaba ang konsentrasyon nito.
original_explanation: What some vendors do to the iced tea to maximize profit. Also, what happens to the "tea" (chismis) when it passes through too many people—it gets diluted and the facts get mixed up.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tiyaking tama ang sukat sa **pagbanto** ng gatas ng sanggol.","translation":"Ensure the correct measurement when **diluting** the baby's milk."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ang **pagbanto** sa mga produktong tulad ng suka at toyo.","translation":"The **adulteration** of products like vinegar and soy sauce is prohibited."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tulong at payo na ibinibigay ng isang kumpanya sa mga taong bumibili o gumagamit ng mga produkto at serbisyo nito.
original_explanation: The art of smiling through the phone while someone yells at you about their slow internet. It's a national sport in the Philippines, thanks to the BPO industry. It's the job that requires the patience of a saint, the script of a robot, and the caffeine intake of a programmer. "Thank you for calling, how may I help you?"
usage_notes: A major industry in the Philippines. The phrase is used universally in English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda ang **customer service** ng kumpanyang iyon, mabilis silang sumagot.","translation":"That company's **customer service** is good, they respond quickly."},{"sentence":"Nagtrabaho siya sa **customer service** ng ilang taon.","translation":"He/She worked in **customer service** for several years."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, lalo na sa isang bata, na matigas ang ulo, mahirap pasunurin, at malikot.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung pamangkin mong ayaw matulog sa hapon, kinakalat 'yung laruan pagkatapos mong magligpit, at tinatanong ka ng 'bakit?' nang 20 times per minute. Siya rin 'yung officemate na laging kontra sa suggestion mo kahit wala namang better idea. Basically, the human version of a cat knocking things off a table for no reason.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para ilarawan ang mga bata, ngunit maaari ring gamitin sa matatanda na may katulad na pag-uugali.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang batang iyon ay napaka-**sutil**; ayaw niyang makinig sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"That child is very **naughty**; he doesn't want to listen to his parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbitaw sa isang bagay upang ito ay bumagsak; o ang pagbibigay ng regular na bayad o kontribusyon para sa isang bagay tulad ng SSS, Pag-IBIG, o insurance.
original_explanation: The act of physically dropping something, like your phone (wag naman sana!). But more importantly, it's what you do every payday for your SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG contributions. "Kailangan ko nang maghulog sa SSS." is the adulting version of "I need to pay my bills."
usage_notes: Has a dual meaning: the literal act of dropping and the common financial term for making installment payments or contributions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, baka **maghulog** ka ng gamit sa hagdan.","translation":"Be careful, you might **drop** something on the stairs."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **maghulog** ng bayad para sa iyong insurance ngayong buwan.","translation":"Don't forget to **contribute** your payment for your insurance this month."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paulit-ulit na paggigiit o pagpapahid ng isang bagay sa ibabaw ng iba upang linisin, pakinisin, o alisin ang dumi.
original_explanation: That intense workout your arms get when scrubbing the 'kaldero' after cooking adobo. It's the friction-filled action of cleaning something, whether it's your back with a 'bimpo', the floor with a 'bunot', or your ex's number from your phone (metaphorically, of course).
usage_notes: Can refer to cleaning, polishing, or even scratching an itch ('pagkakamot').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod siya sa **pagkukuskos** ng sahig buong hapon.","translation":"She was very tired from **scrubbing** the floor all afternoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paanyaya o paghamon sa isang tao na subukin ang kanyang kakayahan, lakas, o tapang sa isang labanan, paligsahan, o anumang mahirap na gawain.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung "Tara, suntukan!" ng mga jologs, o 'yung "Bet?" ng mga conyo. It's that moment someone dares you to do something, from a simple game to a life-changing decision. 'Yung friend mong biglang nagyaya ng unli-wings, 'yan, isang reto 'yan sa diet mo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinatanggap ko ang iyong **reto** na magkarera tayo hanggang sa dulo ng kalsada.","translation":"I accept your **challenge** for us to race to the end of the street."},{"sentence":"Ang pinakamalaking **reto** sa buhay niya ay ang pagtaguyod sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"The biggest **challenge** in his life is providing for his family."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan kung saan ang isang bagay ay banat, hindi kulubot, o tuwid.
original_explanation: The opposite of lukot. It's your state after a good night's sleep and a satisfying stretch. It's what you want your shirt to be before a job interview, or what you wish your life was—straight and without complications. "Sana all unat ang buhay."
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang damit, buhok, o isang nakaunat na bahagi ng katawan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas magandang tingnan ang damit kapag ito ay **unat** at hindi gusot.","translation":"Clothes look better when they are **straightened** and not wrinkled."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang natatanging lalagyan o kahon, karaniwang nasa altar ng simbahan, kung saan itinatago ang Banal na Sakramento o konsagradong ostiya.
original_explanation: That fancy, often golden box you see in a Catholic church, usually near the altar. It's the VIP lounge for the Holy Eucharist. You genuflect (luhod) towards it as a sign of respect. It's basically God's holy pantry in the church.
usage_notes: A purely religious term used within the context of Roman Catholicism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sagraryo** ay yari sa ginto at mamahaling bato.","translation":"The **tabernacle** is made of gold and precious stones."},{"sentence":"Yumuko siya sa harap ng **sagraryo** upang magdasal.","translation":"She bowed before the **tabernacle** to pray."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nananakit, nanunukso, o nang-aapi sa mga taong itinuturing niyang mas mahina.
original_explanation: 'Yung kontrabida sa school life mo. Sila yung mahilig mang-asar, manulak, o kumuha ng baon mo. Sa office, sila yung boss na laging mainit ang ulo o yung officemate na laging nagpaparinig. Sa social media, sila yung mga "basher" na walang ginawa kundi mag-comment ng nega.
usage_notes: Ang salitang ito ay ganap nang naisama sa wikang Filipino, lalo na sa mga kabataan. Ang pandiwa nito ay "mambully" o "binubully".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot na isumbong ang **bully** sa inyong guro.","translation":"Don't be afraid to report the **bully** to your teacher."},{"sentence":"Laging biktima ng mga **bully** si Marco noong elementarya.","translation":"Marco was always a victim of **bullies** during elementary school."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o kagamitan kung saan pinipisa o pinapalimliman ang mga itlog upang maging sisiw.
original_explanation: This is a baby-making machine for chickens. An incubator. It's the place where eggs are kept warm and cozy until they hatch. Think of it as a maternity ward for future fried chicken.
usage_notes: "Pisa" in this context means "to hatch," a specific meaning different from "to crush." This phrase specifically refers to a place or device for hatching eggs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Moderno na ang **pisaan ng itlog** sa kanilang manukan.","translation":"The **hatchery** in their poultry farm is now modern."},{"sentence":"Inilagay niya ang mga bagong itlog sa **pisaan ng itlog**.","translation":"He placed the new eggs in the **incubator**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang punong ehekutibo ng isang lalawigan o estado.
original_explanation: The boss of a whole province. Their face is on every lamppost, tarpaulin, and bag of relief goods during election season. In historical dramas, they're the powerful Spanish dude with a big hat. In modern times, they're the one you blame for traffic in the provincial capital.
usage_notes: The female equivalent is 'gobernadora'. Often shortened to 'Gob' in informal settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **gobernador** ang nanguna sa pamamahagi ng tulong sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The **governor** led the distribution of aid to the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Tatakbo siyang muli bilang **gobernador** sa susunod na halalan.","translation":"He will run again for **governor** in the next election."}]
