meaning_filipino: Isang sisidlang karaniwang yari sa plastik o metal, may hawakan, at ginagamit sa pagsalok o pag-iipon ng tubig at iba pang likido.
etymology: From Spanish 'timbal' (kettledrum), likely due to the shape.
original_explanation: The 'timba' is the unsung hero of the Filipino bathroom. No shower? No problem. 'Timba' at 'tabo' to the rescue! It's also your best friend during a water interruption or for cleaning the house. It's the original ice bucket challenge container. A household isn't complete without one.
usage_notes: A quintessential household item in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Punuin mo ng tubig ang **timba** para may magamit tayo mamaya.","translation":"Fill the **bucket** with water so we have some to use later."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **timba** para ipandilig sa mga halaman.","translation":"He used the **pail** to water the plants."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip na tumutukoy sa kahit na anong tao nang walang pagtatangi o pagpili.
original_explanation: 'Yung all-inclusive, no-VIP-pass na term para sa tao. "Open to sinuman," "For sinuman who is interested..." Ito 'yung sagot mo 'pag tinanong ka kung sino'ng aawayin mo: "Sinuman ang kumain ng lunch ko sa office fridge!"
usage_notes: An indefinite pronoun. Equivalent to 'kahit sino'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sinuman** ang makakita sa aking aso ay may pabuya.","translation":"**Whoever** finds my dog will get a reward."},{"sentence":"Bukas ang paligsahan para sa **sinuman** na nais sumali.","translation":"The contest is open to **anyone** who wants to join."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malinaw na likido na matatagpuan sa loob ng isang murang bunga ng niyog.
etymology: Parirala na binubuo ng mga salitang Tagalog.
original_explanation: The OG sports drink, straight from the source. Before Gatorade, there was buko juice. It's what you drink on a hot day at the beach, or what your lola makes you drink when you have a UTI. Now it's sold in fancy cartons at the supermarket for 10x the price of a fresh buko from a street vendor.
usage_notes: Ang 'buko juice' ay ang mas karaniwang termino sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tubig ng niyog** ay masarap at nakakapresko.","translation":"**Coconut water** is delicious and refreshing."},{"sentence":"Sinasabing mabuti para sa bato ang pag-inom ng **tubig ng niyog**.","translation":"They say drinking **coconut water** is good for the kidneys."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng isang bagay bilang kahalili ng isa pa; ang pagbibigay ng isang bagay at pagtanggap ng iba bilang katumbas.
original_explanation: This is the "sana all" of relationships and gadgets. Kapag luma na, palitan ng bago. Kapag 'di na gumagana, palitan. It's the ultimate upgrade culture verb. Also used for exchanging items, like when you get the wrong size from your online shopping haul. "Pa-palitan ko 'to, besh."
usage_notes: Can be used for replacing something broken ('palitan ng bago'), exchanging goods ('palitan ng kalakal'), or taking someone's place in a shift or duty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo nang **palitan** ang lumang baterya ng iyong telepono.","translation":"You need to **replace** the old battery of your phone."},{"sentence":"Nagkasundo silang **palitan** ng kalakal ang kanilang mga ani.","translation":"They agreed to **exchange** their harvests for other goods."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglahok o pagsama sa isang gawain, usapan, o grupo.
etymology: From pa- + ki- + sali (root word). The pa-ki- prefix denotes a social act or a request to do something with others.
original_explanation: That feeling when your friends are making plans in the group chat and you type "Sama ako!" even if you don't know the details. It's the opposite of being a wallflower; it's being a willing "sawsawero/sawsawera" in a good way. It's the spirit of crashing a Zoom meeting you were invited to at the last minute.
usage_notes: Often used to describe joining an activity, conversation, or group. It implies a voluntary act of including oneself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pakikisali** niya sa usapan ay nagbigay ng bagong pananaw.","translation":"His **participation** in the discussion provided a new perspective."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko sanang subukan ang **pakikisali** sa mga community projects.","translation":"I would like to try **joining in** on community projects."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalakbay o paglilibot sa iba't ibang lugar nang walang tiyak na destinasyon o para sa layuning magliwaliw.
original_explanation: The national pastime. 'Tara, gala tayo!' is the official start of many unplanned adventures (and expenses). It's the opposite of being a 'homebody'. A 'gala' can be a quick trip to the mall, a weekend beach trip, or a month-long backpacking adventure. It's the cure for boredom and the cause of an empty wallet.
usage_notes: Bilang pangngalan, tumutukoy ito sa akto ng paglilibot o sa biyahe mismo. Ang pandiwa nito ay "gumala."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming **gala** sa Vigan ay hindi malilimutan.","translation":"Our **trip** to Vigan was unforgettable."},{"sentence":"Puro ka na lang **gala**, tumulong ka naman sa bahay.","translation":"You're always **out and about**, help around the house for a change."}]

translation: to hammer, to pound, to strike
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pagpalo o paghampas sa isang bagay gamit ang isang kasangkapan tulad ng martilyo o ang sariling kamao.
original_explanation: The official sound of your kapitbahay doing home repairs at 7 AM on a Sunday. It's the sound of a carpenter, or you, trying to hang a picture frame and hitting your thumb instead. Basically, any repetitive hitting action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumukpok** siya ng pako sa dingding para isabit ang orasan.","translation":"He **hammered** a nail into the wall to hang the clock."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko siyang **pumukpok** sa pinto nang malakas.","translation":"I heard him **pound** on the door loudly."}]

translation: to sign (a document) together; to co-sign
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o magkasunod na paglalagda ng dalawa o higit pang tao sa isang kasulatan o dokumento bilang tanda ng pagsang-ayon o kasunduan.
etymology: From mag- + lagda (signature) + -an (suffix indicating a reciprocal or collective action).
original_explanation: This is the verb for when things get official. When you and your BPO team lead both sign your performance review, or when two countries sign a treaty. It's the action of making a deal legally binding with the power of your John Hancocks. It’s a group activity; you don't 'maglagdaan' alone.
usage_notes: This is a reciprocal verb, implying two or more parties are signing. For a single person signing, 'lumagda' or 'maglagda' is used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ay **naglagdaan** ng kontrata para sa bagong proyekto.","translation":"They **co-signed** a contract for the new project."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **maglagdaan** ang mag-asawa sa kanilang marriage certificate.","translation":"The couple needs to **sign** their marriage certificate **together**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lihim na pagsama ng isang lalaki at babae upang magsama bilang mag-asawa, karaniwan nang walang pahintulot ng mga magulang.
original_explanation: The original 'sana all' before it was cool. When a couple decides to skip the family drama, the expensive reception, and just run away together to get married. 'Bes, 'di ba engaged lang sila last month? Nabalitaan ko **tumanan** na daw!'
usage_notes: The root word 'tanan' can also mean 'all' or 'everyone' in other contexts, but the verb 'tumanan' specifically means 'to elope'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil tutol ang kanilang mga pamilya, nagpasya ang magkasintahan na **tumanan**.","translation":"Because their families were against it, the couple decided **to elope**."},{"sentence":"Maraming kuwento sa probinsya tungkol sa mga binatang **tumanan** kasama ang kanilang mga nobya.","translation":"There are many stories in the province about young men who **eloped** with their girlfriends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang ginagamit sa pagbuo ng pautos na patanggi; nagpapahayag ng pagbabawal o pagpigil sa isang kilos.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino stop sign. It's the first word in a hundred parental warnings ("Huwag kang magpagabi!"), friendly advice ("Huwag kang umasa, masasaktan ka lang."), and self-reminders ("Huwag ka nang mag-order sa Shopee, wala ka nang pera!"). It's the gatekeeper of bad decisions. Often shortened to 'wag'.
usage_notes: Used to form negative commands. Often contracted to 'wag' in informal speech and writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Huwag** kang maingay sa loob ng silid-aklatan.","translation":"**Don't** be noisy inside the library."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan ako ni Nanay na **huwag** kalimutan ang aking baon.","translation":"Mom told me **not** to forget my packed lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maka-agham na pag-aaral ng wika. Alternatibong baybay ng 'lingguwistika'.
original_explanation: The old-school spelling for 'lingguwistika'. It's like typing 'd' instead of 'the' – everyone knows what you mean, but the newer version is more standard.
usage_notes: Isang baryanteng baybay ng 'lingguwistika'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kurso niya sa kolehiyo ay **lingwistika**.","translation":"Her course in college is **linguistics**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking natural na daluyan ng tubig-tabang na dumadaloy patungo sa karagatan, dagat, lawa, o isa pang ilog.
original_explanation: The OG highway before SLEX and NLEX. It's where ancient communities were built, where your lola used to wash clothes, and where Pasig River Rehabilitation commercials get their B-roll. Nowadays, it’s either a tourist spot (like Loboc River) or a cautionary tale about pollution. A river is life, history, and sometimes, a giant basurahan, sadly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naligo kami sa malinaw na **ilog** sa aming probinsya.","translation":"We swam in the clear **river** in our province."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na napakalaki, napakahalaga, o kahanga-hanga sa sukat, kalidad, o lawak, na maihahalintulad sa isang monumento.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "monumental". Ang Tagalog na katumbas ay "monumental" din o "napakalaki".
original_explanation: When something is so big, so important, or so much of a hassle, you call it 'monumental'. A 'monumental' achievement is like winning the lottery. A 'monumental' task is like cleaning your room after a month. A 'monumental' traffic jam is just... EDSA on a payday Friday. It's the adjective you use when 'malaki' or 'importante' just isn't enough.
usage_notes: Used in both formal and informal contexts to add emphasis to the scale or importance of something. The spelling and meaning are directly adopted from English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **monumental** na tagumpay ang kanyang pagkapanalo.","translation":"Her victory was a **monumental** achievement."},{"sentence":"Nakaharap tayo sa isang **monumental** na hamon.","translation":"We are facing a **monumental** challenge."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kilos o gawain na isinagawa nang walang pag-iingat, pag-iisip sa kahihinatnan, o pagpili.
original_explanation: Yung friend mong bigla na lang nag-resign sa work nang wala pang bagong offer. Or yung pag-atake sa buffet na parang wala nang bukas. It's the "YOLO" mindset applied to decisions where you probably should have thought twice. No holds barred, no second thoughts, just pure, unadulterated "bahala na."
usage_notes: Often used to describe actions that are rash, careless, or have widespread, unintended consequences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **walang-taros** na pagputol ng mga puno ay nagdulot ng matinding pagbaha.","translation":"The **reckless** cutting of trees caused severe flooding."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **walang-taros** na paggastos, mabilis na naubos ang kanyang sahod.","translation":"Because of his **reckless** spending, his salary was quickly used up."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking langgam na kulay pula o itim, na kilala sa masakit na kagat.
original_explanation: The heavyweight champion of the ant world. The hantik is that big, scary ant that makes you jump when you see it. Its bite is no joke—it's the kind of sting that makes you question all your life choices that led you to that exact spot. They're the bouncers of the insect community.
usage_notes: Often found in gardens and rural areas. Their bite is notably painful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Aray! Kinagat ako ng **hantik**!","translation":"Ouch! I was bitten by a **large red ant**!"},{"sentence":"Maraming **hantik** sa ilalim ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"There are many **large red ants** under the mango tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manggagawa na humuhubog ng metal, karaniwan ay bakal, sa pamamagitan ng pagpapainit at pagpupukpok nito.
original_explanation: Before welders, there was the 'panday'. This is the OG craftsman, the guy who could turn a useless chunk of metal into a deadly 'itak' or a sturdy 'araro'. Today, the most famous one is Flavio, aka Ang Panday, who's basically the Filipino Thor, but his hammer is for forging swords, not summoning lightning.
usage_notes: Can be used more broadly to mean any skilled craftsman or artisan, but its primary meaning is a blacksmith.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpagawa ako ng bagong itak sa isang kilalang **panday** sa aming bayan.","translation":"I had a new bolo knife made by a famous **blacksmith** in our town."},{"sentence":"Ang galing ng pagkakagawa ng rehas, parang isang tunay na **panday** ang gumawa.","translation":"The craftsmanship of the grille is excellent, as if a true **artisan** made it."}]

meaning_filipino: May pagkakahawig sa isa't isa sa katangian, anyo, o kalikasan.
original_explanation: Basically a synonym for 'magkakapareho', but sounds slightly more formal. It's what you say when you notice all the K-Drama male leads have the same haircut, or when all the milk tea shops in your neighborhood have almost the same menu.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'magkakapareho'. 'Magkakatulad' can feel slightly more formal or literary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit kambal sila, hindi lahat ng ugali nila ay **magkakatulad**.","translation":"Even though they are twins, not all their traits are **similar**."},{"sentence":"Napansin ko na **magkakatulad** ang istilo ng kanilang mga pinta.","translation":"I noticed that the style of their paintings are **alike**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o proseso ng pagsasagawa ng isang imbestigasyon o pagsisiyasat sa isang tao o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the "how" of an investigation. It's not the investigation itself (`pag-iimbestiga`), but the *way* it was done. "Ang galing ng `pagkakaimbestiga` ng NBI, nahuli agad ang salarin!" Or the opposite: "Ang gulo ng `pagkakaimbestiga`, walang linaw kung sino ang may kasalanan." It’s the behind-the-scenes CSI stuff, the process that leads to the "Case Closed" stamp.
usage_notes: Focuses on the quality, method, or result of the investigation process.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinuri ng hepe ang maayos na **pagkakaimbestiga** sa kaso.","translation":"The chief praised the orderly **manner of investigation** of the case."},{"sentence":"May mga duda sa naging **pagkakaimbestiga** ng mga pulis.","translation":"There are doubts about the **way the investigation was conducted** by the police."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang panahon ng kahinaan o kabagalan, lalo na sa negosyo, kalakalan, o benta.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "tumal" (sluggishness, dullness), na may unlaping "pa-" na nagpapahiwatig ng isang estado o panahon.
original_explanation: Eto yung "petsa de peligro" feels sa mga tindahan, pagkatapos ng sweldo at bago ang susunod. Yung walang masyadong customer at matamlay ang benta. Parang social life mo, may mga panahong **patumal** at walang ganap. It's the 'off-season' for business and sometimes, for life.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng negosyo at benta. Ang "matumal" ay ang mas karaniwang anyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panahon ng **patumal** ngayon kaya kakaunti ang bumibili.","translation":"It's a **slow season** now that's why few people are buying."},{"sentence":"Nalulugi ang negosyo dahil sa **patumal**.","translation":"The business is losing money because of the **sluggish sales**."}]

translation: to put a veil on someone/something
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapatong ng belo sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The action of putting the veil on. It's what the maid of honor does for the bride, or what you do to a santo during a religious procession. It's the verb form of making something (or someone) look mysterious or ready for a ceremony. This is the more common variant compared to 'beluhan'.
usage_notes: A verb derived from the noun 'belo'. 'Beluhan' is a less common variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **belohan** ang nobya bago siya lumabas.","translation":"Help me **put the veil on** the bride before she comes out."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **binelohan** ang imahen ng Birheng Maria.","translation":"He carefully **put a veil on** the statue of the Virgin Mary."}]

translation: to fight with someone; to quarrel
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsali o pakikilahok sa isang alitan o away sa ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is when you decide to throw down, verbally or physically. It's the "Tara, labas!" (Come on, let's take this outside!) energy. Not just being angry, but actively engaging in a conflict with someone, whether it's over a parking spot, the last piece of chicken, or because they saw your chat history.
usage_notes: Implies a reciprocal action, where both parties are involved in the fight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **makipag-away** sa iyo dahil lang sa maliit na bagay.","translation":"I don't want to **fight with you** over something so small."},{"sentence":"Laging handa siyang **makipag-away** para sa kanyang mga prinsipyo.","translation":"He is always ready **to fight** for his principles."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha ng isang bagay mula sa iba na may kasunduang ibabalik ito sa takdang panahon. Ito ay ang nakaraang anyo ng pandiwang "hiram".
original_explanation: This is what you did with your friend's pen and never returned. It's what your sibling does with your clothes without asking. 'Hiniram ko lang' is the national excuse for 'I took it, and I might give it back... eventually.'
usage_notes: Past tense of "hiram" (to borrow).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hiniram** ko ang aklat na ito sa silid-aklatan kahapon.","translation":"I **borrowed** this book from the library yesterday."},{"sentence":"Ang payong na gamit mo, **hiniram** mo lang ba 'yan?","translation":"That umbrella you're using, did you just **borrow** it?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, paraan, o kasangkapan na ginagamit upang itaas ang isang bagay, o dagdagan ang antas, dami, o halaga nito.
original_explanation: The general term for anything that gives you a "lift." It could be a heel insert for the vertically-challenged, a growth supplement like Cherifer, or the yeast that makes your pandesal rise. In the office, it's that "pampataas ng morale" pizza party after a stressful week. In the market, it's the "pampataas ng presyo" due to inflation.
usage_notes: A very general term. Context is key. It can be for height, price, morale, level, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumagamit siya ng takong na **pampataas**.","translation":"She uses heels as a **height-booster**."},{"sentence":"Ang lebadura ay **pampataas** ng masa ng tinapay.","translation":"Yeast is a **leavening agent** for bread dough."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at malakas na pag-agos o paglabas ng likido mula sa isang makitid na bukasan.
etymology: From `pag-` + `pulandit`. `Pulandit` refers to a forceful spurt of liquid.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you shake a can of soda and then open it. Or when you try to get the last bit of ketchup out of the bottle and it suddenly explodes onto your white shirt. It's that uncontrolled, messy burst of liquid—be it water from a broken pipe, juice from a fruit, or tears of joy (or drama).
usage_notes: Describes a forceful and often messy ejection of liquid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat sa biglang **pagpulandit** ng tubig mula sa nasirang tubo.","translation":"Everyone was surprised by the sudden **gushing** of water from the broken pipe."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpulandit** ng dugo mula sa sugat ay tanda na kailangan itong lapatan agad ng lunas.","translation":"The **spurting** of blood from the wound is a sign that it needs immediate medical attention."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa bawat miyembro o bahagi ng isang pangkat nang paisa-isa.
original_explanation: This is the word you use when you want to make sure no one gets left behind, or when you're pointing out that *everyone* in the group chat saw your message but no one replied. "Bawa't isa sa inyo, seenzoned ako!" It's the ultimate tool for passive-aggressive attendance checking.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit bilang 'bawat isa'. Maaari ring palitan ng 'kada'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bawa't** tao ay may karapatan sa kaligayahan.","translation":"**Every** person has a right to happiness."},{"sentence":"Binigyan ko ng regalo **bawa't** bata.","translation":"I gave a gift to **each** child."}]

translation: to declaim in a poetic joust
meaning_filipino: Bigkasin o ilahad ang isang tula, katuwiran, o kaisipan sa paraang patula at madalas ay may kasamang debate, hango sa tradisyon ng Balagtasan.
etymology: Hango sa pangalan ni Francisco Balagtas, isang tanyag na Pilipinong makata.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino rap battle. Before FlipTop, there was Balagtasan. To 'balagtasin' is to spit bars, but make it romantic, metaphorical, and in formal Tagalog. It's arguing with someone through poetry, where the sickest burns are also the most beautifully worded.
usage_notes: Specifically used in the context of 'Balagtasan', a form of Filipino poetic debate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling siyang **balagtasin** ang mga katwiran ng panig na kanyang ipinagtatanggol.","translation":"He is good at **declaiming** the arguments of the side he is defending."},{"sentence":"Ang paksa tungkol sa pag-ibig ang madalas na pinipiling **balagtasin** sa entablado.","translation":"The topic of love is often chosen **to be debated poetically** on stage."}]

translation: to permit; to allow; to consent to
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng permiso o kapangyarihan sa isang tao o bagay na magpatuloy.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of getting that "go signal." It's what your strict tita finally does after you've explained for the 10th time why you need to go out past 10 PM. "Sige na, pinapahintulutan na kita." It's the moment of victory.
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb. The thing being permitted is the focus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko **pahihintulutan** ang ganitong klaseng pag-uugali sa aking pamamahay.","translation":"I will not **allow** this kind of behavior in my house."},{"sentence":"**Pahintulutan** mo sana akong ipaliwanag ang aking panig.","translation":"Please **permit** me to explain my side."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nanloloko o nandadaya, lalo na sa isang relasyon, laro, o pagsusulit.
original_explanation: The villain in every Filipino teleserye and countless real-life hugot stories. Someone who breaks trust, whether by having a "kabitserye" (a drama with a mistress) or by peeking at your test paper. The ultimate accusation that can start a world war in a relationship.
usage_notes: Used in the same context as in English, but with the added dramatic weight of Filipino relationship culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, **cheater** 'yan!","translation":"Don't believe him, he's a **cheater**!"},{"sentence":"Nahuli siyang may kodigo kaya tinawag siyang **cheater** ng guro.","translation":"He was caught with a cheat sheet so the teacher called him a **cheater**."}]

translation: to weigh; to balance; to consider
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsukat ng bigat ng isang bagay; maaari ring tumukoy sa metaporikal na pagsusuri o pag-iisip sa mga pagpipilian.
original_explanation: What you do literally at the palengke to make sure you're not getting ripped off on the price of chicken. Also what you do figuratively when choosing between saving money and ordering that 500-peso milk tea with extra pearls. You have to **tumimbang** the pros and cons (happiness vs. budget).
usage_notes: Has both a literal meaning (to weigh on a scale) and a figurative one (to weigh options, to consider).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **tumimbang** ng isang kilong bigas sa palengke.","translation":"She **weighed** one kilo of rice at the market."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **tumimbang** nang mabuti bago ka gumawa ng desisyon.","translation":"You need to **consider** carefully before you make a decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdanas at pagkalugod sa isang bagay na kanais-nais, karaniwang bunga ng isang karapatan o pinaghirapan.
original_explanation: Ito yung finally na-achieve mo na ang work-life balance at nine-enjoy mo na ang pinaghirapan mong sahod. Yung feeling na humihigop ka ng kape sa umaga, walang iniisip na deadline. You're not just getting by, you're *relishing* the moment. #SanaAll
usage_notes: Implies a deep sense of enjoyment and fulfillment, often with a sense of deserving it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtamasa** ng kalayaan ay karapatan ng bawat mamamayan.","translation":"The **enjoying** of freedom is the right of every citizen."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng maraming taon ng pagsisikap, nararapat lamang ang kanyang **pagtamasa** sa yaman.","translation":"After many years of hard work, his **relishing** of wealth is only just."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-aayos o pagkukumpuni sa mga punit o butas ng damit sa pamamagitan ng sinulid at karayom.
original_explanation: This is what your lola does to your favorite butas-butas na pambahay pants. It's the OG 'sustainable fashion' before it was cool. It’s the art of saving your 500-peso concert shirt from a tiny hole, extending its life until the next laundry cycle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat ang **panunulsi** ni Lola sa lumang medyas.","translation":"Grandma's **darning** of the old sock is careful."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng sinulid at karayom para sa **panunulsi** ng aking uniporme.","translation":"I need a needle and thread for **mending** my uniform."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong simple, walang arte, at prangka; payak sa kilos at pananalita.
original_explanation: Basically, 'what you see is what you get'. No filters, no pa-sosyal. Minsan medyo 'jologs' or 'baduy' ang dating, but in a raw, authentic way. 'Mas gusto ko siyang kausap, mas yano kasi, hindi maarte.'
usage_notes: Often used colloquially to describe a person's demeanor or style. Can be slightly negative (unsophisticated) or positive (unpretentious) depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit sikat na siya, nanatili siyang **yano** at mapagkumbaba.","translation":"Even though he is famous, he remained **simple** and humble."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong labis ang pagpapahalaga at paghahangad sa salapi; materyoso.
etymology: Mula sa "mukha" (face) at "kuwalta" (money). The face is metaphorically made of money, or only sees money.
original_explanation: The Tita who only shows up at family reunions when she knows there's 'pamana' being discussed. Or that 'friend' who's suddenly super nice when it's payday. They're not necessarily ugly, but their actions scream, "I'm only here for the money!"
usage_notes: A derogatory term for someone perceived as being obsessed with money.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw siyang makasama ng mga tao dahil sa pagiging **mukhang-kuwalta** niya.","translation":"People avoid his company because he is so **money-faced/greedy**."},{"sentence":"Puro materyal na bagay ang gusto niya, talagang **mukhang-kuwalta**.","translation":"She only wants material things, she's truly **materialistic**."}]

translation: to redden; to flush; to blush
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng kulay na nagiging pula o mamula-mula, lalo na ang mukha dahil sa hiya, galit, o init.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your cheeks when your crush says hi, or when your mom calls out your full name in the mall. It’s the body’s natural blush-on, powered by pure emotion.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'mamula'. Usually refers to the face.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilang **mamuka** ang mukha nang purihin siya sa harap ng lahat.","translation":"She couldn't stop her face from **reddening** when she was praised in front of everyone."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mamuka** ang kanyang mga mata dahil sa kakaiyak.","translation":"Her eyes started **to become red** from crying so much."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilabas ang hangin mula sa baga; ipahayag ang saloobin o problema upang gumaan ang pakiramdam.
original_explanation: Two meanings here. First, literally, to breathe out. 'Inhale, tapos ihinga.' Second, and more importantly for your mental health, it means to vent or get something off your chest. When your friend says, 'Ihinga mo lang 'yan,' they're giving you a safe space to unload all your drama, hugot, and work-related stress. It's therapeutic exhalation.
usage_notes: The figurative meaning of 'venting' is extremely common in modern conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ihinga** mo nang malalim para kumalma ka.","translation":"**Exhale** deeply to calm yourself down."},{"sentence":"Tumawag siya para **ihinga** ang lahat ng sama ng loob niya sa akin.","translation":"She called to **vent** all her frustrations to me."}]

translation: prone to mosquito bites; a place with many mosquitoes
meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging madaling kagatin ng lamok, o tumutukoy sa isang lugar na maraming lamok.
original_explanation: If you're the designated pulutan of mosquitoes in your barkada, you are 'lamukin'. You're the person who gets 10 bites while everyone else gets zero. It's also used for places, like that one friend's house near a canal that's basically the lamok version of a 5-star buffet.
usage_notes: Can describe a person ('sweet-blooded') or a place (infested with mosquitoes).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-lotion ka, **lamukin** ka pa naman.","translation":"Put on some lotion, you're **prone to mosquito bites**."},{"sentence":"Huwag tayong tumambay dito, masyadong **lamukin** ang lugar na ito.","translation":"Let's not hang out here, this place has **too many mosquitoes**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking sako na karaniwang gawa sa magaspang na tela tulad ng lona o sako, na ginagamit para sa pag-iimbak at pagbubuhat ng maramihang bagay tulad ng bigas, arina, o uling.
original_explanation: The heavyweight champion of bags. Before eco-bags became trendy, the 'kustal' was the original reusable bag. It's what carries a family's 50kg rice supply, your 'pamasko' from relatives in the province, or sometimes, even a person during a sack race.
usage_notes: Often used for bulk agricultural products. Largely synonymous with 'sako'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipasok mo ang mga uling sa loob ng **kustal**.","translation":"Put the charcoal inside the **sack**."},{"sentence":"Isang **kustal** ng bigas ang aming inuwi mula sa bukid.","translation":"We brought home one **sack** of rice from the farm."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng kawalan ng liwanag; ang pagiging madilim.
etymology: From ka- + dilim + -an, meaning the state or expanse of darkness.
original_explanation: The reason you stub your toe at night on the way to the CR. It's what happens during a brownout when you can't find the emergency light. Figuratively, it's the 'dark side'—the time of despair, ignorance, or evil. 'Nasa kadiliman ako' can mean 'I'm literally in the dark' or 'I'm going through a tough time.'
usage_notes: Used both literally for absence of light and figuratively for ignorance, evil, or despair.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang nawalan ng kuryente at napuno ng **kadiliman** ang buong bahay.","translation":"The power suddenly went out and the whole house was filled with **darkness**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating maging ilaw sa gitna ng **kadiliman** ng lipunan.","translation":"We need to be a light in the midst of society's **darkness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagya o paulit-ulit na paglalagay ng tubig o anumang likido sa isang bagay upang ito ay maging mamasa-masa.
etymology: From `basa` (wet) with reduplication of the first two syllables, indicating a lighter, less intense, or repeated action.
original_explanation: Like when you're trying to tame your tita hairdo in the morning and you just spritz a little water. Or when you're ironing clothes and you need to basa-basain the stubborn wrinkles. It's not a full-on "buhos", just a gentle sprinkle.
usage_notes: Differentiated from `basain` (to wet) by the repetition, which implies a lighter or more distributed application of liquid. The root word is 'basa' (wet).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakitandaan na **basa-basain** lang ang lupa ng halaman, huwag lunurin.","translation":"Please remember to just **lightly wet** the plant's soil, don't drown it."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **basa-basain** ang basahan bago ipunas sa mesa.","translation":"You need to **dampen** the rag before wiping the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tao, grupo, o institusyon na inihabla o kinasuhan sa isang korte; ang panig na sinasakdal.
original_explanation: Kung ikaw ang demandado, ikaw 'yung nasa hot seat. Ikaw 'yung may kaso. Ikaw 'yung kailangang mag-explain sa judge. You are the "defendant" in the legal telenovela of your life. Sila 'yung sinasabihan ng "Objection, your Honor!"
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the defendant in a civil or criminal case.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **demandado** ay hindi dumating sa pagdinig ng kaso.","translation":"The **defendant** did not show up for the case hearing."},{"sentence":"Sino ang abogado ng **demandado**?","translation":"Who is the lawyer of the **accused**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Sa balarila, isang salita na nag-uugnay sa isang pangngalan o panghalip sa ibang salita sa pangungusap, tulad ng 'sa', 'ng', 'para sa'.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga small but terrible words sa grammar: 'sa', 'ng', 'para sa', 'ayon sa'. Sila yung nagbibigay ng direksyon at relasyon sa mga salita. Kung walang **preposisyon**, parang Waze na walang signal ang pangungusap mo.
usage_notes: A grammatical term. In Filipino grammar, this is often referred to as 'pang-ukol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'sa' ay isang halimbawa ng **preposisyon** sa Filipino.","translation":"'Sa' (in/on/at) is an example of a **preposition** in Filipino."}]

translation: to endure, to bear, to tolerate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtitiis o pagtitiyaga sa isang mahirap na sitwasyon, sakit, o tao.
original_explanation: Your life motto during rush hour traffic, long meetings, or when dealing with a toxic boss. It's the Filipino superpower of 'tiis-ganda' or 'tiis-pogi' applied to everything. "Agwanta lang, bes, malapit na ang sahod!" is the national battle cry.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Maaaring banghayin tulad ng isang katutubong pandiwang Tagalog (hal. inaagwanta, agwantahin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **agwantahin** ang sakit para gumaling.","translation":"You need to **endure** the pain to get better."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko na **maagwanta** ang ugali niya.","translation":"I can no longer **tolerate** his attitude."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpindot at pagdiin nang paulit-ulit sa isang masa, karaniwan ay para sa paggawa ng tinapay, gamit ang mga kamay.
original_explanation: This is what you do to pandesal dough, not your stiff shoulders. It's that therapeutic (or exhausting) process of pressing, folding, and turning dough until it's smooth and elastic. Parang 'yung puso mong paulit-ulit sinaktan at minolde, pero naging matatag in the end. #HugotBaker
usage_notes: Not to be confused with 'masahihin' (to be massaged). The root word is 'masa' (dough).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **masahin** nang mabuti ang harina upang maging maganda ang tinapay.","translation":"The flour must **be kneaded** well to make good bread."},{"sentence":"**Masahin** mo ang dough hanggang sa hindi na ito dumidikit sa iyong mga kamay.","translation":"**Knead** the dough until it no longer sticks to your hands."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagkawala ng basa o halumigmig hanggang sa ito ay matuyo.
original_explanation: When your tears finally stop after watching a sad K-drama, 'yan, nagtuyo na. Or when you leave your wet swimsuit out in the sun. It's the opposite of 'basa.' Sometimes it also refers to your love life. Ouch.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang bagay na natutuyo nang kusa, o sa isang taong nagpapatuyo ng isang bagay. Ang konteksto ang susi. Halimbawa: 'Magtuyo ka ng buhok' (Dry your hair) vs. 'Hayaan mong magtuyo ang damit' (Let the clothes dry).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isampay mo ang damit sa labas para **magtuyo** sa ilalim ng araw.","translation":"Hang the clothes outside to **dry** under the sun."},{"sentence":"Hintayin nating **magtuyo** ang pintura bago natin galawin.","translation":"Let's wait for the paint to **dry** before we touch it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabangong bulaklak ng puno ng dalandan o kahel, na kadalasang ginagamit bilang palamuti sa kasal o sangkap sa pabango at pagkain.
original_explanation: This is that fancy, old-school word your lola might use for flowers. Think of the delicate white flowers on an orange tree, often used in traditional wedding bouquets. It’s the Tita-approved, "mabango at mahinhin" (fragrant and demure) scent, a classic that never goes out of style.
usage_notes: Primarily used in literary contexts or discussions about traditional weddings and perfumery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangkasal na korona ng nobya ay gawa sa sariwang **asahar**.","translation":"The bride's wedding crown was made of fresh **orange blossoms**."},{"sentence":"May banayad na halimuyak ng **asahar** ang kanyang pabango.","translation":"Her perfume has a gentle scent of **orange blossom**."}]

translation: to run (a distance/race); to run for (an office)
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakbay sa isang partikular na distansya sa pamamagitan ng pagtakbo; ang pagsali bilang kandidato sa isang halalan.
original_explanation: What you do when you're late for your shift, or what a politician does to get your vote. It's about covering a specific ground, whether it's 5km on a treadmill or a whole province during campaign season.
usage_notes: Verb in the object-focus form. The object is the thing being run (the distance, the race, the position).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kaya mo bang **takbuhin** ang sampung kilometro?","translation":"Can you **run** ten kilometers?"},{"sentence":"Plano niyang **takbuhin** ang posisyon ng pagka-alkalde sa susunod na eleksyon.","translation":"He plans to **run for** the position of mayor in the next election."}]

translation: to let pass; to overlook; to miss an opportunity
meaning_filipino: Hayaan na lumipas o dumaan nang hindi pinapansin o pinipigilan; hindi samantalahin ang isang pagkakataon.
original_explanation: This is when you decide not to engage in online drama, you just **palampasin** mo na lang. Or when you see a 50% off sale on an item you've been wanting, you can't **mapalampas** the opportunity. It's the art of choosing your battles and your bargains.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **palampasin** ang pagkakataong makasama ang iyong pamilya.","translation":"Don't **let the opportunity pass** to be with your family."},{"sentence":"Kahit masakit ang sinabi niya, minabuti ko na lang na **palampasin** iyon.","translation":"Even though what he said was hurtful, I just chose **to let it pass**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang serye ng siyam na misa sa madaling-araw na idinaraos bago ang Pasko, mula Disyembre 16 hanggang 24. Kilala rin bilang Simbang Gabi o Misa de Gallo.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'misa de aguinaldo' ('misa ng regalo').
original_explanation: Another name for Simbang Gabi. It's that 9-day spiritual marathon before Christmas that requires you to wake up at 3 AM. The "Aginaldo" part hints at the "gift" (the birth of Jesus), but for most of us, the real aginaldo is the bibingka and puto bumbong waiting outside the church.
usage_notes: Maaaring ipagpalit sa Simbang Gabi at Misa de Gallo. Ito ay isang uri ng votive Mass para sa Birheng Maria.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumpleto na ba ang siyam na araw mo ng **Misa Aginaldo**?","translation":"Have you completed your nine days of **Aguinaldo Mass**?"},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng **Misa Aginaldo**, diretso kami sa kainan ng puto bumbong.","translation":"After the **Aguinaldo Mass**, we go straight to eat puto bumbong."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahinang tunog na likha ng paggalaw ng mga tuyong dahon, papel, o tela.
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung tunog na naririnig mo sa gabi kapag mag-isa ka lang sa bahay at biglang may dumaang pusa sa basurahan. O kaya 'yung sound ng plastic ng chichirya na pilit mong binubuksan nang dahan-dahan para walang makarinig. That subtle, crinkling, rustling sound that makes you ask, "Sino 'yan?!"
usage_notes: Often associated with light, dry, or stealthy movements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May narinig akong **kaluskos** sa may kusina.","translation":"I heard a **rustling sound** from the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Ang **kaluskos** ng mga dahon ang tanging maririnig sa gubat.","translation":"The **rustling** of the leaves was the only thing audible in the forest."}]

meaning_filipino: Mula sa Koreanong salita na nangangahulugang "sino?". Sa konteksto ng K-Pop, tumutukoy ito sa isang grupo o artist na hindi pa sikat o kilala ng karamihan.
original_explanation: From the Korean word 누구 (nugu), meaning "who?". In the world of K-Pop stans, this is the term for a group that's so unknown you literally have to ask, "Who?". It's not necessarily an insult, more of a descriptor for groups from small companies struggling to make it big. "Besh, may bagong group na nag-debut, pero medyo **nugu** pa."
usage_notes: Used almost exclusively by K-Pop fans.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **nugu** groups ang umaasang sumikat balang araw.","translation":"Many **unknown** groups are hoping to become famous someday."},{"sentence":"Dati silang **nugu**, pero ngayon, sikat na sila sa buong mundo.","translation":"They used to be **unknown**, but now, they are famous worldwide."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasama o kabahagi sa isang debate o pagtatalo.
etymology: From ka- (denoting a companion or partner) + debate (from Spanish 'debate').
original_explanation: Your partner-in-crime sa bardagulan. Yung kasama mong mag-isip ng arguments, rebuttals, at kung paano niyo i-roast yung kabilang team sa school debate. Pwede ring co-worker mo na laging may 'what if' at 'actually' sa bawat suggestion mo sa meeting.
usage_notes: A modern, informal construction common in Filipino where `ka-` is prefixed to a noun (often a loanword) to mean 'fellow X' or 'co-X'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang naging **kadebate** ko sa huling kompetisyon.","translation":"She was my **debate partner** in the last competition."},{"sentence":"Laging mainit ang usapan namin ng **kadebate** kong si Marco.","translation":"The discussion between me and my **fellow debater** Marco is always heated."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng halaman na karaniwang nasa ilalim ng lupa, sumisipsip ng tubig at sustansya; ang mga daluyan ng dugo sa katawan; o ang pinagmulan o sanhi ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Ugat is the OG, the source code, the foundation. Sa halaman, it's what keeps it from falling over. Sa katawan mo, it's the "expressway" for your blood (veins). Sa chismis, ito 'yung "root cause" ng buong drama. When you're looking for the "ugat" of a problem, you're playing detective to find out where it all started.
usage_notes: A versatile word with literal (botany, anatomy) and figurative (origin, cause) meanings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malalim ang **ugat** ng punong narra kaya matatag ito.","translation":"The narra tree's **roots** are deep, which is why it is sturdy."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang mga **ugat** sa kanyang braso.","translation":"The **veins** on his arm are very visible."},{"sentence":"Ano kaya ang **ugat** ng kanilang pag-aaway?","translation":"I wonder what the **origin** of their fight is?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na salita na nangangahulugang nakakainis, nakakagalit, o nakakabuwisit sa sukdulan.
etymology: From `nakaka-` (causative prefix) + `kabayo` (horse). The origin is speculative, possibly related to being driven mad or the frantic/crazy movements of a horse.
original_explanation: This is a level of annoyance beyond 'nakakainis.' This is when your internet dies mid-game, when someone cuts you in line at the bank, or when a Grab driver cancels after you've waited 15 minutes. It's rage-inducing. The term supposedly comes from the idea that the situation is so frustrating it could drive even a horse (kabayo) crazy.
usage_notes: Highly informal and slang. Not to be used in formal writing or speech. It literally means 'makes one a horse' but idiomatically means infuriating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakakabayo** talaga ang traffic sa EDSA tuwing rush hour!","translation":"The traffic on EDSA during rush hour is really **maddening**!"},{"sentence":"Yung paulit-ulit na tanong niya, **nakakabayo** na!","translation":"His repetitive questions are becoming **infuriating**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magiging bunga o resulta ng isang kilos, gawain, o pangyayari.
etymology: A future-tense form of the verb 'lumabas' (to come out), used as a noun. From ka- + la- (reduplicated first syllable of root) + labas + -an.
original_explanation: This is the 'final reveal' or the 'consequences of your actions.' When your mom says, 'Bahala ka sa kalalabasan niyan,' she's basically saying 'You'll face the music,' whether that's a failed project, a bad grade, or getting caught sneaking out. It's the ultimate 'what happens next'.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to the future result of a current action or situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano kaya ang **kalalabasan** ng eleksyon sa susunod na taon?","translation":"I wonder what the **outcome** of the election will be next year."},{"sentence":"Pinag-iisipan niya ang maaaring **kalalabasan** ng kanyang desisyon.","translation":"He is thinking about the possible **consequences** of his decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng komunikasyon na ginagamit sa loob ng isang gusali o sasakyan, na nagpapahintulot sa pakikipag-usap sa pagitan ng iba't ibang silid o lokasyon.
original_explanation: The official sound system of condos, offices, and schools. It's how the school principal announces a surprise class suspension, or how the condo guard tells you, 'Ma'am/Sir, may delivery po kayo ng Shopee,' for the third time this week. It's basically a one-way radio for important (or not-so-important) announcements.
usage_notes: Commonly found in modern buildings and some vehicles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko sa **intercom** na may bisita ako sa lobby.","translation":"I heard on the **intercom** that I have a visitor in the lobby."},{"sentence":"Tawagin mo si Ana gamit ang **intercom**.","translation":"Call Ana using the **intercom**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginamit ang mga paa upang gumalaw mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba; tapos nang isagawa ang paglalakad.
etymology: The 'nag-' prefix marks the completed aspect (past tense) of the root 'lakad'.
original_explanation: What you did when the jeepney was full, the Grab fare was surging, and you were trying to save money. '**Naglakad** na lang ako pauwi mula sa opisina.' It's also what you did to process your 'hugot' feels while listening to sad OPM songs.
usage_notes: The completed aspect (past tense) of 'maglakad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naglakad** kami sa parke noong Linggo.","translation":"We **walked** in the park last Sunday."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa traffic, mas mabilis pa siyang nakarating dahil **naglakad** lang siya.","translation":"Because of the traffic, he arrived faster because he just **walked**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit at matamis na sitrus, na may manipis na balat na madaling talupan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "naranjita" (maliit na kahel).
original_explanation: The smaller, cuter, and usually sweeter cousin of the dalandan. It's the "easy mode" citrus fruit – madaling balatan, walang masyadong buto, and perfectly bite-sized. This is the go-to baon for kids. Think of it as the dalandan's more refined, less-sour sibling.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'sintunis' sa ilang rehiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas matamis ang **dalanghita** kaysa sa dalandan.","translation":"The **tangerine** is sweeter than the native orange."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi siya ng isang supot ng **dalanghita** bilang pasalubong.","translation":"He brought home a bag of **mandarin oranges** as a souvenir."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagkakaroon ng dalawang bahagi na magkatulad o magkatugma sa sukat, hugis, at posisyon sa magkabilang panig ng isang linya o gitnang punto.
original_explanation: What your barber is aiming for but sometimes misses. What you want for your 'kilay' but end up with 'sisters, not twins.' It's that satisfying feeling when everything is perfectly balanced, like a well-made leche flan or when the two sides of your crush's face are equally gorgeous.
usage_notes: A more technical or academic term. 'Balanse' or 'pantay' is used more often in daily conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa sining ang **simetria** ng mga disenyo.","translation":"The **symmetry** of designs is studied in art."},{"sentence":"Kahanga-hanga ang **simetria** sa arkitektura ng lumang simbahan.","translation":"The **symmetry** in the architecture of the old church is admirable."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng sukat para sa masa sa sistemang metriko, katumbas ng isang libong gramo. Ito ang pormang hango sa wikang Espanyol.
original_explanation: The more 'classic' or Spanish-sounding version of kilogram. You might hear this more from your lola or in older textbooks. It's the 'tisoy' cousin of the more Americanized 'kilogram'. Both will get you a kilo of tilapia at the palengke.
usage_notes: Less common than 'kilogram' or the shortened 'kilo' in modern speech, but still understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pamantayang bigat ay isang **kilogramo** ng platino-iridyo na nakatago sa Pransya.","translation":"The standard weight is one **kilogram** of platinum-iridium stored in France."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang **kilogramo** ng baboy.","translation":"Mother bought one **kilogram** of pork."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging balisa, hindi mapakali, o maligalig, na karaniwang ipinapakita sa pamamagitan ng patuloy na paggalaw.
original_explanation: Yung feeling mo kapag nag-text si crush ng "we need to talk" tapos hindi na nag-reply. O 'yung pakiramdam habang naghihintay ng resulta ng exam. Hindi ka mapirmi sa isang lugar, paikot-ikot ka lang.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng estado ng pagkabalisa sa isip o katawan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **alumihit** ang bata dahil sa taas ng lagnat.","translation":"The child became **restless** due to the high fever."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka ba **alumihit** diyan? May problema ba?","translation":"Why are you so **agitated** over there? Is there a problem?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at malakas na tunog ng isang bagay na dumaraan, tulad ng hangin, bala, o sasakyan.
original_explanation: Think of the sound an LBC delivery motorcycle makes when it zooms past your house, or the *whoosh* of the MRT when you're standing a little too close to the yellow line. That's hagunot. It's speed you can hear.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the sound of wind, fast-moving vehicles, or projectiles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **hagunot** ng hangin bago bumuhos ang malakas na ulan.","translation":"I heard the **swoosh** of the wind before the heavy rain poured."},{"sentence":"Ang **hagunot** ng mabilis na kotse ay gumising sa buong kapitbahayan.","translation":"The **whizz** of the fast car woke up the entire neighborhood."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao o sa isang pagkilos na tila hindi nakararamdam ng pagod o patuloy na ginagawa ang isang bagay nang walang hinto.
original_explanation: This is your BPO friend working the graveyard shift, then going to the gym, then meeting up for coffee, all while running an online business. They're an energizer bunny powered by coffee and dreams of a 13th-month pay. They work with **tireless** effort.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ipahayag ang paghanga sa lakas, dedikasyon, o walang-humpay na pagsisikap ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtrabaho siya nang **walang-pagkapagod** para matustusan ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He worked **tirelessly** to provide for his family."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **walang-pagkapagod** na dedikasyon sa sining ay kahanga-hanga.","translation":"His **indefatigable** dedication to art is admirable."}]

meaning_filipino: Tubig na may asin at iba pang sangkap na inilalabas ng katawan sa pamamagitan ng balat, karaniwan dahil sa init o pagod.
original_explanation: The body's natural air conditioning system, especially useful during a commute in a non-airconditioned jeepney at noon. It's the 'glow' you get after climbing five flights of stairs because the elevator is broken. Also a metaphor for hard work: 'dugo't pawis' (blood and sweat).
usage_notes: Can be used literally for perspiration or figuratively for effort.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumatagaktak ang **pawis** niya pagkatapos tumakbo.","translation":"His **sweat** was dripping after running."},{"sentence":"Ang bahay na ito ay bunga ng aming dugo't **pawis**.","translation":"This house is the fruit of our blood and **sweat**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang siyang nangingibabaw, namumukod-tangi, o may pinakamalaking impluwensya sa isang partikular na lugar, panahon, o sitwasyon.
etymology: From nakapang- (a variant of nakapag-) + pamamayani (the state of prevailing), which comes from the root 'yani' (sway, influence).
original_explanation: This is the 'main character' energy. It's the K-Pop group that's topping all the charts, the 'unli-rice' culture in a Filipino restaurant, or the 'hugot' culture on social media. It's whatever is currently the king, the one that dominates the scene.
usage_notes: A formal and literary word used to describe a dominant force, idea, feeling, or atmosphere.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa huli, ang kabutihan pa rin ang **nakapamamayani**.","translation":"In the end, goodness still **prevails**."},{"sentence":"Ang diwa ng Pasko ang **nakapamamayani** sa buong kapuluan tuwing Disyembre.","translation":"The Christmas spirit is what's **predominant** throughout the archipelago every December."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumilos o magbago ng posisyon, lugar, o kalagayan.
etymology: From the root 'galaw' (movement) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: The most basic action. From getting up in the morning to your 'torpe' friend finally making a move on their crush. 'Bes, gumalaw ka na, baka maunahan ka pa!' Also what your boss tells you when you're just staring at your screen pretending to work.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **gumalaw** habang kinukuhanan kita ng litrato.","translation":"Don't **move** while I'm taking your picture."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman kong **gumalaw** ang lupa noong lumindol.","translation":"I felt the ground **move** when the earthquake hit."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nililikha ng isang aso; tahol.
original_explanation: It's the sound a dog makes. The Filipino version of "woof woof" or "bow-wow." You use this when talking to babies or when imitating a dog. "Anong sabi ng aso? Aw! Aw!" The more formal term is 'tahol', but 'aw-aw' is cuter.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal speech, when talking to children, or for onomatopoeic effect. The formal word is "tahol" (bark).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **aw-aw** ng aso sa labas.","translation":"I heard the dog's **bark** outside."},{"sentence":"Itinuro niya sa bata, 'Ang aso ay nagsasabing **aw-aw**.'","translation":"She taught the child, 'The dog says **woof-woof**.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa "Mobile Legends: Bang Bang," ang buong pangalan ng isang kilalang larong online na Multiplayer Online Battle Arena (MOBA).
original_explanation: The full government name of "ML". You use this when you want to sound a bit more formal, or when you're explaining to your tita what game is eating up all your time and data allowance.
usage_notes: The more complete acronym for the game Mobile Legends.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bagong update sa **MLBB** ngayong linggo.","translation":"There's a new update to **MLBB** this week."},{"sentence":"Sumali sila sa isang **MLBB** tournament.","translation":"They joined an **MLBB** tournament."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na labis ang pagiging malikot, mapagbiro, o may pahiwatig ng paglalandi sa kilos o pananalita.
original_explanation: This is the human equivalent of a hyperactive puppy. It can mean a kid who can't sit still (malikot) or an adult who's a little *too* friendly and touchy-feely (malandi). When someone is being maharot, there's a playful, sometimes flirty, energy that can be either charming or annoying, depending on who's doing it and who's receiving it. It's the 'ang kulit mo!' that comes with a little side-eye.
usage_notes: The meaning can range from innocent mischievousness (for children) to flirtatious behavior (for adults). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sawayin mo nga ang anak mo, napaka-**maharot** at ayaw tumigil sa pagtakbo.","translation":"Please tell your child to behave, he's so **mischievous** and won't stop running."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa opisina bilang isang taong **maharot** at palakaibigan.","translation":"She's known in the office as a **flirtatious** and friendly person."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalis o pagpapakalma sa isang bagay na matindi, tulad ng uhaw, pagod, sakit, o alaala.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative) + pawi (erase, vanish). Lit. 'the act of causing to vanish'.
original_explanation: Yung pag-inom mo ng malamig na soft drinks after maglakad sa ilalim ng araw—that's 'pagpapawi ng uhaw'. Yung pag-scroll mo sa TikTok for 3 hours para makalimot sa problema—that's 'pagpapawi ng isipin'. It's the act of getting rid of a 'thirst', whether literal or figurative.
usage_notes: Commonly used for thirst (uhaw), fatigue (pagod), sorrow (lungkot), or hunger (gutom).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabisang pampalipas-oras at **pagpapawi** ng pagod ang paghahardin.","translation":"Gardening is an effective way to pass the time and for the **alleviation** of fatigue."},{"sentence":"Ang malamig na tubig ay para sa **pagpapawi** ng kanilang uhaw.","translation":"The cold water is for **quenching** their thirst."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aabot, pagkakaloob, o paghahandog ng isang bagay na naisagawa na.
original_explanation: Past tense of giving. Your friend **nagbigay** ng unsolicited advice. Your crush **nagbigay** ng mixed signals. The ATM **nagbigay** ng pera. It's the completed act of handing something over, whether it's a gift, a problem, or cash.
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense) of 'magbigay'. This is the most common meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagbigay** siya ng bulaklak sa kanyang ina.","translation":"He **gave** flowers to his mother."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagbigay** sa iyo niyan?","translation":"Who **gave** that to you?"}]

translation: to court; to appease; to win over
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng pagmamahal, paglalambing, o pagbibigay-pabor upang makuha ang loob o pagsang-ayon ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'panliligaw' move. It's when you bring flowers, write poems, or even just buy them their favorite milk tea to win their heart. It can also be what you do to your boss before asking for a day off, or to your mom after you *sumuway*. It’s all about the charm offensive.
usage_notes: A verb in the completed aspect (past tense), actor-focus. The root 'suyo' means to curry favor or to woo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumuyo** siya sa dalaga sa pamamagitan ng harana.","translation":"He **courted** the young lady with a serenade."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **sumuyo** sa aking asawa dahil nagtampo siya sa akin.","translation":"I need to **appease** my wife because she's upset with me."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magdulot ng kadiliman o maging sanhi ng pagkawala ng liwanag.
original_explanation: When something blocks the light, literally or figuratively. It could be thick clouds covering the sun, or a lie that obscures the truth. "Yung mga dambuhalang building sa BGC, nakakadilim ng view."
usage_notes: Often used in a literal sense, but can also be used metaphorically for things that obscure understanding or hope.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang makapal na usok mula sa sunog ay **nakadilim** sa buong kalangitan.","translation":"The thick smoke from the fire **caused darkness** across the whole sky."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga kasinungalingan ay **nakadilim** sa katotohanan.","translation":"His lies **obscured** the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Gamitin ang isang bagay upang takpan o pagtakpan ang iba pa.
original_explanation: The action of using something to cover another. Think putting a lid on a pot of sinigang, or using concealer to hide a pimple. It's your go-to move when you need to hide something in plain sight. "Girl, itakip mo na yang libro sa mukha mo, andyan na si crush!"
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb. The object being used to cover is the focus of the sentence (e.g., 'Itakip mo ang panyo' - 'Use the handkerchief to cover'). The thing being covered is indicated by 'sa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **itakip** ang kumot sa bata?","translation":"Can you **cover** the child with the blanket?"},{"sentence":"Kinuha niya ang takip ng kaldero at **itinakip** ito.","translation":"He took the pot lid and **used it to cover**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa maraming pagkakataon; madalas mangyari o gawin.
original_explanation: This is the more formal cousin of 'madalas.' You use it when you want to sound a bit more polished, like in a school report or a formal email to your boss. 'Kalimitan, traffic sa EDSA' sounds slightly more intellectual than 'Madalas, traffic sa EDSA,' even though they mean the exact same frustrating thing.
usage_notes: Maaaring ipagpalit sa 'madalas' ngunit mas pormal ang dating. Ang 'limit' ay hindi isang malayang salitang Tagalog ngunit nagsisilbing konseptuwal na ugat nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kalimitan** ay umuulan tuwing hapon sa buwan ng Agosto.","translation":"**Often**, it rains in the afternoon during the month of August."},{"sentence":"Ang mga Pilipino ay **kalimitan** nang mapagpatuloy sa mga bisita.","translation":"Filipinos are **usually** hospitable to guests."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsisimula o pag-umpisa ng isang gawain, pangyayari, o proseso.
original_explanation: This is the "go signal" word. Like when your team lead says, "Okay guys, simulan na natin ang meeting," and everyone suddenly pretends to have been working the whole time. It's the opposite of "sana all tapos na."
usage_notes: The -an suffix makes it an object-focused verb, meaning the action is done *to* something. `Simulan mo na ang pagkain` (Start eating the food).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Simulan** na natin ang programa bago pa umulan.","translation":"Let's **start** the program before it rains."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **simulan** ang pag-aaral kung laging puyat.","translation":"It's hard **to start** studying if you're always sleep-deprived."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panahon sa pagitan ng hatinggabi at pagsikat ng araw; bukang-liwayway.
etymology: Pinagsamang 'madali' (sa diwa ng 'malapit na') at 'araw'. Literal na 'malapit nang umaraw'.
original_explanation: The official 'get up for your flight' or 'start of Simbang Gabi' time. It's that magical hour when BPO agents are clocking out, bakers are starting their pandesal, and you're questioning your life choices while cramming for an exam.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'bukang-liwayway'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umuwi siya ng **madaling-araw** kaya nagalit ang kanyang ina.","translation":"He came home at **dawn**, so his mother got angry."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula silang maglakad paakyat ng bundok nang **madaling-araw** pa lamang.","translation":"They started walking up the mountain while it was still **daybreak**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan na walang ingay, gulo, o anumang nakakabulahaw. Tumutukoy din sa isang taong hindi palasalita o mahinahon.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang mula sa isang salitang-ugat na may kaugnayan sa kapayapaan o kawalang-kibo.
original_explanation: Ito yung state of being na hinahanap mo pagkatapos ng isang magulong araw sa EDSA o sa office. Yung moment na walang maingay na kapitbahay na nagvi-videoke. Pwede ring description sa friend mong introvert na mas gustong mag-observe kesa mag-participate sa chismisan. 'A tahimik life is a happy life,' sabi ng mga Tita.
usage_notes: Maaaring ilarawan ang isang lugar, sitwasyon, o personalidad ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap matulog sa isang **tahimik** na kwarto.","translation":"It's nice to sleep in a **quiet** room."},{"sentence":"Siya ay isang **tahimik** na tao, ngunit malalim mag-isip.","translation":"He is a **quiet** person, but a deep thinker."}]

meaning_filipino: Naaayon sa karaniwan, pamantayan, o inaasahang kalagayan; hindi kakaiba o katangi-tangi.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Español at Ingles na 'normal'.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, 'normal' is anything but. It's the traffic, the heat, the political drama, the 5-in-1 coffee. When you ask someone 'Kumusta?' and they say 'Normal lang,' it means they're surviving the beautiful chaos of daily Pinoy life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumalik na sa **normal** ang operasyon ng LRT pagkatapos ng aberya.","translation":"The LRT's operation has returned to **normal** after the glitch."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, **normal** lang na mag-ulam ng kanin sa almusal.","translation":"For him, it's just **normal** to have rice with a viand for breakfast."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng mga gas na bumabalot sa isang planeta tulad ng daigdig; maaari ring tumukoy sa pangkalahatang pakiramdam o 'mood' ng isang lugar.
original_explanation: "Atmospera" is a two-for-one deal. First, it's the science-y thing that keeps us from floating into space. But more importantly, it's the *vibe*. When your friend's house is awkward during a family fight, "ang bigat ng atmospera." When you're at a concert and everyone's singing along, "ang ganda ng atmospera." It's the invisible feeling in a room that tells you whether to have fun or to slowly back away.
usage_notes: Can be used both in a scientific context (atmosphere) and a figurative one to mean 'ambiance' or 'mood'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang polusyon ay nakakasira sa **atmospera** ng mundo.","translation":"Pollution damages the world's **atmosphere**."},{"sentence":"Gumaan ang **atmospera** nang magsimula siyang magpatawa.","translation":"The **atmosphere** lightened when he started making jokes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng tunog na katangian ng isang pusa; pagngiyaw.
original_explanation: What that stray cat outside your window does at 3 AM. Or what you do to get the attention of a cute cat at the park. "**Mag-iingaw** ka para pansinin ka niya." It's the universal language for "Pspspspsps."
usage_notes: Ito ay maaaring gamitin bilang pawatas (infinitive) o aspektong panghinaharap. Ang 'umingaw' o 'ngumingaw' ay mas karaniwang ginagamit, ngunit ito ay naiintindihan pa rin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag gutom ang alaga kong pusa, nagsisimula itong **mag-iingaw** nang malakas.","translation":"When my pet cat is hungry, it starts to **meow** loudly."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, baka **mag-iingaw** ang mga kuting.","translation":"Don't be noisy, the kittens might **meow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pagkain ng bungang ubas.
original_explanation: What you do on New Year's Eve, trying to stuff 12 grapes in your mouth for good luck. Or what you do when you're feeling fancy and want a healthy snack. 'Tara, mag-ubas tayo habang nanonood ng Netflix.'
usage_notes: Isang di-gaanong karaniwang pandiwa dahil mas madalas sabihin ng mga tao ang 'kumain ng ubas'. Ang paggamit ng `mag-ubas` ay isang mas direktang paraan, bagaman hindi gaanong madalas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap **mag-ubas** kapag malamig ito galing sa pridyider.","translation":"It's nice **to eat grapes** when they're cold from the fridge."},{"sentence":"Sino ang gustong **mag-ubas** para sa meryenda?","translation":"Who wants **to eat grapes** for a snack?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na madaling masira, hindi matatag, o mahina ang pagkakagawa.
original_explanation: Like that cheap charger you bought from a tiangge that broke after a week. Or a promise from a "paasa" friend. It's anything that lacks strength and durability, whether it's a physical object or a commitment. "Made in China" stereotype, but make it a Tagalog adjective.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical objects and abstract concepts like relationships or promises.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang bibili ng sapatos na **walang-tibay** dahil masisira lang agad.","translation":"Don't buy shoes that are **not durable** because they will just break immediately."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang pagkakaibigan ay napatunayang **walang-tibay**.","translation":"Their friendship proved to be **fragile**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasangkapan o lugar na partikular na ginagamit sa pagpipirito ng pagkain.
etymology: From 'pirito' (or 'prito') + '-han' suffix, indicating a place or tool for the action.
original_explanation: This is the arena where the magic happens. The battlefield where mantika and your ulam meet. It can be your trusty kawali or the whole corner of the kitchen that smells like, well, pirituhan.
usage_notes: Can refer to both the pan ('kawali') or the general area. 'Prituhan' is also a valid verb form (to fry something for someone), but the noun usage is common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilinis ang **pirituhan** pagkatapos mong gamitin.","translation":"Please clean the **frying pan** after you use it."},{"sentence":"Ang kusina ay naging isang maingay na **pirituhan** tuwing may handaan.","translation":"The kitchen became a noisy **place for frying** during feasts."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagiging nag-iisa o bukod-tangi; walang iba o walang kasama.
etymology: From 'isa' (one), with reduplication of the first syllable to add emphasis.
original_explanation: When it's just one. "Bakit iisa lang ang laman ng Pringles can ko?!" It's that feeling of singularity. Can be romantic ("iisang pag-ibig"), tragic ("iisang bala"), or just plain annoying ("iisang piraso na lang ng chicken nugget?!"). It emphasizes the "oneness".
usage_notes: This is an adjective derived from the number 'isa' (one). The reduplication 'i-i' adds emphasis, meaning "one and only" or "just one."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iisa** lang ang pangarap ko sa buhay: ang yumaman.","translation":"I have **only one** dream in life: to get rich."},{"sentence":"Nag-away pa sila kahit **iisa** lang naman ang kanilang layunin.","translation":"They still fought even though they had the **same** (sole) goal."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at pansamantalang silid o espasyo na karaniwang may partisyon, tulad ng isang tolda o isang maliit na kwarto sa loob ng isang mas malaking lugar.
original_explanation: Think of a VIP room in a prison, a small booth at a trade fair, or a makeshift tent. A `kubol` is any small, enclosed, often temporary space. It became infamous in news reports referring to the surprisingly luxurious "cubicles" or cells some inmates build for themselves in Bilibid Prison.
usage_notes: Nagkaroon ng negatibong konotasyon dahil sa pagkakaugnay nito sa mga iligal na istruktura sa loob ng mga bilangguan sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita sa balita ang mga mararangyang **kubol** sa loob ng pambansang bilangguan.","translation":"The luxurious **cubicles** inside the national penitentiary were seen on the news."},{"sentence":"Nagtayo sila ng **kubol** sa perya para sa kanilang mga paninda.","translation":"They set up a **booth** at the fair for their merchandise."}]

translation: To walk on a tightrope or a narrow path; to traverse a bridge
meaning_filipino: Ang maingat na paglakad o pagtawid sa isang makitid na daanan, tulad ng alambre, lubid, o tulay na kawayan.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping 'man-' at salitang-ugat na 'tulay'.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'the floor is lava'. Remember crossing a log over a stream ('kanal') in the province? That's you, trying to **manulay**. It's all about balance and not falling. Figuratively, it’s what you do every payday: carefully navigating your budget until the next 'sweldo', trying not to fall into the pit of debt.
usage_notes: Ang pandiwang ito ay hindi kasing-karaniwan ng 'tumulay' o 'tumawid sa tulay' ngunit naiintindihan, lalo na sa mga kontekstong pampanitikan o probinsyal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakabahan siyang **manulay** sa makitid na tulay na kawayan.","translation":"He was nervous to **traverse** the narrow bamboo bridge."},{"sentence":"Ang mga sirkero ay sanay **manulay** sa alambre.","translation":"The circus performers are used to **walking on a tightrope**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kabinet, bakod, o harang na yari sa pinagtagpi-tagping alambre o wire mesh.
original_explanation: Think of it as the "screen door" of the Filipino kitchen. It's that wire mesh cabinet where you keep food safe from flies and other uninvited guests (like your sneaky cousin trying to get a piece of the fried chicken before dinner). The alambrera is the low-tech, pre-refrigerator way of keeping your ulam secure.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a structure made of wire mesh, most commonly a food safe or pamingganan (dish rack). It can also mean a wire fence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itago mo ang tinapay sa loob ng **alambrera** para hindi langgamin.","translation":"Keep the bread inside the **wire mesh cabinet** so ants won't get to it."},{"sentence":"Naglagay sila ng **alambrera** sa bintana para hindi makapasok ang mga lamok.","translation":"They installed a **wire screen** on the window to prevent mosquitoes from entering."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng plastik na gawa mula sa nitrocellulose at camphor, na dating malawakang ginagamit sa paggawa ng pelikula at mga potograpiya.
original_explanation: The OG material for movies before everything went digital. This is the stuff that made FPJ and Dolphy's classics possible. When old-timers talk about 'the magic of celluloid,' they're referring to the actual film strip. Think of it as the physical ancestor of your Netflix stream. It's flammable, fragile, and smells like history.
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically to refer to cinema or the film industry itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming luma at makasaysayang pelikula ang nakaimbak pa rin sa **seluloid**.","translation":"Many old and historic films are still stored on **celluloid**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bituin ng **seluloid** noong araw ay may kakaibang karisma.","translation":"The stars of the **celluloid** back in the day had a unique charisma."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mataas na antas ng husay, kakayahan, o kalidad sa isang partikular na larangan o gawain.
original_explanation: This is the 'sana all' of skills. When someone's so good at something—singing, dancing, coding, cooking adobo—you just shake your head and say, 'Ang galing!' It's the opposite of 'pwede na 'yan.' This is the level you want to be at to impress your crush, your boss, or your tita who always asks when you're getting married.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective (magaling) or as a noun (ang galing). The word 'galing' by itself is often used as an exclamation of praise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wow, ang **galing** mo talagang sumayaw!","translation":"Wow, you're really **excellent** at dancing!"},{"sentence":"Ipinamalas niya ang kanyang **galing** sa pagpipinta.","translation":"She showed off her **skill** in painting."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi maikukumpara o maitutulad sa iba; natatangi at bukod-tangi.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate compliment. It's what you say about your mom's cooking, the beauty of a Palawan sunset, or Regine Velasquez's whistle register. It's something so unique and amazing, nothing else can even come close. "Bes, ang galing mo, walang-kahalintulad!"
usage_notes: Isang mabisang salita na ginagamit para sa matinding papuri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal ng isang ina ay **walang-kahalintulad**.","translation":"A mother's love is **incomparable**."},{"sentence":"Nagpakita siya ng tapang na **walang-kahalintulad** sa gitna ng panganib.","translation":"He showed **unparalleled** bravery in the face of danger."}]

translation: to bristle, to stand on end (for hair/fur)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtayo o pagtaas ng mga balahibo sa katawan, karaniwan dahil sa takot, ginaw, o galit.
original_explanation: When you're watching a horror movie alone at 3 AM and you hear a sound from the kitchen, that's when your balahibo will 'bumalukag.' It's your body's built-in 'OMG, is that a multo?' alarm system.
usage_notes: Primarily used for hair or fur standing on end due to a strong emotion or cold.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumalukag** ang mga balahibo ko sa batok nang marinig ko ang iyak.","translation":"The hair on the back of my neck **bristled** when I heard the cry."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding ginaw, **bumalukag** ang balahibo ng pusa.","translation":"Because of the intense cold, the cat's fur **stood on end**."}]

translation: state of being startled or shocked
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkabigla o pagka-gulat dahil sa isang hindi inaasahang pangyayari, tunog, o kilos.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'ka-', ugat na 'gitla' (gulat, bigla), at hulaping '-han'.
original_explanation: That mini heart attack you get when someone sneaks up behind you and yells "BOO!". Or when your phone, which you thought was on silent, suddenly rings at full volume during a meeting. It's the "Ay, kabayo!" moment. Less about terror (kagiklahanan) and more about the sudden jolt.
usage_notes: Bagaman mas karaniwan ang 'gulat', ang 'kagitlahan' ay ginagamit upang ilarawan ang mismong estado o pakiramdam ng pagkabigla, na ginagawa itong bahagyang mas pormal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilan ang sigaw ng **kagitlahan** nang makita ang ahas.","translation":"She couldn't suppress a scream of **shock** when she saw the snake."},{"sentence":"Namatay ang ilaw at sa gitna ng dilim, narinig ang mga bulong ng **kagitlahan**.","translation":"The lights died, and in the middle of the darkness, whispers of being **startled** were heard."}]
