meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang tao na may tumutulong uhog. Ginagamit din bilang isang mapanlibak na termino para sa isang tao na bata pa, walang karanasan, o isip-bata.
original_explanation: Literally, someone with a runny nose. But it's the classic Filipino insult for someone younger or less experienced than you. "Uhugin ka pa lang, nagtatrabaho na ako!" (You were still a snot-nosed kid when I started working!). It's the verbal equivalent of a "noogie."
usage_notes: Can be literal or a figurative insult. The suffix "-in" denotes having the quality of the root word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Palaging **uhugin** ang bunsong kapatid ko tuwing umaga.","translation":"My youngest sibling is always **snotty** every morning."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong pagsabihan, **uhugin** ka pa noong nagsimula ako sa propesyon na ito.","translation":"Don't lecture me, you were still **immature** (a snot-nosed kid) when I started in this profession."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sikat na Pilipinong boy band na kilala sa kanilang musika, sayaw, at pagtataguyod ng P-pop sa pandaigdigang entablado. Sila ay binubuo nina Pablo, Josh, Stell, Ken, at Justin.
etymology: The name is an acronym for "Sound Break," representing their goal to break into the Philippine music scene. "19" is derived from the country code of South Korea (+82) and the Philippines (+63), where 8+2+6+3=19, symbolizing the collaboration between the two countries in their training.
original_explanation: The P-pop Kings who broke the internet and the charts. They're proof that Pinoy talent, when trained with K-pop level discipline, can conquer the world. They're the reason your cousin suddenly knows complex choreo and why "GENTO" became a global dance challenge. They are not just a group; they are a cultural reset, the pride of A'TIN (their fandom).
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the musical group. Capitalization is standard (SB19).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong pakinggan ang mga kanta ng **SB19**.","translation":"I love listening to the songs of **SB19**."},{"sentence":"Nakabili ka na ba ng tiket para sa concert ng **SB19**?","translation":"Have you bought a ticket for the **SB19** concert?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na gumagawa at nagpapadala ng mga electromagnetic wave, tulad ng mga alon ng radyo o telebisyon, upang maghatid ng impormasyon.
original_explanation: The thing that sends the signal for your favorite AM/FM radio station or TV channel. It's the reason you can listen to your favorite DJ in traffic or watch your favorite teleserye. Think of it as the ultimate "pasa-load" machine, but for signals instead of mobile credits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa tuktok ng bundok ang **transmiter** ng istasyon ng radyo para mas malawak ang abot nito.","translation":"The radio station's **transmitter** is on top of the mountain for wider reach."},{"sentence":"Nasira ang pangunahing **transmiter** ng TV network dahil sa malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The TV network's main **transmitter** was damaged by the strong typhoon."}]

translation: to be unfaithful; to cheat (on a partner)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng romantikong ugnayan sa ibang tao habang nasa isang nakataling relasyon.
etymology: From `mang-` + `kaliwa` (left), metaphorically meaning to go to the 'other side' or the 'wrong way'.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sana all' turned into 'sana 'wag na lang.' This is the plot of 90% of Pinoy teleseryes. When your partner starts looking for a 'side-chick' or 'side-hustle' in the romance department. The root word is 'kaliwa' (left), so it's like veering to the 'wrong' or 'other' side.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to romantic infidelity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang nasisira dahil may isang nagpasyang **mangaliwa**.","translation":"Many families are broken because one person decided to **be unfaithful**."},{"sentence":"Nabalitaan kong **nangaliwa** raw ang asawa niya kaya sila naghiwalay.","translation":"I heard her husband **cheated** on her, that's why they separated."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikisama, pakikipag-ugnayan, o pakikipag-usap sa iba't ibang uri ng tao sa isang pagtitipon.
etymology: From 'halo' (mix). 'Pagkahalubilo' is the act of mixing with a crowd.
original_explanation: This is your 'tita' forcing you to go out of your room during a family reunion. It's the small talk you have to master at company events or the art of navigating a crowded party without spilling your drink. Basically, it's the opposite of being an 'introvert'. It's the process of turning strangers into 'beshies' for a night.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahiyain siya kaya iniiwasan niya ang **pagkahalubilo** sa maraming tao.","translation":"He is shy so he avoids **socializing** with many people."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkahalubilo** ay mahalagang bahagi ng pagpapalawak ng iyong network.","translation":"**Mingling** is an important part of expanding your network."}]

translation: to tag along, to follow behind
meaning_filipino: Sumama o sumunod sa isang tao, kadalasan nang walang pormal na imbitasyon; bumuntot sa likuran.
etymology: From `pa-` (prefix indicating action or manner) and `buntot` (tail). Literally, 'to act like a tail'.
original_explanation: That awkward moment when you leave the mall at the same time as a stranger and you're both walking in the same direction, so you slow down para hindi isipin na **pabuntot** ka. It can also mean 'to tag along,' like your younger sibling who always wants to come with you and your friends.
usage_notes: Often used as 'pabuntot-buntot' to mean 'always tagging along'. Can also be a causative verb, e.g. `ipabuntot` (to have someone followed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang laging **pabuntot** sa ate mo, matuto kang mag-isa.","translation":"Don't always **tag along** with your older sister, learn to be independent."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **pabuntot** sa inyo sa Baguio, pwede ba?","translation":"I want to **tag along** with you guys to Baguio, can I?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nagpapahintulot na siya ay abusuhin, apihin, o hindi irespeto ng iba nang walang pagtutol; isang taong sunud-sunuran.
etymology: Mula sa piguratibong kahulugan sa wikang Ingles.
original_explanation: Eto yung friend mo na puro "sana all" na lang ang sagot. Yung laging nag-a-adjust, laging nagpaparaya, laging "okay lang." Basically, ikaw kapag marupok ka at hinayaan mong tapak-tapakan ng iba ang feelings mo. Hugot 101.
usage_notes: Malawakang ginagamit sa Taglish na pag-uusap, lalo na sa mga usaping pang-relasyon at personal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang papayag na maging **doormat** lang niya!","translation":"Don't you dare allow yourself to just be his/her **doormat**!"},{"sentence":"Pagod na akong maging **doormat**, kaya matuto ka nang rumespeto.","translation":"I'm tired of being a **doormat**, so learn to be respectful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggamit o paglaan ng salapi, oras, o lakas para sa isang partikular na layunin o gawain.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your sweldo on 15/30. It's the 'add to cart' and 'checkout' process made into a formal word. But it's not just money! It's also the **paggugol** of time binge-watching a series or the effort you put into a presentation that your boss barely looked at.
usage_notes: A formal term for spending. 'Paggastos' is more common in everyday conversation for money. 'Paggugol' is often used for time, effort, and other resources.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging **paggugol** ng gobyerno para sa proyektong ito.","translation":"The government's **expenditure** for this project was huge."},{"sentence":"Ang **paggugol** ng oras sa pamilya ay isang mahalagang pamumuhunan.","translation":"The **investment** of time in family is an important one."}]

meaning_filipino: Inisin o galitin nang husto ang isang tao hanggang sa punto na halos mawala ito sa kanyang katinuan.
original_explanation: The act of testing someone's sanity. Your slow internet connection during a Zoom presentation? Hinuwisyo ka. That client with never-ending "minor revisions"? They will huwisyuhin you. It's the process of being pushed to the brink of losing your "huwisyo."
usage_notes: A colloquial and expressive verb, indicating a high level of annoyance or exasperation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talaga namang **hinuwisyo** ako ng mga batang iyon sa sobrang ingay!","translation":"Those kids really **drove me crazy** with so much noise!"},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **huwisyuhin** sa mga tanong mong paulit-ulit.","translation":"Don't **exasperate** me with your repetitive questions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling sa iba na linisin ang isang bagay o lugar.
original_explanation: Your mom's command before visitors arrive: "Hoy, palinis mo 'yang kwarto mo!" It's the "pa-" prefix magic that turns a task you should be doing into a task someone else will do for you. Used for cars, shoes, houses, and sometimes, your messy life choices (if only it were that easy).
usage_notes: This is a causative verb. The speaker is causing the action of cleaning to be done by someone else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **palinis** ang kotse bago kami umalis.","translation":"I need **to have** the car **cleaned** before we leave."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang **palinis** ng aircon ngayon?","translation":"How much is it **to have** an aircon **cleaned** nowadays?"}]

meaning_filipino: Sa isang iglap lamang; walang pagkaantala o pag-aatubili; kaagad-agad.
original_explanation: Yung response time ng nanay mo kapag narinig niyang nabasag mo yung paborito niyang plato. O yung pag-seen niya sa message mo pero di nag-reply. "Dagli" is 'The Flash' of Tagalog adverbs. Agad-agad, no waiting.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'agad'. Often used in literature. 'Daglian' is the adjective form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang marinig ang balita, **dagli** siyang umuwi ng probinsya.","translation":"When he heard the news, he **immediately** went home to the province."},{"sentence":"Ang tulong ay **dagli** namang dumating mula sa mga kapitbahay.","translation":"Help **instantly** arrived from the neighbors."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit upang ipahiwatig ang pagsalungat, pagkontra, o pagiging katunggali.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *laban na nangangahulugang 'sumalungat' o 'kumontra'.
original_explanation: Eto yung 'vs.' sa buhay. Ikaw laban sa deadlines. Team KathNiel laban sa Team JaDine. Ang wallet mo laban sa presyo ng bilihin. It shows opposition, like you standing up against your boomer tita's unsolicited life advice.
usage_notes: Palaging sinusundan ng 'sa' kapag ginagamit bilang pang-ukol (hal. 'laban sa gobyerno').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumakbo siya **laban** sa kasalukuyang alkalde.","translation":"He ran **against** the current mayor."}]

translation: to intensify, to worsen, to become severe
meaning_filipino: Lumakas, lumubha, o tumaas ang antas ng isang bagay, sitwasyon, o damdamin.
original_explanation: Parang traffic sa EDSA kapag 5 PM on a payday Friday. It just gets worse. Or yung feelings mo para sa kanya, dati crush lang, ngayon 'di ka na makatulog. The situation or feeling has leveled up, often for the worse.
usage_notes: Used for feelings, weather, situations, pain, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umatindi** ang sakit ng ulo ko dahil sa ingay.","translation":"My headache **intensified** because of the noise."},{"sentence":"Lalo lang **umatindi** ang baha nang hindi tumigil ang ulan.","translation":"The flood only **worsened** when the rain didn't stop."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa "Best Friends Forever," na tumutukoy sa isang pinakamatalik na kaibigan.
etymology: Akronim mula sa Ingles na 'Best Friends Forever'.
original_explanation: The person you send ugly selfies to at 3 AM. The one who knows all your passwords and all your crushes. Your ride-or-die, your kakampi against the world, the other half of your chismis-duo. Your BFF is your chosen family.
usage_notes: Sobra-sobrang karaniwan sa pasulat at pasalitang komunikasyon, lalo na online. Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'best friend'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Anna ang **bff** ko mula pa noong elementary.","translation":"Anna has been my **bff** since elementary school."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng muling pagsusuri, pag-aaral, o pagbibigay ng puna sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: From the English word "review." Ito yung ginagawa mo sa notes mo the night before the exam (cramming!). O yung pag-stalk mo sa social media profile ng ka-date mo to "review" their background. Sa work, ito yung "Let's review the deck" bago ang presentation sa client.
usage_notes: Isang Tagalized na bersyon ng pandiwang Ingles na "to review."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **rebyuhin** ang ating mga sagot bago ipasa ang test paper.","translation":"We need **to review** our answers before passing the test paper."},{"sentence":"**Rebyuhin** mo muna ang kontrata bago ka pumirma.","translation":"**Review** the contract first before you sign."}]

translation: to be selfish with something; to withhold
meaning_filipino: Hindi pagbibigay o pagbabahagi ng isang bagay sa iba dahil sa sobrang pagtitipid o kasakiman.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `i-` (nagsasaad ng sanhi), `pag-` (nagsasaad ng kilos), at `maramot` (selfish).
original_explanation: ‘Yung ayaw mong i-share ‘yung pagkain mo sa office kasi "you deserve it" daw after ng toxic na meeting. Or ‘yung friend mong hindi ka pinapakopya ng notes kasi "pinaghirapan" niya raw. It's the act of being stingy or selfish with something towards someone. Huwag ipagmaramot ang chismis!
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang sawayin ang isang tao sa pagiging madamot o hindi mapagbigay. Ang bagay na hindi ibinabahagi ay ang tuwirang layon ng pandiwa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo namang **ipagmaramot** ang kaalaman mo sa amin.","translation":"Please don't **be selfish with** your knowledge and not share it with us."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo **ipinagmaramot** ang huling piraso ng pizza?","translation":"Why did you **withhold** the last slice of pizza?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging magkadikit, magkabuhol, o pinagsama upang maging isang entidad.
etymology: From `magka-` + `sanib` (to join, to merge; also 'to be possessed by a spirit').
original_explanation: Think of a corporate merger. Two companies becoming one. O kaya yung 3-in-1 coffee, where coffee, creamer, and sugar are all in one sachet. It's a fusion, a joining of forces. Parang Voltes V, "Let's volt in!" at naging isang robot na sila.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical objects, organizations, or even forces.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dalawang kumpanya ay **magkasanib** na ngayon upang palakasin ang kanilang operasyon.","translation":"The two companies are now **merged** to strengthen their operations."},{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng **magkasanib** na pwersa ng pulisya at militar, nahuli ang mga kriminal.","translation":"Through the **combined** forces of the police and military, the criminals were caught."}]

translation: to be able to taste; to discern flavor
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang matikman o matukoy ang lasa ng isang pagkain o inumin.
original_explanation: When you're trying to guess the secret ingredient in your lola's adobo. "May star anise ba 'to?" You're trying to *makalasa* every single note of flavor. Also, what your taste buds do when they're not dead from eating too much instant noodles.
usage_notes: Focuses on the ability to perceive a taste, often implying a subtle or complex flavor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit may sipon ako, sana'y **makalasa** ko pa rin ang paborito kong sinigang.","translation":"Even though I have a cold, I hope I can still **taste** my favorite sinigang."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang anghang, wala na akong ibang **makalasa** kundi sili.","translation":"Because it was so spicy, I couldn't **taste** anything else but chili."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahay o pugad ng mga bubuyog o putakti, karaniwang gawa sa papel na kahoy o putik.
original_explanation: The house of a 'bubuyog' (bumblebee) or 'putakti' (wasp). It's that scary-looking paper-mache-like thing hanging from a tree branch or the corner of your eaves that you tell the kids not to poke with a stick. One wrong move and it's a free-for-all sting-fest.
usage_notes: Refers to the nest of wasps, hornets, or bees. Sometimes used interchangeably with 'pugad ng pukyutan' (beehive).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa **bubuyan** na nakasabit sa puno ng mangga.","translation":"Be careful of the **wasp nest** hanging from the mango tree."},{"sentence":"Tinanggal ng hardinero ang **bubuyan** sa may bintana.","translation":"The gardener removed the **wasp nest** near the window."}]

translation: to treat with extreme contempt; to utterly debase
meaning_filipino: Labis na hamakin, alipustain, o tratuhin nang walang anumang paggalang o pagpapahalaga.
original_explanation: This is beyond simple bullying; it's treating someone like they're less than dirt. It's the level of contempt reserved for villains in teleseryes. Imagine the most intense "api-apihan" scene where the rich kontrabida is stepping on the protagonist's last family photo. That's the vibe. It's to degrade someone completely.
usage_notes: The reduplication of 'dusta' emphasizes the intensity and continuous nature of the contemptuous action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi makatarungan na **pakadusta-dustain** ang sinuman dahil sa kanilang estado sa buhay.","translation":"It is unjust to **treat anyone with extreme contempt** because of their status in life."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo hinahayaang **pakadusta-dustain** ka ng mga taong iyan?","translation":"Why do you let those people **utterly debase** you?"}]

translation: to punish, to inflict a penalty
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapataw ng kaparusahan sa isang tao o entidad bilang resulta ng isang pagkakamali, paglabag, o masamang gawain.
original_explanation: This is what your parents do when you stay out too late or what happens to your data allowance when you binge-watch K-dramas without WiFi. It's the consequence you pay for breaking the rules, from getting grounded to having your Netflix privileges revoked.
usage_notes: 'Magparusa' is the actor-focus form, where the one doing the punishing is the subject. The object-focus form is 'parusahan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang guro na **magparusa** sa mga estudyanteng nahuling nangongopya.","translation":"The teacher decided to **punish** the students who were caught cheating."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magparusa** nang hindi mo alam ang buong kwento.","translation":"Don't **inflict a penalty** without knowing the whole story."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang koleksyon ng mga gawa, dokumento, o pamumuhunan na nagpapakita ng kasanayan, karanasan, o pag-aari ng isang tao o kumpanya.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "portafolio" o Ingles na "portfolio".
original_explanation: Para sa mga creative (writers, artists, designers), ito 'yung collection of your greatest hits. 'Yung pinapakita mo sa client para masabing, "Eto po mga gawa ko, galing ko 'no?" Para sa mga business peeps, ito 'yung listahan ng investments mo. Basically, your professional "resibo".
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical case for carrying documents (a portfolio case) or, more commonly, a collection of work or investments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinasa ng arkitekto ang kanyang **portpolyo** na naglalaman ng mga disenyo niya.","translation":"The architect submitted his **portfolio** containing his designs."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong i-diversify ang iyong investment **portpolyo** para mabawasan ang panganib.","translation":"You need to diversify your investment **portfolio** to reduce risk."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain o proseso ng pagpapanumbalik o pagtatatag ng kapayapaan at katahimikan sa isang lugar, sitwasyon, o sa kalooban ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the act of being the designated "kalma lang" person in the group chat. When your friends are fighting, your intervention is an act of `pagpayapa`. It’s what peacekeepers do, what a good HR manager tries to achieve between warring colleagues, or what a mother does when her kids are wrestling over the remote control. It's about turning chaos into calm.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of conflict resolution, whether on a personal or societal level.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang misyon ng grupo ay ang **pagpayapa** sa nag-aaway na mga tribo.","translation":"The group's mission is the **pacification** of the warring tribes."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang mamagitan para sa **pagpayapa** ng magkabilang panig.","translation":"He tried to mediate for the **pacification** of both sides."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o akto ng pagiging maramot; ang pagtangging magbigay o mamahagi sa iba.
etymology: Mula sa `pag-` + `magmaramot` (maging maramot), na mula sa `maramot` (kuripot), ugat na `damot`.
original_explanation: Ito yung ugali ng kaibigan mong hihingi ng French fry mo pero pag ikaw na ang hihingi, biglang "last piece ko na 'to." Ang supreme art of not sharing. Yung tipong mayaman pero kuripot, o kaya ayaw lang talagang mamigay kahit tissue.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa gawain o ugali ng pagiging maramot o hindi mapagbigay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang **pagmamaramot** kaya walang gustong humingi ng tulong sa kanya.","translation":"He is known for his **stinginess**, so no one wants to ask for his help."},{"sentence":"Sa panahon ng krisis, hindi dapat umiral ang **pagmamaramot**.","translation":"In times of crisis, **selfishness** should not prevail."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas o di-makatarungang pagpigil sa kalayaan, karapatan, o pag-unlad ng isang tao o grupo.
etymology: Root word 'sikil' means to press down, to compact, or to suppress.
original_explanation: This is a heavy word. It's when 'the man' keeps you down. Think martial law, censorship, or a super strict boss who shuts down every idea you have. *Pagsikil* is the act of choking someone's freedom or rights. It's what heroes in movies fight against. It's the ultimate violation of 'you do you.'
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation, often used in political or social justice contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsikil** sa kalayaan sa pamamahayag ay isang malubhang isyu sa maraming bansa.","translation":"The **suppression** of the freedom of the press is a serious issue in many countries."},{"sentence":"Tinuligsa ng mga aktibista ang **pagsikil** sa karapatan ng mga manggagawa.","translation":"The activists condemned the **oppression** of workers' rights."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-ukol na ginagamit upang ipakilala ang paksa o tema ng isang usapan, sulatin, o pag-iisip.
original_explanation: The ultimate chismis starter. Whenever you hear "Uy, alam mo ba yung tungkol kay...", you know the tea is about to be spilled. It's the word that sets the topic, whether it's for a serious thesis ("Tungkol sa Epekto ng Social Media") or just plain office gossip.
usage_notes: Almost always followed by 'sa' for things/places (tungkol sa) or 'kay' for people's names (tungkol kay).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pelikula ay **tungkol** sa isang bayaning Pilipino.","translation":"The movie is **about** a Filipino hero."},{"sentence":"Nag-usap kami **tungkol** sa ating mga plano para bukas.","translation":"We talked **regarding** our plans for tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isinasagawa nang mabilisan; para sa agarang pangangailangan o panandaliang solusyon.
original_explanation: This is the 'Bahala na si Batman' approach to planning. A 'pangmadaliang solusyon' is a quick fix, a band-aid solution, like using tape to fix your glasses. It's the mindset behind instant noodles for dinner or cramming for an exam the night before. It gets the job done now, but you'll probably have to deal with the consequences later.
usage_notes: Often implies that something is a temporary or rushed solution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang umasa sa mga **pangmadalian** na solusyon.","translation":"Don't rely on **hasty** solutions."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng **pangmadalian** na tulong para sa mga biktima ng baha.","translation":"We need **immediate** help for the flood victims."}]

translation: to do something little by little; to ration
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggawa, pagkonsumo, o paghahati ng isang bagay sa maliliit na bahagi o sa dahan-dahang paraan.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'utay-utay'. This is what your mom tells you to do with the last can of Spam before payday. 'Utay-utayin mo lang 'yang ulam, ha? Para may pagkain pa tayo bukas.' It's the art of making things last, whether it's your sweldo, your data plan, or your patience.
usage_notes: The verb form, instructing or describing the action of doing something in small increments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **utay-utayin** ang natitirang tubig hanggang dumating ang tulong.","translation":"We need to **ration** the remaining water until help arrives."},{"sentence":"Mas mainam na **utay-utayin** ang malaking gawain upang hindi ka mapagod.","translation":"It's better to **do** a large task **little by little** so you don't get overwhelmed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang istrukturang itinayo sa ibabaw ng tubig, karaniwang sinusuportahan ng mga poste o haligi, na nagsisilbing daungan ng mga barko at bangka.
original_explanation: 'Yung mahabang tulay na kahoy or semento sa tabi ng dagat where you either wait for a ferry or mag-emote while watching the sunset. This is the setting for many Pinoy movie goodbyes and dramatic reunions. Dito mo rin makikita 'yung mga nagbebenta ng souvenir at 'yung mga nag-aalok ng island hopping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglakad-lakad kami sa **piyer** habang hinihintay ang pagdating ng barko.","translation":"We walked along the **pier** while waiting for the ship to arrive."},{"sentence":"Mula sa **piyer**, tanaw na ang magandang isla.","translation":"From the **pier**, the beautiful island is already visible."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang grupo ng mga tao na magkakasamang nagtatrabaho sa isang partikular na gawain. Sa kolokyal na gamit, tumutukoy din ito sa isang barkada o grupo ng magkakaibigan.
original_explanation: Your work team, your film production team, or your 'barkada'. Kung sa BPO ka, ito yung team niyo sa floor. Kung sa event, sila yung mga naka-black shirt na tumatakbo-takbo. Kung sa barkada, sila yung mga kasama mo sa inuman at sa kalokohan. "The whole crew is here!"
usage_notes: Used both in its formal sense (e.g., flight crew, BPO crew) and its informal, slang sense (group of friends).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng production **crew** ng dalawang cameraman.","translation":"The production **crew** needs two cameramen."},{"sentence":"Tara, sama mo buong **crew** niyo mamaya.","translation":"Come on, bring your whole **crew** (of friends) later."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na ginagamit sa konstruksyon o karpinterya upang tiyakin kung ang isang ibabaw ay patag na pahalang (horizontal) o patayo (vertical).
original_explanation: The official tool of a 'tito' or your friendly neighborhood karpintero. It's that thing with the bubble in the middle. If the bubble is centered, your life, or at least the shelf you're installing, is balanced. Kung wala sa **nibel**, 'yan ang dahilan kung bakit tabingi ang pagkakakabit ng picture frame niyo.
usage_notes: A loanword. In modern contexts, the English word 'level' is also very commonly used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **nibel** para masigurong pantay ang pagkakakabit ng pinto.","translation":"Use the **level** to make sure the door is installed straight."},{"sentence":"Sinusuri ng karpintero kung nasa **nibel** ang sahig.","translation":"The carpenter is checking if the floor is **level**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang nabubuksan at naisasara na ginagamit bilang pananggalang sa ulan o sa sikat ng araw.
original_explanation: That thing you always forget to bring when it suddenly rains. It's also a metaphor for protection, like when your friend becomes your 'payong' from a toxic ex. In the Philippines, it's also a status symbol if it's one of those fancy automatic or Japanese minimalist ones.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for the object or metaphorically for protection or refuge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang magdala ng **payong** dahil mukhang uulan mamaya.","translation":"Don't forget to bring an **umbrella** because it looks like it will rain later."},{"sentence":"Siya ang naging **payong** ko sa lahat ng aking mga problema.","translation":"He/She became my **refuge** in all of my problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa teolohiyang Kristiyano, ito ay tumutukoy sa pag-akyat ni Hesukristo sa langit apatnapung araw matapos ang Kanyang Muling Pagkabuhay.
original_explanation: Ito yung event sa Bible na 'umangat ang a-angat'. After ng resurrection, si Jesus ay umakyat na sa langit. May holiday pa nga para dito, ang 'Ascension Day,' pero hindi ito non-working holiday sa Pinas, kaya balik trabaho pa rin.
usage_notes: Palaging nakasulat na may malaking titik sa simula dahil ito ay isang pangngalang pantangi. Tumutukoy sa isang partikular na kaganapan sa relihiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang ng mga Kristiyano ang Araw ng **Asensiyon**.","translation":"Christians celebrate the Day of the **Ascension**."},{"sentence":"Ang **Asensiyon** ay isang mahalagang doktrina sa pananampalatayang Kristiyano.","translation":"The **Ascension** is an important doctrine in the Christian faith."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasunduan kung saan ang isang bagay, tulad ng isang silid sa otel, mesa sa restawran, o tiket, ay itinatabi para sa iyong paggamit sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is the confirmation you get after calling that fancy restaurant. "Sir, may reserbasyon po ba kayo?" is the question that separates the planners from the 'bahala na' crowd. It's your proof of foresight, your ticket to not waiting in line.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with the English word "reservation", though the latter is more common in casual speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalimutan kong gumawa ng **reserbasyon** sa hotel kaya napuno na sila.","translation":"I forgot to make a hotel **reservation**, so they were already full."},{"sentence":"Pakitingnan kung may **reserbasyon** na nakapangalan sa akin.","translation":"Please check if there is a **reservation** under my name."}]

meaning_filipino: Idikit o ibangga nang may puwersa ang ulo sa isang matigas na bagay.
original_explanation: The classic Filipino parent threat: "Gusto mo iuntog kita sa pader?!" (Do you want me to bump your head against the wall?!). It's the physical manifestation of extreme frustration. Also, what you feel like doing to yourself when you make a really dumb mistake, like sending a 'hugot' text to your boss instead of your friend.
usage_notes: This verb is specific to bumping a head. The object of the verb is the head.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang galit niya sa sarili, gusto niyang **iuntog** ang ulo sa pader.","translation":"In his extreme anger at himself, he wants to **bump** his head against the wall."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, baka **maiuntog** mo ang ulo mo sa mababang kisame.","translation":"Be careful, you might accidentally **bump** your head on the low ceiling."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalis ng dumi, basa, o anumang bagay mula sa isang ibabaw sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng tela, papel, o kamay.
original_explanation: That thing your mom yells at you to do after you spill something. 'Hoy, punasan mo yang kalat mo!' Also, when you need to wipe away tears after watching a sad K-drama, or wipe your phone screen clean from all the thumb marks from scrolling through TikTok.
usage_notes: "Punasan" is the command form. "Pinunasan" is past tense. "Pinupunasan" is present tense. "Pupunasan" is future tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Punasan** mo ang mesa bago dumating ang mga bisita.","translation":"**Wipe** the table before the guests arrive."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **punasan** ang iyong mga paa bago pumasok sa bahay.","translation":"Don't forget to **wipe** your feet before entering the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapad na piraso ng metal o kahoy na hawak bilang pananggalang sa mga suntok o armas; maaari ding tumukoy sa sagisag o coat of arms ng isang pamilya, bansa, o institusyon.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'panangga'. Before face shields, may **eskudo** ang mga mandirigma. It's also the fancy logo of a royal family or a school, like in Harry Potter, that you see on flags and uniforms. Your family's 'brand logo', kung meron man.
usage_notes: Bihira nang gamitin para sa literal na kalasag, mas karaniwan na ngayon sa konteksto ng heraldiya (coat of arms).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **eskudo** ng Pilipinas ay naglalaman ng araw, tatlong bituin, agila, at leon.","translation":"The **coat of arms** of the Philippines contains a sun, three stars, an eagle, and a lion."},{"sentence":"Ginamit ng kabalyero ang kanyang **eskudo** upang salagin ang atake ng espada.","translation":"The knight used his **shield** to block the sword attack."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang pag-akala o pagkilala sa isang tao o bagay bilang iba; magkamali ng pagkakakilanlan.
etymology: A complex verb form. `mapag-` + `kamal` (from `mali`) + `-an`. `Kamal` is an old root related to consciousness or perception. The structure means "to be mistakenly perceived as".
original_explanation: This is what happens when you wave at someone from a distance, only to realize it's not your friend. Awkward. O kaya yung na-replyan mo ng "I love you too" yung group chat ng office imbes na yung chat ng jowa mo. The verb of facepalm moments.
usage_notes: Object-focused verb. The object is the person/thing being mistaken. The person/thing they are mistaken for is usually introduced by `bilang`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madalas akong **mapagkamalan** na mas bata sa aking edad.","translation":"I am often **mistaken** for being younger than my age."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo sanang **mapagkamalan** ang katahimikan ko bilang galit.","translation":"I hope you don't **mistake** my silence for anger."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi tumitigil; tuloy-tuloy at walang patid.
original_explanation: That feeling when you have back-to-back meetings from 8 AM to 5 PM. No breaks, no mercy. It's the non-stop chika from your best friend, the 'sana all' posts on your feed, or the rain during a typhoon. It just keeps going.
usage_notes: Similar to 'walang-tigil' or 'tuloy-tuloy'. Often used to describe actions, sounds, or phenomena that are continuous and often tiring or overwhelming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-iyak ng sanggol ay **walang-humpay** buong magdamag.","translation":"The baby's crying was **incessant** all night."},{"sentence":"Sila ay nagtrabaho nang **walang-humpay** upang matapos ang proyekto.","translation":"They worked **relentlessly** to finish the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghawak at pagkontrol sa renda ng kabayo; sa matalinghagang paraan, ito ay nangangahulugang pagkontrol, pagpigil, o pamamahala sa isang sitwasyon, tao, o damdamin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'renda' (mula sa Espanyol 'rienda') + panlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: From the Spanish 'rienda' (rein). Literally, it's what you do to control a horse. But 99% of the time, we use it figuratively. It's when you need to take control. Got a team member who's going rogue? Kailangan mong rumenda. Is your spending out of control after getting your 13th-month pay? Time to rumenda on your expenses. It's being the adult in the room, even if the room is just your own chaotic brain.
usage_notes: Mas madalas gamitin sa matalinghagang kahulugan ng pagkontrol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **rumenda** ng gobyerno sa pagtaas ng presyo ng bilihin.","translation":"The government needs to **take control** of the rising prices of goods."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **rumenda** sa kanyang galit ngunit huli na ang lahat.","translation":"He tried to **rein in** his anger but it was too late."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang salitang Ingles para sa 'tradisyon' o 'kaugalian'; isang paniniwala, gawi, o kuwento na naipasa mula sa isang henerasyon patungo sa susunod.
original_explanation: The reason why you have to visit all your ninongs and ninangs on Christmas day. It's the 'kasi sabi ni lola' argument that you can never win. Also, the reason for the 12 round fruits on New Year's Eve.
usage_notes: Ang salitang Ingles ay madalas na ginagamit sa mga pangungusap na Taglish, bagaman ang Filipinized na 'tradisyon' at ang katutubong 'kaugalian' ay napakakaraniwan din.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"It's a family **tradition** to eat together every Sunday.","translation":"It's a family **tradition** to eat together every Sunday."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga sa mga Pilipino ang mga **tradition** tuwing Pasko.","translation":"For Filipinos, **traditions** during Christmas are important."}]

translation: to become short; to be shortened
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ikli o pagiging mas maikli kaysa sa orihinal o inaasahang haba; ang pagkaubos o pagliit.
original_explanation: That feeling of dread when your patience starts to **become short** during epic traffic. Or what happens to your salary just a few days after payday. It's the universe telling you, "Oops, that's all you get!"
usage_notes: This verb is intransitive and describes a state of becoming short. It's less common than 'umikli' but carries a slightly more formal or literary tone. Often used for abstract concepts like patience or time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mangikli** ang kanyang pasensya sa kahihintay.","translation":"His patience started to **become short** from waiting so long."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa krisis, tila **mangikli** ang pisi ng pag-asa ng ilan.","translation":"Because of the crisis, it seems the rope of hope for some will **be shortened**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marka o linya na nalilikha sa pamamagitan ng pagtiklop ng isang bagay, tulad ng papel o tela.
original_explanation: This is what your mom yells about when she sees your un-ironed school uniform. 'Anak, ayusin mo yang tupi ng pantalon mo!' It's the OG way of making paper airplanes, origami, and hiding secret notes in class.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **tupi** ang laylayan ng kanyang pantalon.","translation":"There is a **fold** at the hem of his pants."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong lagyan ng **tupi** ang litrato.","translation":"Don't put a **crease** on the photograph."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha, pag-akda, o pagpapatibay ng mga batas.
original_explanation: The main job of people in Congress and the Senate, which we see on TV. It's the formal process of turning an idea (or a political promise) into a rule that everyone has to follow. It’s like being the admin of a massive group chat, setting the rules for millions of members.
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal, political, and governmental contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Kongreso ang may pangunahing kapangyarihan na **magbatas** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The Congress has the primary power to **legislate** in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng mambabatas na **magbatas** para sa kapakanan ng kanyang mga nasasakupan.","translation":"It is the duty of a lawmaker to **make laws** for the welfare of his/her constituents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang laruan na may anyo ng tao, sanggol, o iba pang karakter, na karaniwang ginagamit ng mga bata sa paglalaro.
original_explanation: That toy from your childhood that you used to dress up, put makeup on, and talk to like a real person. Sometimes, it's also what you call someone so beautiful they don't look real. But sometimes, they're also scary, especially at night when you feel like they're staring at you. Hello, Annabelle!
usage_notes: Can also be spelled 'manyika'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Regalo sa kanya ng lola niya ang isang magandang **manika**.","translation":"Her grandmother gave her a beautiful **doll** as a gift."},{"sentence":"Mukha siyang **manika** sa suot niyang bestida.","translation":"She looks like a **doll** in the dress she's wearing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na komunidad o pamayanan, lalo na sa mga pook rural; isang yunit pampamahalaan na mas maliit sa bayan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "barrio", na nangangahulugang "pamayanan" o "distrito".
original_explanation: Before 'barangay' became the official term, there was 'baryo'. It evokes a more rustic, probinsya vibe—think rice fields, carabaos, and a community where everyone knows everyone (and their business). It’s the setting for countless Filipino horror movies and heartwarming family dramas.
usage_notes: Bagama't ang opisyal na terminong administratibo ngayon ay "barangay," ang "baryo" ay malawak pa ring ginagamit sa impormal na pananalita, lalo na upang tukuyin ang mga nayon sa kanayunan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umuwi siya sa kanilang **baryo** sa probinsya para magbakasyon.","translation":"He went home to their **village** in the province for a vacation."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na masusi at maingat sa pagsusuri ng mga detalye; mapag-usisa.
original_explanation: Ikaw 'to kapag chine-check mo 'yung profile ng ka-chat mo, from their first profile pic in 2009 down to their tagged photos and comments. You are being masiyasat. Also applies to your tita who inspects every corner of your room for dust. The Sherlock Holmes of the household.
usage_notes: Ang salitang-ugat na 'siyasat' ay nangangahulugang imbestigasyon. Ang 'masiyasat' ay ang pang-uring anyo nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil **masiyasat** ang detective, natuklasan niya agad ang katotohanan.","translation":"Because the detective was **meticulous**, he quickly discovered the truth."},{"sentence":"Maging **masiyasat** sa pagbabasa ng kontrata bago pumirma.","translation":"Be **thorough** in reading the contract before signing."}]

translation: a person who travels some distance to work on a regular basis
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na regular na naglalakbay mula sa kanyang tirahan patungo sa lugar ng trabaho o paaralan, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng pampublikong sasakyan.
original_explanation: Ang tawag sa ating lahat na nakikipagsiksikan sa MRT/LRT, bus, o jeep araw-araw para lang makapasok sa work. Sila ang mga modern-day bayani na ang kalaban ay traffic, mahabang pila, at minsan, ang sariling body clock.
usage_notes: Isang direktang hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na malawakang ginagamit sa Pilipinas upang tukuyin ang mga pasahero, lalo na ang mga pumapasok sa trabaho o eskwela.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Araw-araw, libo-libong **commuter** ang nahihirapan dahil sa masikip na trapiko sa EDSA.","translation":"Every day, thousands of **commuters** suffer because of the heavy traffic on EDSA."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **commuter**, sanay na ako sa mahabang pila sa istasyon ng tren.","translation":"As a **commuter**, I am used to the long queues at the train station."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpunta sa burol o lamay upang makiramay sa pamilya ng namatayan.
original_explanation: It's the Filipino tradition of paying respects to the deceased, which often involves coffee, biscuits, some mahjong or card games, and catching up with relatives you haven't seen in years. It's a somber reunion, a way of showing you're there for the grieving family.
usage_notes: Refers to the act of visiting a wake. 'Lamay' is the wake itself, while 'paglamay' is the action of going to the wake.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglamay** ay isang paraan ng pagpapakita ng pakikiramay.","translation":"**Attending a wake** is a way of showing sympathy."},{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa probinsya para sa **paglamay** sa aming lola.","translation":"We went to the province to **attend the wake** for our grandmother."}]

meaning_filipino: Itago ang isang bagay, impormasyon, o katotohanan upang hindi malaman ng iba.
original_explanation: That thing your friend does when they have a new jowa but don't want to post it on social media yet. They're trying to maglingid the relationship. It's the act of keeping things 'on the down low'. Very 'private but not secret' energy.
usage_notes: A formal or literary word. More common to say `magtago` or `ilihim`. Often used with `sa kaalaman ng...` (without the knowledge of...).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **maglingid** ng katotohanan, ngunit nalaman din ito ng lahat.","translation":"He tried to **conceal** the truth, but everyone eventually found out."},{"sentence":"Hindi mo maaaring **maglingid** habambuhay ang iyong mga pagkakamali.","translation":"You cannot **keep secret** your mistakes forever."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng pag-ikot ng paningin o pagkahilo, na maaaring sanhi ng sakit, pagkapagod, o pagkalito.
original_explanation: That feeling when you stand up too fast after binge-watching for 8 hours. Or when your crush finally talks to you and your brain just goes 404 error. It's also what you feel when you see your credit card bill after a 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: Describes the physical sensation of dizziness or the mental state of being utterly confused.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang matinding **pagkaliyo** matapos sumakay sa roller coaster.","translation":"She felt extreme **dizziness** after riding the roller coaster."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaliyo** ko ay dahil sa dami ng problemang iniisip.","translation":"My **confusion** is because of the many problems I'm thinking about."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho o gawain ay ang magpatakbo ng isang sasakyan.
original_explanation: The person who holds your life in their hands during rush hour traffic on EDSA. Can be a jeepney driver yelling "barya lang po sa umaga," a Grab driver who's also a part-time therapist, or your dad who complains about gas prices. "Manong, para!"
usage_notes: The Filipino word "tsuper" is also used, but "driver" is more common in modern contexts, especially for private cars or ride-sharing services.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisabi sa **driver** na sa kanto lang ako bababa.","translation":"Please tell the **driver** I'll just get off at the corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginamit ang isang tela o anumang pamunas upang alisin ang dumi o likido sa isang ibabaw; isang kilos na tapos na.
original_explanation: What you did to the table after your messy sibling ate. "Ako na nagpunas ng kalat mo." It's also what you do to your face after crying over a K-drama or a sad hugot song. It's the act of cleaning up, literally or emotionally.
usage_notes: Simple past tense. Indicates a completed action of wiping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpunas** siya ng pawis sa kanyang noo gamit ang panyo.","translation":"He **wiped** the sweat from his forehead using a handkerchief."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos kumain, **nagpunas** agad ako ng mesa.","translation":"After eating, I immediately **wiped** the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang serye ng mga kilos o gawain na isinasagawa ayon sa isang nakatakdang pagkakasunod-sunod, kadalasang may kaugnayan sa seremonyang panrelihiyon o kultural.
original_explanation: Your daily routine before logging in for your BPO shift? That's your ritwal. Making coffee, stretching, and mentally preparing for irate customers. Or that specific set of things you do for good luck before an exam. "May **ritwal** ako tuwing umaga: kape, yosi, tapos check ng memes."
usage_notes: Can be used for both sacred, traditional ceremonies and for mundane, personal habits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-aalay ng pagkain sa mga anito ay isang sinaunang **ritwal**.","translation":"Offering food to the spirits is an ancient **ritual**."},{"sentence":"Naging **ritwal** na niya ang pag-eehersisyo tuwing alas-singko ng umaga.","translation":"Exercising at five in the morning has become his **ritual**."}]

translation: to cover with the hand; to catch
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtakip o paghuli sa isang bagay gamit ang kamay, karaniwang mabilis at biglaan.
original_explanation: Ever tried to catch a fly or a cockroach with your bare hands? That's `tumutop`. It's that quick, cupping motion to trap something small and probably moving. Also what you do when you accidentally say something you shouldn't have and immediately cover your mouth. Oops.
usage_notes: Past/Completed aspect of the verb. Can also be used for catching something abstract like an idea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis siyang **tumutop** ng kamay sa kanyang bibig nang mapagtantong mali ang nasabi.","translation":"She quickly **covered** her mouth with her hand when she realized she said the wrong thing."},{"sentence":"**Tumutop** siya sa nahuhulog na susi bago ito tumama sa sahig.","translation":"He **caught** the falling key before it hit the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit upang ipakilala ang paraan, instrumento, o ahensya kung paano naisakatuparan ang isang kilos o layunin.
etymology: Mula sa `sa` (in/at) + `pamamagitan` (means, agency) + `ng` (of). Ang `pamamagitan` ay nagmula sa `pa-` + `mag-` + `gitan` (gitna, middle).
original_explanation: This is the formal, 'pa-class' way of saying 'using' or 'because of'. You use it in school reports ('Nakuha ang datos sa pamamagitan ng survey') and in office emails ('Ipinapadala ko ang report sa pamamagitan ng email'). It's the corporate and academic cousin of 'gamit ang...'
usage_notes: Isang mahalaga at karaniwang pariralang pang-ukol para sa pagtukoy ng pamamaraan, ahensya, o daluyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-usap kami **sa pamamagitan ng** video call.","translation":"We talked **through** a video call."},{"sentence":"Nakamit niya ang tagumpay **sa pamamagitan ng** pagsisikap at tiyaga.","translation":"She achieved success **by means of** hard work and perseverance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na puno o ang buto nito na nagbibigay ng kulay pulang-kahel na pangkulay sa pagkain.
original_explanation: The secret ingredient that makes your kare-kare and pancit palabok look fiery and appetizing. It's the natural food coloring of the Philippines. You soak these little red seeds in hot water or oil, and presto, you have a vibrant orange-red liquid that screams 'delicious.' It's makeup for your food.
usage_notes: Used primarily as a natural food colorant in many Filipino dishes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maglagay ka ng **atsuete** para magkakulay ang sarsa ng kare-kare.","translation":"Add some **annatto** to give color to the kare-kare sauce."},{"sentence":"Ang buto ng **atsuete** ay kailangang ibabad sa mainit na tubig.","translation":"The **annatto** seeds need to be soaked in hot water."}]

translation: to send word, to inform through someone
meaning_filipino: Ang paghahatid ng mensahe o impormasyon sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng isa pang tao o midyum.
original_explanation: Before group chats and DMs, this was the original 'paki-forward.' It's when you ask a friend, 'Pakisabi kay crush, 'hi'!' or tell your kapatid to tell your mom you'll be late for dinner. It's the analog way of relaying messages, full of potential for 'sabi ni ano...' miscommunications.
usage_notes: Often used with 'kay' or 'kina' to indicate the recipient of the message. The structure is often: (Actor) magpapasabi (to Person A) na (Message) (to Person B).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magpasabi** ka na lang kay Maria kung hindi ka makakarating.","translation":"Just **send word** through Maria if you can't make it."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagpasabi** na kanselado ang meeting?","translation":"Who **sent word** that the meeting was cancelled?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kulisap na walang pakpak, na nabubuhay sa dugo ng mga mammal at ibon.
original_explanation: The uninvited guest on your furbaby. The reason your doggo suddenly stops chasing its tail to scratch frantically. These tiny vampires are a pet owner's worst nightmare and the main customers of pet shop anti-flea shampoos.
usage_notes: While plural in Spanish, `pulgas` is used for both singular ('a flea') and plural ('fleas') in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang paliguan ang aso dahil mukhang may **pulgas** na ito.","translation":"The dog needs a bath because it looks like it has **fleas**."},{"sentence":"Isang **pulgas** lang ang makita mo, ibig sabihin ay marami pa iyan.","translation":"If you see just one **flea**, it means there are many more."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bata na legal na kinupkop at inalagaan ng mga taong hindi niya tunay na magulang.
original_explanation: This is the child you chose, not by blood, but by heart. It's like finding your forever family on Lazada—you picked them out, added them to your cart (legally, of course), and now they're yours to love, cherish, and occasionally remind to clean their room.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwan at neutral na termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal na mahal nila ang kanilang **anak na ampon**.","translation":"They dearly love their **adopted child**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kahilingan o utos na magbayad para sa isang produkto, serbisyo, o utang.
original_explanation: That feeling when your friend "borrows" money and you have to post a cryptic "Yung utang mo, bes" status. "Pabayad po" is the polite but firm way of saying "Where's my money?!" It's the official word of sari-sari store owners, landlords, and that one officemate you treated to lunch last week.
usage_notes: Often used as a gentle reminder or a direct demand for payment. Can be a sign on a counter or a message sent to a debtor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nakasulat na '**pabayad** po' sa pinto ng tindahan.","translation":"There's a sign that says '**payment please**' on the store's door."},{"sentence":"**Pabayad** naman sa mga kumuha ng bigas kahapon.","translation":"**Asking for payment** from those who got rice yesterday."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang nag-iingat; nagpapakita ng sukdulang pag-iingat upang maiwasan ang anumang pagkakamali, panganib, o pinsala.
original_explanation: This is your mom telling you to cross the street, or your boss telling you to handle the VIP client's account. It's not just 'maingat' (careful), it's level 99 careful. The kind of careful you are when you're carrying the lechon at a party or when you're trying to sneak back into the house past curfew.
usage_notes: The repetition of `maingat` with the linker `na` intensifies the meaning to "very" or "extremely" careful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maingat na maingat** niyang binuhat ang bagong panganak na sanggol.","translation":"She carried the newborn baby **very, very carefully**."},{"sentence":"Dapat **maingat na maingat** ka sa mga pipirmahan mong kontrata.","translation":"You must be **extra careful** with the contracts you sign."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sukat o pagtatasa sa kalidad, kasikatan, o halaga ng isang bagay, tulad ng sa isang programa sa telebisyon, produkto, o serbisyo.
original_explanation: Ito yung pinag-aawayan ng mga TV network at fan base. "Mas mataas ang rating ng show namin!" O kaya yung 5-star rating na hinahabol mo sa Grab or Lalamove para good vibes ka sa driver. It's the modern-day report card for everything.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa media, negosyo, at online platforms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumaas ang **rating** ng teleserye dahil sa bagong 'love team'.","translation":"The TV series' **rating** increased because of the new 'love team'."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang magbigay ng **rating** sa ating serbisyo.","translation":"Don't forget to give a **rating** for our service."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang bulalas na nagpapahayag ng matinding inis, galit, o pagkadismaya. Hango sa salitang Espanyol para sa 'gatas'.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "leche" (gatas), na pinaikli mula sa pariralang "mala leche" na nangangahulugang 'bad milk' o malas.
original_explanation: The national expression for when you stub your toe, your internet dies during a final presentation, or you see your ex with a new partner. It's the verbal equivalent of a facepalm. Originally means 'milk' in Spanish, but in the Philippines, it's the milk of human frustration.
usage_notes: Itinuturing na isang banayad na mura. Madalas itong marinig sa di-pormal na usapan at maaaring dugtungan ng ibang salita tulad ng 'leche naman' o 'lecheng buhay 'to'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Leche!** Naiwan ko ang wallet ko sa bahay.","translation":"**Damn!** I left my wallet at home."},{"sentence":"Ang **leche** mong plano, pumalpak na naman!","translation":"Your **darn** plan failed again!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng serbisyo o paglilingkod sa isang tao, pangkat, o institusyon.
original_explanation: This is what you expect from a restaurant with a 10% service charge. It's also the "boss, ano'ng kailangan mo?" mode you have for your team lead. In a deeper sense, it's the core of "public service" – the reason why the office is called "pinaglilingkuran."
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the one being served. 'Pagsilbihan' is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming tanggapan ay handang **palingkuran** ang mamamayan.","translation":"Our office is ready **to serve** the citizens."},{"sentence":"Sino ang dapat nating **palingkuran**? Ang bayan o ang sarili?","translation":"Who should we **serve**? The nation or ourselves?"}]

translation: to export; to transport goods out of a place
meaning_filipino: Pagdadala ng mga produkto o kalakal mula sa isang lugar, karaniwang mula sa probinsya patungo sa lungsod o sa ibang bansa, para ipagbili.
original_explanation: It's what businesses do when they sell products abroad, like exporting mangoes to Japan. It's also what your tita from the province does when she brings a whole bayong of produce to Manila, effectively "exporting" goods from her hometown to the big city. The opposite of `mag-angkat` (to import).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang kumpanya na **magluwas** ng pinatuyong mangga sa Europa.","translation":"The company decided to **export** dried mangoes to Europe."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magluwas** ng mga gulay mula sa Baguio papuntang Maynila.","translation":"We need to **transport** vegetables from Baguio to Manila."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng boses na magaspang, malat, o paos, kadalasan dahil sa labis na pagsasalita, pagsigaw, o sakit.
original_explanation: This is your voice after a karaoke marathon, a championship basketball game, or a really bad cold. You sound like a gravel road feels. You try to talk, but what comes out is 50% air and 50% struggle.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'paos' or 'malat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **paga** ang boses ng mang-aawit matapos ang kanyang concert.","translation":"The singer's voice became **hoarse** after his concert."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka munang kumanta, **paga** pa ang lalamunan mo.","translation":"Don't sing for now, your throat is still **hoarse**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis na balat o sapin na bumabalot o naghihiwalay sa mga bahagi ng isang istrukturang biyolohikal o iba pang bagay.
original_explanation: Think of that thin, papery skin on the inside of an eggshell, or the film on top of your milk tea that's been sitting out. That's lamad. It's that delicate layer between 'this' and 'that'. In a horror movie, it's probably what the alien is made of.
usage_notes: Can refer to biological membranes (e.g., cell membrane) or any thin, film-like layer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May manipis na **lamad** sa pagitan ng puti at pula ng itlog.","translation":"There is a thin **membrane** between the egg white and the yolk."},{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang **lamad** na namumuo sa ibabaw ng lumalamig na sabaw.","translation":"He saw the **film** forming on top of the cooling soup."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasingkahulugan ng maghubad; ang pag-aalis ng kasuotan sa katawan.
original_explanation: The slightly more dramatic twin of 'maghubad'. While 'maghubad' is just taking off clothes, 'maghubo' has a bit more flair, a bit more... finality. It's like the difference between 'leaving' and 'storming out.' Both get you out the door, but one makes a statement.
usage_notes: Largely synonymous with 'maghubad' but can sometimes feel more literary or intense. 'Hubad' is more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan siyang **maghubo** ng damit para sa medical examination.","translation":"He was instructed to **undress** for the medical examination."},{"sentence":"Sa isang iglap, **naghubo** siya ng basang damit at nagbalot ng tuwalya.","translation":"In an instant, she **stripped off** her wet clothes and wrapped a towel around herself."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maluwag na kasuotan na walang manggas na ipinapatong sa balikat at likod; isang balabal.
original_explanation: Think of what superheroes, kings, or biblical figures wear. It's a cape or a cloak, but 'manto' sounds more formal and dramatic. You'd use this word when describing a statue of a saint or a character in an epic play, not for your everyday jacket. It's the ultimate power-dressing accessory from the pre-blazer era.
usage_notes: A formal or literary term. 'Balabal' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang estatwa ng santo ay may hawak na tungkod at may suot na gintong **manto**.","translation":"The statue of the saint is holding a staff and wearing a golden **mantle**."},{"sentence":"Sa ilalim ng kanyang **manto**, itinago niya ang lihim na mensahe.","translation":"Under his **cloak**, he hid the secret message."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng kinikilala ng simbahan bilang banal dahil sa kanyang kabanalan at mga gawa; ginagamit bilang titulo bago ang pangalan ng isang babaeng santo.
etymology: From Spanish `santa`, feminine form of `santo` ("saint, holy").
original_explanation: This is the title for a female saint, the "she" in the holy power couple with "Santo." You'll see "Sta." plastered all over the Philippines as prefixes for town names (Sta. Rosa, Sta. Mesa), churches, and schools. It's the formal honorific for the holy women of the Catholic church.
usage_notes: The abbreviation `Sta.` is extremely common in place names. `Santa` is used for female saints, while `Santo` is for male saints.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang piyesta ng **Santa** Clara ay ipinagdiriwang tuwing Agosto.","translation":"The feast of **Saint** Clare is celebrated every August."},{"sentence":"Nakatira sila sa **Sta.** Mesa, Maynila.","translation":"They live in **Sta.** Mesa, Manila."}]

translation: to befriend; to make friends with
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng hakbang upang maging kaibigan ang isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "kaibigan" (friend). It's what you do when you see someone cool at a party and decide, "Yep, I'm gonna add them to my circle." It's the active process of turning a stranger into a tropa. Think of it as sending a friend request in real life.
usage_notes: Often used as a command or suggestion to make friends with someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kaibiganin** mo siya, mukha namang mabait.","translation":"**Befriend** him, he seems nice anyway."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **kaibiganin** ang taong laging nakasimangot.","translation":"It's hard **to make friends with** someone who is always frowning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na gumagamit ng panlilinlang, panloloko, o pandaraya upang makalamang sa kapwa o makamit ang isang layunin.
original_explanation: This is the person your mom warned you about. The 'budol-budol' expert, the online scammer promising a Nigerian prince's fortune, or that 'friend' who borrows money and suddenly gets amnesia. A 'manlilinlang' plays with your trust for their own gain. They're the human version of a phishing email.
usage_notes: A strong word implying deliberate and malicious deception.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa mga **manlilinlang** na nag-aalok ng mabilisang pagyaman.","translation":"Beware of **deceivers** who offer get-rich-quick schemes."},{"sentence":"Nahuli rin ang kilabot na **manlilinlang** sa kanilang lugar.","translation":"The notorious **swindler** in their area was finally caught."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay na inihanda, isinusuot, o ginagamit para sa natatanging okasyon ng isang pista.
original_explanation: This describes your 'pang-fiesta' outfit or the special 'handa'. That special dress or barong you only break out for town fiestas, Christmas, or when a balikbayan relative is treating everyone. It's the direct opposite of your 'pambahay' clothes; it's your 'pang-flex' gear for special occasions.
usage_notes: Can also function as a noun to refer to the thing itself (e.g., 'Isuot mo ang pamista mo.' - 'Wear your festive clothes.')
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilabas ni Lola ang mga pinggang **pamista** dahil Pasko na.","translation":"Grandma brought out the **festive** plates because it's Christmas."},{"sentence":"Ang barong na ito ang aking damit na **pamista**.","translation":"This barong is my **fiesta** attire."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang siyentipikong pag-aaral ng lipunan, kabilang ang mga pattern ng ugnayang panlipunan, interaksyon sa lipunan, at kultura sa pang-araw-araw na buhay.
original_explanation: The college course that tries to explain why we do the weird things we do. It's the academic study of 'sosyedad'—why we love chismis, why family is so important, why we have certain traditions. It's basically the science of how people 'people'.
usage_notes: Isang akademikong termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa sa mga paborito kong asignatura sa kolehiyo ang **Sosyolohiya** dahil ipinaintindi nito ang kilos ng mga tao sa lipunan.","translation":"One of my favorite subjects in college was **Sociology** because it made me understand human behavior in society."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na minamahal o may natatanging puwang sa puso; irog o sinta. Ginagamit bilang pantawag.
original_explanation: The default login password for your partner's heart (and sometimes their phone). It's a nickname, a term of endearment, and a one-word summary of a relationship. Used when you want to call their attention, like 'Mahal, pa-abot ng remote.'
usage_notes: Gumaganap bilang isang pangngalan, kadalasan bilang direktang pantawag (vocative) sa isang kasintahan, miyembro ng pamilya, o malapit na kaibigan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumain ka na ba, **mahal**?","translation":"Have you eaten, my **dear**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iisa-isa ng mga bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagduduro sa mga ito gamit ang isang matulis na bagay tulad ng patpat.
original_explanation: This is the action you do when making BBQ, isaw, or banana cue. You take pieces of meat or fruit and string them onto a bamboo stick. 'Magtuhog ka na ng baboy para maihaw na natin.' It can also be used figuratively, like stringing together a series of wins or achievements.
usage_notes: Commonly associated with cooking, especially grilling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinulungan niya ang kanyang ina na **magtuhog** ng baboy para sa barbecue.","translation":"He helped his mother **skewer** the pork for the barbecue."},{"sentence":"Kailangan pa nating **magtuhog** ng maraming sampaguita para sa mga kwintas.","translation":"We still need to **string together** a lot of sampaguita for the garlands."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na walang obligasyon o responsibilidad na harapin ang anumang kahihinatnan; walang pananagutan.
etymology: Kombinasyon ng 'di' (not), 'dapat' (should), at 'managot' (to be held accountable), na mula sa ugat na 'sagot'.
original_explanation: The official status of your groupmate who only contributed 'Good job guys!' in the group chat after you pulled an all-nighter to finish the project. They have plausible deniability. Sila yung mga 'seen-zoned' sa GC, pero unang-unang mag-claim ng credit.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa kontekstong legal o pormal, ngunit ginagamit din sa pang-araw-araw na usapan upang ilarawan ang isang taong umiiwas sa responsibilidad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa batas, ang mga menor de edad ay **di dapat managot** sa paraang katulad ng sa mga matatanda.","translation":"According to the law, minors **should not be held liable** in the same way as adults."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matigas at makahoy na panlabas na balat ng bunga ng niyog.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *baquŋ* ("sandok na gawa sa bao ng niyog").
original_explanation: Ito yung pinaglalagyan ng ice cream sa mga beach resort para sa "authentic tropical experience". Ginagamit din itong panggatong, bunot para sa sahig, o laruan noong wala pang Mobile Legends. 'Pag sinabing 'bao ng niyog', specific na ito sa niyog.
usage_notes: Madalas na tinutukoy bilang "bao ng niyog" upang linawin, ngunit ang "bao" lamang ay karaniwang tumutukoy dito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **bao** bilang lalagyan ng tubig.","translation":"He used the **coconut shell** as a container for water."},{"sentence":"Kinikiskis niya ang sahig gamit ang **bao** para kuminis.","translation":"She is polishing the floor using a **coconut shell** to make it shine."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng asin na may malalaki at magaspang na butil, karaniwang hindi gaanong naproseso at nagmumula sa mga minahan ng asin.
original_explanation: The chunky, less-refined cousin of table salt. It's what you use for making ice cream the 'dirty ice cream' way, or for cleansing your crystals if you're into that. It looks like tiny pebbles, hence the 'bato' (rock).
usage_notes: A compound noun. Used in specific culinary or other applications where fine salt is not suitable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit sila ng **asing-bato** at yelo para palamigin ang sorbetes.","translation":"They used **rock salt** and ice to chill the ice cream."},{"sentence":"Mas magandang gamitin ang **asing-bato** sa pag-ihaw ng isda.","translation":"It's better to use **rock salt** when grilling fish."}]

translation: to philosophize (negatively); to be a smart aleck
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng mga pangangatwiran na tila matalino ngunit kadalasan ay walang saysay, nakakainis, o paikot-ikot lamang.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your mom asks you to wash the dishes and you reply with, 'Ano ba talaga ang kahulugan ng 'malinis'? Nasa isip lang ba 'yan?' You're not being deep, you're just trying to get out of a chore. Stop trying to be Pilosopo Tasyo and just get the sponge.
usage_notes: Carries a connotation of being argumentative or talking back in a pseudo-intellectual way, rather than genuine philosophical inquiry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Huwag ka nang **mamilosopo** at sundin mo na lang ang utos ko,\" sabi ng nanay.","translation":"\"Stop being a **smart aleck** and just follow my orders,\" said the mother."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mamilosopo** sa klase kaya madalas siyang napapagalitan ng guro.","translation":"He likes to **philosophize** (talk back) in class, so he often gets scolded by the teacher."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sasakyang de-motor na may apat na gulong, karaniwang ginagamit sa paglalakbay sa kalsada.
original_explanation: Your metal status symbol that spends most of its life stuck in EDSA traffic. It's your ticket to freedom (road trips!) and your biggest source of financial stress (gas prices, coding, parking fees). Having a **kotse** in Manila is a love-hate relationship: you hate the traffic, but you love the aircon.
usage_notes: The most common term for a car in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana hindi ma-coding ang **kotse** ko bukas.","translation":"I hope my **car** isn't subject to the number coding scheme tomorrow."}]

translation: to wander around; to roam aimlessly
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakad o paglilibot sa iba't ibang lugar nang walang tiyak na patutunguhan o layunin.
etymology: From `magpa-` + reduplication of `gala` (to roam). The `magpa-` here acts as an intensifier or indicates a more deliberate, prolonged action of wandering.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you have no plans but don't want to stay home. It's the art of "tambay" but with more steps. You go to the mall, walk from end to end, look at stuff you won't buy, and then go home. It's being a "layas" but in a less rebellious, more bored kind of way.
usage_notes: Implies a lack of direction or purpose in movement. Often has a slightly negative connotation, as if one is wasting time, but can also be used neutrally.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpagala-gala** sa gabi at baka mapahamak ka pa.","translation":"Don't **wander around** at night, you might get into trouble."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magpagala-gala** sa mall kapag Sabado.","translation":"She loves to **roam aimlessly** in the mall on Saturdays."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang karne o laman na nagmumula sa baka, ginagamit sa iba't ibang lutuin tulad ng nilaga, kaldereta, at bistek.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "carne" (karne) at Tagalog na "baka" (cow).
original_explanation: The slightly more "sosyal" cousin of pork. It's what you use for bulalo on a rainy day or a killer bistek Tagalog. Beef is that reliable friend who's always there for the hearty, soul-warming meals. It's the Captain America to pork's Iron Man – classic, strong, and a staple hero.
usage_notes: Ang `karning-baka` ay isang alternatibong pagbaybay ngunit mas karaniwan at pormal ang `karneng-baka`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malambot ang **karneng-baka** na ginamit sa kaldereta.","translation":"The **beef** used in the caldereta is tender."},{"sentence":"Magkano na ang kilo ng **karneng-baka** sa palengke?","translation":"How much is a kilo of **beef** at the market now?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o hanapbuhay ng isang tao o pamilya upang matustusan ang kanilang mga pang-araw-araw na pangangailangan.
original_explanation: This is how you make a living. Your 9-to-5 job, your online store, your 'raket' on the side—anything you do to put food on the table and pay the bills. It's the 'buhay' (life) part of 'hanapbuhay' (search for life/livelihood). When lolas ask 'Ano'ng ikinabubuhay n'yo?' they're asking what your job is.
usage_notes: A very common and important word in discussions about economics, family, and work.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangingisda ang pangunahing **kabuhayan** sa kanilang bayan.","translation":"Fishing is the main **livelihood** in their town."},{"sentence":"Maraming nawalan ng **kabuhayan** dahil sa pandemya.","translation":"Many lost their **livelihood** because of the pandemic."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpatay at paghiwa-hiwalay sa mga bahagi ng isang hayop para kainin.
original_explanation: This is what your friendly neighborhood magkakarne does at the palengke every morning. It’s the process of turning a live chicken into your next tinola. It can also be used figuratively for "slaughtering" a song in karaoke or "butchering" a language. "Huwag mo nang ipilit, kinakatay mo lang yung kanta!"
usage_notes: Can be used literally for animals or figuratively for ruining something, like a performance or language.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Pasko, **nagkakatay** sila ng baboy para sa lechon.","translation":"Every Christmas, they **slaughter** a pig for lechon."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magkakatay** ng manok para sa ating hapunan?","translation":"Who will **butcher** the chicken for our dinner?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malambot at esponghadong laman na tumutubo sa loob ng niyog kapag ito ay nagsisimula nang umusbong; tumutukoy din sa buto sa pinakadulong bahagi ng gulugod ng tao.
original_explanation: The surprise inside an old coconut! It's that spongy, sweetish ball you find when a niyog starts to sprout. A delicious, underrated treat. Also, it's the anatomical word for your tailbone, the part that really hurts when you fall 'tumba' on your butt.
usage_notes: Has two distinct, common meanings. One botanical, one anatomical. Context is key to differentiate between the two.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap kainin ang **tumbong** ng niyog na bagong bukas.","translation":"The **coconut embryo** from a newly opened coconut is delicious to eat."},{"sentence":"Sumakit ang **tumbong** ko sa pagkakaupo buong araw sa opisina.","translation":"My **coccyx** hurts from sitting all day at the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Pasanhiin o maging dahilan ng paglundag ng isang tao, kadalasan dahil sa gulat, tuwa, o bilang utos.
etymology: From pa- prefix + lundag (leap) + -in suffix, a causative verb form.
original_explanation: The effect of a sudden loud noise, a surprise party, or seeing a cockroach fly. It's when you cause someone to perform an involuntary vertical take-off. Often followed by a 'Ay, kabayo!'
usage_notes: 'Lundag' implies a bigger, more forceful jump than 'lukso'. 'Palundagin sa gulat' (to make someone jump in surprise) is a very common collocation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang manggugulat, baka **palundagin** mo sa gulat ang lola.","translation":"Don't startle her, you might **make** grandma **jump** in surprise."}]

translation: to raid; to apprehend in a raid
meaning_filipino: Biglaang salakayin ang isang lugar upang hulihin ang mga taong pinaghihinalaang gumagawa ng ilegal na gawain.
original_explanation: This is the action word for a police raid you see on TV Patrol. When the PDEA decides to crash a party you weren't invited to anyway. 'Nabalitaan mo ba? Nagtimbog daw ng mga tulak sa kabilang kanto.'
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of law enforcement raiding a place to catch criminals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga pulis ay nagplanong **magtimbog** ng isang pugad ng mga magnanakaw.","translation":"The police planned to **raid** a den of thieves."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magtimbog** ng mga ismagler dahil mabilis silang makatakas.","translation":"It's difficult to **apprehend** smugglers in a raid because they escape quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling opisyal na pahayag o buod ng balita na inilalabas para sa publiko.
original_explanation: Parang office memo or yung announcement sa school na pinapaskil sa corkboard. Dito mo malalaman kung may pasok ba bukas dahil sa bagyo, o kung sino na naman ang "employee of the month". Sa panahon ngayon, ito yung mga "public advisory" post sa social media.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa pormal na konteksto tulad ng balita, anunsyo ng gobyerno, o mga pahayag sa paaralan at opisina.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilabas na ng PAGASA ang pinakabagong **bulitin** tungkol sa paparating na bagyo.","translation":"PAGASA has released the latest **bulletin** about the approaching typhoon."},{"sentence":"Basahin mo ang **bulitin** sa pader para malaman ang schedule ng klase.","translation":"Read the **bulletin** on the wall to know the class schedule."}]

translation: to give a noogie, to hit with the knuckles
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpalo o pagdiin sa ulo ng isang tao gamit ang mga buko ng daliri, karaniwang ginagawa bilang isang anyo ng magaspang na pagbibiro.
etymology: Origin is uncertain. Possibly from 'korona' (crown) referring to the crown of the head, or a playful corruption. The meaning 'noogie' is very specific in Philippine context.
original_explanation: This is the punishment your playmate gave you when you lost at a game of pogs or any other game in the 90s. It's that painful but funny grinding of knuckles on your head. The ultimate Pinoy childhood 'punishment.' In English, it's called a 'noogie.' 'One more tease, and I'll **give you a noogie**!'
usage_notes: A colloquial term, very common in childhood games and friendly roughhousing.
