usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil natalo siya sa laro, siya ang **kokornetin** ng grupo.","translation":"Because he lost the game, he's the one the group will **give a noogie** to."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **kornetin**, masakit sa ulo!","translation":"Don't **give me a noogie**, it hurts my head!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aparatong elektrikal na ginagamit upang maglipat ng enerhiyang kuryente mula sa isang sirkito patungo sa isa pa, na karaniwang nagpapabago sa antas ng boltahe.
original_explanation: That grey box on the Meralco post that goes "KABOOM!" before a brownout. It's the reason your charger doesn't fry your phone—it steps down the voltage. Also, Optimus Prime. But mostly the thing that fails during a typhoon.
usage_notes: Ginagamit din ito upang tukuyin ang mga karakter sa sikat na prangkisa ng media na "Transformers".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumabog ang **transpormer** sa kanto kaya nawalan kami ng kuryente.","translation":"The **transformer** on the corner exploded, so we lost power."},{"sentence":"Paborito ng anak ko ang mga laruang **Transpormer**.","translation":"My child's favorite toys are the **Transformers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino na tumutukoy sa bilang ng mga taong nakatalik ng isang indibidwal.
etymology: From English 'body count', originally military jargon for the number of enemies killed, now slang for sexual partners.
original_explanation: The question that can make or break a situationship in 2026. It's the Gen Z version of asking 'Ilan na naging syota mo?' but with more... spice. Whether you're proud of your 'score' or you'd rather plead the fifth, this term is all about your sexual history. It's either a 'slay' or a 'pass' moment, depending on who's asking.
usage_notes: A slang term borrowed directly from English. Used by younger generations. Can be considered a sensitive or private topic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-away sila dahil tinanong ni lalaki ang **body count** ng girlfriend niya.","translation":"They fought because the guy asked about his girlfriend's **body count**."},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, hindi mahalaga ang **body count** ng isang tao.","translation":"For me, a person's **body count** doesn't matter."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na gumigising sa damdamin, interes, o isipan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: 'Yung kanta na bigla kang napapa-senti, or 'yung art film na pinag-isipan mo ng isang linggo. It’s that "makes you think" feeling. A good cup of barako coffee is nakapupukaw ng diwa. A good chismis is nakapupukaw ng interes.
usage_notes: Used to describe things that capture attention, emotion, or intellect. The 'nakapu-' prefix indicates the ability or potential to cause the action of the root word 'pukaw' (to awaken/arouse).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang talumpati ay **nakapupukaw** ng damdamin at pag-asa.","translation":"His speech is **evocative** of emotion and hope."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap ako ng librong **nakapupukaw** ng imahinasyon.","translation":"I'm looking for a book that is **thought-provoking**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging matamlay, mahina, walang sigla, o kawalan ng enerhiya sa katawan at isipan.
etymology: From the root 'tamlay' (listlessness). Formed with the `pan-` prefix, where `pan-` + `tamlay` becomes `pananamlay` due to assimilation (t -> n).
original_explanation: That feeling on a Monday morning when your body has clocked in but your soul is still on weekend mode. It's the 'ayoko na, pagod na ako' mood, the physical and emotional burnout from too much work, adulting, or heartbreak. The official state of being 'walang gana.'
usage_notes: Describes a general state of weakness or lack of energy, which can be physical, emotional, or even economic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa sakit, nakaramdam siya ng matinding **pananamlay**.","translation":"Because of the illness, he felt extreme **lethargy**."},{"sentence":"Ang **pananamlay** ng ekonomiya ay nakaapekto sa maraming negosyo.","translation":"The **weakness** of the economy affected many businesses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng prutas na may berdeng balat, malaking buto sa gitna, at madilaw-dilaw na laman.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "avocado", na nagmula sa Nahuatl na "āhuacatl".
original_explanation: The official fruit of the millennials. Masarap gawing shake na may gatas at asukal, o i-smash sa toast para maging "avocado toast". Medyo high-maintenance, parang jowa mo, kailangan sakto ang pagkahinog. Mabilis masira 'pag napabayaan.
usage_notes: Ang baybay nito ay madalas na ginagawang Filipino bilang 'abokado'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong panghimagas ang **avocado** na may kondensada.","translation":"My favorite dessert is **avocado** with condensed milk."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at siksik na bloke ng mga pinatuyong pampalasa na inihahalo sa tubig upang makagawa ng sabaw.
etymology: From English "broth cube". A direct borrowing.
original_explanation: The magic cube that saves your ulam from being bland. The OG life hack of every nanay, tita, and budget-conscious student. Whether it's chicken, beef, or pork, one brothcube can turn plain hot water into "wow, ang sarap ng sabaw!". It's the MSG-adjacent secret weapon in every Filipino kitchen.
usage_notes: Often refers to a specific brand like Knorr or Maggi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdagdag ka ng isang **brothcube** sa tinola para mas malasa.","translation":"Add one **broth cube** to the tinola to make it more flavorful."}]

translation: to be stained; to be smeared
meaning_filipino: Ang mapahiran o malagyan ng dumi, mantsa, o anumang bagay na nag-iiwan ng marka.
original_explanation: That mini-heart attack when a drop of ketchup lands on your brand new white shirt. 'Naku, nalahiran tuloy!' It can also be used for your reputation. One wrong move sa office party and your good name might get 'malahiran' ng chismis. It's getting an unwanted mark, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical stains (dumi, mantsa) or for tainting one's reputation (dungis, kahihiyan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, baka **malahiran** ng tinta ang iyong damit.","translation":"Be careful, your clothes might **get stained** with ink."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **malahiran** ng anumang bahid ng korapsyon ang kanyang pangalan.","translation":"He doesn't want his name **to be smeared** by any trace of corruption."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng laro na nilalaro ng dalawang koponan na may tig-limang manlalaro bawat isa sa isang parihabang court, kung saan ang layunin ay i-shoot ang bola sa basket ng kalaban.
etymology: From English 'basketball', adapted to Filipino orthography.
original_explanation: The unofficial national religion of the Philippines. It's the reason why your street is closed on a Sunday afternoon, why your dad yells at the TV, and why every guy over 5'5" was told at some point, 'Sayang, 'di ka nag-basketbol.'
usage_notes: The sport and the ball itself are both called 'basketbol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig maglaro ng **basketbol** ang mga Pilipino.","translation":"Filipinos love to play **basketball**."},{"sentence":"Pahiram ng bola ng **basketbol**.","translation":"Can I borrow the **basketball** (ball)?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit sa paggawa ng isang kopya o replika; maaari ring tumukoy sa bayad para sa serbisyo ng pagkopya.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pang-` at `kopya` (mula sa Espanyol na *copia*).
original_explanation: This refers to any tool of the trade for duplication. Back in the day, it was carbon paper. Now, it's the mighty photocopy machine, the scanner, or even just your phone's camera when you're taking a picture of your classmate's notes. 'May barya ka para sa pangkopya?' is a classic student line, referring to the money for the service.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri ("makinang pangkopya") o pangngalan na tumutukoy sa mismong gamit o sa bayad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sira ang makinang **pangkopya** sa opisina.","translation":"The **copying** machine at the office is broken."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng dalawang piso para sa **pangkopya**.","translation":"I need two pesos for **photocopying**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na probisyon, kondisyon, o artikulo sa isang legal na dokumento, kontrata, o kasunduan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung 'fine print' sa kontrata na kailangan mong basahin nang mabuti bago ka pumirma. 'Yung part na nagsasabi kung ano ang mangyayari 'pag hindi ka nakabayad, 'yung mga terms and conditions, 'yung mga 'bawal' at 'dapat'. Each specific rule or condition in a contract is a 'klausula'. Pro-tip: basahin mo lagi 'yan.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit bilang terminong legal o panggramatika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **klausula** sa kontrata na nagsasabing bawal kang umalis sa kumpanya sa loob ng dalawang taon.","translation":"There is a **clause** in the contract that says you cannot leave the company for two years."}]

translation: to put in order, to make peaceful
meaning_filipino: Ayusin ang isang bagay o sitwasyon upang maging kalmado, payapa, at walang gusot.
original_explanation: This is what you try to do with your life after a major "sana all" moment on social media. You try to itiwasay your finances, your relationships, and your messy room. It's the verb form of achieving inner peace, or at least faking it 'til you make it.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or literary contexts, concerning order, peace, and settlement of affairs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinikap ng mga magulang na **itiwasay** ang pag-aaway ng kanilang mga anak.","translation":"The parents tried to **settle** the quarrel between their children."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga na **itiwasay** muna ang isipan bago gumawa ng malaking desisyon.","translation":"It's important to first **make** the mind **peaceful** before making a big decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Tubig na ligtas at malinis para sa pag-inom ng tao, na walang taglay na mapanganib na mikrobyo o kemikal.
etymology: Parirala na binubuo ng mga salitang Tagalog.
original_explanation: This is the fancy way of saying 'water that won't give you diarrhea.' It's the water from your filter, the blue container from the water station, or the bottled water you buy. It's the opposite of 'gripo water' that your tita warns you about.
usage_notes: Isang pormal o teknikal na termino para sa inuming tubig. Ang 'inuming tubig' ay isang mas karaniwang alternatibo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tiyaking **tubig na maaaring inumin** ang ipapainom sa mga bata.","translation":"Ensure that the water given to the children is **potable water**."},{"sentence":"Ang access sa malinis na **tubig na maaaring inumin** ay isang karapatang pantao.","translation":"Access to clean **potable water** is a human right."}]

meaning_filipino: Laging handa, gising ang diwa, at mapagmasid sa anumang maaaring mangyari.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling mo kapag may chismis na kumakalat sa office, alerto ka sa bawat bulungan. O kaya 'yung security guard sa village niyo na laging gising kahit 3 AM, naka-alerto mode.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat laging **alerto** ang mga mamamayan sa paparating na bagyo.","translation":"The citizens must always be **alert** for the coming typhoon."},{"sentence":"Naging **alerto** ang mga pulis matapos makatanggap ng ulat.","translation":"The police became **alert** after receiving a report."}]

translation: mutual giving; reciprocity; give and take
meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon ng palitan o pagkakaloob sa isa't isa; ang diwa ng pagtutulungan at pag-unawa kung saan ang bawat panig ay handang magparaya o magkaloob.
original_explanation: This is the secret to a long-lasting relationship, a peaceful group project, and surviving Metro Manila traffic. It's "give and take." You let a car merge, hoping someone lets you merge later. You wash the dishes today, your partner cooks tomorrow. Without pagbibigayan, everything is just "siraan" and "lamangan."
usage_notes: The `-an` suffix here implies a reciprocal or mutual action between two or more parties. It's different from `pagbibigay` (the act of one person giving).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ang **pagbibigayan** sa isang samahan upang ito'y magtagal.","translation":"**Reciprocity** is needed in a relationship for it to last."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng gulo dahil walang **pagbibigayan** sa pila.","translation":"Chaos erupted because there was no **give and take** in the queue."}]

translation: to be consistently unlucky; to keep having bad luck
meaning_filipino: Ang patuloy na makaranas ng kamalasan o hindi magandang kapalaran.
etymology: Reduplication of the root 'malas' (unlucky) with the verbal affix -in.
original_explanation: You know those days? You wake up late, spill coffee on your white shirt, miss the MRT, and then your boss asks for that report you forgot to finish. That's not just malas, that's being 'malas-malasin'. It's when the universe seems to be personally trolling you, and bad luck follows you around like a stray cat you made the mistake of feeding once. 'Kapag minamalas ka nga naman.'
usage_notes: The reduplication emphasizes the repetitive or continuous nature of the bad luck.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mukhang **malas-malasin** ako ngayong linggo; lahat na lang ng plano ko ay hindi natutuloy.","translation":"It seems I'm **consistently unlucky** this week; all of my plans fall through."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka naman **malas-malasin** habang buhay.","translation":"Don't worry, you won't **keep having bad luck** forever."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o ganting pagkilos ng paglusob o pag-atake sa isa't isa.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + sa- (repetition) + salakay (attack) + -an (locative/reciprocal suffix).
original_explanation: Yung moment na nag-aaway na ang dalawang pamilya sa isang teleserye, 'yun na 'yung pagsasalakayan. Parang bardagulan sa social media, pero may kasamang sandata. Or when two rival departments in the office are sabotaging each other's projects.
usage_notes: Denotes a reciprocal or mutual action of attacking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsasalakayan** ng dalawang tribo ay nagdulot ng malaking pinsala.","translation":"The **mutual attacking** between the two tribes caused great damage."},{"sentence":"Humantong sa madugong **pagsasalakayan** ang alitan sa lupa.","translation":"The land dispute led to a bloody **raiding of one another**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng araw mula sa paglubog ng araw hanggang sa pagsikat nito; gabi.
original_explanation: The official time for BPO workers to start their day, for 'night owls' to come alive, and for your 'marites' neighbor to start gathering the day's chismis. In the Philippines, 'night' is also when the best food parks open and when you finally have an excuse to say 'good night' to your demanding boss's emails. It's the opposite of day, duh.
usage_notes: Used colloquially in Taglish, often as a direct substitute for 'gabi', especially in greetings like 'good night'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan ang gimik mamayang **night**?","translation":"Where's the party later **tonight**?"},{"sentence":"Good **night**! Matulog ka na.","translation":"Good **night**! Go to sleep already."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nagpapanggap na iba sa kanyang tunay na pagkatao, karaniwan upang maging katanggap-tanggap sa isang grupo o magpasikat.
original_explanation: 'Yung friend mong biglang nag-post ng "listening to Nirvana" pero ang alam lang na kanta ay "Smells Like Teen Spirit". Sila 'yung mga nagkukunwaring fan ng isang bagay para lang maki-uso. Classic poser move.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga usapang impormal at sa social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **poser**, aminin mo na lang na hindi mo talaga alam 'yung banda.","translation":"Don't be a **poser**, just admit you don't really know the band."}]

meaning_filipino: Ibalik ang isang bagay sa dati nitong kinalalagyan, may-ari, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: That feeling of dread when your friend lends you money and says, "I-u-li mo agad ha!" It's the action of returning something, whether it's the Tupperware your mom sent to the neighbors, the book you borrowed, or the extra change the tindera gave you by mistake. Good karma points for doing it promptly!
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'isauli' and 'ibalik'. 'Isauli' is considered more formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **iuli** ang librong hiniram mo sa aklatan.","translation":"Don't forget to **return** the book you borrowed from the library."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **iuli** ang sukli dahil sobra ito.","translation":"I need to **return** the change because it's too much."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pangkat ng mga tao na may iisang lahi, wika, kultura, at kasaysayan, na naninirahan sa isang tiyak na teritoryo at bumubuo ng isang estado.
original_explanation: It's the bigger, more formal version of 'bansa'. Think of it as the 'in a relationship' status of a country with its people. It's what politicians talk about during SONA. It’s the whole squad, the entire archipelago, from Aparri to Jolo, united (in theory) by flag, language, and a shared love for adobo.
usage_notes: More formal and less common in everyday conversation than 'bansa'. Often used in political, academic, or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ating **nasyon** ay nahaharap sa maraming hamon sa kasalukuyan.","translation":"Our **nation** is facing many challenges at present."},{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng bawat mamamayan na maglingkod sa kanyang **nasyon**.","translation":"It is the duty of every citizen to serve his/her **nation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay ang pagbebenta ng isda, karaniwan sa palengke. Tinatawag ding mag-iisda o tindero/tindera ng isda.
original_explanation: The master of the early morning hustle in the palengke. They know their galunggong from their tilapia and can descale a fish faster than you can say 'patingin ng hasang.' Sila ang source ng 'bagong huli' at 'sariwa' (kahit minsan questionable).
usage_notes: More common native terms are 'tindero/tindera ng isda' or 'mag-iisda'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Suki ko ang **fish vendor** na iyon sa palengke.","translation":"That **fish vendor** in the market is my regular seller."},{"sentence":"Tinanong ko ang **fish vendor** kung sariwa ba ang tinda niya.","translation":"I asked the **fish vendor** if his wares were fresh."}]

translation: suppression; act of quelling or subduing
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpigil, pagkontrol, o pagpapahinto sa isang bagay na lumalala o nagiging magulo, tulad ng rebelyon, sunog, o malakas na damdamin.
original_explanation: This is what the firefighters do to a raging fire, or what the police do during a riot. On a personal level, it's you trying to suppress your 'kilig' when your crush looks at you, or trying to hold back your anger when your internet connection dies during a ranked game. It's damage control.
usage_notes: A formal word often used in news reports regarding crime, disasters, or controlling uprisings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Agad na rumisponde ang mga bumbero para sa **pagsawata** sa sunog.","translation":"The firefighters responded immediately for the **suppression** of the fire."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sustansiyang alkalina (sodium hydroxide) na ginagamit sa paggawa ng sabon at bilang sangkap sa paghahanda ng ilang kakanin upang magbigay ng kakaibang lasa at tekstura.
original_explanation: The secret ingredient that gives kutsinta and pichi-pichi their distinctively chewy, almost jelly-like texture. It's basically a food-grade chemical that sounds scary (lye?!) but is essential for that kakanin goodness you buy from the suki in the palengke. Just don't drink it straight, okay?
usage_notes: Commonly known as "lye water" in Filipino cooking contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng kaunting **lihiya** para maging makunat ang kutsinta.","translation":"A little bit of **lye water** is needed to make the kutsinta chewy."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paggamit ng **lihiya** dahil ito ay isang mabisang kemikal.","translation":"Be careful when using **lye** because it is a potent chemical."}]

translation: to find something heavy; to be burdened
meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman na ang isang bagay ay may labis na bigat, literal man o matalinghaga.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're carrying all the grocery bags in one trip, or when you're the only one working in a group project. It's the "sana all may tumutulong" moment. Can be physical weight or the emotional weight of your responsibilities, deadlines, and un-replied messages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nabibigatan** ako sa kahon na ito, pwede bang patulong?","translation":"I **find this box heavy**, can you help?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, kahit **nabibigatan** ka sa problema, malalagpasan mo rin 'yan.","translation":"Don't worry, even if you **feel burdened** by the problem, you will overcome it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng likidong panggatong na mula sa petrolyo at ginagamit para sa mga sasakyan na may internal combustion engine.
original_explanation: The lifeblood of your car, motorcycle, or the trike driver who takes you to the palengke. Its price is more volatile than your feelings for your ex. Every price hike makes you wish you just walked. Also known as *gasolina*.
usage_notes: Medyo luma na ang terminong ito at mas karaniwang ginagamit ang "gasolina".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkakaubusan na ng **bensina** sa mga gasolinahan.","translation":"The gas stations are running out of **gasoline**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong magpakarga ng **bensina** bago umalis.","translation":"I need to fill up with **gasoline** before leaving."}]

meaning_filipino: Kulang sa kahulugan, saysay, o kaisipan; hindi makatwiran o walang kabuluhan.
original_explanation: Ever read a poem or saw an indie film and thought, "Ano daw?" That's walang-diwa. It's a conversation that goes in circles, an argument based on feelings instead of facts, or a corporate mission statement full of buzzwords that mean nothing. It's like a hugot line that tries too hard to be deep but just ends up being confusing.
usage_notes: Can describe speech, writing, or actions that lack logic, substance, or purpose.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang talumpati ay maganda pakinggan ngunit **walang-diwa**.","translation":"His speech was nice to listen to but **senseless**."},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **walang-diwa** ang pag-aaway nila dahil sa maliit na bagay.","translation":"For me, their fighting over a small thing is **meaningless**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpilit na pagpapalabas ng hangin mula sa ilong upang alisin ang sipon o anumang nakabara dito.
original_explanation: That moment when your sipon is so bad, you need to excavate your nose like a miner. It's the act of declaring war on your clogged sinuses, usually with a tissue as your only weapon. 'Huy, 'wag dito, kadiri!' is the common reaction from your friends.
usage_notes: Used when telling someone to blow their nose or describing the act of doing so.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magpasinga** ka muna bago ka kumain para hindi ka mahirapang huminga.","translation":"**Blow your nose** first before you eat so you won't have trouble breathing."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang pasyente na **magpasinga** nang dahan-dahan.","translation":"The doctor advised the patient to **blow his nose** gently."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtindig o pag-angat mula sa pagkakahiga, pagkakaupo, o pagkakadapa; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagbawi mula sa isang pagkalugmok o sakuna.
original_explanation: The daily struggle against gravity and your bed. It's your mom's favorite word to shout at 6 AM. Also used as a battle cry for bouncing back from a failed subject, a bad breakup, or a national disaster. 'Bangon, Pilipinas!'
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa anyong pautos na 'Bangon!' (Get up!). Ang mga anyong pandiwa nito ay bumangon, bumabangon, babangon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bangon** na, tanghali na!","translation":"**Get up** now, it's late in the morning!"},{"sentence":"Kailangang **bumangon** muli pagkatapos madapa sa buhay.","translation":"One must **rise** again after stumbling in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng dalawa o higit pang bagay o tao na nasa tabi ng isa't isa.
original_explanation: You and your work bestie whose desks are next to each other. The last two pieces of chicken joy in the bucket. The couple on the bus who are so sweet you can feel the diabetes. `Magkatabi` is the physical state of being close enough to whisper chismis, share food, or accidentally fall asleep on someone's shoulder.
usage_notes: Describes the positional relationship between two or more entities. Can be used for people, places, or things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi silang **magkatabi** sa upuan sa klase.","translation":"They are always **side by side** in their seats in class."},{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas at Vietnam ay hindi **magkatabi** sa mapa.","translation":"The Philippines and Vietnam are not **adjacent** on the map."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na pagbati sa umaga, karaniwang sa araw ng kaarawan ng isang tao, na kinabibilangan ng pag-awit o pagtugtog ng musika sa madaling-araw.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "mañanita" (maliit na umaga, madaling-araw).
original_explanation: The OG birthday surprise! Before surprise parties became a thing, there was the 'mañanita'. It's when your family and friends wake you up at the crack of dawn with a song. It's sweet, traditional, and a little bit jarring if you're not a morning person. In recent times, it gained a whole new, controversial meaning thanks to a certain high-profile birthday party during lockdown. Iykyk.
usage_notes: Ang baybay ay madalas na ginagawang 'manyanita' sa Filipino. Nagkaroon ito ng bagong pampulitikang konotasyon sa Pilipinas dahil sa isang partikular na kaganapan noong panahon ng pandemya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginising siya ng isang **mañanita** mula sa kanyang mga kaibigan noong kaarawan niya.","translation":"He was woken up by a **dawn serenade** from his friends on his birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagguho o pagbagsak ng isang istraktura, tulad ng gusali o pader.
original_explanation: Imagine your Jenga tower finally giving up. Or that sandcastle hit by a wave. That's lugso. It's for things that collapse, cave in, or crumble down. It can also be a metaphor for your life plans after a major plot twist.
usage_notes: Primarily used for inanimate objects and structures, but can be used metaphorically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lugso** ang lumang tulay dahil sa malakas na lindol.","translation":"The old bridge **collapsed** due to the strong earthquake."},{"sentence":"Tila **lugso** ang kanyang mga pangarap nang hindi siya natanggap sa trabaho.","translation":"It seemed his dreams **crumbled** when he wasn't accepted for the job."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang organisadong pangkat ng mga taong may sandata, karaniwang tumutukoy sa militar o hukbong sandatahan ng isang bansa.
original_explanation: The official term for the military, like the AFP (Armed Forces of the Philippines). These are the folks you see in uniform, the ones who are ready to defend the country. It's a serious job, not like your keyboard warrior army on Twitter.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit sa pormal na balita at usapang pampamahalaan. Ang buong tawag ay "Sandatahang Lakas ng Pilipinas."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Sandatahan** ng Pilipinas ay laging handang maglingkod sa bayan.","translation":"The **Armed Forces** of the Philippines is always ready to serve the country."},{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa **sandatahan** pagkatapos ng kolehiyo.","translation":"He joined the **military** after college."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkaing-kalye sa Pilipinas na gawa sa pinrosesong karne ng pusit o isda na hinulmang pabilog, piniprito, at inilalagay sa tuhog.
original_explanation: An essential member of the Tusok-Tusok squad, along with fishball and kikiam. These white, bouncy balls of processed seafood are deep-fried by Manong on his street cart and then drowned in your choice of sweet, spicy, or vinegar-based sauce. It's the go-to merienda after school or a cheap, satisfying snack on your commute. The ultimate question is never "if" you'll get squidballs, but "how many sticks?"
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the popular Filipino street food.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng sampung pisong **squidball**.","translation":"I'd like to buy ten pesos worth of **squid balls**, please."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng sawsawang maanghang para sa **squidball**.","translation":"The spicy sauce for the **squid balls** is delicious."}]

translation: to be able to prepare; to be prepared
meaning_filipino: Ang makapag-ayos o makapagplano nang maaga para sa isang gawain, okasyon, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: The verb form of "Be ready!" When your mom shouts "Maghanda ka na!" it means get ready. So, `mahanda` is the ability to get ready. "Sana **mahanda** ko lahat bago dumating ang mga bisita" (I hope I can prepare everything before the guests arrive). It's the state of being ready for anything, from a surprise quiz to an unannounced visit from your Tita.
usage_notes: Maaaring mangahulugang "maging handa" (bilang isang estado) o "makapaghanda" (bilang isang kilos). Nililinaw ng konteksto ang kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **mahanda** ang lahat ng iyong gamit bago ang biyahe.","translation":"You need to **be able to prepare** all your things before the trip."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya **nahanda** ang kanyang sarili sa biglaang pagsusulit.","translation":"He wasn't **able to prepare** himself for the surprise quiz."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng orkid na pinagmumulan ng pampalasa na may katangi-tanging aroma at lasa, na malawakang ginagamit sa mga panghimagas at pabango.
original_explanation: The flavor you get when you're too scared to try the Avocado-Chili-Salted-Caramel-Delight. **Banila** is the default setting, the "safe choice" in the ice cream world. But hey, sometimes, classic is best. It's the foundation of many great desserts, just like a stable internet connection is the foundation of a good WFH day.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong lasa ng ice cream ang **banila**.","translation":"My favorite ice cream flavor is **vanilla**."},{"sentence":"Nagdagdag siya ng katas ng **banila** sa keyk na kanyang niluluto.","translation":"She added **vanilla** extract to the cake she was baking."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangangahulugang karaniwan, palagian, o ayon sa nakasanayan.
original_explanation: Has two main vibes. 1) The 'suki' vibe: 'Isang large milk tea, **regular** sugar level po.' You're a loyal customer. 2) The 'meh' vibe: 'Kamusta ka?' 'Okay lang, **regular**.' It means things are just normal, nothing spectacular, nothing terrible. The default setting of life.
usage_notes: Used in both its English sense (e.g., regular size) and as a state of being (e.g., 'regular lang ang araw ko').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa na siyang **regular** na customer sa kapihan na iyon.","translation":"He is now a **regular** customer at that coffee shop."}]

translation: to be able to dip; can be dipped
meaning_filipino: May kakayahang ilubog nang bahagya at panandalian sa isang likido, karaniwan sa sarsa o inumin.
original_explanation: The crucial verb for enjoying lumpiang shanghai, french fries, or chicharon. 'Pwedeng makisawsaw?' is the polite way of asking to use the shared bowl of suka, toyo, or ketchup. Without this verb, food is just less fun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mo **masawsaw** ang biskwit kung ubos na ang kape mo.","translation":"You can't **dip** the biscuit if your coffee is all gone."}]

translation: to put a period; to end
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng bantas na tuldok sa dulo ng isang pangungusap; maaari ring mangahulugang tapusin o wakasan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Literally, to put a period at the end of a sentence. Figuratively, it’s what you do to a toxic relationship. 'Tapos na tayo, period, no erase.' You're putting a full stop. It's the ultimate 'It's over,' the final word. 'Panahon na para magtuldok sa lahat ng drama sa buhay mo.'
usage_notes: Can be literal (punctuation) or figurative (ending something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **magtuldok** sa katapusan ng bawat pangungusap.","translation":"Always **put a period** at the end of every sentence."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magtuldok** na sa kanilang pag-uusap.","translation":"She decided to **put an end** to their conversation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tela na gawa mula sa mga hibla ng halamang lino. Ginagamit ito sa paggawa ng damit, kurtina, at mga kagamitan sa bahay.
original_explanation: The official fabric of tita-hood and beach weddings. It's what you wear when you want to look effortlessly classy and rich, even if you're sweating buckets in the Philippine heat. Wrinkles easily, but that's part of the "I'm on vacation" charm.
usage_notes: This is a direct loanword and is used in contexts related to fashion, home goods, and textiles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap matulog kapag bagong palit ang **linen** ng kama.","translation":"It feels great to sleep when the bed **linen** is newly changed."},{"sentence":"Mas presko isuot ang mga damit na gawa sa **linen** kapag tag-init.","translation":"It's cooler to wear clothes made of **linen** during the summer."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbabantay sa isang namatay bago ang libing, karaniwang ginagawa sa bahay o sa isang punerarya.
original_explanation: This is the Filipino wake, a multi-day event that's part solemn vigil, part family reunion, and part 24/7 mahjong and coffee session. It's where you pay your respects to the deceased and offer condolences (and maybe some *abuloy*) to the family. It's the ultimate 'last call' for saying goodbye.
usage_notes: Often shortened to just 'burol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumalaw kami sa **pagbuburol** ng lola ng aming kaibigan.","translation":"We visited the **wake** of our friend's grandmother."},{"sentence":"Magdamag kaming nagbantay sa **pagbuburol**.","translation":"We stayed up all night watching over the **vigil**."}]

translation: to become fierce, to become savage
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging mas mabagsik, marahas, o malupit kaysa sa dati.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your nanay when you come home at 4 AM and she's been waiting all night. Or your quiet officemate who suddenly 'bumangis' during a presentation and destroyed all the arguments. It’s the transformation from a cute kitten to a tiger.
usage_notes: Describes a change in state towards fierceness or cruelty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumangis** ang anyo ng halimaw nang ito'y masugatan.","translation":"The monster's appearance **became fierce** when it was wounded."},{"sentence":"Tila **bumangis** ang kaniyang pagtrato sa mga empleyado matapos siyang ma-promote.","translation":"His treatment of the employees seemed to have **become harsher** after he was promoted."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o paggamit ng insenso sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar, karaniwan bilang bahagi ng isang ritwal o seremonya.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa ng pari sa misa na iwinawasiwas niya 'yung parang gold na parol na may usok (thurible)? 'Yun 'yon. Sa bahay naman, ito 'yung ginagawa ni Lola sa bagong bili na sasakyan para daw iwas-disgrasya. It's basically a spiritual fumigation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan daw **suuban** ang bagong bahay para itaboy ang masasamang espiritu.","translation":"They say the new house needs **to be censed** to drive away evil spirits."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging pinalayas o ipinatapon sa isang malayong lugar bilang parusa.
original_explanation: The OG "ghosting." This is when you're sent away, either literally like Rizal in Dapitan, or figuratively, like when you're kicked out of the family group chat for sending too many weird memes. It’s the state of being an outcast, the ultimate "you can't sit with us."
usage_notes: Often used in historical or political contexts, but can also be used for being cast out from a group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkatapon** ni Rizal sa Dapitan ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng kasaysayan.","translation":"Rizal's **exile** to Dapitan is an important part of history."},{"sentence":"Simula nang mag-iba siya ng landas, ramdam niya ang **pagkatapon** mula sa kanyang mga dating kaibigan.","translation":"Since he changed his path, he has felt his **banishment** from his old friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglilinis ng isang bagay gamit ang tubig, at kalimitan ay may kasamang sabon.
original_explanation: The ultimate chore. It's what you do to your hands to fight germs, to the dishes after you eat (or what you promise your mom you'll do 'later'), and to your feet when you get home from a long commute. The eternal enemy of the 'tamad' and the best friend of 'malinis'.
usage_notes: A general term for washing. For specificity, you add what is being washed, e.g., 'maghugas ng kamay' (wash hands), 'maghugas ng pinggan' (wash dishes). To wash clothes is 'maglaba'. To wash one's body is 'maligo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **maghugas** ng kamay bago at pagkatapos kumain.","translation":"Always **wash** your hands before and after eating."},{"sentence":"Sino ang taya sa **paghugas** ng mga plato ngayong gabi?","translation":"Who is assigned to **wash** the plates tonight?"}]

meaning_filipino: 1. Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nasa ibabaw ng likido at hindi lumulubog. 2. Tumutukoy sa isang taong wala sa sarili, hindi nakapokus, o malayo ang pag-iisip.
original_explanation: This has two meanings. Literally, it's floating, like a log in a river. But 99% of the time, it means your brain has left the chat. You're physically present in the meeting, but mentally, you're planning your dinner or replaying a K-drama scene. When someone asks you a question and all you can say is 'Ha?', you are officially 'lutang'. It's the default state of mind during a 3 PM meeting after a heavy lunch.
usage_notes: The figurative meaning (distracted, spaced-out) is extremely common in modern colloquial speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasensya na, medyo **lutang** ako ngayon dahil kulang sa tulog.","translation":"Sorry, I'm a bit **distracted** today due to lack of sleep."},{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang isang piraso ng kahoy na **lutang** sa ilog.","translation":"He saw a piece of wood **floating** on the river."}]

translation: to straighten; to go straight; to reform
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging diresto o hindi baluktot ng isang bagay; ang pagbabago ng isang tao tungo sa mas mabuting pag-uugali.
original_explanation: Can refer to literally straightening your back ("Tumuwid ka ng upo!") or a road that goes straight. But the more powerful meaning is about people. It's when someone who was a "pasaway" finally gets their act together. They "walk the straight path" or "nagtino." It's the character development arc we love to see in teleseryes.
usage_notes: Past/Completed aspect of the verb. Can be physical or metaphorical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumuwid** ang kanyang landas mula nang magkaroon siya ng anak.","translation":"His path **straightened** ever since he had a child."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng lindol, **tumuwid** ang dating nakatagilid na poste.","translation":"After the earthquake, the previously tilted post **straightened**."}]

translation: act of making something round; act of deceiving
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghugis sa isang bagay upang maging bilog; sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ang panloloko o pagpapaikot sa isipan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what you do to pandesal dough. Figuratively, it's what a con artist or a manipulative ex does to your head ('binibilog ang ulo'). They twist facts and sweet-talk you until you're confused and agree to something you shouldn't. So, be careful if someone is doing a lot of 'pagbilog' on you.
usage_notes: Has both a literal (to make round) and a very common figurative (to deceive, to fool) meaning. The figurative use is often in the phrase 'pagbilog ng ulo' (making the head round/spinning the head).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbilog** ng masa para sa siopao ay nangangailangan ng kasanayan.","translation":"The **act of making the dough round** for siopao requires skill."},{"sentence":"Magaling siya sa **pagbilog** ng ulo ng mga botante tuwing eleksyon.","translation":"He is good at the **act of deceiving** voters during elections."}]

translation: To weed; to clear weeds from (a place)
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-aalis ng mga damo o di-kanais-nais na halaman sa isang taniman, hardin, o bukid.
original_explanation: It's like decluttering your life, but for plants. It's the agricultural equivalent of unfollowing toxic people from your social media feed, but instead of people, you're pulling out pesky 'damo' so your prized talong and ampalaya can thrive and reach their full potential.
usage_notes: A common farming or gardening term. 'Gamas' is the root word (weeding). 'Gamasan' is the verb form 'to weed [a place]'. 'Gamisin' means 'to weed [a specific thing]'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **gamasan** ang bukid bago magtanim ng palay.","translation":"We need to **weed** the field before planting rice."},{"sentence":"Inutusan niya ang mga trabahador na **gamasan** ang kanilang hardin.","translation":"He ordered the workers to **clear the weeds from** their garden."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagpunta muli sa isang lugar, tao, o kalagayan na pinanggalingan.
original_explanation: That ex who keeps sliding into your DMs. Or the amazing feeling of going home to the province for Christmas. It's the act of returning, coming back. 'Ang feelings, parang multo, laging bumabalik.'
usage_notes: Can be used for physical return, or the return of feelings, memories, or situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumabalik** na ang mga OFW para sa Pasko.","translation":"The OFWs **are returning** for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Unti-unti nang **bumabalik** sa normal ang sitwasyon.","translation":"The situation **is** slowly **returning** to normal."}]

translation: to lose heart, to be discouraged
meaning_filipino: Mawalan ng pag-asa, sigla, o tapang na ipagpatuloy ang isang gawain o laban.
etymology: Idiomatic phrase, literally "for the inside/will to be broken".
original_explanation: That feeling when you fail an exam you studied so hard for, or when your crush leaves you on 'seen'. It's the emotional equivalent of a system crash. You want to give up and just binge-watch Netflix for a week. It's the step before "sumuko na."
usage_notes: A common idiom to express discouragement or loss of morale. Past tense is 'nasira ang loob'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **masisira ang loob** kahit maraming pagsubok ang dumating.","translation":"Don't **lose heart** even if many challenges come your way."},{"sentence":"**Nasira ang loob** niyang mag-apply ulit matapos siyang hindi matanggap sa trabaho.","translation":"He **was discouraged** from applying again after he wasn't accepted for the job."}]
related: ["mawalan ng pag-asa","sumuko","panghinaan ng loob","lakas ng loob"]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng benda o panali sa isang sugat o nasaktang bahagi ng katawan.
original_explanation: The act of 'first aid-ing' a cut or sprain. It's what your mom does when you fall off your bike, or what the clinic nurse does when you get a papercut. It's the verb for wrapping something up to protect it, usually a 'boo-boo'.
usage_notes: Verb form derived from 'benda' (bandage).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **bendahan** ang sugat mo para hindi maimpeksyon.","translation":"You need to **bandage** your wound so it doesn't get infected."},{"sentence":"**Binendahan** ng doktor ang kanyang pilay na braso.","translation":"The doctor **bandaged** his sprained arm."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na pinaikling anyo ng salitang "paano," na ginagamit sa pagtatanong tungkol sa paraan, kondisyon, o pamamaraan.
original_explanation: The short, text-friendly, and more "chismis-ready" version of 'paano'. It's what you type when your friend posts a travel pic: "Pano ka nakapunta diyan?!" (How'd you get there?!) or when someone solves a problem you've been stuck on: "Pano mo ginawa yun?" (How'd you do that?). It’s 'how' but with a sense of urgency and casualness.
usage_notes: Mahigpit na itinuturing na kolokyal o impormal. Ang "paano" ang ginagamit sa pormal na pagsulat at pananalita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pano** kung umulan bukas? Tuloy pa ba tayo?","translation":"**What if** (colloquial 'how about if') it rains tomorrow? Are we still on?"},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng luto mo! **Pano** mo 'to ginawa?","translation":"Your cooking is great! **How** did you make this?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasuotang walang manggas na isinusuot sa ibabaw ng pang-itaas na damit, karaniwang bahagi ng isang pormal na terno.
original_explanation: That sleeveless thing you wear to look extra 'pogi' at a formal event, or what your lolo wears over his white sando while reading the newspaper. From Spanish 'chaleco'.
usage_notes: Also used to refer to safety vests or reflectorized vests.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong magsuot ng **tsaleko** bilang bahagi ng uniporme.","translation":"You need to wear a **vest** as part of the uniform."},{"sentence":"Ang gwapo niya sa kanyang itim na **tsaleko** at kurbata.","translation":"He looks handsome in his black **vest** and tie."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa balarila, ito ay isang kataga o titik na nag-uugnay sa dalawang salita, karaniwan ay sa isang pang-uri at pangngalan, upang gawing mas madulas ang pagbigkas.
original_explanation: The wingman of Tagalog grammar. It's that little `-ng`, `-g`, or `na` that connects words so they flow smoothly, like "magandang umaga" instead of the awkward "maganda umaga". It’s the ultimate matchmaker, making sure words stick together beautifully. Without it, our sentences would sound like a robot with a stutter.
usage_notes: A specific grammatical term. The three ligatures in Filipino are 'na', '-ng', and '-g'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pang-angkop** na '-ng' ay ginagamit kapag ang salita ay nagtatapos sa patinig.","translation":"The **ligature** '-ng' is used when the word ends in a vowel."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan namin sa Filipino ang tamang paggamit ng mga **pang-angkop**.","translation":"We are studying the correct use of **ligatures** in our Filipino class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panandalian at bahagyang paglitaw o pagpapakita ng isang bagay o tao.
etymology: Root word 'silay' means a glimpse or a brief look.
original_explanation: This is the 'now you see me, now you don't' of the Tagalog world. It's that fleeting moment you see your crush in the hallway. It's the sun peeking through the clouds after a storm. It’s the 'cameo appearance' of a celebrity at an event. A *pagsilay* is always short, sweet, and leaves you wanting more. It’s the ultimate ‘pa-effect’.
usage_notes: Often used in a poetic or romantic context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsilay** ng buwan sa likod ng mga ulap ay isang magandang tanawin.","translation":"The **brief appearance** of the moon behind the clouds was a beautiful sight."},{"sentence":"Nag-abang ang mga fans para sa kahit isang **pagsilay** man lang ng kanilang idolo.","translation":"The fans waited for even just a **glimpse** of their idol."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsiyasat sa katawan o damit ng isang tao sa pamamagitan ng pagdama o pagkapkap upang maghanap ng mga nakatagong bagay.
original_explanation: This is more specific than 'kumapa'. 'Kumapkap' is what a security guard does to you before you enter a mall or a concert. They're patting you down to check for... well, you know. It’s an inspection by touch, a full-body scan done by hand.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of searching a person's body or clothing for concealed items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasanay na ang mga tao na **kumapkap** ang guwardiya sa kanilang mga bag.","translation":"People are used to the guard **frisking** their bags."},{"sentence":"Maingat na **kumapkap** ang pulis sa suspek.","translation":"The police officer carefully **patted down** the suspect."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang laro kung saan ginagaya ang mga kilos at gawain ng isang sundalo; maaari ring tumukoy sa mga laruang kawal.
etymology: From 'sundalo' with reduplication of the first two syllables and the suffix '-an', indicating a game or imitation.
original_explanation: This is the classic childhood game of playing war with plastic green army men or just running around with a stick yelling 'Bang! Bang!'. It can also be used sarcastically to describe someone acting tough or militaristic without real authority, like a security guard who thinks he's a general. 'Stop with your sunda-sundaluhan, you're not the boss.'
usage_notes: Can refer to the toy soldiers themselves or the act of playing the game.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig maglaro ng **sunda-sundaluhan** ang mga batang lalaki sa kalye.","translation":"The young boys love to play **soldiers** on the street."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **sunda-sundaluhan** ang kanyang kahon ng laruan.","translation":"His toy box is full of **toy soldiers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pandiwa na nangangailangan ng tuwirang layon (direct object) na tumatanggap ng kilos upang mabuo ang diwa ng pangungusap.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng `pandiwa` (verb) at `palipat` (transferring), na tumutukoy sa kilos na 'lumilipat' sa isang layon.
original_explanation: This is a verb that can't be single; it needs a 'jowa'—a direct object—to receive its action and make sense. The verb 'bumili' (to buy) feels incomplete. Bumili ng ano? It needs a target, like 'bumili ng kape.' The action 'lipat' (transfers) to an object. It's a clingy verb.
usage_notes: Isang terminong pang-gramatika. Ang kabaligtaran nito ay 'pandiwang katawanin' (intransitive verb).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'kumain' sa pangungusap na 'Kumain siya ng mansanas' ay isang **pandiwang palipat**.","translation":"The word 'kumain' in the sentence 'He ate an apple' is a **transitive verb**."},{"sentence":"Itinuro sa amin ng guro ang pagkakaiba ng **pandiwang palipat** at katawanin.","translation":"Our teacher taught us the difference between a **transitive verb** and an intransitive one."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng bahagyang pagdikit o pagdama sa isang bagay o tao gamit ang kamay o ibang bahagi ng katawan.
original_explanation: It's that gentle touch. Not the creepy kind, okay? More like when you're testing if the sinigang is still hot, or when your crush's arm accidentally brushes against yours and your whole week is made. It's the physical contact, from a simple tap to a full-on chancing moment (just kidding... mostly).
usage_notes: Often used to describe a gentle or light touch, as opposed to a forceful one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **paghipo** lamang sa kanyang balikat ay sapat na upang malaman niyang naroon ako.","translation":"Just one **touch** on her shoulder was enough for her to know I was there."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang hindi kinakailangang **paghipo** sa mga paninda sa palengke.","translation":"Avoid unnecessary **touching** of the goods at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtatakwil, pagtatapon, o pag-alis sa isang bagay, paniniwala, o responsibilidad.
original_explanation: The Marie Kondo method, but for your life. It's 'thank u, next' in action. This is you deleting your ex's photos, throwing away old habits, or finally deciding to 'unfriend' toxic people. It's the powerful act of saying 'I don't need this in my life anymore' and actually doing it.
usage_notes: A strong word that implies a decisive and often permanent rejection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagwawaksi** sa masamang bisyo ay isang malaking hamon.","translation":"The **renunciation** of a bad habit is a big challenge."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **pagwawaksi** sa dating pamumuhay.","translation":"He showed his **rejection** of his former way of life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang tao, bagay, o sasakyan na nakatagpo habang ito ay gumagalaw sa kasalungat na direksyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung ex mong bigla mong makikita sa mall. You have two options: 1) Tumingin sa malayo at magpanggap na may hinahanap. 2) Mag-smile na parang nanalo ka sa lotto since you broke up. That awkward nod is the default setting. 'Yan ang ultimate kasalubong challenge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-menor ang tsuper nang makita ang paparating na **kasalubong** na trak.","translation":"The driver slowed down when he saw the **oncoming** truck."},{"sentence":"Si Ana pala ang **kasalubong** ko sa hagdan kanina.","translation":"So it was Ana whom I **met coming from the opposite direction** on the stairs earlier."}]

translation: to make excuses; to find loopholes
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na paggawa ng dahilan o paghahanap ng paraan upang makaiwas sa isang tungkulin, pananagutan, o sitwasyon.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `pa-` (causative prefix) + reduplicated `lusot` (to get through, to slip past). The reduplication implies a repeated or habitual action.
original_explanation: Ah, the national sport! This is what you do when you're late for work ('Grabe po 'yung traffic!'), when you haven't finished your report ('Biglang nag-brownout po, Ma'am!'), or when you're trying to get past a checkpoint. It's the art of creatively weaving through rules and responsibilities.
usage_notes: Carries a slightly negative and informal connotation, implying evasiveness or dishonesty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **magpalusut-lusot** at aminin mo na ang iyong pagkakamali.","translation":"Stop **making excuses** and just admit your mistake."},{"sentence":"Mahusay siyang **magpalusut-lusot** tuwing nahuhuli siyang pumasok sa klase.","translation":"He's good at **finding ways to get by** whenever he's late for class."}]

translation: to terrorize, to shock, to horrify
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdudulot ng matinding takot, sindak, o pangingilabot sa isang tao o lugar.
original_explanation: This is what your chismosa tita does for fun. She lives to gimbalin the family with scandalous 'news' during reunions. It's the active form of causing that 'oh no' moment.
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the one being shocked or terrorized.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **gimbalin** ang mga bata sa mga kwentong katatakutan.","translation":"Don't **terrorize** the children with horror stories."},{"sentence":"**Ginimbal** ng balita ang buong bansa.","translation":"The news **shocked** the entire nation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga nakausling bahagi sa gilid ng isang gulong o engranahe na sumasabit sa iba pang bahagi upang magdulot ng pag-ikot o paggalaw.
original_explanation: Not the kind of teeth you brush. These are the teeth in a machine, a bike chain, or a watch. When they don't align, parang kayo ng ex mo, hindi na nag-wo-work.
usage_notes: A specific mechanical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinalitan ng mekaniko ang may sirang **ngipin ng gulong** sa makina.","translation":"The mechanic replaced the broken **gear tooth** in the machine."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi natuloy o ipinawalang-bisa ang isang nakatakdang gawain, pangyayari, o kasunduan.
etymology: From English "cancel" with the Tagalog prefix "na-".
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na ready ka na umalis, bihis na bihis, tapos biglang may mag-text na "Sorry, nacancel." Parang love life mo, akala mo tuloy na, 'yun pala drawing lang. Or 'yung flight mo na nacancel dahil sa bagyo, at stranded ka sa airport. #SanaAllHindiCancelled
usage_notes: A very common Taglish word used in everyday conversation, especially for plans, events, or orders.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sayang, **nacancel** ang concert dahil sa masamang panahon.","translation":"It's a shame, the concert **was canceled** due to bad weather."},{"sentence":"**Nacancel** ang meeting namin kanina kaya umuwi ako nang maaga.","translation":"Our meeting **was canceled** earlier, so I went home early."}]

translation: to be misplaced; to be lost; to stray
meaning_filipino: Ang pansamantalang pagkawala ng isang bagay sa kinalalagyan nito o ang paglihis ng isang tao mula sa tamang landas o grupo.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for when you can't find your keys, your phone, or your wallet. It's not *gone* gone (like 'nawala'), just... misplaced. 'Yung tipong, "Nandito lang 'yon kanina!" Also applies to your friend who suddenly disappears in the middle of a mall sale. "Huy, san na si bes? **Nawaglit** na naman!"
usage_notes: Implies a temporary or accidental loss, often within a known vicinity, as opposed to 'mawala' which can be more permanent or definitive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-ingatan ang salamin ko, ayokong **mawaglit** na naman iyan.","translation":"Please take care of my glasses, I don't want them to **get misplaced** again."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang dami ng tao sa Divisoria, madaling **mawaglit** sa iyong mga kasama.","translation":"With so many people in Divisoria, it's easy to **get separated** from your companions."}]

translation: to be implicated; to be involved
meaning_filipino: Masangkot o maisama sa isang usapin, krimen, o kontrobersiya, kadalasan nang hindi direkta.
original_explanation: 'Yung napadaan ka lang sa gulo ng tropa mo pero bigla kang kasama sa "Guidance, now!" Ito 'yung "nadamay lang po" moment mo. You weren't the main character of the chismis, but you got a supporting role you didn't audition for.
usage_notes: Often used in legal, political, or gossip (chismis) contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **madalawit** sa isyu ng kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He doesn't want to be **implicated** in his friends' issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa matapang na amoy na karaniwang nakasusugat sa pang-amoy, o sa maanghang na lasa ng pagkain.
original_explanation: 'Hanghang' is that kick you get from Bicol Express or the siling labuyo you bravely bit into. It's also the smell of a freshly opened bottle of patis or bagoong that makes your nose twitch. It's the flavor profile that makes you say 'Tubig, please!' but also 'Isa pa nga!'.
usage_notes: While it can mean pungent smell, it is far more commonly used to mean spicy/hot taste. 'Anghang' is the more common modern spelling and pronunciation for the spicy taste.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **hanghang** ang amoy ng nasusunog na plastik.","translation":"The smell of burning plastic is **acrid**."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng sabaw na may kaunting **hanghang**.","translation":"I want soup with a bit of **spiciness**."}]

translation: to like something; to choose to want
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng pagkagusto o pagkakaroon ng pagnanais sa isang partikular na tao o bagay. Ito ay ang pokus sa bagay na ginugusto.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "gusto" when the *thing you want* is the star of the show (object-focus). Think of it as actively choosing to like something. Like when your friend sets you up on a blind date and you're trying your best to find them charming. "Sinusubukan kong gustuhin siya." It's the effort you put into liking someone or something.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of 'gusto'. The subject of the sentence is the thing being liked/wanted. For example, "Gustuhin mo sana ang regalo ko." (I hope you like my gift.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **gustuhin** ang isang taong hindi ka naman pinapansin.","translation":"It's hard **to like** a person who doesn't even notice you."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **gustuhin** ng mga bata ang niluto kong gulay.","translation":"I hope the children will **like** the vegetables I cooked."}]

translation: to shake something off; to dust off
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng malakas o mabilis na pag-alog sa isang bagay upang maalis ang alikabok, tubig, o anumang nakadikit dito.
original_explanation: This is what you do to a rug before bringing it inside, or to your umbrella after walking in the rain. It's a vigorous shake to get rid of the unwanted stuff. Metaphorically, it's what you need to do after a bad day or a toxic encounter—`magwagwag` ng bad vibes! Shake it off, just like Taylor Swift said.
usage_notes: Often used for clothes, rugs, and other fabrics. It implies a more vigorous action than just `pagpag`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magwagwag** ng basahan sa labas para hindi pumasok ang alikabok.","translation":"You need **to shake off** the rag outside so the dust doesn't get in."},{"sentence":"**Nagwagwag** siya ng kanyang buhok na nabasa ng ulan.","translation":"She **shook** her hair that got wet from the rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging tunaw o lusaw ng isang bagay na solido, o ang pagbaba ng konsentrasyon ng isang timpla sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag ng likido.
original_explanation: Ever had iced coffee that sat out for too long? That sad, watery state is pagkalasaw. It's the melting of ice in your drink, making it "matabang" (bland). It's when the "sarsa" (sauce) is too thin. Figuratively, it can even describe a feeling or an idea that has lost its potency or intensity. "Yung galit ko, nag-pagkalasaw na rin sa tagal ng paghihintay."
usage_notes: Often refers to drinks, sauces, or anything that can be diluted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa init, mabilis ang **pagkalasaw** ng yelo sa baso.","translation":"Because of the heat, the **melting** of the ice in the glass was fast."},{"sentence":"Ayoko ng kape na halata ang **pagkalasaw**; gusto ko 'yung matapang.","translation":"I don't like coffee where the **dilution** is obvious; I want it strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagprotekta sa sarili o sa iba laban sa isang atake o panganib; isang paliwanag o argumento upang ipagtanggol ang isang aksyon o paniniwala.
original_explanation: Sa basketball, ito 'yung ginagawa mo para 'di maka-shoot ang kalaban. Sa away-magjowa, ito 'yung 'Let me explain...' mo kapag nahuli ka. It's your shield, your excuse, your justification. 'Wala kang **depensa**!' means you're caught red-handed.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng palakasan, batas, at pang-araw-araw na argumento.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay ang **depensa** ng kanilang koponan kaya sila nanalo.","translation":"Their team's **defense** was excellent, that's why they won."},{"sentence":"Ano ang iyong **depensa** sa mga akusasyon laban sa iyo?","translation":"What is your **defense** against the accusations against you?"}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing dalisay, malinis, o puro ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pag-aalis ng mga dumi, di-kanais-nais na elemento, o kasalanan.
etymology: From 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'dalisay' (pure). 'To cause to be pure.'
original_explanation: This is what you do to water to make it drinkable, or to gold to make it 24k. It's the process of removing the impurities. It can also be very spiritual or emotional. 'Pumunta siya sa retreat para magpadalisay ng kanyang kaluluwa.' (He went on a retreat to purify his soul.) It's about getting back to the pure, essential, unadulterated version of something.
usage_notes: Used both in a literal, chemical sense (refining substances) and a figurative, spiritual/moral sense (purifying the soul/intentions).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga proseso upang **magpadalisay** ng maruming tubig para ito ay maging inumin.","translation":"There are processes to **purify** dirty water to make it potable."},{"sentence":"Ang pagdarasal ay isang paraan upang **magpadalisay** ng puso at isipan.","translation":"Prayer is a way to **refine** the heart and mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panahon ngayon; ang mga pangyayari, kalagayan, o bagay na umiiral sa kasalukuyang sandali o panahon.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa 'sa' + 'lukob' (to cover/encompass), na tumutukoy sa panahong sakop ng ngayon.
original_explanation: The 'now'. Hindi 'yung past na pinagsisisihan mo, hindi 'yung future na pinag-aalala mo. Ito 'yung time na nag-sscroll ka sa phone mo instead of doing what you're supposed to be doing. Live in the kasalukuyan, bes!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **kasalukuyan**, marami pa ring hamon ang kinakaharap ng ating bansa.","translation":"In **the present**, our country still faces many challenges."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi natitiyak, hindi natutukoy, o walang kaalaman tungkol dito.
original_explanation: This is the official status of your love life according to your friends. It's also the answer to 'Kailan ka ga-graduate?' or 'Saan napunta yung 13th month pay mo?'. A state of beautiful, blissful, or stressful ignorance.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit bilang tugon ('Hindi ko alam') o bilang panlarawan ('isang di-alam na dahilan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **di-alam** na dahilan, biglang tumigil ang sasakyan.","translation":"For an **unknown** reason, the car suddenly stopped."},{"sentence":"Ang kinabukasan ay isang **di-alam** na landas na ating tatahakin.","translation":"The future is an **unknown** path that we will walk."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghiwalay o pagbubukod sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay na pinaghihinalaang may nakahahawang sakit upang maiwasan ang pagkalat nito.
original_explanation: Ah, the word that defined 2020. It's when your house became your office, gym, cinema, and prison all at once. The ultimate "staycation" you never asked for, fueled by Dalgona coffee, TikTok trends, and endless Zoom calls. To be 'quarantined' was to be grounded by the universe.
usage_notes: Became an everyday word during the COVID-19 pandemic. Often used in its past tense form "ikinuwarentenas".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **ikuwarentenas** ang sinumang magpositibo sa test.","translation":"Anyone who tests positive needs to be **quarantined**."},{"sentence":"**Ikinuwarentenas** ang buong barangay dahil sa mabilis na pagkalat ng sakit.","translation":"The whole barangay was **quarantined** due to the rapid spread of the disease."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng paghamak, pag-aglahi, o pagtuya sa kapwa sa pamamagitan ng salita o kilos.
original_explanation: That person who always has a sarcastic comment ready. They live for the eye-roll and the backhanded compliment. Kung may Olympic sport for throwing shade, sila ang gold medalist. They find joy in making others feel small. The ultimate Marites antagonist.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa katangian ng isang tao o sa kalikasan ng isang kilos o komento.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **mapanlibak** sa kanyang mga katrabaho.","translation":"She is known for being **scornful** towards her colleagues."},{"sentence":"Isang **mapanlibak** na ngiti ang isinukli niya sa akin.","translation":"He returned a **mocking** smile to me."}]

translation: someone in the same line/row; aligned with
meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na nasa kaparehong hanay, pila, o linya. Sa diwang patalinghaga, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang taong may kaparehong pananaw, prinsipyo, o propesyon.
original_explanation: Your work bestie who gets your struggle because you're both in the same department. When you're lining up for concert tickets and you make friends with the person in front of you, they're your kalinya. It's about being on the same wavelength, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: The prefix 'ka-' indicates companionship or being part of the same group/category.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **kalinya** ko sa aming propesyon bilang mga guro.","translation":"She is **in the same line** as me in our profession as teachers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na butas, siwang, o anumang munting espasyo na maaaring gamitin upang sumilip o tumingin nang palihim.
etymology: Mula sa "silip" + hulaping "-an" na tumutukoy sa lugar.
original_explanation: The analog version of your CCTV. Ito yung maliit na butas sa pinto para malaman mo kung yung delivery rider na ba yan o yung nangungutang mong kapitbahay. The original 'private browsing' window.
usage_notes: Ang diin ay nasa ikalawang pantig (si-LI-pan) para sa pangngalan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumingin muna siya sa **silipan** ng pinto bago ito buksan.","translation":"He looked through the **peephole** of the door first before opening it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mag-iwan ng marka, mantsa, o dungis sa isang bagay, reputasyon, o pangalan.
original_explanation: Can be literal, like when the spaghetti sauce from your Jollijeep meal decides to jump onto your white uniform. Or it can be figurative, like a scandal that can **magbatik** (tarnish) a politician's 'clean' reputation. It's leaving a mark you probably don't want.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally (for physical stains) and figuratively (for reputation).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siyang huwag **magbatik** ng tinta ang kanyang bagong damit.","translation":"He/She was careful not to **stain** his/her new clothes with ink."},{"sentence":"Ang isang pagkakamali ay maaaring **magbatik** sa pangalan ng buong pamilya.","translation":"One mistake can **tarnish** the name of the entire family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang titulong ibinibigay sa Obispo ng Roma na siyang pinakamataas na pinuno ng Simbahang Katolika sa buong mundo.
etymology: From Spanish 'papa' (pope), from Ecclesiastical Latin 'pāpa', from Ancient Greek 'πάππας' (páppas, 'daddy').
original_explanation: The OG. The big boss of the Catholic Church. When he visits the Philippines, it's a national holiday and traffic is insane. He's the one with the cool hat (papal tiara) and the popemobile.
usage_notes: Spelled with a capital 'P' when used as a title for the head of the Catholic Church (e.g., Papa Francisco). The stress is on the first syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumalaw ang **Papa** sa Pilipinas noong 2015.","translation":"The **Pope** visited the Philippines in 2015."}]

meaning_filipino: Ibigay ang isang bagay (tulad ng pagsusulit o porma) sa isang tao upang kanyang sagutan o punan ng mga kasagutan.
original_explanation: This verb is the bane of every student's existence. It's what the teacher does with the test paper. "Ipasagutan ninyo ito sa isang buong papel." It refers to the act of giving a document (like a form, a survey, or a test) to someone for them to answer. It's also what you do when you need your parents to sign a consent form.
usage_notes: The focus of this verb is the thing being answered (the test, the form). Often used with the `i-` prefix (`ipasagutan`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasagutan** mo sa mga estudyante ang survey form na ito.","translation":"**Have the students answer** this survey form."},{"sentence":"Ang buong exam ay **pinasagutan** sa loob lamang ng isang oras.","translation":"The entire exam was **made to be answered** in just one hour."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pamamaraan ng pangangatwiran o argumento na sumusuri sa mga magkasalungat na pananaw upang makarating sa isang mas mataas na antas ng katotohanan o sintesis.
original_explanation: This is some next-level, philosophical stuff. Think of it as a formal debate where you take an idea (thesis), its opposite (antithesis), and smash them together to create a new, more evolved idea (synthesis). It's what happens in your brain when you want to eat lechon (thesis) but also want to be healthy (antithesis), so you decide to just eat a small piece with a side of salad (synthesis). It's the intellectual process of resolving contradictions.
usage_notes: A term used in philosophy, logic, and social theory. Not common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Marxismo ay gumagamit ng materyalismong **diyalektika** upang suriin ang kasaysayan.","translation":"Marxism uses dialectical materialism to analyze history."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan namin sa klase ng pilosopiya ang konsepto ng **diyalektika** ni Hegel.","translation":"We studied Hegel's concept of **dialectics** in our philosophy class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang halaga o bayad sa paglalakbay o pagsakay sa isang pampublikong sasakyan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "viaje" (biyahe) na dinagdagan ng hulaping "-ada" na tumutukoy sa aksyon o halaga na may kaugnayan dito.
original_explanation: Yung pamasahe mo sa jeep, bus, o eroplano. Kung walang biyada, walang biyahe. Sabi nga nila, 'walang forever', pero 'yung pagtaas ng presyo ng biyada, mukhang forever.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit bilang kasingkahulugan ng 'pamasahe'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkano po ang **biyada** hanggang Cubao?","translation":"How much is the **fare** to Cubao?"},{"sentence":"Kulang ang pera ko para sa **biyada** pauwi.","translation":"I don't have enough money for the **fare** going home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pag-iisip kung saan ang isang tao ay nakapag-iisip nang malinaw, lohikal, at walang pagkalito.
original_explanation: Eto yung state of mind mo before mag-send ng resignation letter, o bago ka mag-confess sa crush mo. Hindi ka lasing, hindi ka puyat, hindi ka galit. You've had your coffee, you've meditated, and your brain is running on all cylinders. Perfect for making big life decisions or winning arguments.
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression combining 'maliwanag' (bright/clear) and 'isip' (mind).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong magkape para maging **maliwanag ang isip** ko sa miting mamaya.","translation":"I need to drink coffee so I can be **clear-headed** for the meeting later."},{"sentence":"Mahirap magdesisyon kapag hindi **maliwanag ang isip**.","translation":"It's hard to make a decision when you're not **clear-headed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong parirala na nangangahulugang sinadya ng isang tao na maging mapanukso, palaaway, o magsimula ng gulo sa araw na iyon nang walang partikular na dahilan.
etymology: An internet meme phrase that became popular in the late 2010s and early 2020s.
original_explanation: The official motto for when you log into social media ready to argue. It's when your friend posts a *very* controversial opinion about pineapple on pizza. They didn't just stumble into a fight; they brewed their coffee, stretched, and made a conscious decision to be a public menace for the day. It’s the energy of 'Gusto ko ng gulo.'
usage_notes: Used humorously to describe someone who is being intentionally provocative or argumentative online or in person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe 'yung post ni Marites, she really **woke up and chose violence** today.","translation":"Marites's post was intense, she really **woke up and chose violence** today."},{"sentence":"Nag-reply siya sa lahat ng bashers niya. He literally **woke up and chose violence**.","translation":"He replied to all his bashers. He literally **woke up and chose violence**."}]

translation: to leave a gap; to set slightly ajar
meaning_filipino: Mag-iwan ng puwang o bahagyang pagkakabukas sa pagitan ng dalawang bagay, tulad ng pinto o bintana.
original_explanation: This is what you do to the door when you want some privacy but also want to hear the chismis from the living room. Or leaving the window "naka-awang" just enough for some air but not enough for the neighbor's cat to get in. It's the art of being half-open, half-closed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iawang** mo lang ang pinto para makapasok ang hangin.","translation":"Just **leave the door slightly ajar** so the air can come in."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **iawang** nang malaki ang bintana dahil baka may pumasok.","translation":"Don't **leave a wide gap** in the window because someone might enter."}]

translation: to sparkle; to glisten; to twinkle
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuga ng panandalian at maningning na liwanag, tulad ng sa bituin, diyamante, o tubig na nasisinagan ng araw.
original_explanation: 'Yung mga mata mo nung nakita mo 'yung 13th-month pay mo. Biglang **kumislap**! O 'yung sequins sa damit ni Vice Ganda, kislap kung kislap. It's that ✨bling-bling✨ effect.
usage_notes: A very poetic and descriptive word. Used for literal light (stars, gems) and figurative light (eyes sparkling with joy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumislap** ang mga bituin sa madilim na kalangitan.","translation":"The stars **twinkled** in the dark sky."},{"sentence":"**Kumislap** ang kanyang mga mata nang matanggap ang aginaldo.","translation":"Her eyes **sparkled** when she received the Christmas gift."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbuo, paggawa, o pag-imbento ng isang bagay. Ito ay anyong pautos o pawatas na nakapokus sa bagay na gagawin.
original_explanation: This is the 'To-Do' version of 'likha'. When your boss tells you to 'create a report' or when your inner artist tells you to 'create a masterpiece'. It's the action part. 'Tara, **likhain** natin ang pangarap nating future, chos!'
usage_notes: This is the object-focus infinitive/imperative form. The actor-focus counterpart is 'lumikha'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang utos sa kanila ay **likhain** ang isang mural na nagpapakita ng kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The order for them is **to create** a mural that shows the history of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong **likhain** ang sarili mong bersyon ng adobo.","translation":"Try **to create** your own version of adobo."}]

translation: to stand someone up, to flake on someone
meaning_filipino: Sa kolokyal na gamit, ang kilos ng hindi pagtupad sa isang usapan o plano sa isang tao, na nag-iiwan sa kanya na naghihintay.
etymology: Semantic shift from the literal verb, applied to the slang meaning of "drowing" (failed plan).
original_explanation: The verb form of the slang "drowing". When someone "drowingan ka," it means they flaked on your plans. You were all dressed up, ready to go, and they hit you with the "Sorry, can't make it!" text 5 minutes before you're supposed to meet. The pain is real. It's the act of turning a solid plan into a mere "drowing."
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in its slang meaning of flaking on a plan. Synonymous with "indianin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo naman akong **drowingan** sa Sabado, nakapagpaalam na ako sa nanay ko.","translation":"Please don't **stand me up** on Saturday, I already got permission from my mom."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lihis, tago, o hindi pangkaraniwang daanan; isang sulok o tagong lugar.
original_explanation: That hidden coffee shop in a small alley that only you and your friends know about. That's a **liklik**. Or that shortcut you take to avoid traffic that goes through a weird neighborhood. It's a nook, a cranny, a secret spot, or a detour. A place 'off the beaten path'.
usage_notes: Carries a connotation of being hidden, indirect, or secretive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **liklik** ang eskinita patungo sa kanilang bahay.","translation":"There are many **turns/detours** in the alley going to their house."},{"sentence":"Natagpuan niya ang isang tahimik na **liklik** sa loob ng malaking hardin.","translation":"He found a quiet **nook** inside the large garden."}]

translation: to make something red; to cause to blush
meaning_filipino: Gawing pula ang kulay ng isang bagay; magdulot ng pamumula ng mukha dahil sa hiya o kilig.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'pula' (red) at panlaping 'pa- -hin'.
original_explanation: Two meanings here. First, literally to make something red, like when you add food coloring to your icing. "Papulahin mo 'yung frosting."
