One little click, one little pihit of the virtual knob, and peace is restored.
usage_notes: Often used as a noun, but is the root for verbs like 'pihitin' (to turn/twist something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang **pihit** ng manibela, naiwasan niya ang aksidente.","translation":"With one **turn** of the steering wheel, he avoided the accident."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng dalawang **pihit** sa kanan para mabuksan ang safe.","translation":"It needs two **twists** to the right to open the safe."}]

meaning_filipino: Usapang walang kabuluhan o walang tigil; daldal.
etymology: Maaaring onomatopeya, ginagaya ang tunog ng daldalan.
original_explanation: This is that endless chika that isn't really going anywhere. It's the 'um, so, like, ano na?' conversation that fills the silence but doesn't really say much. Think of the background noise in a coffee shop, but it's all coming from one person's mouth. Less about substance, more about the sound of talking.
usage_notes: Madalas may negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig na ang usapan ay walang saysay o nakakainis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **satsat** at magtrabaho ka.","translation":"Stop the **chatter** and get to work."},{"sentence":"Puro **satsat** lang siya, wala namang gawa.","translation":"He's all **talk**, but no action."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa ilong na matulis at katangian ng pagiging matangos.
original_explanation: Ito yung #NoseGoals. When someone says your nose is 'matangos', it's a compliment. It means it's well-defined, prominent, and not flat ('pango'). It's the kind of nose that looks good from the side profile, the one that makes people ask, "Saan mo pinagawa 'yan?" even if it's all-natural.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe a person's nose. Often as 'matangos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami ang nagsasabi na **tangos** ang kanyang ilong.","translation":"Many say that her nose is **prominent**."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang magkaroon ng ilong na **matangos**.","translation":"She wants to have a **pointed** nose."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sunod-sunod at mabilis na pagpapatunog ng mga kampana ng simbahan, karaniwan bilang panawagan sa misa o pagdiriwang.
etymology: From Spanish 'duplicar' (to duplicate/double), referring to the rapid succession of rings.
original_explanation: This is the OG church notification bell. Before SMS blasts and Facebook events, the dupikal was how you knew it was time for misa or a fiesta. It's that frantic, festive ringing that tells the whole town something important is happening.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious or historical context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig sa buong bayan ang **dupikal** ng mga kampana.","translation":"The **peal of bells** was heard throughout the town."},{"sentence":"Ang **dupikal** ay hudyat na magsisimula na ang prusisyon.","translation":"The **ringing of bells** is the signal that the procession is about to begin."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan tinatambak o itinatapon ang mga basura, dumi, o anumang bagay na maramihan.
original_explanation: The official term for your 'chair-drobe'—that one chair in your room where you pile all your clothes. It's a dumpsite, a landfill, or any place where things are just heaped together. 'Yung kwarto mo, naging tambakan na ng mga kahon galing Shopee!'
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang literal na tapunan ng basura o gamitin bilang hyperbole para sa anumang magulo at bunton na lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **tambakan** ng basura ang bakanteng lote sa kanto.","translation":"The vacant lot on the corner became a **dumpsite** for trash."},{"sentence":"Ayusin mo nga ang mga gamit mo, parang **tambakan** na ang mesa mo.","translation":"Organize your things, your table looks like a **pile**."}]

meaning_filipino: (Pangngalan) Isang tao na may magkahalong lahi, karaniwan ay Pilipino at dayuhan (tulad ng Espanyol, Amerikano, o Tsino). (Pang-uri) Naglalarawan sa isang taong may magkahalong lahi.
original_explanation: The OG 'half-half'. In the Philippines, this usually means someone who is part-Filipino and part-Caucasian or Spanish, often resulting in features like fair skin, a pointed nose, and lighter-colored eyes. They're the ones who often end up as celebrities or models. The female version is 'mistisa'.
usage_notes: The masculine form is 'mistiso', feminine is 'mistisa'. It's a very common descriptor in Philippine society.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming artista sa Pilipinas ay mga **mistiso** at mistisa.","translation":"Many celebrities in the Philippines are **people of mixed race** (mestizos and mestizas)."},{"sentence":"Ang **mistiso** niyang itsura ay namana niya sa kanyang amang Amerikano.","translation":"His **mestizo** features were inherited from his American father."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng karamdaman sa pag-iisip kung saan ang isang tao ay may matinding takot sa mga masisikip o saradong lugar.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung feeling na parang mamamatay ka na 'pag nasa siksikang elevator, 'pag na-stuck sa traffic sa loob ng bus, o 'pag pinilit kang magsuot ng damit na tatlong size na mas maliit. 'Klaustropobya' is the extreme fear of tight spaces, 'yung tipong gusto mo nang sirain 'yung pinto para lang makahinga.
usage_notes: Isang terminong klinikal na naging bahagi na ng pang-araw-araw na usapan upang ilarawan ang takot sa masisikip na lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **klaustropobya**, mas gusto niyang gumamit ng hagdan kaysa sa elevator.","translation":"Because of his **claustrophobia**, he prefers to use the stairs instead of the elevator."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na inirrolyo o pinagsama-sama sa paraang pabilog, tulad ng papel, tela, o dahon.
original_explanation: Parang lumpia, pero hindi pagkain. O kaya parang diploma na naka-roll. 'Yung mga love letters ng lolo't lola mo na tinago sa baul, malamang naka-**bilot** 'yun. Puwede ring bilot ng pera na bigay ni ninong.
usage_notes: Madalas tumutukoy sa papel, mapa, o anumang manipis na bagay na maaaring irolyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniabot niya sa akin ang isang **bilot** ng lumang mapa.","translation":"He handed me a **roll** of an old map."},{"sentence":"May isang **bilot** ng pera sa ilalim ng unan.","translation":"There is a **roll** of money under the pillow."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag ng salungat na opinyon o pagtutol sa isang ideya, panukala, o kilos.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng "di-" (hindi) at "pagsang-ayon" (ang akto ng pagpayag).
original_explanation: That moment in a meeting when your boss has a "brilliant" idea, and you're the only one brave enough (or foolish enough) to say "Sir, with all due respect...". That's di-pagsang-ayon. It's the formal way of saying "I object!" or "pass sa idea mo, bes."
usage_notes: Isang pormal na termino na ginagamit sa mga talakayan, debate, at sa kontekstong legal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **di-pagsang-ayon** ang mga miyembro tungkol sa bagong patakaran.","translation":"The members had a **disagreement** about the new policy."},{"sentence":"Ipinahayag niya ang kanyang **di-pagsang-ayon** sa plano ng pamahalaan.","translation":"He expressed his **dissent** with the government's plan."}]

translation: to get bruised; to get a contusion
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng bangas, pasa, o galos sa katawan, karaniwan sa mukha, dahil sa isang tama o pagkakabangga.
etymology: ma- (potential verb prefix) + bangas (bruise, contusion) + -an (locative/referential suffix)
original_explanation: The result of walking into a glass door you thought was open. Or the minor but annoying injury you get from a 'beso-beso' gone wrong. 'Uy, anong nangyari sa'yo, bakit ka may pasa?' 'Ah, nabangasan lang, 'wag mo nang itanong.' It’s a less severe 'mabukulan'.
usage_notes: Usually refers to a bruise or minor wound on the face or head, but can be used for other body parts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paglalaro at baka ka **mabangasan**.","translation":"Be careful when playing or you might **get bruised**."},{"sentence":"**Nabangasan** ang noo niya nang mauntog sa pader.","translation":"His forehead **got bruised** when he bumped his head on the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagyuko o pagbaba ng ulo at katawan bilang tanda ng paggalang, pagsang-ayon, o pagkuha ng isang bagay mula sa ibaba.
original_explanation: It's that slight bow you give to your elders after saying 'Mano po.' Or the way you bend down to pick up something you dropped. It’s a gesture of respect, submission, or simply a physical action of stooping. In a 'hugot' sense, it's what you do when you finally accept defeat in an argument with your partner: you just bow your head and say, 'Opo, tama ka.'
usage_notes: 'Pagyuko' is a much more common synonym. 'Pagyukdo' sounds a bit more formal or literary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagyukdo** ay isang paraan ng pagpapakita ng respeto sa kulturang Hapones.","translation":"**Bowing** is a way of showing respect in Japanese culture."},{"sentence":"Isang mabilis na **pagyukdo** ang ginawa niya para pulutin ang nahulog na barya.","translation":"He did a quick **stoop** to pick up the fallen coin."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng kawalan ng interes, sigla, o pagkabahala sa mga bagay na karaniwang pumupukaw ng damdamin.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'apatía' o Ingles na 'apathy'.
original_explanation: That "wala akong pake" energy. It's when you see another corruption scandal and you just sigh and scroll past it on Facebook because you've seen it a million times. It's the opposite of being a "woke" Tito/Tita.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pormal o pampanitikang konteksto. Ang "kawalan ng pakialam" ay mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **apatiya** ng mga mamamayan sa halalan ay isang malaking suliranin.","translation":"The **apathy** of the citizens during elections is a big problem."},{"sentence":"Nakakabahala ang lumalaganap na **apatiya** sa mga kabataan ngayon.","translation":"The spreading **apathy** among the youth today is concerning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na paglalakad ng isang grupo ng mga tao, lalo na bilang bahagi ng isang seremonya, parada, o ritwal ng relihiyon.
original_explanation: That slow, solemn walk you see during Holy Week or a town fiesta, usually with saints on carriages (carroza) and people holding candles. It's also a metaphor for anything that moves incredibly slowly, like the line at the LTO. "Grabe, parang prusisyon ang pila sa bangko!"
usage_notes: Mahigpit na nauugnay sa mga gawaing panrelihiyon, lalo na sa Katolisismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang sumama sa **prusisyon** para sa Mahal na Araw.","translation":"Many people joined the **procession** for Holy Week."},{"sentence":"Ang bagal ng usad ng trapiko, parang **prusisyon**.","translation":"The traffic is moving so slowly, like a **procession**."}]

translation: to be able to catch (with a hook); to be able to snag
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang makuha o mahuli ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay isda, gamit ang bingwit o kawil.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na after mo mag-swipe-right sa dating app, may nag-match. Ayun, nakabingwit ka! Pwede ring literal na sa pangingisda, o 'yung pag-snag mo ng last piece ng lechon sa handaan.
usage_notes: This is the 'maka-' actor-focus, potential aspect of the verb. It signifies the ability to catch or hook something, both literally and metaphorically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **makabingwit** ako ng malaking isda mamaya sa lawa.","translation":"I hope I can **catch** a big fish later at the lake."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **nakabingwit** din siya ng magandang trabaho pagkatapos ng maraming buwan.","translation":"Finally, she was able **to snag** a good job after many months."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na ginagamit sa pagkuha o pagsalok ng likido o butil-butil na materyales mula sa isang lalagyan.
original_explanation: Your ultimate weapon against gravity and messy spills. Whether it's for getting water from a 'banga' (clay jar), scooping rice from the sack, or getting the last drop of soup from the pot. The pangsalok is the unsung hero of the Filipino kitchen and banyo. The 'tabo' is the most famous pangsalok.
usage_notes: Can refer to a ladle ('sandok'), a dipper ('tabo'), or any scooping instrument. The specific type is often understood from context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasaan na ang **pangsalok** ng bigas? Ubos na ang laman ng rice cooker.","translation":"Where is the rice **scooper**? The rice cooker is already empty."},{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng **pangsalok** para hindi matapon ang sabaw.","translation":"Use a **ladle** so the soup doesn't spill."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng pagkainis, pagkayamot, o pagkasuklam dahil sa isang bagay na nakagagambala o paulit-ulit.
original_explanation: **Bugnot** is the feeling of being 'pikon' and 'inis' rolled into one. It's the low-key grumpiness you feel when the Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting during an online meeting. It's the exasperation of explaining the same thing five times to a client. It's not explosive rage (that's 'bugnit'), but a deep, simmering annoyance where your face is probably in a permanent frown. You're 'in a mood'.
usage_notes: Describes a state of being annoyed or irritated. The adjective form 'bugnutin' (irritable) is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata sa mukha niya ang **bugnot** habang naghihintay sa napakatagal na pila.","translation":"His **annoyance** was obvious on his face while waiting in the very long line."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **bugnot** ang kanyang boses nang malaman niyang kanselado ang biyahe.","translation":"His voice was full of **exasperation** when he found out the trip was canceled."}]

translation: to fall or sit down sprawled out; to flop down
meaning_filipino: Biglaang mapaupo o mapahiga sa sahig nang walang-ingat at hindi maayos ang posisyon, karaniwan dahil sa pagod o pagkatumba.
etymology: From `ma-` (potential verb prefix) + `salampak` ("to sit or fall sprawled out").
original_explanation: That thing you do on your bed or sofa after a long day at work or school. You don't just sit; you flop. It's an ungraceful, heavy, and deeply satisfying collapse. It’s the physical embodiment of "I give up for today." Also what happens when you slip on a freshly mopped floor.
usage_notes: Conveys a sense of heaviness, exhaustion, or clumsiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod, **nasalampak** na lang siya sa sahig pagdating sa bahay.","translation":"From extreme exhaustion, she just **flopped down** on the floor upon arriving home."},{"sentence":"Nadulas siya sa basang sahig at **nasalampak** nang todo.","translation":"He slipped on the wet floor and **fell down sprawled out** completely."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tubig na pinaghugasan ng bigas bago ito isaing.
original_explanation: The OG, all-natural beauty secret and plant fertilizer of every Pinoy household. Before you throw it out, ask your lola or your plantita/plantito tita if they need it. It's the ultimate 'one man's trash is another man's treasure' in the kitchen.
usage_notes: Often used for watering plants, washing face, or as a base for some broths.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Idilig mo sa mga halaman ang **hugas-bigas** para tumaba sila.","translation":"Water the plants with the **rice water** so they'll grow healthy."},{"sentence":"Sabi ni Lola, maganda raw sa mukha ang **hugas-bigas**.","translation":"Grandma said that **rice water** is good for the face."}]

translation: to throb, to pulsate, to beat (like a heart)
meaning_filipino: Ang ritmikong pagtibok o paggalaw, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa puso, pulso, o isang bahagi ng katawan na may sakit.
original_explanation: It's your heart's reaction when you see your crush walking towards you, going from a chill lo-fi beat to a full-on drum and bass track. Also what your head does the morning after a big night out. That's your brain's tiny drummer reminding you of your bad decisions.
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense). Present: `pumipintig`, Future: `pipintig`. Often used metaphorically for life or excitement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumintig** nang malakas ang puso ko sa kaba.","translation":"My heart **throbbed** loudly with nervousness."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niyang **pumintig** ang kaniyang sugat.","translation":"He felt his wound **pulsate**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyong-heometriko na may apat na gilid at apat na anggulong rekto (90 degrees).
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "parejo" (parehas, pantay) at Tagalog na "haba" (length).
original_explanation: 'Yung shape ng field sa basketball court o 'yung itsura ng isang bond paper. Sa buhay, minsan kailangan mong mag-isip sa labas ng **parihaba** (think outside the box).
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mismong hugis bilang isang pangngalan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumuhit ka ng isang malaking **parihaba** sa gitna ng papel.","translation":"Draw a big **rectangle** in the middle of the paper."}]

translation: to be swarmed or mobbed by
meaning_filipino: Pagsugurin o pag-atakehin ng isang malaking pangkat o pulutong; pagkaguluhan o dumugin.
original_explanation: Imagine you're a celebrity who just announced a free concert, and the crowd goes wild. That's 'dapulakin'. Or, on a less glamorous note, you drop a piece of candy on the ground, and a colony of ants immediately descends upon it. The candy just got 'dapulakin'-ed by ants. It's the feeling of being overwhelmed by a group.
usage_notes: Often used to describe being swarmed by insects, animals, or a crowd of people. The object form of the verb 'dumapulak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dinapulak** ng mga langgam ang natapong asukal.","translation":"The spilled sugar **was swarmed** by ants."},{"sentence":"Halos **dapulakin** ng mga tagahanga ang sikat na artista.","translation":"The famous actor was almost **mobbed** by fans."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ritmikong pagtibok o pag-alon, lalo na ng puso o mga ugat, na sanhi ng pagdaloy ng dugo.
original_explanation: That 'dug-dug-dug' feeling when you see your crush, when you're about to present your thesis, or when you check your bank account after a 12.12 sale. It's the rhythm of life, stress, and kilig.
usage_notes: Most commonly associated with the heart ('pintig ng puso') but can also refer to any rhythmic throbbing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang mabilis na **pintig** ng kanyang puso dahil sa kaba.","translation":"He felt the fast **beat** of his heart due to nervousness."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat **pintig** ay tanda na tayo'y buhay pa.","translation":"Every **pulse** is a sign that we are still alive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na karaniwang yari sa bunot ng niyog o tela na ginagamit sa pagpapakintab o paglilinis ng sahig.
original_explanation: The OG floor polisher before your fancy spinning mops and vacuum robots. It's basically a coconut husk on a stick. Your lola probably made you use this on your hands and knees to polish the wooden floor until you could see your reflection. It's a full-body workout.
usage_notes: Can also refer to the act of polishing the floor with this tool. The most common type is called 'bunot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha ni nanay ang **lampaso** para pakintabin ang sahig.","translation":"Mother got the **floor polisher** to shine the floor."},{"sentence":"Ang paggamit ng **lampaso** ay isang mabisang ehersisyo.","translation":"Using a **floor polisher** is an effective exercise."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalaga, pag-aaruga, at paggabay sa isang tao na tila isang ina, kadalasan sa paraang labis o sobra.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa ng kaibigan mo sa'yo 'pag lasing ka na. "Inom ka tubig," "Kaya mo pa ba?" "Uwi na tayo." O kaya yung officemate mong laging chine-check kung kumain ka na ba at may dalang extra baon for you. It's care, but sometimes, on overdrive. Pwedeng sweet, pwedeng nakakasakal.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga usapang Taglish. Hindi pormal na salitang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang pag-**mothering** mo sa akin, hindi na ako bata.","translation":"Stop **mothering** me, I'm not a child anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Mayroong malakas na pagnanais na kumain; masiglang kumain.
original_explanation: This is the highest compliment you can give to a Pinoy cook. "Uy, ang sarap ng luto mo, **magana** akong kumain!" It means you're eating with gusto, not just nibbling. It's the opposite of being on a diet. When the food is so good you ask for extra rice three times, you're definitely 'magana'.
usage_notes: Usually used as a predicate adjective, e.g., "Magana siyang kumain" (He/She eats with a good appetite).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **magana** sa pagkain ang bata mula nang matikman niya ang adobo ni lola.","translation":"The child **developed a good appetite** ever since he tasted grandma's adobo."},{"sentence":"Kapag masarap ang ulam, siguradong **magana** kang kakain.","translation":"When the dish is delicious, you will surely eat with **a good appetite**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kemikal na compound (sodium hydroxide) na lubhang mapanira at nakakasunog sa balat, ginagamit sa paggawa ng sabon, paglilinis ng bara sa tubo, at sa iba pang industriyal na proseso. Kilala rin bilang caustic soda.
original_explanation: This isn't your kikay Tita Sosa. This is the heavy-duty stuff that declogs your drain when your hair has declared war on your plumbing. It's also the key ingredient for making traditional soap. Handle with care, besh, this stuff is serious business and not for your skincare routine.
usage_notes: Sa Filipino, ang 'sosa' ay halos eksklusibong tumutukoy sa caustic soda/lye, at hindi sa inumin (na tinatawag na 'soft drink').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay si tatay ng **sosa** sa lababo para maalis ang bara.","translation":"Dad put **lye** in the sink to remove the clog."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paggamit ng **sosa** dahil ito ay nakakasunog ng balat.","translation":"Be careful when using **lye** because it can burn the skin."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kasuotan sa ulo, karaniwang may takip sa harap (brim) para proteksyon sa araw.
etymology: From Spanish 'gorra' (cap). Also used in 'bekimon' (gay lingo) to mean 'go'.
original_explanation: The more 'beki' or slang way of saying 'sumbrero'. It's your go-to accessory for bad hair days or when you want to look sporty even if you just woke up. 'Tara, let's make gora na sa mall!' could mean 'Let's go to the mall!'
usage_notes: Commonly used in colloquial speech. It can mean 'cap' or, in gay slang, it can be a verb meaning 'to go'. Context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan ang iyong **gora** dahil mainit sa labas.","translation":"Don't forget your **cap** because it's hot outside."},{"sentence":"Ang cool ng design ng bago mong **gora**!","translation":"The design of your new **hat** is cool!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha ng isang orasan o relo, na kumakatawan sa paglipas ng oras.
etymology: Onomatopoeia, imitating the sound of a clock.
original_explanation: The official sound of your anxiety during an exam, a deadline approaching, or waiting for your crush to reply. It's the relentless beat of time moving forward whether you're ready or not. 'Rinig na rinig ko ang tiktak ng orasan habang naghihintay ng resulta.'
usage_notes: An onomatopoeic word used to represent the sound of a clock or the passing of time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang maririnig mo lang sa silid ay ang **tiktak** ng lumang orasan.","translation":"The only thing you could hear in the room was the **tick-tock** of the old clock."},{"sentence":"Ang **tiktak** ng oras ay paalala na may hangganan ang lahat.","translation":"The **ticking** of time is a reminder that everything has an end."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lugaw na gawa sa malagkit na kanin at pulbos ng kakaw, karaniwang inihahain na may gatas at tuyo bilang panag-ulam.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "champurrado", isang inuming tsokolate mula sa Mexico.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino breakfast for a rainy day. It's that sweet, chocolatey rice porridge that's perfectly balanced by salty 'tuyo' (dried fish). It's a weird combo that just works, like love teams. From Spanish 'champurrado'.
usage_notes: The pairing with 'tuyo' (dried fish) is classic but optional. Evaporated milk is the traditional topping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagluto si nanay ng masarap na **tsamporado** para sa almusal.","translation":"Mom cooked delicious **chocolate rice porridge** for breakfast."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **tsamporado** lalo na kapag maulan ang panahon.","translation":"**Chocolate rice porridge** is especially good during rainy weather."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglago nang malusog at masagana, karaniwan sa mga halaman; maaari ring tumukoy sa pag-unlad ng isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na 'yabong' (kasaganaan, kalusugan ng tubo) at panlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: What you hope your bank account does after payday, but what actually happens to your utang list. It's when something grows wild and healthy, like chismis in the neighborhood or the plants of a certified plantita.
usage_notes: Ang pandiwa ay nasa anyong naganap (completed aspect), ngunit maaari ring gamitin bilang pawatas (infinitive). Ang pangkasalukuyan ay 'yumayabong' at panghinaharap ay 'yayabong'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Yumabong** ang mga halaman sa hardin dahil sa masipag na pag-aalaga.","translation":"The plants in the garden **flourished** due to diligent care."},{"sentence":"Mula sa maliit na negosyo, **yumabong** ito at naging isang malaking kumpanya.","translation":"From a small business, it **thrived** and became a large company."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o resulta ng paghuhula; isang opinyon o konklusyon na batay sa haka-haka sa halip na sa katotohanan o ebidensya.
original_explanation: This is the official term for 'tsismis' before it gets confirmed. It's all speculation, no receipts. Like when you see your ex's IG story and try to piece together who they're with based on the background noise. That's pure 'hula-hula'.
usage_notes: The reduplication emphasizes the speculative and uncertain nature of the act.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro **hula-hula** lang ang mga sinasabi niya at walang basehan.","translation":"What he's saying is all just **guesswork** and has no basis."},{"sentence":"Iwasan natin ang **hula-hula** at alamin natin ang totoong nangyari.","translation":"Let's avoid **speculation** and find out what really happened."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging makakalimutin o paghina ng isip dahil sa katandaan.
etymology: From 'uli' (return) + '-an', implying a return to a former, often childlike, state.
original_explanation: It's that moment when Lola forgets where she put her glasses... while they're on her head. Or when Lolo tells the same story from his youth for the fifth time in an hour. While it's a medical condition, Pinoys often use 'ulianin' with a mix of gentle teasing, concern, and affection for the elderly. It's the 'senior moment' of the Philippines.
usage_notes: The adjective form 'ulianin' is more commonly used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagiging **ulian** na raw ang matanda dahil madalas siyang may nakakalimutan.","translation":"They say the old man is becoming **senile** because he often forgets things."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong pagtawanan ang lolo mo, **ulian** na talaga siya.","translation":"Don't laugh at your grandpa, he's really become **forgetful**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paring Kastila, partikular na isang prayle noong panahon ng kolonyalismo sa Pilipinas.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'amo' na nangangahulugang 'master' o 'panginoon', na naging tawag sa mga pari.
original_explanation: Think Padre Damaso from Noli Me Tángere. The OG 'bossing' of the parish, often portrayed in historical dramas as the powerful figure you don't mess with. Today, it's more of a historical term, but it carries the weight of colonial-era authority and is almost exclusively used to refer to Spanish priests from that specific time.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa kontekstong pangkasaysayan, lalo na kapag tinatalakay ang panahon ng kolonyalismong Espanyol sa Pilipinas. Bihira nang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinatatakutan ng mga Indio ang **among** sa kanilang parokya.","translation":"The natives feared the **friar** in their parish."},{"sentence":"Ang mga nobela ni Rizal ay naglalarawan sa mga pang-aabuso ng ilang **among**.","translation":"Rizal's novels depict the abuses of some **friars**."}]

translation: the act of eating a main dish without rice
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagkain ng ulam nang walang kasamang kanin.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino sin against rice. It's when you eat the crispy pata, lechon, or fried chicken all by itself because you're on a "no rice" diet (or you're just really hungry for the good stuff). Low-carb kunwari, pero high-cholesterol naman.
usage_notes: Used as a noun referring to the act itself. The verb form is 'papakin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe, naubos niya ang isang buong pritong manok sa **papak** lang.","translation":"Wow, he finished a whole fried chicken just by **eating it without rice**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan sa pagluluto na ginagamit sa pag-iihaw ng pagkain, karaniwang sa ibabaw ng uling, gas, o kuryente.
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung ihawan. 'Yung metal rack na pinapatungan ng liempo, isaw, at hotdog tuwing may handaan o outing. Pwedeng de-uling (the best for flavor!) o 'yung mas modern na electric grill na pang-samgyupsal sa bahay.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa inihaw na pagkain mismo (hal. "mixed grill").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilinis naman ang **grill** pagkatapos nating gamitin.","translation":"Please clean the **grill** after we use it."},{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng bagong electric **grill** para sa aming condo.","translation":"We bought a new electric **grill** for our condo."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na madaling makaramdam ng ginaw o lamig kumpara sa karaniwan.
original_explanation: This is a personality trait. You're that person who's always cold. Your friends are in shorts, and you're in a hoodie. The BPO office aircon is your mortal enemy. You're not just cold, you are a ginawin person.
usage_notes: Describes a person's disposition or tendency to feel cold easily. The antonym is 'mainitin' (sensitive to heat).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talaga akong **ginawin**, kaya lagi akong may dalang sweater.","translation":"I'm really **sensitive to cold**, so I always bring a sweater."},{"sentence":"Hinaan mo ang aircon, para sa mga **ginawin** dito.","translation":"Lower the aircon for the **people who get cold easily** here."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging hindi pino o makinis, kapwa sa pisikal na hipo at sa pag-uugali.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pagka-" (estado ng pagiging) at "magaspang" (hindi pino).
original_explanation: Two meanings here. 1) The texture of your skin when you forget to use lotion (parang liha). 2) The attitude of someone who has no filter and says rude things without thinking. The opposite of "smooth", both literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na tekstura na magaspang o sa bastos at hindi pinong paraan ng pagsasalita o pag-uugali.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinagulat ng lahat ang **pagkamagaspang** ng kanyang pananalita.","translation":"Everyone was shocked by the **coarseness** of his speech."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko gusto ang **pagkamagaspang** ng tela ng kumot na ito.","translation":"I don't like the **roughness** of the fabric of this blanket."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng mga palamuti o dekorasyon upang pagandahin ang isang lugar, bagay, o tao.
etymology: From 'mag-' (actor-focus prefix) + 'palamuti' (decoration). The 'pa-' is part of the root word itself.
original_explanation: This is what Pinoys do best during '-ber' months. We 'magpalamuti' the whole house with Christmas lights and parols. It's also what you do to a cake with icing and sprinkles, or what you do to your room to make it 'aesthetic.' It's the act of adding flair and making something look festive or pretty.
usage_notes: The root word 'palamuti' itself means decoration. The verb form is the action of putting up decorations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na silang **magpalamuti** ng bahay para sa Pasko.","translation":"They already started to **decorate** the house for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magpalamuti** ng kanyang kwaderno gamit ang mga sticker.","translation":"She loves to **adorn** her notebook with stickers."}]

translation: a woman of mixed foreign and native ancestry
meaning_filipino: Isang babae na may magkahalong lahing Pilipino at dayuhan, karaniwan ay lahing Europeo o Amerikano.
original_explanation: Yung kaibigan mong maputi, matangos ang ilong, at laging napagkakamalang turista. Sila yung laging bida sa mga teleserye at commercial ng sabon. 'Uy, ang ganda niya, mestisa ba siya?' is a common palengke compliment. The male counterpart is 'mestiso'.
usage_notes: Ang katumbas na panlalaki ay 'mestiso'. Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan (Isang siyang mestisa) o pang-uri (Mayroon siyang mestisang kutis).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming sikat na artista sa Pilipinas ay mga **mestisa**.","translation":"Many famous actresses in the Philippines are of **mixed ancestry**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **mestisa** na itsura, madalas siyang napagkakamalang dayuhan.","translation":"Because of her **mestiza** features, she is often mistaken for a foreigner."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagkalat, paghiwa-hiwalay, o pagputok ng isang bagay mula sa isang sentral na punto.
original_explanation: Like when you open a bag of chips and it explodes everywhere, or when a juicy piece of gossip drops in the group chat and everyone just scatters to tell someone else. It's sudden, messy, and hard to contain.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical explosions or the sudden spread of emotions, news, or ideas. 'Pagsabog' is a more common synonym for a literal explosion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat sa biglaang **pagsambulat** ng bulkan.","translation":"Everyone was shocked by the sudden **eruption** of the volcano."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsambulat** ng galit niya ay ikinatakot ng mga bata.","translation":"The **outburst** of his anger frightened the children."}]

translation: an allusion; an indirect remark or hint
meaning_filipino: Isang salita, pangungusap, o gawaing nagpapahiwatig ng isang bagay na hindi tuwirang sinasabi; isang patama o pasaring.
etymology: Nagmula sa "pa-dinig", kung saan ang /d/ ay nagiging /r/ kapag nasa pagitan ng dalawang patinig.
original_explanation: The national pastime. It's when you're talking loudly about how "some people" don't wash their own dishes in the office pantry, and you know *exactly* who is within earshot. It's the "My Day" post with a cryptic quote that is 100% about your ex. A true art form.
usage_notes: Ang pinakakilalang salita para sa 'passive-aggressive' na komunikasyon sa Pilipinas. Maaari ring maging pandiwa (magparinig).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **parinig** sa social media at harapin mo siya.","translation":"Stop with the **indirect remarks** on social media and confront him."},{"sentence":"Ang sakit ng **parinig** niya, tagos hanggang buto.","translation":"Her **allusion** was so painful, it cut to the bone."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng kawalan ng kaayusan, sistema, o pagkakabuo.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na may event kayo pero walang nakakaalam kung sino ang in-charge sa pagkain, sa program, o sa venue. That's disorganisasyon. It’s chaos in action, the opposite of a well-oiled machine. It's the reason why group projects sometimes fail.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **disorganisasyon** sa opisina ay nagdudulot ng pagkaantala sa trabaho.","translation":"The **disorganization** in the office is causing work delays."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **disorganisasyon**, hindi naging matagumpay ang kanilang proyekto.","translation":"Because of **disorganization**, their project was not successful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat o grupo ng mga hayop, tulad ng mga baka, tupa, o isda, na magkakasamang kumikilos.
original_explanation: Your barkada on a night out? That's a kawan. A group of titas flocking to the latest sale? Kawan din 'yan. It’s the collective noun for when creatures (human or not) move together as one unit, like a school of fish avoiding a shark or your team rushing to the pantry for free coffee.
usage_notes: Isang pangkalahatang termino para sa isang grupo ng mga hayop. Maaari ring gamitin nang metaporikal para sa isang grupo ng mga tao, kadalasan ay may pastoral o relihiyosong konotasyon (hal., ang kawan ng isang pastor).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kawan** ng mga ibon ang lumilipad sa himpapawid.","translation":"A **flock** of birds is flying in the sky."},{"sentence":"Inaalagaan ng pastol ang kanyang **kawan** ng mga tupa.","translation":"The shepherd takes care of his **herd** of sheep."}]

meaning_filipino: Sadyain na ipatid o patumbahin ang isang tao sa pamamagitan ng pagharang ng paa.
original_explanation: This is the move of every kontrabida in a Pinoy teleserye, or that annoying kid in elementary school. When you stick your foot out to make someone fall, you're trying 'na **tisurin** sila'. It's the physical form of 'siraan'.
usage_notes: Implies intention. The root word 'tisod' (to stumble) is more general. 'Matisod' is to accidentally stumble, while 'tisurin' is to intentionally cause someone to stumble.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **tisurin** ang kapatid mo, masasaktan 'yan.","translation":"Don't **trip** your sibling, they'll get hurt."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niya akong **tisurin** habang naglalakad ako sa pasilyo.","translation":"He tried **to trip** me while I was walking down the hallway."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging basag o pagkapira-piraso ng isang bagay na marupok tulad ng salamin o plato.
original_explanation: That heart-stopping sound when a plate slips from your hand. It's the aftermath of a 'Lambing' session with your cat on a shelf full of figurines. Can also be used for a voice that's breaking from emotion, like when you're about to cry while explaining to your boss why you need a raise. 'Yung boses niya, may pagkabasag.'
usage_notes: Used for hard, brittle objects that shatter or break. Also used figuratively for a broken voice or a state of disunity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat niyang pinulot ang mga bubog mula sa **pagkabasag** ng baso.","translation":"He carefully picked up the shards from the **brokenness** of the glass."},{"sentence":"Halata ang **pagkabasag** ng kanyang boses habang nagkukuwento.","translation":"The **breaking** of his voice was obvious while he was telling the story."}]

translation: dismissal (from a job); act of chopping
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalis sa isang tao sa kanyang tungkulin o trabaho; o ang proseso ng pagputol o paghiwa sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay kahoy, gamit ang palakol.
etymology: Root word 'sibak' means to chop or cleave. The metaphorical extension to 'firing' someone is common.
original_explanation: Pagsibak has two moods. The literal one is chopping firewood for your lola's dirty kitchen. The more dramatic, corporate one is getting fired. 'Na-sibak sa trabaho.' It’s the Tagalog for 'you're fired,' but with more finality. From BPO agent to CEO, no one is safe from the dreaded *pagsibak*.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context. "Pagsibak ng kahoy" (chopping wood) vs. "pagsibak sa empleyado" (firing an employee).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang katapatan, naligtas siya sa malawakang **pagsibak** ng mga empleyado sa kumpanya.","translation":"Because of his loyalty, he was spared from the mass **dismissal** of employees in the company."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsibak** ng panggatong ay mabigat na gawain tuwing umaga.","translation":"The **act of chopping** firewood is a heavy task every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng paglubha o pagtindi ng isang sitwasyon, kalagayan, o karamdaman.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you try to 'fix' something but only make it worse. Like adding salt to a wound, literally or figuratively. Or when you keep scratching a mosquito bite. Or when you bring up an old issue during an argument. 'Huwag mo nang palalain' is the Filipino for 'Don't make it worse.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagpupuyat ay maaaring **magpalala** ng iyong sakit.","translation":"Staying up late can **worsen** your illness."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang sasabat, baka **magpalala** ka lang ng sitwasyon.","translation":"Don't interrupt, you might just **aggravate** the situation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tao na nagpasimula, nanguna, o nag-udyok sa isang gawain, lalo na kung ito ay isang kaguluhan, krimen, o masamang balak.
etymology: From pa- + simuno. The root simuno is rarely used now except in grammar ('subject of a sentence'). The word has taken on a mostly negative connotation.
original_explanation: The "utak" behind the kalokohan. Siya 'yung nag-aya mag-cutting classes, 'yung nag-suggest na mag-order pa ng isang bucket kahit may work pa bukas, o 'yung nag-forward ng chain message sa family group chat. The OG, the mastermind, the one you point at when your mom asks, "Sino'ng may pakana nito?!"
usage_notes: Almost always has a negative connotation, implying someone who starts trouble.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahanap ng mga pulis kung sino ang **pasimuno** ng gulo sa rally.","translation":"The police are looking for the **instigator** of the chaos at the rally."},{"sentence":"Ikaw na naman ang **pasimuno** ng kalokohang ito!","translation":"You're the **ringleader** of this mischief again!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bunga o resulta ng isang naunang kilos o pangyayari, na maaaring mabuti o masama.
original_explanation: This is the "what happens next" part of life, the receipt you get for your actions. Nag-cutting classes ka? Ang konsekwensya, bagsak sa quiz. Nag-waldas ka ng sahod? Ang konsekwensya, instant noodles until the next payday. It's the universe's way of saying, "You did that, now deal with this."
usage_notes: Can be used for both positive and negative outcomes, but more commonly associated with negative ones.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Harapin mo ang **konsekwensya** ng iyong mga desisyon.","translation":"Face the **consequences** of your decisions."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtaas ng presyo ng bilihin ay isang **konsekwensya** ng inflation.","translation":"The increase in the price of goods is a **consequence** of inflation."}]

translation: coordination; act of relating or connecting with
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtatatag ng koneksyon, komunikasyon, o ugnayan sa isang tao, grupo, o tanggapan.
original_explanation: This is the BPO/corporate version of "chismis". It's not just talking, it's "coordinating with stakeholders," "liaising with other departments," or "touching base" with a client. It's the professional term for making connections happen, whether it’s for a project, an event, or just to get the WiFi password from the IT guy.
usage_notes: Often used in professional, formal, or organizational contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pakikiugnay** sa iba't ibang ahensya ng gobyerno para sa proyektong ito.","translation":"**Coordination** with different government agencies is important for this project."},{"sentence":"Ang Public Relations officer ang namamahala sa **pakikiugnay** sa media.","translation":"The Public Relations officer is in charge of **liaising** with the media."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong pagtatanghal ng musika o tula, karaniwang ginagawa ng isang tao o isang maliit na grupo.
original_explanation: Ito yung event kung saan kailangan mong panoorin yung pamangkin mo na tumugtog ng "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star" sa piano sa ika-sampung pagkakataon. Or, ito yung final project niyo sa Music class na nagpapakaba sa'yo for weeks. The culmination of all your puyat and practice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May piano **resaytal** ang anak niya sa katapusan ng buwan.","translation":"Her child has a piano **recital** at the end of the month."},{"sentence":"Naghanda siya nang husto para sa kanyang voice **resaytal**.","translation":"She prepared extensively for her voice **recital**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagmamahal, paglalambing, o pag-aaruga sa pamamagitan ng salita o gawa.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung a-type mo na "good morning" message sa jowa mo with matching heart emojis. O 'yung lola mong laging may dalang pasalubong at hahaplusin ang buhok mo. A makarinyo person is naturally sweet and shows affection easily, the opposite of someone na pa-cool lang at 'di showy. From the Spanish word "cariño".
usage_notes: Describes a person's character trait. Can also be used as a verb "magkarinyo" (to be affectionate).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Likas na **makarinyo** sa mga bata ang aking tiyahin.","translation":"My aunt is naturally **affectionate** towards children."},{"sentence":"Masarap magmahal ang taong **makarinyo** at maalaga.","translation":"It's wonderful to love someone who is **affectionate** and caring."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang batayang katotohanan, batas, doktrina, o paniniwala na nagsisilbing gabay sa pag-iisip o pagkilos.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga bagay na pinaninindigan mo sa buhay, kahit gaano kahirap. Parang yung 'No to ghosting' policy mo, or yung 'Bawal umutang pagkatapos ng sweldo' rule. Your non-negotiables. Kapag may prinsipyo ka, you stand for something.
usage_notes: Often used in discussions about morality, ethics, and personal beliefs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **prinsipyo** akong sinusunod kaya hindi ako mandaraya.","translation":"I follow a **principle** so I will not cheat."},{"sentence":"Mahirap kalabanin ang taong may matatag na **prinsipyo**.","translation":"It's hard to go against a person with firm **principles**."}]

translation: to gesture with the hands; to gesticulate
meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw ng mga kamay at braso habang nagsasalita upang magbigay-diin o magpahiwatig ng isang damdamin o ideya.
original_explanation: Know that tita who tells a story and her hands are flying everywhere, almost hitting your face with her gestures? She's an expert at magkumpay. It's using your hands as visual aids, whether you're directing traffic, explaining a super-complicated chismis, or giving a speech like a politician.
usage_notes: Can be neutral, but often used to describe large, expressive hand movements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig **magkumpay** ang guro habang nagpapaliwanag ng leksyon.","translation":"The teacher likes to **gesture with her hands** while explaining the lesson."},{"sentence":"**Nagkumpay** siya na parang sinasabing, 'Lumayo ka!'","translation":"He **gestured** as if to say, 'Go away!'"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o bagay na nasa tabi o gilid ng isa pa.
etymology: From `tabi` (side) with the prefix `ka-` which denotes a companion or someone sharing a state/location.
original_explanation: Your seatmate in class, the person next to you on the MRT who's practically sitting on your lap, or the chismosang kapitbahay whose house is right next to yours. "Katabi" is all about proximity. It can be a source of comfort (katabi matulog) or extreme annoyance (katabi sa jeep na maingay kausap sa phone).
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective (e.g., "ang bahay na katabi") or a noun (e.g., "ang katabi ko"). When used as a noun, it means 'the person next to someone'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **katabi** mo sa sinehan kagabi?","translation":"Who was the person **next to** you at the cinema last night?"},{"sentence":"Ang **katabi** naming bahay ay ipinagbibili.","translation":"The house **adjacent** to ours is for sale."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang butas o siwang kung saan di-sinasadyang tumutulo o lumalabas ang isang likido o gas.
original_explanation: That moment of panic when you see a water spot on the ceiling. Or when your chismosa friend accidentally spills the tea about someone else's secret. It's an unwanted escape, whether it's water from a pipe or secrets from a mouth.
usage_notes: The stress is on the last syllable: ta-GAS. This is a homograph of 'tagas' (gash/chop), which has a different pronunciation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **tagas** ang bubong kaya kailangan itong ayusin bago dumating ang tag-ulan.","translation":"The roof has a **leak**, so it needs to be fixed before the rainy season arrives."},{"sentence":"Nanggaling sa preno ang **tagas** ng langis.","translation":"The oil **leak** came from the brakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Pag-ugnayin o pagtibayin ang tatlo o higit pang hibla ng buhok, sinulid, o katulad na materyales sa isang magkakapatong na disenyo.
original_explanation: This is what your lola did to your hair before school, creating those two perfect braids that were so tight you could feel your eyebrows lifting. It's also what you do with ropes, friendship bracelets, or even wires when you're trying to be organized but end up with a bigger mess. It’s the art of controlled tangling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong ka bang **magsalapid** ng buhok?","translation":"Do you know how to **braid** hair?"},{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magsalapid** nitong mga lubid.","translation":"Help me **braid** these ropes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang koleksyon o kalipunan ng mga bagay, lalo na ng mga bulaklak, na pinagsama-sama at karaniwang tinalian.
original_explanation: Not just one flower, but a whole squad of them. A 'pumpon' is what you get for your mom on Mother's Day or what you hope to receive on Valentine's. It's a group of things huddled together, like a 'pumpon ng saging' (bunch of bananas) or a 'pumpon ng tao' (cluster of people).
usage_notes: Most commonly used to refer to a bouquet of flowers ('pumpon ng mga bulaklak'), but can be used for other clustered items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbigay siya ng isang magandang **pumpon** ng mga bulaklak.","translation":"He gave a beautiful **bouquet** of flowers."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ay nagtipon sa isang **pumpon** sa ilalim ng puno.","translation":"The children gathered in a **cluster** under the tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang Ingles na tumutukoy sa isang pangako o kasiguruhan na ang isang partikular na bagay ay gagawin o hindi gagawin. Madalas gamitin sa impormal na pakikipag-usap.
etymology: Salitang Ingles na direktang hiniram at ginagamit sa Taglish.
original_explanation: This is the English word we use when "pangako" feels too formal or heavy. It's the "pinky swear" of Pinoy conversations. Also, the favorite line of fuccbois and politicians. "I promise, last na 'to."
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa Taglish at impormal na konteksto. Ang pormal na katumbas nito ay 'pangako'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Promise**, babayaran kita sa a-kinse.","translation":"**Promise**, I'll pay you on the 15th."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang paasa, ha? **Promise** mo 'yan.","translation":"Don't get my hopes up, okay? That's your **promise**."}]

translation: to sue; to file a complaint against
meaning_filipino: Magsampa ng pormal na reklamo o kaso sa isang ahensya o hukuman laban sa isang tao.
etymology: From Spanish 'caso' (case), with Filipino affixation. The 's' sound is often duplicated in colloquial speech, leading to 'susuhan' as a variant of 'kasuhan'.
original_explanation: The ultimate threat when someone cuts you in line at the LTO. "Hoy, susuhan kita!" It's the formal, legal way of saying "Isusumbong kita kay Tulfo." It's taking the "away" from the street to the barangay hall or the courtroom.
usage_notes: A colloquial variant of "kasuhan". The perceived root "suso" is incorrect; the actual root is "kaso" (case, complaint).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbanta siyang **susuhan** ang kumpanya dahil sa hindi makatarungang pagtanggal sa kanya.","translation":"He threatened to **sue** the company for his unjust dismissal."},{"sentence":"Kung hindi mo isasauli ang pera, mapipilitan akong **susuhan** ka.","translation":"If you don't return the money, I will be forced to **file a complaint against** you."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay o tao na nakaayos sa isang tuwid na linya o hanay.
original_explanation: 'Yung mga ngipin mo after braces, magkakahanay na. O 'yung mga kotse na stuck sa EDSA traffic, perfectly magkakahanay sa kani-kanilang lanes. It means everything is lined up neatly, like ducks in a row. The opposite of your messy room.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical alignment or figuratively for alignment of ideas or goals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tiyaking **magkakahanay** ang mga upuan bago magsimula ang programa.","translation":"Make sure the chairs are **aligned** before the program starts."},{"sentence":"Dapat **magkakahanay** ang ating mga layunin para magtagumpay ang grupo.","translation":"Our goals must be **aligned** for the group to succeed."}]

translation: to stop flowing; to subside (for a liquid)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtigil ng pagdaloy ng isang likido, tulad ng dugo o tubig.
original_explanation: This is a very specific 'stop'. It's not for traffic, it's for liquids. When the bleeding from your 'sugat' finally stops, it 'umampat'. When the floodwaters finally go down, they 'umampat'. It's the sigh of relief when something wet and flowing finally ceases.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used for liquids like blood, water, or other fluids, to mean the flow has stopped or subsided.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa tulong ng gamot, **umampat** din ang pagdurugo ng kanyang sugat.","translation":"With the help of medicine, the bleeding from his wound finally **stopped flowing**."},{"sentence":"Hintayin nating **umampat** ang baha bago tayo lumabas ng bahay.","translation":"Let's wait for the flood to **subside** before we leave the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bayan sa lalawigan ng Pangasinan sa Pilipinas, kilala sa mahabang kasaysayan nito at bilang isa sa mga pinakamatandang munisipalidad sa rehiyon.
etymology: Ang pangalan ay sinasabing nagmula sa paglaganap ng halamang "balangbang" o sa salitang "bayang-bayang" na nangangahulugang nakabitin.
original_explanation: It's a real place! Specifically, a municipality in Pangasinan famous for its long history and for once holding the Guinness World Record for the longest barbecue grill. So if you hear someone say "Pupunta ako sa **Bayambang**," they're not talking about a mythical land, they're probably going on a road trip up north.
usage_notes: Primarily used to refer to the specific municipality in the province of Pangasinan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pista sa **Bayambang** ay dinarayo ng maraming turista.","translation":"The festival in **Bayambang** is visited by many tourists."},{"sentence":"Ipinanganak ang lolo ko sa bayan ng **Bayambang**, Pangasinan.","translation":"My grandfather was born in the town of **Bayambang**, Pangasinan."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling anyo ng "wika ko" o "sabi ko," na ginagamit sa kolokyal na pananalita.
etymology: Contraction of "wika ko" (my word/I said) or "sabi ko" (I said).
original_explanation: The ultimate "I told you so" shortcut. You use this when you're repeating something you *already* said, usually with a hint of sass. "Bakit ka na-late? **Kako**, umalis ka nang maaga!" It's the verbal equivalent of a receipts-ready clapback.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, spoken Tagalog. It's a contraction and feels very natural in conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kako** sa iyo, magdala ka ng payong dahil uulan.","translation":"**I said** to you, bring an umbrella because it will rain."},{"sentence":"Bumagsak siya sa exam. **Kako** naman kasi, mag-aral siyang mabuti.","translation":"He failed the exam. Like **I said**, he should have studied well."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaan o paggamit ng salapi para sa isang partikular na tao, bagay, o layunin.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'shopee checkout'. It's what you do for your K-Pop merch, your monthly milk tea budget, or when your 'inaanak' shows up for Christmas. To 'pagkagastahan' something is to declare it worthy of your hard-earned sweldo.
usage_notes: Often used to indicate the object or person on whom money is being spent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **pagkagastahan** ang mga bagay na hindi naman niya kailangan.","translation":"She doesn't want **to spend money on** things she doesn't really need."},{"sentence":"Ang edukasyon ng mga anak ang pinakamahalagang **pagkagastahan** ng mag-asawa.","translation":"The children's education is the most important thing for the couple **to spend on**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapadala ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay isang mensahe, email, o pakete.
original_explanation: Yung kaba moment na nagsend ka ng 'I love you' tapos 'seen' lang ang reply. O mas malala, nagsend ka ng maling message sa maling group chat. Time to deactivate, mars!
usage_notes: Past tense. The present tense is 'nagsesend' and the future tense is 'magse-send'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagsend** ako ng email sa HR kaninang umaga.","translation":"I **sent** an email to HR this morning."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagsend** ng mga bulaklak na ito?","translation":"Who **sent** these flowers?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpuna o pag-atake sa isang tao, ideya, o gawa sa pamamagitan ng matatalas na salita, kadalasan sa paraang pampubliko o pampahayagan.
original_explanation: This is the official sport of keyboard warriors and political commentators. It's when you don't just disagree, you write a whole thesis about why someone is wrong, usually with spicy language. Think of it as 'to roast,' but for a more formal, often political, audience. It's the 'cancel culture' verb before 'cancel culture' was a thing.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of journalism, politics, or academic critique.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang kanyang kolum upang **manuligsa** sa mga katiwalian sa gobyerno.","translation":"He used his column to **criticize** the corruption in the government."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot **manuligsa** kung alam mong nasa tama ka.","translation":"Don't be afraid to **criticize** if you know you are in the right."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga bagay na nagmumula sa kalikasan na magagamit ng tao para sa kabuhayan, tulad ng mga puno, tubig, lupa, at mineral.
original_explanation: The OG resource pack for a country. This is everything from the water in your Nawasa bill to the wood for your lola's rocking chair. It's the stuff we learn about in Sibika at Kultura that's supposed to make our country rich but is also the subject of endless debates about mining, logging, and environmental protection.
usage_notes: A standard term used in academics, government, and news. It is a broader term than "likas na kayamanan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sagana sa **likas na yaman** ang bansang Pilipinas, mula sa mga kagubatan hanggang sa karagatan.","translation":"The Philippines is rich in **natural resources**, from its forests to its seas."},{"sentence":"Ang responsableng paggamit ng **likas na yaman** ay mahalaga para sa sustainable development.","translation":"The responsible use of **natural resources** is important for sustainable development."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o pagbuo ng sakit na kanser, na kinikilala sa abnormal at hindi makontrol na pagdami ng mga selula sa katawan.
etymology: From "magka-" (verb prefix indicating acquisition or affliction) + "kanser" (from Spanish "cáncer").
original_explanation: Ito 'yung kinatatakutan ng lahat, 'yung sinasabi ng nanay mo na mangyayari sa'yo 'pag puro ka instant noodles at yosi. "Hala sige, 'pag di ka tumigil diyan, magkakakanser ka!" It's the verb form for developing the dreaded disease.
usage_notes: A serious term used in medical contexts or as a stern warning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa doktor, maaaring **magkakanser** sa baga ang isang taong malakas manigarilyo.","translation":"According to the doctor, a person who smokes heavily might **get** lung **cancer**."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siyang mag-ingat sa pagkain upang maiwasang **magkakanser**.","translation":"He was advised to be careful with his diet to avoid **getting cancer**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglabag o hindi pagsunod sa isang utos, tuntunin, o payo.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo 'pag sinabi ng nanay mo, 'Huwag kang gagabihin,' tapos umuwi ka ng 3 AM. O 'pag sinabi ng Waze, 'Turn left,' pero kumanan ka kasi 'feeling' mo mas mabilis doon. Spoiler alert: you're not always right. This is the act of choosing 'hard mode' in life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya na huwag **suwayin** ang batas trapiko.","translation":"He was advised not **to defy** the traffic laws."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiusap o utos na ipa-encode o ipa-type ang isang dokumento o teksto sa isang typewriter o kompyuter.
etymology: A Taglish coinage from the Filipino causative prefix "pa-" (to ask/cause someone to do something) and the English word "type".
original_explanation: The classic Filipino student or employee request: 'Bes, pa-type naman nito, please?' It's the act of asking someone else to do the typing for you, whether it's for your thesis, a report, or just a quick email. The direct ancestor of 'pa-encode'.
usage_notes: A colloquial and very common verb in offices and schools. It's a perfect example of code-switching becoming a standard word in informal and semi-formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **patype** itong sulat-kamay na report sa sekretarya.","translation":"I need **to have** this handwritten report **typed** by the secretary."},{"sentence":"Pwede bang **patype** ng resignation letter ko sa iyo?","translation":"Can I ask you **to type** my resignation letter for me?"}]

translation: to open one's eyes; to become aware
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbukas ng mga mata pagkatapos matulog; sa metaporikal na antas, ang pagkakaroon ng kamalayan o kaalaman tungkol sa isang bagay, lalo na sa mga isyung panlipunan.
original_explanation: Literally, it's opening your eyes in the morning. But the real tea is its other meaning: to be "woke." It's when you finally realize the harsh realities of the world—the government, adulting, that your friend is actually a "plastik." Mamulat is the transition from blissful ignorance to painful, but necessary, awareness.
usage_notes: Has a strong secondary meaning related to social and political awakening.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **namulat** na siya sa katotohanan tungkol sa kanyang kasintahan.","translation":"Finally, her eyes **were opened** to the truth about her partner."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga para sa kabataan na **mamulat** sa mga isyung panlipunan.","translation":"It's important for the youth to **become aware** of social issues."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahilig magpatawa o magbiro; isang komedyante o mapagbiro.
original_explanation: Yung kaibigan mong laging may baong hirit o punchline, kahit corny minsan. Siya 'yung nagpapagaan ng atmosphere sa group chat o sa inuman. Basically, the designated "class clown" of the barkada.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa impormal na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Cardo bilang **dyoker** sa kanilang opisina.","translation":"Cardo is known as the **joker** in their office."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong seryosohin 'yan, **dyoker** talaga ang taong 'yun.","translation":"Don't take him seriously, that person is really a **joker**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa "gago/gaga 'to, ah," isang ekspresyon ng pagkadismaya, pagkainis, o pagkamangha sa isang kilos o sinabi ng isang tao.
etymology: Acronym from the Tagalog phrase 'gago 'to, ah'.
original_explanation: Internet slang for "Gago/Gaga 'to, ah!" 'Yung reaksyon mo sa chat 'pag may sinabing kalokohan 'yung kaibigan mo o 'pag may nakita kang post na sobrang unbelievable. It's the silent, typed version of raising an eyebrow and saying "Really, dude?"
usage_notes: Highly informal and used primarily in text messages and social media. Can be considered vulgar or offensive if used with strangers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-send siya ng meme na sobrang luma, napasabi na lang ako ng **gta**.","translation":"He sent a really old meme, I could only say **\"gta\"** (what a fool)."},{"sentence":"**GTA**, bakit mo sinabi 'yun sa harap niya?","translation":"**\"GTA\"** (You idiot), why did you say that in front of him/her?"}]

translation: to stay put, to become fixed or permanent
meaning_filipino: Ang pananatili sa isang lugar, posisyon, o estado nang hindi gumagalaw o nagbabago.
original_explanation: Like that one friend who crashes on your couch for a weekend and is still there two weeks later. Or that "temporary" Jollibee branch that's been there for 20 years. It's the act of settling in, sometimes for longer than planned. "Dito na 'ko pipirme." (I'm staying here for good.)
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense). Present: `pumipirme`, Future: `pipirme`. Can mean literally staying in one place or settling down in life (e.g., in a job or location).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula nang dumating siya galing probinsya, sa Maynila na siya **pumirme**.","translation":"Ever since he arrived from the province, he has **stayed put** in Manila."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **pumirme** sa isang trabaho lang.","translation":"He doesn't want to **settle** in just one job."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daglat para sa pariralang Ingles na "one of my followers," na tumutukoy sa isa sa mga tagasubaybay ng isang tao sa social media, karaniwan sa paraang hindi direktang pinapangalanan.
etymology: From the English acronym 'OOMF' (One Of My Followers).
original_explanation: The cryptic way to subtweet someone you know is watching. When you post 'Sana 'yung oomf kong mahilig mag-react sa stories ko ay mag-chat na,' you're talking about a specific follower without calling them out. It's a modern-day *harana* or passive-aggressive callout, depending on the context, delivered via social media.
usage_notes: Prevalent on platforms like X (Twitter) and sometimes Instagram/Facebook, used to talk about a follower indirectly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **oomf** ako na ang galing gumuhit, sana mapansin na siya.","translation":"I have **one of my followers** who's great at drawing, I hope they get noticed."},{"sentence":"To my **oomf** who keeps sending me memes, thank you for making my day.","translation":"To **one of my followers** who keeps sending me memes, thank you for making my day."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagiging baligtad o salungat sa karaniwang posisyon o direksyon. Tumutukoy din sa pagbabago ng paninindigan o pagkampi.
original_explanation: Ever seen a politician switch parties right before an election? That's the ultimate 'talikwas'. It's when something is completely flipped, like your world when you find out your crush is already 'taken', or when you wear your t-shirt inside out by mistake. It's a sudden, often shocking, reversal.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a change of heart, allegiance, or physical position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **talikwas** ang kanyang pananaw matapos ang insidente.","translation":"His perspective became **inverted** after the incident."},{"sentence":"**Talikwas** ang pagkakalagay ng larawan sa dingding.","translation":"The picture is placed **upside down** on the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga puwersa o katangian na nagpapasigla sa pag-unlad o pagbabago sa loob ng isang sistema o proseso.
original_explanation: Ito yung "It's complicated" status ng isang grupo. Ang dinamika ng pamilya, barkada, o opisina. Sino ang bida, sino ang kontrabida, sino ang laging nagpapasimuno ng away, at sino ang tagapamayapa. The unseen forces that make things interesting... or stressful.
usage_notes: Often used in academic, social, or psychological contexts to describe the interactions and forces within a group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalagang pag-aralan ang **dinamika** ng isang pamilya upang maunawaan ang bawat miyembro.","translation":"It is important to study the family **dynamics** to understand each member."},{"sentence":"Nagbago ang **dinamika** ng grupo mula nang dumating ang bagong lider.","translation":"The group's **dynamics** changed when the new leader arrived."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lalaking kasama o katabi ng lalaking ikakasal sa seremonya, na karaniwang malapit na kaibigan o kamag-anak.
original_explanation: He's the groom's official wingman for the wedding day. His job description includes: keeping the rings safe, giving a hopefully not-too-embarrassing speech, making sure the groom actually shows up, and leading the charge at the open bar. He's the Best Man, the Bro of Honor.
usage_notes: Specific term used in the context of weddings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kapatid ng nobyo ang kanyang magiging **abay na lalaki**.","translation":"The groom's brother will be his **best man**."}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pangngalan, isang tao na nagbuwis ng buhay o nagdusa nang labis para sa isang paniniwala, prinsipyo, o pananampalataya. Bilang pang-uri, tumutukoy sa pagiging mapagparaya o labis na mapagtiis sa pag-abuso.
original_explanation: Two flavors. The historical one is a hero like Jose Rizal who died for a cause. The modern, hugot version is that friend who stays in a toxic relationship and loves to say 'Okay lang ako' while crying on the inside. They collect suffering like Funko Pops. 'Huwag ka ngang martir diyan, hiwalayan mo na 'yan!'
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ('a martyr') or an adjective ('being a martyr'). The context determines its function.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Jose Rizal ay itinuturing na isang pambansang **martir**.","translation":"Jose Rizal is considered a national **martyr**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **martir** sa relasyon na iyan; hindi ka niya pinapahalagahan.","translation":"Don't be a **martyr** in that relationship; he/she doesn't value you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na uri, klase, o kategorya ng isang bagay, tao, o konsepto.
original_explanation: This is your "type," pero hindi sa love life. More like, "Anong tipo ng coffee ang gusto mo?" o "Anong tipo ng tao ang ayaw mo sa group project?" It's the category, the classification, the flavor of anything under the sun.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit nang palitan sa mga salitang "uri" o "klase".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong **tipo** ng pelikula ang paborito mo?","translation":"What **type** of movie is your favorite?"},{"sentence":"Hindi ko gusto ang ganitong **tipo** ng tela para sa barong.","translation":"I don't like this **kind** of fabric for the barong."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lugaw o sinangag na may manok, luya, bawang, at nilagyan ng pampalasa. Karaniwang inihahain nang mainit, lalo na bilang pagkain sa umaga o sa mga panahong malamig o maulan.
etymology: Mula sa mga salitang Espanyol na "arroz" (kanin) at "caldo" (sabaw).
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino comfort food for a rainy day, or when you're sick, or just plain sad. It's not just rice and chicken; it's a warm hug in a bowl. The magic is in the toppings: toasted garlic, spring onions, a hard-boiled egg, and a squeeze of calamansi. Perfect after a long shift sa BPO or a night out. It's the more "sosyal" cousin of 'lugaw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap kumain ng mainit na **aruskaldo** kapag umuulan.","translation":"It's delicious to eat hot **chicken rice porridge** when it's raining."},{"sentence":"Nagpadala si nanay ng **aruskaldo** dahil may sakit ako.","translation":"Mom sent over some **arroz caldo** because I'm sick."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gamot, pagkain, o substansiya na nagpapasimula o nagpapabilis ng paghilab ng tiyan o ng matris, karaniwan para sa panganganak o pagdumi.
etymology: From 'pang-' (instrumental prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'hilab' (contraction, cramp). Lit. 'that which is used to cause contractions'.
original_explanation: The 'deadline is tomorrow' of pregnancy. It's the spicy food, the long walks, or the actual medication that tells the baby, 'Eviction notice na, besh!' Can also refer to something that makes you run to the CR, like that sketchy street food you bravely ate.
usage_notes: Has two common meanings: inducing uterine contractions for childbirth, or inducing bowel movements (as a laxative). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na maglakad-lakad bilang natural na **pampahilab**.","translation":"The doctor advised her to walk around as a natural **labor inducer**."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang papaya bilang mabisang **pampahilab** ng tiyan.","translation":"Papaya is known as an effective **laxative**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng bathala o isang babae na may pambihirang kagandahan at karisma.
original_explanation: How you describe your crush when she walks into the room and time slows down. "Ang ganda niya, parang diosa!" It's the ultimate compliment for beauty, grace, and an aura that's just out of this world. The female counterpart to "Adonis".
usage_notes: Often used hyperbolically to praise a woman's beauty. The standard Filipino spelling is 'diyosa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuturing siyang isang **diosa** ng kagandahan sa kanilang bayan.","translation":"She is considered a **goddess** of beauty in their town."},{"sentence":"Sa mitolohiyang Griyego, si Aphrodite ang **diosa** ng pag-ibig.","translation":"In Greek mythology, Aphrodite is the **goddess** of love."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng pagkahilo at pagkaramdam na para bang masusuka.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling mo after mong sumakay sa a la-Viking na biyahe ng bus sa SLEX. O kaya 'yung nararamdaman mo 'pag nakikita mo 'yung ex mo na may bago na. That's alibadbad. The urge to purge, physically or emotionally.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin kasama ng pandiwang 'makaramdam' (to feel).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakaramdam ako ng matinding **alibadbad** pagkatapos kong kumain.","translation":"I felt intense **nausea** after eating."},{"sentence":"Ang **alibadbad** ay isang karaniwang sintomas ng pagbubuntis.","translation":"**Nausea** is a common symptom of pregnancy."}]

translation: chokingly; grasped tightly around the neck
meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit o mahigpit na paghawak sa leeg na tila sinasakal; ginagamit din sa matalinhagang paraan upang ilarawan ang pakiramdam ng pagiging gipit o labis na pagkabalisa.
original_explanation: This is what you feel when you have five deadlines, three exams, and your crush just seen-zoned you. It's the feeling of being overwhelmed, like life has you in a chokehold. "Yung feeling na sakal-sakal ka na sa trabaho at bills."
usage_notes: The reduplication implies intensity, repetition, or a continuous state of the action or feeling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hawak siyang **sakal-sakal** ng magnanakaw habang tinututukan ng patalim.","translation":"The thief held him, **grasping tightly at his neck**, while pointing a blade at him."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **sakal-sakal** na ako sa dami ng utang na kailangang bayaran.","translation":"I feel like I'm already **being choked** by the amount of debt that needs to be paid."}]

translation: to rise; to improve one's status
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtaas mula sa isang mababang posisyon patungo sa isang mas mataas na lebel, pisikal man o sa kalagayan sa buhay.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'Started from the bottom, now we're here' verb. It can be literal, like a plane taking off ('umangat ang eroplano'), or figurative, like getting a promotion ('umangat ang posisyon sa trabaho'). The most 'hugot' version is 'umangat sa buhay' - to rise from poverty and achieve success. It's the Filipino dream, verbalized.
usage_notes: Has both a literal (to go up) and a very common figurative (to improve one's life/status) meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang sipag at tiyaga, **umangat** siya sa buhay.","translation":"Because of his hard work and perseverance, he was able to **improve his status** in life."},{"sentence":"Dahan-dahang **umangat** ang kurtina sa entablado.","translation":"The stage curtain slowly **rose**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pananalita na ginagamit upang magbigay ng mas malinaw, simple, o direktang pagpapaliwanag sa isang naunang sinabi.
original_explanation: This is your "for dummies" button in a conversation. You use it when you've said something complicated and you see the "loading..." icon on someone's face. "**Sa ibang salita**, 'di ka niya gusto." See? Simple, direct, and painful.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa muling pagpapahayag o paglilinaw ng isang naunang pahayag, kadalasan upang gawin itong mas simple.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang poliglota; **sa ibang salita**, marami siyang alam na wika.","translation":"She is a polyglot; **in other words**, she knows many languages."},{"sentence":"Ang proyekto ay may isyung pampinansyal. **Sa ibang salita**, wala na tayong pera.","translation":"The project has financial issues. **In other words**, we're out of money."}]

translation: to strive for; to endeavor to achieve
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng lahat ng pagsisikap, lakas, at kakayahan upang makamit ang isang layunin o mithiin.
etymology: Root word 'sikap' means effort or diligence. The affix 'pag- -an' turns it into a verb directing the action towards an object.
original_explanation: This is the 'work hard, play hard' but mostly just the 'work hard' part. It's the energy you use to get that promotion, finish your thesis, or make your side hustle work. It's the theme song of every OFW and every student trying to make their parents proud. *Pagsikapan* is basically 'hustle' in its purest, most Tagalog form.
usage_notes: This is a verb, often in the imperative or objective-focus form. "Pagsumikapan" is a more formal synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pagsikapan** ang iyong mga pangarap upang ito ay matupad.","translation":"You need **to strive for** your dreams for them to come true."},{"sentence":"Ating **pagsikapan** na mapanatiling malinis ang ating kapaligiran.","translation":"Let's **endeavor to achieve** keeping our environment clean."}]

translation: the way something is divided; division
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o estado ng pagiging hiwalay sa dalawa o higit pang bahagi.
etymology: From `pagkaka-` + `hati` (divide, half). Describes the state or manner of being divided.
original_explanation: This is how you split the bill with friends, or how the last piece of pizza is divided. 'Ayusin niyo ang pagkakahati niyan, dapat pantay!' (Fix how that's divided, it should be equal!). It can also be used for more serious things, like the division of a company's assets or the emotional division within a family.
usage_notes: Can be literal (physical division) or figurative (division of opinion, loyalty, etc.).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi naging pantay ang **pagkakahati** ng mana.","translation":"The **division** of the inheritance was not equal."},{"sentence":"Malinaw ang **pagkakahati** ng opinyon ng mga tao sa isyung ito.","translation":"The **division** of people's opinions on this issue is clear."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kariton o sasakyang maliit na itinutulak at karaniwang ginagamit sa pagtitinda o paghakot ng mga kagamitan.
