usage_notes: Used before a name or pronoun (e.g., ani Rizal, aniya). Often found in literature and formal writing. It's a defective verb, meaning it doesn't have other conjugations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Maganda ang buhay,\" **ani** Lola Basyang.","translation":"\"Life is beautiful,\" **said** Lola Basyang."},{"sentence":"**Ani** Rizal, \"Ang hindi magmahal sa sariling wika ay higit pa sa hayop at malansang isda.\"","translation":"**According to** Rizal, \"He who does not love his own language is worse than an animal and a smelly fish.\""}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag sa matematika na nagpapakita ng pagkakapantay-pantay ng dalawang ekspresyon, na pinag-uugnay ng tandang 'equals' (=).
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "ecuación", na inangkop sa palabaybayang Filipino.
original_explanation: The reason for your high school math trauma. It's that thing with x's and y's that you had to solve. But outside the classroom, it's also used to describe any complex situation. Example: Commute + Rain + Rush Hour = The Ultimate Ekwasyon for Stress.
usage_notes: Ito ang mas karaniwang baybay sa modernong Filipino kumpara sa "ekuwasyon".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **ekwasyon** na E=mc² ay tanyag sa larangan ng pisika.","translation":"The **equation** E=mc² is famous in the field of physics."},{"sentence":"Itinuro ng guro kung paano lutasin ang isang linear **ekwasyon**.","translation":"The teacher taught how to solve a linear **equation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagawa o sinasabi nang maraming beses sa parehong paraan; walang katapusan o walang pagbabago.
original_explanation: Like that one song on TikTok that's stuck in your head. Or your mom's lecture about cleaning your room. Or your daily standup meeting where you say the same thing every day. It’s the human equivalent of a broken record or a GIF.
usage_notes: Can function as an adverb modifying a verb (e.g., "paulit-ulit na sinasabi") or an adjective describing a noun (e.g., "isang paulit-ulit na problema").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paulit-ulit** na lang ang tugtog sa radyo.","translation":"The music on the radio is just **repetitive**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **paulit-ulit** na tanungin, sinagot na kita.","translation":"Don't ask **over and over**, I already answered you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bulgar na termino para sa pagpaparaos sa sarili o pagbibigay-kasiyahan sa sariling ari.
original_explanation: Ah, the 'lonely-night-in' verb. It's what people do when their internet is down and they've already finished their Netflix queue. It's the DIY solution to a biological urge. While it can also mean 'to forge metal,' 99.9% of the time someone uses this word today, they're not talking about making a sword. It's the Philippines' unofficial contribution to Urban Dictionary.
usage_notes: This is considered a vulgar or taboo word in most contexts. Use with extreme caution. The other meaning, 'to forge metal,' is now archaic and rarely used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal pag-usapan ang mga gawaing tulad ng **pagsalsal** sa harap ng mga bata.","translation":"It's forbidden to talk about acts like **masturbation** in front of children."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng malaking sukat mula sa ibaba pataas; may mataas na antas o posisyon.
original_explanation: Describes your standards, your pangarap, or yung building sa BGC. 'Ang taas naman ng bilihin ngayon!' Also describes your blood pressure after seeing your Meralco bill.
usage_notes: The root word 'taas' is often used, but the more common adjectival form is 'mataas'. Using 'taas' alone as an adjective can sound more emphatic or conversational.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **taas** ng lagnat mo!","translation":"Your fever is so **high**!"},{"sentence":"**Taas** talaga ng lipad ng saranggola niya.","translation":"His kite is flying really **high**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso na natanggal, nabakbak, o nabasag mula sa isang matigas na bagay, tulad ng kahoy, semento, o ngipin.
original_explanation: That chunk of cement that falls off a wall, the piece of wood you accidentally chop off, or that heartbreaking chip on your brand new phone screen. It's a piece that was violently separated from the whole. Can also refer to a broken-off piece of a tooth, which is a whole other level of 'aray'.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'mabangal' (to be chipped off).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **bangal** ang gilid ng mesa pagkatapos kong mabuwal.","translation":"There's a **chip** on the edge of the table after I fell."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya sa dentista ang **bangal** na ngipin.","translation":"He showed the dentist the **chipped-off piece of** tooth."}]

translation: ally; follower; one under someone's influence
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kapanalig o nasa ilalim ng impluwensya ng isang makapangyarihang tao, lalo na sa politika.
etymology: A metaphorical extension of 'kabig' (to pull in), as in someone who has been 'pulled into' one's circle of influence.
original_explanation: In the world of Philippine politics, this is your guy, your ally, your 'bata'. It's someone in your political stable. When a new mayor wins, they bring in all their 'kabig' to fill positions. It’s all about who you know and who's on your team.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a political context. The pronunciation stress often shifts to the last syllable to distinguish it from the physical action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ng posisyon sa city hall ay napunta sa mga **kabig** ng bagong mayor.","translation":"All the positions in city hall went to the **allies** of the new mayor."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang tapat na **kabig** ng senador.","translation":"He is known as a loyal **follower** of the senator."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuhos o paglubog ng isang bagay sa kumukulong tubig sa maikling sandali, karaniwan bilang paghahanda sa pagluluto o paglilinis.
original_explanation: It's what you do to your utensils when you're extra OC about germs, or what your mom does to vegetables before stir-frying so they stay crisp. Think of it as a quick, hot bath for food or things. Not a full boil, just a quick dip. Parang "seeing" lang sa chat, mabilisang pasilip lang.
usage_notes: Often used in cooking contexts, especially for vegetables (blanching) or sterilizing baby bottles. The verb form is often 'banlian' (to scald something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Banlian** mo muna ang mga kamatis para madaling balatan.","translation":"**Scald** the tomatoes first so they're easy to peel."},{"sentence":"Kailangang i-**banli** ang mga bote ng sanggol.","translation":"The baby bottles need to be **scalded**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang halimbawa, huwaran, o maliit na bahagi ng isang bagay na ipinapakita upang magbigay ng ideya sa kabuuan nito.
original_explanation: It's a sample. Like 'yung free taste sa supermarket, 'yun ang mustra ng produkto. Or 'yung maliit na fabric swatch na pinapakita sa'yo sa Divisoria bago ka bumili ng isang rolyo. It's the 'see before you buy' concept.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of sewing, construction, commerce, or teaching a process.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipakita mo ang **mustra** ng tela sa kliyente.","translation":"Show the fabric **sample** to the client."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **mustra** ng kulay ng pintura bago ako magdesisyon.","translation":"I need a **sample** of the paint color before I decide."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na pagbaybay at pagbigkas ng salitang Ingles na 'leopard'.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'leopard', na inangkop sa ponolohiyang Pilipino.
original_explanation: Ganito bigkasin ng Pinoy ang 'leopard'. Ito yung usong-usong print sa mga damit, bag, at sapatos sa Divisoria. 'Uy, ganda ng blouse mo, naka-**lepard** print!'
usage_notes: Lubos na kolokyal at impormal. Ginagamit sa kaswal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si ate ng blusang may disenyo ng **lepard**.","translation":"My sister bought a blouse with a **leopard** design."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estratehiya o paraan, na maaaring sikolohikal o praktikal, na ginagamit ng isang tao upang harapin ang mga nakaka-stress na sitwasyon, problema, o matinding emosyon.
etymology: Mula sa terminolohiya sa sikolohiya sa wikang Ingles, "coping" + "mechanism".
original_explanation: Your go-to move when life gets tough. For some, it's retail therapy (add to cart!). For others, it's binge-watching K-dramas, eating a whole tub of ice cream, or going to the gym. Healthy or not, if it helps you get through the day after a stressful meeting with your boss, that's your coping mechanism. 'Ano'ng coping mechanism mo?' is the new 'What's your sign?'
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa parehong pormal na talakayan sa kalusugang pangkaisipan at sa pang-araw-araw na kolokyal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagba-bake ay naging **coping mechanism** niya noong pandemya.","translation":"Baking became her **coping mechanism** during the pandemic."},{"sentence":"Mahalagang magkaroon ng malusog na **coping mechanism** para sa mental health.","translation":"It's important to have a healthy **coping mechanism** for mental health."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapaligid sa isang lugar, tulad ng isang lungsod o kuta, upang pilitin itong sumuko.
original_explanation: Imagine your group chat spamming someone who left you on 'seen'. That's a digital pagkubkob. Or when your tita, tito, and parents all corner you during a family reunion asking when you're getting married. That's a social pagkubkob. It's the act of surrounding something or someone until they give up.
usage_notes: Often used in historical or military contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkubkob** sa Bataan ay isang mahalagang yugto sa kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The **siege** of Bataan is an important chapter in Philippine history."},{"sentence":"Nagtagal nang ilang buwan ang **pagkubkob** ng mga sundalo sa kuta ng mga rebelde.","translation":"The soldiers' **encirclement** of the rebels' fort lasted for several months."}]

translation: to mention, to state, to cite
meaning_filipino: Sabihin o tukuyin ang isang bagay, pangalan, o impormasyon sa isang pahayag o usapan.
original_explanation: The formal way of saying 'i-chika mo.' When your boss says 'Please banggitin the key points,' they mean 'get to the point.' It's the act of dropping a name, a fact, or a piece of info into the conversation. 'Huwag mo akong babanggitin sa nanay ko, ha!' (Don't you dare mention me to my mom!).
usage_notes: A command or infinitive form (object-focus). The root word is 'banggit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **banggitin** ang pangalan ko sa iyong talumpati.","translation":"Don't forget to **mention** my name in your speech."},{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **banggitin** kung saan mo nakuha ang impormasyong iyan?","translation":"Can you **cite** where you got that information?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakulangan ng atensyon, pag-aalaga, o pag-aasikaso sa isang tao, bagay, o tungkulin.
original_explanation: That feeling when you've been "on delivered" for 3 days. Or when your plant dies because you forgot to water it. It's the art of being neglectful. Parang 'yung boss mong hindi pinapansin 'yung mga email mo for a raise. It’s a special kind of "seen-zone" for responsibilities.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa aktibong pagpapabaya o simpleng hindi pagbibigay ng sapat na pansin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kawalang-asikaso** sa mga maliliit na problema ay maaaring magdulot ng malaking pinsala.","translation":"The **neglect** of small problems can lead to major damage."},{"sentence":"Inireklamo siya dahil sa **kawalang-asikaso** sa kanyang mga alagang hayop.","translation":"A complaint was filed against him for his **neglect** of his pets."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghuhugas ng mukha gamit ang tubig at/o sabon. Ito ay isang utos na gawin ang paghihilamos.
original_explanation: The command your mom gives you when you wake up looking like a zombie. 'Anak, hilamusan mo nga 'yang mukha mo!' It's the universal reset button for your face, whether you just woke up, you're stressed from work, or you cried over a breakup.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus, command form of the verb. The root is 'hilamos'. The actor-focus verb is 'maghilamos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hilamusan** mo ang iyong mukha para magising ka.","translation":"**Wash your face** so you'll wake up."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos umiyak, agad niyang **hinilamusan** ang kanyang mukha.","translation":"After crying, she immediately **washed** her face."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding pananakit sa tiyan o bituka, karaniwan sa mga sanggol, na nagdudulot ng walang tigil na pag-iyak.
original_explanation: The reason why new parents look like zombies from a Walking Dead episode. 'Yung iyak ng baby na parang walang bukas, at 'di mo alam kung gutom, basa ang diaper, o may koliko lang talaga. It's the ultimate "what does the baby want?!" mystery.
usage_notes: A medical term, primarily associated with infants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniisip ng ina na baka may **koliko** ang kanyang sanggol kaya ito iyak nang iyak.","translation":"The mother thinks her baby might have **colic**, which is why he is crying nonstop."},{"sentence":"Madalas daw ang **koliko** sa mga sanggol sa unang tatlong buwan.","translation":"**Colic** is said to be common in infants in their first three months."}]

translation: to struggle to get free; to break loose
meaning_filipino: Ang malakas na paggalaw o pag-iwas upang makawala mula sa pagkakahawak, pagkakagapos, o anumang pagpipigil.
original_explanation: The feeling when your boss gives you OT on a Friday night and you try to find an excuse to leave. It's that desperate struggle to escape, whether from a literal hold, a boring meeting, or a toxic relationship. It’s the physical manifestation of 'Let me go!'
usage_notes: Implies a forceful and often desperate struggle against a restraint.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukang **magpumiglas** ng nahuling magnanakaw mula sa mga pulis.","translation":"The caught thief tried to **struggle free** from the police."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko nang **magpumiglas** sa lahat ng aking responsibilidad, kahit isang araw lang.","translation":"I want to **break loose** from all my responsibilities, even for just one day."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging lito, balisa, o hindi mapakali dahil sa pagkalito o pag-aalala.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling mo pagkatapos ng team building niyo tapos 'di mo alam kung anong nangyari pero masaya ka lang. Or 'yung itsura mo kapag sinabi ng boss mo na "we need to talk" pero wala ka namang ginawang mali (sana). Parang lutang.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a state of mental confusion or disorientation. It's a more literary or deep word than 'lito'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwang **alimwang** ang binata matapos siyang iwan ng kasintahan.","translation":"The young man was left **bewildered** after his girlfriend left him."}]

meaning_filipino: Mapunô ng alikabok o dumi na dala ng hangin.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na iniwan mo lang saglit 'yung gamit mo tapos pagbalik mo, pwede mo nang sulatan ng "Wash Me". Ganyan 'pag nagkaalikabok na ang isang bagay, o 'yung feelings niya para sa'yo after a long time of no contact.
usage_notes: Describes the state of something accumulating dust, often from being left untouched.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwanang bukas ang bintana para hindi **magkaalikabok** ang mga kasangkapan.","translation":"Don't leave the window open so the furniture won't **get dusty**."},{"sentence":"Mabilis **magkaalikabok** ang mga libro sa estante.","translation":"The books on the shelf **get dusty** quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, lalo na sa isang babae, na kumikilos o nag-iisip nang mas maaga sa inaasahan; maaari ring tumukoy sa bayad na ibinigay nang pauna.
original_explanation: This is your tita who asks "Kailan ka ikakasal?" the moment you introduce your new jowa. She's jumping the gun, she's adelantada. It can also mean getting your salary in advance (a.k.a. "vale"), which is great until the actual payday comes and you're broke. It's being too forward, whether in a conversation or with your finances.
usage_notes: Can have a slightly negative connotation, implying someone is being presumptuous or nosy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Adelantada** ka naman masyado, hindi pa nga kami, tinatanong mo na kung saan ang kasal.","translation":"You're being too **presumptuous**, we're not even a couple yet and you're already asking where the wedding will be."},{"sentence":"Kumuha ako ng **adelantada** na sahod para sa biglaang gastos.","translation":"I got an **advanced** salary for an emergency expense."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumikilos nang mabagal, walang sigla, o walang ganang gumawa ng isang bagay.
etymology: Reduplication of 'patay' (dead) to indicate a state or manner of being 'half-dead' or lethargic.
original_explanation: That feeling when the internet is slow, your brain is slow, and everything feels like it's buffering. It's the energy of a Monday afternoon after a long weekend. When your boss asks for the report and you move with the speed of a sloth, that's 'patay-patay'.
usage_notes: Describes a lack of energy, enthusiasm, or speed in action. It implies a lethargic way of moving or working.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung **patay-patay** ang kilos mo, hinding-hindi ka matatapos sa trabaho ngayong araw.","translation":"If you move so **sluggishly**, you will never finish your work today."},{"sentence":"Bakit ba **patay-patay** ang serbisyo sa lugar na ito?","translation":"Why is the service in this place so **lackadaisical**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang nagsasalaysay ng isang kuwento o mga pangyayari.
etymology: From Spanish 'cuento' (story). The prefix 'nag-' and the reduplication of the first syllable 'kwe-' signifies the progressive aspect.
original_explanation: This is the national sport of every Filipino tita at a family reunion. They are the ones **telling stories** about the lives of all your cousins. It's the act of spilling the tea, sharing the 'chismis', or just catching up. 'Bes, maupo ka, may ikukwento ako sa'yo!' is the start of a beautiful (and long) conversation.
usage_notes: The progressive form of 'magkwento'. Very common in daily conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Habang **nagkwekwento** ang lola, nakikinig nang mabuti ang mga apo.","translation":"While grandma was **narrating**, the grandchildren were listening intently."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magkwento** tungkol sa kanyang mga paglalakbay.","translation":"He loves **telling stories** about his travels."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar na itinalaga para sa paliligo, tulad ng banyo, batis, o ilog.
original_explanation: The official term for any spot where you can 'ligo' (bathe). It could be your fancy bathroom with a tub, the communal 'banyo' in a dorm, the shower area at a beach resort, or even that specific spot in the river behind your lola's house in the province. If you can get clean there, it's a liguan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan sila na huwag mag-iwan ng kalat sa pampublikong **liguan**.","translation":"They were told not to leave a mess in the public **bathing place**."},{"sentence":"Ang aming **liguan** sa probinsya ay isang malinis na batis.","translation":"Our **bathing place** in the province is a clean stream."}]

meaning_filipino: Isuot o gamitin ang baro.
original_explanation: This is the verb form for putting on a 'baro'. Think of it as the command your lola gives you before a Santacruzan or a school program for Buwan ng Wika. "Baruin mo na 'yan!" means "Wear that baro now!" It's not just getting dressed; it's about wearing a piece of Filipino heritage.
usage_notes: Ang pandiwang ito ay partikular para sa pagsusuot ng isang `baro`. Para sa pangkalahatang damit, ginagamit ang `isuot`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Baruin** mo ang pinakamaganda mong bestida para sa piyesta.","translation":"**Wear** your most beautiful dress for the fiesta."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magiliw at karaniwang tawag sa ina bilang paggalang at paglalambing.
etymology: Isang baryasyon ng 'ina' (mother), na karaniwang ginagamit bilang direktang pantawag.
original_explanation: A softer, more traditional term for mom. It has that 'probinsya' or classic Filipino movie vibe. While others scream 'MOMMY!', the 'inay' user is probably more gentle, asking 'Inay, nasaan po ang paborito kong baso?'. It’s a term of endearment filled with warmth and respect.
usage_notes: Isang pantawag sa ina, katulad ng 'nanay' o 'mama'. Maaaring ituring na mas tradisyonal o pormal kumpara sa 'mommy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal na mahal kita, **Inay**.","translation":"I love you so much, **Mom**."},{"sentence":"Nagmano po ako sa aking **Inay** pagdating ko sa bahay.","translation":"I did the 'mano' gesture to my **mom** when I arrived home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng kahinaan o kabagalan, lalo na sa negosyo, kalakalan, o bentahan.
original_explanation: The dreaded word for every online seller, tindera sa palengke, and business owner. It's that period when customers are ghosting you, sales are flatlining, and your Gcash notifications are silent. It's the 'walang benta' season, often blamed on petsa de peligro.
usage_notes: Functions as a noun (e.g., "May tumal ngayon") or as the root for the more common adjective `matumal` (e.g., "Matumal ang benta").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakararanas ng **tumal** sa benta ang mga tindahan pagkatapos ng Pasko.","translation":"The stores are experiencing a **slump** in sales after Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, salita, o kilos na naglalayong magbigay ng aliw at magpangiti o magpatawa sa iba.
original_explanation: Your go-to meme folder. The 'class clown' of the friend group. That one corny joke your Tito tells at every family reunion. It's anything you pull out to lighten the mood, from a well-timed 'hirit' to a funny TikTok video. Basically, the antidote to a 'pampatamlay'.
usage_notes: Can refer to a joke, a funny story, a gimmick, or a person who is the comic relief.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling siyang magbitaw ng mga **pampatawa** kaya laging masaya sa grupo.","translation":"He's great at delivering **jokes**, so the group is always happy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng koneksyon, relasyon, o pagiging sangkot sa isang partikular na bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
etymology: From 'may' (has) + 'kinalaman' (involvement/relation), which comes from the root 'alam' (know).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "it's complicated" status for any situation. When you ask your friend why they're fighting with someone and they say, "Basta, may kinalaman 'to sa nangyari dati," you know it's deep. It's the go-to phrase for connecting dots, whether you're solving a crime ("May kinalaman ba siya sa krimen?") or just trying to understand office politics.
usage_notes: A very versatile and common phrase to express connection or involvement. The negative form 'walang kinalaman' (has no involvement) is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtaas ng presyo ng gasolina ay **may kinalaman** sa sitwasyon sa Gitnang Silangan.","translation":"The increase in gas prices **has something to do with** the situation in the Middle East."},{"sentence":"\"Wala akong **kinalaman** diyan!\" ang sigaw ng suspek.","translation":"\"I **am** not **involved** in that!\" shouted the suspect."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng nangyayari sa buhay mo ay **may kinalaman** sa mga desisyon mo.","translation":"Everything that happens in your life **is related to** your decisions."}]

translation: contradiction; conflict of opinion; mutual opposition
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng magkasalungat na pahayag, ideya, o interes; ang di-pagkakasundo.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + sa- (repetition) + salungat (opposite, contrary) + -an (reciprocal suffix).
original_explanation: When your friend says "Tara, save money tayo!" and then five minutes later says "Kain tayo sa labas?". That's a pagsasalungatan. It's the conflict in a story, the debate in a meeting, or the internal struggle between your diet and that box of donuts.
usage_notes: Denotes a mutual or internal conflict or contradiction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **pagsasalungatan** sa mga testimonya ng dalawang saksi.","translation":"There is a **contradiction** in the testimonies of the two witnesses."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsasalungatan** ng interes ay isang seryosong isyu sa gobyerno.","translation":"The **conflict** of interest is a serious issue in the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking lupain na hinati-hati sa mas maliliit na lote para sa pagtatayo ng mga tirahan, na karaniwang may sariling mga kalsada at pasilidad.
original_explanation: The Tagalized spelling for 'subdivision'. This is where your tita lives, the one with the gate, the guard, and the homeowners' association that's stricter than your parents. It's the dream: a house and lot, a small garden, and neighbors you can borrow sugar from (or gossip about).
usage_notes: This is the standard Filipino spelling. The English 'subdivision' is also very commonly used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatira sila sa isang pribadong **subdibisyon** sa Quezon City.","translation":"They live in a private **subdivision** in Quezon City."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang seguridad sa aming **subdibisyon**.","translation":"The security in our **subdivision** is strict."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maitim at marupok na materyal na nalilikha mula sa bahagyang pagsunog ng kahoy o iba pang organikong bagay sa kakulangan ng oxygen. Ginagamit bilang panggatong.
original_explanation: The secret ingredient to every authentic Pinoy BBQ and ihaw-ihaw. It's that smoky, dusty stuff your tito buys by the sack from the palengke. The smell of burning 'uling' is basically the official scent of a Filipino weekend cookout.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan pa nating bumili ng isang sakong **uling** para sa handaan.","translation":"We still need to buy a sack of **charcoal** for the party."},{"sentence":"Nagpa-baga siya ng **uling** para mag-ihaw ng isda.","translation":"He lit up the **charcoal** to grill fish."}]

translation: to squeeze each other; to press against each other
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay na pagpisil o pagdiin ng dalawa o higit pang tao sa isa't isa, karaniwan sa isang masikip na lugar.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "pisil" na may panlaping "-an".
original_explanation: The official term for what happens inside the MRT during rush hour. It's like a forced group hug you didn't sign up for. Everyone's trying to fit, so nagkakaroon ng 'pisikan'. Not to be confused with 'pisika' (physics), although the forces involved might feel similar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-umpisa nang mag-**pisikan** ang mga tao sa loob ng bus nang mapuno ito.","translation":"The people inside the bus started to **press against each other** when it became full."}]

translation: social grace; camaraderie; getting along with others
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahan o ugali ng isang tao na makibagay, makisalamuha, at magkaroon ng mabuting ugnayan sa kapwa.
etymology: From paki- (prefix related to interaction/joining) + sama (go with, join).
original_explanation: This is the Filipino social lubricant. It's the reason you'll sing karaoke even if you're sintunado, or drink one beer with the team even if you don't like it. It's about maintaining 'smooth interpersonal relations' (SIR). Having good 'pakisama' means you're a team player; having none means you're the KJ (killjoy) of the group.
usage_notes: A core Filipino cultural value. 'Marunong makisama' (knows how to get along) is a high compliment. 'Walang pakisama' (has no sense of camaraderie) is a strong criticism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Importante ang magandang **pakisama** sa trabaho.","translation":"Good **camaraderie** is important at work."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging marunong **makisama**.","translation":"He is known for being good at **getting along with others**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa kasintahan, nobyo, o nobya.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa pariralang Ingles na 'short time', na orihinal na tumutukoy sa isang kaswal na relasyon, bagama't ang kahulugan nito ay nagbago na upang tukuyin ang isang matatag na kasintahan.
original_explanation: Slang for your significant other. It's the old-school version of 'jowa.' If your tito asks 'May **syota** ka na?', he's asking if you're in a relationship. It's less formal than 'kasintahan' and more tito-vibes than 'jowa.'
usage_notes: Itinuturing na balbal o impormal. Mas karaniwan ang 'jowa' sa mga nakababatang henerasyon ngayon, ngunit malawak pa ring naiintindihan ang 'syota'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakilala ni Mark ang kanyang **syota** sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"Mark introduced his **girlfriend** to his parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Pinaikling anyo ng salitang Ingles na 'video'; isang rekording ng mga gumagalaw na imahe.
etymology: Pinaikling anyo ng salitang Ingles na 'video'.
original_explanation: The short and sweet term for 'video'. Kasi sino ba may time sabihin ang buong salita? 'Send mo na yung vid,' 'Nakita mo ba yung viral vid sa TikTok?' It's what you call the clips you watch, make, and share online. Quick, easy, and very internet-era.
usage_notes: Napaka-impormal at karaniwan sa online chats at social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"I-send mo sa akin ang **vid** ng pusa mo, ang cute!","translation":"Send me the **vid** of your cat, it's so cute!"},{"sentence":"Gawa tayo ng **vid** para sa project natin sa eskwela.","translation":"Let's make a **vid** for our school project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghiling na isailalim sa isang ritwal ng pagbabasbas ang isang bagay, lugar, o tao, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng isang pari o ministro.
etymology: From `pa-` (to ask someone to do) + `bendisyon` (blessing), from Spanish `bendición`.
original_explanation: The final step after buying a new car or moving into a new house. It's like getting the spiritual anti-virus installed. You invite a priest, prepare some food (because a Filipino blessing isn't complete without a feast), and he sprinkles holy water everywhere to ward off bad vibes and evil spirits. "Tara, pabendisyunan natin 'tong bagong office para swertehin!"
usage_notes: Primarily used in a Roman Catholic context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailan mo balak **pabendisyunan** ang bago ninyong bahay?","translation":"When do you plan **to have** your new house **blessed**?"},{"sentence":"Dinala niya ang kanyang bagong rosaryo sa simbahan para **pabendisyunan**.","translation":"She brought her new rosary to the church **to have it blessed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang gulay na tumutubo sa mga basang lugar o tubig, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga lutuing Pilipino tulad ng sinigang at adobo.
original_explanation: The ultimate budget-friendly veggie! Pang-adobo, pang-sinigang, pang-gisa. Pag 'kangkong' na lang ang ulam, alam mong petsa de peligro na. It's the vegetable representation of 'kapit lang, bes!'
usage_notes: Isang napaka-karaniwang gulay sa lutuing Pilipino. Kilala rin bilang 'river spinach' o 'water morning glory'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong ulam ang adobong **kangkong** na may maraming bawang.","translation":"My favorite dish is adobong **kangkong** with lots of garlic."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ilaw na gumagana sa pamamagitan ng kuryente, karaniwang tumutukoy sa bumbilya.
etymology: A compound word from Tagalog 'ilaw' (light) and Spanish 'eléctrica' (electric).
original_explanation: The OG lolo of your ring light and smart bulbs. Ito yung isinisigaw mo sa Meralco kapag brownout. Before LED, ito ang reyna ng gabi.
usage_notes: Often shortened to just 'ilaw' when the context of electricity is clear. It's a bit formal; people usually say 'bumbilya' (bulb).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinalitan niya ang pundidong **ilaw-elektrika** sa kusina.","translation":"He replaced the burnt-out **electric light** in the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Mas matipid daw ang mga bagong **ilaw-elektrika** kumpara sa mga luma.","translation":"They say the new **electric lights** are more economical compared to the old ones."}]

translation: to be insulted; to feel offended
meaning_filipino: Maramdaman ang isang panlalait o kawalan ng paggalang; masaktan ang damdamin dahil sa sinabi o ginawa ng iba.
etymology: From `ma-` (potential verb prefix) + `insulto` (insult) + `-han` (locative/benefactive suffix). 'Insulto' is from Spanish 'insulto'.
original_explanation: That moment when a "joke" from a tito doesn't land right ("Uy, tumaba ka!"). It's when a comment hits a nerve and you're left thinking, "Insulto ba 'yun o compliment?" In the age of social media, it's what happens when you read the comments section.
usage_notes: This is the potential/infinitive form. `Nainsulto` is the completed aspect. It focuses on the person receiving the insult.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **mainsultuhan** kaya hindi na lang ako sasali sa usapan nila.","translation":"I don't want **to be insulted** so I just won't join their conversation."},{"sentence":"Tila nainsultuhan siya sa sinabi mong biro.","translation":"It seems she was offended by the joke you told."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hayop sa tubig na may matigas na talukab, sampung paa kabilang ang dalawang sipit. Isang pangkalahatang termino para sa alimango o alimasag.
original_explanation: This is the Spanish-sounding cousin of 'alimango' and 'alimasag'. Parang yung friend mong galing Spain, 'kangreho' ang sinasabi instead of crab. Medyo old school pakinggan, parang lola mo lang ang gumagamit.
usage_notes: Hindi gaanong karaniwan kaysa 'alimango' (mud crab) o 'alimasag' (blue crab), ngunit naiintindihan. Madalas gamitin sa mga mas pormal o pampanitikang konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap hulihin ang mga **kangreho** dahil mabilis silang magtago sa buhangin.","translation":"It's difficult to catch **crabs** because they quickly hide in the sand."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at mabilis kumalat na apoy o sunog.
original_explanation: This isn't just a small flame from your lighter; this is a full-on, raging inferno. Think of the fire that makes it to the evening news. It's a word that carries a sense of urgency and danger. "Dabdab" is what happens when someone leaves the iron on, times a thousand.
usage_notes: More poetic or literary than the common word "sunog."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **dabdab** ang tumupok sa lumang gusali.","translation":"A huge **blaze** consumed the old building."},{"sentence":"Naging abo ang lahat dahil sa **dabdab**.","translation":"Everything turned to ash because of the **conflagration**."}]

translation: to be outdone; to be surpassed
meaning_filipino: Madaig o mahigitan ng iba sa isang labanan, paligsahan, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The feeling when your officemate gets the promotion you were aiming for. 'Yung ayaw mong mangyari sa videoke night – na may mas magaling kumanta sa'yo ng 'My Way'. It's about not letting others get the upper hand, especially when it's unfair. Ayaw nating malamangan!
usage_notes: Carries a competitive or sometimes negative connotation of being unfairly outdone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **malamangan** kaya't nagsisikap siya nang husto sa trabaho.","translation":"He doesn't want **to be outdone**, so he works very hard."},{"sentence":"Sa negosyo, hindi ka dapat papayag na **malamangan** ng iyong kakumpitensya.","translation":"In business, you should not allow yourself **to be surpassed** by your competitors."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa "Get Ready With Me," na tumutukoy sa isang uri ng video o social media content kung saan ipinapakita ng isang tao ang kanilang proseso ng paghahanda para sa isang okasyon.
original_explanation: Acronym for "Get Ready With Me." Ito 'yung content na pinapanood mo sa TikTok habang nagkakape, kung saan nagme-makeup at nagkukuwento 'yung influencer tungkol sa jowa niyang red flag. Basically, chismis with a makeup tutorial.
usage_notes: Exclusively used in social media contexts, particularly by Gen Z and millennials. It's an acronym, not a word to be conjugated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-film siya ng **GRWM** video para sa kanyang prom.","translation":"She filmed a **GRWM** (Get Ready With Me) video for her prom."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong **GRWM** ay 'yung may kasamang life advice.","translation":"My favorite **GRWM** is the one that comes with life advice."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng labis na pagpayat o paghina ng katawan ng isang tao o hayop.
etymology: From `pang-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root (`pa-` from `payat`) + `payat` + `-in`.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your wallet before payday. It's what stress, heartbreak, or a really bad diet does to a person. To be affected by something that **causes you to become thin** is to be pinangayayat. It's the opposite of "pinataba ng pag-ibig" (made fat by love).
usage_notes: This is a causative verb. It implies an external force or reason causing the thinness. The actor-focus form is 'mangayayat' (to become thin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala nang sobra, baka ka lang **pangayayatin** niyan.","translation":"Don't worry too much, that might just **cause you to become thin**."},{"sentence":"Ang sakit ang **nagpangayayat** sa kanya.","translation":"The illness is what **made him emaciated**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasama o kaibigan mula pa noong panahon ng pagkabata.
etymology: From `ka-` (denoting a companion or one of the same group) + `bata` (child).
original_explanation: Your OG barkada. The one who saw you with sipon, played patintero and tumbang preso with you, and knows your most embarrassing childhood secrets. They are the human version of your baby pictures.
usage_notes: A term filled with nostalgia and a sense of deep, long-lasting friendship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Marco ang aking matalik na **kababata**.","translation":"Marco is my closest **childhood friend**."},{"sentence":"Nagkita-kita muli ang magkaka-**kababata** pagkatapos ng dalawampung taon.","translation":"The **childhood friends** saw each other again after twenty years."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mataas na opisyal ng pamahalaan na namumuno sa isang partikular na kagawaran o ahensya ng estado, o isang pinuno sa isang relihiyosong pangkat.
original_explanation: The OG boss of a government department, like the Secretary of Health or Education. In a religious context, it's your pastor or priest. Basically, someone in charge who probably has a lot of meetings and paperwork.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang miyembro ng gabinete ng gobyerno o sa isang lider ng relihiyon tulad ng pastor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **ministro** ng kalusugan ay nagbigay ng bagong anunsyo.","translation":"The **minister** of health gave a new announcement."},{"sentence":"Isang kagalang-galang na **ministro** ang namuno sa seremonya sa simbahan.","translation":"A respected **minister** led the ceremony at the church."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagpalutang-lutang sa tubig o sa hangin nang walang tiyak na direksyon. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay nangangahulugang pagiging wala sa sarili o kawalan ng pokus.
etymology: Reduplication of the future tense 'lulutang' from the root 'lutang' (to float).
original_explanation: This describes something floating aimlessly, like a piece of plastic in the Pasig River or your brain during a 3-hour Zoom meeting that could have been an email. It can be literal (floating on water) or figurative, like when you're daydreaming and not paying attention. 'Para kang lulutang-lutang' is the Tagalog for 'You seem out of it.'
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for objects and figuratively for a person's state of mind. Often used as an adjective or adverb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang isang bote na **lulutang-lutang** sa dagat.","translation":"I saw a bottle **floating** in the sea."},{"sentence":"**Lulutang-lutang** ang isip ko buong araw dahil sa puyat.","translation":"My mind was **adrift** all day from lack of sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging tagapamagitan o hukom sa isang laro o paligsahan upang matiyak na nasusunod ang mga alituntunin.
etymology: From English 'referee', with Filipino verb affixes.
original_explanation: Ito yung trabaho mo sa basketball court kapag ayaw mong may away-away. Ikaw yung taga-sabi kung foul, out of bounds, o traveling, kahit na lahat ng tao sa court at sa bleachers ay sinisigawan ka. Parang moderator sa group chat pero may pito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **reperihan** ang laban ng Ginebra at Magnolia mamaya?","translation":"Who will **referee** the game between Ginebra and Magnolia later?"},{"sentence":"Mahirap **reperihan** ang laro kapag magkakaibigan lang ang naglalaban.","translation":"It's hard to **referee** a game when it's just friends playing against each other."}]

translation: to be bewitched; to be attacked by an aswang
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging biktima o nasa ilalim ng kapangyarihan ng isang aswang.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you're the main character in a Filipino horror movie. Basically, an aswang has its evil eye on you. It's the supernatural equivalent of being 'seen-zoned' by a monster. They're not just sliding into your DMs; they're sliding into your nightmares.
usage_notes: Often used in folklore and horror stories. Implies being targeted or afflicted by an 'aswang'. The spelling 'aswangin' is a variant of the more common 'aswangin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi ng albularyo, **asuangin** daw ang bata kaya ito laging may sakit.","translation":"The folk healer said the child is **being bewitched by an aswang**, which is why they are always sick."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabahagi ng isang bagay, impormasyon, o karanasan sa iba. Isa itong Taglish na pandiwa.
original_explanation: The act of not being 'madamot' (selfish). From food ('Tara, mag-share tayo sa fries') to feelings ('Gusto ko lang mag-share ng hugot ko'). In the digital world, it's the one-click action that can make something go viral.
usage_notes: Used for both physical items and digital content. The formal Filipino equivalent is 'magbahagi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiyang **magshare** ng iyong mga problema.","translation":"Don't be shy **to share** your problems."},{"sentence":"Paki-**magshare** naman ng presentation mo sa screen.","translation":"Please **share** your presentation on the screen."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos nang mabilis o pagmamadali upang matapos ang isang gawain o marating ang isang lugar sa takdang oras.
original_explanation: This is you when your Grab is 1 minute away and you're still in your towel. Or when the deadline is in 5 minutes and you're just starting the conclusion. To mag-apura is to go into panic mode, to move faster than usual. "Dalian mo!" is its battle cry.
usage_notes: Often interchangeable with `magmadali`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mag-apura** kung ayaw nating mahuli sa flight.","translation":"We need **to hurry** if we don't want to be late for our flight."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-apura** sa pagsagot para hindi ka magkamali.","translation":"Don't **rush** your answers so you won't make a mistake."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakataas na entablado o plataporma kung saan isinasagawa ang isang pagtatanghal, seremonya, o pagtatalumpati.
original_explanation: The stage where you either shine or totally bomb. It's where the guest speaker stands during graduation, where the beauty contestants do their final walk, and where your class presentation anxiety kicks in. The higher the platina, the higher the pressure.
usage_notes: Not a very common word; 'entablado' or the English 'stage' are more frequently used. This word has a more formal, slightly old-fashioned feel. Do not confuse with 'Platino' (platinum).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umakyat sa **platina** ang nagwagi upang tanggapin ang kanyang parangal.","translation":"The winner went up the **stage** to receive their award."},{"sentence":"Mula sa **platina**, nagbigay ng talumpati ang panauhing pandangal.","translation":"From the **dais**, the guest of honor delivered a speech."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang suliranin, tanong, o bagay na mahirap unawain, ipaliwanag, o lutasin, na nangangailangan ng masusing pag-iisip.
original_explanation: This is the official term for 'Which came first, the chicken or the egg?'. It's a riddle, a puzzle, or even your crush's mixed signals. Basically, anything that makes your brain short-circuit trying to figure it out. 'Why did they like your story but not reply to your chat?' — that is a huge **palaisipan**.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging isang malaking **palaisipan** sa mga pulis ang misteryosong pagkawala ng ebidensya.","translation":"The mysterious disappearance of the evidence became a huge **puzzle** for the police."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang sumagot sa mga **palaisipan** sa dyaryo.","translation":"He likes to answer the **puzzles** in the newspaper."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalabas ng hangin mula sa tiyan sa pamamagitan ng bibig, na karaniwang may kasamang tunog.
original_explanation: That sound you make after chugging a whole bottle of Coke. In some cultures, it’s a compliment to the chef. In a BPO meeting, it’s a reason to hit the mute button. It's the body's natural way of saying "busog na po" or "excuse me".
usage_notes: Can be considered impolite if done loudly in public.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **dumighal** sa gitna ng hapunan.","translation":"He suddenly **belched** in the middle of dinner."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **dumighal** nang hindi nagtatakip ng bibig.","translation":"Don't **burp** without covering your mouth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panlabas na bahagi ng isang bagay; ang pook sa hindi sakop ng isang istruktura; ang pagpapalabas o pagiging available sa publiko.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *lə(m)bas na nangangahulugang 'makita' o 'lumitaw'.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'loob'. "Sa labas tayo kumain." (Let's eat outside.) It's where your mom tells you to play, and where your Grab driver is waiting. It can also mean 'release' or 'showing' for a movie. "Kailan ang labas ng bagong Marvel movie?"
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan (ang labas) o pang-abay (sa labas). Ginagamit din sa konteksto ng pelikula o produkto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ingay ay galing sa **labas** ng bahay.","translation":"The noise is coming from **outside** the house."},{"sentence":"Inaabangan ko ang **labas** ng bago niyang album.","translation":"I'm waiting for the **release** of his new album."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na daluyan ng tubig na mas maliit kaysa sa isang ilog.
original_explanation: Not the river, not the ocean, but the smaller, chill cousin of the ilog. It's where you'd catch tadpoles as a kid, or where your paper boat would inevitably get stuck. In the city, it's that 'estero' you hope you don't fall into.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglalaro ang mga bata sa malinaw na **sapa**.","translation":"The children are playing in the clear **creek**."},{"sentence":"May maliit na tulay na kawayan sa ibabaw ng **sapa**.","translation":"There is a small bamboo bridge over the **stream**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likidong kemikal na ipinapahid sa isang ibabaw upang bigyan ito ng kulay, proteksyon, o disenyo.
original_explanation: The stuff you use to give your room a new vibe, or what artists use to create a masterpiece. Also, a metaphor for covering something up. 'Nag-pinta lang ng ngiti' is the 'This is fine' dog meme in Filipino—smiling on the outside but screaming on the inside.
usage_notes: Can refer to the substance (paint) or the result of painting (a painting). The verb form is "magpinta" or "pinturahan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating bumili ng puting **pinta** para sa dingding.","translation":"We need to buy white **paint** for the wall."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **pinta** ni Juan Luna na Spoliarium.","translation":"The **painting** by Juan Luna, Spoliarium, is beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain o paglalakbay kung saan ang pangunahing layunin ay ang kumain, tumikim ng iba't ibang uri ng pagkain, o bisitahin ang mga kilalang kainan.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'food' (pagkain) at 'trip' (paglalakbay; slang para sa gawain).
original_explanation: The national sport of Filipinos. Ito 'yung "Tara, kain tayo!" na nag-evolve into a multi-location, multi-course adventure. Pwedeng mag-start sa isaw sa UP, tapos milk tea sa Maginhawa, at magtatapos sa ramen sa Katipunan. It's a journey where your stomach is the destination.
usage_notes: A very common Filipino-English slang that has become part of the mainstream vocabulary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang saya ng **foodtrip** namin sa Pampanga kagabi!","translation":"Our **food trip** in Pampanga last night was so fun!"},{"sentence":"Niyaya niya ako mag-**foodtrip** sa Binondo.","translation":"He invited me to go on a **food trip** in Binondo."}]

translation: call; summons; something used for calling
meaning_filipino: Isang salita, tunog, o instrumento na ginagamit upang tawagin ang pansin ng isang tao o hayop; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang tawag o panawagan.
original_explanation: Anything you use to call someone's attention. It can be a literal thing like a megaphone (panawag), a bell, or a horn. It can also be a name or a sound, like when you whistle for your dog, that's your panawag. Metaphorically, it's that "call to action" you see in ads, or the "call of duty" (panawagan ng tungkulin) you feel when your friend needs help moving out.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa instrumento na pantawag, sa mismong tawag, o sa isang pangalan o bansag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang kampana bilang **panawag** sa mga mag-aaral.","translation":"He used the bell as a **call** for the students."},{"sentence":"Ang 'Kuya' ay karaniwang **panawag** sa nakatatandang kapatid na lalaki.","translation":"'Kuya' is a common **appellation** for an older brother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang di-karaniwang baryasyon o maling pagbigkas ng salitang 'leeg,' ang bahagi ng katawan na nag-uugnay sa ulo at katawan.
etymology: Posibleng baryasyon o metatesis ng salitang 'leeg.'
original_explanation: Sounds like a typo for 'leeg' that someone just rolled with. It’s that part of your body your tita pinches, where you put your kwintas, or what gets stiff after a whole day of WFH and 'online-sabong' with your boss.
usage_notes: Napakabihira at hindi pamantayan. 'Leeg' ang tama at pangkalahatang ginagamit na termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sakit ng **liab** ko kakayuko sa cellphone.","translation":"My **neck** hurts from looking down at my cellphone."},{"sentence":"Nagsuot siya ng gintong kuwintas sa kanyang **liab**.","translation":"She wore a gold necklace on her **neck**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at marahas na pagsugod o pag-atake sa isang tao o bagay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "daluhong" (pagsugod) at ang gitlaping "-um-".
original_explanation: That intense moment when shoppers charge at the doors during a 12.12 sale. Or when your dog dumaluhong sa'yo pag-uwi mo galing work. It's a sudden, forceful, and often chaotic rush. Not a chill vibe.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang agresibo at mabilis na paglapit o pag-atake.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Galit na **dumaluhong** ang aso sa magnanakaw.","translation":"The dog angrily **charged** at the thief."},{"sentence":"Parang mga langgam na **dumaluhong** ang mga tao sa libreng pagkain.","translation":"Like ants, the people **rushed violently** towards the free food."}]

translation: it is as if; seems to be
meaning_filipino: Isang pagpapaikli ng "animo ay," na ginagamit upang pagdugtungin ang paghahambing sa kasunod na salita o parirala.
original_explanation: This is just the contracted form of "animo ay." It's a smoother, more poetic way to connect "animo" to the next word. Think of it as the literary equivalent of mashing words together in a text message, but for sounding elegant. "Animo'y pangarap" flows better than "animo ay isang pangarap."
usage_notes: A purely literary and formal contraction. You will almost never hear this in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang daloy ng trapiko ay **animo'y** isang ahas na gumagapang.","translation":"The flow of traffic **is as if** it's a crawling snake."},{"sentence":"Nakatitig lang siya sa malayo, **animo'y** may malalim na iniisip.","translation":"He just stared into the distance, **as if** he was deep in thought."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang narkotikong gamot na nakalalango at nakapagpapaantok, na nakukuha mula sa pinatuyong dagta ng halamang poppy. Ito ay pinagmumulan ng morphine, codeine, at heroin.
original_explanation: Ito yung OG na pampatulog, pero yung illegal at delikado. Bago pa nauso ang Netflix para puyatan, ito yung ginagamit ng mga tao sa lumang panahon para 'mag-relax' nang todo. Sa modernong panahon, ito yung source ng mga powerful painkiller at... mga seryosong problema sa batas.
usage_notes: Isang salitang may mabigat na konotasyon dahil sa pagiging ilegal na droga. Madalas mabanggit sa mga araling pangkasaysayan at balita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paggamit ng **opyum** ay mahigpit na ipinagbabawal ng batas.","translation":"The use of **opium** is strictly prohibited by law."}]

translation: to be able to cause drowsiness; to make sleepy
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng antok o pagkahilo na nais matulog.
original_explanation: The superpower of your professor during a 1 PM lecture. The effect of a heavy lunch of kare-kare. The vibe of a rainy, cold afternoon when you're supposed to be working. Anything that makes you want to find the nearest bed and take a nap. "Warning: makaantok ang gamot na ito."
usage_notes: This is a causative verb; it describes something *causing* sleepiness in someone else. The more common form used is 'nakakaantok' (is causing sleepiness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagbabasa ng libro sa gabi ay **nakakaantok** para sa akin.","translation":"Reading a book at night **makes me sleepy**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang iinom ng gamot na **makaantok** kung magmamaneho ka.","translation":"Don't take medicine that **causes drowsiness** if you are going to drive."}]

translation: to agree with; to side with; to support a point
meaning_filipino: Sumang-ayon o pumanig sa isang pananaw, opinyon, o argumento.
etymology: From `maki-` (social prefix) + `katig` (outrigger, support). The root word `katig` refers to the outriggers of a boat that provide balance and support.
original_explanation: It's like saying "+1" in a group chat or "I second the motion" in a meeting. When your friend has a valid 'hugot' and you totally get it, you makikatig in their sentiment. It's a more formal way of saying you're on the same page.
usage_notes: More formal than `sumang-ayon`. Often used in debates, legal contexts, or formal discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami ang **makikatig** sa kanyang panukala dahil ito ay para sa ikabubuti ng lahat.","translation":"Many will **agree with** his proposal because it is for the good of all."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **makikatig** sa isang opinyon na walang sapat na ebidensya.","translation":"It's hard to **support a point** that lacks sufficient evidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging pabaya; kakulangan sa angkop na pag-iingat o atensyon na nagreresulta sa pinsala o panganib.
original_explanation: This is that 'Bahala na si Batman' attitude, but with actual consequences. It's when you were supposed to water the plants, but you forgot, and now they're dead. That's 'kapabayaan'. On a serious note, it's a legal term for when someone fails to do something they're supposed to do, causing harm. It's the ultimate 'you had one job' failure.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa kontekstong legal, pormal, o seryosong usapin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kapabayaan** sa pag-aaral ay maaaring magdulot ng mababang marka.","translation":"**Neglect** in studies can lead to low grades."},{"sentence":"Sinampahan siya ng kaso dahil sa **kapabayaan** na nagresulta sa aksidente.","translation":"A case was filed against him for **negligence** that resulted in an accident."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar, karaniwang isang kariton o puwesto, kung saan nagbebenta at nagluluto ng fishball at iba pang pagkaing-kalye.
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood 'tusok-tusok' station. It's not just a food cart; it's a community center where you catch up on the latest chismis while waiting for your order. The aroma of frying oil and sweet sauce is its bat-signal.
usage_notes: A colloquial term. Can also refer to the vendor themselves, though 'magfi-fishball' is more common for that.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, punta tayo sa **fishballan** sa kanto.","translation":"Let's go to the **fishball stand** on the corner."},{"sentence":"Laging maraming tao sa **fishballan** ni Aling Nena.","translation":"There are always many people at Aling Nena's **fishball cart**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng hiram na salapi o bagay sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of that moment of truth. To 'pautangin' someone is to trust them with your hard-earned cash, hoping it doesn't turn into a ghosting situation. It's the ultimate test of friendship, second only to assembling IKEA furniture together.
usage_notes: The object of this verb is the person receiving the loan. 'Pautangin mo si Juan' means 'Lend to Juan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pautangin** mo muna ako, babayaran kita sa sahod.","translation":"**Lend me some money** for now, I'll pay you on payday."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **pautangin** ang taong hindi marunong magbayad.","translation":"It's difficult **to lend to** a person who doesn't know how to pay."}]

translation: to be able to see from a distance; to glimpse
meaning_filipino: Maaninag o makita ang isang bagay mula sa malayo.
etymology: ma- (abilitative prefix) + tanaw (view from a distance)
original_explanation: That feeling when you're on a bus and you finally see the familiar landmark near your house. Or when you're at the top of a mountain and you can see the whole city. It's seeing something far away, like your sweldo on the 10th of the month, or the possibility of your crush liking you back. "Malayo pa, pero matatanaw na."
usage_notes: Implies seeing something that is far.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula sa bintana ng eroplano, **matatanaw** mo ang maliliit na kabahayan.","translation":"From the airplane window, you **can see** the small houses **from a distance**."},{"sentence":"Sa tuktok ng bundok, **matatanaw** ang buong kapatagan.","translation":"At the top of the mountain, the entire plain **can be seen**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pag-uusap sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao kung saan ang isa ay nagtatanong upang makakuha ng impormasyon, karaniwan para sa isang trabaho, balita, o pananaliksik.
original_explanation: That nerve-wracking meeting where you have to sell yourself better than a real estate agent sells a condo with a 'great view' of a concrete wall. You practice your answer to 'where do you see yourself in 5 years?' while secretly hoping your answer is 'not in another interbiyu like this.' It's the final boss battle before you can get that sahod.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb ('i-interbiyu,' 'interbiyuhin').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumasa ako sa unang **interbiyu** para sa BPO.","translation":"I passed the first **interview** for the BPO."},{"sentence":"Kinakabahan ako para sa **interbiyu** ko bukas.","translation":"I'm nervous for my **interview** tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Nag-uudyok o nag-aakit na gumawa ng isang bagay na karaniwang ipinagbabawal o hindi kanais-nais.
original_explanation: That extra slice of cake when you're on a diet. That "Add to Cart" button during a 12.12 sale. That chismis you know you shouldn't listen to. Anything that makes you say "Sige na nga, minsan lang naman," is nakatutukso. It's anything that tempts you to break the rules (or your diet).
usage_notes: The prefix 'nakatutu-' intensifies the root word, meaning 'very tempting'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakatutukso** ang alok nilang malaking sahod pero sa malayong lugar.","translation":"Their offer of a high salary is **tempting**, but it's in a faraway place."},{"sentence":"Ang amoy ng bagong lutong tinapay ay **nakatutukso**.","translation":"The smell of newly baked bread is **alluring**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at hindi mapigilang pagbuga ng hangin mula sa ilong at bibig, karaniwang sanhi ng iritasyon sa ilong.
original_explanation: That sudden, explosive 'Haaachoo!' moment. One 'pagbahin' and someone's lola will immediately say 'Bless you!' or hand you Katinko. In the time of COVID, a single 'pagbahin' in a crowded LRT could make you the most unpopular person in the world for about 30 seconds.
usage_notes: Refers to the act of sneezing, while 'bahin' is the sneeze itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya mapigilan ang kanyang **pagbahin** dahil sa alikabok.","translation":"He couldn't stop his **sneezing** because of the dust."}]

translation: Hollowness; state of being caved in
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging malukong, may hukay, o pagiging walang laman sa loob.
original_explanation: Imagine mo yung pisngi mo nung tinanggalan ka ng wisdom tooth, or yung pakiramdam ng wallet mo after mag-shopping sa 12.12 sale. Ganun. That hollow, sunken feeling. Not to be confused with 'pagkalungkot' (sadness), though your wallet's pagkalungkong can lead to your pagkalungkot.
usage_notes: Isang napakabihirang salita na madalas mapagkamalang 'pagkalungkot'. Tumutukoy ito sa pisikal na katangian ng pagiging malukong. (A very rare word often mistaken for 'pagkalungkot'. This refers to the physical quality of being concave.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin ang **pagkalungkong** ng kaniyang mga pisngi dahil sa matinding sakit.","translation":"The **hollowness** of his cheeks was noticeable due to severe illness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na pantawag o titulo para sa isang babaeng may-asawa.
etymology: From 'ginoo' (sir) + '-ng' (linker) with a semantic shift for the feminine equivalent.
original_explanation: The formal way to address a married woman, your teacher, or your boss's wife. It’s the equivalent of 'Mrs.' or 'Ma'am.' Use this before you default to 'Tita,' just to be safe.
usage_notes: Abbreviated as 'Gng.' Always capitalized when used as a title before a name.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magandang umaga po, **Ginang** Reyes.","translation":"Good morning, **Mrs.** Reyes."},{"sentence":"Ang susunod na tagapagsalita ay si **Ginang** Cruz.","translation":"The next speaker is **Mrs.** Cruz."}]

translation: not going with, failure to accompany
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng hindi pagsama o pag-ayaw na sumabay sa isang tao o grupo sa isang lakad o gawain.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (hindi) at "pagkasama" (act of going with).
original_explanation: Yung ayaw mong sumama sa outing kasi tinatamad ka or wala kang pera, pero ang dahilan mo "may gagawin ako." It's the polite way of saying "pass muna ako diyan." This is the act, not the state of being excluded (`di-pagkakasama`).
usage_notes: Nakatuon sa aksyon ng hindi pagsama sa isang tao, na kadalasan ay personal na pagpili. Ihambing sa "di-pagkakasama", na tungkol sa pagiging hindi kasali.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinatampo niya ang **di-pagkasama** mo sa kaniyang kaarawan.","translation":"He was hurt by your **not going with** him on his birthday."},{"sentence":"Ang **di-pagkasama** ni Ana ay dahil may sakit ang kaniyang ina.","translation":"Ana's **failure to accompany** us was because her mother was sick."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapakita ng katuwaan o kasiyahan sa pamamagitan ng tunog at paggalaw ng mukha; nasa anyong panghinaharap.
etymology: Mula sa "tawa" (laugh) na may pag-uulit ng unang pantig (ta-) bilang panandang panghinaharap.
original_explanation: Future tense of laughing. This is your reaction when your friend tells a corny joke ('Sige na nga, tatawa na ako.'). Or your evil plan when you see someone about to trip ('Hala, watch this, tatawa ako mamaya.'). It's the future promise of finding something funny, or at least pretending to.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong panghinaharap ng salitang-ugat na "tawa".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguradong **tatawa** ka kapag napanood mo ang pelikulang iyon.","translation":"You **will surely laugh** when you watch that movie."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, walang **tatawa** sa iyo.","translation":"Don't worry, no one **will laugh** at you."}]

translation: what will become of; where will it lead to
meaning_filipino: Isang salitang patanong na tumutukoy sa kahihinatnan, patutunguhan, o resulta ng isang bagay o kilos.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'Saan aabot ang 20 pesos mo?' question, but for life choices. It's the question your Tita asks when you say you're quitting your stable job to become a vlogger. '**Pasasaan** ba 'yang pagv-vlog mo?' It's a mix of genuine concern and a hint of 'I-told-you-so' energy.
usage_notes: Almost always used in rhetorical questions, implying a negative or uncertain outcome. Often paired with 'ba' or 'pa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasasaan** ba ang lahat ng paghihirap na ito?","translation":"**What will become of** all this hardship?"},{"sentence":"Kung hindi ka mag-aaral, **pasasaan** ka?","translation":"If you don't study, **what will become of you**?"}]

translation: to woo; to court; to appease
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalambing, pag-amo, o panunuyo sa isang tao upang makuha ang loob, pag-ibig, o patawad nito.
etymology: Salitang ugat na 'suyo' na may panlaping '-in'.
original_explanation: What you do when your partner is 'tampororot.' You bring them milk tea, their favorite food, or just give them space until they're ready to talk. It's the art of pacifying someone, whether it's for love or to say sorry for forgetting your monthsary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **suyuin** ang iyong kasintahan dahil nagtatampo siya.","translation":"You need to **appease** your girlfriend because she is sulking."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **suyuin** ang dalaga sa pamamagitan ng pag-awit.","translation":"He tried to **woo** the young lady by singing."}]

translation: to see; to be able to see; to find
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kakayahang matanaw, matagpuan, o mapansin ang isang bagay, tao, o lugar gamit ang mga mata o sa diwa.
original_explanation: When you're looking for your phone and you finally spot it under a pillow, you shout 'Ayun! Nakita ko na!' It's the 'ability-to-see' or the successful result of 'looking for' something. It can also be accidental, like when you makita your ex at the mall. Awkward.
usage_notes: 'Makita' is an ability/potential/accidental verb. It's different from 'tumingin' (to look) and 'manood' (to watch). It focuses on the perception or discovery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **makita** ko na ang hinahanap kong libro.","translation":"I hope I can **find** the book I'm looking for."},{"sentence":"Hindi kita **makita** sa dilim.","translation":"I can't **see** you in the dark."},{"sentence":"Nagulat ako nang **makita** ko siya sa sinehan.","translation":"I was surprised when I **saw** him at the cinema."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyong medikal kung saan may labis na likido na naiipon sa mga espasyo sa loob ng mga tisyu ng katawan, na nagdudulot ng pamamaga.
etymology: Mula sa Griyego, sa pamamagitan ng Ingles/Espanyol na "edema".
original_explanation: This is what happens to your ankles after a 12-hour flight or a long day of standing. It's your body retaining water like you retain grudges. In Pinoy context, it's often called 'manas'. "Uy, ang laki ng paa mo, parang may edema!"
usage_notes: Mas kilala sa pang-araw-araw na usapan bilang "manas".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **edema** sa kanyang mga binti ay senyales ng problema sa bato.","translation":"The **edema** in his legs is a sign of a kidney problem."},{"sentence":"Ipinayo ng doktor na itaas ang kanyang paa upang mabawasan ang **edema**.","translation":"The doctor advised elevating her foot to reduce the **edema**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging putol, tanggal, o hiwalay nang biglaan at may puwersa mula sa pinagkakabitan.
original_explanation: Imagine pulling a loose thread on your shirt and—whoops—a whole chunk of fabric comes off. That's pigtal. It's a sudden, forceful tear. It's the state of your earphones after they get snagged on a doorknob. It’s also what happens to your heart when your crush says, 'Friends lang tayo.' Snapped.
usage_notes: Refers to the state of being snapped or torn off. The verb form is 'pigtasin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang **pigtal** na kuwintas sa sahig.","translation":"She saw the **snapped** necklace on the floor."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging pinsala dahil sa **pigtal** na kable ng kuryente.","translation":"The damage was extensive because of the **snapped** electrical cable."}]

translation: to shred (something); to tear (something) to pieces
meaning_filipino: Piraso-pirasuhin o durugin ang isang tiyak na bagay. Ito ang anyong pautos o tumutukoy sa obheto ng pandiwang 'lamuray'.
original_explanation: The command form. It's what your mom tells you to do to the old clothes for rags: "**Lamurayin** mo 'yan!" It's also the silent command your heart gives your brain when you see your ex's new picture: "**Lamurayin** mo ang feelings mo, girl, move on!"
usage_notes: This is the object-focused form of 'lamuray'. The '-in' suffix directs the action to a specific object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kanyang **nilamuray** ang ebidensya upang walang makatuklas.","translation":"He **shredded** the evidence so no one would find out."},{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **lamurayin** mo itong manok para sa ating pansit.","translation":"Please **shred** this chicken for our noodles."}]

meaning_filipino: Pinatuyong tangkay at dahon ng palay pagkatapos itong magiik. Ginagamit itong pagkain ng hayop, pataba, o materyales.
original_explanation: It's the stuff left over after harvesting rice. Basically, it's Filipino hay. You see it in the provinces piled up, used to feed carabaos, or sometimes for art projects. It's the aesthetic of the 'simple life' post on Instagram, complete with a sunset and a carabao.
usage_notes: Primarily associated with agriculture, farming, and rural life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kalabaw ay masayang ngumunguya ng **dayami** sa bukid.","translation":"The carabao is happily chewing **hay** in the field."},{"sentence":"Ginagamit ang **dayami** bilang bubong ng mga tradisyonal na kubo.","translation":"They use **rice straw** as roofing for traditional huts."}]

translation: dismissal; removal; act of making someone leave
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kilos ng pagpilit sa isang tao na umalis sa isang lugar, posisyon, o tungkulin.
original_explanation: This is the formal term for 'kicking someone out.' It could be your landlord serving you an eviction notice, your boss telling you 'we're letting you go,' or your mom telling your noisy friends 'Uwi na!' (Go home!). It’s the action that results from someone overstaying their welcome, whether in a job, a house, or a relationship.
usage_notes: Can refer to eviction from a property, firing from a job, or simply making someone leave a space.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinasama ng loob ng empleyado ang biglaang **pagpapaalis** sa kanya sa kumpanya.","translation":"The employee resented the sudden **dismissal** of him from the company."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang may mga balahibo o hibla na nakakabit sa isang hawakan, ginagamit sa pagpipinta, paglilinis, o paglalagay ng likido.
original_explanation: The bigger, badder cousin of the artist's brush. This is what you use when you're painting a whole wall, not a delicate masterpiece. It's the tool for big jobs, like slapping barbecue marinade on a whole liempo or painting your house for Christmas. Not to be confused with 'brotse' for your hair or clothes.
usage_notes: Typically refers to a larger brush for paint, varnish, or cleaning, as opposed to a smaller artist's brush.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng mas malaking **brotsa** para matapos agad ang pagpipinta ng pader.","translation":"We need a bigger **paintbrush** to finish painting the wall quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampalasa na mula sa hinog na bunga ng halamang Piper nigrum, kung saan tinatanggalan ng balat ang buto bago patuyuin. Ito ay may mas banayad na anghang kumpara sa pamintang itim.
etymology: Tambalang salita ng "paminta" (mula sa Espanyol "pimienta") at "puti".
original_explanation: Ito yung pampalasa na ginagamit mo kapag ayaw mong may itim-itim na tuldok sa luto mo, lalo na sa mga light-colored sauces or soups. Parang yung kaibigan mong lowkey lang pero may sipa pa rin. Hindi kasing-eskandalosa ng black pepper, mas refined.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pagluluto upang magbigay ng lasa nang hindi nagbabago ang kulay ng pagkain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng kaunting **pamintang puti** ang sopas para sumarap.","translation":"Add a little **white pepper** to the soup to make it delicious."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto niyang gamitin ang **pamintang puti** sa kanyang bechamel sauce.","translation":"She prefers to use **white pepper** in her bechamel sauce."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha sa isang bagay mula sa isang tao bilang parusa o sa bisa ng awtoridad, alinsunod sa batas o regulasyon.
original_explanation: Remember when your teacher took your phone in high school because you were texting in class? That's it. It's the official act of taking something away because rules were broken. The MMDA does this to illegal vendors, and your mom does this to your video game console when your grades drop.
usage_notes: Used in legal, official, or authoritative contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumumpiska** ng mga pekeng produkto ang mga ahente ng gobyerno.","translation":"The government agents **confiscated** the counterfeit products."},{"sentence":"**Kumumpiska** ang guro ng mga cellphone habang may pagsusulit.","translation":"The teacher **confiscated** cellphones during the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Palitan ang perang papel ng katumbas na halaga sa barya o mas maliit na halaga ng pera.
original_explanation: The official term for that awkward moment at the sari-sari store when you try to buy a ₱10 candy with a ₱1000 bill. "Pabarya po" is the magic phrase. `Baryahin` is the action of breaking down big money into smol money, a crucial skill for surviving your daily commute.
usage_notes: Kasingkahulugan ng `papalitan` sa konteksto ng pera, ngunit ang `baryahin` ay partikular na nagpapahiwatig ng pagpapalit sa mas maliliit na papel na pera o barya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pwede po bang **baryahin** itong isang libo ko?","translation":"Can you please **change** this one-thousand peso bill of mine?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha o pagdampot ng isang bagay, lalo na mula sa sahig o lupa, gamit ang mga kamay.
etymology: From `pulot` (the act of picking up) + `-in` suffix.
original_explanation: What your mom yells when you drop food on the floor ('**Pulutin** mo 'yan!'). It's the act of picking up something you dropped, finding something on the ground, or gathering scattered items. The 5-second rule totally applies here.
usage_notes: This is the object-focused verb. The synonym 'damputin' often implies picking up smaller things more delicately.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pulutin** mo ang mga laruang nakakalat sa sahig.","translation":"**Pick up** the toys scattered on the floor."},{"sentence":"Nakita kong may sinusubukang **pulutin** ang matanda mula sa kalsada.","translation":"I saw the old man trying **to pick up** something from the road."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglilipat ng teksto o imahe sa papel o ibang materyales gamit ang makina o teknolohiya.
original_explanation: The verb form of what you do at the computer shop when your prof requires a hard copy. From thesis printing to getting your boarding pass, this is the action. "Pa-print" is the command, "umimprenta" is the action that follows.
usage_notes: While "mag-print" is more common in modern colloquial speech due to English influence, "umimprenta" is a valid, slightly more formal verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **umimprenta** ng mga dokumentong ito?","translation":"Who **printed** these documents?"},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **umimprenta** ng isang daang kopya para sa seminar.","translation":"We need to **print** one hundred copies for the seminar."}]

translation: to be able to worsen; to be able to aggravate
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang gawing mas malala o mas seryoso ang isang sitwasyon, kalagayan, o karamdaman.
original_explanation: The opposite of `makapagpabuti`. This is when you try to "fix" something but end up making it worse, like putting salt on a wound or adding more drama to an already complicated chismis. "Ang pagwawalang-bahala sa maliliit na problema ay maaaring makapagpalubha sa sitwasyon."
usage_notes: Often used for problems, illnesses, or negative situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-inom ng maling gamot ay maaaring **makapagpalubha** ng iyong sakit.","translation":"Taking the wrong medicine can **worsen** your illness."},{"sentence":"Ang pagsisinungaling mo ay lalo lang **makapagpapalubha** ng gulo.","translation":"Your lying will only **be able to aggravate** the conflict."}]

translation: to wage war against; to attack
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang opensibang militar o armadong pag-atake laban sa isang lugar, bansa, o pangkat.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'digmaan'. It's what happens when 'diplomatic war' fails and the 'suntukan na lang' energy becomes real. It's the act of invading or attacking someone or something. Figuratively, it's what you want to do to your slow internet connection during a crucial Zoom meeting.
usage_notes: A transitive verb. The object of the verb is the one being attacked or waged war upon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbanta ang malaking bansa na **digmain** ang sinumang papasok sa kanilang teritoryo.","translation":"The large country threatened **to wage war against** anyone who enters their territory."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **digmain** ang isyu, harapin mo nang mahinahon.","translation":"Don't **attack** the issue, face it calmly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, karaniwang lalaki, na mahilig mambola o gumamit ng matatamis na salita upang makakuha ng pabor o para sa panliligaw, kadalasan ay hindi tapat.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Espanyol na 'bolero' (isang taong nagsasabi ng kasinungalingan o bola).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung tipo ng tao na sasabihing 'Ikaw ang pinakamagandang bituin sa kalangitan' kahit tanghaling tapat. Expert sa paggamit ng flowery words para mapa-oo ka. Master ng 'sana all' at 'ikaw lang sapat na' pero bukas, sa iba na sinasabi. Ingat sa mga bolero!
usage_notes: Halos palaging may negatibo o mapaglarong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig ng kawalan ng katapatan. Ang katumbas na babae ay 'bolera'.
