usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniniwala sa kanya, kilalang **bolero** 'yan sa buong opisina.","translation":"Don't believe him, he's a known **sweet-talker** in the entire office."},{"sentence":"Ang galing niyang mambola, tunay na **bolero**!","translation":"He's so good at flattery, a true **flatterer**!"}]

meaning_filipino: 1. Nagpapakita ng pambihirang kakayahan o kahusayan. 2. Nakabawi na mula sa isang karamdaman.
original_explanation: Your go-to word for two kinds of 'winning.' First, it's the ultimate compliment for someone who's a genius at their job, a master chef in the kitchen, or a karaoke god—they're **magaling** (excellent). Second, it's the sigh of relief when someone's finally over the flu—'Hay salamat, **magaling** na ako!' (Thank goodness, I'm recovered!). It's the word for both peak performance and peak health.
usage_notes: The context (praising a skill vs. discussing health) determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magaling** siyang manlalaro ng basketball.","translation":"He is an **excellent** basketball player."},{"sentence":"Buti naman at **magaling** ka na sa iyong sakit.","translation":"It's good that you have **recovered** from your illness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na anunsyo sa pahayagan o ibang midyum na nagbabalita ng kamatayan ng isang tao, kalakip ang mga detalye tungkol sa burol at libing.
original_explanation: This is the `patalastas` nobody wants to be in, but everyone will eventually have. It's the section in the newspaper, usually with a small black and white photo, that announces someone has passed away. It gives the details: where to send your condolences (and abuloy), and when the final goodbye is. It's the formal "RIP" post before social media existed.
usage_notes: Commonly found in the classified ads section of newspapers. In modern times, this has largely been replaced by social media posts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabasa ko ang **patalastas sa pagkamatay** sa dyaryo para malaman ang detalye ng burol.","translation":"I read the **obituary** in the newspaper to know the details of the wake."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagkakamali o gawain na napakabigat kung kaya't hindi maaaring patawarin o palampasin.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (hindi) at "mapagpapaumanhinan" (maaaring bigyan ng paumanhin o patawarin).
original_explanation: Cheating on a final exam, stealing the team's lunch money, or putting pineapple on someone else's pizza without asking. These are acts that are di-mapagpapaumanhinan. It's the ultimate "you've crossed the line" descriptor for an offense so grave, no amount of 'sorry' can fix it.
usage_notes: Isang napakapormal at mabigat na salita para sa malulubhang pagkakasala. Hindi karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pagtataksil sa bayan ay isang krimen na **di-mapagpapaumanhinan**.","translation":"His betrayal of the country is an **unforgivable** crime."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang pagsisinungaling ay isang pagkakamaling **di-mapagpapaumanhinan**.","translation":"For her, lying is an **inexcusable** mistake."}]

translation: to be worried, to be doubtful
meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pahayag na nangangahulugang pagkakaroon ng matinding pag-aalala, pag-aalinlangan, o pangamba.
etymology: Idiomatic expression. 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'alapaap' (high clouds) + 'ang' (the) + 'loob' (inner self). Literally 'for the inner self to become cloudy'.
original_explanation: This is your 'loob' (inner self) having cloudy weather. Parang may bagyo sa feelings mo. It's that anxious, unsettled feeling when you're waiting for exam results or when your crush leaves you on 'seen'.
usage_notes: A highly expressive and somewhat poetic way to describe worry or anxiety.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mag-alapaap ang loob** ng ina nang hindi pa umuuwi ang kanyang anak.","translation":"The mother started **to get worried** when her child had not yet come home."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **mag-alapaap ang iyong loob** dahil lang sa maliliit na problema.","translation":"Don't let yourself **be filled with doubt** just because of small problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw nang pabalik-balik habang nakabitin o nakasabit sa isang bagay, tulad ng isang duyan o pendulo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'tayon' na may kahulugang pag-ugoy o pag-indayog.
original_explanation: Parang pendulum, o 'yung duyan sa probinsya. O 'yung mood mo kapag 'di ka sure kung magre-reply ba siya o hindi. Undayon lang nang undayon ang feelings. It's the gentle, rhythmic back-and-forth motion.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga bagay na gumagalaw na parang duyan o pendulo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig **umundayon** ang mga bata sa duyan sa ilalim ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"The children love to **swing** in the hammock under the mango tree."},{"sentence":"Ang mga sanga ng puno ay **umundayon** dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"The branches of the tree **swayed** because of the strong wind."}]

translation: to put leaves on; to add leaves
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng dahon ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Imagine you're making a lei or a floral arrangement, and you need to add the leafy bits for filler. That's **dahunan**. Or when your mom tells you to **dahunan** the sinigang with more kangkong leaves. It's the act of leaf-ifying something.
usage_notes: A specific verb not commonly used in everyday conversation but understood in context, especially in cooking or crafts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dinahunan** niya ang banga bago ito ilagay sa apoy.","translation":"She **put leaves on** the clay pot before placing it on the fire."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **dahunan** ang salad para magmukhang sariwa.","translation":"We need to **add leaves** to the salad to make it look fresh."}]

translation: to tip off; to inform secretly
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng lihim na impormasyon o babala ang isang tao, lalo na ang mga awtoridad, tungkol sa isang ilegal na gawain.
etymology: From Spanish 'timbre' (stamp, bell). The meaning evolved to 'ringing a bell' or alerting someone.
original_explanation: The OG 'snitch'. It's when you see something sketchy and you slide into the DMs of the barangay tanod. 'May nag-timbre sa pulis tungkol sa iligal na pasugalan kaya nahuli sila.'
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of crime or reporting wrongdoing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang naglakas ng loob na **magtimbre** sa mga awtoridad?","translation":"Who could have had the courage to **tip off** the authorities?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot **magtimbre** kung may nakita kang mali.","translation":"Don't be afraid to **inform secretly** if you see something wrong."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho o propesyon ay ang pagguhit ng mga plano, larawan, o disenyo.
original_explanation: The OG "creative." Before Canva and Adobe Illustrator, this was the person you'd call to draw blueprints for a house, sketch a portrait, or illustrate a comic book. Think of the police sketch artist you see on TV, that's a dibuhante.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha siyang **dibuhante** ng isang malaking kumpanya ng arkitektura.","translation":"He was hired as a **draftsman** by a large architecture firm."},{"sentence":"Ang galing ng **dibuhante** sa pagguhit ng mukha ng suspek.","translation":"The **sketch artist** was excellent at drawing the suspect's face."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain o gamit, na ginagamit sa proseso ng pagdurog ng pagkain sa bibig. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa mismong kasangkapan tulad ng ngipin.
etymology: Mula sa `pang-` at `nguya` (pagdurog ng pagkain sa bibig).
original_explanation: Anything you use for chewing. 'Yung bubble gum na nginunguya mo 'pag bored ka sa meeting. 'Yung chicharon na ang sarap nguyain habang nanonood ng Netflix. Even your own teeth (mga ngiping **pangnguya**) count. Basically, if it's meant for the 'nguya' action, it's this.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa kasangkapan (tulad ng ngipin) o sa bagay na nginunguya (tulad ng chewing gum).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matibay ang kanyang mga ngiping **pangnguya**.","translation":"His **masticating** (chewing) teeth are strong."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng kendi na pwedeng **pangnguya** habang naghihintay.","translation":"Give me a candy that can be **for chewing** while waiting."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkakaroon ng epekto o bisa; pagpasok o pagbaon ng isang bagay, tulad ng gamot sa katawan o talim sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is when the Biogesic finally kicks in and your headache disappears. Or when your hugot quote finally hits your friend and they start crying. It's the moment of impact, when something—be it medicine, a blade, or words—finally works and makes its mark. 'Effective!'
usage_notes: Commonly used for medicine, poison, weapons, and figuratively for words or advice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi agad **tumalab** ang gamot kaya masama pa rin ang pakiramdam niya.","translation":"The medicine did not **take effect** right away, so he still feels unwell."},{"sentence":"**Tumalab** sa puso niya ang bawat salitang sinabi mo.","translation":"Every word you said **penetrated** his heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggulong o pag-ikot ng katawan na ang ulo ay nauuna sa paanan, karaniwang dahil sa pagkadapa o sinasadyang akrobatikong kilos.
original_explanation: That moment when you trip on a random tile in the mall and do an accidental, ungraceful 'bumalintong'. It's the physical version of 'Sana lamunin na ako ng lupa.' Also, what gymnasts do for a living.
usage_notes: Can be used for both accidental tumbles and intentional acrobatic flips.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napatakbo siya nang mabilis kaya't **bumalintong** siya nang madapa.","translation":"He ran so fast that he **tumbled** when he tripped."},{"sentence":"Nakabibilib ang mga atleta na kayang **bumalintong** nang maraming beses.","translation":"It's amazing how athletes can **somersault** multiple times."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na responsable sa paglipat o pagdadala ng isang karga, mensahe, o anumang bagay mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "tagapag-" (doer/agent of action) at sa salitang ugat na "dala" (carry).
original_explanation: The official "taga-bitbit" of the group. Whether it's the groceries, the team's equipment, or your friend's emotional baggage, you're the one carrying it. In logistics, this is your Grab or Lalamove rider.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa tao, hayop, o kahit na isang bagay (hal. 'tagapagdala ng sakit' - carrier of disease).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kalabaw ang nagsilbing **tagapagdala** ng mga aning palay.","translation":"The carabao served as the **carrier** of the harvested rice."},{"sentence":"Siya ang laging **tagapagdala** ng magandang balita sa aming pamilya.","translation":"He is always the **bearer** of good news in our family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lalaking kabiyak o asawa sa isang kasal.
etymology: Possibly from Sanskrit 'bhānu' (sun, master) or a related Austronesian root.
original_explanation: The old-school, almost poetic way to say 'husband'. You'd probably hear this in a classic Filipino movie or a kundiman. If your friend starts calling her BF 'aking bana', she's either being super romantic or super extra. Today, 'asawa' or 'mister' is way more common.
usage_notes: Considered archaic or literary. 'Asawa' is the everyday term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tapat ang pagmamahal ng ginang sa kanyang **bana**.","translation":"The lady's love for her **husband** is faithful."},{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang tula, ang **bana** ang haligi ng tahanan.","translation":"In old poems, the **husband** is the pillar of the home."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang gawain, bagay, o palabas na nagdudulot ng kasiyahan, libangan, o pagpapalipas ng oras.
original_explanation: Your Netflix subscription, your TikTok feed, your K-Pop stan account—lahat 'yan ay aliwan. It's your escape from the soul-crushing reality of adulting, traffic, and bills. It's the "sige, isang episode pa" at 2 AM. Your source of temporary joy.
usage_notes: A broad term covering all forms of entertainment, from watching movies to playing games.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang panonood ng pelikula ang kanyang paboritong **aliwan**.","translation":"Watching movies is his favorite **pastime**."},{"sentence":"Nagpunta sila sa perya para maghanap ng **aliwan**.","translation":"They went to the fair to look for **entertainment**."}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa grupong mang-aawit mula sa Timog Korea na 'Bangtan Sonyeondan'. Ginagamit din bilang hiram na salita para sa 'behind the scenes' o ang mga kaganapan sa likod ng kamera.
etymology: Acronym for the South Korean group 'Bangtan Sonyeondan' (방탄소년단). Also an initialism for the English phrase 'behind the scenes'.
original_explanation: Short for 'Bangtan Sonyeondan,' the K-pop group that your tita, your pamangkin, and maybe even your lolo is obsessed with. Also used by Pinoys to mean 'Behind The Scenes.' Example: 'Uy, pa-share naman ng BTS ng pre-nup niyo!' It's the chismis you really want to see, not just the polished final product.
usage_notes: The meaning is highly contextual. When a teenager screams it, it's the band. When a production manager says it, it means 'behind the scenes'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito ng anak ko ang **BTS**, kaya laging may K-Pop sa bahay.","translation":"My child's favorite is **BTS**, so there's always K-Pop in the house."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong makita ang mga **BTS** footage ng pelikula.","translation":"I want to see the **behind-the-scenes** footage of the movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na hindi marunong bumasa o sumulat; walang pormal na edukasyon.
original_explanation: The formal, almost harsh, term for someone who can't read or write. It's a word you'd find in a history book describing people from a past era, not something you'd casually use today. Calling someone **iliterato** in 2026 is like using a Shakespearean insult—it sounds smart but it's super offensive. We'd rather say 'may learning disability' or 'hindi nakapag-aral.'
usage_notes: This is a formal and somewhat dated term. Using it in casual conversation can be perceived as insensitive. The feminine form is `iliterata`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Layunin ng programa na bawasan ang bilang ng mga **iliterato** sa mga liblib na pook.","translation":"The program's goal is to reduce the number of **illiterate** people in remote areas."},{"sentence":"Itinuring siyang **iliterato** ng lipunan, ngunit napakatalino niya sa mga praktikal na bagay.","translation":"Society considered him **illiterate**, but he was very intelligent in practical matters."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng panloob na palda na isinusuot sa ilalim ng damit o saya upang magbigay-bulto o hugis dito.
original_explanation: Ito yung sinusuot ng lola mo sa ilalim ng bestida niya para magmukhang prinsesa sa lumang pelikula. Parang may sariling aircon sa ilalim ng palda mo. Medyo vintage na ang vibe nito, hindi na 'to pang-OOTD sa mall.
usage_notes: Kadalasan ginagamit sa mga tradisyonal na kasuotan tulad ng baro't saya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan pa ba ng **petikot** para sa isusuot kong Filipiniana sa Linggo ng Wika?","translation":"Do I still need a **petticoat** for the Filipiniana I'll wear for National Language Week?"},{"sentence":"Ang luma niyang bestida ay may magandang burda sa laylayan ng **petikot**.","translation":"Her old dress had beautiful embroidery on the hem of the **petticoat**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang layunin, mithiin, o tunguhin na nais makamit o marating.
etymology: From `hanggan` (limit, end) + `-in` (object suffix), signifying the 'end' one works towards.
original_explanation: Your 'hangganin' is your endgame, your KPI for life. It's the reason you're magti-tiis sa traffic ng EDSA, the motivation for working overtime, or the ultimate goal of your 'sana all' dreams. Think of it as the 'destination' in your Grab booking of life.
usage_notes: More formal than 'layunin' or 'mithiin' in some contexts. Refers to a final aim or purpose.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangunahing **hangganin** ng proyekto ay tulungan ang mga nasalanta.","translation":"The primary **objective** of the project is to help the victims."},{"sentence":"Ano ba ang iyong **hangganin** sa buhay?","translation":"What is your **purpose** in life?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasama sa paggawa o katrabaho sa isang partikular na lugar, proyekto, o kumpanya.
original_explanation: Your 'ka-tropa' at work. The person you share chismis with during coffee breaks, complain about the boss with, and maybe even split the bill with for the team lunch. They're your comrades in the corporate jungle or the BPO floor. The prefix 'ka-' means 'fellow' or 'co-'.
usage_notes: More formal than 'katrabaho'. Often used in speeches, formal writing, or by labor groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang maligayang pagbati sa lahat ng aking mga **kamanggagawa**!","translation":"A warm greeting to all my **co-workers**!"},{"sentence":"Ang unyon ay ipinaglalaban ang karapatan ng bawat **kamanggagawa**.","translation":"The union is fighting for the rights of every **fellow worker**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na ginagamit bilang sangkap o pampalasa sa pagluluto.
etymology: From Spanish 'recado' (message, errand, but in culinary context, ingredients/spices). The prefix 'pan-' indicates 'for the purpose of'.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga magic ingredients ni lola na ginagawang special ang adobo. Hindi lang asin at paminta, kundi yung mga dahon ng laurel, star anise, at kung anu-ano pang sikreto na ayaw niyang i-share. Parang sa buhay, kailangan mo ng 'panrekado' para hindi maging boring.
usage_notes: Used to describe items intended for use as ingredients or spices. Often found in markets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng mga **panrekado** para sa lulutuin niyang menudo.","translation":"Mom bought ingredients/seasonings **for** the menudo she will cook."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bloke ng pagkit o taba na may mitsa sa gitna na kapag sinindihan ay nagbibigay ng liwanag. Ginagamit sa mga seremonyang panrelihiyon, pag-alala sa mga yumaong mahal sa buhay, o bilang pangkagipitang ilaw tuwing may brownout.
original_explanation: The OG emergency light during a brownout, turning your home into a dramatic scene from a horror movie. It's for birthdays, All Saints' Day (Undas), and for when you want to set a ~romantic~ mood. Also, the subject of the song "parang 'sang kandila na dahan-dahang nauupos."
usage_notes: Central to many Filipino cultural and religious practices.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsindi kami ng **kandila** sa puntod ng aming lola.","translation":"We lit a **candle** at our grandmother's grave."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o gusali kung saan isinasagawa ang mga gawaing mekanikal, pagkukumpuni, o paggawa ng mga bagay, lalo na para sa mga sasakyan.
original_explanation: Your car's hospital. The place you go when your four-wheeled baby is 'sick' and needs a check-up. Dito mo rin maririnig ang magic words na, "Sir, papalitan na po ito." at goodbye, 13th month pay.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to an automotive repair shop, but can be used for any kind of workshop (e.g., for carpentry, metalworking).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ko ang kotse sa **talyer** dahil umuusok ang makina.","translation":"I brought the car to the **repair shop** because the engine was smoking."},{"sentence":"May malakas na ingay ng bakal na nagmumula sa **talyer** ni Mang Berto.","translation":"There's a loud noise of metal coming from Mang Berto's **workshop**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging alanganin, hindi komportable, o kakulangan sa kasanayan sa paggalaw o pakikisalamuha.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na first day mo sa work at hindi mo alam kung saan ka uupo, o 'yung first date na pareho kayong nakatitig lang sa menu. That's asiwa. It's the physical and social clumsiness we all feel when we're out of our element. Parang trying to dance to a TikTok trend you've only seen once.
usage_notes: Can describe a person, a situation, or a feeling. "Kaasiwaan" is the noun form (awkwardness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **asiwa** ang lahat nang bigla siyang nag-walkout.","translation":"Everything became **awkward** when he suddenly walked out."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **asiwa** ako sa tuwing kasama ko ang mga boss.","translation":"I feel **awkward** whenever I'm with the bosses."}]

translation: to run over something (with a vehicle)
meaning_filipino: Banggain o daanan ang isang bagay o tao gamit ang isang sasakyan.
original_explanation: This is what you shout when a reckless driver almost hits a pedestrian. "Muntik na akong maisagasa!" It's the verb form of a hit-and-run, but can also be accidental. A very stressful word to hear on the road.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of vehicles hitting something or someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iingat ang tsuper upang walang **isagasa** na hayop sa daan.","translation":"The driver is being careful not to **run over** any animal on the road."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng katawan sa pahalang na posisyon, karaniwan upang magpahinga o matulog.
original_explanation: The official verb for 'Sige, 5 minutes lang' which turns into 3 hours. It's the first step to a glorious nap after a long day of adulting. The ultimate act of surrender to pagod.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na ako, gusto ko nang **mahiga**.","translation":"I'm tired, I want to **lie down** already."},{"sentence":"**Mahiga** ka muna at magpahinga.","translation":"**Lie down** for a while and rest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kemikal na likido na ginagamit bilang panlinis (disinfectant) o sangkap sa mga inuming nakalalasing.
original_explanation: Your pandemic BFF for sanitizing everything from your hands to your Shopee deliveries. Also, the reason for many 'I-Dawn Zulueta mo ako!' moments during Friday night inuman sessions. It's a disinfectant and a social lubricant, depending on the context. Handle with care!
usage_notes: Can refer to both rubbing alcohol (for sanitation) and the intoxicating agent in beverages. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging magdala ng **alkohol** para panlinis ng kamay.","translation":"Always bring **alcohol** to clean your hands."},{"sentence":"Mataas ang porsyento ng **alkohol** sa inuming ito.","translation":"This beverage has a high **alcohol** percentage."}]

translation: The design is very... (humorous and ironic)
meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang nagpapahiwatig ng pagdududa o sarkasmo sa isang disenyo na hindi maganda, hindi praktikal, o katawa-tawa, na madalas kinukumpleto ng isang pang-uri (hal. "human," "Pinoy").
etymology: Nagmula sa isang internet meme, na kadalasang ginagamit upang punahin ang mga disenyong hindi madaling gamitin o lohikal.
original_explanation: The ultimate deadpan comment for when you see something that's so badly designed, it's hilarious. That janky DIY extension cord? "The design is very human." The CR with a glass door? "The design is very open-minded." It's the Filipino way of saying "What were they thinking?!" with a side of shade and a sprinkle of meme culture.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit bilang isang stand-alone na komento o caption sa social media para sa mga larawan o video ng masasamang disenyo. Ang parirala ay sadyang hindi kumpleto, na nag-iiwan sa mambabasa na punan ang blangko ng isang pang-uri na may pahiwatig ng kabalintunaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko yung hagdan na papunta sa pader. Grabe, **the design is very** thoughtful.","translation":"I saw the stairs that led to a wall. Wow, **the design is very** thoughtful."},{"sentence":"Yung gripo ang layo sa lababo? **The design is very** convenient.","translation":"The faucet is so far from the sink? **The design is very** convenient."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa Kristiyanismo, ang panahon ng apatnapung araw mula sa Miyerkules ng Abo hanggang sa Pasko ng Pagkabuhay, na inilalaan para sa pananalangin, pag-aayuno, at paggawa ng kabutihan.
original_explanation: Season of 'no meat on Fridays', 'alms giving', at 'I give up [insert vice here] for Lent'. Sa Pinas, ito rin ang signal for beach trips, a.k.a. Holy Week vacation. Yung iba seryoso sa penitensya, yung iba seryoso sa pag-book ng resort.
usage_notes: Ang katumbas nito sa Tagalog ay 'Kuwaresma'. Ang 'Lent' ay karaniwang ginagamit ng mga Pilipinong nagsasalita ng Ingles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Katoliko ang nag-aayuno tuwing **Lent**.","translation":"Many Catholics fast during **Lent**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng kabilang sa lahing may maitim na balat, partikular na mula sa liping Aprikano. Ginagamit din bilang pang-uri para ilarawan ang isang babaeng may napakaitim na kutis.
original_explanation: This is the female version of 'Negro', straight from Spanish. In the Philippines, it's often used, sometimes neutrally, sometimes... not so neutrally, to describe someone with very dark skin. It's that word your tita might use to describe your cousin who played in the sun too much: "Ay, naging negra na si Maria!" It's a loaded term, so tread carefully. Can be seen as dated or offensive depending on context and tone.
usage_notes: The term can be considered offensive or dated by many, especially when used to mock or stereotype. It's often used descriptively without malicious intent in older generations, but modern usage is more sensitive to its racial connotations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang pelikula, ang kontrabida ay madalas inilalarawan bilang isang matapang na **Negra**.","translation":"In old movies, the antagonist was often depicted as a fierce **Black woman**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong tawaging **Negra** ang kapatid mo dahil lang sa paglalaro niya sa araw; kayumanggi ang kulay niya.","translation":"Don't call your sister **Negra** just because she played under the sun; her color is brown."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng pagdakip o pagsakote sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you're caught breaking curfew by your mom, or when the MMDA finally catches you on the bus lane. It's the "gotcha!" moment, whether it's for a fish, a criminal, or you, five minutes late for your shift.
usage_notes: Can refer to catching something physically (like a ball or fish) or apprehending a person (arrest).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging mabilis ang **paghuli** ng mga pulis sa magnanakaw.","translation":"The police's **apprehension** of the thief was swift."},{"sentence":"Ang **paghuli** ng isda ay ang kanyang ikinabubuhay.","translation":"The **catching** of fish is his livelihood."}]

meaning_filipino: Salitang balbal na tumutukoy sa usapan, kuwentuhan, o tsismis.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish 'charlar' (to chat) or 'chica' (girl), implying girl talk. Its exact origin is debated but it is a staple of modern slang.
original_explanation: The lifeblood of Filipino social interaction. It's not just gossip; it's an exchange of information, updates, and sometimes, baseless rumors. 'Ano'ng chika?' is the Pinoy way of saying 'What's up?' or 'Spill the tea.'
usage_notes: Very common slang. Can be used as a noun (gossip) or a verb ('mag-chika', to chat).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bagong **chika** ako tungkol sa kapitbahay natin.","translation":"I have new **gossip** about our neighbor."},{"sentence":"Tara, mag-**chika** muna tayo habang nagkakape.","translation":"Come on, let's **chat** for a while over coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging padalus-dalos, mapangahas, o walang-ingat sa paggawa ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is your "YOLO" energy, but with potentially bad consequences. It's the audacity to reply-all to a company-wide email, the recklessness of booking a flight without approved leave, or the "kapusukan" of confessing to your crush via a TikTok dance. High risk, questionable reward.
usage_notes: Carries a slightly negative connotation, implying a lack of foresight or caution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dala ng kaniyang **kapusukan**, nasangkot siya sa gulo.","translation":"Because of his **recklessness**, he got involved in trouble."},{"sentence":"Ang **kapusukan** ng kabataan ay dapat gabayan ng mga nakatatanda.","translation":"The **impetuousness** of youth should be guided by elders."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pamumuhay, kabuhayan, o ang mga gawain at kalagayan na bumubuo sa pang-araw-araw na karanasan ng isang tao o pangkat.
original_explanation: How you hustle. Your 9-to-5 job, your side-gigs, your small business—anything you do to pay the bills, buy milk tea, and fund your Shopee/Lazada addiction. It's your personal 'diskarte' in the game of life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagsasaka ang pangunahing **pamumuhay** sa aming probinsya.","translation":"Farming is the main **livelihood** in our province."},{"sentence":"Nagbago ang kanyang **pamumuhay** mula nang manalo siya sa lotto.","translation":"His **way of life** changed since he won the lottery."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang yugto sa isang relasyon kung saan ang isang tao ay nagsasagawa ng panunuyo o panliligaw sa iba.
etymology: Mula sa 'pa-' (nagpapahiwatig ng kilos), 'ligaw' (panunuyo), at '-an' (nagpapahiwatig ng panahon o kaganapan).
original_explanation: The 'getting to know you' stage, but with more effort. Ito 'yung time na nagpapa-impress si boy kay girl (or vice versa), hatid-sundo, bigay bulaklak, at libre sa sine. The whole traditional (or modern) courtship dance before you can change your relationship status to 'In a Relationship'.
usage_notes: Ang salitang-ugat na 'ligaw' dito ay nangangahulugang 'manuyo' (to court), hindi 'mawala' (to be lost).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal din ang naging **paligawan** nina Lolo at Lola noong araw.","translation":"Grandpa and Grandma's **courtship period** back in the day was also quite long."},{"sentence":"Sa panahon ngayon, iba na ang takbo ng **paligawan**.","translation":"Nowadays, the way **courtship** happens is different."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nabuo sa pamamagitan ng pagbaligtad ng mga pantig ng salitang "mismo." Nangangahulugang "tama," "sang-ayon," o "totoo."
etymology: Pagbaliktad ng mga pantig ng salitang 'mismo'.
original_explanation: Baliktad na "mismo". This is the ultimate "I agree" for the cool kids. When your friend says, "Tara, food trip?" and you reply with a firm "**omsim**," it means "hell yeah" and "you read my mind" all in one. It’s a cooler, quicker way to say 'mismo'.
usage_notes: Bahagi ng "millennial/Gen Z slang" na gumagamit ng pagbabaligtad ng salita (hal. lodi, petmalu).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Ganda ng laban kanina, 'no?\" \"**Omsim**!\"","translation":"\"Great game earlier, right?\" \"**Totally**!\""},{"sentence":"**Omsim**, siya nga ang may sabi niyan.","translation":"**That's right**, he was the one who said that."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang paglakas o pag-alab ng apoy; biglaang pagtindi ng isang damdamin o pangyayari.
original_explanation: Imagine the flame on your gas stove when you suddenly turn the knob to max. That's sigid. It's also that sudden flare-up of anger when someone cuts you in line at the MRT, or the intense kilig when your crush finally messages you. It's a sudden burst of something.
usage_notes: Can be used for both literal fire and metaphorical intensity of emotions or situations. It is not a very common word in daily conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat kami sa biglang **sigid** ng apoy mula sa kalan.","translation":"We were surprised by the sudden **flare-up** of the fire from the stove."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **sigid** ng galit nang marinig ang balita.","translation":"He felt the **intensity** of anger upon hearing the news."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-asinta o pag-direkta ng isang bagay sa isang tiyak na target. Ito rin ay nangangahulugang matamang pagsubaybay o masinsinang atensyon.
original_explanation: Two meanings, one vibe: intense focus. 1) Literally aiming, like a cameraman getting the perfect shot or a gamer lining up a headshot. 2) Figuratively, it’s you being glued to the TV for the latest chismis on a talk show or your boss watching your every move before a deadline. It's being 'locked on' to a target.
usage_notes: Context determines whether it's physical aiming or intense focus/monitoring. It implies a closer, more intense focus than 'pagtutuon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng kalmado at tiyak na **pagtututok** ng kamera sa gumagalaw na paksa.","translation":"A calm and precise **aiming** of the camera at the moving subject is needed."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pagtututok** sa balita, alam niya ang lahat ng nangyayari.","translation":"Because of his **intense focus** on the news, he knows everything that's happening."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estruktura na itinayo upang magdugtong sa dalawang magkahiwalay na lugar, tulad ng sa ibabaw ng ilog, bangin, o kalsada, upang maging daanan ng mga tao o sasakyan.
original_explanation: Literally a bridge, like the San Juanico Bridge. Figuratively, it's your friend who introduces you to their cute cousin. “Bes, **tulay** mo naman ako sa kanya.” It's the go-between, the connector, the 'da moves' facilitator.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa isang pisikal na istraktura o metaporikal para sa isang tao o bagay na nag-uugnay sa dalawang panig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumawid kami sa makitid na **tulay** na kawayan.","translation":"We crossed the narrow bamboo **bridge**."},{"sentence":"Nagsilbi siyang **tulay** upang magkaayos ang magkaaway na pamilya.","translation":"He served as a **bridge** to reconcile the feuding families."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng mahabang pangaral o payo sa isang tao, kadalasan dahil sa isang pagkakamali o masamang asal.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you come home late and your mom is waiting for you by the door with her arms crossed. It's a one-way TED talk about your life choices, sponsored by her disappointment. The classic "Hindi kita pinalaki nang ganyan!" moment.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation of being scolded or nagged at length.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **sermunan** na parang bata ako!","translation":"Don't **lecture** me as if I'm a child!"},{"sentence":"Sinermunan siya ng kanyang boss dahil laging huli sa trabaho.","translation":"His boss **lectured** him for always being late to work."}]

translation: to enthrone; to install in a position of power
meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong ekspresyon na nangangahulugang pag-upo o pagtatalaga sa isang tao sa isang mataas na posisyon ng kapangyarihan o karangalan, tulad ng isang hari o reyna.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng pandiwang "iluklok" (mula sa "luklok", umupo) at pangngalang "trono" (mula sa Espanyol na 'trono').
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'You've been promoted!' announcement, but for royalty or someone who just won a pageant. 'Iluklok' means to seat someone, and 'trono' is a throne. So literally, 'to seat on the throne.' You use this when a new king takes over, or when Catriona Gray is crowned Miss Universe. Figuratively, it can also mean installing someone into a powerful position, like a new CEO who's about to rule the company. It's got that grand, ceremonial vibe.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pormal at matalinghagang paraan upang ilarawan ang pag-akyat sa kapangyarihan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos ang seremonya, pormal na **iniluklok sa trono** ang bagong reyna.","translation":"After the ceremony, the new queen was formally **enthroned**."},{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang susunod na **iluluklok sa trono** bilang pangulo ng kumpanya?","translation":"Who do you think will be **installed in the seat of power** as the next company president?"}]

translation: to boast to someone; to show off to
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapakita ng kayabangan o pagmamalaki sa isang tao tungkol sa sariling mga ari-arian, kakayahan, o nagawa.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you post your new iPhone, your travel pics from Europe, or your Starbucks planner on social media. It's the verb form of "flexing." You're not just being proud (`ipinagmamalaki`), you're actively showing off *to* someone (`pinagyayabangan`). It's the "Sana all" that you cause, not the one you feel.
usage_notes: The object of this verb is the person being boasted to. To boast *about* something, you'd use 'ipagyabang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagyabangan** ang iyong mga kaibigan sa bago mong kotse.","translation":"Don't **boast to** your friends about your new car."},{"sentence":"Palagi niya akong **pinagyayabangan** tungkol sa kanyang mga mamahaling gamit.","translation":"He always **shows off to** me about his expensive things."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging banal, sagrado, o karapat-dapat sa sukdulang paggalang.
original_explanation: This is the quality that makes something 'off-limits' for jokes or disrespect. It's the vibe of Quiapo Church during Nazareno, the silence during a wedding vow, or even just your lola's prized collection of antiques. It's the 'bawal hawakan, bawal pagtawanan' energy. The pagkasagrado of a thing demands reverence.
usage_notes: The prefix 'pagka-' turns the adjective 'sagrado' into a noun representing its quality or state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat igalang ang **pagkasagrado** ng kasal.","translation":"The **sanctity** of marriage must be respected."},{"sentence":"Pinaniniwalaan ng mga katutubo ang **pagkasagrado** ng bundok na iyon.","translation":"The indigenous people believe in the **sacredness** of that mountain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggala o paglalakad sa iba't ibang lugar nang walang tiyak na patutunguhan o layunin.
etymology: Reduplication of the root 'laboy' with the prefix 'pa-'. The repetition intensifies the meaning of wandering.
original_explanation: This is you on a Saturday with 100 pesos in your pocket, just walking around the mall with no intention of buying anything. Just enjoying the aircon. It's the upgraded version of 'palaboy', emphasizing the continuous, aimless action.
usage_notes: Often used adverbially to describe how someone moves.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maghapon siyang **palabuy-laboy** sa siyudad dahil wala siyang trabaho.","translation":"He was **wandering around aimlessly** in the city all day because he had no job."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang pusa ninyo na **palabuy-laboy** sa kabilang kanto.","translation":"I saw your cat **roaming around** on the other corner."}]

translation: to be scratched, to get scuffed
meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang pagkaroon ng gasgas o galos sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: That "oh no" moment when your new phone slips from your hand and you pray it didn't get scratched. Or when someone with a massive bag scrapes past your car in a tight parking lot. It's the verb form of every car owner's nightmare.
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb, often used in the involuntary sense ("to get scratched").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang bagong sasakyan para hindi **magasgasan**.","translation":"Take care of the new car so it won't **get scratched**."},{"sentence":"Puwedeng **magasgasan** ang sahig kung hihilahin mo ang upuan.","translation":"The floor might **get scratched** if you drag the chair."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno o ang bunga nitong matigas ang balat at nakakain ang laman kapag niluto, karaniwang iniihaw.
original_explanation: The official Christmas-in-the-malls street food. You know 'ber' months are here when you smell that smoky, sweet aroma of roasted kastanyas being sold by a manong with a giant wok. It's the holiday season's version of fishballs.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with the Christmas season in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Amoy Pasko na dahil sa nagtitinda ng **kastanyas** sa labas.","translation":"It smells like Christmas because of the **chestnut** vendor outside."},{"sentence":"Pabili po ng isang supot ng mainit na **kastanyas**.","translation":"Please let me buy one bag of hot **chestnuts**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan ikinukulong ang mga taong nagkasala sa batas o mga bilanggo.
etymology: From the root word 'piit' (confined) + '-an' suffix (denoting a place).
original_explanation: The physical place where you end up if you get caught doing something you shouldn't. Think Bilibid or your local city jail. It's the place where the 'piit' people go.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'bilangguan' and 'kulungan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ang mga nahuling kriminal sa **piitan**.","translation":"The captured criminals were brought to the **prison**."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay sa loob ng **piitan** ay napakahirap.","translation":"Life inside the **jail** is very difficult."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos o serye ng mga kilos na nangangailangan ng kasanayan at pag-iingat, lalo na sa pagpapatakbo ng sasakyan o sa isang estratehiya.
original_explanation: That tricky move you pull to get the last parallel parking spot in Greenbelt. Or, the 'palusot' you make to avoid doing a chore. It's a calculated move, a stratagem. In office politics, a 'maneobra' could be how you subtly get credit for a project. On the road, it's how a jeepney driver cuts across three lanes.
usage_notes: Used for both physical movements (like driving) and strategic actions (like in politics or business).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang delikadong **maneobra** ang ginawa ng bus sa highway.","translation":"The bus made a dangerous **maneuver** on the highway."},{"sentence":"Pang-pulitika lang ang **maneobra** na iyan para makuha ang boto ng masa.","translation":"That is just a political **maneuver** to get the votes of the masses."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aalis, pagkalas, o pagbaklas ng isang bagay mula sa pagkakakabit o pagkakadikit nito.
original_explanation: Ever tried to peel off a price tag in one go but it tears apart? That struggle is 'pagtangtang'. It's removing the campaign sticker from your gate after elections, taking down the Christmas decors in February (or March, no judgment), or detaching yourself from a toxic situationship.
usage_notes: Often used for things that are stuck, posted, or attached. Synonymous with 'pag-alis' or 'pagbaklas' but with a nuance of peeling or unsticking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging mahirap ang **pagtangtang** ng lumang wallpaper sa pader.","translation":"The **act of removing** the old wallpaper from the wall was difficult."},{"sentence":"Sinimulan na ang **pagtangtang** ng mga poster pagkatapos ng eleksyon.","translation":"They have started the **detaching** of posters after the election."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng madahong gulay na mayaman sa iron at bitamina.
original_explanation: Yung paboritong pagkain ni Popeye na nagpapalakas sa kanya. Sa Pinas, madalas itong ihalo sa mga soup o i-stir-fry. Ito 'yung gulay na sinasabi ng nanay mo na kainin mo para tumalino at lumakas ka, pero mas masarap pa rin daw ang kangkong para sa iba.
usage_notes: Madalas ipagkamali sa kangkong (water spinach) o talbos ng kamote, bagaman magkakaiba sila.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng **espinaka** sa kanyang nilutong manok.","translation":"She put **spinach** in the chicken dish she cooked."},{"sentence":"Ang **espinaka** ay masustansyang gulay.","translation":"**Spinach** is a nutritious vegetable."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas na pakiramdam ng pagiging angkop para sa isang partikular na karera o trabaho; isang banal na tawag sa paglilingkod sa Diyos.
original_explanation: This isn't just a job; it's your "calling." Parang 'yung feeling na pinanganak ka talaga para maging teacher, nurse, o... vlogger. It's that deep sense of purpose that makes you say, "This is what I'm meant to do," kahit OT ka pa at pagod na. It's your soul's career path.
usage_notes: Often used in a religious context (a calling to priesthood or religious life) but also for secular professions one is passionate about.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang pagtuturo ay hindi lang trabaho, ito ay isang **bokasyon**.","translation":"For her, teaching is not just a job, it is a **vocation**."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **bokasyon** na maging isang pari.","translation":"He felt the **calling** to become a priest."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakawala o nakalaya mula sa pagkakatali, pagkakakulong, o anumang pagpipigil.
original_explanation: That feeling when you finally log out of a toxic job or relationship. You're free! Parang asong nakawala sa tali, takbo kung saan-saan. That's hilagpos. Freedom!
usage_notes: Often used for animals that have broken their leash or prisoners who have escaped. It implies breaking through a restraint.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hilagpos** na ang kalabaw mula sa pagkakatali nito sa puno.","translation":"The carabao has **broken loose** from being tied to the tree."},{"sentence":"Nagawa niyang maging **hilagpos** mula sa mahigpit na yakap ng kanyang nakaraan.","translation":"She managed to **break free** from the tight embrace of her past."}]

translation: To twist the face; to grimace
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaluktot o pag-iba ng anyo ng mukha, karaniwang dahil sa sakit, hindi pagkagusto, o pagkasuklam sa isang bagay.
etymology: From 'ngiwi', a grimace or twisted mouth.
original_explanation: This is the face you make when you accidentally take a sip of your friend's super-pait na ampalaya juice. It's that "eww" face, the involuntary facial gymnastics that says "Nope, not for me." Parang na-stroke sa asim.
usage_notes: Often used in its conjugated forms like 'umingiwi', 'ngumiwi', or as part of the phrase 'ingiwi ang mukha'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ingiwi** ang mukha niya nang matikman ang maasim na mangga.","translation":"His face **twisted** when he tasted the sour mango."},{"sentence":"Napangiwi siya sa narinig na masamang balita.","translation":"He grimaced at the bad news he heard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain o salita na nagpapakita ng matinding kawalan ng paggalang, lalo na sa mga bagay na itinuturing na sagrado, sa kapwa, o sa mga nakatatanda.
etymology: From 'lapastangan' (disrespectful) with the 'ka-...-an' circumfix, creating a noun for the state or act of being disrespectful.
original_explanation: This is disrespect level 1000. It's not just being rude; it's being offensive on a deep level. It's like calling your lola by her first name, questioning the boss's decision in front of the whole team with a sarcastic tone, or making a meme out of a sacred image. It's the kind of action that earns you a flying tsinelas or a one-way ticket to the HR office.
usage_notes: A very strong word used for serious offenses against respect, authority, or religion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuring niyang isang **kalapastanganan** ang pagtawa sa loob ng simbahan.","translation":"He considered laughing inside the church an act of **blasphemy**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagsagot nang pabalang sa magulang ay isang uri ng **kalapastanganan**.","translation":"Answering back rudely to a parent is a form of **insolence**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpulupot o pagbilo ng sinulid, kawad, o anumang mahabang bagay sa isang karete o bilog na sisidlan.
original_explanation: Before Netflix and chill, there was... this. It's what lola does with her sewing thread or what you do to your earphones when you're trying to be neat but they end up tangled anyway. "Tulungan mo si Lola na mag-ikid ng sinulid para sa kanyang pananahi."
usage_notes: Often used in the context of sewing, fishing (winding a line), or managing cables.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **mag-ikid** ng sinulid para sa makina.","translation":"I need **to wind** the thread for the machine."},{"sentence":"Mahusay siyang **mag-ikid** ng pamingwit.","translation":"He is good at **winding** a fishing line."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang butong bumubuo sa ibabang bahagi ng mukha na kinakapitan ng mga ngipin; ang panga.
original_explanation: It's your jawline. That thing people get fillers for to achieve that "V-shape" look. Also, what drops when you see your ex's glow-up transformation. "Nalaglag ang pangahan ko."
usage_notes: Refers to the jaw area or the jawbone itself. Often used to describe the shape or structure of the lower face.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matipuno ang kanyang **pangahan** kaya bagay sa kanya ang maikling buhok.","translation":"He has a strong **jawline** so short hair suits him."},{"sentence":"Sumakit ang **pangahan** ko sa katatawa sa mga biro niya.","translation":"My **jaw** hurts from laughing so much at his jokes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-uulat o paghahatid ng mga impormasyon, pangyayari, o kaganapan sa publiko, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng media tulad ng telebisyon, radyo, o pahayagan.
original_explanation: This is the official job of Noli de Castro and the unofficial job of your neighborhood Marites. One gets paid to deliver facts on TV Patrol, the other does it for free over the bakod. Both involve spreading information, but only one will probably get you sued for libel. It's the OG "spilling the tea," but for current events.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tumpak na **pagbabalita** upang malaman ng tao ang katotohanan.","translation":"Accurate **reporting** is important so that people know the truth."},{"sentence":"Nagsasanay si Ana para sa pampaaralang patimpalak sa **pagbabalita**.","translation":"Ana is training for the school's **newscasting** competition."}]

translation: to resent something; to hold a grudge over something
meaning_filipino: Damdamin ng sama ng loob, pagkadismaya, o galit dahil sa isang ginawa o sinabi ng iba na itinuturing na kawalan ng katarungan o pagpapahalaga.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for "sama ng loob." It's that silent, simmering feeling you get when someone does you wrong and you can't just let it go. It's the "seen-zone" sa chat, 'yung 'di ka pinansin sa party, 'yung credit-grabbing sa office. "Huwag mo nang ipaghinanakit 'yan, masasayang lang ang energy mo."
usage_notes: The object of this verb is the cause of the resentment. It's a deep, often prolonged feeling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal niyang **ipinaghinanakit** ang hindi pag-imbita sa kanya sa kasal.","translation":"For a long time, she **resented** not being invited to the wedding."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ipaghinanakit** sa akin ang desisyon ng manager.","translation":"Don't **hold it against** me for the manager's decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang nararanasan sa pamamagitan ng pandamdam, pisikal man o emosyonal.
etymology: From "dama" (to feel) with infix "-in-" and prefix "na-" which forms "nadarama" in the present tense (contemplated form of "maramdaman").
original_explanation: Ito 'yung kilig na nadarama mo kapag nag-reply si crush, o 'yung inis na nadarama mo sa mabagal na internet. It's the internal weather report of your soul. Puwede ring 'yung sakit ng likod na nadarama mo after magbuhat ng mabigat.
usage_notes: Often used for emotions, but can also describe physical sensations. It is the present tense of 'maramdaman'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaking tuwa ang aking **nadarama** sa iyong pagdating.","translation":"I **am feeling** great joy at your arrival."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko maipaliwanag ang lungkot na **nadarama** ko ngayon.","translation":"I can't explain the sadness that I **am feeling** right now."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babae na may kilos o gawi na malandi, mapang-akit, o nagpapakita ng labis na pagpapacute.
original_explanation: Before 'lumandi' became the go-to term, there was 'kire'. It’s that old-school, Maria Clara-esque way of being flirtatious—subtle smiles, playful hair flips, and a certain pa-demure effect. Today, it might be seen as cringey or cute, depending on who's doing it. Think of it as the analog version of sliding into DMs.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin na may bahagyang negatibo o mapanghusgang konotasyon. Halos eksklusibong ginagamit upang ilarawan ang mga kababaihan. Ang mas moderno at karaniwang kasingkahulugan nito ay 'malandi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo nga 'yang pagiging **kire** mo, hindi bagay sa iyo.","translation":"Stop your **flirtatious** behavior, it doesn't suit you."},{"sentence":"Napansin ng lahat ang mga **kire** niyang tingin sa bago nilang kaklase.","translation":"Everyone noticed her **coquettish** glances at their new classmate."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng kapangyarihan, posisyon, o personal na katangian upang baguhin o hubugin ang pag-iisip, desisyon, o kilos ng isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa 'impluwensiya', na mula sa Espanyol na 'influencia'.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa ng mga 'influencer' sa TikTok para bilhin mo yung 'budol' nila. O yung kaibigan mong kinukumbinsi kang mag-order pa ng isang round ng milk tea. 'Huwag kang magpapa-impluwensiyahan sa kanila!' sigaw ng nanay mo, pero na-add to cart mo na.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwa (verb). Ang pangngalan (noun) ay 'impluwensiya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **impluwensiyahan** ang desisyon ng mga hurado.","translation":"He tried **to influence** the decision of the judges."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **impluwensiyahan** ng masamang barkada ang iyong pag-aaral.","translation":"Don't let a bad group of friends **influence** your studies."}]

meaning_filipino: Sangay ng agham panlipunan na nag-aaral sa teorya at praktika ng politika, paglalarawan at pagsusuri ng mga sistema at kilos pampulitika.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung course sa college kung saan pinag-aaralan mo kung bakit laging nag-aaway-away ang mga politiko. Dito mo malalaman ang history ng gobyerno, mga batas, at kung bakit ang "trapo" ay hindi lang basahan. Perfect 'to para sa mga gustong maging a-woke-ned citizen o sa mga future Marites na gusto ng facts bago mag-comment sa FB.
usage_notes: Often used in academic and political discourse. The term 'agham pampulitika' is also used and is considered more formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng kursong **agham politiko** sa unibersidad.","translation":"She took up **political science** in the university."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-aaral ng **agham politiko** ay mahalaga upang maintindihan ang sistema ng gobyerno.","translation":"Studying **political science** is important to understand the system of government."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging yupi o pipi dahil sa pagkakapukpok o pagkakadiin.
original_explanation: What happens to a can of Coke after you run it over with a car. Or what your garlic looks like after you smash it with the side of a knife. "Pitpit na 'yung lata, itapon mo na 'yan." It's not just bent, it's completely flattened, like your hopes and dreams after seeing your electricity bill.
usage_notes: Often describes something that has been deliberately or accidentally hammered or pressed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang bawang na **pitpit** para sa ginisa.","translation":"She used the **flattened** garlic for the sauté."},{"sentence":"Naging **pitpit** ang bubong ng kotse matapos mabagsakan ng puno.","translation":"The car's roof became **flattened** after a tree fell on it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng mga alituntunin at regulasyon na ipinapatupad sa pamamagitan ng mga institusyong panlipunan upang pamahalaan ang kilos ng mga tao.
original_explanation: The official rules of the game of life. It’s what politicians make, lawyers argue about, and what your mom enforces at home ("Batas dito sa bahay, bawal lumabas 'pag gabi!"). It’s the reason you can’t just park anywhere and why "bawal umihi dito" is a legally binding contract with a wall.
usage_notes: A fundamental word in legal, political, and social contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit na ipinapatupad ang **batas** trapiko sa lungsod.","translation":"Traffic **laws** are strictly enforced in the city."},{"sentence":"Walang sinuman ang mas mataas sa **batas**.","translation":"No one is above the **law**."}]

translation: to be able to illuminate; to be able to light up
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagbibigay ng ilaw sa isang lugar o bagay upang ito ay magliwanag o makita.
original_explanation: When Meralco finally fixes the power outage in your area. Or when you finally install that ring light for your TikTok videos and your face is perfectly lit. Figuratively, it's about shedding light on an issue, like when a whistleblower helps to 'mailawan' the corruption in an office.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical light or figuratively for understanding or exposure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **mailawan** na ang madilim na kalsadang ito para iwas-disgrasya.","translation":"I hope this dark street can finally **be lit up** to avoid accidents."},{"sentence":"Umaasa kaming **mailawan** ng imbestigasyon ang katotohanan sa likod ng kaso.","translation":"We are hoping that the investigation will be **able to illuminate** the truth behind the case."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong pagtatalo o hindi pagkakasundo tungkol sa isang bagay na may magkasalungat na opinyon.
original_explanation: Yung issue na pinag-uusapan ng lahat, from your kapitbahay na chismosa to the hosts of a morning show. It's the 'tea' that everyone's sipping, often involving a celebrity, a politician, or a new 'woke' commercial. Example: 'May bagong kontrobersya na naman si celebrity X!'
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa media, pulitika, at pormal na talakayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong batas ay nagdulot ng malaking **kontrobersya** sa bansa.","translation":"The new law caused a huge **controversy** in the country."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **kontrobersya** ang buhay ng sikat na vlogger.","translation":"The famous vlogger's life is full of **controversy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbabalik sa isipan ng isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari mula sa nakaraan sa kasalukuyang sandali. Ito ay ang patuloy na proseso ng paggunita.
etymology: From na- (actor-focus verb prefix, present tense) + reduplication of the first syllable 'a' + alala (memory, remember).
original_explanation: This is the present tense of remembering. It's that feeling when a song plays and suddenly you're back in 2015, or when you smell something that reminds you of your ex. "Uy, naaalala ko pa yung amoy ng pabango niya." It's the active process, the "currently loading..." screen of your memory.
usage_notes: This is the present tense form. 'Naalala' is the past tense. 'Maaalala' is the future tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naaalala** ko ang mga araw na simple lang ang buhay.","translation":"I **am remembering** the days when life was simple."},{"sentence":"Habang nakatingin sa dagat, **naaalala** niya ang kanilang mga pangako.","translation":"While looking at the sea, he/she **is remembering** their promises."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang genre ng musika na nagmula sa Timog Korea, kilala sa malawak na pagkakaiba-iba ng mga elemento ng audiovisual.
etymology: From English 'K-pop', a shortening of 'Korean pop'.
original_explanation: The reason your pamangkin is broke but happy. It's the black hole of music, dance, and visuals that will suck you in with perfectly synchronized choreography and ridiculously good-looking idols. Once you know your bias, there's no turning back. You'll be buying albums, lightsticks, and photocards like it's your job. Annyeonghaseyo!
usage_notes: A globally recognized term that has been fully adopted into Tagalog conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumastos siya ng malaki para sa concert ticket ng paborito niyang **Kpop** group.","translation":"She spent a lot on a concert ticket for her favorite **K-pop** group."}]

translation: Filipina; a female citizen of the Philippines
meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng mamamayan ng Republika ng Pilipinas.
etymology: From `Las Islas Filipinas`, named after King Philip II of Spain. The 'P' is used instead of 'F' based on the traditional Abakada alphabet.
original_explanation: More than just a label, she's the embodiment of 'Laban!'. Whether she's a CEO in Makati, a nurse in Dubai, a lola cooking adobo, or a BPO agent on the night shift, a Pilipina is known for her resilience, resourcefulness, and a smile that can disarm anyone. The modern spelling is 'Filipina'.
usage_notes: The modern and official spelling is 'Filipina', reflecting the updated Filipino alphabet which includes the letter 'F'. However, 'Pilipina' remains widely used and understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang karangalan ang maging isang **Pilipina**.","translation":"It is an honor to be a **Filipina**."},{"sentence":"Ang nanay ko ay isang matapang at masipag na **Pilipina**.","translation":"My mother is a brave and hardworking **Filipina**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi o piraso na mula sa isang kabuuan; ang bahaging nauukol sa isang tao.
original_explanation: Your slice of the pie. Whether it's your 'ambag' for the team lunch pizza or your share of the family inheritance ('mana'), that's your kaparte. It's the 'Hingi ako!' part of life.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of dividing something, like food, money, or property.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kunin mo na ang **kaparte** mo sa pagkain.","translation":"Go get your **share** of the food."},{"sentence":"Bawat isa sa atin ay may **kaparte** sa tagumpay ng grupo.","translation":"Each one of us has a **part** in the group's success."}]

translation: to take root; to grow roots
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtubo o paglago ng ugat ng isang halaman. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ang pagiging malalim o matatag ng isang bagay o ideya.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what plants do to get their life together. Figuratively, it's what happens to a problem you ignore, a chismis that spreads, or a feeling you can't shake off. 'Nag-ugat na ang galit niya sa'yo.' It's deep, it's established, and it's hard to pull out.
usage_notes: Mayroon itong literal (botanika) at isang napakakaraniwang patalinghagang kahulugan (emosyon, problema, tradisyon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **mag-ugat** muna ang bagong tanim bago mo ilipat ng paso.","translation":"Let the new plant **take root** first before you transfer it to another pot."},{"sentence":"Malalim nang **nag-ugat** ang korapsyon sa sistemang iyan.","translation":"Corruption has already **taken deep root** in that system."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng luntiang gulay na pahaba ang hugis, malutong, at matubig, na karaniwang kinakain nang hilaw sa mga ensalada o bilang pampapresko.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino summer sidekick. You'll find it sliced thinly with vinegar as a side for fried fish, chopped up in your palamig, or even placed over your eyes after a long day of staring at spreadsheets (or chismis on Facebook). It’s the chillest vegetable in the palengke, literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: Ang salitang 'pipino' ay isa ring karaniwang baryasyon sa pagbaybay at pagbigkas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghiwa siya ng **pepino** para sa ensalada.","translation":"She sliced a **cucumber** for the salad."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang inihaw na isda na may sawsawan at hiwa ng **pepino**.","translation":"Grilled fish is delicious with dipping sauce and slices of **cucumber**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang madala o maanod, pisikal man o sa damdamin.
original_explanation: Two meanings here. 1) When you're scrolling on TikTok and suddenly it's 3 AM. Napadala ka sa scroll. 2) When your friend starts crying about their ex and you start crying too, even if you're single. Napadala ka sa emotions. It's being swept up by the current, whether it's a river, a feeling, or your social media feed.
usage_notes: Can refer to being physically carried by a current (e.g., in a river) or being emotionally carried away.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **mapadala** sa emosyon mo; isipin mo muna nang mabuti.","translation":"Don't **get** too **carried away** by your emotions; think about it carefully first."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangunahing silid sa isang bahay na karaniwang ginagamit para sa pagtanggap ng mga bisita at paglilibang ng pamilya.
original_explanation: The room where you make your guests wait, where the plastic-covered sofa is, and where the giant wooden spoon and fork are displayed on the wall. It's the family's official showroom, kept pristine for visitors.
usage_notes: The stress is on the first syllable /SA-la/ to differentiate it from 'salà' (fault/sin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanonood kami ng teleserye sa **sala** tuwing gabi.","translation":"We watch TV series in the **living room** every night."},{"sentence":"Pakilinis ang **sala** dahil may darating na bisita mamaya.","translation":"Please clean the **living room** because guests are arriving later."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng opisyal na paglilista o pagrerehistro ng isang pangalan, impormasyon, o kaganapan sa isang talaan.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative prefix) + tala (list, record).
original_explanation: Ah, the joys of bureaucracy! This is the act of getting something officially listed. Think of lining up for voter's registration, enrolling for the next semester ('enlistment season is war!'), or registering your new business. It's the process of putting your name on 'the list.'
usage_notes: Distinct from 'pagtatala' (the act of recording/listing). 'Pagpapatala' is the act of having something or someone registered/listed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas ang huling araw ng **pagpapatala** para sa mga bagong botante.","translation":"Tomorrow is the last day of **registration** for new voters."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapatala** ng mga estudyante ay isinasagawa online.","translation":"The **enrollment** of students is conducted online."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balbal na paraan ng pagbaybay at pagbigkas ng salitang Ingles na "with," na nangangahulugang "kasama."
etymology: From English 'with', shortened and adapted in Filipino text messaging and internet slang.
original_explanation: This is the jeje/text-speak/internet shortcut for 'with'. Why type four letters when you can type three? 'Sama ka wit me?' is peak efficiency (or laziness, depending on who you ask). It's the 'u' to 'you' and 'd' to 'the' of prepositions.
usage_notes: Highly informal. Used primarily in chat, text messages, and social media comments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"G ka ba lumabas mamaya **wit** da barkada?","translation":"Are you G to go out later **with** the friends?"},{"sentence":"Pumunta ako sa mall **wit** my mom.","translation":"I went to the mall **with** my mom."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pinakamalayong lugar o punto; nasa sukdulang distansya.
etymology: Reduplication of the root "layo" with affixes, emphasizing the distance.
original_explanation: This isn't just "malayo." This is "malayong-malayo." This is the province your relatives live in that takes three bus rides and a tricycle to get to. It's the "nasa kabilang dulo ng mundo" kind of far. It's the superlative form of "layo," for when you really want to emphasize the epic journey.
usage_notes: An emphatic adjective used to describe the farthest point or place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagmula pa siya sa **kalayu-layuang** probinsya para lang makapag-aral sa Maynila.","translation":"He came from a **very far** province just to study in Manila."}]

translation: to invite each other; to call on one another (reciprocal)
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o magkakasunod na pag-aanyaya ng mga tao sa isa't isa upang sumama sa isang gawain o patutunguhan.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for "Tara, G!" (Let's go!). It's when the whole barkada spontaneously decides to go for milk tea or an unli-wings dinner. One person suggests it, then everyone else chimes in, "Sama ako!" That's magyakagan. It's the spirit of `bayanihan` but for road trips and food crawls.
usage_notes: This is a reciprocal verb, meaning the action is done by the subjects to each other. It's always plural.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagyakagan** ang magkakaibigan na manood ng sine pagkatapos ng klase.","translation":"The friends **invited each other** to watch a movie after class."},{"sentence":"Tara, **magyakagan** tayo para sa isang beach trip sa Sabado!","translation":"Come on, let's **all invite each other** for a beach trip on Saturday!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng matinding kahirapan o kawalan ng yaman at mga pangunahing pangangailangan.
original_explanation: This is the 'walang-wala' level of poverty. Hindi lang 'petsa de peligro', kundi buong taon na. It's when your wallet has more cobwebs than the haunted house in a horror movie. The state right before you get your 13th-month pay.
usage_notes: A formal and literary term for extreme poverty. 'Kahirapan' is the more common, everyday term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagdaralita** ay isang malaking hamon na kinakaharap ng maraming pamilya.","translation":"**Destitution** is a great challenge faced by many families."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding **pagdaralita**, napilitan siyang mangibang-bansa.","translation":"Because of extreme **poverty**, he was forced to work abroad."}]

translation: to send someone on an errand
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos sa isang tao na pumunta sa isang lugar upang maghatid o kumuha ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The classic 'pabili' culture in verb form. This is what your nanay does when she suddenly remembers she needs garlic in the middle of cooking adobo. You, the 'utusan', are the chosen one. It's the act of delegating a quick mission, usually to the youngest sibling, for which the reward is 'thank you' (if you're lucky).
usage_notes: The subject of the verb is the one giving the order, not the one doing the errand.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magpapasugo** ako kay bunso sa tindahan para bumili ng yelo.","translation":"I will **send** the youngest **on an errand** to the store to buy ice."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang laging **magpasugo** sa akin, may ginagawa rin ako.","translation":"Don't always **send me on errands**, I'm also doing something."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalis ng sariling kahalagahan, pagpapakita ng kababaang-loob, at pagiging mapagkumbaba sa harap ng iba.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + papaka- (intensive prefix) + baba (low). Literally 'the act of making oneself low'.
original_explanation: This is your 'sana all' moment when a VIP lines up for street food just like everyone else. It's the opposite of being a 'feeling close' alta. It’s showing you’re grounded, even if your bank account is in the stratosphere. It's the conscious act of not flexing.
usage_notes: Often associated with religious or moral virtue. Distinct from 'kababaang-loob' which is the state of being humble, 'pagpapakababa' is the *act* of humbling oneself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapakababa** ng isang lider ay hinahangaan ng kanyang mga nasasakupan.","translation":"The **humility** of a leader is admired by their constituents."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng kanyang yaman, kapansin-pansin ang kanyang **pagpapakababa**.","translation":"Despite his wealth, his **act of humbling himself** is noticeable."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng palma (Corypha elata) na may malalapad na dahon na ginagamit sa paggawa ng mga banig, sombrero, at iba pang kagamitan.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung OG source material for your favorite bayong from the palengke or 'yung sombrero na pang-beach. The buli palm is the provider of all things woven and wonderfully native. It's the plant behind the "Baguio" hat you bought in Boracay.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the Corypha elata palm tree and its products.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang aming bayan sa paggawa ng mga produktong yari sa **buli**.","translation":"Our town is known for making products made from the **buri palm**."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng banig na gawa sa dahon ng **buli**.","translation":"She bought a mat made from **buri palm** leaves."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na may balbula para kontrolin ang pagdaloy ng likido, karaniwan ay tubig, mula sa isang tubo.
original_explanation: The OG source of your problems when it won't stop dripping, and the source of life when you're dying of thirst. It's that thing you turn to get water for your morning coffee or to wash your hands after touching something questionable sa palengke. Don't forget to close it properly, or your water bill will give you a heart attack.
usage_notes: The standard term for a water faucet in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisara nang mahigpit ang **gripo** para hindi masayang ang tubig.","translation":"Please close the **faucet** tightly so water isn't wasted."},{"sentence":"Tumutulo na naman ang **gripo** sa banyo.","translation":"The **faucet** in the bathroom is dripping again."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagyakap o pagbibigay ng yakap sa isang tao o bagay. Ito ay nasa pangkasalukuyang anyo (present tense).
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na 'akap' (hug) at panlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your bestie after a long time, or when your mom comforts you after a major 'sana all' moment. It's the act of giving a hug, happening right now. It's the physical manifestation of 'I'm here for you, besh.'
usage_notes: Anyong pangkasalukuyan ng pandiwang 'umakap'. Ang katumbas na anyo nito na may gitlaping '-in-' ay 'yinayakap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **umaakap** sa kanyang ina nang mahigpit.","translation":"She is **hugging** her mother tightly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakumbabang-lubha, kadalasang sa paraang gumagapang o lumuluhod, upang humingi ng pabor o kapatawaran.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'pabida' move for forgiveness, but not in a good way. It's the physical manifestation of 'sige na, please,' when you've messed up big time. Think of a telenovela character begging on their knees in the rain.
usage_notes: A very descriptive and somewhat archaic word that implies a pathetic or desperate form of begging or showing submission.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang **pagduhapang** ng tauhan sa harap ng kanilang amo para hindi matanggal sa trabaho.","translation":"He saw the employee's **groveling** in front of their boss so as not to be fired."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagduhapang** ay tanda ng matinding pagsisisi.","translation":"His **groveling** was a sign of intense regret."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi wasto o naaayon sa katotohanan, pamantayan, o katwiran.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'di-' (hindi) at salitang-ugat na 'tama' (wasto).
original_explanation: When you submitted your report and your boss just replies with "K." You know something's 'di-tama'. It's that feeling when your gut tells you the chismis from your kapitbahay is 10% true and 90% imagination.
usage_notes: Can also be written as "di tama" or "hindi tama". The hyphenated form is common in informal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-tama** ang sagot mo sa ika-limang tanong.","translation":"Your answer to the fifth question is **incorrect**."},{"sentence":"May pakiramdam akong **di-tama** ang ginagawa natin.","translation":"I have a feeling that what we're doing is **wrong**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging marumi, marungis, o kawalan ng kalinisan, lalo na sa moral o espirituwal na aspeto.
etymology: From ka- (state/quality prefix) + dungis (smudge, dirt) + -an (state suffix).
original_explanation: This isn't just about physical dirt, like putik on your shoes. This is the 'stain on your soul' kind of dirty. It’s the opposite of a clean conscience; it’s a reputation that needs more than just Tide to clean.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in a figurative or moral sense to mean impurity, defilement, or a stained reputation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang linisin ang **karungisan** sa kanyang pangalan.","translation":"He wants to clear the **stain** on his name."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtataksil ay nag-iwan ng **karungisan** sa kanilang pagkakaibigan.","translation":"The betrayal left an **impurity** in their friendship."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lupa na malagkit kapag nabasa at tumitigas kapag natuyo, karaniwang ginagamit sa paggawa ng palayok at iba pang seramika.
original_explanation: Basically, mud's more artistic cousin. It's the stuff potters use to make *palayok* or what kids play with to make a mess. Think of that scene in 'Ghost', but probably with more carabao wandering nearby. It's the OG Play-Doh of the provinces.
usage_notes: Also spelled as 'luwad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paggawa ng palayok mula sa **luad** ay isang sinaunang sining.","translation":"Making pots from **clay** is an ancient art."},{"sentence":"Naging madulas ang daan dahil sa basang **luad**.","translation":"The path became slippery because of the wet **clay**."}]

translation: to request something for someone; to plead for something
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling o pagsamo para sa isang bagay o pabor, kadalasan sa ngalan ng iba o para sa isang partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: This is the verb for when you need a *really* big favor. You don't just ask (hingin), you *plead*. "**Ipakiusap** mo naman ako sa boss mo na bigyan ako ng isa pang chance." It's activating your full-on persuasive, pabebe, or desperate mode to get something done through someone else.
usage_notes: The prefix 'ipaki-' adds a layer of politeness and pleading to the request. It's asking someone to make a request on your behalf, or to intercede.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **ipakiusap** sa guro na payagan akong magpasa ng proyekto bukas?","translation":"Can you please **request** from the teacher that they allow me to submit my project tomorrow?"}]

translation: can be moved; is being transferred
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang ilagay o ilipat ang isang bagay, tao, o konsepto mula sa isang lugar, oras, o kalagayan patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: Like when your boss says the deadline naililipat to next week—hallelujah! Or when your flight gets rescheduled. The phrase 'naililipat ang petsa' (the date can be moved) is a classic for event organizers and procrastinators. It's the verb of flexibility and sometimes, of endless waiting. 'Bes, 'yung kasal naililipat, pero 'yung feelings hindi.'
usage_notes: The 'na-' prefix indicates ability, while the '-ili-' infix denotes the ongoing or progressive aspect of a passive action. It means something *can be* or *is being* moved/transferred.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabuti na lang at **naililipat ang petsa** ng ating pagpupulong.","translation":"It's a good thing the date of our meeting **can be moved**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga upuan ay hindi **naililipat** dahil nakapako sa sahig.","translation":"The chairs **cannot be moved** because they are nailed to the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng panghihina ng katawan o kawalan ng sigla at enerhiya.
original_explanation: This is that 'low-batt' feeling. You know, Monday mornings before coffee? Or that afternoon slump after a heavy lunch? That's 'nananamlay'. It's when you have zero energy to do anything, and all you want to do is lie down and stare at the ceiling. Plants can also be 'nananamlay' when they're not watered. Basically, it's the official mood of 'ayoko na, pagod na 'ko.'
