usage_notes: Often used with 'ka-' to form 'kaumpok' (someone in the same group). The verb form is 'nag-uumpukan' (people are huddling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May isang **umpok** ng mga estudyante sa ilalim ng puno.","translation":"There's a **group** of students under the tree."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong gumawa ng **umpok** diyan sa pasilyo, nakaharang kayo.","translation":"Don't form a **huddle** there in the hallway, you're blocking the way."}]

translation: to allow oneself to be punched
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling o pagpapahintulot sa sarili na suntukin ng iba, karaniwang bilang pag-amin sa pagkakamali.
original_explanation: This is what you say when you've messed up so badly, you feel you deserve a punch. "Friend, I forgot our anniversary, *pasuntok* na lang ako." It's a dramatic, half-joking, half-serious way to show remorse. It's the ultimate "I volunteer as tribute" but for a physical (and usually not literal) consequence.
usage_notes: Almost always used hyperbolically to express guilt or frustration with oneself. It's rarely a literal request.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pare, nagkamali ako, sige na, **pasuntok** na lang ako.","translation":"Bro, I messed up, go ahead, I'll **let you punch me**."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang inis ko sa sarili ko, parang gusto kong **pasuntok**.","translation":"I'm so annoyed with myself, I feel like I want to **get punched**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng sama ng loob, pagdaramdam, o pagtatampo sa isang tao o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: When you see your ex with their new partner and they look happy, tapos bigla kang nakaramdam ng kirot? 'Yan 'yung mabigat ang loob. It's that heavy feeling in your chest from resentment, disappointment, or a grudge you can't seem to let go of. It's the emotional equivalent of a traffic jam in your heart.
usage_notes: This is an idiomatic expression. It describes a state of emotional distress, resentment, or holding a grudge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mabigat ang loob** ko sa kanya dahil sa kanyang mga sinabi.","translation":"I **feel heavy-hearted** towards him because of the things he said."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magtanim ng sama ng loob para hindi maging **mabigat ang loob** mo.","translation":"Don't harbor ill feelings so you won't be **heavy-hearted**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipakita o gamitin ang isang bagay na magara o marangya sa paraan na nakakakuha ng atensyon, kadalasan ay may pagyayabang.
original_explanation: This is the next level of `ipagmagaling`, but for things. It's when your tita from the US comes home and 'casually' uses her new designer bag to carry groceries from the palengke. She's not just using it, she's **flaunting** it. It’s making sure everyone sees your 'gara' or luxury.
usage_notes: Similar to `ipagmagaling` and `ipagyabang`, but specifically refers to flaunting luxurious, fancy, or elegant possessions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binili niya ang mamahaling kotse para lang may **ipagmagara** sa kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He bought the expensive car just to have something to **flaunt** to his friends."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya kailangang **ipagmagara** ang kanyang damit dahil simple lang siyang tao.","translation":"She doesn't need to **flaunt** her clothes because she is a simple person."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa isang natural o hilaw na estado; hindi pa pinino, naproseso, o dumaan sa paghahanda.
original_explanation: Describes something that's raw or unrefined. Like your joke that was a bit too 'green' for the family reunion, a first draft of a report full of errors, or a person's rough manners. It's not yet polished or 'GMRC-approved.'
usage_notes: Used to describe materials, data, or even behavior that is unpolished.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga datos na ibinigay ay **krudo** pa at kailangan pang suriin.","translation":"The data provided is still **raw** and needs further analysis."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino para sa personal na karisma, pang-akit, o ang impresyon na nililikha ng isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
etymology: The exact origin of this usage is debated, but it likely evolved from the idea of the 'impact' or 'impression' someone makes upon arrival.
original_explanation: This is the Pinoy 'rizz' or 'vibe.' When someone has 'dating,' they have a certain charm, sex appeal, or cool factor. 'May dating siya!' (He/She has appeal!). It's not just for people; a place or a song can have 'dating'. It's that intangible quality that makes you look twice. It's the difference between 'meh' and 'wow.'
usage_notes: Highly colloquial. Pronunciation is key: stress on the first syllable /DA-ting/ distinguishes it from /da-TING/ (arrival).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit simple lang ang suot niya, malakas ang **dating** niya.","translation":"Even with simple clothes, he/she has a strong **appeal**."},{"sentence":"Wala kang **dating** sa akin.","translation":"You have no **charm** for me."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpunta o paglalakbay mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba, lalo na sa malalayong distansya.
original_explanation: What your feed is full of after a long weekend. To travel, to go on a trip, to escape the harsh realities of adulting. Synonymous with #Wanderlust. Sometimes it just means commuting through EDSA, which is its own kind of extreme travel.
usage_notes: Can refer to a long vacation or a daily commute. The verb 'bumiyahe' is also very common and interchangeable in many contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magbiyahe** sa buong Pilipinas balang araw.","translation":"I want **to travel** all over the Philippines someday."},{"sentence":"Araw-araw siyang kailangang **magbiyahe** nang dalawang oras papasok sa trabaho.","translation":"Every day she needs **to travel** for two hours to get to work."}]

translation: to make automatic; to become automatic
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa sa isang proseso o kagamitan na gumana nang kusa o may kaunting interbensyon mula sa tao.
original_explanation: This is the goal of every tech bro and life-hacker: to make things happen without lifting a finger. Think automatic replies for 'seen-zoning,' smart homes that turn on the lights for you, or that moment your body just knows how to drive to work even when your brain is half-asleep. It's the verb for 'effortless.'
usage_notes: Still a bit of a neologism or technical jargon, not widely used in everyday conversation but is generally understood, especially in technical fields.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ng engineer na **mag-otomatik** ang buong proseso sa pabrika.","translation":"The engineer wants to **make** the entire factory process **automatic**."},{"sentence":"Kapag laging ginagawa, nag-o-**otomatik** na lang ang kilos ng kamay mo.","translation":"When you do it often, the movement of your hands just **becomes automatic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang pumasok sa estado ng pagtulog.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal after a long day of work, adulting, and overthinking. It's the "ability" you desperately wish for at 3 AM when you're staring at the ceiling, thinking about that one awkward thing you said in 2012. The opposite of puyat.
usage_notes: Very common verb. The negative form 'hindi makatulog' (unable to sleep) is just as common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod ako pero hindi ako **makatulog**.","translation":"I'm so tired but I can't **fall asleep**."},{"sentence":"Uminom ako ng gatas para **makatulog** ako agad.","translation":"I drank milk so I could **get to sleep** quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging mapili o pihikan sa mga bagay, pagkain, o tao.
original_explanation: 'Beggars can't be choosers' is a famous English saying, but in the Philippines, we have a word for the chooser: 'choosy'. It's what your mom calls you when you don't want to eat the ampalaya. It's what your friends call you when you've been single for years because 'walang pumapasa sa standards' mo. Being choosy isn't always bad, but be prepared to be called out on it.
usage_notes: Used exactly like its English counterpart but fully integrated into Taglish conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **choosy** sa pagkain, anak.","translation":"Don't be too **picky** with food, child."},{"sentence":"Kaya siya walang jowa, masyadong **choosy**.","translation":"The reason he/she doesn't have a partner is because they're too **choosy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ibigay ang nararapat na paggalang o pagkilala sa isang tao, bagay, o prinsipyo.
original_explanation: The action verb for not being a 'bastos'. It's what you do when your friend has a different political opinion but you choose to just eat your sisig in peace instead of starting World War 3. 'Respetuhin' mo na lang desisyon niya, kahit deep inside you're judging their life choices. It's the 'agree to disagree' of Filipino verbs.
usage_notes: A transitive verb that requires an object to be respected.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **respetuhin** ang desisyon ng nakararami.","translation":"We must **respect** the decision of the majority."},{"sentence":"**Respetuhin** mo ang kanyang pribadong espasyo.","translation":"**Respect** his/her private space."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasapi ng isang partikular na bansa o komunidad na may kaakibat na mga karapatan at tungkulin.
original_explanation: These are the people who pay taxes, vote (hopefully), and complain about traffic on EDSA. You, me, your tita who shares fake news on Facebook—we're all mamamayan. It's the collective 'we' in 'Hay, Pilipinas.'
usage_notes: Refers to the inhabitants of a country or state, emphasizing their rights and duties.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng bawat **mamamayan** na pangalagaan ang kalikasan.","translation":"It is the duty of every **citizen** to protect the environment."},{"sentence":"Nagtipon ang mga **mamamayan** upang ipahayag ang kanilang mga saloobin.","translation":"The **citizens** gathered to express their sentiments."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilagay sa bulsa; tumutukoy sa bagay, lalo na pera, na kinuha o ninakaw.
original_explanation: Ito yung status ng pera na dapat para sa project, pero hindi na mahanap. Nasaan? Ayun, imbulsado na. It's the past tense and adjective form of the shady act of pocketing funds. The money is now officially 'missing' and chilling in someone's bank account.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa kalagayan ng isang bagay na inilagay sa bulsa, karaniwan sa paraang ilegal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ng pondo ay **imbulsado** na ng tiwaling politiko.","translation":"All the funds have been **pocketed** by the corrupt politician."},{"sentence":"Hindi na maibabalik ang **imbulsado**ng pera.","translation":"The **pocketed** money can no longer be returned."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ugnayan o relasyon ng dalawang taong nagmamahalan; ang panahon ng kanilang pagliligawan o pagiging magkasintahan.
etymology: From `sinta` (love) + `-han` (suffix indicating a reciprocal action or relationship).
original_explanation: This is the noun form of the whole lovey-dovey enterprise. Your 'sintahan' is your romantic relationship. It's the story of how you met, the 'ligaw' stage, the first date, the arguments, and the making up. It's the 'kayo na ba?' stage and everything that comes after. Basically, the plot of your personal rom-com.
usage_notes: Can refer to the period of courtship or the entire romantic relationship. 'Pag-iibigan' is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang kanilang **sintahan** noong sila ay nasa kolehiyo pa lamang.","translation":"Their **romance** began when they were still in college."},{"sentence":"Maraming pagsubok ang pinagdaanan ng kanilang **sintahan**.","translation":"Their **relationship** went through many challenges."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging malakas, masigla, at walang sakit ng isang tao, hayop, o halaman.
etymology: From 'lusog' (health, vigor). The '-um-' infix indicates a verb.
original_explanation: 'Yung glow-up ng katawan mo after mo tigilan ang instant noodles at mag-exercise. From looking like a zombie on a night shift to blooming like you just got your 13th-month pay. Your tita will finally say, "Uy, lumusog ka!" instead of "Ang payat mo!"
usage_notes: Often used to describe a positive change in physical health, including gaining a healthy amount of weight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumusog** ang mga alaga kong halaman mula nang gumamit ako ng abono.","translation":"My pet plants **thrived** ever since I started using fertilizer."},{"sentence":"Simula nang mag-ehersisyo siya araw-araw, kapansin-pansin na **lumusog** ang kanyang katawan.","translation":"Since he started exercising daily, his body has noticeably **become healthier**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pandamdam na ginagamit upang ipahayag ang pagkagulat, pagkaasiwa, o bilang reaksyon sa isang hindi nakakatawang biro o maling akala.
etymology: Expressive, likely a variant of 'nge'. Popularized in the 1990s.
original_explanation: The official sound of a corny joke landing with a thud. It's what your friends say when your 'hugot' line makes no sense, or when you realize you've been talking to a mannequin. It’s the Philippines’ answer to a laugh track for awkward moments.
usage_notes: Very informal and often used humorously to react to something awkward, a failed joke, or a minor mistake.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi niya mahal niya ako... bilang kaibigan. **Ngek**!","translation":"He said he loves me... as a friend. **Oof**!"},{"sentence":"Akala ko wallet ko, panyo lang pala. **Ngek**.","translation":"I thought it was my wallet, it was just a handkerchief. **Oops**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagdadawit sa isang tao o bagay sa isang sitwasyon, usapin, o krimen, kadalasan nang walang pahintulot.
original_explanation: That moment in a group project when one member messes up and suddenly the whole group is in trouble. O kaya sa chismis, 'Huwag mo akong isama diyan!' is the defense against someone trying to `magsangkot` you. It's getting dragged into drama you didn't start.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation, implying being unwillingly involved or dragged into something problematic, like a crime, a scandal, or an argument.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **magsangkot** ng ibang tao sa kanyang personal na problema.","translation":"He doesn't want to **involve** other people in his personal problems."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan siyang **isangkot** sa krimen ngunit wala silang nakitang ebidensya.","translation":"They tried to **implicate** him in the crime but they found no evidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi sinang-ayunan o tinanggap; bumagsak o hindi nakapasa sa isang pagsusulit o kurso.
original_explanation: The status of your leave request filed during peak season. Also, the grade you tried to hide from your parents in high school. The opposite of 'Aprub!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Desaprobado** ang kanyang loan application sa bangko.","translation":"His loan application at the bank was **disapproved**."},{"sentence":"Nalungkot siya nang malamang **desaprobado** siya sa exam.","translation":"He was sad when he found out he **failed** the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pananatili sa isang lugar o pag-asam sa isang pangyayari hanggang sa ito ay dumating o maganap. Ito ay ang nakaraang anyo ng pandiwang "maghintay".
original_explanation: That feeling when you're waiting for your Grab for 20 minutes, tapos biglang na-cancel. Or waiting for that "kumain ka na?" text from your crush na hindi naman darating. You **naghintay** in vain.
usage_notes: Past tense of 'maghintay'. An alternative and more common colloquial form is 'nag-antay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Buong araw siyang **naghintay** sa tawag mo.","translation":"He/She **waited** for your call all day."},{"sentence":"**Naghintay** ako sa pila nang dalawang oras para lang sa milk tea.","translation":"I **waited** in line for two hours just for milk tea."}]

translation: to air out; to dry in the wind/sun
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatuyo o pagbibilad sa hangin o araw, karaniwan ay mga damit, butil, o anumang bagay na basa.
original_explanation: That thing your nanay does to your laundry on a sunny day. It's like giving your clothes a sunbath to get rid of that 'amoy kulob' (musty smell). It's also what you do to rice grains after harvest or to daing na isda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **iyangyang** ang basahan para hindi bumaho.","translation":"You need to **air out** the rag so it doesn't stink."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos anihin, ini**yangyang** muna ang mga palay bago igiik.","translation":"After being harvested, the rice stalks are **aired out** first before being threshed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkampi o pagsuporta sa isang tao, grupo, o pananaw sa isang alitan o diskusyon.
original_explanation: This is what happens when the chismis gets real and you have to choose your fighter. Are you Team A or Team B? Your `pagpanig` is your declaration of allegiance. It's the moment in the family reunion or office drama where your silence is no longer an option, and you have to pick a side, for better or for worse (usually for worse).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging malinaw ang kanyang **pagpanig** sa mga manggagawa sa panahon ng welga.","translation":"His **siding** with the workers became clear during the strike."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang siyentipikong pag-aaral ng wika, kabilang ang ponolohiya, morpolohiya, sintaksis, semantika, at pragmatika.
original_explanation: Ito yung subject na nag-aaral kung bakit may 'bekimon', 'jologs', at 'conyo' speak. Pinag-aaralan dito ang buong sistema ng wika, mula sa tunog ('k' vs 'g'), pagbuo ng salita ('kain' vs 'kumain'), hanggang sa pagbuo ng pangungusap at kahulugan. Basically, the anatomy of chismis.
usage_notes: Ang baybay na 'lingwistika' ay karaniwan ding ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naitulong ng **lingguwistika** sa pag-unawa natin sa sariling wika.","translation":"**Linguistics** has greatly helped in our understanding of our own language."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o gusali na nagsisilbing hintuan o terminal para sa mga pampublikong sasakyan tulad ng tren, bus, o dyip. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa isang himpilan ng pulisya, bumbero, o radyo/telebisyon.
original_explanation: Your designated waiting shed for life's next destination, whether it's the MRT to Taft, the bus to Baguio, or the police station because you forgot your face mask. It's the place where you practice the art of 'siksikan' and master the 'para po' with feelings.
usage_notes: Commonly used for transport hubs (bus station, train station) and official posts (police station, fire station).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghihintay ako sa **estasyon** ng tren para sa biyahe pauwi.","translation":"I am waiting at the train **station** for the trip home."},{"sentence":"Dinala ang suspek sa **estasyon** ng pulis.","translation":"The suspect was brought to the police **station**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pananda sa pagsulat, tulad ng kudlit ('), na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkakaltas ng isang tunog o titik sa isang salita. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa mga markang diakritiko.
original_explanation: The 'tudlik' is that tiny little comma floating in the air, like in "rock 'n' roll" or when you shorten 'at saka' to 'tsaka'. It's the grammar ninja that signals a missing letter. In the age of autocorrect, the humble tudlik is often forgotten, but it's a mark of a true wordsmith.
usage_notes: While 'kudlit' is more common for apostrophe, 'tudlik' is a more technical or literary term. It can also encompass other diacritics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **tudlik** upang ipahiwatig na may nawawalang letra sa salitang 'pagkat'.","translation":"He used an **apostrophe** to indicate that there is a missing letter in the word 'pagkat' (from 'sapagkat')."},{"sentence":"Ang mga markang tulad ng tuldik at **tudlik** ay mahalaga sa tamang pagbigkas.","translation":"Marks like accent marks and **diacritics** are important for correct pronunciation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-urong o paggalaw nang bahagya sa isang tabi upang magbigay ng puwang.
original_explanation: That thing you do in a crowded jeepney when someone says "Pa-usog po." It's the physical manifestation of "giving space," whether you like it or not. It's a small, sideways shuffle that says "Okay, kasya pa isa."
usage_notes: Often used with "pa-" as a command: "pa-isod" (please move aside). Synonymous with 'pag-usog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-isod** ng mga tao sa bangko ay nagbigay ng puwang para sa bagong dating.","translation":"The **scooting over** of the people on the bench made space for the newcomer."},{"sentence":"Isang maliit na **pag-isod** lang ang kailangan para magkasya tayong lahat.","translation":"Just one small **move to the side** is needed for all of us to fit."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pastelerya na may palamang munggo, ube, o baboy, na karaniwang bilog o parisukat at nagmula sa kulturang Tsino-Pilipino.
etymology: From Hokkien Chinese 好餅 (hó-piáⁿ), meaning "good pastry".
original_explanation: That flaky, dice-shaped pastry you buy in Binondo that's filled with either munggo (mung bean) or ube. Also, a classic Filipino slang for being "full of hope" but ultimately getting disappointed. "Pinaasa ka lang, teh. Hopia ka na naman." (You were just led on, sis. You're full of false hope again.)
usage_notes: The word "hopia" is also used metaphorically in slang to mean "false hope" or being led on, a play on the English word "hope".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong bilhin ang **hopia** na may palamang ube.","translation":"My favorite thing to buy is **hopia** with purple yam filling."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang umasa, baka maging **hopia** ka lang sa huli.","translation":"Don't get your hopes up, you might just end up being disappointed in the end."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kakanin na gawa sa pinatuyo at pinaputok na bigas na hinaluan ng arnibal o karamelisadong asukal.
etymology: Mula sa Hokkien na 'ām-phau' ( puffed rice).
original_explanation: That sweet, crunchy, airy snack you loved as a kid. It's like a Rice Krispie treat's Filipino cousin who's a bit more straightforward. Deliciously simple, but disappears in your mouth in seconds, leaving you wanting more.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong pasalubong mula sa probinsya ang matamis na **ampaw**.","translation":"My favorite souvenir from the province is the sweet **puffed rice cake**."},{"sentence":"Madaling mabasag ang **ampaw** kaya dapat maingat ang paghawak dito.","translation":"The **puffed rice cake** breaks easily so you should handle it with care."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sama-samang pagtigil sa paggawa ng mga manggagawa upang ipahayag ang kanilang mga hinaing o hiling sa pamunuan.
original_explanation: This is when the employees have had enough and collectively walk out. It's the ultimate "team building" activity when fighting for better pay, benefits, or just basic human decency from the boss. Think of it as a group chat protest that spilled into the real world.
usage_notes: Often associated with labor unions and activism. The more common term is 'welga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdaos ng **aklasan** ang mga manggagawa sa pabrika dahil sa mababang sahod.","translation":"The factory workers held a **strike** due to low wages."},{"sentence":"Ang planong **aklasan** ay isang karapatan ng mga obrero upang ipaglaban ang kanilang kapakanan.","translation":"The planned **strike** is a right of the laborers to fight for their welfare."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng mga letra, disenyo, o larawan sa isang ibabaw sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng isang istensil o molde.
original_explanation: Like when you were a kid in art class, trying to make your project title look perfect so you grab that plastic sheet with the letters cut out. That's `mag-istensil`. It's the OG way of copy-pasting a design before printers became a thing.
usage_notes: Often used in arts and crafts, sign-making, or even for street art.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mag-istensil** ng pangalan ng tindahan sa pader.","translation":"We need to **stencil** the store's name on the wall."},{"sentence":"**Mag-istensil** tayo ng mga bulaklak sa t-shirt para sa project.","translation":"Let's **stencil** some flowers on the t-shirt for the project."}]

translation: state of being fed up; weariness; ennui
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagdama ng pagkabagot, pagkapagod, o kawalan ng interes sa isang bagay o tao dahil sa labis na pagkakalantad dito.
etymology: From `pagka-` (state of being) + `sawa` (fed up, tired of).
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get after eating adobo for the 7th day in a row. It's that "ayoko na, suko na" vibe towards a person, a job, or even a song you've played on loop too many times. The point where your patience and interest have completely flatlined. It's the spiritual sibling of 'umay'.
usage_notes: Can be applied to food, activities, relationships, and situations. 'Pagkaumay' is a very common, more colloquial synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa araw-araw na traffic, nararamdaman ko na ang **pagkasawa** sa pagmamaneho.","translation":"Because of the daily traffic, I'm already feeling the **weariness** of driving."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkasawa** niya sa dati niyang trabaho ang nag-udyok sa kanya na mag-resign.","translation":"His **being fed up** with his old job prompted him to resign."}]

translation: to throw, to discard, to dispose of
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghahagis, pag-aalis, o pagliligpit ng isang bagay, lalo na kung ito ay hindi na pinahahalagahan o kailangan.
original_explanation: What you do to your ex's memories (or try to, anyway). The verb form of 'letting go,' but for physical objects... and sometimes, feelings. Also a basketball move. 'Nice shot! Galing magtapon ng bola!'
usage_notes: The pronunciation shifts stress to the second syllable (/ta-PON/) when used as a root for verbs like 'itapon' or 'magtapon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itapon** mo na ang resibo, hindi na natin kailangan 'yan.","translation":"**Throw** the receipt away, we don't need it anymore."},{"sentence":"Saan ba pwedeng **magtapon** ng basura dito?","translation":"Where can one **dispose** of trash here?"}]

translation: to hold; to grasp; to manage
meaning_filipino: Ang paghawak o pagdikit ng kamay sa isang bagay; ang pagkakaroon ng kontrol o responsibilidad sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: When you're standing in a jampacked MRT, you need to humawak nang mahigpit sa handrail for dear life. Metaphorically, it's the project manager who humahawak ng account, or your strict parent who humahawak ng pera mo. It's all about control, baby.
usage_notes: Can be literal (to hold with hands) or figurative (to be in charge of, to manage).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humawak** siya sa kamay ng kanyang kasintahan habang nanonood ng sine.","translation":"He **held** his girlfriend's hand while watching a movie."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **humahawak** sa proyektong ito?","translation":"Who is **managing** this project?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglala o pagtindi ng isang sitwasyon, karaniwang sa mas malaki o mas seryosong antas.
original_explanation: Nagsimula lang sa simpleng 'di pagkaintindihan sa chat, tapos biglang umeskala at naging world war sa family GC. Or sa BPO, 'pag 'di mo na kaya kausapin 'yung galit na customer, you say, "I need to escalate this," which means ipapasa mo na sa mas mataas.
usage_notes: Used for situations that become more intense or serious.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na **umeskala** ang simpleng argumento at nauwi sa sigawan.","translation":"The simple argument quickly **escalated** and ended in shouting."},{"sentence":"Ayaw naming **umeskala** pa ang problema kaya kami na ang nagparaya.","translation":"We didn't want the problem **to escalate** further, so we were the ones who gave way."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging hindi tuwid, tabingi, o nakahilig sa isang direksyon.
original_explanation: You know when you hang a picture frame and you step back and your head tilts because it's just a *little* bit off? That's pahiwid. It's that slight, annoying slant. It can also describe a sarcastic or sidelong glance, 'yung tingin na pahiwid, na parang may gusto kang iparating nang hindi nagsasalita.
usage_notes: Can describe a physical object's orientation or a non-verbal expression like a glance or a smile.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **pahiwid** ang pagkakatayo ng poste pagkatapos ng malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The post became **slanted** after the strong typhoon."},{"sentence":"Binigyan niya ako ng isang ngiting **pahiwid**.","translation":"He gave me an **askew** smile."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang mahalay, bastos, o hindi kaaya-aya sa paningin, pandinig, o asal.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `napaka-` (nagpapahiwatig ng sukdulang antas) at salitang ugat na `laswa` (lewdness, obscenity).
original_explanation: This is for things that make your conservative tita gasp and clutch her pearls. The "Rated SPG" stuff you wouldn't dare show your lola. It’s the verbal or visual equivalent of a loud, wet fart in a quiet elevator—totally inappropriate and offensive.
usage_notes: A strong word used to describe actions, words, or images that are considered indecent or morally offensive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinanggal sa ere ang palabas dahil sa mga **napakalaswa** nitong eksena.","translation":"The show was taken off the air because of its **very lewd** scenes."},{"sentence":"Ang mga birong binitiwan niya ay **napakalaswa** at hindi angkop sa okasyon.","translation":"The jokes he made were **very obscene** and not appropriate for the occasion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang seryosong usapin o gawain na may malalaking implikasyon o panganib; mga literal na laro para sa matatanda.
original_explanation: When the 'game' involves feelings, money, or politics. Hindi na ito piko o habulan; ito 'yung tipo ng laro na may kasamang 'we need to talk' or 'basta mayaman, mananalo.' It's when the stakes are high and it's definitely not fun and games anymore.
usage_notes: Madalas may negatibong konotasyon na tumutukoy sa mga kumplikado at mapanganib na sitwasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pulitika ay isang **larong-matanda** na hindi para sa mga mahihina ang loob.","translation":"Politics is a **serious game** not meant for the faint of heart."},{"sentence":"Akala niya biro lang, pero napasok siya sa **larong-matanda** na may kinalaman sa malaking pera.","translation":"He thought it was just a joke, but he got into an **adult's game** involving big money."}]

meaning_filipino: Husto na; sapat na at hindi na kailangang dagdagan pa.
original_explanation: This is the Filipino 'Okay, that's enough.' It's what your mom says when you've put too much rice on your plate ('Sukat na 'yan!'). It's what you say to the jeepney driver when you're paying and want him to stop giving you tiny coins for change. It's the verbal stop sign for quantity.
usage_notes: A common phrase used to indicate sufficiency and to stop an action related to quantity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sukat na** ang kanin na iyan, baka hindi mo maubos.","translation":"That rice is **enough**, you might not be able to finish it."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng karpintero, '**sukat na** ang mga pako na ito.'","translation":"The carpenter said, 'these nails are **sufficient**.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakaliit o hindi gaanong mahalagang kantidad o presyo; barya-barya.
etymology: Combination of 'halaga' (value) and 'balasak' (indiscriminate, of little importance).
original_explanation: That feeling when you check your bank account after a 3-day sale. It's the "pang-yosi lang" or "pambili lang ng Zesto" amount. Basically, it's what's left of your bonus after paying off your Shopee/Lazada cart.
usage_notes: A slightly formal or literary term for a very small amount of money. The modern equivalent might be 'barya lang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinenta niya ang kanyang lumang kotse sa **halagang balasak** dahil kailangan niya ng agarang pera.","translation":"He sold his old car for a **trivial amount** because he needed cash immediately."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw sa pamamagitan ng paggapang sa ibabaw ng isang bagay o lugar.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung relationship niyo, hindi mo alam kung saan papunta, basta gapangan lang nang gapangan sa dilim. Also, this is what babies do before they learn to walk and run away from their responsibilities like we do.
usage_notes: The `-an` suffix indicates a location or object upon which the action of crawling is performed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **gapangan** ng sundalo ang putikan para makalapit sa kalaban.","translation":"The soldier had to **crawl on** the mud to get closer to the enemy."},{"sentence":"Hinayaan niyang **gapangan** siya ng mga langgam habang natutulog sa damuhan.","translation":"He let the ants **crawl on** him while sleeping on the grass."}]

translation: act of pulling out suddenly; act of drawing (a weapon)
meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at biglaang paghila o paghugot sa isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito, tulad ng pagbunot ng sandata o ngipin.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa ng pulis sa action movie bago sabihing "Freeze!". O 'yung ginagawa mo sa wallet mo kapag nakita mo 'yung 50% off sale sign. It's a quick, decisive pull. Pwede ring sa ngipin, 'yung mabilisang hila ng dentista para tapos na agad ang 'sana all' moment mo sa sakit.
usage_notes: Implies a faster, more forceful, and more sudden action than 'pagbunot'. Often used in the context of weapons.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat sa mabilis na **pagbunlot** niya ng baril.","translation":"Everyone was shocked by his quick **drawing** of the gun."},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **pagbunlot** lang ang kailangan para matanggal ang damo.","translation":"Just one strong **pull** is needed to remove the weed."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagtanggi o pagtatwa sa isang tao, karaniwan ay miyembro ng pamilya, o sa isang paniniwala.
original_explanation: The ultimate teleserye plot twist. When the rich haciendero father finds out his daughter is pregnant with the poor farmer's son's child, he screams "Itinatakwil na kita!" (I disown you!). It's the Filipino version of "You're dead to me." Brutal.
usage_notes: A very strong word, indicating a formal and often permanent severing of ties. This is the past tense form of 'itakwil'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itinakwil** ng hari ang kanyang sariling anak dahil sa pagsuway nito.","translation":"The king **disowned** his own child for his disobedience."},{"sentence":"Matapos ang eskandalo, **itinakwil** siya ng kanyang partido.","translation":"After the scandal, he was **renounced** by his party."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng kalawang; ang proseso ng pagkasira ng metal dahil sa oksihenasyon.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what happens to your gate after a month of non-stop rain. Figuratively, it’s what happens to your skills when you haven't used them in a while. Your Tagalog is 'pagkamakalawang' if you've been abroad for too long. Your basketball moves are 'pagkamakalawang' if you've been stuck in the office. It's the state of being out of practice.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for metals and figuratively for skills or abilities that have diminished due to lack of use.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inireklamo niya ang **pagkamakalawang** ng nabili niyang bisikleta.","translation":"He complained about the **rustiness** of the bicycle he bought."},{"sentence":"Pasensya na sa aking **pagkamakalawang** sa pagtugtog ng gitara; matagal na akong hindi nakakapraktis.","translation":"Pardon my **rustiness** in playing the guitar; I haven't practiced in a long time."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isda (Chanos chanos) na kilala sa Pilipinas bilang pambansang isda, na may katangiang maraming maliliit na tinik.
original_explanation: The Philippines' national fish and the final boss of Filipino dining because of its million tiny bones (tinik). Whether it's daing na bangus for breakfast, sinigang na bangus for lunch, or rellenong bangus for a fiesta, this fish is everywhere. The 'boneless' version is a gift from the heavens.
usage_notes: Ang 'bangos' ay isang hindi gaanong karaniwang baryante ng pagbaybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang **bangus** kapag prinito hanggang sa maging malutong ang balat.","translation":"**Milkfish** is delicious when fried until the skin is crispy."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong almusal ay sinangag, itlog, at daing na **bangus**.","translation":"My favorite breakfast is fried rice, egg, and dried marinated **milkfish**."}]

translation: to postpone until tomorrow; to have something done tomorrow
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapaliban ng isang gawain, usapan, o pangyayari para sa susunod na araw.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for procrastination, Filipino style. When your friend asks you to do something today and you reply, "Bukas na lang," you are suggesting to *magpabukas* of the task. It's the "mañana habit" in verb form.
usage_notes: The meaning is dependent on the pronunciation of the root word 'bukas' as /BU-kas/, with stress on the first syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil pagod na ang lahat, napagdesisyunan nilang **magpabukas** na lang ng miting.","translation":"Because everyone was tired, they decided to just **postpone the meeting until tomorrow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawang panig o dako ng isang bagay, lugar, o sitwasyon.
etymology: From 'mag-' (prefix indicating plurality or mutuality) + 'kabila' (the other side).
original_explanation: This is like your situationship status: you're getting mixed signals from 'magkabila,' from both sides. One side says 'I miss you,' the other side leaves you on read. It's the 'both sides' of a story, the 'both ends' of the stick you're getting the short end of, or both sides of the MRT platform during rush hour.
usage_notes: Often used with 'panig' (side) or to describe something happening on two opposite sides. 'Magkabilang' is the adjectival form that modifies a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga tindahan sa **magkabila** ng kalsada.","translation":"There are stores on **both sides** of the road."},{"sentence":"Narinig ang sigawan mula sa **magkabila**.","translation":"Shouting was heard from **each side**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lihim na pakikipagkaisa sa isa o higit pang tao upang isagawa ang isang masamang balak o gawain.
etymology: From makipag- (social verb prefix) + sabwat (conspiracy, collusion).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'group project' but for evil deeds. Think of villains in a teleserye plotting the downfall of the bida, or your officemates secretly planning to leave work early together without the boss knowing. It's teamwork, but make it shady.
usage_notes: Always carries a negative connotation of secrecy and malicious intent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalak nilang **makipagsabwatan** upang pabagsakin ang pamahalaan.","translation":"They planned to **conspire** to overthrow the government."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **makipagsabwatan** sa mga taong may masamang hangarin.","translation":"Do not **collude** with people who have bad intentions."}]

meaning_filipino: Nayapakan at nasira; nagusot o nadurog dahil sa pagtapak.
original_explanation: Imagine a beautiful garden, then a herd of unruly kids runs through it. The flowers are now **linas**. Or the state of your white sneakers after surviving a music festival mosh pit. It's that feeling of being stepped on and flattened, literally. A very dramatic way to describe something that's been trampled underfoot.
usage_notes: Often used in its verb form 'linasin' (to trample) or 'nalinas' (was trampled).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Linas** ang mga halaman sa hardin matapos dumaan ang mga aso.","translation":"The plants in the garden were **trampled** after the dogs ran through."},{"sentence":"Nakita niyang **linas** na ang kanyang mga papeles sa sahig.","translation":"He saw that his papers were already **trampled** on the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng panahon na katumbas ng 60 minuto; takdang panahon para sa isang gawain o kaganapan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'horas', pangmaramihang anyo ng 'hora' na nangangahulugang 'oras'.
original_explanation: The one thing you never have enough of, especially on a Monday morning or when your boss asks you to render OT. It's the reason for "Filipino time" and also the reason why your lola tells you to go home before it gets dark. "Anong oras na?" is the national anthem of impatient people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong **oras** na? Baka mahuli tayo sa klase.","translation":"What **time** is it? We might be late for class."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng isang **oras** para tapusin itong trabaho.","translation":"Give me one **hour** to finish this work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panahong darating; ang mga mangyayari sa susunod na mga araw, buwan, o taon.
etymology: From `harap` (front) with `-in-` infix, literally 'that which is being faced'.
original_explanation: It's that thing your parents are always asking you about ('Anong plano mo sa **hinaharap**?'). It's the reason you're saving money, studying hard, or swiping right on a dating app. It's the sequel to your life that hasn't been written yet.
usage_notes: A common synonym for 'kinabukasan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa ating **hinaharap**, kailangan nating mag-ipon.","translation":"For our **future**, we need to save money."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan niya nang mabuti ang kanyang mga desisyon para sa magandang **hinaharap**.","translation":"She is carefully studying her decisions for a good **future**."}]

translation: to switch sides; to change allegiance
meaning_filipino: Isang idyoma na nangangahulugang paglipat sa kabilang panig, karaniwan sa pulitika o kompetisyon; pagbalimbing.
etymology: An idiom derived from the literal act of swimming across a river or body of water to reach the other side.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'balimbing' move. When a politician suddenly joins the rival party after the elections, *nilangoy niya ang kabila*. It's like switching teams in the middle of a game. In office politics, it's that colleague who suddenly becomes best friends with the new boss and forgets all about you. Shady.
usage_notes: A very common political idiom in the Philippines, synonymous with 'tumawid sa bakod' (to cross the fence).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos ang eleksyon, maraming pulitiko ang inaasahang **languyin ang kabila** at umanib sa partido ng administrasyon.","translation":"After the election, many politicians are expected **to switch sides** and join the administration party."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panahon ng taon na karaniwang mainit at walang gaanong pag-ulan, salungat sa tag-ulan.
original_explanation: 'Yan yung panahon na legit ang excuse mong "ang init!" every five minutes. Season ng halo-halo, beach trips (kahit hanggang drawing lang), at pagtaas ng bill sa kuryente dahil sa aircon. Ito rin ang panahon kung kailan mo mami-miss ang lamig ng Pasko.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa salitang "tag-init," bagaman ang "panag-araw" ay mas tumutukoy sa "dry season" sa pangkalahatan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing **panag-araw**, maraming pamilya ang nagbabakasyon sa mga dalampasigan.","translation":"During the **dry season**, many families vacation at the beaches."},{"sentence":"Inilalabas na nila ang mga bentilador bilang paghahanda sa **panag-araw**.","translation":"They are already taking out the electric fans in preparation for the **dry season**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang artista na nagpapatawa sa pamamagitan ng kakaibang kasuotan, pampakulay sa mukha, at kilos; karaniwang makikita sa sirko o mga pagdiriwang.
original_explanation: Literally a clown, like the one at a kid's birthday party. But more often used to describe someone who's being foolish, making a fool of themselves, or not being taken seriously. "Huwag kang maging payaso" is a warning to get your act together.
usage_notes: Can be literal (circus clown) or figurative (a foolish person).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang trabaho ng **payaso** ay magpasaya ng mga bata.","translation":"The job of a **clown** is to make children happy."},{"sentence":"Tumigil ka sa kakatawa, para kang **payaso**.","translation":"Stop laughing like that, you look like a **clown**."}]

translation: to make one; to unite; to consolidate
meaning_filipino: Pagbuklurin o gawing isa ang dalawa o higit pang bagay; pag-isahin.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you have three separate Word documents for your thesis and you finally combine them into one file. "Isahin mo na 'yang mga files." Or when a leader tries to unite a divided team. It's the act of merging multiple things into a single entity.
usage_notes: Similar to "pag-isahin," but can feel more direct.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **isahin** ang lahat ng sangkap bago ito ilagay sa oven.","translation":"You need to **combine** all the ingredients into **one** before putting it in the oven."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng domestikadong kalabaw (Bubalus bubalis carabanesis) na karaniwang ginagamit sa pagsasaka sa Pilipinas at Timog-Silangang Asya; pambansang hayop ng Pilipinas.
original_explanation: The OG tractor of the Philippines. The hardworking, muscle-bound partner of every magsasaka (farmer). It's the symbol of Filipino strength and perseverance. When someone says you're 'lakas-kalabaw' (strong as a carabao), it's a compliment to your physical strength and endurance, perfect for carrying all those grocery bags in one trip.
usage_notes: The national animal of the Philippines, symbolizing hard work and resilience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinutulungan ng **kalabaw** ang magsasaka sa pag-aararo ng bukid.","translation":"The **carabao** helps the farmer in plowing the field."},{"sentence":"Ang gatas ng **kalabaw** ay ginagawang kesong puti.","translation":"**Carabao's** milk is used to make white cheese."}]

translation: to stop, to cease, to be halted
meaning_filipino: Ang paghinto ng isang kilos, gawain, o pangyayari, na maaaring kusa o dahil sa isang panlabas na dahilan.
original_explanation: 'Yung biglang nag-hang 'yung video call niyo ng jowa mo sa kalagitnaan ng "I love you". Or 'yung moment na matigil 'yung music sa party tapos narinig ng lahat 'yung chismis na binubulong mo. Awkward! It's when something abruptly stops.
usage_notes: Can be used for both voluntary and involuntary stoppage. `Tumigil` is the actor-focus form (to stop oneself), while `matigil` is often object-focus or involuntary (to be stopped, to happen to stop).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **matigil** na ang walang katapusang traffic sa EDSA.","translation":"I hope the endless traffic on EDSA will finally **stop**."},{"sentence":"Biglang **natigil** ang kanilang pag-uusap nang dumating ang guro.","translation":"Their conversation suddenly **stopped** when the teacher arrived."}]

meaning_filipino: May magkaparehong haba o sukat; ginagamit sa pagtutulad ng dalawang bagay na may pantay na haba.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'kasing-' at salitang-ugat na 'haba'.
original_explanation: That feeling when the queue for the ATM is 'kasinghaba ng EDSA traffic on a Friday payday.' Or when your friend's 'kwento' is so long, you swear it's 'kasinghaba' of a K-drama series, seasons 1 to 5.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ang pasensya ko ay **kasinghaba** ng pila sa government office.","translation":"I wish my patience were **as long as** the queue at a government office."},{"sentence":"Ang buhok niya ay **kasinghaba** na ng sa akin.","translation":"Her hair is now **as long as** mine."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng hindi paglapit o pag-iwas sa pakikisalamuha sa iba; pagiging malayo ang loob.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng "di-" (hindi) at "pakikipaglapit" (ang akto ng pagiging malapit o pakikisalamuha).
original_explanation: This is the vibe you get from that new officemate who eats lunch alone and has their headphones on 24/7. It's not necessarily being a snob, but it's definitely building a wall. It's the human version of "Do Not Disturb" mode. The art of social distancing before it was cool.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang pag-uugali o saloobin ng pagiging malayo at hindi pakikipag-ugnayan sa iba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **di-pakikipaglapit** ay madalas na napagkakamalang pagkasuplado.","translation":"His **aloofness** is often mistaken for being a snob."},{"sentence":"May dahilan ang kanyang **di-pakikipaglapit** sa mga katrabaho.","translation":"There is a reason for his **keeping distance** from his colleagues."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapasok ng isang bagay sa isang masikip na espasyo, siwang, o sa loob ng iba pang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your shirt to look formal for a job interview. It's also what you do with your wallet in your back pocket, or how you hide money in a book. 'Magsuksok ka ng pamasahe sa medyas mo para 'di manakaw.' A classic Filipino life hack verb.
usage_notes: Implies putting something into a tight or secure place. Can be used for clothes (tucking in a shirt), money (inserting into a pocket or crevice), or any object being placed into a narrow space.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magsuksok** ng iyong polo kapag naka-uniporme.","translation":"You need to **tuck in** your polo shirt when in uniform."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magsuksok** ng liham sa ilalim ng pinto.","translation":"He tried to **insert** a letter under the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtitipon o pag-iipon ng mga bagay, pondo, o impormasyon sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: What you do with all the chismis from your friends to form the complete story. Also, what your mom does with your allowance money 'for safekeeping.' The verb form is 'likumin' or 'maglikom.'
usage_notes: This is a root word. Common verb forms are 'likumin' (to gather something) and 'maglikom' (to gather).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag**likom** ng pondo ay para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The **collection** of funds is for the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Mabilis ang pag**likom** nila ng mga donasyon.","translation":"Their **gathering** of donations was fast."}]

translation: to lower; to bring down; to drop off
meaning_filipino: Ilipat ang isang bagay mula sa mataas na lugar patungo sa mababang lugar; bawasan ang antas, halaga, o tindi ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you ask the jeepney driver to do: "Manong, ibaba mo na po ako sa kanto." It's also what you do with your standards when you're desperate, or what you wish your boss would do with your workload. It means to bring something down, whether it's a bag of groceries, the price of bilihin, or your pride.
usage_notes: Very common in commuting and everyday instructions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ibaba** mo ang iyong boses, natutulog ang bata.","translation":"**Lower** your voice, the child is sleeping."},{"sentence":"Sana **ibaba** na nila ang presyo ng gasolina.","translation":"I hope they **bring down** the price of gasoline."},{"sentence":"Manong, dito na lang po sa kanto **ibaba**.","translation":"Sir, just **drop me off** here at the corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Akronim para sa "For You Page," ang pangunahing feed sa social media app na TikTok kung saan ipinapakita ang mga video na pinili ng algorithm para sa isang partikular na user.
etymology: Acronym from English "For You Page," popularized by the social media platform TikTok.
original_explanation: Stands for "For You Page." This is TikTok's all-knowing, all-seeing algorithm that decides if you're going to spend the next hour watching cooking hacks, dance challenges, or conspiracy theories. When your video lands on the #fyp, it means you've gone viral, baby! It's the digital equivalent of being the "talk of the town."
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of TikTok and other short-form video platforms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wow, lumabas ka sa **fyp** ko!","translation":"Wow, you showed up on my **fyp**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paninirahan o pagtira sa isang partikular na lugar o bayan.
etymology: From `maN-` (verb prefix, where N assimilates) + `bayan` (town, country). The `b` in `bayan` causes `N` to become `m`.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of being a 'taga-doon'. It’s like setting your home address on Google Maps, but for a whole town or city. Not to be confused with `mamamayan` (the citizen), this is the *action* of being a resident.
usage_notes: A less common verb. The noun `mamamayan` (citizen) is far more frequent. `Manirahan` is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinili niyang **mamayan** sa isang tahimik na probinsya.","translation":"He chose to **reside** in a quiet province."},{"sentence":"Ang mga unang tao na **namayan** sa islang iyon ay mga mangingisda.","translation":"The first people who **dwelled** on that island were fishermen."}]

translation: to tell off, to admonish, to inform
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng payo, babala, o paalala sa isang tao; maaari ring mangahulugan ng pagbibigay ng utos o impormasyon.
original_explanation: That dreaded moment when your boss says, "Papasok ka sa office ko, kailangan kitang **pagsabihan**." It can range from a gentle reminder ("Pagsabihan mo si Jun na may meeting bukas") to a full-blown 'sermon' about your performance. The tone is everything.
usage_notes: Can be neutral (to inform) or negative (to scold/admonish). Context is key. The object of the verb is the person being told.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pagsabihan** ang iyong kapatid na mag-ingat sa daan.","translation":"You need to **inform** your sibling to be careful on the road."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan siya ng kanyang ina dahil sa pag-uwi nang gabi.","translation":"She was **told off** by her mother for coming home late."}]

translation: to be trapped; to be ensnared
meaning_filipino: Mahuli sa isang patibong o bitag; hindi makawala sa isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Can be literal, like a mouse getting caught in a trap. But more often, it's used for life situations. Na-friendzone? Nabitag ka. Stuck in a job you hate because of the benefits? Nabitag ka. Na-budol sa online shopping spree? Nabitag ka sa 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: Used for both literal traps and figurative situations of being stuck.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat ang usa upang hindi ito **mabitag** ng mga mangangaso.","translation":"The deer was careful not to **be trapped** by the hunters."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay **nabitag** siya sa isang relasyong walang patutunguhan.","translation":"She felt **trapped** in a dead-end relationship."}]

translation: fernery; a place where ferns grow
meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan maraming tumutubong halaman na pako (fern).
etymology: Mula sa "pako" (fern) + hulaping "-an" (nagpapahiwatig ng lugar na sagana sa isang bagay).
original_explanation: Imagine a lush, green, shady spot in a forest or a big garden that's just overflowing with ferns. That's a 'pakuan'. It sounds like a place where fairies or diwatas would hang out. It's the plantita/plantito's dream corner.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pangngalan, na hango sa halamang 'pako' (fern), hindi sa kagamitang pako (nail).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglakad-lakad kami sa may **pakuan** sa paanan ng bundok.","translation":"We walked around the **fernery** at the foot of the mountain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paglalarawan sa isang tao na may mataas na tindig ngunit payat ang pangangatawan.
etymology: Pagsasama ng 'matangkad' (tall) at 'patpatin' (skinny, from 'patpat' meaning stick).
original_explanation: The 'human-sized stick figure' build. You've got the height, but your body looks like it's perpetually on a diet. Often followed by a tita asking, 'Anak, hindi ka ba kumakain?' It's the look of many models, or your friend who can eat a whole lechon but never gains a pound.
usage_notes: Isang deskriptibong parirala para sa pangangatawan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong bata ako, ako ay **matangkad at patpatin** kaya madalas akong tuksuhin.","translation":"When I was a child, I was **tall and skinny** so I was often teased."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan kung saan mayroong isang patong ng taba sa ilalim ng baba, na lumilikha ng hitsura ng pangalawang baba.
original_explanation: Ito yung sign na masarap ang handaan nung Pasko at New Year. Yung feature na pilit mong tinatago sa selfie by taking it from a high angle. It's not a flaw, it's proof of a well-fed and happy life... or 'yun ang sinasabi natin sa sarili natin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang kanyang **doble-baba** sa litrato.","translation":"His **double chin** is very visible in the picture."},{"sentence":"Nag-eehersisyo siya para mawala ang kanyang **doble-baba**.","translation":"She is exercising to get rid of her **double chin**."}]

meaning_filipino: Simula sa sandaling ito at magpapatuloy sa hinaharap; mula ngayon.
etymology: Pag-uulit ng salitang 'tuwi' (bawat) kasama ang pang-abay na 'na' (now/already).
original_explanation: This is the phrase you use after a major life realization. Like after a bad breakup, you declare, 'Tuwi-tuwi na, I will choose myself.' Or after getting scammed online, 'Tuwi-tuwi na, 'di na ako magpapa-budol.' It’s a very formal and dramatic 'from now on.'
usage_notes: Carries a strong sense of finality and resolve. It is quite formal and not common in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tuwi-tuwi na** ay mag-iingat ako sa aking mga desisyon.","translation":"**From now on**, I will be careful with my decisions."},{"sentence":"Ipinangako niya na **tuwi-tuwi na** ay hindi na siya magsisinungaling.","translation":"He promised that **henceforth** he will no longer lie."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagpapakita ng katapatan at hindi nagbabago ang paninindigan o suporta.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung mga kaibigan na kahit i-seen mo, hindi ka iiwan. 'Yung loyal sa'yo, hindi sa chismis tungkol sa'yo. Sa isang fandom, sila 'yung hindi aalis kahit mag-disband 'yung grupo. Ang tunay na 'ride or die'.
usage_notes: This word is less common and somewhat formal or poetic. It can be confused with the more literal meaning of 'one who places something in front', but this 'loyalist' meaning is the primary sense in this form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa lahat ng pagsubok, nanatili siyang **tagatapat** sa kanilang samahan.","translation":"Through all the trials, he remained a **loyalist** to their group."},{"sentence":"Ang mga tunay na **tagatapat** ng hari ay hindi sumuko.","translation":"The king's true **faithful followers** did not surrender."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian o gawain na nagdudulot ng hirap, pasakit, o pagdurusa sa iba, sa paraang sinasadya man o hindi.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (pagkahilig), unlaping pangkabisa `pa-`, at salitang-ugat na `hirap` (difficulty). "May pagkahilig na magdulot ng hirap."
original_explanation: This could be your terror prof in college, a toxic boss, or a government policy that makes life harder for the common tao. It's anything or anyone that adds an unnecessary level of difficulty to your life. Yung feeling na "Bakit kailangang maging ganito kahirap?"—yan, may **mapagpahirap** na nangyayari.
usage_notes: Maaaring ilarawan ang isang tao, kilos, sistema, o sitwasyon. Nagdadala ng napakatinding negatibong bigat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuligsa ng mga manggagawa ang **mapagpahirap** na patakaran ng kumpanya.","translation":"The workers condemned the company's **oppressive** policy."},{"sentence":"Ang isang **mapagpahirap** na pinuno ay hindi magtatagal sa pwesto.","translation":"An **oppressive** leader will not last long in their position."}]
